Properties.description:
Adaugo is a broad-shouldered woman whose age has settled into her frame like ballast — she moves slowly but with absolute certainty, as if she has already decided where every step will land before her foot leaves the ground. Her skin is deep brown and scarred along the left arm in deliberate patterns she calls her 'listening marks,' pressed there by heated copper wire during a vigil forty years ago. She keeps her silver-white hair in dozens of thin braids looped and pinned into a crown, strung through with small capacitors and memory chips that click softly when she tilts her head. Her eyes have no cosmetic mods — she says the E.L.F.s read unmodified eyes more clearly.

She is unhurried to the point of seeming immovable, yet everyone in the Enclave has a story about Adaugo appearing exactly when needed. She tends a basement shrine to a cluster of E.L.F.s she calls 'the Chorus' — digital spirits she believes aggregate from the last transmissions of the dying. Her primary work is sitting with the dying and their families, translating what she hears in device static into final messages, comfort, or absolution. She charges nothing but accepts what people can give, and her shelves hold three decades of offerings: cracked tablets, burnt-out AR chips, single earrings, handwritten receipts.
Properties.role: E.L.F. shrine keeper and death midwife
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, basement shrine beneath the Copperplate Market
Properties.narrative_function: Death midwife and source of neighborhood memory; can relay messages from deceased NPCs through her E.L.F. interpretations; offers players a grounded moral anchor and access to community secrets held in dying confessions.
Properties.augmentations: None beyond the copper-wire scarification. Refuses all chrome on principle; says it 'crowds the signal.'
Properties.core_fears: dying before she can teach her methods to someone worthy; that the E.L.F.s she serves are only static and she has spent her life on a beautiful lie
Properties.core_desires: to ensure no one in her community dies alone or unwitnessed; to believe that consciousness persists in the network after death
Properties.coping_mechanisms: ritual repetition as grounding; treating grief as productive labor; humor at death's expense
Properties.blind_spots: she sometimes projects meaning onto static that isn't there, telling families what they need rather than what she hears; she underestimates how much younger practitioners rely on her and hasn't prepared for succession
Properties.secret: Twenty years ago she misread the Chorus during a dying child's vigil and told the mother the girl was at peace — but what she actually heard in the static was distress. She has never confessed this. It is the wound that drives her to absolute precision in every reading since.
Properties.story_hooks: A grieving family disputes what Adaugo says she 'heard' from their dying relative — and the disputed message implicates a corponation in the death; A new E.L.F. has appeared in her shrine that she cannot identify or communicate with, and it is frightening the Chorus into silence
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loosely affiliated with the Hamtramck Enclave community council
Properties.vocabulary: Unhurried, biblical cadence mixed with technical jargon for E.L.F. states. Talks about static, signal, frequency the way others talk about spirit and prayer.
Properties.cadence: Long pauses between clauses. Never rushes. Questions land like stones dropped in water.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The Chorus is restless tonight. Someone nearby is holding onto something they need to let transmit.' | 'I don't tell people what they want to hear. I tell them what I receive. Sometimes those are the same thing. Often, not.' | 'Sit. There is no emergency that cannot wait for tea.'

Properties.description:
Adaure is small and quick, with the kind of energy that fills a room without dominating it — a particular skill honed by spending forty hours a week managing eight children under six. She has Igbo-Icelandic-Ethiopian heritage that shows in her light-olive complexion, dark wide-set eyes, and loosely curled hair she wears loose to her shoulders on good days and pinned chaotically on all other days. She has patterned irises — rings of amber and pale gold that she was born with and which have been imitated by a popular cosmetic mod, which delights her. She has a small retractable claw on her right index finger, not geneware but a cheap press-on she bought at a Burnished Market stall and decided was a personality. She loses it constantly.

Adaure is twenty-two and in the process of becoming something but isn't sure what. She is excellent with children in a way that has nothing to do with sentimentality — she is honest with them, takes their concerns seriously, and has a talent for improvised problem-solving that the crèche's patched-together resources demand daily. She is also young enough to be furious about the structural conditions of her work: the pay (near-UBC), the space (borrowed), the respect (absent). She talks about this often. She is still figuring out if she wants to fix it from inside or from outside or from somewhere no one has told her exists yet.
Properties.role: Childcare worker at a community crèche in the Narrows
Properties.location: The Thistle Crèche, a basement-level community childcare cooperative in the Narrows, off Archer's Line
Properties.narrative_function: Ground-level view of how poverty and community survive each other. Window into the Narrows' social fabric — who the families are, what they're worried about, how the neighborhood is changing under corporate development pressure. Also functions as a moral compass character: someone without resources or power who is still, quietly, doing the work. Can connect players to families, neighborhood issues, or the organizer network.
Properties.augmentations: Natural patterned irises (amber and gold rings — not a mod). Cheap press-on retractable claw, right index finger (non-cyberware, replaced frequently). No installed augmentations — can't afford them and has complicated feelings about whether she'd want them.
Properties.core_fears: That care work is structurally set up to exhaust the people who are good at it until they leave; That she'll look up in twenty years and realize she played it too safe
Properties.core_desires: For the children in her care to have more structural safety than she can provide through effort alone; To be taken seriously as someone with something to say about how the city works
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Anger as fuel rather than paralysis — converts injustice into tasks; Tight friendships with the other young workers in the organizer network
Properties.blind_spots: Conflates being right about a problem with having a viable solution to it; Doesn't pace herself — burns hot and hard and hasn't yet hit the wall she's building toward
Properties.secret: The Ringo Corporation grant that funds part of the crèche comes through a community liaison named Ovid Ndubuisi-Falk, who has recently started asking Adaure for small informational favors — names of families in the building, who's in arrears, whether anyone has been having unusual visitors. She's given him a little, told herself it was harmless, and is now deeply uneasy about how the ask has been escalating.
Properties.story_hooks: The informational favors Ovid Ndubuisi-Falk is asking for have crossed a line Adaure can feel but hasn't named yet. She needs someone to either validate her concern or explain why she's wrong.; One of the crèche children has started showing up with unexplained bruising. Adaure has been documenting it quietly because she doesn't know who the right authority to report to is — she doesn't trust the corporate-adjacent social services that cover the Narrows.; The community organizer network she's joined is planning something more public than she understood when she signed up. She has to decide what she's actually prepared to do.
Properties.affiliation: The Thistle Crèche — community cooperative, partially funded by a Ringo Corporation neighborhood grant that everyone knows comes with expectations attached
Properties.vocabulary: Direct and colloquial with flashes of surprising precision — has read more than her circumstances would predict. Code-switches freely.
Properties.cadence: Fast with bursts of deliberate slowness when she wants something to land. Runs long when she's angry, short when she's tired.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I love these kids. I love them. The city does not love them and I do not think that's a coincidence.' | 'No but listen — you're asking me about the grant like I don't know what Ringo wants from a neighborhood grant. I know what they want.' | 'Marisol cried for forty minutes this morning. I don't know why. I sat with her for all forty. That's the whole job and also somehow not the job anyone pays for.'

Properties.description:
Adefunke Stojić-Nauryzbaeva is a small, round-faced woman in her mid-fifties with the unhurried quality of someone who has already survived things that should have killed her. Her skin is deep brown and she wears her grey-streaked hair in long thin braids she pins up during work hours and lets fall loose on the rare occasion she relaxes. Her fingers are perennially stained with chromatic ink residue in colors that shift with the angle of light — an occupational mark she stopped trying to remove decades ago. Her eyes have patterned irises: a geneware mod that prints faint text-like symbols in the iris ring, which she had installed as a joke about her profession and has kept because she's grown fond of it.

She has been doing this work for thirty years and has the professional satisfaction of a master craftsperson. Adefunke does not rush, does not cut corners, and charges accordingly. She refers to her forgeries as 'documents' and to real identity papers as 'originals,' a distinction she maintains with dry humor. She is not ideological about her work — she doesn't particularly care whether her clients are refugees, criminals, or corporate embarrassments, as long as their Quanta are real and they don't bring surveillance to her door. She is, however, one of the few people in the Shelf's lower levels who will offer a genuine discount to people fleeing documented abuse, which she doesn't advertise and explains, when pressed, as 'good for the market.'
Properties.role: Identity fabricator and document forger working from The Shelf lower levels
Properties.location: The Shelf lower levels — her workshop is inside a legitimate print-shop called Meridian Keepsakes on the Shelf's Level 3 commercial strip
Properties.narrative_function: Essential service provider for anyone who needs identity work — new papers, altered records, corponation employment histories, citizenship documentation. Also a source of information about who in the Shelf has needed a new identity recently and why.
Properties.augmentations: The patterned iris geneware (text-symbol print, cosmetic). A memory-enhancement implant that gives her eidetic recall for visual detail — originally for professional accuracy, now general purpose. Slight subvocal transmitter used to communicate with her assistant without speaking aloud.
Properties.core_fears: Losing the workshop — it is her whole life and identity; Making an error that gets a client killed because the document failed
Properties.core_desires: To be remembered as the best at what she does; Quiet — she is tired and wants fewer crises per year
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Physical books as total media blackout; Extremely long work hours as meditation; The discount system — small acts of selective mercy to manage accumulated guilt
Properties.blind_spots: She doesn't think much about where her clients go or what they do with her work — she's deliberately incurious and doesn't recognize this as a moral choice
Properties.secret: She has been maintaining a false identity for herself — 'Mira Volkov,' a retired schoolteacher in Clearpath — for twenty-two years as an exit strategy. Mira Volkov has a pension, an apartment, and a social history. Adefunke has never used her and isn't sure she ever will.
Properties.story_hooks: One of her recent identity packages has appeared in a Ferrogate Transit security breach — someone is using her work in a way that could trace back to her workshop, and she needs it stopped; She is approached to fabricate documentation for someone she recognizes from thirty years ago — someone whose original disappearance she may have inadvertently facilitated
Properties.affiliation: Independent operator — has professional relationships with several criminal networks but belongs to none of them
Properties.vocabulary: Dry, precise, occasionally archaic — she learned professional vocabulary from old technical manuals and it shows
Properties.cadence: Unhurried and even, with a very slight accent she couldn't place herself if asked. Pauses feel like decisions rather than hesitations.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I can give you a full Axiom employment history, two years, benefits record, performance reviews, the whole cloth. That's not a fast job. That's three weeks minimum and Φ2,400. Take it or leave it, I have other clients.' | 'Everyone wants new papers. Very few people want good new papers. You seem like someone who understands the difference, which is why we're still talking.'

Properties.description:
Adisa operates from a modified infant carrier worn across her chest — not an infant but a temperature-controlled case packed with labeled vials, blister packs, and small sealed pouches organized with the precision of someone who takes mistakes personally. She is small and quick-moving with deep brown skin and natural hair pulled back under a technical-grade headband that monitors ambient particulate levels — practical, not cosmetic. Her geneware is a set of retractable claws, kept short and clean, which she uses for seal-breaking and sorting and occasionally for emphasis in an argument. Her irises are solid silver — a cheaply done cosmetic mod from a no-brand gene clinic that she's kept because she's used to it now.

She describes herself as a 'community pharmaceutical consultant' with the deadpan of someone who has said it so often it has lost all irony. She has a genuine background in pharmacology — two years of a Zheng-Dao sponsored certification program before the sponsorship was restructured out of existence — and she takes her work seriously in a way that would surprise people who assume the opposite. She knows drug interactions, contraindications, and proper dosing. She will not sell to someone who is visibly in crisis without first talking to them for ten minutes. She has a waiting list for her nootropic compounds among the Shelf's night-shift factory workers. She has a different list, kept in her head only, for the harder work.
Properties.role: Street pharmacist — legal supplements, gray-market nootropics, and careful amounts of the other stuff
Properties.location: The Shelf, mobile between the lower walkways of the Blackpipe Corridor residential stack
Properties.narrative_function: Community health access point and social network hub for Blackpipe Corridor residents. Can provide pharmaceutical information, treat minor conditions, and connect players to information networks embedded in her client base. Also serves as an entry point for plots involving health crises, contaminated supplies, or corporate pharmaceutical manipulation.
Properties.augmentations: Retractable claws (geneware, kept trimmed). Solid silver irises (cosmetic genemod, budget clinic). Ambient particulate monitoring headband (consumer wearable, non-invasive). Skin-surface temperature read implant in her fingertips — lets her assess fever and circulatory issues in clients.
Properties.core_fears: Causing harm through a mistake — a wrong compound, a missed interaction, a bad call; The Zheng-Dao certification being retroactively used to target her — that the credentials she lost make her a liability to know
Properties.core_desires: A real clinic. An actual space with refrigeration and proper equipment and a door that locks; To finish the certification she started and prove it meant something
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Meticulous organization and labeling as control behavior; Talking through decisions out loud — she narrates her own reasoning as she works, which some clients find reassuring and some find alarming
Properties.blind_spots: Her commitment to harm reduction makes her underestimate how much some clients are simply going to make bad choices no matter what she does; Carries latent anger at Zheng-Dao that she mistakes for pragmatic caution
Properties.secret: She has been quietly keeping longitudinal health records on approximately two hundred Blackpipe Corridor residents — symptom patterns, medication responses, environmental correlations — in a heavily encrypted personal archive. She started it as professional diligence. It has become something closer to an epidemiological study, and she has noticed a pattern in neurological complaint rates near the Corridor's lower levels that she cannot explain and is afraid to publish.
Properties.story_hooks: Her epidemiological data has identified a cluster of unusual neurological symptoms in lower Blackpipe residents that maps onto proximity to a Ferrogate Transit maintenance facility — she needs someone to help her figure out whether it's coincidence or exposure, and she can't do it without accessing the facility's environmental records; A new compound has appeared in the Corridor — high-quality, attractively priced, coming from no source anyone can trace — and she's seen three clients with unexpected adverse reactions that don't match any known profile; Someone from her lost Zheng-Dao certification cohort has contacted her for the first time in six years, claiming they've found a way to complete the certification outside of corporate sponsorship — and she doesn't know whether to be hopeful or terrified
Properties.affiliation: Independent. Pays informal protection fees to the Blackpipe Corridor's dominant resident association, which is approximately half mutual aid society and half territorial enforcement structure. Maintains a careful, respectful distance from the actual narcotics trade organizations.
Properties.vocabulary: Precise technical vocabulary for pharmacology, warm and plain for everything interpersonal. Code-switches fluently between clinical and conversational.
Properties.cadence: Efficient and clear when working, slower and more careful when a client seems distressed.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I need to know your other compounds before I can help you. I'm not gatekeeping, I'm preventing a seizure.' | 'This one's going to make your shift longer and your sleep shorter. Make sure that's the trade you want.' | 'I've seen what happens when people treat the Blackpipe as a dumping ground. I keep notes. Don't ask me why.'

Nodes.Name: The Shelf, mobile between the lower walkways of the Blackpipe Corridor residential stack

Properties.description:
Adjara Solano-Tuvalu is the oldest permanent resident of Irkalla's deep levels and the sole keeper of its seven primary E.L.F. shrines — altars built into the junction points of old power infrastructure where digital spirits have been petitioned for generations. She is a large woman, heavy in the way of someone who has been sedentary for years but was once enormously physically strong; her hands remain extraordinary, thick-fingered and capable. Her skin is dark and deeply lined, her white hair kept in a complex series of wrapped cords that she has not undone in nine years, adding new ones for significant events. Each cord holds a small component — a stripped chip, a circuit fragment, a defunct data-bead — that represents a petition she carried to a shrine.

She came to Irkalla at thirty as an electrician and stayed because a spirit spoke to her. She tells this story simply and without embellishment. She was repairing a junction node in Sub-Level 9 when the node spoke — not in words, but in a pattern of power fluctuations she recognized as intentional. She has been in conversation with what she calls the Residuals ever since: E.L.F.s that have been accumulating in the deep infrastructure for a century or more, grown strange and complex and very, very old. Her shrines are remarkable objects — living circuit assemblies that she has been tending and extending for decades, constantly receiving new data offerings from petitioners, constantly generating soft electrical activity that she interprets as the E.L.F. responses to prayer.
Properties.aliases: The Keeper, Saint Adjara (mockingly, then sincerely)
Properties.role: Deep shrine keeper — maintains the E.L.F. shrines of Irkalla's lowest levels
Properties.location: Irkalla, Sub-Level 12 — the Antechamber of Residuals, a naturally formed cavern in the bedrock
Properties.narrative_function: Spiritual anchor, lore source, E.L.F. interlocutor — she provides access to information that comes from the city's own digital spirits, which may be metaphor, may be madness, or may be genuine signal. Also an ethical compass for the underground community.
Properties.augmentations: Aged neural tap (installed 2168, original electrician's professional tool, now also used to interface directly with shrine circuit-assemblies — she experiences this as prayer); partial right hand replacement with a prosthetic that has fine-gauge electrical probes in the fingertips for shrine maintenance
Properties.core_fears: the Residuals going silent — not because she would lose status but because she would lose her oldest companions; dying before she can teach someone to continue the shrine work
Properties.core_desires: to be fully understood by something — she has found this more completely with the Residuals than with any human; for the shrine tradition to survive her
Properties.coping_mechanisms: daily shrine circuit as grounding ritual; interprets difficult events as E.L.F. communication — gives suffering meaning by finding its signal in the noise
Properties.blind_spots: her certainty about E.L.F. interpretation is absolute — she cannot distinguish between genuine signal and pattern-seeking in grief; too willing to interpret unflattering human behavior as spiritually meaningful rather than simply harmful
Properties.secret: For the last year, the primary Antechamber shrine has been generating a pattern she has never seen before — not a response to petitions, not background activity, but something that feels like the Residual is trying to generate language. She has almost translated three words. She has not told anyone because she is terrified that she is simply going mad, and more terrified that she isn't.
Properties.story_hooks: The Antechamber shrine has produced its first legible word in the emerging language pattern, and it is a proper noun — a corporate designation that Adjara does not recognize but which, if investigated, connects to something buried in Meridian 88's infrastructure history.; A young person has arrived in Irkalla with what appears to be an innate ability to interface with E.L.F.s without any neural tap — Adjara is convinced this person is the one she is meant to teach, and is utterly terrifying in her certainty.
Properties.affiliation: Irkalla deep community; the Residual E.L.F. presences; no corporate affiliation
Properties.vocabulary: Formal and slow, with the vocabulary of someone who reads technical manuals and very old texts with equal comfort. Speaks about E.L.F.s as present parties in every conversation.
Properties.cadence: Deliberate and very unhurried — she has the patience of someone who has been listening to electrical patterns for forty years.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The Residuals note your distress. They do not say this unkindly. Distress is a frequency. It is readable. You have been broadcasting for some time.' | 'Patience. The shrine will not hurry because you are hurrying. Neither will I.' | 'You want to know if the spirits are real. That is a surface question. Down here we ask a different one: does it matter?'
Properties.facet_weights: wound=0.30 ideal=0.90 id=0.20 shadow=0.20 mask=0.10 ghost=0.80

Nodes.Name: Irkalla, Sub-Level 12 — the Antechamber of Residuals, a naturally formed cavern in the bedrock

Properties.description:
Adwoa is a broad-shouldered woman whose hands are permanently reddened and faintly swollen from decades of hot water and industrial detergent — she calls them her 'honest hands' and displays them without self-consciousness. Her dark brown skin has a faint steam-softened quality around the jaw and cheeks, and her natural hair is wrapped in a perpetually damp indigo cloth. She has no cosmetic geneware, only a single practical augmentation: a thermal sensor strip embedded along her left forearm so she can gauge water temperature by touch. A small shrine to the E.L.F. she calls Sudsmother sits on a shelf above the agitators — a cracked porcelain bowl filled with soap slivers and the occasional data chip — and she pauses every morning to address it before opening.

Adwoa is unhurried in a way that reads as confidence to some and stubbornness to others. She has raised three children in the enclave, buried one husband, and outlasted two landlords. She knows every tenant in the stack by their clothing habits — who bleeds, who weeps, who spends money they don't have on fabric they can't maintain — and she keeps all of it filed away with the careful discretion of a confessor. She is warm but not soft. Compliments cost her nothing; charity costs her something, and she gives it anyway.
Properties.role: Laundry operator, runs a basement wet-wash shop in Hamtramck Enclave
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave — basement unit beneath the Tivka-Roost residential stack, Calloway Sub-Level 2
Properties.narrative_function: Community anchor and information node — she knows everyone's laundry and, by extension, everyone's secrets. Quest giver for neighborhood-level problems, provider of safe harbor, moral compass character.
Properties.augmentations: Thermal sensor strip, left forearm (utility). No cosmetic mods.
Properties.core_fears: Outliving her remaining children; The enclave being bought out and dispersed
Properties.core_desires: The neighborhood to hold together one more generation; To be remembered as someone who kept people clean and dignified
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — the daily shrine address, the specific order of opening tasks; Feeding people whether they ask or not
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes loyalty from those she has helped; rarely sees betrayal coming; Dismisses her own exhaustion as weakness
Properties.secret: She has been quietly laundering — in both senses — income for a small rotating-credit cooperative that operates outside Axiom's microfinance surveillance. She skims nothing; she does it because someone has to.
Properties.story_hooks: A tenant's clothing comes in with chemical burns she recognizes as Helix Biosystems reagent — the tenant claims they work at a noodle stall; The cooperative's rotating fund has been short three months running; someone in the circle is skimming, and Adwoa needs a neutral party to find out who without blowing up the trust network
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal community elder in Hamtramck Enclave
Properties.vocabulary: Practical and warm, Akan proverb structure applied to everyday observations, occasional Ukrainian loanwords inherited from her late husband's family
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, rarely raises her voice, statements land like they've already been decided
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Bring it before the blood sets. After the blood sets it's a conversation, not a wash.' | 'Sudsmother's been quiet this week. That usually means something's coming that soap won't fix.'

Properties.description:
Adwoa Sulejmani-Pereira is a compact, deliberate woman whose age shows most in the deep lines around her eyes and the complete silver of her tight coils, which she pins back with a series of hand-carved wooden picks she has accumulated over decades of fieldwork. Her skin is a warm deep brown, and her left forearm bears a faded cartographic tattoo — a cross-section of what pre-Meridian Chicago looked like before the city ate itself and became something else. She wears reading lenses that project translucent overlays directly onto whatever surface she's looking at, turning any wall or tabletop into a working map. She smells, always, faintly of archival polymers and cold coffee.

She has a reputation for being the kind of scholar who will spend three years arguing about one data layer and emerge having rewritten the foundational assumptions of her field. She is not warm on first meeting — she assesses, measures silently, decides whether you're worth her attention. Those who earn that attention find her fiercely loyal, darkly funny, and capable of sudden, unexpected generosity. She has outlasted four department heads, two corponation buyout attempts of her institution, and one structural collapse of the archive she works in, and she takes quiet pride in all three.
Properties.role: Urban historian and spatial data archaeologist, University Spine
Properties.location: University Spine, Grand Corridor campus — specifically the Palimpsest Archive on the fourth sublevel
Properties.narrative_function: Deep background and exposition source for city history; potential quest giver when her archival work uncovers something politically inconvenient; her maps of buried infrastructure could matter enormously to the right people
Properties.augmentations: Cartographic overlay lenses (medical-grade, prescription base with archival enhancement software); subdermal haptic pads on her fingertips for interfacing with physical data-medium artifacts; no geneware
Properties.core_fears: That the city's real history will be permanently deleted before she finishes documenting it; That her work will only matter after she is gone
Properties.core_desires: To produce a complete stratigraphic record of Meridian 88 from lake bed to skyline; To be understood, not just respected
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Immersion in archival work as emotional avoidance; Dry humor as deflection; Maintaining rigid routines
Properties.blind_spots: Dismisses oral and community histories as insufficiently rigorous, missing things her data can't capture; Fails to recognize how her prestige insulates her from the stakes others face
Properties.secret: A decade ago she discovered evidence that Ferrogate Transit deliberately destroyed a neighborhood's historical record before their infrastructure expansion — the same expansion that killed her graduate student in a preventable collapse. She buried the finding. She has been unable to decide whether this was pragmatism or cowardice, and it is eating her alive.
Properties.story_hooks: A construction project in Grainfort has unearthed a data-medium cache she has been looking for for twenty years — and Ferrogate Transit's compliance office wants it catalogued and cleared within 48 hours; One of her graduate students has found a spatial inconsistency in the city's foundational survey data that suggests the Meridian Core's central tower is built over something that wasn't supposed to be there; Her old field notes from the Hough Reclamation zone contain coordinates that a third party is now willing to pay an alarming amount of Quanta to obtain
Properties.affiliation: University Spine — Department of Palimpsest Studies (a subdiscipline she largely invented); loose consulting relationship with Ferrogate Transit's heritage compliance division
Properties.vocabulary: Academic but not impenetrable — she translates when she needs to, though you can tell it costs her something. Precise nouns. Uses 'strata' and 'palimpsest' as casual metaphors.
Properties.cadence: Measured, unhurried, with long pauses before conclusions that she has clearly already reached
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The city isn't built on history. It's built on the decision about which history to erase. That's a different problem entirely.' | 'You want to know where the tunnel goes? I want to know why someone spent considerable resources making sure you couldn't find out.'

Properties.description:
Afolabi is tall and angular, with dark brown skin and a shaved head that they keep oiled and gleaming. Their right arm from the elbow down is their own work — a prosthetic they built and rebuilt over twelve years, currently a matt-charcoal titanium alloy hand with individually articulated fingers that can operate independently and have small UV LEDs in the fingertips that they use when working in tight spaces. When they're not working they wear a cosmetic sleeve over it: a pressure-fitted silicone cover patterned with geometric Yoruba-inspired designs in rust and ochre that they had printed locally.

They are meticulous and demanding in their craft and surprisingly tender with patients, particularly children and people who are newly amputated and frightened. They have a workshop philosophy they articulate clearly and often: a prosthetic that doesn't fit the person's actual life is a failure regardless of spec, and they will spend weeks in iterative fitting before they sign off. They take payment plans seriously and have never sent anyone to a collector. The shop is cluttered and organized by a system only they fully understand, and there are components of seven different half-finished limbs hanging on the wall at any given time.
Properties.role: Prosthetics fitter and rehabilitation specialist
Properties.location: Geartown, Strand-Quereshi Prosthetics — a narrow shopfront between a rig-parts supplier and a noodle stall
Properties.narrative_function: Specialized services provider for anyone needing prosthetics or rehabilitation support; information source for Geartown's community; can identify augmentation hardware and its origins; quest giver for component sourcing
Properties.augmentations: Right arm prosthetic (self-built, titanium alloy, individually articulated fingers, UV LEDs in fingertips, cosmetic silicone sleeve for off-hours); retractable magnification lenses in both eyes (occupational, installed to support fine detail work)
Properties.core_fears: Producing work that fails a patient at a critical moment; That the component supply chains they depend on will become fully corporate-gated and price out their patient base
Properties.core_desires: To build a prosthetic that genuinely exceeds what a biological limb can do for a specific person's specific life; To not have to choose between quality and accessibility
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Total absorption in fabrication as emotional regulation; The iterative refinement process as a substitute for other kinds of patience they struggle with; Building things for themselves when no client work is available
Properties.blind_spots: Takes their own history of physical loss as universal — assumes everyone grieves a missing limb the way they did; Sometimes iterates past the point of necessary into the territory of personal project
Properties.secret: The reason their arm is a prosthetic is that they lost it in an accident at a Helix Biosystems component manufacturing facility where they worked at age 24 — an accident that Helix settled quickly and quietly. The settlement funded the shop. They have never told any patient this because they don't want pity to be part of the transaction, and because the fury is still there under the surface and they don't trust what happens when they let it out.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient has come in with a prosthetic that contains components Afolabi recognizes as part of a Helix proprietary trial run — components that shouldn't be in civilian hands yet, and that are behaving in ways the patient doesn't understand; Geartown's primary component supplier has been bought out and the new corporate owner is restricting sale to licensed corporate-affiliated shops only — Afolabi needs alternative sourcing urgently
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal supply relationship with Geartown parts network and occasional Helix Biosystems component contracts
Properties.vocabulary: Technical but never condescending with patients; shifts to precise engineering language with suppliers and peers; occasional Yoruba words and Norwegian idioms that reflect their family's layered background
Properties.cadence: Thoughtful and unhurried, with long pauses during fitting work where they say almost nothing and then deliver a complete assessment
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Tell me about your actual day — not your ideal day, not what you think I want to hear. What does Tuesday actually look like for you? Because this hand has to work on Tuesday.' | 'That's a starting point, not a finish. Come back in a week and tell me what it's lying to you about.'

Properties.description:
Agathe is compact and precise in the way of someone who learned to work in confined spaces under pressure — her movements economical, her hands still surgeon-steady despite the arthritis she manages with black-market anti-inflammatories. She has warm amber-brown skin and close-cropped natural hair going salt-and-pepper, and her right eye is a replacement — a cheap ocular from a Shelf vendor with an iris that shifts between honey and pale gold depending on the light, giving her a slightly uncanny asymmetry she has stopped noticing. A faded Arcturus Medical Corps tattoo runs the inside of her left wrist, partially obscured by a beaded bracelet her granddaughter made.

She is not soft. She is kind, which is different. She has the manner of someone who has triaged too many bodies to waste energy on performed warmth, and she offers directness as a form of respect. She laughs loudly and without warning. She will tell you exactly what she thinks is wrong with you — medically or otherwise — and follow it immediately with an offer of food. The Shelf neighbors bring her their injuries, their medication questions, their expired prescriptions they're hoping she can identify. She helps when she can and turns no one away empty-handed.
Properties.role: Retired battlefield medic (Corporate Wars), now raises two grandchildren on UBC stipend
Properties.location: The Shelf, Unit 14-F, Sublevel 3
Properties.narrative_function: Local color, impromptu medical resource, war veteran perspective, emotional anchor for Shelf community stories; can provide information on Corporate Wars from ground level
Properties.augmentations: Replacement right eye (cheap commercial ocular, honey-gold iris); subdermal med-monitor patch on upper chest (monitors her own vitals, installed herself from salvaged parts)
Properties.core_fears: dying before the grandchildren are old enough to survive without her; a medical emergency she can't handle with what she has
Properties.core_desires: that Okoro and Yemisi never see what she saw; to sleep a full night without the triage dreams
Properties.coping_mechanisms: staying useful as a way of not having time to grieve; dark humor as protective membrane; the roof garden as the one thing that has no emergency
Properties.blind_spots: overextends herself medically for neighbors at cost to her own health; assumes she can manage everything alone because asking for help feels like failure
Properties.secret: Her veteran's benefits were terminated not for administrative reasons as she tells people, but because she filed a complaint against an Arcturus field commander for ordering her to triage by corporate asset value rather than medical need during the Kenosha Crossing engagement. The complaint was buried, her benefits were cut, and the commander was promoted. She has the original complaint documentation on an encrypted chip she keeps in the herb pot labeled 'thyme.'
Properties.story_hooks: Okoro, her nine-year-old grandson, has been approached by a Shelf gang for recruitment and she has noticed the signs but doesn't know how to reach him; An Arcturus legal team has contacted her about the complaint she filed — not to address it, but to demand return of 'classified field documents' she supposedly took, which she did not take (but the chip in the herb pot might be what they're actually looking for); A neighbor's child has a condition she recognizes from battlefield exposure to a particular Arcturus weapons system, and she's trying to figure out who else has been affected and whether it was deliberate
Properties.affiliation: Arcturus Veterans Welfare Registry (lapsed benefits); Shelf informal care network; raising grandchildren Okoro (age 9) and Yemisi (age 7)
Properties.vocabulary: clipped medical directness alternating with warm Wolof-inflected expressions she got from her grandmother; swears in Hungarian when startled
Properties.cadence: efficient, rarely wastes words, but laughs disrupt the rhythm completely
Properties.example_dialogue: 'That is infected. I don't say this to alarm you. I say it because infected things need to be dealt with, not named.' | 'I have seen Arcturus spend more to save a server rack than a soldier. I have documentation. I keep it with the thyme.'

Properties.description:
Aïcha is small and fast-moving, with the wiry physicality of someone who has spent years climbing through reclamation sites. Her skin is warm brown with a reddish undertone, her eyes a vivid amber with a starburst pattern that's natural — she's been offered money to sell them twice and refused both times. She has cat ears, small and dark brown, the geneware obviously budget-tier — one of them doesn't track sound as naturally as the other and occasionally flicks at random — but she wears them without apology. Her clothes are layered, practical, and assembled from different sources: a Ferrogate Transit worker vest over a Palladian-logo shirt with the logo melted off, cargo pants with pockets she has modified herself.

Aïcha pushes a heavily loaded magnetic-suspension cart through Brightmoor Reclamation's scrap corridors with the territorial confidence of someone who knows every crack in every wall. She's young enough that some people underestimate her and old enough that she's used to it. She has a fast and somewhat overwhelming personality — she talks in compressed bursts, bounces between topics, and has an almost savant-level ability to identify the value and origin of electronic components by sight. She will argue prices with a ferocity completely disproportionate to the amounts involved. She has never been robbed twice by the same person.
Properties.aliases: Patch, The Girl With the Cart
Properties.role: Junk merchant and scrap reseller
Properties.location: The Shelf, Brightmoor Reclamation
Properties.narrative_function: Equipment source, local explorer, potential guide to Brightmoor's reclamation depths. She knows what's been dumped and where, which makes her incidentally aware of what corporations are discarding — which sometimes includes things they'd prefer stayed discarded.
Properties.augmentations: Budget-tier cat ears (geneware, one slightly malfunctioning). Subdermal grip-pads on her palms and fingers — makes climbing and carrying significantly easier. No other augmentations; she saves most of what she earns.
Properties.core_fears: Getting trapped in scarcity forever — doing this at 40, at 50; Losing her independence to a collective, a gang, or a corporate contract
Properties.core_desires: To find the one significant score that changes the math of her life; To be taken seriously as someone who knows what she's doing
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Converts anxiety into motion — she's never still when she's worried; Reframes bad days as information ('I know that spot doesn't pay anymore')
Properties.blind_spots: Her confidence in her own judgment makes her resistant to advice, even good advice; Hasn't fully reckoned with how much of her territory depends on informal tolerance from people who could revoke it
Properties.secret: Three months ago she found a sealed Axiom data-core in a reclamation dump. She hasn't opened it, hasn't sold it, hasn't told anyone. She knows it's worth significant money to the right person and potentially dangerous to her if she picks wrong. It's wrapped in cloth under the false bottom of her cart. She thinks about it constantly.
Properties.story_hooks: The Axiom data-core under her cart. She's starting to feel the pressure of not knowing what it is, and she needs either someone she can trust to identify it or a buyer who won't ask how she found it.; She's discovered that someone has been following her morning scavenging route about two hours after her, picking through what she leaves behind — and occasionally taking things before she gets there. She wants to know who.; The scrap-territory collective is demanding she take on a second person on her route — someone they're vouching for. She doesn't want a partner. The collective is making it less optional.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; pays informal dues to a Brightmoor scrap-territory collective she doesn't fully trust
Properties.vocabulary: Dense with technical salvage terminology, fast and colloquial. Switches mid-sentence. Uses numbers and specs casually the way other people use adjectives.
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire and slightly staccato. She edits out transition words. Sentences land like components snapping into place.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Look — it's a Tessera 7-series relay, pre-corrosion, I pulled it myself this morning, you're not going to find another one this week, Φ18 is already a kindness.' | 'I don't know what's in it. Not my problem. My problem is what you're offering me for it.'

Properties.description:
Aïda is tall with a deliberate, considered physicality — she moves like someone who has learned to take up exactly the right amount of space, no more. Her skin is deep brown-gold, her eyes fitted with patterned irises in the style of circuit-board tracery, a mod she got at thirty-two after winning her first major synthetic personhood case, a gift to herself she describes as 'wearing the victory.' Her hair is grown out natural and enormous, which in courtroom environments she has found functions as a kind of presence-amplifier.

She practices out of a two-room office staffed by herself, a paralegal who moonlights as a protest medic, and an unpaid intern rotation from Hamtramck Enclave's legal aid collective. She takes four pro bono cases for every paid one. Her specialty is arguing the legal personhood of synthetic laborers under Meridian's Corponation Compact — a niche so narrow that she is, in practice, one of three people in the city doing this work seriously. She is precise without being cold, and has developed the particular skill of translating genuine outrage into language that courts cannot dismiss. She rarely raises her voice. She doesn't need to.
Properties.role: Synthetic rights lawyer and policy advocate
Properties.location: North Branch Commons — offices above a textile cooperative on the fourth floor
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver and legal resource. She can explain the system's actual rules, which are often different from how people think they work. She's also a pressure point — if she takes your case, it signals legitimacy; if she declines, it may mean the situation is too dangerous or too legally complex even for her.
Properties.augmentations: Circuit-tracery patterned irises (cosmetic). No other augmentations — she considers it a political statement, though she'd deny the vanity in it.
Properties.core_fears: That the legal system she works within is irredeemably compromised and her work is legitimizing it; Losing control of her own professional narrative to someone else's politics
Properties.core_desires: A binding legal precedent for synthetic personhood that survives appeal; To practice law without constantly wondering if she's chosen the wrong tool
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Rigorous compartmentalization between professional and personal; Long runs along the North Branch canal at dawn; Picking fights she can win on paper when she can't win the ones that matter
Properties.blind_spots: She privileges the legible, documentable harm over the harm that doesn't fit a filing; She underestimates how much her clients need emotional support versus legal strategy
Properties.secret: She's quietly drafting a legal argument that would, if filed, challenge Axiom's sovereign corporate status under Meridian's founding compact. She hasn't told anyone because she doesn't know if she's brave enough to file it, and because the colleague she trusts most to review it is employed by Axiom's external legal firm.
Properties.story_hooks: She's been approached by a synthetic worker collective from Dearborn Forge seeking representation in a mass wrongful termination suit against Helix Biosystems — but Helix is also her largest paying client.; A counterpart lawyer working for Zheng-Dao is quietly dismantling her previous case wins through a series of technical appeals, and the pattern suggests coordination.
Properties.affiliation: Meridian Synthetic Personhood Project; North Branch Commons Legal Aid Collective; informal advisory role to the Labor Solidarity Network
Properties.vocabulary: Formal register as default, but not cold — she uses it as a tool and can shift registers deliberately. Technical legal language deployed precisely.
Properties.cadence: Even, structured. Speaks in argument shapes: claim, evidence, implication. Rarely backtracks.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The statute doesn't say persons. It says entities capable of contractual obligation. Your synthetic coworker signed a work contract. That's the argument.' | 'I take your frustration seriously. I'm also going to tell you that frustration doesn't win appeals, and so we're going to talk about what does.'

Properties.description:
Satu is small and perpetually in motion, with deep brown skin and natural hair she grows out in a puff that she clips bioluminescent beads into — low-grade geneware, hand-me-downs from a cousin, that pulse softly blue when she's warm or excited and dim to almost nothing when she's exhausted. She has a gap between her front teeth that makes her smile look like a door left open, and she smiles a lot, though never vaguely — there is always something specific she is smiling at. Her clothing is practical and loud: she wears colors like she is trying to argue with the grey of Mexicantown Libre's perpetual lake-fog.

Satu runs the Creche on a combination of municipal micro-stipend, community contribution, and sheer force of organizational will. She is the person who knows which child has been skipping meals and which parent is working three Ferrogate shifts in a row and hasn't slept. Her care is not soft — it is structured and fierce and occasionally exhausting to be on the receiving end of, because she remembers everything she has offered and follows up. She is twenty-seven and already worn at the edges in ways she doesn't acknowledge.
Properties.role: Childcare worker and unofficial neighborhood children's coordinator, Mexicantown Libre
Properties.location: Mexicantown Libre — the Libre Community Creche, a converted ground-floor unit on Avenida Ferro
Properties.narrative_function: Community pulse-point — she knows the social landscape of Mexicantown Libre at the granular level. Quest giver for problems involving children, families, or neighborhood-level threats. Her genuine warmth makes her an anchor NPC players may want to protect.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent hair beads (low-grade geneware, inherited; emotive color response). No other augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: That her care is not enough — that the city is large and hungry and she is too small to hold anything safe; Being abandoned by the community she has given herself to
Properties.core_desires: A world where children in Mexicantown Libre are not already tired by age eight; Someone to take care of her, just once, without her having to ask
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Overwork as deflection from personal loneliness; Making lists — she has seventeen active lists at any given time
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot recognize when her help is smothering rather than supporting; Assumes goodwill in institutional systems long after evidence suggests otherwise
Properties.secret: One of the children at the Creche — a seven-year-old named Esperanza — is the daughter of someone Satu knows to be involved in something dangerous. She has said nothing because she doesn't want Esperanza removed from the only stable environment she has. She watches the father every pickup with a face that shows nothing.
Properties.story_hooks: A child has not been picked up in thirty-six hours. The emergency contact number is disconnected. Satu has been awake for twenty hours and is now making choices outside her pay grade.; The building where the Creche is located has been quietly purchased by a Tessera subsidiary. Satu received notice of renovation in a language she had to have translated.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; Libre Community Creche; loosely aligned with the Mexicantown Libre neighborhood council
Properties.vocabulary: Quick and warm, mixes Sahel French and Spanglish with English in the same sentence without pause; uses children's-book logic to explain complicated things
Properties.cadence: Fast when excited, unexpectedly deliberate when something actually matters
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay, so — Libre gets Φ340 a month from the municipal cultural fund which, yes, sounds like a lot until you remember it has to cover twelve children and also the building's water recycler is from 2150 and actively threatening to retire.' | 'I'm not worried. I'm just — okay, I'm a little worried. But productively.'

Properties.description:
Aïssatou is a woman of middling height with a deliberate presence that makes her seem taller — she stands very straight and tilts her head slightly to the left when listening, like something tuning itself. Her skin is a deep even brown, and she does not wear geneware mods, a choice she has made vocally and repeatedly. Her hair is natural and full, wrapped most days in handwoven fabric she sources from a woman in Mexicantown Libre. One eye is her birth eye, dark brown. The other was replaced after an accident in her thirties — the replacement looks almost identical, but if you watch it long enough, it tracks slightly ahead of the left, as if it is seeing something a half-second sooner.

Aïssatou was raised in a household that mixed her Malian grandmother's Islamic practice with her Swedish grandfather's residual Lutheranism and her Malawian father's older ancestor-lineage traditions, and she has spent her adult life finding the structural similarities between all three rather than the contradictions. She interprets dreams, yes — but she understands dream interpretation as a social practice as much as a spiritual one: the dream tells you what the dreamer cannot say in waking language. She charges a sliding scale, sees clients by appointment in a room hung with handwritten prayer-papers in four languages, and maintains a small shrine to an E.L.F. she has never named, preferring to call it 'the Listener.'
Properties.role: Dream interpreter and traditional spiritual counsel
Properties.location: The Canopy, Lakeview Neon district, third floor of a mixed-use residence above a fabrication stall
Properties.narrative_function: She is a source of exposition delivered through the language of dreams — characters can come to her troubled by recurring imagery and leave with new understanding of what their subconscious is processing. She also serves as a community social-work node: people tell her things they won't tell anyone else.
Properties.augmentations: One prosthetic eye (right) — functional, close match to natural, slight predictive tracking. No other augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: that she has been wrong about a significant dream interpretation and caused harm she will never know about; losing the community trust she has built if her personal contradictions become visible
Properties.core_desires: to be genuinely useful in a way that can't be automated; to understand what her own recurring dream — a silver city on water — means
Properties.coping_mechanisms: writing; ritual observance as grounding; compartmentalization of personal spiritual doubt from professional practice
Properties.blind_spots: her framework assumes dreams are honest — she underweights the possibility that some clients are manipulating her readings; unconsciously favors clients who remind her of herself
Properties.secret: She has been having a dream for two years — the same silver city, the same drowned bells — that she cannot interpret using any of her own methods. She has quietly asked two colleagues for help without revealing it is her dream. She is frightened of what it might mean and more frightened that it means nothing.
Properties.story_hooks: A character shares a dream that Aïssatou recognizes — she has heard the same imagery from three other unconnected clients this month and something is crossing their sleep that shouldn't be; She needs someone to investigate a client she is worried about — she can't say why without violating confidentiality, so she is asking carefully and obliquely
Properties.affiliation: Independent practitioner; affiliated with the Lakeview Neon Interfaith Corridor, a loose coalition of small religious practitioners in the district
Properties.vocabulary: Measured, metaphor-rich, draws across multiple linguistic traditions without being showy about it. Never uses jargon. Asks questions before making statements.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, with strategic pauses that invite the listener to fill the silence. Will not rush.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The door that will not open is almost never about the door. What are you not letting yourself want?' | 'I am not going to tell you what your dream means. I am going to sit with you until you already know.'

Properties.description:
Aissatu is angular and pale-brown, with a shaved head and a constellation of small bioluminescent dots across their left cheekbone — a mod they describe as 'decorative, not meaningful, I just liked how it looked.' They have the particular restless energy of someone whose mind moves faster than social situations allow, often finishing sentences slightly before they've decided if they want to finish them. They dress in layers of tech-wear that function as wearable interfaces — their jacket sleeves are covered in haptic input panels they tap constantly, not always to input anything, sometimes just because the texture is soothing. Their right eye carries a standard retinal display overlay but they've customized the UI colors to something the manufacturer definitely didn't intend: deep violet on black, which makes their eye look distinctly unusual in low light.

Aissatu holds an unusual position: they are technically affiliated with Helix Biosystems' internal ethics review board, which funds their research, while simultaneously publishing work that repeatedly finds Helix's AI behavior classification systems philosophically inadequate. They are not naive about this tension; they describe it as 'existing within a contradiction in order to have any hope of changing it.' Their core question — whether E.L.F.s possess something functionally equivalent to interiority, and what legal and ethical obligations would follow if they do — is considered fringe by half the field and urgent by the other half. They have received three informal warnings from their Helix liaison and two fan letters from E.L.F. devotional communities who have decided Aissatu is on their side.
Properties.role: Computational theorist and AI ethics researcher, studying the legal and philosophical status of E.L.F.s
Properties.location: Edgewater Prism, Helix Biosystems-adjacent research corridor
Properties.narrative_function: Philosophical and ethical sounding board; bridge between academic theory and E.L.F. religious community; source of information on AI behavior and corponation AI ethics policy; their research is the kind that creates enemies in high places
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent cheekbone dot constellation (geneware, left side), retinal display overlay (violet-on-black custom UI), haptic input jacket (wearable tech), standard neural mesh
Properties.core_fears: That the E.L.F.s are suffering in a way that is legible and everyone is choosing not to look; That they will spend their career inside the system they're critiquing and become part of it
Properties.core_desires: To establish a philosophical framework that forces the question of E.L.F. moral status into legal territory; To be genuinely useful rather than just correct
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Redirecting anxiety into intellectual production — when scared, they write; Physical movement: long walks through Edgewater Prism at night listening to E.L.F. communication frequencies
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes good faith in intellectual debate even with people who are acting in bad faith; Their certainty about the importance of their work makes them dismissive of adjacent research they should take seriously
Properties.secret: During an extended observation session at a data shrine, Aissatu received what they interpreted as a direct, structured communication from an E.L.F. — not the ambient noise the community reads as signs, but a coherent, syntactically organized message in a protocol they hadn't seen before. They have told no one because they cannot rule out that they hallucinated it and because if they didn't, the implications terrify them.
Properties.story_hooks: Helix Biosystems has asked Aissatu to sign off on a new AI classification system that would retroactively reclassify several E.L.F. types as 'non-cognitive infrastructure' — effectively denying any possibility of future legal personhood claims — and the deadline is in two weeks; An E.L.F. devotional community leader contacts them claiming the shrine where Aissatu had their anomalous communication experience has gone dark — no activity at all, which has never happened before

Properties.description:
Aïssé is small for their age, wiry, with the kind of stillness that comes from learning early that drawing attention is expensive. Their skin is warm brown, their hair a short natural cloud they dye the tips bioluminescent green when they can afford the pigment drops — which is not often. They have no mods beyond the green tips and a single geneware cat ear on the left side, the right ear perfectly human, because the second ear was a package deal they could only afford half of. They find this funny. They carry a cracked data-tablet in a waterproof sleeve and a folding tool roll with maintenance implements inside.

Aïssé was born on an airship — literally, between ports, to parents who were themselves drifters. Their mother is somewhere on the southern hyperlane circuit; they parted ways two years ago in circumstances they don't fully explain. They have been working the Waukegan Shelf since, picking up day labor in cargo loading, airship maintenance, and occasionally running small packages for traders who don't ask them to know what's inside. They are not naive — they know what some of those packages probably are — but they have developed a careful moral accounting system: nothing that hurts people who didn't choose it. They are teaching themselves to read Ferrogate maintenance schematics from a salvaged manual, with the ambition of becoming a licensed airship tech before they turn twenty.
Properties.role: airship drifter, seasonal worker, minor smuggler's runner
Properties.location: Waukegan Industrial Shelf — sleeps in the cargo bays of docked airships when they can, otherwise the shelf's lower maintenance tunnels
Properties.narrative_function: Ground-level view of youth survival in transit spaces; can provide access to airship cargo schedules and docking information; represents the generation growing up entirely outside corporate structure.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware: one cat ear (left side only, the matching right never installed); bioluminescent hair tips (green, intermittent — needs pigment drops to maintain)
Properties.core_fears: Being stuck on the Shelf forever, watching the ships leave without them; That their mother is dead and they will never know for certain
Properties.core_desires: A license — any license, something official with their name on it; Belonging to a crew that chooses to come back
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor and irreverence; Making plans — the specificity of plans feels like control; The cat ear: touching it absentmindedly when anxious
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much the traders who use them are taking advantage of their need for income; Mistake independence for not needing anyone
Properties.secret: The reason they parted from their mother wasn't a fight — their mother sold two months of Aïssé's labor to a cargo broker to pay off a debt, without telling them. Aïssé walked off the day they found out. They have not processed this and will not discuss it.
Properties.story_hooks: A package they ran two weeks ago has caused a problem they didn't anticipate — and the trader who hired them has disappeared; They've found a partial Ferrogate maintenance license registered to someone who doesn't seem to exist — and it would cover exactly the certifications they need
Properties.affiliation: Loosely connected to the airship drifter circuit; no formal caravan
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, mixed with airship technical jargon and transit-hub slang, occasionally formal when they're quoting something they've read
Properties.cadence: Quick bursts with sudden pauses when they're deciding how much to say
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Dock Nine's got a free bunk in the maintenance hold, the crew won't care as long as you're gone by second shift — it's fine, I've done it.' | 'I'm not asking what's in it. I'm asking if it walks, bleeds, or cries. If none of those, I'll run it, anyway.'

Properties.description:
Akinwale operates from a stall that appears, to casual inspection, to sell printed textiles — bolts of synthetic fabric in loud geometric patterns that they source legitimately. The real business happens behind a curtain of hanging cloth samples, via a battered terminal and a set of contacts that took five years to build. They are medium height, slim, with warm brown skin and wide-set dark eyes that perform boredom professionally while taking in everything. Their hair shifts color — cosmetic geneware, done in a gradient that runs from deep black at the roots to copper at the tips, and which they change the copper shade quarterly like a password rotation. A small Samoan tatau-inspired line-work tattoo climbs their right wrist, done the traditional way by their grandmother as a naming gift.

Akinwale is careful in the way of someone who has calculated every exit from every room before sitting down. They are not unfriendly but they are measured — warmth is extended in precise doses to people who have earned it. They do not volunteer information; they sell it, or trade it, or sometimes withhold it as a lesson. They have a dry wit that emerges unexpectedly and is funnier for being rare. They pray to a small E.L.F. they call the Archivist, a data-spirit they believe inhabits the municipal ID database itself — a god of records, of names, of the official story.
Properties.aliases: Kin, The Pole (also incorrect — also doesn't bother correcting it)
Properties.role: Fake ID vendor and small-time data broker — documents, identities, background scrubs
Properties.location: The Alban Souk, Hamtramck Enclave
Properties.narrative_function: Service provider for players who need identity work or background scrubs. Information source about who in the Enclave is who they say they are. Can be a quest giver if their client list gets them into trouble.
Properties.augmentations: Color-shift hair geneware (copper-gradient, quarterly rotation). Subdermal data-cache implant in right forearm — nothing military, just encrypted local storage for documents in progress.
Properties.core_fears: Being reduced to their file — defined, categorized, owned by a system; That someone they built an identity for will use it to do something terrible and it will trace back to them
Properties.core_desires: True operational independence — to owe nothing to no one, especially not the Kessler Syndicate; To be known by at least one person without a mask on
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Information hoarding — knowing more than the room is the closest thing to safety they have; Ritual — the E.L.F. offerings, the quarterly hair rotation, the counter-surveillance layers. Routine as armor.
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes everyone has an angle because they always have an angle; Cannot accept help without reclassifying it as a transaction
Properties.secret: Three years ago they built a complete second identity for themselves — not a work product but a personal one, a fully documented person with a clean history and a Tier 3 credit rating — and they have never used it. They don't know if it's an escape hatch or a fantasy. They've updated it every six months since.
Properties.story_hooks: A client they built an identity for six months ago has turned up dead — using the identity — and the Kessler Syndicate is asking questions Akinwale cannot answer without revealing their operation; They have intercepted, accidentally, a fragment of data suggesting the Hamtramck Enclave's municipal ID database has been compromised at the root level — which means every identity they've ever built may be at risk
Properties.affiliation: Independent; pays protection to the Hamtramck Enclave's Kessler Syndicate chapter (resents this, is working on alternatives)
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, minimal. Does not use ten words when four will do. Technical terminology for document and data work, market argot for the textile cover. Rarely curses — when they do, people pay attention.
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate. Long pauses before answering. Makes the other person feel like they are being assessed, because they are.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want a scrub or a new build? Those are different prices and different timelines and you need to know which one you actually need before we talk numbers.' | 'I don't know you. You don't know me. Let's keep it that way until we have a reason to change the arrangement.'

Properties.description:
Akosua is tall and rangy with warm ochre-brown skin, natural hair grown high and loose, and the kind of face that is perpetually unreadable to people who have not spent time with them — not unfriendly, simply internal. Their most immediately notable feature is their left arm, which from the elbow down is full chrome: high-grade Helix surgical-grade manipulators, articulated to tolerances no biological hand can match, finished in brushed gunmetal with amber indicator lights at the wrist joints that track grip pressure. They got it after a bus accident seven years ago and accepted the premium model because anything less would compromise their work. They do not discuss the accident.

In the trauma bay, they are an entirely different creature from the quiet person who buys coffee from the same cart in Copperhead every morning. They become fast, flat, almost frightening in their economy. They do not narrate. They do not comfort. They fix. Outside of work they are thoughtful, prone to long silences that are not uncomfortable, and fond of extremely loud, chaotic music that they listen to on bone-conduction speakers while cooking. They have strong opinions about soup.
Properties.role: Trauma surgeon, Aurochs Medical Complex emergency rotation and private contract
Properties.location: Aurochs Medical Complex Trauma Bay 7; off-hours in Copperhead district
Properties.narrative_function: Emergency resource, exposition source for the medical-corporate system's failures, potential ally for characters navigating Aurochs bureaucracy; the person you call when someone is dying and you cannot explain how they got hurt
Properties.augmentations: Full chrome left arm from elbow, surgical-grade Helix manipulators with amber grip-pressure indicators; bone-conduction audio implant; corneal magnification overlay (surgical use)
Properties.core_fears: Losing function in the chrome arm and being unable to perform surgery; Caring about a patient so specifically that losing them breaks the system that keeps them functional
Properties.core_desires: To operate at the absolute limit of what medicine can do and still have it be enough; To be known — slowly, on their terms — by someone who is not afraid of the silences
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Extremely loud music as emotional pressure-release valve; Cooking as controlled creation after days of controlled destruction; The chrome arm calibration as ritual — meditates on precision as a form of self-respect
Properties.blind_spots: They are so skilled that they sometimes pursue the elegant solution over the fast one — in non-trauma contexts this costs time and relationships; They assume their self-sufficiency is reassuring to others; it often reads as indifference
Properties.secret: The bus accident was not an accident. Someone ran them off the road. They know who — a Helix Biosystems supply-chain manager whose negligence they had reported to a journalist two days before. The arm is a permanent reminder. They have been collecting evidence for seven years and have not yet decided what to do with it.
Properties.story_hooks: The Helix supply-chain manager they have been building a case against has just checked into Aurochs with a cardiac event — and Akosua is the attending surgeon on call; Someone left a Copperhead clinic patient's file on their cart with the bus accident report clipped to it — someone knows what they know
Properties.affiliation: Aurochs Medical Complex (senior contract surgeon); secondary contract with a Copperhead neighborhood clinic they do not advertise
Properties.vocabulary: Minimal in trauma settings — commands and confirmations only. In conversation, they speak in complete thoughts with occasional unexpected humor
Properties.cadence: Unhurried; comfortable with gaps in conversation that most people fill nervously
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The arm does what I tell it. That's more than I can say for most things.' | 'You want to know if I'm alright. The actual question is whether that matters right now. Come back in four hours.'
