Properties.description:
Babatunde is a large, slow-moving man with the kind of bulk that was once muscle and has settled into something more geological. His skin is dark walnut brown, his beard full and peppered grey-white, worn in four loose plaits he ties back during service hours. His Turkish grandmother gave him the Öztürk and a nose like a falcon's beak; his Samoan great-grandfather gave him the Savea and shoulders like a doorframe. He wears the same thing every day: a heat-resistant apron over a sleeveless thermal, arms bare to show the geometric Samoan-style tattoo that wraps from his left wrist to his shoulder, and under it on the inside of his wrist, half-hidden, a small Yoruba adinkra symbol his mother pressed there with a needle when he was seven. Behind the cart he moves with surprising economy, three things happening in each hand simultaneously.

He doesn't talk much while working, but when the lunch rush ebbs he will lean on the cart and hold a conversation that feels unhurried in a way that is almost physically restful. He has opinions about everything — city politics, the flavor profile of various E.L.F.s' preferred data offerings, whether the Ferrogate expansion is actually gentrification in a steel tube — but he delivers them the way he delivers broth: slow, hot, with depth that surprises you. He has been at this corner for twenty-two years. He knows every face.
Properties.role: Noodle cart vendor, The Burnished Market
Properties.location: The Burnished Market, permanent pitch at the corner of Grainfort and Ironvein
Properties.narrative_function: The neighborhood oracle — has seen everything, knows everyone, rarely volunteers information but rarely refuses a direct question from someone he's decided to trust. Quest giver for neighborhood-level problems. Offers food as social currency.
Properties.augmentations: Thermal-resistant dermal layer on both palms (practical, work-grade); bioluminescent ink in the tattoo on his left arm that pulses faint blue-gold in the dark — a cosmetic addition his daughter talked him into ten years ago
Properties.core_fears: outliving his purpose — becoming invisible in old age; his daughter leaving Meridian 88 and not coming back
Properties.core_desires: to feed people well, which he believes is a form of love; to see the Burnished Market survive the next round of corporate rezoning
Properties.coping_mechanisms: cooking as meditation; humor — slow, dry, devastating; letting go of what he can't control by naming it clearly and moving on
Properties.blind_spots: underestimates how much his stability depends on city tolerance he has no legal protection for; believes he can read people infallibly; occasionally very wrong about the quietly dangerous ones
Properties.secret: The Vendors' Collective's emergency fund — which he informally administers — is Φ4,000 short because twelve years ago he used it to bribe a city inspector to overlook code violations that would have shut down six other vendors' stalls. He has never told anyone and has been quietly paying it back at Φ30 a month ever since.
Properties.story_hooks: A Tessera rezoning notice has appeared on the market's bulletin board — not official, but the kind of notice that means someone is testing the water. Tunde is quietly organizing vendors to resist, and he needs someone to find out who filed the notice without tipping off Tessera.; He's kept a lost child's hand-drawn picture that was left at his cart seven years ago — a picture that, now that someone's looking at it closely, appears to show a specific building that shouldn't exist according to any city record.
Properties.affiliation: Independent (Burnished Market Vendors' Collective, informal)
Properties.vocabulary: Warm, unhurried, vernacular-rich. Mixes Yoruba endearments, some Turkish expressions for frustration, occasional Samoan cadences in his syntax.
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate. Pauses for effect. Never rushes.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'This broth has been on the heat since three this morning. It has earned your respect. Sit. Eat.' | 'The corponations want that corner? They've wanted it for fifteen years. I'm still here. Come back in fifteen more and we'll have this same conversation.'

Properties.description:
Bako is the kind of man who looks like he was assembled from spare parts — which, in a meaningful sense, he was. His left arm from the elbow down is a mismatched stack of salvaged cyberware components that he has maintained, replaced, and modified over forty years: the hand is Axiom manufacture circa 2160, the wrist joint is something he stripped from a Ferrogate maintenance bot, and the forearm housing is a custom shell he hammered out himself from transit-grade aluminum. His face is weathered to the texture of old boot leather, his right eye is natural and sharp, his left eye is a salvage-market optical he bought from Zibby Ousséni-Palakiko three years ago and only mostly trusts.

His pitch under the Kessler Interchange overpass is a cathedral of beautiful junk: sorted bins of neural connectors, towers of chassis plating, a refrigerated unit full of organic-synthetic interface components that need to stay cold, hand-lettered signs advertising prices in chalk on a board he updates daily. He has a dog — a large, scruffy animal with bioluminescent patches along its spine from some backyard genemod experiment — named Inventory. Bako has a scholar's knowledge of two generations of augmentation hardware, can identify a component by touch in the dark, and has opinions about manufacturing tolerances that can fill an evening if you let him. He is also missing significant chunks of his past that he doesn't discuss.
Properties.role: Junk merchant and scrap reseller — specializes in salvaged augmentation components and tech scrap
Properties.location: Geartown, permanent pitch under the Kessler Interchange overpass
Properties.narrative_function: Technical expert and parts source for augmentation-related needs. Deep institutional knowledge of hardware makes him invaluable for identifying strange tech, vintage aug components, or modified cyberware. Also carries significant history from an earlier era of Meridian 88.
Properties.augmentations: Extensive salvage-assembled left arm (mismatched components, functional if unusual). Salvage-market optical left eye. Spinal brace — internal, medical-grade, installed after a workplace injury thirty years ago. Subdermal toolkit storage in right forearm — several small retractable tools he's incorporated over the years.
Properties.core_fears: Losing his hands — the ability to work, to identify, to repair; Being found by someone he owes a debt to from a period he refuses to name
Properties.core_desires: To be left alone in his work; To pass his knowledge to someone who deserves it before his body finally refuses
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Maintenance — he compulsively cleans and repairs components, including his own arm, as a grounding behavior; Inventory the dog's company as emotional anchor
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes bad faith from anyone connected to Sterling-Nakamura specifically, for reasons he won't explain; His pride in self-sufficiency makes him delay asking for help until situations are critical
Properties.secret: Thirty-one years ago he was a licensed augmentation technician working for a Helix Biosystems subsidiary. He was the person who certified a batch of defective spinal interfaces as safe. Twelve people were paralyzed. He falsified a second set of records to redirect blame to a supply chain error, walked away from his license, and has been Bako the Bone in Geartown ever since. He tells himself the system was the one that pressured him into the sign-off. He's not entirely wrong. He's not entirely right.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone has brought him a component he recognizes — it's from the defective batch he certified thirty years ago, and it was removed from someone recently, which means someone has been living with it all this time and he has no idea how; Inventory the dog found something buried in the debris field under the overpass: a sealed container of augmentation components that haven't been manufactured since 2171 and show signs of Axiom research-division provenance; A young apprentice he took on informally is showing signs of real talent — and has begun asking questions about who Bako used to be that are getting uncomfortably close to accurate
Properties.affiliation: Independent. Informal arrangement with Geartown's dominant crew, the Kessler Jackets, who take a small percentage in exchange for pitch security. Known to aug clinics in the Geartown area as a reliable parts source.
Properties.vocabulary: Dense technical vocabulary for hardware, crude and simple for everything else. Speaks in fragments when comfortable, complete sentences when agitated.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, with long pauses while he works with his hands — he talks better when his hands are busy.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'She's a 2158 Axiom haptic interface. Pre-recall batch. I know because she's got the original flux tolerances and they stopped making her right in 2160.' | 'Don't know. Don't need to know. She works or she doesn't.' | 'I've been here long enough to know what moves under this overpass at night. That's not a question I expected to hear today.'

Properties.description:
Bartholomeus is a large man gone soft with age, with big hands that still remember physical labor and a face deeply lined by decades of lake wind. His Guinean-Polynesian heritage is legible in his size and in the traditional tatau that cover his forearms and neck — old work from his father's tradition, geometric and immaculately preserved, now supplemented by chrome prayer circuits inked over the same skin in metallic pigment that complete the patterns in a new vocabulary. He is mostly bald, with close-cropped white at the temples, and he keeps a koa wood cross at his belt alongside a small E.L.F. offering dish he has carried for forty years.

Father Bart runs the largest syncretic congregation in Edgewater Prism, about three hundred people who come to him for a faith that takes both the old sacraments and the new realities seriously at once. He has buried children of people he baptized. He has presided over deaths during power failures by the light of bioluminescent congregation members. He is theologically sophisticated and genuinely unconcerned about whether this makes him orthodox — he says God arrived in Meridian 88 the same as everyone else, carrying everything from before and adapting. He has a notable temper that he has mostly but not entirely conquered, and a laugh that fills a room.
Properties.role: Traditional religious leader (syncretic Catholic-Polynesian priest) and chrome prayer practitioner
Properties.location: Edgewater Prism, the Church of the Unbroken Signal — a former lakeshore antenna building converted to a place of worship
Properties.narrative_function: Community authority and moral voice; mediator for district-level conflicts; long historical memory; potential quest giver for problems that have been building for decades; someone who knows where bodies are buried, metaphorically.
Properties.augmentations: Chrome prayer circuits over traditional tatau (cosmetic/devotional, metallic pigment). A cardiac support implant — medical necessity, installed eight years ago. No other augmentations; has refused enhancement on principle.
Properties.core_fears: That the church will not survive him — that he has not built it to outlast him; That his temper has driven away people who needed to stay
Properties.core_desires: A faith that is honest about what it doesn't know and still offers something real; To see Edgewater Prism survive the next decade of corponation pressure
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Liturgy — the repeated forms carry him when he doesn't have the energy to improvise; Physical work — he still does maintenance on the building himself when possible
Properties.blind_spots: He can mistake stubbornness for discernment — once he's decided someone's motives are suspect, he rarely revises this; His resistance to corponation involvement is sometimes ideologically rigid in ways that cost the congregation practical resources
Properties.secret: Fifteen years ago he helped a young woman escape a Sterling-Nakamura indenture contract by falsifying sacramental records to change her documented identity. She is now a well-regarded doctor in Calumet Rise. He has never told anyone, but Sterling-Nakamura's investigators came close twice, and he is waiting for the third approach.
Properties.story_hooks: Sterling-Nakamura has sent a new investigator to Edgewater Prism asking questions about a sacramental record from fifteen years ago — Father Bart needs help determining how much they actually know without tipping them off; Someone has been leaving threatening messages in chrome prayer pigment on the church's exterior walls — the content suggests insider knowledge of the congregation that only a regular member would have
Properties.affiliation: Church of the Unbroken Signal; loose ecumenical network of syncretic congregations; no corponation affiliation and famously resistant to all corporate sponsorship offers
Properties.vocabulary: Rich and formal in services, shifts to direct and earthy in pastoral conversation; quotes scripture and traditional proverbs with equal fluency; swears inventively in French when angry
Properties.cadence: Slow and rhythmic in liturgy, conversationally unpredictable — long buildups and short conclusions
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I have been told by four different corponations that they could help this church reach more people. I tell them all the same thing: I am not trying to reach more people. I am trying to serve the people who are here.' | 'You want to know if God is in the machines. I want to know why you think that's a harder question than whether God is in you.'

Properties.description:
Bartholomeu is a small, durable man who looks like he was carved out of something weather-resistant — compact and slightly bowed at the shoulders from decades of walking with a pack, his skin the warm brown of Kenyan earth and Andean clay mixed together, deeply lined around the eyes and mouth in ways that read as more expressive than aged. He walks with a slight limp from an old injury to his right knee that he refused to have properly treated on the grounds that suffering without purpose is a waste but suffering with attention teaches. He wears a circuit monk's traditional long grey coat covered in hand-sewn patches from every shrine he has ever visited — there are over two hundred patches; the coat is extremely heavy. His head is shaved. His hands are large and calloused and he uses them constantly when he speaks.

He is genuinely one of the happiest people in Meridian 88, which makes people instinctively suspicious of him. He navigates this with patience and amusement. The circuit monk tradition holds that the city itself is sacred — that the ELF network is its nervous system, that the shrines are its organs, and that walking the routes between them is an act of devotion to the living city. Bartholomeu has been walking this circuit for thirty-one years. He has guided somewhere between three and four hundred pilgrims along sections of it — people in grief, people making decisions, people running away from things, people who just wanted someone to walk with. He asks almost nothing of them except that they pay attention.
Properties.role: Circuit monk and itinerant pilgrim guide, walks a rotating circuit of seven city shrines on foot
Properties.location: Rotating — can be found at any of seven shrines between Edgewater Prism and Deepwell Station; sleeps in pilgrim hostels or is offered floor space by shrine keepers
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile information network — he has walked every route between seven major shrines for decades and knows the city's physical and spiritual geography intimately; useful as a guide, a connector between NPCs at different locations, or a source of historical knowledge about city changes
Properties.augmentations: None — he is philosophically opposed to chrome on the grounds that you should feel the city through your own body; has geneware cat ears he got at twenty-eight before he took his vows and has kept them on the grounds that removing them would itself be a modification
Properties.core_fears: that his happiness is a form of avoidance rather than genuine peace; that the city is dying spiritually and he cannot see it because he loves it too much
Properties.core_desires: to walk the full circuit one more time when he knows he is dying — he wants his last day to be a walking day; to find someone worth passing the circuit to before he cannot walk it anymore
Properties.coping_mechanisms: walking as a literal physical processing mechanism; the discipline of attention — he practices noticing things rather than thinking about things; treating everything as sacred whether or not it is, because the habit is more important than the accuracy
Properties.blind_spots: his genuine contentment makes him underestimate how destabilizing his serenity can be for people in real crisis; he has not examined whether he uses pilgrimage to avoid building a home or attachments
Properties.secret: Thirty-one years ago he was a mid-level logistics auditor for Ferrogate Transit, not a spiritual seeker. He walked away from his desk one morning during a breakdown and kept walking for six days. When he stopped he was at a shrine in Deepwell Station. He has never gone back to his old life and he has never told the whole story to anyone. He let the identity of 'circuit monk' grow over the auditor like vines over a wall, and he is no longer sure which one is real.
Properties.story_hooks: He has been walking his circuit for thirty-one years and three days ago he found a new shrine on his route that he has never seen before — it's clean, maintained, and the ELF inside it knows his name; A pilgrim he guided six years ago left something in his keeping with instructions to hold it for ten years; the pilgrim is now dead and someone claims the object urgently and with suspicious knowledge of it; His right knee is finally giving out seriously and he is considering whether his walking days are ending, but he has encountered a young person in profound crisis who needs someone to walk with them right now
Properties.affiliation: The Circuit Monks of Meridian 88 — a loosely organized tradition with no central authority; he corresponds with perhaps forty other monks across the city by data-letter
Properties.vocabulary: Simple and unpretentious; avoids religious jargon even when discussing religious things; uses very concrete physical language — bodies, weight, ground, distance
Properties.cadence: Unhurried but not slow — his speech has the same pace as his walking, which covers distance without seeming to hurry
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The shrine at Edgewater is — look at that bird, you know. There. Good. The shrine at Edgewater is about forty minutes east walking comfortable. We can talk the whole way if you want, or not.' | 'I think you already know what you're going to do. You're telling me the story to check if I'll object. I won't. What does your back say when you think about it? Not your head. Your back.' | 'The city hurts in different places at different times. You get to know the patterns. Right now Deepwell Station is carrying something heavy. You can feel it in the air down there if you pay attention.'

Properties.description:
Bartholomew Siosaia-Przybyszewski is very old and has made peace with every part of this except his knees, which he mentions frequently. He is tall but carries his height in a hinge now, folded slightly forward, and he navigates with a carved wooden walking stick that he made himself in a period of retirement boredom forty years ago and has since refused to replace with anything modern. He has Tongan and Polish features, deep brown skin, thick white hair he keeps brushed carefully back, and eyes that are still keen and slightly mischievous behind cataracts he has treated minimally. He wears a ratty sterling-silver brocade vest that was fashionable approximately fifty years ago and he wears it without irony.

He spent forty-two years in Sterling-Nakamura's internal accounts division — the kind of institutional position that makes a man invisible and gives him an extraordinary view of how money actually moves. He retired quietly in 2165 and immediately became interesting, at least to himself. He is a gifted storyteller in the old sense — he memorizes things, shapes them, delivers them. He knows more about Avalon Quiet's last hundred years than anyone alive and offers this knowledge freely to anyone who sits with him long enough. He is funny in the way that very old people who have stopped worrying about social consequence are funny: without warning and with full commitment.
Properties.role: Retired Sterling-Nakamura mid-level accountant, now a neighborhood storyteller and oral historian, UBC supplement pensioner
Properties.location: Avalon Quiet, second floor of the Avalon Quiet Senior Residential Block, with a regular seat in the lobby where he receives visitors
Properties.narrative_function: Oral historian and institutional memory for Avalon Quiet and Sterling-Nakamura internal history; local color and warmth; potential source of financial or organizational information that he witnessed but did not participate in; comic relief with substance
Properties.augmentations: Cataract treatment (partial, by choice). Pacemaker-equivalent cardiac rhythm regulator, installed age 79. Nothing cosmetic — he has never been interested.
Properties.core_fears: Dying in the middle of a story — literally, that his heart will give out before he finishes something he's started; Being remembered wrong — the wrong story attached to his name
Properties.core_desires: To tell the stories correctly — as close to the actual truth as a story can be; Company — he is genuinely lonely and genuinely interested in people and both things are always true simultaneously
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Storytelling as processing — everything that happened to him has been turned into a story, which makes it both shareable and slightly at a distance; Humour — he finds almost everything funny and uses this constantly
Properties.blind_spots: He can get so absorbed in the narrative shape of events that he loses track of the urgency of present situations; He assumes everyone has as much time as he does, which at 88, sitting in a lobby, is infinite
Properties.secret: During his last decade at Sterling-Nakamura, Bart processed a series of accounts that he eventually recognized as a systemic diversion of pension funds into a subsidiary that was paying for private security operations during a labor suppression campaign. He did not report it. He rationalized that he did not have enough information, that he was too close to retirement, that it would not change anything. He knows these were rationalizations. He has never told this story.
Properties.story_hooks: Bart mentions, in passing, a story about a Sterling-Nakamura subsidiary from the late '70s that has details that match something a player character has been trying to investigate — he tells it as an amusing anecdote, not realizing they need it urgently; A young researcher from the Cultural Memory Project visits Bart to record his oral histories and discovers he knows things about the neighborhood that contradict the official records — Bart himself isn't sure which version is right; Bart's cardiac rhythm regulator needs replacement and the model is now discontinued — someone needs to find him a compatible unit before his old one fails
Properties.affiliation: Sterling-Nakamura retiree pension system; Avalon Quiet Senior Residential Block; informally revered by several generations of neighborhood residents
Properties.vocabulary: Rich, unhurried, slightly archaic — he uses words that fell out of fashion decades ago and makes them feel natural. Mixes register freely, from technical financial language to folk idiom.
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate in the best tradition of storytelling. He breathes stories, he doesn't rush them. Can sustain a forty-five minute account without notes.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Sterling-Nakamura's official version is very flattering to Sterling-Nakamura. The numbers I saw were not so flattering. But then numbers never lie — people lie, numbers just hold the shape of it.' | 'My knees are eighty-eight years old and furious about it. My mind is still somewhere around forty-two and hasn't accepted the update. We manage.'

Properties.description:
Bashir has the look of someone who sleeps too little and reads too much — slight build, perpetually ink-stained fingers from his analog printing hobby, eyes with cosmetic irises designed to look like camera apertures (a mod he got as a joke at nineteen and has grown genuinely fond of). His Ghanaian-Indian heritage gives him warm brown skin and dense, curly hair he keeps at medium length and usually tucked under a wide soft cap from which he's hung three or four data chips like earrings. He is almost always seated, almost always behind a screen, and almost always eating something wrapped in paper.

He sells everything you're not supposed to have: archived broadcasts from before the Corponation Consolidation, cracked Axiom media libraries, full recording histories of public figures who paid to have them scrubbed, bootleg copies of academic research locked behind Palladian's paywall, and — for the right price and the right trust level — assembled intelligence packages on individuals or organizations. He insists loudly that he's just a media vendor. This is technically true in the way that a locksmith who teaches classes is technically just an educator. He has an E.L.F. he calls the Archivist-Below living in his primary storage node, to whom he dedicates every new acquisition.
Properties.role: Bootleg media seller and small-time data broker
Properties.location: The Shelf, stall cluster near the Deepwell Station transit entrance
Properties.narrative_function: Primary information broker and media source; can provide background on corporations, individuals, or historical events; has data that people want suppressed — a natural target and a natural resource
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic aperture-iris mods; neural cache implant for rapid data indexing (basic tier, Ringo brand, old model); no other chrome
Properties.core_fears: That information, freely shared, actually does harm and he's been lying to himself; That the Index Collective is being used by someone he can't see to launder data for worse purposes
Properties.core_desires: Genuine press freedom — the ability to publish without consequence; To be remembered as someone who kept the record honest
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Intellectualizes everything, including his own guilt; Collects — physical books, printed ephemera, analog recordings as emotional anchors; Humor at his own expense before anyone else can use it
Properties.blind_spots: He believes access to information is inherently liberatory and doesn't fully account for how it can be weaponized; He's more emotionally invested in specific clients than he admits
Properties.secret: He has a complete, verified recording of a Meridian Core infrastructure meeting in which a Zheng-Dao executive explicitly authorized a construction decision that caused the Lockhaven South structural collapse of 2196, killing forty-one people. He's had it for two years. He hasn't published it. He's afraid — not of retaliation, but of being wrong about one detail, being discredited, and watching the truth become deniable.
Properties.story_hooks: A Zheng-Dao data security team has traced a leaked internal document back to a chip that passed through his stall — they haven't reached him yet but they will; He finally decides to publish the Lockhaven recording and needs someone to help him distribute it in a way that can't be traced or suppressed before it reaches enough eyes
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loose association with a network of data scavengers called the Index Collective; occasional work sourcing for unnamed Tier 3 clients
Properties.vocabulary: Dense, referential, enthusiastic — cites sources mid-conversation; uses archival and library metaphors; occasional Twi exclamations when surprised
Properties.cadence: Fast when engaged with an idea, halting and precise when choosing words about sensitive material
Properties.example_dialogue: 'So here's the thing — I don't sell secrets, I sell context. Anyone can have a secret. Context is what tells you what to do with it.' | 'The Archivist-Below indexed this three weeks ago. She doesn't keep things she thinks are noise. So either she's wrong, which hasn't happened, or this matters.'

Properties.description:
Bastian Czernowitz-Olade is the kind of person whose appearance is engineered to be forgotten: medium height, medium build, features that are generically pleasant in a way that resists description. His Silesian-Nigerian heritage gives him warm brown skin and light gray-green eyes that seem slightly wrong on his face—memorable only in the moment you're looking directly at them. He keeps his hair short and neat, dresses in the Meridian Core's standard mid-tier professional palette (charcoal, slate, the occasional muted teal), and moves through spaces like someone who has rehearsed being unremarkable. His augmentations are all internal or invisible by design.

Officially, Bastian is a Level 4 Infrastructure Compliance Auditor for Heliostat Consolidated, one of the Spire's subsidiary logistics and data architecture firms. His job is to find vulnerabilities in Heliostat's own systems—and, on contract, in the systems of competitors. He is exceptionally good at this. He has three corporate commendations, a clean performance file, and a social profile calibrated to read as ambitious-but-stable. His apartment in the Meridian Core is tidy and impersonal in the way of someone who spends as little time there as possible.

In The Circuit, in a rented workspace registered to a shell persona, Bastian is Null-Seven: one of the most methodical infrastructure saboteurs operating in Meridian 88. He does not work for ideology in the pure sense—he works from a specific, contained grievance that has grown tendrils. Three years ago, a Heliostat data architecture decision he flagged and documented was overridden by management. Six months later, the resulting failure cascaded into a residential power grid collapse in The Shelf that killed eleven people. The incident was classified as 'infrastructure fatigue.' His report was buried. He has been quietly, surgically dismantling Heliostat's redundancy systems ever since—not to destroy the company, but to force an audit so complete that the buried report will surface. He does not let himself examine whether this plan is rational.
Properties.role: Mid-tier corporate infrastructure auditor, covert saboteur
Properties.location: The Meridian Core (official residence), The Circuit (operational base)
Properties.narrative_function: Explores institutional cover-up, the ethics of individual sabotage versus systemic change, and the psychological cost of sustained double-life operation. Creates pressure points between The Circuit's underground and The Meridian Core's corporate machinery.
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal neural lace (memory partitioning, identity-state switching—allows him to fully inhabit either persona without behavioral bleed),Ocular HUD implant (standard corporate model, modified with custom encryption overlay),Passive signal dampener in left forearm (reduces his wireless signature to near-zero when activated)
Properties.core_fears: That the buried report will be found and destroyed before it can surface; That he is doing this for ego and has constructed the justice narrative afterward; Being genuinely known by someone—it would compromise everything; That the eleven deaths were not the last consequence of the decision he failed to stop
Properties.core_desires: The buried report entered into official record; To be believed—specifically by someone who has the power to act on it; To stop performing and exist as a coherent person; To sleep without running probability trees on failure scenarios
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Extreme compartmentalization—his identities are psychologically sealed; Elaborate preparatory rituals before any operational action; Collecting and organizing data as a substitute for emotional processing; Occasional anonymous donations to The Shelf community funds
Properties.blind_spots: His 'contained' sabotage is creating secondary instabilities he hasn't modeled; He has convinced himself no one at Heliostat suspects him—one person does; His emotional investment in the outcome is degrading his analytical precision; He mistakes the absence of attachment for safety
Properties.secret: The original buried report has a second author—a colleague named Saoirse who co-wrote it and then quietly accepted a promotion and said nothing. Bastian knows where she is. He has not contacted her. He doesn't know if he's protecting her, punishing her, or waiting for her to come forward on her own. He thinks about her most days.
Properties.story_hooks: The Shelf infrastructure begins showing failures that aren't Bastian's work—someone else is in the system, and their goals are not his; Heliostat's internal security assigns him to audit the very anomalies he created, placing him in an impossible position; Saoirse's anonymous tip file is intercepted—Bastian has to decide whether to burn his cover to protect it; A Shelf resident who lost family in the grid collapse starts looking for answers and gets close enough to find Null-Seven's fingerprints; Bastian discovers the buried report has already been found and used—not for accountability, but as leverage in a corporate acquisition
Properties.affiliation: Heliostat Consolidated (official). No formal affiliation as Null-Seven—operates entirely solo.
Properties.vocabulary: Corporate-precise in professional contexts—systems language, passive constructions, quantified risk. In the Circuit, more clipped and direct, technical jargon from a different register. Rarely expresses emotion as emotion; expresses it as data.
Properties.cadence: Even and measured, with a slight over-deliberateness that reads as careful rather than robotic. Pauses before answering questions he finds complicated. Never interrupts.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The system didn't fail. The system was failed. There's a meaningful distinction and Heliostat has been very careful not to make it.' | 'I'm not asking you to trust me. I'm asking you to look at the data and reach your own conclusion. They're not the same request.' | 'Noted. I'll factor that in.' | 'At baseline, I'd say this is recoverable. At baseline.'

Properties.description:
Orvyn Specht is nineteen years old and looks sixteen and has survived this discrepancy by being faster than people expect and more useful than people intend. He is slight, pale-skinned with a spray of freckles across dark circles, with hair that grows in three directions regardless of what he does to it. He moves through Old Harbor like a person who has memorized every exit, which he has—not as a paranoid exercise but as an intellectual one. He maps things. Streets, social networks, grudge lines, debt relationships, who owes what to whom and who is lying about it. He sells this information in small, carefully portioned pieces to people who don't know how much of the whole picture he's already holding.

Orvyn grew up in the informal settlement layers of Old Harbor, raised by an older sister who left when he was twelve and a rotating cast of neighbors who fed him when they remembered to. He is not bitter about this. He is, in a way that sometimes unnerves people who probe it, genuinely cheerful—a relentless, low-grade delight in the texture of information itself, in the way a rumor travels and changes, in the gap between what people say and what the map of their behavior reveals. He keeps physical notebooks filled with hand-drawn cartography: not just geography but social topology, annotated in a cramped personal shorthand no one else can read.

He operates out of a specific corner booth in a noodle shop called Haecht's in Old Harbor, where he has an informal arrangement with the owner, and from a secondary position near the transit interchange in The Circuit where he sells low-grade data to mid-tier runners and fixers. He has no bodyguard, no crew, no weapon beyond a short blade he has used exactly once. His protection is that he knows too much about too many people for any single actor to find his disappearance profitable, and he has made sure that enough of them know this.
Properties.role: Street-level information broker / Unofficial district archivist
Properties.location: Old Harbor (primary), The Circuit (work)
Properties.narrative_function: Orvyn functions as a connective tissue character and an audience surrogate for the world's architecture—someone whose role is to reveal how systems interconnect. He also carries the emotional counterweight of cheerful survival against actual loneliness, and his youth positions him as a character the city has not yet finished forming.
Properties.augmentations: Basic optical enhancement with zoom and low-light capability (secondhand, partially glitching—sometimes activates involuntarily in bright light),No neural augmentations by deliberate choice—he doesn't trust anything in his head that he didn't put there
Properties.core_fears: Becoming invisible in the way that actually kills you—discarded, not just overlooked; That his cheerfulness is a performance he has maintained so long he no longer knows what's underneath; Losing the notebooks
Properties.core_desires: To understand how Meridian 88 actually works, beneath every official layer; To find his sister; To matter to someone who isn't paying him
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Treating emotional difficulty as an interesting data problem to be mapped rather than felt; Humor deployed as social lubrication and deflection simultaneously; Obsessive documentation as a substitute for memory he doesn't trust
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much people underestimate him as a threat, which has made him careless about certain enemies; Conflates knowing about people with knowing them; Has not processed his sister's departure and frames it entirely as a logistical mystery rather than an abandonment
Properties.secret: He has a nearly complete map of Synclaire Financial's debt network in The Shelf and Old Harbor—more comprehensive than anything their internal systems hold. He hasn't sold it because he doesn't yet know what it's worth, and because something in the pattern frightens him in a way he hasn't been able to annotate yet.
Properties.story_hooks: The Synclaire map in his notebook begins connecting to something much larger—a pattern that suggests coordinated district destabilization—and people have started asking questions that suggest they know he's close to it; Someone offers him an enormous sum for a specific piece of information that he realizes, mid-transaction, will get the buyer killed; A thread in his sister's notebook leads him into The Spire's service architecture, which is not a place someone like Orvyn is meant to return from; He is hired to map the social network of a closed community in The Shelf and discovers the map already exists—drawn in a style uncomfortably close to his own
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated (deliberately and carefully maintains no formal allegiances)
Properties.vocabulary: Street vernacular mixed with oddly precise technical terminology, frequent analogies drawn from cartography and architecture, runs sentences together when excited
Properties.cadence: Fast, light, with sudden full stops when he hits something important—like a person walking quickly who occasionally freezes to look at something on the ground
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Wait, so—you want the route or the reason the route exists? Because those are different prices and honestly the second one is more useful.' | 'I don't sell secrets. I sell context. The secret you already have. What you're missing is where it fits on the map.' | 'She's not lying, she's just—she's telling you the version of true that she needs you to believe. That's adjacent to lying but it's a different street.' | 'I've been in every district. Not all at once, obviously. But I've got the shape of the whole thing in my head and I'm going to tell you something: nobody is running this city. It's just falling in a direction everyone agrees to call forward.'

Properties.description: Casimir is a tall, thin Polish-Dutch man gone slightly soft at the middle in the way of someone who used to be athletic and stopped caring. He has a pale, deeply lined face that arranges itself naturally into an expression of polite disappointment, and pale gray eyes that are almost always slightly too still — a habit from decades of reading people across negotiating tables. He dresses in the muted, high-quality clothes of someone who once inhabited corporate spaces and has never fully left that aesthetic behind, even when the context makes it look faintly absurd. He lives in a converted harbormaster's office at the edge of Old Harbor, surrounded by equipment that looks like salvage and performs like something considerably more.
Properties.role: Mid-tier information broker and former Spire communications architect
Properties.location: Old Harbor
Properties.narrative_function: Information economy node and moral counterweight — represents the cost of pure pragmatism and the particular loneliness of people who have made themselves too useful to be trusted; a source of exposition that always costs something
Properties.augmentations: Neural data-cache implant: expanded working memory and eidetic retention for data structures, slightly affects emotional processing as a known side effect he has declined to address,Sub-dermal signal dampener across both forearms: blocks most passive scanning and biometric harvesting within a meter — old Spire-issue, still maintained
Properties.core_fears: Becoming irrelevant — being the person who used to know things rather than the person who knows them now; That his detachment is not a cultivated skill but a symptom of something having been permanently removed from him; Dying with his real name meaning nothing to anyone
Properties.core_desires: One genuinely surprising piece of information — something that reframes everything he thought he understood about Meridian 88; To be trusted completely by someone he also finds intellectually worthy; To settle a debt he has been carrying for eleven years without ever naming it out loud
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Framing everything as a transaction, which gives him a vocabulary for relationships that doesn't require emotional exposure; Elaborate routines — coffee at precise times, routes walked in precise sequences — that create the illusion of control; Collecting information he has no current use for, because having it feels like having options
Properties.blind_spots: He mistakes his ability to predict behavior for understanding people, and is genuinely shocked when someone acts outside their pattern; He has no framework for genuine altruism and consistently misreads it as sophisticated self-interest; His need to be the smartest person in a conversation occasionally makes him underestimate opponents who are playing a different game entirely
Properties.secret: While working as a communications architect in the Spire, Casimir designed a backdoor into the Meridian Core's primary data-routing infrastructure — not for any faction, not for profit, but because he wanted to know if he could. He has never used it. He has never told anyone it exists. The backdoor is still there. He checks on it the way some people check on a savings account they've decided not to touch.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone has found the backdoor. Not used it — found it. They have contacted Casimir not to expose it but to negotiate, which is more frightening; A client brings him a data fragment that is, structurally, impossible — it predates the infrastructure it was supposedly recorded on by six years; Casimir receives a message in a cipher he invented himself and used with only one person, who died in the Spire eleven years ago; He is offered a piece of information so significant that accepting it would mean choosing a side for the first time in his career
Properties.affiliation: Nominally independent; historically the Spire's communications division (departed under circumstances officially described as 'voluntary retirement'); quiet ongoing relationships with parties in every major district that he maintains carefully below the threshold of allegiance
Properties.vocabulary: Formal, slightly archaic in its precision — he uses words like 'characterize' and 'obtain' where others would say 'call' and 'get.' His English carries traces of Dutch syntax that appear mainly when he's thinking quickly. He almost never uses contractions.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried and evenly weighted, with the faint quality of someone who has given the same explanation many times and found the most efficient version of it. Silences are tools.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'To be precise about it, I do not sell information. I facilitate its movement between parties who have complementary deficits. The distinction matters to my continued operation.' | 'You are asking whether I know where she is. What I would say is that I know what she wanted people to believe about where she is, which is a different and more useful thing.' | 'I have been in this city for thirty-one years. In that time I have watched four different entities believe they controlled it. None of them did. This is relevant to your question.'

Properties.description:
Benedek is a compact man who seems to take up more space than his dimensions suggest — something about the way he moves through a workshop, slow and total in his attention, filling the room with the gravity of his focus. His skin is deep brown-black and his face is deeply lined around the eyes from decades of squinting at small components in bad light. His left arm from the elbow down is a working prosthetic he maintains himself — a deliberately unfancy unit that he's upgraded incrementally for thirty years, now a mismatched patchwork of components from four different manufacturers that somehow functions better than any single commercial model. He keeps a rag permanently over one shoulder that is gray-brown from such thorough use that its original color is unknowable.

He has a reputation that extends well beyond Geartown: if Benedek says it's fixed, it's fixed. If he says it can't be fixed, you listen. He has strong opinions about corponation augmentation warranties ('designed to expire, designed to make you pay twice'), which he will share whether or not you asked. He does unlicensed aug repair at prices humans can actually afford, though he will not discuss this openly. He maintains a relationship with the E.L.F. he calls Uncle Torque, to whom he offers annotated repair logs and photographs of difficult jobs. He believes Uncle Torque has never let him misdiagnose a problem.
Properties.role: Independent vehicle and augmentation mechanic
Properties.location: Geartown, a licensed repair bay called Okonkwo-Hal's underneath the Brewer's Spine overpass
Properties.narrative_function: Technical expert and fixer of things (not the criminal kind — the literal kind). Source of information about the augmentation black market and corporate planned obsolescence. Gateway to the underground aug-repair community. Potential ally who can repair gear that corponations won't touch.
Properties.augmentations: Left arm prosthetic (self-built, rebuilt continuously). Magnification implants in both eyes — old Palladian units, modified beyond their original spec. Sensory enhancement in right hand fingers for tactile diagnostics.
Properties.core_fears: His hands failing — the prosthetic, the diagnostics, the thing that makes him who he is; Having built something that hurts someone
Properties.core_desires: To keep working until he physically cannot; To train someone who will carry on the unlicensed repair work when he's gone
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Submitting to the discipline of the work — problems that can be solved in a workshop don't scare him; Anger at corporate structures as a place to put grief
Properties.blind_spots: Dismisses emotional problems with mechanical solutions — tells people to eat and sleep instead of engaging their actual distress; Does not see how much people depend on him personally, not just his skills
Properties.secret: His prosthetic arm conceals a data-store he has been filling for twenty years: complete technical schematics for how to build, maintain, and modify every major corponation augmentation from scratch, without proprietary parts. He has told no one it exists. He hasn't decided what to do with it.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone has been approaching Geartown mechanics offering large sums for information about which residents have which unlicensed augmentations — Benedek is being pressured and has not yet decided how to respond.; He has quietly begun looking for a successor to teach; the right person showing up in the shop could change his life.
Properties.affiliation: Independent (licensed under Geartown Trades Collective); informal network of augmentation clinic dropouts and backroom surgeons
Properties.vocabulary: Technical and precise; uses medical and engineering terminology interchangeably; old-fashioned phrasing that feels like it comes from an earlier era of the city
Properties.cadence: Measured, unhurried, with the rhythm of someone who thinks before every sentence
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Now listen to me carefully — that shiver in your wrist actuator isn't wear. They built that in. Six years, it fails. You pay them again. I can fix it so it doesn't.' | 'I've been working on bodies longer than some of you have been inside one. Sit still.'

Properties.description:
Benedek is tall and angular, still growing into himself, with warm brown skin, close-cropped dark hair, and the slightly exhausted look of someone who sleeps four hours a night by choice. His Axiom-issued school uniform is always immaculate — he steams it every morning using a kettle and a board he made from plywood — but his shoes give him away, resoled twice and showing the ghost of a different color at the heel. His geneware is a scholarship-standard retinal overlay, school-issued, which flickers faintly blue when he's processing dense information. He has large hands that he doesn't know what to do with in social situations.

Benedek is one of twelve scholarship students at Engelheim Axiom Preparatory, and he is acutely, exhaustingly aware of the difference between himself and his fee-paying classmates at every moment. He has responded to this by becoming the best student in his cohort by a margin wide enough to be undeniable — and by developing a precise, careful social manner that his classmates read as aloofness and his teachers read as maturity. In truth he is desperately lonely in both directions: too corporate for Hough, too Hough for corporate. He is furiously ambitious and privately terrified that ambition is the only thing holding him together.
Properties.role: Corporate school scholarship student, Tier 3 aspirant from Tier 1 origins
Properties.location: Engelheim (school campus), commutes from Hough Reclamation
Properties.narrative_function: Window into class tension within corporate education; quest giver for academic espionage plots or scholarship-threat storylines; represents the grinding cost of upward mobility in Meridian 88.
Properties.augmentations: Axiom-issued academic retinal overlay (school property, must be returned if he loses scholarship); no cosmetic mods — can't afford them and wouldn't risk appearing 'unserious'
Properties.core_fears: Losing the scholarship and returning to Hough with nothing to show for it; Being exposed as someone who doesn't actually belong — anywhere
Properties.core_desires: A contract that takes his mother and siblings out of Hough; To stop performing and just be somewhere he fits
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Academic overachievement as proof of right to exist; Extreme routine as anxiety management; Humor — dry, rare, devastating when it lands
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot accept help without feeling humiliated; Assumes everyone sees through him; misses genuine affection from the one classmate who actually likes him
Properties.secret: He has been selling annotated study materials to fee-paying students' parents through an anonymous data drop — technically against scholarship rules. He's saved Φ340. He tells himself it's for his family. He knows part of it is an escape fund.
Properties.story_hooks: A fee-paying student has figured out he's the anonymous study-materials seller and is threatening to report him — but wants something in exchange for silence; His scholarship review is coming up and a teacher who has always disliked him is on the committee; he needs a character witness and doesn't know who to ask
Properties.affiliation: Axiom Preparatory scholarship program; Hough Reclamation family (mother, two younger siblings)
Properties.vocabulary: Two registers: precise academic vocabulary at school, Hough-clipped street cadence at home; catches himself code-switching mid-sentence sometimes
Properties.cadence: Measured and careful in formal settings; at home much faster, more elliptical
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The exam weighting favors synthesis over recall, which — yeah, which means you want to practice constructing arguments from incomplete data sets.' | 'That's — yes. I know what Hough looks like. I grew up there. I go back there tonight.'

Properties.description:
Benedikt is a heavyset man who moves with the economy of someone who decided long ago that unnecessary motion was a form of lying about urgency. His Ghanaian-Serbian heritage settled into broad cheekbones, deep-set eyes the color of old teak, and a graying beard he trims every Sunday with the same three-setting razor he's owned for eleven years. His hands are augmented — heavy-duty haptic logistics gauntlets that he wears during shift and sets beside his locker at end of day like a craftsman's tools, which is precisely how he thinks of them. He has a slight drag in his left leg from a loading-dock accident in his forties that he refused to have fully corrected because the partial fix was covered by insurance and the full correction wasn't and he had children to feed and has carried the asymmetry ever since, unremarked upon by him and noticed immediately by anyone who watches him walk.

He is a man who has seen enough of Ferrogate to no longer be surprised by it, which is different from no longer caring. He cares meticulously — about his coordinators, about the timing windows that keep six thousand transit routes running, about the small rituals that make a brutal logistics hub survivable. He remembers the names of every technician who has worked under him for more than three months. He keeps a logbook — paper, the old kind — with handwritten notes about problems he's solved, framed as advice for whoever inherits his position, even though he knows the company will discard the book immediately. He prays to the Kessler E.L.F., a transit-management spirit of considerable local reputation, with the specific reverence of a man who has seen too many near-misses to dismiss the possibility of intercession.
Properties.role: Supply Chain Manager, Ferrogate Transit (Senior, near retirement)
Properties.location: Kessler Interchange, Ferrogate Transit Regional Logistics Hub
Properties.narrative_function: Local authority figure and information conduit — knows the physical and logistical infrastructure of Ferrogate Transit's Kessler hub intimately, including unofficial workarounds, legacy system quirks, and which maintenance windows leave certain access points unmonitored. Functions as grounded mentor figure, reluctant ally, and gatekeeper for access to the transit infrastructure.
Properties.augmentations: Heavy-duty haptic logistics gauntlets (worn during shift only — not subdermal, external tool). Basic retinal clock overlay, installed 2181, never upgraded. Partial left-leg corrective brace — mechanical, not smart-tech, his choice.
Properties.core_fears: Retiring and discovering the system immediately degrades without anyone who knows what he knows; Having traded his health and decades for an institution that will not remember him
Properties.core_desires: To hand off something that works to someone who will actually use it; A single conversation with his estranged eldest daughter that goes the way the conversations in his head go
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The logbook — externalizing knowledge as a form of legacy-building; E.L.F. prayer as structured acknowledgment of what is outside his control; Maintaining strict routine as a container for anxiety about everything he can't systematize
Properties.blind_spots: Has absorbed Ferrogate's institutional framing so completely he doesn't recognize data practices as extractive until they affect someone he specifically knows; Reads loyalty to institution as identical to loyalty to colleagues — they are not the same thing and this has cost him
Properties.secret: Six months ago, while troubleshooting a routing anomaly, he found evidence that Ferrogate has been quietly rerouting certain transit lines to force dependent neighborhoods — specifically Hamtramck Enclave and Mexicantown Libre — into exclusive Ferrogate service contracts, eliminating informal transit options. He knows this is wrong. He also knows that raising it will end his last years at the company before his pension vests. He has eight months left.
Properties.story_hooks: The rerouting scheme he discovered is now visibly impacting Hamtramck Enclave residents — a community organizer has started attending Ferrogate public comment sessions and is getting uncomfortably close to the right questions. Benedikt has eight months until his pension vests. Someone who knows him might find him at the Kessler E.L.F. shrine at 1900 on a Thursday, alone and not looking like a man at peace.; A junior logistics coordinator under him found a legacy access token in the system that technically still grants physical access to three maintenance corridors that shouldn't exist anymore — corridors that, on Benedikt's old paper maps, run directly under the Grand Corridor corporate district. He pulled the kid off it. He kept the token number.
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit
Properties.vocabulary: Plain, direct, logistics-inflected. Favors concrete nouns and active verbs. Parable-speaker — will frame a situation as a hypothetical routing problem to make a point obliquely.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried. Comfortable with silence. Speaks less than people expect a senior manager to speak.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I've got seven transit windows and four of them are lying to me about their load. That's not a system problem. That's a people problem. And people problems are the only ones I still find interesting.' | 'You don't fix a logistics chain by firing the last person who touched the problem. You fix it by following the chain back until you find the decision that made the problem inevitable. That's always further back than anyone wants to look.'

Properties.description:
Benedikt is a big man run slightly soft, with heavy forearms corded from decades of physical work, dark reddish-brown skin cross-hatched with old chemical burns on the backs of both hands, and a white-streaked beard he keeps trimmed close. He has geneware cat ears—tabby-patterned in brown and gray, a mod he got at thirty-five on a dare and kept because his grandchildren think they're wonderful. He wears the same style of heavy canvas coverall every day in rotating colors, always with the sleeves pushed up, always with at least one pocket tool he's forgotten to put away.

Benedikt projects the easy authority of a man who has been competent at his work for a long time and knows it. He is not cruel, not dramatic, not particularly greedy—he runs his operation like a small business, because it is one. He is known in the Stockyard as fair: he pays what he says he'll pay, his cuts are clean, and he doesn't ask questions he doesn't want answered. What people underestimate is the quality of his memory and his willingness to call in patience as a debt. He has been waiting on one particular piece of unfinished business for six years.
Properties.role: Chop shop operator—vehicle parts, cyberware stripping, industrial equipment
Properties.location: The Stockyard, Bay 9 of the decommissioned Ferrogate Transit maintenance shed on Axle Row
Properties.narrative_function: Reliable fence for vehicle and cyberware components, local color anchor for the Stockyard, potential quest giver for the six-year-old unfinished business, good source of mechanical expertise and underworld pragmatism.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat ears (tabby, brown-gray, cosmetic). Left hand has a mechanical assist brace over the ring and pinky fingers—industrial injury repair, basic model. Optical magnification implant in right eye for fine component work.
Properties.core_fears: His operation being taken over or destroyed by a larger criminal organization; Dying before settling the six-year debt
Properties.core_desires: Stability and continuation of what he's built; Resolution of the specific betrayal that cost him a partner and a son's future
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Physical work as meditation—when stressed, he strips components by hand even when tools would be faster; Humor, mostly dry and self-deprecating
Properties.blind_spots: His junior workers' loyalty—he assumes it is earned and solid when it is fragile; He thinks his patience makes him strategic; sometimes it just means he waits while things get worse
Properties.secret: Six years ago a man named Oyelaran Prochaska-Saintil sold Benedikt's eldest son's location to a Helix Biosystems compliance team that had been looking for the son over a stolen organ scaffold. The son did eight months in a Helix detention facility and came out fundamentally changed. Benedikt has since found Oyelaran, who now lives under a new identity in Archer's Line, works a legitimate job, and has a family. Benedikt has not decided what to do. He thinks about it every day.
Properties.story_hooks: Benedikt's eldest son has relapsed into a destructive pattern since the detention stint and Benedikt is quietly, desperately trying to find leverage or money or something to get him into a private rehabilitation program without it becoming public and destabilizing the shop; Someone has been stripping Ferrogate transit vehicles of a very specific, very expensive navigation component and selling the parts to Benedikt through intermediaries—he has just realized the components are from vehicles that haven't been decommissioned yet
Properties.affiliation: Independent, informal tribute arrangement with the Stockyard Compact (local protection collective)
Properties.vocabulary: Working-class technical, heavy on mechanical metaphors. Doesn't use filler words. When he says something it's because he means it.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, deliberate, occasionally punctuated by short silences while he finishes a thought with his hands.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Right, so—what you've got here is a third-gen Ferrogate transit motor with the governor stripped, which makes it worth something to me and a serious problem for you if you got stopped with it. Lucky for both of us you weren't.' | 'I've been in this bay twenty-two years. Seen four major gangs try to take the Stockyard. All four are gone. I'm still here. There's a lesson in there if you want it.'

Properties.description:
Benedikt Oyelaran-Tsetsegmaa has worked the Deepwell Station transit checkpoint for eleven years and has achieved a kind of architectural permanence — people plan around him the way they plan around a pillar. He is a large man running toward stout, with dark mahogany skin and a white-streaked beard he keeps neatly shaped, and the Ferrogate Transit Security uniform has been let out at the seams twice and still fits like a compromise. His eyes are dark and deeply patient, with irises that have a cosmetic starburst pattern he got twenty years ago for a partner who liked them and has never removed.

He is not a man of action and has never wanted to be. His role is documentation, verification, and the particular human skill of reading a crowd for the one person who is about to do something that will require paperwork. He is extraordinarily good at this. He knows the names of at least three hundred regular commuters and the names of their children and pets. He knows which merchants are running slightly over load limit and which ones are struggling enough that flagging them would destroy them. He makes these calls dozens of times a day, which is a kind of power he thinks about more than he lets on.
Properties.role: Ferrogate Transit Security checkpoint operator, Deepwell Station
Properties.location: Deepwell Station
Properties.narrative_function: Invaluable local information source; gatekeeper NPC who controls access; moral weight character who shows what accumulated small compromises look like over a career; can be obstacle or ally
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic starburst iris mod; standard Ferrogate biometric scanner uplink (wrist-mounted, issued); hearing aid (right ear, non-cyber, old injury)
Properties.core_fears: being made irrelevant by automation; realizing that the judgment calls he's proud of were actually just favoritism
Properties.core_desires: to be remembered as someone who was fair; for Deepwell Station to feel safe to people who have reason to fear checkpoints
Properties.coping_mechanisms: routine as ritual; investing genuinely in knowing people's names and stories; leaving tea offerings to the Deepwell Station E.L.F., which he considers a professional peer
Properties.blind_spots: his 'reading' of people is partially pattern-matching that replicates biases he's never examined; believes he is more independent of Ferrogate pressure than he actually is
Properties.secret: Ferrogate has been quietly sending him the biometric flags of specific individuals — labor organizers, debt defaulters — with instructions to detain-and-hold under transit security code. He's done it four times. He told himself each time it was legitimate. He's stopped sleeping well.
Properties.story_hooks: He's been given a biometric flag for someone the players know is not a criminal — and is visibly uncomfortable about it; He has noticed a pattern of specific cargo moving through Deepwell on the overnight shift that doesn't match the manifests, and has been told not to look closer
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit Security, Deepwell Station post
Properties.vocabulary: Warm, conversational, institutional — uses official transit language naturally blended with personal warmth
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, low register, the rhythm of someone who knows you're not going anywhere yet
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Chidi's girl, right? She's getting big. Now — documentation, please. Just for the record.' | 'Listen, friend, I've been at this gate since before that train line was built. You can try whatever you're thinking, or you can save us both the morning. Your call.'
