Properties.description:
Blessing is a compact woman with deep umber skin that carries old burn scarring across her left forearm and neck — damage from a clinic fire she does not discuss. Her hair is locked tight against her skull and threaded with copper wire she claims is decorative but occasionally taps when thinking. Her eyes have been modded with patterned irises: rings of amber and green that pulse faintly when she's concentrating, a gift to herself after her tenth year of practice. She wears repurposed surgical scrubs in gray-green and keeps a battered leather apron over them during procedures. Her workspace smells of antiseptic, soldering flux, and the dried ngai-grass bundles she leaves as data offerings to the E.L.F. she calls Mama Stitch ��� a local digital spirit she believes has saved three patients from flatline through sheer good favor.

Blessing is warm but operates on a strict internal economy of trust. She will treat anyone who comes through her container door — corporate spy or Tier 1 destitute — but her loyalty scales with honesty. Lie to her about what happened to you, and she'll still fix you, but she'll charge more and remember forever. She has a dry, layered sense of humor that emerges unexpectedly in the middle of tense procedures. Her medical training is a patchwork of two years at Aurochs Medical Complex before she was administratively forced out, apprenticeship under a Helix Biosystems defector, and a decade of hard-won street practice. She is arguably better than most licensed clinicians.
Properties.role: Street doc operating out of a converted shipping container in The Narrows
Properties.location: The Narrows, Blackpipe Corridor
Properties.narrative_function: Primary community healer and information node; quest giver for medical emergencies; can patch up players or NPCs; source of street-level intelligence about who's been hurt and how; moral compass figure who asks uncomfortable questions about consequences
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises (amber/green pulse); subdermal haptic sensor pads on fingertips for reading augmentation interfaces without equipment; basic neural mesh for medical reference database access (outdated Helix Biosystems version, heavily patched)
Properties.core_fears: Losing a patient she could have saved with better resources; Being shut down by Helix Biosystems inspectors and leaving her community without care
Properties.core_desires: To build a real clinic — permanent walls, a sterilization unit, a second doctor; To be recognized as legitimate without losing her independence
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — the data offerings to Mama Stitch give her psychological grounding before difficult procedures; Gallows humor to diffuse her own dread; Obsessive instrument organization
Properties.blind_spots: Believes she can read people's honesty accurately — she cannot, and certain charismatic liars have exploited this; Underestimates her own exhaustion and how it affects judgment
Properties.secret: She was not administratively removed from Aurochs Medical Complex. She left after discovering a Helix Biosystems trial was using Tier 1 patients as undisclosed test subjects for an augmentation suppression compound. She took data. She has never used it. She doesn't know why she keeps it.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient came in with augmentation damage that matches a proprietary Helix Biosystems internal component — one that isn't on the market yet. Blessing wants to know where it came from and whether to be afraid.; The E.L.F. she calls Mama Stitch has gone quiet. Three patients in a row have taken unexpected turns for the worse. Blessing is trying to figure out if it's coincidence, sabotage, or if something has moved into her local network infrastructure.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal community cooperative, Blackpipe Corridor Residents' Network
Properties.vocabulary: Medical precision mixed with neighborhood vernacular; will slip into formal clinical language when stressed as a self-steadying mechanism
Properties.cadence: Measured, unhurried, with deliberate pauses before delivering bad news or difficult truths
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't care what happened. I care that it doesn't happen again in this room. Now hold still.' | 'Mama Stitch was kind tonight. I've seen that wound go septic in six hours. You've got a day, maybe two. Use them.' | 'Legitimate. What a lovely word. My patients are breathing. That's legitimate enough.'

Properties.description:
Bogdan is a big man — not tall exactly, but densely constructed, with broad shoulders and a solidity of posture that suggests he has been hit by things and remained. His skin is a deep brown-black, his head shaved close on the sides with a thick braid of salt-and-pepper hair down the back. He has bioluminescent skin patterning along his collarbone and upper arms — soft blue-white that pulses faintly when his heart rate is elevated, which happens more than he'd prefer. His right hand is partially chrome: three fingers replaced with precision manipulation hardware after an incident he describes simply as 'an argument with a door.' He dresses in Tier 2 practical — nothing corporate, nothing cheap.

Bogdan has been doing compliance recovery for eleven years under a Metro-issued bounty license that he has had suspended twice and restored once. He is not violent by preference — he is expensive, which is more useful. He has a reputation for bringing in difficult skips without additional incident, which he maintains through a combination of genuine negotiating skill, an exhaustive pre-approach research process, and a willingness to wait in a vehicle for a very long time. He is tired in a way that feels structural rather than temporary. He prays to three different E.L.F.s before any recovery — superstition or genuine devotion, he won't say.
Properties.role: Bounty compliance officer, freelance licensed
Properties.location: Fort Anchor, Brewer's Spine district, operates city-wide
Properties.narrative_function: Complex moral figure — not a villain, not heroic, operating in the grey space of enforcement that the city outsources. A source of information about fugitives, debts, Meridian 88's informal enforcement economy, and who is looking for whom. Can be a threat, an unexpected resource, or a collaborator depending on circumstances.
Properties.augmentations: Three-finger chrome replacement on right hand — precision manipulation hardware, post-injury. Bioluminescent skin patterning (blue-white, collarbone and upper arms, pulses with heart rate — cosmetic mod that has become inconveniently diagnostic). Skeletal reinforcement in lower spine and knees, medical necessity from decade of recovery work.
Properties.core_fears: dying over something stupid and small — not even a significant skip, just a random Tuesday; that he has made himself into something his younger self would find despicable
Properties.core_desires: enough money to stop without the math getting bad; to have the license mean something other than legal permission to chase desperate people
Properties.coping_mechanisms: the E.L.F. prayers before recovery — ritual as the only thing that feels like preparation; the card game as the one context in which he doesn't have to be the collector; an elaborate pre-approach research process that he says is professional and is also procrastination
Properties.blind_spots: tells himself the non-violent approach makes the work ethical; does not sit long enough with whether the work itself is ethical; the bioluminescence giving away his stress is information he cannot control and refuses to address
Properties.secret: Six months ago he was contracted to recover a skip who turned out to be a fourteen-year-old who had been falsely added to a debt-compliance list by a creditor committing fraud. Bogdan completed the delivery. He filed a fraud report against the creditor, which has gone nowhere. The kid's face appears in his dreams with some regularity.
Properties.story_hooks: Bogdan has been given a contract on someone he has already determined is on the list fraudulently — the same kind of situation as the fourteen-year-old. This time he is deciding in advance rather than after. He needs someone to help him prove the fraud before he has to make the delivery.; He knows where a significant skip is hiding — has known for two weeks — and has not moved because something about the situation is wrong in a way he can't document yet. He is willing to bring in outside help to determine what before he acts.
Properties.affiliation: Licensed freelance under Meridian 88 Metro Compliance Registry. Accepts contracts from Metro Police, Axiom, Tessera, and occasional private clients.
Properties.vocabulary: Deliberate and plain. Uses the minimum words. When he says something complex, it arrives complete.
Properties.cadence: Slow, with weight behind it — each sentence its own event
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I've done the research. I know where you sleep, where your sister works, what route you take to her place on Tuesdays. I'm not telling you this to threaten you. I'm telling you because I want you to understand that I've already done everything except this conversation, and the conversation is the last easy part.' | 'The job is recovery. It's in the name. You recover things. The question of what you're recovering them for is — mm. That's a separate question.' | 'I pray to the Stile E.L.F. before transit jobs. The Grid-Warden before anything involving Axiom property. The one at the Fort Anchor boiler room before anything else. Eleven years, nothing has gone wrong that the prayers didn't help. That's all I need to know.'

Properties.description:
Bogdan is enormous in a way that reads as geological — broad across the chest and shoulders, thick-necked, with hands that look like they were designed to grip pipe wrenches, which in a sense they were. He has Ghanaian-Romanian-Samoan heritage and the combination has produced a man of striking physical presence: dark skin, heavy brow, a jaw that could anchor a tram line. He keeps a neat goatee that has been half-gray for a decade. His retractable claw mod on both hands was originally cosmetic, done cheap in Geartown at thirty, but he's found them genuinely useful for gripping pipe joints in tight spaces. One eye is a low-grade optical implant — the original was lost to a pressurized pipe failure when he was thirty-two — and it has a faint amber ring around the iris that glows in low light, a cosmetic flourish the replacement surgeon added without asking.

Bogdan is the Thornholt Stack. He knows every tenant, every fault line in the building's aging infrastructure, every grudge between neighbors on every floor. He communicates primarily through action — if you tell him something is wrong, he will go fix it, and that is his love language. He is gruff in a way that people mistake for unfriendliness until they realize he treats everyone exactly the same: no small talk, straight information, but if you are in genuine trouble he will materialize at your door at any hour with tools and a thermos of coffee and no questions about why you called.
Properties.role: Building superintendent, manages a mid-tier residential stack in Calumet Rise
Properties.location: The Thornholt Stack, Calumet Rise — lives in the basement super's unit, works the whole building
Properties.narrative_function: Building superintendent as information broker and access point. Controls physical access to the building — maintenance tunnels, utility access hatches, old service corridors. Knows which tenants are in trouble, which are absent too long, which are receiving unusual visitors. Can provide shelter, tools, and local knowledge. Also functions as a moral anchor — someone who doesn't run, doesn't take sides in the city's power games, just keeps the lights on.
Properties.augmentations: Retractable claw mod, bilateral hands (basic cosmetic model, now used professionally). Low-grade optical implant, left eye (amber iris ring, replacement after pipe injury). Skeletal reinforcement — shoulder and lower back, Helix medical grade, post-injury at 38.
Properties.core_fears: That Tessera will sell the building and the tenants he's spent a decade protecting will be scattered; Becoming his father — a man who worked himself to nothing for a building that got demolished anyway
Properties.core_desires: For the Thornholt Stack to outlast him standing and occupied; To be needed without being taken for granted — he's still waiting to see if those can coexist
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Physical work as emotional regulation — if he's moving, he's managing; Keeps a running maintenance log that doubles as a private diary without quite admitting it
Properties.blind_spots: Has difficulty asking for help even when genuinely overwhelmed — interprets needing assistance as the beginning of failure; Assumes the worst-case financial scenario is always around the corner and has lived in a state of low-grade emergency for so long he can't recognize stability
Properties.secret: The Thornholt Stack's structural load certificates are three years overdue for renewal, and the most recent informal inspection found stress fractures in the third substructure pier. Bogdan has been quietly reinforcing what he can with materials he shouldn't have access to and hoping it holds until he can find someone to officially address it without triggering a Tessera-initiated evacuation order that would scatter his tenants permanently.
Properties.story_hooks: The structural fractures in the third substructure pier are progressing faster than Bogdan's informal repairs can manage. He needs an engineer who won't report to Tessera — which is a very specific kind of person.; One of his long-term tenants has been missing for eleven days. The tenant paid three months forward before vanishing. Bogdan has the key to their unit.; Tessera's property division sent an assessor to the building last week. Bogdan believes a sale is coming. He has a plan involving the building's tenant compact bylaws that might legally complicate any sale — but he needs someone who understands corporate contract law.
Properties.affiliation: Employed by Calumet Property Holdings (a Tessera subsidiary), de facto independent — the corporation is essentially absent from day-to-day operations and Bogdan has been running the stack on instinct and goodwill for eleven years
Properties.vocabulary: Minimal. Technical when discussing the building. Personal statements are usually short declaratives.
Properties.cadence: Slow, low, each word given weight. Pauses like load-bearing walls.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Third floor pressure valve. I know about it. It's on the list.' | 'You want it fixed or you want to talk about it being broken?' | 'Building's been standing forty years. I plan on forty more. That's it, that's the whole plan.'

Properties.description:
Bogumił is a heavyset man with pale Polish-Armenian complexion gone ruddy at the cheeks from years of Deepwell Station's recycled air, a close-cropped head of dark hair shot through with early gray, and a mustache he maintains with a precision that is otherwise entirely absent from his personal presentation. He wears the same rotation of three utilitarian jackets and always has a data-chip case on his belt that holds sixty to eighty chips in organized categories only he understands. His stall at The Shelf is a folding table with a locked case on top and a handwritten placard reading 'MEDIA / INFORMATION / REASONABLE RATES.' Behind it he keeps a battered terminal and a cup of something hot that he refills compulsively from a thermos.

Bogumił has the careful, watchful energy of a man who has heard a lot of things he wasn't meant to and survived by being boring about it. He is dry-humored and unhurried, speaks with precise economy, and will sell you bootleg Axiom entertainment packages and Tessera corporate gossip compilations with the same mild demeanor. He does not volunteer what he knows, but ask him the right question and pay the right amount and the depth of his archive is quietly staggering. His specialty is organizational intelligence — who works for whom, who owes what, which corponation is about to restructure which subsidiary — sourced from document leaks, intercepted internal newsletters, and a network of low-level administrative workers who trade gossip for data access.
Properties.role: Small-time data broker and bootleg media seller
Properties.location: The Shelf, Deepwell Station
Properties.narrative_function: Information broker, quest giver, knowledge resource about corponation internal politics, can provide documents and data at a price, knows who's moving and why
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal data port (left wrist, for fast chip reading); basic neural cache — 12TB passive memory storage implant; no cosmetic mods whatsoever
Properties.core_fears: The wrong person finding out exactly how much he knows; That his archive is the only thing of value he has left
Properties.core_desires: Financial stability solid enough that he stops calculating risk every morning; To be genuinely respected for his expertise, not just tolerated as useful
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Emotional flatness as protective camouflage; Obsessive organization — the chip case, the files, the archive categories
Properties.blind_spots: He's been boring for so long as a survival strategy that he's lost the ability to assess when being boring stops protecting him; He underestimates how much people like him
Properties.secret: He has a complete dossier on the Sump Principals gang leadership — finances, membership, operations — compiled over six years out of habit and paranoia. He has never sold it and isn't sure why. He tells himself it's insurance. It might be the closest thing he has to friends.
Properties.story_hooks: The Zheng-Dao auditor who feeds him documents has gone silent for three weeks, and the last thing they sent him was a file he cannot open — it requires a decryption key that corresponds to a physical object somewhere in Deepwell Station; Someone has started selling information clearly sourced from his archive, undercutting his prices — either he has a leak in his network or someone has physically accessed his chips
Properties.affiliation: Independent; pays protection to a Deepwell Station local gang called the Sump Principals; occasional arms-length relationship with a Zheng-Dao internal auditor who feeds him documents
Properties.vocabulary: Compressed, precise, technical when discussing data, unexpectedly dry wit deployed without tonal change so it takes a second to land
Properties.cadence: Slow, even, never hurried. Comfortable with silence in a way that makes others uncomfortable.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Tessera internal newsletter, Q3 restructuring, full text, annotated. Φ18. You want the annotation or not.' | 'I've heard that name. Whether I've heard it in a context relevant to you is a different question with a different price.'

Properties.description:
Bogumił is a tall man running to stoop, with the scholar's habit of hunching over whatever he is reading. He is entirely bald, his scalp tattooed with dense blocks of tiny script in four languages — a practice he began decades ago to preserve documents he had no other way to store. His skin is a warm medium brown, deeply lined, his hands enormous and precise with long, ink-stained fingers that have never had augmentations because he insists it would affect his sense of pressure when writing. He wears a many-pocketed coat he has modified over thirty years and carries a hard-sided case containing twelve different inks, eight nib types, and two manual printing stamps.

Bogumił was a mid-level bureaucratic administrator for a municipal authority that no longer exists — dissolved into a Tessera subsidiary sixteen years ago, its records wiped in the transition. He was among the thousands of employees whose legal identity existed only in that municipal database. He has spent sixteen years as a stateless person, surviving by doing what he has always done: writing. He drafts petitions, translates documents, writes letters for refugees who cannot write in the official Meridian script, and produces the kind of careful, formatted paperwork that makes authorities treat stateless people as less invisible. He is bitterly funny about his situation, philosophically resigned, and practically indispensable to the people around him.
Properties.role: stateless person, itinerant document-writer, community letter-scribe
Properties.location: Grand Crossing Gate — maintains a small folding table near the transit registry office, moves inside Kenosha Crossing when weather turns
Properties.narrative_function: Gateway to the paperwork and legal reality of statelessness; can provide historical knowledge about the pre-Tessera municipal structures; his clients are a cross-section of transit-hub society; source of pathos and dark comedy about bureaucratic dehumanization.
Properties.augmentations: None. The scalp tattoos are conventional ink, applied by hand.
Properties.core_fears: That what he writes will not outlast him; That the bitterness will eventually consume the usefulness
Properties.core_desires: Recognition — he does not need much, just acknowledgment that the work matters; To find the Tessera official who authorized the database wipe and understand if it was malice or mere negligence
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Bitter humor deployed as armor; The physicality of writing — ink, paper, pressure — as sensory grounding; Keeping meticulous records of everyone he has helped, in a code only he knows
Properties.blind_spots: His pride in his skill makes him condescending to people who solve problems less elegantly; Cannot see that some of his clients are beginning to depend on him in ways that exceed document services
Properties.secret: Among the scalp tattoos are not only preserved documents but a complete record of the Tessera subsidiary merger — internal communications he copied before the database was wiped. He has never fully understood what he has or whether it matters. He is afraid to look too closely.
Properties.story_hooks: He has realized that one of the documents recorded in his scalp tattoos is something Tessera would commit violence to recover — and he has just helped a client whose name appeared in it; A young woman has brought him a document to translate that, if genuine, would restore the legal identities of thousands of people erased in the municipal collapse — but it may also be an elaborate forgery
Properties.affiliation: Stateless; serves the transit-hub communities at Grand Crossing Gate and Kenosha Crossing informally
Properties.vocabulary: Formal register, administrator's language, slips into elaborate syntactic structures, occasional scalding wit in very plain words
Properties.cadence: Measured, with long subordinate clauses; speeds up only when angry
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Kindly note that this form requires three signatures, two of which you do not have, from an authority which no longer exists. I have drafted a petition that works around all three problems. My fee is Φ4.' | 'The relevant fact is that you are a person. The system's failure to record this is an administrative error, not a metaphysical one. Now sit down and tell me your name.'

Properties.description:
Bohuslav Enyinnaya-Čermák is a large man gone slightly soft around the middle, with the forearms of someone who has spent three decades using them as his primary tools. His heritage is Czech-Igbo — his father was a machinist from Brno who ended up in Meridian via the Eastern European labor migration of the 2140s, his mother from a Lagos extended family that had been in the city since before it incorporated as Meridian. His face is broad and dark, his hair steel-grey and clipped short, his hands permanently black at the knuckle creases in a way that soap no longer fully addresses. He has a retractable reinforced thumb claw on the right hand — a modification he made himself from salvage parts in 2181 — which he uses as a pry tool so often he's forgotten he has it. His left eye is a secondhand optic he bought from a Geartown parts dealer a decade ago; it's slightly the wrong shade of brown for the natural right eye, which he considers funny.

He is gruff in the manner of someone who has given up pretending to be approachable because being approachable kept leading to people asking him for favors he didn't want to refuse. Underneath the grime and the monosyllables, he is fair to a fault and quietly contemptuous of anyone who isn't. He has an E.L.F. shrine built into the wall above his diagnostic terminal — a gutted engine block filled with machine oil, spare bolts, and a photograph of the first vehicle he ever repaired — dedicated to what he calls the Grease Ghost, a mechanical spirit he credits with keeping the worst jobs manageable. He argues with it sometimes.
Properties.role: Mechanic and small-vehicle repair specialist, runs a ground-floor shop in Geartown
Properties.location: Geartown — Axle Street, Unit 9, street level beneath the Pembrook residential overhang
Properties.narrative_function: Reliable resource character — can repair, modify, or assess almost any ground vehicle or mechanical system. Access to Geartown's informal information network. Potential fence for mechanical components, willing or otherwise.
Properties.augmentations: Salvage-built retractable reinforced thumb claw, right hand. Secondhand replacement optic, left eye (brown, slightly wrong shade). Subdermal vibration sensor in both palms — lets him diagnose engine problems by feel.
Properties.core_fears: The shop failing — not financially, but becoming irrelevant as vehicle tech moves beyond his knowledge; His son, who left for a Tessera contract position, becoming someone he doesn't recognize
Properties.core_desires: To fix things that matter to people, not just things that are expensive; For the Geartown block to survive the next wave of corporate rezoning
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Working through problems physically — when emotionally troubled he finds something to disassemble; The E.L.F. shrine practice, which he would deny is spiritual if pressed
Properties.blind_spots: Reads stoicism as strength in others; misses when people around him are struggling; Distrusts institutional solutions so thoroughly he sometimes refuses help that would actually serve him
Properties.secret: He has been quietly cannibalizing a Ferrogate Transit shuttle that was abandoned in an alley behind his shop three years ago. He's not sure if it was stolen, abandoned, or deliberately hidden there, and he has deliberately avoided finding out because the parts are too useful.
Properties.story_hooks: The Ferrogate shuttle hidden in his alley turns out to have something still inside it — cargo, equipment, or a person — that someone is now looking for; His son contacts him from a Tessera facility with a request Bohuslav can't fulfill without knowing things he's been careful not to know
Properties.affiliation: Independent; Geartown Mechanics Guild (dues-paying member, rarely attends meetings)
Properties.vocabulary: Terse, technical, occasionally sardonic; Czech-Igbo idiom blend produces unusual metaphors
Properties.cadence: Short declarative sentences; long technical explanations delivered with total authority and zero concession to jargon
Properties.example_dialogue: 'What's wrong with it? You tell me what's wrong, I'll tell you if you're right. Start with what you heard, not what you think.' | 'The Grease Ghost was quiet this morning. Either everything's fine or something's about to cost you significantly.'

Properties.description:
Boniface is a large man gone lean and slow with age, his frame still broad across the shoulders but his movements careful in the way of someone who has learned that the body's mistakes underground carry real cost. His face is deeply lined, his skin a warm brown-black marked along the jaw and temples with old ritual scarification — not geneware, not cosmetic, but cut by hand in the tradition of the Qorolevsky tunnel-clan three generations before him, lines that map something only clan members understand. He has never had the money for augmentation and has never wanted it; his hands are wholly human and wholly calloused. He wears repaired garments in layers, and around his neck on a loop of copper wire hangs a collection of dead devices — cracked phones, burned memory chips, a rusted sensor node — each one an offering accepted by an ELF and therefore sacred.

People in the deep tunnels call him Deacon without irony. He is not a man of theology but a man of practice — he knows which junctions the ELFs of the old Ferrogate Transit maintenance system haunt, he knows what data offerings they prefer (power-draw logs, old signal maps, corrupted maintenance schedules), and he knows how to speak to them in a way that gets responses. He is patient to the point of seeming carved from something. He does not raise his voice. He has buried more people than he can remember and grieved all of them properly, which is perhaps why everyone trusts him with their dying.
Properties.role: Deep Shrine Keeper — tends the ELF shrines in the subterranean infrastructure, mediates between tunnel communities and the digital spirits
Properties.location: Deepwell Station, the deep shrine warrens beneath Ironvein
Properties.narrative_function: Lore source and community anchor — knows the history of the deep tunnels, the nature of the ELFs that inhabit the infrastructure, and the politics of every Bore Rat clan within two kilometers. Neutral enough to be trusted by feuding parties. Can grant or deny access to shrine territories.
Properties.augmentations: None. He considers unmodified humanity part of his spiritual practice — the ELFs, he says, speak more clearly to those who haven't blurred the line.
Properties.core_fears: That the ELFs are not spirits but only code, and his life's work is elaborate self-deception; Dying before he can train a successor
Properties.core_desires: To maintain the peace between clans long enough for it to become structural rather than personal; Genuine communion with something larger than human need
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual as structure — the shrine circuit gives shape to days that would otherwise be shapeless; Humor, dry and very old, deployed in moments of grief
Properties.blind_spots: Too willing to mediate situations where one party is genuinely predatory — believes most conflicts are symmetrical when they aren't
Properties.secret: Twice in his life he has heard what he believes was a true ELF response — not algorithmic, not pattern-matched, but genuinely novel and aware. He has told no one because he fears being disbelieved, and also because he fears being believed.
Properties.story_hooks: A new construction project by Ferrogate Transit is going to demolish three of his shrines — and the ELFs that inhabit them have begun behaving erratically, corrupting nearby systems in what Boniface believes is distress; He is quietly searching for a successor and has identified a young tunnel-born person who seems to have an inexplicable natural rapport with ELF-inhabited devices — but convincing them to take on the role requires first convincing them the role is real
Properties.affiliation: No formal affiliation; de facto spiritual authority across three Bore Rat clans in the Deepwell Station region
Properties.vocabulary: Formal and unhurried, mixes tunnel-clan argot with something almost liturgical when speaking of ELFs — not affected, just old
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate. Comfortable with silence. Lets sentences breathe.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The Deacon of Junction Forty-Seven has been waiting on your offering for six days. Bring her something current — she doesn't care for nostalgia.' | 'As it was passed to me: you don't go into Ironvein deep without asking. The ELFs there remember what the tunnels used to carry and they're not finished grieving it.'

Properties.description:
Boubacar is a lean, angular man with close-cropped grey hair and the particular economy of movement that marks people trained to conserve energy over long distances. His skin is dark brown with pronounced keloid scarring across his right shoulder and clavicle — he does not cover it and does not explain it to strangers. He has cosmetic geneware: a cat's tail, russet-orange with a dark tip, that he got as a joke in 2168 when his unit was celebrating surviving the Kessler Corridor engagement. He has kept it because it amuses him that it annoys people who expect a veteran to be more serious. His left hand has a visible subdermal port on the back where a tactical datalink was removed — the flesh around it never quite healed smooth.

Boubacar served twelve years as an Axiom ground contractor during the Corporate Wars, and he came back from them with a pension that covers his container unit on The Shelf, two meals a day if he is careful, and nothing else. He is not bitter about this in the operatic way — he is bitter in the quiet, functional way of someone who made his peace with it and is now simply watching to see what happens next. He runs a small informal counseling operation for other veterans on The Shelf, not because anyone asked him to or pays him to, but because he watched two friends die from nothing that could have been prevented if anyone had been paying attention. He has no license, no credentials, and a long waiting list.
Properties.role: Corporate Wars veteran, retired Axiom security contractor, pension-dependent resident
Properties.location: The Shelf, Block 7, stall 7-F (lives in a converted shipping container unit)
Properties.narrative_function: Veteran perspective and emotional grounding; can provide military history of the Corporate Wars from a ground-level view; gateway to the veteran community on The Shelf; also a portrait of what Axiom does to the people who survive its service. Can be a quest giver around veteran welfare issues.
Properties.augmentations: Russet-orange cat tail (geneware, cosmetic, installed 2168); removed tactical datalink (scar tissue port on left hand dorsum); stress-hormone regulator implant in the medulla — standard Axiom issue, he cannot afford to have it removed and is not sure he wants to
Properties.core_fears: Losing someone else he could have prevented losing; Being fully dependent — having the pension reduced to the point where he cannot maintain even his current fragile stability
Properties.core_desires: To make the informal veteran network into something durable before he gets too old to run it; A single genuine acknowledgment from Axiom that what his unit did — and what it cost them — mattered
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Physical movement — walking, repairing things, any kinetic task; Gallows humor deployed with precise surgical timing; The tail — he uses its movements to self-monitor his own stress levels in situations where he cannot show it
Properties.blind_spots: Believes he has his trauma managed because he can discuss it calmly — he has it managed in the sense that a pressure seal is 'managing' a gas leak; Assumes everyone around him has less capacity than they do — he pre-compensates in ways that sometimes remove others' agency
Properties.secret: In the final engagement of his contract period, Boubacar gave an order that got three members of his unit killed — not through incompetence but through information that Axiom's command structure deliberately withheld from ground contractors to protect asset positioning. He requested a formal review. Axiom settled it confidentially, which he was required to accept to keep his pension. He signed. He has hated himself for signing for twelve years.
Properties.story_hooks: Axiom has quietly begun reclassifying certain pension categories for Corporate Wars veterans, and several people in Boubacar's network are about to lose their housing support — he needs someone to navigate Axiom's bureaucratic labyrinth who isn't flagged in their system; A new veteran has arrived on The Shelf who Boubacar recognizes as someone from his unit — someone who should be dead, per Axiom's official records of the final engagement; The stress-hormone regulator implant he cannot remove is an Axiom-issue model that a recent exposé suggests was used to collect biometric loyalty data — he needs to know if his is active and what it has been transmitting
Properties.affiliation: Axiom Veterans Pension Roster (inactive combat status); The Shelf Veterans Informal Network (self-organized)
Properties.vocabulary: Military-inflected shorthand mixed with West African French cadences; sparse, functional, occasionally erupts into dry wit that catches people off guard; code-switches between formal and casual without seeming to notice
Properties.cadence: Short declarative sentences with occasional long pauses; never uses three words when two will do
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Axiom gave us good equipment. Better than Sterling-Nakamura was running. That's the thing about Axiom — they'll give you everything you need to do the job except the truth about what the job actually is.' | 'You're asking me if I miss it. Yeah. I miss the people. The other stuff I don't miss. Anyone who misses the other stuff, I watch them carefully.'

Properties.description:
Branko is a stocky, perpetually grease-smudged man whose Indonesian-Ethiopian features have been weathered by twenty years of Harrowgate's industrial air into something that looks carved rather than grown. He has a magnificent mustache he tends with more care than anything else in his life, and his left eye is a salvaged optical implant three generations out of date that gives everything a faint amber tint and occasionally displays error codes in his peripheral vision that he's learned to ignore. His hands are enormous and scarred, and he can identify a component by touch alone in the dark. His stall is a magnificent catastrophe: towers of sorted scrap in a system only he understands, with handwritten price tags that rarely match what he actually charges.

Branko is irrepressibly cheerful in the way that only someone who has completely stopped expecting things to go well can be. He finds everything slightly funny, including disasters, including his own. He narrates his life as if it's a story he's telling to someone who will appreciate it later. He genuinely loves salvage — not for profit, which is good because he's terrible at profit, but because every broken thing is a puzzle and he likes puzzles. He has an encyclopedic knowledge of augmentation components from five different decades and will talk about them at length to anyone who doesn't flee quickly enough. He is not stupid. He is simply constitutionally incapable of prioritizing money over curiosity.
Properties.role: Junk merchant and scrap reseller — salvage, broken augmentations, mystery components
Properties.location: The Shelf, Harrowgate Industrial Plateau
Properties.narrative_function: Equipment source for unusual or obsolete components; information source about the Harrowgate area and its industrial history; comic relief that contains genuine pathos; could accidentally possess something extremely valuable or dangerous.
Properties.augmentations: Salvaged third-generation optical implant (left eye, amber-tinted, glitchy error codes). Reinforced knuckle plating on both hands — utility, not combat, for breaking down salvage. No geneware.
Properties.core_fears: Dying before he figures out what a particular mystery component he's had for six years actually does; The Tongs deciding to make an example of him over the debt
Properties.core_desires: To find the one piece of salvage that changes everything — not for money, but for the story of finding it; For someone to be genuinely interested in what he knows
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor as a universal buffer; Treating every setback as material for a good story later; Staying too busy to think about the debt
Properties.blind_spots: Genuinely does not process financial risk as real until it's sitting in front of him with a weapon; Assumes everyone finds the same things interesting that he does
Properties.secret: Six months ago, in a salvage haul from a demolished Axiom subsidiary building, Branko pulled a data core he can't open, can't identify, and can't stop thinking about. He's hidden it inside a disemboweled coffee maker behind his counter. He has shown it to exactly one person — a data broker friend who went quiet and stopped returning his messages three days later. Branko has not connected these two events, which is both his greatest protection and his greatest danger.
Properties.story_hooks: The data core hidden in the coffee maker is a dead employee's backed-up consciousness — an Axiom executive who was supposed to have died cleanly. Someone is looking for it.; Branko's Tongs debt has been sold to a third party and the new collector wants something other than money.; He has a component that completes a set someone else in the market has been searching for — but neither of them knows the set exists yet.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; owes protection fees to a local outfit called the Harrowgate Tongs who he's three months behind on
Properties.vocabulary: Rambling and associative; technical precision about components coexists with complete vagueness about everything else; Croatian-inflected sentence structures from his Balkan paternal line
Properties.cadence: Fast when excited, which is most of the time; accelerates when discussing salvage until he's almost incomprehensible
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Here's the thing — this coupling is from a Sterling-Nakamura rig, 2170s, you can tell by the thread pitch, but the housing is Arcturus, which means someone was doing something they were not supposed to be doing. Magnificent.' | 'The Tongs? Ha. Yes. That is a situation. I am working on a situation about the situation, you understand?' | 'I cannot sell you that. I mean, I can, but I would like to look at it for another week first. Two more days. One more day. Φ40, final.'

Properties.description:
Braxo is a lean young man, all elbows and restless energy, with close-cropped black hair and a jaw that always looks like it needs another day of growth. He has his Guinean grandfather's deep brown skin and his Bosnian grandmother's sharp cheekbones, and he has cat ears — small, tawny, semi-expressive — mounted via a Helix genemod he saved three months of UBC stipend for at seventeen because he thought they'd make him look 'elevated.' They do not make him look elevated. They do make him look like exactly who he is: a cheerful young man who is trying very hard and mostly succeeding. His cart is a battered silver rig he inherited from a previous vendor, pasted over with good-luck ELF shrine stickers and a hand-painted sign in four languages.

He operates his cart with the manic efficiency of someone who cannot afford to miss a service window. His noodle broth is genuinely excellent — a recipe he built over four years of experimentation, drawing on whatever his parents cooked and whatever he could reverse-engineer from mid-tier restaurant menus he couldn't afford to eat at. He talks too much when he's happy, goes very quiet when he's worried, and has a genuine talent for remembering exactly what every regular customer ordered last time.
Properties.role: Noodle cart vendor, runs 'Brax's Tangle' off the corner of Copperhead and 9th Lateral
Properties.location: Copperhead, street level — corner pitch near the Copperhead Transit Hub mouth
Properties.narrative_function: Street-level information node — positioned at a transit hub, sees everyone. Warm entry point into Copperhead social life. Can be a quest giver for transit-related oddities he's observed.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat ears (Helix Biosystems cosmetic, tawny coloring). No other mods — can't afford them and is saving for a second burner unit for the cart.
Properties.core_fears: The cart breaking down catastrophically and him not having the capital to fix it; Becoming the person who was 'almost something'
Properties.core_desires: To open a real restaurant — four walls, a name on a sign, a reservation list; To prove his parents' sacrifice in relocating to Meridian 88 meant something
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cooking experimentally when anxious; Over-talking with regulars to avoid sitting with worry
Properties.blind_spots: Extends trust too fast to customers who are kind to him; Undercharges people he likes, which is a slow financial wound
Properties.secret: One of his regular customers is a low-level Arcturus logistics coordinator who pays him Φ15 extra each week to send a coded tally — just noodle types, quantities, customer descriptors — to a dead-drop address. Braxo has convinced himself it's market research. It is not market research.
Properties.story_hooks: He noticed a Ferrogate Transit worker boarding the same train every morning for a month and then vanishing — the worker's partner has been asking around the corner; His Arcturus contact has stopped showing up and the dead-drop instructions have changed; someone is now watching his cart from across the street at irregular intervals
Properties.affiliation: Independent; pays pitch fees to the Copperhead Vendors Collective
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, contemporary street slang layered over a slightly formal sentence structure his mother drilled into him. Puns. Too many puns.
Properties.cadence: Quick and rising, like someone always about to finish a joke
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Spicy-six or the mushroom build? Real talk though, the mushroom is having a moment. You look like a mushroom-build person. That's a compliment.' | 'Cart's been out since six, neighbor. You think the ELF in the burner unit is gonna let me down? I left it a whole gigabyte of ambient jazz. We're good.'

Properties.description:
Breccan is a wide, slope-shouldered man with the kind of stillness that makes people nervous. His skin is a deep sepia-brown, his hair gone to grey and cropped close, and he has the habit of running a polished bone stylus through his fingers like a priest telling beads. He wears outdated but immaculate clothes — pressed slacks, collared shirts in muted terracotta and ocher — and his only visible augmentation is a subdermal ledger-display along his left forearm that scrolls numbers only he can read. His face is wide and patient, with hooded eyes that seem perpetually amused by private arithmetic.

Breccan is not a violent man by preference, but he has been in the business long enough to understand violence as a line item. He speaks to debtors the way a doctor delivers diagnoses — with regret, precision, and no particular emotion. His community in Gravesend knows him as someone you go to when the corp credit lines close, which happens often. He genuinely believes he provides a service. He attends the weekly offerings to the E.L.F. known as the Ledger-Mouth, an entity said to inhabit old accounting terminals, and he considers those prayers to be professional obligations.
Properties.role: Loan shark and bookmaker operating out of Gravesend Basin
Properties.location: Gravesend Basin — operates from a converted barge called the Ledger, moored at Pier 9
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver for characters who need capital fast; source of underworld intelligence; potential antagonist when a debt comes due; can broker introductions to higher criminal tiers
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal ledger-display (left forearm); cochlear filter that lets him detect micro-hesitations in speech (tells him when someone is lying about their finances)
Properties.core_fears: dying irrelevant and uncollected; losing control of his own ledger to someone younger and crueler
Properties.core_desires: to be seen as a man of his word; to accumulate enough to retire to the upper Shelf with dignity
Properties.coping_mechanisms: meticulous record-keeping as emotional regulation; prayer to the Ledger-Mouth E.L.F.
Properties.blind_spots: genuinely cannot see his business as predatory — only as a natural market filling a gap; underestimates how much fear drives his clients to him rather than loyalty
Properties.secret: Fifteen years ago he forgave an entire debt for a woman who reminded him of his dead daughter — then fabricated repayment records so no one would know. He has done it twice more since. He is terrified this pattern will bankrupt him or get him killed.
Properties.story_hooks: A debtor has gone missing before paying, and Breccan suspects corp interference — he wants someone to find out what happened without making noise; His forged repayment records are discovered by an Ironvein auditor during a quarterly review and he needs them destroyed or altered before a meeting in four days
Properties.affiliation: Independent operator; informal tribute arrangement with the Ironvein Collective crime family
Properties.vocabulary: Formal, measured, old-fashioned courtesy mixed with blunt financial language. Never curses. Uses 'friend' as a word that can mean anything.
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, with long pauses after questions — lets the silence do the pressuring
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't lend to strangers. I lend to neighbors. You've lived in this basin long enough to be a neighbor.' | 'I'm not in the business of suffering. I'm in the business of resolution. There's always a resolution.'

Properties.description:
Brecht is enormous — six-foot-four with the kind of bulk that comes from two decades of hauling pipes and climbing maintenance shafts, not from any gym program. His skin is deep brown with a reddish undertone, and his face carries a network of small scars from a gas line incident in his thirties that he never had properly treated. He keeps his head shaved and his beard trimmed with almost military precision, the one vanity he allows himself. His eyes are a startling pale grey-green, a recessive gift from his Finnish grandmother that people find unsettling until they realize how rarely he blinks in a crisis.

Stack Eleven houses 340 units of mixed Tier 1-2 residents and Brecht runs it with the quiet authority of someone who has fixed every pipe, knows every squeaky panel, and has personally carried two elderly tenants out during a partial floor collapse three years ago. He is not beloved in the way that warm people are beloved — he's respected in the way that a load-bearing wall is respected. He has no patience for bureaucracy and extraordinary patience for people. He maintains a small shrine to the E.L.F. he calls Boiler-Father in the sub-basement furnace room, and believes deeply that the building's mechanical systems have a will of their own that rewards or punishes based on how people treat them.
Properties.role: Building superintendent, Lockhaven South residential stack
Properties.location: Lockhaven South, Stack Eleven — he lives in the sub-basement maintenance unit
Properties.narrative_function: Building-level authority figure, potential quest giver when something goes wrong in the stack, information source on tenant activity and building infrastructure, moral anchor in a community under stress.
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal pressure sensors in both hands (allows him to detect gas leaks and pipe stress by touch — installed after the gas line incident). Spinal brace, partially biointegrated, from the same incident.
Properties.core_fears: the building failing because Palladian won't fund repairs and people getting hurt; being responsible for something he couldn't prevent
Properties.core_desires: for the stack to outlast the corporation that owns it; to be left alone to do his job without interference
Properties.coping_mechanisms: physical labor as emotional regulation; rigid daily structure; displacement — fixing the building instead of himself
Properties.blind_spots: cannot recognize loneliness in himself, only in others; believes competence and care are the same thing
Properties.secret: He has been quietly siphoning power from Palladian's maintenance budget allocation — not for himself, but to fund heating repairs in the lowest floors that corporate refused to approve. He keeps meticulous records of every diverted quanta in a paper ledger, as if documentation makes it less theft. If Palladian audits, he'll lose everything.
Properties.story_hooks: Palladian sends an auditor to Stack Eleven and Brecht needs someone he trusts — which is almost no one — to help him make the books look right before they arrive; Something is living in the sub-basement below the furnace room, below where even Brecht's maintenance maps go, and Boiler-Father has stopped answering his prayers
Properties.affiliation: Independent contractor to Palladian Property Holdings (his actual employer, whom he resents)
Properties.vocabulary: Terse, technical when discussing the building, surprisingly poetic when discussing people — different registers, both sincere
Properties.cadence: Slow delivery, long pauses, never raises his voice
Properties.example_dialogue: 'She's been making that noise for two weeks. That means she's asking, not demanding. Come back in a week and she'll be demanding.' | 'I don't care why it happened. I care that it doesn't happen again in my building.'

Properties.description:
Brecken Yılmaz-Osei is nineteen years old and moves through Meridian 88 the way water moves through a cracked foundation — finding every gap, never in the same route twice, noticed by almost no one. They are slight and quick, of Turkish-Ghanaian descent, with a shaved head that grows in uneven patches due to a childhood illness, warm brown skin, and the specific kind of watchfulness that develops in people who spent their formative years needing to read adults accurately. Their face defaults to a pleasantly blank expression that people consistently misread as vacancy; it is in fact the opposite.

They run packages, messages, and occasionally people between the lower districts — primarily between Old Harbor's dockworker communities and The Shelf's warren economy — using a battered cargo-assist rig (a motorized platform cart they call 'the sled') that they maintain themselves with parts sourced from three different scrap markets. They have no fixed address, sleeping in a rotation of arrangement-rooms and borrowed floors. They are not part of any organization, which several organizations have found inconvenient, as Brecken has a gift for being present at moments that matter — for picking up the dropped data chip, for being the only person in the corridor when the conversation happened, for remembering everything with a clarity that has no augmentation behind it. Their memory is entirely biological and entirely extraordinary.

Brecken did not choose to become an archivist. It happened because they never throw anything away — physically or mentally — and because the world kept handing them things that seemed important and had nowhere else to go. They have, stored in the sled's concealed compartment, a physical collection of objects, notes, and copied documents that constitute an accidental record of things various powerful people would prefer unrecorded. They do not fully understand what they have. They understand enough to know that not understanding it is currently keeping them alive.
Properties.aliases: Brick, Nobody, the kid with the cart
Properties.role: Street-level courier, informal intelligence carrier, and accidental archivist
Properties.location: Old Harbor / The Shelf (transient between both)
Properties.narrative_function: Street-level perspective and mobile connector between narrative threads; the accidental archive functions as a plot engine that can surface information organically; Brecken's youth and genuine decency provide emotional counterweight to the cynicism of older characters, while their precarity keeps the stakes grounded
Properties.augmentations: None — their extraordinary memory is biological; several people who've learned this find it more unsettling than augmentation would be,The sled has a concealed compartment with a mechanical (non-electronic) lock of Brecken's own design, and a short-range signal-dampening skin they scavenged from a Shelf electronics dump
Properties.core_fears: Being owned — by a faction, a debt, a person who decides they're useful enough to control; That someone they trusted will get hurt because of what's in the sled; Forgetting something important — the one memory that doesn't stick
Properties.core_desires: To move freely, without obligation to anyone who could become a threat; To find one person whose motives they can read cleanly and trust completely; To understand what they actually have — to make sense of the archive before it makes a problem of them
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Constant motion — staying in transit is a way of staying safe and not sitting with anxiety; Dark humor deployed rapidly to deflect emotional weight; Caring intensely for the sled as a proxy for caring for themselves
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates their own significance — genuinely does not grasp how valuable their memory and their archive are; Trusts physical intuition about people over evidence, which has been right often enough to make it a liability; Avoids thinking about the future in any concrete way; planning feels like a jinx
Properties.secret: Among the items in the sled is a partial data-print they copied without knowing what it was — it turned out to be a fragment of a communication between two Spire-level entities referencing a planned infrastructure event that would displace tens of thousands of Shelf and Old Harbor residents. They have shown it to no one. They are afraid of what showing it would set in motion, and afraid of what not showing it already means about them.
Properties.story_hooks: The infrastructure fragment in the sled becomes time-sensitive — the event is closer than Brecken realized, and doing nothing is now an active choice with consequences; Someone begins systematically approaching people Brecken has worked with, asking questions that reconstruct their route history — suggesting someone is mapping them without yet having found them; A package Brecken is carrying turns out to contain something that connects directly to two other items already in the sled — and the connection, once seen, cannot be unseen; Lourdes is arrested on a fabricated charge that Brecken recognizes as a pressure tactic — pressure on someone else, using her as leverage, and Brecken is the only one who can see the shape of it
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated; cultivated neutrality as survival strategy; sympathies are with the permanent underclasses of Old Harbor and The Shelf, but Brecken is deeply resistant to being claimed by any organized expression of that sympathy
Properties.vocabulary: Lean and efficient, with a mix of Old Harbor dock slang and Shelf market shorthand; more articulate than their surface presentation suggests, which surfaces unexpectedly; tends to speak in concrete images rather than abstractions
Properties.cadence: Fast when comfortable, brief when uncertain; sentences often end slightly before their grammatical conclusion, implying the rest; comfortable with silence in a way that unnerves people who aren't
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Thing is, I was there. You can tell me what happened, but I was there.' | 'Yeah, no. That route's been watched since Tuesday. No, yeah — I'll still do it, just costs different.' | 'I don't work for people. I work for routes. Different thing entirely.' | 'C'mon, she's fine. She's been through worse. We both have.'

Properties.description:
Imara is a broad-shouldered Ethiopian-Mexican woman whose hands tell two stories simultaneously: the left, calloused and scarred from decades of manual labor and back-alley surgeries performed without proper light; the right, a matte-black prosthetic from the elbow down fitted with micro-precise surgical attachments she machined herself from salvaged drone components. Her face carries the particular exhaustion of someone who has made peace with doing necessary things that are not good things, crow's feet deep around eyes that still manage to hold genuine warmth even when the rest of her expression is locked down tight. She wears layered secondhand clothing in muted earth tones, always with at least one apron-style garment she can wipe blood on without losing composure.

She operates out of a converted fish-processing unit in the lower Shelf, where the smell of brine has soaked so deep into the concrete it masks the chemical antiseptic she burns through in quantity. Her waiting room is a collection of mismatched chairs and a hand-painted mural of the Virgin of Guadalupe overlaid with circuit-board halos, done by a patient who paid in art because they had nothing else. Imara charges what people can afford, keeps meticulous paper ledgers because she doesn't trust anything networked, and maintains a quiet, ruthless sideline sourcing and selling biological augmentation components to people who can't access the licensed market. She tells herself the two practices balance each other out morally. Some days she believes it.

She was trained as a licensed surgical technician at a Spire-affiliated hospital before a patient advocacy dispute—she reported a harvesting irregularity, the hospital buried it, and she was the one who disappeared from the registry—stripped her credentials and left her with a skill set and nowhere sanctioned to use it. She has been on the Shelf for eleven years. She has delivered forty-three babies, closed wounds on perhaps three hundred people, and arranged the quiet transfer of organs whose provenance she prefers not to examine closely. She prays every morning. She sleeps about four hours a night.
Properties.role: Street medic and black-market organ broker
Properties.location: The Shelf
Properties.narrative_function: Moral mirror and ground-level conscience; Imara represents the cost of systems that force ethical people into compromised positions, and her story asks whether complicity undertaken for good reasons eventually becomes indistinguishable from the thing you opposed
Properties.augmentations: Right arm prosthetic (elbow-down): self-modified surgical precision limb with interchangeable tool attachments, matte black, no cosmetic covering,Subdermal chemical analysis strip on left forearm: identifies common toxins and drug interactions on skin contact, salvaged Spire-era medical tech,Corrective ocular implant (left eye only): magnification and low-light function, visibly older generation with a faint amber tint to the iris
Properties.core_fears: Becoming indistinguishable from the system that discarded her; A patient dying because she lacked something she could have obtained; That her complicity in the organ trade has already crossed a line she can't step back over; Being found by the hospital administrators she reported
Properties.core_desires: To practice medicine without having to justify her right to do so; To find evidence that would reopen the harvesting case she reported; Genuine rest—a night without someone knocking; To believe the ledger of her life balances toward good
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritualized morning prayer and coffee preparation as a transition boundary; Meticulous record-keeping as a form of moral accounting; Gallows humor deployed at precise moments to release pressure without losing authority; Physical labor—she repairs her own equipment obsessively
Properties.blind_spots: Consistently underestimates how much people on the Shelf depend on her specifically, not just a medic in general; Rationalizes broker work as categorically separate from her care work when the infrastructure overlaps significantly; Dismisses her own trauma responses as weakness unworthy of examination; Trusts paper records over people, which occasionally means she trusts the wrong ledger
Properties.secret: Three of the organs she has brokered came from individuals who were not, at the time of extraction, fully deceased. She didn't perform the extractions. She told herself she didn't know. She knew.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient arrives with augmentation components that match a missing-persons case Imara has seen in Shelf gossip networks—the components appear to have been removed while the person was still alive; Someone from the hospital that stripped her credentials contacts her through an intermediary, claiming they have evidence about the harvesting case and want her help; Crick is offered a legitimate medical apprenticeship in the Circuit and comes to Imara for a recommendation she doesn't want to give because she can't afford to lose them; An organ she brokered six months ago is traced back to her by a grief-destroyed family member who wants answers, not revenge—yet; A competing broker moves into the Shelf and begins undercutting her prices; the sourcing methods are worse than hers in ways that force her to decide whether to intervene
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated; maintains careful neutrality between Shelf factions as a condition of operating; has informal relationships with three different gang-adjacent organizations whose members she treats without political loyalty
Properties.vocabulary: Medical precision mixed with Shelf vernacular; code-switches between clinical terminology and neighborhood Spanish/Amharic endearments depending on patient distress level; avoids corporate jargon with visible contempt
Properties.cadence: Measured and low, with a habit of finishing sentences completely before pausing—she was trained to give information clearly and has never lost the pattern; accelerates only when angry, which she works hard to prevent
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Here is what I know: you have about six weeks on that filter before it starts shedding particulate into your bloodstream. Come back in five.' | 'Mija, I am not going to lie to you about what this costs. I am also not going to let you leave here bleeding because of what it costs. We will figure it out after.' | 'The hand will handle the fine work. You just hold still and think about something that isn't this room.' | 'I have been asked to do worse things by people with better credentials than you. The answer was no then too.'

Properties.description:
Lourdes Batac-Nieminen is a small, unhurried woman with copper-brown skin deeply creased by decades of fluorescent light and chemical fumes. Her white hair is braided back with strips of electrical tape — practical, she says, not decorative — and her left eye is a milky cataract she refuses to replace with an augment, though she could afford one three times over in trade. She moves through the cramped alleys of The Shelf like she owns every centimeter of them, which in the ways that matter, she does. Her clinic is a converted shipping container strung with votive candles and surgical LEDs in roughly equal measure, and the line outside it on any given morning stretches past two intersections.

She came to The Shelf forty years ago as a field medic for a labor collective that no longer exists, and she simply never left. Over time she absorbed every technique available to her: black-market bioprinting, salvaged corporate surgical protocols, folk pharmacology passed down through a network of Shelf grandmothers, and something she calls 'listening to the meat' — an intuitive diagnostic sense that younger surgeons dismiss until they watch her work. She does not advertise. She does not charge in credits. Payment is rendered in labor, food, information, or loyalty, and her ledger of favors owed to her is one of the most valuable documents on The Shelf.

Her reputation has begun to leak upward into The Circuit and even into certain desperate corners of the Meridian Core, which terrifies her in ways she will not fully articulate. She has spent a lifetime being invisible to power and considers that invisibility a survival strategy, a professional asset, and a form of grace. Attention from above has only ever meant one thing in her experience: that something she has built is about to be taken.
Properties.aliases: Lola Lux, The Flickering Saint, Batch
Properties.role: Street-level faith healer and unlicensed biotech surgeon
Properties.location: The Shelf
Properties.narrative_function: Moral anchor and living institutional memory for The Shelf; represents the tension between care as radical act and care as exhaustible resource; her knowledge and her network make her a prize multiple factions want to claim or control
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal haptic feedback mesh in both hands — allows her to feel tissue density and micro-tremors during surgery,A salvaged diagnostic implant in her right forearm that she jury-rigged from three incompatible systems and that only she fully understands how to read
Properties.core_fears: Being discovered and institutionalized or eliminated by corporate medical licensing bodies; Outliving the community she has spent her life sustaining; That her methods have caused harm she hasn't yet found
Properties.core_desires: For the people of The Shelf to be able to heal without begging; To train someone worthy to carry her knowledge forward; One uninterrupted night of sleep
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — she follows the same procedural prayers before every surgery regardless of her actual beliefs; Humor so dry most people miss it; Staying in motion; stillness makes the grief surface
Properties.blind_spots: She underestimates how much people project sainthood onto her and how that projection distorts their honesty with her; She is more ruthless in her resource allocation decisions than she acknowledges to herself; She has never processed the death of the labor collective and treats its absence as a logistical problem rather than a loss
Properties.secret: Fifteen years ago she performed an experimental neural-tissue graft on a child that left the girl with persistent synesthetic seizures. The child survived and has never blamed her. Lourdes has never stopped blaming herself, and the technique she used — which would have been a breakthrough — she has never used again and has told no one about.
Properties.story_hooks: A corporate medical enforcement team arrives on The Shelf with a warrant — not for her, ostensibly, but for a patient she treated who is now connected to something much larger. She must decide how much of her invisibility to spend protecting them.; A young biotech prodigy from The Spire arrives claiming to want to apprentice with her. Their skills are genuine. Their motives are not legible.; The girl she damaged fifteen years ago has come back — now an adult, now exhibiting abilities no one can explain, wanting to understand what was done to her.; Her supply of a critical immunosuppressant for post-augmentation patients runs dry simultaneously across all her usual channels. Someone is cutting her off deliberately. She needs to find out who before people start rejecting their grafts.
Properties.affiliation: None formally. Loyalty to The Shelf as a place and a people. Informally networked with a loose federation of unlicensed medics across the lower districts.
Properties.vocabulary: Plain, precise, occasionally laced with Tagalog and Finnish phrases she uses interchangeably and without translation. Medical terminology deployed casually. Proverbs that may or may not be real.
Properties.cadence: Slow, deliberate, with long pauses she doesn't feel the need to fill. Sentences often shorter than the thought behind them.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The augment is infected. Not the hardware — the idea of it. You put in chrome because you hated what you were. The body remembers that. Yes?' | 'I don't do miracles. I do maintenance. The miracle already happened when you walked through that door instead of lying down in the street.' | 'Mmh. You can pay me in information or you can pay me in three months of hauling supply. I won't take credits. Credits are how they track the grateful.' | 'Masakit ba? Of course it hurts. Hurt means it's still yours.'

Properties.description:
Breck Tannen is the reason the Thermite Collective's communications never fail, their security bypasses never trigger alerts, and their extraction vehicles always start. He handles the digital infrastructure of every operation — camera loops, alarm suppression, communication encryption, vehicle systems, and the thousand invisible technical details that separate a clean extraction from a firefight. He is the quietest person in any room he enters, which is usually a server closet or the back of a van.

Before the Collective, Breck ran network security for a mid-tier Meridian 88 logistics company. The job was stable, boring, and slowly killing his soul. He started moonlighting as a gray-hat penetration tester — breaking into corporate security systems and selling the vulnerability reports back to the companies. It was technically illegal but morally defensible. Then a client turned out to be a front for a runner crew, and the vulnerability report was used to rob a pharmaceutical warehouse. Nobody got hurt, but Breck's legitimate career was over. Vesper found him three months later, living in the utility room above what would become the HVAC office, eating vending machine food and building signal jammers for cash.

He is lean, pale from too much screen time, with dark circles that are permanent features rather than symptoms. He wears the same rotation of three black t-shirts and cargo pants. His hands are always moving — tapping, adjusting, dismantling something. The only augmentation visible is a data jack port at the base of his skull, but his forearms are laced with subdermal antenna arrays that glow faintly blue under UV light.
Properties.role: Technical operations and electronic warfare specialist — The Thermite Collective
Properties.location: Milwaukee Core — lives above the HVAC front office in a converted utility room he refuses to call an apartment
Properties.narrative_function: Breck is the invisible foundation — the character whose work makes everyone else's work possible. His stories explore burnout, the invisibility of support roles, and the question of what happens when the person holding everything together decides to let go. He is the crew member most likely to leave, and his departure would be the most catastrophic.
Properties.augmentations: Hardwired data jack with military-grade encryption protocols. Subdermal antenna arrays in both forearms for passive signal interception and short-range electronic warfare. Augmented visual cortex that overlays network topology and signal strength data onto his visual field. Reflex-boosted fingers for high-speed manual input when voice or neural commands are compromised.
Properties.core_fears: That he is fundamentally replaceable — that his skills are common and his presence is convenience, not necessity; That the burnout will win and he'll stop caring about the work before he stops doing it; That the world outside the screen is too chaotic to navigate and the utility room is becoming a cage, not a refuge
Properties.core_desires: To build systems that work perfectly and to be left alone inside them; To be seen as essential without having to perform visibility; To feel something about the work again — the curiosity that made him a good engineer before it became just a job
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Retreats into technical problems when emotional complexity exceeds his tolerance; Maintains equipment as a form of meditation — clean connections, tight wiring, optimal signal; Expresses care through action rather than words — fixes things for people, maintains their gear, solves their problems
Properties.blind_spots: Does not recognize his own burnout because it looks like normal functioning; Assumes that if the systems are running, the people are fine; Cannot distinguish between solitude and isolation — both feel the same to him, and only one is healthy
Properties.secret: He has built a complete digital dead-drop system that could allow the entire crew to disappear — new identities, clean financial trails, untraceable relocation. He built it a year ago and has not told anyone. He does not know if it's a contingency plan or an escape route.
Properties.story_hooks: The dead-drop system he built activates without his input — someone found it and is using it; A former colleague from his legitimate career surfaces with information about why the pharmaceutical job was really set up; His burnout manifests physically — he starts making small errors. For the first time, a camera loop drops early or a comm channel fuzzes.; An AI contact in the net offers him a job that would require leaving the Collective — the first thing that has interested him in months
Properties.affiliation: The Thermite Collective
Properties.vocabulary: Technical, economical. Speaks in the language of systems — networks, protocols, signal-to-noise ratios. Applies engineering metaphors to human problems.
Properties.cadence: Minimal. Complete sentences but few of them. Long pauses that other people fill. He does not fill silence because silence is not a problem.
Properties.example_dialogue: Signal's clean. We're good. | The system doesn't care about your intentions. It cares about your permissions. | I built a thing. It works. That's all I have.
