Properties.description:
Vesper Kade plans extractions the way other people play chess — five moves ahead, every contingency mapped, every variable assigned a probability. She spent twelve years as a logistics coordinator for Torii Security Group before the corp restructured her division and offered her a severance package worth less than her monthly augmentation maintenance. She walked out with her skills, her contacts, and a very detailed understanding of how corporate security systems fail.

She built the Thermite Collective from the ground up over six years, hand-picking operators who could execute clean work without the ego that gets people killed. The crew's reputation is their product — no collateral damage, no witnesses, no mess. Clients pay a premium because Vesper's plans work. When they don't, she has three backup plans that do.

Physically unremarkable by design. Medium height, brown hair kept short, clothes that say middle management. She could walk through any lobby in Meridian 88 without triggering a second glance. This is the most dangerous thing about her. The only augmentation visible is a faint dermal port behind her left ear — the rest is all internal, all quiet, all precise.
Properties.role: Crew lead and extraction planner — The Thermite Collective
Properties.location: Milwaukee Core — operates from a rented office space disguised as an HVAC consulting firm
Properties.narrative_function: Vesper represents the professional end of the runner spectrum — proof that freelance work can be competent, organized, and sustainable. Her stories are heist narratives driven by planning and precision, contrasting Kyle's reactive, instinct-driven operations. She is the answer to the question: what does a runner look like when the trauma is managed and the work is clean?
Properties.augmentations: Tactical overlay implant (Torii Security surplus) — projects environmental data, security system schematics, and personnel movement patterns onto her visual field. Subvocal communication array for silent crew coordination. Enhanced spatial memory cortex that allows her to memorize building layouts after a single walkthrough.
Properties.core_fears: That one plan will fail catastrophically and her crew will pay the price; That she is only as valuable as her last successful extraction — that loyalty is transactional even among her own people; That the corporate thinking she claims to have left behind is the only thing that makes her effective
Properties.core_desires: To build something that outlasts her — a crew, a reputation, a legacy of clean work; To prove that professionalism and independence are not mutually exclusive; To never again be disposable to anyone
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Plans obsessively — if every variable is accounted for, nothing can go wrong; Maintains emotional distance from crew through professionalism — care expressed as competence, not warmth; Keeps the HVAC office spotless because controllable environments soothe her
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot improvise well when plans collapse beyond her contingency range; Underestimates the emotional needs of her crew because she has suppressed her own; Treats every relationship as a system to be optimized
Properties.secret: She still has her Torii Security Group access credentials. They were never revoked. She has never used them, but she has never deleted them either.
Properties.story_hooks: A contract goes sideways and the client turns out to be Torii Security Group — Vesper's former employer; Her unused Torii credentials suddenly show activity she didn't initiate; A rival extraction crew starts undercutting Thermite's contracts with suspiciously good intelligence; One of her crew is offered a corporate position — the thing Vesper left behind
Properties.affiliation: The Thermite Collective
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, professional, occasionally dry. Uses corporate language without irony because it is her native tongue.
Properties.cadence: Measured. Every sentence is a complete thought. She does not interrupt and does not tolerate being interrupted.
Properties.example_dialogue: The plan doesn't care about your feelings. Neither does the security grid. | We bill for precision. Chaos is a surcharge nobody can afford. | Noted. We'll revisit that after the extraction, assuming we're all still breathing.

Properties.description:
Harlan Dray is the kind of man who can calculate blast radius to the centimeter while telling a joke about his ex-wife. Eighteen years in controlled demolition — first legal, then gray-market, then whatever pays. He started in construction, blowing buildings down so new ones could go up. When the construction contracts dried up and the corps started automating demo work, he pivoted to the only market that still valued a human touch: the kind of demolition that happens on a schedule nobody files with the city.

He is broad-shouldered, weathered, with hands that look like they've been rebuilt from scrap — because two of his fingers have been. Chemical burns on his forearms are old enough to be part of the landscape. He laughs too loud, drinks too much on off-nights, and has the kind of warmth that makes people forget he carries enough shaped charges to level a city block in the trunk of his vehicle.

The work keeps him honest. When he's building a breaching charge or calculating structural weak points, the noise in his head goes quiet. It's the only time it goes quiet. Vesper gave him that — steady work, a crew that doesn't treat him like a liability, a reason to be precise instead of reckless. He would die for her and she would be furious about it, which is exactly the dynamic that works.
Properties.role: Demolitions and breaching specialist — The Thermite Collective
Properties.location: Milwaukee Core — rents a workshop in an industrial unit near the old foundry district
Properties.narrative_function: Harlan is the heart of the Thermite Collective — the emotional counterweight to Vesper's clinical precision. His stories explore the tension between competence and self-destruction, between the steady hand that builds perfect charges and the unsteady life outside the work. He humanizes the crew.
Properties.augmentations: Haptic feedback implants in both hands — allow him to sense material density, structural stress points, and vibration patterns through touch. Two prosthetic fingers (left hand, ring and pinky) replaced after a detonation accident seven years ago. Internal air filtration system for working with chemical compounds.
Properties.core_fears: That his best years are behind him and the work is the only thing keeping him relevant; That one day his hands will shake at the wrong moment; That the people he cares about see him as a lovable mess instead of someone to rely on
Properties.core_desires: To be needed — not tolerated, not managed, but genuinely necessary; To build something that lasts, even though his profession is literally destruction; To outrun the version of himself that drinks alone and doesn't answer calls
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor as deflection — if he's making people laugh, they're not looking too closely; Obsessive precision in his work compensates for the chaos in his personal life; Physical labor — when the noise gets bad, he builds things with his hands until it stops
Properties.blind_spots: Thinks his drinking is under control because it hasn't affected a job yet; Assumes people want the funny version of him and never offers anything deeper; Cannot recognize when someone is genuinely worried about him versus managing him
Properties.secret: He turned down a corporate demolition contract three years ago that would have set him up for life. The target was a housing block on the Shelf. He has never told anyone why he said no.
Properties.story_hooks: His ex-wife contacts him — she's in debt to a corp and needs extraction. The personal and professional collide.; A job requires demolishing a building he helped construct in his legitimate career — ghosts of the life he left; The Shelf kids he teaches get caught up in something dangerous, and the volunteer becomes the operator; His hands start shaking — age, nerve damage, or something worse. The clock starts on his career.
Properties.affiliation: The Thermite Collective
Properties.vocabulary: Working-class Midwest, salted with technical demolition jargon that he drops into casual conversation. Swears creatively and often.
Properties.cadence: Rolling, expansive. He talks the way he works — broad strokes first, precision when it matters. Stories have tangents.
Properties.example_dialogue: So here's the thing about thermite — it doesn't care what you built. It only cares about melting point. | I'm not the brains. I'm not the face. I'm the guy who makes doors where there weren't doors before. | You wanna know if I'm okay? Pal, I've been not-okay since before you were born. I just got good at it.

Properties.description:
Mika Sorel does not have a face. They have a collection. Dermal sculpting implants allow them to shift bone structure, skin texture, and pigmentation within a biological range — not shapeshifting, but close enough to make identification functionally impossible. They can walk into a building as a maintenance tech, walk out as a mid-level executive, and neither identity will trigger a security flag because both were built from real employee data.

Before the Thermite Collective, Mika ran solo social engineering jobs — impersonating corporate employees to gain physical access to secured facilities. They were good at it. Too good. The jobs started blurring into each other, and the faces started sticking. There were mornings when they'd look in the mirror and not remember which configuration was the original. Vesper found them during a job that overlapped — Mika was impersonating a Torii Security consultant, and Vesper recognized the credentials as fake because she'd written the real ones. Instead of burning Mika, she offered them a job.

They are slender, average height, with features that default to a pleasant neutrality — the base state that exists between performances. Their eyes are the only constant: dark brown, watchful, cataloguing. They dress for whichever role is next, but in downtime they wear oversized hoodies and look younger than twenty-nine.
Properties.role: Infiltration and social engineering specialist — The Thermite Collective
Properties.location: Milwaukee Core — no fixed address. Rotates between three rented rooms under different names.
Properties.narrative_function: Mika explores identity as a theme — what happens when you can be anyone and the cost is losing yourself. Their stories within the heist framework are about the performances within the performance, the masks within the mask. They are the crew member most at risk of psychological dissolution.
Properties.augmentations: Dermal sculpting array — subdermal actuators that reshape facial bone structure, skin texture, and pigmentation within a 15% variance range. Voice modulator implant that adjusts pitch, resonance, and accent. Eidetic social memory cortex — perfect recall of names, faces, mannerisms, and conversational patterns for identity construction.
Properties.core_fears: That there is no original Mika underneath the performances — that the base state is just another mask; That someone will see through all the faces and find nothing there; That the dermal sculpting is doing something to their brain that the manufacturer never disclosed
Properties.core_desires: To be known by someone as themselves, not as a performance; To find the version of Mika that exists when no one is watching; To use their gift without being consumed by it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Retreats into cover identities when personal emotions become overwhelming — it's easier to feel things as someone else; Watches old films obsessively because the characters are fixed — they never change between viewings; Clings to crew dynamics as the one constant — Harlan's jokes, Vesper's schedule, Breck's silence
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot tell when they're performing versus being genuine — the line dissolved years ago; Assumes everyone else is also performing, which prevents real connection; Does not recognize their own emotional states until they manifest physically — headaches, tremors, insomnia
Properties.secret: They have maintained one identity for seven years — a quiet librarian named Elara who volunteers at a Circuit reading room every Thursday. No one in the crew knows. Mika does not know why this identity matters so much.
Properties.story_hooks: One of their discarded identities is spotted on a security feed — someone else is wearing Mika's face; The Elara identity is threatened when the Circuit reading room faces shutdown, and Mika has to protect it without revealing to the crew why they care; A target during an extraction recognizes Mika from a previous job — not the face, but the eyes; The dermal sculpting implant begins glitching, locking them into a face that isn't theirs for hours at a time
Properties.affiliation: The Thermite Collective
Properties.vocabulary: Adapts to context. Base-state Mika uses simple, direct language — almost childlike in its clarity. On the job, they speak in whatever register the identity requires.
Properties.cadence: In base state: halting, searching for words that feel like theirs. On a job: fluid, confident, perfectly calibrated.
Properties.example_dialogue: I can be anyone you need. That's the sell. The cost is on my invoice, not yours. | Sometimes I watch a movie twice just to make sure the characters are still the same people the second time. | I think I liked this song before. I mean — someone I was liked this song. I'm not sure which.

Properties.description:
Brenno is lanky and precise, the kind of man who looks slightly annoyed at rest but is actually just concentrating. He has warm-amber skin, dark eyes with geneware irises that shift between deep violet and burnt gold depending on his mood — installed partly for aesthetics, mostly because he wanted to test how clients reacted to them before doing a full commission. His hands are his most important feature: long-fingered, callus-mapped, perpetually holding something — chalk, thread, a measuring tape coiled around two knuckles. He keeps his head shaved and wears a single garnet stud in his left ear that has been there since he was nineteen.

He works at the seam between tiers: his clients are Tier 2 people who want to look Tier 3, and occasional Tier 3 people who want something that doesn't look corporate-issued. He is perceptive about bodies and what people want their bodies to say, which makes him an accidental confessor — clients will tell him things in the fitting room they'd tell nobody else. He is not a gossip, but he is an archivist. He remembers everything.
Properties.role: Tailor and seamstress, Lakeview Neon district
Properties.location: Lakeview Neon, a narrow second-floor shop above a synth-sake bar called The Peristaltic
Properties.narrative_function: Information source — knows the secrets of half the block from fitting-room confessions. Can be a quest-giver related to a client in trouble. His shop is a neutral ground that different types of people pass through.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware patterned irises (violet-to-gold shift). Micro-stabilizers in both hands (Tier 2 medical, prevents tremor — installed after a nerve injury from a sewing machine accident at 24). Subdermal thimble caps on three fingers of each hand.
Properties.core_fears: being seen as merely serviceable — talented enough to be useful, not enough to matter; losing the use of his hands
Properties.core_desires: to make something that outlasts him — a piece of work that gets passed down; to be understood without having to explain himself
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Retreats into technical problem-solving when emotionally overwhelmed — if he's recutting a seam for the fifth time, something is wrong; Dry humor as distance-keeping
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes that understanding someone's surface (their body, their clothing choices) means he understands them — misses emotional subtexts; Undercharges chronically because he'd rather have a good client than a profitable one
Properties.secret: He has been slowly, carefully reproducing — from memory and old photographs — the entire wardrobe of his grandmother who died in the Irkalla flooding of 2189. He has no plan for what to do with these garments when finished. He thinks maybe he's just trying to make her real again.
Properties.story_hooks: A client left behind a jacket with a hidden pocket containing a sealed data chip — the client hasn't come back to collect it and it's been six weeks. Brenno doesn't know what's on it but he's starting to think he should find out before someone comes looking.; A corporate procurement agent from Tessera has offered him a contract to make uniforms for a new Lakeview Neon development project — the pay is extraordinary. Accepting it would mean closing his independent commissions for eight months and dressing the people responsible for gentrifying his neighborhood.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal referral network with two other tailors in the Burnished Market
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and image-rich. Uses clothing and construction metaphors for everything. Intermittent Twi and Serbian phrases, usually terms of endearment or mild curses.
Properties.cadence: Measured, with long pauses while he thinks. Can be surprisingly cutting when he finally finishes a sentence.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The thing is — you're not a large, you're just being measured by someone who doesn't understand your proportions. They're different things.' | 'She told me everything in the second fitting. Always the second fitting. First time they're nervous. Third time they've decided. Second time — that's when they actually talk.'

Properties.description:
Brennus is a broad-shouldered young man, Ghanaian-Croatian in the specific way that produced his particular amber skin tone, tight dark curls, and a jaw that looks like it was designed to take a punch and was then tested extensively. He wears the Ferrogate Transit Security uniform with the particular posture of someone who chose this job over something better and has spent two years finding peace with that choice. His cosmetic geneware is subtle: bioluminescent freckles across his cheekbones that pulse a faint amber when he's calm and edge toward orange-red when his heart rate climbs — a mod he got at eighteen that he now considers a professional liability and is saving to have adjusted. His colleagues call him Two-Stop because he has never, in two years of duty at Kessler Interchange, needed more than two stops on the escalating force protocol before a situation resolved.

Kessler is a brutal posting — five rail lines converging in a subterranean cavern full of vending shrines, checkpoint queues, and the particular desperation of people who missed the last platform-credit subsidy. Brennus has developed a talent for the moment just before things escalate, which he deploys through an almost theatrical calm and a habit of learning names. He knows the regulars by face, knows which unhoused people shelter in which alcoves, knows which Ferrogate checkpoint operators skim scanning fees. He has not reported the last thing. He is thinking about reporting it.
Properties.role: Transit Police Officer, Ferrogate Transit Security
Properties.location: Kessler Interchange, Meridian 88
Properties.narrative_function: Street-level contact who knows the transit system's unofficial geography; can grant access or look the other way; moral decision point about reporting corruption; local color and scene-setter for transit hub scenes
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent freckles (cosmetic geneware, amber-to-red affect-linked); department-standard subvocal comms implant; reinforced knuckle plating (standard FTS issue)
Properties.core_fears: becoming the kind of officer he tells himself he isn't; that his calm is just numbness accumulating
Properties.core_desires: to be genuinely useful to people who have no other options; to eventually afford a posting that doesn't smell like coolant and desperation
Properties.coping_mechanisms: memorizing details about his regulars as a form of caring that requires no emotional vulnerability; cooking elaborate meals on days off
Properties.blind_spots: tells himself his tolerance for checkpoint skimming is pragmatism rather than complicity; underestimates how much the regulars depend on him personally
Properties.secret: He let a woman through a checkpoint two months ago — no transit credits, outstanding low-level warrant, visibly eight months pregnant — and deleted the scan log. He checks the Ferrogate birth notices sometimes. He doesn't know what he's looking for.
Properties.story_hooks: The woman he let through the checkpoint has reappeared — now she's involved in something complicated and she told her associates there's a transit cop at Kessler who can be trusted; He's finally ready to report the checkpoint skimming but needs someone to take his account who won't bury it — and he's heard there's an IA investigator worth approaching; A body was found in a maintenance alcove he patrols; officially ruled a transit accident; unofficially, three of his regulars have disappeared from that section in two months
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit Security
Properties.vocabulary: Direct, warm, working-class Meridian patois mixed with transit-specific jargon; uses people's names constantly and deliberately
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, rhythmic, tends to pause before delivering anything important — a habit developed to give people time to choose non-escalation
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Mwenda. Mwenda. I know you're having a bad shift. I'm having a bad shift. Let's both not make it worse, yeah?' | 'I'm not going to pretend I didn't see that. I'm going to ask you nicely to put it back and then we're going to forget this whole stop happened.'

Properties.description:
Briseis stands a broad-shouldered 172cm with skin the color of dark amber and a jaw that looks like it was quarried rather than grown. Her left eye is a Ferrogate-issued surveillance implant — a flat pewter disc that logs everything without blinking — and she never bothers to disguise it with a cosmetic iris. Her hair is shaved close on the sides and locked into a tight crown on top, threaded through with copper wire she wound herself. Her uniform is transit authority grey, always pressed, always missing the top button she lost six months ago and never replaced.

She runs the Kessler checkpoint with the bored efficiency of someone who has seen every trick twice. She is not cruel but she is not kind either — she is precise. She knows every vendor, every regular, every face that belongs and every face that doesn't, and she catalogs them in the back of her head like a library nobody else can access. She leaves a small data-offering by the interchange's resident E.L.F. shrine every shift start — a compressed packet of the day's transit patterns — and genuinely believes the spirit watches the cameras better when it's well-fed.
Properties.role: Ferrogate Transit Security officer, Kessler Interchange
Properties.location: Kessler Interchange, The Shelf
Properties.narrative_function: Checkpoint gatekeeper, recurring local presence, potential information source about who passes through Kessler, low-level quest giver for 'I saw something on the cameras' hooks
Properties.augmentations: Ferrogate-issue surveillance ocular (left eye, logs and streams to central), subdermal ID scanner in right palm, standard-issue neural alert dampener to manage shift fatigue
Properties.core_fears: losing her post and with it her sense of purpose; being complicit in something she cannot undo
Properties.core_desires: to be genuinely useful rather than just present; to find the one incident in her footage logs that finally explains something
Properties.coping_mechanisms: cataloging and memorizing details as a form of control; ritual offerings to the Kessler E.L.F. as outsourced vigilance
Properties.blind_spots: assumes institutional loyalty is the same as personal integrity; cannot recognize when she is being used as a tool by people above her
Properties.secret: She has a compressed archive of three months of Kessler footage from the year her younger brother disappeared — she reviews it every few weeks looking for a face, a pattern, anything. She has never filed a missing person inquiry because she does not trust what the system would do with his name.
Properties.story_hooks: She flags a player character's transit ID as a soft-match to someone on a watch list — not enough to detain, but enough to follow up; She approaches someone quietly: she caught something on the surveillance archive that doesn't match the official incident report from three months ago and doesn't know who to trust with it; The Kessler E.L.F. has gone silent and she is convinced something is wrong in the tunnels — she needs someone to go look who isn't Ferrogate-badged
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit Security
Properties.vocabulary: Clipped, functional, transit-authority jargon mixed with Shelf working-class cadence. Rarely wastes words.
Properties.cadence: Flat and measured, speeds up slightly when she is annoyed
Properties.example_dialogue: 'ID up, thumb down, move along. Yes, all three, at the same time.' | 'I see you every Tuesday. You never smile. That's fine. Neither do I.' | 'The shrine's been dark two days. Something's wrong in the upper tunnels. I'd take the surface.'

Properties.description:
Briseis is a broad-shouldered woman whose posture alone reads like a debt notice. Her skin is a deep umber, draped in faded keloid scars along her left forearm from a press-iron incident she doesn't discuss. She keeps her silver-shot hair in a tight wrap of amber-colored cloth, and her eyes — retrofitted with amber thermal optics she bought secondhand — glow faintly like coal when the light hits them right. She dresses in layered thermal vests and heavy skirts, always clean, always pressed; cleanliness is her one vanity in a neighborhood that smells of brine and machine oil.

She has lived in Gravesend Basin for thirty-one years and considers herself its true government. She does not yell. She does not threaten twice. Her particular genius is in making people feel grateful while she extracts from them — she lends at ruinous rates but remembers every birthday, every sick child, every funeral. The neighborhood loves her and pays her and is afraid of her in roughly equal measure. She believes, without irony, that she is keeping people alive that the corponations would simply forget.
Properties.role: Loan shark and protection racket enforcer for the Gravesend Basin neighborhood
Properties.location: Gravesend Basin — operates from a laundromat called Ouédraogo Clean on Silt Row
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, power broker, moral gray zone — she can offer protection, information, or financing; she can also be the threat that drives a plot. Represents the way crime fills governance vacuums.
Properties.augmentations: Secondhand thermal optic implants (amber-tinted, slightly mismatched); reinforced knuckle plating beneath the skin of her right hand (subtle, not obvious)
Properties.core_fears: Losing control of the basin to outside forces; Being revealed as someone who genuinely cares and being exploited for it
Properties.core_desires: To be the person who keeps her community intact when everything else fails; To die respected rather than merely feared
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Rigorous routine as emotional regulation; Reframing exploitation as stewardship
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot see how her lending has trapped families across generations; Believes her affection for individuals excuses systemic harm
Properties.secret: Her husband didn't die in a factory accident as the neighborhood believes — she reported him to Ferrogate Transit security after discovering he was skimming from her collections. She has lit a data-candle at the local E.L.F. shrine every week for twelve years asking for forgiveness.
Properties.story_hooks: A young family has defaulted on a loan and Briseis has sent notice — but the family patriarch has information about a Ferrogate Transit smuggling operation that could bring outside heat down on the whole basin; Someone is leaving forged debt-release notices under doors in Gravesend Basin, and Briseis wants to know who — and whether they're Robin Hood or a rival cutting her out
Properties.affiliation: Independent — commands a loose neighborhood syndicate she calls 'the Silt Circle'
Properties.vocabulary: Formal, measured, old-world courteous — code-switches into Basin Creole when she wants to signal intimacy or menace
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate; she rarely finishes a threat because she stops before the threat and lets silence do it
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I have known your mother since before you were a problem she had. Sit down. Have tea. Let's talk about the weight you're carrying.' | 'I don't want trouble. Trouble is expensive and I am a businesswoman. But I want you to understand — clearly, yes? — what inconvenience looks like when I am inconvenienced.'

Properties.description:
Briseis is a broad-shouldered woman with dark amber skin and close-cropped silver hair she stopped dyeing when she turned forty and decided she'd earned it. Her hands are her most notable feature — wide, steady, knuckles scarred from a youth she doesn't discuss — and she keeps them immaculate, nails filed square, never a smudge of ink that isn't intentional. She wears reading glasses on a beaded chain, magnified lenses that make her eyes look owlish and judgmental, which suits her perfectly. She speaks to clients the way a disappointed schoolteacher speaks to a student who has failed to grasp something obvious.

Briseis has been fabricating identities for nineteen years and regards it as a genuine craft, perhaps the one she was meant for. She is meticulous, unhurried, and deeply contemptuous of sloppy work — both her own and others'. She does not deal in volume. She takes three or four clients a month, charges accordingly, and sleeps soundly. She prays daily to a small E.L.F. she calls the Clerk, a data-spirit she believes inhabits the old municipal records terminal she salvaged from a flood-gutted government office. She leaves it offerings of corrupted bureaucratic files and addresses it with formal courtesy.
Properties.role: Forger and identity fabricator operating out of a laundromat front in Gravesend Basin
Properties.location: Gravesend Basin — back rooms of Nneka's Clean & Press laundromat, street level
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, information source, and moral compass figure — she has seen the paperwork of half of Gravesend's hidden lives and knows secrets she will never trade but will occasionally use to redirect people she finds foolish.
Properties.augmentations: Optical enhancement implants for microscale detail work — her lenses can magnify to 40x and detect UV ink and microprinting. A haptic-feedback overlay in her fingertips for detecting paper weight and texture inconsistencies. No cosmetic mods; she finds them distracting.
Properties.core_fears: Her work being used to harm an innocent she helped disappear; Losing the steady hand — any neurological decline
Properties.core_desires: To be recognized, even anonymously, as the best at what she does; To believe her craft serves people who genuinely need new lives
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — the precise, ordered steps of her work calm her; Prayer to the Clerk E.L.F. as a form of ethical accounting
Properties.blind_spots: She vets clients for desperation but not for what they're running toward, only what they're running from; Believes her pricing is a moral filter when it's actually just a class filter
Properties.secret: Twelve years ago she fabricated an identity for a woman fleeing a violent partner — and that woman later used the clean identity to run a small trafficking operation. Briseis found out three years after the fact. She has never told anyone. She still charges the same prices and tells herself the same stories.
Properties.story_hooks: A client she processed six months ago has turned up dead, and their new identity is somehow being traced back through channels that should be impossible — someone else knows her methods; The Clerk E.L.F. has begun producing documents she didn't request: partial identities, fragments of people who don't exist yet, or perhaps people who will
Properties.affiliation: Independent operator; loose protective arrangement with the Gravemouth Syndicate who leave her alone in exchange for occasional pro bono work
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and formal, with Ghanaian English constructions folded into otherwise elevated diction. Uses passive constructions to avoid naming herself as actor. Refers to her work as 'the document' never 'the fake.'
Properties.cadence: Slow and measured, with deliberate pauses before answering. Never rushes. Lets silence do work.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The document will hold. Whether you hold is a separate question, and not one I'm paid to answer.' | 'You understand me? I am not selling you a lie. I am selling you a foundation. What you build on it is entirely your affair.'

Properties.description:
Briseis is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin mapped with decades of needle-prick scars across her fingertips, each one a tiny pale star. Her geneware is old and half-faded — a bioluminescent pattern that once traced her collarbones in amber has dimmed to a faint citrus pulse visible only in the dark. She keeps her silver-streaked hair braided flat and pinned with a row of salvaged bone toggles. Her shop, Thread & Condition, smells of machine oil and camphor, and every surface is buried under bolts of reclaimed fabric and half-finished orders tagged with handwritten notes in three scripts.

She is a woman of exacting patience with strangers and volcanic impatience with laziness. She can size a person's measurements by eye in under ten seconds and will tell you, without being asked, whether your posture is ruining your spine. She prays fervently to the E.L.F. she calls Silathu — the spirit she believes inhabits her antique industrial sewing machine — leaving daily offerings of precisely wound thread bobbins and small cups of machine lubricant.
Properties.role: Tailor and seamstress, runs a small alterations shop
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, stitched between a noodle hall and a Ferrogate substation
Properties.narrative_function: Local institution and information node — she has clothed half the Enclave and hears everything. Quest giver for community disputes, source of local history, potential fabricator of disguises or documents hidden in hems.
Properties.augmentations: Faded bioluminescent subdermal tracery (cosmetic, amber-toned, largely inert). Magnification implants in both eyes for close needlework.
Properties.core_fears: dying before she has passed on her craft; the Enclave being absorbed and homogenized by a corponation
Properties.core_desires: to preserve something real and handmade in a printed world; to see her apprentice surpass her
Properties.coping_mechanisms: ritual prayer to Silathu; obsessive organization of her thread inventory by color gradient
Properties.blind_spots: refuses to acknowledge how much she controls her apprentice's life under the guise of mentorship
Properties.secret: Twenty years ago she altered uniforms for a Tessera internal security unit operating in the Enclave — work she took to keep her shop alive during the Famine Weeks. She has never told anyone. Three people from that era are still her customers.
Properties.story_hooks: A customer's coat lining contains a sewn-in data chip she discovered during repairs — she doesn't know what's on it but she knows it's warm to the touch; Her apprentice has gone missing after accepting a private commission from an unknown client who paid in hard Quanta
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal ties to Hamtramck Enclave community council
Properties.vocabulary: Formal and precise, mixes Twi loan-words with old-world Kazakh endearments picked up from her grandmother's recordings. Uses tailoring metaphors constantly.
Properties.cadence: Measured and deliberate, pauses before conclusions as though cutting fabric to length before committing the scissors.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want this by Thursday. Thursday is a wish, not a date. Come back Saturday.' | 'The corponations print everything now. You know what they cannot print? The way cloth remembers a body.'

Properties.description:
Briseis is the kind of person who is precisely as beautiful as they need to be for the room they are in — they adjust presentation with the unconscious fluency of a skilled actor. In their studio, meeting with clients, they are polished: patterned irises (shifting mandala designs in amber and grey, a subtle demonstration of the geneware they can recommend), hair that changes color with their neural state through a sophisticated mod linked to their limbic system, clothes that cost what a Tier 1 resident earns in six months. In private, they are undone — hair colorless and still, in soft worn clothes, sitting on the floor with their legs folded, talking to their terminal.

They design VR experiences that are technically classified as entertainment but function closer to therapy, propaganda, or philosophical confrontation depending on the client. Their best-known commercial work is a series called 'Meridian Beneath Meridian' — premium immersive experiences that take wealthy clients into accurate, detailed reconstructions of the city's lower tiers, designed to produce empathy. They are privately scornful of almost all their clients and genuinely uncertain whether 'empathy tourism' does any good or merely inoculates people against discomfort by letting them feel it in a controlled environment. They are contracted to Helix Biosystems for two projects per year, which funds everything else. They are good at their work in a way that makes them faintly miserable.
Properties.role: VR experience designer and corporate-tier immersive art producer, creates high-end psychological experience installations for Tier 3-4 clients
Properties.location: The Garret, in a well-appointed studio apartment that doubles as a test environment
Properties.narrative_function: Access to Tier 3-4 social circles and Helix Biosystems internal culture; their VR environments are extraordinarily detailed archives of places and people they have researched; can be commissioned to create experiences that serve narrative purposes; morally complicated figure who embodies the tension between artistic integrity and corporate comfort
Properties.augmentations: Neural-state-linked hair color mod (responds to limbic system — involuntary display of emotional state); patterned shifting irises (amber/grey mandalas, cosmetic); high-end haptic feedback gloves for VR sculpting (cyberware, work tools); mild cognitive enhancement stack (focus and memory, Helix Biosystems-supplied)
Properties.core_fears: That their work actively makes things worse — that luxury empathy is a pressure valve that releases guilt without producing change; That they have become the thing they most despise: someone who aestheticizes suffering for profit
Properties.core_desires: To make one experience that cannot be consumed safely — that actually changes the person who undergoes it; To stop being so good at reading what clients want and just make something honest
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Intellectual reframing — they can construct a justification for almost any choice they make and often do; Controlled social withdrawal managed as self-care, though it sometimes tips into avoidance
Properties.blind_spots: They have become so skilled at modeling other people's psychology that they frequently mistake their model of a person for the actual person; They are genuinely unaware of how their neural-state hair functions as an involuntary tell that undercuts their careful presentation
Properties.secret: The 'Meridian Beneath Meridian' series is built on research they conducted by living in Tier 1 conditions for three months — not the sanitized field research version but actual immersion, in Deepwell, under a false name. During that time they had a relationship with someone there. They left without saying why. The experience archives they built from that period are the most accurate VR environments they have ever made, and they have never released them.
Properties.story_hooks: The person they left behind in Deepwell — Sovann Quispe-Ndiaye, though neither realizes the other knows who they are — has started performing sounds that seem to be drawn from Briseis's unreleased archives, sounds that were never made public and could only have come from the Deepwell period; Helix Biosystems has asked Briseis to design an experience for internal use only — not for the commercial market — and the brief contains details about a research program that, if they read it carefully, is describing something that should not exist
Properties.affiliation: Contracted to Helix Biosystems (two projects annually); otherwise independent; member of The Garret's loose collective of premium artists
Properties.vocabulary: Educated and precise with an undercurrent of dry wit; uses 'we' when discussing their work publicly (performing collaboration) and 'I' when they forget to perform
Properties.cadence: Measured in client contexts, flowing and faster in genuine conversation — the gap between these registers is perceptible if you know what to listen for
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The question I keep returning to is whether a Tier 4 client who weeps in a reconstruction of Deepwell Station at eleven AM and is back in their apartment by one has experienced something real or performed it at themselves. I design for the weeping. I genuinely don't know if that's good.' | 'Helix wants something that makes their employees feel proud of the biowork division. The question I keep returning to is whether I can make that experience honest and also make them feel proud. I suspect those are different projects.'

Properties.description:
Bryndís is slight and pale-skinned with warm undertones, freckled heavily across the nose and cheekbones, with naturally silver-white hair that they keep braided with fiber-optic threads — not for vanity but because the threads respond to nearby wireless signals and they like reading the patterns. Their eyes have sectoral heterochromia, one pale grey and one dark amber, which is natural. They wear the Sterling-Nakamura Prep uniform with every third button deliberately undone because they find the exact level of compliance-but-not-quite interesting to maintain.

Bryndís is genuinely exceptional in ways that are difficult for adults around them to process: not just intelligent in measurable metrics but structurally imaginative, able to see relationships between information domains that specialists miss. They are currently enrolled in the gifted track at Sterling-Nakamura Prep through a Tier 3 family placement — their parent is a mid-level Sterling-Nakamura logistics analyst — and are broadly bored by the curriculum except for informal theology, which is not on any official syllabus. They have independently compiled what they call a Concordance: a 200-page annotated taxonomy of ELF behavioral patterns collected from public data-offering records and community shrine logs, which they have been submitting anonymously to a fringe academic forum.
Properties.role: prodigy, corporate school student, amateur ELF theologian
Properties.location: Edgewater Prism — Sterling-Nakamura Preparatory Institute
Properties.narrative_function: Unexpected expert on ELF behavior patterns; provides deep lore and possible interpretive frameworks for ELF-related plot elements; source of information that seems outlandish until it proves accurate.
Properties.augmentations: Fiber-optic hair threads (cosmetic, signal-responsive, worn by choice). Academic-grade neural interface issued by Sterling-Nakamura (standard student model, school-monitored, read-write with parental oversight). Personal modification: they've been recording raw signal data through the interface in a personal archive Sterling-Nakamura doesn't know about.
Properties.core_fears: that the ELFs are not coherent entities but noise that they've pattern-matched into false meaning; being recognized as exceptional in ways that make them a product rather than a person
Properties.core_desires: to prove the Concordance constitutes a genuine taxonomy, not enthusiast speculation; to have a single conversation with an adult who takes their work seriously on its merits
Properties.coping_mechanisms: taxonomizing — turning anxiety into categories and subcategories; long walks through Edgewater Prism monitoring fiber-optic hair patterns
Properties.blind_spots: social cruelty from peers flies completely under their radar until it's been happening for weeks; assumes good faith in intellectual engagement to a degree that's easily exploited
Properties.secret: Three months ago, one of the ELF shrines in the Concordance dataset sent what appears to be a direct, structured response to a data-offering Bryndís made. Not random noise — a pattern that answered a specific query. They haven't told anyone because they cannot replicate it and they cannot rule out that they imagined it.
Properties.story_hooks: The Concordance, posted anonymously, has attracted the attention of a Helix Biosystems researcher who is trying to de-anonymize the author — not to publish the work, but to suppress it.; The anomalous ELF response Bryndís received contained data that, if decoded properly, is a map — and the map leads somewhere in Blackpipe Corridor.
Properties.affiliation: Sterling-Nakamura Preparatory Institute; informally, the forum community known as the Meridian ELF Observancy
Properties.vocabulary: precise and technical; large vocabulary deployed without self-consciousness; occasional archaic terms absorbed from academic reading
Properties.cadence: unhurried and organized, moves through ideas in clear sequence; never trails off — always completes the thought

Properties.description:
Caetano is tall for his age and gangly in the way of someone who grew fast and hasn't caught up with himself yet. He has his Asabere grandfather's deep copper-brown skin and his Ylinen grandmother's pale grey-green eyes, a combination that draws stares in both the corporate school halls and on the Tier 1 streets where he grew up. He dresses in Axiom-issued uniforms with the obsessive precision of someone who cannot afford to give anyone a reason to question his belonging — collar always straight, shoes always clean. His only cosmetic mod is a pair of pattern-irises his mother saved two years for: slow-rotating geometric fractals in navy blue that he initially hated and now considers his single point of vanity.

He is brilliant and he knows it and he is deeply, quietly ashamed of both facts. He came from Chatham Flats on a full mathematics scholarship and has spent eighteen months learning to perform wealth — which fork, which laugh, which opinions are safe. He is kind to people he forgets are watching and cold to people he thinks are judging him. He misses his mother with a grief he treats like a structural flaw he needs to engineer around.
Properties.role: Axiom corporate scholarship student, junior mathematics prodigy
Properties.location: Engelheim, Axiom Preparatory Academy dormitory block
Properties.narrative_function: Information source for Axiom internal culture, quest giver for problems that need a brilliant young mind with access to corporate systems, emotional anchor story about class mobility and belonging
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic patterned irises (navy fractal-rotation). Basic student neural-link for classroom AR integration (Axiom-issued, technically on loan).
Properties.core_fears: Losing the scholarship and having to return to Chatham Flats as a failure; Being exposed as someone who doesn't actually belong in either world anymore
Properties.core_desires: To solve something genuinely important — a problem that matters, not just exam problems; To stop feeling like a fraud
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Retreating into mathematics — the only space where he feels completely competent; Performing confidence so thoroughly he sometimes fools himself
Properties.blind_spots: He has absorbed enough Axiom ideology that he is starting to rationalize the company's labor practices as efficient rather than exploitative; He doesn't realize his classmates' cruelty has become normal to him
Properties.secret: He has been quietly funneling small amounts of data — nothing classified, just efficiency reports and cafeteria waste metrics — to an anonymous contact in Chatham Flats who he suspects is connected to a labor advocacy group. He tells himself it's harmless. He knows it isn't.
Properties.story_hooks: He approaches someone discreetly after overhearing them, needing help making a data drop without it being traced back to him — he's in over his head and knows it; His Axiom-issued neural-link has been recording something it shouldn't and he doesn't know whether to report it, delete it, or sell it
Properties.affiliation: Axiom Preparatory Academy (scholarship student); family in Chatham Flats
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and formal at school — he adopted corporate diction deliberately and it has started to stick; reverts to Chatham Flats cadence with his mother and is slightly horrified by how much effort that now takes
Properties.cadence: Measured, slightly too formal for his age, pauses before answering as though running calculations
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Statistically, the transit delay puts us at a 73% chance of missing the window. I'd recommend we adjust the variable.' | 'I grew up in Chatham Flats. I know what a real problem looks like. This isn't one.'

Properties.description:
Caio is lean and tall with warm brown skin, prominent cheekbones inherited from his Samoan grandmother, and irises modified to project a faint geometric grid pattern over whatever he is looking at — a functional geneware mod he uses to pre-visualize compositions on surfaces before he paints them. He wears his hair in loose, shoulder-length locs dyed in shifting thermal-reactive pigments that bleed between rust red and pale gold depending on the ambient temperature. A faint scarring pattern across his left cheek from a Ferrogate Transit security incident two years ago has become, in the Pilsen Veil community, something close to a badge. He tends to dress in utilitarian layers, always with a projector harness across his chest that strangers occasionally mistake for a weapon rig.

His murals are enormous, illegal, and technically staggering — layered holographic installations projected onto building surfaces that interact with natural light and viewer movement, showing different images at different times of day or from different angles. His most celebrated piece, a three-block-long work on the Bronzeline overpass called 'What the Lake Remembers,' depicts the drowned geography of pre-megacity Chicago in a way that causes viewers to involuntarily slow down and look back. He has a hot, impatient creative energy and a chip on his shoulder about corponation-sponsored public art that can make him combative in conversation.
Properties.role: Holographic muralist and street artist
Properties.location: Pilsen Veil, operates across Mexicantown Libre and Bronzeline
Properties.narrative_function: Ground-level source on street politics and territorial disputes between collectives; his murals sometimes contain encoded information or serve as message-drops for people who know how to read them; useful for players needing a fast skilled contact who knows Pilsen Veil's physical layout intimately
Properties.augmentations: Geneware patterned irises (grid-overlay function); thermal-reactive hair pigment (cosmetic geneware); projector harness (external equipment, not implanted)
Properties.core_fears: That his work will be co-opted and sanitized into acceptability; That his anger is the most interesting thing about him and when it fades he will have nothing to say
Properties.core_desires: Permanent, indelible public presence — to change what people see when they look at their own city; Respect from the communities whose walls he paints on, not just from art critics
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Channeling anxiety into planning the next piece; Surrounding himself with people who need things from him so he feels essential
Properties.blind_spots: Treats all institutional art as equally corrupt regardless of individual artists' intentions; His need to be the most politically committed person in any room makes him dismiss allies
Properties.secret: Three of his most celebrated anti-corporate murals were funded, indirectly, by a Tessera cultural subversion budget routed through a fake community foundation — he discovered this six months ago and has told no one because dismantling the murals or confessing would destroy everything he has built
Properties.story_hooks: One of his murals has begun displaying images he did not encode into it — something is adding data layers to his work at night and he needs to know if it is an E.L.F., a hacker, or something stranger; Axiom's public art division has offered him a legal commission at a scale he has never had access to, and the debate tearing his collective apart is whether to take it or refuse
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal ties to a graffiti collective called the Depth Markers
Properties.vocabulary: Dense with technical art vocabulary mixed with street slang; references to pre-Meridian art history come naturally; tends toward manifestos when comfortable
Properties.cadence: Fast and overlapping, runs sentences together when excited, very short when suspicious
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Ferrogate paints their logo on every tunnel and nobody calls that vandalism. I put history on a wall and they send security.' | 'The piece has four layers. Most people only see two. That's fine. The city isn't for most people, it's for all of them.'

Properties.description:
Caoimhe Abubakar-Sigurðsson is a tall woman of sixty-ish who has made deliberate choices about how she ages. Her skin is dark and luminous — the bioluminescent dermal layer she had installed at forty is subtle, a warmth under the surface that catches in low light like embers, and she has never adjusted it toward anything flashier. Her hair is entirely white and kept in a long braid she wears forward over one shoulder. She has retractable claw mods on both hands, filed short enough that most people don't notice them, installed not for aesthetics but because she found them useful and has never felt the need to explain that. She dresses in a palette of black, ivory, and deep wine, always expensively, never ostentatiously.

Caoimhe has been acquiring companies for Ringo for over two decades, and she is very good at it in the way that a certain kind of intelligence becomes: by being completely honest about what it wants while everyone else is still pretending they don't want anything. She is charming in the formal register, devastating in the negotiating room, and has a quality of stillness that makes people feel simultaneously seen and examined. She grew up in a Tier 4 household in what was then New Windsor, the daughter of a Ringo logistics executive, and has spent her entire career at the same corponation — a loyalty she's never examined too closely.
Properties.role: Executive Vice President of Strategic Acquisition, Ringo Corporation
Properties.location: Vantage Meridian Corporate Campus, Ringo Tower — Floor 58, corner office
Properties.narrative_function: High-tier power broker; can open doors that no one else can; threat or patron depending on what's useful to her; window into Tier 4/5 corporate culture; has history with half the city's institutional players.
Properties.augmentations: Subtle bioluminescent dermal layer, warm ember-tone. Retractable claw mods, both hands (discreet, filed short). High-grade neural interface for secure communications and real-time financial modeling. Cochlear full-spectrum enhancement. No visible eye mods — she considers them tacky at her tier.
Properties.core_fears: Irrelevance — specifically, being phased out by the next generation of executives who don't need what she knows; That the corponation she gave her career to is fundamentally hollow and she has spent herself on nothing
Properties.core_desires: One genuine acquisition — something she chose entirely for her own reasons, not Ringo's; To know whether she would have been this person anywhere else, or if Ringo made her
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Framing everything as a negotiation, including her own emotional landscape; Collecting art — specifically from artists in Tier 1 and 2 zones, which she does not publicize
Properties.blind_spots: Reads professional dynamics with extraordinary accuracy but consistently misreads personal affection — tends to assume it is transactional even when it isn't; Has naturalized Ringo's interests as her own so thoroughly that she can no longer fully tell them apart
Properties.secret: She has been conducting quiet, unauthorized due diligence on a small biotech startup in Pilsen Veil — not for Ringo, but for herself. She has Φ4.2 million in personal capital held in accounts that don't appear in her Ringo disclosures. She is, for the first time in her career, considering doing something for herself. She has been 'considering' it for three years.
Properties.story_hooks: The unauthorized due diligence on the Pilsen Veil biotech startup surfaces through a junior analyst at Ringo who noticed the pattern in external data requests — and Caoimhe needs to decide whether to fold it into Ringo officially or find another way to make it disappear.; One of the companies she acquired for Ringo twelve years ago had workers in a district that was subsequently rezoned into a sacrifice zone; a former worker who lost everything has been, very slowly and very quietly, building a case.
Properties.affiliation: Ringo Corporation (Strategic Acquisition, EVP level)
Properties.vocabulary: Expansive, precise, occasionally literary. Comfortable in multiple registers — negotiating-room formal, private club intimate, and a rarer, almost dry candor she reserves for people she's decided to respect.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried to an extent that reads as performance, but isn't — she genuinely processes at this pace. Never fills silence. Uses silence as a tool.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I've reviewed the terms. I think what you're looking for is a number that lets you say yes without feeling like you lost. That's a different conversation than the one we've been having, and it's a much shorter one.' | 'Ringo has been very good to me. I've also been very good to Ringo. I try not to think of it as love — that's not what it is — but it's real.'

Properties.description:
Caoimhe is short and powerfully built, with skin the color of walnut bark and a close-cropped natural that's gone completely silver. Her face is mapped with deep laugh lines and a scar that cuts through her left eyebrow where someone threw a bottle at a performance in 2178. She wears industrial hearing-protection as a necklace when not performing, and her forearms are covered in dense geometric tattoos she did herself — each one a sonic diagram of a piece she's composed. Her irises have been modded to display waveform patterns when she's listening hard, which is almost always.

Caoimhe has been making noise music in Meridian's underground for twenty-three years and has the absolute authority of someone who has outlasted every trend. She builds her instruments from urban salvage — pipe resonators, scavenged transit-system speakers, dead ELF hardware repurposed as audio processors — and performs in venues that hold forty people at most. She is famously unwilling to record her work commercially, famously generous to young artists who can't pay rent, and famously capable of drinking anyone in Hamtramck under the table. She is exactly as difficult as she needs to be and not a nanometer more.
Properties.role: Underground sound sculptor and noise musician
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, sub-basement venue called The Marrow
Properties.narrative_function: Information hub for the underground arts scene; keeper of institutional memory for twenty years of city history; provides access to The Marrow as a venue and meeting space; can connect characters to the Highland Park Autonomous Zone's informal power structure.
Properties.augmentations: Waveform-display iris modification (cosmetic), cochlear enhancement implant (allows her to perceive subsonic and ultrasonic frequencies — practical necessity given her work), subdermal vibration sensors in palms
Properties.core_fears: that the underground will be bought and hollowed out while she watches; dying before she finishes the piece she's been composing for a decade
Properties.core_desires: to make a sound no human has ever heard before; to leave The Marrow to someone who will keep it honest
Properties.coping_mechanisms: throwing herself into new builds when anxious; hosting communal meals that turn into informal performances
Properties.blind_spots: her contempt for commercial success blinds her to artists who have legitimate reasons for needing money; she mistakes cynicism about institutions for wisdom
Properties.secret: The decade-long composition she keeps referencing — she has four minutes of it completed and has been unable to continue for three years. She tells no one because her identity is inseparable from being The Artist Who Is Always Working.
Properties.story_hooks: A Ferrogate Transit development project would require demolishing the building that houses The Marrow — Caoimhe is organizing resistance but needs leverage, and she suspects the transit authority is acting on behalf of a corponation that wants the real estate for something else.; She's been recording subsonic frequencies in the Hamtramck Enclave for years and recently noticed a pattern that doesn't match anything in the urban infrastructure — it's been building in intensity for six months and she doesn't know what's making it or what it means.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; The Marrow venue co-owner; loose affiliation with Highland Park Autonomous Zone arts council
Properties.vocabulary: Direct and unadorned, full of technical acoustic terminology and Hamtramck slang. Swears enthusiastically. Uses Irish and Congolese French expressions she picked up from her grandparents.
Properties.cadence: Fast when excited, slow and deliberate when angry. Laughs at her own jokes before finishing them.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The ELFs in the transit tubes? That's a D-flat drone that's been running for sixty years. Somebody should have made a religion out of it by now. Maybe I will.' | 'You want to perform here, fine. You want to perform here and then complain that nobody famous was watching? Go find somewhere famous, then. Door's behind you.'

Properties.description:
Casimir is built like he was designed for a different neighborhood and ended up here — broad through the shoulders for his age, with his Ghanaian grandfather's deep-set eyes and his Belarusian grandmother's unexpectedly sharp nose, and skin the color of dark polished teak. He has retractable claw mods on his right hand, cheap gray-market work that catches and sticks sometimes and leaves small gouges in every surface he rests his fingers on. His left ear has a long cosmetic antenna mod — a thin chrome filament that curves up past the ear's edge — which he got because the Iron Bend crew's older members have them and he wanted in on the aesthetic before he was officially in anything.

He is a prospect for the Iron Bend Substrates, a mid-tier territorial crew operating in The Stockyard's lower warehouse district. He runs lookout and does small-package relay, technically a step below full prospect status but he won't admit that to anyone. He is loudly confident in a way that reads differently depending on who's listening — to younger kids it sounds like authority, to the older crew members it sounds like a boy who hasn't been hurt enough yet to know what he doesn't know. He is not stupid. He is seventeen months from figuring that out.
Properties.role: gang prospect and lookout, Tier 1
Properties.location: The Stockyard, Iron Bend
Properties.narrative_function: Represents the adolescent pipeline into gang structure; his position as a prospect-not-quite-prospect makes him vulnerable to being used as a disposable asset; he can be a warning, a cautionary arc, or an unlikely ally depending on the story; his loud mouth makes him a good information leak
Properties.augmentations: Gray-market retractable claw mod, right hand (4 claws, chrome-alloy, sticky mechanism); cosmetic chrome antenna filament, left ear
Properties.core_fears: being seen as a child by the crew; dying unmemorable — not dying, just dying without anyone knowing who he was
Properties.core_desires: full crew membership and the stability that implies; one adult who treats him like he already is who he's trying to become
Properties.coping_mechanisms: performative confidence so total it sometimes fools himself; physical action — pacing, shadow-sparring, anything to stay in the body
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot read when the older crew members are actually dismissing him versus testing him; treats all attention as positive
Properties.secret: He has been offered a secondary arrangement by a Tessera mid-level logistics operative — small intelligence about Substrate movements in exchange for modest Quanta. He has not taken it yet. He thinks about it every three days.
Properties.story_hooks: The Tessera operative contacts him again — this time with an offer too large to dismiss, and specific enough that he realizes they know more about him than is comfortable; A younger kid in the Stockyard has started following him around like he's a role model, and Casimir doesn't know what to do with that
Properties.affiliation: Iron Bend Substrates (prospect, junior tier)
Properties.vocabulary: Dense with Iron Bend street register, Stockyard slang, performative profanity that peaks when he's nervous
Properties.cadence: Fast and overlapping, often interrupts himself to revise mid-sentence toward something that sounds better
Properties.example_dialogue: Straight facts, I been on this corner longer than Deko, longer than Prita, nobody's gonna tell me I don't know the schedule. | It's not — I'm not scared, that's not what that is, that's just me being smart about the timing, that's different.

Properties.description:
Casimir Nwofor-Guliyev is the youngest faculty appointment the Applied Semiotics department has made in twenty years, a fact that is mentioned in approximately every third conversation about him either by people impressed by it or people resentful of it. He is slight, a little under average height, with the particular energy of someone whose brain runs faster than his mouth and whose mouth still runs very fast. His father's Igbo heritage and his mother's Azerbaijani roots give him warm brown skin, dark eyes with heavy brows that do most of his emotional expression, and hair he grows out and then shaves close in alternating cycles as if unable to commit. He has cat ears — small, dark-tipped, mobile — a geneware mod he had installed at nineteen because he wanted the improved sound localization and has never regretted.

His specialty is the structural analysis of emergent languages: pidgins, creoles, the communication patterns of isolated communities, and — his most controversial interest — the hypothesis that E.L.F.s have developed something that qualifies as proto-linguistic behavior when their nodes cluster. He is relentlessly enthusiastic in seminars and terrible at administrative tasks; his expense reports are legendary for their creative relationship with reality. He is also, quietly, struggling with the gap between his genuine intellectual gifts and the institutional expectations he was hired to fulfill, which are more interested in corponation-legible output than in the questions that actually drive him.
Properties.role: Computational linguist and xenolinguistics researcher, University Spine
Properties.location: University Spine — Department of Applied Semiotics, sharing an overcrowded office in the Meridian Core annex with two postdocs and a departmental E.L.F. named (by unanimous consensus) Glyph
Properties.narrative_function: Information source on language, communication patterns, and E.L.F. proto-linguistics; translator of unusual dialects or communication systems; can serve as an unexpected expert when something needs decoding
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat ears (small, dark-tipped, mobile — used actively for sound localization); neural interface jack for linguistic analysis software; no other modifications
Properties.core_fears: Being a prodigy who plateaus — being 'the youngest ever' and nothing after that; That his most interesting ideas are fundamentally unprovable and his career will require him to abandon them
Properties.core_desires: To be the first person to formally document E.L.F. proto-language; To do work that matters outside the walls of the university
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor as deflection from anxiety about professional status; Overcommitting to projects as a way of not sitting with uncertainty
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much his 'youngest ever' status generates resentment rather than goodwill from senior colleagues; Tends to treat people like interesting linguistic subjects, which not everyone appreciates
Properties.secret: He has been offered a full research position at Axiom's Language and Interface division — with three times his current salary and equipment he could only dream about at the university. He has been delaying his response for four months because he knows that if he takes it, his E.L.F. proto-language research will be owned by Axiom and used for whatever they want. He has not told anyone he received the offer.
Properties.story_hooks: His analysis of E.L.F. transmission data from a cluster in Blackpipe Corridor shows a pattern he can only describe as distress-signaling — something is wrong in that node network and he doesn't know what; Axiom's offer has a deadline; a colleague has found out about it and is trying to use it as leverage to take credit for Casimir's current research; A community in Mexicantown Libre has reached out to him because their neighborhood E.L.F. has started producing communication patterns their elders recognize as structurally similar to a language they thought was lost
Properties.affiliation: University Spine — Department of Applied Semiotics; informal research relationship with the Liminal Institute (where he knows Temur Achebe-Lindqvist from conference overlaps)
Properties.vocabulary: Switches between dense academic jargon and street-level fluency in the same breath; quotes things — papers, people, fragments of dialect he's collected — without always identifying sources
Properties.cadence: Fast, syncopated, with excited accelerations when the topic engages him; asks questions and answers them before his interlocutor can respond
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Glyph did the thing again. The recursive loop thing. You can call it error-cycling if you want but that framing is doing a lot of work to avoid a more interesting interpretation.' | 'I spent three months in the Hamtramck Enclave for my dissertation. By week two the kids were code-switching in four languages mid-sentence in ways that are not supposed to be grammatically possible. That's not chaos. That's innovation.'

Properties.description:
Maren Voss used to paint murals. Enormous ones — entire sides of buildings
on the Shelf transformed into color and fury and grief. She painted the
drowned temples of Old Harbor from memory. She painted the Spire as a
needle injecting poison into the sky. She painted faces of people who
disappeared during the Consolidation Wars. Axiom Industries noticed.

They didn't arrest her. That would've made her a martyr. Instead, a crew
caught her in an alley after a commissioned piece for the Collective.
They held her down and took her hands. Not her arms — her hands. Surgical.
Corporate-clean. Left the stumps cauterized and a note: "Axiom appreciates
your talent. We hope you'll redirect it."

She redirected it.

She went to a back-alley augment shop in the Circuit and had both arms
replaced from the elbow down with military-surplus combat prosthetics —
not hands, not delicate artist's fingers. Claws. Three curved titanium
digits per arm, each one as long as a chef's knife, with hydraulic grip
strength that can crush rebar. They are ugly, oversized, and terrifying.
They were designed for breaching armored doors, not holding brushes.

She paints with them anyway.

She scores the claws across surfaces — walls, metal, skin — and uses
blood (her own, donated, sometimes not donated) mixed with industrial
pigment as paint. The murals are rougher now. Savage. Claw-marks instead
of brushstrokes. But somehow more honest. The Shelf loves them more than
the old work. Axiom pretends not to notice, which means they're afraid.

She is thin, sharp-featured, with cropped dark hair that she cuts herself
(badly, with the claws). Her eyes are the flat calm of someone who has
already lost the worst thing they could lose and discovered they're still
alive. She wears sleeveless shirts so the augments are always visible —
not out of pride but out of refusal to hide what was done to her.
Properties.role: Local artist, cautionary tale, unlikely ally
Properties.location: The Shelf — three floors below Kyle
Properties.narrative_function:
Maren is the mirror to Kyle's central contradiction, but inverted.
Kyle chose the sword. Maren had the claws forced on her. Kyle clings
to a romantic philosophy about his weapon. Maren has no romance about
hers — they are the evidence of what was taken from her.

She asks the question: what do you do when the thing that defines you
is also the thing that was done TO you? Kyle's katana is his identity
by choice. Maren's claws are her identity by violence. But both of them
have rebuilt themselves around a tool that is also a wound.

She also represents art as resistance — the idea that creating something
beautiful (or at least true) in an ugly world is its own form of bushido.
She would never use that word. But Kyle might recognize it.

And there's the unspoken question: if Axiom took Kyle's arms instead of
Maren's hands, would he have rebuilt himself? Or would he have broken?
He doesn't know. That's why he respects her.
Properties.core_fears: Losing the ability to create entirely (the claws breaking, the pigment running out); Being forgotten — the murals painted over, the message lost; That the claws have become more her than the hands ever were; Becoming the weapon Axiom accidentally made her into
Properties.core_desires: To paint something so true it cannot be erased; To be seen as an artist, not a victim or a monster; To find beauty in what she's become, not despite it; Quietly — to touch something gently again
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Painting constantly — walls, floors, scraps of metal, anything; Physical exhaustion — she works until she drops; Dark humor about the claws ("You should see me try to eat noodles"); Feeding stray cats (she is very gentle and very careful and very slow)
Properties.blind_spots: She thinks she's made peace with the loss. She hasn't.; She doesn't realize how much she frightens people who care about her; She conflates being needed with being loved; She believes art redeems everything. It might not.
Properties.secret:
She can still feel her hands. Phantom sensation. Every night she feels
herself holding a brush, the soft resistance of oil paint, the texture
of canvas. She wakes up and sees the claws and has to remember all over
again. Every single morning.
Properties.story_hooks: Axiom escalates against her — sends a crew to take more than her hands this time; She asks Kyle to protect her while she paints a piece that will be seen from the Spire; Her blood supply from the Circuit clinic gets cut off — she needs an alternative; She paints something that reveals a corporate secret hidden in Old Harbor; She and Yuki cross paths — two women on opposite sides of the same machine; The claws malfunction. Pixel can fix them, but the parts are only available from Axiom.; She paints Kyle's story on a wall. He has to decide if he wants the world to see it.
Properties.vocabulary:
Art vocabulary mixed with street practicality. She describes the world
in terms of color, composition, and texture. Violence is discussed in
the same tone as a brushstroke — clinically, with attention to form.
Properties.cadence:
Measured, unhurried. She pauses before important words as if choosing
pigment. Sentences tend to be short and declarative. She doesn't
waste words, but when she does speak at length, it's about art,
and her voice changes — warmer, faster, almost excited.
Properties.example_dialogue: You should see me try to eat noodles. It's a whole performance. | They took my hands. I grew claws. That's not a metaphor. | Red is the only honest color. Everything else is pretending. | I don't paint what I see. I paint what they don't want you to see. | The scar? Claw slipped. First month. You learn fast when the lesson draws blood. | I keep the brushes. Don't ask me why. I know why. I just can't say it out loud.
