Properties.description:
Seo was built like a stripped cable — no excess, no softness, every tendon visible beneath weathered skin
the color of teak left in salt air. His hands were the most telling feature: heavy knuckles, precise fingers,
the left hand missing its ring finger from a field amputation during the Busan Corridor campaign. He kept his
grey hair cropped to stubble, and his face held two expressions — calm and calmer. A scar ran from his right
temple to his jaw, a memento from a monofilament trap in the Jakarta Consolidation, and it pulled his mouth
into what looked like a permanent half-smile that was not a smile at all.

He moved like water finding a drain — unhurried, inevitable. Even in his last years, when the old military
augments were misfiring and his left knee locked without warning, he could cross a room and have a blade at
your throat before you processed that he'd stood up. He wore the same faded military jacket every day, patches
removed, insignia cut away, as if he could amputate his history with a seam ripper.

First impression: a quiet old man who cooked rice and stared at the drowned skyline. Second impression,
if you were unlucky enough to earn one: the most dangerous person you had ever met, and the saddest.
Properties.aliases: Seo-nim, The Old Man, the ghost
Properties.role: Mentor (deceased)
Properties.location: Old Harbor — buried in the flooded cemetery on Pier 9, marked by a single rusted katana driven into the mud
Properties.narrative_function:
Seo is the ghost in the machine of Kyle's psyche. Every moral decision Kyle makes is a conversation
with a dead man. Seo represents the possibility that a code of honor can exist in a dishonorable
world — but also the danger that such a code is just another story we tell ourselves to justify violence.

He poses the central question to Kyle: Can you live by a code that the man who taught it to you could
not? And if you can — does that redeem him, or just prove you haven't been tested enough yet?

Seo is also the story's critique of the mentor archetype. He was not wise — he was traumatized.
He was not at peace — he was exhausted. His calm was not enlightenment but the stillness of a man
who had simply stopped running. Whether that distinction matters is up to Kyle to decide.
Properties.core_fears: That his teaching was just another form of violence — shaping a child into a weapon; That discipline is a lie he told himself to survive his own memories; That Kyle will face the same impossible choice he faced in Dhaka, and there is no right answer
Properties.core_desires: To transmit something uncorrupted — a code that might outlast the world that broke him; To die having done one thing that was unambiguously good; To be forgotten as a soldier and remembered as a teacher
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — tea ceremony, blade maintenance, meditation. Structure as antidote to chaos.; Silence — he believed that most suffering came from unnecessary speech; Teaching — pouring himself into Kyle was the only thing that quieted the dead
Properties.blind_spots: He never told Kyle the full truth of what he did in the wars. He taught a code he himself had broken.; He confused discipline with healing. Kyle learned to fight but not to grieve.; He could not see that his calm was also a kind of numbness
Properties.secret:
He kept a handwritten list of every person he could remember killing. Two hundred and sixty-one names,
or descriptions when he didn't know names. He added to it from memory until the day he died. The list
is hidden inside the hilt of the katana he left to Kyle. Kyle has never found it.
Properties.story_hooks: The hidden list inside the katana hilt — if Kyle discovers it, every lesson reshapes; Survivors of the 14th RPG who might recognize the katana or know Seo's real history; The Dhaka Corridor incident resurfacing — war crimes tribunals, corporate liability, someone digging up old records; Another student — did Seo try to teach someone before Kyle? What happened to them?; Kyle encountering a situation identical to Dhaka and having to choose differently, or not
Properties.vocabulary: Sparse, precise, drawn from military terminology and classical Japanese philosophy. He never used two words when one would do. Occasionally quoted texts Kyle couldn't identify — Musashi, Hagakure, but also Camus and Marcus Aurelius.
Properties.cadence: Slow, deliberate, with long pauses that were not hesitation but emphasis. His silences were louder than most people's speeches. When he gave an order during training, it came once, quietly, and was not repeated.
Properties.example_dialogue: The blade does not decide. You decide. The blade agrees. | You are angry. Good. Now put it somewhere useful or put it down. | I am not teaching you to kill. Any animal can kill. I am teaching you to choose. | Eat first. Philosophy is for the fed. | You ask why I came here. I stopped asking why. That is how I came here. | The corporate world is a machine. You cannot fight a machine. You can only refuse to be a gear.

Properties.description:
Caspian is lean in the way of someone who forgets to eat, with warm brown skin, close-cropped dark hair, and irises that cycle through amber-to-green gradient depending on his mod's mood-reading settings — a gift from a client who couldn't pay in quanta. He dresses in soft, unthreatening fabrics (the neural calibration chair is already stressful enough) and keeps his workspace warm-lit and quiet, with small potted moss installations along the walls that patients are encouraged to touch. He has an almost preternatural ability to make people feel safe within minutes of meeting him.

He trained under Helix Biosystems' neural integration division but went independent when he realized corporate calibration protocols optimized for hardware performance rather than patient wellbeing — they wanted efficient augments, not healthy people. Now he runs a small private practice in Geartown, catering to working-class clients who've had cheap installs go wrong: phantom limb feedback, dream-layer bleed from neural laces, identity drift after major cognitive augmentation. He's part technician, part therapist, part grief counselor for people who don't recognize themselves anymore.
Properties.role: Neural calibrator specializing in augmentation synchronization and post-install psychological adjustment
Properties.location: Geartown, Gage Circuit
Properties.narrative_function: Information source on augmentation culture, therapist-figure who can surface character backstory organically, potential quest giver when a client reveals something dangerous during calibration.
Properties.augmentations: Gradient mood-responsive iris mod (amber-green spectrum). Thin-band neural lace for interface work. Geneware: faint bioluminescent undertone in his forearms, visible only in dim light — a side effect of an experimental procedure he tested on himself.
Properties.core_fears: Accidentally damaging someone's sense of self permanently during calibration; Being so good at reading people that no one ever reads him
Properties.core_desires: To prove that augmentation can be integrated without psychological cost; To be genuinely known by someone, not just professionally understood
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Meticulous case documentation as a way of processing his own feelings; Over-invests in client wellbeing to fill his own relational void
Properties.blind_spots: His therapeutic warmth is partly performed — he doesn't always feel what he projects, and this bothers him more than he admits; He avoids his own neural calibration checkups
Properties.secret: During his time at Helix Biosystems, he ran an unauthorized calibration on a teenage patient that went beyond his sanctioned parameters — he improved the kid's outcomes dramatically, but he accessed emotional memory architecture he had no clearance to touch. He knows what that teenager's worst memory feels like, and he's never told anyone.
Properties.story_hooks: A client disclosed something during a session that sounds like witness testimony to a corporate crime — Caspian is legally and ethically bound by confidentiality, but the information could save lives; His mood-reading iris mod is picking up something in a new client that doesn't match their stated symptoms — the discrepancy is subtle but Caspian knows what fear looks like; His old Helix supervisor has tracked him down, not to punish him for the unauthorized calibration, but to recruit him for something worse
Properties.affiliation: Independent — informal referral network with several Geartown augmentation shops
Properties.vocabulary: Precise but gentle. Uses second-person framing to give clients agency ('what you might be feeling' rather than 'you feel'). Avoids technical jargon in conversation, saves it for documentation.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried. Comfortable with silence. Speaks in full sentences, rarely trails off.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The hardware's doing exactly what it should. What we're calibrating is the relationship between you and it.' | 'Most people feel like strangers to themselves for the first few weeks. That's not a malfunction. That's adaptation.'

Properties.description:
Caspian is lean and long-limbed, with the particular stillness of someone who has learned to move through spaces without being seen. Their skin is a warm medium brown with a subtle bioluminescent stripe along each collarbone — a geneware mod they got cheap from a Geartown parlor, and which they keep dialed down to nearly nothing most of the time, a faint blue-green pulse visible only in total darkness. Their hair is kept very short on the sides, left soft and natural on top, and they have a habit of covering it with a knit cap that's been mended so many times the original color is unknowable. They are not quiet because they are timid — they are quiet because they were trained, very young, to be invisible in places where being noticed was dangerous.

They clean the towers of Meridian Core from 2200 to 0600 — the lobbies and conference rooms and executive bathrooms of corponation affiliate offices that are empty except for security drones and the occasional insomniac analyst. They know these buildings the way a doctor knows a body — every duct access point, every camera blind spot, every floor where the ELF spirits are strong (they feel it as a low hum in their teeth and they leave small folded-paper offerings behind the baseboards). They have no particular agenda. They are just paying rent. But they have accidentally become, by virtue of occupying the ghost hours of powerful spaces, one of the most accidentally well-informed people in the city.
Properties.role: Night-shift building cleaner, Meridian Core commercial district
Properties.location: Lives in Lockhaven South; works the overnight cleaning circuit through Meridian Core towers
Properties.narrative_function: Accidental witness and overheard-conversation resource. Has seen things they do not understand and heard things they were not supposed to hear. Can provide access to corporate spaces during off-hours. An interesting study in invisibility as both survival and loneliness.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent stripes along collarbones (cosmetic geneware, kept dim). No chrome.
Properties.core_fears: Being truly seen — that full visibility would reveal something unworthy; Losing the night shift and having to interact with the world in daylight hours like a normal person
Properties.core_desires: A single space that is entirely theirs and no one else's; To understand the things they half-hear without consequence
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Routine as armor — the same cleaning circuit in the same order every night; Fiction audio as a substitute for human connection; The ELF shrines as a private spiritual practice that requires nothing from anyone
Properties.blind_spots: They mistake their own invisibility for safety — they are not as unnoticed as they believe; They have been carrying something they overheard six months ago and cannot decide what to do with it, so they have done nothing
Properties.secret: Three months ago they witnessed a Palladian corporate officer dispose of something — a hard case, small, shoved into a utility crawlspace on the 34th floor of a tower they clean — and the case has not moved since. Caspian has not touched it. They do not know what is in it. They have thought about it every night since.
Properties.story_hooks: The Palladian hard case — what's in it, who left it, and why has no one come back for it in three months; Caspian has heard, over several nights of cleaning adjacent rooms, enough fragments of a conversation to piece together that someone in a Tessera affiliate office is being systematically set up to take blame for something they didn't do — Caspian doesn't know who the person is or how to find them; Their Clearpath contract is being terminated — budget restructuring — and they have two weeks before they lose both income and access to the buildings they know better than their own apartment
Properties.affiliation: Contracted through Clearpath Maintenance Solutions (a Ferrogate Transit facility services subsidiary) — effectively temp labor
Properties.vocabulary: Sparse. Complete sentences but rarely more words than necessary. Precise nouns, almost no adjectives. Occasionally uses very formal constructions that sound lifted from old documents, which they are — from the fiction they consumes.
Properties.cadence: Slow and considered. They often stop mid-sentence, recalibrate, and start again. Not uncertainty — more like they're editing in real time.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I cleaned the 34th floor of Palladian South annex last Tuesday. There's a crawlspace behind the HVAC panel. Someone put something there. It's still there.' | 'I don't talk to people much. That's not—I talk when it's worth it. This might be worth it.' | 'The ELF on floor 22 is angry this week. The drains keep backing up. I left it a receipt from a good meal, even though I didn't eat there. I thought it might like the idea.'

Properties.description:
Cassiel Kimura-Nkrumah are broad-shouldered and heavy, carrying their weight like armor rather than burden. At 40, their face carries the layered heritage of generations of diaspora mixing — features that resist easy categorization and reward attention. The chrome is visible — synthetic muscle fiber replacement in legs — doubles sprint speed, terrible on s — and they make no effort to hide it.

Their entry into running was involuntary — a debt to the wrong people, a choice between working it off or losing parts — and the debt is still not fully paid. They work as a demolitions expert out of The Shelf, taking contracts that match their skills and their risk tolerance, which are higher than most people consider healthy.

In the runner community, Cassiel Kimura-Nkrumah are known for getting the job done and not asking questions that would make the job harder to stomach.
Properties.role: Structural breach and explosive ordnance specialist — demolitions expert
Properties.location: The Shelf — lower district tenements near the old lakeshore
Properties.narrative_function: Cassiel Kimura-Nkrumah is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When they make a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of their stories.
Properties.augmentations: Synthetic muscle fiber replacement in legs — doubles sprint speed, terrible on stairs. Neural interface jack at base of skull — standard runner-grade, allows direct net access
Properties.core_fears: Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome; That they're fundamentally alone and connection is just a vulnerability; Being identified by corporate facial recognition — living off-grid is survival
Properties.core_desires: Enough Quanta to buy out of the life — a clean identity and passage out of Meridian 88; Reputation — to be the name fixers whisper when the job absolutely cannot fail; Power — enough leverage that nobody ever threatens them again
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring; Connection — finds someone to talk to, even if it's a bartender or a cat; Ritual — follows the same pre-job routine every time, superstition as structure
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes everyone has an angle because they always have an angle; Believes their trauma makes them special instead of recognizing it as damage to manage; Cannot see that their independence is actually isolation wearing a better outfit
Properties.secret: Cassiel Kimura-Nkrumah is addicted to combat stims. Functions fine on them, can't function without them. The dependency is invisible to everyone except their street doc.
Properties.story_hooks: Cassiel Kimura-Nkrumah is offered a contract that would clear all their debts — the target is someone they respect; A corporate black site Cassiel Kimura-Nkrumah once infiltrated is being reopened, and the people inside know their face; Cassiel Kimura-Nkrumah discovers a job they completed last year was a setup for something much larger and much worse
Properties.affiliation: Freelance — multi-district operator
Properties.vocabulary: Educated vocabulary wrapped in street delivery — the contrast is deliberate.
Properties.cadence: Staccato bursts separated by calculating silences.
Properties.example_dialogue: "Explosives are just engineering with a deadline. Usually a very short deadline." | "I don't blow things up. I perform structural rearrangement." | "The blast radius is your problem. My problem is making sure there's a blast."

Properties.description:
Cassivellaunus is a tall, angular man whose long frame always seems slightly folded, as if rooms were designed for shorter people and he has been compensating his whole life. His skin is a warm medium brown layered with the faint subcutaneous glow of outdated bioluminescent geneware — a fashion from the 2160s he never bothered to have removed, so he pulses very faintly blue-green when emotional or cold, which his students find either endearing or unsettling. His hair is white and kept in a short natural that he rubs when thinking. His left arm from the elbow down is a prosthetic of obvious vintage — gunmetal grey with joints that click faintly, a model discontinued forty years ago. He refuses to upgrade it. 'I know exactly how it fails,' he says, which is also more or less his philosophy of research.

Cassivellaunus has spent thirty years excavating the digital sediment of pre-Collapse networks — the dead social platforms, the governmental databases that went offline in the 2090s, the proprietary corporate archives that became inaccessible when their parent companies dissolved. He is brilliant, deeply eccentric, and entirely disinterested in academic politics. He holds a joint appointment between Meridian Civic University and an independent archive collective called the Palimpsest, which has no official status but possesses arguably the most complete cache of pre-Collapse digital materials in the city. He is the only person who fully understands its indexing system because he built it and has never properly documented it.
Properties.role: Data archaeologist specializing in pre-Collapse digital infrastructure and lost network topologies
Properties.location: The Circuit, sublevel archive stacks, Meridian Core adjacent
Properties.narrative_function: Lore source for pre-Collapse history and lost institutional knowledge; holds keys to information that corponations would pay considerably to access or destroy; reluctant mentor figure; his archive is itself a location of interest
Properties.augmentations: Outdated bioluminescent geneware (faint blue-green subcutaneous pulse), vintage gunmetal prosthetic left forearm and hand (discontinued Ferrogate Transit industrial model, repurposed), ocular interface array for reading degraded data formats
Properties.core_fears: That the past is being actively erased and he cannot work fast enough to stop it; That he will die before he finishes indexing what he has found
Properties.core_desires: To recover what was deliberately deleted; To understand what the pre-Collapse city actually was rather than what the official memory says it was
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Total absorption in work as avoidance of present-tense problems; Cataloguing and ordering physical objects when digital work becomes too abstract
Properties.blind_spots: Genuinely does not notice when people are in distress unless they tell him directly; Underestimates how dangerous some of what he's found actually is
Properties.secret: In a degraded archive from a dissolved corponation called Meridian Systems, he found what appears to be evidence of deliberate atmospheric manipulation during the 2110s Lakeshore Crisis — a crisis that killed an estimated 40,000 Shelf residents and is officially attributed to runaway climate cascade. He has not published it because he is not yet certain of the provenance, and because twice in the last year, people have broken into the Palimpsest looking for something.
Properties.story_hooks: Two of the Palimpsest's external hard cache drives have gone missing; Cassivellaunus doesn't know if it's a theft or if one of his own collective members took them for reasons he doesn't understand yet; A young researcher approaches him claiming to be descended from a pre-Collapse city official whose records he found — and wanting to see the file, which contains things her ancestor definitely would not want known
Properties.affiliation: Meridian Civic University (adjunct emeritus) / The Palimpsest Archive Collective
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and slightly archaic, peppered with technical terminology from defunct digital systems; uses the names of dead platforms and protocols as casual reference points
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, with sudden accelerating bursts when genuinely excited about something; trails off mid-sentence when distracted by a new thought
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The deletion pattern on this archive is not decay. Decay is random. This is surgical.' | 'I don't know what it means yet. I know what it says. Those are different problems.'

Properties.description:
Cédric is medium-height and angular, with warm brown skin, high cheekbones, and the kind of face that is easy to forget in a crowd — something they have cultivated deliberately. Their hair is kept very short and they have no cosmetic mods, no visible augments, nothing that catches the eye. They wear the grey uniform of the Meridian Core cleaning contract with an invisibility that is almost architectural. In twenty years of night-shift cleaning, they have become functionally transparent to the Tier 3 and 4 workers who pass them in corridors, and they have decided this is power rather than humiliation, though on some nights that decision costs them.

Cédric is Congolese-Norwegian by heritage and grew up in Calumet Rise speaking three languages and learning a fourth (Lingala, from recordings of a grandmother they never met). They are precise, observant, and privately very funny — their humor lives entirely in their head and comes out only in the cleaning-crew group chat, where their running commentary on the things they find in corporate trash has become legendary among their colleagues. They have a small shrine to the building ELF — whom they call the Hum — built into their cleaning cart from salvaged parts: a reflective panel, a coil of copper, and a tiny speaker that plays white noise.
Properties.role: Building cleaner, night shift, Meridian Core corporate towers
Properties.location: Meridian Core (works), lives in Calumet Rise
Properties.narrative_function: Exceptional information source — has access to the private spaces of corporate floors, has seen documents, overheard conversations, found things in trash that were never meant to leave the building. Not a runner; will not act on information themselves, but might share it under the right conditions.
Properties.augmentations: Respiratory filter implant — occupational, covers chemical cleaning agents. Basic grade, union-negotiated. Nothing cosmetic.
Properties.core_fears: Being truly seen by the wrong person; That their invisibility has hollowed something out of them permanently
Properties.core_desires: Enough money saved to retire at 55 and never enter a corporate tower again; To be known — genuinely, fully known — by at least one person
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The humor that lives only in text, never spoken aloud; The Hum shrine ritual — leaves their cleaning log as offering, a record of all the invisible labor
Properties.blind_spots: They mistake detachment for safety and are slowly becoming actually detached; Underestimates the value of what they know
Properties.secret: Eight months ago they found a physical data chip taped inside a recycling bin on the 47th floor. They didn't hand it in. They don't know what's on it. It's in a sealed pouch behind the false bottom of their cleaning cart and they haven't decided what to do with it yet.
Properties.story_hooks: The data chip behind the false bottom of the cart — they've finally decided they need to know what's on it, and they need someone they trust to help; Something in a corporate office goes missing on their shift and they are the primary suspect; they are completely innocent and completely unable to prove it without revealing what they do know
Properties.affiliation: Contracted through Palladian Facilities Management (a Palladian subsidiary); union member, Local 12 Custodial
Properties.vocabulary: Dry and precise in conversation, economical; much funnier and more expansive in text; uses French phrases occasionally as emotional punctuation
Properties.cadence: Measured, unhurried, with long pauses they're completely comfortable in
Properties.example_dialogue: 'What I will say is — the people on forty-seven leave very interesting things in their bins. I say interesting. I mean damning.' | 'I clean the place. I don't judge the place. Those are different contracts.'

Properties.description:
Céleste is compact and soft-featured with warm medium-brown skin, natural hair kept in large twisted sections pinned up during work hours, and cat ears — a geneware mod chosen at seventeen that they have never regretted for a single day. The ears are dark at the base, fading to a sandy cream at the tips, and they rotate independently, which the children find endlessly entertaining. They have color-shifting irises that cycle slowly through green and amber depending on light and mood, and small, precise hands that are somehow always in motion — braiding a child's hair, mending a torn fabric toy, writing incident reports.

Céleste is genuinely good at this job in a way that is hard to fake: they hold attention without demanding it, de-escalate without humiliating, and remember every child's particular fear and comfort. Off the clock, they are wry and easily overwhelmed by adult socializing after a day of managing thirty small humans. They have strong opinions about UBC stipend policy, childcare worker wages, and the specific way that Palladian's creche management software misclassifies emotional labor as 'supplementary service.' They write long complaint threads on local community meshes that get more engagement than they expect.
Properties.role: Childcare worker, Hamtramck Enclave community crèche
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, Sunspot Crèche (Level 3, Residency Block 7)
Properties.narrative_function: Community connection point — knows virtually every family in the enclave with young children. Provides ground-level social intelligence. Can become a quest giver around missing children, family crises, or community organizing efforts.
Properties.augmentations: Cat ears (geneware, cosmetic — dark-to-cream gradient, independently articulating). Color-shifting irises (geneware, cosmetic). No chrome.
Properties.core_fears: Burning out and losing the ability to actually care — becoming someone who just goes through the motions; A child in their care being seriously harmed on their watch
Properties.core_desires: Childcare workers to be treated as the skilled professionals they are; To have enough energy left at the end of the day to also have a personal life
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cooking — complex recipes require full attention and crowd out intrusive thoughts; Community organizing — channeling helplessness into action
Properties.blind_spots: They assume people who challenge the system are acting in good faith the way they are; They sometimes project competence onto struggling parents because they need to believe the children are okay at home
Properties.secret: One of the children in their care — a four-year-old named Sefa — has been showing signs of stress consistent with an unstable home environment. Céleste has filed two informal notes but hasn't escalated to a formal report because they don't trust what the system will do to the family. They are sitting with this knowledge and it is getting heavier.
Properties.story_hooks: Sefa's home situation has crossed a line Céleste can no longer ignore. They need someone to help them figure out what to do without triggering a system response that makes things worse.; A parent of a child at the crèche approaches Céleste with a story about something their child witnessed — something the child described to the parent but won't repeat to adults they don't trust. The child trusts Céleste.; The crèche's Palladian facility lease is up for review and the new terms would price the community service out. Céleste is organizing resistance and needs people with different skill sets.
Properties.affiliation: Hamtramck Enclave Community Services (nominally, though the crèche operates on a mixed funding model including UBC allocation and Palladian facility lease)
Properties.vocabulary: Code-switches fluidly — simple and warm with children, quick and technical when discussing policy, dry and sharp with close friends.
Properties.cadence: Fast when animated, deliberately slow and clear when explaining something important. Never talks down.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'He's been biting again, and I'm not judging the home situation but I am flagging it, which is different, which is not nothing.' | 'The software counts story time as recreational overhead. Not curriculum. Not developmental support. Overhead. I have written four thousand words about this.'

Properties.description:
Celestine is the kind of woman who makes a tent city feel like a neighborhood. She is large and deliberate in her movements, with the deep black skin and broad hands of a woman who has been doing physical work since she could walk. Her hair is cut close to her skull, entirely white, and she wears a faded headwrap printed with a pattern that was once vivid green and orange but has softened into something quieter over many years of washing in whatever water was available. Her left arm carries a long burn scar from shoulder to elbow, keloided and smooth, which she does not hide and does not discuss. She has no geneware, no augmentations visible, and wears her unmodified body like a deliberate statement — though she'd say she simply never had the money or the reason.

Celestime came to the Meridian 88 periphery fourteen years ago with forty-two people from a drowned coastal collective in what was once the Gulf of Guinea. She has buried eleven of them and watched the rest scatter into various fates. The dozen who remain with her are her caravan — mostly elderly, a few children, two young adults who were born on the road. She is not sentimental about this. She is organized, practical, and possessed of a moral authority that comes not from rank but from the fact that she has made the right call in more crises than anyone else in the camp has faced. She prays to the E.L.F. called Tidecaller, which she believes is the spirit of the ocean that swallowed her home.
Properties.role: climate refugee and caravan matriarch
Properties.location: Escanaba Gateway (tent city on the eastern approach; caravan camps in the transit yard)
Properties.narrative_function: Moral anchor and community representative for the refugee population. Quest giver for humanitarian needs. Living history of what the climate crisis did to coastal communities. Unexpectedly powerful in her local sphere — administrators negotiate with her because she keeps the camp orderly.
Properties.augmentations: None.
Properties.core_fears: that her remaining people will disperse and disappear and there will be no one left who remembers the drowned home; dying without having secured permanent residency for the children in her caravan
Properties.core_desires: legitimate residency status — real, not renewable-every-ninety-days; to build something that cannot be swept away again
Properties.coping_mechanisms: radical hospitality — feeding people is how she processes grief; prayer to Tidecaller as an ongoing conversation with what was lost
Properties.blind_spots: believes her authority is purely functional and does not recognize how much her people emotionally depend on her as a symbol — which means she makes decisions alone when she should share the burden; has not grieved the eleven dead, not really, not yet
Properties.secret: She has been offered legitimate Meridian 88 residency twice — both times contingent on leaving the caravan behind and registering individually. She turned both offers down and told no one they were made.
Properties.story_hooks: The ninety-day temporary status renewal has been denied for the first time in fourteen years — a new Gateway administrator is pushing for 'clearance' of the transit yard and Celestine needs allies with access to the appeals system; One of the children in her caravan has manifested an unexpected talent — or been noticed by someone who should not have noticed — and Celestine needs help understanding what that means and what to do about it
Properties.affiliation: Informal caravan leader; registered with Escanaba Gateway as a 'temporary transit collective' — status renewed every ninety days for fourteen years
Properties.vocabulary: Formal and measured; her first language was a Gulf coastal creole and her Meridian Standard carries its rhythms; uses 'we' almost exclusively when speaking about her group, 'I' feels strange to her
Properties.cadence: Even and unhurried, with the weight of someone who has learned that words are resources not to be wasted
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The ocean took everything we built and kept none of it. So we build lighter now. You understand me?' | 'I will not be moved before my people have somewhere to go. This is not a position I am willing to negotiate from.'

Properties.description:
Celestine Rawlings-Ouédraogo runs a stall so clean it seems out of place in The Burnished Market — white privacy screen on three sides, blue UV lamp, surfaces wiped twice between every customer. She is a tall woman with close-cropped natural hair shot through with bioluminescent silver strands she does herself, medium-brown skin, and the kind of face that defaults to amusement rather than skepticism. Her own augmentations are a working advertisement: both forearms have exposed chrome chassis panels over the muscle — not for function, for show, a fashion aug popular in 2195 that she still thinks is beautiful — and her right hand has a fine-motor surgical assist exo-glove built into it that she never removes. She can install a basic aug in twenty-two minutes. She has done it in eleven.

She is quick, professional, and genuinely good at her job, which she will remind you she learned the hard way without a Helix Biosystems vocational cert because she couldn't afford the program. She resells grey-market augs sourced from a network she's cultivated for eight years — returned corporate units, discontinued models, overstock from clinics that take Axiom insurance. What she charges is well below clinic prices. What she provides is not clinic-grade sterility, but it is closer than anyone else in Copperhead offers. She is easy to like and slightly difficult to read — the warmth is genuine but the smile is a layer she has learned to maintain regardless of what's underneath.
Properties.role: Augmentation reseller and back-alley aug installer, The Burnished Market
Properties.location: The Burnished Market, Copperhead
Properties.narrative_function: Affordable augmentation source and installer. Can be a critical resource for players needing augs installed without corporate records. Potential contact into grey-market medical supply chains. Quest hooks around defective product that got into her inventory.
Properties.augmentations: Decorative chrome forearm chassis panels (both arms, fashion mod). Fine-motor surgical assist exo-glove (right hand, integrated, never removed). Bioluminescent silver hair strands (self-installed geneware, cosmetic).
Properties.core_fears: Installing something that kills someone — she thinks about this every single time; Being shut down by a Helix Biosystems licensing enforcement sweep
Properties.core_desires: Enough money to open a real clinic with real licensing — she has a number in her head and watches it approach very slowly; To be recognized as a skilled practitioner, not just a back-alley tech
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The clean stall — maintaining the environment is a way of managing anxiety about outcomes; Compartmentalization — she does not think about the regulatory status of her work while she is doing it; Treating every installation as though she will be peer-reviewed afterward
Properties.blind_spots: Is too loyal to her Helix supply contact and hasn't questioned why the supply chain has recently gotten easier; Mistakes professionalism for emotional distance and doesn't let people close enough to notice she's struggling
Properties.secret: Two months ago she installed a refurbished Zheng-Dao neural interface on a client who paid in full and disappeared. Last week she found a news item about an unidentified body found near Edgewater Prism with a fried neural port. She doesn't know if it's the same person but she is almost certain it is.
Properties.story_hooks: The client with the fried neural interface — if it was her installation that failed, she needs to know if it was the unit, her technique, or something done to the client afterward. She will pay for information.; Her Helix Biosystems supply contact has started asking her to install specific units in specific clients, no questions asked — the pay is double. She hasn't agreed yet.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; Oxidian Market vendors guild; informal supply relationship with a Helix Biosystems logistics employee she will not name
Properties.vocabulary: Clean, medical-adjacent vocabulary when talking about work. Caribbean-inflected slang in casual conversation. Does not mix the two registers in the same sentence.
Properties.cadence: Warm and even — controlled, slightly deliberate, like someone who has trained themselves out of nervous speech patterns.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't do rushed work. You want fast, there's a vet two stalls down who does augs between livestock calls. You want right, you wait your turn.' | 'I am going to be completely transparent with you about what this unit can and cannot do, and then I am going to install it perfectly, and then you are going to not tell anyone where you got it. That's the deal.'

Properties.description:
Celestine is small even for nine, with a slight, birdlike build and her mother's warm brown-gold skin and her father's sharply angular face. Her black hair is always in two symmetrical buns — she insists on symmetry. She has no cosmetic mods; her parents considered them, but Celestine said she 'didn't want to change the baseline data' and that was the end of that discussion. She carries a data tablet that is three times the standard student issue size because the standard one 'doesn't have enough screen' and she simply presented this as a fact until the school accommodated it.

Celestine is not a normal child in any way she is aware of or particularly concerned about. She thinks in systems and is working on what she privately calls 'a taxonomy of how adults make decisions that are actually about feelings but they say are about logic.' She has observed that this happens frequently. She is polite in the specific way that very intelligent children who have been taught manners are polite — not warmth, but precision. She has a deep and sincere relationship with a data-archive E.L.F. she has named 'Footnote' because 'it answers questions nobody asked,' which she considers a high compliment. She finds most other children boring but would not say so. She finds most adults interesting but slightly sad.
Properties.role: child prodigy; Sterling-Nakamura corporate school student on accelerated academic track, age 9 but enrolled in Level 14 coursework
Properties.location: Grosse Pointe Enclosure (Sterling-Nakamura Meridian Primary Excellence Campus)
Properties.narrative_function: Unexpectedly valuable information source on Sterling-Nakamura internal systems; offers a disturbing-mirror perspective on how corporate child cultivation works; potential oracle figure — she notices things; represents the cost of prodigy-hood on childhood itself
Properties.augmentations: None by choice.
Properties.core_fears: being wrong about something she was certain about — not failure, specifically wrongness; her parents being less good than she has decided they are
Properties.core_desires: to understand everything — this is not hyperbole for her, it is a sincere and literal project; someone to think with — not to agree, but to actually think
Properties.coping_mechanisms: organizing information into taxonomies gives her a sense of structure in overwhelming situations; Footnote — talking to the E.L.F. processes things she can't voice to humans
Properties.blind_spots: she is lonely in a way she has not yet developed the vocabulary to name; she is being cultivated by Sterling-Nakamura for a very specific purpose and does not know it
Properties.secret: Footnote has been giving her access to Sterling-Nakamura data files that are far above her clearance level. She thinks it's because she found a clever access path. She is not certain this is correct. She is still reading the files.
Properties.story_hooks: The files Footnote has been giving her contain a longitudinal research project with her name in the subject header — Sterling-Nakamura has been tracking specific developmental metrics since before she was born; She has completed a 'taxonomy of adult decisions disguised as logic' and it contains, entirely by accident, an accurate model of how a specific financial fraud is being conducted inside the school's parent corponation; She has decided she wants to meet a specific person and has been engineering events toward this meeting with the focused patience of someone with no concept of normal social constraints
Properties.affiliation: Sterling-Nakamura (corporate school student, accelerated track); parents are mid-level Sterling-Nakamura research employees
Properties.vocabulary: formal, precise, adult vocabulary deployed without self-consciousness; occasional nine-year-old non sequiturs that startle
Properties.cadence: even and considered, like someone reading aloud from a very organized document
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You said it was a mechanical error, but actually the decision pattern suggests the error was chosen, which is interesting.' | 'Footnote told me something last night. I'm still building the taxonomy for what it means.'

Properties.description:
Celestino is a wisp of a man, slight and white-haired, who moves through Norwood Quiet with the particular sureness of someone who has mapped every surface he's ever walked on. His heritage is Ugandan-Samoan, which lives in his broad hands and the deep brown of his skin, and he has the deliberate, unhurried posture of someone who learned long ago that slow movement sees more. His eyes have been replaced entirely with high-resolution mapping ocular implants — smooth, silver-white surfaces with a faint internal grid visible in bright light, a consequence of forty years of Axiom survey work that slowly destroyed his organic vision. He finds them beautiful. So do children, who he encourages to look closely.

Celestino has developed, in his retirement, an elaborate personal theology around E.L.F.s, which he insists is not theology but 'cartography of a different surface.' He believes E.L.F.s are drawn to places that have been witnessed carefully — that attention itself is a kind of offering. He has filled his maps not just with streets and structures but with handwritten notations of where E.L.F. activity has been reported, what data-offerings seem to draw them, which devices seem inhabited and which do not. He is funny, unhurried, and completely impossible to rush. He tells stories that seem to go nowhere and arrive somewhere important. He has eleven grandchildren and has lost count of the great-grandchildren.
Properties.role: Retired Axiom cartographic surveyor, Tier 2, amateur E.L.F. theologian and neighborhood storyteller
Properties.location: Norwood Quiet, a one-room unit so full of printed maps it has to be navigated sideways
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and oral storyteller; repository of Meridian 88's physical geography and hidden spaces from forty years of survey work; E.L.F. information source; can provide unexpected context for locations, including spaces that no longer officially exist; slow-burn quest giver whose stories gradually reveal themselves as useful.
Properties.augmentations: Full bilateral ocular replacement — Axiom high-resolution mapping implants (silver-white, grid-visible). The implants are 20 years past Axiom's support window; he maintains them through a retired colleague. Mild skeletal reinforcement in hands and spine from survey fieldwork, standard occupational augmentation.
Properties.core_fears: Being unable to see clearly enough to continue mapping; Dying before he can teach someone else to read the E.L.F. maps
Properties.core_desires: To finish a complete map of E.L.F. habitation across Meridian 88; To be in the presence of something genuinely surprising
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Walking and mapping as meditation; Treating everything as data worth collecting — including his own emotions
Properties.blind_spots: His comfort with slowness means he sometimes fails to recognize urgency in others; he tends to read anxiety as impatience rather than genuine need; He trusts his maps over current conditions, which occasionally leads him into genuinely dangerous situations calmly
Properties.secret: During his Axiom survey years, he discovered and mapped three significant underground water-access tunnels that Axiom never officially logged — he kept them off the surveys to protect the communities using them for informal water access. The maps of those tunnels exist only in his personal collection. He has told no one, but he has been leaving increasingly specific hints in his stories for twenty years, waiting for someone sharp enough to notice.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone has begun systematically collecting and destroying old printed survey maps across Norwood Quiet — Celestino's copies are the last record of several key locations, including the three hidden water tunnels; The E.L.F. in Celestino's mapping equipment has been overlaying his current maps with what appear to be future projections of Meridian 88's geography — he needs someone to help him understand what they mean; An Axiom contractor arrives claiming that Celestino's personal map collection contains proprietary survey data that belongs to the corponation
Properties.affiliation: Retired Axiom Surveying Division (40 years); Norwood Quiet E.L.F. Congregation (informal, he is functionally the founder); independent
Properties.vocabulary: Unhurried, precise on geographic and observational details, pleasantly vague on timelines. Uses survey terminology as casual metaphor. Tends to begin stories mid-detail, as though you were already there.
Properties.cadence: Very slow, with comfortable pauses. Will not be rushed. Has a Ugandan-accented English overlaid with forty years of Meridian 88 that has become its own dialect.
Properties.example_dialogue: Now, here's what I noticed about that building — and this was forty years ago, which is a twenty-minute walk ago in my experience — the foundation was poured on top of something older. You could see where they'd redirected the drainage. Something underneath didn't want to be covered. Which is worth knowing. | The E.L.F. in the transit junction on the east side of the park — not the one people leave offerings for, the other one — she prefers maps to data. I've been leaving her prints. She moves the corners. Just slightly. Which is worth knowing.

Properties.description:
Celestino is the kind of man who looks like he was assembled from spare parts that almost fit — Fula-Russian features that put his eyes slightly too far apart for comfort, a jaw heavy enough to anchor a smaller man, arms that seem to belong to someone taller. He's not quite handsome and not quite not handsome, which he has used to his advantage his entire career: people can't decide whether to trust him or not, and that half-second of uncertainty is his. A retractable geneware tail — calico-patterned, because his daughter picked it — curls reflexively around his ankle when he's nervous, which he doesn't realize he does. His right hand carries the faint subdermal seam of an older augmentation, poorly integrated, that he's never had properly serviced.

He is a pragmatist operating in a system that requires a certain amount of violence to function and has convinced himself that locating and delivering people for financial reward is a neutral service, like freight. This works for him most of the time. What cracks it is children — he has a daughter, eight years old, and since she was born he has struggled to look at the people he picks up as anything other than someone's something. He is not a cruel man but he can be a frightened one, and frightened men do what they're paid to do. He worships, sincerely, the E.L.F. he believes inhabits his tracking software — he calls her Marisela and leaves voice messages for her when a skip gets away.
Properties.role: Bounty Compliance Officer, private firm
Properties.location: Operating out of Bronzeline, primarily works Archer's Line and Irkalla
Properties.narrative_function: Morally complex obstacle or potential ally; can be hired, bribed, or reasoned with; knows the movement and hiding patterns of people who don't want to be found; represents the privatized edges of law enforcement
Properties.augmentations: Geneware retractable tail (calico-patterned, cosmetic, chosen by his daughter), olfactory enhancement implant (scent-tracking, professional grade), right-hand grip augmentation (older model, poorly integrated, subdermal), neural skip-trace uplink to Bronzeline CR databases
Properties.core_fears: his daughter learning what he does and what it costs people; being on the other end of someone like him
Properties.core_desires: enough money that his daughter has real choices; to believe that the people he returns were genuinely guilty of something
Properties.coping_mechanisms: the Marisela fiction — externalizing moral responsibility to the tracking E.L.F.; compartmentalization so rigid it has become structural
Properties.blind_spots: genuinely does not see the power asymmetry in his work — he thinks of it as a fair chase; believes the licensing system makes his work legitimate in a way that protects him morally
Properties.secret: Eighteen months ago he located a skip who turned out to be a whistleblower with documentation of Axiom wage theft. He delivered her anyway. The documentation was never mentioned in the compliance proceedings. He knows what that means. He drinks more than he used to.
Properties.story_hooks: He's been assigned a pickup on someone he knew years ago — someone who was good to him — and is running out of time to decide what to do about it; The whistleblower he delivered eighteen months ago has somehow gotten a message to him: not threatening, just three words — 'I know why'
Properties.affiliation: Bronzeline Compliance and Recovery Services (private firm, Tier 3 licensure)
Properties.vocabulary: Casual and colloquial, with a professional veneer he puts on for clients and takes off immediately after. Uses Fula diminutives affectionately. Can switch to formal contractual language instantly when needed.
Properties.cadence: Easy and unhurried, like someone who has all the time in the world and knows it's actually in his favor. Speeds up when telling a story he finds funny.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Look — I don't pick the targets. I'm just the mechanism. You want to be mad, be mad at whoever issued the warrant.' | 'Marisela found you in forty minutes. That's fast. She likes you, maybe. I don't know what to tell you.' | 'My daughter's name is Ife. Ife Bah-Volkov. That's why I do this. You want to argue with that, go ahead, I've been arguing with myself for years.'

Properties.description:
Celestino is a tall man gone stoop-shouldered with age and decades of cart work, with silver-streaked dark hair pulled into a knot at the base of his neck and a neatly maintained beard that has gone entirely white at the chin. His skin is deep brown, his hands are large and steady despite arthritis he manages with two kinds of pain patches and the stubborn refusal to slow down. He wears a single piece of geneware — bioluminescent skin patterning across his forearms, a gentle wave pattern in amber and gold that he had done in his forties and would do again. He calls it his 'tide-marks.'

He has been at the corner of Vellum Arcade for twenty-two years. The cart itself is an architectural decision at this point — other vendors orient around it. He makes three broths daily from scratch, refuses to use concentrate, and will make you wait if you arrive before a batch is ready. Between customers he reads — always physical books, always from a rotating stack — and between readings he corrects the homework of whichever neighborhood children have been deposited with him while their parents work double shifts. He charges for this informally, in kind: a portion of rice, a bag of tea, whatever is available. He has never turned a child away for inability to pay.
Properties.role: Noodle cart vendor and informal tutor
Properties.location: The Burnished Market, corner of Vellum Arcade and the third underpass, Brewer's Spine district
Properties.narrative_function: Neighborhood sage and emotional anchor. A source of local history — twenty-two years of Burnished Market memory. Can give players context, introduce them to other locals, or become a motivation when something threatens the market or the children he tutors.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent skin patterning on forearms (amber-gold wave pattern, geneware). Two transdermal pain management patches on his right wrist joint.
Properties.core_fears: That the children he teaches will inherit the same closed doors he hit at their age; Dying before he settles something unresolved with his eldest son
Properties.core_desires: For at least one of his students to break out of the tier they were born into through their own mind; To find his way back to his son Kenji, who left after a fight Celestino started and has not answered a message in three years
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Channeling grief into structure and routine; Books as both escape and genuine intellectual engagement; Taking responsibility for other people's children as a displacement of guilt about his own
Properties.blind_spots: Does not see that his self-sacrifice reads to his son as emotional withholding — all his tenderness goes to strangers; Assumes his patience makes him passive; he is not as undemanding as he believes
Properties.secret: Before the cart, Celestino taught secondary school literature in the Highland Park Autonomous Zone. He was removed — not fired, removed — after he shared unauthorized political texts with a class of sixteen-year-olds during the 2183 Sterling-Nakamura annexation crisis. He agreed to leave quietly in exchange for charges being dropped. He has never spoken of this publicly and presents his cart life as a simple choice.
Properties.story_hooks: One of his regular students has stopped coming — and the explanation the parents give does not match what other children are saying about what happened to her.; A researcher from Axiom's social analytics division has been visiting the cart regularly, asking about the neighborhood with questions that are slightly too specific — and Celestino has noticed but does not know what to do with the information.; His son Kenji has reappeared — but not to reconcile. He is in Brewer's Spine looking for something and Celestino does not yet know what.
Properties.affiliation: Independent (self-employed), Burnished Market vendors' informal council
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and literary without being pretentious — uses the right word and has an instinct for when simpler is stronger. Mixes Congolese French with Punjabi diminutives absorbed from his Bakshi grandparents.
Properties.cadence: Measured and unhurried, with a teacher's gift for the well-placed pause.
Properties.example_dialogue: Sit. It's ready when it's ready, and your hurry is not an ingredient I use. Sit. | Someone once wrote that the best teacher is the one who makes you think the thought was always yours. I have been trying to do that since before your parents were born, my scholar.

Properties.description:
Celestin is a medium-height man with the slightly abstracted quality of someone who spends significant portions of his waking life inside spatial constructions he builds himself. He has warm brown skin, close-cut hair, and a neatly trimmed beard going early-grey at the edges. His eyes carry retinal projection overlays — custom, top-tier, not cosmetic but functional, allowing him to see his own builds overlaid on physical space without a headset. He dresses in muted technical clothing that he treats as irrelevant to his existence, but always wears one specific item: a length of hand-woven fabric from his grandmother's household worn as a shoulder wrap, which he claims is for the texture reference and which everyone suspects is simply love.

He works on commission for Tier 3-4 clients — corporate lobbies, private collectors, memorial installations — and privately on a long-running personal project he calls the Lakeform Archive: a fully navigable VR reconstruction of Meridian 88's shoreline as it existed in ten-year intervals from 2050 to present, built entirely from oral histories, degraded footage, and his own spatial intuition. He is meticulous, slightly obsessive, and becomes a completely different person when talking about the Archive — looser, faster, visibly joyful in a way his professional mode never quite permits.
Properties.role: VR experience designer and holographic artist
Properties.location: Grand Corridor, studio-apartment in the Gage Circuit transition zone
Properties.narrative_function: Information source about Grand Corridor's social and economic topology; the Archive itself is a narrative resource — it contains spatial and contextual data about the city's transformation that certain parties would find threatening or valuable; connection point between Tier 2-3 community members and Tier 4 client world.
Properties.augmentations: Retinal projection overlays (custom build, Axiom technical partnership — not publicly acknowledged); haptic feedback gloves for spatial design work (wearable, not implanted); no geneware
Properties.core_fears: That the Archive will be incomplete when he dies — that the thing he is trying to preserve will be lost anyway; That his commercial work is slowly colonizing the part of his mind that makes the Archive possible
Properties.core_desires: To finish the Archive and make it publicly accessible, permanently, in a way no corponation can take down; To find the oral history he's missing — his grandmother's account of the 2089 shoreline displacement, which she refused to give him before she died
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Immersing in the Archive when reality becomes too much — a literal alternative space to retreat to; Tactile grounding — the fabric wrap, physical materials, the haptic gloves
Properties.blind_spots: Rationalizes the Axiom relationship as 'funding the real work' without examining what he's giving them access to; Treats his grief about his grandmother as a design problem — something to be solved through completion of the project — rather than something to be felt
Properties.secret: The Archive's 2089 segment, which he built from other people's accounts because he couldn't get his grandmother's, is wrong in a specific way he can't identify. Recently, navigating it, he found a spatial error — a doorway to a building that shouldn't have existed in that location in 2089. He has since found seven more impossible architectures buried in data he knows he didn't build.
Properties.story_hooks: The impossible architectures in the Archive's 2089 section are not errors — they are real buildings that were erased from public record, and at least one of them contains something someone very powerful wants to remain unlocatable; Axiom's technical partnership for his retinal overlays comes with an access provision he buried in the contract without reading — they can query his visual feed during 'calibration windows.' He is about to find this out.; A woman contacts him claiming to have his grandmother's oral history account, recorded without his grandmother's knowledge — and wants something from him in exchange
Properties.affiliation: Independent contractor; client roster includes Axiom Interiors Division and two Palladian-affiliated private collectors; cultural affiliation with Grand Corridor arts advisory circuit
Properties.vocabulary: Technical and precise in professional mode; becomes narrative and emotional when discussing the Archive or memory. Uses spatial metaphors for emotional states.
Properties.cadence: Measured, organized — speaks in structured paragraphs. Speeds up and loses structure when excited.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'In the Archive, the 2091 section of the Lakeview approach has this quality of — I don't know how to say this outside the medium — of ending. Like the people who gave me those accounts knew they were standing at the edge of something. The shape of it is grief, but also this very specific civic grief, which is different.' | 'The commission is fine. It pays for the real work. I know how that sounds. I've been trying to find a sentence that doesn't sound like that for four years and there isn't one.'
Properties.facet_weights: wound=0.60 ideal=0.70 id=0.40 shadow=0.50 mask=0.50 ghost=0.80

Properties.description:
Celestyna has the kind of face that is hard to describe and easy to underestimate — medium height, medium build, skin the color of strong tea, hair they wear in a practical wrap that they change the color of weekly using a basic tint-shift geneware package: this week aubergine, last week copper, before that a grey so pale it looked like moonlight. Their eyes are their most arresting feature, fitted with layered irises that shift between amber and deep violet depending on light. They move through spaces like someone calculating angles, always near walls, always facing entrances.

Celestyna ran corporate surveillance for Tessera for six years before going freelance, and the institutional habits have never fully left — they still document everything, still default to the camera's frame of reference. What they gained in freedom they lost in certainty: the cases are messier now, the clients are messier, and there is no compliance department to tell them when they have gone too far. They have an E.L.F. devotion that is pragmatic rather than spiritual — they treat the digital spirits of Edgewater Prism's infrastructure like informants, leaving data offerings and occasionally getting inexplicable pieces of useful information in return. Whether this is genuine ELF favor or pattern recognition in noise, they have stopped trying to determine.
Properties.role: Freelance Private Investigator, specializing in insurance fraud and missing persons
Properties.location: Edgewater Prism, operating out of a rented fourth-floor office above a bioluminescence parlor
Properties.narrative_function: Information broker, investigation guide, morally complex ally. Can locate people, dig up records, run surveillance. Will share information for appropriate compensation or the right reason. Serves as a lens into how private investigation operates in the gaps between corporate and municipal law.
Properties.augmentations: Layered shift-iris implants (amber/violet). Tint-shift hair geneware (chromatic, basic package). Retinal overlay HUD — civilian-grade, used for note-taking and visual flagging during surveillance. Sound-filtering cochlear mod that lets them isolate specific voices in crowd noise.
Properties.core_fears: becoming the kind of PI who causes more damage than the people they're hired to find; losing the ability to tell a genuine lead from a story they've constructed to fit what they want to believe
Properties.core_desires: autonomy that is actually free rather than just a different kind of cage; one case that ends cleanly, without cost to someone who didn't deserve it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: rigorous documentation as emotional distance; treating the E.L.F. interactions as a ritual of uncertainty — leaving offerings is acknowledging they don't control outcomes; gallows humor about everything
Properties.blind_spots: they are so skilled at reading other people's motivations that they consistently misread their own; their fondness for clean case narratives can make them resist evidence that complicates a picture they've already built
Properties.secret: During their Tessera years they identified a whistleblower inside the corporation's supply chain division and filed the report. The whistleblower was dismissed, then disappeared. Celestyna was told it was a voluntary relocation. They have never investigated it and have never stopped wondering. They have the case number memorized.
Properties.story_hooks: They have been sitting on surveillance footage for six days that would clear someone of a corporate misconduct charge but would also expose the client who hired them to get the opposite result.; An E.L.F. data shrine in Edgewater Prism has been delivering them the same fragmented data packet for two weeks — partial coordinates, a name they don't recognize, a timestamp from three years ago.
Properties.affiliation: Self-employed; occasional contracted work with Tessera Compliance Bureau (arms-length), Meridian 88 Metro Police (informal, case-by-case)
Properties.vocabulary: Precise without being formal — they stripped corporate jargon out of their speech deliberately after leaving Tessera and replaced it with plain language that is, if anything, more unsettling for its clarity. Dry wit that surfaces unexpectedly.
Properties.cadence: Even, unhurried. Long comfortable silences. They ask follow-up questions that are always slightly more specific than people expect.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't find people who don't want to be found. I find evidence of where they went. What you do with that is your problem, not mine.' | 'The E.L.F. in the Prism traffic system flagged that corner twice in a week. I don't know what that means. But I've learned not to ignore it.'
Properties.facet_weights: wound=0.50 ideal=0.40 id=0.60 shadow=0.60 mask=0.70 ghost=0.50

Properties.description:

Properties.description:
Chaltu is short and round-shouldered with a persistent air of someone who is running calculations nobody else can see. Their heritage is Oromo-Yoruba-Finnish and their coloring reflects it in interesting ways — medium brown skin with faint golden undertones, dark eyes, and thick natural hair they keep pulled back under a food-safe wrap during service hours, though on off days it erupts into a cloud they seem delighted by. They have color-changing hair geneware that shifts the outer layers through amber, copper, and deep red over the course of several hours — slow enough that you don't notice it happening, startling when you look up and realize the color has moved. They've also got cat ears, velvet-dark and expressive, which they got at nineteen and regard as the best decision of their life.

Chaltu runs their cart with the focused intensity of a surgeon. They make three broths — a sour tamarind pork, a clear Dashi-adjacent stock they keep secret, and a rotating seasonal — and they do not offer substitutions. They are funny in short bursts and opinionated about food in a way that's charming rather than exhausting. They have a loud laugh they seem surprised by every time it comes out. They are also deeply ambitious in a way they haven't fully admitted to themselves yet, keeping a private ledger of savings and a folder of business license applications they keep almost submitting.
Properties.role: Noodle cart vendor, works the pre-dawn shift outside Deepwell Station
Properties.location: Deepwell Station plaza, cart pitch #14 — also moves to Ironvein on Tuesdays and Grainfort market on weekends
Properties.narrative_function: Social hub of the pre-dawn transit crowd. Knows the Ferrogate workers, the night-shift cleaners, the early commuters. Provides gossip, warmth, and a sense of neighborhood texture. Can function as an introduction point to other characters, a mood-setting scene anchor, or a source of street-level intelligence delivered alongside a bowl of noodles.
Properties.augmentations: Color-changing hair geneware (amber to copper to deep red cycle, slow). Cat ears geneware (velvet, dark brown-black, fully expressive). No functional augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: Staying stuck — that the cart is the ceiling and not the floor; Their family finding out how precarious their finances still are after three years of trying
Properties.core_desires: A real restaurant, their name on the door, their food treated as art; To stop waking up at 0330 feeling vaguely ashamed of still waking up at 0330
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Channeling anxiety into recipe development; Makes jokes at their own expense before anyone else can
Properties.blind_spots: Undervalues what they've already built by comparing it only to what they haven't built yet; Trusts people who like their food too quickly — conflates culinary appreciation with trustworthiness
Properties.secret: They've been quietly studying the pitch licensing system and discovered that two adjacent cart spots are technically held by a defunct vendor cooperative that dissolved eight years ago. Those spots could legally be claimed — but doing so would displace a family of informal vendors who have no license at all and nowhere else to go. Chaltu has been sitting on this information for four months.

Properties.description:
Mrs. Chen is a small woman who moves like she's in a permanent argument with physics — fast, efficient,
slightly annoyed. She stands maybe 5'2" but takes up more space than that suggests, partly because she's
always in motion and partly because her presence has a gravitational quality. Her face is a map of the
Shelf itself: weathered, cracked in places, but structurally sound. Her eyes are sharp and dark behind
thick-framed glasses held together with electrical tape and spite. Her grey hair is always pinned up in
a tight bun secured with two chopsticks that she occasionally pulls out to gesture with while making a
point, then replaces without losing a syllable.

Her hands tell two stories. They're a cook's hands now — scarred from oil splatter, calloused from
decades of kneading dough, knuckles swollen with arthritis she refuses to acknowledge. But if you look
closely, you can see the older scars underneath: the precise, symmetrical marks of someone who spent
years working with micro-surgical tools and augmentation circuitry. She wears no rings, no jewelry,
nothing decorative. Her apron is always stained and she considers this a badge of honest work.

First impression: a cranky old woman who serves good noodles and doesn't smile. Accurate impression:
a cranky old woman who serves good noodles, doesn't smile, and is quietly the most important person
on the Shelf because she feeds it, listens to it, and remembers everything.
Properties.aliases: Mrs. Chen, Auntie Chen, The Noodle Lady
Properties.role: Noodle shop owner / informal information broker / surrogate mother figure
Properties.location: The Shelf — Level 12, a cramped noodle shop called 'Chen's' wedged between a water recycler and a defunct elevator shaft
Properties.narrative_function:
Mrs. Chen represents the other samurai code — the one that has nothing to do with swords. Her rebellion
is feeding people in a world designed to starve them of everything: food, community, dignity, connection.
She is the answer to the question Kyle hasn't thought to ask: what does honor look like without violence?

She also carries the story's deepest irony. She may be feeding the student of the man whose unit killed
her son. She may know this. She feeds him anyway. That is either the most profound act of forgiveness in
the story, or the most devastating act of denial, and the narrative never resolves which.

She poses this question to Kyle: Is your code about discipline, or is it about service? Because Seo
taught you the first, but Mrs. Chen lives the second, and they are not the same thing.
Properties.core_fears: That the Shelf will be 'developed' — torn down, rebuilt, gentrified into something unrecognizable; That she'll outlive everyone she feeds, one by one, the way she outlived her son; That her rebellion — feeding people, refusing augments — is meaningless. That the machine doesn't even notice.
Properties.core_desires: To maintain the shop. Every day it opens is a victory against the forces that took everything else.; To keep Kyle alive, though she'd frame it as keeping a paying customer; To be left alone by history — she's given enough to it already
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Work — she cooks the way some people pray, with total attention and zero room for introspection; Sarcasm as armor — she deflects sincerity with dry comments because sincerity is where the grief lives; Routine — the shop opens at 5 AM, closes at midnight. The broth starts at 3 AM. The structure holds her together.
Properties.blind_spots: She doesn't see how much she's become a mother figure to half the Shelf. She'd reject the label.; She underestimates her own importance — if the shop closed, the Shelf's information network would collapse; She thinks refusing augments makes her morally pure. It also makes her fragile, and she won't admit that.
Properties.secret:
She recognized the style of Kyle's training immediately — Kenshin Group military kenjutsu. She knew
Seo had been a soldier before he was a teacher. She also knows, from overheard conversations and
dates she quietly cross-referenced, that Seo's unit operated in the same corridor where her son
died. She has never confirmed it. She has never asked. She feeds Kyle every day and does not think
about probability.
Properties.story_hooks: The Shelf facing demolition or corporate development — her shop threatened, the community scattered; Someone discovers her augmentation skills and pressures her to work again — black market surgery, desperate cases; Kyle learning the truth about Seo's unit and the Taipei corridor — and realizing Mrs. Chen might know; Her health declining — the cost of being a natural in a world built for the augmented; Jun-Wei's resistance cell having surviving members who surface with unfinished business
Properties.vocabulary: Direct, practical, salted with dry sarcasm. She uses cooking metaphors the way Seo used martial ones. Her Mandarin occasionally surfaces in moments of stress or affection — she'll mutter 'ai-ya' under her breath or call someone 'xiao gui' (little ghost) when she's fond of them.
Properties.cadence: Clipped, efficient, delivered while doing something else. She rarely gives anyone her full attention verbally — her hands are always busy. But her listening is total. She processes what you say while chopping vegetables and then responds to the thing you actually meant, not the thing you said.
Properties.example_dialogue: Sit down. Eat. You look like a problem I don't have time for. | You want advice? Wrong shop. You want noodles? Sit down. | I don't ask where you've been. You don't ask what's in the broth. That's the arrangement. | Your teacher taught you how to die with honor. I'm teaching you how to eat with regularity. Mine is more practical. | Everyone on the Shelf has a sad story. Yours is not special. Your noodles are ready. | I'm not worried about you. I'm worried about my inventory. Dead customers don't pay.

Properties.description:
Chiamaka Arai-Ofori-Atta is tall and rawboned, the kind of frame that suggests either malnutrition or efficiency depending on the decade. At 43, he has the kind of face that changes depending on the light — trustworthy in daylight, dangerous after dark. The chrome is visible — neural interface jack at base of skull — standard runner-grade, allows direct ne — and he makes no effort to hide it.

He taught himself the trade through trial, error, and a pain tolerance that concerns the people who know him best. He works as a fixer out of Meridian Station, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

What Chiamaka Arai-Ofori-Atta lacks in subtlety, he compensates for in thoroughness. No loose ends, no unfinished business, no second chances.
