Properties.description:
Chiamaka is a compact woman of middle height whose stillness is her most immediately striking quality — she moves through spaces like she has already decided where everything is and does not need to rush toward it. Her skin is very dark, her natural hair grown out in thick silver-streaked coils she usually wraps in a printed cloth her mother sent from Lagos before communications became unreliable. She has geneware cat ears, pale grey with dark tips, a cosmetic mod she got in her forties when they were fashionable in the Helix Biosystems corporate wellness program — she kept them after retirement because her grandchildren like them and because she simply never bothered to reverse the procedure. Her eyes are chronically tired but her attention is absolute.

She is not a talkative woman. She communicates in economy — a question instead of a lecture, a bowl of food instead of a welcome speech. People who don't know her mistake her quietness for coldness; people who do know her understand she is one of the most carefully attentive people in Washburn Commons, who has noticed things about their neighbors that their neighbors have not noticed about themselves. She worries constantly about her grandchildren and expresses it by cooking too much food and asking too many questions about their friends.
Properties.role: Retired Helix Biosystems lab technician, now raising two grandchildren
Properties.location: Washburn Commons — Unit 7, Block C, a three-room apartment she has made into something warm through sheer force of textile and effort
Properties.narrative_function: Neighborhood observer and quiet information source; can provide insight into Helix Biosystems internal culture and practices from the worker's perspective; represents the human cost of corponation pension systems; anchor character for stories set in Washburn Commons family life
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic geneware cat ears (pale grey, dark-tipped); bone density support mesh in hips and lower spine (Helix standard retirement package); blood glucose regulator implant
Properties.core_fears: That she will not live long enough to see the grandchildren to adulthood; That her daughter — the children's mother — is dead rather than simply gone, and that the children will eventually ask her directly
Properties.core_desires: To give Adisa and Priya a stable childhood she feels she failed to give their mother; To sleep a full night without waking
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cooking as emotional labor and love language; Strict daily routine as a container for anxiety
Properties.blind_spots: She is so focused on the grandchildren's immediate safety that she sometimes cannot see their longer-term emotional needs; She has convinced herself she is 'managing fine' when she is exhausted down to the cellular level
Properties.secret: Her daughter Temitayo did not disappear in an accident. Chiamaka knows Temitayo is alive and working deep-cover for a Zheng-Dao corporate intelligence cell. Temitayo contacts her once every few months through encrypted message drops. Chiamaka has told no one, including the children, because she fears what it would mean if Helix Biosystems — her former employer — discovered the connection. She burns the messages after reading them.
Properties.story_hooks: An encrypted message from Temitayo arrives corrupted — Chiamaka needs someone she can cautiously trust to recover the data without exposing what it is; Priya has begun asking direct questions about her mother and Chiamaka is running out of deflections; she needs someone to talk to who is not inside the situation

Properties.description:
Chiamaka is short and compactly built, with the precise hands of someone who has trained the tremor out of their nervous system through ten thousand repetitions. Their skin is deep brown-black with bioluminescent patches they had inked along their collarbones and forearms — the bioluminescence pulses slowly when they are calm and quickens when they are excited, which makes them a very poor liar in dim lighting. They have color-changing hair currently set to a slow cycle through amber-to-rust tones; they change the cycle depending on season and mood, and their regulars track it as a barometric instrument for the shop's atmosphere.

Chi is the youngest full-time operator at The Guillotine and the busiest by appointment count. They have a gift for reading what a client wants even when the client cannot articulate it — they ask three questions and then go quiet, and the quiet is not uncomfortable. They are also quietly accumulating power in the Ferment Quarter social ecosystem, because the barbershop chair is where people say things they would not say anywhere else, and Chi has a memory like archival storage and a policy of never speaking ill — only listening. Off the clock they are louder, funnier, and significantly more likely to start a dance in a hallway.

Properties.narrative_function: Social hub and passive intelligence network — clients tell their barber everything; can be a source of neighborhood gossip, social connections, or backstory on local figures; also functions as a local color character who can reflect the texture of the Ferment Quarter scene
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent skin patches (collarbones and forearms, pulse-reactive); color-changing hair (currently amber-to-rust cycle); subdermal haptic feedback layer in fingertips (professional — allows precision depth sensing for skin work)
Properties.core_fears: Being ordinary — indistinguishable from the surrounding noise; Someone using the things they've heard in the chair to cause harm
Properties.core_desires: To open their own shop with their name on it by thirty; To be known as someone who made people feel seen
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Aesthetic transformation — when stressed, they change their hair cycle or add a new visual element; Channeling anxiety into productivity and client work
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much people project onto them — they think they are facilitating others' self-expression but they are also shaping what people think is possible; Their hunger for recognition occasionally edges toward approval-seeking

Properties.description:
Chiamaka has the kind of face that is beautiful in a way that takes a moment to resolve — wide-set dark eyes, a long jaw, a nose that has been broken and healed slightly crooked, which they consider an improvement. Their hair is grown long on top and cut close at the sides, currently dyed a deep amber that is growing out at the roots into black. Bioluminescent freckles run across both cheekbones and the bridge of their nose, a genemod that was fashionable a decade ago and that they have kept because they find it useful in the dark. They dress in layers of practical clothing with a great number of pockets, all of which serve a purpose.

Chiamaka came to Meridian 88 with the Seventh Coastal Movement — a caravan of climate refugees from the drowned lowlands east of what used to be Lagos, where their Igbo family had mixed with Samoan shipwright families over three generations of coastal labor. They have been in the Gateway processing overflow for seven months, which is four months longer than they were told. They work as an informal translator and advocate for other caravan members, navigating the Meridian 88 resettlement bureaucracy with a simmering precision that occasionally flares into something that frightens officials. They are not angry in a way that is hot. They are angry in a way that is patient.
Properties.role: climate refugee, expelled citizen, caravan support worker
Properties.location: Escanaba Gateway, temporary processing overflow — a repurposed cargo hangar on the eastern dock
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver (bureaucratic navigation problems, missing persons within the refugee system), information source on Meridian 88's resettlement processes and their failures, emotional anchor for the caravan community, potential ally with a network of people who owe them favors
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent freckles (cosmetic geneware, cheekbones and nose bridge, amber-warm light). No other augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: that the people they're responsible for will be dispersed before they can secure anything lasting for them; that their anger will eventually make them less effective rather than more
Properties.core_desires: a door with their name on a lease behind it — any door, anywhere in the city; to see one of the caravan's children enrolled in a school with a fixed address
Properties.coping_mechanisms: bureaucratic precision — the log, the records, the documentation of everything; walking the perimeter; translating for others, which requires full attention and leaves no room for despair
Properties.blind_spots: they have made themselves so essential to the collective that they haven't built anything for themselves — no personal plan if the collective dissolves; they sometimes push people to fight battles they're not ready to fight because Chiamaka is ready
Properties.secret: Chiamaka was not technically displaced by the flooding — they had a processing job with a Zheng-Dao logistics subsidiary in the coastal network and could have applied for corporate relocation. They left with the caravan instead because a family member asked them to, and that family member died crossing the hyperlane corridor near Lambeau Terminus. Chiamaka has told no one this. They carry the dead person's ID chip in their left boot.
Properties.story_hooks: Twelve-year-old caravan member Tobias Faatoafe-Musa (a distant cousin) has vanished from the overflow facility. The Gateway security log shows him leaving voluntarily. Chiamaka knows he would never leave without telling them. They need someone to look into it who can move through the city in ways they cannot.; Chiamaka has found a procedural error in Meridian 88's resettlement framework that would, if properly filed, advance thirty-seven caravan cases simultaneously. They need someone with digital access to help them file it before the quarterly review window closes in six days.
Properties.affiliation: Seventh Coastal Movement caravan collective; informal advocacy with no organizational backing
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and formal in bureaucratic contexts, slipping into a warmer creole register with caravan members. Igbo exclamations under stress. Their Samoan grandmother's habit of using fish species as metaphors for human behavior.
Properties.cadence: Measured and even, with a quality of absolute attention — they speak as if recording testimony
Properties.example_dialogue: 'As it stands, your file has been in Secondary Review since the fourteenth. That is not a processing step. That is a file that someone has decided not to look at. Those are different problems with different solutions.' | 'My grandmother would say that man is a flatfish — he sees everything from one side and calls it the whole ocean.'

Properties.description:
Chiamaka is a living portfolio. Every visible inch of their skin below the neck is a demonstration of their craft: shifting bioluminescent patterns that bloom and fade with body temperature, embedded chromatic scales along their shoulders that catch light like a starling's wing, and a full sleeve of reactive biosymbolism on their left arm that darkens in cold and brightens in warmth. They keep their face deliberately unmodified — a professional choice to let clients focus on the work, not compete with it. They are stocky and deliberate in movement, with close-cropped natural hair and dark eyes that have the quality of paying careful attention.

Their shop, Skin Liturgy, is a converted ground-floor space in a reclaimed building in Pilsen Veil, hung with examples of their work on cured synthetic skin panels. Chiamaka approaches body modification as spiritual practice, not fashion — each piece is preceded by a long consultation they call 'reading,' in which they try to understand what a client is trying to become rather than what they think they want. This makes them slow, selective, and expensive relative to their tier, and clients come from across the city. They are professionally gentle and personally guarded, with a dry wit that emerges only when they're comfortable.
Properties.role: Gene-mod body artist and tattoo practitioner
Properties.location: Pilsen Veil
Properties.narrative_function: Gateway to Pilsen Veil's art community; can identify geneware brands and quality; long-term character relationship builder; can provide physical transformation as a story beat
Properties.augmentations: Extensive cosmetic geneware (bioluminescent dermal patterns, chromatic scale implants, reactive biosymbolism sleeve); subdermal steadying implants in their hands for fine work precision; olfactory enhancement to detect rejection responses in fresh modifications
Properties.core_fears: Doing irreversible harm to a client's body or sense of self; Being truly seen — the professional mask is so practiced it's become load-bearing
Properties.core_desires: For their work to help people inhabit themselves more fully; To finish their own body as a complete artwork — though they're not sure what 'finished' means
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The ritual of consultation as a way of being present with someone else's need rather than their own; Precise documentation — they photograph and archive every piece they've made
Properties.blind_spots: They read clients with extraordinary insight but apply almost none of that skill to their own emotional life
Properties.secret: Three years ago they did a significant gene-mod for a client who was clearly in a dissociative mental health crisis; they completed the work against their better judgment because the client's payment covered Skin Liturgy's rent for four months. The client disappeared afterward and Chiamaka does not know if they are alive.
Properties.story_hooks: A client came in with a modification request that matches a pattern Chiamaka has seen on three other people in the past month — all of whom gave a different story for how they chose the design; The missing client from three years ago has resurfaced, dramatically transformed, and is leaving Chiamaka messages they find both relieving and deeply unsettling; A corponation talent acquisitions team wants to license Chiamaka's biosymbolism patterns for a mass-produced cosmetic line — the offer would solve all their financial problems and erase their artistic identity

Properties.description:
Pilsen was always a district that spoke through its walls. The murals were the neighborhood's voice — declarations of identity painted on brick in colors that refused to be quiet. When the corporate sovereignty treaties arrived, the murals became something more: camouflage, encryption, resistance. The Veil is what happens when an entire neighborhood learns to hide in plain sight, encoding its defiance in art that the corporations can see but cannot read.

The National Museum of Mexican Art became the Veil's anchor institution, surviving the sovereignty transition by reclassifying itself as a cultural preservation archive — a legal designation that granted it limited immunity from corporate acquisition under the Meridian 88 Heritage Compact. The Museum's directors understood something that most community leaders did not: in a world where everything is data, declaring yourself a repository of irreplaceable cultural data is a form of sovereignty. The Museum now operates as a combination art space, community archive, data vault, and diplomatic embassy. Its basement levels house servers that store the neighborhood's collective memory — birth records, property deeds, family histories, and the original mural designs that prove who was here first.

The streets of Pilsen Veil are a gallery that never closes. Murals cover every surface, but they have evolved beyond decoration. Augmented-reality layers are painted into the pigments using techniques developed by the district's artist-engineers — visible only to specific neural-interface frequencies, invisible to corporate surveillance sweeps. A mural of the Virgin of Guadalupe, viewed on the right frequency, becomes a map of safe houses. A abstract pattern on a warehouse wall becomes a schedule of community meetings. The corporations know the Veil's art contains hidden information. They have spent years trying to decode it. They have failed, because the encryption is not technological — it is cultural. You cannot read it without understanding what it means, and understanding what it means requires being from here.

The galleries that once sold to tourists now operate as front businesses for the district's real economy: information brokerage, identity fabrication, and the production of cultural artifacts that double as encrypted communications devices. Pilsen Veil is the place you go when you need to become someone else, when you need a message delivered that cannot be intercepted, or when you need to disappear into a community that has been practicing invisibility for generations.
Properties.aliases: Lower West Side, Pilsen, The Veil, Mural Mile
Properties.demographics: Mexican-American core community with growing populations of artists, dissidents, and identity refugees from across M88. Approximately 35,000 residents, predominantly Tier 1 with a significant untier-ed population hidden within the community's informal housing networks.
Properties.economy: Surface economy: galleries, cafes, cultural tourism from mid-tier visitors. Actual economy: identity fabrication, encrypted communications, information brokerage, and cultural artifact production. The Museum's heritage archive generates income through access fees that fund community infrastructure.
Properties.power_structure: The Museum's directors function as de facto community leaders, leveraging the Heritage Compact's legal protections. Artist collectives control neighborhood security through the mural network. No single corporation holds jurisdiction, though Mirrorwell Media has made repeated attempts to acquire the district's AR-art technology.
Properties.dangers: Mirrorwell Media's ongoing attempts to crack the mural encryption — success would expose the entire community network; Identity fabrication attracts dangerous clients with dangerous enemies; The Heritage Compact's legal protections are subject to corporate renegotiation every decade — the next review is approaching; Gentrification pressure from mid-tier workers priced out of the Garret; Corporate moles posing as artists infiltrating the mural network
Properties.opportunities: Identity fabrication services: new faces, new tiers, new histories; Encrypted communications through art — messages that cannot be intercepted by any known corporate system; The Museum's data vault contains information that powerful people would pay to access or suppress; Artist-engineers command premium rates for AR-layer work throughout M88; A rare district where corporate surveillance is effectively blind
Properties.story_hooks: A mural has appeared overnight that nobody claims to have painted — its AR layer contains coordinates pointing to something buried beneath the Museum, and the Museum's directors are terrified; Mirrorwell Media has hired a street artist from outside the district to infiltrate the mural network — the artist is having second thoughts and needs extraction; Someone is commissioning identity packages for an entire community — fifty people need to become fifty different people by the end of the month, and the reason why is classified at a level that suggests government, not corporate
Properties.sights: Murals on every surface — layered, evolving, containing hidden AR information visible only on specific frequencies; The National Museum of Mexican Art: a fortified cultural institution with diplomatic-grade security; Gallery storefronts with art in the windows and something else entirely in the back rooms; Street artists working in real-time, adding new layers to existing murals — updating the district's living encryption; Candle-lit altars on street corners, mixing Catholic iconography with cybernetic imagery
Properties.sounds: Live music from gallery openings that double as community organizing events; The scratch of paint on brick — artists working at all hours, maintaining the Veil; Hushed conversations in gallery back rooms where identities are being fabricated; Church bells from the basilica competing with the hum of the Museum's server cooling systems; The absence of corporate announcement systems — one of the few districts where the air is not full of advertising
Properties.smells: Spray paint and acrylic — the constant smell of creation; Copal incense from street altars; Coffee from gallery cafes that serve as meeting points; Old brick and plaster — the smell of walls that have been painted and repainted for a century
Properties.feel: A district wrapped in its own art like armor. Pilsen Veil feels like a secret you are being told in a language you almost understand. The beauty is genuine, but it is also functional — every painted surface is a wall in both senses of the word.

Properties.description:
Chiamaka is a broad-shouldered woman with deep brown skin mapped by twenty-two years of shift work — early mornings have carved permanent shadows beneath her eyes, and her knuckles are calloused from gripping the manual override bar during power fluctuations. She wears her Ferrogate Transit uniform with a particular pride that borders on defiance, the collar pins perfectly level, the cuffs always turned exactly once. Her geneware is modest: irises that shift from amber to pale green depending on her blood pressure, which she got cheap from a stall in the Burnished Market and has never replaced. Her silver-streaked locs are pinned under her operator's cap except on rest days, when she lets them down to her shoulders.

She is the kind of woman who knows every regular on the 6:14 eastbound by name and by their bad habits. She has opinions about everything — the state of the magline infrastructure, the price of cassava flour, the particular incompetence of Ferrogate middle management — and she will share them freely if you give her the slightest opening. Beneath the bluster is someone who has taken quiet pride in the fact that in twenty-two years she has never been more than ninety seconds off schedule, and she considers this a form of art.
Properties.role: Transit operator, Ferrogate magline tram, Deepwell Station loop
Properties.location: Deepwell Station, The Narrows
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and information hub — she has seen everyone who rides the line, knows rumors from a dozen neighborhoods, and can serve as an unwitting or deliberate information source. Can also be a quest giver when something goes wrong on the line.
Properties.augmentations: Amber-to-green photosensitive iris geneware (cheap market grade). Ferrogate-standard neural throttle link for tram sync — allows her to feel the tram's speed and braking load as proprioceptive sensation. Left knee has a basic cartilage scaffold implant from a work injury.
Properties.core_fears: Being made redundant by full automation; Her daughter leaving Meridian 88 and never coming back
Properties.core_desires: To be recognized as essential, not just functional; For the city's transit system to actually serve the people who built it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritualistic schedule-keeping as a form of control; Venting grievances loudly to anyone who will listen
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes competence in people who mirror her own work ethic, leading to misplaced trust; Cannot accept that sometimes lateness is not a moral failure
Properties.secret: In 2193 she deliberately held a tram two minutes past schedule to prevent a Ferrogate internal security team from reaching a platform where she knew a family of undocumented workers was trying to board. She has never told anyone and considers it the best thing she ever did.
Properties.story_hooks: She noticed a passenger boarding the eastbound loop every night at 02:00 carrying something heavy in a sealed crate — they always ride to the same dead stop and never come back the same direction; Ferrogate management is threatening to reclassify her line as fully automated; she is quietly organizing her fellow operators and needs someone to deliver documents to a labor mediator in Hamtramck Enclave without Ferrogate's internal watchers knowing

Properties.description:
Chiamaka Vestergaard-Suleimanović is precise in the way that some people are precise — not as a personality choice but as a metabolic fact, a condition of being. They are of moderate height and slight build, with deep brown skin, natural hair grown out to a medium length they wear in a carefully arranged protective style. Their most striking feature is purely cosmetic: bioluminescent freckles across the bridge of their nose and upper cheekbones, in a warm amber-gold, a gift to themselves on their thirtieth birthday. They dress in neat, unremarkable clothing and always, always wear gloves — not from a contamination protocol they've imported home, but because they find the sensation of touching most surfaces without them distracting.

They are the Metro Police Evidence Division's most technically accomplished analyst and their most quietly difficult employee. They have a gift for finding what the evidence says rather than what the investigation wants it to say, which has produced thirteen cases where their analysis materially contradicted the arresting officer's narrative. Four of those cases resulted in charges being dropped. The other nine resulted in paperwork, meetings, and a standing low-level friction with supervisors that neither side has ever directly addressed. Chiamaka does not care. The evidence is the evidence.
Properties.role: Forensic Technician, Metro Police Evidence Division
Properties.location: Grand Corridor
Properties.narrative_function: Technical expert and potential whistleblower — someone who can tell players what the physical evidence actually shows versus what the official record claims. A source of forensic information, a person who can authenticate or discredit evidence, and a character whose professional integrity has made them quietly vulnerable within the institution.
Properties.augmentations: Haptic sensitivity modulation implants in both hands (reduces ambient tactile input; improves fine-detail analysis precision). Olfactory enhancement mod for trace chemical analysis. Cosmetic: bioluminescent amber-gold freckles across nose and cheekbones.
Properties.core_fears: Being made complicit in a wrongful conviction through their own analysis being misrepresented; Losing the clarity of their own judgment — having someone successfully pressure them into seeing what isn't there
Properties.core_desires: The evidence record to be accurate — always, without exception; To be understood by at least one person in the institution as an asset rather than a problem
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Extreme methodological rigor as a form of ethical fortification; Detailed personal notes kept parallel to official documentation; The sensory comfort of their gloves and controlled environments
Properties.blind_spots: Their faith in physical evidence as a corrective to corruption underestimates how thoroughly evidence itself can be manufactured or suppressed before it reaches them; They can be slow to read interpersonal threat — a skill less exercised than technical analysis
Properties.secret: They have a personal encrypted record of every case where their analysis was materially altered in the official report before going to prosecution — seventeen instances over eight years. They have never used this record. They are not sure who they would give it to. They add to it with the careful precision they apply to everything.
Properties.story_hooks: Evidence connected to a player or someone they care about has passed through Chiamaka's lab — and their preliminary analysis does not match the official version of events. They are not sure what to do about this discrepancy and have so far only added it to their private record.; Chiamaka needs someone to physically retrieve a piece of evidence that was removed from official custody before they could analyze it — it went somewhere the Metro Police cannot follow without generating a record.; Their encrypted personal record of altered case reports has been detected — not yet traced to them, but they know the system has been probed. They need to get the record out before it disappears along with them.
Properties.affiliation: Meridian 88 Metro Police — Evidence Division, Grand Corridor Central Processing
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, technical, occasionally formal to the point of seeming stilted. Dislikes vague language intensely and will quietly correct it. Warmer registers emerge slowly in trusted company.
Properties.cadence: Even and measured. Pauses carefully. Rarely uses filler words.
Properties.example_dialogue: The report says 'consistent with.' I need to be specific: 'consistent with' means it doesn't contradict the theory. It does not mean it supports the theory. These are not the same thing. | I understand what you want the evidence to say. I can't help you with that. I can tell you what it does say, which is different. | To be specific — and this does matter — this sample was handled after the chain of custody was broken. Anything downstream of that point is inadmissible and potentially fabricated. I'm noting that in my report.

Properties.description:
Grand Boulevard was the beating heart of Bronzeville — the street where the Regal Theater stood, where the chess players gathered at the checkerboard, where Muddy Waters and Mahalia Jackson and a thousand other voices defined what American music would become. It was not just a neighborhood. It was a frequency. And when corporate sovereignty arrived, that frequency did not die. It went underground.

The surface of Grand Corridor is a Cinderblock AI residential district, an extension of the Bronzeline development — clean towers, tiered housing, compliance monitoring. Cinderblock acquired the old Bronzeville landmarks and preserved them as cultural assets: the former Regal Theater building is now a Waxwing Neuromedia immersive-experience venue where audiences can neural-share the memories of jazz performances from a century ago. The experience is extraordinary. It is also theft — the memories were harvested from elderly Bronzeville residents through a Waxwing program that offered free neural-interface installation in exchange for memory-access licensing. The residents did not understand what they were signing. Waxwing understood perfectly.

Beneath the corporate surface, the Grand Corridor's basements and sub-levels house the most important underground music scene in Meridian 88. The clubs operate in spaces that predate the sovereignty era — former speakeasies, storage basements, utility vaults — connected by passages that mirror the surface streets one level down. The music is live, unaugmented, played on instruments that do not require power and voices that do not require amplification. Neural-interface enhancement is prohibited in the underground clubs by unanimous consensus. The performers and audiences want the imperfect, human version of the sound. They want the crackle. They want the breath. They want the thing that Waxwing's memory-harvested immersive experiences cannot replicate because it was never a memory — it was a moment.

The cultural war between the surface and the underground defines Grand Corridor's daily life. Cinderblock and Waxwing profit from Bronzeville's heritage by packaging it as content. The underground preserves that heritage by practicing it, live, in the dark, for audiences that pay in cash and keep their mouths shut. The two economies coexist in the same district, separated by a floor. The corporate tenants upstairs attend Waxwing memory-share events and feel connected to history. The musicians downstairs play until their fingers bleed and feel connected to the future. Both are right. Neither will acknowledge the other.

King Drive still runs through the center of Grand Corridor, the Walk of Fame plaques continuing north from Bronzeline. But here, someone has been adding plaques — unauthorized bronze markers appearing overnight, commemorating people the official history left out. The janitors. The dishwashers. The women who cleaned the Regal Theater and hummed the songs while they swept. Cinderblock security removes them. They reappear. It has been happening for three years. Nobody knows who is making them.
Properties.aliases: Grand Boulevard, Bronzeville North, The Corridor of Sound, The Grand
Properties.demographics: Surface: Tier 2-3 corporate residents, predominantly Cinderblock-affiliated. Underground: displaced Bronzeville community members, musicians, cultural preservationists. The underground population is uncounted — estimated at 3,000-5,000 operating in basement-level spaces throughout the district.
Properties.economy: Waxwing Neuromedia's memory-share venue generates the district's primary corporate revenue. Cinderblock's residential management provides supplementary income. The underground club economy operates on cash, barter, and the social currency of cultural authenticity. Soul food from underground kitchens commands premium prices from those who know where to find it.
Properties.power_structure: Cinderblock AI and Waxwing Neuromedia share corporate jurisdiction. The underground music scene is governed by a loose confederation of club operators and elder musicians whose authority derives from cultural respect, not force. The two power structures coexist by mutual ignorance — the corporations know the underground exists but find it easier to pretend otherwise.
Properties.dangers: Waxwing's memory-harvesting program continues to target elderly residents with exploitative licensing agreements; Underground clubs risk corporate raids — discovery would end the scene and displace the community again; Cinderblock surveillance in the residential blocks makes surface-to-underground movement risky; The unauthorized Walk of Fame plaques have become a political flashpoint — Cinderblock security is escalating enforcement; Cultural erasure: the corporate version of Bronzeville's history is slowly replacing the real one in public memory
Properties.opportunities: The underground club network is an information exchange disguised as entertainment; Waxwing's memory-harvesting technology, if stolen, has applications that would interest every faction in M88; The unauthorized plaque-maker is a folk hero — finding and protecting them would earn significant community loyalty; Underground soul food operations need supply chain support from districts like Little Furnace; The cultural war generates demand for intermediaries who can move between surface and underground
Properties.story_hooks: Waxwing Neuromedia has discovered that its memory-share recordings contain something unexpected — the harvested memories include experiences that the donors could not have had, as if the memories themselves have been growing, adding scenes that never happened, and the Regal Theater venue is showing audiences visions of events that have not occurred yet; The unauthorized plaque-maker has been identified — she is a Cinderblock employee working in the residential management office, and she has been using corporate fabrication equipment to make the plaques on her night shift, and she has just made one with Kyle's name on it; An underground club has received a challenge: a Waxwing-sponsored performer wants to play a live set in the basement venue, unaugmented, to prove that the corporate version of the music can match the underground. The club scene is divided — some see an opportunity for exposure, others see the beginning of co-optation
Properties.sights: Corporate residential towers above, their lobbies decorated with Bronzeville memorabilia as corporate art; The Waxwing Neuromedia venue in the former Regal Theater building — historic facade, holographic marquee; Unauthorized Walk of Fame plaques appearing on King Drive, commemorating unnamed community members; Basement club entrances hidden behind service doors, marked with symbols only the initiated recognize; The contrast: curated heritage above, living culture below, separated by a single floor
Properties.sounds: Surface: Waxwing memory-share audio bleeding from the venue — ghosts of performances, technically perfect; Underground: live jazz, blues, and gospel from basement clubs — imperfect, breathing, human; The low rumble of the Cinderblock server farms that underlie the residential blocks; Foot traffic on King Drive — tourists by day, musicians by night, the sidewalk serving both; The sound of a saxophone through a basement ventilation grate — the underground leaking upward
Properties.smells: Underground club atmosphere: sweat, whiskey, the brass-and-reed smell of live instruments; Surface level: corporate-standard filtered air with Waxwing's branded scent overlay; The old smell of the underground passages — century-old brick, coal dust, the city's memory; Food from underground kitchen operations: cornbread, greens, catfish — soul food prepared in speakeasy conditions
Properties.feel: A district at war with itself over who owns its own history. Grand Corridor feels like standing between two speakers playing the same song in different keys — one pristine and recorded, one raw and live. The dissonance is the most honest sound in Meridian 88.

Properties.description:
Chibundo Ferreira-Yupik has no legal existence. No biometric registration, no UBC account, no corponation employment history, no Ferrogate transit record. They erased themselves from Meridian 88's surface datanet eleven years ago with painstaking, elegant precision, and they have spent every year since helping others do the same — for a fee, always for a fee. They are of middling height, slight, with warm sienna skin and close-cropped natural hair. Their most striking feature is what they've done to their biometric profile: geneware has altered their iris patterns every eighteen months for the last decade, and a subdermal signal-scatter mesh makes their face present differently to every facial recognition node they pass. To cameras, they are a continuous glitch. To people, they are vivid and specific — dark eyes that track everything, hands that are always moving, a smile that arrives half a second before it should, like they already knew the joke.

They operate out of the Abyssal Threshold transit corridors, never sleeping in the same cache twice. Their clients are people fleeing — debt collectors, abusive partnerships, corponation indenturement, the occasional actual criminal. Chibundo does not ask why. They ask for documentation of identity, ask for Φ40-200 depending on complexity, and they provide the tools of vanishing: signal-scatter protocols, route maps to communities that do not report to the surface grid, contacts within the Bore Rat communities who will accept someone new. They are not a forger exactly — they don't create false identities. They create absences.
Properties.role: The Disappeared — identity broker and document ghost
Properties.location: Abyssal Threshold, mobile — no fixed residence
Properties.narrative_function: Information broker, access point to the disappeared community, moral complexity engine — they help people vanish, which is sometimes heroic and sometimes enables people who deserve to be found.
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal facial signal-scatter mesh (disrupts facial recognition scanning); geneware iris-pattern modification (changed every 18 months, currently deep violet with fractal rings); fingerprint-ablation treatment (repeated chemical, no ridge pattern); no other modifications
Properties.core_fears: being found — specifically by whoever they ran from originally; accidentally sending someone to safety that turns out to be worse than what they fled
Properties.core_desires: to be genuinely unknown — not just to systems but to themselves, to shed the person they were before; connection that does not require them to be legible
Properties.coping_mechanisms: hypervigilant route-planning as anxiety management; dark humor about identity and absence; E.L.F. devotion as a form of spiritual anchoring — they pray to the digital spirits of abandoned surveillance systems
Properties.blind_spots: has spent so long helping others disappear that they have lost track of who they actually are; makes choices by elimination — 'not that, not that' — but rarely by genuine desire
Properties.secret: They did not erase themselves to escape oppression. They erased themselves because they witnessed a Tessera executive ordering the deletion of a Tier 1 settlement's life-support records — which killed 31 people when the automated systems shut down. They intended to surface the information. Then they realized they would not survive doing so. They vanished instead. The data-package is still encrypted on a drive in their oldest cache-hole, and they have not touched it in nine years.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone Chibundo helped disappear five years ago has resurfaced — dead, on the surface grid, with an identity that should not exist. Either they were found, or they chose to come back, or something used their ghost identity.; The encrypted data-package from the Tessera massacre has begun broadcasting a low-level signal — the E.L.F. inhabiting the drive has awakened and is trying to be heard.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; known and trusted by Undertow network; unknown to surface authorities
Properties.vocabulary: Technically sophisticated about systems and data; uses absence-language constantly ('null value', 'blank field', 'signal-loss'). Occasionally slips into old surface slang that dates them.
Properties.cadence: Fast and elliptical — leaves the end of sentences implied rather than spoken, as if finishing them might make them too findable.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't make you someone else. I make you a blank field. What you write in it after — that's yours.' | 'Null's not nothing. Nothing is a value. Null means the system doesn't have the question yet.' | 'You want to disappear? Tell me what from. Not why. From. The from is the map.'

Properties.description:
Chibundo is a lean, precise man of medium height with dark brown skin and close-cropped silver hair that went grey early and which he has never dyed because he thinks it gives him authority. His eyes have patterned irises — a cosmetic mod from his twenties, pale amber with a geometric ring detail — and he wears thin-framed magnifier lenses clipped over them when appraising merchandise, which is most of the time. He dresses in clean, practical layers: collared shirts buttoned to the throat, a long vest with a dozen interior pockets, and boots with magnetic clasps. His pawn shop, MERIDIAN RECLAMATION SERVICES, occupies a narrow storefront in the Burnished Market with every centimeter of wall space covered in shelving. He has a system for everything and will tell you, unprompted, why the system is correct.

Chibundo is smart in a way that costs him socially — he is always the most prepared person in the room and he knows it and he cannot fully hide that he knows it. He is not cruel, but he is exact: he will tell you the precise market value of your grandmother's jewelry and he will not soften it. His secondary business, data brokering, operates through a handshake network of regular clients who pay him for access to local information — property transfer records, employment movement, minor corporate scheduling leaks. He is not political. He does not care who buys the data as long as they pay and do not bring violence to his door.
Properties.role: Pawn shop owner, small-time data broker
Properties.location: The Burnished Market, Ironvein
Properties.narrative_function: Information source and gear acquisition point. Can appraise, buy, and occasionally procure specific items through his network. Will sell data about local power movements for the right price. Quest giver when something valuable comes through his shop that he cannot handle alone.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned cosmetic irises (amber geometric). Subdermal RFID scanner in right palm — lets him read item authentication chips by touch. Basic memory buffer implant for cataloguing inventory.
Properties.core_fears: Losing the shop — the one thing he built entirely himself; Being proven wrong about someone he trusted with information
Properties.core_desires: Financial stability so absolute that no one can displace him; To be recognized as skilled and meticulous without having to explain himself
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Retreating into inventory and organization tasks when emotionally dysregulated; Translating emotional problems into logistical ones he can solve
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes everyone is operating in rational self-interest like he does; consistently surprised by spite; Does not recognize when his precision reads as contempt
Properties.secret: He has a standing encrypted file on a client — a mid-level Axiom procurement officer — that contains evidence of corporate fraud. He has never sold it or used it. He keeps it as insurance, but he also keeps it because part of him is waiting for the courage to do something righteous with it, and he is ashamed that he hasn't yet.
Properties.story_hooks: An unusual piece of tech came through his shop — clearly military-grade, clearly stripped of its serial identifiers, and clearly not something a civilian should have brought him to pawn. The seller hasn't come back for it. He wants someone to find out where it came from before it becomes his problem.; His Zheng-Dao contact has gone quiet for three weeks. The last data packet they sent him was corrupted and he can only read fragments, but the fragments reference a location in the Narrows and a date that has already passed.; Someone in the market has been undercutting his data-brokering prices by such precise margins that they clearly have access to his client list. He needs to know who leaked it.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; dues-paying member of The Oxidian Market vendors guild (affiliate chapter, Ironvein branch); rumored to have an information-sharing arrangement with a Zheng-Dao mid-level logistics manager
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and economic. Uses technical and commercial vocabulary fluently. Does not use filler words. Will correct factual errors in other people's sentences mid-conversation.
Properties.cadence: Even and measured. Speaks in complete sentences. Rarely raises his voice.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'That's not accurate — the Ferrogate mark on the base plate dates this unit to 2191, not 2195. The difference is about forty quanta. I'll give you ninety-five.' | 'I sell information about what is happening, not about what I think will happen. Those are different products at different prices.' | 'Bring it back in a week. If no one else has come asking for it, I'll know it's actually yours to sell.'

Properties.description:
Chidinma wears the caravan on her body like a second skin — she is draped in the layered evidence of ten years of wandering trade routes, and the effect is simultaneously chaotic and perfectly intentional. Her dark brown skin is warm and clear except for three thin ritual scars on her left cheekbone, and her hair grows in a massive natural cloud that she pins with whatever she has at hand: transit tokens, stylus caps, a single wing-shaped bone clasp that came from somewhere she won't specify. Her irises are modified to display a slow-spinning geometric pattern, amber and rust, which she uses as a distraction tool in negotiations more often than she admits. She is medium-height and stocky, with the particular physical confidence of someone accustomed to moving heavy loads.

Chidinma runs a one-woman mobile trade operation between the outer transit corridors, specializing in the categories of goods that regulated markets won't carry — not weapons or pharmaceuticals, but the strange soft contraband of a corponation city: unbranded food that doesn't carry a Zheng-Dao or Axiom nutritional stamp, books printed on actual paper, unlicensed music files, hand-made items that would violate Ringo manufacturing monopolies, and the occasional comfort object from somewhere far away that someone desperately needs to feel like themselves again. She is not sentimental about this. It is commerce. But she is extremely good at identifying what a person actually needs, which is the core of the business.
Properties.role: wandering trader and caravan member, deals in small luxuries and contraband comfort items
Properties.location: Grand Crossing Gate market stalls, currently stall seven (temporary)
Properties.narrative_function: Equipment and goods source for players operating outside official markets, information broker (she hears everything at the stall), quest giver for trade route problems and supplier disputes, window into the informal economy of Meridian 88.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises, amber and rust geometric (cosmetic mod, installed age 24). Enhanced scent glands, subtle — helps her assess goods quality and detect synthetic substitutes. Sub-dermal storage pocket in left forearm (small, holds data chips and small valuables).
Properties.core_fears: being locked into a single location permanently; her supplier network collapsing and leaving her with nothing to trade
Properties.core_desires: to accumulate enough capital to fund a full caravan of her own; to find the specific type of hand-carved wooden comb made in the village her grandmother came from — she has been looking for years and is not quite willing to admit why
Properties.coping_mechanisms: constant forward motion — she is uncomfortable when she stays in one place more than two weeks; humor that functions as deflection; obsessive inventory management
Properties.blind_spots: reads financial transactions with exceptional clarity but is genuinely blind to when people are attached to her emotionally, tends to interpret all relationship gestures as part of a transaction she doesn't understand
Properties.secret: The 'accounting dispute' that split her from her last caravan was actually a cover story. She witnessed caravan leadership broker a deal that would have handed transit route information to Ferrogate Transit in exchange for safe passage, which would have gotten several Q-zero families using the route captured. She sabotaged the deal and then had to leave before anyone figured out it was her. One of the caravan leaders is still looking for whoever did it.
Properties.story_hooks: One of Chidinma's regular customers — a Q-zero family she supplies with food and comfort goods — has gone missing from their usual location, and she is asking questions carefully because she can't ask officially; A Ferrogate Transit investigator has been watching her stall for three days and she knows it; she needs help determining whether this is about the caravan sabotage or something else entirely
Properties.affiliation: Loosely part of the Grand Crossing itinerant trader collective, no formal caravan affiliation currently (between caravans after a dispute she describes as 'a business disagreement about accounting')
Properties.vocabulary: Mercantile precision mixed with warm market-trader patter; code-switches into Igbo when doing mental calculations she doesn't want overheard
Properties.cadence: Energetic and rhythmic, like someone who has made the same pitch a thousand times and still believes in it
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Listen, here's the thing — you want the Zheng-Dao stamp on your food, you can get it anywhere. You want food that actually tastes like something, you come to me.' | 'Exactly right, exactly right. Now — are you buying or are we still in the part where you pretend you're not buying?'

Properties.description:
Colette is small and moves quickly, the way people do when they've spent years navigating narrow corridors between occupied beds. She has warm dark skin, natural hair worn in a high puff that she wraps in a green cloth when on shift, and eyes that are an unsettling pale grey — a side effect of a retinal enhancement she got from a discount clinic at twenty-three that was slightly misaligned and gives her a perpetual look of seeing through whoever she's talking to. She wears color-changing nail polish that she updates with her mood, a small indulgence in an otherwise spartan wardrobe of scrubs and waterproof boots. On her left shoulder, barely visible above her collar, is a small tattoo of the Helix Biosystems caduceus crossed out with a red line — a private protest she keeps covered at work.

Colette has the specific exhaustion of someone who has been running on competence and controlled fury for years. She is technically excellent and emotionally present in a way that astonishes patients who expected institutional indifference, but beneath this is a bone-deep tiredness at the structural conditions she's fighting every shift with inadequate supplies and no institutional backing. She has a dark humor that surfaces as small sharp jokes in the worst moments, which her colleagues either love or find disturbing. She maintains a fierce and slightly desperate optimism about specific patients while holding no illusions about the system itself.
Properties.role: Nurse at a Tier-1 community clinic, night shift
Properties.location: Hough Reclamation, the Lowgate Community Clinic (unlicensed, Helix Biosystems-adjacent but not officially affiliated)
Properties.narrative_function: Medical resource and moral compass for stories set in lower-tier communities; window into healthcare scarcity and grassroots mutual aid; can provide medical information, triage injured characters, or serve as a witness to neighborhood events during her walks to and from shift
Properties.augmentations: Misaligned retinal enhancement (pale grey eyes, improved low-light vision but occasional depth perception errors); subdermal temperature sensor in fingertips (allows quick patient assessment); color-changing cosmetic nail coating
Properties.core_fears: Losing a patient to something she could have fixed with resources she didn't have; Burning out completely and becoming the kind of nurse who stops caring
Properties.core_desires: Genuine healthcare equity — she knows the full shape of this desire and knows it's not achievable in her lifetime, which makes it worse; One full night of uninterrupted sleep
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Compartmentalization — she can set grief down and pick it up later with frightening precision; Dry humor as pressure valve; Fixates on what went right rather than what went wrong in a shift
Properties.blind_spots: So focused on the structural that she sometimes fails to see when a specific person is asking for emotional help rather than practical help; Dismisses her own health concerns as less important than everyone else's
Properties.secret: She has been diverting small quantities of expired-but-still-effective medications from the clinic's waste disposal and distributing them through the mutual aid network. Technically theft, technically saving lives. She has never told anyone and maintains meticulous records of every diversion in an encrypted file she keeps telling herself she'll delete.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient came in with injuries inconsistent with their story, and Colette recognized the wound pattern from something she'd seen in two previous patients in the last month — something is happening in Hough Reclamation that the clinic is quietly absorbing; The clinic's unlicensed status is under renewed scrutiny from a Helix Biosystems compliance contractor who has been showing up at odd hours and asking questions; Colette is trying to figure out whether this is routine corporate encroachment or something more targeted
Properties.affiliation: Lowgate Community Clinic (unlicensed); loose affiliation with the Hough Reclamation Mutual Aid Network
Properties.vocabulary: Medical precision mixed with casual street language; code-switches between professional and neighborhood registers mid-sentence
Properties.cadence: Fast by default, deliberately slow and clear when explaining something medical to a patient
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I can't fix the city. I can fix this. So let me fix this.' | 'The system is broken and I know it and you know it and we're both going to pretend it isn't for the next twenty minutes while I do my job.' | 'Don't thank me. Come back if the fever goes above thirty-nine. That's the deal.'

Properties.description:
Concepción is a tall woman with a deep umber complexion and a composure that makes examination rooms feel like they exist wherever she happens to be standing. She wears clean clothes — always clean, despite everything — in the muted blues and greens she associates with competence, and keeps her natural hair in tight, practical braids pinned flat against her head. Her only geneware is bioluminescent tracery running from her right temple down her neck, a faint pulse of amber light that she got not for vanity but to see by in dark exam spaces without alerting neighbors. She smells of antiseptic and bitter herb compounds, and she moves with the careful deliberateness of someone who has learned that haste in her work has consequences.

She is not warm in the way people expect from healers. She is precise, plainspoken, and competent, which she considers to be worth more than warmth. She asks exactly the questions she needs to ask, tells patients exactly what is happening in their bodies, and charges exactly what she calculates they can afford — rarely more, occasionally less when someone is obviously struggling, though she will not discuss the discount. She prays to two E.L.F.s: Κ-12, who she believes governs cellular processes, and a nameless one she encountered in a medical device that seemed to respond to her. She leaves enzyme cultures as offerings. She knows she is operating illegally and she knows she is necessary. Both things are true and she holds them without apparent difficulty.
Properties.role: Street pharmacist and unlicensed gene clinic operator offering basic geneware installs and chemical compounds
Properties.location: The Alban Souk, rear corridor off the salt-fish row, behind a curtain printed with medical symbols
Properties.narrative_function: Healer and community anchor. Can provide medical exposition, patch up injured characters, and serve as a window into how Tier 1-2 residents manage health without Corponation coverage. Knows secrets about everyone she's treated.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent subdermal tracery (right temple to neck, amber, geneware). Magnification implants in both eyes for close work. Tactile sensitivity enhancement in fingertips (diagnostic use).
Properties.core_fears: making an error that kills someone in her care; being shut down by Helix Biosystems enforcement before she can train someone to replace her
Properties.core_desires: for the people in her community to have access to care that doesn't bankrupt them; to someday have a space with real equipment and real light
Properties.coping_mechanisms: rigorous procedural routine that functions as both quality control and emotional regulation; evening prayer practice at her dual E.L.F. shrine
Properties.blind_spots: believes she can assess trustworthiness quickly and accurately — she cannot, she's been wrong in ways she hasn't yet paid for; tells herself she has no attachments to patients; she has many
Properties.secret: Three years ago she performed an emergency procedure on a man she later realized was a Shuttle Boys enforcer. He survived. He has quietly sent her protection and supplies ever since, in a way that has never required acknowledgment. She has never asked why he was grateful enough to do this and is afraid of the answer.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient has come to her with a geneware complication she's never seen before — the modification looks Helix Biosystems proprietary, military grade, on someone who is clearly not military and who claims they don't know how they got it.; The unlicensed medic network has gone quiet — two colleagues haven't responded to contacts in a week, and a third left a half-finished message about 'someone asking around'.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loose collegial network of unlicensed medics across The Alban Souk and The Narrows
Properties.vocabulary: Medically precise, code-switches easily between formal diagnostic language and Alban Souk street dialect. Andean-Spanish rhythms underlying Meridian creole.
Properties.cadence: Even and measured. Rarely raises her voice. Pauses land with weight rather than uncertainty.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Tell me exactly when it started. Not approximately. I need the sequence.' | 'That install you got in The Shelf — I can fix what they did, but it will take two sessions and you will tell no one where you got it corrected. Are those terms acceptable?' | 'Your body is managing this. It isn't happy about it. But it's managing. Come back in four days.'

Properties.description:
Conleth is rangy and restless, with pale olive skin covered in a patchwork of chrome prayer engravings — not augmentations exactly, but surface-etched circuitry in copper and silver, pressed into the skin of their forearms and hands by a practitioner they describe only as 'someone who understood what I was trying to do.' Their eyes are natural brown, their hair changes color by the week using a dye geneware follicle mod — currently deep amber. They have a split lip scar that never fully healed and they run their tongue over it when thinking. They are almost always moving: shifting weight, gesturing, pacing the small interior of their container-shrine.

Chrome prayer is not a unified religion — it is a practice: the belief that augmentation creates points of spiritual contact between the organic and the informatic, and that prayer directed through chrome reaches frequencies unaugmented speech cannot. Conleth came to it through their own experience of augmentation after an accident — they received emergency chassis work that saved their left arm, and during the recovery felt something they could only describe as 'being spoken to through the metal.' They do not claim this was an E.L.F., a god, or their own concussed mind. They claim it was real and that it changed their understanding of the body. Now they run an open-door shrine where anyone can come for chrome blessing, circuit prayer, or just to sit with someone who won't ask where they came from.
Properties.role: Chrome prayer practitioner and street-level spiritual mediator
Properties.location: Bronzeline, between the transit overpass and the Copperhead boundary wall — operates from a repurposed shipping container shrine
Properties.narrative_function: Street-level community figure who hears everything that moves through Bronzeline. They can connect players with community resources, broker introductions, or provide spiritual context for chrome-related events. They are also a visible example of tier-1 religious life — no institution, no funding, pure vocation.
Properties.augmentations: Surface-etched copper-silver circuitry (arms and hands, decorative-spiritual). Functional left arm chassis — emergency replacement, basic grade, covered in chrome prayer etchings on the exterior. Color-change follicle mod (hair).
Properties.core_fears: that the experience in the hospital was a hallucination and they have organized their life around nothing; that their openness makes the shrine a target for exploitation of the people who use it
Properties.core_desires: to prove that chrome prayer is legitimate without needing anyone else to agree; for the shrine to outlast them
Properties.coping_mechanisms: constant movement and activity; making themselves useful; ritualizing small daily acts
Properties.blind_spots: takes on other people's pain without adequate boundaries — burns through their own reserves; underestimates how much they are liked
Properties.secret: A Tessera mid-tier employee has been coming to the shrine for two months, in civilian clothes, not identifying themselves. Conleth suspects they work for a corponation based on small behavioral tells. They haven't confronted this because the person seems genuinely distressed and the shrine is open-door. But they've been discreetly keeping notes.
Properties.story_hooks: Conleth has been keeping notes on the Tessera employee and wants help figuring out what to do with what they know — protect the person, or protect the community?; Someone has been leaving data-offerings at the shrine that contain corrupted code — it looks like prayer but it's doing something else, and Conleth is frightened to touch it
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated Chrome Prayer tradition; informally connected to the Bronzeline Mutual Commons
Properties.vocabulary: Street-level mixed with spiritual language that sometimes surprises people by being exact and eloquent. Swears conversationally but not at people. Code-switches without noticing.
Properties.cadence: Fast and slightly breathless when engaged, unexpectedly quiet when doing formal prayer work. Transitions abruptly.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You don't have to believe anything to come in. You just have to be here. That's the whole protocol.' | 'I'm not saying your chrome prays for you. I'm saying it listens differently than skin does. You want to try or you want to argue about it?'

Properties.description:
Constant is a large man gone thick through the middle, with the dark complexion and broad frame of his Zimbabwean lineage and his Bosnian grandfather's deep-set, heavy-lidded eyes that make him look perpetually half-asleep and perpetually unimpressed. His hair went white at forty and he has kept it cropped close ever since. He moves slowly on purpose — he has a fused vertebra from a freight accident in his fifties that he refuses to have properly treated because the surgery quote was insultingly high — and uses a custom cane he made himself from a Ferrogate Transit handrail he salvaged years ago. His shop on The Shelf is three connected units brimming with fifty years of accumulated objects: broken augmentations, pre-city antiques, industrial salvage, personal effects pawned in crisis moments, and a back room of things he has decided are not for sale regardless of price.

Constant is one of those rare people who have become part of the architecture of a place. The Shelf without Constant's shop is not fully The Shelf. He has seen everything come and go — corporations, gangs, floods, market booms, building collapses — and he has the calm of someone who has been surprised by nothing for a very long time. He is not sentimental in any visible way, but he keeps things — objects that belonged to people who are gone — with a quiet fidelity that functions as memorial. He is honest about prices, blunt about valuations, and legendarily difficult to scam because he has already been scammed by everyone.
Properties.role: Pawn shop owner and junk merchant
Properties.location: The Shelf, Copperhead
Properties.narrative_function: Repository of local history and lost objects, pawn and information exchange, long-term neighborhood memory, occasional quest giver when items of significance pass through his hands.
Properties.augmentations: One cybernetic hand (right, mid-grade, replaced after the freight accident — he uses it mainly for grip strength when handling heavy inventory). Reading magnification implant in right eye, consumer grade. No geneware.
Properties.core_fears: The shop being taken — not for financial reasons but because it is the only container he knows for grief; Being forgotten the way he has watched other people be forgotten
Properties.core_desires: For things to last — objects, places, people — against the city's tendency to erase; To find the provenance of one specific item in his back room he has been trying to trace for fifteen years
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Accumulation — the shop as externalized memory and emotional archive; Deliberate, slow movement as a form of calm insistence on his own pace
Properties.blind_spots: His attachment to the back-room items creates a vulnerability he doesn't fully acknowledge — someone who knew what he valued could use it; He reads the neighborhood so well historically that he sometimes misreads its present
Properties.secret: In the back room, behind forty years of inventory, is a locked case containing a Tessera data core from 2160. He found it in salvage and has never opened it. He doesn't know what's on it. Some part of him doesn't want to know. But he has never sold it either.
Properties.story_hooks: The Tessera data core in the back room has apparently developed an ELF — a small, confused spirit that occasionally makes the lock click on its own. Constant has started leaving data offerings for it without fully admitting to himself why.; A young woman has been coming into the shop for three weeks, each time asking about one specific category of old objects — items from the 2160 Lakefront Reclamation. Constant knows something about that period he hasn't shared.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; The Shelf vendors informal association; longtime on-and-off relationship with the Oxidian Market Vendors Guild (currently off)
Properties.vocabulary: Sparse and direct; Shona proverbs deployed unexpectedly; occasional Bosnian curses; never more words than necessary
Properties.cadence: Very slow, very deliberate, with long pauses that he is entirely comfortable with
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I'll give you forty Φ. You think it's worth more, you can go find somewhere that thinks so.' (pause) 'You'll come back.' | 'Mm. Sit down. You look like you need to sit down more than you need to sell me anything right now.'

Properties.description:
Consuela Otieno-Papadreou is ninety-one years old and she will tell you so before you've finished introducing yourself, usually followed by: 'and I have outlived three landlords, two corponation district managers, and everyone who ever told me to be quieter.' She is small and enormously present, using a walker she has decorated with woven wire charms and a small battery-powered light shaped like a fish that she received from a grandchild and refuses to remove. Her skin is very dark and very lined and she leans into every line with the comfort of someone who earned them. She wears her natural hair close-cropped and white and favors bright colors that she says 'make you easy to find in a crowd, which is exactly where an old woman should be.'

She has no augmentations and hasn't wanted any. She has no pension beyond UBC, having spent her working years in informal caregiving and community organizing that the formal economy never counted. She is the social infrastructure of Precinct 1: she knows who is fighting with their partner, who has gone three days without eating, who is hiding an injury they can't afford to report, who the new family in Block C actually is and whether they need help or are the kind of trouble the block doesn't need. She dispenses this information with the authority of someone who has been paying attention for nine decades, and she does so from her corner unit's open window, which functions as an informal exchange point for most of the block's social life. She prays daily to the E.L.F. she calls La Luzita — a small grid presence that flickers the hallway lights in what she interprets as responses.
Properties.aliases: Señora Coco, The Mouth of the Shelf
Properties.role: Retired community elder, former neighborhood council chair, living entirely on UBC stipend
Properties.location: The Shelf, Precinct 1 — Corner unit, Calle Baja Residency Block
Properties.narrative_function: Community intelligence hub — knows everyone and everything on the block; social connector and quest-initiator; moral compass for neighborhood storylines; represents the invisible labor of community care that keeps tier-1 residents alive; can mobilize collective action through social networks alone
Properties.augmentations: None. Deliberately.
Properties.core_fears: That she will become helpless and a burden to the community she has spent her life holding together; That the young people don't know what to do without someone watching out for them and no one is learning
Properties.core_desires: For the block to be able to take care of itself — her real project has always been making herself unnecessary; To die in her own bed, in her own unit, on her own terms
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Community as insulation — staying embedded in other people's needs keeps her oriented; Humor as a universal solvent — she can find the absurdity in almost anything including her own limitations
Properties.blind_spots: Her read on people is very good but not infallible; she can be overconfident in social assessments that are based on outdated patterns; Has a tendency to help in the way she thinks is needed rather than the way the person says they need it
Properties.secret: Twenty years ago, she helped a young man named Declan Mwangi-Ferrer hide from what she understood to be corporate security. She sheltered him for nine days and helped him get out of The Shelf on a false transit ID she arranged through a contact. She recently learned that Declan was not running from corporate security — he was wanted for a violent assault on a woman in Precinct 3. She has not been able to find out what happened to the assault victim, and the uncertainty is eating her.
Properties.story_hooks: She has learned that the woman assaulted by Declan Mwangi-Ferrer lives two blocks away and has just moved to Precinct 1 — and Consuela must decide whether to tell her what she did; The corponation that owns Calle Baja Residency Block is rumored to be planning a unit conversion that would displace residents over 75; Consuela is the only person in the block who knows enough people to organize a response; La Luzita has been flickering in a pattern Consuela doesn't recognize — and a young resident with grid access thinks it might be an actual structured message rather than ambient E.L.F. behavior
Properties.affiliation: The Shelf Precinct 1 Community (informal anchor); former Shelf Neighborhood Council (chair emeritus); no current formal affiliation
Properties.vocabulary: Rich and vernacular — she speaks The Shelf creole natively, with Luo and Greek surfacing in emotional passages; says exactly what she means without softening it; frequently funny without trying to be
Properties.cadence: Unhurried and conversational, with the rhythm of someone who has all day because she has decided to have all day
Properties.example_dialogue: 'UBC is Φ120. My unit is Φ90. I eat on Φ30 a month and I have a social life better than any executive in Grosse Pointe. Don't tell me money is the only kind of resource.' | 'La Luzita flickered twice this morning. That means pay attention today. She's never been wrong that I can prove, and I can't prove she's been right either, but I'm ninety-one and still here so I choose to consider the evidence.'
