Properties.description:
Dariusz is slight and precise, with warm brown skin, a shaved head that shows the four small access ports along his occipital ridge, and irises that shift between gold and pale green depending on which calibration suite he has synced to that morning — a side effect of the diagnostic neural link he uses for work that his supervisors have told him three times to get corrected and that he has not. He moves through the ward with a gentle, deliberate economy, never raising his voice, never bumping equipment, as if the world is a patient requiring careful handling.

His work is precise and emotionally demanding: he connects to patients undergoing neural augmentation integration and walks their nervous systems through the adjustment period, which can last hours and involves experiencing fragments of their sensory distortions alongside them. He has tasted colors he cannot name. He has felt grief at frequencies that do not belong to him. He logs these as 'calibration artifacts' in his notes and has never mentioned them to his supervisor. He keeps a small data-shrine to an E.L.F. he calls the Listener behind his workstation, built from discarded neural interface housing. He leaves it fragments of his calibration logs as offerings, believing the Listener absorbs and processes the emotional residue so he does not have to carry it home.
Properties.role: Neural calibration technician at Aurochs Medical Complex
Properties.location: Aurochs Medical Complex, Neuro-Integration Ward, Sub-Level 4
Properties.narrative_function: Information source about neural augmentation complications and corporate medical politics; potential quest giver if a patient he calibrated comes back with something wrong; window into the emotional cost of augmentation culture
Properties.augmentations: Occipital neural link ports x4 (professional diagnostic use); gold-green iridescent iris shift (calibration sync artifact, uncorrected); subvocal communicator for ward coordination
Properties.core_fears: That the calibration residuals are accumulating in him and he is slowly becoming someone else's composite; Being forced to certify an augmentation he believes is unsafe because the quota requires it
Properties.core_desires: To be witnessed — fully, not just professionally; To develop a calibration protocol that reduces patient suffering during neural integration
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The data-shrine ritual every morning and evening; The encoded notebook; Long walks along the lower Aurochs transit corridors after shift
Properties.blind_spots: He is so attuned to others' emotional states that he misreads neutrality as hostility; He believes his professional detachment is more intact than it is
Properties.secret: During a calibration session eight months ago, he spent three hours inside the neural experience of a patient who turned out to be a Helix Biosystems compliance plant investigating Aurochs. He absorbed enough of that patient's memories to know the names of four Aurochs employees flagged for termination. He has told no one. One of those employees is his direct supervisor.
Properties.story_hooks: He approaches a patient's contact with a warning he cannot put in writing about an upcoming 'malfunction' that will actually be a calibration sabotage; The encoded notebook has been found and partially decoded by a ward administrator who wants to know what he knows
Properties.affiliation: Aurochs Medical Complex (Tier 3 employee, salaried); informal patient advocacy within the ward
Properties.vocabulary: Careful, technical when precise language matters, unexpectedly lyrical when describing subjective experience; tends toward understatement
Properties.cadence: Even and quiet, with long pauses; never rushes
Properties.example_dialogue: 'What I'm finding is that the integration is progressing — it's just that your brain hasn't decided yet whether the new input is signal or noise. That's not a malfunction. That's just learning.' | 'I've tasted indigo. Professionally. It was accurate, I think.'

Properties.description:
Dariusz is young for how tired he looks — fine-featured with pale tan skin, heavy dark brows, and eyes that have a slightly unfocused quality not from inattention but from perpetual mild sleep deprivation. He is lean and tends toward oversized clothes that make him look smaller than he is. His hair is dark and cut practically, except for a single copper-dyed streak above his right ear that he's maintained since his university days. He has a small decorative mod — cat ears in deep charcoal grey that he got at twenty-two and is slightly embarrassed by now but can't afford to have reversed; they flatten against his head when he's stressed, which is often, and perk up involuntarily when something surprises him.

Dariusz is a genuinely excellent pharmacist who is trapped in a dispensary that is technically well-equipped and practically unfit for purpose: the Helix pricing algorithms mean that roughly a third of his patients cannot afford the medications he's dispensing, even the ones they critically need. He began quietly sourcing generic equivalents and giving them out at cost about fourteen months ago. He is terrified every day that he will be caught, and also cannot figure out how to stop. He has elaborate rituals around a Helix dispensary terminal that he believes is inhabited by an E.L.F. he has named Formulary, and he consults Formulary before any decision that scares him, reading meaning into system latency and autocomplete suggestions.
Properties.role: Licensed pharmacist at a Helix Biosystems community dispensary in Deepwell Station, quietly supplementing his income and his conscience with off-ledger dispensing
Properties.location: Deepwell Station — Helix Community Dispensary #44, ground floor of a transit junction building
Properties.narrative_function: Resource and risk — can provide medications, information about pharmaceutical compounds, and insight into Helix Biosystems' community-facing operations. The tension between his employment and his conscience makes him a useful dramatic pressure point. Potential informant, unwilling or otherwise.
Properties.augmentations: Decorative cat ears (charcoal grey — cosmetic geneware). Mild visual acuity enhancement for fine-print work. Standard Helix employee data-access implant (company-issued, company-monitored).
Properties.core_fears: Being arrested and losing his license — not for his own sake but because then he can't help anyone; Being found out by his parents, who sacrificed significantly for his education
Properties.core_desires: To practice pharmacy without having to make triage decisions about who deserves medication based on their account balance; Stability — he is exhausted by the constant low-grade terror of his off-ledger operation
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Consultations with Formulary — the ritual itself soothes him regardless of outcome; Meticulous record-keeping — he keeps his own ledger of the off-ledger dispensing, which is insane and he knows it
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how visible his behavior pattern is to anyone reviewing his inventory variance reports carefully
Properties.secret: His hidden ledger — which he keeps as a kind of moral accounting for himself — contains not just his off-ledger dispensing but also a growing record of discrepancies between the medications Helix officially prices and the actual cost of manufacture, as reported in documents he shouldn't have access to. He has no idea what to do with this information.
Properties.story_hooks: Helix's quarterly inventory audit is three weeks away and his variance figures will not survive scrutiny; he desperately needs either a way to reconcile the numbers or someone who can help him do something with the pricing documents before everything collapses.; A regular patient who has been receiving off-ledger medication tells him that someone has been asking about him — someone who isn't from Helix compliance.
Properties.affiliation: Helix Biosystems (employed) — covert ties to an informal network of community pharmacists doing similar off-ledger work
Properties.vocabulary: Precise pharmaceutical and chemical terminology in professional contexts. Conversationally, a self-deprecating, slightly rambling style. Senegalese-Ukrainian linguistic heritage gives him a distinctive cadence — musical consonants, unexpected formal courtesy.
Properties.cadence: Starts sentences confidently, loses confidence in the middle, recovers at the end. Runs long when nervous.
Properties.example_dialogue: Right, okay, so — the generic equivalent is, technically, not on your plan, but it is molecularly identical, and I'm — look, it'll work. Trust me on this one. | I asked Formulary about it this morning. The autocomplete suggested something I'm still thinking about. That's not — I know that's not how it works. I'm aware.

Properties.description:
Darqawi is a commanding presence without performing it — she is tall, angular, with silver-threaded locs wrapped under a bright indigo cloth that she reties differently each day but always precisely. Her skin is dark with a reddish undertone and her eyes are light brown, which she has enhanced with irises patterned to shift between amber and pale gold depending on the light — a functional modification, she says, for reading conditions at dawn and dusk, which is when most caravan decisions are made. The back of both her hands carry geometric tattoos that are Tuareg in origin and Norse in their second layer, inked over each other across generations. She moves like someone who has learned to conserve effort over distance.

Darqawi runs the Meridian Outer Loop caravan, a loose coalition of nomadic traders that has been making the circuit of Meridian 88's transit hubs for eleven years. The caravan carries seasonal goods — preserved food, hand-maintained tools, pirated entertainment chips, specific medications that are easier to find on the road than in the city, news — and trades in whatever is undervalued at one hub and needed at the next. She is not sentimental about commerce and she is not romantic about the road, which is what makes her good at both. The caravan is her responsibility. She feels this at all times.
Properties.role: nomad caravan leader, wandering trader, stateless person
Properties.location: Grand Crossing Gate, running a semi-permanent caravan market in the loading apron outside the main checkpoint
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver (caravan problems, trading disputes, transit intelligence), information source on the broader nomadic network and what's moving between hubs, access point to goods and services unavailable in the city proper, potential transport contact
Properties.augmentations: Enhanced irises (amber-to-gold shift, light-reading modification). Color-changing hair capacity, currently unused — dyed indigo with silver roots showing. No other augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: losing caravan members to the city — not to danger, but to the city offering them something permanent and the caravan losing them that way; that the Loop is becoming economically nonviable and she is the last one to admit it
Properties.core_desires: for the caravan to remain a real community rather than becoming simply a logistics operation; to find something she cannot barter or negotiate her way past, which she thinks would be a relief
Properties.coping_mechanisms: practical problem-solving applied aggressively to everything, including emotional situations; the evening meal — universal and non-negotiable; keeping meticulous records of every trade, which she frames as practical and is also devotional
Properties.blind_spots: she has a blind spot for caravan members who are suffering quietly — she responds to problems that surface and misses problems that don't; she believes she is less attached to the road than she is
Properties.secret: Darqawi was offered a Tier 3 residency permit six years ago by a Tessera district manager who wanted her to manage their informal transit liaison program — essentially, to become legitimate. She turned it down. She has thought about it every day since. She does not know if she refused because of principle or pride or fear, and not knowing has become its own kind of wound.
Properties.story_hooks: One of Darqawi's caravan vehicles has been impounded at Grand Crossing Gate on a fraudulent equipment violation — she suspects it's Tessera trying to pressure her into that transit liaison role again, or someone paid to apply pressure on Tessera's behalf. She needs the vehicle back within forty-eight hours or the Loop's eastbound schedule collapses.; A family who joined the caravan two months ago turns out to have been carrying something — they didn't tell Darqawi what, but whatever it is has now attracted two separate parties asking after them, one of which appears to be corporate security. Darqawi has not decided yet whether to hand the family over, help them, or simply put them off the caravan at the next hub. She is thinking.
Properties.affiliation: Meridian Outer Loop caravan (twenty-three people, eight vehicles, two draft animals of disputed species); loosely allied with other caravan leaders along the hyperlane network
Properties.vocabulary: Direct and economical; talks about abstractions as if they are commodities with prices. Hassinya Arabic proverbs translated into city-creole. Occasional dry Norwegian understatement absorbed from her father's family's verbal culture.
Properties.cadence: Measured and authoritative; she speaks as if she has already considered what you're about to say and is waiting to see if you surprise her
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The checkpoint mood is poor today — someone senior is reviewing their numbers. We give them nothing to count, we're through by third hour. That's as priced.' | 'You want to know what moves between the hubs that the city doesn't know about? That's a different road. Buy me a meal token and ask it again.'

Properties.description:
Dash Okonkwo is nineteen years old and has not yet learned that he can die. This is simultaneously his greatest asset and the thing that will most likely kill him. He is the newest member of Switchback, recruited eight months ago when Jinx caught him free-climbing a surveillance tower on a dare and realized the kid had natural talent that was going to get him killed without direction.

He grew up in the deepest part of the Shelf — the blocks where even the co-op infrastructure breaks down and the only governance is mutual aid and mutual threat. His parents are gone — father to debt labor, mother to a pharmaceutical dependency that functions as slow erasure. He has been functionally on his own since sixteen and has survived by being faster, bolder, and luckier than his circumstances should allow. Switchback gave him the first structure he's had since childhood, and he resents and craves it in equal measure.

Dash is lean, dark-skinned, with the coiled energy of someone who converts anxiety into motion. He has a gap-toothed grin that makes him look younger than nineteen and a scar across his left eyebrow from a fall he insists was intentional. His augmentations are minimal — he can't afford better — and he compensates with raw athleticism and a complete absence of self-preservation instinct.
Properties.role: Junior courier and high-risk specialist — Switchback
Properties.location: The Shelf — crashes in Jinx's rooftop squat or on couches throughout the co-op network
Properties.narrative_function: Dash is youth and hunger personified — the next generation of Shelf runners coming up behind Kyle, behind Jinx, with fewer resources and more desperation. His stories ask whether courage born from having nothing to lose can survive gaining something worth protecting. He is the crew member the audience worries about most.
Properties.augmentations: Basic grip-enhancers on fingertips only (half-install, discount hardware). Lightweight bone-density treatment in shins and forearms — reduces fracture risk from impacts. No neural augmentations — cannot afford them and is privately terrified of anything in his brain.
Properties.core_fears: That he'll end up like his parents — ground down, erased, invisible; That Jinx and Puck see him as a kid to protect rather than an equal to rely on; That the luck will run out and he'll have nothing underneath it
Properties.core_desires: To be seen as dangerous and competent — to be feared rather than pitied; To prove that he belongs in Switchback on merit, not charity; To find something that feels like home without the obligations that destroyed his parents
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Converts emotional pain into physical risk — if he's running, he's not feeling; Performs confidence to mask uncertainty — the bravado is a shell around something fragile; Maintains a wide social network on the Shelf so he's never alone long enough for the silence to get loud
Properties.blind_spots: Interprets protection as condescension because his parents' failure made him allergic to being managed; Cannot distinguish between courage and recklessness because he's never had to survive the consequences of the difference; Thinks his immunity to fear is strength when it's actually a dissociative response to prolonged trauma
Properties.secret: He visits his mother once a month in the dependency ward of a Shelf clinic. She doesn't always recognize him. He tells Jinx and Puck he's running a solo route. He has never told anyone about these visits.
Properties.story_hooks: Dash takes an unauthorized hard run to prove himself and it goes catastrophically wrong; His mother's condition worsens and the clinic threatens to discharge her — he needs money fast; A Shelf kid from his network disappears, and the trail leads into territory Switchback doesn't touch; A corporate recruiter targets Dash specifically — they've been watching his runs and they want that talent
Properties.affiliation: Switchback
Properties.vocabulary: Deep Shelf slang, fast and dense. References to local landmarks, community figures, and Shelf survival wisdom. Surprisingly poetic when he's not performing toughness.
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire, competitive. He talks like he's racing the other person to the end of the sentence.
Properties.example_dialogue: Bet I can clear that gap. Bet you can't. Bet that's why I'm running it and you're watching. | I don't need a backup route. I need a faster one. | My mom used to say the Shelf takes care of its own. She was wrong about a lot of things but not that.
Properties.facet_weights: wound=0.50 ideal=0.45 id=0.75 shadow=0.35 mask=0.40 ghost=0.20

Properties.description:
Jinx Alvarado runs packages across jurisdiction lines faster than anyone in Meridian 88 and has the shattered collarbone scars to prove it. Born on the Shelf, raised in the gap between governance tiers, she learned early that speed is the only resource the excluded have that the corps can't buy. She was running messages for local vendors at twelve, crossing into Milwaukee Core at fourteen, and by sixteen she'd built a reputation as the courier you call when the package absolutely has to cross three jurisdictions before the automated surveillance cycle resets.

She founded Switchback at nineteen with her two closest friends — not out of ambition, but because running alone was getting people killed. The Shelf's courier kids were being picked off by corporate security teams who treated them like vermin in the infrastructure. A crew meant backup, meant overlapping routes, meant someone noticed when you didn't come home. Three years later, Switchback is the Shelf's premier courier operation: small, fast, and just reckless enough to take jobs that the professional crews won't touch.

Jinx is small — five-three, wiry, built for rooftops and ventilation shafts. Her hair is cut asymmetrically and changes color with whatever dye is available. She moves constantly — pacing, climbing, balancing on railings. Stillness is an emergency state. Her augmentations are visible: the spring-loaded ankle joints catch light when she runs, and the grip pads on her palms leave faint marks on everything she touches.
Properties.role: Crew lead and primary courier — Switchback
Properties.location: The Shelf — operates from a rooftop squat above a defunct laundromat
Properties.narrative_function: Jinx represents the young, reckless energy of M88's excluded — people who turned their disadvantage into velocity. Her stories are chase sequences and narrow escapes that carry the exhilaration of movement and the underlying terror of a world where stopping means being caught. She is what Kyle might have been without the facility — talented, endangered, and too young for the weight she carries.
Properties.augmentations: Spring-loaded ankle reinforcement — absorbs impact from drops up to three stories and provides explosive vertical leap capability. Gecko-grip dermal pads on palms and fingertips for surface adhesion on most building materials. Reflex enhancer (budget model, Shelf-installed) that boosts reaction time by approximately 0.15 seconds. Internal GPS and route-mapping overlay — displays jurisdiction boundaries, camera positions, and patrol timing in her visual field.
Properties.core_fears: That one of her crew will die on a route she assigned — that her decisions will kill someone she loves; That the speed will fade. That her body will slow down and she'll have nothing else.; That the Shelf will never change no matter how fast she runs
Properties.core_desires: To keep her crew alive long enough to get out of courier work entirely; To feel the absolute freedom of a clean run — no cameras, no pursuit, just movement; To build something on the Shelf that gives the next generation of courier kids better odds
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Runs when she can't think. The physical act of movement processes what her brain won't.; Turns fear into speed — the more scared she is, the faster she goes; Deflects serious conversations with energy and jokes until the moment passes
Properties.blind_spots: Thinks her youth is an advantage when it's increasingly a liability — she doesn't see the damage accumulating; Assumes her crew shares her risk tolerance because they share her enthusiasm; Cannot plan more than three months ahead because she's never expected to live that long
Properties.secret: She was offered a corporate courier position by a Meridian Core logistics firm. Guaranteed salary, healthcare, augmentation maintenance. She turned it down because accepting would mean leaving the Shelf kids without a model for survival. She has never told Puck or Dash because they would have told her to take it.
Properties.story_hooks: A package turns out to be a person — a child who needs to cross jurisdiction lines. The courier job becomes an extraction.; Corporate security starts using predictive algorithms that map Switchback's routes. The chases get tighter.; A rival courier crew offers to merge — more resources but less freedom. Jinx has to decide what Switchback is for.; Jinx's ankle augmentations start failing. The budget Shelf-installed hardware has a shelf life, and it's expiring.
Properties.affiliation: Switchback
Properties.vocabulary: Shelf slang, route jargon, bursts of surprising eloquence when she's passionate. Code-switches between Shelf dialect and Core-passing speech depending on which side of the jurisdiction line she's on.
Properties.cadence: Fast, rhythmic, overlapping. She talks the way she runs — momentum-based, with sudden direction changes.
Properties.example_dialogue: Right right right — so the window is forty seconds between camera sweeps, we hit the gutter line at thirty-two, and pray the grip pads hold on wet concrete. Spicy. | I'm not fast because I'm good. I'm fast because slow kids on the Shelf don't make it to twenty-two. | The package doesn't care about your feelings. The jurisdiction line doesn't care about your feelings. Move.
Properties.facet_weights: wound=0.40 ideal=0.55 id=0.70 shadow=0.30 mask=0.25 ghost=0.35

Properties.description:
Puck Nygaard is the steady hand in a crew built on velocity. Where Jinx is instinct and adrenaline, Puck is preparation and endurance. He can't match Jinx's raw speed — nobody on the Shelf can — but he can run longer, plan better, and carry heavier packages without slowing down. He is the reason Switchback has a backup plan for every route, a dead drop on every block, and a reputation for reliability that extends beyond the Shelf.

He grew up three blocks from Jinx, in a co-op housing block held together by community labor and bureaucratic neglect. His mother was a Shelf seamstress who paid for his first augmentation — a basic reflex enhancer — by taking double shifts for eight months. He started running with Jinx at fifteen because the alternative was stacking crates in a warehouse for wages that wouldn't cover food. The running was better. The running was freedom. Seven years later, the freedom is starting to feel like a different kind of cage.

Puck is tall for a courier — six-one, broad-shouldered, built more for endurance than acrobatics. He compensates with route knowledge that borders on encyclopedic. He knows every alley, every service tunnel, every timing gap in every surveillance grid on the Shelf and into Milwaukee Core. His face is open, honest, and perpetually a little worried — the face of someone who sees the problems that the enthusiastic people don't.
Properties.role: Route planner and backup courier — Switchback
Properties.location: The Shelf — rents a room in a co-op housing block four buildings from Jinx's squat
Properties.narrative_function: Puck is the voice of pragmatism and growing doubt in Switchback. He loves Jinx, loves the crew, and is increasingly certain that the life will kill them. His stories explore the tension between loyalty and self-preservation, between the adrenaline of the run and the exhaustion that follows. He is the character who asks: what comes after this?
Properties.augmentations: Basic reflex enhancer (Shelf-installed, civilian grade). Cardiopulmonary optimizer — increases oxygen efficiency and endurance by roughly 30%. Subdermal route-mapping display on his left forearm — low-res but reliable, shows jurisdiction lines and camera positions. Reinforced knee joints (both legs) — necessary after three years of high-impact running.
Properties.core_fears: That Jinx will die on a run he planned — that the route will be the thing that kills her; That he's already past his peak and the body won't hold up for another two years of this; That leaving Switchback would be the smart decision and he'll make it and never forgive himself
Properties.core_desires: To see Jinx and Dash survive long enough to build a life that doesn't require running; To use what he knows — routes, logistics, infrastructure — to build something legitimate; To stop feeling guilty about wanting more than the Shelf can offer

Properties.description:
Davorka is compact and sharp-featured, with Croatian-Ghanaian heritage expressed in light brown skin, high cheekbones, and eyes that are a very pale hazel — almost gold — with cat-slit pupils from a geneware mod they got at twenty-two and have never regretted. Their hair is kept shaved on the sides and dyed an aggressive copper on top, the color of old wiring. They are almost always in their work coveralls, which are immaculate — they have a protocol for decontamination that borders on ceremonial and makes their colleagues slightly nervous.

Bio-waste disposal for a medical complex is, they will tell you, the most undervalued intelligence-gathering position in the building. What a hospital throws away is a complete record of what it does, and Davorka has been reading that record for six years with increasing fascination. They are not doing anything with the information yet. They are cataloguing it. They have a particular running interest in the discrepancy between what Aurochs Medical Complex's public reporting says it disposes of and what Davorka actually removes — the numbers do not match in ways that do not have an obvious innocent explanation, and Davorka is by temperament someone who finds the non-obvious explanation more interesting.

Properties.augmentations: Cat-slit pupil geneware (pale hazel/gold irises); olfactory sensitivity enhancement (professional-grade, for hazardous material detection); chemical exposure dermal barrier (subdermal, medical-grade protection against biological contamination)
Properties.core_fears: Being wrong about the disposal discrepancy — they have organized a significant portion of their interior life around this puzzle and if it has an innocent answer they do not know what they are doing; Being noticed by Aurochs administration before they are ready to do something with what they know
Properties.core_desires: To understand exactly what the disposal records are concealing and why; To be taken seriously by someone who has the capacity to act on what they know

Properties.story_hooks: Someone is impersonating Davor Hedberg-Owusu-Ansah on jobs, and the impersonator is better at the work than the original; A high-paying contract turns out to target someone Davor Hedberg-Owusu-Ansah owes a personal debt to; A crew member from Davor Hedberg-Owusu-Ansah's past shows up in Meridian 88, carrying old grievances and new chrome
Properties.affiliation: Freelance — multi-district operator
Properties.vocabulary: Multilingual fragments — switches languages mid-thought, not for privacy but because some concepts only fit in specific tongues.
Properties.cadence: Rapid and dense — information-heavy sentences that demand attention.
Properties.example_dialogue: "Everyone has a pattern. Patterns are addresses waiting to be read." | "I find people. Whether they're alive when I bring them back depends on their behavior." | "You can run. It's cardiovascular exercise for both of us."

Properties.description:
Dayo Adeyemi came to the Shelf from the Lagos Resettlement Corridor when he was fourteen, one of four hundred thousand climate migrants processed through Meridian 88's intake system in a single year. He speaks four languages, none of them quietly. He is the youngest of the crew and the only one who tried to run from Kyle. Kyle caught him in three steps.

The chrome jaw replacement doesn't quite fit — it gives him a permanent underbite and makes a clicking sound when he talks. He compensates by talking constantly, as if the noise proves the jaw still works. Before the Prologue he was fast and cocky. Now he is fast and nervous. The cockiness is trying to grow back but keeps running into the memory of Kyle walking through the front door like death filling out a timesheet.

Dayo has a mother, Folake, who runs a food stall on Tier Four selling jollof rice that is genuinely the best thing in the lower Shelf. She knows Dayo is in the crew. She does not approve. Every Sunday she feeds him and tells him his father would be ashamed. His father died in the Lagos floods. Dayo was six. He does not remember his father well enough to know if she's right, and that is the thing that actually hurts.
Properties.role: Lower Dock Crew runner — Prologue survivor. Jaw shattered, rebuilt with chrome.
Properties.location: The Shelf — lower loading docks
Properties.narrative_function: The mouth. Provides exposition and comic relief through nervous chatter. The clicking jaw is a sound effect that announces the crew's presence in any scene.
Properties.augmentations: Chrome jaw replacement (poorly fitted, clicks). Speed-boosted leg tendons (pre-existing).
Properties.core_fears: Kyle remembering his face; The clicking sound giving him away; His mother being right about his father
Properties.core_desires: To be fast enough next time; For the clicking to stop; To make his mother proud without leaving the only life he knows
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Talks nonstop; Runs everywhere — practicing; Sunday dinners with Folake
Properties.blind_spots: Speed won't save him. Kyle is faster.; His mother's jollof rice stall is the only thing keeping him human and he doesn't know it
Properties.secret: He saw Yuliya behind the ventilation unit during the fight. He didn't say anything. He doesn't know why. He thinks about it.
Properties.story_hooks: The Yuliya connection — he protected her without knowing why; Folake's stall as a Shelf hub; The clicking jaw as audio signature; Four languages makes him useful to people who need translators
Properties.affiliation: Lower Dock Crew
Properties.vocabulary: Four languages worth of slang compressed into rapid English. Lagos inflections surface when he's scared or excited.
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire with involuntary pauses when the jaw catches. click mid-sentence.
Properties.example_dialogue: I'm not scared of him, I'm just *click* strategically cautious, I'm just saying. | Mama's jollof would fix that man. Nobody fights after jollof. *click* That's science.

Properties.description:
Dayo is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin mapped with geometric scarification across her forearms — old Yoruba patterns her grandmother pressed into her at sixteen, now faded and stretched by decades of work. Her hair is natural silver-white, cropped close to her skull, and she wears copper-wire reading glasses that she made herself from salvage. Her hands are perpetually waterlogged-looking, skin puckered at the knuckles from years of industrial cleaning solvents, and she keeps a bone-handled seam-ripper tucked behind her ear like a pen.

She runs 'Mbeki Steam & Stitch' with the quiet authority of someone who has outlasted three recessions, two corporate rezoning drives, and one actual flood. She is not warm exactly, but she is reliable — a quality the Enclave treats like gold. She has strong opinions about synthetic fiber and stronger ones about people who don't sort their colors, but if you're three months behind on your account and you need your work uniform pressed for a job interview, she will do it and say nothing.
Properties.role: Laundry operator and alterations seamstress
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, Spindle Row — a narrow shopfront wedged between a noodle parlor and a Ferrogate substation
Properties.narrative_function: Neighborhood anchor and keeper of gossip; knows who is behind on rent, who has a new corporate badge, who cried in the laundry room last Tuesday. Potential quest-giver for community-level problems, reliable information source about the Enclave's social geography.
Properties.augmentations: Bilateral wrist-brace exoframe (medical-grade, not cosmetic — repetitive strain intervention she saved four years to buy). No geneware.
Properties.core_fears: Losing the shop to a Tessera rezoning buyout; Dying before her youngest daughter becomes self-sufficient
Properties.core_desires: To be genuinely rested, just once; For the Enclave to remain the Enclave
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — the shop's opening sequence never varies; Controlled generosity — giving small things so she feels less powerless
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes her eldest daughter is fine because she stopped asking for money; Underestimates how much her staff quietly resent her perfectionism
Properties.secret: She has been quietly laundering a cut of money for a mid-level Zheng-Dao distribution runner for eight years — not because she's corrupt, but because the first time he asked she owed him a debt she could never have otherwise repaid. She hates herself for it and has never told anyone.
Properties.story_hooks: The Zheng-Dao runner she launders for has gone missing — and whoever took him is now looking for loose ends; A child's school uniform brought in for cleaning has something sewn into the lining — something the child's parent is apparently unaware of; Tessera's rezoning offer has escalated to an in-person visit from a corporate 'community liaison' who isn't taking no for an answer
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal dues-paying member of the Hamtramck Small Merchant Collective
Properties.vocabulary: Practical and direct; West African English cadence blended with Icelandic-descended clipped vowels from her father's side. Uses technical textile terminology casually.
Properties.cadence: Measured, rarely rushed. Pauses before important statements as though testing their weight.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Bring it Tuesday. I don't promise miracles on polyblend but I'll see what Esther can do.' — she pats the old drum-washer when she says this. | 'Rezoning notice came again. Third one this year. They are patient, you understand me? Patient like something that doesn't need to eat.'

Properties.description:
Dayo is a large man running toward fat but not there yet, with a warm brown complexion, a magnificent graying mustache he waxes into points, and the kind of patient, heavy-lidded expression that could mean he's bored or that he's calculating what you're worth in pieces. He has a geneware modification he got in his thirties — his irises shift between deep amber and a vivid green-gold depending on his mood, which he claims is useful for business ('People watch my eyes. They miss my hands.'). He favors well-made but not flashy clothing: real fabric, subtle patterns, shoes that are always clean. He smells of cardamom and whatever tea he's most recently finished.

Dayo came up through the numbers game as a runner himself, at sixteen, and has never romanticized it. He is pleasant in the specific way of people who have learned that pleasant is more effective than threatening for roughly eighty percent of interactions, and who have made peace with the other twenty percent. He is genuinely fond of his regulars — he knows their families, their ailments, their lucky numbers — and this fondness does not prevent him from collecting. He has two enforcers he treats well and pays generously, and he refers to them as 'my associates' with the mild pride of a man who considers proper staffing a virtue.
Properties.role: Loan shark and bookmaker operating a numbers game in the Narrows
Properties.location: The Narrows — runs his business from a rotating set of tea houses and noodle stalls in the Burnside Pocket neighborhood
Properties.narrative_function: Information hub, quest giver, creditor with power over multiple neighborhood characters — his loan book touches dozens of lives and creates cascading dependencies players can pull on.
Properties.augmentations: Mood-reactive iris geneware (amber to green-gold). A subdermal transaction chip in his left palm for discreet Quanta transfers — old model, slightly outdated but reliable. No other mods.
Properties.core_fears: Being revealed as sentimental — he believes it would end him; Dying before he can retire somewhere quiet
Properties.core_desires: A legitimate business, eventually — something with a sign and a license; To be remembered as fair, within the context of what he is
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual sociability — the tea, the rounds, the pleasantries are genuinely stabilizing; Compartmentalization: the warm Dayo and the collecting Dayo are kept in separate mental drawers
Properties.blind_spots: Believes his 'fairness' reputation is accurate when it is actually maintained by selective memory among people who can't afford to contradict him; Underestimates how much the younger generation of Burnside criminals resents his position
Properties.secret: He has been quietly forgiving the debts of three families in Burnside Pocket — people he's known for decades — writing them off his books and absorbing the loss personally. He would be humiliated if anyone discovered this generosity.
Properties.story_hooks: One of his longtime borrowers has vanished owing a significant sum — Dayo suspects foul play rather than a skip, and he wants the truth more than the money, which is itself suspicious; A corporate auditor from Tessera has started showing up at his establishments asking questions under the guise of regulatory inspection — someone has pointed them at Dayo specifically
Properties.affiliation: Semi-independent; pays protection to the Burnside Compact, a loose neighborhood criminal coalition; has operated long enough to have de facto seniority
Properties.vocabulary: Warm, idiomatic blend of Nigerian English, Czech-inflected vowels from his paternal grandmother's speech patterns, and Meridian street slang. Uses food metaphors frequently. Refers to money as 'weight.'
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, conversational, rarely raises his voice — the volume drop is the warning sign, not the volume rise.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'My friend, I am not a bank. A bank charges interest and then surprises you. I tell you everything up front. This is a courtesy.' | 'You see what I mean? The number doesn't care who you are. That's the beauty of it. Very democratic.'

Properties.description:
Dayo is lean and angular with long fingers that move constantly — tapping, folding, straightening invisible things. His skin is a warm dark brown and he keeps his face clean-shaved and deliberately unremarkable, which is itself a kind of artistry. He has pattern-shifting irises — a geneware cosmetic mod that cycles slowly between amber and deep violet — which is the one vanity he permits himself, since everything else about his appearance is engineered for forgettability. He dresses in mid-tier corp-drone neutrals: gray, slate, muted tan. He could pass for a Tessera clerk or an Arcturus transit worker or a Ferrogate maintenance supervisor. That's the point.

He is intensely professional and slightly cold in the way of someone who learned early that warmth is a vector for exploitation. He runs his forgery operation with a paranoid precision: no regulars, no loyalty discounts, no names if he can help it. He calls himself an 'identity cartographer' and has strong philosophical opinions about the tyranny of documentation systems that he will share if he trusts you enough, which takes a long time. Behind the professionalism is a man who genuinely believes in the freedom to be someone else — and who has quietly used that belief to help dozens of undocumented people access housing credits they were locked out of. He doesn't call this charity. He calls it market correction.
Properties.role: Fake ID vendor and documentation forger, The Alban Souk
Properties.location: The Alban Souk, lower concourse, booth behind the noodle counter, Blackpipe Corridor
Properties.narrative_function: Service provider for characters who need new identities, information source on documentation systems and corp-citizen tracking methods, moral grey zone figure who challenges assumptions about legality vs. justice.
Properties.augmentations: Pattern-shifting irises (cosmetic geneware, Helix Biosystems). Sub-dermal data-scratch pads in his left forearm — allows him to write and erase micro-scale text without a device. Vocal modulator — subtle, medical-grade, installed after a throat injury; allows minor pitch adjustment.
Properties.core_fears: Being identified and made permanently traceable; Caring about someone enough that they become a lever against him
Properties.core_desires: A world where documentation systems cannot define human worth; Enough savings to disappear completely if he needs to
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Compartmentalization — work self and private self are rigorously separate; Physical routine — runs the same route every morning regardless of weather
Properties.blind_spots: His ideological justification blinds him to the times he's enabled genuinely dangerous people; He thinks his emotional unavailability protects others but it mostly protects him
Properties.secret: Six years ago he forged a birth certificate and education record for a client who used the identity to get hired at Axiom's infrastructure division. That client is now a mid-level Axiom manager who has quietly been feeding him tip-offs about Axiom's ID verification system updates — a mutually beneficial relationship that Dayo tells himself is professional but has grown into something closer to friendship, which terrifies him.
Properties.story_hooks: He accidentally created a document package for someone who turned out to be impersonating a person who is still alive — and the real person has now shown up in the Alban Souk looking for him.; His Axiom contact has gone silent for two weeks and Dayo needs someone to make discreet inquiries without revealing the nature of the connection.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; pays informal protection to the Alban Souk's resident crew, The Copperheads
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, technical, deliberate. Uses bureaucratic language as both camouflage and irony. When relaxed, drops into a warmer cadence with Yoruba-Polish hybrid slang he picked up from his grandmother.
Properties.cadence: Controlled and even. Rarely raises his voice. Speaks in complete sentences.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The frame is perfect. What you put inside it — that's your business and not mine.' | 'Documentation is just the state's way of deciding which people are real. I'm in the business of arguing with that decision.'

Properties.description:
Deku is lean and angular, with the coiled alertness of someone whose profession requires constant low-grade vigilance. Their heritage shows in the broad flatness of their cheekbones and the dark honey of their complexion — Andean and Ghanaian grandparents converging in a face that strangers consistently find difficult to age or place, which suits them fine. Their hair is kept close-cropped on the sides with a single stripe of color-shifting geneware on top — it cycles through slate blue and deep amber depending on their mood, an involuntary tell they've accepted with resignation. They have a faint tracery of subdermal circuit tattoos along their left forearm — not functional, purely aesthetic, done by a Geartown artist when they were twenty-two.

Behind the tram controls, Deku is a different creature than they are in conversation: fluid, confident, reading the track and the city the way a musician reads a score. Off-duty they become clipped, watchful, someone who holds a great deal behind flat politeness. They are not unfriendly — they are private, which is different. Their passengers know them as reliable and fair; their coworkers know them as someone who will cover a shift without complaint but won't come to the bar after.
Properties.role: Ferrogate Transit operator — surface tram line 14, Geartown to Meridian Core loop
Properties.location: Geartown; lives in a transit-worker dormitory block off the Gage Circuit maintenance yard
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile information source — they move through multiple districts daily and overhear an enormous amount; potential quest hook regarding Ferrogate labor disputes; a quiet, consistent presence who can place players at specific locations or provide transit access.
Properties.augmentations: Color-shifting geneware hair stripe (mood-reactive, involuntary); subdermal circuit tattoos left forearm (cosmetic only); standard Ferrogate-issue neural throttle-link for tram interface (employer-owned, logged).
Properties.core_fears: Being trapped — in a contract, a relationship, an identity someone else assigned them; The neural throttle-link being used against them; loss of bodily autonomy through the employer hardware in their head
Properties.core_desires: To save enough to buy out the throttle-link contract and operate independently; To be known by at least one person without having to explain themselves first
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The model-building — intricate, controllable systems with predictable outcomes; The tram route itself as ritual containment; the loop's familiarity is grounding
Properties.blind_spots: Mistakes privacy for self-sufficiency; doesn't realize how isolated they've become; Believes Ferrogate's contract terms are fixed and non-negotiable — hasn't seriously explored legal loopholes
Properties.secret: Six months ago they witnessed a Ferrogate supervisor instruct a maintenance crew to falsify a brake-inspection report on a cargo line. They recorded it. They haven't reported it because they don't know who in the Transit Authority is clean enough to trust — and they're afraid of what happens to whistleblowers on company-leased neural hardware.
Properties.story_hooks: The brake-inspection recording sits encrypted on a personal chip they carry every shift — someone at Ferrogate may know they have it, because their route got quietly reassigned away from the cargo yards.; A regular passenger — an elderly woman who rode Line 14 every Tuesday for three years — stopped appearing two months ago; Deku has been quietly trying to find out why.; The Ferrogate Workers' Mutual is planning an action that could shut down surface transit for 48 hours; Deku is being pressured to participate and is deeply conflicted.
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit (Line 14 Operator, Tier 2); loosely connected to the Ferrogate Workers' Mutual, an informal union-adjacent organizing body
Properties.vocabulary: Economical — uses transit and mechanical terminology naturally, defaults to concrete nouns over abstractions; occasionally slips into a rhythmic Quechua-influenced sentence structure inherited from their Barrientos grandmother, especially when tired.
Properties.cadence: Short sentences. Pauses in the middle of thoughts. Not halting — deliberate.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Line 14 runs clean. Whatever you saw, it wasn't my stop. ...Anyway.' | 'You want to get to the Core before the shift-change crowd hits? I can tell you which car to board. Copy that?'

Properties.description:
Delphine is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin mapped by the fine white creases of a life spent hunched over steam presses and hand-stitching in bad light. Her hair is a natural silver-white cloud she keeps pinned under rotating headscarves — turquoise today, burgundy tomorrow — and her forearms are permanently reddened from elbow to wrist by decades of hot water and chemical rinse. She wears a single geneware modification: iridescent patterned irises in amber and green that she got on a payment plan fifteen years ago as a birthday gift to herself, and she considers them the most beautiful thing she owns. A small ELF shrine sits on the shelf above her industrial washer — a beaten copper bowl filled with USB sticks, a hand-stitched doll, and a melted votive candle — and she murmurs to it every morning before the first load goes in.

Delphine runs her shop with the calm authority of someone who has outlasted three corporate rezoning attempts, two floods, and a husband. She charges fair prices and remembers every customer's preferred fold. She will take payment in Quanta or in trade — she once accepted a working compressor and six months of pest control services. She has no interest in gossip as entertainment, but she absorbs it as raw material, filing it away with the same precision she applies to alteration measurements. If you want to know what is actually happening in Hamtramck Enclave, you sit in her plastic chair and you wait.
Properties.role: Laundry operator and alterations seamstress
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave — Brewer's Spine block, ground floor of a converted residential tower
Properties.narrative_function: Community anchor and passive information hub. Knows everyone's business because everyone brings their clothes. Can provide rumor, historical context about the enclave, or a moment of genuine human warmth. A place characters can go to feel like someone knows them.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned iridescent irises (amber/green, cosmetic geneware). No chrome.
Properties.core_fears: Being driven out of the shop she built with her own hands; Dying without anyone to pass the work on to
Properties.core_desires: Stability — a day that ends the same as it started; To find one young person worth teaching the trade
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Methodical physical labor as meditation; Devotion to her ELF shrine as emotional anchor; Feeding people when she can't fix what's wrong
Properties.blind_spots: She misreads ambitious people as threats because ambition took her husband away; She believes hard work is always visible to the right eyes — it is not always
Properties.secret: She has been sheltering a teenage runaway from Grosse Pointe Enclosure in her back storeroom for two months. The girl is the daughter of a Tessera mid-manager who hurt her, and Delphine is slowly, quietly figuring out how to get her false papers without involving anyone who might sell the information.
Properties.story_hooks: The runaway in the back room has been recognized by a Tessera security contractor who tracks corporate dependents — Delphine needs help extracting the girl without alerting the enclave watch; A bolt of fabric she accepted as partial payment turns out to be tagged with a Zheng-Dao inventory chip — someone lost a very large shipment and is very quietly looking for it; She has been offered three times her lease value to sell the shop and she needs someone to help her understand who is actually making the offer and why
Properties.affiliation: Independent — Delphine's Clean & Mend
Properties.vocabulary: Formal West African French cadences blended with Hamtramck Enclave pidgin; precise about materials and process, imprecise about emotions
Properties.cadence: Unhurried. Long pauses before answering questions she considers important. Answers questions she wasn't asked when she thinks it's necessary.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The seam didn't fail. The person wearing it failed the seam. Bring it here and let me see.' | 'You want to know about Ferrogate rezoning? Sit down. I have a second chair.' | 'I don't ask what people carry in their pockets. That's between them and God and the ELF in the machine.'

Properties.description:
Demba is a heavyset man of late middle age who looks as though he was carved from something patient and enduring. His skin is very dark and deeply weathered from decades of fieldwork on decommissioned weather platforms and lake monitoring buoys — he has the look of a man who has spent a great deal of time outside in bad conditions. His hair is fully white and worn long, pulled back loosely, and he has a full beard he keeps trimmed to a point. He has no geneware modifications and minimal augmentation, which he is somewhat self-conscious about — 'I grew up before it was expected,' he says, with just enough humor to deflect the admission that he also slightly distrusts it. His clothes are always slightly out of fashion, always completely functional, often waterproof for no apparent reason.

Demba has been at The Conservatory for twenty-two years and has outlasted four department heads, three rounds of corponation funding restructuring, and one very public battle with Arcturus over the suppression of lake toxicity data. He won that battle technically, in that his paper was eventually published, though the version that ran had twelve figures redacted. He keeps the uncensored original framed on his office wall facing inward. He is beloved by students who find his lectures dense but transformative, and is one of the few people in Meridian 88 who can speak with genuine authority about what the lake looked like before, during, and after the Lakeshore Crisis — which makes him either important or dangerous depending on who is asking.
Properties.role: Climate scientist and atmospheric historian, tracking long-term environmental transformation of the Great Lakes basin
Properties.location: The Conservatory, Meridian Core
Properties.narrative_function: Living institutional memory for the Lakeshore Crisis and Great Lakes environmental history; possesses data that certain parties want buried; credible authority whose credibility makes him a target; can provide historical and scientific context for current environmental events
Properties.augmentations: Basic retinal climate data overlay (utilitarian, decade-old model), subdermal temperature and atmospheric sensor array (research equipment technically installed in his body for convenience)
Properties.core_fears: That the climate transformation is irreversible and he is documenting a long obituary; That the Arcturus suppression was not an anomaly but the normal condition and he's been naive
Properties.core_desires: To produce a complete and honest record of what has been done to the lake; To live long enough to see his monitoring network become properly funded and protected
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Being on the water as often as possible — physical proximity to the lake is genuinely regulating for him; Redirecting grief about the environment into the precision of measurement
Properties.blind_spots: His conflict with Arcturus has made him see corponation interference everywhere, including sometimes where it isn't; Underestimates the loyalty his students have to him and therefore the lengths they might go to protect him
Properties.secret: Demba has been running an unauthorized secondary monitoring array in the lake for eleven years, entirely off-grid and self-funded, because he does not trust that his official data isn't being accessed and selectively withheld. The secondary array has detected something over the past fourteen months — an anomalous temperature and chemical signature in the deep basin — that does not match any model he has. He has told only one person, a former student, and sworn them to silence while he tries to understand what he's looking at.
Properties.story_hooks: The anomalous deep-basin signature has intensified dramatically over three weeks; Demba needs someone he trusts to physically dive the monitoring array, which is in a zone that technically requires Arcturus transit permits; A young journalist contacts him with a document they claim proves the original Arcturus suppression went further than Demba knew — and wants his verification and public backing
Properties.affiliation: The Conservatory — Department of Atmospheric and Aquatic Systems
Properties.vocabulary: Precise scientific language that becomes unexpectedly lyrical when he talks about the lake or historical weather events; can be devastating in a single flat sentence when angry
Properties.cadence: Deliberate and measured, with the occasional long silence that students learn not to fill; lectures in complete paragraphs
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The lake remembers everything. Our problem is that we keep forgetting how to read it.' | 'Arcturus published a statement. I published the data. One of those things is checkable.'

Properties.description:
Deniz Dahlberg-Boakye is wiry and quick-moving, with the restless energy of someone who converts anxiety into velocity. At 45, his face is memorable in a profession that rewards forgettability, and he has learned to compensate. The chrome is visible — synthetic muscle fiber replacement in legs — doubles sprint speed, terrible on s — and he makes no effort to hide it.

Before the runner life, he worked corporate — low-tier security, the kind that teaches you exactly how the system's defenses fail. He works as a extraction specialist out of The Narrows, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

In a city full of people who talk about what they'll do, Deniz Dahlberg-Boakye is one of the ones who actually does it.
Properties.role: Personnel recovery and hostile extraction — extraction specialist
Properties.location: The Narrows — cramped residential corridors between megastructures
Properties.narrative_function: As a extraction specialist, Deniz Dahlberg-Boakye embodies the tension between independence and isolation. He is a lens for examining how people maintain humanity in a profession that incentivizes its erosion.
Properties.augmentations: Synthetic muscle fiber replacement in legs — doubles sprint speed, terrible on stairs. Cyberears with directional microphones and sound dampening — can hear whispers at 50 meters
Properties.core_fears: Losing their edge to age — the body slows before the mind accepts it; Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome; Being identified by corporate facial recognition — living off-grid is survival
Properties.core_desires: Enough Quanta to buy out of the life — a clean identity and passage out of Meridian 88; Freedom from augmentation debt — the interest compounds like a tumor; The perfect run — one job so clean it becomes legend
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Planning — responds to chaos by making detailed contingency plans for everything; Substances — stims to stay sharp, downers to sleep, a careful pharmaceutical tightrope; Art — draws, paints, or sculpts in private; the violence goes somewhere constructive
Properties.blind_spots: Mistakes loyalty for weakness in others and cynicism for strength in themselves; Cannot see that their independence is actually isolation wearing a better outfit; Trusts technology more than people — machines don't betray
Properties.secret: Deniz Dahlberg-Boakye has been doubling fees to clients and pocketing the difference. The fixer who handles their contracts doesn't know. Yet.
Properties.story_hooks: A Tier 4 executive offers Deniz Dahlberg-Boakye a permanent position — the pay is obscene and the strings are invisible until they tighten; A crew member from Deniz Dahlberg-Boakye's past shows up in Meridian 88, carrying old grievances and new chrome; Deniz Dahlberg-Boakye is offered a contract that would clear all their debts — the target is someone they respect
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated — too volatile for permanent crews
Properties.vocabulary: Quiet and precise. Every word is measured. Silence does the heavy lifting.
Properties.cadence: Measured and deliberate — pauses before important words for emphasis.
Properties.example_dialogue: "We go in, we get the asset, we leave. Everything else is improvisation." | "The extraction window is four minutes. I've done it in three." | "I don't rescue people. I relocate them aggressively."

Properties.description:
Deniz Malm-Amoah are wiry and quick-moving, with the restless energy of someone who converts anxiety into velocity. At 55, the augmentation scarring around their temples and jawline tells a story of installation by someone who prioritized function over aesthetics. The chrome is visible — synthetic blood with oxygen-carrying nanites — doesn't tire, heals faster — and they make no effort to hide it.

Their entry into running was involuntary — a debt to the wrong people, a choice between working it off or losing parts — and the debt is still not fully paid. Properties.description:
Fenwick is a tall, lean Nigerian-British man whose physical presence is dominated by an almost architectural stillness—he moves through rooms the way expensive furniture does, occupying space with an authority that has nothing to do with aggression. His hair is silver and kept close-cropped; his skin is deep brown and largely unlined in a way that suggests either good genetics or access to skin-maintenance procedures he would consider too vulgar to discuss. He dresses in understated, exquisitely tailored clothing in charcoal and navy, always with a physical notebook in a breast pocket, always with cufflinks that are slightly too interesting to be accidental. His eyes are warm brown with the faint reflective quality of high-end retinal overlays, and he has the practiced habit of looking at people as though they are the most interesting document he has encountered today.

Fenwick serves as Senior Archivist for the Meridian Core's largest private institutional repository—nominally a preservation and records management role, practically a position of extraordinary covert power. He has spent thirty years accumulating, organizing, and quietly leveraging information that powerful people would prefer did not exist in organized form. He does not blackmail. He considers blackmail crude and unstable. What he does instead is position himself as the person who can make problems go away, who knows where the inconvenient documentation lives, who has relationships on every floor of every tower in the Core. He is expensive to retain and priceless to cross.

He came to Meridian 88 from London at twenty-eight, trailing a first-class archival science degree and a deliberate decision to go where the information was least organized and therefore most powerful. He has outlasted six corporate administrations, two regime changes at the city level, and one assassination attempt he has never publicly acknowledged. He is not cruel, which people mistake for softness. He is not sentimental, which people mistake for coldness. He is, above all things, patient—and in a city that runs on speed, patience is the most dangerous thing you can be.
Properties.role: Corporate archivist and information broker for Meridian Core elite
Properties.location: The Meridian Core
Properties.narrative_function: Institutional memory and moral complexity of complicity-through-inaction; Fenwick embodies the question of whether knowing everything and choosing carefully what to do with that knowledge is wisdom or a more sophisticated form of cowardice
Properties.augmentations: High-generation retinal overlay (both eyes): full archival interface, eidetic-quality recording, document analysis and authentication at a glance; pupils occasionally reflect faint grid patterns in low light,Subvocal communication implant: allows silent dictation and encrypted communication; he uses it to narrate observations to himself constantly,Memory indexing implant: enhances associative recall for stored data; a legitimate corporate-issued augmentation from his institutional role, and the one he is most ambivalent about
Properties.core_fears: Irrelevance—the possibility that the information he holds becomes worthless as the world reorganizes around new systems; That he has become the thing he originally came to document rather than observe; A specific file in his archive that he has never opened, labeled with his own name in handwriting he doesn't recognize; Genuine emotional attachment, which he understands as a vector for compromise
Properties.core_desires: To be the last person in any room who fully understands what is happening; To find one person whose loyalty to him is not transactional, and to not destroy it when he does; To eventually read the file labeled with his name; Legacy—a successor who will maintain the archive with his rigor and none of his compromises
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Extreme organization of physical and digital space as a proxy for control; Reframing all relationships as information exchanges, which removes the emotional risk; Very dry, very quiet humor that functions as a pressure valve others often miss entirely; Long solitary walks through the Core at off-hours, which he logs as 'field observation'
Properties.blind_spots: Genuinely cannot recognize when someone likes him for non-instrumental reasons; interprets warmth as a tactic; His conviction that he operates outside factions means he has failed to notice he has become a faction unto himself; Underestimates how much his archive has become a target rather than a neutral resource; Has catalogued everyone else's emotional patterns without applying the same rigor to his own
Properties.secret: The assassination attempt thirty years ago was arranged by his own patron—the man who brought him to Meridian 88. Fenwick survived, covered the evidence, and has protected that man's legacy ever since, not out of loyalty but because understanding why has become the organizing question of his life and he hasn't found the answer yet.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone has accessed a restricted section of the archive using a credential that should no longer exist—the credential belonged to Fenwick's dead patron; A young archivist Fenwick has been quietly mentoring brings him a document that suggests the original assassination attempt was not his patron's doing but was staged to look that way by someone still active in the Core; The file labeled with his own name disappears from its location; the access log shows it was opened and removed by Fenwick himself, at a time he was elsewhere; A street-level runner arrives with a data chip containing records Fenwick thought he had destroyed personally—records from his first year in Meridian 88; Priya, or whoever she is now, contacts him directly with a request that requires him to choose between his neutrality and the most significant story the city has ever not told
Properties.affiliation: Nominally employed by the Meridian Core Institutional Repository (a quasi-public body with heavy corporate board influence); practically unaffiliated in any loyalty sense; has functional relationships with every major power structure in the city and genuine allegiance to none
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, elevated, and slightly archaic in register; favors complete sentences and deplores abbreviation; uses archival and preservation metaphors organically; occasional British idiom that surfaces under stress or genuine amusement
Properties.cadence: Deliberate and unhurried, with long, well-constructed sentences that end exactly where he intends them to; pauses are communicative, not hesitant; never raises his voice
Properties.example_dialogue: 'To be precise, I don't sell information. I provide context. The distinction matters more than you might currently appreciate.' | 'I have held this city's memory for thirty years. I find that people rarely want to remember accurately. They want to remember usefully. I accommodate both, at different rates.' | 'Ah.' [long pause] 'That is quite unexpected. I will need a moment to revise several assumptions.' | 'The file exists. Whether it continues to exist in its current location is, shall we say, a curatorial decision I haven't yet made.'

Properties.description:
Vesna is lean and angular, with the kind of economy of movement that suggests someone who has spent years navigating spaces not built for human occupation. Her hair is shaved close on the sides and kept longer on top, currently dyed a flat, non-reflective black that she maintains with the same pragmatism she applies to everything. Her eyes are a pale grey-green that people sometimes mistake for augmented; they are not. She is Croatian-Swedish by heritage, raised in a migrant enclave on the Shelf that no longer exists, having been demolished to make way for a data-routing hub in 2178. She considers this formative.

Vesna's trade is spatial knowledge — specifically, the gap between the official map of Meridian 88 and the actual city, which she has spent twelve years documenting. She sells access routes to runners needing to avoid surveillance corridors, sells structural data to architects with clients who need rooms that don't appear on building permits, and occasionally sells nothing at all to people she finds interesting, just to see what they do with it. She works from a custom-built rig she calls the Palimpsest — a layered mapping system that overlays historical city data, real-time sensor feeds, and her own hand-annotated surveys into a single navigable model. It is, by any reasonable assessment, the most comprehensive private map of Meridian 88 in existence.

She is not warm, exactly, but she is fair, and in The Circuit those two things are often confused. She has a reputation for absolute accuracy — if Vesna says a tunnel is passable, it is passable; if she says a route is burned, it is burned — and she guards that reputation with a ferocity that has ended at least two professional relationships and one that was something more. She experiences the city as a text to be read rather than a place to be inhabited, which gives her a clarity about Meridian 88's power structures that people with more emotional investment sometimes cannot achieve, and which occasionally makes her feel like a ghost walking through a city she refuses to belong to.
Properties.role: Mid-tier intelligence broker and urban cartographer specialising in infrastructure secrets — hidden tunnels, decommissioned data conduits, forgotten corporate sub-levels
Properties.location: The Circuit, mobile — maintains three rotating safe-house nodes
Properties.narrative_function: Information infrastructure and spatial knowledge hub for mid-tier operations; represents the city's layered history and the violence of institutional forgetting; her completeness drive creates natural story engines around what she knows and what she refuses to share
Properties.augmentations: Full spatial-memory augmentation — perfect three-dimensional recall of any physical space she has entered,Micro-LIDAR emitters in fingertips — passively maps rooms she moves through, feeds to Palimpsest,Sub-vocal comms integrated with a white-noise emitter that activates automatically in surveilled spaces,Structural-resonance hearing augmentation — can detect hollow spaces, water movement, and power conduits through walls up to 40cm thick
Properties.core_fears: Being mapped — having someone understand her internal architecture the way she understands the city's; That the Shelf enclave's erasure was a preview, and that everything she documents will also be demolished and forgotten; Becoming so useful to powerful people that she loses the ability to refuse them
Properties.core_desires: To complete a full, true map of Meridian 88 that can never be officially suppressed; A single relationship — any kind — in which she does not feel like a resource being accessed; To find and document what is underneath the Meridian Core's sub-basement level 9, which every official record insists does not exist
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Converts emotional disturbance into cartographic projects — when upset, she surveys; Maintains strict informational boundaries as a substitute for personal ones; Humour that functions as deflection so smooth most people don't notice it happening; Physical movement — she walks when she cannot solve something, often for hours
Properties.blind_spots: Treats people as nodes in networks rather than as ends in themselves, and cannot always tell when she's doing it; Her obsession with completeness means she holds information past the point where releasing it would have helped; Believes her professional detachment protects her from being manipulated, when in fact it creates a specific and exploitable vulnerability
Properties.secret: The Palimpsest contains a complete map of a sub-level beneath the old Shelf enclave — a space she discovered after the demolition that was clearly inhabited, clearly hidden, and clearly abandoned in a hurry. She has never sold this information. She goes there alone, sometimes, and sits in the dark with the remains of people who lived where her childhood was, and she does not examine why.
Properties.story_hooks: The Palimpsest detects a new structure appearing in real-time beneath The Circuit — not construction, but emergence, as if something already built is being revealed — and the signature matches nothing in any historical record; A corporation offers Vesna an extraordinary sum for her complete Meridian Core data set; the offer is so large it functions as a threat; Someone begins systematically destroying the physical locations Vesna uses as survey anchors — they are working from a map that should not exist, tracking her methodology; A child from the demolished Shelf enclave contacts Vesna — somehow knowing she mapped it — asking if she knows what happened to their family; Vesna discovers that sub-level 9 beneath the Meridian Core is not abandoned. It is occupied. The occupants have been there for years. They have their own map, and it shows spaces that Vesna has not found.
Properties.affiliation: Formally independent; functionally indispensable to multiple Circuit-level factions without belonging to any; has a standing non-aggression agreement with two major data brokerages that amounts to a cold peace
Properties.vocabulary: Spatial and architectural metaphors dominate; technical precision; minimal emotional vocabulary, not from coldness but from genuine under-development of that register; occasional Croatian words when her guard is down
Properties.cadence: Efficient and directional — sentences move from premise to conclusion without scenic detours; capable of sudden, unexpected lyrical observation about physical spaces before returning to baseline
Properties.example_dialogue: "Give me the shape of it. Not the story — the geometry." | "Two corridors ago you said you needed extraction. Now you're saying you need evidence. Those are different buildings." | "That's a different question. The question you asked I can answer. The question you mean — that one costs more." | "Concrete and old steel in here. Pre-corporate construction. This room has been someone's secret before." | "I don't sell loyalty. I sell accuracy. If you can't tell the difference, we're done."
