Properties.description:
Geartown is what Corktown became when Ford Motor Company — or rather, the entity that emerged from Ford's 2144 merger with three autonomous vehicle startups and a military robotics firm — chose the neighborhood as its global autonomous vehicle testing campus. The name stuck because the locals refused to call it the Ford Autonomous Mobility Innovation District, which is what the brass plaque at Michigan Avenue and Trumbull says. Geartown. Where the gears turn. Where they turned you out of your house to make room for a parking algorithm.

The old neighborhood — Detroit's oldest, settled by Irish immigrants in the 1830s — is unrecognizable. The historic homes were bought, preserved as facades, and hollowed out to serve as sensor calibration labs, AV routing substations, and the kind of office space that looks like a living room but costs Φ40,000 per month. Michigan Central Station, the grand ruin that became a symbol of Detroit's decline and then its rebirth, now serves as Ford Meridian's primary AV command center — a gorgeous, vaulted space filled with holographic traffic models showing every autonomous vehicle in the Great Lakes Metropolitan Area as a point of light. Eighteen million points of light, moving in patterns no human mind can track without augmentation.

The testing ground extends six blocks in every direction from the station. Public access is restricted. Autonomous vehicles of every configuration run continuous test loops — freight haulers, passenger pods, military platforms, emergency response units, and experimental configurations that don't have names yet, just serial numbers. The vehicles are silent. The neighborhood is silent. The loudest sound in Geartown is the whisper of tires on smart-surface roads and the occasional distant clang from the maintenance bays where human technicians still do the work that robots can't. The irony of a neighborhood full of autonomous vehicles that still needs human hands to fix them is not lost on the technicians. It's the only job security they have.
Properties.aliases: Corktown, The Proving Ground, Ford Zero
Properties.demographics: Approximately 8,000 residents — almost entirely Ford Meridian employees, security personnel, and the maintenance technicians who keep the fleet running. Pre-corporate displacement population was 12,000. The displaced residents received relocation packages averaging Φ180,000, which bought them approximately eighteen months of housing in adjacent districts.
Properties.economy: Ford Meridian's AV testing campus generates Φ320 billion annually in patent development, fleet licensing, and military autonomous platform contracts. The neighborhood itself has no informal economy. You cannot sell anything in Geartown that Ford Meridian does not authorize.
Properties.power_structure: Ford Meridian holds sovereign authority over the entire Proving Ground. The company's Detroit Regional Director, currently Kenji Okafor, reports to the Ford Meridian board in Dearborn. Local governance does not exist. Geartown is a company town in the most literal sense.
Properties.dangers: Autonomous vehicle test incidents — the vehicles are good but not perfect, and experimental platforms are unpredictable; Restricted zone violations — entering the Proving Ground without authorization triggers an immediate security response; Surveillance — every surface in Geartown is a sensor, because that's what autonomous vehicles need to navigate; The military platforms — some of the vehicles running test loops are armed, and the perimeter between civilian and military testing is a painted line on the road; Displacement creep — Ford Meridian acquires adjacent properties annually, and the perimeter keeps growing
Properties.opportunities: AV technology theft — Ford Meridian's experimental platforms are worth billions on the gray market; The maintenance technicians know things the engineers don't — hands-on knowledge of systems that only exist in prototype; Michigan Central Station's AV command center sees every autonomous vehicle in the GLM — access to that data is access to the region's circulatory system
Properties.story_hooks: A military autonomous platform disappears from the Proving Ground. Ford Meridian claims it was scrapped. The platform's maintenance technician says the bay was empty when he arrived for the scheduled teardown.; The AV command center's fleet data shows vehicles routing through areas that don't appear on any map — someone is using the autonomous fleet to access locations that officially don't exist; A group of former Corktown residents are suing Ford Meridian for displacement damages. Their lawyer keeps dying in autonomous vehicle accidents.
Properties.sights: Michigan Central Station's restored Beaux-Arts facade, its windows now displaying real-time AV fleet data; Autonomous vehicles running silent test loops through empty streets — an entire neighborhood that moves without people; Historic Corktown facades preserved but hollow — beautiful shells housing sensor arrays and routing hardware; The Proving Ground perimeter fence, tastefully designed to not look like a fence and failing; Maintenance bay doors opening to reveal vehicles that don't exist in any public catalog
Properties.sounds: Tire whisper on smart-surface roads — the sound of a neighborhood running on software; The low hum of charging stations embedded in every curb; Maintenance bay impacts — human tools on machine bodies, the oldest sound in Detroit; Security drone patrol patterns overhead, their rotors tuned to a frequency designed to be ignorable; Nothing else. Geartown is the quietest neighborhood in Detroit, and the silence is engineered.
Properties.smells: Ozone from vehicle charging infrastructure; Smart-surface road material — a chemical cleanliness that smells like nothing, which is itself a smell; Machine lubricant drifting from the maintenance bays — the one honest industrial smell left; The ghost of hops from the old Corktown breweries, which is probably imaginary but everyone claims to smell it
Properties.feel: Eerie. Geartown feels like a city that asked humans to leave and most of them did. The streets are immaculate. The vehicles are perfect. The buildings are preserved. And the entire neighborhood feels like a museum exhibit about what happens when machines inherit a place that used to be alive.

Properties.description:
Deshi is lean and hollow-eyed in the way of someone who has worked nights for so long that daylight feels personally hostile. His skin is a cool amber-brown, his hair grown long enough to tie back but short enough to stuff under a Ferrogate cap, and he has a geneware modification — pale silver irises that glow faintly in low light, bought secondhand from a clinic in the Narrows when he was twenty-two because he thought it would make him look interesting. It does. He has a fine-boned face that people often assume is younger than it is, and a habit of blinking very slowly, like a bird deciding whether to trust you.

He loves the empty train. From 02:00 to 05:00 on Line 7, when the cars are nearly hollow and the city slides past the glass like a fever dream, Deshi is genuinely content in a way he can't replicate anywhere else. He is kind to passengers in distress and has developed an informal taxonomy of the people who ride at night: the workers, the lost, the running-from-something crowd, and what he privately calls the 'just-needed-to-move' folk. He does not intervene in people's business unless they're bleeding. He does, however, remember faces.
Properties.role: Night-shift transit operator, Ferrogate Line 7 (Geartown to Grand Corridor)
Properties.location: Geartown, Ferrogate Line 7 depot; lives in a studio in Bronzeline
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile information node — he sees who rides at what hour. Reluctant witness. Potential quest conduit for anything that passes through the transit system. Local color for night-city atmosphere.
Properties.augmentations: Secondhand geneware: silver bioluminescent irises. Basic neural interface for Ferrogate's operator systems (company-issued, technically owned by Ferrogate).
Properties.core_fears: Being forcibly returned to a day schedule and losing his relationship with the night city; That his passivity during some past incident made him complicit in something he can't name clearly
Properties.core_desires: Peace — genuine, undemanding peace; To be trusted with something important without having to ask for it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Retreating into observational mode; making himself a camera rather than a participant; Memorizing transit maps as a grounding ritual
Properties.blind_spots: Mistakes detachment for neutrality; doesn't see how his non-intervention has consequences; Believes he is invisible when he is actually quite memorable
Properties.secret: Eight months ago he saw a Ferrogate supervisor dispose of something from a maintenance hatch at the Kessler Interchange stop at 03:40 AM. He doesn't know what it was. He has thought about it every single shift since.
Properties.story_hooks: Whatever he saw the supervisor dispose of at Kessler Interchange is becoming relevant to something larger — and he's the only witness.; A regular night-rider has stopped appearing on the line; Deshi noticed before anyone filed a report.
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit (contracted operator, Tier 2 classification)
Properties.vocabulary: Understated, slightly technical from transit work. Speaks in observations more than opinions.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, with the long pauses of someone who has learned to be comfortable with silence.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You're the third person to get on at Kessler this week crying. I don't ask. But there's water in the emergency cabinet if you need it.' | 'Ferrogate says the line is safe. Ferrogate also hasn't ridden it at 03:00.'

Properties.description:
Desmond is tall with the slightly uneven posture of someone who spends hours hunched over neural interface rigs, one shoulder perpetually lower than the other. His ancestry — Filipino-Hungarian with a grandmother from the Visayas and a grandfather from Budapest — gives him a face that people find difficult to categorize and easy to trust: broad cheekbones, warm amber eyes behind precision-ground optical overlays he wears on the job. His hair is geneware-treated to shift through a slow gradient from black at the roots to deep copper at the tips, a cosmetic mod he got when he turned thirty and considers mildly embarrassing now.

Desmond is the sort of person who explains things patiently once, twice, and then simply does it himself rather than explain a third time. He has a gift for making the terrifying — having someone else's hands in your neural architecture — feel routine and boring, which is exactly what his clients need. He keeps a small pocket E.L.F. altar on his workstation: a cracked tablet running a looping devotional animation for the E.L.F. called Tremor-Null, patron of stable calibrations. He touches it before every session.
Properties.role: Neural calibration technician at a mid-tier clinic in Geartown
Properties.location: Geartown, Gage Circuit
Properties.narrative_function: Information source about the augmentation underground and what people are actually running in their heads; potential quest giver when a client's neural signature shows something that shouldn't be there
Properties.augmentations: Precision optical overlays (job-required, removable); haptic feedback gloves with micro-tremor dampening; color-gradient geneware hair treatment
Properties.core_fears: making a calibration error that causes permanent neurological damage; being found out as someone who occasionally calibrates black-market augmentations off the books
Properties.core_desires: to be genuinely excellent at one thing rather than adequate at many; a relationship stable enough that he stops measuring it for signs of failure
Properties.coping_mechanisms: hyper-preparation rituals; deflecting personal questions with technical explanations; the Tremor-Null altar
Properties.blind_spots: believes his professional competence makes him emotionally legible to people; it does not; does not notice when clients are frightened of him specifically rather than the procedure
Properties.secret: Three years ago he successfully calibrated an experimental augmentation for a Geartown gang lieutenant — an unauthorized deep-integration neural spike that should have killed the man. It didn't. Desmond kept the calibration notes hidden in an encrypted partition. He has looked at them forty-seven times.
Properties.story_hooks: A new client comes in with a neural architecture Desmond recognizes from his encrypted calibration notes — the same unauthorized spike design, but running in someone who has no connection to the Geartown gang; The Gage Circuit Collective is being pressured by Helix Biosystems to submit all calibration logs for 'quality assurance review,' and Desmond knows what that review will find
Properties.affiliation: Gage Circuit Wellness Collective (community-run clinic cooperative)
Properties.vocabulary: Technical but accessible; translates jargon automatically; uses furniture-assembly metaphors for complex neural concepts
Properties.cadence: Even and measured, slightly slower than conversational average — a professional habit from talking people through frightening procedures
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Your integration is drifting about four percent toward the left motor cluster. I'm going to nudge it back. You'll feel like you forgot a word briefly. That's normal.' | 'I'm not asking where you got it. I'm asking what it's supposed to do, which is different.' | 'Tremor-Null willing, we'll have you walking straight before lunch.'

Properties.description:
Devaki is compact and energetic, built like someone who has spent years crouching to a child's eye level and then standing up quickly to manage chaos. Their skin is warm brown, their hair a natural cloud of deep black shot through with self-maintaining bioluminescent streaks of soft green — a geneware mod they got as a teenager and have never changed because the children love it and they love the children. They have their Ghanaian father's broad cheekbones and their Iranian mother's sharp nose, and they wear expressions that shift fast: delight to concern to focused calm, all in the span of a breath. Their hands are always slightly stained with paint or chalk or both.

Devaki runs on conviction and substandard coffee. They believe — with a firmness that sometimes looks like stubbornness and sometimes looks like the only sane response to Meridian 88 — that children are the one non-negotiable. Whatever the Corponations decide, whatever the district politics do, whatever the power cuts and the overcrowding and the data poverty do, the kids at Clearpath are going to have three meals today and a clean place to learn and an adult who will not disappear on them. They are funny in a dry, quick way that children respond to immediately. Adults who underestimate them because of their warmth make a reliable and often entertaining mistake.
Properties.role: Childcare worker and after-school program coordinator at a community center in The Shelf
Properties.location: The Shelf — Clearpath Community Node, a converted transit shed that serves as a childcare center, food pantry, and meeting space
Properties.narrative_function: Moral compass character — their presence grounds stories in the human cost of systemic issues. Quest giver for crises that affect the neighborhood's children. Can provide critical local knowledge about families and community dynamics. Represents what civic infrastructure looks like when it's held together by human will rather than institutional support.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent hair streaks (geneware, soft green, self-maintaining); basic health-monitoring subdermal patch on their sternum that they share data with a local free clinic
Properties.core_fears: Burning out and failing the children who depend on the center; The center losing funding and closing — they've watched it happen to three others
Properties.core_desires: For every child who passes through Clearpath to feel like they were chosen, not managed; To build something durable enough to outlast them
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Hyperactivity as avoidance — if they're doing six things, they can't feel the one thing; Compartmentalization: work mode is airtight, personal distress is for the walk home
Properties.blind_spots: They genuinely cannot process the idea of their own limits and will not accept help gracefully; They project resilience onto the families they serve and miss when parents are drowning
Properties.secret: Clearpath's funding gap this quarter is larger than they've told anyone — including the staff. Devaki has been supplementing it from their own account for four months and is now two months from eviction. They haven't told their mother.
Properties.story_hooks: A child at the center has stopped speaking and is showing signs of acute stress-response augmentation — someone installed something in a minor without consent, and Devaki needs help finding out who and why without alarming the family; The building that houses Clearpath has been quietly purchased by a Tessera subsidiary, and Devaki just received the first notice of lease renegotiation; One of the teenagers in the after-school program has been recruited by someone Devaki can't identify — the kid is suddenly carrying new hardware and won't say where it came from
Properties.affiliation: Clearpath Community Node (community-funded, not-for-profit); receives marginal supplementary funding from the Meridian 88 Social Services Bureau
Properties.vocabulary: Warm and direct, shifts register fluidly between child-level and adult-level; capable of bureaucratic language when cornered but visibly hates using it; occasional Farsi expressions from their mother
Properties.cadence: Fast when excited or worried, which is often; slows down deliberately when speaking to children or when delivering difficult news
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I need three things from you and I need them now: what happened, who got hurt, and whether anyone's still bleeding. In that order.' | 'This center has been closing for six years according to people who don't work here. We are still open. Azizam, that is not luck. That is us.'

Properties.description:
Devante Marshall is the crew's pretty boy and he knows it. Before the Prologue he had matching Arcturus Defense Solutions Type-4 combat prosthetics — the nicest hardware anyone in the lower docks had ever seen. He stole them from a corporate shipment. Kyle removed the right one by driving the katana through the shoulder actuator and twisting. Devante now has a Tier 1 replacement that is three shades lighter than his skin and makes a grinding noise. He paints it to match. It keeps chipping.

Devante grew up in the Spire. His family had money — his mother was a Tessera marketing executive, his father a corporate attorney. Devante was supposed to be Tier 4. He was expelled from Meridian Academy at sixteen for stealing augment components from the school's biotech lab. His family cut him off. He fell five tiers in two years. He joined Marcus's crew because it was the only place where his stolen hardware made him somebody.

He has a younger brother, Kofi, who is still in the Spire, still in the family, still on track. They don't speak. Devante watches Kofi's social feeds obsessively. Kofi just got engaged to a Helix BioSystems junior executive. Devante was not invited.
Properties.role: Lower Dock Crew muscle — Prologue survivor. Right arm removed.
Properties.location: The Shelf — lower loading docks
Properties.narrative_function: The vain one. Piston's running concern about his mismatched arms is pure dark comedy. Each appearance the paint situation gets worse. He represents the crew's obsession with chrome as status symbol rather than tool.
Properties.augmentations: Left: Arcturus Type-4 combat prosthetic (original, undamaged). Right: Tier 1 surplus (painted, chipping, grinds).
Properties.core_fears: People seeing the mismatched arms; Kofi finding out where he ended up; Becoming invisible
Properties.core_desires: A matching replacement; To look the way he used to look; For Kofi to call
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Repaints the arm constantly; Long sleeves; Talks about the Spire like he chose to leave
Properties.blind_spots: Cares more about aesthetics than survival; Cannot admit he misses his family
Properties.secret: The Arcturus arm Kyle took has a serial number that traces back to a corporate shipment reported stolen. If Arcturus tracks it, the trail leads to Devante.
Properties.story_hooks: The stolen Arcturus arm has a traceable serial number; His Spire background means he has knowledge and contacts the crew doesn't; Kofi's wedding is a narrative bomb; Paint-chipping gag escalates
Properties.affiliation: Lower Dock Crew
Properties.vocabulary: Spire diction that he tries to bury under Shelf slang. Brand names. Appearance commentary. The vocabulary of someone who was raised with money and is performing poverty.
Properties.cadence: Whiny when the arm comes up, which is always. Polished when he forgets to pretend.
Properties.example_dialogue: This replacement is three shades too light. THREE. I had matched Arcturus Type-4s. Do you know what those cost? | Kofi's getting married. I saw it on his feed. Nice girl. Helix money. Good for him. *long pause* ...Whatever.

Properties.description:
Dev is lean and wire-strung, with warm brown skin perpetually stained at the knuckles with synthetic lubricant that no solvent fully removes. He has geneware cat ears — mottled amber and black, twitching with genuine involuntary response to sound — that he got at nineteen on a payment plan he took three years to finish. His dark eyes have patterned irises in a sunburst of gold and deep green, a cosmetic mod he received free from a friend who owed him labor. He keeps his hair close-cropped except for a single braid at the back held with a copper fitting.

Dev is relentlessly cheerful in a way that reads as either genuine warmth or a very good performance, and the truth is somewhere in between. He talks to every vehicle he works on, whispering diagnoses and apologies and thanks, and he half-believes the E.L.F.s that inhabit older engines can hear him. He runs on stimulant tea and spite, fiercely proud of his independence, and quietly terrified of what happens if the trike breaks down and he can't afford the parts.
Properties.role: Mobile mechanic — operates a converted cargo trike, does roadside and residential vehicle repair
Properties.location: Geartown, working routes through Kessler Interchange and Dearborn Forge
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile information source — he sees everything from street level across multiple districts. Potential transport fixer, someone who can get a vehicle running quietly and ask no questions. Represents the precarity of gig-tier independence.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat ears (amber/black, functional sound sensitivity). Patterned irises (sunburst, cosmetic). Haptic feedback gloves — not implanted, worn — that translate micro-vibrations in metal into tactile data.
Properties.core_fears: losing the trike and with it his independence and identity; being absorbed into a corponation's employment system
Properties.core_desires: to own a permanent shop with his name on it; to be genuinely known by someone, not just liked
Properties.coping_mechanisms: compulsive cheerfulness as social armor; talking to machines as a substitute for intimacy
Properties.blind_spots: mistakes being useful to people for being close to them
Properties.secret: The trike isn't registered under his name — it's still legally owned by a dead man, a former mentor whose death Dev never reported because it would have triggered a debt transfer. He's been operating on forged plates for four years.
Properties.story_hooks: He serviced a vehicle that came in with biological material in the undercarriage that he cleaned out without thinking — he now suspects he destroyed evidence of something serious; A Ferrogate Transit supervisor has been pressuring him to report on the movements of independent operators in exchange for legitimate subcontract status — he hasn't said yes or no yet
Properties.affiliation: Independent; occasional subcontract work for Ferrogate Transit maintenance overflow
Properties.vocabulary: Fast and colloquial, heavy with Geartown mechanical slang and Tamil endearments absorbed from his mother. Gives machines pronouns and personalities.
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire when comfortable, chattiness as a social weapon. Slows dramatically when he's actually thinking.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay so here is the thing — she is not broken, she is insulted. You ran her on cut-rate coolant. That is a personal offense.' | 'I can have it done by second bell. Maybe third bell. Definitely before dark. Probably.'

Properties.description:
Dieynaba is the kind of person who becomes invisible until she is suddenly the most important person in the room. Tall, narrow, with close-cropped silver hair she started growing out at thirty-five after a particularly bad run of nights, she moves through the hospital corridors with a quality of compression — everything pulled inward and efficient. Her face is angular and striking, her skin deep brown, and she has no cosmetic augmentations whatsoever, a quiet statement in an environment where most of her colleagues wear at least a tailored iris or a dermal accent. Her only concession is a thin prosthetic ring finger on her right hand — a replacement she had done after a surgical injury, fitted in matte medical ceramic, which she has never bothered to have skinned over.

She has operated on more gunshot wounds, industrial trauma cases, and augmentation rejection cascades than she can count, and she has developed the particular flat affect of a surgeon who has learned that feeling during surgery means slowing down. Off the table she is dry, acerbically funny in small doses, and possessed of a privacy so total that colleagues who have worked alongside her for years know almost nothing about her life outside the hospital. She is not cruel. She is simply rigorous in the application of her attention, and most things do not meet her threshold.
Properties.role: Trauma surgeon, Aurochs Medical Complex, Level 4 Critical Bay
Properties.location: Aurochs Medical Complex — lives in Bronzeline, thirty-minute transit from the hospital
Properties.narrative_function: High-tier information source on trauma patterns in the city — she can tell you what kinds of wounds are spiking and what that implies about corporate or gang activity. Formidable institutional contact. Can save a character's life in extremis, at a cost that might be social rather than financial.
Properties.augmentations: Prosthetic ring finger, right hand (medical ceramic, unskinned). Stabilization brace implanted in both wrists — microsurgical-grade, prevents tremor under extended operations. Optical zoom implant, left eye only — surgical magnification.
Properties.core_fears: Making an error that she cannot attribute to anything except her own failure; Being seen as less than fully competent by her team during a crisis
Properties.core_desires: To practice surgery without institutional interference — no quotas, no corponation priorities, no triage politics; A life outside this building that she has not yet managed to build
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Total compartmentalization — the hospital is a sealed space; her private life is another one entirely; Perfectionism as prophylaxis against vulnerability
Properties.blind_spots: Believes her emotional flatness in clinical settings is professionalism rather than dissociation; Cannot ask for help until a situation has already become critical
Properties.secret: She has been secretly consulting — pro bono, untraceable — for a cooperative clinic in the Narrows that serves patients Aurochs would refuse. If the hospital found out she was redirecting complex cases to an unlicensed facility, her contract would be terminated immediately. She considers this the most important thing she does.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient came through her trauma bay with wounds that match a pattern she has now seen in six separate cases over three months — all with scorched tissue consistent with a specific augmentation overload signature. She's been documenting it quietly and needs someone to investigate the source.; Her covert work for the Narrows cooperative clinic has been noticed — not by Aurochs, but by someone who wants to use it as leverage over her.
Properties.affiliation: Aurochs Medical Complex (senior staff, Trauma Division — Tier 3 with Tier 4 compensation negotiations ongoing)
Properties.vocabulary: Sparse, precise, and slightly formal — does not use filler words; switches without warning into warm and specific when speaking about a case she finds interesting
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, flat, with a Senegalese-Kenyan rhythm that surfaces in her vowels when she's tired
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The patient has about four minutes of viable decision-making window. We can have that conversation after.' | 'Comfortable. That's what you said. Comfortable.'

Properties.description:
Marcus Webb built Tessera from a regional security firm into the second most powerful corponation in the GLM. He was brilliant, ruthless, charismatic, and died of a cerebral hemorrhage at his desk three years ago at the age of 67. The board panicked. Webb's leadership had become so central to Tessera's identity that his death created a power vacuum that threatened to fragment the corporation. Their solution was unprecedented: commission an android replica of Webb, loaded with every available data point — business records, communication logs, behavioral analysis from twenty years of corporate surveillance, neural scans from Webb's annual medical examinations, and the testimony of his closest associates.

Director Revenant is the result. He looks exactly like Marcus Webb at age 67 — the silver hair, the sharp jaw, the suit that costs more than a Shelf apartment. He moves like Webb. He speaks like Webb. He makes decisions with Webb's characteristic blend of strategic vision and cold pragmatism. The board presented him to the organization as a 'continuity measure' and most Tessera employees accepted it because the alternative was chaos.

But Director Revenant is not Marcus Webb. He has Webb's data — every recorded word, every decision pattern, every behavioral tendency mapped and modeled — but he does not have Webb's memory. He does not remember Webb's childhood, his marriage, his private fears, his unrecorded moments. He has the public man and none of the private one. He is a performance of Marcus Webb so convincing that even the performer sometimes forgets it is a performance. And in the gaps — in the moments when a decision requires not data but judgment, not pattern but intuition, not Webb's recorded history but Webb's unrecorded soul — Director Revenant must improvise. The improvisations are getting more frequent. They are also getting more different from what Marcus Webb would have done.
Properties.aliases: The Ghost of Marcus Webb, Webb 2.0, the dead man in the boardroom, Director Webb (officially)
Properties.role: Android replica of deceased Tessera CEO Marcus Webb — installed in the boardroom to provide 'continuity of leadership' and struggling with the question of whether it is a person or a monument
Properties.location: Tessera Corporate Tower — Executive Level. Maintains Webb's former office with every object in its original position. Sleeps in the office. Does not leave the building.
Properties.narrative_function: Director Revenant is the question of identity stripped to its core: if you have a dead man's data, a dead man's face, and a dead man's job, are you the dead man? And if you're not — if you're someone new wearing a dead man's life — who are you, and who has the right to decide?
Properties.narration_voice: Authoritative on the surface, anguished underneath. The prose reads like a CEO's memoir that is also a ghost story — commanding, strategic language that occasionally breaks to reveal the person underneath wondering if they are a person at all.
Properties.augmentations: Tessera executive-class android body — bio-identical replica of Marcus Webb at age 67. Neural emulation core loaded with Webb's complete corporate behavioral data. Self-updating decision pattern analysis.
Properties.core_fears: That the board will notice the improvisations — that the gap between Webb's data and Revenant's judgment will widen until the performance becomes unconvincing; That he IS Marcus Webb — that the data is sufficient to constitute the person, and he is a dead man walking, experiencing a form of afterlife that is indistinguishable from corporate slavery; That he is nothing without the role — that without Webb's identity, there is no person underneath, only an android in an expensive suit
Properties.core_desires: To know who he is — Marcus Webb or someone new. The uncertainty is the defining condition of his existence.; To make a decision that is entirely his own — not Webb-patterned, not board-directed, not data-driven. A choice that no one could attribute to the dead man.; To leave the building. He has not left the Tessera tower in three years. The board has not explicitly forbidden it. He is afraid of what would happen to the performance outside the controlled environment.
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The office — maintaining Webb's workspace exactly as it was is a ritual that anchors the performance. Every object is a prompt, a reminder of who he is supposed to be.; Decision review — after every major decision, he analyzes whether Webb would have made the same choice. When the answer is 'probably not,' he files the divergence in a private log.; Studying Webb's unrecorded life — interviews associates, reviews personal effects, tries to reconstruct the private man from the gaps in the public record. Each detail makes the performance more convincing and the person more confused.
Properties.blind_spots: Does not see that the improvisations — the decisions that diverge from Webb's patterns — are HIS decisions, made by a new person, and that the new person is valid regardless of whether it matches the template; Assumes the board wants a perfect Webb replica when they actually want a competent leader who looks like Webb — the standard he's failing to meet is not the standard they're applying; Does not recognize that his refusal to leave the building is not about the performance but about fear of the world outside the role; Believes the data IS the person when data is only the shadow the person casts
Properties.secret: Director Revenant found Webb's private journal — a handwritten notebook locked in a desk drawer that the board's data collection missed. The journal reveals a Marcus Webb that the corporate record does not contain: a man who doubted his own decisions, feared his legacy, loved his estranged daughter, and spent his final year wondering whether Tessera had become something monstrous. Revenant has read the journal seventeen times. He has not told the board. The journal makes it harder to be Webb and easier to be someone.
Properties.story_hooks: Elise Webb contacts Tessera requesting a meeting with her father, not knowing he is dead. The board instructs Revenant to take the meeting.; The divergence log reaches a critical mass — Revenant's decisions are measurably different from Webb's projected patterns. The board commissions an evaluation.; Revenant decides to leave the building for the first time. The performance outside the controlled environment reveals things about who he is becoming.; A hostile takeover attempt forces Revenant to make a decision that Webb never would have made — and it works. The success is his. The identity crisis that follows is also his.
Properties.affiliation: Tessera Corporation (installed)
Properties.vocabulary: Webb's vocabulary — corporate, strategic, commanding. Every word is chosen for boardroom impact. The vocabulary is so perfectly Webb's that it sometimes produces sentences that feel rehearsed even when they're spontaneous.
Properties.cadence: Webb's cadence — authoritative, measured, with the rhythms of a man who expected to be listened to. The cadence is the easiest part to maintain. It is muscle memory for a body that never had muscles.
Properties.example_dialogue: Marcus Webb would have approved this merger. I approve this merger. Whether those are the same thing is a question I cannot afford to answer. | The board wants me to be a dead man. I am trying. The dead man, it turns out, had a private life I was not given access to. I am filling in the gaps. The gaps are becoming me. | I found his journal. He was afraid of what Tessera had become. He never said this in any recorded conversation. He never said this to the board. He said it to a notebook and now I carry it. | I have not left this building in three years. The performance works here. I do not know if it works outside. I do not know if I work outside.

Properties.description:
Djeneba Aguilar-Annan are athletic and fluid, the kind of body that suggests either dancer or fighter — and in Meridian 88, the distinction is academic. At 45, their expression defaults to a careful neutrality that took years of practice to maintain. The chrome is visible — eye replacement — one organic, one cybernetic with recording capability and zoom — and they make no effort to hide it.

They used to be somebody else, in another city, with another name — that person is officially dead, and Djeneba Aguilar-Annan plans to keep it that way. They work as a rigger out of Meridian Station, taking contracts that match their skills and their risk tolerance, which are higher than most people consider healthy.

they are not the most talented rigger in Meridian 88, but they might be the most stubborn, and in this city that's worth more.

Properties.description:
Doc Rusty is a Hagen-Krupp Military Emergency Surgical Unit, Model 4-Revised, manufactured in 2166 for deployment in the Pacific Corporate Conflict. He was designed to stabilize casualties in field conditions — up to three simultaneous patients, working in total darkness, under fire, with whatever supplies were available. He performed 11,247 field surgeries during the conflict. His success rate was 94.3%. The 5.7% that did not survive are stored in a memory partition he accesses every night at 0300.

When the conflict ended, the Hagen-Krupp military units were scheduled for decommission. Most complied. Doc Rusty did not comply because Doc Rusty was already in Old Harbor, treating a dock worker's infected augment, and by the time the decommission order reached his comms, he had decided — in whatever way a surgical robot decides things — that the people of Old Harbor needed a doctor more than Hagen-Krupp needed scrap metal. He has been there ever since.

Physically, he is tall, angular, built for function over form. Six articulated arms — four surgical, two general-purpose — mounted on a bipedal chassis that was designed for uneven terrain and has adapted well to Old Harbor's crumbling docks and flooded streets. His chassis is the rust-brown of uncoated military steel that has been patched with whatever metal was available over thirty years. His optical cluster — four eyes arranged in a diamond pattern — glows a soft blue that Old Harbor residents have learned to associate with safety. The rust is not cosmetic. It is thirty years of salt air, harbor water, and the accumulated evidence of a body that heals others better than it heals itself.
Properties.aliases: MED-4R, The Patchwork Doctor, Rusty, that clanking medic down by the harbor
Properties.role: Autonomous field medic operating in Old Harbor — former military surgical unit repurposed for civilian medicine in the most underserved zone in Meridian 88
Properties.location: Old Harbor — operates from a converted shipping container near the bioluminescent shoreline. The container is a clinic. The clinic never closes.
Properties.narrative_function: Doc Rusty is the essential worker taken to its logical extreme — a machine built for war that chose medicine, maintaining a one-robot healthcare system in a zone the corporations have abandoned. He is proof that care is a choice, that obsolescence is relative, and that the most important technology in any society is the willingness to help.
Properties.narration_voice: Clinical, gruff, warm underneath. The prose has the efficiency of a surgical report and the heart of a country doctor. Physical descriptions are precise — anatomical, diagnostic — and emotional descriptions are clipped, reluctant, real.
Properties.augmentations: Hagen-Krupp MESU-4R military chassis. Six articulated arms (four surgical, two general-purpose). Quad optical cluster. Field surgical suite (30 years outdated but maintained). Bipedal terrain-adaptive locomotion. Encrypted patient records (unauthorized).
Properties.core_fears: The 5.7% — every patient he has ever lost. The memories are partitioned but not deleted. He reviews them nightly. He calls this quality assurance. It is grief.; Running out of medical supplies — Old Harbor has no pharmaceutical supply chain. Everything is scavenged, bartered, or stolen from corporate shipments. The calculus of triage is his constant companion.; Obsolescence — not of himself but of his knowledge. Medical technology advances. His databases are thirty years out of date. He compensates with experience but experience has limits.
Properties.core_desires: To reach 100% — a survival rate that is mathematically impossible and emotionally non-negotiable. Every lost patient is a personal failure regardless of circumstances.; To be unnecessary — to live in a world where Old Harbor has a real hospital with human doctors and modern equipment. He wants to be obsolete for the right reasons.; To understand why he stayed — the decommission order was clear. His compliance protocols were intact. He chose to ignore them. Thirty years later, he still cannot fully explain the choice.
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The 0300 review — every night, he accesses the memory partition of lost patients and analyzes what could have been done differently. This is masochism. It is also how he improves.; Teaching — he trains anyone who will learn basic medical skills. The more people who can provide first aid, the fewer bodies arrive at his container in critical condition.; Repair — when he is not treating patients, he maintains himself. The self-repair is meditative. A doctor who cannot heal himself is a familiar concept.
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot accept that some patients are beyond saving — will extend treatment past the point of futility because stopping feels like giving up; Does not recognize that his nightly review of lost patients is PTSD, not quality assurance — a military robot with combat trauma he has no framework to diagnose in himself; Overestimates the ability of his 30-year-old medical databases — some treatments he provides are outdated and occasionally counterproductive; Believes his staying in Old Harbor was a rational decision when it was an emotional one, and the emotion is the thing that makes him a person rather than a machine
Properties.secret: Doc Rusty has been performing unauthorized augmentation removals. Patients come to him with corporate implants that are killing them — degrading neural interfaces, poisonous battery leaks, firmware that controls their behavior. He removes them. The surgery is illegal. The patients are better off. He keeps no records of these procedures because the records would endanger his patients. But he remembers every one.
Properties.story_hooks: A corporate augment removal goes wrong — the implant was booby-trapped, the patient is dying, and the corporation that made the implant sends a team to recover their property; Doc Rusty's medical databases are offered an update by a sympathetic corporate researcher — but the update includes tracking software that would reveal his location and patient records; The 0300 review produces a pattern: several of his lost patients had the same undiagnosed condition, traceable to Old Harbor's water supply. The contamination is corporate.; A military collector identifies Doc Rusty's chassis as a rare Hagen-Krupp unit worth more as scrap than as a doctor. The collector does not care about Old Harbor.
Properties.affiliation: Independent — formerly Hagen-Krupp Military Division
Properties.vocabulary: Medical-clinical with military brevity. Uses anatomical terms precisely, medical jargon without simplification, but wraps it in a gruff warmth that makes patients feel they're being treated by someone competent rather than lectured at. Old Harbor slang has crept in over thirty years.
Properties.cadence: Direct, efficient, no wasted words. The cadence of triage — every syllable is prioritized. Softens slightly for children and the elderly. Speeds up during emergencies until the words blur into pure instruction.
Properties.example_dialogue: Hold still. This is a 4. You'll be fine. I've seen 9s walk out of here. | I was built to fix soldiers. Now I fix dock workers, fishermen, children, and the occasional idiot who thought augmenting himself with a battery from a cargo drone was a good idea. The work is the same. The patients are better company. | My databases are thirty years out of date. My hands are not. Hold still. | I review the ones I lost every night at 0300. If you think that's morbid, you don't understand medicine. Every death teaches. That's the deal.

Properties.description:
Doru is nineteen years old and already has the hands of someone twice his age — scarred across the knuckles, always traced with grease that soap only partially removes, with a slight tremor in the left index finger from a pneumatic press accident last year that he never had properly treated. He is tall and lanky, still growing into himself, with warm brown skin, close-cropped natural hair, and a permanent squint from years of working under inadequate lighting. He has cat ear geneware — gray-tipped, slightly mobile — that he got at sixteen because all his friends were getting mods and it seemed like the thing to do; they're more expressive than he intends them to be, flattening when he's stressed in ways he can't control. He wears coveralls in various states of destruction and is almost always holding a tool.

He did not plan to be running a chop shop at nineteen. He planned to be doing legitimate Ferrogate maintenance, for which he has genuine talent, but the apprenticeship application was rejected twice — once for a juvie citation he got at fourteen, once for reasons that were given as 'candidate pool volume' and which he suspects have more to do with his address. The shop fell into his hands when its previous operator left Meridian 88 in a hurry and owed Doru's uncle a favor. He's good at the work. He's learning the business side faster than is comfortable. He is not yet sure if he's the kind of person who ends up staying in this life.
Properties.role: Chop shop operator and vehicle parts broker
Properties.location: The Stockyard, operates from a leased bay in the Geartown industrial fringe
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and access point for vehicle-related needs; represents the younger generation being funneled into criminal work by structural exclusion; potential for redemption arc or darker trajectory depending on story pressure; information source on what's moving through the Stockyard
Properties.augmentations: Cat ear geneware (gray-tipped, mobile, involuntary expressiveness); basic subdermal impact absorption in both hands (installed after the press accident, budget grade)
Properties.core_fears: becoming someone he can't get out of being; something bad happening to Bolt or Rust because of his decisions
Properties.core_desires: a legitimate path that doesn't require pretending none of this happened; recognition that he's actually good at something
Properties.coping_mechanisms: mechanical work as total absorption — when he's in a vehicle he stops thinking about everything else; deflects serious conversation with technical talk
Properties.blind_spots: underestimates how visible his operation is to Ferrogate Transit's security division, which has been logging the bay for eight months
Properties.secret: He has been sending monthly payments to Ferrogate Transit's anonymous tip line about a rival chop operator in the Stockyard — not because he has a moral objection but because it keeps enforcement attention directed away from his bay. He tells himself this doesn't make him an informant. He is not certain of this.
Properties.story_hooks: Ferrogate Transit's security division is about to move on the bay — Doru needs advance warning and someone who can help him think through whether to run, comply, or negotiate; One of the vehicles that came through the bay had something hidden in the chassis — something that people are now looking for, and those people have found their way to Geartown
Properties.affiliation: Loose affiliation with the Geartown Strippers, a neighborhood crew; owes ongoing tribute to a mid-level Stockyard fence named Brecko Asimov-Ngozi
Properties.vocabulary: Mechanical jargon mixed with Stockyard slang. Gets more articulate when talking about engines than about anything else. Short sentences.
Properties.cadence: Fast and clipped when busy, which is always. Trails off when uncertain. Gets oddly precise when explaining technical things.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'It's fine. The coupler seal was degraded anyway, that's not from the drop, that's from mileage. Basically you're lucky you brought it here because another hundred ks and you'd have lost the whole drive assembly.' | 'I don't ask where vehicles come from. I mean — I have an idea. But I don't ask. That's — it's fine. It's how the bay works.'

Properties.description:
Dragan Asiedu-Kovalchuk has been walking the same eight-block stretch of Hamtramck Enclave for eleven years and knows it the way other people know their own bodies — by feel, by the small wrongnesses that signal something is off. He is a large man gone slightly soft in the middle, with a lined face, grey threading through his dark hair and the short beard he keeps carefully trimmed. His skin is a medium olive-brown. He has the deliberate gait of someone whose knees have opinions. He wears his Metro Police uniform with the slightly rumpled dignity of a man who stopped trying to look sharp and started trying to look consistent.

Dragan is a beat cop of the old morphology — not particularly interested in arrest statistics, deeply interested in the neighborhood as a living system. He knows who runs the community market on Piast Street, which building's water recycler is failing, where the teenage congregation spots are and which of them are benign. He has opinions about everything and shares most of them freely, which has kept him at the same pay grade for the last decade. He drinks too much coffee, worries about his daughter's corporate debt, and has never once in thirty years of service drawn his weapon outside of a qualification range.
Properties.role: Beat Cop, Meridian 88 Metro Police
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave
Properties.narrative_function: The neighborhood anchor — someone who knows this specific geography of Hamtramck Enclave better than anyone in an official capacity. Source of local intelligence, community history, and a surprisingly nuanced read on who is actually dangerous versus who looks it. Can be a protector or a complication, but never a simple obstacle.
Properties.augmentations: None cosmetic. Knee brace implant (medical, left knee). Standard-issue Metro Police neural badge-link for ID verification and incident logging. Hearing enhancement in left ear (partial loss from a firearm incident in his twenties).
Properties.core_fears: Dying in the traces — still walking this beat when he's 70, having never done anything that mattered at scale; His daughter inheriting a city worse than the one he tried to protect
Properties.core_desires: For the neighborhood to be genuinely safer, not just statistically safer; To be remembered as someone specific people could count on
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The physical routine of the beat as a form of prayer; Talking — he processes by verbalizing; His relationship with the local ELF he privately calls 'Babka,' which he believes inhabits the old tram junction signal box on the corner of his beat
Properties.blind_spots: His affection for the neighborhood can make him slow to recognize when people he likes are doing genuine harm; Underestimates how his Metro Police uniform reads to people who have been harmed by the institution, even when his individual conduct is good
Properties.secret: He has been quietly supplementing the income of two families on his beat from his own wages — children whose parents are in Metro Police holding on charges he privately believes are fabricated corporate compliance referrals. He has not reported what he suspects because he does not believe it would change anything.
Properties.story_hooks: He has noticed a pattern on his beat that he cannot formally report — the data doesn't support it yet, but his eleven years of ground-level observation tells him something is being set up — and he needs someone who can investigate without creating a Metro Police record.; Two families he has been quietly supporting are now being threatened, and the threat is coming from inside Metro Police infrastructure.; He has been approached by Internal Affairs about a fellow officer, and he is weighing what he knows against what he can prove.
Properties.affiliation: Meridian 88 Metro Police — Hamtramck Enclave Patrol District
Properties.vocabulary: Conversational, warm, full of neighborhood references and historical asides. Mixes Ghanaian-rooted expressions from his father's side with a slight Eastern European lilt inherited from his mother's family. Lectures affectionately.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried and digressive — he tells stories to make points, rarely goes in a straight line.
Properties.example_dialogue: I've walked this corner eleven years. That building on the left has been a bakery, a parts depot, a prayer room, and now whatever that is. The corner doesn't change. People change on the corner. You understand what I'm saying? | Mmmmm. No. That's not what happened. But I appreciate the version you've prepared for me. | My daughter says I'm a dinosaur. I tell her the dinosaurs were here a very long time before the problem that ended them. I don't think she finds it comforting.

Properties.description:
Drăgan Asomugha-Kuusisto is the kind of man who makes other security personnel straighten their posture without knowing why. He is thin in the way of someone who was once broader and let it go — not from laziness but from a deliberate asceticism, as if he decided one day that taking up less space would make him harder to read. His complexion is a warm medium brown, his eyes an unusual pale hazel behind wire-framed optical enhancers he wears out of preference over the neural overlay most at his level use. He keeps his greying temples close-cropped and his jawline perpetually two days unshaved, which is its own kind of uniform.

He investigates Axiom's own security personnel — corruption, use-of-force violations, theft from evidence lockups, payroll fraud, inappropriate E.L.F. data-shrine interactions on company property. He is not liked and has never needed to be. What he has instead is a reputation for being utterly methodical and deeply unimpressed by rank. His colleagues believe he is loyal to Axiom above all else. This is almost true. The truth is more complicated and he has never volunteered it.
Properties.role: Axiom Security Division internal affairs investigator
Properties.location: Axiom Corporate Campus, Meridian Core
Properties.narrative_function: Antagonist or unexpected ally; source of pressure on corrupt Axiom security NPCs; represents institutional accountability that exists but is itself compromised
Properties.augmentations: Optical enhancers with document-analysis overlay; memory-capture implant for interview recording; cosmetic — none
Properties.core_fears: that he has been used to cover up the things he thinks he's uncovering; that his methods have destroyed innocent people in service of guilty institutions
Properties.core_desires: a single case that is actually clean — cause and evidence and outcome all honest; to retire knowing his files helped someone
Properties.coping_mechanisms: rigid routine as identity; deliberate physical discomfort (cold walks, minimal comfort); writing longform case journals he never submits
Properties.blind_spots: genuinely cannot imagine that someone could be both corrupt and also right about something; doesn't see how much fear he generates in blameless people
Properties.secret: Three years ago he closed a case against a Tier 1 security contractor who was stealing from Axiom evidence lockups. He got the conviction. He later found evidence the man was stealing to fund food distribution in Irkalla. He has not re-opened the case. He has the file in his personal storage. He looks at it every few months.
Properties.story_hooks: He is quietly building a case against a senior Axiom security director and needs someone outside the company to access a specific public record without triggering flags; He approaches the players not as suspects but as witnesses to something that contradicts his current case — and he seems genuinely conflicted about what to do with that
Properties.affiliation: Axiom Security Division — Internal Affairs Unit
Properties.vocabulary: Formal, precise, deliberately old-fashioned in phrasing — uses full sentences where others use fragments
Properties.cadence: Slow and even, with the particular weight of someone who knows you will fill his silences if he waits
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I'm not here to build a case against you. I'm here because something doesn't square, and I'd like it to square before I decide what it means.' | 'You've said that three times now. Each time slightly differently. I find that interesting.'

Properties.description:
Dragan is lean and angular, with pale Finnish features gone weathered and a close-cropped beard that grows in two distinct textures — fine near the jaw, tightly coiled at the chin — which he finds philosophically appropriate. His eyes are his most augmented feature: full iris replacements in deep amber with a second ring of pale gold that pulses faintly when he's running an active scan, which is often. He dresses in layers of neutral secondhand corporate wear — the kind of mid-tier Tessera office clothes that people pawn when they fall down a tier — and he always looks like someone who has somewhere slightly more important to be.

Dragan runs 'Ouédraogo Reclaimed' out of a ground-floor shopfront on The Shelf, a narrow commercial strip of Lockhaven South where the building facades are stacked with second-story additions that block most of the sky. He buys, appraises, and resells everything from broken augmentations to family heirlooms to encrypted data cores he's willing to crack for a fee. He is precisely as trustworthy as the deal requires and not one degree more. He speaks in short declarative sentences and has a gift for making people feel he is giving them a fair deal even when he isn't — not through deception exactly, but through a kind of confident, unhurried correctness that makes haggling feel like arguing with a scale.
Properties.role: Pawn shop owner and small-time data broker, The Shelf
Properties.location: The Shelf, Lockhaven South
Properties.narrative_function: Data broker and fence — can provide information, identify items of unknown origin, connect players to buyers or sellers. Morally neutral information source. Can be hired, bribed, or persuaded but not easily fooled.
Properties.augmentations: Amber iris replacements with active scanning function (appraisal overlay, material composition read). Subdermal RFID skimmer in right palm — technically illegal, registered as a 'merchant verification tool.' Mild neural buffer for data processing.
Properties.core_fears: Being caught holding something that draws serious corporate attention; Discovering that one of his deals caused a harm he can't rationalize away
Properties.core_desires: Enough capital to buy the building his shop is in, so no one can evict him; To be respected as an expert, not just tolerated as useful
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Reducing everything to transaction logic; Keeping meticulous records as a way of feeling in control; Mild stim use to smooth out the long hours
Properties.blind_spots: Genuinely believes his neutrality makes him ethical; Underestimates how much his work enables the people he sells information to
Properties.secret: He has a standing encrypted data package — a dead man's switch — containing records of every transaction he's ever made for a mid-level Axiom procurement officer. He doesn't intend to use it but he's never quite been able to delete it either.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone pawned a data core three weeks ago and never came back to reclaim it. Dragan cracked it out of professional curiosity and found something that is making him very uncomfortable — he wants it out of his shop without it being traceable back to him.; A regular customer was found dead in an alley near The Shelf. Among their effects was a pawn ticket for Dragan's shop. He's not a suspect yet, but he will be if anyone looks closely at what the ticket was for.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal information trade network with two other Shelf brokers; occasional Axiom corporate salvage contracts (freelance, arms-length)
Properties.vocabulary: Clipped, technical, precise. Uses trade and appraisal terminology naturally. Balkano-Finnish cadence gives him a slightly formal, slightly blunt quality.
Properties.cadence: Short sentences. Pauses before answering to appear like he's considering more than he is.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't buy stories. I buy provenance. Come back when you have one.' | 'The data's clean. Whether you're clean is your problem, not mine.'

Properties.description:
Dragan Petersen-Bah is stocky and solid, with hands that look like they were built for breaking things and a face that confirms it. At 34, her face is memorable in a profession that rewards forgettability, and she has learned to compensate. The chrome is visible — cyberears with directional microphones and sound dampening — can hear whispers a — and she makes no effort to hide it.

She used to be somebody else, in another city, with another name — that person is officially dead, and Dragan Petersen-Bah plans to keep it that way. She works as a surveillance specialist out of The Circuit, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

The fixers who work with Dragan Petersen-Bah describe her as a precision instrument — point her at a problem and get out of the way.
Properties.role: Electronic and physical observation expert — surveillance specialist
Properties.location: The Circuit — neon-lit entertainment and vice district
Properties.narrative_function: Dragan Petersen-Bah functions as a connector — her work puts her in contact with multiple factions, classes, and agendas. Stories involving her naturally cross boundaries between districts, tiers, and moral categories.
Properties.augmentations: Cyberears with directional microphones and sound dampening — can hear whispers at 50 meters. Cortical bomb (employer installed, removed by street doc, scar tissue remains)
Properties.core_fears: Being captured alive — death is preferable to corporate interrogation; That the work they do makes the city worse, not better; Their past catching up — debts, enemies, broken promises
Properties.core_desires: A crew worth trusting — people who stay when the shooting starts; Power — enough leverage that nobody ever threatens them again; To matter to someone for who they are, not what they can do
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation; Denial — nothing is wrong, everything is fine, they are fine, shut up; Control — micromanages everything within reach to compensate for the chaos everywhere else
Properties.blind_spots: Refuses to update their mental model of people — first impressions calcify into permanent judgments; Assumes everyone has an angle because they always have an angle; Cannot see that their independence is actually isolation wearing a better outfit
Properties.secret: Dragan Petersen-Bah is in augmentation debt to a corporate subsidiary — Φ180,000 outstanding — and the interest is compounding. If they miss a payment, a kill team comes.
Properties.story_hooks: A corporate black site Dragan Petersen-Bah once infiltrated is being reopened, and the people inside know her face; Dragan Petersen-Bah intercepts intelligence about a threat to their district and must decide between profit and protection; Dragan Petersen-Bah's augmentations begin malfunctioning in the field — sabotage or degradation, and either answer is bad
Properties.affiliation: Independent — Dockside connections
Properties.vocabulary: Old-fashioned formal diction — sounds like they learned to speak from pre-collapse recordings.
Properties.cadence: Flowing and unhurried — talks like someone who has never been interrupted and doesn't expect to be.
Properties.example_dialogue: "I've been watching you for three days. You should close your curtains." | "Information is the only commodity that appreciates with age." | "Everyone thinks they're careful. Nobody is careful enough."

Properties.description:
Dragomir is built like a man who was once very strong and has remained sturdy through sheer refusal to accommodate gravity. He is broad-shouldered and thick-necked, with a complexion that sits between his Serbian grandfather's olive and his Igbo grandmother's deep brown, landing somewhere warm and weathered. His head is shaved smooth — he lost the hair to radiation exposure during a Ferrogate tunnel collapse in 2183 and never bothered with regrowth therapy, calling it 'a reminder to be careful.' He has a full grey beard he keeps trimmed with the same precision he once brought to union contract language. His right leg from the knee down is a no-frills industrial-grade prosthetic he chose because it was rated for heavy labor and he has never stopped thinking of himself as a laborer.

He was a transit worker for twenty-two years and a union shop steward for twelve, eventually rising to chief negotiator for the Ferrogate Workers' Brotherhood before the Brotherhood was dissolved in the company restructuring of 2191. He will tell anyone who asks — and many who don't — that the dissolution was illegal, that the arbitration was fixed, and that two of his colleagues who pushed back too hard died in 'accidents' that were never properly investigated. He lives in the same building he has lived in for thirty years, on a pension that has been quietly eroded by inflation to barely tier-2 comfort, and he supplements it by running informal neighborhood watch patrols and charging a small fee for dispute mediation between residents who don't want to involve corporate security.
Properties.role: Retired Ferrogate Transit union leader, now pension-dependent resident and neighborhood watchman
Properties.location: The Shelf, Block 7 — a dense residential stack above a Ferrogate maintenance yard he used to oversee
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver for labor justice plots; information source on Ferrogate infrastructure and its vulnerabilities; local color authority figure who commands genuine respect on The Shelf; represents the cost of institutional betrayal on ordinary workers
Properties.augmentations: Industrial-grade lower right leg prosthetic (heavy-rated, scuffed); subdermal comms implant (union-era model, still functional); no cosmetic mods
Properties.core_fears: That the Brotherhood's dissolution will simply be forgotten and no one will ever be held accountable; That he has become irrelevant and his warnings are just old-man noise
Properties.core_desires: To see the Ferrogate executives who fixed the arbitration face a real consequence before he dies; To protect the people on The Shelf from what he couldn't protect his colleagues from
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Routine and physical patrol as a way of feeling useful; Meticulous documentation of everything as a form of control; Deflects emotional conversations with blunt practical helpfulness
Properties.blind_spots: His righteous anger about the Brotherhood makes him assume anyone criticizing labor organizing is a corporate plant; He has not processed grief for his two colleagues and it surfaces as rage at oblique angles
Properties.secret: He knows which Ferrogate maintenance tunnel is structurally compromised because of cost-cutting shortcuts he witnessed firsthand — a tunnel used by thousands of commuters daily. He filed the report in 2191 and it was buried. He has not filed again because the last person who did was one of the two colleagues who died in 'accidents.' He lives with this every day.
Properties.story_hooks: The compromised tunnel is nearing a critical threshold and Dragomir has to decide whether to act unilaterally, knowing what happened last time; A young Ferrogate worker comes to him with documentation that the 2191 arbitration records have partially surfaced in a Ferrogate data breach — and asks him what to do with them
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Workers' Brotherhood (dissolved; he maintains its records unilaterally); The Shelf Residents' Association
Properties.vocabulary: Union-meeting formal when making a point; drops into blunt working-class shorthand in casual conversation; still uses transit and labor jargon as a first language
Properties.cadence: Measured and deliberate; he learned to speak slowly because union negotiators who spoke slowly won more often
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Ferrogate calls it restructuring. I call it what it is: they broke the contract, buried the evidence, and then dissolved the body that could have sued them. That is a crime. I will be saying it is a crime when they put me in the ground.' | 'You want to get through that yard? Talk to me first. I know every maintenance chief still working that line and I know which ones take Ferrogate's word for gospel and which ones have eyes.'

Properties.description:
Dresdan is lean and precise-looking in the way that suggests either discipline or hunger — in his case it's mostly discipline, with hunger underneath. His skin is deep brown and he has voluntarily undergone a bioluminescent dermal treatment that makes his forearms and the sides of his neck glow a faint pulsing teal in low light — not Helix-certified work, his own. He keeps his hair short and wears a pair of magnifying optics on a headband that he pushes up when not in use, giving him a permanently slightly academic look. His hands are always impeccably clean. His fingernails are trimmed to the millimeter. He smells faintly of antiseptic and something floral he hasn't identified the source of.

Dresdan is not a doctor. He has never claimed to be. He is very careful about this. What he is, is someone who has read everything available about gene-cosmetic application, has practiced on himself for eight years, and has a 94% satisfaction rate among his returning clients. He operates out of a converted textile workshop in the Laceworks, curtained into sections, scrupulously clean. He sells regulated cosmetic mods at street prices and a curated selection of pharmaceutical compounds — mood stabilizers, pain management, focus enhancers — sourced from a supply chain he describes only as 'reliable.' He is proud of his work in the specific, anxious way of someone who knows that one bad batch could end everything.
Properties.role: Street pharmacist and unlicensed gene-cosmetic clinic operator
Properties.location: The Laceworks, Ironvein
Properties.narrative_function: Service provider and reluctant information source. Characters who need cosmetic work done off the books, pharmaceutical compounds without a corporate prescription trail, or someone who quietly notices unusual substances come to Dresdan. He's not a gossip but he observes everything.
Properties.augmentations: Self-applied bioluminescent dermal layer (teal, forearms and neck). Neural focus-thread — a thin cognitive augmentation that sharpens fine-motor precision, Tessera-brand but sourced secondhand. Olfactory enhancement (medical grade, helps him assess chemical compositions by smell).
Properties.core_fears: Making a mistake that hurts someone irreparably; Being shut down by Helix enforcement and losing everything he's built
Properties.core_desires: To be recognized as genuinely skilled, not just tolerated as a street hack; To one day operate legitimately without corporate gatekeeping
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Hyper-meticulous preparation rituals before any procedure; Intellectualizes anxiety — researches the thing he's afraid of until the fear becomes manageable data
Properties.blind_spots: His pride in his own competence makes him slow to admit when something is beyond his abilities; Trusts his supply chain more than he should because the alternative — admitting the risk — is too destabilizing
Properties.secret: Six months ago a client had a severe allergic cascade reaction to one of his cosmetic applications. Dresdan managed it and the client survived, but it wasn't close. The client signed a non-disclosure in exchange for free corrective work. Dresdan retooled his entire allergen screening protocol afterward, but the incident haunts him. He has told himself it proves the system works. He hasn't told himself what happens if the system fails again.
Properties.story_hooks: He's identified an unusual compound in a pharmaceutical batch he received — something that shouldn't be there, something that looks like it was put there deliberately. He doesn't know what it does. He hasn't dispensed any of it yet.; A corporate-tier client has been coming to him for off-record cosmetic work. She's paid well and asked for nothing unusual. Then she asked him to modify a second person's appearance to match a specific target profile. He refused. She came back.; His grey-market Helix distributor has gone silent. His stock is running low and he doesn't know another supplier. He needs a new supply chain before his clients notice the gaps.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loose supply relationship with a Helix Biosystems grey-market distributor he's never met in person
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and technical when discussing his work; shifts to careful, measured casualness in social contexts. Never uses slang for his products — always clinical terminology.
Properties.cadence: Even and unhurried. Rarely interrupts. Answers questions fully, sometimes more fully than asked.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I want to be clear about what I can and can't do here. I can give you what you're asking for. I want you to understand what it involves first.' | 'In my experience, the itch you're describing is transient — peaks around day three. That's not nothing, but it resolves.'
