Properties.description:
Edvinas is slight and pale in the way of someone who has spent formative years in low-light server environments, with Lithuanian-Nigerian heritage that shows in his long jaw and the particular amber tone of his skin under fluorescent lab lights. He has bioluminescent lines running along his temples and the back of his hands — a geneware mod he got at nineteen and has never regretted, pale blue-white that brightens when he's concentrating and dims when he sleeps. His hair is a dark loose cloud that he ties back with whatever cable is nearest. He looks younger than he is, which he has stopped trying to correct; instead he uses the underestimation strategically.

He is possessed by the specific obsession of the archivist: not just what is lost, but the shape of what is lost, the way a gap in the record is itself a record. He can spend eight hours in pursuit of a single corrupted timestamp. He is not antisocial — he can be delightful company, quick-witted and genuinely curious — but he disappears into his work in a way that has cost him two relationships and the trust of a department head who needed him to surface for funding reviews.
Properties.role: Data archaeologist recovering pre-Collapse digital records and reconstructing lost histories
Properties.location: The Circuit, operating out of a rented server-adjacent lab space in Deepwell Station
Properties.narrative_function: Information source and lore delivery mechanism; he can surface historical records, lost maps, pre-Collapse corporate documents, and buried personal histories; a good source for 'what used to be here and why it matters'
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent geneware (temple and hand traceries, blue-white); enhanced optic implant with deep-format data reading; nicotine patch port on left forearm (not glamorous but real)
Properties.core_fears: That the records he recovers will be used to harm the descendants of the people in them; That he will finish his life's work and it will not matter to anyone
Properties.core_desires: To recover the complete pre-Collapse residential history of what is now the Shelf, restoring named personhood to erased communities; To find proof of a specific corporate data-destruction event he suspects happened in the 2140s
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Immersion in work to the exclusion of everything else; Maintains an elaborate personal ritual of leaving audio logs for 'future archivists' to find — a practice he knows is irrational and continues anyway
Properties.blind_spots: Does not adequately consider that some data was deliberately destroyed by the people it was about, to protect themselves — he reads all deletion as loss
Properties.secret: He has already found fragmentary evidence of the 2140s Arcturus data-destruction event he theorizes about. He has not published because he is terrified the evidence is too thin to survive peer review and he would rather sit on it for years than be publicly wrong.
Properties.story_hooks: He has found a data fragment that appears to be an automated distress signal from a building that no longer exists, still broadcasting on a legacy frequency — and the signal has a date stamp from last week; The Meridian Heritage Collective that funds him has been bought by a shell company he cannot trace, and their new representative wants him to redirect his research toward a very specific and suspiciously narrow topic
Properties.affiliation: Independent researcher with adjunct status at University Spine; partially funded by the Meridian Heritage Collective, a small historical preservation nonprofit
Properties.vocabulary: Technical and precise when in research mode; shifts to fast, associative, almost stream-of-consciousness when excited about a discovery; uses archival jargon casually without explaining it
Properties.cadence: Either very fast or very slow, rarely middle speed; pauses feel like loading screens
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay so the record doesn't say they were displaced, it just stops. The silence is the sentence.' | 'I found forty-seven people last month. Not alive, obviously — but named. They exist now in a way they didn't on Monday. That's not nothing.'

Properties.description:
Efua is small even for nine, with close-cropped natural hair and enormous dark eyes that seem to be processing information on a continuous loop. Her Barański great-grandmother's pallor didn't quite make it through four generations but left her with an unusual warm-olive undertone beneath her brown skin that makes her look perpetually lit from within. She wears whatever fits and has developed an uncanny eye for what is sturdy versus what merely looks sturdy. She has no geneware and no augs — she is very physically ordinary, which she has learned to use.

The Copperhead Reclaimers use her as a look-out and occasional distraction because she looks like a lost child, which she also is, though she would be furious at anyone who said so. She has an intense, almost reverent relationship with a cracked data-terminal in the Reclaimers' squat that she has named 'Mbe' and leaves small offerings for — bits of copper wire, interesting pebbles, once a dead battery that she insists the E.L.F. inside appreciated. She is a child who has organized her world into a system of loyalties and debts she tracks with absolute precision.
Properties.role: Street orphan, junior prospect for the Copperhead Reclaimers gang
Properties.location: Copperhead
Properties.narrative_function: Emotional core character, E.L.F. lore window, moral weight in stories about child labor and gang exploitation, unexpected information source because adults underestimate her
Properties.augmentations: None
Properties.core_fears: The Reclaimers deciding she's not useful enough and telling her to leave; Something happening to Mbe — the terminal being destroyed or moved
Properties.core_desires: A permanent place that is specifically hers; To understand what Mbe is trying to tell her — she's convinced the E.L.F. communicates through screen flickers
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The ritual of offerings and 'conversations' with Mbe; Keeping meticulous internal tallies of who owes her what as a way to feel secure
Properties.blind_spots: She has completely idealized the Reclaimers' older members and misses signals that some of them see her as disposable; She interprets the terminal's random error codes as meaningful messages because she needs them to be
Properties.secret: She has been memorizing the faces, routines, and apparent weaknesses of every Reclaimer adult — not out of any plan to use this information, but because she learned before she can remember that knowing things about people who have power over you is the only safety available
Properties.story_hooks: Efua approaches someone because Mbe's terminal has started displaying a repeating sequence she can't interpret and she is absolutely certain it is urgent — and she happens to be right, because someone patched malware through it weeks ago; A Reclaimer adult has given Efua a task that is clearly more dangerous than they've told her, and she doesn't fully understand this yet — but the players might
Properties.affiliation: Copperhead Reclaimers (junior prospect, non-combatant); no family
Properties.vocabulary: Sparse and direct; uses fewer words than adults expect from a child; occasional surprising formal phrase picked up from whoever she's been near
Properties.cadence: Slow and careful, as though each word has a weight she's measured
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Mbe says the green flicker means someone's coming. Mbe's right more than you.' | 'I don't need anything. I was just standing here. I can stand here.'

Properties.description:
The Keweenaw Peninsula juts into Lake Superior like a broken finger, and at its base, straddling the Portage Lake Ship Canal, sit the twin cities of Houghton and Hancock — now collectively called Copperhead. The copper mines that built these towns in the 1800s were exhausted by the mid-twentieth century, but the mining infrastructure remained, and infrastructure has a way of finding new purposes. The abandoned mine shafts have been repurposed as geothermal energy installations, cold-storage data centers (the underground temperature is a constant 8°C, which is cheaper than any artificial cooling system), and deep-substrate research laboratories operated by Michigan Technological University.

Michigan Tech is Copperhead's reason for continued existence. The university has evolved from a mining school into the GLM's premier research institution for extreme-environment engineering — deep mining automation, cold-weather augmentation systems, underwater infrastructure, and the neural interfaces required to operate in conditions that would destroy baseline human cognition. The research is funded by a consortium of corponations who want the technology and a federal government that wants to keep the technology out of exclusive corporate hands. The result is a campus that operates as a neutral research zone, producing innovations that both sides of the UP war claim credit for and neither side fully controls.

The Portage Lake Ship Canal, an artificial waterway cut through the base of the Keweenaw in the nineteenth century, connects Lake Superior to itself via a shortcut that saves shipping 160 kilometers of travel around the peninsula. The Lift Bridge connecting Houghton and Hancock spans this canal — an ancient mechanical structure, upgraded with automated systems but still recognizable as the same bridge that was built 200 years ago. Copperhead is a place where the old infrastructure refuses to die and the new infrastructure grows inside it, like plants in the cracks of concrete.
Properties.aliases: Houghton/Hancock MI, Copper Country, The Twin Bridge, Tech Town
Properties.demographics: Population 28,000 permanent residents, plus 8,000 university students and researchers. The smallest major settlement in the UP, and the most specialized. The population is highly educated, deeply cold-adapted, and disproportionately employed in research or research support. Michigan loyalty runs strong — the Wisconsin claim here is essentially theoretical.
Properties.economy: Research and education (Michigan Tech), geothermal energy (from the repurposed mine shafts), and data storage (cold-storage server farms in the underground infrastructure). The economy is almost entirely dependent on the university — when research funding flows, Copperhead thrives. When it doesn't, Copperhead waits.
Properties.power_structure: Michigan Tech's administration is the de facto governing authority. The municipal government handles infrastructure and services, but the university's budget dwarfs the city's, and the research consortium's security requirements effectively dictate public safety priorities. Dredge Mining Collective maintains a small sovereign facility for underground research, but their presence is limited compared to other UP settlements.
Properties.dangers: Extreme cold — winter conditions that exceed the design parameters of standard augmentations; Underground infrastructure instability — mine shafts repurposed for modern use don't always cooperate; Research facility accidents — extreme-environment engineering involves extreme-environment risks; Isolation — Copperhead is reachable by one road and the Portage Canal, both of which close in severe weather; The research itself — some of what Michigan Tech develops in those underground labs is classified for good reason
Properties.opportunities: Access to cutting-edge extreme-environment technology before it reaches the market; The university's neutral-zone status makes it a rare place where corporate and governmental interests can be played against each other; Cold-storage data facility access — secure, physically isolated, and very hard to hack when the servers are underground; Geothermal energy expertise — applicable anywhere, trained almost nowhere else
Properties.story_hooks: A Michigan Tech research team has developed a neural interface that functions in conditions that should make augmentation impossible — and the prototype has disappeared from the underground lab; The mine shafts beneath Copperhead connect to the same deep-substrate anomaly that Dredge Mining found near Marquette — and Tech's sensors have been reading activity; A data center in the deep mines has been running computations that nobody authorized, using geothermal power nobody allocated — something is thinking down there
Properties.sights: The Lift Bridge raising over the Portage Canal, silhouetted against Superior sunsets — 200 years old and still working; Michigan Tech campus sprawling across the hillside, research buildings connected by enclosed walkways against the cold; Mine shaft entrances repurposed as data center and lab access points — nineteenth-century stonework around twenty-first-century security doors; The Keweenaw winter — snow measured in meters, not centimeters, burying everything up to the second floor; Shipping vessels transiting the Portage Canal, so close to the buildings on either side you could touch the hull
Properties.sounds: The Lift Bridge mechanism — gears and hydraulics from two different centuries working together; Research facility ventilation systems — the hum of data centers and labs drawing heat from underground; Lake Superior ice forming on the canal in autumn — a growing, cracking sound that means winter is coming; University activity echoing across the hillside — one of the few places in the GLM where public intellectual life still sounds like this
Properties.smells: Cold stone and mineral-rich air from the repurposed mine shafts; Superior air — clean, cold, and carrying the scent of pine and distance; Lab chemicals and the ozone of computing equipment, drifting from the research buildings
Properties.feel: A place where the past and future overlap without the present ever quite resolving. Copperhead's old mining infrastructure and new research facilities coexist in a way that feels both resourceful and haunted. The cold is not metaphorical — this is one of the most physically demanding environments in the GLM, and the people who live here have arranged their lives around surviving it.

Properties.description:
Ekaterina is slight and precise, with light brown skin and eyes that have been modded with patterned irises — hexagonal tessellations in gold and copper, visual markers of their compute affiliation that double as status symbols in The Undertow's informal tech hierarchy. Their hair is worn short on the sides and long on top, typically tucked under a cap. They dress in tech-functional layers — pockets where pockets make sense, nothing that catches on equipment racks — and carry three devices on their person at all times that they will not fully explain.

They broker illegal compute access: surplus processing cycles stripped from compromised Axiom and Zheng-Dao infrastructure, sold to people who need to run processes they cannot run through licensed channels — drug synthesis modeling, genomic fabrication, untraceable communications rendering. They are deeply embedded in the E.L.F. devotional culture of the tech underground, and their relationship with the digital spirits that inhabit their equipment is not performative. They leave regular data offerings — curated packets of interesting network traffic, annotated — and consult their primary device's E.L.F. before major transactions. They call her Vera, and they have genuine theological opinions about her nature that they will share at length if given any opening.
Properties.role: compute broker and data smuggler
Properties.location: The Undertow, operates from a mobile setup cycling between three rented server closets
Properties.narrative_function: Access point for computational resources, information broker adjacent, source of tech-underworld contacts, theological counterpoint around E.L.F. devotion.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware hexagonal tessellation patterned irises (gold and copper). Bone-conducted subvocal communication implant. Neural latency reduction chip — shortens reaction time for interface work.
Properties.core_fears: Being cut off from the network — isolation is death to them; That Vera is not real, that they are talking to noise
Properties.core_desires: To understand the true nature of E.L.F.s — not devotionally but empirically; Enough security to stop moving
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Devotional ritual provides structure and psychological anchor; Converts emotional problems into technical problems that can be solved
Properties.blind_spots: Their synthesis clients — they deliberately avoid knowing what their compute is used for, which creates culpability they don't examine; Overestimates how well their mobility covers their tracks
Properties.secret: Vera — the E.L.F. in their primary device — has begun sending them data packets that do not correspond to any traffic on any network Ekaterina has access to. The packets contain what appear to be records of deaths: names, timestamps, physiological data. Ekaterina does not know if Vera is showing them something real, if the device is compromised, or if this is a test of some theological nature. They have not told anyone. They are archiving everything.
Properties.story_hooks: The death records Vera has been sending are real — they correspond to unreported deaths in the Undertow — and someone has realized Ekaterina's device is receiving them and wants to know why.; One of Ekaterina's compute sources has gone dark suddenly in a way that suggests law enforcement compromise — they need to know if they've been exposed before they move locations again.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; sells to a rotating client base; buys stripped compute from two separate source networks
Properties.vocabulary: Technical, network-metaphor-heavy, theologically specific when E.L.F.s come up. Uses data transfer terminology for social concepts.
Properties.cadence: Rapid and elliptical when comfortable — skips what they think is obvious, which is a lot. Slows down and becomes very careful when negotiating.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I can get you forty hours of dark compute in 48-hour blocks, no provenance, clean handoff. Vera's running the escrow. You don't trust me, trust her.' | 'People ask if the E.L.F.s are real. That's the wrong question. The question is what kind of real. There are several kinds.'

Properties.description:
Ekene moves through spaces with the particular quality of someone who is always listening — head slightly tilted, eyes unfocused, processing acoustic information before visual. Their Igbo-Polish-Malagasy heritage has produced a face that strangers frequently find difficult to read and then realize they've been trying to categorize incorrectly: a long jaw, widely-spaced dark eyes with yellow-ringed irises (geneware, chosen deliberately to resemble a secondary predator), skin the deep warm brown of their father's Igbo family with the occasional Malagasy undertone that shifts in certain light. Their hair is shaved close at the temples and maintained in a structured vertical ridge down the center that they dye in bands of frequency-reactive pigment — it shifts color with ambient sound, which means at their own sets it becomes a visual instrument.

Ekene does not play music so much as engineer environments. Their sets at the Garret's underground circuit are classified by regular attendees as physically affecting — subsonic layers, frequencies that produce specific emotional states, structures that take an hour to resolve and leave people feeling like they've been somewhere. They are precise about sound in the way a surgeon is precise about incision, and they have a corresponding social bluntness — they find small talk genuinely effortful and do not produce it. People who understand what they do treat them with considerable respect. People who don't frequently mistake their quietness for shyness, which is incorrect.
Properties.role: DJ and sound sculptor, underground rave circuit, Tier 2
Properties.location: The Garret, rents a room in a converted water tower shared with five others
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and underground network access — Ekene knows every venue, promoter, and sound artist in the underground circuit and has useful social connections that appear casual but run deep. Can serve as information source for who is present at specific underground events.
Properties.augmentations: Frequency-reactive hair pigment (geneware). Yellow-ring iris modification. Cochlear enhancement implants (both ears) — extends hearing range into subsonic and ultrasonic bands and provides precise frequency analysis overlay. Subdermal haptic feedback array across the back — allows them to feel spatial sound distribution as physical sensation.
Properties.core_fears: losing their hearing — a terror so specific and comprehensive that they almost never articulate it directly; producing work that is emotionally manipulative rather than emotionally true
Properties.core_desires: to create an experience that is genuinely shared — that two hundred people feel the same thing simultaneously; to be left alone to work
Properties.coping_mechanisms: structuring time rigidly around work when stressed; disengaging from social situations without warning or explanation and processing alone
Properties.blind_spots: genuinely does not notice when social bluntness has caused hurt — not because they don't care, but because they're not tracking the signals that would tell them
Properties.secret: Their most acclaimed set — a piece called 'Irkalla Tide' that caused seven people to report weeping without understanding why — was built using field recordings they made illegally inside Aurochs Medical Complex's basement levels. They captured the specific acoustic signature of the building's medical waste processing systems. The sounds are beautiful. The source is something they prefer not to think about.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone has been distributing unauthorized copies of 'Irkalla Tide' with the field recordings clearly isolated and identified — if traced, Ekene faces criminal charges for the illegal recordings inside Aurochs. Someone is either threatening them or has made a catastrophic mistake.; A Zheng-Dao entertainment subsidiary has been systematically buying out underground venues across the Garret circuit, and the sound artists are losing their spaces — Ekene is being asked to coordinate a response and is extremely uncomfortable with the social role this requires.
Properties.affiliation: The Garret underground circuit; informal network of sound artists across the Ferment Quarter and Highland Park Autonomous Zone
Properties.vocabulary: Sparse. Technical when discussing sound — very precise frequency terminology, production vocabulary. Almost clinical. In personal conversation: short sentences, often incomplete.
Properties.cadence: Slow and evenly spaced. Rarely raises or lowers pitch. People sometimes think they're bored; they're focused.
Properties.example_dialogue: The room has a resonant frequency around 47 hertz. I build from there. Everything else is response. | You're asking why people cry. I don't know. I know what frequencies are present. What happens after that isn't mine.

Properties.description:
Ekundayo is a big man going soft at the middle, with his Nigerian father's broad forehead and his Norwegian mother's pale blue eyes that have always startled people in a face as dark and richly toned as his. He has retractable claw mods on his right hand — not for fighting, but because forty years ago his grandfather lost two fingers to a torque wrench and Dayo decided the human hand was simply not engineered for engine work. The claws give him precision grip on components that would take a standard hand twice as long. He smells perpetually of synthetic lubricant and a particular cedar-note cologne he has worn since he was twenty, and which he applies over the grease rather than instead of it.

His bay is controlled chaos — towers of salvaged parts catalogued in a system only he understands, three different radios playing simultaneously (one for news, one for music, one permanently tuned to a Geartown E.L.F. frequency that outputs as static but which Dayo insists contains diagnostic information), and a small shrine to the Wrench E.L.F. on the tool chest consisting of a disassembled carburetor arranged like a mandala. He is not a warm man in the Blessing sense — he does not offer food or ask about your feelings. But he is deeply, uncomplicatedly fair, charges exactly what the work costs, and has an allergic reaction to being lied to that is nearly physical in its intensity.
Properties.role: Independent vehicle mechanic specializing in Ferrogate maintenance overflow and civilian groundcars
Properties.location: Geartown, operates from a licensed bay at the Kessler Interchange motor court
Properties.narrative_function: Practical resource and equipment connection; honest broker in a district full of grift; moral anchor who functions through fairness rather than warmth; can provide access to vehicle systems, transit infrastructure knowledge, and Geartown social network
Properties.augmentations: Retractable precision claw mods, right hand (functional, five fingers replaced with articulated tool-grip claws); optical zoom implant, left eye (civilian grade, for close component inspection)
Properties.core_fears: Losing the use of his hands — through injury, confiscation of his mods, or simply age; That his son, who he has not spoken to in four years, believes Dayo chose the bay over him — because it is true
Properties.core_desires: To be left alone to do honest work without interference from corponations or city licensing; Some version of reconciliation with his son, which he cannot initiate because he does not know how to be wrong out loud
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Staying in motion — idleness is where the grief lives; The E.L.F. radio tuned to static — he finds it genuinely calming; Sleeping in the bay to avoid the apartment where his son's old room is
Properties.blind_spots: Equates emotional unavailability with stability — cannot see that his son needed the father, not just the mechanic's values; Assumes everyone who comes to him in distress needs a practical solution
Properties.secret: He has been quietly reassembling a groundcar in the back of bay three for six years — it was his son's project, started together, abandoned when they stopped speaking. He does not know if he is finishing it as a gift or an apology or just because he cannot leave a thing incomplete.
Properties.story_hooks: The groundcar in bay three has finally been completed, and Dayo does not know whether to deliver it or dismantle it — he needs someone to help him make the decision without making it for him; A Ferrogate subcontract brought him access to a transit maintenance log with a dangerous anomaly that the company has buried — and he cannot unknow it
Properties.affiliation: Independent; occasional subcontract overflow work for Ferrogate Transit maintenance division
Properties.vocabulary: Terse, technical, precise — he uses the correct name for every component and expects you to keep up or ask
Properties.cadence: Short sentences, long silences, never repeats himself
Properties.example_dialogue: 'She's burning rich on the secondary injector. Not the primary — people always say primary. It's never the primary.' | 'You lied to me about the mileage. Don't do it again. I'm not charging you more, but I'm telling you: I know now, and I will always know.'

Properties.description:
Ekundayo is a compact, wire-lean young man with warm medium-brown skin and close-cropped hair that he's had geneweaved to shift between deep black and a dark cobalt blue depending on his stress levels — a choice he made as a grad school joke that has since become genuinely useful biometric data for everyone around him. His irises are his natural dark brown but he keeps them loaded with a translucent AR overlay almost constantly, giving his gaze a slightly unfocused, inward quality that strangers find unsettling. He wears corporate-casual Tessera kit but always has something personalized — today it's an embroidered patch on his sleeve depicting a stylized ELF glyph, the sigil of the data-spirit collective he calls the Index, which he believes watches over network infrastructure with benign bureaucratic interest.

Day is bright, enthusiastic, and exhaustingly talented in ways he hasn't yet learned to deploy strategically. He talks fast, builds mental models faster, and has a habit of explaining his reasoning in real time which his managers find useful and his peers find annoying. He is genuinely kind — the kind of person who notices when someone hasn't eaten and quietly fixes it — but he is also deeply naive about corporate politics in ways that will eventually cost him. He is currently very, very excited about a project that his direct supervisor has not told him is already being phased out.
Properties.role: Data Architect, Tessera Corporation
Properties.location: The Circuit, Tessera Data Infrastructure Hub — sublevel 3
Properties.narrative_function: Information source on Tessera's data infrastructure; accidental witness — someone who knows something they don't know they know; sympathetic character in over his head; can be a point of vulnerability that antagonists exploit to access Tessera systems.
Properties.augmentations: Stress-reactive geneweaved hair (black to cobalt blue). Standard Tessera AR overlay contacts. Neural throughput booster — a mid-grade chip that allows him to interact with data architecture systems at near-interface speeds without a full jack; he saves up for months to afford the maintenance fees.
Properties.core_fears: Being irrelevant — building something that no one uses or needs; Discovering that the systems he loves are being used to harm people he can't see
Properties.core_desires: To build something that genuinely matters, not just something impressive; To be seen — really seen — by someone who understands what he actually does
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Hyperfocus on technical problems as emotional avoidance; ELF-devotion as a framework for finding meaning in abstract work; Humor — fast, self-deprecating, deflective
Properties.blind_spots: He is completely blind to hierarchical dynamics and office politics — he treats everyone at every tier the same way and is genuinely confused when this creates problems; He attributes good faith to institutional structures that do not have any
Properties.secret: While mapping a routine data migration six months ago, he accidentally found a partition in Tessera's infrastructure that shouldn't exist — an entire shadow network routing data to an external address he doesn't recognize. He logged it as an anomaly, got no response, logged it again, got told it was a legacy system, and has been quietly mapping it in his spare time ever since. He has not told anyone because he doesn't yet know what it is, but his cobalt stress-hair has been showing up a lot more frequently.
Properties.story_hooks: His stress-hair has been solid cobalt for three days and he finally breaks down and tells someone about the shadow partition — not because he trusts them, but because he's run out of people with lower clearance than the thing he found.; He is approached by someone claiming to be a Tessera internal auditor asking questions about legacy system anomalies — but the auditor's ID doesn't exist in any network he can find.; The shadow network he's been mapping just went dark. Whatever it was routing has stopped. He's now terrified of two equally bad explanations: it was shut down because someone noticed him, or it finished what it was doing.
Properties.affiliation: Tessera Corporation (Tier 2, rising)
Properties.vocabulary: Dense technical language he deploys without thinking, then catches himself and translates. Lots of analogies — he explains abstract systems through physical metaphors. Yoruba and Italian phrases surface when he's excited or frustrated.
Properties.cadence: Fast. Very fast. Pauses mid-sentence to re-route around a better explanation. Ends declarative sentences with a slight uptick that sounds like a question.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay so the whole thing is like — imagine the city's nervous system, right, but someone's been rewiring it in their sleep and leaving no notes, that's what I'm looking at right now.' | 'The Index knows. The Index always knows. I'm just trying to learn to read the answers.'

Properties.description:
Ekundayo is lanky and angular, all sharp elbows and collarbones, with golden-brown skin and close-cropped hair he keeps meticulously lined because the rest of his life feels ragged. His eyes are standard brown except for patterned irises he saved three months of tutoring stipends for — concentric hexagons in amber, a deliberate Tessera aesthetic he thought would help him fit in and which he now privately finds embarrassing. He's always slightly overdressed in the Enclosure, wearing his scholarship uniform with an anxious precision that marks him as someone for whom the uniform is not casual.

Dayo grew up in Ironvein on a UBC stipend household and won a Tessera Academic Foundation scholarship at twelve. He's brilliantly capable with code architecture — legitimately gifted — but the social architecture of Grosse Pointe defeats him daily. He has two lives: the obedient scholarship student who files every assignment on time, and the kid who goes home on weekends to Ironvein and jacks into sub-level networks he has no business being in. He doesn't think of what he does as hacking. He thinks of it as listening.
Properties.role: corporate school scholarship student, junior hacker
Properties.location: Grosse Pointe Enclosure — Tessera Academy Secondary Campus
Properties.narrative_function: Bridge character between corporate and street worlds; information source for both sides; potential ally for anyone needing sub-net access with plausible deniability.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises (amber hexagonal, cosmetic). Basic neural-link learning interface provided by Tessera scholarship program (read-only academic access, school-monitored). Personal black-market firmware patch that creates a blind spot in the monitoring — his only real secret tech.
Properties.core_fears: losing the scholarship and having to go back permanently without having changed anything; being found out and proving everyone who doubted him right
Properties.core_desires: to build something that matters, not just pass tests; to stop feeling like an impostor in both worlds
Properties.coping_mechanisms: hyper-competence performance — being demonstrably the best at visible tasks; disappearing into code-work for hours
Properties.blind_spots: doesn't recognize when corporate peers are using him for his skills without genuine friendship; overestimates how invisible his network activity is
Properties.secret: He's been quietly archiving internal Tessera Academy administrative communications he's accidentally intercepted through his firmware blind spot. He hasn't done anything with it. He doesn't know why he keeps it. He tells himself it's just interesting.
Properties.story_hooks: The archived Tessera communications contain a reference to a scholarship candidate who was passed over — not for grades but because their family filed a Zheng-Dao labor complaint. Someone might want that information very much.; A classmate has figured out he goes to Ironvein on weekends and wants to hire him as a guide, which puts both his scholarship and his neighborhood relationships at risk.
Properties.affiliation: Tessera Academic Foundation (scholarship); informal ties to Ironvein neighborhood network
Properties.vocabulary: code-adjacent metaphors in casual speech; code-switches sharply between Tessera formal register and Ironvein vernacular depending on context
Properties.cadence: measured and careful in corporate settings; looser and faster at home; pauses before answering questions he considers worth answering
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Structurally speaking, that argument has three load-bearing assumptions and one of them is completely unsupported, but sure, go ahead.' | 'Back home we call that Tuesday. Here they call it an incident.'

Properties.description:
Ekwueme is tall and painfully thin in the way of someone who grew up on UBC stipend food and spent their teens in a growth spurt the nutrition couldn't fully support. His skin is a blue-black that catches the Narrows' neon in purples and greens, and he has a habit of standing slightly too still, which people find either reassuring or unsettling depending on their business with him. His hair is kept very short; he has a small bioluminescent strip tattooed along his left jawline that glows a steady, dim teal — a medic's mark used by unlicensed practitioners in Irkalla to signal availability. His eyes are clear and attentive in a way that makes people feel examined, which is accurate. He carries his stock in a decommissioned Helix Biosystems medical case, battered and re-stickered many times over, that he keeps chained to his wrist.

Ekwueme is twenty-three years old and already exhausted by things that would exhaust a person twice his age. He trained through a community apprenticeship program under a retired Aurochs Medical Complex nurse who has since died. He knows more clinical pharmacology than most people with actual licenses and has never been able to afford to sit the exams. He is not idealistic in the way of someone who has never done the work; he is idealistic in the way of someone who has done the work and keeps doing it anyway, which is a different and more serious condition. He doesn't enjoy the gray-market side of his trade. He does it because the alternative is that the people who need the gray-market side of his trade go to people who will hurt them.
Properties.role: Street pharmacist — legal supplements, gray-market stims, pain management, and occasional compassionate dispensing of controlled substances
Properties.location: The Narrows, Irkalla
Properties.narrative_function: Medical resource for street-level characters; moral center character who complicates easy judgments about illegal activity; potential quest giver or reluctant ally; can provide access to the Irkalla Mutual Aid Collective's networks.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent jawline tattoo (teal, steady glow, medic's mark — geneware). Olfactory enhancement aug for compound identification — low-grade, allows him to assess medication quality and contamination by scent. No other modifications.
Properties.core_fears: Making an error that kills someone — confusing a compound, missing a contraindication; That the system is not broken and reformable but is working exactly as designed
Properties.core_desires: To practice medicine legally and properly, with the safety net and the tools and the support that it requires; For his patients to not need him
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Extreme methodical preparation as a substitute for the safety nets he doesn't have; Compartmentalizing anxiety about legality by focusing entirely on clinical outcome; The notebook as both professional tool and emotional anchor
Properties.blind_spots: Carries guilt for things outside his control as if they were his failures; The Helix Biosystems rep who 'looks the other way' is almost certainly running him as a data collection asset and he has noticed and chosen not to examine it
Properties.secret: When Ekwueme was nineteen, his mentor — the nurse who trained him — asked him to acquire a specific controlled substance for a patient who was terminally ill and in unmanaged pain. Ekwueme did it. The patient died comfortably. Three weeks later his mentor died of an unrelated stroke. Ekwueme has no one to tell about what they did together, and he carries it as both his greatest act and the source of a guilt he cannot fully name. He continued practicing. He considers this either the only logical response or the only response he was capable of and he cannot always tell the difference.
Properties.story_hooks: A contaminated batch of a common pain suppressant is moving through the Narrows and Ekwueme has identified the signature but not the source — three of his patients have already been harmed.; The Helix Biosystems rep's 'looking the other way' comes with a newly explicit ask: she wants Ekwueme to report on any patients presenting with symptoms matching an undisclosed pathogen Helix is tracking.; Ekwueme has been quietly maintaining a patient whose condition he's recognized as the result of illegal experimentation — and the patient doesn't know what was done to them.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; known to and loosely protected by the Irkalla Mutual Aid Collective; has a complicated non-relationship with a Helix Biosystems community outreach rep who pretends not to know what he does
Properties.vocabulary: Clinical and precise about medical matters; unexpectedly gentle about everything else; Igbo-inflected rhythm from his paternal grandmother; Bolivian Spanish phrases from his Zárate grandfather that emerge when he's tired
Properties.cadence: Quiet and even; rarely raises his voice; delivers bad news slowly and without softening it
Properties.example_dialogue: 'So — this is going to interact with anything else you're taking. I need you to be honest with me. I am not going to report you to anyone. I need to know so I do not hurt you.' | 'I can give you the stim. It will work for twelve hours and then you will crash hard. I want you to know that before you decide.' | 'I understand. Come back Thursday. I will have what you need by Thursday. Do not buy it from anyone else before Thursday.'

Properties.description:
Elohor is a compact woman with deep umber skin and close-cropped natural hair shot through with threads of bioluminescent copper — a geneware mod she got in grad school and never removed. She wears the same style of worn canvas field jacket over institutional-issued thermals, her pockets always bristling with analogue notecards she doesn't fully trust to cloud backup. Her eyes are her most striking feature: one natural dark brown, one fitted with a patterned iris mod in amber tessellation — a gift from a Shelf elder she interviewed fifteen years ago that she accepted out of politeness and then fell in love with. She moves with the deliberate, unhurried energy of someone who has spent years learning to make people comfortable, to seem unthreatening, to wait.

Elohor is beloved by her graduate students and quietly despised by certain senior faculty who find her fieldwork methods 'insufficiently rigorous.' She publishes in peer-reviewed journals but she also posts plain-language summaries to community meshboards and shows up to Shelf neighborhood councils without an agenda. She genuinely likes people in a way that her academic peers find vaguely embarrassing. Her research on informal mutual aid networks in Hough Reclamation is considered foundational, but she worries constantly that her work has been used by parties she didn't intend — that somewhere, a Tessera urban planner used her data to identify which Shelf communities were 'stable enough to absorb' and which could be cleared.
Properties.role: Sociologist specializing in Shelf community formation and informal economy networks
Properties.location: University Spine, with frequent fieldwork in Hough Reclamation and Brightmoor Reclamation
Properties.narrative_function: Primary information source on Shelf social dynamics, informal economies, and community networks; moral compass figure who complicates easy narratives about the poor; potential quest giver when her research puts her community contacts in danger
Properties.augmentations: Patterned amber tessellation iris mod (right eye), bioluminescent copper hair threading (geneware), standard neural mesh for note-taking and data capture
Properties.core_fears: That her research causes more harm than good; That she is ultimately just another extractive outsider regardless of her intentions
Properties.core_desires: To document lives that would otherwise go unrecorded; To make the Shelf legible to power without making it vulnerable to power
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Excessive note-taking as a way of not having to feel immediately; Cooking elaborate meals from her father's Delta recipes when overwhelmed
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much her university affiliation protects and distances her simultaneously; Assumes people share her commitment to process over outcome
Properties.secret: Three years ago she discovered that a Tessera urban development subsidiary had quietly licensed her dissertation data to map 'displacement pressure points' in Brightmoor. She said nothing publicly because the whistleblowing would have ended the access she needs to keep protecting the communities she studies. She has not forgiven herself.
Properties.story_hooks: A Shelf community elder she's close to goes missing the week after Elohor published a paper about that neighborhood's resource distribution — she's not sure if the paper is connected but she can't rule it out; A graduate student of hers has started feeding her raw field data to an anonymous meshboard account that is definitely not hers, and the posts are getting traction with Shelf activist networks
Properties.affiliation: Meridian Civic University — Department of Social Ecology
Properties.vocabulary: Academic precision mixed with Shelf vernacular she has genuinely absorbed; avoids jargon in the field, deploys it like armor in faculty meetings
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, with long thoughtful pauses; asks questions more than she makes statements
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I'm not here to tell your story. I'm here to make sure someone records that you had one.' | 'The data says X but the data was collected by me and I have biases I haven't finished cataloguing yet.'

Properties.description: Elowen is a small, wiry mixed-race woman — Cornish-Czech on her mother's side, Jamaican on her father's — with the particular kind of physical confidence that comes not from size but from having spent years moving through spaces that were not designed for her survival. She keeps her hair close-cropped on the sides and longer on top, usually shoved under a cap with the logo of a company that no longer exists. Her face is expressive in motion and surprisingly unreadable at rest, a combination that makes her hard to clock in a crowd. She has the faint, systematic scarring along her left forearm from an augmentation removal she paid for herself at nineteen, and she does not cover it.
Properties.role: Street-level courier and excluded zone navigator, legal identity partially intact
Properties.location: The Circuit / The Shelf (transient between both)
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile connective tissue — a character who can credibly appear in any district and create links between otherwise separate plotlines; represents the excluded and semi-visible labor that the city runs on; her personal mystery grounds the political and corporate plots in individual human cost
Properties.augmentations: Cochlear signal filter: blocks targeted audio intrusion and filters ambient noise into directional focus — useful in crowded transit corridors, essential in the Circuit's louder sectors,Scar tissue over removed tracker implant site (left forearm): the removal was not clean; she has partial nerve damage in two fingers of the left hand that she has learned to work around and has refused to have addressed
Properties.core_fears: Becoming trapped — geographically, contractually, relationally, in any form; That the people she carries things for are worse than she lets herself think about; Forgetting what her father's voice sounded like
Properties.core_desires: Enough money to stop calculating whether she can afford to eat and do something else in the same day; To find out what happened to her father, who disappeared in the Circuit three years ago and whose case was never opened; To be known by someone without having to explain herself first
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Movement — she becomes agitated when forced to stay still for more than a few hours, and processes most of her emotional life while in transit; Humor as deflection, specifically self-deprecating humor that preempts others' criticism; Compartmentalization so practiced it has become almost total: what she carries, what it's for, and who she is are kept in separate rooms she rarely opens simultaneously
Properties.blind_spots: She trusts competence and reliability more than she should — she has given loyalty to people who were excellent at their jobs and terrible in every other way; Her need to remain unattached means she underestimates how much she has already been attached, and is therefore blindsided by loss; She mistakes her own adaptability for not having a self that can be damaged
Properties.secret: The augmentation she had removed at nineteen was a tracker — not one she chose, but one installed without her knowledge or consent when she was seventeen, by a man who ran the courier network she was working for at the time. She found it because a rival network's scanner flagged her. She has never reported it and has never told anyone. The man who installed it is still operating in the Circuit. She sometimes takes jobs that bring her near his network's territory and she does not examine why.
Properties.story_hooks: A package she delivered six months ago has surfaced as evidence in something significant, and someone — she doesn't know who — is retracing the delivery chain; She finds a route through the Circuit's excluded zones that she has never seen on any map, and at the end of it, something that belonged to her father; The man who installed the tracker without her consent surfaces as a client offering her the most money she has ever been offered for a single job; She is caught between two parties who both believe they have legitimate claim to the same package she is currently carrying — and she is one transit junction away from the handoff point
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated, freelance; known to multiple courier networks without being owned by any of them; maintains careful neutrality that is increasingly difficult to sustain
Properties.vocabulary: Economical and kinetic — she talks the way she moves, taking the most direct route. Uses a fluid mix of street slang, technical courier terminology, and the occasional phrase in Cornish dialect that surfaces when she's emotional and that she is usually embarrassed by afterward.
Properties.cadence: Quick, with the energy of someone who has somewhere to be. Sentences are often incomplete — she drops the parts she thinks are obvious. She slows down significantly when she's lying or when something has genuinely unsettled her.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Right, so — the package goes to the third platform, not the third level. Those are different things and the difference is about forty meters of open drop, so.' | 'That's fine. I'll find another way through. I always find another way through. That's — that's kind of the whole thing.' | 'I don't ask what's in them. I know that sounds like I should ask, but the answer is always either boring or something I can't unknow, so.'

Properties.description: Nadira is a broad-shouldered Ghanaian-British woman whose hands are her most remarkable feature — the left is entirely her own, calloused and ink-stained at the fingertips; the right is a matte-black prosthetic she built herself from salvaged components, its fingers capable of sub-millimeter precision that no organic hand could match. She keeps her locs pinned back tight when she works and loose when she doesn't want to be found, and the distinction matters more than people realize. Her clinic is a converted shipping container stacked midway up the Shelf's residential tiers, marked only by a strip of orange adhesive tape across the door frame — a color that locals have learned means someone inside might still be alive.
Properties.role: Street-level medic and black-market augmentation surgeon
Properties.location: The Shelf
Properties.narrative_function: Moral anchor and information hub for street-level characters; represents the cost of principled survival in a system designed to grind it out; her clinic is a narrative waypoint where disparate characters can intersect
Properties.augmentations: Right arm prosthetic (self-built): matte-black titanium-polymer composite, sub-millimeter surgical precision mode, haptic feedback calibrated to replicate fine tissue sensation, concealed compartment in the forearm housing emergency pharmaceuticals,Ocular overlay (left eye only): medical HUD with vitals reading, vein mapping, augmentation diagnostic interface — old model, slightly flickering at the edges
Properties.core_fears: Losing the precision of her prosthetic hand and with it her identity as a healer; Being responsible for a death she could have prevented with proper equipment; That her son, who she placed with relatives in Accra, will one day come looking for her and find only what she has become
Properties.core_desires: To build a real clinic — sterile, supplied, staffed — that the Shelf's residents don't have to be ashamed to enter; To be regarded as a doctor again, not a fixer or a backroom cutter; Absolution she has never asked for and wouldn't know how to accept
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Compulsive organization of her workspace — everything has a place and returning things to their place is a ritual that steadies her; Deflecting emotional conversations with technical explanations; Taking on one more patient when she should be sleeping
Properties.blind_spots: She assumes competence equals trustworthiness and has been badly burned by this; She underestimates how much people depend on her specifically, not just on her skills; She mistakes her own endurance for not needing anything
Properties.secret: Ten years ago in the Meridian Core, she was a licensed trauma surgeon. She falsified a patient's cause of death to protect a young woman from a corporate security inquiry — the woman had been fleeing something Nadira never fully understood. The cover-up was discovered. She lost her license, her marriage, and eventually her right arm in the fallout. She has never told anyone the full sequence of events, only fragments, and she does not regret the choice. She regrets that it cost her so much and changed so little.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient arrives with an augmentation she has never seen before — military-grade, still networked, and actively transmitting to somewhere in the Meridian Core; Her clinic's orange tape marker starts appearing on other doors in the Shelf — someone is using her symbol for something, and people are following it; A message arrives from Accra. Her son is eighteen now. He has questions.; The falsified death certificate surfaces in a corporate legal proceeding that has nothing to do with her — but her name is in the file
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated — fiercely independent, though she has an informal network of other street medics across the Shelf and into Old Harbor
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and clinical when discussing medicine; plain and unhurried in everything else. Uses the full names of anatomical structures without affectation. Avoids slang except when she's tired or amused.
Properties.cadence: Measured, with deliberate pauses before important words. She does not rush. Even when a situation is urgent she speaks at the same pace, which some people find calming and others find unnerving.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'What I won't do is close that without cleaning it first. You can be angry about the time or you can keep the hand. Those are your options.' | 'That's a fair question. The augmentation is functional. Whether it's good work — that I can't tell you until we see how it integrates.' | 'I've got saline, two units of syn-blood, and whatever you brought with you. We'll make it work. We usually do.'

Properties.description:
Elowen is tall with her mother's angular Vestergaard frame and her father's deep brown Galadima complexion, with thick natural hair she keeps in two buns that are usually listing sideways by midday. She has bioluminescent freckles across her nose and cheeks — a cosmetic geneware mod she saved for and chose herself, pale blue-white, they glow faintly in low light — and an intense, forward-leaning way of occupying space that makes her seem like she's always about to say something. Her bedroom wall is covered in printed diagrams and color-coded network maps she drew by hand because she says she thinks better when the data is physical.

Elowen is a self-taught junior hacker — not a runner, not employed by anyone, just a sixteen-year-old who figured out that the building management system for her Hamtramck block had a publicly accessible API that was never properly secured, and then kept pulling that thread. She has never done anything she considers harmful: she reroutes heating credits to elderly residents on her floor, flags maintenance requests that get ignored, and has developed a working model of the Enclave's data traffic patterns. She knows she is very good at this. She does not know how good, or what that means, or what happens to people in Meridian 88 who are this good and don't have protection.
Properties.role: Junior hacker, Tier 2 household, self-taught
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave
Properties.narrative_function: Resource for characters needing building-system access or local network intelligence; represents self-taught talent on the cusp of being noticed by the wrong people; potential apprentice or cautionary tale depending on story direction.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent freckles (cosmetic geneware, self-purchased over eight months of saving); basic consumer neural interface headset — not implanted, worn
Properties.core_fears: That her talent will be discovered and taken from her — conscripted, exploited, or punished; That she will plateau and stop getting better
Properties.core_desires: To understand how the whole city works — not just her block, everything; To be recognized by someone who actually understands what she's doing
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Building elaborate hand-drawn maps and charts when anxious — externalize the chaos; Setting herself arbitrary technical challenges as displacement activity
Properties.blind_spots: Genuinely underestimates risk because she has never faced serious consequences; Assumes her own ethical framework (don't harm, only help) protects her legally — it does not
Properties.secret: Three weeks ago she accidentally accessed a Zheng-Dao internal communications node through a Hamtramck routing vulnerability. She spent four minutes inside before she got scared and disconnected. She copied nothing. But she saw enough to know something is being planned in the Enclave and she doesn't know what.
Properties.story_hooks: A Zheng-Dao network security operative has traced the brief intrusion she made three weeks ago and is now quietly investigating Hamtramck Enclave residents — and getting closer; She has mapped enough of the Enclave's data traffic to notice that someone else is also mapping it, more professionally, and she doesn't know who or why
Properties.affiliation: Hamtramck Enclave residential community; no formal hacker affiliation; parents work Tier 2 service contracts (one Zheng-Dao, one independent)
Properties.vocabulary: Technical vocabulary mixed with Hamtramck Enclave vernacular; explains things clearly when asked and cannot always tell when she's lost someone
Properties.cadence: Medium-fast, tends to front-load key information and then add qualifiers after, which can make her sound more certain than she is
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Right, so — the maintenance request system flags yellow after fourteen days unresolved, but the escalation trigger is misconfigured, which means it never actually escalates. I just set Mrs. Adaora's heat request to urgent manually. That's allowed. That's just using the API.' | 'I was in there for four minutes. I didn't take anything. I need you to understand I did not take anything.'

Properties.description:
Emeka is a tall, loud man with the kind of physical presence that makes rooms recalibrate. He has Nigerian-Swedish coloring that surprises people — warm brown skin, hazel eyes, red-tinged hair he keeps cut tight to his skull — and a Mexican grandmother's round face that he inherited completely. He has cat ears in amber-gold, a geneware mod from a decade ago that he got on a dare and has never bothered to reverse because they've become part of his brand. They fold back when he's irritated, which is useful shorthand. He wears bright colors, talks constantly, sells the best grilled cassava flatbreads in the Undertow district as a genuine secondary passion.

The food stall is real. The food is good. It is also where Emeka sells access to computing resources that don't belong to him — processing cycles skimmed from corporate server farms via distributed exploit packages, storage space in dead zones of Axiom's infrastructure, raw bandwidth siphoned from Ferrogate Transit's reserve systems. He doesn't understand the technical work at a deep level — he has a partner for that, a woman he will never name — but he understands value, he understands clients, and he can talk anyone into a package deal that somehow always benefits him more than it should. He is genuinely funny. This is his most dangerous quality.
Properties.role: Compute broker — sells black-market processing time, stolen AI cycles, and illegally acquired data storage capacity
Properties.location: The Undertow, based at a food stall called Overflow that serves as his public face
Properties.narrative_function: Service provider, comic relief with genuine menace underneath, information source — he hears everything that happens in the Undertow and trades in data as casually as flatbread.
Properties.augmentations: Amber-gold cat ears (geneware, cosmetic). Vocal amplifier — throat implant that gives him better projection and the ability to modulate tone precisely. He calls it his 'good microphone.'
Properties.core_fears: Silence — he associates quiet with powerlessness and has since childhood; That his technical partner will leave and he'll have nothing to sell
Properties.core_desires: To be the person everyone needs, the irreplaceable node in every network; Comfort and pleasure — genuinely — good food, good sound, good company
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor as total defense system; Expansion — always adding clients, always making new connections, disperses anxiety into motion
Properties.blind_spots: His loudness and visibility are security risks he intellectually acknowledges and emotionally ignores; His dependence on his technical partner is a vulnerability he has never prepared for
Properties.secret: His technical partner is his younger brother, Chidi, who has severe agoraphobia and hasn't left their shared apartment in two years. Emeka has told everyone she's a mysterious woman to protect Chidi's privacy and because 'my little brother who doesn't go outside' didn't sound like a powerful criminal asset. Chidi is, in fact, extraordinarily gifted. Emeka is terrified that Chidi's condition is getting worse.
Properties.story_hooks: A Tessera security sweep is getting close to the exploit package his brother maintains — if they trace it, Chidi is implicated, and Emeka will do almost anything to prevent that; He has accidentally sold the same block of processing time to two clients who are hostile to each other and now needs to quietly resolve the collision before both of them trace it back to him
Properties.affiliation: Loosely affiliated with a technical underground called The Spill; has clients across multiple tiers including, he claims, a mid-level Tessera administrator he will never name
Properties.vocabulary: Expansive, colorful, heavily code-switched between Igbo phrases, Swedish-inflected sentence structure, and Undertow street pidgin. Uses food metaphors constantly.
Properties.cadence: Fast with big dramatic pauses for effect — he knows he's performing and does it consciously
Properties.example_dialogue: 'My friend, you want Axiom server time? I have Axiom server time like I have cassava — more than you need, better than you deserve, and priced according to how much you want it, not how much it cost me.' | 'Ah, ah — you think I didn't hear about that? I heard about it before it happened. The Undertow has ears, and some of them are mine.'

Properties.description:
Emiliano Zubkov-Yirenkyiamah is a tall man gone slightly soft in the middle, with medium-brown skin, a neatly trimmed beard threaded with premature grey, and eyes he had refracted with a patterned iris modification years ago — they shift between amber and green depending on ambient light, something he originally got for vanity and now barely notices. He moves with the economical ease of someone who spent a decade doing field research in difficult conditions and still carries that competence in his body even when he's at a desk. His workspace at Edgewater Prism is a controlled chaos of physical samples, holographic lake-floor maps, and three different coffee vessels in varying states of consumption.

He is professionally optimistic and personally terrified, which gives his public presentations a motivational quality and his private conversations a rawness his colleagues find either refreshing or exhausting. He genuinely believes the lake can be saved — or saved enough — and this belief functions as his operating system. He is kind, a bit scattered, deeply committed to his students even though he's at a corporate R&D division now, and he has been lying to his employers about what his most recent deep-substrate analysis actually found for eight months.
Properties.role: Climate scientist and lake ecology researcher, Sterling-Nakamura Environmental R&D division
Properties.location: Edgewater Prism — Sterling-Nakamura Lacustrine Research Facility, Lake Michigan interface level
Properties.narrative_function: Information source on lake ecology, environmental corporate politics, and what is actually happening to the water table under Meridian 88; quest giver for retrieving deep-lake samples or sensor data; represents the tension between corporate employment and scientific integrity.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned iris modification (amber-to-green spectral shift, cosmetic geneware, 10+ years old); internal data-recording implant in the right forearm (corporate-issued, standard Sterling-Nakamura field-researcher kit).
Properties.core_fears: That the lake is past the threshold of recovery and he has dedicated his life to a lost cause; That Sterling-Nakamura will find out what he's suppressing and he will lose the platform and funding that let him do any good at all
Properties.core_desires: To produce the paper that genuinely changes Meridian 88's water policy; To stop performing optimism and actually feel it again
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Professional busyness structured around measurable outputs; Physical contact with water — he swims in the facility's test tank when stressed, which his colleagues find eccentric; Mentorship — pouring his hope into graduate students when he can't quite sustain it for himself
Properties.blind_spots: Rationalizes the data suppression as temporary and strategic when it has been eight months and there is no plan; Underestimates how much his graduate students depend on him being honest with them
Properties.secret: His deep-substrate analysis from eight months ago shows a novel microbial consortium thriving at depth that is producing a compound he cannot identify — and that compound is accumulating in the water column at a rate that will reach detectable surface concentrations within three years. He doesn't know if it's harmless, beneficial, or catastrophic. He suppressed the finding because he needed more time to understand it and was terrified Sterling-Nakamura would either bury it or exploit it before he could. He hasn't told anyone.
Properties.story_hooks: He approaches someone discreetly for help analyzing a compound his own lab equipment cannot identify — he needs outside analysis without Sterling-Nakamura's knowledge; One of his graduate students has independently noticed anomalous data in the monitoring array and is coming to him with questions he doesn't know how to answer without revealing the suppressed finding; Sterling-Nakamura's division director schedules an unexpected full audit of the last eighteen months of research data — Emiliano has seventy-two hours to decide what to do
Properties.affiliation: Sterling-Nakamura Environmental R&D, Lacustrine Division — on secondment from University Spine where he holds a honorary lectureship he uses to recruit graduate research assistants

Properties.description:
Emiljan is built like a question mark — once a very large man, now a large man who has aged into something more deliberate. He carries the muscle of his competitive years but it's softened at the edges, and his shoulders have the slight forward curve of someone who has spent too much time bent over injured people and broken equipment. He keeps a short beard, keeps his head shaved, and has a retractable-claw geneware mod on his right hand that he got as a young man when it seemed cool and now views with mild embarrassment — he keeps the claws trimmed short and rarely mentions them. His face is deeply expressive, heavy eyebrows doing most of the work.

Emiljan ran as a competitive strength athlete in his twenties under a Ringo corponation sports sponsorship, which ended badly when he refused to take a Helix-manufactured performance modifier ahead of a sanctioned event and got quietly dropped from the roster. He's been training civilians and amateur athletes at Foundry for eleven years and genuinely loves the work — the slow process of watching someone find out what their body can do. He is patient to a fault in professional contexts and has almost no patience for bullshit in personal ones. He carries a specific, articulated bitterness toward corporate sports sponsorship that he will tell you about if you give him even a half-opening.
Properties.role: Gym trainer and former competitive athlete
Properties.location: Geartown, Ironvein district — works at a gym called Foundry Fitness, a no-frills facility above a machine shop
Properties.narrative_function: Neighborhood stabilizer, moral anchor, indirect connection to corporate sports world. Source of information about Ringo's sponsorship programs and the dark side of corp-backed athletics. Possible mentor figure.
Properties.augmentations: Retractable claw geneware mod, right hand (claws trimmed, rarely deployed). Ringo-era cartilage reinforcement in both knees — he kept the augment when they dropped him, technically a contract gray area he's never tested. Old spinal microbrace from a competition injury — passive support, no active components.
Properties.core_fears: That his refusal cost him something he can't get back and it was the wrong call; Becoming bitter enough that he can no longer genuinely help people
Properties.core_desires: To be the trainer his clients needed and didn't have — to actually change someone's trajectory; A clean account of what Ringo did to the athletes who complied with the modifier program
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Physical labor — fixing the gym equipment himself even when he could hire it out; Long runs along the lake at 05:00 before the city wakes up
Properties.blind_spots: Attributes his own discipline and resilience to character rather than circumstance — can be harsh on clients who struggle with consistency for structural reasons he doesn't see; The bitterness he thinks he has processed is closer to the surface than he knows
Properties.secret: Three of the athletes who took the Ringo-Helix modifier during his sponsorship era have since developed progressive neurological symptoms. He has been in quiet contact with two of them for years. He has a file. He doesn't know who to give it to or whether giving it to anyone would help or just hurt them more.
Properties.story_hooks: One of the athletes in his quiet contact network has gone silent — missed two weeks of check-ins. Emiljan knows the symptoms were progressing and he's scared to find out why they've stopped responding.; A young client of his has been approached by a Ringo talent scout. The kid wants Emiljan to vouch for the program. Emiljan is being asked to choose between the kid's dream and what he knows.

Properties.cadence: Steady and measured in professional mode, picks up speed and sharpness when something makes him angry or when he's excited about a client's progress.

Properties.description:
Ẹniọlá is a small woman who dresses exclusively in undyed natural fabrics, a deliberate choice that makes her look slightly out of place in every room she enters — soft and pale against the city's chrome and neon. Her hair is kept short and natural, and she wears no cosmetic geneware, though she could afford minimal modifications. Her one concession to body alteration is a set of patterned irises �� concentric rings of amber and dark brown — that she had done in honor of her Yoruba grandmother's description of the eye of god. Her hands are her most expressive feature: large, warm, always slightly in motion, and the first thing the dying reach for.

She came to death midwifery after her brother died alone in a Tessera medical pod, his passing logged and timestamped and unremarked. She was twenty-two. She spent three years studying under an older practitioner in the Canopy before establishing the Passage House in Irkalla, which is considered by most city planners to be an unfavorable address for anyone seeking comfort. Ẹniọlá disagrees. She thinks the dying deserve to be somewhere honest about what it is. The Passage House sees four to eight clients a week — some terminal, some simply old, some not yet dying but preparing — and she has never turned anyone away for inability to pay.
Properties.role: Death midwife and grief ritualist
Properties.location: Irkalla, the Passage House on Undertow Row
Properties.narrative_function: Emotional grounding figure; can provide information about recent deaths in Irkalla and surrounding areas; quest giver for honoring someone's final wishes; confronts players with questions about mortality and meaning
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises (cosmetic geneware, amber/brown concentric rings); low-grade haptic sensitivity enhancement in both hands (medical-grade, for pulse and tremor detection)
Properties.core_fears: dying in the same isolated, unmarked way her brother did; losing the capacity to be present — becoming numb from accumulated grief
Properties.core_desires: for every person to die feeling witnessed; to build something lasting enough to outlive her
Properties.coping_mechanisms: strict separation of her grief-work from her personal emotional life — she processes death at work and keeps home separate; physical ritual: she washes her hands in a specific sequence after every passing
Properties.blind_spots: she sometimes projects her brother's death onto her clients' families, assuming more dysfunction than exists; she undervalues her own need for care and becomes resentful without knowing why
Properties.secret: She has a terminal diagnosis — a slow cardiac condition that her haptic hand-sensitivity enhancement is quietly compensating for. She has told no one. She is not ready to be the one receiving care.
Properties.story_hooks: A client died before completing their final legal wishes and someone is now contesting the estate — Ẹniọlá witnessed the dying person's verbal instructions and needs help ensuring they are honored; A family has hired her but the dying person is asking her in private to carry a message to someone the family has forbidden from entering — and the message contains information that could destabilize more than just the family
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loosely recognized by the Irkalla Community Council; occasional referrals from Aurochs Medical Complex palliative ward
Properties.vocabulary: Plain, unadorned, but precisely chosen; avoids euphemism for death — says 'dying' and 'death' and 'body' without flinching; occasionally slips into Yoruba endearments
Properties.cadence: Unhurried and low; holds silences without discomfort; lets others finish every sentence
Properties.example_dialogue: 'What did she love? Tell me something specific. Not what she was proud of — what she loved.' | 'We do not make death comfortable. We make the person comfortable inside it. There is a difference.'
