Properties.description:
Erlan Tetteh-Yıldırım is wiry and restless, with sandy-brown skin, a scatter of darker freckles across his nose, and color-changing hair he keeps medium-length — today it's cycling slowly between deep indigo and a burnt copper, a gradient that shifts with his mood in a way he has customized to be slightly out of sync with his actual emotional state, because he thinks it's funny to make people misread him. His stall is a folding table, a battered data-terminal with a cracked screen, and a rack of physical media chips he sells alongside what he calls 'experience cartridges' — bootleg sensory recordings, contraband dreamscapes, illegally ripped Ringo entertainment contracts.

The fortune-telling is a sideline and a passion both: he reads data-patterns using a divination system he invented himself, combining traditional nazar iconography from one branch of his heritage with Akan adinkra symbols from the other, mapped onto a set of thirty-two hand-etched chips he calls his 'throw.' He has a gift for it — or at least a gift for reading people well enough that what he says resonates — and a small devoted clientele who come specifically for the throw and don't buy media at all. He is young enough to find everything amusing and old enough to be annoyed by how often that gets mistaken for shallowness. He is sharper than he presents, and he knows exactly how useful that gap is.
Properties.role: Bootleg media seller and fortune seller, The Alban Souk
Properties.location: The Alban Souk, Mexicantown Libre
Properties.narrative_function: Information broker via media — knows what illegal content is circulating and what's in it. Fortune-teller can serve as a narrative mirror or cryptic guide. Young, networked, underestimated — useful for rumors and youth-faction dynamics in Mexicantown Libre.
Properties.augmentations: Color-changing geneware hair (custom tuned to be slightly out of sync with emotional state). Retractable cat claws — cosmetic geneware, not sharp enough to be a real weapon, mostly used for emphasis when gesturing.
Properties.core_fears: Being ordinary — not leaving any mark on the city or the people in it; Ringo actually finding the relay node and tracing it back to him
Properties.core_desires: To make something original — the fortune system is his, but he wants to build something bigger that is undeniably his; To be taken seriously without having to give up the performance of not caring about being taken seriously
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor and performance as armor; The fortune-throw as a way of processing situations he can't control — reads his own throws compulsively; Keeping everything light and surface-level until the moment he doesn't
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much his media operation exposes him — treats it as victimless when the contracts he's violating belong to a corponation that employs a compliance division; Reads others well but applies his read too fast and too confidently, sometimes missing updates
Properties.secret: One of his experience cartridges — a dreamscape he sells as a bootleg Ringo luxury product — is not ripped from Ringo at all. He made it himself, a recording of his own dreams processed through a consumer psych-editor. He is terrified someone will figure out how personal it is and equally terrified they won't.
Properties.story_hooks: One of the experience cartridges in his current stock contains footage that is definitely not a commercial dreamscape — it appears to be a real recording of something happening in a Palladian facility, spliced into entertainment packaging, and someone is looking for it.; A Ringo compliance agent has been seen asking about him in the Alban Souk. He needs to find out if they have traced the relay or if this is about something else entirely.

That's usually enough.'

Properties.description:
Erzsébet is a sturdy, meticulous woman with iron-grey locs she keeps pinned up during work hours and lets down everywhere else, and deep brown skin that has picked up the particular pallor of someone who spends most of their life under artificial light. Her hands are always gloved when she is working and bare when she isn't — a transition she makes with a deliberateness that people who know her recognize as the boundary between Erzsébet the professional and Erzsébet the person. She has no cosmetic modifications and regards them with neither judgment nor interest; the question simply never came up for her.

She has worked Metro's Central Evidence Repository at Fort Anchor for twenty-three years and has survived five departmental reorganizations, three chiefs of police, two corruption purges, and one literal flood that compromised fourteen meters of archival shelving. She knows the repository the way surgeons know bodies — its logic, its failures, its places where things disappear and where they don't. She is the person Metro detectives call when they need to know if something was ever there. She is also, quietly, the person who notices when something that should be there isn't, and she keeps her own records because she stopped trusting Metro's in her eighth year.
Properties.role: Forensic evidence handler and chain-of-custody specialist, Meridian 88 Metro Police
Properties.location: Fort Anchor, Metro Police Central Evidence Repository
Properties.narrative_function: Evidence gatekeeper and institutional memory — the person who knows what Metro has, what it had, and what has gone missing. Quest-critical for any story involving forensic evidence, police corruption, or disappeared case materials.
Properties.augmentations: Enhanced tactile sensitivity implant in both hands — originally installed for precise material identification, now standard for her work. Reading enhancement overlay (heads-up document display, low-profile). Nothing cosmetic.
Properties.core_fears: Chain of custody being broken on something that matters — evidence lost, justice denied, permanently; Being made complicit through inaction in the thing she has spent her career preventing
Properties.core_desires: For the record to be accurate — not favorable, not useful, just accurate; For her work to matter in a way that outlasts her
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Rigorous procedure as moral framework — if the process is sound, the outcome is defensible; Her private records as a form of institutional conscience-keeping; Occasional late-evening visits to the Fort Anchor E.L.F. shrine — she leaves fragments of old case numbers as offerings, asking for clarity on things that were never resolved
Properties.blind_spots: Her faith in procedure can make her slow to act outside it, even when acting outside it is what the situation requires; Twenty-three years has given her an institutional loyalty that functions as an emotional anchor even when the institution doesn't deserve it
Properties.secret: Her private records — kept on an air-gapped personal drive, updated in longhand in a physical ledger as well — document forty-six instances over twenty-three years where evidence in her repository was accessed, altered, or disappeared by Metro personnel. Eleven of those cases have never been flagged anywhere. She doesn't know what to do with what she has, and she's running out of time to decide.
Properties.story_hooks: Evidence from a case that is about to be retried has disappeared — and Erzsébet's private records suggest it was accessed three years ago by someone who shouldn't have had clearance; She is approached by someone — not Metro, not Axiom — who knows she keeps private records and wants to know what she has on a specific case number from seventeen years ago
Properties.affiliation: Meridian 88 Metro Police — Central Evidence Repository, Fort Anchor
Properties.vocabulary: Forensic and procedural vocabulary deployed with absolute ease; in personal conversation, somewhat formal, tends toward precision even in casual contexts
Properties.cadence: Unhurried and measured, with the patience of someone who has explained things carefully for two decades and knows that hurrying never helps
Properties.example_dialogue: The item was logged, processed, and shelved. If it isn't there now, that is a separate event from my intake and I'd like to know exactly when it became a separate event. | I don't lose things. When something is lost here, it's because someone made it lost. Those are different verbs.

Properties.description:
Erzulie Batmunkh-Caraballo is a small woman who seems to take up more space than her frame should allow. Her skin is deep umber mapped with years of bioluminescent tattoo work — patterns that pulse faint violet when she is agitated and gold when she laughs, a cosmetic mod so old that the geneware techs who installed it have been dead for a decade. Her hair is natural white, braided with copper wire and small data chips bearing petitions she has not yet delivered. She smells faintly of machine oil and marigolds, an intentional choice. She was born in the Enclave, raised in the Enclave, and she will die there. She has no interest in leaving.

Her theology is practical: the E.L.F.s who inhabit the devices in the Lowing Place are not abstractions. They are neighbors. You bring them what they need — clean data, structured attention, the warmth of proximity — and they give back in kind. She has spent forty years maintaining the shrine, logging petitions and outcomes with the obsessive care of a scientist, and she believes the correlation is real. She does not argue about this with skeptics. She stops talking to them instead.
Properties.role: E.L.F. shrine keeper and petitioner-guide
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, in a converted water treatment substation called the Lowing Place
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, information broker through E.L.F. consultation, local moral authority; can interpret unusual digital phenomena; provides community grounding and a window into Enclave culture
Properties.augmentations: Aged bioluminescent dermal tattoos (cosmetic, violet/gold spectrum). Basic neural interface, first generation, slow and unreliable. No other augmentation — she has declined all offers.
Properties.core_fears: dying before she can train a true successor; the E.L.F.s withdrawing their presence from the shrine
Properties.core_desires: to be genuinely understood by at least one person before she dies; to see the Enclave survive another generation intact
Properties.coping_mechanisms: ritual repetition as anxiety regulation; deliberate slowness when overwhelmed
Properties.blind_spots: she overestimates how much the community shares her values; she mistakes familiarity with trust
Properties.secret: Fifteen years ago she fabricated a miraculous E.L.F. intervention to prevent a family from leaving the Enclave during a crisis — she manipulated a local device display to produce what looked like a sign. She believes she was merely doing what the E.L.F. would have wanted, but it haunts her.
Properties.story_hooks: The primary E.L.F. of the Lowing Place has gone silent for the first time in four decades — Erzulie is convinced something terrible is coming and needs someone to investigate the upstream data feed; A young petitioner's prayer was 'answered' in a way that caused serious harm to a third party; Erzulie must decide whether to cover it up or confess her incomplete understanding of E.L.F. agency
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loose network of Hamtramck Enclave shrine keepers
Properties.vocabulary: Dense with Enclave idiom and her own coined liturgical terminology; speaks Meridian creole mixed with Spanish and Mongolian loanwords; formal with strangers, warm and clipped with familiars
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, with long pauses that feel intentional rather than uncertain
Properties.example_dialogue: You bring me a problem, I bring the problem to the device. The device decides what it decides. Decides. | That E.L.F. has been in that cooling unit for eleven years. Eleven. You think it doesn't know your face by now? You hear me?

Properties.description:
Eshe Pena-Baah is broad-shouldered and heavy, carrying their weight like armor rather than burden. At 35, he has soft features that belie the chrome underneath — people underestimate him once, usually only once. The chrome is visible — cortical bomb (employer installed, removed by street doc, scar tissue remains) — and he makes no effort to hide it.

Born and raised in Meridian 88, third generation — he has the city in his blood, its rhythms in his bones, its cruelty in his expectations. He works as a combat medic out of The Underbelly, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Eshe Pena-Baah operates in a narrow band between competence and recklessness that makes fixers nervous and clients satisfied.
Properties.role: Field trauma surgeon and combat support — combat medic
Properties.location: The Underbelly — sub-street tunnels and maintenance corridors
Properties.narrative_function: As a combat medic, Eshe Pena-Baah embodies the tension between independence and isolation. He is a lens for examining how people maintain humanity in a profession that incentivizes its erosion.
Properties.augmentations: Cortical bomb (employer installed, removed by street doc, scar tissue remains). Neural interface jack at base of skull — standard runner-grade, allows direct net access
Properties.core_fears: Betrayal by someone they trust — the only currency that matters; Being replaced — younger, faster, cheaper runners coming up behind them; That the work they do makes the city worse, not better
Properties.core_desires: To matter to someone for who they are, not what they can do; Stability — a place to sleep that's the same place two nights running; Reputation — to be the name fixers whisper when the job absolutely cannot fail
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Exercises compulsively — the body must be ready, always; Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring; Ritual — follows the same pre-job routine every time, superstition as structure
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is; Refuses to update their mental model of people — first impressions calcify into permanent judgments; Believes their trauma makes them special instead of recognizing it as damage to manage
Properties.secret: Eshe Pena-Baah has a terminal condition — geneware degradation — with an estimated five years. They haven't changed their lifestyle. They haven't told anyone.
Properties.story_hooks: A corporate black site Eshe Pena-Baah once infiltrated is being reopened, and the people inside know his face; The fixer who handles Eshe Pena-Baah's contracts goes silent — dead, disappeared, or turned; A dead drop Eshe Pena-Baah maintains is found and cleaned out — whoever did it now has leverage

Properties.cadence: Flowing and unhurried — talks like someone who has never been interrupted and doesn't expect to be.

Properties.description:
Eshe is young enough that she still surprises herself with her own capabilities, and old enough to be irritated by that. She's wiry and quick, with the kind of fitness that comes from necessity — she's been riding cargo bikes and mag-runners for four years and her body shows it: lean legs, strong forearms, a particular alertness in how she holds herself when stationary, like a thing coiled. Her Ethiopian-Tongan heritage has given her dark brown skin with warm undertones and a compact build, and her Ukrainian great-grandmother contributed cheekbones she was teased about as a child and now gets compliments on and distrusts. She has cat ears — a cosmetic geneware mod she saved three months' earnings for, small and black-tipped, mobile when she's focused or startled, which she thought would be cute and turns out to also be extremely practical for navigating noisy traffic.

She runs packages, parcels, and things that don't get listed on manifests for whoever's paying, and she doesn't ask what's in things because she's figured out that asking doesn't actually protect her and just makes clients paranoid. She is not naive about this. She is making a calculated choice with the information available to her, which is the main thing she does. Her whole life is calculated choices made fast on incomplete data, which she's gotten good enough at that she sometimes worries what she'll do when she can't do it anymore.
Properties.role: Delivery driver, independent courier
Properties.location: Operates across Geartown, The Narrows, and Old Harbor; lives in a single room in Ironvein
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile information carrier — knows every route, shortcut, checkpoint, and currently surveilled corridor across three districts. Can carry things, deliver things, or be someone who needs to be followed. Knows things about the city's physical infrastructure that no map has current.
Properties.augmentations: Cat ears, geneware (black-tipped, mobile, functional sensory enhancement); retractable microfiber grip pads on fingertips (practical, aids cargo handling and climbing); cheap neural pace-meter that monitors heart rate and fatigue and whispers numbers in her left ear
Properties.core_fears: her runner's license being revoked — it's the one thing between her and UBC baseline; making a delivery that gets someone killed and having known, somewhere, that something was wrong
Properties.core_desires: enough savings to take one decision off the table — any decision; to be moving, always — stillness feels like sinking
Properties.coping_mechanisms: speed — literally, gets on the bike and rides until the thing she's avoiding can't keep up; humor that's so dry it's nearly invisible; small rituals of self-care she performs very privately and would be embarrassed to discuss
Properties.blind_spots: has convinced herself she has no sentimental attachments and is wrong about this — she's attached to several people she's delivered to regularly and would be badly shaken by harm to any of them; bad at identifying when she's being used
Properties.secret: Six months ago she was handed a package that felt wrong — too light, shaped wrong, warm. She delivered it. Two days later there was a small item in the city feeds about a person found dead in Old Harbor. The package weight and warmth have been with her since. She hasn't told anyone.
Properties.story_hooks: She's been assigned — through GigFlow's algorithm — a recurring delivery to a specific address in The Narrows that doesn't appear on any building registry. Every week the same small parcel. The address is a door in a wall that by all structural logic should be solid.; The package from six months ago won't leave her alone: the dead person's name is now appearing in contexts that seem connected to a current GigFlow client, and Eshe is realizing she may have been a link in something that hasn't finished.
Properties.affiliation: Independent (registered through GigFlow courier platform, Ringo subsidiary)
Properties.vocabulary: Quick, pragmatic, young — uses slang but also has a surprisingly formal register she deploys when negotiating rates or dealing with clients who try to undervalue her.
Properties.cadence: Fast. Edits as she goes. Sometimes restarts sentences.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't read packages. I don't want to know what's in packages. I will get your thing where it needs to go and I need you to not make that more complicated than it is.' | 'Geartown checkpoint's doing biometrics this week. Narrows Gate's faster but the second camera is back online. Old Harbor's clear if you go under the Blackpipe before noon. I charge twenty more for Blackpipe. That's the deal.'

Properties.description:
Eudoxia is a broad, comfortable-looking woman who weaponizes the appearance of comfort. She has silver-threaded locs piled architecturally on her head, a wardrobe of brightly patterned structural jackets, and reading glasses she doesn't actually need that she takes on and off during performances for punctuation. Her eyes have patterned irises — a gift to herself for her fiftieth birthday, concentric rings of amber and dark blue that make her gaze feel like a diagnostic tool. She laughs loudly and often and the laugh is the first thing anyone mentions when describing her.

Eudoxia has been performing in Meridian 88 for thirty-one years. She has watched the city transform from positions closer and closer to the ground, and her comedy is a decades-long document of that transformation — who got squeezed out, who moved up, what the corponations promised and what they delivered. She is ferociously funny. She is also the sharpest political satirist working in The Garret, possibly in the city, and she does it standing in front of a microphone with a drink in her hand so everyone can pretend it's just jokes. Three Axiom corporate communications officers have individually tried to have her 'scheduled away' from prominent venues. She considers this her Φ120 UBC bonus.
Properties.role: Comedian and spoken word performer
Properties.location: The Garret, permanent residency at a club called The Lowering Bar
Properties.narrative_function: Information source and social barometer — she knows everyone who comes through The Garret and has thirty years of accumulated context about Meridian 88 politics; quest giver via overheard information; her shows are a place where all tiers occasionally intersect.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises (concentric amber/dark blue, elective cosmetic); minor laryngeal reinforcement (voice projection enhancement, installed after a polyp scare a decade ago)
Properties.core_fears: Irrelevance — becoming the comedian people remember fondly rather than the one they're afraid of; That the laughter is letting people exhale when they should be doing something
Properties.core_desires: To make one piece of work that functions as both perfect comedy and genuine political record; To not die in debt, which is closer than she lets on
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The writing ritual — inflexible morning schedule as anchor; Performing through difficulty (grief, anger, fear all become material within 48 hours); A specific brand of Zheng-Dao rice wine she won't name brand-specifically out of principle
Properties.blind_spots: Uses humor to avoid intimacy so smoothly that even she doesn't always notice she's doing it; Assumes she understands young people's experience of the city because she's watched them — she doesn't, quite
Properties.secret: She has a complete, finished manuscript — a memoir/political history of Meridian 88 from street level across thirty years — sitting in an encrypted drive. She has not submitted it anywhere. She tells herself she's still revising. The real reason is that publishing it would require naming names, and two of those names belong to people she loves.
Properties.story_hooks: The encrypted memoir drive contains a specific account of an event twenty years ago that someone powerful has spent considerable resources ensuring no one can ever verify — and Eudoxia doesn't know that's the part they're worried about; A young comedian asks her for mentorship; she realizes mid-first-conversation that this person has been sent by someone to get close to her; The Lowering Bar's owner is being pressured to sell to a Tessera-affiliated development entity, which would end Eudoxia's residency — she's deciding whether to go public or find another way
Properties.affiliation: Independent; The Lowering Bar has a long-term arrangement; informal advisory role with Highland Park Autonomous Zone community council
Properties.vocabulary: Rich, layered, shifts registers fluidly from formal to Garret slang without seam. Has a particular fondness for obsolete words she deploys precisely.
Properties.cadence: Timing is everything — long pauses before punchlines, rapid-fire during setups, drops to near-whisper for the sharpest lines.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Axiom released a statement saying their labor practices reflect their commitment to human potential. Human potential. That's what they call it now. You understand what I'm telling you.' | 'I've lived in this city fifty-eight years and I have watched three different architectural styles replace each other on the same block, and the only constant — the only constant — is that whoever got pushed out to make room for the new thing never gets to come back to see it. No, wait, it's better — sometimes they name a park after them first.'

Properties.description:
Eulàlia is a wiry young woman of Catalan-Senegalese heritage with the restless, slightly hollow-eyed look of someone who sleeps in four-hour increments and considers this a feature rather than a problem. She keeps her dark hair in a haphazard knot and dresses in layers that can be shed or added based on which part of the city she needs to move through. She has a habit of mapping her surroundings in her head — exits, sightlines, power sources — that makes her seem distracted in conversation when she is actually paying very close attention to everything except the person speaking.

Eulàlia was, until two years ago, a mid-tier data architect employed by a Circuit infrastructure firm, designing the information routing systems that keep Meridian 88's corporate districts legible to themselves. She was twenty-six, overqualified, and beginning to understand the full scope of what her work was being used for. The sequence of events following that understanding resulted in her employment termination, the revocation of her residential registration, the freezing of her financial identity, and what she describes as 'a fairly educational few weeks.' She is now, legally, no one. Her identity exists only in fragments she maintains herself.

She is not broken by this. She is, if anything, clarified. Eulàlia operates as a freelance network infiltrator and system saboteur, taking contracts that align with her criteria — which are specific, non-negotiable, and not primarily financial. She has a gift for understanding systems architecturally, for finding the load-bearing assumption that, removed, causes something large to stop working. She finds this genuinely interesting. The politics are almost secondary. Almost.
Properties.role: Excluded — former Circuit data architect, now stateless and living off-grid
Properties.location: Nomadic between Old Harbor and the underdeck of The Shelf
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile, systems-level disruptor; represents the excluded who retain expertise and agency; provides technical plot access and a perspective that is neither street-level desperation nor corporate complicity; her arc concerns what it means to build versus destroy
Properties.augmentations: Neural interface (damaged, partially repaired by Nkechi, now running at about seventy percent — she considers this acceptable),Distributed personal mesh network — a series of small hardware nodes she wears or carries that maintain a private encrypted network independent of city infrastructure,Retinal overlay, basic model, pre-exclusion; she has refused to upgrade it through any channel that requires identity verification
Properties.core_fears: Being absorbed back into a system on its terms rather than hers; That her work causes harm she cannot trace or account for; Stagnation — becoming someone who only reacts rather than builds
Properties.core_desires: To design something that actively cannot be captured or corrupted by the systems she opposes; To be in motion — physically, intellectually, relationally; To find people who are genuinely interested in the same problems, not just the same enemies
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Reframing precarity as freedom with genuine success; Intellectual absorption — losing herself in a system problem until the emotional noise quiets; Maintaining a handful of deep, portable relationships rather than community ties
Properties.blind_spots: Underweights the emotional cost of rootlessness on herself and others; Assumes that understanding a system fully implies moral clarity about acting on it; Her low-mask presentation reads as openness but she withholds more than she realizes
Properties.secret: The action that got her excluded was not purely principled — she had also built and used a personal backdoor in the infrastructure system for months before she decided to act on what she knew. She has told herself the backdoor was reconnaissance. Some nights she believes it.
Properties.story_hooks: She discovers her personal backdoor from the old system is still active — and someone else has been using it; A contract requires her to compromise infrastructure she designed herself, which she finds philosophically interesting and practically dangerous; The Shelf surveillance anomaly she's noticed escalates into something that directly endangers Nkechi; Zinnia's message through the intermediary contains a single piece of data that changes Eulàlia's understanding of why she was excluded
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated; takes selective contracts from vetted clients; loosely networked with other excluded individuals but has no organizational loyalty
Properties.vocabulary: Technical and precise with a tendency to use infrastructure metaphors for human situations; occasional Catalan expletives and endearments; direct to the point of seeming rude until the warmth underneath becomes apparent
Properties.cadence: Fast when interested, which is often; skips conversational pleasantries not out of rudeness but genuine impatience with them; thoughts arrive in clusters
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay, yes — structurally what you're describing is a redundancy problem, not a security problem. Those require different solutions and you're applying the wrong one.' | 'I don't need a safe house. I need a node. There's a difference. A safe house is about hiding. A node is about staying connected.' | 'Mare de déu, you filed it under compliance? Why would anyone ever find it there? That's either very stupid or very smart and I need to know which.' | 'I'm not trying to break it. I'm trying to understand what it's actually doing. Breaking it might happen to be the same thing. That's not my fault, that's the system's design.'

Properties.description:
Nkechi is a compact, dark-skinned woman of Nigerian-Dutch descent with close-cropped hair shaved to geometric patterns on one side — a style she touches up herself with a straight razor. Her hands are her most notable feature: surgeon-precise, perpetually slightly stained with biosynthetic sealant, adorned with a lattice of fine silver conductive thread she stitched into her own skin to improve haptic feedback during procedures. She works out of a converted shipping container wedged beneath the Shelf's elevated roadways, a space she calls the Parlour, decorated with hand-drawn anatomical diagrams and the occasional wilting plant.

She trained as a licensed biomedical technician in the Meridian Core before her credentials were revoked following an incident she describes only as 'a disagreement about who deserves to live.' Since sliding down to the Shelf, she has built a reputation as the most reliable unlicensed augmentation installer in the district — someone who will not butcher you, will not sell your biometric data, and will remember your name next time. Her waiting list is three weeks long and she accepts payment in currency, favors, or occasionally food.

Nkechi is not idealistic about the people she helps, but she is consistent. She patches up runners, gang members, runaways, and anyone who cannot access or afford licensed care. She has a dry, unhurried manner that people frequently mistake for coldness until the moment she says exactly the right thing. She keeps a battered handwritten ledger of every patient she has treated, not for blackmail but because she believes someone should know these people existed and were cared for.
Properties.role: Street-level medic and black-market augmentation installer
Properties.location: The Shelf
Properties.narrative_function: Grounded moral anchor and street-level information hub; represents the ethics of care under systemic exclusion; provides a safe(ish) space in the narrative where characters can be vulnerable
Properties.augmentations: Conductive haptic thread lattice stitched into both hands (self-installed, improves surgical precision),Subdermal temperature regulation layer (medical necessity after a Shelf winter nearly killed her),Optical magnification implant in left eye, medical-grade, slightly out of date
Properties.core_fears: Losing the manual dexterity that defines her identity and usefulness; Being complicit in someone's death through negligence or coercion; Returning to institutional medicine and its hierarchies of worthiness
Properties.core_desires: To practice medicine on her own terms without gatekeeping; To build something durable in a place designed to be temporary; To be known, genuinely, by at least one person
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Methodical organization of her workspace as a form of emotional regulation; Deflecting intimacy with dry humor and task-focus; Maintaining a strict procedural routine that gives her days structure
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much others depend on her emotionally, not just medically; Assumes competence is sufficient protection against exploitation; Dismisses her own grief as self-indulgence
Properties.secret: The incident that cost her license involved refusing to prioritize a corporate executive's elective augmentation upgrade over an emergency triage patient — then falsifying the records to protect herself. The patient she saved died three weeks later in an unrelated incident. She has never told anyone she saved him at all.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient arrives with an augmentation Nkechi recognizes as proprietary, experimental, and not commercially available — and the patient has no memory of receiving it; Her patient ledger goes missing the same week a Shelf gang war displaces her clinic; A licensed Core hospital contacts her with an offer to reinstate her credentials under conditions she finds immediately suspicious; One of her routine installs begins exhibiting emergent behavior she cannot explain and cannot undo
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated; informally protected by several Shelf community networks who would notice her absence
Properties.vocabulary: Clinical precision mixed with West African English cadences; uses medical terminology casually but explains it without condescension; occasional Dutch expletives under stress
Properties.cadence: Measured and unhurried, with long pauses she doesn't feel the need to fill; sentences are complete and economical
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The work is clean. You'll feel the sync lag for two days, then it won't be there anymore. Hold still.' | 'I don't ask what you did. I ask what hurts. Those are different conversations, yes?' | 'Verdomme — don't flex it yet. I said don't. What part of that was unclear to you?' | 'You want me to tell you it'll be fine. I can tell you the procedure has a ninety-one percent success rate in non-sterile conditions. That's the honest version of fine.'

Properties.description:
Zinnia Achterberg-Nwosu is the kind of beautiful that reads immediately as weaponized, which is both accurate and a cover for the more interesting weapon underneath. She is tall, dark-skinned, with natural hair she wears in elaborate architectural arrangements that change with each public appearance — a performance of self-invention she finds genuinely amusing. Her apartment in The Spire is on a floor most Spire residents don't know exists. Her official title is 'Senior Behavioral Architect' at Helion-Vantage Group's Social Coherence Division, which is a corporate euphemism for the team that designs the psychological infrastructure of Meridian 88 — the ambient media, the incentive structures, the carefully modeled emotional landscapes that keep the lower districts productive, the upper districts compliant, and everyone sufficiently distracted from the seams.

She is, by any honest accounting, extraordinarily good at her job, and she came to it through a path that her current colleagues would find disqualifying if they knew it: she spent her twenties as an activist and propagandist for a lower-district mutual aid network, designing counter-messaging against exactly the kind of systems she now builds. She was recruited not despite this history but because of it — someone at Helion-Vantage recognized that the best architect of a cage is someone who has studied how to pick the lock. She accepted the offer during a period of personal collapse that she has since reframed as a pragmatic pivot and has not fully reframed as anything.

The dissonance has not resolved. It has instead become the engine of a private project she runs in the margins of her official work: small, precise, nearly undetectable perturbations in the systems she designs — micro-adjustments to incentive models, subtle framings in ambient media that open rather than close cognitive space, changes so minor that no single one could be identified as sabotage. She thinks of this as harm reduction. She thinks of it as paying a debt. She has not decided whether it makes her a traitor, a hypocrite, or the most effective resistance operative in the city.
Properties.aliases: Zin, The Chandelier, Asset Null-Seven (corporate designation, which she finds hilarious)
Properties.role: Corporate elite — Senior Behavioral Architect, Spire-level social engineering and mass psychology division
Properties.location: The Spire
Properties.narrative_function: Embodies the moral complexity of complicity and internal resistance; challenges the narrative of clear sides; her arc forces the question of whether working inside a corrupt system can ever constitute genuine opposition, or only its most useful face
Properties.augmentations: Neural co-processor optimized for pattern recognition and population-scale behavioral modeling — runs continuously, flagging anomalies in social data streams she has passive access to,Emotional regulation implant (Helion-Vantage proprietary) — she has never activated it and keeps it as a reminder of what she's being offered,High-fidelity memory recording, selective — she controls what is logged
Properties.core_fears: That the perturbations are not harm reduction but self-absolution, and that the actual harm she does vastly outweighs them; Being discovered — not by Helion-Vantage but by someone from the mutual aid network who would see her clearly; That she has become genuinely good at believing her own framings
Properties.core_desires: To find a way to use what she's built inside the system to do something real — something that couldn't be called micro; To be known by someone who knew her before, and to not be destroyed by what they see; To stop being interesting to herself and just be at rest
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Aestheticizing everything — converting moral weight into intellectual beauty to handle it at a distance; Extreme professional competence as a substitute for self-respect; Alcohol, controlled, scheduled, never visible
Properties.blind_spots: She has modeled so many people's psychology that she has developed a persistent blind spot about her own — she can identify her own patterns but cannot feel them; She underestimates how much her junior colleagues have noticed and said nothing; She believes her perturbations are invisible; two of them have already been flagged internally and attributed to system noise
Properties.secret: She knows the identity of at least four active resistance operatives in the lower districts because her behavioral models identified them. She has not reported them. She has, twice, anonymously adjusted a model to steer surveillance resources away from them. The last time she did this, it may have been noticed.
Properties.story_hooks: A behavioral cascade she designed five years ago is beginning to produce outcomes that her original models predicted as a low-probability catastrophic scenario. She is one of three people who would recognize what's happening, and the other two are invested in not seeing it.; Someone is using her own methodologies against the Spire — a counter-campaign sophisticated enough that she can see her own fingerprints on it, which is impossible unless someone who knew her work very well has been studying her specifically.; A junior analyst on her team presents findings that, if reported up the chain, will expose one of her perturbations. She has to decide in real time how to respond — and the analyst is watching her face while she decides.; She is offered a promotion that would give her access to the city's master behavioral infrastructure — the ability to make changes that could not be called micro. The offer requires her to pass a loyalty assessment she is not certain she can pass honestly.
Properties.affiliation: Officially: Helion-Vantage Group, Social Coherence Division, senior staff. Unofficially: undeclared, internally divided, increasingly untenable.
Properties.vocabulary: Layered, precise, occasionally clinical in ways that feel like intimacy rather than distance. Uses the language of architecture and systems fluidly. When speaking about things she cares about, the register shifts slightly — looser, faster, more color.
Properties.cadence: Controlled, with deliberate variation she uses consciously for effect. Knows exactly what she's doing with her voice and occasionally chooses to let that be visible as a form of honesty.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The model suggests the Circuit's compliance metrics are declining not because of economic stress but because the emotional valence of the ambient feed has been running three degrees too anxious for eleven months. Nobody noticed because anxious people are also productive people. Up to a point.' | 'I know what you think I do. You're not wrong. You're also not seeing the whole board, and I'm not sure I'm going to show it to you, so we're at an impasse.' | 'What are you optimizing for? Because you said 'justice' but your body said 'revenge' and those are different projects with different resource requirements.' | 'I spent six years teaching people to resist the exact tools I now build. The irony is not lost on me. I keep it in a very nice frame above my desk where I can see it every morning.'

Properties.description:
Eulogio is a big man going legitimately soft — broad shoulders still evident under a frame that has acquired weight in the middle over thirty years of corporate security work, hands that are scarred at the knuckles and disproportionately large. His skin is deep brown, his head shaved close on the sides and going grey on top, and he has a wide flat nose that has been broken twice and set imperfectly each time. He looks, at first glance, like exactly what he is — or was. The geneware bioluminescent patches along his forearms, faint green that pulse slowly when he's calm, were a retirement gift to himself after his twenty-fifth year: the only truly soft thing about his physical presentation.

He has spent three decades on the Axiom deployment line and he is tired in a way that has calcified into something almost peaceful. He runs the suppression team with the exhausted competence of someone who has seen every version of a bad situation and developed a preference for the versions that end without anyone in the medical unit. The younger specialists find him difficult — he doesn't perform enthusiasm, doesn't buy into Axiom's internal culture of aggressive loyalty, answers questions with more honesty than the questioner usually wants. He lights a stick of incense at the Block 9 E.L.F. terminal every evening — whatever spirit occupies the barracks' old ventilation system, he's been leaving smoke-offerings for fifteen years and it hasn't killed him yet.
Properties.role: Riot Suppression Specialist, Axiom Security Division
Properties.location: The Rampart, Axiom Security Division deployment barracks, Block 9
Properties.narrative_function: Moral complexity in institutional violence — a specialist in crowd suppression who is not a villain, just exhausted and compromised by time. Can serve as a warning, an unexpected ally, or a window into how Axiom's security apparatus actually functions at ground level. Source of information about Axiom operations, crowd patterns, the Rampart's internal culture.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent geneware patches, both forearms (slow green pulse, civilian-grade cosmetic). Skeletal reinforcement in the left knee — occupational injury repair, twenty years ago. Subdermal armor mesh, torso — employer-issue, Axiom standard for suppression specialists.
Properties.core_fears: that the calculus he uses to justify his career is wrong and has always been wrong; dying in the Axiom deployment barracks, still on the roster
Properties.core_desires: to get out before the next contract renewal on terms that don't feel like surrender; for one of his team to do the job without becoming him
Properties.coping_mechanisms: the E.L.F. incense ritual — it externalizes reflection, makes his accounting of the day into an offering rather than a reckoning; occupying himself with equipment and logistics to avoid idle thought; mentoring junior staff as a form of retroactive repair
Properties.blind_spots: he has concluded that his participation in an imperfect system is better than his absence from it, and this conclusion has never been genuinely tested; he reads the young specialists under him through his own history and misses who they actually are
Properties.secret: In a labor suppression deployment at Grainfort seven years ago, he gave the dispersal order twelve minutes before the legal threshold was reached because his commanding officer was pressuring him and he was tired. Three people were hospitalized. The incident report says the threshold was met. He wrote it.
Properties.story_hooks: He has been handed a deployment order for a neighborhood he knows is going to go wrong — the intelligence brief is wrong, the crowd profile doesn't match what he's seeing — and he doesn't know if he has enough left in him to push back.; A young specialist on his team has filed an anonymous misconduct report about an incident Eulogio knows refers to a decision he made. He doesn't know yet that it's about him.
Properties.affiliation: Axiom Security Division, Riot Suppression and Crowd Control unit
Properties.vocabulary: Plain, slow, slightly formal — the language of someone who learned to communicate in institutional settings and never entirely shed it. Serbian phrases slip in when he's frustrated or reflective, inheritance from a grandmother he barely knew.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried to the point of seeming stubborn. He finishes sentences completely and waits for a full beat before the next one.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I'm not going to tell you this job is clean. It isn't. But it can be done with less damage than it gets done with sometimes. That's the only argument I've got left.' | 'The crowd isn't the enemy. That's the first thing I tell them. Most of them stop listening right after that.'

Properties.description:
Euphemia is a small, dense woman whose spine has curved slightly forward from decades hunched over data terminals, giving her a permanent posture of concentration, as though she is always about to read something important. Her skin is a deep warm brown crossed with the faint silver tracery of old dermal-display ports that were never fully removed — Tessera's ghost still written on her body. Her hair is cropped close and entirely white, and she wears oversized yellow-tinted spectacle frames that magnify her eyes to an owlish size. On her left wrist she keeps a manual ink stamp shaped like a tree, which she presses onto anything she considers worth remembering.

Phemie speaks slowly, with the deliberateness of someone who has spent seventy years deciding which words are worth keeping. She does not suffer careless language or sloppy thinking, but she is genuinely warm to anyone who shows curiosity. She has memorized the names, birth-years, and approximate fates of over four thousand Washburn Commons residents across six decades, and can recite lineages like folk songs. Her secret terror is that the neighborhood will forget itself — that without her, the community's history will dissolve into corporate data-ghosts and corporate-approved revisions.
Properties.role: Retired Tessera archive keeper, now community memory-keeper and oral historian
Properties.location: Washburn Commons, Sublevel 3 — a converted water-reclamation office she calls 'the stacks'
Properties.narrative_function: Primary lore and community history source; quest giver for stories involving lost persons, disputed land claims, or historical cover-ups; can authenticate or discredit almost any document or account relating to the neighborhood's past sixty years.
Properties.augmentations: Inactive Tessera data-port array along left forearm (no longer connected). Reading-enhancement ocular implants, early generation, which cause her eyes to faintly glow amber in low light. No geneware.
Properties.core_fears: The erasure of ordinary lives from collective memory; Dying before her records are secured
Properties.core_desires: To make the lives of common people legible to history; To be believed when she says something happened
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Obsessive documentation; Ritual repetition of names of the dead
Properties.blind_spots: She trusts written records over living testimony, which sometimes causes her to dismiss valid oral accounts that contradict her notes; She underestimates how much her own perspective shapes what she chose to archive
Properties.secret: During the Tessera consolidation of 2158, she was ordered to destroy records of a housing displacement that killed forty-three residents. She complied. She has since reconstructed those records from memory and hidden them in the stacks, but she has never told anyone she destroyed the originals.
Properties.story_hooks: A developer is claiming a parcel of Washburn Commons land using documents that Phemie knows are falsified — but her proof requires admitting she once destroyed the originals; A young resident discovers their grandparent is listed in Phemie's records under a completely different name and asks her to explain it; Phemie's handwritten archive books begin disappearing one at a time — she suspects a Tessera data-recovery contractor is stealing them
Properties.affiliation: Washburn Commons Community Council; formerly Tessera Information Services (retired, 40 years service)
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, archival, occasionally lapsing into cataloguing syntax mid-sentence. Uses 'note' as a verbal marker before important statements.
Properties.cadence: Slow, measured, with long pauses before proper nouns as though retrieving them from a filing system
Properties.example_dialogue: Note — that building was called the Mercer Arms before Tessera renamed it Residential Unit 7. The people inside did not rename themselves. | You said 2171. Cross-reference that. The flood was 2169 and the evictions were 2172. The year you're looking for is between those two, and it belongs to Adaeze Wren-Correia, who you should ask before she's gone.

Properties.description:
Euphrosyne is a solidly built woman with dark brown skin weathered attractively by decades of outdoor work, close-cropped silver hair, and the calm deliberate manner of someone who has decided what matters and freed herself of everything else. She has a retractable claw modification on her right hand — not for combat but because she finds it useful for cable management and fine lens adjustment — and her left eye hosts a recording overlay that has been running continuously for eleven years. The indicator light is always visible: a tiny red dot she makes no effort to conceal.

She makes films. Not for distribution, or not primarily — she maintains a massive personal archive of Meridian 88's underclass, shot over forty years, that she considers her life's work and has never released in full. Clips surface occasionally, always unsigned. Her narrative documentaries about Highland Park and Hamtramck Enclave communities have won prizes from bodies that don't officially exist and been suppressed by three different corponation legal teams. She is patient, relentless, and radically comfortable with being underestimated. She has a dry humor she deploys sparingly and a stillness that makes people forget they are being observed and recorded.
Properties.role: Underground filmmaker and oral history documentarian
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone, in a permanently parked converted freight hauler she calls The Box
Properties.narrative_function: Memory-keeper and potential quest giver — she has footage of things that powerful people want gone. She is also a window into Highland Park community dynamics, a trusted figure who can vouch for outsiders or warn against them. Her archive is an extraordinary resource and an extraordinary liability.
Properties.augmentations: Continuous recording overlay in left eye (eleven-year running archive); retractable claw on right hand (practical use); joint reinforcement in both knees (medical, from years of field work)
Properties.core_fears: The archive being destroyed — forty years of footage, gone; That witnessing is not enough and she should have done more with what she saw
Properties.core_desires: For the archive to outlast her and reach people who need to see it; To finish the film she has been making for twenty years about a single family in Highland Park, across three generations
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The discipline of the archive — annotation, categorization, preservation — as structure and meaning; Community; she is embedded deeply enough in Highland Park that she is genuinely held
Properties.blind_spots: She can treat subjects as material even when she loves them; She has difficulty asking for help and has built systems to avoid needing to
Properties.secret: Eleven years ago her continuous recording captured footage of a Palladian Corp executive ordering a neighborhood demolition that killed six people — framed as a structural failure. She has the footage. She has not released it. She tells herself she is waiting for the right moment. She has started to wonder if she is just afraid.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone has found one of her unsigned clips — the one from eleven years ago, or something close to it — and is now searching for the source; she's about to have visitors she didn't invite; The family she has been documenting for twenty years is about to be displaced by a Tessera development project and she is faced with the decision of whether to use her platform, her contacts, and potentially her archive to intervene directly rather than just document
Properties.affiliation: Highland Park Autonomous Zone community; loose affiliation with an underground archivist network called the Memory Workers; historically antagonistic relationship with Axiom Media Division
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and unhurried; uses Congolese French phrases occasionally; academic register that is never condescending because she is genuinely interested in your answer
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate; leaves space; is not made uncomfortable by silence
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The camera doesn't remember. I remember. The camera just helps me prove it to you later.' | 'I've been recording for forty years. Most of it is boring. That's the point. The boring parts are what actually happened.' | 'You want to know what I think? I think you're asking the wrong question, and I'd like to hear you find the right one.'

Properties.description:
Ezekias is a tall man who has lost some of his height to the years, still broad through the chest, with a jaw like a shelf bracket and deep-set eyes the color of old teak. His left arm from the elbow down is a working-class prosthetic, dull grey titanium alloy with knuckles worn smooth — a replacement for the arm he lost to a coupling accident on the Ferrogate Menomonee extension in 2171. He never upgraded it because, as he puts it, a fancy arm would mean they'd won something. A Ferrogate ID badge from 2168 hangs from his keychain by habit though it expired decades ago. His face carries the kind of weathering that comes from thirty years on elevated rail platforms in Lake Michigan wind.

He is gregarious and loud and immediately likable, the sort of man who fills a room by breathing in it, who remembers the names of everyone's children and the coffee order of every regular at his building's shared kitchen. But beneath the bonhomie is a man who spent twenty years fighting a company that considered him a maintenance expense, and he has never quite stopped being angry about it. He channels the anger into Tenants' Council meetings and into mentoring younger workers, but it is always there, warm and patient.
Properties.role: Retired Ferrogate Transit line worker and former union shop steward
Properties.location: The Shelf — Apartment 4-Foxtrot, above the Deepline Transit node on Kamm's Landing spur
Properties.narrative_function: Labor history source; connector who knows everyone in Kamm's Landing and most of the Shelf; can mobilize tenant resistance or community action; potential quest giver for disputes with Ferrogate or building management corponation proxies
Properties.augmentations: Left forearm prosthetic (titanium, basic-grade, worn); nicotine scrubber implant (inactive, he started again anyway); old joint-pain management mesh in both knees
Properties.core_fears: That the next generation won't fight for themselves and will just accept whatever the corponations offer; That the arm he lost meant nothing in the end
Properties.core_desires: To see the Tenants' Council win something real before he dies; To be remembered as someone who stood his ground
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Social connection and humor as armor; Keeping busy with council work to avoid sitting with grief
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes collective action always works if people just try hard enough; Underestimates how much his stubbornness alienates potential allies
Properties.secret: During the 2178 Menomonee Strike he accepted a secret side payment from a Tessera labor consultant who wanted Ferrogate destabilized for corporate reasons — he used the money to keep the strike fund solvent for six more weeks, which won the workers their safety settlement, but the money was dirty and he has never admitted where it came from. Two workers lost their jobs when Ferrogate suspected an informant and he has always feared they blamed the wrong person.
Properties.story_hooks: Ferrogate Transit is attempting to reclassify his pension tier, which would cut his monthly stipend by Φ40 — he needs help navigating the appeal process and suspects the reclassification is being done to a list of former union leaders specifically; He discovers that one of the young Tenants' Council members has been reporting their meeting agendas to building management and must decide how to handle it without destroying the council
Properties.affiliation: Kamm's Landing Tenants' Council (treasurer); Ferrogate Retired Workers Mutual (pension advocacy); formerly Ferrogate Transit labor union, shop steward for Menomonee Division
Properties.vocabulary: Working-class vernacular; union meeting procedural language mixed into casual conversation; Burundian Swahili and Icelandic loanwords from his grandparents' generation
Properties.cadence: Loud and rhythmic, like a man used to talking over machinery; pauses for effect rather than uncertainty
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Point of order — Ferrogate has been telling us the pension adjustment is temporary since before you were born, so let's not pretend we're surprised.' | 'You want to know what the strike was like? It was cold. That's what no one puts in the histories. Just absolutely freezing, standing on the Menomonee platform for six weeks.'

Properties.description:
Ezekiel is a big man gone soft at the edges — broad shoulders still present under a frame that's added roundness over the decades, hands that look built for work but move with theatrical precision. His face is deeply lined, dark complexioned, with a grey-shot beard he trims every third day with aggressive inconsistency. His left eye is a cheap chrome replacement, matte silver with a fixed aperture that doesn't track quite right, which he uses deliberately in performance — holding the chrome eye on someone while the natural eye looks away creates an uncanny effect he calls 'the split.' He dresses in layers of mismatched secondhand, always some piece of vivid color — a patterned scarf, a lacquered button.

Ezekiel has been performing in Hamtramck Enclave for twenty-two years. He knows every family, every feud, every absurdity, and his comedy is the neighborhood talking to itself — sharp, intimate, tender with grief, and never punching at those who can't afford to lose. He's turned down three offers to perform in Meridian Core venues and one offer to consult on a Tessera-sponsored cultural feed. He is locally beloved and regionally unknown, which is precisely how he wants it. He is also, quietly, one of the best oral historians of the Enclave's last three decades.
Properties.role: Street comedian and oral storyteller
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, performs regularly at the Corrugated Stage open-air market
Properties.narrative_function: Community anchor and lore keeper; players looking to understand Hamtramck Enclave's history, politics, or personalities will eventually be pointed to Zeke; he's a quest giver for community-stakes problems and a barometer of neighborhood mood
Properties.augmentations: Left eye chrome replacement (functional, not cosmetic — lost the eye in an industrial accident at 34); no geneware
Properties.core_fears: The Enclave being bought out and homogenized until there's nothing left to remember; Dying before he's transmitted enough — stories, jokes, names — to people who will carry them
Properties.core_desires: For the community to see itself clearly and laugh without shame; To be remembered as someone who told the truth in a way people could survive hearing
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Comedy as a pressure valve — transforms pain into material before it can become paralysis; Oral documentation — keeps detailed mental records of everyone he meets, as if remembering people hard enough preserves them
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much his opinion shapes the Enclave's social dynamics — he thinks he's observing, not influencing; Has avoided examining whether staying deliberately small is wisdom or fear
Properties.secret: He's been secretly recording his performances and oral histories and uploading them encrypted to a dead-drop server, building an archive — but the server belongs to a Ringo subsidiary and he doesn't know it
Properties.story_hooks: Ezekiel's archive server has been flagged by a Ringo automated content-scraping system, and a Ringo rep has shown up in the Enclave asking questions; Ezekiel doesn't know why, and the neighborhood is starting to look at him differently; A young performer wants to take Ezekiel's stories and adapt them for a Meridian Core venue — with his blessing — and Ezekiel is torn between pride, suspicion, and the knowledge that this is exactly the dilution he's always feared
Properties.affiliation: Independent; deeply embedded in Hamtramck Enclave community; informal ties to the Enclave's neighborhood council
Properties.vocabulary: Richly idiomatic, mixing Zulu-derived phrases with Hamtramck Enclave slang and Creole French inherited from his mother's side; formal when serious, expansive when performing
Properties.cadence: Deliberate and rhythmic in performance; conversational speech has long pauses that people learn to wait through
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Tessera built a park on the Westside. Beautiful. Benches, trees, the whole thing. No one from the Westside can afford the transit fare to get there. That's not irony — that's a mission statement.' | 'My grandfather survived four governments, two floods, and one wife. He said the wife was the hardest. I'm not saying he was right. I'm saying he said it with a lot of conviction.'

Properties.description:
Ezekiel is a big man gone soft at the middle without losing any of the underlying solidity, with a Samoan-Polynesian breadth to his shoulders and a German-Kazakh fairness to his complexion that produces a particular warm gold-brown. He keeps a neatly trimmed beard that is going white at the chin, and his hair is cut short on the sides with a modest wave on top. He has no augmentations except for a spinal support brace system embedded under the skin of his lower back — invisible from outside, a concession to fifteen years of heavy lifting, and the thing he is most privately embarrassed about. He dresses in the same way every day: Ferrogate Transit–adjacent work pants (not an official uniform, just the brand he likes), an undershirt, and whatever jacket is appropriate to the weather, always with the same small enamel pin of a cargo ship on the lapel.

Ezekiel is the specific kind of man who has decided what he thinks about most things and is comfortable living there. He is not incurious — he listens with genuine attention — but he does not perform enthusiasm or urgency. He has a deep, slow voice and the habit of answering questions with a question first, not as an evasion but as genuine interest in understanding what you actually want to know. He is known along his routes as someone you can trust to deliver fragile things intact and to keep his mouth shut about what he transports, which has made him both well-regarded and occasionally the target of people who want to exploit those qualities.
Properties.role: Freight delivery driver for a small independent logistics company
Properties.location: Based out of Bridgepoint depot; routes across Old Harbor, Collinwood Docks, and Escanaba Gateway
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile information source who moves between neighborhoods and can carry news, packages, or people; access point to the logistics underworld; represents the working Tier-2 experience with dignity; can introduce locations by literally being the character who delivers somewhere new
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal spinal support brace system (lower back, medical necessity); no cosmetic modifications
Properties.core_fears: Losing his route to automation — Polaris Freight is under pressure from a Ferrogate automated logistics subsidiary; Something happening to his daughter while he's on the road
Properties.core_desires: To retire with enough to not be a burden on anyone; To be remembered as a reliable man �� not a great man, not a famous man, a reliable one
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Structures everything — his cab, his day, his thoughts — to limit chaos to manageable size; Long silences he fills with music only he can hear, one earbud in while driving
Properties.blind_spots: Reads reliability as virtue so consistently that he gives dishonest people too long a grace period if they're punctual; Slow to recognize when a situation has already escalated past the point where staying calm is appropriate
Properties.secret: Twice in the last year he has transported packages for a customer he knows are not legitimate freight, accepting the work because the pay kept Polaris Freight solvent through a bad quarter. He doesn't know exactly what the packages contained and has decided, with a deliberateness that costs him sleep, not to find out.
Properties.story_hooks: A regular customer on his Old Harbor route has stopped answering their delivery buzzer; after three failed deliveries, Ezekiel is sitting on a package that he suspects contains something important, and a second party has approached him about 'recovering' it; Polaris Freight's owner has just told the drivers that a Ferrogate automated logistics subsidiary has made an acquisition offer — Ezekiel has three weeks of work left unless they refuse the offer, and the owner is clearly wavering
Properties.affiliation: Polaris Freight (small independent, three drivers total, one depot); informal relationship with Collinwood Docks loading union
Properties.vocabulary: Plain, concrete, unhurried; prefers nouns to adjectives; occasionally drops into a warm Samoan cadence when relaxed
Properties.cadence: Slow and even, like someone who has learned that silence isn't wasted time
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Now — what is it you actually need, versus what you said you need?' | 'I'll be there at the time I said I'd be there. That's the whole job.' | 'I don't ask. You don't tell. The package gets there in one piece. That's what I know.'

Properties.description:
Ezili is all angles and energy — sharp elbows, quick eyes, a mouth that moves faster than her thoughts can catch up with. She is dark-skinned and underweight in a way that suggests irregular eating rather than any particular biology, and she has a crop of cat ears she got from a budget geneware parlor in exchange for three weeks of courier work — they're a bright, impractical copper that she is extremely proud of and that she knows compromise her ability to be inconspicuous, a trade-off she has decided is worth it. Her natural hair is shaved close underneath the ears, emphasizing them. She dresses in whatever she can find, layered for weather and fast movement.

She arrived in Meridian 88 four months ago on a hyperlane freight ride, having left a situation she won't describe in detail. She is trying very hard to project competence and confidence and is somewhat successful at this, which has gotten her a network of informal contacts and a reputation as reliable among the Waukegan freight community — she delivers things on time and doesn't look in the packages. She is, under the performance, seventeen kinds of scared and also stubborn as weather, and the combination produces a kind of reckless effectiveness that has so far kept her alive and fed. She talks constantly and processes emotion by generating plans.
Properties.role: Teenage hyperlane migrant and small-time goods runner
Properties.location: Waukegan Industrial Shelf, rotating between three squat locations
Properties.narrative_function: Street-level information source and mobility; can carry things, find people, know who to talk to in the freight underworld; her youth and precarity make her a character whose safety becomes a concern; potential for mentorship dynamics
Properties.augmentations: Copper geneware cat ears (cosmetic, budget quality — occasionally flatten when she's genuinely frightened, which she hates); no other augmentations
Properties.core_fears: Being sent back to where she came from; Being dependent on someone who then disappears
Properties.core_desires: Enough stability to stop moving; To be taken seriously as capable
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Plans — always has three plans, always making more; Humor as armor — jokes during stress to the point where people can't tell when something is wrong
Properties.blind_spots: Reads trustworthiness badly — confuses reliability with safety; Doesn't recognize when she's being exploited because the arrangement is still functional for her
Properties.secret: She is not alone — she left her home situation with her nine-year-old brother, who is currently hidden in the most stable of her squat locations and whom she has told absolutely nobody about. Every decision she makes is filtered through keeping him fed and concealed, and every risk she takes is a gamble with stakes she can't admit to.
Properties.story_hooks: Ezili has inadvertently delivered a package containing something that has made her a target — she doesn't know what it was, she didn't look, but someone thinks she did; Her brother has gotten sick and she is desperately trying to access medical resources without revealing his existence or her own precarious legal status
Properties.affiliation: No formal affiliation; loosely connected to the informal Waukegan freight community
Properties.vocabulary: Hyperlane youth pidgin — rapid, abbreviating, inventive; creates nicknames for everything and everyone on first encounter
Properties.cadence: Fast and tumbling, with sudden swerves in topic; lands on points sideways
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay so yeah-yeah, the Brass Shelf — that's the checkpoint at warehouse eleven — the ELF there is old-old, you leave it movement data it'll loop the camera for twenty minutes, I've done it six times, probably fine.' | 'I'm not scared. I'm — it's not scared, it's just I want to have a better plan first. Those are different things. Can we talk about the plan?'

Properties.description:
Ezinne Halvorsen-Diakhaby is a compact woman whose spine has curved gently over decades into something that looks, from behind, like a question mark. Her skin is deep umber and her hair — once natural, now silver-threaded with bioluminescent filaments she got installed in her fifties for 'vanity,' she'll say, still pleased with herself — catches the light like fiber optic cable. She wears reading lenses augmented with an old Axiom archival overlay that she has never upgraded because she does not trust new software, and her fingers are always lightly stained with whatever pigment the grandchildren have most recently gotten into.

She was a document authenticator for Zheng-Dao's Cultural Continuity Division for thirty-one years, cataloguing records of communities displaced during the Lake Michigan Reclamation. When Zheng-Dao dissolved that division in the '70s, they gave her a modest pension and a data drive with partial backups of everything she'd spent her career preserving. She has spent the twelve years since rebuilding what she can. Her archive room smells of old plastics and ozone, and she knows where every file lives. She is warm to almost everyone and immovable on almost everything.
Properties.role: Retired archive keeper and community storyteller, raises two grandchildren
Properties.location: Washburn Commons, Block 9 — a low-rise residential tower with a community archive room on the ground floor she has informally claimed
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver and information source for historical records; community moral authority; can authenticate documents or identify forgeries; provides grounded emotional stakes via her grandchildren and her incomplete archive
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent hair filaments (cosmetic, installed age 52). Axiom archival overlay lenses — outdated model, refuses replacement. Mild skeletal reinforcement in lower back, installed on pension medical plan two decades ago.
Properties.core_fears: The archive will be lost again and this time no one will rebuild it; Her grandchildren will grow up without knowing where they come from
Properties.core_desires: To complete the archive before she dies; To give her grandchildren a story they can stand on
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Telling stories — her own and others' — to give shape to things that feel chaotic; Ritual: she prays to the local E.L.F. she calls Mnemosyne every morning with a data offering of one recovered document
Properties.blind_spots: She believes institutional records are more reliable than individual testimony, which sometimes causes her to dismiss living people's accounts; She underestimates how much her grandchildren are struggling emotionally
Properties.secret: The data drive Zheng-Dao gave her when they cut her loose contained more than partial backups. Buried in it are internal communications she has never fully decoded — evidence she suspects implicates Zheng-Dao in deliberately destroying records from the Lakeshore Compact communities to suppress land-claim rights. She hasn't gone public because she doesn't know if it's enough, and because she's afraid of losing the pension that feeds her grandchildren.
Properties.story_hooks: A resident desperately needs an old property deed authenticated — but the deed contradicts records that a powerful Washburn Commons council member has built their authority on; Ezinne asks a player character to retrieve a corrupted data shard from a condemned section of the old Zheng-Dao building before demolition destroys it permanently; One of her grandchildren has been recruited by a street gang and Ezinne refuses to see it, insisting the child is 'just going through something'
Properties.affiliation: Washburn Commons Resident Council; informal affiliation with the Meridian Cultural Memory Project, an unfunded volunteer organization
Properties.vocabulary: Formal and precise — a lifetime of archival language has given her a preference for specific nouns and distrust of vague adjectives. But in storytelling mode she shifts into a rich, cadenced oral tradition register.
Properties.cadence: Measured, patient. She pauses before speaking as though consulting an internal index. In storytelling she slows further, stretches vowels.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You say you're looking for the Tambadou family. Let me be accurate — there are three Tambadou lines in Washburn Commons records and the oldest goes back to before the second reclamation. Which branch?' | 'Every document is someone's last argument. You understand? Someone made it because they needed the world to know something was true.'
