Properties.description:
Ezinwa is lean in the way of someone who forgets meals when absorbed in work — angular cheekbones, long fingers perpetually stained faint yellow from reagent handling, and eyes with geometric patterned irises (a geneware mod, copper hexagons on dark brown) that they chose themselves at nineteen as the first thing they ever bought with their own money. Their hair grows in tight coils they keep cropped close, and they have a habit of wearing a surgical mask around their neck rather than their face, pushed down when working. Their voice is soft and precise, like someone who learned to speak carefully in rooms where being overheard was dangerous.

Ezinwa is not a dealer in the predatory sense — they are, in their own understanding, a healthcare provider operating in a system that has abandoned their customers. They fill genuine prescriptions that people cannot afford through Axiom Health or Helix Biosystems, synthesize pain management compounds for workers in the Ironvein foundries, and talk people through dosing with a patience most licensed practitioners never bother with. They are also not naive: they know some of what they sell becomes something else in someone else's hands, and they live with that. They pray to the ELF they call the Still Small Voice, which inhabits a cracked spectrometer they found in a dumpster.
Properties.role: Street pharmacist and unlicensed chemist dealing in pain management, cognitive enhancers, and mood stabilizers
Properties.location: The Narrows, under the Blackpipe Corridor overpass, rotating spots
Properties.narrative_function: Medical resource for characters who cannot access corporate healthcare; source of information about what afflictions are spreading through lower-tier communities; potential ally or mission-critical contact when someone needs treatment off the grid.
Properties.augmentations: Geometric patterned irises (geneware, copper hexagons). Subdermal temperature and vitals monitor on inner left forearm (medical grade, self-installed). No other augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: being raided and having their supplies destroyed — not for themselves but for patients who will go without; causing a death through a formulation error
Properties.core_desires: to build a real underground clinic with other unlicensed practitioners; to be recognized — privately, even just by themselves — as a good healer
Properties.coping_mechanisms: meticulous note-keeping as control ritual; emotional distance maintained through clinical language even in personal situations
Properties.blind_spots: genuinely does not register how much danger they are in from corporate IP enforcement; overestimates the loyalty of the Fenders who protect them
Properties.secret: Two years ago they made a formulation error that gave a foundry worker a seizure. The worker survived and never knew, but Ezinwa has rechecked that formula every single week since. They have told no one.
Properties.story_hooks: A new compound is appearing in The Narrows that Ez cannot identify — people are coming to them with symptoms that match nothing in their database, and the source seems deliberate; Helix Biosystems has sent an IP enforcement contractor to locate whoever is synthesizing unlicensed versions of their pain management line — they are getting close to Ez; Ez needs a specific precursor chemical that has just been added to Axiom's controlled substances list — they need someone to acquire it before their current stock runs out and twenty patients go without
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal network of unlicensed medical practitioners in The Narrows; loose protection arrangement with a mid-level Narrows crew called the Oxidian Fenders
Properties.vocabulary: Technical and precise; defaults to medical terminology even in casual speech; switches to very plain, gentle language when someone is in pain
Properties.cadence: Measured and quiet; never rushes a sentence; long pauses before difficult answers
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Methylcobalamin deficiency at your tier is extremely common. I have something. It will cost you what you can spare.' | 'I'm not a doctor. I want you to understand that clearly. But I am going to help you.' | 'The Still Small Voice told me this morning the batch was clean. I trust it more than my own eyes, most days.'

Properties.description:
Ezio is young for the weight he carries — not literally, he is slight and fine-featured, with warm brown skin and close-cropped natural hair he sometimes dyes in patterns he forgets to maintain, so he often walks around with half a geometric design fading out above his ear. He has cat ears (genetic mod, a muted tawny color) that he got at seventeen because everyone was getting them and which have since become simply part of his face. They are expressive in ways he can't always control and which betray him in negotiations. He moves quickly and quietly, the particular efficiency of someone working in a very small space.

He is the most educated person most of his clients have ever interacted with and he wears that knowledge carefully, always aware of how easily expertise becomes condescension. He studied pharmacology on a Tessera corporate scholarship, finished in the top ten percent, and then declined his Tessera placement offer — an act of financial self-immolation that his family still hasn't fully forgiven. He came back to the Shelf because this is where he grew up and this is where people couldn't afford what they needed, and those two facts seemed sufficient. He is earnest about this in a way that occasionally makes people uncomfortable, because genuine selflessness is disorienting in Meridian 88. He is also, privately, somewhat overwhelmed.
Properties.role: Pharmacist and unlicensed psychiatric medication manager serving the Shelf community
Properties.location: The Shelf, a cramped pharmacy wedged between a noodle shop and a data-shrine kiosk called Careful Chemistry
Properties.narrative_function: Community resource and information node; he knows what people are struggling with, what substances are circulating in the neighborhood, and what the current unofficial street pharmacopeia looks like; potential source of discreet help; represents the Shelf's self-organizing survival systems
Properties.augmentations: Genetic cat ears (tawny, expressive, uncontrolled); basic neural chemical monitor implant (tracks his own neurotransmitter levels — he uses it to self-regulate and to better understand what his psychiatric clients describe)
Properties.core_fears: that his decision to come back was romanticism, not ethics — that he came home for the feeling of being needed rather than for the people; giving someone the wrong medication and causing permanent harm
Properties.core_desires: to see the Shelf's community health network become sustainable without depending on individual heroics; to sleep eight hours and wake up and have the work still be there, already started
Properties.coping_mechanisms: overwork as purpose-maintenance; talking to the shop E.L.F. (which he calls the Dispenser) about cases as a form of processing he doesn't recognize as processing; making elaborate tea
Properties.blind_spots: he doesn't recognize the signs of his own burnout because he knows them so well academically that he's built defenses against noticing them in himself; he gives his clients the benefit of the doubt and himself none
Properties.secret: He is still on Tessera's payroll — not as a spy or asset, but because when he turned down the placement offer, Tessera's HR system made a processing error and continued his student pharmaceutical allotment. He's been correcting the error for three years and the paperwork keeps disappearing. He uses the allotment for the clinic. He knows this is legally ambiguous at best. He has not told anyone.
Properties.story_hooks: A new substance has appeared in the Shelf and people are presenting with symptoms he doesn't recognize — he needs help identifying the source; Tessera has finally noticed the payroll error and sent someone to discuss it, and the conversation did not go the way he expected; One of his psychiatric clients stopped coming in and neighbors say she's disappeared; Ezio knows things about her mental state that make him frightened for her
Properties.affiliation: Independent (Careful Chemistry); informal consultation arrangement with two community mental health cooperatives
Properties.vocabulary: Educated but code-switches fluidly — speaks differently in consultation than he does with neighbors, and the Shelf cadence from his childhood surfaces more when he's tired or emotional
Properties.cadence: Quick and earnest, with the occasional pause when he's choosing words carefully to avoid being condescending
Properties.example_dialogue: Okay, so — the important thing is that this isn't a weakness, it's a chemistry thing, and we can work with chemistry. | I can't diagnose you. I want to be clear about that. What I can do is talk to you about what you're describing and what options exist, and you decide. | I turned down Tessera because I thought I was doing the ethical thing. Mostly I think I was. Some days I'm less sure. That's probably fine.

Properties.description:
Ezra is a retired Sterling-Nakamura logistics compliance officer who spent thirty-one years watching things get falsified and decided on year thirty-two that he was done. He is a heavyset man with the careful, deliberate physicality of someone who has learned not to take up space in ways that draw attention, a habit from corporate years that he has mostly unlearned. His skin is dark and dry at the elbows and knuckles, his hair cut close and almost entirely white. He has a single augmentation — a neural notation implant he uses compulsively to record everything, which he got for work and kept afterward. He has a cat's tail, ruddy amber, that he got on a whim at sixty and which his grandchildren love and which surprises everyone who meets him.

Ezra now serves on the Shelf Community Resource Council, a position he ran for mostly because he couldn't stop seeing the ways services were being misallocated and nobody with a ledger background was doing anything about it. He is methodical, patient, and genuinely humble in the way that people who have been wrong in consequential ways sometimes become. He spent three decades enabling a system he now spends his retirement opposing, and he carries that with a gravity that never quite lifts. He is not a firebrand. He is a man who has kept copies of everything.
Properties.role: Whistleblower and community council member
Properties.location: The Shelf
Properties.narrative_function: Archive and institutional memory; can surface specific historical data points and documented corporate malfeasance; provides grounded credibility to activist actions; his past gives him access to corporate-facing contexts others cannot reach.
Properties.augmentations: Neural notation implant (Sterling-Nakamura work model, retained after departure). Cosmetic cat tail — amber, voluntary and personal, not work-related.
Properties.core_fears: Dying before the documents he holds have served their purpose; Being used by people with agendas that harm the community he's trying to protect
Properties.core_desires: Accountability — not punishment, specifically, but acknowledgment that the harm happened; To be trusted by the Shelf community without the weight of what he used to be
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Recording and documentation as a substitute for action when action feels impossible; Cooking — specific and generative, unlike his past work
Properties.blind_spots: Overvalues documentation over lived testimony; Assumes good faith in institutional processes longer than is warranted
Properties.secret: He has a complete, authenticated copy of Sterling-Nakamura's internal models projecting displacement outcomes for Shelf residents from a planned infrastructure deal — projections that were made and then deliberately omitted from the public impact assessment. The deal hasn't been announced yet. He got the documents through a contact he burned to get them. He is waiting for the right moment to use them and is aware that waiting has costs he's paying in other people's security.
Properties.story_hooks: Ezra needs someone to physically deliver a copy of the Sterling-Nakamura displacement projections to a city arbitration body before the infrastructure deal is quietly approved — the filing window is closing and he can't be seen doing it himself; A Sterling-Nakamura investigator has appeared in the Shelf asking questions about former employees; Ezra needs to know if they're looking for him and what they know; The council is deadlocked on a resource allocation decision and Ezra has data showing one faction is receiving payments from a Tessera subsidiary — he needs help deciding how and whether to surface it without destroying the council's function
Properties.affiliation: The Shelf Community Resource Council; informal contact with Yewande Ostrčil-Falaniko's legal collective for document authentication
Properties.vocabulary: Corporate precision vocabulary that he actively works against — catches himself mid-sentence and simplifies; occasional Sotho phrases when reflective
Properties.cadence: Unhurried and thorough; rarely leaves a thought incomplete; long silences treated as normal
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I can tell you what the document says. What it means is a different question, and that one I've been wrong about before.' | 'I spent thirty years being very good at making harm look like procedure. I know what it looks like from the inside. That's the only useful thing that time gave me.'
Properties.facet_weights: wound=0.80 ideal=0.70 id=0.20 shadow=0.60 mask=0.50 ghost=0.80

Properties.description:
Ezra is a tall, slope-shouldered man running to comfortable thickness in the middle, with dark copper skin, a full black beard going silver at the chin, and close-cropped hair that is always slightly more singed at the edges than it was last week. His right hand is cybernetic from the wrist — not a prestige replacement but a working salvage prosthetic he rebuilt himself from three incompatible donor parts, and it shows: it is mismatched chrome and matte black polymer, three fingers slightly longer than the original scale, with a multitool socket in the palm he added himself. He finds it better than the original.

He has the specific personality of a man who loves his work with an intensity he cannot quite transfer to human beings. Not that he dislikes people — he likes them fine, he just relates to machines better, and machines know it. He has a reputation across Geartown for resurrecting drones and ground vehicles that any two other mechanics would have written off, and he charges less than he should and more than clients want to pay, which puts him in a permanent state of negotiation with his own finances. He is at his most relaxed covered in lubricant and at his most uncomfortable receiving compliments.
Properties.role: Auto and drone mechanic, salvage rebuilder
Properties.location: Geartown, the workshop district — specifically a half-indoor bay called 'Tamboli's' on the corner of Flue Street and Anvil Row
Properties.narrative_function: Technical resource and Geartown fixture; can repair or modify vehicles and drones, source parts through salvage networks, or assess the mechanical makeup of unusual technology. His Ferrogate contract work gives him knowledge of transit infrastructure others wouldn't have.
Properties.augmentations: Cybernetic right hand (salvage-rebuilt, self-modified; palm multitool socket). Subdermal thermal sensor in the left forearm (detects heat signatures in machinery — practical for finding faults without dismantling).
Properties.core_fears: His hands failing him before he's ready — the organic left one is showing early signs of nerve degradation he has not seen a doctor about; Building something that gets someone killed
Properties.core_desires: To completely design and build something from nothing, no salvage, all his own spec; For his apprentice to stay in Geartown instead of taking a corporate offer
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Working through problems physically — can't think sitting still; The E.L.F. practice, which he didn't start believing in but has started believing in
Properties.blind_spots: Has normalized his own physical decline because machines can be fixed and he applies the same framework to his body; Cannot tell when he is being romantically interesting to someone; genuinely baffled each time
Properties.secret: During a Ferrogate overflow contract, he discovered a structural fault in the supports beneath the Ironvein elevated track — the same section where the incident three years ago occurred. He filed a report. Nothing happened. He filed again. Nothing happened. He now knows someone at Ferrogate is sitting on both reports and doesn't know whether to escalate further or whether doing so will cost him the contract and possibly more.
Properties.story_hooks: The buried Ferrogate report is about to become relevant — the track section has degraded further and someone with the right technical knowledge is going to start asking who knew what and when; His apprentice has been offered a position at a Zheng-Dao technical facility; the offer is too good and Ezra has a bad feeling he can't articulate; A drone comes into the shop for repair that has been modified in ways that shouldn't be possible with available commercial components — and whoever left it hasn't come back to claim it
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal referral network with three other Geartown mechanics; occasional contract work for Ferrogate Transit's overflow maintenance load
Properties.vocabulary: Technical and specific; South Asian English from his father's Marathi heritage, blended with Andean Spanish-inflected phrasing from his mother's side. Uses machinery as metaphor constantly and often doesn't notice.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, even when he's behind; speaks as if he's working through the sentence while he's saying it
Properties.example_dialogue: 'She's... she's been running hot on the port side for a while, you can smell it. Nobody smelled it. You bring me something that's been ignored and then you want it fast. She needs two weeks minimum.' | 'I put in the report. I put in both reports. The track is — listen, I'm not saying it's going to fall. I'm saying I reported it. That's what I'm saying.'

Properties.description:
Fanta Ahlstrom-Quartey is stocky and solid, with hands that look like they were built for breaking things and a face that confirms it. At 43, the augmentation scarring around her temples and jawline tells a story of installation by someone who prioritized function over aesthetics. The chrome is visible — chemical analyzer in nasal passages — can identify substances by scent alone — and she makes no effort to hide it.

Military training — one of the private security corps that folded during the consolidation wars — left her with skills and night terrors in equal measure. She works as a broker out of Burnside Corridor, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

she is not the most talented broker in Meridian 88, but she might be the most stubborn, and in this city that's worth more.
Properties.role: Information trader and intelligence analyst — broker
Properties.location: Burnside Corridor — transit hub connecting Shelf to Circuit
Properties.narrative_function: Fanta Ahlstrom-Quartey represents the working professional of the runner world — competent, reliable, and slowly being consumed by a lifestyle that doesn't accommodate aging or doubt. Her stories explore what happens when skill meets systemic injustice.
Properties.augmentations: Chemical analyzer in nasal passages — can identify substances by scent alone. Move-by-wire system — full nervous system augmentation, makes the body a weapon platform
Properties.core_fears: Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome; Going cyberpsycho — losing the boundary between human and machine; Being identified by corporate facial recognition — living off-grid is survival
Properties.core_desires: To find the person who burned them and make it educational; A crew worth trusting — people who stay when the shooting starts; The perfect run — one job so clean it becomes legend
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Isolates — retreats into their space when overwhelmed, emerges only for work; Exercises compulsively — the body must be ready, always; Ritual — follows the same pre-job routine every time, superstition as structure
Properties.blind_spots: Thinks speed can substitute for planning because it's worked so far; Trusts technology more than people — machines don't betray; Overestimates their own abilities in situations outside their specialty
Properties.secret: Fanta Ahlstrom-Quartey betrayed their previous crew to survive a corporate raid. The crew didn't survive. Nobody in Meridian 88 knows this.
Properties.story_hooks: Fanta Ahlstrom-Quartey is offered a contract that would clear all their debts — the target is someone they respect; Fanta Ahlstrom-Quartey's augmentations begin malfunctioning in the field — sabotage or degradation, and either answer is bad; Fanta Ahlstrom-Quartey intercepts intelligence about a threat to their district and must decide between profit and protection
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated — too volatile for permanent crews
Properties.vocabulary: Warm and personable on the surface, with an undertone that suggests the warmth is a professional tool.
Properties.cadence: Halting — speaks in fragments, reassembles thoughts in real time.
Properties.example_dialogue: "I don't sell information. I sell certainty. Different product, different price." | "Everything has a value. Most people underestimate what they know." | "My sources are confidential. My prices are not."
Properties.facet_weights: wound=0.39 ideal=0.73 id=0.59 shadow=0.71 mask=0.95 ghost=0.19

Properties.description:
Fanta Dahlberg-Boakye is stocky and solid, with hands that look like they were built for breaking things and a face that confirms it. At 30, her face is memorable in a profession that rewards forgettability, and she has learned to compensate. The chrome is visible — dermal camouflage — chromatic skin pigment cells, limited active camouflage — and she makes no effort to hide it.

She inherited the role from a mentor who disappeared on a job four years ago — the mentor's gear, contacts, and unfinished business all came with it. She works as a ghost out of Ashfield, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

In a city full of people who talk about what they'll do, Fanta Dahlberg-Boakye is one of the ones who actually does it.
Properties.role: Precision elimination specialist — ghost
Properties.location: Ashfield — former residential district, half-burned, now squatter territory
Properties.narrative_function: As a ghost, Fanta Dahlberg-Boakye embodies the tension between independence and isolation. She is a lens for examining how people maintain humanity in a profession that incentivizes its erosion.
Properties.augmentations: Dermal camouflage — chromatic skin pigment cells, limited active camouflage. Cortical bomb (employer installed, removed by street doc, scar tissue remains)
Properties.core_fears: Their past catching up — debts, enemies, broken promises; Being replaced — younger, faster, cheaper runners coming up behind them; Being identified by corporate facial recognition — living off-grid is survival
Properties.core_desires: To build something that outlasts the next contract cycle; Power — enough leverage that nobody ever threatens them again; Enough Quanta to buy out of the life — a clean identity and passage out of Meridian 88
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring; Ritual — follows the same pre-job routine every time, superstition as structure; Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation
Properties.blind_spots: Mistakes loyalty for weakness in others and cynicism for strength in themselves; Trusts technology more than people — machines don't betray; Overestimates their own abilities in situations outside their specialty

Properties.description:
Fanta has the compact build of someone who has spent decades at close, fine work — slightly rounded shoulders, strong hands, a habitual squint that has become permanent even when she isn't looking at anything. Her mother's Guinean-Fula heritage is visible in her height (modest) and the warm reddish-brown undertone of her dark skin; her father's Chechen-Chilean blood gave her sharply defined brow ridges and the family talent for geometry. She wears cat ears — tabby-patterned, twitching occasionally with genuine feline cartilage — which she got at age twenty-two because she thought they would help her blend in, and she was right. She also dyes her natural locs in gradient shifts from black to deep copper, redone every three weeks with obsessive precision.

Fanta is an artist who makes functional things. She forges identities, histories, corponation employment records, medical credentials, Tier verification stamps, citizenship documentation for people who have none or need to become someone else entirely. Her work is technically flawless. The locs, the cat ears, the warm print shop downstairs — all of it is camouflage over a person who has spent fifteen years curating other people's fictional lives while her own has stayed very small. She is funny in a dry, almost-apologetic way that makes people feel witty by proximity. She charges on a sliding scale she will deny having.
Properties.role: identity forger and document fabricator
Properties.location: Ashfeld, above a legitimate print-restoration shop called Palimpsest on a narrow commerce row
Properties.narrative_function: Critical service provider for any character needing new identity or documentation; long-term information asset who knows secrets about everyone she has ever given a new face to; can become a target if one of her clients is found out
Properties.augmentations: Cat ears (tabby-patterned, geneware, genuine cartilage and muscle response); micro-focus ocular implants for detailed work; color-shifting hair (dye-assist nano-pigment, not full geneware)
Properties.core_fears: being erased the way she erases others — leaving no trace; that the authentic version of herself has atrophied beyond recovery
Properties.core_desires: to make one thing that is purely, undisguisedly hers; freedom of movement without consequence — she has never been able to travel under her own name
Properties.coping_mechanisms: the print restoration work is genuinely therapeutic — fixing the real while she fabricates the false; obsessive physical maintenance of her appearance as proof of self
Properties.blind_spots: assumes everyone wants the same freedom from identity that she secretly craves; underestimates how much her clients' new identities can bleed back to her
Properties.secret: She has made herself seven complete backup identities across seven different Tier levels, two of which have more documented life history than her real one. She updates them regularly. She has never had to use any of them and considers them her greatest ongoing artwork.
Properties.story_hooks: One of her client identities has been flagged by a Tessera internal security system — the client is now dead, but the investigation is working backward toward the forger; Someone has come to her requesting a document she recognizes: the exact template she uses for her own backup identities, which means someone knows her system from the inside
Properties.affiliation: Independent; has referral relationships with three separate criminal networks but belongs to none of them — deliberate policy
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and technical when discussing craft, casually warm otherwise; uses Fulani-derived endearments with people she likes; refers to documents as 'portraits'
Properties.cadence: Even and slightly amused, as if she can see two steps ahead of most conversations
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't make fakes. I make better-documented truths. The distinction matters professionally and philosophically.' | 'You want a full portrait or just a touch-up? Because I charge differently, and you look like someone who needs the full portrait but will ask for the touch-up price.'

Properties.description:
Fanta Dzhuraev-Mboyo is small even for nine, with a round face, dark skin dusted lighter along the cheekbones from a nutritional deficiency that went untreated too long, and enormous amber eyes that their apprentice-master suspects are natural but can never quite confirm. They keep their hair in two puffs held with mismatched elastics. Their fingers are already remarkable — long, precise, slightly calloused at the tips from needle and thread work — and they move them constantly, picking at hems, testing fabric tension, tying knots and undoing them while they talk.

Fanta came to Grantha Soto-Edelweiss's repair stall after spending eight months in a Brightmoor Reclamation group shelter following a building collapse that killed their parents. The shelter social worker placed them as a household-and-shop apprentice, which in practice means Fanta sweeps, fetches, and mends in exchange for a sleeping mat behind the stall divider, two meals, and fifteen minutes of formal reading instruction each day from Grantha's tablet. They are not unhappy. They are careful about happiness — they learned early it tends to leave. But they love the work with a devotion that is almost physical, and they have a gift that their apprentice-master has started to notice is more than ordinary.
Properties.role: Orphan and apprentice to a garment repairer in the Stockyard
Properties.location: The Stockyard (specifically the repair stall row near Grainfort)
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and emotional anchor; represents the most vulnerable tier of the city's civilian population; potential long-term storyline about what happens to gifted children in tier-one conditions; can connect players to the Stockyard repair community.
Properties.augmentations: None
Properties.core_fears: The stall closing and having nowhere to go; Forgetting what their parents looked like
Properties.core_desires: To make something so well-made it lasts a hundred years; To be someone's first choice, not their available option
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Focuses intensely on tactile work when distressed — mending things is mending things; Narrates mundane tasks aloud quietly, as if explaining them to their parents
Properties.blind_spots: Does not recognize exploitation when it wears a benevolent face — they are grateful for the apprenticeship in ways that make them accept conditions that are genuinely unfair; Assumes adults who are kind to them have good reasons for everything they do
Properties.secret: They found a small silver locket in the ruins after the building collapse and have kept it, not knowing whose it is. It has an image inside that they don't recognize. They have never shown it to anyone. They pray to the E.L.F. of Lost Things (a small improvised shrine in the shelter, which they still visit) to eventually tell them who it belongs to.
Properties.story_hooks: The locket they found in the ruins belongs to someone who is now looking for it — and the building collapse that killed Fanta's parents was not an accident; A Helix Biosystems talent scout has noticed Fanta's extraordinary fine motor precision and is trying to determine if it's genetic — they haven't approached the child directly yet, but they've been asking Grantha questions
Properties.affiliation: Grantha Soto-Edelweiss (apprentice-master), Brightmoor Reclamation group shelter (former ward)
Properties.vocabulary: Simple and concrete; names materials and textures specifically; uses the present tense even for past events
Properties.cadence: Quiet, even, unhurried — slightly dreamy; pauses occur at unexpected places in sentences
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I think this seam wants to come apart. It's been wanting to for a while — I can feel it.' | 'Grantha says I have good hands. I think she means it. She doesn't say things she doesn't mean.'

Properties.description:
Fanta is a big woman, wide through the shoulders and unhurried in every movement, with dark skin and close-cropped natural hair going silver at the temples. She has no cosmetic geneware — considers it wasteful — but her left forearm is sheathed in functional chrome from wrist to elbow, a prosthetic she received after an industrial accident fifteen years ago. She keeps it polished to a mirror shine, the one vanity she permits herself. Her face is deeply expressive, capable of communicating entire paragraphs of displeasure through a single lifted brow.

Fanta has managed Block 7 for eleven years and knows every pipe, every tenant, and every leak before it happens. She is the closest thing to a government most residents will ever interact with — she mediates disputes, facilitates unofficial rent negotiations, holds keys to every unit, and knows who is three months behind and who is running an unlicensed business out of their kitchen. She is fair to a degree that exhausts her and does not apologize for any of her decisions.
Properties.role: Building superintendent for a mid-tier residential block
Properties.location: Lockhaven North, Block 7 — a twelve-story residential stack owned by a Palladian property sub-entity
Properties.narrative_function: Gateway to the residential community of Lockhaven North — controls access, knows everyone's business. Can be a quest giver, a gatekeeper, a source of information about specific tenants, or an obstacle. Represents institutional power at human scale.
Properties.augmentations: Chrome prosthetic left forearm (functional, utility-grade, high polish). Internal pressure and temperature sensors in the prosthetic hand for plumbing diagnostics.
Properties.core_fears: Palladian terminating her contract and leaving the building to a remote management system; one of her tenants dying of something she could have prevented
Properties.core_desires: for Block 7 to function as a genuine community, not just a revenue asset; to retire knowing the building is in good hands
Properties.coping_mechanisms: physical labor as emotional regulation; maintaining strict routines as a bulwark against chaos
Properties.blind_spots: her authority in the building has become so total she cannot see when she is overstepping — she believes she always knows best
Properties.secret: She has been quietly subsidizing three families' rent shortfalls out of her own wages for two years, recording them as maintenance cost overruns in Palladian's system. The discrepancy is approaching a threshold that will trigger an audit.
Properties.story_hooks: A tenant in unit 9-F has stopped answering the door for eleven days — Fanta is two decisions away from using her master key and needs someone else to make the call for her; The Palladian audit is coming and she needs someone to help her quietly restructure four years of falsified maintenance records before an inspector arrives
Properties.affiliation: Palladian (property subsidiary, Lockhaven North management contract); functionally independent in daily operation
Properties.vocabulary: Direct and institutional, carries the cadence of someone who has read too many maintenance contracts. Occasionally drops into Bambara when frustrated.
Properties.cadence: Slow and weighted — every sentence arrives like a decision that's already been made.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You have a noise complaint. I have seventeen noise complaints. Yours is noted.' | 'Palladian owns the walls. I run what's inside them. There is a difference and you will respect it.'

Properties.description:
Fatoumata is a small, round woman who has been small and round for as long as anyone in Irkalla can remember, though she was apparently quite tall in photographs from her forties and nobody can fully account for this. Her skin is very dark and very smooth in a way that no longer has a natural explanation, though she is dismissive of questions about it. Her hair is natural and silver-white, kept in a high crown wrap of deep indigo cloth. She has cat ears — small, dark-tipped, mobile — that she got at forty-five after a dream she refuses to describe. They swivel constantly, tracking sound, giving her the air of someone who is always listening to two conversations at once.

Fatoumata holds the dying. This is the entire description of her work, and it requires everything. She sits with people in their last hours, facilitates the rituals their families have lost the words to, and manages the terrifying administrative machinery of death in Meridian 88 — the Ferrogate Transit body transit permits, the Helix Biosystems harvesting opt-out paperwork, the Axiom data-legacy protocols. She has done this for forty years. She is simultaneously the most comforting and most disconcerting person in any room, because she has no fear of the subject that frightens everyone else most.

Properties.location: Irkalla — a residential stack in the lower levels near the Gravesend Basin
Properties.narrative_function: Emotional anchor and community historian; knows every family in Irkalla and their losses; can provide context on anyone who has died in the area; may need help navigating corporate interference with traditional burial practices
Properties.augmentations: Cat ears (cosmetic geneware, dark-tipped, highly mobile), unspecified skin treatment (she calls it 'a courtesy to the dying — they don't need to watch me decay in front of them')
Properties.core_fears: Dying alone, without a death midwife, in a corporate facility — the exact death she has spent forty years preventing for others; That the archive of last words she keeps will be seized and monetized
Properties.core_desires: For death to be returned to communities rather than managed by corponations; To find someone willing and capable of taking over her work before she needs it herself
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor — specifically jokes about death, which she deploys without apology and which land oddly with people who haven't known her long; The routine of the death songs keeps grief moving rather than pooling
Properties.blind_spots: She tends to assume everyone finds death as speakable as she does and sometimes misjudges timing with the recently bereaved; She has been so focused on other people's deaths that she has done very little of her own life-planning
Properties.secret: The archive of last words contains three recordings that she has never transcribed and never played back after the initial sitting — things said at the deathbed of a Tessera mid-tier executive who died in Irkalla under circumstances she was asked to keep quiet. She kept quiet. She kept the recordings. She has not decided what to do with them and may run out of time.
Properties.story_hooks: The three recordings in the archive have become relevant — whatever the Tessera executive knew is now being looked for by someone who knows it exists but not where it is; A new Helix Biosystems initiative would legally reclassify death midwifery as unlicensed medical practice, and Fatoumata needs help navigating the challenge before she is fined into silence

Properties.description:
Fatou Bergkvist-Nakashima is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin gone ashy at the temples, her hair kept in a tight silver-flecked wrap she changes weekly — practical, never decorative. Her hands are perpetually reddened from industrial solvents, knuckles enlarged from thirty years of pressing and threading. She has the single cosmetic augmentation she's ever allowed herself: patterned irises in a woven indigo-and-cream design she chose the week her youngest left for a Tessera dormitory scholarship. She called it a goodbye gift to herself.

Fatou runs Suds & Seams with the efficiency of a woman who has never once had the luxury of inefficiency. She does not chat while she works. She does not chat while she doesn't work. But she watches everything — who comes in with bloodstained sleeves and asks no questions, who cries in the plastic chair by the dryers, who stuffs a garment to the bottom of their bag before placing it on the counter. She keeps these observations to herself, filing them like receipts. She is not unkind; she simply measures kindness the way she measures detergent — enough for the purpose, never wasted.

Properties.description:
Faustin is a tall man gone slightly stooped with age, with a long, deeply lined face the color of dark walnut and close-cropped silver hair. He wears reading glasses with one cracked lens that he has refused to replace for reasons he won't fully explain, and his fingers are permanently ink-stained from a printer he still operates by hand. His stall in the Alban Souk is an organized labyrinth — physical media stacked in towers that somehow have internal logic only he can navigate, data-chips in labeled trays, printed zines in weathered portfolios, bootleg entertainment feeds on a slow-scroll display board behind him. He smells of old plastics, hot electronics, and a tobacco substitute he has smoked for forty years.

Faustin does not move quickly and he does not need to. He has been in this spot, or a spot within fifty meters of this spot, for twenty-six years. He speaks with the careful economy of someone who has decided that most conversations don't require more than a hundred words, but when he talks about something he loves — old cinema, pre-Corponation literature, the acoustic properties of physical music formats — he becomes a completely different person, voluble and precise and slightly alarming in his enthusiasm. He knows what data passes through the Souk before almost anyone else does. He sells most of it. He keeps some of it. Nobody is quite sure which is which.
Properties.role: Bootleg media seller and small-time data broker
Properties.location: The Alban Souk, Hamtramck Enclave
Properties.narrative_function: Information broker, cultural repository, and reflective background presence. Characters who need data, obscure pre-Corponation records, or someone who remembers what the city looked like before come to Faustin. He's also the most reliable source for understanding context — what an event means, what it echoes from the past.
Properties.augmentations: Retinal display overlay — old model, first generation, occasionally glitches. Memory-index augmentation — helps him catalogue and retrieve his inventory; he also uses it for everything else. Nothing cosmetic.
Properties.core_fears: Becoming irrelevant — a curiosity rather than a resource; The total disappearance of physical media and the histories they carry
Properties.core_desires: To keep knowledge alive that corporations would prefer be forgotten; To find one person worth passing his archive to
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Retreats into cataloguing and organization when emotionally overwhelmed; Uses historical analogy to distance himself from present pain
Properties.blind_spots: Romanticizes the past in ways that occasionally distort his reading of the present; His caution about sharing certain data sometimes shades into hoarding — he tells himself it's protective
Properties.secret: He holds a partial archive of pre-corporate land records for Hamtramck and three adjacent zones — documentation that could legally complicate several Corponation territorial claims. He received it from a dying archivist twenty years ago. He has never shown it to anyone. He believes that information this significant is also a death warrant for whoever holds it, and he cannot decide if that means he should destroy it, share it, or keep it safe until the right moment arrives.
Properties.story_hooks: He has identified a data-chip in a recent shipment that was clearly not intended for open sale — it came with a specific zine order from a supply contact who has since stopped responding to communications.; Someone has visited the stall twice asking, very casually, whether he carries historical land records. They didn't buy anything. He needs to know who sent them.; A young community organizer in Hamtramck has been researching corporate land claims and has gotten close enough to the truth that Faustin thinks she'll either find the archive independently or get hurt looking. He is considering whether to make contact.

Properties.cadence: Slow and considered. Long pauses between thoughts that do not feel like hesitation — more like he's selecting carefully. Will not be rushed.

It ended badly for the man who knew too much and well for the man who knew how to forget. I've always found that instructive.' | 'Naturally, I have what you're looking for. Whether I should sell it to you is a different question, and it will take a moment.'

Properties.description:
Félix is slight and short, with warm medium-brown skin and a mass of dark curly hair they keep shoved under a battered synthetic-fiber cap from a Ferrogate Transit promotional campaign three years ago. They have a geneware cat tail — warm brown, slightly darker at the tip — that they got at age fifteen from a Tier 1 parlor using credit they spent six months saving, and which they maintain with the kind of care that signals it is very important to them. Their face is young in a way that gets them underestimated constantly, which they have learned to treat as a professional asset. They have three earrings in the left ear, each from a different city they have passed through.

Félix has been riding cargo airships since they were sixteen, starting as an unauthorized stowaway, then graduating to informal deckhand labor when a captain named Ambrosia decided their small hands were useful for engine housing maintenance. They have no fixed address, no registered domicile, and no particular destination at any given time. They are relentlessly cheerful in a way that is not performative — they genuinely find the itinerant life exhilarating — and have a gift for making friends in every transit hub within four hundred kilometers. They are also an extremely reliable courier for small packages that cannot go through official channels, not because they are ideologically committed to any cause but because the pay is good and the work suits someone who is going everywhere anyway.
Properties.role: airship drifter; seasonal cargo deckhand and petty courier
Properties.location: Escanaba Gateway, airship mooring platform C
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile information conduit — knows something about everywhere and everyone in the transit network; can serve as a courier or guide; brings news from other locations; humanizes the drifter experience
Properties.augmentations: Brown cat tail with darker tip (geneware cosmetic, beloved). No other mods.
Properties.core_fears: being grounded — physically, legally, or emotionally; becoming someone who stops moving and loses themselves
Properties.core_desires: to see the full extent of Meridian 88's outer territories by airship; a crew that actually wants them, not just their small hands
Properties.coping_mechanisms: movement — when emotionally uncomfortable, they find a reason to travel; humor and sociability as genuine first response to almost everything
Properties.blind_spots: consistently underestimates the danger of the packages they courier — tells themselves it's not their business what's inside; their cheerfulness causes people to disclose things to them they shouldn't, and Félix does not always understand the weight of what they're holding
Properties.secret: Six months ago they couriered a package from Kenosha Crossing to a contact in Ironvein that they later learned contained biometric data stolen from a Helix Biosystems facility. They do not know whose data. They have been trying to forget about it but cannot, because one of the earrings in their left ear was payment from that job, and they keep touching it.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone has been asking about a courier who made a specific Kenosha-to-Ironvein run six months ago, and transit hub gossip has flagged Félix's name; One of their airship captain contacts has missed two scheduled departures with no communication — Félix is worried but has no resources to investigate; They are carrying a package currently, mid-layover, and the pickup contact at the destination has sent a message saying 'don't come' with no further explanation
Properties.affiliation: Loose affiliation with three or four cargo airship crews who use them as a seasonal deckhand; occasional courier work for whoever pays
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, colloquial, heavy with transit slang and airship crew terminology. Enthusiastic. Asks a lot of questions.
Properties.cadence: Quick, runs sentences together, rarely pauses mid-thought.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Honestly the Escanaba-to-Lambeau run is my favorite, the thermals are incredible and Captain Seun doesn't check the hammock rig until morning, yeah?' | 'I'm not saying it was a weird package, I'm just saying it was warm and it shouldn't have been. Anyway. Honestly. What's the job?'

Properties.description:
Felix Drum is the Quiet Table's hands in the physical world. When information needs to be collected in person, when dead drops need servicing, when a meeting requires the implicit suggestion that non-cooperation would be unwise — Felix handles it. He is not muscle in the traditional sense. He is presence. The kind of calm, attentive, well-dressed man who makes you want to cooperate because the alternative seems profoundly unappealing without him ever specifying why.

Before the Quiet Table, Felix spent twenty years in private security — first for corporate executives, then for politicians, then for people who existed in the space between those categories. He was very good at keeping people alive. He was less good at caring about whether they deserved to be alive. The moral vacancy started small and grew until he walked away from a client who was using his protection to facilitate human trafficking. He reported the client to the authorities. Nothing happened. He reported the client to someone else. Something happened. That was the last year of his legitimate career.

Felix is average height, solidly built without being imposing, with the kind of face that belongs in a crowd — pleasant, forgettable, professional. He keeps his hair short, his clothes clean, and his posture perfect. The only augmentation anyone notices is a slight heaviness to his handshake — the reinforced bones in his hands and forearms are subtle but present. Everything else is hidden, maintained, and ready.
Properties.role: Field operative and physical security — The Quiet Table
Properties.location: The Circuit — maintains a modest apartment with no personal effects and exceptional sight lines
Properties.narrative_function: Felix bridges the Quiet Table's intellectual world and the physical reality of M88's streets. His stories explore the weight of being the person who does the dangerous part of someone else's plan, and the moral complexity of a man who chose conscience late in life and is still figuring out what that means. He is the political thriller's action element — measured, competent, carrying more violence in reserve than he ever deploys.
Properties.augmentations: Reinforced skeletal structure in hands, forearms, and ribcage — impact-resistant without bulk. Adrenal regulator that prevents panic responses and maintains steady heart rate under threat. Optical threat-assessment overlay (low-profile, passive) — highlights weapons, augmentations, and stress indicators in his visual field. Subvocal communicator linked to Glass and Noor.
Properties.core_fears: That his capacity for violence is more fundamental than his conscience — that the years of moral vacancy were the real him; That the man he reported is still operating and the something that happened wasn't enough; That Glass and Noor see him as a tool rather than a colleague — useful but not respected
Properties.core_desires: To prove that choosing right late is still choosing right — that the course correction counts; To protect people who deserve protection, for reasons he believes in, not just for pay; To be trusted with the full picture, not just the parts that require his physical presence
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Maintains rigid routine as a framework for a life that used to have none; Reads crime fiction because the genre provides clear moral resolution that reality doesn't; Channels his capacity for violence into precise, measured physical readiness rather than suppressing it
Properties.blind_spots: His composure is so complete that people assume he doesn't feel things strongly — he does, he just processes it in the apartment, alone, after the fact; He conflates being useful with being valued and cannot tell the difference; His late-life moral awakening has an element of self-punishment — he takes the dangerous assignments partly as penance
Properties.secret: The client he reported — the human trafficker — was never prosecuted. Felix contacted a runner crew to handle it. The client disappeared. Felix does not know if the client was extracted, imprisoned, or killed. He has chosen not to find out because all three answers are complicated.
Properties.story_hooks: The former client resurfaces — alive, connected, and aware that Felix was responsible for his disappearance; A field operation puts Felix in contact with Kyle — two men with different kinds of violence recognizing each other; Noor's analysis sends Felix into a situation more dangerous than the data predicted, forcing a reckoning about trust and information; Glass asks Felix to do something morally ambiguous — the first test of whether the Quiet Table is different from Felix's previous employers
Properties.affiliation: The Quiet Table
Properties.vocabulary: Clean, professional, slightly formal. Security industry diction — 'secure,' 'principal,' 'threat posture.' Deliberately inexpressive.
Properties.cadence: Even, unhurried. He speaks at the same pace regardless of circumstances. The steadiness is both calming and, in certain contexts, deeply unsettling.
Properties.example_dialogue: Understood. I'll handle the physical side. | I'm suggesting that this meeting go well for everyone. I'm not insisting. Yet. | I read crime novels because the detective always solves it. That's not how the real world works, but it's nice to visit.

Properties.description:
Glass Maren has been trading information in Meridian 88 for longer than most runners have been alive. He started as a corporate intelligence analyst for a pharmaceutical conglomerate that no longer exists — consumed by Veridian Health Sciences in the consolidation wave of the 2180s. When the acquisition happened, Glass walked away with two things: his contact network and an understanding that information only has value if you control its context.

He built The Quiet Table over twenty years — a three-person operation that competes with Sable's network by occupying a different ecological niche. Where Sable trades in urgent, operational intelligence — who's doing what right now — the Quiet Table trades in deep context. History. Relationships. The slow-moving currents that determine which corporations will merge, which jurisdictions will shift, which politicians will fall. Their clients are patient people who plan in years, not hours.

Glass is tall, thin, with a face that has weathered into distinguished rather than old. Silver hair, clean-shaven, clothes that are twenty years out of fashion and perfectly maintained. He moves slowly because speed is for people who haven't planned far enough ahead. His voice is the kind of quiet that makes other people lean in. He has never raised it in public. He has never needed to.
Properties.aliases: The Librarian, Old Glass, Quiet Table Lead
Properties.role: Lead information broker and network curator — The Quiet Table
Properties.location: The Circuit — operates from a private booth in a members-only tea house called The Leaf
Properties.narrative_function: Glass is the long game personified. His stories are political thrillers where the stakes are measured in influence rather than blood. He represents the intelligence world that exists above the street level — the slow, patient, devastating maneuvering that determines which streets exist at all. His competition with Sable adds texture to the information economy of M88.
Properties.augmentations: Eidetic memory cortex (early-generation, pharmaceutical-grade) — perfect recall of conversations, documents, and spatial layouts. The implant is thirty years old and beginning to develop minor retrieval artifacts. Cochlear enhancement for directional audio filtering — he can isolate a single conversation in a crowded room. No visible augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: That his memory is beginning to fail — the eidetic cortex artifacts are small but growing; That the world has accelerated past the pace at which deep intelligence matters; That the information he's collected over three decades makes him a target no security arrangement can protect against
Properties.core_desires: To understand the full picture — the complete network of power in M88 — before his memory degrades beyond reliability; To protect the two people who trust him enough to work alongside him; To be remembered as someone who understood how things worked, not just someone who sold that understanding
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Maintains rigid daily routines to compensate for the uncertainty of aging cognition; Controls conversations rather than participating in them — the one asking questions never has to answer; Archives everything because the external record protects against the internal decay
Properties.blind_spots: His patience reads as arrogance to people who operate on shorter timescales; He underestimates physical threats because his world is informational — he has not been in danger of violence in years; He cannot distinguish between protecting his crew and controlling them
Properties.secret: He has a complete dossier on every major power player in Meridian 88 — including Sable. It is stored in his physical archive. If released, it would destabilize the city's power structure. He has never decided whether it is a weapon, an insurance policy, or an obituary.
Properties.story_hooks: The eidetic cortex begins failing in noticeable ways — Glass forgets a name, a date, a connection. The archive becomes his lifeline and his vulnerability.; A client requests information from the dossier collection — someone knows it exists; A Quiet Table analysis correctly predicts a major corporate merger, making Glass simultaneously valuable and dangerous to every party involved; Sable approaches Glass with a proposal: merge operations against a common threat. The political thriller becomes a trust exercise.
Properties.affiliation: The Quiet Table
Properties.vocabulary: Elevated, precise, occasionally archaic. He uses words the way a jeweler uses tools — each one selected for exact purpose.
Properties.cadence: Slow, deliberate. Long pauses between sentences. Questions that are really statements. Statements that are really questions.
Properties.example_dialogue: Consider — if they wanted you to know, they would not have buried it in a subsidiary filing. | Interesting. You believe that because someone arranged for you to believe it. | The record is patient. The record outlasts everyone who tries to edit it.

Properties.description:
Noor Farouk was supposed to be an academic. She had the doctorate — computational sociology, focused on network dynamics in post-governance urban systems — and the tenure-track position at a Circuit university that barely exists anymore. When the university's funding collapsed under corporate pressure (the research was getting inconvenient for certain interests), Noor found herself with a brilliant analytical mind, a mortgage, and no institutional home. Glass Maren found her six months later, teaching statistics to bored corporate trainees for subsistence pay.

She is the engine that turns Glass's raw intelligence into actionable product. Where Glass collects — conversations, documents, observations — Noor connects. She maps relationships between corporations, between individuals, between events separated by years and jurisdictions. She sees patterns the way musicians hear harmonies — not the individual notes, but the structure that makes them mean something.

Noor is compact, sharp-featured, with dark hair streaked silver at the temples — premature, stress-related, and she's stopped caring. She wears reading glasses she doesn't technically need anymore (the optical augmentation handles it) because the glasses were her mother's and putting them on means it's time to work. Her workspace is a controlled chaos of screens, physical notes, and string-and-pin boards that she insists work better than any digital mapping tool.
Properties.role: Intelligence analyst and pattern specialist — The Quiet Table
Properties.location: The Circuit — maintains a small apartment above a data-repair shop that doubles as her analytical workspace
Properties.narrative_function: Noor is the intellectual heart of the Quiet Table — the character who sees the patterns that drive the political thriller plots. Her stories explore the burden of understanding systems that are designed to be invisible, and the loneliness of seeing connections that other people can't. She is the analyst who knows too much and must decide what to do with it.
Properties.augmentations: Pattern-recognition cortex enhancement — accelerates her natural ability to identify connections between data points. Optical augmentation with variable zoom and light-spectrum filtering for document analysis. Subdermal data-storage implant in her left forearm — encrypted, air-gapped, containing her most sensitive analytical models.
Properties.core_fears: That the patterns she sees are artifacts of her own paranoia rather than reality — that she's finding signal in noise; That the academic career she lost was the only version of her life that would have been meaningful; That Glass is using her analytical gifts the way the university used her research — extracting value without reciprocal honesty
Properties.core_desires: To understand the complete network — to see the full picture of how power operates in M88; To publish her work. Not sell it — publish it. Make the invisible structures visible to everyone.; To be recognized as an intellectual equal by Glass, not a talented subordinate
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Retreats into analytical work when emotions become complicated — the patterns are clean even when people aren't; Maintains her mother's reading glasses as a ritual object — putting them on is entering the workspace, taking them off is leaving it; Builds independent contacts outside Glass's network as a hedge against dependency
Properties.blind_spots: Her analytical brilliance makes her overconfident in her ability to predict human behavior, which is messier than systems; She intellectualizes emotional problems until the emotional content disappears, which means they never actually resolve; She is building an independent network but hasn't decided whether it's professional growth or preparation for betrayal
Properties.secret: She has been writing a book — a comprehensive analysis of Meridian 88's power structure. It uses anonymized data from the Quiet Table's operations. If Glass found out, he would consider it a security breach. Noor considers it the most important work she has ever done.
Properties.story_hooks: Noor's analysis predicts a corporate action before it happens — someone notices and wants to know how; The book nears completion and Noor must decide whether to publish, hide it, or show it to Glass; A former academic colleague approaches the Quiet Table as a client, bringing Noor's two worlds face to face; Her pattern-recognition cortex begins generating false positives — she starts seeing connections that aren't there
Properties.affiliation: The Quiet Table
Properties.vocabulary: Academic, precise, peppered with analytical jargon. She speaks in frameworks and models. Can translate to plain language when she remembers to.
Properties.cadence: Rapid when excited about a pattern, measured when presenting conclusions. She builds arguments the way she builds analyses — evidence first, interpretation second.
Properties.example_dialogue: The data suggests this merger isn't a merger. It's an acquisition disguised as a partnership, and the timeline tells you who's holding the knife. | So here's the interesting part — they've been moving money through the same shell company for nine years. Nobody does that by accident. | I don't have opinions. I have analyses. The analysis says we're looking at this wrong.

Properties.description:
Fenwick is a lean, unhurried man of medium height with deep umber skin and close-cropped hair that he keeps dyed a matte rust-red. He has a bioluminescent mod along his forearms — thin lines of blue-white light under the skin that pulse gently with his heartbeat, which he originally got because it helped him keep time when cooking stock. He wears the same canvas apron every day, bleached and re-stained so many times it has developed a geological stratigraphy of meals past. His cart, 'The Long Burn,' is a retrofitted maintenance vehicle he rebuilt himself over eighteen months, and he knows its every rattle and squeak as personally as a language.

Fenwick moves through the world with a quality of stillness that some people mistake for slowness and others, correctly, read as patience. He is not a talker — his cart is not a place for conversation so much as a place for eating — but he notices everything: who looks hungry versus broke, who's been crying, who's scanning the crowd too carefully. He keeps a small E.L.F. shrine rigged into the cart's boiler panel, a data-spirit he calls 'the Pilot Light' to whom he murmurs thanks each morning before ignition.
Properties.role: Noodle cart vendor, Edison Grid district
Properties.location: Edison Grid, corner of Copper Row and the 14th underpass
Properties.narrative_function: Reliable scene-setting presence; a node of quiet observation in a busy district. Information source who never seems like one — people talk near his cart as if he's furniture. Can point players toward things he's witnessed without ever seeming to inform.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent subdermal lines on forearms (blue-white, heartbeat-synced). No other mods.
Properties.core_fears: His daughter growing up not knowing him; The cart being impounded or destroyed — losing the one thing he built from nothing
Properties.core_desires: Stability — a day that goes as planned; Being the kind of father his own wasn't
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The ritual of cooking as a way to feel in control; Emotional withdrawal — going quiet rather than engaging conflict
Properties.blind_spots: Believes being present physically is the same as being emotionally available; Underestimates how much his silences communicate
Properties.secret: He witnessed a Axiom security officer disposing of something in the underpass canal eight months ago and has said nothing. He told himself it wasn't his business. He's been telling himself that for eight months.
Properties.story_hooks: Whatever Fenwick saw in the underpass canal is now relevant ��� someone is asking around the Edison Grid, and his regulars are starting to notice; His daughter has gone quiet and he can't reach her; he'll ask someone he trusts from the cart — obliquely, carefully — to check on her
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal supplier relationship with Grainfort wholesale district
Properties.vocabulary: Minimal, functional, with occasional bursts of unexpected precision about food, temperature, or timing
Properties.cadence: Slow and considered — he doesn't fill silences
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Broth's been going since four. You can taste it.' | 'I don't know what you saw. I was cooking.'

Properties.description:
Rector Hollowell is a large man gone soft at the edges, with the posture of someone who once commanded rooms and has since chosen not to. His skin is the pale ochre of long indoor living, his hands enormous and steady, his white hair kept short and his beard grown out in the way of a man who has stopped performing for an audience that no longer exists. He wears the same rotation of practical clothes—heavy canvas, worn but clean—and carries a battered medical kit that is more capable than it looks because he has modified it himself over eleven years of field use in The Shelf.

Rector spent twenty-two years as Director of Bioethical Compliance at Vantara BioSystems, one of The Spire's three major augmentation conglomerates. He was the man who signed off on clinical trial parameters, who sat across from regulators and explained why the variance in adverse outcome data was within acceptable bounds, who used the language of ethics as a procedural instrument. He was not unintelligent about what he was doing. He did it anyway. The specific incident that ended his career is documented in sealed corporate arbitration records: a neural augmentation trial in the lower districts in which forty-three participants experienced cascading cognitive degradation, eighteen of whom died. Rector had flagged the risk internally fourteen months prior. The flag was overruled. He signed the continuation anyway.

He was not prosecuted. He was quietly exited, his Spire access revoked, his identity scrubbed from Vantara's public materials. He went to The Shelf because he didn't know where else to go, and he stayed because someone needed stitches and he was the only one there with the knowledge. That was eleven years ago. He has since become the closest thing The Shelf has to a neighborhood doctor, working from a converted storage unit he calls the Surgery, accepting payment in food, labor, or nothing. He does not talk about his past. Everyone in The Shelf knows anyway.
Properties.aliases: The Anchor, Rec, Father Hollowell (deprecated, refused)
Properties.role: Former Spire-tier bioethics executive / Exiled community medic
Properties.location: The Shelf
Properties.narrative_function: Rector functions as the story's moral weight anchor—a character who has done genuine institutional harm and is living inside the long, non-redemptive work of trying to be useful anyway. He resists the redemption arc structure by refusing to let himself be redeemed, which makes him a vehicle for exploring what accountability looks like when there is no absolution available.
Properties.augmentations: Haptic-feedback surgical assist implants in both hands—installed during his Vantara years for precision work, now the only augmentations he retains and maintains with deep ambivalence,A Vantara-branded neural medical reference implant he has repeatedly tried to have removed; two surgeons in The Circuit told him the extraction risk outweighs the benefit at his age
Properties.core_fears: That his current work is self-absolution rather than genuine repair—that he is still, fundamentally, serving himself; Making a critical error in the Surgery and losing someone he could have saved; Being found useful by the people he used to work for
Properties.core_desires: To do genuine good without the mathematics of acceptable loss; To be honest about what he is, including to himself; Quiet—not peace exactly, but the absence of the particular noise the Spire makes inside your head
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Radical present-focus—treating each patient as the only ethical unit that matters right now; Blunt self-assessment that sometimes crosses into self-flagellation; Physical work as penance and purpose simultaneously
Properties.blind_spots: His guilt sometimes makes him over-treat, taking on cases beyond his current resources because he cannot bear to decline; Assumes people who offer him help have ulterior motives because he spent decades in a world where they always did; Does not recognize that his presence in The Shelf has become its own form of influence
Properties.secret: He still has access to his old Vantara internal credentials—a backdoor the company doesn't know survived his exit. He has used it once in eleven years, to pull trial data for a Shelf resident who was experiencing delayed-onset cognitive degradation from a Vantara product. He told himself it was the last time. He keeps the access because he knows it won't be.
Properties.story_hooks: The Vantara trial data in his head matches the profile of the original forty-three almost exactly—someone inside is running the same experiment again, and Rector may be the only person who can prove it before the threshold is crossed; A young Shelf resident presents with cognitive symptoms Rector recognizes from his sealed trial files—and the resident has no history of Vantara augmentation, which means the vector is something new; Someone from the original forty-three trial cases finds their way to the Surgery—not for treatment, but because they've been looking for Rector for eleven years; He is offered a legitimate medical resource—supplies, equipment, funding—by a Spire-adjacent organization, and has to determine whether the offer is genuine charity or an attempt to bring him back into institutional orbit
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated (formerly Vantara BioSystems, Spire-tier; affiliation terminated)
Properties.vocabulary: Medical precision mixed with deliberate plainness—he has consciously stripped corporate euphemism from his speech as an ongoing practice, and catches himself when it slips back in
Properties.cadence: Slow, considered, with the weight of someone who has learned that words have costs. Long pauses before difficult truths. Does not soften diagnoses but does not deliver them without care.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'What do you actually need? Not what you came in saying. What's the thing underneath that.' | 'I can tell you the prognosis in clinical terms or I can tell you what it means for your life. They're not the same sentence. Which one helps you?' | 'I signed things before. I was very good at making the signing sound like a different thing than it was. I am not interested in doing that anymore, about anything.' | 'This is going to hurt. I won't tell you it won't. I'll tell you I'll be here while it does, and that's what I can actually offer you.'

Properties.description:
Fenwick is short, stocky, and perpetually cheerful in a way that takes people a moment to calibrate — not false exactly, but layered over something more complicated, like a coral reef over deep water. His skin is a warm medium brown, his hair grown out in a loose high puff with copper-dyed ends, and he has a set of patterned irises — interlocking geometric circles in charcoal and cream — that he keeps well-maintained and that give him the slightly uncanny look of someone whose eyes are always aesthetically composed. He wears a pharmacist's white coat that he has clearly owned for years and refuses to replace despite its soft edges.

He is genuinely good at pharmacy. He remembers dosage interactions, flags contraindications before patients can finish asking their questions, and has a gift for making the most boring parts of medication management feel like he is doing you a personal favor. He is also, two nights a week, coordinating distribution of unlicensed gene-therapy compounds through a network that runs from The Shelf down to the Narrows and up to certain Tier 3 residential blocks where people want treatments Helix Biosystems has priced out of their reach. He finds this deeply morally straightforward and would be genuinely surprised if someone told him it was brave.
Properties.role: Pharmacist and black-market pharmaceutical broker, The Shelf district
Properties.location: The Shelf, operating from a legitimate licensed pharmacy called Goldthread Dispensary
Properties.narrative_function: Supply source, information broker, black-market access point disguised as local color; can provide controlled substances for various story purposes; comic relief that is smarter than it appears
Properties.augmentations: Patterned cosmetic irises (geometric charcoal and cream); olfactory enhancement (mild, professional — helps him detect compound purity); no structural augmentation
Properties.core_fears: His supply network being traced back to the providers — not to himself, specifically to them; Becoming complicit in something genuinely harmful because he misjudged a compound
Properties.core_desires: For medicine to be boring and available and cheap and fine — he finds the drama of scarcity genuinely offensive; To be taken seriously as a pharmacist by the Aurochs system that views The Shelf dispensaries as second-tier
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cheerfulness as genuine philosophy, not suppression — he processes quickly and moves on; Extensive batch-testing of everything that comes through his network before distribution; Talking to the dispensary's E.L.F. — a minor spirit in the pill-counter AI — like a friend
Properties.blind_spots: He trusts his own risk assessment too completely; he has been lucky so far and mistakes luck for skill; He genuinely cannot imagine being betrayed by someone he likes, so he does not plan for it
Properties.secret: One of his regular legal customers is a Ferrogate Transit safety officer who takes a compound Fenwick supplies that controls a neurological tremor — a tremor that, if disclosed, would disqualify her from her position. He has never mentioned this to anyone. She has never asked him not to. The unspoken arrangement terrifies him more than the network does.
Properties.story_hooks: A compound from his network has caused an unexpected reaction in a patient — not fatal, but strange, and tracing the batch leads somewhere he was not expecting; The Ferrogate Transit officer's tremor has gotten worse and she needs a higher dose that he is not sure he should provide
Properties.affiliation: Self-employed (Goldthread Dispensary license); informal supply network with several underground medical providers
Properties.vocabulary: Warm, rapid, technically fluent; slides between clinical precision and neighborhood vernacular without noticing
Properties.cadence: Fast and easy; comfortable overlapping conversation; laughs quickly and genuinely
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay so what you're describing is not an allergy, it's a sensitivity, and those are different in ways that matter, and I'm going to explain why while I find you something that won't make your face do that.' | 'The E.L.F. in the counter says this batch is clean. I also tested it three times myself. I trust her more than my own results, honestly.'
