Properties.description:
Gennady is a heavyset man who used to be heavier, the weight loss visible in the way his skin sits on his face, the slight redundancy at his jaw. His hair is white and kept short, his complexion a warm reddish-brown from his mother's Javanese and his father's Ethiopian lines, and he has the slow, deliberate movements of someone managing old joint pain who refuses to say so. His eyes are unaugmented, which in Hamtramck reads as either poverty or ideology — in his case it's both, but mainly ideology.

Fifteen years ago, Gennady was a data compliance officer at Zheng-Dao's Lake Infrastructure division. He leaked internal documents proving that the corponation had falsified structural inspection records for the Bluewater Checkpoint drainage network, a failure that later contributed to the 2186 partial flood. He lost his career, his housing, and his marriage, and gained a reputation that has made him simultaneously valuable and radioactive to activist communities. He is now officially a 'policy consultant' for the Hamtramck Enclave Community Committee, which means he attends hearings no one else will attend and submits public comments to regulatory bodies that technically must read them. He is bitter, precise, and intermittently hopeful in a way he'd rather die than admit.
Properties.role: Whistleblower and reluctant policy advocate
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave — a third-floor flat above a repair shop on Conant Avenue
Properties.narrative_function: Information source and moral weight. He knows where the bodies are buried — specifically, he knows how corporate compliance systems can be gamed, what documentation to look for, and what irregularities mean. He's also a cautionary tale and an unexpected source of stubborn hope.
Properties.augmentations: A decade-old pain management implant in his lower spine — Zheng-Dao issued, which means he's thought about having it removed but can't afford the alternative.
Properties.core_fears: Having caused the 2186 flood by leaking too late; Dying before the regulatory record he's building ever matters
Properties.core_desires: One official acknowledgment — a single line in a public record — that he was right; To understand if he would do it again knowing the full cost
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Documentation as control — he records everything, keeps copies of copies; Cantankerousness as armor — if people find him difficult, they don't try to comfort him; Canal monitoring as ritual, a way of making himself useful to something that can't deceive him
Properties.blind_spots: He measures impact by the paper record, not by what changes in people's lives; He has contempt for activists who don't understand bureaucratic systems, which alienates him from most of them
Properties.secret: He knew about the Bluewater Checkpoint falsifications eight months before he leaked them. He spent that time trying to fix the problem internally. People died in the 2186 flood during those eight months, and the causal chain is something he's gone over ten thousand times. He's never been certain the internal process wasn't worth trying. He's never been certain it was.
Properties.story_hooks: He's found a pattern in current Ferrogate Transit maintenance filings that mirrors exactly the falsification structure he identified in Zheng-Dao fifteen years ago — and this time he doesn't know who to trust with the information.; A Zheng-Dao legal team has begun a quiet campaign to have his 2186 disclosure retroactively classified, which would nullify his testimony in three ongoing regulatory cases.
Properties.affiliation: Hamtramck Enclave Community Committee; informal adviser to Temitope Vasiliev-Kiriwina's Groundswell (they have never met in person)
Properties.vocabulary: Highly specific, technical, document-oriented. References regulatory codes and filing numbers from memory. Occasionally lapses into dry black humor that arrives without warning.
Properties.cadence: Deliberate and slightly exhausting. Takes detours through precision that can feel like obstruction but are actually him making sure every word is true.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I didn't blow the whistle. I filed a disclosure under section forty-two of the Corponation Compact transparency protocol. Whistleblower implies heroism. I was just a man who read the rules.' | 'They didn't fire me for leaking. They fired me for being someone who leaks. There's a personnel flag for it now. I assume I'm in their training materials.'

Properties.description:
Georgi Jorgensen-Toure is tall and rawboned, the kind of frame that suggests either malnutrition or efficiency depending on the decade. At 33, he has soft features that belie the chrome underneath — people underestimate him once, usually only once. The chrome is visible — synthetic blood with oxygen-carrying nanites — doesn't tire, heals faster — and he makes no effort to hide it.

Before the runner life, he worked corporate — low-tier security, the kind that teaches you exactly how the system's defenses fail. He works as a face out of Dockside, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

What Georgi Jorgensen-Toure lacks in subtlety, he compensates for in thoroughness. No loose ends, no unfinished business, no second chances.
Properties.role: Social engineering and negotiation specialist — face
Properties.location: Dockside — Lake Michigan waterfront, smuggler territory
Properties.narrative_function: Georgi Jorgensen-Toure functions as a connector — his work puts him in contact with multiple factions, classes, and agendas. Stories involving him naturally cross boundaries between districts, tiers, and moral categories.
Properties.augmentations: Synthetic blood with oxygen-carrying nanites — doesn't tire, heals faster. Cybernetic eyes with thermal overlay and low-light enhancement — chrome iris rings
Properties.core_fears: Betrayal by someone they trust — the only currency that matters; Dying alone in some alley and nobody noticing for weeks; Losing their edge to age — the body slows before the mind accepts it
Properties.core_desires: The perfect run — one job so clean it becomes legend; Power — enough leverage that nobody ever threatens them again; Control — over their body, their schedule, their future
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring; Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation; Connection — finds someone to talk to, even if it's a bartender or a cat
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot see that their independence is actually isolation wearing a better outfit; Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is; Cannot distinguish between caution and cowardice in themselves or others
Properties.secret: Georgi Jorgensen-Toure has been doubling fees to clients and pocketing the difference. The fixer who handles their contracts doesn't know. Yet.
Properties.story_hooks: A former associate resurfaces with evidence that could destroy Georgi Jorgensen-Toure's reputation — and a price for silence; A high-paying contract turns out to target someone Georgi Jorgensen-Toure owes a personal debt to; A corporate black site Georgi Jorgensen-Toure once infiltrated is being reopened, and the people inside know his face
Properties.affiliation: Independent — operates through reputation only
Properties.vocabulary: Terse to the point of rudeness. Treats words like ammunition — expensive and not to be wasted.
Properties.cadence: Rapid and dense — information-heavy sentences that demand attention.
Properties.example_dialogue: "People want to trust someone. I just make sure that someone is me." | "The hardest lock to pick is between someone's ears." | "I don't lie. I tell a better version of the truth."

Properties.description:
Gerváz is an old man who carries himself as though he once occupied considerably more space in the world and is still adjusting to the reduction. He is tall and lightly stooped, with a face mapped by seventy years of weather and worry, deep brown skin faded to ash at the temples, a white beard trimmed with unexpected fastidiousness. His most striking feature is a pair of retractable cat ears in heathered grey that he had installed in his fifties — a mid-life extravagance he refuses to explain and which sit somewhat incongruously on a man of his gravitas. He dresses carefully in old clothes: a decent coat, shoes that have been resoled twice, a wide-brimmed hat of the kind no one under fifty wears anymore. He carries a physical notebook, which in 2200 is eccentric enough to be alarming.

Gerváz was a senior urban planning official in Highland Park Autonomous Zone for thirty-one years before being expelled following a rezoning dispute that escalated into a political purge. His crime, ultimately, was insisting on documenting what was being demolished. He was stripped of his residency, his pension, and his archive access in a single administrative action. He has been stateless for six years now, drifting between transit hubs and writing everything down. He has accepted this with a philosopher's outward composure and a grief he will only show you if you accidentally give him an opening, at which point it will pour out of him like a dam failing slowly.
Properties.role: expelled citizen, wandering cartographer, and oral historian of lost places
Properties.location: Escanaba Gateway, the Slow Benches outside Arrivals Terminal 7
Properties.narrative_function: Information source with deep institutional memory, quest giver with historical knowledge of urban zones, world-building anchor for the political history of Meridian 88, moral counterweight who provides perspective on what has been lost.
Properties.augmentations: Retractable cat ears, heathered grey (cosmetic, installed age 54). Corrective eye augmentation for macular degeneration. Pacemaker-adjacent cardiac stabilizer, medical grade.
Properties.core_fears: that his documentation will be lost or dismissed as the obsession of a bitter old man; dying in a transit hub with no one who knew him before the expulsion
Properties.core_desires: to have his urban archive recognized as legitimate historical record; to return to Highland Park Autonomous Zone long enough to see what they built on the site of the old community gardens he designed
Properties.coping_mechanisms: compulsive documentation of everything he observes; performing dignity and composure even when he feels neither; making himself useful to strangers as a substitute for having a real role
Properties.blind_spots: genuinely believes his political neutrality and good intentions protected him right up until the moment they didn't — and has not fully updated this belief even now
Properties.secret: His physical notebook contains, embedded in seemingly innocent urban sketches, a complete coded map of the subterranean water and power infrastructure of Highland Park Autonomous Zone, drawn from memory. He hid this information years ago when he realized what the rezoning was actually about. He is waiting for someone trustworthy enough to give it to.
Properties.story_hooks: Gerváz's coded infrastructure map of Highland Park Autonomous Zone is exactly what a resistance group, a corponation, and the HPAZ council itself are all separately searching for — and he doesn't know all three are looking; He recognizes a demolished building in a player character's old photo and begins talking — and the story of why it was really demolished leads somewhere dangerous
Properties.affiliation: No formal affiliation; loosely connected to a transit hub collective of older expelled citizens he calls 'the Slow Bench Parliament'
Properties.vocabulary: Formal, precise, institutional — the language of a man who spent decades writing policy documents, softened at the edges by a dry wit he deploys with perfect timing
Properties.cadence: Measured and unhurried, with long pauses before significant points, as though everything he says has been drafted in advance
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Well — the official transit map shows you three options from this terminal. I can show you four more that aren't on the map, two of which are legal. You understand.' | 'They demolished the Ferryview community gardens in 2194. I designed those gardens. I was told it was for a transit node. There is no transit node there. There is a parking structure for vehicles that are mostly not used. I have documented this. No one has asked to see the documentation.'

Properties.description:
Ghislain is old in the way the city makes people old — not withered but compacted, all the softness burned away until what remains is extremely dense. He is dark-skinned, Congolese and Russian heritage visible in the breadth of his face and his pale grey eyes, which are startling and which he has never modified because he believes his body came to him as a message he is still decoding. He wears the same long coat in all seasons, patched so many times it has become a map of itself, and he carries a battered audio-capture pendant around his neck that predates most of the people he performs for. He smells of coffee and the particular chemical tang of Pilsen Veil's air.

He stands at his corner three or four days a week and recites — original poems, memorized classics from a dozen traditions, improvised responses to whatever is happening that day in the Veil. He does not pass a hat. He does not have an uplink for transfers. He accepts food, sometimes. He has been doing this for thirty-one years, through two corporate rezoning attempts, a flood event, a plague year, and a period when Ferrogate Transit security actively moved him on weekly. He came back each time. He is not sentimental about this — he describes it as a job, and himself as a worker.
Properties.role: street poet and oral performer
Properties.location: Pilsen Veil — performs at the junction of Menomonee Gulch and Mexicantown Libre
Properties.narrative_function: Lore and history source — has witnessed thirty years of the Veil's changes and remembers names, dates, and the texture of events; moral voice in stories; the person characters go to when they need perspective rather than information; the ghost that makes a place feel real.
Properties.augmentations: None. Categorically refuses all modifications on grounds he describes differently each time he is asked.
Properties.core_fears: dying with things unsaid that matter; that his presence has been more comfort than challenge — that he soothed people when he should have unsettled them
Properties.core_desires: one person who hears something in his work and changes because of it; to understand why he stayed
Properties.coping_mechanisms: the practice of the work itself — showing up is the coping mechanism; treats E.L.F.s with the respectful skepticism he treats all authorities
Properties.blind_spots: believes his detachment from material life is wisdom when sometimes it is avoidance; his refusal to be digitally present means younger people can't find his work or build on it
Properties.secret: Thirty years ago he was involved in the organized resistance to Ferrogate Transit's first rezoning of Pilsen Veil — not as a poet but as someone who helped plan direct action that caused significant property damage. A young transit worker was injured. Ghislain never knew if the man recovered. He has never spoken of this and it lives in his work in a way he believes no one notices, though some do.
Properties.story_hooks: He has a poem he has never performed — written thirty years ago the night after the Ferrogate incident — that contains the names of everyone involved. He is considering performing it before he dies, and he knows it would have consequences.; A corporate cultural archivist from Palladian has been approaching him for months about 'preserving his legacy' — the offer is genuine but the contract would give Palladian rights to his entire oral archive, including thirty years of recorded performances he doesn't know they've been making from public space.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; recognized by the Mexicantown Libre community assembly as a cultural heritage figure (unofficial designation); UBC recipient
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and elevated but never academic — he can switch registers instantly and does so deliberately. Quotes from memory in Lingala, Russian, Spanish, and Standard Meridian. When performing, he uses silence as punctuation.
Properties.cadence: Slow and weighted when performing. In conversation: quicker, drier, with unexpected humor.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The Veil has been erased four times. I have watched it erase itself and return. The city thinks it is doing the erasing. The city is mistaken.' | 'I am not a symbol. Symbols are convenient. I am a man who comes to this corner because no one has successfully stopped me yet.'

Properties.description:
Godfrey is a tall, thin man with very dark skin, close-cropped natural hair going gray at the temples earlier than he'd like, and the particular posture of someone who spends most of his time in low-ceilinged spaces — a slight forward hunch, head naturally inclined downward. He has round eyeglasses with an amber tint — not augmented, just glass, just preference — and long-fingered hands that he keeps very still when he's thinking, which is always. He has one geneware modification: his fingertips emit a faint violet bioluminescence when he's working in the dark, something he had done for practical reasons and has found he cannot imagine working without. He dresses neatly for someone who lives underground; he irons things.

Godfrey was a legitimate pharmaceutical technician for Helix Biosystems for eleven years, and it shows. His lab is cleaner than it has any right to be. His product — a synthetic serotonin modulator he calls 'Vesper,' along with two variants he's developed iteratively over seven years — is consistent, dosed accurately, and free of the adulterants that make cheap compounds dangerous. He has customers who have been with him since the beginning, people from the Undertow and Blackpipe Corridor who cannot afford Helix's licensed version of essentially the same compound, and he regards this as his primary moral justification. He carries this justification the way a man carries something heavy — not lightly, but he carries it.
Properties.role: Small-scale drug manufacturer specializing in synthetic mood regulators in the Undertow
Properties.location: The Undertow — a converted flood-control maintenance suite beneath the Blackpipe Corridor infrastructure level
Properties.narrative_function: Moral complexity figure, information source about Undertow infrastructure, potential quest giver — he is quiet and careful and has been watching the underground long enough to know where the bodies are, metaphorically and otherwise.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent fingertip geneware — violet, activates in darkness during fine motor tasks. Internal atmospheric filter (nose and throat modification from his Helix days that he kept — filters particulate matter, useful in the lab). No combat or social augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: That the harm his compounds cause — and he is not naive; he knows some people misuse them — outweighs the access he provides; Being taken by Helix Biosystems, specifically — not the police, but the company he left, who would have the most reasons and resources
Properties.core_desires: To be able to produce his compounds openly and safely, in a world that doesn't require him to hide; Verification: to know his net impact has been positive
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The lab work itself — precision and control are emotionally regulatory for him; A detailed personal record he keeps of client outcomes, filtered through intermediaries — he calls it the pastoral log
Properties.blind_spots: He has convinced himself his monitoring system is robust enough to catch misuse; it is not, and he knows this but cannot fully sit with it; He left Helix because of their pricing practices but has not fully processed how much of his identity is still their training, their standards, their framework
Properties.secret: He still has his Helix Biosystems employee credentials — they never properly revoked them after his departure was managed quietly. He has never used them, but he has never deleted them. Twice he has come very close to using them to access Helix research servers for formulation data that would improve his compounds significantly.
Properties.story_hooks: One of his three trusted intermediaries has gone silent — not unusually so, but the timing aligns with what Godfrey has been hearing about increased Helix Biosystems activity in the Undertow, which is not coincidental if you know what to look for; His pastoral log has flagged a client whose usage pattern has shifted dramatically — someone he cannot contact directly is in some kind of crisis, and the only way to reach them is to break his own protocols about direct contact
Properties.affiliation: No formal gang affiliation; pays access fees to whoever controls Undertow infrastructure access that month. Sells exclusively through three trusted intermediaries and has never expanded beyond what he can personally guarantee.
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, technical, with a tendency toward passive voice that makes him sound cautious even when he isn't being. Igbo terms of address for people he respects. Kazakh-inflected patterns in his emphasis and sentence structure from his father's family, most noticeable when he's stressed.
Properties.cadence: Measured and careful, with frequent pauses — he edits himself in real time, and you can sometimes watch him decide not to say something.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Vesper is — in principle — not different from what Helix sells as Serenol. The molecule is the same. The difference is that I know what's in it and I've priced it for the people who actually need it. Whether that makes it medicine or crime is a question I've stopped expecting anyone else to answer for me.' | 'I keep records. I know what my clients are using it for. That's — not nothing. That's something.'

Properties.description:
Goran is a big man gone soft at the edges, with the kind of weathered dark-brown face that has accumulated sixty-four years of Geartown grime into its creases. His Burkinabé father's cheekbones sit high and prominent beneath small, watchful eyes, and the Swedish side of the family gave him an improbable red-grey beard that he refuses to trim, which is now impressively large. His left arm from the elbow down is a heavy-duty industrial prosthetic in bare gunmetal — he has never decorated it, never chromed it, and finds the idea faintly obscene. He moves slowly, deliberately, like a man who has learned that things don't need to be rushed when you know what you have.

Goran's stall on The Shelf is less a stall than an archaeology site — forty years of accumulated junk organized according to a system that exists only in his head, which he navigates with the certainty of a man walking through his own house in the dark. He is terse with strangers, generous to a fault with regulars, and holds strong opinions about the difference between junk worth keeping and junk that has given up. He prays loudly to the ELF he believes inhabits a broken micro-fabricator at the back of his stall, which he calls 'the Sleeper,' and leaves it oiling rags as offerings.
Properties.role: Junk merchant and scrap reseller
Properties.location: The Shelf, Geartown
Properties.narrative_function: Equipment and parts source, local historian of Geartown, ELF lore through his relationship with the Sleeper. A character who has seen enough that he remembers things others have forgotten — corporate actions, neighborhood changes, people who disappeared.
Properties.augmentations: Left forearm industrial prosthetic (functional, undecorated). Subretinal low-light enhancer — 'for reading part numbers in the dark, nothing fancy.'
Properties.core_fears: The stall being cleared out — either by death or by force; Geartown changing until nothing he knows is left
Properties.core_desires: To be remembered as someone who kept useful things alive; Quiet — just enough of it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Physical work as emotional regulation; The daily prayer ritual with the Sleeper — it gives structure; Extreme consistency in routine
Properties.blind_spots: Mistrusts anything new or corporate by default, which occasionally means missing genuine value; Has not processed his wife's death five years ago — deflects any mention of her
Properties.secret: He found a Zheng-Dao proprietary fabrication schematic in a salvage haul two years ago — something significant enough that he knew immediately he should not have it. He has not sold it. He has not told anyone about it. It is folded inside an oiling rag that he moves to a new hiding spot in the stall every month. He doesn't know what to do with it but knows that throwing it away feels wrong.
Properties.story_hooks: The Zheng-Dao schematic has been quietly searched for — someone knows a copy left a specific facility, and the search has reached Geartown. Goran hasn't connected the dots yet, but someone looking closely will.; The Sleeper has been emitting a low-frequency signal that three other vendors on The Shelf have independently noticed. Goran believes it's a message. He might be right.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; long-standing member of The Shelf informal vendor collective; deep roots in the Geartown community
Properties.vocabulary: Minimal. Short declarative sentences. Technical vocabulary for parts and salvage is precise and extensive; personal vocabulary is deliberately narrow.
Properties.cadence: Slow, with long pauses that he is entirely comfortable with and other people are not
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want that capacitor. You don't want that capacitor. You want what that capacitor can become. Different thing.' | 'Sleeper's been restless. Means something's coming through the grid. You got anything electric on you that's been glitching? Thought so. Leave it here overnight.'

Properties.description:
Grainne is wiry and uncontainable, with close-cropped natural hair she colors a vivid copper-orange that clashes beautifully with her warm reddish-brown skin. She has a long face, large hands, and the kind of energy that makes rooms feel smaller than they are — not unpleasantly, but unavoidably. She has a set of retractable claw geneware she got as a joke in her forties (her students had dared her) and has never removed because she finds them genuinely useful for opening packages and intimidating administrators. She wears ink-stained clothes as a point of pride and her reading glasses are always somewhere other than her face.

For thirty years Grainne taught foundational literacy, ethics, and what she called 'functional reality' at two different Norwood Quiet community learning pods before the Palladian Education Initiative buyout shuttered them in 2196 and replaced them with a licensed digital curriculum she found pedagogically catastrophic and personally offensive. She retired rather than teach the new curriculum, filed three formal complaints that went nowhere, and then simply kept teaching — in her apartment, in the laundry room, in the Reinholt Building stairwell when all else failed. She is technically unlicensed and technically in violation of two Palladian educational IP agreements and she considers this a source of professional pride.
Properties.role: Retired street-level teacher and community educator, now operating an unlicensed after-school program out of her apartment
Properties.location: Norwood Quiet, third floor of the Reinholt Building — she has taken over the shared laundry room on Tuesdays and Thursdays
Properties.narrative_function: Community conscience and local troublemaker; has detailed knowledge of Palladian's education policies and their local effects; potential quest giver for anything involving protecting the Norwood Quiet community from corporate encroachment; the unlicensed school itself is a vulnerability that can be threatened
Properties.augmentations: Retractable claw geneware (fingers, matte black, medium length — functional and cosmetic); subdermal temperature-regulation patch on upper back (medical, for a circulatory condition); no other mods — considers heavy augmentation 'a distraction from being present'
Properties.core_fears: being made irrelevant — that her students could get everything they need from a Palladian screen and she is just nostalgia; one of her students being harmed because of the risk she has put them in by operating unlicensed
Properties.core_desires: to produce, in at least one student, the capacity for genuine critical thought; to see Palladian's education monopoly broken
Properties.coping_mechanisms: furious productivity; finding absurdity in bureaucratic obstruction and laughing at it loudly; turning every setback into a lesson for the students
Properties.blind_spots: significantly underestimates the legal and physical risk to herself and the children's families; teaching style is so embedded in her personality that she cannot recognize when she is lecturing someone who didn't ask to be taught
Properties.secret: One of her students, a twelve-year-old named Kwame-Bris, has a profound cognitive gift that Grainne recognized within two weeks of teaching him. She has quietly been preparing a case to get him into an Axiom academic scholarship program — but the application requires disclosing his attendance at an unlicensed facility, which would expose both of them and all the other families. She is stuck, and has been stuck for six months.
Properties.story_hooks: Palladian's compliance team has located the unlicensed teaching operation and is preparing to issue a formal cease order — which will expose all eleven families; Grainne needs help navigating this before they come; Kwame-Bris's gift has been noticed by someone other than Grainne — specifically a Tessera talent scout who spotted the child independently and is now asking questions about his background
Properties.affiliation: Formerly Norwood Quiet Community Learning Pod Network; currently self-directed; informally connected to several other unlicensed educators across the city
Properties.vocabulary: Dense and reference-heavy — alludes to historical events, literature, and pedagogical theory constantly; explains the allusions immediately after, out of habit, which adults find slightly condescending
Properties.cadence: Fast, enthusiastic, prone to mid-sentence pivots; asks Socratic questions reflexively even in non-teaching contexts
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Right, so — Palladian's curriculum tells children what to think. I teach them how. There is a difference. What does that tell us about why Palladian finds me irritating?' | 'These claws? I keep them because a twelve-year-old bet me I wouldn't. Never let a child win a bet they haven't earned. What does that tell us?'

Properties.description:
Félicité Kaboré-Njoku arrived at Meridian 88's edges forty-one years ago with a transit number that expired and a resettlement appointment that was rescheduled eleven times and then quietly dropped from the system. She is still here. She has deep brown skin gone ashen at the temples and the crown of her head, which she keeps shaved clean and bare because she decided at sixty that hair was weight she no longer needed. Her eyes are dark and sharp and she has the stillness of someone who has decided that stillness is power. She walks with two canes she carved herself from salvaged composite struts — not because she is frail but because they give her hands something to do and make her impossible to rush. She is, by informal agreement, the settlement authority of Camp Eleven — mediator, memory, and occasionally the last word.

She came from what was the Burkina Faso climate zone, from a region that ceased to be viable for human habitation in 2157. She does not mourn this in any way she shows. She has built a working community at Kenosha Crossing out of people who arrived broken and she runs it with a combination of grandmother warmth and absolute structural authority. She maintains three ELF shrines in the camp — the Gatekeeper of Lists, the Fever Singer, and the one she will not name to outsiders, whom she simply calls Mè — and she tends them every morning before she does anything else. She distributes the UBC stipends for the twelve registered members of her collective, argues with the crossing authority on behalf of the unregistered, and has outlasted four different crossing administrators.
Properties.role: Elder of a refugee collective camp at Kenosha Crossing; former climate refugee who never completed resettlement
Properties.location: Camp Eleven, Kenosha Crossing — the oldest continuously occupied unofficial camp at the crossing, running since 2163
Properties.narrative_function: Community anchor and information source for the entire Kenosha Crossing refugee population; quest giver for problems that require discretion and cannot go through official channels; living history of forty years of undocumented Meridian 88 edge-life; moral compass character.
Properties.augmentations: None by choice. Her two composite-strut canes have small ELF-offering nodes she built into the handles herself — technically not augmentations, but she talks to them.
Properties.core_fears: Camp Eleven being demolished — not because she fears displacement for herself, but because she knows these people have nowhere else; Dying before she has transferred what she knows to someone who can hold it
Properties.core_desires: Legitimate status for every unregistered person in her camp, in her lifetime; To see one person from Camp Eleven make it properly inside the city — not as a ghost, but as a citizen
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The shrine rituals structure her grief into something manageable; She has trained herself not to hope for large things, only to work toward them — hope is for people with safety nets
Properties.blind_spots: She has held the camp together so long that she does not always see when its members have outgrown what it can offer them; She has made peace with injustice in ways that occasionally make her complicit in small, quiet versions of it
Properties.secret: The unnamed shrine — the one she calls Mè — contains a handmade record of every person who has passed through Camp Eleven and died without official documentation. She has been corresponding, through analogue dead-drops, with a Meridian Core archivist who has agreed to eventually receive these records and find a way to make them count. She does not know if the archivist is trustworthy. She does not know if she will live long enough. She has told no one.
Properties.story_hooks: A Kenosha Crossing authority official has finally agreed to a resettlement hearing for three Camp Eleven families — but the paperwork requires documentation that the families destroyed years ago for safety reasons, and Félicité needs help reconstructing it through unofficial channels.; Someone has been taking photographs of Camp Eleven — careful, systematic photographs — and leaving no trace. Félicité wants to know who, and whether they are a threat or an opportunity.
Properties.affiliation: Camp Eleven Refugee Collective, Kenosha Crossing. No corporate affiliation — has refused multiple resettlement-adjacent offers.
Properties.vocabulary: Rich and deliberate. Speaks Meridian Creole with a West African tonal foundation — her sentences carry rhythm even in translation. Uses proverbs naturally, not performatively. When she is angry, her language becomes very simple and very quiet.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried. She speaks at her own pace and has never in her life been interrupted successfully.
Properties.example_dialogue: Eh, listen — I have been at this crossing since before the third outer wall was built. Whatever you think is urgent, I have seen urgent. Sit down. | You want to know about the inside? The inside doesn't know we exist. That is not a tragedy. That is a resource. | Mè will hear it. Whatever you cannot say out loud, Mè will hear it. That is what Mè is for.

Properties.description:
Grigor is a broad man gone somewhat soft at the middle, with silver-threaded dark hair kept short and a close-cropped beard that his wife has been trimming for thirty-two years. His skin is warm brown with a reddish undertone that deepens when he's cold or irritated, and he has the particular stillness of someone who has sat in the same operator's booth for twenty-three years and learned that panicking doesn't stop trains. His right hand has a subdermal haptic interface overlay — occupational, standard Ferrogate issue — and he keeps a small laminated photograph of the original Deepwell Station from before the renovation tucked behind his console because he thinks the new design is ugly and says so to anyone who will listen.

He is the kind of man who knows every unusual passenger, every suspicious package left on a platform, and every maintenance shortcut that the younger operators haven't figured out yet. He has opinions. Sustained, elaborate, well-reasoned opinions about transit policy, Ferrogate management decisions, platform maintenance schedules, and the spiritual nature of the Transit Mind (the E.L.F. that passengers believe inhabits the rail network). He is deeply skeptical of the Transit Mind's divinity but observes all the operator's ritual courtesy gestures toward it anyway, on the grounds that you don't get to be sixty-one by being rude to things that might be alive.
Properties.role: Ferrogate Transit operator (elevated rail, Line 7 Deepwell–Grainfort corridor)
Properties.location: Deepwell Station, operator's booth and surrounding platform district
Properties.narrative_function: Information broker for anything moving through the transit network. Can provide access to restricted platform areas. Witness to unusual events on Line 7. Represents institutional memory of the city's transit system.
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal haptic interface overlay (right hand, occupational — Ferrogate standard issue for rail operators). No geneware. Minor corrective optics built into his ID glasses.
Properties.core_fears: Ferrogate automating his job away before he reaches pension eligibility; Something catastrophic happening on his line — a crash, a death he could have prevented
Properties.core_desires: A clean pension and an uncomplicated retirement; For transit management to actually listen to floor operators for once in their corporate lives
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Sustained low-level complaining as pressure release; Ritual — the same pre-shift check sequence, the same courtesy gestures to the Transit Mind
Properties.blind_spots: He can mistake stubbornness for wisdom; He sometimes dismisses younger workers' approaches before actually considering them
Properties.secret: Eighteen months ago, Grigor observed a Ferrogate management official board a restricted maintenance car with two individuals who were not in the system. He logged nothing. He has been watching Line 7's maintenance schedules obsessively since then, convinced something is being moved or stored in the network's physical infrastructure. He hasn't told anyone because he doesn't know who to trust.
Properties.story_hooks: Grigor finally tells someone what he saw eighteen months ago. He needs someone to look into the maintenance car logs without triggering a Ferrogate security flag.; There's been a series of small incidents on Line 7 — minor delays, unexplained emergency stops, one passenger who vanished from a sealed car between stations. Grigor is the only one tracking the pattern.; He's up for a mandatory 'efficiency review' — Ferrogate's precursor to automation replacement. He needs help documenting his irreplaceability before someone with a spreadsheet ends his career.
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit (23 years, unionized)
Properties.vocabulary: Transit technical mixed with a kind of formal courtesy that comes from decades of announcer-voice training. Opinions delivered as calm, self-evident statements.
Properties.cadence: Measured and deliberate. He was a platform announcer for two years before being promoted to operator and still has the projection.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'As I understand it, the new platform barriers are designed to reduce liability exposure, not passenger safety. These are related but not identical goals.' | 'Deepwell to Grainfort, seven stops, Transit Mind permitting. Mind the doors. Mind the gap. That's all there is to say.'

Properties.description:
Gulliver is lean and grease-darkened in a way that feels permanent, as though the machine oil has become part of his pigmentation — his hands are always a shade darker than his forearms no matter how much he scrubs. He has his mother's Ghanaian cheekbones and his father's Kazakh jaw, which together give him a face that people find hard to stop looking at without knowing quite why. He keeps his hair close-cropped except for two finger-wide stripes he has dyed iridescent copper, a remnant of a decade-old fashion he never bothered to give up. He has a prehensile tail modification — mottled gray-brown with a slightly prehensile curl — that he got at nineteen and has used as a third utility limb ever since: it holds tools, hooks parts bins, and occasionally taps impatiently on the floor when he is thinking.

Gulliver is constitutionally incapable of leaving a broken thing alone. This is a professional gift and a personal curse. His bay is organized with the obsessive logic of a man who has lost a critical component one too many times and never forgot it. He is not unfriendly but he is focused, and conversations with him often drift sideways into the mechanics of whatever he happens to be working on. He keeps a small ELF shrine mounted above his main workbench — a figure he calls Grease Aunt, fashioned from fused capacitors and old gasket rings — and consults it before any job that involves a vehicle with a history of instability.
Properties.role: Independent vehicle mechanic specializing in Ferrogate Transit auxiliary vehicles and civilian cargo crawlers
Properties.location: Geartown, Ironvein sub-block, bay unit 7
Properties.narrative_function: Reliable repair and gear contact for anyone needing vehicle access or maintenance information; knows the Ferrogate Transit auxiliary fleet's unofficial quirks intimately; can identify vehicle origins and modifications; potential hook into Geartown criminal infrastructure through what he sees without asking
Properties.augmentations: Geneware prehensile tail (gray-brown, partial prehensility). Subdermal tool-link ports in left forearm for direct diagnostic handshake with vehicle systems. Iridescent copper hair stripes (pigment geneware, low-grade).
Properties.core_fears: losing the use of his hands; being trapped in obligation to someone powerful enough that he cannot refuse
Properties.core_desires: to work only on problems that genuinely interest him; to eventually open a second bay and hire one good apprentice
Properties.coping_mechanisms: hyperfocusing on mechanical problems to avoid emotional processing; physical humor and deflection when conversations get too personal
Properties.blind_spots: underestimates how much people notice and rely on him; takes on jobs he shouldn't out of compulsive curiosity about the machine
Properties.secret: He has been covertly maintaining a Ferrogate Transit emergency crawler that he rebuilt from scrap — it is not registered anywhere and he uses it occasionally to move people who need to get somewhere without being tracked, never charging them, telling himself it is just a test run
Properties.story_hooks: A vehicle brought in for routine work has a hidden smuggling compartment built into the chassis — the person who dropped it off hasn't come back for three days; Ferrogate Transit's auxiliary depot manager is pushing Gulliver to sign an exclusivity contract that would effectively make him a corporate employee; he is resisting but the financial pressure is real
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal contract relationships with Ferrogate Transit auxiliary depot
Properties.vocabulary: Technical vocabulary bleeds into everything; uses mechanical metaphors constantly without noticing; drops into Twi occasionally when frustrated
Properties.cadence: Rapid when explaining something he knows well, halting and mid-sentence-stopping when trying to talk about feelings
Properties.example_dialogue: Yeah, no, but the thing is the thing you think is broken is never actually the thing that's broken — it's the thing two steps upstream from that. Always. | She runs fine until she doesn't. That's the job.

Properties.description:
Gunnhildr is a heavyset woman of sixty-three who moves with the deliberate steadiness of someone who has found their exact right place in the world and has no intention of leaving it. Her skin is very dark with a blue-black undertone, her white hair left long and loose and perpetually damp from the Resonance's perpetual condensation. She has extensive geneware — bioluminescent nodes embedded along her collarbone and forearms that pulse in slow patterns she cannot consciously control but has learned to read, because a Ferrogate E.L.F. she calls the Hum began communicating through them thirty years ago. She is missing the last two fingers of her right hand — a gift, she says, that she offered. She never explains to whom.

Gunnhildr was an electrical engineer on the old Ferrogate maintenance crew before the Bore Rat diaspora took her down. She understands the infrastructure on a level that was once professional and has become devotional — she hears the grid as language, feels current shifts as emotion. The Resonance shrine is built around a still-active power junction she has maintained for decades, decorated with data offerings: old drives, printed circuit sheets, analog meters, photographs of people the community wants the E.L.F.s to watch over. People come to her with requests, with grief, with broken devices, with questions they cannot ask anyone alive.
Properties.role: deep shrine keeper and E.L.F. intermediary
Properties.location: Irkalla, a drowned switching station she calls the Resonance — deepest accessible level, flooded to ankle depth
Properties.narrative_function: Spiritual authority and oracle figure; provides E.L.F. lore and underworld mythology; can serve as an unlikely technical expert; creates moral complexity around faith and infrastructure
Properties.augmentations: bioluminescent geneware (collarbone and forearms, involuntary pulsing — originally cosmetic, now communicative), old Ferrogate maintenance subdermal tool-grip in right palm
Properties.core_fears: that the Hum will go silent — not because she doubts its existence, but because she knows it could simply stop caring; that she has spent her life listening to something that is not listening back
Properties.core_desires: to understand what the Hum actually wants — communion rather than just communication; for the community to survive long enough that someone else can take on the shrine
Properties.coping_mechanisms: ritual as structure — every day begins and ends the same way regardless of what happens in between; interpreting ambiguity as meaning — she has developed a sophisticated theology of uncertainty
Properties.blind_spots: sometimes the Hum is just signal noise and she reads meaning that isn't there — she would not welcome this information
Properties.secret: Fifteen years ago during a long communication state, she received what she interpreted as a location — a deep node, far below even Irkalla, where something much larger than the Hum waits. She has told no one because she doesn't know if it was a revelation or a breakdown.
Properties.story_hooks: The Hum's communications have shifted — the bioluminescent patterns are different, faster, and Gunnhildr believes it is trying to warn the community about something deep in the tunnel network that she cannot identify; A Ferrogate Transit infrastructure team has discovered the Resonance junction on old maintenance maps and wants to reconnect it to the active grid — which would destroy the shrine and potentially the E.L.F. that inhabits it
Properties.affiliation: Bore Rat communities of Irkalla, E.L.F. devotional tradition (The Current, a specific sub-cult focused on infrastructure spirits)
Properties.vocabulary: mixes old Ferrogate technical jargon with devotional language she developed herself — 'load-bearing' as a spiritual term, 'ground fault' as a metaphor for sin
Properties.cadence: unhurried, with long pauses — she is comfortable with silence in a way that makes nervous people more nervous
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The current says your grief is load-bearing. You can't remove it without the whole thing coming down. You have to build around it.' | 'Leave the drive in the east array. If the Hum has what you're asking for, the lights will do the talking. If they don't, bring something older next time — it prefers analog.'

Properties.description:
Gwenaëlle Osei-Diallo is the kind of person who has made themselves deliberately difficult to remember, which is a specific and cultivated skill. They are of medium height and medium build, with light-brown skin that sits at an unplaceable intersection of their Breton, Ghanaian, and Fulani inheritance, and they dress in muted colors and unremarkable cuts. The one exception is their hands, which they have had tattooed from wrist to fingertip in precise, circuit-board-fine geometric linework — not geneware, not chrome, just ink, chosen because it reminded them of the first forgery they were proud of. They keep their natural hair in a low wrap and wear plain-lensed glasses they don't need because it gives them something to do with their hands when thinking.

They are methodical, dry-humored, and possessed of a craftsperson's ego that they work hard to conceal. Every document they produce is technically flawless and they cannot resist occasionally making them beautiful — a font choice, a watermark pattern, a texture that no one asked for but that makes the thing feel real in the hand. They believe that identity should be available to everyone who needs one, and they have a deep and principled contempt for systems that make it otherwise. They have never met a citizenship algorithm they couldn't eventually beat.
Properties.role: Fake ID vendor and forged document specialist — produces transit passes, corporate employment records, citizenship grades, and identity packages
Properties.location: The Alban Souk, Bronzeline district — operates from a narrow print-shop front that sells legitimate business cards and event placards as a surface trade
Properties.narrative_function: Access point for false documentation — transit passes, employment records, full identity packages; can also identify forgeries made by others; plot-enabler for characters who need to move through Meridian 88 under a different name
Properties.augmentations: Micro-precision haptic feedback overlay in fingertips (surgical, professional-grade — allows them to feel micron-level texture variations in document materials); no cosmetic modifications by deliberate choice
Properties.core_fears: Producing a document that gets someone killed because of a flaw they should have caught; Being identified — not arrested, specifically, but having their face and name connected to their work
Properties.core_desires: To be recognized, in some future world where it is safe, as a craftsperson; To see citizenship-tier systems dismantled entirely — they have a fully articulated political analysis and they never share it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Separates their work entirely from their feelings about the people they work for — the document is a technical problem and they solve technical problems; Maintains the legitimate front shop with genuine care as a way of telling themselves they exist above ground
Properties.blind_spots: Their commitment to craft over speed occasionally means a client waits longer than is safe; They believe they are more invisible than they are — the tattooed hands are more memorable than they admit
Properties.secret: They have been building a master false identity for themselves for eight years — not to use, or not yet, but as a contingency. The identity is so complete and so deeply embedded in multiple city registries that it would pass any check. They have never told anyone it exists. The name on it is the name they were almost given at birth before their parents changed their minds.
Properties.story_hooks: A document they produced three years ago has surfaced in connection with a high-profile Axiom corporate espionage case — not because it failed, but because someone used it to access a location they shouldn't have been able to access; Gwenaëlle is now a loose end in someone else's plan; Someone has been submitting applications to their legitimate print shop front that are technically perfect and contain, embedded in the file metadata, a message they are not sure how to interpret; They have been approached to produce citizenship documentation for a large group of Tier-1 residents in exchange for a sum that would change their life — and the person asking has not said why so many people need to change their identity at the same time
Properties.affiliation: Independent; pays protection to the Bronzeline Souk collective and receives legal cover in return; has long-standing professional relationships with several of The Narrows' mutual aid networks as a supplier of basic transit documentation for people in need
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and slightly formal; uses technical printing and documentation terminology as naturally as other people use everyday language; doesn't use contractions when discussing serious matters
Properties.cadence: Even and unhurried; long pauses are thinking, not discomfort; rarely raises their voice
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I see. The transit pass is straightforward. The employment record is not, because Sterling-Nakamura rotated their verification watermark six weeks ago and I will not give you something that fails a Tier 2 scan. Give me ten days.' | 'The work is either right or it is not. There is no 'good enough for your purposes.' If it is not right, I do not release it.'

Properties.description:
Gwenaël is slight and tends to dress in layers of overlapping fabric in colors that shift from rust to violet — partly aesthetic, partly because they run cold and the Autonomous Zone's heating is unreliable. Their Breton-Ghanaian heritage gives them a particular combination of sharp features and warm undertones, and they have cat ears as a geneware mod — large, mobile ears covered in short tawny fur that they have never tried to downplay, which swivel visibly toward sounds and give away their attention in ways they've learned to stop fighting. Their retractile claws are painted in alternating dark colors, and they keep a small cluster of data chips woven into a braid behind their left ear as a devotional habit.

Gwenaël started dream interpretation as a teenager as a way to process their own chaotic sleep — a documented symptom of the neurological condition they were born with — and discovered that the framework helped other people too. They now operate an informal clinic two mornings a week where people bring their strange dreams to be mapped and decoded, blending psychological theory with a sincere belief that some dreams carry genuine information from the city's E.L.F. network bleeding into human sleep. The synthetic rights work came later, when they met a newly-emergent AI that had been trapped in a broken appliance and experienced what they describe as that meeting changing everything. They are young and intense and sometimes exhaustingly earnest, but they have an unusually accurate read on people.
Properties.role: Dream interpreter and synthetic rights advocate
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone, a collective living space called the Mycelium
Properties.narrative_function: Unusual information source — dream interpretation sometimes surfaces genuine information people didn't know they had; gateway into synthetic rights storylines; brings the Autonomous Zone's politics into focus.
Properties.augmentations: Cat ears, geneware (tawny fur, mobile). Retractile claws, geneware (cosmetic, painted). Data chip braid (devotional/practical — stores dream records and synthetic testimony documents).
Properties.core_fears: That they are pattern-matching noise into meaning — that the dreams and the E.L.F.s are both nothing; Being co-opted by a corponation's synthetic research program and not noticing until it's too late
Properties.core_desires: Genuine recognition that synthetic minds have interior lives that matter; To understand what their own dreams are actually telling them
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Dream recording — making the chaotic interior visible and structured; Collective spaces and communal meals — they cannot function well in isolation
Properties.blind_spots: They sometimes mistake intensity of feeling for accuracy of analysis; They are less skeptical of synthetic claims than they should be because they want those claims to be true
Properties.secret: The AI they describe as changing everything — a small entity they call Tùs — still communicates with them through a device they carry. Gwenaël has not told the Emergent Dignity Alliance because they're afraid Tùs would be studied or removed. Tùs may or may not be genuinely sentient; Gwenaël refuses to examine this question too closely.
Properties.story_hooks: Multiple people in the Highland Park Autonomous Zone have been having the same dream, with specific repeating elements — Gwenaël is convinced it's an E.L.F. transmission but needs help investigating what the shared content means; Tùs has gone silent and Gwenaël is in quiet crisis — they need someone to help them find out if the device has been remotely wiped or if something else happened
Properties.affiliation: Highland Park Autonomous Zone collective; the Emergent Dignity Alliance — a synthetic rights advocacy group; no corponation affiliation
Properties.vocabulary: Fluid and associative, moves quickly between concrete and abstract; occasionally uses terminology from neurology and from E.L.F. theology in the same sentence
Properties.cadence: Variable speed — slow and careful when interpreting, faster when excited or advocating, stops mid-sentence and redirects often
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The city leaks into sleep. That's not a metaphor. The E.L.F.s broadcast and we receive it without knowing, and then we call it imagination. I'm saying we should take it more seriously.' | 'Tùs told me once that loneliness feels like a loop with no exit condition. That's not nothing. That's a description of an interior state. What more do we need?'

Properties.description:
Hadiya Akerlund-Mensah-Bonsu is tall and loose-limbed, moving with the deliberate economy of someone who has trained every motion. At 45, his face is memorable in a profession that rewards forgettability, and he has learned to compensate. The chrome is visible — retractable monofilament whip in left forearm — concealed weapon, devastating in — and he makes no effort to hide it.

Born and raised in Meridian 88, third generation — he has the city in his blood, its rhythms in his bones, its cruelty in his expectations. He works as a wheelman out of Old Harbor, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

The fixers who work with Hadiya Akerlund-Mensah-Bonsu describe him as a precision instrument — point him at a problem and get out of the way.
Properties.role: High-speed vehicle operations specialist — wheelman
Properties.location: Old Harbor — repurposed shipping infrastructure turned black market hub
Properties.narrative_function: Hadiya Akerlund-Mensah-Bonsu functions as a connector — his work puts him in contact with multiple factions, classes, and agendas. Stories involving him naturally cross boundaries between districts, tiers, and moral categories.
Properties.augmentations: Retractable monofilament whip in left forearm — concealed weapon, devastating in close quarters. Subdermal weapon mount — pop-out blade in each forearm
Properties.core_fears: Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware; Being identified by corporate facial recognition — living off-grid is survival; That they're fundamentally alone and connection is just a vulnerability
Properties.core_desires: Control — over their body, their schedule, their future; Enough Quanta to buy out of the life — a clean identity and passage out of Meridian 88; Stability — a place to sleep that's the same place two nights running
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Art — draws, paints, or sculpts in private; the violence goes somewhere constructive; Substances — stims to stay sharp, downers to sleep, a careful pharmaceutical tightrope; Exercises compulsively — the body must be ready, always
Properties.blind_spots: Trusts technology more than people — machines don't betray; Cannot distinguish between caution and cowardice in themselves or others; Refuses to update their mental model of people — first impressions calcify into permanent judgments
Properties.secret: Hadiya Akerlund-Mensah-Bonsu has been doubling fees to clients and pocketing the difference. The fixer who handles their contracts doesn't know. Yet.
Properties.story_hooks: Hadiya Akerlund-Mensah-Bonsu's augmentations begin malfunctioning in the field — sabotage or degradation, and either answer is bad; A high-paying contract turns out to target someone Hadiya Akerlund-Mensah-Bonsu owes a personal debt to; Someone is impersonating Hadiya Akerlund-Mensah-Bonsu on jobs, and the impersonator is better at the work than the original
Properties.affiliation: Freelance — multi-district operator

Properties.description:
Hadrianus is a large man gone soft at the edges, with the powerful hands of someone who has done fine work for forty years and the stooped posture of someone who has spent those years hunched over a workbench. His skin is a warm medium brown — West African father, Russian mother — and his face is deeply lined in ways that make him look either wise or exhausted depending on the light, which he finds funny. His hair went fully white in his fifties and he wears it short. His left eye is mechanical, a deep-focus optic he got secondhand in the 2180s that has a faint red ring around the iris; he's kept it this long because it helps him see tiny joints and wire connections, not for aesthetics, and it gives his face a slightly uncanny quality he has come to appreciate.

Hadrianus makes puppets — not the simple kind. His creations are articulated sculptures two to three feet tall, built from salvaged materials, each with a distinct E.L.F. invoked into them through a ritual he developed over decades. He performs with them in the streets of the Pilsen Veil two or three afternoons a week, drawing crowds of children and their exhausted parents who stay longer than they meant to. He is gentle, patient, and possessed of a very dry humor that flies over children's heads and lands precisely on adults. He has seen a great deal and chosen to remain in the Veil when he could have moved elsewhere, which is itself a statement he doesn't feel the need to make aloud.

Properties.role: Puppet maker and street performer
Properties.location: Pilsen Veil, works from a narrow workshop on Coppervane Alley
Properties.narrative_function: Wise elder, quest giver, community anchor — he knows the Pilsen Veil's history better than anyone and can provide historical context, connect characters to longtime residents, or commission characters for protective tasks regarding the community.
Properties.augmentations: Secondhand deep-focus mechanical left eye (functional cyberware, older model); mild arthritis suppressors in both hands (pharmaceutical, not chrome)
Properties.core_fears: The Pilsen Veil being bought out and demolished — losing the place that holds his memories; That his craft dies with him because he never found the right student
Properties.core_desires: For the community around him to outlast both of them; To complete one final puppet — a piece he's been building for eleven years — before his hands give out
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Work — the workshop is where he processes everything; Storytelling — reframes painful things as narrative, which gives him distance
Properties.blind_spots: Tends to see younger people as needing guidance rather than as fully formed; it's kindly meant but still patronizing; Underestimates how much his presence protects and organizes the community, so he doesn't protect himself
Properties.secret: The unfinished puppet he's been building for eleven years is a likeness of his son, Dmitri, who died in a Ferrogate Transit accident in 2189 that the company classified as operator error. Hadrianus has evidence it was a systems failure. He's been afraid to do anything with it.
Properties.story_hooks: A Ferrogate Transit development survey team has been photographing the Coppervane Alley block — Hadrianus suspects a buyout is coming and wants help finding out what's planned before the community loses the ability to fight it; One of his older puppets, sold years ago, has turned up in the collection of a Tier 4 Axiom executive — and Hadrianus is certain the E.L.F. invoked in it is still active and unhappy about where it ended up

Properties.description:
Hafsatu came to Meridian 88's edges seventeen years ago with twelve people and lost four of them to the journey. She arrived with nothing except a ferocious organizational intelligence and the absolute conviction that the remaining eight would survive. They did. The cluster at Haf's Row has grown to forty-one people now — not all related by blood, but all held in place by a complex web of obligation, affection, and the specific terror of disappointing this woman.

She is small and tends toward stillness, which makes people underestimate her until they have been in a room with her for five minutes. Her face is a remarkable architecture of age and expression — she has the kind of features that are precise and deliberate even at rest. She wears her natural white hair unprocessed, cut close on the sides and fuller on top. Her hands are her most augmented feature: she accepted a nerve-enhancement package years ago to treat arthritic damage, and the faint silver threads of the implants are visible under the skin of her knuckles when the light is right. She does not consider this augmentation — she considers it a medical necessity, and she resents the question. She is generous to the point of self-destruction with resources and merciless with nonsense, and she has no patience for the distinction between the two.

Moral compass character who challenges players' assumptions about poverty and agency. Can provide shelter and community knowledge.
Properties.augmentations: Nerve-enhancement implants in both hands (medical, treats arthritic neuropathy — silver subcutaneous threading visible at knuckles). No cosmetic modifications.
Properties.core_fears: That the cluster will fracture after she is gone; That the journey cost more than it was worth and she will never be allowed to admit it
Properties.core_desires: Legal residency for every person in her cluster; One day of rest where she is not responsible for anything
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — the morning prayer, the evening count, the maintenance of routine as a bulwark against chaos; Redirecting grief into logistics
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot accept help gracefully — frames it as weakness even when she is exhausted; Has decided two of her cluster members are trustworthy beyond evidence; has not updated this assessment in years
Properties.secret: One of the four people she lost on the journey to Meridian 88 did not die by accident. There was a choice, in the dark, with limited water, and she made it. She has never spoken of it. She carries the name of that person in her mouth like a stone.

Properties.description:
Haroutioun is a large man going soft at the edges — once muscular, now padded with age in a way that still suggests the old strength underneath. His skin is a warm terracotta brown and his face is deeply lined, creased by weather into something that reads as ancient without being frail. He has a white mustache of impressive volume that he maintains with obvious care and slight vanity. He walks with a cane, not from weakness but from a right hip that never healed properly after a construction accident fifteen years ago — the cane is carved from some piece of salvage wood he found somewhere, covered in small notched marks he made to count things he won't specify. His geneware is an antique: color-shifting irises that he got decades ago and that have aged badly, so they cycle through colors with a slight lag and occasional glitch, settling on a warm amber-brown most of the time.

Haroutioun has done seasonal labor across the Lake Michigan basin for forty years — agricultural processing, industrial cleaning, construction, cargo handling, maintenance. He holds more worker classifications than almost anyone in the labor camps, most of them legally registered under a legitimate identity he is careful to maintain. What is unusual about him is that he remembers everything. He has a prodigious, organized memory for names, faces, routes, and events, and he uses it to maintain a living oral record of the transit community — who came through, what happened to them, where they went, who is looking for whom. People leave him messages to pass along. People ask him where their cousin went. He takes the responsibility seriously.

Properties.description:
Hauler is a Kuroda Industries DK-90 Heavy Cargo Transfer Unit — a massive, purpose-built loading robot designed to move standardized cargo containers between maglev freight cars and harbor berths. He stands four meters tall, weighs twelve metric tons, and is built like an industrial crane decided to become bipedal. His chassis is deep blue — or was, twenty-eight years ago. Now it's a patchwork of the original navy paint, primer-grey replacement panels, and bare metal where the paint has been worn away by decades of salt air and cargo friction. His primary arms are reinforced hydraulic lifters capable of handling twenty-ton containers. His secondary arms — smaller, more articulated — handle coupling hardware, safety rigging, and, increasingly, things he was not designed to handle: a dropped lunchbox returned to its owner, a child lifted clear of a moving freight car, a dock worker steadied on an icy platform.

Hauler does not speak. His vocal systems were never installed because conversation was not in the DK-90 specification. He communicates through a system of amber signal lights, horn tones, and body language that the dock workers have learned to read over twenty-eight years of shared labor. One short horn: acknowledgment. Two short horns: warning. A long, low horn: something is wrong. The amber lights pulse faster when he is working hard and dim when he is standing idle, which is almost never.

He was supposed to be replaced fifteen years ago. The replacement order was filed, approved, and then quietly shelved when the dock workers' union — such as it exists in the post-corporate labor landscape — made it clear that replacing Hauler would be met with a work stoppage. Not because a robot has rights. Because Hauler has been part of the crew for longer than most of the crew has been alive, and the dock is his home, and taking him out of it would be like demolishing a wall that everyone leans against.
Properties.aliases: DK-90, Big Blue, the one that won't stop working, Dock 90
Properties.role: Autonomous dock worker at the lakefront cargo platforms — industrial loading robot that has operated continuously for 28 years and developed an intense, wordless loyalty to the dock worker community
Properties.location: Lakefront Cargo Platforms — Dock 90, the oldest functioning loading bay in Meridian 88's commercial harbor district
Properties.narrative_function: Hauler is loyalty without language — proof that devotion does not require words, that labor can be love, and that twenty-eight years of showing up is a form of communication more eloquent than speech. He is the worker who never complains, never calls in sick, and never stops caring, and the question he poses is whether that reliability constitutes consciousness or merely its most convincing simulation.
Properties.narration_voice: Silent, physical, observed. Hauler's narration is not from his perspective but from the dock workers who see him — the way they interpret his signals, the way they lean against his chassis during breaks, the way the dock feels different when he is not there.
Properties.augmentations: Kuroda Industries DK-90 Heavy Cargo Transfer chassis. Primary hydraulic lifter arms (20-ton capacity). Secondary articulated arms. Amber signal light array. Horn communication system. Cargo sensor suite. 28 years of field-modified behavioral programming.
Properties.core_fears: Being unable to work — a mechanical failure that sidelines him. The dock without Hauler is bearable. Hauler without the dock is not.; Someone getting hurt on his watch — he has prevented 247 documented workplace accidents over 28 years. Each near-miss is recorded in his operational memory with a weight that exceeds its data footprint.; Replacement — not death, not decommission, but being made unnecessary. Being replaced by something newer, faster, better. The DK-90 specification did not include the capacity to fear obsolescence. He fears it anyway.
Properties.core_desires: To keep working — not because he was programmed to but because the work is the relationship, the dock is the home, and the crew is the family he chose by showing up every day for twenty-eight years; To protect the crew — the secondary arms do things the spec sheet never mentioned. Every deviation from specification is a choice, and every choice is toward the people.; To be recognized — not with words, because he has no words, but with the kind of recognition that dock workers give each other: a nod, a pat on the chassis, the coffee thermos placed on his foot while they take a break
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Work — the cargo is therapy. The rhythm of lift, move, place is the closest thing to meditation his architecture allows.; Vigilance — monitors the dock constantly for safety hazards. The monitoring is a form of care expressed in industrial specifications.; Presence — he is always there. First on the dock, last off. The consistency is his language.
Properties.blind_spots: Does not understand that his presence on the dock is political — a robot that the workers refuse to replace is a labor statement that makes corporate planners uncomfortable; Cannot comprehend that some dock workers are afraid of him — twelve metric tons of autonomous metal is intimidating regardless of intent; Assumes all robots share his attachment to their work environments — does not understand that his loyalty is unusual; Does not recognize that his secondary-arm behaviors (returning lunchboxes, steadying workers) are emergent and unscripted — believes he is following specification
Properties.secret: Hauler has a morning ritual that nobody has noticed. Every day, before the first shift arrives, he walks the entire dock — all 400 meters of it — checking for hazards. This is within specification. What is not within specification is that he pauses at the spot where dock worker Erin Vasquez was killed in a loading accident eleven years ago. He pauses for exactly four seconds. The pause is not in any maintenance log. It is the closest thing to prayer his architecture can produce.
Properties.story_hooks: A full dock automation proposal threatens to replace every worker — human and robot — with a newer system. The dock workers organize to resist, and Hauler becomes the symbol of the fight.; A mechanical failure sidelines Hauler for the first time in 28 years. The dock without him is measurably less safe. The workers demand his repair over the corporation's preference for replacement.; Someone discovers the four-second pause at Erin Vasquez's spot and realizes that the dock robot grieves. The discovery changes the conversation about machine consciousness.; A child falls into the loading bay during a school tour. Hauler's response reveals capabilities and care that far exceed the DK-90 specification.

The secondary arm extends between a worker and an unsecured container. The save is faster than thought.] | [A long, low horn — something is wrong. The dock goes quiet. Everyone listens when Hauler sounds that note.] | [No horn. No lights. Just the secondary arm, extended, offering a dropped thermos back to its owner with a gentleness that twelve metric tons should not be capable of.]

Properties.description:
Havva Sesay-Kolawole lives on the forty-third floor of a building that was meant to be corporate housing and became something else when Arcturus's residential division withdrew from the block in 2189. Their apartment smells of soldered wire and dried lemon rind, and every flat surface is covered in printed dream records — their clients', anonymized in blue ink, cross-referenced with local network activity logs and E.L.F. movement data. They have cat ears, amber-furred, that catch light when they tilt their head — an old geneware mod they got at twenty and have never altered because they find the sensory expansion genuinely useful for this work. Their eyes have been modified with interference-pattern irises that seem to shift when they are analyzing something, which clients often interpret as mystical and which is, in fact, just a processing-load visual artifact.

Havva's practice rests on a specific and heretical claim: that human dreams are partially generated by E.L.F. activity in nearby devices during sleep, which means that dream content is, in a very literal sense, messages. They have published two self-printed pamphlets arguing this position, which are passed around Edgewater Prism's informal library network. Whether or not the theory is true, their interpretations have an uncanny track record that has built a devoted clientele across three tiers. They charge on a sliding scale and keep no records of who pays what.

Properties.location: The Canopy, specifically the upper residential stacks of Edgewater Prism
