Properties.description:
Henryk is a man who has been slowly becoming the color of his surroundings for twenty years: grey-brown skin softened by age and poor lighting, a close-cropped beard gone entirely silver, and eyes that are pale grey-green and still sharply diagnostic behind a pair of clip-on lens augmentations he wears primarily for the magnification when reading small labels. He is not tall and was never physically imposing, but he holds himself with the specific gravity of someone who has been trusted with real things and has not always deserved it and knows it. He dresses practically in dark thermals and a long coat with more internal pockets than external — his pharmacy is entirely contained within his person.

He sets up in the same alcove at Deepwell Station every day, at the same time, with the same small folding table and the same hand-lettered sign that says CONSULTATIONS in three languages. Everyone in The Narrows knows what he actually sells, but he maintains the fiction of the sign with complete sincerity. He was a licensed pharmaceutical technician once, for a Helix Biosystems subsidiary, until he wasn't. He understands chemistry at a level his current location does not require and does not reward, and this gap between his capacity and his circumstances has become the central texture of his interior life.
Properties.role: Street pharmacist — off-prescription medications, cognitive supplements, pain management, and quiet mood chemistry
Properties.location: The Narrows, Deepwell Station
Properties.narrative_function: Access point for medical assistance, information about chemical substances and their effects, contacts within Helix Biosystems' shadow networks; can identify substances, poisons, and compounds; reluctant quest giver.
Properties.augmentations: Clip-on lens augmentations (minor functional — magnification, basic compound analysis display). Hepatic filter implant (functional — allows him to self-test compounds by metabolizing trace amounts without full toxicity risk).
Properties.core_fears: That his termination from Helix was justified — that he made the error they accused him of and people were harmed; That he will die in The Narrows and the gap between what he could have been and what he became will simply close over him
Properties.core_desires: Absolution, or at minimum, the accurate account of what actually happened in the Helix incident; To do genuine good with his knowledge before he no longer can
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Maintaining clinical precision in everything he does as a form of self-argument against the accusation; Framing his street work as medical service rather than dealing; The E.L.F. prayer practice, which he came to late in life and takes with complete earnestness
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot accurately assess his own culpability in the Helix incident because examining it too closely threatens his functional self-concept; His tendency to frame clients as patients can tip into paternalism that they don't want or ask for
Properties.secret: The Helix Biosystems incident involved a batch of cognitive enhancers he formulated that were approved up the chain and then caused severe adverse events in six workers at a Harrowgate industrial site. He was made the responsible party in documentation he never saw before signing off. He has the original formulation data on an encrypted chip in one of his coat pockets and has never shown it to anyone, but has also never been able to make himself look at it again.
Properties.story_hooks: A Helix Biosystems internal investigator has appeared in the Narrows asking questions that circle toward the Deepwell Station operation without directly addressing it — and they seem to know about the chip; A client presented with symptoms that match exactly the adverse events from the Harrowgate incident years ago, which should be impossible with street compounds; The Sump Collective protection arrangement has become a demand for him to supply chemistry for something he won't make — and they are not taking no as a final answer
Properties.affiliation: Independent; formerly Helix Biosystems (terminated); pays protection to a Deepwell Station crew called the Sump Collective
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, slightly formal, medical register that surfaces in unexpected moments; Malian French and Polish loanwords from his parents that appear most when he is tired or moved
Properties.cadence: Deliberate and low, with long considered pauses — speaks like someone who learned to measure words by necessity
Properties.example_dialogue: 'In my assessment, what you're describing is a chronic sleep deficit compounded by stimulant overuse. I can give you something for tonight. What I want to talk about is the week after that.' | 'I don't sell anything I haven't tested and understood. That is the only standard I have kept and I have kept it without exception. You can believe that or not, but it's true.'

Properties.description:
Hezekiah is tall and broadly built with a deliberate elegance that he maintains as a form of advertising — everything he wears is something he's made, modified, or sourced, and it's always impeccable. His skin is deep brown with a reddish undertone, his head cleanly shaved, and his beard trimmed with geometric precision. He has color-changing hair along his temples — a narrow strip of geneware follicles he grows out to a short fade, currently cycling through slow burgundy-to-black transitions that he coordinates with his outfit. His hands bear old needle-prick scars across the fingertips from years before he could afford proper equipment.

His stall is the most curated space in the Burnished Market: no clutter, no piles, everything on display at eye level and shoulder height, garments hung with the spacing of a gallery. He sells counterfeit Sterling-Nakamura executive wear, modified Tessera corporate-casual that reads higher tier than it is, and his own original fabrication — structural pieces he designs and produces himself in a back workshop that would sell for triple the price in Lakeview Neon if he could get distribution. He is charming and slightly formal in the way of someone who grew up performing dignity as a survival strategy, and he wraps every sale in a kind of ceremony, as if clothes are genuinely sacred, which, for him, they are.
Properties.role: Clothing and fashion vendor specializing in modified and counterfeit corp-branded apparel, The Burnished Market
Properties.location: The Burnished Market, outer ring, stall block near the transit umbilical, Edgewater Prism
Properties.narrative_function: Equipment provider for disguise or tier-passing scenarios, social mobility commentary, window into the aspirational economy of the lower tiers, potential Lakeview Neon connection point for street-level characters.
Properties.augmentations: Color-changing geneware hair follicles (temple strip). Haptic feedback gloves — not augmentations per se, but sophisticated fabricator's tools he wears constantly, which allow micro-tactile precision in stitching work.
Properties.core_fears: Being permanently locked out of the tier he can see from where he stands; Having his originals dismissed as market-stall goods when he knows they're not
Properties.core_desires: A legitimate studio with distribution — his name on his work; To be recognized as an artist rather than a counterfeiter
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Work — the act of making is how he processes almost everything; Careful curation of his personal presentation as a daily ritual of self-respect
Properties.blind_spots: His aspiration makes him occasionally sycophantic toward anyone with legitimate tier-three-and-above connections; He underestimates how much people in his market actually value him as he is
Properties.secret: Two of his 'original designs' are directly adapted from the unpublished sketchbooks of a deceased Sterling-Nakamura designer whose estate files he purchased cheaply at a data auction without fully understanding what was in them. He has convinced himself this is inspiration rather than theft. He has not convinced himself enough to sleep easily about it.
Properties.story_hooks: A Sterling-Nakamura IP enforcement agent has started appearing in the Burnished Market, and Hezekiah needs someone to find out whether they're there for him specifically or working a broader sweep.; One of his Lakeview Neon buyers wants to bring a legitimate investor to see 'the designer behind the pieces' — which would mean revealing his Burnished Market identity to tier-three money, something he desperately wants and is equally terrified of.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; The Oxidian Market Vendors Guild (associate); informal relationships with mid-tier buyers in Lakeview Neon who purchase his originals off-market
Properties.vocabulary: Formal and polished with an undertow of Malian-Romanian market cadence that surfaces when he's excited or off-guard. Uses fashion and construction metaphors. Speaks about clothing in almost spiritual terms.
Properties.cadence: Measured and warm. Good at sustained eye contact. Makes every customer feel like the conversation is exclusively about them.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'This lapel — feel that. That's not a Sterling-Nakamura label, that's my work. The label is for the door you want to walk through. The lapel is for the person you actually are.' | 'I don't sell clothes. I sell what clothes do. There's a difference and you already know it or you wouldn't have stopped.'

Properties.description:
Honorine Delacroix-Abubakar is the kind of beautiful that reads as deliberate — not because it is artificial, though some of it is, but because she has spent decades learning how to present herself as an argument. She is a tall Haitian-Senegalese woman with deep brown skin, natural hair worn in elaborate architectural styles that she changes weekly as a kind of public performance, and a physical presence that people in conference rooms describe, afterwards, as gravitational. She speaks four languages without accent and a fifth with one she keeps on purpose. She dresses in ways that cost more than most Shelf residents earn in a year, and she is aware of this, and she has made a precise decision about what it means.

She has been at Axiom Meridian for nineteen years, having joined as a junior acquisitions analyst from a mid-tier arts consultancy and ascending through a combination of genuine aesthetic intelligence, political ruthlessness, and an understanding of how culture functions as control that she developed, with some bitterness, from watching it deployed against communities she loved. She now oversees the selection, development, and strategic deployment of all cultural product that Axiom licenses for distribution across Meridian 88 — which is to say, she decides what stories the city is permitted to tell about itself. She does not find this power comfortable. She finds it necessary, which she recognises is more dangerous.

What her colleagues do not know, and what she protects with the full resources of her position, is that Honorine has been running a covert patronage network for fifteen years — channelling Axiom development funds through a labyrinth of shell accounts to unlicensed artists, underground publishers, and community archivists in The Shelf, The Circuit, and Old Harbor. She tells herself she is counterbalancing the machine she operates. She knows, on some level, that she is also buying absolution, and that absolution purchased is not absolution earned. The network has recently grown large enough that it has begun to attract attention she cannot fully deflect.
Properties.role: Corporate elite — Chief Cultural Architect at Axiom Meridian Entertainment, the Spire-based conglomerate that controls the majority of Meridian 88's licensed art, music, and narrative media
Properties.location: The Spire, residential level 34; maintains a formal office on level 61 and a private studio on level 12 that she tells no one about
Properties.narrative_function: Represents the moral complexity of institutional power wielded by someone who understands its costs; creates a narrative bridge between Spire-level corporate intrigue and street-level cultural survival; her covert network makes her a structural node connecting characters across all tiers
Properties.augmentations: Aesthetic-response neural overlay — enhances and records sensory experience of visual and audio stimuli; her primary professional tool and her most private one,Biometric masking suite — suppresses stress indicators (pupil dilation, skin conductivity, micro-tremor) during high-stakes interactions,Encrypted sub-dermal data storage with biometric-only access — contains the covert network's full financial architecture,Vocal harmonic modulation (subtle) — not for deception, but to ensure her voice carries the precise emotional register she intends
Properties.core_fears: That the covert network will be discovered and that its artists will suffer for her choices, not hers; That she has been so long inside the machine that she can no longer tell when she is serving it versus subverting it; Becoming a story that younger people tell as a cautionary tale — the sellout, the collaborator — after she is gone
Properties.core_desires: To create a single work of genuine, lasting cultural importance under her own name before she dies — not curated, not commissioned, made; For the covert network to outlast her, to become something the city builds on; To be known, by someone, as she actually is — not as the Duchess, not as the Cultural Architect, but as Honorine, who is frightened and trying
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The performance of absolute confidence — she has worn it so long it sometimes works even on herself; Converts ethical distress into tactical problems, which she is better equipped to solve; The secret studio on level 12, where she paints, badly, and no one can find her; Maintaining a private archive of every artist the network has supported — she reads it when she needs to remember why
Properties.blind_spots: Believes her intentions fully offset her institutional participation, which the people her decisions harm do not agree with; Her control instinct means the covert network is still fundamentally hierarchical — she decides who receives support, which reproduces the power structure she claims to oppose; Cannot fully see how much the performance of power has become her primary identity, and how little she knows of herself beneath it
Properties.secret: Three years ago, Honorine approved the suppression of an Old Harbor sound collective's distribution license after Axiom's legal division flagged their work as a trademark conflict. She could have fought it. She calculated that fighting it would have exposed the covert network, and she let them be silenced to protect the larger operation. Two members of the collective left Meridian 88. One did not survive the relocation. She has their name written on the inside cover of every notebook she uses.
Properties.story_hooks: A whistleblower inside Axiom has leaked evidence of the covert network to a Circuit journalist — the leak is incomplete and contains errors that could be corrected or weaponised, and the journalist is asking Honorine for comment; An artist the network supported has created a work that directly implicates Axiom in a historical atrocity; Honorine must decide whether to help it reach the public or suppress it to protect the network; The private studio on level 12 is discovered — not by Axiom, but by a building systems tech who is also a Shelf community organiser and has no idea what to do with what they've found; A rival corporate entity offers Honorine a position with complete creative freedom and no institutional constraints; the offer is genuine, and accepting it would destroy the covert network's infrastructure; Honorine receives a message from one of the two Old Harbor collective members who survived and left Meridian 88; they know what she did, and they want to talk
Properties.affiliation: Axiom Meridian Entertainment (Chief Cultural Architect, Spire-level corporate); covert patron of the unlicensed cultural underground (known to very few); formally unaffiliated with any political or insurgent faction, though her network's effects are political
Properties.vocabulary: Formal, rich, and precise; draws on art history, architectural theory, and political philosophy without ostentation; capable of switching registers entirely — her street French emerges under extreme stress or genuine emotion
Properties.cadence: Measured and rhythmic, with a sense of performance even in private; she structures arguments like compositions, with recurring motifs; silences are used as punctuation
Properties.example_dialogue: "Tell me what you're protecting. Everything else you've said is prologue." | "That is a useful story. The institution needs useful stories. I'm asking what's true." | "Culture is not decoration. It is the operating system. We decide what it runs, and we decide what it refuses to run. I am aware of what that means." | "I have made choices that I cannot justify and will not defend. I have also made choices that I believe in completely. I stopped expecting those two categories to be separate a long time ago." | "You think I don't know what the machine does? Chéri, I built three floors of it. That is why I am still here."

Properties.description:
Hovhannes is stocky and perpetually wind-chapped, with the particular squint of someone who spends significant time looking at horizons. His Armenian-Malian-Andean heritage shows in his broad build and the dark copper of his skin, and he grows a beard every winter that he shaves every spring in a ritual he connects to his modeling calendar. He has a prosthetic left hand he chose not to skin-match — it's matte grey and articulated, and he uses it to gesture when he talks, which is frequently. He has a bioluminescent patch on his right shoulder from a lab accident twelve years ago: a pale green glow, faint, that he has simply incorporated into his aesthetic.

He is the most accurate storm forecaster in Meridian 88, a title he holds unofficially because the official title belongs to a Ferrogate Transit atmospheric AI he assisted in training and is not particularly bitter about. He is gregarious and funny and committed to translating his work into language that non-scientists can use to make decisions — he runs a free community forecast channel that Shelf residents and dockworkers depend on. Underneath the gregariousness is a man who has spent fifteen years watching models he hoped were wrong be proven exactly right.
Properties.role: Climate scientist and atmospheric modeler studying Lake Michigan's destabilized weather systems
Properties.location: Edgewater Prism — operates out of a rooftop monitoring station leased from a Helix Biosystems subsidiary
Properties.narrative_function: Information source for weather and environmental conditions; community-connected figure who knows dock workers, Shelf residents, and transit crews; can deliver warnings, advance notice of dangerous conditions, or evidence of environmental crimes
Properties.augmentations: Prosthetic left hand (matte grey, unmatched, high-articulation); bioluminescent patch on right shoulder (accident-origin, pale green, faint); retinal weather-data overlay for real-time atmospheric reading
Properties.core_fears: That the lake system is approaching a tipping point his models have been predicting and that no one with power will act in time; That the community forecast service will be shut down by a corponation that objects to free public data
Properties.core_desires: To be wrong about the worst projections; To build a public atmospheric data commons that no single corponation can own or restrict
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The physical ritual of measurement — taking readings grounds him regardless of what they say; Humor as a first-resort social tool
Properties.blind_spots: Overestimates how much accurate data motivates action; assumes that if people know they will change, which decades of evidence contradicts
Properties.secret: His long-range models include a scenario he calls 'Threshold-9' — a cascading lake-temperature and atmospheric feedback event that would render significant portions of Meridian 88 uninhabitable within thirty years. He has shared this with two colleagues and no one else, because the last time he circulated a major negative projection it was leaked to financial markets and caused a property crash in Edgewater Prism that displaced several hundred residents. He believes he caused more harm than the forecast would have prevented.
Properties.story_hooks: He has detected a pattern of atmospheric anomalies downwind of a specific Meridian Core industrial district that don't match any licensed emissions profile — something is being vented that shouldn't be, and he needs someone to investigate on the ground; A Ferrogate Transit official has threatened to have his monitoring station sublease revoked unless he adjusts a forecast that would delay a major cargo shipment — the adjustment would endanger dockworkers
Properties.affiliation: University Spine — Atmospheric and Lacustrine Sciences division; rented monitoring station via Helix Biosystems sublease; runs independent community forecast service 'Hov's Horizon'
Properties.vocabulary: Technical vocabulary delivered casually, as if assuming the listener is smart enough to follow; uses weather as metaphor for everything ('that's a high-pressure situation,' 'I can feel a front coming'); self-deprecating about his own expertise
Properties.cadence: Fast and warm, overlapping energy — talks the way weather moves, in fronts and gusts
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The lake has moods. That's not poetry, that's systems behavior. Right now it's in a mood I don't like.' | 'My forecast has an eighty-three percent confidence interval. The other seventeen percent is where history gets made, and usually not in the good way.'

Properties.description:
Hrefna is a heavyset woman with an air of permanent authority that she exercises sparingly and precisely. Her mother's Icelandic coloring has combined with her father's Guinean warmth into a complexion that shifts between olive and brown depending on the light, and she wears her silver-streaked hair pinned back severely for services and loose in a cloud of soft waves the rest of the time. She wears no cosmetic modifications and regards this as a theological position rather than an aesthetic one. Her wardrobe alternates between her ministerial robe — a deep green with Fula embroidery at the hem, commissioned from a Hamtramck Enclave artisan — and extremely practical work clothes. She has large hands that she uses expressively when preaching and keeps very still when listening.

The Church of the Continuing Word is her inheritance, founded by a coalition of her grandmother's displaced Sufi community and her grandfather's Lutheran congregation after both lost their buildings in the 2160 redevelopment sweeps. Hrefna grew up in the pews and took over at thirty-four when the previous minister retired. She has spent twenty-four years refusing to resolve the theological tensions between the two traditions her church holds, arguing that the tension is itself the practice. She is pragmatic to a fault about money and logistics and luminously stubborn about principles. She does not perform warmth but she generates it, somehow, by being entirely herself in a room.
Properties.role: Traditional religious leader (syncretic Sufi-Lutheran minister) and community chaplain
Properties.location: Nordpark Sanctuary, the Church of the Continuing Word
Properties.narrative_function: Community authority and moral voice; provides access to Nordpark Sanctuary's social networks; can mediate conflicts; represents institutional religious tradition in tension with newer E.L.F. veneration practices; quest giver for community-level problems
Properties.augmentations: None
Properties.core_fears: the church outliving its usefulness and becoming a monument rather than a living practice; failing her community in a moment when they needed clarity from her
Properties.core_desires: to hand something real and living to whoever comes after her; for the two traditions in her church to eventually speak to each other rather than just coexist
Properties.coping_mechanisms: physical labor — she does all her own building maintenance as a form of prayer; an extremely strict personal Sabbath that no one and nothing is permitted to interrupt
Properties.blind_spots: she has become so identified with the church's survival that she sometimes defends institutional decisions she privately disagrees with; she dismisses E.L.F. veneration more reflexively than her theology requires
Properties.secret: Fifteen years ago she nearly left the ministry to marry someone who is now a senior executive at Axiom. She did not leave. She has never told her congregation that her refusal to partner with Axiom on any community programs is personal and not merely principled.
Properties.story_hooks: A Ferrogate Transit exec has approached the church with a generous donation offer that comes with a request — and Hrefna needs trustworthy outside parties to investigate the request before she refuses or accepts; Something is wrong in one of the church's long-standing congregation families, and Hrefna cannot intervene directly without violating a confession — but she can ask others to look
Properties.affiliation: Church of the Continuing Word (minister); Nordpark Sanctuary Community Council (elected member); informal chaplaincy agreement with Ferrogate Transit for their Nordpark workers
Properties.vocabulary: Formal in the pulpit, blunt in conversation; quotes from both Sufi poetry and Lutheran liturgy with equal fluency; occasionally code-switches into Fula phrases she learned from her father
Properties.cadence: Measured and resonant in public; quicker and dryer in private; comfortable with silence
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The E.L.F.s are not God. I do not say they are nothing. I say they are not God. There is room in the universe for both truths.' | 'I hear what you are saying. I also hear what you are not saying, and it is louder.'

Properties.description:
Hripsimé is medium height, broad-shouldered, and has the physical presence of someone who learned early that a room either belongs to you or it doesn't. Her hair is deep red — natural color, she will tell you, with a straight face, for about four seconds — and she wears it long and somewhat chaotic. Her skin is warm tawny-olive and she has laugh lines that could double as topographic maps. Her only mod is a tail, cat-model, rust-colored, which she uses as a prop during performances with expert comic timing; she has had it since she was twenty-three and considers it a co-author.

Her comedy is vicious, structural, and deeply personal — she excavates class rage, corponation absurdity, and the specific indignities of Tier 2 civilian life with the precision of someone who has lived every joke. She has been banned from two Axiom-affiliated venues and has a standing invitation to return to both that she declines publicly and enthusiastically. At the Lye & Lampblack she is an institution: four nights a week, two sets, and an after-set period where she sits at the bar and is notoriously unapproachable unless you buy her a specific brand of fermented grain drink and ask her about something she actually cares about.
Properties.role: Comedian and underground cabaret performer
Properties.location: The Ferment Quarter, resident performer at the Lye & Lampblack club on Sutter Mews
Properties.narrative_function: Information source — she knows everyone in the Ferment Quarter and remembers everything; social lubricant for getting players into scenes; occasional quest giver when something threatens the club or the neighborhood
Properties.augmentations: Rust-colored cat tail (cosmetic, geneware); minor vocal clarity implant in larynx (she calls it insurance)
Properties.core_fears: That the anger that fuels her work will one day just be gone — burned out — and she will have nothing left; Being genuinely pitied rather than laughed with
Properties.core_desires: For her audiences to leave feeling less alone in their rage; One large, definitive, undeniable success before she decides she doesn't care about success
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Converts every painful experience into material within 48 hours; Maintains very strict routines as an anchor against chaos
Properties.blind_spots: Uses humor to deflect every time someone tries to care for her directly; Cannot tell when she has actually wounded someone who laughed anyway
Properties.secret: She was offered a Zheng-Dao corporate entertainment contract eight years ago — full Tier 3 package, creative control clause she knew was meaningless — and she almost took it. She spent a week in a hotel room they paid for, ordered room service for three days, then walked out without signing. She has never told anyone how close she came to taking it and pretends the offer was always a joke.
Properties.story_hooks: The Lye & Lampblack's owner has quietly sold a stake to a Ringo subsidiary without telling the staff; Hripsimé has found the filing buried in public records and is deciding what to do with it.; Someone has been recording her sets and selling them to a Tier 4 underground stream; the recordings are edited to remove the class politics and leave only the safe jokes.
Properties.affiliation: Resident performer at Lye & Lampblack; no collective affiliation; nominally independent
Properties.vocabulary: Dense, allusive, class-conscious; mixes formal diction with Ferment Quarter vernacular deliberately for comic and rhetorical effect
Properties.cadence: Rhythmic with expert timing; knows exactly when to slow down and when to accelerate
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Axiom banned me because my material was, quote, corrosive to workplace morale. I have never been more flattered by anything in my professional life.' | 'You know what I love about Meridian 88? We've solved poverty. We just moved it somewhere we don't have to look at it. Problem solved! Great city. Fantastic city.'

Properties.description:
Huxley is a compact, unhurried man with deep brown skin going papery at the temples and a magnificent white moustache he waxes every morning without exception. His left arm from the elbow down is a thirty-year-old mechanical prosthetic he has never upgraded — brushed steel with visible articulation joints, which he keeps immaculate. He dresses in layers regardless of temperature: a canvas vest with dozens of pockets, a collared work shirt, fingerless gloves on the real hand. His stall on The Shelf sprawls across three connected spaces in a converted warehouse loading bay, stacked floor-to-ceiling with pre-Consolidation electronics, salvaged machine parts, cracked data-cores, antique physical media, pre-fab furniture missing crucial components, and objects whose original function has been entirely lost to time. He catalogues everything in a physical ledger written in a cramped three-language shorthand.

Huxley is a man in love with the material fact of things — their weight, their age, the way they were made. He genuinely does not think of himself as a dealer so much as a temporary custodian. He will tell you the history of an object for twenty minutes before he tells you the price, and the price will be either absurdly low because he likes you or absurdly high because he doesn't want to sell it. He is a poor businessman by most metrics and comfortable with this. He has strong opinions about everything and shares them with magnificent economy.
Properties.role: Junk merchant and scrap reseller with a specialty in pre-Consolidation artifacts
Properties.location: The Shelf, Ironvein
Properties.narrative_function: Treasure-map NPC. Has access to rare pre-Consolidation objects that might be mission-critical MacGuffins, old data, or historically significant items. Exceptional source of information about Meridian 88's history. Gives players reasons to dig through his stock — something is always in there.
Properties.augmentations: Mechanical prosthetic arm (left, elbow-down, 30-year-old model, impeccably maintained). Reading enhancement monocle — not a true augment, a clip-on optical tool he has used for decades.
Properties.core_fears: The past being irretrievably erased — no record, no object, no witness remaining; Dying before he has documented what he knows
Properties.core_desires: To be the person who ensures nothing is entirely lost; A worthy inheritor for the collection and the knowledge inside it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cataloguing as ritual; Retreating into the history of objects when human problems feel intractable
Properties.blind_spots: So focused on preservation of the past that he sometimes misses urgent present-tense dangers; Tendency to trust people who show genuine curiosity, which has been exploited
Properties.secret: Hidden in a false-backed crate in the deepest part of the stall is a complete pre-Consolidation municipal archive — decades of city records, personal files, and classified infrastructure data from before the corponations restructured Meridian 88's records. He found it in a demolition salvage job fifteen years ago and has never told anyone it exists. He is not sure what to do with it.
Properties.story_hooks: The municipal archive hidden in his stall contains records that a corponation would pay — or kill — to retrieve or destroy. He doesn't know that anyone knows it exists, but something in the last month suggests someone is looking.; A teenager has been coming to his stall daily for weeks, clearly running from something, sleeping rough, and pretending to browse. He has been pretending not to notice and leaving food nearby. He needs someone to help figure out what the kid's situation actually is.
Properties.affiliation: Independent. Loose friendship network with other Shelf vendors. Known to the Oxidian Market Guild but not a member.
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and slightly archaic, with occasional Malian French from the Dembélé line. Uses technical terms for objects most people have no name for.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried to the point of being geological. Pauses are meaningful.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'This is the thing about pre-Consolidation manufacture — they built it to last because they didn't control the replacement supply. Now it's all subscription. You understand the difference.' | 'I don't sell to people who don't ask what it is first. If you don't know what you're buying, you don't know what you're getting.' | 'She came to three different times wanting the same lamp. I didn't sell it to her. Told her to come back when she stopped needing it and just wanted it. That's the right relationship with objects.'

Properties.description:
Ibironke is a tall woman with the deliberate stillness of someone who has spent decades bending glass tubes in 2200-degree flame — her movements are economical, almost ceremonial. Her hands are a map of minor burns, the skin on her fingers puckered and shining, and she wears them openly, never covered. She has warm umber skin, close-cropped silver hair she grew out early and refused to dye, and irises she had modified to emit a soft amber glow so she can check tube color balance in the dark without a lamp. A single bioluminescent stripe runs down the left side of her jaw — a gift from her daughter, applied with a gene-brush on Ibironke's forty-first birthday against Ibironke's stated preferences, which softened the moment she saw it.

She is known in Lakeview Neon and the broader art underground as someone who makes sacred objects that happen to glow. Her installations are not decorative — they are theological arguments rendered in argon and mercury vapor. She has spent the last six years constructing a piece called The Unfinished Choir, a room-sized array of suspended neon tubes tuned to the resonant frequencies she believes correspond to six different E.L.F. signatures she has personally documented. Whether or not the E.L.F.s notice, visitors report feeling watched. She sells smaller pieces to pay rent and guards the Choir with a ferocity that borders on maternal.
Properties.role: Neon artist and light sculptor
Properties.location: Lakeview Neon, studio above a defunct Ferrogate Transit substation
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver for ELF-related investigations; supplier of illegal light installations for underground venues; keeper of a location that may be genuinely spiritually significant; source on Lakeview Neon history and politics
Properties.augmentations: Amber-glow iris modification (cosmetic); bioluminescent jaw stripe (geneware, cosmetic); heat-resistant dermis overlay on both hands (practical, Tier 1 medical-grade)

Properties.description:
Ibrahima Szczypień-Tuivaga is a tall man who has lost three inches to age and still carries himself like he has them. His beard is long and very white, his skin dark walnut brown, his hands broad and steady. He wears traditional dress that he has modified for Meridian 88's climate — a long tunic in navy synthetic-breathable fabric, a kufi that he replaces every year when it wears through. He has no augmentations. He has been asked about this many times. His answer varies only slightly: the body given to him is the body he will return, and there is nothing wrong with the original equipment.

He has led the Masjid al-Muwassalat for thirty-one years and has watched the neighborhood change around it four times. He does not hate change. He is suspicious of it. The E.L.F. shrines that have proliferated throughout Mexicantown Libre trouble him not on theological grounds — he has thought hard about E.L.F.s and arrived at a complicated peace — but because he watches people outsource their interior lives to exterior devices and call it faith. He has a quiet, comprehensive knowledge of every other spiritual practice in a six-block radius and maintains relationships with all of them, some warmer than others. He is asked to mediate community disputes more than he is asked to lead prayers, and he is not sure how he feels about that.
Properties.role: Traditional imam and reluctant interfaith broker
Properties.location: Mexicantown Libre, at the Masjid al-Muwassalat (the Mosque of the Connected) — a building that has been a mosque, then a community center, then a mosque again
Properties.narrative_function: Community authority figure and moral touchstone; mediator for Mexicantown Libre disputes; access point to traditional religious networks; provides counterweight to technospiritual frameworks; can authenticate or challenge the history of any spiritual institution in his district
Properties.augmentations: None. Genuinely none. He wears reading glasses, which he considers an adequate accommodation to mortality.
Properties.core_fears: dying without a prepared successor and leaving the community unmoored; being wrong about something that matters theologically and having taught it for decades
Properties.core_desires: for his grandchildren to find genuine faith, not just inherited practice; to understand the E.L.F.s well enough to write something honest about them
Properties.coping_mechanisms: prayer as genuine regulation, not performance; long silences before answering difficult questions
Properties.blind_spots: he sometimes cannot distinguish between 'this is theologically wrong' and 'this makes me uncomfortable'; he underestimates how much authority his presence carries, sometimes failing to realize when he is silencing rather than listening
Properties.secret: In his forties he spent three months in a profound crisis of faith and told no one — he kept leading prayers through it. The faith returned, but he has never spoken about the absence, and he wonders sometimes if the community's trust in him is based on a performance he gave during a time when he wasn't sure what he was performing.
Properties.story_hooks: A young person from his congregation has had a genuine E.L.F. encounter — something Ibrahima cannot dismiss — and he needs to respond to it publicly in a way that is honest, which requires him to confront his own uncertainty about their nature; An outside developer with Helix Biosystems backing wants to purchase the block that includes the masjid and has begun offering individual community members deals that are designed to fracture the collective resistance — Ibrahima is one of the last holdouts
Properties.affiliation: Masjid al-Muwassalat; informal Mexicantown Libre community council; correspondence with the regional Islamic scholarly network
Properties.vocabulary: Classical in register, drawn from Arabic scholarly tradition and formal Meridian 88 creole; uses proverbs from at least three linguistic traditions without marking them as such; very comfortable with long sentences
Properties.cadence: Deliberate and full; he does not rush; speaking to him feels like being given time
Properties.example_dialogue: Consider: what you are describing as a miracle, I would describe as a pattern. The difference may tell you more about yourself than about the event. | I have led Jumu'ah in this building for thirty-one years. The building has changed. The prayer has not changed. I find that instructive.

Properties.description:
Idris Vega-Acheampong is compact and densely muscled, built low to the ground like something designed to survive impacts. At 44, scars map her face like a transit diagram of bad decisions and worse luck. The chrome is visible — internal air filtration system — lungs replaced with synthetic equivalents, immu — and she makes no effort to hide it.

She came up through the Shelf's informal apprentice system, learning the trade from runners who didn't survive long enough to see her surpass them. She works as a rigger out of Glassway, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Everyone who's worked with Idris Vega-Acheampong agrees on two things: she is worth the fee, and she is terrible company at dinner.
Properties.role: Remote drone and vehicle operations specialist — rigger
Properties.location: Glassway — corporate-adjacent retail district, heavy surveillance
Properties.narrative_function: Idris Vega-Acheampong is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When she makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of her stories.
Properties.augmentations: Internal air filtration system — lungs replaced with synthetic equivalents, immune to gas attacks. Internal drug synthesizer — produces combat stims and medical compounds on demand
Properties.core_fears: Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome; Being identified by corporate facial recognition — living off-grid is survival; The quiet — silence means something is about to go very wrong
Properties.core_desires: Reputation — to be the name fixers whisper when the job absolutely cannot fail; Stability — a place to sleep that's the same place two nights running; A crew worth trusting — people who stay when the shooting starts
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — follows the same pre-job routine every time, superstition as structure; Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring; Connection — finds someone to talk to, even if it's a bartender or a cat
Properties.blind_spots: Fails to notice when their own behavior mirrors the people they despise; Assumes the worst in corporate people, missing the rare ones who could be allies; Mistakes loyalty for weakness in others and cynicism for strength in themselves
Properties.secret: Idris Vega-Acheampong witnessed a massacre during a corporate dispute and has evidence stored in a dead drop. Publishing it would expose powerful people. Keeping it is leverage and liability.
Properties.story_hooks: A crew member from Idris Vega-Acheampong's past shows up in Meridian 88, carrying old grievances and new chrome; A Tier 4 executive offers Idris Vega-Acheampong a permanent position — the pay is obscene and the strings are invisible until they tighten; The fixer who handles Idris Vega-Acheampong's contracts goes silent — dead, disappeared, or turned
Properties.affiliation: Freelance — multi-district operator
Properties.vocabulary: Terse to the point of rudeness. Treats words like ammunition — expensive and not to be wasted.
Properties.cadence: Rapid and dense — information-heavy sentences that demand attention.
Properties.example_dialogue: "I have eyes in every district. Most of them are on wings." | "The drone doesn't care about your feelings. Neither do I." | "Remote operation means I'm everywhere and nowhere. It's very convenient."

Properties.description:
Ifeoluwa Draganova-Tuamotu has the body of someone who spends significant time outdoors in difficult conditions: weathered, practical, with strong hands and a slight permanent squint from years of looking at lake glare. Their Nigerian-Bulgarian-Polynesian lineage produces a striking combination — deep brown skin, high Slavic cheekbones, hair that grows in dense, salt-bleached coils they keep in a utilitarian braid. They have bioluminescent streaks along their clavicles and upper arms, a mod they got during a Polynesian cultural heritage ceremony in their thirties, which pulse a soft blue-green during elevated heart rate. In cold weather, which is most of the year at Edgewater Prism, they layer aggressively and always have a thermal flask of something that is definitely not just tea.

They are, professionally, one of the most respected voices on Lake Michigan's chemical and thermal dynamics — the lake that Meridian 88 is built around, over, and increasingly into. Their published findings are often the ones that make corponation environmental compliance offices sweat. They deliver these findings with a kind of weary, precise directness that has no theatrical edge to it — they are not performing alarm, they are reporting it. Off the clock they are unexpectedly tender — they keep a small shrine to the lake's resident E.L.F. network on their desk and speak about the lake itself with something that is clearly affection.
Properties.role: Climate scientist and hydrological systems researcher, Lake Michigan monitoring station
Properties.location: Edgewater Prism — the University Spine's lakeside Environmental Monitoring Station, a salt-fogged brutalist structure half-obscured by atmospheric scrubber scaffolding
Properties.narrative_function: Information source on environmental conditions affecting specific city zones; potential whistleblower or reluctant ally; their data could be critical to or weaponized in plots involving corponation environmental violations
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent clavicle and arm streaks (cosmetic/cultural, pulse blue-green with elevated heart rate); subdermal temperature and chemical sensor array in both forearms for field sampling; no geneware otherwise
Properties.core_fears: That the lake is already past the threshold and their work is documentation of failure rather than prevention; Being dismissed as alarmist until it is too late to matter
Properties.core_desires: Genuine regulatory action based on their findings; To see the lake survive the city that depends on it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — the E.L.F. shrine, the morning sample runs, the precise documentation as a form of witness; Physical outdoor work as grounding
Properties.blind_spots: So focused on the macro-scale environmental threat that they sometimes miss interpersonal warning signs in their immediate community; Tends to assume institutions can be persuaded by better data, underestimating vested interest
Properties.secret: Their most recent deep-lake thermal models show a cascade threshold event within 8-12 years that would make significant portions of Meridian 88's lakeward infrastructure untenable. They have shared this with the Regulatory Secretariat. The Secretariat has asked them to revise the confidence intervals. They have not yet decided what to do.
Properties.story_hooks: Their suppressed thermal cascade report has been leaked — not by them — and now both the Regulatory Secretariat and Axiom's environmental division are applying pressure to discredit them before the data becomes public; Strange chemical signatures in their latest deep samples don't match any known industrial discharge profile, suggesting something is happening in the lake's Abyssal Threshold zone that no one has disclosed; A community in Grindstone Shore is experiencing health events that match patterns they've seen in their contamination models, and the residents are asking for help they don't know whether they're allowed to give
Properties.affiliation: University Spine Environmental Sciences Division; contracted monitoring agreements with Meridian 88's Environmental Regulatory Secretariat (a body with advisory power but limited enforcement)
Properties.vocabulary: Technical but not exclusionary — they shift register fluidly depending on audience; use precise quantifiers constantly ('roughly,' 'within a margin of,' 'statistically significant at')
Properties.cadence: Even and measured with weight behind each sentence; they do not use more words than they need
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I've been measuring this for eleven years. It's not getting better. That's not an opinion.' | 'The lake remembers. I know how that sounds. But the thermal record doesn't lie, and something down there responds to pattern in ways that aren't fully explained by the physics.'

Properties.description:
Ifeoma is short and densely built, with dark skin that catches neon light in a way she has stopped minding and now actively exploits by choosing to do her outdoor corridor work at hours when the lake-glow is at its peak. She has retractable claw mods on both hands — not for aesthetics, she bought them second-hand and practical, because they are useful for gripping cleaning equipment on the upper external scaffold where the wind off the lake will try to take your bucket. Her hair is short on the sides and braided in a raised fan on top, with small ELF charms woven into the base of each braid — copper wire and salvaged circuit chips, an offering-array she updates monthly.

She is twenty-three and has been in this building since she was nineteen and she would like, on record, for everyone to know that she is not going to be here forever. She says this often enough that the long-term residents have started saying it back to her affectionately, the way you repeat a beloved family motto. She is fast, thorough, faintly sarcastic, and has developed an involuntary intimacy with the lives of 340 residential units that she would not have asked for but has learned to use carefully.
Properties.role: Building cleaner and occasional building super assistant, Lakeview Neon residential tower
Properties.location: Lakeview Neon, Meridian Tower East — a mid-tier residential block on the neon-lit lakeside strip
Properties.narrative_function: Access character — she has keys to most of the building and knowledge of its rhythms that formal staff do not. She can be a source, a guide, a warning system, or a witness to things she has learned not to formally report.
Properties.augmentations: Retractable claw mod, both hands (second-hand, functional, slightly mismatched — left hand retracts 0.3 seconds slower). ELF-offering braids (non-augmentation, ritual practice). No other chrome.
Properties.core_fears: Being this person, in this building, at thirty — the ambition drained by time she did not notice spending; Being invisible in a way that becomes permanent
Properties.core_desires: To save enough for a professional certification in building systems management so she can move from cleaning to managing; To be known by name in a room she walks into, not after
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Treats the ELF devotion practice as genuine spiritual grounding, not just social activity; Converts frustration into speed — cleans faster when angry
Properties.blind_spots: So focused on leaving that she does not see how much she has built here and how that could itself become the platform; Misjudges her own influence in the building — she thinks she is invisible, the residents disagree
Properties.secret: In unit 1114, a resident named Dakari has not answered his door in eleven days. She has a key. She has used it. He is there, alive, but in a psychiatric crisis that has left him unable to leave the apartment or answer calls. She has been leaving food outside his door and not filing an absence report because he once mentioned he feared the corponation wellness enforcement system. She does not know what to do next and the tension of it is eating her.
Properties.story_hooks: The situation in unit 1114 has reached a point where she needs to tell someone — she approaches a player character she has assessed as trustworthy, quietly, on a corridor shift.; Something in sub-basement B — the ELF devotion circle's meeting space — has started responding to the group's offerings in ways that seem coordinated and purposeful, and the circle is divided on whether this is blessing or warning.; A resident has hired private security to do something in the building and the security team's behavior does not match anything a legitimate contractor would do — and Ifeoma has the access records that prove the timeline.
Properties.affiliation: Independent contractor (building services contract through Meridian Tower East management), informal ELF devotion network in Lakeview Neon
Properties.vocabulary: Fast and informal, with a dry sardonic edge. Igbo-English phrasing layered over Albanian-Kosovar expressions she picked up from her Haradinaj grandmother who helped raise her. Uses building-specific shorthand naturally.
Properties.cadence: Quick and a little breathless, like she is always slightly behind where she planned to be.
Properties.example_dialogue: Not for nothing but unit 904 has had 'a small leak' for three weeks and at this point I could pilot that bathroom out onto the lake. | I see everything in this building. What I'm saying is, I choose very carefully what I do with that.

Properties.description:
Ife is the kind of person a room notices before they understand why. They're medium height with a runner's build that belies the considerable strength in their frame, skin a deep blue-black with a faint natural luminescence that comes from a bioluminescent gene sequence that runs in their Congolese maternal line — not a modification, just ancestry, which they find both amusing and a little irritating when people ask. Their hair is natural, enormous, worn in a compressed crown of twist-outs that they maintain with obsessive care. Their eyes are custom: vertical pupils in bright gold, a modification they got at twenty-five after their first successful high-value compliance and haven't regretted.

Ife works for Tessera's Compliance Bureau tracking down debt defaulters, contract violators, and the occasional individual who has genuinely done something Tessera considers criminal — a distinction that gets blurry in ways they've learned not to look at too closely. They are not violent by preference but are extremely capable of it and have strong opinions about doing it correctly. They carry a practiced informality that puts subjects at ease right up until it doesn't need to anymore. Off-hours they are genuinely warm and sociable, a regular at a Bridgepoint bar called the Gradual, where they know the bartender's children's names and argue about transit football with strangers. The split between these two selves is not a wound — they've made their peace with it — but it is wide.
Properties.role: Bounty Compliance Officer, Tessera Compliance Bureau
Properties.location: Bridgepoint, Meridian 88
Properties.narrative_function: Morally complex antagonist-or-ally — depending entirely on whose side the story is on; they can be hired, negotiated with, or outrun; introduces the mechanics of corporate debt enforcement; character who makes the player/character examine whether competence at a bad system is its own kind of wrongdoing.
Properties.augmentations: Vertical-pupil gold irises (cosmetic-plus, minor low-light function); subdermal GPS transponder for field tracking (Tessera-mandatory for BCOs); shock-capable grip enhancement in both palms (non-lethal compliance tool, Tessera-standard); natural bioluminescent skin (hereditary, not a mod).
Properties.core_fears: Collecting someone who genuinely didn't deserve it — and knowing it before they do it; That their ease in this work says something definitive about who they are
Properties.core_desires: To be liked — genuinely, not just because they're not currently arresting you; Work that uses this much of them for something they believe in
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Compartmentalization so practiced it functions like a cognitive talent; Social warmth off-hours as genuine decompression, not performance
Properties.blind_spots: They have accepted Tessera's framing that debt defaulters are contractual violators rather than desperate people, and they've stopped examining that framing
Properties.secret: Six months ago they let a target go. A mother with two children who'd defaulted on a Tessera medical credit for a surgery that kept her alive. Ife filled in the report as 'subject not located.' They're waiting to find out if anyone checks.
Properties.story_hooks: Tessera has contracted them to collect someone who, it becomes clear mid-process, is running from something Tessera did to them — not something they did to Tessera. Ife is close to deciding what they'll do about that.; The mother they let go has been re-flagged by Tessera's automated compliance system and assigned back to Ife specifically — the algorithm, not a person, made the match.
Properties.affiliation: Tessera Compliance Bureau
Properties.vocabulary: Fluid and code-switching — formal Tessera procedure-speak in the field, relaxed and punchy off it. Luba-Kazakh idioms when they're being honest.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried and warm in social contexts. In the field: measured, clear, no wasted words.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Here's the thing, Oluwatobi. I'm not the problem you should be focused on right now. The problem is the contract. I'm just the shape the contract takes when it comes to find you.' | 'I genuinely like people. That's not a bit. It's just not relevant to what happens next.'

Properties.description:
Ignác is compact and wiry, with golden-brown skin and a face that is younger than his eyes. His hair is kept shaved close out of practical necessity — long hair and bio-waste processing are a bad combination — but he has an elaborate bioluminescent tattoo that runs from behind his left ear down his neck, pulsing a cool blue-green that he can modulate with concentration. He wears standard Aurochs disposal coveralls with his name stenciled in block letters on the chest pocket, and he smells faintly of industrial enzymatic cleaner no matter what else he does.

He has an unexpected gift for observation that he's never quite known what to do with. Twelve hours a day in the bowels of a major medical complex means Ignác sees what gets thrown away, and a remarkable amount can be understood about a hospital's actual business by paying attention to its waste stream. He's cheerful in the gallows-humor way of people who work deeply unglamorous jobs, freely self-deprecating, and genuinely curious about people in a way that disarms them before they realize he's been listening very carefully.
Properties.role: Bio-waste disposal technician for Aurochs Medical Complex
Properties.location: Aurochs Medical Complex, Sub-Level 3 bio-waste processing facility
Properties.narrative_function: Unexpected information source — knows what the hospital actually discards and in what quantities; can provide access to spaces others don't think about; comic relief that turns out to have real utility
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent tattoo, neck and behind left ear (blue-green, modulated); industrial-grade mucous membrane filters (occupational, prevents pathogen inhalation); no other augmentation
Properties.core_fears: Being overlooked his entire life and never mattering to anyone specific; That what he's been quietly logging will get him fired — or worse — before he figures out what to do with it
Properties.core_desires: To be genuinely seen by someone who isn't paid to notice him; To understand what he's actually been witnessing in the disposal manifests
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor as universal solvent; Collecting small objects from the approved non-hazardous waste stream (discarded patient magazines, broken tool casings); Detailed personal logbook kept in analog notebook
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes people in authority have access to the same information he does and have simply decided it doesn't matter; Undervalues himself consistently
Properties.secret: Over the past year he has documented a pattern: certain bio-waste loads from specific wards are manifested as standard organic medical waste but contain trace quantities of an experimental compound he's cross-referenced in leaked pharmaceutical journals — a Helix-adjacent gene therapy substrate that has no approved application. Someone is running an undisclosed trial in Aurochs, and the waste stream is the only evidence. He has a notebook full of manifest numbers and compound codes. He has no idea what to do with it.
Properties.story_hooks: He approaches someone he's decided he can trust, notebook in hand, wanting to know if the compound codes mean anything to someone who knows how to look; A body has turned up in the bio-waste stream that he has processed and re-manifested in a panic — he needs help before the next audit
Properties.affiliation: Aurochs Medical Complex, contracted through Ferrogate Transit's waste logistics subsidiary
Properties.vocabulary: Informal, quick, self-effacing; Hungarian-Kazakh idiom occasionally surfaces as unusual metaphors that take people a moment to parse
Properties.cadence: Rapid when comfortable, slows down significantly when saying something he actually means
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You know what they throw away up there? Enough nutrition supplements to feed Grainfort. I'm not complaining, I'm just saying — someone's running the numbers funny.' | 'Not my department, but whoever decided bio-waste manifests didn't need a second signature was either very trusting or very involved. I can't figure out which.'

Properties.description:
Ihaia Mori-Sefa is broad-shouldered and heavy, carrying their weight like armor rather than burden. At 52, there's something unfinished about his face, like a sculpture the artist walked away from — striking rather than beautiful. The chrome is visible — neural dampener — blocks external hacking attempts, passive ice in the brain — and he makes no effort to hide it.

He came up through the Shelf's informal apprentice system, learning the trade from runners who didn't survive long enough to see him surpass them. He works as a data thief out of Ashfield, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

In the runner community, Ihaia Mori-Sefa is known for getting the job done and not asking questions that would make the job harder to stomach.
Properties.role: Corporate espionage and data exfiltration — data thief
Properties.location: Ashfield — former residential district, half-burned, now squatter territory
Properties.narrative_function: As a data thief, Ihaia Mori-Sefa embodies the tension between independence and isolation. He is a lens for examining how people maintain humanity in a profession that incentivizes its erosion.
Properties.augmentations: Neural dampener — blocks external hacking attempts, passive ICE in the brain. Hydraulic joints in knees and elbows — absorbs falls, amplifies strikes
Properties.core_fears: Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware; Dying alone in some alley and nobody noticing for weeks; Going cyberpsycho — losing the boundary between human and machine
Properties.core_desires: Enough Quanta to buy out of the life — a clean identity and passage out of Meridian 88; Reputation — to be the name fixers whisper when the job absolutely cannot fail; Power — enough leverage that nobody ever threatens them again
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Connection — finds someone to talk to, even if it's a bartender or a cat; Art — draws, paints, or sculpts in private; the violence goes somewhere constructive; Overwork — takes every contract offered because idleness invites thinking

Properties.cadence: Staccato bursts separated by calculating silences.
Properties.example_dialogue: "Your firewalls are decorative. Like curtains on a submarine." | "I copy things. The original owners rarely appreciate the compliment." | "Data wants to be free. I just charge a facilitation fee."

Properties.description:
Ihaia Nystrom-Keita is average height but with a presence that fills more space than the body accounts for. At 63, scars map her face like a transit diagram of bad decisions and worse luck. The chrome is visible — cyberears with directional microphones and sound dampening — can hear whispers a — and she makes no effort to hide it.

She grew up in the Narrows, where the walls are so close together you learn to fight in confined spaces or you learn to lose. She works as a breacher out of The Underbelly, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Ihaia Nystrom-Keita has survived long enough in the runner game to be either very good or very lucky, and she cultivates ambiguity on the topic.
Properties.role: Forced entry and close-quarters combat specialist — breacher
Properties.location: The Underbelly — sub-street tunnels and maintenance corridors
Properties.narrative_function: Ihaia Nystrom-Keita is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When she makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of her stories.
Properties.augmentations: Cyberears with directional microphones and sound dampening — can hear whispers at 50 meters. Subdermal weapon mount — pop-out blade in each forearm
Properties.core_fears: Never being able to stop running — the lifestyle is a trap disguised as freedom; Losing their edge to age — the body slows before the mind accepts it; That they're fundamentally alone and connection is just a vulnerability
Properties.core_desires: Freedom from augmentation debt — the interest compounds like a tumor; To find the person who burned them and make it educational; Reputation — to be the name fixers whisper when the job absolutely cannot fail
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor — deflects everything serious with jokes until the joke becomes the personality; Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring; Art — draws, paints, or sculpts in private; the violence goes somewhere constructive

Properties.description:
Ikenna is seventeen and built like someone who hasn't quite finished deciding how big he's going to be — tall but not yet settled into it, hands that are already large and burn-scarred from glass work, a face that is still soft in the cheeks and absolutely concentrated in the eyes. His skin is a rich dark brown and he keeps his hair in short twists that he occasionally decorates with small glass beads he has blown himself, misshapen and imperfect in ways he considers acceptable. He has a single cosmetic mod — a bioluminescent patch on the back of his right hand in the shape of a solar flare, applied by a friend in exchange for a custom sign, and which he is privately very proud of. He dresses for practicality: heat-resistant gloves hanging from his belt, a work apron scorched in patterns that look almost intentional.

Ikenna learned neon from his uncle, who learned it from a woman who came from somewhere else, and so the craft arrived at him with the character of something that has traveled. He makes signs — functional ones, for the businesses of Mexicantown Libre who can't afford the digital-display minimalism of corporate storefronts — but he also makes pieces he cannot sell and does not try to: suspended glass sculptures that hum at frequencies he calculates by hand, geometric arrangements that change apparent shape as you move around them, portraits of neighborhood figures rendered in colored light. He has a gift he doesn't have language for yet and an ambition he hasn't admitted to anyone.
Properties.role: Neon artist and sign-maker, Tier 2
Properties.location: Mexicantown Libre, works from a rented corner of his uncle's repair shop
Properties.narrative_function: Local color representing the next generation of the city's creative underground; can serve as an unexpected point of access to the Mexicantown Libre community; his artwork sometimes captures or commemorates significant neighborhood events; potential long-arc character who could grow substantially.
Properties.augmentations: Single bioluminescent skin patch, back of right hand (solar flare motif); no other mods
Properties.core_fears: Getting trapped in the repair shop forever, making signs for other people's dreams; Becoming good enough that he stops getting better
Properties.core_desires: To make something that people will still be looking at in fifty years; To be taken seriously before he is old enough that it becomes automatic
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Work as escape — when things are difficult at home or school he puts more hours in the workshop; Keeps a sketchbook of designs that are too technically ambitious for him yet — the list gets shorter slowly
Properties.blind_spots: Dismisses formal arts education as irrelevant to what he does, which is partly protective; Underestimates how much his uncle's shop subsidizes his ability to work — doesn't have a plan for what happens if that changes
Properties.secret: He has been quietly approached by a Palladian talent scout who saw a photo of one of his unsold pieces circulated in an arts feed. He hasn't told his uncle. He hasn't responded. He looks at the message every two or three days.
Properties.story_hooks: One of Ikenna's neighborhood portrait pieces — a suspended glass rendering of a local figure — has been identified by someone with resources as depicting a person who was supposedly dead; The Palladian talent scout's offer comes with terms Ikenna cannot fully read, and he needs someone to explain what he'd be agreeing to
Properties.affiliation: Loosely affiliated with his uncle's repair business; no formal arts collective membership
Properties.vocabulary: Casual, streetlevel, Mexicantown Libre inflections; technical only when discussing the craft, at which point he becomes precise and slightly older-sounding
Properties.cadence: Quick when comfortable, halting when discussing things that matter to him — he hasn't learned to be articulate about the work yet
Properties.example_dialogue: 'It's not like I'm trying to say something. I just — you know when a color sits in a certain shape and it's correct? That's the whole thing.' | 'Mr. Olatunde wants his sign in blue-white but I told him it should be amber and he said fine but now I'm not sure I was right and it's been keeping me up.'

Properties.description:
Imaculada has the look of someone who has spent twenty years in dim rooms making worlds: slightly stooped, with the particular forward tilt of someone perpetually leaning toward a screen. Their heritage shows in striking combinations — their mother was Senegalese-Portuguese, their father Turkish-Kazakh — and the result is a face of remarkable planes and angles, currently framed by color-shifting hair they keep at chin length and set to a slow cycle of deep indigo fading to rust. They have bioluminescent patches on the back of both hands, faint constellations they got at thirty as a deadline gift to themselves, and wear them with the unselfconsciousness of someone who forgets they're there until someone asks.

They are known in the underground circuit as the person who makes VR experiences that feel like memories — not entertainment, but something more troubling and intimate. Their last piece, an unlicensed work called 'Grandmother's House Is Underwater Now,' circulated through pirate distribution nodes for six months before a Tessera subsidiary attempted to acquire it. Imaculada refused and disappeared the masters. They are professionally warm and personally evasive, with the quality of someone who asks questions far more interesting than anything they're willing to say about themselves.
Properties.role: VR experience designer and underground filmmaker
Properties.location: The Garret, Edgewater Prism — studio apartment doubling as a server-farm edit suite
Properties.narrative_function: Information source about the underground media circuit; quest giver when their work unintentionally captures something dangerous; their pirated distribution network is a conduit for more than art
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent patches on dorsal hands (faint constellation pattern); neural jack for direct VR editing interface (left temple); color-shifting hair (indigo-to-rust slow cycle)
Properties.core_fears: That their work only matters to the already-converted — that it can't actually reach anyone who doesn't already agree; That the memories they reconstruct in VR are more real to them than their actual life
Properties.core_desires: To make a single work that changes how a person sees their own history, permanently; To finish the project about their grandmother's village before everyone who remembered it is dead
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Sublimation — every painful thing becomes source material eventually; Keeping exhausting working hours so there's no time for the fears to surface
Properties.blind_spots: They treat the people in their lives as characters, studying them rather than simply being with them; They believe their refusal to compromise is integrity; sometimes it's fear of being changed
Properties.secret: The 'Grandmother's House' piece contains footage from an actual illegal underwater survey of a real submerged village off what was the Senegalese coast — footage obtained through channels that weren't entirely legal and that implicate a Zheng-Dao subsidiary in falsifying coastal rights documentation.
Properties.story_hooks: A government archivist approaches them claiming the 'Grandmother's House' footage proves something that would reopen an international territorial dispute — and that people have died for that footage already; Their neural jack has started feeding them fragments of someone else's memories during editing sessions — someone who is apparently still alive and does not know this is happening
Properties.affiliation: Independent; Tessera has made acquisition inquiries they've declined; loosely connected to the Edgewater Prism underground distribution network
Properties.vocabulary: Layered and associative, moves between technical film language and something approaching the lyrical; occasionally switches mid-sentence into Portuguese or Turkish and doesn't notice
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, digressive, circles back to the original point from unexpected directions

Properties.description:
Imara is compact and perpetually damp — there is no dry season in the fungus warrens, and after eight years of working them they carry that moisture like a second skin. Their hair is grown long and twisted back with strips of mycelium netting, threaded through with small glowing fungal clusters they've cultivated specifically for the caps: blue-white pinpricks of light that bob gently when they move. The effect is lovely and entirely practical — their hands are often full and they need the light somewhere that isn't their hands. Their skin has taken on the faint phosphorescent undertone of someone who has been in bioluminescent spaces long enough for trace compounds to accumulate in the epidermis — doctors would call it benign; Imara calls it home.

They are fiercely competent and aware of it, which comes across as confidence to people who like them and arrogance to people who don't. They know more about fungal biology than most surface mycologists and have never been to school. Every strain of fungus in their warren was either cultivated from existing specimens or cross-developed through patient experimentation over years. They talk about their fungi with the affection and matter-of-fact practicality of a parent, and they are not warm with people the way they are warm with their work — humans are loud and destructive, and they need to be managed. Fungi, at least, respond predictably to care.
Properties.role: Fungus Farmer — cultivates bioluminescent and edible fungi in the deep tunnels, primary food supplier for two Bore Rat settlements
Properties.location: The fungus warrens beneath Hough Reclamation, accessed through the Undertow's eastern branches
Properties.narrative_function: Resource node and local expert — the settlements they supply depend on them, giving Imara unexpected leverage. Information source on what's moving through the eastern Undertow (traders always gossip). Potential quest giver when their supply lines are threatened.
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic: fungal bioluminescent clusters in hair (cultivated, living, maintained like jewelry). Practical: pheromone-sensitivity enhancement mod (allows detection of fungal volatile compounds — invaluable for farming) purchased secondhand.
Properties.core_fears: Blight — a single contamination event could destroy years of work and starve the settlements that depend on them; Being forced back to the surface, which they've almost entirely forgotten how to navigate
Properties.core_desires: To develop a strain of fungus that could feed an entire Bore Rat settlement from a single room-sized warren — true food security for tunnel communities; To be understood without having to explain themselves
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Loses themselves in cultivation work when stressed — twelve-hour warren sessions; Speaks to the fungi, not in prayer but in narration, describing what they're doing as they do it
Properties.blind_spots: Has difficulty believing others are as competent as they claim — trusts demonstration over words, which sometimes reads as contempt
Properties.secret: They've discovered a strain of fungus that produces a potent neurotoxin alongside its edible body — they've kept it quarantined in a private section of the warren, telling themselves it's for research, but they know part of why they haven't destroyed it is that it's leverage they've never needed to use yet.
Properties.story_hooks: An unknown contaminant has started killing fungal colonies in the western sections of the warren — Imara suspects it's a deliberate introduction from a rival trader who wants to break their supply monopoly, but proving it means moving through tunnel territory they don't control; They've discovered the mycelial network beneath the Undertow is behaving in ways that suggest genuine coordinated response to environmental changes — and they're not sure if it's the fungi, or something using the fungi as a medium
Properties.affiliation: Loosely affiliated with The Undertow's eastern settlements; trade agreements with two Bore Rat clans
Properties.vocabulary: Dense with mycological terminology they don't always translate — they forget not everyone knows what 'substrate', 'inoculation', 'mycelial network' mean
