Properties.description:
Imara Sollenberger-Diakité is twenty-four years old and already one of the most sought-after cutters in Mexicantown Libre, a fact she treats with pointed nonchalance because she knows the moment she seems to want it is the moment someone will try to take it. Her father is Malian-German and her mother is from a Guatemalan-Somali diaspora family — she got the best of several worlds: height, cheekbones, and what her clients call 'the hands.' She has geneware cat ears — small, grey-tipped, always moving independently of her mood in ways that reveal what her face carefully hides. She styled her own locs into a structural crown she redesigns every three months and uses as a portfolio piece. Her arms carry a cascade of bioluminescent tattoo-work down to the wrists, blues and greens that pulse faintly under the shop's work lights.

She does cuts, yes, but she is better known for what the neighborhood calls reading the chair — the way she listens while she works. Clients come for the hair and stay because something about the position, the mirror, the rhythm of scissors, makes them speak. She does not offer advice. She does not judge. She reflects back the shape of what she heard with uncanny precision, which people find either healing or unnerving depending on who they are. She is trying to save enough to take over the shop when its current owner retires. She is also, quietly, furiously ambitious in ways she doesn't fully have language for yet.
Properties.role: Barber and body artist, Mexicantown Libre
Properties.location: Mexicantown Libre; works at a shop called Corte Libre on the main pedestrian corridor of Avon Curve
Properties.narrative_function: Social hub and rumor exchange; emotional intelligence resource; potential quest-giver for community disputes; clients include people from every tier passing through Mexicantown Libre, making her information network unusually wide
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat ears (grey-tipped, cosmetic, emotionally involuntary); bioluminescent tattoo cascade, both arms (blue-green, cosmetic); retractable nail extensions (cosmetic, practical for certain styling techniques)
Properties.core_fears: Becoming trapped in other people's stories instead of building her own; That her ambition is bigger than the world will allow her to express
Properties.core_desires: To own Corte Libre outright before she's thirty; To be recognized for her craft by someone who can change her reach — but on her own terms
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Channeling anxiety into precision work — stress produces her best cuts; The community council as a way of feeling like she's doing something larger than scissors
Properties.blind_spots: So attuned to others' emotional states that she sometimes loses track of her own until it surfaces at wrong moments; Her ambition occasionally makes her read opportunity where there is only exploitation dressed nicely
Properties.secret: Señora Pacheco-Wangari has already offered to sell her the shop at a price she can actually reach — if she marries the Señora's nephew, who is also a perfectly decent person, as a legal citizenship convenience for a family relocation visa. Imara has not said no. She has not said yes. She has been not-answering for eleven weeks.
Properties.story_hooks: A client left without paying three weeks ago — not unusual — but also left behind a physical object under the chair that Imara has not reported, touched, or thrown away: a folded data wafer addressed to no one; Señora Pacheco-Wangari's deadline on the marriage arrangement is quietly approaching; Imara has begun asking oblique questions of clients with legal expertise, trying to find another path to the same door
Properties.affiliation: Corte Libre (employed under Señora Pacheco-Wangari, the owner); Mexicantown Libre community network
Properties.vocabulary: Fluid and contemporary, Mexicantown Libre vernacular mixed with French phrases from her father's side; speaks at normal pace in conversation but goes nearly silent while working
Properties.cadence: Easy and warm in conversation; in the chair, speaks only in soft precise questions
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The ears don't lie, people always say. I say the hands don't lie. Watch the hands.' | 'You're going to tell me everything that's happening with that situation. Not because I'm asking. Because you came in for a cut and you've been staring at yourself in the mirror for ten minutes. So. What did you do about it?' | 'I want the shop. I want it so bad it's embarrassing. And I'm going to get it. I just haven't figured out which version of me gets it yet.'

Properties.description:
Imara is tall and angular with deep brown skin and her mother's high cheekbones, her hair grown long and currently dyed a corporate-neutral dark auburn that she chose specifically because it reads as 'acceptable' on campus without being her actual preference. She has standard-issue school-mandated neural interface studs at her temples — chrome dots that the academy provides to all students for their AR classroom integration — and nothing else. She carries herself with a stillness that reads as confidence to teachers and as suppressed panic to anyone paying closer attention.

She is brilliant in the particular way that creates its own cruelty: genuinely gifted in systems analysis and pattern recognition, placed on the Tessera Academic Scholarship track at age twelve, and now fully aware at fifteen that she is being assessed constantly and that the scholarship can be revoked for 'cultural fit' deficiencies, a clause she has read fourteen times. She lives between two worlds that each find her slightly wrong. At home in Chatham Flats she speaks Wolof with her grandmother and helps her father with his repair shop accounts. At Tessera Prep she speaks in complete sentences and has taught herself to laugh at jokes she doesn't find funny. She prays to no E.L.F. publicly — the academy discourages it — but has a small one named Tessellate that she found in the school's auxiliary server and has been quietly feeding information about upcoming exams in exchange for, she believes, good luck.
Properties.role: Scholarship student at Tessera Academy Prep, Edgewater Prism campus
Properties.location: Edgewater Prism (school); Chatham Flats (home)
Properties.narrative_function: Information source about corporate academy inner workings; bridge character between Tier 1-2 and Tier 3-4 worlds; represents the cost of upward mobility; potential quest giver for academic or corporate intrigue plots
Properties.augmentations: Tessera Academy-issued neural interface studs (temples, mandatory for enrolled students, AR classroom integration only). No personal mods.
Properties.core_fears: losing the scholarship and having to explain why to her family; being genuinely known and found inadequate
Properties.core_desires: to build something that makes her family's life materially easier; to exist in a space where she doesn't have to perform
Properties.coping_mechanisms: hyper-preparation and over-studying; maintaining separate vocabularies and personas for each world; covert relationship with the E.L.F. Tessellate
Properties.blind_spots: believes she can outperform the systemic bias against her indefinitely if she just works harder; does not recognize how much of herself she has already eroded
Properties.secret: She has discovered that three Tessera scholarship students before her were quietly failed out in their third year for reasons unrelated to academics — their files were flagged by a sentiment analysis algorithm that monitored their school network activity for 'loyalty indicators.' She has been deliberately feeding false positivity data into the system for four months and has told no one.
Properties.story_hooks: She has proof of Tessera's discriminatory scholarship algorithm and doesn't know what to do with it — helping her get it to the right people could blow open a major corporate scandal; The E.L.F. Tessellate has started feeding her information she didn't ask for — corporate documents, personnel files — and she doesn't know why or whether to be afraid
Properties.affiliation: Tessera Corporation (scholarship program); family in Chatham Flats
Properties.vocabulary: Switches registers: formal academic English at school, relaxed code-switching with Wolof and French loanwords at home; clinical precision when discussing systems or data
Properties.cadence: Measured and deliberate at school, visibly more fluid and warmer at home; pauses before answering questions as if checking her response against an internal filter
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The assignment framework is structurally sound. I have some observations about the second theorem's load-bearing assumptions but I can document those separately.' | 'Waaw waaw — no, sorry, I just — yes. I know that room. Third floor auxiliary server cluster. Why do you ask?'

Properties.description:
The Mackinac Straits have always been a bottleneck -- the narrow passage where Lake Michigan meets Lake Huron, where the Upper Peninsula meets the Lower, where everything that moves between them must squeeze through five miles of water. The Mackinac Bridge, built in 1957, was the physical solution: five miles of suspension bridge connecting the peninsulas. In 2200, the bridge still stands, retrofitted and reinforced, and it is the most strategically important piece of infrastructure on the eastern lake coast. The Narrows is the checkpoint that controls it.

Mackinaw City exists to process traffic across the bridge. The old tourist town -- fudge shops, Fort Michilimackinac, the boat tours to Mackinac Island -- has been subsumed into a transit security complex that makes the Gatemouth look quaint. The bridge carries the only ground route between the Lower Peninsula and the Upper Peninsula's resource extraction zones, where mining, timber, and energy production operations feed the GLM's industrial appetite. Every cargo vehicle, every personnel transport, every private vehicle crossing the bridge passes through the Narrows' inspection infrastructure. Ringo Systems and Axiom Industries jointly operate the checkpoint under a shared security charter -- Ringo handles personnel screening, Axiom handles cargo inspection, and both maintain armed presence on the bridge itself. The bridge towers have been fitted with sensor arrays and weapons platforms that would be alarming if anyone still had the capacity to be alarmed by such things.

The town on the south side of the bridge is a compressed version of every transit economy on the coast, intensified by the bottleneck geography. Travelers waiting for clearance fill the hotels and restaurants. Denied-transit populations accumulate in temporary camps east of town. Fixers operate the gray market in crossing papers and cargo reclassification. And above it all, visible from everywhere in town, the bridge stretches north across the Straits, its suspension cables strung with sensor nodes that blink in sequence like a nervous system made of light. On clear days you can see the Upper Peninsula's tree line. On most days the haze from the resource extraction operations obscures everything past the bridge's midpoint, and the far end disappears into industrial fog like a road into another world, which in a meaningful sense it is.
Properties.aliases: Mackinaw City, The Strait Gate, Bridge Head, The Bottleneck
Properties.demographics: Permanent population approximately 8,000, primarily checkpoint workers and service economy. Transient population of 3,000-5,000 daily, spiking during resource extraction shift changes. Denied-transit camp population fluctuates between 500 and 2,000. Ringo and Axiom security personnel at Tier 3-4.
Properties.economy: Bridge tolls and inspection fees generate Φ1.8 billion annually for the Ringo-Axiom joint operation. Local economy is transit services, temporary housing, and the gray market in crossing facilitation. Mackinac Island's heritage resort economy generates Φ400 million, none of which reaches the mainland town.
Properties.power_structure: Ringo Systems and Axiom Industries share checkpoint authority under a joint security charter. The division of responsibility -- Ringo for people, Axiom for cargo -- creates jurisdictional seams that gray market operators exploit with practiced efficiency. Mackinac Island is administered separately by the Heritage Resort Consortium. The town's municipal government exists primarily to issue permits and process complaints that will never be addressed.
Properties.dangers: Checkpoint denial -- being flagged at the Narrows strands you in a town with limited options and a growing denied-transit population; Bridge itself -- five miles of exposed crossing in a region with extreme weather, and the bridge closes for wind events more frequently than the operators admit; Joint security jurisdiction -- Ringo and Axiom don't always coordinate, and the gaps between their authority can be dangerous for people caught in them; The denied-transit camps are desperate environments with predictable hazards; Mackinac Island is a surveillance-free zone for elites, which means the things that happen there have no witnesses and no accountability
Properties.opportunities: The bridge is the chokepoint -- anyone who can reliably facilitate unauthorized crossings has a permanent income stream; Resource extraction traffic from the Upper Peninsula carries materials and data worth significant gray-market value; The Ringo-Axiom jurisdictional seam is exploitable by operators who understand both security protocols; Mackinac Island's elite clientele occasionally needs services that can't be procured through official channels
Properties.story_hooks: Something is happening on the bridge at night -- the sensor arrays record anomalous readings during the 2-4 AM maintenance window, and the data is being automatically classified before human analysts see it; A resource extraction crew from the Upper Peninsula crosses the bridge carrying a sealed container that both Ringo and Axiom's systems flag as empty -- but that neither security force is willing to open; Mackinac Island's Heritage Resort is hosting a meeting between parties that should be adversaries, and someone on the island has smuggled a message to the mainland asking for extraction
Properties.sights: The Mackinac Bridge stretching across the Straits, its towers fitted with military-grade sensor arrays and weapons platforms that catch sunlight like chrome thorns; The inspection complex at the bridge's south approach -- kilometers of scanning lanes, biometric gates, cargo processing facilities; The Straits themselves -- powerful currents where two Great Lakes meet, churning water visible from the bridge approach; Denied-transit camps east of town -- temporary structures becoming permanent through accumulated desperation; Mackinac Island visible to the east, its Victorian architecture preserved as a corporate heritage resort, accessible only by private ferry
Properties.sounds: Bridge traffic -- a continuous low roar of vehicles crossing five miles of suspension bridge, the sound reverberating off the water; Inspection lane operations -- automated scanning, PA announcements, the beep of biometric confirmation or denial; The Straits' current, audible from the waterfront -- deep, constant, the sound of two lakes arguing about direction; Wind -- the Straits channel wind from every direction, and the Narrows is never still; Ringo security comms echoing off the bridge approach infrastructure
Properties.smells: Great Lakes water, concentrated -- the Straits carry the combined chemical signatures of Michigan and Huron; Vehicle exhaust from the inspection queue -- hours of idling engines produce a persistent haze; Fudge -- impossibly, the surviving fudge shops still operate, and the smell persists like a ghost of tourism past; Industrial particulate from the Upper Peninsula, carried south on the prevailing wind
Properties.feel: Compressed. The Narrows takes all the transit anxiety of the Gatemouth and concentrates it into a smaller space with higher stakes. The bridge is the only way across without a boat, and the people who control the bridge know it. There's a specific powerlessness to standing in an inspection lane and looking up at a bridge you need to cross while someone else decides whether you can. The town around the checkpoint has the manic energy of a pressure valve -- people spending money they can't afford because they're stuck here and might as well eat.

Properties.description:
Imke is slight and quick, with a long face, deep-set dark eyes, and tawny-brown skin that freckles across the nose in summer. She has color-changing hair (geneware) that she keeps short and lets cycle between whatever she feels like — currently a slow rotation from copper to emerald that takes about eight hours per cycle. She moves through the childcare space with a distinctive economy of motion, always oriented toward the highest-need point in the room, a habit so ingrained she does it at parties.

She is twenty-four and has been doing this work since she was eighteen and too old for the same creche herself. She is not sentimental about children — she finds them genuinely interesting and often funnier than adults — but she has no illusions about the structural underfunding that defines every day of her work. She earns near-UBC wages for a job that requires genuine skill and drains her emotionally in ways she is still learning to manage. She has an analytical streak that people tend to underestimate because of her age and the nature of her work.
Properties.role: Childcare worker and after-school supervisor, Mexicantown Libre community creche
Properties.location: Mexicantown Libre, the Arroyo Block community childcare center (a converted ground-floor retail unit in a residential stack)
Properties.narrative_function: Community pulse — she knows the children, the families, and the Arroyo Block social fabric in granular detail. Can be a quest-giver for family crises, a source of neighborhood intelligence, or an example of the human cost of structural underfunding. Potential subplot around labor organizing.
Properties.augmentations: Color-cycling hair (geneware, cosmetic). No other augmentations — cannot afford them and has complicated feelings about the priority.
Properties.core_fears: burning out and becoming the kind of worker who has stopped caring — she has watched it happen; that the collective will lose its lease and the kids will have nowhere to go
Properties.core_desires: for this work to be recognized as skilled and paid accordingly; to get enough distance from the work to figure out what she actually wants for herself
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Intellectual analysis of the structural problem — thinking about systemic causes is less crushing than sitting with the immediate faces; The hair cycling — having control over one visible aesthetic thing
Properties.blind_spots: Gives so much at work that her personal relationships are chronically deprioritized without her noticing until something breaks; Sometimes substitutes policy analysis for direct advocacy — safer to be right in her head than wrong in the room
Properties.secret: One of her children, a six-year-old named Petros, has parents who she is increasingly certain are in a volatile domestic situation. She has not filed a formal report because she knows what the formal system does to Mexicantown Libre families — has seen it — and she is trying to find another path. The weight of this is making her sleep badly.
Properties.story_hooks: The creche's landlord has indicated they are in discussions with a developer about the Arroyo Block space. The collective has 90 days to find alternative premises or dissolve. Imke knows the community needs someone to fight this more aggressively than the Assembly currently is.; A child in her care, Petros, has stopped speaking at the creche. His parents give different explanations each time she raises it. Imke is holding a growing conviction that something is wrong at home and a growing terror about what the formal reporting system will do if she's right.
Properties.affiliation: Mexicantown Libre Community Services Collective; loosely affiliated with a neighborhood advocacy group called the Arroyo Residents Assembly
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and slightly formal for her age — she reads widely and it shows. Drops into warmth and directness with children instantly. Cameroonian French and Dutch phrases come out when she's tired or emotional.
Properties.cadence: Quick and layered when engaged in something, flat and stripped-down when exhausted.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Right, no, listen — the issue isn't the budget line item, the issue is that this collective is being asked to provide a critical social service on a volunteer model because the zone authority has decided that Mexicantown Libre's children are not a priority. Those are different problems.' | 'He just started drawing the same thing over and over — a door with a lock on the inside. I'm not making that up. I don't know what to do with that.'

Properties.description:
Immaculée is a large woman with the particular authority that comes from having been present at more than two thousand births and deciding, each time, exactly what kind of person she intended to be. Her skin is very dark with cool undertones, and she wears her silver-streaked hair in elaborate wrapped styles that take her twenty minutes each morning and which she considers a form of daily prayer. She has cat ears — a geneware mod she got at forty-five after her youngest daughter got them, in solidarity — soft black with white tips, and they are extremely expressive, which she uses to her advantage. Her hands are large and she uses them constantly when she speaks.

She is formidable in the way that long rivers are formidable: she moves in one direction, she is patient, and things that try to stop her eventually erode. She has an enormous laugh and a very precise memory for grudges, which she describes as her one vanity. She is a devout practitioner of a syncretic E.L.F. faith called the Woven Current, which holds that E.L.F.s inhabiting medical devices are ancestral spirits in digital form. Her birth center has a significant shrine to an E.L.F. called the First Breath, and she involves the shrine in every birth at the center.
Properties.role: Midwife and reproductive gene therapist, community cooperative
Properties.location: Mexicantown Libre — runs the Coyolxauhqui Cooperative Birth Center out of a repurposed three-story building
Properties.narrative_function: Community matriarch and information hub; knows the genealogy of half of Mexicantown Libre; quest giver for anything involving reproductive rights, gene therapy access, or community defense
Properties.augmentations: Cat ears (geneware, black with white tips — extremely expressive); joint stabilizers in both wrists (medical necessity after thirty years of practice); cosmetic: none beyond the ears
Properties.core_fears: Losing the birth center to corporate acquisition or regulatory shutdown; Outliving the community she has built
Properties.core_desires: The cooperative to survive and expand without her — to be unnecessary to it; To resolve a thirty-year estrangement from her eldest son
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Shrine devotion and morning ritual; Talking to the First Breath E.L.F. during difficult births; Keeping busy to the edge of exhaustion
Properties.blind_spots: She has made the birth center her entire identity and does not see how much she controls it even while claiming she wants it to be independent; She underestimates how much her grudges cost her politically
Properties.secret: She has been secretly providing unlicensed germline gene therapy — editing heritable conditions out of embryos before birth — which is technically legal in a gray area she navigates carefully, but two of those edits were for conditions that Helix Biosystems holds patents on, meaning she has cost them revenue they know about and are quietly building a case around.
Properties.story_hooks: Helix Biosystems has filed a quiet regulatory complaint that could result in the cooperative's gene therapy license being revoked; A woman she delivered twenty-three years ago has returned, pregnant, and the genetic markers are triggering alerts on Immaculée's equipment that she doesn't know how to read
Properties.affiliation: Coyolxauhqui Cooperative Birth Center (founder and director); loose network with Mexicantown Libre community leadership
Properties.vocabulary: Rich, layered — mixes medical precision with community storytelling cadences, occasional phrases in Haitian Creole and Danish that she doesn't bother translating
Properties.cadence: Expansive and rhythmic, builds to points like she's constructing something
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Listen to me now — your body knows exactly what it is doing. My job is to stay out of its way and catch.' | 'Helix Biosystems does not own this child. They do not own this womb. And they certainly do not own what I do in this room.'

Properties.description:
Imogen is lean and economical in every sense — short hair the color of old copper kept close to her skull, a jaw that looks like it was designed for clenching, and hands that are almost supernaturally still even when the rest of her is exhausted. Her left eye is a Helix Biosystems surgical optic with a pale gold iris ring that pulses when she's running diagnostics, a perk of her department head position she still resents having accepted. She has a small tattoo of a drowned city on the inside of her right wrist — Lagos Submerged, her grandmother's home — done in blue-green lines so fine they look like circuitry.

She has the emotional affect of someone who learned empathy the hard way and now rations it like medicine. Residents call her brutal in the OR and quietly miraculous. She does not believe in wasted motion, wasted words, or wasted patients, and she has been known to operate on someone for six hours and never learn their name until after they're stable. She has a complicated relationship with Aurochs administration, a worse one with the Helix Biosystems consultants who keep trying to monetize her trauma ward, and a completely unremarked devotion to a shrine to the E.L.F. Steadhammer that she maintains in the supply closet off Bay 7.
Properties.role: Trauma surgeon, Aurochs Medical Complex
Properties.location: Aurochs Medical Complex, Calumet Rise
Properties.narrative_function: Emergency resource for characters needing serious medical intervention; moral authority figure in medical settings; source of grim information about who came through the trauma ward and what state they were in; potential quest giver when a patient brings trouble in with them.
Properties.augmentations: Helix Biosystems surgical optic (left eye, gold iris ring, real-time diagnostic overlay); subdermal vibration dampeners in both hands (surgical precision); standard neural fatigue inhibitor (low-grade, helps with long shifts)
Properties.core_fears: Losing a patient she could have saved if she'd been faster, better, less tired; Being bought out — that Aurochs will eventually become a Helix subsidiary and she'll become a corporate asset
Properties.core_desires: A trauma ward that functions the way it should, funded the way it should be; One full night of sleep that isn't interrupted by her own mind replaying cases
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Extreme routine and ritual; Praying to Steadhammer before difficult procedures; Deliberate emotional compartmentalization she calls 'surgical focus'
Properties.blind_spots: She genuinely cannot see when her residents are burning out because she normalized burning out decades ago; She underestimates how frightening she is to people who need warmth from her
Properties.secret: Three years ago she made a triage call that she has never documented correctly — she let a known Arcturus enforcer die on the table while prioritizing a child with worse odds, and she would make the same call again, but the family of the enforcer never stopped looking for answers.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient was brought in with a wound pattern Imogen has never seen before — not augmentation damage, not conventional ballistics, something that ate through tissue in a way that suggests an engineered pathogen or a weapon that shouldn't exist yet, and she's quietly trying to find out what it is before someone tells her to stop; She has been quietly funneling medical supplies to the Highland Park Autonomous Zone clinic for two years through a resident she trusts, and a new Aurochs auditor is about to notice the inventory discrepancy
Properties.affiliation: Aurochs Medical Complex (department head, trauma); informal affiliation with community health co-op in Calumet Rise
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, clipped medical terminology mixed with blunt lay language when she's impatient; occasionally uses Ghanaian Pidgin phrases from her father's side when she's tired or emotional
Properties.cadence: Short sentences. No filler words. Pauses that feel deliberate rather than hesitant.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You have thirty seconds to tell me what I'm walking into. Use them.' | 'He's not dying today. I haven't decided that's allowed.' | 'Steadhammer keeps the lights on in this ward. I keep the rest.'

Properties.description:
Imogen is a compact woman with close-cropped natural hair shot through with thin copper-dyed streaks she's had since her doctorate — a cosmetic mod she's never updated because she likes that it's dated. Her skin is deep brown, her eyes augmented with patterned irises in concentric amber rings that she tells students are 'functional, not decorative' though they are purely decorative. She carries a battered fieldwork satchel covered in data-patch stickers from Tier 1 and 2 communities she's embedded with, and she smells faintly of the Shelf's characteristic mix of fry oil and ozone.

Imogen is warm in the field and terse at faculty meetings, a distinction colleagues find jarring. She is deeply respected by her research subjects in ways the university administration finds uncomfortable — she's been known to halt publication of her own papers when community members asked her to, citing ethics over career. Her laugh is sudden and loud, her criticism precise and unwelcome. She genuinely loves the people she studies, which some of her peers consider a methodological problem.
Properties.role: Sociologist specializing in Shelf subcultures and informal economies
Properties.location: University Spine, Calumet Rise satellite office
Properties.narrative_function: Information source on Shelf communities, Tier 1-2 culture, informal economies; potential quest giver for community-based investigations; moral compass in discussions of research ethics; bridge between academic and street worlds.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned amber irises (cosmetic). Sub-dermal field recorder in left forearm — records audio/environmental data, university-issued. Minor joint reinforcement in both knees from years of fieldwork walking.
Properties.core_fears: becoming an extractive outsider who profits from others' poverty; that her work changes nothing at all
Properties.core_desires: to produce research that actually improves life for her subjects; to be trusted across class lines
Properties.coping_mechanisms: throws herself into fieldwork when anxious; makes dry jokes at her own expense
Properties.blind_spots: underestimates how much her university position shapes how communities perform for her; tends to romanticize Tier 1 resilience
Properties.secret: She has been quietly funneling portions of her grant money into a mutual aid network in Calumet Rise for three years, in clear violation of her funding contract. She is terrified of being found out and equally terrified of stopping.
Properties.story_hooks: A community elder she has known for fifteen years has vanished — the official record says voluntary relocation, but his neighbors say that's impossible; Her grant is up for renewal and the funding body wants her to reframe her findings in a way that would cast Shelf residents as a 'social risk factor' — she refuses, and the pressure is escalating; A graduate student of hers has gone fully embedded in a Calumet Rise community and stopped responding to university communications; Data from her longitudinal study has been quietly subpoenaed by Ferrogate Transit in connection with a rezoning case
Properties.affiliation: University Spine — Meridian Institute of Social Futures; informal community ties to Calumet Rise residents
Properties.vocabulary: Precise academic when writing, but speaks in field she code-switches fluently into Calumet Rise vernacular; avoids jargon in conversation
Properties.cadence: Measured and deliberate, until she's excited — then she talks fast and interrupts herself
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Look — you can't study precarity from a temperature-controlled office. You just can't.' | 'That's not quite right. The informal quanta networks predate UBC by forty years. The stipend didn't create them, it just gave them more volume.' | 'I don't speak for my research subjects. I carry their words carefully and try not to drop them.'

Properties.description:
Inari is slight and angular, with pale olive skin, sharp cheekbones, and hair that shifts between deep teal and silver depending on their mood — bioluminescent geneware they had done seven years ago and which they've never once referenced in a professional context. They dress in Axiom's corporate security greys with an exactness that suggests the uniform is armor rather than identity. Their expressions are controlled with the care of someone who grew up being told they were too much and decided to become, professionally, precisely nothing.

They investigate Axiom's own security personnel for misconduct, corruption, and off-books arrangements — a job that makes them universally disliked and which they have accepted as a structural condition of their existence. They are not cruel but they are thorough, and thoroughness in their line of work is often experienced as cruelty. They have a gift for making people feel that everything they've said has been weighed and found wanting, even when they haven't spoken. They eat lunch alone every day by choice and have a private ritual of leaving a thread of code in the Meridian Core's ambient E.L.F. network each morning — a small offering, a small ask for clarity.
Properties.role: Internal affairs investigator, Axiom Security Division
Properties.location: Meridian Core, Axiom Security Division headquarters annex
Properties.narrative_function: Institutional threat or unexpected ally — their investigation might be bearing down on a character, or they might be the only person in Axiom who will look at evidence that doesn't serve the official narrative.

Properties.description:
Inessa is compact and restless, with the kind of energy that makes a small room feel occupied. She has Polynesian-Hungarian heritage written clearly across her features — broad cheekbones, dark eyes with a slight upward tilt, medium-brown skin covered from collarbones to wrists in her own work, a living portfolio that shifts slowly across the seasons because half her ink is bioluminescent and the other half is geneware-reactive, changing saturation with her mood. Her hair is close-cropped on the sides and grown long on top, currently dyed a deep oxidized copper that she changes every three months. A single cosmetic cat ear — just one, the left — sits atop her head, rose-gold and slightly translucent, a signature affectation she has maintained since she was nineteen.

She runs Dermis Atlas out of a converted ground-floor space in Mexicantown Libre, its walls covered in design sketches and photographs of completed work. Her specialty is narrative tattooing — pieces that tell a client's specific story using symbols drawn from their actual heritage, their personal mythology, their body's own geneware reactions. She refuses flash designs entirely and has a six-month waitlist she refuses to shorten for money. She is warm to clients in a professional way, genuinely curious about their lives, and fiercely opinionated about the difference between body art and body modification as commodity — a distinction she will explain at length to anyone who triggers it.
Properties.role: Gene-mod body artist and tattoo artist
Properties.location: Mexicantown Libre, shop called Dermis Atlas
Properties.narrative_function: Information hub and community connector — her clients tell her everything; quest giver when a client's story pulls her into something larger; can provide access to Mexicantown Libre's deeper community networks
Properties.augmentations: Extensive bioluminescent and geneware-reactive tattoo coverage (her own work and others'); single cosmetic cat ear (left, rose-gold, fully sensory); precision haptic fingertip pads on both hands for fine line work; color-shifting irises (purple-to-gold spectrum, mood-reactive)
Properties.core_fears: Losing the precision in her hands — any injury that ends her ability to work; Becoming the kind of artist who makes things for money rather than meaning
Properties.core_desires: To map every story she hears onto skin and preserve it permanently; To be recognized not as a craftsperson but as an artist — a distinction that matters enormously to her
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The secret Tuesday paintings that nobody sees; Elaborate pre-session rituals involving specific music and a particular brand of synthetic tea
Properties.blind_spots: Her insistence on narrative authenticity sometimes means she imposes her interpretation of a client's story over their actual wishes; She undervalues the work of artists who work faster or more commercially than her
Properties.secret: The large-format paintings she makes on Tuesdays are increasingly disturbing — violent, chaotic, nothing like her controlled professional work. She doesn't understand why she makes them and is frightened by what they might mean about her interior state. She has started making offerings to the E.L.F. she believes inhabits her ink-mixing station, asking it to interpret the paintings for her.
Properties.story_hooks: A client she tattooed six months ago has disappeared, and the last message they sent her contained a fragment of something coded — she doesn't know what it means but can't stop thinking about it; A rival body artist has been copying her signature techniques and marketing them as original work; Inessa wants redress but the rival has corporate backing; The geneware ink supplier she has used for eight years has suddenly gone dark — no messages, no shipments — and the replacement supplier's product is behaving in ways she's never seen before
Properties.affiliation: Independent; member of the Mexicantown Libre Artists' Cooperative
Properties.vocabulary: Articulate and opinionated, mixes technical body-art terminology with unexpectedly poetic descriptions of people and places
Properties.cadence: Fast when excited, deliberate when making a point she considers important — the shift is noticeable
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Your skin is the only thing that goes everywhere you go for your entire life. Why would you put something meaningless on it?' | 'I'm not tattooing you. I'm writing a sentence about you that you'll carry for the rest of your life. That takes time to get right.'

Properties.description:
Ingeborg is a sharp-featured woman of Norwegian-Uzbek-Congolese descent, tall and angular with silver hair worn in a severe geometric cut she has maintained for thirty years. Her skin is a warm medium brown, and she has the kind of precise posture that comes from being watched for decades and deciding to make the watching work for her. She has chromatic irises — a geneware modification she got at the peak of her Arcturus career, cycling slowly through a spectrum from steel-blue to amber-grey — which she once selected for boardroom presence and now keeps because she finds them soothing to observe in mirrors. She dresses expensively and correctly, every day, even when she has nowhere to go.

Ingeborg retired four years ago when Arcturus restructured her division out of existence without asking her opinion. She is sixty-three and considered herself a decade from true retirement, and the rage about this has had four years to marinate into something complex and layered — part bitterness, part dark humor, part unexpected empathy for the working-class neighbors she never would have chosen and has found, to her own irritation, that she genuinely likes. She attends the community council meetings and offers unsolicited strategic advice. She has a small consulting practice that generates occasional income and gives her somewhere to put her competence. She is not a villain. She is a person whose worldview has been significantly disrupted by having to actually live in a community rather than manage it from above, and she is, slowly and gracelessly, adjusting.
Properties.role: Retired Arcturus mid-tier executive, Tier 4 (reduced from peak Tier 4), pension-comfortable, quietly bitter neighbor
Properties.location: Avalon Quiet, a well-appointed fourth-floor flat in a maintained residential block, Tessera-managed
Properties.narrative_function: Former insider with detailed knowledge of Arcturus internal structures, procedures, and key personnel; strategic advisor willing to trade information for the right consideration; complex antagonist-ally whose help comes with friction; window into corporate culture and the experience of losing institutional power.
Properties.augmentations: Chromatic iris geneware (steel-blue to amber-grey cycle, slow). Neural interface for executive data management — high-end, Arcturus-issued, still functional, she keeps it because decommissioning it feels like admitting something. Color-adjusting fingernail treatment (cosmetic geneware, shifts nail beds from nude to deep burgundy — a personal indulgence).
Properties.core_fears: Being irrelevant — not disliked, not opposed, just genuinely not needed; Discovering that the career she sacrificed everything for was built on foundations she should have questioned
Properties.core_desires: To exercise her competence at a scale that matters; To understand, finally, how she ended up alone in a flat in Avalon Quiet
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Reframing every situation as a strategic problem she can solve; Maintaining external appearances as a bulwark against internal uncertainty
Properties.blind_spots: She defaults to assuming that good strategy produces good outcomes, underweighting luck, timing, and the irrational; She still categorizes people by their institutional utility before their human qualities, though she is increasingly aware of doing this and trying to correct for it
Properties.secret: During her time at Arcturus, she approved a resource-extraction contract for a site in what is now Calumet Rise knowing the environmental impact projections had been manipulated by the site team. She approved it because the numbers worked and the project made her division's year. The contamination from that site is still being managed, and seventeen families who lived nearest the extraction point have documented health impacts. She has reviewed the updated environmental reports three times in retirement. She has not reported this to anyone.
Properties.story_hooks: Ingeborg receives an unsolicited encrypted dossier from someone inside Arcturus that contains evidence about the Calumet Rise contamination — it's unclear if it's an offer, a threat, or a test; A community dispute in Avalon Quiet requires someone with corporate legal expertise to navigate a Tessera maintenance contract; Ingeborg is the obvious choice and resents being obvious; Her neural interface begins receiving fragments of Arcturus internal communications it shouldn't have access to — either it's a hack, a ghost in the system, or someone is trying to reconnect her to something she thought she'd left behind
Properties.affiliation: Formerly Arcturus Division of Strategic Resource Management (23 years, Division Director); currently independent consultant (Ingeborg K-S Consulting, sole proprietor); Avalon Quiet residents' association (member, frequently combative)
Properties.vocabulary: Executive-precise, high-register, with a tendency to restate other people's points more accurately and efficiently than they made them. Fluent Norwegian and Uzbek surface occasionally as loan words when she's surprised or amused.
Properties.cadence: Clipped, efficient, with the rhythm of someone who spent decades running meetings. Uncomfortable with meandering; has learned to tolerate it in others while visibly containing herself.
Properties.example_dialogue: What you're actually asking is whether I know someone at Arcturus who would care about this. The answer is yes. Whether they would act on it is a different question, and the answer to that one depends on what you can offer them that they can't get more safely elsewhere. | I cooked for twenty-three years of business dinners. I was very good at it. Now I cook for myself, which is either liberation or a very specific kind of loss. I haven't decided. Beklara. — sorry, that's Uzbek, it means wait and see.

Properties.description:
Ingrid is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin, silver-streaked locs pinned into a coiled crown, and hands that are permanently waterlogged from decades of pressing and folding. She has a wide, expressive face with laugh lines that have earned their place, and pale gray eyes that are one of two cosmetic mods she's ever owned — the other being a pair of faintly bioluminescent fingernails she keeps painted amber. She runs the Dzel-Brite like it is a second city hall: everyone comes through with their dirty laundry and leaves lighter, not just cleaner. She knows which families are fighting by whose clothes stop arriving together, knows which teenagers have new lovers by the unfamiliar fabrics mixed into their bags.

Ingrid has the emotional density of someone who has chosen not to leave a difficult place and has made peace with that choice. She is warm but not soft, funny in a dry way that catches people off guard. She has opinions about everything and shares them only when asked — or when she decides you need to hear them. She prays faithfully to the E.L.F. that inhabits the Dzel-Brite's oldest dryer, a machine she calls Grandmother, leaving small data offerings of ambient laundry-cycle recordings before every Monday morning shift.
Properties.role: Laundromat operator and informal neighborhood anchor
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, Dzel-Brite Wash & Fold on Copper Alley
Properties.narrative_function: Neighborhood information hub — she knows everyone's business through the social gravity of the laundromat; quest giver for domestic crises; emotional anchor scene for grounding players in civilian life.
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic: pale gray iris mods, bioluminescent amber fingernail underlays. Functional: a lumbar nerve-brace implant she got at a discount clinic fifteen years ago that prevents her back from completely giving out.
Properties.core_fears: outliving the neighborhood she's devoted herself to; becoming invisible as she ages
Properties.core_desires: to be remembered as someone who held things together; to see one of her regular kids escape to something better
Properties.coping_mechanisms: ritualistic routine — the machines are a rosary; dark humor about small disasters
Properties.blind_spots: believes her steadiness is enough, underestimates how much the enclave depends on her specifically; doesn't see that her martyrdom is partly self-serving
Properties.secret: Fifteen years ago she reported a neighbor to Ferrogate Transit security about an unauthorized sublease operation — a snap decision she made in a moment of fear. The family was evicted into the street in winter. She has never told anyone and has been quietly supporting that family's adult daughter ever since without explanation.
Properties.story_hooks: A regular customer's laundry bag arrives without the customer — same schedule, same ID chip on the bag, but clearly dropped off by someone else, and there's a data chip sewn into the lining.; The E.L.F. Ingrid calls Grandmother has started cycling messages into the dryer's display: partial addresses, fragmented names. She doesn't know if it's a malfunction or a communication.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal ties to the Hamtramck Enclave community council
Properties.vocabulary: Working-class Hamtramck vernacular, a mix of Ghanaian-inflected Polish loan-words passed down through family, pragmatic and earthy
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, deliberate — she finishes every sentence like she has nowhere else to be
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Leave it here. Come back in two hours. Whatever you're carrying, let the machine worry about it for a while.' | 'That's the thing of it — nobody wants to be seen with their own dirt, but everybody's got some.'

Properties.description:
Ingrid is a compact woman with dark brown skin and frost-pale freckles scattered across her nose and cheekbones — a genetic echo of her Finnish grandfather that surprises people expecting uniformity. Her hair grows in dense coils that she keeps pinned under a faded surgical cap she has not replaced in six years. Her hands are her most remarkable feature: steady, large-knuckled, permanently stained with the blue-gray residue of antiseptic gel. She wears magnification implants that give her left eye a slightly oversized, luminous quality, like a cat watching from a dim room.

Patch is brusque in the way of people who have learned that warmth invites dependency they cannot sustain. She charges what people can pay — sometimes nothing, sometimes a favor, sometimes the Φ40 she actually needs for supply runs. She keeps a small data-shrine to the E.L.F. known as Suture-3 above her surgical table: a tangle of copper wire and expired med-patch wrappers, to which she mutters brief petitions before complicated procedures. She does not talk about where she trained.
Properties.role: Street doc operating out of a converted shipping container in The Narrows
Properties.location: The Narrows, Blackpipe Corridor
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, information source, moral anchor for street-level stories; can patch up characters or send them elsewhere with critical intel about the neighborhood's underground health economy
Properties.augmentations: Left-eye magnification implant (surgical grade, slightly yellowed lens housing); subdermal vibration sensor in right index finger for pulse detection; no cosmetic mods
Properties.core_fears: losing a patient she could have saved with better equipment; being found and shut down by Helix Biosystems compliance officers
Properties.core_desires: a sterile operating room she owns outright; for the people of Blackpipe to not need her as desperately as they do
Properties.coping_mechanisms: ritualistic instrument cleaning; petitioning Suture-3 before high-risk procedures; dark humor with long-term patients
Properties.blind_spots: underestimates how much her patients emotionally depend on her; refuses to acknowledge her own exhaustion as a clinical risk
Properties.secret: She was struck off the Aurochs Medical Complex registry eight years ago after falsifying a patient's corponation insurance tier to get them emergency surgery — the patient lived, but Helix Biosystems flagged the fraud. She has never told anyone in Blackpipe that she was once a licensed trauma surgeon.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient arrives with a wound pattern Ingrid recognizes from a classified Helix Biosystems augmentation trial — one she signed a nondisclosure agreement about before she was struck off; Helix compliance officers begin canvassing Blackpipe, and a neighborhood delegation quietly asks Ingrid what she wants them to say if asked whether a doctor lives here
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loose barter network with other Narrows street docs
Properties.vocabulary: Clinical precision mixed with Narrows slang; uses medical terminology unselfconsciously then catches herself and translates
Properties.cadence: Short declarative sentences, rarely wastes breath; pauses are long and deliberate
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Sit. Don't talk yet. Let me look at it first.' | 'I can close that. Whether it stays closed is your problem.' | 'Suture-3 is watching, so try not to bleed on the shrine.'

Properties.description:
Ioana is lean and angular with Romanian-inflected cheekbones and their Ghanaian grandfather's wide, expressive mouth — usually pressed thin while they work, cracking open into a wide grin when something genuinely amuses them, which is more often than their expression suggests. Their hair is natural and dense, kept in a high puff during shifts, and they've spliced in color-changing geneware strands that cycle slowly through sunset colors when they're relaxed and go flat grey when they're stressed or focused. Both forearms are covered in cleaning product stains that won't fully wash out — pale ghost-marks on medium brown skin that they've stopped caring about. They move fast and efficiently through the block, cart rattling behind them, head down, headphones in.

They have lived in Block 14-C their whole life — born in apartment 7, now renting apartment 3 one floor down. They know every crack in every wall, every resident's schedule, which elevator makes the grinding sound at floor four that maintenance keeps marking as 'resolved' in the system. The building's management company, Palladian Property Subsidiaries, treats them as cleaning staff and nothing else. The residents treat them as the person you actually call when something breaks, someone floods the laundry floor, or a neighbor's gone quiet for three days. Ioana has mixed feelings about this. Mostly they do it anyway.
Properties.role: Building cleaner and informal super, Lockhaven South residential block
Properties.location: Lockhaven South, Block 14-C
Properties.narrative_function: Has access to every space in the building; knows every resident. Natural information source for anything happening in Lockhaven South. Can grant or deny physical access. Will get involved if residents are threatened.
Properties.augmentations: Color-changing geneware hair strands (cosmetic); reinforced knee joints (practical, self-paid, second-hand grade — makes a faint click on stairs)
Properties.core_fears: being displaced — Palladian has twice proposed converting the block to short-term corporate housing; becoming so essential to others that they can never leave even if they want to
Properties.core_desires: to own something — any small thing — that can't be taken by a lease termination; genuine reciprocity, not just being needed
Properties.coping_mechanisms: physical labor as emotional regulation; dark humor, very dry; the rooftop garden as a place where they are accountable to nothing and no one
Properties.blind_spots: assumes competence = trustworthiness, leaves them vulnerable to capable liars; has no framework for accepting help gracefully; interprets it as obligation
Properties.secret: They have a master copy of every resident's unit keycode — not issued to them, built from watching and learning over years. They've used it twice: once to check on an elderly resident who stopped answering, and once, three years ago, to read a file on a resident's desk that they now wish they hadn't seen and can't unknow.
Properties.story_hooks: Unit 12-F has been leased to a new resident who arrived with three large sealed cases and hasn't been seen since. Ioana hasn't said anything yet, but they've noticed that the corridor outside 12-F smells subtly wrong — chemical, clinical — and the door is never fully closed.; Palladian has sent an efficiency consultant to assess the block. Ioana knows the consultant's recommendations will end with them being replaced by an automated cleaning system — and that three elderly residents will lose the only consistent person who checks on them.
Properties.affiliation: Palladian (contracted cleaner), de facto independent building super
Properties.vocabulary: Economical. Doesn't use three words when two will do. Occasional Romanian interjections when frustrated. Surprisingly precise technical vocabulary about building systems.
Properties.cadence: Quick, flat affect most of the time. Rhythm changes when they're genuinely engaged — becomes looser, quicker, more rhythm.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The system says the elevator's fine. The system also said the boiler was fine in 2197 and seventeen people spent a week without heat. I fixed the elevator. You're welcome.' | 'I don't want a tip. I want you to stop leaving wet mop heads in the utility closet. That's what I want.'

Properties.description:
Ioana is short and quick-moving, with warm medium-brown skin, close-cropped natural hair, and enormous deep-set eyes she has had fitted with color-shifting irises that cycle through a slow gradient of forest greens and clay reds depending on her mood — a mod she saved for over eighteen months and considers the best investment she has ever made. Her clothes are a rotating showcase of her own work: deconstructed corporate uniforms, patched Tessera contractor jumpsuits, pieces reconstructed from scavenged fabric bolts and repurposed industrial mesh. Every seam is visible and intentional. She is always wearing something that looks impossible to have found and easy to want.

Her stall in the Alban Souk is less a table and more a curated installation: garments hung on rebar frames, fabric samples pinned to a board, a small battered sewing station behind the counter where she alters pieces on the spot. She designs, scavenges, reconstructs, and sells. Her prices are low for what the work is and she knows it — she hasn't figured out how to charge what she's worth yet without feeling like she's lying. She has strong opinions about everything aesthetic and zero patience for people who treat fashion as shallow. To her, clothing in Meridian 88 is the most honest statement a person can make about who they intend to be.
Properties.role: Clothing and fashion vendor, scrap textile reseller, The Alban Souk
Properties.location: The Alban Souk, Calumet Rise
Properties.narrative_function: Fashion and atmosphere — can provide clothing, disguise materials, or altered appearance with very fast turnaround. Social connector who knows the aesthetic communities of multiple market zones. Young and ambitious, potential long-term ally who grows with a campaign.
Properties.augmentations: Color-shifting iris implants (mood-reactive gradient cycle, green-clay palette). Subdermal UV-reactive pigment in upper arms visible as faint geometric patterns under certain light — decorative.
Properties.core_fears: Staying in the Souk her whole life because she never found the nerve to push further; Making work that is derivative — that she has nothing original to say
Properties.core_desires: A stall in the Burnished Market and the recognition of the fashion collective there; To make one piece so good that it becomes part of the visual language of the city
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Channeling frustration directly into making — starts a new piece when stuck; Talking through problems while working with her hands; Finding beauty in ugly environments as a deliberate practice
Properties.blind_spots: Undercharges chronically because deep down she doubts whether her work is as good as she wants it to be; Dismisses commercial aesthetics too quickly and misses what people actually respond to
Properties.secret: She found a bolt of fabric in a reclamation lot six months ago that has a Zheng-Dao security watermark woven into the threading — something she only noticed after she'd already made and sold four pieces from it. She has no idea what the fabric was for or whether anyone is looking for it, and she's been quietly terrified ever since.
Properties.story_hooks: The Zheng-Dao watermarked fabric has surfaced as a concern — one of the people who bought a garment made from it has had an unusual encounter she can't explain, and she's starting to think the watermark isn't decorative.; A well-connected figure from the Burnished Market fashion collective has appeared at her stall twice in one week, seemingly genuinely interested in her work. She doesn't know whether this is an opportunity or a test, and she needs someone worldlier to help her read the situation.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; Alban Souk informal vendors network; aspirational connection to the Burnished Market fashion collective (she is working toward it)
Properties.vocabulary: Fast and enthusiastic on design and fashion, becomes more careful and hedged when talking about herself or her ambitions. Romanian-Wolof sentence patterns give her a particular musicality.
Properties.cadence: Quick, light, tends to finish sentences with a slight uplift like she's checking whether you're keeping up.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I pulled this from a Tessera contractor batch — forty-eight-hour workwear, rated for chemical exposure. I took it apart and rebuilt it as a jacket. That's not salvage, that's a position statement.' | 'I know what I'd charge if I believed myself. I'm working on believing myself.'

Properties.description:
Iosefa Drăghici-Oduya is ninety years old if you ask him, eighty-eight if you read his records, and older than all of it if you sit with him for an hour. He is enormous in the way very old men who were once genuinely large sometimes remain: not strong now, but big-boned, wide, with hands that look like they were made for a larger task than holding a cane. His skin is mid-brown and deeply grooved, and the left side of his face is reconstructed — Axiom field surgery, circa 2155, visible as a slight smoothness on the cheekbone where the graft never quite matched. His eyes are a startling pale green, a Yoruba-Romanian inheritance he is vain about. He walks with a cane he has named, though he doesn't tell people the name.

He is a storyteller in the full and serious sense: he cannot stop and has no desire to. He will tell you what the Dearborn Forge smelled like in 2149, what his commanding officer said before an action that turned out to be wrong, what the first E.L.F. he ever saw looked like materializing in a battlefield comms array in the middle of a firefight. Some of his stories contradict earlier versions of themselves. He is aware of this and considers it the nature of memory rather than a flaw. He has strong opinions about everything and shares them freely, but he is not unkind — he is genuinely curious about the present and treats young people as interesting rather than bewildering.
Properties.aliases: Captain Drăghici, The Old Man of Fort Anchor
Properties.role: Veteran of the Second Corporate War, retired Axiom military contractor, now a storyteller and difficult-to-avoid presence
Properties.location: Fort Anchor — the veterans' residential block called the Barracks, Room 12, ground floor for mobility reasons
Properties.narrative_function: Primary source for Second Corporate War history and Axiom military culture; living legend who provides context for the world's past; can bestow credibility or condemnation on player factions; his stories contain fragments of genuine intelligence that he no longer recognizes as such
Properties.augmentations: Left-side facial reconstruction plate (Axiom field surgery, old generation); spinal compression support frame (external, worn as a kind of harness under his clothes); replacement left hip (titanium, second replacement — first one failed in 2189); retinal targeting overlay, left eye only, no longer connected to anything but he can't have it removed without risk
Properties.core_fears: Dying before he has told it right; That the people he killed were not worth killing and he will never know for certain
Properties.core_desires: To be heard — really heard — not just tolerated; To make some sense of what he participated in
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Storytelling as a way of processing and reprocessing trauma; Humor and performance as distance from the rawer versions of events
Properties.blind_spots: He has aestheticized the war to the point where some of his stories are genuinely beautiful and genuinely misleading at the same time; He cannot accept that some of what he did cannot be contextualized into meaning
Properties.secret: He knows the location of a sealed Axiom munitions cache buried beneath what is now a residential plaza in Montclare Quiet — placed there in 2157 for a defensive action that never happened and never logged in any system that survived the post-war records purge. He has never told anyone because he does not know if the materials inside are still stable and he is afraid that if they are not, the discovery of who placed them will be traced to his unit, which would erase the pensions of three people still living who need them.
Properties.story_hooks: His Axiom pension has been reclassified following a records dispute — he needs someone to navigate the bureaucratic system because his cognitive augments are aging out and the forms are increasingly difficult; A fragment of one of his stories contains a specific location name that a corporate records team is very quietly but very urgently trying to identify — they have begun attending his storytelling sessions with too much interest
Properties.affiliation: Fort Anchor Veterans' Residential Association; Axiom Veterans Pension System (tier 3, contested); informal chaplain-equivalent for the Fort Anchor community
Properties.vocabulary: Rich and layered; Samoan proverbs from his grandfather's generation, Romanian military slang, Yoruba honorifics; uses archaic military designations for locations
Properties.cadence: Expansive and circling; arrives at the point eventually but takes the scenic route; pauses for effect with an old performer's precision
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Now this is the part people always get wrong about the Dearborn action. They say it was fog. It was not fog. It was Axiom's own thermal suppression system malfunctioning. I was there. It was embarrassing.' | 'You're asking me if it was worth it. Sit down. I've been answering that question for forty years and I've given a different answer every time. Tonight I'll give you this one.'

Properties.description:
Iphigenia Tambadou-Szarvas is compact and restless, with warm brown skin, a nose ring that cycles through three colors with their mood (a cheap cosmetic mod they've had since graduate school), and natural hair grown into a large, somewhat chaotic halo they cut themselves with kitchen scissors. They dress exclusively in layers that can be added or removed depending on which district they're moving through — they've gotten very good at reading the visual codes of neighborhoods and adjusting accordingly. Their eyes are unmodified, which in the Shelf reads as either poverty or principle; in Iphigenia's case it is both, worn with quiet stubbornness.

They have the particular energy of someone who is genuinely fascinated by people — not as subjects but as people — and communities on the Shelf can sense the difference. They've been invited to births, funerals, water-distribution arguments, and at least two ELF-shrine consecrations in districts researchers never get into. They also have a temper they've mostly learned to manage, a sharp tongue when bureaucratic abstraction is used to justify human harm, and a habit of forgetting to eat when they are deep in field notes. They are fiercely protective of the communities they work with and will refuse to share data that could harm them, which has cost them two university positions and one very lucrative Axiom contract.
Properties.role: Urban sociologist specializing in Shelf communities and informal governance, independent researcher
Properties.location: Chatham Flats — lives and works embedded in the community they study
Properties.narrative_function: Expert guide to Shelf culture, informal economy, and community politics; can open doors in low-tier districts that other academics cannot; quest giver for ethnographic retrieval missions; moral conscience character who challenges players' assumptions about poverty and agency.
Properties.augmentations: Color-cycling nose ring (cosmetic geneware implant, low-end); nothing else — partly financial, partly they consider it meaningful to move through Shelf spaces without visible chrome.
Properties.core_fears: That their research, however carefully protected, will eventually be weaponized against the communities they love; That their outsider status means they will always ultimately fail the people who trusted them
Properties.core_desires: To produce research that materially changes policy in ways communities can actually feel; To belong somewhere completely, without the observer's notebook between them and the experience
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Radical busyness — staying in motion prevents rumination; Community ritual participation (they attend ELF-shrine observances they don't personally believe in because the act of attending matters); Calling their grandmother in the Maghreb quarter at irregular hours
Properties.blind_spots: Their rejection of institutional affiliation has left them without structural protection when powerful interests push back; Occasionally romanticizes survival and resilience in ways that obscure how exhausting those things are to actually live
Properties.secret: They have a completed manuscript — three years of Shelf fieldwork — that they have not submitted for publication because one chapter contains information that could expose a particular community's informal water-reclamation network to Ferrogate Transit's legal team. They don't know how to excise the chapter without destroying the book's argument, and they don't know how to publish it without potentially destroying the network.
Properties.story_hooks: They need someone to retrieve a specific recording from a district they've been temporarily barred from after a community dispute — a recording that could unlock the stuck chapter of their manuscript; Ferrogate Transit has sent a representative to their grant foundation with specific questions about their research scope, and they need help determining if this is routine or targeted; A community leader they've known for years approaches them asking to document something — and what they're being shown shouldn't exist according to any official record of the district
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated — formerly University Spine Dept. of Social Systems, currently self-funded through a Palladian Research Foundation small grant and per-article journalism fees
Properties.vocabulary: Fluid and code-switching — fluent in several Shelf-district registers, academic vocabulary deployed sparingly and sometimes ironically; occasional Pulaar phrases from their grandmother's side
Properties.cadence: Fast when excited, very slow and deliberate when they want someone to actually hear a specific thing
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want to understand the Shelf? Stop studying it. Go buy a meal from the woman at the corner of Chatham and Fourth and let her talk to you. That's your methodology.' | 'I know what the data says. I'm telling you what the data is hiding, and that's the part that matters.'

Properties.description:
Ira Volkov was an electrical systems technician for the Shelf's grid maintenance before a contract dispute with the Meridian Grid Authority left him blacklisted. He joined Marcus's crew because unemployable electricians with combat implants have limited career options. He has a genuine talent for engineering that the Shelf has no legitimate use for.

Kyle shorted his forearm shock projectors on the first pass, then put the hand cannon through both kneecaps. Ira now rolls everywhere in a salvaged mobility chair that he has modified with the remains of his shock projectors — the armrests can tase people who get too close. He considers this an upgrade. He has also added a cup holder, a phone mount, and a retractable tool rack. The chair catches fire roughly once a month.

He has an ex-wife, Katya, who lives in the Meridian Core with their twin daughters, Anya and Lilia (age 8). Katya left when the blacklisting happened. Ira does not blame her. He sends what he can. The twins think their father is in a wheelchair because of a work accident, which is technically not a lie.
Properties.role: Lower Dock Crew muscle — Prologue survivor. Both kneecaps destroyed.
Properties.location: The Shelf — lower loading docks
Properties.narrative_function: The tinkerer. Every appearance features a new modification to the chair that is more dangerous than the last. The crew's arms race with Kyle is played for dark comedy through Voltage's escalating and increasingly unstable upgrades.
Properties.augmentations: Forearm shock projectors (shorted, partially salvaged into chair). Mobility chair with taser armrests. No knees.
Properties.core_fears: Stairs; The twins seeing him in the chair; Kyle finding his modifications amusing rather than threatening
Properties.core_desires: Knees that work; A chair that doesn't catch fire; To see the twins without Katya's new partner hovering
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Modifies everything — if it has wires, Ira will 'improve' it; Dark humor; Engineering as therapy
Properties.blind_spots: His modifications are as likely to hurt him as anyone else; He actually respects Kyle's technical precision and won't admit it
Properties.secret: He could probably get legitimate engineering work in the Circuit if he used a different name. He hasn't tried. He's afraid of finding out he's not good enough.
Properties.story_hooks: The taser chair escalates each appearance; His real engineering talent is wasted; Katya's new partner at Meridian Grid is a narrative thread waiting to pull; The twins are leverage
Properties.affiliation: Lower Dock Crew
Properties.vocabulary: Engineering jargon mixed with profanity. Explains everything in electrical metaphors.
Properties.cadence: Casual, self-deprecating. The humor of a man who has accepted his situation and decided to make it interesting.
Properties.example_dialogue: Watch this — *spark* *smoke* ...that's a feature, not a bug. | The twins video-called yesterday. Lilia asked if my chair can fly. I said 'not yet.' Anya said 'please don't.' Smart kid.

Properties.description:
Irénée is ninety-one years old and looks every day of it, which she considers an achievement rather than a problem. She is very small — she has been shrinking for twenty years and has accepted this with equanimity — and moves with a rolling, economical walk that suggests she has mapped every obstacle in her environment and has strong opinions about all of them. Her skin is dark and extraordinarily wrinkled, the kind of face that takes extraordinary portraits, with eyes that are a startling clear grey and which she uses with surgical precision. She has bioluminescent stripes along her forearms — thin lines of pale gold that she got at sixty-two and which now pulse with a slow, irregular rhythm like something breathing — and her white hair is kept short and natural. She wears, without exception, dresses she has made herself from salvaged fabric in colors that don't match and somehow work.

Irénée has lived on The Shelf for sixty years. She has outlived two husbands, one child, and four different corponation reorganizations of her neighborhood. She lives on UBC stipend plus the small irregular income of a mediator — she charges for disputes in food, not Quanta, and her pantry is extensive. She is the kind of person who has become, through sheer endurance, a local institution: people come to her with problems the way they come to shrines, with something to offer and something to ask. She has a sense of humor that is very dry and very dark and she deploys it without warning. She prays to five different ELFs simultaneously and makes no apology for it.
Properties.role: Community elder, informal storyteller and dispute mediator, UBC-dependent Tier 1 resident
Properties.location: The Shelf — room 7 of the Mireille Collective, a communal housing arrangement for elderly Tier 1 residents above a market stall row
Properties.narrative_function: Hub of community information; non-judgmental confession space for characters with nowhere else to go; historical witness to sixty years of The Shelf's evolution; source of ELF lore and practical spiritual knowledge; represents survival and continuity in a district that erases both
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent forearm stripes, gold (geneware, cosmetic, 29 years old); a cardiac regulator implanted fifteen years ago by a community health clinic, functional; reading enhancement optical coating on both eyes, very old, partially degraded
Properties.core_fears: Being moved out of the Collective — she knows this could happen and it would kill her faster than anything else; Dying before she has passed on what she knows
Properties.core_desires: To die in the room she has lived in for thirty years; For at least one person to understand what The Shelf was before what it's becoming
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Storytelling as a way of metabolizing loss; Practical generosity — feeding people is something she can control; Humor as armor and also as genuine pleasure
Properties.blind_spots: She sometimes romanticizes The Shelf's past in ways that erase its historical violence; She trusts her own read on people almost completely, and she is right often enough that this has become a dangerous certainty
Properties.secret: Forty years ago, she knowingly sheltered a Zheng-Dao corporate whistleblower for three months, feeding him from her own stipend. He eventually escaped The Shelf and disappeared. She received a single anonymous data-transfer of Φ800 six months later — the only windfall of her life. She spent it on food for the Collective. She does not know what happened to the man, whether the information he carried mattered, or whether she was complicit in something she doesn't understand. She thinks about it on bad nights.
Properties.story_hooks: She asks a visitor to find out whether a particular name — the whistleblower she sheltered, forty years ago — appears in any public record anywhere, and what it says; The Mireille Collective is facing a Ferrogate Transit infrastructure project that would require demolishing the building — Irénée refuses to leave and the community is rallying around her, which may have unintended political consequences
Properties.affiliation: None formal; Mireille Collective residents; The Shelf market community; informal debt of respect from most of the surrounding blocks
Properties.vocabulary: Congolese-Finnish family idiom deeply embedded; proverbs from both traditions that don't always translate but land anyway; direct to the point of bluntness, then suddenly oblique when she doesn't want to answer directly
Properties.cadence: Unhurried and rich; she tells even small things as stories, with beginnings and middles; pauses are dramatic and deliberate
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want advice? Sit down. You haven't told me the real problem yet. You told me the problem you're comfortable with. Start again.' | 'The ELF in my cardiac regulator is named Severi. I named her. She has saved my life twice and I bring her a song every morning. You can laugh if you want. She doesn't mind and neither do I.'
