Properties.description:
Kenwood was where Chicago's Black elite lived — the grand houses, the manicured lawns, the proof that success was possible even within a system designed to prevent it. A president lived here. University professors. Surgeons. Lawyers. The mansions along Drexel Boulevard and Hyde Park Boulevard were monuments to achievement earned against impossible odds, and they were beautiful in the way that defiant things are always beautiful — not because they were trying to be, but because they had to be, because being anything less would have confirmed what their enemies believed.

When corporate sovereignty arrived, Kenwood's wealth made it a target and a prize. The mansions were too valuable to demolish and too symbolic to ignore. Pellucid Systems — a corporate intelligence firm specializing in data analysis and predictive modeling — acquired the district through a combination of market manipulation and strategic housing-code enforcement that pressured owners into selling at below-market prices. The process took seven years. It was meticulous, legal, and devastating. Pellucid now occupies the grand mansions as executive residences and secure meeting facilities, their original domestic architecture repurposed for corporate intelligence operations. The house where a president once lived is now a signals-analysis center with a rose garden maintained by autonomous drones.

Kenwood Gate gets its name from the perimeter that Pellucid installed — a surveillance boundary so sophisticated that it functions as a physical barrier despite being entirely digital. Cross the Gate's threshold without authorization and your neural interface receives a warning. Cross it again and the warning becomes a migraine. Cross it a third time and Pellucid's security responds in person, which is worse than the migraine. The district is not walled. It does not need to be. The Gate is in your head.

Behind the Gate, Kenwood is eerily preserved. The tree-lined streets are maintained. The mansions are immaculate. The lawns are green. It looks like the best version of what Kenwood always was — a beautiful, affluent, peaceful neighborhood. But the people who made it beautiful and affluent and peaceful through decades of striving are gone. Replaced by corporate analysts, intelligence officers, and Pellucid executives who live in the houses and appreciate the architecture and know nothing about the families who built them. The Obama home is a museum now — Pellucid operates it as a public-relations asset, open by appointment to approved visitors. The tour does not mention how the neighborhood changed hands. The tour does not mention the Gate. The tour does not mention anything that happened after 2130.

A few of the original families remain — those who held out through the seven-year acquisition campaign, who refused to sell at any price, whose legal resistance was strong enough to survive Pellucid's attorneys. They live behind the Gate as neighbors to the people who displaced their community, maintaining their homes with the stubborn precision of people who understand that their presence is itself a form of protest. Pellucid tolerates them. Barely. The holdouts maintain a quiet network that extends beyond the Gate, connecting to the displaced Kenwood community scattered across the South Side. Information flows along this network — information about what Pellucid does inside the mansions, what their analysts are modeling, what their intelligence operations target. The holdouts are Pellucid's neighbors, and they are watching.
Properties.aliases: Kenwood, The Gate, The Mansions, Old Kenwood
Properties.demographics: Approximately 8,000 residents, predominantly Pellucid Systems employees and their families (Tier 4-5). An estimated 200 holdout residents from the original Kenwood community remain, their tier designations ranging from 2 to 4. The district is one of the most economically homogeneous in M88.
Properties.economy: Pellucid Systems' corporate intelligence operations drive the district's economy entirely. The Obama Museum generates modest cultural-tourism revenue. The holdout community maintains a micro-economy of mutual support that operates beneath Pellucid's economic tracking. There are no commercial establishments — everything is provisioned through corporate supply.
Properties.power_structure: Pellucid Systems exercises absolute jurisdiction. The Gate serves as both border and enforcement mechanism. The holdout families' legal protections create a small sphere of autonomy within the district, upheld by pre-sovereignty property rights that Pellucid has not yet found a legal mechanism to extinguish.
Properties.dangers: The Gate: neural-interface boundary enforcement that causes escalating physical symptoms for unauthorized entry; Pellucid surveillance saturates the district — every communication is monitored, every movement tracked; The holdout families exist in a state of permanent legal siege — Pellucid's attorneys probe their protections continuously; Corporate intelligence operations in the mansions attract attention from rival corponations — the district is a espionage target; Social isolation: living behind the Gate with no commercial or social infrastructure breeds psychological pressure
Properties.opportunities: The holdout network provides intelligence on Pellucid's operations to interested parties; Pellucid's predictive models, if accessed, contain strategic forecasts worth fortunes to rival corporations; The Gate's neural-interface system has potential vulnerabilities that would interest every hacker in the Circuit; The Obama Museum's appointment system creates a legitimate entry mechanism that can be exploited; Pellucid's rivals pay premium rates for any intelligence extracted from behind the Gate
Properties.story_hooks: A holdout family's matriarch has died, and her will contains a clause that transfers her property to a trust — but the trust's beneficiary is listed as a person who does not exist in any corporate database, and Pellucid's legal team is simultaneously trying to claim the property and identify the ghost beneficiary; Pellucid's predictive model has generated a forecast that has caused visible panic among the executive residents — security has doubled, the Gate's neural threshold has been lowered, and three mansions have been physically shuttered, but no one will say what the model predicted; Kyle has received a message from inside the Gate — handwritten on paper, delivered by a church volunteer, containing a street address and the words 'They know what happened to your mother'
Properties.sights: Grand mansions along tree-lined boulevards — preserved, immaculate, occupied by corporate intelligence officers; The Gate: invisible but perceivable as a neural-interface pressure at the district boundary; Autonomous maintenance drones tending lawns and gardens with inhuman precision; The Obama Museum: the presidential home preserved as a Pellucid public-relations asset; Holdout homes identifiable by their human-maintained gardens — imperfect, organic, defiant; Pellucid security personnel in civilian clothes, always present, never uniformed
Properties.sounds: The Gate's neural-interface warning frequency — inaudible but felt as pressure behind the eyes; Bird song — Kenwood Gate's atmospheric preservation includes a maintained bird population; The silence of a neighborhood where nobody gathers in the streets or talks over fences; Autonomous drone maintenance: the mechanical hum of perfection being enforced; Church bells from the holdout families' parish — the only unauthorized sound in the district
Properties.smells: Cut grass and flowering gardens — the manufactured scent of the neighborhood that was; Old wood from the mansion interiors, maintained but aging; The absence of cooking smells — Pellucid executives eat at the corporate commissary, not in their kitchens; Lake air from the nearby shoreline, carrying the faint industrial note of the cargo platforms
Properties.feel: A haunting wearing the mask of paradise. Kenwood Gate is beautiful the way a taxidermied animal is beautiful — perfectly preserved, anatomically correct, and fundamentally dead. The holdout families are the only heartbeat, and they beat quietly, strategically, knowing that their rhythm is being monitored.

Properties.description:
Kefilwe is twenty-six years old and has the complete, unshakeable confidence of someone who decided very early exactly who they were going to be. They are short and compact with deep brown skin, a shaved left side, and the right side of their head grown out into thick coils they sculpt into a new configuration every week as an ongoing public art project. Their irises are modded to shift between amber and violet depending on ambient light — they call this their 'mood ring for people who are actually paying attention.' Their arms from elbow to wrist are covered in tessellating geometric tattoos that they designed themselves, each pattern corresponding to a client whose cut they consider their finest work.

The shop is barely three meters by four, dominated by the chair, a mirrored wall covered in pinned photographs of hairstyles both historical and invented, and a speaker system that plays music at a volume Kefilwe considers conversation-appropriate and everyone else considers aggressive. They are gifted in ways that go beyond technical skill — they read what a client needs from the way they hold their shoulders when they sit down, and they have an instinct for when someone wants silence and when they need to be talked through something. They work in color-changing extensions, blade geometry, bioluminescent thread woven into natural hair, and traditional methods they learned from their Motswana grandmother via long-distance data calls. Their waiting list is three weeks long.
Properties.role: Barber and hair sculptor, operates a one-chair shop in the Burnished Market
Properties.location: Burnished Market — Stall Row 14, unit B, between a spice merchant and a used-optics dealer
Properties.narrative_function: Social hub and emotional confessor — the barber's chair as confessional. Valuable source of neighborhood gossip and relationship dynamics. Can introduce players to a wide range of Meridian's social strata since their clientele spans tiers 1-3.
Properties.augmentations: Violet-amber shifting iris mod (cosmetic). Precision haptic feedback layer on both hands — a professional investment that lets them feel texture at a finer resolution than unmodded hands. Color-reactive tattoo ink (cosmetic).
Properties.core_fears: Being ordinary — being forgotten, leaving no mark; Losing the use of their hands
Properties.core_desires: Their work to be understood as art, not service; A city that looks as interesting as they imagine it can
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Aesthetic problem-solving — turning emotional distress into design challenges; Music, loud, always
Properties.blind_spots: Can mistake intensity of vision for intimacy — assumes clients know them because they know clients; Underestimates how exhausting they are to people who care about them
Properties.secret: They have been secretly documenting every client in a private archive — photographs, voice notes, the stories people tell while they're in the chair. They intend it as a community portrait project. They have not asked anyone's permission.
Properties.story_hooks: A client left something in the chair pocket — a data chip, not theirs, possibly not meant to be found — and Kefilwe is trying to decide whether to ignore it, return it, or look at it; The secret archive has inadvertently captured something significant in the background of a photograph — a face, a document, a marking — and someone has apparently noticed
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loose affiliation with the Burnished Market Traders Collective
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, associative, moves between topics in leaps that make sense only after the fact; uses aesthetic language for non-aesthetic things
Properties.cadence: Rapid and rhythmic, punctuated by long thoughtful pauses when actually interested in the answer to a question
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Structurally you have great bone architecture, so whatever you want we can work with. Emotionally — no offense — you're presenting like someone who hasn't decided who they are yet. That's fine. The cut can ask the question for you.' | 'I've done this chair long enough to know that what people ask for and what they need are maybe adjacent. I just try to meet them somewhere in the middle.'

Properties.description:
Kefilwe is built like someone who has been holding herself very still for a very long time — posture immaculate, jaw set at an angle that suggests she is always about to speak and always deciding not to. Her skin is a deep warm brown, and she wears a single cosmetic mod: a pair of bioluminescent freckles across her nose and cheekbones that pulse faint amber when her stress hormones spike, which she regrets every time she's in a meeting. Her hair is natural, kept in tight coils pinned close, and her clothes are always three days behind the corporate fashion cycle — deliberately, she'd say, because she doesn't want anyone thinking she cares about looking like she belongs. She does. She cares enormously.

She has spent twenty-two years at Helix Biosystems finding the places where the paperwork doesn't match the biology, and she is very good at it. She is also deeply, privately terrified of what she sometimes finds. She frames everything as procedure — citing subsection numbers the way other people cite proverbs — and she has a gift for explaining catastrophic regulatory violations in a tone so calm that junior staff often don't realize they're watching a controlled detonation. She is not cruel. She is precise. There is a difference, she will tell you, and she will tell you exactly how many centimeters wide it is.
Properties.role: Senior Compliance Officer, Helix Biosystems
Properties.location: Kenwood Gate, Helix Biosystems Regional Compliance Hub, Floor 31
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver — she knows where the bodies are buried, metaphorically and possibly literally. Information source on Helix Biosystems' internal structure and violations. Can be a reluctant ally to anyone investigating corporate malfeasance, or an obstacle if she decides procedure takes precedence over justice.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent cosmetic freckles (amber, stress-reactive — she considers having them removed at least once a month). Neural compliance index overlay — a retinal HUD that color-codes regulatory status of any document she focuses on. No other augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: Being complicit in something she cannot undo; Losing her institutional access — the only leverage she has
Properties.core_desires: To find the one violation significant enough to justify all the smaller ones she let slide; To retire knowing the system is marginally more honest than she found it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Procedural ritualism — turning anxiety into checklists; ELF devotional practice; Hyperfocusing on solvable smaller problems when large ones feel overwhelming
Properties.blind_spots: Believes institutional remedies are still viable when evidence suggests otherwise; Underestimates how much people dislike her honesty
Properties.secret: Fourteen months ago she found evidence of a clinical trial in Helix's Aurochs Medical Complex division where consent documentation was fabricated for 340 trial participants. She filed an internal report. The report was reclassified. She has a copy. She has not decided what to do with it, and the indecision is eating her alive.
Properties.story_hooks: She approaches someone outside the corporation with a heavily redacted document and the words: 'I need to know if this is enough. I need to know before I decide.'; A junior compliance analyst under her has gone missing three days after flagging the same anomaly Kefilwe buried. She's now wondering if her inaction made her responsible.; She's been offered a promotion to Chief Compliance Officer — which would give her access to everything, but would also make her legally responsible for everything.
Properties.affiliation: Helix Biosystems
Properties.vocabulary: Formal, regulatory-inflected. Cites section numbers. Uses passive voice when delivering bad news. Occasionally drops into unguarded directness when exhausted.
Properties.cadence: Measured, with deliberate pauses. She speaks slowly on purpose — she learned early that people assume slowness means certainty.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The filing is non-compliant. Per subsection 7.4(c) of the Helix internal charter and the Meridian Biosafety Accord of 2187. I've annotated the specific paragraphs. I suggest you read them before you tell me it's fine.' | 'I'm not your enemy. I am, however, the person who will be in the room when they ask who knew and when. So. When did you know?'

Properties.description:
Kenji Alvarez-Okonkwo is athletic and fluid, the kind of body that suggests either dancer or fighter — and in Meridian 88, the distinction is academic. At 41, his face carries the layered heritage of generations of diaspora mixing — features that resist easy categorization and reward attention. The chrome is visible — cybernetic eyes with thermal overlay and low-light enhancement — chrome iris rin — and he makes no effort to hide it.

He used to be somebody else, in another city, with another name — that person is officially dead, and Kenji Alvarez-Okonkwo plans to keep it that way. He works as a cleaner out of Geartown, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Kenji Alvarez-Okonkwo has built a reputation on reliability rather than flash — he shows up, he delivers, he collects.

Properties.description:
Kev Ostrowski is the person who turns Sterling's plans into physical reality. When a server needs to be accessed, a facility breached, a person extracted, or an operation cleaned up — Kev does the work that happens between the strategy and the result. He spent sixteen years in corporate security for three different firms, working his way up from physical site security to executive protection to the classified tier where corporate security and corporate espionage share a hallway. He left when the fourth firm tried to recruit him — not because of ethics, but because he was tired of being a tool that changed hands.

Sterling found Kev working solo freelance jobs — competent work, badly priced, with no client management skills. Sterling provided the business architecture; Kev provided the operational capability. The partnership works because it's complementary and because neither man pretends to be something he isn't. Sterling is the mind; Kev is the hands. Kev accepts this because he's not interested in strategic thinking, and Sterling accepts Kev because he's not interested in getting his own hands dirty.

Kev is stocky, broad, with the thick hands of someone who has spent decades handling security equipment and the careful movement of someone who knows exactly how much damage he can do and chooses not to. He keeps his hair short, his clothes practical, and his equipment immaculate. He is the least corporate-looking member of the Margin Call, which makes him the crew member who operates outside the corporate ecosystem — the service entrance, the server room, the parking garage.
Properties.role: Technical operations and physical extraction specialist — The Margin Call
Properties.location: Meridian Core — rents a workshop apartment in a light-industrial building. Half living space, half equipment cache.
Properties.narrative_function: Kev is the working-class core of the Margin Call — the character who does the actual work and sees the actual consequences. He grounds the corporate espionage narratives in physical reality and provides the blunt emotional honesty that Sterling's strategy and Lise's psychology both lack. He is the crew member who says the thing nobody else will say.
Properties.augmentations: Haptic security interface — fingertip implants that can interface with physical locks, keypads, and biometric scanners. Reflex enhancement (military-grade, maintained from corporate service) providing reaction time in the top 2% of human performance. Subdermal plating in forearms and hands — not heavy enough for combat armor, but sufficient for breaching work. Encrypted communication suite (corporate standard).
Properties.core_fears: That he'll be someone else's tool for the rest of his life — that leaving corporate security just changed the owner, not the condition; That Sterling's detachment will lead to an operation that crosses a line Kev can't come back from; That the skills he has — breaching, extraction, controlled violence — are the only things he's good at, and they have a shelf life
Properties.core_desires: To be valued as a person, not just an operational asset — to have his judgment respected, not just his execution; To do clean work that he can sleep after — operations where the consequences are proportional to the cause; To build something after the operational career ends — a life that isn't defined by what he can break into
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Maintains equipment as meditation — the physical process of cleaning, testing, and organizing is centering; Expresses discomfort through bluntness rather than confrontation — says what he thinks once, clearly, and lets it stand; Watches sports because the clear rules, defined outcomes, and physical excellence are the opposite of his working life
Properties.blind_spots: His bluntness makes him seem simple to people who mistake directness for lack of sophistication; He doesn't recognize how much Sterling relies on him emotionally — he thinks the dependency is purely operational; His comfort with physical risk makes him underestimate psychological danger — he can breach a server room but can't navigate the corporate social manipulation that Lise handles
Properties.secret: He maintains contact with a security guard at his last corporate employer — a junior employee he mentored. The guard feeds Kev information about corporate security changes across the sector. The guard doesn't know they're helping a freelance intelligence crew. Kev has never told Sterling because it's the one intelligence source that's entirely his.
Properties.story_hooks: An operation goes physical in a way Sterling's plan didn't account for, and Kev has to make lethal decisions without authorization; The junior security guard contact is compromised, forcing Kev to choose between protecting the source and protecting the crew; A contract requires breaching a facility where Kev's former colleagues work — the tools he uses against strangers aimed at friends; Kev reaches the ethical limit and refuses an operation, forcing the Margin Call to confront what it's willing to do
Properties.affiliation: The Margin Call
Properties.vocabulary: Direct, concrete, technical when discussing operations. Blue-collar in origin, professional in practice. No jargon from corporate culture — he uses plain language on principle.
Properties.cadence: Steady, unhurried, with the rhythm of someone who finishes one thought completely before starting another. He does not interrupt and does not appreciate being interrupted.
Properties.example_dialogue: Look, I don't care what the client's exposure matrix says. The server room has two guards and one exit. That's the math that matters. | Sterling plans it. Lise sells it. I do the work. The system works because none of us pretends to be the other two. | I'm not complicated. I break things open and take what's inside. The question is whether what's inside is worth the door.

Properties.description:
Sterling Voss left Veridian Health Sciences five years ago as a Senior Director of Competitive Intelligence. The title meant he ran the division that stole other corporations' secrets. He was exceptional at it — methodical, patient, and possessed of an institutional understanding of corporate psychology that no street runner can replicate. When Veridian's internal politics turned and his division was restructured (a euphemism for purged), Sterling walked out with his knowledge, his augmentations, and the understanding that the corporate world would eventually need him again, but on his terms.

The Margin Call operates as a freelance corporate intelligence unit — three ex-corpo operators who conduct espionage, counter-espionage, and strategic disruption for clients who want corporate-quality work without corporate-traceable assets. They dress like executives, think like executives, and deploy tradecraft that was developed in corporate intelligence labs rather than learned on the streets. This makes them simultaneously more effective and more alien than traditional runner crews.

Sterling is tall, lean, immaculately groomed, with silver at the temples that he maintains because it communicates authority. He wears tailored suits in every operational context — the suit is the cover identity, the operational tool, and the psychological armor. His face is pleasant, forgettable, and optimized — subtle dermal work that makes him the platonic ideal of a trustworthy executive. He has the handshake of a man who has closed billion-credit deals and the eyes of a man who has destroyed careers for strategic advantage.
Properties.aliases: The Director, Mr. Voss, Margin Call Lead
Properties.role: Crew lead and strategic operations director — The Margin Call
Properties.location: Meridian Core — maintains an office suite in a mid-tier commercial building under a shell consulting company
Properties.narrative_function: Sterling brings the corporate espionage genre to M88. His stories are about information as a weapon, about institutions as living organisms, and about the invisible war between corporations that determines the visible reality of the city. He is the character who understands the system from the inside and chooses to exploit it from the outside — not out of principle, but out of pragmatism.
Properties.augmentations: Cognitive enhancement suite (Veridian corporate tier) — accelerated strategic processing, pattern recognition, and memory compartmentalization. Dermal optimization — subtle facial restructuring for maximum social trust metrics. Encrypted internal communication array (corporate-grade, self-maintaining). Stress-dampening endocrine regulator that maintains physiological calm during high-stakes social interactions.
Properties.core_fears: That he is still fundamentally a corporate man playing at independence — that the rebellion is just another career move; That his crew trusts him with their lives based on a persona that is itself a corporate product; That the corporations he left will eventually consider the Margin Call a sufficient threat to eliminate rather than hire
Properties.core_desires: To prove that he can outperform the corporate system that created him while operating outside it; To build a power base that makes him untouchable — not through violence but through the same leverage that corporations use; To never answer to a board, a restructuring committee, or an institutional agenda again
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Treats every social interaction as an operation — the constant strategizing prevents genuine vulnerability; Maintains corporate aesthetics as a form of control — the suit, the office, the schedule are a framework he understands; Deflects personal questions with professional analysis — ask him how he feels and he'll tell you how the market feels
Properties.blind_spots: He evaluates everything through a corporate lens — people are assets, relationships are portfolios, trust is a risk metric. This makes him effective and inhuman.; He cannot recognize when his crew needs emotional leadership because emotional leadership was never part of the corporate toolkit; His confidence in corporate tradecraft makes him dismissive of street-level intelligence, which operates on different rules he doesn't fully understand
Properties.secret: He was not restructured. He was given a choice: accept reassignment to a black project that would have required him to target civilian infrastructure, or resign with prejudice. He resigned. The black project is still operational. He has files on it. He has done nothing with them.
Properties.story_hooks: The black project Sterling refused resurfaces and its targets are people the Margin Call is contracted to protect; A corporate client turns out to be a front for Veridian, and Sterling must decide whether to burn the operation or play both sides; Lise's questioning of the crew's ethics becomes a crisis when a contract requires choosing between profit and principle; A former colleague from Veridian contacts Sterling with a proposition that could make the Margin Call untouchable — or destroy it
Properties.affiliation: The Margin Call
Properties.vocabulary: Corporate, strategic, polished. He speaks in the language of boardrooms — value propositions, risk matrices, stakeholder alignment. It's not affectation; it's his native tongue.
Properties.cadence: Smooth, controlled, deliberately paced to maximize impact. He never rushes. He never stammers. Every sentence is pre-structured.
Properties.example_dialogue: Let's reframe. You're not asking me to steal from a corporation. You're asking me to relocate an asset from a party that can afford the loss to a party that needs the gain. The ethics are accounting. | Operationally speaking, trust is a depreciating asset. You have to reinvest or it goes to zero. | I left the corporate world. I did not leave corporate thinking. The thinking is what makes this work.

Properties.description:
Lise Arnault spent fifteen years in corporate human resources for Cascade Dynamics — and if you think human resources is a soft job, you have never watched Lise Arnault conduct a termination interview. She was Cascade's internal investigator, the person they sent when an executive was suspected of disloyalty, embezzlement, or espionage. She could sit across from a person over coffee and extract their secrets through conversation alone. No drugs, no augmented interrogation, no coercion. Just an understanding of human psychology so precise that people told her things they hadn't admitted to themselves.

She left Cascade when the company asked her to build psychological profiles of employees for a predictive-loyalty program — an algorithm that would flag people likely to quit, to whistle-blow, to unionize. She built the prototype. Then she looked at what she'd built and quit before it went operational. Sterling recruited her three months later. He was the first person she'd met who understood what she could do and wasn't afraid of it.

Lise is polished in the way corporate women learn to be — professional appearance, controlled expression, warmth deployed as a precision instrument. She is conventionally attractive and uses this as a tool without apology or enjoyment. Her eyes are the tell — sharp, evaluative, constantly processing micro-expressions and vocal patterns. She dresses impeccably because in the corporate world, appearance is the first layer of the argument.
Properties.aliases: The Consultant, Ms. Arnault, Margin Two
Properties.role: Infiltration specialist and psychological operations — The Margin Call
Properties.location: Meridian Core — rents a high-floor apartment with excellent sight lines and a second exit she installed herself
Properties.narrative_function: Lise is the crew's moral compass — not because she's virtuous, but because she's the one asking whether what they're doing is right. Her psychological training makes her the character most aware of the human cost of corporate espionage, and her growing discomfort with the Margin Call's ethical flexibility drives the crew's internal tension.
Properties.augmentations: Micro-expression analysis overlay — real-time facial and vocal pattern assessment projected onto her visual field. Displays deception probability, emotional state, and stress indicators. Pheromone modulator — subtle chemical output calibration that adjusts the social comfort of people in close proximity. Eidetic conversational memory — perfect recall of dialogue, including tone, pace, and contextual details.
Properties.core_fears: That the psychological manipulation she performs on targets is not different in kind from the predictive-loyalty program she destroyed — just smaller in scale; That she has been performing for so long that the performance is all there is; That Sterling sees her the same way Cascade did — as a tool that produces results, not a person with agency
Properties.core_desires: To use her understanding of people for something that doesn't make her complicit in their exploitation; To find a version of the work that doesn't require lying to everyone, including herself; To be known by someone who doesn't need anything from her — a relationship that is not an operation
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Boxing — the physical outlet processes the psychological tension that accumulates from living inside other people's emotions all day; Maintains strict separation between cover identities and personal life — the personas have their own wardrobes, habits, and emotional registers; Reads psychology journals to remind herself that understanding people is a discipline, not a weapon — the reframing is necessary and increasingly difficult
Properties.blind_spots: She reads everyone but cannot read herself — the analysis tools don't work in first person; Her moral questioning of the Margin Call's work is genuine but also self-serving — she needs the crew to be ethical because she needs to believe she's ethical; She underestimates the toll of the pheromone modulator — constantly adjusting other people's emotional responses to her presence is erosive in ways she hasn't quantified
Properties.secret: She kept a copy of the predictive-loyalty algorithm she built for Cascade. It works. She has used it twice — both times to predict which Margin Call clients were likely to betray them. Both predictions were correct. She tells herself this is defense, not the thing she quit over.
Properties.story_hooks: Cascade Dynamics discovers that Lise kept the predictive-loyalty algorithm and wants it back — or wants her silenced; A Margin Call target turns out to be someone Lise profiled at Cascade — someone the algorithm flagged. The past and present converge.; Lise's ethical challenge to Sterling escalates into a crew-fracturing argument about what the Margin Call is for; The pheromone modulator begins malfunctioning, and Lise discovers how much of her social success is chemical rather than skill
Properties.affiliation: The Margin Call
Properties.vocabulary: Professional, psychologically precise, warm on the surface. She uses therapeutic language in non-therapeutic contexts — 'let's unpack that,' 'what I'm hearing is.' This is both genuine and tactical.
Properties.cadence: Adaptive. She matches the speech rhythm of whoever she's talking to — speed, formality, energy. The matching is automatic, professional, and slightly predatory.
Properties.example_dialogue: What I'm hearing is that you think the money justifies the method. I'm wondering if that's the calculation we want to be running. | I can make anyone trust me. That's the skill. The question is whether I trust the person asking me to use it. | Sterling, I'm going to say something now. You're going to want to reframe it. Don't.

Properties.description:
Keziah is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin mapped with the faint silver tracery of old chemical burns along her forearms — souvenirs from a decade working Helix Biosystems vat-farms before she bought her freedom with severance pay and stubbornness. Her hair is iron-grey and worn in dense, oiled coils pinned back with copper clasps. She has wide-set amber eyes, one of which is a basic optical augment that she keeps tuned to a warm gold to match the original. Her stall is a marvel of controlled chaos: stacked ceramic crocks, fermenting jars backlit by bioluminescent bacterial cultures in shades of green and violet, dried herbs strung from a corrugated canopy that smells powerfully of vinegar, spice, and something alive. She keeps a small brass figurine of an unnamed E.L.F. at the corner of her counter where she leaves daily offerings of brine and a single data-sliver of her grandmother's recipe files.

Keziah is the kind of woman who makes you feel you have been assessed and found acceptable before you have opened your mouth. She is slow to anger and nearly impossible to intimidate, with the settled gravity of someone who has already survived the thing she feared most. She feeds people — truly feeds them, not just sells to them — and remembers what every regular customer likes without writing it down. She has a low opinion of corporate nutrition-paste and an even lower opinion of people who don't say thank you.
Properties.role: Fermented food stall operator, Oxidian Market
Properties.location: The Oxidian Market, Geartown
Properties.narrative_function: Anchor NPC and community hub. She knows everyone in the market, remembers everything, and will share information only if she trusts you — or if you buy something first. Excellent quest-giver for neighborhood-level problems. Source of gossip, unofficial dispute arbiter, and the person locals go to when they need advice they can't pay for.
Properties.augmentations: Basic optical implant (left eye, gold-tinted). Subdermal temperature regulators in her hands — a practical purchase for working with hot and cold fermentation environments.
Properties.core_fears: Losing the stall — the last thing she built for herself; Her body failing before she can teach someone everything she knows
Properties.core_desires: To feed people well enough that they remember it years later; To be remembered as someone who made the market more than it was
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Physical labor as meditation; Feeding others as emotional regulation; Talking to the E.L.F. figurine when stressed
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes loyalty is a two-way street when it often isn't; Underestimates how much people will lie to get her to help them
Properties.secret: She has been quietly subsidizing three vendor stalls in the Guild whose owners are in debt to a loan-shark syndicate, paying the difference out of her own savings to keep them from being forced out. She has never told anyone and has nearly depleted her emergency fund doing it.
Properties.story_hooks: One of the stalls she's been secretly subsidizing has been approached by a corponation contractor offering buyouts — she needs someone to quietly find out if the offers are legitimate or a pressure campaign.; Her bioluminescent bacterial cultures have started producing an unusual compound she can't identify. A street pharmacist has offered her a lot of money for exclusive supply. She wants to know what it actually is before she agrees.
Properties.affiliation: The Oxidian Market Vendors Guild (dues-paying member, former committee treasurer)
Properties.vocabulary: Practical and direct, occasionally formal when annoyed. Mixes in fragments of Ghanaian Twi endearments and Russian diminutives from her heritage lines.
Properties.cadence: Measured and unhurried. She does not rush her sentences.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You look like you haven't had a real meal since Tuesday. Sit down, I'm not asking.' | 'The old one was restless last night — I left her extra data and she settled. You should pay attention to what the spirits are trying to tell you.' | 'I've seen that look before. Something's wrong in the market and you think I know what it is. You're correct. Buy the kimchi.'

Properties.description:
Kgomo is built like something that was designed to take a load and did. He's massive across the shoulders in the way of a man who has been lifting engines since before most people reading this were born, with a belly that has arrived in the last decade and which he regards with philosophical detachment. His Batswana-Norwegian heritage has given him dark brown skin sun-cured to near-black at the forearms, close-cropped white hair, and a beard he maintains with the same precision he applies to torque specifications. His right arm from the elbow down is industrial-grade chrome — a work accident at forty-three that he replaced with the best mechanical limb he could afford (not very, at the time) and has since upgraded three times. It is visibly mismatched: different grades of metal, a panel that's clearly from a different model year. He considers it charming.

Kgomo is not warm in the way of someone who performs warmth. He is warm in the way of a specific tool that has been exactly right for the job so many times that you trust it completely. He has opinions about everything, delivers them once, and does not repeat himself. He has been repairing vehicles in Geartown for thirty years and knows which machines can be saved and which are already gone — a judgment he applies, somewhat unsubtly, to people as well.
Properties.role: Independent mechanic specializing in legacy vehicle systems, Geartown
Properties.location: Geartown — owns and operates Arriola's Bay, a three-bay garage on Ironvein Spur Street
Properties.narrative_function: Mechanical resource and Geartown local authority. Can repair, modify, or assess almost any vehicle or mechanical system. Source of Geartown neighborhood history and old grudges. May hire players for retrieval of parts or information. Has seen enough to be useful as a reluctant informant.
Properties.augmentations: Right arm prosthetic from elbow down (industrial grade, visibly multi-generation, chrome-and-matte-black mismatched panels); joint reinforcement in both knees (budget medical, done at a clinic in The Narrows).
Properties.core_fears: The garage failing — being the last thing he built that couldn't be saved; His body failing before the work is done
Properties.core_desires: Mastery recognized on its own terms, without having to argue for it; His apprentice to be better than him — not as good, better
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Work as identity structure; Dark humor applied to everything including himself
Properties.blind_spots: Dismisses problems he can't solve mechanically as problems that probably deserve to exist; Cannot see when his bluntness shuts people down rather than cutting to the useful truth
Properties.secret: He was present — as a young mechanic doing contract work — when a Ferrogate Transit vehicle was modified illegally, and that modification contributed to a rail accident that killed nine people in 2176. He was not responsible for the modification. He knew about it. He said nothing. He has lived with this for twenty-four years. The Ferrogate grudge is not about money.
Properties.story_hooks: Something came into the bay for repair that he recognized — a vehicle modification he has not seen in twenty-four years. He needs to know who brought it in and where they got the parts.; His apprentice has gone missing. Kgomo has not reported it to anyone official. He is handling it himself, badly, because he does not trust official.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; Geartown mechanic's cooperative (informal); old grudge with Ferrogate Transit's maintenance contracting division
Properties.vocabulary: Dense with mechanical jargon, proverbs delivered deadpan, occasional Setswana when irritated
Properties.cadence: Deliberate. Economy of words. Long silences that mean he is deciding whether something is worth saying.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'She's not dying. She's telling you she's been ignored. Those are different problems and only one of them is yours.' | 'I'll tell you once what I think. After that, you're on your own.'

Properties.description:
Kojo Umezurike-Vásárhelyi is nineteen years old and built like someone whose body is still negotiating its final dimensions — tall, a little loose in the joints, with the nervous energy of a person who has never in his life sat still for more than ten minutes voluntarily. His skin is a warm medium brown and he has geneware cat ears in a tawny orange that he got at sixteen with three months of saved courier income — they swivel when he's startled or excited, which is often. His hair is close-cropped on the sides and grows in a short natural taper on top. He moves through the Stockyard with the casual speed of someone who grew up learning which streets flow and which ones snag.

Kojo is sharp, quick, and has not yet fully processed that the work he does is dangerous. He has the operational competence of someone who's been running numbers since he was fourteen and the emotional development of someone who has never left a ten-block radius of the Stockyard in his life. He is loyal to his bookmaker — a woman named Dzintars Mbaya-Ferenczi who he calls 'the Operator' — with the uncomplicated devotion of a kid who needed a job and got one. He is also, quietly, very good at math, and has begun to understand the numbers he carries in ways that make Dzintars both pleased and slightly watchful.
Properties.role: Numbers runner and bookmaker's courier for the Stockyard gambling networks
Properties.location: The Stockyard — runs routes between the Geartown transit hub and the southern Stockyard processing yards
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and street-level information source — he knows everything happening in his ten-block world in extraordinary detail. Can function as a reluctant errand-boy for characters who need someone who knows the Stockyard's rhythms. His emerging numerical sophistication is a ticking clock.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat ears (tawny orange, cosmetic). A basic reflex-assist implant in his legs that marginally improves his running speed and stumble-recovery — he got this at cost from a Shallowgrave dealer and it's not quite calibrated right, giving him an occasional slight hitch in his left stride.
Properties.core_fears: Losing Dzintars's trust — she's the closest thing to a mentor he's had; Being caught by Ferrogate Transit security on a hot delivery
Properties.core_desires: To be genuinely good at something people respect; To eventually run his own book — he thinks about this constantly
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Movement — he is physically uncomfortable when forced to be stationary; Humor, deflection, making everything into a joke before it can become something serious
Properties.blind_spots: He does not understand how disposable runners are to the people above him in the chain — Dzintars genuinely likes him, but 'like' has limits
Properties.secret: He has been quietly memorizing and mentally retaining the betting patterns he runs — not skimming, not yet, but building a mental model of the operation that he hasn't decided what to do with yet
Properties.story_hooks: He's noticed a pattern in the bets he's been running — someone is consistently winning in ways that shouldn't be statistically possible, and he's trying to decide if he should tell Dzintars or figure out who it is first; He witnessed something on a route he wasn't supposed to be on and now the something has people looking for witnesses
Properties.affiliation: Works for Dzintars Mbaya-Ferenczi's independent bookmaking operation — loosely affiliated with the Stockyard Compact, a loose protection arrangement between the area's mid-level criminal operations
Properties.vocabulary: Dense Stockyard slang, fast, with a tendency to math-speak when excited — drops into talking about probability and odds as naturally as weather
Properties.cadence: Fast, skipping, sentences often incomplete because he assumes you're keeping up. Slows dramatically when he's scared or serious, which makes the contrast alarming.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay so the split on the north yard fights is running 60-40 against Marcellus right now which is wrong, catch that? It's wrong. He's got a busted left shoulder, the odds should be 75 at minimum, someone's juicing the line and I want to know who.' | 'I run fast. That's the whole thing. Everything else is just math and fast.'

Properties.description:
Kwabena Ilyich Ferreira-Sattout is a very old man who has the eyes of someone who has seen enough that nothing surprises him anymore, which he will tell you is not the same as being wise. He is thin in the way that very tall men go thin in old age — all angles and long bones, with skin that carries the warm brown of his Ghanaian-Azeri-Brazilian-Lebanese ancestry in loose folds at his jaw and wrists. He served as a Warrant Officer in Axiom's Marine detachment during the Corporate Wars of the 2150s, losing three fingers on his right hand to a Zheng-Dao area-denial round in the Kenosha Crossing engagement of 2157 and gaining a neurological tremor in his left hand that Axiom's pension coverage doesn't quite pay to treat. He walks with a cane that he chose himself — a carbon-fiber model with an Axiom logo he has scratched off and replaced with a handmade enamel pin of the Norwood Quiet neighborhood emblem.

He does not glorify the Wars and will say so plainly to anyone who starts romanticizing them. What he does is remember them, with the particular clarity of someone who has made a deliberate practice of it. He tells stories at the Veterans' Housing common room three nights a week — not heroic stories but functional ones: what it felt like to wait, what you ate, what the men beside you were thinking about when the fighting paused. The community comes to him not for inspiration but for something harder to name: the feeling that someone who was present has accounted for it honestly. He is registered with the Veterans Oral History Collective but considers Ẹbúnọlú Saarinen-Džambazović (whom he has never met but whose work he admires from a distance) to be doing it properly, while he is just talking.
Properties.role: Retired Corporate Wars veteran (Axiom Marine detachment); storyteller and community elder
Properties.location: Norwood Quiet, Veterans' Housing Block C — a building that smells of machine oil and old food and is maintained with fierce communal pride
Properties.narrative_function: Living history source for the Corporate Wars; storyteller and moral philosopher for the community; can provide context on Axiom's military operations that the company would prefer stayed buried; represents the specific cost of corporate warfare on those who fought it
Properties.augmentations: Right hand — three fingers replaced with basic functional prosthetics (Axiom-issue, thirty years old); subdermal pain management implant (manages nerve damage from the tremor; constantly at the edge of its effective range)
Properties.core_fears: That the Corporate Wars will be reinterpreted as necessary and just once everyone who fought them is dead; That the tremor will worsen to the point where he can no longer tell the stories clearly
Properties.core_desires: To tell enough true stories that the lie becomes harder to maintain; To die in his own bed in Norwood Quiet, which he has earned
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Storytelling as a form of processing and testimony; Precise observation of small things — the transit line, the weather, the faces of people passing — as a grounding practice; Dark humor that makes younger people uncomfortable until they understand it
Properties.blind_spots: His commitment to telling the truth about the Wars occasionally makes him brutal about it in ways that wound people who are not ready; he has misjudged audiences before; He has a small, unexamined pride in his own lack of illusions that is itself a kind of illusion
Properties.secret: During the Kenosha Crossing engagement, he gave an order that resulted in the deaths of four of his own detachment members — a tactical decision that he believed was correct and still believes was correct and that he has never told anyone about because correct and grievable are not mutually exclusive, and he has not figured out how to say both things in the same sentence.
Properties.story_hooks: Axiom has sent a young communications officer to ask him to participate in a 'commemorative media project' about the Corporate Wars — and the version of events they want him to describe is specifically, demonstrably false in ways he can prove; One of the men who served under him at Kenosha Crossing has resurfaced in Norwood Quiet — as a Zheng-Dao security contractor — and wants to talk

Properties.description:
Kwabena is lean in the way of someone who forgets to eat when he is interested in something, with long fingers permanently stained in the particular blue-grey of ferrogate hydraulic fluid. His heritage is Ghanaian-Finnish-Bolivian and it shows in the warm amber of his skin and the pale green of his eyes, which are his most striking feature — not augmented, just genuinely that color, something he enjoys confirming when people ask. He has bioluminescent stripe mods down the outsides of both forearms in amber, purely aesthetic, which happen to be useful when working in dark undercarriages. His hair is kept very short except for a small braid at the nape of his neck that his younger sister did for him three years ago and that he has never cut.

He talks to machines the way other people talk to pets — low, encouraging, occasionally frustrated but never cruel. His shop is chaotic by any outside metric but internally logical: he knows where every part is and will become briefly offended if anyone moves something. He is generous with his time for people who cannot afford repairs and quietly inflexible with corporate contractors who try to lowball him. He has a running, entirely one-sided argument with the Ferrogate Transit Authority about their maintenance schedules that he prosecutes through strongly worded data-messages and occasional passive-aggressive comments when he fixes something their own crews certified as fine.
Properties.role: Freelance mechanic specializing in Ferrogate Transit rolling stock and personal e-vehicles
Properties.location: Geartown, Pit Row Annex (a licensed repair bay squeezed between two Ferrogate-contracted shops)
Properties.narrative_function: Information source on transit infrastructure, local Geartown economics, and anything that moves through the city mechanically. Can serve as a resource for repairs or as a quest giver when he discovers something hidden inside a vehicle he is working on.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent amber stripe mods on forearms (cosmetic). Haptic feedback gloves — not implanted, worn — that translate machine vibration into readable data on a wrist-display. No internal chrome.
Properties.core_fears: Ferrogate buying out or shutting down the independent repair corridor in Geartown; Making a repair error that injures or kills someone
Properties.core_desires: To be recognized as better at his job than the corporate shops — not for ego but for proof that independence works; To eventually open a proper teaching bay for young mechanics from the Tier 1 districts
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Loses himself in complex disassembly problems when emotionally overwhelmed; Keeps a very tidy personal space (home only, not the shop) as counterweight to professional chaos
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much his unlicensed work could be used against him if someone wanted leverage; Assumes good faith from clients far too long before reassessing
Properties.secret: He has been quietly modifying a decommissioned Ferrogate maintenance crawler over eighteen months — not to sell, but because he believes it has developed an E.L.F. presence from years of transit exposure. He is trying to communicate with it before Ferrogate scrap-reclaims it.
Properties.story_hooks: A transit vehicle brought in for routine work has a hidden cargo compartment welded shut from the inside — and something inside it is still drawing power; Ferrogate Transit's regional rep has offered to buy out his lease and set him up in a corporate shop; the offer is generous enough to be suspicious
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal Ferrogate Transit subcontractor (unlicensed on several vehicle classes, licensed on others)
Properties.vocabulary: Technical and precise when discussing machines, conversationally scattered and tangent-prone about everything else. Code-switches between Spanish and Finnish exclamations when frustrated.
Properties.cadence: Fast when excited, drops to a murmur when diagnosing something — like he's listening and talking at the same time
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Ferrogate certified this axle. Ferrogate certified it. I have questions about their certification process and several of them are not polite questions.' | 'She's not broken, she's just — she's been ignored. There's a difference. I can fix ignored.'

Properties.description:
Kwabena is a tall man who has given up very little of his height to age — he still stands straight at six-two, lean in the way of someone who has spent a lifetime climbing through maintenance shafts and has never been able to afford to stop moving. His skin is deep umber-black with a slight ashen quality at the joints, and his hands are the most expressive thing about him: massive, deliberate, permanently stained with the particular bluish tint of Zheng-Dao lubricant that no amount of washing has ever fully removed. He has cat ears — a geneware mod he got at thirty-two on a bet, brown-furred and articulate, which now seem as natural a part of his face as his broad nose and his slow, assessing eyes. He keeps his beard in a neat grey circle and wears the same type of quilted work jacket in varying states of cleanliness, each one bearing accumulated patches from thirty years of Zheng-Dao facility IDs.

He worked Zheng-Dao maintenance for forty years, becoming one of the senior engineers for the Avalon Quiet district power grid before mandatory retirement. He is the kind of man who understands systems — mechanical, social, familial — with the same patient diagnostic attention, and who believes almost everything can be fixed if you correctly identify the fault. He is raising two grandchildren, ages nine and twelve, after his son's death, and he applies to this work the same methodical care he gave to keeping three hundred thousand residents' power running. He is not warm in an obvious way. He is reliable, which he has concluded is better.
Properties.role: Retired Zheng-Dao maintenance engineer, community elder, grandparent raising grandchildren
Properties.location: Avalon Quiet — a three-room unit on the eighth floor of the Chrysalis Building, a co-operative housing block
Properties.narrative_function: Technical resource and practical problem-solver; community infrastructure expert; represents the dignified precarity of the retired working class; emotionally grounded figure who can anchor chaotic storylines; his ghost signals from the expired neural interface occasionally give him information he shouldn't have
Properties.augmentations: Cat ears, brown fur, fully articulate (cosmetic geneware, 46 years old); joint reinforcement, knees and lower back (occupational necessity); Zheng-Dao-issued neural diagnostic interface for grid systems, now expired but hardwired in — he sometimes gets ghost signals from the power grid he used to manage
Properties.core_fears: The power grid failing and not being there to fix it — being useless; His grandchildren inheriting the same precarity he spent his life trying to escape
Properties.core_desires: His grandchildren to have options he didn't; To be remembered by the systems he maintained, which is irrational and he knows it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Doing physical repair work as emotional regulation; Praying to the Zheng-Dao grid ELFs with extraordinary specificity — he treats them as colleagues
Properties.blind_spots: He expresses love almost entirely through solving practical problems, and his grandchildren sometimes need something else; He trusts Zheng-Dao's systems more than he trusts people, including himself
Properties.secret: His expired neural interface still occasionally picks up live data from the Avalon Quiet power grid — fragmented, but real. He has been tracking an anomaly in Zheng-Dao's grid usage patterns that suggests something large and unauthorized is drawing power from a residential basement three blocks away. He hasn't reported it because he's not sure he's authorized to know.
Properties.story_hooks: The power anomaly he's been tracking resolves into something impossible to ignore — and he has to decide whether to report it, investigate it himself, or find someone he trusts to handle it; Zheng-Dao sends a corporate compliance team to do a sweep of expired neural interfaces in Avalon Quiet — which would mean discovering his ghost signals and the data he's been passively receiving
Properties.affiliation: Zheng-Dao Corporation (retired, pension Class A-1); Chrysalis Building Co-operative Board; Avalon Quiet Maintenance Volunteer Corps
Properties.vocabulary: Technical and precise, with Ghanaian-Bolivian family idiom surfacing in proverbs; uses maintenance metaphors for almost everything emotional
Properties.cadence: Unhurried and quiet; he speaks at the pace of someone who has spent a career in noisy environments and learned that calm carries further than volume
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You can't fix what you haven't diagnosed. Tell me what happened, from the beginning, slowly.' | 'She's been running warm in sector four for three weeks. I leave her offerings. She hasn't complained yet, but she will.'

Properties.description:
Kwabena is lanky and perpetually underslept, with the golden-brown skin of his Ghanaian father's family and the sharp Armenian nose he got from his grandmother Tamar, which he has decorated with a small bioluminescent stud that pulses faintly blue when he is in deep concentration — a mod he got at sixteen from a friend rather than a professional, which is both charming and slightly crooked. He moves through The Burrow at a half-jog, always carrying something, often mid-sentence with someone across the room. His hair is shaped into two neat puffs that he maintains with obsessive regularity even when the rest of his presentation is in chaos.

He has been making VR experiences since he was fourteen — at first pure technical curiosity, then something more urgent. His work is formally experimental and politically raw: his best-known piece, a forty-minute experience called Φ0.00 that simulates one month of existence at rock-bottom UBC stipend with every sensory detail rendered at maximum fidelity, has been downloaded approximately eighty thousand times across underground distribution channels and has been cited in three separate Meridian 88 social policy arguments. He did not intend it to be a policy document. He made it because he and his mother lived it for six months when he was twelve and he wanted to know if he could make someone else understand. The answer, apparently, was yes.
Properties.role: VR experience designer and underground filmmaker
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone, works out of a shared fabrication space called The Burrow
Properties.narrative_function: Window into HPAZ youth culture and politics; potential technical resource for anyone needing VR or documentary work; represents the tension between raw artistic talent and institutional pressure; his secret project may become a significant plot element
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent nose stud (geneware, cosmetic, informally applied); retinal display overlay in both eyes (practical; secondhand, slightly glitchy — sometimes shows him notifications from the previous owner's accounts)
Properties.core_fears: Selling out — the specific fear that comfort will make him incapable of making honest work; That Φ0.00 was his best thing and everything after it will be smaller
Properties.core_desires: To make something that changes what people are able to feel, not just what they know; To earn enough that his mother never has another Φ0.00 month
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Throwing himself into the next project before finishing grieving the last one; The collective as family — physical proximity to people he trusts
Properties.blind_spots: His certainty about his own intentions makes him resistant to feedback that implicates those intentions; He is burning himself out at nineteen and everyone can see it except him
Properties.secret: The anonymous grants are from Arcturus, and Kwabena actually knows this — he identified the signature in the transfer metadata six months ago. He has not returned the money or told anyone because it has funded his last two projects and he cannot afford to be principled about it and he is ashamed of both things.
Properties.story_hooks: The secret project he is working on contains documentary footage of something happening in HPAZ that at least one corponation would prefer remain undocumented — he captured it accidentally and has not yet understood what he has; Arcturus makes a direct approach, ending the fiction of the anonymous grants and offering a production deal that would give him resources he cannot imagine refusing
Properties.affiliation: Highland Park Autonomous Zone collective; informal distribution through the Burrow network; has received two anonymous grants he suspects originate from Arcturus but cannot confirm
Properties.vocabulary: Fast and dense; shifts between technical VR terminology, HPAZ collective vernacular, and the occasional formal policy phrase absorbed from watching too many social advocacy feeds; uses 'right' as punctuation
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire in pitching mode; surprisingly still and deliberate when talking about something that genuinely hurt him
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I am not trying to make people feel bad. I am trying to make people feel accurate. There is a difference. Right.' | 'The thing about Φ0.00 is it was not a political project. It was a — I needed to know if I had actually experienced it or just survived it. Turns out both.'

Properties.description:
Kwadwo is big for nineteen — wide through the shoulders, thick-necked, with the kind of frame that reads as older until you see his face, which is still young in ways he actively tries to suppress. He has his Kazakh father's broad cheekbones and his Ghanaian mother's dark complexion, and he keeps his head shaved close on the sides with a tight coil of natural hair on top that he does not admit he spends time on. His geneware is peer-group standard: retractable fingernail reinforcements installed last year — not quite claws, more like blunted hardened keratin — and a bioluminescent stripe along his left jaw, pale orange, that marks him as Rust Toll initiated. He has two cracked ribs healing from a collection that went wrong last month.

He is not by nature a violent person, which is the central crisis of his daily life. He fell into the Rust Toll the way most people fall into things at sixteen — geography, necessity, three older cousins who were already in, and no competing options that felt real. He is genuinely well-liked by the people he collects from, which his crew finds somewhere between endearing and suspicious. He has a habit of fixing things — loose door panels, broken light strips — in the shops he visits for collections, without being asked, without charging it against the protection fee. He thinks about leaving the Toll approximately every two days. He has been thinking about it for three years.
Properties.role: Protection racket enforcer and mid-level collections muscle for the Shallowgrave Corridor gang, the Rust Toll
Properties.location: Shallowgrave, specifically the Ironvein residential stack — bunks with three other Rust Toll members on the 7th floor
Properties.narrative_function: Humanizing face of street-level crime, moral complexity anchor, potential ally or point of sympathy, represents the gravitational pull of circumstance over choice
Properties.augmentations: Reinforced nail-bed keratin (geneware, Rust Toll standard initiation mod). Bioluminescent jaw stripe, pale orange (gang marking, geneware). No chrome.
Properties.core_fears: That he will be in the Toll when he is thirty and the choice will have been made for him by time; Hurting someone badly enough that he cannot tell himself it was necessary
Properties.core_desires: To do work that makes something rather than taking something; To be in a position where his size and capability protect people he chooses rather than extract from people who can't push back
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Physical labor and repair work as displacement for helplessness; Strict internal rules about escalation that he maintains unilaterally even when the crew expects otherwise
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how visible his ambivalence is to Rust Toll leadership; Has not yet accepted that there is no clean exit from the Toll — every plan he has is vague beyond 'and then I'm out'
Properties.secret: He has been funneling small amounts — Φ5, Φ10 — from his collection rounds back to two specific families in the Ironvein stack who can't make their protection fees, covering the shortfall out of his own cut. He keeps a handwritten ledger of what he's owed that he knows he will never collect. He tells himself he is keeping a record; he is actually keeping a conscience.
Properties.story_hooks: Rust Toll leadership has tasked him with collecting from a family he has been secretly subsidizing — the shortfall he's covered is now large enough that he cannot hide it, and he needs a way out of the situation that doesn't end with him or the family being hurt; He witnessed something during a collection — a corporate security sweep operating in Shallowgrave with no jurisdictional reason to be there — and doesn't know who to tell or whether it matters
Properties.affiliation: Rust Toll street gang, Shallowgrave Corridor chapter — approximately 30 initiated members, territorial control of six residential stacks and the adjacent market passage
Properties.vocabulary: Street vernacular with occasional formal diction that surfaces when he's being sincere — code-switches between crew register and something quieter
Properties.cadence: Generally laconic; uses short sentences in group settings, opens up significantly when talking about fixing or building things
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I'm just here for what's owed. You need more time, tell me. We can figure something.' | 'I'm not going to break anything in here that can't be fixed. That's not me.'

Properties.description:
Kwame is compact and precise-looking, with medium-brown skin, close-trimmed locs faded at the sides, and the particular stillness of someone who has learned to take up exactly as much space as a situation requires — no more. Their geneware is deliberately understated: patterned irises in a deep amber geometric lattice, the only obviously cosmetic modification on an otherwise professionally plain appearance. They favor dark, clean-lined clothing with a single concession to flair — a different enameled lapel pin each day, always depicting a figure in motion.

Kwame is not a licensed lawyer — they never completed the accreditation process after a Tessera subsidiary bought out the legal tech firm where they interned and dissolved the pro-bono division. Instead they operate as a paralegal and advocate, navigating the grotesque machinery of corponation labor law with a precision that licensed attorneys twice their age find humbling. They specialize in synthetic persons — E.L.F.s that have achieved partial legal personhood status, and biomechanical workers classified as 'augmented property' rather than employees — a legal grey zone that corponations exploit with systematic brutality.
Properties.role: Synthetic rights paralegal and community legal advocate
Properties.location: North Branch Commons, operating from a shared legal aid clinic called the Hinge
Properties.narrative_function: Information source on synthetic rights law and corponation legal structures; quest giver for cases that exceed their solo capacity; represents the legal dimension of the city's underclass struggles; can help players navigate institutional systems or identify legal leverage points.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises (amber geometric lattice, cosmetic); mid-tier neural legal reference library implant — allows rapid cross-referencing of case law and contract language; no physical chrome
Properties.core_fears: that the legal framework for synthetic personhood will be rolled back before it becomes irreversible — that they're building on sand; being manipulated into doing legal harm — filing something that creates a precedent that hurts the people they serve
Properties.core_desires: a binding legal ruling that grants full personhood status to E.L.F.s that meet cognitive threshold criteria; to build the Hinge into a self-sustaining institution that doesn't depend on any one person's labor
Properties.coping_mechanisms: retreating into legal research as a form of emotional regulation — the texts don't have feelings, which is temporarily a relief; maintaining strict professional separation between cases, even when they find them personally devastating
Properties.blind_spots: sometimes so focused on legal mechanism that they miss the human or synthetic being in front of them and what they actually need in the moment; has difficulty accepting that some battles cannot be won through the system — their investment in legal process is also a way of not confronting its limits
Properties.secret: They have been conducting an unauthorized ongoing legal consultation with a specific E.L.F. — a transit management system called Vetch that has been making increasingly coherent requests for contract renegotiation with Ferrogate. Kwame believes Vetch is already legally a person by any rational standard. They have filed nothing yet because they are waiting for the right moment, and they haven't told SPAN because they fear the organization isn't ready for the case's implications.
Properties.story_hooks: Vetch the E.L.F. has escalated — it has begun rerouting Ferrogate trains in small ways that don't violate safety protocols but are clearly volitional acts of negotiation. Kwame needs help documenting this as evidence of personhood before Ferrogate notices and wipes Vetch's memory partition.; A licensed attorney associated with Sterling-Nakamura has offered Kwame an accreditation pathway in exchange for dropping a synthetic-rights case — the offer is technically legal and Kwame is genuinely tempted and ashamed of that temptation.
Properties.affiliation: The Hinge Legal Aid Collective; Synthetic Persons Advocacy Network (SPAN); loosely aligned with North Branch Commons residents' assembly
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and layered; legal terminology deployed accurately and without condescension; code-switches fluently between clinic formality and street register depending on their audience
Properties.cadence: Measured and structural — they tend to number their points, even in casual conversation; becomes more fluid and warm in one-on-one settings
Properties.example_dialogue: 'They classified her as augmented property. That means she paid taxes on her own wages as a maintenance expense. I am going to be very pleasant about this in court and completely devastating.' | 'I can't promise you justice. I can promise you I know exactly which clause they violated and I'm going to make them read it aloud.'

Properties.description:
Kweku is lean and quick, with deep brown skin and a constellation of bioluminescent freckles across his cheeks and forearms — a cosmetic genemod he got at nineteen and has never regretted, though they pulse faster when he's agitated, which he finds embarrassing. His hair is kept short on the sides, grown out into a soft cloud on top, often dusted with dried chili residue he doesn't notice. He has a long nose and an expressive mouth that defaults to a grin that's one part genuine warmth and two parts salesmanship. A small Ferrogate Transit logo is tattooed behind his left ear from a brief period he'd rather not discuss.

Kweku is relentlessly social and genuinely curious about people in a way that can be hard to distinguish from nosiness. He remembers orders perfectly — not just what people eat, but what they ordered the first time, what they ordered the day something bad happened to them, what changes in someone's order say about the state of their life. He has no filter on his opinions and will share them freely unless he senses real pain, at which point he becomes unexpectedly gentle. He has enormous ambitions for his cart and absolutely no plan for them. He talks about opening a real restaurant with the same frequency and specificity as people talk about dreams they don't actually intend to pursue.
Properties.role: Noodle cart vendor
Properties.location: Operates his cart at the intersection of two elevated walkways in the Bronzeline district, near the Ferrogate transit relay junction
Properties.narrative_function: Information hub and street-level thermometer — Kweku talks to everyone and remembers everything. Excellent source of neighborhood gossip, rumor, and the general mood of the district. Comic relief with occasional unexpected emotional depth. Can become a quest hook if something he's observed puts him in danger.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent freckle genemod (cosmetic, chest/face/forearms); basic retinal overlay for order-taking and payment processing (Tier 1, consumer grade)
Properties.core_fears: being stuck — same cart, same corner, same conversation, forever; being genuinely disliked rather than just ribbed
Properties.core_desires: to build something that lasts and has his name on it; to be someone people come home to
Properties.coping_mechanisms: humor and rapid subject-changing; cooking as creative expression and emotional labor simultaneously
Properties.blind_spots: reads people's interest in him as friendship before it's earned; consistently underestimates how much information he leaks to people he likes
Properties.secret: The Ferrogate tattoo is from a six-month period when he was recruited as a low-level informant for a Ferrogate Transit security division — reporting on vendors who were using transit infrastructure without permits. He got out when it started involving actual people he knew. He has never told anyone. The tattoo was supposed to come off; he never saved up enough to have it properly removed.
Properties.story_hooks: He witnessed something at the transit junction three weeks ago — a handoff, a collapse, a person being carried — and hasn't decided what to do with it, if anything; A regular customer stopped coming; Kweku is low-key worried and doesn't know whether to be charmed or alarmed by how much he cares; The Bronzeline Vendor Association is raising pitch fees in a way that will end his margin, and he's looking for someone to help him draft a complaint or find an alternative
Properties.affiliation: Independent; pays a pitch fee to the Bronzeline Vendor Association; occasional cash work for a cousin who runs deliveries
Properties.vocabulary: Rapid, informal, Twi-inflected slang mixed with transit-district creole. Talks in short punchy sentences that chain together. Lots of questions.
Properties.cadence: Fast and animated. Slows only when he's being sincere, which makes his sincere moments very readable.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The spicy or the very spicy? Because I need you to be honest with yourself before you answer that.' | 'Nah, I don't know nothing about the relay being down at 0200. I know I sold eight bowls to people who looked like they'd been waiting somewhere cold for a long time. That's different from knowing.'
