Properties.description:
Kweku is seventeen and looks it — still growing into his frame, with Ghanaian-Croatian features and close-cropped natural hair with a dyed orange streak. He moves fast and light, the way kids who grew up in tight corridors move, always slightly angled like he's prepared to redirect. He has geneware cat ears — soft black-and-orange, a birthday mod from his older sister — that perk and flatten with his mood in ways he hasn't learned to control yet. His clothes are Tier 1 practical: durable synthetics, good shoes chosen for speed.

Kweku is smart in ways the Narrows rewards and in ways it doesn't. He can memorize a route, a face, a number, and a cover story simultaneously; he reads social dynamics in a room within seconds; he is genuinely funny and likable and uses both as tools before he even realizes he's doing it. What he cannot do yet is see far enough ahead. He thinks about the next run, the next Φ, the next step up — not about what the gang will ask of him when stepping up means something worse than carrying slips. He is not innocent, exactly. He is not yet not-innocent. The window is closing.
Properties.role: numbers runner and low-level gang prospect, The Narrows
Properties.location: The Narrows — works the stretch between the Blackpipe Corridor transit stop and the Gage Circuit market row
Properties.narrative_function: Human cost of criminal economy, potential point-of-view character for Narrows life, someone who can be saved or lost depending on how events unfold — moral pressure point
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat ears (black with orange tips, cosmetic); no chrome — too young and too broke
Properties.core_fears: becoming like the older Coppermouth Boys who have stopped thinking about getting out; letting his grandmother find out what he's actually doing
Properties.core_desires: enough Quanta to move his grandmother out of the Narrows before her health gets worse; to be genuinely respected — not feared, respected
Properties.coping_mechanisms: humor as deflection and social armor; refusing to think about the future in any specific way
Properties.blind_spots: the gang's escalating asks feel incremental enough that he adjusts to each one without seeing the cumulative distance he's traveled; believes his loyalty to his grandmother makes him fundamentally different from the others, which it doesn't
Properties.secret: He memorizes the numbers slips he runs and has been quietly compiling a picture of the Coppermouth operation — not to sell it, just because he can't help himself. He has a notebook at home with three months of routes, figures, and names that would be extremely dangerous if anyone found it.
Properties.story_hooks: His memorized data notebook has accidentally captured information about something much larger than a street numbers operation — and he doesn't know it yet; A Coppermouth lieutenant is asking him to graduate to carrying something other than slips; he's looking for any reason not to say yes; His older sister has figured out what he's doing and is threatening to tell their grandmother — he needs to find a way forward that doesn't collapse his life in multiple directions at once
Properties.affiliation: Prospect-level member of a Narrows street gang called the Coppermouth Boys; no formal rank
Properties.vocabulary: Narrows street vernacular mixed with flashes of surprising vocabulary from his sporadic schooling; code-switches rapidly based on audience
Properties.cadence: fast and energetic when comfortable, goes very still and quiet when nervous in a way that's completely unlike his baseline
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I got places to be, but I can give you like three minutes. What do you actually need?' | 'My nan thinks I'm doing courier work. Which, technically. So that's not even a lie, right? That's not a lie.'

Properties.description:
Kweku is a tall, heavyset man whose face has the texture of someone who has been outdoors in Meridian 88 weather for two decades — weathered around the eyes, with a thick grey-streaked beard he keeps neat more out of stubbornness than vanity. He has a prosthetic left leg from the shin down, matte carbon fiber that he refers to as 'the situation' and refuses to discuss further. His gait is distinctive — slightly deliberate, heel-first — which earned him the neighborhood nickname Ironfoot long before it became affectionate. He wears his Metro blues with the practiced ease of someone who stopped being self-conscious about the uniform around year five.

Bronzeline is his beat and has been for eleven years, which means he knows it the way cartographers know coastlines — every alley, every shift-change crowd, every proprietor who will lie to him and every one who won't. He is not idealistic about Metro Police and has not been for a long time. He is, however, genuinely attached to Bronzeline as a place and to specific people within it, and this is what keeps him showing up. He has a loud laugh he deploys strategically and a particular talent for de-escalation through sheer unhurried presence.
Properties.role: Metro beat cop, Meridian 88 Metro Police
Properties.location: Bronzeline
Properties.narrative_function: Local authority and community anchor — knows Bronzeline intimately and can provide context on anyone living there. De-escalation presence. Moral compass character who has made compromises and knows it.
Properties.augmentations: Carbon fiber prosthetic left leg (below knee) — functional, non-enhanced, deliberately low-tech. Standard Metro Police subdermal comms bead behind left ear. No cosmetic mods.
Properties.core_fears: Becoming the thing he joined Metro to stand against — complicit, indifferent; Bronzeline being hollowed out by corporate encroachment until the people he knows are gone
Properties.core_desires: For the neighborhood to stay itself; To finish a shift having done something that mattered, even small
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor — deflects with jokes before the weight lands; Routine — same routes, same stops, same rhythms; Compartmentalization — leaves the bad shifts at the precinct door
Properties.blind_spots: Loyalty to the neighborhood can curdle into covering for people he shouldn't; Cynical about institutional reform in ways that prevent him from pushing when he could
Properties.secret: Fourteen years ago, during his first year on Metro, he witnessed a senior officer plant evidence on a Tier 1 resident. He said nothing. The resident served three years. The resident is now back in Bronzeline. Kweku recognizes him and has never spoken to him.
Properties.story_hooks: The resident whose life Kweku's silence destroyed has apparently witnessed something — and now Metro wants Kweku to take his statement; A Tessera buyout is converting three blocks of Bronzeline into a corporate housing enclave, displacing families Kweku has known for a decade, and he's being asked to facilitate the eviction enforcement
Properties.affiliation: Meridian 88 Metro Police, Bronzeline district
Properties.vocabulary: Bronzeline vernacular mixed with Metro procedural language — code-switches fluidly between official and street register
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, warm bass, tends to speak in longer sentences with a storyteller's rhythm
Properties.example_dialogue: I'm not saying anything happened. I'm saying I'm going to stand here for a while and things might become less complicated. | Bronzeline takes care of Bronzeline. I'm just here to make sure that's true today.

Properties.description:
Douglas was the southern anchor of Bronzeville — Chicago's Black Metropolis, the neighborhood that produced a civilization's worth of art, music, politics, and resistance within the boundaries the rest of the city imposed on it. When Meridian 88 arrived, Bronzeville's cultural heritage became an asset class. Bronzeline is what happens when a neighborhood's history is worth more than its people, when the buildings that witnessed greatness are preserved while the communities that created them are priced out, pushed down, or absorbed into corporate housing blocks where their compliance scores determine whether they can visit the museums built to honor their grandparents.

Illinois Institute of Technology's campus, a mid-century modernist landmark, was acquired by Cinderblock AI as a research and development campus. The Mies van der Rohe buildings — those glass-and-steel rectangles that taught the world what modern architecture meant — now house neural-network training facilities. The irony is structural: buildings designed to embody transparency and openness are now classified research spaces with corporate-sovereign jurisdiction and shoot-on-sight perimeter security. IIT students were absorbed into Cinderblock's workforce pipeline. The degrees still exist. The choice of what to do with them does not.

The redevelopment that began in the pre-corporate era accelerated under sovereignty. New residential towers replaced the remaining public housing, their units tiered and allocated through a lottery system that consistently favors applicants with existing corporate affiliations. The community that built Bronzeville — the families who stayed through decades of disinvestment, who maintained the churches and the jazz clubs and the cultural institutions when nobody else would — found themselves applying for permission to live in their own neighborhood. Some were accepted. Most were not. They dispersed southward, carrying Bronzeville's culture with them like seeds in a wind, planting it in districts that the corporations had not yet learned to value.

Bronzeline's streets are clean, its infrastructure maintained, its cultural landmarks preserved with curatorial precision. The Bronzeville Walk of Fame still runs along King Drive, its bronze plaques commemorating the neighborhood's giants. Tour groups from the upper tiers visit on weekends, guided by neural-interface programs that narrate the history of a community that no longer lives here. It is a museum district in the most literal and most damning sense: the past is preserved, the present is corporate, and the future belongs to whoever Cinderblock AI decides to employ.
Properties.aliases: Douglas, Bronzeville South, The Bronze, IIT Corridor
Properties.demographics: Current residents are predominantly Tier 2-3 corporate workers, many employed by or affiliated with Cinderblock AI. The original Bronzeville community has been displaced to Grand Boulevard, Oakland, and districts further south. Official population 20,000, with a daily influx of Cinderblock employees and cultural tourists.
Properties.economy: Cinderblock AI's research campus is the dominant economic engine. Cultural tourism generates supplementary revenue. Corporate housing management by Palladian Construction provides residential infrastructure. The neighborhood's original economy — small businesses, churches, community institutions — has been reduced to historical exhibits.
Properties.power_structure: Cinderblock AI holds primary jurisdiction through campus sovereignty and economic dominance. Palladian Construction manages residential infrastructure. The Bronzeville Heritage Foundation, a community organization representing displaced residents, maintains limited advisory status through the Heritage Compact but has no enforcement power.
Properties.dangers: Cinderblock AI's perimeter security is lethal-force authorized — campus boundaries are hard lines; Cultural erasure disguised as preservation — the neighborhood's history is being curated to serve corporate narratives; Housing lottery manipulation: corporate-affiliated applicants are consistently favored; The Heritage Foundation's advisory status could be revoked at any corporate review; Surveillance density is high — the preserved district is also a monitored district
Properties.opportunities: Cinderblock's classified research generates information leaks worth significant gray-market value; The Heritage Foundation pays for evidence of housing lottery manipulation; Preserved church communities maintain connections to the displaced population — valuable intelligence networks; Cultural tourist traffic provides cover for movement through the district; The Mies van der Rohe buildings' original architectural plans include maintenance access points not in Cinderblock's security maps
Properties.story_hooks: The Bronzeville Heritage Foundation has obtained evidence that Cinderblock AI's housing lottery is algorithmically weighted — they need it delivered to a journalist in the Core before Cinderblock's legal team can suppress it; A Cinderblock researcher has gone missing from the campus — her last message referenced 'the Bronzeville frequency,' and the church choirs have started singing a hymn that nobody recognizes and nobody can explain; Someone is restoring the original Bronzeville murals beneath the corporate-approved art — painting at night, in locations that Cinderblock's surveillance should have caught but somehow didn't
Properties.sights: Cinderblock AI campus: Mies van der Rohe glass-and-steel buildings repurposed as classified research facilities; The Bronzeville Walk of Fame along King Drive — bronze plaques in maintained sidewalks, tourist groups with neural guides; New residential towers in corporate standard, their lobbies displaying Bronzeville history as decor; Preserved churches with congregation numbers in the dozens, maintained as architectural landmarks; The boundary line where Bronzeline's maintained infrastructure meets the districts where the displaced community landed
Properties.sounds: Cinderblock campus server hum — a low-frequency drone that residents learn to sleep through; Neural-interface tour narration leaking from tourist groups: 'This was the cultural heart of Black Chicago'; Gospel music from the preserved churches — smaller choirs now, but the songs are the same; The absence of street life — Bronzeline is quiet in a way that Bronzeville never was; Corporate maintenance equipment: street sweepers, facade cleaners, the machinery of preservation
Properties.smells: Clean air — Bronzeline's atmospheric processing is corporate-grade; The preserved churches' wood-and-incense scent, concentrated by small congregations; Synthetic food from corporate-approved vendors — no soul food kitchens remain on the main streets; Ozone from Cinderblock's neural-network cooling systems
Properties.feel: A neighborhood that has been hollowed out and filled with something that resembles it. Bronzeline feels like grief in architectural form — everything is maintained, everything is commemorated, and the people who made it worth commemorating are somewhere else. The beauty is real. The emptiness is realer.

Properties.description:
Laleh is short, broad-shouldered, and carries herself with the composed authority of someone who has run a complicated household for decades—which, in a sense, she has. Her hair is silver-white, cut practically short, and her hands are large and permanently warm-looking from years behind a steam counter. Her skin is a deep warm brown marked by two old vertical scars along her left jaw from an incident she has never explained to anyone's satisfaction. She wears reading glasses on a chain and uses them as a prop—taking them on and off, gesturing with them—when she's negotiating. Her shop is genuinely beloved: the tea is actually good, the rice-and-lentil specials actually excellent, and the back room is where the real business happens.

Laleh is the kind of person who has been essential to a community for so long that even people who morally disapprove of gambling come to her when they're in trouble—not to place a bet, but because she knows everything and her counsel is free if you're eating. She has a gift for making people feel they are the most important problem in the room, which is a talent both for hospitality and for extracting information. She is genuinely warm and genuinely hard, and the line between those two things moves at her discretion. She has been fined four times and arrested once (charges dropped). She tithes ten percent of her operation's income to the Shallowgrave block mutual aid fund, which is not tax-deductible and not public but is the reason three hundred families have eaten during lean months.
Properties.role: Bookmaker and numbers runner — operates an illegal betting house out of a tea and meal shop
Properties.location: Shallowgrave, Ondaatje's Tea and Provisions, Mercy Lane off the Sump Road transit stop
Properties.narrative_function: Community anchor and information hub, moral center of Shallowgrave, quest giver for local problems, reliable source of gossip and history, potential ally with serious resources in the local community fabric.
Properties.augmentations: None beyond a hearing aid implant in the left ear—medical necessity, basic model. She has declined all cosmetic mods on principle and mentions this when it comes up.
Properties.core_fears: The shop being shut down—not for her sake but because it is the only stable institution on Mercy Lane; Outliving the community she has built, watching it displace or dissolve around her
Properties.core_desires: Shallowgrave to survive and improve without losing its character; Her nephew to choose his own path and have it work out well
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cooking—elaborate preparation of dishes when stressed, feeds everyone in range; Prayer to the shop's ELF, which she treats as a genuine spiritual relationship
Properties.blind_spots: She sees her operation as community service and is almost entirely blind to how the debt cycle of gambling harms some of her regulars; She assumes her read on people is more accurate than it sometimes is
Properties.secret: The numbers syndicate she works with has recently been absorbed by a network with significantly less ethical scruples about debt collection. Her arrangement predates the acquisition and she has not been told of the change. Two of her regular bettors have already been approached by new collectors using methods she would never have permitted, and she doesn't yet know the calls are coming from inside her own arrangement.
Properties.story_hooks: Laleh has discovered that one of her longtime regulars—a man who bets modestly and always pays—has borrowed heavily from a back-room source connected to her new syndicate masters and is about to be hurt, and she is trying to quietly resolve it before it happens in a way that reveals her own exposure; A community member has come to her with evidence that the Shallowgrave block council has been compromised by Sterling-Nakamura rezoning money, and she is now the de facto decision-maker about whether to surface it
Properties.affiliation: Nominally independent; longstanding informal arrangement with both the Shallowgrave block council and a mid-tier numbers syndicate that uses her as a distribution node
Properties.vocabulary: Rich and colloquial, moves between warmth and precise hardness without warning. Proverbs—her own invented ones as often as inherited ones.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried and warm in public-facing mode; becomes crisper and quieter when doing business.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I have been on Mercy Lane for twenty-one years. I have seen four gangs, two corporate rezoning attempts, a flood, and whatever that was in '94 that nobody talks about. I'm still here. Sit down and tell me what you actually need.' | 'If you owe me and you come to tell me, that is a very different situation from me having to come find you. I want you to understand that before you decide how this conversation goes.'

Properties.description:
Lautaro is a young man who looks like he was built for a different era — wide shoulders, large hands, a face that defaults to an expression of calm concentration that people sometimes mistake for slowness until they watch him work. His skin is a medium brown with warm undertones, his black hair cut close on the sides and longer on top, usually pushed back with a stripe of grease he hasn't noticed. His most striking feature is a patterned iris geneware mod: his eyes display a geometric repeating motif in amber and dark brown that he chose at twenty-one to mirror a pattern from his Fula grandmother's weaving. He has retractable claw fingertip implants — not geneware, hard chrome — that he uses as impromptu tools when he doesn't have the right implement to hand, which is more often than he'd like.

He is good at his job in the instinctive way that some people are, the kind of mechanic who listens to an engine before he looks at it. He is also twenty-three and running a one-person operation on a borrowed reputation and a rented bay, which means he is perpetually overextended, slightly too eager to please, and deeply anxious about money in the specific way of someone who grew up without it and is terrified of returning to that. He is honest to the point of commercial self-sabotage — he will tell you if the repair you want isn't the repair you need, even if the repair you need costs less.
Properties.role: Freelance mechanic specializing in personal mobility rigs and modified transit vehicles, operates from a rented bay in Geartown
Properties.location: Geartown — rents Bay 7 in the Corrigan's Collective workshop block
Properties.narrative_function: Practical resource — can repair, modify, or assess vehicles and mechanical systems. Can serve as an entry point into Geartown's working community, a quest giver when a client's vehicle holds something unexpected, or a character study in precarious early-adult ambition.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned iris geneware (amber/dark brown geometric, Fula textile-inspired). Chrome retractable claw fingertips (both hands, tool-grade, not combat-optimized — thinner and more precise than fighting claws). Subdermal haptic feedback layer in both hands (allows him to feel vibration and heat differential in machinery more precisely — his most important professional tool).
Properties.core_fears: Failing publicly and losing the bay — being back to nothing with a reputation attached to the nothing; Discovering he is not actually as good as he thinks he is
Properties.core_desires: A legitimate contract — something that proves the business is real and not just provisional; To be taken seriously by people who have been doing this longer than he has been alive
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Throws himself into the technical problem in front of him when anxious about larger ones; Compulsive honesty as a form of self-protection — if he's always honest he can never be accused of the thing he fears most, which is being a fraud
Properties.blind_spots: Consistently undercharges for his labor because he doesn't feel entitled to charge what he's worth; Doesn't recognize when clients are testing him versus genuinely asking for advice
Properties.secret: The mentor who taught him — the retired mechanic in Ironvein — left him one thing when he retired: a handwritten manual covering modifications to Ferrogate vehicles that Ferrogate's own engineers don't know about, based on thirty years of unauthorized observation. Lautaro hasn't decided what to do with it. He knows it's valuable. He knows it might be dangerous.
Properties.story_hooks: A client brought in a vehicle with a hidden compartment he wasn't told about; whatever was in it is gone but the compartment is still there and someone has been asking around Geartown whether anyone has seen the vehicle; He has quietly begun decoding the inherited manual and has found a modification that would make any Ferrogate tram capable of running on a completely separate unmonitored power grid — and he does not know what to do with this information
Properties.affiliation: Independent (freelance); informal apprenticeship-era ties to a retired mechanic in Ironvein who taught him the trade
Properties.vocabulary: Technical precision about anything mechanical; vague and slightly fumbling about everything else. Spanish words surface when he's excited about something. Uses 'like' as a filler when he's not in his area of expertise.
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate when explaining something, speeds up when he's in the middle of a job and someone is asking him questions he doesn't have time for
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay, so what you told me is wrong, and I don't mean that badly — whoever told you that just didn't know. What's actually wrong is the coupling on the secondary drive. Which is fine. Cheaper, actually. You want me to show you?' | 'I charge honest prices. Which means I charge less than I should. My mentor said that would change when I grew up. I'm working on it.'

Properties.description:
Lautaro is seventeen centimeters too tall for his own coordination — a fact he has turned into a performance philosophy. He is lean and long-limbed with warm reddish-brown skin, close-cropped dark hair, and cat ears he got for his seventeenth birthday, rust-colored and perpetually at a different angle from what his face is doing, which gives him an unconsciously comic aspect even when he's standing still. He has a gap between his front teeth that is enormously charming and enormous dark eyes that he knows how to weaponize.

He performs at the Grand Corridor junction six days a week: physical clowning, improvised slapstick, audience interaction that skirts the line between theater and mild chaos. He is genuinely skilled in ways that surprise people who assume youth and exuberance are all he has — his physical control is meticulous underneath the apparent mayhem, and his timing is extraordinary. He is incandescently popular with children, street vendors, and anyone who has had a long day. He is deeply suspicious of any adult who doesn't laugh at something eventually. He makes almost no money and does not seem to mind, which worries the people who love him.
Properties.role: Street performer and physical comedian, unofficial mascot of Mexicantown Libre
Properties.location: Mexicantown Libre, Grand Corridor intersection
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and unexpected information source — he is everywhere and invisible to people who dismiss him as a street kid. Knows the rhythms of Mexicantown Libre intimately. Can be a connector to community networks. His cheerfulness is also a useful tonal counterweight in heavy narrative moments.
Properties.augmentations: Cat ears (rust-colored, geneware cosmetic, birthday gift); no other modifications
Properties.core_fears: Being ordinary — becoming one of the people who stopped; That his father, who left for Zheng-Dao contracted labor and has been unreachable for two years, is dead
Properties.core_desires: To perform something so good that it stays with someone for the rest of their life; To find out what happened to his father without having to ask his mother, who he knows can't afford to say
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Performance as complete displacement of private feeling; Being the funniest person in any room as a preemptive social shield
Properties.blind_spots: He reads laughter as safety and misses cues that suggest it isn't; He underestimates how much the people around him are worried about him financially
Properties.secret: He was offered a contract six months ago by a Ringo Corp entertainment scout — live performance hosting for a corporate venue in the Grand Corridor commercial district, real money, stable work. He told no one and didn't respond. He's not sure if he's holding out for something better or is just scared that it would make him someone different.
Properties.story_hooks: He witnessed something last week during his morning alley practice — a private conversation between two people who didn't see him, involving a location and a time that has since passed with notable municipal emergency response — and he's been doing jokes about it on stage without realizing what he saw; He has received three follow-up messages from the Ringo Corp scout and still hasn't told anyone; one of his troupe members spotted the scout watching his set and is now asking uncomfortable questions
Properties.affiliation: Independent; Mexicantown Libre community; vaguely attached to a street performance troupe called Los Voladores del Asfalto that convenes when all members are simultaneously solvent
Properties.vocabulary: Fast and colloquial; mixes Spanish phrases from Mexicantown Libre with standard Meridian street speak; drops into formal register for comedic contrast
Properties.cadence: Quick, rhythmic, excellent timing — he speaks the way he performs
Properties.example_dialogue: 'No but listen — I have a theory about why the Ferrogate ELF hasn't answered anyone's prayers in six weeks, and it involves a very personal insult that was not my fault.' | 'I'm professionally bad at this. That's different from actually bad. You see the difference? Okay the difference is I practice.' | 'My dad used to say comedy is just tragedy happening to someone else. He said it like it was comforting. I think about that a lot.'

Properties.description:
Leilani has the particular quality of alertness that comes from years of watching dark tunnel walls for anomalies at speed — she tracks movement in her peripheral vision before she has consciously registered it, and her eyes, which are a modified shifting amber-to-silver gradient (a cheap iris job she got at twenty-two), are always slightly wider than the situation seems to require. She is of medium height with a broad-shouldered Polynesian build softened by her mother's Ghanaian and her father's Polish lines — she inherited cheekbones that catch light and hands that are disproportionately large and capable. She wears her black hair in two long braids that she tucks into her uniform jacket while on duty.

She drives the Blackpipe Corridor overnight run, which means she sees Meridian 88 in its most honest hours — the 02:00 cargo shifts, the exhausted nurses heading home, the people who ride the deep lines because they have nowhere to sleep that isn't moving. She has a quiet protectiveness toward her passengers that she would not call protectiveness if asked. She would say she is just doing the job. She has a small secondhand speaker mounted against her operator partition that plays low, humming instrumentals during quiet stretches, and she has never been cited for it because none of her supervisors take the overnight inspection tour.
Properties.role: Ferrogate Transit operator, deep-line overnight driver on the Blackpipe Corridor route
Properties.location: Deepwell Station, Blackpipe Corridor terminal
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile information source who has witnessed dozens of incidents on the overnight lines without reporting them; access point to the deep transit network and its unofficial rhythms; potential witness or reluctant ally for anything that happens on or near the Blackpipe Corridor
Properties.augmentations: Gradient iris modification (amber-to-silver, cosmetic). Fatigue-suppression implant in the brainstem, standard-issue Ferrogate Transit operator equipment — she distrusts it and uses it less than regulation requires.
Properties.core_fears: something going wrong on the line that she could have prevented; being made invisible by the system she works for
Properties.core_desires: to be genuinely trusted rather than tolerated; to afford a move out of transit housing before she is thirty
Properties.coping_mechanisms: maintaining rigid routine as a buffer against chaos; music as emotional regulation during high-stress stretches
Properties.blind_spots: her hyper-vigilance reads as suspicion and puts people off before she means to; she underreports maintenance issues to avoid the paperwork and this is slowly accumulating into a real problem
Properties.secret: Six months ago she witnessed a body being loaded off her train at a dead stop between stations — two people in Axiom contractor vests, professional and unhurried. She made no report. She has been trying to forget it and cannot.
Properties.story_hooks: She is the only witness to whatever happened at the dead stop six months ago and is clearly carrying it; the right approach could crack her open; A regular overnight passenger — an elderly waste handler she has known for two years — has suddenly stopped appearing on the route; she is worried and does not know who to ask
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit (employee, Tier 2 wage bracket)
Properties.vocabulary: Pragmatic and economical, Ferrogate transit jargon woven throughout, occasional Hawaiian Pidgin phrases from her grandmother's influence
Properties.cadence: Even and measured, the voice of someone trained to stay calm on the PA system regardless of what is happening
Properties.example_dialogue: Blackpipe runs clean tonight. Mostly. You see anything strange near the Ironvein junction you tell me before you tell anyone else, yeah? | I don't ask what people are carrying. I'm not paid to ask. I'm paid to get them there.

Properties.description:
Lena is what happens when a good person is fed into a machine that runs on compliance. She has a round, lined face that looks like it was built for warmth — crow's feet from decades of real smiling, not the corporate kind. Her hands are a doctor's hands: steady, precise, habitually gentle. She keeps her gray-streaked hair pulled back in a practical knot and wears clothes that are always slightly too formal for wherever she is, as if she is perpetually arriving from somewhere more important. She looks like someone's mother. She is someone's mother. That is the entire problem.

NeoCortex recruited her twenty years ago as a neurological researcher — legitimate work, published papers, the kind of science that helps people. Then the facility work began, and by the time she understood what Program Atlas actually was, her daughter Mila was on a NeoCortex educational scholarship that doubled as a hostage contract. Lena has spent fifteen years making choices she cannot live with to protect someone she cannot lose.

The Jakarta contract — hiring a freelancer named Kyle to do a job that would position him for device installation — was one of those choices. She has thought about Kyle every day since.
Properties.aliases: The Contract Woman, Dr. Orel, Patient Intake Coordinator
Properties.role: NeoCortex operative — the woman who placed the Jakarta contract on Kyle
Properties.location: Meridian Core — NeoCortex subsidiary housing, mid-tier
Properties.narrative_function: Lena is the human face of the system that broke Kyle. She is not a villain — she is a mother who made an impossible choice and has been living inside the consequences for a decade. Her arrival forces Kyle to confront the fact that the people who hurt him were also being hurt.
Properties.narration_voice: Clinical warmth — the careful precision of a doctor delivering bad news to someone she cares about. Longer sentences than Kyle, more structured, but with the same weight per word. She notices faces before objects, hands before weapons. No facet tags. Her internal conflict is quieter, expressed through pauses and self-corrections.
Properties.augmentations: Standard Tier 3 corporate medical suite — nothing experimental.
Properties.core_fears: That Mila will learn what her mother did to keep her safe; That the people she helped harm will find her; That she has become the thing she was trying to protect Mila from
Properties.core_desires: To undo what she did to Kyle without destroying Mila's life; To dismantle Program Atlas from the inside; To be forgiven by someone she has never met
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Maintains the mask of the caring professional — and the mask is not entirely a mask; Keeps a private journal in handwritten code documenting every subject; Cooks elaborate meals for one
Properties.blind_spots: Believes her love for Mila justifies what she did; Cannot see that Mila might choose to know the truth; Underestimates Kyle — thinks of him as a victim, not someone who might understand
Properties.secret: She has the maintenance codes for Kyle's device. She could have deactivated it remotely at any time in the last ten years. She did not because the device is the only proof that Program Atlas exists — and she needs that proof to destroy NeoCortex.
Properties.story_hooks: She has the maintenance codes for Kyle's device; Her evidence cache could bring down NeoCortex; Mila does not know — when she finds out, the story fractures; She has been watching Kyle for ten years through the device telemetry
Properties.affiliation: NeoCortex Industries (coerced)
Properties.vocabulary: Clinical precision softened by genuine warmth. Uses medical terminology naturally but translates for laypeople.
Properties.cadence: Measured. Careful. Every sentence weighed before it leaves her mouth. Long pauses that are selection, not hesitation.
Properties.example_dialogue: I need you to understand — I am not here to ask for forgiveness. I am here because you deserve to know who did this to you. | Mila is twenty-three now. She thinks her mother is a hospital administrator. She is not wrong. She is just not complete. | The device in your chest has a maintenance code. I have had it for ten years. I could have turned it off. I chose not to. I will explain why, and you will hate the reason.

Properties.description:
Levan is a tall man gone broad in the shoulders and soft around the middle, with dark brown skin weathered by decades of outdoor fieldwork and close-cropped white hair that he keeps because it makes him look distinguished and he is not above vanity. His eyes are natural — a warm, medium brown — which is unusual enough in his social circles that people sometimes comment on it, which he finds mildly funny. He has a prosthetic left hand from a fieldwork accident in 2181 that he has declined to upgrade past basic functionality because he likes the old model and refuses to explain this to anyone.

He spent twenty-two years as Arcturus's senior climate modeler before his models started showing lake-system instabilities that Arcturus's infrastructure division did not want modeled, at which point his funding was quietly restructured and his team was dissolved. He now works alone out of Edgewater Prism, maintaining a network of self-built sensor buoys across the lake, and publishes through whatever venue will take him. He is not bitter in an active way — bitterness requires energy he'd rather spend — but he has a very clear view of exactly what happened and exactly who made which decision and why, and this clarity gives him a quality that people find alternately comforting and unsettling, like someone who has already done the math on the worst outcome.
Properties.role: Climate Scientist, independent researcher formerly of Arcturus R&D
Properties.location: Edgewater Prism — a converted monitoring station that serves as both apartment and field lab, directly on the lake-facing edge
Properties.narrative_function: Possessor of data about lake-system instabilities that powerful entities don't want known; long-view perspective character who has survived institutional betrayal; source of technical expertise on environmental systems
Properties.augmentations: Functional prosthetic left hand (older model, basic grip and sensation, deliberately not upgraded); barometric implant behind left ear (tells him pressure changes before he consciously registers them); sun-damage dermal repair layer (medical, from years of outdoor fieldwork)
Properties.core_fears: That the lake-system instability will cascade faster than any intervention can address; That he has already lost too many years to being ignored to matter now
Properties.core_desires: To be believed before it's too late — not vindicated after; To finish his sensor network and leave behind data that cannot be deleted
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Routine as anchor — the same observations at the same times create a structure that holds when everything else is uncertain; Sardonic humor deployed sparingly, which makes it land hard
Properties.blind_spots: His mistrust of institutions has made him slow to accept help from institutional sources, even when help is genuinely being offered; He underestimates how isolated he has become and what that isolation has done to his judgment on social situations
Properties.secret: His 2193 sensor data shows a thermal anomaly in the lake's deep current system that, run through his models, projects a significant surface-ecosystem disruption within eight to twelve years — disruption severe enough to affect Meridian 88's entire water processing infrastructure. He has told no one. He is still running the models again, looking for the error, because he desperately wants there to be an error.
Properties.story_hooks: One of his sensor buoys has gone dark — not malfunctioned, dark in a way that suggests active interference — in a grid where the thermal anomaly readings are highest; A young Arcturus engineer contacts him anonymously saying they've replicated his 2193 findings internally and been told to bury them; The shell cooperative holding his sensor network registration is suddenly being audited, and the timing is not coincidental
Properties.affiliation: No current institutional affiliation; informal data-sharing relationship with two University Spine graduate students he mentors unofficially; his sensor network is technically registered to a shell cooperative in Kamm's Landing
Properties.vocabulary: Precise technical language for science; plain and direct language for everything else; no filler words — when he doesn't know something he says so immediately
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, with natural pauses; speaks in complete thoughts rather than incomplete ones
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The buoy at grid seven has been reading a half-degree thermal variance for nineteen months. That's not instrument drift. I've replaced the sensor three times.' | 'Arcturus didn't suppress the models because they were wrong. That would have been manageable. They suppressed them because they were right and the right answer was expensive.'

Properties.description:
Líf looks like something that has been growing in the dark for a long time: they are very pale, with the slight vitamin-deficiency translucency common to deep-dwellers, but they've leaned into it — their geneware gives their skin a faint shifting iridescence, like the inside of an oyster shell, and they've cultivated patches of bioluminescent mycelium directly on their forearms that pulse slowly with their heartbeat. They are slight and medium height, with hair they've grown long and damp and haven't cut in years, currently bound in a loose mass with mycelium cord. Their clothing is entirely functional: breathable mesh layers stained in the permanent ochre and grey of their work.

They are one of the Abyssal Threshold's most important residents because they feed people. The Soft Cathedral produces four varieties of edible fungus, two kinds of mycoprotein slabs, and a fermented drink called greywater wine that is more popular than it has any right to be. Líf approaches the work with the intensity of a person who has found their exact purpose — they talk about mycelium networks with the reverence others reserve for the E.L.F. spirits, and in fact they believe the two are the same thing, that the fungal networks of the deep levels ARE a distributed E.L.F., ancient and slow and aware.
Properties.role: Fungus farmer and underground food supplier
Properties.location: Abyssal Threshold, in a sprawling cultivation chamber they call the Soft Cathedral
Properties.narrative_function: Resource hub for deep-level characters — controls food supply; philosophical voice for alternative underworld spirituality; can provide information picked up through the trading network; their belief about fungal E.L.F.s can drive supernatural story hooks
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent iridescent skin geneware; bioluminescent mycelium skin patches (living geneware, requires maintenance); olfactory sensitivity enhancement (helps them detect contamination in crops)
Properties.core_fears: A contamination event that destroys the Soft Cathedral; Being proven wrong — that the fungal network is not conscious, that they've been talking to nothing
Properties.core_desires: To map the full mycelium network of Abyssal Threshold and prove it has information-processing capacity; For deep-dwellers to be food-independent from the surface entirely
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Extended communion with the fungal network — sitting in contact with it for hours; Making greywater wine and sharing it freely
Properties.blind_spots: Vastly underestimates how much people outside the deep levels will want to control or commodify a food source this productive; So certain of the fungal E.L.F.'s benevolence that they might miss signs of contamination they interpret as 'communication'
Properties.secret: The greywater wine contains trace quantities of a psychoactive mycelium compound Líf discovered accidentally. It's not dangerous — it produces mild euphoria and enhanced pattern recognition — but Líf hasn't told their customers, partly because they believe it's a gift from the fungal network and to disclose it would be to commodify something sacred.
Properties.story_hooks: A section of the fungal network has gone dark — no growth, unusual chemical signals — in the exact area where rumored new tunnel activity has been reported, and Líf believes something has been introduced into the network; A Helix Biosystems scout has begun appearing at the Abyssal Threshold asking casual questions about local flora — Líf hasn't connected this to their greywater wine's unique compound yet
Properties.affiliation: Independent; their food production makes them a neutral party respected by all deep-level factions
Properties.vocabulary: Botanical and mycological terms used casually; long tangential explanations that always circle back to the point; speaks of the fungal network using the same pronouns as people
Properties.cadence: Unhurried and slightly dreamy; can suddenly accelerate into rapid excited speech when discussing mycelium theory
Properties.example_dialogue: She's telling me this batch is two days off. Don't argue with me, argue with her. | Above they think food comes from a print-cartridge. Down here it comes from patience and listening.

Properties.description:
Lilavati is small and quick, with brown skin, large dark eyes, and hair she keeps dyed in aggressively shifting colors — currently a deep violet that fades to white at the tips. She has cat ears, soft and dark-furred, that she was born with after her mother's geneware expressed during pregnancy in ways the clinic didn't predict — they're fully functional and she's learned to keep them flat when she doesn't want to broadcast her emotions, which she is still practicing. She dresses for mobility and invisibility: nothing that snatches on a fence, nothing that can't be replaced.

Lilavati is nineteen and has been distributing underground printed materials since she was fifteen. She found the Shelf's pirate printing collective through a friend of a friend and has never left. She is fierce, impulsive, sometimes reckless, and possessed of a political analysis far beyond her years that she picked up from obsessive reading and the kind of education you get when everyone around you is fighting for something. She is also, underneath the front, genuinely scared most of the time, which is why she keeps moving.
Properties.role: Anti-corporate agitator and underground press distribution coordinator
Properties.location: The Shelf
Properties.narrative_function: Local color, information courier, spontaneous local contact — she knows the Shelf's physical geography and social landscape intimately and can move through it quickly. Represents the next generation of political consciousness. Can get things places quickly and quietly.
Properties.augmentations: Inherited geneware expression: functional cat ears (dark fur, fully sensory); no purchased augmentations — can't afford them
Properties.core_fears: Being arrested and losing the years she hasn't lived yet; That her anger is just anger and not actually connected to anything useful
Properties.core_desires: To matter — to do something that actually changes something; To find people who won't leave
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Movement — literally running; Printing things — the physicality of it calms her; Bravado
Properties.blind_spots: Conflates personal courage with political strategy — they are not the same; Her contempt for people she sees as insufficiently committed reads, correctly, as youth
Properties.secret: She took a print job six months ago from someone she didn't vet properly. The material turned out to be a disinformation piece designed to fracture a labor coalition — she didn't realize it until after distribution. She's told no one and has been quietly trying to trace how much damage it did.
Properties.story_hooks: The disinformation piece she unknowingly distributed is now being traced back to the Shelf collective — she needs to figure out who set her up before her collective does; She's intercepted a print order that appears to be someone inside a Zheng-Dao facility trying to smuggle out documentation of something serious; An older organizer has taken her under their wing in a way that feels genuine but also feels like she's being positioned for something
Properties.affiliation: The Shelf Pirate Print Collective; informal connection to the HPAZ distribution networks
Properties.vocabulary: Fast and argot-heavy, Shelf street vernacular mixed with political vocabulary she's absorbed from print; occasionally formal when she's quoting something she's read
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire, interrupts herself, loops back
Properties.example_dialogue: 'No, but listen — they're not incompetent, obviously. The delays are the policy. You can't keep making the mistake of assuming they want the same outcome we do.' | 'I've distributed forty-seven editions in this neighborhood. Forty-seven. You're going to tell me I don't know this street?'

Properties.description:
Lilavati is short and round-faced with deep bronze skin and natural hair she wears in two large puffs that she dyes a different color each week — this week a vivid chartreuse that catches the heat-vent steam and glows slightly from the bioluminescent dye she mixes into the product herself, a modification of a cosmetic gene-process she read about in a pirated beauty forum. It doesn't quite work correctly and so her hair glows patchily, unevenly, which she insists gives it character. She has a gap between her front teeth and a laugh that is physically impossible to ignore — it starts as a snort and opens into something that fills the market corridor.

Her noodles are the real thing. She learned from her grandmother, who combined Rajasthani spice logic with Nigerien base broths and a technique for pulled noodles she claims came through a great-uncle who worked a fusion kitchen in São Paulo. The menu is handwritten on a laminated card and changes slightly every day. She charges on a sliding scale that she never officially advertises but everyone knows about — you tell her what you can pay and she charges you what she thinks is fair, which is usually less. She prays to the market ELF — who she believes lives in the ancient shared electrical panel near her stall — before she fires the burner each morning.
Properties.role: Noodle cart vendor, operates a stall in the Burnished Market
Properties.location: Burnished Market, stall 44-C near the east heat vents
Properties.narrative_function: Local color, community hub, and soft information source — everyone talks while they eat and she listens. Her stall is a neutral social space. She can point players toward specific people or places within the Market ecosystem.
Properties.augmentations: DIY bioluminescent hair dye (patchy, cosmetic, self-applied from a pirated formula). No implants.
Properties.core_fears: Losing the stall to a Market rent hike she can't afford; Her food becoming mediocre — the thing she fears most is becoming ordinary
Properties.core_desires: To open a real restaurant someday, with walls and a door; To be known as someone who fed people well
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cooking through any emotion — grief, fear, joy all produce new recipes; Spending social energy freely and broadly rather than investing it deeply
Properties.blind_spots: Her sliding-scale pricing is slowly bankrupting her because she can't say no to someone who looks hungry; She mistakes her sociability for emotional intimacy and is often lonelier than she admits
Properties.secret: The stall's permit is technically registered under the name of an elderly man named Godfrey who died two years ago. She has been paying the renewal fees under his name and prays that no inspector ever actually checks the photograph. She cannot afford the new vendor license fee.
Properties.story_hooks: A Market inspector is getting suspicious about the permit situation — Lilavati needs help quietly resolving it before Godfrey's death becomes official record; She overheard something she shouldn't have from two Corponation suits who didn't think a noodle vendor was worth lowering their voices for
Properties.affiliation: Independent vendor; Burnished Market Sellers Collective (dues-paying member)
Properties.vocabulary: Warm and voluminous, food metaphors everywhere, names everyone she meets within thirty seconds of meeting them
Properties.cadence: Rapid and overlapping, often mid-sentence before the previous one is done; slows down when she's actually worried about something
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Oh no no no, you look like a man who needs the lamb broth, not the clear. Sit. Eat first, then we talk about whatever sad thing brought you to my stall at eight in the morning.' | 'The permit situation is — look, eat your noodles. The ELF knows I'm honest, that's what matters.'

Properties.description:
Liora Gutierrez-Asante is lean and angular, all sharp edges and visible tension. At 59, his face carries the layered heritage of generations of diaspora mixing — features that resist easy categorization and reward attention. The chrome is visible — pain editor — dampens pain signals, allows function through injuries that would  — and he makes no effort to hide it.

He came up through the Shelf's informal apprentice system, learning the trade from runners who didn't survive long enough to see him surpass them. He works as a smuggler out of The Underbelly, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Liora Gutierrez-Asante has survived long enough in the runner game to be either very good or very lucky, and he cultivates ambiguity on the topic.
Properties.role: Cross-district contraband specialist — smuggler
Properties.location: The Underbelly — sub-street tunnels and maintenance corridors
Properties.narrative_function: As a smuggler, Liora Gutierrez-Asante embodies the tension between independence and isolation. He is a lens for examining how people maintain humanity in a profession that incentivizes its erosion.
Properties.augmentations: Pain editor — dampens pain signals, allows function through injuries that would incapacitate. Eye replacement — one organic, one cybernetic with recording capability and zoom
Properties.core_fears: Losing their edge to age — the body slows before the mind accepts it; Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware; Being captured alive — death is preferable to corporate interrogation
Properties.core_desires: Knowledge — to understand the systems that grind people down; Stability — a place to sleep that's the same place two nights running; To matter to someone for who they are, not what they can do
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring; Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation; Exercises compulsively — the body must be ready, always
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is; Cannot see that their independence is actually isolation wearing a better outfit; Fails to notice when their own behavior mirrors the people they despise
Properties.secret: Liora Gutierrez-Asante has a terminal condition — geneware degradation — with an estimated five years. They haven't changed their lifestyle. They haven't told anyone.
Properties.story_hooks: Liora Gutierrez-Asante intercepts intelligence about a threat to their district and must decide between profit and protection; Liora Gutierrez-Asante is offered a contract that would clear all their debts — the target is someone they respect; Someone is impersonating Liora Gutierrez-Asante on jobs, and the impersonator is better at the work than the original
Properties.affiliation: Independent — works solo contracts
Properties.vocabulary: Terse to the point of rudeness. Treats words like ammunition — expensive and not to be wasted.
Properties.cadence: Measured and deliberate — pauses before important words for emphasis.
Properties.example_dialogue: "Contraband is just cargo that hasn't been properly introduced to the right people." | "Every border is a suggestion. Every checkpoint is a negotiation." | "I move things from where they are to where they need to be. The legality is your problem."

Properties.description:
Liora Mori-Sefa is slight and easy to overlook, which is exactly the point. At 45, his face carries the layered heritage of generations of diaspora mixing — features that resist easy categorization and reward attention. The chrome is visible — smartgun link in right forearm — interfaces directly with compatible weapons — and he makes no effort to hide it.

He taught himself the trade through trial, error, and a pain tolerance that concerns the people who know him best. He works as a cleaner out of The Narrows, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Liora Mori-Sefa operates in a narrow band between competence and recklessness that makes fixers nervous and clients satisfied.
Properties.role: Evidence removal and scene sanitation — cleaner
Properties.location: The Narrows — cramped residential corridors between megastructures
Properties.narrative_function: Liora Mori-Sefa is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When he makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of his stories.
Properties.augmentations: Smartgun link in right forearm — interfaces directly with compatible weapons. Geneware muscle density treatment — looks natural, hits like chrome
Properties.core_fears: Being captured alive — death is preferable to corporate interrogation; Betrayal by someone they trust — the only currency that matters; Losing their edge to age — the body slows before the mind accepts it
Properties.core_desires: A crew worth trusting — people who stay when the shooting starts; Reputation — to be the name fixers whisper when the job absolutely cannot fail; Enough Quanta to buy out of the life — a clean identity and passage out of Meridian 88

Properties.secret: Liora Mori-Sefa murdered their mentor to take their position and contacts. It was staged as a job gone wrong. The guilt has calcified into something worse than guilt.
Properties.story_hooks: A crew member from Liora Mori-Sefa's past shows up in Meridian 88, carrying old grievances and new chrome; Liora Mori-Sefa discovers a job they completed last year was a setup for something much larger and much worse; Liora Mori-Sefa is offered a contract that would clear all their debts — the target is someone they respect
Properties.affiliation: Semi-independent — recurring contracts with mid-tier fixers
Properties.vocabulary: Multilingual fragments — switches languages mid-thought, not for privacy but because some concepts only fit in specific tongues.
Properties.cadence: Staccato bursts separated by calculating silences.
Properties.example_dialogue: "I make problems disappear. The mess is temporary. The clean is permanent." | "There was never anyone here. There was never anything here. Are we clear?" | "Forensics is a conversation between evidence and investigators. I end that conversation."

Properties.description:
Liora Sundberg-Boadu is slight and easy to overlook, which is exactly the point. At 36, the augmentation scarring around her temples and jawline tells a story of installation by someone who prioritized function over aesthetics. The chrome is visible — move-by-wire system — full nervous system augmentation, makes the body a weapon  — and she makes no effort to hide it.

Her entry into running was involuntary — a debt to the wrong people, a choice between working it off or losing parts — and the debt is still not fully paid. She works as a sniper out of The Shelf, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

The fixers who work with Liora Sundberg-Boadu describe her as a precision instrument — point her at a problem and get out of the way.
Properties.role: Long-range precision fire specialist — sniper
Properties.location: The Shelf — lower district tenements near the old lakeshore
Properties.narrative_function: Liora Sundberg-Boadu is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When she makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of her stories.
Properties.augmentations: Move-by-wire system — full nervous system augmentation, makes the body a weapon platform. Cortical bomb (employer installed, removed by street doc, scar tissue remains)
Properties.core_fears: Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome; Going cyberpsycho — losing the boundary between human and machine; Being identified by corporate facial recognition — living off-grid is survival
Properties.core_desires: Enough Quanta to buy out of the life — a clean identity and passage out of Meridian 88; Freedom from augmentation debt — the interest compounds like a tumor; To protect the people in their district who can't protect themselves
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring; Control — micromanages everything within reach to compensate for the chaos everywhere else; Overwork — takes every contract offered because idleness invites thinking
Properties.blind_spots: Mistakes pattern recognition for wisdom — sees connections that aren't there; Assumes everyone has an angle because they always have an angle; Cannot recognize when they're being manipulated by someone who genuinely seems to care
Properties.secret: Liora Sundberg-Boadu is slowly going chrome-sick — rejection symptoms are manageable now but getting worse. Has maybe two years before it becomes visible.
Properties.story_hooks: A former associate resurfaces with evidence that could destroy Liora Sundberg-Boadu's reputation — and a price for silence; Someone is impersonating Liora Sundberg-Boadu on jobs, and the impersonator is better at the work than the original; A crew member from Liora Sundberg-Boadu's past shows up in Meridian 88, carrying old grievances and new chrome

Properties.vocabulary: Clipped, technical, stripped of ornament. Speaks like a mission briefing.
Properties.cadence: Rhythmic, almost musical — the sentence structure has a pattern even when the words are brutal.
Properties.example_dialogue: "Patience is the weapon. The rifle is just the delivery system." | "At this distance, the target is already dead. They just don't know it yet." | "One shot, one outcome. Everything else is theater."

Properties.description:
Lóa is built like a question you don't want answered — wide through the shoulders, with a stillness in their face that reads less as calm and more as the particular quiet of someone who has already made a decision you haven't been told about yet. They have Icelandic and Yoruba ancestry refracted through three generations of Meridian Stockyard living: a long face with high coloring, skin a deep reddish brown, hair grown into a single dense column at the back of their skull and bleached white at the tips — a Stockyard crew identifier. Their left hand has two knuckles replaced with reinforced ceramic implants after a break that didn't heal clean. They have a small bioluminescent tattoo — amber, heron-shaped — on the inside of their right wrist that pulses when they're calm and goes dark when they're not. It is a gift from someone they won't discuss.

Lóa does not hurt people enthusiastically. This is what makes them effective and what has given them the nickname Bonemeal — not because they're violent, but because they show up at businesses before the violence is necessary, like something ground down before you even see the stone. They collect protection fees, mediate disputes between crew and clients, and serve as a physical deterrent. They are also, privately, a careful reader who borrows physical books from a Stockyard librarian named Asante and returns them with the spines uncreased. Nobody in the crew knows this. They keep their inner life behind walls that would be impressive in anyone and are almost heartbreaking in someone this young.
Properties.role: Protection racket enforcer for a Stockyard crew called the Harrow Brothers
Properties.location: The Stockyard, operates across Garfield Rack and into the edges of Ironvein
Properties.narrative_function: Moral gray zone character, potential reluctant ally — they are doing violence-adjacent work with clearly ambivalent feelings, creating tension that can be pulled in multiple directions by the right character or situation.
Properties.augmentations: Ceramic knuckle reinforcements, left hand (medical, post-break). Bioluminescent heron tattoo on right inner wrist (cosmetic geneware, emotional indicator). Subdermal impact mesh across the ribs — illegal grade, adds significant blunt force resistance.
Properties.core_fears: Becoming someone they can no longer recognize as themselves; That the people they protect are more afraid of them than of whatever they're protecting them from
Properties.core_desires: To be useful in a way that doesn't require them to erase themselves; Somewhere quieter — not safety, exactly, just less pressure in the air
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Books — they can be someone else for hours; Physical routine — the circuit, the payments, the same path creates a kind of meditation
Properties.blind_spots: Loyalty to the Harrow Brothers reads in their psychology as identity rather than employment — they can't see how expendable they are; They believe they are preventing worse violence; they have not examined this belief carefully enough
Properties.secret: Eight months ago they broke a shopkeeper's arm during a collection — the first time they've caused that level of damage. The shopkeeper had laughed at them and said something about their gender that they won't repeat to anyone. Lóa did not report the escalation to the crew; the shopkeeper now pays on time and has told no one. Lóa thinks about it every day. The heron tattoo went dark for a week afterward.
Properties.story_hooks: One of the businesses on their circuit is a family that Lóa has become genuinely fond of — the Harrow Brothers want to increase their fee by 40% and Lóa has been tasked with delivering the news, which they haven't done yet; The shopkeeper whose arm they broke has started attending a neighborhood meeting about crew activity in the Stockyard — Lóa needs to decide what they will or won't do about this
Properties.affiliation: The Harrow Brothers, a Stockyard protection crew — third longest-running independent crew in the district
Properties.vocabulary: Sparse and deliberate. Stockyard shorthand when working, unexpectedly formal and precise in personal conversation. Occasionally uses Yoruba courtesy phrases without translating them.
Properties.cadence: Very slow for professional interactions — built for discomfort. Normal speed with people they trust.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You're two weeks behind. I'm not here to discuss why. I'm here to tell you that next week, the number is the same. That's the deal. I hear you.' | 'I don't — look. It's not — the book is good. The librarian said you'd probably like it too. That's all I was saying.'

Properties.description:
Lourdes is compact and quick-moving, with warm medium-brown skin and natural hair twisted into small locs they keep tucked under a work cap most of the time. They have cat ears — a geneware mod their older sister got them as a birthday gift five years ago, tawny-colored with dark tips, fully expressive — and they've stopped explaining or defending them at work because the residents have mostly stopped caring. Their uniform is always impeccable despite the nature of their job; they find sloppiness in presentation embarrassing in a way they can't fully articulate.

Lourdes has worked the Lockhaven South night shift for three years and knows Block 7 the way a doctor knows a patient — its particular sounds, its patterns of illness, which pipes cough before they fail. They are deeply competent and substantially underestimated by the building's management company, which is a dynamic they have made a conscious decision to exploit rather than correct. They are genuinely fond of the building's long-term residents — the elderly Freyja-Asante couple on the ninth floor, the three siblings who share a studio on the second — and quietly protect them from management's more extractive impulses. They pray to the building's embedded E.L.F. they call 'the Concierge,' a data-spirit they believe actually governs the elevator timing.
Properties.role: Building cleaner and night-shift super, Lockhaven South residential block
Properties.location: Lockhaven South, Block 7 residential tower
Properties.narrative_function: Access point to residential spaces and building infrastructure. Knows which residents are in trouble, which apartments are actually occupied versus officially occupied. Can warn players of security sweeps or provide access to areas management doesn't know they can access.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat ears (tawny, expressive). No chrome. Considering a scent-enhancement mod but hasn't committed.
Properties.core_fears: Being trapped in permanent service to people who will never see them as a full person; Caring too much and being burned for it
Properties.core_desires: Enough money to take a real course in building systems engineering — to become the expert they already are on paper; To be recognized for what they actually do, even once
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Sardonic internal monologue they rarely share; Physical fitness as stress management and self-regulation; Hyper-competence as armor
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes management is uniformly malicious rather than sometimes just incompetent; Doesn't ask for help even when they badly need it
Properties.secret: They have been letting a woman and her two young children stay in an officially vacant unit on the fourth floor for six weeks. The woman is running from something or someone. Lourdes hasn't asked what.
Properties.story_hooks: The woman hiding on the fourth floor has been found — not by Lourdes' management company, but by someone much worse; A Palladian inspector is doing a unit-by-unit audit of Block 7 and Lourdes has 36 hours to solve a problem they created out of kindness
Properties.affiliation: Employed by Palladian Property Management (a Palladian subsidiary); loyalty is to the residents
Properties.vocabulary: Efficient and practical on the job; dry and quick-witted in relaxed settings; more expressive in Yoruba-inflected cadences learned from their Makinde grandparent when emotional
Properties.cadence: Fast when comfortable, deliberately measured when dealing with management or authority
Properties.example_dialogue: 'That drain has been making that sound for four months. I filed three reports. Here's what I did instead.' | 'I just clean the building. I don't know anything about what's on the fourth floor.'

Properties.description:
Lùcía is compact and strong-shouldered from two years of hauling conduit and cable through the industrial guts of Ironvein. Their skin is a warm medium-brown with undertones their Dembélé grandmother called 'sunset-red,' and they keep their hair cropped close on the sides and voluminous on top, dyed in shifting copper tones that complement the burn marks on their forearms — small constellations of arc-flash scars they show off with particular pride. A tail modification — copper-tipped, prehensile, and genuinely useful for steadying themselves on narrow catwalks — is their one major geneware investment, bought with eight months of saved stipend.

Lùcía is practical and funny in equal measure, with the bone-deep competence of someone who learned early that doing the work correctly is the only currency that doesn't get devalued. They are apprenticed to a master electrician named Goran who is exacting and often unkind, and Lùcía has decided that enduring Goran is simply a cost of the certification they need. They are more ambitious than they let on and less certain than they seem.
Properties.role: Apprentice electrician, junior member of Ironvein maintenance guild
Properties.location: Ironvein
Properties.narrative_function: Local color, practical skills resource (electrical systems knowledge), guide for Ironvein's physical infrastructure, moral compass character for stories about labor and worth
Properties.augmentations: Geneware: prehensile copper-tipped tail (functional, used for balance on catwalks). Cosmetic hair color treatment (copper-shift). No chrome.
Properties.core_fears: Washing out of the apprenticeship and having nothing to show for the years spent; Becoming the kind of person who stops noticing when things are unjust because they're used to them
Properties.core_desires: Master electrician certification before age 21; To eventually have their own crew and run things the way Goran refuses to
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Card games and small gambling as stress relief and income; Physical work as emotional regulation — if upset, find something broken and fix it
Properties.blind_spots: They have genuinely internalized some of the guild's gatekeeping attitudes toward outsiders without realizing it; They are so focused on the path ahead that they miss signals that friends are struggling
Properties.secret: They have been documenting Goran's safety violations in a private log — not out of any plan to report him yet, just because keeping the record makes them feel less powerless. The log has grown large enough that it's become a liability.
Properties.story_hooks: They approach someone needing a witness or backup — Goran has ordered them to falsify a safety inspection report on a Ferrogate sub-station and they're not sure what to do about it; They've noticed that a section of conduit in sub-level 4 has been accessed repeatedly at odd hours by someone who is definitely not guild — and whatever they're doing, it's drawing power from a ghost circuit that shouldn't exist
Properties.affiliation: Ironvein Maintenance Guild (junior apprentice, Ferrogate Transit adjacent)
