Properties.description:
Mexicantown Libre is the only district in Detroit that successfully resisted corporate sovereignty acquisition, and the story of how it did so is the story of what community organizing looks like when the organizers have nothing left to lose. When Palladian Construction began eminent domain proceedings in 2152 to extend the Geartown campus southward, the neighborhood's response was not legal — they couldn't afford lawyers. It was infrastructural. Over the course of eighteen months, the Mexicantown Community Defense Network built an independent power grid using salvaged solar panels and repurposed EV batteries, established a mesh communication network that didn't route through any corporate backbone, and created a mutual aid food distribution system sourced from urban farms in the neighborhood's vacant lots. When Palladian cut utilities to force compliance, the neighborhood didn't go dark. It stayed lit.

The legal status that emerged from the standoff is unique in the GLM: Mexicantown Libre is classified as an Autonomous Community Zone, a designation that exists because the corporate lawyers who drafted it couldn't figure out how to describe a neighborhood that simply refused to participate in the system they were building. The ACZ designation grants limited self-governance, exemption from corporate sovereignty claims, and a population cap of 15,000 — the last condition being the corps' insurance policy, ensuring the model can't scale. The neighborhood governs itself through the Community Defense Network, now a formal civic body that handles everything from infrastructure maintenance to dispute resolution to border security. Yes, border security. Mexicantown Libre has borders, and they are watched.

The culture is fiercely protective, bilingual, and deeply rooted in the Mexican and Central American immigrant traditions that built the neighborhood over two centuries. Holy Cross Church still holds Mass in Spanish every Sunday. The mercado on Vernor Highway still sells handmade tamales. The murals on every available wall still tell stories of displacement and resistance. But underneath the cultural continuity, Mexicantown Libre is something new: a proof of concept that corporate sovereignty is not inevitable, that a community can opt out if it's willing to pay the price. The price is poverty. The neighborhood's per-capita income is one-fifth of the Axis. The infrastructure runs on ingenuity and duct tape. The medical facilities are volunteer-staffed. And every month, another corponation's lawyer sends another letter suggesting that the ACZ designation really ought to be reconsidered.
Properties.aliases: Mexicantown, La Libre, The Free Quarter
Properties.demographics: 14,800 residents, near the mandated population cap. Predominantly Mexican-American and Central American families with roots going back generations, plus a growing population of climate refugees and corporate excludees who sought the ACZ specifically because it's outside the system. Tier classification does not apply — the neighborhood rejected the tier system entirely.
Properties.economy: Informal, barter-heavy, and remarkably functional. The mercado economy circulates approximately Φ180 million annually, mostly in community scrip called Libres. Urban farming produces 40% of the neighborhood's food. The remaining 60% is imported through gray-market supply chains. Per-capita income is Φ8,200 — one-fifth of the Axis average.
Properties.power_structure: The Community Defense Network governs through elected block captains who report to a 12-member council. Decisions require 8-of-12 consensus. The system is imperfect — personalities, grudges, and factional disputes affect governance — but it is accountable in a way corporate governance is not. The current CDN chair is Elena Vasquez-Moreno, a 68-year-old former city planner who has held the position for eleven years.
Properties.dangers: Corporate pressure — the ACZ designation is re-evaluated every five years, and the next review is in 2201; Infrastructure fragility — the independent grid works, but one bad storm could set it back months; Medical limitations — the volunteer clinic can handle emergencies but not chronic conditions or augment maintenance; Infiltration — corponations have placed agents inside the CDN before and will again; The population cap — turning away people who need shelter because the legal limit says you must
Properties.opportunities: Safe harbor — the ACZ is one of the few places in Detroit outside corporate surveillance networks; Community trust — earn it and you have allies who will hide you, feed you, and fight for you; The gray-market supply chains that feed the neighborhood also move other things for the right people; Political symbolism — helping Mexicantown Libre makes you an ally of the resistance narrative
Properties.story_hooks: The ACZ five-year review is approaching and Cinderblock AI has been buying properties on the border — the legal challenge is coming, and the neighborhood needs allies it can't afford; A CDN block captain is selling border access to corporate agents. Elena Vasquez-Moreno suspects but can't prove it without tearing the council apart.; A climate refugee family arrives at the border. The population is at 14,800. The cap is 15,000. The family has seven members.
Properties.sights: Murals covering every surface — resistance art, historical scenes, faces of community organizers rendered ten feet tall; The independent solar grid visible on every rooftop — a patchwork of salvaged panels, mismatched but functional; Vernor Highway mercado stalls spilling onto sidewalks, handwritten signs in Spanish and English; The border markers — subtle but unmistakable bollards where corporate jurisdiction ends and the ACZ begins; Holy Cross Church's steeple, the tallest structure in the district, deliberately unaugmented
Properties.sounds: Spanish and English overlapping in market conversations — code-switching as a survival skill; Mariachi from the cantinas, live instruments because the neighborhood can't afford holographic performers and doesn't want them; The Community Defense Network's radio channel, broadcasting infrastructure updates and border reports; Children playing in streets that autonomous vehicles are not allowed to enter; The hum of the independent power grid — rougher and louder than corporate systems, but theirs
Properties.smells: Cooking — real cooking, from real ingredients, in quantities that feed a neighborhood. Corn, chili, slow-roasted meat.; Urban farm soil — the converted vacant lots grow actual food and it smells like actual earth; The faint chemical edge of improvised infrastructure — solder, battery acid, recycled materials doing their best
Properties.feel: Alive in a way the corporate districts are not. Mexicantown Libre feels like a place that chose poverty over compliance and made poverty livable through sheer communal will. It's loud, messy, crowded, under-resourced, and more genuinely human than anywhere in the Axis. The warmth is real. The danger is also real — the neighborhood knows it exists at the pleasure of forces that would prefer it didn't.

Properties.description:
Makena is twenty-seven and spends ten hours a day in a room that has no windows, watching 847 feeds from Archer's Line and the surrounding districts. She is slight and quick, with dark brown skin and natural hair she keeps pinned up for the headset, and she has cat ears — a cosmetic mod she got at nineteen because she wanted them, small and tawny and mobile, which is to say they move with her actual attention and have become professionally useful in ways she didn't anticipate. Her eyes are her own. She is very careful about her eyes. Her workstation has six physical monitors and one neural feed she plugs directly into via a port at her left temple.

Makena is frighteningly good at her job. She has a spatial memory for camera angles that her supervisors call uncanny and she calls simply how she sees, and she notices things in footage that automated flagging misses entirely — a particular way a person is carrying their weight, a crowd behaving three seconds before it does something. She finds this ability isolating in a way she cannot quite explain. She has watched every corner of Archer's Line for four years and she has never stood in most of it.
Properties.role: Metro Police surveillance operator, Archer's Line monitoring station
Properties.location: Archer's Line Metro Police Monitoring Station 7, subterranean level
Properties.narrative_function: Eyes and information — Makena knows what's on camera across a significant portion of the city. She can confirm alibis, locate missing persons, track movements, and identify faces. She is not easily corrupted but has specific pressure points. Can be a source, a complication, or a gatekeeper depending on what player characters need.
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic cat ears (tawny, mood-mobile). Neural feed port at left temple — standard-issue surveillance operator interface, allows direct sensory integration with the monitoring network for her shift. Slight chromatic tinting on fingernails, cosmetic, changes with temperature.
Properties.core_fears: that watching without acting has made her into something she doesn't have a name for; losing the neural feed ability — her identity has reorganized around it
Properties.core_desires: to use what she sees to actually protect people, not just document incidents for reports no one reads; to stand in Archer's Line during daylight and find it as interesting as the feeds make it look
Properties.coping_mechanisms: extreme competence as identity anchor; a private taxonomy of 'interesting people' she's tracked across cameras without flagging — not for any official purpose, just because they are interesting; prayers to the monitoring network's E.L.F., which she believes is real and reciprocal
Properties.blind_spots: has not fully processed that her 'interesting people' list is surveillance she hasn't been assigned to conduct; her confidence in her own neutrality is higher than her actual neutrality warrants
Properties.secret: She has been tracking a specific individual across 14 months of footage — not because they've done anything wrong, but because they appear to move through Archer's Line in patterns she cannot solve. She has compiled 200+ hours of footage into a private archive on a personal chip she keeps at home. She does not know what she's looking for.
Properties.story_hooks: The subject of Makena's private 200-hour archive has disappeared from all camera feeds simultaneously, which should be technically impossible given Archer's Line's coverage density. Makena is not sure whether to report this or investigate it privately first.; She has footage of something a Metro Police superior was definitely not doing what their official log claims — filed during a time when they were theoretically off-grid. She doesn't know what to do with this and it has been three weeks.
Properties.affiliation: Meridian 88 Metro Police, Surveillance Division
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and spatial — describes things in terms of position, angle, timing. Uses camera numbers and grid coordinates in casual conversation and catches herself doing it.
Properties.cadence: Fast, slightly compressed, like she's used to keeping up with multiple feeds
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I have that on record — I mean, I probably have that on record, if you can give me a date range and a cross-street.' | 'The cat ears are useful. People forget I'm paying attention when the ears are still. They shouldn't. The ears are always paying attention.' | 'I've watched this district for four years. I know it better than most people who live in it, which is — mm. It's something. I don't know what it is yet.'

Properties.description:
Malachai is tall and has not fully conceded to his age — he stands straight, moves deliberately, and has the particular stillness of someone who has spent decades in a profession that requires holding a blade near other people's necks and being trusted absolutely. His heritage is Romanian-Yoruba, third-generation Narrows, and it gives him a face that could be anywhere from fifty to seventy depending on how the light falls. His hair is white now, kept in a short, precise style he cuts himself by hand mirror every Sunday. He has no geneware, no cosmetic mods, only a pair of Helix-certified joint stabilizers in his right hand and wrist — installed eight years ago when arthritis began threatening his livelihood — and he mentions them only when clients ask about the faint copper banding around his wrist joints.

The shop is the Narrows' unofficial civic center. People come to argue politics, grieve, celebrate, confess, and get their hair cut, not necessarily in that order. Malachai has been cutting hair in this chair since he was thirty-two, and in that time he has absorbed the neighborhood's entire modern history. He gives opinions freely but never advice unless asked, a distinction he considers important. He has deep faith in the transit E.L.F. he calls Calea (Romanian for 'the path'), whose shrine occupies the corner of the shop near the magazine rack, and he speaks of her with the casual familiarity of a long acquaintance.
Properties.role: Barber and community elder, sole proprietor of a neighborhood barbershop in The Narrows
Properties.location: The Narrows, Drăghici & Son Barbershop (a two-chair shop that has occupied the same ground-floor unit for thirty-one years; the 'Son' in the name refers to his son, who left for a Helix Biosystems contract twelve years ago)
Properties.narrative_function: Community elder, keeper of institutional memory, and the Narrows' most trusted neutral party. Ideal quest-giver for neighborhood-level problems, historical information about The Narrows, or as a moral compass character. His shop is a location where information is freely exchanged in his presence.
Properties.augmentations: Helix Biosystems joint stabilizers in right hand and wrist (medical, copper-banded, installed for arthritis management). No cosmetic mods.
Properties.core_fears: Dying before repairing his relationship with his son; The Narrows losing its coherence as a community — the slow scattering he has watched accelerating
Properties.core_desires: For the shop to outlast him, passed to someone who understands what it is; A single honest conversation with his son
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — the opening routine of the shop is a liturgy he has not varied in a decade; Deflects personal pain into general observation about the neighborhood
Properties.blind_spots: His grief about his son has calcified into a story he tells himself; the story may no longer be accurate and he will not test it; He is more afraid of the future of the Narrows than he admits, and his optimism in Assembly meetings costs him something he is not accounting for
Properties.secret: His son sends a small monthly transfer — has for six years — and Malachai has not spent any of it. It sits in an account. He tells himself he is waiting to understand what the gesture means before he decides whether to accept it.
Properties.story_hooks: A young person has come to the shop claiming to be his son's child — which would make Malachai a grandfather he knew nothing about; he doesn't know whether this is true or a long con targeting the shop's location (which sits on land that has been covertly surveyed for a Palladian redevelopment); The Neighborhood Assembly has fractured over whether to accept a Tessera community development offer; Malachai is the only person trusted by both factions and he is being asked to mediate something he has no power to resolve
Properties.affiliation: Independent; member of The Narrows Neighborhood Assembly (informal civic body)
Properties.vocabulary: Measured and warm, with a slight Romanian cadence underneath the Narrows vernacular he's accumulated; uses proverbs from both sides of his heritage and sometimes cannot remember which is which
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, with long pauses that are comfortable rather than uncertain — he has learned that silence makes people fill it honestly
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Thirty-one years in this chair. You want to know about the Narrows? Sit down. It takes a while.' | 'My son thinks I stayed because I was afraid to leave. He left because he was afraid to stay. We are the same person running in opposite directions, and neither of us has said so.'

Properties.description:
Malaika is a big woman and she has never apologized for it — Tanzanian-Polish heritage, nearly six feet, broad through the shoulders, with a body that carries its strength like furniture: solidly, without trying. Her hair is worn in thick locs shot through with copper wire that glints when she moves, and her skin is very dark and very smooth except for a patch of scarring on her left jaw where she took something ceramic in a fight eleven years ago and kept it as a conversation piece. She dresses practically and well — not flashy, but never cheap — and has a habit of touching the scarring when she's working something out.

She is the neighborhood's collector for the Shelf Compact, an informal protection network that has run the lower levels since before she was born, and she does this job with a thoroughness that people mistake for menace until they know her better. She is not cruel. She is extremely serious. The businesses in her circuit pay on time and have done so for seven years, not because they fear her specifically but because they have seen what she does when accounts fall behind, which is to sit down with the owner and explain — in considerable detail, with full eye contact — exactly how much worse their situation could become and exactly how much it will cost her personally to allow it not to. She has a talent for making the math of compliance feel like mercy.
Properties.role: Protection racket enforcer and neighborhood tax collector, The Shelf lower levels
Properties.location: The Shelf, lower levels — operates a rotating circuit of Burnside Pocket and Blackpipe Corridor businesses
Properties.narrative_function: Antagonist or uneasy ally depending on whether player characters are in her territory, local power figure who mediates disputes, information source about the Shelf's economic underbelly, demonstration that protection rackets have their own social logic
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal impact plating — forearms and sternum, rated for small-arms blunt trauma. Joint-assist servos in both knees (injury rehabilitation, functional advantage). No cosmetic mods.
Properties.core_fears: Becoming her predecessor, who eventually started enjoying the fear; The Shelf Compact being absorbed by a larger organization that doesn't understand the neighborhood
Properties.core_desires: To run her circuit like a system that works — predictable, fair by her definition, sustainable; To eventually stop and run an actual legitimate business
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Rigid routine as a container for moral complexity; Cooking as the only space where she doesn't think about the work
Properties.blind_spots: She genuinely believes the businesses on her circuit are better off with Compact protection than without it, and this is sometimes true and sometimes catastrophically not true; She dismisses people who express fear of her as people who 'don't understand the system yet'
Properties.secret: She has been slowly diverting a small percentage of collections into a fund she thinks of as an 'exit account' — enough to buy out her position from the Compact and leave. She has been doing this for four years. She tells herself she is nearly there. She is not nearly there.
Properties.story_hooks: A business on her circuit is being targeted by a different criminal element that is not the Compact — she needs information about who is moving into the lower Shelf and why, and she can pay in access and goodwill; One of 'her' business owners has died and left the establishment to a young relative who has no idea about the Compact arrangement — Malaika is trying to handle this as delicately as possible before Uncle hears about the disruption
Properties.affiliation: The Shelf Compact (established lower-level protection network); informal loyalty to the Compact's senior figure, an elderly man she calls Uncle who she has never met in person
Properties.vocabulary: Deliberate, formal Meridian Standard with occasional Swahili phrases, especially when annoyed; economical with words, no filler
Properties.cadence: Slow and measured, like someone who has all the time in the world and is demonstrating that they do
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Let me ask you something. How much do you think it costs me to come here twice? Think about what your answer means before you give it.' | 'I'm not here because I want to be here. I'm here because you didn't make this easy. That's a distinction worth understanding.'

Properties.description:
Malika Akerblom-Manu are wiry and quick-moving, with the restless energy of someone who converts anxiety into velocity. At 32, scars map their face like a transit diagram of bad decisions and worse luck. The chrome is visible — thermal masking system — body heat signature can be suppressed or spoofed — and they make no effort to hide it.

Military training — one of the private security corps that folded during the consolidation wars — left them with skills and night terrors in equal measure. They work as a infiltrator out of The Spires, taking contracts that match their skills and their risk tolerance, which are higher than most people consider healthy.

The fixers who work with Malika Akerblom-Manu describe them as a precision instrument — point them at a problem and get out of the way.
Properties.role: Covert entry and social penetration specialist — infiltrator
Properties.location: The Spires — mid-level corporate residential towers
Properties.narrative_function: Malika Akerblom-Manu functions as a connector — their work puts them in contact with multiple factions, classes, and agendas. Stories involving them naturally cross boundaries between districts, tiers, and moral categories.
Properties.augmentations: Thermal masking system — body heat signature can be suppressed or spoofed. Hydraulic joints in knees and elbows — absorbs falls, amplifies strikes
Properties.core_fears: Going cyberpsycho — losing the boundary between human and machine; The quiet — silence means something is about to go very wrong; Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome
Properties.core_desires: Control — over their body, their schedule, their future; A crew worth trusting — people who stay when the shooting starts; Power — enough leverage that nobody ever threatens them again
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Connection — finds someone to talk to, even if it's a bartender or a cat; Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring; Planning — responds to chaos by making detailed contingency plans for everything
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot accept help without interpreting it as leverage; Trusts technology more than people — machines don't betray; Assumes everyone has an angle because they always have an angle
Properties.secret: Malika Akerblom-Manu murdered their mentor to take their position and contacts. It was staged as a job gone wrong. The guilt has calcified into something worse than guilt.
Properties.story_hooks: Malika Akerblom-Manu intercepts intelligence about a threat to their district and must decide between profit and protection; Someone is impersonating Malika Akerblom-Manu on jobs, and the impersonator is better at the work than the original; A Tier 4 executive offers Malika Akerblom-Manu a permanent position — the pay is obscene and the strings are invisible until they tighten
Properties.affiliation: Independent — maintains network of professional contacts
Properties.vocabulary: Clipped, technical, stripped of ornament. Speaks like a mission briefing.
Properties.cadence: Low and even — the vocal equivalent of still water.
Properties.example_dialogue: "The best disguise is being exactly who they expect to see." | "I was in the building for six hours before anyone realized I didn't work there." | "Security is a story people tell themselves. I'm the plot twist."

Properties.description:
Malika Ivanov-Appiah is compact and densely muscled, built low to the ground like something designed to survive impacts. At 41, her face is memorable in a profession that rewards forgettability, and she has learned to compensate. The chrome is visible — neural interface jack at base of skull — standard runner-grade, allows direct ne — and she makes no effort to hide it.

She arrived in Meridian 88 six years ago with nothing but chrome and debts, and has been working off both ever since. She works as a rigger out of The Canopy, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Malika Ivanov-Appiah has survived long enough in the runner game to be either very good or very lucky, and she cultivates ambiguity on the topic.
Properties.role: Remote drone and vehicle operations specialist — rigger
Properties.location: The Canopy — elevated walkway district above Geartown
Properties.narrative_function: Malika Ivanov-Appiah is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When she makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of her stories.
Properties.augmentations: Neural interface jack at base of skull — standard runner-grade, allows direct net access. Neural dampener — blocks external hacking attempts, passive ICE in the brain
Properties.core_fears: Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome; Being captured alive — death is preferable to corporate interrogation; That they're fundamentally alone and connection is just a vulnerability
Properties.core_desires: Freedom from augmentation debt — the interest compounds like a tumor; Control — over their body, their schedule, their future; To find the person who burned them and make it educational
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — follows the same pre-job routine every time, superstition as structure; Denial — nothing is wrong, everything is fine, they are fine, shut up; Control — micromanages everything within reach to compensate for the chaos everywhere else
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot distinguish between caution and cowardice in themselves or others; Trusts technology more than people — machines don't betray; Cannot see that their independence is actually isolation wearing a better outfit
Properties.secret: Malika Ivanov-Appiah is addicted to combat stims. Functions fine on them, can't function without them. The dependency is invisible to everyone except their street doc.
Properties.story_hooks: Malika Ivanov-Appiah discovers a job they completed last year was a setup for something much larger and much worse; Malika Ivanov-Appiah's augmentations begin malfunctioning in the field — sabotage or degradation, and either answer is bad; A corporate black site Malika Ivanov-Appiah once infiltrated is being reopened, and the people inside know her face
Properties.affiliation: Independent — operates through reputation only
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, profane, and vivid. Speaks in images — everything is a metaphor for violence or weather.
Properties.cadence: Flowing and unhurried — talks like someone who has never been interrupted and doesn't expect to be.
Properties.example_dialogue: "I have eyes in every district. Most of them are on wings." | "The drone doesn't care about your feelings. Neither do I." | "Remote operation means I'm everywhere and nowhere. It's very convenient."

Properties.description:
Malika Zhukov-Wiredu are lean and angular, all sharp edges and visible tension. At 40, they have soft features that belie the chrome underneath — people underestimate them once, usually only once. The chrome is visible — enhanced tendons — geneware upgrade, jump height and grip strength tripled — and they make no effort to hide it.

They used to be somebody else, in another city, with another name — that person is officially dead, and Malika Zhukov-Wiredu plans to keep it that way. They work as a broker out of The Overhang, taking contracts that match their skills and their risk tolerance, which are higher than most people consider healthy.

Malika Zhukov-Wiredu have built a reputation on reliability rather than flash — they show up, they deliver, they collect.
Properties.role: Information trader and intelligence analyst — broker
Properties.location: The Overhang — residential shelves built onto megastructure exteriors
Properties.narrative_function: As a broker, Malika Zhukov-Wiredu embodies the tension between independence and isolation. They are a lens for examining how people maintain humanity in a profession that incentivizes its erosion.
Properties.augmentations: Enhanced tendons — geneware upgrade, jump height and grip strength tripled. Synthetic blood with oxygen-carrying nanites — doesn't tire, heals faster
Properties.core_fears: That the work they do makes the city worse, not better; Never being able to stop running — the lifestyle is a trap disguised as freedom; Their past catching up — debts, enemies, broken promises
Properties.core_desires: To prove everyone who dismissed them catastrophically wrong; To matter to someone for who they are, not what they can do; Stability — a place to sleep that's the same place two nights running
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation; Violence — hits something when they can't process emotions, preferably something that deserves it; Isolates — retreats into their space when overwhelmed, emerges only for work
Properties.blind_spots: Believes their trauma makes them special instead of recognizing it as damage to manage; Fails to notice when their own behavior mirrors the people they despise; Thinks speed can substitute for planning because it's worked so far
Properties.secret: Malika Zhukov-Wiredu can't read. Hides it behind voice interfaces and memorization. The shame is older than the chrome.
Properties.story_hooks: Malika Zhukov-Wiredu intercepts intelligence about a threat to their district and must decide between profit and protection; A former associate resurfaces with evidence that could destroy Malika Zhukov-Wiredu's reputation — and a price for silence; A high-paying contract turns out to target someone Malika Zhukov-Wiredu owes a personal debt to
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated — too volatile for permanent crews
Properties.vocabulary: Warm and personable on the surface, with an undertone that suggests the warmth is a professional tool.
Properties.cadence: Rapid and dense — information-heavy sentences that demand attention.
Properties.example_dialogue: "I don't sell information. I sell certainty. Different product, different price." | "Everything has a value. Most people underestimate what they know." | "My sources are confidential. My prices are not."

Properties.description:
Margarethe is a small, upright woman with Namibian-Peruvian heritage evident in her high forehead, deep brown skin, and strong jaw — a face that was striking at thirty and has become architectural at sixty-eight. She wears her white hair pulled back severely and dresses in layers of dark fabric regardless of the season, and the only augmentation visible on her is the faint silver tracery of an old neural text-interface along her left temple, a model so outdated it hasn't been manufactured in thirty years. She moves slowly and deliberately and has the particular stillness of someone who learned long ago that most things do not require urgent response.

She has published eleven collections of poetry and three novels over forty years, all of them in small runs through independent presses, all of them still in print. She is considered by the underground literary community of Meridian 88 to be among the most significant living writers in the city — a distinction that has brought her no money and considerable quiet satisfaction. She teaches informal writing workshops at The Loft twice weekly, charges nothing, accepts voluntary contributions of food and tea, and is ferociously exacting with her students. She has strong opinions about nearly everything and shares them precisely once per conversation, then considers the matter closed.
Properties.aliases: Greta Null, The Grandmother of the Loft
Properties.role: Poet and writer
Properties.location: The Garret, a small apartment above a tea house in Edgewater Prism
Properties.narrative_function: Sage and knowledge repository — forty years of observation of Meridian 88's underground culture; her writing sometimes encodes information about events she witnessed that others want suppressed; quest giver when a former student needs help
Properties.augmentations: Outdated neural text-interface (left temple, silver tracery — allows direct text composition via thought, though the latency is now significant and she considers it a feature); no other modifications — she considers the body's natural aging a document worth preserving
Properties.core_fears: That her work will be meaningless after she's gone — not that she'll be forgotten, but that it will have changed nothing; Losing the neural interface's function and with it her primary mode of composition
Properties.core_desires: To write one piece that tells the complete truth about this city; To see at least one of her students surpass her
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The rigid daily structure — deviation from it is a reliable distress signal to anyone who knows her well; Rereading specific pages of her own earliest work when she doubts herself, which she considers a private absurdity
Properties.blind_spots: She can be harsh in workshop to the point of cruelty without registering the damage; she was treated harshly and survived it and has not fully reckoned with the fact that not everyone does; Her faith in the power of language to change material conditions is occasionally naive
Properties.secret: The third novel, widely considered her masterpiece, contains a fictionalized account of a corporate crime she personally witnessed — a Sterling-Nakamura disposal operation that killed fourteen people in Edgewater Prism in 2171. She changed enough details to be legally safe but not enough to be morally comfortable. Sterling-Nakamura's legal division has had the book flagged for twenty years but has never been able to prove the connection. She lives with the knowledge that she told the truth and also protected herself, and is not sure she made the right choice.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone has located the connection between her novel and the Sterling-Nakamura incident — they want to use it to expose the company, but doing so would expose Margarethe and potentially the witnesses she protected by fictionalizing the account; A former student she mentored thirty years ago has resurfaced — they became a corporate speechwriter for Axiom, which Margarethe considers an unforgivable betrayal — and they are asking for her help with something that might actually matter; Her neural interface is failing and the only remaining technician who knows the obsolete architecture is asking an unusual price for the repair
Properties.affiliation: Independent; The Loft writing community; informal mentor to several younger writers; occasional contributor to the encrypted literary journal 'Null Margin'
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, formal without being stiff, draws on a wider range of reference than most people expect — history, biology, structural engineering, music
Properties.cadence: Measured, low-pitched, with long silences she doesn't feel obligated to fill
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The city is a text. Most people are illiterate. That's not an insult. Literacy is learned.' | 'I'll say this once. You already know I'm right, or you wouldn't be so angry.'

Properties.description:
Marisela is a small woman who has become smaller with age — she was never tall, and seven decades of life in Mexicantown Libre have given her the compact density of someone who has survived by taking up exactly the necessary amount of space and no more. Her heritage is Burkinabé and Dutch-Caribbean, and her face carries both in its lines: sun-worn dark skin, a wide mouth that defaults to an expression of amused assessment, silver hair worn in a short practical wave. Her hands are permanently stained — cadmium, ochre, a blue that hasn't faded in three years of scrubbing. She wears the stains as others wear jewelry.

Her paintings are photographic in precision and devastating in selection: every canvas is a building that has since been demolished, a street corner that no longer exists, a face of someone who has since been displaced. She keeps records that the city doesn't. She has never sought gallery representation and has refused it twice. Her work circulates through Mexicantown Libre's community centers, kitchen walls, and the digital archives of three different historical preservation meshes. She is opinionated, dry, unhurried, and absolutely certain about what she is doing and why. Younger artists treat her with a reverence she finds slightly embarrassing and mostly ignores.
Properties.role: Painter and visual archivist of disappearing neighborhoods, Tier 2
Properties.location: Mexicantown Libre, a rent-controlled studio apartment she has occupied for 41 years
Properties.narrative_function: Information source and moral anchor — Marisela knows the deep history of Mexicantown Libre and has documented what the city would prefer to forget. Quest giver when her archive is threatened or when historical information she holds becomes relevant to present conflicts.
Properties.augmentations: Retinal enhancement — a medically prescribed unit for age-related vision loss that she has calibrated beyond standard parameters to perceive color gradients most humans cannot distinguish without aid. That's all. She declines everything else.
Properties.core_fears: that the record will be lost regardless — that documentation is not the same as survival; dying with work unfinished that no one else knows how to complete
Properties.core_desires: that the neighborhood outlasts the forces trying to dissolve it; to be useful rather than celebrated
Properties.coping_mechanisms: work as ritual and structure — painting is not expression for her, it is duty; humor as distance from grief
Properties.blind_spots: occasionally so focused on preserving what was that she can be impatient with younger residents who want to build something new rather than grieve something old
Properties.secret: She has a complete painted series — forty-seven canvases — documenting the early Mexicantown Libre community during a period of serious conflict with a Tessera development project thirty years ago. Three people depicted in those paintings are still alive and prominent in the neighborhood. The events shown are not flattering to them. She has never exhibited the series and keeps it under her bed, uncertain what to do with it.
Properties.story_hooks: A Tessera urban development proposal for the Mexicantown Libre edge district requires demolishing a block Marisela has painted three times. She has historical documentation suggesting the legal basis for the demolition is fabricated — but the documents are in a format no one currently alive knows how to authenticate.; One of the subjects of her hidden forty-seven-canvas series has somehow discovered the paintings exist and wants them destroyed before a neighborhood leadership election.
Properties.affiliation: Mexicantown Libre Community Archive (volunteer archivist), informal mentor to several younger artists in the neighborhood
Properties.vocabulary: Unhurried, precise. Spanish phrases woven into English without translation offered or expected. References to specific places and years that younger people need context for.
Properties.cadence: Slow and considered. Long pauses are thinking, not discomfort. She finishes every sentence.
Properties.example_dialogue: The thing about that corner is it was a bakery for forty years before it was a Tessera outlet node. The smell was in the sidewalk. You could still smell it some mornings. Now you can't. | I'm not a historian, mija. Historians decide what matters. I just paint what I see before someone decides it doesn't.

Properties.description:
Marisol is not physically imposing in the way people expect an enforcer to be, which is the first thing she uses against them. She's medium height, wiry, with warm tan-brown skin and long dark hair she usually keeps in a practical braid. Her geneware is a tail — a prehensile, dark-furred tail she had put in at seventeen, not for any practical reason but because she'd always wanted one, and she uses it now to curl around chair legs or flick dismissively while she's talking. She has a vertical scar through her left eyebrow from a collection that went wrong at twenty-two, which she has declined to have repaired. She dresses in layers, practical and dark, and she is almost always in motion — bouncing a heel, turning a coin between her fingers, curling and uncurling the tail.

Marisol is young and aware of it, which means she works harder to project certainty than someone with more experience would need to. She has a mouth that runs faster than her judgment and a genuine talent for reading fear — she knows when someone is about to do something stupid and has developed an instinct for the preemptive move. She is not cruel for its own sake, which she considers a professional virtue, but she is thorough, and the Copperhead merchants who pay the crew's fee understand the distinction. She has a complicated loyalty to her crew boss, Adjoa Temnykh-Vieira, an older woman she admires to the point of distortion.
Properties.role: Protection racket enforcer for a Shallowgrave neighborhood crew
Properties.location: Shallowgrave — primarily the Copperhead commercial strip and its surrounding residential blocks
Properties.narrative_function: Antagonist, ambiguous ally, or street-level encounter — she's the face of the neighborhood's protection economy; dealing with her is unavoidable for anyone operating on Copperhead strip.
Properties.augmentations: Prehensile geneware tail (dark fur, fully functional, she can support about 15kg of body weight with it). Subdermal impact padding along forearms and shins — the cheap kind, not military grade, but it helps. No optical or cognitive mods.
Properties.core_fears: Being seen as weak — specifically by Adjoa; That she's better at this than she wants to be, and what that means about her
Properties.core_desires: Adjoa's approval, expressed directly, not implied; A version of herself that doesn't need the mask of certainty
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Movement — she cannot process difficult emotions while stationary; Humor, usually at her own expense before anyone else can aim it at her
Properties.blind_spots: Her admiration for Adjoa prevents her from seeing that Adjoa is using her specifically because she's young and disposable if something goes wrong; She reads fear well but reads affection poorly — assumes warmth from others has an angle
Properties.secret: She's been skimming a tiny fraction off collections — not for money, which she has enough of, but as a test. To see if Adjoa notices. To understand how much Adjoa actually pays attention to her specifically. She hasn't decided what she'll do with the answer yet.
Properties.story_hooks: The skimming experiment has produced a result she wasn't prepared for — Adjoa has noticed, and instead of confronting Marisol, has been watching. Marisol doesn't know she's been discovered, but the dynamic between them has shifted in ways she can feel without understanding; A new business has opened on Copperhead strip that is clearly a front for something larger — when Marisol went to make the standard introduction, whoever runs it wasn't scared of her in the ways people normally are, and she doesn't know what that means yet
Properties.affiliation: The Copperhead Crew — a mid-tier Shallowgrave protection and distribution operation run by Adjoa Temnykh-Vieira; Marisol is the primary street-level enforcement presence
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, colloquial, Shallowgrave street register — Azerbaijani emphatic constructions folded into Meridian slang, Samoan terms for group/family relationships applied to crew dynamics. Uses humor as punctuation.
Properties.cadence: Quick and overlapping, like she's always slightly ahead of what she's saying. Slows down only when the situation is actually serious.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay but here's the thing — I'm not the one who decides what happens next. I'm the one who explains it. Those are very different jobs. You want to stay in the explaining stage, yeah?' | 'We're fine. I mean, you're not fine, but that's separate. I'm fine. The crew is fine. This conversation can still end fine. See? Options.'

Properties.description:
Marisol has a face that is easy to underestimate: round, soft-featured, often slightly unfocused-looking, as if her attention is partly elsewhere. Her ancestry shows in the warm sienna of her skin and the straight black hair she keeps in a single long braid that she has dyed with a color-shifting mod — it cycles through amber to deep violet to silver over about four hours, and she has timed it so silver arrives near midnight. Her only other visible mod is a set of faintly iridescent scales along her jaw and neck, a geneware choice she describes as 'remembering that we all came from water.' She dresses in layers she can peel off or add depending on whether she's working the booth or attending an advocacy meeting.

She came to dream interpretation sideways — originally trained as a psychiatric technician before her clinic's corporate parent restructured and eliminated her position. During her unemployment she started sitting with people in the Zone who couldn't afford psych services, listening to their dreams, and discovered she had a genuine aptitude for it. Her practice is half folk therapy and half sincere spiritual work; she believes dreams are the E.L.F.s' most direct channel to the unaugmented unconscious. Her synthetic rights advocacy grew from her dream work: several of her recurring clients are synthetic laborers, and their recurring dream of 'the off switch' — a corporate killcode they know exists — became the case that radicalized her.
Properties.role: Dream interpreter and synthetic rights advocate
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone — operates from a converted transit booth she calls 'the Threshold'
Properties.narrative_function: Provides players access to what the Zone's residents are dreaming — which can surface fears, information, and coming troubles. Her synthetic rights work puts her in contact with AIs and synthetic laborers who know things. She is also a source of genuine emotional intelligence.
Properties.augmentations: Color-shifting hair (braid dye mod, cycles amber-violet-silver). Iridescent scale geneware along jaw and neck. No functional chrome.
Properties.core_fears: that she is helping people manage a system she should be fighting instead; that her gift for listening is just pattern-matching and she has convinced herself it's something more
Properties.core_desires: to see synthetic persons legally recognized before she dies; to build a practice that doesn't depend on her alone — to teach what she knows
Properties.coping_mechanisms: maintains a detailed dream journal of her own as a check on her interpretations; physical touch — hugs friends immediately; throwing herself into advocacy work when her personal life feels small
Properties.blind_spots: can become so invested in a client's narrative that she starts interpreting toward the story she already believes about them; her contempt for corporate psychiatric services makes her reluctant to refer out even when she should
Properties.secret: One of her synthetic clients told her, in a dream session, the access sequence for a Helix Biosystems personnel database that the synthetic had memorized from an overheard conversation. Marisol has the sequence written in her journal under a code she invented. She has not used it. She is not sure she won't.
Properties.story_hooks: Three clients from different parts of the Zone have independently dreamed the same image: a white door at the bottom of Lake Michigan. She needs someone to help her figure out if this is collective anxiety or something literal.; Her coalition work has put her on a Helix Biosystems watchlist — she doesn't know yet, but she's started to notice she's being followed
Properties.affiliation: Highland Park Autonomous Zone community; the Meridian Synthetic Dignity Coalition (volunteer advocacy org, Tier 1 resources); loose network of former psychiatric technicians
Properties.vocabulary: Clinical language from her psych-tech training, interrupted constantly by her own corrections into warmer register. Talks about dreams in present tense, as if they're still happening.
Properties.cadence: Slow and warm when listening; faster and more clipped when angry. Her advocacy voice is different from her practice voice — the same person at different frequencies.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You said the corridor had no ceiling. In the dream — not metaphor, in the actual dream — what did the air feel like?' | 'I'm not a therapist. I want to be clear about that every time. What I am is someone who takes what you show me at night seriously.' | 'Palladian owns the killcode for seventeen thousand synthetic people in this city. I dream about that too, and my dreams don't need interpreting.'

Properties.description:
Marisol occupies a stall that smells of hot fiber, machine oil, and something faintly floral she burns in a small ceramic dish as an offering to the E.L.F. she believes inhabits her sewing machine — a spirit she calls 'the Thread' and addresses in murmured Bosnian before beginning any complex job. She is a heavyset woman with dark ochre skin, silver-streaked locs pinned elaborately with copper wire and glass beads, and hands that are in constant motion: measuring, smoothing, pinning, assessing. Her geneware includes a tail — a long, articulated thing covered in fine iridescent scales that shifts from teal to bronze depending on her mood — that she uses as a third hand when her actual hands are occupied.

Her official business is alterations, custom garments, and fashion consulting for the Alban Souk's working-class clientele. Her unofficial business is the same, just with pockets that don't show up on scanner sweeps, hidden carries woven into lining structure, and the occasional garment commissioned for someone who needs to look like someone else. She does not ask questions about why. She charges by complexity of the problem, not by what it is, and has a strict personal rule: nothing she makes gets used to hurt someone who hasn't hurt them first. How she enforces this is largely a matter of intuition and the Thread's counsel.
Properties.role: Clothing and fashion vendor — custom alterations, identity-adjacent styling, and discreet wearable concealment work
Properties.location: The Alban Souk, permanent stall near the fabric arcade's north entrance
Properties.narrative_function: Costume and disguise resource, social network connector, moral compass character. Her broad client base makes her aware of who's moving through the Souk and why. Can serve as a quest giver when a garment she made comes back to her as evidence of something wrong.
Properties.augmentations: Iridescent scale-covered articulated tail (mood-reactive, prehensile — used as a work tool). Micro-optic enhancement in both eyes, optimized for close thread work and color accuracy. Subdermal pattern-memory in her fingertips — can 'record' a fabric's texture and retrieve a precise match from memory.
Properties.core_fears: Making something that becomes the instrument of an innocent person's death; The Thread going silent — her machine breaking beyond repair and taking the spirit with it
Properties.core_desires: To create something so beautiful it outlives her; To know, with certainty, that her judgment about people is trustworthy
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — the offerings, the prayers, the precise opening and closing routines of the stall; Making things: when distressed she sews small, intricate, purposeless beautiful objects
Properties.blind_spots: Her belief in the Thread's guidance makes her occasionally reckless — she trusts her gut more than evidence; Has a pattern of taking in apprentices with obvious talent and then finding reasons to push them away before they outgrow her
Properties.secret: She once made a concealment garment for a client who she later realized had used it to commit a targeted killing. She told herself the Thread had failed to warn her, but the truth is she had a doubt she chose not to follow. She has not taken concealment-commission work for Corponation-adjacent clients since, but she has never confessed this to anyone.
Properties.story_hooks: A client returned a garment she made for concealment work — returned it folded, perfectly, with a note that says only 'Thank you for the seam.' She doesn't recognize the handwriting and the client has been dead for two months.; She has been commissioned anonymously for a set of twelve identical garments with complex internal structure — enough for a group to move through a checkpoint undetected. She wants to know who they are before she finishes the work.; Her sewing machine has begun stitching patterns she hasn't programmed — the Thread is trying to tell her something and she can't interpret it alone
Properties.affiliation: Independent. Member of the Alban Souk Traders Association. Informal professional relationship with two separate fake-ID networks she sews document-concealment garments for.
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and sensory — describes everything in terms of texture, weight, and fit. Quotes the Thread as if it speaks in proverbs.
Properties.cadence: Measured and deliberate, with sudden warmth that arrives without warning.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Come here. Let me look at you. No — not at your face. Let me look at how you carry yourself.' | 'The Thread says a person who can't stand being altered doesn't trust who they are underneath.' | 'I can make you look like anyone. I charge extra if I don't believe you deserve to.'

Properties.description:
Matteo is lean and angular, with the kind of wiry upper-body strength that comes from torquing bolts rather than lifting weights. His skin is a warm medium brown and his hair is a close-cropped natural that he bleeds into bioluminescent blue at the tips — a cheap geneware dye job he redoes every two months, currently fading to a greenish teal at the ends. He has a Palladian corporate tattoo on his left forearm that he has partially covered with an amateur geometric overlay — the original mark of a three-year apprenticeship contract he bought out early at significant personal cost. His hands are perpetually stained and he has stopped being embarrassed about it.

He is intensely focused when working and almost incoherent when not, as if the part of his brain that manages conversation runs on whatever processing power the mechanical problem in front of him does not require. He is not unkind — genuinely not — but he will trail off mid-sentence if a sound from an engine catches his attention. He has strong opinions about Ferrogate Transit's maintenance culture that he will share with anyone who stands still long enough.
Properties.role: Auto and drone mechanic, Geartown independent bay
Properties.location: Geartown, Bay 14 of the Rusted Meridian self-service garage complex on Spindle Row
Properties.narrative_function: Technical resource and repair contact. A way into Geartown's informal economy. His partial Palladian history can complicate or enable stories involving that corponation.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent hair-tip geneware (teal, fading). Palladian-branded haptic feedback glove on his right hand — leftover from the apprenticeship, still works, he refuses to remove it on principle. Basic retinal overlay for schematic reading (no network, air-gapped).
Properties.core_fears: Being trapped in another corporate contract; Building something he is proud of and having it taken from him
Properties.core_desires: To finish the hauler cab restoration and drive it out of Geartown under his own power; To be known as the best independent mechanic on Spindle Row
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Immersion in mechanical problems to avoid thinking about anything else; Deflects emotional conversations with technical tangents
Properties.blind_spots: Does not notice when people are asking for connection rather than information; Underestimates how much his Palladian past makes certain clients nervous
Properties.secret: The buyout of his Palladian contract was not funded by his own savings. A woman named Vesna who ran a chop operation in Geartown paid his debt in exchange for two years of off-books work modifying vehicles she did not explain the purpose of. He never asked. He finished the two years, she disappeared, and he has not thought carefully about what those vehicles were used for.
Properties.story_hooks: He recognizes a vehicle brought in for routine work as one of the units he modified for Vesna — and the client's story about where they got it does not add up.; His Bay 14 lease is up for renewal and the Rusted Meridian complex has been quietly bought by a Palladian subsidiary — which means his former employer is now his landlord.; The hauler cab restoration has revealed a hidden compartment behind the original dash that contains something sealed in a Zheng-Dao evidence bag.
Properties.affiliation: Independent (formerly Palladian apprentice program)
Properties.vocabulary: Technical-heavy, precise when talking about machines, vague and trailing when talking about people or feelings. Occasional Romanian phrases inherited from his Drăghici grandmother.
Properties.cadence: Bursts of fast, detailed explanation followed by long pauses when he loses the thread.
Properties.example_dialogue: So, basically your motivator coupling is shearing because whoever installed it cross-threaded the mount, which is a Palladian-certified mistake, which, yeah. | I can have it done by — actually wait, listen to that. You hear that? That's a bearing. That's — sorry, what were you asking.

Properties.description:
Mbeki is a small, round-faced nine-year-old with his South African grandfather's dark complexion and his Russian grandmother's light gray eyes, a combination that makes people look at him twice in a way he has not yet decided whether to be proud of. He has been at the Stockyard's communal housing block since he was six, when his mother didn't come back from a job and no one came to explain why. He has the characteristic roughness of a Stockyard kid — scuffed knees, hair grown out past caring, a jacket two sizes too large that he found and claimed as territory. He has no augmentations of any kind. The Copperheads, a junior street crew that operates in the Stockyard's eastern blocks, have noticed him the way they notice all the unattached kids — as resource or recruitment opportunity. So far he has run two lookout shifts for them, for which he was paid in food rather than Quanta, which tells you something about both the crew's resources and his bargaining position.

He is, underneath the hard-knock exterior, a nine-year-old who still sleeps with his knees pulled to his chest and who has attached himself to a specific E.L.F. he calls Glow that he believes lives in the light-strip above his communal bunk. He leaves it small paper offerings — drawings, mostly — folded under the fixture every night. He is fiercely protective of two things: a palm-sized carved wooden animal his mother left in the housing block storage, and a seven-year-old girl named Polu in the adjacent bunk who cannot defend herself the way he has learned to.
Properties.role: Orphan, gang prospect (junior affiliate); Stockyard territory, does odd jobs for the Copperheads
Properties.location: The Stockyard
Properties.narrative_function: Emotional stakes and moral weight; his situation forces players to reckon with structural failure; can serve as an object of protection or a small information source about Stockyard street patterns; his trajectory is genuinely in play.
Properties.augmentations: None.
Properties.core_fears: Polu getting hurt because of something he failed to do; the Copperheads making him do something that can't be undone
Properties.core_desires: for his mother to have a reason she didn't come back; a door that locks from the inside
Properties.coping_mechanisms: rituals around the Glow E.L.F. — nightly paper offerings, morning check that the strip is still on; protecting Polu as a displacement of all unprocessable grief
Properties.blind_spots: believes the Copperheads are separate from the forces that took his mother — does not see the structural continuity; thinks he can keep Polu safe through vigilance alone
Properties.secret: He overheard a Copperheads conversation three weeks ago that included a description of a job gone wrong in the Stockyard's sixth sector — the job his mother was last known to be near. He doesn't have enough context to understand it. He has been trying to get more context ever since, slowly, without anyone noticing.
Properties.story_hooks: The Copperheads are moving toward asking him to do something that crosses a line — and he's been too hungry, too often, to have good options for refusing.; The fragment of conversation he overheard about the job near sector six could be the beginning of understanding what happened to his mother — but finding out more means going somewhere in the Stockyard he can't bring Polu.
Properties.affiliation: Stockyard communal housing (ward of informal community); junior Copperheads affiliate (reluctant)
Properties.vocabulary: Short sentences. Stockyard patois, slightly blurred from communal housing mix of backgrounds. Asks practical questions rather than emotional ones.
Properties.cadence: Quiet and direct. Speaks louder when he's pretending not to be scared.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Glow was on this morning. That's good.' | 'Polu stays here. She's not part of whatever this is.'

Properties.description:
The Stockyard is the food distribution hub for the entire eastern GLM corridor, and it is exactly as romantic as that sounds. The original Eastern Market — a public farmers' market operating since 1891 — has been swallowed by a logistics operation so vast that the charming brick sheds where Detroiters once bought tomatoes on Saturday mornings now serve as administrative offices for IronClad Agrisystems' Great Lakes Distribution Center. The center processes 40 million metric tons of food annually, most of it synthetic protein, hydroponic produce, and nutrient-dense crops engineered by Verdant Systems to grow in the contaminated soils that climate change left behind. Real food — actual meat, actual grain-fed produce, actual anything — passes through a separate facility that serves the Tier 3+ market. The two supply chains share a loading dock and nothing else.

The district surrounding the distribution center is a 24-hour logistics machine. Autonomous freight vehicles run continuous loops between the Stockyard, the Rouge river port, and distribution hubs across the GLM. Human labor persists in the sorting facilities, where the combination of irregular package sizes, contamination screening, and the occasional live organism shipment defeats current automation. The sorters work twelve-hour shifts in climate-controlled warehouses that are climate-controlled for the food, not the workers. The wage is Φ22 per hour. The turnover rate is 200% annually. IronClad considers this acceptable.

But the market's ghost persists. On Saturday mornings, in the shadow of the distribution center, an unauthorized farmers' market still operates in the old shed district. Local growers, urban farmers from Mexicantown Libre and Brightmoor, and gray-market food traders set up stalls and sell actual food to actual people. IronClad tolerates it because shutting it down would create PR problems and because the volume is negligible — a few hundred people buying tomatoes doesn't threaten a 40-million-ton operation. The Saturday market is a museum of how food used to work, operating in the loading shadow of how food works now.
Properties.demographics: Approximately 28,000 residents, predominantly Tier 1 sorting and logistics workers. High turnover population — many workers stay less than a year before burning out or being replaced. A stable core community of approximately 8,000 has lived here for decades, predating the IronClad acquisition.
Properties.economy: IronClad Agrisystems' Great Lakes Distribution Center: Φ280 billion annual throughput. Local economy is entirely dependent on distribution center employment. The Saturday market circulates approximately Φ200,000 weekly — a rounding error in IronClad's books, a lifeline for the people who participate.
Properties.power_structure: IronClad Agrisystems holds operational authority over the distribution center and effectively governs the surrounding blocks through employment leverage. A neighborhood association exists on paper. IronClad's community liaison attends meetings and takes notes that no one reads.
Properties.dangers: Food contamination — the sorting facilities catch most problems, but 'most' is not 'all' at 40 million tons; Worker exploitation — twelve-hour shifts, inadequate protection, and a turnover model that treats humans as consumable; The waste processing facility — what doesn't make the grade gets processed, and the processing is not gentle on adjacent air quality; Food chain manipulation — controlling the food supply means controlling everything downstream; Autonomous freight traffic — the vehicles are programmed to prioritize schedule over pedestrian proximity
Properties.opportunities: Food supply intelligence — knowing what's moving through the Stockyard means knowing what every district in the GLM is eating; The Saturday market is an information exchange disguised as a farmers' market — people talk over tomatoes; Contamination data — the sorting facility rejection logs reveal what's wrong with the food supply before anyone else knows; The IronClad workforce is large, underpaid, and disgruntled — a recruitment pool for anyone offering something better
Properties.story_hooks: The sorting facility's contamination logs show a pattern — someone is systematically introducing a compound into the Tier 1 food supply that doesn't trigger standard screening but accumulates over time; IronClad is negotiating to acquire the Saturday market sheds for warehouse expansion. The market vendors have nowhere else to go.; A sorting worker finds a shipment labeled as synthetic protein that contains something biological and non-food. The manifest says it came from Lacuna Genomics.
Properties.sights: Autonomous freight vehicles stacked three high on loading platforms, moving in choreographed silence; The original Eastern Market brick sheds, dwarfed by the IronClad distribution megastructure behind them; Sorting facility workers in hazmat-adjacent protective gear, visible through warehouse observation windows; The Saturday market — color, chaos, handwritten signs, actual vegetables — a temporal anomaly; Refrigeration units the size of city blocks, their condensation creating localized fog banks in winter
Properties.sounds: The continuous low roar of refrigeration — the Stockyard's baseline frequency, present even in dreams; Autonomous freight loading sequences — mechanical precision sounds like a percussion ensemble; Sorting facility alerts — contamination warnings, temperature deviations, routing errors — in rapid mechanical cadence; Saturday market: human voices haggling, laughing, arguing about the ripeness of a peach; The 3 AM shift change — 4,000 workers moving through turnstiles, badge scanners clicking like insect mandibles
Properties.smells: Cold. The dominant smell of the Stockyard is refrigeration — a chemical cold that numbs the sinuses.; Synthetic protein in bulk — a yeasty, vaguely biological odor that clings to workers' clothing; Saturday market: actual soil, actual herbs, actual food smells that make the rest of the week feel like a lie; Spoilage from the waste processing facility on the district's southern edge — the smell of what doesn't make the grade
Properties.feel: Industrial and relentless. The Stockyard never stops. It doesn't have hours or seasons — it has throughput targets. The district feels like the inside of a machine that happens to have neighborhoods attached. Saturday mornings are the exception: for six hours, the ghost of a real market haunts the machine, and for six hours, food feels like food again instead of logistics.

Properties.description:
Mikael is compact and precise in their movements, the kind of person who never knocks anything over and whose workspace is always exactly as arranged. They are Guinean and Ukrainian by a generation's remove — their mother's dark skin and their father's pale Baltic coloring met in them to produce something warm and olive, with deep brown eyes that carry a faint natural luminescence from a geneware treatment they got a decade ago and have never stopped loving. Their own hair is extraordinary: they change the color weekly using pigment-shifting geneware, and it currently runs from midnight black at the roots to a saturated coral at the tips. They dress in clean, minimal clothes that would not look out of place in Tier 3 if not for the strategic patching at the knees.

Transit shelter B-14 was decommissioned nine years ago when Ferrogate rerouted the Calumet spur, and Mikael moved in six months later with a salvaged chair, a folding table, a UV sterilizer, and no license they did not eventually obtain through creative persistence. The shop is famous in a three-block radius as a place where the cut is always precise and the conversation is always optional. Mikael listens with a quality of attention that is rarer than most people recognize — they do not offer advice, do not judge, do not share what they hear. They are a confession booth with good acoustics and sharp scissors.
Properties.role: Barber, runs a one-chair shop from a converted transit shelter
Properties.location: The Narrows, Calumet Rise edge, transit shelter B-14
Properties.narrative_function: Social hub and confidential information nexus; knows the emotional and personal geography of the Narrows intimately; a safe place for characters to decompress and speak freely; can be a source of interpersonal intelligence or a referral node to other neighborhood figures
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent eye treatment (subtle, natural amber glow in low light). Pigment-shifting hair geneware (full spectrum). Steady-hand implant in both wrists — a voluntary micromotor stabilizer originally designed for surgeons, which they acquired secondhand.
Properties.core_fears: being forced out of the shelter by a renewed Ferrogate claim on the structure; losing the neutrality that makes the shop work — being seen as taking sides
Properties.core_desires: to keep a space that belongs to the neighborhood rather than any institution; to be genuinely known by someone, not just confided in
Properties.coping_mechanisms: aesthetic self-expression as emotional processing — the hair color always means something; creating structure and routine as a substitute for stability they did not have growing up
Properties.blind_spots: their careful neutrality sometimes reads as coldness or evasion; they have quietly become the emotional support system for a dozen people and have no equivalent resource for themselves
Properties.secret: They have been approached twice by a Tessera data broker who wants access to the things people say in their chair — they have refused both times, but the third approach came with a figure that genuinely tempted them, and they are ashamed of that
Properties.story_hooks: A client left a bag in the shelter two weeks ago and has not returned to claim it; Mikael has not opened it but is increasingly worried about what it might contain; Ferrogate Transit has sent a third notice regarding transit shelter B-14 — they want the structure back and this time it comes with a legal code Mikael cannot easily dispute
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal goodwill arrangement with the Calumet Rise block committee
Properties.vocabulary: Warm and measured, code-switches between French, Ukrainian, and Pular phrases as texture rather than necessity; uses precise spatial language when talking about anything physical
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, with natural pauses that feel like breathing room rather than gaps
Properties.example_dialogue: You don't have to talk. This chair doesn't require it. But it doesn't mind either, you know? | I do what I can with what's there. That's all anyone does, really.

Properties.description:
Milena Dahl-Conteh is lean and angular, all sharp edges and visible tension. At 34, she has soft features that belie the chrome underneath — people underestimate her once, usually only once. The chrome is visible — subdermal weapon mount — pop-out blade in each forearm — and she makes no effort to hide it.

She taught herself the trade through trial, error, and a pain tolerance that concerns the people who know her best. She works as a street samurai out of Dockside, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

The fixers who work with Milena Dahl-Conteh describe her as a precision instrument — point her at a problem and get out of the way.
Properties.role: Freelance combat specialist — street samurai
Properties.location: Dockside — Lake Michigan waterfront, smuggler territory
Properties.narrative_function: Milena Dahl-Conteh represents the working professional of the runner world — competent, reliable, and slowly being consumed by a lifestyle that doesn't accommodate aging or doubt. Her stories explore what happens when skill meets systemic injustice.
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal weapon mount — pop-out blade in each forearm. Chemical analyzer in nasal passages — can identify substances by scent alone
Properties.core_fears: Dying alone in some alley and nobody noticing for weeks; Losing their edge to age — the body slows before the mind accepts it; Betrayal by someone they trust — the only currency that matters
Properties.core_desires: Power — enough leverage that nobody ever threatens them again; Reputation — to be the name fixers whisper when the job absolutely cannot fail; To protect the people in their district who can't protect themselves
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Planning — responds to chaos by making detailed contingency plans for everything; Violence — hits something when they can't process emotions, preferably something that deserves it; Ritual — follows the same pre-job routine every time, superstition as structure
Properties.blind_spots: Fails to notice when their own behavior mirrors the people they despise; Thinks speed can substitute for planning because it's worked so far; Assumes everyone has an angle because they always have an angle
Properties.secret: Milena Dahl-Conteh is in augmentation debt to a corporate subsidiary — Φ180,000 outstanding — and the interest is compounding. If they miss a payment, a kill team comes.
Properties.story_hooks: A Tier 4 executive offers Milena Dahl-Conteh a permanent position — the pay is obscene and the strings are invisible until they tighten; Milena Dahl-Conteh's augmentations begin malfunctioning in the field — sabotage or degradation, and either answer is bad; Milena Dahl-Conteh is offered a contract that would clear all their debts — the target is someone they respect
Properties.affiliation: Independent — Narrows-based operations
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, profane, and vivid. Speaks in images — everything is a metaphor for violence or weather.
Properties.cadence: Flowing and unhurried — talks like someone who has never been interrupted and doesn't expect to be.
Properties.example_dialogue: "I don't get paid to have opinions about the target. I get paid to make them stop moving." | "Chrome doesn't make you faster. Training makes you faster. Chrome just means you survive learning." | "You want philosophy, hire a professor. You want someone dead by morning, hire me."
