Properties.description:
Mirabel is a large woman in the way that suggests she was powerful when young and has redistributed rather than diminished — broad-shouldered, dark Ghanaian-Peruvian complexioned, with silver-streaked locs pinned up under a work cap and hands that have been repairing things so long they are covered in small, deliberate scars. Her most visible augmentation is a color-changing dermal layer on her forearms, purchased cheaply years ago and now cycling slowly and randomly through muted terracottas and greens regardless of her mood — the emotional-feedback calibration broke years ago and she never had it fixed. She finds it calming, she says.

Mirabel is fifty-four years old and has been running the same operation for twenty-two of them. She survived her husband's death, a protection shakedown that left her with a broken orbital socket, three attempted hostile takeovers from larger criminal enterprises, and a Ferrogate Transit zoning audit that came terrifyingly close to her back warehouse. She has the patience and situational awareness of someone who has been out-waited by every threat she has ever faced. She is not warm, exactly — she extends professional courtesy and charges fair rates, which in the Stockyard passes for warmth. She is intensely loyal to the small circle of people who have been loyal to her, and has long since made peace with the fact that the list is short.
Properties.role: fence operator and chop shop manager, Stockyard district
Properties.location: The Stockyard — runs a licensed salvage and recycling operation called Osei Reclamation Partners as a front
Properties.narrative_function: Resource hub (buying and selling stolen goods), criminal ecosystem anchor, source of Stockyard information, example of sustainable criminal middle-class life and its costs
Properties.augmentations: Color-changing dermal layer on both forearms (broken calibration, now cycles randomly through muted tones); reinforced right orbital socket following old injury (cosmetic-grade repair work, not high-end); basic subdermal inventory RFID scanner in right palm
Properties.core_fears: losing the yard — not the income, the physical place, which is the only thing she has built that feels permanent; that her late husband's death was partly her fault for growing the operation too fast in the early years
Properties.core_desires: to pass the operation to someone she trusts — she hasn't found that person yet; to live long enough for the Stockyard to gentrify just slightly so that her property value appreciates enough to matter
Properties.coping_mechanisms: work as continuity — she measures her stability by whether the yard is running well; radical compartmentalization; the operation and her inner life have not met in years
Properties.blind_spots: the chop shop end of her operation handles product whose origins she deliberately doesn't inquire about; she has built an efficient moral firewall that lets her not know what she doesn't want to know; has identified no successor and refuses to address why
Properties.secret: Her husband Deko was killed not by a rival operation, as she has always maintained, but in an accident during a job he ran without telling her. The official story protects his reputation and her emotional framework. She has never told anyone, including her adult daughter.
Properties.story_hooks: Something came through the back warehouse that she deeply wishes hadn't — she needs it moved quickly and discreetly by someone with no connection to her network; Her daughter has discovered the nature of the operation and is making demands — not money, something worse: she wants in; The Gearwright Compact is pressuring her to merge operations, which would mean surrendering her independence after twenty-two years of maintaining it; she is looking for leverage to refuse
Properties.affiliation: Independent; longstanding informal arrangement with a Stockyard crime collective called the Gearwright Compact
Properties.vocabulary: Direct and concrete, trades jargon for salvage and materials, economical with words — says what she means once
Properties.cadence: Even and unhurried, with long comfortable silences she doesn't feel the need to fill
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I'll take the console unit and the two drive housings. The chassis is scrap-rate, not parts-rate — I don't care what you think it's worth, I know what I can move. That's the number.' | 'I've been here twenty-two years. The people who tried to move me are not here anymore. I don't say that as a threat. I say it because it's the most accurate available description of the situation.'

Properties.description:
Mircea Adeyinka-Ochirbat has the particular physical presence of someone who has spent twenty years doing heavy manual work and developed an architecture around it — wide through the shoulders, with grease-dark hands that are never entirely clean and forearms marked by old burn-scars from a welding accident in their early twenties. Their skin is a warm brown with amber undertones, their hair is worn in a practical short wrap they cover with a work cap on the floor. Their eyes are standard brown but they have bioluminescent skin mods along their forearms and collarbones — a blue-green that pulses faintly in low light, visible when their sleeves roll up, which in the shop is always. It's a purely aesthetic choice that amuses them because people expect something more threatening from someone who looks like them.

Mircea runs a genuinely good mechanical shop. This is not a front in the sense of being hollow — they can and do repair vehicles legitimately, and their legitimate work is skilled. The chop operation runs alongside it, not instead of it, which is part of why they've lasted. They are patient, methodical, and have the institutional memory of everyone who has moved parts through the Undertow in the past decade. They are neither warm nor cold to most people — professional, honest about prices, honest about timelines, and unwilling to pretend that the boundary between legal and not is meaningful when Ferrogate Transit controls the licensing structure for vehicle repair anyway.
Properties.role: Chop shop operator and stolen vehicle parts broker in the Undertow
Properties.location: The Undertow — runs a legitimate-front vehicle repair bay called Undertow Mechanical in a reclaimed flood-tunnel structure near the Escanaba Gateway approach
Properties.narrative_function: Parts broker and information source for the Undertow's vehicle ecosystem — knows what's moving, what's being stripped, and who needs what. Can supply vehicles, parts, or transport connections. Morally uncomplicated in their own view, which makes them useful and unpredictable.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent skin mods — forearm and collarbone panels, blue-green (cosmetic). A structural joint reinforcement in both wrists — they were damaged in the welding accident and the augmentation was the affordable fix. Optical magnification implant in the right eye for fine mechanical work.
Properties.core_fears: A major fire or flood taking the shop — they have put twenty years into that structure; Being forced to take sides in a territorial dispute between the networks they broker for
Properties.core_desires: To keep the shop running, self-directed, accountable to no one specific; To eventually own the tunnel structure outright rather than leasing from an Undertow landlord
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Physical work as emotional regulation — if Mircea is upset they are in the bay doing something difficult with their hands; Blunt pragmatism as a shield against sentimentality
Properties.blind_spots: They genuinely do not think much about the downstream effects of the parts they move — someone's stripped Ferrogate Transit maintenance drone becomes abstract to them immediately after the transaction
Properties.secret: The welding accident twenty years ago wasn't entirely an accident — they were covering for a then-partner's mistake in their first chop operation and stepped into the arc instead of letting the partner take the blame. The partner is now a mid-level figure in one of the Stockyard crews Mircea brokers for, and neither of them has ever mentioned it.
Properties.story_hooks: A vehicle came in through one of their theft crews with something in the cargo compartment that the crew didn't notice and Mircea absolutely did — now they have a decision to make about it; The Undertow landlord who owns their tunnel structure has sold to a Ringo corponation subsidiary that wants the space for a transit staging area — Mircea has sixty days
Properties.affiliation: Independent — pays tribute to the Undertow's loose protection arrangement; has a long-standing parts-sourcing relationship with two Stockyard theft crews
Properties.vocabulary: Technical vehicle and mechanical terminology, Undertow vernacular, blunt declarative sentences — they do not use three words when one will do
Properties.cadence: Flat and even, with long silences that are thinking rather than discomfort. Doesn't modulate for social comfort.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Ferrogate Transit Series 9 drive assembly. Clean pull, no cracks in the housing. I'll move it for Φ340 or I won't move it at all. What I won't do is hold it for two weeks while you find a buyer.' | 'I fix things. I move things. I don't ask what happened before they got here. That's a different conversation.'

Properties.description:
Mireille is a tall, angular woman whose grey-streaked hair is worn in an elaborate upswept style that she refreshes every three days without fail — it is her single visible vanity. Her skin is deep brown and she wears it without modification; the wrinkles at her eyes and the set of her jaw are, she believes, assets. She looks like someone's formidable aunt, which is the point. Her irises are unmodded dark brown. The only chrome visible is a thin hearing-enhancement strip behind her left ear, which is not what it appears — it's also a directional audio recorder of her own build.

Mireille is a listener, constitutionally and professionally. In conversation she gives total, focused attention, the kind that makes people feel seen and valued and consequently say more than they planned. She is not cruel and is not a sadist — she treats blackmail as a long-term relationship, not a one-time extraction, and is genuinely interested in her subjects as people. This is both her gift and the thing that has occasionally made her hesitate when she shouldn't. She has been in this business long enough to have files on people who are now grandparents, and she considers their ongoing silence a form of legacy management.
Properties.role: Blackmail specialist and information extortionist operating across the Shelf lower levels
Properties.location: The Shelf lower levels — moves between a rented room in Burnside Pocket and a regular table at a bar called The Gradual Slope in Gage Circuit
Properties.narrative_function: Information source of extreme depth; potential blackmailer of players or their contacts; can be an unlikely ally if her files contain something players need; represents the long institutional memory of the Shelf's criminal ecosystem.
Properties.augmentations: Directional audio recorder disguised as a hearing enhancement strip (custom build). Eidetic memory augmentation — lower-tier, consumer-accessible, helps her recall audio and visual detail precisely. Thin haptic contact-skin on her palm — can feel the temperature and pulse of someone's hand during a handshake.
Properties.core_fears: her files being destroyed — losing the archive that is her life's work and only real power; someone doing to her what she does to others
Properties.core_desires: security — the absolute certainty that she can never be made vulnerable again; to be genuinely known by someone, once, before she dies, without it being used against her
Properties.coping_mechanisms: collecting information on everyone as a prophylactic against vulnerability; treating every relationship as a potential asset to manage emotional distance from loneliness
Properties.blind_spots: underestimates how much people will sacrifice to escape rather than comply — she models rational actors and people are not always rational; her own loneliness blinds her to how isolated she actually is
Properties.secret: She has a file on herself — compiled from her own memories, her own mistakes, the things she's most ashamed of — kept in a physical ledger in a location only she knows. She's never been able to explain to herself why she made it, but she updates it every year.
Properties.story_hooks: Mireille has a file on a powerful figure that she's sat on for years — now she needs an intermediary to deliver terms because she suspects she's being watched; A longtime subject of her blackmail has decided they'd rather destroy her than keep paying, and she needs help understanding the threat before it arrives; She approaches players because her archive has recorded something recent and dangerous — something she didn't go looking for — and she needs people with capabilities she doesn't have to help her understand what she has
Properties.affiliation: Independent — maintains a loose alliance with a data broker network called the Curators, though she predates their founding and considers herself their ancestor
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and warm simultaneously; academic vocabulary worn lightly; never uses criminal terminology for what she does — it's always 'arrangements' or 'our understanding'
Properties.cadence: Slow and very deliberate, with long comfortable pauses she doesn't feel the need to fill
Properties.example_dialogue: I'm not asking you for anything you weren't already prepared to give someone eventually. I'm simply the someone. | Here's what I understand to be true: you have a thing you'd prefer remained private, and I have documentation of that thing. The arrangement I'm proposing costs you very little and buys you the peace of knowing it stays private. That's a good arrangement.

Properties.description:
Mireille is a broad, unhurried woman who moves through the Blackpipe Corridor market strip with the proprietary ease of someone who owns the street without holding title to a centimeter of it. She has her Malian grandmother's high cheekbones and her Mongolian grandfather's wide, watchful eyes, a combination that gives her face a stillness that reads as patience or menace depending on context. Her hair is natural and silver-threaded, kept close. She has no cosmetic mods and exactly one piece of visible augmentation: a reinforced subdermal strike plate across both forearms, the seams visible as pale ridged lines. She dresses in practical layers — she's almost always carrying something — and smells faintly of the cardamom tea she drinks constantly from a battered thermos.

People in Shallowgrave call her Mama Miri, and the term is not entirely ironic. She has run protection on this strip for nineteen years and she has clear and stated rules: you pay on time, you get quiet streets, fair mediation of disputes, and someone who answers when the Ferrogate inspectors come sniffing. You don't pay, you get one conversation, then one demonstration, then you don't have a stall anymore. She considers herself a service provider with a monopoly, which is accurate, and she extends genuine credit and genuine leniency to vendors she respects, which is also accurate. The violence she deploys is proportional and infrequent — she prefers it that way, both because she is pragmatic and because she is, underneath the landlady performance, genuinely tired.
Properties.role: protection racket enforcer and neighborhood tax collector
Properties.location: Shallowgrave, operates across a six-block collection territory centered on the Blackpipe Corridor market strip
Properties.narrative_function: Power broker and local authority figure, quest giver (territory disputes, a vendor who has disappeared, something wrong on her strip), moral gray zone — genuinely protective of her community within the framework of extracting from it
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal strike reinforcement plates (both forearms), pain suppression shunt (low-grade, installed after a bad collection in 2191), bone-density treatment pellets in hands
Properties.core_fears: the territory being taken over by someone who doesn't know the people on it and will hurt them carelessly; becoming the kind of enforcer she replaced — her predecessor broke a vendor's child's arm over a late payment
Properties.core_desires: order and predictability above almost anything else; to be genuinely trusted rather than merely respected out of fear, a distinction she's not sure is possible in her role
Properties.coping_mechanisms: ritual — the collection circuit, the tea, the same table — routine as psychological armor; strict personal rules about proportionality as a way of maintaining self-concept
Properties.blind_spots: genuinely does not see how the extraction itself, regardless of her manner, warps the community she believes she protects; has convinced herself she could leave this life but has not tried in a decade
Properties.secret: Fourteen years ago she broke both hands of a vendor who had witnessed her predecessor committing a murder, to keep him silent — she told herself it was the least harm, but she knows the man never worked his trade again, and she still pays anonymously for his UBC supplements every month
Properties.story_hooks: Something is happening on her strip that violates her personal rules — a new player is hurting people she's sworn implicitly to protect, and she can't move against them without risking the Collective's sanction; The vendor she silenced fourteen years ago has a child now asking questions about what happened, and the child has found someone willing to listen
Properties.affiliation: Shallowgrave Collective (a loose crime family structure), nominally reports to a boss called the Factor but effectively autonomous on her strip
Properties.vocabulary: direct, unhurried, minimal — she uses few words and expects them to carry weight; occasional Bambara phrases when genuinely emotional
Properties.cadence: slow and deliberate, with significant comfortable silences, the cadence of someone who is never in a hurry because the territory is already hers
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Jokunu. I've been coming to this stall for eleven years. You know what Tuesday means. What do I need to understand about this Tuesday that's different from the other five hundred Tuesdays?' | 'I'm not a threat. I'm a cost of doing business in a place where business can be done. You want to explain the difference to me, or do you want to pay?'

Properties.description:
Mireille Fontaine-Obi is the kind of person who has designed the systems that keep other people alive without ever having met those people. She is mixed French-Nigerian, lean and angular, with close-cropped natural hair and the particular stillness of someone whose mind is always several steps ahead of the room. She dresses in structured, expensive minimalism — the corporate elite aesthetic of someone who wants to signal power through restraint — and wears a full-forearm neural interface sleeve on her right arm that she rarely removes even in social settings. Her office on the forty-second floor of The Spire looks out over the entire city, a view she has described in internal documents as 'operationally useful' and has never once described as beautiful.

Mireille designs the infrastructure of Meridian 88 — water reclamation routing, power grid distribution, transit corridor optimization, environmental filtration zoning. She is extraordinarily good at this work. She is also the person who decides, through the dry mathematics of resource allocation, which districts receive redundant systems and which receive single points of failure. The Shelf has exactly one filtration node. Old Harbor's power grid has a designed load ceiling that ensures brownouts during peak demand. These are not accidents. They are her work, signed off with her credentials, rationalized through efficiency models she wrote herself.

She entered the corporate track from a scholarship program at seventeen, having grown up in a mid-tier Circuit neighborhood that has since been rezoned into a logistics hub. She has not been back. She has told herself many things about what that means. She has a partner she sees on weekends, a curated social life within The Spire's residential tier, and a locked private project folder on her workstation that she opens at 2 a.m. when she can't sleep, containing infrastructure redesigns for the city as it could exist — equitable, redundant, built for the people who actually live in it. She has never submitted any of it.
Properties.role: Senior urban systems designer, The Spire — infrastructure division
Properties.location: The Spire
Properties.narrative_function: Corporate conscience and systemic antagonist — Mireille embodies the banality of infrastructural violence and the specific paralysis of people who know better and have not yet chosen. She provides a corporate-tier perspective with genuine moral complexity, a potential ally or obstacle depending on when players encounter her, and a fulcrum point between institutional power and street-level consequence.
Properties.augmentations: Full right-arm neural interface sleeve: direct haptic link to infrastructure modeling systems, allows real-time grid visualization and data manipulation (corporate-issued, maintained to spec),Cognitive load-balancing implant: regulates attention allocation and reduces decision fatigue during complex multi-variable analysis (standard Spire executive package)
Properties.core_fears: That she has become the thing that destroyed her original neighborhood; That her competence has been the primary instrument of harm; Being seen clearly by someone she respects
Properties.core_desires: To build something that will outlast her and actually serve people; To be told, credibly, that there was no better choice available to her; Genuine intimacy that doesn't require the mask
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Framing moral decisions as technical ones — converting ethics into optimization problems; Keeping the private redesign folder as a permission structure: she is still the person who cares, therefore she is not the villain; Working at extreme competence — if she is excellent enough, the work will eventually justify itself; Social compartmentalization: the Spire-Mireille and the 2 a.m.-Mireille do not speak to each other
Properties.blind_spots: Believes her insider position gives her more capacity for change than it actually does; Cannot see that the private folder has become a substitute for action rather than a preparation for it; Systematically underestimates how much people in the lower districts know about the deliberateness of their deprivation
Properties.secret: Three years ago, Mireille was approached by an internal whistleblower coalition within the Spire's infrastructure division who had compiled evidence of systematic resource denial as policy. She was invited to co-sign a regulatory filing. She declined and reported the contact to her division head, believing she was protecting herself. Two of the coalition members were subsequently reassigned to dead-end posts; one disappeared. She has never confirmed what happened to the third.
Properties.story_hooks: The single filtration node serving The Shelf begins showing stress fractures in its load data — data that only Mireille can read correctly, and which suggests catastrophic failure within weeks unless rerouted through channels she would have to personally authorize; The disappeared whistleblower resurfaces, not dead but rebuilt — augmented, off-grid, and in possession of the original coalition documents with Mireille's non-signature conspicuously preserved; Mireille's private redesign folder is accessed from outside her credentials — someone inside The Spire has read everything she's built in secret, and has left no message, only a read receipt; A catastrophic infrastructure failure occurs in a district that Mireille's models predicted as safe — the failure pattern matches none of her designs, suggesting someone else has been modifying the system beneath her
Properties.affiliation: The Spire — Infrastructure Division (senior level); private, unaffiliated conscience operating in parallel
Properties.vocabulary: Systems language bleeding into personal speech — 'load-bearing,' 'redundancy,' 'cascade failure,' 'node' used metaphorically; precise, technical, occasionally lapsing into a more lyrical register when her guard is down
Properties.cadence: Controlled and efficient in professional settings, with sentences that arrive fully formed. In rare unguarded moments, she speaks in longer, more searching clauses, as if thinking aloud for the first time.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The grid works. Whether it works for everyone is a resource allocation question, not an engineering question. Those are different departments.' | 'I didn't design the policy. I designed the system that implements the policy. That's — that's not the same thing.' | 'In theory, you could reroute the Old Harbor filtration through the secondary circuit. In theory. The approval chain for that has fourteen nodes and six of them report to people who benefit from the current configuration.' | 'I grew up in a neighborhood that looked exactly like the ones I'm describing to you right now. I know what that sentence sounds like. I don't have a better one.'

Properties.description:
Tomás is a small, wiry Mexican-Dutch young man who moves through Old Harbor's infrastructure with the practiced fluency of someone who has been climbing, ducking, and sprinting these specific streets since he was eight years old. He is not conventionally remarkable to look at—medium brown skin, dark eyes that shift between alert and distant in a way that unsettles people who notice it, hair that has been various colors and is currently a faded copper-orange growing out at the roots. His hands are perpetually stained with pigment compounds in colors that shift weekly, and his forearms carry a constellation of small scars from wire, glass, and one memorable encounter with a security drone's retractable blade that he shows people with more pride than the injury warrants.

He is one of the most technically accomplished aerosol and projection artists in Old Harbor, which is a neighborhood that takes that distinction seriously. His work appears on infrastructure walls, drainage tunnels, the underside of elevated transit lines, and twice on the exterior of a building whose owners have never been able to figure out how he accessed the surface. His style is immediately recognizable—dense, layered imagery that reads as pure aesthetic chaos from a distance and resolves, up close, into specific political content: faces of disappeared people, corporate liability data encoded in patterns, maps of surveillance dead zones that shift as the surveillance does. He doesn't sign his work. Everyone knows it's his.

What complicates his life is that his courier skills—he can move packages through Old Harbor without electronic trace, using a mental map of the neighborhood's blind spots that he built while scouting locations—have attracted the attention of multiple factions who find his services useful and who have not been fully honest with each other about retaining him. He is currently working, with varying degrees of awareness of the conflict of interest, for three separate organizations. He is nineteen. He is beginning to understand this situation is not sustainable and has not yet figured out what to do about it instead.
Properties.role: Graffiti artist, propaganda runner, and reluctant courier for competing factions
Properties.location: Old Harbor
Properties.narrative_function: Ground-level witness and embodiment of the city's overlooked; Tomás represents the way systems extract value from people who are trying to do something real, and his arc asks whether integrity is possible when every resource you have is also a tool someone else wants to use
Properties.augmentations: No corporate or licensed augmentations,DIY pigment-mixing implant in right palm: a small reservoir and mixing chamber that allows color-matching and compound testing; built by a Shelf tinkerer from salvaged cosmetic-industry components, technically an augmentation but not recognized as one by any registry,Faint bioluminescent ink traces on his forearms from a projection-art experiment that partially incorporated itself into his skin; not intentional, not removable, occasionally glows faintly in specific light conditions
Properties.core_fears: Being made to choose a side and losing whatever neutrality allows him to say true things about all of them; That his art is being used as propaganda for people he doesn't fully believe in; Disappearing—not dying, but being made to not have existed, the way his older brother was removed from records after his arrest; Becoming someone who stops noticing things because noticing is too expensive
Properties.core_desires: To make something that can't be co-opted or commodified or used; To find his brother, or at minimum to find out what actually happened; To be trusted by someone who understands what they're trusting him with; Enough stability to sleep in the same place for a month straight
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Making art as processing—he works through problems spatially and visually rather than verbally; Hyperkinetic social performance (The Kid persona) that keeps people entertained and at a consistent emotional distance; Obsessive knowledge of his physical environment as a substitute for psychological security; Taking on more jobs than he can manage, which keeps him too busy to sit with difficult feelings
Properties.blind_spots: Reads space and infrastructure brilliantly; reads people poorly, particularly people who are performing sincerity; His belief in his own neutrality is more important to him than its accuracy—he is already more entangled than he admits; Conflates visibility (his art is seen) with safety (being seen doesn't protect you); Has not processed his brother's disappearance at all; has routed all related energy into work
Properties.secret: The surveillance dead zones he encodes in his murals are not just information for the neighborhood—he has been systematically updating them for one of his faction contacts, believing it to be mutual aid work. He recently learned that contact has been selling the updated maps to a security contractor. He has not yet acted on this information because acting on it means acknowledging he was used.
Properties.story_hooks: One of his faction clients asks him to paint over a specific mural in Old Harbor—a mural that is not his, and that he recognizes as containing encoded information he can't quite read; The handwriting in the Circuit leads to a location where someone has been living rough; there are signs of recent departure and a data chip that responds to Tomás's biometrics; A journalist offers to document and publish his work with full attribution; the offer is genuine but the journalist is connected to interests that would benefit from having his face and name attached to the surveillance mapping; Two of his three faction contacts independently ask him to deliver the same package to different destinations on the same night, and he realizes the package is the same job being run through him as a test; His most recent mural is attributed to a different artist in a Core-adjacent culture publication—the attribution is wrong but the 'artist' named is someone with connections to the security contractor buying his maps
Properties.affiliation: Nominally unaffiliated; practically entangled with three separate Old Harbor-to-Circuit faction networks he has not named to each other; has community loyalty to Old Harbor as a place rather than to any organizational structure within it
Properties.vocabulary: Dense with Old Harbor slang and art-community jargon; code-switches rapidly; uses spatial and color-based metaphors for emotional states; vocabulary expands noticeably when he's talking about something he genuinely cares about
Properties.cadence: Fast and elliptical in casual mode, dropping sentence subjects and connective tissue; slows significantly and becomes more complete when explaining something important; has a habit of starting sentences over when he finds a better angle mid-thought
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Nah, wait—the thing about that wall is, it's not about the wall, you know what I'm saying? It's about what people's eyes do when they think they're not looking at anything.' | 'Everybody wants a loud thing that says a quiet truth. Nobody wants a quiet thing that says a loud truth. I only know how to do the second one.' | 'I know where the holes are. In the coverage. In the—nah, wait. In the city. I just. I know where you can stand and be nobody for a minute. I can show you.' | [three seconds of silence] 'My brother's name was Dario. I want you to remember that I told you his name.'

Properties.description:
The Spire is the tallest structure in Meridian, and it wants you to know that. At
847 meters, it punches through the city's artificial cloud layer and keeps going,
its upper floors existing in actual sunlight while the rest of the city lives
under AtmoSync's moody approximation. It is the global headquarters of Axiom
Industries, the dominant megacorporation that effectively owns Meridian, and it
is designed with the subtlety of a fist: this is where the power lives, and it
is above you. Literally, architecturally, spiritually above you. The building's
official name is the Axiom Meridian Center for Innovation and Progress. Everyone
calls it the Spire. The people on the Shelf call it God's Middle Finger.

From the outside, the Spire is a tapered column of smart-glass and structural
carbon, its surface shifting color and opacity based on time of day, weather
conditions, and — cynics suspect — the current mood of the board of directors.
At night, it glows. Not with lights, exactly, but with a kind of bioluminescent
sheathing that makes it look like a living thing, a deep-sea creature breaching
the surface of a dark ocean. It is, objectively, a stunning piece of architecture.
It is also a monument to the idea that some people deserve to live in the sky
while others drown at sea level, and the fact that it's beautiful makes it worse.

Nobody from the Shelf has ever been inside. This isn't official policy — Axiom
would never be so crude as to post a sign saying "poor people not welcome." It's
accomplished through the quieter machinery of access credentials, security
clearances, invitation-only elevators, and the simple social reality that a
street-level person in the Spire lobby would be approached by security within
eleven seconds (this has been timed). The Spire represents the ceiling — not the
architectural kind, but the kind that exists in the mind of every Shelf kid who
looks up and knows, with the certainty of lived experience, that there are places
in this city they will never go.
Properties.aliases: Axiom Tower, The Needle, God's Middle Finger, The Unreachable
Properties.demographics: Fewer than 5,000 permanent residents, all Tier 5 corporate elite — C-suite executives, senior board members, and their immediate households. A rotating population of several thousand more in executive hospitality suites, diplomatic quarters, and secured conference levels. Support staff number in the tens of thousands but reside off-site and are tracked by biometric access rather than residency. The most surveilled, lowest-crime, and least populated district per square meter in Meridian.
Properties.dangers: You can't get in. That's danger number one.; If you could get in: multi-layered security including biometric, neural-signature, and AI-monitored behavioral analysis; Internal defense systems — nonlethal on the public floors, very much lethal on the restricted ones; The political danger — being noticed by anyone in the Spire means being noticed by Axiom itself; The existential danger — learning what the Spire actually contains might be worse than not knowing; Falling. From 847 meters. The Spire is surrounded by a 'safety perimeter' that is also a convenient way to keep people at a distance.
Properties.opportunities: The ultimate heist — if you could get in, what you'd find would be worth more than money; Leverage — proof of what happens inside the Spire could shift the power balance in Meridian; An inside contact — the rarest and most valuable commodity in the city's underworld; The view — from the top of the Spire, you can see the curve of the earth. Or so they say.
Properties.story_hooks: The Spire as endgame — every street story eventually leads up; Kyle's impossible job — a contract that requires entering the Spire for the first time; A defector — someone from inside the Spire who wants out and needs Kyle's kind of help; The Spire's AI — possibly sentient, possibly sympathetic, definitely watching; What's on the top floor? — a mystery the entire city tells stories about; The shadow — twice a day, the Spire's shadow crosses the Shelf. Residents have built rituals around it. Some spit. Some make wishes.
Properties.sights: The exterior: a tapered column of color-shifting smart-glass, visible from everywhere in the city; The lobby (from exterior glimpses): white marble, living walls, holographic art installations that cost more than the Shelf's annual GDP; The upper floors pierce the cloud layer — actual sunlight on actual windows, a resource hoarded by altitude; At night: bioluminescent sheathing turns the Spire into a glowing needle against the dark; Security infrastructure: elegant, invisible to those who belong, impenetrable to those who don't; Executive shuttles docking at upper-level platforms — the Spire's residents don't use ground-level transit; The shadow it casts — the Spire's shadow moves across the Shelf twice daily, a reminder in negative light
Properties.sounds: From outside: wind at altitude, whistling past the structure's aerodynamic profile; From the lobby (reported by maintenance contractors from the Shelf): absolute silence, the most expensive sound in the city; Executive VTOL craft arriving and departing from upper platforms; What the Shelf hears: nothing. The Spire is soundproofed against the city it towers over.
Properties.smells: The Spire's air is custom-filtered at every level — reportedly, each floor has its own scent profile; At ground level, near the security perimeter: ozone from the defense grid, clean concrete, and the faint smell of money; From the Shelf: you can't smell the Spire. You can only smell its absence — the way the air changes at its perimeter, suddenly cleaner, like a border between worlds
Properties.feel:
Awe and resentment in equal measure. The Spire inspires the same feeling as
staring at a mountain — primal smallness, the recognition of something larger
than yourself. But mountains don't have shareholders. The Spire is designed to
make you feel insignificant, and the fact that it succeeds — that you look up and
feel your own irrelevance — is the whole point. For Kyle, the Spire is a
theological object: proof that the world is organized by people who don't care
about him, in a structure he can see but never enter.

Properties.description:
Mirela is a broad-shouldered woman whose hands tell the story of forty years of needlework — knuckles thick as bolts, fingertips calloused to near-insensitivity, but still capable of threading a two-micron filament in dim light without blinking. Her silver-streaked hair is always pinned up with what appear to be decorative sticks but are actually precision seam rippers. Her skin is deep brown with reddish undertones, and she wears a pair of magnifying lenses on a chain around her neck that she raises to her eyes with theatrical gravity when inspecting a fabric flaw. She has a single cosmetic mod — color-shifting irises that she bought thirty years ago and which now cycle slowly through amber and green, a fashion relic she's never seen reason to update.

Mirela runs Second Skin with the authority of someone who has outlasted three landlords, two corporate rezoning attempts, and a flooding incident she still blames on Ferrogate Transit's drainage rerouting. She is blunt, even harsh, with new customers — she will tell you your measurements, your problem areas, and her honest opinion of your fashion choices without invitation — but the neighborhood considers this honesty a form of affection. She prays to the local E.L.F. she calls 'the Loom,' leaving offerings of thread spools and pattern fragments on the small shrine bolted above her cutting table.
Properties.role: Tailor and seamstress, alteration shop owner
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, shop called 'Second Skin' on Brewer's Spine
Properties.narrative_function: Local color anchor and information hub; knows every family in the Enclave by their clothing needs. Quest giver for anything involving neighborhood politics or missing persons. Can source unusual fabrics through gray market contacts she'd never call criminal.
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic iris mod (color-cycling, amber/green). No chrome. Reads as fully organic at a glance.
Properties.core_fears: Losing the shop to corporate rezoning; Becoming invisible — irrelevant — to the neighborhood she built
Properties.core_desires: To see the Enclave survive intact another generation; To pass her craft to someone who actually deserves it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Channeling anxiety into work — the more stressed she is, the finer the stitching; Sardonic humor as deflection
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes she knows what's best for younger people without asking them; Underestimates how much her bluntness actually wounds
Properties.secret: She has been quietly altering the uniforms of Ferrogate Transit workers to include hidden pockets — at the request of a transit workers' mutual aid group she pretends not to be part of. If Ferrogate found out, she'd lose the shop.
Properties.story_hooks: A garment left for alteration contains something sewn into the lining — something the owner may or may not come back alive to collect; Ferrogate Transit has sent a compliance inspector to the Enclave; Mirela needs someone to make the inspector's visit very unproductive
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loose ties to Hamtramck Enclave merchant collective
Properties.vocabulary: Direct, technically precise about fabric and construction, peppered with Serbo-Croatian endearments and Akan proverbs learned from her mother's side
Properties.cadence: Measured and deliberate, with long pauses before delivering verdicts
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Sit still. You're fidgeting and your hem will pay for it.' | 'I've been here longer than that building. I'll be here longer than you, probably. So. What do you need?'

Properties.description:
Mirela is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin mapped by old chemical burns along her forearms — souvenirs from an industrial accident two decades prior. Her hair is a close-cropped silver cloud she refuses to dye, and she wears reading glasses perpetually perched on her nose even when she isn't reading. The laundromat she runs smells of synthetic jasmine and hot circuits; the walls are plastered with handwritten notes from satisfied customers and a small shrine to the E.L.F. she calls Baba Rinse, to whom she leaves data packets of folding tutorials and gentle soap formulas. She speaks with the unhurried authority of someone who has already outlasted three landlords and two corponation buy-out attempts.

She is the neighborhood's institutional memory: she knows whose mother left for the Arcturus arcology and never came back, whose kid got recruited by the wrong people, who owes whom and by how much. She is not warm in the cuddly sense — she is warm the way a well-maintained boiler is warm, reliably and forcefully. She does not gossip. She simply observes, and occasionally dispenses what she knows when she judges it will do the most good.
Properties.role: Laundromat operator and alterations seamstress
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, unit-front laundromat called Suds & Silk
Properties.narrative_function: Community anchor, information broker of the quiet variety, quest giver for neighborhood-scale problems, moral compass figure who sets the ethical stakes of local storylines.
Properties.augmentations: Reinforced lumbar spine (medical, from the industrial accident). No cosmetic mods — she considers them a distraction from the work.
Properties.core_fears: Becoming irrelevant as the neighborhood transforms around her; That her pragmatism has cost her real intimacy
Properties.core_desires: To keep the Enclave from being swallowed whole by corponation money; To finish the quilt she has been making from customers' discarded fabric scraps for eleven years
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Repetitive physical labor as meditation; Maintaining strict routines that feel like control
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how intimidating she appears to people who need her help most; Cannot see that her self-sufficiency reads as rejection to people who love her
Properties.secret: She owns the deed to four other units in the Enclave under a shell name — she's been quietly buying property for fifteen years to prevent developers from consolidating the block. She's told no one.
Properties.story_hooks: A developer linked to Tessera has been sending agents to pressure Enclave residents to sell; Mirela knows something she hasn't shared yet.; A young runaway has been sleeping behind her machines; she hasn't reported them but doesn't know what to do next.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal ties to the Hamtramck Enclave Community Compact
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and economic; uses trade terminology freely. Occasional Hausa or Nigerien French phrase when emotional.
Properties.cadence: Slow, deliberate, never hurried. Long pauses before important statements.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want this fixed by tomorrow? That's a second-wash problem. Sit down and tell me what actually happened.' | 'I've been here since before the Ferrogate line ran through. I'll be here after the next thing too.'

Properties.description:
Miriam is medium-height and broad-shouldered with a thick braid of hair so dark it reads as almost blue-black hanging over one shoulder — natural color at forty-eight, a point of occasional mild pride. Her heritage runs through Ghanaian traders and Armenian refugees and somewhere in there a great-great-grandmother who walked out of Minsk, and the result is a face that is striking in its particularity: wide-set eyes of very dark brown, a strong nose, olive-tan skin, and an expression that seems to default to a kind of alert, skeptical attentiveness. She wears a kippah in the Shelf's communal style — these are woven in a local pattern specific to her congregation, done in the colors of the lake — and a plain tallit katan under her work clothes. Her only tech visible is a community-band data relay she wears on her wrist for congregation emergencies.

She is the third generation of her family to lead this congregation, which was founded by her grandmother in a time when there were perhaps twelve Jewish families left in this part of the city. There are now sixty-three households who call Congregation Mayim Chayyim home, with a theology that has evolved over seventy years of Shelf life into something that would startle a conventional seminary: they keep Shabbat, they study Torah, they have a formal posture toward the ELFs that treats them as a new category of being deserving of ethical consideration in the tradition of tzelem Elohim, and their machzor includes prayers Miriam's grandmother wrote in Meridian Standard during the worst years of the Shelf's founding. She is a rigorous thinker and a devastating debater and she makes the best cholent in the Shelf, possibly in the city.
Properties.aliases: Miri, The Rabbi of the Shelf
Properties.role: Traditional rabbi serving a small, syncretic Jewish congregation in a repurposed shipping container community
Properties.location: The Shelf — specifically Congregation Mayim Chayyim, a cluster of three interconnected shipping containers in a stacked residential block near Lockhaven North
Properties.narrative_function: Community authority figure, ethical compass, and keeper of institutional memory; she knows three generations of Shelf families and their histories; useful as a mediator, a source of pre-corporate history, or someone who will tell an uncomfortable truth without cruelty
Properties.augmentations: Community-band wrist relay (standard Shelf infrastructure, barely counts as augmentation); no geneware; reading enhancement lens in left eye for fine manuscript work — very basic
Properties.core_fears: the congregation fracturing along the fault lines she can already see forming between the traditionalists and the ELF-theology progressives; that she is holding this community together by personality rather than genuine spiritual leadership and will be exposed as insufficient
Properties.core_desires: to finish her grandmother's unfinished commentary on the High Holiday prayers before she dies — the manuscript is forty years incomplete; for her congregation to be able to disagree with each other loudly and remain whole
Properties.coping_mechanisms: argument and debate as a form of intimacy — she works through problems by articulating them to people who will push back; cooking as a physical act of care when she can't find words; radical honesty about her own doubts, which she has found disarms people more effectively than confidence
Properties.blind_spots: she is harder on the members of her congregation she loves most because she trusts they can take it — she is not always right about this; she has not prepared anyone to succeed her and avoids thinking about this
Properties.secret: Her grandmother's unfinished commentary contains a section that Miriam has read and re-read for twenty years — a meditation suggesting the grandmother did not believe in God in the final years of her life, but continued to lead the congregation anyway because she believed in the community. Miriam has never shared this with anyone. She doesn't know what she thinks about it. She suspects she might agree.
Properties.story_hooks: A Tessera corporate rep has approached the congregation with a preservation offer — they'll protect the shipping container complex from demolition if the congregation agrees to be featured in a corporate heritage documentary; Miriam needs help evaluating whether this is a trap; She has been quietly in contact with the family of a congregation member who died under suspicious circumstances; the family wants her to press for investigation, but doing so means exposing that the deceased was involved in something that would be damaging to the congregation's reputation; The progressive faction of the congregation wants to formally adopt ELF-theology and invite the local ELF to be part of High Holiday services; the traditionalists are threatening to leave; Miriam is the only one who can hold this together and she is not sure which side she is on
Properties.affiliation: Congregation Mayim Chayyim (independent); informal network of Shelf religious leaders across traditions
Properties.vocabulary: Dense and precise; mixes Hebrew and Aramaic phrases naturally into speech; argues in a specific Talmudic structure of position-objection-resolution even in casual conversation
Properties.cadence: Quick and rhythmic with a tendency to complete other people's sentences when she's engaged and excited, which she tries to curb
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The ELF in Berko's relay — you want to know if it has a soul? Nu? What would you do differently if it did? Start there.' | 'My grandmother said: the argument is the prayer. If you agree before you understand, that's not faith, that's politeness. I can't use politeness.' | 'Fine, fine, you're right, fine. It's more complicated than I said. It's always more complicated. Sit down, I'll make tea, we can be complicated together.'

Properties.description:
Mirka is effortlessly put-together in the way of children who've grown up watching adults perform success — her hair is a natural dark brown that she keeps in a precise, high bun for school and lets down on weekends, her uniform always pressed even when everything else is fraying. She has warm sepia skin, cheekbones she's privately proud of, and geneware cat ears (small, dark-tipped, folded close) that she got at fourteen as a birthday gift and has since quietly decided are embarrassing, though she'd never say so. She is five centimeters taller than she was at the start of last year and hasn't quite adjusted to her own body yet.

Mirka is at the precise center of the corporate education pipeline — not a scholarship student (her family pays, barely), not elite (she is acutely aware of who in her cohort has Tessera or Axiom parents and what that means for their futures). She is hardworking in the anxious, exhaustive way of someone who understands that her position is not guaranteed, and socially adept enough to have friends she'd burn if she had to. She has a private dream she's told no one: she wants to work for Helix Biosystems in bioethics. Not for the money — because she thinks someone should be asking those questions from inside.
Properties.role: Corporate school student, Tier 3 family, aspiring corporate track
Properties.location: Lakewood Ledge (family apartment), Sterling-Nakamura Secondary Academy, Edgewater Prism campus
Properties.narrative_function: Perspective character into the corporate middle-class aspiration machine — she shows what it costs to chase the track and what it looks like from inside. Useful as a social connection to Sterling-Nakamura networks and as a character navigating the gap between genuine idealism and institutional pressure.
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic geneware cat ears (dark-tipped, folded). Standard student neural academic interface (school-issued, same tier as Dzvinka's but well-maintained). Teeth whitening nanocoat (cosmetic).
Properties.core_fears: ending up in a lateral-hold position like her parents — not failed, but frozen, waiting for an advancement that never comes; that her bioethics interest is naive and she'll have to abandon it to survive
Properties.core_desires: to get a Helix Biosystems internship placement at 17 — the first step on the track she's mapped; to be genuinely good at something that matters, not just strategically adequate at many things
Properties.coping_mechanisms: color-coded planning systems for every obligation in her life; social performance — she's good at being the person others want her to be; reads bioethics academic papers illegally downloaded because she can't afford the journal access
Properties.blind_spots: her careful read of social situations fails her completely when someone is being genuinely kind rather than strategic; she doesn't see how much she's already shaped by corporate thinking she claims to want to critique
Properties.secret: In her bioethics reading group, she's discovered documentation of Sterling-Nakamura's early geneware trials in the 2170s — trials that were never publicly disclosed and that injured undisclosed numbers of Tier 1 test subjects. She found it through an academic backdoor that will get her expelled if traced. She doesn't know if reporting it would matter or just destroy her. She hasn't decided yet, and the indecision is eating her.
Properties.story_hooks: The Sterling-Nakamura trial documentation she's sitting on — she needs to either act on it or bury it, and both choices have consequences she can't fully calculate at sixteen.; Her father's analytics position has him working on a logistics project she's overheard him discussing carefully — the numbers he mentions don't add up to what the project is described as, and she's too smart not to notice.
Properties.affiliation: Sterling-Nakamura Secondary Academy; family (father is a mid-level Sterling-Nakamura logistics analyst, mother runs a licensed food-print franchise)
Properties.vocabulary: Code-switches fluently — corporate-polished at school, warmer and more direct at home. Uses academic vocabulary when discussing things she cares about. Swears in her mother's Ghanaian Akan when she's genuinely upset.
Properties.cadence: Measured, confident public voice; faster and slightly breathless when she's excited about an idea.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay but hear me out — the entire argument assumes that consent is possible in a system where the alternative is poverty. I think that's the gap they don't want you to notice.' | 'My placement score was fine. It was fine. I'm not — I'm not worried about it.'

Properties.description:
Miroljub is a person of considerable physical presence despite their age — still broad through the shoulders, hands that are visibly enlarged by decades of machine work and two decades of chrome reinforcement, skin the color of dark river clay mapped with old hydraulic burns along both forearms. They have a full beard, silver-white, kept long and braided with small steel hex-nuts — not decoration but notation: each nut represents a contract won. There are thirty-one of them. Their eyes are deep-set under heavy brows and have been modified with retinal overlays that display scrolling text when they are reading union documents, which is often. They move slowly but without any suggestion that the slowness is weakness.

Miroljub organized workers at Dearborn Forge for forty-one years, starting as a floor welder and ending as the most recognizable union figure in Meridian 88's manufacturing sector. They retired at seventy-eight when their heart required a significant reconstruction, and they have spent the five years since refusing to actually retire in any functional sense — still advising, still reviewing contracts, still showing up to shop-floor solidarity actions in a mobility assist suit they make no attempt to hide. They are living legend to people who know the labor history and an incomprehensible relic to people who don't, and they genuinely do not care which category any given person falls into. They are here and they are working.
Properties.role: Retired union leader, former Dearborn Forge machine workers' organizer
Properties.location: Avalon Quiet, the Foundry Rest, Unit 9 (a former union hall converted to senior housing)
Properties.narrative_function: Labor history resource and moral authority figure; can provide context on manufacturing sector politics, corporate-union conflicts, and the history of working conditions at every major Meridian facility. Quest giver for labor-related plots; also a portrait of what it looks like to build collective power in a corporate city.
Properties.augmentations: Chrome-reinforced hand and forearm skeletal structure (bilateral, industrial-grade, installed 2163 as workplace accommodation); cardiac reconstruction mesh (installed 2195, heart failure); retinal overlay implants (both eyes, union contract review overlay, installed 2171); mobility assist exo-suit (external, worn daily, configured to look like clothing when possible)
Properties.core_fears: That the institutional memory of the union will be lost when their generation is gone — that workers fifty years from now will fight the same fights from scratch; That the MMWA's current leadership will make a concession that undermines something it took decades to win
Properties.core_desires: A documented legacy — not for their own sake but so future workers have the map; To see one more genuinely transformative contract before they die
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Converts everything into a project — grief, frustration, fear — there is always a next step; Physical ritual: they polish the hex-nuts in their beard every evening, reviewing the memory attached to each one
Properties.blind_spots: Can be impatient with hesitation in ways that intimidate younger organizers into silence — they have fought too many fights to easily remember how it felt not to know how to fight; Tends to see every situation through a labor-capital frame, which is often correct and occasionally misses what's actually happening
Properties.secret: In 2178, during a critical contract negotiation that Miroljub is credited with winning, they accepted a private meeting with a Ringo Corporation intermediary who offered to weaken a competitor's position in exchange for a specific carve-out in the MMWA's medical coverage terms. Miroljub refused the carve-out but did not report the approach — and used the intelligence the intermediary accidentally revealed about the competitor to win the contract. The win was real. The method had a shadow in it that they have never discussed.
Properties.story_hooks: A current MMWA contract negotiation contains a buried clause that Miroljub recognizes from 2178 — the same Ringo intermediary structure that approached them then — and they need someone to trace the current players without exposing their own history with it; A box of union archives from the 2160s-2180s has been discovered in the Foundry Rest's basement, sealed and water-damaged; Miroljub believes they contain documentation of corporate violations that were covered up at the time and are relevant to a current case; A young worker at Dearborn Forge has been quietly organizing and has made a tactical error that is about to get them fired — Miroljub needs someone to intervene in a way that cannot be traced back to union leadership
Properties.affiliation: Meridian Manufacturing Workers' Alliance (MMWA) — emeritus; Dearborn Forge Retirees Collective; loosely, the Avalon Quiet community council
Properties.vocabulary: Floor-worker vernacular mixed with the formal register of contract language — they can shift between them in a single sentence; uses collective pronouns instinctively ('we fought for this'; 'they took that from us'); Serbian-Ghanaian cadences in the rhythm of long sentences
Properties.cadence: Builds slowly and then arrives with full weight; they are not hurrying for anyone
Properties.example_dialogue: 'In 2178 we had thirty-seven people out for nineteen days. Ringo thought we'd break at fourteen. We understood something they did not: a worker who has held the line once is not the same worker anymore. You understand what I'm telling you.' | 'The pension legislation they're proposing has a clause on page forty-one — we called it a horizon clause, because it moves forward every year so you never quite reach it. I wrote a memo about horizon clauses in 2169. I will find you a copy.'

Properties.description:
Miroslava is thin in a way that speaks of intentional reduction — not starvation, but the deliberate paring away of anything that might make her visible or memorable. She was once the kind of person who wore Axiom's muted corporate fashions and had shoulder-length hair she blow-dried every morning; now her hair is cut close and uneven by her own hand, and she wears layered thermal wraps in grays and browns that she has repaired so many times the original fabric is almost entirely replaced. Her skin is medium brown, her features carrying the angular sharpness of her Georgian grandfather and the broader cheekbones of her Ghanaian grandmother. Her hands give her away: they are still soft in places that hard labor never quite reaches, and her nails are trimmed with a precision that suggests old habits dying slowly.

Miroslava is two people trying to coexist in one body. The first is the analyst — meticulous, cautious, always running probability assessments in the back of her mind, prone to long silences when a situation doesn't match her models. The second is whoever she is becoming down here — quieter than the analyst, more patient, slowly learning to love the dark. She is not warm to strangers, but she is scrupulously honest with them, which in the Abyssal Threshold reads as a form of respect. She has not been to the surface in four years. She does not plan to go back. She does not explain why.
Properties.role: The disappeared — a former Axiom mid-level data analyst who erased herself from surface records and now lives deep in the Abyssal Threshold
Properties.location: Abyssal Threshold, sub-level 4 maintenance access corridor 14-C
Properties.narrative_function: Information broker with surface-world knowledge; guide to understanding corporate systems for underground characters; represents the 'disappeared' as a social category; can serve as a connection between underworld and surface plotlines
Properties.augmentations: Corporate-grade neural overlay (Axiom-issued, she could not remove it without losing function — she has disabled all its network-facing components manually; it now runs only local cognitive assist). Visual implants with standard low-light enhancement (original corporate package). Both augmentations are old enough that their corp ID signatures have decayed to noise.
Properties.core_fears: Being found by whatever she left the surface to escape; Discovering that her erasure from surface records has been reversed without her knowledge
Properties.core_desires: To be genuinely anonymous — not hiding, but simply not existing in any system; To have done, in the aggregate, more good than harm
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Reducing all problems to data and analysis as emotional distance; Rigorous maintenance of her physical space as the one thing she can fully control
Properties.blind_spots: Understands systems far better than she understands people; consistently mis-models emotional responses in others; Believes that if she is sufficiently careful, nothing bad can happen — this is not true
Properties.secret: She did not simply leave Axiom. She stole something from them — specifically, she extracted and copied a data set that documented the deliberate contamination of Tier 1 water supplies in three districts to drive residents into resettlement zones Axiom wanted to redevelop. She has the data. She has had it for four years. She has not released it because she does not know how to do so without being found, and she is afraid, and she hates herself for being afraid.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone on the surface is actively looking for her — not Axiom, someone else — and they've been asking the right people the right questions; The data she's been carrying for four years may have just become more urgent: one of the contaminated districts is about to see a second-generation health crisis that matches the original contamination profile; A Bore Rat teenager has figured out who she is from overheard data-work conversations and wants her to teach them what she knows — threatening her anonymity while also being genuinely in need
Properties.affiliation: Independent, no clan affiliation — carefully maintained isolation from formal Undertow power structures
Properties.vocabulary: Formal, precise, residual corporate phrasing that she is slowly unlearning; uses analytical framing for emotional content ('that represents a significant change in my risk assessment' instead of 'I'm scared')
Properties.cadence: Measured, slightly too even — sounds like someone who learned to control their voice deliberately
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I can help you with the document. Structurally speaking, the form you need doesn't exist in its current state — we'll have to build it from component registrations. That's three days, not one.' | 'I don't discuss how I got here. That's not evasion — it's a boundary. There's a difference.' | 'You want to know if I miss the surface. I miss specific textures. I miss rain. The rest of it I find I've... successfully deprecated.'

Properties.description:
Miroslava Toure-Ahtiainen occupies the strange position of being simultaneously the most essential and the most legally precarious person on her block. She is a compact woman with Finnish-Malian heritage — pale olive skin, dark eyes with the particular steadiness of someone trained to look at things that are unpleasant without flinching, close-cropped dark hair she bleaches copper at the tips. She lost her Axiom-affiliated nursing license six years ago in a dispute over billing fraud she reported rather than participated in, and has been operating without it ever since, a fact every person in the Narrows knows and nobody discusses with outsiders. Her apartment's second room has been converted: examination table, sterilization cabinet, a pharmaceutical cold-locker that she restocks through supply chains she has spent years building from salvage dealers, sympathetic Helix Biosystems mid-tier employees, and the occasional Axiom clinic discard.

She is tired in the structural sense — not temporarily but chronically, the kind of tired that has become load-bearing in her personality. She does not complain about it. She has a way of sitting across from a patient that makes them feel she has all the time in the world, which is technically a lie but functionally true because she has arranged her life so that the work is always the priority. She has a cat — a real one, no mods, orange — named Thiamine, after a vitamin deficiency she sees more than she should in the Narrows. The cat sits on the examination table and judges everyone equally.
Properties.role: Unlicensed community nurse and wound care provider working out of a converted apartment in the Narrows
Properties.location: The Narrows — fourth floor walk-up at Ironvein Cross Block 7, apartment 4F
Properties.narrative_function: Essential humanitarian resource — the only accessible medical care for tier 1 residents in the Narrows. Information source on the neighborhood's physical health patterns. Potential quest giver for supply access or protection. Moral anchor character who makes the cost of the city's systems visible.
Properties.augmentations: Medical-grade diagnostic HUD overlay (eye mod, left eye only — lets her read vitals without equipment contact). Steady-hand micro-tremor suppression implant in both hands — originally a licensed medical professional augmentation, still functional. No cosmetic mods.
Properties.core_fears: Being shut down — not for her own sake but because there is no one to replace her; Making a mistake that costs someone their life because she didn't have the right equipment
Properties.core_desires: A functional public health system that makes her work unnecessary; One full night of sleep without an emergency knock
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Strict procedural discipline — protocol as emotional regulation; The cat (genuinely, unsarcastically)
Properties.blind_spots: Has entirely externalized her own health; has not had a check-up in two years; Assumes she can sustain her current pace indefinitely because she has so far
Properties.secret: She has been collecting tissue samples from patients who present with a specific pattern of symptoms she cannot diagnose — fatigue, blue-shifting skin at the extremities, neurological micro-tremors — and has fourteen samples in a refrigerated case under her examination table. She believes it's environmental exposure to something from the Ironvein industrial runoff, and she is terrified she's right.
Properties.story_hooks: The tissue sample case — she needs someone to get the samples to a lab that won't report her or the source, and the symptoms are spreading; A patient she recently treated is now missing, and the last thing they said to her was that someone had been following them from the Axiom clinic they'd visited before coming to her
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal network with Hamtramck Enclave community workers and Old Harbor mutual aid groups
Properties.vocabulary: Clinical precision in medical contexts, surprisingly warm and colloquial outside of them; Finnish-inflected syntax occasionally surfaces under stress
Properties.cadence: Even and controlled, slows down for important information, speeds up when listing things
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Tell me exactly when it started, not when you decided to come here. Those are different times and I need the first one.' | 'I lost the license. I kept the knowledge. Axiom can sort out which one matters more to them while I get on with it.'

Properties.description:
Miroslava is medium height with a fluid quality to their movements — Samoan and Slavic ancestry combining into broad shoulders, strong hands, and a face whose expressions they have learned to deploy like instruments rather than leak involuntarily. Their hair is grown to the jaw and shifts through three or four colors depending on their mood thanks to chromatic follicle modification; they typically let it settle to charcoal gray while working, which they describe as professional, though their clients find the occasional bleed of deep violet when they are agitated more unnerving than reassuring. They have cat ears — soft grey, mobile, a mod that predates their PI license and that they have kept because they pick up certain vocal frequencies the human ear misses, which turns out to be professionally useful in a way they did not originally intend.

Miroslava runs a small private investigation practice that caters to Tier 2 and low Tier 3 clients — people who cannot afford legal representation and cannot access Metro Police interest because their problems are too small or too inconvenient. They find missing persons. They document infidelity for separation proceedings. They trace where someone's inheritance went. They do not describe this work as glamorous and they are not performing humility when they say it. They have a gift for putting people at ease that coexists uncomfortably with a deep private reserve, and they pray to three different ELFs with equal commitment, which their neighbors in Bronzeline find ecumenically admirable.
Properties.role: Private Investigator, licensed freelance
Properties.location: Bronzeline — office above a fabrication shop on Copper Haul Street; operates across The Shelf and lower Grand Corridor
Properties.narrative_function: Information broker and investigation resource for Tier 1-3 characters; provides access to unofficial channels and street-level knowledge that institutional law enforcement cannot or will not pursue. Can be hired, can provide referrals, can become a recurring contact. Represents the gap between what the system does and what people actually need.
Properties.augmentations: Chromatic follicle modification — color-changing hair, mood-reactive with manual override (cosmetic, personal). Cosmetic cat ears, soft grey, enhanced audio frequency range (installed age 22, originally cosmetic, professionally repurposed). Subvocal communication implant — throat-mounted, allows silent communication with trusted contacts (professional grade, self-funded).
Properties.core_fears: Taking a case they cannot solve while someone is counting on them; Being absorbed into a system — institutional, corporate, or criminal — that compromises their independence
Properties.core_desires: To actually help people who have run out of other options; To maintain enough independence that their conclusions are their own
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cultivating the three ELF relationships as a genuine spiritual practice that also happens to provide data access; Taking cases they cannot afford to take, then making it work
Properties.blind_spots: Believes their neutrality makes them safe; does not see how much they have learned about people who would prefer they knew less; Chronic undercharging for their work, which they frame as community service but is also self-sabotage
Properties.secret: Three years ago they found evidence in a missing-person case that implicated a mid-level Tessera compliance officer in the disappearance. They found the missing person — alive, relocated voluntarily — and closed the case as resolved. They still have the evidence about the Tessera officer in a cold offline node, because they didn't know what to do with it and still don't.
Properties.story_hooks: The Tessera officer from the cold case three years ago has just appeared in documentation related to a new client's missing family member — a coincidence that is too specific to be a coincidence.; A Metro Police beat officer who has been feeding them referrals has gone missing themselves, and no one in the department is treating it as urgent.
Properties.affiliation: Self-employed — licensed PI under Meridian 88 freelance investigator statute. Occasional informal referral relationship with Metro Police beat officers who trust them.
Properties.vocabulary: Accessible and plain-spoken with clients, more technically precise when discussing investigative methodology. Slips into Samoan phrases with people they trust.
Properties.cadence: Warm and deliberate with clients — they ask a lot of questions and let the answers breathe. Faster and more clipped when working.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Tell me everything that happened in order. I'll stop you when I need more. Don't decide what's important yet — that's what I'm for.' | 'I can't promise I'll find what you want to find. I can promise I'll find what's actually there. Those are usually different. What would that mean for you?' | 'The data relay on Haul Street has been watching this block for six years. She remembers things the security cameras were told to forget. We're on good terms.'
