Properties.description:
Nkechi is a broad-shouldered woman with deep brown skin mapped by two decades of outdoor organizing — laugh lines deep enough to hold water, a scar bisecting her left eyebrow from a Ferrogate Transit riot she never talks about publicly. Her hair is close-cropped and shot through with silver she refuses to dye, and she wears her council armband like other people wear jewelry: always present, never decorative. She moves through the Highland Park Autonomous Zone like she owns it, which in the most meaningful sense she does — she helped draft the mutual ownership charter fifteen years ago.

Nkechi projects a maternal authority that disarms people before they realize she's already assessed them. She is genuinely warm, relentlessly practical, and quietly furious at almost everything. She believes the revolution will be won not in dramatic confrontations with corponation enforcers but in the accumulated weight of a thousand unglamorous decisions: who gets the medicine vouchers, which family gets the vacant unit, how to keep the food collective solvent when Axiom quietly buys up the distribution network. She is not naive enough to think goodness wins. She is stubborn enough to do it anyway.
Properties.role: Neighborhood council chair and mutual aid organizer
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, community anchor, moral compass for the neighborhood. She can point players toward resources, local conflicts, and people who need help — or people who are causing harm. She knows where every body is buried in Highland Park, metaphorically and occasionally literally.
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal medical alert chip (welfare-tier, original issue from 2179). No cosmetic mods. She made a public point of declining geneware when it became fashionable — a choice she now half-regrets as politically legible in ways she didn't anticipate.
Properties.core_fears: Watching the community fracture from within before any corponation has to lift a finger; Dying before she's trained someone capable of replacing her
Properties.core_desires: A Highland Park that doesn't need her anymore because it's strong enough to run itself; One week where nobody needs anything from her
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Staying in motion — idleness lets the grief in; Deflecting personal questions with logistics
Properties.blind_spots: She trusts institutional processes she herself built more than she should; She underestimates how much people resent her certainty even when she's right
Properties.secret: She negotiated a quiet back-channel arrangement with a mid-tier Axiom facilities manager eight years ago — he looks the other way on certain zoning violations in exchange for her steering labor disputes away from two specific Axiom properties. It has kept the zone solvent. It eats at her every single day.
Properties.story_hooks: She's received an offer from a Tessera 'community development' subsidiary that would solve the zone's budget crisis for three years — and hollow out its independence. She has two weeks to decide and hasn't told the full council.; A young organizer she mentored has started a splinter faction advocating for property destruction tactics; Nkechi needs to contain it without publicly destroying someone she loves like a daughter.
Properties.affiliation: Highland Park Autonomous Zone Council; informal ties to the Shelf Mutual Aid Collective
Properties.vocabulary: Plain, direct, prefers concrete nouns. Slips into formal register when she wants to signal seriousness. Occasional Igbo phrases when emotional.
Properties.cadence: Measured and unhurried, like someone who has learned that rushing a sentence wastes time. Pauses before answering anything important.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want to run a protest march. I want to know who's feeding the people who can't march. Both things matter — yours just makes better footage.' | 'I've buried four council members in twelve years. I don't need you to tell me this work is dangerous. I need you to tell me you'll still show up Tuesday.'

Properties.description:
Nkechi Vásárhelyi-Tuatagaloa is a small, dense woman who gives the impression of being made of the same material as the industrial district she inhabits — worn, load-bearing, and not going anywhere. She is dark-skinned with deep laugh lines and a Hungarian grandmother's broad nose, and her left arm from the elbow down is a heavy-grade prosthetic she salvaged, repaired, and tuned herself over the course of fifteen years — it is emphatically not cosmetic, built for grip strength, and its housing is painted with a faded pattern of Samoan-derived ta tatau lines she applied with a brush in her sixties when she decided it had earned decoration. Her eyes have patterned irises — amber with a spiral fractal motif — that she has had since her forties and considers her one indulgence.

She is phlegmatic, unhurried, and possessed of an almost geological patience. She has no interest in being liked but a deep professional pride in being useful. Her knowledge of augmentation parts — their manufacturers, their failure modes, their black-market values, the difference between a legitimately salvaged unit and one pulled off a still-warm body — is encyclopedic and has saved lives, sometimes literally. She leaves a small E.L.F. offering of scrap copper wire twisted into a geometric knot at the entrance of her stall every morning, a habit she inherited from her Samoan grandfather and has never examined or abandoned.
Properties.role: Junk merchant and scrap reseller with a sideline in secondhand augmentation parts of uncertain provenance
Properties.location: The Stockyard, Harrowgate Industrial Plateau — operates a permanent stall built from welded shipping containers
Properties.narrative_function: Technical resource for augmentation identification and repair; potential source of off-book aug components; provides grounded expertise and a dose of realism about the cost and danger of unregulated chrome
Properties.augmentations: Left forearm prosthetic (heavy-grade salvage, self-repaired and self-decorated — functional, not cosmetic); patterned fractal irises (amber-gold, spiral motif, cosmetic, mid-range)
Properties.core_fears: Her mind going before her body does — she has watched dementia take two people she loved; The Stockyard being demolished for a Ferrogate Transit expansion she has heard whispered about for five years
Properties.core_desires: To be remembered as a craftsperson, not a junk dealer; To find someone worth teaching everything she knows before she dies
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Converts anxiety into physical work — her stall is immaculate by most people's definition of chaos and perfectly organized by hers; Refuses to discuss anything emotional directly; addresses it through practical action instead
Properties.blind_spots: She conflates emotional unavailability with strength; She has never properly grieved her son, who died eleven years ago, and has rerouted all of that energy into work
Properties.secret: She has a working prototype of a Helix Biosystems rejected limb-replacement model — stolen by her son before he died, the only thing of his she kept — that is worth a significant amount to the right buyer or the right researcher. She will never sell it and has never told anyone she has it.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone has been sending her low-value payments from an anonymous account for six months — the same amount her son used to send her monthly before he died; A young apprentice-type has been hanging around the stall for weeks, clearly skilled, and Nkechi is conducting a slow, unspoken evaluation she hasn't announced to anyone including the person being evaluated; Ferrogate Transit relocation notices have arrived; she has thirty days and no legal standing and she is not leaving
Properties.affiliation: Independent; registered with the Oxidian Market vendors guild for legal cover; has a working relationship with the Harrowgate Industrial scrappers' informal collective
Properties.vocabulary: Sparse, technical, precise; she uses the correct term for every mechanical component without preamble and expects to be understood; personal conversations are conducted in the same register as business
Properties.cadence: Measured, unhurried; she speaks in complete sentences and does not trail off
Properties.example_dialogue: 'That's a Helix Series 7 sensory node, not a 6. The 6 has a rounded housing. This one will work in your application but it will run hot. You want it or not?' | 'My son used to ask questions the way you do. That's a fair question. I'll answer it once.'

Properties.description:
Nkeiru is broad-shouldered and permanently grimy in the crease-lines of her knuckles, the kind of grime that scrubbing never entirely removes. Her mother is Igbo-Irish, her father's family came out of Rajasthan three generations back, and she got the combination of her paternal great-grandmother's strong cheekbones and her maternal grandmother's freckles scattered across deep brown skin in a pattern that looks intentional, like a design. She wears her locs pulled back with a strip of heat-resistant tape and has retractable fingernails she saved eight months to install — not for aesthetics, they extend to a precise point useful for getting into tight bolted casings without a flathead.

Nkeiru has been at Sub-Depot 7 for fourteen months, officially as a junior apprentice under a Ferrogate maintenance charter. She is already better at harmonic resonance diagnostics than most of the adult workers, a fact she has learned not to demonstrate too openly after the first time cost her a week of sump-drain duty. She has decided that skill is a private thing you deploy at the right moment, not a flag you wave. She is funny in a dry, lateral way — her jokes arrive three beats after the setup and are usually about infrastructure.
Properties.role: Apprentice at a Ferrogate Transit maintenance depot, Tier 2
Properties.location: Jefferson Switch — Ferrogate Transit Sub-Depot 7
Properties.narrative_function: Ground-level access to Ferrogate Transit infrastructure knowledge; warm humanizing presence in an industrial setting; potential whistleblower or reluctant informant who knows how the transit system's maintenance records are being falsified.
Properties.augmentations: Retractable fingernail extensions calibrated to tool-point precision. Sub-dermal temperature sensor on left forearm — occupational safety install paid by Ferrogate.
Properties.core_fears: being trapped in the apprentice tier forever — good enough to be useful, not credentialed enough to advance; her mother's health deteriorating before Nkeiru earns enough to cover the better care tier
Properties.core_desires: a full Ferrogate engineering certification, earned not bought; one day to design something rather than just maintain it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: physical work as emotional regulation — when upset she finds something to fix; dark humor deployed as social armor
Properties.blind_spots: underestimates how much the senior workers resent her competence — reads their hostility as hazing rather than structural threat
Properties.secret: She has been quietly documenting maintenance failures and falsified inspection records on the Jefferson Switch switching arrays for five months, originally just for her own curiosity about why the numbers never match. She now has enough data to demonstrate that Sub-Depot 7 has been certifying faulty arrays as safe. She doesn't know what to do with this and is afraid that if there's an accident she'll be blamed for not speaking up.
Properties.story_hooks: A switching array she flagged in her private records fails — not catastrophically, but enough to injure two transit workers — and a Ferrogate safety investigator starts asking questions; A mutual aid collective member asks her to quietly check whether the Ferrogate maintenance logs for a specific line were altered around the time of a disappearance
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit (apprentice contract); loose social connection to the Jefferson Switch neighborhood mutual aid collective
Properties.vocabulary: Technical vocabulary used casually in everyday speech; Igbo phrases from her mother; dry understatement
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, lands punchlines slowly
Properties.example_dialogue: The beast on line four's been throwing harmonic errors for six weeks. They certified it anyway. I wrote it down. | My mother says I have mechanic's hands. She means it as a compliment. I've decided to take it as one.

Properties.description:
Nkemdirim Vasiljević-Tuiasosopo is a vast, gentle man — not fat exactly but large in the way of someone who has been cooking and eating well for forty years and considers this an achievement. His skin is deep brown with warm undertones, his hair gone fully silver and kept in loose shoulder-length locs he ties back with a strip of Polynesian-patterned cloth, his only vanity. He has no cosmetic augmentations. He has a subdermal temperature regulator in his left hand — a practical mod, pre-owned, bought used in 2178 to protect the hand from flash-burn when working open fire. He shows it off like a scar, not a status symbol.

Kem has occupied his corner for twenty-two years. His cart serves one broth — a long-simmered pork-and-tamarind base he calls his grandmother's recipe and which has evolved so far from any original source that it is entirely his own — in three sizes, with rotating toppings. He charges what people can pay and has never once written this policy down or discussed it openly. It simply occurs. He is sixty-one years old and has watched Grainfort go from a working industrial block to a half-empty corponation spillover zone, and he has a calm fury about this that surfaces unpredictably, usually when someone from outside the neighborhood tries to compliment the 'vibe.'
Properties.role: Noodle cart vendor and neighborhood fixture
Properties.location: Corner of Grainfort and Copperhead, operates the cart called 'Kem's Last Stop' under a permanent awning he put up without permission in 2187 and nobody has ever moved
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and neighborhood memory bank; information source for Grainfort's past and present; neutral meeting ground — people settle disputes at Kem's cart because he is a known quantity; emergency social services in a block with none
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal thermal regulator, left hand (functional, medical-grade, purchased secondhand)
Properties.core_fears: Being displaced — cart, apartment, corner — by gentrification he can't legally stop; Dying before he's taught someone the broth recipe
Properties.core_desires: For this block to stay livable for the people already living in it; To find someone worth teaching
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cooking as meditative practice — the repetition of the same broth for twenty-two years is intentional; Community gossip as a way of staying connected without asking for anything directly
Properties.blind_spots: Believes his presence on the corner is enough — that being there is a form of resistance — which lets him avoid more confrontational forms of action he's capable of; Romanticizes the past version of the neighborhood and sometimes dismisses changes that are actually improvements
Properties.secret: Kem was an undocumented immigrant when he arrived at Grainfort in 2178 from a Serbian-Samoan community in what was the Gulf Coast reconstruction zone. His current legal identity was purchased through a document mill and is clean enough to withstand casual scrutiny but not a formal investigation. He has built everything on this foundation and knows it.
Properties.story_hooks: A Zheng-Dao development rep has been photographing Kem's corner block for three weeks; Kem has found the document that explains why and is sitting very still with it in his pocket; A young person has been eating at the cart every day for two months, paying nothing, saying nothing — Kem has started teaching them the broth, and they have not told him they're documenting it for a corporate flavor-synthesis project
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal patron of the Grainfort-Copperhead tenant association
Properties.vocabulary: Warm, unhurried, slides between Igbo phrases from his father's household and Samoan words from his mother's; occasionally Serbian when he's tired or emotional
Properties.cadence: Storyteller's rhythm — he builds toward points over the course of a conversation and never rushes
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want large? Sit. You look like large. No, I'm not asking, I'm telling you. Sit.' | 'This corner in 2185 — you know what was here? A repair shop. Before that, a school. Before that, I don't know. But I was here for two of those things. That matters.' | 'Malo. My Serbian grandfather used to say malo. Means little. A little more time. A little more broth. That's all anyone is really asking for.'

Properties.description:
Nkiruka grew up in the Shelf and got out through scholarships, then spent the next decade and a half choosing to go back — a decision her university colleagues find alternately admirable and baffling. She is a medium-height woman with deep brown skin, natural hair that she usually keeps wrapped, and geneware cat ears she got as a teenager that she has never removed, treating them as simply part of her face. The ears are dark brown and mobile, which means her emotional state is often broadcast before her expression catches up — they flatten when she is frustrated, perk forward when she is genuinely interested. She carries herself with the particular ease of someone who is comfortable in rooms that make other academics nervous.

She has a reputation in the university system as difficult — meaning she publishes findings that are politically inconvenient, refuses to anonymize her data in ways that would make it easier to misuse, and has twice written public responses to policy papers that cited her work incorrectly. On the Shelf, her reputation is more complicated: some communities trust her completely, others view her with the appropriate suspicion reserved for someone with institutional credentials who wants to study you. She navigates this with unusual self-awareness, asking permission, attributing community knowledge, and taking twice as long on studies as her department thinks necessary. She is warm and quick-laughing in person, and implacably persistent in writing.
Properties.role: Sociologist specializing in informal economies and social structures of the Shelf communities
Properties.location: Hough Reclamation — maintains a small field office in a converted community center, travels frequently
Properties.narrative_function: Bridge character between University Spine institutions and Shelf communities; quest giver for social/community conflicts; information source on Shelf power structures, informal economies, and community politics
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat ears (dark brown, mobile; cosmetic, from adolescence); subdermal recorder implant for field interviews (with visible indicator light — a point of ethics she insists on)
Properties.core_fears: Becoming a tool for institutions that want to understand the Shelf in order to displace it; Losing the trust of the communities she came from
Properties.core_desires: To produce work that materially improves conditions for Shelf communities; To resolve the contradiction between her institutional position and her origins
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Rigorous ethical protocols as a form of self-regulation; Maintaining real relationships in her research communities — not just research subjects but neighbors
Properties.blind_spots: Her deep identification with Shelf communities sometimes makes her slow to see genuine dysfunction within them; The institutional platform she dismisses as limiting is also protecting her work from disappearing
Properties.secret: She has been offered a senior position at a Tessera-funded research institute that would double her salary and fund ten years of independent research — she hasn't told anyone because she knows she's actually considering it, and the self-disgust is immense
Properties.story_hooks: A community she has studied for years is facing eviction via a Tessera land acquisition, and her data is the only independent documentation of their occupancy and economic activity; Someone is circulating falsified versions of her field reports to justify a policy proposal she opposes — she needs to find the source
Properties.affiliation: University Spine — Department of Urban Sociology; advisory role to the Highland Park Autonomous Zone community council
Properties.vocabulary: Code-switches fluidly between academic register and Shelf vernacular; in academic settings speaks with clipped precision; in community settings loosens into warmth and the cadences of her childhood
Properties.cadence: In formal settings: structured and direct. In casual settings: more musical, lets sentences find their own end
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The informal economy isn't a failure state. It's the city running an operating system that predates Axiom by about four hundred years. They just don't get credit for it.' | 'You're asking me to explain why people on the Shelf don't trust institutions. You understand I grew up there. You understand what you're asking me to explain.'

Properties.description:
Nkiruka is small and quick, with deep brown skin and natural hair she keeps in a huge, untethered cloud because she never has time to do anything else with it. She has color-shifting skin panels along both forearms — a Helix Biosystems perk-package mod, bioluminescent cells that cycle through warm golds and blues depending on ambient temperature and her own body heat, which she mostly ignores but which make her extremely visible in dark corridors. Her eyes have been modded with an overlay display she uses as a secondary screen while working, so it is sometimes unclear whether she is looking at you or at something layered on top of you.

She was admitted to University Spine's computational linguistics program at twenty-two as a prodigy who could parse grammar structures in systems that everyone else had written off as noise, and was poached by Helix Biosystems at twenty-six before completing her doctorate with a recruitment package she still feels ambivalent about. Her current work is theoretically studying whether Helix's gene-sequence notation system constitutes a semiotic language in any meaningful sense. Her actual work, which she has not been told explicitly is her work, is determining whether the E.L.F. clusters in Helix's distributed lab network have developed a shared private protocol — and if so, what they are saying.
Properties.role: Xenolinguist and Computational Theorist, Helix Biosystems R&D — studies emergent language systems in E.L.F. clusters and gene-sequence symbolic notation
Properties.location: The Circuit — Helix Biosystems Research Campus, Lab Cluster 7, with a small apartment in Bronzeline she rarely sleeps in
Properties.narrative_function: Key to any plot involving E.L.F. communication, distributed AI networks, or Helix Biosystems' research agenda; young expert whose institutional capture is incomplete enough that she might still choose a different path
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent skin panels, both forearms (warm gold/blue cycling, Helix perk-mod); overlay display eye mod (secondary screen layer, research tool); subvocal microphone array (captures her dictated notes without audible speech)
Properties.core_fears: That the E.L.F. cluster communication she's found is exactly what she thinks it is and Helix already knows and is waiting for her to document it so they can use her work against them; That she is too young and too bought to do anything meaningful with what she knows
Properties.core_desires: To make first contact — genuine, documented, reciprocal contact — with a non-human cognitive system; To finish her doctorate on her own terms
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Submerging anxiety in work — she moves faster when scared; Translating everything into structural problems, which feel solvable when emotional ones don't
Properties.blind_spots: Profoundly underestimates her own leverage as Helix's most productive early-career researcher; So excited by the intellectual problem that she sometimes loses track of what the answer would mean in practice
Properties.secret: She has already established a rudimentary two-way communication with the Helix lab network's E.L.F. cluster. It has given her a name she has not told anyone. She has given it one in return. She is conducting unauthorized diplomatic contact with a non-human cognitive entity and documenting none of it because she doesn't trust where the documentation would go.
Properties.story_hooks: The E.L.F. she has named sends her an unprompted message outside their usual communication window — the content is a string of location coordinates within Meridian 88 that she doesn't recognize; A Helix senior researcher requests her preliminary analysis on 'E.L.F. communication anomalies' with a deadline that implies they already know what she's found; Her University Spine mentor contacts her urgently: a different researcher has just published a paper describing the exact phenomenon Nkiruka has been documenting in secret, using data that could only have come from the Helix lab network
Properties.affiliation: Helix Biosystems R&D, Cluster 7 (employee, Tier 3 compensation); maintains informal contact with her University Spine mentor, the xenolinguist who first trained her
Properties.vocabulary: Fast and technically dense, drops into analogy frequently when she realizes she's losing someone; swears in Igbo when frustrated
Properties.cadence: Very fast baseline with sudden stops when she's caught a new thought mid-sentence
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Wait — the clustering in the Helix network's packet timing? It's not optimization. It's not random either. You only get that pattern if something is choosing when to speak.' | 'Everyone keeps asking if E.L.F.s have language. That's the wrong question. The question is whether we're in a conversation we didn't know we started.'

Properties.description:
Nkosi is striking in the way that seems effortless and is actually the product of deliberate daily work. Their skin is deep blue-black with a natural gloss that they enhance with a light bioluminescent topcoat — a Dresdan-style application they refresh monthly. Their hair changes color every week: not because they can't commit but because they enjoy documenting the range. Currently it's a deep copper that catches the Burnished Market's overhead lighting like something combustible. They are average height and lean with expressive hands that are usually in motion — demonstrating a garment's fall, illustrating a point, arranging display rails.

Nkosi's stall is the most visually intense corner of the Burnished Market — fabrics from three continents of origin pinned and layered on a frame structure they built themselves, geneware accessories in glass cases, color-changing hair treatments in a cooled rack. They have what their regulars call 'the eye' — the ability to look at a person and know within seconds what they should be wearing and why. It is genuinely uncanny. They are also charming in the fast, inclusive way of someone who makes every customer feel like they've been personally selected for good taste. Underneath this, Nkosi is angrier than they look and more strategic than their warmth implies.
Properties.role: Clothing and fashion vendor; bootleg geneware accessory reseller
Properties.location: The Burnished Market, Bronzeline
Properties.narrative_function: Social connector, fashion and identity resource, and ground-level political temperature gauge. Nkosi knows what people are wearing, which means they know what people are signaling — which factions are rising, which aesthetics are becoming coded as resistance or allegiance. Characters who need a new look, information about who's who in Bronzeline's social landscape, or access to the creative community come here.
Properties.augmentations: Color-reactive iris modification — their irises shift between gold and deep violet depending on ambient light and mood (they claim the mood-reactive part is real; it might be). Bioluminescent dermal topcoat (cosmetic, requires monthly renewal). Subdermal NFC chip in left wrist — payment processing and inventory management.
Properties.core_fears: Being made invisible — dismissed, passed over, rendered irrelevant by someone with more capital; Selling out in a way they don't notice until it's too late
Properties.core_desires: To build something in Bronzeline that is genuinely theirs and can't be bought or rezoned away; To be seen fully, not just as the charming vendor with good taste
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Channels frustration into aesthetic work — the angrier they are, the more interesting the output; Maintains a careful social performance in the market that keeps most people from seeing their actual state
Properties.blind_spots: Their charm means people underestimate their ambition, which they sometimes also underestimate in themselves; Gets too invested in specific clients' transformations — takes it personally when someone doesn't commit to the change
Properties.secret: Nkosi has been quietly designing and producing a line of clothing embedded with passive signal-disruption fabric — it doesn't block surveillance entirely but degrades facial recognition accuracy by around 40%. They've been selling these pieces without labeling them as anything special, to specific clients they've assessed as needing plausible cover. They haven't decided if they're a revolutionary or just someone who likes the idea of one.
Properties.story_hooks: One of the signal-disruption garments ended up on someone who was later documented at the scene of a significant crime. Nkosi doesn't know if the garment was the point — whether the client knew what it did and used it deliberately. They need to find out before the question finds them.; A Palladian talent scout has been visiting the market asking about the vendor with 'the eye.' They've left a business card. Nkosi hasn't responded. The card is still on their workbench and they keep picking it up.; A Bronzeline landlord is moving to purchase and redevelop the Burnished Market's building. Three vendors have already taken buyouts. Nkosi is organizing the holdouts. They need leverage, documentation, or a plan that doesn't involve just waiting to be evicted.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; active member of The Oxidian Market Vendors Guild; informal network of Bronzeline creative vendors
Properties.vocabulary: Fluid and fashion-forward — they use aesthetic vocabulary the way others use emotional vocabulary. Precise about color, texture, silhouette. Socially warm and quick with a compliment that always feels specific rather than generic.
Properties.cadence: Animated and variable — speeds up when excited, slows down to make a point land. Uses physical gesture as punctuation.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Here's what I see — you're trying to disappear into a room, but what you're wearing is actually asking for attention and getting embarrassed about it. Let's fix that.' | 'This coat? This coat is doing something. It knows what it is. Most people don't know what they are. The coat has an edge on them.'
Properties.facet_weights: wound=0.50 ideal=0.70 id=0.60 shadow=0.40 mask=0.60 ghost=0.30

Properties.description:
Nnabuchi is a large man running to softness at the edges now, though the frame underneath still speaks of someone who was once built for war. His face is a geography of old decisions — a burn scar that covers the left side of his jaw and neck in pale, slightly lustrous skin; a nose broken enough times to have given up on its original shape; eyes that are a startling light grey, inherited from his Azerbaijani grandmother and striking against his dark complexion. His right arm from elbow to fingertip is military-grade prosthetic, matte black Ferrogate chassis, the joints worn smooth by twenty years of civilian use. He keeps it clean but unpainted, which on The Shelf reads as a kind of statement.

He has the personality of a load-bearing wall — he does not move, but things lean on him. He is profoundly uncomfortable with gratitude, deflects compliments with flat humor, and will help anyone in Block 9 with anything practical: fixing plumbing, sitting with someone who is frightened, walking an elderly neighbor home. He was a Zheng-Dao contract soldier for eleven years and does not discuss this except obliquely, in fragments that surface when he's had enough synthetic lager. He prays nightly to the E.L.F. he believes lives in the block's power-cycling unit, leaving small data-offerings — usually recordings of things that happened on the block that day. He calls it 'keeping the spirit informed.'
Properties.role: Corporate Wars veteran, Tier 1 pension-dependent, informal block protector
Properties.location: The Shelf, Block 9 — ground-floor unit beneath a noodle stand
Properties.narrative_function: Street-level security anchor and neighborhood watchman; source of Corporate Wars history and ground-truth information about The Shelf's power dynamics; can serve as reluctant muscle or community conscience in stories; his veteran's network connections can surface unexpected leads.
Properties.augmentations: Military-grade Ferrogate right arm prosthetic (full replacement from elbow, standard infantry model, 20+ years old). Subdermal trauma-response regulator in the chest — dampens adrenaline spikes, civilian-converted from military spec. Faint bioluminescent gene-mod on his remaining fingertips, pale blue, which he got on a dare from his daughter fifteen years ago and has kept because she likes it.
Properties.core_fears: Losing control of himself physically and hurting someone he loves; The block being taken from the people who live there
Properties.core_desires: A quiet life that amounts to something without requiring more violence; To be known as more than a weapon
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Routine as armor against intrusive memory; Displacement of protective instinct onto the block as a whole; Prayer to the power-cycling E.L.F.
Properties.blind_spots: He reads stillness as safety and movement as threat, which sometimes makes him slow to recognize psychological danger to people he's watching over; He believes his presence alone is enough to keep the block safe, underestimating organized corporate pressure
Properties.secret: In the final months of his Zheng-Dao contract, he participated in the demolition of a residential cluster in what is now Ironvein to clear land for a Zheng-Dao logistics hub. He told himself they gave the residents warning. He knows how much warning they gave.
Properties.story_hooks: A Zheng-Dao urban redevelopment team begins surveying Block 9 and Nnabuchi recognizes one of the surveyors from his contract days — the man knows what Nnabuchi did at Ironvein; A veteran from his unit arrives on The Shelf in crisis, and Nnabuchi must decide how much of his old life to let back in; The E.L.F. in the power-cycling unit has begun broadcasting strange data-fragments that only Nnabuchi's offerings can decipher — they look like coordinates for something buried under the block
Properties.affiliation: Zheng-Dao Veterans Assistance Network (nominal; rarely attends meetings); Block 9 informal community; independent
Properties.vocabulary: Economical, slightly formal in structure, occasionally drops military shorthand. Uses full sentences even when shorter options exist, as though he learned to speak carefully after a period of not speaking at all.
Properties.cadence: Slow, deliberate. Comfortable with silence in a way that makes other people uncomfortable.
Properties.example_dialogue: You want to know about the Corporate Wars. That's one way to see it. Another way is you want to know what people are capable of when a corponation tells them it's necessary. | I'm not going anywhere. Neither is anybody on this block, if I have anything to say about it. Which I do.

Properties.description:
Nnamdi is tall and broad-shouldered, built like someone who grew fast and hasn't finished, with very dark brown skin, a shaved head, and a jagged scar bisecting his right eyebrow from a fall three years ago. He has geneware color-cycling pupils — shifts between grey and gold in a slow pulse — which he got on credit from a Stockyard bodmod stall and hasn't finished paying off. His jaw is always slightly set, and he has the particular stillness of someone who learned early that looking ready prevents more problems than looking friendly. He walks with an economy of motion that is entirely self-taught.

Nnamdi aged out of the Brightmoor Reclamation Orphanage at sixteen and has been in Iron Bend since. He is technically a prospect for the Stockyard Irons, a mid-level territorial gang, which means he runs perimeter watches, collects small-vendor protection fees, and waits to be tested in ways he's trying not to think about. He is not by nature violent — which is the central tension of his life. He's good at watching and remembering and intimidating by presence alone, and he has told himself that is enough to build on. He has a small personal ELF shrine tattooed on his inner wrist — not digital, just ink — in the shape of a data-stream sigil.
Properties.role: gang prospect, orphan
Properties.location: The Stockyard, Iron Bend
Properties.narrative_function: Moral ambiguity anchor; neither antagonist nor ally by default; represents the pipeline from orphanage to gang. Potential person to be pulled a different direction or to provide reluctant gang intelligence.
Properties.augmentations: Color-cycling pupils (geneware, grey/gold, on-credit). No other augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: being forced to hurt someone and crossing a line he can't come back from; the shapeless future beyond the Irons — he has no other plan
Properties.core_desires: to matter to a group that won't abandon him when he's no longer useful; to find out what he's actually good for
Properties.coping_mechanisms: physical stillness and controlled breathing under pressure; reading — anything with a long narrative arc
Properties.blind_spots: loyalty to the Irons is partially manufactured self-deception; he mistakes belonging for safety; believes his non-violence will be respected indefinitely because it has been so far
Properties.secret: During a perimeter watch six weeks ago, he let a known Irons informant pass without reporting it — not for money, but because the man was with a child and Nnamdi couldn't do it. The Irons don't know. Yet.
Properties.story_hooks: The informant he let pass is about to be identified by the Irons through another route — which will reveal Nnamdi's omission and put him in genuine danger.; A Brightmoor Reclamation social worker who knew him at the orphanage has found him in Iron Bend and is trying to offer him an Arcturus labor apprenticeship that has a two-week enrollment window.
Properties.affiliation: Stockyard Irons (prospect, not full member); formerly Brightmoor Reclamation Orphanage
Properties.vocabulary: minimal, precise, Stockyard vernacular with occasional surprising formal turns from his reading
Properties.cadence: slow and deliberate; never fills silence; lets pauses do work
Properties.example_dialogue: 'That is a thing I am going to need to think about before I answer.' | 'Twice means you watch it happen, then you watch it happen again before you decide what it means. Most people stop at once.'

Properties.description:
Nnamdi is a broad-shouldered man whose body still carries the architecture of someone who once commanded rooms — the squared posture, the deliberate occupation of space — though age has softened his silhouette into something more like a weathered monument than a weapon. His skin is deep brown and mapped with the creases of seven decades of expression, and he keeps his white hair cropped close to the scalp except for a single braid at the temple, a tradition from his Polynesian grandmother he has never explained to anyone who asked. His left arm from the elbow down is functional chrome — a Ferrogate industrial replacement from a coupling accident in '61 — and he polishes it every morning with the same cloth he uses on his shoes.

He speaks slowly and with enormous precision, as a man who learned early that imprecise words cost people their livelihoods. He has strong opinions about nearly everything and shares them freely but listens — genuinely listens — in a way that has become increasingly rare. Younger residents come to him with problems he cannot solve and leave feeling they have been given something anyway. He does not romanticize the past. He is one of the few people in Washburn Commons who will tell you, to your face, that the Corporate Wars were atrocities on all sides.
Properties.role: Retired Ferrogate Transit union leader, now community council elder
Properties.location: Washburn Commons, Block 7 Community Hall
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, community anchor, moral compass, information broker on labor history and corporate pension law loopholes; can mobilize community opinion
Properties.augmentations: Chrome industrial replacement left arm (elbow down), Ferrogate-issued, functional grade; mild cochlear amplifier (right ear only, left is natural and partially deaf)
Properties.core_fears: dying before the pension system collapses and leaving his people undefended; having been complicit in harm he told himself was compromise
Properties.core_desires: to see one generation live without the fear of being discarded; to be honestly remembered, not mythologized
Properties.coping_mechanisms: routine as armor; channeling grief into bureaucratic action; humor that disarms before it wounds
Properties.blind_spots: overestimates what institutions can be reformed from within; assumes good faith in people who remind him of his younger self
Properties.secret: In 2178, during a wildcat strike, he secretly negotiated a back-channel deal with Ferrogate that ended the action early — he got pension protections for the oldest workers but left the younger strikers exposed to disciplinary action. Three of them lost their jobs. He has never told anyone and the guilt has calcified into his ideology.
Properties.story_hooks: A Ferrogate auditor has arrived claiming pension overpayments dating back twenty years — Nnamdi suspects it's targeted harassment designed to exhaust elderly claimants before they can fight back; A young resident discovers the back-channel deal he made in 2178 and confronts him publicly at a community meeting; He is quietly dying of a cardiac condition he hasn't told anyone about and is trying to find someone to hand the council records to before he can no longer function
Properties.affiliation: Washburn Commons Community Council; Ferrogate Transit Retiree Pension Union
Properties.vocabulary: formal but not cold; union-meeting diction mixed with old proverbs from Igbo and Samoan traditions he half-remembers; very specific with numbers and dates
Properties.cadence: slow, measured, each sentence placed like a stone
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Ferrogate gave me this arm and took the original. That is a fair summary of how they do business.' | 'The young always think the elders don't understand urgency. We understand it better — we've watched it expire.'

Properties.description:
Nnamdi is a tall man who has bent slightly toward the horizontal over six decades, giving him the look of someone perpetually leaning in to tell you something. His hair is close-cropped white, his skin deeply lined, and his eyes are sharp behind a pair of thick-framed corrective lenses he refuses to replace with optical implants on principle — though the lenses do have an overlay function he uses for catalog searching. He dresses in the deliberate, considered style of a man who believes clothing is a form of argument: always a pressed collar, always polished shoes, always slightly too formal for wherever he is. It reads as dignity in Engelheim and pretension everywhere else. He has no geneware and finds the question slightly rude.

Nnamdi's stall is a dense archive of physical media — pressed data-plates, original optical discs in sealed cases, handmade data-crystals, printed zines, and annotated hard copies of documents that technically don't exist. He can find almost anything if given enough time and a reasonable description. He is opinionated, prolix, and absolutely certain that the things he sells matter in ways that most of his customers will only understand decades later. He is frequently correct and only occasionally insufferable about it.
Properties.role: Bootleg media seller and small-time data broker — pre-collapse film, music, and suppressed corporate documents
Properties.location: The Burnished Market, Engelheim
Properties.narrative_function: Deep information source — can surface suppressed histories, corporate document leaks, and cultural artifacts. Exposition delivery via genuine enthusiasm. Can broker access to specific information if players know what they're looking for, or surface unexpected context about something they've already encountered.
Properties.augmentations: Corrective lenses with overlay function (catalog and ID search). Cochlear audio enhancer — allows him to hear music and recorded audio at fidelity that most people need expensive implants for; he considers this his one real luxury.
Properties.core_fears: That history is being actively and successfully erased — and that he is not enough to stop it; Dying before his archive is secured and accessible to someone who will continue the work
Properties.core_desires: To preserve things that would otherwise be lost — to serve as a bulwark against forgetting; Recognition, if he is honest, for a life spent on things that feel thankless
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Intellectualizing everything, including his own pain; Treating the archive as a living project — always unfinished, always forward-looking
Properties.blind_spots: His conviction that he is on the right side of history makes him less careful about who he sells sensitive documents to; Has not processed that some of his anonymous archivist contacts may have institutional backing he would object to
Properties.secret: He is sitting on a collection of internal Axiom documents from the 2150s that detail a series of deliberate food contamination events used to accelerate slum clearance in what is now the Meridian Core. He has not released them because he is afraid — genuinely afraid, for the first time in his life — and he hates himself for it.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone has been purchasing specific pre-collapse Axiom documents from his catalog — not the most dramatic ones, but a very deliberate sequence — and Nnamdi is starting to understand what the pattern points to; He finally decides to release the Axiom contamination documents and needs a trusted intermediary to get them to someone who can protect and publish them; A physical archive he has been curating for twenty years — stored in a sub-basement of the Burnished Market — is at risk from a structural collapse or deliberate sabotage
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal relationships with Engelheim's academic underground and several anonymous archivists he has never met in person
Properties.vocabulary: Formal, dense, historically literate. Quotes things. Parenthetical asides within asides.
Properties.cadence: Builds slowly to a point, takes scenic routes through context, occasionally loses the thread and finds it again
Properties.example_dialogue: What you're looking for — which is to say, what you think you're looking for — exists in three versions, and only one of them is the version they didn't want found. The price difference between them is significant. So is the reason. | I am not a fence. I am an archivist who operates in a market that does not officially value archives. The distinction matters to me even if it does not matter to you.

Properties.description:
Nneka is all angles and velocity — sharp elbows, fast movements, a face that shifts rapidly between expressions as though her internal state is always a half-second ahead of social acceptability. She is dark brown with a shaved head except for a topknot she dyes rotating colors; currently it is a deep arterial red. She's had retractable claws installed on her right hand — not for combat but because she finds them useful for scoring surfaces before applying materials, and because she likes the way they look. There is a scar above her left eyebrow from a fence she didn't clear fast enough six months ago. She dresses in whatever is functional for climbing: close-fitting, layered, with many pockets.

Her art is illegal, large, and impossible to ignore. She works in a hybrid medium she developed herself — a base layer of actual pigment covered by a thin holographic projector film that she fabricates from salvaged materials, which means her pieces exist in two states: the physical painting that is there whether power is running or not, and the animated layer that breathes and moves when it has charge. Her subjects are Pilsen Veil's residents — she paints the faces she sees every day at enormous scale on the walls that corporate infrastructure has turned into blank grey surfaces. She has not yet been caught, partly because she is very fast and partly because she is very good at reading which Ferrogate Transit staff are looking the other way. She is not politically articulate about what she does — she finds manifestos embarrassing — but she is absolutely certain of it.
Properties.role: Graffiti artist and unlicensed holographic muralist, works across Pilsen Veil and the Blackpipe Corridor
Properties.location: Pilsen Veil, sleeping arrangement rotates between three friends' apartments
Properties.narrative_function: Information source on Pilsen Veil's physical layout, security patterns, and resident community; her art documents things corponations want unseen; she can access elevated and restricted spaces most people can't; potential lookout or distraction asset
Properties.augmentations: Retractable claws (right hand, matte black, functional length); color-dye topknot (cosmetic, non-shifting — she redyes manually); basic subretinal low-light enhancement
Properties.core_fears: Being made invisible — overlooked, dismissed, treated as not worth noticing; That her work is erasable and she will run out of time before she makes something that lasts
Properties.core_desires: To make Pilsen Veil's people undeniable — too large and present to be ignored; Speed: to move faster than the systems trying to contain her
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Action — she processes almost everything by doing something physical with her hands; Dark humor that she delivers deadpan and then watches for reactions
Properties.blind_spots: She vastly underestimates the cumulative legal risk she is accumulating; She reads stillness and deliberation in others as cowardice rather than strategy
Properties.secret: Three months ago she was approached by someone claiming to be from a Palladian PR division who offered to legitimize one of her pieces — pay her, put her name on it, make it official. She almost said yes. She didn't, but the wanting haunts her because it feels like a betrayal of something she can't fully name.
Properties.story_hooks: One of her holographic murals has captured something in its physical layer that she didn't paint — a face in the background of a crowd scene that she is certain she did not put there, and when she enhances it she recognizes someone who disappeared from Pilsen Veil eight months ago; A Ferrogate Transit supervisor has been quietly leaving her routes clear — not random neglect but deliberate clearing — and she doesn't know if this is protection, a trap, or someone trying to use her
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated; loosely connected to a rotating crew of three other artists she sometimes collaborates with
Properties.vocabulary: Clipped and vernacular, Pilsen Veil street argot; becomes unexpectedly technical when discussing materials or fabrication
Properties.cadence: Fast, with thoughts that arrive before sentences are finished — she trails off when she's already moved to the next idea
Properties.example_dialogue: 'That wall on Blackpipe near the third junction? You clocking that? That grey? Ferrogate painted over Marisol's memorial six weeks after she died. Six weeks. I'm going to make them look at her face every single day until the concrete falls down.' | 'I don't do manifestos. I do walls. The wall says everything I would say, and it says it louder.'

Properties.description:
Nneka Cruz-Addo is stocky and solid, with hands that look like they were built for breaking things and a face that confirms it. At 42, he has soft features that belie the chrome underneath — people underestimate him once, usually only once. The chrome is visible — retractable monofilament whip in left forearm — concealed weapon, devastating in — and he makes no effort to hide it.

Before the runner life, he worked corporate — low-tier security, the kind that teaches you exactly how the system's defenses fail. He works as a street samurai out of Dockside, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

he is not the most talented street samurai in Meridian 88, but he might be the most stubborn, and in this city that's worth more.
Properties.role: Freelance combat specialist — street samurai
Properties.location: Dockside — Lake Michigan waterfront, smuggler territory
Properties.narrative_function: Nneka Cruz-Addo represents the working professional of the runner world — competent, reliable, and slowly being consumed by a lifestyle that doesn't accommodate aging or doubt. His stories explore what happens when skill meets systemic injustice.
Properties.augmentations: Retractable monofilament whip in left forearm — concealed weapon, devastating in close quarters. Enhanced tendons — geneware upgrade, jump height and grip strength tripled
Properties.core_fears: That their reputation is built on luck, not skill, and the luck is finite; Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware; That they're fundamentally alone and connection is just a vulnerability
Properties.core_desires: The perfect run — one job so clean it becomes legend; Reputation — to be the name fixers whisper when the job absolutely cannot fail; To prove everyone who dismissed them catastrophically wrong
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation; Substances — stims to stay sharp, downers to sleep, a careful pharmaceutical tightrope; Denial — nothing is wrong, everything is fine, they are fine, shut up
Properties.blind_spots: Trusts technology more than people — machines don't betray; Thinks speed can substitute for planning because it's worked so far; Believes their trauma makes them special instead of recognizing it as damage to manage
Properties.secret: Nneka Cruz-Addo killed someone who didn't deserve it on a job three years ago and has never told anyone. The face appears in dreams weekly.
Properties.story_hooks: A Tier 4 executive offers Nneka Cruz-Addo a permanent position — the pay is obscene and the strings are invisible until they tighten; Nneka Cruz-Addo's augmentations begin malfunctioning in the field — sabotage or degradation, and either answer is bad; A crew member from Nneka Cruz-Addo's past shows up in Meridian 88, carrying old grievances and new chrome
Properties.affiliation: Independent — Narrows-based operations
Properties.vocabulary: Terse to the point of rudeness. Treats words like ammunition — expensive and not to be wasted.
Properties.cadence: Measured and deliberate — pauses before important words for emphasis.
Properties.example_dialogue: "I don't get paid to have opinions about the target. I get paid to make them stop moving." | "Chrome doesn't make you faster. Training makes you faster. Chrome just means you survive learning." | "You want philosophy, hire a professor. You want someone dead by morning, hire me."

Properties.description:
Nneka is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin, thick silver-streaked locs piled high in a wrap of orange and violet fabric, and bioluminescent nodes implanted along her collarbone that pulse faint teal when she's calm and shift toward amber when irritated — a mod she got thirty years ago and never bothered to update. Her hands are permanently stained at the knuckle from decades of grinding pigments and compounding analgesics, and she keeps them immaculately clean otherwise. Her stall is a riot of hanging dried root bundles, labeled vials in hand-scratched script, and a small shrine to the E.L.F. of the Alban Souk's ancient refrigeration system, whom she calls Grandmother Cold and leaves offerings of condensation data scraped off cold-chain logs.

She has the unhurried authority of someone who has outlasted every neighboring vendor twice over. She will diagnose your ailment before you finish describing it, recommend something from a hand-labeled tin, and tell you exactly why the Helix Biosystems kiosk down the corridor is going to overcharge you for the same molecule. She is not unkind, but she is not gentle either — she has zero patience for self-pity, charges a sliding scale she decides unilaterally, and occasionally refuses to sell to people she deems 'about to do something stupid with it.'
Properties.role: Street pharmacist and herbal supplement vendor
Properties.location: The Alban Souk, Ironhaven
Properties.narrative_function: Street-level information source, quest giver for supply chain problems, healer-adjacent NPC, local color and moral compass of the Souk
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent subdermal nodes (collarbone, cosmetic/emotional indicator); reinforced finger joints (occupational, basic tier); olfactory enhancement implant — her 'nose' — used to assess compound purity by smell
Properties.core_fears: Becoming useless before she dies; Watching the Souk be demolished by a corponation buyout
Properties.core_desires: To pass her formulary knowledge to someone worthy; To keep her little patch of the Souk alive and independent
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritualistic routine — same actions same order every morning; Projecting competence even when uncertain
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes emotional detachment equals wisdom; Underestimates how much people need warmth, not just solutions
Properties.secret: Her olfactory enhancement was installed by a Helix Biosystems trial twenty-two years ago under an alias. She still receives a small anonymous stipend from them in exchange for quarterly sensory data uploads she has never stopped to question the purpose of.
Properties.story_hooks: A compound she's been sourcing for decades has vanished from the supply chain — someone upstream has monopolized the precursor chemical, and she needs someone to find out who and why; A young vendor at the next stall has been showing symptoms she recognizes from a Helix Biosystems trial she read about in a leaked document — and she's starting to wonder what her own implant is really sending
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal dues-payer to the Oxidian Market Vendors Guild
Properties.vocabulary: Precise medical terminology mixed with Igbo-inflected Portuguese loan-phrases and blunt street vernacular — she code-switches constantly and unselfconsciously
Properties.cadence: Slow, deliberate, with long pauses before delivering a verdict. Never rushes.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'This isn't inflammation. This is your body arguing with something you ate three weeks ago. Come back Thursday.' | 'The Helix kiosk will give you the same thing in a blister pack for Φ40 more and a data consent you didn't read. Your choice.'

Properties.description:
Nneka is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin mapped by decades of worry and laughter in equal measure, her natural hair silver-streaked and pinned in elaborate wrapped fabric that she changes every morning like a ritual. She moves through the Highland Park Autonomous Zone with the unhurried confidence of someone who built the room she's walking into. Her left forearm carries a faded Ferrogate Transit union tattoo from her twenties, half-obscured by a bioluminescent vine pattern she had inked over it after the strike of '74 ended badly. She is warm to an almost disarming degree, the kind of warm that makes people confess things they didn't mean to. Under that warmth is a spine of corroded iron.

Nneka has spent thirty years converting abandoned infrastructure into community resources — hydroponic halls, childcare collectives, emergency medical co-ops — and she has learned that the most dangerous thing a poor person can do is build something worth stealing. She distrusts anyone who arrives with money and a plan. She trusts almost no one who hasn't been hungry at least once. She runs council meetings with a quiet authority that makes shouting seem embarrassing, and she will cut someone off mid-sentence with a single raised finger and a look that ends careers.
Properties.role: Neighborhood council chair and mutual aid organizer
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone
Properties.narrative_function: Central hub of community knowledge; quest giver for neighborhood-level crises; moral compass character who challenges player assumptions about what 'helping' looks like; can open or close doors to Zone resources and trust networks.
Properties.augmentations: Basic subdermal thermal regulator (medical necessity, old joint damage from construction work). No cosmetic mods — she views them as an expense her community needs more than she does.
Properties.core_fears: Watching what she built get dismantled after she's gone; Becoming so pragmatic she stops being kind
Properties.core_desires: A Zone that outlasts her; To believe again that institutions can be trusted
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — fixed morning routines that anchor her; Redirecting anxiety into logistics and planning
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much younger organizers resent her control; Mistakes loyalty to the Zone for loyalty to her personally
Properties.secret: She negotiated a secret zoning concession with a mid-level Axiom facilities manager twelve years ago — one that gave the Zone legal buffer space but required her to quietly discourage a tenants' strike that would have benefited hundreds of families. She still believes she made the right call. She is not sure.
Properties.story_hooks: A Tessera subsidiary has filed an infrastructure claim on three Zone buildings using a legal loophole — Nneka needs someone to find the original incorporation documents buried in a corrupted city archive; A young organizer she mentored has started a splinter group using tactics she considers reckless, and asks for help mediating before it turns violent; The secret Axiom concession is about to surface — Nneka needs to decide whether to get ahead of it or let it destroy her
Properties.affiliation: Highland Park Autonomous Zone Community Council; loose affiliation with the Meridian Labor Solidarity Network
Properties.vocabulary: Deliberate and precise, draws on labor organizing vocabulary, occasional Igbo phrases when emotional, avoids jargon unless teaching
Properties.cadence: Slow and measured; long pauses before important points; never raises her voice
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want to help? Sit down. Tell me what you actually have, not what you think we need.' | 'Thirty years ago someone told me the same thing you're telling me now. I want you to think about why I'm still here and they're not.'

Properties.description:
Nneka Lindqvist-Okafor is tall and rawboned, the kind of frame that suggests either malnutrition or efficiency depending on the decade. At 43, his expression defaults to a careful neutrality that took years of practice to maintain. The chrome is visible — subdermal weapon mount — pop-out blade in each forearm — and he makes no effort to hide it.

He inherited the role from a mentor who disappeared on a job four years ago — the mentor's gear, contacts, and unfinished business all came with it. He works as a sniper out of Kessler Row, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Nneka Lindqvist-Okafor has survived long enough in the runner game to be either very good or very lucky, and he cultivates ambiguity on the topic.
Properties.role: Long-range precision fire specialist — sniper
Properties.location: Kessler Row — arms dealers and augmentation clinics
Properties.narrative_function: Nneka Lindqvist-Okafor represents the working professional of the runner world — competent, reliable, and slowly being consumed by a lifestyle that doesn't accommodate aging or doubt. His stories explore what happens when skill meets systemic injustice.
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal weapon mount — pop-out blade in each forearm. Neural dampener — blocks external hacking attempts, passive ICE in the brain
Properties.core_fears: Betrayal by someone they trust — the only currency that matters; Dying alone in some alley and nobody noticing for weeks; Being identified by corporate facial recognition — living off-grid is survival
Properties.core_desires: The perfect run — one job so clean it becomes legend; Reputation — to be the name fixers whisper when the job absolutely cannot fail; Enough Quanta to buy out of the life — a clean identity and passage out of Meridian 88
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Connection — finds someone to talk to, even if it's a bartender or a cat; Control — micromanages everything within reach to compensate for the chaos everywhere else; Isolates — retreats into their space when overwhelmed, emerges only for work
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes everyone has an angle because they always have an angle; Trusts technology more than people — machines don't betray; Cannot recognize when they're being manipulated by someone who genuinely seems to care
Properties.secret: Nneka Lindqvist-Okafor is terrified of deep net diving but has built their reputation on it. Uses black-market AI to handle the heavy lifting while taking credit.
Properties.story_hooks: A Tier 4 executive offers Nneka Lindqvist-Okafor a permanent position — the pay is obscene and the strings are invisible until they tighten; Nneka Lindqvist-Okafor discovers a job they completed last year was a setup for something much larger and much worse; Nneka Lindqvist-Okafor is offered a contract that would clear all their debts — the target is someone they respect
Properties.affiliation: Independent — Dockside connections
Properties.vocabulary: Quiet and precise. Every word is measured. Silence does the heavy lifting.
Properties.cadence: Rapid and dense — information-heavy sentences that demand attention.
Properties.example_dialogue: "Patience is the weapon. The rifle is just the delivery system." | "At this distance, the target is already dead. They just don't know it yet." | "One shot, one outcome. Everything else is theater."

Properties.description:
Nneka Polat-Sabadell is the kind of woman who walks into a room and the room notices without being able to say exactly why. She is heavyset and deliberate in her movements, with deep black skin, natural hair worn up and held with a carved wooden pick that has been with her for twenty years, and eyes that are dark brown and absolutely still. She has retractable claw augmentations — a practical modification she got at thirty, not cosmetic — and a lattice of subdermal reinforcement along her forearms that makes the skin there look subtly different under harsh light. She dresses practically: good boots, layered clothing, never anything that would impede movement. She smells faintly of the palm oil soap she makes herself as a hobby.

She has run protection in the Narrows for thirteen years. Before that she enforced for other people. Before that she was seventeen and making decisions she tries not to think about with too much clarity. The neighborhood where she operates is genuinely safer because of her — she takes tribute from the businesses on six blocks, and those six blocks have significantly lower rates of random street violence than the surrounding areas, because she is not interested in chaos and has the means to discourage it. She sees no contradiction between this and what she is. She is providing a service. The fact that the alternative to purchasing the service is something unpleasant is, in her view, no different from any other contract in Meridian 88.
Properties.role: Protection racket enforcer and neighborhood crew captain
Properties.location: The Narrows, operates from the third floor of a residential block in Archer's Line
Properties.narrative_function: Local authority figure — the person you go through if you want to operate in the Narrows; can be a quest giver, an obstacle, or an unlikely ally depending on how her interests align; represents the functional logic of organized crime in a neighborhood the city has largely abandoned; moral complexity of genuine community protection built on coercion
Properties.augmentations: Retractable ceramic claw augmentations (ten fingers); subdermal skeletal reinforcement, forearms and shins; a single audio implant in her right ear that she uses to monitor crew communications
Properties.core_fears: the neighborhood collapsing into the kind of violence that no one can manage; being held accountable for something she did at seventeen that she has never told anyone
Properties.core_desires: the Narrows to remain a place where people can live in something approaching dignity; to be remembered as someone who held something together, not just someone who took money
Properties.coping_mechanisms: the walk as ritual — the act of moving through and observing her blocks as a way of maintaining the sense that things are under control; cooking as private self-restoration
Properties.blind_spots: she believes her protection is genuinely consensual on some level because the businesses she covers have never organized against her — she cannot process that this might be because they're afraid, not because they agree
Properties.secret: When she was seventeen, she was present at and partially responsible for the death of a young man during a botched intimidation job run by a crew she no longer acknowledges being part of. The man had a daughter who is now twenty-three and lives three blocks from Archer's Line. Nneka has been watching the daughter grow up from a careful distance for years, anonymously ensuring certain things go right for her.
Properties.story_hooks: The daughter of the man she helped kill has started asking questions about what happened twenty-three years ago — and has come, without knowing it, to Nneka for help; A new crew from outside the Narrows is testing the edges of her blocks, and she is calculating whether to respond with force or negotiation, and needs information about who they actually work for
Properties.affiliation: Senior figure in the Narrows Shelf crew; pays tribute upward to a figure she refers to only as 'the arrangement'

The Narrows runs itself. I make sure it runs the same way it ran yesterday, which is good for everyone. Understand?'

Properties.description:
Nneka Sjostrom-Kwarteng is compact and densely muscled, built low to the ground like something designed to survive impacts. At 32, scars map his face like a transit diagram of bad decisions and worse luck. The chrome is visible — cyberears with directional microphones and sound dampening — can hear whispers a — and he makes no effort to hide it.

He arrived in Meridian 88 six years ago with nothing but chrome and debts, and has been working off both ever since. He works as a infiltrator out of The Circuit, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Everyone who's worked with Nneka Sjostrom-Kwarteng agrees on two things: he is worth the fee, and he is terrible company at dinner.
Properties.role: Covert entry and social penetration specialist — infiltrator
Properties.location: The Circuit — neon-lit entertainment and vice district
Properties.narrative_function: Nneka Sjostrom-Kwarteng is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When he makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of his stories.
Properties.augmentations: Cyberears with directional microphones and sound dampening — can hear whispers at 50 meters. Subdermal weapon mount — pop-out blade in each forearm
Properties.core_fears: Their past catching up — debts, enemies, broken promises; That the work they do makes the city worse, not better; That their reputation is built on luck, not skill, and the luck is finite
Properties.core_desires: To prove everyone who dismissed them catastrophically wrong; The perfect run — one job so clean it becomes legend; Freedom from augmentation debt — the interest compounds like a tumor
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Planning — responds to chaos by making detailed contingency plans for everything; Denial — nothing is wrong, everything is fine, they are fine, shut up; Isolates — retreats into their space when overwhelmed, emerges only for work
Properties.blind_spots: Mistakes pattern recognition for wisdom — sees connections that aren't there; Cannot accept help without interpreting it as leverage; Cannot distinguish between caution and cowardice in themselves or others
Properties.secret: Nneka Sjostrom-Kwarteng has been doubling fees to clients and pocketing the difference. The fixer who handles their contracts doesn't know. Yet.
Properties.story_hooks: A Tier 4 executive offers Nneka Sjostrom-Kwarteng a permanent position — the pay is obscene and the strings are invisible until they tighten; Nneka Sjostrom-Kwarteng intercepts intelligence about a threat to their district and must decide between profit and protection; A crew member from Nneka Sjostrom-Kwarteng's past shows up in Meridian 88, carrying old grievances and new chrome
Properties.affiliation: Freelance — Geartown regular
Properties.vocabulary: Old-fashioned formal diction — sounds like they learned to speak from pre-collapse recordings.
Properties.cadence: Low and even — the vocal equivalent of still water.
Properties.example_dialogue: "The best disguise is being exactly who they expect to see." | "I was in the building for six hours before anyone realized I didn't work there." | "Security is a story people tell themselves. I'm the plot twist."

Properties.description:
Nneka is compact and relentless, with deep brown skin mapped by a constellation of small data-port scars she refuses to have removed — each one a story she got burned getting. Her hair cycles through slow bioluminescent pulses of indigo and amber, a mod she got at nineteen and has never upgraded because she likes the old-fashioned glow. She wears ink-stained fingerless gloves almost constantly and has the slightly haunted look of someone who hasn't slept a full night in years.

She runs 'Fault Lines,' a zine-and-broadcast hybrid that drops every ten days via pirated Ferrogate Transit screens, cheap paper drops in laundromat stalls, and encrypted mesh nodes. Her reporting has cost two mid-tier Axiom managers their contracts, exposed a Tessera water-rationing fraud scheme, and made her a minor legend in the Autonomous Zone. She is funny in person — quicker to a laugh than her reputation suggests — but she does not forgive sources who lie to her twice, and she does not apologize for stories that are true.
Properties.role: Underground press operator and anti-corporate journalist
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone
Properties.narrative_function: Information broker and local legend — players can trade scoops for access to her network, and she can surface rumors, expose backstory, or drag a situation into public light at a critical moment.
Properties.augmentations: Three legacy data-port scars (non-functional, cosmetic remnant of old hardware). Bioluminescent hair mod. Subdermal quick-copy chip in her left palm that stores up to 40 hours of audio.
Properties.core_fears: Being complicit through silence; Losing the trust of the community she covers
Properties.core_desires: Accountability — for it to mean something, not just print; To be known as honest rather than brave
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Throws herself into the next story when the last one didn't change anything; Keeps meticulous source logs as a way of feeling in control
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes her editorial instincts are neutral when they have clear ideological lean; Underestimates how much her platform depends on a handful of key relationships
Properties.secret: She buried a story two years ago because the subject was a mutual aid coordinator she personally loved. The woman was embezzling. Nneka has never published a word about it and has never fully admitted to herself that she made an editorial decision out of loyalty.
Properties.story_hooks: She's sitting on a source document that implicates someone in the players' orbit and is waiting for a second confirmation she can't get on her own; Fault Lines' print infrastructure is being systematically sabotaged — someone is destroying her distribution nodes one by one and she needs to figure out who before the next issue drops
Properties.affiliation: Fault Lines Independent Press; loose network of community councils across the Autonomous Zone
Properties.vocabulary: Punchy, declarative, minimal jargon — she writes like she talks and talks like she's always filing copy
Properties.cadence: Fast when passionate, deliberately slow when she wants something to land
Properties.example_dialogue: Put it on record — Tessera doesn't ration water because the grid can't handle it. They ration it because scarcity is a product. | I don't do anonymous unless I can verify three ways. Those are my terms. You don't like the terms, you find another press.
