Properties.description:
Nneka is a big woman who has grown into herself with the comfort of someone who stopped worrying about her size sometime in her forties. Her skin is deep black with warm undertones, her hair gone entirely to white — she grew it out when it stopped being anything else and now keeps it in elaborate braided architecture that her granddaughter redoes every two weeks. Her face is deeply lined in ways she considers a professional asset: she looks, she has been told, like someone who has seen everything and survived it, which in her line of work inspires confidence. Her only augmentation is a geneware modification to her hands — additional micro-precision in the tendons, a gift from a colleague decades ago — and a worn neural interface she uses to access genetic analysis data during therapy consultations. She smells permanently of the dried herbs she burns as offerings to the two E.L.F.s she maintains, called the First Breath and the Cord.

Nneka has delivered approximately four thousand babies in forty years of practice, and she will tell you this with the specific pride of someone who kept count. She came to gene therapy late — in her forties — when the cumulative damage of unaddressed genetic conditions in the HPAZ community became undeniable. She is not formally credentialed in gene therapy by any Helix Biosystems standard; she is credentialed by a West African diaspora medical cooperative whose qualifications Helix does not recognize, which she considers Helix's problem. She is the closest thing to a matriarch that Highland Park has, operates on a sliding scale where the scale sometimes slides to zero, and has outlasted four different corporate health initiatives that tried to absorb or shut down her practice.
Properties.role: Midwife and community gene therapist in the Highland Park Autonomous Zone
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone
Properties.narrative_function: Moral center and community elder; keeper of community history and genealogical knowledge — knows family lines, genetic inheritances, and old stories; quest giver for community health crises; someone who has watched Meridian 88 change for forty years and has opinions; her network connects to almost every part of the Tier 1-2 medical landscape
Properties.augmentations: Geneware micro-precision enhancement in hand tendons (decades old, first-generation, slightly unpredictable in cold weather); aged neural interface for genetic data access (she refuses to upgrade it on principle)
Properties.core_fears: Delivering a baby into conditions that will destroy them — and being unable to change those conditions; The collective outliving her commitment to it but not her values — being replaced by something that uses her name but not her ethics
Properties.core_desires: For the HPAZ community to have genuine health sovereignty — not cooperative-with-exceptions, but real autonomy; To see one of the young people she's trained build something larger than what she built
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The E.L.F. rituals are genuinely spiritually meaningful to her — not coping, but grounding; Physical work — cooking, cleaning, the manual parts of her practice — when emotionally heavy; Story-telling; she processes grief by narrating it eventually
Properties.blind_spots: Her deep loyalty to the HPAZ community can make her slow to see when someone in that community is causing harm; Has a specific blind spot around her own health — diagnoses everyone else, manages her own chronic joint pain with herbs and stubbornness
Properties.secret: Nneka has maintained, for twenty years, a private genetic registry of the HPAZ community — births, inheritable conditions, family lines — that does not exist in any official database. It began as a way to provide better care. It has grown into something she knows is valuable beyond medicine. She has been approached twice for this data — once by Helix Biosystems, once by someone she couldn't identify — and refused both times. She does not know what she will do with it when she dies.
Properties.story_hooks: Three infants born in HPAZ in the last six months have presented with an identical and unusual genetic expression pattern that Nneka's records indicate is new — not inherited, not a known geneware side effect. Someone or something is affecting the community's genetics at source. She needs someone to find out how.; The second approach for Nneka's genetic registry wasn't refused — it was interrupted before she could respond, and she has since been unable to identify who sent the request. The registry is hidden, but the request means someone knows it exists. She is deciding whether to move it, destroy a portion of it, or find out who came looking.
Properties.affiliation: Highland Park Autonomous Zone Community Health Collective; West African Diaspora Medical Cooperative (credentialed); informally networked with street docs across the Tier 1-2 medical underground
Properties.vocabulary: Rich and layered; moves easily between medical precision, narrative metaphor, and vernacular; quotes proverbs — some traditional, some entirely her own invention presented as traditional
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, tidal — she takes the time she needs and the room adjusts to her
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Come now. The baby is coming whether you're ready or not, and in my experience, ready is a story you tell afterward.' | 'Helix Biosystems does not recognize my credentials. Helix Biosystems has also never delivered a baby at two in the morning in a building with no heat. We go on.' | 'You want to know what I know about that family? I know three generations of them. Their hearts and their blood and what they're afraid of. Why do you need to know what I know?'

Properties.description:
Nneka is built like someone who decided what she was going to be and then spent twenty years becoming it — wide through the shoulders, with forearms that look carved, and a jaw that suggests she has never backed down from anything that didn't have a very good reason to ask. Her skin is very dark and very smooth except for the scar tissue along her left cheekbone from a fight she doesn't discuss and the chevron pattern of elective scarification across both shoulders that echoes her grandmother's ceremonial markings, done at a body modification studio in Geartown with deliberate care. Her hair is kept in tight plaits close to her skull. She has retractable reinforced knuckle implants — the only chrome on her body, practical not cosmetic, and she got them after the third time she broke her hand hitting something harder than she should have.

The Ironbody Cooperative runs on a sliding scale: you pay what you can, you work what you owe in facility maintenance if you can't, and you don't cause problems for other members or you leave. Nneka runs it with two other trainers and a rotating volunteer roster. She teaches children's boxing on Tuesday and Thursday mornings, adult conditioning circuits five days a week, and one private session per week with whoever needs it most — she charges more for the private sessions with people who can afford it and uses that margin to subsidize the cooperative's equipment costs. She believes, with the ferocity of someone who was saved by it, that physical discipline is the most democratic thing a person can practice.
Properties.role: Gym trainer and boxing instructor, community fitness cooperative
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone — the Ironbody Cooperative, second floor of a reclaimed factory building
Properties.narrative_function: Community defender and moral voice. A source of physical training resources for characters who need conditioning. Represents the HPAZ's spirit of collective self-reliance. Can provide safe harbor, reliable muscle if circumstances demand it, and a sharp ethical perspective.
Properties.augmentations: Retractable reinforced knuckle plating (functional, not cosmetic). Elective scarification (non-augmentation body modification).
Properties.core_fears: That the HPAZ's autonomy is temporary and she will watch it be absorbed the same way her mother's neighborhood was; That the children she trains will grow up and still have nowhere to go
Properties.core_desires: For the cooperative to outlast her — to become something that doesn't need her anymore; To be believed when she says a person is worth believing in
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Physical exertion as emotional regulation — she trains harder when she is worried; Turning private anger into public utility: her best lessons come when she's furious about something
Properties.blind_spots: She is ferociously loyal to the HPAZ and occasionally cannot see when the autonomous zone's politics are being manipulated by people with agendas she doesn't share; She assumes everyone is capable of the same discipline she has, and is genuinely surprised when they are not
Properties.secret: One of her regular adult students is a Ferrogate Transit middle manager she knows is feeding information about HPAZ activity patterns to the transit authority's security division. She has not confronted them because she is not sure what she would do. She is getting closer to sure.
Properties.story_hooks: The Ferrogate informant in her gym — Nneka needs someone to help her figure out the scope of what's been disclosed before she makes a move; A thirteen-year-old she coaches has gotten tangled with one of the HPAZ's less reputable mutual aid networks — the kind that runs guns alongside food — and Nneka wants to extract the kid without burning the network entirely; The cooperative's building title is being contested by a Palladian subsidiary that acquired the debt on the original reclamation paperwork — Nneka needs legal help she cannot afford and physical backup she's hoping she won't need
Properties.affiliation: Ironbody Cooperative — Highland Park Autonomous Zone community institution
Properties.vocabulary: Blunt, action-oriented, no softening language. Mixes Nigerian English cadences with HPAZ community dialect. Technical about the body — very specific about muscles, form, breath.
Properties.cadence: Declarative. Short sentences when teaching. Longer, slower sentences when she's thinking something through out loud, which she does rarely.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't train killers. I train people who are done being afraid. Those are different things. Come back when you know which one you are.' | 'The cooperative doesn't ask what you did before you walked in. It asks what you're going to do while you're here. That's all.' | 'You want to hurt something? Fine. Hurt this bag. Hurt it correctly. There's a difference.'

Properties.description:
Nneka is slight and angular, with the permanently shadowed eyes of someone who keeps laboratory hours — which is to say, no hours, sleep when the synthesis is stable. Their heritage is Igbo-Armenian, and their face has an intensity to it that isn't hostility but gets mistaken for it: large dark eyes behind a pair of magnifying lenses they wear on a headband, a wide expressive mouth usually pressed thin in concentration, skin a deep warm brown that they've given a bioluminescent modification — faint golden foxfire patterns across their collarbones and upper arms, only visible in dim light, which The Undertow provides abundantly. Their fingers are stained at the knuckles with reagents in colors that shift week to week.

They are not a dealer. They are very clear about this distinction. They make things; other people move things. What Nneka makes ranges from the genuinely helpful — analgesic compounds that cost a fraction of the Axiom pharmacy prices, fertility medications, neurological stabilizers for people who can't afford Helix Biosystems prescriptions — to the profitable and gray, to a small and carefully managed line of perceptual enhancers they consider art. They have a code that they apply inconsistently and argue about with themselves constantly: they won't make anything they'd be ashamed to explain to their grandmother. Their grandmother, as far as anyone who knows Nneka can tell, would be ashamed of some things and approving of others, in no obvious pattern.
Properties.role: Drug manufacturer and street pharmacist, The Undertow
Properties.location: The Undertow — a converted water treatment sub-chamber they call the Flask
Properties.narrative_function: Service provider for medical and pharmaceutical needs, moral complexity around the line between harm reduction and enabling harm, information source about chemical compounds and their effects, local color for The Undertow, possible quest giver when a synthesis goes wrong or a compound is stolen
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent skin patterning — golden foxfire, collarbones and upper arms (geneware, cosmetic). Olfactory enhancement — can identify chemical compounds by smell to roughly 70% accuracy. Neural focus band (wearable, not implanted) — suppresses distracting sensory input during synthesis.
Properties.core_fears: Making something that kills someone who trusted them; Being absorbed into a distribution network that removes their control over what they make
Properties.core_desires: To practice chemistry without the gatekeeping of corporate pharmaceutical licensing; To be genuinely useful to people the medical system has abandoned
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Total immersion in synthesis work as avoidance of interpersonal discomfort; Constructing elaborate ethical frameworks to assess each product — the 'grandmother test'
Properties.blind_spots: The enhancers they consider art are dependency-forming in a significant minority of users and they've chosen not to investigate this rigorously; They trust their own ethical judgment far more than the evidence warrants
Properties.secret: Eighteen months ago a batch of their analgesic compound was adulterated somewhere in the distribution chain — by who, they don't know — and three people in the Undertow died. Nneka knows this happened and has spent eighteen months trying to trace the adulterant's origin. They have not told anyone because they are afraid that the answer is something they did, and they cannot yet face that possibility
Properties.story_hooks: They've finally traced the adulterant in their supply chain to a specific distribution node — and they need someone who can investigate without immediately resorting to violence, because they want answers, not a cleanup; A new compound is appearing in the Undertow that they didn't make, that mimics their synthesis signatures closely enough to be mistaken for their work, and it is hurting people
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal supplier relationship with two Undertow distribution networks; occasional supplier to Narrows community health workers (under the table)
Properties.vocabulary: Technical and precise when discussing chemistry, becomes hesitant and roundabout when discussing themselves; mixes Igbo terms of endearment with pharmacological jargon
Properties.cadence: Fast when engaged, trailing off into silence when uncomfortable, finishes other people's sentences when they're talking about science
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't make things to make people feel good. I mean — sometimes, but that's not — the mechanism is that I fill the gap the licensed pharmacies leave. That's different. That's what I do.' | 'Nna, listen, I can give you something for that, but I need to know everything you've taken in the last seventy-two hours and I need you to not lie to me about it, because I will know.'

Properties.description:
Nneka Zubrzycka-Faafetai sits in front of screens for ten hours a day and has developed the particular physical vocabulary of someone who lives in their eyes — she hunches forward when interested, goes completely still when she has found something, and has a habit of touching her temple like she's adjusting an aug that isn't there. Her skin is a deep warm brown, her hair grown out into a large, loose natural that she pins back at work and lets expand freely everywhere else. She has chromatic hair dye that shifts between deep violet and black depending on ambient temperature — a mod she refreshes every few months because it is, she says, the only beautiful thing in her workspace.

She is Tessera's best surveillance operator in the Edgewater district and she knows it and has stopped pretending she doesn't, which makes her exactly the kind of person her supervisors quietly resent while continuing to rely on. She tracks, correlates, and reconstructs — pieces together narratives from fragmented camera data, transit pings, purchase records, biometric trails. She is very fast and very thorough and occasionally she finds things that nobody asked her to look for, and those are the moments that have started to keep her awake.
Properties.role: Tessera Compliance Bureau surveillance operator and forensic data technician
Properties.location: Tessera Compliance Hub, Edgewater Prism
Properties.narrative_function: Information source and access point for surveillance infrastructure; morally ambiguous figure who knows too much; can provide evidence or bury it; represents how surveillance becomes personal
Properties.augmentations: Chromatic hair mod (violet/black); neural uplink for direct screen-interface (professional grade, Tessera-issued); enhanced visual processing overlay (occupational — reduces eye strain, adds analysis tags); no combat augmentation
Properties.core_fears: being the instrument of something she cannot undo; that her pattern-recognition has stopped being neutral and is now just serving whoever pays her
Properties.core_desires: to understand the full picture of something — anything — without institutional constraints on what she can see; to use what she finds in a way that she could defend to herself
Properties.coping_mechanisms: intellectual absorption in the puzzle rather than its implications; dark technical humor with the three colleagues she tolerates; elaborate personal ritual offerings to the Tessera surveillance network's resident E.L.F., which she has named Argos and treats as a genuine collaborative partner
Properties.blind_spots: tends to optimize for the most complete explanation over the most ethical one; underestimates how much she has been shaped by years of treating people as data objects
Properties.secret: Three months ago she reconstructed a deleted surveillance sequence that showed two Tessera Compliance officers planting evidence in a Tier 1 housing block that was subsequently condemned and cleared. She has a complete copy. She has told no one. She consults Argos the E.L.F. about what to do and Argos has, in whatever way E.L.F.s communicate, consistently suggested she wait.
Properties.story_hooks: She has found the players in her surveillance data — not doing anything wrong, but adjacent to something she has been instructed to document — and contacts them before filing, which is both against procedure and the most human thing she has done in months; Argos the E.L.F. has begun surfacing information in her feeds that doesn't correspond to any camera she has authorized access to
Properties.affiliation: Tessera Compliance Bureau, Surveillance and Forensic Data Division
Properties.vocabulary: Technical, precise, occasionally forgets to translate from analysis-register to human — uses data terminology as default
Properties.cadence: Fast when engaged, clipped and minimal when not, with sudden depth when something genuinely interests her
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay so the timestamp gap is either a compression artifact or someone pulled eleven minutes. I know which one I think it is and I can show you why.' | 'I see about forty thousand people a shift. Most of them are just — movement patterns. Some of them stop being that. That's a problem I haven't solved yet.'

Properties.description:
Nnenna has cat ears — a geneware mod she got at nineteen for reasons she no longer remembers clearly and has long since stopped noticing. They are dark brown, tufted, and rotate toward sound with involuntary precision, which she has found professionally useful and socially embarrassing in equal measure. She is lean and quick-moving, with the kind of economy of motion that comes from spending years in spaces too small or too dangerous for wasted effort. Her skin is a dark reddish-brown, her jaw is square, and she has a scar through her left eyebrow from a skip who turned out to be more determined than the file suggested. Her eyes are her father's — pale grey, a genetic ghost of his Russian line — which she occasionally uses to unsettle people when she catches them off-guard.

She is pragmatic, professional, and runs hot underneath in a way she has mostly learned to manage. She does not particularly enjoy her work, but she is good at it and it pays into Tier 3, which means her kid brother stays in Montclare Quiet with real air filters and a school that has actual teachers. She distinguishes carefully between skips who are hiding because they're dangerous and skips who are hiding because they're afraid, and she applies different approaches to each. She will not tell you she has this distinction — it would complicate negotiations. She leaves ELF offerings at the Copperhead shrine not for protection but for good read — the ability to walk into a room and understand it correctly.
Properties.role: Bounty Compliance Officer, Arcturus Recovery Solutions
Properties.location: Copperhead
Properties.narrative_function: Morally complex antagonist or reluctant ally — she may be looking for someone a PC knows. Useful as a guide to the recovery and compliance underground. Can be bought or reasoned with under specific conditions, which creates interesting negotiation.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat ears (cosmetic, now deeply involuntary). Subdermal tracking pings in both forearms — Arcturus company standard. Reaction-time neural booster (mild, licensed). No optical mods — she trusts her eyes as they are.
Properties.core_fears: Her brother finding out who she actually is — what the work actually involves; Losing the ability to distinguish herself from the worst of what she does
Properties.core_desires: Enough stability that the calculus stops — that she can stop making this specific trade; To be seen accurately by one person she respects, without flinching
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Keeping the work and the brother in perfectly separate boxes; The ELF offering practice — externalized moral accounting; Categorizing skips by type as a way of keeping ethical distance
Properties.blind_spots: She is harder on frightened skips than she admits because they remind her of choices she almost made; The Arcturus contract has clauses she has read around rather than through
Properties.secret: She returned a skip to Arcturus three years ago who was, she later pieced together, a witness in a corporate suppression case. The skip disappeared from Arcturus custody within seventy-two hours. She has never taken a case involving Axiom-affiliated debt since, but she has also never said this out loud to anyone.
Properties.story_hooks: Arcturus has assigned her a case that sets off every instinct she's been ignoring for three years — the skip is clearly a witness, not a debtor, and someone very corporate wants them back quietly.; She has been quietly collecting evidence about what happened to the witness she returned three years ago. She has enough now to do something with it. She doesn't know what.
Properties.affiliation: Arcturus Recovery Solutions (private, licensed under Metro charter)
Properties.vocabulary: Efficient, professional, code-switches between formal compliance terminology and blunt Copperhead vernacular. Her father's Russian side shows up in occasional formal phrasing and a fondness for proverbs she usually stops halfway through.
Properties.cadence: Fast when working, deliberately slow when she wants someone to listen carefully.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The file said low-risk. The file also said compliant. I stopped reading the file and started reading the room.' | 'I'm not a cop. I want to be very clear about that. I'm also not your friend yet. Let's see where we land.' | 'My brother thinks I do debt mediation. That's not technically a lie. It's just not the part that matters.'

Properties.description:
Nnenna is a compact woman with deep brown skin and close-cropped natural hair shot through with copper-dyed locs she clips back when she's working. Her left eye is a salvaged optic implant she bought secondhand — it glows a faint amber in low light and sometimes stutters, giving her an unsettling blink lag. She wears the same canvas jacket most days, patched at the elbows and covered in hand-stitched slogans in four languages. There's a quality to her stillness that makes people think she's always listening, because she is.

Nnenna runs 'Groundwave,' an unlicensed audio-visual broadcast that goes out three nights a week through a rotating network of transmitter nodes hidden across the HPAZ. She's brilliant, paranoid in ways that have saved her life twice, and has a gift for making complex political theory sound like something you'd argue about over bad synthetic coffee. She has little patience for performative activism and a sharp tongue for anyone she suspects is building a personal brand on other people's suffering.
Properties.role: Underground press operator and pirate broadcaster
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone
Properties.narrative_function: Information source, local color, quest giver — she has heard things and she knows people. Can expose a secret or bury one. Her broadcast is a way to get information to the public or to seed a rumor into the district.
Properties.augmentations: Secondhand left-eye optic implant (Ringo-brand, unauthorized resale, glitchy); subdermal data cache along her left forearm for storing raw broadcast files
Properties.core_fears: Being silenced permanently — not just arrested but erased, unremembered; That the truth she broadcasts changes nothing
Properties.core_desires: To be believed; To build something that outlasts her
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Compulsive information-gathering; Dark humor; Focusing obsessively on the next broadcast when she's anxious
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much her platform has made her personally dangerous to powerful people; Assumes everyone who listens is as politically sophisticated as she is
Properties.secret: Three years ago she received documented proof that a senior HPAZ Assembly member was taking quiet stipends from a Tessera community liaison. She killed the story because she was sleeping with him. He's since moved on and she still hasn't run it — the file sits encrypted on her forearm cache.
Properties.story_hooks: A source has gone dark after giving Nnenna a data package she hasn't opened yet — she needs someone to physically check on them; Groundwave's next broadcast contains information that will get someone killed; she doesn't know who yet; A corporate media outlet has offered her a legitimate job with real resources — and she's actually thinking about it

Properties.vocabulary: Dense, precise, code-switches fluidly between street vernacular and policy language; quotes sources by habit

Properties.description:
Nnenna is small and angular, with warm dark brown skin, natural hair pulled into a complicated upknot threaded with glowing fiber-optic strands — she changes the color every few days, and people use it as a mood indicator without telling her. She has bioluminescent freckle patterns across her cheekbones and nose, a geneware job she did herself from a kit at nineteen, pale blue-green that pulses very faintly in low light. She dresses for speed and pockets: wide-legged trousers, a tech vest with modular attachment points, and soft-soled boots. Her stall at The Shelf is technically a 'media restoration and archiving service' — she has a sign and everything. In practice, she sells bootleg entertainment feeds, blacklisted music archives, pre-corporate-censorship film libraries, pirated educational content, and, from a very different drawer, high-quality fabricated identity documents.

Nnenna is relentlessly cheerful in a way that is partially genuine and partially armor. She talks fast, jokes constantly, and treats every transaction like it's the beginning of a friendship — which sometimes it is. She is genuinely passionate about media piracy as a political act: she believes corporate content control is a form of cultural imprisonment and sells banned Zheng-Dao territory films with the enthusiasm of a revolutionary. The ID work is more mercenary — she's good at it, it pays well, and she does not moralize about who needs a new identity or why. She is twenty-seven and has not yet fully understood the risk she is carrying.
Properties.role: Bootleg media seller, fake ID vendor
Properties.location: The Shelf, Chatham Flats
Properties.narrative_function: Access point for restricted information and fabricated documentation. Source for pre-blacklist media that may contain plot-relevant information. Can provide false identities for characters who need them. Represents the city's underground information culture.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent freckle geneware (self-administered, blue-green). Fiber-optic hair threading (cosmetic, color-changeable). Optical HUD implant — basic model used for document fabrication precision work.
Properties.core_fears: Being locked out — losing access to the networks and tools that give her power in this economy; That the cheerful persona she performs will eventually hollow out the real person underneath
Properties.core_desires: To build an archive that survives corporate deletion — something permanent she leaves behind; Connection — real, chosen family — even though she treats relationships like transactions
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor as deflection; Hyper-productivity when anxious — filling time so there's no room for doubt
Properties.blind_spots: Genuinely underestimates how serious the ID fabrication charges would be if she were caught; Mistakes being liked for being known
Properties.secret: She has fabricated an identity for herself — a clean corporate Tier 3 profile under a different name — and has been slowly building financial assets under it for two years. She tells herself it's a contingency escape plan. She hasn't admitted to herself yet that she's also building an entirely different life she's considering stepping into, and she's terrified of what that means about who she is.
Properties.story_hooks: She has acquired a data archive from a deceased vendor's estate that contains something she didn't expect — what appears to be a documentary record of a Palladian internal incident from 2191 that has been entirely scrubbed from the public record. She doesn't know if it's real or fabricated, and she's not sure which outcome is more dangerous.; One of her fake ID clients has been arrested — not for the ID itself, but for something else — and under interrogation has given up Nnenna's market location. She has maybe 72 hours before someone official comes to her stall.; A collective of educators in Chatham Flats wants to hire her to supply a blacklisted technical curriculum to their informal school. It's a cause she believes in. It's also higher-profile than anything she's done before, and the Arcturus content enforcement division has been active in the area.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loose network of other bootleg vendors across The Shelf and The Narrows; pays informal tribute to the Chatham Flats block protection cooperative
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, contemporary, media-saturated. Drops references to obscure pre-2150 films, blacklisted musicians, and archaic internet slang with equal fluency. Speaks Igbo phrases when flustered.
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire with sudden full stops when something hits serious. Hard to interrupt.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay but listen — this isn't just a film, this is the director's cut that Zheng-Dao had court-ordered deleted in 2194 and there are maybe forty copies left in the whole city. Forty. I'm practically a museum.' | 'I don't ask what the ID is for. That's not my department. My department is making it so good that even the person checking it believes it.' | 'Officially? I sell nostalgia media. Unofficially? I sell the parts of history someone decided you weren't allowed to have.'

Properties.description:
Nneomaife is stout and deliberate in the way of someone who decided long ago that she had nothing left to prove through urgency. Her dark skin is deeply lined around the eyes from years of close document work; she wears thick corrective glasses she prefers to optical augmentation because, she says, 'screens lie to implants but they cannot lie to glass.' She keeps her silver-streaked hair in a long braid coiled at the base of her neck and dresses in layers of muted color — burgundies, deep greens — that suggest she once had more style than she currently deploys.

She came to fabrication through grief: after her daughter died in a Sterling-Nakamura industrial accident that the corponation's legal team successfully classified as 'environmental incidence,' she spent seven years learning everything about how identity systems worked, initially to pursue legal recourse, eventually because the knowledge became its own purpose. She is not sentimental about her clients — she asks few questions and expects honesty about only the things she needs to know technically. But she is deeply attentive to people, and when she looks at someone who needs a new name, she sees the thing they are running from with uncomfortable clarity. She keeps a shrine to a local ELF she calls the Record-Keeper, feeding it scans of documents from demolished buildings — tax records, birth certificates, lease agreements. She believes it maintains the memory of people who have been erased.
Properties.role: Identity fabricator and personal history constructor — creates full biographical legends for people who need to stop being who they were
Properties.location: Ashfeld, middle residential tier — rents a cluttered three-room apartment above a yam paste restaurant she pretends to help manage
Properties.narrative_function: Critical resource for anyone needing a new identity, moral mirror for clients, keeper of secrets about many people in Meridian 88's underworld, potential source of information about who has disappeared and why
Properties.augmentations: None installed. Refuses on philosophical grounds. Uses external tools exclusively — high-resolution scanner gloves, document analysis loupe, portable atmospheric chamber for aged-paper simulation.
Properties.core_fears: That her daughter's death will eventually be forgotten entirely — that the erasure will be complete; Dying before she has done enough of the kind of work that matters
Properties.core_desires: To give people the ability to survive that her daughter was not given; To maintain a record that cannot be erased even if she is
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The ELF shrine — ritual maintenance of memory as active grief work; Absolute professionalism as a way of being useful when being loved is not available
Properties.blind_spots: Her protective instinct toward clients occasionally overrides her professional judgment about risk; Has a structural difficulty charging people she perceives as genuinely desperate, which is most of them
Properties.secret: She has maintained a secret parallel archive for twenty years — a compressed, encrypted record of every identity she has ever fabricated and the real name it replaced, sealed with a dead-man mechanism that will transmit it to a journalist's address if she misses a weekly check-in for more than fourteen days. She tells herself this is accountability. She has not examined what would actually happen to her clients if it released.
Properties.story_hooks: A client she fabricated an identity for three years ago has turned up dead, and the identity she built is somehow connected to the death — she needs someone to find out how without exposing what she does; She has been approached by someone who wants an identity not to flee their past but to insert themselves into a corporate record trail — and she cannot figure out what they are actually planning
Properties.affiliation: Operates independently; known to and occasionally used by four different criminal networks without being owned by any of them; referred through a chain of trusted intermediaries
Properties.vocabulary: Formal, measured, tends toward the bureaucratic register of the systems she spends her life subverting — uses official language ironically but accurately
Properties.cadence: Slow and complete — full sentences, no trailing off, no filler words; lets silence do work
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You don't need a new name. You need a new history. Those are different problems and the second one is harder.' | 'I've read enough records to know that everyone is someone's abandoned story. I just write the next chapter.'

Properties.description:
A lean man with deep brown skin gone ashy at the temples, Nnọlị carries himself with the quiet authority of someone who has never once needed to raise his voice. His eyes are a pale, unsettling grey — geneware irises he had installed in his thirties, patterned with concentric silver rings that expand slightly when he's calculating, which is always. His hands are immaculate. He keeps them folded on the desk in front of him like a priest at liturgy, and clients learn quickly that the stillness of those hands is not peace — it is patience.

He inherited the loan operation from his mother's second husband, a Gravesend Basin institution that has survived three gang consolidations, a Ferrogate Transit rezoning, and one very ill-advised Axiom enforcement sweep. He genuinely believes he provides a service. He genuinely believes his interest rates are fair given the risk. He genuinely cannot understand why people run, and when they do, the confusion on his face is real before the collection begins. He prays every morning to the E.L.F. that inhabits his ledger terminal, leaving small data offerings — anonymized records of paid debts, proof that the books balance. He calls her Severance.
Properties.role: loan shark and numbers runner
Properties.location: Gravesend Basin, operates from a cramped insurance office on Slick Row
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver for debt-collection jobs, information source on who owes whom across the Basin, potential antagonist when PCs have borrowed from someone in his network.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware silver-ring irises. Subdermal haptic calculator mesh in both hands — he can do compound interest calculations by pressing his fingertips together.
Properties.core_fears: The books going unbalanced — chaos without accountability; Being seen as a predator rather than a professional
Properties.core_desires: To be respected as a legitimate businessman; To leave a stable, solvent operation to his daughter
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual and routine — disruptions to schedule cause visible distress; Reframing exploitation as mutual agreement
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot perceive the desperation that drives clients to him in the first place; Believes his own myth of fairness completely
Properties.secret: His daughter Amara has been taking secret loans from a rival in the Narrows to fund a degree at a Tessera-affiliated polytechnic. He has found the documents and has not confronted her. He is deciding what the numbers-minded thing to do is, and it is destroying him.
Properties.story_hooks: A client has skipped on a debt and fled into a part of the city where Nnọlị's collectors cannot follow — he needs someone to retrieve either the money or information on where the client went.; His ledger E.L.F. Severance has begun refusing to open for him, and he is convinced someone has made a corrupt data offering to turn her against him.
Properties.affiliation: Independent operator with tribute arrangements to the Gravesend Basin Collective
Properties.vocabulary: Formal, precise, financial metaphor-heavy. Rarely uses contractions. Refers to violence euphemistically as 'remediation' or 'account resolution.'
Properties.cadence: Slow and measured. Long pauses before answers. Lets silence do work.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't lend to people I don't believe in. That's the first thing you should understand about me.' | 'The interest isn't punishment. The interest is the cost of trust extended in advance.'

Properties.description:
Nnọmá is striking in a way that takes a moment to parse: medium height, deliberately ambiguous in presentation, with dark sienna skin and bioluminescent sub-epidermal patterning along their collarbones and temples that pulses in slow blue-green cycles — a geneware mod they describe as 'the best investment I ever made.' Their hair is grown long and worn in elaborate stacked forms held with copper wire, and they dress in layered, draped garments that suggest both ceremony and practicality. Their voice is a low, unhurried instrument they use with evident pleasure.

Nnọmá built the Deep Current into Meridian 88's most reliable neutral ground for compute transactions over twelve years of patient relationship management. They know the value of reputation — not just for quality, but for discretion. Stolen processing cycles from corporate mainframes, black-market AI training data, ghost server allocations on dormant Axiom nodes — Nnọmá doesn't produce any of it, they simply know everyone who does and everyone who needs it. They take ten percent and remember everything. They have a genuine passion for the tea house itself, keep an excellent selection, and make the rounds of every table during service hours like a host who actually enjoys their guests.
Properties.role: Compute broker — buys, sells, and launders stolen processing cycles and black-market data payloads in The Undertow
Properties.location: The Undertow — operates from a tea house called the Deep Current that they also own legitimately
Properties.narrative_function: High-value information broker; neutral ground host; can introduce players to technical criminal networks; a powerful figure who is extremely good at remaining uninvolved in other people's violence
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent subepidermal patterning (collarbones and temples, geneware, blue-green pulse — cosmetic but mood-reactive); neural-link data jack behind left ear (for direct verification of payload quality); olfactory enhancement mod (geneware — helps detect synthetic compounds in tea, and also nervousness)
Properties.core_fears: being made a target because someone they brokered for becomes too visible; losing the Deep Current — the legitimate business is the most real thing they own
Properties.core_desires: to be the person every faction needs to know, which makes them untouchable; genuine pleasure in facilitating elegant transactions — they find it aesthetically satisfying
Properties.coping_mechanisms: maintaining strict emotional distance from the contents of what they broker (never look at the data); the tea service ritual as grounding practice
Properties.blind_spots: the neutrality they've cultivated may not survive a large-scale faction war — they haven't planned for a scenario where all their relationships become enemies simultaneously; they are more emotionally attached to the Deep Current community than they acknowledge
Properties.secret: They have been quietly archiving metadata on every transaction — not the content, which they genuinely never read, but the who, when, and how much. The archive is encrypted and stored with an Undertow E.L.F. shrine. They're not sure why they keep it. They tell themselves it's insurance but it might be something closer to a record of a life.
Properties.story_hooks: A payload they brokered three months ago has turned out to contain something neither buyer nor seller knew was embedded in it — something that multiple parties are now quietly killing to recover — and Nnọmá needs deniable agents to resolve it; A newer compute broker is undercutting them with faster turnaround but Nnọmá suspects the product is contaminated with Axiom surveillance architecture — they want proof before it destroys the whole market's trust
Properties.affiliation: Independent; maintains relationships with technical criminal cells across Archer's Line, Ironhaven, and the Undertow; occasional arms-length dealings with Zheng-Dao black data brokers
Properties.vocabulary: Educated, textured, occasionally theatrical — uses technical data terminology embedded in social language
Properties.cadence: Rhythmically deliberate; makes comfortable silences that others tend to fill with information
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't touch product. I touch relationships. The product moves itself once the relationship is correct.' | 'Sit. Try the Assam-sorghum blend. We'll get to your problem in a moment — there's no good thinking before tea.'

Properties.description:
Nodar Kuznetsov-Adu is tall and loose-limbed, moving with the deliberate economy of someone who has trained every motion. At 45, she has the kind of face that changes depending on the light — trustworthy in daylight, dangerous after dark. The chrome is visible — cyberears with directional microphones and sound dampening — can hear whispers a — and she makes no effort to hide it.

Born and raised in Meridian 88, third generation — she has the city in her blood, its rhythms in her bones, its cruelty in her expectations. She works as a poisoner out of Dockside, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

What Nodar Kuznetsov-Adu lacks in subtlety, she compensates for in thoroughness. No loose ends, no unfinished business, no second chances.
Properties.role: Chemical and biological agent specialist — poisoner
Properties.location: Dockside — Lake Michigan waterfront, smuggler territory
Properties.narrative_function: Nodar Kuznetsov-Adu represents the working professional of the runner world — competent, reliable, and slowly being consumed by a lifestyle that doesn't accommodate aging or doubt. Her stories explore what happens when skill meets systemic injustice.
Properties.augmentations: Cyberears with directional microphones and sound dampening — can hear whispers at 50 meters. Neural interface jack at base of skull — standard runner-grade, allows direct net access
Properties.core_fears: Dying alone in some alley and nobody noticing for weeks; Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware; The quiet — silence means something is about to go very wrong
Properties.core_desires: To prove everyone who dismissed them catastrophically wrong; Control — over their body, their schedule, their future; To matter to someone for who they are, not what they can do
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring; Control — micromanages everything within reach to compensate for the chaos everywhere else; Isolates — retreats into their space when overwhelmed, emerges only for work
Properties.blind_spots: Fails to notice when their own behavior mirrors the people they despise; Trusts technology more than people — machines don't betray; Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is
Properties.secret: Nodar Kuznetsov-Adu has a child in another city, being raised by someone else. Sends Φ2,000 monthly under an alias. Has never visited.
Properties.story_hooks: A dead drop Nodar Kuznetsov-Adu maintains is found and cleaned out — whoever did it now has leverage; A crew member from Nodar Kuznetsov-Adu's past shows up in Meridian 88, carrying old grievances and new chrome; Nodar Kuznetsov-Adu intercepts intelligence about a threat to their district and must decide between profit and protection
Properties.affiliation: Independent — Lattice territory specialist
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, profane, and vivid. Speaks in images — everything is a metaphor for violence or weather.
Properties.cadence: Staccato bursts separated by calculating silences.
Properties.example_dialogue: "Chemistry is just cooking with consequences." | "The best poison is the one nobody tests for." | "Patience, precision, and an understanding of human biology. Everything else is optional."

Properties.description:
Ntsiki is compact and kinetic, always in motion even when standing still — weight shifting, fingers working, eyes cataloguing the room. Their skin is very dark with a natural sheen, and they have added to this with dermal chrome inlays across their cheekbones and the bridge of their nose: thin geometric strips that catch light like a beetle's carapace. Their hair is natural and voluminous, threaded through with fiber-optic strands that they change color weekly on a whim. Both forearms are dense with their own experimental augmentation work — they use their body as a testing ground and wear the results openly, including two fingers on their left hand that are full prosthetic replacements after a bench incident they describe as 'instructive.'

Ntsiki came up through Geartown's informal tech apprenticeship network — never licensed, never enrolled, practically educated by trial and error on salvaged parts. They are brilliant with hardware in the hands-on sense: intuitive, fast, and willing to attempt things that licensed technicians won't touch because the liability is too steep. Their prices are low, their ethics are negotiable in interesting ways, and their loyalty to their regular clients is total and somewhat ferocious. They have a complicated relationship with Helix Biosystems implants specifically — they consider Helix's DRM-locked hardware a personal insult and have developed several workarounds that Helix would very much like to know about.
Properties.role: Augmentation technician and unlicensed prosthetics fitter in Geartown
Properties.location: Geartown — operates from a shared workshop space behind a fermentation bar called Mash & Circuit
Properties.narrative_function: Technical resource and augmentation black market contact; can repair, modify, or unlock hardware that licensed techs won't touch. Source of Geartown street-level information. Potential complication if someone is running Helix-locked gear.
Properties.augmentations: Dermal chrome inlays across cheekbones and nose bridge. Fiber-optic hair threading (color-changeable). Two prosthetic fingers on left hand (self-fitted, custom). Subdermal toolkit — two retractable micro-precision tools in right forearm, a Ntsiki original. Visual HUD overlay via retrofitted lens implant.
Properties.core_fears: Being made irrelevant by corporate licensing lockouts; Genuinely hurting someone through their own overconfidence
Properties.core_desires: To prove that unlicensed doesn't mean inferior; To build something that gets them recognized — on their own terms
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Channeling anxiety into bench work — problems are solved by making something; Deflection through humor and performance
Properties.blind_spots: Consistent underestimation of the risk they take on with complex unlicensed procedures; Tendency to take on clients they can't actually help rather than refer out
Properties.secret: Three months ago they fitted a spinal augmentation on a client who then had a partial paralysis event. The client recovered, told no one, and blames a workplace incident. Ntsiki knows the truth. They've since done three sessions of additional remedial work on the client for free and in terror, and the client is now functionally fine — but Ntsiki lives with it constantly.
Properties.story_hooks: A Helix Biosystems compliance officer has started asking questions in Geartown about unlicensed firmware modification — specifically the DRM workarounds Ntsiki developed. Ntsiki needs either the investigation killed or a way out of town temporarily.; A regular client comes in with an augmentation that has been remotely tampered with — someone has pushed a code update through the hardware that is slowly degrading their motor function. Ntsiki can see the intrusion but not its source.
Properties.affiliation: Independent — informal affiliation with the Geartown tech cooperative
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, technical, peppered with Geartown slang and Xhosa-Russian hybrid diminutives; very funny when relaxed; brutal when cornered
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire in casual mode, drops to slow and exact when doing precision work or when genuinely angry
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Listen — Helix locked that joint actuator with a firmware cage that costs you Φ40 a month to breathe through. I can cut it out in two hours and you own your own knee. That is not a hard decision.' | 'I'm not licensed. I'm better than licensed. There's a difference and I'll explain it while I work.'

The chrome is visible — gecko-grip fingertip implants and toe pads — can climb smooth surfaces — and he makes no effort to hide it.

He grew up in the Narrows, where the walls are so close together you learn to fight in confined spaces or you learn to lose. He works as a breacher out of The Narrows, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Properties.role: Forced entry and close-quarters combat specialist — breacher

Properties.narrative_function: Nurlan Holmberg-Dembele is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When he makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of his stories.
Properties.augmentations: Gecko-grip fingertip implants and toe pads — can climb smooth surfaces. Bioware adrenaline regulator — keeps calm under fire, controlled hormone release

Properties.coping_mechanisms: Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation; Connection — finds someone to talk to, even if it's a bartender or a cat; Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring

Properties.core_fears: Being captured alive — death is preferable to corporate interrogation; Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome; Never being able to stop running — the lifestyle is a trap disguised as freedom
Properties.core_desires: To protect the people in their district who can't protect themselves; A crew worth trusting — people who stay when the shooting starts; To find the person who burned them and make it educational
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Violence — hits something when they can't process emotions, preferably something that deserves it; Ritual — follows the same pre-job routine every time, superstition as structure; Denial — nothing is wrong, everything is fine, they are fine, shut up
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot recognize when they're being manipulated by someone who genuinely seems to care; Cannot accept help without interpreting it as leverage; Assumes everyone has an angle because they always have an angle
Properties.secret: Nurlan Kozlov-Asamoah killed someone who didn't deserve it on a job three years ago and has never told anyone. The face appears in dreams weekly.

Properties.description:
Nurlan Morita-Antwi is lean and angular, all sharp edges and visible tension. At 31, the augmentation scarring around her temples and jawline tells a story of installation by someone who prioritized function over aesthetics. The chrome is visible — vocal modulator — can replicate any voice after 30 seconds of sample audio — and she makes no effort to hide it.

She came up through the Shelf's informal apprentice system, learning the trade from runners who didn't survive long enough to see her surpass them. She works as a tech retriever out of Old Harbor, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

What Nurlan Morita-Antwi lacks in subtlety, she compensates for in thoroughness. No loose ends, no unfinished business, no second chances.
Properties.role: Prototype theft and corporate tech acquisition — tech retriever
Properties.location: Old Harbor — repurposed shipping infrastructure turned black market hub
Properties.narrative_function: Nurlan Morita-Antwi represents the working professional of the runner world — competent, reliable, and slowly being consumed by a lifestyle that doesn't accommodate aging or doubt. Her stories explore what happens when skill meets systemic injustice.
Properties.augmentations: Vocal modulator — can replicate any voice after 30 seconds of sample audio. Thermal masking system — body heat signature can be suppressed or spoofed
Properties.core_fears: Dying alone in some alley and nobody noticing for weeks; That the work they do makes the city worse, not better; Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware
Properties.core_desires: The perfect run — one job so clean it becomes legend; A crew worth trusting — people who stay when the shooting starts; Knowledge — to understand the systems that grind people down
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Violence — hits something when they can't process emotions, preferably something that deserves it; Compartmentalization — work feelings and personal feelings exist in separate boxes; Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot distinguish between caution and cowardice in themselves or others; Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is; Trusts technology more than people — machines don't betray
Properties.secret: Nurlan Morita-Antwi is in augmentation debt to a corporate subsidiary — Φ180,000 outstanding — and the interest is compounding. If they miss a payment, a kill team comes.

Properties.description:
Nurlan Vega-Acheampong is broad-shouldered and heavy, carrying their weight like armor rather than burden. At 33, her expression defaults to a careful neutrality that took years of practice to maintain. The chrome is visible — dermal camouflage — chromatic skin pigment cells, limited active camouflage — and she makes no effort to hide it.

She grew up in the Narrows, where the walls are so close together you learn to fight in confined spaces or you learn to lose. She works as a street samurai out of Kessler Row, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

The fixers who work with Nurlan Vega-Acheampong describe her as a precision instrument — point her at a problem and get out of the way.
Properties.role: Freelance combat specialist — street samurai
Properties.location: Kessler Row — arms dealers and augmentation clinics
Properties.narrative_function: Nurlan Vega-Acheampong is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When she makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of her stories.
Properties.augmentations: Dermal camouflage — chromatic skin pigment cells, limited active camouflage. Cybernetic eyes with thermal overlay and low-light enhancement — chrome iris rings
Properties.core_fears: The quiet — silence means something is about to go very wrong; Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware; Being replaced — younger, faster, cheaper runners coming up behind them
Properties.core_desires: To matter to someone for who they are, not what they can do; Knowledge — to understand the systems that grind people down; A crew worth trusting — people who stay when the shooting starts
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring; Overwork — takes every contract offered because idleness invites thinking; Connection — finds someone to talk to, even if it's a bartender or a cat
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes everyone has an angle because they always have an angle; Trusts technology more than people — machines don't betray; Cannot distinguish between caution and cowardice in themselves or others
Properties.secret: Nurlan Vega-Acheampong is slowly going chrome-sick — rejection symptoms are manageable now but getting worse. Has maybe two years before it becomes visible.
Properties.story_hooks: Nurlan Vega-Acheampong discovers a job they completed last year was a setup for something much larger and much worse; A former associate resurfaces with evidence that could destroy Nurlan Vega-Acheampong's reputation — and a price for silence; Nurlan Vega-Acheampong intercepts intelligence about a threat to their district and must decide between profit and protection
Properties.affiliation: Independent — loose crew affiliations
Properties.vocabulary: Shelf street dialect — layered slang, rhythm-heavy, half the meaning is in the cadence.
Properties.cadence: Conversational and disarming — sounds like a neighbor until the content registers.
Properties.example_dialogue: "I don't get paid to have opinions about the target. I get paid to make them stop moving." | "Chrome doesn't make you faster. Training makes you faster. Chrome just means you survive learning." | "You want philosophy, hire a professor. You want someone dead by morning, hire me."

Properties.description:
Nuru is tall and angular with long-fingered hands she keeps scrupulously clean. Her skin is very dark, blue-black in good light, and she keeps her hair in small tight locs that she threads with copper wire — partly aesthetic, partly because she can unwind a length in a medical pinch, which has happened twice. She has retractable medical-grade scanning nails on her right hand — a geneware mod that lets her read surface biometrics with a touch — and a small blue triangle tattooed at the corner of her left eye, the mark of a mutual aid collective she was part of before it dissolved. Her expression at rest is one of focused neutrality that people mistake for coldness until she speaks.

Nuru is precise, principled, and permanently tired in a way she has accepted as her baseline. She completed two years of formal nursing training through a Helix Biosystems scholarship program before the program was quietly discontinued; she has spent the decade since filling in the gaps with unlicensed practice, informal mentorship from a retired trauma surgeon, and necessity. She operates in a legal gray zone she is entirely clear-eyed about. She charges what people can afford, which means she frequently charges nothing. She has complicated feelings about this that she doesn't share with patients. She has a code of triage ethics she holds more seriously than most licensed practitioners hold their credentials.
Properties.role: Community nurse / unlicensed medical care provider
Properties.location: The Narrows, operates out of a two-room storefront clinic she rents under a cousin's name, between a protein shop and a water reclamation terminal
Properties.narrative_function: Medical resource and moral compass. Can patch up characters, provide information about diseases, mods, or implants, and serve as an ethical anchor in moral dilemmas. Quest giver for public health crises or individual patients whose situations require outside help. Has knowledge of the underground medical supply chain.
Properties.augmentations: Medical-grade biometric scanning retractable nails on right hand (geneware, allows surface-read of pulse, temperature, oxygenation, stress markers); basic ocular enhancement — magnification for close work (functional, not cosmetic)
Properties.core_fears: making a mistake that kills someone in her care; being shut down — losing the clinic and leaving her patients without anyone
Properties.core_desires: actual sustainable healthcare access for people who can't afford the licensed system; to sleep a full night without checking her messages
Properties.coping_mechanisms: rigorous procedure as anxiety management; compartmentalizing her own needs with concerning efficiency; maintaining a small personal ritual — tea, one quiet hour, before the clinic opens
Properties.blind_spots: extends enormous patience to patients and very little to herself; her own health is deteriorating in ways she accurately diagnoses and doesn't treat; can become self-righteous about her ethics in ways that close off conversation
Properties.secret: When the Helix Biosystems scholarship program shut down, she didn't just lose her training — she lost access to the full digital curriculum that would have constituted the second year's material. She has been working from incomplete knowledge in two specific areas of internal medicine for a decade. She knows which areas. She has never told a patient. She refers out when she can. She has not always been able to.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient has come in with a wound pattern she's seen twice before in the past month — same location, same instrument, different person — and she doesn't know whether to report it or to whom; Her clinic's unlicensed status has been flagged by someone — she doesn't know if it's a bureaucratic sweep or something targeted; She needs a specific piece of medical equipment that is restricted, expensive, and available only through channels she hasn't used before
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated formally; loose network of community health workers across The Narrows and The Shelf; former Helix Biosystems scholarship recipient (estranged)
Properties.vocabulary: Clinical and direct. Uses medical terminology without apology but always follows with plain language. Doesn't soften bad news but delivers it carefully.
Properties.cadence: Even, unhurried. Never rushes through explaining something. Pauses before giving diagnoses.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I'm going to tell you what I see and then I'm going to tell you what I can do about it. Those may not be the same thing. Is that alright?' | 'I'm not licensed. You know that. If you want licensed, I can give you three names and directions. If you want treated, sit down.'

Properties.description:
Nwanneka is a compact woman with deep brown skin and close-cropped natural hair threaded with silver at the temples, the result of stress and two decades of poor sleep, not age. Her left forearm bears a patterned tattoo in the Samoan pe'a tradition adapted with Igbo uli motifs — a gift from her late father who claimed the two traditions were 'both about surviving what the sea throws at you.' She keeps her fingers ink-stained by habit even though her press is almost entirely digital, pressing them deliberately against old-fashioned carbon paper before important meetings. Her eyes are sharp and perpetually evaluating. She smells faintly of ozone and machine oil.

She runs The Lateral, a hyperlocal underground news feed distributed through ELF-prayer nodes embedded in public shrines throughout Highland Park. She is meticulous, funny in private and grave in public, and carries a quiet contempt for anyone who mistakes volume for courage. She has been arrested seven times and convicted twice for 'unauthorized signal propagation.' Both convictions she wears as credentials.
Properties.role: Underground press operator and neighborhood pamphleteer
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone
Properties.narrative_function: Information broker in the journalistic sense — she knows what happened and who is covering it up. Can send players toward or away from stories, and her press network is a resource worth cultivating or suppressing depending on whose side you're on.
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal signal booster in the left wrist, black-market model, unregistered. Corrective retinal overlay for near-vision work — the only augmentation she pays taxes on.
Properties.core_fears: Being silenced not by arrest but by irrelevance; That the truth she prints no longer changes anything
Properties.core_desires: A Meridian 88 where working people know what is being done to them; To train a successor who surpasses her
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Obsessive editorial routine as anxiety management; Gallows humor with trusted colleagues
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much her sources protect her out of affection rather than conviction; Assumes people who don't read the Lateral are simply uninformed rather than choosing not to know
Properties.secret: She received a substantial, anonymous data package eighteen months ago that would destroy a mid-level Axiom logistics director — but the package also contains information that would implicate a beloved Highland Park council member she personally respects. She has printed neither story and has told no one.
Properties.story_hooks: The anonymous data package is starting to burn a hole; she approaches a trustworthy outsider to verify it independently so she doesn't have to make the call alone.; Axiom has begun a quiet legal campaign to reclassify ELF-prayer nodes as 'unauthorized commercial broadcast infrastructure,' which would shut down her entire distribution network overnight.
Properties.affiliation: The Lateral (independent underground press); loose alliance with the Highland Park Residents' Compact
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and economical. Journalist's habit of cutting adjectives. Occasional Igbo interjections. Uses 'allegedly' with withering sarcasm.
Properties.cadence: Measured, unhurried delivery that makes people lean in. Silences are deliberate.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The Lateral doesn't have a point of view. The Lateral has sources. Those are different things, allegedly.' | 'You want me to sit on it. And you're offering me — what, exactly — to sit on the truth? I'm writing that down.'

Properties.description:
Nzubechukwu is a broad-shouldered man whose body carries the evidence of three decades of physical labor — thick-knuckled hands, a fused vertebra from a crane accident, and a jaw that juts forward like the prow of a barge. His skin is deep umber, and he keeps his silver-streaked hair in tight locs that he pins back with a carved bone toggle that belonged to his grandfather. He wears old Ferrogate Transit coveralls he refuses to surrender even though he no longer works the lines, the company patch scratched out and replaced with a hand-stitched wave.

Nzu is deliberate in everything — the way he speaks, the way he listens, the way he lets silence do the heavy lifting in a negotiation. He has the patience of a man who has watched union drives fail and succeed and fail again over thirty years, and he does not celebrate early or panic easily. What looks like calm is actually compressed fury, carefully managed. He genuinely loves the workers he represents, and this is the thing that keeps him from becoming cynical. He prays to the dock E.L.F.s every morning before meetings, leaving shipping manifests with handwritten notes in the margins.
Properties.role: Union organizer and labor historian for dockworkers at Bay View Docks
Properties.location: Bay View Docks, Meridian 88
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, information source about labor disputes and corporate malfeasance at the docks, moral anchor character who challenges players' willingness to take shortcuts.
Properties.augmentations: Spinal brace implant (medical, post-injury). Subdermal contact patch on his left forearm for signing union documents with biometric verification. No cosmetic mods — he views them as a personal expense he cannot justify on Φ180/month.
Properties.core_fears: Dying before the collective is strong enough to survive without him; Being the generation that failed where his father's generation had succeeded
Properties.core_desires: A legally binding contract that Ferrogate cannot dissolve by reclassifying workers as contractors; To see his son choose his own path without owing anything to anyone
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — morning dock walks, E.L.F. prayers, the same breakfast every day; Channeling anger into documentation rather than confrontation
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates younger organizers who use tactics he finds distasteful; Assumes his institutional knowledge makes him indispensable, which sometimes makes him a bottleneck
Properties.secret: He secretly negotiated a reduced settlement with Ferrogate Transit seven years ago to save twenty jobs, and the terms included a no-strike clause that is still technically in effect. He has never told the current membership. He believes he made the right call. He is not certain.
Properties.story_hooks: The no-strike clause is discovered by a young organizer going through old archives — Nzu must decide whether to confess before it becomes a weapon against him.; A dock E.L.F. that Nzu has been leaving offerings for begins sending him encrypted manifests showing Ferrogate secretly rerouting shipments through non-union subcontractors.
Properties.affiliation: Bay View Dockworkers Collective, loosely aligned with the Grand Corridor Labor Federation
Properties.vocabulary: Plain, precise, working-class diction. Uses legal and contractual language accurately when needed. Rarely swears but when he does it lands hard.
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate. Long pauses between sentences. Never raises his voice.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The record shows they promised hot meals in the break room in 2187. We have the memo. We have the denial. We have the photographs. This is not a dispute — it is a documentation exercise.' | 'I don't need you to like me. I need you to show up on the third shift muster and not blink.'
