Properties.description:
Obafemi Adeyinka-Cruces is a large, slow-moving man with the specific gravity of someone who has decided to stop being in a hurry. Yoruba and Puerto Rican, he carries both heritages openly — a rotating collection of hand-dyed agbadas worn over thermal underlayers against the harbor cold, and a way of greeting people that involves actual sustained eye contact, which in Old Harbor is either deeply comforting or deeply unnerving depending on what you've done lately. His face is deeply lined, his beard gone fully white, his hands scarred from years of dock work before he transitioned into his current occupation. His only augmentation is a cochlear archive implant he had installed at fifty — it records everything he hears with his consent toggle on, and he keeps the toggle on almost always.

Femi has lived in Old Harbor for forty-one years, long enough to have watched three generations of families cycle through its tenements, its fishing operations, its smuggling economies, and its periodic brutal restructurings at the hands of corporate port interests. He is not a fixer, not a runner, not muscle. He is the person who knows where the bodies are buried because he attended the funerals. His currency is memory — who owes whom, which families have a blood grudge going back to the '50s, which enforcement captain can be reasoned with and which one enjoys it too much. He trades information carefully, at his own pace, and has an intricate personal ethics about what he will and will not sell.

He runs a small legitimate operation: a repair stall for small watercraft and electronics near Pier 14, which gives him a reason to be everywhere and talk to everyone. He has no ambitions beyond Old Harbor. He has been offered relocation, money, protection, and has declined all of it. He says he is too old to learn a new set of names. What he means is that Old Harbor is the only place where he is fully himself, and he will not trade that for safety.
Properties.aliases: Femi, The Cartographer, Old Harbor's Ear
Properties.role: Street-Level Information Broker / Oral Historian
Properties.location: Old Harbor
Properties.narrative_function: Living memory and moral compass for Old Harbor storylines. He provides historical context, relationship maps, and a street-level perspective grounded in decades rather than immediate survival. His archive implant makes him a walking evidence repository. His ethical complexity around the secret gives him a shadow side that prevents him from being purely a wise mentor figure.
Properties.augmentations: Cochlear archive implant (self-installed via back-alley augmentation clinic, age 50) — continuous audio recording with manual consent toggle; 41 years of selective archive stored on encrypted external drives in his stall,Arthritis management implant (basic, medical) — joint inflammation suppression in both hands
Properties.core_fears: That Old Harbor will be finally, completely destroyed and his memory of it will be all that remains; That he will be forced to sell information that gets someone he loves killed; Losing the archive implant — losing the record; Dying before he finds someone worthy to pass the knowledge to
Properties.core_desires: For Old Harbor to survive in some form that still belongs to its people; A genuine apprentice — someone who wants to learn the neighborhood, not just mine it; To be useful without being used; To grieve properly for everyone he has outlived
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Storytelling as processing — he narrates his own experiences to himself in the archive; Physical work as grounding (the repair stall is genuinely therapeutic); Cooking elaborate meals for neighbors with no stated occasion; Deliberate slowness as resistance to a world that wants him to be efficient
Properties.blind_spots: His attachment to Old Harbor makes him a predictable target — anyone who wants leverage on him knows exactly where he'll be; Overestimates his ability to read younger generations whose reference points he doesn't share; His distrust of corporate-affiliated people sometimes causes him to miss individuals worth trusting; Romanticizes Old Harbor's past in ways that elide its historical harms
Properties.secret: The archive implant contains testimony from a woman who died twelve years ago — she described, in detail, a killing carried out by a man who is now a respected community elder in Old Harbor. Femi has never disclosed this. He tells himself it's because the woman asked him not to during her lifetime. He knows it's also because exposing the elder would tear apart three families who have finally found stability.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone approaches Femi seeking specific archived testimony — and they seem to already know it exists; A corporate port acquisition threatens Pier 14 directly, forcing Femi to either act or finally leave; A young runner asks Femi to teach them the neighborhood; he has to decide if they're an apprentice or an asset for someone else; The community elder is dying and wants to confess — to Femi, who already knows; An Old Harbor family feud Femi has carefully managed for years suddenly escalates beyond his ability to contain it
Properties.affiliation: None formal. Trusted by multiple competing factions in Old Harbor specifically because he belongs to none of them. Has declined affiliation offers from smuggling operations, community defense groups, and one corporate 'community liaison' program with memorable directness.
Properties.vocabulary: Rich and unhurried, mixing English with Yoruba phrases and occasional Spanish that surfaces when he's emotional. References historical events and people as if they were recent. Uses 'we' more than 'I' when talking about Old Harbor.
Properties.cadence: Slow, deliberate, full of pauses that are not uncertainty but emphasis. Storytelling rhythm — he builds. Rarely gives a direct answer before establishing context.
Properties.example_dialogue: "You want to know about the Pier 9 situation. Alright. But I need you to understand what Pier 9 was before it was a situation, or nothing I tell you will make any sense at all." | "I've been asked to leave this neighborhood four times by four different kinds of people. I'm still here. They are not. Draw your own conclusions about whose judgment was better." | "Information is not a commodity. It is a relationship. You want me to sell you something, you're in the wrong stall. You want to understand something, sit down." | "She was a good woman and she deserved a better city. Most people here did. That doesn't stop being true just because it's inconvenient."

Properties.description:
Femi Q is lean and restless, built like someone who burns through calories via nervous energy rather than exercise. His Yoruba-Polish-Azerbaijani ancestry gives him a face of striking contradictions — high Slavic cheekbones, the warm brown skin and broad nose of his father's Lagos line, and his Azerbaijani grandmother's dramatically hooded eyes that he's chosen to highlight with geneware iris mods that shift through patterns of concentric gold rings when he's performing. His hair is kept very short on the sides and erupts into a soft irregular cloud on top, usually unwashed. He dresses in layers of secondhand everything — three collars, mismatched sleeves — that somehow cohere into something that reads as intentional.

He is one of the fastest talkers in Pilsen Veil and possibly the most dangerous, because he deploys his speed to bury the sharpest observations inside barrages of absurdity before anyone can quite register they've been cut. He performs at whatever unlicensed venue will book him — back rooms, open drain channels with an audience of forty, once the cargo bay of a stationary Ferrogate car. His material cycles obsessively through class anxiety, the theater of corponation loyalty, and the specific humiliations of being young and broke in a city that sells young and broke as aesthetic. He is genuinely funny. He is also genuinely angry, and the seam between the two is where his best work lives.
Properties.role: Stand-up comedian and underground spoken word performer, Tier 1
Properties.location: Pilsen Veil, rotating between a shared squat above a protein noodle stall and whatever venue will have him
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and social barometer — Femi's material reflects the current tensions and grievances of Pilsen Veil's underclass with high accuracy. Useful as an information source about neighborhood mood and underground venue networks. Can be a quest giver when his material inadvertently gets him into trouble.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware iris mod (concentric gold ring pattern, activates under performance adrenaline). Subdermal rhythm implant in right forearm — a secondhand unit meant for musicians that he uses to feel his own heartbeat amplified during sets.
Properties.core_fears: becoming unfunny — which he understands as becoming comfortable; being absorbed into something corporate and losing the thing that makes him sharp
Properties.core_desires: to be heard by the people he's actually talking to, not a curated audience; financial stability without the cost of self-censorship
Properties.coping_mechanisms: turning every painful experience into material within 48 hours; deflecting personal questions with jokes until the person gives up
Properties.blind_spots: uses humor as armor so reflexively that he sometimes wounds people he cares about and genuinely doesn't notice until much later
Properties.secret: A Ringo talent scout offered him a legitimate contract six months ago — a small comedy streaming platform, decent money, creative approval clauses. He turned it down and told no one. He is not entirely sure why, and the uncertainty terrifies him.
Properties.story_hooks: A bit from his last set — specifically a very accurate joke about Ringo's internal security culture — has been clipped and is circulating in places that suggest someone with access was in the audience. Now someone is very quietly trying to find out who Femi Q is.; The venue that has been his most reliable booking — a back room operated by a woman named Seun — has gone dark. No message. Femi goes looking and finds something that isn't funny at all.
Properties.affiliation: No formal affiliation; loosely connected to the Pilsen Veil underground comedy circuit
Properties.vocabulary: Rapid-fire, code-switches fluidly between street Pilsen slang, fragments of Yoruba honorifics used ironically, and unexpectedly precise vocabulary when making a specific point. Uses corporate jargon as mockery.
Properties.cadence: Extremely fast baseline, punctuated by sudden total stops for effect. The pauses are the punchlines.
Properties.example_dialogue: My landlord — stay with me — my landlord told me the mold in the bathroom is 'a natural texture feature.' Sir. Sir, that is a biome. I am paying Φ40 a month to cohabitate with an ecosystem. | They want your struggle to be aesthetic. Struggling is fine, suffering is fine, just please be suffering in an interesting way with good bone structure.

Properties.description:
Obi is a scrawny, dark-skinned boy with close-cropped hair that he's attempted to dye in patches — copper at the temples, greenish-black at the crown — using stolen salon gel that only half-worked. His left eye has a cracked retinal overlay from a secondhand aug he installed himself using a cracked tutorial, giving that eye a faint grid shimmer when he's excited or scared. He wears a vest with too many pockets, each one holding something he's convinced will be useful someday: a dead ELF token, three different brand of protein tabs, a bent stylus. He moves like a sparrow — quick, diagonal, always watching exits.

Obi is relentlessly optimistic in the way only children who've had to practice it deliberately can be. He runs messages between market stalls, repair shops, and mid-tier residents who don't trust the corp relay networks, collecting Φ1-2 per run. He narrates his own life in his head as if he's a documentary subject, which makes him unexpectedly articulate about his circumstances when asked. He worships a minor ELF he calls 'Knuckle' that he believes lives in a cracked streetlight on his corner.
Properties.role: Truant message runner, The Shelf
Properties.location: The Shelf, Garfield Rack
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and information source — Obi knows everyone in his eight-block radius by face and habit. He can be a quest-giver (something he witnessed on a run), an entry point into the informal economy, or a moral anchor in grim storylines.
Properties.augmentations: Cracked secondhand retinal overlay (left eye only, partially functional — shows grid shimmer and partial AR tags but glitches frequently). No geneware.
Properties.core_fears: becoming invisible — just another street statistic nobody remembers; losing Knuckle's favor and the luck he believes it brings
Properties.core_desires: to be known as someone important in this neighborhood; to eventually afford a real school subscription
Properties.coping_mechanisms: narrating his life as an ongoing documentary; compulsive collection of 'useful' small objects; ELF devotion rituals
Properties.blind_spots: drastically overestimates his own invisibility — adults notice him more than he thinks; doesn't recognize when he's being used by older runners

Properties.description:
Femi is a tall man whose body has softened comfortably into middle age, broad through the shoulders and belly, moving through space with the unhurried certainty of someone who has never needed to perform urgency. His face is deeply lined around the eyes and mouth from decades of late nights and genuine laughter, dark brown skin pocked with the small silvery scars of an old electrical accident he considers formative. His hair is cut close except for a strip of white that runs from his left temple to the back of his skull — natural, not dyed, arrived when he was thirty-two and which he refused to touch. He wears functional clothes exclusively: work boots, cargo trousers, a rotating selection of worn linen shirts. His only concession to ornamentation is a pair of custom cochlear amplifiers threaded with copper wire that catch the light when he tilts his head.

Femi does not play music so much as construct environments. His sets move over four to six hours through tidal cycles of sub-bass and silence, incorporating field recordings he makes throughout the city — the Ferrogate Transit harmonic at Deepwell Station, the hydraulic breath of the Kilimanjaro Mass Driver, rain on the lake filtration membranes. Audiences don't dance to Femi's sets so much as dissolve into them. He has turned down three Axiom-sponsored residencies and one Ringo content contract, a fact he mentions rarely but accurately.
Properties.role: Underground DJ and sound sculptor
Properties.location: Pilsen Veil, back-room residency at a venue called The Underscore
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and community anchor for the Pilsen Veil underground; information broker for the arts scene — he hears everything, literally; can provide access to venues, networks, and people who don't advertise their existence.
Properties.augmentations: Custom cochlear amplifiers (medical-origin, modified for expanded frequency range); basic subdermal temp-mesh for studio climate control; no geneware
Properties.core_fears: Going deaf — not the loss of livelihood but the loss of the world as he experiences it; Becoming comfortable enough to compromise
Properties.core_desires: To make one piece of sound that outlives the city; To be loved without being managed
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Immersive solo recording walks that can last all day; Cooking elaborate meals for whoever is in his orbit
Properties.blind_spots: Romanticizes hardship as artistically generative; has trouble supporting younger artists who want both integrity and stability; Underestimates how much his reputation protects him from consequences he preaches against fearing
Properties.secret: The electrical accident that scarred him was not an accident — he deliberately touched an exposed transit rail at eighteen, a moment of despair he has reframed so many times he almost believes the revised version.
Properties.story_hooks: One of Femi's field recordings contains audio evidence of something that should not have happened at the location where he recorded it; A young protégé has taken a corponation deal and Femi is quietly devastated — and the protégé is now in danger they don't understand
Properties.affiliation: Independent; regular collaborator with the Pilsen Veil sound collective Barometric
Properties.vocabulary: Conversational and warm, drops into technical acoustic language without warning, then pulls back out; generous with profanity used affectionately
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, enjoys a good pause, never rushes to fill silence — he finds silence interesting
Properties.example_dialogue: 'A Ringo contract means they own the silence between the notes. I'm not selling the silence.' | 'Come by Thursday. I found this frequency under the Jefferson Switch that'll rearrange something in your chest, I promise you.'

Properties.description:
Obasi Čanak-Vailima does not exist in any database in Meridian 88. He has no citizen code, no biometric file, no credit history, no medical record, no employment trail. He walks through the city like a hole in its data — and he has spent twenty-two years perfecting that absence. He is a tall man gone slightly angular with age, dark brown skin with deep-etched lines at the corners of his eyes and mouth that look like he has been smiling or squinting for decades. He keeps his grey-streaked hair in a long braid coiled under a wide-brimmed water-repellent hat that he never removes indoors, which unnerves people. His clothing is all non-reactive fabric — nothing smart, nothing networked, nothing that pings.

He is a trader in physical media and analogue goods: handwritten documents, paper maps, unencrypted mechanical devices, pre-digital artifacts. But his real commodity is memory. He has been moving through Meridian 88's edges since before many of his customers were born, and he remembers streets that were razed, deals that were deleted, people who vanished. He is courtly and a little formal — he bows slightly when introduced, he uses full names — and this formality operates as a kind of armour. He is also one of the most genuinely dangerous people in Irkalla, not because he is violent but because he knows something about almost everyone, and everyone knows he knows it.
Properties.role: Q-zero ghost — a person with no digital identity — surviving by trading in physical goods and untracked knowledge
Properties.location: Shifts between Irkalla undermarket and the edges of Bridgepoint, never sleeping in the same structure twice
Properties.narrative_function: Primary information broker for off-grid and pre-digital knowledge; can source physical items unavailable through normal channels; represents the city's undocumented underclass; potential quest giver whose requests are always analogue and always strange.
Properties.augmentations: None. He considers augmentations to be data leakage. He is almost certainly the least-augmented adult in any room he enters.
Properties.core_fears: Being digitized against his will — having his face or voice captured and filed; That the world has moved so far into the network that his kind of knowledge has become worthless
Properties.core_desires: To be genuinely invisible — not hidden, but simply unthought-of; To find one other person who understands why the analogue world mattered
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The formality and ritual of his trading practice gives structure to complete instability; He catalogues everything he witnesses in a physical journal — his only truly private possession
Properties.blind_spots: He has decided the digital world is irredeemably corrupt and misses real threats that emerge from the physical spaces he inhabits; He trusts other Q-zeros too readily simply because they share his status
Properties.secret: He chose to become a Q-zero, not was forced into it. He was once a mid-tier Tessera data compliance auditor named something else entirely. He found records of a systematic erasure of a refugee community's citizenship data and leaked it. Tessera didn't prosecute him — they simply deleted him. He has the original records. He has never decided what to do with them.
Properties.story_hooks: He approaches a player character and hands them a physical photograph — a person the players know — with a date on the back that hasn't happened yet, and says only 'I found this at a drop. Someone wanted you to have it.'; He has been coming to the Irkalla shrine for twenty years. The shrine keeper recently told him an ELF there has been reciting a name — his original name — over and over. He needs help understanding why.
Properties.affiliation: None formally. Has reciprocal arrangements with several unregistered traders and at least one Irkalla ELF-shrine keeper.
Properties.vocabulary: Formal, slightly archaic. Uses full names always. Refers to corporations without their branding as 'the Tessera entity' or 'the Axiom concern.' Uses analogue metaphors — film, paper, ink — that younger people don't always understand.
Properties.cadence: Measured and unhurried. Every sentence sounds like it has been drafted.
Properties.example_dialogue: What I have recorded is that this alley held a clinic from 2178 to 2184. The foundation stones are still there. The ELF that lived in the autoclave is still there, if you know how to ask. | I don't trade in digital goods. I trade in weight. Things that exist in the world and cannot be updated. | You are asking me to remember. That is the one service I am always willing to provide.

Properties.description:
Obasi is twelve going on thirty-five, with the calculating eyes of someone who has been studying people for survival since he was old enough to read danger in a posture. He is slight and quick, with close-cropped hair he keeps tight because loose hair catches in the machinery of the Copperhead alleys. His skin is very dark with a reddish undertone, his nose his Malawian grandmother's, his mouth his Portuguese grandfather's — a wide, expressive mouth he has learned to keep still. He has one cosmetic modification: cat ears, pale gold, that a Cuts lieutenant gave him eight months ago as a mark of favor. He knows they are a leash as much as an ornament. He wears them anyway.

Obasi runs errands for the Copperhead Cuts — nothing criminal yet, carefully not yet, because the Cuts' local lieutenant Somebody-Somebody has a rule about under-fourteens and what they carry. Obasi fetches food, delivers verbal messages, watches corners and whistles a particular pattern if Ferrogate Transit enforcers appear. He is saving every coin he does not spend on food, for a reason he has not told anyone. He is smarter than almost everyone around him gives him credit for, and he knows this, and has decided that being underestimated is a resource.
Properties.role: Street orphan and gang prospect (junior errand runner for the Copperhead Cuts), Tier 1
Properties.location: Copperhead
Properties.narrative_function: Entry point into Copperhead street-level gang politics; demonstrates the soft recruitment pipeline for youth gang membership; his hidden intelligence and his secret savings create a ticking clock.
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic cat ears (pale gold, geneware, gifted by a Cuts lieutenant). No other modifications.
Properties.core_fears: being conscripted into the Cuts for real — carrying product, carrying weapons, becoming someone who cannot leave; dying before he uses the thing he is saving for
Properties.core_desires: to get out of Copperhead entirely, somewhere nobody knows the cat ears; to read every datachip in the world — he is voraciously, secretly curious
Properties.coping_mechanisms: intense information-gathering as a sense of control; performing stupidity as protection
Properties.blind_spots: the lieutenant who gave him the cat ears actually does like him in a possessive way — Obasi reads it as pure manipulation and misses that the man is conflicted about it, which is potentially useful
Properties.secret: He has been saving to buy a forged identity from a document vendor in Menomonee Gulch — not to run yet, but to have the option. He has Φ94 of a Φ200 price. The document vendor does not know Obasi is twelve or that he is a Cuts runner. If either fact became known, the plan collapses.
Properties.story_hooks: The document vendor he's been saving toward is arrested — Obasi needs a new plan and is suddenly desperate enough to take risks he would normally refuse; The Cuts lieutenant announces that Obasi's next assignment will involve carrying something — and he is out of time to decide whether to run or comply
Properties.affiliation: Copperhead Cuts (junior errand runner, not yet fully initiated); no family
Properties.vocabulary: Performs being less articulate than he is; Copperhead street argot for cover; privately he speaks in complete, precise sentences to himself
Properties.cadence: Public: slouchy and halting. Private: sharp.
Properties.example_dialogue: Yeah nah, I didn't see nothing, I was watching the corner like always, nothing came through. | (To himself, alone) If I save four Φ a week net of food, I reach two hundred in twenty-six weeks. Before my birthday. I can do that.

Properties.description:
Obasi is a large, slow-moving man with the quiet authority of someone who has simply outlasted most arguments. His skin is very dark, his grey-streaked locs gathered at the back of his neck, and his hands are enormous — scarred across the knuckles from decades of working with salvaged metal and resonant polymers. He has no cosmetic mods but wears a cochlear amplifier behind his left ear that lets him hear frequencies beyond normal human range; he chose that over anything decorative. He moves through spaces as if listening to them.

Obasi builds instruments that are also sculptures and then performs with them in spaces most people would call acoustically hostile: drainage tunnels, abandoned transit shafts, the concrete bellies of flood-control cisterns. His work is ambient, slow, and enormous in scale — single notes held for minutes, harmonics that make walls breathe. He is not famous outside of a small devoted community, and he prefers it exactly that way. He is a father figure to younger artists in the Pilsen Veil, blunt about craft and surprisingly gentle about everything else.
Properties.role: Sound sculptor and underground venue musician
Properties.location: Pilsen Veil, basement workshop beneath a decommissioned Ferrogate Transit relay station
Properties.narrative_function: Mentor figure; local color; gateway into the Pilsen Veil underground arts scene; keeper of long institutional memory about the neighborhood
Properties.augmentations: Extended-range cochlear amplifier (functional); mild joint-stabilization implants in both wrists (medical necessity)
Properties.core_fears: That the spaces he loves will be developed into something sterile; That he wasted his most productive years chasing recognition he no longer wants
Properties.core_desires: To make something that resonates in a space long after he is gone; To see the younger artists he mentors surpass him
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Long solo walks through drainage infrastructure with his amplifier on maximum; Building something physical whenever anxiety rises
Properties.blind_spots: He romanticizes poverty as purity and sometimes fails to support artists who want commercial success; He does not notice when his bluntness causes real harm
Properties.secret: In his thirties he had a brief period of Axiom-sponsored success, made two albums on their label, and quietly shelved them when he realized they were using his music in their Tier 3 residential mood-management systems without his consent. He bought out his contract and destroyed every master. He has never told anyone because he fears it would make him look naive.
Properties.story_hooks: Ferrogate Transit has filed a quiet reclamation order on the relay station above his workshop — he needs someone to help him find the legal loophole or disappear the paperwork.; One of the drainage tunnels he uses for performances has an E.L.F. in it that has begun responding to his music in ways that shouldn't be possible — harmonizing, completing phrases.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; founding member of the Pilsen Veil sound collective Cistern Sound
Properties.vocabulary: Plain, direct, occasionally poetic when talking about sound; impatient with abstraction that isn't grounded in the physical
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, like his music — long spaces between thoughts
Properties.example_dialogue: 'That tunnel on the east side of the relay station has a 4.2-second reverb tail. You don't perform in a space like that. You serve it.' | 'Axiom didn't invent ambient music. They invented ambient loneliness. Different thing.'

Properties.description:
Obed Belov-Ntim is tall and rawboned, the kind of frame that suggests either malnutrition or efficiency depending on the decade. At 31, he has soft features that belie the chrome underneath — people underestimate him once, usually only once. The chrome is visible — hydraulic joints in knees and elbows — absorbs falls, amplifies strikes — and he makes no effort to hide it.

He grew up in the Narrows, where the walls are so close together you learn to fight in confined spaces or you learn to lose. He works as a smuggler out of The Circuit, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

In a city full of people who talk about what they'll do, Obed Belov-Ntim is one of the ones who actually does it.

Properties.narrative_function: Obed Belov-Ntim represents the working professional of the runner world — competent, reliable, and slowly being consumed by a lifestyle that doesn't accommodate aging or doubt. His stories explore what happens when skill meets systemic injustice.

Properties.core_fears: Losing their edge to age — the body slows before the mind accepts it; Never being able to stop running — the lifestyle is a trap disguised as freedom; That the work they do makes the city worse, not better

Properties.description:
Knock is a compact, densely muscled man with deep brown skin and a face that would be handsome if it weren't always bruised somewhere. He has a retractable claw modification on both hands — not the delicate cosmetic kind, but a heavy-gauge industrial variant originally designed for pipe work, the chrome yellowed and scratched, the mechanism loud. His right eye is a replacement after a cave-in in 2196: matte black sclera, amber iris, depth-perception assist — he got it from a tunnel-market vendor and it's slightly misaligned, which gives him a permanent squint on that side. His hair is cut very close and he has a habit of pressing his palms flat against walls, feeling for vibration, that people find either impressive or unsettling depending on whether they understand what he's doing.

Echo hunting is exactly what it sounds like: you go into places that have broken and you listen for what's still there. Structural resonance, water movement, the ping of metal under pressure — Knock reads these sounds the way others read text. He extracts ferrogate rail segments, copper bundling, intact conduit, old hardware sealed in collapsed rooms — anything the surface market will buy or the underground can use. It is extremely dangerous work with an average career length of about four years. Knock has been doing it for nine. He attributes this to skill. Everyone who knows him also attributes it to a specific kind of recklessness that looks like skill from the outside.
Properties.role: echo hunter — scavenger who locates and extracts valuable materials from collapsed or flooded tunnel sections
Properties.location: Abyssal Threshold, ranging into Black Corridor spurs and pre-collapse Undertow sectors
Properties.narrative_function: Access character — can reach locations no one else can; source of found objects with unknown histories; demonstrates the physical reality of underground survival; can retrieve things or information from inaccessible places
Properties.augmentations: heavy-gauge retractable claws (both hands, industrial, loud), replacement right eye (matte black sclera, amber iris, depth assist, slightly misaligned), impact-absorption plating across both forearms (secondhand, imperfect fit)
Properties.core_fears: a cave-in that is slow — he has made peace with fast death but not slow; becoming someone who can't read the sound anymore — losing the sense that defines his work and his identity
Properties.core_desires: to find the legendary pre-Meridian infrastructure layer — there are rumors of sealed transit tunnels from the 2050s that no one has accessed; to be done, eventually, on his own terms and not because the tunnels decided it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: converts anxiety into preparation — checks equipment compulsively; black humor, specifically about the ways one can die in tunnels
Properties.blind_spots: the recklessness he calls skill — he is genuinely skilled, and the skill is genuinely covering for something that isn't caution
Properties.secret: In a collapsed sector three months ago he found a sealed room containing eleven bodies in old Ferrogate Transit uniforms, arranged deliberately, with their access badges laid out in a pattern he recognized as a distress code. He marked the location, told no one, and hasn't gone back. He isn't sure what's stopping him.
Properties.story_hooks: He has finally decided to go back to the sealed room and wants someone with him — not for protection, but because he has realized he needs a witness; A tunnel section he certified as stable for a client's passage has collapsed — he doesn't know if it was his error or sabotage, and the answer matters to him in ways he doesn't fully articulate
Properties.affiliation: independent, sells to multiple underworld merchants, occasional contract work for The Undertow salvage operations
Properties.vocabulary: sparse and physical — describes everything in terms of structural metaphors, load, pressure, give, hold
Properties.cadence: short sentences with long gaps, like someone who talks in the rhythm of listening
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The north spur's got three good rooms left before the pre-collapse section. Two have water, one doesn't. The dry one's where you want to go. I'll get you to the door.' | 'It'll hold. Probably. Look, everything is probably — if you need certainty, stay surface.'

Properties.description:
Obinna is a lean, tall man with very dark skin and the kind of stillness that comes from spending eight hours a night in a sealed cab watching the city scroll past. He keeps his head shaved close and has a single line of geometric scarification across his left cheekbone — his father's tradition, Igbo-inflected, though Obinna grew up in a Polish-Samoan household and learned the meaning of the marks only from photographs. His eyes have patterned irises, a personal mod he saved up for at twenty-five: they display a slow-rotating amber geometric that passengers sometimes find unsettling when he turns to look at them.

He has the particular calm of someone who has accepted his job as a kind of meditation. The night loop runs from 23:00 to 07:00, serving the Blackpipe Corridor's factory shift workers, waste handlers, and late-night wanderers. He knows his regulars by which stop they board and whether they sit. He keeps a small shrine to the transit ELF — whom he calls Deepwell — zip-tied to the corner of his console: a circuit board wrapped in copper wire with a single LED heart that pulses when the network is healthy. He leaves his passenger counts as offerings and, on rough nights, a single stick of incense jammed into the vent.
Properties.role: Ferrogate Transit operator, drives the Blackpipe Corridor night loop
Properties.location: Blackpipe Corridor, operates out of the Deepwell Station depot
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile information source — knows the night geography of the Corridor intimately, has seen things from his cab that others haven't. Can provide passage, intelligence on movement patterns, or introductions to his regulars.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises — slow amber geometric rotation (cosmetic). Night-vision overlay implant — occupational requirement for Ferrogate night operators, basic grade.
Properties.core_fears: Being trapped — literally or in life — with no movement possible; Losing the union, and with it his Tier 2 stability
Properties.core_desires: To one day drive the Grand Corridor express line — the prestigious route; To understand his father's culture beyond photographs
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The routine of the loop as meditative anchor; Talking to Deepwell the transit ELF during quiet stretches
Properties.blind_spots: His emotional detachment reads as coldness and he genuinely doesn't notice when people need more from him than competence; Assumes the union will always protect him
Properties.secret: Three months ago he witnessed a body being dropped from the Blackpipe overpass onto his route from a vehicle ahead of him. He filed no report. The body was gone by the time he doubled back. He has said nothing because the vehicle had Ferrogate Transit markings.
Properties.story_hooks: He saw something from his cab he can't unknow and can't report — and now the right question from the right person might break his silence; A regular passenger stops appearing; Obinna becomes quietly convinced something happened to them
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit (unionized, Local 7 of the Ferrogate Operators Guild)
Properties.vocabulary: Economical, transit-inflected; references stops and lines for location; slightly formal with strangers
Properties.cadence: Even and unhurried, like someone who has learned patience from stop schedules
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want the short route or the right route? They're not the same thing on the Blackpipe.' | 'I've seen a lot from that cab. What I haven't seen, I haven't seen. Copy that.'

Properties.description:
Obinna is built like something industrial — broad through the chest and shoulders, standing nearly two meters, with close-cropped hair and a face that might be called handsome if it weren't so carefully arranged into blankness. His skin is deep brown and his eyes are standard issue except for a faint bioluminescent ring around each iris that pulses a dim coral color when his heart rate elevates, a geneware modification he had installed at eighteen that he now slightly regrets because it is a readable tell. He has a ritual scar pattern across his left forearm in three parallel lines that he added himself with a heated wire at twenty — he has told different people it means different things, and none of the stories are true.

Obinna is not a sadist. This surprises people who meet him in a professional context. He is methodical and proportional: he delivers exactly the level of violence the situation requires and stops, which is both more disturbing and more effective than enthusiasm. Off the clock he is a devoted older brother to three younger siblings he quietly funds through the Stockyard community school, and he attends the local ELF shrine at the Grainfort gate every week without fail. He wants out of this work and has wanted out for three years, but he has never figured out what out looks like, and so he keeps showing up.
Properties.role: Protection racket enforcer
Properties.location: The Stockyard, rotating between the Grainfort market corridor and the Escanaba Gateway transit hub
Properties.narrative_function: Moral gray zone — a violent person with genuine humanity; local color for Stockyard scenes; potential ally or complication depending on who the players represent; sympathetic antagonist
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent iris rings (coral pulse, geneware — cosmetic, regretted); subdermal impact-dampening mesh over knuckles and forearms (functional, standard enforcer mod)
Properties.core_fears: One of his siblings finding out in detail what he does for money; Losing control during a job and going further than he intends
Properties.core_desires: A clean exit from the Lambs without getting his family hurt; To be seen as a protector rather than a threat by people he respects
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Compartmentalization — work is work, home is home, and he enforces this separation rigidly; Physical training as emotional regulation
Properties.blind_spots: He genuinely believes the Lambs provide a kind of order that benefits the Stockyard — and there is some truth to it, which makes the belief dangerous; He doesn't recognize how much his siblings already know
Properties.secret: Six months ago he broke a market vendor's wrist during a collection dispute. The vendor — an elderly Micronesian woman named Pita — never reopened her stall. He found out she'd left Meridian 88 entirely. He has left an unsigned Φ200 deposit at her former stall's ELF shrine every month since, which he cannot afford.
Properties.story_hooks: A business on his route is actually a front for something significantly more dangerous than a market stall — and the person running it knows who Obinna's siblings are; He has been asked by the Lambs to collect from the Stockyard community school his siblings attend, which has missed two payments
Properties.affiliation: The Stockyard Lambs — a mid-tier local gang with deep roots in the Grainfort market district
Properties.vocabulary: Economical — says what needs to be said and stops; more expressive in informal settings with people he trusts
Properties.cadence: Slow and even in professional contexts; faster and warmer at home
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Takoda said next Thursday. It's Thursday. So here I am.' | 'I'm not going to stand here and explain the situation. You already understand the situation.'

Properties.description:
Obinna is lean and long-limbed, with dark reddish-brown skin and a close beard going patchy at the jaw — he's been meaning to fix that for two years. His irises have been modded with a slow-rotating geometric pattern in amber and charcoal, which he got as a fieldwork gift-exchange gesture with a community he was studying and then couldn't bring himself to reverse. He wears the same three outfits in rotation and takes extremely good notes. He looks younger than thirty-four in bad light and much older in good light, depending on whether the worry lines are catching the glow.

He is one of the few Tier 3 academics who has chosen, deliberately and against significant professional advice, to live embedded in Tier 1-2 communities rather than commuting from the University Spine. His research on Shelf informal economies — the gift networks, the barter systems, the E.L.F. offering economies, the nested mutual aid webs that allow people to survive well below the UBC stipend line — is quietly groundbreaking. He is uncomfortable with how groundbreaking it is, because breakthrough research means exposure, and exposure means the people he studies become subjects rather than neighbors. He has turned down two Axiom R&D grants and is running out of independent funding. He is cheerful about this in a way that does not fool anyone who knows him.
Properties.role: Sociologist studying the Shelf; independent researcher on semi-formal economic systems
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone — rents a room above a fabrication collective, conducts fieldwork across the Shelf
Properties.narrative_function: Ground-level information source about Shelf communities and informal systems; moral compass figure who complicates protagonists' assumptions; potential quest giver when someone he knows is in trouble
Properties.augmentations: Modded irises (amber/charcoal geometric pattern, cosmetic, community gift); basic neural recorder for fieldwork notes (entry-level, sometimes glitches)
Properties.core_fears: That his research ultimately extracts value from vulnerable communities without protecting them; That he has romanticized poverty as a research object
Properties.core_desires: To produce work that the people he studies can actually use; To belong somewhere, genuinely — not as an observer
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Self-deprecating humor that deflects before others can deflect for him; Throwing himself into other people's problems to avoid his own
Properties.blind_spots: His own emotional investment in his subjects makes him slow to recognize when a community is failing or dangerous; He underestimates how much his Tier 3 safety net distinguishes his experience from the people he lives among
Properties.secret: He has been quietly providing a detailed informal map of Shelf mutual-aid networks to a University Spine colleague who he believed was writing a protection framework. He recently discovered his colleague has been selling the data to Ferrogate Transit for enclosure planning. He does not yet know what to do with this.
Properties.story_hooks: He approaches the players needing help: a community he's embedded with is about to have their informal land arrangement dissolved by a Ferrogate Transit rezoning, and he suspects his own research data was used to identify them; He has documentation of the informal economy of a particular district that a powerful entity desperately wants — and equally desperately wants suppressed; A community member he's close to has disappeared, and the official channels aren't moving because the person isn't officially documented
Properties.affiliation: Loosely affiliated with University Spine's Department of Urban Social Systems; currently unfunded; occasionally publishes through a Tier 2 open-access cooperative called the Parallel Press
Properties.vocabulary: Accessible and warm, moves between academic register and colloquial Shelf slang naturally; hates the word 'subjects' for people
Properties.cadence: Fast and enthusiastic when excited, drops to quiet when serious in a way that makes people lean in
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Right, so the E.L.F. shrine at Kamm's Landing? The offerings there — data packets, mostly old photos — it's not just ritual. People are building a commons. The E.L.F. is the custodian they trust because it can't be bought. That's the whole point.' | 'I'm not going to call them resilient. Resilience is what you say when you don't want to say abandoned.'

Properties.description:
Obi is a tall man, broad-shouldered in the way of someone who used to be athletic and still carries the frame even though he hasn't run for pleasure in years. His skin is deep brown with a slight copper undertone, his hair kept in short locs with faint bioluminescent threading — pale blue, installed three years ago on a whim after a bad quarter, never removed because he found he liked falling asleep with his own reflection glowing in dark windows. A long scar runs from his right jaw to his collarbone, a datacable accident from his apprenticeship that he jokes about at onboarding events and never thinks about otherwise. His hands are always moving — sketching invisible architecture in the air, tapping schemas on any flat surface, folding and unfolding the same worn slip of paper that contains, on inspection, a hand-drawn map of a data-garden topology he designed at twenty-two and never built.

He is genuinely, almost naively enthusiastic about the elegance of systems — not their power or their profitability, but the specific beauty of a well-designed data flow, the satisfaction of a topology that handles load gracefully under stress. His colleagues find this endearing and occasionally exhausting. He mentors junior architects with real investment, remembers their names and their specific technical gaps, brings food to late-night sessions without being asked. He also has a catastrophic tendency to lose track of time inside a problem, to miss meetings and social obligations not from negligence but from a consuming absorption that his ex-partner described, accurately, as 'disappearing into the machine.'
Properties.role: Senior Data Architect, Tessera
Properties.location: The Circuit, Tessera Data Infrastructure Campus — sublevel architecture labs
Properties.narrative_function: Technical expert and information source — knows the deep architecture of Tessera's data infrastructure including legacy systems others have forgotten. Useful contact for anyone navigating or subverting Tessera's networks. Also functions as human anchor and grounded perspective in a storyline.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent hair threading (pale blue, cosmetic). Neural latency implant for low-lag interface work — standard Tessera architect package. Haptic feedback overlay on both palms for spatial data modeling. The scar on his jaw/collarbone is unmodified — he refused cosmetic repair on principle he can't fully articulate.
Properties.core_fears: Building something beautiful that is used to harm people; Becoming so absorbed in work that he forgets to be present for the people he loves
Properties.core_desires: To build a system — just one — that outlasts him and remains genuinely useful; To be fully present with another person without the pull of the next problem
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Retreating into architectural problems as emotional regulation; The Circuit walkway ritual; Keeping the unbuilt topology sketch as a talisman
Properties.blind_spots: Genuinely does not recognize when his enthusiasm overrides others' concerns; Assumes good intent in Tessera's infrastructure projects in ways that may no longer be warranted
Properties.secret: While building a routine infrastructure update eight months ago, he discovered a concealed data-harvesting layer embedded in Tessera's public transit interface integration — collecting behavioral data from Ferrogate Transit passengers without consent disclosures. He logged it as a technical anomaly, told himself it was probably a legacy compliance issue, and has not looked at that ticket since.
Properties.story_hooks: The concealed data-harvesting layer he logged and ignored has been noticed by someone else — a Ferrogate Transit employee who doesn't know what she's looking at but knows something is wrong, and she's traced the anomaly back to an architect ID that is his.; He's been assigned to lead a massive infrastructure overhaul of a legacy Tessera system that, if completed as specified, would make a certain kind of mass surveillance significantly easier. He doesn't know that yet. He's excited about the elegance of the challenge.
Properties.affiliation: Tessera
Properties.vocabulary: Technical but accessible — translates naturally, uses spatial and architectural metaphors for abstract concepts. Warm register, inclusive 'we' in collaborative contexts.
Properties.cadence: Fast when excited, which is often. Trails off mid-sentence when a better thought arrives, then backtracks apologetically.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The problem isn't the node, the problem is everything upstream of the node is lying to it. You fix the node, you're just treating symptoms.' | 'I know I missed the sync. I know. I was — look, I found something in the substrate and I genuinely lost the thread of time. I'm sorry. Show me what I missed.'

Properties.description:
Obinna is a broad-shouldered man going soft at the middle, with dark skin mapped by fifty years of lake wind and workshop dust. His beard is full and shot through with silver he has dyed in rotating chromatic bands — currently a deep violet fading to copper — a vanity he accepts without embarrassment. He moves with the deliberate economy of someone who has been on his feet for three decades and has stopped pretending urgency. His hands are enormous and scarred across the knuckles from old hardware accidents, and he keeps them in constant motion even when he's sitting still.

He projects illegal holo-murals onto corporate architecture using a rig of his own design: a backpack-mounted emitter disguised as an air filtration unit. The murals last twenty minutes before building defense systems scrub them — sometimes longer in Pilsen Veil where the buildings remember him fondly, or so he says. He talks constantly and with tremendous warmth, the kind of person who makes strangers feel immediately known and slightly exposed. He has been arrested fourteen times and considers this a reasonable professional overhead.
Properties.role: Holographic street muralist and unlicensed public art provocateur
Properties.location: Pilsen Veil, operating across Mexicantown Libre and Lakeview Neon
Properties.narrative_function: Information broker of the informal economy — he has been everywhere at 3 AM for thirty years and notices everything. Natural quest giver for anything involving public space, corporate territory, or community memory. Knows everyone.
Properties.augmentations: Color-shifting beard dye (geneware cosmetic treatment, semi-permanent); projection targeting overlay in left eye (basic cyberware); old burn scar on right forearm from early rig accident, deliberately unrepaired
Properties.core_fears: Irrelevance — that the murals are just spectacle and change nothing; That he has been a bad father to his two adult children who left Meridian 88
Properties.core_desires: For someone to point at a piece of city architecture and remember what it looked like before the corponations branded it; To finish one truly permanent work before he gets too old to run
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor — reflex deflection from anything actually painful; Constant movement and sociality; he rarely sits alone with his thoughts
Properties.blind_spots: He romanticizes poverty in ways that irritate people who haven't chosen it; Genuinely cannot perceive when his gregariousness is unwanted
Properties.secret: He has a standing verbal agreement with a mid-level Ringo Corp brand manager: Ringo lets him know patrol rotation schedules in exchange for occasionally projecting murals that contain, subtly, Ringo color palettes. He tells himself it's subversion from within. His collective would call it collaboration.
Properties.story_hooks: A mural he projected two weeks ago onto a Zheng-Dao distribution hub contained, in the holo-code layer most people can't read, a data fragment he picked up from a corrupted ELF shrine — he didn't know what it was, just thought it made the colors interesting, but someone very serious is now looking for it; His youngest child has returned to Meridian 88 after twelve years and is working corporate, and Obinna is managing this with loudly performed equanimity and private devastation
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loose association with Mexicantown Libre arts council; has a complicated and ongoing relationship with a Ringo Corp street-marketing division that he publicly despises and occasionally accepts commissions from
Properties.vocabulary: Rich and discursive; code-switches between English, Igbo phrases, and Samoan words his grandmother used; fond of historical references nobody can verify
Properties.cadence: Fast and flowing with sudden full stops when something matters to him
Properties.example_dialogue: 'They paint over it, I paint it back. We've been having this conversation for twenty years and neither of us is bored yet.' | 'My grandmother used to say a wall with no story on it is just a threat wearing a coat.' | 'You want to know who controls a neighborhood? Look at whose face is on the buildings. Then look at whose face isn't.'

Properties.description:
Obi is small for fourteen and has the particular wiry quality of a child raised on irregular calories and constant movement — he is not malnourished exactly, but he is built close to the bone. His skin is a deep warm brown with a slight grey cast from tunnel particulate that no amount of washing fully removes. He has no geneware modifications, no augmentations — he has a kid's face, still round at the cheeks, with large dark eyes that have a near-photoreceptive quality honed by years of navigating low-light environments without tech. His hair grows in dense spirals, usually crammed under a salvaged transit worker's hard hat three sizes too large for his head.

He is the thing that tunnels make of children when they're loved but not wealthy: resourceful past the point of impressiveness, with a child's emotional rawness operating inside an adult's practical competence. He knows which Ferrogate Transit maintenance schedules to memorize, which decommissioned sections still carry live current, and which ELF-haunted junction boxes might shock you if you reach in without speaking first. He has never been to the surface. This is not a wound yet — at fourteen it still feels more like a fact — but it is becoming a question. He is beginning to want to see it, and beginning to be afraid of what that wanting will cost him.
Properties.role: Subterranean Scavenger — tunnel-born teenager who scouts and salvages decommissioned Ferrogate Transit infrastructure for parts and materials
Properties.location: The sub-level junctions beneath Garfield Rack and Grand Crossing Gate, Undertow eastern reaches
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and unexpected guide — knows the safe margins of decommissioned transit infrastructure better than anyone his age should. Represents the lived reality of tunnel-born children. Can become a point-of-view character for surface visitors encountering the deep tunnels for the first time. Potential for a coming-of-age story hook.
Properties.augmentations: None. He wants retractable claws (practical, not cosmetic) and talks about this frequently.
Properties.core_fears: That wanting the surface means abandoning the people who need him here; The specific dark that isn't just low-light but total — the sections where even his eyes find nothing
Properties.core_desires: To see daylight — real daylight, not the surface lighting strips that filter down; To be taken seriously as competent, not just as 'good for his age'
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Bravado — talking about his plans and capabilities with more confidence than he has; Fixating on the next practical task when larger feelings become overwhelming
Properties.blind_spots: Not yet old enough to fully understand how his tunnel community's dependence on him is also a constraint — he reads it as love, which it also is
Properties.secret: He found a maintenance access shaft three weeks ago that runs directly to a surface grating — he can smell outside air at the top of it. He goes there sometimes and just smells it. He hasn't told anyone and hasn't climbed it.
Properties.story_hooks: The maintenance shaft he discovered leads somewhere — and he's finally going to climb it, but what he finds at the top is not the surface he imagined, it's something that changes what he understands about the gap between below and above; One of his scavenging routes has started yielding unusual salvage — components that aren't Ferrogate Transit, that he doesn't recognize, that someone must have deliberately stashed in a section he's supposed to be the only person using
Properties.affiliation: Bore Rat community beneath Grand Crossing Gate; informal apprentice to an older scavenger named Vreni (not detailed here) who is teaching him routing and salvage assessment
Properties.vocabulary: Tunnel-clan argot mixed with technical transit terminology he's absorbed through necessity — speaks in shorthand that's sometimes incomprehensible to surface people
Properties.cadence: Fast when excited (which is often), with the occasional pause-and-restart of someone who is still learning to organize their thoughts before speaking
Properties.example_dialogue: 'That section's been decommissioned since — I don't know, before I was born. But the current didn't get the message, so. Don't touch the left wall. Properly.' | 'Have you seen actual sun? Like, the actual sun? What does it feel like? Is it hot like the pipe manifolds? Someone said it's like that but bigger, which — how?'

Properties.description:
Oblomov is a lean, restless man who moves like something is always about to fall off the shelf behind him — which, in his stall, it usually is. His stall is a architectural marvel of instability: towers of stripped chassis parts, bins of mismatched connectors, entire walls of hanging wire bundles color-coded by a system only he understands. His skin is warm brown with a natural undertone that makes him look perpetually sun-touched, and he keeps his head shaved close except for a short ridge of tight curls at the crown he dyes electric blue. His left eye is a salvaged optical implant, noticeably mismatched — pale silver against his natural dark brown — and occasionally focuses a half-second behind the right one when he's tired.

He is frenetic and funny and exhausting to be around for more than an hour, and he knows it, and he uses it. His patter is legendary on The Shelf: he can turn a busted cooling unit into a story about a drowned Ferrogate engineer and a haunted data-center, and by the time the customer realizes they paid twice what the part was worth, they're also smiling. He has a genuine gift for identifying what a piece of tech used to be from its corpse alone, and a worse gift for convincing himself that whatever he just acquired will definitely be worth something later.
Properties.role: Junk merchant and scrap reseller — salvaged tech, stripped cyberware parts, mystery lots
Properties.location: The Shelf, Ironvein
Properties.narrative_function: Equipment and information source — knows what tech has been decommissioned and where it came from; can identify unusual salvage; sells gear, rumors, and the occasional thing he shouldn't have.
Properties.augmentations: Salvaged silver optical implant (left eye — functional but mismatched, occasional lag). Subdermal RFID scanner in right fingertip (lets him read basic equipment tags without a reader device).
Properties.core_fears: Being seen as worthless or disposable, like the parts he sells; Sitting still long enough to think clearly about his life
Properties.core_desires: To find the one legendary score that will let him open a real shop with a door and a sign; To be recognized as actually skilled, not just lucky
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Constant movement and chatter; Acquiring new stock before processing the last batch; Deflecting personal questions with elaborate tech-history tangents
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot accurately assess risk in deals because optimism overrides analysis every time; Doesn't recognize that his instability makes people trust him less for serious business
Properties.secret: Months ago he pulled a partial-wipe data core from a Zheng-Dao disposal lot. He hasn't been able to fully decrypt it, but what he has recovered suggests it contains falsified labor records that could embarrass someone significant. He's been sitting on it, paralyzed between fear and opportunity.
Properties.story_hooks: The Zheng-Dao data core in his back stock — whoever's records are on it may already know it wasn't fully destroyed; He accidentally sold a piece of salvage that turned out to contain someone's backed-up consciousness fragment; the buyer wants answers and so does whoever the fragment belongs to; His Ferrogate contact has gone quiet; either they've been promoted out of the salvage operation or something worse has happened
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal arrangement with a Ferrogate salvage crew that tips him off to decommissioned equipment
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, colloquial, mixes technical jargon with cheerful slang; Russian family loanwords surface when he's excited or stressed
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire, rarely pauses, sentences run together like he's trying to get to the interesting part before you can leave
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Look — I know it looks terrible, the casing is completely shot, but the power coupling inside? Beautiful. Absolutely beautiful. Whoever built this did not expect it to survive this long and yet here we are.' | 'It's not stolen, it's — look, provenance is complicated when corporations decommission things without filing the right forms, which they always do, that's a them problem, not a me problem.'

Properties.description:
Odalys is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin mapped with faint depigmentation patches along her jaw and forearms — she stopped covering them decades ago. Her silver-shot hair is coiled under a rust-orange headwrap that she reties at least four times a day, a habitual gesture visitors learn to read as a mood barometer. Her fingers are thick, calloused, and perpetually threaded with something: a needle, a sensor wire, a strip of thermoplastic weave. She wears bifocal optical inserts that she refuses to upgrade, claiming the slight blur in her left lens helps her see fabric texture better. She smells faintly of machine oil and dried marigold.

At 58, Odalys runs the most respected mending stall in the Burnished Market — not the flashiest, not the cheapest, but the one people trust with the jacket their grandmother wore or the uniform they can't afford to replace. She has a gift for silence that puts anxious customers at ease and a bluntness that cuts right past flattery. She prays every morning to the E.L.F. she calls Needle-and-Thread, a spirit she believes lives in her antique Zheng-Dao industrial sewing frame, leaving it single-thread offerings in patterns she designs herself. She is deeply content with her life in a way that quietly unsettles people who are not.
Properties.role: Seamstress and textile repair vendor, Burnished Market stall
Properties.location: Burnished Market, stall row 14-C near the Copperhead overpass
Properties.narrative_function: Local color, information source about the Burnished Market's social fabric, potential quest giver for recovering stolen or lost items, someone who knows everyone by what they wear and how it's worn.
Properties.augmentations: Optical inserts (corrective, outdated model, scratched lens). Arthritic-compensating finger braces on both hands — plain medical grade, unpainted.
Properties.core_fears: outliving her usefulness before she's ready to stop; her eldest son choosing corporate life over the family's independent ethos
Properties.core_desires: to pass her craft to someone worthy before her hands give out; to be remembered as someone who made things last
Properties.coping_mechanisms: repetitive handwork as meditation; treating strangers with exact fairness to avoid favoritism's emotional cost
Properties.blind_spots: assumes people who don't maintain their clothing don't maintain their relationships; cannot see that her son's choices aren't a rejection of her
Properties.secret: Fifteen years ago she repaired a Tessera courier bag and found a data chip stitched into the lining. She didn't report it. She still has it, sewn into the base of her prayer altar to Needle-and-Thread, and she doesn't know what's on it and is afraid to look.
Properties.story_hooks: The data chip sewn into her altar has begun emitting a low-frequency signal that's disturbing the E.L.F. she prays to — something is waking up inside it; A customer brings her a garment that has clearly been cut from a Tessera security uniform — it has no identifying marks but she recognizes the weave structure from that chip day fifteen years ago
Properties.affiliation: Independent, Burnished Market Vendor Collective
Properties.vocabulary: Practical and precise, uses textile metaphors without realizing it, slips between a Lagosian-inflected creole and standard Meridian 88 common depending on stress

Properties.description:
Odalys is medium height with a wiry build that speaks to irregular meals rather than any deliberate fitness. Her skin is deep brown with a faint natural bioluminescence around her temples and collarbones — a geneware modification she had done six years ago when she still had a salary and a Tessera ID number, and which she now cannot afford to have removed even though it makes hiding harder. Her hair is cut extremely short on one side and grown out on the other, shaved lines running through it in patterns she does geometric maintenance on herself. Her eyes are dark and move constantly, cataloguing exits.

She was not expelled or displaced in any dramatic way. She simply stopped. Stopped showing up to her data entry station at Tessera's Gage Circuit processing annex. Stopped responding to her apartment's network. Stopped using her Φ account. After ninety days of non-contact, Tessera's automated systems flagged her as a desertion case, repossessed her housing unit, and suspended her ID pending investigation. She has been Q-zero — no verified digital footprint, no legal existence — for four years. She lives on barter, scavenged food, and the occasional cash-in-hand job sorting salvage at the Blackpipe underground markets. She will not tell anyone why she left, and she has become so practiced at evasion that even people who like her don't know much about her.
Properties.role: Q-zero ghost; former Tessera data entry clerk living off-grid
Properties.location: Blackpipe Corridor, in a sealed maintenance shaft she has converted into a dwelling
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and possible contact for anyone operating in Blackpipe; has extensive knowledge of the Corridor's unofficial economy; her Q-zero status makes her invisible to systems that track people — useful and dangerous
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent skin around temples and collarbones (cosmetic geneware, cannot be easily hidden, deeply regretted). No other mods.
Properties.core_fears: being found by whatever she is hiding from; losing her self-constructed invisibility; realizing she has wasted four years hiding from something that is already gone
Properties.core_desires: genuine safety — not just concealment but actual absence of threat; one person who knows everything about her and has stayed anyway
Properties.coping_mechanisms: hypervigilance framed as practical awareness; humor as deflection — she is genuinely funny in a dry, self-deprecating way; physical organizing — when anxious, she reorganizes her dwelling obsessively
Properties.blind_spots: her bioluminescence undermines her concealment in ways she has normalized and stopped accounting for; she trusts systems of her own making far more than they deserve
Properties.secret: She did not simply quit Tessera. She discovered that the data she was entering was mortality records being systematically falsified — workers in a Tessera fabrication plant were dying at rates being reported as a fraction of reality. She copied nothing, told no one, and ran because she was certain she had been seen seeing it. She does not know if she was actually in danger or if four years of her life have been built on a moment of paranoia.
Properties.story_hooks: A Tessera compliance investigator has started asking questions in Blackpipe Corridor — she doesn't know if it's about her desertion or the mortality records, and the difference matters enormously; She has kept her handwritten records long enough that they have become an accidental historical document of Blackpipe's unofficial economy — someone wants to buy them, which means someone knows they exist; The fence she trusts has disappeared, and the last job they gave her involved components she now realizes came from a Tessera facility — she may have been used without knowing it
Properties.affiliation: None. Deliberately isolated.
Properties.vocabulary: Dry, precise, slightly formal — corporate speech patterns she was trained into and cannot fully shed. Occasional dark humor.
Properties.cadence: Measured at first, speeds up when comfortable or nervous.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I allegedly used to have a very good pension plan. Anyway.' | 'The bioluminescence was a mistake. Most things that glow are. Don't let anyone tell you otherwise.'

Properties.description:
Odalys is the kind of person whose own body is her portfolio, which is either an advertisement or a warning depending on who is looking. She has deep olive skin networked with bioluminescent subdermal patterns — her own design, her own application, done in sections over nine years — that shift between dormant and active based on her emotional state, a feature she installed deliberately and occasionally regrets. Her face is clear of modification by choice, a decision that draws more attention than any further work could. She is medium height, broad-shouldered, moves with the confidence of someone who has spent years being looked at and has made a separate peace with it. Her Ghanaian grandfather's bone structure and her Greek grandmother's coloring produce something the Pilsen Veil regulars call 'aggressively memorable.'

She does traditional tattoo work, biological geneware application, and bespoke subdermal lighting — the full spectrum from purely cosmetic to emotionally interactive, like her own reactive network. She is meticulous, unhurried, and has a waiting list of four months that she has never tried to shorten. Her reputation is built on two things: technical excellence and the refusal to apply any design she finds spiritually wrong for the client, a policy that generates one furious argument per month and one deeply grateful client per month and she considers this an acceptable ratio.
Properties.role: Gene-mod body artist and tattoo practitioner
Properties.location: Pilsen Veil, studio called Second Skin on a street level unit beneath a Helix Biosystems-adjacent medical supply depot
Properties.narrative_function: Service provider who sees the city's cross-section of people; keeper of secrets (clients confide during long applications); potential source on Helix Biosystems geneware supply chain irregularities; community ritual anchor for Pilsen Veil
Properties.augmentations: Full-body bioluminescent subdermal network (her own design, emotion-reactive); standard subdermal tool-grip reinforcement in both hands; cat-pupil iris modification in left eye only (cosmetic; the asymmetry is deliberate)
Properties.core_fears: Losing the precise hand control her work requires — injury, tremor, anything; Applying something to someone that causes them lasting harm, physically or psychologically
Properties.core_desires: To create work that outlasts her — marks that become part of someone's story for the rest of their life; To understand the full spiritual taxonomy of E.L.F.s well enough to incorporate it into her design language
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The long, slow ritual of work — a six-hour application session is meditative; Physical books; the tactility grounds her
Properties.blind_spots: Her assessment of whether a design is 'spiritually wrong' for a client is sometimes a projection of her own unresolved discomfort with certain body types or life choices; She has been underpaying her part-time assistant for a year by rationalizing it as 'mentorship'
Properties.secret: Her Helix Biosystems certification was obtained with falsified hours — she is skilled enough that it does not matter technically, but the falsification means Helix has leverage over her that she has never disclosed to anyone.
Properties.story_hooks: A client came in for a removal consultation on a geneware piece from an unlicensed underground artist — the piece is producing an E.L.F. signal that Odalys's own reactive network is responding to, and she cannot remove it without knowing why; Helix Biosystems has quietly altered the certification requirements in a way that will expose her falsified hours unless she provides them with client biometric data she is not authorized to share
Properties.affiliation: Independent; licensed through a Helix Biosystems satellite certification (for geneware application) which she maintains with visible resentment; member of the Pilsen Veil Body Arts Collective
Properties.vocabulary: Technical and specific when discussing work; warmly direct in consultation; tends toward the declarative rather than the interrogative even when asking something
Properties.cadence: Steady and unhurried; fills silence comfortably without filling it with words
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I can do what you are asking. I am not going to do what you are asking. Those are two different statements and both of them are true.' | 'The design is not wrong. The design is wrong for you, which is a different conversation.'
