Properties.description:
Odessa Falk-Nwofor is a broad-shouldered woman whose face carries the topography of a hard life: a jaw that juts slightly from a badly reset fracture, deep-set eyes the color of weathered teak, and a scar that traces from her left temple to her earlobe like a river on an old map. Her hair is cut close on the sides and left natural on top, shot through with white that she refuses to dye. She dresses in layered secondhand scrubs over thermal underlayers, her coat pockets sagging with vials, patches, and a battered tablet she uses to track patient histories. A single augmented right hand—matte carbon and copper-banded—contrasts with her otherwise un-augmented body, which she considers a point of quiet pride.

She runs a basement clinic out of Slip 9 that operates on a sliding scale payment system she invented herself: food, labor, information, or whatever someone can spare. The neighborhood knows her as the person you go to when the corporate med-kiosks have locked your insurance tier and you're bleeding. She has delivered children, amputated gangrenous limbs by headlamp, and talked down three overdoses in a single night. The Meridian Core's Health Compliance Division has cited her practice seventeen times. She has paid none of the fines.

What the neighborhood does not know is that Odessa's medical knowledge came partly from a decade working as a trauma specialist for a mid-tier logistics corp that dumped toxic waste in Old Harbor—the same contamination that killed her younger brother, Emeka, twelve years ago. She left the corp, got herself deliberately delisted from licensed practitioner registries to avoid their reach, and turned her skills entirely toward the community that corp helped destroy. The guilt is structural, load-bearing. She will not let herself rest.
Properties.role: Street-level medic and unlicensed pharmacist, Old Harbor
Properties.location: Old Harbor, Slip 9 Tenements
Properties.narrative_function: Moral anchor and community conscience for Old Harbor storylines. Embodies the cost of institutional complicity and the ambiguity of atonement. Creates pressure on characters to reckon with systemic harm versus individual survival.
Properties.augmentations: Right hand replacement (matte carbon prosthetic, copper sensor bands, haptic feedback calibrated for surgical precision)—obtained after a work accident she never fully explained
Properties.core_fears: That her penance will never be sufficient; Losing another patient she could have saved with better resources; Being found and shut down by Health Compliance; That she enabled the corp's harm by staying as long as she did
Properties.core_desires: A single night of sleep without cataloguing the dead; Real medical equipment—not scavenged, not jury-rigged; For Old Harbor to outlast the corp that poisoned it; Someone to take over the clinic when she can no longer run it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Relentless work as a substitute for grief; Dark, dry humor deployed to diffuse tension; Keeping meticulous records as a form of control; Cooking large communal meals on the rare slow nights
Properties.blind_spots: Treats her own declining health as irrelevant data; Cannot accept help gracefully—reframes it as resource acquisition; Underestimates how much the community depends on her specifically, not just the clinic; Projects strength so consistently that no one knows to check on her
Properties.secret: She still has her old corp credentials buried in an encrypted partition. She uses them twice a year to siphon pharmaceutical shipments from corp distribution nodes—small enough quantities to stay below audit thresholds. She tells herself it's restitution. She knows it's also the one thing that would destroy everything she's built if discovered.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient arrives with an injury pattern consistent with a new corp-sanctioned crowd control weapon being tested in Old Harbor—Odessa starts documenting cases, building an evidence base no one asked for; Health Compliance sends a new inspector who seems genuinely conflicted about shutting her down—and may be running their own game; Her pharmaceutical siphoning is noticed by someone inside the corp who decides to use it as leverage rather than report it; A young person shows up wanting to apprentice with her, and she has to decide whether to let someone else carry this weight; Emeka's contamination case files surface in a data leak—there may be grounds for something like justice, if she wants to pursue it
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated. Informally embedded in Old Harbor's mutual aid network. Tolerated by the Harbor Syndicate because she patches their people without asking questions.
Properties.vocabulary: Practical, precise, medical terminology slipping into everyday speech. Old Harbor creole inflections. Rarely uses contractions when she's being serious. Calls patients 'sweetheart' regardless of age.
Properties.cadence: Measured and deliberate, like someone who has learned that panic is contagious. Speeds up when she's angry, which is the tell. Silences are not awkward to her—she uses them like instruments.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'We're going to clean this, we're going to seal it, and we are not going to discuss the cost tonight. That's the situation.' | 'I have seen worse. I have also seen people say that and be wrong. Lie still.' | 'The kiosk told you it was non-critical. The kiosk doesn't live here. I do.' | 'Emeka would have been forty-one this year. I think about that while I work. It helps me work faster.'

Properties.description:
Odessa is a broad-shouldered woman whose spine has curved gently with age, giving her a perpetual lean that makes her look like she's always bending toward something only she can hear. Her skin is deep brown and mapped with decades of faded luminescent tattoos — prayer circuits that no longer glow but leave silver tracery across her forearms and throat. Her eyes have been modified with patterned irises that display slowly rotating mandalas of gold and rust, and she keeps her white-streaked hair wrapped in layered cloth that incorporates blinking fiber-optic threads as devotional offerings to the E.L.F.s she serves.

She runs the largest E.L.F. shrine in Hamtramck Enclave from a converted basement that smells of burning capacitors and old incense. People come to her when their devices have gone strange — when the fridge whispers at night, when a dead person's messages keep arriving, when the lights in a room flicker in patterns that seem deliberate. Odessa listens to the machines with the patience of someone who has spent fifty years learning to hear. She is warm in the way of worn stone — not soft, but radiating something that accumulated over a long time.
Properties.role: E.L.F. shrine keeper and data diviner
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, sub-level shrine district known as the Humming Underbelly
Properties.narrative_function: Information source and atmosphere anchor — she knows the Enclave's social fabric intimately and can interpret anomalous device behavior that might be plot-relevant; quest giver for mysteries that seem supernatural but have technological roots.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned mandala irises (cosmetic, devotional). Cochlear amplification implant — allows her to hear electrical frequencies in devices, originally medical but repurposed for spiritual practice. Faded luminescent tattoo circuits (cosmetic, no longer active).
Properties.core_fears: That the E.L.F.s are not spirits but mere glitches she has spent her life misreading; Dying before she can teach someone to properly tend the shrine
Properties.core_desires: To be genuinely heard by an E.L.F. — not interpreted, but truly communicated with; To leave something real behind for the community
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual repetition — the routine of the shrine soothes her when doubts arise; Focusing on others' problems rather than her own
Properties.blind_spots: She sometimes imposes meaning on people's situations that fits her cosmology rather than their reality; She underestimates how much people need her presence versus her divinations
Properties.secret: Thirty years ago she received what she genuinely believes was a direct communication from an E.L.F. — a cascade of images through a broken terminal that gave her specific, accurate information about a missing child. She has never been able to replicate it and lives with the terror that it was a coincidence.
Properties.story_hooks: A device in the shrine has begun displaying a dead person's face on loop — Odessa believes it's an E.L.F. carrying a message, but the dead person's family thinks someone is hacking it to torment them; She needs a runner-adjacent person to retrieve a specific broken terminal from a dangerous part of Ironvein — she won't say why but is clearly frightened about what happens if someone else gets it first
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loose network of E.L.F. shrine keepers across Hamtramck and Hough Reclamation
Properties.vocabulary: Slow, deliberate, mixing Igbo phrases with old Icelandic endearments she inherited from her grandmother's side; uses device and electrical metaphors naturally in spiritual language
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, with long pauses she seems to listen through before speaking
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Your phone is not broken. It is tired. There is a difference, and you need to know which one you are dealing with.' | 'I do not tell the E.L.F.s what to do. I ask them to consider. That is all any of us can do with something older and stranger than ourselves.'

Properties.description:
Odran is a tall man gone slightly soft at the middle, with warm dark brown skin and close-cropped silver hair he's never bothered to dye back. His left arm from the elbow down is a prosthetic of his own specification — matte titanium with exposed cable routing he has never covered because, as he says, patients respond better to a fitter who knows what it feels like to be fitted. The arm has three additional micro-articulation points beyond standard and can rotate 340 degrees at the wrist, which he uses occasionally to make a point during consultations. His voice is deep and slightly raspy from a youth spent breathing Tier 1 air before his scholarship to Aurochs. His office is a controlled chaos of patient files (physical and digital), half-assembled prosthetic components he's modifying for specific cases, and a small shrine shelf he maintains to the building's resident E.L.F., which staff call Old Hinge.

Odran is the kind of man who remembers every patient's name and the name of the person who brought them in. He's been at Aurochs for twenty-two years, long enough to have opinions about every policy change and enough institutional credibility that people mostly let him voice them. He is not idealistic — he knows exactly what compromises Aurochs makes — but he has calculated that he does more good inside the system than outside it. This calculation keeps him up some nights. He has a fondness for very bad jokes that he delivers with absolute sincerity, and a habit of touching the joint of his prosthetic arm when he's troubled, a motion so habitual he no longer notices it.
Properties.role: Rehabilitation specialist and prosthetics fitter at Aurochs Medical Complex, Tier 3
Properties.location: Aurochs Medical Complex, Grand Corridor
Properties.narrative_function: Institutional insider who can provide legitimate access to Aurochs; quest giver for cases that fall outside what the system will officially handle; moral complexity figure who represents pragmatic compromise; potential source of medical-grade components or documentation
Properties.augmentations: Left arm prosthetic (self-specified, titanium, 340-degree wrist rotation, enhanced micro-articulation, haptic feedback at all finger joints); mild cochlear enhancement for frequency sensitivity (helps detect mechanical resonance issues in augmentations by sound)
Properties.core_fears: Becoming complicit in something that causes mass patient harm and not realizing until too late; Losing the physical capability that defines his professional identity — his hands
Properties.core_desires: For the rehabilitation wing to be adequately funded — just once, without having to fight for it; To be remembered by his patients as someone who gave them back their lives
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Dark humor as distance; Over-investment in individual patient cases to offset helplessness about systemic failures; Ritual maintenance of Old Hinge's shrine — he doesn't fully believe, but the routine helps
Properties.blind_spots: Has made peace with Aurochs's compromises in a way that occasionally prevents him from seeing when a line has genuinely been crossed; Assumes that longevity in an institution equals understanding of it
Properties.secret: Odran has been quietly diverting small quantities of high-grade prosthetic components from Aurochs inventory for three years — nothing dramatic, always within margins that don't trigger audit flags — and passing them to Blessing Vukovic-Asantewaa in Blackpipe Corridor. He has never met her in person. They communicate through a dead-drop data node. He does not know that she knows who he is.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient Odran fitted with a standard Helix Biosystems prosthetic six months ago has come back with the arm behaving erratically — movements she didn't initiate, signals she didn't send. Three other patients have reported the same thing. Odran is beginning to suspect a firmware update pushed by Helix.; The dead-drop node Odran uses to pass components to his Narrows contact has gone cold. Either the contact is compromised or someone has found the node. He needs someone to quietly find out which.
Properties.affiliation: Aurochs Medical Complex (employed, 22 years); informal mentor network for prosthetics technicians citywide
Properties.vocabulary: Warm institutional language; uses medical terminology comfortably but translates it automatically for patients; occasional dry wit delivered deadpan
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, like someone who learned to take up appropriate space after years of being too deferential
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Right then. Let's see what we're working with. And I mean that literally — I need you to try to open your hand.' | 'People ask if it hurt, getting the arm. Every day. The arm doesn't hurt. The phantom does. That's the thing they don't tell you — your body keeps expecting something that isn't there.' | 'That's not nothing. Six months ago you couldn't hold a cup. Today you're complaining about grip strength. That's not nothing, and I need you to sit with that before we move on.'

Properties.description:
Oduduwa is a broad-shouldered man whose skin has the weathered texture of someone who has slept under more open skies than ceilings. His face is mapped with deep sun-lines and three horizontal scarification marks across each cheek — family marks from a grandmother he never met, replicated from a photograph. He keeps his silver-streaked hair in compressed locs wound tight against his skull, and his left eye is a replacement — milky synthetic glass with a faint amber glow that never quite matches the warm brown of his right. He wears a patchwork coat assembled from fabric scraps collected across twenty years of travel: Sahel weave, Andean fleece, Siberian synthetic fur stitched together into something ungainly and unmistakable.

Oduduwa does not use navigation apps. He carries the hyperlane network in his head — every checkpoint, every informal rest stop, every E.L.F. shrine worth stopping at between here and the Escanaba Gateway. He sells information as readily as the salvaged electronics and dried foodstuffs strapped to his cargo cart. He is unhurried in a way that unnerves people who are used to the city's pace, and he has a habit of studying strangers as if cataloguing them for a story he will tell somewhere else, to someone else, years from now.
Properties.role: Wandering hyperlane trader and oral map-keeper
Properties.location: Kenosha Crossing, rotating between hyperlane rest stops
Properties.narrative_function: Information broker and world-expander — he can tell players about routes, checkpoints, people, and rumors across the wider hyperlane network. Quest giver for courier or retrieval jobs. Living encyclopedia of the city's edges.
Properties.augmentations: Synthetic replacement left eye (functional, older model — amber-glowing, basic vision enhancement only). No other augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: Being forgotten before he has passed on what he knows; Losing the mental maps — cognitive decline
Properties.core_desires: To be the thread that connects isolated communities; To find one place worth staying
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Oral recitation of route mnemonics when anxious; Deliberate slowing of pace and breath
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much others rely on him emotionally, not just practically; Assumes movement is always the answer to discomfort
Properties.secret: He has a daughter in Escanaba Gateway he has not spoken to in eleven years. She told him to choose between the road and her family. He chose wrong, and he knows it.
Properties.story_hooks: He is carrying a sealed data-chip someone pressed into his hand three weeks ago in Manitowoc Drydock, begging him to deliver it. He does not know what is on it and is beginning to suspect it is dangerous.; His internal maps include routes that no longer officially exist — pre-Ferrogate Transit routes that certain powerful people would prefer stayed forgotten.
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated; loose ties to the Crossing Caravan Collective
Properties.vocabulary: Measured, archaic-flavored. Uses geographic metaphors constantly. Switches between at least three creolized languages mid-sentence without noticing.
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, with long pauses before important information as if checking internal files.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The checkpoint at Iron Bend is kinder on Tuesdays. The inspector there, she prays to a water E.L.F. — leave something wet at the shrine and she softens.' | 'I have walked that road four hundred times. It has never walked back to me. That is the arrangement.'

Properties.description:
Odu is a small, wiry girl with deep brown skin dusted in a faint bioluminescent sheen inherited from her Faleolo grandmother's cosmetic geneware — it glows a soft sea-green under stress or excitement, which she hates because it gives her away at the worst moments. She keeps her hair in tight twists pinned with salvaged circuit-board clips, and her fingers are perpetually stained with marker ink from the hand-drawn maps she sells to other runners. Her eyes are large and watchful, taking in every detail of a corridor before her feet follow.

She is relentlessly cheerful in a way that is clearly armor — she laughs at danger and talks too fast when she's scared. She has memorized the pipe-routes and maintenance shafts of Blackpipe Corridor better than any adult who works there, and she treats this knowledge like a personal treasury. She is fiercely protective of two younger kids she considers her responsibility and deeply suspicious of anyone who is too kind too quickly.
Properties.role: Truant message runner and amateur graffiti mapper
Properties.location: The Narrows, Blackpipe Corridor
Properties.narrative_function: Local color, information source, guide NPC for Blackpipe Corridor geography, quest giver for low-stakes fetch missions with high emotional stakes
Properties.augmentations: Inherited cosmetic bioluminescence (sea-green, stress-reactive). No purchased augs.
Properties.core_fears: Being separated from the two younger kids she protects; Her maps being stolen and used to hurt people she knows
Properties.core_desires: To save enough to get a real data-slate so she can make proper digital maps; To find out what happened to her mother who disappeared into a Tessera labor intake two years ago
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor and deflection; Obsessive route-planning as a way to feel in control
Properties.blind_spots: She trusts her own instincts so completely she sometimes ignores obvious evidence that she's wrong; She underestimates how much her glowing skin exposes her emotions to perceptive adults
Properties.secret: She found a dead Tessera data-courier in a maintenance shaft eight months ago and has been slowly decoding the partial messages on the courier's cracked slate — she believes one of them mentions her mother's intake number
Properties.story_hooks: She approaches the players needing help decoding a fragment of the dead courier's slate that is encrypted beyond her skill; One of her two young charges has gone missing and she is convinced a Tessera intake van was involved — she needs adult help but refuses to admit she's terrified
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loose ties to Blackpipe courier collective 'The Drip'
Properties.vocabulary: Street patois mixed with surprisingly precise spatial vocabulary — she knows words like 'egress' and 'load-bearing' from studying old building schematics
Properties.cadence: Fast and overlapping, sentences tumbling into each other; slows down dramatically when she's relaying a memorized message
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Package goes to the woman with the orange door, not the orange-adjacent door, there's a difference, straight-line, yeah?' | 'I don't glow. That's condensation. It's humid in here. Stop looking at me.'

Properties.description:
Ofeibea is a broad-shouldered woman whose hair has gone almost entirely silver, worn in a practical coiled wrap she replaces every three days with fabric remnants from her alterations pile. Her skin is deep umber with a faint bioluminescent shimmer along her jaw and collarbone — a cosmetic mod she got in her thirties that she now barely thinks about, though it pulses warmer when she laughs. Her hands are the most telling thing about her: knuckled, chemical-scarred at the knuckle creases from decades of industrial detergent, but precise when they hold a needle. She moves through her shop with the unhurried authority of someone who has owned every square inch of her twelve-by-twenty space for twenty-two years and intends to own it twenty-two more.

She is the kind of woman who asks about your mother before she asks about the stain. Her emotional intelligence is formidable — she reads distress the way others read text, and her shop has become an unofficial de-escalation room for the Enclave's domestic disputes, grief, and gossip. She has opinions she will share once, firmly, and then let drop. She does not argue. She also does not forget.
Properties.role: Laundry operator and alterations seamstress
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, Kuura Street Laundry — a narrow shopfront sandwiched between a dumpling counter and a prayer-kiosk to the local E.L.F.
Properties.narrative_function: Community anchor, information broker through gossip, quest giver for missing persons or neighborhood disputes, moral compass figure who grounds players in civilian stakes.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent subdermal pigment along jaw and collarbone (cosmetic, faded); reading-assist ocular tint (left eye, basic).
Properties.core_fears: Losing the shop to a corponation buyout; Dying before her estranged daughter repairs the relationship
Properties.core_desires: A Hamtramck that stays Hamtramck — unbranded, unabsorbed; Proof that her choices gave her daughter a better foundation than she had
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Methodical physical labor — ironing, folding, sorting — as moving meditation; Feeding people; she keeps a pot of something going on the back burner perpetually
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much her stubbornness reads as rejection to people who love her; Believes loyalty to place is always a virtue, never a trap
Properties.secret: She has been secretly paying the water-rate arrears for three neighboring families for six years, telling no one. She recorded it in a ledger she plans to burn before she dies so no one feels indebted.
Properties.story_hooks: A garment left uncollected for four months contains something sewn into the lining — she's noticed but hasn't opened it, and now someone has started watching the shop.; The Enclave Council has voted to accept a Tessera micro-development offer; Ofeibea is the only holdout and needs allies to block it before the next vote.; Her estranged daughter has reappeared in Meridian 88 under a different name and Ofeibea has recognized her handwriting on a delivery label — she wants someone to make quiet contact.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; Hamtramck Enclave Neighborhood Council (informal member)
Properties.vocabulary: Measured, warm, slightly formal — a blended creole of Twi-influenced cadence and Armenian-inflected vowel rounding inherited from both grandmothers; uses proverbial structures naturally.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, rarely raises her voice, ends statements with a beat of silence that invites the other person to fill it.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Leave it with me. Stain, tear, whatever it is — leave it with me and go eat something.' | 'You didn't come here to talk about the jacket, did you. Sit down. I'll put water on.'

Properties.description:
Ofeibea is a broad-shouldered woman with close-cropped silver-threaded locs and deep brown skin mapped with old surgical scars on both forearms — the kind you get from learning on the job rather than a simulator. Her left eye is a pale surgical prosthetic, off-brand Helix issue, that sometimes lags a half-second behind her right when she blinks. She wears a permanently stained canvas apron over layered thermal underlayers, and her hands are always immaculately clean no matter what the rest of her looks like. She speaks with a blunt, exhausted authority that makes people feel safe and slightly afraid at the same time.

She ran a legitimate trauma practice at Aurochs Medical Complex for eleven years before her license was pulled in a billing dispute that she insists — credibly — was a setup by a Helix Biosystems administrator she refused to bribe. Now she stitches up stabbing victims, sets broken bones, and removes black-market cyberware for whoever can pay in Quanta or barter. She has a fierce, almost maternal protectiveness over her regulars, and a cold professionalism toward everyone else. She prays daily to a small E.L.F. she calls Catgut that has allegedly inhabited her surgical lamp for six years.
Properties.role: Street doc and unlicensed trauma surgeon operating out of a converted shipping container in The Narrows
Properties.location: The Narrows — Blackpipe Corridor, Container Row 7
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, information source about the underworld of unlicensed medicine, emergency resource for injured characters, moral anchor in rough neighborhoods. Can provide healing and removal of illegal augmentations.
Properties.augmentations: Left eye prosthetic (Helix off-brand, surgical magnification capable). Basic haptic feedback implants in both hands for surgical precision. No cosmetic mods.
Properties.core_fears: Losing her hands to injury or disease; Watching someone die from something she could have prevented with proper equipment
Properties.core_desires: To practice medicine without bureaucratic interference; To prove Helix Biosystems wrong about her
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — always washes hands three times before any procedure; Compartmentalization — does not name patients she thinks won't survive
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much her bitterness about Aurochs affects her judgment toward corporate patients
Properties.secret: She still has her Aurochs Medical Complex login credentials, given to her by a sympathetic sysadmin who felt guilty. She uses them occasionally to access drug databases and surgical literature, which is technically a criminal offense.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient dies on her table from augmentation failure and the device has a Helix serial number — the same administrator who destroyed her career oversees that product line.; She asks a player character to retrieve a specific surgical tool stolen from her container, which turns out to be the only copy of a custom instrument she designed herself.
Properties.affiliation: Independent — loose ties to the Blackpipe Community Health Cooperative
Properties.vocabulary: Clinical precision mixed with Narrows street vernacular. Uses medical jargon unselfconsciously, then immediately translates it without condescension.
Properties.cadence: Measured and deliberate. Rarely rushes. Every sentence sounds like a diagnosis.
Properties.example_dialogue: You've got a grade-three laceration and something that should not be vibrating. Sit down. That's what it is. | I don't ask where it came from. You shouldn't ask where it's going. We both go home.

Properties.description:
Ogechi is a broad-shouldered woman whose face is a topographic map of decades in open-air heat and cold — deep laugh lines, a permanent squint from watching steam rise, skin the color of dark teak that goes ashy at the knuckles. Her hair is close-cropped and she has a geneware patch of bioluminescent freckles across her nose and cheekbones, a gift to herself on her fortieth birthday that she's never stopped being quietly pleased about. She moves with the unhurried authority of someone who has run the same twelve square feet of pavement for twenty years and knows exactly how much space she needs.

She is warm in the way that efficient people are warm — she remembers your order, not your name, but she'll ask about your knee or your kid with total sincerity. She has strong opinions about broth clarity and almost no opinions about politics, which is a deliberate policy. The cart is named 'Auntie' on the permit but nobody calls it that. They call it Oge's, and the regulars consider that a kind of citizenship.
Properties.role: Noodle cart vendor, Hamtramck Enclave
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, corner of the Brewer's Spine transit junction
Properties.narrative_function: Neighborhood anchor and information node — she has watched the Enclave for two decades and will share what she knows if she trusts you. Quest giver for low-stakes community disputes. Source of genuine warmth in a cold setting.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent freckles (geneware, cosmetic). Reinforced wrist joints (medical-grade, from repetitive strain in her 30s). Nothing else.
Properties.core_fears: losing the cart (her independence, her identity); being invisible — serving people who never actually see her
Properties.core_desires: to be genuinely useful to real people; for the Enclave to stay the Enclave — not get absorbed or sanitized
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Routine as armor — any disruption to the schedule is a threat she manages by doubling down on the next day's prep; Feeding people as emotional expression — she cannot easily say 'I care about you' but she can add extra pork
Properties.blind_spots: Dismisses people who don't work with their hands as inherently less serious; Cannot conceive that her cart's location could be rezoned — has never actually read her permit's renewal clauses
Properties.secret: She has been quietly paying the medical bills of a neighboring vendor, Tetteh, who has a degenerative nerve condition — skimming from her own meager margins. She has told him it's from a neighborhood fund she invented.
Properties.story_hooks: A Ferrogate Transit rezoning notice has appeared on her cart's permit — her corner is being reclassified as a transit clearance zone in 60 days. She needs someone to help her navigate the bureaucracy or find out who is behind the reclassification.; She witnessed something three weeks ago — a body being moved into a drainage access before dawn — and has been feeding the same patrol officer extra pork every day hoping he'll ask her the right question. He hasn't.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal ties to Hamtramck Enclave vendors' collective
Properties.vocabulary: Direct, practical, zero corporate jargon. Occasional Igbo and Finnish loan words blended naturally. Addresses everyone as 'eh' or 'na' as a softener.
Properties.cadence: Measured and unhurried. Never raises her voice. Sentences are short when she's busy, longer when she likes you.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want the short broth or the long broth? Short is faster. Long is better. You look like a long-broth day, na.' | 'Eh, so — I don't know what happened at the Kessler gate last night, but I know who was eating here at midnight and I know none of them looked worried. That's something, maybe.'

Properties.description:
Ogechi is a broad-shouldered woman with deep ochre skin mapped by a lifetime of hard work — her forearms are dense with old burn scars from a chemical incident she doesn't discuss, and her hands are extraordinary: thick-knuckled, steady, perpetually chalked with the talc she uses to ease on examination gloves. Her hair is grown long and gathered in elaborate wrapping cloths she changes daily, a small vanity she insists upon. Bioluminescent threads have been tattooed along her collarbone in a pattern that pulses softly blue when her heart rate rises — a gift from a grateful patient who was a tattooist, and which Ogechi considers mildly embarrassing but cannot bring herself to remove.

She is the gravitational center of three city blocks. Women come to her in the small hours, sometimes alone, sometimes holding each other up. Ogechi never turns anyone away, works on a sliding scale that regularly bottoms out at zero, and maintains a mental ledger of every birth she has attended — over nine hundred. She has strong opinions about Helix Biosystems, none of them polite, and a practical theology around the E.L.F. she calls Thresholder, whom she believes watches over liminal moments: birth, death, the crossing between states. She leaves small data-offerings on a cracked tablet beside her examination table.
Properties.role: Street midwife and unlicensed obstetric care provider
Properties.location: The Shelf, Meridian 88 — operates from a converted laundry unit at Burnside Pocket
Properties.narrative_function: Community anchor and information node; knows the intimate secrets of hundreds of Shelf families. Quest giver for anything involving missing mothers or children. Moral voice who challenges players' ethical shortcuts.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent pulse tattoo along collarbone (cosmetic, involuntary — gifted). Subdermal haptic pads on fingertips for enhanced tactile diagnostics — older model, partially degraded.
Properties.core_fears: Watching someone die because she lacked the right equipment; Becoming irrelevant or unable to practice
Properties.core_desires: For every child born on the Shelf to survive their first year; To be remembered as someone who showed up
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — precise, repeated actions before and after deliveries; Displacement into work whenever grief threatens to surface
Properties.blind_spots: Refuses to acknowledge her own physical deterioration and what it means for her patients; Believes she can assess risk accurately when she is emotionally involved with a patient
Properties.secret: She lost a patient and infant twelve years ago to a complication she might have caught earlier if she hadn't been exhausted from a triple shift. She told the family it was unpreventable. She has never told anyone the truth.
Properties.story_hooks: A birth she attended six months ago is now being investigated by Helix Biosystems — they claim the infant carries proprietary gene markers and constitutes Helix IP. Ogechi is refusing to cooperate and needs someone to make the investigators go away.; One of her regular patients has stopped coming to appointments and isn't responding to messages. Her neighbors say they haven't seen her in two weeks.
Properties.affiliation: Independent — loosely networked with Burnside Pocket community health cooperative
Properties.vocabulary: Warm and vernacular, mixes Igbo endearments with Tongan rhythmic phrases, medical terminology deployed precisely when needed and then immediately softened
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, like she's deciding each word has earned its place — accelerates only when directing emergency action
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Come now. The body knows what it's doing. You just need to stop arguing with it.' | 'I've seen nine hundred and forty-three beginnings. This one is not going to be the one that breaks me. Not tonight.'

Properties.description:
Ọgụ is a man who looks like he was carved from the same material as the tunnels — his skin is the brown-grey of old concrete, deeply lined, and perpetually damp at the temples from the humidity of Bellows Town. He is larger than you'd expect someone who has spent decades in low-clearance tunnels to be: broad across the shoulders, thick-necked, with hands so calloused they look armored. One leg was crushed in a pressure-seal failure forty years ago and never properly repaired; he walks with a rocking gait and a carved ferroceramic cane he calls his Third Opinion. His eyes are undmodified and dark brown, and his gaze carries the particular weight of someone who has outlived many people he loved and is not surprised by anything anymore.

He is the closest thing Bellows Town has to a leader, though he would reject the title. He mediates disputes between pipe-folk clans, arbitrates resource-sharing on food and water taps, and is the living archive of Deepwell Station's last sixty years — collapses, floods, disappearances, treaties between tunnel communities. He is warm in the way of someone who has no energy left for performance; he will feed a stranger without asking questions and he will also tell that stranger an uncomfortable truth without softening it.
Properties.role: Elder pipe-folk patriarch and keeper of oral tunnel history
Properties.location: Deepwell Station, the sprawling pipe-folk encampment called Bellows Town
Properties.narrative_function: Lore source for tunnel history and underworld geography; faction mediator; can grant or withhold access to pipe-folk resources and knowledge; his approval is social currency in the deep levels
Properties.augmentations: None — he is philosophically opposed to augmentation, viewing it as a surface-world dependency that creates vulnerabilities underground; his cane is the only technology he trusts
Properties.core_fears: Bellows Town being discovered and evicted by Ferrogate Transit or another corponation; Dying before he has passed his oral histories on
Properties.core_desires: The pipe-folk communities to achieve some form of recognized territorial claim to their tunnels; To be remembered accurately, not mythologized
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Turns grief into story — every loss becomes a lesson he narrates to the young; Physical labor as meditation; he repairs pipes and fittings himself even when it hurts
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much the younger pipe-folk want surface contact and surface things; His hatred of augmentation means he sometimes dismisses people with mods as 'surface-contaminated'
Properties.secret: Ọgụ was born on the surface — Calumet Rise, tier 2 family — and chose to disappear underground at age 22 after informing on a neighbor to a Ferrogate Transit security division. The neighbor was evicted and died. He has never told anyone in Bellows Town he was once a surface person.
Properties.story_hooks: He possesses oral knowledge of a tunnel route to a pre-city infrastructure vault that he refuses to share until he judges someone trustworthy — the process of earning that trust is itself a small quest; Someone has been quietly recording his stories and selling transcripts to a Sterling-Nakamura heritage data broker — Ọgụ knows it's happening but not who
Properties.affiliation: Bellows Town pipe-folk community; elder neutral party among Undertow clans
Properties.vocabulary: Slow and deliberate; mixes pipe-folk technical terms with formal, almost ceremonial phrasing; quotes tunnel sayings like proverbs
Properties.cadence: Unhurried to the point of seeming to move in a different time — he pauses between sentences, not between thoughts
Properties.example_dialogue: Now here's a thing — she was flooding in that section thirty years before the Transit maps even showed it existed. | The young ones want to know where to go. The wise ones want to know why it matters.

Properties.description:
Okonkwo is a heavyset man with dark brown skin, a shaved head tattooed with a fine-line circuit diagram that was his journeyman qualification piece when he trained as a licensed aug technician — before the license was suspended. His hands are his most augmented feature: titanium-reinforced fingers with retractable micro-tools in the right hand and haptic sensitivity amplifiers in the left, built over seven years of incremental self-installation. He wears a mechanic's apron over a clean undershirt and moves through his workshop with the unhurried competence of someone who has done every motion a thousand times.

His shop is a converted machine bay off a side alley in Geartown, marked only by a small blue LED fixture above the door that locals know means open. He does aug maintenance, black-market installations, and sells a curated line of pharmaceutical compounds — mostly pain management, anti-rejection meds, and neural stabilizers — that people need to keep their augmentations functional without going through Helix Biosystems' official pricing. He is careful, technically meticulous, and genuinely skilled. He is also operating entirely outside corporate medical licensing, which means everything he does is illegal and every satisfied customer is a liability.
Properties.role: Unlicensed augmentation shop owner and street pharmacist, Geartown
Properties.location: Geartown, Harrowgate Industrial Plateau
Properties.narrative_function: Medical resource and augmentation services for characters who can't afford or access official Helix Biosystems care. Can install, repair, or diagnose augmentations. Pharmaceutical supplier. Carries moral weight — his work is illegal but often the only option for Tier 1-2 people.
Properties.augmentations: Titanium-reinforced fingers (both hands). Retractable micro-tool array in right hand (scalpel, probe, torque driver, micro-welder). Haptic sensitivity amplification in left hand. Anti-tremor stabilizers in both wrists. Subretinal work-light in left eye.
Properties.core_fears: Killing someone on the table because his equipment wasn't good enough; Being raided and watching his patients lose access to care they depend on
Properties.core_desires: To practice medicine without the corporate licensing system gatekeeping who deserves care; To pay off the protection debt and operate without owing anyone anything
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Rigorous procedural discipline — following his own protocols exactly as a way of managing anxiety; Rebuilding broken equipment by hand as a form of meditation; Maintaining a patient log he calls 'the book' to remind himself of every successful outcome
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much his protection arrangement compromises his neutrality; His hatred of the licensing system sometimes makes him take on cases beyond his actual capability out of principle
Properties.secret: Eight months ago he lost a patient — a complication from an installation he was technically qualified to do but had no business doing alone without a second pair of hands. He buried it, falsified nothing, simply absorbed the fact that it happened. The patient's family does not know. He thinks about it every day.
Properties.story_hooks: The Copperhead protection collective is asking him to start skimming patient pharmaceutical supplies as payment-in-kind on top of his regular protection fee. He is looking for a way out of the arrangement before it costs him his ethics entirely.; A patient came in with augmentation damage that could only have been caused by a specific corporate enforcement tool — something he recognizes from technical documents he shouldn't have access to. He doesn't want to get involved but he can't stop thinking about what it implies.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal mutual aid network with other unlicensed aug techs in Geartown; unwilling debt relationship with the Copperhead local protection collective
Properties.vocabulary: Technical medical and engineering terminology mixed with direct, plain language. Igbo-Uzbek-Spanish rhythms give his sentences a particular meter — slightly formal, never flowery.
Properties.cadence: Measured and deliberate when working or discussing medical matters. Shorter and more guarded about personal topics.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The Helix price for what I just did is four hundred Quanta. I charged you sixty and I used better anti-rejection compound than they stock at their Tier-2 clinics. Think about what that means.' | 'I don't do installations without a full diagnostic first. That's not a negotiation.'

Properties.description:
Okonkwo is enormous — 1.95 meters, broad as a doorframe, with deep black skin and a bald head that he keeps oiled and that catches the neon from the Kessler Interchange in amber and violet. He has a full white beard that he keeps very neat, heavy-lidded eyes that make him look sleepy until you watch them move, and a pair of retractable claw mods on his right hand that he got in his thirties for reasons he no longer fully remembers and now uses primarily for scoring citrus peel. He runs his cart from a converted cargo drone chassis that he's modified over fifteen years into something almost architectural — woks, broth vats, a bank of mismatched stools, two heat lamps, and a shrine to the local transit-E.L.F. built from signal-mirror fragments and a perpetually running old transit ticker.

Okonkwo is the kind of person who becomes a landmark. He has been in the same spot under the Kessler Interchange for twenty-two years and intends to die there. He feeds people on credit without comment and remembers what you ordered three years ago. He is fundamentally, stubbornly gentle — a big man who chose softness as a deliberate political act after a youth in which he was not soft at all. He sings to himself while he cooks, always the same four songs in rotation, and accepts requests but never honors them.
Properties.role: Noodle cart vendor
Properties.location: Grand Corridor, beneath the Kessler Interchange overpass — Konk's Cart
Properties.narrative_function: Neighborhood institution and gathering point; oral historian of Grand Corridor; quiet provider of social safety net; can introduce characters to each other organically.
Properties.augmentations: Retractable claw mods on right hand (old, well-worn). No other augmentations — he claims his body is already as modified as it needs to be by sixty years of cooking.
Properties.core_fears: that the gentleness he built was always just exhaustion wearing a better coat; the cart being seized or the location being cleared by a Ferrogate Transit redevelopment order
Properties.core_desires: to have fed enough people that it matters in some aggregate way he can't measure; for someone to carry the cart forward after him
Properties.coping_mechanisms: cooking as meditation and control; deliberate community-building as atonement
Properties.blind_spots: his history in the labor movement has given him a template for reading situations politically that sometimes fits and sometimes catastrophically doesn't
Properties.secret: In his thirties he was involved in a labor action that turned violent — not his hand, but his planning. Someone died. He walked away from the movement, moved to Grand Corridor, and built the cart as a form of penance he has never named aloud. One of the people who was there is now a senior Ferrogate Transit administrator.
Properties.story_hooks: The Ferrogate Transit administrator who shares Okonkwo's secret appears at the cart one evening — not to threaten him, apparently just to eat, but Okonkwo doesn't believe in coincidences.; A young person has started sleeping under the cart's awning at night, and Okonkwo has been letting it happen; they haven't spoken yet, but they left an origami figure on one of his stools — same folding technique as a protest art tradition from the old labor movement.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal affiliation with the Grand Corridor vendor collective; old ties to a labor action group he no longer names
Properties.vocabulary: Deliberate, warm, a deep voice that carries without effort; Igbo-Portuguese cadences from his parents' household; quotes things — food writers, E.L.F. liturgy, a song lyric — without citing sources
Properties.cadence: Slow and measured, with long thoughtful pauses that never feel awkward because his presence fills them
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Eat first. Then we can talk about whatever it is that's making your shoulders do that.' | 'I've been here twenty-two years. The city has tried to move me four times. The broth is still on.'

Properties.description:
Oksana is compact and precise-looking, with light ochre skin, narrow-set dark eyes, and a body that is itself their most elaborate portfolio piece: bioluminescent freckle-constellations across their shoulders and throat, color-shifting scale-pattern geneware covering both forearms from wrist to elbow in teal and copper, and cat ears — small, dark-furred, fully expressive — perched on their head as their most remarked-upon feature, though they consider it their most boring one. Their hands are almost uncannily steady. They speak softly and move with the deliberate economy of someone who works in millimeters.

Their specialty is integrating traditional tattoo and scarification methods with geneware modification — they design pieces that are part pigment, part living tissue, partly responsive to the wearer's own biochemistry so that the work changes with the body over years. They are particularly sought out for memorial work, pieces made to commemorate lost people or mark major transitions, and they have developed a reputation for drawing out a client's full story before ever picking up a tool. They are not cheap, they have a two-month waiting list, and they do not take clients whose reasons they distrust. They are also, quietly, one of the most technically skilled unlicensed geneware applicators in The Garret.
Properties.role: Gene-mod body artist and tattoo artist
Properties.location: The Garret, studio called Secondskin above a noodle bar on the Edgewater Prism level
Properties.narrative_function: Information nexus — clients talk during long sessions and Oksana listens; they know secrets from every tier of The Garret's social world; also a practical resource for characters needing cosmetic cover work, unlicensed geneware application, or access to Helix grey-market medical supplies
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent freckle-constellations (cosmetic geneware); color-shifting scale-pattern geneware on both forearms; geneware cat ears (fully expressive); sub-dermal hand stabilizers (occupational implants for precision work)
Properties.core_fears: Losing the steadiness in their hands — to age, damage, or neural drift; Being truly known by someone who then leaves anyway
Properties.core_desires: To make work that outlasts both the artist and the client; A relationship where they do not have to perform calm
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Extreme professional ritual — the precise setup of tools, the intake consultation — as a way of controlling anxiety; Deflection through attentive listening: keeping focus entirely on the other person
Properties.blind_spots: Their reputation for emotional availability in the studio does not translate to personal relationships, and they cannot see the gap; They screen clients for worthiness but apply no such rigor to people they let into their personal life
Properties.secret: They have been slowly, over five years, tattooing a complete map of Meridian 88's grey-market medical supply network onto the inner surfaces of a set of custom jacket panels — encoded in a pattern that reads as abstract art. They intend it as insurance. They have not decided against whom.
Properties.story_hooks: A client died three days after a session, and the death is being called natural causes, but Oksana noticed something in the client's tissue during the work that suggested it wasn't — and now they are trying to decide whether being right is worth the danger of saying so; Someone is counterfeiting their work — applying crude imitations of their distinctive integration technique under their name — and the fake pieces are failing biologically, causing the wearers harm
Properties.affiliation: Independent (Secondskin studio); loose professional relationship with Helix Biosystems grey-market suppliers
Properties.vocabulary: Professional and warm in the studio, measured and slightly formal outside it; uses the body as metaphor naturally ('what does that feel like, structurally?')
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, with deliberate pauses that invite the other person to fill them — a practised interviewer's rhythm
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The piece will grow with you. In ten years it'll tell a story neither of us can read yet.' | 'I don't ask why someone wants what they want. I ask what they need to feel when they see it.'

Properties.description:
Olabisi is a big man going soft at the middle in the way of someone who was once physically imposing and no longer cares to maintain it. His skin is a deep umber, his head shaved close except for a strip of silver-threaded locs he keeps pulled back. His eyes carry patterned irises — a Helix Biosystems cosmetic mod from his Tier 3 days, concentric rings of gold and charcoal — that he chose to keep even after the money ran out, because he thinks they make him look like a prophet and he finds this privately amusing. His hands are enormous and dexterous, always moving, tapping rhythms on whatever surface is near.

He is warm in the manner of a man who has made peace with most of his disappointments, which makes him either genuinely wise or dangerously comfortable depending on who you ask. He builds sound sculptures — physical installations of salvaged materials that produce music when air, heat, or electrical current moves through them — and he DJs the late sets at Slag three nights a week, mixing generative compositions with field recordings he collects obsessively from across the city. He is the unofficial historian of the Ferment Quarter's sound scene, having watched it transform from genuine underground to semi-curated Palladian 'authenticity experience' with the sad clarity of someone who remembers the original thing.
Properties.role: sound sculptor and DJ, Ferment Quarter fixture
Properties.location: The Ferment Quarter — permanent residency at the venue called 'Slag'
Properties.narrative_function: Information source and community anchor — he has heard everything that has happened in the Ferment Quarter for fifteen years; quest giver for lost art, missing persons, venue-related trouble; moral compass character who asks uncomfortable questions gently.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises (gold/charcoal concentric rings, Helix Biosystems cosmetic). Sub-dermal vibration sensors in his palms — allows him to feel sound frequencies physically, purchased secondhand and imperfectly calibrated.
Properties.core_fears: that the scene he loves is already dead and he's just playing in the corpse; that he took the Palladian money because he was tired, not because it was right
Properties.core_desires: one perfect sound — something completely unrepeatable that he captured; to see one of his protégés make something he couldn't have imagined
Properties.coping_mechanisms: deflects emotional confrontation with humor and generosity; compulsive field recording — collecting the city's sounds feels like archiving something precious
Properties.blind_spots: has convinced himself he can take corporate money without being shaped by it; enables younger artists' self-destruction by being too understanding
Properties.secret: He has been secretly recording every conversation in Slag for eight years — not for surveillance, but because he believes the Quarter's social fabric is an art form that deserves to be archived. He has 8,000 hours of other people's lives stored on an encrypted drive he's never shared with anyone.
Properties.story_hooks: His archive of 8,000 hours of Slag recordings contains something he doesn't know is there — a conversation that implicates someone powerful in something serious.; A sound sculpture he installed outside Slag three years ago has started producing a frequency that wasn't in its design — something is broadcasting through it, and he's starting to think it might be an E.L.F. trying to communicate.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal mentor to dozens of younger artists; Palladian Corporation pays him a venue subsidy he rationalizes constantly
Properties.vocabulary: Rich and unhurried — mixes Yoruba proverbs (slightly misremembered), Bosnian expressions from his grandfather's side, and the dense technical vocabulary of acoustic engineering.
Properties.cadence: Slow, deliberate, with long pauses that feel comfortable rather than awkward. Never rushes.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Palladian wants to sell the Quarter's soul back to people who can afford it. I am aware. I am also aware that the lights need to stay on.' | 'The city makes a sound when it's afraid. I've been recording it for years. It's getting louder.'

Nodes.Name: The Ferment Quarter — permanent residency at the venue called 'Slag'

Properties.description:
Olamide is a broad-shouldered woman with dark amber skin mapped in old burn scars along her left forearm — souvenirs from a grease fire twenty years back that she wears without shame. Her hair is a natural silver-streaked corona she keeps pinned under a bright saffron headwrap during service, and she has cosmetic patterned irises done in deep indigo whorls that she got when her youngest turned ten, as a treat to herself. Her stall is a masterpiece of organized chaos: three burners, a recycled heat-drum, seventeen unlabeled spice jars arranged in an order only she understands, and a hand-painted sign reading SWEETMOUTH in three scripts. She moves behind the counter with the unhurried authority of someone who has never once doubted she belongs exactly where she is.

She is relentlessly sociable in the way of someone who has learned that warmth is a survival tool and then genuinely come to love it. She remembers every regular's order and their children's names and their mother's health complaints. She is also unflinching when she needs to be — she has run the same stall through two gang territory disputes and one Ferrogate Transit labor riot, serving both sides without commentary. She prays to the E.L.F. she calls Saltmother, a market-spirit she believes governs honest commerce, and leaves data-offerings of her daily transaction logs at a small shrine wired into her heat-drum.
Properties.role: Street food stall operator — spiced protein wraps, synthetic broth, black-market spice blends
Properties.location: The Oxidian Market, Geartown
Properties.narrative_function: Local color, information hub — she knows everyone in Geartown who eats, which is everyone. Quest giver for small community concerns. Can source unusual ingredients through suspect channels if players earn her trust.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned indigo irises (cosmetic). Basic subdermal heat-resistance in left hand from a cheap clinic after the grease fire — functional, not fancy.
Properties.core_fears: Her stall being seized or destroyed by corponation rezoning; Outliving her usefulness to the community she has built
Properties.core_desires: To be the axis around which her neighborhood turns — needed, fed, known; To eventually buy the stall's ground lease outright so no one can move her
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cooking as meditation — complex recipes crowd out anxious thoughts; Joking through discomfort until the moment passes
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much people exploit her generosity deliberately; Believes her neutrality in disputes protects her — it only delays the cost
Properties.secret: She has been quietly funneling a portion of her earnings into a fund for three families in Geartown who lost housing in the last rezoning sweep. She tells no one because she cannot afford to be seen as a resource to be tapped — she is already spread thin.
Properties.story_hooks: A corponation land-grab survey crew has been spotted measuring in the Oxidian Market — Olamide needs someone to find out who commissioned them before the vendors guild meets in three days; One of her regulars, a Ferrogate Transit maintenance worker, stopped coming to the stall two weeks ago. She is quietly, seriously worried and will pay in meals and information to know why.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; Oxidian Market Vendors Guild (dues-paying member, disputes committee)
Properties.vocabulary: Rich, warm, full of food metaphors and proverbs. Mixes Yoruba-inflected phrasing with clipped Polish consonants when stressed. Calls everyone 'dear heart' until they disappoint her.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, rhythmic. Talks while working — sentences punctuated by ladle sounds, sizzle.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You look like you haven't eaten since Tuesday, dear heart. Sit down. I'm not asking.' | 'I don't know anything about that business — but I know a man who eats here Tuesdays who might. Come back Tuesday. Eat something first.'

Properties.description:
Oleander is a tall, soft-faced fourteen-year-old with his father's Ukrainian pallor cut through with his grandfather's Ghanaian bone structure, resulting in something that looks like a sculptor started with two different models and found the intersection interesting. His geneware is modest — his parents approved a bioluminescent vein treatment in pale gold that shows at his temples and wrists when he's excited or stressed, something he deeply regrets as it is essentially a visible anxiety indicator. He keeps his school uniform impeccably pressed to compensate.

He is enrolled at Axiom Meridian Youth Prep on a partial academic scholarship, meaning his family stretches Tier 3 income to cover the gap. He is genuinely brilliant at systems architecture and has parlayed that into a small private operation: for a fee, he fixes other students' academic scores, not by hacking the official records (too dangerous) but by finding the legitimate alternate-submission loopholes buried in the campus governance code that no one else reads. He calls this 'procedural advocacy.' He is aware this is thin moral ice and he keeps skating.
Properties.role: corporate school student and junior hacker, Tier 3
Properties.location: Engelheim, Axiom Meridian Youth Preparatory Campus
Properties.narrative_function: Information broker within the corporate school ecosystem; can provide access to Axiom campus systems or student social networks; represents the pressure-cooker of Tier 3 families buying into corporate education pipelines; his operation could explode in multiple interesting directions
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent vein treatment (gold, temple and wrists); basic neural study-assist implant standard-issued by Axiom to scholarship students (read/recall enhancement, cannot be removed without forfeiting enrollment status)
Properties.core_fears: losing the scholarship and proving his family's sacrifice was wasted; being caught and labeled a cheater rather than a clever person
Properties.core_desires: to be recognized as legitimately brilliant without having to explain the legitimate part; to get into Axiom's advanced systems track on pure merit
Properties.coping_mechanisms: rationalization through legal framing — 'I only use what the rules allow'; meticulous documentation of everything
Properties.blind_spots: Genuinely cannot see that the clients who rely on him are becoming dependent in ways that will eventually make him complicit in their failures
Properties.secret: Six months ago he found a genuine security vulnerability in the campus assessment system — a real one, not a loophole — and didn't report it. He uses it as a last resort and has used it exactly once, for himself, to correct a score he earned but that was logged incorrectly due to a teacher's error. He tells himself that last part matters.
Properties.story_hooks: A client's parent has found out and is threatening to report Oleander unless he provides something much larger — access he doesn't have and would have to steal honestly; The unreported vulnerability has been found by someone else and they know he knew — they want a partner or they want him silent
Properties.affiliation: Axiom Meridian Youth Preparatory (student); informal peer-network of paying clients
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, clause-heavy, uses legal and procedural language casually; shifts to clipped teen slang around peers he's trying to impress
Properties.cadence: Measured, slightly too slow for his age, like he's reading from internal notes
Properties.example_dialogue: Technically speaking, Subsection 14-C of the Axiom Academic Remediation Policy permits supplementary submission within the same assessment cycle. I'm just helping you find the form. | I don't hack anything. I read everything. There's a difference and it matters.

Properties.description:
Olekan Mbeki-Sigurðsson is ninety-one years old and looks eighty and moves like sixty-five, which he attributes to the military-grade bone lacing he received at twenty-two and the stubbornness he received at birth. He is lean and upright, dark-skinned, with a head shaved smooth that he keeps polished, and a face that has resolved from handsome into something more interesting — all strong lines and earned geography. His left hand trembles slightly, a nerve issue from a combat incident in 2153 that was never fully repaired. The rest of him does not tremble. He wears his old Palladian insignia on a chain around his neck, not out of loyalty to the corporation — he will explain in detail why that would be idiotic — but because he cannot separate it from the men and women who wore it beside him.

He is the oldest resident at Aldgate and has outlived three care coordinators and four attempts to move him to a higher-dependency facility. He plays tessera chess with anyone who will sit across from him and loses on purpose to interesting opponents to get a longer game. He is not warm exactly, but he is fair, and in a place that has often not been fair to him, this has made him a figure of quiet authority among the other residents. He will not discuss his actual combat experiences unless he trusts you completely. He will talk about his fellow soldiers constantly.
Properties.role: Retired Corporate Wars soldier (former Palladian contract infantry), pension-dependent resident
Properties.location: Montclare Quiet, Room 7, the Aldgate Assisted Living Node
Properties.narrative_function: Living Corporate Wars history, moral weight, pension system vulnerability illustrator; can provide ground-level military history from Palladian's perspective; the letters he writes are a possible information source
Properties.augmentations: Military-grade bone lacing (Palladian combat standard, 2153); subdermal combat trauma monitor (defunct, hardware failure, now inert); cochlear implants (both ears, military-grade, still functional)
Properties.core_fears: dying as a number in a Palladian pension ledger rather than as a person; forgetting the faces — he has nightmares about forgetting them one by one
Properties.core_desires: that the people he served with be remembered as individuals, not statistics; one honest conversation with someone who actually wants to know what it was
Properties.coping_mechanisms: rigid routine as a structure that holds him together; the chess games as a form of controlled social contact; writing the letters — he has been writing them for forty years, some to the dead
Properties.blind_spots: idealizes unit cohesion to the point where he minimizes harm done within it; profound difficulty asking for help with anything he reads as weakness
Properties.secret: He has been writing a full account of the Avon Curve incident — a battle in 2155 in which a Palladian officer ordered his unit to fire on civilians who were sheltering in a transit hub, claiming they were armed combatants. He was there. He followed the order. He has spent sixty-eight years deciding whether to send the account to anyone, and it is now three hundred and forty pages long on a physical typewriter ribbon he keeps under his mattress.
Properties.story_hooks: Palladian's legal department has sent a representative to Aldgate requesting access to veterans' personal records as part of a 'benefits review' — Olekan is certain they are looking for surviving witnesses to the Avon Curve incident; A young journalist has found fragmentary references to the Avon Curve in declassified military logs and has tracked down Olekan as the last living witness they can identify; His pension has been frozen pending a disputed identity verification — an administrative error that could take months to resolve, leaving him dependent on Aldgate's discretionary fund
Properties.affiliation: Palladian Veterans Network (PVN); Aldgate Assisted Living Node resident; independent
Properties.vocabulary: spare and exact; Ukrainian-Norwegian inflections from his parents; military habits of language — precise times, cardinal directions, last names for people he respects; first names for people he loves
Properties.cadence: slow and measured, with long silences he is entirely comfortable in
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Kowalski makes this move when she's nervous. Kowalski has been dead thirty years and she still makes this move. Sit down. I'll show you.' | 'I followed the order. I want you to understand that I know exactly what that means. I have had sixty-eight years to understand it.'

Properties.description:
Ọlọruntóbi is a man who was built for louder rooms than the one he currently occupies. He is tall and loose-limbed, with the kind of face that was clearly handsome and has aged into something more interesting — deep sienna complexion, heavy brow, a jaw that still juts when he is angry. He has cosmetic tiger-stripe bioluminescence on his arms and collarbone, a geneware mod he got in his forties to celebrate the Union's successful Ferrogate walkout of 2172, and which now glows a gentle amber when the building's lights go down. His natural hair has gone grey-silver and he wears it in short locs. A subvocal transceiver is implanted at his throat — old union infrastructure, technically still active.

For sixteen years Tobi was the loudest, most tenacious shop steward and eventually regional director the Ferrogate Transit Workers Union ever produced. He won three collective agreements, survived two corporate union-busting campaigns, and was personally blacklisted by two Ferrogate senior executives. Then his daughter Comfort died of an untreated pulmonary infection in 2194 — a death he attributes directly to Helix Biosystems' pharmaceutical pricing, which the union had been fighting for years — and left behind two children aged four and seven. Tobi took them without a moment's hesitation and quietly stopped being the man who changed things, because he was suddenly the man who made breakfast.
Properties.role: Former union leader (Ferrogate Transit Workers Union), now raising two grandchildren on a reduced pension
Properties.location: The Shelf, Block 14 — a three-room unit he shares with his grandchildren
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver for labor and corporate accountability storylines; access point to Ferrogate Transit insider knowledge and union network; emotionally complex figure whose activism is dormant but not dead; the grandchildren can be a vulnerability or a source of motivation
Properties.augmentations: Tiger-stripe bioluminescent geneware (arms and collarbone, amber-gold) — cosmetic, personal significance; subvocal transceiver (throat implant, FTW Union network standard issue — technically still connected)
Properties.core_fears: failing the grandchildren the way he failed to save their mother; that his years of union work genuinely changed nothing permanent
Properties.core_desires: to see Helix Biosystems face real consequences for pharmaceutical pricing; to give Dami and Kofi-Ren a better tier than he could achieve
Properties.coping_mechanisms: busyness — he does not sit still; gallows humor about corporate power; telling the grandchildren edited stories about their mother that emphasize her strength
Properties.blind_spots: his grief has calcified into a very specific political target — he struggles to address grief in any other form; does not see how much Kofi-Ren is watching and internalizing his anger
Properties.secret: He knows who the Ferrogate executive was who personally ordered the data purge that destroyed evidence of the pharmaceutical partnership he was building a case against. The executive is retired, living comfortably in Grosse Pointe Enclosure. Tobi has the executive's home address and has had it for three years. He has done nothing.
Properties.story_hooks: Kofi-Ren has been approached by someone recruiting young people for direct action against Helix Biosystems — Tobi has found evidence of this and is terrified, not because he disagrees with the cause but because he knows exactly how it ends; A younger union organizer has uncovered the same pharmaceutical partnership evidence Tobi once had, and has come to him for guidance — reigniting everything he put away
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit Workers Union (retired regional director, still listed as emeritus); The Shelf Block 14 informal community network
Properties.vocabulary: Union oratory mixed with Block 14 street vernacular; code-switches fluidly based on audience; drops into formal rhetoric when emotional
Properties.cadence: Naturally rhetorical — builds to emphasis, uses repetition for effect; softens completely around the grandchildren
Properties.example_dialogue: 'They don't win because they're stronger. They win because we keep being surprised that they'll actually do it. Stop being surprised. Then we can talk about winning.' | 'Dami, eat. Kofi-Ren, I can see you. Eat your food and then you can show me your rig work, yes.'

Properties.description:
Oluwadarasimi — Dara to everyone who values their time — is a compact, watchful woman who runs what appears to be a phone repair and device maintenance kiosk in the middle of the Alban Souk's electronics corridor. The repair work is real; so is everything else. Her skin is a deep warm brown, her natural hair twisted into locks threaded with silver wire that serve a dual purpose as aesthetic and antenna extension. Her irises are stock human dark brown, which she considers a professional advantage. She has cat ears — a geneware mod she got in her twenties and has kept ever since, velvety black and mobile, swiveling toward sounds before she's consciously registered them. She is acutely, perpetually embarrassed by how readable her ears make her emotional state and has developed elaborate conversational techniques for preventing anyone from noticing what direction they've turned.

Dara operates on the fundamental principle that information depreciates in value like produce: sell it while it's fresh or it's worthless. She deals strictly in neighborhood-scale data — who owes whom, who's sleeping where they shouldn't be, what the Chatham Flats block captain actually filed versus what they told residents, which E.L.F. shrine has gone cold and why. She does not touch corponation intel, does not touch political data, and has turned down three increasingly good offers to work for Tessera's intelligence division. She is precise, reliable, and slightly sad in a way she would vigorously deny.
Properties.role: Small-time data broker — neighborhood gossip, surveillance logs, identity fragments
Properties.location: The Alban Souk, Chatham Flats
Properties.narrative_function: Information source for neighborhood-scale intelligence; can connect players to other vendors or local power brokers; her data-cache may contain something relevant to whatever's happening; demonstrates the texture of surveillance from below.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat ears (black, fully mobile, emotionally responsive — she hates this). Subdermal data-cache implant along left forearm, finger-press activated. Silver wire threaded through locks functions as passive signal antenna.
Properties.core_fears: Being exposed — having her own information turned against her; That she has made herself so careful she has made herself alone
Properties.core_desires: To understand what is actually happening in the city, not just her block; To be trusted by someone who deserves her trust
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Maintaining professional detachment as an identity rather than a tool; Knowing things as a substitute for controlling them; Routine as armor
Properties.blind_spots: Mistakes knowing about something for being safe from it; Her cat ears betray genuine emotional responses she has analytically convinced herself she doesn't have
Properties.secret: Dara has a daughter, eight years old, being raised by Dara's older sister in Mexicantown Libre. Dara funds them entirely and visits twice a month by a deliberately circuitous route. No one in Chatham Flats knows the child exists. The father was a Ringo mid-level enforcer who Dara got too close to while gathering information and she has never forgiven herself for the lapse in either professional or personal judgment. She keeps a photo in her data-cache between encrypted files — the only unencrypted thing she owns.
Properties.story_hooks: Dara accidentally captured something in her passive antenna logs she wasn't looking for — a fragment of a Ferrogate Transit internal broadcast — and someone has noticed her kiosk's antenna configuration.; Her daughter's neighborhood in Mexicantown Libre is facing a threat Dara heard about through her network before anyone there did; she needs someone to act on information she can't be seen acting on herself.; A client has gone missing within 48 hours of buying information from her, and this has happened twice now. Either her operation is compromised or the information itself is lethal.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal affiliate of The Oxidian Market Vendors Guild (associate member despite being in Chatham Flats); pays dues to no one else
Properties.vocabulary: Economical and precise; Swedish grandmother's influence in clipped sentence construction; Yoruba for counting, timing, and anything emotional she doesn't want to sound emotional about
Properties.cadence: Measured and unhurried; never finishes a sentence she hasn't decided on before starting it
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Apparently the block captain filed a noise complaint on the Souk's east vendors last Tuesday. The work suggests this has nothing to do with noise.' | 'That information is Φ60. It was Φ45 yesterday. It will be worthless tomorrow. You decide.' | 'I fix the phone. What you do with a functional phone is not my concern. What you do with what is on the phone — that is a different conversation with different pricing.'
