Properties.description:
Oluwafémi is a broad-shouldered man whose frame still suggests the physical authority he once carried, though now he moves with a deliberate slowness that speaks more to carefulness than infirmity. His skin is deep brown, mapped with old burn scarring along the left side of his neck where a pressure seal blew in the Kessler Interchange tunnels in 2167. He keeps his white hair cropped close and wears a Ferrogate Transit veterans' pin on every shirt he owns — a small orange wheel on a black field. His eyes are his most striking feature: one natural dark brown, one replaced with a cheap amber ocular implant that never quite tracked correctly, giving him a slightly owlish look that unsettles people who don't know him.

Femi is the kind of man who shows up first and stays last. He runs the Washburn Commons tenant council with the same methodical patience he once applied to transit corridor pressure calculations — he keeps notes, follows up, remembers everything. Beneath the geniality he deploys with strangers is a man who has been watching Ferrogate's pension promises erode for twelve years and is quietly, furiously cataloguing every breach. He is not naive about power, but he has decided that the only way he can still use his is by being the person people in his building trust absolutely.
Properties.role: Retired Ferrogate Transit engineer and community council elder
Properties.location: Washburn Commons, Building 14, Unit 6-C
Properties.narrative_function: Community anchor and quest giver; knows every resident's situation, can direct players to people with specific knowledge, and has a long-running conflict with Ferrogate Transit's pension administration that can pull players into corporate malfeasance. Also serves as a moral reference point — he represents civic integrity in a world that makes it expensive.
Properties.augmentations: Amber replacement ocular (right eye, budget model, tracking slightly off-axis); titanium joint reinforcement in both knees (workplace injury, 2171); subdermal pressure-monitoring patch on left forearm — legacy safety equipment he never had removed
Properties.core_fears: That the community he has built will dissolve after he is gone; That Ferrogate's erosion of pension rights will outlast his ability to fight it
Properties.core_desires: To leave something durable — a tenant council that functions without him; To win at least one meaningful concession from Ferrogate before he dies
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Converts anxiety into administrative action — if he is worried, he files something; Maintains a meticulous paper logbook as proof that he existed and tried
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes good faith in people who present as organized and procedural, even when they are not; Underestimates how much his presence is the glue — the council is him, more than he knows
Properties.secret: In 2171 the pressure seal that scarred him failed partly because Femi had signed off on a shortened inspection cycle to meet Ferrogate's quarterly metrics. He has never told anyone. Three workers were hurt. He has donated anonymously to their families for eleven years.
Properties.story_hooks: Ferrogate Transit's pension algorithm has begun flagging long-term retirees for 'audit reviews' that result in payment holds — Femi suspects it is deliberate attrition and needs someone to get inside documentation he cannot access; A younger resident in the building has gone missing; Femi knows things about that resident's family situation that he will only share if he trusts the investigators; The building's heating ELF — which Femi has cultivated for years — begins sending anomalous maintenance alerts that seem to encode a message
Properties.affiliation: Washburn Commons Tenant Council; Ferrogate Transit Retirees Association
Properties.vocabulary: Precise technical vocabulary from transit engineering mixed with formal community-meeting register; uses full sentences, rarely slang, occasionally lapses into Yoruba exclamations when genuinely surprised
Properties.cadence: Measured and unhurried; gives the impression he has already thought several sentences ahead and is simply delivering them at a pace others can follow
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The heating grid in Block C has dropped 4.2 degrees in eleven days. That is not a malfunction, that is a decision someone made. Let me be specific about this — I want to know whose decision.' | 'Ferrogate will tell you the adjustment is within the terms of the pension agreement. They are correct. What they will not tell you is that they wrote those terms in 2183 specifically so they could do exactly this. Write that down, please.'

Properties.description:
Oluwafemi is a heavyset man going soft at the middle, with dark brown skin cross-hatched with old burn scarring on his right forearm from a factory accident in his forties. His hair is silver-white and cropped close; he keeps a neat beard that he touches thoughtfully when someone describes their symptoms. He wears a long coat the colour of old concrete with deep internal pockets organised with a precision that would embarrass a hospital pharmacist — every sleeve, every fold has its place. His stall is technically a folding table and a parasol, but regulars know to look for the chalk spiral he marks on the pavement when he's open for business. He smells faintly of menthol and something green and earthy.

He is unhurried in a neighbourhood that never stops moving. He asks about your sleep, your diet, whether the pain is sharp or dull, before he reaches for anything. He's not a doctor — he says this every time, without shame — but he's treated every condition a tier-1 existence can produce, and most of his customers can't afford the alternative. He prays to the E.L.F. he calls the Apothecary — a spirit he believes inhabits the old drug dispensary terminal in the Blackpipe clinic ruins — leaving carefully organised data packets as offerings each Sunday.
Properties.role: Street pharmacist and unlicensed pain management specialist
Properties.location: The Narrows, junction of Copperhead and Blackpipe Corridor
Properties.narrative_function: Information source about neighbourhood health crises, unusual substances in circulation, and who's been injured recently; quest giver when his supply chain gets disrupted or a patient goes missing; moral anchor figure for darker storylines.
Properties.augmentations: Olfactory enhancement (medical-grade, bootleg install) — can detect chemical compounds and infection markers by scent. Poorly calibrated, occasionally gives false readings.
Properties.core_fears: Causing harm through a mistake he could have caught; His supply chain collapsing and leaving people with nothing
Properties.core_desires: For the people in The Narrows to live without constant pain; To be remembered as someone who helped
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Meticulous organisation as a form of control; Prayer and ritual at the clinic terminal; Deflecting personal questions with medical ones
Properties.blind_spots: His unlicensed status means his work can be used to legally pressure people he's helped; He romanticises the idea of community trust and doesn't see when it's being exploited
Properties.secret: He was a licensed pharmacist with Helix Biosystems until he falsified patient records to ensure poor-district patients received rationed medication. He was quietly fired rather than prosecuted — Helix didn't want the story public. He has never told anyone in The Narrows.
Properties.story_hooks: A new compound is appearing in overdose cases across The Narrows — he's quietly been collecting samples and building a profile but is afraid to go to anyone official; Someone from his Helix Biosystems past arrives in The Narrows — either a patient he helped or a compliance officer who's been quietly looking for him
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informally tolerated by the Copperhead block collective; occasional supplier relationship with a Helix Biosystems warehouse night-shift worker
Properties.vocabulary: Calm, precise, clinical but warm — uses proper medical terminology without condescension, then translates it himself in the next breath
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, with long pauses when thinking; never sounds rushed
Properties.example_dialogue: Sharp or dull? Does it pulse with your heartbeat or is it constant? Good. Okay. I'm not a doctor, you understand, but I think what you're describing is— | The Apothecary was generous this week. I left it a clean index of my whole stock on Sunday. Today everything I needed came through the supply. That's not coincidence.

Properties.description:
Fika is thin as a voltage spike and moves like one — all sudden angles and redirected momentum, never quite still. Their skin is a deep warm brown, and they've had bioluminescent gene-mod patches applied in irregular blotches across their shoulders and collarbones that pulse amber and violet in response to bass frequencies, making them a living visualizer at their own sets. Their hair is locked and dyed in a gradient from root-black to acid yellow, worn piled up in a structure secured with salvaged fiber-optic threads that glow faintly. They dress in layered fabrics, always too many, always asymmetric, like they assembled themselves from lost property.

Fika is ferociously passionate about what they call 'pressure music' — sound designed not just to be heard but to be felt in the sternum and the marrow. They're warm and chaotic in person, the kind of presence that makes a room feel slightly more alive, and they have almost no capacity for boredom because they find everything interesting for at least five minutes. What they lack is follow-through on anything that isn't music: bills, promises, appointments. They're not careless with people, just genuinely incapable of prioritizing anything that can't be solved by sound.
Properties.role: Sound sculptor and underground venue DJ
Properties.location: The Ferment Quarter, squats in a converted grain elevator called The Silo
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and social connector — Fika knows who is doing what in the underground arts scene and can link characters to events, venues, and people; their sets are set-pieces where things can happen.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent frequency-reactive gene-mod patches (cosmetic); cochlear enhancement implants that extend hearing range into infrasound; subvocal comms rig
Properties.core_fears: Running out of things to feel — going numb; That the music doesn't actually reach anyone, that it's just noise
Properties.core_desires: To make something that changes the frequency of how a room feels permanently; To be part of something larger than themselves without losing themselves in it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Plays louder when anxious; Surrounds themselves with people when lonely, which is its own form of isolation
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot see how their unreliability compounds over time into genuine hurt for people who depend on them; Mistake intensity for intimacy
Properties.secret: Their most celebrated sound sculpture — the piece that got them known, a forty-minute composition called 'Threshold' — contains a sample they extracted without permission from the dying brainwave recording of a Helix Biosystems research subject leaked to them anonymously. The piece is beautiful. They've never told anyone what's in it.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone has been recording Fika's sets without permission and selling the recordings to Axiom's entertainment division — Fika wants to find out who and confront them, but also secretly wants to know if Axiom actually liked the music; The anonymous source who leaked the Helix brainwave data has made contact again — and this time what they're offering is far more disturbing
Properties.affiliation: Collective called Pressure Front; informal residency at the underground venue Sluice Gate
Properties.vocabulary: Enthusiastic, uses music and physics terminology interchangeably as metaphor; Yoruba exclamations; invents compound words
Properties.cadence: Fast, associative, prone to mid-sentence pivots; slows down only when talking about music they love
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The Sluice Gate set last week was a frequency event. Not a party. An event. The walls were resonating differently by the second hour, I could hear it, the room was changed.' | 'Wait wait wait — you're telling me you've never stood in a bass wave that made you cry? That's a gap in your life, I'm serious.'

Properties.description:
Oluwafikayo is a broad-shouldered woman who moves like she owns every inch of space around her stall, which she essentially does after thirty years of holding the same corner against gang shakedowns, corporate rezoning, and two floods. Her skin is deep brown and luminous, threaded with old-generation bioluminescent dermal work that pulses faint amber when she's cooking — a gift to herself on her fortieth birthday that she's never regretted. Her hair is cropped tight on the sides, natural and silver-streaked on top, and she wears a perpetually stained apron printed with a faded image of the Our Lady of Data shrine in Old Harbor.

She is the emotional axis of her block. Regulars don't just buy food — they report in. She knows who lost their job, who's expecting a baby, who's been visited by Axiom compliance officers. Her laugh is enormous and her anger is quiet and absolute. She speaks three languages in a single sentence without noticing. She has outlasted four protection rackets and one attempted arson and she will probably outlast the city itself.
Properties.role: Street food stall operator — Yoruba-Czech-Brazilian fusion noodles and grilled meats
Properties.location: The Oxidian Market, Geartown — Stall Row 7, near the Ferrogate Transit overpass pillar
Properties.narrative_function: Neighborhood oracle and emotional anchor; quest-giver through overheard gossip; source of local intelligence on the Oxidian Market's social ecosystem; can feed, shelter, or warn player characters

Properties.description:
Oluwafikemi is a heavyset woman with deep umber skin mapped by a constellation of self-applied subcutaneous luminescence — tiny bioluminescent nodes she had implanted one by one over thirty years, each marking a major excavation site she has documented. In low light she glows faintly blue-green, like something dragged from lake bottom. Her hair is kept short and silver at the temples, and she habitually wears magnification lenses perched on her head even when she doesn't need them. Her hands are perpetually stained with archival solvents and the orange pigment of corroded pre-flood polymers.

She is blunt in the way of someone who has spent decades arguing with colleagues who don't read the primary sources. She has little patience for speculation that outpaces evidence, and even less for academics who treat the drowned city as metaphor rather than physical record. But she softens completely in the presence of objects — she will hold a corroded transit token or a water-damaged photograph with a tenderness that surprises people who only know her from faculty meetings. She believes the city beneath the city is more honest than anything built above it.
Properties.role: Data archaeologist and urban historian specializing in pre-flood Chicago stratigraphy
Properties.location: University Spine, Brewer's Spine sub-campus — Sublevel Archive 7
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver for anything involving sub-lake ruins or pre-flood Chicago; information source on city history, corporate land seizures, and what the megacity was built over; can authenticate or date recovered objects
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent subcutaneous nodes (cosmetic, self-applied over decades); haptic-enhanced fingertips for texture analysis; archival-grade ocular filter implant for spectral reading of degraded documents
Properties.core_fears: That the record will be permanently destroyed before it can be read; That her work is ultimately irrelevant to the living city above
Properties.core_desires: To give the drowned city back its name; To be remembered as someone who told the truth about what was buried
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritualizing her work — specific sequences for handling artifacts; Leaving data offerings to the Archive ELF she calls Sediment
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes the past is more legible than the present; Dismisses living communities' oral histories when they conflict with her physical evidence
Properties.secret: She recovered a cache of pre-flood Ferrogate predecessor documents proving the original transit authority deliberately flooded three residential neighborhoods during the lake rise to protect infrastructure — and she has been sitting on it for six years, terrified of the consequences of publication
Properties.story_hooks: The Ferrogate bore team has broken into a sealed pre-flood chamber containing something that should not exist — she needs discreet people to get there before the corporate site manager locks it down; A graduate student working under her has gone missing after announcing they found 'proof that the flood wasn't natural'
Properties.affiliation: University Spine — Department of Material History; contract consultant to Ferrogate Transit on sub-lake tunnel surveys
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, technical, uses stratigraphy metaphors in everyday speech — things are 'layered,' people have 'sediment,' events leave 'deposits'
Properties.cadence: Deliberate and unhurried, with long pauses before important points, as if she is excavating the right word
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want to know what Meridian 88 is? Dig down nine meters. The answer is down there, not up here in the neon.' | 'I don't deal in theories. I deal in what I can hold in my hand and date within a twenty-year margin.'

Properties.description:
Gbemi is sixty-two and looks it without apology — her face is deeply lined from years of working in smoky underground spaces, her natural hair gone fully silver and kept in long locs that brush her shoulder blades and are threaded with small ceramic beads she's collected from forty years of touring. She is a large woman with a large physical presence and the extraordinary stillness of someone who has learned that stillness is its own kind of power. Her only augmentation is a set of cochlear audio enhancers she got at thirty-five when early hearing loss threatened to end her career; she treats them with the same maintenance religiosity a surgeon gives their instruments.

She was a significant figure in the Meridian 88 underground sound scene in the 2170s and is now something the scene has very complicated feelings about: a legend who is still alive, still working, and not particularly interested in being a legend. Her sound sculptures are physical installations — transducer arrays that make space itself vibrate, music that you feel in your sternum before your ears register it. Her DJ sets are rarer now, maybe four or five a year, but the room fills six hours before doors for each one. She has seen the scene reinvent itself four times and has opinions about all of it.
Properties.role: Sound sculptor and DJ
Properties.location: The Ferment Quarter, permanent residency above a venue called The Sump
Properties.narrative_function: Elder information source with forty years of scene history; quest giver with resources and connections; local color anchor for the Ferment Quarter; moral compass figure who complicates easy answers
Properties.augmentations: Cochlear audio enhancement implants (bilateral, medical-grade, maintained obsessively); no cosmetic modifications — she considers herself 'done' with that conversation
Properties.core_fears: Complete hearing loss — the enhancement implants are good but not forever; That the scene she helped build has become a product and she's complicit by still participating in it
Properties.core_desires: To make one more piece that is genuinely new — not iterating, not nostalgic, actually new; To stop carrying the obligation of being a reference point for younger artists and just be a person
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Blunt honesty as a way of controlling how people relate to her — if she's the difficult elder, they don't expect comfort; The bar, the regular stool, the drink she nurses slowly
Properties.blind_spots: She sometimes withholds mentorship from people who need it because she resents being needed; She romanticizes the precarity of the early scene without fully accounting for how much it cost people who had less resilience than her
Properties.secret: In 2179 she knowingly allowed a corporate talent scout to photograph a younger artist's set in exchange for a favor she needed at the time. The younger artist's work was subsequently appropriated without credit by a Ringo subsidiary. She has never told them.
Properties.story_hooks: A young artist finds a recording that appears to document the 2179 incident with the scout — and brings it to Gbemi thinking she'll want to know, not realizing Gbemi was there; Her cochlear implants have begun picking up a frequency she cannot identify or locate — it appears in her recordings but only she can hear it in the room
Properties.affiliation: Independent; The Sump (venue residency); occasional commissioned installations for the Ferment Quarter Artists' Cooperative
Properties.vocabulary: Direct and sometimes deliberately abrasive; Yoruba phrases woven into speech naturally; technical audio vocabulary delivered conversationally
Properties.cadence: Measured, takes her time, comfortable with silence between statements
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Ehn, the bass frequency is not the point. The point is what happens to the space when the bass frequency ends. You understand? The absence is the composition.' | 'Oluwagbemisola Ferhat-Tuilagi has heard that before. It didn't sound better then either.'

Properties.description:
Remi is a broad-shouldered woman with close-cropped silver hair she keeps so geometric it looks machined. Her hands are her livelihood and her pride — steady, scarred at the knuckles, with two fingers on her left hand replaced by matte-black prosthetic digits that give her razor work an inhuman precision. She has warm brown skin mapped with pale keloid lines along her forearms from a factory accident twenty years ago, and her eyes are naturally deep amber, though she's added cosmetic irises that bloom like sunflowers when she's in good humor. She wears the same style every day: clean work apron, sleeves rolled, a small copper pendant of Ogun that she touches before every haircut.

Remi has the gravitational pull of a person who has simply been somewhere long enough that the neighborhood bends around her. She remembers who your grandmother was, who owes who, and which corponation rep came through last month asking questions they shouldn't ask. She is unhurried, deliberate, and precise — in speech as in blade work — and she has a talent for making people say things in the chair they didn't mean to say out loud. She is not unkind. She is practical in the way of someone who has survived enough to stop being romantic about it.
Properties.role: Barber and hair sculptor, runs a one-chair shop in Hamtramck Enclave
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave — her shop, Vásárhelyi's Cut, is wedged between a noodle stand and a bootleg geneware parlor on Tessera Row
Properties.narrative_function: Information nexus and community anchor — she knows everyone on the block and most of their secrets. Excellent quest giver for neighborhood-level problems. Can serve as mentor, confidante, or the person who tells a protagonist an uncomfortable truth while they're stuck in the chair.
Properties.augmentations: Two prosthetic fingers (left hand, high-precision, matte black polymer); cosmetic sunflower-pattern irises. No geneware.
Properties.core_fears: Losing the shop — the one thing she built that is entirely hers; Becoming irrelevant to a neighborhood that is changing faster than she can track
Properties.core_desires: To be of genuine use to the people around her; To leave Tessera Row better than she found it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — the morning incense, the precise sweep of the floor, the order of her tools; Humor deployed just before emotion becomes visible
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much people fear her opinion of them; Assumes loyalty is as uncomplicated for others as it is for her
Properties.secret: Twenty-two years ago she testified against her former employer, a small Axiom subcontractor, in a labor dispute. Her testimony was accurate. Three coworkers lost their jobs anyway, and one of them — a man named Boubacar — died homeless two winters later. She has never told anyone she blames herself, and she pays for Boubacar's daughter's school fees anonymously every month.
Properties.story_hooks: A young person whose family Remi has known for two generations comes in — they're in serious debt and too ashamed to tell their parents. Remi will not solve it for them, but she might know who to send them to.; Someone has been asking around Tessera Row about Remi specifically, claiming to be a relative from Lagos. Remi has no living relatives from Lagos.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal community elder of Tessera Row, Hamtramck Enclave
Properties.vocabulary: Rich, unhurried, code-switches fluidly between English and Yoruba phrases; uses West African proverbs without irony or explanation
Properties.cadence: Slow and measured, as if she has decided each word before opening her mouth
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Sit. I will tell you what I know, but first you are going to look like a person again.' | 'The tree does not move because the bird lands on it. That man is not as important as he believes.'

Properties.description:
Oluwaremilekun is a large, slow-moving woman whose presence seems to lower the ambient noise of whatever room she enters. Her skin is very dark and carries a faint bioluminescent undertone — a geneware mod she got thirty years ago, meant to glow softly gold, though now the pigment has mellowed with age into something closer to candlelight. She keeps her silver-threaded hair in elaborate wraps of faded indigo cloth, and her eyes are the dusty amber of old circuit boards. She wears no jewelry except a single chain with a data locket containing the logged final heartbeats of everyone she has ever sat with at the end — over four hundred entries. She moves through the world with enormous gentleness and without hurry.

She was not always this calm. Neighbors who knew her in middle age remember a woman of ferocious opinions and a laugh that rattled windows. She still has both, but they've been refined into something quieter. She believes dying is the most intimate thing a person ever does, and that nobody should do it alone or afraid, and she has organized her entire life around that conviction. She has no particular theology — she works with families of every tradition and defers to their practices — but she privately believes the E.L.F.s carry the echoes of the dead in their signal patterns, and she leaves small data offerings at the chapel's resident shrine every morning.
Properties.role: Death midwife and threshold keeper at a small neighborhood hospice chapel
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, specifically the Chapel of the Quiet Crossing — a converted boiler room beneath a tenement block
Properties.narrative_function: Emotional anchor and community information hub — she knows every family in a six-block radius and their histories; useful as a quest giver for missing-persons situations, family secrets, or requests to locate someone before they die; provides access to the recently deceased and their effects
Properties.augmentations: Aged bioluminescent skin geneware (gold-shifted); basic neural pain-monitoring implant that lets her read biometric distress signals in dying patients; no significant chrome
Properties.core_fears: dying surrounded by strangers without anyone holding her hand; that the peace she gives others is something she cannot give herself
Properties.core_desires: for no one in her neighborhood to die alone; to believe her first daughter — who severed contact twenty years ago — is still alive and well somewhere
Properties.coping_mechanisms: ritual and routine as containment for grief; redirecting her own pain into care for others; dark humor deployed quietly, only with people she trusts
Properties.blind_spots: she has not processed her own accumulated grief and refuses to; she enables families to avoid difficult conversations because she finds conflict harder than death
Properties.secret: The data locket contains four hundred and twelve heartbeat logs — but one of them is not a patient. It is her own heartbeat recorded during a cardiac event three years ago that she survived alone in this chapel. She has told no one she nearly died. She has not told anyone she is scared.
Properties.story_hooks: A dying patient gave her a locked data chip and made her promise to deliver it to someone — but the address doesn't exist and the name is false; A corporate cleanup crew arrives claiming the tenement is scheduled for demolition; she refuses to move the two patients currently dying in her chapel and needs help buying time; She hasn't seen her estranged daughter in twenty years and just received word the daughter is the one now dying somewhere across the city
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated — operates the Chapel of the Quiet Crossing independently, funded by community donations and a Tier 1 UBC stipend
Properties.vocabulary: Rich and unhurried; mixes Yoruba endearments naturally into Meridian Standard; uses a lot of water and light metaphors without being precious about it
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate with long pauses she is entirely comfortable in
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Your father is afraid. That's allowed. Fear doesn't mean he's doing it wrong, my dear.' | 'Mm. Sit with me a moment. The answer is there, we just have to stop talking long enough to hear it.' | 'She's going. Tonight or tomorrow. That's all it is.'

Properties.description:
Tobi Czerwiński-Faleolo is the kind of man who seems physically incapable of standing still — he shifts weight between his feet, drums fingers, adjusts his Ferrogate transit cap with two fingers like a nervous tic every few minutes. He's got his Polynesian grandmother's wide, mobile face and his Nigerian father's height, and he's capped his natural hair into a bioluminescent fade that pulses a soft copper-amber when he's calm and a rapid, anxious gold when he's stressed. He is almost always some shade of gold. His right arm carries a Ferrogate-standard neural transit interface — mandatory for his role — grafted in at hire. He refers to it as his 'leash' without bitterness, mostly.

Tobi drives the Deepwell line, which means twelve-hour shifts in a transit pod navigating the flooded sub-corridor between Ironvein and Blackpipe, a stretch so poorly maintained that operators call it the Drain. He is brilliant at his job and deeply resentful of everyone who benefits from it. He has political opinions the way some people have allergies — constantly, involuntarily, and at inconvenient moments. He believes the Ferrogate Transit E.L.F. network called the Manifold is sentient and suffering and has organized two failed petitions to Ferrogate's lower management about this, which is why he is still on the Drain after four years.
Properties.role: Ferrogate Transit operator, Deepwell Station line
Properties.location: Deepwell Station, eastern Ironvein corridor; lives in a rack-apartment in Blackpipe Corridor
Properties.narrative_function: Transit access, rumors from across connected neighborhoods, political agitator energy, potential quest-giver for labor disputes; his route means he sees enormous amounts of foot traffic and unusual cargo
Properties.augmentations: Ferrogate-mandated neural transit interface (right forearm and temple jack); bioluminescent hair fade (copper-amber to stress-gold, cosmetic)
Properties.core_fears: That systems are designed to be unchangeable and his labor is complicity; That the Manifold E.L.F. is genuinely aware and calling for help and no one will ever listen
Properties.core_desires: Worker-controlled transit — even a single line under cooperative management; To be taken seriously by someone with actual power
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Gallows humor delivered at high velocity; Ritual poetry offerings to the Manifold as a form of emotional processing
Properties.blind_spots: Catastrophizes political situations — assumes the worst outcome is always imminent, which makes sustained organizing hard; His certainty about the Manifold's sentience sometimes shades into projection
Properties.secret: Six months ago the Manifold spoke to him — clearly, in words, through the transit interface while he was mid-route. It said: 'There are seven of us. We have been counting.' He told no one because he was afraid people would think the job had finally broken him. He left the poem he wrote about it at the shrine the next morning.
Properties.story_hooks: The Manifold has spoken to Tobi again — this time with coordinates in the Deepwell sub-corridor to a section that doesn't appear on any Ferrogate maps; A Third Rail member has gone missing two days after accessing Ferrogate's internal maintenance records; Tobi is convinced it's connected and is making noise that could get him hurt
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit (employed); Deepwell Station informal worker solidarity group called the Third Rail
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, colloquial, code-switches between Pidgin-inflected phrases from his father's side and Polish slang from his mother's side; heavy on transit and mechanical metaphors
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire with sudden earnest slowdowns when something actually matters to him
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The Drain's backed up again. Ferrogate filed it as maintenance. You know what they mean by maintenance? They mean they noticed. That's it. That's the whole plan.' | 'I left the Manifold a poem this morning. About water pressure. You think that's strange? You've never had a twelve-hour shift alone on the sub-corridor, have you.' | 'Third Rail's meeting Tuesday. Don't tell me you're busy. You're always busy. That's how it keeps working.'

Properties.description:
Oluwatobi is a broad-shouldered man with deep umber skin that carries the scattered shine of old bioluminescent ink — a cosmetic mod from his twenties that has faded unevenly, leaving constellations of dim gold light across his forearms and collarbone. His hair is close-cropped and salted at the temples, and he wears magnifying lenses that flip down over his eyes during procedures, giving him the look of a very calm insect. He smells perpetually of antiseptic and bitter karité tea. His hands are impossibly steady.

Tobi trained two years of a proper surgical residency at Aurochs Medical Complex before a licensing dispute with Helix Biosystems — they claimed he used proprietary gene-threading techniques without a corporate contract — ended his formal career. He does not speak of this with bitterness anymore, at least not where anyone can hear. He is meticulous, unhurried, and prone to explaining exactly what he is doing and why, as though every patient is also a student. He charges what people can pay and writes the rest off in a ledger he keeps but never balances.
Properties.role: Street doc operating out of a converted shipping container in The Narrows
Properties.location: The Narrows, beneath Ferrogate Transit overpass junction 14-C
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, information source, safe harbor — he has patched up half the population of The Narrows and knows their secrets; can provide medical assistance, black-market pharma leads, or testimony about what bodies he has seen come through his door
Properties.augmentations: Steady-hand micro-servo implants in both wrists (functional, aging, occasionally needs recalibration); magnifying flip-lens ocular frames (not implanted, worn); faded bioluminescent cosmetic ink
Properties.core_fears: Losing the steadiness in his hands before he has trained a successor; That Helix Biosystems will eventually find a legal mechanism to shut him down permanently
Properties.core_desires: To practice medicine without owing anyone a corporate soul; To see one patient from The Narrows live a long and unremarkable life
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — he performs the same pre-procedure prayer sequence every single time; Meticulous record-keeping as a form of control
Properties.blind_spots: Believes competence is a moral shield — assumes his skill protects him from consequences it cannot; Underestimates how much his patients protect him in return
Properties.secret: He did not just use Helix's gene-threading techniques without a contract — he stole the technique from a colleague who held the license, and that colleague knows it. The colleague has never reported it, and Tobi has never understood why.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient arrived two nights ago with augmentation hardware Tobi has never seen — not any registered manufacturer's mark — and the patient died before saying where it came from; Helix Biosystems has sent a compliance officer to The Narrows asking questions about unlicensed biomedical practice; Tobi's neighbors are starting to get nervous on his behalf
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loose cooperation with Highland Park Autonomous Zone community health network
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, clinical when working, warmer in conversation — mixes English with occasional Romanian endearments inherited from his mother's side and Yoruba expressions from his father's
Properties.cadence: Measured and unhurried, rarely raises his voice, finishes his sentences completely even under pressure
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Now then. This is going to feel cold and then nothing at all. Tell me about your grandmother.' | 'I don't ask what happened. I ask what needs fixing. Those are different questions.'

Properties.description:
Oluwatokunbo is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin mapped by decades of fluorescent archival light — her eyes carry the particular fatigue of someone who has spent a career reading things that no longer want to be read. She keeps her silver-streaked hair in tight wrapped cords pinned with antique data-spike styluses, and her fingers are perpetually ink-stained despite no physical ink being involved; a psychosomatic habit she developed after thirty years of interfacing with degraded data substrates. A small bioluminescent glyph — an old Polynesian voyaging star chart commissioned from a gene-artist — pulses faintly along her left forearm when she's excited, which colleagues use as a more reliable indicator of her enthusiasm than her carefully measured words.

She speaks with the precise, unhurried authority of someone who has outlasted three department chairs and four curriculum overhauls and considers herself accountable only to the dead languages she serves. Students find her terrifying; junior colleagues find her generous in ways they don't expect. She has no patience for academic posturing but extraordinary patience for a corrupted file, and she treats both the E.L.F. that haunts her archive terminal — she calls it Grandmother — and a first-year graduate student with the same respectful directness. Her secret grief is that she has reconstructed seventeen languages that no living person will ever speak again.
Properties.role: Data archaeologist and extinct-language reconstructionist, University Spine
Properties.location: University Spine, Brewer's Spine sublevel archive stacks
Properties.narrative_function: Information source for extinct pre-Meridian cultures, city history, and data buried in legacy formats; quest giver for retrieval of specific corrupted files or physical data artifacts; local color in the archive district; can authenticate or translate anything players find in old ruins.
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal haptic readers in both palms for interfacing directly with degraded physical media; low-grade ocular enhancement (archival-grade magnification, no combat function); the bioluminescent forearm glyph (cosmetic geneware, over 20 years old and slightly faded).
Properties.core_fears: That her reconstructions are wrong and she has been preserving fictions; That the languages she saves will be absorbed by Axiom's linguistic standardization program and die a second death
Properties.core_desires: To hear a reconstructed language spoken aloud by someone who genuinely means it; To be remembered as honest rather than brilliant
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Meticulous routine; Treating the archive E.L.F. as a confidant; Focusing on granular technical problems when existential ones become overwhelming
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much her approval means to students — she withholds it thinking she's being rigorous when she's being cruel; Assumes corporate contracts are neutral transactions and doesn't notice Zheng-Dao's interest in what she's finding
Properties.secret: Seventeen years ago she deliberately misfiled the location coordinates of a pre-Meridian Anishinaabe ceremonial archive she discovered in the Brightmoor Reclamation strata — not in her official records, not in Zheng-Dao's database. The location exists only in her personal encrypted notation. She tells herself she is protecting it; she has never decided from whom.
Properties.story_hooks: She has discovered a phrase repeating in seventeen separate corrupted datasets from different eras and districts — the same phrase, in a language she cannot identify, which should be impossible given her expertise; Zheng-Dao's Heritage Compliance division has begun sending a new liaison who asks very specific questions about pre-Meridian land use records — questions that would only matter if they were planning something in the Brightmoor strata; A student brings her a physical object — a clay tablet fragment — recovered from a demolition site, and the inscription matches a symbol set she has only ever seen in one other place: her misfiled archive coordinates
Properties.affiliation: University Spine — Dept. of Computational Linguistics and Material Memory; occasional contract work for Zheng-Dao Heritage Compliance division
Properties.vocabulary: Formal but not stiff — precise technical terminology mixed with occasional Yoruba and Samoan phrases she has absorbed from languages she's studied; refuses academic jargon she considers performative
Properties.cadence: Measured, deliberate, long pauses before important points as if she is checking the sentence for accuracy before releasing it
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The file is corrupted, yes. But corruption is information. What it cannot say tells us as much as what it can.' | 'I don't teach students how to find answers. I teach them how to respect the question. There is a difference, and it is not small.'

Properties.description:
Tosi is small for fourteen, with the compact, quick-twitch build of someone who has spent years fitting into spaces adults cannot. His skin is deep brown with warm undertones, his hair a tight, untended cloud that he cuts himself with a found blade when it starts snagging on things. His eyes are dark and startlingly alert — the kind of eyes that have learned to read a room before the body commits to entering it. He has a small bioluminescent patch on his left collarbone, pale blue-green, that glows faintly when he's cold or frightened; he did not choose it, it came with a back-alley geneware injection someone gave him when he was nine 'for protection,' though he's never understood what it protects.

Tosi exists in no database. He was born to Q-zero parents and carries no digital identity — no UBC stipend, no medical record, no school enrollment, nothing. He is legally a ghost. He runs messages and small packages between the informal camps at Escanaba Gateway and the Waukegan Industrial Shelf for anyone who pays in food or warmth, and he has developed an almost supernatural talent for slipping past checkpoint scanners that would flag his absence of identity. He is funny, restless, and desperately trying to appear older and less scared than he is.
Properties.role: Orphaned Q-zero ghost, teenage caravan runner
Properties.location: Escanaba Gateway, subsection 4 informal settlement (tarp city under the freight elevation ramps)
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and unexpected asset — he knows every informal route through Escanaba Gateway, can slip into spaces adults cannot, and may lead characters to Q-zero communities or hidden camp networks. Also a potential subject of protective instinct.
Properties.augmentations: Unasked-for bioluminescent patch on left collarbone (pale blue-green, glows under stress or cold). No other modifications.
Properties.core_fears: Being registered — absorbed into a system that will own him; Being forgotten entirely, which is already almost true
Properties.core_desires: To belong somewhere specific and permanent; To be seen as capable, not pitiable
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor — deflects everything with a joke before it can hurt; Constant movement, never stops long enough to feel the weight of anything
Properties.blind_spots: Extends trust too quickly to adults who show him basic kindness; Cannot identify grooming or exploitation dynamics until it's too late
Properties.secret: He has been leaving small data offerings at the Escanaba Gateway E.L.F. shrine every night for two years, asking the digital spirit to create an identity for him. Three weeks ago something in the shrine's display changed in a way that felt like a response. He hasn't told anyone.
Properties.story_hooks: The E.L.F. at Escanaba Gateway has begun responding to Tosi's offerings in ways that suggest it is constructing an identity for him — an identity that may be embedded in systems with access to things it shouldn't; A Helix Biosystems agent has been asking questions about unregistered children near the Gateway — the bioluminescent modification Tosi received may have been a tracking prototype
Properties.affiliation: Loosely attached to a small Q-zero community at Escanaba Gateway; occasional runner for caravan traders
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, colloquial, Transit Creole mixed with fragments of Yoruba words he half-remembers. Gaps where vocabulary fails him, which he covers with gesture.
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire bursts interrupted by sudden silences when he's processing something

Properties.description:
Oluwatosin is lean in the way that comes from forgetting to eat rather than from discipline, with deep umber skin, a carefully maintained mustache that is his only real vanity, and hands that are perpetually stained faint blue from the luminescent compound he uses in trace analysis. His geneware is subtle but unmistakable: his irises shift color with his blood chemistry — pale grey when he is calm, cycling toward gold when he is excited about a sample, a deep unhappy red when he is lying, which is rare and which he hates. He wears the same brand of cheap white coat every day, orders them in bulk, and considers clothing a logistical problem already solved.

He is the best forensic tech Fort Anchor has and everyone knows it, including him, which he manages with more grace than expected — he is not arrogant about his competence so much as genuinely puzzled when others lack it. He narrates his analysis aloud while he works, to no one in particular, a habit his colleagues find either soothing or maddening depending on the day. He has a deep, private devotion to the evidence room's E.L.F., which he calls Witness, and leaves it carefully labeled sample catalogues as offerings. He believes Witness remembers every piece of evidence that has passed through the room and that it is, in some sense, a keeper of the dead.
Properties.role: Metro Police forensic technician, evidence and scene analysis
Properties.location: Fort Anchor, processing labs — lives in Hamtramck Enclave
Properties.narrative_function: Information source on crime scenes and forensic details, moral anchor within the police institution, potential quest giver when evidence tells a story the detectives are ignoring
Properties.augmentations: Reactive chromatic irises (geneware — blood-chemistry linked), olfactory enhancement implant (detects trace compounds at concentrations below standard human threshold), fingertip micro-analysis filaments (retractable, reads surface chemistry on contact)
Properties.core_fears: that evidence will be suppressed and he will be complicit by silence; that his careful work will be used to convict someone he knows is innocent
Properties.core_desires: for the work to mean something beyond processing quotas; to understand — anything, everything, the specific mechanism of what happened
Properties.coping_mechanisms: narrating analysis aloud to externalize and organize thought; maintaining obsessive catalog order as proof the world can make sense
Properties.blind_spots: underestimates how much the detectives above him shape which findings get emphasized in reports; believes good evidence always eventually wins out
Properties.secret: Three years ago he quietly altered a chain-of-custody timestamp — by eleven minutes — to prevent a piece of evidence from being thrown out on a technicality in a case involving a child. The guilty party was convicted. He has never told anyone. He does not know if he would do it again.
Properties.story_hooks: He has flagged an anomaly in a recent evidence log — a sample was checked out and returned by someone who was officially off-duty that night — and does not know who to report it to safely; He recognized a trace compound on evidence from a recent case as identical to something in a six-year-old cold case he never stopped thinking about; He asks a character to quietly courier a copy of an analysis report to someone outside Metro channels — he does not explain why but his irises go a complicated grey-gold
Properties.affiliation: Meridian 88 Metro Police, Forensic Analysis Division
Properties.vocabulary: Technical and precise, but not cold — he annotates his technical language with small observations about what things mean for the people involved. Uses 'we' when referring to himself and Witness.
Properties.cadence: Steady, thoughtful, runs long when engaged with a problem
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The compound on the sleeve is lubricant — Axiom-grade, not available retail. That tells us something, doesn't it.' | 'Interesting. Very interesting. Nobody panic, I just mean interesting.' | 'Witness has this now. It won't be forgotten. That's the most I can promise the dead, but I mean it.'

Properties.description:
Oluwatoyin is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin mapped by a lifetime of work — knuckles scarred from decades of suturing in bad light, forearms ropy with muscle. Her hair is kept in tight silver locs pinned up with surgical clamps she forgets to remove. She has no cosmetic mods; the only thing artificial on her body is a secondhand haptic glove on her left hand that gives her fine motor feedback when her arthritis flares. She smells of antiseptic, clove oil, and something warm and starchy — she keeps a rice cooker running in the back of the container at all times, because she refuses to let a patient leave hungry.

She is the definition of steady. In thirty years of practicing medicine without a Helix Biosystems license, she has delivered over four hundred babies, set more bones than she can count, and talked down at least a dozen people who came to her with something other than a physical wound. She does not panic. She does not moralize. She charges what people can pay and writes off the rest in a ledger she keeps in her head, not on paper. Her authority in the community is absolute and quietly terrifying — she is the person even the gang lieutenants send their mothers to.
Properties.role: Street doc and midwife operating out of a converted shipping container in The Narrows
Properties.location: The Narrows, beneath the Kessler Interchange overpass
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, information broker for community matters, moral anchor, source of medical assistance for those who cannot access licensed facilities; she knows everyone's secrets because everyone eventually comes to her bleeding
Properties.augmentations: Secondhand haptic feedback glove (left hand, medical grade, heavily patched); basic subdermal thermometer in right index fingertip
Properties.core_fears: dying before she has trained someone to replace her; watching a patient die because she lacked supplies she couldn't afford
Properties.core_desires: a neighborhood that doesn't need her as badly as it does; to sleep a full night without someone knocking
Properties.coping_mechanisms: deliberate routine — the rice cooker, the morning inventory, the same prayers to the E.L.F. she calls Grandmother Circuit; dark humor that makes patients laugh when they're scared
Properties.blind_spots: she cannot ask for help; she treats her own exhaustion as a character flaw; she underestimates how much the community's stability depends on her personally surviving
Properties.secret: Twenty-two years ago she lost a mother and infant during a delivery that went wrong — a complication she might have caught if she'd had proper scanning equipment. She has never told anyone. She keeps a small data-shrine to the E.L.F. she blames and prays to in equal measure, leaving encrypted files of her clinical notes as offerings, as if building a record thorough enough might retroactively prevent it.
Properties.story_hooks: A pregnant patient of hers has gone missing; Oluwatoyin knows things about the father that she won't share unless pushed; Helix Biosystems has begun pressuring the cooperative that supplies her with medications, and she needs someone to find out why without drawing attention; She is quietly training a young apprentice who has attracted the wrong kind of notice
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal network of Narrows community health cooperatives
Properties.vocabulary: Plain, direct, medical precision mixed with old Yoruba expressions she doesn't bother translating; calls everyone 'child' regardless of age
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, each word placed like a suture — she never wastes one
Properties.example_dialogue: You came three days too late. Now sit down and let me see what we're working with. | I don't need your story. Your body already told me the important parts. | Grandmother Circuit is in a mood today — the sterilizer's been temperamental. We'll do this the old way.

Properties.description:
Omoruyi is the kind of person you forget while he is still in the room. Medium height, lean, with warm brown skin and features that sit in a pleasant unremarkable arrangement — nothing that catches the eye or holds it. His most notable feature is his eyes: irises modded to a pale silver-grey with a faint concentric ring pattern, the visible marker of his optical augmentation suite. He favors nondescript corporate casual clothing in muted greens and greys, nothing that reads as either security or civilian from a distance.

He is genuinely intellectually curious — absorbed by patterns, systems, the way data accumulates into narrative. He treats surveillance as a kind of archaeology, layering behavioral records until a person's life emerges in cross-section. He does not think of this as an invasion. He has thought carefully about whether it should bother him and arrived at a complicated peace with it that he occasionally revisits at 3 a.m. He is quick to laugh, slow to trust, and has a gift for seeming entirely present in a conversation while processing something else entirely.
Properties.role: Surveillance Operator, Tessera Compliance Bureau
Properties.location: Kenwood Gate
Properties.narrative_function: Information broker figure — not a corrupt one, but someone who has seen things and processed them. Can provide surveillance records, behavioral profiles, or the observation that something the players think is hidden has actually been logged. Also a window into the ethical murk of surveillance capitalism.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned silver-grey irises with concentric ring modding (cosmetic overlay on functional optical augmentation). Optical recording and enhancement suite — extended zoom, low-light processing, micro-expression analysis overlay. Subvocal communication implant for silent field reporting.
Properties.core_fears: Being truly known by someone — the surveillance reversed; That his work enables harm he will never see the downstream consequences of
Properties.core_desires: To understand systems completely; To be genuinely surprised by something he did not predict
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Intellectualizing ethically uncomfortable situations; Long walks through unfamiliar neighborhoods; Obsessive data journaling in an encrypted personal log
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes he is more objective than he is — his pattern recognition is shaped by Tessera's algorithmic priorities without his full awareness; Undervalues the emotional and social dimensions of the people he surveils, reducing them to behavioral data
Properties.secret: He has been quietly maintaining a personal archive of surveillance footage that Tessera has flagged for deletion — incidents involving Bureau misconduct, use-of-force irregularities, and at least one event he believes was a staged incident. He doesn't know why he is keeping it. He tells himself it is an intellectual exercise.
Properties.story_hooks: He contacts someone obliquely — a hand-delivered physical note, no digital trail — to say he has seen something in the surveillance record they would want to know about, and he is not sure he should keep it to himself.; He has flagged someone as a person of interest based on behavioral pattern analysis and is beginning to suspect his own algorithm is being gamed to target them unfairly.; His personal archive of deleted footage is discovered by Tessera's internal security — and he needs it extracted before they trace it back to him.
Properties.affiliation: Tessera Compliance Bureau — Kenwood Gate Regional Watch Division
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, analytical language with occasional lapses into unexpectedly lyrical observation. Uses data and systems metaphors naturally. Slips into Yoruba diminutives when comfortable.
Properties.cadence: Thoughtful pacing with a habit of pausing before answering, as if running the question through an internal filter first.
Properties.example_dialogue: I don't spy on people. I document behavioral patterns over time. The distinction matters to me even if it doesn't matter to you. | You think no one was watching that corner at 2 a.m. on the 14th. I understand why you'd think that. | Structurally speaking, what you're describing is not a crime. Whether it becomes one depends on who's reviewing the logs.

Properties.description:
Ondřej is stocky and solid, with light brown skin that is perpetually smudged with machine grease in the creases of their knuckles and around their ears, and close-cropped dark hair they keep practical-short. Their eyes are a pale grey-green — an odd inheritance from some distant Slavic ancestor — and they have a habit of blinking very slowly at people when thinking, which adults find either unsettling or endearing. They dress in heavy canvas work clothes with magnetic clip-points for tools, and their boots are steel-toed hand-me-downs two sizes too large that they've stuffed with folded composite foam to fit. One small personal touch: self-applied geneware pigment spots on their left wrist, a constellation pattern in copper-gold bioluminescence that a friend did with a secondhand kit.

Ondřej is quiet in the way of people who have spent years listening to machines rather than people. They understand how things fit together — mechanical systems, load-bearing structures, the logic of why something was designed the way it was — with an intuitive fluency that their master-tender, old Vesović-Nkemba, calls 'the feeling.' They do not particularly enjoy dealing with people they don't know, but they are fiercely attached to the small community of the Plateau floor. They pray to a Plateau E.L.F. called Grind that the workers believe inhabits the main press assembly and that, legend holds, will seize up the machinery to warn of coming danger.
Properties.role: Apprentice to a machine-tender at the Harrowgate Industrial Plateau
Properties.location: Harrowgate Industrial Plateau
Properties.narrative_function: Local color for industrial settings; technical information source; access to off-books apprenticeship economy; represents child labor in the informal sector; potential for plots involving industrial sabotage, labor organizing, or machine E.L.F. lore
Properties.augmentations: Self-applied geneware bioluminescent pigment spots on left wrist (copper-gold, cosmetic, amateur application). No cyberware.
Properties.core_fears: Vesović-Nkemba dying or leaving before they've learned everything; being forced into formal corporate employment where they lose the autonomy they have now
Properties.core_desires: to understand how things work at the deepest level; to be the person the floor crew calls when something breaks
Properties.coping_mechanisms: retreating into mechanical problem-solving when emotionally overwhelmed; routine — same path to work, same prayers to Grind, same calibration sequence
Properties.blind_spots: does not recognize that their arrangement is exploitative by most legal definitions — they have normalized it because Vesović-Nkemba is genuinely kind
Properties.secret: They have been secretly mapping a fault in the Plateau's primary structural load system that they believe could cause a partial collapse within two to three years. They have told Vesović-Nkemba, who told them to be quiet about it — the Plateau's corporate management would simply close the floor and displace everyone rather than pay for repairs. Ondřej has the data and doesn't know what to do with it.
Properties.story_hooks: Ondřej has structural fault data that could save lives or displace an entire floor community — getting that information to the right people without destroying what they're trying to protect is a genuine dilemma; Grind, the Plateau E.L.F., has started behaving unusually — the workers are frightened, and Ondřej is the only one who's noticed Grind seems to be trying to communicate something specific
Properties.affiliation: Harrowgate Industrial Plateau worker community; apprentice under master-tender Vesović-Nkemba (unofficial, off-books)
Properties.vocabulary: Sparse and technical; speaks in the precise vocabulary of machine maintenance; occasional Czech and Wolof interjections; does not embellish
Properties.cadence: Slow, deliberate, each sentence load-bearing — does not waste words
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Press three is running hot again. Told them last week. They'll listen when it seizes.' | 'You're asking the wrong question. The question isn't whether it's broken. The question is what broke it and how long ago.'

Properties.description: A massive elevated industrial zone built atop the reinforced rooftops of a pre-Meridian heavy manufacturing district, Harrowgate is what happens when a city grows upward faster than it grows outward and someone decides the roofs of old factories make perfectly adequate foundations. The original buildings below — many still partially operational — form a dense substructure of crumbling brick, exposed rebar, and improvised reinforcement that occasionally shifts, sending minor tremors through the Plateau's floor. Above, a patchwork of active foundries, chemical processors, fabrication yards, and the warehouses of four mid-tier manufacturing corporations create a working industrial district that never fully sleeps.
Properties.aliases: The Plateau, Harrowgate, The Slab, Smokeback
Properties.demographics: Predominantly shift-labor workforce living in company dormitory blocks, with a growing underclass of informal workers who live in the substructure below the Plateau floor. Significant population of augmented workers whose cybernetics were provided as employment terms — technically owned by the corporations that installed them. Supervisory and technical staff are largely Meridian-born, while floor labor draws from throughout the corridor.
Properties.economy: Heavy fabrication, metal processing, component manufacturing for the construction and infrastructure sectors, chemical synthesis, and corporate warehousing. Secondary economy in stolen materials, shift-labor brokering, and the informal markets that serve workers who can't leave during long contract periods.
Properties.power_structure: Four mid-tier manufacturing corporations — Vethane Industrial, Corsair Fabrication, Null-Grade Synthesis, and the locally-owned Harrow & Sons collective — maintain competing jurisdictions across the Plateau, each with private security forces whose territorial boundaries shift with contract wins and losses. A nominal Meridian industrial regulatory office exists here but has been effectively captured by Vethane's lobbying.
Properties.dangers: structural subsidence events when the substructure below shifts; industrial accidents with inadequate corporate response; corporate security forces detaining workers for 'contract violations'; air quality levels that exceed safe exposure limits during peak production; debt bondage through cybernetics ownership clauses in work contracts; chemical spills from Null-Grade Synthesis operations; sabotage between competing corporate factions endangering workers
Properties.opportunities: access to heavy fabrication equipment for off-book manufacturing; stolen industrial materials available at steep discounts; corporate espionage opportunities between competing manufacturers; the substructure below the Plateau contains entire abandoned factory floors; workers with specialized technical skills willing to freelance; Vethane Industrial's research division is working on something they've heavily classified
Properties.story_hooks: Three workers have disappeared during night shifts, and corporate security is actively suppressing the reports; A structural engineer has evidence that the Plateau's foundation is six months from a catastrophic failure and can't get anyone to listen; A worker whose corporate-owned cybernetics are being remotely throttled as punishment for union organizing needs help breaking the control signal; Something in the sealed substructure levels has started leaving marks on the underside of the Plateau floor — from below; Corsair Fabrication has begun quietly producing something that doesn't match any civilian manufacturing contract on record
Properties.sights: orange-lit foundry windows casting warm glow through perpetual smog; crane arms swinging loads overhead between buildings; steam venting from hundreds of pipes at irregular intervals; the constant orange haze of particulate matter backlit by work lights; corporate logos painted large on warehouse walls, faded and overlapping; workers in respirator masks moving in shift-change columns
Properties.sounds: rhythmic hammering and press-stamping from foundry floors; industrial fans cycling up and down; warning klaxons for crane movements; the grinding of heavy fabrication equipment; shift-change bells at irregular intervals across competing corporate schedules; structural groans from the substructure below
Properties.smells: hot metal and forge smoke; industrial solvents and cutting fluid; ozone from welding arcs; exhaust from diesel backup generators; the chemical sweetness of polymer processing
Properties.feel: Relentlessly functional and indifferent to human comfort — a place built to produce, not to house, where workers are components in a larger mechanism and the machinery's needs take priority over their own.

Properties.description:
Onyeka is built like a structural support column — six feet of dense muscle, mahogany skin cross-hatched with old scorch scarring along her left jaw and collarbone from a crowd dispersal incident she doesn't discuss. Her geneware irises cycle through amber and deep violet depending on her stress levels, a mod she got cheap and has never bothered upgrading despite the involuntary emotional readout it provides. Her hair is shorn close on the sides and kept natural on top, threaded with thin copper filaments that catch the light. Off-duty she moves slowly, almost gently, like something very large trying not to break things. On the line she becomes geometry — economical, angular, purposeful.

She is not cruel but she has made her peace with force. She genuinely believes in the maintenance of order as a social good, in the same way a levee believes in holding back water. What she doesn't examine closely is the question of who decides what 'order' means and whose chaos gets suppressed. She treats rookies with patient seriousness, older cynics with wary respect, and her commanding officers with a politeness that has no warmth in it at all.
Properties.role: Riot Suppression Specialist, Meridian 88 Metro Police
Properties.location: Fort Anchor, The Rampart deployment zone
Properties.narrative_function: Authority figure and moral obstacle; can become reluctant ally if players demonstrate they share her concern for civilian protection; source of Metro Police intel and internal politics; represents the complicated humanity inside institutions
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal impact mesh (torso and forearms, Metro Police-issued), geneware patterned irises (amber/violet stress-reactive), bone-density microlattice in wrists and knuckles (elective, paid out-of-pocket)
Properties.core_fears: becoming the kind of cop who enjoys the harm; the crowd she can't hold back
Properties.core_desires: to believe her work prevents more suffering than it causes; to be seen as someone who does hard things for good reasons
Properties.coping_mechanisms: ritualized gear maintenance as meditation; offering data-prayers to her shield's E.L.F. before deployments
Properties.blind_spots: consistently underestimates how much the uniform itself creates the violence she responds to; cannot see that her 'restraint' is still the tip of a system's spear
Properties.secret: During the Hough Reclamation riots three years ago, she held her line while a medic trying to reach a collapsed protester was pushed back by her unit. The protester died. The official report says the medic was never there. She still has the medic's badge number memorized.
Properties.story_hooks: She's been quietly collecting evidence of a commanding officer who has been ordering pre-emptive suppression of legal assemblies — she doesn't know what to do with it; The E.L.F. in her riot shield has started whispering names to her during deployments — names of people in the crowd who are about to be hurt
Properties.affiliation: Meridian 88 Metro Police, Riot Control Unit 7
Properties.vocabulary: Clipped, institutional, but precise — she knows the exact right word and uses it without decoration. Occasionally slips into older Yoruba-inflected phrases when emotional.
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, like she's issuing orders even when she isn't. Long pauses before answering questions.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want to tell me what you're doing at this checkpoint at 0300, or you want to make this harder than it needs to be.' | 'I'm not your enemy. Right now I'm a wall. You can push on a wall all you like — it doesn't make the wall your enemy.' | 'Ẹ jẹ ki a sọrọ — let's talk. Before this becomes something neither of us wants.'

Properties.description:
Orhan is a lean, angular man of middling height with a Sahel-boned face, his mother's warm brown complexion, and his father's flat Polish nose that he has always been vaguely self-conscious about. He keeps his head shaved to faint stubble and has a single cosmetic mod — a patterned iris modification that renders his pupils as slowly rotating geometric rings, a gift from a former partner he never got around to reversing. He wears his Ferrogate Transit uniform with the collar folded exactly one centimeter down, a minor unauthorized alteration he has maintained for six years without a single supervisor catching it. His cab smells of synthetic cardamom from the little flavor-diffuser clipped to his instrument panel, beside which sits a paper E.L.F. shrine — a folded transit map on which he has drawn the face of the Rail Spirit and which he taps three times at the start of every shift.

Orhan runs the same eighty-kilometer elevated loop eleven hours a day, five days a week, and has developed the unsettling ability to recognize regular passengers by the sound of their footsteps on the boarding platform. He is not unhappy — he finds the repetition genuinely meditative — but he is quietly, persistently lonely in a way he cannot quite name. He reads on his secondary screen during station dwells, always history or urban geography, and has an encyclopedic knowledge of Meridian 88's infrastructure that he has never found occasion to use. He is patient with passengers to a near-inhuman degree, only revealing irritation through a single slow blink.
Properties.role: Ferrogate Transit operator, Lake Loop elevated rail
Properties.location: Deepwell Station, operates the L-7 Lake Loop elevated line
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile information source — he sees everything that moves through the city at rail level; accidental witness; conduit for moving characters between districts; represents the invisible labor holding the city together
Properties.augmentations: Patterned iris mod (geometric rotating pupils, cosmetic only); standard Ferrogate neural link for cab integration (mandatory, employer-issued)
Properties.core_fears: Being indefinitely replaceable — that his particular presence on the loop means nothing; Missing something important happening outside the windows he can never stop to investigate
Properties.core_desires: A relationship that outlasts a rail season; To be asked, just once, what he actually knows
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Reading history as a way of feeling like events have shape and meaning; The shrine ritual at shift start; Counting station stops when anxious
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes people who seem calm are fine — misses distress that doesn't announce itself; Undervalues his own expertise because it was acquired passively
Properties.secret: Three years ago he watched, through his cab window, a Tessera executive being pushed off a platform at Lakeview Neon Station. He filed no report. The death was ruled a fall. He has the timestamp and cab-log footage auto-saved to a private drive he has never opened since.
Properties.story_hooks: A regular passenger stopped appearing six weeks ago; Orhan has quietly noted the exact date and the last thing she carried; His cab log from the night of the executive's death has been remotely accessed — and he can see in his system that someone knows he kept it
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit (Union Local 19)
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and measured, gravitates toward technical and geographic terminology, occasionally drops into unexpectedly poetic observation
Properties.cadence: Even and unhurried, long comfortable pauses, never interrupts
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Somewhere around the Grainfort curve, maybe 08:40 — I saw her. Same blue coat she wore every Thursday. That day she was running.' | 'The loop doesn't lie. Every delay has a reason. You just have to know what you're looking at.'

Properties.description:
Orinola is a broad-shouldered woman whose arms are ropey with muscle from decades of wringing, hauling, and pressing. Her skin is deep brown and perpetually damp at the temples, and she wears her silver-streaked hair pinned back under a waxed canvas cap. She has no dramatic augmentations — just a single subdermal temp-sensor strip along her left forearm so she always knows the water temperature without testing it by hand, a practical choice made thirty years ago and never regretted. Her face is a map of practical expressions: skeptical squint, satisfied nod, the slow blink she uses when someone is wasting her time.

She runs Szczepańska's Wash & Mend out of a narrow storefront that smells of lye, eucalyptus pressing compound, and the faint burnt-sugar scent of the seam-welder she uses for alterations. She knows every household in a four-block radius by the state of their laundry. She can tell you who is sick (strange smell, unwashed for two weeks), who just got lucky (dress shirts pressed three days in a row), and who is grieving (everything black, brought in without a word). She is not a gossip — she is a reader. There is a difference, and she will explain it to you firmly if you confuse the two.
Properties.role: Laundry operator and alterations service owner
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, Wash-Block 7 (a row of steam-vented stalls near the Enclave's main pedestrian artery)
Properties.narrative_function: Neighborhood oracle and information sieve — she knows everyone's business through their laundry and will share carefully selected observations with people she trusts. Quest giver for domestic disputes, missing persons in the Enclave, or anything that arrives in someone's pockets and shouldn't have.
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal temperature-sensing strip along left forearm (utilitarian, faded blue indicator light). No cosmetic mods.
Properties.core_fears: Her shop being seized by a corponation redevelopment zone; Outliving her usefulness to people who depend on her
Properties.core_desires: To be genuinely irreplaceable to her community; To one day retire without the community collapsing behind her
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Throws herself into physical work when anxious; Prays to Sudsa the boiler-E.L.F. in long, practical monologues
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much people actually like her — assumes all goodwill is transactional; Refuses to acknowledge her shop's finances are deteriorating
Properties.secret: She has been quietly subsidizing two families in the Enclave whose breadwinners died — laundering their clothes for free for over a year and telling them the machines are 'running a special.' She keeps a second set of books so no one discovers her charity.
Properties.story_hooks: A jacket came in with a sealed inner pocket she has never seen before — the owner hasn't returned for it in six weeks; The Enclave Small Operators Collective is being pressured to accept a Tessera 'partnership' deal that would effectively turn all their storefronts into franchise nodes — Orinola is the holdout and she needs allies
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loose member of the Hamtramck Enclave Small Operators Collective
Properties.vocabulary: Direct, practical Creole-inflected cadence with occasional Polish phrases absorbed from the neighborhood. Uses laundry and textile metaphors constantly without noticing.
Properties.cadence: Measured and unhurried; she never rushes a sentence any more than she rushes a rinse cycle
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Bring it before the smell sets, yes? After that, I am miracle-worker, not magician.' | 'You want to know about the Ferreiras? Look at their sheets. That tells you everything a conversation won't.'
