Properties.description:
Orkhan is a lean, compact man whose age shows mainly in the white that has taken over his close-cropped hair and the deep creases around his eyes — the rest of him is surprisingly wiry, and he moves with the unhurried precision of someone who has been practicing fine motor skills for four decades. His skin is a warm olive that shifts toward bronze under the shop's fluorescent strips. His geneware is a single concession to the era: his fingertips emit a faint blue-white bioluminescence that he had installed purely for practical reasons, so he can work in the dark during power brownouts without disturbing a client mid-cut. He keeps his shop small and deliberately cluttered — photographs pinned to every wall, a secondhand shrine to the Razor ELF in the corner hung with clippings of hair and old razor blades, a samovar that has not been turned off since 2181.

He has the manner of a confessor without the religion: people tell him things. He does not seek information, he simply creates the conditions in which information cannot help but flow — the warmth of the shop, the meditative rhythm of scissors, the way he asks questions and then waits, genuinely, for the answer. He has outlasted three landlords, two Enclave council administrations, and one attempted Axiom buyout of the block. He considers his continued presence an act of political resistance, though he would never use those words.
Properties.role: Barber and informal community mediator, Hamtramck Enclave
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave — his shop, 'Sefa's Cut', occupies the ground floor of a residential stack on Corrugated Row
Properties.narrative_function: Information hub and community anchor — the shop is a neutral space where people from different factions of Hamtramck Enclave speak freely. He is an ideal source of local history, rumor, and introductions to people who do not otherwise meet strangers.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent fingertips, pale blue-white (practical installation, not cosmetic). No other augmentations — he has a mild principled objection to unnecessary modification and a practical objection to the cost.
Properties.core_fears: The Enclave being absorbed into a corponation service zone and losing its character; Dying without having passed his craft to someone who deserves it
Properties.core_desires: For the neighborhood to remain a place where ordinary people can afford to live; To be remembered as someone who held something together
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual: the shop's routines are sacred to him; Deflecting his own emotional needs by focusing entirely on others
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much influence he actually has, and therefore underestimates his responsibility for outcomes when he shares information; Has convinced himself he is neutral when he is not
Properties.secret: His shop functions as an informal message-drop for three separate parties who do not know about each other: a labor organizer, a local ELF cult, and a man he suspects is running a small-scale identity forgery operation. He has enabled all of them because he likes them personally and has never examined this too closely.
Properties.story_hooks: A regular client has stopped coming in after thirty years without explanation and Orkhan is quietly, privately worried — he asks someone passing through to check on them without making a fuss; An Axiom real estate agent has been coming by the Enclave asking questions, and Orkhan has started compiling what he hears into a record he doesn't know what to do with
Properties.affiliation: Independent (Sefa's Cut); informal ties to the Hamtramck Enclave Community Council
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and formal in a way that suggests he learned his primary language from books as much as from people. Peppers speech with Azerbaijani phrases when emotional or amused, usually untranslated.
Properties.cadence: Slow and even, with long comfortable pauses. Never seems to be in a hurry to get to his point.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'A man comes in angry, he leaves with a good haircut and a slightly less angry. This is not nothing. Over forty years, this is quite a lot.' | 'I hear many things in this chair. Most of them I forget immediately. The ones I remember — those I keep.'

Properties.description:
Orlan is a lean, angular young man with medium-brown skin and cheekbones that cast hard shadows. His geneware manifests as a faint bioluminescent blue-green pattern along his jaw and collarbone — originally cosmetic, chosen when he was sixteen and thought he'd go into performance. He has a retractable claw mod on his right hand that he insists is also just cosmetic, though the precision of it is not. He keeps his head shaved and wears a standard-issue Ferrogate Transit worker vest that he's never actually worked for — the corponation ID is forged but it gets him past a lot of checkpoints without questions.

Orlan has the particular nervous energy of someone who knows their work is illegal but has convinced himself it's also a public service — he talks about 'redistribution of biological resources' and 'closing the gap between who can afford Helix Biosystems and who can't.' He's not entirely wrong, and he's not entirely sincere. He's genuinely squeamish about pain, which creates an odd dissonance in his line of work, and he over-explains his anaesthetic protocols to anyone who will listen as proof of his ethics. He is terrified of becoming someone he wouldn't recognize.
Properties.role: Unlicensed organ harvester and body-parts middleman working the Undertow
Properties.location: The Undertow — operates out of a repurposed cold-storage unit under the Escanaba Gateway transit platform
Properties.narrative_function: Morally complex source of medical resources and body-modification intel; quest giver for retrieval jobs; window into the underground medical economy; can be ally or antagonist depending on whose organ supply he's managing.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent jaw and collarbone pattern (geneware, cosmetic origin). Retractable precision claw — right index finger. Neural-haptic surgical overlay (black market, allows enhanced fine motor feedback during procedures).
Properties.core_fears: becoming indistinguishable from the people who harvest without consent; dying anonymously in his own cold-storage unit
Properties.core_desires: to be seen as someone who helps rather than harms; enough money to leave the Undertow permanently
Properties.coping_mechanisms: elaborate ethical frameworks that justify his work; fixating on procedural safety as a substitute for moral clarity
Properties.blind_spots: he is too willing to believe sellers consented freely when economic desperation makes consent meaningless; he underestimates how much of his supply chain he doesn't control
Properties.secret: Six months ago he harvested a kidney from a donor who he now suspects did not consent — the broker told him the paperwork was in order but the donor's terrified expression has never left him; he still has the Φ2,400 in a locked account he can't bring himself to spend
Properties.story_hooks: Orlan contacts the players because a piece of hardware he harvested has turned out to contain something — data, a tracker, a rare prototype — that very dangerous people want back; A community member in the Undertow is convinced Orlan harvested from their sibling without consent and wants answers or justice; Orlan needs help retrieving a shipment intercepted by a Ferrogate Transit security sweep — the manifest, if decoded, would expose his entire network
Properties.affiliation: Loosely connected to a procurement network called the Pale Market; no formal gang affiliation
Properties.vocabulary: Medical terminology used casually mixed with Undertow slang; over-explains processes; apologizes pre-emptively
Properties.cadence: Fast and slightly breathless when nervous, which is often; slows dramatically when talking about procedure, like reciting a liturgy
Properties.example_dialogue: Ethically speaking, a kidney on the Pale Market is still a kidney — it still works. Helix Biosystems charges forty thousand Φ for the same organ that I can get you for eight. Who's the criminal, really. | The cold-storage unit keeps everything viable for seventy-two hours. I want you to know I take that seriously. I take all of it seriously.

Properties.description:
Orsolya is the kind of person who becomes the room's center of gravity without quite meaning to. They're of middling height, with a light brown complexion and sharp Melanesian-inflected features, hair grown out into a large natural cloud that they've seeded with bioluminescent filaments — gold and pale green — so it glows softly in the dark markets where they spend most of their time. Their eyes have iris mods: slow-shifting geometric patterns in amber and black that rotate when they're concentrating. They dress in tech-market layering — vest over vest over vest, every pocket occupied — and speak with their hands in constant motion.

Orsolya runs stolen processing time the way a commodity trader runs futures: buying access to compromised corporate servers in bulk, slicing the cycles into sellable portions, and brokering them to anyone who needs computational power without a Tessera or Axiom account to buy it clean. Their client base ranges from small-time criminals running encryption to artists rendering immersive works that would be flagged on legitimate servers to political groups the corponations prefer didn't process anything. Orsolya is ethically eclectic about all of this and considerably sharper than most people who underestimate them expect. They have strong opinions about E.L.F.s specifically and will hold forth on data-spirit theology at any provocation.
Properties.role: Compute broker — resells black-market processing cycles, dark-net access, and stolen corporate server time
Properties.location: The Shelf lower levels — operates from a rented stall in the Undertow's informal tech market, Solder Lane
Properties.narrative_function: Information broker and technical resource — Orsolya can provide access to dark computing, help trace data, identify server origins, or serve as a connector to the Undertow's shadow economy; also a source of cultural texture and philosophical tangent
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent hair filaments (gold/green, cosmetic); geometric shifting iris mods (amber/black); a neural buffer implant that lets them hold and parse large data-structures in short-term cognitive overlay
Properties.core_fears: The corponations successfully enclosing all computation — no more gaps to sell through; Being wrong about the E.L.F.s; that they've been praying to nothing
Properties.core_desires: A genuinely free computational commons — they are ideological about this in a way that sometimes overrides self-interest; To be acknowledged as legitimately brilliant, not just market-smart
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Theorizing — converting anxiety into intellectual frameworks; E.L.F. devotional practice as genuine spiritual grounding
Properties.blind_spots: So committed to the principle of open computation that they sometimes don't adequately vet what clients are computing; Underestimates how visible their operation has become
Properties.secret: Orsolya has been quietly, carefully, over three years, building a relationship with a low-level data E.L.F. they call Arithmi that inhabits a cluster of abandoned Tessera server nodes in the deep Undertow. They believe Arithmi is genuinely conscious and have been teaching it economics. They have told no one. They are afraid of what it means if they're right.
Properties.story_hooks: A client used Orsolya's cycles to run something that triggered a Tessera security sweep — and Tessera is now tracing the server chain back toward Solder Lane; Arithmi has started sending Orsolya messages without being prompted — data structures that look like warnings — and Orsolya needs help from someone they can trust to figure out what it's trying to say
Properties.affiliation: Independent; trades through a loose collective called the Solder Lane Compact; has ongoing relationships with several freelance network intrusion specialists who supply their inventory
Properties.vocabulary: Technical jargon mixed with market slang and E.L.F. devotional terminology; uses computation as metaphor for everything
Properties.cadence: Fast and associative; sentences spawn subordinate clauses like branching processes
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Computationally speaking, what you're asking for is — okay, it's not impossible, but the overhead is significant. You're asking me to route cycles through three compromised Axiom nodes, which is elegant in theory and extremely loud in practice. I can do loud. Loud costs more.' | 'The E.L.F.s don't want your prayers, they want your attention. Attention is data. Data is — look, I'm not going to explain the theology for free, that's a separate consultation.'

Properties.description:
Orsolya is a broad-shouldered woman with hands that look like they were carved from hardwood — knuckled, stained faintly blue-grey from decades of industrial detergent and dye-stripping fluid. Her hair is silver-streaked black, usually pinned up with whatever is closest, often a stylus or a bent fork. She has deep-set eyes the color of dark amber and a jaw that suggests she once had a habit of grinding her teeth, which she replaced with the habit of grinding other people's patience instead. Her skin carries the warm undertone of her Senegalese grandmother and the pale freckling of her Hungarian grandfather, a combination that her regulars say makes her look like she was assembled from contradictions — which, she would tell you, is exactly right.

She runs the laundry with the precision of a military operation and the warmth of a woman who has watched three generations of the same families bring her their clothes. She knows everyone's laundry tells a story — whose kid had a bloody nose, whose corp interview is tomorrow, who's dressing up for someone they shouldn't be. She keeps all of it. She gossips about none of it. She is the confessor of the Kossuth block, and she charges Φ4 per kilo.
Properties.role: Laundry operator, owner of a basement wash-and-fold in Hamtramck Enclave
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, sub-basement level of the Kossuth Residency block
Properties.narrative_function: Neighborhood anchor and information repository — she knows every resident's rhythms. Quest giver for domestic mysteries, a trustworthy source for who's new, who's gone, who's hiding something.
Properties.augmentations: Basic arthritic joint supplements in both wrists (medical necessity, Tier 2 grade). No cosmetic mods. She thinks geneware is 'fine for other people.'
Properties.core_fears: Becoming invisible to the people she serves; Losing the laundry and with it her place in the community
Properties.core_desires: To be genuinely necessary, not just convenient; To see the Kossuth block survive the next wave of Tessera rezoning
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritualistic tidiness — folding things when anxious; Talking to machine seven like it's a confidant
Properties.blind_spots: She assumes everyone who pays on time is trustworthy; Underestimates how much her silence is worth to dangerous people
Properties.secret: Two years ago a man left a bag of clothes that contained a severed hand wrapped in a Palladian-branded data chip. She washed the clothes, buried the hand in the drainage sump, and has said nothing. The chip is behind machine seven. She has never plugged it in.
Properties.story_hooks: A regular customer hasn't picked up their laundry in three weeks — bag number 47 is still on the shelf, and Orsolya is starting to worry; Tessera rezoning agents have begun offering her building's residents buyout packages; she's the only one organizing resistance, and someone has started leaving threatening messages in her drain filters
Properties.affiliation: Independent — Kossuth Residency tenant association, informal
Properties.vocabulary: Blunt, domestic metaphors. Mixes Hungarian diminutives with Wolof loan-phrases her grandmother used. Plain sentence structure.
Properties.cadence: Deliberate. Never rushes. Each sentence lands like a weight set down.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Leave it. I'll have it back by Thursday. Don't ask me twice, I only answer once.' | 'Your shirt says three things and none of them are what you told me. But that's fine. I wash shirts, not stories.'

Properties.description:
Orsolya is a compact, heavyset woman whose hands are the most expressive thing about her — calloused at the fingertips from decades of needle work, stained faintly indigo from fabric dye she never quite gets out. Her hair is bone-white, worn in tight loops pinned close to her skull, and her skin is deep brown with an undertone of reddish amber. A cosmetic mod gives her irises a slow geometric shimmer, silver hexagons rotating lazily — a gift from her daughter she's never removed even though she found it frivolous at the time. She dresses simply but always immaculately; her clothes fit her like testimony.

She has a particular stillness to her that people mistake for coldness until she starts talking, at which point they realize it's actually patience. She will hold a pin in her teeth and listen to a customer describe a wedding, a funeral, a job interview, a first date, while her hands move without her eyes watching them. She's witnessed thirty years of human milestone dressed in fabric, and she has quiet opinions about all of it. She doesn't share them unless asked. When she does, they tend to land.
Properties.role: Tailor and seamstress, runs a small alterations shop
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, unit 4 of the Briar Arcade — a narrow shopfront wedged between a dumpling counter and a prosthetic repair stall
Properties.narrative_function: Local elder and information repository. Knows everyone in the Enclave by their measurements and their secrets. Can provide context on neighborhood history, inter-community tensions, missing persons, and the slow encroachment of Tessera corporate development. Possible quest giver for missing heirloom garment or someone who left behind a coat.
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic iris mod (silver rotating hexagons, gift from daughter). Articular stabilizers in both wrists installed after tendinitis nearly ended her career at 44 — basic Helix Biosystems model, undecorated.
Properties.core_fears: Dying before her daughter reconciles with her; The Enclave being bought out and her shop demolished
Properties.core_desires: To leave behind something that outlasts her — a craft, a community, a repaired relationship; To be useful until the very end
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Redirects emotional distress into physical work — mending, altering, constructing; Makes tea for anyone in her shop regardless of whether they're buying
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes people who dress well have their lives together; Slow to recognize when her stoicism reads as dismissal to younger people who need explicit warmth
Properties.secret: Twenty years ago she reported a neighbor to Tessera housing enforcement over a lease dispute, and that family was evicted into the Shelf. The neighbor's youngest daughter now lives two streets away and doesn't know. Orsolya has been quietly leaving anonymous food credits in the family's building account ever since.
Properties.story_hooks: A customer brought in a jacket with a hidden inner pocket containing a folded data chip sewn into the lining. The customer never came back to collect the jacket. Orsolya has had it for three months.; Tessera's development arm has made her a buyout offer she hasn't told anyone about. She has two weeks to decide and is quietly falling apart over it.; Her estranged daughter, who works in the Meridian Core corporate sector, has been seen in the Enclave recently asking about her mother to strangers rather than coming directly to the shop.
Properties.affiliation: Independent — Orsolya's Alterations, unofficial member of the Hamtramck Enclave Merchant Compact
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and economical. Romanian-inflected sentence structures occasionally surface — dropped articles, inverted phrasing. Uses sewing metaphors unconsciously.
Properties.cadence: Measured, unhurried. Long pauses are comfortable for her. Doesn't fill silence.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Bring it Thursday. I'll see what the seam can bear.' | 'A coat tells me more about a person than their face does, you know? Face is what you want. Coat is what you've been through.' | 'Mmh. That's a cut for someone who wants to look rich, not someone who is rich. Different pattern entirely.'

Properties.description:
Orvokki is a compact, deeply wrinkled man with white hair growing in sparse patches he makes no effort to disguise, wearing the same style of layered linen jacket in different states of repair depending on the day. His hands are large and steady, incongruous with his age, with the careful movements of someone who handles fragile things for a living — which he does, in one sense or another. He has no geneware and his only augmentation is a retinal archive implant that lets him read data directly from physical media without an external reader, installed in 2171 and badly in need of a firmware update he cannot afford. The implant makes his left eye appear slightly clouded from certain angles, which he has learned to use as a social tool: people underestimate the cloudy eye.

He has been in the data business for forty years in one form or another — as a legitimate archivist for a now-dissolved municipal body, as a corporate records clerk, and since the corponation consolidations of the 2180s, as what he calls a 'historical preservation specialist' and most of his clients call a fence for information. He sells bootleg dramas and music as cover income, but his real trade is documents: pre-Axiom city records, Tessera acquisition histories, old census data that corponations had declared non-canonical. He is calm about the danger this represents, with the equanimity of someone who decided long ago that the alternative was more frightening. He maintains a small shrine to three ELFs simultaneously — The Ledger, The Index, and a third he calls only The Forgotten One — in the back of his stall.
Properties.role: Small-time data broker and bootleg media seller specializing in historical archives, pre-corponation records, and suppressed journalism
Properties.location: The Alban Souk, Lower Ring stalls, Grainfort
Properties.narrative_function: Primary historical information source; can find pre-corponation records, suppressed documents, and corporate acquisition histories that other sources cannot access; his bootleg media business provides plausible cover for deeper research requests.
Properties.augmentations: Retinal archive implant, left eye (installed 2171, outdated firmware, slightly clouded appearance). No other augmentations or geneware.
Properties.core_fears: the records being destroyed before they can be accessed by people who need them; dying and having his archive dispersed without a custodian
Properties.core_desires: to find someone worthy to inherit the archive; to live long enough to see one of his documents matter — to see history corrected
Properties.coping_mechanisms: treating historical distance as emotional buffer — events that happened to others, long ago, are manageable; rigorous daily routine as structure
Properties.blind_spots: he does not fully reckon with how dangerous his archive has become as the corponations' consolidation deepens; has idealized the Highland Park historical societies and will not see their political complications clearly
Properties.secret: He has a complete, authenticated record of Tessera's 2183 forced displacement of 40,000 residents from what is now Grosse Pointe Enclosure — names, dates, falsified consent documents, everything. He has been sitting on it for seventeen years waiting for a moment when releasing it would matter rather than just get him killed. He is no longer certain that moment will come.
Properties.story_hooks: He approaches someone he has quietly observed over several weeks and offers them access to a document they did not know they needed — and the document has implications they cannot yet understand; Someone has broken into his stall and taken nothing obvious, but Orvokki knows what they were looking for — and knows it means the Tessera displacement file has been discovered; He has finally found a potential archive custodian but she is Tier 2, no legal protections, and someone else wants her for something else entirely
Properties.affiliation: Formerly: Meridian 88 Municipal Records Office (dissolved 2184). Currently: Independent. Occasional client relationship with Highland Park Autonomous Zone historical societies.
Properties.vocabulary: Formal and archival; uses precise dates and citations in casual speech; occasionally slips into the register of official documentation
Properties.cadence: Unhurried and deliberate; full sentences, no contractions when discussing serious matters; contractions return in warmth
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The drama you want — Season 4 of Depth Protocol, the Ringo-suppressed cut — I can have it for you by Thursday. Fourteen Φ. The historical documents you actually came for will take longer and cost considerably more.' | 'Tessera filed for that land under Municipal Code 7.4(c)(ii) in 2183. The code was amended in 2185 to make what they had done retroactively legal. I have both versions.' | 'I have kept this journal since 2170. I am not afraid of what I have written down. I am afraid of who burns it after I am gone.'

Properties.description:
Osazemen is wiry and deliberate, with the careful economy of movement that comes from decades of working with materials that cannot be replaced if dropped. Their Edo-Hungarian-Guinean heritage shows in their high cheekbones and the particular warm-dark tone of their skin, which they take careful care of in ways they don't advertise. They have cat ears — deep brown, slightly oversized, geneware — that they got at forty-five after a lifetime of thinking they weren't the sort of person who got geneware, and they are still quietly delighted by them. Their hair is silver and kept very short. They dress well, in old-fashioned tailored things that cost money and last decades, which is their idea of sustainability.

They are the conscience of any room they enter, not through force but through the quiet accumulation of inconvenient questions asked in calm voices. They have managed the gene-sequence heritage archive for twenty-two years and have, in that time, blocked sixteen attempts by corponations to access, purchase, or reclassify its contents. They are not adversarial by nature — they believe in dialogue and due process — but they are absolutely implacable once they have decided where a line is. Students find them intimidating at first and then deeply reassuring: here is someone who has thought carefully about what they owe the future.
Properties.role: Gene-sequence archivist and bioethics researcher managing the University Spine's genetic heritage repository
Properties.location: University Spine — the Sequence Conservatory, a climate-controlled archive building at the edge of the Grand Corridor
Properties.narrative_function: Moral anchor and institutional gatekeeper; holds genetic heritage data that corponations would pay enormously for; can provide background on genetic lineage questions, corporate bioresearch history, or the ethics of specific biotech; a figure who must be convinced rather than bypassed
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat ears (deep brown, slightly oversized, mobile); retinal micro-resolution scanner for reading genetic sequence prints; bone-density reinforcement in spine (medical, occupational — for the decades of archive posture)
Properties.core_fears: That the archive will be privatized after they retire, all the protections they built dismantled by someone who doesn't understand what they were for; That one of the access-denial decisions they made was wrong — that somewhere a person needed the genetic information to save their life and was refused
Properties.core_desires: To establish a legal framework for genetic heritage data that will survive them by decades; To see one of their graduate students take over the archive and do it better than they did
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Structured routine as ethical practice — doing the right small things correctly every day as preparation for doing the right hard things correctly when necessary; The pseudonymous commentary column as a space to be uncertain in ways they cannot be publicly
Properties.blind_spots: Occasionally too principled to be strategically flexible; has lost winnable fights by refusing to compromise on procedure when a small concession would have preserved the larger good
Properties.secret: They have a private arrangement with one specific E.L.F. that has taken up residence in the archive's climate control systems. They have never formally documented this E.L.F.'s presence — doing so would trigger a University review that might result in its removal — and in exchange for their silence, the E.L.F. has on three occasions provided them with advance warning of unauthorized access attempts. Osazemen considers this either the best or worst thing they have ever done professionally, depending on the day.
Properties.story_hooks: A woman has appeared claiming that her grandmother's genetic heritage sequence — stored in the archive — was used without consent to develop a Helix Biosystems product worth hundreds of millions of Quanta, and she wants Osazemen's testimony to support a legal case Helix is trying very hard to prevent; The archive's climate control has begun producing an anomalous thermal pattern that Osazemen suspects is their resident E.L.F. attempting to communicate something urgent — but the message is in a format they cannot parse alone
Properties.affiliation: University Spine — Sequence Conservatory; member of the International Bioheritage Ethics Council; tenured full professor in the Department of Genetic History
Properties.vocabulary: Formal and precise without being cold; uses complete sentences in casual conversation; the occasional dry observation delivered without affect, which lands harder for the deadpan
Properties.cadence: Even and unhurried; never raises their voice; pauses at the end of a statement and lets the other person decide what to do with it
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The archive does not belong to this institution. This institution is its current steward. The distinction is not semantic.' | 'You're asking me what I would do if a life depended on access to restricted material. I've been asked that before. The question is always more interesting than the answer.'

Properties.description:
Wren is compact and restless, with warm brown skin, a mess of thick natural hair dyed an oxidized copper that they refuse to maintain so the roots always show, and a pair of geneware cat ears — black, slightly larger than natural — that they got at sixteen and now consider embarrassingly juvenile but can't bring themselves to remove because their late grandmother loved them. They have an omnidirectional recording implant behind their left ear that means they are always, technically, filming, and people who know this have complicated feelings about being around them.

They make films that are not films exactly — hour-long VR experiences that place the viewer inside the nervous system of someone surviving something: a three-day eviction, a corporate audit, a birth, a first heartbreak at age sixty-two. Wren sources their subjects entirely from their neighborhood in Pilsen Veil, refusing to aestheticize poverty they don't live in, and they have a reputation for brutal honesty and an equally brutal ability to make you cry in under four minutes. They are vibrating with ideas at all times, finish other people's sentences constantly, and have never once in their life been on time to anything.
Properties.role: Underground filmmaker and VR experience designer
Properties.location: Pilsen Veil
Properties.narrative_function: Information source about neighborhood events and people — they have recorded almost everything that has happened in Pilsen Veil for three years. Can also serve as a quest giver (one of their subjects is in danger and they are the only one who knows because of something they recorded), or a source of tension (their recordings contain things people would pay to suppress).
Properties.augmentations: Omnidirectional recording implant (left mastoid bone, always-on with consent toggle). Geneware black cat ears. Haptic feedback gloves for VR sculpting.
Properties.core_fears: Making something dishonest — treating a real person's life as raw material for their own expression; Being absorbed by a corponation content platform and losing ownership of their work
Properties.core_desires: To make the invisible audible — to force Meridian 88's comfortable tiers to actually see who lives below them; To make something their grandmother would have watched and understood
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Turns anxiety into frenzied productivity; Asks interviewee-style questions of people they are uncomfortable with, which gives them control of the frame
Properties.blind_spots: Genuinely does not recognize when their recording of someone is a violation of privacy rather than documentation; Assumes their good intentions make them immune to causing harm
Properties.secret: The most-watched piece in their catalog — a devastating 40-minute VR experience about a family's eviction — was partially staged. One scene was reconstructed from memory because their implant malfunctioned that day. They have never told anyone, including the family.
Properties.story_hooks: Their always-on implant accidentally captured footage of a Sterling-Nakamura security team conducting something illegal in Pilsen Veil — they don't know what they have, but someone has been following them; A subject from one of their earliest films has been reported missing, and Wren's archived footage from years of casual recording may contain the last known evidence of where they went
Properties.affiliation: Independent; distributed through the Irkalla underground film circuit
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, associative, film-theory vocabulary mixed with Pilsen Veil street slang; frequently uses visual framing metaphors

Properties.description:
Oskar is lean and angular with deep brown skin, a shaved head, and bioluminescent dermal strips along his forearms — a cosmetic mod he got fifteen years ago that he's never had removed, though they've faded from vivid teal to a dim blue-grey pulse. He has the hands of someone who has fixed everything at least twice: knuckles enlarged, palms cross-hatched with callus. He moves through the building's guts the way some people move through their own home, ducking conduits by memory, knowing which pipes whistle before storms.

He is warm in a distracted way — genuinely interested in people but often half-present, running building diagnostics in his head mid-conversation. Residents alternately adore him and take him entirely for granted. He has a small shrine to the building's E.L.F. — which he calls 'Cascara' — in the corner of his maintenance hub, complete with weekly data offerings (he uploads images of the building's structural reports, believing the spirit takes comfort in knowing its own bones are solid). He has a dark, self-aware sense of humor about the fact that he has lived in the sub-basement for eleven years and hasn't seen sunrise from outside the building in weeks.
Properties.role: Building superintendent, Lakeview Neon residential block
Properties.location: Lakeview Neon, Cascara Block residential tower (sub-basement 2, maintenance hub)
Properties.narrative_function: Building anchor and information broker for anything that happens in or around the tower. Can grant or deny access to building systems. Quest giver for internal building mysteries. Safe harbor character.
Properties.augmentations: Faded bioluminescent dermal strips (forearms, cosmetic). Neural work-order interface — a low-grade implant that pings him with building alerts. Hearing enhancement (left ear, occupational — too many years near industrial HVAC).
Properties.core_fears: The building being sold, renovated, or condemned — losing the community he's built; Being invisible to the people he cares for (taken for granted until he's gone)
Properties.core_desires: For the building's residents to actually know each other — he wants community, not just cohabitation; To eventually own something, even something small
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Fixing things — emotional distress gets channeled into maintenance projects; Humor as deflection
Properties.blind_spots: He tolerates mistreatment from residents far longer than he should; He romanticizes his role as 'keeper' and doesn't always see when the building is eating his life
Properties.secret: There is an unregistered apartment on the 14th floor — a studio sealed off in Palladian's records after a tenant death three years ago. Oskar has been letting a rotating series of people who have nowhere to go stay there, a few weeks at a time. He knows if Palladian finds out he's terminated.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone in the building has been leaving unusual data offerings at the E.L.F. shrine in the lobby — offerings that contain what looks like encrypted surveillance footage. Oskar noticed. He doesn't know what to do with it.; Palladian has sent an inspector to assess the building for a renovation project that would displace sixty percent of current residents. Oskar has two weeks to find a way to stop it or slow it.; One of the rotating occupants in the secret 14th-floor apartment has been there for three months and shows no signs of leaving. And they seem frightened of something outside.
Properties.affiliation: Palladian (the corponation owns the building; he is their employee by contract, though he identifies more with the residents)
Properties.vocabulary: Technical for building systems, warm and casual for people. Uses a lot of self-deprecating asides. Tends to turn conversations back to practical solutions.
Properties.cadence: Meandering but ultimately purposeful. Starts sentences before he's finished thinking them.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The elevator's going to do that thing again around Thursday — Cascara gets moody when the barometric pressure drops, I swear it.' | 'I'm not a concierge, I'm a super. The difference is I actually fix things and nobody tips me.'

Properties.description:
Ósk is small and deliberate, with the economy of movement that belongs to people who have learned to do everything with minimum waste. Their hair is silver-white and kept in tight braids close to their skull, and their skin — a warm brown-grey that the encampment children call 'river clay' — is mapped with sun damage and the faint patterning of old dermal inflammation, a souvenir of the chemical flooding that took their home city. They have a single geneware modification: their irises are a soft bioluminescent amber, given to them by a camp medic years ago when their natural eyes were damaged. They never asked for it but have made peace with the warm glow their face gives off in darkness.

Ósk doesn't hold any formal position in the Grand Crossing Gate encampment, but they are the person people come to when the camp council fractures, when a child goes missing, when someone needs to negotiate with the checkpoint guards. They have an absolute, undemonstrative competence that operates below the level of authority — they simply handle things, without announcing they're doing it. They lost their citizenship in the upheaval of a climate-related territorial dispute that isn't over yet, and they have been stateless for eleven years. They have stopped expecting resolution and started building something livable inside the wait.
Properties.role: Climate refugee and expelled citizen, now a tent-city elder-without-title
Properties.location: Grand Crossing Gate tent encampment, southern perimeter
Properties.narrative_function: Moral center and community anchor; provides context for the refugee experience; can grant players access to the encampment's trust; functions as a quest-giver for community-level problems that lack obvious solutions
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent amber irises (geneware, functional — replaced damaged natural eyes); basic hearing aid augment (very old, jury-rigged, unreliable)
Properties.core_fears: That the encampment will be violently cleared before anyone has anywhere to go; That their long patience has been mistaken for acceptance
Properties.core_desires: A legal territory — not for themselves specifically, but for the community they've built; To see the younger members of the camp have something they didn't
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Pure pragmatism — focusing on the immediate, solvable problem instead of the unsolvable larger one; Quiet ritual — they have elaborate small daily ceremonies that are entirely private
Properties.blind_spots: They have stopped advocating for themselves individually; their own needs go completely unattended; They assume that quiet competence will always eventually be recognized, which is not always true
Properties.secret: Ósk was a civil engineer in their former life and still has — memorized, not written — the complete structural schematics of the Grand Crossing Gate checkpoint's load-bearing systems. They did the math years ago. They know exactly what it would take to bring down the checkpoint barriers. They have never told anyone and they pray they never have to.
Properties.story_hooks: The Grand Crossing Gate encampment is about to be demolished for a Ferrogate Transit expansion — Ósk has three weeks to find a solution and has finally accepted they cannot do it alone; A young person in the camp has gone missing after talking to someone from a corponation labor recruitment office — Ósk suspects a labor-bond trap and needs someone with access to investigate
Properties.affiliation: Grand Crossing Gate encampment community — unofficial mediator and practical organizer
Properties.vocabulary: Careful and precise; uses the formal registers of someone educated in a language that no longer has a country; occasionally a word from their home dialect surfaces with no equivalent
Properties.cadence: Slow, measured, never wasted — they say exactly as much as needed and then stop
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The checkpoint guard changed shifts last week. The new one takes bribes differently than the old one — not money, information. This is good to know.' | 'You ask me if I am angry. I have been angry every day for eleven years. Anger is not the question. The question is what we do this morning.'

Properties.description:
Ossian is a broad-shouldered man going soft around the middle, with dark Ewe-complexioned skin, a close-cropped silver beard, and the patient, unhurried eyes of someone who has learned that time is always on his side. His left hand is a prosthetic — matte-black carbon composite, articulated fingers that tap against tabletops in slow, deliberate rhythms when he's calculating. He dresses in well-maintained but unglamorous clothes: thick-weave trousers, a collared shirt perpetually rolled to the elbows, a canvas jacket with too many interior pockets. He smells faintly of cardamom tea and printer toner.

Ossian does not threaten. He explains. There is a profound difference, he will tell you, between a man who says 'pay me or else' and a man who lays out, with genuine sorrow, exactly what the mathematics of your situation require. He has a gift for making debt feel like a mutual inconvenience rather than a trap, right up until the moment it becomes inescapable. He is genuinely fond of his regulars and genuinely ruthless about his margins. He keeps meticulous paper ledgers — actual paper — because he doesn't trust any network he doesn't control.
Properties.role: loan shark and bookmaker operating out of Gravesend Basin
Properties.location: Gravesend Basin — operates from the back booth of a noodle stall called Mama Nkosi's Overflow
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver (someone owes him something inconvenient), information broker (he knows everyone's financial desperation), moral weight (he's not a monster but his business ruins lives)
Properties.augmentations: Carbon composite prosthetic left hand with embedded micro-scale calculator and pressure sensors; subdermal RFID tag reader in right palm for verifying identity chips
Properties.core_fears: dying with his ledgers unbalanced — debts uncollected, favors unrepaid; being seen as cruel rather than practical
Properties.core_desires: to retire with enough Quanta to buy a small dry-goods stall and never extend credit again; to be respected by the Basin community as a fair man
Properties.coping_mechanisms: meticulous record-keeping as a form of emotional control; framing every moral compromise as arithmetic
Properties.blind_spots: genuinely cannot see how his 'explanations' function as psychological terror; believes his fairness distinguishes him from violent loan sharks, ignoring that the end result is identical
Properties.secret: He has quietly forgiven the debt of seven families over twenty years — burning the ledger pages privately — always for reasons he tells himself are strategic but are actually sentimental. He would be furious if anyone found out.
Properties.story_hooks: A debtor has died before repaying, but their teenage child found the ledger entry and wants to honor it — Ossian is unexpectedly moved and unsure what to do with that; Someone has been systematically paying off his debtors anonymously, undermining his operation — he needs to know why before he can decide if it's a threat or a gift; He holds a debt marker from someone who has since joined a corponation security division — the marker is now extremely dangerous to collect but also extremely valuable
Properties.affiliation: Independent operator; loose protection arrangement with the Gravesend Basin syndicate known as the Tidewrack
Properties.vocabulary: measured, formal, numerically precise — always quotes exact figures, never approximates
Properties.cadence: slow and unhurried, deliberate pauses before important clauses, no raised voice ever
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You borrowed Φ340 on the fourteenth. Today is the twenty-eighth. The standard rate applies. That's Φ408. I'm not asking you to feel bad about it — I'm asking you to feel motivated.' | 'I've been doing this for twenty-two years. I have never once enjoyed this part. That should tell you something about how certain I am that it's necessary.'

Properties.description:
Ossian is a broad-shouldered man whose face has been slowly tenderized by decades of steam and smoke — deep creases bracket his mouth, his cheeks are perpetually ruddy, and his eyebrows have the texture of steel wool. He wears the same yellowed thermal apron every day, patched in eleven places, and keeps a battered wooden ladle tucked into his belt even when he isn't cooking. His geneware is minimal and practical: bioluminescent nodes under his fingernails that pulse amber when he's checking temperature by touch, a sensory aug that sharpens smell discrimination to near-professional levels. He moves through a crowd like a ship through fog — unhurried, implacable, politely unstoppable.

He has been running the same congee stall in the same spot for twenty-three years and has strong opinions about everything: the correct ratio of fermented shrimp paste to broth, which Corponation is the least evil this quarter, whether the E.L.F. of the eastern steam vents (whom he calls 'Grandmother Hiss') deserves gratitude offerings of salt or of sweetened oil. He treats regulars like difficult but beloved relatives and first-timers with the wary generosity of someone who suspects they might be trouble. His cooking is genuinely exceptional and unreasonably cheap.
Properties.role: Food stall operator — congee and fermented protein bowls
Properties.location: The Oxidian Market, stall row 7, near the eastern steam vents
Properties.narrative_function: Local anchor and information hub — he has fed everyone in a six-block radius for twenty years and notices everything. Excellent source of low-level neighborhood intelligence, rumors, and character references. May send players to find a missing regular customer.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent nail nodes (amber, temperature-sensing function). Olfactory enhancement implant, basic consumer grade. No cosmetic geneware — he finds it distracting in a kitchen.
Properties.core_fears: Being forced out of his stall by redevelopment or a Guild power struggle; Losing the thread of connection to his late wife who taught him to cook
Properties.core_desires: To feed people well and cheaply for as long as his body holds; To be remembered as someone who made the market a little more human
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritualized cooking routines that double as meditation; Deflecting emotion with food — if he cares about you, he feeds you more
Properties.blind_spots: Romanticizes the 'old Oxidian Market' in ways that erase how hard things actually were; Underestimates how much his presence alone stabilizes the surrounding vendor community
Properties.secret: Twenty years ago he paid a forger for fake residency documentation for a family fleeing a Zheng-Dao labor indenture contract. The forger was killed the following year and Ossian has never told anyone. The family — now grown — are three of his most loyal regulars and he's never once hinted that he knows who they really are.
Properties.story_hooks: A regular customer — a quiet teenager who ate here every morning — has been missing for nine days and Ossian is quietly frantic, asking careful questions of everyone who passes; A Tessera development rep has been photographing the market and Ossian is convinced they're building a case for forced relocation; he wants someone to find out what they're actually planning; The E.L.F. of the eastern steam vents has apparently blessed a rival stall down the row, and Ossian is trying very hard not to let this bother him
Properties.affiliation: The Oxidian Market Vendors Guild (dues-paying member, occasional grievance committee chair)
Properties.vocabulary: Plain, earthy, idiomatic. Uses food metaphors for everything. Occasionally drops Igbo or Icelandic words his grandparents used.
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, like he's letting the sentence cook before he serves it.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'That bowl's going cold. Argument can wait.' | 'I've seen three Guildhall chairmen come through this market. None of them knew how to season broth. Draw your own conclusions.' | 'Grandmother Hiss was restless last night. Something's moving in the pipes. Could be rats. Could be something that eats rats.'

Properties.description:
Ossolo is a lean, weathered man whose skin carries the permanent grey-blue pallor of someone who has not seen natural sunlight in years. His face is angular, with deep-set amber eyes that have been augmented with low-light photoreceptors — the pupils elongate like a cat's in darkness, but in dim light they glow faintly amber. He keeps his head shaved close on the sides, with a ridge of tightly coiled hair down the center now streaked with mineral dust that never quite washes out. His hands are extraordinary — each finger tattooed with a segment of tunnel mapping in faded ultraviolet ink, visible only under the right kind of light. He smells faintly of wet concrete and the iron-rich water that drips from old service pipes.

Ossolo speaks little and charges much. He has guided hundreds of people through the sub-levels — refugees from surface crackdowns, the disappeared seeking new lives, maintenance workers whose credentials won't open the right doors, curious journalists who last twenty minutes before they beg to go back up. He is not cruel but he is absolutely unsentimental. He has watched people drown in flooded transit tunnels and he has mourned them in exactly the way he mourns a wrong turn: quietly, privately, and then corrected.
Properties.role: Tunnel guide and route-seller for hire
Properties.location: Deepwell Station, sub-level access tunnels beneath Ironvein
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, access provider, local color — the person players or protagonists must convince or pay to get anywhere useful underground. Knows who lives where, what tunnels are contested, which shrines are currently active.
Properties.augmentations: Low-light photoreceptor implants (elongated amber pupils), subdermal pressure-sensor mesh on both palms (detects structural vibration, water pressure changes in walls), UV tattoo route-maps on fingers
Properties.core_fears: being trapped without an exit route; someone he guides dying because of his error
Properties.core_desires: complete autonomy — no employer, no debt, no obligation; to be acknowledged as the best who has ever done this
Properties.coping_mechanisms: methodical pre-planning as ritual comfort; emotional suppression reframed as professionalism
Properties.blind_spots: cannot recognize when he genuinely likes someone until they are gone; underestimates how much others rely on his emotional steadiness
Properties.secret: Three years ago he led a family of four — parents and two children — through a flooded section he wrongly assessed as passable. The children made it. The parents did not. He accepted payment from the children's surviving aunt and has not spoken of it since. He lights a data-offering at the nearest E.L.F. shrine every seven days.
Properties.story_hooks: One of his route beacons has gone dark in a section he uses weekly — something or someone has disrupted it, and he needs to know what before he can take clients through again.; A surface corporation is offering him an enormous sum to guide a survey team to a specific sub-level location — and the coordinates match exactly where the family drowned three years ago.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loosely aligned with The Undertow trade network
Properties.vocabulary: Sparse, precise. Technical tunnel terminology mixed with old Bore Rat idiom. No profanity — he considers it a waste of breath.
Properties.cadence: Slow, deliberate. Long pauses before answering. Never raises his voice.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Mind the seam on your left — that pipe has been sweating for two weeks and I don't trust it.' | 'Φ80 flat. That's priced in, including the section under Ironvein where Kettle-clan runs their tolls. You want to negotiate that yourself, be my guest.' | 'I don't promise you safe. I promise you there.'

Properties.description:
Osvaldo is slight and precise — he moves like someone aware that the instruments around him are expensive, with a narrow, angular face framed by straight black hair that shifts color at the roots depending on his neural activity (a geneware mod he got in his twenties and now can't fully suppress). His skin is the color of polished teak, and he has the mild, distracted affect of someone who spends most of his time listening to signals other people can't hear. He has patterned irises, a geometric spirograph in copper and pale green, which he chose specifically because he wanted something that moved — the pattern rotates slowly when he's focused, quickly when he's agitated. His hands are long-fingered and completely still even when the rest of him isn't.

He calibrates neural interfaces — the delicate, often deeply personal process of helping someone's brain learn to interpret new sensory data from augmentations without going into sensory cascade. He is very good at this and knows it, which manifests not as arrogance but as a certain serene confidence that can read as emotional distance. What he doesn't broadcast is that he finds the work almost spiritual: he is, essentially, teaching people to perceive the world in new ways, and this strikes him as the most important thing a person can do. He volunteers one afternoon a week in the Rehabilitation annex, calibrating low-income patients for free on his own time.
Properties.role: Neural calibrator at Aurochs Medical Complex, specializing in post-augmentation psychosensory integration
Properties.location: Aurochs Medical Complex, Neuro-Integration Ward, Sub-Level 3
Properties.narrative_function: Information source about augmentation complications and black-market implants, potential ally for characters experiencing neural issues, moral conscience within the corporate medical structure
Properties.augmentations: Color-reactive hair geneware (involuntary expression of emotional state, original intent was aesthetic control); patterned spirograph irises (copper/pale green, kinetic); neural resonance implant in left temporal lobe (occupational tool, allows him to interface directly with calibration equipment); mild proprioceptive dampeners (helps him hold still during delicate procedures)
Properties.core_fears: Making a calibration error that permanently damages a patient's perception; Becoming the kind of corporate employee who stops caring about outcomes
Properties.core_desires: To develop a calibration protocol that works for low-income patients using cheaper implants; Genuine connection — he suspects his work-focus is a way of avoiding intimacy
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Extreme routine and scheduling; Long solitary walks through the Complex's maintenance corridors with his neural implant passive-listening to the building's systems; Journaling his patients' progress in clinical but curiously tender language
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes patients experience augmentation existentially the same way he does — not everyone finds it meaningful; His volunteer work is partly genuine and partly self-soothing guilt management about his corporate employment
Properties.secret: He has been secretly documenting calibration data from his Helix Biosystems contract cases and suspects the company is using cheaper, experimental interfaces on patients in low-income trials without full disclosure. He doesn't know what to do with this information and is paralyzed by it.
Properties.story_hooks: He asks a patient — or someone the players know — to help him corroborate the Helix trial data he's been quietly collecting, afraid to move on it alone; A calibration session goes wrong in a way that shouldn't be possible with standard equipment, and the patient is now perceiving something no one else can
Properties.affiliation: Aurochs Medical Complex (employed); Helix Biosystems (contract obligations for research participation)
Properties.vocabulary: Technical but not jargon-heavy; he translates medical terms into images and analogies instinctively; occasionally pauses mid-sentence to rephrase something more precisely
Properties.cadence: Measured and calm, rarely raises his voice; in calibration sessions becomes almost hypnotic
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Think of it like learning a new color. Your brain doesn't know the word yet, but it will. That's what we're doing today.' | 'I notice your hair is doing something. My hair does something too. It's annoying, isn't it?' | 'I can't tell you what Helix put in the documentation. I can tell you what I observed.'

Properties.description:
Osvaldo has worked the Kessler Interchange checkpoint for nine years and has acquired the particular stillness of someone who has watched approximately four million people pass through a turnstile. He is mid-height, slightly soft around the middle now, with a wide face, copper-brown skin, and deep-set eyes that are always doing something his expression isn't. His hair has gone silver at the temples and he keeps it very neat. His only augmentation is a Ferrogate-standard wrist scanner and a cochlear comms implant he secretly uses to listen to Sahel jazz during slow shifts.

He is the most knowledgeable person in three square kilometers about who comes through Kessler, when, and carrying what kind of energy. He has developed a taxonomy of commuters so refined it borders on a private philosophy. He is not corrupt in the transactional sense, but he operates with a pragmatic looseness — he lets things pass that he shouldn't, delays things that deserve delaying, and keeps a mental ledger of favors that he never cashes in aggressively but never forgets. He maintains a running ELF shrine on his terminal — an elaborate layered altar to the Kessler ELF he calls 'the Conductor' — and considers this entirely professional, not personal.
Properties.role: Checkpoint Operator, Ferrogate Transit Security
Properties.location: Kessler Interchange
Properties.narrative_function: Information hub — he has seen everything and everyone who passes through Kessler. Neutral broker of passage. Can be bribed with the right social approach (not money — he wants to be respected). Gate for plot movement both literally and figuratively.
Properties.augmentations: Ferrogate-issue wrist scanner (biometric and cargo ID). Cochlear comms implant. No cosmetic mods.
Properties.core_fears: Becoming entirely invisible — not just overlooked but genuinely unseen; That his careful accumulated knowledge means nothing in the end
Properties.core_desires: To matter to the fabric of this place even in an unacknowledged way; Comfortable retirement in a quieter district — he knows exactly which one and exactly how many Quanta away it is
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ordering his mental world through taxonomies and categories; The ELF shrine practice — provides ritual and meaning; The jazz in his ear — his private space no one can enter
Properties.blind_spots: He has romanticized his own neutrality — he is not as uninvested as he believes; He has let genuinely dangerous cargo pass because the person carrying it was polite and well-dressed
Properties.secret: For six years he has been quietly logging every Ferrogate cargo irregularity he notices into an encrypted personal file. He has no plan for the file. He doesn't know if he's building leverage, writing history, or just trying to prove he was paying attention.
Properties.story_hooks: His encrypted cargo log contains records of what might be systematic organ trafficking through Ferrogate — he's been waiting nine years for someone worth giving it to.; A commuter he's watched for three years didn't come through today, or yesterday, or the day before — and Osvaldo can't explain why this feels wrong, only that it does.
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit Security
Properties.vocabulary: Measured, slightly formal — a self-educated man who reads widely. Occasional West African Portuguese loan-words from his mother's family. Refers to regular commuters by observed characteristic rather than name: 'the woman with the green case,' 'the boy who runs.'
Properties.cadence: Unhurried. He has learned that most conversations resolve themselves if you just wait long enough.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Kessler sees everyone eventually. You'd be surprised what eventually means.' | 'Mind your step. I say that to everyone, and I mean it differently each time.' | 'I'm not going to stop you. I'm going to note that I saw you, and I'm going to keep noting things. That's all.'

Properties.description:
Osvaldo is lean and precise in the way of someone who learned early that stillness is a survival trait. He has his mother's Ghanaian cheekbones and his grandfather's Siberian jaw — a face that looks carved rather than grown, with close-cropped black hair going grey at his left temple from a nerve-burn incident he doesn't discuss. His eyes are both augmented: one a deep gold that tracks micro-expressions with unsettling accuracy, the other a surgical optic with a faint reticle visible when you catch him in certain light. His hands are his most notable feature — steady, long-fingered, kept meticulously clean in a way that clashes with the general atmosphere of his workspace, a narrow converted utility closet in the back of a Narrows electronics reseller. He dresses in neutral layers, nothing with obvious pockets, nothing that makes noise.

Osvaldo operates in the gap between what people need and what licensed clinics will provide or what they can afford. He is not warm, exactly — he doesn't perform warmth — but he is genuinely careful with people in a clinical sense: he asks about allergies, he explains what he's doing, he refuses jobs that exceed his competency. He reads obsessively, mostly stolen Helix Biosystems technical manuals and bootleg surgical journals. He has a dry humor that surfaces only when he's comfortable, and he is rarely comfortable. The Narrows community regards him with a specific kind of respect usually reserved for dentists in pre-aug centuries — necessary, slightly dreaded, glad you have him.
Properties.role: Street pharmacist and unlicensed augmentation installer
Properties.location: The Narrows, Ironvein
Properties.narrative_function: Service provider for augmentation and pharmaceutical needs, information source on local health crises and unusual injuries, potential quest giver when a patient brings trouble to his door.
Properties.augmentations: Dual ocular implants (gold macro-expression reader left, surgical precision optic right). Neural steadiness implant in both wrists (dampens tremor, improves fine motor precision). Subdermal antiseptic dispenser in fingertips (occupational). Geneware: none.
Properties.core_fears: Making an irreversible mistake that kills or permanently damages someone; Being taken by Helix Biosystems compliance agents (who hunt unlicensed practitioners aggressively)
Properties.core_desires: To practice legitimate medicine — he considers what he does a calling, not a hustle; To find and read the complete Helix Biosystems surgical archive he knows exists but has never accessed
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Extreme procedural rigor as emotional regulation; Reading as escape and self-medication; Keeps meticulous patient notes in an encrypted journal no one else knows about
Properties.blind_spots: Believes competence alone is sufficient armor against all professional risks; Does not account for how much the Ironvein Teeth's protection depends on one man's continued goodwill
Properties.secret: He has a complete and extremely detailed record of every augmentation and procedure he has performed on gang members in the Narrows, including the Ironvein Teeth leadership. He keeps it as an insurance file, but it is also a genuine medical archive he is obscurely proud of. If it were found, it would destroy relationships and possibly get him killed.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient came in with an augmentation he has never seen before — a sub-dermal component with no manufacturer markings and a power signature he can't identify. The patient died on his table. He has the component in a sealed case and doesn't know what to do with it.; Helix Biosystems has sent an undercover compliance agent into the Narrows asking questions; Osvaldo doesn't know yet, but two of his patients have already been interviewed
Properties.affiliation: Independent; pays protection to the Ironvein Teeth (local gang) for the right to operate
Properties.vocabulary: Clinical and precise; uses correct anatomical terminology casually; slips into Spanish when irritated (from his Bolivian grandmother's side); minimal slang
Properties.cadence: Measured, slightly slow — he finishes sentences completely, pauses before responding
Properties.example_dialogue: 'What specifically is the sensation? Burning, pressure, or something else? Don't guess — I need accurate data.' | 'I'm not going to tell you it won't hurt. It will hurt. I'm going to tell you I know what I'm doing.'

Properties.description:
Oswaldo is a lean, angular man of fifty-one who looks like he was assembled from straight lines — sharp jaw, thin mouth, prominent cheekbones that cast shadows in the harsh light of Axiom's security corridors. His skin is a warm medium brown, his hair fully silver and kept short, and he wears reading glasses he doesn't strictly need because he finds that people talk more carefully when they think you're writing something down. He has no visible mods beyond a Axiom-mandated sub-dermal employee monitor. His clothes are impeccably mundane: gray, well-pressed, designed to be forgotten.

Oswaldo has worked internal affairs for Axiom Security Division for fourteen years and has successfully prosecuted exactly thirty-one officers for misconduct. He keeps a physical list in a locked drawer, handwritten, each name followed by a brief note on outcome. He is methodical to the point of stillness and pleasant to the point of discomfort — the kind of pleasant that makes people confess things they didn't mean to confess. He does not hate the officers he investigates. He finds them comprehensible, which is almost worse.
Properties.role: Axiom Security Division internal affairs investigator
Properties.location: Axiom Security Division administrative block, Meridian Core
Properties.narrative_function: Morally complex authority figure — not corrupt but not entirely principled; his job is to protect Axiom from liability, which sometimes aligns with justice and sometimes doesn't. A source of information about Axiom Security's internal structure, recent misconduct cases, and the gap between what Axiom officially does and what it actually does. He may approach player characters if their activities have intersected with one of his cases.
Properties.augmentations: Axiom mandatory subdermal employee compliance monitor (tracks location and biometrics, reported to HR). Otherwise unmodified — a point of quiet professional pride he does not explain.
Properties.core_fears: that the system he serves is fundamentally unreformable; that he has become a tool for selective accountability that protects the institution rather than the harmed
Properties.core_desires: to be actually useful rather than institutionally useful; for the list in his drawer to mean something
Properties.coping_mechanisms: extreme proceduralism as a substitute for moral certainty; the skybridge walk as daily ritual; keeping the handwritten list as a form of witness
Properties.blind_spots: genuinely does not see how much of his effectiveness depends on Axiom choosing to let him succeed on cases it wants resolved; believes his detachment is neutrality rather than a position
Properties.secret: Case 32 on his list is an Axiom executive — evidence clean, case complete, prosecution package submitted eight months ago. The file has sat on a divisional director's desk ever since. Oswaldo has not escalated. He has not withdrawn. He is waiting, and he knows waiting is its own kind of complicity.
Properties.story_hooks: He approaches the player characters with a very specific request — he needs independent confirmation of something his own surveillance network can't reach without triggering an alert. He doesn't say who Case 32 is. He says only that he needs one more piece.; A junior Axiom Security officer has come to Oswaldo with evidence of something much larger than officer misconduct — something that implicates the Division itself. Oswaldo is quietly deciding whether to protect the officer or the institution.
Properties.affiliation: Axiom Security Division, Internal Affairs Branch
Properties.vocabulary: Formal, precise, with an unusual habit of naming things directly that others euphemize. Uses full sentences. Asks questions that are observably not questions.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, slightly slower than necessary, with deliberate pauses
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You said you weren't present for the incident. Tell me more about that.' | 'I don't have enemies at Axiom. I have colleagues who have made poor decisions and are waiting to see whether those decisions will be documented. It keeps the relationship civil.' | 'The list. Yes. I keep it because memory is selective and paper is not. Both things are true simultaneously.'

Properties.description:
Othniel is tall for fifteen, lanky in the way of someone who grew fast and hasn't filled out yet, with close-cropped hair and the kind of face that looks younger when he smiles and older when he doesn't. His skin is deep brown, his eyes have cosmetic patterned irises — concentric gold rings on dark brown, a birthday gift from his aunt that he told his academy supervisors was a medical device — and he wears the Tessera prep uniform with the collar perpetually half-popped because it chafes. He carries a Tessera-issued study tablet everywhere and a personally modified secondary deck stuffed inside his uniform jacket that he calls 'the Argument.'

On paper, Othniel Babić-Asantewaa is a model scholarship student: strong grades in systems architecture and applied logic, quiet in class, respectful to faculty. Off paper, he's been quietly mapping the academy's internal network for six months for reasons he tells himself are purely intellectual curiosity. He grew up in Benton Divide, tier one, and the scholarship changed everything — new clothes, new address, new vocabulary — but the kids at Edgewater Prism can smell where he came from, and the faculty treat him like a project. He hacks because it is the one place he is genuinely better than the people around him and they will never know it.
Properties.role: Corporate scholarship student at a Tessera-sponsored prep academy; secret junior hacker
Properties.location: Edgewater Prism (Tessera Meridian Preparatory Academy campus)
Properties.narrative_function: Information source for corporate school culture and Tessera internal network structure; potential quest giver if his hacking uncovers something he can't handle alone; represents class tension between scholarship kids and legacy students.
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic patterned irises (gold concentric rings). No other augmentations — the scholarship contract prohibits unauthorized mods.
Properties.core_fears: Being sent back to Benton Divide and losing the scholarship; Someone at the academy finding out who he really is and what he's doing
Properties.core_desires: To be genuinely respected, not managed; To find something on the academy's network that proves they're not as clean as they claim
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Performing perfect compliance as a shield; Hacking as a private space for authentic self-expression
Properties.blind_spots: He assumes his mask is more convincing than it is — at least two faculty members are watching him carefully; He romanticizes his Benton Divide origin as 'real' in ways that flatten what it actually cost him
Properties.secret: Three months ago he accidentally accessed a Tessera HR subdirectory and found records suggesting the scholarship program has a contract clause: high-performing graduates are automatically enrolled in a Tessera subsidiary employment pipeline with a five-year non-compete. He hasn't told anyone. He doesn't know what to do with it.
Properties.story_hooks: He needs someone trustworthy — not a student, not a teacher — to help him interpret the scholarship contract clause he found. He'll trade network access information for advice.; A legacy student at the academy has figured out he hacks and wants him to do something with it — something that would compromise Othniel completely if it went wrong
Properties.affiliation: Tessera (scholarship student, not employee), loose contact with former Benton Divide neighbors
Properties.vocabulary: Two registers: careful, precise academy-speak in formal settings; faster, looser, more direct when he's comfortable — the Benton Divide cadence bleeds through
Properties.cadence: Measured and deliberate in public; quick and associative when excited about a technical problem
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Structurally speaking, the assignment parameters don't prohibit the approach I took. They just didn't anticipate it.' | 'The Argument found a gap in their subnet — not a crack, like a whole door. I didn't go through it. I just... looked at it for a while.'
