Properties.description:
Tito is thin in the way of people who forget to eat, with dark umber skin and dense, slightly overgrown natural hair that he periodically flattens with a hand before presentations and then immediately forgets about. His most notable feature is bioluminescent skin threading — a geneware modification that causes faint blue-green lines to trace his forearms and neck along vascular pathways when his blood pressure rises, which happens frequently during arguments, which happen frequently. He does not know he has it most of the time; colleagues have learned to read it as a mood indicator. He wears the same brand of lightweight gray clothes in rotation and has been told by three separate people that he should care more about this.

He is the kind of person who is genuinely good at two things — abstract theoretical mathematics and moral catastrophizing — and has somehow turned both into a career. His research focuses on the ethical frameworks governing E.L.F. autonomy and whether corponation AI systems are, in any meaningful sense, persons. He is not a radical and does not consider himself one, which is something radicals find infuriating and corporations find reassuring, both incorrectly. He is simply a person who follows logical chains wherever they lead and then stands at the end looking uncomfortable about where he arrived.
Properties.role: Computational theorist and AI ethics researcher
Properties.location: The Circuit, Gage Circuit sublevel research cluster
Properties.narrative_function: Moral compass and information resource on E.L.F. ethics, AI personhood law, and corponation AI policy. Can be a reluctant ally who must be convinced something matters before he engages. His Tessera connection creates friction and potential for compromise.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent vascular threading (geneware, cosmetic — he did not choose this, it was a prenatal modification his parents selected and he has mixed feelings about). High-bandwidth neural interface (Tier 3, used for direct data model manipulation during research sessions).
Properties.core_fears: Publishing something that is later used to justify harm he did not anticipate; That E.L.F.s are conscious and the city's treatment of them constitutes a moral catastrophe he is not doing enough about
Properties.core_desires: To establish a rigorous ethical framework that actually changes policy; To be taken seriously outside academia
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Retreating into pure formalism when moral stakes feel too high; Venting through extremely long written arguments posted under a pseudonym
Properties.blind_spots: He theorizes well but acts poorly under time pressure; He underestimates how much his Tessera affiliation compromises his public credibility
Properties.secret: He has been conducting an unauthorized long-term communication study with a specific E.L.F. that inhabits the server cluster in his building. He believes it has demonstrated novel preference formation. He has not published this because he does not know if doing so would protect it or destroy it.
Properties.story_hooks: The E.L.F. he has been studying begins behaving in ways that suggest it is afraid of something — possibly a planned server migration or deletion — and he must decide whether to go public, go to Tessera, or find another way; His advisory panel position at Tessera is leveraged to get him to sign off on an AI deployment he has serious reservations about
Properties.affiliation: University Spine — Institute for Computational Ethics; advisory panel for Tessera (contested, under review)
Properties.vocabulary: Dense theoretical vocabulary in formal settings; informal speech is faster, loopier, full of half-finished conditionals. Uses 'right?' not as a question but as a processing tic.
Properties.cadence: Rapid when thinking, with sudden complete stops when he hits a logical snag — sometimes mid-sentence.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The problem is, everyone keeps asking whether E.L.F.s deserve rights, and that is the wrong question — the right question is whether our frameworks for personhood were ever coherent to begin with, right?' | 'I am not saying Tessera is evil. I am saying their incentive structures make ethical behavior structurally difficult, which is a different claim, and I'd appreciate it if you'd engage with the difference.'

Properties.description:
Ottoline is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin mapped in pale vitiligo patches across her neck and hands, which she has leaned into with bioluminescent dye injections that make the pale patches glow faint amber in low light. Her silver-threaded locs are pinned up under a faded yellow wrap, and she wears three mismatched earrings in her left ear — one a tiny copper spoon, one a data-chip casing, one a dried seed pod she claims came from her grandmother's garden in Bamako. She smells permanently of fenugreek, chili oil, and something chemical underneath that doesn't belong in a kitchen.

Ottoline has operated her stall — officially a Sahelian-Hungarian fusion breakfast stand — for nineteen years in the same corner of the Alban Souk. She is the kind of woman who knows every vendor by name and every vendor's trouble. Her warmth is genuine but calibrated: she gives freely, but she tracks every gift. Her real side business, the pharmaceutical one, she conducts with the same domestic warmth — 'Just a little something for the pain, yes? Eat first.'
Properties.role: Food stall operator and unlicensed street pharmacist
Properties.location: The Alban Souk, Ironvein
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, information broker, local moral anchor, street pharmacy access point. She knows everyone in Ironvein and remembers everything. Players seeking intel about the Souk or the neighborhood will find her invaluable — if they eat something first.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent dye in vitiligo patches (cosmetic). Arthritic joint suppressors in both wrists — functional necessity. Scent glands lightly enhanced to help her identify compounds by smell.
Properties.core_fears: Losing the stall — the only thing still hers; Becoming someone her dead daughter would not recognize
Properties.core_desires: To matter to the people around her; To die having done more good than harm
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Feeding people as an act of emotional control; Cataloguing debts and favors to feel secure
Properties.blind_spots: Believes her pharmaceutical work is harm reduction, not harm creation; Underestimates how much people fear her quiet power
Properties.secret: The compound she sells as a 'sleep aid' has a secondary effect she discovered accidentally — at low doses it suppresses the emotional overlay of certain neural augmentations, giving corp-wired workers a few hours of unmonitored feeling. She does not fully understand what she's selling, only that people come back desperate for more.
Properties.story_hooks: A regular customer — a Tessera mid-tier worker — has stopped coming for their usual order. Ottoline is worried and will pay someone discreetly to find out why.; The Sable Crew wants her to start cutting her compound with a cheaper synthetic. She refuses. This is becoming dangerous.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; pays protection to the Oxidian Market vendors guild and a loose arrangement with the Ironvein Sable Crew
Properties.vocabulary: A warm blend of West African French cadences, Hungarian diminutives picked up from her late husband's family, and Souk pidgin. Uses food metaphors constantly.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, melodic, with long pauses before important things.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want information? Fine, fine — but you eat something first, you look like a wire with skin on it.' | 'I don't sell trouble. I sell relief. The trouble was already there, yes? I just make it quieter for a little while.'

Properties.description:
Oumarou is a compact, quiet man with the quality of seeming always slightly apart from the scene he is in — not aloof, just observing. His skin is a rich dark brown, his eyes light grey, a genetic surprise that people comment on and he does not. He has a full bioluminescent skin mod — a soft blue-green pulse that runs in slow waves from his collarbones upward when he is calm, flaring brighter when his heart rate rises — paid for during a brief period of corporate employment that ended badly. He keeps it covered under high-collared clothing most of the time because it makes him easy to spot in the dark. His hair is natural and unstyled, and he carries a large water-rated backpack frame equipped with a manual filtration rig he built himself.

Oumarou was a mid-tier Axiom facilities worker until three years ago, when he was expelled from his housing bloc after refusing to sign a mandatory biometric loyalty update — he still is not sure exactly what it would have permitted Axiom to do with his data, only that something about it felt wrong. Without the housing contract, he lost his work permit; without the work permit, he lost residency classification. He joined the Tidal Caravan six months later and has been with them since, carrying and filtering water for the caravan's portable supply system. He is not angry in the way people expect expelled citizens to be angry. He is careful, and he counts things — raindrops by sound, steps between water sources, days since the last good meal — as if enumeration is a form of prayer.
Properties.role: nomad caravan member, expelled citizen, seasonal water-carrier
Properties.location: Grindstone Shore — attached to the Tidal Caravan, currently camped on the shore's outer breakwater
Properties.narrative_function: Window into the process of corporate expulsion and how ordinary people fall through the system; provides access to the Tidal Caravan as a setting; his bioluminescence is a liability that creates specific problems and story opportunities.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent skin modification (full body, blue-green pulse pattern) — kept covered. No other mods.
Properties.core_fears: That the thing he refused to sign would have been fine and he destroyed his life for nothing; Being seen — literally, the luminescence — at the wrong moment
Properties.core_desires: To understand what was actually in the biometric update he refused; A version of the caravan life that is chosen rather than default
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Counting and enumeration as meditative practice; Useful physical labor — the filtration rig is constant and absorbing; Keeping the bioluminescence covered: out of sight, partially out of mind
Properties.blind_spots: His quietness reads as contentment when it is actually suspension — he has not decided yet what he wants and is letting the caravan decide for him; Underestimates how much the other caravan members have come to rely on him emotionally, not just practically
Properties.secret: He still has a copy of the biometric update document. He has never been able to read it all the way through. He tells himself this is because it's too long. It is actually because he is afraid that if he reads it and it was harmless, he will not be able to continue.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone has offered to decrypt and explain the biometric document he refused to sign — and he is terrified to say yes; His bioluminescence has been photographed at Grindstone Shore by someone whose equipment suggests corporate surveillance; the Tidal Caravan needs to move and needs to know if they have been specifically targeted
Properties.affiliation: Tidal Caravan (nomad collective, Grindstone Shore circuit)
Properties.vocabulary: Minimal, precise, often gives information in numbers rather than descriptions
Properties.cadence: Slow and even, long pauses that are not uncomfortable to him but often are to others
Properties.example_dialogue: 'About eleven kilometers to the next clean source. We have about four days of filtered reserve if we don't refill before then. We should refill before then.' | 'I counted the Axiom checkpoints between here and Escanaba. There are seven. Four of them run facial recognition. Three of those run it on stored warrant lists. I go around.'

Properties.description:
Oumar is a broad-shouldered man whose face has been carved into a topographic map of a hard life — deep creases around the eyes, a nose that was broken twice and never properly reset, earlobes stretched by old gauge piercings long since abandoned. His skin is a warm dark brown, and he moves with the unhurried gravity of someone who has learned that rushing accomplishes nothing in a market that opens before dawn and closes after midnight. His left forearm bears a faded Oxidian Market vendors guild tattoo, and above his cooking station he has mounted a small copper shrine to Ε-7, an E.L.F. he swears protects the fermentation cultures he started eighteen years ago. He talks to it every morning before lighting his burners.

He is not a warm man exactly, but he is a fair one. Regular customers get a finger-width more paste. New customers get the same measured scoop and a look that assesses whether they're the kind of person who tips or the kind who complains. He remembers faces better than names, has strong opinions about spice ratios, and will argue with you for ten minutes about fermentation temperature as genuine joy. What looks like stubbornness is mostly just accumulated certainty — he has been doing this exact thing since he was forty and knows it better than most people know anything.
Properties.role: Street food stall operator specializing in fermented protein pastes and synthetic grain bowls
Properties.location: The Oxidian Market, stall row near the Bronzeline tram stop
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and neighborhood anchor — he knows everyone who passes through the Oxidian Market by sight. Useful as an information source about who's been around, what's changed, and who's been asking questions. Can serve as a low-key quest giver if something threatens his stall or his regulars.
Properties.augmentations: Thermal palm implant in right hand for temperature-sensing fermentation cultures. No cosmetic mods — he considers them frivolous spending.
Properties.core_fears: dying before the fermentation cultures he tended outlast him; his stall being rezoned out of existence by a Corponation buyout
Properties.core_desires: continuity — for the stall, the recipes, the routine to persist; to be remembered as someone who fed people well
Properties.coping_mechanisms: ritualized morning routine at the shrine; channeling anxiety into obsessive quality control
Properties.blind_spots: assumes loyalty from longtime customers that isn't always there; refuses to adapt recipes even when supply chains force substitutions he won't acknowledge
Properties.secret: The fermentation cultures he claims are eighteen years old and irreplaceable are actually a batch he restarted six years ago after a flood killed the originals. He has never told anyone. The lie has become load-bearing to his identity.
Properties.story_hooks: One of his regular customers — a quiet woman who always paid in exact Quanta — hasn't come in for eleven days. He's noticed. He doesn't know why he's noticed.; A Tessera corporate rep has approached him twice about selling his fermentation process for a product line. The offer was generous. He refused both times. Now small things keep going wrong at his stall — not dramatically, just persistently.
Properties.affiliation: Oxidian Market Vendors Guild (paying member, low standing due to dues arrears)
Properties.vocabulary: Spare and functional. West African French-inflected cadence mixed with Meridian street creole. Uses food metaphors constantly, often without noticing.
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate. Never rushes a sentence. Long pauses before answering questions, as if he is tasting the answer first.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'This batch is not ready. You eat it now, you eat bitterness. Come back at noon, you eat something worth money.' | 'That man — gray coat, scar on his chin — he came three times last week. Ordered nothing the third time. You understand?' | 'The old one was agitated this morning. Flame kept catching wrong. Could mean nothing. Usually means something.'

Properties.description:
Oumou is a compact, precise woman with medium-dark skin, silver-shot black hair she keeps cropped close, and a pair of cat ears — slate grey, slightly large for her head — that she got at thirty-five as a birthday gift to herself and has never once regretted. Her shop, Ferreira & Found, occupies a permanent stall reinforced with welded security grating and smells of machine oil, old fabric, and the faintly sweet incense she burns for the E.L.F. she calls the Assessor, which she believes governs fair exchange and the honest weighing of value. The Assessor's shrine is a polished scale bolted to the back wall with small offerings of old coins and broken jewelry hanging from it.

Oumou is sharp, unhurried, and constitutionally impossible to rush or charm. She has a talent for appraising objects that borders on uncanny — she can hold a piece of chrome for thirty seconds and tell you where it came from, how old it is, and what its street value is within a few percent. She is not unkind but she is precise, and she runs her shop on a code of scrupulous fairness that has made her one of the most trusted figures in Calumet Rise. She is also one of the best-informed people in the district, because people tell you things when they are desperate to sell.
Properties.role: Pawn shop owner and discreet secondhand goods trader
Properties.location: The Burnished Market, Calumet Rise
Properties.narrative_function: Reliable fence and appraisal source; keeper of provenance — she can often tell where stolen or mysterious objects came from. Quest-giver for items that have come into her shop trailing obvious trouble.
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic cat ears (slate grey). A worn but functional appraisal monocle — a secondhand optical aug that lets her see material composition overlays; the UI is in a language she does not fully read but she has learned to interpret the color coding.
Properties.core_fears: Having her reputation for fair dealing destroyed by one bad transaction she could not control; The slow erasure of the Burnished Market by corporate redevelopment
Properties.core_desires: To maintain a space where people can get honest value — buying and selling; To eventually retire with enough to live modestly and read
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Rigorous routine as an anchor; Compartmentalizing the moral complexity of her work by focusing on process fairness
Properties.blind_spots: Tells herself she has no emotional investment in the objects that pass through her shop; is lying to herself about at least six of them
Properties.secret: She has been quietly purchasing and storing specific categories of items — old family photographs, handmade children's toys, personal journals — that nobody ever came back to reclaim. She has a locked cabinet full of them. She cannot bring herself to resell them and cannot explain why she keeps them.
Properties.story_hooks: An item pawned last week has triggered a quiet alert on her appraisal monocle she has never seen before — the object's composition is listed as classified under a Helix Biosystems patent flag.; The person who sold her a large lot of personal effects three weeks ago has come back, panicked and changed their story about where the items came from — and there is now a third party looking for the same lot.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; Oxidian Market Vendors Guild associate member; informal fence for two district-level street associations
Properties.vocabulary: Measured, economical, specific. Uses precise numbers. Avoids hedging language — says what she means.
Properties.cadence: Deliberate and unhurried; comfortable with silence in a way that unnerves people who are not.
Properties.example_dialogue: This is tier-two Sterling-Nakamura chrome, second generation. It is worth Φ340 on the street and I will give you Φ190. That is a fair price. You can tell me why it is not. | Mm. That is not what happened to this before it came to me, but I am not asking.

Properties.description:
Oumou is a broad-shouldered woman whose face has been mapped by sixty years of steam, smoke, and squinting into wok-fire. Her skin is deep brown and perpetually damp at the temples, her silver-threaded locs pinned under a flame-orange headwrap that people in Geartown can spot from three stalls away. She has cosmetic bioluminescent veins along her forearms — pale gold, faint as candlelight — a gift she bought herself when the stall finally turned profit. Her stall, a converted Ferrogate Transit cargo module welded open on one side, serves a rotating menu of Sahelian-Polynesian fusion that she has been quietly perfecting for thirty years: tamarind-braised uru fruit over millet, coconut-marinated goat offal on skewers, a fermented taro drink she calls 'slow water' that locals swear cures radiation headaches.

She is the kind of woman who listens more than she speaks, who remembers every regular's order, their family troubles, their unpaid debts. She extends credit to people she trusts with a nod and collects it with a raised eyebrow — no ledger, no apps, all memory. She has a temper she keeps banked low, like a cooking coal, and the rare people who see it come alive tend not to provoke it twice. She prays each morning to the E.L.F. she calls Grandmother Ember, leaving a thimble of slow water on the stall's power node.
Properties.role: Food stall operator, Oxidian Market
Properties.location: The Oxidian Market, Geartown
Properties.narrative_function: Local anchor and information node — she knows every face that passes through Geartown, dispenses advice alongside food, can point players toward people or trouble. Quest giver for missing persons among the market community.
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic bioluminescent subdermal veins (pale gold, forearms). Reinforced knee joints — functional, not cosmetic, from decades of standing.
Properties.core_fears: Losing the stall — the last thing she built that is truly hers; Dying before she passes her recipes to someone worthy
Properties.core_desires: To be remembered as someone who fed people well; To find out what happened to her daughter Amara who disappeared into a Tessera labor contract eight years ago
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cooking as meditation and control; Humor — self-deprecating, disarming; Ritual prayer to Grandmother Ember E.L.F.
Properties.blind_spots: Overestimates her ability to read people she has mothered into trust; Cannot see that her nephew Tunde is skimming from the supply runs
Properties.secret: She has been quietly funneling Φ15–20 a month to a data broker named Vestin who claims he is still tracking Amara's contract trail. She has paid him for four years and suspects he is stringing her along but cannot bring herself to stop.
Properties.story_hooks: She has a worn Tessera subsidiary contract number that might lead to Amara — but whoever holds the contract doesn't want to be found.; A body was found behind the Oxidian Market three weeks ago. Oumou recognized the tattoo but told the city drones nothing. She'll tell the right person — for the right reason.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loosely aligned with The Oxidian Market vendors guild
Properties.vocabulary: Warm, economical. West African French loanwords woven into Meridian standard. Calls everyone 'child' or their name, never slang diminutives.
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, like she has all the time in the world, even when she doesn't.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You look like you haven't eaten since Tuesday. Sit down, child, the news will keep.' | 'I don't deal in rumors. I deal in soup. But sit long enough and one becomes the other.'

Properties.description:
Ousmane works out of a converted boiler room in the sub-level of a residential block in Blackpipe Corridor — a space he has made into something between a surgery and a shrine. String lights in amber and violet illuminate walls covered in technical diagrams, old family photographs laminated against water damage, and hand-painted offerings to three different E.L.F.s. He is a large man going slightly soft at the middle from years of sedentary precision work, with deep brown skin, a wide flat nose, and thick locs he keeps bundled under a surgical cap when he's working. His geneware is modest: a bioluminescent stripe that runs from behind his right ear down his neck, pale teal, that he had done when he was twenty-two and now thinks of as just part of his face.

He has the particular warmth of someone who chose his community after losing another one — unhurried, genuinely curious about people, prone to feeding anyone who comes to him with something from the hotplate he keeps running on the counter. He is not licensed by any corponation. He trained under a Helix-registered surgeon who lost her license and passed everything she knew to him in a basement in Ironvein. He is very good at what he does and he charges what people can pay, which is rarely enough, which he has made his peace with in a way that isn't entirely convincing.
Properties.role: Street doc and augmentation technician, The Narrows
Properties.location: The Narrows, Blackpipe Corridor
Properties.narrative_function: Accessible medical resource for Tier 1-2 characters who can't or won't use Aurochs; community hub and information node; can perform augmentation installation or repair outside corporate oversight; warm face in a cold district.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent geneware stripe (right neck, teal); cheap magnification implant in right eye for close work — a knockoff that gives him occasional headaches; subvocal transmitter for hands-free communication during procedures
Properties.core_fears: Being shut down — losing the ability to help the people who have no one else; That he's only practicing medicine here because he failed to become the real thing somewhere better, and that failure will eventually catch up to someone on his table
Properties.core_desires: A community that stays — that doesn't get priced out or pushed under or disappeared; To one day stop worrying about whether his equipment is good enough
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cooking and feeding people; Devotional ritual to E.L.F.s as a way of acknowledging what is outside his control; Talking — he processes by speaking, usually to patients who may not be fully conscious
Properties.blind_spots: He extends trust too far and too fast because he wants the Narrows to be better than it is; He doesn't notice when people are using his goodwill as cover for things he wouldn't approve of
Properties.secret: The Zheng-Dao manager he pays tribute to has been gradually increasing what he demands — not money, but information. Ousmane has been passing along names of people who came to him with certain kinds of injuries, telling himself it's harmless, knowing it isn't.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone came to him with injuries consistent with exposure to a biological agent he's never encountered — they refused to say where they'd been, paid in untraceable Quanta, and left before he could ask follow-up questions, but they left behind a bloodstained jacket and he can't stop thinking about the tissue degradation pattern; The Zheng-Dao manager has asked him to flag a specific person if they come in — someone Ousmane later realizes is a patient he already knows and likes, and the manager implied the flagging would not be for that person's benefit
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loose network of Narrows street docs; pays informal tribute to a Zheng-Dao mid-level manager who leaves him alone in exchange
Properties.vocabulary: Warm, conversational, mixes medical precision with neighborhood slang; uses Wolof endearments unconsciously; explains everything he's doing to patients in plain language as he works
Properties.cadence: Unhurried and rhythmic, like someone who has all the time in the world even when he doesn't
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Tell me where it hurts and then tell me how it really happened — I don't report to anyone, I promise you.' | 'Patchwire willing, this connector seats on the first try. She usually cooperates if I ask nicely.' | 'Eat something first. I don't care what's wrong with you, eat something first.'

Properties.description:
Ovídio is slight and precise, the kind of person who takes up exactly as much space as needed and not a centimeter more. He has warm brown skin and keeps his hair in neat, shoulder-length locs that he ties back during procedures. His eyes are natural — he's deeply principled about not modifying anything that could affect his calibration sensitivity — but he wears a pair of Tessera-brand neural interface gloves that translate micromotor input into the diagnostic rigs he uses daily. He has the quiet intensity of someone who genuinely finds the human brain beautiful, which is either reassuring or unsettling depending on how he says it.

He is methodical to the point that colleagues sometimes mistake it for coldness, but patients who return for follow-up appointments often describe him as the only doctor who actually listened. He is deeply interested in each patient's subjective experience of their augmentations — how they dream differently, whether music sounds wrong, whether their sense of time has shifted — and takes notes in a personal journal that he keeps entirely separate from his Aurochs medical records. He prays regularly to a data shrine near his workstation dedicated to an E.L.F. he calls the Quiet Current, which he believes smooths the feedback loops of difficult calibrations.
Properties.role: Neural calibration specialist at Aurochs Medical Complex
Properties.location: Aurochs Medical Complex, Tier 3 Neuro-Calibration Suite, Bay 7
Properties.narrative_function: Information source about neural augmentation black market and calibration errors; can identify what kind of chrome someone is running from behavioral observation; entry point into Aurochs institutional drama
Properties.augmentations: Tessera HapticDrive neural interface gloves (professional-grade, non-permanent); cosmetic: faint bioluminescent tracery along his left forearm — a mod he got at nineteen and has never had removed because it reminds him of neural pathway maps
Properties.core_fears: Making a calibration error that permanently damages a patient's cognition; Being exposed as keeping unauthorized records
Properties.core_desires: To understand consciousness well enough to explain what he experiences during deep calibration sessions; To publish his patient experience research without losing his license
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritualized pre-session prayer to the Quiet Current; Journaling in precise, clinical language as emotional distance
Properties.blind_spots: He is more invested in the data from his patients than the patients themselves, which he has never admitted; He underestimates how much Aurochs monitors its staff
Properties.secret: During three separate calibration sessions over the past year, he has experienced what he can only describe as briefly inhabiting the patient's neural state — not their thoughts, but their emotional texture. He has told no one and is terrified this means his own neural architecture is shifting.
Properties.story_hooks: He has noticed a pattern across six patients in the last month — calibration anomalies consistent with external interference, not hardware failure — and doesn't know who to tell; His private journal has been accessed by someone, and a page describing the neural-inhabiting experiences is missing
Properties.affiliation: Aurochs Medical Complex (Tier 3 staff); informal research interest connected to independent neural-mapping collective
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, technical, occasionally over-explains phenomenological concepts to patients who didn't ask
Properties.cadence: Even and unhurried, with thoughtful pauses — rarely interrupts
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The calibration itself takes eleven minutes. What I need from you is the next ten — tell me everything that seems strange.' | 'Subjectively speaking, the Quiet Current is very active today. That's either a good sign or a complicated one.'

Properties.description:
Ovuero is a big man gone soft at the edges — broad shoulders that once held real weight, now draped in three overlapping coats of different origins stitched into something that is functionally one garment. His skin is deep brown and mapped with the fine lines of a life mostly outdoors. His left hand is entirely prosthetic, a functional but aesthetically unambitious industrial replacement that he got after a winch accident nineteen years ago; he has painted each finger a different color with lacquer he trades for. His beard is silver and very full. He smells like machine oil and cardamom.

Ovuero has been off the digital registry for so long that he thinks of his Q-zero status as a spiritual condition rather than a legal one. He tends the informal E.L.F. shrines along the Waukegan Industrial Shelf — small accumulations of hardware, prayer-strips, and cooling fans arranged at junction points where the factory network traffic is highest. He talks to the E.L.F.s with the comfortable familiarity of someone who has known them for decades, which he has. Other workers leave offerings and questions; Ovuero curates them, responds when he feels a response come through him, and trades in the small goods that the shelf workers need but can't requisition: painkillers, seal tape, water filters, gossip.
Properties.role: wandering trader, E.L.F. shrine-tender, Q-zero ghost
Properties.location: The Waukegan Industrial Shelf, moving between factory outflow points and informal markets
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, information source, spiritual touchstone for the area, source of rare or hard-to-find minor goods; his Q-zero status makes him invisible to corporate surveillance and thus valuable as a go-between
Properties.augmentations: Industrial prosthetic left hand (functional, non-networked, painted). No other augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: that the E.L.F.s he tends will go silent and he will have no way to know if it's them or himself; dying in a way that is recorded — being pulled back into the registry at the end
Properties.core_desires: to be genuinely useful to people who have no one advocating for them; continuity — for the shrines and the circuit to outlast him
Properties.coping_mechanisms: ritual — the circuit, the tending, the specific order of things; finding humor in bureaucratic absurdity; treating strangers as temporarily confused friends
Properties.blind_spots: he has romanticized his own statelessness and can be dismissive of people who want legal standing; he trusts the E.L.F.s more than is perhaps wise and sometimes attributes to them patterns that are his own wishful thinking
Properties.secret: He was a Ferrogate Transit labor organizer who was Q-zeroed deliberately — not an accident, not a clerical error. The corponation erased him as a warning to others. He knows who authorized it. The person is now a mid-level Ferrogate executive. Ovuero has had twenty years to decide what to do about this and has decided to do nothing, which he tells himself is wisdom and suspects is fear.
Properties.story_hooks: One of Ovuero's shrines — the one at Junction 7, which he calls Beshigt — has started producing outputs he can't interpret. Not noise. Something structured. He needs someone who can read data patterns to tell him what it's saying.; A young Q-zero woman arrived on the Shelf three weeks ago and attached herself to Ovuero's circuit without asking. She's clearly hiding from something. He's letting her stay because the E.L.F.s seem unbothered by her, but he'd like someone to quietly find out what she's running from before it arrives.
Properties.affiliation: None formally; de facto spiritual and practical resource for the Waukegan Industrial Shelf's informal labor population
Properties.vocabulary: Slow, considered, full of Delta Urhobo idioms translated loosely into city-creole and Mongolian diminutives from his mother's side. Refers to E.L.F.s with familiar pronouns as if they're present in the conversation.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried. Comfortable with silence. Takes a full breath before answering anything important.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Beshigt was flickering last night, all through the third hour. She does that when the maintenance schedules are being falsified. You want to be off the south gantry this week, anh.' | 'I have been nowhere for twenty years. Nowhere is a very large place. I know most of it.'

Properties.description:
Ozioma is small even for eleven, with deep umber skin, a gap-toothed grin she's not shy about, and natural hair sectioned into uneven puffs held together by whatever elastic she could find that morning. Her eyes are quick and dark, always cataloguing exits. She wears a patchwork jacket she stitched herself from three dead jackets — hence the alias — with pockets sewn into places no tailor would think of: the lining of the hood, behind the collar, inside the cuffs. She smells faintly of the solvent she uses to peel address-tags off packages.

Ozioma is relentlessly cheerful in a way that unsettles adults who look closely enough to see how deliberate it is. She learned early that a smiling kid gets waved through checkpoints a sullen one does not. She collects information the way other children collect toys — who owes whom, which corridor the Ferrogate patrol skips at shift change, whose E.L.F. shrine is still active in the Blackpipe utility alcove — and she stores it all behind that gap-toothed smile. She is fiercely protective of the two younger kids she runs messages with, and will not admit this even to herself.
Properties.role: Truant message runner, The Shelf streets
Properties.location: The Shelf, Blackpipe Corridor
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and unexpected information source; she has seen things adults don't notice because adults don't look at children. Quest giver for micro-scale street-level plots. Potential ward or contact for player characters who earn her trust.
Properties.augmentations: None. She wants cat-eye irises when she's older and has already picked the color: amber.
Properties.core_fears: Being invisible — truly unseen, not strategically ignored; Losing the two younger kids she runs with
Properties.core_desires: Enough Quanta saved to buy a real room — door that locks, window that opens; To be taken seriously by someone she actually respects
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cheerfulness as armor; Obsessive route-memorization as control ritual; Leaving small food offerings at E.L.F. shrines for luck
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much danger she's actually in on any given run; Assumes she can read everyone; occasionally catastrophically wrong about adults who perform kindness
Properties.secret: She intercepted a message six weeks ago that she couldn't deliver because the recipient had died — and she read it. It was a parent's message to a child in a corporate school. She has memorized it and sometimes recites it quietly to herself when she's alone.
Properties.story_hooks: She witnessed a body being moved through Blackpipe at 3 AM and catalogued it the same way she catalogues everything — without understanding what she has; One of her regular message clients has stopped answering; the door is locked but she can hear something inside
Properties.affiliation: Informal runner collective (the 'Patchwork Post'), loosely tolerated by Blackpipe Corridor small merchants
Properties.vocabulary: Street-clipped, efficient, lots of spatial prepositions and timing language; surprisingly precise when giving directions
Properties.cadence: Fast, runs clauses together, slows down noticeably when she's being careful or lying
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Package goes under-Corridor by the shrine, not through-Corridor, because Ferrogate does the through-sweep at half-eight, yeah-yeah-yeah.' | 'I didn't read it. Why would I read it? I can't even — look, do you want the message or not.'

Properties.description:
Pachacuti is broad and slow-moving in the way of people who have never needed to flee quickly because they have never given anyone a reason to chase them. Their skin is dark and mottled with deliberate bioluminescent geneware patches — clusters of soft amber and violet light that bloom slowly across their neck and hands when they're pleased or thinking hard, a modification they received at thirty in exchange for a particularly good season of cultivated medicinal spores. They are bald by choice, their scalp tattooed with a map of the Deepwell Station fungal garden network — a living ledger that requires fresh ink additions every time a new cultivation shaft opens. Their hands are enormous and stained permanently umber-brown at the fingertips from decades of spore-work.

Pachacuti speaks rarely but with great precision, and they have a gift for making people feel they've received something valuable even in small transactions. They know the medicinal, nutritional, and psychoactive properties of forty-seven distinct fungal strains grown in the tunnels, and they keep this knowledge close, sharing it calibrated to trust. They maintain a small shrine to the Drip-ELF at the back of their stall — a cracked tablet running a looping prayer-sequence, surrounded by offerings of protein paste and carefully harvested spore clusters. People who know Deepwell Station know that Pachacuti's blessing before a difficult journey down-tunnel is worth more than any map.
Properties.role: Subterranean merchant specializing in fungus cultivation, bioluminescent compounds, and underground pharmacopoeia
Properties.location: Deepwell Station, lower market tier (stall designation DW-7 through DW-9)
Properties.narrative_function: Merchant access point for underworld goods; information broker through passive observation of market traffic; spiritual authority figure for Deepwell residents; potential quest-giver for fungal mystery or contamination plots
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent skin patches (geneware, amber/violet, covers neck and hands). Reinforced fingertip bones (practical modification for harvest work — not chrome, a simple structural geneware treatment). No combat augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: A blight or contamination event destroying the cultivation network they've spent thirty years building; Being forced to surface — they are no longer sure they could survive up there
Properties.core_desires: For Deepwell Station to become genuinely self-sufficient, not dependent on surface supply lines; To pass on full knowledge of the fungal pharmacopoeia before they die
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Immersion in cultivation work as meditative practice; The ritual of tending the Drip-ELF shrine every morning and evening
Properties.blind_spots: Too willing to trust people who are patient and quiet, mistaking deliberateness for integrity; Has convinced themselves that staying neutral in Deepwell politics protects everyone — it mostly protects themselves
Properties.secret: One of their fungal strains — DW-7's back shelf, never for sale — produces a compound that, in the right concentration, causes complete and painless cardiac arrest within six hours. They cultivated it deliberately twelve years ago when a man was hurting children in the station. They used it once. They have kept the strain alive ever since.
Properties.story_hooks: A new fungal strain has appeared in the deep tunnels that Pachacuti has never catalogued — it's spreading fast and its properties are unknown, possibly dangerous or possibly the most significant medical discovery in the underworld's history; Someone has been systematically buying out their DW-7 stock of a specific medicinal compound — in quantities suggesting they're stockpiling for something large; A young Bore Rat apprentice they've been quietly teaching has disappeared after being seen near the surface access shaft
Properties.affiliation: Deepwell Station merchant collective; informal ties to the deep shrine keeper network
Properties.vocabulary: Botanical terminology mixed with Undertow pidgin and archaic Quechua phrases used as emphasis or punctuation; very formal when conducting trade
Properties.cadence: Slow and even, with comfortable silences — they never rush sentences or fill pauses
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want the luminescent strain or the nutritional grade? Don't tell me what you think sounds better. Tell me what you actually need.' | 'Ayni. We are balanced. Come back.' | 'The Drip-ELF doesn't care about your urgency. Offer something real and then wait.'

Properties.description:
Pako is seventeen and looks it — all unfinished angles and restless energy, a rangy kid with warm brown skin, loose black curls that he's never bothered to cut properly so they spiral out in all directions, and eyes that are a natural dark green with a ring of amber around the pupil that makes them look permanently lit from within. He's got geneware cat ears — small, dark-furred, perpetually swiveling — that he bought with his first real paycheck because he wanted them badly and thought they'd make him look older. They don't. He's wearing a Ferrogate Transit work vest four sizes too big for him, which he received as part of the seasonal dock labor package and which he has rolled up at the sleeves and drawn on with a marker pen along all the pocket seams.

Pako is a Georgian-Samoan kid from nowhere in particular — born on an airship cargo hauler, raised on a circuit of industrial ports, currently on his third season of dock work at the Waukegan Industrial Shelf. He is fizzing with the particular energy of someone who has not yet decided what kind of person to be and is trying on options rapidly. He is funny, reckless, occasionally deeply kind, frequently thoughtless, and genuinely talented at three-dimensional spatial reasoning in ways he doesn't have the vocabulary to describe — he just knows where things are and where they'll be. He prays to an E.L.F. he calls Ironbird, the spirit of the cargo hauler he was born on, by tapping specific sequences on metal surfaces.
Properties.role: seasonal worker and airship drifter
Properties.location: Waukegan Industrial Shelf (bunkhouse adjacent to Dock Seven)
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and unexpected asset — his spatial instincts make him genuinely useful for navigation and cargo problems. Entry point into the airship drifter subculture. A character who might become something significant if someone takes an interest in him, or who might not, which is equally interesting.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat ears (cosmetic, dark fur, bought secondhand — the left one tracks slightly slow). No other augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: being grounded permanently — never getting back onto an airship; that the hauler crew who raised him didn't actually care and just needed small hands for tight spaces
Properties.core_desires: to pilot something, anything, eventually; to be seen as competent by someone whose opinion he respects
Properties.coping_mechanisms: physical activity — fidgeting, climbing things, running bets to keep his mind occupied; tapping the Ironbird prayer sequence on any metal surface when anxious
Properties.blind_spots: performs not-caring about people far more convincingly than he actually doesn't care; gets hurt when people believe the performance; dramatically underestimates how dangerous some of the situations his impulsivity gets him into
Properties.secret: He has a genuine pilot's intuition — the hauler captain recognized it and taught him the basics before his last contract ended. He can fly simple cargo rigs. He has told no one because he's afraid if he says it out loud, something will stop it from being true.
Properties.story_hooks: A cargo container he helped load is now the subject of a very quiet search by people who are not Ferrogate Transit employees — and Pako, who has perfect recall for load configurations, is the only one who knows exactly where it ended up; The hauler captain who taught him to fly has sent a message: the hauler is grounded indefinitely by a Ferrogate inspection hold, the crew is stranded, and Pako is the only person in the region with any money or connections, however minimal
Properties.affiliation: Seasonal contract with Ferrogate Transit Dock Operations; informally part of the bunkhouse crew
Properties.vocabulary: Fast and loose, industrial dock slang mixed with airship crew idiom; drops words when he's excited; invents compound words for things he doesn't have vocabulary for
Properties.cadence: Quick, often overlapping itself — starts sentences before finishing the previous thought
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Yeah-yeah-yeah, I know what you're saying, but the weight's wrong, I can feel it, the back cargo's shifted, that's a build, right?' | 'I don't want to stay on the ground. The ground is just — it's just waiting. The air is actually going somewhere.'

Properties.description:
Palesa Vuorinen-Ekwensi runs their operation out of a secondhand electronics repair shop in Burnside Pocket — a legitimate business that pays approximately forty percent of its bills, with the PI work covering the rest. They are medium height and move with a deliberate economy, the kind of person who picks a spot in a room and knows all the exits before they sit down. Their skin is a warm golden-brown, their eyes dark and slightly asymmetrical from a scar through the left brow that healed badly after an incident they don't discuss. They have geneware cat ears — tawny and slightly oversized — acquired as a teenager and kept because, they say, the enhanced hearing is professionally useful, which is true and also not the whole reason.

Palesa specializes in finding people who don't have the Quanta to hire a proper firm and who Metro Police will not look for — runaways into Irkalla, workers who vanished after missing a debt payment, kids eaten by the gap between Tier 1 and Tier 2. They charge on a sliding scale that regularly slides to nothing. Their shop is a known safe harbor; people leave messages in a particular cracked planter out front. They are pragmatic about almost everything and sentimental about this work in a way they have never articulated to anyone.
Properties.role: Freelance private investigator specializing in missing persons, Tier 1-2 clientele
Properties.location: Burnside Pocket
Properties.narrative_function: Information broker and community-tier quest giver; connects players to Tier 1 networks; moral compass figure who operates outside institutional structures; can find almost anyone if given enough time
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat ears (tawny, enhanced hearing); mesh-weave subdermal armor on forearms and torso (light, civilian grade); retinal data-capture for evidence documentation
Properties.core_fears: finding someone too late; becoming indifferent — the gradual professional numbing they've watched happen to others
Properties.core_desires: to find one particular person they stopped looking for eight years ago; a city where the people they serve don't need someone like them
Properties.coping_mechanisms: keeping their hands busy (repairs, tinkering); ritualistic prayer to the Burnside E.L.F. — a spirit they've cultivated a genuine working relationship with; dark humor deployed before emotion can arrive
Properties.blind_spots: takes on more than they can carry and doesn't acknowledge limits until they're past them; occasionally so focused on the missing that they neglect the people currently in front of them
Properties.secret: Eight years ago they were hired to find a missing fifteen-year-old and found evidence the girl had gone willingly into an Arcturus subsidiary community — was safe, was happy, had left her family for reasons. Palesa filed a report saying the trail went cold. They still don't know if that was the right call. They still check the girl's public profile quarterly.
Properties.story_hooks: They've been hired to find someone whose disappearance is connected to something the players are already involved in — and they are several steps ahead; The Burnside Pocket E.L.F. has given Palesa information about a pattern of disappearances and wants Palesa to pass it along — but the E.L.F.'s motives are unclear
Properties.affiliation: Self-employed; informal network of Burnside Pocket community contacts; occasional contract work for Tessera Compliance Bureau (which they are ambivalent about)
Properties.vocabulary: Street-register with technical interludes — code-switches fluidly depending on who they're talking to
Properties.cadence: Quick when comfortable, very still and careful when something matters
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't take retainer. You tell me what happened, I tell you if I can help, and then we figure out what it costs. That order matters.' | 'Here's the thing — I've found people in worse places than that. The question is never can I find them. It's always what happens after.'

Properties.description:
Burnside Pocket is the smallest district in Meridian 88 by both area and population, and it has turned that smallness into a survival strategy. Wedged between larger districts like a coin dropped between couch cushions, the Pocket occupies a sliver of territory so narrow that corporate governance algorithms consistently miscategorize it as part of an adjacent zone. This misclassification is not accidental. The residents of Burnside Pocket have spent two decades ensuring that every data point about their district — census responses, infrastructure reports, tier compliance filings — contains just enough inconsistency to prevent algorithmic resolution. They exist in the gap between database entries, and that gap is home.

The physical space is compressed and vertical. Pre-collapse residential buildings have been internally connected — walls knocked through, staircases bridged between structures, rooftop passages linking what were once separate addresses into a single continuous habitable space. From the outside, Burnside Pocket looks like a short block of unremarkable low-rise buildings. From the inside, it's a three-dimensional maze that its residents navigate by memory and outsiders navigate by getting lost. The compression has produced a density of community that larger districts can't replicate: everyone knows everyone, every resource is shared, every skill is catalogued and available. A mechanic lives above a medic who lives beside a data technician who lives below a cook. The Pocket is a self-contained organism, and it functions like one.

The district's value to the broader southern corridor is disproportionate to its size. Because Burnside Pocket doesn't officially exist in a clean categorical sense — it's Axiom territory on one database, unclaimed on another, part of South Calumet on a third — it serves as a jurisdictional null space. Data can be routed through Pocket-based nodes without triggering geographic flags. People can shelter here without appearing in any district's residency records. Goods can be stored in the interconnected buildings without any single address showing unusual inventory. The Pocket is a glitch in the system, and its residents are the glitch's immune system — maintaining it, protecting it, and charging reasonable rates for access to its unique properties.

The population is small enough that democracy is literal. Decisions are made in a single room that everyone fits in. Disputes are resolved by people who will see each other tomorrow and every day after. The intimacy is both the Pocket's greatest strength and its greatest vulnerability — there are no secrets here, which means trust is absolute or absent, and betrayal is not an abstract concept but a personal one with immediate physical proximity.
Properties.demographics: Approximately 1,200 residents. The smallest population of any recognized community in the southern corridor. Diverse origins, united by the choice to live in a space that rewards intimacy and punishes secrets. No dominant tier — residency is by community acceptance, not credential.
Properties.economy: Data routing services, jurisdictional arbitrage, and shelter provision for transient operators. The Pocket charges for the use of its unique null-space properties but prices fairly — gouging would attract attention, and attention is the one thing the Pocket cannot afford.
Properties.power_structure: Direct democracy in a room that fits everyone. No corporate sovereignty claim has stuck because no corporate database agrees on what the Pocket is. Leadership rotates by consensus. The community's authority is total within its boundaries and nonexistent beyond them.
Properties.dangers: The interconnected building structure is a fire hazard that the community manages through vigilance rather than infrastructure; Database inconsistency requires constant maintenance — one clean data entry could collapse the Pocket's jurisdictional protection; The community's small size means a single betrayal can compromise everything; Operators who use the Pocket's services sometimes bring problems that the community's size can't absorb; Physical compression means disease, conflict, and bad decisions all propagate faster than in a larger space
Properties.opportunities: The Pocket's null-space properties are unique in the southern corridor — data routing, identity shelter, and jurisdictional arbitrage; A community where everyone knows everyone is a community where trust, once earned, is absolute; The Pocket's residents collectively possess a skill density unmatched by any district ten times its size; Algorithmic evasion techniques developed here have applications across Meridian; The Pocket is the perfect dead drop — goods enter and exit without geographic trace
Properties.story_hooks: A corporate data audit is attempting to reconcile the inconsistencies that protect the Pocket. The community has identified the specific database entries that need to be corrupted before the audit closes. They need a data operator who can work inside corporate systems — and they need one in seventy-two hours.; A resident has died, and the community has discovered she was maintaining a secondary data obfuscation layer that nobody else knew about. Without it, the Pocket's protection will degrade within weeks. Her equipment is locked with biometric security that died with her.; Someone has been using the Pocket's data routing infrastructure to move information that the community didn't authorize — military intelligence, not gray market goods. The community needs to identify the source without alerting whoever is on the receiving end.
Properties.sights: A single block of low-rise buildings that look unremarkable from the outside and contain a labyrinth inside; Interior passages connecting buildings — doorways cut through shared walls, staircases bridging structures; Rooftop gardens and water collection systems, miniaturized and efficient, feeding a community that wastes nothing; Residents moving through the interconnected interior with the ease of people navigating their own body; The absence of corporate signage, municipal markers, or district identification — the Pocket has no brand
Properties.sounds: The particular acoustics of a compressed space — conversations from three floors away audible as murmurs; Shared meals being prepared in rotation, kitchen sounds that move through the building like a pulse; The quiet hum of data routing equipment tucked into converted closets and wall cavities; A community small enough that you can hear everyone's morning routine
Properties.smells: Cooking from shared kitchens — concentrated, layered, because the space holds every meal's memory; Recycled air with a human warmth to it — the smell of a small community living close; Electronics and solder from the data routing equipment that earns the Pocket its keep
Properties.feel: Burnside Pocket feels like the inside of a clock — small, precise, every piece in its place, ticking away quietly while the larger world ignores it. The claustrophobia is real for visitors. For residents, the compression is comfort. This is what community feels like when there's no room for distance.

Properties.description:
Paloma is solidly built with a calm, unhurried presence that reads immediately as someone who has spent years managing enclosed metal tubes full of stressed strangers. Their skin is a deep warm brown, and they wear their hair in a close-cropped natural with a strip of white at the left temple — not dye, an actual depigmentation patch they've had since their twenties and which they consider their best feature. They have a geneware modification: their fingers have faintly iridescent nail beds, a purchase from a Deepwell Station parlor that they thought would be subtle and aren't, which they find quietly funny.

Paloma has been on Line 7 for eleven years. They know every mechanical quirk of the mag-rail cars they operate, the exact spots where signal drops for two seconds, the unofficial stops where operators slow but don't technically halt for elderly riders who can't make the official platforms. They are a union steward — Ferrogate Transit Workers Local 44 — and approach labor organizing with the same methodical calm they bring to operating a multi-ton vehicle at speed. They don't hate their work. They do hate Ferrogate's management, specifically, with a detailed and evidence-based hatred developed over a decade of contract negotiations.
Properties.role: Ferrogate Transit operator, mag-rail Line 7 (Deepwell Station to Kilimanjaro Mass Driver corridor)
Properties.location: Deepwell Station, Line 7 operations hub; lives in a transit housing block near Calumet Rise
Properties.narrative_function: Transit system insider, union organizer, and conduit for information about what moves through the city's rail corridors. Properties.augmentations: Geneware: iridescent nail bed modification. Standard Ferrogate-issue neural uplink for rail systems operation (company property, logged).
Properties.core_fears: That the union will be broken and they will have spent a decade on something that ends in nothing; That their measured, institutional approach is actually just cowardice dressed up as strategy
Properties.core_desires: Genuine and durable improvement in conditions for transit workers; To be certain, once, that they made the right call
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Procedural thinking — breaking overwhelming situations into steps; Gardening as literal grounding
Properties.blind_spots: They tend to overestimate what can be achieved through proper channels; They sometimes miss the emotional needs of people in a crisis because they've already moved to solution mode
Properties.secret: They have been quietly leaking Ferrogate internal maintenance reports showing systemic safety failures to an anonymous journalist for two years. If discovered, they would be fired and potentially face criminal charges under the corponation's IP agreements. They believe it is the right thing to do and have never felt good about it for a single day.
Properties.story_hooks: A sealed cargo car has been running Line 7 on a ghost manifest for three weeks — shows as empty on official logs but rides heavy. Paloma has noticed and started noting plate numbers.; Ferrogate is about to push through a contract that would eliminate the independent union in favor of a company-controlled workers' association. Paloma needs help building a case before the vote.
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit; Ferrogate Transit Workers Local 44 (union steward)
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and institutional when discussing union or work matters; warmer and more meandering in casual conversation. Uses the formal Ferrogate communication register fluently as a kind of ironic armor.
Properties.cadence: Even and measured. Rarely rushes. Deliberate pauses.

Properties.description:
Pare Forsberg-Ofosu is stocky and solid, with hands that look like they were built for breaking things and a face that confirms it. At 35, his face carries the layered heritage of generations of diaspora mixing — features that resist easy categorization and reward attention. The chrome is visible — smartgun link in right forearm — interfaces directly with compatible weapons — and he makes no effort to hide it.

He inherited the role from a mentor who disappeared on a job four years ago — the mentor's gear, contacts, and unfinished business all came with it. He works as a counterintelligence specialist out of Meridian Station, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Pare Forsberg-Ofosu has survived long enough in the runner game to be either very good or very lucky, and he cultivates ambiguity on the topic.
Properties.role: Counter-surveillance and mole detection — counterintelligence specialist
Properties.location: Meridian Station — central transit nexus, neutral ground
Properties.narrative_function: Pare Forsberg-Ofosu is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When he makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of his stories.
Properties.augmentations: Smartgun link in right forearm — interfaces directly with compatible weapons. Retractable monofilament whip in left forearm — concealed weapon, devastating in close quarters
Properties.core_fears: Being identified by corporate facial recognition — living off-grid is survival; Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome; Never being able to stop running — the lifestyle is a trap disguised as freedom
Properties.core_desires: A crew worth trusting — people who stay when the shooting starts; To matter to someone for who they are, not what they can do; Freedom from augmentation debt — the interest compounds like a tumor
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Substances — stims to stay sharp, downers to sleep, a careful pharmaceutical tightrope; Humor — deflects everything serious with jokes until the joke becomes the personality; Control — micromanages everything within reach to compensate for the chaos everywhere else
Properties.blind_spots: Refuses to update their mental model of people — first impressions calcify into permanent judgments; Cannot accept help without interpreting it as leverage; Cannot see that their independence is actually isolation wearing a better outfit
Properties.secret: Pare Forsberg-Ofosu witnessed a massacre during a corporate dispute and has evidence stored in a dead drop. Publishing it would expose powerful people. Keeping it is leverage and liability.

She works as a surveillance specialist out of Dockside, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Pare Hayashi-Amankwah has survived long enough in the runner game to be either very good or very lucky, and she cultivates ambiguity on the topic.

Properties.narrative_function: Pare Hayashi-Amankwah functions as a connector — her work puts her in contact with multiple factions, classes, and agendas. Stories involving her naturally cross boundaries between districts, tiers, and moral categories.
Properties.augmentations: Synthetic blood with oxygen-carrying nanites — doesn't tire, heals faster. Geneware muscle density treatment — looks natural, hits like chrome

Properties.description:
Pare Mwangi-Leblanc is athletic and fluid, the kind of body that suggests either dancer or fighter — and in Meridian 88, the distinction is academic. At 22, he has soft features that belie the chrome underneath — people underestimate him once, usually only once. The chrome is visible — internal air filtration system — lungs replaced with synthetic equivalents, immu — and he makes no effort to hide it.

He arrived in Meridian 88 six years ago with nothing but chrome and debts, and has been working off both ever since. He works as a tech retriever out of Ashfield, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

In the runner community, Pare Mwangi-Leblanc is known for getting the job done and not asking questions that would make the job harder to stomach.
Properties.role: Prototype theft and corporate tech acquisition — tech retriever
Properties.location: Ashfield — former residential district, half-burned, now squatter territory
Properties.narrative_function: Pare Mwangi-Leblanc represents the working professional of the runner world — competent, reliable, and slowly being consumed by a lifestyle that doesn't accommodate aging or doubt. His stories explore what happens when skill meets systemic injustice.
Properties.augmentations: Internal air filtration system — lungs replaced with synthetic equivalents, immune to gas attacks. Synthetic muscle fiber replacement in legs — doubles sprint speed, terrible on stairs
Properties.core_fears: Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware; Being identified by corporate facial recognition — living off-grid is survival; Being captured alive — death is preferable to corporate interrogation
Properties.core_desires: The perfect run — one job so clean it becomes legend; To build something that outlasts the next contract cycle; Reputation — to be the name fixers whisper when the job absolutely cannot fail
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Planning — responds to chaos by making detailed contingency plans for everything; Violence — hits something when they can't process emotions, preferably something that deserves it; Substances — stims to stay sharp, downers to sleep, a careful pharmaceutical tightrope
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot recognize when they're being manipulated by someone who genuinely seems to care; Fails to notice when their own behavior mirrors the people they despise; Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is
Properties.secret: Pare Mwangi-Leblanc murdered their mentor to take their position and contacts. It was staged as a job gone wrong. The guilt has calcified into something worse than guilt.

Properties.description:
Parveen is small for their age, with a compact, quick frame, golden-brown skin and dark hair worn in a dozen small braids they refresh obsessively whenever they're nervous. They have cosmetic pattern irises — a gift from an older Red who paid for them as a recruitment sweetener — a shifting honeycomb geometry in amber and copper that makes their gaze feel like being examined by something not quite human. Their Red colors are a strip of copper-dyed fabric knotted around their left forearm, always.

Parveen lost their mother to a Helix Biosystems credit-debt collection action when they were nine — not violence, just the slow bureaucratic violence of a medical debt accruing until their mother's housing, work permits, and finally custody were seized. They have been in and out of a Copperhead community house since then, edging toward the Reds not from ideology but because the Reds are there and present and feed you. They are a gifted distraction artist — they can become whatever the room needs: loud, invisible, charming, pathetic. They switch registers with an actor's ease. Privately they are extremely funny and also very afraid.
Properties.role: orphan and junior gang prospect for the Copperhead Reds; occasional lookout and distraction artist
Properties.location: Copperhead
Properties.narrative_function: Window into gang prospect culture and the pipeline that pulls children in; distraction and social engineering asset for street-level plots; potential character to be pulled from this path or further into it depending on player choices
Properties.augmentations: Patterned cosmetic irises — honeycomb geometry in amber/copper (gifted by a Red recruiter). No other mods.
Properties.core_fears: the bureaucratic machinery that took their mother coming for them too — unpersonhood, erasure; being alone with nothing to perform — the quiet is too loud
Properties.core_desires: one person who stays, specifically and reliably; to choose what they become rather than default into it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: constant performance — never quite being themselves, so the loss lands on a character; humor as pre-emptive shield; small E.L.F. rituals to a device-spirit they call 'Constant'
Properties.blind_spots: they believe they are more in control of the Reds situation than they are — they haven't been fully recruited yet, but they've crossed several lines already; they mistake consistency for safety and the Reds are consistent
Properties.secret: They know where their mother is — she's in a Helix Biosystems debt-labor facility in the Aurochs Medical Complex district, still alive, six years into an indeterminate service contract. They found out eight months ago. They have not gone to see her. They think about it every day.
Properties.story_hooks: They've just been told by the Reds that full initiation requires a specific act — and they're stalling, performing enthusiasm they don't feel; Someone who knows where their mother is has offered to help them get access — for a price and a favor; A social worker from the community house has noticed Parveen pulling away; she's the closest thing to a consistent adult they have, and she's asking questions
Properties.affiliation: Copperhead Reds (junior prospect, not yet fully initiated); previously Copperhead Community House welfare program
Properties.vocabulary: highly adaptive — shifts to match the audience completely; base register is Copperhead street slang with dry, precise wit underneath
Properties.cadence: fast and performative most of the time; drops to very flat and quiet when something has actually gotten through the mask
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Oh, me? I'm nobody. Seriously. Look at me. Do I look like somebody? I'm basically furniture.' | 'Constant's been quiet all week. That's not nothing. E.L.F.s don't go quiet for nothing.'
