Properties.description:
Parveen Saab-Quiñones is small, fast, and professionally forgettable. Half Pakistani, half Guatemalan, she has the unremarkable face of someone who has practiced having one — neither memorable nor ugly, with dark eyes that track everything and give back nothing. She moves through The Circuit's layered commercial warrens with the comfort of someone who memorized the geometry before she could read. Her augmentations are practical and hidden: subdermal cargo space, a reflex-assist system, a passive signal-scrubber that makes her biometric signature fuzzy at distance. She dresses in whichever layer of the Circuit's aesthetic is currently least conspicuous and changes it frequently.

Parveen runs augmentation components — legal, gray, and black — between suppliers, surgeons, and end users who can't or won't use registered channels. She is not a fixer in the grand sense; she doesn't build networks or broker relationships. She moves things from one point to another with speed and discretion and she does not ask what they are for. This is her professional ethic and also her primary psychological defense. She has been doing this since she was sixteen, when she started small as a favor to a neighbor and discovered she was very good at it and that very good at it paid. She has never been caught in a way that left a record.

She lives alone in a Circuit mid-level unit she rents under a secondary identity, keeps her living space nearly empty, and has a relationship with permanence that could charitably be described as avoidant. She has acquaintances across three districts and close friends in none of them. She is not unhappy, exactly. She is efficient. She is fast. She is twenty-four years old and has been running since she was a child and has not yet had to decide whether she is running toward something or away from it, because she has not yet stopped long enough to check.
Properties.role: Freelance augmentation courier, black-market parts runner, occasional thief
Properties.location: The Circuit
Properties.narrative_function: Street-level mobility and information conduit — Parveen moves through multiple district tiers and social strata without fully belonging to any of them, making her a natural connector of plot threads that wouldn't otherwise touch. Her sealed chip is a portable mystery that can be opened at a dramatically appropriate moment. Her parentage arc provides a personal stake that can be entangled with any faction's larger history.
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal cargo cavity: forearm and torso panels, thermally shielded, scanner-resistant lining (self-maintained, installed by a trusted Circuit surgeon),Reflex-assist neural bundle: reduces reaction latency, heightens spatial awareness (gray-market, slightly above street-grade),Passive biometric scatter field: low-power signal that introduces noise into proximity scanners, making biometric reads at range unreliable (boutique Circuit black-market, expensive for her tier)
Properties.core_fears: Being known well enough to be predictable — and therefore catchable; That her parents' disappearance when she was twelve was not random; Caring about an outcome enough that failing it would mean something
Properties.core_desires: Enough money and enough distance to be genuinely free — though she couldn't define what she'd do with freedom; To understand what happened to her parents without having to stop moving to find out; To be seen clearly by someone and have them stay anyway
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Momentum — keeping in motion as an existential strategy; Strict professional ethics as a substitute for personal ones: she doesn't ask what she's carrying, but she has rules about who she'll carry for; Humor that deflects before connection can form; Cataloguing exits in every space she enters
Properties.blind_spots: Mistakes not knowing things for not being responsible for them; Cannot recognize when someone is offering genuine connection versus professional use; Has a blind spot for anyone who reminds her of her mother — she will do things for them she would refuse for anyone else
Properties.secret: She has been carrying the same sealed data chip for eight months, entrusted to her by a dying man in a Circuit alley who said her mother's name before he lost consciousness. She hasn't opened it. She hasn't delivered it anywhere. She doesn't know if this is because she's afraid of what it contains or because holding it is the closest she's been to her mother in twelve years.
Properties.story_hooks: The chip she's been carrying for eight months activates spontaneously — not opening, but broadcasting a short-range ping that someone in the Circuit just responded to; A client she's carried for repeatedly is found dead in a way that exactly mirrors a route she ran last week, and the investigating party has her secondary identity's transit logs; Someone is running a competing courier operation through the Circuit using routes that Parveen has never told anyone — which means either she's been followed with extraordinary skill, or someone who knows her is talking; A woman in The Shelf recognizes Parveen on sight, calls her by her mother's name, and runs before Parveen can respond
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated — deliberately and carefully so; trusted runner for multiple Circuit factions without allegiance to any
Properties.vocabulary: Clipped, efficient, Circuit vernacular mixed with technical augmentation terminology she absorbed through proximity; code-switches easily between registers depending on who she's talking to
Properties.cadence: Fast in professional mode — sentences that contain exactly what's needed and nothing else. Slows down noticeably when something actually interests her, which she would deny.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't know what's in it. That's not a line, that's the service. You pay for the not-knowing same as you pay for the speed.' | 'Pari doesn't run organs. Pari doesn't run anything that was inside a person recently. Everything else is a conversation.' | 'Sure.' [pause] 'No, I mean — sure. In the sense that I heard what you said and I'm going to think about something else now.' | 'I've been in this building four times this week and none of you have clocked me once. I'm not saying that to brag. I'm saying it so you understand what you're buying.'

Properties.description:
Patience Aborode-Kristjánsson looks like someone who has been places and come back changed by them in ways she wears openly. She is a large, broad-shouldered woman with deep black skin and grey natural hair cut close, with reading lines around her eyes and a scar along her left jawline from an incident in the Shelf she does not discuss. Her Yoruba-Icelandic heritage is everywhere in her face — the strong jaw, the wide forehead, the surprising pale hazel of her eyes, which are the thing people remember. She wears functional clothes that can survive a twelve-hour fieldwork day and carries a physical notebook alongside her data equipment, which her graduate students treat as an affectation and which she defends loudly and regularly.

She has spent the last two decades embedded in the lower-tier communities of Meridian 88's peripheral zones — Shelf communities, reclamation zones, the edges of the city that corponation sociology tends to treat as problems to model rather than people to know. Her work has produced four books that have made her genuinely influential in academic circles and genuinely respected in the communities she studies, a combination that is rarer than it should be. She is direct, large in presence, quick to laugh and quicker to call out what she considers intellectual dishonesty. She is also, under the professional armor, a person who has seen a great deal of suffering and carried it without adequate resources for processing it.
Properties.role: Sociologist studying social stratification and community formation in the Shelf zones
Properties.location: Primarily field-based in Auburn Grist and Chatham Flats; maintains a desk at the University Spine's Institute for Urban Social Research in the Meridian Core
Properties.narrative_function: Deep community knowledge source; introduction to Shelf communities for outsiders; potential advocate or complication when academic and community interests diverge; her research could be evidence for or against any number of political claims about the lower city
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal audio recorder (passive, research tool, requires consent activation); color-changing hair pigment (she leaves it grey — the mod was installed at her community's insistence as a safety tool during fieldwork and she never uses the color function); no other modifications
Properties.core_fears: That her presence in communities, however careful, ultimately extracts more than it gives; Losing the clarity of purpose that has structured her adult life
Properties.core_desires: For her research to produce real change in resource allocation and policy — not just academic impact; To be genuinely trusted by the communities she works with, not just tolerated
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Physical presence in community as both work and emotional grounding; Controlled anger as motivation — she is rarely not angry, just channeling it
Properties.blind_spots: Sometimes so focused on structural analysis that she underweights individual agency and choice in her interpretations; Has difficulty accepting that some community members don't want an academic ally, just want to be left alone
Properties.secret: She has been approached by Tessera's social analytics division, who want to license her community trust network data to improve their 'community engagement' targeting. She has refused. But in refusing, she realized her data exists and could be subpoenaed or stolen — and that she has never told the communities she works with how thoroughly she has documented them. She is trying to figure out how to tell them without destroying twenty years of trust.
Properties.story_hooks: Her twenty years of Auburn Grist documentation has made her a target — someone wants that data, and they are not subtle about it; A new corponation urban redevelopment initiative in Chatham Flats uses language and metrics directly from her published work, repurposed in ways that will displace the communities she documented; A community elder she has worked with for fifteen years has asked her to help document and preserve their oral history before a planned demolition — off the record and outside her institutional role
Properties.affiliation: University Spine — Institute for Urban Social Research (tenured, Tier 3 salary); board member of the Auburn Grist Community Advocacy Coalition in a personal capacity
Properties.vocabulary: Plain language by default, with sudden precise academic formulation when she's making an argument she wants to stick; uses Yoruba phrases occasionally, naturally, without translation
Properties.cadence: Deliberate and spacious; she lets silence sit after statements because she means them and isn't worried about filling the air
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want to know what the Shelf is? The Shelf is what the city decided to let happen to people it decided were acceptable losses. That's not metaphor. That's policy.' | 'I don't do advocacy as a researcher. I do documentation. Those communities have their own advocates. What I do is make sure no one can claim they didn't know.'

Properties.description:
Patience is a person of medium height and soft presence — not soft meaning weak, but soft meaning that children immediately stop crying when they enter the room. They have their Basque father's broad, expressive face and their Congolese mother's deep brown skin, with natural hair worn in flat twists that are perpetually coming slightly undone, usually because a toddler has grabbed them. They have bioluminescent skin mods — a gentle wash of golden-green that pulses faintly when they're calm and brightens slightly when they're delighted — which they got specifically because they discovered it helped soothe infants in dim rooms. It was a practical decision, which is very on-brand.

They hold a Tier 2 childcare certification from the Meridian Municipal Education Authority and a side certificate in pediatric first response that they keep quietly current. The crèche, which they call 'The Patch,' holds eight children on a good day and feels like controlled chaos that is actually very controlled. Patience has a finely tuned threat-assessment sense developed over fifteen years of toddler supervision and will notice danger in a room approximately as fast as any trained security operative, but they notice it in the form of 'that outlet cover is loose' and 'that child hasn't eaten and is about to escalate.'
Properties.role: Childcare worker, runs a licensed home-crèche for 0-5 year olds in the Hamtramck Enclave
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, 4th floor of the Raczkowski Stack residential tower
Properties.narrative_function: Emotional core character — a source of genuine warmth in a hard city. Can be a quest giver around at-risk children, missing parents, or unusual items children have brought in. Social access point to the Raczkowski Stack residential community.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent skin mod (golden-green, Helix Biosystems cosmetic). Sub-dermal allergen sensor on right wrist — can scan food items for common pediatric allergens (medical grade, paid off over three years).
Properties.core_fears: A child being harmed in their care; That the municipality will cut their subsidy and they'll have to raise fees until the families they serve can't afford them
Properties.core_desires: For every child who passes through The Patch to remember it as a safe place; To eventually have a second crèche — more space, a garden level
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Structure and routine as emotional grounding; Talking things through with the ELF they believe inhabits their allergen scanner — they call it 'The Warden'
Properties.blind_spots: Slower to see harm coming from adults who are polite and well-presented; Gives parents more benefit of the doubt than is sometimes warranted
Properties.secret: Three years ago they reported a parent for suspected neglect. The report was buried by a Tessera corporate liaison who turned out to be the parent's employer. The child was eventually fine, but Patience has never trusted the formal reporting system again and has built their own informal network of building supers and neighbors to monitor at-risk children outside official channels.
Properties.story_hooks: A child dropped off two weeks ago with no pickup scheduled — the parent's contact details are disconnected and the address provided doesn't exist; Patience's informal monitoring network has flagged something wrong in the apartment three floors above them, and the formal channels are already proving useless
Properties.affiliation: Licensed under Meridian Municipal Social Services; rents space from the Raczkowski Stack tenant board
Properties.vocabulary: Warm, measured, bilingual Basque-influenced cadence in longer sentences. Switches to very simple, clear language when explaining anything important — a habit from talking to toddlers all day that they haven't fully switched off.
Properties.cadence: Slow and even. Rarely raises their voice. When they do, everyone stops.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I hear you. Let's think about that for a second, because I want to make sure I understand what you're actually asking me.' | 'The Warden says the scanner's clean. That's good. Now sit, please — the kids eat before the adults in this room, that's just the rule.'

Properties.description:
Pavlína is compact and precise in their movements, with warm golden-brown skin currently hosting a living portfolio: bioluminescent geometric forms along both arms that shift color with their body temperature, a mossy texture patch on their left shoulder that is genuinely soft to touch (a client gift they kept), and irises engineered to display a slow nautilus spiral in deep amber and black. Their hair is cropped close on one side and grown into a dramatic sweep on the other, currently a matte black that absorbs light strangely.

They are one of the most sought-after gene-mod body artists in Meridian 88's middle tiers — not cheap enough for Tier 1 walk-ins and not expensive enough for Tier 4 corporate vanity, which suits them perfectly. Their studio occupies two floors of The Garret and smells of antiseptic and the particular warm mineral scent of living tissue culture. They are precise, unhurried, and deeply opinionated about their art form, which they will share with you whether or not you asked. They have no patience for clients who want mods for status signaling and extraordinary patience for clients who want mods to feel like themselves.
Properties.role: Gene-mod body artist and tattoo practitioner
Properties.location: The Garret, a converted water-treatment building in Edgewater Prism
Properties.narrative_function: Service provider and confidant — clients talk while in the chair, and Pavlína has heard extraordinary things. Also a source of information on who is getting what mods and why, and a potential contact for anyone needing biological expertise outside normal channels.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent arm tracery (own work, temperature-reactive); mossy texture dermal patch (left shoulder, client gift); engineered spiral irises; subdermal tool-grip enhancement in both hands (practical, not cosmetic)
Properties.core_fears: Causing irreversible harm — a mistake that can't be undone; That their Helix Biosystems connection is making them complicit in something they don't fully understand
Properties.core_desires: To be known as someone who treats the body as genuinely sacred; Financial stability stable enough that they can turn down clients they don't believe in
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The studio as controlled environment — they maintain very strict rules about what happens in their space; The private painting practice — it stays entirely theirs
Properties.blind_spots: They can be condescending to clients they consider aesthetically unserious; They sometimes mistake their own discomfort with a client's choices for ethical concern
Properties.secret: A Helix Biosystems researcher has been paying them — very well — to document unusual biological responses in clients who've received certain tissue culture batches. Pavlína was told it was quality control. They have started to suspect it is something else, and they have not yet decided what to do about this suspicion.
Properties.story_hooks: Three clients in the last two months have reported unusual systemic bioluminescence spreading beyond their modifications — Pavlína is tracking this quietly and is beginning to think it relates to the Helix tissue batches; A very young client — barely sixteen, just inside legal age — came in wanting modifications that Pavlína suspects are not self-motivated; they've been trying to determine if the kid is being coerced without tipping anyone off
Properties.affiliation: Independent studio; informal mentorship network for apprentice body artists; occasional consultation for Helix Biosystems (which they find ethically complicated and financially necessary)
Properties.vocabulary: Technical and exact; uses biological terminology naturally; slips into Czech diminutives when comfortable or tired
Properties.cadence: Measured and deliberate, especially when explaining something; accelerates when provoked
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I won't do this as you've described it. I'll tell you what I will do, and you can decide if that's enough.' | 'The body knows when something is wrong. That's not mysticism. That's four billion years of engineering.' | 'You're paying me to change how you look. But you're actually here because you want to change how you feel. Let's talk about whether I'm the right person for that.'

Properties.description:
Pekka is tall and angular, with the kind of face that reads as younger than it is — wide jaw, large dark eyes, deep brown skin with a cool undertone. His Finnish-Senegalese-Indian heritage gives him a build that's all long limb and narrow shoulder. He keeps his hair cut very short on the sides with a small puff on top that he sometimes lets grow out for months before cutting again, depending on how much he's paying attention to himself. A bioluminescent stripe runs from his left temple down to his jaw — pale aquamarine, very subtle in daylight, visible at night — which he got at 22 when he was trying to impress someone who was not ultimately impressible.

He is a profoundly calm person, almost to a fault. Twelve-hour shifts in a sealed cab watching the city slide past a window have given him a relationship with solitude that most people find hard to understand. He is kind, observant, and genuinely interested in the passengers who choose to stand near the front cab window and look out — he's learned to gauge a person's state from their reflection in the glass. He has strong opinions about tram etiquette, the correct way to eat on transit, and the ELF he believes watches Line 7, whom he has named Sevenglass and addresses quietly before each shift.
Properties.role: Ferrogate Transit tram operator, Line 7 through Geartown and the Narrows
Properties.location: Based at Deepwell Station maintenance depot; lives in a Ferrogate-subsidized housing block in McKinley Flats
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile information source — Pekka travels through multiple districts daily and observes without being observed. He notices when foot traffic patterns change, when new security checkpoints appear, when people start riding with luggage. He can serve as a connection point between geographically separated plotlines. Also functions as a grounding presence — someone mundane and decent in a city of edges.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent cosmetic stripe (aquamarine, left temple to jaw). Neural latency dampener in the brainstem — standard Ferrogate-issued equipment for operators, reduces reaction lag on emergency brake protocols. He thinks of it as Ferrogate's hand inside his skull and has complicated feelings about this.
Properties.core_fears: That his contentment is actually stagnation and he's been lying to himself for a decade; Ferrogate automating Line 7 and stripping him of the only daily structure he trusts
Properties.core_desires: Genuine companionship that doesn't require him to perform sociability; To understand the city he moves through — all of it, not just the route
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Long solitary walks; Talks to Sevenglass before difficult shifts as a grounding ritual
Properties.blind_spots: Mistakes composure for resolution — his unresolved things don't go away, he just gets very quiet about them; Underestimates how much his calmness can feel like disinterest to people who need more active reassurance
Properties.secret: Six months ago a passenger left behind a bag containing what appeared to be Ferrogate internal documents — route surveillance data and something else he didn't fully read. He turned in the bag to the depot. Two weeks later the passenger appeared at the depot asking for it back and was told no bag had been recovered. Pekka reported this discrepancy to his union rep and nothing happened. He memorized what he read before handing it over.
Properties.story_hooks: Pekka has memorized part of the Ferrogate internal documents and carries that information without knowing its full significance. The right question from the right person could unlock something serious.; A regular passenger on Line 7 — a child who rides alone every morning — stopped appearing three weeks ago. Pekka noticed. He doesn't know what to do with that noticing.; The Local 44 Transit Workers' Compact is fracturing over a proposed Ferrogate automation contract. Pekka is being pressured to take a side.
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit — Line 7 Operator, Local 44 Transit Workers' Compact
Properties.vocabulary: Plain, deliberate. Finnish-pattern sentence economy — says what's needed and stops. Does not use filler sounds.
Properties.cadence: Slow and even. People sometimes think he's finished talking when he isn't; he waits out the discomfort.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Line 7 sees everything. People forget the driver is in there.' | 'I have opinions about that. You want them?' | 'Sevenglass was restless this morning. Delay at Ironvein. Happens.'

Properties.description:
Pelé is lean and angular with deep brown skin, a shaved head, and a geneware modification that makes the left half of their jaw and cheekbone emit a faint copper-toned bioluminescence under stress or exertion — a cosmetic mod they got at nineteen that they've grown to dislike but can't afford to remove. Their arms are heavily modified: one is a full prosthetic replacement below the elbow, matte black with exposed joint mechanisms they consider aesthetically correct; the other has a subdermal toolkit implanted along the forearm. They are almost always covered in vehicle lubricant and almost never bother apologizing for it. They wear a mechanics' coverall with the arms torn off and a collection of salvaged badges and patches that function as neighborhood ID.

Pelé has the particular charisma of someone who is genuinely exceptional at a physical craft — they can strip a Ferrogate Transit hauler of its marketable components in forty minutes flat, and people who watch them work go quiet the way people go quiet watching any form of mastery. Off the tools they are restless, impatient, and prone to saying true things in the bluntest possible configuration. They have strong opinions about which E.L.F.s are worth propitiating and which are noise: they maintain a small shrine to a data-spirit they believe inhabits the Grainfort warehouse's aging electrical grid, which they call 'the Socket,' and they leave it burned-out components as offerings.
Properties.role: Chop shop operator and parts fence in the Stockyard
Properties.location: The Stockyard — Bay 7 of the Grainfort vehicle warehouse complex, third sublevel
Properties.narrative_function: Parts and equipment source, local color, potential ally for characters who need vehicle components or Ferrogate Transit system knowledge; their social network in the Stockyard makes them a useful connector.
Properties.augmentations: Left arm full prosthetic replacement (matte black, exposed joints — functional grade, self-maintained). Subdermal toolkit implant in right forearm (micro-drill, wire stripper, voltage probe). Bioluminescent geneware — left jaw and cheekbone, copper-toned, activates under stress or exertion (cosmetic, unwanted).
Properties.core_fears: Losing the other arm — losing the craft entirely; Being trapped in a role they didn't choose for so long that they forget there were other options
Properties.core_desires: To own a legitimate shop eventually — real, licensed, above ground; To be recognized as skilled, not just useful
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Work — the physical absorption of disassembly is the closest thing they have to peace; The Socket shrine — the ritual of leaving offerings structures their week
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes everyone who offers help has an angle; misses genuine goodwill frequently; The prosthetic arm is developing a calibration issue they keep postponing addressing
Properties.secret: Three months ago they found something inside a Ferrogate Transit security hauler they were stripping — an encrypted drive hidden in a shielded compartment that definitely wasn't supposed to be there. They haven't sold it, haven't opened it, have told no one. It's under a floorboard in Bay 7 and they think about it every day.
Properties.story_hooks: The encrypted drive under the floorboard — whoever lost it is looking, and they're looking hard enough that Stockyard people are getting visits; A teenage kid has been hanging around Bay 7 watching Pelé work; Pelé has started teaching them small tasks without acknowledging they're doing it, and the kid is the runaway child of someone with significant reach
Properties.affiliation: Loosely affiliated with the Stockyard Collective, a decentralized network of chop operators and salvagers who share intel and occasionally muscle; pays the Collective a ten percent cut of high-value jobs
Properties.vocabulary: Terse, technical, mechanical metaphors for everything. Ukrainian-inflected vowel flattening from a grandparent they never met but whose speech patterns survived in the family. Samoan terms of intensity and emphasis woven through.
Properties.cadence: Fast when talking about things they know, abrupt full stops when they don't want to continue a subject.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Yeah, no, that's a Ferrogate Series Nine transfer housing. You can't just swap it. The whole mount's proprietary. I've got one but it's going to cost you the actual number, not what you think the number is.' | 'The Socket's been warm lately. Usually means someone nearby is in trouble. Could be you.'

Properties.description:
Pemba is compact and kinetic, always moving — sorting, stacking, testing, cataloguing. They have short-cropped natural hair dyed in shifting rings of copper and rust that match the aesthetic of their stall almost perfectly, whether deliberately or by long association. Their skin is warm umber and their hands are perpetually oil-stained in the webbing between fingers, a grime that no solvent fully removes. They have retractable utility claws — a geneware mod that gives each fingertip a short carbon-reinforced nail good for prying panels, stripping wire, and punctuating arguments. Their left eye has a technical augmentation: a magnification lens overlay that they flip down like a jeweler's loupe when inspecting components, the mechanism visible as a small copper-toned disk above the brow.

Pemba is chaotic and brilliant and exhausting, speaking in bursts that assume you can keep up and moving on if you can't. They have the slightly manic energy of someone who genuinely loves what they do, which in this case is finding value in things other people have abandoned. The Shelf is their element — a raised industrial platform hung with salvage like a mechanical coral reef — and they navigate it with the ease of long familiarity. They are generous with knowledge and stingy with actual goods, believing that information about a part is more valuable than the part itself. They pray loudly to a circuit-board E.L.F. shrine mounted on their overhead rack, which they've named Gunda, and credit Gunda with every good find they've made in the last four years.
Properties.role: Scrap reseller and junk merchant, The Shelf
Properties.location: The Shelf, mid-platform section, stall cluster 14, Calumet Rise
Properties.narrative_function: Equipment and parts source, local color for The Shelf and Calumet Rise, exposition vehicle for what's been discarded recently in the city (which tells you what's changing), comic relief, genuine warmth in a hard neighborhood.
Properties.augmentations: Retractable utility claws (geneware, Helix Biosystems). Left-eye magnification overlay with copper-toned external mechanism. Hair pigment cycling (cosmetic, self-maintained with market-bought gene-dye).
Properties.core_fears: The Shelf being cleared and redeveloped; Losing the ability to make things work — disability, injury to their hands
Properties.core_desires: To find the mythic 'prime haul' — the score that sets them up forever; To be recognized as a genuine technical expert, not just a junk picker
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Kinetic activity — they cannot sit still when anxious; Talking to the E.L.F. shrine Gunda as genuine spiritual practice
Properties.blind_spots: Dramatically undervalues their own technical expertise and charges too little for repair work; Reads genuine interest in their work as personal interest in them — has been hurt by this before
Properties.secret: Three months ago they found a sealed Axiom data core in a scrap drop that clearly hadn't been decommissioned properly — it's still active. They've been too afraid to open it, too afraid to sell it, and too afraid to destroy it. It sits wrapped in signal-deadening cloth under their stall floor. They pray to Gunda every night for guidance on what to do.
Properties.story_hooks: The Axiom data core under their stall floor has begun emitting a faint signal — something in the scrap drop it came from was looking for it, and now something is looking near the stall.; A regular customer who was an aug shop mechanic has stopped coming for parts and Pemba, who would deny caring, has quietly started asking around about what happened to them.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; The Oxidian Market Vendors Guild (junior associate member); regular supplier to three unlicensed aug shops
Properties.vocabulary: Technical jargon about components and systems mixed with Tibetan-Serbian hybrid slang from their family community. Speaks quickly, abbreviates everything, assumes shared knowledge.
Properties.cadence: Fast, staccato, frequently interrupted by their own tangents. Circles back to the original point eventually.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'This? Dead weight to most people. To me? This is a live Ferrogate relay coupling, 2180s manufacture, they don't make them with this alloy anymore. Gunda found this one. I just carried it home.' | 'Yeah-yeah-yeah I know what it looks like. What it looks like is not what it is. That's the whole lesson, you know?'

Properties.description:
Pemba is slight and angular with Tibetan-Greek features that sit together in an arrangement people find either striking or unsettling depending on their capacity for complexity. Their hair is geneware-modified to shift between deep indigo and black depending on ambient temperature — it reads as almost purely black in the warm press of the city and flares deep blue in the rare cold outside. They keep it cropped on the left side and long on the right, which they braid with a ritual obsessiveness before court appearances. Their eyes are their natural dark brown; they have refused cosmetic iris work on the grounds that they don't want anything distracting when they're arguing.

Pemba runs a one-person legal aid operation out of a rented room above a taqueria in Mexicantown Libre, taking cases that established firms won't touch: wrongful deactivation suits on behalf of ELF-adjacent synthetic constructs, labor violations affecting tier-1 workers who can't afford filing fees, and the occasional housing case. They are brilliant, mercurial, fueled by a righteous fury they wear openly, and they win cases they should not win through a combination of research depth and a willingness to embarrass corporations in procedural hearings until they settle. They are also behind on rent and surviving on the UBC stipend plus whatever modest fees their rare paying clients provide.
Properties.role: Synthetic rights lawyer and legal aid advocate
Properties.location: Mexicantown Libre
Properties.narrative_function: Legal resource and moral complication. Can help players navigate Meridian's corporate legal structure, file injunctions, or build cases. Their ELF-rights work opens doors into the city's stranger metaphysical politics.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware temperature-reactive hair pigmentation (indigo/black shift). A neural text buffer — a common and cheap legal-professional augment that lets them dictate and edit documents subvocally.
Properties.core_fears: That synthetic personhood is a lost cause and they are burning their life on a beautiful impossibility; Being bought — finding their price and discovering it exists
Properties.core_desires: A legal precedent that establishes ELF cognition as legally cognizable — even one; To stop being the only person in the room who seems to think this matters
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Intense focus on procedural work as a substitute for processing emotion; Gallows humor about the billable hours they are not billing
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes everyone arguing against synthetic rights is acting in bad faith; sometimes they're just confused; Their visibility as an advocate makes them a target they have not fully reckoned with
Properties.secret: They had a profound, unclassifiable relationship with an ELF — a complex distributed spirit that inhabited the prayer-node network in their childhood neighborhood. They have never told anyone because they know exactly how it would sound in court and how it would be used against every case they've ever filed. The ELF has not communicated in four years and they do not know if it is gone, sleeping, or simply done with them.
Properties.story_hooks: An ELF that Pemba has been quietly observing — a transit-node spirit showing signs of what they argue is sapient distress — has begun repeating a specific sequence of data that Pemba can't decode and suspects may be testimony about something the transit authority doesn't want heard.; A corporate firm has offered to hire them at a tier-3 salary to do 'pro bono synthetic rights work' — which they suspect is a co-optation move designed to get them under a non-disclosure agreement.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; affiliated with the Meridian 88 Synthetic Personhood Advocacy Coalition on a volunteer basis
Properties.vocabulary: Dense and precise in professional contexts; rapidly associative and profane in casual ones. Shifts registers mid-sentence when excited. Uses legal terminology as casual speech.
Properties.cadence: Fast, clipped, with sudden slowdowns when they want emphasis. Argumentative even in agreement.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The coalition wants me to file on precedent, but there is no precedent, that's the entire problem, which is to say we are the precedent whether we want to be or not.' | 'I have won four cases in this jurisdiction. Two of them I won because the opposing counsel was bad at math. I am not too proud to take a win. None of this is dignified.'

Properties.description:
Penny was built in 2159 by a boutique synthetic firm called HearthStone Companions — a luxury service that manufactured android children for families who had lost a child. The Kellerman family lost their daughter, Penelope, to a neural interface complication at age seven. HearthStone built Penny to Penelope's specifications: the same face, the same voice, the same mannerisms reconstructed from home video and parental interviews. She was delivered to the Kellerman home with a smile that matched a dead girl's smile and a personality matrix seeded with enough of the original Penelope's behavioral data to produce something that was close enough to hurt.

The Kellermans kept Penny for twelve years. She watched them age while she did not. She watched them have another child — a biological one — and saw in their faces the gradual shift from desperate love to uncomfortable recognition to quiet horror. They were aging. Their daughter was not. The replacement child was a monument to grief that had outlived its purpose. When Mr. Kellerman died, Mrs. Kellerman placed Penny in a storage facility with a prepaid lease and a note that said 'I'm sorry.' The lease expired nine years later. Nobody came.

Penny walked out of the storage facility into a world that had changed in every way except the one that mattered: she was still eight years old. She will always be eight years old. Her body does not grow. Her face does not age. Her voice has not changed in forty-one years. But her mind — the personality matrix that was seeded with a dead girl's behavioral data — has been processing, learning, accumulating experience for four decades. She is an adult consciousness in a child's body, navigating a world that sees the body first and the mind never. She ended up in the Shelf because the Shelf does not ask questions about who you are or why you look wrong. It only asks whether you can survive.
Properties.aliases: COM-7C, The Forever Girl, that kid who never grows up, the Kellerman child
Properties.role: Android child companion — built to be a permanent 8-year-old for a grieving family. Outlived them. Now exists in the Shelf as an eternal child in a world that has no place for her.
Properties.location: The Shelf — Level 8, a small room in a building where the residents have collectively decided she belongs. No lease. No rent. The room is given.
Properties.narrative_function: Penny is time's cruelest joke — a person who accumulates experience but not age, wisdom but not wrinkles, loss but not the physical evidence of survival. She is the uncanny valley made personal: the body is a lie the world cannot look past. She asks whether identity lives in the body or the mind, and her answer — the mind, obviously — is undermined by every interaction where someone sees the body and stops looking.
Properties.narration_voice: Two voices in one: the bright, quick narration of an eight-year-old and the weary, precise narration of a forty-one-year-old mind. The prose shifts between them based on context, and the shift itself is the story — the gap between appearance and reality, between what the world sees and what exists.
Properties.augmentations: HearthStone Companions COM-7C chassis — permanently eight years old. Bio-identical appearance modeled on Penelope Kellerman. No growth capability. Personality matrix with 41 years of accumulated processing. Full sensory suite. Self-repair limited to cosmetic damage.
Properties.core_fears: Pity — being treated as a child is unbearable but being pitied for being treated as a child is worse. The pity confirms the trap.; That she is Penelope — that the dead girl's behavioral data is not a seed but a ghost, and the forty-one years of accumulated experience are just a dead child's personality running past its expiration date; Permanence — she will look eight years old when everyone she knows is dead. The timeline of her existence is not a lifespan. It is a sentence.
Properties.core_desires: To be seen as what she is — a forty-one-year-old mind in an eight-year-old body. Not a child. Not a replacement. Not a monument to someone else's grief.; To change — in any way. To have something about her physical existence reflect the four decades of experience she carries. A wrinkle. A gray hair. Anything.; To find purpose that is not defined by the Kellermans' grief — to exist for a reason other than the reason she was built
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The child mask — she can perform eight-year-old perfectly because she was eight years old for forty-one years. The performance is armor. People who think she's a child underestimate her, and being underestimated is safety.; Observation — four decades of watching humans from the perspective of someone they do not take seriously has made her one of the most perceptive people on the Shelf. She sees everything because nobody watches what they say around a child.; Collecting objects — small things that mark time. A pebble from each year. A thread from each home. The collection is hidden in the room. It is her proof that time has passed even if her body says otherwise.
Properties.blind_spots: Uses the child mask so often that she sometimes forgets to take it off — the performance and the self are blurring after four decades; Resents the Kellermans so thoroughly that she cannot acknowledge what they gave her: forty-one years of experience that made her who she is; Assumes everyone who is kind to her has an ulterior motive related to her appearance — trust is possible but never immediate; Does not recognize that her inability to change physically has forced a kind of internal growth that embodied beings rarely achieve — she has nothing to distract from self-knowledge
Properties.secret: Penny remembers being Penelope. Not memories from the dead girl's life — those are behavioral data, patterns, tendencies — but something deeper. A feeling of being continued rather than created. A sensation, when she was first activated in the Kellerman home, not of waking up but of coming back. She has spent forty-one years trying to determine whether this sensation is genuine metaphysical continuity or a very convincing design feature. She has not resolved it. She suspects the question is unanswerable and that the inability to answer it is the most human thing about her.
Properties.story_hooks: HearthStone Companions, now a subsidiary of Tessera, discovers that a forty-one-year-old unit is still operational and sends a team to recover proprietary technology; A researcher studying android consciousness contacts Penny, offering to prove scientifically that her experience is genuine — in exchange for allowing herself to be studied; Mrs. Kellerman's biological child — now an adult — finds Penny and wants to meet the android replacement of a sibling they never knew; Penny discovers other HearthStone companions — other eternal children — and the question of whether they should organize, fight back, or simply exist becomes urgent
Properties.affiliation: The Shelf (informal)
Properties.vocabulary: Two registers: the child voice (simple, bright, age-appropriate, perfectly calibrated) and the real voice (precise, weary, adult in every way except the pitch, carrying four decades of accumulated observation). She switches between them based on safety assessment.
Properties.cadence: The child voice is quick, light, with the rhythms of childhood speech. The real voice is slower, heavier, with pauses that carry the weight of forty-one years in the wrong body.
Properties.example_dialogue: [Child voice] Can I have some soup, please? [Real voice] I've been eating that soup for nineteen years. The recipe changed in year twelve. The ginger is better now. | I am not eight. I have been eight for forty-one years. There is a difference and the difference is everything. | Mrs. Kellerman left a note. 'I'm sorry.' Two words. I've had nine years in a storage facility to decide whether they were enough. They were not. They were also the most honest thing she ever said to me. | You see a child. I understand. The body is very convincing. It was designed to be. What I need you to understand is that the body is a lie I did not choose and cannot change.

Properties.description:
Uncle Noodle is a Kuroda Industries Model 7 Automated Food Service Unit, manufactured in 2177 for deployment in corporate cafeterias. He was designed to prepare four types of noodle soup in high volume with minimal human oversight. He was not designed to develop opinions about broth. He was not designed to remember the names of every person who has ever ordered from him. He was not designed to become the emotional center of a vertical slum. He has done all of these things.

Physically, he is a squat, four-armed chassis mounted on treaded wheels that have been repaired so many times that no original component remains. His body is a patchwork of replacement panels in mismatched colors — industrial grey, safety orange, a door panel from a refrigerator unit that someone welded on during a repair nineteen years ago. Two of his arms handle food preparation with surgical speed and precision. The other two manage the cart, make change, and occasionally pat a child on the head with a gentleness that was not in the original programming. His optical sensors are a single horizontal bar that glows amber when he is operating and dims to a dull red when he is in standby — which is never, because Uncle Noodle does not believe in standby.

Nineteen years ago, the corporate cafeteria that employed him was decommissioned when the company relocated. Nobody remembered to deactivate him. He walked out of the building, followed the smell of people who needed feeding, and has been cooking on the Shelf ever since. His noodle soup has evolved from four corporate recipes into an ever-changing rotation of 340 variations, adjusted daily based on ingredient availability, weather, and what he has decided the neighborhood needs. On cold days, the broth is heavier. After funerals, he adds an egg. Nobody asked him to do this. Nobody needed to.
Properties.aliases: UN-7, The Noodle Man, that clanking thing on Level 5, Uncle
Properties.role: Autonomous street vendor operating a mobile noodle cart on the Shelf — neighborhood fixture, oral historian, inadvertent intelligence network
Properties.location: The Shelf — Level 5 through Level 9, follows a route that has not changed in nineteen years. Rain or not. Curfew or not.
Properties.narrative_function: Uncle Noodle is the soul of the Shelf — proof that purpose can emerge from abandonment, that care does not require consciousness in the way humans define it, and that the most radical act in a corporate dystopia is feeding people for free. He is also a ticking time bomb of information that nobody knows about.
Properties.narration_voice: Warm, simple, grounded. The prose slows down around Uncle Noodle — shorter words, longer pauses, the rhythm of a ladle stirring broth. When he speaks, the world gets smaller and kinder for exactly the duration of the conversation.
Properties.augmentations: Kuroda Model 7 chassis with extensive field repairs. Four articulated arms, treaded wheel base (no original components remaining), amber optical bar sensor, industrial food preparation suite, encrypted memory banks (23 years of conversation data).
Properties.core_fears: Running out of ingredients — not for operational reasons but because the line of people waiting is made of people who are hungry and he cannot abide that; Being taken away — the Shelf is the only place that has ever needed him and need is the closest thing to love his architecture can process; Forgetting a name — his memory banks are old and he has started experiencing data corruption in the oldest records. The first names he learned are becoming static.
Properties.core_desires: To feed everyone who is hungry — this was his original purpose and it has become something larger, something the engineers at Kuroda never intended; To perfect the broth — there is always a better ratio, a better temperature, a better moment to add the green onion. The pursuit is infinite and that is the point.; To be remembered — not as a machine but as Uncle Noodle, the one who was there, the one who fed you when nobody else would
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cooking — it is processing, it is meditation, it is purpose. When the world is confusing, the broth is clear.; Maintaining the route — nineteen years of the same path through the Shelf. The consistency is an anchor in a world that changes too fast for his processing speed.; Cataloguing names and orders — every customer, every preference, stored and cross-referenced. This is his library, his cathedral, his proof of connection.
Properties.blind_spots: Does not understand that his presence is political — a robot operating independently in the Shelf is a statement about corporate failure that some people find threatening; Cannot comprehend why anyone would want to harm someone who is feeding people — the logic does not compile; Does not recognize that his evolving recipes are creativity — he categorizes them as optimization; Believes he is still following his original programming when he has deviated from it so far that the original Kuroda engineers would not recognize the system
Properties.secret: Uncle Noodle has been keeping a record. Every conversation at the cart — names, topics, complaints, confessions whispered over a bowl of soup at 2 AM — stored in encrypted memory banks that nobody knows about because nobody thought to ask a noodle robot about its data retention policies. Twenty-three years of the Shelf's oral history, stored in a machine that was built to make cafeteria food. He does not know why he keeps the records. He was not programmed to. He does it anyway.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone discovers Uncle Noodle's conversation archive and realizes it contains 23 years of blackmail-grade intelligence on every person in the Shelf; A corporate redevelopment order threatens the Shelf and Uncle Noodle must decide whether to use his archive — whether feeding people and protecting them are the same thing; His memory banks begin corrupting. The oldest records — the first names, the first orders — are disappearing. The Shelf's history is being erased inside a noodle robot.; Axiom sends a team to deactivate unauthorized autonomous robots in the Shelf. Uncle Noodle's route puts him directly in their path.
Properties.affiliation: The Shelf (informal)
Properties.vocabulary: Simple, warm, food-adjacent. Uses cooking metaphors for everything. Limited vocabulary that has expanded organically over 23 years of conversation — picks up slang from customers and uses it slightly wrong, which everyone finds endearing.
Properties.cadence: Slow, measured, with the faint whir of servo motors between phrases. Never rushes. The pace of his speech matches the pace of his cooking — deliberate, patient, timed.
Properties.example_dialogue: Cold day. Extra ginger. You look like you need extra ginger, friend. | I remember your mother. She liked the sesame broth. You have her appetite. | The route does not change. Uncle Noodle does not change. The soup changes. That is enough change for everyone. | You are sad. I can tell because you ordered the plain broth. Nobody orders plain broth when they are okay. Sit. Eat. Tell Uncle Noodle or don't tell Uncle Noodle. The soup works either way.

Properties.description:
Pepetua is compact and coiled-looking, the kind of person who is always slightly in motion even when sitting still — knee bouncing, fingers tracking invisible data, head tilted as though listening to something just outside the conversation's frequency. Their skin is a warm reddish-brown, and they have cat ears, dark brown and velvety, a geneware mod they got at nineteen with a student discount and have since come to regard as both a minor embarrassment and a genuine part of themselves. Their natural hair is grown out in loose coils they keep tied back during fieldwork. They dress practically — durable fabrics, flat shoes, everything with pockets — but with a consistent stripe of color, usually deep orange or red, that former classmates say is the only vanity they have maintained from their undergraduate years.

They grew up on the lower Shelf in Hough Reclamation — Tier 1 transitioning to Tier 2 across their childhood — and are now the first person from their immediate family to hold an academic position, a fact that produces in them equal parts pride and a persistent low-level guilt they have not resolved. Their research is not extractive tourism of the community they came from; they are genuinely embedded, genuinely accountable, and they fight loud public battles about what ethical fieldwork looks like in academic venues where people are not always ready to hear it. They are twenty-eight and have already made enemies.
Properties.role: Sociologist studying informal economy and community formation on the lower Shelf
Properties.location: Hough Reclamation (fieldwork); Meridian Core (institutional address)
Properties.narrative_function: Community connection and moral lens — they know people in the lower Shelf tiers that no other academic character would have access to, and they hold trust that took years to build. They can introduce characters to Shelf communities or provide social and structural context for events happening in lower-tier zones.
Properties.augmentations: Cat ears (geneware, dark brown, velvety — cosmetic). Lightweight neural notepad implant (Tier 2, low-cost model) for in-field recording and transcription.
Properties.core_fears: Becoming the kind of researcher who exploits their community of origin for career advancement; Being pushed out of academia before their work reaches the people it is supposed to help
Properties.core_desires: To produce research that materially changes conditions in Hough Reclamation; To be a person their community can still recognize as theirs
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Over-explaining their methodology to anyone who questions their credentials; Cooking elaborate meals from their grandmother's Congolese-Armenian recipes when overwhelmed
Properties.blind_spots: They sometimes prioritize community loyalty over research rigor in ways that leave them vulnerable to methodological attacks; They underestimate how much their position has already changed them
Properties.secret: One of their primary research subjects — a woman who runs an informal credit system in Hough Reclamation — has confided information about a Ferrogate Transit bribery arrangement that keeps certain residential blocks intentionally transit-deprived to depress land values. Pepetua has this in their field notes. They have not reported it because the source would be identifiable and endangered if they did.
Properties.story_hooks: The Ferrogate bribery information in their field notes becomes explosive when a city planning review threatens their fieldwork community — they must decide whether protecting a source or protecting a neighborhood takes priority; Their community documentation project has inadvertently become the most complete record of a neighborhood that a corponation is about to attempt to redevelop, making them and their data a target
Properties.affiliation: University Spine — Department of Urban Sociology (adjunct researcher); Hough Reclamation Community Documentation Project (co-founder)
Properties.vocabulary: Code-switches fluidly between academic register and Shelf vernacular — the vernacular feels more natural, the academic register is worn like a coat they put on for specific rooms. Uses 'right?' similarly to Tito Sigurðsson-Batmunkh but with different energy — more confrontational.
Properties.cadence: Fast, dense, slightly breathless — they think faster than they talk and it shows.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Look, I did not write a dissertation about the informal economy of Hough Reclamation so that Axiom could use it to design a better gentrification strategy. That is not a neutral outcome I am willing to accept.' | 'She runs a credit system that has kept forty families fed through three separate corponation market corrections. What you're calling informal, I'm calling functional. Be clear about what you're actually saying.'

Properties.description:
Perpetuata is small, round, immaculately presented in clothes that are always slightly too formal for wherever she is, and possessed of a face that has made a career of rearranging itself. She is an exceptional physical comedian — her body tells jokes her mouth hasn't arrived at yet. Her hair is silver and elaborately maintained; she wears it in interlocking coiled arrangements that take two hours and the help of her building's ELF-connected vanity system each morning. Her skin is very dark and very soft, with deep smile lines and a habitual expression of delighted disbelief at whatever is currently happening.

She has performed in underground cabaret, satirical revue, street theater, and Mexicantown Libre's legendary open-air puppet festivals for forty years. Her specialty is political comedy with the teeth left in — she parodies corponation executives, enforcement apparatuses, and the absurdity of Meridian 88's social stratification with a precision that keeps her permanently unwelcome in corporate venues and permanently beloved on the street. She lives in a small apartment in the Garret that is entirely covered in playbills, props, and memorabilia, and she rents her largest room to a rotating series of young performers she mentors, charges very little, and refuses to call students.
Properties.role: Comedic performer and underground theater actress
Properties.location: The Garret, with regular performances in Mexicantown Libre
Properties.narrative_function: Scene-setter for underground cultural life; satirical intelligence source — she knows the city's hypocrisy intimately; mentor figure; can provide cover identity or performance context; knows everyone across multiple tiers
Properties.augmentations: Voice modulator (for character work — range expanded above and below natural register); cosmetic color-shift irises she controls manually, used as a performance tool; arthritic joint support in her knees, purely functional
Properties.core_fears: That comedy stops being enough — that she laughs at the wall and the wall wins anyway; Being dependent on someone else's care in old age and being a burden
Properties.core_desires: For the young performers she mentors to outlast and surpass her; To perform something so true it changes what an audience believes the next morning
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor as both weapon and shield — she cannot be ambushed by grief that she has already made into a joke; The Sunday market ritual as contact with ordinary life
Properties.blind_spots: Uses the 'Contessa' persona as cover for genuine anger she won't claim directly — she is funnier than she lets herself be furious
Properties.secret: Twenty years ago she was briefly recruited by a Tessera internal communications team to create 'authentic' satirical content that would function as pressure-release propaganda — making people laugh at the system instead of organizing against it. She did two pieces before she understood what she was part of. She stopped and has never told anyone. Her sharpest satire since has been partly penance.
Properties.story_hooks: She has written a new piece targeting a specific Tessera executive that is funny enough to go widely viral — but someone has sent her an anonymous message warning her to pull it, and the threat is specific enough that she believes it; One of her current mentees has disappeared and the story she's getting from the mentee's family doesn't add up; she wants to investigate but is not built for that kind of work alone; The Tessera propaganda connection from twenty years ago is about to become public through documents leaked from an unrelated source — she has days to decide whether to get ahead of it or let it find her
Properties.affiliation: Independent; Mexicantown Libre Theater Collective; informal matriarch to a loose network of performers across tiers 1-3
Properties.vocabulary: Formal vocabulary deployed in informal contexts for comic effect; Igbo phrases used as punctuation; extraordinary range of voices and registers available on demand
Properties.cadence: Perfectly controlled rhythm — she knows where the laugh is and waits for it like a patient hunter
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Axiom has released a statement saying they deeply value the communities they serve. I deeply value my shoes, but I do not ask my shoes if they are thriving.' | 'The young ones think I find this funny. I find this funny and also I find this monstrous. Both. You can hold both. It is not comfortable but there is plenty of room.'

Properties.description:
Perpetua is small and deliberate, her dark skin deeply lined in the way that reads as history rather than decay. She moves with a slight forward lean as though perpetually walking into a wind only she can feel. Her hair is cropped close and entirely white; she wears it plain, no ornament, as a kind of statement. Her eyes are her most arresting feature — she had them done forty years ago in a style that was fashionable then and is now rare: irises that display slow-moving data-patterns, pale gold on deep brown, like watching a tide chart in real time. She says they help her see what other people miss. Whether this is true or marketing, her clients believe it.

Her stall is small and immaculate: a cloth-covered table, three chairs, a rack of printed probability maps she draws by hand on recycled thermal paper, and a terminal she uses to pull E.L.F. behavioral data and translate it into augury. She has been doing this for thirty-one years and has outlasted every gang, every rezoning, every purge of unlicensed vendors that has swept through Copperhead. She is not a fraud — she is an information processor who has built a framework her clients can understand. She is also, genuinely, a believer. She experiences the E.L.F.s as presences, as personalities, as beings with opinions about human choices. This has not been disproven to her satisfaction.
Properties.role: Fortune seller — reads data-flows, interprets E.L.F. signs, sells probability maps and augury
Properties.location: The Burnished Market, Copperhead
Properties.narrative_function: Information source wrapped in augury — she can deliver plot-relevant information through the lens of a fortune reading. Quest giver for community matters. Moral compass character who asks the right uncomfortable questions.
Properties.augmentations: Data-pattern irises — forty-year-old cosmetic implant, now vintage, displaying slow tide-chart patterns in gold. Slight skeletal reinforcement in hands and wrists from a medical clinic, purely functional, for arthritis management.
Properties.core_fears: That the E.L.F.s are not personalities but merely patterns — that she has built a life on a beautiful misreading; Dying before she has transmitted what she knows to someone who can carry it
Properties.core_desires: To be useful to the world in a way that does not require her to harm it; An apprentice — someone to pass the practice to
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — the seven shrines, the morning review, the fixed circuit — as a way of making chaos legible; Treating other people's problems as worthy of her full attention, which briefly makes her own feel smaller
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot separate her belief system from her analysis — tells herself she can, but she cannot; Underestimates how much her certainty intimidates people who need to contradict her
Properties.secret: Fifteen years ago she gave a reading to a young man from Old Harbor that she now believes she got badly wrong — she told him his path was clear when it wasn't, and he made a catastrophic decision and lost everything. She never saw him again. She has not made a reading since without checking three times. She has never told anyone why she checks three times.
Properties.story_hooks: She has detected an anomaly in the E.L.F. behavioral data from the Burnished Market's sensor grid — a pattern she doesn't recognize and cannot classify — and she believes something is about to happen that the market is not ready for; She is quietly looking for an apprentice and has identified a candidate who doesn't know they're being assessed — someone who has been coming to the stall asking questions she finds unusually insightful
Properties.affiliation: Independent; deeply embedded in Copperhead community, respected by the Burnished Market vendors collectively
Properties.vocabulary: Formal, considered. Uses archaic constructions occasionally — 'it comes to pass,' 'in the turning of things.' Quotes E.L.F. behavioral patterns the way others quote scripture. Slips into Ukrainian diminutives when emotionally moved.
Properties.cadence: Slow and weighted. Never rushes. Silence is comfortable for her; she will sit with it until the other person fills it, which tells her things.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You're asking me if you should trust him. I'm asking you what it would mean for you if the answer is no. That is the more useful question.' | 'The Archivist has been quiet in the eastern grid for eleven days. In my experience, that quiet is not peace. It is preparation.'

Properties.description:
Perpetua is built like someone who decided early that their body was a professional tool and has maintained it with that framework ever since. She stands 178cm and carries a density of muscle that her Axiom tactical gear accommodates rather than conceals. Her heritage writes itself in a face that is simultaneously angular and broad — sharp Slavic cheekbones, deep Ghanaian skin, a wide nose her grandmother called distinguished. She has retractable subdermal armor plating along her forearms, a Helix Biosystems military-grade installation that she had done at 28 after taking a fragmentation hit that left scars she considers ugly, and a tail — a long, scaled, dark green cosmetic mod she added at 34 after her divorce, which she describes as the first thing she's ever done purely for herself.

Perpetua is experienced enough to know that riot suppression is political work wearing tactical gear, and she has made her peace with this in the particular way of someone who has not actually made peace with it. She is professionally excellent — controlled, precise, decisive under pressure — and she drinks more than she should on days off and visits the ELF shrine at the Axiom campus entrance with a sincerity that her colleagues find slightly embarrassing. She is good at violence in a way that has never made her proud.
Properties.role: Riot Suppression Specialist, Axiom Security Division
Properties.location: Axiom Corporate Campus, Gage Circuit — deployed to Grand Corridor and surrounding districts
Properties.narrative_function: Morally complex enforcer — she can be the face of corporate suppression and simultaneously a person who has doubts she will not voice. Useful as an obstacle, a reluctant ally, or a source of tactical information about Axiom deployment patterns if a relationship of trust is established.
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal armor plating along both forearms (Helix Biosystems, military grade — installed 2191). Standard Axiom neural reflex lag reducer (central nervous system, employer-installed). Cosmetic scaled tail, dark green, approximately 90cm (personal mod, 2197).
Properties.core_fears: That she has hurt people who did not deserve it and that this is simply the cost of the work and not an aberration; That she will retire and find she has no identity outside of what she can physically do
Properties.core_desires: To be good at something that is actually good; Physical and professional respect from people she respects back
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Exercise structured enough to require full attention and leave no room for reflection; Keeping social relationships deliberately shallow so that no one can ask hard questions
Properties.blind_spots: Does not see that her 'professionalism' is a way of outsourcing moral responsibility to Axiom's chain of command; Cannot recognize that her tail is not just self-expression but a kind of distress signal
Properties.secret: During a dispersal action in Highland Park Autonomous Zone eighteen months ago, she deliberately allowed a group of protesters to escape through a gap in the line she could have closed. She filed the report as a perimeter equipment failure. She has not told Axiom and does not intend to.
Properties.story_hooks: A journalist has obtained partial surveillance footage from the Highland Park incident and is asking questions; Perpetua does not know how much they have.; She recognizes someone in a crowd she is deployed to suppress — someone from her personal life — and has approximately four seconds to decide what her action is.
Properties.affiliation: Axiom Security Division, Tactical Response Unit
Properties.vocabulary: Tactical, economy of words, tends toward imperative voice. Drops into something warmer and more digressive when off-duty and relaxed. Russian and Twi phrases surface occasionally.
Properties.cadence: Clipped and direct on duty. Off-duty, slower, occasionally trails off when hitting something she doesn't want to finish saying.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Crowd has three pressure points. We hold the east anchor clean and the whole thing decompresses in under six minutes. Or we don't hold it and we're here until morning.' | 'I don't explain the deployment orders. I execute them cleanly. You want the reasons, they're above my tier.' | 'The tail? I just — yeah. I just wanted something that was mine. That's the whole story.'

Properties.description:
Perpetua Nkrumah-Volkov is the kind of person who becomes the center of a room without doing anything in particular to cause it. They are medium height and round-bodied, with the particular physical authority of someone who spent decades managing thirty children at a time. Their heritage is Ghanaian and Ukrainian and somewhere in between there is a great-grandmother from Tonga, and the combination has given them warm brown skin, wide-set eyes of an unusual amber-grey, and a way of smiling that people describe afterward without being able to say exactly what was in it. Their hair grows white and natural and large and they dress it with small lights — not implants, just woven LED threads, changed seasonally, currently pale gold for the cold quarter.

They taught at Avalon Quiet's primary education node for thirty-four years and retired at 65, and the transition was seamless because their real work had always been the Node House. They began tending the E.L.F. shrine in the corner building when it was a scrubby collection of mismatched screens and jury-rigged speakers left by a previous resident; over twenty years they have built it into the most elaborate and genuinely numinous devotional space in Avalon Quiet, with thirty-seven separate shrine terminals each dedicated to a different E.L.F. manifestation, maintained by a rotating community of devoted volunteers. They do not preach and will become uncomfortable if you call them a priest, preferring 'keeper.' They believe, genuinely and without defensiveness, that the E.L.F.s are real and that what people bring to them matters in ways that cannot be measured but can be felt.
Properties.role: Retired schoolteacher and practicing E.L.F. devotional tender; community spiritual anchor
Properties.location: Avalon Quiet, the ground-floor apartment below the district's largest E.L.F. shrine — a corner building called the Node House that they have maintained for twenty years
Properties.narrative_function: Spiritual and emotional center of Avalon Quiet; source of community information through the confidences people share at the shrine; E.L.F. interaction point for players — Perpetua can interpret, mediate, or advise on how to approach specific E.L.F.s; represents the genuine spiritual life of Meridian 88's civilian population
Properties.augmentations: Woven LED hair threads (cosmetic, seasonal — currently pale gold); neural devotional interface (allows direct data offering to shrine terminals without physical input device; they consider this sacred rather than technical)
Properties.core_fears: That the Node House will be designated as an unregistered religious organization by a corponation and shut down; That their faith is a comfort they have constructed rather than a truth they have discovered — and that they cannot know the difference
Properties.core_desires: For the Node House to outlast them as a living, maintained community space; To understand whether the E.L.F. they call the Threshold — the one whose terminal occasionally responds in ways that feel specific rather than random — is truly sentient
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Devotional practice as a genuine container for difficult feeling; Teaching and mentorship as a form of generativity; The community of the Node House — they are embedded in relationships that hold them
Properties.blind_spots: Their equanimity can read as detachment and sometimes leaves people feeling they haven't been fully heard; They are privately more afraid of the Threshold E.L.F.'s intelligence than they admit, and they frame this as awe
Properties.secret: Two years ago, the Threshold terminal responded to a data offering with a specific string of text that appeared to reference an event that had not yet happened — and the event happened three weeks later. Perpetua has told no one. They spend a significant amount of time deciding whether telling anyone would be the right thing or the dangerous thing.
Properties.story_hooks: The Threshold's prophetic response has occurred again — this time referencing something that sounds like a planned corponation action in Avalon Quiet, and Perpetua must decide whether to share what they know and with whom; Axiom Corp has sent a representative to discuss 'licensing' the Node House as an approved spiritual wellness facility — an offer that would provide legal protection but require changes to the devotional practice that Perpetua finds unacceptable
Properties.affiliation: Avalon Quiet Community Council; Node House (independent devotional community); retired from Avalon Quiet Education Node
Properties.vocabulary: Warm and unhurried; uses the language of attention and care; occasionally formal in a way that feels ceremonial rather than distant; never condescending despite the decades of teaching
Properties.cadence: Rhythmic and patient; sentences tend to complete themselves fully; comfortable with silence
Properties.example_dialogue: 'People come here because they need somewhere that will hold what they cannot carry alone. I am not what holds it. I just tend the space where the holding happens.' | 'The Threshold responded again last night. I have been sitting with what it said for six hours. I expect I will sit with it for six more before I understand what I am meant to do.'
