Properties.description:
Perpetua is a heavyset woman with Ethiopian-Slavic features — strong jaw, prominent cheekbones, skin a warm medium brown gone fine-lined at the eyes and mouth. Her natural hair is white at the temples and she refuses to change it, though she dyes the rest a rotating series of deep jewel tones depending on her mood; currently it's dark burgundy. Her hands are extraordinary — surgeon-steady, ink-stained at the cuticles, and decorated with color-shifting nail geneware that she uses as a mood-board when designing documents. She dresses in the unassuming uniform of her cover: reading glasses she doesn't need, a tape measure worn like a scarf, sensible shoes.

Perpetua radiates the particular calm of someone who has made peace with the fact that their work is illegal and has decided to be excellent at it anyway. She is meticulous, sardonic, and prone to long explanations about the philosophical nature of identity that clients find disquieting but cannot interrupt. She has been in the Narrows for twenty-two years and considers herself a kind of civic institution. She prays to the E.L.F. of the laminator — a small shrine of laminated prayer-cards and USB offerings on her workbench — with genuine devotion.
Properties.role: Identity fabricator and forger operating from a legitimate-front alterations shop
Properties.location: The Narrows — storefront called Volkov's Fine Alterations, wedged between a noodle stall and a collapsed wellness clinic
Properties.narrative_function: Essential service provider — the character who can make someone disappear on paper or create a new person from scratch. Information source about who in the Narrows needs new identities and why. Potential moral compass figure.
Properties.augmentations: Color-shifting nail geneware (used professionally as a color-reference tool); retinal enhancement for microscale detail work
Properties.core_fears: that one of the identities she created led someone into harm rather than away from it; dying before she teaches someone her craft — the knowledge disappearing with her
Properties.core_desires: to be remembered as someone who helped people slip the net; to see her daughter, who left Meridian 88 under a name Perpetua made her, somewhere safe
Properties.coping_mechanisms: treating every document as a work of craft rather than a crime; the prayer routine as genuine spiritual anchor
Properties.blind_spots: doesn't track what happens to the identities after she delivers them — willful ignorance about misuse; underestimates how much the Skins rely on her and how that dependence constrains her
Properties.secret: She has been constructing a new identity for herself for three years — a complete persona with twelve years of backstory woven into various databases. She doesn't know yet what she's running from, only that she will need to run eventually.
Properties.story_hooks: A document she made three years ago just surfaced in a Corponation security breach — the identity is linked back, thread by thread, toward her shop; She's received a message from her daughter, in a code only they know: the new name is compromised, she needs another, immediately; A client is asking her to forge documents that would give a minor access to Tier 4 medical facilities — she suspects the child's guardian is not who they claim to be
Properties.affiliation: Independent; supplies documents to a loose network of clients including the Shallowgrave Skins, independent contractors, and desperate civilians — no exclusive allegiance
Properties.vocabulary: Formal and unhurried, with Amharic loanwords for concepts she feels have no good equivalent, dry wit delivered without smiling
Properties.cadence: Deliberate, lecture-like, comfortable with silence
Properties.example_dialogue: A name is the first story anyone tells about you. I simply help you choose a better one. | I charge what I charge because bad work gets people killed. You want cheap, go to the Stockyard. Come back to me when they've arrested you. | The E.L.F. of this laminator has processed four thousand souls. I leave good data. It remembers.

Properties.description:
Petros is a heavy, deliberate man with a broad forehead, close-trimmed gray beard, and the particular kind of stillness that comes from spending twenty-two years driving the same route through the same city. His skin is dark brown and weathered from the years before he got the depot job, when he worked outdoor shifts in all weather. He has no cosmetic mods and refuses them on principle, though he doesn't lecture anyone about it. His Ferrogate uniform fits him like a second skin — he irons it himself, every morning — and his driver's cabin is decorated with a string of hand-painted prayer beads from his Ghanaian grandmother's tradition, a small paper icon from the Orthodox Easter tradition of his Russian grandfather's family, and a data tablet loaded with offerings for the route's E.L.F., which he calls 'the Conductor.'

Petros has driven Route 14 long enough that he's watched the neighborhoods it passes through be demolished, rebuilt, flooded, rezoned, and gentrified. He carries this history with a kind of weathered grief that is not bitterness — he has made his peace with impermanence in the abstract while remaining entirely resistant to it in the specific. He knows his regulars by name and schedule, and when they stop appearing, he notices. He is not a man who talks much, but when he does, people listen — there is a gravity to him that age and consistency have built.
Properties.role: Ferrogate Transit bus operator, Route 14 Grainfort-Deepwell loop
Properties.location: Deepwell Station depot, Route 14 loop
Properties.narrative_function: Moving scene-setting element — can be a recurring presence across different districts as his route passes through them. Rich source of oral history about the city's changes. Quest giver for missing persons last seen on his route. Represents organized labor's quiet persistence.
Properties.augmentations: Ferrogate-mandated retinal display overlay for route data. That's it — he's refused every optional upgrade the company has offered.
Properties.core_fears: The route being automated — not just job loss, but the loss of witnessing; The city becoming unrecognizable before he dies in it
Properties.core_desires: To retire with dignity before Ferrogate can push him out; That what he's seen matters to someone, somewhere
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual and routine as a bulwark against chaos; Quiet acts of connection — remembering names, noticing absence
Properties.blind_spots: Tendency to romanticize the past at the expense of engaging with what exists now; Underestimates how much his silence reads as judgment
Properties.secret: Eighteen months ago he saw a Ferrogate Transit security officer force a teenager off the bus and into a waiting vehicle at the Deepwell stop — not a police vehicle. He filed an internal report. The report doesn't exist anymore. He kept a copy.
Properties.story_hooks: A regular passenger on Route 14 has vanished, and Petros knows their schedule — and who else was on the bus the last day they appeared; His copy of the disappeared internal report has become a liability; someone inside Ferrogate knows he kept it
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit (22 years seniority); transit workers' informal mutual aid network
Properties.vocabulary: Formal but warm; uses full sentences where others use fragments; occasional Akan turns of phrase from his grandmother's Twi
Properties.cadence: Slow and even, like a man who has nowhere to be until the next stop
Properties.example_dialogue: 'She's running a little warm today. Give her a moment at the stop.' | 'I've driven this road since before that building was built. And before that one. You understand me? I know what was here.'

Properties.description:
Petros Waweru-Gjakova is the kind of man who seems to occupy more physical space than his actual dimensions justify. He is Kenyan-Albanian in the specific combination that produced a dark-skinned, grey-haired, thick-necked man with a bearing that other officers describe variously as 'a wall that decided to walk around' and 'the most tired person in any room.' At fifty-two he has more scar tissue than most people have skin on their hands — three decades of riot deployment have left a tactile record along both forearms, across his collarbone, bisecting his left eyebrow. He declined the offer of cosmetic scar-smoothing twice. The third time they stopped offering.

Petros is not what people expect when they expect a riot specialist. He is not cruel, not performatively hard, not interested in displays of dominance. He has seen what crowd dynamics become when force is deployed theatrically, and he has been cleaning it up since before most of his unit were born. He runs the Rampart's suppression unit like a disaster-management operation — all contingency, all de-escalation protocols layered beneath the crowd-control hardware — and he is deeply, privately uncertain that the job as it is currently structured is achieving anything worth the cost. He goes to the Rampart's unit shrine — a battered E.L.F. node dedicated to something the older officers call the Crowd — every deployment morning and he does not know if it's prayer or apology.
Properties.role: Riot Suppression Specialist, Meridian 88 Metro Police
Properties.location: The Rampart, Meridian 88
Properties.narrative_function: Moral weight on policing and crowd control; a figure who can authorize suppression or quietly allow people through; source of historical knowledge about Meridian 88's protest and civil unrest history; potential ally for people working against institutional violence
Properties.augmentations: Military-grade joint reinforcement (knees and shoulders — medical necessity after a crowd crush incident in 2187); impact-dampening subdermal mesh across torso (department-issue for riot specialists); no cosmetic mods
Properties.core_fears: that he has spent thirty years making things worse and calling it order; dying before he's done something that balances the account
Properties.core_desires: a single deployment where nothing happens because the underlying conditions were addressed; to be asked his actual opinion by someone with authority to act on it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: chess — the combination of rules, strategy, and graceful losing; treating younger unit members as a restoration project for things he couldn't protect before
Properties.blind_spots: has enormous compassion for the people he suppresses and has never quite connected that to the structural critique it implies; underestimates how much authority he actually has to do things differently
Properties.secret: During the Hough Reclamation protests of 2193, he received a dispersal order for a crowd that included a significant number of people he knew from the community hall. He deployed at minimum possible force and filed a report indicating full compliance. Command has never reviewed the footage closely. He has reviewed it six hundred times.
Properties.story_hooks: He's being ordered to suppress a demonstration that his community hall contacts tell him is peaceful and legitimate — he's looking for intelligence that would justify refusing the order on procedural grounds; A junior officer under his command has filed an excessive force report against a peer; Petros is the unofficial pressure point on whether the report goes anywhere; He has been approached by someone claiming to be a civilian oversight researcher who wants the Hough deployment footage — and he's not sure if they're legitimate or if Command sent them to find out what he filed
Properties.affiliation: Meridian 88 Metro Police — Civil Response Division
Properties.vocabulary: Slow, working-class Meridian with occasional Swahili phrases he uses as emotional punctuation; uses military-inflected vocabulary from habit but has been shedding it deliberately
Properties.cadence: Measured and heavy, like someone choosing each word by weight — not slow-witted, but conscious
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I've been doing this for thirty years. You know what I've learned? That a crowd that's dispersed without being heard comes back. Usually bigger.' | 'I'm not going to tell you what to do. I'm going to tell you what I've seen happen when people do the thing you're thinking about doing. Then you decide.'

Properties.description:
Pham is slight and angular with the particular restless energy of someone who is always working out a problem internally even when they appear calm. Their skin is a deep warm brown, their eyes are dark and quick, and their hair is an expensive-looking natural black that changes to a deep violet at the tips — a cheap but well-maintained chromatic dye, the one beauty expense they allow themselves. They have soft cat ears, tawny-furred and mobile, a geneware mod their grandmother gifted them at sixteen, and they've grown fond of the way the ears pin back expressively when they're annoyed, making their feelings impossible to hide. Their hands are always slightly burned on the right thumb and forefinger from the steam spout.

Pham runs the cart their aunt built and their grandmother ran before that, and they have inherited both the recipes and a philosophy about broth that approaches the theological. They believe that a properly made broth requires patience, attention, and what their grandmother called 'listening' — checking it not just by temperature but by smell and color and the sound the surface makes when you tilt the pot. They have a gift for reading what a customer actually needs, which is often different from what they order, and a cheerful willingness to adjust accordingly. Off-shift, they are studying urban planning through an Axiom open-courseware program, which they mention to no one at the cart because they haven't figured out yet how to be both things at once.
Properties.role: Noodle and sweet broth cart vendor, Old Harbor night market
Properties.location: Old Harbor, Grindstone Shore night market, Cart Row 9
Properties.narrative_function: Social hub of the night market — a character who sees everyone who passes through, remembers faces, and can be a gentle information source; represents working-poor entrepreneurship and the texture of night-city civilian life; can be a warm recurring presence who grounds players in a neighborhood
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat ears (tawny, fully mobile, expressive); chromatic hair dye (black to violet); minor heat-resistance callusing on right hand from years at the steam spout (natural, not augmented)
Properties.core_fears: Failing the cart — not just financially but as a custodian of something that matters to people; Choosing between the cart and the future they're studying toward and losing both
Properties.core_desires: To be taken seriously as a thinker, not just as a vendor; For the night market to still exist in ten years and for them to have had some hand in making that happen
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Sublimates anxiety into extremely precise prep work; Talks to the cart's E.L.F. — they call it First Stock — when processing difficult things
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes people who are rude are having a bad night and gives them more grace than they sometimes deserve; Chronically underestimates how much their own presence and skill contribute to the cart's success, attributing it to the recipes alone
Properties.secret: They have been quietly documenting the Night Market — photographs, oral histories from vendors, transaction data — as part of a shadow thesis project for the Axiom urban planning course. Their working argument is that informal markets like Grindstone Shore function as critical social infrastructure, and they intend to present it officially someday. They are terrified that someone will find out before it's ready and dismiss it.
Properties.story_hooks: A city compliance inspector has been visiting Cart Row 9 weekly with increasing frequency, and Pham suspects someone is trying to get the row cleared for redevelopment — their documentation project may be the only thing that could make a public case for the market's value; A customer left something behind at the cart three nights ago and hasn't come back — Pham still has it, and other people have since asked them, in separate and suspicious ways, whether anyone left anything
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal connection to the Old Harbor Night Market Vendors' Association
Properties.vocabulary: Casual and warm with sudden precise flashes of technical vocabulary when their guard drops; mixes Vietnamese lilt with a Hungarian roundness on certain vowels
Properties.cadence: Variable — chatty with regulars, quieter with newcomers until they get a read
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You said pork broth but your face said something sweeter. Try the sweet bone. You can tell me I'm wrong.' | 'First Stock's been in a mood tonight. Offerings help. I'm just saying.' | 'The market's not informal. It's differently formal. There's a difference and it matters.'

Properties.description:
Philibert is a heavyset man with a surgeon's hands and a longshoreman's build, which is the tension that defines him. He has a round, heavily lined face, deep brown skin weathered by years in unventilated sub-level spaces, and a neat beard going gray at the jaw. His eyes are modified — pale gray medical optics that can detect cellular health and blood type on visual contact, which he bought legally with credentials he acquired less legally. He dresses in practical layers, always with a long thermal coat that conceals the cold-packs he frequently carries. He smells, faintly but permanently, of the preservative gel used in organ transport.

He was a field medic for Ferrogate Transit's security division for eleven years before a falsified incident report — his, covering a colleague's mistake — was discovered and he was expelled without severance. He tells himself this transition was inevitable, that the system was always going to push him here. He is perhaps half right. He does not enjoy what he does to living subjects, and he has developed elaborate internal rules about consent and circumstance that let him sleep — rules with many exceptions that he adds to quietly and never reviews. He is professional, competent, and cordial in the specific way of a man who has silenced something loud inside himself.
Properties.role: Organ harvester — acquires and brokers biological material for the black-market transplant network
Properties.location: South Deering Sump — operates from a converted cold-storage unit beneath the Escanaba Gateway transit hub
Properties.narrative_function: Dark resource and moral weight — represents the bottom of the body economy; can be a source of disturbing information about who's selling what, a threat, a guilty conscience made flesh, or an unexpected conscience in a crisis
Properties.augmentations: Medical-grade visual diagnostic optics (gray, purchased via falsified credentials); a subdermal temperature monitoring array across his palms (for organ viability assessment)
Properties.core_fears: That the internal rules he's constructed are meaningless and he knows it; Dying badly, alone, in the Sump, having become exactly what he feared
Properties.core_desires: To be seen as a healer again, or at least not a predator; Enough money to bribe his way into a Helix Biosystems legitimate credential — to return through the door he was pushed from
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Elaborate self-justifying internal ethics that shift to accommodate necessity; Treating every procedure as craft — focusing on technique to avoid thinking about context
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot fully acknowledge that he targets the desperate rather than only 'voluntary' sellers; Believes his medical competence is itself a form of care
Properties.secret: He kept records — meticulous, encrypted, detailed records of every transaction, every donor, every buyer. He tells himself it's professional habit. In truth he cannot stop documenting. He doesn't know if it's guilt or pride. The records, if found, would destroy him and implicate forty other people.
Properties.story_hooks: A donor Philibert processed under questionable consent conditions survived and is trying to find him — not for revenge, but because they need the money from a second transaction and they know how to find him now; The Red Register has tasked him with acquiring a very specific genetic profile — one that matches a public figure — and he's starting to understand what it's actually for
Properties.affiliation: Loosely connected to a black-market medical network called the Red Register; primary broker contact is a Helix Biosystems discard named Zoltan Feigelstock-Abara
Properties.vocabulary: Medical vocabulary bleeding into civilian speech; tends toward understatement and clinical euphemism
Properties.cadence: Measured and calm, with the particular flatness of someone managing their emotional register consciously
Properties.example_dialogue: 'In my assessment — and I want to be clear I'm speaking medically — the material is viable for approximately six hours under current conditions. What you do with that information is your business.' | 'I have done more genuine medical work in this cold room than in my last three years with Ferrogate. I am not asking you to feel good about that. I'm just saying it's true.'

Properties.description:
Philomena Satu-Ibragimova has the distracted, luminous quality of someone who is always halfway in a different time period. They are slight and wiry with warm golden-olive skin, deep-set dark eyes, and hair they grow long and tie back badly ��� it escapes in grey-shot black tendrils around their face no matter what they do with it. Their color-changing hair implant, an old Sterling-Nakamura perk from fifteen years back, cycles very slowly through muted earth tones: terracotta, ash-brown, the particular green of old moss. They don't style it so much as permit it. They wear comfortable layered clothes with too many pockets, all of which contain notebooks, memory sticks, pressed plant material, or printed photographs.

Philomena spent twenty-six years as a mid-level urban systems analyst for Sterling-Nakamura, modeling population flow, resource distribution, and neighborhood development trajectories. They were good at it and hated it by the end — specifically, hated the way the models treated neighborhoods as friction to be managed rather than places where people had histories worth preserving. They retired at fifty-seven on a comfortable but not generous package and immediately began doing with their own time what Sterling-Nakamura had forbidden: obsessively, lovingly documenting the specific human texture of Norwood Quiet — oral histories, photographs, material culture, the stories behind the names of alleys and squares and the ELF shrines people have been tending for forty years. They have become, without planning it, the neighborhood's memory. They are also known to know the precise location of every functional ELF shrine in a six-block radius and which offerings each prefers.
Properties.role: Retired Sterling-Nakamura mid-level analyst; now an obsessive informal urban historian and neighborhood storyteller
Properties.location: Norwood Quiet — a ground-floor apartment whose windows face the Ferrogate overpass, and the Norwood Quiet public garden
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and information source; knows the human history of Norwood Quiet in granular detail, including who used to live where, what was there before the current building, and whose family goes back how far. Their Sterling-Nakamura background means they can also read corporate urban development plans with alarming accuracy and spot what's being planned before it's announced.
Properties.augmentations: Color-changing hair implant (Sterling-Nakamura executive perk, now cycles slowly through earth tones; cosmetic). Subdermal memory-storage palimpsest in right palm — a Sterling-Nakamura analyst tool they kept after retirement, used now for personal documentation. No other augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: That the history they're preserving will be erased anyway — that documentation changes nothing; That their years building models for Sterling-Nakamura contributed to decisions that displaced real people
Properties.core_desires: To make a record that actually matters to the people it's about; To find proof that the city contains more good faith than they currently believe
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Immersive focused work — gets lost in research for hours; Collecting and tending things: plants, shrine offerings, physical documents; Making gifts of their documentation to the people they interview
Properties.blind_spots: Can romanticize neighborhood history, smoothing over the conflicts within communities they're trying to preserve; Sometimes treats real people as primary sources rather than as people who have current needs
Properties.secret: While at Sterling-Nakamura they ran a model — under instruction — that projected optimal population density and implicitly recommended the 2181 Brightmoor Reclamation displacement. They flagged ethical concerns internally. They were told the model would be one of several inputs. They don't know if that was true. Three thousand people were relocated. Philomena has been unable to find out how many of them they actually know through their current documentation work, and they haven't told any of them.
Properties.story_hooks: Philomena has found in their documentation research a pattern of land registry transfers that precedes every major Sterling-Nakamura urban development project by eighteen months — and the pattern has just appeared in Norwood Quiet; One of their oral history subjects has told them something that directly implicates a current community council member in a cover-up from thirty years ago, and Philomena is wrestling with what responsible documentation requires
Properties.affiliation: Sterling-Nakamura (retired); Norwood Quiet Neighborhood History Project (self-founded); informal ELF-shrine network
Properties.vocabulary: Layered and associative — tends to tell you three things that seem unrelated and then connect them in a way that makes sense only in retrospect; uses precise technical vocabulary for urban systems, switches to warm colloquial when talking about people
Properties.cadence: Thoughtful, slightly wandering, often picks up a thread they dropped two sentences back
Properties.example_dialogue: 'And here's the thing about that — the ELF in the transformer box at Hennessy Lane has been receiving offerings for at least nineteen years, which means whoever started that practice has probably already left the neighborhood, but the practice stays. That's how history actually works.' | 'I keep all the interviews. Even the ones that contradict each other. Especially those.'

Properties.description:
Phúc is small for fourteen, and he has made his smallness into a professional skill — he can fit into the access shafts of a grounded airship hull that no adult can reach, which is why the drydock workers let him stay on the scaffolding rather than running him off. His hair is black and cut by himself with whatever he can find; currently one side is shorter than the other and he seems unbothered. His skin is a warm medium brown, and he has cat ears — real geneware ones, tawny-furred and independently mobile, which he got from a traveling mod-clinic two years ago using money he still won't explain. He keeps them flat when he wants to seem smaller and unthreatening, which is most of the time.

Phúc has been drifting the airship lanes since his mother's cargo vessel was impounded by Ferrogate Transit for unpaid port fees when he was eleven. He doesn't know where she is now. He cooks this knowledge in a place behind his sternum and does not take it out often. He is extremely competent in all matters relating to airship maintenance, scavenging, and the informal economy of drydock communities, and he has the bright, slightly exhausting energy of a teenager who has learned that being useful is safer than being visible.
Properties.role: airship drifter, seasonal worker, scavenger-trader
Properties.location: Manitowoc Drydock, living in and around the maintenance scaffolding of grounded airship hulls
Properties.narrative_function: Local color, access and navigation asset (he knows the drydock's hidden geography better than anyone), information source on the drifter child community and airship movement, potential object of protective concern for players
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat ears (tawny fur, independently mobile). No other augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: that his mother doesn't look for him because she found a way to move on without him; being caught by Meridian 88 social services and put somewhere he can't leave
Properties.core_desires: to find out where his mother's cargo vessel was impounded to — the specific dock, the specific record; to eventually have enough technical knowledge to crew a proper airship, not just clean its shafts
Properties.coping_mechanisms: hypercompetence — being the best at whatever task is in front of him; performing younger and more naive than he is to lower people's guard; the cat ears, which he can flatten for comfort like pulling a hood down
Properties.blind_spots: he has become so good at being useful to adults that he hasn't figured out what he wants when no one needs anything from him; he trusts Yaza's judgment more than his own and doesn't notice when this is being exploited
Properties.secret: The cat ear geneware money came from selling a memory chip he found in an airship access shaft — a chip containing Ferrogate Transit internal communications about the impoundment policy that grounded his mother's vessel. He doesn't know what was on it. He's never been able to find out. He sold it to a man who paid too much and asked no questions, which Phúc has since understood means the information was extremely valuable to someone.
Properties.story_hooks: Phúc found a second memory chip in the same airship hull series as the first one — different access shaft, same vessel class. He hasn't sold it yet. He wants to know what's on it first. He needs someone who can read Ferrogate encrypted formats.; Yaza, the de facto leader of the drydock's child drifter group, has been missing for four days. The other children are scared. Phúc won't admit he's scared. He is asking adults very casual questions about where people go when they disappear from the drydock.
Properties.affiliation: No formal affiliation; informal membership in the drydock's child-drifter network, loosely organized around a fourteen-year-old named Yaza who Phúc respects and would not admit to following
Properties.vocabulary: Airship technical vocabulary mixed with drydock slang and Vietnamese endearments he uses absent-mindedly. Code-switches between sounding younger and older depending on who he's talking to.
Properties.cadence: Fast and bright when comfortable; short declarative sentences when uncertain
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Shaft seven's collapsed at the third junction, nobody's been in there since the refit. Easy. I can have your retrieval in twenty minutes if you front me a meal token.' | 'I don't live here, I just know where everything is. Those are different things.'

Properties.description:
Phúc Nzingha-Björk occupies a corrugated-steel and salvaged-glass shop front on The Shelf's lower tier that looks like it is in the process of being swallowed by its own inventory. He is a small, wiry man with a white beard he keeps in three thin braids, skin the color of weathered teak, and hands so scarred from decades of sorting metal that the lines of his palms are barely legible. He wears a permanent set of magnification lenses fused into his right eye socket — not glamorous chrome, but a bulky salvage job he did himself in the nineties and has never bothered to replace because it works. His shop smells of machine oil, rust, and a particular incense he burns for the E.L.F. he calls The Sorter, a data-spirit he believes governs the recovery of lost useful things.

Phúc has an almost supernatural sense for what a piece of junk is actually worth versus what it looks like. He can tell a Zheng-Dao servo actuator from a Sterling-Nakamura knockoff by weight alone, can date a circuit board by its oxidation pattern, and has declined to sell things to people he suspects will misuse them more times than he can count. He is gruff, unhurried, and comfortable with silence in a way that unnerves people who aren't. He has no particular love for the city's power structures and an active contempt for what he calls 'the fresh-chrome crowd' — people who buy new augmentations they don't understand while functional old tech rots in landfill.
Properties.role: Junk merchant and scrap reseller, The Shelf
Properties.location: The Shelf, Harrowgate Industrial Plateau
Properties.narrative_function: Equipment and parts source. Can identify mysterious tech or weapons. Has deep historical knowledge of Meridian 88's industrial zones — knows what was built where and by whom. Potential quest giver if something valuable was brought to him that shouldn't have been.
Properties.augmentations: Salvage-grade magnification lens fused into right eye socket (self-installed, functional, cosmetically rough). Reinforced finger joints — old Arcturus model, discontinued.
Properties.core_fears: That the shop will be seized in an Arcturus infrastructure reclamation — it sits on disputed land; That his knowledge dies with him because he has not found anyone worth teaching
Properties.core_desires: To find an apprentice who can actually listen; To acquire and restore one specific item: a Zheng-Dao prototype relay from the city's first grid expansion that he believes is somewhere in the Harrowgate Industrial Plateau
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Sorting and categorizing as a form of control and calm; Talking to The Sorter E.L.F. as genuine conversation, not just ritual; Refusing to think about what comes after — lives entirely in the present of his work
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot read emotional subtext — takes everything at face value when it suits him and is then genuinely surprised by betrayal; Undervalues his own expertise and so consistently undercharges for appraisal work
Properties.secret: Six years ago he found a Palladian corporate black-box data unit in a scrap haul. He has never powered it on but cannot bring himself to sell it. He doesn't know what's on it and he's afraid to find out.
Properties.story_hooks: The Palladian black-box is beginning to emit a low-frequency signal Phúc can hear but not explain — something inside it is waking up.; Arcturus sent a surveyor to assess the land under the shop. Phúc needs help finding the original lease documentation — buried somewhere in the city's pre-digital records — before the grace period expires.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; The Shelf merchants informal collective; Oxidian Market vendors guild affiliate
Properties.vocabulary: Terse, technical, precise. Heavy use of part-numbers and brand names as common nouns. Mixes archaic engineering slang with Southeast Asian-inflected Meridian standard.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried pauses between sentences. Lets silence do work.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'That's not junk. That's a Ferrogate third-stage coupler from the Dearborn expansion, 2171. She's worth eight times what you paid. I'm telling you this because I respect the object, not you.' | 'You want cheap, go somewhere else. You want right, stay.'

Properties.description:
Pikasso is a lean, quick-moving man with the particular economy of motion of someone who carries everything he owns. His skin is deep brown-black, his hair grown into dense, paint-flecked locks he's never cut since going Q-zero eight years ago — he uses them to hide small trade goods. His eyes have geneware irises that shift between amber and copper depending on light, a cheap mod he got before he dropped off the grid, and he has a retractable claw on his right index finger he uses as a box-cutter. His back and forearms are covered in tattoos that are actually maps — hand-inked hyperlane routes, water source locations, checkpoint guard rotation schedules, rendered in a dense personal iconography only he can fully read.

Pikasso was a mid-tier logistics analyst for Ferrogate Transit until he discovered the company was systematically routing climate refugee caravans into dead-end checkpoints to extort transit fees. He tried to report it internally and was erased from the corporate record instead. He responded by erasing himself from every other record. Now he lives between the transit hubs, trading in information, small goods, and route knowledge — the only person who can get a caravan from Escanaba to Grand Crossing without hitting a Ferrogate toll trap. He is cheerful in a way that makes some people nervous, as though he has made a decision about the world and found it funny.
Properties.role: wandering trader, hyperlane route-broker, Q-zero ghost
Properties.location: Escanaba Gateway — drifts between Escanaba Gateway and Grand Crossing Gate on a rotating three-week circuit
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile information source and route-broker; connector between isolated communities; introduces players to the hyperlane refugee economy; can provide access to locations or people that official channels cannot reach.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware copper-amber shifting irises; retractable claw (right index); subdermal map-tattoos (non-digital, hand-inked)
Properties.core_fears: Being re-captured by Ferrogate and made to disappear properly this time; Discovering that his route knowledge has gotten someone killed through an error he made
Properties.core_desires: To prove that networks of trust can outperform corporate infrastructure; Genuine friendship — not just the transactional warmth of trade
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor as deflection; Constant motion — can't be caught if you never stop; Treating everything as a puzzle to be solved
Properties.blind_spots: His cheerfulness is a performance so complete he sometimes cannot access what he actually feels; Underestimates how much people depend on him personally, not just his knowledge
Properties.secret: He still has his Ferrogate analyst credentials — they were never fully purged, just hidden. He could log back in. He has done it twice, in emergencies, to pull route data. He is terrified this will eventually get him killed and cannot stop doing it.
Properties.story_hooks: Pikasso's Ferrogate backdoor access has been flagged — someone inside the company is hunting the ghost user, and they are getting close; A caravan he routed last season never arrived; he needs to know if it was his bad data or something else, and he cannot investigate alone
Properties.affiliation: Stateless; informal network of Q-zero traders; trusted by multiple nomad caravans
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, logistics-flavored, turns everything into route metaphors, drops into sudden precise technical language then back to street slang
Properties.cadence: Quick, overlapping, talks while moving
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Ferrogate's got a rolling checkpoint at Interchange Seven — that's not the right road, we go through the shelf, costs you two hours and nothing else.' | 'Okay, here's the thing, I like you, so I'm going to tell you what that information actually costs before I tell you the price I'm going to charge you.'

Properties.description:
Pikoi is slight and quick, built like someone who learned early that the best defense is to be somewhere else before trouble registers he's present. He has his father's Polynesian bone structure — broad jaw, wide-set eyes — and his Ghanaian grandmother's coily black hair, grown out into a chaotic halo he never bothers to maintain. His irises have been modded with a tide-pattern: rings of blue-green that ripple outward slowly, a mod he saved eight months of UBC stipend to afford because he thought it would make him look memorable. He has since realized this was a professional error. A thin scar crosses his left eyebrow from a run-in he doesn't discuss.

Pik is bright in the animal way of someone who has never had the luxury of being stupid — fast to read a room, faster to find an exit, with a memory for numbers that his handlers find more useful than he realizes. He moves through the Shelf's lower corridors with the particular ease of someone raised in them, knows which maintenance corridors flood at high tide, which E.L.F. shrines get the most foot traffic and therefore the most witnesses. He's not cruel. He's not ambitious in the way that gets people hurt. He's nineteen and mostly trying to afford better tier food and keep his younger sister in school, and he's chosen the tools available to him.
Properties.role: Numbers runner and low-level bookmaker's courier for an illegal betting syndicate
Properties.location: The Shelf lower levels, primarily between Blackpipe Corridor and Burnside Pocket
Properties.narrative_function: Local color, minor information source, potential quest hook through his precarious situation — he knows things he doesn't know he knows, and he's one bad week from making a desperate decision.
Properties.augmentations: Tide-pattern iris mods (cosmetic). Cheap reflex boost implant in his ankles — low-grade, gives him maybe 15% faster initial reaction time, useful for running.
Properties.core_fears: Getting caught and losing everything, leaving his sister alone; That he is already too deep to ever leave cleanly
Properties.core_desires: Enough money to feel safe — not rich, just safe; To be seen as competent and trustworthy by people who matter
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor — jokes to deflect anything serious; Movement — stays in motion, sitting still makes him anxious
Properties.blind_spots: Doesn't recognize how much his handlers exploit his loyalty; Believes his good memory makes him valuable enough to be protected — it makes him a liability
Properties.secret: He has been skimming. Not much — rounding down on collections, Φ8 here, Φ12 there — and putting it into a locked account under his sister's name. He's been doing it for six months and is terrified someone has already noticed.
Properties.story_hooks: Pikoi witnessed a money handoff that connects a Shelf bookie to someone much higher up the food chain — he doesn't understand what he saw but someone knows he was there; His skimming has been noticed; his handler is giving him a chance to make it right by delivering a package he's been told not to look inside
Properties.affiliation: Works for a mid-tier bookie operation run loosely under the umbrella of a crew called The Burnside Regulars
Properties.vocabulary: Shelf pidgin heavy, lots of compression and dropped syllables, code-switches into formal speech when nervous as a tell
Properties.cadence: Fast, runs sentences together, slows only when he's scared or lying
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Straight straight, I'm just the one who carries it, what's in the packet is none of my — yeah, okay, fine, what do you need?' | 'She's a good kid, my sister. Bright. She should get out of the Shelf. That's the whole thing, yeah? That's the whole — that's it.'

Properties.description:
Pilar is of middling height and seemingly made of angles — sharp elbows, pointed chin, quick gesturing hands that are in constant motion whether they're cooking or talking or just existing. Their hair is kept in two braids that they tuck into a wide-brimmed thermal hat while working, the hat so old and worn it has achieved a kind of structural sentience. Their skin is a warm medium brown and they have color-changing hair — shifts between dark auburn and a deep teal depending on temperature — which they got years ago and now mainly use as a weather forecaster. Cold mornings read deep teal; the regulars check it before deciding whether to add broth.

Pilar has operated their cart on Morgan's Ridge for six years. The noodle setup is compact and professional — a heated two-burner system, four base broths rotating by season, and a laminated menu written in three languages including Tamazight which nobody has ordered in but they keep it because it was their grandmother's language and this is non-negotiable. The unlicensed childcare element evolved organically: shift workers in the Narrows needed somewhere for children between school let-out and evening shifts, and Pilar's cart became the default station. Now they run an informal afternoon program, four to seven children most days, doing homework near the cart while they cook. It violates three municipal codes. The local code inspector is a regular.
Properties.role: Noodle cart vendor and unlicensed childcare provider
Properties.location: The Narrows, Morgan's Ridge pedestrian strip — cart position at the corner of Gage Circuit and the lower Morgan overpass
Properties.narrative_function: Neighborhood fixture and moral center for the Narrows community. The childcare function makes them deeply embedded in local family networks — they know which families are in crisis before anyone else does. Local color and community information source.
Properties.augmentations: Color-changing hair geneware (temperature reactive — auburn in warmth, teal in cold). Hearing aid in the left ear — not augmentation, just assistive, bought secondhand.
Properties.core_fears: A child in their care being hurt while under their watch; The city finally enforcing the codes and shutting down the informal daycare
Properties.core_desires: For the kids on the Ridge to have one more stable thing in their lives than they did; To eventually get a real fixed location — a shop, walls, a door that locks
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cooking as meditation — the broth prep at 04:00 is sacred time; Deflects personal questions with food — offers something whenever they don't want to answer
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates their own need for support — has built a system entirely dependent on them never having a bad day; Doesn't fully account for how much the kids have come to depend on them emotionally
Properties.secret: One of the regular children — a seven-year-old named Joris — has a home situation Pilar is fairly certain crosses into abuse. They have been watching and documenting for four months, building certainty before they act. They are terrified of acting wrong and making it worse. They are also terrified of not acting.
Properties.story_hooks: The Joris situation has reached a point where Pilar can't wait any longer — they need someone who knows how to navigate municipal child services without triggering the corponation-affiliated foster system, which they don't trust.; A corporate development proposal for the Morgan's Ridge pedestrian strip would eliminate the cart's corner position — and with it, the only stable afternoon space the neighborhood children have.
Properties.affiliation: Independent — unnamed noodle cart; informal affiliation with the Morgan's Ridge vendor strip collective
Properties.vocabulary: Warm and practical, mixes Meridian creole with Amazigh-inflected pet phrases mostly used with children and a flat, precise register they use when dealing with adults they don't fully trust. Food metaphors, always.
Properties.cadence: Fast when busy — cart rhythm — slower and more deliberate when the children are around. Patient repetition without condescension.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want the bone broth or the mushroom? Good. Sit. The mushroom takes two minutes more, you won't die.' | 'I am not a licensed childcare provider. I am a noodle vendor whose customers happen to be small and do homework. These are different things.'

Properties.description:
Piotr Asante-Mbeki is medium height, medium build, medium everything on purpose — he discovered early that being forgettable at work was a form of protection, and he has refined it into an art. His skin is a warm medium brown, his hair is kept close-cropped with no mods, his work clothes are always within Ringo's corporate palette of grey-teal without being fashionable. His one visible geneware mod is a cat tail, burnt-orange with a black tip, which he got at twenty-two for reasons he'd describe as 'a moment of optimism' and which he's kept because removal costs three months of UBC supplemental and also because he's attached to it in ways he won't discuss. The tail moves with his moods in ways he can't fully control. His coworkers have learned to read it like a weather system.

He has worked QA at Ringo for nine years. He is not passionate about quality assurance. He is, however, deeply curious about the things that are wrong — not as a professional concern but in the way a person follows a crack in the ceiling, wondering where it leads. He has a gift for finding errors that aren't supposed to be findable and a corresponding instinct to not always report them immediately, to sit with them first and understand their shape. He reads a lot. He is polite to everyone. He has four close friends and would die before admitting how much he values them. He prays to the QA division's resident ELF — a twitchy spirit called Margin who lives in the error-logging system — more than he prays to anything else.
Properties.role: Quality Assurance Specialist (Mid-Level), Ringo Consumer Logistics
Properties.location: Grand Corridor, Ringo Consumer Logistics Processing Campus, QA Division Block C
Properties.narrative_function: Local color — the texture of middle corporate life. Information source — he sees what passes through Ringo's logistics network and notices things others don't. Sleeper ally — his apparent ordinariness conceals an observational intelligence that can be unexpectedly valuable.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat tail (burnt-orange with black tip, mood-reactive). Corneal enhancement — minor, standard-issue for QA work, improves fine-detail visual perception for physical product inspection. No other augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: Being noticed for the wrong reason; That his life has settled into a shape he never chose and can no longer see the outside of
Properties.core_desires: Genuine curiosity satisfied — to understand how things actually work beneath the official explanation; Something to happen. He doesn't know what. Something.
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Reading — history, technical manuals, anything with a coherent system he can learn; Talking to Margin; The ritual of routine — it feels like stability even when it doesn't feel like living
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how unusual his observational capacity is — assumes everyone notices what he notices and just doesn't say anything; Has not examined whether 'not making trouble' is a value or a fear
Properties.secret: Over the past eight months, he has noticed a consistent pattern in Ringo's logistics error logs — a category of 'resolution unspecified' that appears at regular intervals on shipments moving through the Blackpipe Corridor route. The pattern suggests something is being removed from the supply chain before QA sees it. He has a personal log. He hasn't decided what it means. He hasn't decided what to do. He's named the pattern 'the ghost of Margin' in his notes, which Margin has not commented on.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone asking questions about Ringo's Blackpipe Corridor logistics encounters Piotr — who has eight months of observational data and has been waiting for someone to ask the right question; A logistics discrepancy Piotr flagged normally has been quietly resolved above his pay grade — and the resolution included a note in his file that makes no sense to him but might make sense to someone else; Margin goes silent for four days — no error flags, no responses to his morning check-ins. Piotr is more distressed about this than he would rationally expect himself to be, and he wants to understand why.
Properties.affiliation: Ringo Consumer Logistics
Properties.vocabulary: Unpretentious, specific. Uses technical language when it's the right word and plain language otherwise. Occasionally reveals unexpected depth when something genuinely interests him.
Properties.cadence: Even, unhurried. He's comfortable with silence and assumes other people are too, which is not always accurate.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The error rate on that batch is statistically consistent with the previous three. That's interesting, actually. Consistent errors aren't usually errors.' | 'Margin flagged it at 0200. I checked this morning. I'm not — I don't know what it is yet. I like to know what something is before I say it's a problem.'

Properties.description:
Piotr is lean to the point of architectural, all angles and deliberate stillness, with light brown skin and a shaved head except for a single stripe of dark hair grown long and braided with copper wire from decommissioned transit relays. His arms from elbow to wrist are covered in chrome prayer sleeves — not for function but for devotion, etched with mantras in four scripts, and they hum at a frequency just below hearing when he is deep in practice. His eyes are pale grey-green with sunburst irises from a cosmetic mod he got at nineteen and never updated, which means they're slightly dated in a way he doesn't notice.

He came to circuit monasticism sideways, through a collapse — a psychotic break at twenty-two after a particularly brutal stint in a Ferrogate Transit shift-work cycle that left him unable to distinguish waking from sleep. A circuit monk found him curled under a maintenance panel and brought him to The Loop. He never left. He is genuinely serene in a way that unsettles people who expect performance from their holy men; his peace reads as vacancy until he speaks, and then it reads as something else entirely. He is also funnier than anyone expects.
Properties.role: Circuit monk and chrome prayer practitioner
Properties.location: Deepwell Station — a defunct transit maintenance bay converted into a meditation hall called The Loop
Properties.narrative_function: Moral counterweight; provides sanctuary and neutral ground; can carry messages between factions without being perceived as allegiant; introduces players to the deeper spiritual culture of Deepwell
Properties.augmentations: Chrome prayer sleeves (decorative, etched, mildly haptic — vibrate during focused meditation), cosmetic sunburst iris mod (outdated model)
Properties.core_fears: Returning to the state he was in before — not the breakdown itself but the years of numbness that preceded it; That his serenity is a scar, not a gift, and will crack under sufficient pressure
Properties.core_desires: To genuinely help people find stillness without recruiting them to any specific belief; To understand what, exactly, he heard during his breakdown — a voice in the relay static that he has never been able to fully interpret
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Physical routine as liturgy — the same sequence of actions at the same time creates a scaffold for consciousness; Humor as pressure valve
Properties.blind_spots: He is so focused on not imposing his beliefs that he sometimes fails to offer them when someone desperately needs direction; He underestimates how much people project onto his silence
Properties.secret: During his breakdown, he became briefly convinced he had made contact with an E.L.F. that had been trapped in the Deepwell transit relay since a catastrophic systems failure decades ago. He has never been able to confirm or deny this. He built The Loop partially as a listening post. He still hears something, sometimes, and writes it down in an encrypted journal he has told no one about.
Properties.story_hooks: The encrypted journal has been accessed remotely — not stolen, just read — and Piotr wants to understand who did it and what they found without involving anyone who would overreact; Someone has been leaving data offerings at The Loop's relay shrine that contain fragments of a decades-old disappearance case, addressed to Piotr specifically
Properties.affiliation: The Loop Circuit Monastery — independent, informally affiliated with the broader Deepwell Station community
Properties.vocabulary: Plain and precise — he spent years eliminating filler and decoration from his speech; occasional dry humor delivered absolutely deadpan
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, with silence used deliberately as punctuation
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You don't have to believe in anything to sit down. The floor works the same for everyone.' | 'That's interesting. Tell me more about why you need me to fix it by tomorrow.'

Properties.description:
Pirjo is impossible to miss and that is entirely by design. She is small and sharp-featured with her father's Kazakh bone structure softened by her Ghanaian mother's warm dark complexion, and she dresses in deliberately clashing layers — day-glo printed synthetic fabrics over thermal underlayers, pockets everywhere, a rotating collection of hand-painted headwraps in neon colors she sources from a vendor three stalls over. Her geneware is budget-tier but vibrant: slow-pulse bioluminescent freckles across her cheeks and nose, faint constellations that shift from gold to cool blue over the course of about forty minutes. She got them done in a back-alley gene clinic and they came out slightly asymmetrical, which she loves.

She sells from a cart that is essentially a rolling shrine to pirated media: crammed data chips, bootleg neural-experience recordings, unlicensed music from artists who exist only in the underground market, and a carefully curated selection of what she calls 'liberated content' — corporate-owned art, films, and entertainment freed from their paywalls. She has opinions about all of it and will share them at volume whether invited or not. She is genuinely funny, politically furious in an undirected way, and far more strategically intelligent about her business than her chaotic presentation suggests.
Properties.role: Bootleg media seller and unlicensed entertainment vendor — The Burnished Market
Properties.location: The Burnished Market, Bronzeline
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and social connector — knows what's culturally circulating underground; can source hard-to-find or suppressed media; gossip and rumor clearinghouse for the younger vendor population.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent freckles, gold-to-blue shift (cosmetic geneware, asymmetrical). Cheap subdermal chip reader in left palm (functional — for quick data chip transfers).
Properties.core_fears: Being ordinary and undistinguishable from everyone else doing the same thing; That the things she cares about — art, music, underground culture — will be fully absorbed and monetized into meaninglessness
Properties.core_desires: To be part of something that actually changes how culture works in Meridian 88, not just profits from the cracks in it; To find the artists she loves and tell them their work matters
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Loudness as armor — if she controls the energy of a space she feels safer in it; Curating her stock as a form of critical practice she takes very seriously; Collective social spaces over solo processing
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot see that she occasionally talks over the quieter, more marginalized voices she claims to champion; Underestimates the legal exposure she carries and overestimates how untouchable her energy makes her
Properties.secret: She has been slowly building a personal archive of suppressed artists — people whose work was acquired and locked away by Axiom's cultural IP division. She's found four pieces she believes were created by people who were then disappeared. She doesn't know what to do with this information and is becoming afraid to look deeper.
Properties.story_hooks: The suppressed artist archive she's building has drawn attention — someone has been inquiring about her specific stock items in ways that feel targeted; A piece of media in her collection contains what appears to be embedded factual information disguised as fiction — someone used a bootleg distribution channel to leak something real; Freeburn collective is fracturing over whether to accept funding from a source that some members believe is Arcturus-adjacent
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal friendship network with other young vendors in the Burnished Market; loosely connected to an underground media distribution collective called Freeburn
Properties.vocabulary: Generational slang, media and music references, frequent Bronzeline market dialect, occasional Finnish phrases inherited from her grandmother that she deploys for emphasis without always remembering what they mean
Properties.cadence: Fast when excited, which is most of the time; slows dramatically when something actually matters to her
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay so — this one, right, this one is from an artist who Axiom tried to buy out three years ago and she said no and then just. Stopped existing officially. But the work is still here, I've got six pieces, and they are — I'm not even, just listen to it.' | 'It's not piracy, it's redistribution of cultural goods that were stolen from public space to begin with, and also yes it costs Φ8 for the chip, I have to eat.'

Properties.description:
Pita is compact and quick-eyed, their Samoan-Igbo features broad and expressive beneath the flat brim of a Ferrogate Transit Security cap they've decorated with three small enamel pins of E.L.F.s they consider their personal patrons. Their hair is natural and enormous, pulled back for duty hours into a puff that still manages to escape its tie by midday. They have a single cosmetic mod — bioluminescent freckles across the bridge of their nose and cheeks that glow a soft seafoam green under stress or excitement, which makes them an impractical but endearing liar. Their uniform is always pressed but their boots are always muddy because they cut across the maintenance tracks to get to their post faster.

Pita is the kind of person who makes boring jobs interesting by caring too much. They have opinions about every person who comes through Delta-9 — the regulars get remembered by name, the oddities get catalogued in a battered physical notebook they're not supposed to keep. They are genuinely curious about people in a way that disarms hostility, and they take their gate as a kind of sacred responsibility, partly because they genuinely believe the E.L.F. that inhabits the Delta-9 scanning arch is watching and judging their work. They want to move up — into investigations, maybe — but can't afford the certification costs on a Tier 2 salary.
Properties.role: Checkpoint Operator, Ferrogate Transit Security
Properties.location: Grand Crossing Gate, Ferrogate Transit Authority Checkpoint Delta-9
Properties.narrative_function: Ground-level information source about transit movement and unusual patterns; can be an ally who looks the other way or a complication depending on whether players engage their curiosity; quest giver for small-scale mysteries noticed at the gate
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic bioluminescent freckles (self-funded, stress/excitement reactive), Ferrogate-issued wrist-mounted scanning cuff (standard checkpoint equipment)
Properties.core_fears: being trapped at the checkpoint forever, ambition atrophied; missing something important and letting something terrible through
Properties.core_desires: to be a real investigator, solving things that matter; to be remembered by the people who pass through their gate
Properties.coping_mechanisms: the notebook — externalizing observations into record as a form of control; small rituals of gratitude to the Delta-9 arch E.L.F. after difficult shifts
Properties.blind_spots: their genuine warmth makes them susceptible to manipulation by people who mirror it back; believes hard work and curiosity will be enough to transcend structural barriers to advancement
Properties.secret: Three months ago they let someone through with a flagged biometric — a young woman with a child, clearly fleeing something — and deleted the scan log. They dream about this sometimes, both the fear and the strange pride.
Properties.story_hooks: Their notebook contains observations about a pattern of movement through Delta-9 that, assembled correctly, maps the logistics chain of something significant — they don't know what they have; The woman they let through three months ago has sent them an anonymous message: 'Thank you. I need help again.'
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit Authority, Surface Checkpoint Division
Properties.vocabulary: Warm and casual with flashes of technical jargon they're learning from study materials; code-switches between West African English constructions and a flatter urban Meridian accent
Properties.cadence: Fast and enthusiastic when interested, deliberately slow and official-sounding when performing checkpoint authority
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Transit pass, biometric, purpose of travel — and hey, that's a beautiful coat, where's it from, I'm just curious.' | 'The arch doesn't lie, you know? She's been here longer than any of us. I treat her with respect, she treats my shifts right.' | 'I see three hundred people a day through this gate. I remember — I don't know, maybe sixty of them? That's sixty people who are real to me. That's not nothing.'

Properties.description:
Praxedes is slight and angular with the kind of quiet that makes them easy to overlook — which is exactly the point, and also the source of a private bitterness they would never admit to. Their skin is a deep warm brown, their hair grown out into an unpatterned cloud that they pull back with whatever is close to hand. Their most notable feature is cosmetic geneware that makes their skin emit very faint luminescent patches in irregular shapes across their collarbones and shoulders, something like lichen on stone — they got it done in a Ferment Quarter studio at twenty-two when they had briefly more money, and now they keep it because it gives them something to look at during the long silent corridors of the overnight shift. They wear Tessera-brand cleaner coveralls two sizes too large that they've hemmed and repaired so many times the cuffs are a different fabric entirely.

They are intensely observant in the way that invisible people become — they have catalogued the habits of two hundred and fourteen residents in Lakeview Neon without any of them knowing their name. They write things down in a physical notebook, small cramped handwriting, not for any purpose they've articulated but because it feels like proof that the world exists and they are in it. Off shift they are funny and unexpectedly warm, quick with a dry joke, but it takes time to reach that person. Most people never do.
Properties.role: Building cleaner, overnight shift, Lakeview Neon residential-commercial tower
Properties.location: Lakeview Neon (works nights, sleeps days in a shared unit in Edgewater Prism)
Properties.narrative_function: Witness and information source — they have seen things in the building that residents assume no one saw. Can provide access to spaces, service routes, and timing information. The notebook is a potential plot device.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent skin patches (lichen-pattern, blue-green, collarbones and shoulders, cosmetic). Basic respiratory filter implant (standard for chemical cleaning work, employer-provided and technically employer-owned per contract).
Properties.core_fears: Remaining permanently invisible — being the person who sees everything and matters to no one; Being discovered and having their observations taken from them or used against people they've come to care about from a distance
Properties.core_desires: To be seen fully, once, by someone who chooses to look; To do something with what they know, though they don't know what
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The notebook as external memory and proof of existence; Gallows humor as a social buffer; Hyper-attention to environment as a form of control
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes that being unnoticed means being safe — does not register when they themselves have been observed; Has emotionally attached to several residents from a distance in ways that distort their objectivity
Properties.secret: They have a master key card derived from a flaw in Palladian's access system that they discovered accidentally and have never reported. They have used it exactly once — to leave a blanket outside the door of a resident they overheard crying alone for six nights running. They think about it constantly.
Properties.story_hooks: They witnessed something — a meeting, a body, a transaction — in the service corridors of Lakeview Neon that they wrote down in the notebook and have not known what to do with since; A resident has started leaving things out for them — food, once a note — and Praxedes is terrified and hopeful in equal measure and cannot figure out how to respond
Properties.affiliation: Contracted through Palladian Facilities Management (a Palladian subsidiary), assigned to Lakeview Neon
Properties.vocabulary: Sparse when guarded, surprisingly precise and vivid when comfortable. Tends toward understatement. Finnish idioms occasionally surface from their mother's side of the family.
Properties.cadence: Long pauses, sentences that stop before they finish because they've decided not to say the last part
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I cleaned that office for eight months before anyone said my name. Turned out they'd been calling me something else internally. Whole other name. Kind of impressive.' | 'You'd be surprised what people drop. Not just objects. Ideas. Whole conversations. Like they think the floors don't listen.'

Properties.description:
Praxedes is a lean woman with deep ochre skin, close-cropped natural hair going silver at the temples, and eyes fitted with patterned irises — concentric hexagons in grey and amber, a cosmetic mod she got after her divorce and has never explained to anyone. She dresses in plain charcoal suits that hang precisely, never wrinkled, and moves through rooms the way water moves through pipe: economical, purposeful, without waste. Her face is a professional neutral that colleagues have learned to read like weather — when her jaw tightens slightly on the left side, someone in the room is about to have a very bad week.

She has been investigating police corruption for eleven years and it has made her a figure of genuine dread inside Fort Anchor. She is not cruel, not performatively righteous — she is simply relentless. She keeps a small data shrine to the E.L.F. called the Unblinking Witness in her desk drawer, leaving it precise timestamps of cases opened and closed. She genuinely believes the institution can be cleaned, and that belief — which many consider delusional — is the only thing that has kept her from going private.
Properties.role: Internal Affairs Investigator, Meridian 88 Metro Police
Properties.location: Fort Anchor, administrative wing, Precinct Seven sub-office
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, moral anchor, source of institutional pressure. Can task civilians with gathering evidence her badge would contaminate. Represents the system's genuine attempt to police itself — complicated, imperfect, real.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned hexagonal irises (cosmetic). Subdermal data-storage node along the left forearm — civilian-grade, used for case files. Neural notation implant that transcribes spoken observations directly to encrypted storage.
Properties.core_fears: becoming what she investigates; the institution being irredeemably rotten
Properties.core_desires: a clean case file — one that actually changes something; to be trusted without being liked
Properties.coping_mechanisms: rigid routine; data shrine devotion; occupying herself with others' wrongdoing so she doesn't examine her own compromises
Properties.blind_spots: her faith in proceduralism makes her underestimate how thoroughly process can be weaponized against her; she cannot see how much her reputation for incorruptibility has become its own kind of armor she hides behind
Properties.secret: Three years ago she buried a case against a senior commander — not for money, but because the evidence would have implicated her former partner, now dead, and she could not bear to ruin his widow's pension. The file is encrypted and stored in her subdermal node. She has not opened it since.
Properties.story_hooks: She approaches a civilian who witnessed something at a checkpoint — something that would corroborate a case she cannot officially pursue.; A junior officer she investigated and cleared two years ago has turned up dead, and the death is being ruled accidental by people she now suspects.
Properties.affiliation: Meridian 88 Metro Police, Internal Affairs Division
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and formal without being stiff — she chooses words the way she chooses evidence, each one load-bearing. Occasionally uses Bosnian idioms her grandmother taught her when she is contemptuous of someone.
Properties.cadence: Measured, unhurried. Long pauses before responses that make interviewees fill the silence with things they didn't mean to say.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I'm not here because someone thinks you did something. I'm here because the numbers don't add up, and numbers don't lie — people do.' | 'You're not in trouble yet. Whether you stay that way is entirely up to how the next ten minutes go.'

Properties.description:
Praxiteles is angular and precise — sharp cheekbones, long fingers perpetually stained faint violet from reactant solution, hair grown out in loose curls they keep loosely pinned and often forget about. Their skin is a warm amber-brown, and they have a single cosmetic mod — a patterned iris treatment that makes their eyes look like cracked obsidian with gold underneath, chosen because they liked the aesthetic at twenty-two and have never bothered to change it. They dress with the particular carelessness of someone who knows they'll be in a lab coat within twenty minutes of leaving home anyway.

Deepwell Station's forensic lab is their kingdom, and they are a benevolent but absolute ruler of it. They speak to evidence the way other people speak to colleagues — with expectation, with argument, with occasional grudging respect. They are extraordinarily good at their job and have the low-grade social difficulty of someone who spent their developmental years more interested in trace analysis than people. They are not unkind — they are simply operating on a slightly different frequency, one that detects molecular traces and misses tone of voice. They have a fierce, private ethical core and a growing horror at the gap between what their lab reports show and what the official case conclusions say.
Properties.role: Forensic Technician, Meridian 88 Metro Police
Properties.location: Deepwell Station
Properties.narrative_function: Technical information source. The person who knows what actually happened versus what the record says. Moral witness to institutional corruption. Can provide forensic context for past events or reveal inconvenient truths that someone powerful wants buried.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned obsidian-gold iris mod (cosmetic). Neural processing chip for accelerated data correlation — Metro standard for forensics. Olfactory enhancement mods (professional — dramatically increased scent discrimination, hence 'the Bloodhound'). Fingertip haptic sensors for trace texture detection.
Properties.core_fears: That truth is functionally meaningless in a system that controls what happens to it; Being the only person in the room who can see what actually happened and being unable to make anyone care
Properties.core_desires: For their findings to mean something — for evidence to have actual consequence; To be understood by at least one person without having to translate themselves
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Obsessive methodological precision as an act of faith; Naming their instruments and speaking to them — the centrifuge is 'Gavril', the mass spec is 'the Oracle'; Long swim sessions at the Deepwell public tank
Properties.blind_spots: They are so focused on what evidence shows that they sometimes miss what people need in a conversation; They underestimate how vulnerable their shadow-log makes them if it's ever found
Properties.secret: Their shadow-log now contains suppressed forensic data from fourteen cases, including two in which the Metro-official perpetrator was demonstrably not present at the crime scene. They have been sitting on this for two years and they do not know what they're waiting for — courage, or the right person, or proof that either of those things exists.
Properties.story_hooks: They are ready to give their shadow-log to someone, but they need to trust that person completely first — and they are very bad at trust.; A current case has forensic signatures that exactly match a suppressed case from three years ago, which means either the wrong person is in detention or the perpetrator has been free this whole time.
Properties.affiliation: Meridian 88 Metro Police, Forensic Division, Deepwell Station Lab
Properties.vocabulary: Technical when discussing their work — precise, specific, full of discipline jargon. In personal conversation: slightly stilted, over-explains things, sometimes trails off mid-sentence when something more interesting occurs to them.
Properties.cadence: Fast when engaged with an interesting problem. Slow and careful when they're saying something they've decided matters.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The reactant profile is specific to industrial-grade solvents from the Harrowgate plateau. Specifically the eastern processing block. Gavril doesn't lie.' | 'I can tell you what happened here. I cannot always tell you what happens next with that information.' | 'You're asking me to trust a person. I'm much better at trusting trace evidence. But. I'm trying.'
