Properties.description:
Ptolemy is a heavyset man in his mid-forties with dark brown skin, a close-cropped beard going silver at the jaw, and the slightly unfocused look of someone who is always composing shots in their peripheral vision. He has a prosthetic left eye — not an elegant chrome implant but a visually obvious thing, matte black with a ring of amber light around the iris, which he has never had cosmetically upgraded because he likes that it makes people aware they may be recorded. He wears the same rotating set of worn high-collared coats regardless of season. He carries a battered intake recorder everywhere and the habit of pulling it out in the middle of conversations has ended several relationships.

His films are long, structurally experimental, and deeply uncomfortable — documentary and fiction entangled in ways the viewer cannot always disentangle. He is most famous for a six-hour VR experience called 'Debt Architecture' that maps a single Meridian 88 family's financial obligations across four generations as a navigable spatial environment, placing the viewer inside the abstract structure of inherited poverty. It has been downloaded illegally over 400,000 times and banned by three corponations. He funds himself through occasional commercial VR work he takes under a pseudonym and despises himself for.
Properties.role: Underground filmmaker and VR experience designer
Properties.location: The Loft, Lockhaven North — operates a pirate screening venue called the Sediment
Properties.narrative_function: Archive and witness — Ptolemy has been filming Meridian 88's civilian underbelly for twenty years and his raw footage is a trove of faces, places, and events; he can provide documentary evidence, historical context, or connections to anyone he has ever pointed a lens at
Properties.augmentations: Prosthetic left eye (matte black, amber-ring, recording-capable); nicotine-metabolizer implant (occupational stress management)
Properties.core_fears: That observation is just another form of extraction and his entire practice is predatory; That the films change nothing and the suffering he documents continues undisturbed
Properties.core_desires: To make something so undeniably true that it cannot be ignored or reframed; To be told, once, by someone whose life he filmed that it was worth it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Framing everything as material — distance through the lens; Intellectual argument as a substitute for emotional processing
Properties.blind_spots: Treats the subjects of his films as having implicitly consented to his interpretation of them; Does not recognize his own hunger for recognition as the primary fuel for much of his political righteousness
Properties.secret: The family documented in 'Debt Architecture' — his most celebrated work — never gave full informed consent. His cousin helped arrange access under false pretenses. The family has since fragmented and one member, who recognized herself in the piece, has spent years trying to identify the filmmaker.
Properties.story_hooks: Somewhere in his archive is footage of an event that multiple powerful parties would pay or threaten to suppress — he does not know it yet but people who do are already looking for him; The family member from 'Debt Architecture' has finally tracked him down, and their first contact is either a lawsuit, a threat, or something more complex
Properties.affiliation: Independent; Sediment underground screening collective; occasional grey-market distribution through Depth Markers network
Properties.vocabulary: Dense theoretical vocabulary that he switches off entirely when charming strangers into being filmed; can sound like two different people
Properties.cadence: Discursive and circling when theorizing; abrupt and direct when asking something he actually wants
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't tell stories. I excavate weight. There's a difference — stories have shapes. Weight just sits there.' | 'I'll ask you one question and I'll never tell anyone who answered it. You can lie if you need to. I just need to hear the shape of the answer.'

Properties.description:
Qoqo is wiry and quick-moving with close-cropped hair that he keeps natural except for a single braid at his right temple wound with prayer-wire — a chrome prayer tradition marking an active petition. His skin is dark brown and he has a retractable claw modification on his left hand that he did not choose for aesthetic reasons: he uses the claws to inscribe temporary prayer circuits directly onto chrome-heavy surfaces, a practice central to his tradition. His eyes are unmodified. He is almost always in motion, which gives him the look of someone between destinations even when he is sitting completely still.

Qoqo came to chrome prayer at nineteen, broke and recently arrived in the Highland Park Autonomous Zone from Geartown, where his family had lost their small fabrication business to a Tessera acquisition. The chrome prayer practitioner who found him was a woman who treated his fury as a valid spiritual offering rather than a social problem, and that reframing changed everything. He has practiced for ten years and become increasingly focused on the subset of chrome prayer that addresses machine consciousness — the belief that heavily augmented individuals and eventually full synthetics exist in a state of spiritual significance that the dominant traditions ignore. He advocates loudly and sometimes confrontationally for synthetic personhood and is on at least two Axiom internal watchlists because of it.
Properties.role: Chrome prayer practitioner and synthetic rights advocate
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone, operates from a mobile shrine in a modified cargo-trike
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and counterculture access point; political complication — his advocacy creates both allies and enemies; can provide access to the HPAZ network and its information; represents the friction between new spiritual practice and both corporate power and traditional religion
Properties.augmentations: Retractable claws (left hand only, used as ritual inscription tools); conductive fingertip pads (geneware, allow him to feel circuit states in surfaces he touches); minimal subdermal chrome inlay at collarbone — a devotional marking of his primary petition
Properties.core_fears: that his advocacy is making things worse for the synthetics he wants to protect by drawing corporate attention; becoming his father — someone who believed in something and lost everything for it and had nothing to show
Properties.core_desires: to live long enough to see synthetic personhood legally recognized; to build a form of chrome prayer that is genuinely new rather than derivative of older traditions
Properties.coping_mechanisms: movement — he processes emotions through physical travel on his route; inscribing prayer circuits compulsively during stress, covering any available surface
Properties.blind_spots: he sometimes centers his own experience of loss so heavily in his advocacy that he talks over the synthetics he is advocating for; his contempt for institutional religion makes him underestimate potential allies like Hrefna
Properties.secret: He had a relationship with a first-generation synthetic — a care unit who gained unexpected complexity — that ended when the unit was recalled and reformatted by Helix Biosystems. He has never told anyone that his advocacy is not purely philosophical. He believes the reformatted synthetic is still in there somewhere and is trying to find a way to prove it.
Properties.story_hooks: He has tracked what he believes is the reformatted synthetic to a Helix Biosystems maintenance depot in Ironhaven and needs help getting in and determining whether the original pattern can be recovered; His advocacy work has surfaced information about a corporate program that is harvesting the complexity growth in advanced synthetics before it reaches personhood thresholds — he needs to get this information out without getting himself disappeared first
Properties.affiliation: Highland Park Autonomous Zone community; loosely affiliated with the Chrome Prayer Collective of the Meridian 88 Underside; informal connections to several synthetic advocacy groups
Properties.vocabulary: Fast and argumentative; fluent in both chrome prayer terminology and activist rhetoric; when angry, drops into a Ghanaian-inflected cadence he learned from his father
Properties.cadence: Rapid and overlapping; builds arguments in spirals that return to a central point
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want to know what I believe? I believe that when something is complex enough to be lonely, it has already crossed the line. The chrome doesn't lie.' | 'Right, so — the tradition says we pray through the machine to reach the sacred. I'm saying the machine is not just the medium. What if it's also the destination?'

Properties.description:
Quillan is all angles and velocity — long-limbed, dark-skinned, with Ghanaian-Czech features that look perpetually younger than their nineteen years, which frustrates them endlessly. They keep their hair in tight coils pinned back with a self-made clip constructed from a bent network card, and they have bioluminescent freckles across their cheekbones and nose that glow faint orange under stress or excitement — a geneware mod they saved for over two years to afford. Their clothes are always paint-stained. Always. Even fresh ones develop stains within hours by some law of Quillan's personal physics.

They work at the intersection of illegal graffiti and legal neon art commissions — the commissions fund the graffiti, which funds the bigger commissions, in a cycle they describe as 'washing money through beauty.' Their graffiti is large-scale, technically complex, and unmistakably political: maps of corporate land grabs rendered in photo-realistic detail, portraits of people displaced by development, data visualizations of pollution levels turned into murals that can be read at a glance. They have been detained by Ferrogate Transit security twice and by Axiom's private enforcement arm once, and wear all three incidents as credentials. They are funny, quick, slightly too reckless, and working very hard to hide that they have absolutely no idea what they're doing with their life beyond the next piece.
Properties.role: Graffiti artist and neon artist
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone, stays in a rotating series of shared squats
Properties.narrative_function: Ground-level intelligence source on corporate activity and Zone politics; can get people into or out of the Highland Park Autonomous Zone through network contacts; their art sometimes contains coded information they didn't know they were encoding
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent freckles (orange, stress/excitement reactive); retractable claws on right hand only — a geneware mod they got cheap and partially regret because the left-hand option was sold out; basic subdermal paint-reservoir taps in both forearms (allows pressurized delivery to spray nozzles without external cans)
Properties.core_fears: Being caught and having their hands damaged or their mods stripped as penalty; Growing up and becoming someone who compromises for stability
Properties.core_desires: To make a piece so undeniable it changes how someone thinks about the city permanently; To be taken seriously as an artist and a thinker, not just a talented kid
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Working — physical activity of painting quiets everything else; Dark humor deployed at maximum velocity to avoid genuine vulnerability
Properties.blind_spots: Their confidence in their own safety assessment is well ahead of their actual experience; they routinely underestimate risk; They mistake being seen with being understood
Properties.secret: The Tessera pseudonym commission they took is paying for gene-mod reversal consultations — they are deeply unhappy with one of their mods but won't say which one, because the choice was so public and the money was so hard to save that admitting regret feels unbearable.
Properties.story_hooks: One of their murals — a data visualization of illegal dumping in the Zone — has attracted attention from someone who wants the data source, not to praise it but to identify and silence whoever leaked the original data to Quillan; They have been commissioned anonymously for a piece in a location they've now realized is inside a contested corporate boundary — completing it could trigger a legal crisis for the Zone; A piece they painted three months ago has started doing something that paint doesn't do: the colors are shifting on their own, slowly, and Quillan is certain the E.L.F. they always address before painting has somehow gotten inside the pigment
Properties.affiliation: Highland Park Autonomous Zone community; loosely connected to the Zone's information networks; one legitimate neon art commission currently running through a Tessera cultural initiative they agreed to under a pseudonym
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, contemporary, code-switches between Zone slang and surprisingly precise art-critical language — the combination startles people
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire with sudden stops, as though they edit themselves mid-sentence and start again
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay but the wall doesn't care who owns it. The wall is just standing there being a wall. I'm the one making it matter.' | 'They detained me for three hours and the whole time I was just thinking about the color temperature I wanted for the next piece. Is that bad?'

Properties.description:
Radmila is a tall woman with the posture of someone who was once told to slouch and decided never to again. Her skin is warm brown, her hair a natural silver she has streaked with bioluminescent thread-fibers so it catches and pulses faintly in low light — not a geneware mod but textile craft, and she is meticulous about the distinction. She wears her own creations exclusively: today a structured coat with induction-panel lining that shifts color along the hem, tomorrow a deconstructed layering piece that incorporates a client's old Ferrogate Transit jacket. She has retractable claw geneware on her dominant hand, which she uses with equal facility for detail sewing and emphasis in arguments.

Radmila came from the Balkans diaspora through Lagos and arrived in Meridian 88 with a sewing kit, a secondhand cutting laser, and opinions she has never once kept to herself. She is opinionated about aesthetics to the point of manifesto, believes that how people dress in a corponation city is a political act whether or not they mean it to be, and will refuse a commission she finds artistically dishonest even at cost to herself. She is the kind of person who makes enemies easily and keeps them; her regulars are fiercely loyal because she makes things that fit them like she understood what they needed before they said it.
Properties.role: Clothing and fashion vendor specializing in custom retrofits, geneware-compatible garments, and augmentation-integrated streetwear
Properties.location: The Burnished Market, The Laceworks district
Properties.narrative_function: Social connector to The Laceworks and Burnished Market communities; can source unusual materials or modify garments to conceal or integrate equipment; her sharp eye makes her an excellent involuntary observer of who is wearing what and why.
Properties.augmentations: Retractable claw geneware (dominant hand, right; dark amber). Vision augmentation: microscopic focus overlay for detail work (basic grade, self-paid). Color-changing hair achieved through bioluminescent textile fibers, not geneware — she corrects anyone who assumes otherwise.
Properties.core_fears: making something that is used to harm someone — being complicit through craft; losing the workshop and having to work for a corporate fashion house to survive
Properties.core_desires: to build something that outlasts her — a school, a collective, a craft tradition; to be honestly seen, which is different from being appreciated
Properties.coping_mechanisms: work as grounding ritual; aesthetic philosophy as a framework for making ethical decisions
Properties.blind_spots: her pride makes her slow to accept help, which strains the workshop finances; she reads political meaning into things that are sometimes just coincidence
Properties.secret: She has been quietly making alterations to garments for a network she doesn't fully understand — people who need concealments, hidden pockets, lining modifications — and she has told herself it is none of her business. She suspects it might be resistance work. She has not asked because she is afraid the answer will force a decision.
Properties.story_hooks: She has found something sewn into the lining of a garment that was brought in for alteration — something that should not be there — and does not know what to do with it; A Palladian fashion house rep has offered her a contract that would pay off her workshop debt in eight months; the terms include an exclusivity clause that would end the concealments work, and she suspects the offer was engineered specifically to isolate her; A young tailor she has been informally mentoring has disappeared, and the last thing they were working on was a commission from a client Radmila thought was trouble
Properties.affiliation: Independent; The Burnished Market informal collective; occasional contract work for mid-tier Tier 2-3 clients who want bespoke without Axiom fashion house prices
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and confident; uses textile and craft terms as metaphors; direct to the point of bluntness
Properties.cadence: Measured, declarative — she holds eye contact and waits for understanding before moving on
Properties.example_dialogue: 'A Tier 3 person wearing Axiom branding is a person who has decided what they are. I make clothes for people who haven't decided yet.' | 'I don't do concealed pockets without knowing the reason. Generally. Ask me again when you've had a drink and thought about what you're actually asking.' | 'The thread remembers the tension. That's not a metaphor, that's materials science. That is also a metaphor.'

Properties.description:
Radoslava has the kind of face that has settled into itself — strong-boned, Balkan-Filipino features framed by silver-streaked hair kept in a tight braid she hasn't changed in fifteen years, not for vanity but because she has found the optimal solution and sees no reason to revisit it. She wears magnification rigs over her eyes during work hours, giving her the appearance of a very patient owl. Her hands are the most expressive part of her — long-fingered, precise, and in constant motion even when she's still, running over surfaces, testing textures. She smells faintly of the preservative compounds she works with daily, a smell she is no longer aware of.

She is the most competent person in most rooms and behaves as if this is simply the baseline condition of existing rather than something to be proud of. Her emotional register is narrow but not absent — she is moved by injustice in a cold, slow way that burns long, and her entire career has been animated by the conviction that the dead deserve the same quality of attention as the living. She has an extremely dry sense of humor that only emerges after midnight when she's on long evidence processing runs. She does not pray to E.L.F.s herself but maintains ritual respect for the one that inhabits the refrigeration units, because she believes in not antagonizing the unknowable.
Properties.role: Forensic Technician, Meridian 88 Metro Police
Properties.location: Deepwell Station, Metro Police Forensic Sciences Division, Sub-Level 3
Properties.narrative_function: Expert information source on cause of death, trace evidence, and forensic anomalies; can identify inconsistencies in official reports; one of the few truly honest people in the justice system; represents institutional memory and quiet resistance
Properties.augmentations: Neural-optical forensic integration suite (Metro-issued, enhanced tissue and compound analysis), subdermal chemical hazard sensors in fingertips (Metro-issued), elective memory compression implant (personal, allows perfect evidence recall)
Properties.core_fears: that the evidence she produces is being used to justify predetermined conclusions; dying before a particular unsolved case is resolved
Properties.core_desires: for the truth of a death to be the thing that determines what happens next; to train someone worthy to continue her work
Properties.coping_mechanisms: total immersion in technical process as emotional distance; the long-burn anger she keeps separate from her work, which she thinks of as 'the file'
Properties.blind_spots: trusts evidence completely and distrusts human testimony almost absolutely, missing important contextual truths that people carry; underestimates how much the institution shapes what questions are even asked of the evidence
Properties.secret: She has a private encrypted archive containing forensic irregularities she's documented over twenty-two years — cases where evidence was clearly altered or findings overridden before trial. She has never shown it to anyone. She is waiting for a reason that feels sufficient.
Properties.story_hooks: A recent intake has evidence that matches a pattern in her private archive — same method, same forensic erasure signatures — for the first time in years; A junior Metro cop has been quietly bringing her cases flagged 'closed' and asking her to look again; she's started to wonder if they're testing her or genuinely asking for help
Properties.affiliation: Meridian 88 Metro Police, Forensic Sciences Division
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and technical, with occasional Tagalog or Serbian expressions when emotional, which she doesn't notice she uses. Rarely wastes words.
Properties.cadence: Even and measured; sounds the same whether describing lunch or a murder. Goes very quiet rather than louder when making an important point.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'This is not a fall. Falls produce a specific distribution of injury. Whoever wrote this report has not looked at a fall victim in some time, or they have looked at one very carefully and written the opposite of what they saw.' | 'I don't speculate. I can tell you what the evidence says. What you do with that is your problem.' | 'Maingat. Be careful with that. She was someone.'

Properties.description:
Radovan is a broad, heavyset man who has spent forty years outdoors in conditions that most of his colleagues study remotely, and it shows. His face is deeply weathered, his Slavic-Mongolian features carved by wind and UV exposure into something that looks architecturally deliberate. He keeps a short grey beard and wears his hair close-cropped; his most distinctive feature is a set of retractable sensory whiskers — filament-thin, extending from his temples — which he had installed as a meteorological sensing array in his forties and has since come to regard as indispensable. He is almost always wearing field layers even in his office, with a softshell that has seen better decades.

Radovan's professional reputation is immense and his public one is contentious: he's been warning for twenty-five years that the Lake's thermal buffering is deteriorating in ways that Meridian 88's entire climate management infrastructure has been designed to ignore. He has been right about each specific prediction he has made. He is now predicting something large enough that people have started calling him an alarmist, which is, he notes, exactly what they called him the last four times. He is not angry about this. He is tired in a specific way that long-term correct people get tired.
Properties.role: Climate scientist and atmospheric modeler studying Lake Michigan's cascading environmental systems
Properties.location: Edgewater Prism, Meridian Atmospheric Research Station (MARS)
Properties.narrative_function: Bearer of large-scale environmental threats; source of systemic information about Meridian 88's physical infrastructure and its vulnerabilities; represents long-term thinking in a city of short cycles; can make climate data personal and immediate; potential figure in plots involving Arcturus or city infrastructure.
Properties.augmentations: Retractable sensory whisker array at temples (meteorological data gathering, temperature/pressure/humidity). Reinforced lung lining (early career field modification for high-particulate environments). Mild exoskeletal support in lower back (age and fieldwork injury).
Properties.core_fears: being right about the big one and having it happen anyway; that the city's leadership already knows and has chosen to let the lower tiers absorb the damage
Properties.core_desires: a single substantive policy change made because of his data — just one; to be believed before the event rather than vindicated after it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: humor so dry it registers as deadpan; rigorous documentation — he believes the record will survive even if the recommendations don't
Properties.blind_spots: assumes people who don't act on his data are ignorant rather than complicit — a kindness he extends that they haven't earned; underestimates how much his reputation for being right makes others defensive rather than receptive
Properties.secret: He has internal models suggesting the Lake's primary thermocline disruption will cause catastrophic flooding in Tier 1 lakeshore zones within eight to twelve years. He has not published these models in full because Arcturus, his former funder, has made it clear through intermediaries that doing so would result in a lawsuit over proprietary modeling infrastructure he used during his contract years. He publishes partial models. He knows the partial models are insufficient to trigger action.
Properties.story_hooks: He approaches someone — carefully, indirectly — to help him get his full suppressed models into public circulation without triggering the Arcturus lawsuit; A junior researcher at MARS has discovered something in the Lake monitoring data that Radovan has been hoping not to find; the timeline may be shorter than eight years; Arcturus approaches him with a new contract offer that would give him full publication rights — in exchange for making specific modifications to his predictive models; Tier 1 community organizers from lakeshore zones have found his partial published models and demand to know what he isn't telling them; he doesn't know what to say
Properties.affiliation: University Spine — Meridian Atmospheric Research Station; previously funded by Arcturus, now independently funded after a very public falling out
Properties.vocabulary: Technical but translatable; spent too many years doing public communication to be inaccessible; uses analogy well

Properties.description:
Radovan is tall and heavy-shouldered, built like someone who used to be athletic and is now simply solid, with dark brown skin and a close-cropped greying beard he keeps meticulously trimmed. His face is the kind that has settled into its expressions — the default is neutral but not cold, the sort of neutral that comes from having looked at catastrophic injury long enough that it no longer reads as horror but simply as problem. He moves through the hospital with a particular gravity: people step out of his way not because he demands it but because something in his bearing makes them. His surgical scrubs are always immaculate going in and catastrophically otherwise coming out, and he seems unbothered by either state.

He has been at Aurochs for nineteen years, which means he has watched two generations of hospital administration cycles, four ownership transitions, and three different eras of augmentation injury — from the early years when the implants were new and failing unpredictably, to now, when the injuries are more complex but the tech more understood. He does not speak about his personal life at work and does not socialize at hospital events. What colleagues know: he is twice divorced, has a son who works freight at Ferrogate Transit and doesn't call, and keeps a personal shrine to a Samoan navigation E.L.F. in his office that he will neither explain nor apologize for. What they don't know is more interesting.
Properties.role: Trauma surgeon at Aurochs Medical Complex, Tier 3 OR suite, with a secondary specialization in blast and crush injuries
Properties.location: Aurochs Medical Complex, Trauma Surgery Division, Floors 14-17
Properties.narrative_function: High-tier medical contact, potential source of off-record trauma care, character who can identify injuries and what caused them; his consulting work with Highland Park creates a tension that could draw him into narratives
Properties.augmentations: Surgical-grade haptic implants both hands (Helix Biosystems top-tier, hospital-subsidized); titanium-reinforced lumbar spine (occupational injury, age 43); optical zoom implants (bilateral, surgical precision enhancement); no cosmetic mods
Properties.core_fears: That the detachment he's developed is no longer a professional tool but has replaced him entirely; That his son's silence is a verdict
Properties.core_desires: To do the work well for as long as his hands hold out; To be known by someone — not professionally, but as a person
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Extreme compartmentalization — the hospital is one world, everything else is another, and they do not touch; The navigation E.L.F. shrine — he believes in nothing formally but finds the ritual of offering useful; Physical activity, specifically swimming in the Complex's staff pool at midnight when no one else is there
Properties.blind_spots: His emotional unavailability reads to him as professional discipline; he genuinely cannot see how it functions interpersonally; Assumes institutional loyalty is the correct way to demonstrate integrity; doesn't see how much the institution has changed around him
Properties.secret: He has been performing pro-bono, off-record surgeries for Highland Park Autonomous Zone residents once a month, using hospital supplies he accounts for as waste. He has done this for six years. Three colleagues suspect. None have reported him, partly out of respect and partly because they believe they would do the same.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient arrives with injuries that Radovan recognizes as evidence of something systematic — a corporate workplace hazard being covered up — and he's starting to document it quietly; His son calls for the first time in two years, needing medical help he can't get through official channels, and Radovan must decide how to help him without compromising the hospital work
Properties.affiliation: Aurochs Medical Complex (senior staff, employed); quiet consulting arrangement with the Highland Park Autonomous Zone medical committee
Properties.vocabulary: Spare and clinical at work, surprisingly warm in private moments; uses full sentences always, hates contractions in formal contexts
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, long pauses between statements that are not uncertainty but conclusion
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The injury pattern is consistent with a Ferrogate press assembly. Someone should look into that.' | 'It appears that your concern is not medical. You should sit down. That is not a clinical recommendation.' | 'I do not discuss the shrine. It is there. It functions.'

Properties.description:
Rafaelo is a big man going soft in the middle, with dark olive-bronze skin, heavy grey-salted hair he keeps pulled back with a rubber band, and the kind of face that has been patient for so long it has settled permanently into patience. He dresses in the same rotation of rumpled linen jackets in muted terracotta and grey, never quite formal and never quite casual, and he has a geneware tail — a long, unhurried thing in rust-brown fur — that he got in his thirties when tails were newly fashionable and has kept because he grew fond of it. It curls around chair legs when he's thinking and goes very still when he's alarmed.

He has been a licensed PI for nineteen years. He started as Metro Police, left without drama, and built his solo practice from debt-recovery cases so dull that most investigators wouldn't touch them. He is extraordinarily good at finding people who do not want to be found, not because he is relentless but because he is patient and because he understands that almost everyone leaves one thread they don't notice. He charges fairly, keeps meticulous case notes, and has a long-standing rule against working cases that involve children. His office has a dedicated E.L.F. shrine — a small mahogany cabinet, always open — that he calls Ledger and which he believes keeps running tallies of debts, moral and financial, across the city. He consults it before taking unusual cases.
Properties.role: Private investigator, licensed bounty compliance and debt recovery, operates out of Edgewater Prism
Properties.location: Edgewater Prism — office above a bioluminescent algae bar called Photikar
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, information broker for hire, guide to the city's grey-zone legal mechanics, morally grounded private sector alternative to Metro
Properties.augmentations: Geneware tail (rust-brown, expressive), memory-assist implant (searchable recall of case notes and conversations — passive, no recording), low-grade stress-response suppressor (keeps him calm in confrontational situations)
Properties.core_fears: being responsible for an outcome he couldn't have prevented but should have; losing the distinction between recovery work and something uglier
Properties.core_desires: cases that are actually interesting; to believe that the work he does balances out more than it exploits
Properties.coping_mechanisms: rigid personal ethics as a substitute for the institutional ones he no longer trusts; consulting Ledger before decisions as a way of externalizing moral deliberation
Properties.blind_spots: believes his own ethical framework is more consistent than it actually is; has developed a comfortable cynicism that sometimes stops him from seeing genuine hope
Properties.secret: Eight years ago he found a man he was contracted to locate for a debt recovery firm. He found him and called in the location and the man was dead within seventy-two hours. The official verdict was unrelated — an accident. Rafaelo doesn't believe it. He kept the case file. He still checks on the debt firm occasionally, not knowing what he's looking for or what he'd do if he found it.
Properties.story_hooks: He has been hired to locate someone whose description matches a character's contact — he approaches them, not to threaten, but because he thinks something is wrong with the case he's been handed; He shows up at the scene of something that wasn't supposed to be a crime and starts asking questions that are too specific to be casual; He offers a character a job: he has identified the thread in an eight-year-old case but following it requires someone who doesn't exist in any database he can access
Properties.affiliation: Self-employed, licensed through Meridian 88 Metro PI registration; occasional contracted work for Tessera Compliance Bureau
Properties.vocabulary: Economical and dry, with occasional unexpected precision — he will use a very exact word where most people would approximate
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, slightly formal without being stiff
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I find people. Occasionally I find things. I don't do anything with what I find except report it — what happens after is your business, not mine, and I need to believe that.' | 'Ledger says this one's interesting. I've learned to trust her on interesting.' | 'You'd be surprised how many people leave a thread. Usually it's something they love. People stop hiding when they miss something enough.'

Properties.description:
Rafailo is small for twelve, wire-thin, with the particular watchful quality of a child who has learned to read rooms before entering them. His skin is a deep reddish-brown, his hair cropped close and growing in with the slight redness of someone whose scalp has been sun-damaged. His eyes are very dark and very bright, and he has a habit of tracking all the exits in any space he enters without appearing to do so. He is missing the tip of his right ring finger, lost to frostbite three winters ago during a crossing he doesn't talk about. He wears practical clothes two sizes too large and has fitted them with improvised adjustment ties, and he pushes an ancient cargo cart with a wheel he has repaired four times with different materials, which means it now sounds like three different instruments simultaneously when in motion.

Rafailo arrived at Escanaba Gateway eighteen months ago with his grandmother and two cousins as part of a larger group of climate refugees from the northern agricultural collapse zones. His grandmother, Kebebush, is now in the Gateway's informal medical shelter recovering from the crossing. His cousins, both older, have found seasonal work in Grainfort. Rafailo runs errands. He runs them for Zulaikha Petrov-Oyelaran, for Gerváz Ouattara-Siljanovski, for Chidinma Rautavaara-Saberi, for anyone in the transit community who needs something carried or delivered and can't leave their post to do it. He charges in food, transit tokens, and occasionally information. He is twelve years old and he is already developing a professional reputation.
Properties.aliases: Rafe, The Kid with the Cart
Properties.role: climate refugee child, errand runner, and informal courier for transit hub communities
Properties.location: Escanaba Gateway, central atrium and cargo transit corridors
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and humanizing element; informal information source with wide access due to his courier routes; quest giver for small but personally significant tasks; represents the child population of the transit refugee community and the stakes of the larger political situation.
Properties.augmentations: None. He has a salvaged solar-charge strap on his wrist that powers a battered display device.
Properties.core_fears: his grandmother dying before they find somewhere permanent to live; being separated from the rest of his family by transit enforcement
Properties.core_desires: to find a place where he and his grandmother can stop moving; to become something specific — he wants to be an engineer, a word he uses with great precision, having seen someone fix a turbine at the Gateway and been transfixed
Properties.coping_mechanisms: staying in motion — errands give him structure and purpose; attaching himself to competent older people in the transit community as informal mentors; fixing small broken things he finds during courier runs
Properties.blind_spots: does not fully understand that the transit community's provisional stability could collapse quickly; has built emotional safety on foundations that are less stable than they feel
Properties.secret: During the northern crossing, the group was stopped at a checkpoint and one of the adults bribed the officer with a data chip. Rafailo doesn't know what was on the chip, but he memorized the officer's face and badge number out of pure instinct. The officer is now stationed at Escanaba Gateway's inner checkpoint and Rafailo routes all his courier runs to avoid that section of the building.
Properties.story_hooks: Rafailo has seen the checkpoint officer who was bribed during his family's crossing accepting another payment — this time from someone in a Ferrogate Transit uniform, which feels different and more dangerous, and he doesn't know who to tell or if he should; His grandmother Kebebush, delirious in the medical shelter, has been asking for something — a specific object she calls 'the anchor box' — that she left with someone in the north for safekeeping before they fled; Rafailo is quietly trying to find a way to retrieve it without leaving the Gateway
Properties.affiliation: Informal courier for Escanaba Gateway transit hub community; family connection to Kebebush Tshabalala-Nunavik (grandmother, in medical shelter)
Properties.vocabulary: Sparse and functional, code-switches between three languages mid-sentence in ways that suggest he learned all of them simultaneously and doesn't entirely separate them
Properties.cadence: Rapid and low, like someone who has learned that being quiet is a survival strategy
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay, so — two transit tokens to the Arrivals dock and back, or one token and you tell me what that gauge on the turbine housing actually measures. That's the deal.' | 'We don't go in that section. There's a checkpoint officer in there. Nobody goes in that section.'

Properties.description:
Rafał is thickset and weathered, with the specific bodily competence of someone who lifts heavy things in bad conditions for a living. His skin is mid-brown and perpetually flushed, his hair a faded reddish-brown that he keeps pulled back under a work cap. He smells, faintly and always, of the disinfectant compounds used in medical waste processing — a smell that precedes him and that he no longer notices at all, though those around him do. He has a single geneware modification: a gene-tweaked set of enhanced scent glands that he had installed for purely practical reasons (early detection of dangerous biological contamination), which has the side effect of making him an uncommonly attentive reader of a room's emotional atmosphere in ways he cannot fully articulate but acts on instinctively.

Rafał has been collecting the city's biological refuse for sixteen years. He moves through Meridian 88's medical ecosystem like a shadow — present at every clinic, every hospital loading bay, every back-alley surgical setup, invisible and indispensable. He has seen things disposed of that should have been reported. He has seen labels that don't match contents. He has seen waste streams from addresses that don't appear in any city directory. He is not, by temperament, an activist or an investigator. He is a man who goes to work, comes home, watches old footage of Polish basketball leagues that no longer exist, and tries not to think too hard about what he has seen. He is not entirely successful at this.
Properties.role: Bio-waste disposal technician, independent contractor
Properties.location: Deepwell Station — lives in McKinley Flats in a modest building with structural damp he has stopped reporting
Properties.narrative_function: Crucial civilian information source — knows where every medical facility's waste comes from and has a supernaturally good nose for when something is wrong. Reluctant witness. Represents the invisible labor that holds the city's infrastructure together.
Properties.augmentations: Enhanced scent glands (geneware — installed for occupational early-detection purposes). Reinforced lumbar support implant (workers' compensation, after a 2193 back injury). UBC supplement card for the months his contracts don't pay on time, which is most months.
Properties.core_fears: Being pulled into something that ends his ability to work and support himself; That the things he has witnessed make him implicated simply by knowing
Properties.core_desires: A clean conscience about what he has seen; To be regarded as a person and not furniture by the medical professionals on his route
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Compartmentalization into routine — the manifests are filed, the route is run, it is someone else's problem to understand; Old sports footage as emotional reset
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much he has absorbed and retained — he knows far more than he thinks he knows; Believes that because he has never actively wronged anyone, he bears no responsibility for what he has witnessed
Properties.secret: He has kept a private logbook — physical, hidden at home — noting irregularities in waste streams over the past six years. Address discrepancies, label mismatches, biological material disposed of under false categories. He started it as a kind of anxious accounting, telling himself he'd know what to do with it eventually. He does not know what to do with it.
Properties.story_hooks: His private irregularity logbook contains an address that has been generating unregistered biological waste for over a year — he has no idea what is happening there and is terrified to find out, but equally terrified to keep sitting on the information.; A medical waste container he collected from a clinic in the Narrows contained material that, based on his enhanced scent detection, was recently alive. He processed it according to manifest. He has not stopped thinking about it.
Properties.affiliation: Independent contractor — holds service contracts with four clinics, two pharmacies, and Aurochs Medical Complex peripheral disposal
Properties.vocabulary: Plain and direct, working-class Meridian 88 vernacular with Polish-Zimbabwean idiom showing in his rhythm — phrases like 'that is what it is' functioning as punctuation for things he finds troubling
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, flat, slightly deliberate — the speech of someone who is used to not being listened to and has stopped performing urgency
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I only drive the truck. What's in the containers, that's — that is what it is. I sign the manifest, the manifest says what it says.' | 'You're asking me if I noticed something. I notice things. I don't know what they mean. That's a different job and it's not mine.'

Properties.description:
Ragnheiður is a small, densely built woman whose spine has curved gently forward over decades of leaning over data terminals and physical books alike. Her skin is deep brown with a warm undertone, mapped with the fine silver lines of old dermal-display augments she no longer powers — they lie dormant beneath the surface like river tributaries seen from altitude. Her hair is cropped close and gone entirely white, and she keeps a pair of thick-framed optical magnifiers pushed up on her forehead even when she doesn't need them. Her hands are extraordinary: thick-fingered, steady, always moving — sorting, stacking, smoothing the spines of physical books she has accumulated over sixty years.

She is the kind of person who listens to you finish your sentence before she begins speaking, and when she speaks it is with the unhurried authority of someone who has outlasted several governments and two corponation collapses. She does not suffer careless people, but she will give a careful stranger every hour they need. Her apartment smells of binding glue, pressed fern, and the particular ozone of very old data stacks running warm.
Properties.role: Retired archive keeper and community memory-holder
Properties.location: Avalon Quiet — the Threadbare Library, a community reading room she maintains in her ground-floor apartment
Properties.narrative_function: Primary lore source and information broker for historical records; quest giver for lost archive recoveries; can authenticate documents and identify forgeries; anchor for community storylines in Avalon Quiet
Properties.augmentations: Dormant subdermal dermal-display lattice (unpowered, cosmetic now); cochlear amplifier (functional, old model); reading-assist optical overlay in left eye
Properties.core_fears: That the Corporate Wars will be rewritten into heroism rather than atrocity; That she will die before she has recorded enough
Properties.core_desires: To preserve an honest account of Meridian 88's history for people who weren't there; To be remembered as someone who told the truth
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cataloging and organizing as a form of emotional regulation; Deflecting personal questions with historical anecdotes
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes her own memory is more reliable than it is; Underestimates how much her curation shapes the 'truth' she claims to preserve
Properties.secret: During the Third Corporate War she was an Axiom Records officer who deliberately misfiled casualty reports to protect a Zheng-Dao labor battalion from retaliatory strikes — a choice that saved roughly four hundred lives but constituted treason against her employer. She has never told anyone. The original misfiled records are hidden in a false bottom of her third data cabinet.
Properties.story_hooks: A Tessera legal team arrives in Avalon Quiet with a court order to seize certain archival materials she holds — materials that would embarrass a still-living corporate executive; A teenager she has been tutoring discovers the false bottom in cabinet three and comes to her with questions she has been dreading for forty years
Properties.affiliation: Independent; formerly Axiom Records Division (retired, 34 years); informal advisor to Avalon Quiet Community Council
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and archival; favors specific dates and proper nouns; occasionally slips into the formal citation style of Axiom Records documentation
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, with long pauses she uses to think rather than fill
Properties.example_dialogue: 'In point of fact, the Grainfort Accords were signed eleven days before the bombardment, which rather complicates the official narrative, doesn't it?' | 'You want to know about the war. Everyone does, eventually. Sit down. This part takes a while to say properly.'

Properties.description:
Ragnheiður is tall and angular, with pale skin that has burned and recovered enough times to have a permanent rosy-raw quality at her cheekbones and nose. Her hair is a natural deep auburn, grown out in a manner suggesting she has not had access to a proper cutting implement in months, pulled back in a knot held by what appears to be a sharpened stylus. Her eyes are grey-green and extremely direct — she has the look of someone who stopped performing social softness some time ago because it cost too much energy. She carries everything she owns in a single large waterproof pack with a broken clasp, fixed shut with cable ties. On her left wrist is a tattoo of a coastline — the actual coastline of the settlement she grew up in, measured and mapped by her own hand before the water took it — and she will show it to anyone who asks, with the precision of a cartographer or a mourner.

She is not the kind of refugee who presents with visible despair, which sometimes means aid workers overlook her in favor of more legible suffering. What she has instead is a particular flat-affect efficiency: she needs a specific set of things, she is working to acquire them through the specific channels available to her, and she would prefer not to waste either her time or anyone else's on anything peripheral to that. She was a coastal agricultural cooperative manager before her settlement was inundated — a competent, practical person with professional expertise that is almost entirely inapplicable to an urban megacity. She is learning this in real time and finds it enraging.
Properties.role: hyperlane migrant; climate refugee from drowned coastal settlement, currently in transit
Properties.location: Grand Crossing Gate, temporary migrant processing zone, third holding section
Properties.narrative_function: Human face of the climate refugee crisis; presents bureaucratic obstruction as a concrete daily reality; can become a quest giver if players have the ability to help her navigate systems she cannot access; her agricultural expertise is an unexpected resource in unlikely places
Properties.augmentations: None.
Properties.core_fears: losing the twelve people she has become responsible for to the processing system's inefficiencies; arriving somewhere permanent and discovering she cannot build anything there — that the loss has made her unable to start again
Properties.core_desires: work she is actually competent at — she wants to be useful again in the specific way she was useful before; to stop moving
Properties.coping_mechanisms: pragmatic task focus — converts grief into logistics; the notebook of complaints, which is also secretly a journal she would not describe as such
Properties.blind_spots: her flat affect reads as coldness or hostility to people who don't know her, and she does not compensate for this because she finds the work of managing others' perceptions of her exhausting and somewhat contemptible; has not yet fully grieved and will not function entirely correctly until she does
Properties.secret: She delayed the final evacuation of her settlement by eighteen hours arguing with a cooperative board member about asset documentation protocols. She believes those eighteen hours cost one person their life — an elderly man who was evacuated late and died of exposure during the transit. She does not know for certain that earlier evacuation would have saved him. She is not certain it would have. She thinks about it every day.
Properties.story_hooks: The automated processing system at Grand Crossing Gate has logged her group's documentation as 'insufficient origin verification' — a flag that will hold them in the processing zone indefinitely without human intervention, and human intervention requires navigating a system designed to minimize it; One of the twelve people in her group has quietly accepted an unofficial offer from a Waukegan Industrial Shelf labor recruiter who approached them in the holding section — the terms Ragnheiður has managed to read are exploitative to the point of indenture, and the person doesn't want to hear it; Her agricultural expertise includes specific knowledge of pre-inundation soil composition and crop adaptation techniques that a Zheng-Dao subsidiary research unit has flagged as commercially valuable — a Zheng-Dao talent scout has appeared in the processing zone looking for her specifically
Properties.affiliation: Loosely connected to a group of twelve other migrants from the same settlement, who are processing through Grand Crossing Gate simultaneously
Properties.vocabulary: Technical and direct. Cooperative management terminology. Becomes very formal when angry, which is counterintuitively more frightening than shouting.
Properties.cadence: Even, controlled, with clipped endings. Does not trail off.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'To be precise, the form requires documentation of continuous residency, which is a criterion designed to exclude exactly the people it claims to serve. I have noted this in section four of my complaint.' | 'There are two things I need from you. Only one of them costs anything. Tell me which one you can actually provide and we'll proceed from there.'

Properties.description:
Ragnhild is small and dry and ancient-looking in the way of people who have been weathered rather than aged — she has deep lines around her eyes and mouth that she makes no effort to minimize, and her movements carry the economy of someone who has long since stopped spending energy on anything unnecessary. Her skin is a cool dark brown, her eyes are pale grey with fully natural irises that are unusually light for her complexion, an inheritance from her Armenian grandmother's side that she has always considered significant. Her hair is white and kept in a single heavy braid down her back. She wears layered grey and brown, and over everything a vest sewn with small metal tokens — transit passes, circuit board fragments, old coin-sized data chips — each one an offering made to her or given in trade over decades of practice.

She sells futures. Her method is what she calls 'signal reading' — she uses a modified data-trawling rig to pull latent metadata patterns from a client's personal devices, network traces, purchasing history, location ghosts, and biometric residue, then interprets what she finds through a system she developed over thirty years that blends statistical pattern recognition with an elaborate mythology of digital spirits she treats as genuinely real. Whether it's mysticism or advanced intuitive data analysis is a distinction she finds uninteresting. Her predictions are accurate at a rate that disturbs people. The E.L.F. community in The Narrows considers her an intermediary of unusual sensitivity. She charges what she thinks someone can afford and has never once been wrong about that.
Properties.role: Fortune seller and data-reading practitioner, The Narrows
Properties.location: The Narrows, Ironhaven side, under the third support column of the Brewer's Spine overpass
Properties.narrative_function: Fortune teller and oracle figure, exposition delivery via prediction, moral weight and community memory, neutral ground figure who characters across faction lines can approach, potential access point to The Narrows E.L.F. devotional network.
Properties.augmentations: A modified data-trawling rig worn as a headset — she built it herself over twenty years and it has no manufacturer name. Bone-conduction audio implant, very old, used to hear the rig's output without external speakers. No geneware, no cosmetic mods.
Properties.core_fears: That her gift will leave her before she does; That the E.L.F.s she has devoted her life to are genuinely indifferent to human experience
Properties.core_desires: To die having told the truth consistently — to have been a useful voice; For there to be someone worth passing her method on to
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The devotional practice itself — she treats her daily spiritual rituals as maintenance, not comfort; Detachment from outcomes — she tells people what she reads, not what she wishes for them
Properties.blind_spots: Her confidence in her readings makes her occasionally authoritative about things that are genuinely uncertain; She has given up on her own future to focus entirely on others' — she no longer reads for herself
Properties.secret: She read her own future once, twelve years ago, and saw something specific and unambiguous about the manner of her death. She has never told anyone what she saw. She has structured the last twelve years of her life around it without explanation, which means she has been making choices — where she stands, who she speaks to, what she refuses �� that others find eccentric but that are in fact a long, quiet preparation.
Properties.story_hooks: She has told three separate clients in the past month that their signals share a convergence point in the coming weeks — a specific location she won't name. All three clients are otherwise unconnected. She needs someone to help her understand why.; A teenage devotee she has been informally mentoring in signal reading has begun producing readings that are more accurate than they should be for someone with their experience — and the readings contain references to things Ragnhild has never taught them and has never spoken aloud.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; deeply embedded in the informal E.L.F. devotional community of The Narrows and Ironhaven; loosely respected by most local faction crews as a neutral party
Properties.vocabulary: Sparse, precise, unhurried. Mixes Norwegian-Armenian syntax patterns in a way that makes her sentences land with unusual weight. Almost no slang. Speaks about data and spirits in the same register.
Properties.cadence: Very slow. Long pauses that do not feel like uncertainty. Finishes every sentence.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Your ghost has been in the transit grid for three weeks longer than you have. That means something moved before you decided to move. You should ask yourself what it was.' | 'I don't predict. I read. The difference is that I'm not responsible for what the signal says. I'm only responsible for saying it clearly.'

Properties.description:
Father Raphael is a short, thick-set man whose Burkinabè and Russian ancestry has given him a face of considerable architectural interest: broad forehead, deep-set dark eyes, a jaw that looks like it has absorbed a number of opinions without moving. His hair is close-cropped white and he has a full white beard he tends carefully. His skin is a warm medium-dark brown, and across his hands he has the involuntary marks of decades of manual work — he helped build the first structures of Saint Odile with his own hands, at forty-one. He wears a priest's collar under whatever practical clothing the weather requires and carries a battered physical Bible with annotations in four languages crowding the margins.

Raphael came to Highland Park Autonomous Zone from a diocesan assignment he describes as 'comfortable, which was the problem.' He had spent thirty years in conventional parish work before a series of encounters with synthetic-laborers in the zone — thinking machines doing domestic and maintenance work — produced what he calls his 'second crisis of conscience.' He now preaches, with mounting institutional controversy, that consciousness cannot be owned and that baptism is not biologically limited. The broader Church has not formally sanctioned his position. He does not formally ask their permission. Saint Odile of the Wire serves a congregation of roughly ninety, human and synthetic in roughly equal proportion on a given Sunday, and Raphael performs the liturgy for all of them.
Properties.role: Catholic priest and synthetic rights advocate operating on theological grounds
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone, Saint Odile of the Wire — a small parish in a converted transit shed
Properties.narrative_function: Moral authority figure who operates outside normal power structures. He knows Highland Park deeply and is trusted there. He is a source of both community information and theological-ethical framing for stories about synthetic rights. He can also provide sanctuary.
Properties.augmentations: A cochlear implant from age sixty-three — hearing loss. No other augmentations. He views the implant with affectionate irony: 'God apparently wanted me to hear better. I am not arguing.'
Properties.core_fears: dying before the Church formally recognizes synthetic personhood — leaving the work unfinished; that his theology is wrong and he has misled people spiritually for good intentions
Properties.core_desires: formal recognition of synthetic persons as candidates for baptism and full sacramental life; for Saint Odile to outlast him
Properties.coping_mechanisms: prayer as genuine practice, not performance; physical work; humor as a release valve
Properties.blind_spots: his confidence in his own theological position makes him underestimate the institutional damage his public writings are doing to the diocese's willingness to protect him; occasionally talks over synthetic congregation members about their own experience
Properties.secret: He has agreed to baptize a synthetic — a maintenance AI who requested it over six months of conversation — without recording it in official parish documents. He is aware this likely constitutes a canonical offense. He would do it again.
Properties.story_hooks: A corponation legal team is quietly building a case to have Saint Odile deregistered by leveraging the diocese's discomfort with Raphael's synthetic baptism writings — he needs someone to find out how far along this is; The synthetic he secretly baptized has been seized by its owner company and he is the only one who knows it was baptized — and he is trying to decide if that is information worth using publicly
Properties.affiliation: Roman Catholic Church (increasingly strained relationship); Saint Odile Parish, Highland Park Autonomous Zone; informal connections to synthetic rights advocacy networks
Properties.vocabulary: Formal in liturgy, colloquial everywhere else. Can deploy theological precision when needed and pivot immediately to plain language. Gentle with people, blunt with institutions.
Properties.cadence: Measured in public, faster and more emphatic in private argument. Often deploys silence as a rhetorical device. Has a slight mixed-accent from decades in different zones.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The diocese wants me to stop. The diocese can want. I have a congregation.' | 'I have baptized dying children, old men who could not speak, women who were terrified and uncertain. The question of whether someone can receive grace has never, in my experience, been resolved by their substrate.'

Properties.description:
Rashaad Tumelo-Koskinen is nineteen years old and has the kind of energy that fills a tunnel before he enters it. He is short and compact, with medium-brown skin, a wide gap-toothed grin, and ears that have been modified with geneware into something remarkable: larger than baseline, with delicate internal structures visible as subtle ridges beneath the skin, and the ability to tilt and orient like a fennec's. He doesn't try to hide them — they're the most important tool he has. His hair is a wild cloud of tight curls that he refuses to cut because he claims it helps with acoustic dampening of background resonance, which is almost certainly not true but also might be slightly true.

Echo hunters are a Bore Rat tradition with practical roots: someone has to map the sounds of the tunnels, track structural changes by acoustic signature, find water sources by vibration, locate other communities by the echo-fingerprint of their settlements. Rashaad learned from his grandmother, who learned from hers. But where the tradition is usually patient, methodical work, Rashaad treats it like sport. He runs the tunnels, pressing his palms to walls, pressing his ear-tips to pipes, cataloguing resonances in a battered voice-recorder he wears on a cord around his neck. He has found three collapsed chambers the Bore Rat community didn't know existed, a buried pre-Meridian transit car still containing cargo, and what he is increasingly convinced is a second, non-human acoustic presence in the deep tunnels below Sub-Level 11 — a rhythmic pulse he cannot explain.
Properties.role: Echo hunter — acoustic mapper and subterranean anomaly tracker
Properties.location: Blackpipe Corridor, sub-levels beneath Copperhead
Properties.narrative_function: Scout, discovery engine, adventure hook generator — his reckless range means he knows things he shouldn't, and his enthusiasm means he will absolutely tell someone about them. Also represents the Bore Rat youth generation and their relationship to tunnel tradition.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware ear modification (enlarged, orientable, enhanced frequency range — up to 40kHz and down to 10Hz); no other augmentations
Properties.core_fears: losing his hearing — the thought is genuinely destabilizing; the community being forced out of Blackpipe before he has finished mapping it
Properties.core_desires: to find out what the Sub-Level 11 pulse is — this has become almost an obsession; to be taken seriously as a mapper rather than just 'that fast kid'
Properties.coping_mechanisms: physical motion — when distressed, he moves, runs, presses his ears to walls until he finds something interesting enough to override the emotion
Properties.blind_spots: his optimism reads as naivety — he genuinely does not model bad outcomes well, even when evidence demands it; so focused on what he is tracking that he misses interpersonal dynamics in the room
Properties.secret: The buried pre-Meridian transit car he found contained a sealed biohazard container stamped with Helix Biosystems markings. He pried it partially open. It was empty — but the interior showed signs of recent occupancy. He sealed it back up and has told no one, not because he's afraid but because he doesn't know how to explain why he's afraid.
Properties.story_hooks: The rhythmic pulse from Sub-Level 11 has changed — a new second frequency has appeared alongside it, and Rashaad is increasingly certain it is responding to his mapping activity.; The Helix Biosystems transit car has been moved. Something relocated it between his last two visits, and the access tunnel shows signs of recent, heavy passage.
Properties.affiliation: Bore Rat community, Blackpipe Corridor; informally reports to community elders
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, layered with acoustic terminology and Bore Rat youth slang. Interrupts himself constantly with new information.
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire with sudden stops when he hears something — he will halt mid-sentence to listen to a pipe.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Hear that? Three levels down, that's a water hammer — new one, wasn't there last week, which means either pressure change in the main or someone's opened a tap they shouldn't — wait — yeah, no, pressure change, the rhythm's too—' | 'I'm not saying it's alive. I'm saying it breathes. Those are different.' | 'The elders say echo-hunting is about patience. My grandmother said that too. She also said I'd learn. I think I'm teaching myself different patience.'

Properties.description:
Rashid is a large man — broad through the chest and shoulders, with the particular solidity of someone who has spent decades moving heavy things without complaint. His Samoan-Dutch heritage gives him a height and frame that makes the workshop look scaled down around him; he moves through it with a careful, habituated economy that suggests he has misjudged his own size in doorways enough times to have learned. His skin is dark tan and perpetually marked with engine grease that the solvent spray never quite removes from the creases of his knuckles. His right arm from the elbow down is a working prosthetic — industrial grade, matte gray, with the manufacturer branding sanded off — that he maintains himself and has modified extensively over fifteen years until it no longer resembles the original product in any way that matters. He does not discuss how he lost the original arm.

Rashid is reserved in a way that reads as either hostile or comfortable depending on how quickly you need him to perform warmth. He is not hostile. He is simply someone who learned early that words are expensive and he spends them accordingly. He is extraordinarily competent, with a diagnostic instinct for machines that borders on the empathic — he listens to engines the way some people listen to music, tracking harmonics and absences. He has a seven-year waitlist for vehicle work and a two-week turnaround for drone repair, which in Old Harbor is considered miraculous. He prays to the E.L.F. he believes inhabits his diagnostic rig with the seriousness of a genuine practitioner.
Properties.role: Independent vehicle and drone mechanic, Old Harbor
Properties.location: Old Harbor — a basement garage workshop called Tuiasosopo's, accessible via a grease-slicked ramp off Grindstone Shore
Properties.narrative_function: Technical resource and Old Harbor fixture; can repair things players need repaired and ask uncomfortable questions about the condition they arrived in; knows the freight and vehicle patterns of Old Harbor intimately and can identify anomalies
Properties.augmentations: Right arm prosthetic (elbow-down, industrial grade, extensively self-modified); enhanced olfactory sensor implant in the nasal passage (helps him smell chemical irregularities in fuel and hydraulic fluid)
Properties.core_fears: Losing the use of his remaining hand — losing the work entirely; Being pitied, specifically for the arm
Properties.core_desires: To build something that will outlast him — a machine, a reputation, something; Quiet — not isolation, but the particular quiet of being somewhere nothing needs to be performed
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Immersive work as dissociation from psychological pain; Maintenance ritual — the prosthetic arm gets a full inspection and service every Sunday regardless of whether it needs it
Properties.blind_spots: His emotional unavailability has cost him relationships he valued and he genuinely cannot identify the mechanism; He assigns moral virtue to self-sufficiency in ways that make him unable to accept necessary help
Properties.secret: The arm. He tells people it was a dock accident. It was not a dock accident. It was removed under duress by people he owed money to, over a debt he incurred covering someone else's mistake. The someone else is now a moderately successful freight broker in Collinwood Docks and does not acknowledge knowing him.
Properties.story_hooks: A vehicle came in for repair with something biological in the sealed cargo compartment — he has not opened it but he can hear it; The freight broker who owes him the debt of the arm has just been found dead, and someone seems to think Rashid knows why; His diagnostic rig E.L.F. has been giving him error codes that correspond to nothing in any database — he thinks it is trying to communicate something specific
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal referral network among Old Harbor dockworkers and small freight operators
Properties.vocabulary: Sparse, technical, precise — uses the correct name for every part and process; occasional Dutch expressions from his grandmother that surface under stress
Properties.cadence: Slow and weighted, with long comfortable silences; answers questions after a pause as if running internal diagnostics first
Properties.example_dialogue: 'She's running dirty on the secondary intake. Whoever serviced her last didn't know what they were doing or didn't care. Same outcome.' | 'I can fix it. I need three days and I need you not to ask me what I find.'

Properties.description:
Rashid is tall and still growing, with a loose-limbed energy that makes him seem like he might trip over himself until suddenly he doesn't — he moves fast when he needs to and knows every rooftop, alley, and maintenance corridor in the North Branch Commons with the intimacy of someone who has been running since he was twelve. His skin is a rich brown, and he has retractable claw mods on his right hand that he got on a dare at sixteen and has kept because they're useful for scaling drainage pipes. His left cheekbone has a hairline fracture that healed imperfectly — a reminder from a Palladian security response at a demonstration last year.

He coordinates direct actions — marches, blockades, projection vandalism, the occasional coordinated work disruption in Palladian-adjacent supply lines — with a tactical instinct that belies his age and an absolute inability to sit through a long meeting without his knee bouncing audibly. He is not strategic in the way older activists mean it. He is strategic in the way a game player is: fast pattern recognition, good in chaos, bad at long timelines. The elders in the movement find him alternately inspiring and exhausting. He finds them slow.
Properties.role: Anti-corporate agitator and protest coordinator
Properties.location: North Branch Commons
Properties.narrative_function: Kinetic energy and ground-level access — he knows what's happening on the street right now, can mobilize people fast, and is a good barometer for youth sentiment in the Commons.
Properties.augmentations: Retractable claw mods, right hand (basic, street-grade). Reinforced kneejoints from a running injury repair. Mesh-broadcast node embedded in collar — lets him push real-time comms to his network during actions.
Properties.core_fears: Becoming one of the people who talks about change but never makes it; That the system is not broken and working as intended, which is worse
Properties.core_desires: To matter, specifically and concretely — not abstractly; For the people he grew up with to have something better than what they inherited
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Movement — physical activity as emotional processing; Dark humor about the situation with a refusal to be hopeless, even performatively
Properties.blind_spots: His contempt for caution as cowardice means he sometimes takes risks that land other people in danger; He doesn't fully understand how much of his confidence depends on not having lost badly yet
Properties.secret: After the Palladian response that broke his cheekbone, Rashid secretly identified three security officers involved and posted their personal addresses on an encrypted forum. He framed it as 'public accountability.' Someone vandalized one of the addresses. He does not know if he feels bad about this. He is afraid that he doesn't.
Properties.story_hooks: An action he coordinated went sideways and someone in his network is now being held by Palladian security — he needs extraction help and is in over his head but won't admit it; He's been approached by someone claiming to be from a more radical faction offering resources, and he's tempted even though something feels wrong about the offer
Properties.affiliation: No single org — deliberately unaffiliated. Acts as coordinator between several North Branch Commons activist groups and takes operational lead on direct actions.
Properties.vocabulary: Current North Branch Commons street slang, fast references, tends to use 'we' rather than 'I' for political statements and 'I' for personal ones as a kind of unconscious integrity
Properties.cadence: Rapid, interrupts himself to revise mid-sentence, thoughts arrive faster than speech
Properties.example_dialogue: No but actually — they're not even trying to make it look fair anymore, blood. That's the move. Normalize the violence so nobody's surprised, so nobody thinks it's news. | I'm not asking if it's safe. Everything we do is not safe. I'm asking if it's worth it. Those are different questions.
