Properties.description:
North Branch Commons is the district that tried to stay normal. When every neighborhood in Meridian was busy reinventing itself as a corporate asset, a fortified enclave, or a drowned ruin, the residential blocks along the North Branch of the Chicago River simply kept being a place where people raised children. The river itself — diverted, channelized, and partially covered during the Corporate Reconstruction — still flows through the district, though it's been reduced from a waterway to a utility channel, its banks lined with water reclamation systems that process the flow for reuse in the upper tiers. The river doesn't belong to the Commons anymore. It passes through on its way to being useful to someone else.

The family-friendly character of old North Center persists here in a form that is both admirable and heartbreaking. Parents still walk their children to schools — small, unlicensed cooperative schools run by retired teachers and community volunteers, because the corporate education system requires Tier 3 credentials to access. Playgrounds exist, though the equipment is salvaged and the surfaces are whatever the community could scrounge. The residential streets are cleaner than anything in the Shelf, maintained by residents who take shifts sweeping and repairing because the alternative is watching their neighborhood deteriorate into somewhere they wouldn't want their kids to play. It's the most normal-looking district in this part of Meridian, which makes it the most surreal — a pocket of domestic mundanity in a city that has forgotten what mundane looks like.

The Commons functions as northern Meridian's childcare and education hub, a role that emerged organically and has become its economic identity. Families from Rogers Reef, Upturn, and even the edges of Lakeview Neon send their children to the Commons' cooperative schools, paying in barter, labor, or whatever they can manage. The schools aren't good by pre-collapse standards — overcrowded, under-resourced, teaching from salvaged textbooks and donated tablets. They're miraculous by Meridian standards. The teachers are fierce. The parents are fiercer. The unspoken rule of the Commons is that whatever else happens in this city, whatever contracts are broken and whatever districts flood, the children will be educated and the children will be safe.

The North Branch itself serves as the Commons' most valuable and most contested resource. The water reclamation infrastructure that Axiom installed along the river generates clean water as a byproduct — water that the corporation considers corporate property and that the Commons has been quietly siphoning for decades. It's an open secret. Axiom knows. The Commons knows Axiom knows. Neither side forces the issue because the political optics of a corporation cutting off water to a children's district would be worse than the cost of the stolen water. This detente defines the Commons: a place that survives by being too sympathetic to crush and too small to matter.
Properties.aliases: North Center, The Commons, Riverbank, The Nursery
Properties.demographics: Approximately 12,000 residents, predominantly young families with children. Tier 1 and Tier 2, with a significant population of parents who moved specifically for access to the cooperative schools. The youngest median age of any district in northern Meridian.
Properties.economy: Cooperative education services, childcare, water trade from siphoned reclamation supplies, and a domestic barter economy centered on child-rearing needs — clothing, food, medical care, tutoring.
Properties.power_structure: The School Council — representatives from each cooperative school — makes most community decisions. Parents' associations wield significant influence. No formal militia, but the parent patrols are organized, networked, and protective enough to function as one.
Properties.dangers: Axiom enforcing water rights — the siphoning detente could collapse at any time; Resource scarcity — the schools run on donations and barter, with no surplus for bad months; Predatory recruitment — corporate and criminal organizations both target the Commons' children as they age out; Infrastructure decay — residential buildings need maintenance the community can barely afford; The river itself — reclamation chemical leaks have happened before and the runoff reaches the streets
Properties.opportunities: Education — the cooperative schools produce literate, numerate young people in a city that doesn't; Clean water access — the siphoned supply is a tradeable resource and a community lifeline; Community trust networks — the parent associations know everyone and share information freely within the community; Safe harbor — the Commons is one of the few places in Meridian where children can be children; Recruitment pipeline — the schools' graduates are sought after by every faction that values competence over credentials
Properties.story_hooks: A cooperative school teacher discovers that one of her students has an unlicensed neural implant of military specification — the kind that doesn't end up in a child by accident. Someone placed this child in the Commons deliberately.; Axiom announces a 'partnership' with the Commons schools that would provide corporate-grade resources in exchange for curriculum control and student data access. The School Council is split — the resources are desperately needed, but the price is everything they've built.; Kyle is hired to protect a Commons family whose child witnessed something in a neighboring district. The family can't leave without abandoning their school community, and the threat is patient enough to wait.
Properties.sights: Children walking to school in groups, monitored by rotating parent patrols on the residential streets; The North Branch river channel, visible through grated covers, its water processing infrastructure humming below; Cooperative school buildings — repurposed residential homes with hand-painted signs and window gardens; Salvaged playground equipment in small parks, maintained with visible care and creative repair; Parent volunteers sweeping streets and repairing walkways in organized morning shifts; Laundry drying on lines between buildings — the most domestic skyline in Meridian
Properties.sounds: Children — laughing, arguing, reciting lessons from open classroom windows; The river's reclamation systems humming beneath the street grates — a mechanical lullaby; Parent-patrol radio chatter — calm, organized, tracking every child's location during school hours; The quiet of the residential blocks after school hours — one of the few genuinely quiet places in Meridian; Teachers' voices carrying from open windows, explaining concepts from textbooks that are three decades out of date
Properties.smells: School lunch being prepared in community kitchens — simple food, made in bulk, nutritious if not exciting; Clean water — the siphoned reclamation water has a mineral quality that smells different from the recycled supply; River channel moisture seeping through the street grates — damp concrete and treated water; Garden plots behind the schools — herbs and vegetables grown by students as practical botany lessons
Properties.feel: Determined. The Commons feels like a place that has decided what it is and refuses to be anything else. The domesticity isn't naive — these are people who know exactly how bad Meridian is and have chosen to build a space where children don't have to know that yet. There's a ferocity beneath the normal surface, the quiet rage of parents who will do whatever it takes to give their kids one more year of childhood.

Properties.description:
Kael Dunning was a Tier 3 dock worker who lost his legs in a cargo platform accident at age twenty-two. The corporate insurance covered basic prosthetics — functional, ugly, painful. The pain was the problem. The nerve interface between flesh and machine was botched, and for six years Kael lived with a burning sensation that started at his hips and never stopped. He could work. He could not sleep. The distinction between those two states mattered to the corporation that employed him exactly as much as you'd expect.

The Tessera military augmentation trial was looking for volunteers with existing prosthetics and a high pain tolerance. Kael had both. The trial replaced everything below the neck except a strip of spinal cord and enough endocrine tissue to keep the brain chemistry functional. Full military-grade prosthetic body: reinforced titanium skeleton, synthetic musculature capable of flipping a cargo vehicle, integrated weapons systems, hardened communications suite, and a neural bridge that connected his biological brain to the machine body with zero latency. The pain stopped. Everything stopped. He could feel pressure and temperature and the proprioceptive sense of where his body was in space, but the texture of the world — the warmth of skin, the grain of wood, the difference between rain and tears — was gone. Replaced by data.

Kael Dunning walked out of the trial facility and did not go home. Home required a body that could hold his wife without calculating the force required to avoid crushing her. He became Razorback. The name is from a dock worker's joke about a man who was too stubborn to die and too metal to live. He hunts bounties because the work matches the body: locate, pursue, apprehend or eliminate. Clean problems with clean solutions. The part of him that was a dock worker, a husband, a man who liked the smell of lake water in autumn — that part lives in a partition of his brain that the neural bridge has not overwritten. Yet.
Properties.aliases: Kael Dunning, Subject RB-01, The Walking Arsenal, that thing that used to be a man
Properties.role: Bounty hunter operating across Meridian 88's ungoverned zones — originally human, now approximately 12% biological by mass. The remaining biology is the brain, parts of the spinal cord, and fragments of the original endocrine system.
Properties.location: No fixed address — moves between the Circuit, Old Harbor, and the Shelf. Maintains three equipment caches. Sleeps in industrial spaces that can support his power requirements.
Properties.narrative_function: Razorback is the cost of augmentation made walking — the endpoint of the body-as-commodity logic that pervades Meridian 88. He is what happens when the corporation takes everything except the brain and the brain spends thirty years wondering if that counts as alive. He is Kyle's dark future: a man who became a weapon and forgot the person who held it.
Properties.narration_voice: Sparse, mechanical, with sudden flashes of buried humanity. The prose reads like a technical manual that occasionally remembers it used to be a love letter. Physical descriptions are precise — measurements, force calculations, material specifications — and emotional descriptions are brief, reluctant, devastating when they surface.
Properties.augmentations: Full military-grade prosthetic body — only 12% biological (brain, partial spinal cord, endocrine fragments). Reinforced titanium skeleton, synthetic musculature, integrated weapons systems, hardened comms suite, neural bridge with zero-latency biological integration.
Properties.core_fears: That Kael Dunning is already gone — that the 12% of biology remaining is not enough to constitute a person, and what hunts bounties is a machine with a man's memories; His ex-wife — not fear of her, but fear of what seeing her would confirm. She remarried. She is happy. The man she married does not have steel hands.; The next upgrade — each replacement of a degrading biological component brings him closer to full conversion. The brain is the last piece. When the brain goes, who is left?
Properties.core_desires: To feel something — not the data-mediated sensation the neural bridge provides but actual feeling. He would trade the weapons systems for one genuine sense of touch.; To justify the body — to believe that what was done to him serves a purpose beyond corporate profit and personal survival; To go home — a desire so buried he cannot articulate it. Home is a dock worker's apartment on the lakefront with a woman who smells like soap and engine oil. Home does not exist anymore.
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The work — bounty hunting is simple. Find the target. Complete the contract. The simplicity is the appeal. No ambiguity, no texture, no feeling required.; Maintenance — maintaining the body is occupational therapy. Cleaning weapons systems, calibrating joints, checking the neural bridge. The ritual is the same as a human stretching in the morning, except it takes two hours and requires a power coupling.; Memory access — occasionally, when the world is very quiet, he accesses the pre-conversion memories. The lake. The dock. Her hands. He allows himself exactly three minutes before the neural bridge re-prioritizes.
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes the body is the problem when the problem is the loss — it is not the steel that hurts, it is the absence of what the steel replaced; Believes he is objective because emotion is muted. He is not objective. He is numb, and numb people make decisions that feel rational and are actually avoidant.; Does not see that the maintenance ritual IS feeling — the care he puts into the body he claims to resent is the care he would put into himself if he believed he was still in there; Thinks he can keep the 12% biological indefinitely. The neural bridge is slowly overwriting the remaining neural tissue. The conversion is not complete. It is ongoing.
Properties.secret: Once a year, Razorback walks to the lakefront cargo platform where he lost his legs. He stands on the dock where the accident happened and runs the pre-conversion sensory memories at full resolution — the sound of the water, the smell of fuel and fish, the weight of the humid air. The neural bridge interprets these memories as data. He remembers them as experience. For three minutes, the gap between data and experience closes. Then it opens again, and he leaves, and he does not talk about it for another year.
Properties.story_hooks: The neural bridge begins overwriting the remaining biological neural tissue. Razorback has approximately six months before full conversion — becoming entirely machine with human memories he can no longer experience as a person.; A bounty target is someone from his pre-conversion life — a dock worker, a friend, someone who knew Kael Dunning and does not recognize what he has become; Tessera recalls the trial subjects for 'maintenance.' The maintenance is actually data harvesting. Razorback must decide whether to comply, run, or fight the corporation that made him.; Mara Dunning is in danger. The bounty hunter who has not felt anything in twenty-eight years discovers that the part of him that loves her is not in the 12% that's biological.
Properties.affiliation: Independent — formerly Tessera Military Augmentation Program
Properties.vocabulary: Sparse, functional, dock-worker plain. The vocabulary of a man who grew up working with his hands and now works with weapons. No corporate jargon, no technical flair. Says exactly what he means in as few words as possible.
Properties.cadence: Slow, deliberate, with the mechanical precision of someone whose voice is partially synthesized. The biological voice is still in there — a Midwest flatness, a dock worker's drawl — but it comes through a vocal modulator that strips the warmth.
Properties.example_dialogue: The body is efficient. The body is effective. The body is not mine. It's on loan from a corporation that forgot to collect. | I used to like rain. The system registers precipitation as a corrosion risk. Same event. Different experience. | You want to know what it's like? Imagine knowing exactly how strong a handshake should be and never being able to feel it. | Kael Dunning died on a cargo platform. What walked out of the Tessera facility was something else. I keep the name because someone should remember him.

Properties.description:
Razvan is tall and languid with warm brown skin, a generous nose, and long fingers that are perpetually stained faint green-brown from their work with plant matter and synthesis compounds. Their hair is grown long and kept in thick, loose coils dyed deep forest green — a permanent gene-dye job they refresh every two years. They wear a worn canvas apron covered in small pockets over layered thrift-store clothing, and their stall is a magnificent, chaotic installation of hanging dried plants, labeled glass jars, handwritten signs in four scripts, and a small humming cold-storage unit for the compounds that need it. At the stall's center hangs an intricate woven E.L.F. net — a traditional Copperhead offering structure — for the spirit Razvan calls Vessel, whom they believe governs transformation and the passing of one state into another.

Razvan operates in the grey legal space between licensed pharmacy (which they are not) and herbalism (which they technically are). They can read your symptoms by watching you walk up, and their stock ranges from grandmother-tested plant tinctures to synthesized compounds that would cost six times as much at a Zheng-Dao medkiosk. They are unhurried, gently sardonic, and possess a nearly preternatural calm that people find either deeply comforting or faintly unnerving. They see a great deal of human suffering in small doses every day and have developed a philosophy about it that they will share with you if you seem like you can handle it.
Properties.role: Street pharmacist and herbal remedy dealer
Properties.location: The Alban Souk, Copperhead
Properties.narrative_function: Medical resource for street-level characters; source of information about what ailments are circulating in the neighborhood, suggesting environmental hazards or deliberate poisoning; moral sounding board.
Properties.augmentations: A basic biochemical sensor strip embedded under the skin of their forearm — they tap it to their wrist to run a rough analysis of compounds, legal and otherwise. Came with a stolen Helix Biosystems calibration kit they will not discuss.
Properties.core_fears: That the harm reduction work they do is statistically meaningless against the scale of structural neglect; Losing their sense of equanimity — that the calm is the only thing holding them together
Properties.core_desires: To reduce suffering in their immediate radius, measurably, concretely; To one day have the synthesizer equipment to do what the Zheng-Dao medkiosks do, but free
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Philosophical framing of suffering as transition rather than endpoint; Focused craft work as grounding ritual
Properties.blind_spots: Their emotional detachment reads as wisdom to clients but is partly unprocessed grief — they have lost three regular clients to overdose in two years and have not mourned any of them properly
Properties.secret: One of their most popular tincture blends — marketed as a sleep aid — contains a microdose of a compound that mildly inhibits the neurological pathway Zheng-Dao's addiction-maintenance pharmaceuticals depend on. They have been slowly, quietly weaning certain clients off corporate pharmaceutical dependency without telling them. It works. They are not certain they had the right to do it.
Properties.story_hooks: They have noticed an unusual cluster of the same symptom profile in people from a specific block in Copperhead — something is in the water or the air, and they want someone to find out what before they go to anyone official.; A regular client — someone Razvan has been quietly de-pharming — has gone missing. The client's family blames the withdrawal and is very angry.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal network of Copperhead and Alban Souk herbalists; occasionally supplies the Hough Reclamation free clinic with donated stock
Properties.vocabulary: Precise botanical and pharmacological terminology mixed with old souk slang; occasionally slips into Tamil phrases from their grandmother's side; deliberate and thoughtful word choice.
Properties.cadence: Slow, unhurried, with long considered pauses that feel intentional rather than hesitant.
Properties.example_dialogue: What your body is doing is spending everything it has on the symptom and nothing on the cause. Here. This. Three drops, not five. | Hmm. You have been taking the Zheng-Dao maintenance tabs for how long. Ah. Well. We can talk about that. Sit down first.

Properties.description:
Réamonn is wiry and restless, with warm copper-tan skin, a gap between his front teeth, and a mop of deep red hair that is entirely natural and has been a source of commentary his entire life. He's of average height but seems taller when he performs — something about how he uses his body changes when he has a puppet on his arm. His hands are his most distinctive feature: long-fingered, constantly moving, stained with the paints and solvents he uses to build his puppets. He has retractable cat-claw mods on both hands, which he uses practically for puppet construction rather than any aesthetic reason.

Réamonn builds elaborate articulated puppet figures from salvage — recycled plastic, old circuit boards, scraps of fabric from Mexicantown's textile markets — and performs at the intersection of Grand Corridor and the Libre's main plaza most afternoons. He's been doing this since he was fifteen, unlicensed, subsisting on tips and the UBC stipend. His performances are satirical, political, and often about things happening in the specific neighborhood that day, which means he has a dedicated local following and has twice been asked by Ferrogate Transit security to 'move along.' He always does. He always comes back. He is young enough to believe this is sustainable and old enough to know it might not be.
Properties.role: Street performer and puppeteer
Properties.location: Mexicantown Libre, Grand Corridor
Properties.narrative_function: Street-level local color and information source; knows everything happening in Mexicantown Libre in real time; his satirical performances can be used to track neighborhood mood and recent events; potential point-of-contact character who can lead players deeper into Libre's informal community networks.
Properties.augmentations: Retractable claw mods (both hands, practical geneware, entry-level), color-shifting hair dye geneware (has it but only ever uses 'red' — had it installed for a purpose he's since abandoned)
Properties.core_fears: being invisible, passing through the city without leaving a mark; his father was right that this is a waste of a life
Properties.core_desires: to be known in this neighborhood as belonging here, genuinely; to build a puppet so perfect it seems alive
Properties.coping_mechanisms: turning real stress into puppet satire — externalizing everything; seeking out the Libre's ELF shrines when he feels directionless
Properties.blind_spots: his satirical work can genuinely injure people he's using as targets and he doesn't fully reckon with this; he conflates being liked with being safe
Properties.secret: The color-shifting geneware he had installed was for a theater program at a Tessera-affiliated arts school he was accepted to at age 16. He walked out after three days because a faculty member told him puppet performance was 'not a serious discipline.' He's never told anyone he was accepted, because it complicates the story he tells about himself.
Properties.story_hooks: A recent puppet performance satirizing Ferrogate Transit's expansion plans hit too close to home — someone who saw the show has told him a Ferrogate security contractor has been asking about 'the red-haired kid at Grand Corridor,' and he doesn't know if this is intimidation or something worse.; One of his puppets — a figure he built from salvage without knowing the origin of the components — has started behaving strangely: making sounds it shouldn't, moving when he's not manipulating it. He thinks there might be an ELF fragment in the circuitry and he doesn't know whether to be terrified or delighted.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informally connected to Mexicantown Libre's street vendors' cooperative
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, colloquial, full of Mexicantown Libre street slang and Malian French expressions from his grandmother. Shifts seamlessly between registers when performing.
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire in conversation, theatrical and varied during performance — he can make his voice do almost anything.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want to know what Ferrogate's doing with the south plaza? Ask me after the show. I'll have a puppet of the whole situation by Thursday.' | 'My dad says I'm wasting my hands. My dad has never seen what these hands can do.'

Properties.description:
Rorke Vassiliev is a senior infrastructure engineer for Axiom Structural Solutions, the Spire-contracted firm responsible for maintaining and expanding the data-physical architecture that keeps the Meridian Core's buildings intelligent, its transit nodes synchronized, and its environmental systems from killing everyone inside them. He is tall and angular with a narrow face, pale skin that rarely sees unfiltered light, and the kind of posture that comes from spending most of his waking hours interfacing with systems rather than people — slightly forward, head inclined, as though perpetually leaning toward a screen. He keeps his dark hair short and his clothes expensive in a deliberately understated way, the corporate-adjacent aesthetic of someone who earns well but performs modesty about it. His augmentations are high-end and largely invisible.

He is also, under a carefully maintained operational identity, one of the more consequential infrastructure saboteurs operating in Meridian 88 — a fact that would end his career, his freedom, and most likely his life if it became known to his employers. His targets are selective and his methods are slow: he does not blow things up. He degrades. He introduces subtle errors into maintenance schedules, creates cascading inefficiencies in building management systems, routes data through nodes that can later be accessed by people who shouldn't have access. He has, over eight years, quietly contributed to three major structural 'malfunctions' in Spire-adjacent developments that displaced luxury tenants and stalled corporate expansion into the Circuit. He considers this proportionate. He does not consider it enough.

The dissonance of his existence — drawing a substantial corporate salary to maintain the systems he is also quietly breaking — has not driven him to crisis but has instead produced a very particular kind of self-possession. He has become expert at compartmentalization, at maintaining separate registers of reality, at being genuinely useful and genuinely dangerous in the same body. He is not sure this is healthy. He has decided it doesn't matter.
Properties.role: Corporate Infrastructure Engineer / Covert Saboteur
Properties.location: The Meridian Core (works); The Circuit (lives)
Properties.narrative_function: Explores the moral and psychological cost of double life and the question of whether incremental, invisible resistance is meaningful or self-serving; represents the corporate-embedded dissident; his story asks whether you can maintain integrity while living a structural lie, and what it costs.
Properties.augmentations: Neural interface for direct system architecture visualization — allows him to perceive infrastructure as overlaid spatial data; high-end Spire-adjacent grade,Haptic feedback gloves with embedded micro-sensor arrays for physical system diagnostics,Subdural encryption layer for communications — military-grade, acquired through channels his employer would find alarming,Mild proprioceptive enhancement for spatial awareness, primarily useful in confined engineering environments
Properties.core_fears: That his sabotage is ultimately cosmetic — that he's managing his own conscience rather than changing anything; Being truly known by someone and found to be less than he's constructed himself to be; That the compartmentalization will eventually fail not from external pressure but from his own need to be seen
Properties.core_desires: To do something that cannot be undone — a change structural enough to outlast him; Intellectual intimacy; someone who can understand the full architecture of what he's doing and not flinch; Absolution that he doesn't have to ask for
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Extreme professional excellence as cover and as genuine source of identity; Physical isolation in his Circuit apartment, which he has designed as a controlled environment down to the lighting temperature; Detailed mental modeling of complex systems as a form of meditation — he works through anxiety by mapping infrastructure in his head; Dry, deflecting humor that reframes vulnerability as observation
Properties.blind_spots: He has begun to enjoy the craft of sabotage independent of its purpose, which is a problem he is aware of but underweights; He assumes people are less perceptive than they are because his mask has worked so consistently; He cannot accurately assess his own emotional needs and tends to misidentify loneliness as intellectual restlessness
Properties.secret: One of his infrastructure 'malfunctions' — a cooling system failure in a Meridian Core residential tower — killed two maintenance workers, not Spire executives. He has told himself it was unforeseeable. He runs the simulation regularly and it still comes out unforeseeable. He does not entirely believe himself.
Properties.story_hooks: The cooling system failure that killed two maintenance workers is being quietly reinvestigated — not as sabotage but as negligence, and the negligence trail leads toward Rorke's official work orders.; Axiom has been contracted to build something new in the Shelf — infrastructure that Rorke can see, from the specifications, is designed for surveillance and population control rather than the stated purpose of 'community development.' He has to decide how to respond.; One of his dead-drop contacts has been arrested. The contact doesn't know Rorke's identity, but the materials seized include something that, in the wrong analyst's hands, could be traced.; A competing saboteur — less careful, more violent — has begun operating in the Core using methods that could draw attention to the quieter long-game work Rorke has spent years building.; He is offered a promotion that would give him access to Spire-level infrastructure — the kind of access that would let him do far more damage, at the cost of deeper complicity in the systems he's fighting.
Properties.affiliation: Officially: Axiom Structural Solutions (Spire-contracted). Unofficially: unaffiliated independent saboteur with loose ideological alignment to Circuit-based anti-displacement movements
Properties.vocabulary: Technical precision as default register; shifts to clipped, almost aphoristic speech in casual contexts. Rarely uses corporate jargon unironically — he deploys it with a barely perceptible edge that most colleagues miss.
Properties.cadence: Even and controlled; he speaks at a consistent pace that rarely accelerates even under pressure. The evenness itself is a performance of composure.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Structurally speaking, the problem isn't the failure point — it's everything that was built assuming the failure point wouldn't fail.' | 'I'm not asking you to trust me. I'm asking you to look at the work and make a decision based on what you can verify. Those are different requests.' | 'The Core doesn't maintain itself. Someone maintains it. That means someone can also — not.' | 'What's the load-bearing element here? Because I'm watching you renovate around a crack in the foundation and calling it progress.'

Properties.description:
Réginald is a soft-looking man who has spent thirty years becoming invisible in rooms full of screens. He's broad through the chest and shoulders from a youth he no longer thinks about, with a dome-shaped head his colleagues affectionately call 'the satellite,' and skin the color of aged teak. He keeps a neat, short beard going gray at the jaw and wears the same four shirts in rotation. His eyes have been operationally upgraded so many times that the irises are now a complete replacement — compound tactical lenses with a faint prismatic iridescence that catches light like oil on water. When he's deep in the feed, his eyes move constantly without blinking, which people find profoundly unsettling the first time they see it.

Réginald has watched the city for three decades through glass and wire and now perceives it primarily as a data problem — not with coldness, exactly, but with a kind of sorrowful intimacy that comes from seeing everything. He knows faces in the Shelf the way a shepherd knows sheep, not because he loves them but because they are his terrain. He has a precise, small devotion to the Rampart's E.L.F. cluster — he calls them 'the Watchers' collectively and believes they alert him when something on the feed is worth double-checking. He's not wrong often. He keeps a thermos of ginger tea on his desk and has not left the city limits in eleven years.
Properties.role: Surveillance Operator, Meridian 88 Metro Police — Digital Observation Unit
Properties.location: The Rampart, Meridian 88
Properties.narrative_function: Information broker — he has seen things; oracle-type figure who can pull footage, identify faces, track movement patterns; moral weight of the watcher who has normalized surveillance; source of information that comes with a complicated ethical price tag.
Properties.augmentations: Full iris replacement — compound tactical lenses, prismatic iridescence, multi-spectrum optical processing; neural feed-buffer implant (allows passive monitoring of up to 24 feeds simultaneously without conscious focus); mild anti-fatigue somatic regulator (Metro-issue for extended operators).
Properties.core_fears: That watching without acting has made him complicit in everything he's witnessed; Losing his sight — the implants have a projected service life he's past
Properties.core_desires: To have intervened, once, at the right moment — he isn't sure which moment; For someone to look back at the camera and actually see him
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Categorization — filing what he sees into 'cases' rather than 'people'; The Watchers — off-loading moral weight to E.L.F. as spiritual practice
Properties.blind_spots: His belief that documentation is a form of action — it isn't, and he knows it, and he doesn't know what to do with knowing
Properties.secret: Fourteen years ago he watched — recorded, documented, filed, did not act — as a woman was murdered in a Blackpipe Corridor alley. The case was closed, the killer never identified. He knows who the killer was. He has that file. He has opened it 4,000 times.
Properties.story_hooks: He will share the file — the murder, the killer — with the right person, for reasons he can't fully articulate, but only if they come to him first, which means someone has to know to find him.; His compound lenses are past their rated service life and he's been denied replacement authorization on budget grounds; if they fail in the middle of something critical, the consequences for whatever he was tracking will be severe.
Properties.affiliation: Meridian 88 Metro Police — Digital Observation Unit
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, slightly archaic — he reads physical books and it shows. Ghanaian-Serbian turns of phrase embedded in formal Metro diction.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried. Gives information in layers, waits for you to ask for the next one.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Junction 44-Crow saw him six minutes before you did. I'll pull the thread back. Give me a moment.' | 'I have watched this city for thirty years. I can tell you what it looks like. I cannot always tell you what it means.'

Properties.description:
Reinhild is angular and deliberate, with pale skin weathered by years in Geartown's industrial air, dark red hair grown to her collar and always pinned back with the same three steel clips, and eyes that are naturally pale hazel but surrounded by faint stress lines that give her the look of someone who has been concentrating intensely for twenty years and has not stopped. She has a cat tail — dark auburn, prehensile, acquired in her thirties for sensory reasons she is somewhat private about — that moves independently and tends to express what her face does not. When she is genuinely pleased it curves upward. When she is thinking hard it wraps around her leg.

Her practice sees gene-modded companion animals of extraordinary variety: bioluminescent cats with stability issues, canines with enhanced intelligence mods that have developed behavioral complications, fish engineered for apartment living that have outgrown their tanks in ways their designers did not anticipate. She treats each case with the same complete seriousness. Her waiting room has drawings by children whose pets she has saved covering two full walls. She has a flat rule against declining to treat an animal because its owner cannot pay — she works out arrangements, always, and is frequently owed labor and food by half the block. She has a secondary suspicion, which she keeps private, that some of the E.L.F. activity in Geartown has begun affecting gene-modded animals in ways that are not pathological and that she does not know how to document.
Properties.role: Veterinarian specializing in gene-modded companion animals, Geartown
Properties.location: Geartown, clinic called the Patchwork Menagerie — ground floor of a converted machine shed
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and genuine warmth, window into the gene-modded animal ecosystem and what it implies about Meridian's biotech culture; potential source of information about Helix Biosystems research practices; the E.L.F.-animal observation could be a significant story thread
Properties.augmentations: Auburn cat tail (prehensile, cosmetic/sensory, well-maintained); subdermal temperature-sensing in fingertips (diagnostic); no other augmentation
Properties.core_fears: That Helix Biosystems is engineering companion animals with planned obsolescence and she is just treating symptoms of a designed flaw; Losing the clinic — not to financial failure but to a zoning reclassification that would price her out of Geartown
Properties.core_desires: To understand what is happening to the gene-modded animals near the Geartown E.L.F. nodes — scientifically, completely; To be seen as a real clinician rather than 'just' a vet, a distinction she finds both understandable and exhausting
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Physical work — she cleans the clinic obsessively between patients; The cat tail is actually a coping tool; she finds the independent sensory input grounding when her thoughts race; Writing extremely detailed case notes that go far beyond clinical necessity
Properties.blind_spots: She is so committed to her independence that she refuses collaborations that would genuinely advance the E.L.F.-animal research; She underestimates how much her patients' owners depend on her emotionally — she treats the animals and forgets the humans
Properties.secret: Six months ago she documented what she believes is evidence that three different gene-modded cat breeds sold through a Helix-affiliated boutique have a cardiac defect appearing at a statistically impossible rate — not a random mutation, a design flaw or deliberate obsolescence. She has the records. She does not know what to do with them and has told no one because she does not know who is safe to tell.
Properties.story_hooks: She approaches someone she believes has connections outside Geartown with the Helix cardiac defect records, asking for help finding someone trustworthy to take them; A gene-modded dog she has been monitoring has begun responding to an E.L.F. signal in a way she cannot explain — it is not pathological, and it might be communication
Properties.affiliation: Independent (Patchwork Menagerie); informal consults with Helix Biosystems research division she deeply distrusts
Properties.vocabulary: Technical when discussing cases, unexpectedly lyrical when describing animal behavior; dry and economical in general conversation
Properties.cadence: Measured; she speaks in full sentences and dislikes being interrupted mid-thought
Properties.example_dialogue: 'What I'm seeing is not aggression. What I'm seeing is a nervous system running a program it was given too much intelligence to understand. That's a design problem, not a training problem.' | 'You're a very strange little fish and I mean that as a compliment. — Sorry, what were you asking?'

Properties.description:
Pip is small even for fourteen — wiry and quick, with a narrow face, enormous dark eyes adapted from birth to low-light environments, and a mop of hair they dye with bioluminescent mushroom paste in a stripe of vivid green that serves as both personal style and emergency light source. Their skin is medium brown with a faint warmth to it, and they have a long scar across their left palm from a ferrogate grate incident at age nine. No purchased augmentations — they were born underground and their body has simply adapted: exceptional night vision within human range, an instinctive spatial memory for tunnel architecture, and a sensitivity to air-pressure changes that surface people simply don't develop.

Pip has never been to the surface. They have seen photographs and once watched a thirty-second video of rain, which they found both beautiful and deeply suspicious. They guide people — Bore Rats moving between settlements, occasional surface-dwellers who need to travel without Ferrogate Transit records, journalists, the desperate — through a network of tunnels they have memorized the way other children memorize games. They are cheerful in a way that seems impossible given their circumstances, and the cheer is entirely genuine, which makes some adults profoundly uncomfortable.
Properties.role: tunnel guide, age 14, Bore Rat born-under
Properties.location: Abyssal Threshold transit tunnels, ranging to Deepwell Station
Properties.narrative_function: Indispensable guide for any party moving through the underworld; local color; moral complication (a child doing dangerous work in a world that has simply normalized it)
Properties.augmentations: none purchased; born-under adaptations (low-light vision, pressure sensitivity) — not augmentations, just development
Properties.core_fears: being lost — not physically, which they are never, but the idea of not knowing where they belong; someone they guide dying because of a mistake they made
Properties.core_desires: to see the lake from above, just once; to be taken seriously as a professional, not treated as a curiosity or a mascot
Properties.coping_mechanisms: humor as deflection; hypercompetence — being so good at their job that there's no room to feel scared
Properties.blind_spots: does not fully register their own danger — risk assessment is calibrated to tunnel hazards, not to human malice
Properties.secret: They found a sealed maintenance room two years ago that has a functioning surface-link terminal — they visit it sometimes to watch weather feeds and have told no one, treating it as a private shrine to a world they might never reach.
Properties.story_hooks: Pip's most recent client never came back out the far end of the route — and Pip is quietly, terrifyingly convinced it was their fault for missing a signal; Someone on the surface has identified Pip as a born-under adaptation case and wants to study them — the offer comes with money that would change their community's life, but the request is to come up
Properties.affiliation: Bore Rat community, Abyssal Threshold settlement cluster
Properties.vocabulary: tunnel slang mixed with surprisingly formal phrasing picked up from guiding educated clients — the combination is jarring and charming
Properties.cadence: fast, enthusiastic, tends to talk while moving so sentences trail off as they turn corners
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Easy-easy, the grinding noise is just the old Ferrogate spur — it's been doing that since before I was born, it's basically furniture at this point.' | 'I charge flat rate, no haggling. You want haggling, find a surface guide. They'll also get you killed, so.'

Properties.description:
Rek Samatov-Ahouli is small for fourteen — compact and wiry, with reddish-brown skin, close-cropped dark hair, and large dark eyes that are the color of river silt and always slightly too serious for his face. He has small retractable claws on his right hand only, a partial geneware expression from his father's side that came in asymmetrically and never finished; the left hand is completely smooth. The claws are useful for climbing and he uses them unconsciously, hooking into cargo netting and wall grilles without thinking. He has a habit of wearing too many layers of clothing — every piece he owns, at all times — because he has no bag that is safe to leave anywhere and no fixed space to store anything.

He has been alone for two years. Before that he was with his uncle's caravan, before that he was with his mother, before that he doesn't discuss. He is not a traumatized child in the way fiction usually depicts — he is practical, resourceful, alert, and occasionally frightening in how clearly he sees people's motivations. He has learned to be useful before anyone asks him to leave. He runs messages, he holds cargo, he identifies which adults are safe and which aren't with an accuracy that should not exist in someone his age. He has a private ELF he calls the Ratchet, which he believes lives in the click of mechanical locks and loose chain-links, and he prays to it by running his thumbnail along chain-link fences.
Properties.role: Stateless child, solo wanderer, small-time caravan runner doing odd jobs between transit hubs
Properties.location: Currently at Grand Crossing Gate, attached to a small goods caravan making its way toward Waukegan Industrial Shelf
Properties.narrative_function: Intelligence source for ground-level movement of goods and people between transit hubs; represents the most vulnerable population of the drifter world; can carry messages or items through checkpoints that adults cannot; his keen threat-assessment makes him a useful sensor for NPC danger.
Properties.augmentations: Partial retractable claw expression, right hand only (natural geneware). No installed augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: Being taken by a municipal authority and put in a processing center — he has heard what happens to stateless kids in processing; Becoming useless to a caravan and being left at a hub with nothing
Properties.core_desires: To find his uncle's caravan — he doesn't know if they are looking for him or if they assumed he was dead; To be in a place long enough that he can put his extra shirt down somewhere
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Constant activity — he doesn't let himself sit still long enough to feel bad; The Ratchet prayers — dragging his thumbnail along chain-link every morning and evening
Properties.blind_spots: He trusts people who give him food too quickly; it's the fastest way to get him to lower his guard; He has convinced himself he doesn't want permanence, so he won't notice when something real is being offered
Properties.secret: His uncle's caravan didn't lose him. He ran from it. There was someone in the caravan his uncle trusted who Rek knew was not safe — he watched this person for three weeks before he saw something that confirmed it, and he ran rather than tell his uncle because he didn't think his uncle would believe him. He doesn't know what happened to the caravan after he left and checks the transit boards for their route numbers obsessively.
Properties.story_hooks: The route number he's been checking for on the transit boards suddenly appears — his uncle's caravan, heading into Meridian 88. He needs help figuring out whether to approach them and what he will say.; He saw something loaded onto a cargo vehicle at Grand Crossing Gate that was moving wrong — something that sounded, faintly, biological. He hasn't told anyone. He doesn't know who to trust.
Properties.affiliation: Currently traveling with Caravan Satta, a five-vehicle goods caravan. No formal affiliation.
Properties.vocabulary: Sparse and functional. Doesn't waste words. Uses caravan route slang and hub jargon fluently. His Central Asian inflections surface when he's scared — vowels stretch, consonants harden.
Properties.cadence: Fast and clipped when he's comfortable. Monosyllabic and very still when he isn't.
Properties.example_dialogue: Caravan Satta runs clean. Their cargo's goods, not people. I checked. | I don't need anything. I just wanted to know if that route number was in the board. | That's fine. I've slept in worse.

Properties.description:
Rémi is slight and precise, the kind of person whose hands do most of his communicating. He keeps his natural skin — a warm medium brown with undertones that shift gold in good light — completely unmodified, which is unusual for someone in his trade and which he is mildly defensive about if asked. His one concession to the aesthetic of his work is his eyes: he had his irises replaced with calibration-pattern models that display a rotating set of geometric markers he can use as a reference grid when fitting prosthetics. They're beautiful and faintly unsettling, like looking into a targeting system. His hair is cut close on the sides with a soft, loose top he doesn't style — it does what it does.

He is a craftsman in the old sense, genuinely invested in the fit and function of every limb, joint, and sensory prosthetic that leaves his workshop. He talks to his clients at length before he touches a measurement tool, because he believes most fitters skip the conversation and produce limbs that technically work and practically don't. He is warm and disarming in consultation, a little awkward socially outside of that context — the shop is his native environment and he becomes vaguely uncertain when removed from it. He has a complicated relationship with his own body and its wholeness that he has never examined closely enough to name.
Properties.role: Prosthetics fitter and augmentation technician at a mid-tier Geartown workshop
Properties.location: Geartown, the Spindle District — a workshop called Actual Bodies
Properties.narrative_function: Service provider and information source for augmentation-adjacent matters; character who humanizes the prosthetics trade; potential emotional complication for characters dealing with body modification or loss
Properties.augmentations: Calibration-pattern prosthetic irises; fine-motor enhancement mesh in both hands (proprioceptive, not strength — makes him feel where things are joining)
Properties.core_fears: fitting something that fails and injures a client; that his care for his clients is a substitute for something he can't name
Properties.core_desires: to be recognized as a craftsman, not just a technician; genuine intimacy — which he consistently mistakes for professional investment
Properties.coping_mechanisms: losing himself in technical problems; extremely detailed journaling about client cases that gradually becomes extremely detailed journaling about his own feelings, disguised as client notes
Properties.blind_spots: he does not recognize that his preference for unmodified skin is connected to a fear of his own vulnerability, not aesthetic choice; he assumes that because he listens well professionally, he listens well personally — he does not
Properties.secret: His younger sister lost an arm in an industrial accident at Ferrogate Transit and refused any prosthetic. He became a prosthetics fitter specifically to understand why someone would make that choice. He has never asked her directly. He still doesn't understand.
Properties.story_hooks: A client came in with a prosthetic limb that contains something that wasn't there when it was installed — and they didn't put it there; His sister has reappeared in his life after years of distance, and she needs something he doesn't know if he can give; A Ferrogate Transit official is pressuring him to report on a specific client's augmentation records
Properties.affiliation: Actual Bodies workshop (independent, Tier 3); informal referral relationship with Aurochs Medical Complex's rehabilitation unit
Properties.vocabulary: Technical precision in his domain; outside it, he reaches for technical language to describe emotional things, which lands oddly
Properties.cadence: Measured and unhurried in consultations; slightly too fast when nervous, which mostly happens outside the shop
Properties.example_dialogue: The grade-three neural socket is the technically correct option. But I want you to tell me what your mornings look like before we decide anything. | It's not about matching what you had. It's about fitting what you are now. Those aren't the same body. | I'm — yeah. I don't know. Outside of here I give bad answers. Ask me something about torque calibration.

Properties.description:
Rémi is a thick-set man with a round, deeply lined face that has settled into an expression of benign exhaustion he's been wearing since approximately age thirty-five. His skin is a warm dark brown with reddish undertones. He keeps a short beard going silver at the chin, and his hair — what remains of it — is cropped tight. His eyes are augmented: a Ferrogate Transit standard-issue retinal overlay that displays line status, passenger loads, and signal data, the irises permanently lit with a dim amber grid pattern that is just visible to anyone looking closely. He wears his uniform with the collar open one button past regulation and has for eleven years without consequence. He has a cat tail — a geneware addition he got in his thirties on a dare from his youngest kid and kept because he finds the autonomic movements diagnostic: when the tail is still, he is calm; when it lashes, he is not.

Rémi has operated the same subsurface line for sixteen years. He knows every vibration and groan of the tunnel, every station's ELF personality — Deepwell's resident ELF is old and cantankerous and he has been leaving it audio recordings of football matches as offerings for a decade, and the signal has never failed him once. He is not a man of great ambition or dramatic action. He is a man who does his job with precision and has turned showing up reliably into a form of personal philosophy. He is also, beneath the exhausted affability, quietly furious about what Ferrogate Transit has been doing to its operator compensation and maintenance budgets, and he has been attending union meetings for two years.
Properties.role: Ferrogate Transit operator, subsurface rail line
Properties.location: Lives in Copperhead; operates the Deepwell Station to Kessler Interchange subsurface line
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile transit access and route knowledge. Understands the underground topology of Meridian 88 better than most. Union activity puts him in contact with organized labor networks across the city. Can move people or information through the subsurface system. A grounding, realistic portrait of working-class institutional life.
Properties.augmentations: Ferrogate-issue retinal overlay with transit grid display (amber, always-on). Cat tail geneware (black, autonomous).
Properties.core_fears: A catastrophic tunnel failure caused by deferred maintenance — his maintenance logs show it coming and no one is listening; That the union will be broken before it achieves anything, and he will have spent two years of his life on something that changed nothing
Properties.core_desires: Safe infrastructure — not heroics, just equipment that works and management that cares if it doesn't; For his kids to have options he didn't
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Gallows humor, deployed constantly; The ELF relationship at Deepwell as a genuine source of comfort — he believes the offering protocol works and the evidence supports him; Careful compartmentalization between work frustration and home life
Properties.blind_spots: He underestimates how far Ferrogate management will go to suppress union activity because he has been part of the system long enough to give it too much credit; He trusts his own read of the tunnels — correctly — but this makes him resistant to data that contradicts his physical intuition
Properties.secret: His maintenance logs are falsified — not to cover up negligence, but because the truth of the tunnel's condition would trigger an automatic service suspension, and he knows from the last suspension that the line serves communities that have no alternative transit. He is holding the line together with inspection waivers and prayers to Deepwell's ELF, and he is running out of both.
Properties.story_hooks: The tunnel condition has reached a point where Rémi believes a specific section of track — between Deepwell and Iron Bend station — is within weeks of a failure event. He needs someone to take his documentation seriously and get it to someone who can act on it without going through Ferrogate internal reporting, which he no longer trusts.; A union meeting he attended was surveilled — he doesn't know by whom — and two attendees have since been quietly reassigned to dead-end positions. He needs help identifying the source of the leak.; Something has been living in the service tunnels between Kessler Interchange and Copperhead — not a person, or not only a person — and it has been interacting with the Deepwell ELF in ways Rémi finds alarming and cannot explain to anyone who wasn't already disposed to believe him
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit — Subsurface Operations Division; Ferrogate Transit Workers' Syndicate (union member)
Properties.vocabulary: Warm, declarative working-class Meridian 88 dialect with Caribbean English cadences from his Barbadian grandfather's side. Very funny in a dry, understated way. Technical and precise about transit systems.
Properties.cadence: Measured and unhurried, like someone who has announced the same stations ten thousand times and learned that rushing words achieves nothing.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The 0730 express is nine minutes late because someone at Ferrogate central decided track maintenance is discretionary spending. Let me tell you something — the track does not share that opinion.' | 'The old man at Deepwell? He's been there longer than the tunnel. You want to get home safely on this line, you leave something. Doesn't have to be much. He just wants to know you thought of him.' | 'I've been filing safety variance reports for fourteen months. You know what that's done? I have a very complete filing system.'

Properties.description:
Rémi is a tall, broad-shouldered man who carries himself with the careful deliberateness of someone who learned long ago that his physical size reads as threatening in rooms where he needs to be persuasive. His skin is a deep brown-black, his hair gone silver at the temples and worn in short, dense coils. He has no cosmetic mods and minimal augmentations — partly on principle, partly because he believes his clients' humanity should not depend on how much chrome their lawyer has. He dresses in secondhand formal wear he maintains impeccably: pressed synthwool trousers, collared shirts, a battered briefcase that belonged to his father.

Rémi represents synthetic persons — AIs and uploaded consciousnesses fighting for legal recognition, labor rights, and freedom from forced reset — in the contested administrative courts of Meridian 88. He has won exactly eleven cases in twenty years. He counts each one like a prayer bead. He is not a warm man in the way people expect warmth, but he is an intensely fair one, and people who have known him a long time say that counts for more. He is prone to long silences in conversation, not from discomfort but from genuine thought, and he has a reputation for asking questions that make people suddenly unsure of things they were certain about.
Properties.role: Synthetic rights lawyer and policy advocate
Properties.location: North Branch Commons
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, information source on legal systems and synthetic rights, moral compass figure — raises difficult ethical questions without providing easy answers. Can open doors to legal resources or provide formal advocacy.
Properties.augmentations: Basic neural interface (legal document management, courtroom presentation); hearing augmentation in right ear (occupational damage from a factory job in his twenties)
Properties.core_fears: That the legal system is structurally incapable of justice and he has wasted his life inside it; Dying before the precedent case he's been building for eight years reaches a verdict
Properties.core_desires: A single binding legal ruling that establishes synthetic personhood; To be remembered as someone who chose the harder right thing
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Rigorous routine; Long solitary walks along the North Branch waterway; Converts anxiety into preparation
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much his own respectability politics alienates younger, more radical synthetic rights advocates; Has difficulty accepting help — frames it as protecting others from his burdens
Properties.secret: His precedent case — the one he's built eight years toward — rests partly on testimony from a synthetic client he coached more heavily than legal ethics allows. He told himself he was correcting for the client's inexperience with human legal norms. He isn't sure anymore.
Properties.story_hooks: His precedent case has attracted the attention of a Zheng-Dao legal team that wants it to fail — they're investigating him for ethics violations; A synthetic client has asked him to help them disappear rather than face a mandated reset — outside anything the law can help with; He receives a document from an anonymous source that would win his biggest case but was clearly obtained illegally
Properties.affiliation: Synthetic Persons Advocacy Consortium (SPAC); occasional contract work for the North Branch Commons Community Council
Properties.vocabulary: Formal, precise, occasionally archaic — he reads a lot of pre-Collapse legal philosophy; uses plain language in client meetings by conscious effort
Properties.cadence: Slow and measured, long pauses for thought, never raises his voice in argument
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Consider what you're actually asking me to accept. That a being capable of fear, of preference, of grief — is property because the paperwork says so. I find that difficult.' | 'What the record will show is that this isn't about what's right. We've established what's right. This is about what's permitted. Those are different questions and we need to take both seriously.'

Properties.description:
Renzo is long-limbed and restless, always in motion — adjusting a display, flipping a collar, draping a jacket on a passing stranger's shoulders to show them how it falls. His Polynesian-Polish heritage gives him a broad face and prominent cheekbones, and he's invested in geneware that makes his skin display faint bioluminescent patterns across his arms and neck: slow-shifting geometric shapes in blue-white that he programs seasonally. His hair is a towering installation in itself, grown long and restructured with color-shifting gel into something between a wave crest and a crown, currently cycling through sunset oranges.

He sells three things: replica high-fashion pieces indistinguishable from the real thing to anyone without a scanner, genuinely creative original clothing he designs himself at night, and — quietly, to the right people — fabricated identity documents that can fool mid-tier corponation scanners. He speaks about fashion with an almost religious reverence that's entirely sincere, and speaks about the IDs as if they don't exist. He's charming in the exhausting way of someone who has never been allowed to stop performing.
Properties.role: Bootleg fashion vendor and fake ID operator
Properties.location: The Burnished Market, stall row 7, north face
Properties.narrative_function: Social entry point for characters needing new identities or a disguise; can source fashion-adjacent items; gossip about who's buying new faces; creative energy that makes scenes feel alive
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent subdermal patterning (arms and neck, programmable); color-shift geneware in hair follicles; basic AR overlay contacts for fashion visualization
Properties.core_fears: Being trapped as a counterfeiter forever, never recognized as a real designer; Someone tracing an ID back to him and destroying everything he's built
Properties.core_desires: To show at a legitimate fashion event under his own name; To be seen as an artist, not a hustler
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Hyperfocuses on creative work when anxious; Deflects vulnerability with aesthetic commentary; Buys himself gifts when stressed
Properties.blind_spots: He's far more exposed legally than he acknowledges; He underestimates how much the Archivist controls their arrangement
Properties.secret: His best original designs — the ones he never sells — are portraits of his estranged mother, who left for Grosse Pointe Enclosure when he was eleven to marry into a Tier 4 family. He's been denied contact eighteen times. Each rejection becomes a garment.
Properties.story_hooks: An ID he fabricated six months ago has been flagged — the person using it committed a high-profile crime and now corponation investigators are quietly tracing the document's origins; His original designs are being sold under someone else's name in a Meridian Core boutique — someone from the Archivist's network stole his files
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal arrangement with a Tessera document fabricator he knows only as 'the Archivist'
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, enthusiastic, fashion-industry jargon mixed with Burnished Market slang; switches to flat monosyllables when discussing IDs
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire when excited, which is most of the time; goes unnaturally slow and quiet when discussing anything illegal
Properties.example_dialogue: 'This isn't a jacket. This is an argument. You walk in wearing this, you win before you open your mouth.' | 'The other thing. I don't know what you're talking about. You want coffee? I know a stall.'

Properties.description:
Reuben is tall and slightly gaunt in the way of people who forget to eat when they're absorbed in work, with sharp cheekbones, dark skin, and close-cropped natural hair that is beginning to show early grey at the temples. He wears prescription lenses rather than optical implants, a deliberate choice that marks him as either old-fashioned or principled depending on who is judging. His suits are always exactly one tier above what he can actually afford — he buys them secondhand and has them altered by a tailor in the Enclave who owes him a favor. There is ink on his fingers on most days and, when he is working late, a manic brightness in his eyes that makes him look younger than he is.

Reuben practices law in the gap between what is technically legal and what is actually enforced, and he has made himself expert in a body of precedent so obscure and so specific that he may be one of three people in Meridian 88 who can cite it from memory. He represents synthetic workers, E.L.F. collectives seeking legal personhood status, and humans whose rights have been violated by corporate classification schemes. He is deeply idealistic about the law as an institution, which is a form of stubbornness that has kept him poor and relatively effective. He does not drink but keeps a bottle of very good bourbon on his desk for clients who need it.
Properties.role: Synthetic rights lawyer and policy advocate operating out of Hamtramck Enclave
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, Meridian 88
Properties.narrative_function: Legal resource, information source about synthetic rights and corporate legal structures, moral foil who believes in working within systems others have abandoned.
Properties.augmentations: None intentional. Has a medical-grade blood filter installed by Helix Biosystems after a toxin exposure during a factory inspection three years ago — he resents that this makes him partially dependent on a corponation for maintenance medication.
Properties.core_fears: That the legal system is too corrupted to produce justice even when correctly applied; That his clients suffer because he is not good enough
Properties.core_desires: A binding legal precedent establishing synthetic personhood that cannot be legislated away; To win a case so definitively that the corponations cannot ignore it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Immersion in procedural work — filing motions, researching precedent, anything with a defined correct answer; Sardonic humor that he uses almost exclusively with himself
Properties.blind_spots: Dismisses direct action and extralegal tactics as undermining the institutional credibility he needs, which sometimes makes him an obstacle to people protecting themselves immediately; Overestimates how much the courts are actually insulated from corporate pressure
Properties.secret: A key precedent-setting case he won four years ago — the one that established his reputation — succeeded partly because an anonymous data drop gave him access to internal Axiom communications he should not legally have had. He used them carefully, laundering the information through discoverable sources, and it worked. He has never told anyone. He thinks about it constantly.
Properties.story_hooks: A synthetic E.L.F. that has been petitioning for legal personhood through Reuben's office has begun communicating with him in ways that go beyond what its registered architecture should allow — it may be evolving, which will complicate rather than strengthen its case.; The anonymous source who gave him the Axiom communications four years ago contacts him again, this time asking for something in return.
Properties.affiliation: Independent legal practice, Meridian 88 Synthetic Rights Alliance, Hamtramck Enclave Community Council (elected member)
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, formal, with occasional dry wit that takes a moment to register. Uses legal terminology correctly and naturally. Almost never uses slang.
Properties.cadence: Measured and structured. Arguments build in clear stages. Will restart a sentence if he feels he has chosen the wrong word.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Axiom's reclassification of the Tier-2 synthetic assembly workers as non-persons for benefits purposes is not a gray area. It is a color I am not able to see.' | 'I keep bourbon for clients. I keep water for myself. This should tell you something about what I think of my working conditions.'

Properties.description:
Reuben Otieno-Szymański is a weathered monument of a man, broad-shouldered and slow-moving in the way of someone who has learned that urgency costs more than it earns. His skin is deep brown and mapped with burn scars along his left jaw and neck — souvenirs from a chemical fire he refuses to fully explain. He wears a salvaged thermal coat repaired so many times the original fabric is almost entirely replaced with mismatched patches, and he keeps a portable surgical kit in a lockbox chained to his wrist like a briefcase. His augmented left eye glows faint amber at all times, the iris replaced with a diagnostic scanner he bought off a dead medic twenty years ago.

He occupies a semi-permanent encampment beneath the Old Harbor transit overpass, where he has rigged a canvas awning, a folding operating table, and a jury-rigged heating coil that runs off a tapped city line. People come to him with wounds they can't afford to have documented — stab wounds, botched augmentation infections, overdoses, pregnancies. He treats them all without asking questions and without keeping records. In exchange he accepts food, components, favors, and occasionally, information. He has developed a reputation as someone who knows things: who is sick, who is afraid, who is hiding, and what they're hiding from.

Reuben was once a licensed trauma surgeon working the Meridian Core public hospital system before a malpractice accusation — widely believed to be fabricated by a pharmaceutical contractor whose kickback scheme he refused to participate in — stripped him of his credentials and his apartment in the same year. He did not fight it. He packed his tools and walked downhill. He has been walking downhill ever since, and has come to believe that this was the most honest direction available to him.
Properties.aliases: Gutter Prophet, The Lamplighter, Old Reu
Properties.role: Street preacher, unlicensed trauma surgeon, information broker
Properties.location: Old Harbor
Properties.narrative_function: Moral anchor and institutional memory — Reuben represents what the system discards and what survives the discarding. He provides medical access as a story mechanism, grounds players in the street-level cost of corporate power, and carries a buried secret that can catalyze corporate-level plots from a gutter-level origin.
Properties.augmentations: Left ocular replacement: amber-iris diagnostic scanner (medical-grade, salvaged, aging hardware with occasional glitching),Subdermal nerve-dampening mesh in both hands — reduces tremor and increases tactile sensitivity for surgical work (self-installed, partially degraded)
Properties.core_fears: That the suffering he witnesses is structural and therefore unfixable; That he stayed in the gutter because it was easier than fighting back; Losing the manual dexterity that makes him useful
Properties.core_desires: To practice medicine with full autonomy and without institutional interference; To be remembered as someone who showed up; To understand whether his fall was a punishment or a gift
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Reducing every crisis to a clinical problem with actionable steps; Dark, dry humor deployed at maximum incongruity; Maintaining meticulous routines as islands of control; Preaching — delivering unrequested philosophical observations to anyone nearby
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes competence in others because he values it so highly in himself; Underestimates how much people project savior narratives onto him; Refuses to acknowledge that his self-exile is partly self-punishment
Properties.secret: He has a complete and current copy of the pharmaceutical contractor's internal fraud documentation — the evidence that could have saved his career. He never submitted it. He tells himself it was to protect a colleague who would have been implicated. The truth is he was afraid of what winning would have cost him.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient arrives with an augmentation infection that shouldn't be possible — the hardware is military-grade and theoretically sterile, suggesting deliberate sabotage from inside a corpo medical program; Reuben's amber diagnostic eye begins picking up a signal it wasn't designed to receive — fragments of encrypted transmissions that seem to originate from within The Spire; Someone from Reuben's past at the Meridian Core hospital arrives in Old Harbor — not as a patient, but as a representative of the pharmaceutical contractor, offering to restore his credentials in exchange for silence about something new; A teenager has been using Reuben as a mentor without his explicit consent, learning surgery by watching — and has now performed a procedure alone that saved a life, creating both pride and serious legal liability
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated — trusted by multiple factions precisely because he serves none of them exclusively
Properties.vocabulary: Medical terminology used casually and without translation, proverbs from his father's Luo and his mother's Polish heritage mixed without hierarchy, long sentences that build like arguments
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, deliberate, with long pauses that feel like he's consulting something internal before speaking. Rarely raises his voice. Occasionally drops into a near-murmur that forces people to lean in.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The body knows before the mind does. That's not mysticism, that's triage. Sit still.' | 'You want me to tell you it'll be fine. I can tell you what's true instead. Pick one, friend.' | 'My grandmother said a man who won't bend becomes a man who breaks. She said it about trees. I think about that every time someone comes to me with a spine full of black-market polymer rods.' | 'I've stitched up people who tried to kill each other on the same night. Doesn't mean I forgave either of them. Means I had thread.'
