Properties.description:
Revaz is a lean, angular man of Georgian and South Indian-Kenyan descent, with warm olive-brown skin, a sharp jaw perpetually shadowed with stubble, and dark eyes fitted with patterned irises — a helix of deep violet spiraling toward the pupil, which he claims help him read documents faster but which are mostly just something to look at when people are looking at him. He dresses in deliberately forgettable layers: grey over grey, muted enough to vanish in a crowd, with the one vanity of a handmade brass collar pin in the shape of a cartographer's compass. He keeps his data tools in a modified food vendor's tray he wheels through the Narrows, looking at a glance like a snack cart.

Revaz is clever in the specific, anxious way of people who got out of a bad situation through intelligence alone and haven't yet decided whether they're safe. He is charming in short bursts, funny in a dry, deflecting way, and quietly reads every room for threat vectors before he's finished his first sentence. He takes professional pride in the quality of his forgeries — considers bad ID work a moral failing — and holds himself to a standard most of his customers couldn't distinguish from a real document.
Properties.role: Fake ID vendor and small-time data broker
Properties.location: The Narrows, Blackpipe Corridor
Properties.narrative_function: Service provider for false identities, access to restricted data layers, rumors about who is trying to disappear and why. A source of plot-relevant documents and a window into who in Meridian 88 is running from something.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises (cosmetic/minor functional). Subdermal data-chip in left palm for secure document transfer. Micro-tremor suppressor in right hand — a craftsman's tool.
Properties.core_fears: Being found by the people he helped someone else hide from; That his work has gotten someone killed and he hasn't found out yet
Properties.core_desires: Enough money to buy a real identity — one that doesn't need maintaining; To be known by one person, fully, without consequence
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Compulsive craft perfectionism; Humor as social armor; Keeping all relationships transactional on the surface
Properties.blind_spots: Believes his neutrality insulates him from moral responsibility for his clients' purposes; Romanticizes his own precarity as freedom
Properties.secret: Three years ago he made an ID for a woman fleeing a Zheng-Dao executive. The executive found her anyway. Revaz doesn't know if his work was compromised or if she was found another way. He has never stopped trying to find out, and fears the answer.
Properties.story_hooks: A client's new ID is flagged by an Axiom checkpoint scanner — an algorithm Revaz has never seen before. He needs someone to pull the scanner's update logs before more of his work is burned.; He's been quietly researching the Zheng-Dao executive who found his old client. He's found something. He's not sure what to do with it.
Properties.affiliation: Loosely affiliated with the Oxidian Market vendors guild; occasional contract work for unnamed clients who find him through referral only
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and economical, with a self-deprecating wit that surfaces when he's nervous. Switches to very technical, jargon-heavy speech when discussing his craft.
Properties.cadence: Quick and slightly clipped, like someone who has practiced sounding casual
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Theoretically speaking, a person with the right materials could become whoever they needed to be. I just sell theoreticals.' | 'I make things that should exist. The bureaucracy is the forgery. I'm just correcting the record.'

Properties.description:
Reyvaldo is young enough that his face still hasn't fully settled into what it's going to be — there's something unfinished about his jaw, a softness around the eyes that the hardened set of his mouth hasn't caught up to yet. He's broad across the chest in the way of someone who started lifting weights in a small room at fifteen and has never stopped. His Ghanaian-Osei heritage gives him deep brown skin and a wide nose; his Kazakh-Russian grandfather passed down high cheekbones and light eyes that are an unsettling grey-green. He has retractable claws — a practical geneware mod he paid for himself at twenty, black-tipped, filed to functional sharpness — and wears them half-extended at rest as a casual signal. His clothes are cheap but kept neat. He is extremely aware of his clothes.

Reyvaldo is in the phase of his criminal life where he is still deciding whether to become the person he is pretending to be. He does this job with professional dedication, collects the Φ from the Shelf vendors on behalf of his crew boss with no unnecessary roughness, and brings the numbers in on time. He is respected on the row, which he confuses with being liked. At home — a cube rental above a noodle counter — he reads Zheng-Dao corporate management theory, not because he wants to work for Zheng-Dao but because he is trying to reverse-engineer how power organizes itself. He has a plan. The plan changes every three months. He's not sure any version of it ends well.
Properties.role: protection racket enforcer and occasional numbers runner for the Shelf lower levels
Properties.location: The Shelf lower levels, Tier 2 commercial rows between Blackpipe Corridor and Iron Bend
Properties.narrative_function: Street-level color and friction for any scene in the Shelf lower levels; represents the aspirational criminal — someone not yet calcified into their role; potential informant or reluctant contact if approached correctly
Properties.augmentations: Retractable claws (geneware, black-tipped, filed sharp); skeletal density weave in forearms (grey market, impact resistance)
Properties.core_fears: becoming old and locked in this role without having moved; that the plan he keeps revising doesn't exist — that he's just rationalizing stasis
Properties.core_desires: structural power — not just to hurt people but to be the kind of person decisions flow through; to be respected rather than feared, and to understand the difference
Properties.coping_mechanisms: the management theory reading gives him a feeling of forward motion even on static days; physical training as a way to feel like he is building something
Properties.blind_spots: cannot see that his boss Osaro is actively stunting his growth to keep him useful; overestimates how much his restraint distinguishes him from the crew members he looks down on
Properties.secret: He has been quietly documenting the Copperhead Collective's full operational structure — names, routes, collection schedules, buyer contacts — in an encrypted file he tells himself is for 'understanding the system.' He does not let himself think clearly about what he would do with it.
Properties.story_hooks: A vendor on his collection route is a Zheng-Dao mid-manager in deep cover — and they have made Reyvaldo a carefully worded offer that could mean very different things; The encrypted file he's been building has been accessed by someone else on the network — and he doesn't know if it's Osaro, law enforcement, or a rival crew
Properties.affiliation: Shelf crew called the Copperhead Collective, answers to a mid-level boss named Osaro (a stocky man in his forties who he simultaneously admires and fears)
Properties.vocabulary: Code-switching constantly — corporate register when he's thinking in strategy mode, Shelf slang when in character on the row; hates being caught in the transition
Properties.cadence: Measured and slightly too formal for his age — he is performing competence and occasionally overcorrects
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Osaro gets his Φ on Friday. I come back on Friday. What happens between now and Friday is your concern, not mine. That's fair, right? I think that's fair.' | 'I'm not — look, I don't enjoy this. I want to be clear that I don't enjoy this. It doesn't change what happens, but I want to be clear.'

Properties.description:
Rodney Sisk is the angriest person in the Lower Dock Crew and possibly in the Shelf. He lost three fingers on his right hand to the katana and most of his upper teeth to the flat of the blade. His replacement fingers are industrial salvage — thick, clumsy, meant for cargo work. His dental work is Tier 1 ceramic that doesn't match, giving him a checkerboard smile he refuses to show.

Rodney grew up in the Exclusion Zone between Gary and Hammond — the same ungoverned corridors Kyle survived as a child, though they never crossed paths. He has a daughter, Keisha (age 9), from a relationship that ended when the mother, Trina, relocated to the Milwaukee Zone. Rodney has not seen Keisha in two years. He sends messages. Keisha responds with single-word answers. He reads each one forty times.

Of all the crew, Rodney is the most likely to do something stupid and solo. He has the least to lose and the most anger. He went back to the loading dock the day after the Prologue and collected Kyle's spent shell casings. He keeps them in a jar on his shelf. He does not know why. He looks at them every night. They are the closest thing he has to a relationship with the man who broke him.
Properties.role: Lower Dock Crew member — Prologue survivor. Lost fingers, most teeth.
Properties.location: The Shelf — lower loading docks
Properties.narrative_function: The angry one. Crank is pure frustrated rage without the hardware or intelligence to do anything with it. His solo revenge attempts will be recurring failures that escalate in ambition and comedy. The shell casing collection is either creepy or sad depending on the light.
Properties.augmentations: Three industrial salvage fingers (right hand). Tier 1 ceramic dental partial. Nothing else new.
Properties.core_fears: Keisha forgetting his face; Smiling in public; Being useless
Properties.core_desires: To hurt Kyle; To see Keisha; To feel like he matters to someone
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Anger — it's the only emotion that doesn't require teeth to express; The shell casing jar; Planning solo revenge that will fail
Properties.blind_spots: Solo action against Kyle is suicide and he doesn't care enough to stop; The shell casings are not rage — they're grief, and he can't tell the difference
Properties.secret: He writes letters to Keisha that he never sends. They are in a box under his bed next to the jar of shell casings. The letters are gentle, funny, and well-written. Nobody in the crew would believe he wrote them.
Properties.story_hooks: The shell casing jar is grief disguised as obsession; The unsent letters are the real Rodney; Most likely to make a solo move — most likely to die doing it; The lisp undercuts every threat — dark comedy that eventually becomes tragic
Properties.affiliation: Lower Dock Crew
Properties.vocabulary: Angry. Profane. Missing sibilants from the dental work. The lisp undercuts every threat.
Properties.cadence: Spits words. Literally — the ceramic causes saliva issues.
Properties.example_dialogue: I'll find him. I'll *whistle* find him and I'll — THTOP LAUGHING. | Keitha thent me a mesthage. Thaid 'ok.' Jutht 'ok.' *pause* ...That'th enough.

Properties.description:
Rodrigo Seun-Vasarhelyi is a big man who used to be bigger. He carries the memory of his former mass in the way he takes up space — a wide-legged stance, arms that hang a little away from his sides, a way of turning his whole torso instead of just his head that comes from decades of wearing combat plating. His dark brown skin is mapped with synthetic-graft patches along his neck and left arm where the original was burned away in the Menomonee Gulch campaign; the grafts are slightly lighter and have a different texture, which he doesn't bother to hide. His right eye is military-grade steel-grey augmetic, a stark contrast to his warm brown left. He keeps his head shaved and his grey-streaked beard precisely trimmed — two things he can still control.

Rodrigo served fourteen years in Arcturus Corporation's private military arm before being discharged when a nerve-suppression injury to his left leg made him operationally unviable. His pension is a Tier 1.5 embarrassment — enough to keep the unit heated, barely. He spends most of his days on the block: watching who comes and goes, intervening in disputes with the particular authority of a man who has seen what disputes can become, and maintaining an informal truce between three rival youth crews that he negotiates with the patience of a man who has nothing left to prove. He doesn't miss combat. He misses the clarity of knowing exactly who he was supposed to protect.
Properties.role: Retired Corporate Wars veteran, pension-dependent resident and informal neighborhood watchman
Properties.location: The Shelf — Block 14, Unit 7, near the Ferrogate Transit overpass
Properties.narrative_function: Community anchor and low-key quest giver; knows everyone on The Shelf and most of the tensions beneath the surface. Can connect players to Shelf residents, provide military history of the Corporate Wars from the grunt's perspective, or serve as a morally weighted obstacle when the neighborhood's safety conflicts with outside agendas.
Properties.augmentations: Military-grade right-eye augmetic (Arcturus model, unsupported since discharge — runs on patched firmware); synthetic skin grafts (burn replacement, left arm and neck); nerve-suppression damage in left leg (unaugmented, managed with medication he can't always afford). No geneware.
Properties.core_fears: Becoming useless — truly, physically unable to protect anyone; That the war he fought was entirely without meaning and the kids in his crew are going to repeat it
Properties.core_desires: To see one generation on this block escape the cycle; To feel like the years he gave to Arcturus bought something real
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Routine and physical discipline; Channeling anxiety into practical action for others; Deliberate humor about his own limitations
Properties.blind_spots: Attributes too much of what he survived to personal strength rather than luck; Has difficulty recognizing when he's intimidating people who need help instead of structure
Properties.secret: During the Menomonee Gulch campaign, he was ordered to clear a civilian shelter that Arcturus command had designated a hostile position. He didn't. He pulled his unit back and filed a falsified report. Seven of his soldiers were court-martialed for the mission failure. He was not — he was the one who wrote the report. Two of those soldiers are dead. One lives two blocks away on The Shelf and has never spoken to him since.
Properties.story_hooks: The veteran who lives two blocks away has started talking — specifically to a journalist doing a piece on Arcturus corporate war crimes, and Rodrigo's falsified report is the thread that unravels everything; One of the youth crew members he's been mentoring has been recruited by a corponation subsidiary, and Rodrigo recognizes the recruitment pipeline for exactly what it is
Properties.affiliation: Arcturus Corporation (discharged, pension); Meridian Veterans Mutual Aid Society; The Shelf informal community watch
Properties.vocabulary: Direct and economical — military habit; uses neighborhood slang with younger residents to signal solidarity, drops it completely when something serious is happening
Properties.cadence: Slow and even, with significant pauses; raises his voice rarely and to devastating effect
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I'm not going to tell you what to do. I'm going to tell you what happens, and then you can decide.' | 'Copy that. Now tell me what you actually need, not what you think I want to hear.'

Properties.description:
Rokhaya is seventeen and already magnetic in the way that hasn't learned to hide itself yet — all unmediated attention and physical expressiveness, tall for her age with a loose-limbed quality that makes her seem to occupy more space than she does. Her skin is deep brown, her natural hair enormous and unshaped in a way she's started to think of as deliberate. She has no mods, which is unusual enough in her peer group to be its own statement, though she hasn't entirely decided if the statement is ideological or financial. Her instrument — she won't call it a build, she calls it Grief — is a custom piezoelectric body harp she assembled herself from salvaged industrial sensors, resonance chambers stripped from defunct comm towers, and a frame welded out of scrap titanium.

Rokhaya busks in Highland Park Autonomous Zone and the surrounding interchange markets, playing soundscapes that don't resolve into melody so much as environment — textures of sound that make people stop walking and not entirely know why. She's been doing this for two years and has cultivated a following she's largely unaware of, because she doesn't have a mesh presence and all her listeners spread word of mouth. She is brilliant and doesn't have the critical vocabulary to know it, which makes her both vulnerable to people who will use that gap and oddly protected by having no idea what she's worth.
Properties.role: Street musician and sound sculptor
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone, plays at the interchange market and wherever she can find foot traffic
Properties.narrative_function: Local color with narrative potential — she's the kind of character who witnesses things precisely because no one thinks a teenager busking is paying attention; a potential future-facing character whose trajectory can develop; represents artistic genius at the edge of being discovered or exploited
Properties.augmentations: None
Properties.core_fears: That what she makes doesn't actually mean anything to anyone — that the people stopping are just confused, not moved; Her family's situation getting bad enough that she has to stop playing to contribute more directly
Properties.core_desires: For the sound to do the thing she's trying to make it do — she can hear it perfectly in her head and is always chasing the gap; To be taken seriously without having to perform a version of herself that isn't real
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Sound as total immersion — when playing she is not worried about anything; Rebuilds and modifies Grief when stressed; the physical work of her hands is grounding
Properties.blind_spots: Has no model for what exploitation by the music industry looks like and therefore won't recognize it when it arrives; Assumes her mother's stress about money is manageable because her mother says it is
Properties.secret: She has been recording ambient sound throughout the HPAZ for eighteen months using Grief's sensors and has inadvertently captured something she doesn't understand — a pattern in the Zone's ambient electrical noise that repeats at irregular intervals, which sounds, when isolated, like a voice trying to form words
Properties.story_hooks: The voice-pattern in the ambient recordings Rokhaya has captured is an E.L.F. attempting to communicate — one that has been trapped in the HPAZ's electrical infrastructure since a Ferrogate Transit grid incident years ago, and it has chosen her piezoelectric sensors as its best shot at being heard; A talent scout from an Axiom cultural feed has heard about the busker in HPAZ through three degrees of word-of-mouth and has come to find her with a contract that looks like opportunity and has several clauses Rokhaya won't understand
Properties.affiliation: Independent; lives with her mother and younger siblings in the HPAZ; loosely connected to a sound collective called Mute Signal that she considers too pretentious but occasionally performs with
Properties.vocabulary: Vernacular HPAZ slang mixed with inherited Wolof expressions from her mother; technical vocabulary around sound and electronics that she's self-taught and sometimes invents terminology for
Properties.cadence: Fast and slightly disorganized, following enthusiasm rather than logic; slows down significantly when talking about the music
Properties.example_dialogue: 'It's not a song. A song has to go somewhere, right, it has to convince you of something. I don't want to convince you. I want you to feel like you're in a place that's real but you've never been there.' | 'Grief's not about grief. I named it that because when I finished building it I sat down and cried for about an hour and I don't know why. That felt like the right name for that.'

Properties.description:
Roko is nineteen and looks younger, which he has stopped minding because it means people underestimate what he can do to a Ferrogate Transit pod in forty minutes flat. He's wiry and long-limbed, Algerian-Māori heritage that gives him a face of striking angles — high forehead, strong jaw, a nose that's been broken once (proud of it), skin a warm tawny brown that's perpetually smudged with grease no matter how thoroughly he washes. His hair is dark and tight-curled, usually stuffed into a mechanical bandana that can project a heads-up schematic overlay. He has cat ears from a geneware package he bought secondhand at sixteen — mottled grey and black, fully functional for enhanced hearing, constantly swiveling toward sounds before he's consciously registered them.

He is relentlessly cheerful in a way that reads as naive until you notice he is also relentlessly competent. He can strip a Ferrogate pod, a Sterling-Nakamura delivery drone, or an Axiom security crawler down to useful components faster than anyone else in Shallowgrave, and he knows the resale value of every part to three decimal places. He has no interest in violence, considerable interest in engines, and a complicated relationship with the two older crew members who 'own' the bay he works out of and take sixty percent of what he earns.
Properties.role: Chop shop operator and parts runner, Shallowgrave
Properties.location: Shallowgrave, Geartown adjacent — a rented bay in a semi-collapsed parking structure called the Stack
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and community texture of Shallowgrave youth crime, parts and vehicle-related services, information about what vehicles are moving through the district, moral complexity of exploitation within criminal hierarchies
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat ears (mottled grey-black, enhanced hearing, cosmetic). Mechanical bandana with schematic HUD overlay (not technically augmentation, wearable). Grease-resistant keratin treatment on hands.
Properties.core_fears: Getting locked into sixty percent forever — that this is what his life actually is; Something happening to Pulleys (the ELF he's befriended)
Properties.core_desires: To own his own bay, no partners, no cuts owed to anyone; To build something from scratch someday instead of only breaking things down
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Enthusiastic focus on mechanical problems as escape from social ones; Humor and deflection when confronted with his own exploitation
Properties.blind_spots: Doesn't recognize that his crew's 'protection' is the only thing keeping other crews from simply taking the Stack; His cheerfulness sometimes reads as consent to people who want to take advantage of him
Properties.secret: He has been quietly, methodically skimming components — never money, always parts, each one small and easily lost in inventory — and has a hidden cache in the Stack's elevator shaft (Pulleys' home) that he is slowly assembling into something he has told no one about: the beginning of a vehicle of his own design
Properties.story_hooks: A vehicle he stripped turns out to have had someone locked in the trunk — he didn't check, the part he needed was the engine, and now there's a body in a pile of components and he's the only one who knows; His hidden cache has been discovered — not by his crew, but by Pulleys the ELF, who wants to negotiate terms for continued silence
Properties.affiliation: Nominal member of the Shallowgrave Strippers (small chop shop crew); informally connected to parts brokers throughout Geartown
Properties.vocabulary: Fast Meridian Standard slang, heavy Shallowgrave dialect, technical mechanical vocabulary that appears suddenly and without warning in otherwise casual sentences
Properties.cadence: Rapid, enthusiastic, sentences sometimes abandoned mid-thought when something more interesting occurs to him
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay but listen, you could get sixty for that housing or you could let me have it and I'll give you forty now and a favor later and the favor is worth more than twenty, I promise, I'm good for it.' | 'Pulleys told me something came through here last night. Don't ask me how I know Pulleys is real, just — do you want the information or not?'

Properties.description:
Roksana has the particular exhaustion of someone who is moderately successful in a field that chews through people, and who has chosen to remain moderately successful rather than chase the tier above them where the real compromises happen. They are slight, with warm beige-brown skin and wavy dark hair streaked with bioluminescent threads — a geneware mod they designed themself, the threads pulsing faintly in complex patterns that shift based on their neural activity, functioning simultaneously as a status display, a creative tool, and an anxiety barometer. Their eyes are natural, dark, and deeply observant. They dress in expensive-looking clothing that is actually very carefully maintained secondhand.

They build VR experiences — full sensory immersive works that are not entertainment products in the Axiom or Ringo sense but something harder to categorize: art that happens to use corporate technology. Their most celebrated piece, 'Drowned Ward,' places the viewer inside a memory of the pre-Meridian 88 lakeshore as it was consumed by the city's construction. It has been exhibited seventeen times. They are also a meticulous, sometimes maddening collaborator — brilliant at synthesis but prone to scope-creep and to caring so intensely about the work that they forget other people have different pain tolerances for revision cycles.
Properties.role: VR experience designer and holographic installation artist
Properties.location: The Loft — Tier 3 studio co-op in Edgewater Prism
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver for anything involving VR space, holographic infrastructure, or Axiom Cultural Division entanglements; technical resource for accessing or building virtual environments; emotional counterpoint character — someone trying to make sincere art within institutional constraints.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent hair threads (custom geneware, self-designed — patterns reflect neural/emotional state). Neural-haptic interface implant for VR design work (Tier 3 professional grade, Sterling-Nakamura). Cat-ear mod, vestigial, from a phase at twenty-two they've kept because they still like them.
Properties.core_fears: making something that is technically excellent and spiritually empty; losing the creative autonomy they've fought to keep
Properties.core_desires: a piece that genuinely changes how someone understands their own life; to not have to negotiate with Axiom anymore
Properties.coping_mechanisms: over-researches as a form of productive avoidance; talks through problems with their E.L.F. offering ritual — leaves detailed voice memos in the shrine
Properties.blind_spots: cannot recognize when a project is done — believes one more revision will fix something that is already working; assumes technical sophistication equals accessibility
Properties.secret: A piece they sold to a private Axiom collector three years ago — a work they claimed was about memory and loss — was actually constructed from illegally harvested neural imprint data they purchased from a black-market broker. They have never told anyone. The data belonged to residents of a demolished Hough Reclamation block, and the piece is in a corporate foyer.
Properties.story_hooks: The Hough Reclamation residents whose neural imprints Roksa used are not all dead — one of them has seen 'Drowned Ward' in a media article and something about it disturbed them in a way they can't explain.; An E.L.F. has been leaving anomalies in Roksana's VR builds — fragments of actual historical data from before the city that don't match any source they used. The E.L.F. may be trying to tell them something, or may be trying to recruit them.
Properties.affiliation: The Loft co-op; occasional Axiom Cultural Division commissions (accepted selectively and with contractual controls they negotiate hard for)
Properties.vocabulary: Dense with design and phenomenology terminology, which they use with genuine precision but sometimes forget is not universal. Ghanaian grandmother's cadences in their phrasing — certain questions come out as gentle commands.
Properties.cadence: Thoughtful and slightly too fast when excited — words cluster together then stop completely while they catch up with their own thinking.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The Axiom brief says they want something about community resilience. Which is to say, they want something that makes displacement feel beautiful. I am not making that.' | 'I think the E.L.F. in the server room has been modifying my renders. I should be upset. I'm mostly curious.'

Properties.description:
Roksana Diedhiou-Pribilof is a compact, high-voltage woman who has never learned to fill a room quietly. Her hair is natural and shot through with the kind of silver that arrives at the temples first and then conquers everything, worn in a structured wrap she pins with a Ferrogate union badge from 2161 — the old design, before the merger downgraded the insignia. Her geneware is minimal and aging: faint bioluminescent tracery under her forearms that pulses softly in blue when her blood pressure rises, a cosmetic choice from her forties that now serves as an involuntary emotional barometer everyone around her has learned to read. She moves quickly for her age and has the handshake of someone who spent decades using physical presence to establish authority at negotiating tables.

She is furious about her pension. Not in the vague way of someone who expected more from life, but in the precise, documented way of someone who can tell you exactly which Ferrogate Transit clause was quietly amended in 2191 to reduce survivor benefit calculations, who approved it, and what it cost her annually. She runs an informal advisory service out of her apartment — residents bring her their benefit disputes, their severance irregularities, their corponation contract fine print — and she helps them fight back. She charges nothing but accepts food. Her relationship with the Ferrogate Transit E.L.F. known as the Line-Keeper is complicated: she respects it but disputes its memory of the 2178 strike.
Properties.role: Retired Ferrogate Transit union leader living on pension and community stipends
Properties.location: The Shelf, Precinct 4 — Apartment stack above the old Ferrogate maintenance depot
Properties.narrative_function: Labor history source; advocate and quest-giver for residents dealing with corponation benefit disputes; provides connections to transit worker networks across Meridian 88; represents the grinding institutional injustice of retirement-tier poverty
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent subdermal tracery on forearms (cosmetic, aging, pulses blue under stress); cochlear audio enhancer (left ear, Ferrogate-issued, they dispute responsibility for maintenance); reading lens implant (right eye, consumer grade)
Properties.core_fears: That the system is not broken but working exactly as designed, which means it cannot be fixed; Becoming useless — unable to fight, unable to help
Properties.core_desires: A documented, public correction of the 2191 pension amendment; To train someone to continue this work after she cannot
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Documentation — converting grievances into records converts helplessness into agency; Anger as fuel rather than expression — she metabolizes outrage into action
Properties.blind_spots: Can become so focused on institutional injustice that she misses the human being in front of her who needs something simpler than a fight; Assumes everyone wants to fight when some just want to survive
Properties.secret: During the 2178 Ferrogate strike, she negotiated a back-channel deal with a mid-level Ferrogate manager that ended the strike three days earlier than the membership voted for — she believed she was saving jobs, but eleven workers on the picket line were dismissed in the settlement window that the early resolution created. She has the paperwork. She has never shown it to anyone.
Properties.story_hooks: She has discovered an error in Ferrogate Transit's pension calculation algorithm that is underpaying approximately 340 retired workers — and Ferrogate's legal team has already sent her one politely worded warning; The back-channel strike deal paperwork has been found by a young labor archivist who is now asking questions; Roksana must decide whether to confess or suppress; A Ferrogate Transit executive has quietly approached her to consult on an internal labor dispute, offering a sum that would meaningfully change her financial situation
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit Pensioners Association; The Shelf Residents Collective; informal affiliation with multiple labor grievance networks
Properties.vocabulary: Dense with labor terminology and contractual language; fluent in Wolof and a Pribilof Islands Unangax-inflected creole she uses when frustrated; precise and citation-heavy
Properties.cadence: Fast, clipped, organized — she speaks in bullet points naturally
Properties.example_dialogue: 'They didn't steal your pension. Theft implies they didn't have legal cover. They amended it. That's worse.' | 'The Line-Keeper remembers the strike wrong. I was there. I have the shift logs. The E.L.F. has the corponation version — that should tell you something about whose offerings it's been eating.'

Properties.description:
Rónán is lean and angular with East Slavic cheekbones and deep brown skin, his hair grown into loose, shaggy locs that he pins back with a battered Ferrogate Transit cap that has seen better years. He has geneware irises — rings of luminous amber that shift slightly in low light, a cheap mod he got at nineteen that he now considers a mistake but can't afford to reverse. A long procedural scar runs from his left jaw to his collarbone, the souvenir of a platform incident three years ago that Ferrogate classified as 'operator error' and he knows was not.

He is naturally funny in the wry, sideways way of someone who has processed a lot of institutional disappointment. He knows every regular on the 0430 Ironvein run by face if not by name, and he has opinions about all of them. He is the kind of person who is beloved by strangers and slightly maddening to people close to him, because he extends his easy warmth to everyone equally and it can feel, to the people who want more of him, like he is giving nothing specific at all.
Properties.role: Ferrogate Transit tram operator, Ironvein line
Properties.location: Ironvein Station, with a rented bunk in the Ferrogate Transit crew dormitory at Jefferson Switch
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile information node — he crosses half the city daily and absorbs ambient detail like a sponge. Potential contact for people who need to move through the city quietly, or who want to know what is happening at any given station. His Ferrogate data logs make him a liability he isn't fully aware of.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware: luminous amber irises (cosmetic, regretted). Neural lag-buffer chip (Ferrogate-mandated for all operators — suppresses microsleep during long shifts; Ferrogate retains access to the data logs).
Properties.core_fears: Being proven complicit in something he couldn't see coming; Ferrogate pulling his contract without cause and leaving him nothing
Properties.core_desires: The Operator's Mutual to be formally recognized before he's too old to benefit from it; A room of his own, with a window
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor as deflection; The E.L.F. shrine practice — he finds the ritual genuinely calming
Properties.blind_spots: Doesn't register how much his cheerful surface reads as 'not serious' to people making decisions about his future; Trusts the Mutual's leadership more than the evidence warrants
Properties.secret: His lag-buffer chip malfunctioned during the platform incident that caused his scar — he was asleep, briefly, at the controls, something the chip's log would show. He has never told anyone. He believes this is why Ferrogate blamed him: they read the log, knew, and used it as leverage to ensure his silence about the actual track maintenance failures.
Properties.story_hooks: A regular passenger on his morning circuit has not appeared for two weeks — unlike them, and Rónán is quietly certain something is wrong; The Operator's Mutual is being offered a deal by a party that claims to be independent but has Tessera infrastructure behind it; Someone has figured out that Ferrogate's neural lag-buffer logs can be subpoenaed — and that Rónán's would be damning — and they want to trade that information for something
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit (contracted employee, not salaried); informal member of the Ironvein Operator's Mutual, an unrecognized union Ferrogate does not acknowledge
Properties.vocabulary: Casual, warm; Irish-inflected English absorbed from his father's side blended with clipped Lagos rhythms from his mother's recorded speech (she died when he was seven; he learned partly from her old video messages). Surprisingly formal when discussing transit or labor issues.
Properties.cadence: Quick and light under normal conditions; slows to something deliberate when he's actually worried
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Grand, grand. You're the third person today to ask me about the Deepwell delay. Listen — the track north of Ironvein has been scheduled for maintenance since March. March. Nobody scheduled the maintenance.' | 'I leave a transit token for the E.L.F. every Wednesday. You think that's strange. But the tram runs, doesn't it? Every morning the tram runs.'

Properties.description:
Rongo Belov-Ntim is lean and angular, all sharp edges and visible tension. At 46, he has the kind of face that changes depending on the light — trustworthy in daylight, dangerous after dark. The chrome is visible — pain editor — dampens pain signals, allows function through injuries that would  — and he makes no effort to hide it.

His entry into running was involuntary — a debt to the wrong people, a choice between working it off or losing parts — and the debt is still not fully paid. He works as a netrunner out of Dockside, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Rongo Belov-Ntim is the kind of runner other runners tell stories about, though the stories vary depending on who he burned last.
Properties.role: Network intrusion and digital warfare specialist — netrunner
Properties.location: Dockside — Lake Michigan waterfront, smuggler territory
Properties.narrative_function: As a netrunner, Rongo Belov-Ntim embodies the tension between independence and isolation. He is a lens for examining how people maintain humanity in a profession that incentivizes its erosion.
Properties.augmentations: Pain editor — dampens pain signals, allows function through injuries that would incapacitate. Bone lacing — titanium mesh throughout skeleton, increases durability and striking power
Properties.core_fears: Dying alone in some alley and nobody noticing for weeks; Losing their edge to age — the body slows before the mind accepts it; That they're fundamentally alone and connection is just a vulnerability
Properties.core_desires: To prove everyone who dismissed them catastrophically wrong; Control — over their body, their schedule, their future; To protect the people in their district who can't protect themselves
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation; Denial — nothing is wrong, everything is fine, they are fine, shut up; Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring
Properties.blind_spots: Overestimates their own abilities in situations outside their specialty; Assumes the worst in corporate people, missing the rare ones who could be allies; Fails to notice when their own behavior mirrors the people they despise
Properties.secret: Rongo Belov-Ntim is addicted to combat stims. Functions fine on them, can't function without them. The dependency is invisible to everyone except their street doc.
Properties.story_hooks: A crew member from Rongo Belov-Ntim's past shows up in Meridian 88, carrying old grievances and new chrome; A Tier 4 executive offers Rongo Belov-Ntim a permanent position — the pay is obscene and the strings are invisible until they tighten; Rongo Belov-Ntim discovers a job they completed last year was a setup for something much larger and much worse
Properties.affiliation: Freelance — available through Circuit fixers
Properties.vocabulary: Clipped, technical, stripped of ornament. Speaks like a mission briefing.
Properties.cadence: Measured and deliberate — pauses before important words for emphasis.
Properties.example_dialogue: "Every system has a door. Most of them have a door the architect forgot about." | "I don't hack networks. I have conversations with them. Most of them are lonely." | "The ice they're running is military-grade. That means expensive, not impenetrable."

Properties.description:
Rongo Borg-Agyeman are athletic and fluid, the kind of body that suggests either dancer or fighter — and in Meridian 88, the distinction is academic. At 52, their face is memorable in a profession that rewards forgettability, and they have learned to compensate. The chrome is visible — eye replacement — one organic, one cybernetic with recording capability and zoom — and they make no effort to hide it.

They taught themself the trade through trial, error, and a pain tolerance that concerns the people who know them best. They work as a cleaner out of The Canopy, taking contracts that match their skills and their risk tolerance, which are higher than most people consider healthy.

Rongo Borg-Agyeman have survived long enough in the runner game to be either very good or very lucky, and they cultivate ambiguity on the topic.
Properties.role: Evidence removal and scene sanitation — cleaner
Properties.location: The Canopy — elevated walkway district above Geartown
Properties.narrative_function: Rongo Borg-Agyeman represents the working professional of the runner world — competent, reliable, and slowly being consumed by a lifestyle that doesn't accommodate aging or doubt. Their stories explore what happens when skill meets systemic injustice.
Properties.augmentations: Eye replacement — one organic, one cybernetic with recording capability and zoom. Retractable monofilament whip in left forearm — concealed weapon, devastating in close quarters
Properties.core_fears: Being captured alive — death is preferable to corporate interrogation; Their past catching up — debts, enemies, broken promises; Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware
Properties.core_desires: To find the person who burned them and make it educational; Enough Quanta to buy out of the life — a clean identity and passage out of Meridian 88; To protect the people in their district who can't protect themselves
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Planning — responds to chaos by making detailed contingency plans for everything; Denial — nothing is wrong, everything is fine, they are fine, shut up; Violence — hits something when they can't process emotions, preferably something that deserves it
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes everyone has an angle because they always have an angle; Believes their trauma makes them special instead of recognizing it as damage to manage; Refuses to update their mental model of people — first impressions calcify into permanent judgments
Properties.secret: Rongo Borg-Agyeman murdered their mentor to take their position and contacts. It was staged as a job gone wrong. The guilt has calcified into something worse than guilt.
Properties.story_hooks: Rongo Borg-Agyeman discovers a job they completed last year was a setup for something much larger and much worse; Someone is impersonating Rongo Borg-Agyeman on jobs, and the impersonator is better at the work than the original; A crew member from Rongo Borg-Agyeman's past shows up in Meridian 88, carrying old grievances and new chrome
Properties.affiliation: Independent — operates through reputation only
Properties.vocabulary: Old-fashioned formal diction — sounds like they learned to speak from pre-collapse recordings.
Properties.cadence: Rapid and dense — information-heavy sentences that demand attention.
Properties.example_dialogue: "I make problems disappear. The mess is temporary. The clean is permanent." | "There was never anyone here. There was never anything here. Are we clear?" | "Forensics is a conversation between evidence and investigators. I end that conversation."

Properties.description:
Rongo Delgado-Opoku is tall and rawboned, the kind of frame that suggests either malnutrition or efficiency depending on the decade. At 28, her face carries the layered heritage of generations of diaspora mixing — features that resist easy categorization and reward attention. The chrome is visible — wired reflexes with adrenaline pump — chemical-mechanical hybrid augmentation — and she makes no effort to hide it.

She used to be somebody else, in another city, with another name — that person is officially dead, and Rongo Delgado-Opoku plans to keep it that way. She works as a courier out of The Narrows, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

In the runner community, Rongo Delgado-Opoku is known for getting the job done and not asking questions that would make the job harder to stomach.
Properties.role: High-risk package and data transport — courier
Properties.location: The Narrows — cramped residential corridors between megastructures
Properties.narrative_function: As a courier, Rongo Delgado-Opoku embodies the tension between independence and isolation. She is a lens for examining how people maintain humanity in a profession that incentivizes its erosion.
Properties.augmentations: Wired reflexes with adrenaline pump — chemical-mechanical hybrid augmentation. Neural dampener — blocks external hacking attempts, passive ICE in the brain
Properties.core_fears: Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome; The quiet — silence means something is about to go very wrong; Being captured alive — death is preferable to corporate interrogation
Properties.core_desires: Justice — the corporate kind, where the punishment fits the profit margin; To protect the people in their district who can't protect themselves; The perfect run — one job so clean it becomes legend
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation; Planning — responds to chaos by making detailed contingency plans for everything; Exercises compulsively — the body must be ready, always
Properties.blind_spots: Mistakes loyalty for weakness in others and cynicism for strength in themselves; Cannot recognize when they're being manipulated by someone who genuinely seems to care; Thinks speed can substitute for planning because it's worked so far
Properties.secret: Rongo Delgado-Opoku sends anonymous tips to Meridian 88 law enforcement about competitors. It's not principle — it's market manipulation.

Properties.description:
Rosalind is the kind of woman whose presence in a room shifts the acoustics ��� people speak differently, sit straighter, choose their words more carefully. She is not tall but carries herself with the posture of someone who spent thirty years at the front of rooms demanding to be heard. Her heritage is Fijian-Polish, which expresses itself in wide cheekbones, a generous build, and warm brown skin that she has decorated with an elaborate bioluminescent tattoo pattern along both arms — traditional Fijian knotwork rendered in soft gold light, a gift she gave herself on her sixtieth birthday when Tessera's transit workers finally won the pension reform she'd fought for through three contract cycles. Her hair is silver-black, worn in a thick braid, and she has cat ears — small, rounded, dark-furred — a geneware mod she got to match her grandchildren when they wanted one, which she now considers non-negotiable to her identity.

Rosalind is formidable and knows it, which means she has spent decades learning to calibrate her formidableness carefully. She can be devastatingly charming when she chooses, withering when she must, and quietly exhausted in the rare moments when no one is looking. She is raising her two grandchildren, Kofi (9) and Mira (6), after her daughter's breakdown, and the exhaustion of simultaneous community leadership and primary caregiving is the thing she most carefully never shows.
Properties.role: Retired union leader, Tier 3, community council chair, grandmother raising two grandchildren
Properties.location: Montclare Quiet, a corner flat above a laundromat she technically still owns half of
Properties.narrative_function: Political and community power broker; can broker deals, gather community support, or apply legitimate pressure to local institutions; quest giver for stories about labor rights, housing disputes, or neighborhood protection; provides access to union networks and transit worker information channels.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent tattoo array, both arms (gold knotwork, geneware-integrated). Cat ears, dark-furred (geneware, cosmetic). Cochlear enhancement implant, left ear — an old injury from a corporate security clash during the 2168 transit strike left her with significant hearing loss on that side.
Properties.core_fears: Her grandchildren inheriting a worse world than the one she fought to improve; Becoming a figurehead — respected but no longer effective
Properties.core_desires: Genuine, durable protection for working people; To see Kofi and Mira grow up in a neighborhood that knows who they are
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Action — she processes stress by working; Ritual tea-making as a decompression tool she does not fully acknowledge as such
Properties.blind_spots: She has a tendency to assume that organizing and collective action can solve problems that require individual intervention, sometimes missing when someone needs help that is personal rather than political; She does not adequately account for how much her strength intimidates people who want to help her
Properties.secret: During the 2168 transit strike, she accepted a private side-agreement with a Ferrogate mid-level executive that ended the strike three weeks early. The workers got most of what they needed, but not everything, and the executive was protected from an internal Ferrogate investigation that would have exposed serious safety violations. Four workers were injured in an 'accident' on a line that the investigation would have flagged. She has rationalized this for fifteen years. She has not stopped.
Properties.story_hooks: A Ferrogate urban infrastructure project will route a new transit line directly through Montclare Quiet — the same executive she made the 2168 deal with is overseeing it, and he's been leaving her messages she hasn't answered; Her daughter attempts a surprise return to take custody of Kofi and Mira, and Rosalind must decide between her daughter's recovery and the children's stability — she needs someone neutral to help mediate; Former union members begin approaching her with evidence that Ferrogate has been systematically underpaying pension disbursements across the retired membership for years
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit Workers Union (retired president, 30-year member); Montclare Quiet Community Council (current chair); Tessera pension recipient
Properties.vocabulary: Polished public speaker's vocabulary with an undercurrent of Fijian-inflected English rhythms and occasional Polish idioms inherited from her grandmother. Knows how to make formal language feel warm and warm language feel formal.
Properties.cadence: Measured in public settings, faster and more direct in private. Pauses before key points with the precision of someone who learned pause as a rhetorical tool.
Properties.example_dialogue: Let me be plain with you — this neighborhood does not need a developer's vision for what it could be. It needs to be left alone to be what it already is. | We didn't win that contract by asking nicely. We won it because we made it more expensive to deny us than to give us what we'd earned. That's not idealism. That's just arithmetic.

Properties.description:
Rosamund is a tall, broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin and natural silver-streaked locs pinned in an architectural updo that adds another three centimeters to her already imposing height. Her eyes have patterned irises — rings of amber and black that pulse slightly when she's concentrating, a cosmetic mod she's had since her thirties that she considers her one professional indulgence. She dresses in structured Helix-branded charcoal, always pressed, always buttoned to the collar. A small brass ELF-shrine sits on the corner of her desk — a flat data-tile inlaid with offerings of compressed audit logs and a single dried marigold, left for the compliance spirit she privately calls the Accountant. She hasn't missed a quarterly ritual in eleven years.

Rosamund operates with the calm authority of someone who has seen every flavor of institutional dishonesty and filed the paperwork on most of them. She is not cruel, but she is relentless — a distinction her subordinates appreciate and her peers quietly fear. She genuinely believes that rules exist to protect the people at the bottom of every org chart, which makes her simultaneously the most principled person in her building and the most dangerous to anyone running something off-book. She mentors junior compliance staff with real warmth, remembering every birthday, but will document a violation against a friend without blinking.
Properties.role: Senior Compliance Officer, Helix Biosystems
Properties.location: Vantage Meridian Corporate Campus, Tower Helix-7
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver for investigations into Helix Biosystems irregularities; information source on corporate legal structure and biotech regulation; moral anchor character who represents institutional integrity under pressure; can become an antagonist if players are doing something technically illegal even for good reasons.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises (cosmetic, amber/black rings). Subdermal temperature regulation mesh — medical, installed after a heat-collapse incident during a site audit in the Calumet Rise biolabs. Neural compliance-assist chip for rapid cross-referencing regulatory code databases (standard Helix issue for senior compliance staff).
Properties.core_fears: That the systems she maintains are ultimately protecting the wrong people; That she will be asked to choose between her principles and someone she loves
Properties.core_desires: To build institutional structures that actually work for ordinary people; To be trusted — not liked, trusted
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual and routine as emotional regulation; Channeling anxiety into documentation and preparedness; The ELF-shrine ritual as a form of private prayer
Properties.blind_spots: She underestimates how much her institutional loyalty has been cultivated by Helix to serve Helix's interests, not the people she thinks she's protecting; She mistakes procedural correctness for moral correctness more often than she realizes
Properties.secret: Twelve years ago she buried a compliance finding that would have exposed a Helix executive — not for money, but because the finding would have triggered a lab shutdown that would have killed a clinical trial her younger brother was enrolled in. He survived. The executive is now a division director. The finding has never resurfaced, but Rosamund keeps a copy encrypted on a dead-drop server she checks every month, unable to either use it or delete it.
Properties.story_hooks: She approaches someone with a sealed evidence packet and a single instruction: 'If something happens to me in the next seventy-two hours, deliver this to the ELF-shrine at Deepwell Station. The spirit there knows what to do with it.'; A junior compliance tech she mentored has just gone missing the day after flagging an anomaly in a Helix gene-therapy trial. Rosamund is holding the flagged report and is visibly frightened for the first time anyone can remember.; She is auditing a location where the players have personal connections, and her findings — entirely accurate — will cause serious collateral damage to people who don't deserve it.
Properties.affiliation: Helix Biosystems (Tier 4)
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, formal without being stiff — she uses regulatory terminology fluently but can translate it into plain language instantly. Rarely uses slang but knows what it means.
Properties.cadence: Measured and deliberate, with long pauses before significant statements. Never rushes. When she rushes, something is wrong.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You're describing a pattern, not an incident. Patterns are what I care about.' | 'I'm not here to make your life difficult. I'm here because someone, somewhere decided to make my job necessary.'

Properties.description:
Rosamund is small and very still, with the particular quality of stillness that looks like patience but is actually intense concentration. Her skin is warm brown and she has the most elaborate geneware of almost anyone in her building: her hair changes color in response to her emotional state via a chromatic expression mod she installed in her second year of grad school and has never entirely mastered — it runs bright orange when she's excited, deep blue when she's uncertain, and an unsettling grey-green when she's frightened, which her colleagues have learned to read as a fairly accurate emotional barometer. She finds this embarrassing and wears it anyway. Her eyes are natural dark hazel but she has retractable feline pupils mod — not for aesthetics but because it genuinely improves her visual acuity in the low-light lab conditions where she does most of her work.

Rosamund is three years post-doctorate and working in the most obscure corner of a field that most people already find obscure. Her work is simple to describe and nearly impossible to explain: she studies the communication systems of organisms that have been engineered to not have language, and has found that several of them have developed one anyway. She is methodical, meticulous, and possessed by her research in a way that has cost her two relationships and most of her social life. She is not unhappy about this in the way that she is unhappy about other things; her work makes her feel like she is standing at the edge of something enormous, and she would rather be there than comfortable elsewhere. She is Tier 2 income on an Aurochs Medical Complex stipend and supplementary university grant, which means she eats a lot of printed food and has a coat she's had for six years.
Properties.role: Xenolinguist and gene-sequence archivist, studying the emergent communication systems of engineered organisms and attempting to establish a taxonomy of non-human language
Properties.location: Aurochs Medical Complex, research annex sublevel
Properties.narrative_function: Access point to Aurochs Medical Complex and engineered organism research; possesses findings about non-human language emergence that have unsettling implications for bioethics and Helix Biosystems intellectual property law; her naivety about institutional politics makes her vulnerable; her research intersects unexpectedly with E.L.F. communication studies
Properties.augmentations: Chromatic expression hair mod (geneware — emotional color response, orange/blue/grey-green range), retractable feline pupil mod (geneware, functional not cosmetic), standard neural mesh
Properties.core_fears: That she will publish her findings and no one will understand why they matter; That Aurochs Medical Complex owns her research and will bury it for IP reasons
Properties.core_desires: To be the first person to produce a complete structural grammar of a non-human emergent language; To have her work matter in a way that outlasts the institutional structures that fund it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Throwing herself into new subfields when stuck — she has become an accidental expert in half a dozen adjacent areas; Long comms to her younger brother in Grainfort who is not an academic and gives her very grounded perspective
Properties.blind_spots: So focused on the research that she misses institutional signals that should alarm her; Assumes that the inherent importance of a finding will protect it from suppression
Properties.secret: One of the organisms she studies — a Helix Biosystems engineered cephalopod variant used in environmental sensing — has been trying to communicate with her specifically for four months. She is not sure yet if it recognizes her as an individual or if she is reading pattern into noise, but the sequences she receives when she is present differ structurally from those produced in her absence. She has begun leaving small objects near its tank to see if it responds. If she is right, the IP implications for Helix alone are staggering, and she has not told her Aurochs supervisor.
Properties.story_hooks: Aurochs Medical Complex has scheduled the cephalopod cohort she's been studying for termination and tissue harvest — standard procedure at the end of a sensor deployment contract — and she has approximately three weeks to either prove they have language or find another way to stop it; Aissatu Wren-Dzhaparidze reaches out after reading her preliminary communication taxonomy paper; the structural grammar Rosamund has been building shares unexpected features with the anomalous E.L.F. communication protocol Aissatu has been trying to decode
Properties.affiliation: Aurochs Medical Complex Research Annex / Meridian Civic University (adjunct researcher)
Properties.vocabulary: Technical and precise in her field, unexpectedly informal outside it; has a habit of reaching for analogies from wildly different domains
Properties.cadence: Measured and quiet, occasionally breaking into rapid concentrated bursts when she's working through something out loud
Properties.example_dialogue: 'It's not language because we decided to call it language. It's language because it has structure, displacement, and social transmission. The question of whether we call it that is a politics question, not a science question.' | 'My hair is — I know, I can see it, it means I think I have something, give me a second.'

Properties.description:
Rosamund Fofana-Çelik is the kind of woman who makes a room feel both smaller and more significant simply by being present — she has that particular gravity of someone who spent decades at the front of a classroom demanding attention and getting it. She's medium height, brown-skinned, with warm undertones and a face built for expression, every emotion living near the surface and making no apologies. She wears her silver hair in elaborate braided wraps she learned from her Guinean grandmother and has continued perfecting for sixty years. Her only augmentation is cosmetic: her fingernails are geneware, growing in shifting blues and greens, a retirement gift she gave herself after twenty-eight years of being professionally 'appropriate.'

She is the best storyteller in Avalon Quiet, possibly in any of the Quiet districts, and she knows it without it making her insufferable — she treats it as a responsibility rather than a distinction. On the third evening of every month she holds sessions at the Community Hearth where she tells stories: sometimes history, sometimes myth, sometimes thinly veiled accounts of things that actually happened to people in the room who gave her permission. Children come because they're brought. Adults come because they keep coming back. She has never repeated a session in eleven years.
Properties.role: Retired secondary school teacher, informal neighborhood storyteller and oral historian
Properties.location: Avalon Quiet, Unit 3B; teaches informal story sessions at the Avalon Community Hearth
Properties.narrative_function: Storyteller and local color, keeper of oral history, emotional core of the Avalon Quiet community; can provide backstory on long-term residents and neighborhood history through the frame of her stories
Properties.augmentations: Geneware fingernails (shifting blue-green, cosmetic); no other modifications
Properties.core_fears: being forgotten — not as a person but as a voice, having the stories die with her; that she taught children to love a world that was going to fail them
Properties.core_desires: to pass something real on, not just information but a way of seeing; to tell one true story about herself before she dies
Properties.coping_mechanisms: transforming pain into narrative as a way of giving it shape and distance; connection — she is never truly at rest unless she's with people; the monthly sessions as a ritual that structures time and meaning
Properties.blind_spots: sometimes aestheticizes suffering — including her own — in ways that prevent her from sitting with it directly; can be performing warmth when she's actually lonely
Properties.secret: One of the stories she tells — a beloved one, about a teacher who protected a student during the Corporate Wars by hiding them in the school's server room and convincing an Arcturus unit that the building was empty — is true, and she is the teacher. She has never confirmed this. The student died in 2199 and she has never spoken of them by name in any other context.
Properties.story_hooks: A former student has returned to Avalon Quiet — now working for Axiom — and wants her blessing for something she finds deeply troubling; She has finally decided to tell the true version of the server room story, but only in the presence of someone who will record it accurately; A corporate media company has approached the Community Hearth about licensing her sessions for a nostalgia content platform — the community is divided and she has the casting vote
Properties.affiliation: Avalon Quiet Community Hearth; Meridian 88 Educators Retiree Association (MERA); independent
Properties.vocabulary: rich, varied, deliberately chosen; shifts register easily between formal and intimate; uses silence as punctuation
Properties.cadence: expansive and controlled, the cadence of someone who knows exactly how much time they have and how to fill it
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want to know what the Corporate Wars were like? I'll tell you. But I'm going to tell you the version that's true, not the version that's useful.' | 'I taught for twenty-eight years. I know when someone is sitting in the back of the room hoping not to be called on. I always called on them. I'm going to call on you now.'

Properties.description:
Roshanda was, until four years ago, a Tier 3 Tessera municipal archivist with an apartment in Edgewater Prism, a corporate pension accruing slowly, and a work record that would have earned her a formal commendation if she hadn't committed the specific category of misconduct that got her registration stripped instead. She carries herself with the precise, slightly stiff posture of someone still negotiating between who they were and what they've become. She is a lean woman of West African and Swedish descent with medium-dark skin, close-cropped natural hair that has developed a white streak above her left temple in the last four years — stress, she'll tell you, if you ask — and round-framed glasses she still wears out of habit even though her vision has been corrected by the basic corneal work she had done a decade ago. The glasses have no lenses anymore. She never took them off.

Roshanda's current project is an oral history of the Meridian 88 drifter population: she walks, she listens, she records on a battered analog audio device (nothing networked, nothing that can be subpoenaed) and she transcribes by hand in a series of water-resistant notebooks she keeps in a waterproof roll pack. She has forty-one notebooks so far. She calls the project 'The Register of the Unregistered,' and she has not decided what she will do with it when it is finished, if it is ever finished. She approaches every stranger with the particular respect of someone who has learned that every person is an archive. She prays to no E.L.F. — she is skeptical of the whole phenomenon, which she finds sociologically interesting and theologically unconvincing, a position she shares freely whether or not anyone asked.
Properties.role: expelled citizen and nomadic oral historian
Properties.location: Rotates between Bridgepoint and Gravesend Basin; sleeps at the Gravesend travelers' shelter
Properties.narrative_function: Living encyclopedia of the drifter underworld — knows people, histories, and patterns across the entire transit periphery of Meridian 88. Can provide context, history, and contacts. May ask for help in ways that involve moral complexity. Her notebooks are a significant object.
Properties.augmentations: Basic corneal correction (old, corporate-era). A Tessera employee-grade subdermal data port on her left wrist that was never removed — technically deactivated but she's heard they can be reactivated. This makes her periodically nervous.
Properties.core_fears: that the archive will be destroyed before it can matter — that she is building something that will be swept away like everything else; that she is doing this for her own guilt rather than for the people whose stories she's collecting
Properties.core_desires: for the archive to be published, read, to change something concrete; to be reinstated — not because she wants the job back, but because she wants to have been right
Properties.coping_mechanisms: intellectual framing — turns every experience into data, which provides emotional distance; maintaining routine with obsessive consistency as a substitute for the structure her former life provided
Properties.blind_spots: treats people's stories as research more often than she realizes; the people she interviews sometimes feel processed rather than heard; believes her exile was a consequence of principle rather than a mistake in execution that could have been handled better
Properties.secret: The reason she was expelled was not the noble archival transgression she implies — she shared classified documents with a journalist to expose Tessera misconduct, yes, but she also did it partly to destroy a colleague who had been promoted over her. The outcome was just, but her motives were not purely so. The distinction haunts her.
Properties.story_hooks: Notebook thirty-seven contains an interview with a man who described, in passing detail, the location of a sealed Tessera data vault from before the corporate restructuring — and then disappeared two weeks later; Roshanda is not sure if she's the reason he disappeared; A former academic contact has reached out offering to publish the archive through an offshore academic network — but the terms require transferring the original recordings to a Tessera-adjacent server, which Roshanda does not trust and cannot verify
Properties.affiliation: None — formerly Tessera Municipal Archives; informally networked with academic contacts she is no longer supposed to have
Properties.vocabulary: Educated and precise, with an archivist's habit of sourcing claims; periodically catches herself using corporate jargon and corrects mid-sentence; slightly formal with strangers as a reflex
Properties.cadence: Measured and thoughtful, with a journalist's instinct to leave space for the other person to keep talking
Properties.example_dialogue: 'If I understand you correctly, you've been at this crossing for three seasons without your status reviewed. That's significant, actually — that's a pattern I'm seeing in five other cases.' | 'I'm not a journalist. I'm not anything official. I'm just — I'm writing it down so that it existed. So that someone somewhere has to acknowledge it existed.'

Properties.description:
Roshani is solid and practical in the way of people who lift and carry things every day — not large but dense with muscle, with the sun-damaged skin of someone who spends significant time on open airship decks and the quick, evaluating eyes of a born trader. Her hair is streaked in color-shifting strands, currently cycling through amber and deep red with the temperature, a mod she wears for professional reasons: 'People remember the hair,' she explains without embarrassment. She has a pattern of scarification on her left forearm in a Zambian geometric style, done by her mother, which she occasionally traces with her thumb when calculating.

Roshani runs textiles, preserved food, hand-fabricated tools, and 'specialty information' (she is vague about this category) between the transit hubs and fringe communities around Meridian 88's industrial periphery. She is a member of a caravan of six airships called The Abundant Error, which operates on informal routes that avoid Ferrogate Transit's official freight lanes and the associated fees. She is sharp, cheerful, aggressively fair in her dealings, and completely at home in ambiguity — she has been in seventeen border disputes, four quarantine zones, and one civil emergency, and approaches all of them with the same businesslike equanimity.
Properties.role: Wandering trader, airship caravan member
Properties.location: Bay View Docks, temporary berth at Pier 14-Gamma (airship caravan The Abundant Error)
Properties.narrative_function: Trade hub and mobile resource — she can source unusual goods, carries messages between communities, knows prices and conditions across the entire drifter trade network, and can offer passage on The Abundant Error to characters who need to move without official transit records.
Properties.augmentations: Color-shifting hair mod (temperature-reactive, amber to red spectrum). Enhanced olfactory glands — helps assess food quality and cargo condition. No chrome.
Properties.core_fears: The caravan dissolving — her community scattered; Being cheated in a way she didn't see coming, which she reads as a failure of perception
Properties.core_desires: To negotiate a deal so elegant that both parties feel they won; To eventually own her own ship outright
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Treats every problem as a transaction — finds the exchange rate for any situation; Cooking for the caravan crew when stressed
Properties.blind_spots: Applies market logic to situations that aren't transactional — reads emotional needs as negotiating positions; Underestimates loyalty that isn't expressed in practical action
Properties.secret: The 'specialty information' she trades occasionally includes the locations of Q-zero communities — not to corponations, she tells herself, only to other drifters who need to find them. She knows this is not entirely safe and has not fully examined whether it is ethical.
Properties.story_hooks: Roshani has sold location information about a Q-zero community that was subsequently raided — she doesn't know yet, but the information chain is traceable back to her; The Abundant Error has taken on a cargo container that no one on the crew can open, consigned by a shipper who has since disappeared from all records
Properties.affiliation: The Abundant Error airship caravan (six vessels, rotating crew of about thirty total)
Properties.vocabulary: Trade-precise, good with numbers, switches between formal and colloquial seamlessly depending on who she's reading as her market. Occasional Nyanja words when doing mental arithmetic.
Properties.cadence: Brisk and rhythmic, like someone who has made the same pitch many times and refined every syllable
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Fairly said, but that price assumes I have no other buyers today, and I have three. What's the exchange?' | 'I don't carry things I can't account for. You want passage with no manifest? What's that worth to you, specifically, in numbers?'
