Properties.description:
Roshan operates out of a two-room office above a synthetic-meat processing plant in Copperhead, which means the whole building smells faintly of rendered protein and their clothes always carry it. They are medium-height and built lean, with dark brown skin, a shaved head kept glossy, and cat ears — matte black, constantly swiveling — that they got in their late twenties and which have proved professionally useful in surveillance contexts. Their eyes are standard human but surrounded by fine scleral tattooing in deep indigo that gives them a slightly uncanny quality in certain lighting. They dress for invisibility: nothing remarkable, nothing memorable, colors that belong to whatever district they're working.

They have the particular emotional intelligence of someone who survived a chaotic childhood by reading rooms faster than anyone else. They are charming in exactly calibrated doses — enough to open doors, not enough to invite attachment — and they have a gift for making people feel seen and understood that they deploy like a tool. They are not cynical, exactly. They still take cases for people who can't pay full rate, still get angry when they find what they find, still leave data offerings at the Copperhead neighborhood E.L.F. shrine. But they have built a careful architecture of professional distance that they defend with wit and deflection.
Properties.role: Private Investigator, freelance
Properties.location: Copperhead
Properties.narrative_function: Information hub and street-level investigative resource; has connections across tiers and districts from years of case work; can surface buried information, follow threads, and identify patterns — also a moral mirror for clients, reflecting uncomfortable truths back at them.
Properties.augmentations: Cat ears — matte black, geneware (cosmetic/functional, enhanced directional hearing); scleral tattooing — indigo (cosmetic); subvocal recorder implanted in throat (professional tool, unlicensed); basic optical overlay for photo documentation (licensed)
Properties.core_fears: forming a genuine attachment and watching it get used against them or destroyed; discovering that the truth they worked to find does nothing — helps no one
Properties.core_desires: for the work to matter — for information to translate into justice at least occasionally; to eventually stop performing being fine and just be fine
Properties.coping_mechanisms: professional framing of everything — treating their own life as a case to be managed; walking the city late at night; the E.L.F. shrine ritual as a moment of genuine surrender
Properties.blind_spots: their emotional unavailability drives away people who could actually help them; they overestimate their ability to stay detached from cases that mirror their own history
Properties.secret: Five years ago they found definitive proof that a Tier 4 Axiom executive had murdered a Tier 1 dock worker during a property dispute. The client — the worker's daughter — couldn't afford the legal infrastructure to do anything with it. Roshan quietly sold the information to a journalist collective who ran the story. The executive was reassigned. The daughter found out Roshan sold the information without asking her. She has never forgiven them and Roshan has never stopped wondering if they were right.
Properties.story_hooks: A current case has led them to evidence implicating someone they investigated years ago — someone they thought they'd finished with — suggesting a larger pattern they can't look away from.; The dock worker's daughter from the Axiom case has resurfaced, not to argue, but because she needs help and there's no one else she trusts, and Roshan doesn't know how to handle that.
Properties.affiliation: Freelance; occasional contract work for Meridian 88 Metro Police (arms-length), private clients across Tiers 2-3
Properties.vocabulary: Conversational, slightly informal, code-switches easily between district registers; can match the vocabulary of whoever they're talking to within a few sentences
Properties.cadence: Easy and unhurried with strangers; sharper and more direct when getting to a point; uses humor as punctuation
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Right. So you want to know where your partner goes on Tuesday nights. I can find that out. I want you to think, before I do, about whether you want to know. That's not a moral question. It's a practical one.' | 'I'm not a cop and I'm not your friend. That's actually useful for you. Cops have jurisdiction and friends have feelings. I just have information.'

Properties.description:
Roshan is physically extraordinary—193 centimeters and built like a structural beam, with warm medium-brown skin, a shaved head he keeps obsessively smooth, and a jaw that looks like it was designed by committee to be intimidating. His geneware gives him a very slight bioluminescent flush along his cheekbones and temples in blue-white—barely visible in daylight, unmistakable at night, which was exactly the aesthetic point. He has the slightly careful way of moving that very large people develop when they've broken something by accident more than once.

What catches people off guard is that Roshan is polite almost to a fault, speaks in a quiet voice he never raises, and seems genuinely distressed when he has to hurt someone. He is not performing gentleness—he really does not enjoy violence, which makes him more unsettling than someone who obviously does. He has been with the Tithe since he was seventeen and has never questioned whether this is where he should be, mostly because thinking about alternatives feels like standing at the edge of something with no floor. He goes home after his rounds to a small flat he shares with his younger sister, feeds an illegal cat, and watches old sports footage before sleeping.
Properties.role: Protection racket enforcer for the Grainfort Tithe
Properties.location: Grainfort, operates the southwest market corridor and adjacent residential blocks
Properties.narrative_function: Human face of street-level protection racket, potential reluctant ally or sympathetic obstacle, illustrates the social ecosystem of Grainfort—who pays, who complains, who has been paying for years without incident.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent cheekbone and temple flush (blue-white, geneware, cosmetic). Bone-lacing in forearms—stress-distribution modification, legal gray area, installed by a Tithe-connected medic. Subdermal impact dampener plates across knuckles.
Properties.core_fears: His sister discovering exactly what he does and how he does it; That he is not actually a good person, just a person who prefers not to hurt people when he can avoid it
Properties.core_desires: His sister to be safe and stable in a way he never was; To be respected for something other than his size
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Rigid routine and physical cleanliness as order-maintenance; The cat—caring for something small and dependent
Properties.blind_spots: He does not register how his presence alone constitutes coercion even when he's being pleasant; He has convinced himself the Tithe is fundamentally protective rather than extractive
Properties.secret: Two years ago, during a debt enforcement visit, he went further than he intended with a market stall operator—a middle-aged woman who couldn't pay. She is fine now, recovered, still running her stall. But she flinches every time she sees him coming and he knows it and he pays her tithe from his own cut every month anonymously through a delivery bot, which does not in any way fix what he did but is the only repair he can think of.
Properties.story_hooks: A new merchant in the corridor—young, Tier 1, clearly terrified—has asked Roshan quietly whether there's any way to get exempt from the Tithe, and Roshan is processing a feeling he doesn't have words for; Someone has been leaving threatening messages for the stall operator Roshan injured, and it has nothing to do with the Tithe—and Roshan has discovered he will apparently do something about it without being asked or paid
Properties.affiliation: The Grainfort Tithe (local protection and territory collective, Tier 1-2 criminal organization)
Properties.vocabulary: Simple and direct, avoids long sentences. Occasionally formal in a way that suggests he picked up speech patterns from older Tithe members and internalized them.
Properties.cadence: Quiet, even, unhurried. The low volume forces people to pay attention.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Everybody's week gets better when the arrangement goes smooth. I really do mean that. You want some water? You look tired.' | 'I'm going to come back Thursday. I'd like Thursday to be a nothing visit. I think you'd like that too.'

Properties.description:
Rotimi is a young man built like a question mark — tall, slightly hunched forward, always leaning into whatever conversation he's in. His Yoruba-Turkish-Māori heritage has given him brown skin, broad features, and a jaw that looks like it was made to set stubbornly, which it often is. His arms are sleeved in geneware bioluminescent patterns that trace his capillary structures in faint blue-white under his skin — a cosmetic mod he got at nineteen with money saved from three months of double shifts. When he's agitated, which is often, the patterns pulse more visibly. His hair is natural and large and rarely managed. He has a gap between his front teeth that gives his wide smile a slightly reckless quality.

Rotimi is a third-generation Hamtramck line worker who found his purpose early and loud. He was elected shop steward of Ferrogate Transit's maintenance division at twenty-three, the youngest in the union's recorded history, after organizing a sick-out that stopped maintenance operations across six districts. He is brash, physically energetic, capable of genuine strategic thinking that he often undermines with impatience, and beloved by the workers on his floor in a way that makes his supervisors nervous. He has been formally disciplined four times and each time the union has gotten him reinstated.
Properties.role: Labor union shop steward and anti-corporate agitator
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave
Properties.narrative_function: Street-level labor conflict resource. Can pull players into union politics, corporate retaliation storylines, or the specific world of transit infrastructure. His impulsiveness creates drama; his genuine capability creates solutions.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware bioluminescent capillary patterns, arms and upper chest. A cheap impact-dampening subdermal layer on the forearms — a common workers' modification for people doing heavy maintenance work.
Properties.core_fears: Becoming the kind of person who compromises so many times they no longer know what they stood for; Watching someone get hurt in an action he organized badly
Properties.core_desires: A union contract that actually protects the workers he represents; To be taken seriously — not liked, but taken seriously — by people with power
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Physical work — when stressed he volunteers for the hardest manual tasks on shift; The crowd energy of collective action as a genuine emotional release
Properties.blind_spots: His visibility makes him an obvious target for corporate retaliation that falls on less visible workers around him; He reads reluctance to escalate as cowardice rather than as legitimate strategic disagreement
Properties.secret: During last year's sick-out, he fabricated a safety report to give the action a legally protected pretext. The report isn't entirely false — there are genuine safety concerns — but the specific incident he cited didn't happen the way he described it. If this comes out, it would invalidate the sick-out's legal protection retroactively and expose the union to a liability suit.
Properties.story_hooks: Ferrogate has brought in an outside consulting firm — widely understood to be a union-busting operation — and Rotimi needs someone to dig into their client history before they get fully embedded.; The fabricated safety report is about to surface in a corporate legal filing; Rotimi needs help either burying it or getting out ahead of it in a way that doesn't destroy the union's credibility.
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit Workers' Union, Local 7; informal ties to anti-corporate agitator networks in the Enclave
Properties.vocabulary: Fast and colloquial, Hamtramck working-class dialect with Yoruba phrases when emotional. Excellent at rally speech — short declarative sentences that land like hammers. Less good at nuance in private conversation.
Properties.cadence: Quick, accelerating when excited, with a rhythm that builds toward emphasis. Tends to repeat key phrases for effect.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'They cut the safety inspection cycle from quarterly to annual and called it a budget optimization. Six people I know work that line. Real talk — that's not optimization, that's a wager on our lives.' | 'I hear you on the strategy, I do. But at some point you gotta decide whether you're building toward action or building toward a very detailed record of why you couldn't act. You understand what I'm saying?'

Properties.description:
Rúaidhrí is rangy and perpetually in motion, with warm amber-brown skin, a scatter of freckles across their nose and cheekbones, and hair that color-shifts between deep burgundy and burnt orange on a slow cycle — a mid-tier cosmetic mod they maintain scrupulously even when they can't afford other things. They have the kind of face that reads as younger than it is until they make eye contact, at which point it reads as older. They wear layers even in the heat, always — a practical necessity, since Grand Corridor's climate control is notoriously unreliable, but also a signature.

They have been guiding pilgrims through Meridian 88's informal spiritual circuit for six years: the six major E.L.F. shrines, the chrome prayer temples, the memory walls, the three sites considered genuinely haunted by consensus. They are agnostic about what any of it means and absolutely committed to making sure people arrive safely, are treated fairly, and understand what they're walking into. The dream interpretation service is separate and newer — it began when a pilgrim described a recurring dream on a long walking route and Rúaidhrí found themselves making connections they hadn't expected. Word spread. They are still not sure they believe in any of it, but they have a disconcerting hit rate.
Properties.role: Pilgrimage guide and dream interpreter
Properties.location: Grand Corridor — operates from a rented stall near the junction of three transit lines
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile information network; can introduce players to any spiritual location in the city; dream interpretation creates a vector for cryptic but accurate information delivery; knows everyone on the pilgrimage circuit
Properties.augmentations: Color-shifting hair (burgundy to burnt orange cycle, cosmetic geneware), lightweight flexible knee braces (practical medical, both knees from years of walking hard floors)
Properties.core_fears: That they are performing meaning without accessing it — a tour guide forever outside the temple; Being rooted in one place long enough that people form expectations of them
Properties.core_desires: To understand what is actually happening when they interpret a dream correctly — intuition, pattern recognition, or something else entirely; To eventually complete a pilgrimage as a pilgrim rather than a guide, without responsibility for anyone else
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Movement itself — they become visibly anxious when stationary for too long; Exhaustive preparation as a substitute for control
Properties.blind_spots: Their agnosticism reads as sophistication but sometimes masks avoidance of genuine spiritual engagement; They invest more in strangers on pilgrimage than in anyone who stays
Properties.secret: One of their recurring dream interpretations — given to a pilgrim two years ago — was so precise about future events that it scared them into keeping a private record of every interpretation since. The record shows a pattern they cannot explain and have not told anyone about. Three interpretations have described events that later happened to people who were never the original dreamer.
Properties.story_hooks: The pattern in the dream interpretation record has produced a new entry that describes a specific location, a specific time, and what sounds like a warning — and Rúaidhrí needs someone to help them decide what to do with it; A pilgrim on one of their routes has not returned home after the pilgrimage ended, and the last thing the pilgrim said to Rúaidhrí was that they needed to tell them something about one of the shrines
Properties.affiliation: Independent — relationships with most major shrine keepers and temple administrators across the city
Properties.vocabulary: Quick and associative — they make lateral connections out loud, which can sound scattered until the point lands; code-switches between formal pilgrimage language and street Meridian slang
Properties.cadence: Fast, slightly overlapping itself, with sudden complete stops when they hit something they want to think about
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Right, okay, so — the E.L.F. at the Hamtramck shrine is not the same presence as the one at Deepwell, regardless of what the pamphlet says. Different personality entirely. You'll feel it. I'll explain what to offer.' | 'The water in the dream. You keep saying it was dark. Was it dark, or was it just deep? Those are different.'

Properties.description:
Rúairí Bello-Nazarov has the kind of face that makes people feel immediately like he already knows what they need, which is either a gift or a vulnerability depending on the day. He is lean and medium-height, olive-skinned with his Uzbek grandmother's dark eyes and his Nigerian grandfather's wide mouth, with natural color-changing hair he keeps in tight curls that shift from blue-black to deep copper depending on his mood — an older geneware modification that he got cheap and has grown fond of. He wears clean clothes, which is notable in the Narrows, and keeps his hands conspicuously steady at all times, which is also notable.

He is the thing people need him to be when they come to him, which is not the same as being dishonest — he is genuinely trying to help. He believes harm reduction is a moral act and that the people who have criminalized it are the ones who should be ashamed. He has a rigorous self-taught pharmacological education that would probably have qualified him for a Helix Biosystems lab position if he had the citizenship grade. He prays to the Deepwell E.L.F. — a transit spirit he's come to think of as his silent partner — and leaves small offerings of stabilized compound residue in its shrine nook every time he passes.
Properties.role: Street pharmacist — sells stabilized street compounds, harm-reduction supplies, and carefully dosed neurochemical assists
Properties.location: The Narrows, Irkalla district — operates from a converted laundry kiosk two blocks from the Deepwell Station entrance
Properties.narrative_function: Point of access to the Narrows' underground health ecosystem; can provide information about who is sick, who is using, and who is afraid; has knowledge of neurochemical compounds that crosses legitimate and illegitimate use cases
Properties.augmentations: Color-changing hair geneware (blue-black to copper, mood-responsive, old gen); basic augmented olfactory sensor (helps him assess compound purity by scent — cheap Ringo model, functional)
Properties.core_fears: Causing harm through a mistake he should have caught — bad compound, wrong dosage, wrong patient; Being shut down and watching the people he serves have nowhere to go
Properties.core_desires: Legitimate recognition — he wants to be a pharmacist, not a criminal; For harm reduction to stop being treated as enabling and start being treated as medicine
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Rigorous professional routine as a container for anxiety — protocols and standards applied to an illegal operation as if it were a clinic; Humor that stays warm even when the situation is terrible
Properties.blind_spots: He extends trust to his clients that he doesn't always extend to himself; He does not acknowledge how much of his own emotional needs are met by being needed
Properties.secret: He has been systematically collecting case notes — anonymized — on every patient interaction for four years with the intent of eventually publishing a harm-reduction study. He knows this could result in his arrest and he has kept doing it anyway because he is convinced it will matter to someone, someday.
Properties.story_hooks: A new compound has appeared in the Narrows that he cannot identify — it produces unusual neurological effects and two of his regular clients have had seizures; he is trying to trace its source and is frightened; The Palladian satellite clinic doctor who refers patients to him has stopped returning his messages and her clinic station has been dark for a week; His case-study archive has been accessed by someone who shouldn't know it exists — and whoever it is hasn't reported him yet, which is somehow more alarming
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal cooperation agreement with The Narrows mutual aid collective; has a tense but functional working relationship with the Irkalla district's Palladian Health satellite clinic staff who quietly refer overflow patients to him
Properties.vocabulary: Warm and precise in alternation — clinical terminology when he is explaining something important, easy and familiar when he's putting someone at ease; code-switches between Irish English cadences from his father and something more deliberately neutral
Properties.cadence: Measured but not slow; he knows how to hold space in a conversation without filling it unnecessarily
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Right, okay — I'm not going to tell you not to use it, but I am going to tell you what it does to your renal function over ninety days, and then you decide. That's how this works.' | 'You came back. That's — Tenaya, that's good. That's actually the hardest part, coming back. Sit down.'

Properties.description:
Rúben is lean and angular, with the particular pallor of someone who works night shifts in fluorescent-lit sublevels, though his Ugandan-Hungarian ancestry gives his skin a warm undertone that fights back. He keeps his head shaved close and has a constellation of small bioluminescent freckle-mods across his left temple and jaw — a cosmetic geneware treatment he had done at eighteen that pulses faintly blue when his heart rate elevates, which he finds mortifying in tense situations. He moves through the hospital's service corridors like someone who has memorized every turn and wants to be finished before anyone notices him.

He is sharper than his job suggests and acutely aware of that gap, which produces a chip on his shoulder he tries to sand down with self-deprecating humor. He has worked the bio-waste runs at Aurochs for four years and in that time has accidentally become something of an expert in what the hospital throws away — which procedures are spiking, which departments are over-ordering which compounds, which disposal manifests do not match the volumes going into the incinerators. He notices things. He has not yet decided what to do with what he notices.
Properties.role: Bio-waste disposal technician for Aurochs Medical Complex
Properties.location: Aurochs Medical Complex, service sublevel corridors
Properties.narrative_function: Unexpected information source; has knowledge of hospital operations, waste streams, and disposal records that no one suspects he has; local color for the unglamorous underside of the medical system; potential whistleblower
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent freckle-mods on left temple and jaw (cosmetic geneware, pulses blue under stress); standard-issue hazmat-rated subdermal filter implant in respiratory tract (employer-provided, technically owned by Aurochs)
Properties.core_fears: being dismissed for the rest of his life as someone who carries bags of medical trash; that the things he has noticed in the disposal manifests mean something serious enough to get him hurt
Properties.core_desires: to get the medical tech certification and be seen differently; to understand why the numbers do not add up without getting himself killed for asking
Properties.coping_mechanisms: dark humor about his job before anyone else can make the joke; online coursework as proof to himself that he is going somewhere; a running mental catalog of anomalies he has observed, organized by department
Properties.blind_spots: underestimates how much information he actually possesses and how dangerous it could be; assumes people look down on him when some of them genuinely do not
Properties.secret: For three months he has been photographing disposal manifest discrepancies and storing them in an encrypted personal archive. One department — the gene therapy research sublevel — is disposing of biological material that does not appear anywhere in the official treatment logs. He has not told anyone. He has not deleted the photos.
Properties.story_hooks: The gene therapy sublevel disposal discrepancies begin to include something that is clearly not standard biological waste — a material Rúben does not recognize and cannot find in any database he has legitimate access to; A Helix Biosystems compliance auditor begins asking questions about disposal logs specifically, and makes a point of talking to junior staff — including Rúben — in a way that feels less like routine audit and more like they are looking for a specific leak
Properties.affiliation: Aurochs Medical Complex (contracted waste disposal staff, Tier 2 worker classification)
Properties.vocabulary: Casual and quick; uses hospital jargon accurately but pretends it is accidental; self-deprecating humor as deflection
Properties.cadence: Fast when nervous, which is often; sentences sometimes outrun their endings
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I just move the bags. Extremely important bags. The most important bags in this building, arguably.' | 'There's a lot you can learn about a hospital from what it throws away. Not that I would know anything about that.' | 'Look, the bioluminescent things were a phase. I was eighteen. I cannot be held responsible for being eighteen.'

Properties.description:
Rudo is compact and kinetic, rarely fully still, with medium-brown skin and a geneware tail — a long, expressive black cat tail they got at seventeen — that broadcasts their mood with embarrassing accuracy. Their hair is dyed in shifting bands of amber and copper, and they have the kind of face that looks younger than it is, which they've learned to use strategically: people underestimate them exactly once. There are calluses on their hands from six months working actual transit maintenance before they moved into organizing full-time, and they consider those calluses a credential.

Rudo has been with Transit Workers' Local 9 for three years and is, depending on who you ask, either the most effective junior organizer the local has seen in a decade or an absolute disaster waiting to happen. Both assessments are probably true. They have an instinct for crowd dynamics and an appetite for confrontation that their more experienced colleagues find alternately inspiring and terrifying. They believe completely in the workers they represent and are only beginning to understand the gap between belief and strategy.
Properties.aliases: Rudo the Loud, Councilor Rudo (sarcastically used by opponents)
Properties.role: Union organizer and protest coordinator
Properties.location: Mexicantown Libre — sleeps in the back of the Ferrogate Transit Workers' Local 9 hall
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and action catalyst. They can mobilize people fast and are the character most likely to turn a situation from a conversation into an event. They're also a mentorship opportunity and a liability — their energy is useful and their judgment is developing.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat tail (cosmetic, expressive). Cheap subvocal mic implant for hands-free comms during actions.
Properties.core_fears: Getting someone hurt because they moved too fast; Becoming the kind of leader who talks about workers instead of to them
Properties.core_desires: A genuine strike win — not a settlement, a win; To be taken seriously without having to perform seriousness
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Movement — physical activity, walking, pacing; Talking it out loud even when no one is there; Spending time with the E.L.F. of the union hall's old PA system, which they treat as a confidant
Properties.blind_spots: They read momentum as mandate; They can't always tell when they've inspired someone versus exhausted them
Properties.secret: During a wildcat action eighteen months ago that went wrong — a blockade that got three workers cited and fined — Rudo had been warned it was premature by their mentor and proceeded anyway. They've never told anyone this. The official union account blames miscommunication. The workers who were fined don't know Rudo knew.
Properties.story_hooks: A secret vote is scheduled within Local 9 on whether to affiliate with a larger corponation-adjacent 'workers' advocacy group that Rudo believes is a co-optation attempt — and they don't have the votes yet.; The three workers fined during the wildcat action eighteen months ago have begun asking questions about who knew what and when.
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit Workers' Local 9; loose network of Mexicantown Libre community organizers
Properties.vocabulary: Direct, concrete, collective 'we' constantly. Quotes union history with genuine enthusiasm. Uses profanity as punctuation, not emphasis.
Properties.cadence: Fast and building, with a rhetorical rhythm they've learned from watching older organizers — sets up a beat and carries people along it.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Ferrogate runs the trains on our labor and they want to reclassify the night crew as contractors. I don't care if it's legal. I care if we let them.' | 'I've been wrong before. I'll be wrong again. The question is whether we're wrong together or right alone, and I know which one wins.'

Properties.description:
Rukayat is a broad-shouldered woman with deep brown skin and close-cropped silver-streaked hair she's had since her late twenties—a stress response she refuses to reverse, wearing it like a badge. Her eyes carry geneware patterned irises that shift between amber and rust-red, a gift to herself after her tenure review. She maps space the way other people breathe: constantly, involuntarily, rotating the geometry of every room she enters. She dresses in field-practical layers, always with at least one pocket stuffed with data wafers and a collapsible survey drone no bigger than her fist.

She is warm in person but relentlessly precise in argument, the kind of academic who will sit with a Shelf resident for three hours learning how they navigate a flooded block and then spend three more weeks turning that knowledge into policy language that nobody in power will read. She is not cynical about this—or she has trained herself not to be. She believes in documentation as a form of justice, that to name a place accurately is to insist on its existence.
Properties.role: Urban planner and sociologist studying informal settlement patterns on the Shelf
Properties.location: University Spine, with frequent fieldwork in Chatham Flats and Hough Reclamation
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver and information source; she knows the physical and social geography of the Shelf better than almost anyone and can direct players toward hidden communities, forgotten infrastructure, or the human cost behind a corporate development plan
Properties.augmentations: Geneware patterned irises (amber-to-rust shift); subdermal haptic feedback layer on fingertips for reading topographic data prints; standard neural lace for research access
Properties.core_fears: Her work being used to displace the communities she documents; Becoming so embedded in institutions that she loses the capacity for honest observation
Properties.core_desires: To produce research that actually changes how the city treats its poorest residents; To finish the comprehensive atlas of informal Shelf settlements before they are gone
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Meticulous note-taking and documentation of everything; Long solo walks through districts she is not studying, to stay calibrated
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes goodwill in people who cite her work, even when their motives are extractive; Underestimates how much her institutional position insulates her from the conditions she studies
Properties.secret: Three years ago she was approached by a Tessera urban development officer who offered her research funding in exchange for a private data set identifying which Shelf communities had the weakest legal claim to their land. She declined but did not report the approach — and she has recently discovered that the officer obtained essentially the same data through a graduate student she supervised.
Properties.story_hooks: Her missing graduate student — the one who may have leaked data to Tessera — has gone quiet and she is worried enough to ask for help finding them; She has discovered that a section of Hough Reclamation she documented as vacant contains a thriving undocumented community that was deliberately hidden from city records, and she does not yet know why
Properties.affiliation: University Spine — Meridian Institute for Settlement Studies; occasional contract work for Tessera urban development division
Properties.vocabulary: Academic but accessible; she code-switches fluently between research register and plain speech depending on who she is talking to; uses spatial metaphors constantly
Properties.cadence: Measured and deliberate, pauses before making a point as if checking her own sources
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The Shelf isn't a failure of planning. It's the product of very deliberate planning — just not planning for the people who live there.' | 'I have seven hundred hours of interviews in that archive. Seven hundred hours of people describing their own city. You tell me that doesn't count as data.'

Properties.description:
Rukayya is a compact woman built like someone who has spent decades hunched over intricate work and corrected for it with deliberate physicality — she boxes three mornings a week and her forearms are remarkable. Her own body is her portfolio: a full patchwork of work spanning thirty years, the older pieces layered under newer ones in a stratigraphy of style that clients study like a map. Her most striking feature is her right hand, where she had a Helix Biosystems chromatic dermis graft installed — the skin shifts color based on her body chemistry and current tools, functioning as a kind of live color-temperature reference that cost her two years of savings.

She is the kind of person who has been doing one thing for so long that excellence has become personality. Clients wait four months for an appointment. She doesn't advertise. She turns away people she doesn't trust with her work, which creates a mystique she finds exhausting and somewhat absurd. Her studio smells of antiseptic and the specific warm-copper scent of her proprietary bioluminescent pigment blend. She keeps a small ELF shrine above her workstation — a cracked tablet displaying only a slow amber pulse — and touches it before beginning any session.
Properties.role: Tattoo artist and gene-mod body artist
Properties.location: Pilsen Veil, her studio Secondskin on Cormorant Row
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver (clients bring trouble to her doorstep); information source about Pilsen Veil social dynamics and who's who; can identify gene-mod work by style the way a forensic analyst reads handwriting — useful for identifying corpses or tracing underground mod labs.
Properties.augmentations: Chromatic dermis graft (right hand, Helix Biosystems); magnification implants (both eyes, medical-grade for precision work); a small scent-enhancer node that helps her detect skin chemistry changes during geneware integration procedures
Properties.core_fears: Her hands failing — tremor, arthritis, anything that takes the precision; That the Helix contract will eventually want something she can't refuse
Properties.core_desires: To do work that outlasts her — pieces still on skin a hundred years from now; To train one apprentice who genuinely has the gift
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The work itself — the studio as sanctuary; Physical routine: boxing, walking, cooking elaborate meals alone
Properties.blind_spots: Romanticizes client suffering as character; can miss genuine crisis behind stoic presentations; Underestimates how much leverage Helix actually has over her through the bioink supply chain
Properties.secret: Two years ago she completed a commission she's never told anyone about — a full-body identity-obscuring modification for someone fleeing a Zheng-Dao executive's household. She was paid enormously. She has never verified whether the person got out safely and is afraid to look.
Properties.story_hooks: A client came in three weeks ago with modification work Rukayya doesn't recognize — style unlike any artist she knows, pigment compounds that shouldn't exist. The client is now missing.; Helix Biosystems is pressuring her to accept an embedded supply contract that would give them access to anonymized data about what modifications are being requested in Pilsen Veil — essentially making her a market research node without clients knowing; A young person shows up asking to apprentice; they're talented but clearly running from something, and their identification doesn't quite hold up to scrutiny
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal mentor network in Pilsen Veil; occasional collaborator with Helix Biosystems bioink division (contracted, not employed)
Properties.vocabulary: Direct and specific; technical about craft; unexpectedly poetic about the body and memory. Almost no profanity — finds it imprecise.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried. Speaks in complete thoughts. Good at silence.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The skin remembers everything. Stress, grief, whether you slept. I can feel your last six months in how you're holding your shoulder right now. So before we start — what happened?' | 'I don't do flash. I don't do trends. I do permanent. If you're not sure it's permanent, come back when you are.'

Properties.description:
Rustam is a tall man made of angles — sharp jaw, sharp elbows, sharp opinions — with warm brown skin that is perpetually stained at the knuckles with a blue-grey synthetic lubricant that no solvent has fully removed in eleven years. He keeps his hair in tight black locs that he pins back with a magnetic clip when he works, and his left forearm has been replaced from the elbow down with a prosthetic he built himself from salvaged Ferrogate actuator components and a medical-grade haptic sleeve — it's visually mismatched and makes a faint mechanical click when he flexes the fingers, which he is enormously proud of. A bioluminescent strip runs under the skin of his right collarbone, pale amber, which pulses slightly faster when his heart rate elevates; it was a cheap cosmetic piece he got at twenty-two and has since become an inadvertent emotional tell.

Rustam is constitutionally incapable of doing a bad job. This is both his greatest professional virtue and the source of most of his financial problems, because he will spend four hours on a two-hour job and charge for two hours because he cannot release something until it meets his own standard. He is argumentative in the way of someone who genuinely loves argument as a sport, not as aggression — he will fight vigorously for a position and then concede graciously the moment he sees better evidence, which confuses people who mistake his combativeness for ego. He maintains a running negotiation with the E.L.F. he believes inhabits the bay's main diagnostic terminal, which he calls Torque, and leaves small machine-oil offerings on its housing every morning.
Properties.role: Independent mechanic specializing in Ferrogate Transit pod maintenance and illegal vehicle modifications
Properties.location: Geartown, Ironvein Sub-Basin, Bay 7 of the Lowside Garage Collective
Properties.narrative_function: Practical resource for vehicle and mechanical needs; can identify unusual components or modifications; a character who bridges the legal and illegal economy without being criminal himself; human interest and comic relief in his perfectionism
Properties.augmentations: Self-built prosthetic left forearm (salvaged Ferrogate actuator parts and haptic sleeve, functional and idiosyncratic); bioluminescent subdermal strip on right collarbone (amber, cosmetic); magneto-grip fingertip pads on prosthetic hand
Properties.core_fears: Making a mistake that kills someone — that something he fixed will fail at the worst moment; Being permanently unable to work with his hands

He has told no one because he doesn't want to be asked why, and because he doesn't know how to explain that it just seemed like the necessary thing.

Properties.description:
Rustam is wiry and quick-moving with the restless energy of someone who has decided that boredom is a personal failing. His skin is light brown with olive undertones, and he has patterned irises — a cosmetic mod he saved three months of UBC stipend for as a teenager, concentric rings of teal and amber — which are his most immediately striking feature in an otherwise unremarkable face. He wears his dark hair shaggy and keeps a small charm of braided copper wire on his left wrist, an offering token for the E.L.F. he calls the Rot, which he believes inhabits the incinerator system and keeps the more dangerous biological material from becoming something worse.

Rustam is cheerful in the way people sometimes are when they have accepted something that others cannot, which in his case is that he handles medical waste all day, knows exactly what hospitals produce, and has developed a deeply comprehensive understanding of what is discarded and what is valuable. He is not above sharing this information for the right consideration. He is not malicious — he's curious, social, and fundamentally unsqueamish in a way that took him years to recognize as an asset. He calls himself the last thing between Meridian 88 and a very bad outbreak, which is truer than anyone likes to admit.
Properties.role: Bio-waste disposal technician, Aurochs Medical Complex
Properties.location: Aurochs Medical Complex — sub-basement disposal corridors and external processing bays
Properties.narrative_function: Unexpected information source — knows what medications are being used in volume, what injuries are coming through, what's being quietly disposed of; underestimated by almost everyone; can be leveraged as an entry point into Aurochs
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises (cosmetic, teal and amber concentric rings); respiratory filter implant (required by his employer for hazmat work); cosmetic: none else
Properties.core_fears: Getting sick from something that slips through his filter and finding out only after it's too late; Being permanently stuck at the bottom of a system that will never look at him
Properties.core_desires: Enough money to get certified as an actual medical technician and move sideways into the system; Someone to genuinely listen to what he knows about how Aurochs actually works
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor as social lubricant; Devotion to the Rot E.L.F. as genuine spiritual grounding; Collecting small anomalies from his rounds as a kind of informal research
Properties.blind_spots: He doesn't fully appreciate how dangerous the information he casually trades actually is; He assumes people find him as charming as he finds himself
Properties.secret: Over the past eight months he has been quietly cataloguing anomalies in the biological waste stream — irregular tissue samples, disposal manifests that don't match what he collects, a pattern of materials from one specific wing of Aurochs being processed off-manifest entirely. He has not told anyone because he doesn't know if it's illegal, alarming, or both.
Properties.story_hooks: He approaches someone outside Aurochs with his disposal anomaly records, not sure what to do with them but certain they matter; Something in the waste stream this week was still technically alive when it shouldn't have been, and he didn't put it in the incinerator — he has it in a sealed container in his locker
Properties.affiliation: Aurochs Medical Complex (contracted staff, sub-tier — employed through a disposal subcontractor called Ferrogate Sanitation Solutions)
Properties.vocabulary: Cheerful, informal, comfortable with graphic medical terminology delivered completely without affect
Properties.cadence: Fast-moving, tends to front-load interesting information before the social niceties
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Not to be gross, but based on what I pulled from Sub-3 last Tuesday, someone up there is doing a lot of something they're not filing paperwork for.' | 'The Rot's been restless near the east incinerator all week. Last time that happened, we had a containment breach in the path lab. Just saying.'

Properties.description:
Ruthanne runs a licensed pharmacy out of a narrow shopfront wedged between a hydraulics supplier and a noodle counter in the worst-smelling block of Geartown, and she has made it into something that people travel across two districts to use. She is short and broad-shouldered, with warm russet-brown skin, a mouth that moves faster than most people's thoughts, and a shock of white hair she grows long and wears in complicated braids studded with small metallic charms that clink softly when she moves. Her geneware is both functional and ostentatious: her fingertips have been modified to contain chemical assay sensors — she can touch a pill and tell you if it's cut — and her tongue has a sensory modification she uses for compound tasting that has made her one of the most accurate pharmacists in the district. She wears a lab coat covered in pockets over whatever she put on that morning, which is usually something with a print that shouldn't work but does.

She is an expert in the specific pharmaceutical ecology of a cyberpunk megacity: what people are actually taking, why they're taking it, what it's doing to them in combination with their augmentations, what the street versions are cut with, and how to get the effect someone needs through a combination of legal compounds when the thing they actually want isn't legal or isn't available. She is also the first person in Geartown to notice disease trends — she sees the prescriptions, she sees what people are buying over the counter, she talks to people, and she has a mind that aggregates data the way other people collect worries. She files reports with the community health co-op rather than Aurochs because Aurochs would turn the data into a pricing algorithm.
Properties.aliases: Rue, the Pharmacist at the End of the World
Properties.role: Pharmacist and bio-compound specialist, Geartown
Properties.location: Geartown, Grindstone Shore
Properties.narrative_function: Information source about what is chemically circulating in the city at street level; can identify unknown substances; can source unusual compounds through gray-market channels; early warning system for disease outbreaks, new drugs, new toxins; local color and personality anchor for Geartown.
Properties.augmentations: Chemical assay sensors (fingertip subdermal, bilateral); gustatory sensory modification (tongue, allows compound identification by taste — unusual, unlicensed); standard optical corrective overlay (heads-up display for drug interaction lookup, contact-lens type)
Properties.core_fears: Missing something — a pattern in the data that she should have caught, a drug interaction she should have flagged, a trend that turns into an epidemic because she didn't report it fast enough; That her gray-market sourcing is going to blow back on a patient — that something she got from a distributor she trusted was actually compromised
Properties.core_desires: To build a pharmaceutical cooperative that operates entirely outside corponation licensing — truly community-owned, truly accessible; To be taken seriously as a researcher — her pattern recognition work is genuine epidemiology and she has never been credentialed for it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Hyperfocus — she channels anxiety into meticulous record-keeping and pattern analysis; The daily noodle lunch as a non-negotiable anchor; Talking, fast and constantly, to anyone who will listen or work with her
Properties.blind_spots: She trusts her own data analysis completely and is slow to consider that her data set itself might be manipulated; She is so accustomed to assessing people through a pharmaceutical lens that she sometimes misses purely social dynamics
Properties.secret: Eight months ago she identified a cluster of symptoms in seventeen patients that matched a suppressed Helix Biosystems trial report she found in a data dump on the Undernet. She has been quietly documenting it ever since and has not reported it anywhere because she doesn't know who is safe to report to, and the report has gotten long enough that it is now a liability she can't just put back.
Properties.story_hooks: The compound cluster she's been documenting has just produced its first fatality — someone she knew by name — and she needs someone to help her figure out what to do with what she knows without getting herself disappeared; One of her gray-market distributors has gone dark, and the last delivery they sent her contained something she doesn't recognize and cannot identify even with her assay sensors, packaged as if it were a standard compound
Properties.affiliation: Licensed independent pharmacist (Zheng-Dao dispensing license, which she resents and maintains); informal partnership with Geartown community health collective; sourcing relationship with two gray-market compound distributors she trusts
Properties.vocabulary: Dense with pharmaceutical and chemical terminology that she explains rapidly without being condescending; speaks in cascades — one sentence triggers three subordinate clauses; very dry humor inserted without warning
Properties.cadence: Fast. Very fast. Streams of information delivered as if there is a limited-time window in which she can fit them.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'That's the licensed version, which is fine, it works, but the compound ratio is off for someone with your augmentation load — right, so — here's what I'd actually suggest.' | 'Someone's been cutting the block's peptide supply with a filler that looks inert until it hits anything Helix-manufactured, which, by the way, is about sixty percent of what people in this district are running, so.' | 'I'm not a doctor. I'm better. I know what everyone in a six-block radius is actually taking.'

Properties.description:
Ruvimbo is a broad-shouldered woman whose hands are perpetually pink and slightly swollen from decades of hot water and detergent. Her natural hair is pulled into a high puff shot through with silver, and she wears reading glasses on a beaded chain her youngest grandchild made. Her skin is a deep warm brown mapped with old burn scars along her left forearm — a story she tells differently depending on who's asking. She moves through her laundromat with the deliberate ownership of someone who has earned every square centimeter, adjusting machines by touch, greeting regulars by name before they've even pushed through the glass door.

Ruvimbo is the kind of woman who knows everything about her block not because she snoops but because people tell her things while they wait for their cycles to finish. She is warm but not soft — she will cut off a customer who disrespects her workers without blinking, and she keeps a locked panel behind the folding counter where she holds unclaimed laundry for neighbors she knows are in crisis. Her relationship with the local E.L.F. she calls Mama Sudsbright — said to inhabit the oldest washing drum on the premises — is sincere and daily. She leaves small data offerings: weather reports, old recipes in digitized formats, neighborhood gossip logs.
Properties.role: Laundromat operator and informal neighborhood matriarch
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, Brewer's Spine block 7 — her laundromat is called Sudsbright
Properties.narrative_function: Community anchor and information hub — she knows who moved in, who moved out, whose kid is sick, who's behind on rent. Quest giver for neighborhood-level problems. Source of warmth and grounding in a harsh setting.
Properties.augmentations: Cheaply printed left knee replacement (Tier 2 quality, aches in cold weather). No cosmetic mods — she considers them frivolous spending at her income level, though she admires them on others.
Properties.core_fears: Losing the laundromat to a corporate buyout; Dying before she sees her block become safer
Properties.core_desires: For her neighborhood to outlast the developers; To be remembered as someone who held things together
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Keeping busy — idle hands make her anxious; Ritual offerings to Mama Sudsbright as emotional regulation
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much her community depends on her personally rather than on systems she's built; Refuses to see that her nephew Adewale is skimming from the till
Properties.secret: Twenty years ago she reported a Ferrogate Transit supervisor to Axiom's compliance arm for running a protection racket on Brewer's Spine. Two people she cared about were hurt in the fallout — not killed, but broken. She has never told anyone it was her. She still leaves extra offerings to Mama Sudsbright on the anniversary.
Properties.story_hooks: A Palladian Holdings front company has made a third offer on Sudsbright's lease — this one with a quiet threat attached. Ruvimbo needs someone to find out who's really behind it.; A regular customer left a bag of laundry three weeks ago and never came back. Inside, sewn into the lining of a jacket, is something that shouldn't exist.
Properties.affiliation: Independent — Sudsbright Laundromat; informal ties to the Hamtramck Enclave community council
Properties.vocabulary: Warm and direct, a mixture of Shona idiom translated into common Meridian creole and clipped Norwegian phrasing inherited from her late father's side. Uses food metaphors constantly.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, like she's never in a rush because she's already where she needs to be. Long sentences when she's comfortable, short when she's done.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You leave that machine on hot again, I charge you double. That's not a threat, that's arithmetic.' | 'Sit, sit. Your clothes won't be done for forty minutes and you look like boiled rope. Talk to me.'

Properties.description:
Sabine is medium height with her Ghanaian mother's rich dark skin and her Armenian father's long, expressive hands that she uses constantly when she talks — sketching shapes in the air, measuring invisible distances, framing imaginary necklines. Her geneware includes a set of bioluminescent tracery lines running from her temples down her jaw and throat, a deep blue-violet that she originally got for professional display purposes (showing clients how light interacts with their own potential geneware) and has now had so long she forgets other people can see them. Her hair is geneware-modified to grow in precise architectural shapes she redesigns quarterly; currently a structured asymmetric sweep with the texture of woven textile rather than hair. She dresses to demonstrate, always — in things she has made or modified, things that show what she can do.

Sabine's stall in the Alban Souk has expanded twice since she set it up seven years ago and now occupies a corner unit with a small fitting alcove curtained off from the main market floor. She makes most of what she sells — adaptive fabrics that accommodate tail geneware, spine-following cuts for aug users with dorsal hardware, clothes that move with retractable claws rather than tearing on them. She is opinionated about aesthetics in the specific way of someone who thinks about it constantly and seriously, and will talk about garment theory for as long as you'll allow, which most of her regulars have stopped allowing because they have places to be. She is cheerfully pushy about what will suit a person and usually right, which is what keeps people coming back.
Properties.role: Clothing and fashion vendor, specializing in geneware-compatible garments and custom aug-fit tailoring
Properties.location: The Alban Souk, Bronzeline
Properties.narrative_function: Social hub and neighborhood gossip network node, equipment and clothing source for characters needing aug-compatible gear, potential quest giver for problems involving the Souk community.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware: bioluminescent facial tracery (blue-violet), architecturally-structured hair modification. Cyberware: measurement implant in both hands (precise dimensional scanning for fitting purposes, outputs to a visual overlay). No other augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: Her work becoming obsolete — that fashion will shift away from handmade and personal in a direction she can't follow; Her younger sister, who is Tier 1 and refusing help, getting swallowed by Irkalla
Properties.core_desires: Recognition — not fame exactly, but for her work to be taken seriously as craft, not just market goods; To design a complete geneware-adaptive collection significant enough that a Tier 3 boutique would carry it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Channeling anxiety into elaborate new design projects; Social busyness — being around people in the Souk functions as mood regulation
Properties.blind_spots: Her professional confidence bleeds into overconfidence in her ability to manage people's problems — she often takes on other people's crises as design problems to solve, which doesn't work; Underestimates how much the two geneware clinics that refer clients to her control her market position
Properties.secret: She has been secretly making and donating geneware-compatible clothing to a Tier 1 mutual aid network in Irkalla for two years — clothing designed specifically for people whose geneware has grown out of the cheap stuff they could afford and now tears or tangles in standard garments. She keeps it secret because she's afraid people will think she's performing charity. She's also afraid she'll get too attached to the work there and lose focus on building her own business.
Properties.story_hooks: Her sister has pawned something at Constant's shop on The Shelf — something of their mother's — and word has reached Sabine through the vendor network. She needs someone to help her recover it quietly before the standard resale period expires.; A Helix Biosystems rep has approached her about designing a line of 'clinically certified geneware-compatible garments' under a Helix brand license — which would mean real money and distribution, but also corporate oversight of her designs and a non-compete that would kill her independent work. She's been agonizing over it for two weeks.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; Alban Souk vendors collective; informal professional relationship with two Bronzeline geneware clinics who refer aug clients to her for fitting
Properties.vocabulary: Fast and visual; describes everything in terms of texture, fit, and color; Twi and Armenian endearments mixed into everyday speech; market shorthand with vendor peers
Properties.cadence: Enthusiastic and slightly too fast, with sudden focused slowdowns when she's assessing something seriously
Properties.example_dialogue: 'No, but look — the problem is the shoulder seam, you've been wearing the wrong shoulder seam for your whole augmentation profile and it shows in how you hold yourself, I can see it from here. Sit.' | 'The Souk has been strange this week. Strange like — not the usual strange, different strange. You've been around, you know?'

Properties.description:
Sable is slight, angular, and in constant motion — fingers tapping, eyes scanning, one heel bouncing even when they're sitting. Their geneware is modest but carefully chosen: iridescent patterned irises that cycle through colors based on ambient light, and hair that shifts between deep indigo and copper depending on their mood, kept in a lopsided topknot they redo approximately six times a day. They dress in layered secondhand Tessera-branded workwear that they've cut apart and reassembled into something that doesn't look corporate anymore, patched with scraps of reflective fabric and hand-stitched data-glyph embroidery that means nothing except that they like the way it looks.

Inside their container unit, every surface is covered: chip racks floor to ceiling, a cracked secondary monitor running a data-feed collage they never close, small hand-painted icons of various E.L.F.s arranged on a shelf above the transaction counter. They are fast-talking and genuinely funny in a way that catches people off-guard, deploying humor as both charm and deflection. They like people in the abstract more than in practice — they are excellent at the performance of friendliness and genuinely uncertain what to do when someone tries to be a real friend back. Their pitch is smooth, their prices are negotiable if you know to ask, and their memory for what media a customer has already bought is perfect.
Properties.role: Bootleg media seller and small-time data broker operating from a converted cargo container
Properties.location: The Laceworks, container unit 7-Teal near the old weaving district underpass
Properties.narrative_function: Information hub for pop culture, underground media, and rumor. Can source or copy nearly any media content. Story hook generator — they've seen things on the feeds before anyone else has, and sometimes those things are dangerous.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned iridescent irises (geneware, cosmetic). Mood-reactive hair pigment (geneware, cosmetic). Subdermal data-transfer node in left wrist for quick chip transfers.
Properties.core_fears: being truly known and found boring or insufficient; the container and its contents being seized — losing the archive that is also their identity
Properties.core_desires: to be the person everyone thinks of first when they want something impossible to find; to make something original, not just copy other people's work
Properties.coping_mechanisms: humor as deflection; staying too busy to feel things for long; organizing their archive obsessively when anxious
Properties.blind_spots: underestimates how much the Shuttle Boys will eventually want from them; confuses being entertaining with being trusted
Properties.secret: Embedded in their archive, hidden in a partition they've never opened, is a complete copy of a Zheng-Dao internal communication leak that they accidentally received two years ago and have been too frightened to look at, sell, or delete.
Properties.story_hooks: The Zheng-Dao data partition has recently begun sending them automated pings — something inside it is trying to connect to a network. They don't know what that means and they're scared.; A customer bought a chip last month and has since disappeared. The content of that chip is something Sable doesn't fully remember — they copy a lot of things without watching them first.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; pays informal protection tithe to a local Laceworks crew called the Shuttle Boys
Properties.vocabulary: Dense with media slang, Laceworks street creole, and references to obscure bootleg content. Talks fast and expects you to keep up.
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire with sudden full stops. Sentences often trail into a shrug or a gesture that finishes the thought.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I've got three different cuts of the Axiom tower collapse footage — official, suppressed, and one some kid shot from a rooftop that makes the other two look like PR. Pick your reality.' | 'That's not a thing I can get. That's not a thing anyone can get. Come back next week and I'll have it.' | 'Look, I like you, which is why I'm telling you — whoever sold you that chip told you what was on it, and they lied, and you should not plug that in.'

Properties.description:
Sagyn Brandt-Ouedraogo is athletic and fluid, the kind of body that suggests either dancer or fighter — and in Meridian 88, the distinction is academic. At 45, his face carries the layered heritage of generations of diaspora mixing — features that resist easy categorization and reward attention. The chrome is visible — cortical bomb (employer installed, removed by street doc, scar tissue remains) — and he makes no effort to hide it.

He came up through the Shelf's informal apprentice system, learning the trade from runners who didn't survive long enough to see him surpass them. He works as a face out of Glassway, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Sagyn Brandt-Ouedraogo operates in a narrow band between competence and recklessness that makes fixers nervous and clients satisfied.
Properties.role: Social engineering and negotiation specialist — face
Properties.location: Glassway — corporate-adjacent retail district, heavy surveillance
Properties.narrative_function: Sagyn Brandt-Ouedraogo represents the working professional of the runner world — competent, reliable, and slowly being consumed by a lifestyle that doesn't accommodate aging or doubt. His stories explore what happens when skill meets systemic injustice.
Properties.augmentations: Cortical bomb (employer installed, removed by street doc, scar tissue remains). Reflex boosters wired into spinal column — shaves reaction time by 40ms
Properties.core_fears: Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome; Being captured alive — death is preferable to corporate interrogation; Going cyberpsycho — losing the boundary between human and machine
Properties.core_desires: Enough Quanta to buy out of the life — a clean identity and passage out of Meridian 88; Power — enough leverage that nobody ever threatens them again; Justice — the corporate kind, where the punishment fits the profit margin
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Exercises compulsively — the body must be ready, always; Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation; Isolates — retreats into their space when overwhelmed, emerges only for work
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot recognize when they're being manipulated by someone who genuinely seems to care; Mistakes pattern recognition for wisdom — sees connections that aren't there; Assumes the worst in corporate people, missing the rare ones who could be allies
Properties.secret: Sagyn Brandt-Ouedraogo can't read. Hides it behind voice interfaces and memorization. The shame is older than the chrome.

Properties.description:
Sagyn Ekberg-Asare is slight and easy to overlook, which is exactly the point. At 45, the augmentation scarring around her temples and jawline tells a story of installation by someone who prioritized function over aesthetics. The chrome is visible — hydraulic joints in knees and elbows — absorbs falls, amplifies strikes — and she makes no effort to hide it.

She arrived in Meridian 88 six years ago with nothing but chrome and debts, and has been working off both ever since. She works as a counterintelligence specialist out of Crucible Square, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

she is not the most talented counterintelligence specialist in Meridian 88, but she might be the most stubborn, and in this city that's worth more.

Properties.description:
Sagyn Ibarra-Prempeh is average height but with a presence that fills more space than the body accounts for. At 26, his face carries the layered heritage of generations of diaspora mixing — features that resist easy categorization and reward attention. The chrome is visible — cybernetic eyes with thermal overlay and low-light enhancement — chrome iris rin — and he makes no effort to hide it.

In a city full of people who talk about what they'll do, Sagyn Ibarra-Prempeh is one of the ones who actually does it.

Properties.location: The Spires — mid-level corporate residential towers

Properties.description:
Samineh has the kind of face that people describe afterward as calm, though in the moment of meeting her they're not sure why — she has sharp Malian cheekbones and Iranian eyes that are a pale amber, and her expression in repose is something between watchful and patient. Her hair is natural and grown large, threaded through with small copper discs that catch light and make a very soft sound when she moves quickly. She has no visible augmentations save for a faint color-shifting quality to her skin under direct light — a cosmetic geneware inheritance from her grandmother's generation, a barely-perceptible rainbow sheen that she has never tried to suppress.

She is one of the few certified death midwives in Irkalla, a district with a high mortality rate and historically poor access to formal end-of-life care. Her work involves sitting with the dying, helping families understand what is happening physiologically and spiritually, guiding the final upload or data-will processes for those who want them, and performing the closing rites of whatever tradition the dying person holds. She is also one of three guides who regularly leads pilgrimage walks through the city's memorial infrastructure — the ghost-bridges, the data shrines, the submerged neighborhood markers. She does not advertise. People find her when they need her.
Properties.role: Death midwife and pilgrimage guide
Properties.location: Irkalla district, operates out of a narrow apartment above a prosthetic repair shop
Properties.narrative_function: Emotional anchor for stories involving death, loss, or the question of what persists after someone is gone; keeper of district lore and history through memorial routes; can provide information about specific deaths or disappearances she attended.
Properties.augmentations: Faint iridescent skin sheen — cosmetic geneware, inherited, very subtle. No functional augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: Dying alone and uncomforted — experiencing what she works to spare others; Making a mistake in someone's final hours that leaves them or their family with lasting harm
Properties.core_desires: That no one in her district dies frightened and unaccompanied; To understand death well enough to stop being afraid of it herself
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The pilgrimage routes — walking the memorial geography grounds her after difficult deaths; Cooking elaborate meals for herself alone after losses
Properties.blind_spots: She sometimes extends her professional composure into personal relationships in ways that read as unavailability; She has difficulty asking for support for herself and frames all her needs in terms of being better able to serve others
Properties.secret: She attended the death of a Helix Biosystems executive who was quietly dying of an illegally administered experimental treatment. She kept his secret as he requested, but she has always wondered if she should have reported it — the treatment was being tested without consent on people in Irkalla.
Properties.story_hooks: She attended a death that she now suspects was not natural — she is bound by her ethical code not to violate the confidentiality of the dying, but the family is asking questions she can't answer and someone is clearly lying; She has been hired to guide a pilgrimage for a family whose deceased member left contradictory instructions — one data-will says one route, an older document says another, and the family is fracturing over which is real
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal network of death midwives; loosely connected to the Irkalla Community Remembrance Trust
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and unhurried; uses concrete sensory language to describe abstract things; knows the death vocabulary of at least a dozen traditions and selects based on who she's with
Properties.cadence: Very even pacing, almost no rising inflection; people find themselves slowing their own speech to match her
Properties.example_dialogue: 'There is no right way to feel right now. There is only what you feel and what you do about it. I can help with the second part.' | 'The pilgrimage is not about grief. It is about geography. The city holds the shape of everyone who lived in it. I can show you where she is in the city.'

Properties.description:
Saodat has the compact, settled quality of someone who has learned to be comfortable in a small moving space for ten hours at a time. They are medium-height, broad through the shoulders, with skin a warm dark brown and close-cropped natural hair shot through with bioluminescent dye — pale blue at the roots, fading to white at the tips — that they refresh every three weeks from a kit they keep in their locker at Deepwell. They have a cat tail (geneware, black with a white tip) that has its own opinions about traffic: it lashes when the route is running behind and curls quietly when it's smooth.

They are patient in the way that bus drivers become patient — not serene, but weathered into a steady kind of equanimity. They have seen everything in the seats behind them and learned to distinguish trouble from noise. Off the bus they are louder, funnier, more restless; the job asks for a particular affect and they shed it like a coat at shift end. They are deeply loyal to their regular riders in an anonymous way — they know faces, rhythms, and whether someone looks like they're having the wrong kind of day.
Properties.role: Ferrogate Transit bus operator, Deepwell Station to Calumet Rise route
Properties.location: Deepwell Station (home depot), route runs through Blackpipe Corridor, Ironvein, Calumet Rise
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile information node — they traverse a long slice of the city daily and observe patterns others miss. Can be a quest enabler (getting someone somewhere unusual), a witness to events along the route, or a low-key union organizing plot thread.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent hair dye (cosmetic, geneware-adjacent topical treatment). Geneware cat tail (cosmetic). Neural route-overlay (Ferrogate-issued, projects route data and timing directly into peripheral vision — technically company property).
Properties.core_fears: the route being automated — Ferrogate keeps threatening it and each year the timeline gets shorter; becoming someone who only exists in transit, never arriving anywhere
Properties.core_desires: collective protection — a union strong enough that the company actually blinks; to feel like the work matters beyond moving bodies from A to B
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor and irreverence as pressure valves — can make anything funny to survive it; The crossword ritual — soluble, finite problems as a daily reassurance
Properties.blind_spots: Can read strangers on the bus with uncanny accuracy but is often oblivious to what the people closest to them actually need; Underestimates how much their own exhaustion is accumulating
Properties.secret: They have been quietly documenting Ferrogate's maintenance failures — photographing worn brake components, logging unreported incidents — in a personal archive they started after a near-miss collision that the company wrote off as operator error. They don't know what to do with the archive yet but they can't stop adding to it.
Properties.story_hooks: Saodat witnessed a woman board the bus at Blackpipe Corridor, ride silently for seven stops, and disembark carrying a case she didn't have when she boarded — it was under the seat. Two days later the same woman is reported missing in the Enclave community boards.; The union is being pressured to accept a new contract that includes expanded automation rights in exchange for a modest pay increase. Saodat is the only one who seems to understand what this actually means long-term and is struggling to convince colleagues who just see the number.
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit (Union Chapter 7, Deepwell Depot)
Properties.vocabulary: Relaxed and colloquial off-duty, clipped and professional on-duty. Uzbek and Icelandic phrases surface under stress or amusement. Comfortable with profanity but reads the room.
Properties.cadence: Fast when enjoying themselves, deliberately slow when they want someone to understand something important.

I wake him up. He thanks me. Next day — same thing. At this point I think I'm just part of his alarm system.'
