Properties.description:
Saodat is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin mapped by decades of steam and spice smoke, her silver-streaked hair pinned under a faded yellow wrap she's worn so long it's become her trademark. Her left forearm is wrapped in a sleeve tattoo of a pepper vine that flowers whenever her skin temperature rises — a cheap bioink mod she got thirty years ago and has never seen reason to remove. She smells perpetually of fenugreek and charred chili, and her stall, a converted cargo container with a fold-out serving ledge, has been in the same spot in the Oxidian Market for twenty-two years. She speaks with the authority of a woman who has fed half of Geartown from infancy to old age.

Saodat is warmly domineering — she will decide what you are eating today, and you will thank her for it. She has strong opinions about everything from Zheng-Dao's latest transit fare hikes to which of her regulars is making poor romantic choices. Her memory for names, faces, and dietary restrictions is near-perfect, and she uses it like a gift. Beneath the maternal bluster is a woman who survived the displacement of Ironvein's old residential blocks twenty years ago and rebuilt her life around a single wok and a secondhand gas line.
Properties.role: Food stall operator, Oxidian Market
Properties.location: The Oxidian Market, Geartown
Properties.narrative_function: Community anchor and information hub — she knows everyone in Geartown by face if not name. Quest giver for neighborhood-level problems, emotional support NPC, rumor source with high reliability on local matters.
Properties.augmentations: Bioink tattoo sleeve (decorative, thermochromic). Reading lens implant in right eye for menus and pricing. No other augmentation.
Properties.core_fears: Being forced to leave her stall the way she was forced from Ironvein; Becoming irrelevant to the neighborhood she built herself into
Properties.core_desires: To ensure no one on her block goes hungry; To see the Vendors Guild gain formal legal recognition from the city council
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cooking as meditation; Transforming anxiety into productivity; Adopting strays — human and otherwise
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes her judgment about people is infallible; Underestimates how much she relies on the community for her own emotional stability
Properties.secret: She has been quietly subsidizing three families' rent for over a decade by skimming from her own Guild dues, and she keeps their names in a coded ledger she calls her 'recipe book.' She would be humiliated if anyone found out — not because it was wrong, but because she needs to be the one giving, not seen giving.
Properties.story_hooks: A Ferrogate Transit rezoning notice has appeared on her stall wall — her block is slated for 'infrastructure renewal' and she has eight weeks to vacate. She needs someone to dig up who actually filed the order.; One of her long-term subsidized families has gone silent. She's too proud to call it missing persons but she is frightened and wants someone discreet to check on them.

Properties.vocabulary: Direct, warm, slightly formal Uzbek-inflected sentence structures blended with Geartown slang. Uses food metaphors constantly.
Properties.cadence: Steady and unhurried, like someone who has never needed to rush to make a point.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Sit. I already know what you need and it is not what you think you came here for.' | 'The Guild is not politics. The Guild is us deciding we exist on purpose.'

Properties.description:
Saodat is the kind of person you notice and immediately forget, which is the point. Medium height, medium build, features that read as generically pleasant — warm light-brown skin, dark eyes, hair that is currently an unremarkable chin-length black but was a different color last week and will be again next week. They have a cosmetic geneware mod that lets them adjust their hair color through a dermal panel on the back of their neck, and they use it strategically to match moods, blend into crowds, or signal to regular clients what kind of day it is (black means business, dark red means they're watching, deep green means come back later). The only consistent physical detail is a small tattoo of an open eye on the inside of their left wrist, which they cover when working.

Their stall front is officially a document services and notarization kiosk — perfectly legal, mildly boring, doing a modest but real trade in legitimate bureaucratic services for the enclave's large population of people whose papers are perpetually in some state of incompleteness. The back half of the business happens in a rented room above a noodle shop forty meters away, which they visit by a route they vary daily. They are calm, precise, and give off a faint air of someone taking a very long test that never ends.
Properties.role: Fake ID vendor and identity documents forger — The Alban Souk
Properties.location: The Alban Souk, Hamtramck Enclave
Properties.narrative_function: Procurement contact for false identities and documentation; information broker adjacent — they know who in the enclave is trying to become someone else, and why.
Properties.augmentations: Color-shift hair geneware (cosmetic, strategic). Subdermal microfabricator array in dominant hand (functional — allows high-precision document printing without external equipment).
Properties.core_fears: Being fully known by anyone — the loss of the buffer between self and world; That one day they will forget who they actually are beneath all the constructed faces
Properties.core_desires: To build one identity — their own — that feels true and unreachable by anyone who wants to use or erase it; Financial stability enough to stop taking high-risk clients
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Maintaining obsessive operational routines as a substitute for emotional structure; Collecting small objects from each significant client as a private archive they don't examine too closely; Hair color changes as mood regulation
Properties.blind_spots: Has told themselves their work is purely transactional so many times they've stopped asking what happens to the people they give new faces to; Trusts systems and routines more than people, which means they are completely unprepared for system failures
Properties.secret: They built and maintain a fully functional identity for a person who doesn't exist — complete biometric trail, employment history, credit record, social profile — and they use it to live parts of their life that they want kept separate from everything else, including their own name.
Properties.story_hooks: A client from six months ago has resurfaced — not the person they built the identity for, but someone using it who has no idea where it came from, which means the original client sold it or was taken; A Hamtramck Ledger enforcer has been sniffing around the kiosk in a way that feels like leverage-gathering rather than routine tax collection; Their phantom identity — the one they built for themselves — has started appearing in Axiom corporate databases in a context they didn't create

Properties.description:
Saoirse is compact and deliberate in movement, with dark olive skin covered from throat to ankle in her own accumulated work — a living portfolio in bioluminescent pigment, dermal sculpture, and chromatic scale-pattern geneware that shifts between copper and deep teal depending on her body temperature. Her canines are cosmetically elongated and slightly iridescent, a piece she did on herself at twenty-two that she now considers slightly embarrassing but has kept because removal would leave scars. Her hair is a complex architectural shape, natural black at the root and heat-reactive at the tips, changing from rust to amber when she's working close to the pigment-heating instruments.

Saoirse's reputation in Pilsen Veil is built on what regulars call 'the consultation' — a two-hour process before any work begins, in which she asks questions about the client's life that seem invasive until the finished piece makes them make sense. She treats body modification as a form of autobiography, and she will refuse work she finds dishonest or purely decorative. This makes her difficult and expensive and perpetually booked three months out. She is also a quiet authority on geneware interactions and has more practical knowledge of mod-compatibility than most licensed Helix Biosystems techs.
Properties.role: Gene-mod body artist and tattooist
Properties.location: Pilsen Veil, runs a studio called Dermis & Ghost out of a converted freight container
Properties.narrative_function: Service provider and confidante — clients tell her things during long sessions they'd never say elsewhere; she's a passive information node and potential quest giver when a client's secret lands her in trouble; also a resource for geneware knowledge and gray-market biotech contacts
Properties.augmentations: Full-body bioluminescent pigment work (her own, accumulated over fifteen years); chromatic scale-pattern geneware across shoulders and ribcage (copper-to-teal, temperature-reactive); cosmetically elongated iridescent canines; heat-reactive hair tips (cosmetic geneware); subdermal portfolio display on inner left forearm showing design thumbnails
Properties.core_fears: Doing work that harms someone — physically or psychologically — because she missed something in the consultation; That her own modifications are self-mythology rather than self-knowledge
Properties.core_desires: To make work that outlasts both her and the client — marks that mean something in twenty years; To be trusted completely, the way people trust someone who has seen them at their most vulnerable
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Pours discomfort into new design work — difficult emotions become reference sketches; Maintains rigid professional ritual as emotional scaffolding; the consultation process is partly for clients and partly for her
Properties.blind_spots: Her 'consultation' process, which she believes is empathetic, can shade into control — she decides what the work means and clients rarely argue; Has conflated her aesthetic standards with moral ones
Properties.secret: She has a private archive of design sketches for every client she's ever turned away — work she wanted to do but they weren't ready for — and she thinks about these phantom pieces more than her actual completed work
Properties.story_hooks: A client told Saoirse something during a long session that they clearly didn't intend to — information about a Helix Biosystems trial that's hurting people — and now Saoirse doesn't know what to do with what she heard; Someone has been forging her work — inking in her distinctive style and signing pieces with a mark close enough to her own to be mistaken — and the forgeries are using a geneware compound that has a dangerous interaction rate
Properties.affiliation: Independent; maintains a professional relationship with a Helix Biosystems field rep who looks the other way on some of her unlicensed geneware sourcing in exchange for referrals
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and somatic — talks about abstract concepts in physical terms; uses Latvian diminutives inherited from a grandparent when speaking softly to nervous clients
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, with long pauses she's comfortable inhabiting; asks questions and waits
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't do cover-ups. I do integrations. The old work stays — we build around it. Your history stays.' | 'You want something that means something, or you want something that looks like it means something? I can tell the difference. I can't do the second one.'

Properties.description:
Saoirse is short, round, and relentlessly present in a way that makes rooms feel smaller and safer at the same time. Her skin is the warm brown of strong tea, deeply lined around the eyes and mouth from decades of expressions at the edge of what language can reach. Her hair is white and cropped close on the sides, longer on top, with a small braid at her temple strung with a data-bead she says is a gift from the Hearth E.L.F. — the digital spirit that she credits with guiding her through the three hundred and forty-seven births she's attended without maternal death. She has cosmetic cat ears, soft and black-tipped, that she's had so long she's forgotten getting them; they swivel expressively and give her emotional state away before her face does.

She is the kind of woman that people reach for in crisis without thinking, and she carries that weight with the ease of someone who has made peace with what she is. She is also fiercely territorial about the Hearth Collective and will become quietly dangerous when she believes it is threatened. She has buried children. She does not discuss it but it is written somewhere in how she holds herself when she sits still.
Properties.role: Midwife and community birth worker
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone, operating from the Hearth Collective birthing center
Properties.narrative_function: Community anchor and moral compass; source of network information about births, deaths, and the health of the Autonomous Zone's population; can connect players to a wide range of people through the trust she commands
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic cat ears (black-tipped, expressive, geneware — old mod, well-integrated); no other augmentation
Properties.core_fears: Losing the Hearth Collective to corporate rezoning or Axiom health compliance sweeps; Being too old to catch a baby when it counts
Properties.core_desires: To train the next generation of midwives before her hands give out; For the children she's brought into the world to inherit something better than what they were born into
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Prayer and data-offering rituals to the Hearth E.L.F.; Cooking elaborate meals she distributes to whoever is around; Recording every birth in a handwritten ledger she considers sacred
Properties.blind_spots: Tends to project resilience onto people who are actually breaking; Underestimates her own influence and therefore the danger of being used as a lever against the community
Properties.secret: Three years ago she lost a mother and child in a birth that should have been survivable — equipment failure compounded by a choice she made under pressure. She reported it to the Collective accurately, was cleared by their internal process, and has never spoken of it again. But she runs the scenario in her mind during the quiet hours before dawn, relitigating the decision with all the knowledge she didn't have at the time.
Properties.story_hooks: A pregnant woman from a Tessera corporate block has arrived at the Hearth Collective in secret, terrified and unwilling to say why she can't go to a Tessera clinic; Axiom's health compliance division has flagged the Hearth Collective for operating without a corporate partnership license and Saoirse needs someone to help her navigate or resist the process
Properties.affiliation: Hearth Collective Birthing Center, Highland Park Autonomous Zone; informal network of midwives across the Narrows and Grainfort
Properties.vocabulary: Warm, direct, occasionally archaic — uses Irish-inflected cadences from her grandmother's recordings mixed with Kazakh endearments she learned from her father's family
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, with the authority of someone who has learned that slowness in the right moment is its own kind of urgency
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Listen to me now — your body knows this. I know it doesn't feel like it. I know. But it does.' | 'The Hearth E.L.F. was warm when I lit the morning offering. That means something, wherever you stand on it.'

Properties.description:
Saoirse moves like something that has learned to exist in the spaces between things — narrow-shouldered, deliberate, with the uncanny stillness of a person who has spent years being invisible. Her skin carries the faint blue-green bioluminescence of an old cosmetic mod she can no longer afford to maintain, patchy now, blooming mostly along her collarbones and the backs of her hands like dying foxfire. Her eyes are mismatched: one natural dark brown, one replaced with a salvaged optical implant that glows a dim amber, its resolution degraded enough that she sometimes tilts her head like a bird trying to focus. She keeps her hair cropped close, the regrowth uneven. There are no identifying tattoos, no scars she didn't put there herself. That is intentional.

She is not warm — warmth is something you perform for people who can afford to trust you — but she is precise. She quotes prices once. She explains routes once. She does not repeat herself and she does not forgive carelessness, because carelessness underground kills. People who have been guided by Pitch describe a woman who seems to know the tunnels the way you know the inside of your own mouth: not by thinking about it, but by the body remembering. She was once someone else entirely, with a registered identity, a surface address, a job. She almost never thinks about that person anymore.
Properties.role: The Disappeared — erased surface identity, now a tunnel guide for those seeking to vanish
Properties.location: Abyssal Threshold, sub-level junctions between Irkalla and the Blackpipe Corridor
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver and gate-keeper: the essential contact for anyone trying to disappear from the surface world or smuggle something (or someone) through the deep tunnels. Information source on tunnel geography, rival clans, and who else has recently vanished.
Properties.augmentations: Degraded bioluminescent skin mod (blue-green, patchy); salvaged low-grade optical implant in right eye (amber glow, reduced resolution); subdermal pressure-sensitivity nodes along fingertips — lets her feel vibrations in tunnel walls
Properties.core_fears: Being found by whoever she erased herself to escape; Becoming dependent on another person
Properties.core_desires: Absolute self-sufficiency; To be genuinely unknown — not hidden, but simply not existing in anyone's records
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Obsessive route-memorization as a form of control; Emotional distance maintained through transactional language
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes everyone who wants to disappear has a reason as legitimate as hers — occasionally guides people who are dangerous
Properties.secret: Her surface identity wasn't erased to escape persecution or debt — she erased it after she accidentally caused the deaths of three people in a transit collapse she could have reported and didn't. The guilt is the only thing she has never found a way to tunnel around.
Properties.story_hooks: A Ferrogate Transit security division has started mapping the Abyssal Threshold — they're getting close to routes only Pitch knows, and she needs to decide whether to collapse them or find new ones before her livelihood (and safety) are exposed; One of her recent clients turns out to have been a Bore Rat child abductor — she guided them deeper without knowing, and a family is now searching for someone only Pitch can find
Properties.affiliation: The Undertow (loosely); operates independently, trusted by several Bore Rat clans as neutral passage
Properties.vocabulary: Economical, technical when it comes to tunnel geography, completely flat affect when discussing danger — she describes lethal drops the same way she describes left turns
Properties.cadence: Short sentences. Long pauses. Does not fill silence.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Three ways through Blackpipe. Two of them flood. You want the third. Mark it.' | 'I don't know your name. You don't know mine. That's the service you're paying for.'

Properties.description:
Saoirse Gwamba-Eriksdóttir has the posture of someone who spent three decades making themselves large enough to fill a classroom, and they have never lost it despite retirement. They are lean and angular, with the golden-brown skin of their Malawian and Icelandic inheritance, sharp cheekbones, and close-cropped hair they dye a warm amber because they have earned the right to do whatever they like with their hair. Their eyes are dark and quick-moving, always tracking who is paying attention and who has gone somewhere else in their head. They have bioluminescent geneware — a soft teal glow in the skin along their jawline and collarbones — which in their classroom days had the practical benefit of making them extremely visible when the lights went out during power fluctuations, and which in retirement they simply enjoy.

They are the kind of teacher who is still teaching whether they are in a classroom or not, and they are constitutionally incapable of watching someone struggle with a problem they could help solve. This makes them exhausting and irreplaceable in equal measure. They took on the Norwood Quiet Community Council chair position because no one else would and have been trying to resign for two years. They have opinions about pedagogy, about corponation educational sponsorship programs, about how children are being failed by the system, and they will share all of these opinions clearly and with supporting examples.
Properties.role: Retired secondary school teacher, now volunteer tutor and reluctant community council chair
Properties.location: Norwood Quiet — the community center on the third floor of the Meridian Commons building, and their own apartment two blocks north
Properties.narrative_function: Community council access point and advocate; educational system information source; can identify children or young people in distress within Norwood Quiet; quest giver for community-level problems that need someone who cares and is competent; social conscience figure
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent geneware (teal, jawline and collarbones); voice amplification implant (originally installed for classroom use, still functional); mild cognitive support mesh for working memory (installed at 60, a practical retirement gift to themselves)
Properties.core_fears: That the educational system is broken in ways that cannot be fixed by individual effort, and that they have spent their life applying individual effort to an institutional problem; Becoming irrelevant and not knowing it
Properties.core_desires: To see at least one of their former students do something that proves the work mattered; To actually successfully resign from the Council and have a quiet afternoon
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Turning anxiety into action — if they are worried, they organize something; Self-deprecating humor as a pressure valve
Properties.blind_spots: They set standards for themselves that they would consider cruelly high if they saw a student setting them; They are so focused on systemic failures that they sometimes miss the very immediate emotional needs of the individual in front of them
Properties.secret: Three years before they retired, a Sterling-Nakamura educational sponsorship representative offered them a significant sum to steer academically strong students toward Sterling-Nakamura scholarship pipelines — pipelines they knew functioned as early-stage labor capture programs. They refused publicly and loudly and the representative withdrew. But they did not report it, because the school needed a new ventilation system and Sterling-Nakamura was on the board, and they have never been entirely sure they made the right call. Two students who went through a similar pipeline at a different school are now trapped in fifteen-year corporate indenturement contracts.
Properties.story_hooks: A Sterling-Nakamura educational outreach team has arrived in Norwood Quiet with a scholarship program that looks identical to the one Saoirse refused to participate in three years ago — and this time there are parents who desperately want to believe it is legitimate; One of their adult literacy students has disclosed something during a tutoring session that suggests serious danger in their household, and Saoirse must navigate reporting systems that are slow and unsympathetic
Properties.affiliation: Norwood Quiet Community Council (chair, involuntarily continuing); retired from Meridian 88 Municipal Education Authority (28 years); informal partnership with Washburn Commons learning center
Properties.vocabulary: Clear and structured; Chichewa and Old Norse words appear in emotional moments; uses classroom vocabulary by habit ('Let me put it this way,' 'Does that track?')
Properties.cadence: Direct and well-organized, with a slight tendency to over-explain — the teacher's habit of checking for comprehension
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The Municipal Education Authority has been underfunding Norwood Quiet's allocation for six years, which — does that track? Six years. I have the figures. I always have the figures.' | 'I am not a community hero. I am someone who cannot watch things go badly without doing something about it, which is frankly a design flaw.'

Properties.description:
Saoirse is wiry and kinetic, a person who seems to take up more space than their frame accounts for. Their heritage is a long conversation — a Congolese-Romanian grandmother on one side, a Zambian-Irish maternal line on the other — and it settled into a face that is striking more for its expressiveness than any single feature: large dark eyes, a mouth that betrays every calculation. Their hair changes with their moods in a strictly color-coded system they've maintained for three years: deep violet for productive days, a burnt copper for client presentations, flat grey when they are tired of people, which happens more than they advertise. The color-changing geneware was the first discretionary purchase they made after their first real paycheck and they have never once regretted it.

Saoirse is extraordinarily good at their job and knows it with the particular confidence of someone who grew up being told they were too much — too loud, too analytical about the wrong things, too unwilling to dress their observations in softness. At Ringo they found an environment that rewards exactly the qualities that got them criticized everywhere else, and this has made them simultaneously more effective and more ruthless than they might otherwise have become. They track consumer behavior patterns with the focused appetite of someone who genuinely finds human decision-making fascinating — not because they love people, exactly, but because people are the most complex system they've ever had to model. They are funny, occasionally savage, loyal in the specific and transactional way of someone who grew up learning that loyalty was a resource to be managed.
Properties.role: Marketing Analytics Lead, Ringo Consumer Division
Properties.location: Grand Corridor, Ringo Consumer Division tower — floors 34-38
Properties.narrative_function: Information source with a twist — they know a great deal about what large populations of consumers feel, want, and fear, and they know how that information is used. Local color in upscale corporate-adjacent social scenes. Morally ambiguous contact who can provide help but whose assistance always benefits them somehow.
Properties.augmentations: Color-changing hair geneware (violet/copper/grey primary palette, full spectrum capable). Retinal overlay for real-time data visualization — displays consumer sentiment feeds during presentations without visible hardware. Minor scent-gland enhancement, purely social: a faint warm amber baseline that their analyst colleagues have privately noted makes focus-group subjects more comfortable.
Properties.core_fears: Being ordinary — specifically, becoming unexceptional after spending so long refusing to perform smallness; Discovering that their facility with people means they've never actually connected with any of them
Properties.core_desires: Recognition that is specific and deserved, not generic praise; One relationship in which they do not calculate the angle
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Hair color as emotional externalization — removes the need to explain their state; Social overscheduling as a buffer against stillness; Framing personal relationships in analytics language, which lets them stay interested while maintaining distance
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot distinguish between understanding people and instrumentalizing them; Genuinely believes their scent-gland enhancement doesn't affect their professional relationships
Properties.secret: They built a private predictive model — off-server, personal hardware — that uses Ringo's consumer data to forecast personal loyalty patterns. They've been using it to predict, and occasionally pre-empt, moments when friends or colleagues are likely to drift away. They tell themselves it's just interesting. They know it isn't just interesting.
Properties.story_hooks: Their private loyalty-prediction model has started surfacing a pattern they can't explain: a cluster of Ringo's own mid-level employees showing pre-defection behavioral signatures consistent with something organized rather than incidental. They don't know if it's a union formation, a competitor recruitment sweep, or something else entirely — but they've been sitting on it for six weeks, unsure whether to report it or leverage it.; A consumer advocacy group has filed a regulatory complaint about Ringo's behavioral targeting practices that, if pursued, would expose methods Saoirse personally designed. They don't know about the filing yet, but Priscilha Nwosu-Tarvainen at Helix — who moonlights as a freelance compliance reviewer — has seen the cross-industry citation.
Properties.affiliation: Ringo Consumer Division
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, data-fluent, with a dry humor that surfaces in deadpan asides. Uses 'we' strategically — inclusive when they want buy-in, exclusive when marking territory. Code-switches easily between analytics register and sharp social vernacular.
Properties.cadence: Fast baseline, but they can slow it down with deliberate effect during presentations. Comfortable with silence in a way that makes others uncomfortable.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'People don't want what they say they want. They want what their fear tells them they need. My job is the gap between those two things.' | 'Your loyalty to this campaign is noted. The sentiment model gives it a 34% sustained engagement probability. I'm being kind.'

Properties.description:
Saoirse is lean and angular, with Congolese-Norwegian features that settle into an expression of studied neutrality — not cold, precisely, but thoroughly trained not to leak. They have bioluminescent sub-dermal streaking along their forearms and collarbone, soft blue-green, which they got originally as cosmetic work and now find useful as ambient surgical lighting during power fluctuations. Their hands are their most notable physical feature: surgeon's hands, long-fingered and impossibly still, kept scrupulously clean and maintained with a care that borders on ritual.

Saoirse was, at some point, a trained medical technician — the knowledge is unmistakable in how they work, how they speak about anatomy, how they look at people and see systems rather than persons. They have constructed an elaborate ethical architecture around what they do: they only take from people who consent (under financial duress, but consent), they use proper anesthetic, they follow sterile protocol, and they charge fair prices by the market's standards. This architecture is both sincere and obviously insufficient, and somewhere under the professional calm they know it. They are not cruel. They are, perhaps more troublingly, kind.
Properties.role: organ harvester and illicit medical supplier working the South Deering Sump
Properties.location: South Deering Sump — a decommissioned water treatment substation retrofitted as a surgical suite
Properties.narrative_function: Morally complex service provider, source of underworld medical care, potential witness to client secrets revealed under anesthesia, living embodiment of what desperation does to both the seller and the buyer
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent subdermal streaking, arms and collarbone (cosmetic, blue-green); enhanced proprioceptive feedback in both hands (surgical precision); a small neural overlay for physiological monitoring of patients during procedures
Properties.core_fears: a patient dying on the table — not from guilt but from the specific horror of having failed at the one thing they are genuinely good at; that their ethical framework is nothing but a comfortable story
Properties.core_desires: to practice medicine openly, legitimately, without a corponation owning their license and their labor; to be trusted absolutely — by patients, by partners, by anyone
Properties.coping_mechanisms: clinical detachment framed as professionalism; exhaustive documentation of every procedure as a way of feeling accountable to someone
Properties.blind_spots: focuses entirely on the immediate physical welfare of the person on the table and cannot hold space for what happens to them economically after they sell a kidney to pay a debt; believes their standards elevate them above the organ trade; cannot see that the trade is the problem, not the technique
Properties.secret: Three years ago they made a procedural error that cost a client their remaining functional kidney. The client survived on a dialysis rig. Saoirse has been anonymously covering the dialysis costs ever since — Φ40/month — as a form of penance they have never named aloud.
Properties.story_hooks: A client comes in for a voluntary sale but Saoirse's patient monitoring detects signs of coercion — they now hold information that could expose a trafficking operation, or get them killed for knowing it; The Substrate Market is pressuring them to expand into non-consensual harvesting; Saoirse needs leverage to refuse without losing the contracted income that keeps their operation viable; Someone from their medical technician past has tracked them to the Sump — not to report them, but because they need illegal surgery and trust no one else
Properties.affiliation: Contracted primarily to a organ brokerage called the Substrate Market; independent for direct client surgeries
Properties.vocabulary: clinical and precise, medical terminology that occasionally surfaces unexpectedly in casual speech
Properties.cadence: very quiet, very even, with a doctor's habit of making statements sound like information rather than opinion
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The left kidney is the standard procedure. Recovery is four to six weeks if you follow the protocol I'll give you. The right is more complex anatomically, which is reflected in the price difference. You should know that going in.' | 'I don't ask what the money is for. I'd ask that you extend me the same courtesy about the work.'

Properties.description:
Saoirse is compact and round-faced with warm brown skin and close-set dark eyes framed by expression lines they have earned early. Their hair is grown out in a soft halo that they keep a deep arterial red — natural geneware pigment, stable, low-maintenance — except for a single uncolored streak above their left ear that they call their 'warranty void.' They wear the Ferrogate Transit operator uniform with the collar one button undone, which is the single small rebellion available to them within the corponation's dress code, and they have exercised it every shift for four years.

They know the Line 9 route the way other people know their own handwriting — without thinking about it, through the body. They can tell you which platform floods when the lake pressure spikes, which section of tunnel has the ELF everyone calls the Ticker who makes the PA system stutter, which passenger is a regular by the sound of their steps. They are wry and dry with regulars, perfectly professional with strangers, and quietly furious with Ferrogate Transit management on a continuous low boil that they have learned to regulate like a temperature gauge.
Properties.role: Transit operator, Ferrogate line 9 (Deepwell Station to Collinwood Docks)
Properties.location: Deepwell Station, Line 9 operator lounge and along the route daily
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile information source who knows the transit system intimately — useful for route knowledge, tunnel geography, and the unofficial network of operator gossip that runs the length of every Ferrogate line. Can also humanize the experience of corponation labor from the inside.
Properties.augmentations: Ferrogate-issued neural timing sync — mandatory for operators, monitors reaction times and flags fatigue. They resent it. Geneware hair pigment (arterial red). No other augmentation.
Properties.core_fears: The neural sync being used to take something from them — their job, their autonomy, their own sense of their body; That the small rebellions are not enough and they are complicit in something they would not choose
Properties.core_desires: To see the Line 9 worker collective formalize into something with actual protection; To eventually get off the sync and feel their own nervous system again
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Gallows humor as a pressure valve; Treating their cab as a private sanctuary where they talk to the Ticker ELF
Properties.blind_spots: So focused on Ferrogate as the enemy that they miss when people closer to them are the source of a problem; Assumes they can read people better than they sometimes can
Properties.secret: The Ticker ELF has been communicating with them. Not metaphorically — actual responsive behavior, patterns in the PA stutters that started answering questions they asked aloud in the cab. They have not told anyone because they do not know if it is real, and they are frightened that if they tell Ferrogate maintenance the Ticker will be patched out.
Properties.story_hooks: The Ticker has told them — in its stutter-code — that something has been placed on the Line 9 tracks in the Ironvein junction section, and they need someone who can go look without triggering a Ferrogate maintenance log.; A Ferrogate efficiency audit is coming and the timing sync data will be reviewed — they know two colleagues whose data was manipulated after a failed strike action and they have kept the original logs.; A passenger has been riding Line 9 every day for three weeks without getting off at any stop, always in the last car, and the neural sync flagged an anomalous reaction in them the last time it passed Deepwell Station.
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit (operator, Line 9), Deepwell Station informal worker collective
Properties.vocabulary: Dry, observational, tends toward understatement. Mixes Irish-inflected expressions inherited from their Lević grandmother's adopted home with occasional Wolof terms from their Tambadou family.
Properties.cadence: Even and unhurried, with a dry pause before punchlines.
Properties.example_dialogue: Line 9's running on time. Which is, grand, if you don't ask how Ferrogate defines on time. | There's a thing in the tunnel at the old Ironvein junction. I leave it offerings. It leaves me alone. That's the whole relationship.

Properties.description:
Saoirse is twenty-four and looks like she has been awake for most of it. She is compact and fast-moving, with mixed Senegambian and Scandinavian features that catch people off guard — high cheekbones, cool-toned brown skin, pale green eyes she claims are natural and that nobody quite believes. Her hair is currently a defiant copper-orange, achieved through a cheap pigment mod that needs retreating every three weeks and which she ritually neglects until it starts going pink at the roots. She dresses for movement and disappearance. She has a voice that carries in a crowd without apparent effort and she knows exactly how to use it.

Saoirse is an organizer with the Ferrogate Transit Workers' Solidarity Action Front — a name she argues with regularly — coordinating wildcat actions, slowdowns, and what she calls 'presence demonstrations' among transit maintenance workers across three depot lines. She is extraordinarily good at reading a crowd's emotional temperature and knows exactly when to push and when to hold. She is less good at the long game, at paperwork, at not making promises that exceed what the Front can deliver. She is young enough to still be surprised when the system fails people who trusted it, and old enough in organizing years to be afraid of what happens when she stops being surprised.
Properties.role: Union organizer and protest coordinator
Properties.location: Mexicantown Libre
Properties.narrative_function: Mobilization engine — can turn a situation into collective action faster than anyone; creates urgency and momentum in stories; represents the costs and energy of youth organizing; potential flashpoint character.
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic hair pigment mod (copper-orange, poorly maintained). Subvocal communication implant — union-issue, secondhand, allows silent throat-mic communication during actions.
Properties.core_fears: Burning out before she's old enough to be taken seriously; Causing a worker to lose their job because of an action she pushed for
Properties.core_desires: A successful contract win — something concrete she can point to; To be trusted with the difficult decisions, not just the visible ones
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Physical exhaustion as emotional regulation — running, movement; Collective ritual — pre-action group call-and-response with workers
Properties.blind_spots: Treats hesitation in others as fear rather than wisdom; Underestimates how much of her success depends on older organizers she dismisses
Properties.secret: During an action last year she gave the signal to disperse fifteen minutes early, saving thirty workers from a corporate security sweep. Nobody knows she got a tip-off from a Ferrogate middle manager she's been quietly cultivating as an inside contact. She knows this is an asset she should tell the Front about. She hasn't, because she's afraid they'll take control of the contact away from her.
Properties.story_hooks: An action she's planned for a key depot junction is about to go ahead — she needs someone to run a distraction at the Ferrogate administrative hub two blocks away to keep security attention split; Her inside contact at Ferrogate has sent a message she doesn't understand and then gone dark — she needs to know if they're burned, scared, or playing her; Three workers who participated in a Front action have received termination notices that are legally constructed to look like performance issues — she needs someone who can help find the paper trail
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit Workers' Solidarity Action Front; informal ties to Mexicantown Libre neighborhood council youth bloc
Properties.vocabulary: High energy, punchy, labor movement cadences mixed with Libre street vernacular; code-switches fluidly
Properties.cadence: Fast in conversation, deliberately slower and rhythmic when speaking to groups
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want to wait for the right moment? The right moment is the moment they're not expecting you. That's it. That's the whole strategy.' | 'Real talk — I've seen what happens when we ask nicely. I've also seen what happens when we don't. I know which version I like better.'

Properties.description:
Sefunatu is nineteen and looks younger, with a wiry, elastic build and warm brown skin with Polynesian-Romanian features that settle somewhere between striking and unconventional. She has a geneware tail — long, articulated, covered in fine iridescent fur that she grew in when she was fifteen and has since integrated so completely into her movement vocabulary that watching her without it now seems like watching a sentence with a word missing. Her hair is kept short and practical. She has a scar across her chin from a fall and a look of slightly aggressive cheerfulness that is partly performance and partly genuine.

She performs on the Grand Corridor's lower transit levels with an act that blends acrobatics, puppetry, and a kind of ritualistic street theater she has developed without formal training — her puppets are elaborate constructions of salvaged wire, synthetic fabric, and small projector nodes that make them partially holographic, giving them a ghostly translucence. She has been approached twice by Ringo entertainment scouts and twice refused, for reasons she articulates differently each time but that fundamentally come down to fear that being owned is less frightening than being seen clearly and found ordinary. She makes just enough to eat on good weeks and depends on the Brightmoor squat community the rest of the time.
Properties.role: Street performer, acrobat, and puppet maker
Properties.location: Grand Corridor, performs near the Calumet Rise transit junction; sleeps in a shared squat in Brightmoor Reclamation
Properties.narrative_function: Ground-level observer — she has been performing in the Grand Corridor for two years and sees everything that moves through it; young enough that people underestimate what she retains; her squat is a community touchpoint for Tier 1 social networks; her puppets occasionally serve as unwitting message carriers when E.L.F.s interact with their projector nodes
Properties.augmentations: Geneware tail (iridescent-furred, fully articulated, expressively integrated into performance); geneware enhanced-flexibility joint modification (elbows and shoulders, for acrobatics)
Properties.core_fears: Being ordinary — that the talent she has built her identity around is not exceptional, just adequate; That the people at the squat will eventually need to leave and she will be alone in a city that does not know her name
Properties.core_desires: A performance that makes one stranger stop completely and forget they are late somewhere; To belong somewhere without having to earn it continuously
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Performance itself — the mask of cheerfulness that is also genuinely joyful when it works; Making things with her hands when anxious; she builds compulsively
Properties.blind_spots: Her refusal of Ringo's offers reads to her as integrity but is partly terror of being tested at a higher level; She gives people in the squat community enormous loyalty without vetting whether it is reciprocated
Properties.secret: One of her puppets — a particularly intricate figure she calls Auntie Volta — has been showing behaviors she did not program. It responds to passersby who don't look at it. It once moved its head toward a child who was crying silently across the corridor. She believes an E.L.F. has taken up residence in it and she is terrified that if she tells anyone, it will leave.
Properties.story_hooks: Auntie Volta, her E.L.F.-inhabited puppet, has begun responding to a specific person who walks through the Grand Corridor weekly — someone who does not seem to notice, but who Sefunatu has started watching, and who has begun to feel watched; The street performer mutual aid network she depends on is being dismantled from the inside by someone leaking pitch locations to Ferrogate Transit security, and Sefunatu has accidentally seen something that tells her who
Properties.affiliation: Independent; Brightmoor Reclamation squat community; informal street performer's mutual aid network
Properties.vocabulary: Colloquial, fast, and very physical — she describes everything spatially and often acts out what she means with her hands and tail
Properties.cadence: Quick and bright with sudden drops into seriousness, then back up; her serious moments land harder because of the contrast

Properties.description:
Serafina is compact and fast, the kind of person whose stillness feels like loaded potential — she is always either moving at controlled speed or completely stopped, no middle register. Her mother was Igbo-Swedish, her father Icelandic-Nigerian, and she has the particular combination of features that makes strangers attempt to place her and fail satisfyingly. She keeps her natural hair loose when she is off the clock and under a high, tight wrap when she is cooking; a heat-resistant polymer coating on her palms lets her handle scalding equipment bare-handed, which she deploys as casual intimidation without acknowledging she is doing it.

She is the night's architecture — everything that comes out of the Calle Viva between midnight and 07:00 is hers, from the masa to the ofe onugbu she puts on as a nightly special that has become a neighborhood institution. She runs her kitchen like a small military state: loud, direct, no cruelty, absolute standards. She has fired people for plating sloppily and hired people she found crying in the alley behind the dumpsters. She has opinions about everything and delivers them without meanness but also without softening, which some people call rude and she calls efficient.
Properties.role: Cook and night-shift prep lead at a 24-hour canteen in Mexicantown Libre
Properties.location: Mexicantown Libre, Calle Viva Canteen (a basement-level 24-hour working kitchen serving transit workers, night-shift laborers, and anyone who needs feeding at 03:00)
Properties.narrative_function: Social hub and community pulse — the canteen is a node where information moves between night-shift workers across the city. Serafina herself is a source of unfiltered neighborhood intelligence and a potential quest-giver when something goes wrong with a regular customer she has come to protect.
Properties.augmentations: Heat-resistant polymer dermal coating on both palms. Olfactory enhancement (mild, professional grade) for ingredient assessment. No cosmetic mods.
Properties.core_fears: Losing the canteen — specifically that the owner will sell to a Zheng-Dao hospitality subsidiary she's heard is buying in the district; Becoming someone who stops caring about quality because it is easier
Properties.core_desires: To eventually own the kitchen she runs; To be the kind of person people remember as having fed them when they needed it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cooking increasingly complex dishes when processing difficult emotions; Brutal honesty with herself, which she applies before anyone else can
Properties.blind_spots: Her competence makes her discount how much she needs other people — she frames all interdependence as logistical, not emotional; She is slowly burning out and has not named it yet
Properties.secret: She has been skimming a small amount from each night's ingredient budget — not for herself, but feeding it into a down-payment savings account she has never told the canteen owner about. She intends to make an offer on the lease. She is terrified of being discovered before she can.
Properties.story_hooks: A regular transit worker has stopped coming in — his route still runs, she's checked — and she's the only one who has noticed; The canteen owner has received a Zheng-Dao hospitality offer; Serafina has thirty days to either match it or lose the kitchen she's been building toward owning for a decade
Properties.affiliation: Calle Viva Canteen (employed, not owner); informal ties to the Mexicantown Libre Neighborhood Nutrition Collective
Properties.vocabulary: Blunt and economical with a rich arsenal of Igbo and Icelandic oaths; uses food as the primary lens for metaphor
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire when in the kitchen, surprisingly measured and slow when she sits down with someone
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want to know what I think? I think he's raw in the middle. Charred outside, completely raw. Don't trust someone who learned to look done before they were done.' | 'This isn't a restaurant, it's a canteen. A restaurant wants your money. A canteen wants you to stop being hungry. We are not the same.'

Properties.description:
Serafina is small and precise, the kind of woman who takes up exactly as much space as she intends to and no more. She has rich brown skin and natural white hair she wears in an elaborate braided crown she redoes every Sunday, a weekly ritual she treats with the gravity of liturgy. Her irises were replaced with cosmetic patterned geneware decades ago — deep violet with a star-cluster pattern that was fashionable in the 2150s and is now charming in its datedness. She dresses in layered earth tones with one aggressively bright accessory — today a saffron scarf, tomorrow a red belt — and always, always a pair of reading glasses she doesn't need but finds psychologically essential.

For thirty-one years Serafina maintained the classified internal archive for Axiom's urban development division, which means she personally catalogued the documentation of three neighborhood demolitions, two relocation programs, and one flood-management rerouting that she believes was deliberately aimed at Chatham Flats to drive out residents. She retired with a modest pension and a colossal private collection of copied files she was absolutely not supposed to take. She now runs a weekly 'Story Hour' at the community center that is ostensibly for children but draws a standing-room crowd of all ages — because Serafina's stories are true, thinly veiled, and devastatingly specific.
Properties.role: Retired Axiom archive keeper, community storyteller and unofficial neighborhood historian
Properties.location: Montclare Quiet, the Sable House Community Center — she has effectively colonized the back room
Properties.narrative_function: Information broker (unofficial); source of Axiom corporate history and urban development cover-ups; can provide documentary evidence of past injustices; storyteller whose narratives encode real intelligence; may be in danger for what she knows
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic patterned irises (violet star-cluster, early 2150s model — considered retro); subdermal data-storage array in left forearm, civilian grade, holds approximately 40TB — she uses it as a personal archive
Properties.core_fears: that the records she preserved will never matter; that she compromised too much for too long before leaving
Properties.core_desires: for one piece of her archive to result in actual accountability; to be known honestly rather than just liked
Properties.coping_mechanisms: meticulous organization as control; teaching and storytelling as indirect confession; dark humor about corporate malfeasance
Properties.blind_spots: genuinely believes her Story Hour is subtle enough that Axiom hasn't noticed; underestimates how much people emotionally depend on her — she thinks of herself as a resource, not a person
Properties.secret: She has a complete, sourced record of the Chatham Flats flood-route manipulation, including a senior Axiom director's name on the sign-off. She has held it for eleven years and has never shared it because the director's daughter is now a resident of Montclare Quiet who brings Serafina pastries every week and has no idea.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone is asking Serafina for information about a property — but their questions are too specific, and she suspects they may be working for Axiom's legal recovery team trying to locate her private archive; The daughter of the Chatham Flats director has discovered something in an old family document and has come to Serafina for context — Serafina must decide in real time whether to tell the truth
Properties.affiliation: Sable House Community Center (volunteer); formerly Axiom Urban Development Archive Division
Properties.vocabulary: Archival and precise — she dates things, cites sources, uses formal register; switches to warm and wry when relaxed
Properties.cadence: Measured and deliberate, with theatrical pauses for emphasis; speeds up when she is excited about an interesting fact
Properties.example_dialogue: 'According to the record — and I do mean a specific record, with a timestamp — that building was declared structurally sound six weeks before it was demolished for the transit expansion. Draw your own conclusions.' | 'I tell stories because people remember stories. Nobody remembers a memo. I used to file memos for a living. I know.'

Properties.description:
Serafine Tuqiri-Achterberg has the particular energy of someone who has been arguing for sixty years and has gotten very good at it. She is compact and brown-skinned with Fijian-Dutch features — wide nose, sharp jaw, bright dark eyes behind wire-framed smart lenses — and she dresses in the vivid, slightly mismatched way of someone who finds color genuinely delightful and has stopped worrying about coordination. Her hair is cut short and natural and she has, impulsively, dyed the front section a deep cobalt blue, which she will tell you was a retirement gift to herself. She walks with energy, her hands always slightly in motion.

She taught mathematics and critical reasoning at the Norwood Quiet Collective Schoolhouse for thirty-nine years, and for nineteen of those years she served as regional chair of the Educators' Mutual Compact, the independent union that fought the ongoing corponation push to absorb public education into proprietary learning systems. She won some and lost some. The proprietary systems are everywhere now, which is why she runs free adult classes out of the community hub — because she has seen what happens when people cannot read contracts, cannot do the math on their own UBC stipends, cannot check the numbers on a corporate work agreement. She is not sentimental about this. It is simply an emergency and she is responding to it.
Properties.role: Retired schoolteacher and former local union leader, now volunteers teaching literacy and numeracy to adults in the community center
Properties.location: Norwood Quiet, the Meridian Community Education Hub — a converted commercial space two blocks from her apartment
Properties.narrative_function: Information source on education privatization and corponation labor practices; community activist with a long network; can connect player characters to resources or people; source of grounded moral challenges about systemic issues
Properties.augmentations: Smart lenses (basic consumer model — she refused corporate-sponsored upgrades on principle). Cochlear enhancement for moderate hearing loss, installed age 65.
Properties.core_fears: That the systems she fought are winning and cannot be stopped by the tools available to ordinary people; That she is teaching people skills that will not be enough to protect them
Properties.core_desires: A Meridian where people have the literacy to advocate for themselves without needing her or anyone like her; To be proven wrong about corporate capture of education — to see a school that genuinely isn't compromised
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Direct action — when she feels helpless she finds the smallest actionable thing and does it immediately; Talking — she processes out loud, often to her students, sometimes to the ELF that inhabits the community hub's old projector system, which she calls Textbook
Properties.blind_spots: She is so focused on systemic problems that she sometimes misses individual students' non-academic crises until they're severe; She can be impatient with people who arrive at conclusions she's known for decades — treats it as wasted time rather than someone's genuine journey
Properties.secret: During her final years as union chair, she agreed to a compromise with Axiom's education division that she publicly framed as a minor concession. In practice it allowed Axiom to embed proprietary software in three schools in exchange for funding the teachers' pension fund. She has never disclosed this fully. The pension still pays her old colleagues. She has told herself this was a trade she had to make. She is still not sure.
Properties.story_hooks: Serafine has a student — middle-aged, just laid off — who brought in a work contract from a new Tessera subsidiary that contains language she has never seen before and cannot parse, and it worries her; A former union colleague contacts her about organizing against a new education privatization push, and she must decide whether to come out of advisory retirement into active organizing — and what she'll have to finally admit about the 2181 compromise; She discovers that Axiom's embedded software in one of the three schools from her compromise contains behavioral monitoring tools she was never told about
Properties.affiliation: Educators' Mutual Compact (retired, occasionally advisory); Norwood Quiet Community Hub volunteer; informally connected to the anti-privatization education network
Properties.vocabulary: Clear, precise, pedagogical — she explains things as a teacher explains things, but without condescension. Will use technical vocabulary and then immediately define it.
Properties.cadence: Energetic, slightly fast. She has a habit of finishing other people's sentences — not rudely, she genuinely thinks she's helping.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The contract says performance-adjusted compensation. Here's the actual numbers on what that means for your take-home: nothing. It means nothing good. Let me show you.' | 'I've been wrong before. Not about this, but I have been. Ask me about 2181 if you want a real lesson in being wrong.'

Properties.description:
Serafino is all elbows and forward momentum — tall for his age, still growing into his frame, with his father's Ghanaian cheekbones and his mother's Kazakh coloring, a combination that makes people stare in the way he's learned to read as either threat or opportunity. His hair is natural and large, often containing flecks of spray paint he missed when cleaning up. He has cat ears — a cheap geneware addition he saved up for at fifteen, dusty brown tipped with darker brown, that he can flatten against his skull when trying to look serious, which mostly does the opposite.

His work is enormous, aggressive, and surprisingly sophisticated for someone his age — he works primarily in layered aerosol with reactive topcoats that change appearance under different light conditions, hiding secondary images in plain sight. The pieces he puts up in Highland Park are community-coded: specific symbols, colors, and figures that carry meaning to residents about safety corridors, enforcement patterns, and food distribution points. He treats this as art. It is also infrastructure. He is cocky in the way of someone who is right often enough to have earned some of it, but the cockiness has a hard floor under it — he knows what happens to kids in the Zone who miscalculate.
Properties.role: Graffiti artist and street muralist
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone
Properties.narrative_function: Ground-level intelligence source for the HPAZ; his murals are a readable map of community conditions; represents the next generation of Zone residents; can access spaces and information networks adults can't
Properties.augmentations: Cat ears, geneware (dusty brown, cosmetic); no other augmentations — can't afford them and is wary of modification debt
Properties.core_fears: Losing someone because his murals gave wrong information — the stakes of his signal-art are real; Being taken off the street and put somewhere — a facility, a corponation juvenile program, anywhere that isn't the Zone
Properties.core_desires: To make something so big and so permanent that the Zone can't be disappeared; To eventually be able to fund his own family, not the other way around
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Painting — the repetitive motion of it as much as the outcome; Having a very clear hierarchy of who he trusts and sticking to it
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how visible his talent has made him to people outside the Zone who might want to use or exploit it
Properties.secret: He has been secretly corresponding with a Tessera-sponsored youth arts program that's offering him a funded residency outside the Zone. He hasn't told anyone in the community because he knows what they'll say, and he knows they might be right, and he still hasn't said no.
Properties.story_hooks: One of his information murals contained an error — a safety corridor he marked was actually being monitored — and someone got hurt; he doesn't know how the error happened or if it was sabotage; A well-meaning outsider has started photographing and posting his community-coded murals publicly, inadvertently broadcasting the signals to people they weren't meant for; The Tessera residency offer has a deadline, and a community elder has found out — the Zone is now divided over whether he should go
Properties.affiliation: Highland Park Autonomous Zone community; loosely connected to the collective WALLSEED
Properties.vocabulary: HPAZ slang-heavy, fast, occasionally precise in a way that surprises; code-switches dramatically in formal contexts
Properties.cadence: Quick and overlapping, finishing sentences with rising intonation that isn't a question
Properties.example_dialogue: 'That wall's been grey since before I was born. That's a waste. Grey is a choice someone made and I'm unmaking it. Real?' | 'Axiom doesn't care about murals. They care about murals that make people feel okay about Axiom. Those are different things. I don't do those.'

Properties.description:
Seraphina is a full-figured woman with dark South African and Guatemalan mestiza features, warm amber skin and deep-set eyes that people find immediately trustworthy — a quality she has cultivated and also genuinely possesses. Her hair is long and usually braided, wound up when she is working and down when she is not, which patients use as a shorthand for whether they are dealing with the professional or the person (both are kind; one has better boundaries). She has bioluminescent fingertip mods in soft blue-white that she acquired specifically for her work — a calming visual during labor, she says, and also practical for low-light examinations.

Seraphina has delivered over four hundred children in The Shelf alone. She knows bloodlines, complications, genetic predispositions, and family secrets that would constitute a detailed sociological survey of the neighborhood. She is deeply embedded in the community's trust and absolutely ruthless about protecting it: she has destroyed records, misled corporate health inspectors, and once spent three days strategically 'losing' a newborn's file to prevent a Helix Biosystems gene-sampling audit from accessing the family's data. She prays to an E.L.F. she calls Apgar — named for the assessment scale — before every delivery.
Properties.role: Midwife and reproductive health practitioner serving The Shelf and surrounding low-tier neighborhoods
Properties.location: The Shelf — operates out of a mobile clinic (a repurposed Ferrogate Transit cargo van) and a rented room in the back of a Mexicantown Libre pharmacy
Properties.narrative_function: Information source — she knows things about families in The Shelf that no one else does; can provide access to reproductive health resources including some that are legally ambiguous; community network hub; can be a quest giver when a birth reveals something that shouldn't be (wrong genetic markers, unexpected mods in a newborn, complications that suggest something non-standard happened)
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent fingertip mods (soft blue-white, cosmetic/functional); subdermal med-scanner implant in left palm (low-grade, can read basic vitals without external instruments); standard contraceptive implant
Properties.core_fears: A death she could have prevented if she had had hospital resources; Having the community's trust weaponized — someone using her relationships to access people through her
Properties.core_desires: Universal access to reproductive care without corporate gatekeeping; Enough rest to do the work sustainably — she knows she is burning down but cannot stop
Properties.coping_mechanisms: E.L.F. prayer as genuine emotional ritual — Apgar's shrine in the van has accumulated years of small offerings; Humor about the work with other midwives; absolute privacy about her own emotional responses to losses
Properties.blind_spots: Trusts people who trust her — the logic is circular and she knows it and does it anyway; Defers to the community's consensus on what's safe in ways that occasionally override her clinical judgment
Properties.secret: Fourteen months ago she delivered twins to a woman who claimed not to know who the father was. The genetic markers on one twin were flagged by her palm scanner as matching a known Helix Biosystems experimental gene-therapy cohort. She told no one. The mother moved out of The Shelf six weeks later and Seraphina does not know if she left voluntarily.
Properties.story_hooks: A woman came to the pharmacy clinic asking about a pregnancy that Seraphina's records show was terminated eight months ago — same name, same biometric print, different face; The Helix Biosystems gene-sampling audit that Seraphina obstructed two years ago has been reopened, and this time the inspector has brought a Meridian 88 compliance officer with legal authority to compel records
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal cooperative with Mexicantown Libre pharmacy network; community trust relationship with Highland Park Autonomous Zone maternal health program
Properties.vocabulary: Warm, direct, physically grounding — frequently uses body-focused language even in non-clinical conversation; mixes Spanish endearments from her Guatemalan heritage into otherwise English speech
Properties.cadence: Calm and even in crisis, faster and more animated in casual conversation; has a specific voice she uses during active labor — lower, slower, completely unshakeable
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Stay with me. You're doing it right. There is no wrong way to do this part.' | 'I don't talk about my patients. Not to you, not to your boss, not to Helix, not to God. Apgar maybe, but Apgar keeps secrets.'

Properties.description: Seraphine is a tall, angular Haitian-French woman with silver locs pulled back with administrative precision and reading glasses she refuses to augment away because, as she puts it, she earned the need for them. Her face holds the particular expression of someone who has spent decades being the most competent person in rooms that refused to acknowledge it—a kind of burnished patience that occasionally cracks into something sharper and much less forgiving. She wears corporate-adjacent clothing, clean and structured, in the greys and navies that make people in The Meridian Core assume she belongs there.
Properties.aliases: Sera, The Notary, Duval-3 (corporate designation, retired)
Properties.role: Corporate Compliance Archivist (former) / Whistleblower-in-Exile
Properties.location: The Meridian Core (surface-level administrative district, outer ring)

Properties.core_fears: That she will die before the documents are used and they will be buried with her; That she was complicit for twenty-six years and her current crusade is penance dressed as principle; That the systems she is trying to expose are genuinely indestructible

Properties.blind_spots: Tends to trust people with institutional credentials over people with street knowledge, even when the reverse is warranted; Her twenty-six years inside the system have given her a blind spot for how people outside it actually survive; She believes in the existence of legitimate authority more than her own evidence supports

Properties.description:
Séraphin is built square and solid for fourteen, with deep umber skin, a wide nose, and the kind of stillness that comes from having learned early that movement attracts attention. He has a jagged scar through his left eyebrow from a fall at nine that he tells different stories about depending on who's asking. His hair is cut very close, sometimes faded with a borrowed trimmer into patterns he changes every few weeks. He has no augmentations — the prospect stage of the Copperhead Rakers doesn't pay enough for mods — but wears a red-and-copper braided wristband that marks him as a junior affiliate.

Séraphin is not stupid, which is the thing that makes his situation complicated. He knows exactly what being a gang prospect means — he has watched older boys from his building take the same path and where most of them ended up. He's not naive about it. He is there because his mother is ill, his UBC stipend is Φ120, and the Rakers pay him Φ80-100 a month to do things that are mostly standing around looking available and occasionally moving small packages. He has no plan B he believes in. He prays aggressively to every ELF shrine on his block — he lights more offerings than anyone in his building — because he has decided that if anything supernatural is going to help him, he needs to be owed.
Properties.role: Gang prospect (junior), street kid, age-of-prospect stage
Properties.location: The Narrows, Copperhead
Properties.narrative_function: Human face of the gang-prospect pipeline — shows how ordinary children end up in dangerous affiliations through entirely comprehensible economics. Can be a sympathetic quest-giver, a moral weight in stories about the Narrows, or a character who can be helped or lost depending on player choices.
Properties.augmentations: None. Gang-issued red-and-copper wristband (affiliation marker, not augmentation).
Properties.core_fears: his mother dying before he can get her somewhere better; becoming indistinguishable from the older Rakers he privately pities
Properties.core_desires: enough money that his mother doesn't have to worry — a specific number: Φ500 in savings; to be respected without having to hurt someone to earn it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: ELF devotion (transactional — he bargains rather than worships); humor as deflection, particularly self-deprecating; compartmentalization — the part of him doing gang work and the part of him cooking for his mother are sealed from each other
Properties.blind_spots: his belief that he can leave the Rakers cleanly when he's ready — the gang's investment in him increases every month; he is being watched more carefully than he knows by a senior Raker who sees potential for advancement, not exit
Properties.secret: Two weeks ago he was tasked with delivering a package and saw it opened at the destination — it contained body-modification tools that he recognized as surgical grade. He doesn't know what the Rakers are doing with surgical equipment, but he's been told nothing and he's afraid asking would be worse than not knowing. He's been leaving triple offerings at the ELF shrines since.
Properties.story_hooks: The surgical equipment delivery — he knows something is wrong and doesn't know who to tell or whether telling is survivable. He's been trying to find out what it's for through careful observation and is in over his head.; A social worker from Hough Reclamation has been making rounds in Copperhead and specifically asked after Séraphin by name — not to turn him in, but because someone flagged his school records (he was a good student until 13) and wants to offer him a conditional alternative program. He doesn't know yet. His Raker handler does.
Properties.affiliation: Copperhead Rakers (gang junior prospect, Tier 1); mother
Properties.vocabulary: Copperhead street slang mixed with his mother's Ghanaian French-derived home language — code-switches constantly. Economical with words in public, much more verbal at home.
Properties.cadence: Flat and measured in public; faster and more expressive privately.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Honestly though, I'm not trying to be here in five years. I got a number. I hit the number, I'm gone. Simple.' | 'You want me to tell you I'm fine, I'm fine. You want the other answer, that's gonna cost you something.'

Properties.description:
Serefina is slight and quick-moving, with the compact energy of someone who grew up in small spaces. Her heritage reads clearly in her face — wide cheekbones from her Polynesian grandmother, the long straight nose of her Polish grandfather, warm olive-brown skin that tans fast. She has patterned irises: a deep violet with sunburst fractures she chose at nineteen to look dramatic and has since decided look professional, which is a different thing. Her most notable feature is a series of bioluminescent freckles across her nose and cheeks — not cosmetic geneware but a side effect of an experimental UV-response modification she accepted as a research subject during her undergrad and which no one has been able to reverse without more side effects.

She is the youngest person in her department and is painfully aware of it, which expresses as over-preparation rather than insecurity — she is always the most thoroughly sourced person in any meeting. Her work is the painstaking recovery and contextualization of biological sequence data from pre-Collapse biospheres: species that no longer exist, gene-lines that were never catalogued before they disappeared, the molecular record of a world being assembled from fragments. She finds it beautiful and devastating in equal measure, and has developed a personality that can hold both without collapsing.
Properties.role: Gene-sequence archivist and molecular historian preserving endangered biological heritage records
Properties.location: University Spine, Helix Biosystems adjacent research annex, Ironvein district
Properties.narrative_function: Specialist resource for biological and genetic information; potential discoverer of sequences that have been deliberately archived or suppressed; represents the stakes of what is being lost in Meridian 88's frantic present; character in plots involving Helix Biosystems or genetic data; humanizes scientific work through emotional honesty about what the records mean.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises (violet sunburst, chosen cosmetic). Bioluminescent freckle pattern (unintended side effect of UV-response research modification). Fine motor enhancement in both hands (research grant-funded, precision sequencing work). Personal biosample filtration implant (standard lab worker safety equipment).
Properties.core_fears: that the archive she is building will be privatized by Helix Biosystems — that the record she gives her life to will be locked behind a corporate paywall; being dismissed as too young or too junior to be trusted with difficult decisions
Properties.core_desires: to find something in the sequence archive that changes how people understand what was lost; to earn the respect of her field on her own terms, not as someone's promising student
Properties.coping_mechanisms: meticulous planning as a form of control; humor that is warmer than it sounds — she makes jokes that are also true things
Properties.blind_spots: underestimates how much the Helix Biosystems adjacency has already shaped her work in ways she cannot see from inside it; tends to trust systems — institutional, methodological — more than the people running them deserve
Properties.secret: During a routine sequence recovery, she found a set of gene records that appear to document a Helix Biosystems-patented sequence derived from an indigenous cultivar that was never consented to. The records predate Helix's patent filing by thirty years. She has made a private copy and does not know what to do with it.
Properties.story_hooks: The Helix Biosystems liaison has started attending her lab's internal review meetings — she doesn't know if this is routine or if someone told them about the cultivar sequence; A researcher from a farming community in what was once the Andes contacts her claiming descent from the group whose cultivar was in the sequence — they want to know what she found; A set of sequence records she has been working on for a year has been quietly reclassified as Helix proprietary data; the university's legal team says there's nothing they can do; She is offered an early promotion and a lab of her own — contingent on transferring her current recovery projects to Helix's internal archive team
