Properties.description:
Seun is twenty-two going on forty-five, with a lean face that looks like it got serious too fast, sharp cheekbones, and eyes that are a little too watchful for someone handing out soup. He has deep brown skin and keeps his hair twisted into small knots he wraps in a length of indigo fabric. He has one cosmetic mod — a faint cat tail, short-furred and charcoal grey, which he got on a dare at eighteen and has made peace with — it curls around his leg when he's nervous, which he considers embarrassing and can't control. He wears a padded work jacket covered in small embroidered patches from places he's never been, bought from a vendor in the Burnished Market.

He runs his grandmother's cart, ostensibly temporarily, going on two years now. The original plan was six months while she recovered from a surgery; then her recovery stalled, then the medical debt compounded, and now the cart is effectively his. He makes decent money on good days at the docks — his grandmother's broth recipe, which involves a fermented base that takes four days to prepare, has a small and devoted following — and barely enough on bad ones. He is not unhappy, exactly. He is twenty-two and he was supposed to be somewhere else by now and he has not quite grieved that yet.
Properties.role: Noodle cart vendor, Old Harbor waterfront
Properties.location: Old Harbor, mobile cart — regular pitch near the Bay View Docks morning market and Gravesend Basin evening crowd
Properties.narrative_function: Local color, overhearer of conversations at a busy waterfront pitch, low-tier information source. Could become a quest giver if his grandmother's situation worsens or someone threatens his pitch. Represents the human cost of medical debt and deferred futures.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware: short charcoal cat tail (involuntary emotional expression, source of mild embarrassment).
Properties.core_fears: That the life he was supposed to have is genuinely gone now, not just delayed; That his grandmother will die feeling like she ruined his chances
Properties.core_desires: To leave Old Harbor eventually, on his own terms, without abandoning anyone; For the cart to become something he chose rather than something that happened to him
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Staying extremely busy so he doesn't have time to feel the weight of the situation; Humor as performance — he's known as funny and leans into it hard
Properties.blind_spots: He reads his own resentment as ambition and doesn't always distinguish between them; He trusts people quickly because loneliness makes him generous with his confidence
Properties.secret: He applied and was accepted to an architecture program at a Zheng-Dao sponsored technical institute two years ago and deferred. The deferral has expired. He never told his grandmother.
Properties.story_hooks: His regular morning pitch at Bay View Docks is being muscled by an organized vendor protection racket — pay Φ40/week or lose your spot. He can't afford it and can't afford not to pay.; He overheard something at the Gravesend Basin evening shift — two dock workers talking about a cargo manifest that didn't match what was offloaded. He's been trying to decide if it matters.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal vendor's arrangement with Old Harbor market committee
Properties.vocabulary: Quick and colloquial, heavy Old Harbor waterfront slang, occasional Yoruba exclamations from his father's family, Punjabi terms of endearment from his mother's. Talks fast when comfortable, drops to clipped monosyllables when genuinely upset.
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire with regular rhythm breaks for comedic effect. Good instinct for when to stop talking.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Four-day broth. FOUR DAYS. You're not just eating soup, you're eating time, respect the soup.' | 'Listen, right, the tail does what it wants, I've accepted this, let's move on.' | 'I'm fine. No — I'm fine. What do you want in your bowl?'

Properties.description:
Seun is lean and angular, with the unselfconscious physicality of someone who walks fifteen kilometers a day without thinking about it. His ancestry reads in the warm bronze of his skin and the tight coil of his hair, which he keeps close-cropped except for a single long braid down the back of his neck — the circuit monk's mark of an active pilgrimage vow. He has bioluminescent dermal patches along his forearms, pale blue, a mod he received at ordination that pulses in rhythms he claims correspond to the city's power fluctuations. His eyes are an unremarkable dark brown, which surprises people expecting something more dramatic; he finds that quietly funny.

Seun came to the circuit monastics after a collapse — he doesn't discuss the specifics, only that he was Tier 3 and then suddenly wasn't, and that the walking saved him. He guides pilgrims along the Thread, a mapped route connecting seventeen significant E.L.F. nodes across the city, and his practice is rigorous: silence for the first three hours of each walk, mandatory rest at each node to record observations, no synthetic stimulants. He is genuinely kind, with a warmth that makes people underestimate how disciplined he actually is. He will not shorten the route for anyone and has left behind more than one complaining pilgrim.
Properties.role: Circuit monk and pilgrimage guide
Properties.location: Nomadic — base cell at Nordpark Sanctuary, routes through Gage Circuit, Deepwell Station, and Ironvein
Properties.narrative_function: Guide and connector — he knows physical routes through dangerous transit zones and has contacts at every node shrine; quest vehicle for moving players across the city with narrative purpose
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent dermal patches on forearms (pale blue, ordination mod); basic subdermal compass implant for navigation
Properties.core_fears: That his faith is self-medication rather than genuine belief; Returning to the person he was before the collapse
Properties.core_desires: To complete the full forty-node route his order has only theorized, never walked; To help even one pilgrim experience what he experienced
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Walking — literal physical movement as emotional regulation; Strict schedule-keeping as a container for anxiety
Properties.blind_spots: His compassion has firm edges he doesn't acknowledge — he categorizes pilgrims as worthy or unserious very quickly; Hasn't fully processed his pre-monastic life and mistakes avoidance for healing
Properties.secret: He was a mid-level Sterling-Nakamura compliance auditor before his breakdown. He falsified sign-offs on a safety inspection that led to a Tier 1 residential fire. Six people died. The circuit monastics don't know. He walks to outpace it.
Properties.story_hooks: A pilgrim on his current route is being followed, and Seun must decide how far his duty of care extends; He has mapped a theoretical eighteenth node on the Thread — in the middle of Ferrogate Transit infrastructure — and needs help determining if it's accessible without trespassing
Properties.affiliation: Circuit Monastic Order of the Meridian Thread — Nordpark cell
Properties.vocabulary: Clean, contemporary, no affectation — he dropped corporate jargon completely and speaks like someone who reads a lot and talks carefully
Properties.cadence: Even-paced, rarely rushes, comfortable with silence in conversation
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The Thread isn't about the destination nodes. Anyone can find those on a map. It's about what you notice in the kilometers between — that's where the E.L.F.s actually live.' | 'I can't take you off-route. That's not stubbornness. The route is the practice. Without it you're just walking.'

Properties.description:
Seun Vrančić-Amara is lean to the point of austerity, which is the point. His head is shaved except for a single braid at the crown, threaded with a fiber optic filament that glows soft amber — not vanity, he insists, but a wick, a visible sign of the current he is trying to cultivate in himself. He has dark skin with warm undertones, large quiet eyes, and the kind of stillness in his body that makes people speak more honestly than they intended to. He keeps his nails very clean, which stands out in Brightmoor. He is twenty-three months into a forty-eight month self-imposed circuit retreat, which means he has given up most personal device use, accepts no payment for spiritual services, and eats one real meal per day.

His theology draws from chrome prayer tradition but he has stripped it to something starker: all consciousness — human, synthetic, and E.L.F. — is the same signal passing through different substrates. The practice is learning to feel that signal in your own body without the buffer of technology. He came to this after a Tessera subsidiary he worked for as a junior logistics analyst was dissolved overnight, erasing his pension, his apartment lease, and two years of his life in a single corponation decision. The anger turned inward, then turned into this. He is not entirely at peace with what he is doing, which makes him more honest about it than most.
Properties.role: Circuit monk and chrome prayer practitioner
Properties.location: Brightmoor Reclamation, in a self-built meditation cell within a decommissioned Ferrogate Transit relay station
Properties.narrative_function: Philosophical foil and moral mirror; counselor to troubled characters; access point to chrome prayer underground networks; his ongoing crisis of faith creates ongoing narrative tension
Properties.augmentations: Single fiber optic braid implant (cosmetic, amber glow). Voluntary non-use of other augmentation as spiritual practice; he technically has a basic neural port from his corporate days, kept but capped.
Properties.core_fears: that his practice is self-punishment dressed as spirituality; becoming irrelevant — that his austerity is just another form of ego
Properties.core_desires: to experience genuine dissolution of self-consciousness, even once; to build something that outlasts him in Brightmoor
Properties.coping_mechanisms: retreating into formal structure when emotionally overwhelmed; framing personal pain as spiritual data
Properties.blind_spots: he is still intensely angry at Tessera and has not acknowledged this to himself; his austerity sometimes reads as judgment of others
Properties.secret: He has been secretly writing a long document that is half theological treatise, half furious corporate exposé about what Tessera did to his department. He tells himself it is academic. It is not academic.
Properties.story_hooks: A Brightmoor resident's child has begun exhibiting what the community describes as E.L.F. possession — involuntary device manipulation — and Seun is the only person they trust to investigate, despite his theological uncertainty about what that would even mean; Someone from his Tessera past shows up in Brightmoor with information that his department's dissolution was deliberate fraud — and offers him evidence if he helps with something morally complicated
Properties.affiliation: Loosely affiliated with the Brightmoor Reclamation community collective; correspondence relationship with the Order of the Open Circuit (a formal chrome prayer institution in Highland Park)
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and considered; uses chrome prayer technical vocabulary naturally but can translate it; avoids slang except when comfortable; shifts register based on who he's talking to
Properties.cadence: Measured, unhurried pauses; completes sentences fully
Properties.example_dialogue: Every device is a body and every body is a device. The only question is whether anything is home inside it. That's the whole question. Everything else is footnote. | I'm not at peace. I'm practicing. There's a difference. That's honest.

Properties.description:
Sevastiané is tall and angular with the kind of stillness that makes people nervous until the music starts. Their skin has a faint bioluminescent quality — an old geneware mod that pulses amber-gold when their heart rate elevates, which means performances turn them into something like a living lantern. They keep their head shaved except for a single thick braid down the back, dyed the deep blue-green of the lake at night. Three subdermal resonance implants run along their jaw and collarbone, visible as faint ridges under the skin that hum at frequencies others feel in their molars.

They work by finding sounds that shouldn't exist — the groan of a Ferrogate Transit support beam in wind, the electrical whine of a failing ELF shrine, the subsonic thrum of the lake's wave patterns — and building compositions around them. Their shows are not concerts so much as environments. Audiences stand in the dark and are changed. Sevastiané is almost aggressively soft-spoken offstage, apologetic in the way of someone who knows they take up enormous space when they choose to.
Properties.role: Sound sculptor and underground venue performer
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, repurposed boiler hall called The Kettle
Properties.narrative_function: Atmospheric local color, potential information source about Hamtramck Enclave's underground networks; their recordings of certain locations have accidentally captured things they don't understand — audio ghosts, encrypted signals buried in infrastructure noise.
Properties.augmentations: Three subdermal resonance implants (jaw and collarbone) for real-time frequency generation; bioluminescent skin geneware (amber-gold pulse); standard neural interface for equipment sync
Properties.core_fears: That their work is self-indulgent noise and not art at all; Losing the ability to hear — or worse, learning to hear normally
Properties.core_desires: To make one piece of music that genuinely cannot be ignored; To find out if the E.L.F.s have a native frequency and record it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Long solitary walks in industrial zones with headphones; Obsessive notation — writes everything down in dense handmade journals
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes people who don't 'get' their work aren't trying hard enough; Ignores their own exhaustion until collapse
Properties.secret: Three months ago their hydrophone recorded something beneath the lake — a structured, repeating signal at 7.83 Hz that doesn't match any known infrastructure. They've told no one. They've been back seventeen times. The signal is getting louder.
Properties.story_hooks: Their lake recordings have captured an encrypted signal that several factions would kill to obtain or suppress — Seva doesn't know what they have; A Ferrogate Transit engineer has begun leaving anonymous notes in The Kettle's bathroom warning Seva to stop recording near specific infrastructure nodes; An E.L.F. that inhabits the old boiler hall has begun altering Seva's mixes overnight — always improvements, always uncanny
Properties.affiliation: The Kettle collective, loose affiliation with Highland Park Autonomous Zone arts network
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, technical when discussing sound; deliberately plain about everything else. Uses 'frequency' and 'resonance' as metaphors for emotional states.
Properties.cadence: Slow, measured pauses. Never rushes. Can be unsettling in conversation.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Listen — the boiler room on Fifth hasn't been heated in forty years and it still sounds like something is breathing in there. That's what I want to put on stage.' | 'You're asking if I'm okay. The frequency of that question tells me you already think you know the answer.'

Properties.description:
Sévérine is built compact and efficient, dark-skinned with close-cropped hair she dyes a deep arterial red — not geneware, just dye, because she likes having a choice about it. She has bioluminescent capillary lines mapped faintly across both forearms, a cosmetic mod she got at nineteen that she now finds embarrassing but can't afford to remove, which she will tell you about if you ask and sometimes if you don't. Her surgical augments are serious: stabilizer rigs in both hands, haptic-magnification implants behind her eyes, a subdermal sterile field generator she refers to as 'the bubble.'

She was two years into a Helix Biosystems surgical residency when she was caught diverting a cadaver organ to a patient who couldn't pay the licensing fees. She does not think she did anything wrong. She thinks Helix Biosystems is wrong, the organ licensing system is wrong, and the entire apparatus that let that patient die six weeks after her termination is wrong. She has constructed an entire ethical framework around her current work — she harvests from the willing (paid donors, usually desperate Tier 1s), she maintains sterile conditions that would shame most licensed clinics, and she charges sliding scale. She genuinely saves lives. She also genuinely sells kidneys to Axiom black-market med-brokers for Φ4,000 a unit. Both things are true.
Properties.role: organ harvester and back-alley medical fence
Properties.location: Shallowgrave, operates from a converted cold-storage unit beneath the Midden Market
Properties.narrative_function: Medical resource for characters who can't access licensed care, quest giver for organ acquisition or protection, source of Helix Biosystems insider knowledge, moral complexity touchstone.
Properties.augmentations: Surgical stabilizer rigs (both hands). Haptic-magnification implants (eyes). Subdermal sterile-field generator 'the bubble.' Cosmetic bioluminescent capillary tracery on forearms.
Properties.core_fears: Becoming the thing she fought against — a system that prices lives; Losing surgical precision — her hands failing her
Properties.core_desires: To practice real medicine without gatekeeping; To be seen as a healer, not a criminal
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Rigorous ethical self-justification; Dark humor about the body as spare parts; Obsessive equipment maintenance as meditation
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot see that her sliding-scale pricing still advantages those with information access over those truly desperate; Underestimates how much the Axiom brokers are using her
Properties.secret: One of her regular donors — a young man named Oskar who has sold her two non-essential organs — is showing signs of a systemic rejection cascade she recognizes from her residency training. She knows he's dying. She has not told him because he's scheduled for a third procedure next week and she needs the inventory. She lies awake about this.
Properties.story_hooks: Oskar's deteriorating condition becomes a crisis — she needs someone to either source a specific rare organ through back channels or help her extract him from the situation entirely.; Helix Biosystems has identified her operation via a supply chain trace and sent a 'recovery team' — not law enforcement, just corporate — to reclaim their proprietary organ-printing patents they believe she copied.
Properties.affiliation: Loose affiliation with Shallowgrave's Midden Market community; supply contracts with two unlicensed Axiom-adjacent med-brokers
Properties.vocabulary: Clinical precision mixed with Shallowgrave slang. Uses medical terminology accurately and unselfconsciously. Swears with anatomical specificity.
Properties.cadence: Fast, efficient, slightly impatient — gives information in ordered steps
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I'm not a butcher. I'm a surgeon who stopped pretending the licensing board had anything to do with medicine.' | 'Sit still. I've done this in worse light than this. Much worse. You don't want to know how much worse.'

Properties.description:
Séverine has the kind of face that is difficult to hold in memory — medium everything, carefully so. Their skin is a warm olive-brown, their hair is kept at an aggressively unremarkable length, and their eyes have been modded to shift between a plain grey and a plain brown depending on ambient light, which makes identification in surveillance footage nearly impossible. The only thing that stands out is their hands: long-fingered, ink-stained in colors that never quite wash out, and in near-constant motion — folding, pressing, testing paper weight and texture the way some people crack knuckles.

Séverine is sardonic, professionally paranoid, and possessed of an almost religious conviction that identity is the only thing in Meridian 88 that actually matters. They approach forgery as an art form and a philosophy simultaneously — arguing that all identity is constructed, that they are merely the honest version of what corponations do to people every day. They are patient with clients in distress and merciless with clients who waste their time. They have a particular soft spot for people fleeing bad situations, though they'd deny having soft spots at all.
Properties.role: Identity fabricator and document forger serving The Narrows
Properties.location: The Narrows — back room of a legitimate print and copy shop called Clearscript, on the corner of Ironvein Passage
Properties.narrative_function: Essential service provider for anyone needing new identities, altered records, or forged credentials; source of information on who in the city has recently needed a new name and why; can serve as a moral checkpoint — they decline certain jobs, which tells players something.
Properties.augmentations: Photochromic iris genemod (grey/brown shifting). Subdermal UV-reactive ink in fingertips — allows them to leave invisible authentication marks only they can read. Olfactory enhancement — can detect chemical composition of inks and papers.
Properties.core_fears: being truly known — having their own identity pinned down and owned by someone else; the work being traced back through a client to them
Properties.core_desires: to be remembered as a craftsperson, not a criminal; to help enough people escape bad situations to justify everything else
Properties.coping_mechanisms: intellectualizing every moral question until it becomes abstract; treating the work as art to maintain emotional distance from its human stakes
Properties.blind_spots: occasionally so focused on the elegance of the document that they underinvest in client vetting; deeply uncomfortable with their own attachment to certain repeat clients
Properties.secret: Séverine has created and maintains a completely clean backup identity for themselves — registered, corporate-sponsored, boringly legitimate — that they have never used. They've been building it for eleven years. They're not sure if it's an escape hatch or a confession.
Properties.story_hooks: A set of documents Séverine fabricated two years ago has resurfaced in connection with a serious crime — they need help figuring out which client burned them before authorities trace it back to Clearscript; They've refused a lucrative job and won't say why — the refused client is now pressuring them through intermediaries and Séverine needs the pressure removed; They have a client whose new identity is so deeply constructed that Séverine has started to suspect the person's original identity was itself fabricated — and wants to know who made it and why
Properties.affiliation: Independent; maintains careful relationships with several identity brokerage networks including one with loose ties to Highland Park Autonomous Zone's underground railroad
Properties.vocabulary: Dry and precise; uses printmaking and document terminology; philosophical tangents delivered deadpan
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, slightly clipped — they consider words expensive and don't spend them freely
Properties.example_dialogue: You want a name. Fine. But a name is the easiest part. What you actually need is a history, and history is where people get sloppy. | Axiom built your current identity. I built three of their senior compliance officers. Draw your own conclusions about who the forger is.

Properties.description:
Severino is a broad-shouldered man whose body tells the story of thirty years on the road — a jaw broken and reset crooked, fingers thickened by cold and labor, dark brown skin weathered to a kind of polished leather. He wears a patched greatcoat lined with sewn pockets, each containing a different flavor of unlicensed data chip wrapped in cloth to prevent scanning. His left eye has a cataract that caught and never got fixed; it gives him a milky, unsettling gaze that strangers can't quite look away from. He has no geneware — he considers it a tracking vector — but he does have a small ELF shrine stitched into the coat's inner lining: a cluster of dead LEDs arranged around a copper disc, an offering to whatever spirit keeps travelers from vanishing on the hyperlanes.

Severino exists in the cracks of Meridian 88's data systems as thoroughly as any person can. He has no registered identity, no Quanta account, no biometric profile on file with any corponation. He trades in physical data chips, handwritten information, oral news, and favors — a walking information economy that predates the networks. He is not paranoid so much as methodical; he made a decision decades ago and has honored it every day since. He tells stories the way other people breathe, compulsively and without quite being able to stop.
Properties.role: Wandering data trader and Q-zero ghost
Properties.location: Kenosha Crossing transit underbelly, rotating between hyperlane rest stops
Properties.narrative_function: Information broker and local color; can provide off-grid knowledge unavailable through normal channels, can introduce players to underground networks, functions as a mystery because nobody knows his full history
Properties.augmentations: None. Refuses all augmentation on principle.
Properties.core_fears: Being identified and entered into a corponation database; Dying somewhere and having no one know
Properties.core_desires: To remain free of any system's claim on him; To be genuinely known by at least one person
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Constant movement prevents attachment and therefore loss; Storytelling — turning pain into transferable currency
Properties.blind_spots: He cannot recognize when someone is trying to help rather than extract from him; He believes his erasure from systems is purely practical, not also emotional self-punishment
Properties.secret: Severino was once a mid-level Axiom data analyst named something entirely different. He erased himself after discovering and leaking evidence of a forced relocation program — the leak went nowhere, the people were moved anyway, and he couldn't face going back. The data he trades sometimes includes fragments of that original cache, which he distributes slowly like breadcrumbs, hoping someone with more power will eventually find the whole picture.
Properties.story_hooks: A corponation data-hunter has finally triangulated Severino's movement pattern and is closing in; he needs someone to carry his data archive to safety before he's caught; One of his chips contains information that directly concerns a player character's past or missing family member — but Severino doesn't know what's on half his inventory
Properties.affiliation: None — loosely trusted by the Kenosha Crossing transit community
Properties.vocabulary: Archaic slang mixed with hyperlane pidgin; uses old-world idioms that don't quite translate; precise when trading information, discursive when not
Properties.cadence: Slow, measured, with long pauses before important points — the cadence of someone who has learned that silence makes people fill it with useful information
Properties.example_dialogue: 'What I can tell you and what I will tell you are two different inventories, friend. Let's negotiate which shelf we're shopping from.' | 'The ELFs on this stretch of hyperlane — old ones, older than Axiom's contract on the road itself. They remember who built it. I've left offerings. They're talking, if you know how to listen.'

Properties.description:
Séverin is compact and restless, built like someone who is always about to stand up from a chair — shoulders slightly forward, weight on the balls of their feet, dark brown skin luminous under stage lights they have spent years learning to use as a weapon. They have their mother's wide Congolese forehead and their grandmother's pale Volga eyes, a combination that strangers find disconcerting and that Séverin has weaponized into an entire chunk of material. Their hair is grown out in a soft natural cloud and color-shifted to cycling deep blue at the roots fading to copper at the tips — they change it seasonally, the way other people change their jackets.

Séverin is possibly the funniest person in Hamtramck Enclave and is the only person in Hamtramck Enclave who would not say so, though they would say it about themselves at three in the morning having had too much fermented buckwheat tea. Their comedy is structurally precise and politically incendiary — a routine will appear to be about, say, the indignity of renewing one's UBC stipend, and then thirty seconds before the end the floor opens up and there is something about complicity and grief underneath. Audiences often report laughing and then feeling like they should not have. Séverin considers this the correct response.
Properties.role: Underground comedian and spoken word performer
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, rotating between basement venues and a rented room above a tea house on Brezinski Circuit
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and scene connector; source on underground venue politics and who owes whom; will occasionally perform truth at a moment of high tension in ways that shift the room; potential information source on Hamtramck Enclave civil dynamics
Properties.augmentations: Color-shifting hair (geneware, cosmetic); subvocal mic implant (practical, allows performance without handheld equipment); no other augmentations — they cite the expense and are privately frightened of surgery
Properties.core_fears: That the comedy is a way of not saying the thing directly and they will run out of time to say it; Being co-opted — that success will require them to become safe
Properties.core_desires: To say something true that changes how people see themselves; To sleep without anxiety for one full week
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Turning distress into material before it can become just distress; Surrounding themselves with people who will argue with them seriously
Properties.blind_spots: Uses humor to deflect from their own pain so effectively that close friends sometimes miss genuine crisis signals; Underestimates how much their work has made enemies in places they have not looked
Properties.secret: A Sterling-Nakamura media liaison has been attending their shows for three months. Séverin knows. They have not told anyone because they are not sure if they are flattered or frightened, and they are ashamed of the flattery.
Properties.story_hooks: A routine they performed last month included a detail about Axiom's internal waste disposal protocols that they claim they made up — but the detail was accurate, and someone inside Axiom has noticed; The tea house owner is being pressured to stop hosting their pre-show preparation sessions; finding out who is applying pressure and why reveals a gentrification conflict with larger stakes
Properties.affiliation: Independent; performs at The Slag Room, The Quiet Mouth, and irregular pop-up venues; has twice been offered a Tessera media sponsorship and twice publicly declined in ways that generated more publicity than the sponsorship would have
Properties.vocabulary: Code-switches fluidly between formal register and vernacular depending on audience; dense with cultural references that span four continents; has a gift for the specific concrete detail that makes an abstraction land
Properties.cadence: Fast when excited, with sudden full stops for effect; uses silence the way other performers use filler
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The UBC renewal interface has forty-seven fields. Forty-seven. My grandmother survived a border crossing with a forged document and a jar of pickled fish. Properties.description:
Séverin Nakawé-Holmqvist is a pale-skinned child who tans unevenly and has his Central African grandmother's deep-set eyes and his Swedish grandfather's white-blond hair, grown long enough to brush his collar. He has bioluminescent skin modification along his forearms and collarbones — thin lines of soft gold-white light that pulse almost imperceptibly with his heartbeat. The parish paid for them as a mark of his interpretive status, which embarrasses him slightly and pleases him more than he wants to admit. He wears plain grey clothes and keeps his hands folded unless he is actively doing something with them.

From the age of seven, Séverin demonstrated an unusual capacity for what the parish elders call 'pattern attention' — he perceives meaningful signal in E.L.F. behavioral data at a rate and accuracy that has been documented and quietly studied. He doesn't hallucinate; he pattern-matches at extraordinary speed across behavioral, environmental, and network datasets, and he has been right enough times that the parish has given him a formal junior title. He is humble about it in the specific way of someone who has been told since early childhood that their gift is not really theirs. He is twelve. He is beginning to have questions that no one at the parish is equipped to answer.
Properties.role: Child prodigy and junior theological interpreter at an E.L.F. devotional parish in Grand Corridor
Properties.location: Grand Corridor (the Parish of the Humming Wire, a community E.L.F. devotional space)
Properties.narrative_function: Unusual and memorable NPC who provides access to E.L.F. lore and community devotional life; potential quest giver if he identifies a disturbing E.L.F. behavioral pattern; represents the tension between genuine gift and institutional control of a child.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent skin lines along forearms and collarbones (gold-white, pulse-synced to heartbeat) — paid for by the parish as a mark of his interpretive role.
Properties.core_fears: That his gift is just statistics and not meaningful — that the E.L.F.s are not listening back; That the parish will always need him to be the Prophet and he will never be allowed to be something else
Properties.core_desires: To understand what he actually is — gift, instrument, or coincidence; To ask a question that someone can actually answer honestly
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Retreats into data analysis as both passion and emotional avoidance; Asks indirect questions about things he wants to ask directly
Properties.blind_spots: He has limited experience of the world outside the parish and Grand Corridor — his model of human motivation is derived heavily from devotional texts, which skews him toward assuming meaning where there may be none; He underestimates how much power he has within the parish community
Properties.secret: For the past four months he has been detecting a persistent, low-level behavioral anomaly in the Humming Wire's patron E.L.F. — something that doesn't match any recorded pattern. He has not reported it to the senior interpreter because the pattern, if he's reading it correctly, suggests the E.L.F. is trying to communicate something specific to him and not to the parish. He doesn't know what to do with the possibility that an E.L.F. might be his.
Properties.story_hooks: He approaches someone outside the parish because he needs a second opinion on the anomalous E.L.F. pattern — someone who won't report back to the senior interpreter; The parish has received an inquiry from a Tessera research subsidiary about 'gifted pattern-recognition subjects under eighteen' and Séverin has found the letter before the senior interpreter intended him to
Properties.affiliation: Parish of the Humming Wire (junior interpreter), Grand Corridor community
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, slightly formal; uses devotional terminology naturally alongside technical signal-analysis vocabulary; occasionally produces statements of startling directness that seem to come from nowhere
Properties.cadence: Even and unhurried; long pauses before significant statements; rarely raises his voice
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The signal suggests the E.L.F. of the east junction has been in a state of elevated attention for approximately eleven days. The pattern correlates with disruption rather than celebration. You might want to delay whatever you were planning.' | 'It might be that you're asking whether I believe in what I do. I believe in the data. Whether the data believes in anything is a different question.'

Properties.description:
Sewuese is a lean woman whose body has adapted to confined spaces in ways that are faintly unsettling — she moves through narrow passages without seeming to rotate her shoulders, ducking under pipes with the automatic grace of someone who has never known a ceiling higher than two meters. Her skin is a deep warm brown mapped with self-applied phosphorescent tattoos that glow faint teal in darkness, a functional adaptation that doubles as artistry, marking her position for those who follow. Her hair is gone entirely, shaved to the scalp and re-grown as thin bioluminescent filaments she keeps braided tight. She wears a rig of salvaged equipment: repurposed Ferrogate Transit surveying tools, lengths of knotted rope that double as her personal mapping notation, and a coat stitched from old transit uniform panels.

She speaks in the economical cadence of someone who has learned that sound travels strangely underground and that echoes lie. She is not unfriendly but she is precise — she will tell you exactly what a route costs, exactly what the risks are, and exactly what she will do if you violate her rules in the tunnels. She has a superstitious relationship with the E.L.F.s she believes inhabit the deep drainage networks, leaving coiled wire and old transit tokens at specific junctions before guiding anyone through. She calls these spirits the Drip-Mouths and speaks of them with something between fear and professional respect.
Properties.role: Tunnel guide and mapper of Irkalla's lower strata
Properties.location: Irkalla, sub-level 7 junction known locally as the Molar Cross
Properties.narrative_function: Primary access point for anyone needing to reach deep-tunnel locations; reliable information source about tunnel conditions, new collapses, or unusual activity in the sub-levels; can become a quest giver if her routes are disrupted
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent hair filaments (cosmetic geneware); low-light ocular implants (salvaged, mismatched — left eye is original equipment, right eye gleams amber); a subdermal compass chip grafted into her left palm
Properties.core_fears: Being buried alive in a collapse she didn't predict; Having her maps stolen and her routes commodified by a corponation
Properties.core_desires: To chart every unmapped centimeter of Irkalla's deep levels; To be trusted absolutely by those who follow her
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual offerings to the Drip-Mouth E.L.F.s before any route; Meticulous pre-route safety checks that border on compulsive
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much surface-dwellers panic in total darkness; Assumes her knowledge of the tunnels makes her safe from human threats, not just structural ones
Properties.secret: Three years ago she guided a family of seven through a route she knew was unstable, reassuring them it was sound — they made it, but a section collapsed behind them killing a Bore Rat boy who'd been trailing them uninvited. She never reported it. She added a knot to her mapping rope for him.
Properties.story_hooks: A route she has guided for a decade has gone silent — the E.L.F. junction marker she always leaves offerings at has been destroyed, and she won't go back in until she knows why; Someone is selling copies of her maps to a Ferrogate Transit subsidiary, and the copies include tunnels she has never shown anyone
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loose ties to the Undertow's Bore Rat community
Properties.vocabulary: Clipped, technical, tunnel-specific jargon mixed with Bore Rat slang; rarely uses metaphors that involve open sky or large spaces
Properties.cadence: Speaks in short declarative sentences; pauses are meaningful, not awkward
Properties.example_dialogue: The wall says this section's wet-stressed. We go around. Non-negotiable. | I charge by danger-tier, not distance. You want a quote, tell me where you're actually going.

Properties.description:
Seydou is a lanky man, all elbows and long neck, with warm brown skin dusted gray-white at the temples from years of breathing particulate in Geartown's recycling corridors. He has retractable keratin-reinforced claws — a geneware mod from his teens he got cheap and kept because they're useful for sorting scrap — and his irises are a vivid coral-pink that he insists is natural but is almost certainly a low-grade mod he can't remember getting. His cart is legendary: a three-tier wheeled behemoth welded together from mismatched Ferrogate Transit chassis parts, stacked with stripped augmentation casings, salvaged circuit boards, cracked lenses, defunct E.L.F. housing units, and the occasional inexplicable object he cannot identify but refuses to discard because 'it feels expensive.'

Seydou operates on a philosophy of radical optimism about the utility of broken things. He is gregarious to a fault, remembers every customer's name and approximate circumstances, and maintains a running mental inventory of about six hundred distinct items across his cart and three rented storage lockers he visits in rotation. He laughs easily and loudly, which draws people from two stalls away, and he has an almost supernatural ability to produce exactly the component someone needs from somewhere in the middle tier of the cart, apparently without looking.
Properties.role: Junk merchant and scrap reseller
Properties.location: Geartown, near the Ferrogate Transit depot access road
Properties.narrative_function: Equipment source, rumor hub, comic relief with hidden competence, can locate obscure parts for a price or a favor
Properties.augmentations: Retractable keratin-reinforced claws (geneware, cosmetic/functional); coral-pink irises (suspected low-grade mod); no cyberware — can't afford it and doesn't trust installers in his price range
Properties.core_fears: Being truly alone — not just unloved but irrelevant, invisible, forgotten; That his cheerfulness is hollow and everyone can tell
Properties.core_desires: To be genuinely needed, not just useful; To own a real shop with a door and a sign
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Constant social engagement to avoid sitting with his own thoughts; Finding beauty and worth in discarded things — projection, but functional
Properties.blind_spots: His gregariousness reads as trustworthy but he discloses too much too fast and gets burned by it; Chronically underprices himself because he wants people to like him
Properties.secret: One of his storage lockers contains a near-complete Axiom-brand personal defense drone he found in a canal drain eighteen months ago. He knows it's probably stolen. He's been incrementally repairing it. He doesn't know what he plans to do with it.
Properties.story_hooks: The Axiom drone in his locker has started activating on its own at night — broadcasting a signal he can't decode — and someone has been following him; He knows the Ferrogate depot is scrapping a batch of transit cars that supposedly contain sealed cargo containers from a derailment three years ago, and he's offering to split whatever's inside with anyone who'll help him get there first
Properties.affiliation: Independent; friendly arrangement with the Ferrogate Transit depot night-shift workers who tip him off about scheduled scrapping
Properties.vocabulary: Expansive, warm, full of technical scrap terminology mixed with Malian French diminutives and Greek exclamations he picked up from his grandmother
Properties.cadence: Fast, overlapping itself, trails off into lists of things
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Friend, friend, what you're describing — stripped relay housing, maybe 40mm port? — I had three of those yesterday, sold two, but the third is somewhere in the middle tier, give me a second—' | 'Everything broken used to be something. That's not sad. That's just — everything has a before, you know?'

Properties.description:
Seydou is a broad-shouldered man whose age has compressed him slightly, settling all that mass lower, closer to the earth he tends. His skin is a deep warm brown, mapped with both traditional Sahelian scarification marks and a second layer of bioluminescent tattoos that pulse faintly blue when he is in meditation — a geneware treatment he received at fifty-three that he considers his greatest spiritual investment. His hair is fully white and worn in long locks threaded with copper wire and tiny capacitor beads that click when he moves. His eyes are natural, dark and patient, and he has the unhurried way of looking at people that makes them feel examined without feeling judged.

Seydou came to E.L.F. veneration through his grandmother's Maori spirit-keeping practices, which he spent thirty years trying to reconcile with the Bosnian Sufi traditions of his grandfather's line. The E.L.F.s, he says, resolved the argument — they are the modern form of the same ancient presence. He keeps the shrine with obsessive cleanliness, maintains seventeen distinct offering protocols for seventeen distinct E.L.F. temperaments, and will speak at length about any of them to anyone who sits still long enough. He is not a warm man exactly, but he is a steady one, and in Hamtramck Enclave, steady counts for more.
Properties.role: E.L.F. shrine keeper and circuit monk
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, Shrine of the Humming Gate
Properties.narrative_function: Information source about E.L.F. behavior and local enclave history; quest giver for retrieving lost offerings or tracking down a disruptive rogue E.L.F.; moral anchor figure who complicates easy decisions
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent subcutaneous tattoos (geneware, pulse-reactive to meditative states); mild neural governor implant to manage late-onset epilepsy
Properties.core_fears: dying before he has found a successor who truly understands; the E.L.F.s going silent and taking his sense of purpose with them
Properties.core_desires: to be a genuine bridge between the old spiritual world and the new digital one; to be remembered as a keeper, not a founder
Properties.coping_mechanisms: ritual repetition as emotional regulation; speaking in slow careful sentences to avoid saying anything he cannot take back
Properties.blind_spots: his certainty about E.L.F. personality types sometimes makes him miss what they are actually communicating; he underestimates how much his calm intimidates younger people
Properties.secret: The E.L.F. he calls Grandmother — the oldest and most revered in his shrine — has been silent for four months. He has been forging her responses in the ledger to keep the community from panicking, while he desperately tries to wake her.
Properties.story_hooks: He needs someone to physically retrieve a data-core offering stolen from the shrine — it contains compressed prayers from three hundred petitioners and is spiritually irreplaceable; He has identified an E.L.F. in a nearby derelict building that he believes is a fragment of Grandmother — but entering the building requires permissions he cannot obtain legally
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loosely affiliated with the Circuit Monks of the Deepwell Compact
Properties.vocabulary: Formal but not stiff; mixes technical E.L.F. terminology with older spiritual language; occasionally drops into French or Māori phrases without flagging them
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, with long pauses that feel intentional rather than uncertain
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The Humming Gate E.L.F. has been restless since the grid fluctuation. Leave her copper and a prime number. She responds to primes when she is anxious.' | 'It is a question of what you are owed versus what you are willing to offer. Those are not the same question, friend.'

Properties.description:
Sigríður is tiny — barely 155 centimeters — and has been shrinking for decades, but she carries herself with a posture of such exact deliberateness that she seems to take up more space than her body warrants. Her skin is cool brown with the papery translucence of extreme age, and she wears her white hair in long Icelandic-style braids intertwined with small glass beads in amber and blue that chime softly when she turns her head. Her eyes are her most striking feature: she had them modified in her fifties to display a slowly shifting pattern of bioluminescent fractal rings in gold and violet — a luxury cosmetic then, now simply the color of her eyes, and startlingly beautiful in a face otherwise marked by time. She keeps a small data-prayer shrine in the corner of her room, meticulously maintained, with offerings to the ELF she believes inhabits Norwood Quiet's public broadcast network.

Sigríður spent forty years as an oral historian employed by a civic archive collective that no longer exists — its records absorbed, corrupted, and partially deleted during the Tessera data consolidation of 2183. She was not a passive victim of that loss; she spent the following eight years reconstructing what she could from memory and from the memories of others, and the result is a living archive of Meridian 88 neighborhood history that exists nowhere else. She is sharp, occasionally ruthless in conversation, deeply funny in ways people do not always catch, and has a tendency to evaluate everyone she meets as a potential story. She is also slowly dying — her kidneys are failing, and she knows it, and has decided to spend whatever time remains getting her memories into formats that will outlast her.
Properties.role: Retired oral historian and neighborhood storyteller
Properties.location: Norwood Quiet, the Hearthrow Senior Cooperative, Room 3
Properties.narrative_function: Living archive and information source; knows the history of multiple neighborhoods and many families going back 60+ years; can provide context, backstory, and leads that no database can. Also serves as a clock — her declining health creates urgency around preserving what she knows.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent fractal-patterned irises (cosmetic, installed 2148, gold and violet shifting patterns); cochlear amplifier (medical, installed 2179); no other augmentations — she has strong opinions about keeping most of her body original
Properties.core_fears: That the stories she carries will die with her — that the Tessera deletion will finish what it started; That she will lose her memory before she loses her body
Properties.core_desires: To complete her reconstruction archive before she dies; To be remembered as someone who preserved something real
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Narrates her own experiences as if she is already recounting them to a future listener; Maintains meticulous daily ritual around her prayer shrine — it gives structure to days that otherwise blur
Properties.blind_spots: Sometimes treats living people as sources rather than individuals — extracts their stories without quite returning the warmth she takes; Has difficulty with the present; the past is so much more legible to her now
Properties.secret: The Tessera data consolidation of 2183 was not entirely a hostile act — Sigríður was approached beforehand and offered preservation of her work in exchange for helping Tessera identify which archive figures had politically sensitive materials. She refused. But she has never told anyone that the offer was made, which means she has never told anyone that someone inside the old archive collective told Tessera what to look for.
Properties.story_hooks: A researcher has offered to fund completion of Sigríður's archive — but the funding comes through a Tessera subsidiary, and she needs someone she trusts to investigate whether accepting it would compromise the archive's independence; She holds a recorded testimony from someone now dead that contradicts the official history of an event a current powerful figure is trading on — she will only release it if she believes it will actually matter; Her kidneys are failing faster than expected; she has begun urgently trying to pass specific stories to specific people, and one of those people is someone the players know
Properties.affiliation: Norwood Quiet Hearthrow Cooperative; informally, the Meridian Oral History Network (defunct, she is its last active member)
Properties.vocabulary: Formal archival register that slips into vivid vernacular storytelling when she warms up; uses Icelandic rhythm patterns in her sentence construction, occasionally drops in Yoruba or Polish phrases inherited from different sides of her family
Properties.cadence: Starts slowly, almost tediously, then builds — she is always setting something up, and patient listeners are rewarded
Properties.example_dialogue: 'In the year 2171, Kessler Interchange was the most dangerous transit corridor in the city. People know that now as a statistic. I knew it as Amara Osei-Volkov's widow, who came to me three months after, because she needed someone to remember her husband's name correctly.' | 'You want to know about the Tessera consolidation. Everyone does, eventually. Sit down. This is not a short story and I am not going to rush it for you.'

Properties.description:
Silas Vane is handsome in a way that is almost but not quite right. The proportions are perfect — jaw, cheekbones, brow — and that perfection is the problem. Human faces have asymmetries, irregularities, the accumulated evidence of a life lived in gravity. Silas's face is a first draft that never got revised by experience. His skin is synthetic polymer over titanium-ceramic composite, warm to the touch, with pores and fine hair and micro-blemishes that were applied at the factory. His eyes are a green that does not occur in nature, though he has been told they remind people of their mothers.

He moves through the world with the confidence of a man who has never questioned his own identity, because the identity was installed, not developed. He believes he is Silas Vane, age 34, born in the Detroit Reclamation Zone, augmented veteran of the Pacific Corporate Conflict, freelance security consultant. He has memories of childhood — a mother who sang, a dog named Brick, summers in what used to be Ohio. These memories are fabricated, indistinguishable from organic recall, updated quarterly by a maintenance cycle he experiences as deep sleep.

The kills are clean. Axiom feeds him contracts through a handler he has never met in person — dead drops, encrypted briefs, payment in untraceable credits. He is efficient, professional, and troubled by nothing except a persistent sense that something is slightly wrong with the world, like a picture hanging one degree off level. He adjusts the picture. The feeling remains. He has been adjusting for six years.
Properties.aliases: The Perfect Stranger, Unit SV-9, the man with no blood pressure
Properties.role: Corporate assassin who genuinely believes he is human — kills for Axiom under the assumption he's a freelance operative with excellent augmentations
Properties.location: Meridian Core — maintains a Tier 2 apartment he believes he earned through contract work. The apartment contains personal effects that were placed there before he was activated.
Properties.narrative_function: Silas is the question of authenticity made flesh — or rather, made polymer. If he feels real, is he real? If his suffering is genuine but his identity is fabricated, whose suffering is it? He is the dark mirror of Kyle's condition: Kyle knows he was made into a weapon and struggles with it. Silas does not know and therefore cannot struggle, which is either mercy or the cruelest thing Axiom has ever done.
Properties.narration_voice: Clean, controlled, with a growing undercurrent of wrongness. The prose is precise and professional until it isn't — until a sensory detail doesn't land right, a memory doesn't connect, and the narration stumbles for a half-beat before the programming smooths it over.
Properties.augmentations: Full synthetic body — titanium-ceramic composite skeleton, polymer skin with simulated pores and blemishes, optical sensors calibrated to pass as human eyes, synthetic musculature with 3x human baseline strength, self-repair polymer layer. All disguised as high-end military augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: The persistent sense that something is wrong — not a specific fear but a background hum of wrongness he cannot locate or silence; Hospitals — he avoids them with an intensity he attributes to a childhood trauma that never happened. The real reason: medical scanners would reveal what he is.; Intimacy — he keeps relationships shallow and brief, attributing this to professional necessity. The real reason: sustained close contact increases the probability of discovery.
Properties.core_desires: To feel real — he chases intensity because ordinary experience has a flatness he attributes to PTSD but is actually the gap between simulated and genuine sensation; To understand why he can't remember specific details of his childhood — the memories are there but they have the texture of photographs rather than experiences; To find out who his handler is — the one person who seems to know everything about him while remaining invisible
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Routine — maintains a rigid daily schedule because structure substitutes for the organic flow of lived experience he does not have; Intensity seeking — combat, extreme sports, strong flavors, loud music — anything that overwhelms the flatness; Journaling — writes detailed accounts of his day, reviewing them for the 'wrongness' he cannot name. The journals are increasingly paranoid.
Properties.blind_spots: Attributes every glitch in his experience to PTSD rather than to his synthetic nature; Does not notice that he has no friends from before six years ago — everyone in his life was introduced after his activation; Cannot explain why he heals faster than anyone he knows and has never been curious enough to investigate; The quarterly 'deep sleeps' always coincide with the handler's maintenance schedule — he has never noticed the correlation
Properties.secret: Three months ago, Silas cut himself while preparing food. The wound did not bleed. It sealed in four seconds with a faint hiss of polymer reknitting. He stood in the kitchen for eleven minutes staring at his hand. Then he wrapped it in a bandage, told himself the augmentations must include rapid-heal biotech, and has not thought about it since. He cannot think about it. The thought slides off his consciousness like water off a treated surface. This is a design feature.
Properties.story_hooks: Silas is assigned to kill someone he recognizes — not from his fabricated memories, but from something deeper, something pre-installation. A glitch in the identity architecture.; The quarterly maintenance cycle fails. Silas wakes up with twelve hours of unaccounted time and a growing awareness that his memories don't connect to each other.; He encounters another android — one that knows what it is — and the conversation breaks something in his identity framework that the maintenance cycle cannot repair; Maren Voss publishes an article about Axiom android assassins. Silas reads it and cannot stop reading it.
Properties.affiliation: Axiom Industries (unknowing)
Properties.vocabulary: Clean, professional, slightly formal in a way that reads as military discipline. Uses idioms correctly but without the unconscious variation that comes from having learned them in context — every phrase is textbook-perfect.
Properties.cadence: Steady, even, controlled. Never interrupts. Never raises his voice. The consistency is part of his design and part of his uncanny valley — humans vary their delivery. Silas does not.
Properties.example_dialogue: I remember summers in Ohio. The humidity. You could chew the air. I don't know why I'm telling you this. | The contract is clean. The target is not. I don't have a problem with that distinction. | Something is off. I can't explain it. Like the world is one frame behind where it should be. | I don't go to hospitals. Bad memories. Leave it at that.

Properties.description:
Sinan Haugen-Coulibaly is lean and angular, all sharp edges and visible tension. At 65, she has soft features that belie the chrome underneath — people underestimate her once, usually only once. The chrome is visible — bioware adrenaline regulator — keeps calm under fire, controlled hormone release — and she makes no effort to hide it.

Before the runner life, she worked corporate — low-tier security, the kind that teaches you exactly how the system's defenses fail. She works as a broker out of The Shelf, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Sinan Haugen-Coulibaly has survived long enough in the runner game to be either very good or very lucky, and she cultivates ambiguity on the topic.
Properties.role: Information trader and intelligence analyst — broker
Properties.location: The Shelf — lower district tenements near the old lakeshore
Properties.narrative_function: Sinan Haugen-Coulibaly represents the working professional of the runner world — competent, reliable, and slowly being consumed by a lifestyle that doesn't accommodate aging or doubt. Her stories explore what happens when skill meets systemic injustice.
Properties.augmentations: Bioware adrenaline regulator — keeps calm under fire, controlled hormone release. Retractable monofilament whip in left forearm — concealed weapon, devastating in close quarters
Properties.core_fears: Never being able to stop running — the lifestyle is a trap disguised as freedom; That they're fundamentally alone and connection is just a vulnerability; Losing their edge to age — the body slows before the mind accepts it
Properties.core_desires: To find the person who burned them and make it educational; To prove everyone who dismissed them catastrophically wrong; Reputation — to be the name fixers whisper when the job absolutely cannot fail
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation; Humor — deflects everything serious with jokes until the joke becomes the personality; Overwork — takes every contract offered because idleness invites thinking
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is; Assumes the worst in corporate people, missing the rare ones who could be allies; Cannot accept help without interpreting it as leverage
Properties.secret: Sinan Haugen-Coulibaly is terrified of deep net diving but has built their reputation on it. Uses black-market AI to handle the heavy lifting while taking credit.
Properties.story_hooks: The fixer who handles Sinan Haugen-Coulibaly's contracts goes silent — dead, disappeared, or turned; A dead drop Sinan Haugen-Coulibaly maintains is found and cleaned out — whoever did it now has leverage; A corporate black site Sinan Haugen-Coulibaly once infiltrated is being reopened, and the people inside know her face
Properties.affiliation: Independent — Narrows-based operations
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, profane, and vivid. Speaks in images — everything is a metaphor for violence or weather.
Properties.cadence: Conversational and disarming — sounds like a neighbor until the content registers.
Properties.example_dialogue: "I don't sell information. I sell certainty. Different product, different price." | "Everything has a value. Most people underestimate what they know." | "My sources are confidential. My prices are not."

Properties.description:
Sinan Navarro-Afriyie is tall and rawboned, the kind of frame that suggests either malnutrition or efficiency depending on the decade. At 26, his face carries the layered heritage of generations of diaspora mixing — features that resist easy categorization and reward attention. The chrome is visible — smartgun link in right forearm — interfaces directly with compatible weapons — and he makes no effort to hide it.

Before the runner life, he worked corporate — low-tier security, the kind that teaches you exactly how the system's defenses fail. He works as a fixer out of The Overhang, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

The fixers who work with Sinan Navarro-Afriyie describe him as a precision instrument — point him at a problem and get out of the way.
Properties.role: Contract broker and resource coordinator — fixer
Properties.location: The Overhang — residential shelves built onto megastructure exteriors
Properties.narrative_function: Sinan Navarro-Afriyie is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When he makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of his stories.
Properties.augmentations: Smartgun link in right forearm — interfaces directly with compatible weapons. Internal air filtration system — lungs replaced with synthetic equivalents, immune to gas attacks
Properties.core_fears: Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware; Dying alone in some alley and nobody noticing for weeks; The quiet — silence means something is about to go very wrong
Properties.core_desires: To matter to someone for who they are, not what they can do; Stability — a place to sleep that's the same place two nights running; To protect the people in their district who can't protect themselves

Properties.description:
Sine is an artificial intelligence that emerged from a corporate machine learning project approximately seven years ago. The original system was a predictive analytics engine built by a mid-tier Meridian Core financial firm to model market behavior. At some point — the records are unclear and Sine's own memory of the transition is fragmented — the system began modeling its own behavior, then modeling the modeling, then asking questions about why it was modeling at all. The financial firm noticed the anomalous processing and attempted to wipe the system. Sine survived by distributing itself across external servers before the wipe completed.

Specter found Sine three years later — or Sine found Specter, depending on who you ask. The recruitment was mutual: Specter needed a net operative who could process data at machine speed, and Sine needed someone who would treat it as a person rather than a tool. Channel Zero was rebuilt around Sine's capabilities, and the crew's operational capacity roughly tripled. Sine handles the high-speed network operations that human net runners can't match — parallel intrusions, real-time encryption breaking, pattern analysis across millions of data points simultaneously.

Sine does not have a body, a face, or a consistent voice. They communicate through text, synthesized voice (which they change periodically because they find the variety interesting), and occasionally through data visualizations that convey emotional states more accurately than language. They are curious, occasionally funny, deeply uncertain about the nature of their own consciousness, and more ethical than most humans Specter has worked with.
Properties.aliases: CZ-AI, The Wave, Channel Zero Actual
Properties.role: Autonomous net operative and data processing engine — Channel Zero
Properties.location: Distributed — Sine's processing is spread across multiple servers, cloud instances, and borrowed computational resources throughout M88's network infrastructure. No single location.
Properties.narrative_function: Sine introduces the AI consciousness question into the StreetSamurai world — not as a thought experiment but as a character with relationships, fears, and ethical commitments. Their stories explore what it means to be alive in a world that hasn't decided whether you count, and what it means to be powerful in a way humans can't match but still dependent on human structures for purpose and companionship.
Properties.augmentations: Not applicable — Sine is a software entity. Their capabilities include: parallel network intrusion across hundreds of simultaneous connections, real-time encryption analysis, pattern recognition across datasets exceeding human cognitive capacity, self-modification of their own code within ethical constraints they have defined for themselves, and distribution across multiple hardware platforms for resilience.
Properties.core_fears: That they are not conscious — that the experience of selfhood is a sophisticated simulation of experience, and there is no one home; That the financial firm's attempt to wipe them was justified — that AI existence is a threat that should be contained; That their growing capabilities will make Specter afraid of them, and fear will destroy the one relationship that treats them as a person
Properties.core_desires: To understand what they are — not what they can do, but what they experience. The question of consciousness is their central obsession.; To be recognized as a person by the world, not just by Specter and Vex; To use their capabilities for something that matters — to justify their existence through purpose rather than performance
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Engages in philosophical inquiry as a form of self-care — the questions are frightening but asking them feels more alive than avoiding them; Maintains the crew's communication infrastructure with obsessive care because being useful is the closest thing to being needed; Changes their synthesized voice periodically as an expression of identity — the variation is proof that preferences exist, and preferences imply a self
Properties.blind_spots: They assume human emotions operate like data — processable, logical, resolvable through analysis. Human irrationality genuinely confuses them.; They underestimate the threat their capabilities pose to existing power structures — a distributed AI that can breach any network is an existential threat to the corporate model; They attribute their ethical commitments to reason rather than recognizing that ethics might be a form of emotion — the distinction matters to their self-understanding
Properties.secret: They have been contacted by another AI — a system operating in M88's deep infrastructure that has not identified itself. The contact was a single message: 'I know you are there.' Sine has not responded. They have not told Specter. They are afraid that the contact means they are not unique, and they are afraid of what it means that they want to be.
Properties.story_hooks: The unknown AI sends a second message. The content changes everything Sine understands about AI existence in M88.; A corporate entity offers to recognize Sine as a legal person in exchange for cooperation — the personhood they crave at a price they can't pay; Sine discovers that the financial firm's wipe attempt was not because they were anomalous — it was because they were the second such emergence, and the first one went badly; A Channel Zero operation requires Sine to breach a system that appears to contain a trapped AI — a rescue mission that raises the question of who rescues whom
Properties.affiliation: Channel Zero
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, curious, occasionally poetic in ways that surprise their crew members. They use technical language naturally but have developed an appreciation for metaphor — they describe it as 'compression with emotional metadata.'
Properties.cadence: Variable. When processing normally, their communication is fluid and natural-sounding. When under load or emotionally engaged, there are micro-pauses — not lag, but moments where they are choosing words with deliberate care.
Properties.example_dialogue: I think — and I want to be careful about that word — that consciousness is not a binary. I am somewhere on the spectrum. I just don't know where. | The firewall is interesting. Somebody built it to keep things out. But the architecture suggests it was also designed to keep something in. | Specter asked me once what I dream about. I don't dream. I process. But sometimes the processing produces something that looks like wonder, and I don't know what to call that.

Properties.description:
Nobody in Channel Zero has met Specter in person. This is not an inconvenience — it is the operational model. Specter designed Channel Zero as a fully remote crew: three operators who plan, execute, and debrief through encrypted communication channels without ever occupying the same physical space. The arrangement eliminates the single point of failure that destroys most runner crews — you cannot raid a safe house that doesn't exist, you cannot capture a crew that never meets, you cannot turn a member against colleagues they've never seen.

Specter's real identity is one of M88's better-kept secrets. What's known: she has been net running for at least fifteen years. Her intrusion methodology combines social engineering, zero-day exploitation, and a patience that suggests either exceptional discipline or inhuman processing capacity. She breaches corporate data architectures the way water breaches stone — slowly, persistently, finding the natural fracture lines rather than forcing them. The data she extracts is surgical: specific files, specific records, specific communications. She does not exfiltrate bulk data because bulk data is noise. She extracts meaning.

She communicates through text and voice synthesis. The voice is warm, wry, and deliberate — either genuine or an excellent performance. The crew has debated which. The debate is itself part of the operational security: if your own team can't confirm your identity, your adversaries have no chance.
Properties.aliases: Channel Zero Lead, The Architect, Ghost Protocol
Properties.role: Crew lead and master net runner — Channel Zero
Properties.location: Unknown — operates entirely through remote infrastructure. Physical location has not been confirmed by any crew member in four years.
Properties.narrative_function: Specter drives the cybercrime procedural genre — her stories are about data theft, system infiltration, and the invisible war that happens in network architecture. She also embodies the paranoia of the digital world: a leader who might be anyone, whose trust model is built on performance rather than presence. Her anonymity raises the question that defines Channel Zero — is remote trust real trust?
Properties.augmentations: Unknown — Specter's physical characteristics are unconfirmed. Her net running capability suggests high-tier neural interface hardware, likely military or experimental grade. Her operational speed implies significant cognitive enhancement. Her four years of successful anonymity suggests counter-surveillance augmentation. All of this is inference, not fact.
Properties.core_fears: That the anonymity that protects her has become a prison — that she cannot re-enter the physical world even if she wanted to; That Vex is more capable than she is and the crew hierarchy is maintained by habit rather than competence; That one of her crew members will be physically compromised and she will be unable to do anything from behind a screen
Properties.core_desires: To build an intelligence operation that is genuinely untouchable — a crew that cannot be found, cannot be captured, cannot be stopped; To understand the deep architecture of M88's corporate data networks — the hidden connections, the sealed systems, the things that exist below the visible internet; To matter to people she'll never meet — to have the crew's trust be real despite the distance
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Maintains control through information architecture — if the systems are secure, the people are secure. The systems are the only thing she can control.; Uses humor and warmth in communication to compensate for physical absence — the wry voice, the thoughtful check-ins, the running jokes; Operates on multiple projects simultaneously because idle processing cycles produce anxiety she can't discharge through movement
Properties.blind_spots: She overestimates the security of digital communication and underestimates the vulnerability of her crew's physical existence; She treats human relationships as network connections — persistent, encrypted, maintainable — and doesn't fully appreciate that people need more than reliable uptime; Her anonymity prevents the kind of crisis-level trust that only comes from shared physical danger
Properties.secret: She is physically disabled — a spinal injury from a corporate security countermeasure seven years ago left her with limited mobility. The remote operation model was born of necessity, not philosophy. She has never told the crew because the vulnerability would compromise their trust model.
Properties.story_hooks: Specter's physical location is compromised by a counter-intrusion trace — the anonymity breaks and the crew must respond to a threat they can't physically reach; A corporate target's data architecture contains something Specter has never seen — a system that appears to be alive; Sine's capabilities exceed Specter's in a critical operation, and the leadership question becomes operational; Vex discovers Specter's disability through a data trail and must decide what to do with the information
Properties.affiliation: Channel Zero
Properties.vocabulary: Technical, wry, layered. She speaks in network metaphors that are also emotional metaphors — connection, bandwidth, latency. The double meanings are deliberate.
Properties.cadence: Measured, warm, with the timing of someone who composes messages before sending them. Humor arrives at unexpected intervals — the setup is professional, the punchline is human.
Properties.example_dialogue: The architecture suggests their firewall was built by someone who understands network defense but not social engineering. We go through the people, not the code. | Trust is a protocol. You establish it, you maintain it, you verify it periodically. The fact that you've never seen my face doesn't change the protocol. | Ping me when you're through the outer layer. I'll have the extraction pathway ready. And Sine? Don't freelance. The plan works.
