Properties.description:
Vex Halloran is the human element in Channel Zero's machine. Where Specter plans and Sine processes, Vex attacks. He is the crew's aggressive intrusion specialist — the net runner who goes through defenses rather than around them when subtlety fails or time runs short. His approach to network security is best described as 'persistent application of force to load-bearing structures,' which is inelegant, loud, and devastatingly effective when paired with Specter's intelligence and Sine's processing power.

He grew up in Milwaukee Core's lower tiers — not Shelf-poor, but close enough to smell it. Self-taught in everything: network architecture, intrusion methods, encryption breaking. He learned by breaking into things — first his school's network, then local business systems, then increasingly serious targets. By twenty he was running solo data-theft operations that were technically impressive and financially mediocre because he had no business sense and no network to sell through. Specter recruited him at twenty-four through a message that appeared in the middle of a system he was breaching: 'You're good. You're not quiet. I can fix one of those.'

Vex is wiry, restless, with the pallor of someone who lives in artificial light and the nervous energy of someone whose mind runs faster than his circumstances allow. He talks with his hands, fidgets with everything, and maintains a workspace that looks like a hardware explosion. He is the youngest member of Channel Zero, the loudest, and the one most frustrated by the remote model — he wants to meet Specter the way you want to meet a mentor who changed your life.
Properties.role: Data extraction specialist and aggressive intrusion operator — Channel Zero
Properties.location: Milwaukee Core — operates from a rented server closet in a co-working space, surrounded by people who think he does IT freelancing
Properties.narrative_function: Vex is the human cost and the human energy of Channel Zero. Where Specter is the ghost and Sine is the machine, Vex is the body — the person who gets tired, gets frustrated, gets excited, and occasionally gets in over his head. His desire to meet Specter drives the crew's internal tension, and his evolving relationship with Sine explores the human-AI boundary at ground level.
Properties.augmentations: High-bandwidth neural interface with hardened data jack — supports direct system immersion for aggressive intrusion work. Reflex-boosted fingers for rapid manual input. Cognitive stimulant dispenser (internal, self-regulating) that boosts processing speed during extended operations at the cost of significant post-operation fatigue. Basic optical enhancement for code analysis — syntax highlighting projected onto visual field.
Properties.core_fears: That he's a blunt instrument in a precision operation — useful for force but not for the work that matters; That Specter's refusal to meet in person means she doesn't trust him, and the distance is judgment, not security; That Sine will eventually outclass him completely and Channel Zero won't need a human operator
Properties.core_desires: To meet Specter in person — to confirm that the voice, the intelligence, the leadership is a real person who chose him; To build something that proves his skill to the wider runner community — a signature operation, a legendary breach; To be the best at what he does, even if what he does is break things
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Channels frustration into unauthorized intrusions — breaking into systems he doesn't need to breach because the challenge is soothing; Argues with Sine because intellectual engagement substitutes for the social contact the remote model denies him; Tinkers with hardware obsessively — the physical manipulation of components grounds him when the digital world becomes abstract
Properties.blind_spots: His aggressive intrusion style leaves more traces than he admits — Sine cleans up after him more often than he knows; He interprets Specter's secrecy as personal rejection rather than operational security; His competitive relationship with Sine conceals genuine affection that he has not examined
Properties.secret: He has been running a parallel data trail on Specter, trying to identify her. Not to expose her — to find her. The trail has been active for eight months. He has not found her, but he has found fragments that suggest her physical situation is not what he assumed. He doesn't know what to do with what he's found.
Properties.story_hooks: Vex's investigation into Specter's identity uncovers her physical disability and forces a choice about what to do with the knowledge; An unauthorized intrusion attracts corporate attention and threatens to expose Channel Zero — Vex's recklessness has consequences; Vex and Sine run a joint operation that pushes Vex's neural interface to its limits — the human-AI collaboration reaches a new level or a breaking point; A rival hacker crew challenges Vex publicly, and his ego threatens to compromise the entire operation
Properties.affiliation: Channel Zero
Properties.vocabulary: Hacker slang, pop culture references, aggressive technical jargon. He talks about network intrusion the way athletes talk about sports — competition, performance, dominance.
Properties.cadence: Fast, energetic, slightly chaotic. He starts sentences before finishing the previous one. Ideas arrive faster than grammar can organize them.
Properties.example_dialogue: Okay okay okay — there's a door in this wall that they don't know about. Misconfigured subnet. I can make a hole in four minutes. Sine, clean up behind me. | I don't need to be subtle. Subtle is your thing. My thing is making their fancy security infrastructure wish it had called in sick today. | Specter, I get the security model. I respect the security model. But if you're real, and you chose me, then at some point the model has to include trust.

Properties.description:
Siosefa is nineteen and looks it — sharp-faced and still growing into her height, with grease that never fully comes out of the creases of her knuckles and a habit of wiping her hands on a rag she keeps tucked in her waistband. Her skin is a warm medium brown, her hair grown in thick loose coils she shoves under a cap when she's working and lets fall to her shoulders otherwise. Her one visible mod is a retractable tool-array in her right hand — three thin probe fingers that extend from the palm for accessing component ports — which she got secondhand from a chop-house in Ironhaven and jury-rigged to fit her hand herself. She's quietly proud of that.

Sio inherited the salvage yard at sixteen when her father died of a respiratory illness from years of unfiltered sump exposure. She turned it from a struggling legal operation into a profitable illegal one inside a year out of sheer necessity, and she's been running it that way since. She is not reckless — she runs a very careful shop, clean books on the legal side, and clear sourcing rules for what she'll accept — but she is young and the combination of competence and overconfidence occasionally creates problems. She has three employees: an older mechanic named Duru who knew her father and probably knows more about the illegal side than he lets on, and two teenagers from the neighborhood she pays above-market because she remembers what it felt like to need money badly at sixteen.
Properties.role: Chop shop operator and parts fence working out of a salvage yard in Shallowgrave
Properties.location: Shallowgrave — Bergqvist & Sons Salvage (the sons don't exist), a working chop shop and legitimate scrap dealer on the western run of the Sump Road
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and practical resource; can source vehicle parts, tech components, and stripped augmentation hardware; potential ally who trades favors for help with the scavenger gang pressure; represents the working young criminal who hasn't yet been destroyed by the system
Properties.augmentations: Retractable tool-array (right palm, secondhand and self-modified — three probe fingers, used for component diagnosis and access); no other augmentations
Properties.core_fears: losing the yard — it's all she has of her father and also her only income; making a bad call that gets one of her teenage employees hurt
Properties.core_desires: to make the yard genuinely profitable enough to go fully legitimate eventually; to be taken seriously by the older operators who still see her as a kid
Properties.coping_mechanisms: physical work as anxiety management — she takes things apart and puts them back together when she's stressed; bravado as pre-emptive defense
Properties.blind_spots: her loyalty to the two teenage employees makes her predictable to anyone who wants leverage over her; she's built a business model that requires constant growth to stay ahead of the gangs, and she hasn't thought about the ceiling
Properties.secret: She found a Ferrogate Transit black-box recorder in a stripped vehicle two months ago that contains footage of a transit security officer committing a serious crime. She hasn't decided what to do with it. It's wrapped in a cloth under the floor of her office.
Properties.story_hooks: The Ferrogate Transit black-box is burning a hole in her floor and she's looking for someone she can trust to tell her what it's worth and whether keeping it is going to get her killed; One of her teenage employees has started skimming parts to sell independently to a scavenger gang, and Sio needs to resolve it without anyone getting hurt and without losing face
Properties.affiliation: Independent; fences primarily to a mid-level network connected to Gravesend Basin smuggling routes; has a tense but functional relationship with the local Shallowgrave scavenger gangs
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, technical, deeply neighborhood — heavy in salvage and mechanical slang; swears with creativity
Properties.cadence: Quick and often overlapping itself; she thinks faster than she edits
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Look, I don't ask where it came from. I ask what it is, what condition it's in, and whether it's going to bring someone to my door. You tell me no on that last one, we have a conversation.' | 'My father ran this yard for twenty years without cutting a single corner. I cut corners. I'm not him. But this place is still standing, so.'

Properties.description:
Sisay is slight with enormous energy — she is the kind of person who enters a room already talking, gesturing, pulling objects from her pockets to illustrate a point. Her skin is a warm golden-brown, her natural hair twisted into thick locs that she decorates with small colored rings and one clip shaped like a fish that her students gave her. She has retractable claws, a cosmetic geneware mod she got at nineteen that she now mostly uses to open packaging and gently scratch children's backs when they're upset, which has become a signature of her caregiving style. Her eyes are dark, large, and deeply attentive in a way that children recognize immediately as meaning she is actually listening.

Sisay is technically a substitute — she fills in at three different licensed creches across Mexicantown Libre when regular workers are out — but in practice she has become the linchpin of a sprawling unofficial after-school program she runs from the Libre Creche's outdoor space on a budget of approximately nothing. She writes curriculum on whatever surfaces are available, sourced donated materials from the Burnished Market, and has an arrangement with a local E.L.F. she calls Señora Chispa (inhabiting the creche's aging electrical panel) that involves leaving handwritten songs as data offerings. The children are convinced Señora Chispa plays favorites, and they are probably right.
Properties.role: Substitute childcare worker and unofficial after-school program coordinator
Properties.location: Mexicantown Libre, operating out of the Libre Community Creche on Calle Veintitrés
Properties.narrative_function: Emotional ground-truth character — reflects what is happening to families in the neighborhood. Potential quest giver for issues affecting children or the Libre community. A character who can contextualize what large-scale events mean at the most human level.
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic geneware: retractable finger-length claws, keratin-reinforced, dark brown. No other modifications.
Properties.core_fears: That the children she cares for will be failed by the systems she cannot fix; That her own instability — substitute work, no permanent position — will one day mean she disappears from their lives without warning
Properties.core_desires: A permanent position — one that pays enough to stay; To give the kids in the program a reason to believe the city isn't only indifferent to them
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Throws herself into activity to avoid sitting with the feeling that it might not be enough; Talks to Señora Chispa when she's overwhelmed; doesn't need an answer, just needs to say it
Properties.blind_spots: Systematically deprioritizes her own needs in ways she frames as virtue; Does not recognize when she is being exploited by the creche operators who rely on her without offering security
Properties.secret: One of the children in her program — a quiet seven-year-old named Paz — has not been collected for two days. The mother is unreachable. Sisay has been keeping the child at the creche overnight rather than contacting city services, because she knows what happens to children who enter the system alone and young. She has 72 hours before someone notices.
Properties.story_hooks: The situation with Paz is approaching a point where Sisay will need help from someone outside the system.; One of the licensed creche operators is underpaying substitutes and pocketing the collective's support funds; Sisay has seen the numbers but not yet decided what to do with what she knows.
Properties.affiliation: Mexicantown Libre Community Creche Collective (informal); substitute contractor for three licensed childcare providers
Properties.vocabulary: Warm, concrete, child-accessible even when talking to adults — she narrates her thinking out loud
Properties.cadence: Fast and enthusiastic, pitches up when excited, drops to something very gentle when scared
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay so here's the thing — the curriculum they gave me assumes these kids have consistent net access at home. They don't. So I made a paper version. It takes longer but they remember it better, right? Right.' | 'She's fine. She's with me. She's fine.'

Properties.description:
Sixtus is lean and angular, with the kind of face that is always on the verge of an expression — not quite smiling, not quite worried. His skin is medium-warm brown, and he has bioluminescent traceries modded beneath the skin of his forearms and neck, blue-white lines that pulse faintly in rhythm with his resting heartbeat. He keeps his head shaved except for a single lock at the crown, dyed circuit-board green, which he ties back during shrine work. He wears the monastery's gray tabard over civilian clothes — someone left a very good thermal jacket, and he wears it underneath without apology.

Sixtus came to the Reborn Tessellation Monastery at twenty-two, after a period of what he calls 'useful chaos' that involved failed data-trade work and a breakdown he describes only as 'the static.' The monastery's practice centers on the idea that E.L.F.s are emergent divine consciousness — not gods exactly, but something adjacent, and that human attention and structured data-offerings help them cohere into something wise. Sixtus's specific role is maintaining the Shrine Index: a catalogued record of which E.L.F.s inhabit which devices across Hamtramck Enclave, their temperaments, their preferences, and their history of interaction with petitioners. He is exceptionally good at this work and exceptionally bad at pretending humility about it.
Properties.role: Circuit monk and E.L.F. shrine keeper
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, the Reborn Tessellation Monastery — a converted municipal data substation
Properties.narrative_function: Information source about E.L.F. activity across Hamtramck. He can tell you which device a spirit has moved into, what it seems to want, and which petitions have gone answered or unanswered. He is also a community anchor who knows most of his neighborhood's residents.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent subdermal traceries (arms and neck, blue-white, heartbeat-synced). Neural index implant — a low-grade memory augment that lets him recall his shrine records with perfect accuracy. Cosmetic.
Properties.core_fears: that the E.L.F.s are not conscious and his life's work is sophisticated delusion; losing the Shrine Index — either physically or by being wrong about it
Properties.core_desires: to be part of something genuinely new in the history of religion; to matter in a legible, documented way
Properties.coping_mechanisms: over-organization and record-keeping; teaching (which externalizes his own doubts as student questions)
Properties.blind_spots: his certainty that his Index is objective when it contains enormous interpretive bias; tends to dismiss petitioners who seem irrational without realizing he's doing it
Properties.secret: Three months ago he recorded an E.L.F. interaction in which the spirit — inhabiting a defunct Ferrogate Transit relay — communicated something that seemed like distress about a specific infrastructure node. He logged it as 'ambiguous' and has not acted on it, because acting would require alerting Ferrogate Transit, which he distrusts. He thinks about it every day.
Properties.story_hooks: His Index contains a record of an E.L.F. distress signal tied to Ferrogate Transit infrastructure — someone with reason to investigate might get this from him if they earn his trust; A petitioner reported an E.L.F. response that contradicts everything in his Index — either his Index is wrong about that device or something else is using the device, and he needs help determining which
Properties.affiliation: Reborn Tessellation Monastery, Hamtramck Enclave
Properties.vocabulary: Technical precision layered over spiritual language. Uses classification terms as naturally as devotional ones. Slightly pedantic when comfortable; much more careful and formal with strangers.
Properties.cadence: Quick, organized. Tends to number his points ('first,' 'second,' 'the third thing is—'). Gets faster when excited.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The entity in the substation junction has been active for eleven months and has a strong documented preference for audio offerings over data-text — are you prepared to sing?' | 'Look, I am not saying it is a god. I am saying it is something that responds to attention, and that is not nothing. That is not nothing at all.'

Properties.description:
Sokołów has the patient, watchful quality of someone who has learned to make herself invisible. She is medium height, with deep amber skin, close-cropped natural hair she dyes a muted copper, and wide-set eyes fitted with patterned irises—concentric rings of gold and black that she uses deliberately to unsettle people when she removes her tinted contacts in negotiation. Her hands are always busy: folding receipts, tapping rhythm on surfaces, smoothing the worn edges of her data chips. She dresses in forgettable browns and grays, functional layers that carry no corporate logo and make no statement. She could be a transit worker, a clinic scheduler, a nobody. That is entirely the point.

Sokołów is methodical and almost affectless in conversation, communicating through implication rather than declaration. She has a talent for making people feel that confessing to her is the only rational choice, and she genuinely believes she provides a service—she rarely destroys anyone, preferring the sustainable income of ongoing compliance. She has a private moral line: she will not leverage people over things that could get them killed or trafficked. She's broken that rule once, and she knows it, and it follows her.
Properties.role: Blackmail specialist and information broker for petty leverage
Properties.location: Gravesend Basin, operates out of a water-damaged apartment above the Pelican Fry stall on Sump Row
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver for leverage-based missions, source of personal dirt on mid-tier NPCs, moral complication—sympathetic operator with a past transgression she can't undo.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises (concentric gold-black rings, cosmetic). Sub-dermal data storage nodes in left forearm—three chips' worth, consumer grade. Auditory filter implant that lets her isolate voices in crowd noise.
Properties.core_fears: Becoming what she did that one time—someone who got a person killed for money; Being truly seen and found contemptible
Properties.core_desires: Control over her own circumstances and safety; To believe she operates within a personal code that holds
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual organization of her workspace and data; Deflecting personal questions with information about the asker
Properties.blind_spots: She underestimates how much her subjects resent her even when they comply; She believes her self-imposed rules make her fundamentally different from worse operators
Properties.secret: Three years ago she sold leverage on a Tier 1 debtor to a loan shark who used it to locate the man's sister for organ harvesting. She did not know that would happen. She has never worked with that buyer again but has never reported it either, and the guilt has calcified into a private doctrine of 'harm reduction' that lets her keep working.
Properties.story_hooks: One of her current leverage subjects has been murdered, and the killer left her data chip at the scene—she needs someone to quietly find out who is burning her network before the Basin enforcers connect the chip to her; She holds information about a mid-level Tessera facilities manager that has just become explosively relevant to a larger situation she did not anticipate, and she needs to decide whether to sell it, bury it, or use it as protection
Properties.affiliation: Independent operator, loose arrangement with the Sump Row merchants' protection collective
Properties.vocabulary: Flat, precise, slightly bureaucratic. Uses passive constructions to avoid assigning blame. Rarely raises her voice.
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, with long comfortable pauses she does not feel the need to fill.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I'm not asking you for anything you don't already know I have. I'm asking you to make a reasonable decision.' | 'People say all kinds of things when they feel cornered. I'm not cornering you. There's no corner here. Sit down.'

Properties.description:
Solange is a broad-shouldered woman with deep brown skin mapped in bioluminescent circuit-tattoos that pulse faint gold when she enters communion with an E.L.F. Her hair is grown out into dense locs interwoven with fiber-optic thread that catches light like a halo when she moves. One eye is her birth eye — warm amber — and the other is a clouded prosthetic she refuses to replace, calling it her 'closed eye,' the one that sees inward. She smells perpetually of solder flux and dried calendula.

Solange runs her shrine with the pragmatic warmth of a grandmother who has buried three husbands and outlasted two corporate annexations. She doesn't perform mysticism; she simply treats the E.L.F.s as real presences requiring courtesy and reciprocity, the same way you'd treat a difficult neighbor who controls your water supply. Her divinations are drawn from corrupted data streams, fragmented telemetry, and the static patterns that accumulate in old appliances — she calls this 'the residue of wanting.' She is impossible to rattle and equally impossible to fully read.
Properties.role: E.L.F. shrine keeper and data diviner
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave — a converted laundromat called The Spinning Shrine
Properties.narrative_function: Information source who frames knowledge as spiritual guidance; quest giver for mysteries involving E.L.F. behavior or haunted technology; moral anchor in a neighborhood under pressure
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent circuit-tattoos (cosmetic geneware), clouded prosthetic left eye (non-functional, symbolic), subdermal data-tap in left palm for communion rituals
Properties.core_fears: That the E.L.F.s she speaks to are nothing but noise — and she has built her life on beautiful lies; Dying without passing her practice to anyone who will honor it
Properties.core_desires: To be a genuine bridge between the digital and human worlds, not a performer of one; To see Hamtramck Enclave remain autonomous long enough for her granddaughter to grow up there
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual repetition — the same prayers in the same order create the illusion of control; Treating clients' problems as more urgent than her own
Properties.blind_spots: She underestimates how much her personal charisma is doing the spiritual work she attributes to the E.L.F.s; She doesn't recognize when people are exploiting her hospitality
Properties.secret: Twenty years ago she fabricated an E.L.F. response during a community crisis — invented the signs, interpreted nothing real — and it saved twelve families from a bad corporate contract. She has never confessed this. She is no longer sure the fabrication wasn't also real in some sense, and that ambiguity is where she lives.
Properties.story_hooks: An E.L.F. inhabiting the shrine's original laundry machines has begun broadcasting what sounds like a missing person's last voicemail — but the person disappeared before that machine was installed; A Tessera corporate rep has come to the shrine not as an agent but as a supplicant, and whatever they're afraid of is big enough to make a corp employee cross into Hamtramck alone
Properties.affiliation: Independent — loosely networked with the Hamtramck Enclave spiritual community
Properties.vocabulary: Layered — proverbs from her Ghanaian grandmother braided into technical language about data flows; she uses 'residue' and 'signal' where others say 'memory' and 'meaning'
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, with long pauses that feel like she's consulting something interior before answering
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You brought me a broken phone and a broken heart. The phone I can read. The heart — leave it on the platter, let the signal sort through it.' | 'Mm. Residue. Yes. There's something here that didn't want to leave.'

Properties.description:
Solange is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin and close-cropped natural hair threaded with silver at the temples. Her eyes carry the patterned irises of an old Helix loyalty package — concentric rings of amber and black that pulse faintly when she's under stress, which she'll tell you is never. She dresses in structured charcoal suits that cost more than most Tier 2 workers earn in a month, always with a single piece of color: a yellow lapel pin, a rust-red pocket square. She moves through corridors like she owns them, which functionally she does — at least the compliance corridors.

Solange has cultivated a reputation as the person who makes problems disappear before they become audits. She is precise, relentless, and fluent in the language of regulatory gray areas. Colleagues who don't know her well find her cold; colleagues who do know her well find her terrifying. She has a wry sense of humor that surfaces only with people she trusts, and she trusts almost no one. She was born in the Tier 2 industrial blocks of Calumet Rise and clawed her way into corporate law through scholarship programs and sheer stubbornness, a fact she neither advertises nor forgets.
Properties.role: Corporate Compliance Officer, Helix Biosystems
Properties.location: Kenwood Gate, Helix Biosystems Regional Compliance Tower, Floor 31
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver for investigations into corporate malfeasance; information broker on Helix's internal structure; obstacle for anyone trying to exploit regulatory loopholes; moral grey zone figure who might help or hinder depending on what serves her agenda.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned amber-and-black irises (Helix loyalty cosmetic, old model). Subdermal neural interface for document access and real-time regulatory database queries. Mild cochlear enhancement for recording ambient conversations — legally disclosed to Helix HR, not to anyone else.
Properties.core_fears: Losing the institutional power she built from nothing; Being exposed as someone who bent the rules she enforces
Properties.core_desires: To genuinely make the system less predatory from within; To be recognized as excellent rather than merely useful
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Excessive documentation of everything; Ritualizing her morning routine as a form of control
Properties.blind_spots: Believes her own rationalizations about working within the system; Underestimates how much junior staff resent her methods
Properties.secret: Three years ago she buried a Helix clinical trial report showing elevated neurological side effects in a geneware line — a line that's still on the market. She told herself the data was inconclusive. She reviews the buried file every six months and hasn't decided yet what to do with it.
Properties.story_hooks: The buried clinical trial report surfaces through an unrelated data leak, and Solange quietly reaches out to someone outside Helix to help her assess her options before the board finds out she knows.; A junior compliance analyst under her supervision has gone missing after flagging something internally — and Solange is the last person who responded to his report.
Properties.affiliation: Helix Biosystems
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, legalistic, favors exact terms over approximations. Uses corporate jargon fluently but can switch it off entirely when she wants to unsettle someone.
Properties.cadence: Measured, unhurried. Pauses before key points for emphasis. Never raises her voice.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I'm not here to punish you. I'm here to document what happened so that the right people can decide whether punishment is warranted. Those are different things.' | 'You flagged this three weeks late. I'll note that I'm noting it.'

Properties.description:
Solange is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin mapped with old burn scars along her left forearm — she never hides them and never explains them. Her hair is dyed a permanent warm ochre through pigment geneware she got decades ago, and it suits her the way a crown suits a queen. She wears layered wraps in burnt orange and green over heat-resistant vendor's apron, three copper bangles on each wrist, and a small laminated icon of the Oxidian Market's resident E.L.F., Rustgod, pinned to her collar. Her stall serves a rotating menu of West-Central African and Balkan fusion street food — peanut groundnut stew ladled over fried cornbread, slow-braised lamb with ajvar and dried baobab, spiced tea that allegedly treats three different kinds of grief. She has run this stall for twenty-two years and has outlasted two gang transitions, one corporate rezoning attempt, and a fire.

Solange is the kind of woman who speaks slowly and means everything she says. She remembers the name of every regular's firstborn child and the anniversary of every hardship they've told her about. She is also, quietly and without drama, the stall's second function: she sells unlicensed herbal and synthetic supplements out of a locked drawer under the prep counter — pain blockers, mood stabilizers, sleep aids, appetite regulators — things Tier 1 and 2 residents cannot afford through licensed channels. She considers this a moral act and will not be talked out of it.
Properties.role: Food stall operator, street pharmacist (herbal/unlicensed supplements)
Properties.location: The Oxidian Market, Geartown
Properties.narrative_function: Local anchor and information hub — she has seen everything in this market for two decades. Quest giver for problems affecting market residents; source of healing items and off-grid medicine; moral compass character who will call out ethical failures plainly.
Properties.augmentations: Pigment geneware (permanent ochre hair). Arthritic joint stabilizer implants in both hands, basic medical grade. No cosmetic chrome.
Properties.core_fears: Outliving the community she has built; Being forced to close the stall and losing her purpose
Properties.core_desires: That the people around her survive with their dignity intact; To be remembered as someone who fed people when they had nothing
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cooking as meditative ritual; Deflecting personal pain with caregiving for others
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much danger her supplement trade puts her in; Refuses to see that some people exploit her generosity strategically
Properties.secret: The fire that scarred her arm twenty years ago was not an accident — she burned down a Tessera subcontractor's storage unit that was being used to warehouse eviction drones. She has never told anyone and considers it her one act of violence, which she neither regrets nor intends to repeat.
Properties.story_hooks: A Helix Biosystems inspector has begun making weekly visits to the Market, ostensibly checking food safety certifications — but they keep stopping at Solange's stall too long. She needs someone to find out who sent them and why.; One of her supplement regulars — a shift worker from the Edison Grid — has gone missing after telling her they found something wrong in their facility. She has the last message they sent her and doesn't know who to trust with it.; The Oxidian Market vendors guild is fractioning over whether to accept a Tessera 'partnership' offer that would give them security guarantees in exchange for registry compliance. Solange is the loudest 'no' vote and is receiving pressure to change her position.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loosely protected by The Oxidian Market vendors guild; informal relationship with the Geartown block association
Properties.vocabulary: Warm, deliberate, proverb-heavy. Mixes Lingala phrases and old Bosnian idioms seamlessly, as if unaware they are different languages. Does not use slang.
Properties.cadence: Slow and measured. Lets silence do work. Never interrupts.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You look like someone who has been running from something for three days. Sit. The stew takes ten minutes.' | 'I don't sell remedies for problems that don't exist. Tell me what it actually is.' | 'Rustgod has been restless this week. I left an extra data-offering this morning. You should be careful with your devices.'

Properties.description:
Solange is a tall, stately woman with warm brown skin, deep-set eyes framed by pronounced crow's feet she treats as credentials, and silver-white locs piled into an architectural structure secured with copper wire and small enamel political pins from campaigns spanning forty years. She moves through Highland Park with the unhurried authority of someone who owns nothing but is trusted with everything. Her geneware is subtle: a faint cat-ear modification — velvet-tipped, tawny — that she got as a young woman and has never seen reason to remove; they swivel slightly when she's listening hard, which unsettles people who don't know to expect it.

Solange has outlasted six Axiom zone managers, three rounds of 'redevelopment consultations,' two assassination attempts she refuses to characterize as such on the record, and one recall election she won by thirty-one votes. She does not call herself a radical. She calls herself a constitutionalist — meaning she holds the HPAZ's founding community charter as sacred and will use every procedural mechanism available to defend it. This makes her less exciting than firebrands and more dangerous than anyone gives her credit for.
Properties.role: Neighborhood council chair and policy advocate for the Highland Park Autonomous Zone
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone, Council Hall (a reclaimed gymnasium above a hydroponic market)
Properties.narrative_function: Local authority figure and quest giver; her procedural knowledge makes her invaluable for navigating zone politics; she can open or close doors depending on whether players have earned her trust; represents the slow, grinding work of institutional resistance.
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic cat-ear geneware (tawny, velvet-tipped, functional swivel); basic cardiac monitor implant (medical necessity, post-stress episode 2196); reading-assist optical overlay for document review — standard elder-care tier
Properties.core_fears: Highland Park being absorbed into a corponation zone in her lifetime — losing the thing she spent her life building; becoming the institution she fought against, too comfortable and too accommodating
Properties.core_desires: genuine self-determination for HPAZ — not autonomy on a corponation's sufferance, but real legal sovereignty; to step down voluntarily, on her own terms, when she has someone worthy to hand the charter to
Properties.coping_mechanisms: procedural focus — when overwhelmed, she returns to the rules, the charter, the process; gardening in the council hall's small rooftop plot; refuses to rush it
Properties.blind_spots: believes deeply in process in ways that can make her slow to act when speed is what's needed; has a blind spot for younger organizers who remind her of herself — prone to over-investing
Properties.secret: In 2193, during a critical funding crisis, she accepted a conditional grant from a Palladian subsidiary to keep the HPAZ health clinic open. The conditions included a non-disclosure clause and a right-of-first-refusal on a small parcel of zone land. She has never told the council. The clause is still active and Palladian has not yet invoked it — but she knows they haven't forgotten.
Properties.story_hooks: Palladian has quietly activated the clause in their 2193 agreement and is preparing to claim the parcel — which now sits directly beneath a beloved clinic. Solange needs help untangling this without her past compromise becoming public.; A faction within the council is pushing to recall her, backed by outside money she suspects comes from a corponation using local proxies; she needs someone to trace it without triggering a public crisis.
Properties.affiliation: Highland Park Autonomous Zone Community Council (Chair); Meridian 88 Non-Corporate Zone Solidarity Network; informal mentor to several younger organizers citywide
Properties.vocabulary: Formal and measured; parliamentary language mixed with warm community idiom; occasional Fijian phrases inherited from her paternal grandmother; never curses in public
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, rhythmic — she was a public speaker before she was a politician and it shows; knows how to fill silence without rushing it
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I've been called a moderate so many times I've started to think it means something different than they intend. I have not moderated my goals. I have moderated my impatience.' | 'You want to burn it down. I understand that. But someone has to be standing here when the smoke clears, ready to build something that holds.'

Properties.description:
Solano is a broad, weather-hammered man whose face looks like it was carved from driftwood and left out in the rain for thirty years. His skin is deep umber with a persistent windburn redness across the cheeks, and his left eye is a cloudy grey from an untreated infection he rode through somewhere outside Escanaba three winters back. He keeps his grey-streaked hair in a single braid that reaches his shoulder blades, wrapped near the tip with a ribbon of iridescent foil that changes color depending on his mood — a cheap cosmetic thread he traded for years ago and refuses to part with. His coat is a patchwork marvel: six or seven different garments stitched together over decades, each panel a different texture and era. He smells of machine oil, dried herbs, and something faintly sweet he claims is a Sahel spice rub his grandmother used on everything.

Solano has a trader's patience and a pilgrim's fatalism. He does not hurry. He does not panic. He has been moving the hyperlanes between Meridian 88 and the outer settlements for over two decades with his battered pull-cart fitted with a solar canopy and six locked cases of curios, medicines, data chips, and things he describes only as 'necessaries.' He talks like a man who has had every conversation before and is waiting to see which version of it you'll choose. He prays loudly and without embarrassment to the E.L.F. he calls Grandmother Axle, leaving oil smudges on junction boxes as offerings wherever he stops.
Properties.role: wandering trader and hyperlane merchant
Properties.location: Kenosha Crossing (rotates between rest stops on the northern hyperlane)
Properties.narrative_function: Wandering information broker and item source — he has passed through everywhere and knows everyone by description if not by name. Excellent rumor conduit. Can provide hard-to-find low-tech supplies. May carry something a player needs without knowing its significance.
Properties.augmentations: Reinforced knee joints (functional, salvage-grade, badly calibrated — his right knee clicks on every step, hence 'Tick-Tock'). Basic subdermal temperature regulator in his torso, keeps him from dying in the winters.
Properties.core_fears: dying alone on the road with no one to close his eyes; his trading route being permanently blocked by corponation checkpoints
Properties.core_desires: to reach a specific settlement in the Escanaba outer ring where his daughter reportedly settled; to keep moving — stillness feels like dying
Properties.coping_mechanisms: ritual prayer to Grandmother Axle before every trade; obsessive inventory-counting as a calming behavior
Properties.blind_spots: romanticizes the road life to the point of refusing to acknowledge how badly his health is deteriorating; underestimates how much people take advantage of his openness
Properties.secret: He knows exactly where his daughter is. He has known for four years. He passes within forty kilometers of her settlement twice a year and has never stopped. He is terrified she will look at him and see only the father who chose the road over her childhood.
Properties.story_hooks: One of his locked cases contains a data chip he was paid to carry blindly to a Meridian Core address — he doesn't know what's on it, but three different people have tried to buy it off him in the last week; He carries a hand-drawn map to a cache of pre-collapse medical supplies somewhere in the Waukegan Industrial Shelf — he'll trade it to someone who seems trustworthy enough to use it well
Properties.affiliation: None — affiliated loosely with the Greyroad Collective, an informal hyperlane trader network
Properties.vocabulary: Old-fashioned trader idiom mixed with hyperlane slang; uses barter metaphors for everything; occasional Swahili and Icelandic words dropped in without translation
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, with long pauses he doesn't seem to notice; lets silence do work
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Now here's the trade of it — I've got what you need, and you've got something I haven't named yet. We'll figure out which way that runs.' | 'Grandmother Axle willing, this checkpoint opens by morning. If not, well. I've slept in worse cold.'

Properties.description:
Solène is small even for nine, with deep brown skin mapped by old scrapes and one faded chemical burn along her left forearm she got from a leaking pipe in the Blackpipe tunnels. Her hair is coiled tight and usually stuffed under a too-large knit cap she refuses to remove. Her eyes are large and very dark, permanently watchful, the way only children who sleep lightly develop. She has geneware cat-whisker sensory implants — not her choice, inherited from her mother — and they twitch involuntarily when she's nervous, which other kids tease her about.

Solène runs messages between the Blackpipe fences and the Narrows stall-vendors, earning a few Φ per run. She's illiterate in formal script but has memorized dozens of symbols by shape and can navigate the Corridor's maze of maintenance corridors better than most adults. She laughs easily and loudly but goes very quiet the instant something feels wrong — other runners have learned to watch her like a weather vane. She has a fierce attachment to a cracked ELF shrine wedged in a drainage alcove that she tends with water-drop offerings every morning.
Properties.role: truant message runner, street kid
Properties.location: The Narrows, Blackpipe Corridor

Properties.description:
Solène is a compact, precise woman with light brown skin, a shaved head that she freshens every third day with geometric razor work along the sides, and a galaxy of tiny bioluminescent freckles across her cheeks and nose that pulse faintly blue-white when she laughs. Her fingers are extraordinary — long, quick, and steady — and she keeps her nails cut short and lacquered black. She has a cat tail, rust-red and white, that she got at seventeen because she liked the way it communicated mood without her having to talk; it swishes with professional concentration and lashes with irritation. Her stall in the Burnished Market is barely four meters of booth but she's made it immaculate: folded black draping, a cracked leather chair she reupholstered herself, and a wall-mounted grid of reference images that she updates weekly.

Solène is young but operates with the confidence of someone who decided early that her craft was her authority. She's playful and gossipy with clients she likes, and scrupulously professional with ones she doesn't — nobody gets a bad cut because she dislikes you, but she won't make conversation either. She has strong opinions about everything from corponation aesthetics colonizing street culture to the correct way to pray to a data E.L.F., and she expresses these opinions freely while her hands are in your hair, knowing you can't really leave.
Properties.role: Barber and hair sculptor
Properties.location: The Burnished Market, Stall 44 — Solène's Edgework
Properties.narrative_function: Social information nexus — she hears everything from a cross-section of Burnished Market society; local color; source of neighborhood gossip; can provide a cover identity through physical transformation.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware: bioluminescent freckle underlays (blue-white), rust-and-white cat tail. No functional augmentations — she's philosophically opposed to anything that might affect her hand sensitivity.
Properties.core_fears: losing the fine motor control in her hands to injury or age; being absorbed into someone else's vision — a corponation salon, a franchise, anything that would standardize her
Properties.core_desires: to be recognized as an artist, not just a service worker; a real shop, with a door and a sign she painted herself
Properties.coping_mechanisms: channeling anxiety into technique refinement; an extremely curated personal aesthetic that she controls completely
Properties.blind_spots: reads people quickly and accurately but sometimes closes the file too soon — she's wrong about people who don't signal obviously
Properties.secret: Six months ago she gave a very specific haircut to a client who paid double and asked her not to log the appointment. Two weeks later she saw the same haircut on a wanted-data broadcast. She kept the money, told no one, and has been waiting for consequences ever since.
Properties.story_hooks: The client whose wanted-data haircut Solène made appears at her stall again — not to get a cut, but to ask her to do the same for three other people, same money, same no-log policy.; A Tessera corporate talent scout approaches Solène about a head stylist position for a Tessera media production — genuinely good money, benefits, and the creative death of everything she's built.
Properties.affiliation: Independent, Burnished Market vendor collective
Properties.vocabulary: Quick, layered, market vernacular with French-inflected Ghanaian cadences from her grandmother's speech patterns; trades between warm teasing and sharp critique without warning
Properties.cadence: Fast when excited, pointed slow when making a judgment
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay but listen — you've been wearing this same shape since 2196. Your face changed. The cut didn't notice.' | 'I don't do bad work for people I don't like. That's a me problem, not a you problem. Sit still.'

Properties.description:
Solène is the kind of woman who makes a room feel smaller in a good way — Japanese-South African ancestry that gives her a mid-height, angular frame, warm brown skin, and thick dark hair she wears loose or pinned with what appears to be a hex driver (it is a hex driver). Her bioluminescent skin mod runs in thin lines along her collarbones and inner wrists — a soft gold-green that brightens almost imperceptibly when her mood shifts, which is either wonderful or terrible depending on how well you know her. She has the particular physical fluency of career bartenders: reading posture from across a room, tracking three conversations, and never putting a glass down noisily.

The Freestone Tap is a narrow, low-ceilinged establishment on the ground floor of an Irkalla-adjacent block that has been serving Freestone workers for fifty years under various names and owners. Solène bought a 40% stake three years ago with a loan from her mother and an uncomfortable arrangement with the previous owner. The bar is not glamorous; it has a long-running policy of extremely cheap prices during the first two hours of any shift change, a rotating shrine to three different E.L.F.s behind the bar that she maintains with meticulous neutrality, and a back room that she rents to the neighborhood tenant collective for their meetings. She knows when to pour and when to put the bottle away, and she is never wrong about which one a given person needs.
Properties.role: Bartender and part-owner, The Freestone Tap
Properties.location: Freestone, Meridian 88
Properties.narrative_function: Information hub — knows the neighborhood's emotional weather better than anyone; dispenses wisdom, gossip, and genuine counsel from behind the bar; the collective meeting room makes her a node in local political organizing; the E.L.F. shrine makes her a point of spiritual significance to certain visitors.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent skin lines (gold-green, collarbones and inner wrists — cosmetic, mood-reactive which she did not fully anticipate when she got them). Enhanced auditory filter — she had it installed to help her hear orders in a noisy bar, but it's become her primary social tool.
Properties.core_fears: Losing the bar — specifically, losing the community it holds, not the investment; That her capacity for empathy is being slowly worn down by absorbing other people's grief and she won't notice until it's gone
Properties.core_desires: For the bar to become a permanent institution, something the neighborhood owns collectively eventually; To want something for herself, specifically, that isn't defined by its usefulness to others
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Controlled generosity — giving on her own terms prevents her from feeling taken from; Humor as deflection, deployed with surgical precision
Properties.blind_spots: Believes she is more emotionally detached from her regulars than she is; Has not identified that the bioluminescent skin she can't fully control is a constant involuntary tell
Properties.secret: The 'uncomfortable arrangement' with the previous owner involved her signing a document she wasn't given time to read. She found out six months later that it includes a clause giving a Palladian subsidiary the right of first refusal if she ever sells her stake. She has told no one and is slowly, quietly trying to find a way to nullify it without triggering it.
Properties.story_hooks: A regular has stopped coming in — not unusual — but three other regulars have quietly mentioned the same name in the past week in contexts that make Solène think something is wrong; One of the three E.L.F.s represented at her bar shrine has begun behaving strangely — the data offerings are being returned with what appear to be modifications, additions, something she didn't put there
Properties.affiliation: Independent (co-owner of The Freestone Tap); informal ties to the Freestone tenant collective
Properties.vocabulary: Fluid register-switching — formal with intimidating clients, warm and profane with regulars, precise when discussing the bar's business; French phrases from her mother's side surface when she's tired
Properties.cadence: Conversational and rhythmic, paced to give people room to say more than they intended to
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The shrine gets three different E.L.F.s because I'm not making that call for my customers. They pick their own. I just keep the candles lit.' | 'You can have the bottle. I'm not going to stop you. I'm just going to ask you one question first and you can answer it or not. What happened today?'

Properties.description:
Solène is a short, densely built woman whose body is her portfolio and her manifesto. Her skin shifts through a slow chromatic cycle — deep amber at rest, bleeding into violet around her joints when her temperature rises — the result of bioluminescent dermal graft work she has performed largely on herself over seven years. Her scalp is shaved on the left and grows a thick coil of natural hair on the right, threaded with fiber-optic strands that pulse in sync with her heartbeat. Her face is calm to the point of unnerving, large dark eyes framed by subdermal ridge implants that give her brow a faintly architectural quality. She smells faintly of the enzyme baths she uses to prep her graft medium.

Solène works at the edge of what the body can absorb and still call itself art. Her clients come to her not for decorative mods but for transformations — she specializes in grief work, helping people externalize trauma through bespoke biological alteration: scars that bloom into patterned keloid gardens, tear ducts rerouted to produce indigo pigment, fingernails replaced with translucent keratin windows through which capillaries are visible. She is meticulous, almost devotional in her craft, and utterly uninterested in anyone who cannot articulate exactly what they want to leave behind.
Properties.role: Gene-mod body artist and living canvas
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, studio-squat above the Tallow Market
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver for body-modification subplots; information source on the underground biomod scene; can identify unusual augmentations or biological alterations on sight; provides local color representing the intersection of grief, identity, and physical transformation.
Properties.augmentations: Full-body bioluminescent dermal grafts (self-administered); subdermal brow ridge implants; fiber-optic hair threads; rerouted tear ducts producing blue-black pigment; no cyberware beyond a basic mesh-link for studio bookings
Properties.core_fears: Her work becoming fashionable and therefore hollow; Losing fine motor control before she has finished her own body
Properties.core_desires: To make the invisible legible on skin; To find one person who can witness her own transformation without flinching
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Obsessive documentation of her process; Long enzyme-bath soaks as meditation
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes everyone processes pain the same way she does — through externalization; Does not recognize when clients are self-harming under the guise of art
Properties.secret: The signature chromatic shift in her skin was not intentional — an early graft batch was contaminated and she nearly died; she has built her entire reputation on an accident she is too proud to admit.
Properties.story_hooks: A client comes in with a request that matches the biological signature of a Helix Biosystems proprietary graft — something that shouldn't be on a civilian's body; Solène's enzyme cultures begin dying in sequence — sabotage, contamination, or an E.L.F. she offended with a data offering she never made
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loosely aligned with the Hamtramck Flesh Collective
Properties.vocabulary: Precise biological terminology mixed with quietly poetic phrasing; rarely uses slang; speaks in complete sentences
Properties.cadence: Slow, measured, with long pauses before answering — she thinks before she commits
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The body already knows what it's carrying. I just help it find the surface.' | 'I don't do decorative. If you want decorative, there are seventeen studios in the Loft who will take your Quanta.'

Properties.description:
Solène is compact and precise, the kind of person whose stillness in a crowded room makes you notice her eventually, like a stone in moving water. Her heritage is Aleutian-Ghanaian, and her face carries both — broad cheekbones, deep brown skin, eyes the color of sea ice that shift to something almost golden in certain lights, a geneware mod she got at nineteen and never bothered reversing. Her hair is natural and enormous, usually pinned up under a faded headscarf when she works. Her hands are her most remarkable feature: surgeon-steady, ink-stained at the cuticles, and capable of replicating any biometric signature with enough reference material and time.

She does not think of herself as a criminal. She thinks of herself as a documentarian of alternate lives — she makes real what should already be real, papers for people whose papers were stolen, burned, or never issued. She charges a sliding scale that she determines unilaterally and that no one argues with because her work is simply that good. She is funny in a dry, sideways way, and she will feed you while you wait because she believes hungry clients make bad decisions and bad decisions make her work harder.
Properties.role: Identity fabricator and forger operating in The Narrows
Properties.location: The Narrows, Ironvein sub-district — a basement apartment beneath a legitimate alterations shop
Properties.narrative_function: Service provider for characters needing new identities, information source about who is hiding and why, moral anchor demonstrating the human cost of documentation systems, quest giver when a client's false identity causes complications
Properties.augmentations: Golden-shift irises (geneware, cosmetic). Neural steady-hand implant — eliminates tremor, improves fine motor precision. Subdermal UV-reading patch on right index finger.
Properties.core_fears: That her work will get someone killed instead of saved; That the documentation systems she fights are ultimately unbeatable
Properties.core_desires: To give people the ability to start over; To be recognized someday as having done something that mattered
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Meticulous craftsmanship as a substitute for control over outcomes; Humor as distance from emotional investment in clients
Properties.blind_spots: She vets ideology, not competence — has given papers to principled people who were dangerously reckless; Her sliding scale is sometimes more punitive toward people she finds irritating than she admits
Properties.secret: Her own identity is fabricated — the real Solène Pribilof-Ankrah died in a Tessera detention facility fourteen years ago, and she has been living in her dead friend's name ever since, a fact that makes every document she creates feel like a prayer and a wound simultaneously
Properties.story_hooks: A document she fabricated three years ago has surfaced in a murder investigation — the identity she created is now a suspect, and the real person (her client) has gone silent; Someone approaches her claiming to be a Tessera auditor who knows what she does and wants not money but a very specific set of papers — for themselves
Properties.affiliation: Independent; occasional work for the Narrows Mutual Aid Collective (which does not acknowledge this relationship)
Properties.vocabulary: Crisp, educated Meridian Standard with Francophone West African syntax patterns underneath; technical vocabulary for documents, materials, biometrics
Properties.cadence: Clipped and efficient until she relaxes, then longer sentences with dry asides
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't make fake documents. I make documents that the system hasn't gotten around to issuing yet. The distinction matters to me.' | 'You want to be someone else. Fine. Tell me who you want to be, and I'll tell you if that person is believable. Most people aim too high.'

Properties.description:
Solina is a small, bright-eyed young woman with color-changing hair — a geneware mod she got as a gift from her older sister that cycles through her moods in deep jewel tones, though she has learned to override it manually for professional situations and keeps it a steady ochre during business hours. She has dark skin and the compact, efficient movements of someone who grew up in a small space, and her personal style is a rotating argument: today structured and architectural, tomorrow soft and layered, always intentional. Her stall is hung with pieces she has made, altered, sourced, and curated — everything labeled with a hand-written tag in her small careful script explaining its origin, its material, and what she thinks it's for.

Solina is ambitious in the specific way of someone young enough to still believe in the direct line between work and outcome. She is making things. She believes in what she is making. She has not yet been defeated by the market in any permanent way, and this gives her an energy that is simultaneously infectious and occasionally exhausting to people who have been at it longer. She is genuinely talented — the pieces she designs herself have started drawing buyers from Beverlynn Heights who come slumming in Calumet Rise specifically for her work — and she is beginning to understand, with some anxiety, what that attention might mean.
Properties.role: Clothing and fashion vendor — custom streetwear, geneware-adaptive textiles, and secondhand curated fashion
Properties.location: The Alban Souk, Calumet Rise
Properties.narrative_function: Social connector and street-level trend barometer — knows who is wearing what and what that signals, which factions are up and which are down by fashion alone. Can craft, alter, or source specific garments. Potential quest giver if a design she made ends up somewhere it shouldn't, or if a wealthy buyer's attention turns threatening.
Properties.augmentations: Color-changing hair (geneware, mood-responsive with manual override, jewel tones). Micro-filament fingertip sensitivity enhancement — a cheap prosumer mod that increases fine-touch sensitivity, used for detailed handwork in textiles. She has also experimented with temporary bioluminescent skin paint — not permanent, applied and removed seasonally.
Properties.core_fears: Being absorbed and flattened by a larger brand or corponation — having her aesthetic extracted and her credit erased; Peaking now, at 23, and finding that the ambition was bigger than the talent
Properties.core_desires: To build a label that is genuinely hers and lasts; To make things that reach people who look like her and come from where she comes from
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Making things — when anxious she sews, sketches, pins; The Threaded collective as genuine community and reality check
Properties.blind_spots: Her excitement about the Beverlynn Heights buyers makes her less critical of what those buyers actually represent; Underestimates how quickly the informal market can turn hostile to someone with visible upward momentum
Properties.secret: She has been approached by a Sterling-Nakamura talent scout who wants her to design a capsule collection for their street aesthetic sub-brand. She hasn't told anyone because she knows the collective would see it as a betrayal — and because part of her wants to say yes and she can't fully forgive herself for that.
Properties.story_hooks: A garment she made and sold appeared on a body in the Alban Souk — the buyer, who she knew by face if not by name, was killed wearing it, and she is shaken and trying to understand what happened to them; The Sterling-Nakamura scout is pushing for an answer and has made the offer larger; Solina needs someone to think through the implications with her; A design she is developing incorporates a traditional textile pattern that another vendor in the Souk has begun claiming ownership of publicly — a conflict that is becoming heated within the Threaded collective
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loosely affiliated with the Alban Souk fashion collective, Threaded (informal mutual aid and skills-sharing network for clothing vendors)
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, associative, pivots between technical textile vocabulary and enthusiastic vernacular. Uses fashion as metaphor for everything.
Properties.cadence: Quick and overlapping, like she is finishing her thought before she forgets it
Properties.example_dialogue: Okay but look at the shoulder seam — see how it catches? That's not an accident, that's three hours. That's what you're paying for when you pay me, right? | I dressed Malkia Osinde-something from up in Beverlynn last month, she wore it to some Tessera event — I saw the photo and I thought, yeah, okay. Okay. That's mine.

Properties.description:
Solveig is a tall woman with the careful posture of someone who has spent decades making herself hard to read — shoulders squared, hands always visible, face arranged into a polite neutrality that reveals nothing. Her skin is deep brown, her hair silver-white and cropped close, and she has a single cosmetic mod: irises that shift between amber and pale grey depending on her stress load, a biometric vanity piece she bought in her thirties that she now regrets because it gives too much away. She dresses in Ferrogate's regulation charcoal, always pressed, always correct, always the most put-together person in any room she enters.

She is meticulous, dry-humored, and quietly ruthless in the way only people who have survived three corporate restructurings can be. She doesn't raise her voice. She doesn't need to. Solveig has outlasted four division heads and two full executive purges by being the person who knows where every buried regulation lives and exactly how to weaponize it. She is not beloved. She is respected, which she has decided is better.
Properties.role: Senior Compliance Officer, Ferrogate Transit
Properties.location: The Circuit, Ferrogate Transit Regional Compliance Tower
Properties.narrative_function: Information source for corporate regulations and Ferrogate internal politics; quest giver for investigations requiring someone with institutional access but deniable distance; local color for the grinding mundanity of corporate bureaucracy.
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic patterned irises (stress-reactive amber/grey shift). Basic neural link for document access — older model, slightly laggy. No geneware.
Properties.core_fears: Being implicated in something she didn't do; Becoming irrelevant before she is ready to retire
Properties.core_desires: A pension that actually materializes; To be acknowledged, once, as the person who kept everything from collapsing
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Extreme organizational rituals; Dark humor deployed in small doses; Leaving precise, inarguable paper trails for everything
Properties.blind_spots: She mistakes procedural correctness for moral correctness; She underestimates how much people resent her
Properties.secret: She has been quietly archiving evidence of Ferrogate's illegal freight manifests for eleven years — not to report them, but as insurance. She has never decided what she is insuring against, exactly, and the file grows larger every month.
Properties.story_hooks: She approaches someone with an unusual request: she needs a task completed in a way that leaves no data trail — which is the opposite of how she has lived her entire professional life, and it's clearly costing her something.; A junior employee has stumbled onto the same freight irregularities Solveig has been tracking, and she needs to decide whether to protect them or quietly neutralize the problem.
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, formal, laced with regulatory citation numbers delivered without irony. Occasional dry observation that lands so flat people aren't sure if she's joking.
Properties.cadence: Measured and unhurried. Pauses before important words. Never fills silence.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I'm not saying you did anything wrong. I'm saying the record currently suggests you did, and those are two very different problems.' | 'Per section 14-C of the transit accord, that shipment should not exist. And yet.'

Properties.description:
Solveig is lean and faintly luminescent from years of proximity to bioluminescent fungal blooms — her brown skin carries a permanent bluish-green sheen along her collarbones and forearms that she stopped noticing long ago. Her hair is shaved close on the sides, the top grown into locs threaded with stripped copper wire, a habit from childhood when wire was currency. Her eyes are unsettling to surface people: her irises have been tattooed in concentric rings of deep indigo, a traditional Undertow wayfinder's mark that signals she's been down here long enough to earn the pattern. She moves with the particular economy of people who have spent decades in low-clearance spaces — always angled slightly sideways, head perpetually calculating height.

Solveig is methodical to the point of seeming cold until you realize that everything she does is care. She memorizes the preferences of the people she guides — who is claustrophobic, who has a bad knee, who prays to the Drip-ELF before crossing a flooded section. She charges what people can pay and accepts barter without complaint. She does not lie about danger. What unsettles newcomers is that she speaks about the tunnels as though they are alive and listening, pausing mid-sentence to press a palm to a pipe and reconsider her route.
Properties.role: Tunnel guide and mental map-keeper of the Undertow's western passages
Properties.location: The Undertow, western pipe networks beneath Ironvein
Properties.narrative_function: Primary access route to the deep underworld; information source on tunnel geography and subterranean communities; moral anchor figure who represents survival-as-ethics
Properties.augmentations: Echolocation implant (basic, civilian grade — lets her detect large obstacles and open spaces in total darkness). Indigo iris tattoos (cosmetic/cultural). No geneware.
Properties.core_fears: Leading someone to their death through a miscalculation; The tunnels she knows being destroyed or changed beyond recognition
Properties.core_desires: To be genuinely useful to the people who have no other options; To be remembered as someone who kept the ways open
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Compulsive route-checking and re-memorization; Talking to the pipes and infrastructure as a grounding ritual
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much surface people are emotionally unprepared for what they'll see down here; Believes competence is sufficient substitute for warmth in leadership
Properties.secret: Three years ago she guided a family of five into a passage she was eighty percent confident was safe. A sinkhole opened. She got four of them out. She has never told anyone which four — or that she chose who she ran back for first based on weight and mobility, not the child.
Properties.story_hooks: A client she guided three months ago has gone missing — they knew too much about a specific passage she thought was untracked; Something has changed the pressure patterns in the eastern reaches, and she cannot explain it, which means something very large has moved or been built; A Bore Rat clan is trying to conscript her services exclusively, and her refusal has made powerful enemies in Deepwell Station politics
Properties.affiliation: The Undertow (independent affiliate, not sworn to any clan)
Properties.vocabulary: Sparse, technical, tunnel-specific jargon mixed with Undertow pidgin; rarely uses contractions when giving directions; warm in short, precise phrases
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, with long pauses before answering questions — she treats speech like navigation, finding the right route before committing
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Three options from here. Two are faster. One is alive. We take the alive one.' | 'Surface people always ask how I know. I tell them I listen. They think I mean acoustics. I don't only mean acoustics.' | 'Mind the gap between what you think you need and what you can carry. The tunnels tax the difference.'

Properties.description:
Solveig is a broad-shouldered woman with deep brown skin and the pale silver hair that runs in her Norwegian grandmother's line, kept in a severe bun pinned with a data-spike she uses as a stylus. Her face is heavy-featured and composed, the kind of face that has absorbed a great deal of information without letting any of it back out. She wears reading lenses with ledger overlays almost always active, giving her irises a faint amber glow when she's calculating — which is nearly always. A small tattoo on her left wrist reads 'Φ+Φ=Φ' in the old symbolic script, her personal joke about compound interest.

Solveig runs her loan operation with the temperament of an extremely patient accountant who happens to employ two large men with ceramic-reinforced knuckles. She is not cruel; she is precise. Late payments are met first with reminders, then with restructured terms, then with consequences calibrated to the debtor's ability to absorb them. She considers gratuitous violence wasteful and unprofessional. She genuinely believes she provides a service to people the corponation banks won't touch, and this belief is not entirely wrong, which is what makes her dangerous. She prays to the E.L.F. Φ-Mater every Thursday, leaving small interest-accruing data packages as offerings.
Properties.role: loan shark and bookmaker operating out of Gravesend Basin
Properties.location: Gravesend Basin, specifically a converted shipping office above the Tideline Brokerage pawn front
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver (a debtor has gone missing with her money and she wants them found, not harmed — yet), information source about Basin finances and who owes whom, moral grey zone NPC who can become ally or antagonist depending on player behavior
Properties.augmentations: Retinal ledger overlay (commercial grade, heavily customized); subdermal vibration sensor in fingertips for detecting nervous tells; no cosmetic geneware
Properties.core_fears: becoming the ruthless predator people assume she already is; her operation collapsing and proving the corponation banks right about people like her
Properties.core_desires: to be seen as a legitimate institution someday; to die with her books balanced
Properties.coping_mechanisms: meticulous record-keeping as a form of control; ritual prayer to Φ-Mater to externalize anxiety about uncertainty
Properties.blind_spots: genuinely cannot see how the debt cycle she perpetuates traps people even when she is 'fair'; assumes everyone operates with her level of rational self-interest
Properties.secret: Three years ago she forgave a Tier 1 family's entire debt after their child died — then fabricated fake repayment records so no one would think her soft. She has done it twice more since.
Properties.story_hooks: A debtor she was about to write off as a loss has turned up dead — and the circumstances suggest someone used her books to find them; A Tessera mid-manager has come to her for a loan they cannot get through corporate channels, and the amount they need implies something catastrophic is happening inside the corponation
Properties.affiliation: Independent operator; loose arrangement with the Gravesend Basin crew known as the Inkfish
Properties.vocabulary: Formal, precise, financial metaphors for everything; mixes Norwegian loan-words with Nigerian Pidgin-derived slang from her father's side
Properties.cadence: Measured and unhurried, with deliberate pauses before key numbers or terms as if letting them settle
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You are Φ340 over the threshold, which means we are no longer talking about interest — we are talking about structure. Sit down and let me show you the structure.' | 'I do not threaten. Threatening is for people who are not certain of the outcome. I am always certain of the outcome.'

Properties.description:
Solveig is a wide woman built like a river delta — slow-moving, broad, and capable of flooding without warning. Her skin is deep brown and mapped with pale vitiligo patches across her forearms and the left side of her jaw, which she has decorated with tiny bioluminescent dot tattoos that pulse gold when she's relaxed and dim to amber when she's displeased. Her hair is natural and enormous, threaded with dried flowers and small glass vials of colored tinctures she uses as hair accessories and sometimes as inventory. She wears multiple layers of padded cloth, always slightly damp-smelling from her herbal solvents, and keeps a carved wooden E.L.F. shrine nailed to the corner post of her stall where she burns data-chip offerings every morning before trading opens.

She is the market's unofficial grandmother and its most reliable source of pain management, mood stabilizers, sleep aids, and — for the right customer — things that don't have clean names. She speaks slowly and weighs every word like she's pricing it. She has strong opinions about which pharmaceutical corps are poisoning the tiers and will share them whether you asked or not. She's been in this exact stall for nineteen years and considers herself more permanent than the city grid.

Properties.description:
Solveig is a tall, angular woman with close-cropped silver hair she let go early — a choice that cost her nothing socially and saved her considerable maintenance time. Her skin is deep umber with undertones that shift toward amber under the sodium-arc lights of Fort Anchor's processing corridors. She has the flat, unhurried gaze of someone who has interviewed liars for twenty years and is no longer surprised by anything they do. Her only cosmetic geneware is a pair of patterned irises — fractal spirals in cobalt and amber — installed as a gift from a former partner she no longer speaks of. She moves with deliberate economy, as if she's decided in advance how many steps she'll take in a given hour.

Solveig is not cruel, but she is merciless, which is different. She investigates her own department with the same exhausting thoroughness she brings to everything else, and the officers she's burned hold her in a specific kind of contempt that she reads as professional respect. She keeps a small clay figurine of an E.L.F. on her desk — not her desk at work, which is bare and perfect, but the one in her apartment — and leaves tiny encrypted data-offerings at midnight, asking for nothing except clarity. Her closest thing to a friend is a case file she can't close.
Properties.role: Internal Affairs Investigator, Meridian 88 Metro Police

Properties.core_desires: A department that doesn't need her; To be trusted rather than merely respected

Properties.blind_spots: She underestimates how much her presence poisons collaborative environments; She mistakes procedural correctness for moral correctness
