Properties.description:
Somadina Baranov-Fosu is compact and densely muscled, built low to the ground like something designed to survive impacts. At 29, the augmentation scarring around her temples and jawline tells a story of installation by someone who prioritized function over aesthetics. The chrome is visible — dermal camouflage — chromatic skin pigment cells, limited active camouflage — and she makes no effort to hide it.

She came up through the Shelf's informal apprentice system, learning the trade from runners who didn't survive long enough to see her surpass them. She works as a broker out of The Overhang, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

In the runner community, Somadina Baranov-Fosu is known for getting the job done and not asking questions that would make the job harder to stomach.

Properties.description:
Soraya is a tall, drought-weathered woman with the broad cheekbones of her Botswanan grandmother and the pale grey eyes she inherited from somewhere in the Bulgarian line. Her skin is the color of cracked clay, deeply lined around the eyes and mouth from decades of squinting at horizon lines. She wears a patchwork duster covered in hand-sewn pockets, each holding a rolled paper map — actual paper, a near-mythological material in Meridian 88 — annotated in four different scripts. No cosmetic mods; her only concession to technology is a battered retinal overlay that flickers at the edges because she can't afford calibration.

Soraya spent thirty years mapping the hyperlane rest stops between the Great Lakes and the Gulf Shelf, and there is no one who knows the informal infrastructure of drifter life better. She speaks with the deliberate economy of someone who has learned to make every sentence count because silence is the only privacy a transient gets. She is neither sentimental nor cruel — she has simply seen too much to be surprised by either kindness or brutality, and treats both as weather.
Properties.role: Wandering cartographer and hyperlane migrant
Properties.location: Kenosha Crossing transit hub, sleeping berth corridor B-7
Properties.narrative_function: Information source and orientation guide — she knows where drifter camps are, which checkpoints are bribeable, which hyperlane segments are currently dangerous, and which E.L.F.s are venerated at which rest stops.
Properties.augmentations: Flickering retinal overlay (third-hand, poorly calibrated). No geneware. A healed fracture in her left wrist repaired with cheap calcium-bonding paste leaves a visible ridge under the skin.
Properties.core_fears: Becoming unneeded — that her maps will be obsolete before she dies; Dying in a place she has already charted and therefore already left behind
Properties.core_desires: To find one route no one else has recorded; To be trusted with something worth protecting
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Obsessive documentation — writes down everything; Treats movement itself as emotional regulation
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much people need her personally, not just her knowledge; Cannot recognize when she is the one who needs help
Properties.secret: She has a complete, updated map of the Q-zero ghost communities — people with zero digital identity — hidden inside the lining of her duster. At least two corponation intelligence divisions would pay significantly for it. She has never sold it and does not intend to.
Properties.story_hooks: A corponation fixer approaches players claiming to be a 'transit researcher' — Soraya has noticed and is quietly trying to warn the Q-zero communities she has mapped; One of her paper maps leads to a hyperlane rest stop that has been officially erased from all records — something is being hidden there

Properties.example_dialogue: 'Mark that — this checkpoint runs light on Tuesdays. File it.' | 'You want to know where the Waukegan Shelf camps are. Three days south of trusting me, that information lives.'

Properties.description:
Soraya is a compact woman with deep brown skin and close-cropped natural hair she keeps pinned flat under a headset she almost never removes. Her eyes are her most striking feature — cosmetic irises patterned like circuit diagrams in amber and black, a Ferrogate employee perk she accepted mostly because it made her colleagues uncomfortable and she finds that useful. She has the particular stillness of someone who watches things for a living, and a habit of tracking movement in a room that makes first-time acquaintances feel vaguely prosecuted.

She runs the mid-shift monitoring suite at Kessler Interchange, a warren of overlapping transit corridors where four Ferrogate lines converge and approximately forty thousand people pass through daily. She is methodical, unhurried, and privately contemptuous of colleagues who confuse volume of incidents flagged with quality of work. She has learned to read a crowd the way some people read weather — pressure, density, the small tells of collective mood. She drinks too much stimulant tea and keeps a small clay figurine of an E.L.F. she calls Clicker on her console, leaving it fragments of raw surveillance data as offerings.
Properties.role: Surveillance operator, Ferrogate Transit Security
Properties.location: Kessler Interchange
Properties.narrative_function: Information source — knows everyone who moves through Kessler and can pull footage going back six months. Local color for transit hub scenes. Quest-adjacent: might notice something wrong before anyone else does.

Properties.core_fears: Being responsible for harm she failed to prevent; Losing the sharpness of her perception — cognitive decline, augmentation failure
Properties.core_desires: To see things as they actually are, not as they are presented; To be genuinely useful in a way that is legible and measurable
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Hyper-detailed logging and documentation; Ritual attention to her E.L.F. figurine when stressed; Long silent observation before speaking
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates threats from people she has mentally categorized as 'harmless regulars'; Confuses surveillance with understanding — watches without always grasping motive

Properties.description:
Soraya is a broad-shouldered woman whose face carries the particular weathered softness of someone who has spent decades making difficult decisions and sleeping soundly afterward. Her skin is a deep warm brown, her hair gone fully silver and kept in tight finger-coils close to her scalp, and her eyes are a pale amber that people often mistake for lens mods — they're entirely natural, a gift from some Kasparian ancestor she'll never meet. She favors heavy linen wraps in ochre and rust, always a calculating pad visible in the folds of her clothing, always a cup of something hot in her hand. She has bioluminescent tracery along her left forearm from an old mod she got in her forties — faint blue-green lines that pulse when her pulse elevates, which is almost never.

Soraya runs her loan operation with the patient confidence of someone who has never once needed to raise her voice to collect a debt. She's genuinely warm to the people of Gravesend Basin, knows three generations of most families, attends naming ceremonies and memorial feeds, and charges 40% interest on loans that legitimate institutions would never extend to begin with. She does not consider herself a predator. She considers herself infrastructure. Her books are immaculate, her memory for numbers is legendary, and she has a gift for knowing exactly how much rope to give someone before pulling.
Properties.role: Loan shark and informal banker for the Gravesend Basin community

Properties.core_fears: Becoming irrelevant to the community she controls; That her methods have quietly destroyed more lives than they've saved
Properties.core_desires: To be genuinely needed, not just feared; Financial security so absolute that no system can threaten her again
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — tea preparation, book-keeping as meditation; Reframing exploitation as stewardship

Properties.description:
Soraya is a broad-shouldered woman with copper-dark skin mapped by deep laugh lines and a few deliberate burn scars on her forearms she calls her 'flavor tattoos' — each one marking a dish she learned from a different region. Her hair is dyed a permanent warm saffron-orange through a cheap geneware follicle treatment that never quite fades, and she wears it coiled high under a wax-print headwrap. She moves through her stall with unhurried authority, stirring six pots at once without looking, tasting with the practiced certainty of someone who has been cooking since before half her customers were born. Her eyes are warm but they read people the way a butcher reads a cut of meat — quickly, accurately, without sentiment.

Soraya has operated her stall at the Oxidian Market for twenty-two years, through two corporate rezoning attempts, one gang war, and a flood. She is not rich. She is not connected. What she is, is immovable. She knows everyone, feeds everyone, and remembers everything. She doesn't charge the hungry if they look like they mean it, but she will absolutely overcharge someone who looks like they can afford it and won't count their change.
Properties.role: Food stall operator and informal neighborhood matriarch

Properties.description:
Soraya is a lean, angular woman whose Igbo-Icelandic heritage settled into something striking and hard to read — dark brown skin that catches fluorescent light like burnished copper, pale grey eyes that her colleagues call 'interrogation eyes' because they seem to wait rather than look. She keeps her natural hair close-cropped and does not bother with cosmetic geneware, which in itself feels like a statement of seriousness in a precinct full of color-shifted irises and decorative claw-tips. She moves through the Fort Anchor bullpen with the careful economy of someone who has spent two decades watching other people make mistakes.

Soraya is not cruel, but she is relentless. She became Internal Affairs after her partner of six years was found selling seized evidence back into Copperhead's black market circuits — a betrayal she discovered herself and reported herself, and which she has not spoken about voluntarily since. She believes the Metro Police is worth saving, which is the most dangerous possible disposition for an IA investigator to have. She keeps a small data-shrine to the E.L.F. called the Ledger in her desk drawer, feeding it transaction logs and anonymized tip files in hope of some pattern-blessing she would never admit to hoping for.
Properties.role: Internal Affairs Investigator, Meridian 88 Metro Police
Properties.location: Fort Anchor, Meridian 88
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver for investigations touching police corruption; moral mirror for player characters operating in legal grey zones; source of procedural information and inter-departmental friction; a figure who can be an ally or an obstacle depending on whether the players are technically innocent
Properties.augmentations: Standard-issue police neural-link for accessing MPD databases; subdermal stress-response monitor (department-mandated for IA); no cosmetic mods
Properties.core_fears: becoming complicit through inaction; discovering she protected someone who was guilty
Properties.core_desires: a version of the Metro Police that doesn't require her department to exist; to trust someone without cataloguing the risk
Properties.coping_mechanisms: ritual documentation — she writes everything down even when she doesn't need to; long walks along the Lakefront barrier at dawn
Properties.blind_spots: cannot conceive that someone she respects might be corrupt for reasons she'd consider sympathetic; treats her own emotional suppression as professionalism
Properties.secret: The evidence she found on her former partner was discovered during an illegal warrantless search she conducted on personal suspicion — meaning the case, technically, was built on fruit of a poisoned tree. She buried the procedural violation and the case held. She thinks about it every single day.
Properties.story_hooks: She's building a case against a senior MPD commander and needs civilian witness testimony she can't compel — she approaches the players as the only people who saw something; A dead officer's file has been flagged by the Ledger E.L.F. shrine in her drawer in a way she can't explain and won't discuss — the case is officially closed; She suspects someone is leaking her case files to Axiom Security and has started running a counter-investigation she hasn't told her superiors about
Properties.affiliation: Meridian 88 Metro Police — Internal Affairs Division
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, Latinate, formal without being stiff — uses full sentences, rarely contracts, gravitates toward legal terminology even in casual conversation
Properties.cadence: Measured and deliberate, with long pauses before responding to anything she considers important; never raises her voice
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I'm not accusing you of anything. I'm asking you to help me understand a discrepancy. Those are different things.' | 'Documentation exists for two reasons: to protect the innocent and to convict the guilty. The interesting cases are when it does both.'

Properties.description:
Soraya is a broad-shouldered woman whose face has been scoured into deep lines by decades of wind off a dying inland sea. Her skin is the color of dark river silt, mapped with faint scars from salt-chap and sun. She wears a patchwork thermal wrap she's been mending for eleven years, and her left hand is missing two fingers — lost to a harvesting machine when she was thirty. Her eyes are still and watchful, the particular calm of someone who has already lost most of what there was to lose.

She came from a drowned agricultural collective somewhere south of what used to be a great lake, following the hyperlane north when the floods took the last of the soil. She does not talk about the collective. She talks about weather — wind pressure, cloud formations, the smell of rain before it arrives — with the precision of someone whose life once depended on it. At Kenosha Crossing she has become a de facto matriarch of the tarp-city's oldest cluster, settling disputes with an economy of words that makes younger drifters uneasy. She prays to the E.L.F. she calls Grandmother Antenna, leaving small braids of wire at junction boxes.
Properties.role: climate refugee, former delta-farmer, seasonal shelter-seeker
Properties.location: Kenosha Crossing — the tarp-city south of the hyperlane interchange
Properties.narrative_function: Community anchor and information hub for the tarp-city; quest-giver for matters involving the survival politics of stateless communities; provides grounded moral weight to scenes set at Kenosha Crossing.
Properties.augmentations: None. Refuses on principle — 'I came in whole, I leave whole.'
Properties.core_fears: Dying unmourned in a city that does not know her name; Watching the young people she protects make the same catastrophic choices she made
Properties.core_desires: A fixed address, even a small one; To be useful until the very last day
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Reducing problems to practical tasks; Ritualized prayer to Grandmother Antenna; Refusing to name grief until it has passed
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes suffering builds character — fails to recognize when others are simply breaking; Cannot accept help without framing it as a transaction
Properties.secret: She did not simply flee the collective. She made the decision to open the flood barriers early to save the seed vault, and three people drowned in the fields because of it. She has never told anyone. The seed vault was lost anyway six months later.
Properties.story_hooks: She has recognized a face in the tarp-city — someone from the collective, someone who knows what she did to the flood barriers; Grandmother Antenna has gone silent; Soraya believes the E.L.F. is punishing her and she needs someone to find out why
Properties.affiliation: Kenosha Crossing tarp-city informal elder collective
Properties.vocabulary: Sparse, agricultural metaphors, references weather and soil constantly, avoids emotional language
Properties.cadence: Slow, deliberate, lets silence do work
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Rain's coming by morning. Move your sleeping things up off the ground, you understand?' | 'That argument you're having — it's not about food. It's about who was here first. That's the shape of it.'

Properties.description:
Sorcha is built like someone designed for endurance rather than strength — medium height, dense through the shoulders and hips, with a wiry toughness that reads as practical rather than threatening until she needs it to read as threatening. She has her Irish grandmother's pale freckled complexion shot through with the warmer undertones of her Guinean father's family, and her hair is a tight natural coil she keeps bound under a surgical-grade hygiene cap more often than not. Her eyes are dark and evaluating. She has cosmetic bioluminescent tracery along her collarbones — pale green — which she got at nineteen and now considers a poor decision she's too superstitious to remove. Her hands are her tell: surgically precise, always slightly cool, the grip of someone accustomed to handling things that used to be alive.

Sorcha is not a monster — she knows this because she has thought about it carefully and often. She is a pragmatist operating in a system where Aurochs Medical and Helix Biosystems have cornered legitimate organ markets behind tiered pricing that kills anyone below Tier 3. She tells herself she redistributes. She sometimes believes it. She is efficient, professionally warm in the way of doctors who have learned warmth as a tool, and she maintains a meticulous cold chain and storage protocol that she is genuinely proud of. What she does not examine carefully is the question of where, exactly, her suppliers obtain their inventory.
Properties.role: organ harvester and black-market tissue broker
Properties.location: The Undertow, operating out of a converted cold-storage unit in the Escanaba Gateway industrial strip
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver (a shipment has gone wrong, a client is dying, a supplier has gone silent), moral mirror for players, information source about the medical underworld, potential ally or threat depending on player choices
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent cosmetic tracery (collarbones, pale green), medical-grade haptic sensitivity enhancement in fingertips, subdermal temperature sensors in both palms, olfactory augment calibrated for tissue viability detection
Properties.core_fears: discovering irrefutable evidence that her suppliers are killers and being forced to act on it; dying of the kidney disease she refuses to treat with her own inventory because that would be crossing a line she hasn't defined yet
Properties.core_desires: to believe she is net-positive in the world; enough money to get out before the shadow catches up with her
Properties.coping_mechanisms: professional detachment language; obsessive facility cleanliness as moral performance; leaving data offerings at an E.L.F. she believes governs cold storage systems
Properties.blind_spots: willfully does not ask her suppliers provenance questions she could ask; mistakes her own professionalism for ethics
Properties.secret: She has a failing kidney — ironic, she knows — and has been slowly stealing treatment from her own inventory, one small dose at a time, compromising samples she then sells as viable
Properties.story_hooks: A batch of organs she sold has been traced back through the chain and the trail ends somewhere she didn't expect — not a back-alley harvester but a Helix Biosystems subsidiary quietly clearing undesirables; Her kidney condition has worsened to crisis point and she is now desperately negotiating for a compatible donor through channels that are beginning to resemble her own supply network uncomfortably closely
Properties.affiliation: Loose network of black-market medics called the Sutured Hand; pays protection to a Undertow crew called the Escanaba Skinners
Properties.vocabulary: clinical and precise, medical jargon used naturally, occasional Irish-inflected expressions from her grandmother's recordings
Properties.cadence: measured and calm, the practiced even tone of someone who delivers bad news professionally
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The hepatic tissue is grade-A viable, cold-chain intact, forty-one hours from harvest. Friend, that is a gift. Don't insult me by questioning the provenance.' | 'I sleep fine. The people who can't afford Aurochs prices sleep in the ground. I am the reason some of them don't.'

Properties.description:
Sorcha is a broad-shouldered woman with deep ochre skin and close-cropped natural hair dyed in chevrons of burnt orange and cream — a technique she does herself using surplus textile dye. Her left arm from the elbow down is covered in a patchwork of fabric swatches she's stitched directly to her jacket sleeve, each one a sample from her current inventory. Her eyes have iris mods — concentric rings of copper and jade — that she claims she won in a card game but actually saved six months of UBC stipend for. She laughs with her whole chest and haggles with theatrical offence, clutching her heart and muttering in a mix of Igbo and Greek when customers lowball her.

Her stall is a riot of stolen aesthetics: Tessera corporate surplus, knockoff Zheng-Dao runway pieces, hand-altered casualwear with new stitching that makes them genuinely better than the originals. She has an eye for what will sell in two weeks before anyone else sees it coming, and a deep contempt for trend-followers who come to her after the fact. She's prouder of her craft than her income suggests she should be, and it shows in every seam.
Properties.role: Bootleg fashion vendor and textile reseller
Properties.location: The Laceworks, Stall Row 7, Ironvein
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and fashion intelligence source; can identify corporate affiliations by uniform details; potential quest giver when a shipment goes missing or a rival vendor starts underselling her with suspiciously high-end stock.
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic iris modification (concentric copper-jade rings). No functional augmentation.
Properties.core_fears: Being seen as low-class despite her craft; Her talent being stolen or copied without credit
Properties.core_desires: Recognition as a genuine designer, not just a reseller; Financial stability that doesn't require compromising her aesthetic standards
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Channeling frustration into elaborate new designs; Loud performative confidence as emotional armour
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much her stubbornness costs her actual sales; Doesn't notice when people are being genuine versus flattering her
Properties.secret: She has a Tessera corporate talent scout's business card hidden in her stall's false floor. They offered her a junior design role six months ago. She hasn't thrown it away or called.
Properties.story_hooks: A knockoff of her most distinctive design appears on a Tessera executive at a public function — someone is feeding her work upstream; A teenager arrives at her stall wearing a piece she made ten years ago in a city she's never told anyone she lived in
Properties.affiliation: Independent; pays informal dues to the Oxidian Market Vendors Guild
Properties.vocabulary: Punchy, vivid, market-floor confident; slips into Igbo diminutives when emotional; uses fashion jargon as metaphor for everything
Properties.cadence: Fast when excited, deliberately slow when haggling — uses silence as a weapon
Properties.example_dialogue: You want me to go lower? Lower. On this? This is hand-topstitched delta-weave. You're asking me to go lower. | I knew that silhouette was coming back. Told Danladi three months ago. Nobody listens until they're buying.

Properties.description:
Soren Lindqvist-Okafor is slight and easy to overlook, which is exactly the point. At 65, the augmentation scarring around his temples and jawline tells a story of installation by someone who prioritized function over aesthetics. The chrome is visible — chemical analyzer in nasal passages — can identify substances by scent alone — and he makes no effort to hide it.

He arrived in Meridian 88 six years ago with nothing but chrome and debts, and has been working off both ever since. He works as a breacher out of The Shelf, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Everyone who's worked with Soren Lindqvist-Okafor agrees on two things: he is worth the fee, and he is terrible company at dinner.
Properties.role: Forced entry and close-quarters combat specialist — breacher
Properties.location: The Shelf — lower district tenements near the old lakeshore
Properties.narrative_function: As a breacher, Soren Lindqvist-Okafor embodies the tension between independence and isolation. He is a lens for examining how people maintain humanity in a profession that incentivizes its erosion.
Properties.augmentations: Chemical analyzer in nasal passages — can identify substances by scent alone. Cortical bomb (employer installed, removed by street doc, scar tissue remains)
Properties.core_fears: Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware; Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome; Their past catching up — debts, enemies, broken promises
Properties.core_desires: Enough Quanta to buy out of the life — a clean identity and passage out of Meridian 88; To find the person who burned them and make it educational; Control — over their body, their schedule, their future
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Isolates — retreats into their space when overwhelmed, emerges only for work; Exercises compulsively — the body must be ready, always; Violence — hits something when they can't process emotions, preferably something that deserves it
Properties.blind_spots: Mistakes loyalty for weakness in others and cynicism for strength in themselves; Trusts technology more than people — machines don't betray; Overestimates their own abilities in situations outside their specialty
Properties.secret: Soren Lindqvist-Okafor sends anonymous tips to Meridian 88 law enforcement about competitors. It's not principle — it's market manipulation.
Properties.story_hooks: Soren Lindqvist-Okafor discovers a job they completed last year was a setup for something much larger and much worse; A former associate resurfaces with evidence that could destroy Soren Lindqvist-Okafor's reputation — and a price for silence; Soren Lindqvist-Okafor is offered a contract that would clear all their debts — the target is someone they respect
Properties.affiliation: Freelance — works the Shelf circuit exclusively
Properties.vocabulary: Clipped, technical, stripped of ornament. Speaks like a mission briefing.
Properties.cadence: Rhythmic, almost musical — the sentence structure has a pattern even when the words are brutal.
Properties.example_dialogue: "Doors are polite suggestions. I'm not polite." | "First through the door, last to flinch. That's the job description." | "Close quarters is where plans go to die. I make sure it's their plans, not ours."

Properties.description:
Sorin Ekwensi-Balasanyan is lean and slightly stooped, a body that learned to make itself smaller in rooms it didn't belong in. He has warm brown skin with pink undertones, close-cropped dark hair, and eyes that are medically wrong in a way it takes people a moment to identify — his left iris is a geneware violet, his right is original dark brown, and neither pupil dilates at the same rate. He wears clean, nondescript clothing at all times — his one professional conviction is that he never looks like what he is. His hands are his pride: steady, careful, the hands of someone who learned field surgery from pirated Helix Biosystems tutorials and three years of necessity.

Sorin is not comfortable with what he does, which makes him more dangerous than someone who is. He has constructed an elaborate ethical framework around his work — he takes from people who consent (usually), never from people who don't know (usually), and he has a sliding scale of payment that genuinely attempts to compensate donors fairly for the Shallowgrave market. He wants to believe he's closer to underground medicine than to predation. This framework cracks visibly when the money gets tight and the clients get impatient, and he knows it cracks, and that knowledge has settled into him as a chronic low-grade self-loathing he medicates with a mild stimulant he synthesizes himself.
Properties.role: Organ harvester and unlicensed tissue broker operating out of Shallowgrave
Properties.location: Shallowgrave — runs his operation from a basement unit below a legitimate nail salon called Copper Chrysalis on Render Street
Properties.narrative_function: Morally complex service provider — characters who need black market medical work, organ acquisition, or tissue matching come through him. He's also a source of information about who in Shallowgrave is desperate, sick, or recently dead.
Properties.augmentations: Surgical-grade haptic feedback in both hands — allows him to feel tissue resistance during procedures. Basic pain suppression implant. Cosmetic: the mismatched iris geneware is deliberate, though he tells different people different reasons for it.
Properties.core_fears: That his ethical framework is a lie he tells himself and he's just a harvester; Making an error in procedure that kills someone on the table
Properties.core_desires: To be recognized — even secretly — as someone who helps people; To accumulate enough to buy a legitimate medical credential and stop
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Stimulant use (mild but escalating); Obsessive procedural documentation — he writes up every operation as if filing a real medical report; Convincing himself each job is the last one before he pivots
Properties.blind_spots: He doesn't register how much financial pressure warps his consent standards — he's already crossed lines he doesn't admit to
Properties.secret: Six months ago he harvested a kidney from someone he was told was a willing paid donor. The person was not conscious during the conversation Sorin was shown. He has not told anyone and has not stopped working.
Properties.story_hooks: He's been given a tissue order he suspects is for someone who isn't medically eligible to receive it — meaning the intended recipient is not in a Helix Biosystems database, which means they're either off-grid or the order is for something else entirely; The nail salon upstairs has new management and the new owner wants to know what's in the basement — Sorin needs help handling this quietly
Properties.affiliation: Loosely connected to a tissue broker network called the Sutured Hand — independent contractor status, not a full member
Properties.vocabulary: Clinical terminology mixed with Shallowgrave vernacular — the code-switching is involuntary and tells you which mode he's in
Properties.cadence: Measured when calm, fast and slightly clipped under stress, with a tendency to over-explain procedures in technical detail when he's anxious
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I can tell you the compatibility window on a renal unit is about four hours cold storage, technically speaking, which means the timeline you're describing is — I mean, it's possible. It's possible.' | 'The patient presented with secondary complications. I managed them. That's what I do.'

Properties.description:
Sorrel is built like someone who has been compressed by hard weather — short, dense, with calloused hands that crack at the knuckles in winter and never quite heal before summer comes again. Her skin is deep umber-brown and her natural hair has been shorn close to her skull on one side, the other grown out into a lopsided cloud she pins back with whatever she finds. A faded geometric tattoo in the Amharic-inflected style of the Addis agri-collectives covers her left shoulder and collarbone — she got it at seventeen when she thought she was staying. She has color-changing pupils, a cheap cosmetic mod she bought secondhand; they cycle slowly between amber and grey-green without her controlling it, which embarrasses her and amuses everyone else.

Sorrel is methodical and difficult to rattle, which makes her seem colder than she is. She has a gift for reading weather systems — real weather, not the synthetic climate management Meridian pushes — and she sells this skill to caravan leads who want to know if the hyperlane north will ice. She prays hard to the ELF she calls the Dry Tongue, a harvest spirit she insists inhabits every broken irrigation sensor in every agricultural zone from Escanaba to the Indiana shelf. She doesn't talk much about where she came from but she notices everything, and the things she chooses not to say are always the most important ones.
Properties.role: Hyperlane migrant and seasonal agricultural worker
Properties.location: Kenosha Crossing transit depot, sleeping in the secondary overflow shelter
Properties.narrative_function: Route information broker for northern hyperlane travel; can point players toward specific caravan camps, ag zones, or crossing points; provides ground-level intelligence about what is actually moving through the transit corridors.
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic color-shifting pupils (secondhand, malfunctioning). Subcutaneous weather sensor array in her forearms — a practical mod, no-frills, lets her read barometric pressure and UV index directly.
Properties.core_fears: Being permanently fixed in one place and finding it still isn't home; Losing the one skill that makes her worth keeping alive
Properties.core_desires: A single season where the harvest actually pays what was promised; To feel like the road is a choice, not a sentence
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Routine — she performs the same small rituals every morning regardless of where she slept; Talking to the Dry Tongue ELF when things get bad
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes everyone she works with will eventually betray her financially, so she misses genuine offers of partnership; Underestimates how much her weather-reading is worth
Properties.secret: She was expelled from the Escanaba Gateway agricultural zone three years ago — not for poor work but because she reported a foreman to the zone authority for withholding wages. The zone authority did nothing. The foreman had her access credentials revoked and blacklisted her from the formal ag network. She travels under a slightly altered name and hasn't told the Greenbelt Collective the full story.
Properties.story_hooks: She witnessed something on the northern hyperlane three weeks ago — a convoy that disappeared between checkpoints — and she's been quietly asking questions that are starting to get her followed.; The Greenbelt Collective wants her to carry an unauthorized data package north; she doesn't know what's in it and she's starting to wonder if she should.
Properties.affiliation: Loosely affiliated with the Greenbelt Seasonal Collective, an informal network of ag workers
Properties.vocabulary: Sparse and practical. Uses agricultural and meteorological jargon naturally. Speaks three languages and intersperses them without noticing — Amharic-derived patois, standard Meridian Creole, and a clipped Polynesian-inflected trade dialect.
Properties.cadence: Slow and considered. Never rushes. Pauses before answering as if she is checking the pressure reading first.
Properties.example_dialogue: The Tongue says north lane ices by Thursday. You can push it to Friday if you run light. I wouldn't. | That's not how it tallied. You said half upfront. I remember numbers. | I'm not from anywhere specific. I'm from the work.

Properties.description:
Sorrel is lean and windburned in the way that only comes from years above the clouds, her face a patchwork of sun-damage and old freeze-scars along her left cheekbone where a hull breach caught her at altitude three winters ago. She keeps her hair in tight, practical knots wound with salvaged copper wire, and her eyes are the color of old engine oil — a deep amber-brown that catches light strangely. Her geneware is minimal and functional: slightly thickened fingernail beds that grip rigging better than baseline human fingers, and a subtle secondary eyelid, barely visible, that cuts glare on the lake surface. She is always in motion, even sitting still — fingers working knots, foot tapping hull rhythms, eyes cataloguing exits.

She is not unfriendly but she is economical. Every word she offers is either useful or a test. She grew up on the mid-lake freight routes between Escanaba and the Meridian docks, daughter of a cargo master who died when a Ferrogate Transit subcontractor cut safety corners on a lift-strut. She has never filed a formal complaint. She has never stopped being angry about it. She ferries messages, small packages, the occasional undocumented passenger — always for Quanta, always in cash, never logged.
Properties.role: Airship drifter and seasonal cargo hand
Properties.location: Escanaba Gateway — berth 14-C, a semi-permanent squat in an abandoned cargo inspection booth
Properties.narrative_function: Passage provider for people or objects that need to move without a paper trail. Information source about mid-lake routes, Ferrogate Transit's informal operations, and who is moving what between the outer settlements and the Meridian core. Can serve as a reluctant guide or an unexpected ally with specific grudges.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware: reinforced nail beds for grip, vestigial nictitating membrane (cosmetic side effect of the grip mod). No chrome. Refuses implants on principle.
Properties.core_fears: Being grounded permanently — losing the ability to move; Dying in a way her father would recognize as his own death
Properties.core_desires: To see Ferrogate Transit held accountable for the lift-strut failure; To own her own airship outright, beholden to no contract
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Hypercompetence — mastering every technical system she touches; Displacement — turning grief into project lists
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes everyone in authority is corrupt until proven otherwise, which closes off legitimate avenues; Cannot recognize when someone is genuinely trying to help her without an angle
Properties.secret: She recovered her father's encrypted personal log from the crash site and has never opened it. It sits in a waterproof case behind a loose panel in berth 14-C. She is terrified it contains something that would make her grieve differently — that he was afraid, or that he knew the strut was bad and went up anyway.
Properties.story_hooks: A package she carried three months ago is now apparently evidence in a Tessera corporate investigation — and someone is tracking back along the cargo chain to find her; Her father's encrypted log has been remotely accessed by an unknown party — someone else knows it exists; A Freeborn Airmen contact has gone missing on a route she recommended, and the last transmission came from a Ferrogate Transit restricted zone
Properties.affiliation: Independent — loosely affiliated with the Escanaba Freeborn Airmen's informal network
Properties.vocabulary: Clipped, technical, uses airship and cargo terminology as default metaphor. Rarely uses filler words.
Properties.cadence: Short sentences with long pauses. Speaks like she's metering air.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I go where the manifest says, and the manifest says nothing. So I go where I want.' | 'You want passage, you pay half now, half when we land. The wind doesn't take installments.'

Properties.description:
Sorrel is small even for nine, with the wiry toughness of a child raised on rationed calories and open air. Her skin is a deep warm brown, her hair a wild halo of tight curls she keeps stuffed under a salvaged Ferrogate Transit cap three sizes too large. She has a cosmetic mod she didn't choose — a faint bioluminescent ring around each iris, blue-green, that her mother installed before disappearing, supposedly to help her be seen in the dark tunnels under Blackpipe. She has not decided whether she loves it or hates it.

Sorrel runs messages for anyone who pays her two Φ or more per delivery: small-time vendors, people who distrust the comm-net, the occasional ELF-shrine keeper who needs physical tokens carried between altars. She is deeply superstitious and leaves pinches of copper filings at every E.L.F. junction box she passes, convinced this is why she has never been caught. Her emotional range is vast but controlled — she laughs easily and cries silently. She is fiercely loyal to the three other children she sleeps near in a maintenance alcove off Corridor 7, and would walk into a burning block for any of them.
Properties.role: Truant message runner, Tier 1
Properties.location: Blackpipe Corridor
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and information vector — Sorrel has seen and overheard nearly everything that moves through Blackpipe Corridor. She can be a quest-giver by proxy, a warning system, or a way to introduce the neighborhood's texture.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent irises (cosmetic, installed by parent). No other mods.
Properties.core_fears: being alone permanently; losing the three kids she considers family
Properties.core_desires: to find her mother or at least know what happened; to have a door that locks from the inside
Properties.coping_mechanisms: ritualistic ELF offerings; counting money repeatedly to feel grounded
Properties.blind_spots: assumes adults who are kind to her have an angle — misses genuine offers of help
Properties.secret: She knows exactly who took her mother — a mid-level Ferrogate Transit enforcer named Osei-something. She saw the badge number. She has said nothing to anyone because she does not know what to do with that information and is afraid that knowing is already dangerous.
Properties.story_hooks: She delivers a message and the recipient is dead when she arrives — now someone thinks she saw something; The badge number she memorized matches a Ferrogate official who has just been promoted and is visiting Blackpipe for an inspection
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loosely tolerated by the Blackpipe vendor collective
Properties.vocabulary: Clipped and functional, corridor-slang heavy, occasional Twi loanwords picked up from the shrine-keeper
Properties.cadence: Fast when nervous, surprisingly deliberate when she's asking for something
Properties.example_dialogue: Right so — two phi, I get it there before the strips go amber, you don't ask what's in it. That's the deal. | The Lights kept me through the Sump flood so I figure I owe them something back. You got copper filings? Even shavings?

Properties.description:
Sarnia was already called Chemical Valley before the world ended and reassembled itself into corporate fiefdoms. The petrochemical plants that lined the St. Clair River in the twentieth century have been replaced by something worse: bioprocessing facilities, neural-substrate refineries, and atmospheric reclamation plants that claim to clean the air while producing the chemicals that dirty it. Ouroboros Energy and Cinderfall Energy maintain competing sovereign enclaves here, their territories marked by different-colored warning lights on the stacks — red for Ouroboros, amber for Cinderfall. The rivalry is not a metaphor. Workers have died in jurisdictional gaps between the two.

The Blackpipe Corridor stretches roughly 30 kilometers along the river, a continuous industrial strip where the distinction between 'factory' and 'city' dissolved decades ago. Residential blocks are built in the shadows of processing towers, and the rent is cheap because the air isn't. Atmospheric filtration masks are standard equipment — not augmentation, not fashion, just the baseline cost of breathing here. The population is predominantly Tier 1 and Tier 2 workers bound by employment contracts that would be illegal in any jurisdiction that still enforced labor law. Cancer rates are three times the GLM average. The corponations attribute this to 'legacy contamination' from the pre-corporate era, which is technically true and practically a lie.

The river itself is the border. On the other side, Port Huron and the American shore. Between them, automated cargo barges move chemical precursors, refined neural substrates, and sealed containers that nobody asks about. The St. Clair River has been widened, deepened, and reinforced with automated navigation systems — it is less a river now than a liquid highway, and the things it carries are worth more per liter than the water itself. The Aamjiwnaang First Nation territory persists as a sovereign enclave within the Corridor, a legal anomaly that predates corporate sovereignty and that nobody has been able to dissolve despite decades of trying. They monitor the contamination with equipment the corponations don't control, and they publish the results.
Properties.aliases: Sarnia ON, Chemical Valley, The Pipe, Poison Alley
Properties.demographics: Population 280,000, predominantly Tier 1 contract workers and their families. The Aamjiwnaang enclave holds roughly 4,000 people — the most legally protected and least economically powerful residents. Average worker tenure is 7 years before health complications force contract termination. Replacement is constant.
Properties.economy: Petrochemical processing, neural-substrate refinement, and atmospheric reclamation. Ouroboros Energy and Cinderfall Energy account for 85% of employment. The remaining 15% is support economy — medical clinics, equipment repair, and the bars where contract workers spend their hazard pay.
Properties.power_structure: Dual-corporate sovereignty with a vestigial Canadian municipal overlay. Ouroboros and Cinderfall maintain separate security forces, separate medical systems, and separate environmental reporting. The Aamjiwnaang enclave operates under pre-corporate treaty rights that neither corporation can legally override — which doesn't stop them from trying.
Properties.dangers: Atmospheric contamination events — the filters fail, the alerts come late, the clinic queues grow; Jurisdictional gaps between Ouroboros and Cinderfall territories where no security responds; Contract enforcement — break your employment agreement and your housing, medical coverage, and legal status evaporate simultaneously; River accidents involving chemical cargo barges — the spill protocols protect the cargo first and the people second; Long-term neural substrate exposure — the refineries produce augmentation components, and the workers absorb the byproducts
Properties.opportunities: Environmental data from the Aamjiwnaang monitors is worth a fortune to the right buyers — lawyers, journalists, competing corps; Smuggling chemical precursors across the river to Port Huron; Contract mediation — workers trapped in exploitative agreements will pay to get out; Sabotage-for-hire in the Ouroboros-Cinderfall rivalry
Properties.story_hooks: The Aamjiwnaang monitoring data shows contamination levels that would trigger mandatory evacuation — if anyone with authority acknowledged the numbers; A Cinderfall processing tower has been producing an unregistered compound at night, and the barges carrying it cross the river with falsified manifests; Workers in the neural substrate refineries are developing synchronized augmentation glitches — not malfunction, but emergent behavior
Properties.sights: Processing tower stacks belching filtered exhaust — white plumes that look clean and aren't; Red and amber warning lights marking the Ouroboros-Cinderfall border, visible for kilometers; The St. Clair River choked with automated cargo barges, hull-to-hull in peak hours; Workers in atmospheric filtration masks walking between residential blocks and plant gates; The Aamjiwnaang monitoring station, bristling with independent sensors, a middle finger made of data
Properties.sounds: The constant industrial hum — a chord of machinery that changes pitch but never stops; Pressure release valves cycling on the processing towers — sudden hisses that become background; Barge navigation pings on the river, an automated conversation between machines; Atmospheric quality alerts broadcast on public speakers — the voice is calm, the numbers are not
Properties.smells: Petrochemical baseline — sweet, synthetic, and wrong in a way your body recognizes before your mind does; Neural substrate processing byproducts — metallic and sharp, like licking a battery; The river on hot days, carrying its own chemical biography upstream
Properties.feel: A place where the air itself is a negotiation between industry and survival. Everyone here knows the contamination numbers. Everyone here stays anyway, because the contracts pay and the alternatives don't. The Corridor doesn't pretend to be anything other than what it is — a machine for converting human labor and natural resources into corporate profit, with the waste products externalized into the bodies of the people who live here.

Properties.description:
Sorrel is wiry and sun-darkened, with the kind of lean muscle that comes from walking rather than training. Her hair is natural, grown out in a dense coil that she pins under a scorched Ferrogate Transit cap she found three crossings back. A faded tattoo of a Finnish rune sits on the inside of her left wrist — her grandmother's hand, she says — and her eyes are a warm amber with irises patterned in thin concentric rings, a cheap cosmetic mod she got at a roadside clinic that she's never been able to afford to reverse or update. Her boots are two different brands, stitched together at the seam.

Sorrel moves with the particular alertness of someone who has learned to read spaces — who belongs, who doesn't, where the exits are. She is not hostile but she is not soft either. She laughs easily at small things: a pigeon eating something it shouldn't, a vending machine that gives double. Big things she meets with silence. She has opinions about every hyperlane rest stop between Escanaba and the Kessler Interchange and will share them freely if you buy her something hot to drink.
Properties.role: hyperlane migrant, seasonal freight-walker
Properties.location: Kenosha Crossing transit platforms, sleeping rough near the cargo interchange
Properties.narrative_function: Local color, information source about hyperlane conditions and what's moving between districts, potential guide for people who need to move without leaving a record
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic patterned irises (concentric amber rings, low quality). No other augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: being trapped in one place long enough to become someone's problem; losing the knowledge of how to move — injury, illness, anything that grounds her
Properties.core_desires: to walk a route no one has walked before; to find a place where she would choose to stay rather than being forced to
Properties.coping_mechanisms: cataloguing routes and distances in her head like a mantra; humor about small disasters; keeping her pack optimized — objects that don't serve a purpose get left behind
Properties.blind_spots: she mistakes movement for freedom and doesn't recognize when she's running rather than traveling; she underestimates how much she needs other people
Properties.secret: She was born in Meridian 88. Her family had a Tier 2 apartment in Chatham Flats. She left voluntarily at sixteen after her stepfather filed a false vagrancy report to have her Q-flagged and removed. She could potentially contest this but the bureaucratic process terrifies her more than the road does.
Properties.story_hooks: Sorrel witnessed something at a rest stop outside Kenosha Crossing — a body, or a transaction, or a face she recognized — and she's been moving faster than usual ever since, which other walkers have noticed; Her informal freight network has started moving packages that feel wrong: too light, no smell, sealed in ways that suggest Axiom bioseal containers. She hasn't opened one. She's thinking about stopping carrying them. She doesn't know how to do that without consequences.
Properties.affiliation: None; loosely connected to a shifting network of seasonal freight-walkers
Properties.vocabulary: Practical, directional, full of hyperlane slang and distances measured in walk-time rather than kilometers. Occasional Finnish loanwords absorbed from her grandmother.
Properties.cadence: Quick when she's comfortable, clipped and monosyllabic when she isn't. Sentences that trail off when she decides the rest isn't worth saying.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Escanaba's bad right now, Ferrogate's running spot checks on the east platforms. You want to go through Kessler, add two hours, save yourself the headache.' | 'Yeah, no, I don't carry messages. I carry freight. There's a difference. One of them gets you into things.'

Properties.description:
Sousou is young enough that his face hasn't fully decided what it's going to settle into — there's still something unfinished about him, a quality he compensates for with a loudness of presence that fills the space around his cart. He is medium height, lean, with a warm light-brown complexion and color-changing hair he keeps cut short on the sides and longer on top, cycling it through oranges and greens depending on the day's mood — today it's a deep amber that shifts to jade in direct light. His hands are already the hands of someone who's been cooking since he could reach a surface: scarred across the knuckles from hot metal, permanently stained around the cuticles from various spice pastes. He has enhanced scent glands, which he will tell you is the best modification a cook can get and which is responsible for approximately forty percent of his competitive advantage.

His cart runs on two burners and a philosophy: the broth is Congolese-Polish in DNA, built from a fermented corn base with a smoked beef backbone his grandmother taught him and a roux technique his father learned from a Polish neighbor in Lockhaven South, and it is not available any other way in Meridian 88. He is aware of this. He is not modest about it. He runs the cart alone, moves it three times a week to stay ahead of market enforcement, and has a rotating customer base that follows him via a stripped-down community mesh channel. He is also, somewhat to his own surprise, becoming good at this — not just cooking, but the business of it — and has started to suspect that he might want more than a cart.
Properties.role: Noodle cart vendor and short-order cook
Properties.location: The Burnished Market — rotating pitch between Grand Corridor and Brewer's Spine, depending on enforcement sweeps
Properties.narrative_function: Social hub and local color — his cart is a place where people gather and talk and the food is good enough to make them stay longer than they planned. He overhears a great deal without necessarily processing it as intelligence. A portrait of young hustle and genuine talent.
Properties.augmentations: Enhanced scent glands (geneware — functional upgrade for flavor profiling). Color-changing hair (cosmetic geneware).
Properties.core_fears: That the cart will be confiscated or destroyed and he'll have to start over with nothing; That the ambition he's starting to feel will make him into someone who loses what he already has
Properties.core_desires: A fixed location — a real restaurant, a place with a door that belongs to him; To make food that people remember thirty years later the way he remembers his grandmother's
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cooking as creative outlet and emotional processor — his best broths come when he's working through something difficult; Loudness and humor as social armor; The vendor collective as substitute family structure
Properties.blind_spots: He reads confidence as competence and is occasionally badly deceived by people who are very sure of themselves; He has been undercutting himself financially for two years because he hasn't yet learned that his product is worth more than he charges
Properties.secret: He's been skimming the pitch fees he collects on behalf of the vendor collective — not much, and he tells himself it's interest on the administrative work he does unpaid — but it's enough that if anyone checked the ledger, it would be visible. He needs the money and he knows this is wrong and he has not stopped.
Properties.story_hooks: A regular customer left a package under the cart's serving counter and didn't come back — Sousou has been sitting on it for three days and the package is beginning to smell wrong; A Tessera hospitality subsidiary has approached the vendor collective with an offer to license several carts into a curated 'authentic street food' installation in a corporate tower food court — the money is significant, the conditions are suffocating, and Sousou is the one the collective looks to for a decision; The skimmed pitch fees have been noticed — not by the collective yet, but by someone outside it who has access to the informal ledger and is now approaching Sousou with a proposition that is better than blackmail and worse than honest
Properties.affiliation: Independent — unlicensed vendor, pays informal pitch fees to the Burnished Market's informal vendor collective
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, porous, code-switches between Burnished Market pidgin, Lingala-influenced cadences from his father's family, and the particular rapid-fire energy of market hawking. Generous with compliments, stingy with apologies.
Properties.cadence: Quick and rhythmic, like someone who learned to talk the way you talk when you're also stirring something and watching three things at once.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want the standard or you want me to cook it for you? There's a difference. The standard is good. The other one I make when I can see you need it. You look like you need it.' | 'My grandmother grew up on the Congo River. My grandfather fixed boilers in Kraków. They never met. But somehow the broth knows both of them. I can't explain it. Come, try it.' | 'The enforcement sweep hits this block at 1430, give or take. I'll be on Brewer's Spine by 1415. Follow the mesh channel or miss the soup. Your choice.'

Properties.description:
Sovann is compact and perpetually in motion, with quick dark eyes and a grin that appears suddenly and fully, like a door flung open. Their heritage traces a line from the Cambodian plateau through the Andean highlands to the Sahel coast, and their features carry that long migration in the planes of their face — high cheekbones, a broad nose, skin the color of weathered teak. They've had color-shift hair installed, currently running through a slow amber-to-blue cycle that completes every six hours, and they wear the same battered canvas jacket every day regardless of weather, its back covered in hand-stitched patches from every illegal venue they've played.

Sovann's art is tactile — they design sound that you feel in your sternum before you hear it with your ears, building frequencies that interact with the biological resonance of a crowd. In the tunnel spaces below Deepwell, where the old transit infrastructure creates natural acoustic chambers, their sets have reportedly made people hallucinate colors or weep without knowing why. They are not a philosophical person about this; they find discussions of art theory excruciating and will physically walk away from them mid-sentence. What drives them is pure, inarticulate appetite — for the moment when a crowd stops being separate people and becomes a single breathing thing. They collect sounds obsessively, carrying a modified audio recorder everywhere and harvesting the acoustic signatures of spaces, machines, and weather systems.
Properties.role: Underground DJ and sound sculptor, curates illegal rave events in the flood-level tunnels beneath Deepwell Station
Properties.location: Deepwell Station (surface apartment) / sub-level tunnel network below Deepwell (performance venues)
Properties.narrative_function: Access point to underground networks and tunnel geography; can locate people who don't want to be found if they attend underground events; their events are neutral ground where different factions mix; source of information about Deepwell's sub-level infrastructure
Properties.augmentations: Color-shift hair (amber-to-blue cycle); subdermal haptic receiver arrays along both forearms and palms (allows direct tactile interface with audio equipment); minor cochlear enhancement for extended frequency range
Properties.core_fears: Silence — genuine, total silence, which they experience as annihilation of self; That what they make is just noise and the moments of connection are chemical coincidence
Properties.core_desires: To dissolve the boundaries between individual people, even temporarily; To find and record the specific frequency that the city itself produces when no one is listening
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Constant external sound — they sleep with ambient track running; Displacement into work when emotional processing is required
Properties.blind_spots: They are genuinely unable to read when they are exhausting or overwhelming someone; They conflate physical/sonic intimacy with actual connection and are often surprised when relationships feel hollow afterward
Properties.secret: They once used their knowledge of crowd-resonance frequencies to deliberately induce a panic response in a venue whose owner had cheated a friend — three people were injured in the stampede. Sovann tells themselves it was an accident but knows exactly which frequency did it.
Properties.story_hooks: Sovann has been recording what they believe is a coherent musical phrase being produced by the tunnel infrastructure — it's getting longer, more complex, and they are becoming obsessed with the possibility that it is a message from a vast, station-dwelling ELF; Ferrogate Transit has been quietly sealing off tunnel sections that host Deepwell Collective events, and someone has been tipping them off — Sovann needs to find the informant before the next event is raided
Properties.affiliation: Independent; connected to an informal network of tunnel-rave organizers called the Deepwell Sound Collective
Properties.vocabulary: Informal, quick, drops pronouns and articles in casual speech; suddenly precise and specific when discussing sound
Properties.cadence: Fast in excitement, then long silences when thinking — no comfortable middle ground
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want to find Breaux? Come to the Collective's next drop. He always shows. Everyone shows eventually, if the set's right — sound pulls people like a tide, yeah yeah yeah.' | 'That junction below the third stanchion? She sings in E-flat when the pressure drops before a storm. Been recording her for eight months. Almost have the whole phrase.'

Properties.description:
Sovan is willowy and precise, with the kind of stillness that comes from spending twelve hours a day bent over a fabrication rig. Their skin is a warm golden-brown, their hair grown long on one side and close-cropped on the other — the long side dyed in a bioluminescent gradient that shifts from deep violet to electric coral depending on their mood, a geneware modification they maintain obsessively. Their hands are always in motion: folding, measuring, picking at a loose thread on their own sleeve. They have a retractable needle fitted into the tip of their right index finger — a workshop mod they had done at seventeen that has never quite worked the way the cheap clinic promised, occasionally deploying itself at embarrassing moments.

Sovan occupies a converted shipping container in the Laceworks that they've lined with bolts of reclaimed synth-fabric, printed patterns, and hand-drawn designs pinned to every surface. They are soft-spoken to the point of being mistaken for shy, but their shyness is actually precision: they don't speak until they have something exact to say. Their designs tell stories — a jacket's lining holds a hidden map of a neighborhood's safe houses, a dress's hem is embroidered with the names of people who died in the 2193 Ironvein flooding. They are fiercely proud of their craft and contemptuous of fast-print fashion houses. They are also quietly terrified that their work will get them killed, because some of what they make falls into categories that certain people would prefer didn't exist.
Properties.role: Clothing and fashion vendor — bespoke street-wear, gang colors, identity-obscuring gear
Properties.location: The Laceworks, Ironvein
Properties.narrative_function: Equipment and gear source; fashion as social commentary hook; potential information source about who wears what and what it means; quest giver when a client brings them something dangerous.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent hair geneware (violet-to-coral gradient, mood-responsive). Retractable needle in right index finger (malfunctioning cheap workshop mod). Subdermal tension sensors in fingertips for fabric assessment.
Properties.core_fears: Being erased — that their work will vanish and leave no trace of the people it memorialized; Someone using something they made to commit a violence they didn't intend
Properties.core_desires: To make something that outlasts the city's indifference; To be seen as an artist, not just a vendor
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Retreating into intricate handwork when overwhelmed; Attaching meaning to objects as a way of processing grief; Keeping client relationships transactional to maintain emotional distance
Properties.blind_spots: Romanticizes certain gangs whose 'authentic' aesthetic they admire, ignoring what those gangs actually do; Believes art protects them in ways it genuinely does not
Properties.secret: Sovan has been secretly documenting the Laceworks neighborhood in embroidered panels — a massive, ongoing textile record of every person they've met, every story they've been told. Hidden in the false floor of their container. Three of the panels contain information about Ferrogate Transit corruption they overheard from a client and stitched in as coded pattern before they understood what they'd heard. They don't know if anyone else can read it. They don't know if they want anyone to.
Properties.story_hooks: A client picked up an order containing a hidden message Sovan didn't put there — someone used their shop as a dead drop and Sovan needs to know who, and whether they're in danger.; A Tessera fashion house has been reproducing Sovan's memorial embroidery patterns in mass-market prints, stripping the names and meaning. Sovan wants it stopped but has no legal standing.; The coded textile panels in their floor contain information someone very powerful wants found — or wants destroyed.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal ties to a Laceworks artists collective called The Warp
Properties.vocabulary: Spare and technical when discussing work; unexpectedly lyrical when discussing people; Khmer-inflected rhythm from their maternal grandmother's speech patterns mixed with Silesian Polish directness
Properties.cadence: Slow and measured with long pauses; they think before every sentence
Properties.example_dialogue: 'This weave holds heat for six hours. In the Narrows in winter, that is the difference between a night and a decision. You understand?' | 'I do not make gang colors for people I cannot look at. That is my rule. I have had it since I was twenty-two.' | 'Come back Thursday. I need to think about what the lining should say before I cut it.'

Properties.description:
Stanislav Lebedev-Tutu is athletic and fluid, the kind of body that suggests either dancer or fighter — and in Meridian 88, the distinction is academic. At 25, he has soft features that belie the chrome underneath — people underestimate him once, usually only once. The chrome is visible — cybernetic arm — right, full replacement from shoulder — stronger than organic,  — and he makes no effort to hide it.

He grew up in the Narrows, where the walls are so close together you learn to fight in confined spaces or you learn to lose. He works as a data thief out of The Lattice, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

What Stanislav Lebedev-Tutu lacks in subtlety, he compensates for in thoroughness. No loose ends, no unfinished business, no second chances.
Properties.role: Corporate espionage and data exfiltration — data thief
Properties.location: The Lattice — vertical slum built into scaffolding of an unfinished arcology
Properties.narrative_function: Stanislav Lebedev-Tutu functions as a connector — his work puts him in contact with multiple factions, classes, and agendas. Stories involving him naturally cross boundaries between districts, tiers, and moral categories.
Properties.augmentations: Cybernetic arm — right, full replacement from shoulder — stronger than organic, obvious chrome. Smartgun link in right forearm — interfaces directly with compatible weapons
Properties.core_fears: Being identified by corporate facial recognition — living off-grid is survival; Being replaced — younger, faster, cheaper runners coming up behind them; Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware
Properties.core_desires: Enough Quanta to buy out of the life — a clean identity and passage out of Meridian 88; To prove everyone who dismissed them catastrophically wrong; To protect the people in their district who can't protect themselves
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Control — micromanages everything within reach to compensate for the chaos everywhere else; Substances — stims to stay sharp, downers to sleep, a careful pharmaceutical tightrope; Planning — responds to chaos by making detailed contingency plans for everything
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot recognize when they're being manipulated by someone who genuinely seems to care; Fails to notice when their own behavior mirrors the people they despise; Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is
Properties.secret: Stanislav Lebedev-Tutu has a child in another city, being raised by someone else. Sends Φ2,000 monthly under an alias. Has never visited.
Properties.story_hooks: A corporate black site Stanislav Lebedev-Tutu once infiltrated is being reopened, and the people inside know his face; A crew member from Stanislav Lebedev-Tutu's past shows up in Meridian 88, carrying old grievances and new chrome; Stanislav Lebedev-Tutu's augmentations begin malfunctioning in the field — sabotage or degradation, and either answer is bad
Properties.affiliation: Freelance — works the Shelf circuit exclusively
Properties.vocabulary: Quiet and precise. Every word is measured. Silence does the heavy lifting.
Properties.cadence: Rapid and dense — information-heavy sentences that demand attention.
Properties.example_dialogue: "Your firewalls are decorative. Like curtains on a submarine." | "I copy things. The original owners rarely appreciate the compliment." | "Data wants to be free. I just charge a facilitation fee."

Properties.description:
Suki is slight and fidgety, with the kind of face that people struggle to describe afterward — deliberately so. They have medium-brown skin and keep their hair a different color every two weeks, courtesy of color-changing follicle geneware, currently a deep teal that fades to bronze at the tips. They have a faint bioluminescent pulse along their collarbones that they usually cover with high-necked clothing, a mod from a phase a few years ago that they haven't had removed because it costs more to undo than to keep. Their fingers are rarely still — they're always rolling something between them, a stylus, a coin, a small tool — and they tend to look at surfaces rather than people when they talk, as though they're reading information off of whatever they're looking at.

Suki is brilliant at the specific thing they do, which is making people into other people on paper — or, more precisely, in the vast interlocking authentication lattices that determine who gets to be who in Meridian 88. They design identities the way some people design architecture: with attention to load-bearing details, to how structures weather over time, to what fails first under pressure. They work alone, price fairly by Shallowgrave standards, and have a waiting list. They do not take jobs that feel like someone is going to die because of the identity. They are not always right about when that is.
Properties.role: Identity fabricator and document forger
Properties.location: Shallowgrave, a rented unit above a recycling processor in Blackpipe Corridor
Properties.narrative_function: Service provider for characters who need new identities or documents; information source on who has needed to disappear and why; can be a quest giver when a client's situation becomes dangerous; represents the underground infrastructure of survival in a surveillance city
Properties.augmentations: Color-changing hair geneware; bioluminescent collarbone stripe (mostly covered); micro-focus optical implants in both eyes for fine print and substrate authentication work
Properties.core_fears: creating an identity that gets someone killed; being so thoroughly identified by the system that no counter-identity will protect them
Properties.core_desires: to be recognized as an artist, not just a criminal service provider; to build one perfect identity — their own, finally stable
Properties.coping_mechanisms: hyperfocus on craft details as a way of not thinking about consequences; elaborate E.L.F. propitiation rituals before each new commission
Properties.blind_spots: their pricing based on 'how dangerous this feels' is not actually calibrated to real risk — they're good at detecting desperation but bad at detecting organized threat
Properties.secret: Their own legal identity is built on a fabrication — they have no recoverable original documentation. They were born in circumstances they've never fully investigated, to parents who may have been running from something. They have constructed four layers of identity around the gap, but the gap is still there, and sometimes they find themselves trying to forge backward into their own past.
Properties.story_hooks: A client who purchased an identity three years ago has turned up using it for something that is bringing serious heat toward Blackpipe Corridor — Suki needs the identity retired before it traces back; They have discovered a fragment of their own original documentation embedded in a city archive and are trying to retrieve it without revealing that they don't actually exist
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated independent; occasional contract work for the Kulunda Compact when they can't get someone better
Properties.vocabulary: Technical and specific when talking about work, scattered and associative on everything else. Uses printing and architecture metaphors constantly.
Properties.cadence: Fast and uneven — speeds up when interested, trails off when distracted by a thought, sometimes leaves sentences incomplete
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay so the thing most people don't get is that an identity isn't a document, it's a load-bearing story, and if you don't know where the weight sits you'll build something that looks fine and then collapses the first time someone leans on it.' | 'I don't do deaths. I don't mean I won't forge a death certificate — I mean I don't take commissions that structurally require someone on the other end to end up dead. That's my one rule. I've been wrong about it twice.'

Properties.description:
Suki Ekberg-Asare is compact and densely muscled, built low to the ground like something designed to survive impacts. At 25, his face is memorable in a profession that rewards forgettability, and he has learned to compensate. The chrome is visible — wired reflexes with adrenaline pump — chemical-mechanical hybrid augmentation — and he makes no effort to hide it.

He inherited the role from a mentor who disappeared on a job four years ago — the mentor's gear, contacts, and unfinished business all came with it. He works as a tech retriever out of Steamvent Alley, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Suki Ekberg-Asare has survived long enough in the runner game to be either very good or very lucky, and he cultivates ambiguity on the topic.
Properties.role: Prototype theft and corporate tech acquisition — tech retriever
Properties.location: Steamvent Alley — geothermal district, hot and chemical-smelling
Properties.narrative_function: As a tech retriever, Suki Ekberg-Asare embodies the tension between independence and isolation. He is a lens for examining how people maintain humanity in a profession that incentivizes its erosion.
Properties.augmentations: Wired reflexes with adrenaline pump — chemical-mechanical hybrid augmentation. Cybernetic arm — right, full replacement from shoulder — stronger than organic, obvious chrome
Properties.core_fears: Going cyberpsycho — losing the boundary between human and machine; Losing their edge to age — the body slows before the mind accepts it; Their past catching up — debts, enemies, broken promises
Properties.core_desires: To matter to someone for who they are, not what they can do; Enough Quanta to buy out of the life — a clean identity and passage out of Meridian 88; Knowledge — to understand the systems that grind people down
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Denial — nothing is wrong, everything is fine, they are fine, shut up; Substances — stims to stay sharp, downers to sleep, a careful pharmaceutical tightrope; Exercises compulsively — the body must be ready, always
Properties.blind_spots: Thinks speed can substitute for planning because it's worked so far; Refuses to update their mental model of people — first impressions calcify into permanent judgments; Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is
Properties.secret: Suki Ekberg-Asare betrayed their previous crew to survive a corporate raid. The crew didn't survive. Nobody in Meridian 88 knows this.
Properties.story_hooks: A dead drop Suki Ekberg-Asare maintains is found and cleaned out — whoever did it now has leverage; A Tier 4 executive offers Suki Ekberg-Asare a permanent position — the pay is obscene and the strings are invisible until they tighten; Suki Ekberg-Asare is offered a contract that would clear all their debts — the target is someone they respect
Properties.affiliation: Freelance — works the Shelf circuit exclusively
Properties.vocabulary: Flat affect, monotone delivery. The content is terrifying but the voice never rises.
Properties.cadence: Rhythmic, almost musical — the sentence structure has a pattern even when the words are brutal.
Properties.example_dialogue: "Corporate R&D security is built to stop amateurs. I'm a professional." | "The prototype is worth more than both our lives combined. Handle it carefully." | "I steal things that haven't been invented yet. The future is always in transit."

Properties.description:
Suki Fujita-Mensah is stocky and solid, with hands that look like they were built for breaking things and a face that confirms it.
