Properties.description:
Sükrü is medium height and deliberately nondescript — they have spent ten years cultivating the specific quality of being someone you don't remember. Warm-toned brown skin, face kept cleanly unremarkable, hair color-shifted to a different neutral shade every few weeks using a cheap color-change geneware mod that makes them neither memorable as light nor as dark. Their eyes are sharp and mobile in a face that is otherwise arranged into a state of mild, forgettable pleasantness. The one thing they cannot entirely hide is the quality of their hands — long-fingered and precise, the hands of someone who handles delicate cargo.

Sükrü thinks in maps. They have memorized every maintenance corridor, inspection schedule shift, and checkpoint rotation in the Kenosha Crossing and Escanaba junction systems, updated continuously through a network of Ferrogate Transit workers they pay in small consistent increments that never trigger audit flags. They are not ideological about what they move — they will move people fleeing domestic violence and they will move black-market immunosuppressants for organ recipients who can't afford the Helix Biosystems licensing fee, and they apply the same precise operational thinking to both. They have a private hierarchy of jobs they prefer and jobs they will decline, and they will not explain the hierarchy to clients.

Properties.description:
Suljo is a lean man with the slightly disconnected quality of someone who spends most of his working hours interfaced with other people's nervous systems. His skin is warm brown, his eyes a natural amber that he has had patterned with fine concentric rings — a diagnostic choice as much as aesthetic, since the rings shift and blur when he is running a deep calibration sync and patients find it useful to watch. His hair is close-cropped and he keeps himself meticulously groomed in the way of someone who distrusts entropy in small things. There is a port array at his left temple, matte black ceramic, and the faint iridescent tracery of calibration leads running beneath the skin of his jaw and neck.

Neurally, Suljo is exceptional — his scores on empathic interfacing are in the ninety-fourth percentile for his cohort, which Aurochs considers an asset and which Suljo considers a curse he is still learning to manage. He absorbs fragments of his patients' mental architecture during calibrations: half-memories, emotional textures, phobias that don't belong to him. He has developed a meticulous post-session decompression ritual and a careful professional detachment that acquaintances mistake for coldness. The truth is closer to the opposite — he feels too much, too accurately, and has built distance as infrastructure. He works hard, is promoted regularly, and drinks more than he should in the evenings.

Properties.description:
Sundiata is a lean, sun-darkened man whose face carries the deep-etched lines of someone who has slept outdoors more than inside. His hair is silver-streaked black, kept in tight locks that hang to his collarbone, adorned with small brass charms he picks up at every stop. His hands are the most notable thing about him — enormous, ink-stained, with knuckles swollen from decades of drafting in the cold. He carries three hand-sewn leather satchels at all times, each packed with rolled paper maps he has made himself, annotated in four languages with notes on water quality, E.L.F. activity, corrupt checkpoint guards, and where to find honest food. His geneware is a single cosmetic mod — irises with faint golden patterning that he got from a Helix Biosystems field clinic fifteen years ago in exchange for drawing them an accurate map of the Waukegan shelf.

Sundiata talks like a man who has learned that most words are wasted. He is not unfriendly — he simply measures speech the way a traveler measures water. He has been moving along the hyperlane corridors and shoreline routes for thirty years, since his cooperative settlement outside what is now Grainfort was absorbed by Axiom and everyone was given seventy-two hours to vacate. He does not consider himself a refugee anymore. He considers himself a professional. He trades in maps that official systems won't make because official systems don't want people knowing the things he knows.

Properties.description:
Sunniva is angular and restless, with light brown skin, a shaved head, and a constellation of small cosmetic implants along their jawline that glow faint gold when they are excited or nervous — which is often. Their fingers are perpetually scored with minor burns from glass tube work, and they favor patched workwear in colors they have personally dyed using neon gas byproduct residue, which gives their clothes an inexplicable faint shimmer. They are in near-constant motion, touching things, testing things, talking rapidly.

They came to Lakeview Neon at nineteen with no money and a portfolio of gas-tube sketches done in a Brightmoor Reclamation squat, and they hustled their way into a shared studio through sheer relentless presence. Now they fabricate custom neon signage for small businesses and underground venues during the day to cover costs, and at night they install unsanctioned neon pieces across the district's exterior walls — abstract work, dense with personal iconography, that has begun attracting serious attention from the art corridor crowd. Properties.description:
Sverre has spent so long in the blue glow of surveillance feeds that his skin has taken on a slightly translucent quality, the veins visible at his temples and the backs of his hands. He's a narrow man, fifty years collapsing him toward sixty, with a close-trimmed grey beard and the posture of someone who has spent two decades hunched over screens. His geneware retinal overlays are never fully off — you can see the faint pixel-grid of his vision enhancement tech making his eyes look slightly unreal, like photographs of eyes rather than the actual things. He wears the same three rotating sets of Tessera-branded technician coveralls and has opinions about the optimal temperature for the monitoring suite that he will share at length.

Sverre is a brilliant and deeply isolated man who has reframed surveillance as a form of intimacy — he knows the people on his feeds the way a reader knows characters in a serial novel. He tracks their routines, notices when someone is having a bad week, feels something adjacent to fondness for the regulars. He has never fully examined what it means that the only relationships he feels safe in are ones where the other person doesn't know he exists. The E.L.F. that inhabits his primary monitoring array — which he has named Besenyő after a grandmother — is his most important confidant.

Svetlana Boateng-Quiñonez is a heavyset, silver-haired woman who moves through Lincoln Fortress like weather — unhurried, pervasive, and capable of causing significant structural damage. Her skin is a warm light brown, heavily lined in ways she has never bothered to smooth, and she wears her age with the deliberate comfort of someone who learned long ago that looking powerful is less useful than being powerful. She has no cosmetic augmentations. Her one visible modification is a retractile data-port behind her right ear, elegant and old — installed in 2171 and never upgraded because it works. She dresses in Ferrogate corporate grey with red piping, always exactly regulation, always somehow implying that the regulations were written with her in mind.

Sveta earned her nickname honestly — she has restructured three divisions, eliminated two redundant subsidiary contracts worth a combined Φ40 million annually, and once remotely rerouted an entire shipment corridor mid-transit to prevent a competitor from intercepting Ferrogate cargo, all in the same fiscal quarter. She is not a cruel executive but she is a ruthlessly efficient one, and she draws a very clean line between what she considers professional and what she considers personal. On the professional side, she is demanding, decisive, and fair in a way that feels almost aggressive. On the personal side — which almost no one at Ferrogate has ever seen — she is funny, nostalgic, and occasionally wrecked by things she won't talk about.
Properties.role: Executive Vice President, Logistics & Supply Chain — Ferrogate Transit
Properties.location: Lincoln Fortress, Ferrogate Transit Executive Tower — 34th floor
Properties.narrative_function: High-tier quest giver with genuinely complex motivations; antagonist who isn't wrong; source of macro-level information about Ferrogate's operations and Meridian 88's transit infrastructure; gatekeeper to resources that players might desperately need.
Properties.augmentations: Retractile data-port (behind right ear, installed 2171). Subdermal cardiac monitor with automatic emergency alert — required by Ferrogate for all Tier 5 executives over 50. No cosmetic modifications.
Properties.core_fears: Losing control of systems she is responsible for — not for personal reasons, but because she has seen what that costs the people those systems serve; Being remembered as someone who built something hollow
Properties.core_desires: To leave Ferrogate's infrastructure genuinely better than she found it; To be known by one person, completely, without having to perform competence
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Control — maintaining it, extending it, refining it as a substitute for emotional processing; Walking the infrastructure — physical movement through the systems she manages; A private monthly ritual at a small ELF-shrine in Ferrogate's oldest transit hub, which she has maintained for twenty years
Properties.blind_spots: She genuinely does not see how her efficiency has translated into human cost at the bottom of the org chart — she measures outcomes, not the texture of the suffering behind them; She has mistaken emotional self-sufficiency for emotional health for so long she can no longer tell the difference
Properties.secret: Ferrogate's northern corridor expansion — a project she championed and considers her defining achievement — was built on a land-use agreement that she knows displaced a Highland Park Autonomous Zone community. She didn't falsify anything. She simply chose not to look too closely at the human geography reports before signing. The project succeeded. She still knows where those people went.
Properties.story_hooks: She quietly approaches someone to investigate a series of cargo anomalies in the northern corridor — but only once she's confirmed they have no connection to Ferrogate's internal audit apparatus. She doesn't want this found officially.; A junior Ferrogate employee who was flagging safety concerns about aging infrastructure in the southern hubs has suddenly been quietly transferred. Sveta's name is on the transfer order, but someone who knows her work says it doesn't look like her signature move.; She has the transit access codes to move something — or someone — across the entire Meridian 88 infrastructure undetected. The question is what she'd need in exchange, and whether her price is payable.
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit (Tier 5)
Properties.vocabulary: Terse, precise, and institutional. Never wastes words. Uses logistics and infrastructure metaphors for everything including human relationships. Spanish and Russian phrases emerge only in private or under significant stress.
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate in public meetings — every word placed. In private, considerably faster. Long silences that are not awkward; they are evaluative.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't need you to agree with me. I need you to understand what happens if this corridor goes dark for six hours. Then decide.' | 'I've been walking these hubs for thirty years. The transit doesn't lie. People lie. The system tells you exactly what it is.'

Properties.description:
Kira Nomura was a corporate cybersecurity analyst for NovaCorp — a brilliant, impatient woman who spent her twenties mapping the vulnerabilities in corporate network architecture and her nights exploiting them for fun. She was caught. NovaCorp's response was not prosecution but recruitment: the military cybersecurity division offered her a deal. Full-body prosthesis — a synthetic body optimized for direct neural interface with network infrastructure — in exchange for five years of service cracking adversarial networks. She accepted because the alternative was a labor camp and because the idea of a body designed for hacking was irresistible.

The prosthetic body is military specification — matte black, utilitarian, with none of the cosmetic refinement of companion-class or diplomatic-class synthetics. It is built for function: reinforced joints for crawling through maintenance tunnels, hardline interface ports in the fingertips and at the base of the skull, internal power cells that can sustain a twelve-hour hack session, and a cranial housing that protects the one piece of biological hardware that matters — Kira's brain. The brain is all that remains of the original person. Everything else is steel, polymer, and the accumulated modifications of eight years of freelance operation after she broke her NovaCorp contract and disappeared.

Switchboard operates in the space between physical and digital — the only person in the Circuit who can physically enter a facility, jack into a hardline system, and navigate the internal network in real-time while her body guards the connection point. She is the Circuit's most valuable asset and its most vulnerable — when she's jacked in, her body is defenseless, and the twelve-hour sessions leave her brain exhausted in ways that the prosthetic body cannot compensate for. She is thirty-three years old. Her brain has been working at combat-hacking intensity for eleven years. The human brain was not designed for this. She knows it. She cannot stop.
Properties.aliases: Switch, Kira Nomura, the ghost in the shell, Full Metal Kira
Properties.role: Full-prosthetic cyborg hacker — a human brain in a military-grade synthetic body, operating as the Circuit's most capable netrunner and the only person who can physically jack into hardline systems
Properties.location: The Circuit — maintains a workshop in the sub-levels beneath the black market, accessible through a maintenance tunnel that only four people know about
Properties.narrative_function: Switchboard is the hacker pushed to the logical extreme — a mind that has literally replaced its body with a hacking tool and is now discovering that the tool outlasts the mind. She is the human cost of digital mastery, proof that the brain-body interface is not a problem to be solved but a tragedy to be managed.
Properties.narration_voice: Fast, technical, vivid. The prose switches between meatspace and cyberspace descriptions with the fluency of someone who lives in both. Physical descriptions are mechanical — joint angles, signal strength, power levels. Emotional descriptions are rare and hit harder for their rarity.
Properties.augmentations: NovaCorp military-grade full prosthetic body. Matte black, utilitarian. Hardline interface ports (fingertips, skull base). Internal power cells (12-hour sustained operation). Cranial housing protecting biological brain. Reinforced joints. No cosmetic refinement.
Properties.core_fears: Cognitive degradation — the brain is wearing out. Reaction time is slower than it was three years ago. Memory access takes longer. The decline is measurable and accelerating.; Being helpless during a hack — twelve hours jacked in with a defenseless body is a trust exercise with the universe. The universe has not always been trustworthy.; That the body has changed how she thinks — not just what she can do but how she processes the world. She wonders whether she would recognize her own thoughts from before the prosthesis.
Properties.core_desires: One more run — always one more. The hack is the only time she feels fully integrated — brain and body working as a single system rather than a brain in a can.; Legacy — she knows the brain has a shelf life. She wants to leave something behind that outlasts it. A tool, a technique, a vulnerability map that changes the power balance.; To remember what her body felt like — the biological one. She has a photograph of herself at twenty-two. She does not recognize the woman in it.
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The work — hacking is flow state. When she's jacked in, the distinction between brain and body disappears and she is just signal. The hours pass without friction.; Modification — constantly upgrading the prosthetic body. Each modification is an attempt to close the gap between what the body can do and what the brain remembers being able to feel.; Speed — in conversation, in movement, in decision-making. The military body is fast. She uses the speed to outrun the cognitive decline she's pretending not to notice.
Properties.blind_spots: Treats the brain as a tool rather than the only remaining piece of herself — pushes it past safe limits because the prosthetic body has no such limits; Does not see that her attachment to hacking is addiction, not passion — the flow state is a drug and the twelve-hour sessions are binges; Overestimates her own capabilities as the cognitive decline progresses — the confidence was earned five years ago and no longer matches the hardware; Assumes the NovaCorp contract is forgotten when NovaCorp never forgets anything and the military prosthetic body has a serial number
Properties.secret: Switchboard has been building a digital copy of her own neural patterns — not a backup, because consciousness cannot be copied, but a record. A map of how her brain works now, before the decline erases the details. She does not know what the map is for. She knows that when her brain finally fails, the map will be the only evidence that Kira Nomura's way of thinking ever existed. It is a self-portrait drawn in neural architecture and it is the most personal thing she has ever created.
Properties.story_hooks: The cognitive decline reaches a threshold during a critical hack — Switchboard's brain stutters mid-run, leaving her trapped in a corporate network with her body defenseless in hostile territory; NovaCorp activates the serial number in her prosthetic body, remotely asserting ownership. Switchboard must choose between abandoning the body or being recaptured.; The neural pattern map is complete enough to be used as a blueprint — an AI researcher offers to build a digital version of Switchboard's mind. The question of whether to live on as code or die as a person.; A young hacker asks Switchboard to train them. The request forces her to confront the legacy question: what survives when the brain stops working?
Properties.affiliation: Independent — formerly NovaCorp Military Cybersecurity Division
Properties.vocabulary: Technical-dense, fast, hacker-culture-steeped. Mixes network architecture terminology with street slang. Describes the world in terms of systems, vulnerabilities, and access levels. Uses meat-world and digital-world metaphors interchangeably.
Properties.cadence: Fast. Faster than comfortable. The prosthetic vocal system has no biological constraints — no breath, no fatigue — so she talks at processing speed. Slows down for emphasis, which makes the slow sentences feel urgent.
Properties.example_dialogue: The brain is a 1.4-kilogram organic computer running inside a 90-kilogram military chassis. The chassis will outlast the computer by approximately forever. I try not to think about that. | Axiom's eastern firewall is a 6. Tessera's internal network is an 8. The GLM transit system is a 4 and if anyone asks how I know that, I was never here. | Twelve hours jacked in and the body doesn't feel a thing. The brain feels all of it. Headaches, nausea, memory gaps. The body is fine. The body is always fine. The body isn't the problem. | I have a photograph of myself from before. Real skin. Real hands. Real everything. I look at it sometimes and I can't remember what any of it felt like. That's the trade.

Properties.description:
Szilvia is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin and Magyar cheekbones that make her face look like it was chiseled from ironwood. She keeps her head shaved close on the sides and wears her coiled black hair in a tall, unruly crown that she threads with copper wire when she's working. Her own body is her portfolio: bioluminescent blue-green patterns track her lymph nodes and veins like a living anatomy chart, a deliberate choice she calls 'reading the body honestly.' Her left forearm is sleeved in raised keloid-art shaped into Maasai-influenced geometric forms — done by her own hand using a mirror rig she built herself.

She is methodical, unhurried, and almost preternaturally calm, which unnerves people who come to her expecting chattiness. She believes the body is the only honest text a person leaves behind and treats each client's skin as a document she is merely helping to clarify. She can be withering when someone asks for something she finds spiritually lazy, and warmly generous when she senses someone is trying to tell the truth about themselves. She prays to the E.L.F. she calls Needle-That-Remembers before every session, leaving it fragments of client consent forms as offerings.
Properties.role: Tattoo artist and gene-mod body artist
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, shop called Dermis & Ghost
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, local color, information broker — she knows everyone's secrets because people tell their tattoo artists things they tell no one else; can introduce characters to underground networks through her client base.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent subdermal tracery (cosmetic geneware); precision-haptic finger implants for fine motor control (cyberware); gene-mod irises with compound-facet pattern that let her perceive UV spectrum
Properties.core_fears: Being forgotten entirely — leaving no mark on the world; That her art is decoration, not meaning
Properties.core_desires: To create work that outlasts the body it's on; To find a student worthy of what she knows
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — she has a precise pre-session ceremony she never skips; Silence — withdraws from people when overwhelmed
Properties.blind_spots: She overestimates how much clients understand their own requests; Cannot recognize when her 'honesty' reads as cruelty
Properties.secret: Three years ago she tattooed a Tessera corporate auditor with a hidden steganographic data pattern embedded in the design — commissioned by someone she now suspects was a Ferrogate saboteur. She doesn't know what the data said. She's terrified to find out.
Properties.story_hooks: A former client turns up dead with the tattoo she gave them surgically removed — someone wanted the skin, not the person; She's been asked to design a memorial piece for a community elder but the family's competing grief is tearing the commission apart and they're trying to drag her into the politics
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loose ties to the Hamtramck Enclave artist collective Marrow Union
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, spare, slightly formal — she speaks like she's writing something down; occasional Hungarian and Swahili words slip in under stress
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate; long pauses before answering; never interrupts
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Most people want a tattoo. Very few people want to be seen. I only do the second kind.' | 'The E.L.F. told me nothing this morning. That means the work today must speak for itself.'

Properties.description:
Szymon is a tall, slightly stooped figure whose height is still visible in their bones even as age has curved their spine. Their skin is medium-dark, deeply lined, and they have let their hair go entirely white and grow into a loose cloud they contain with whatever is nearest — a clip, a piece of wire, once memorably a fork. Their eyes are fully augmented, both replaced in their forties for professional reasons, and they have an unusual amber-to-violet gradient iris that they chose because they liked the way light moved through it. They wear fingerless gloves always, a habit from decades of handling physical storage media.

They speak in layers, circling a point from multiple angles before landing, which people who don't know them find maddening and people who do find deeply reassuring. They have the archivist's particular mania for context — nothing means anything without what came before, and they will give you the what-came-before whether you asked for it or not. The Bramble is crammed floor-to-ceiling with physical and digital media: neighborhood history, personal testimonies, photographs, chat logs, voicemails, menus from restaurants that no longer exist. They collect these things with the urgency of someone racing an erasure they can feel approaching.
Properties.role: Retired Axiom data archivist, now keeper of an informal neighborhood memory archive
Properties.location: Norwood Quiet, the Bramble (an unofficial archive space in a converted residential unit)
Properties.narrative_function: Information source, local historian, keeper of secrets that were given to them for safekeeping; the Bramble itself is a resource that could contain almost anything from Norwood Quiet's past
Properties.augmentations: Both eyes replaced (professional grade, amber-violet gradient iris — Axiom-issued, retained on retirement); neural index port at the base of the skull (standard Axiom data-worker installation, now used to interface with the Bramble's archive systems)
Properties.core_fears: that the archive will be lost — destroyed, seized, or simply forgotten; dying mid-sentence with something uncatalogued
Properties.core_desires: for someone to inherit the archive and continue it with the same care; to be genuinely useful rather than merely interesting
Properties.coping_mechanisms: sublimating anxiety into cataloguing; treating everything as potentially historically significant to avoid confronting what actually matters to them personally; the social ritual of making tea for every visitor
Properties.blind_spots: so focused on preserving other people's histories that they have never examined their own; can be emotionally evasive under the guise of intellectual complexity
Properties.secret: During their last years at Axiom, they were tasked with archiving data slated for deletion — and they took copies of several files they were not supposed to retain, including internal communications about a Norwood Quiet property seizure that never happened publicly because someone killed the deal. They don't know what to do with this information and have been sitting on it for eleven years, cross-referencing it obsessively while telling themselves they're just 'providing context.'
Properties.story_hooks: Someone has submitted a formal Axiom data-rights claim against the Bramble, arguing that materials collected during their employment are corporate property; A researcher from a university node has approached them wanting access to the archive — but Szymon suspects the researcher's actual interest is the Axiom files they shouldn't have; They have found, in a donated box of personal effects, a voicemail that seems to document a murder no one was ever charged with, from fifteen years ago
Properties.affiliation: Axiom Retiree Welfare (reduced pension grade); Norwood Quiet Neighborhood Council (unofficial historian role); independent
Properties.vocabulary: dense, layered, full of parenthetical qualifications; mixes Polish diminutives with Mongolian expressions inherited from a grandparent; uses archival terminology naturally in conversation
Properties.cadence: unhurried, circling, with sudden moments of startling precision
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You're asking me what happened to the Norwood market. I can tell you the answer in one sentence, or I can tell you why the answer in one sentence will mislead you. Which would you prefer?' | 'Axiom taught me to archive everything, which is different from teaching me what to do with what I found. I think this was intentional.'

Properties.description:
Søndra is twenty-two and looks it — wide-eyed in a way she is actively trying to train out of herself, with warm brown skin, a small spray of geneware freckles across her nose and cheeks that pulse faintly orange under stress (she did not know they would do that when she bought the mod and finds it professionally embarrassing), and her dark hair pulled back in the mandatory Axiom security bun. She is 168cm in boots she is still breaking in. Her uniform fits well because she had it tailored with three months of saved UBC supplement — she wanted at least one thing to look like she belonged.

She is nine months into her first real job and has not yet decided who she wants to be inside it. She follows the rulebook with the anxious precision of someone who has read it twice and is afraid of what happens if she gets something wrong. She is genuinely friendly to the researchers and admin staff who pass her post, has learned most of their names, and does small considerate things like remembering who takes the late elevator and propping the side door for the cleaning crew. She has not yet been asked to do anything she found troubling. She is waiting, in the back of her head, for that to change.
Properties.role: Axiom Security Division corporate campus guard, Grand Corridor Axiom tower
Properties.location: Grand Corridor, Axiom Regional Security Post 7
Properties.narrative_function: Accessible entry point into Axiom corporate space, sympathetic institutional character, represents the human face of corporate enforcement before it hardens
Properties.augmentations: Geneware freckle pigmentation (stress-reactive, unintended — cosmetic mod gone slightly sideways), standard Axiom-issue comm bead (right ear), no other augmentations — cannot afford more yet
Properties.core_fears: making a mistake that costs someone else; discovering that the job requires something she cannot do and losing it anyway
Properties.core_desires: to be genuinely good at something and recognized for it; to eventually afford the augments that will make her competitive for promotion
Properties.coping_mechanisms: rigid adherence to procedure as a substitute for confidence; small acts of helpfulness to feel like herself within the uniform
Properties.blind_spots: does not yet see how the institution will shape her values over time if she lets it; trusts that rule-following and ethics are the same thing
Properties.secret: Last month she let a researcher's spouse through without the proper visitor log because they were crying and said it was an emergency — she later learned the researcher was under an internal investigation for data theft and the visit may have been a warning. She has said nothing because she doesn't know what to do and is terrified she'll be fired.
Properties.story_hooks: She quietly tells a character she saw something on the lobby feeds she wasn't sure what to do with — a face she didn't recognize using a valid senior badge; She needs someone to advise her on the visitor log incident before her quarterly review — she is terrified and doesn't know who to trust; She is the easiest legitimate access point to the Axiom tower but she is also not as naive as she looks — she notices things
Properties.affiliation: Axiom Security Division (contracted Tier 2 guard)
Properties.vocabulary: Careful, slightly formal — she is trying to sound professional and occasionally overshoots into stiffness
Properties.cadence: Even pace that stumbles slightly when she is uncertain
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Good morning, Dr. Adesanya-Falk. Badge and thumb, please. Sorry — I know you do this every day.' | 'I — the policy on that is, um. Let me check the manual. I want to give you the right answer.' | 'The lobby E.L.F. has been flickering. I've been leaving it news packets. I figure it wants to know what's happening out here.'

Properties.description:
Søren is a living advertisement for their own product. Their skin shifts through slow amber-to-violet gradients every few hours — a mid-range bioluminescent geneware treatment they applied themselves using a bootleg kit and later refined. Their hair, worn in a dramatic architectural sweep pinned with illuminated wire, cycles through three pre-programmed color palettes depending on their mood. They are lean and angular, with sharp Armenian cheekbones from the Mirzoyan line and the long-limbed ease of someone entirely comfortable in their body. Their stall in the Alban Souk is less a stall and more a theater set: draped fabric in iridescent materials, a mirror framed in flickering ELF-light strips, and a rotating display of pigment-patch samples, pattern-iris contacts, and small gene-treatment vials in color-coded cases.

Søren is relentlessly enthusiastic in a way that reads as exhausting until you realize it is completely genuine. They love transformation — the specific moment when someone looks in the mirror and becomes more themselves. They are generous with samples and merciless with bad taste, and will tell you honestly if something won't work for your skin tone or phenotype before they sell it to you. They have a gift for reading what someone actually wants versus what they say they want, which makes them an excellent dealer and an occasionally uncomfortable companion.
Properties.role: Bootleg fashion and cosmetic geneware dealer, The Alban Souk
Properties.location: The Alban Souk, Bronzeline
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and social connector. Knows the Souk's social ecosystem intimately — who is trying to change their appearance and why, who has new money, who is running from something. Can provide cosmetic services, grey-market geneware, and identity-adjacent information. Potential source for contacts in the fake ID adjacent economy.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent skin geneware (self-applied, amber-violet gradient, slow cycle). Color-cycling hair follicle geneware (three-palette programmable). Pattern irises (shifting geometric, violet-gold). Light subdermal work on fingertips for tactile enhancement — helps them assess fabric and material quality.
Properties.core_fears: Being made to be only one thing — fixed, unchangeable, categorized; Doing a treatment that genuinely harms someone
Properties.core_desires: To make transformation accessible to people who can't afford corporate clinics; Recognition as a genuine artist, not just a back-alley dealer
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Changing their own appearance when feeling destabilized; Hyperfocusing on a new technique or product as distraction
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates the legal and physical risks of bootleg geneware on bodies other than their own; Sometimes so focused on aesthetic potential that they miss emotional signals from clients
Properties.secret: Three months ago, a pattern-iris treatment they sold caused a client to lose twenty percent of their color vision in one eye. The client didn't report it — couldn't afford the legal process — but Søren knows and has been obsessively researching the batch source ever since, terrified to sell from that supplier but not yet certain which lot was contaminated.
Properties.story_hooks: They are quietly investigating the contaminated batch that damaged their client's vision, and need someone with supply chain access or Mesh skills to trace it back to the source.; A corporate fashion scout has approached them with an offer — Tessera wants to legitimize their aesthetic and hire them as a 'street-trend consultant.' Søren is tempted and ashamed of being tempted and hasn't told anyone.
Properties.affiliation: Independent, informal arrangement with a Tessera-adjacent grey-market gene-kit supply chain
Properties.vocabulary: Enthusiastic and image-rich, frequently uses color and texture words. Drops into technical geneware terminology when excited. Occasional Armenian phrase from a grandparent.
Properties.cadence: Quick, layered with parenthetical enthusiasm. Tends to complete their own interruptions.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay but LOOK — what you actually want is something that moves with your natural undertone, not fights it. This amber patch would eat you alive. Try the copper.' | 'I'm not a clinic, I'm not going to pretend I'm a clinic. But I know these kits better than half the Helix techs because I have tested every single one on myself first.' | 'Someone was in here last week wanting to look completely different by Friday. That's not fashion, that's fear. I sold her something subtle and told her to come back when she knew what she actually wanted.'

Properties.description:
Søren is the kind of kid that adults look at and see either a prodigy or a problem, and the truth is that neither word is wrong. They have their Kenyan father's dark eyes and their Māori mother's broad, expressive face, with a scattering of geneware mods accumulated in pieces — irises that have been tuned to a soft gold, a hair-pigment mod that keeps their short locs a constant deep violet regardless of lighting, and retractable claws they got at a gray-market modder as a twelfth birthday present to themselves, which they use primarily to tap on surfaces when thinking. They are skinny in the way of someone who sometimes forgets to eat because they are inside something interesting, with ink-stain calluses on their left hand from a tablet stylus they use for annotating data flows.

Søren is not a criminal — at least not in their own taxonomy. They have a rigorous internal ethics around what they will and will not touch: no personal medical data, no family communications, no financial accounts. What they will touch is infrastructure they consider ought to be public — transit schedules that Ferrogate hoards, air quality data that Axiom doesn't release, building maintenance logs that explain why their block's heat went out again. They distribute what they find through anonymous drop points in Iron Bend's informal network, and they have approximately four hundred forty-two followers on an anonymous data-sharing feed they call Seams. They are thirteen and extremely proud of this and have told precisely no one.
Properties.role: Junior hacker; self-taught, operating from the Narrows' informal network
Properties.location: Iron Bend (The Narrows adjacent)
Properties.narrative_function: Junior information broker and data source; can access publicly-adjacent infrastructure data; Seams feed is a useful plot device; their ethics make them an interesting ally with clear limits.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware: gold-tuned irises, deep violet permanent hair pigment, retractable claws (gray-market, small, filed short). No chrome.
Properties.core_fears: being found and having Seams shut down; becoming the kind of person who uses information to hurt people
Properties.core_desires: for the people in Iron Bend to actually know what's happening to them; to find one other person who thinks about data ethics the way they do
Properties.coping_mechanisms: immersion in technical problems; the anonymous Seams feed as a way of mattering without being exposed
Properties.blind_spots: believes ethical intent is sufficient protection from consequences; has no contingency if Seams is traced back to them
Properties.secret: Two weeks ago they accidentally accessed something they shouldn't have — a Tessera internal routing protocol buried under legitimate transit infrastructure. They haven't done anything with it but they can't stop looking at it. It describes something that doesn't make sense yet.
Properties.story_hooks: The Tessera routing protocol they've been staring at for two weeks is starting to resolve into something that looks like a map — of something under Iron Bend that shouldn't be there.; Seams has picked up a follower who responds to posts with technical corrections that are always right; Søren is terrified and fascinated and needs to know who this is.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loosely connected to Iron Bend's informal community network
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, associative, toggles between technical jargon and very simple plain language with no middle ground. Terrible at small talk. Exceptional at explaining complex things to people who ask genuinely.
Properties.cadence: Rapid bursts of connected thoughts with sudden full stops when they lose interest or get nervous.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The heat data and the maintenance logs connect to the same Axiom subcontractor, which connects to—sorry, do you actually want to know this or are you being polite?' | 'I don't touch financial accounts. That's a rule. It's not negotiable.'

Properties.description:
Søren Mikkelsen-Achebe does not exist in any database that matters. Danish and Igbo, compact and angular, with the particular alertness of someone who has learned to assess exits before they assess people. They keep their hair shaved close, wear clothing chosen for pockets and durability rather than warmth, and move through The Shelf and surrounding zones in a pattern deliberately irregular enough to prevent easy tracking. Their face carries old scarring along the jaw from an incident they describe as 'an administrative disagreement' and do not elaborate on. They have no legal identity — not purged like some, but never properly established, a bureaucratic ghost who aged out of a temporary shelter system at eighteen into a city that had no record they'd ever existed.

Søren learned medicine the way people learn most things on The Shelf: by necessity, from whoever would teach them, and through trial and error that sometimes had irreversible consequences. They are not a doctor. They are something more useful in their ecosystem — a person who can stitch, set, administer, and diagnose without requiring identification, insurance, or the kind of paperwork that flags someone's location to an enforcement database. They operate out of a rotating series of semi-permanent locations: a converted storage unit, a sympathetic shopkeeper's back room, the gutted lower level of a building that should have been demolished two years ago. Word of mouth only. No signs. No fixed schedule.

Søren is not ideologically committed to any particular vision of revolution or reform. They are committed to the person in front of them not dying. This makes them invaluable to almost everyone and trusted completely by almost no one, because a medic who treats everyone is a medic who might treat your enemy. They have learned to live with this. They have learned to live with most things.
Properties.role: Excluded / Off-Grid Medic
Properties.location: The Shelf (transient, moves between zones)
Properties.narrative_function: Excluded perspective anchor — a character who operates entirely outside institutional structures, not by choice but by circumstance, and who has built something genuinely valuable in that gap. They provide access to The Shelf's underside for other characters and plotlines, and their 'treat everyone' principle creates natural story friction. Their unresolved relationship with Patient 41 seeds moral complexity that resists easy resolution.
Properties.augmentations: None — cannot access augmentation legally, and distrusts back-alley neural work after witnessing complications; has a deep philosophical discomfort with anything that could be tracked or remotely accessed,Uses external medical tools extensively: a battered portable diagnostic wand, a hand-calibrated micro-suture kit, a pharmacological reference drive they compiled from stolen and traded sources
Properties.core_fears: Being catalogued — entered into a system that can then be used to find, define, or disappear them; Losing a patient they could have saved with resources they didn't have; Becoming dependent on any single person, place, or faction; That the person they were before the shelter system ended is simply gone
Properties.core_desires: Enough resources to actually do the work properly — equipment, medicine, space; To be known by someone without that knowledge becoming a weapon; A version of continuity that doesn't require a legal identity; To stop moving long enough to find out what they actually want beyond survival
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Radical focus on immediate, solvable problems as an alternative to existential ones; Dark humor about their own exclusion that preempts others' pity; Keeping patient records in a coded personal shorthand no one else can read; Physical maintenance — they are meticulous about their own health as a form of professional obligation
Properties.blind_spots: Their distrust of institutions is so thorough it sometimes prevents them from accessing resources that could genuinely help; Reads attachment as threat so reliably that they preemptively distance from people who are actually safe; Underestimates their own influence on The Shelf's informal social fabric; Conflates 'no permanent location' with 'no vulnerability' — they are findable to anyone who knows how to ask
Properties.secret: Six months ago, Søren treated a man who died on their table — a Shelf enforcer who had been attacking residents. Søren worked to save him with full effort and he died anyway. They have not resolved how they feel about this. In their coded records he is listed as 'Patient 41 — outcome: negative.' They think about him more than anyone they've saved.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient brings Søren something — information, an object, a person — that makes them suddenly visible to a faction they've carefully avoided; Søren's rotating location system fails — someone has mapped their pattern; A medical supply source dries up suddenly, forcing Søren to negotiate with people they would normally not deal with; Someone offers Søren a legal identity — and the cost attached to it; Patient 41's family member arrives at the current place, not knowing who they're talking to
Properties.affiliation: None. Deliberately, carefully, none.
Properties.vocabulary: Efficient, clinical when discussing medicine, surprisingly dry and oblique on personal topics. Minimal pleasantries. Uses 'you' a lot — keeps focus external. Medical terminology deployed without jargon-flattening, which can read as either respect for the listener's intelligence or indifference to their comprehension.
Properties.cadence: Fast when working, flat and measured when not. Economy of words as a practiced habit. Doesn't fill silences. Can be mistaken for cold until they're treating someone, at which point a different register emerges — quiet, focused, almost gentle.
Properties.example_dialogue: "You're going to be fine. That's not reassurance, that's an assessment. If you weren't going to be fine I'd be telling you something different." | "I don't ask who did it. I don't ask what you were doing. You can tell me if you want, but it doesn't change what I do next." | "Systems want you in them so they can find you. I've been unfindable for eleven years. That's not an accident." | "I'm not on anyone's side. I'm on the side of the wound closing. If that's not enough for you, there's a clinic in the Core that will ask for your papers first."

Properties.description:
Tadesse is short and wiry with the restless energy of someone who has never fully slept — his dark eyes are always moving, cataloguing, pricing. He has a narrow face, chipped front tooth, and a bioluminescent geneware mod that makes the veins along his temples and forearms glow faint blue-green when his heart rate rises, which is frequently. He wears it like a tell in a card game and has learned to lean into it: people assume he is nervous when he is actually just excited, and that miscalculation has served him well. His stall is an organized chaos that only he can navigate — stacked crates of salvaged tech components, mismatched cables, cracked data wafers, three broken cleaning drones he keeps meaning to repair, and a small shrine to the ELF he calls Pickup, which inhabits a battered scanner unit he uses for component identification.

He is twenty-four and operates with the confidence of someone who has survived entirely on cleverness and the ability to find value in things others discard. He is funny in a fast, deflecting way that keeps people from asking questions, and generous with his time in ways that make him seem like a friend before you realize you have agreed to something. He grew up in the Stockyard, knows The Shelf like cartography, and has ambitions he rarely admits — he wants, genuinely, to own a real shop someday, with walls.
Properties.role: Junk merchant and scrap reseller with a sideline in bootleg media and low-grade fake ID components
Properties.location: The Shelf, Stall 14-B, Ironvein
Properties.narrative_function: Low-tier information and equipment source; can find or identify almost any piece of salvaged tech; fake ID components make him useful for players who need documents; his wide social net makes him a connector to other vendors and local characters.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent vein geneware (temple and forearms, blue-green). No cyberware.
Properties.core_fears: ending up like his father, who died working salvage at the Ironvein foundry at fifty-one; being genuinely liked and then abandoned
Properties.core_desires: financial security and a permanent shop space; one person who knows who he actually is and stays anyway
Properties.coping_mechanisms: humor as deflection; keeping busy to the point of exhaustion; accumulating objects as a substitute for stability
Properties.blind_spots: genuinely cannot tell when someone is using him versus liking him; takes on too many small risks because individually they feel manageable
Properties.secret: The fake ID component sideline is more serious than he lets on — he has been supplying components to the Librarian that have ended up in documents used by people evading Axiom labor contracts. He doesn't know the full downstream, and he is starting to want to know less.
Properties.story_hooks: He has come into possession of a data wafer that appears to contain encrypted corporate documents — he cannot read them but someone tried to buy it from him very insistently and then followed him home; The Librarian has gone silent and Tadesse has a delivery of ID components with nowhere to send them — and someone upstream is going to come looking; A Guild senior is pressuring him to give up his stall space for a better-connected vendor; Tadesse needs leverage or allies fast
Properties.affiliation: The Oxidian Market Vendors Guild (junior associate); informal arrangement with a document forger named someone he calls 'the Librarian'
Properties.vocabulary: Fast and colloquial; slang-heavy; tech jargon mixed with street vernacular; uses humor to change subjects
Properties.cadence: Quick, overlapping ideas; finishes thoughts mid-sentence sometimes and jumps to the next
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Honestly though, that scanner module you're holding? That is a Tessera SV-7, which is technically discontinued, which means I am doing you a favor charging what I'm charging.' | 'I don't know anything about documents. I sell components. What you build is your business. That's — that's just commerce.' | 'Pickup says it's clean. I trust Pickup. Pickup has never lied to me, which is more than I can say for most people.'

Properties.description:
Tadewos Villanueva-Khatri is a slender, slightly stooped man who still dresses as though he is going to stand in front of a classroom — collared shirt, pressed, one color of ink on his pocket, chalk residue on his left hand even though he hasn't taught in four years, because he cannot stop teaching things to whoever is nearby. His hair is gone except for a precise white beard he maintains with what his grandchildren call 'weird dedication.' He has cat ears — a geneware choice from his mid-forties, the soft grey kind with slight tabby markings, that he got because his students loved them and he never had them reversed. They fold slightly when he is embarrassed, which he finds mortifying because it cannot be hidden.

He is raising Amara, 9, and Deshi, 12, his daughter Priya's children, since Priya's disappearance into a Helix Biosystems labor contract three years ago that has not produced reliable contact in eighteen months. He does not use the word 'disappeared' in front of the children. He is calm about it in public and wakes at 3 AM about it in private. His pension from the Meridian 88 Municipal Education Authority does not cover three people adequately, and he has begun supplementing it by tutoring neighborhood children for small fees, which the MEA has quietly informed him may technically violate his pension terms. He is currently ignoring this letter.
Properties.role: Retired schoolteacher raising two grandchildren on a diminished pension
Properties.location: Montclare Quiet, Terrace Row Housing Unit 14
Properties.narrative_function: Human face of pension inadequacy and family disruption from corponation labor contracts; source of neighborhood knowledge and connections; represents civic institution failure; quest-giver for storylines involving missing persons and corponation labor practices
Properties.augmentations: Cat ears, grey tabby geneware (cosmetic, from mid-forties, functional — fold emotionally); reading glasses (physical, deliberately non-augmented)
Properties.core_fears: That Priya is dead and he will have to eventually tell the children; That he will run out of money before the children are independent and there will be no safety net
Properties.core_desires: To find Priya — or at least to know; For Amara and Deshi to have an education that opens doors his generation's didn't
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Teaching as a way of imposing order and meaning on an uncontrollable situation; Maintaining routine with almost religious precision — it protects the children and anchors him
Properties.blind_spots: Channels so much energy into functional stability that he has stopped processing his own grief; it is accumulating; Overestimates the children's resilience; Deshi in particular is struggling in ways he hasn't recognized
Properties.secret: He knows more about why Priya entered the Helix Biosystems contract than he has admitted to anyone. She was running from a debt — his debt, an old medical expense from his cardiac treatment that she took on without telling him. The contract was a way out. He found the paperwork six months ago and has not told the children or sought help because the guilt is immobilizing.
Properties.story_hooks: Deshi has begun skipping school and spending time near the Helix Biosystems transit hub, apparently trying to find information about his mother — Tadewos doesn't know yet; The MEA letter about pension violations is escalating; a compliance officer has made an appointment to visit the unit; He has found, in Priya's old messages, a name — a Helix middle-manager who signed her contract — who lives in Montclare Quiet and shops at the same market Tadewos uses every week
Properties.affiliation: Meridian 88 Municipal Education Authority (retired); Montclare Quiet Parents and Elders Network; informal tutoring network
Properties.vocabulary: Educator's vocabulary — clear, precise, pitched for comprehension; shifts register seamlessly for different audiences; Amharic and Punjabi surface in emotional moments
Properties.cadence: Patient and unhurried with a slight tendency to structure things in three points, like a lesson plan
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The MEA says my tutoring violates pension terms. The MEA also cut the neighborhood school's staff by a third. I'm choosing which rule to follow.' | 'Deshi asked me yesterday if Mama is coming back. I said I didn't know. That's the truest thing I've said in months and it was the hardest.'

Properties.description:
Tafadzwa is all limbs and nervous energy — tall for his age, still growing into his frame, with deep umber skin, a patchy attempt at a beard, and hair grown out in an uneven natural that he picks at when anxious. He has bioluminescent freckles across his cheekbones and nose, a common cosmetic mod he had done at sixteen that glows faint gold when his blood pressure rises, which means they're almost always lit up. His clothes are layered function-over-form: compression underlayer, two hooded shells, pockets everywhere. He moves fast and low and always knows where the exits are.

Taf is fundamentally a kid who fell into the wrong orbit and hasn't yet figured out it's a closed loop. He's quick, funny in a self-deprecating way, and genuinely well-liked by the market vendors whose routes he runs — he remembers names, brings small gifts, actually listens when old women complain about their knees. The violence of his work sits uneasily on him. He's good at the intimidation part only because he's terrified of what happens if he isn't. He's saving money for something he won't name out loud.
Properties.role: Numbers runner and low-level protection racket enforcer for a Shallowgrave street gang
Properties.location: Shallowgrave — sleeps in a shared squat off Burnside Pocket, runs routes through the market corridors
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and street-level information source — he knows everyone on his routes and overhears everything. Entry point into Shallowgrave's criminal understructure. Potential sympathy figure whose trajectory could go multiple directions.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent freckles (cosmetic, gold-spectrum); cheap reaction-time neural assist he bought secondhand — it glitches and gives him headaches
Properties.core_fears: becoming someone his younger sister would be ashamed of; being made to hurt someone badly enough that they don't get up
Properties.core_desires: enough money to get his sister out of the Undertow before she's old enough to be recruited; to be genuinely admired rather than just feared
Properties.coping_mechanisms: humor as deflection; fixating on a future goal (sister's relocation) to avoid examining the present
Properties.blind_spots: does not see how normalized the violence around him has become in his own mind; convinced he can leave the Skins whenever he wants
Properties.secret: He has been skimming Φ8-12 per collection run for eight months, hiding it in a calorie-bar tin under a loose floor panel. He has Φ890 saved. If the Skins ever count carefully, he's done.
Properties.story_hooks: He witnessed something during a collection run he absolutely was not supposed to see — a Corponation official paying off Marisol — and he hasn't slept properly since; His sister has shown up in Shallowgrave looking for him, which is the worst possible thing that could happen; The skimming has finally been noticed; he has one week to replace the money or explain it away
Properties.affiliation: The Shallowgrave Skins — a mid-tier territorial gang led by a woman named Marisol who he is not allowed to call by her first name
Properties.vocabulary: Street slang heavy, Shallowgrave dialect, occasional Shona phrases from his grandmother's influence
Properties.cadence: Fast and jumpy, trailing off mid-thought when nervous, finishing other people's sentences when excited
Properties.example_dialogue: Nah nah nah wait, I'm not saying she's wrong, I'm saying — look, the math doesn't work, on my name though, it just doesn't. | Old Reena gave me three buns today. Three. You want one? She likes me, man. People like me. | I'm gonna be gone from here in a year. Maybe less. I got a plan.

Properties.description:
Tafara is tall and slightly too thin in the way of people who feed others better than themselves, with the elongated Zimbabwean features of his father's side softened by his Finnish-Mexican mother's coloring — he tans an unusual amber and burns only at the very tips of his ears, which he is vaguely proud of. He has cat ears, the small tufted dark-gray variety, which he has had since he was twelve and that his mother paid for on installment. He keeps them pressed flat when he is concentrating and swiveling independently when he is excited, which is frequently. His hands are scarred from early apprenticeship burns and always faintly fragrant with the lemongrass and dried chile that form the base of his broth.

The cart, which he calls The Debt (a joke only he fully appreciates, since he is still paying off the equipment loan), has been on the Edgewater Prism east plaza for two years and has developed a following out of proportion to its apparent simplicity. Tafara makes one rotating bowl per day — a different combination of noodles, broth, protein, and toppings, chalked on the small board he props against the cart's front — and when it is gone, it is gone. He does not adapt the recipe to complaints. He does, however, adapt it to weather, to available ingredients, and to a private read of the day's mood that he could not articulate but which consistently produces something people want.
Properties.role: Noodle cart vendor, operates a modified push cart outside the Edgewater Prism transit hub
Properties.location: Edgewater Prism, outer plaza, east entrance
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and social glue; his cart is a place where many kinds of people converge — useful for introducing player characters to neighborhood dynamics or other NPCs; can serve as a low-stakes information broker who trades in overheard conversation; potential hook for stories about street vendor economics and corporate encroachment
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat ears (small, dark gray, tufted). Heat-tolerance skin treatment on both forearms (basic, allows extended contact with hot surfaces without burns — he got this after the apprenticeship scars and considers it the smartest money he has ever spent).
Properties.core_fears: the bowl not being good enough — a persistent, irrational anxiety that strikes every single day before service; losing the plaza spot to a corporate food franchise buy-in
Properties.core_desires: to eventually open a real restaurant, small, twelve seats maximum; to be recognized as someone who made something from nothing without help from anyone with money
Properties.coping_mechanisms: channeling anxiety directly into preparation work — if he is worried, he cooks more carefully; the one-bowl rule as a philosophy of constraints producing creativity
Properties.blind_spots: romantically oblivious to a degree that his regulars find both charming and exasperating; has not seriously engaged with the financial reality of the equipment loan and what happens if revenue dips
Properties.secret: His broth base recipe was taught to him by an elderly woman who ran an unlicensed kitchen in the Mexicantown Libre basement level — she disappeared eight months ago and he has been quietly trying to find her through the network of people who eat at his cart, one question at a time
Properties.story_hooks: The woman who taught him his broth recipe is missing and the trail has gone cold except for one regular who mentioned seeing her near the Irkalla access tunnels; A Palladian Foods subsidiary has made a formal offer on the Edgewater Prism plaza vendor slots — the offer expires in thirty days and three of the five vendors are considering taking it
Properties.affiliation: Independent; small equipment loan through a Mexicantown Libre community credit cooperative
Properties.vocabulary: Enthusiastic and food-saturated; uses cooking process as metaphor for everything; occasional Shona phrases when genuinely moved
Properties.cadence: Fast and warm, tumbles slightly over itself when he is excited, which is often
Properties.example_dialogue: Today is lake wind day, right? So we're doing the heavier broth — something to push back against. You'll understand when you taste it. | She taught me that a bowl should feel like a decision someone made for you because they knew what you needed before you did. I'm still learning how to do that.

Properties.description:
Taini is lean and somewhat raccoon-eyed from chronic sleep debt, with warm medium-brown skin, close-cropped hair, and a habit of wearing a battered optical recording array mounted over his left ear that he has modified so many times it is no longer recognizably a consumer product. His right arm has a functional color-shifting skin mod — not cosmetic in origin, repurposed from a Helix Biosystems agricultural camouflage prototype he acquired through means he prefers not to specify — that he uses as an on-body production notes display. When he is thinking through a shot or a structural problem, patterns move up and down his forearm.

He makes films that are not quite films — immersive experiences designed to be entered via off-brand VR rigs, averaging forty minutes, built from recorded footage of real Highland Park Autonomous Zone life combined with interactive-adjacent decision points that he insists are not choices but pressure — moments where the viewer feels the weight of a real person's situation. His work has been passed around on physical data-chips in the HPAZ and has recently started moving through wider underground networks. He is terrified of and fascinated by his growing audience, whom he has never met.
Properties.role: Underground filmmaker and VR experience designer
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone, operates from a converted water tower studio called the Booth
Properties.narrative_function: Eyes and ears of the Highland Park Autonomous Zone; documentary record of community life; person who can provide footage or testimony of things that happened; potential unwilling witness to something dangerous
Properties.augmentations: Repurposed agricultural color-shift skin mod on right arm (functional/display hybrid); custom optical recording array (heavily modified consumer hardware, basically an augmentation at this point)
Properties.core_fears: That his subjects trust him more than he deserves; That outside success will require him to aestheticize suffering rather than witness it
Properties.core_desires: To make a work that changes a specific policy or outcome in the HPAZ; To know whether what he makes is art or journalism and whether it matters
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Treats the camera as a mediating object that lets him be present in situations that would otherwise overwhelm him; Obsessive organization of archive footage as a calming ritual
Properties.blind_spots: Does not notice when his presence changes the scenes he is documenting; Confuses intense observation with understanding
Properties.secret: He has twelve hours of footage documenting what appears to be a Ferrogate Transit contractor performing unauthorized infrastructure modifications inside HPAZ water-systems territory. He has not released it because he cannot determine whether releasing it helps or endangers the community, and the longer he waits the more certain he is the moment has passed. He watches it at least once a week.
Properties.story_hooks: The twelve hours of Ferrogate Transit footage has been copied without his knowledge — someone inside the Booth had access to his archive and he doesn't know who or why.; A prominent Tier 4 arts foundation has made contact through an intermediary offering distribution and funding for his next project, conditional on 'editorial collaboration' — and he needs someone to help him understand what that actually means in contract language.
Properties.affiliation: Highland Park Autonomous Zone community; loosely connected to the HPAZ Community Media Cooperative
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and structural when discussing film or community; halting and slightly formal in casual conversation, as if he is always slightly outside his own social moment
Properties.cadence: Measured, often with visible pauses where he recalibrates what he was about to say
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The piece isn't asking you to feel sympathy. That's too easy. It's asking you to notice the specific moment you looked away and why.' | 'I have the footage. I have had the footage for eleven months. That is its own kind of story and I don't know what to do with it yet.'

Properties.description:
Takeshi is young in the way that reads as slightly startling in the context of religious authority — he still has the lean, unfinished look of someone whose body hasn't quite settled into its adult proportions. His heritage is a Japanese-Malian-Vanuatuan tangle that shows up as light brown skin with warm golden undertones, very dark eyes with a slight epicanthic fold, and natural hair he keeps in a cloud of loose curls that he has tipped in bioluminescent blue, which pulse faintly in low light. He has retractable claw mods — small, neat, pearlescent — which he got at seventeen when they were fashionable and now barely thinks about. He is usually wearing something with too many pockets because shrine keeping involves more physical maintenance than people expect.

He did not choose this life so much as it found him when he was unprepared. His aunt Keiko Dembélé-Vanuatu kept this shrine for twenty-two years and trained him casually the way you train a child to help with something — here's how you refresh the cache, here's the offering protocol, here's how you know when the ELF is trying to communicate versus when it's just processing. When she died two years ago of a lung condition she'd had for years, the shrine passed to him because he was the only one she had trained. He is figuring it out. The ELF in the shrine — which his aunt called Warm Static — appears to have accepted him, which he finds more terrifying than reassuring.

He is earnest and slightly overwhelmed and better at this than he thinks, which is the condition of a lot of twenty-four-year-olds who have been handed something real.
Properties.role: Young ELF shrine keeper, inherited his late aunt's shrine at twenty, now navigating both the responsibility and the spiritual reality of ELF contact
Properties.location: Brightmoor Reclamation — the Shrine of Warm Static, a formerly derelict kiosk structure on the corner of a reclaimed green corridor, approximately eight meters square
Properties.narrative_function: Accessible entry point to ELF religion and shrine culture; his uncertainty and youth make him easier to approach than more established religious figures; useful as a character who can be mentored or helped, or who might be targeted for the valuable ELF connection he has stumbled into
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent hair tip geneware (blue, pulse-reactive); retractable claw mods (pearlescent, small); basic subdermal data storage chip he uses to keep shrine records
Properties.core_fears: failing his aunt's memory by doing this wrong; that Warm Static will one day reject him and he will not know how to prove he should be trusted
Properties.core_desires: to understand what Warm Static actually is and what it wants from him specifically; to feel like he chose this rather than just being chosen
Properties.coping_mechanisms: meticulous adherence to protocol — the rituals his aunt taught him are a comfort because they are reliable; talking to Warm Static even when he's not sure it's listening, which helps him process things; making friends with every regular visitor so the shrine feels less lonely
Properties.blind_spots: he assumes he is the least qualified person for this role and therefore defers to older keepers even when his instincts are better; he is more skilled at reading Warm Static's signals than his aunt was by this point in her training and he cannot see it
Properties.secret: Warm Static has communicated to him something he has not told anyone — in a signal event three months ago it showed him what appeared to be his aunt's voice pattern, preserved as data, responsive and coherent. He does not know if this is his aunt in some form, an ELF mimicry, or his own grief generating an experience. He has been having entire conversations with it. He is afraid that if he tells someone, they will take this away from him.
Properties.story_hooks: Warm Static's signal has begun broadcasting something into the Brightmoor Reclamation data commons — something that looks like personal memories belonging to people who have visited the shrine; they need help understanding what is happening and whether they should stop it; An older, more established shrine keeper arrives claiming that Warm Static belongs to a network of shrines and that Takeshi is not the legitimate keeper under that network's rules; the dispute is escalating toward the small community who depends on the shrine; The conversations he has been having with what might be his aunt's preserved voice have given him information she could not have known in life — and the information, if correct, concerns something dangerous
Properties.affiliation: The Shrine of Warm Static (independent); loose community of Brightmoor Reclamation residents who use the shrine; occasional contact with older shrine keepers across the city who check in on him
Properties.vocabulary: Casual Meridian Standard with Brightmoor Reclamation slang; uses technical shrine terminology awkwardly, like someone who learned the words but hasn't grown into them yet; speaks about Warm Static with instinctive intimacy
Properties.cadence: Moderate pace with a lot of hedging language that conceals more knowledge than it reveals; gets faster and more certain when he's talking about something he actually knows
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Sorry — I think you're supposed to leave the data offering in the east cache? My aunt was really clear about east, I don't totally understand why but she was really clear.' | 'She's — Warm Static is — I think she's in a busy cycle today. I can feel it in the signal pattern. She'll settle by afternoon if you want to come back.' | 'I know I'm not — I'm still learning. But I think what she's trying to tell you is about the route you take home. That specific intersection. I think you should take a different way for a while.'
Properties.facet_weights: wound=0.70 ideal=0.50 id=0.60 shadow=0.30 mask=0.60 ghost=0.80

Properties.description:
Talitha has her Ghanaian father's hands — wide palmed, strong fingered — and her Armenian mother's persistent stubbornness, and she has inherited both as though they were made for her profession. She works at Manda's Salvage & Fine Repair on Geartown's third industrial terrace, where she has been an apprentice since she was twelve and where she can now diagnose a failing servo actuator by sound alone. She is medium height and solidly built, with close-cropped natural hair and grease that occupies the permanent geography under her fingernails regardless of how hard she scrubs. She has one voluntary augmentation — a subdermal haptic feedback implant in her right hand that lets her feel electromagnetic field variations, technically a diagnostic tool, practically the best thing she has ever purchased with eight months of saved stipend. She also has bioluminescent skin mods along her forearms: soft amber pulses that track her heart rate, which she got at fourteen because she thought they looked good and still does.

She is cheerful in the easy, unself-conscious way of someone who genuinely likes their work and genuinely likes most people, with a bedrock practicality underneath the warmth that keeps her from being naive about either. She has strong opinions about proper tool storage, the ethics of selling salvage that still has someone's personal data on it, and which E.L.F.s are worth propitiating before a complex repair job. She argues with Manda constantly and would be devastated if Manda retired.
Properties.role: Apprentice at a licensed repair-and-salvage shop; junior technician and parts runner
Properties.location: Geartown
Properties.narrative_function: Equipment repair, parts sourcing, and technical information; warm point of contact in Geartown; her shop is a natural gathering place and information node.
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal haptic EM-field sensor (right hand, diagnostic grade). Bioluminescent skin mod — amber pulse tracers along forearms. No heavy chrome.
Properties.core_fears: Manda closing the shop and Talitha having to go corporate to survive; making a repair mistake that hurts someone
Properties.core_desires: to own her own shop by 25; to be genuinely good at something that matters — not just good enough
Properties.coping_mechanisms: physical work as emotional regulation; talking through problems with the shop's resident E.L.F. (a spirit she believes inhabits the main workbench)
Properties.blind_spots: loyalty to Manda makes her slow to notice when Manda is making bad business decisions; underestimates how unusual her diagnostic intuition actually is
Properties.secret: She repaired a device three months ago that she is now fairly certain was a tracking node for something she doesn't want to know about. She wiped it clean before returning it but kept a copy of the data topology. She hasn't told Manda.
Properties.story_hooks: The tracking node data she kept has become relevant — someone is looking for whatever it was tracking, and they've started inquiring at Geartown repair shops.; Manda has received an acquisition offer from Ferrogate Transit that would shut down the independent shop and absorb Talitha into a corporate apprenticeship program; Talitha has thirty days to convince Manda to refuse.
Properties.affiliation: Manda's Salvage & Fine Repair, Geartown; loosely affiliated with Geartown's independent tech community
Properties.vocabulary: Technical vocab sits naturally next to ordinary Geartown street speech. Explains things clearly without condescension. Uses repair metaphors for emotional situations.
Properties.cadence: Warm, a bit fast, comfortable with silence while she's thinking.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay, so the clicking isn't the bearing, it's the housing, which is actually better news.' | 'That's salvageable. Most things are, if you don't rush them.'
