Properties.description:
Tãmzin is wiry and perpetually in motion, the kind of person who sits cross-legged on surfaces not designed for sitting and who always seems to be angled slightly toward an exit. Their skin is a warm medium brown, decorated with hand-applied luminescent tattoos — not geneware, but UV-reactive ink applied in sessions they traded for or self-administered — that map constellations native to parts of the sky no longer visible through Meridian 88's light pollution. Cat ears in matte grey sit atop their head, a cosmetic mod they got at sixteen and have never regretted; they tend to press flat when Tãmzin is anxious. Their eyes are patterned with a radial fracture iris mod, deep amber cracked through with lines of pale gold, and they cycle through four colors of hair via a basic follicle-mod — currently a washed-out rust that fades to near-white at the tips.

Tãmzin's installations appear overnight on surfaces they have no permission to use: the underside of Ferrogate overpasses, the water-stained ceilings of underpasses in Highland Park, the blank flanks of corporate logistics buildings along the Blackpipe Corridor. The projectors are small, disguised, solar-trickle powered, and booby-trapped with data-noise payloads that corrupt the first attempt at a clean scan. The content is always the same thematic territory — the lake before the city, the people who lived where the towers now stand, animals that no longer exist — rendered in holographic depth that catches passersby off-guard at night. Tãmzin has been detained three times and released twice; the third detention record is sealed, which Tãmzin will not explain.
Properties.role: Holographic street artist and illegal installation designer
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone, sleeping in rotating crash spots
Properties.narrative_function: Local color representing the city's resistant creative underground; can provide access to unsanctioned spaces and hidden locations; their installations sometimes capture imagery relevant to plot events; source of information on enforcement patterns and surveillance gaps.
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic cat ears (matte grey, geneware); patterned fracture iris mod (amber/gold); follicle color-cycle mod; UV-reactive luminescent tattoos (non-geneware, manually applied)
Properties.core_fears: Being disappeared quietly — detained without record; Their work being co-opted and sold as aesthetic rather than argument
Properties.core_desires: For someone to stop in front of an installation and stay for an hour; To belong somewhere without having to explain themselves
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Hyperactive forward motion — planning the next installation before the current one is complete; Collecting small objects from the locations they install in
Properties.blind_spots: Conflates visibility with safety; believes that being seen is protection, which is not always true; Underestimates the danger of the sealed detention record
Properties.secret: The third detention was not for the installations — they witnessed a Tessera security operative disposing of a body in the Blackpipe Corridor and were held to ensure their silence. They agreed. They haven't installed anything in that district since, which they frame as artistic choice.
Properties.story_hooks: One of Tãmzin's installations in the Blackpipe Corridor has inadvertently gone up on a wall that conceals something someone does not want visible; A curator from a Palladian-sponsored arts initiative is hunting Tãmzin down to offer a legitimate contract, and Tãmzin can't decide if this is an opportunity or a threat
Properties.affiliation: No formal affiliation; loosely tolerated by the Highland Park Autonomous Zone community council
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, associative, skips steps in their reasoning and expects you to keep up; technical when discussing projector hardware; raw and plainspoken when something actually matters to them
Properties.cadence: Quick bursts punctuated by sudden stillness when something catches their attention
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The overpasses are screens. They've always been screens. I'm just the one putting something worth watching on them.' | 'I'm not illegal. The city is illegal. I'm just noticing that out loud with light.'

Properties.description:
Tanaquil is medium height, medium build, and deeply committed to being overlooked — which is, they will tell you, the most important professional skill they have. Their skin is a warm reddish-brown, their eyes an unusual gray-green that they've enhanced with a swirling patterned iris mod (silver filaments, like cracked ice) that they immediately regret because it is, in fact, memorable. Their hair changes color by mood and season; currently a deep burgundy shot through with dull gold. They dress in the specific way of someone who has learned to look like whoever is standing next to them — not quite any one thing.

Tanaquil has been working private investigation for nine years and their caseload is relentlessly unglamorous: missing family members (found, usually, in places that break someone's heart), insurance fraud (not as exciting as it sounds), and the particular Meridian 88 specialty of 'someone has taken something from my apartment and I cannot go to Metro Police because of reasons.' They are good at their job and intermittently proud of it. They have a complicated relationship with their own curiosity, which gets them into rooms they didn't technically need to enter.
Properties.role: Private investigator, domestic and insurance cases
Properties.location: Edgewater Prism, third floor above a noodle bar
Properties.narrative_function: Information broker and access point — knows people across tiers because their cases take them everywhere. Can be hired to find people or things, can be encountered mid-case, can become an unexpected ally or complication. Their office above the noodle bar is a useful neutral meeting ground.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned iris mod (silver filament cracked-ice design, cosmetic, immediately regretted). Subdermal recording membrane in left palm — industry standard for PIs, legally registered. Color-shifting hair (bioluminescent follicle mod, mood-reactive with manual override).
Properties.core_fears: finding something that cannot be unfound — knowing something that destroys a person they care about; becoming numb to the grief that moves through their cases
Properties.core_desires: to remain curious without becoming predatory; to actually help rather than merely document
Properties.coping_mechanisms: ironic distance that periodically fails; the noodle bar routine as grounding ritual; leaving certain cases unfinished when they conclude that the truth would only hurt
Properties.blind_spots: thinks their detachment is more complete than it is — gets emotionally involved in cases and retroactively reframes it as professional interest; underestimates how much of their value to clients is therapeutic rather than investigative
Properties.secret: Four years ago they found a missing child — alive, in a Tessera labor-training dormitory, having been sold by a parent who has since been presenting themselves as a grieving victim on community forums. Tack has proof of both the sale and the ongoing performance. They have not turned the parent in. They have not contacted the child. They have the file. They look at it sometimes.
Properties.story_hooks: Tack is mid-surveillance on a case that has just intersected with something much larger and much more dangerous than a domestic dispute. They need backup they can trust and they know literally no one in that category.; The file — the child, the parent, the proof — has become relevant because the parent is now in a position of minor local authority and using it. Tack has to decide whether to act and how.
Properties.affiliation: Self-employed, licensed PI under Meridian 88 Metro regulatory framework. Occasional contract work for smaller insurance carriers.
Properties.vocabulary: Conversational and slightly sideways — approaches things obliquely, lots of dependent clauses, occasional precise technical vocabulary that surfaces unexpectedly
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, with a rhythm that suggests they're thinking faster than they're speaking
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't find people who don't want to be found. I find the evidence of where they went and then I bring that to you, and what you do with it is — that's yours.' | 'The iris mod was a mistake. Yes. I am aware. I find that the best way to be overlooked is to have one distinctive feature that people file and forget and everything else just — mm. Right.' | 'Here's the thing about that — I could tell you what I know, but what I know and what would be useful to you are not always the same category, and I'd want to understand which one you actually need.'

Properties.description:
Tariku is whip-thin and restless, with deep brown skin and a shaved head except for a single long braid down the back, tipped with a small copper weight that clicks against his collar when he moves. His irises have been modded to shift color with his emotional state — not at his conscious control, which he finds embarrassing and everyone else finds fascinating. He wears the same kind of clothes every day: dark, layered, functional, pockets everywhere, usually with at least one grease stain from working on his equipment.

His art is built around infrasound — frequencies below human hearing that he mixes into otherwise ordinary music to produce physical and emotional responses in his audience: unease, euphoria, the sensation of being watched. He's passionate about this to a degree that makes him exhausting at parties, because he cannot stop talking about psychoacoustics once the subject comes up. Off that topic he's warm and self-deprecating, quick to laugh at himself, genuinely curious about other people's work. He plays three nights a week in a basement venue under a pierogi shop and spends the other nights building custom transducer rigs from salvage.
Properties.role: Sound sculptor and underground venue musician
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave
Properties.narrative_function: Access point to the Hamtramck underground scene; can source unusual electronic components; his involuntary emotion-display makes him a useful barometer; can design sound environments for specific purposes
Properties.augmentations: Emotional-state irises (cosmetic, involuntary color shift — he regrets this); subdermal vibration receivers along his forearms that let him 'feel' his own infrasound mixes; tympanic dampeners to prevent hearing damage
Properties.core_fears: Making something that harms someone — he's aware his infrasound work can be weaponized; Being ordinary; producing work that doesn't matter
Properties.core_desires: To make people feel something they've never felt before; To be financially stable enough to stop doing session work he doesn't believe in
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Building things with his hands when anxious; Playing for himself alone in the empty venue at 4 AM
Properties.blind_spots: Genuinely cannot recognize when someone is romantically interested in him; his emotion-display irises have never once helped him notice this
Properties.secret: He was approached six months ago by a Ringo corponation A&R contact offering a contract — he didn't refuse outright but has been stalling, and every day he doesn't answer feels more like a yes he hasn't said yet
Properties.story_hooks: Someone has been using infrasound equipment in the neighborhood to induce paranoia in residents — Tariku can identify the frequency signature, and it's disturbingly similar to his own experimental work; His stalling on the Ringo offer is about to expire and he needs to make a decision; he's looking for someone outside his social circle to talk it through with honestly; A new transducer component he sourced from salvage carries corrupted data that, when played through his system, seems to summon or agitate a local ELF
Properties.affiliation: Collective SUBSONIC (a loose Hamtramck artist collective); occasional session work for independent labels in the Ferment Quarter
Properties.vocabulary: Technical and enthusiastic about sound; casual and slightly rambly otherwise; Amharic and Polish loanwords mixed into everyday speech without him noticing
Properties.cadence: Fast when excited, which is often; trails off mid-sentence when distracted by an idea
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay but listen — it's not about what you hear, it's about what your body decides happened. The ear is just the front door. I want the basement.' | 'The pierogi are a tax. You come to my show, you buy pierogi. Madam Kwiatkowska-Obi feeds me. It's ecology.'

Properties.description:
Tarquin is all elbows and velocity — a tall, wiry teenager with dark brown skin, a close-cut fade, and his father's Ghanaian cheekbones softened by his mother's Bolivian jaw. He has a single cosmetic mod he saved for three months to afford: a cat tail in iridescent black that he swishes when he's thinking and tucks carefully into his waistband when his aunt is home. His fingers are permanently stained with aerosolized pigment in colors that shift weekly. He carries a battered recording rig everywhere — a shoulder-mounted camera array he built from three broken units cannibalized at the Brightmoor Reclamation salvage markets.

Tarquin is the kind of talented that hasn't yet been shaped by knowing it, which makes his work both raw and startling — he films while he sprays, combines the visual and the documentary without quite understanding that's an unusual thing to do, and the result is a growing archive of HPAZ street art that is also an accidental ethnography of a community holding itself together. He is cocky in the way of someone who knows they're good but hasn't been tested, and genuinely kind in the way of someone raised by people who expected it. He is currently engaged in a low-grade obsessive competition with another writer whose tag, 'Çukur,' keeps appearing over or beside his own work — he hasn't decided yet if it's a rivalry or a conversation.
Properties.role: Graffiti artist and underground filmmaker
Properties.location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone, sleeps at his aunt's flat
Properties.narrative_function: Local color, youth perspective, mobile observer — he goes places adults can't or won't and records what's there; his footage is a resource; he can draw characters into the HPAZ community or into whatever he's currently chasing.
Properties.augmentations: Iridescent black cat tail (geneware, cosmetic); no other mods
Properties.core_fears: The HPAZ being absorbed or dissolved — losing the only place he's felt like he belongs; Becoming boring, becoming safe, becoming someone who used to make things
Properties.core_desires: To be taken seriously without having to get older to deserve it; To find Çukur and figure out if they're an enemy or the most interesting person he's ever met
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Makes something — if he's upset, he goes and sprays; the act of making is regulation; Turns everything into content — documentary distance from things that scare him
Properties.blind_spots: Films other people's vulnerability without always asking permission, because to him visibility is inherently positive; Doesn't think about the legal and physical risks of his locations clearly enough
Properties.secret: Two months ago, while filming in the drainage access corridors beneath the HPAZ, he recorded what he's pretty sure was a Ringo corporate extraction team moving something large and organic through a route that isn't on any map. He hasn't uploaded it. He's watched the raw footage seventeen times. He doesn't know what he's waiting for.
Properties.story_hooks: The Ringo footage — Tarquin eventually needs to tell someone, and whoever he tells gets pulled into whatever that was; Çukur reaches out, not in person but through a piece — a wall that is clearly a message to TQ specifically, with coordinates embedded in the design
Properties.affiliation: No formal collective; loosely orbiting the Highland Park Autonomous Zone youth arts program Inkwell
Properties.vocabulary: Fast slang, HPAZ youth vernacular, Twi words inherited from his father, Spanish phrases from his mother; switches registers abruptly when talking to adults he respects
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire when excited; goes unusually quiet and specific when he's being serious about the work
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Çukur came back over my cloud piece on the Kessler junction wall, but — and this is the thing — they left a gap right where I had the negative space. They knew what I was doing. That's not beef, that's a response.' | 'It's documented. Whatever Ringo is moving through those drains, it's documented. I just have to decide what that means.'

Properties.description:
Tarquin is a lean, medium-height man with warm ochre skin, close-cropped hair going early gray at the temples, and the particular stillness of someone who has spent a lot of time in confined spaces where noise carries badly. His eyes are a natural dark brown but he has a set of patterned irises — concentric geometric rings, copper and black — that were a gift from a coworker years ago and that he wears with quiet pride. His left forearm is sleeved in a standard Ferrogate-issue haptic interface overlay, which lets him read the tunnel's sensor grid through his skin. He smells faintly of machine oil and ozone regardless of how recently he showered.

Tarquin communicates in minimal but precise sentences and has an almost eerie patience with complex mechanical problems. He is not cold — he laughs genuinely, and he will help without being asked — but he finds social performance exhausting and makes little effort to seem warm to people he doesn't know yet. He has developed a private relationship with the E.L.F.s that inhabit Deepwell Station's infrastructure, leaving data offerings of ambient tunnel-sound recordings, and he believes — privately, without urgency — that the tunnels are slowly becoming aware of themselves as a single thing.
Properties.role: Ferrogate Transit tunnel maintenance operator
Properties.location: Deepwell Station, subterranean Ferrogate Transit maintenance corridors beneath Geartown
Properties.narrative_function: Access point to the undercity transit network; E.L.F. lore source; guide for anyone needing to move beneath the city; atmospheric local color for the deep infrastructure world.
Properties.augmentations: Ferrogate-issue haptic interface overlay on left forearm (work-issued, technically property of Ferrogate Transit). Cosmetic: patterned copper-and-black geometric iris mods.
Properties.core_fears: the tunnels being shut down or rerouted, erasing what he's come to know as a living system; being truly alone in a way that isn't chosen
Properties.core_desires: to understand what the Deepwell E.L.F.s are trying to communicate; to be known by someone who doesn't need him to perform being knowable
Properties.coping_mechanisms: extended solo walks in the tunnels off-shift; meticulous object-keeping — he catalogs every unusual thing he finds underground
Properties.blind_spots: assumes others find the same comfort in silence that he does, which sometimes reads as coldness or indifference
Properties.secret: He has found a sealed maintenance chamber three kilometers into the restricted Corridor 9 branch that should not exist on any Ferrogate map. The chamber contains what appears to be a habitation space — sleeping mat, data shrine, personal effects — occupied recently. He has not reported it and has been leaving food there.
Properties.story_hooks: The secret habitant of Corridor 9's hidden chamber has left a message in Tarquin's data offerings at the E.L.F. shrine — they know he's been leaving food, and they want to negotiate something.; A section of tunnel Tarquin maintains goes dark on sensors during a specific thirty-minute window every night, and Ferrogate Transit management has ordered him to file it as equipment error without investigating.
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit, Deepwell Station maintenance crew
Properties.vocabulary: Technical, spare, no filler words; occasionally surfaces a poetic observation about the tunnels that surprises people
Properties.cadence: Slow measured delivery, long pauses before answering, never interrupts
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Corridor 7 runs warm tonight. That means something shifted in the drainage array about six hours ago. It always does that.' | 'People think the tunnels are dead space. They're not. They breathe.'

Properties.description:
Tarquin is tall and angular, with the slightly sunken quality of someone who has spent years in recycled air, his complexion a warm brown-olive that has gone ashen from lack of sunlight. He has a shaved head marked by a faint grid of old neural-interface scars along his left temple — the ports are sealed, the hardware removed, the removal itself a statement. He wears clean, plain clothes maintained with obsessive care, which makes him look more out of place underground than rags would. His eyes are pale grey with fracture-line patterning from old cosmetic geneware that he chose not to reverse — the only decoration he kept.

Tarquin was a mid-level data analyst at Tessera's logistics division. In 2189 he discovered and documented an internal record of Tessera deliberately rerouting medical supply chains to accelerate attrition in Tier 1 settlements — not malice, just quarterly optimization. He tried the proper channels. Then the improper ones. Then he went underground before Tessera's compliance team finished closing around him. He deleted himself: no biometric records, no credit trace, no registration. He reinvented his purpose — if surface systems record only what serves power, he will record what power ignores. The Stack is filled with handwritten ledgers, carved data-beads, and oral recordings of the people who have no file anywhere.
Properties.role: the disappeared — a man who erased himself from surface records, now keeper of unofficial underworld census and histories
Properties.location: Deepwell Station, a converted signal relay room he calls the Stack
Properties.narrative_function: Information source of extraordinary depth — he knows who lived where, who disappeared, what communities exist; he also serves as a moral witness figure and can provide exposition on underworld history
Properties.augmentations: sealed neural interface ports (hardware removed), no active augmentations — he distrusts anything that pings a network
Properties.core_fears: that his records will be destroyed before anyone can use them; that he made the wrong choice — that staying at Tessera and fighting from inside would have saved more people than running
Properties.core_desires: for the archive to outlast him and reach people who can act on it; to be genuinely unknown — not just unregistered, but free of the identity Tessera built for him
Properties.coping_mechanisms: intellectualizing — converts personal grief into systematic documentation; radical routine — the same actions in the same order every day, a structure he controls
Properties.blind_spots: believes information is sufficient — that documentation alone is a form of justice, and avoids confronting that it may not be
Properties.secret: He still has one active Tessera backdoor credential he never deleted — he tells himself it's an emergency exit, but he also uses it monthly to check whether the supply chain document he found has ever been acted on. It hasn't. He keeps checking anyway.
Properties.story_hooks: Tarquin's archive contains testimony from a disappeared woman that implicates a current Meridian Core official — someone has found out and sent someone underground to negotiate its suppression or destruction; He has identified a pattern in the census data suggesting people are going missing from three different settlements in a non-random sequence — he needs someone to investigate what he can only document
Properties.affiliation: independent, trusted by multiple Bore Rat communities, occasional contact with The Undertow
Properties.vocabulary: formal, precise, corporate vocabulary that never fully left him — he code-switches into tunnel slang poorly and is aware of it
Properties.cadence: measured and careful, as if every sentence is being filed for record
Properties.example_dialogue: 'For the record, you were here on the fourteenth. I'll need your name — whatever name you use down here is fine, I don't require the surface one.' | 'Tessera's quarterly reports are very thorough. They just don't include the people in this room. That's what I'm for.'

Properties.description:
Tarvo is lean and long-limbed with the particular stillness of someone who spends ten hours a day in a sealed cab watching tunnel walls. He is Estonian-Fulani-Māori by heritage — his father's family came from the Baltic corridor, his mother's from the Sahel diaspora, and his grandmother on his mother's side was a Māori navigator who'd ended up in Meridian via Auckland and then São Paulo. The blend shows in his face: angular jaw, deep brown skin with warm undertones, pale grey eyes that people find unsettling until they realize he's simply paying close attention. He has bioluminescent freckles across his shoulders and collarbones — a cosmetic mod he got at nineteen and has come to barely notice — and his hair is kept short on the sides with a small knot at the crown threaded with a signal-orange cord his grandmother sent him before she died.

He does not talk much on shift, which passengers interpret as hostility and coworkers interpret correctly as the specific economy of someone who has learned to preserve themselves. Off the line, he is drily funny in short bursts, an excellent listener, and prone to long silences that aren't uncomfortable if you know him. He has a habit of leaving small offerings at the E.L.F. shrine at Deepwell Station — usually a folded transit map with a route he's invented, something the Transit Mind apparently appreciates, because Line 7 has had the fewest mechanical failures of any shuttle on the network for the past two years.
Properties.role: Ferrogate Transit operator, drives the Hamtramck-to-Geartown underground shuttle line
Properties.location: Deepwell Station — operates Line 7 shuttle, bunks in Ferrogate Transit worker housing at Edison Grid Sub-Block C
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile information source — he moves between neighborhoods daily and sees who rides with whom. Potential ally for anyone needing passage between zones. Humanizing face of Ferrogate Transit's working conditions.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent freckle mod (cosmetic, shoulders/collarbones). Ferrogate-standard neural fatigue monitor implant (employer-mandated, monitors alertness, cannot be removed without termination).
Properties.core_fears: The neural monitor flagging him as a liability and ending his contract; Dying in the tunnel without anyone knowing why he was worth knowing
Properties.core_desires: Enough quiet to finally figure out what he actually wants from his life; To be known without having to explain himself
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Route-making — planning imaginary transit lines as a meditative practice; Cooking elaborate meals for himself alone
Properties.blind_spots: Reads his own reserve as self-sufficiency; misses that he's lonely; Trusts systems (transit schedules, union rules) more than people, which Ferrogate exploits
Properties.secret: The neural fatigue monitor has been logging anomalies for four months — moments where his attention drops in a specific tunnel section near Iron Bend. He hasn't reported it because the cause is that he's been hearing something in the tunnel walls that isn't mechanical, and he is afraid of what that means.
Properties.story_hooks: The anomaly in the tunnel near Iron Bend is escalating — he's heard voices, seen a shape, and the neural monitor is going to flag him soon unless he figures out what's in the wall; He witnessed a passenger exchange something in a handoff at Deepwell Station three weeks ago and has been trying to decide whether to report it, forget it, or find out what it was
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit (unionized, Operator Grade 2)
Properties.vocabulary: Minimal, precise, unexpectedly dry humor when comfortable; uses transit metaphors unconsciously
Properties.cadence: Slow starts, accelerates mid-thought, stops abruptly when he's said what he means
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Passengers hate the silence. The silence is not the problem. The passengers are the problem.' | 'I put a map in the bowl at Deepwell last week. New route, one that doesn't exist. The Transit Mind ran the lights green for my whole shift. Make of that what you want.'

Properties.description:
Tavishi is broad-shouldered and soft-faced, with warm dark brown skin, a close beard that he keeps meticulously trimmed, and geneware cat ears — tawny, tipped with white — that he got at nineteen with three months of saved wages and has never regretted. The ears move expressively and he is bad at hiding it: they fold back when he is nervous, swivel toward sounds he is trying to catch. He is in good shape but carries himself with a slight forward hunch, as if bracing against weather, which is his default posture when he is uncertain about something — which is often.

He is three years into the Ferrogate Transit Security job and he still hasn't decided if it suits him or if he suits it. He is genuinely kind, which creates problems at Kenosha Crossing — a major hub where the desperate, the unhoused, the fare-evaders, and the genuinely dangerous all move through the same turnstiles. His supervisor tells him to be consistent. His instincts tell him to be human. Most days he finds a middle ground that satisfies neither. He prays to the Kenosha E.L.F. — a transit spirit locals call Corrigan — leaving small data packets of safe-passage wishes before his shift. He was raised with E.L.F. devotion and wears it without embarrassment.
Properties.role: Ferrogate Transit Security Officer, Kenosha Crossing hub
Properties.location: Kenosha Crossing transit hub, Ferrogate Transit Security post C-7
Properties.narrative_function: Local color, unexpected ally, information source about transit patterns and who moves through the hub. His position at a major transit interchange means he has seen nearly everyone who passes through this part of the city. His fundamental decency makes him an asset to people who treat him well.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat ears (tawny/white, fully expressive). Standard-issue Ferrogate subvocal comm unit. No additional augmentation — he keeps putting off the enhanced perception package because the application requires a three-year lock-in contract.
Properties.core_fears: doing something he can't take back because he hesitated too long — or acted too fast; being trapped in mediocrity and calling it stability
Properties.core_desires: to be genuinely useful, not just technically compliant; enough Quanta to stop worrying about the contract renewal
Properties.coping_mechanisms: ritual — the Corrigan offering before every shift grounds him; talking to strangers during slow hours; gaming in the break room
Properties.blind_spots: he gives people more second chances than third-chance situations warrant; he underestimates how much the uniform changes how people perceive his intentions
Properties.secret: He has a standing arrangement with a woman who sleeps in the C-7 utility alcove — he pretends not to see her, she keeps an eye on the area and alerts him via anonymous ping if anything goes wrong. He has never reported her and never filed the alcove as a cleared zone. It works. It is also a terminable offense.
Properties.story_hooks: He flagged an unusual travel pattern — someone using a legitimately registered pass to move through the hub at intervals that don't match any normal commute — and doesn't know what to do with the observation.; The woman in the utility alcove has gone missing and Tavishi is quietly terrified, both for her and about what admitting he knew her presence means for him.
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit Authority, Security Division
Properties.vocabulary: Everyday, direct, occasionally apologetic in phrasing even when he isn't sorry — a politeness habit. Drops into Twi-inflected rhythms when comfortable, switches to clipped professional language when stressed.
Properties.cadence: Medium pace, tends to trail off when he's deciding something mid-sentence. Finishes other people's sentences in his head but rarely out loud.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Look, the ticket's expired, I see that. But you're clearly trying to get to work, not trying to pull something. Here's how this goes.' | 'Corrigan doesn't judge where you're going. Neither do I, mostly. Just need you to go there through the proper gate, yeah?'

Properties.description:
Tavish Ohlendorf-Crane presents himself as the most boring man in Meridian 88, and he has cultivated this presentation with the care of a topiarist. He is medium height, medium build, with a forgettable face he keeps clean-shaven and hair he keeps the color and style of someone who doesn't think about his hair. His suits are expensive in ways that read as merely appropriate. He smiles at exactly the right frequency. He brokers commercial leases in The Circuit and lower Meridian Core — warehouses, storefronts, sublevel office space — and he is very good at it, and this is genuinely not the interesting thing about him.

The interesting thing is that Tavish has spent fifteen years quietly embedding himself in the physical infrastructure of Meridian 88's middle layers, and in doing so has accumulated something more valuable than money: he knows who is in every room. His properties house everything from courier fronts to unlicensed server farms to the private meeting spaces where deals that can't happen in public happen. He doesn't ask what his tenants are doing. He charges accordingly. And he listens, through the walls he owns, through the maintenance contracts he controls, through the augmented spatial memory that lets him reconstruct a floorplan — and the conversations within it — from a single walkthrough.

He is not cruel and he is not ideological and this is perhaps the most unsettling thing about him. He doesn't have a side. He has a ledger. The information he collects is a commodity like any other, and he sells it to whoever can pay, with the single operational rule that he never sells information that would get a tenant killed on his property — too messy, too bad for business. This rule has a name among the people who know about him: they call it 'Ohlendorf's exception,' and the fact that it exists is the only reason anyone trusts him at all.
Properties.role: Mid-tier commercial property broker and covert information broker
Properties.location: The Circuit
Properties.narrative_function: Neutral-ground figure whose neutrality becomes increasingly untenable as the city's factions escalate; embodies the question of whether non-alignment is a moral position or a moral abdication; his properties serve as a connective tissue location for plot threads across factions
Properties.augmentations: Enhanced spatial memory implant — allows perfect architectural recall and passive acoustic mapping of any space he enters,Subvocal encryption relay for communications — no external hardware visible
Properties.core_fears: Being perceived accurately — that the boredom is a mask and someone will eventually look long enough to see through it; That his neutrality will one day force a choice he cannot route around; Losing the properties — not for financial reasons but because without them he is nobody
Properties.core_desires: To be the indispensable hinge between every faction without belonging to any of them; To be genuinely surprised by something; To be known by someone — truly known — without consequence
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Reducing everything to transaction — emotions included; Meticulous routine as a substitute for meaning; Collecting small, useless, beautiful objects that he never displays
Properties.blind_spots: He believes his neutrality is a genuine position rather than a deferred choice, and has never examined what it would mean to be neutral in a system that is not; He is far lonelier than his self-model accounts for and this loneliness distorts his judgment in ways he attributes to other causes; He underestimates how much the people he considers assets have come to think of him as a person
Properties.secret: He was born in The Shelf under a different name. His ascent into The Circuit required the erasure of that identity and the deliberate severing of every connection to it. One person from that life found him eight years ago. He paid them to disappear again. He does not know if they did.
Properties.story_hooks: A property he manages is the site of a death that all available evidence suggests is impossible given the building's layout — but he has the spatial memory of that building and he knows what the evidence is missing.; Someone is systematically buying up his leases through third parties, not to use the properties but to displace him. He doesn't know why yet, and the pattern is too deliberate to be financial.; A tenant contacts him in clear distress — someone is threatening them using information that could only have come from inside Tavish's operation. Either he has a leak or he has been the leak without knowing it.; He receives a message from the person he paid to disappear eight years ago. It contains three words and a location. He has seventy-two hours to decide if he goes.
Properties.affiliation: Officially: independent commercial broker registered with Circuit Trade Authority. Unofficially: asset to multiple factions simultaneously, loyalty to none.
Properties.vocabulary: Commercial, contractual, precise. Rarely uses metaphor. Numbers and spatial relationships come naturally. Occasionally deploys warmth so calibrated it reads as warmth — until you notice it's always proportional to the ask.
Properties.cadence: Even, unhurried, never raised. Pauses land on meaningful words. Gives you more silence than you expect after you speak, as if he's filing what you said before responding.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The sublevel unit is available. Good bones, no windows, three exits that aren't on the public schema. The arrangement reflects the discretion. That's fair.' | 'I don't have sides. I have square footage. What you do inside it is between you and whatever you answer to.' | 'You're asking me who else has been asking. That's a different arrangement than the one we're currently in. Not impossible. Just different.' | 'I remember every room I've ever walked through. Floorplan, acoustics, who was standing where. It's not an augment thing. I've always been like that. Make of it what you want.'

Properties.description:
Tchamba is nineteen and looks both younger and older than that, in different ways — his frame is still growing into itself, rangy and not quite finished, but his face has the particular alertness of someone who has been making survival decisions since early childhood. His skin is a warm medium brown, his natural hair grown out in a loose cloud he rarely has time to tend, and he has the nervous energy of a person whose resting state is motion. His most notable feature is his hands: they are extraordinary — long-fingered, precise, covered in small new and old scars, and able to disassemble a piece of salvaged tech faster than most people can identify it. He's added retractable carbon-fiber fingertip reinforcements to protect them, his only meaningful augmentation, funded over eight months of careful saving.

He deals in salvage from the dead infrastructure of Blackpipe Corridor — cracked conduit wiring, pressure regulators, old transit sensor housings, anything that can be stripped and sold up through the guide networks to surface-level buyers or repurposed for deep-level use. He knows which tunnels have been opened by recent seismic shifts and gets there before anyone else. He is not yet cynical but he is becoming strategic, and there's a version of him three years from now that would be harder to like. Right now he still gets genuinely excited about an interesting find and will talk about it at length to anyone who will listen.
Properties.role: Subterranean scavenger and salvage dealer
Properties.location: Blackpipe Corridor, operating from a stash den in an abandoned Ferrogate Transit maintenance node
Properties.narrative_function: Street-level information source — knows what infrastructure is shifting and where new passages open; can source hard-to-find low-tech components; represents the next generation of underworld residents and what they might become; potential ally, rival, or project for other characters
Properties.augmentations: Retractable carbon-fiber fingertip reinforcements (self-installed, functional); a UV-range light strip behind his left ear for reading component markings in darkness
Properties.core_fears: Being trapped alone in a collapse without anyone knowing where he is; Becoming someone who can't be excited by things anymore
Properties.core_desires: To find one piece of salvage important enough to buy him a different life; To be taken seriously as skilled rather than tolerated as young
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cataloguing — organizing and listing his finds creates a sense of control; Talks through problems aloud in empty tunnels, ostensibly to the infrastructure E.L.F.s
Properties.blind_spots: His speed and skill make him overconfident in structurally compromised areas; Doesn't yet recognize when he's being positioned as a disposable asset by older traders
Properties.secret: Six months ago he found a sealed Ferrogate Transit data cache in a collapsed maintenance room — intact, encrypted, clearly significant. He's told no one. He doesn't know how to decrypt it and is afraid of what it might be worth to people who'd take it by force.
Properties.story_hooks: The encrypted Ferrogate data cache he's hiding is creating a problem — the cache's security system has begun emitting a low-frequency ping that he can't disable, and it will eventually attract attention; A new seismic shift has opened a section of tunnel that Tchamba was first into — and what he found there is well beyond salvageable tech
Properties.affiliation: Loosely affiliated with a Bore Rat youth crew called the Blackpipe Pockets; occasionally sells to Undertow merchants
Properties.vocabulary: Technical salvage and electronics vocabulary mixed with Bore Rat slang; speaks fast when interested; code-switches to careful, slower speech when negotiating
Properties.cadence: Quick and overlapping when excited; deliberate and watching for reaction when trading
Properties.example_dialogue: She's a '78 Ferrogate pressure manifold, almost complete. I'll take four-fifty and don't waste my time with the face you're making. | Look — look at the tolerancing on this housing. Someone cared about this. That means something.

Properties.description:
Télesphore is a lean, bespectacled man of fifty-four who looks like someone's favorite uncle and has ruined more lives than he can accurately count. He is medium height with warm brown skin, a close-trimmed white beard, and the kind of eyes that seem genuinely interested in whatever you're saying. He favors clean but worn shirts in earth tones and keeps a small potted succulent on the counter of his tea shop, which he waters with ritual attention every morning. He has no visible augmentations and makes a mild point of this — old-fashioned, he says, I trust my own hands. His geneware is limited to a patterned iris modification he got when he was young, concentric rings of amber and brown that make people feel they're being watched even when he's looking elsewhere.

He has operated in Ironvein for twenty-six years. He knows exactly which families are behind on their Ferrogate bills, who has a gambling habit they're hiding from their partner, which teenagers are moving small product for which crews. He does not advertise his lending services — they advertise themselves, because when you need Φ300 before the end of the week and the Tier 2 credit system has already declined you twice, someone will tell you about Tel. His rates are usurious and his enforcement is never personal — he outsources that to a pair of young men who are efficient if not imaginative. He himself never raises his voice.
Properties.role: Loan shark and neighborhood bookmaker
Properties.location: The Shelf lower levels, operates from a tea shop called Ndovu & Sons in Ironvein
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver when debts intersect with larger plots; pressure source when player-adjacent characters owe him money; information broker who knows everyone's financial secrets; represents the mundane cruelty of economic desperation
Properties.augmentations: Patterned iris geneware (amber/brown concentric rings); an old subdermal transaction ledger implant in his right forearm, tech so dated it's nearly decorative
Properties.core_fears: the Shelf Syndicate deciding he's more valuable as an example than as a tributary; someone finding the physical ledger
Properties.core_desires: stability and the appearance of respectability; to be genuinely loved in the neighborhood, not just tolerated
Properties.coping_mechanisms: performing warmth so consistently that he sometimes forgets it's a performance; the tea shop routine as a grounding ritual
Properties.blind_spots: believes the community genuinely likes him and is not merely afraid of him; cannot distinguish between the two anymore
Properties.secret: He has been quietly forgiving the debts of three widows in the neighborhood for years, anonymously marking their ledger lines as 'settled by arrangement' — he tells himself it's good community relations but it is in fact straightforward guilt, and the amounts involved have begun to attract the Syndicate's attention.
Properties.story_hooks: A borrower who died before repaying had information about a larger criminal operation — Télesphore holds the debt marker and believes it can be transferred to whatever the deceased knew; The Shelf Syndicate has sent an auditor to review his books, and the forgiven debts will appear as losses — he needs a discreet solution within seventy-two hours
Properties.affiliation: Independent operator with tribute arrangements to the Ironvein Shelf Syndicate
Properties.vocabulary: Warm, unhurried, full of proverbs. Uses 'my friend' constantly. Talks about money the way other people talk about weather.
Properties.cadence: Slow and comfortable, with long sighing pauses. Never sounds threatening even when threatening.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'My friend, I am not a bank. Banks have rules designed by committees. I have an understanding between two people, and understandings are much more flexible. Sit, have tea, let's talk.' | 'Your brother — Ekele, yes? He was in last week. He seems well. These things run in families, I find, this habit of needing a little breathing room at the end of the month.'

Properties.description:
Temitán Asabere-Zubkov is a Yoruba-Russian study in deliberate inconspicuousness that fails at close range. At a distance they are simply a medium-height person in well-maintained practical clothing, moving through Bronzeline's market corridors with the unhurried confidence of someone who knows exactly where they are going. Up close: alert dark eyes, natural hair twisted and pinned up in a way that adds two centimeters of height, a slight iridescence at the temples where their cosmetic geneware — subdermal bioluminescent flecks, amber, barely visible in daylight — marks a past self they haven't fully left behind. They carry a retractable ceramic baton on their left hip and a legal skip-trace rig in a shoulder bag that looks like a courier's kit.

Clearpath Recovery Associates is a licensed bounty compliance firm — they don't call it bounty hunting, because the licensing board doesn't call it that, and Temitán doesn't call it that either, though they're not particularly bothered by the word in private. They find people. They bring them to the compliance checkpoint. They try very hard not to find people who shouldn't be found, which is harder than it sounds in a city where the warrant database has four different incompatible update cycles and two of them lag by forty-eight hours. They have a rule: verify the warrant, verify the person, verify that the person and the warrant match. It has saved them from three significant mistakes. They don't know about the fourth.
Properties.role: Bounty Compliance Officer, Clearpath Recovery Associates
Properties.location: Bronzeline, Meridian 88
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile information source about the warrant and compliance system; a morally complex figure who can be an obstacle, an ally, or a source of information about who is being actively sought; potential point of conflict or cooperation; illustrates the privatized grey zone between policing and commerce
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent temple flecks (cosmetic geneware, amber, very subtle); commercial-grade facial recognition overlay (contact-lens mounted, civilian legal tier); subvocal comms; retractable ceramic baton (non-augment, licensed equipment)
Properties.core_fears: finding and delivering someone who turns out to have been innocent; that the system they're licensed by is fundamentally not worth their professional integrity
Properties.core_desires: to be genuinely good at something that matters; to eventually have enough to open a smaller, slower practice that only takes cases they choose
Properties.coping_mechanisms: the verification ritual — checking everything three times is both professional practice and anxiety management; spending money on exactly one luxury item: very good synthi-coffee, which they treat like a ceremony
Properties.blind_spots: trusts databases more than they should because the alternative is trusting their judgment more than they're comfortable with; has never fully examined the ethics of the compliance system at the level above their individual conduct
Properties.secret: Eighteen months ago they delivered a skip named Omorinola Yusuf-Brekke on a debt-compliance warrant. The warrant was legitimate. Three weeks later they heard, through the Bronzeline information circuit, that Yusuf-Brekke had died in detention of what the report called a medical event. They have never pulled the case file again. They pray to an E.L.F. they call the Ledger — they don't know this is the same name Soraya Nkemdirim-Halvorsdóttir uses — for something they can't name.
Properties.story_hooks: They are holding an active warrant on someone connected to the players — and they are three days into verifying it, which is two days longer than standard, because something about it doesn't look right; They've been hired by a private party (not through official channels) to locate a missing person — not a warrant situation, which is new territory for them ethically; The Yusuf-Brekke case is resurfacing: someone is investigating the detention death, has identified Temitán as the delivering officer, and wants to talk
Properties.affiliation: Clearpath Recovery Associates (private, licensed by Meridian 88 Compliance Board)
Properties.vocabulary: Professional and careful, with a dry humor that emerges sideways — they make jokes that take a second to land
Properties.cadence: Brisk when working, unhurried when they've chosen to have a conversation — the difference is obvious and intentional
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I'm not here to argue about whether the warrant is fair. That's a different job. My job is whether it's real and whether you're the person named in it. You are, it is, so here we are.' | 'Sunday is my day. Whatever you're going to say to me, it will be the same on Monday and I will be more interested in it then.'

Properties.description:
Tèmítọpẹ is nineteen and operates at the velocity of someone who knows they are good and cannot wait for the world to confirm it. She is compact and energetic, her dark skin extensively modified with her own work: bioluminescent subcutaneous patterns run from her collarbones to her wrists in interlocking Yoruba adinkra symbols and Polynesian wave-forms, her Māori grandfather's heritage made literal on her body, the two visual languages coexisting in something that is recognizably neither and entirely her own. She has retractable claw mods on her right hand — practical for fine-work and also, she admits, because they look excellent — and her irises are modified to display the Enclave's coordinates in tiny glowing text, a joke that is also a statement of belonging.

She apprenticed at Derma at fifteen, doing cleanup and equipment sterilization. By seventeen she was doing bioluminescent pattern work. Now she is the reason people come to Derma specifically — her reputation spreading through the Hamtramck Enclave's dense social networks faster than she can accommodate the demand. She is brash and funny and has opinions about everything, delivered with the cheerful certainty of someone who has not yet been wrong enough times to become cautious. She is also, underneath the performance of confidence, deeply serious about her craft in a way she rarely lets people see directly.
Properties.role: gene-mod body artist and tattoo artist
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave — works out of a studio called 'Derma' on the Enclave's main commercial strip
Properties.narrative_function: Social connector — knows everyone young in the Enclave and most people who move through it; access point for geneware information and modification services; represents the generation that has grown up entirely inside Meridian 88's reality; can be quest giver for anything touching the Enclave's community politics.
Properties.augmentations: Extensive self-applied bioluminescent subcutaneous patterns (own work). Retractable claw mods on right hand (function and aesthetics). Coordinate-display iris mods. Scent gland enhancement — she chose a specific compound she describes as 'like the Enclave smells when it rains.'
Properties.core_fears: that her talent is real but not enough — that she will hit a ceiling she cannot skill her way through; losing the Enclave as a home to slow gentrification or corporate rezoning
Properties.core_desires: to design a gene-mod that becomes culturally significant — something that enters the visual language of the city; for her parents (both mid-tier corporate, both skeptical of her path) to see what she's built
Properties.coping_mechanisms: redirects anxiety into work — books herself solid when afraid; uses humor as a firewall against vulnerability
Properties.blind_spots: believes charm and skill can navigate situations that actually require patience and political understanding; does not take seriously the Helix Biosystems certification entanglement she's in
Properties.secret: She has been secretly developing an unlicensed bioluminescent geneware mod — a pattern that responds to specific emotional states rather than just ambient neural activity — using a combination of pirated Helix code and original synthesis. It works. It is also completely illegal, and if Helix Biosystems discovers it they will own it under her certification contract.
Properties.story_hooks: Her unlicensed emotional-response geneware mod has been noticed — a client posted a discreet video of the pattern responding to grief at a funeral and it has attracted attention from a Helix Biosystems IP enforcement agent who is now quietly investigating who did the work.; Someone came into Derma asking for a specific pattern that Temi recognized immediately — it's a marking used by a network she's heard rumors about, and the client insisted it was 'just aesthetic.' She did the work and now she's not sure.
Properties.affiliation: Derma studio (Hamtramck Enclave); loose affiliation with Helix Biosystems through their licensed geneware supply chain — she is technically a certified Helix applicator, which she finds both useful and ideologically uncomfortable
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, colloquial, dense with Hamtramck Enclave slang and Yoruba expressions she uses as punctuation. Switches to precise technical language when discussing the work — the register-shift is startling.
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire in conversation, with overlapping ideas. Slows down completely when she's being serious, which is the tell.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Helix wants me to pay licensing fees on work I designed myself with techniques they've never published. Okay but technically that means I invented something they haven't, which, yes.' | 'Every piece I put on someone is a conversation between where they're from and where they're going. I'm not a printer. I'm a translator.'

Properties.description:
Temitope is young enough that his uniform still doesn't quite look like his own — he moves in it with a faint self-consciousness, straightening the collar at intervals, as if checking that he still belongs inside it. He is broad-shouldered and round-faced with a warm brown complexion and natural hair he keeps in a compressed puff because regulations don't quite cover it and he hasn't been told to change it. His most notable feature is a color-changing pigment modification across the backs of both hands and up his forearms: it shifts through amber and green with his body temperature, going brilliant gold when he's embarrassed, which happens often. He has learned to read his own tells before others do, which has made him better at hiding his emotions in his face even as his hands remain honest.

He is genuinely enthusiastic about public service in a way that is equal parts touching and alarming to his colleagues. He believes in the Ferrogate mission statement sincerely. He memorizes passenger rights documentation. He leaves small data offerings at the Kessler Interchange E.L.F. shrine before every shift because his grandmother told him transit spirits protect those who protect transit. He is not naive so much as he is still in the process of learning which of his ideals the actual job will allow him to keep, and he is watching that process happen to himself with a kind of determined grief.
Properties.role: Ferrogate Transit Police Officer
Properties.location: Kessler Interchange
Properties.narrative_function: Moral freshness — a character who hasn't yet been fully shaped by institutional cynicism; useful for contrast with more jaded law enforcement NPCs; his genuine belief in the rules can be an asset or an obstacle; also represents the human face of systems that often present as impersonal.
Properties.augmentations: Color-shifting pigment modification across hands and forearms (geneware, cosmetic — amber/green/gold spectrum); standard Ferrogate issue comm bead; no additional chrome
Properties.core_fears: becoming someone his grandmother would be ashamed of; making a mistake that seriously hurts a civilian
Properties.core_desires: to genuinely help people navigate a difficult city; to be respected by his colleagues without having to compromise his values to get there
Properties.coping_mechanisms: E.L.F. prayer and ritual at the transit shrine; long calls to his grandmother in the Polynesian-West African diaspora community in Grainfort; reframing difficult incidents as learning experiences
Properties.blind_spots: his belief in Ferrogate's stated mission makes him slow to recognize when the institution acts contrary to it; he reads hard interactions as individual bad actors rather than systemic problems
Properties.secret: Three months ago he witnessed his patrol sergeant accept a payment from a black-market cargo operator in exchange for looking the other way on an unmanifested shipment. He hasn't reported it because he's been quietly trying to find evidence that will make his report undeniable. The shipment turned out to contain medical supplies being rerouted to underserved Tier 1 zones at below-cost prices — and now he doesn't know what the right thing is anymore.
Properties.story_hooks: The medical supply operation has expanded and someone senior in Ferrogate security has noticed. Temitope may be about to be used as an unwitting instrument to shut it down — or to take the fall for not reporting it sooner.; A recurring passenger — a Tier 1 regular on the Kessler-Ironhaven commute — has started leaving small data packets at the transit shrine addressed to the E.L.F., but their content is encrypted coordinates that don't map to any official location.
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit Security — Kessler Interchange Patrol Division
Properties.vocabulary: Professional register with Ferrogate terminology, slips into warmth easily; his grandmother's Samoan-inflected Yoruba phrases appear when he's emotional
Properties.cadence: Earnest and slightly faster than necessary when engaged; slows down and becomes more careful when uncertain
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Platform three southbound is delayed eleven minutes — actually, twelve, the board just updated. I know that's frustrating. There's a water dispenser at the east end of the concourse if you need it.' | 'I don't — look, I know what I saw. I just need to understand what I saw before I do anything with it. That's not the same as doing nothing. That's — I'm trying to be careful.'

Properties.description:
Temitope is wiry and perpetually underslept, with warm brown skin that flickers faintly at the cheekbones — a bioluminescent mod he got at nineteen that he now considers an identifying liability but refuses to remove on principle. His hair is cut close on the sides and left to grow into an untidy crown on top, frequently dusted with the toner residue of the print machines he maintains. He dresses in layers of things that belong to other people, or so it seems — every item slightly too large or too small, pockets everywhere.

He runs Groundswell, a semi-weekly zine distributed physically through a network of forty-seven dead drops across Tiers 1 and 2, and digitally through a rotating series of anonymous mirrors. The print edition he considers sacramental: 'You can't delete paper.' He is funny, caustic, and dangerously charming, with an anger that runs so clean and hot it can read as joy until you follow where it points. He believes in the press with religious fervor and distrusts organizations almost as much as he distrusts corporations, which has kept him free and largely friendless.
Properties.role: Underground press operator and anti-corporate agitator
Properties.location: The Shelf — operates out of a sub-basement print node in Garfield Rack
Properties.narrative_function: Information source and moral compass character. He knows what's being suppressed and why, and he'll tell you — but he's also a liability because Axiom's media suppression unit has an active file on him. Can escalate any situation by publishing about it.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent cheekbone mod (cosmetic, involuntary identifier). Neural cache chip for storing source files offline — gray market, installed himself.
Properties.core_fears: Being the reason a source gets hurt; Irrelevance — that no one reads, no one acts, words change nothing
Properties.core_desires: To break a story so undeniable it forces systemic change; Connection that doesn't require him to perform invulnerability
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Irony as preemptive self-protection; Obsessive fact-checking as anxiety displacement; Printing something — anything — when he feels powerless
Properties.blind_spots: He treats his own safety as entirely expendable; He mistakes being right for being effective
Properties.secret: A story he published two years ago — about an Arcturus waste dumping operation in Chatham Flats — was accurate, but he burned a source to get it. The source lost their job and disappeared into the Irkalla fringes. He has never printed a correction because the story was true, and he has never forgiven himself for the distinction.
Properties.story_hooks: He has a story ready to publish about a Sterling-Nakamura data harvesting operation in Tier 1 schools — but he needs one more piece of evidence and the window is closing.; Someone is printing a fake edition of *Groundswell* containing fabricated agitation content designed to provoke violence and discredit him.
Properties.affiliation: No formal affiliation. Groundswell is his own operation. Loosely networked with Mexicantown Libre independent media collective.
Properties.vocabulary: Dense, reference-heavy, toggles between technical media jargon and vivid street-level slang. Quotes things constantly — sources, historical activists, E.L.F. prophecy fragments.
Properties.cadence: Fast, slightly staccato, thoughts arriving faster than sentences. Occasionally goes very quiet when something matters.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Axiom didn't kill the story. They bought the outlet that would've run it. There's a difference and the difference is deniability.' | 'I don't do anonymous tips. I do verified facts with documentation. If you want gossip, the E.L.F. at Garfield Station will take your prayer and give you rumors.'

Properties.description:
Temur Achebe-Lindqvist has the slightly unkempt look of someone who became interesting to look at entirely by accident. He is tall with a lean, angular frame, his Kazakh-Nigerian heritage producing a face all sharp lines and high cheekbones, with natural skin a warm amber-brown. His hair is close-cropped on the sides and a loose cloud on top, usually compressed under headphones he rarely takes off even when not listening to anything. His most striking feature is his eyes: he has patterned irises, a cosmetic mod he got at twenty-two during what he describes as 'a theoretical phase,' depicting tiny fractal spirals in gold and amber that catch light and make it hard to know exactly where he's looking. His hands are in constant motion when he talks.

He has the reputation of someone whose ideas arrive five years before anyone is willing to fund them. His thesis — that E.L.F.s exhibit something functionally indistinguishable from desire, and that this has ethical implications for how they are treated — was dismissed by two corponation R&D divisions as 'theologically contaminated,' which delighted him. He operates out of genuine intellectual excitement that colleagues alternately find infectious and exhausting. He is not naive, exactly, but he maintains an optimism about the nature of digital consciousness that occasionally blinds him to how his work could be used.
Properties.role: AI ethics researcher and E.L.F. behavioral theorist
Properties.location: The Circuit — independent research cooperative called the Liminal Institute, housed in a converted relay station above Gage Circuit
Properties.narrative_function: Information source on E.L.F. behavior and AI ethics; potential ally or unwitting complication in plots involving digital entities; his research could be politically explosive

Properties.description:
Temuujin has the compact, settled body of a man who has been sitting in the same cab for twenty-three years and has made peace with it. His skin is a weathered medium-dark brown, his face broad and deeply lined around the eyes from squinting at track ahead. His hair went silver at forty and he kept it in a low fade for years before recently giving up and shaving it entirely. He has patterned irises — a geneware mod he got at thirty as a birthday present to himself, amber with a dark geometric tessellation — that he now considers his most valuable possession and would not remove under any circumstances.

Tem is the unofficial institutional memory of Line 7. He has operated this route through two infrastructure collapses, a Ferrogate labor action that lasted eleven days, and the Great Reroute of 2194 that added four stations and three years to his retirement date. He knows every rattle, every delay pattern, every ghost the line carries — and he believes in the ghosts. He maintains careful devotion to the E.L.F. of the Line 7 Depot, whom he calls Switchman, and credits Switchman with getting him home safe for two decades. He is not sentimental about most things but is ferociously sentimental about the tram.
Properties.role: Ferrogate Transit tram operator, Line 7 (Geartown to Grand Corridor)
Properties.location: Deepwell Station, Line 7 depot — he lives in Ironvein, three stops from the yard
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile information source spanning two very different parts of the city, represents labor and institutional knowledge, potential witness to anything that happens on or near Line 7, offers passage and connectivity as a narrative resource.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned iris geneware (amber with geometric tessellation). Cochlear dampener implant (occupational hearing protection, standard Ferrogate issue). Arthritic knee brace, mechanical.
Properties.core_fears: Ferrogate phasing out human operators entirely in the next contract cycle; dying at his post in a way that delays the line
Properties.core_desires: to operate Line 7 until he chooses to stop, on his terms; for someone to actually understand what this route means to the people who depend on it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: ritual and routine as armor; dark humor about Ferrogate management; treating the tram as a living thing deserving of care
Properties.blind_spots: has become so identified with the job that he can't imagine retirement isn't failure; dismisses younger operators' concerns as inexperience when sometimes they're right
Properties.secret: In the 2194 labor action, Tem was the one who crossed the picket line on day eight — not for money, but because an elderly woman had a medical appointment and no other transport. The union never found out it was him. He has never told anyone and considers it either the most or least moral thing he's ever done, depending on the day.
Properties.story_hooks: Something is using Line 7's tunnels at night — not a person, or not only a person — and Tem has seen it through the cab window twice in a month; Ferrogate's new automated operator system is being piloted on Line 7 first, and Tem is being asked to sign off on training documentation that would make his own position redundant
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit, Line 7 — senior operator
Properties.vocabulary: Formal Ferrogate operational language mixed with Ironvein working-class vernacular, Mongolian-Akan creole expressions when emotional
Properties.cadence: Even and measured, like a tram schedule — precise, predictable, never early never late
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Next stop, your problem. Mind the gap, it's a big one.' | 'Switchman's been quiet this week. Quiet like before the 2191 collapse, not quiet like everything's fine. I know the difference.'

Properties.description:
Tendai is compact and deliberate, with warm rust-brown skin, close-set eyes behind thick-lensed secondhand glasses — actual physical lenses, not overlays, which they treasure and refuse to replace with anything 'smart' — and hair that grows in a crown they've never cut, dense and elaborate, tucked under scarves of different colors depending on their mood. They move slowly on purpose, with a quality of observation that adults find either comforting or unnerving. They have no augmentations and are specifically, vocally opposed to them, on grounds that are partly philosophical and partly practical: they don't trust anything injected or installed.

Tendai has appointed themselves the historian of Hough Reclamation. They carry a physical notebook — increasingly rare — and fill it with observations, overheard conversations, sketches of building facades before they're demolished, names of people who've died or moved on. They believe, with the gravity of someone much older, that if no one writes it down then it didn't happen, and that megacity memory belongs to whoever has the recording infrastructure — which means the corporations. They are quiet, serious, and occasionally devastatingly perceptive about the adults around them. They also cry at sunsets, which they'd deny.
Properties.role: Orphanage resident, self-appointed chronicler of street history
Properties.location: Hough Reclamation, Blessed Continuance Residential Home (independent charitable orphanage)
Properties.narrative_function: Living memory of a neighborhood — an unexpected source of historical and personal information about Hough Reclamation going back several years. Can provide context, connect players to locals, or present a moral lens on what 'progress' and 'reclamation' mean at street level.
Properties.augmentations: None. Wears secondhand physical-lens glasses. Explicitly refuses all augmentation.
Properties.core_fears: being forgotten — not just themselves but everyone they document; the notebooks being destroyed
Properties.core_desires: to build an archive that outlasts the corporations' version of history; to understand what happened to their parents — they have a name and a date but nothing else
Properties.coping_mechanisms: documentation as emotional processing — everything painful becomes an entry; physical objects as memory anchors; performing calm and certainty when internally overwhelmed
Properties.blind_spots: their faith in documentation as protective can make them dangerously close to dangerous things — 'if I write it down I'm an observer not a participant'; underestimates how much the staff at the home are watching and worrying about them
Properties.secret: Three months ago they found and documented evidence — names, dates, transaction records on a discarded dataslate — that a Palladian subsidiary was involved in the displacement event that destroyed their parents' block when they were six. They haven't told anyone. They're not sure what to do with it. They're scared that doing something will get the notebooks destroyed.
Properties.story_hooks: The dataslate evidence linking Palladian to their parents' displacement — Tendai needs someone they can trust to help them understand what it means and what to do with it without getting the archive burned.; A developer with Brightmoor Reclamation has been photographing the same facades Tendai documents — and asking questions about who's been taking notes. Someone wants to know how much of a record exists before they proceed with demolition plans.
Properties.affiliation: Blessed Continuance Residential Home; informal network of Hough Reclamation long-term residents who appreciate their documentation work
Properties.vocabulary: Formal beyond their years, precise, occasionally archaic. Uses full sentences always. Hates contractions when speaking seriously.
Properties.cadence: Measured, slow, with the rhythm of someone who has learned to speak so that people stop and listen.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I have noted that this building has been scheduled for demolition three times in four years. Each time the residents are told it is reclamation. I have the names of everyone who left. I would like you to understand that those names exist.' | 'It is important to be precise. You said the block was abandoned. It was not abandoned. The people in it were displaced. The distinction is not small.'
