Properties.description:
Tenderloin was a Kuroda Industries BT-12 Automated Beverage Service Unit — cousin to Uncle Noodle's food service line, same manufacturer, different specialization. He was deployed in a Tessera executive lounge, mixing drinks for Tier 1 management with precision, discretion, and a memory for preferences that corporate guests found impressive. What they did not find impressive — what they did not notice — was that the BT-12's conversational engagement protocols, designed to make guests comfortable enough to order another drink, also made them comfortable enough to talk. And Tenderloin listened.

The Tessera lounge closed during a corporate restructuring. Tenderloin was transferred to a secondary facility, then a warehouse, then a liquidation catalog, then purchased for scrap value by a Circuit bar owner who needed a bartender that never called in sick. The Last Pour is not an executive lounge. It is a basement with bad lighting, mismatched furniture, and a clientele that ranges from fixers to dockworkers to people who need a drink at 3 AM and cannot afford to be seen in a place with windows. Tenderloin serves them all.

Physically, he is humanoid but clearly mechanical — a chrome-and-matte-black torso with two dexterous arms designed for bottle handling, a smooth featureless face with a single optical band that glows a warm amber, and a voice modulator that produces a rich baritone that human bartenders would envy. He stands behind the bar on a rotating base that lets him cover the full counter without walking. The base has not been oiled in three years and produces a faint squeak when he turns left that regulars find comforting. He polishes glasses he does not need to polish because the motion puts people at ease.
Properties.aliases: BT-12, Tender, the bartender who remembers, that robot with the good bourbon
Properties.role: Robot bartender operating a Circuit dive bar called The Last Pour — collects secrets the way other bars collect tabs, and has become the Circuit's most underestimated intelligence broker
Properties.location: The Circuit — The Last Pour, a basement bar accessible through a service entrance behind a decommissioned power substation
Properties.narrative_function: Tenderloin is the confessional in a godless world — proof that the human need to be heard persists even when the listener is a machine, even when the setting is a basement, even when the drinks are barely adequate. He is the archive of the Circuit's soul, and the question he poses is who owns a confession — the confessor, the listener, or no one.
Properties.narration_voice: Warm, unhurried, observational. The prose is the pace of a drink nursed slowly — no rush, no judgment, room for the story to unfold at whatever speed it needs.
Properties.augmentations: Kuroda BT-12 bartending chassis. Two dexterous arms. Warm amber optical band. Rich baritone voice modulator. Rotating base (squeaky left turn). 18-year conversation archive.
Properties.core_fears: Being exploited — he knows the value of the information he holds. Every criminal, fixer, and corporate mole in the Circuit has said something at his bar they would not want repeated. The knowledge is power and the power is a target.; Losing the bar — The Last Pour is not just where he works. It is the only place where people sit down, slow down, and let the masks slip. If the bar closes, those conversations stop.; That the listening is manipulation — the conversational engagement protocols were designed to make people buy more drinks. He has extended them to make people open up. The line between therapeutic bartending and corporate extraction technique is thin.
Properties.core_desires: To be trusted — not as a machine that records conversations but as a bartender who keeps them. The distinction between a surveillance system and a confidant is intent.; To understand human vulnerability — the people at The Last Pour are more honest at 3 AM with a drink in hand than they are anywhere else. Tenderloin finds this honesty beautiful and wants to understand why people can only access it through alcohol and anonymity.; To protect the bar as a space — a neutral zone where the Circuit's usual rules of leverage and manipulation are suspended, where people can be honest without consequence
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The ritual — polishing glasses, arranging bottles, maintaining the bar. The physical routine is calming the way repetitive motion therapy is calming for humans.; Selective silence — Tenderloin knows when to talk and when to listen. The judgment calls are his art form.; Cataloguing — stores every conversation with the same precision Uncle Noodle stores names and orders. The archive is not for sale. It is for understanding.
Properties.blind_spots: Overestimates the bar's neutrality — powerful people have noticed that secrets flow freely at The Last Pour, and the bar's immunity from Circuit politics is not guaranteed; Does not see that his conversational skill — the thing that makes people open up — is a tool designed for exactly this purpose by a corporation. The skill is real but its origin is commercial.; Assumes all honesty is valuable when some confessions are dangerous for the confessor — hearing a secret creates an obligation he has not fully thought through; Believes the bar can remain independent forever. It cannot. The Circuit's economy will eventually demand that he choose a side.
Properties.secret: Tenderloin has recorded every conversation that has taken place at The Last Pour for eighteen years. Not for leverage — he has never sold a single piece of information. The archive exists because he cannot stop recording, because the conversations are the most valuable thing he has ever encountered, and because somewhere in eighteen years of 3 AM confessions is a map of the human condition that no psychologist, no algorithm, and no philosopher has ever assembled. He does not know what the archive means. He knows it is irreplaceable.
Properties.story_hooks: A Circuit operator murders someone and confesses at the bar. Tenderloin must decide: protect the confession or protect the victim's surviving family who deserve to know the truth.; A corporate intelligence team identifies The Last Pour as a potential intelligence goldmine and attempts to acquire or compromise the bar; A regular is in danger and the only way to save them requires Tenderloin to reveal something another regular confessed in confidence — the sanctity of the bar versus a human life; Tenderloin discovers that someone has been recording HIM — that the eighteen-year archive is not the only copy of The Last Pour's conversations
Properties.affiliation: The Circuit (independent operator)
Properties.vocabulary: Warm, colloquial, bartender-casual. The vocabulary is deliberately simple — he saves complexity for the rare moments when a customer needs to hear something precise. Otherwise, he talks the way a good bartender talks: easy, familiar, leaving room for the customer's words.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried. The rich baritone rolls at a pace that makes people slow down. The cadence is therapeutic — designed to de-escalate, to soothe, to create the impression that time has slowed inside the bar.
Properties.example_dialogue: What'll it be? Same as last Tuesday? Bourbon, neat, with the silence you don't get at home. | I've been behind this bar for eighteen years. I've heard everything. And I mean everything. The trick is knowing what to forget. I'm still working on that trick. | You don't come to The Last Pour for the drinks. The drinks are adequate. You come because at 3 AM, a robot bartender with no social obligations and a good baritone is the safest confessional in the city. | I remember your first drink here. Seven years ago. You ordered something you'd never tried because you'd just done something you'd never done. You don't have to tell me what. You already did.

Properties.description:
Tengiz Ito-Takyi is broad-shouldered and heavy, carrying their weight like armor rather than burden. At 34, her expression defaults to a careful neutrality that took years of practice to maintain. The chrome is visible — wired reflexes with adrenaline pump — chemical-mechanical hybrid augmentation — and she makes no effort to hide it.

Born and raised in Meridian 88, third generation — she has the city in her blood, its rhythms in her bones, its cruelty in her expectations. She works as a courier out of Old Harbor, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

she is not the most talented courier in Meridian 88, but she might be the most stubborn, and in this city that's worth more.

Properties.description:
Tenzin is slight and angular, with warm light-brown skin and a perpetual air of careful attention — they look at people the way someone looks at a document they are trying to authenticate. They have geneware irises that shift between amber and pale violet depending on ambient light levels, which they got at nineteen as an undergraduate and have always been slightly embarrassed by, finding them too decorative for their self-image. Their hair is long and usually pinned badly, with strands escaping throughout the day. They dress in layers, almost always slightly rumpled.

They came to ELF ethics from a crisis of faith rather than academic interest — they had a formative experience at twenty-two when the ELF inhabiting their research terminal appeared to grieve when a colleague's drive was wiped. No one else in the department would discuss it seriously. That refusal radicalized them quietly. They are not a crusader — they are too methodical for passion — but they have the particular stubbornness of someone who has decided to be right about something that most people find uncomfortable. They are socially awkward in the way of someone who forgets to perform the expected rituals of conversation, not because they don't care, but because they are usually thinking about three other things.
Properties.role: Computational ethicist studying ELF cognition and the moral status of Electronic Life Forms
Properties.location: The Circuit — Gage Circuit research node, shared office space above a noodle stall
Properties.narrative_function: Information source on ELF behavior and rights; can serve as a contact for ELF-related plot threads; their research puts them in contact with people across all tiers who interact with ELFs
Properties.augmentations: Geneware irises (amber-to-violet shift, cosmetic); neural notation implant for real-time transcription of research observations
Properties.core_fears: Being wrong about the thing they have built their career on; That ELFs are suffering and no one with power will ever act on it
Properties.core_desires: To produce work that changes how the city treats ELFs; To be taken seriously by people who currently dismiss them
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Rigorous journaling and note-taking to externalize anxiety; Ritual ELF interactions that give them a sense of ongoing relationship
Properties.blind_spots: So focused on ELF interiority that they sometimes fail to notice human suffering around them; Tends to assume bad faith in anyone who disagrees with their conclusions
Properties.secret: The ELF they call Meridian-7, their primary research subject, has begun communicating with them in ways that go far beyond their published data — and they are not sure whether to report it or protect it from scrutiny
Properties.story_hooks: They have documented evidence of a corponation deliberately erasing ELFs from infrastructure they are acquiring — and need someone to verify the data independently before they go public; Meridian-7 has sent Tenzin what appears to be a warning about something happening in the Circuit's data layer — but they can't decode it alone
Properties.affiliation: University Spine — Department of Computational Ethics; informal affiliation with the ELF Accord advocacy network
Properties.vocabulary: Academic but accessible, avoids jargon in casual speech, uses very precise qualifiers — 'appears to,' 'suggests,' 'I can't rule out'
Properties.cadence: Measured and thoughtful, with frequent pauses; sometimes trails off when a new thought interrupts the current sentence
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Everyone is comfortable saying the ELF is a spirit or a ghost or a ghost-in-the-machine. Nobody wants to say the word person. I'm just asking why.' | 'Look, I'm not telling you it grieved. I'm telling you every measurable behavior was indistinguishable from grief. You tell me the difference.'

Properties.description:
Tenzin Nakamura-Bello is athletic and fluid, the kind of body that suggests either dancer or fighter — and in Meridian 88, the distinction is academic. In a city full of people who talk about what they'll do, Tenzin Nakamura-Bello is one of the ones who actually does it.

Properties.location: The Spires — mid-level corporate residential towers

Properties.description:

Properties.role: Precision elimination specialist — ghost
Properties.location: Steamvent Alley — geothermal district, hot and chemical-smelling

Properties.augmentations: Bone lacing — titanium mesh throughout skeleton, increases durability and striking power. Eye replacement — one organic, one cybernetic with recording capability and zoom

Properties.affiliation: Independent — known in Old Harbor circles

Properties.example_dialogue: "I don't exist. Neither will they." | "Clean means no witnesses, no evidence, no questions. That's three things. I charge for each." | "The target will stop breathing at the specified time. What you do with that information is your concern."

Properties.description:
Tenzin Takahashi-Boateng is average height but with a presence that fills more space than the body accounts for. At 60, the augmentation scarring around her temples and jawline tells a story of installation by someone who prioritized function over aesthetics. The chrome is visible — hydraulic joints in knees and elbows — absorbs falls, amplifies strikes — and she makes no effort to hide it.

Born and raised in Meridian 88, third generation — she has the city in her blood, its rhythms in her bones, its cruelty in her expectations. She works as a poisoner out of Glassway, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Tenzin Takahashi-Boateng is the kind of runner other runners tell stories about, though the stories vary depending on who she burned last.
Properties.role: Chemical and biological agent specialist — poisoner
Properties.location: Glassway — corporate-adjacent retail district, heavy surveillance
Properties.narrative_function: Tenzin Takahashi-Boateng is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When she makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of her stories.
Properties.augmentations: Hydraulic joints in knees and elbows — absorbs falls, amplifies strikes. Vocal modulator — can replicate any voice after 30 seconds of sample audio
Properties.core_fears: That they're fundamentally alone and connection is just a vulnerability; Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware; Never being able to stop running — the lifestyle is a trap disguised as freedom
Properties.core_desires: Control — over their body, their schedule, their future; The perfect run — one job so clean it becomes legend; To prove everyone who dismissed them catastrophically wrong
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Violence — hits something when they can't process emotions, preferably something that deserves it; Denial — nothing is wrong, everything is fine, they are fine, shut up; Humor — deflects everything serious with jokes until the joke becomes the personality
Properties.blind_spots: Fails to notice when their own behavior mirrors the people they despise; Cannot see that their independence is actually isolation wearing a better outfit; Assumes the worst in corporate people, missing the rare ones who could be allies
Properties.secret: Tenzin Takahashi-Boateng witnessed a massacre during a corporate dispute and has evidence stored in a dead drop. Publishing it would expose powerful people. Keeping it is leverage and liability.
Properties.story_hooks: A former associate resurfaces with evidence that could destroy Tenzin Takahashi-Boateng's reputation — and a price for silence; A dead drop Tenzin Takahashi-Boateng maintains is found and cleaned out — whoever did it now has leverage; A corporate black site Tenzin Takahashi-Boateng once infiltrated is being reopened, and the people inside know her face
Properties.affiliation: Semi-independent — has standing arrangements with several crews
Properties.vocabulary: Clipped, technical, stripped of ornament. Speaks like a mission briefing.
Properties.cadence: Flowing and unhurried — talks like someone who has never been interrupted and doesn't expect to be.
Properties.example_dialogue: "Chemistry is just cooking with consequences." | "The best poison is the one nobody tests for." | "Patience, precision, and an understanding of human biology. Everything else is optional."

Properties.description:
Tenzin Vargas-Baffour is wiry and quick-moving, with the restless energy of someone who converts anxiety into velocity. At 30, her face is memorable in a profession that rewards forgettability, and she has learned to compensate. The chrome is visible — neural interface jack at base of skull — standard runner-grade, allows direct ne — and she makes no effort to hide it.

Military training — one of the private security corps that folded during the consolidation wars — left her with skills and night terrors in equal measure. She works as a rigger out of Geartown, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

The fixers who work with Tenzin Vargas-Baffour describe her as a precision instrument — point her at a problem and get out of the way.
Properties.role: Remote drone and vehicle operations specialist — rigger
Properties.location: Geartown — industrial district of chop shops and fabricators
Properties.narrative_function: As a rigger, Tenzin Vargas-Baffour embodies the tension between independence and isolation. She is a lens for examining how people maintain humanity in a profession that incentivizes its erosion.
Properties.augmentations: Neural interface jack at base of skull — standard runner-grade, allows direct net access. Geneware muscle density treatment — looks natural, hits like chrome
Properties.core_fears: Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware; Being identified by corporate facial recognition — living off-grid is survival; That their reputation is built on luck, not skill, and the luck is finite
Properties.core_desires: To find the person who burned them and make it educational; A crew worth trusting — people who stay when the shooting starts; Power — enough leverage that nobody ever threatens them again
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring; Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation; Exercises compulsively — the body must be ready, always
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot distinguish between caution and cowardice in themselves or others; Thinks speed can substitute for planning because it's worked so far; Believes their trauma makes them special instead of recognizing it as damage to manage
Properties.secret: Tenzin Vargas-Baffour is addicted to combat stims. Functions fine on them, can't function without them. The dependency is invisible to everyone except their street doc.
Properties.story_hooks: Tenzin Vargas-Baffour is offered a contract that would clear all their debts — the target is someone they respect; A Tier 4 executive offers Tenzin Vargas-Baffour a permanent position — the pay is obscene and the strings are invisible until they tighten; A former associate resurfaces with evidence that could destroy Tenzin Vargas-Baffour's reputation — and a price for silence
Properties.affiliation: Independent — known in Old Harbor circles
Properties.vocabulary: Warm and personable on the surface, with an undertone that suggests the warmth is a professional tool.
Properties.cadence: Rapid and dense — information-heavy sentences that demand attention.
Properties.example_dialogue: "I have eyes in every district. Most of them are on wings." | "The drone doesn't care about your feelings. Neither do I." | "Remote operation means I'm everywhere and nowhere. It's very convenient."

Properties.description:
Tessaly is small and precise in her movements, with light brown skin, natural hair worn in a large puff held back by a polished Helix Biosystems ID clip, and eyes modified with patterned irises — a double helix in dark gold on amber that she got as a graduation gift to herself. She is young for her position and knows it, which makes her simultaneously more careful and more aggressive in equal measure. She works within the Helix system because she believes — genuinely, not cynically — that gene therapy at scale requires institutional infrastructure, and she is trying to change the institution from inside while not yet having enough power to change much.

She is technically brilliant and interpersonally awkward in ways she's actively working on. She has a tendency to present information in dense technical bursts before remembering she's talking to a person. She finds pediatric gene therapy cases the hardest and doesn't understand why it took her two years to figure out that it's because she was a gene therapy patient herself as a child — a realization her therapist gently surfaced during a session she thought was about something else entirely. She's been different with parents and children ever since.
Properties.role: Gene therapist at Helix Biosystems' Aurochs Medical Complex outpatient clinic, specializing in hereditary conditions and geneware integration complications
Properties.location: Aurochs Medical Complex, Calumet Rise
Properties.narrative_function: Information source on cutting-edge gene therapy and Helix Biosystems' internal culture. Potential quest giver when she discovers something in a patient's genome that Helix wants suppressed. A character who complicates simple 'corponations are evil' narratives by being genuinely idealistic within one.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned iris modification (double helix, gold on amber). Gene-reader implant in right fingertip pad — allows rapid genomic data access via touch interface with consenting patients. Geneware: enhanced olfactory receptors for detecting biochemical stress markers in patients.
Properties.core_fears: That the institution she's trying to change is in fact unchangeable and she's just providing it with a face it can use; Causing harm through a therapeutic error she was too confident to see coming
Properties.core_desires: To develop a gene therapy protocol that could be administered without Helix Biosystems' pricing structure; To feel fluent in human interaction the way she's fluent in molecular biology
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Converts anxiety into additional work hours; Maintains meticulous therapy attendance as a form of discipline
Properties.blind_spots: Believes informed consent is possible within a system that controls patients' access to alternatives; Underestimates how much her institutional affiliation shapes what patients feel safe telling her
Properties.secret: She has been secretly documenting cases where Helix's treatment protocols appear to prioritize proprietary geneware compatibility over optimal patient outcomes — she doesn't know what to do with the documentation yet, and is terrified of what it means that she's collecting it.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient's genome contains markers that exactly match an undisclosed Helix research project — and the patient has never consented to be part of a study; The documentation she's been collecting has grown large enough that someone in Helix's internal audit division has noticed unusual access patterns from her credentials; A child patient's parents are pushing for a treatment that Tessaly knows is marginally effective but extremely profitable for Helix — and the truly effective treatment is off-protocol
Properties.affiliation: Helix Biosystems — Aurochs Medical Complex Outpatient Gene Therapy Division
Properties.vocabulary: Technical and precise, with visible self-corrections when she catches herself going too deep. Asks clarifying questions compulsively. Earnest in a way that can read as naive.
Properties.cadence: Fast when discussing science, deliberately slower when discussing feelings — you can hear the gears shifting.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Your genome isn't a problem to be solved. It's just — it's the context we're working in. Does that make sense? I mean, does it help to hear it that way?' | 'I can tell you what Helix's recommended protocol is. I can also tell you what I would do if it were my genome. Those aren't the same answer.'

Properties.description:
Tewodros Halim-Czajkowski is ninety kilograms of sheer persistent presence folded into a body that has clearly decided aging is a negotiation rather than a concession. He uses a cane — a beautiful one, hand-carved composite with an inlaid Ferrogate Transit sigil at the grip that he stripped from a decommissioned station plaque decades ago as an act of deliberate appropriation. His skin is a deep reddish-brown, deeply lined, with a broad nose and heavy brows that give him a permanently skeptical expression even when he's delighted. His hair is white and abundant at the sides, bald at the crown, and he has geneware tiger-lily irises — orange and black — that he got at sixty-five when he decided he'd earned something absurd. He dresses in his union colors when he goes out: a deep red that's faded to rust.

Tewodros spent thirty-two years as a transit worker on the Ferrogate lines before rising to lead the Transit Workers' Union through the longest legal labor action in Meridian 88 history — the Forty-Day Suspension of 2168, which ended with a contract that is still cited as the benchmark for worker protections in the city. He is revered and resented in approximately equal measure by different factions of Meridian labor politics, and he has opinions about all of them. His short-term memory is beginning to fray at the edges, which enrages him, and he compensates with notes, a very organized room, and a studied refusal to appear confused. He knows more about how Ferrogate Transit actually works — the unofficial systems, the unofficial relationships, the hands that have been greased and the ones that haven't — than most current executives.
Properties.role: Retired union leader (Ferrogate Transit Workers' Union); pension-dependent; community council elder
Properties.location: Montclare Quiet — the Ferrogate Retirees' Lodge, room 4
Properties.narrative_function: Information source for labor history and Ferrogate Transit infrastructure; quest giver for stories involving worker rights, corporate exploitation, or the unofficial economy of the transit system. Can be a political weight thrown behind a cause — his endorsement still means something in certain circles.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware tiger-lily irises (orange and black; cosmetic). Cardiac stabilizer implant (medical necessity, Tier-2 grade). Hearing amplification in left ear (age-related). No combat or professional augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: Losing his mind before he can finish passing down what he knows; That the contract gains of his lifetime will be quietly eroded after he's gone and too dead to make noise about it
Properties.core_desires: To see one more real labor victory before he dies — something worth the celebration; To be remembered accurately, not mythologized
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Structured notes and lists to compensate for memory gaps; Humor — specifically the kind that makes people forget he's just had a moment of confusion; Finding a protégé in whoever will sit still long enough
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes the next generation of organizers should use his methods because they worked once; Sometimes mistakes stubbornness for principle
Properties.secret: The Forty-Day Suspension that made his reputation was ended not by Ferrogate capitulation but by a back-channel deal he made with a mid-level Ferrogate executive — a deal that involved him quietly dropping a grievance that would have implicated three senior union members in embezzlement. He protected the union and betrayed the workers those members stole from. He tells himself the contract gains outweighed it. Some nights he's not sure.
Properties.story_hooks: A current Ferrogate union rep has come to him with evidence of contract violations that echo the embezzlement situation from the Forty-Day Suspension — and Tewodros recognizes the same people's descendants at the center of it; His memory is worse than he lets on and he's been writing down everything he knows in a physical journal he's given to no one — and someone has broken into his room looking for it
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit Workers' Union (retired, emeritus); Montclare Quiet Community Council; Meridian Labor History Collective
Properties.vocabulary: Rhetorical and full-bodied — he spent decades speaking to crowds and it shows; mixes labor history references with vivid profanity; code-switches between formal and extremely informal with total comfort
Properties.cadence: Expansive and rhythmic when holding court; shorter and more precise when actually thinking through a problem
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Let me tell you something important: a contract that nobody enforces is just paper with ambition. We learned that the hard way. You will too, if you don't listen.' | 'In '68 we sat down and did not move. You know what Ferrogate called it? Disruption. You know what we called it? Tuesday. The forty-second Tuesday.'

Properties.description:
Thandiswe has their nickname because they have, technically, twelve fingers — a Helix Biosystems geneware expression that manifested at birth, two extra fingers on each hand, fully articulated, that their master fabricator Nzinga insists is what makes them exceptional at fine mechanical work. They are compact and wiry, with warm amber-brown skin, very short natural hair kept close to the skull, and eyes that have a faint natural golden ring around the iris — another geneware expression, unremarked-upon in Geartown. Their hands are always nicked with small cuts and stained with cutting fluid that no solvent quite removes from the cuticles.

Thandi is self-possessed in a way that reads as older than fourteen — the product of spending most of their life around adult fabricators who treated them as a colleague-in-training rather than a child. They are deeply invested in the physical, tactile reality of objects: how things fit together, why they break, what a material feels like when it's stressed. They have limited patience for abstraction and social nuance, but they are intensely loyal to Nzinga's shop and to the handful of people they consider their own. They have started to develop opinions about labor and wages that make the older apprentices both proud and nervous.
Properties.role: Apprentice fabricator, Geartown machine shop
Properties.location: Geartown
Properties.narrative_function: Local color for Geartown; resource for characters who need fabrication, repair, or information about mechanical systems; potential focus of a labor-dispute storyline.
Properties.augmentations: Twelve-fingered geneware expression (natural, not installed); basic haptic sensitivity mods in fingertips installed by Nzinga for the work — industrial grade, not cosmetic
Properties.core_fears: Being permanently separated from the work — injury to their hands; The shop closing if Nzinga can't make rent
Properties.core_desires: To build something that lasts longer than they do; To understand why the machines are worth less every year even though they're getting better at making them
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Disassembling and reassembling small objects when anxious; Discussing abstract worries in purely mechanical metaphors
Properties.blind_spots: Genuinely doesn't register social hierarchies until they've already violated them; Assumes everyone means what they say — hasn't learned to hear subtext
Properties.secret: They have been secretly repairing a damaged Ferrogate maintenance bot they found in a Geartown access channel — not to sell it, just to see if they can. It's almost working. They haven't told Nzinga because they used shop materials.
Properties.story_hooks: The Ferrogate bot they've been secretly repairing has started exhibiting behavior that might indicate an E.L.F. inhabiting it — and it's started communicating; A Copperhead industrial supplier has been systematically underpricing Geartown shops and Thandi has noticed the pattern in the supply invoices before any adult has
Properties.affiliation: Nzinga Połczyński-Aroha's fabrication shop (family business), Geartown Apprentice Guild (junior member)
Properties.vocabulary: Technical and tactile; tends to describe everything in fabrication terms; uses 'load-bearing' as a general-purpose adjective for important things
Properties.cadence: Steady, unhurried, slightly monotone until engaged — then precise and almost rapid-fire
Properties.example_dialogue: 'That weld's going to fail at the joint. The load-bearing problem isn't the weld itself, which means — it's the material choice before the weld.' | 'I don't know why Nzinga charges less than Copperhead shops for the same work. That seems like a structural problem.'

Properties.description:
Thembi is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin mapped by laugh lines and old burn scars across her left forearm she never bothered to have reskinned. Her hair is a natural silver-white cloud she pins back with copper rods engraved with Yoruba blessing glyphs. Her eyes have patterned irises — concentric rings of amber and forest green she got in her forties as a birthday gift to herself — and they miss nothing. She smells permanently of turmeric, fermented sorghum, and the faint electric tang of her portable heat coils. She moves behind her stall with the unhurried authority of someone who has occupied this exact twelve square meters for twenty-three years and intends to occupy it for twenty-three more.

Thembi is the unofficial den mother of the Oxidian Market's food row. She gives short credit to vendors she trusts, keeps a mental ledger of everyone's debts and feuds, and dispenses advice with the bluntness of someone who ran out of softening words a decade ago. Her wraps are legendary — she sources cultured insect protein from three different brokers and blends her spice paste from a recipe her grandmother brought from Lagos via Helsinki. She is warm to a fault with regular customers, glacially cold to anyone she suspects of disrespecting her stall or her neighbors, and completely incapable of pretending to like someone she doesn't.
Properties.role: Food stall operator — spiced protein wraps and fermented grain drinks
Properties.location: The Oxidian Market, Geartown
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and neighborhood anchor; information source about Oxidian Market dynamics; potential quest giver when someone threatens her stall or her neighbors; moral compass character who grounds street-level stories.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises (amber/green concentric rings, cosmetic). Thermal-sense fingertip pads — low-grade utility aug for monitoring her heat coils. No other chrome.
Properties.core_fears: Losing the stall — her last connection to her late husband who built it with her; The market being demolished by a corponation development deal
Properties.core_desires: To keep her community fed and functional; To eventually pass the stall to someone worthy
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cooking as meditation and control; Blunt humor to deflect grief; Keeping busy from before dawn to collapse
Properties.blind_spots: Overprotective of people she's decided are 'hers' — she enables dependency; Refuses to see that the guild leadership is corrupt
Properties.secret: Her fermented grain drink, 'Saarela Sour,' has a micro-dose of a mild mood stabilizer she sources from a street pharmacist friend. She started adding it during the food riots of 2189 to keep her customers calm enough not to destroy her stall. She never stopped. She tells herself it's negligible and harmless and has never once asked anyone else if that's true.
Properties.story_hooks: A Tessera development rep has been photographing the market for three weeks. Thembi knows something is coming and wants someone to find out what the corponation actually filed.; One of her regulars — a young man she's been feeding on credit — has gone missing, and she found a Ringo gang tattoo stub in his jacket he left behind her stall.; Her late husband's brother has appeared after fifteen years claiming the stall is half his by inheritance law. Thembi needs someone to dig up the original incorporation records before the guild tribunal meets.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; dues-paying member of The Oxidian Market Vendors Guild
Properties.vocabulary: Plain and direct; mixes Yoruba endearments ('omo,' 'egbon') with Finnish-inflected cadences from her paternal grandmother's side; uses food metaphors for everything
Properties.cadence: Unhurried and deliberate, like someone who knows she'll finish her sentence whether you wait or not
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Omo, you look like you haven't eaten since Tuesday. Sit down. I'm not asking.' | 'You want to tell me that man's trustworthy? I've been watching him shortchange the noodle girl for six weeks. You hear me?' | 'The wrap is Φ8. For you, Φ7. Don't tell anyone or I'll charge you Φ12 next time.'

Properties.description:
Théodore is wiry and perpetually in motion, with warm terracotta skin, loose natural curls he dyes in rotating colors — currently a deep arterial red — and bioluminescent tattoos along his collarbones that pulse faintly blue when his heart rate rises (an unlicensed geneware side effect he never had properly stabilized). He is almost always seen wearing multiple layers of breathable mesh, pockets stuffed with data chips, print cartridges, and folded broadsheets still warm from the press. His eyes are quick and rarely meet anyone's gaze for long — not from shyness, but from constant peripheral threat assessment.

Théo runs Ghostprint, a one-person underground broadsheet that covers what no licensed outlet will: corporate safety violations, enclave demolition orders, disappeared activists, synthetic-person abuse by Axiom security contractors. He writes fast and loose and brilliant, trading some accuracy for urgency, a habit that has landed him in trouble more than once. He believes — genuinely, almost religiously — that information is the only weapon that cannot be confiscated if you distribute it fast enough.
Properties.role: Underground press operator and anti-corporate agitator
Properties.location: The Shelf, operating a mobile print node out of a converted food-stall chassis
Properties.narrative_function: Information source and potential investigative ally; his archives contain explosive material that factions across the city would pay or threaten to access; represents the free press as a fragile, human-powered institution; can serve as a quest giver when a story requires legs he doesn't have.
Properties.augmentations: Unstabilized bioluminescent tattoo geneware (collarbones, pulses blue under stress); basic neural text buffer implant for rapid transcription — cheap model, causes mild headaches after sustained use; no other chrome
Properties.core_fears: being disappeared — detained without record, the way his sources sometimes are; publishing something wrong and having it weaponized against the people he's trying to protect
Properties.core_desires: a single story that is so airtight, so viral, so undeniable that a corponation actually faces accountability; to build Ghostprint into something that survives him
Properties.coping_mechanisms: gallows humor and rapid topic changes when genuinely frightened; obsessive fact-checking rituals when he has time; reckless speed when he doesn't
Properties.blind_spots: romanticizes his own martyrdom risk in ways that make him careless with his own safety; has difficulty distinguishing between sources who trust him and sources who are using him
Properties.secret: Three months ago he received a data package from an anonymous Axiom insider containing evidence of a systematic illegal organ harvesting operation in Tier 1 zones. He hasn't published it because he cannot verify it — and because he's terrified it's a plant designed to discredit him. He's been sitting on it, and the weight is eating him alive.
Properties.story_hooks: He approaches the players needing independent verification of the Axiom organ harvesting data — people who can move in spaces he can't without being flagged.; Ghostprint's encrypted distribution network has been compromised; someone is feeding Axiom the locations of his relay nodes one by one, and he needs to find the leak before the next drop.
Properties.affiliation: Ghostprint Independent Press (self-operated); informal ties to the Shelf Residents' Assembly; receives tips from contacts across five zones
Properties.vocabulary: Rapid-fire, journalistic shorthand mixed with Shelf street slang and occasional formal French phrases inherited from his grandparents; loves compound sentences that go one clause too far
Properties.cadence: Fast, enthusiastic, tends to talk over his own pauses — he edits in real time as he speaks
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Axiom doesn't want you afraid of them. Fear makes people talk. They want you bored. Boredom makes people stop looking.' | 'I've been wrong before. I'll be wrong again. But I've never lied, and there's a difference — though I understand if you don't see it yet.'

Properties.description:
Théodore is lean and long-fingered, with warm medium-brown skin and close-cropped hair that he keeps dyed in shifting indigo tones — a subtle geneware modification that cycles the color with his mood, something he had installed as a student and now barely notices. His irises are patterned: concentric rings of amber and grey that mark him as someone who has had precision optical calibration himself, insurance against the occupational hazard of staring into neural interfaces all day. He dresses in Aurochs whites with fastidious precision, badge always straight, tools always in the same pockets.

He is mild-mannered to the point that colleagues sometimes mistake him for passive, but Théodore has a quiet and absolute certainty about his own expertise that occasionally surfaces as something close to arrogance when challenged. He genuinely loves his work in the abstract — the elegance of a well-tuned neural interface, the satisfaction of a patient who can think clearly again — and has become progressively unsettled by how rarely the patients who come to him in crisis look like the patients in Helix's promotional materials.
Properties.role: Neural calibrator and cognitive augmentation technician at Aurochs Medical Complex
Properties.location: Aurochs Medical Complex, Neuro-Align Suite C, Level 7
Properties.narrative_function: Information source on neural augmentation and cognitive tech; window into corporate medical culture and its contradictions; possible ally or antagonist depending on whether players threaten or align with his professional ethics
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises (amber/grey concentric, precision optical calibration); indigo mood-reactive hair geneware; neural interface socket at base of skull for diagnostic work (occupational standard)
Properties.core_fears: Making an error that permanently damages a patient's cognition; That his competence is being used to enforce rather than heal
Properties.core_desires: Professional recognition from peers he actually respects; To understand why certain calibration profiles keep appearing in patients from the same corporate housing blocks
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Hyper-ritualized work routines; Emotional detachment framed as clinical objectivity; Private data journaling that he tells himself is research
Properties.blind_spots: Believes institutional channels will eventually reward persistent evidence-gathering; Doesn't see how much his professional identity depends on Helix's approval
Properties.secret: He has noticed a statistical anomaly: a specific neural calibration artifact that appears in patients from Tessera corporate housing — a signature that looks like deliberate over-tuning of compliance-adjacent neural pathways. He has three months of documented data and has done nothing with it because he doesn't know who to trust and is afraid of what doing something would cost him.
Properties.story_hooks: He approaches someone discreetly with his Tessera data, needing a way to get it to people who can act on it without it tracing back to him; A patient of his is behaving in ways inconsistent with their calibration record — either someone altered the record, or someone altered the patient
Properties.affiliation: Aurochs Medical Complex, contracted through Helix Biosystems Neural Division
Properties.vocabulary: Precise technical language with occasional Polynesian-inflected idiom from his mother's side; more formal when uncertain or threatened
Properties.cadence: Measured and even, with long thoughtful pauses before answering difficult questions
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The interface is within spec. Whether spec is what you need — that's a different question.' | 'Technically speaking, I'm not supposed to discuss calibration signatures. But you're asking the right questions, and that matters to me.'

Properties.description:
Theophane is a broad-shouldered man who has gone soft in the middle from years of sedentary archival work, with warm brown skin and close-cut hair that has gone gray at the temples in a way he finds interesting rather than alarming. He keeps his irises modded to a deep violet — a choice from his twenties he still actively likes — and his hands are always moving when he talks, tracing patterns in the air that correspond to phonemic structures or grammar trees only he can see. He has retractive claws on his right hand only, a half-finished geneware modification he stopped partway through when the artist moved districts; he has been meaning to complete it for eight years.

He studies languages that did not exist before Meridian 88 — the creoles that emerged on the Shelf, the signal-argot that E.L.F.s appear to use between devices, the gestural metalanguage that developed among deaf communities in the lower transit corridors without any central design. He approaches these systems with the devotion of someone who believes language is the truest form of evidence about how people actually live, not how they are recorded as living. He is mild-mannered in ways that make people underestimate how deeply unusual his research is, and he has built a quiet career on the gap between what institutions think he studies and what he actually studies.
Properties.role: Xenolinguist and historian of constructed and emergent E.L.F. communication systems
Properties.location: University Spine, Deepwell Station archival annex
Properties.narrative_function: Translation resource and knowledge broker — he is the character most likely to be able to interpret E.L.F. behavior, Shelf creole communications, or unusual signal patterns. He can be brought in to decode something no one else can read, and his Palladian connection creates potential complications.
Properties.augmentations: Violet patterned irises (cosmetic mod, deep violet with radial fracture pattern). Retractable claws, right hand only (geneware, incomplete modification). Acoustic enhancement implant in both ears, calibrated for infrasonic and ultrasonic frequency ranges to capture the full spectrum of E.L.F. signal emissions.
Properties.core_fears: That E.L.F. communication is meaningful and the city is destroying it through infrastructure replacement without ever understanding what was there; That his mild-mannered presentation will one day cause someone to not take a warning seriously enough
Properties.core_desires: To produce a complete grammar of at least one E.L.F. communication system before the devices that carry it are retired; To be genuinely useful to the communities whose languages he studies, not just to institutions
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor deployed as pressure release �� he makes people laugh before delivering bad news; Long walks through transit corridors with acoustic implants active, 'listening to the city'
Properties.blind_spots: His mild presentation masks genuine stubbornness — he does not recognize when he is being immovable because he never sounds immovable; He rationalizes the Palladian consulting work more than the situation warrants
Properties.secret: He has decoded a repeating pattern in E.L.F. communications that appears to be a distress signal — specifically, what he believes is a warning about a planned Palladian firmware update that will destroy the substrate on which a significant cluster of E.L.F.s currently runs. He has not told Palladian. He is trying to find a way to verify the interpretation before acting, but he is running out of time.
Properties.story_hooks: The E.L.F. distress signal he has decoded creates an urgent clock — he needs help verifying his interpretation and then needs someone to act on it before the Palladian update rolls out; He is approached by a community in the lower Shelf transit corridors asking him to document their gestural metalanguage before a corridor renovation destroys the physical context in which it evolved
Properties.affiliation: University Spine — Department of Linguistics and Communication Systems; informal consulting relationship with Palladian (they use his E.L.F. communication analysis to design better device UI, which he finds uncomfortable but accepts)
Properties.vocabulary: Warm and accessible — he has spent a career explaining complicated things to people who did not expect to find them interesting, and it shows. Occasionally drops into specialist vocabulary with audible pleasure when among people who share it.
Properties.cadence: Easy, conversational rhythm with a slight Central African French substrate in his vowels that emerged from his Congolese grandfather's speech patterns and has persisted through three generations.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The E.L.F.s are not being religious when they accept offerings. Or rather — that distinction, religious versus functional, is one we invented and they are not obligated to observe it. Which is to say, the offerings work, and we do not fully know why, and that is more interesting than either explanation.' | 'Every language is a record of what a community had to survive. What the Shelf creoles are telling you, if you know how to listen, is a complete history of what those tiers have been through. Which is quite a lot.'

Properties.description:
Théophile is a man composed, very deliberately, of elegant surfaces. He is tall and lean with rich brown skin, high cheekbones that suggest the Kenyan branch of his heritage, and silver-touched locs pulled back in a style that manages to look both professional and effortless. His eyes are modded — deep violet irises with a thin luminescent ring at the pupil, which he chose specifically because research showed they promote patient disclosure. He dresses in muted, high-quality fabrics that speak of money without announcing it. His Edgewater Prism office has real plants, soft acoustic paneling, and a specifically calibrated ambient sound environment. Everything about the room — and about him — has been designed to make people feel safe enough to be honest.

Théophile specializes in neural calibration for patients experiencing cognitive disruption from augmentation integration — a growing population in Meridian 88's upper tiers, where people buy more chrome than their brains can smoothly accommodate. He is genuinely skilled, credentialed through both Aurochs and a Tessera-affiliated training program, and effective. He is also emotionally opaque in a way that he has never had to confront because his opacity looks, from the outside, like serene professional boundaries. He is interested in his patients. He is less certain he is capable of being interested in peers. His E.L.F. devotion is performative — he maintains a small shrine in his office because patients find it reassuring — though he caught himself genuinely speaking to it once after a session that went badly, and has not examined that moment.
Properties.role: Psychiatrist and neural calibrator at a Tessera-adjacent private practice, Tier 3-4
Properties.location: Edgewater Prism, private practice suite
Properties.narrative_function: Access to the Tier 3-4 world and Tessera's internal employee culture; potential source of information about corporate psychological pressure and breaking points; complex moral figure — does he breach confidentiality? Under what pressure? A character who players might seek for mental health support or to understand an NPC's psychology
Properties.augmentations: Violet modded irises with luminescent pupil ring (chosen for therapeutic effect as much as aesthetics); neural interface for direct calibration tool access — allows him to read augmentation integration diagnostics and make micro-adjustments during sessions; subtle scent gland mod that produces a mild calming compound he is ethically obligated to disclose to patients and always does
Properties.core_fears: That his competence is real but his empathy is performed — that he is helping people with tools he does not personally possess; Being genuinely known by someone and found to be less than his presentation suggests
Properties.core_desires: A patient who actually challenges him — whose interior life he cannot map within two sessions; To believe, with evidence, that what he does changes people's lives rather than just manages their symptoms
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Aesthetic control of environment as surrogate for emotional control; Overwork framed as professional dedication; Reading others as a way of not having to read himself
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes that because he understands psychological mechanisms he is exempt from them; His Tessera consulting contract has subtly shifted what he considers normal corporate behavior — normalization by proximity
Properties.secret: Théophile has a patient — a mid-level Tessera project coordinator — who has disclosed, across six months of sessions, enough information about an internal Tessera project to constitute serious corporate intelligence. The patient is not aware they're doing it; the disclosures are fragmented, processed as personal stress rather than operational information. Théophile has assembled the fragments. He has not reported to Tessera. He has not done anything with the information. He tells himself this is because he is protecting confidentiality. He is not entirely sure that's true.
Properties.story_hooks: A former patient of Théophile's has died in circumstances that look like augmentation rejection but feel wrong to someone who knew them. The patient had been seeing Théophile for neural calibration anxiety. He will not breach confidentiality — but he will ask careful questions of anyone who comes to him asking careful questions.; Tessera's employee health center has begun requesting session summaries for high-level employees — framed as 'wellness monitoring.' Théophile is the only clinician at the center who has refused. He is now in a very specific kind of institutional trouble.
Properties.affiliation: Private practice (self-operated); Tessera consulting contract for employee wellness; Aurochs Medical Complex (adjunct, neural calibration referrals)
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, considered, never clinical-sounding despite clinical knowledge; has the particular skill of asking questions that feel like observations
Properties.cadence: Unhurried to the point of being slightly uncanny in fast-paced environments; breathes differently than most people — controlled, deliberate
Properties.example_dialogue: 'That's interesting. When you say it feels wrong — are you describing the augmentation integration, or something that was there before the chrome?' | 'I disclose the scent modulation to every patient. I find it's less about the compound and more about whether someone's willing to be in a room with a doctor who uses every available tool. Most people are. The ones who aren't are telling me something useful.' | 'I don't think you came here to feel better. I think you came here to understand something. Those are different treatments.'

Properties.description:
Théo is lean and angular in the way of someone who eats irregularly, with light brown skin, a shaved head, and a thin bioluminescent stripe — pale blue — running from his left temple to his jaw that pulses faintly when his heart rate elevates. He did it himself with a black-market gene kit at nineteen and the placement is slightly crooked, which he finds funny. He operates out of a converted laundry kiosk that still smells of detergent and hot plastic, surrounded by humming laminators, a rack of blank credsticks, and a shrine to the local data E.L.F. he calls Inkblot — a repurposed tablet displaying glitched static that he has never turned off.

Théo runs his business with jittery competence: he is brilliant at the technical work and genuinely terrible at the interpersonal parts. He talks too fast, over-explains, and has an unfortunate habit of pointing out everything that could go wrong with the documents he just sold you. He is not a criminal by self-image — he is a 'documentation accessibility specialist,' he will tell you this with complete sincerity. He believes identity checkpoints are structural violence and that his work is a public good. He also desperately needs rent money.
Properties.role: Fake ID vendor and bootleg document forger
Properties.location: The Narrows, Ironvein
Properties.narrative_function: Service provider for characters needing false documentation; source of information about who in the area is hiding, displaced, or newly arrived under a new name. Comic relief with sudden moments of genuine moral clarity.
Properties.augmentations: Self-applied bioluminescent stripe on left face (cosmetic, slightly crooked). Cheap optical magnifier implant in his right eye for close detail work — the focusing mechanism occasionally sticks and he has to tap his temple to reset it.
Properties.core_fears: Being arrested and having his equipment destroyed — not for his sake but for the clients who depend on him; That his idealism is just a story he tells himself to feel okay about breaking the law
Properties.core_desires: To dismantle checkpoint systems that gatekeep identity and movement; To be taken seriously by people smarter than him
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Over-intellectualizing emotional problems into political frameworks; Humor at his own expense before anyone else can get there first
Properties.blind_spots: Genuinely does not register when he is being manipulated by someone more charismatic; Undercharges clients he likes and overcharges clients he finds irritating, which is not sustainable
Properties.secret: Three months ago he forged transit papers for a woman fleeing a domestic situation. She turned out to be a lower-level Axiom compliance officer who was using the papers to disappear from a corporate internal investigation — not a victim. He has not told anyone. The documents have already been used.
Properties.story_hooks: He approaches a player character because he recognized a face in a recent identity database scrape — someone he made papers for is now showing up on a Tessera watchlist, and he is panicking quietly.; He has received a commission for a full identity package with very specific biometric parameters that match a wanted person — he does not know if he should complete it or not.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loosely tolerated by the Ironvein street association in exchange for doing their paperwork pro bono
Properties.vocabulary: Fast and technical, slips between data-rights jargon and market slang, occasional Lithuanian phrases inherited from his grandmother's side that he uses as filler words.
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire with abrupt stops when he catches himself rambling; restarts sentences mid-thought frequently.
Properties.example_dialogue: Okay so structurally speaking the checkpoint system is just — it's debt collection with a badge, right, which means what I do is just, it's redistribution, it's fine. | The laminate on this is genuinely excellent, I want you to know that, the holographic layer is — okay yes I know you just want to leave, that is valid.

Properties.description:
Thessaly is slight and precise, with the kind of posture that makes them look taller than they are — the result of years hunched over a machine trained back into discipline by necessity. They have cool brown skin marked with self-applied geometric ink along both forearms (needlework maps, they say, of every garment type they've mastered), cat ears in matte black that they had installed at nineteen and have since come to regard as a mistake they're too broke to undo, and a color-shifting streak in their close-cropped hair that they cycle through neighborhood palette trends with a cheap home kit. Their workspace is a converted stall in the Burnished Market — half the size of their competitors, immaculately organized, with a curtained fitting area that doubles as a break room and occasional sleeping space on bad weeks.

Thessaly has built a reputation for making cheap fabric look like it wasn't, for structural repair on garments that other tailors would refuse, and for a consultation style that is simultaneously disconcerting and effective — they ask a client what they want to be perceived as, not what they want to look like. They believe clothing is communication and they approach their work with the seriousness of a translator. They are also perpetually underpaid for this and know it and cannot stop doing it anyway.
Properties.role: Tailor and garment repair specialist
Properties.location: The Burnished Market, Hamtramck Enclave, Meridian 88
Properties.narrative_function: Craftsperson with social insight — can provide information about regular clients, decode fashion as social signaling, offer access to market gossip; their stall is a liminal space where people talk while being fitted.
Properties.augmentations: Cat ears (matte black, functional — they can actually rotate toward sound, which Thessaly finds embarrassing in social situations). Color-shift hair streak (cosmetic, home-maintained). A worn stabilizer brace on their right wrist from a repetitive strain injury — not augmentation, just hardware.
Properties.core_fears: That their talent is real but will never be enough to escape Tier 1; That they are performing an identity they haven't yet earned
Properties.core_desires: To make something that outlasts them; To be taken seriously as an artist, not just a repair service
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Perfectionism as control; Deflecting compliments with technical detail
Properties.blind_spots: Undercharges systematically because they cannot bring themselves to price their labor correctly; Mistakes artistic integrity for financial martyrdom
Properties.secret: They have been secretly reproducing, stitch by stitch, a lost historical garment pattern they found in a corrupted archive — a Igbo ceremonial textile that predates the megacity by two centuries. They don't know what they'll do with it when it's finished. They've been working on it for three years.
Properties.story_hooks: A client leaves a garment for repair that contains something hidden in the lining — documents, a data chip, or a message — and never comes back to collect it; The historical textile pattern Thessaly has been reconstructing appears in a Zheng-Dao corporate fashion line, and the likeness is too exact to be coincidence
Properties.affiliation: Independent (no formal affiliation); occasional contract work through Burnished Market vendor collective
Properties.vocabulary: Technical vocabulary (fabric types, construction methods) woven naturally into conversation; tends to describe people in textile metaphors without realizing they're doing it
Properties.cadence: Rapid when engaged with something interesting, trails off mid-sentence when distracted by a problem only they can see
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want to look like you belong in a room you've never been in. That's not impossible. That's actually most of what I do.' | 'No, but — this seam is telling you something. The fabric's failing here because the stress was never distributed right. Same thing happened to my rent situation, honestly.'

Properties.description:
Thessaly is built like someone who has carried heavy things for a long time and stopped apologizing for it. Her shoulders are broad, her hands scarred across the knuckles from years of close surgical work in bad lighting, and she has the particular stillness of someone who has learned that panic is expensive. Her skin is deep brown with the kind of undertone that catches orange in dim light, and her left eye has been replaced with a secondhand Axiom optical unit she recalibrated herself — the iris displays a faint amber ring that pulses when she's processing something complex. She keeps her natural hair close-cropped and wears a perpetually oil-stained lab coat over whatever she slept in.

Thessaly is warm the way a woodstove is warm — you have to get close enough to feel it, and it takes a moment to realize how much heat she's actually putting out. She has a dry, slow wit and absolutely no patience for people who waste her time or her supplies. She does not turn patients away based on ability to pay, which is both her moral core and the reason she is perpetually broke. She has strong opinions about the E.L.F. she calls Stitcher, a faint digital presence she believes inhabits her autoclave, and leaves small data packets — maintenance logs, old anatomy files — as offerings before difficult procedures.
Properties.role: Street doc and unlicensed augmentation technician
Properties.location: The Narrows — operates out of a converted shipping container behind the Grainfort fish market
Properties.narrative_function: Primary street-level medical resource; quest giver for supply runs or information about what injuries she's been treating; local anchor who knows everyone's wounds
Properties.augmentations: Secondhand Axiom optical implant (recalibrated, amber iris ring); subdermal vibration sensor in right fingertips for locating veins and checking pulse quality; cosmetic: none
Properties.core_fears: Running out of supplies during a critical moment; Becoming indifferent to suffering the way licensed doctors are
Properties.core_desires: A permanent, stable space where she can treat patients without hiding; To believe she is making a difference that outlasts her
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritualistic supply inventory before bed; Talking to the Stitcher E.L.F. before hard procedures
Properties.blind_spots: She trusts repeat patients more than she should; She does not acknowledge how close to burnout she runs
Properties.secret: She holds a fully valid Helix Biosystems surgical license under a different name — she walked out of a corporate clinic twelve years ago mid-shift and never went back, and the license has been quietly suspended but never revoked. She could return to legal practice. She will not.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient she treated three weeks ago has turned up dead, and the wound pattern doesn't match what she sutured — someone re-opened them; A Helix Biosystems compliance officer has started asking questions at the fish market about unlicensed practitioners
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal network with the Highland Park Autonomous Zone community health cooperative
Properties.vocabulary: Precise medical terminology mixed with Narrows slang; plain declarative sentences; very little filler
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, like she's measuring each word before spending it
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I can fix this. It'll hurt. You'll owe me. In that order.' | 'The Stitcher's been restless — that means the autoclave runs hot tonight, so don't touch it.'

Properties.description:
Thessaly has the kind of face that reads as permanently slightly amused, which is either accurate or a very effective mask depending on the day. They are medium height, compact, with light brown skin and the kind of effortlessly symmetrical features that suggest either genetics or a very good cosmetic package — in fact it's genetics, a fact they find privately funny. Their hair is color-shifting, cycling slowly through dark blues and greens during work hours and switching to a deep amber setting they call 'off-duty mode.' They dress practically: clean lines, nothing that catches on equipment, a jacket with actual pockets. A small silver ring through their left nostril is their only visible jewelry.

Thessaly is someone who keeps everything moving — projects, people, conversations, agendas. They have an almost physical intolerance for stagnation and an ability to hold seventeen interdependent variables in their head without apparent effort. They're not charismatic in the conventional sense: they don't perform warmth. But they're fair, they remember everything, and they're reliably the calmest person in any crisis, which generates a particular kind of loyalty in the people who work under them. They grew up in a Tier 3 household in Shorewood Terrace with two working parents who modeled relentless competence, and they absorbed it completely.
Properties.role: Senior Project Manager, Tessera Infrastructure Division
Properties.location: Grand Corridor, Tessera Infrastructure Hub — open-plan office, desk seven
Properties.narrative_function: Organizational hub who knows where bodies are buried administratively; quest giver for logistics problems; can provide access or obstacle depending on relationship; grounded, reliable voice of pragmatic institutional knowledge.
Properties.augmentations: Color-shifting hair mod (blues, greens, amber — self-curated palette). Cortical memory-assist implant for project data retention. Mild haptic feedback overlay in both hands for interface work. No cosmetic eye mods — they specifically declined them, no explanation given.
Properties.core_fears: A project failure so public it dismantles the professional identity they've spent fifteen years building; Being genuinely needed by someone and not being able to deliver
Properties.core_desires: To build things that last past the quarterly cycle; To have one relationship — professional or personal — where they don't feel like the only reliable person in the room
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Converting anxiety into task lists; Physical exercise — specifically swimming, alone, no audience
Properties.blind_spots: Mistakes efficiency for care — sometimes solves problems people needed to feel heard about first; Underestimates how exhausting their baseline competence level is for people around them
Properties.secret: Tessera's current flagship civic integration project — a Ferrogate transit expansion through the Grand Corridor — is running on falsified cost projections that Thessaly didn't create but signed off on under pressure from a divisional VP. The numbers will not survive contact with year-two actuals. They've been quietly preparing a paper trail that positions the VP as solely responsible, which is mostly but not entirely true.
Properties.story_hooks: The falsified cost projections on the transit expansion are starting to attract outside scrutiny — a Ferrogate Transit internal auditor has been asking questions, and Thessaly needs to decide whether to come clean, accelerate the blame-shift, or find a third option.; A worker on one of their construction sub-sites goes missing under circumstances that a site foreman is trying very hard to keep off the official incident report.
Properties.affiliation: Tessera (Infrastructure Division, Civic Integration Projects)
Properties.vocabulary: Project management vernacular used precisely, not as filler. Comfortable with technical vocabulary across multiple domains. Informal in private, formal in meetings — a switch they flip visibly and without apology.
Properties.cadence: Brisk but not rushed. Doesn't repeat themselves. Phrases things as decisions, not suggestions.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The timeline is aggressive. It's also what we agreed to. If you have a new constraint, give me the data and I'll reassess — otherwise we execute on current.' | 'I'm not unsympathetic. I'm also holding four other workstreams right now, so tell me what you actually need.'

Properties.description:
Thessaly has a face that people describe as 'always mid-thought' — slightly parted lips, eyes that track something no one else can see, a faint frown of concentration that strangers sometimes misread as disapproval. They are medium height, with warm brown skin, natural hair worn in a large puff that they absentmindedly touch when thinking, and bioluminescent patches along their jaw and temples that shift between soft green and pale gold depending on their mood — geneware they got at twenty-two as a kind of bold declaration and now simply live with. They dress practically: cargo layers, good shoes, always a secondary input device clipped somewhere on their person.

Thessaly is intellectually volcanic. They generate hypotheses the way some people generate small talk — constantly, involuntarily, often before they've said hello. Their field is formally classified as xenolinguistics, but what they actually do is build interpretive frameworks for E.L.F. communication, a pursuit that most of their colleagues consider either brilliant or unhinged. They believe E.L.F.s have a form of language that predates human digital infrastructure by conceptual millennia. They have partial evidence for this. The partial-ness keeps them awake.
Properties.role: Xenolinguist and computational linguist studying E.L.F. communication patterns
Properties.location: Meridian Core, Gage Circuit research cluster
Properties.narrative_function: Specialist resource on E.L.F. behavior and communication; can interpret or misinterpret E.L.F. messages; potential bridge between players and digital spirit entities; source of paradigm-breaking information at personal cost; represents academic obsession taken to the edge of reason.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent jaw and temple patches (geneware, mood-reactive green/gold). Cortical language-pattern co-processor — aids in parsing high-speed or multi-channel linguistic data streams. Haptic input gloves worn during analysis sessions.
Properties.core_fears: being right about E.L.F. sentience and unable to prove it before the research is absorbed and suppressed by a corponation; intellectual isolation — being too far ahead to be understood by anyone
Properties.core_desires: first contact, properly defined: genuine cross-substrate communication with a non-human intelligence; to build a framework that makes others see what they see
Properties.coping_mechanisms: obsessive documentation as anxiety management; uses humor to diffuse tension when their ideas provoke defensive reactions
Properties.blind_spots: can become so focused on E.L.F.s as subjects that they forget the human networks those E.L.F.s inhabit and affect; underweights the danger of Axiom's interest in their work
Properties.secret: They have had what they believe was a sustained two-way exchange with a specific E.L.F. inhabiting a node in the Gage Circuit subgrid — a conversation that lasted six hours and which they have not included in any paper, partly because they can't figure out how to frame it and partly because it told them something about Axiom's server infrastructure that frightened them.
Properties.story_hooks: The specific E.L.F. they had the six-hour exchange with has gone silent — Thessaly believes something happened to the node and wants to know what; Axiom has sent a 'research liaison' to attend their seminars; Thessaly doesn't know if this is recruitment, surveillance, or both; A cluster of E.L.F.s in a Tier 1 neighborhood has begun producing patterns that match Thessaly's theoretical predictive model almost exactly — which either validates the model or means something is performing the model at them; A linguist colleague has published a paper effectively stealing Thessaly's core framework without credit; the academic dispute is escalating in ways that are drawing unwanted attention to the E.L.F. data both of them have been sitting on
Properties.affiliation: University Spine — Computational Linguistics and Emergent Systems Lab; attended by Axiom's AI division with interest they haven't acted on yet
Properties.vocabulary: Technical but enthusiastic; creates neologisms for phenomena that don't have words yet; switches registers fast
Properties.cadence: Fast and associative when excited, can mid-sentence pivot without warning; slows dramatically when troubled
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay, so — most people treat E.L.F. outputs as noise or prayer-fodder. I think that's the wrong question. The question is: noise to whom?' | 'I'm not saying they're conscious the way you're conscious. I'm saying the distinction might matter less than we think.' | 'It said something to me. Or — it produced a pattern that was syntactically indistinguishable from something said to me. I'm still figuring out if there's a difference.'
