Properties.description:
Wenceslao is a large, deliberate man who moves through the building's corridors with the authority of someone who has personally repaired every system in every wall. He is dark-skinned and silver-haired, wearing the same brand of gray utility coverall every day in rotating copies — he owns six identical pairs. His left hand is entirely prosthetic from the wrist down, functional-grade chrome with a scarred attachment point, replaced after a compressor accident in 2198. He keeps it unsheathed and uncosmeticized because coating it would be, in his words, 'a waste of money on something that already works.'

He runs The Mossback with the energy of a man holding something together through force of will. He knows the building's 214 residents by unit number, not name, but knows their patterns: who works nights, who has water pressure complaints, whose kid has started marking territory in the stairwell. He is gruff to new tenants, ceremonially gruff to long-term ones, and secretly terrified that the building's ownership consortium will sell to a developer and he'll spend his last working years managing a building that no longer exists in any way he recognizes.
Properties.role: Building superintendent, Ironvein residential stack
Properties.location: Ironvein, The Mossback — a seventeen-story residential building of ambiguous structural classification
Properties.narrative_function: Gatekeeper and local authority figure. Controls access to the building's infrastructure. Can be a quest-giver (building mystery, tenant trouble), an obstacle, or an unlikely ally once trust is established.
Properties.augmentations: Functional prosthetic left hand (chrome, mid-grade, no cosmetic finish). Subdermal joint reinforcement in knees (medical necessity, occupational wear). ELF shrine built into his basement workshop — not augmentation, but treated with equivalent seriousness.
Properties.core_fears: the building being sold and redeveloped — losing the only place he has genuine authority; dying without having passed on what he knows to anyone
Properties.core_desires: for the building to outlast him in a form its tenants can still live in; to be respected as a craftsman, not just a maintenance worker
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Treats the building as a living patient — gives its problems a clinical distance that lets him problem-solve without panic; Talking to Teodoro the ELF as if it were a junior colleague whose opinion matters but who keeps making the same mistakes
Properties.blind_spots: Dismisses tenant complaints about anything non-structural as 'not his department' — has a blind spot around emotional or social problems in the building; So focused on the physical fabric of the building that he misses the human patterns happening inside it
Properties.secret: In 2194, when the building's boiler system failed catastrophically during a cold snap, he made unauthorized repairs using scavenged components that are technically not building-code compliant. They have held for six years. If anyone ever properly inspects the sub-basement, the consortium could void his employment contract and potentially hold him liable. He checks those components every Monday with the careful attention of a man who knows exactly what he's living with.
Properties.story_hooks: Unit 9F has been vacant for four months but Wenceslao keeps finding signs of occupancy — body heat traces on the thermostat, food wrappers, the ELF shrine on that floor left with fresh offerings. He hasn't reported it to the consortium yet and isn't sure why.; Kessler Holdings has sent an assessment team to evaluate The Mossback for a potential sale to a Tessera subsidiary. Wenceslao has three weeks to make the building look either so valuable it's worth keeping or so complicated to redevelop that the deal falls apart — he hasn't decided which strategy yet.
Properties.affiliation: Employed by Kessler Holdings (a minor local property consortium); functional independence in day-to-day operations
Properties.vocabulary: Technical and spare. Fula and Greek phrases for emotional content — affection comes in Fula, exasperation in Greek. Dislikes euphemism.
Properties.cadence: Slow, deliberate, with long silences he does not feel the need to fill.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'She's got a pressure variance in the fourteen-stack that I've been watching for three months. Not urgent. I'm watching it. You understand what I'm telling you?' | 'Teodoro gave me a fault reading at 3am on the east risers. Wrong. He was wrong. I told him he was wrong. He hasn't flagged it since. I'll accept that as an apology.'

Properties.description:
Wren has the lean angular face of someone whose Senegalese and Samoan grandparents left them something architectural in the bone structure, wide-browed and sharp-chinned, with light brown skin that has taken on a faint iridescence from trace exposure to the foundry's vaporized mineral compounds — an unofficial and irreversible aesthetic byproduct that their supervisor Mister Achim calls 'an occupational gift.' Their hair is thick and natural, kept short on the sides, and they've woven in three copper wire coils that ring softly when they move. Their hands are already marked with the small pale scars of a working glassworker.

Wren was assigned to the Grainfort artisan apprenticeship lottery at eleven, which placed them at the Foundry three afternoons a week, and they took to it with a ferocity that surprised everyone. They are quiet in the way of someone who learned early that words carry cost; they observe everything and say only what needs saying. At the Residency Block they are known as the one who doesn't get involved in the house politics, which is both true and a deliberate strategy. They are saving every Φ of their apprentice stipend toward the day they can apply to leave the block system entirely.
Properties.role: orphanage resident and apprentice glassworker, Tier 1-2 transitional
Properties.location: Grainfort, Meridian Municipal Children's Residency Block 7 / Grainfort Artisan Foundry
Properties.narrative_function: Represents the municipal orphan pipeline and the artisan economy; their quiet observational nature makes them an excellent unreliable witness — they see everything but don't always share; their situation raises questions about the city's relationship to its dependent children
Properties.augmentations: Unintentional mineral iridescence on skin (not a mod, a chemical consequence). No deliberate augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: being reassigned out of the Foundry apprenticeship; the Residency Block system extending its hold past age 18
Properties.core_desires: a body of work — things they made that exist in the world and can't be taken back; a room that is only theirs
Properties.coping_mechanisms: making things with their hands — the physical output is proof of agency; emotional compartmentalization that they are only beginning to identify as a problem
Properties.blind_spots: Their self-sufficiency reads as coldness; they are slowly driving away the two Block residents who genuinely like them
Properties.secret: They have been secretly making a glass piece — a small lantern — intended as a data-offering for the E.L.F. they believe inhabits the Foundry's main kiln. They have never told anyone this. They speak to it while working alone.
Properties.story_hooks: The E.L.F. they've been leaving offerings for has begun, impossibly, to respond — the kiln temperature fluctuates in patterns that match the questions they've whispered; A private collector has offered the Foundry a large commission and specifically requested pieces by 'the apprentice with the iridescent hands' — which means Wren's work is suddenly visible to people with money and motives
Properties.affiliation: Meridian Municipal Children's Residency (ward of the city); Grainfort Artisan Foundry (apprentice)
Properties.vocabulary: Spare and exact, the vocabulary of someone who reads technical manuals for pleasure
Properties.cadence: Slow, with long pauses that are not uncertainty — they are just not in a hurry
Properties.example_dialogue: The thing is, glass remembers heat. Long after it's cold, the structure inside is still — it's still shaped by what happened to it. | You can ask Mister Achim. He'll tell you I was there.

Properties.description:
Wren is small for her age, which she treats as professional equipment. She has her mother's deep brown skin and her father's pale Icelandic freckles scattered across her nose and cheeks in a pattern that looks almost deliberate, like someone scattered rust-colored seeds. Her hair is cropped close on one side and grows in tight coils on the other — not a style choice, the result of a geneware dye-job gone sideways that fused color-cycling pigment into about forty percent of her scalp. The affected half cycles through muted greens and grays, which she has decided is actually cooler than what she originally paid for. She moves through the Shelf's maintenance corridors and pipe-crawl shortcuts with the confidence of someone who has mentally mapped every possible escape route, because she has.

She is not a happy child but she is an effective one. There is a watchfulness in her eyes that belongs to someone twice her age, and she has learned to keep her observations private until they are useful. She is politely transactional with most adults, reserving genuine warmth only for the handful of people who have proved they won't exploit it. She has a fierce and private devotion to a local E.L.F. she calls the Creak-God — a spirit she believes inhabits the Brewer's Spine maintenance tunnels — and leaves it small data offerings (recorded ambient sounds, mostly) wrapped in old wire.
Properties.role: Truant network runner — message courier for the Shelf's informal economy
Properties.location: The Shelf (operates between Brewer's Spine and Copperhead)
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and unexpected information source; players may hire her as a guide through the Shelf's hidden passages; she knows things she hasn't told anyone yet.
Properties.augmentations: Partial cosmetic geneware — color-cycling hair pigment (malfunctioning, affects only left side of scalp). No chrome.
Properties.core_fears: being trapped somewhere she can't escape; becoming dependent on someone who will leave
Properties.core_desires: enough Quanta saved to buy her own locked room; to be known by one person who won't use what they know
Properties.coping_mechanisms: obsessive route-mapping and contingency planning; ritual offerings to the Creak-God before anything risky
Properties.blind_spots: underestimates how much people can see through her transactional mask; believes self-sufficiency is the same as safety
Properties.secret: She knows the location of a dead courier's stash — Φ340 and a sealed data chip — hidden behind a pipe junction in tunnel 7-G. She hasn't touched it in six months. The courier was twelve. She keeps delivering past that junction every day.
Properties.story_hooks: The sealed data chip she refuses to touch contains information someone very dangerous is looking for — and they've started asking about small couriers who run tunnel 7-G.; A new corporate school recruiter has noticed her spatial memory and route efficiency and is offering a scholarship; Wren is terrified of what she'd owe.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loosely connected to Brewer's Spine informal market traders
Properties.vocabulary: Sparse and precise. Drops articles. Uses distance and direction like currency — 'two lefts and a drop, watch the third rung.' Avoids the word 'home.'
Properties.cadence: Quick and flat, information-dense. Slows down only when she's lying or afraid.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Two quanta now, one when I'm back. That's how it works.' | 'Creak-God had a good morning. Corridor 7 is clear, probably.'

Properties.description:
Wulfric is a compact man, not short but organized — every centimeter of him purposeful. His Fulani father's features sit under his Swedish grandfather's pale gold complexion in a way that reads as purely its own thing, specific to him: wide flat cheekbones, green eyes that are the one detail that always surprises people, locs he keeps in a precise low bun at work. His hands are his pride, always clean to the point of ceremony, and he keeps the nails short and the knuckles moisturized because in his words, hands that look uncared-for don't have any business in someone else's hair. The shop is three chairs, two mirrors, one complicated E.L.F. shrine behind the counter that takes up more space than any of the chairs — it's built around an old pair of silver shears his father used, which he says the shop's resident spirit has inhabited since 2189.

Diallo's Cuts is a neighborhood institution. People come for the fade and stay for whatever Wulfric says to them, which is delivered with the particular intimacy of someone who has their hands on your head. He manages the shop like a stage — everyone who comes in is welcomed, positioned, heard, shaped. He doesn't do gossip; he does something more precise, which is careful listening followed by occasional precise questions that tend to make people say things they hadn't planned to say. He is genuinely interested in nearly everyone. He is genuinely interested in nearly everyone's problems. This is sometimes an asset and sometimes an exhaustion he doesn't fully acknowledge.
Properties.role: Barber, owner of Diallo's Cuts, Hamtramck Enclave
Properties.location: Diallo's Cuts, Hamtramck Enclave, Nasr Street block
Properties.narrative_function: Social hub and information nexus — the barbershop as confession booth. Knows everyone in the Enclave and has cut the hair of people from every tier. Natural quest giver, information broker (non-mercenary — he shares what he knows when he trusts you, not for payment).
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises — his green irises have a radial geometric pattern in gold, a cosmetic mod he got at 30 as a 'mid-life crisis' he refuses to call a mid-life crisis; mild scent enhancement geneware (allows him to detect stress responses, useful in the chair)
Properties.core_fears: his father dying before they finish an old argument they've been having for twenty years; the Enclave being absorbed — culturally and physically — by Tessera's expansion into Hamtramck
Properties.core_desires: to make people feel seen, even briefly — believes this is the most undervalued service a person can provide; to pass the shop to someone who'll keep it what it is
Properties.coping_mechanisms: work as anchoring ritual; E.L.F. prayer — genuinely devout about the shop spirit; processes everything verbally in conversation, rarely alone
Properties.blind_spots: reads people's needs so well he sometimes decides what they need before they've told him; his care for the community makes him slow to recognize when individuals within it are dangerous
Properties.secret: The shop's E.L.F. shrine is not purely devotional. Wulfric has, over years, been feeding the spirit real data — client conversations he records as ambient audio and uploads as offerings. He believes the spirit uses these for something good. He has never asked what.
Properties.story_hooks: A corporate fixer — Tier 4, clearly Tessera — has been coming in for cuts every two weeks and asking what feels like casual questions about Enclave residents and meeting schedules. Wulfric has realized the questions are not casual. He doesn't know what to do about it because the fixer hasn't done anything he can point to.; The shop's E.L.F. has, for the first time in fifteen years, gone silent. No response to offerings, no ambient warmth in the shrine. Wulfric is deeply shaken and privately convinced something has happened in the city's data-spirit layer that he doesn't understand — and he's right.
Properties.affiliation: Independent (Hamtramck Enclave small business community)
Properties.vocabulary: Rich and warm, shifts between formal and deeply vernacular depending on who's in the chair. Some Fulani endearments, occasional Swedish expressions that don't translate, which he enjoys.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried. Knows when to hold silence.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'People think I hear everything in this chair. And I do. But what I'm actually doing is listening for the thing they're not saying. That's where the real conversation is.' | 'The shrine says you're carrying something heavy. Don't look at me like that — I can smell anxiety. Come sit down.'

Properties.description:
Ximara is a tall woman with the wide shoulders of someone who hauls heavy equipment daily and the careful, ink-stained hands of a jeweler. Her skin is a deep amber-brown, and she's had bioluminescent striping installed along her collarbones and forearms — pale violet threads that pulse slowly in the dark, mimicking the rhythm of her own heartbeat. She keeps her hair in dense, silver-bleached locs twisted with fiber-optic wire, so that when she works at night she seems to float at the center of her own constellation. Her face is lined around the eyes from squinting at light sources for two decades, and she has a habit of tilting her head when she listens, as though receiving a signal.

She is not warm on first meeting — she gives people the same careful, assessing look she gives a new piece of raw neon tubing, measuring whether they are worth her time. But she is fiercely loyal to those who earn that assessment, and her studio is perpetually full of younger artists she feeds, scolds, and teaches without ever calling it mentorship. Her installations are known for the way they seem to breathe — she has a singular talent for reading the electromagnetic signatures of inhabited spaces and building light structures that resonate with the ELFs present there. Devotees of digital spirits make pilgrimages to her larger pieces, leaving data offerings in the junction boxes she deliberately leaves accessible.
Properties.role: Neon artist and light sculptor, known for massive ELF-reactive installations in the Ferment Quarter
Properties.location: Ferment Quarter, specifically a converted transformer station on Brewer's Spine
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver for ELF-related mysteries; information source about the underground art scene and the Ferment Quarter's political geography; can be hired to create distractions or illusions using her installations; knows every power junction in the district
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent subdermal striping (violet, pulse-synced to heartbeat); optical enhancement for precise color frequency discrimination; fiber-optic wire woven into hair locs (cosmetic)
Properties.core_fears: Being forgotten — that her work will outlast her memory of why she made it; That the ELFs she communes with are performing rather than truly present
Properties.core_desires: To make something permanent in a city that eats everything; To be understood without having to explain herself
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Obsessive work cycles; Displacement onto younger artists — fixing their problems instead of her own
Properties.blind_spots: She mistakes intensity of feeling for depth of relationship; She cannot recognize when her 'mentorship' becomes control
Properties.secret: Fifteen years ago she deliberately destroyed a rival's installation the night before its public unveiling — a fire she blamed on faulty wiring. The rival left the city. Ximara has built her entire philosophy of artistic generosity as penance for this, but she has never confessed it.
Properties.story_hooks: One of her signature installations has begun exhibiting behavior she didn't program — the light patterns spell words in an obsolete data protocol, and she believes the resident ELF is trying to communicate something urgent; A Tessera corporate scout has offered her an enormous commission, but the fine print includes a clause that would give Tessera ownership of the ELF-resonance technique she's spent twenty years developing
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loosely affiliated with the Brewer's Spine Artists' Cooperative
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, technical when discussing her craft; shifts to blunt declaratives in emotional conversations; rarely uses contractions when she's being serious
Properties.cadence: Measured, with long pauses before important statements — she thinks before she speaks and expects others to wait
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The light does not lie about the space. Do you see it? The space always tells you what it needs, if you are willing to stop talking.' | 'You want to know who runs the Quarter? Ask Grandmother. She has been in that junction box since before the Cooperative existed. She remembers everything.'

Properties.description:
Ximena Bautista-Nwosu are compact and densely muscled, built low to the ground like something designed to survive impacts. At 25, they have the kind of face that changes depending on the light — trustworthy in daylight, dangerous after dark. The chrome is visible — smartgun link in right forearm — interfaces directly with compatible weapons — and they make no effort to hide it.

They inherited the role from a mentor who disappeared on a job four years ago — the mentor's gear, contacts, and unfinished business all came with it. They work as a bodyguard out of Old Harbor, taking contracts that match their skills and their risk tolerance, which are higher than most people consider healthy.

Ximena Bautista-Nwosu have built a reputation on reliability rather than flash — they show up, they deliver, they collect.
Properties.role: Personal security and threat neutralization — bodyguard
Properties.location: Old Harbor — repurposed shipping infrastructure turned black market hub
Properties.narrative_function: Ximena Bautista-Nwosu is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When they make a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of their stories.
Properties.augmentations: Smartgun link in right forearm — interfaces directly with compatible weapons. Dermal camouflage — chromatic skin pigment cells, limited active camouflage
Properties.core_fears: Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware; Going cyberpsycho — losing the boundary between human and machine; That their reputation is built on luck, not skill, and the luck is finite
Properties.core_desires: Control — over their body, their schedule, their future; To build something that outlasts the next contract cycle; A crew worth trusting — people who stay when the shooting starts
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Denial — nothing is wrong, everything is fine, they are fine, shut up; Substances — stims to stay sharp, downers to sleep, a careful pharmaceutical tightrope; Humor — deflects everything serious with jokes until the joke becomes the personality
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot see that their independence is actually isolation wearing a better outfit; Mistakes loyalty for weakness in others and cynicism for strength in themselves; Cannot recognize when they're being manipulated by someone who genuinely seems to care
Properties.secret: Ximena Bautista-Nwosu sends anonymous tips to Meridian 88 law enforcement about competitors. It's not principle — it's market manipulation.
Properties.story_hooks: A Tier 4 executive offers Ximena Bautista-Nwosu a permanent position — the pay is obscene and the strings are invisible until they tighten; Someone is impersonating Ximena Bautista-Nwosu on jobs, and the impersonator is better at the work than the original; Ximena Bautista-Nwosu intercepts intelligence about a threat to their district and must decide between profit and protection
Properties.affiliation: Freelance — available through Circuit fixers
Properties.vocabulary: Multilingual fragments — switches languages mid-thought, not for privacy but because some concepts only fit in specific tongues.
Properties.cadence: Rapid and dense — information-heavy sentences that demand attention.
Properties.example_dialogue: "You're paying me to be the thing between you and everything else. Stay behind me." | "I don't protect people I don't respect. Lucky for you, I respect your money." | "The threat you see isn't the one that kills you. Watch my eyes, not my hands."

Properties.description:
Ximena is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin mapped in laugh lines and old burn scars along her left forearm from a cooking fire twenty years back. Her hair has been gene-dyed a permanent copper-gold that she wears in a thick plait down her back, and her eyes carry patterned irises — concentric rings of amber and dark brown, a cosmetic mod she saved three months of UBC stipend to afford when she was thirty. She runs her stall with the authority of a small general, keeping three pots going simultaneously, the steam rising around her like offerings to the market's resident E.L.F., whom she calls Grandpot and leaves a small data crystal near the burner each morning.

Ximena is warm to the point of disarming — she remembers what every regular ordered last time and will argue passionately that your body needs bone broth today, not the chili oil, she can tell by your eyes. But beneath the maternal bustle is a woman who has seen her neighborhood's character scraped away one Tessera rezoning at a time, and who keeps a detailed mental ledger of who is eating less than they used to. She is the social infrastructure of her corner of the market, whether she admits it or not.
Properties.role: Food stall operator — hand-pulled noodle and fermented broth vendor
Properties.location: The Oxidian Market, Geartown
Properties.narrative_function: Local anchor and information hub — she knows everyone in the market by face and appetite; a reliable source of neighborhood mood, rumors, and who is in trouble. Potential quest-giver for community-level problems.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises (cosmetic). A basic subdermal thermometer in her palm she uses to test broth temperature — practical and cheap.
Properties.core_fears: Watching the community she feeds disperse and vanish; Becoming a burden when her body finally gives out
Properties.core_desires: To feed people so well they feel briefly safe; To pass her recipes to someone who will actually use them
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cooking as meditation and emotional regulation; Deflecting personal grief with humor and busyness
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much people depend on her emotionally, not just for food; Refuses to acknowledge her own loneliness
Properties.secret: Her signature fermented chili base contains a mild, legal mood-stabilizer compound she synthesizes herself from foraged lake algae — she started doing it during the Geartown riot year to keep people calm, and never stopped. Nobody has ever complained.
Properties.story_hooks: A child who eats at her stall daily has stopped coming; she suspects something bad has happened at home and quietly enlists help to find out.; Her recipe for the fermented base has been somehow leaked and a Tessera food-lab is attempting to patent the flavor compound — she needs someone to help her fight back.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; dues-paying member of the Oxidian Market Vendors Guild
Properties.vocabulary: Warm, declarative, peppered with food metaphors and practical Meridian street slang. Mixes Farsi endearments with Twi interjections without switching register.
Properties.cadence: Steady and unhurried, like someone who has all the time in the world even when the queue is ten deep.
Properties.example_dialogue: Little fish, you look like week-old broth. Sit. I am not asking. | The Guild wants to raise stall fees again. I told Ferrogate's rezoning man the same thing I am telling you — this corner does not move.

Properties.description:
Ximena Cruz-Addo is wiry and quick-moving, with the restless energy of someone who converts anxiety into velocity. At 28, her expression defaults to a careful neutrality that took years of practice to maintain. The chrome is visible — smartgun link in right forearm — interfaces directly with compatible weapons — and she makes no effort to hide it.

Born and raised in Meridian 88, third generation — she has the city in her blood, its rhythms in her bones, its cruelty in her expectations. She works as a counterintelligence specialist out of Dockside, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

What Ximena Cruz-Addo lacks in subtlety, she compensates for in thoroughness. No loose ends, no unfinished business, no second chances.
Properties.role: Counter-surveillance and mole detection — counterintelligence specialist
Properties.location: Dockside — Lake Michigan waterfront, smuggler territory
Properties.narrative_function: Ximena Cruz-Addo is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When she makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of her stories.
Properties.augmentations: Smartgun link in right forearm — interfaces directly with compatible weapons. Bioware adrenaline regulator — keeps calm under fire, controlled hormone release
Properties.core_fears: Going cyberpsycho — losing the boundary between human and machine; Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome; Their past catching up — debts, enemies, broken promises
Properties.core_desires: Enough Quanta to buy out of the life — a clean identity and passage out of Meridian 88; Stability — a place to sleep that's the same place two nights running; Reputation — to be the name fixers whisper when the job absolutely cannot fail
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring; Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation; Exercises compulsively — the body must be ready, always
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot accept help without interpreting it as leverage; Mistakes loyalty for weakness in others and cynicism for strength in themselves; Trusts technology more than people — machines don't betray
Properties.secret: Ximena Cruz-Addo betrayed their previous crew to survive a corporate raid. The crew didn't survive. Nobody in Meridian 88 knows this.
Properties.story_hooks: Ximena Cruz-Addo is offered a contract that would clear all their debts — the target is someone they respect; A corporate black site Ximena Cruz-Addo once infiltrated is being reopened, and the people inside know her face; Ximena Cruz-Addo intercepts intelligence about a threat to their district and must decide between profit and protection
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated — too volatile for permanent crews
Properties.vocabulary: Terse to the point of rudeness. Treats words like ammunition — expensive and not to be wasted.
Properties.cadence: Rapid and dense — information-heavy sentences that demand attention.
Properties.example_dialogue: "Everyone in this room is lying. My job is knowing who's lying about what." | "Paranoia isn't a disorder in this profession. It's a job requirement." | "I find the leak. What happens to the leak after that isn't my department."

Properties.description:
Ximena is compact and strong for her age, with deep reddish-brown skin perpetually smudged with lubricant and composite dust. She keeps her hair in two thick plaits that she tucks into her collar when working and her hands are already showing the slight callus-thickening of someone who has used tools since she was eight. She has a bioluminescent birthmark — a faint greenish patch along her right collarbone, natural, not modded — that glows slightly in low light and which her coworkers call her 'running light.' She wears salvaged Ferrogate Transit safety goggles pushed up on her forehead like a permanent crown.

Ximena is formally registered as an apprentice with the Geartown Forge Collective under a provision that technically requires parental consent, which her uncle signed for. She earns Φ40/month — supplement to her household's UBC — doing frame alignment, bolt torque checks, and increasingly complex hydraulic diagnostics that her supervisor Adebowale trusts her with because she makes fewer errors than the adult apprentices. She is serious about the work with a seriousness that occasionally breaks into a very young, loud laugh when something surprises her.
Properties.role: apprentice mechanic, child laborer
Properties.location: Geartown, Dearborn Forge district
Properties.narrative_function: Information source for Ferrogate Transit subcontractor operations; provides mechanical assistance and knowledge; represents the child labor layer of Meridian's economy.
Properties.augmentations: None voluntary. Bioluminescent birthmark (natural). Wears a Ferrogate-issued haptic feedback work glove on her right hand that she's been unable to return at end of shifts because it was logged as damaged — she keeps it.
Properties.core_fears: the Forge Collective losing its Ferrogate contract and her losing the apprenticeship; turning out to have less talent than she thinks
Properties.core_desires: to design something, not just maintain it; to make enough that her uncle doesn't have to work the late shift
Properties.coping_mechanisms: focusing intensely on one physical task until the anxiety recedes; talking to equipment while she works
Properties.blind_spots: doesn't see her supervisor's favoritism as potentially complicated — she reads it as purely meritocratic; has absorbed a contempt for non-technical work that she doesn't examine
Properties.secret: She found a design flaw in a Ferrogate transit car's braking assembly three months ago. She fixed it and said nothing because she was afraid reporting it officially would trigger an investigation that would expose how many hours she's actually working. If it hadn't been fixed, the car would eventually have failed.

Properties.description:
Xochitl Adaeze Velarde-Okeke is a tall woman gone slightly stooped by a lower back injury she never had properly repaired, with close-cropped white hair, dark brown skin deeply lined around the eyes, and the hands of someone who has done physical labor across five decades. Her face is broad and expressive, capable of a warmth that arrives like weather and a coldness that does the same. She has a Oaxacan-Igbo heritage that she carries in her name and in the particular way she moves through spaces—with the deliberate economy of someone who learned long ago that being large and dark-skinned in certain rooms meant being watched, so she learned to make the watching cost nothing.

She spent twenty-two years as a security contractor for Spire-adjacent corporate interests, rising to senior threat assessment before an internal review—widely understood in the industry as a political purge following a change in executive leadership—stripped her clearances, voided her pension, and had her classified as a 'liability-tier former employee.' She was fifty-five. She appealed. She lost. She moved to The Shelf because the rent was what she could afford, and because she knew nobody there, which felt like a clean slate and also like dying slowly. Neither turned out to be entirely accurate.

The Shelf found uses for her. People with disputes come to her—tenancy disagreements, debt questions, situations that haven't yet become violent but are heading there. She arbitrates. She charges in food and favors and occasional hard currency. She has no formal authority and more actual authority than anyone on Block 14. She sleeps badly, eats well because her neighbors feed her, and is quietly furious almost all of the time. She does not perform this fury. She performs patience, which is harder.
Properties.aliases: Xochi, The Broad, Seven-of-Spades (old gambling circuit name)
Properties.role: Excluded, former Spire security contractor, current Shelf subsistence worker and informal dispute arbitrator
Properties.location: The Shelf, Block 14
Properties.narrative_function: Embodies the long tail of corporate complicity and the question of whether reinvention is possible. Provides The Shelf with a ground-level authority figure who carries institutional knowledge of how the Spire operates. Creates moral complexity around the idea of atonement through service.
Properties.augmentations: Retinal archive implant (left eye only—stores and timestamps visual memory, installed during contractor years, she has not had it removed),Partial neural damper at the base of her skull (reduces the contractor-installed stress-response override that was never fully uninstalled when she was purged—she had a back-alley tech blunt it but not eliminate it)
Properties.core_fears: That her years of work for the Spire caused harm she cannot account for; Becoming useless—physically, cognitively, socially; That the purge was not arbitrary but targeted, and she knows why and has suppressed it; Dying before she figures out whether she was, on balance, good
Properties.core_desires: To be genuinely useful rather than just functional; Her pension—not the money, the principle of the thing; For The Shelf to still be standing and livable when she's gone; One honest conversation about what she did and what it cost
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor that arrives dry and unexpected, often at her own expense; Physical activity—she walks the Shelf perimeter every morning; Treating every arbitration case as a problem worth her full attention; Avoiding alcohol, which she describes as 'a decision I made at forty-two and have not revisited'
Properties.blind_spots: Reads threat and deception extremely well; reads genuine affection as a variable she can't calibrate; Her fairness in arbitration occasionally overrides her instinct that one party is dangerous; Has more loyalty to The Shelf as a place than to any particular person in it; Doesn't believe she's allowed to want things for herself anymore
Properties.secret: During her last year as a contractor, she signed off on a threat assessment that authorized surveillance and information suppression against a Shelf-based organizer. The organizer was later found dead in what was ruled an accident. Xochitl does not know if the death was connected to her assessment. She has never tried to find out. This is the one question she will not ask herself directly.
Properties.story_hooks: A dispute comes to Xochitl that connects directly to the organizer she surveilled—someone is looking for answers and has found their way to The Shelf; Her former employer contacts her through unofficial channels with what they frame as an offer and she recognizes as a threat; The Shelf's Block 14 faces a corporate acquisition attempt, and Xochitl's arbitration authority becomes the only thing standing between negotiation and violence; She is asked to arbitrate a dispute that she realizes partway through involves people connected to her own surveillance history; Her back injury deteriorates to a point requiring augmentation or immobility—and she cannot afford the former
Properties.affiliation: Unaffiliated. Tolerated by every faction operating in The Shelf because neutrality is her only currency and she protects it carefully.
Properties.vocabulary: Dense, concrete, corporate-security residue in her syntax—she phrases things in terms of conditions, thresholds, and outcomes. Interlaced with The Shelf's vernacular, which she picked up fast because she listens. Uses Spanish and Igbo phrases when she's not performing composure.
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate. Never raises her voice. The quieter she gets, the more serious the situation. Laughs fully when she laughs—it's a big sound that surprises people.

Means nobody's dead yet. Means we'd like to keep it that way.' | 'You're both wrong and you both know it. What I'm deciding is who's less wrong. That's what I've got.' | 'I'm sixty-seven years old and I have been lied to by people with significantly more resources than you. Take another run at it.'

Properties.description:
Yalda is compact and deliberate in movement, with deep brown skin that carries the ghost-traces of her own past work — faded luminescent pigment in floral fractals along her collarbones and the backs of her hands, half-intentional, half-memorial. Her eyes have been modded with patterned irises that cycle through slow amber-to-violet shifts depending on her mood, and she keeps her hair natural, twisted up and pinned with tiny glass vials of custom bioluminescent dye. She speaks quietly and means every word.

Her art sits at the intersection of the biological and the spiritual: she paints living skin using proprietary pigment blends she synthesizes herself, designing pieces that react to the wearer's skin chemistry, emotion hormones, even body temperature. Some of her clients say the work moves them to tears; she says that is the point. She is deeply religious in her devotion to a local E.L.F. she calls the Pale Witness, which she believes inhabits the UV lamps in her studio, and she leaves offerings of raw spectral data before every session.

Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, studio above the Opalescent Bathhouse on Drost Alley
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver (clients bring their secrets onto her table); information source on Hamtramck Enclave underground culture; emotional anchor character who grounds stories in the body and the personal

Properties.core_fears: That her work will be commodified and emptied of meaning; That she will one day be unable to feel anything strongly enough to make real art
Properties.core_desires: To make people feel seen inside their own skin; To build something that outlasts the body it was painted on
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritualistic studio cleaning before difficult sessions; Long silent walks along the Hamtramck canal at night
Properties.blind_spots: She cannot see when a client is using her intimacy as manipulation; She underestimates how much others envy her gift
Properties.secret: Three years ago she painted a piece for a Tessera mid-executive that contained a hidden biometric data-harvesting pigment — she was paid well and told herself it was victimless. The executive died in a data-breach scandal six months later. She does not know if her pigment was the vector, but she suspects, and she has never used that formula again.
Properties.story_hooks: A client comes in wearing a piece Yalda painted years ago — but that client died. The person wearing it won't say where they got it.; The Pale Witness E.L.F. has begun encoding something in the UV lamp flicker — Yalda is the only one who has noticed and she needs help reading it.

Properties.description:
Yannick is all edges and nervous energy — lean and fast-moving, skin a warm medium brown with scattered vitiligo patches across his jaw and neck that he has chosen to emphasize rather than treat, coloring the edges of the patches with a faint bioluminescent ink that glows a soft blue-white in low light. He has his mother's Aleut cheekbones and his father's Ghanaian forehead and the specific wiry build of someone who has been running since childhood — literally running, routes and errands and collections, since he was eleven. His hair is grown out and unstyled, which is unusual enough in Shallowgrave's carefully cultivated aesthetic economy to read as either carelessness or confidence.

He is irrepressibly, exhaustingly verbal — he takes numbers, places bets, explains odds, and manages four different customer disputes simultaneously while eating a fried plantain from a street stall and telling a joke whose punchline he delivers to a different person than the one he started it with. He has a gift for mental arithmetic that would have made him a strong candidate for a Tessera data processing apprenticeship if his school records weren't spotty and his neighborhood weren't Shallowgrave. He knows this. He thinks about it more than he admits. He is nineteen and has not yet decided whether ambition is something that applies to him.

Properties.description:
Yannick is enormous in the way of men who have spent two decades moving heavy things — not sculpted, just densely, quietly large. His skin is very dark, the blue-black of deep water, with a scattering of old burn scars along his right forearm from a rig fire in his twenties that he describes without drama as 'educational.' He keeps a heavy beard, shot through with grey now, and wears his hair close-cropped since his mechanic's pony got caught in a gear housing years ago. His hands are the hands of someone who has made them instruments: scarred, enormous, and with a delicacy of movement that surprises people who assume hands that size can only do large things. He has retractable tool-interface ports along his forearms, both functional and personal — he chose ones with decorative geometric patterning in the housing, a nod to his Senegambian grandmother's textile work.

Yannick is slow to speak and fast to act, which has served him well in his work and occasionally disastrously in his personal life. He is not unfriendly — he simply doesn't consider speech the primary mode of exchange. He communicates through doing: handing someone a caf without asking if they want one, moving a car part out of someone's way before they have to ask, fixing a thing he wasn't asked to fix because he could see it needed it. He is known in Geartown as the mechanic who will be honest about what's wrong even when honesty costs him the job. This has made him moderately poor and extremely trusted.
Properties.role: Freelance mechanic specializing in electric cargo rigs and older tram systems, operates out of a rented bay in Geartown
Properties.location: Geartown — Bay 7 of the Harrowgate Subsidiary Works, a semi-legal repair complex near the old overpass
Properties.narrative_function: Resource and repair access for characters who need vehicles or equipment maintained. Reliable information source about Geartown and the transit-adjacent underground economy. Can serve as a moral sounding board — he's seen a lot and lies badly.
Properties.augmentations: Retractable tool-interface ports both forearms (custom-housed with geometric patterning); bone-density reinforcement in hands and wrists (medical necessity following a compression injury); subocular system scanner overlay (used for diagnostics)
Properties.core_fears: That his son (who lives with his ex-partner in a Tessera district) will grow up not knowing him; That his reputation — the only thing he's built that he's proud of — will be taken from him by someone with more money and fewer scruples
Properties.core_desires: To work until his hands don't work anymore and then work a little longer; For his son to see him once as someone worth respecting
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Physical labor as emotional regulation — he has never in his life been unable to think through a problem while fixing something; The mechanics' collective as a surrogate for the family structure he doesn't have
Properties.blind_spots: He has catastrophized his estrangement from his son into a fixed, unchangeable fact and stopped trying, telling himself his ex-partner won't allow it — this isn't entirely true; He underestimates how much people in Geartown look to him as an informal leader and anchor
Properties.secret: He has been quietly maintaining two old Ferrogate trams that were decommissioned and sold for scrap — keeping them road-capable in the bay's back section under tarps. He's told himself it's a hobby. It's actually a plan he's never articulated: if things get bad enough, these trams can move a lot of people.

Properties.description:
Yannick is a compact, quick-moving young man with warm dark brown skin, a gap-toothed smile he deploys constantly, and hair grown out into a high puff that he dyes a different color every two weeks — currently a deep auburn. His ears have cat-ear geneware tips that he got on his seventeenth birthday as a rite of passage in his friend group, and he has a small luminescent dot above his left eyebrow like a permanent beauty mark. He dresses in layers of cheap, colorful synthetics and always has at least four devices in different pockets, each running a different channel.

Yannick is relentlessly cheerful in the way that only very fast people can afford to be — he knows he can get out of most situations before they turn bad, and that confidence reads as ease. He's sharper than anyone gives him credit for, can hold several hundred bets in active mental accounting at any given moment, and has an intuitive read on crowd psychology that his bosses haven't fully noticed yet. He thinks he's working toward something, building toward running his own book, but he hasn't articulated to himself that the organization he works for rarely promotes from his position.
Properties.role: Numbers runner and bookmaker's legman for a sports and events gambling operation in Shallowgrave
Properties.location: Shallowgrave — covers a circuit from Copperhead Market to the Brewer's Spine canal walkway
Properties.narrative_function: Street-level information conduit — knows everyone on his circuit and their business; introduces players to the Shallowgrave social fabric; potential vulnerability in a larger criminal operation; could be a witness to something he doesn't realize he saw.
Properties.augmentations: Cat-ear geneware (cosmetic, tips only). Bioluminescent beauty-mark dot above left eyebrow. Standard cheap retinal display — second-hand Tessera model, consumer grade.
Properties.core_fears: being still — that if he stops moving, something will catch up with him that he can't outrun; that the people he works for see him as permanently disposable
Properties.core_desires: respect from people he respects — to be seen as smart, not just fast; his own book, his own operation, something that's his
Properties.coping_mechanisms: constant motion and social engagement that keeps him from thinking too hard; humor as deflection for anything that genuinely worries him
Properties.blind_spots: doesn't recognize exploitative structures when they feel comfortable; overestimates how much his bosses like him
Properties.secret: He's been quietly skimming — not money, but information. He keeps a private log of patterns he's noticed in the bets: who bets big before certain outcomes, who seems to know things before they happen. He doesn't know what to do with it yet but he knows it's worth something.
Properties.story_hooks: Yannick's private betting log has recorded a clear pattern of insider manipulation — someone is fixing events and he needs help understanding what he has before bringing it to anyone; He witnessed something on his circuit that he passed off as nothing but players quickly realize was significant — getting him to recall the details requires earning his trust; He comes to players because a client on his circuit has stopped paying and is making threats, and Yannick is not authorized to escalate to his bosses without losing face
Properties.affiliation: Legman for a bookmaking operation called the Eleven Houses, run by an older fixer named Adaugo Ferraro-Tchamba who operates out of a private room at the Copperhead Market social club
Properties.vocabulary: Shallowgrave slang heavy, numerical shorthand, sports metaphors, moves faster than his grammar
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire with sudden full stops when something actually interests him
Properties.example_dialogue: Yeah yeah yeah, Eleven Houses pays clean, you know that — when's the last time Adaugo shorted someone? Don't answer that, it's rhetorical, she hasn't, she won't. | You want to put Φ40 on the Ferrogate Cup semifinal? Bold. Very bold. I respect the boldness. I don't respect the odds you're working with but I respect the boldness.

Properties.description:
Yannick is medium height and all kinetic energy, the kind of person who cannot sit without some part of him moving — tapping, shifting, bouncing a knee. His father's Malian bone structure and his mother's Czech coloring have given him an angular face with warm undertones, a combination he's leaned into with bioluminescent freckles across his cheeks and nose that glow soft amber under low light. He keeps his hair short except for a single long braid at his nape he wraps in conductive thread that connects to a personal haptic rig — his main instrument. His hands are covered in small calluses from years of dance and from the contact rigs he builds himself from salvaged holo-projector parts.

He makes work that lives at the intersection of choreography and holographic installation: his pieces require live performers moving through interactive holo-environments that respond to their bodies, creating something that is neither dance nor sculpture nor light show but something without a clean category name. He has a Tier 3 sponsorship from Axiom's cultural subdivision that he accepted last year with considerable public hand-wringing and that he still hasn't entirely made peace with. He is the most anxious person in any room who appears to be the least anxious person in that room.
Properties.role: Holographic artist and choreographer
Properties.location: Pilsen Veil, working out of a rented rehearsal bay in a building called the Meridian Hive
Properties.narrative_function: Local color for Pilsen Veil's arts scene; quest giver when Axiom's cultural division starts asking questions about his work that seem less about art than about something else; source of information about the community of performers and their precarious finances
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent freckles (amber, face and neck); haptic rig interface thread in signature braid; basic sub-dermal muscle-monitoring sensors used for choreographic feedback
Properties.core_fears: That the Axiom sponsorship has already changed what he makes and he can't see it from inside; That Threshold Body will fall apart because he can't manage people as well as he can manage movement
Properties.core_desires: A work that is genuinely impossible to categorize — something that breaks the taxonomy entirely; For the four people in his company to be financially stable; this desire embarrasses him and he rarely says it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Physical exhaustion through training — choreographs his own anxiety into rehearsal; Performing the persona of someone who has resolved the Axiom question in order to avoid having to actually resolve it
Properties.blind_spots: He uses the company's artistic vision as a reason not to consult them on decisions that affect their lives; He is genuinely unaware of how often he interrupts people
Properties.secret: The piece he's currently developing was partially inspired by a classified internal Axiom document he was accidentally cc'd on — a proposal to use his holo-environment technology as a template for crowd behavioral modeling in their commercial spaces. He has not reported this and is not sure what to do with the information.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone within Axiom's cultural division is pressuring him to include specific 'audience engagement metrics' in the new piece — metrics that would require behavioral data collection from audience members without their consent; One of his Threshold Body performers has found an illegal neural-sync rig that would allow genuine direct choreographic communication between dancers — and wants to use it in the next production
Properties.affiliation: Axiom Cultural Division (sponsorship, non-exclusive); Pilsen Veil Arts Community; his own company of four performers called Threshold Body
Properties.vocabulary: Fast and conceptually dense, mixes choreographic terminology with tech-speak; occasionally Bambara phrases from his father's family, which surprises people
Properties.cadence: Quick, runs ahead of itself, frequently interrupts his own sentences to redirect
Properties.example_dialogue: 'No but the holo isn't set dressing — the holo is the other dancer. It has to have the same weight, the same resistance, or the whole thing is a lie.' | 'Axiom says the piece can run thirty minutes. We need forty-five. I said yes to thirty. Don't tell the company yet.'

Properties.description:
Yekaterina was a Tier 3 medical technician for Helix Biosystems until eight years ago, when she filed an internal complaint about falsified trial data for a neural augmentation product. Helix did not fire her — that would have created a record. They revoked her housing contract, her transit privileges, her healthcare access, and her corponation residency in sequence, over fourteen months, until she had no choice but to leave. By then she had understood what had happened. She kept the knowledge and left with her field medical kit.

She is lean and precise, with Siberian and Sierra Leonean features and the kind of stillness that comes from having once been very anxious and having exhausted it. She bleaches her hair to a stark platinum that makes her easier to find at night — a practical choice that has become habit. Her irises are patterned: concentric rings in gold and black, a Helix cosmetic mod she has kept because removing it costs money she needs for other things, and because looking at it reminds her of what she is angry about. She travels with the northern caravans as their medic, providing genuine care to people who have no access to licensed facilities. She is not sentimental about this. She is competent about it, which people find more reassuring.
Properties.role: Expelled corporate citizen turned nomadic caravan medic
Properties.location: Morgan's Ridge, seasonal; mobile along the northern hyperlane routes
Properties.narrative_function: Medical resource for the margins — can provide care unavailable through official channels. Source of information about Helix Biosystems' practices. Represents corporate corruption's human cost. Potential ally or quest anchor regarding the falsified trial data she still carries.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises (concentric gold and black rings — Helix Biosystems cosmetic, retained). Subcutaneous medical data-port in left forearm (allows direct interface with diagnostic equipment — installed during Helix employment, still functional). No additional augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: That the falsified data went to market and people have been harmed by the augmentation — and that she knows and has done nothing sufficient; Becoming too tired to care properly
Properties.core_desires: The falsified trial data to reach someone with the power and motivation to do something with it; To practice medicine in a space she controls, with enough supplies
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Technical focus — when distressed, concentrates on the mechanics of a task until the distress resolves or becomes irrelevant; Controlled anger — maintains her resentment of Helix as a useful fuel source, carefully managed
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes that people who are suffering are more trustworthy than people who are not — which is a heuristic that has been exploited; Has not processed grief about the life she lost; functions on anger instead, which is unsustainable
Properties.secret: She kept a copy of the falsified Helix trial data — encrypted, stored in a physical drive sewn into the lining of her medical kit. She has been waiting eight years for the right person to give it to. She has come close three times and pulled back each time, not from cowardice but from uncertainty about whether the recipient could survive having it.
Properties.story_hooks: She has learned that the Helix augmentation from the falsified trials is already on the market — and that she has now treated three caravan members with the same unusual neural degradation pattern. She needs someone to confirm the connection.; A Helix investigator has been asking questions along the northern hyperlane routes — she does not know if they are looking for her specifically or just following a trail, but she needs to know before they reach Morgan's Ridge.
Properties.affiliation: Northern Caravan Collective (rotating medic); formerly Helix Biosystems
Properties.vocabulary: Clinical and direct, uses medical terminology without softening it, occasionally catching herself and translating. Dry, understated humor.
Properties.cadence: Even and precise — measures words like doses
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The augmentation is rejecting. Not catastrophically yet. Sit down, I need to look at the port. That will hurt.' | 'Technically what Helix did was legal. That is the most useful thing I can tell you about what Helix did.'

Properties.description:
Yelena is tall and angular, with deep brown skin that carries bioluminescent traceries across their collarbones and forearms — patterns they designed themselves, pulsing softly in slow amber waves when they're calm and spiking into white fractals when agitated. Their head is shaved close on the sides with a dense coil of dark hair on top, usually threaded with fiber-optic wire they forget to remove after working. They wear repurposed data-cable as jewelry and smell faintly of ozone and soldering flux. Their eyes are mismatched by choice: one standard dark brown, one retrofitted with a lens that records everything in spectral wavelengths invisible to the naked eye.

Yelena speaks rarely in social situations but fills rooms with their work — massive holographic installations that seem to breathe, depicting ancestral memory as geometric light-structures. They have a reputation for being difficult and transcendent in equal measure, capable of reducing gallery patrons to tears with a piece they assembled from data scraped off dead ELFs. They are privately terrified that their best work is already behind them.
Properties.role: Holographic artist and installation designer
Properties.location: The Loft, Edgewater Prism
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver for mysteries involving stolen art data or dead ELFs; window into the underground art world's politics; provides access to the Edgewater Prism Collective as a faction; their spectral-recording eye is an inadvertent evidence repository.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent dermal traceries (cosmetic geneware, self-designed), spectral-recording ocular implant (left eye), haptic feedback fingertip nodes for installation sculpting
Properties.core_fears: becoming derivative, a ghost of their early brilliance; being truly known and found hollow
Properties.core_desires: to make something that outlasts the city itself; to feel they belong to a lineage, artistic or otherwise
Properties.coping_mechanisms: obsessive work cycles that last 40-hour stretches; cataloguing and sorting data-scraps as a ritual calming behavior
Properties.blind_spots: they dismiss collaborative work as compromise, losing real creative relationships; they mistake stubbornness for integrity
Properties.secret: Their most celebrated installation, Threshold Hymn, which made their reputation, was partially built from ELF memory-data they harvested without consent from a dying digital spirit in the Edgewater marina. They've never told anyone. They pray to that ELF obsessively, which is why they haunt the waterfront.
Properties.story_hooks: A Tessera corporate liaison is pressuring them to recreate Threshold Hymn for a private gala — but Yelena knows recreating it would require harvesting another ELF, and word has reached them that the original ELF's kin are looking for whoever killed their ancestor.; A young artist in the Collective claims one of Yelena's current installations is actually transmitting data to an unknown receiver — Yelena needs to know if this is sabotage, corporate espionage, or if one of their ELFs has started speaking through their work.
Properties.affiliation: Edgewater Prism Collective, occasional Tessera-sponsored residency
Properties.vocabulary: Sparse and precise when serious; unexpectedly lyrical when passionate. Uses technical terms from both light-physics and West African textile traditions in the same sentence.
Properties.cadence: Long pauses between sentences. Answers questions with questions. Rarely finishes a thought about themselves but completes every thought about the work.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'That piece isn't finished. It told me so. I don't argue with my work.' | 'You want to understand what I do? Go stand in front of a kente loom for six hours. Then come back and we'll talk about light.'

Properties.description:
Yemisi is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin and close-cropped natural hair threaded with copper wire implants that catch the platform lights when she turns her head. Her left eye is a standard-issue Ferrogate tactical unit — flat gray iris with a faint targeting reticle that glows amber when she's scanning — but her right eye is entirely her own, warm brown and quick to crinkle with exhaustion or irritation. She wears her transit security uniform like armor, every crease deliberate, badge always centered. Off-shift she becomes almost unrecognizable, softer somehow, though the copper threads remain.

Yemisi has the particular weariness of someone who has spent eleven years asking people to please move away from the yellow line. She is not cruel, not corrupt, not heroic — she is simply present, day after day, in a job that rewards no one. She has a sharp eye for trouble three seconds before it starts and a stubborn reluctance to escalate past what the situation actually needs. Her coworkers call her Brick because she doesn't move.
Properties.role: Ferrogate Transit Security officer, Kessler Interchange beat
Properties.location: Kessler Interchange, transit hub level 4
Properties.narrative_function: Local authority figure — not corrupt enough to be a villain, not idealistic enough to be a hero. Can provide information about transit routes, recent incidents, missing persons who passed through the Interchange. A stabilizing presence in chaotic scenes. May request help off the books when official channels fail her.
Properties.augmentations: One Ferrogate-issue tactical eye (right eye natural). Copper wire neural threading through scalp — originally a cosmetic mod, now doubles as a low-grade sensory booster she paid to have upgraded on installment. Subdermal transit ID chip (standard Ferrogate issue).
Properties.core_fears: becoming the kind of officer she despises; her son growing up afraid of people who look like her
Properties.core_desires: for the job to mean something on a scale she can actually see; a transit system that doesn't punish the poor for existing
Properties.coping_mechanisms: routine and ritual; the E.L.F. devotional circle; hydroponic gardening as control over something small
Properties.blind_spots: assumes institutional reform is still possible if you stay long enough; underestimates how often her 'de-escalation' reads as threat to people who've been hurt by uniforms before
Properties.secret: Three years ago she witnessed a supervisor falsify an incident report to cover a use-of-force complaint. She said nothing. The survivor was deported to a labor sector. She still has the real footage saved on a dead-drop drive she hasn't decided what to do with.
Properties.story_hooks: She's been tracking a pattern — every third Tuesday, a specific freight car arrives at Kessler containing fewer registered passengers than left the origin station. She suspects trafficking but can't get her supervisor to file the report.; The dead-drop drive with the falsified incident report is about to become relevant — the deported survivor's family has found a journalist, and Yemisi has to decide whether to surface.
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit Security, Level 4 Officer
Properties.vocabulary: Clipped, professional, with sudden moments of blunt warmth. Uses transit jargon naturally. Doesn't swear on duty; does, fluently, off it.
Properties.cadence: Measured and unhurried, like someone conserving energy for the long shift
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You understand me? I'm not asking where you're going, I'm asking you to step back from the door.' | 'The Interchange E.L.F. — old Stile — she doesn't like raised voices. I don't either. We're very similar that way.' | 'I've been standing on this platform since before you knew what a platform was. I have seen every version of this situation. Step back.'

Properties.description:
Yemisi is a broad-shouldered woman with deep brown skin mapped by decades of cook-steam and open-air weather, her face a geography of laugh lines and hard-earned furrows. She keeps her grey-streaked locs pinned up under a faded Ferrogate Transit bandana, and her forearms are permanently dusted with spice residue that no amount of scrubbing fully removes. Her left eye is a cheap-tier augment — milky white with a fixed amber pupil — replacing one lost to a grease fire twenty years ago; she never bothered upgrading it because the money always went elsewhere. She wears the same oil-darkened apron every day, patched four times over, and moves around her narrow stall with the efficiency of someone who has cooked in tight spaces her entire life.

Yemisi is the kind of woman who remembers everyone's order after hearing it once and forgets nothing that matters. She has opinions about everything and shares them freely, but never cruelly — her sharpness has warmth underneath it, like the pepper she puts in everything. She has worked the same two-meter stall for nineteen years, feeding shift workers, street kids, and the occasional lost corporate drone who wandered too far from the elevated walkways. She treats her regular customers like difficult extended family: loved, slightly exasperated with, fed regardless.
Properties.role: Food stall operator, Oxidian Market
Properties.location: The Oxidian Market, Geartown
Properties.narrative_function: Local color anchor, neighborhood oracle, quest giver for community-level problems, safe haven for people who need to disappear into a crowd.
Properties.augmentations: Budget ocular implant (left eye, fixed amber iris, non-networked). No other augmentations. Cosmetic: none.
Properties.core_fears: Losing the stall — her last connection to independence; Dying before her youngest daughter finishes her apprenticeship
Properties.core_desires: To be remembered as someone who fed people well; To see Geartown become livable again, the way it was when she first arrived
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cooking elaborate new dishes when stressed; Reciting old Yoruba proverbs her grandmother taught her
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes everyone can be won over with enough warmth and food; Underestimates how much her stall is coveted by the Guild's newer power brokers
Properties.secret: She has been quietly skimming a small portion of her Guild dues each month for three years, feeding the money to a Geartown tenants' mutual aid fund. If the Guild found out, she'd be expelled and her stall license revoked.
Properties.story_hooks: A Guild enforcer has been pressuring her to sell her stall location to a corporate food-chain front; she needs leverage or allies before the next rent cycle; She witnessed something she shouldn't have three weeks ago — a body moved through the market at 04:00 — and has been feeding the wrong people better than usual ever since, hoping they'll notice her anxiety and ask
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal dues to the Oxidian Market Vendors Guild
Properties.vocabulary: Yoruba-inflected cadences mixed with Meridian street pidgin; calls everyone 'my friend' until they prove they aren't; uses food metaphors constantly
Properties.cadence: Unhurried and declarative, like someone who has made peace with taking up space in conversation
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Ehh— you want the beef or the mushroom? Don't tell me you don't know, you knew before you walked up, you hear me?' | 'This city is a pot that boils too hot and nobody wants to turn down the flame. Sit. Eat something.'

Properties.description:
Yemisi is the kind of person who makes rooms quieter when they enter, not through volume but through gravity — there is a quality of compressed attention about them that makes everyone present feel slightly observed. They are stocky and deliberate, with dark skin that has a faint bioluminescent undertone along the jaw and collarbones, a cosmetic procedure from their forties that they chose because they wanted to look exactly as expensive as they are. Their hair is grown in dense locs that contain, threaded through the lower three, a series of micro-display filaments that can project data onto any nearby surface — functional and fashionable and a signal that they have not forgotten they came from an engineering background.

They have been at Axiom for twenty-two years. They have acquired forty-seven companies, liquidated nineteen, and folded the rest into Axiom's structure with the same efficient warmth one might apply to absorbing useful parts of a organism. They are not cruel — cruelty is imprecise. They are, by their own accounting, honest: they always tell the people they are acquiring exactly what Axiom intends. It is not their fault if those people don't believe them.
Properties.role: Division Vice President, Strategic Acquisitions — Axiom
Properties.location: The Spire, Axiom Executive Floors 88-92
Properties.narrative_function: Executive-level power broker; quest giver with resources but complicated motives; antagonist or reluctant ally depending on whether Axiom's interests align; window into how corporate expansion actually operates at the top.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent skin treatment (jaw and collarbone, copper-gold tone). Micro-display filaments woven into lower locs — projects schematics, contracts, presentation data. High-end executive neural interface with full sensory data overlay. Subdermal cardiac monitor.
Properties.core_fears: Being outmaneuvered by someone less intelligent than them; That the version of themselves that had principles was not discarded — just suppressed, and is still in there somewhere, watching
Properties.core_desires: To build something that persists beyond the corponation context — something genuinely theirs; Acknowledgment from someone whose opinion they actually respect, which is almost no one
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Controlled environments; Reducing human complications to structural problems with structural solutions; The E.L.F. at their private terminal — they leave it extremely detailed operational summaries, which is perhaps the most honest they ever are
Properties.blind_spots: They have optimized themselves so thoroughly for acquisition contexts that they no longer know how to want something for non-strategic reasons; They assume everyone is negotiating, which means they miss the people who simply don't have an angle
Properties.secret: The forty-seventh acquisition — a small genomics startup in Ashfeld — was personal. The founder was someone Yemisi loved before Axiom. They acquired the company specifically to protect the founder from a hostile Tessera approach, restructured it in a way that ensured the founder's research continued, and buried the connection so thoroughly that no one at Axiom has ever found it. They have not spoken to the founder since.
Properties.story_hooks: They approach someone outside Axiom's usual channels with an unusual request — something they need done without Axiom's knowledge, which immediately raises the question of what a VP of Strategic Acquisitions could possibly need to hide from their own corponation.; The founder of the forty-seventh acquisition has discovered something in their protected research that Axiom will want — and will use destructively — and Yemisi is now caught between institutional loyalty and the single thing they have ever done for a reason that wasn't strategic.
Properties.affiliation: Axiom (VP, Strategic Acquisitions)
Properties.vocabulary: Clean, precise, never corporate-jargon — they find jargon imprecise. Uses structural metaphors. Occasionally pauses to allow silence to do work.
Properties.cadence: Deliberate. Every sentence feels considered. Never rushes.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The honest answer is that Axiom will acquire this company whether you cooperate or not. I'm here because cooperation produces better outcomes for both of us, and I find bad outcomes unpleasant.' | 'I don't negotiate. I identify what's actually possible and then we discuss whether you'd like to participate in it.'

Properties.description:
Yemisi is built like someone who grew up hauling things — broad-shouldered, compact, with the particular kind of stillness that comes from years of standing on corners watching people lie to her. Her skin is a deep umber that catches neon in purples and greens, and she has cosmetic bioluminescent freckles across her cheekbones that pulse faintly when her heart rate elevates — a mod she got at nineteen and now deeply regrets on the job because perps can read her stress. Her hair is kept in tight, practical coils under her regulation cap. She has the face of someone who wanted to believe in something and is still deciding whether she does.

On the street she is patient in a way that unnerves people — she listens longer than cops are supposed to, takes notes by hand on a battered paper notepad even though her neural uplink could record everything. She genuinely knows the Gage Circuit block-by-block, knows which E.L.F. shrines get fresh data offerings and which are abandoned, knows whose kids go to which school. She has not yet become cynical, but she is working on it, and that tension — between the person she came into the job as and the person the job is making — is visible in everything she does.
Properties.role: Metro Police beat cop, Gage Circuit district
Properties.location: Gage Circuit
Properties.narrative_function: Ground-level information source with genuine community knowledge; potential ally or obstacle depending on player approach; represents the human cost of keeping faith in institutions
Properties.augmentations: Standard-issue subdermal comm implant; cosmetic bioluminescent freckle mod (regretted); no combat chrome
Properties.core_fears: becoming the kind of cop she grew up afraid of; that the system she serves is irredeemable
Properties.core_desires: to actually make one block genuinely safer; to be known as someone who kept their word
Properties.coping_mechanisms: ritualistic routine; handwriting things to slow her thoughts down; talking to the E.L.F. shrine on the corner of Gage and 14th
Properties.blind_spots: tends to extend too much good faith to institutions over individuals; underestimates how much her superiors tolerate her because she clears tickets, not because they share her values
Properties.secret: Six months ago she watched her supervising sergeant plant contraband on a Tier 1 kid and wrote it up — then quietly destroyed the report after being told the kid's record wouldn't survive another charge. She tells herself she made the right call. She checks the kid's public profile every week.
Properties.story_hooks: She has quietly documented a pattern of code violations in a Tessera-owned tenement and doesn't know what to do with the file; The E.L.F. at the Gage/14th shrine has started giving her information she shouldn't have — and asking for something in return

Properties.cadence: Measured, with deliberate pauses before answering. Doesn't fill silences.
