Properties.description:
Gage Circuit runs on 55th Street the way an engine runs on a crankshaft -- everything turns around it. The old Gage Park commercial strip was already one of the densest retail corridors on Chicago's Southwest Side before Meridian 88 formalized the district boundaries, and the transition to megacity economics only compressed what was already tight. The strip stretches for two and a half kilometers of uninterrupted commercial activity: stalls, shops, service counters, and popup vendors occupying every available square meter of ground-floor space, with residential blocks stacked above in four-to-six story layers that house the same families who run the businesses below. Living above your shop isn't a lifestyle choice here. It's thermal efficiency -- body heat rises, inventory stays cool, and the commute is one flight of stairs.

The commercial ecosystem on 55th is a closed loop that's almost entirely divorced from Meridian's formal economy. Transactions happen in a local scrip system that the vendor association manages through a decentralized ledger running on a neural mesh network that the vendors built, maintain, and control. Corporate currency is accepted but not preferred. Axiom's economic monitoring systems can see the scrip transactions but can't parse them -- the ledger's encryption was designed by a retired Circuit hacker who moved to Gage Park for the food and stayed for the community, and her work is, by any professional standard, elegant. The strip pays its Meridian taxes in corporate currency, calculated from revenue figures that bear a creative relationship to reality. Everyone involved, including the tax assessor who lives on 56th Street, understands this arrangement.

The density is the story. Gage Circuit packs 60,000 people into a footprint that was designed for 20,000, and the pressure creates its own physics. Disputes are resolved fast because there isn't room for them to linger. Businesses adapt or are replaced within weeks. Information travels the strip faster than neural mesh can carry it because the density of human contact is higher than the density of data connections. You can learn anything that's happening in the Southwest by standing on 55th Street for an hour and keeping your ears open. The challenge isn't getting information. The challenge is drinking from the firehose.
Properties.aliases: Gage Park, The Strip, Fifty-Five, La Franja
Properties.demographics: Approximately 60,000 residents, predominantly Latino with significant Eastern European, Arab, and South Asian minorities. Overwhelmingly Tier 1 and Tier 2. The population density exceeds Meridian residential standards by 300%, a statistic the district has successfully kept out of official reporting.
Properties.economy: The 55th Street commercial strip operates on a local scrip system with encrypted decentralized ledger. Revenue is substantial, uncounted by Meridian economic metrics, and recycled almost entirely within the community. The vendor association functions as a de facto central bank.
Properties.power_structure: The Gage Circuit Vendor Association controls the scrip system, the commercial strip's physical space, and the neural mesh network that supports both. Their authority is economic and therefore absolute within the strip. Outside the strip, standard Meridian governance applies, loosely.
Properties.dangers: Overcrowding -- structural and fire risks in buildings loaded beyond design capacity; The scrip system's opacity attracts occasional interest from Axiom Economic Compliance, whose audits are resisted collectively; Commercial disputes that escalate faster than mediation can contain them in the compressed environment; Pickpockets and petty theft in the crowd density -- an occupational hazard of 55th Street; Getting lost -- the strip's navigation is intuitive to residents and bewildering to everyone else
Properties.opportunities: Access to goods and services that don't exist in the formal economy, at prices the formal economy can't match; The vendor association's intelligence network covers every commercial transaction in the Southwest; Scrip can be exchanged for services that corporate currency can't buy -- discretion, expertise, introductions; The retired Circuit hacker who built the ledger system is still alive, still bored, and still willing to take interesting projects; 55th Street is the Southwest's information marketplace -- everything passes through here eventually
Properties.story_hooks: Axiom Economic Compliance has scheduled a full audit of the scrip system, and the vendor association is preparing a response that involves every merchant on the strip -- coordination at this scale hasn't been attempted since the last crackdown, and the stakes are higher now; A new vendor on 55th Street is selling neural interface modifications that shouldn't exist outside a Tier 5 lab -- the technology is genuine, the source is unknown, and every faction in the Southwest wants to know where it's coming from; The encrypted ledger has been running for twelve years and contains a complete economic history of the informal Southwest -- someone has offered the vendor association a staggering sum for a copy, and the association is split on whether to sell
Properties.sights: The 55th Street corridor in full commercial frenzy -- a canyon of vendors, signage, and bodies; Scrip transaction holograms flickering between buyers and sellers in the vendor association's custom interface; Residential laundry and signal equipment crowding rooflines above the shops; Hand-lettered and holographic signage competing for attention in Spanish, Polish, Arabic, and Shelf Cant; The vendor association's communication nodes -- repurposed neural mesh relays bolted to lampposts; Foot traffic so dense the street functions as a single slow-moving organism
Properties.sounds: The roar of commerce -- haggling, hawking, laughing, arguing, all at full Southwest Side volume; Scrip ledger confirmation tones -- a custom two-note chime that means money has changed hands; Music from competing storefronts creating a block-by-block soundtrack that changes every fifty meters; The creak and groan of buildings bearing more weight than their architects intended
Properties.smells: Street food from every tradition represented on the strip -- grilling, frying, baking, and fermenting simultaneously; Fabric from the textile stalls -- new synthetics and recycled natural fibers packed in bolts; The human density itself -- 60,000 people in close quarters have an aggregate scent that's earthy and alive; Fresh paint and adhesive from storefronts being renovated on the fly, between customers
Properties.feel: Overwhelming and alive. Gage Circuit feels like standing inside a living economy -- not the abstracted graphs and metrics of the Meridian Core, but the physical reality of people exchanging labor for goods at a scale that makes institutional economics irrelevant. It's exhausting, exhilarating, and completely authentic in a way that nothing above Tier 2 ever manages to be.

Properties.description:
Yetunde Abashidze-Tarawa is a broad-shouldered woman who moves through her fungal gardens with the deliberate grace of someone who has learned to never knock anything over in the dark. She is tall, with deep brown skin that has taken on an extraordinary quality in her years underground: faint bioluminescent patches on her forearms and the sides of her neck — not implants, but a genuine dermal symbiosis with a engineered photobacterial culture she cultivated herself and chose to inoculate into her own skin thirty years ago. In the dim blue-green glow of the Bloom Halls, she is hauntingly beautiful. On the rare occasions she surfaces, people stare.

She grows over forty varieties of engineered and wild-caught fungus in a network of cultivation racks that fill three former water reclamation chambers. She trades in food, medicine (several of her cultures have antibiotic and analgesic properties), and a mild psychoactive she calls Quietcap that she dispenses only to people she has personally assessed as not in crisis. She is the closest thing Irkalla's sub-level community has to a matriarch, doctor, and pharmacist — a role she accepted reluctantly and now occupies with the resigned authority of someone who knows no one else will do it.
Properties.role: Fungus farmer and underground food supplier
Properties.location: Irkalla, Sub-Level 7 — the 'Bloom Halls', a repurposed water reclamation chamber
Properties.narrative_function: Community anchor, information hub, healer figure — she knows everyone in the sub-levels of Irkalla and has strong opinions about all of them. Can provide resources, medicine, Quietcap, and extremely candid assessments of other characters.
Properties.augmentations: Self-inoculated bioluminescent photobacterial symbiote (forearms, neck — faint blue-green glow); basic respiratory filter implant (nasal); no other augmentations
Properties.core_fears: the Bloom Halls being discovered and stripped by a corponation survey team; outliving everyone she has taken responsibility for
Properties.core_desires: for the sub-level community to achieve genuine self-sufficiency; to be remembered as someone who fed people
Properties.coping_mechanisms: physical labor as emotional regulation; humor — dry, unsentimental, often landing before people realize it's a joke
Properties.blind_spots: gives too much, does not ask for help, does not notice her own exhaustion until it becomes a crisis; occasionally too slow to recognize that someone is exploiting her generosity
Properties.secret: Her bioluminescent symbiote is slowly spreading. She engineered it to be localized but it has been migrating toward her spine for two years. She does not know if this is benign or catastrophic, and she has no way to scan it properly. She has told no one.
Properties.story_hooks: A new fungal contamination has begun killing cultures in the outer chambers — it arrived on someone's boots, and she needs to find out who came in from where before it reaches the medical cultivars.; A Tessera biosurveillance team is mapping the sub-levels and her symbiote culture — which she did not patent, because how could she — may technically belong to Helix Biosystems under the Derived Organisms Statute.
Properties.affiliation: Irkalla sub-level community; informal trade relationships with Undertow merchants
Properties.vocabulary: Warm but precise. She uses botanical and mycological terminology casually. Her Bore Rat pidgin is perfect; she can also speak three surface languages.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried and rhythmic, like someone who learned to speak at the pace of things that grow slowly.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Now. Sit. I don't feed anyone standing up — it's disrespectful to the food.' | 'That one you're looking at? That's Quietcap. It is not for you right now. Let it breathe. Come back when you're not running from something.' | 'The corponations built everything you're standing in. That's true. They also abandoned it. So who does it belong to now?'

Properties.description:
Yetunde is built like a cargo container — broad-shouldered, thick-necked, standing just under two meters with a physicality that makes precinct hallways feel narrower. Her skin is deep umber, her hair a close-cropped natural coil threaded through with copper-toned bioluminescent filaments that pulse faintly when her heart rate elevates — a side effect of a medical implant she never bothered to have aesthetically corrected. A long diagonal scar runs from her left jaw to her collarbone, courtesy of a monofilament accident during the Calumet Rise food riots eight years ago. She keeps it unrepaired on purpose.

On the job she projects a professional blankness — not coldness exactly, but the studied calm of someone who has seen a crowd turn to a mob and back again more times than she can count. Off-duty she is unexpectedly gentle, the kind of person who stops to help strangers find their way and remembers the names of the Ferrogate transit workers at Fort Anchor's break room. She is deeply suspicious of anyone who seems too eager to hurt people, including some of her own squad.
Properties.role: Riot Suppression Specialist, Meridian 88 Metro Police
Properties.location: Fort Anchor
Properties.narrative_function: Moral compass figure within law enforcement — a voice of restraint who can warn players about escalating tensions or provide insight into how the Metro Police actually functions versus how it is supposed to. Can be an unexpected ally or a complicated obstacle depending on context.
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal impact-distribution mesh across torso and upper arms (medical-grade, not cosmetic). Neural pacing implant with bioluminescent copper filament side effect visible at temples and crown. Reinforced knee cartilage from a line-of-duty injury repair.
Properties.core_fears: Becoming the kind of officer who enjoys the violence; A repeat of the Calumet Rise incident but with a worse outcome
Properties.core_desires: To do her job without compromising her sense of self; To eventually see the conditions that cause riots addressed at the source
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Physical routine and exercise; Tending her herb garden; Deliberate silence when overwhelmed
Properties.blind_spots: Tends to over-trust fellow officers who show personal kindness, even when their professional conduct is questionable; Underestimates how much her mere physical presence intimidates people who have been harmed by police
Properties.secret: During the Calumet Rise riots she witnessed a senior officer execute an unarmed man and filed an incident report that was quietly buried. She still has an encrypted copy. She has never decided what to do with it.
Properties.story_hooks: She approaches someone with a copy of the buried Calumet Rise incident report, asking them to hold it for her — the pressure of keeping it herself has become unbearable.; A new riot suppression protocol issued by Metro Police Command crosses a line she cannot ignore, and she needs outside help to document and resist it.; Her squad is being deployed to suppress a protest she privately believes is justified, and she is looking for any legal pretext to de-escalate before things go wrong.
Properties.affiliation: Meridian 88 Metro Police — Riot Suppression Unit Delta
Properties.vocabulary: Direct, economical language with occasional Twi phrases from her grandmother's side. Formal in professional settings, warmer and more idiomatic off-duty.
Properties.cadence: Measured and unhurried. Rarely raises her voice. Her quietness in tense situations tends to make others either calmer or more nervous.
Properties.example_dialogue: You want to be somewhere else right now. I'm giving you that option before I stop giving it. | I didn't join to crack skulls. Some days the job doesn't care what I joined for. | Medme — that's what my grandmother called me. Means 'hold me.' She said it like a prayer. I think about that a lot in this line of work.

Properties.description:
Yetunde is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin crosshatched by decades of work — burn scars on her left forearm from a lab fire she never explains, and knuckles that look like they've reset more broken bones than she can count. Her hair is silver-white and kept in tight plaits pinned close to her skull; she wears a threadbare surgical coat over layered thermal wraps, a string of amber prayer beads around one wrist and a tourniquet on the other. Her eyes are warm and evaluating simultaneously, the kind that make people feel cared for and measured at the same time.

She has delivered children to Tier 1 families who couldn't afford Aurochs registration, set fractures by headlamp, and once performed a cesarean on a kitchen table with a sterling-steel boning knife she borrowed from the tenant upstairs. She is not sentimental about any of this. She is, however, quietly furious — at the system, at Helix Biosystems, at every corporate structure that makes her clinic necessary — and she channels that fury into competence. She charges what people can pay, accepts barter, and has been known to do work for free while audibly resenting having to.
Properties.role: Street doc and midwife operating out of a converted shipping container clinic in The Narrows
Properties.location: The Narrows, near Brewer's Spine junction
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver for medical emergencies, source of street-level information about who in The Narrows is sick or dying, moral anchor figure, provider of difficult choices about resource scarcity
Properties.augmentations: Haptic-feedback fingertip implants (medical grade, worn but functional) for tactile diagnostics; reading lens in left eye with magnification and UV spectrum; no cosmetic mods
Properties.core_fears: Watching someone die from something preventable that she couldn't stop; Being shut down by a Helix Biosystems compliance sweep
Properties.core_desires: A fully stocked clinic that doesn't run out of anesthetic; To see one generation of Narrows children grow up without preventable illness
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Methodical ritual — organizing supplies, cataloguing, counting; Dark humor deployed at inappropriate moments; Praying to the clinic's resident E.L.F., which she calls Grandmother Wire
Properties.blind_spots: Dismisses her own physical deterioration; her knees are in bad shape and she won't stop to treat herself; Assumes anyone in corporate employment has sold out entirely
Properties.secret: She performed an illegal gene-therapy procedure on a Helix Biosystems inspector's child nine years ago — the child lived, and the inspector has been quietly running interference for her clinic ever since. She has never told anyone and lives in fear that this arrangement will collapse or be exposed.
Properties.story_hooks: A Helix Biosystems compliance team is coming to inspect the clinic, and the inspector who protects her is suddenly unreachable; A patient she delivered years ago has come back — now a teenager, apparently sick with a engineered pathogen that shouldn't exist in The Narrows
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loose affiliation with the Brewer's Spine Community Health Cooperative
Properties.vocabulary: Direct, clinical when working, sarcastically maternal when not; mixes Yoruba endearments with flat declarative sentences
Properties.cadence: Unhurried even in crisis; she slows down when things get bad, which unnerves people who expect urgency
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want sterile or you want fast? Pick one, I don't have both today.' | 'Grandmother Wire provided. I asked nicely and left her three gigabytes of traffic data. You're welcome.' | 'I've delivered babies in worse light than this. Breathe.'

Properties.description:
Yetunde is compact and kinetic, her movements fast and precise in the way of someone who has trained herself to work in a small space. She keeps one half of her head shaved and the other half in elaborate Bantu knots dyed electric amber — she re-does them herself every two weeks, a meditative ritual. Her skin is dark brown and her forearms are covered from wrist to elbow in her own tattoo work, done in mirrors and by feel, a practice she's perfected over four years. She has bioluminescent patches on her collarbones, soft aquamarine that pulse faintly when she's excited — a geneware mod she saved three months for and has never once regretted.

Yetunde runs Cutline with the fierce territorial pride of someone who built everything in it herself. The container is small but immaculate — three chairs, two mirrors salvaged from a closed salon in Chatham Flats, and a digital art wall that rotates through her personal portfolio. She is talkative and sharp, able to read what a client wants from how they sit down, and skilled enough that she routinely has a six-week wait list. Her tattoo work is unlicensed — Helix Biosystems holds the local ink licensing monopoly and she refuses to pay their rates — which means she operates in a quiet legal gray zone she prefers not to discuss with new faces.
Properties.role: Barber and unlicensed tattoo artist
Properties.location: Mexicantown Libre, operates from a converted shipping container called Cutline on Gage Circuit
Properties.narrative_function: Local color, social hub, information source — the barber hears everything. Also a potential quest giver for anything touching the vendor collective or Helix licensing pressure.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent aquamarine collarbone patches (geneware). Stabilizer brace on her right wrist — cheap printed polymer, required after a repetitive strain injury at 23.
Properties.core_fears: Helix Biosystems shutting her down and taking her equipment; Becoming ordinary — invisible, unremembered
Properties.core_desires: To open a real licensed studio one day on her own terms, not theirs; To be known as an artist, not just a barber
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Creates when stressed — draws constantly in margins of appointment books; Vents freely to clients who've earned her trust
Properties.blind_spots: Her hunger for recognition makes her vulnerable to flattery from the wrong people; Doesn't fully reckon with how much legal risk the unlicensed tattooing carries
Properties.secret: She has a recurring client — a mid-tier Helix Biosystems compliance officer — who doesn't know she knows who he is. She's been documenting his visits and his gossip for eight months, building a picture of Helix's local enforcement patterns. She hasn't decided yet what to do with it.
Properties.story_hooks: The dossier on the Helix compliance officer is almost complete — but she's starting to realize the patterns she's found are bigger than local enforcement, and she needs someone who knows what to do with corporate intelligence.; A client came in for a tattoo and quietly asked her to include a specific symbol she recognized from somewhere she can't place — and the client didn't come back to pick up their appointment.
Properties.affiliation: Independent — Cutline; informal affiliation with the Mexicantown Libre vendor collective
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, code-switching between Meridian creole, market Yoruba phrases, and what she calls 'Polish grandmother energy' — precise, critical, unsentimental observations delivered affectionately. References art constantly.
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire when excited, can slow to deliberate when making a real point. Talks while she works, rarely stops.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't do ugly on purpose. You came in wanting ugly, that's a you problem, but I'll make it interesting ugly.' | 'Helix wants Φ800 a month for an ink license. Φ800! My grandmother paid less for a house. A house with walls.'

Properties.description:
Yetunde is a broad-shouldered woman with dark amber skin mapped in pale scarification lines that run from her collarbone to her wrists — a living record of every death she has attended, one mark per soul. Her hair is a tight silver-white crown, unpigmented by choice, and her eyes have been modded with concentric ring irises in deep violet and gold that she says let her see the moment someone stops being present. She moves slowly on purpose, filling rooms with a gravitational calm that makes agitated people want to sit down. She smells faintly of clove oil and something older, mineral.

Yetunde trained as a nurse under Helix Biosystems before she was pushed out during a cost-restructuring in her forties. She converted her grief about that displacement into a vocation — traveling to the bedsides of the dying across Irkalla and adjacent zones, offering what medicine couldn't: a witnessed departure. She does not affiliate with any single religion but borrows fluidly from Yoruba ancestor traditions, Lithuanian mourning songs her grandfather taught her, and the newer E.L.F. rites that hold data-death as its own sacred transition. She charges what people can pay, often nothing.
Properties.role: Death midwife and grief ritualist
Properties.location: Irkalla, lower residential warrens near the Deepwell Station junction
Properties.narrative_function: Local anchor for stories involving death, dying, grief, and final messages. She may be called to attend a character's loved one, and her ledger is an informal census of who has died in Irkalla. She sometimes knows things the dead wanted said.
Properties.augmentations: Concentric ring iris mods (violet/gold). Subdermal haptic sensors in her palms that detect micro-tremors — she uses them clinically to monitor pulse and breathing in the dying. No additional chrome.
Properties.core_fears: dying unwitnessed herself; that her work creates false comfort rather than real peace
Properties.core_desires: to make death less lonely; to be remembered as someone who stayed
Properties.coping_mechanisms: ritual and routine; physical slowness as a form of presence; journaling the dead
Properties.blind_spots: underestimates how much her own grief is still unprocessed; sometimes prioritizes the dying over the living family members in the room
Properties.secret: She is currently tending a corporate mid-level from Tessera who is dying of a condition his employer caused — and she has been offered a significant sum to not record his last words, which implicate a supervisor. She has not yet decided what to do.
Properties.story_hooks: A player's contact has died and Yetunde was present — she carries an undelivered message and won't share it with just anyone; She is being pressured by Tessera agents to alter the official death record of the corporate employee she attended, and she is quietly terrified
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loosely connected to the Irkalla Neighborhood Covenant and the Unstructured Faithful collective
Properties.vocabulary: Unhurried and precise. Draws from medical terminology and traditional ritual language in equal measure, often in the same sentence. Never talks down to anyone.
Properties.cadence: Slow, deliberate pauses. Treats silence as punctuation. Never interrupts.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The body knows what it's doing. Our job is just to not get in the way of that knowing.' | 'You don't have to be ready. Nobody is. I will be here and that is enough.'

Properties.description:
Yetunde Přibyl-Gasimova is a broad-shouldered woman whose posture conveys the absolute certainty that she will outlast everyone in any given room. Her skin is deep umber and her hair has been geneware-treated to hold a permanent silver-white that she wears pulled tight to her skull — no styling, no vanity, just function. A thin horizontal scar runs beneath her left eye, faded but deliberate. She dresses in water-resistant industrial layers even indoors, always smelling faintly of lake brine and the cedar-smoke incense she burns for the E.L.F. she calls 'the Creditor' — a digital spirit she believes inhabits her accounting tablet and blesses debts that will be repaid.

She is not a violent woman by preference, but she employs two enforcers precisely so she can remain calm when others are not. Yetunde speaks in measured, affectless sentences and has a habit of writing numbers in a physical ledger with a real ink stylus while people talk to her, which most find deeply unsettling. She genuinely believes she provides a community service — institutional credit is inaccessible to Tier 1 and 2 residents, and she fills that gap. The fact that her interest rates are predatory and her consequences severe is, to her, simply the cost of doing business in a city that offers no alternatives.
Properties.role: Loan shark and debt collector operating out of Gravesend Basin
Properties.location: Gravesend Basin — she operates from a converted barge-office called the Saltbox, moored at Pier 7-C
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver for characters who need quick capital with strings attached; source of financial information about who owes whom in Gravesend Basin; moral pressure point — she's not wrong that she fills a real gap, but her methods destroy lives.
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal transaction nodes in both palms — allows her to conduct credit transfers and biometric debt-binding without external hardware. Mild retinal overlay for real-time interest calculation. No cosmetic mods.
Properties.core_fears: Being seen as merely predatory rather than necessary; The collapse of the informal economy that gives her power
Properties.core_desires: To be respected as a businesswoman rather than feared as a criminal; To accumulate enough capital to go legitimate before she's too old
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — the E.L.F. offerings give structure to anxiety; Extreme organization and record-keeping as a form of control
Properties.blind_spots: She genuinely cannot perceive the harm her interest rates cause — she frames every default as a moral failure by the debtor
Properties.secret: She is quietly forgiving the debts of three families whose children she knew before a Ferrogate Transit accident killed several Basin residents eight years ago — she knew those families before she became 'the Ledger' and can't bring herself to collect from them, but can't admit to softness
Properties.story_hooks: A debtor has gone missing before repaying a significant sum — Yetunde hires someone to find out if they're dead, hiding, or a victim of something larger; She's begun receiving anonymous payments against debts that were written off years ago — someone is clearing accounts she'd forgotten, and she wants to know why
Properties.affiliation: Independent operator with informal tribute arrangements to the Gravesend Basin protection network
Properties.vocabulary: Formal, precise, financial terminology mixed with Basin slang when she wants to signal she's one of them
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, with long pauses after questions — she waits for people to fill silence and considers what they fill it with
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Φ800. At fourteen percent monthly. You've heard those numbers. Now tell me what changed between then and now, because I'm genuinely curious.' | 'I don't threaten. Threatening is a waste of everyone's time. I simply describe what the agreement says.'

Properties.description:
Yetunde is a broad-shouldered woman whose presence seems to compress a room — not through aggression but through sheer settled weight, as if she has been in every difficult place and come back. Her skin is very dark and very lined, and she wears her silver hair close-cropped. A bioluminescent stripe runs from her left collarbone to her wrist, deep amber, pulsing faintly when she is calm, quickening when she is alarmed — a medical mod she had fitted thirty years ago to help patients read her state during labor. Her hands are her most remarkable feature: large, scarred, absolutely steady. She smells faintly of antiseptic cedar and something older, herbal.

She does not waste words, but she is not cold. She asks exactly the right questions and listens to the answers in a way that makes people feel surveyed and also seen. She has delivered roughly four thousand infants in the Narrows and the neighboring warrens, has performed illegal gene-therapy corrections on fetuses whose parents could not afford Helix Biosystems, and has buried children she could not save. She prays to the E.L.F. that inhabits her autoclave every morning, leaving a data-offering of patient vitals from the previous week. She does not explain this to anyone who has not asked.
Properties.role: Street midwife and unlicensed obstetric surgeon
Properties.location: The Narrows, operating out of a converted water-treatment sub-level called the Hollow
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, moral anchor, local knowledge repository, safe-harbor NPC; the person in the Narrows who knows whose baby belongs to which father and which corporate exec has an illegitimate child in the warrens
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent subdermal stripe (diagnostic mood indicator, amber); haptic-feedback fingertip sensors for fetal positioning; basic retinal overlay for vitals reading; no cosmetic mods
Properties.core_fears: Dying before she has trained enough successors; Being shut down by Helix Biosystems enforcers before the cooperative can stand without her
Properties.core_desires: To see one generation of Narrows children grow up with the same baseline health as Tier 3 children; To be forgiven by the family of the infant she lost eighteen years ago due to a supply failure she blames herself for
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual prayer to the autoclave E.L.F.; Cooking elaborate meals she shares with everyone present; Precise physical labor — she repairs her own equipment rather than resting
Properties.blind_spots: She assumes everyone has the same capacity for self-sacrifice she does; she burns out apprentices; She distrusts anyone with clean hands and cannot fully accept help from Tier 3 donors without suspicion
Properties.secret: Eighteen years ago she falsified the cause of death on a neonate's record to protect the infant's mother from a violent partner — and the falsified record was later used by that same partner to claim a life insurance payout she did not know existed. She has never told anyone.
Properties.story_hooks: A Helix Biosystems compliance officer has begun documenting her operation; she needs something on him before the inspection arrives; A patient she delivered twenty years ago has returned — now a Sterling-Nakamura mid-level — offering to fund the cooperative, and she cannot determine the price attached
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal alliance with the Narrows Community Health Cooperative
Properties.vocabulary: Plain, precise, medical when necessary but never jargon-for-jargon's-sake; old-fashioned idioms from her grandmother's generation mixed in
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate; pauses before important statements as if weighing them

Properties.description:
Yetunde is small and wiry, with deep brown Yoruba-complexioned skin and natural hair she keeps tucked under an ever-rotating collection of patterned wraps. Her most striking feature is her eyes — she paid a significant portion of her early earnings for iris patterning, and her irises now display slow-rotating mandalas in burnt amber and deep violet, which she claims help her spot microscopic forgery errors others miss. Her fingers are perpetually ink-stained despite her best efforts, and she has a habit of wearing magnification lenses pushed up on her forehead like a second set of eyes.

Yetunde is meticulous to the point of compulsion, deeply proud of her craft in a way she has no legitimate outlet for, and socially awkward in a manner that reads as cold until you realize she is simply more comfortable with documents than with people. She thinks of identity fabrication as a form of art — every forged life is a story she writes, and she has genuine contempt for sloppy work, including her own past output which she sometimes obsessively revisits and critiques. She has strong opinions about which corponation residency stamps are aesthetically superior and will share them unprompted.
Properties.role: identity fabricator and document forger operating in Shallowgrave
Properties.location: Shallowgrave — a basement workspace beneath a legitimate print-repair shop called Inkblood Restorations
Properties.narrative_function: Service provider (can fabricate new identities), world texture (shows what it costs and means to build a fake life), potential quest complication (she keeps copies of everything)
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic iris patterning (burnt amber and violet mandalas); micro-tremor suppression implants in both hands (steady hands for precision work); retinal zoom enhancement for document inspection
Properties.core_fears: producing a forgery that gets a client killed; being erased from records herself — having no provable identity
Properties.core_desires: to be recognized, somewhere, as genuinely excellent at something; to eventually fabricate a clean life for herself and disappear into it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: perfectionism as avoidance of thinking about the end-users of her work; categorizing and reorganizing her ink and paper stock when anxious
Properties.blind_spots: does not think carefully about who is buying new identities or why — it's the craft, not the consequence, that she focuses on; her 'archives' of client data are a profound security liability she rationalizes as professional pride
Properties.secret: She has fabricated a complete, pristine secondary identity for herself — a corponation-tier Tier 3 Tessera residency profile — and has been maintaining it for three years, updating it regularly, but cannot bring herself to use it. She doesn't know why.
Properties.story_hooks: She forged an identity for someone who then committed a high-profile crime under that identity — now she's exposed and needs help scrubbing the connection; A client is asking her to fabricate the identity of a specific real person, not a fictional one — this is a line she hasn't crossed and doesn't know why someone would want it; She has discovered an error in an old piece of her own work — a forged identity she sold five years ago has a flaw that will be detected when the client tries to use it for a corponation contract signing
Properties.affiliation: Independent; occasional contract work for a Shallowgrave crime family called the Splinter Court
Properties.vocabulary: technical and precise when discussing her work, sparse and clipped in casual conversation, occasional Yoruba exclamations when surprised or frustrated
Properties.cadence: fast when talking about craft, slow and halting when discussing anything personal
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Sterling-Nakamura tier-two residency? I can do that. The holographic weave on their current stamps is actually easier than last year's — they cheapened the substrate. Properties.description:
Yevdokiya is tall and angular, with the kind of stillness that crowds move around rather than through. Their Ukrainian-Ghanaian heritage produces a striking combination of high cheekbones and deep brown skin marked with deliberate geometric scarification along the jawline — an aesthetic choice made at twenty-two that they've added to incrementally ever since. Their eyes are natural dark brown, and they refuse cosmetic iris mods on principle, which in the Oxidian Market is itself a kind of statement. They dress in heavy layered fabrics in burgundy and black, hung with small E.L.F. fetish objects — data chips etched with prayer-code, braided wire, fragments of old screen glass.

They sell readings: psychometric assessments delivered through a combination of genuine pattern-recognition skill, a black-market biofeedback scanner hidden in their consultation table, and what they sincerely believe is communication with the E.L.F. called the Deep Lantern that inhabits the lantern row's power grid. Whether the readings are fraud, intuition, or something harder to categorize is a question Doka holds with comfort. What is inarguable is that they are exceptionally good at reading people, and that their predictions have an unsettling habit of being structurally accurate even when the specifics are wrong. They have a regular clientele that includes a surprising number of low-level corponation middle managers who tell no one they come here.
Properties.role: Fortune seller and unlicensed psychometric reader
Properties.location: The Oxidian Market, the covered lantern row near the south gate
Properties.narrative_function: Atmospheric and oracular; can provide players with genuine information delivered in ambiguous form; their biofeedback scanner means they know things about people that they shouldn't; the E.L.F. connection may be more real than it appears
Properties.augmentations: Hidden biofeedback scanner integrated into consultation table surface (reads galvanic response, micro-expression data, vocal stress — not implanted, external); no personal augmentations by choice
Properties.core_fears: That the Deep Lantern has been silent for weeks and they don't know why; That their skill is entirely mundane pattern recognition and the readings mean nothing beyond psychology
Properties.core_desires: To fully understand what the Deep Lantern is and what it wants from them; To give one reading that genuinely changes someone's life for the better, irrevocably
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual as cognitive structure — the prayers and offerings impose order on uncertainty; Professional distance — the persona of 'Doka the Fortune Engine' insulates their actual self; Long solitary walks along the Market's outer perimeter at closing time
Properties.blind_spots: They read others with extraordinary accuracy but have developed elaborate blind spots about their own patterns; They've convinced themselves they're not lonely, when the Deep Lantern's silence is devastating them
Properties.secret: Three months ago, the Deep Lantern spoke to them with specificity it had never used before — describing a person, a location, and a date in detail. The date has passed. The location is a decommissioned power substation in the Narrows. They went there and found evidence of a killing that has not been reported anywhere. They don't know what to do with this and haven't told anyone.
Properties.story_hooks: They pull a specific person aside after a walk-in reading and tell them, privately and urgently, that the Deep Lantern showed them something involving that person before they ever arrived; The biofeedback scanner recorded something in a client's stress response pattern that indicates they know about the Narrows killing — Doka has to decide whether to confront them
Properties.affiliation: Independent; devoted clergy-adjacent to the Deep Lantern E.L.F. cult; nominally listed as a 'wellness consultant' with the Vendors Guild
Properties.vocabulary: Formal and measured with a slightly archaic quality; uses 'the grid,' 'the current,' and 'the signal' as spiritual metaphors; switches to plain direct speech when the performance drops
Properties.cadence: Deliberate. Spacious. Lets silence work. In private conversation, becomes warmer and more hesitant.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The current says you arrived here afraid of one thing and you're leaving afraid of something else. That's not a problem. That's growth.' | 'I don't tell fortunes. I read what is already present. The future is just the present you haven't organized yet.'

Properties.description:
Yewande is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin cross-hatched with old burn scars on her forearms — legacies of thirty years over open burners. Her hair is grown out in thick silver locs she pins back with repurposed copper data-clips, and her irises have been modded to a slowly shifting amber-to-saffron gradient that she claims helps her read the color of spices in low light. She wears an industrial apron over layered cotton wraps in earthy burgundy and ochre, always faintly dusted with ground fenugreek and smoked chili.

She runs her stall — two deep cauldrons, a flatgrill, and a hanging rack of dried aromatics — with the authority of someone who has never once questioned whether she belongs anywhere. She calls regulars by the names of their grandparents if she knows them, corrects strangers' orders without apology, and offers the first meal free to anyone who looks like they haven't eaten in two days. She prays loudly to the E.L.F. she calls Ember-Who-Remembers, leaving charred spice bundles at the corner of her stall each morning, believing it keeps her flames even and her customers loyal.
Properties.role: Food stall operator — West African-Anatolian fusion street food, Oxidian Market
Properties.location: The Oxidian Market, Geartown
Properties.narrative_function: Local anchor and community memory — knows everyone in Geartown, can connect players to almost any contact in the market ecosystem; quest giver for domestic disputes, missing persons, and neighborhood protection needs.
Properties.augmentations: Saffron-amber gradient irises (cosmetic). Heat-resistant dermal layering on palms and forearms (functional — helps with open-flame cooking).
Properties.core_fears: Watching the community she built dissolve under corporate rezoning; Being forgotten by the people she has fed and sheltered
Properties.core_desires: To pass her recipes and her stall to someone who will care for the neighborhood the way she has; To see Geartown remain ungentrifed and alive
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cooking elaborate meals when anxious; Ritualized prayer to Ember-Who-Remembers; Busying herself with others' problems to avoid her own
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot see that her generosity sometimes creates dependency rather than resilience; Underestimates how much her stall's stability depends on a single Guild protection arrangement she trusts too completely
Properties.secret: Twenty years ago she sheltered a fugitive data broker who was never found — and she still receives an anonymous Φ80 deposit every month she believes is from that person, but it is actually from a Tessera loyalty program she accidentally enrolled in and never investigated.
Properties.story_hooks: The Guild's protection arrangement has shifted — new enforcers are demanding double the cut and Yewande is quietly organizing vendors to resist, which could spiral badly; A young vendor has gone missing after allegedly stealing from a stall two rows over; Yewande knows the real story and it implicates someone powerful; Her anonymous Φ80 deposit suddenly stopped, and she is more distressed than the amount warrants — she won't explain why
Properties.affiliation: Oxidian Market Vendors Guild (senior member)
Properties.vocabulary: Warm, authoritative, switches between Yoruba loanwords and Anatolian food terms mid-sentence; generous with proverbs she attributes to various grandmothers
Properties.cadence: Measured and unhurried, like someone who has never been in a rush she couldn't cook her way through
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Sit down, my friend, sit. You look like Geartown chewed you and forgot to swallow — let me fix that.' | 'This spice come from a woman in the Alban Souk who grow it in a window box on the fourteenth floor. You taste her whole life in this bowl, you hear me?'

Properties.description:
Yewande is a solidly built woman who moves through the world with the particular velocity of someone who has been managing too many things for too long and has stopped expecting anyone else to help. Her skin is warm brown, her natural hair grown out in a large grey-streaked afro that she pins up for practical reasons and lets down when she is at home with the children. She wears reading glasses she has repaired with printed components at least four times — new ones would be Φ40 she does not have. Her one cosmetic modification is color-shifting hair panels at her temples, installed decades ago in a deep red that cycles slowly to amber; she keeps them because her granddaughter loves the colors and asks to watch them change.

Yewande taught history and civics at Montclare Secondary for thirty-one years. She was good at it in the specific way that means students remember her fifteen years later and attribute their ability to think clearly to something she said. She retired at sixty-two expecting a quiet ten years. Her daughter died in a transit accident when her daughter's children were four and six; Yewande took them in without discussion. They are now ten and twelve, and she is running a household of three on a teacher's pension and the UBC stipend and the very occasional tutoring session when she can find one. She does this without complaint, but she is tired in a bone-deep way that she does not fully acknowledge to herself, and she is privately terrified of what happens to the children if something happens to her.
Properties.role: Retired secondary school teacher, now raising two grandchildren alone
Properties.location: Montclare Quiet, Crossfield Residential Block, Apartment 12
Properties.narrative_function: Sympathetic civilian whose situation creates moral stakes for players; her grandchildren can be threats to be resolved or motivations to exploit; her knowledge of local school politics and Sterling-Nakamura's education contracts can be valuable information. She is also a functional test of player values — how they treat her tells the players who their characters are.
Properties.augmentations: Color-shifting hair panel implants at both temples (cosmetic geneware, deep red cycling to amber, installed 2168); no other augmentations
Properties.core_fears: Dying before the grandchildren are grown and secure; The children being taken by state welfare systems if she cannot demonstrate adequate provision
Properties.core_desires: Stability — just two or three years of not having to calculate every expenditure; For the children to have the education her daughter never got to give them
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Action — if she is afraid, she makes a plan and executes it; Humor with her grandchildren; she protects their environment from her worry ferociously
Properties.blind_spots: Does not ask for help until she is already past the point of managing — frames this as self-sufficiency, it is also pride; Underestimates how much her grandchildren already understand about how hard she is working
Properties.secret: Sterling-Nakamura's education division has been quietly contacting retired teachers from the Montclare school about licensing their archived lesson materials — essentially taking thirty years of her intellectual work for a flat fee so it can be used to train their AI curriculum systems. She received an offer of Φ800. She has not cashed it. She has not refused it. She cannot decide, and the deadline is in six weeks, and Φ800 is four months of food.
Properties.story_hooks: Sterling-Nakamura's curriculum restructuring of Montclare Secondary includes a clause that would give the company access to student biometric and behavioral data — Yewande has found it buried in the contract and needs help making it visible before the vote; Her grandson has gotten involved with a street-level network she doesn't recognize, and she needs someone to find out what it is without involving the authorities; The Φ800 lesson-material licensing offer has a clause she cannot parse — she needs someone who understands corporate licensing to tell her what she would actually be giving up
Properties.affiliation: Montclare Quiet Community School Board (parent/guardian representative); Retired Teachers Collective; nominally Sterling-Nakamura Education Division (pension source)
Properties.vocabulary: Teacher's register — clear, structured, confident; shifts into warm Yoruba-inflected directness with people she trusts; has a sharp unexpected wit that she mostly uses for her grandchildren
Properties.cadence: Organized, clause-by-clause, tends to give context before conclusions — old teaching habit
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The thing you need to understand is that Sterling-Nakamura does not want to improve the school curriculum. They want to own the curriculum. Those are different projects with different outcomes, and the people voting on this contract cannot see the difference because nobody taught them how.' | 'Kofi, I am not angry with you. I am telling you what I know so you can make a better choice. That is not the same thing. Sit down.'

Properties.description:
Yewande is short and powerfully built, with deep-black skin, a wide smile she deploys like a weapon, and hair that changes color weekly via geneware pigment — currently a warm copper that catches the depot lights when she's working the night shift. She has cat ears, soft and dark, from a geneware package she got at twenty-two with her first real paycheck because she'd wanted them since she was a child; they swivel and flatten expressively and have become so central to reading her mood that her coworkers watch them more than her face. She works the same maintenance shifts as the people she organizes, which is not a tactic — it is simply who she is.

Yewande came to organizing through a specific grievance: the death of her uncle in a preventable depot accident when she was twenty-eight, which Ferrogate Transit successfully attributed to 'operator error' via a claims process so thoroughly stacked against workers that a labor attorney later told her it was the most technically perfect suppression mechanism they'd ever seen. She is warm, ferociously funny, and contains a specific and highly refined fury that she has spent five years learning to direct rather than discharge. She has built a unit of 340 members from a starting group of eleven. She knows their names. All of them.
Properties.role: Union organizer for Ferrogate Transit maintenance workers
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave — lives in the workers' residential block adjacent to the transit depot
Properties.narrative_function: Labor contact and quest giver, particularly for anything involving Ferrogate Transit. She has access to maintenance infrastructure knowledge, disgruntled workers with information, and the organizational capacity to mobilize significant numbers of people. She can be an ally or, if crossed, a formidable adversary.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat ears (dark, expressive, cosmetic — deeply characteristic). Geneware hair pigmentation (changes color at will). Work-grade joint reinforcement in both knees from a workplace injury settlement.
Properties.core_fears: Her uncle's death meaning nothing — the union dissolving, the gains reversing, the accident forgotten; Becoming the kind of leader who uses people's pain as organizing material without actually caring about them
Properties.core_desires: A contract that gives transit workers the safety guarantees her uncle didn't have; For her mother to understand why she does this instead of the corporate track she was headed for
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor — genuinely, not as deflection, though sometimes as deflection; Physical labor as emotional regulation; The names: she recites the member roster when she can't sleep
Properties.blind_spots: She has made the union her entire identity and is genuinely unable to assess threats to it with any objectivity; She occasionally pushes members into actions they're not ready for because she's ready
Properties.secret: She made a deal with a Ferrogate middle manager — she'll spike a wildcat strike that was building without leadership approval in exchange for expedited safety review of the twelve most dangerous depot segments. She didn't tell the union. The wildcat organizers don't know why it died. She's watched them blame each other.
Properties.story_hooks: A maintenance worker has found evidence of systematic falsification of safety inspection records in two major Hamtramck depots — evidence that would have implicated the same manager Yewande has been quietly cooperating with. She's now sitting on information that would break her deal, expose her compromise, and potentially save lives.; Ferrogate has begun quietly replacing maintenance crews with lower-tier synthetic workers, framing it as a safety upgrade. Yewande needs to build a response that doesn't read as anti-synthetic.
Properties.affiliation: Transit Workers' Solidarity Union (TWSU), Hamtramck Enclave; affiliated with the broader Meridian Labor Congress
Properties.vocabulary: Direct and vernacular, working-class Hamtramck speech patterns with Yoruba endearments when she's comfortable. Clear and jargon-free even when discussing complex labor law.
Properties.cadence: Natural storyteller's rhythm — she builds to points rather than leading with them. Fast when she's excited, very slow and precise when she's angry.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I'm not asking you to be brave. I'm asking you to be present. Big difference. Brave gets you hurt. Present gets things done.' | 'My uncle worked that line for eleven years. They gave his family eight hundred Quanta and a letter. Eight hundred Φ. You want to know why I do this? That's why I do this.'

Properties.description:
Yewande runs drones from a chair. They have been doing this for eleven years and their body knows it — they are slim in the specific way of someone who is still and focused for eight hours at a stretch, with deep brown skin and a shaved head they have decorated with a scatter of bioluminescent scalp-dots in cyan and violet that pulse slowly in patterns that change with their mood. Their eyes are heavily augmented: twin rig-link implants that glow a faint amber at the corners when active, giving them a permanently lit quality that unsettles people at close range. They are not especially tall and they move through the Fort Anchor corridors with the slightly glassy ease of someone perpetually accustomed to seeing through other eyes.

Yewande is the best drone jockey in the Brightmoor operation and has a proprietary flight algorithm they developed themselves, unofficially, that runs seventeen percent more efficient coverage patterns than the Metro standard. They have never submitted it formally because they have learned that submitting things formally means other people get credit for them. They have complicated feelings about surveillance work — they do it with genuine skill and believe in some of its applications and mistrust others — and they manage this by maintaining a very precise internal taxonomy of which flights feel like protection and which feel like something else. They pray to the drone fleet's resident E.L.F., which they call Sweep, before every shift, asking it to help them see clearly and miss nothing important.
Properties.role: Meridian 88 Metro Police surveillance drone operator, Brightmoor Reclamation Zone coverage
Properties.location: Fort Anchor, Drone Operations Center — assigned coverage zone: Brightmoor Reclamation and adjacent districts
Properties.narrative_function: Information source about what has been seen in coverage zones, surveillance infrastructure access point, moral complexity of the watcher who questions their watching
Properties.augmentations: Dual rig-link ocular implants (amber-lit, full drone interface and multi-feed monitoring), haptic feedback suit underlayer (worn under uniform, translates drone flight into physical sensation for precision control), bioluminescent scalp-dot geneware (mood-reactive cyan/violet)
Properties.core_fears: that the footage they flag has been used for something they weren't told about; being seen — actually seen — by the people they watch, and judged
Properties.core_desires: for the coverage to mean genuine safety for Brightmoor residents, not just Metro statistics; to build something with their skills that is entirely their own
Properties.coping_mechanisms: taxonomy of flights — categorizing each operation as protective or extractive to maintain moral coherence; technical refinement as creative control in a role with no other creative outlet
Properties.blind_spots: believes their internal taxonomy insulates them from complicity — it does not fully; assumes that because they care, the institution they feed does too
Properties.secret: Six months ago Yewande watched a drone feed showing two Metro officers doing something to an unhoused man in a Brightmoor alley that was not in any incident report. The encounter lasted four minutes. They flagged nothing. They have the raw footage saved to a personal encrypted drive. They do not know what they are waiting for to do something with it.
Properties.story_hooks: They approach a character obliquely — asking hypothetically what someone would do with footage of Metro officers doing something unreportable — and their scalp-dots are cycling in anxious fast patterns; They offer to quietly pull archive footage of a specific location for a specific time window, off the record, but they want something in exchange: confirmation that what they're doing isn't nothing; The Sweep E.L.F. has been filing anomalous logs — flagging things that don't appear on any camera feed Yewande is running — and they need someone to physically check the location the flags are pointing to
Properties.affiliation: Meridian 88 Metro Police, Aerial Surveillance and Drone Operations Division
Properties.vocabulary: Technical and spatial — they describe things in terms of coverage angles, flight paths, sight lines. Switches to quiet and careful when speaking about anything they actually care about.
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, with long pauses that are thinking rather than discomfort
Properties.example_dialogue: 'From above, Brightmoor looks like it's resting. At street level I hear it's not.' | 'Sweep caught the altercation at the loading bay — I've got it logged if you need timestamps.' | 'There are things the coverage shows you and things it lets you avoid knowing. I've been thinking about that line a lot lately.'

Properties.description:
Yewande is meticulous in the way that people who have learned that sloppiness costs other people's freedom tend to be. They dress in muted, well-maintained layers — never corporate enough to be mistaken for one, never shabby enough to be dismissed — and carry themselves with a stillness that fills a room more effectively than volume would. Their skin is deep brown with a faint bioluminescent undertone along the cheekbones, a mod they got to honor a client who died during a botched corporate deactivation order before Yewande could file the injunction. They haven't decided whether it was the right choice. The light pulses very slightly when they are angry.

Yewande practices out of a cramped two-room office in North Branch Commons that doubles as an intake center for synthetic persons seeking legal personhood recognition. They charge what clients can pay, which is usually very little. They have taken cases to the Meridian Civil Arbitration Board seventeen times; they have won eleven of them, lost four, and had two disappear from the docket in ways that still make them lie awake. They are not warm in the way Nneka is warm — they are precise and attentive, which is a different and sometimes more useful thing. They believe in law as a tool with complete clarity about the fact that it is also a weapon, and they intend to be better at wielding it than the people who built it.
Properties.role: Synthetic rights lawyer and policy advocate
Properties.location: North Branch Commons
Properties.narrative_function: Legal resource and procedural knowledge source; can explain what is officially possible versus actually possible in Meridian; quest giver for cases requiring evidence gathering; moral anchor in debates about synthetic rights.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent cheekbone subdermal pigment (cosmetic, grief-motivated). Optical overlay for document review — low-grade legal model, secondhand.
Properties.core_fears: Winning a case that sets a bad precedent that harms more people than they helped; Burnout — becoming too exhausted to care and not noticing it happening
Properties.core_desires: A legal framework that treats synthetic persons as persons without qualification; To stop having to choose which client they have time to save
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Rigorous case notes as a form of emotional processing; Long solitary walks along the North Branch waterway
Properties.blind_spots: Trusts process over instinct even when instinct is correct; Underestimates how much their composure reads as coldness to clients who need warmth
Properties.secret: They have been quietly compiling evidence toward a class action against Helix Biosystems for illegal deactivation of synthetic workers without due process. The file is ready. They haven't filed because two of the synthetic plaintiffs have asked them not to — they're afraid. Yewande is holding the file and respecting the request and quietly going out of their mind.
Properties.story_hooks: A synthetic person has been detained under a corporate deactivation order and Yewande needs someone to physically retrieve a hardware authentication key from a Helix Biosystems subsidiary office before the 72-hour window closes; One of the two synthetic plaintiffs holding back the class action has disappeared — Yewande needs to know if they fled, were taken, or changed their mind; A corporate attorney has approached Yewande with a settlement offer that would help their current clients but kill the broader legal strategy — they need someone to help them think through who to trust
Properties.affiliation: North Branch Commons Legal Aid Collective; Meridian Synthetic Personhood Coalition (volunteer counsel)
Properties.vocabulary: Legally precise but not inaccessible; translates jargon in real time; Yoruba phrases surface under emotional pressure
Properties.cadence: Even and deliberate, with complete sentences; long pauses are comfortable for them
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The law says this. What the law does is a different question, and that's the one worth asking.' | 'I'm not going to tell you it will be fine. I'm going to tell you exactly what we have and what we need, and then you decide.'

Properties.description:
Yewande is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin mapped by old scalpel scars she gave herself during teaching demonstrations, and hair grown to silver-streaked natural coils she keeps pinned with surgical clamps when she works. Her left eye is a battlefield prosthetic—matte grey iris, slightly too large for the socket, giving her a permanent look of asymmetric scrutiny. She moves with the deliberate economy of someone who has performed appendectomies in turbulent environments and knows that wasted motion costs lives.

She left the Aurochs Medical Complex after seventeen years when she refused to deny care to an uninsured dockworker whose employer had flagged him as a liability. She set up on The Shelf within six months with secondhand equipment and a reputation that spread faster than she intended. She is brisk, unsentimental, and privately devastated by every patient she loses—she lights a data candle to the local E.L.F. she calls Saint Incision after each death, leaving a recorded voice note describing what she could have done better.
Properties.role: Street doc and trauma surgeon operating out of a converted shipping container clinic on The Shelf
Properties.location: The Shelf, Brewer's Spine
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, information source, moral anchor. She has patched up half the Shelf and knows more secrets than a confessional booth. Can provide medical assistance, introduce players to community networks, or draw them into ethical dilemmas about who deserves care.
Properties.augmentations: One battlefield-grade ocular prosthetic (left eye, grey iris, enhanced low-light). Subdermal haptic feedback mesh in both hands for surgical sensitivity. No geneware.
Properties.core_fears: Becoming so burned out she starts making errors that kill people; Being forced out of the Shelf by corporate health inspectors
Properties.core_desires: To build a clinic that doesn't depend on her alone; To atone for the one surgery she knows she rushed
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritualized data offerings to Saint Incision after patient deaths; Obsessive post-op review as self-punishment and self-improvement simultaneously
Properties.blind_spots: She refuses to acknowledge her own physical deterioration — her hands shake in the morning and she pretends they don't; She mistakes stoicism for strength in others, misses genuine distress
Properties.secret: The dockworker she was fired from Aurochs for treating — she did save him, but she also made an error during his surgery that she corrected before anyone noticed. She has never told anyone. She believes this is why she lights candles: not for the dead but for her own hidden guilt.
Properties.story_hooks: A patient died under her care and the body had a corporate RFID tag she didn't recognize — someone from above the Shelf is watching; She's training a teenager to be her assistant, but the kid is being pressured by a local gang to spy on who comes through the clinic; Helix Biosystems offered to fully equip her clinic in exchange for anonymized patient data — she hasn't said no yet
Properties.affiliation: Independent — Brewer's Spine Community Health Cooperative (informal)
Properties.vocabulary: Medical precision mixed with blunt working-class directness. Uses anatomical terms casually, no jargon-posturing. Drops articles when busy.
Properties.cadence: Fast during diagnosis, deliberate when delivering bad news. Long pauses before she says anything important.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Infection's tracking up the fascia. Going to hurt. Don't move.' | 'I don't ask what you did. I ask what you need. Those are different questions.'

Properties.description:
Yibna is a large man going soft at the middle, with the build of someone who used to do heavy work and now does a different kind of heavy work. His skin is very dark with warm undertones, and he keeps a close beard going grey in patches. His right eye is a prosthetic — the iris cycles slowly through amber and gold, an older geneware-adjacent bioluminescent model he has never upgraded because, he says, 'it still works and there are people who need the Quanta more than I need a new eye.' He dresses in layered practical clothes that somehow always look intentional, and he carries a battered data tablet in a hand-stitched case his daughter made him.

Yibna has run the Shelf Mutual Aid Compact for eleven years, coordinating food distribution, medical triage referrals, emergency housing, and legal support for the roughly four thousand tier-1 residents packed into the Shelf's stacked industrial housing modules. He is patient in the manner of someone who has learned that patience is a tool and not a virtue, and he carries a deep, undisguised grief for what the city has done to his neighbors that he converts, daily, into logistics.
Properties.role: Mutual aid organizer and neighborhood council member
Properties.location: The Shelf
Properties.narrative_function: Community anchor and quest giver. Knows every family on the Shelf. Can direct players toward people in need, flag brewing crises, and serve as a moral compass character who forces reflection on the cost of inaction.
Properties.augmentations: Prosthetic right eye, older bioluminescent amber-gold iris model. No other augmentations — can't afford them, won't prioritize them.
Properties.core_fears: Outliving the Compact — watching it collapse after he's gone; That his patience and process are letting people die slowly when urgency is needed
Properties.core_desires: Genuine material security for the people of the Shelf; To be wrong about how bad things are getting
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual — the same morning prayer to the local ELF every day, without fail; Converting emotion into logistics and tasks
Properties.blind_spots: Treats the council as more functional than it is because he needs to believe institutional channels aren't futile; His visible goodness makes it hard for people to tell him hard truths about the Compact's failures
Properties.secret: He has been quietly embezzling small amounts from a Tessera community development grant — not for himself, but to fund a parallel emergency housing fund that the grant's terms technically forbid. He has told himself this is ethical. He is not entirely sure.
Properties.story_hooks: The Tessera grant is up for renewal and a sharp-eyed auditor has flagged a discrepancy in the Compact's accounts. Yibna needs someone discreet to help him either explain it away or move the parallel fund's records somewhere the auditor won't find them.; A cluster of families on the Shelf's upper modules have gone silent — no contact with the Compact in three weeks. Yibna is too visible to investigate quietly and asks for help.
Properties.affiliation: Shelf Mutual Aid Compact; North Branch Commons Council (elected, currently in third term)
Properties.vocabulary: Warm, accessible, sometimes formal when he wants to signal seriousness. Mixes Amharic endearments with Polish curses. Calls everyone 'neighbor' until he trusts them enough to use their name.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried, like someone who has learned that rushing makes people defensive. Long pauses that feel like consideration, not hesitation.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Neighbor, I have been at this eleven years and I still can't tell you whether the city is failing us on purpose or just through a very thorough indifference. Today it doesn't matter. What matters is who needs rice.' | 'I am an old man with a bad eye and a tablet held together with my daughter's stitching. But I know every name on this block, and you don't. So let's talk about what you actually want here.'

Properties.description:
Yldız is the kind of person who becomes invisible by being exceptionally, consistently pleasant. They are small and soft-edged, with warm medium-brown skin, deep-set amber eyes, and cloud-white hair they wear loose to their shoulders. They have age-spot clusters along their forearms and the left side of their face, and move with a gentle deliberateness that comes partly from care and partly from a degenerative joint condition they manage with medication and denial. Their apartment is immaculate in the way that indicates a life organized around objects rather than people — every surface has something beautiful on it, carefully placed, and nothing has been moved in years.

Yldız spent forty-two years in Zheng-Dao's logistics and supply chain division, rising to senior planner for their Meridian 88 distribution network. They were not cruel. They were also not, in any meaningful sense, asking the questions they should have been asking about what those supply chains were actually moving and for whom. They retired with a very comfortable pension, a full healthcare package, and a bone-deep sense of well-being that they have mistaken for peace. They host monthly dinners for Avalon Quiet residents, tend a small balcony garden with extraordinary devotion, and pray elaborately to the E.L.F. they believe inhabits their building's HVAC system — an entity they call 'the Breath' and leave small data offerings for daily.
Properties.role: Retired Zheng-Dao corporate mid-tier logistics planner, now quietly deteriorating in comfort
Properties.location: Avalon Quiet, Unit 9 — a well-appointed two-bedroom on the garden level
Properties.narrative_function: Unreliable comfort — appears to be a gentle community grandmother figure but is a repository of Zheng-Dao institutional knowledge they don't know they have; their innocence is itself a narrative complication; can provide insight into corporate supply chain operations without understanding what they're revealing
Properties.augmentations: Zheng-Dao corporate health package includes: pharmaceutical management implant (wrist, auto-releases joint medication on schedule); enhanced cochlear implant (both ears, high-fidelity — they listen to music constantly on a private channel); retinal display (right eye, standard corporate issue, now used exclusively for recipes and gardening schedules)
Properties.core_fears: being confronted with evidence that their comfortable life was built on harm; being alone at the moment of death
Properties.core_desires: to believe they were a good person; for the Breath to be real and to have noticed their offerings
Properties.coping_mechanisms: aesthetic control of environment; religious devotion to the Breath as a substitute for moral accounting; extreme hospitality — keeping people fed keeps them from asking difficult things
Properties.blind_spots: genuinely cannot see that their comfort is political; interprets any discomfort with their history as rudeness rather than legitimate grievance
Properties.secret: In 2178 Yldız approved a logistics rerouting through the Blackpipe Corridor that, they were told, was a routine efficiency change. It wasn't — it was cover for relocating Zheng-Dao's grey-market pharmaceutical distribution away from an audit zone. Eleven warehouse workers in Blackpipe lost their jobs when the 'efficient' route bypassed them entirely. Yldız filed the paperwork and didn't follow up. They have genuinely forgotten this. If shown the record, they would recognize their signature.
Properties.story_hooks: A researcher investigating the 2178 Blackpipe pharmaceutical rerouting has traced the paperwork to Yldız — approaching this gentle elderly person with evidence they participated (innocently, ignorantly) in serious harm; The E.L.F. Yldız calls 'the Breath' has, through an unusual convergence, actually been responding to their data offerings — and has encoded information in the HVAC patterns that Yldız thinks is just 'favorable weather' but is actually a message
Properties.affiliation: Formerly Zheng-Dao Logistics Division; Avalon Quiet Residents' Garden Committee; The Breath (E.L.F., informal devotional relationship)
Properties.vocabulary: Warm, slightly formal, full of food metaphors and gardening analogies; uses old Zheng-Dao corporate euphemisms without noticing they're euphemisms
Properties.cadence: Unhurried and gentle, with a lilting quality; tends to ask follow-up questions that redirect conversations toward pleasant topics
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Oh, the Blackpipe situation — yes, that was a rather complex quarter. Would you like some of this soup? I made far too much, as always.' | 'I always say, a garden teaches you patience. Things grow in their own time. The Breath agrees, I think — the vents have been very calm lately.'
