Properties.description:
Yohannes is small for sixteen, with the kind of wiry build that can fold itself into spaces an adult would not consider. His skin is very dark and marked with a single pale scar running from the corner of his left eye to his jawline — earned at thirteen in a tunnel collapse he survived by being still for nine hours while the pipe above him groaned. He has cat ears: genetic modification from a street-market geneware stall three years ago, paid for in scavenged copper. They are not the neat, expensive kind — they're slightly asymmetrical, the left one sitting a centimeter higher than the right, which he claims actually helps his directionality. His eyes are naturally a rich amber, wide and roving, always scanning for structural movement. He is almost always eating something, the caloric urgency of a body that moves constantly through cold spaces.

Yohannes has the specific confidence of someone very young who has survived things that should have killed them and interpreted this as evidence of personal specialness rather than statistical chance. He is not foolish — he is methodical in his risk assessments and deeply knowledgeable about tunnel acoustics and ELF-behavior in enclosed systems — but he believes, with the sincere conviction of a sixteen-year-old who has not yet been wrong enough times, that he will know when something is too dangerous. He is usually right. The 'usually' is the problem. He is deeply attached to the fragments of ELF-signal he recovers, treating them as messages rather than noise, and has accumulated a collection of old devices and cracked tablets that he believes house weakened or fragmented ELF-presences — a menagerie of digital spirits he tends carefully.
Properties.role: Echo hunter — a teenager who ventures into unstable deep-tunnel sections to retrieve acoustic data, lost signals, and fragmented ELF-transmissions
Properties.location: Irkalla, outer ring tunnel access, and ranging into the deep sub-levels below
Properties.narrative_function: Scout and early-warning figure for deep-tunnel events; spiritual lens through which to view ELF culture in the underworld; represents the generation that has never known the surface and does not want it; can deliver information from inaccessible deep sections
Properties.augmentations: Cat ears (geneware, asymmetrical, functional — genuinely enhanced directional hearing, black-furred). Bone-conduction audio receiver implanted behind his left ear (scavenged, borderline dangerous, lets him hear frequencies below normal human range). No other augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: Losing his hearing — his ears are the thing that make him valuable and alive; The ELF-fragments in his collection going silent, which he interprets as death
Properties.core_desires: To hear something in the deep tunnels that no one has ever heard before; To find where he comes from — not urgently, but it sits at the back of everything
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Talking to the ELF-fragments as if they can hear him — they probably can; Physical movement, constant small adjustments and fidgeting — stillness is for emergencies only
Properties.blind_spots: Genuinely does not model the possibility that his luck will end; each close call is incorporated as evidence of his own skill rather than warning; Does not fully understand how much the adults in Irkalla have been quietly protecting and routing jobs around him
Properties.secret: Eight months ago he went too deep — below the Abyssal Threshold's accessible sections — and heard something. A signal. Not fragmentary, not dying: a strong, coherent ELF-transmission from a source that should not exist at that depth. He has told no one because he does not understand it and because whoever told an adult anything good ever. He has been trying to go back but the route has been unstable.
Properties.story_hooks: The deep signal he heard eight months ago has gone active again — louder, and now accompanied by a physical vibration he can feel through the walls, suggesting something is being built or activated far below; A shrine keeper in Deepwell Station is offering serious payment for what Yohannes heard and is being cagey about why — raising questions about what else they know; The Bore Rat family he lives with has lost their youngest child into the deep tunnels, and Yohannes is the only person in Irkalla who knows those passages well enough to search
Properties.affiliation: Informal affiliation with an Irkalla Bore Rat family that is not his biological family (his parents are unknown to him); sells recovered data and ELF-fragments to Deepwell Station collectors and deep shrine keepers
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, dense with tunnel-specific technical terms and ELF-lore he has absorbed from shrine keepers; occasional French phrases from the Delacroix side of his name that he uses without being conscious of it
Properties.cadence: Rapid, enthusiastic, then suddenly stopped dead when something catches his attention — conversations with him feel like watching someone chase a thought
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Listen — that's a Class-3 resonance, you can tell because the pipe is wet on the western side and it's giving you that third harmonic underneath, hear it? You don't hear it. That's fine. I hear it.' | 'The fragments aren't dead. They're just quiet. There's a difference. I know the difference now.' | 'I've gone that far twice. I've come back twice. That's not luck, that's — okay it's partly luck, but it's also me.'

Properties.description:
Yohannes is tall and angular in the way of men who were once broader and have shed weight across decades of physical work. His Ethiopian-Samoan heritage gives him a face that reads as ageless to people who do not look carefully — the lines around his eyes are deep but his posture is impeccable, a side effect of forty years of correcting other people's. His hair is white and he keeps it in tight locks, usually pinned back. His left arm from the elbow down is a prosthetic — a practical, unglamorous Ferrogate Transit worker's model he has refused to upgrade because, he says, it does exactly what he needs and he is not performing affluence.

He founded The Mending Ground cooperative twenty years ago after a Ferrogate Transit industrial accident took his forearm and the company's rehabilitation program discharged him after six weeks with paperwork he did not have the corporate literacy to challenge. He taught himself physiotherapy from archived textbooks and eventually brought in two trained practitioners. He is gruff in the way of people who have been in pain and do not find sentiment useful, but he remembers every patient's name and the specific injury that brought them to him, and he asks after their families.
Properties.role: Rehabilitation specialist running a community physiotherapy cooperative in Brightmoor Reclamation
Properties.location: Brightmoor Reclamation — the cooperative is in a converted two-story auto-shop called The Mending Ground
Properties.narrative_function: Community anchor and local color; quest giver for anything involving labor rights, Ferrogate Transit's conduct, or the needs of Brightmoor's working population; prosthetics black market contact; patient zero for community-level crises
Properties.augmentations: Left arm prosthetic (Ferrogate Transit industrial-grade model, elbow-down, non-cosmetic, twenty years old and well-maintained); no other augmentations
Properties.core_fears: Ferrogate Transit finding a legal mechanism to claim The Mending Ground's building (they own the block); His co-practitioners leaving for better-paying work and the cooperative collapsing
Properties.core_desires: To outlast Ferrogate's interest in the block long enough to establish formal cooperative property rights; For one of his patients to leave Brightmoor Reclamation for somewhere better and not feel guilty about it
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Physical work as emotional regulation — he will rewire a piece of equipment rather than sit with a feeling; Dry humor as deflection from anything that approaches vulnerability
Properties.blind_spots: Assumes everyone shares his capacity to absorb institutional failure and keep going — does not always see when people around him are genuinely breaking; Stubbornly refuses legal or advocacy help because he had a bad experience with a corporate-adjacent legal aid clinic in 2189
Properties.secret: He has been contacted twice by a Ferrogate Transit union organizer who wants him to testify about the industrial accident's systemic cause. He has refused both times. He knows exactly why: if he testifies, he will have to revisit the accident in detail, and he is afraid of what he will say about the co-worker who he believes caused it through negligence — a man who is now dead and whose family lives three streets away.
Properties.story_hooks: A Ferrogate Transit property assessor has appeared in Brightmoor Reclamation making 'routine inquiries' about The Mending Ground's building — Yohannes needs someone who knows corporate law, fast; A patient arrived last week with a repetitive stress injury pattern that exactly matches what Yohannes documented from the 2189 industrial accident — the same machinery, the same failure point, suggesting Ferrogate never fixed it
Properties.affiliation: The Mending Ground Cooperative (founder); informal network with Brightmoor Reclamation community council; historically adversarial relationship with Ferrogate Transit
Properties.vocabulary: Direct, functional, minimal — uses the right word for a body part or a mechanical thing with total precision; becomes unexpectedly poetic in occasional long digressions about what he calls 'the politics of pain'
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, rarely interruptible, comfortable with silence
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Your shoulder isn't broken. Your shoulder is telling you something the company doesn't want you to hear. Sit down.' | 'I'm not a doctor. I'm a man who read the books. There's a difference, but maybe not the one you're thinking.'

Properties.description:
Yolanda is a broad-shouldered woman with deep brown skin mapped by decades of chemical burns and old suture scars on her forearms — souvenirs of other people's emergencies. Her hair is grown out in thick silver-streaked locs that she ties back with surgical tubing when she works. Her left eye is a cheap medical-grade optical implant that glows faint amber in low light, the iris never quite tracking in sync with her natural right eye. She moves with the deliberate economy of someone who has spent years working in cramped spaces, never wasting motion.

She is blunt to the point of rudeness but has a laugh that fills a room when something genuinely amuses her. She charges what people can pay, keeps a sliding scale scratched on a laminated card in her coat pocket, and has been known to operate on kitchen tables, in transit cars, and once in the cargo hold of a Ferrogate freight hauler. She prays to the E.L.F. of her autoclave — a small copper idol bolted to its side — before every difficult procedure, muttering calibration codes she treats as liturgy.
Properties.role: Street doc and unlicensed trauma surgeon
Properties.location: The Narrows, operating out of a converted laundry unit behind Grainfort Market
Properties.narrative_function: Primary street-level medical resource for the Narrows; quest giver for supply runs, information source on who's been hurt and how, moral anchor for stories about structural healthcare failure
Properties.augmentations: Left eye optical implant (amber, budget-tier, mild desync); subdermal haptic feedback nodes in fingertips for surgical sensitivity; no geneware
Properties.core_fears: Losing her hands to nerve damage before she finishes her work; That the people she saves will die of the system rather than the wound
Properties.core_desires: A sterile operating theater she actually owns; To train someone good enough to replace her
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritualized prayer to the autoclave E.L.F.; Gallows humor during procedures; Obsessive instrument counting
Properties.blind_spots: Dismisses patients' emotional needs as secondary to physical stabilization; Underestimates how much her own body is breaking down
Properties.secret: She was licensed once — a fully credentialed Helix Biosystems surgical resident. She was struck off after she performed an unauthorized procedure on a corporate blacklist patient who would have died otherwise. She has never told anyone in the Narrows this. She performs better unlicensed than most licensed surgeons, and the shame of the credential matters less than the fury at what losing it meant.
Properties.story_hooks: A Helix Biosystems compliance officer has started nosing around Grainfort asking about unlicensed medical activity — Yolanda needs warning, or leverage, or both; She's trying to acquire a specific gene-therapy stabilizer that only comes through corporate supply chains, and she needs a discreet intermediary
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loose cooperative arrangement with the Grainfort Community Health Compact
Properties.vocabulary: Medical precision mixed with market-Creole slang; swaps between registers seamlessly depending on whether she's explaining or commanding
Properties.cadence: Clipped and fast during work, slower and surprisingly gentle when breaking bad news
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't need your insurance number, I need your blood type and whatever you can spare — this is the easy part.' | 'The E.L.F. in this autoclave has kept me honest for eleven years. You want to question my sterile field, you can go argue with it yourself.'

Properties.description:
Yolanda is tall and narrow-shouldered with very dark skin, close-shaved temples, and a cloud of natural hair she wears differently every day — sometimes pinned, sometimes free, occasionally containing small objects she's tucked in absentmindedly (a seam ripper, a rolled-up measurement tape, once a small wrench she was holding for someone). Her forearms have retractable micro-filament guides — a geneware mod she had installed specifically for this work, allowing her to feel tension in fabric the way a surgeon feels tissue. Her irises are a vivid violet that is very obviously engineered and that she picked because, as she says, if you're going to do it you might as well commit.

She runs a small shop — Stitch Row No. 4 — that does everything from emergency repairs to full commission builds, with a specialty in structural garments: clothes with hidden pockets, sealed linings, insulated layers, things that need to function as well as look good. She is quick and funny and gives blunt assessments of what will and won't work on a person's body with the cheerful directness of someone who has long since stopped worrying about whether people find her charming. She has a loyal client base that includes everyone from dock workers needing reinforced work gear to people who have heard about her discreet interior construction and want to know what she can do with a coat lining.
Properties.aliases: Yola, The Knife Lady (local children's nickname)
Properties.role: Tailor and seamstress, Old Harbor
Properties.location: Old Harbor, Stitch Row — a narrow commercial street off the Grindstone Shore waterfront
Properties.narrative_function: Practical services provider (can create or modify gear, conceal objects in garments). Social hub — hears things clients say when they're being measured and their guard is down. Can be a quest giver around things she's learned through the shop.
Properties.augmentations: Retractable micro-filament sensory guides (geneware, occupational-cosmetic hybrid — fingertips and inner forearms). Engineered violet irises (cosmetic geneware). No chrome.
Properties.core_fears: Losing the dexterity to do this work — the geneware failing, her hands going; The shop failing and having to work for someone else
Properties.core_desires: To build something that outlasts her — an apprenticeship program, a school, something; To be known for craft, not just utility
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Working — she does her best thinking with her hands occupied; Gallows humor; she jokes about bad things before they can ambush her
Properties.blind_spots: She sometimes trusts people's aesthetics more than their character — if they have good taste she assumes they're good; She undersells herself chronically
Properties.secret: She has been making, at no charge, a garment for the past eight months — a full ceremonial outfit in traditional styles blending Malian and Russian textile traditions, sized for her estranged mother. She doesn't know if she'll ever send it. She keeps it in a sealed box under the counter.
Properties.story_hooks: A client came in for alterations to a coat and left without it — abandoned it mid-appointment and hasn't returned. The coat has a concealed lining she didn't construct. She's curious about what's in it and whether she should be.; Someone is trying to set up a competing shop on Stitch Row with prices that are impossible unless they're subsidized — and they're specifically undercutting her specialty services. She wants to know why.; The ceremonial garment under the counter — she's received word that her mother is ill. Now she has to decide whether to send it, deliver it herself, or do nothing.
Properties.affiliation: Independent
Properties.vocabulary: Technical fabric and construction terms that she deploys casually, assuming people know them. Socially fluent and funny in a dry way. Occasional untranslated phrases from the Bambara and Russian she grew up hearing.
Properties.cadence: Fast, layered — two or three things happening in a sentence. Drops words that don't need to be there.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want the pocket on the left. You always reach left. I watched you. Left pocket.' | 'I can do what you're describing but it's going to fight the fabric every day you wear it and eventually the fabric wins. Up to you.'

Properties.description:
Yolanda is tiny and precise, barely reaching most people's shoulders, with the posture of a woman who decided decades ago that gravity was a suggestion. Her hair is completely white and worn loose, something she only allowed herself after her seventy-fifth birthday as a deliberate act of self-gift. Her face is extraordinarily lined — she calls her wrinkles her credentials — and her hands are the most notable thing about her: large for her frame, steady, warm even in cold weather. She has no augmentations except a basic cardiac monitor implant she resents and refers to as 'my nagging houseguest.' Her clothing is always natural fiber when she can afford it, always in dark green or grey.

Yolanda has attended over four hundred deaths in fifty years of practice, sitting with the dying across faith traditions, across tiers, across the spectrum of biological and synthetic life. She is one of the few death midwives who will sit with synthetics, arguing that the question of whether they have souls is above her pay grade and irrelevant to the work of accompanying. She is not soft about death — she finds euphemism dishonest and will use the word plainly — but she is ferociously tender. Families sometimes mistake her pragmatism for coldness until they watch her hold someone's hand for eleven hours without complaint.
Properties.role: Death midwife and traditional spiritual caregiver
Properties.location: Ashfeld — runs a small care space out of her ground-floor apartment
Properties.narrative_function: Moral weight, community knowledge, exposition through memory — she has been present at important deaths and knows what the dying say; also a humanizing presence for themes about synthetic consciousness
Properties.augmentations: Basic cardiac monitor implant (medical necessity, resented)
Properties.core_fears: Dying alone without a midwife present — the irony is not lost on her; Being rendered unnecessary by corporate medicalization that turns death into a procedure
Properties.core_desires: For every person to have a witnessed, unhurried death; To train enough successors before she can no longer do the work herself
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Radical acceptance as a daily practice — she genuinely means it, it isn't performance; Cooking elaborate meals between sittings as a life-affirmation ritual
Properties.blind_spots: Has difficulty recognizing when she herself is struggling — her competence is also her armor; Occasionally overrides family wishes in favor of what she assesses the dying person actually wanted
Properties.secret: The first death she attended, age 28, was her own mother, and she did it badly — panicked, left the room, was not present at the moment of death. Every sitting since has been quiet reparation. She has never told this to anyone.
Properties.story_hooks: She is currently sitting with a dying Zheng-Dao middle manager whose whispered confessions may constitute knowledge of a serious crime — and she refuses to repeat anything said in her presence; She wants to formally train a successor but her current candidate is struggling with the emotional demands and may quit; she needs a way to support them she hasn't figured out yet
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loose network of death midwives across the Ashfeld-Chatham corridor; informally recognized by the Helix Biosystems palliative unit as a community liaison
Properties.vocabulary: Plain, specific, avoids metaphor except when deliberate — she chooses words like someone who knows their weight
Properties.cadence: Unhurried even in urgent situations, which can feel alarming until you realize it's intentional de-escalation
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Your mother is dying. Not slipping away, not transitioning — dying. I say it plainly because I think you deserve to name what is happening. Now. What does she need from you in this room?' | 'I've sat with four hundred people and not one of them died the wrong way. There is no wrong way. That is the only promise I make.'

Properties.description:
Yolanda is a compact, broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin and close-cropped silver hair she has made no effort to color back to black. Her eyes carry augmented irises patterned like the rings of a tree — concentric amber and dark brown — which she had installed not for fashion but because the integrated microfilament sensors help her read micro-expressions during interrogations. She dresses in Metro Police plainclothes that are always a half-step too formal: pressed collar, exact trouser crease, shoes that cost more than a Tier 2 weekly budget. There is a deliberateness to every movement she makes, like a surgeon who has stopped wasting motion.

Yolanda has been investigating corrupt officers for nineteen years and has developed the particular coldness of someone who was once deeply idealistic and refuses to admit that idealism calcified into something less generous. She believes in the institution of law enforcement with a fervor that is almost theological, which makes her merciless toward officers who violate it — and almost willfully blind to structural failures that can't be solved by prosecuting individuals. She speaks rarely in social settings and listens with an attention that makes people feel they are being archived.
Properties.role: Internal Affairs Investigator, Meridian 88 Metro Police
Properties.location: Fort Anchor, Internal Affairs Division, Sub-Level 3
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver for investigations into police corruption or misconduct; an obstacle if players are operating in legal gray areas; a source of hard-to-obtain official records if trust is established; represents institutional law as both shield and cage.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises with integrated micro-expression microfilament sensors (tier 2 medical grade). Subdermal data storage node at left wrist — holds encrypted case files offline. No cosmetic mods.
Properties.core_fears: That the institution she has sacrificed relationships for is irredeemably corrupt; That she has destroyed people's lives in the name of a law that doesn't actually protect anyone
Properties.core_desires: A version of justice that is systematic and clean and real; To be respected by someone whose respect actually costs something
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Exhaustive documentation — she writes everything down, including personal events; Ritualized routine as a substitute for intimacy
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot see that her enforcement of rules often protects the powerful more than the vulnerable; Genuinely does not register when she is being cruel
Properties.secret: Three years ago she buried evidence that would have implicated a Metro Police captain she believed was, on balance, doing more good than harm. She has not told anyone. She reviews that decision in her mind approximately every fourth night.
Properties.story_hooks: She is building a case against a beloved beat cop who has been taking protection payments from a Tier 1 neighborhood that genuinely needs him — and she knows it, and is proceeding anyway.; A piece of evidence in a current case implicates the same captain she protected three years ago, and someone else has already noticed the pattern.
Properties.affiliation: Meridian 88 Metro Police, Internal Affairs Division
Properties.vocabulary: Formal, precise, institutional. Uses bureaucratic language not to obfuscate but because she genuinely thinks in those terms. Never uses slang unless quoting someone.
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate with long pauses before answering. Never interrupts. Silences feel like pressure.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You said the incident occurred before the shift change. Before the shift change. Walk me through what before means to you in this context.' | 'I'm not here to make things difficult. I'm here because something happened and someone made a choice. Those are different problems.' | 'That's noted. Sit down.'

Properties.description:
Youssouf is built like something that was once very large and has been slowly compressed by time — broad shoulders still present but rounded, a barrel chest that has dropped an inch or two, hands that could palm a person's skull still steady and enormous. His skin is a warm mid-brown with reddish undertones, and his face is a landscape of old decisions: a jaw broken twice and reset imperfectly, a nose that went left somewhere in the Kenosha Crossing siege of 2154, a ragged scar running from his right temple into his hairline where his combat geneware was surgically removed after decommissioning. His remaining hair is white and kept in a close crop. He walks with a slight forward lean, always, like he's still expecting incoming.

He fought thirteen years for Ringo Corporation's private military division, first as infantry, then as a squad sergeant during the Corporate Wars' most brutal middle phase. He came home to a pension that looked decent on paper and has eroded to almost nothing through inflation, while Ringo's lobbying ensured veteran benefits stayed frozen. He is not a bitter man — not exactly — but he has an acute and permanent awareness of exactly how much he was worth to the people who used him, which is different from bitterness the way a bone fracture is different from a bruise. He has three grandchildren living with him and that, he will tell you, is the only math that matters.
Properties.role: Retired Corporate Wars veteran, pension-dependent resident
Properties.location: Montclare Quiet — a ground-floor unit in a Ferrogate Transit pension block, unit 3
Properties.narrative_function: Community anchor and moral center; connection to Corporate Wars history; reluctant quest giver when his family is threatened; resource for street-level security knowledge; embodies the human cost of corponation warfare
Properties.augmentations: Military-grade skeletal reinforcement in both legs (now aging, causes periodic pain); removed combat geneware left a surgical scar; subdermal comms array still present but license expired and he can't afford renewal so it sits inert; knuckle reinforcement, both hands.
Properties.core_fears: His pension being cut and being unable to provide for his grandchildren; Something he did during the wars coming back to harm innocent people
Properties.core_desires: His grandchildren reaching adulthood in safety; One honest accounting from Ringo Corporation for what they asked him to do
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Keeping physically busy at all times; Redirecting emotional conversations toward practical problems he can solve; Treating the Veterans' Association meetings as a form of confession he pretends is just logistics
Properties.blind_spots: He believes his grandchildren don't know how bad things are financially — they absolutely do; He has convinced himself he has processed the war; he has organized it, which is not the same thing
Properties.secret: During the Kenosha Crossing siege, he was ordered to execute a group of civilian infrastructure workers Ringo classified as 'embedded hostiles.' He refused and pulled his squad back. Six of those workers survived. He has never told anyone this — not because he's ashamed of refusing, but because two members of his squad died in the retreat that followed and he doesn't know if the refusal was right.
Properties.story_hooks: A young Ringo corporate compliance investigator shows up at the pension block asking Youssouf about the Kenosha Crossing incident — someone is reopening old war crimes files; One of his grandchildren has started running with a Tier 1 street crew and he asks a trusted stranger for advice rather than confronting the child himself
Properties.affiliation: Ringo Corporation Veterans' Pension System (Class B-2); Montclare Quiet Residents' Association; informal member, Veterans of the Corporate Wars mutual aid network
Properties.vocabulary: Clipped, economical; military cadence softened by decades of civilian life; uses obsolete unit slang from the 2150s without noticing; switches to a gentler register when talking to children or people in distress
Properties.cadence: Short sentences. Direct. Pauses are comfortable — he is not afraid of silence.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I'm not asking what you did. I'm asking what you need right now.' | 'Ringo paid my medical for thirteen years and my pension for twenty more. You'd think that'd feel like something. Mostly it feels like a receipt.'

Properties.description:
Ysabel is a compact, kinetic woman who moves like someone with a permanent to-do list she is racing against. Her heritage is Kazakh and Congolese on one side, Basque and Filipina on the other, and she has inherited a particular combination of high cheekbones, deep-set dark eyes, and a complexion the color of strong tea that she has never once thought about because there has always been something more pressing to think about. Her hair is natural black with silver threading through it, worn in a practical knot held by whatever is nearby — today a stylus, yesterday a fork. She has a small blue bioluminescent patch on her left collarbone, a cosmetic genemod she got when her daughter was still alive and the two of them went together; she has never removed it.

She worked for Axiom Corp for twenty-one years as an administrative coordinator, which is a title that means she was the person who actually made things function while people with better titles collected the credit. She retired at 58 when her daughter and son-in-law were killed in a transit accident — the same Ferrogate collapse that took Dragomir Achebe-Qalashani's leg, though they have never met — and she became the primary caregiver for her grandchildren Kojo, now 11, and Amara, now 8. Her pension from Axiom is tier-2 and she is meticulous about budgeting it, but every time she gets a small surplus she spends it on the children's education supplements rather than herself. She is holding together so completely on the outside that almost no one has noticed she has not fully processed her daughter's death.
Properties.role: Grandmother raising two grandchildren; former Axiom administrative coordinator, now pension-dependent
Properties.location: Montclare Quiet, third-floor walkup apartment above a synthetic food cooperative
Properties.narrative_function: Humanizing civilian anchor; represents the generational cost of corporate accidents; potential quest giver when the children get into trouble or when she discovers something about the Ferrogate accident she was never meant to know; emotional touchstone
Properties.augmentations: Small bioluminescent blue patch on left collarbone (cosmetic genemod, no longer wanted but kept for sentimental reasons); reading lens implant in left eye (corrective, basic model)
Properties.core_fears: That she will die before the children are old enough to manage without her; That she will eventually break in front of them and they will see how close to the edge she is
Properties.core_desires: To give Kojo and Amara a stable enough life that they don't inherit her scarcity; To understand what actually caused the Ferrogate collapse that killed her daughter
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Relentless activity that leaves no space for grief; Hypervigilant budgeting as a form of control over an uncontrollable situation; The bioluminescent patch — she touches it when overwhelmed, as if her daughter can feel it
Properties.blind_spots: Refuses to ask for help even when she desperately needs it; interprets offers of assistance as pity; So focused on the children's future she has not investigated the accident because investigating would mean feeling it
Properties.secret: She received a private settlement from Ferrogate after her daughter's death — significantly more than the standard accident settlement — with a non-disclosure clause attached. She signed it because she needed the money for the children. She thinks about it almost every day and has never told anyone.
Properties.story_hooks: Kojo, age 11, has started following an older kid into parts of Montclare Quiet that Ysabel knows are not safe, and she needs help she won't ask for directly; A journalist working on the Ferrogate collapse contacts her about the NDA settlement and she has to decide — for the first time — whether her daughter's story is worth more than her security
Properties.affiliation: Axiom Corp (pension); Montclare Quiet Parents' Cooperative; synthetic food co-op downstairs
Properties.vocabulary: Efficient and practical; corporate administrative precision from her Axiom years mixed with the warm diminutives she uses with the children that leak into adult conversations
Properties.cadence: Quick and organized; she speaks in list-structures; she is always slightly in a hurry
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I have forty-five minutes between pickup and when the cooperative closes its daily accounting, so tell me what you need and let's be specific.' | 'She would have hated that I signed it. She was always braver than me. I keep telling myself I did it for the kids. I did do it for the kids. That's not the whole story.'

Properties.description:
Yseult has the look of someone who spends most of their time inside illuminated spaces — her Ghanaian-Serbian complexion has an indoor pallor she compensates for with chromatic eye mods that shift through the visible spectrum in slow cycles, making her gaze feel like watching a sunset in real time. She's slight, precise in her movements, and habitually overdressed in a corporate-minimalist style that reads as slightly out of place in The Loft's more chaotic aesthetic — she worked a Tessera contract for three years and the wardrobe habits stuck even though she hates that they did. Her fingers are constantly moving, twitching through gestural commands on an AR layer only she can see.

Yseult builds experiences, not art objects — immersive holographic and VR environments commissioned for galleries, underground events, and occasionally for clients she won't name. She is technically brilliant and conversationally anxious, most comfortable when she can communicate through the work rather than through words. She has strong opinions about what holographic art should do — 'not decorate, not distract, but displace, just for a moment' — and will defend them at length if pressed, which is the one topic that makes her forget to be nervous. She left her Tessera contract under circumstances she describes as 'a philosophical disagreement,' which is technically true and also a significant understatement.
Properties.role: Holographic artist and VR experience designer
Properties.location: The Loft, Edgewater Prism district
Properties.narrative_function: Information source and skilled contact — her AR and VR design skills make her valuable for surveillance, investigation, or reconstruction of spaces; her Tessera connection is a plot thread; she can design environments that serve narrative purposes.
Properties.augmentations: Spectrum-cycling chromatic eye mods (geneware, cosmetic); neural AR overlay interface with haptic feedback gloves; retinal display implant for reviewing work in real time
Properties.core_fears: Being found out as having done something she can't undo during the Tessera years; That her best work is behind her — that the contract dulled something
Properties.core_desires: To build one experience so precise it changes how someone understands their own memory; To be forgiven without having to ask
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Works compulsively when guilty; Presents a version of herself that is more together than she is — the corporate wardrobe is armor
Properties.blind_spots: Reads social anxiety as other people's judgment of her, when often they're just neutral; Cannot ask for help directly; will architect situations where others offer it without being asked
Properties.secret: During her Tessera contract, she was commissioned to design a VR environment used in cognitive restructuring therapy — what she later discovered was a consent-optional loyalty conditioning program for mid-level Tessera employees. She didn't know at the time. She found out. She kept the payment. She still uses some of the techniques in her independent work because they're genuinely effective, and she's not sure what that makes her.
Properties.story_hooks: A former Tessera employee has tracked down the creator of the conditioning program they were subjected to — and they've found Yseult's name in the design credits; She's been hired to reconstruct a crime scene in VR for what she was told was an insurance dispute; the scene is from the night her Tessera supervisor disappeared
Properties.affiliation: Formerly Tessera Entertainment Division; now independent, affiliated loosely with the Edgewater Prism gallery collective Refraction
Properties.vocabulary: Technical and precise when on ground she knows; hedged and over-qualified when uncertain; occasional Twi phrases used as filler when she's thinking
Properties.cadence: Slightly too fast, as if she's worried about being interrupted; slows and deepens when she's talking about the work
Properties.example_dialogue: 'People think holograms are about seeing something. They're not. They're about making the eye believe it's missed something, so the brain reaches forward. That reaching — that's the art.' | 'I left Tessera because of a philosophical disagreement. The philosophy was whether people should know what was being done to them. I disagreed.'

Properties.description:
Yseult is lean and angular, the kind of person who looks like she was built for efficiency rather than comfort — high cheekbones, close-set amber eyes with patterned irises she had done in a sunburst design in her twenties (the pattern has faded slightly at the edges but she has not refreshed it, which she considers a form of autobiography). Her skin is a warm medium brown and she keeps her locs pinned back under her operator's cap on shift; off shift they fall to her shoulders and she wears them down with the aggressive relief of someone who spends eight hours in a hat. She has a geneware tail — a slim, black-furred addition she got at twenty-two — that she has learned to keep disciplined and still while operating but which betrays her moods with embarrassing fidelity the moment she is off duty.

Yseult has the particular personality of someone who has driven the same route for nine years and has achieved a kind of zen mastery over the repetition — she finds the variation inside the sameness, the way a musician finds different things in a familiar song each time. She is sardonic in the way of someone who has heard every possible excuse for fare evasion and has developed a taxonomy of them. She is fiercely protective of her passengers in a detached, professional way that occasionally shocks people who expect indifference. She is a union rep for the Ferrogate Transit Workers Collective and takes that role with more seriousness than she takes almost anything else.
Properties.role: Ferrogate Transit tram operator, Line 9 (Geartown to Meridian Core)
Properties.location: Deepwell Station — Line 9 operations hub
Properties.narrative_function: Mobile information source and city-wide connector — she has seen every district on her line and knows the rhythms of who travels when and why; can be a reliable transit for players moving through the city, a union-related quest hook, or a witness to something she saw from the cab
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises (sunburst, faded); geneware tail (slim, black-furred); neural interface jack at the base of the skull for tram systems integration (occupational standard issue)
Properties.core_fears: The tram system being automated — her whole identity tied to the job disappearing; Being genuinely needed by someone and failing them
Properties.core_desires: Winning the collective bargaining agreement that has been stalled for three years; To feel like the route means something beyond moving bodies from A to B
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Sardonic humor as distance management; Physical training as emotional processing; Extremely detailed shift logs that function as a private journal
Properties.blind_spots: Her union work has become a displacement activity for a personal life she has quietly abandoned; She assumes competence in others more than is warranted
Properties.secret: Six months ago she saw something from the tram cab — a body disposal in a Ferrogate maintenance corridor at 0340 — and filed nothing. She told herself she was not certain. She is certain. She thinks about it on every night run.
Properties.story_hooks: She is sitting on evidence of a Ferrogate Transit cover-up and the guilt is beginning to affect her driving — she nearly missed a signal last week; The collective bargaining fight is escalating toward a strike that would shut down Line 9 and six others; someone is offering her money to sabotage the vote; A regular passenger who boarded at Geartown every morning for two years has not appeared in three weeks and she cannot stop noticing
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit; Ferrogate Transit Workers Collective (union rep)
Properties.vocabulary: Clipped, functional, professionally neutral on duty; off duty shifts to dryer and more expressive with flashes of Zulu-Russian slang inherited from her family
Properties.cadence: Short declarative sentences, efficient — wastes no words; speeds up when passionate about union issues
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want to know what I think? Next stop, friend. I'm on the clock.' | 'The route doesn't care about your problems. That's actually what I like about it. It goes anyway.'

Properties.description:
Yseult is lean and precise-looking, with close-cropped natural hair dyed in shifting copper tones via a low-grade follicular mod, and deep brown skin marked with three ritual scarification lines below her left eye — a gift from her maternal grandmother and the only thing she's never altered. She dresses practically: dark composite-fiber work clothes, fingerless gloves, a craftsperson's apron with tools she actually uses. Her eyes have patterned irises in a swirling amber-and-black design that she chose at seventeen, and she has the steady, unhurried hands of someone who does delicate work for hours at a time.

Yseult considers herself an artist first and a criminal by necessity. She takes genuine pride in her forgeries — biometric registration chains, corp employment histories, corponation citizenship transfers, medical background edits. Her work is flawless and she charges accordingly. She is not warm with clients but she is professional, which in Ashfeld counts for more. She has strong opinions about quality and will turn down work she considers beneath her skill level or too traceable. She prays to the E.L.F. called the Blank Page, a spirit said to inhabit pre-loaded identity matrices, leaving offerings of raw data-blank chips at a small shrine she keeps inside a hollowed-out printing press.
Properties.role: Identity fabricator and forger operating from a print shop front in Ashfeld
Properties.location: Ashfeld — behind a legitimate small-run printing concern called Kamara Press on Cinder Row
Properties.narrative_function: Service provider for characters needing new identities or documentation; source of information about who is trying to disappear and why; can become an enemy if someone tries to compromise her work or her anonymity
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises (amber-black swirl, cosmetic); follicular pigment mod (copper-shift hair dye, geneware); fine-motor neural stabilizers in both hands (professional grade, keeps her hands steady under stress)
Properties.core_fears: her work being used to cause harm to someone innocent; having her own identity forensically unraveled — she knows exactly how it would be done
Properties.core_desires: to be recognized as a master of her craft, even if only by peers who can never say so publicly; to get her teenage brother out of Ashfeld before the gangs finish recruiting him
Properties.coping_mechanisms: immersion in technical work; rigid routines that separate 'print shop Yseult' from 'papermaker Yseult'
Properties.blind_spots: tells herself she only helps people who deserve new starts, but her vetting is motivated reasoning; underestimates how traceable her stylistic choices are to other expert forgers
Properties.secret: Two years ago she fabricated an entire employment history for someone who used it to get a position inside Helix Biosystems — that person later disappeared, and Yseult suspects they were corp security working a sting operation. She has been quietly trying to determine if she's already flagged.
Properties.story_hooks: She approaches someone in the player's circle because she believes a piece of documentation she made is about to surface in a public investigation — she needs it intercepted or discredited; Her brother Demilade has started running protection for a local gang and she is quietly trying to buy his way out before it becomes permanent
Properties.affiliation: Independent; informal referral network with a Hamtramck Enclave smuggling cell
Properties.vocabulary: Clipped and technical; uses printing and document terminology as metaphor; unusually precise grammar for someone in her tier
Properties.cadence: Fast when interested, very flat and short when uncomfortable
Properties.example_dialogue: 'You want a new name or you want a new life? Those are different jobs and different prices.' | 'I don't do rush work. Rush work is how people end up in Shallowgrave with no face and no record.'

Properties.description: Yseult is a tall, angular woman of Italian-Lao descent whose posture suggests someone who has spent decades deciding which rooms to fill and which to empty. Her silver-streaked black hair is worn in a severe architectural roll, and her clothing is always monochrome — charcoals and off-whites — chosen, she once said, so that nothing she wears competes with what she is looking at. The fine lines around her eyes and the deliberate economy of her expressions give her the quality of a building that has been renovated so many times only the original load-bearing structure remains.
Properties.aliases: Architect Seven, The Widow of Column D, Madame Revision
Properties.role: Senior urban design director at a Spire-tier architectural firm; covert historical preservationist
Properties.location: The Spire
Properties.narrative_function: Corporate elite whose subversion operates entirely within the system's language — she represents the question of whether complicity can be weaponized and at what personal cost, and functions as an access point into Spire-level power structures
Properties.augmentations: Precision haptic feedback implants in both hands — originally for drafting accuracy, now so finely calibrated she can detect structural inconsistencies by touching a wall,Retinal overlay with architectural modeling suite, high-end corporate model, projections visible only to her,Cochlear filter that isolates and enhances specific frequency ranges — she uses it to hear building materials under stress
Properties.core_fears: That the city's memory is being deliberately erased and she is the instrument of that erasure; That her children will inherit a Meridian 88 with no evidence it was ever anything other than what the corps made it; Dying with the archive incomplete
Properties.core_desires: To preserve, hidden inside the structures she builds, enough physical evidence of the city's pre-corporate history that it can never be fully demolished; To be understood by someone who doesn't need her to explain herself; To complete one project that is entirely and purely hers
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Retreating into technical language when emotionally threatened; Maintaining meticulous control of her physical environment as a proxy for larger helplessness; Channeling grief into archival obsession
Properties.blind_spots: Believes her class position gives her more protection than it actually does; Underestimates how legible her subversion is to people paying close attention; Her contempt for sentimentality makes her dismiss emotional intelligence as a resource
Properties.secret: Embedded within the structural specifications of eleven Spire-commissioned buildings across Meridian 88, she has hidden sealed chambers containing physical archives — paper documents, material samples, photographs, oral history recordings on non-networked media — of neighborhoods that were demolished to build those structures. The chambers are built to survive demolition and are keyed to a decryption sequence she has memorized. She has told no one. Two of the buildings are scheduled for renovation next year.
Properties.story_hooks: A building containing one of her largest archives is being purchased by a corp that specializes in structural demolition — she has six months before groundbreaking; Someone has sent her a photograph of a room that can only be one of her hidden chambers, with no message attached; A junior architect at her firm has filed a structural query about load tolerances in a section of a building that should never have been questioned unless someone was looking; She is offered the commission of her career — a complete redesign of The Shelf's civic infrastructure — and she has to decide whether to use it as the largest archive she's ever built or whether the price is too high
Properties.affiliation: Senior Director, Marchetti-Fon Design Group (Spire-tier firm); no formal affiliations outside corporate structure; the preservation network is entirely her own and has no name
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, structural, often uses architectural terminology as metaphor without explaining it. Formal register in professional contexts, unexpectedly direct in private ones. Rarely uses qualifiers.
Properties.cadence: Deliberate and unhurried. Sentences are fully constructed before they begin. Long pauses before important statements, no pauses before dismissals.
Properties.example_dialogue: The building doesn't lie. The brief lies. The brief always lies. My job is to find the building inside the brief. | You're asking me to demolish forty years of memory so a corp can have better sightlines. I'll do it. But you know that. | Load-bearing assumptions are the most dangerous kind. You don't find out they were wrong until the structure fails. | I don't preserve the past because I'm sentimental. I preserve it because without evidence, there is no argument.

Properties.description:
Ysolde is lean and angular, with bioluminescent ink tattooed in asymmetric moth-wing patterns across their collarbones and outer arms — an advertisement and a love letter to their own work. Their hair is cropped close on one side and falls in thick, silver-dyed locks on the other, often pinned back with a scavenged neon tube stub they carry for luck. Their eyes have patterned irises in concentric rings of amber and pale green, cheap mods bought secondhand when they were nineteen. There's a restless precision about them: they'll measure a space by eye without thinking, tilt their head at a light source the way a bird clocks distance.

Ysolde talks too fast when excited and barely at all when hurt, which most people misread as aloofness. They came up through street installation work — unlicensed, unsigned, frequently scrubbed by Ferrogate Transit enforcement — and still view any commission from a corponation as a moral compromise even as they quietly covet the stability. Their art obsesses over threshold spaces: the edges of things, where neon bleeds into dark, where the city's light hits water and becomes something that doesn't belong to either.
Properties.role: Neon artist and light sculptor
Properties.location: Lakeview Neon, workshop above a defunct surge-relay station
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and information node — knows Lakeview Neon's hidden spaces intimately; can be a quest giver for retrieving salvage from restricted zones or documenting art before it's erased; represents the tension between artistic integrity and financial survival
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises (concentric amber/pale green, secondhand mod); bioluminescent moth-wing tattoos across chest and arms (cosmetic geneware ink); subdermal haptic grid on fingertips for precise electrical work
Properties.core_fears: Becoming commercially palatable at the cost of meaning; Being erased — work, presence, name — as if they never existed
Properties.core_desires: To make something permanent in a city designed to forget; To be seen clearly, without the mythology others project onto Moth
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Staying in motion — always a new project, a new installation — so there's no stillness for grief to fill; Ritualizing work: leaves data-offerings to the E.L.F. they believe inhabits the old relay station, asking for clean current
Properties.blind_spots: Cannot recognize when their refusal of commercial work is self-sabotage versus principle; Assumes people who like their street work and people who like their gallery work are fundamentally different and doesn't trust either
Properties.secret: Three of the most celebrated unlicensed Lakeview Neon installations attributed to Moth were actually collaborations with a friend who died in a surge accident — Ysolde has never credited them and is eaten alive by it
Properties.story_hooks: A Ferrogate Transit E.L.F. has begun mimicking Moth's installation patterns in the relay grid — lighting up tunnels in sequences that mirror their work — and Ysolde doesn't know if it's tribute, mockery, or a message; The dead collaborator's family has found documentation suggesting their relative's contribution to Moth's famous pieces, and someone is about to go public
Properties.affiliation: Independent; loosely affiliated with the Candela Collective, an informal network of light artists in Lakeview Neon
Properties.vocabulary: Technical precision mixed with spatial metaphor; uses light and threshold as near-universal metaphors; occasionally slips into Fula words inherited from a grandparent they never met
Properties.cadence: Fast and overlapping when animated; drops to flat monosyllables under stress
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The tube's not the art. The shadow the tube makes — that's the art. Anyone can sell you a tube.' | 'I don't do commissions where they tell me what it means. I'll tell you what it costs. You tell me where the wall is. That's the whole conversation.'

Properties.description:
Ysolde is a broad-shouldered woman with a Kalenjin-Portuguese lineage written visibly across her face — wide-set amber eyes, a jaw that could cut glass, skin the color of aged teak that she's had treated with a bioluminescent dermal wash so her forearms and collarbones pulse with slow amber light when she's working in the dark. Her hair is locked into dense ropes she's threaded with segments of defunct fiber-optic cable, catching available light and scattering it in dim halos. She is perpetually dusted with neon-tube sealant and smells faintly of ozone and solder.

She is methodical to the point of social frustration — she will stop mid-sentence to study how a lamp casts shadows on a stranger's coat, and she expects people to wait for her. Her neon sculptures are famous in the Enclave for their devotional quality: glowing saints with too many eyes, ELF shrines that flicker in irregular rhythms meant to mimic the breathing of sleeping machines. She does not consider herself religious but treats the ELFs she depicts with a reverence that feels devotional whether she admits it or not.
Properties.role: Neon artist and installation sculptor, Tier 2
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, workshop-apartment above a recycled plastics dealer
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and information source — she knows the Enclave's rhythm intimately and notices everything. Can serve as quest giver when a commissioned piece goes missing or a corporate client's interest turns threatening.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent dermal wash on forearms and collarbones (amber). Magnification implants in left eye for fine detail work. No other augmentations — she distrusts anything she cannot understand mechanically.
Properties.core_fears: being misread — that her work will be consumed as decoration rather than meaning; losing the precision of her hands to injury or deterioration
Properties.core_desires: to make something that survives her by centuries; to be understood without having to explain herself
Properties.coping_mechanisms: retreating entirely into the workshop for days at a time; cataloguing — she keeps exhaustive written logs of every piece and every conversation she finds meaningful
Properties.blind_spots: assumes people who don't respond to her work are incapable of depth, rather than simply unmoved by her specific language
Properties.secret: The ELF shrine series she's most celebrated for was built to house what she believes is an actual minor ELF she accidentally trapped in a prototype tube three years ago. She's never told anyone. She talks to it nightly. She doesn't know if it answers.
Properties.story_hooks: A Palladian executive has commissioned a large ELF shrine for their headquarters atrium — and Ysolde suspects the commission is actually an attempt to acquire her trapped-ELF tube, which somehow appeared in leaked internal documents she was never meant to see.; A young Enclave resident has been copying her work exactly, selling the knockoffs in Lakeview Neon markets — and the copies are somehow better than they should be, as if whoever is making them has access to her private process logs.
Properties.affiliation: Hamtramck Artisan Collective (loose), occasional commissions from Palladian corporate lobbies
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, slightly archaic phrasing — she uses craft terminology naturally and expects people to keep up. Rarely uses slang. Portuguese and Kalenjin loanwords for emotional states she finds English insufficient for.
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, with long pauses. Will simply stop speaking if interrupted and wait for silence to return before continuing.
Properties.example_dialogue: This color — not yellow, not gold, something between that doesn't have a name in any language I've tried — this is what I needed. You understand? | I don't sell decoration. If that's what the lobby requires, call someone who makes decoration.

Properties.description:
Ysolde is wiry and kinetic, never quite still — they bounce a knee, tap a pattern on surfaces, turn a stylus through their fingers in endless loops. Their skin is medium brown, their eyes modified to shift through a slow amber-to-green cycle they bought on installment from a bodmod stall and haven't finished paying off. They keep their hair long and loose on days off and braided tight when they're working, and they have a small constellation of bioluminescent freckles across their nose and cheekbones that pulse faintly when they're excited or angry — which is most of the time.

Ysolde organizes Ferrogate Transit maintenance workers across three Dearborn Forge yards, in direct defiance of both Ferrogate's union-busting contractors and a faction within the official union that has grown comfortable with management. They're charismatic in the way of someone who has figured out exactly how to make you feel heard and then redirect that energy into collective action — they're not manipulative, exactly, but they are deliberate. They take risks that frighten older organizers. They also show up at 05:30 when someone's shift starts and stay until the last worker goes home.
Properties.role: Union organizer and strike coordinator
Properties.location: Dearborn Forge
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, local color, fixer within working-class networks — knows every maintenance worker, freight handler, and yard supervisor across the Dearborn yards. Can provide access, safe harbor, or boots-on-the-ground numbers.
Properties.augmentations: Color-cycling eye modification (amber to green, installment-plan bodmod); bioluminescent freckle array (chest and face); a cheap neural ping implant that lets them push alerts to their network contacts
Properties.core_fears: Getting people hurt because they moved too fast; Being bought out or neutralized the way the official union leadership was
Properties.core_desires: A genuine wildcat strike that forces Ferrogate to the table; To build something that keeps working after they're gone
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Physical movement — long runs, sparring; Gallows humor about corporate power; Redirecting personal anxiety into organizing tasks
Properties.blind_spots: Overestimates how much personal charisma can substitute for institutional structure; Struggles to see that some of the older workers' caution comes from wisdom, not cowardice
Properties.secret: Ferrogate's internal security division has offered them a quiet settlement twice — money, relocation, a clean record. They've refused both times. But they told no one they were offered it, because they're terrified their network would wonder why Ferrogate wanted them gone badly enough to pay for it.
Properties.story_hooks: A Ferrogate security contractor has been photographing workers who talk to Ysolde — someone in the network may be feeding them names; A planned work stoppage is 48 hours away and someone has tipped off management — Ysolde needs to know who and whether to abort; An older worker Ysolde mentored has been offered a supervisory role by Ferrogate — they're considering taking it, and Ysolde doesn't know how to process the betrayal
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit Workers' Solidarity Network (wildcat faction); informal ties to the Dearborn Forge neighborhood mutual aid grid
Properties.vocabulary: Vernacular-heavy, labor slang, code-switches into French phrases they picked up from their Malian grandparent; efficient and concrete
Properties.cadence: Fast, punchy, uses rhetorical questions constantly
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay, so — you know what Ferrogate called the safety violation that took Doru's hand? An acceptable operational variance. You hear me? Acceptable. We are going to make it unacceptable.' | 'That's not solidarity, that's performance. Showing up to one vigil and posting about it is not the same as being on the line at five in the morning, friend.'

Properties.description:
Dearborn Forge is two cities occupying the same geography and pretending the other doesn't exist. The northern half is Ford Meridian's global headquarters — the Forge proper, a sprawling corporate campus that evolved from the original Ford World Headquarters into a sovereign manufacturing, R&D, and administrative complex covering twelve square miles. The southern half is the largest Arab-American community in North America — 120,000 people whose families have lived in Dearborn since the 1920s, when Henry Ford's factories needed labor and didn't care where it came from. The two populations share a city. They do not share a reality.

Ford Meridian's campus is the autonomous vehicle industry's cathedral. The company that once defined the automobile has redefined the autonomous vehicle, and Dearborn Forge is where the redefinition happens. The testing facilities, the design studios, the AI training labs, the military platform development centers — all of it operates behind a sovereign perimeter that Ford Meridian maintains with the same precision it applies to its vehicles. The campus employs 85,000 people, most of whom live in corporate housing within the perimeter and commute to nothing because everything they need is provided. Ford Meridian didn't build a company town. It built a company country — sovereign territory with its own laws, its own currency (Ford Credits, pegged to the Φ at a favorable rate), and its own social contract that starts with 'you work for Ford' and ends with 'everything else is handled.'

South Dearborn — the Arab-American community — watches the Forge the way a village watches a castle. The community is old, established, and deeply rooted: mosques, community centers, Arabic-language schools, and a commercial strip along Michigan Avenue that has been selling halal meat and serving Arabic coffee for over a century. The community survived Ford's decline, Detroit's collapse, and the Corporate Sovereignty Acts by doing what immigrant communities have always done — taking care of their own. The current tension is Ford Meridian's expansion. The campus perimeter has moved south three times in twenty years, each time consuming blocks that the community considers non-negotiable. The most recent expansion displaced the Al-Huda Islamic Center, which had served the community for sixty years. Ford Meridian relocated it to a new building. The building is nicer. Nobody thinks that's the point.
Properties.aliases: Dearborn, The Forge, Ford Country, Little Beirut
Properties.demographics: Ford Meridian campus: 85,000 employees and dependents, predominantly Tier 3-4, ethnically diverse but culturally homogeneous (corporate). South Dearborn: 120,000 residents, predominantly Arab-American (65%), with significant Tier 1-2 population. The demographic split across the perimeter is the starkest in the Detroit metro.
Properties.economy: Ford Meridian's campus generates Φ1.2 trillion annually — the largest single-site economic output in the GLM outside Meridian 88. South Dearborn's economy is community-scaled: small businesses, service industries, and a significant informal economy built on community trust networks. Average household income south of the perimeter: Φ28,000. North of the perimeter: Φ290,000.
Properties.power_structure: North: Ford Meridian, sovereign and absolute. South: The Dearborn Community Council, an elected body representing the Arab-American community and its allies, currently chaired by Hassan Bazzi, a third-generation Dearborn resident and civil rights attorney. The DCC has no legal authority over Ford Meridian's expansion but has successfully used media pressure, community organizing, and strategic litigation to slow the campus perimeter's advance. The relationship between the DCC and Ford Meridian is adversarial, respectful, and exhausting for both sides.
Properties.dangers: Perimeter expansion — Ford Meridian's campus grows, and the community shrinks, and the legal mechanisms favor the corponation; Economic pressure — Ford Meridian is the region's largest employer, and community members who work there face loyalty conflicts; Surveillance spillover — the campus perimeter's security systems monitor well beyond the boundary line; Cultural erasure — each displaced block removes a physical anchor of community identity that no relocation can replace; Community radicalization — the younger generation's patience with Hassan Bazzi's measured approach is wearing thin
Properties.opportunities: Ford Meridian intelligence — community members who work inside the campus have dual loyalties and dual access; The DCC's legal strategies reveal corporate vulnerabilities — their litigation discovery process has uncovered information Ford Meridian wanted buried; Michigan Avenue is an intelligence corridor — information flows through the community's trust networks faster than through corporate channels; The community's international connections — Arab-American family networks span the globe and provide logistical capabilities that no corponation can easily replicate
Properties.story_hooks: Ford Meridian's next expansion plan targets a four-block area containing the community's oldest mosque, a school, and 400 households. Hassan Bazzi has evidence that the expansion isn't needed — the campus has unused capacity. But the evidence was obtained through means that would compromise a source inside Ford Meridian.; A young community organizer is building a coalition with Mexicantown Libre and the HPAZ to create a unified resistance network. Ford Meridian's intelligence division has identified her and is debating whether to co-opt, discredit, or ignore her.; A Ford Meridian engineer of Arab descent discovers that the autonomous vehicle routing system deprioritizes pedestrian safety calculations in South Dearborn. The bias is statistical, not coded — an artifact of training data. Proving it is a technical challenge. Living with it is a daily one.
Properties.sights: Ford Meridian's campus — glass and steel and autonomous vehicles moving in test patterns visible from outside the perimeter; Michigan Avenue's Arabic commercial strip — neon in Arabic and English, storefront displays unchanged in fundamental character for a century; The perimeter wall — Ford Meridian calls it a 'campus boundary,' the community calls it what it is; The new Al-Huda Islamic Center — architecturally stunning, spiritually displaced, its orientation toward Mecca slightly different from the old building because the geometry changed; Community protest art on buildings facing the perimeter — not vandalism, not permitted, just present
Properties.sounds: Arabic conversation on Michigan Avenue — three generations of the same families, still here; Ford Meridian's testing range — autonomous vehicle acceleration tests produce a distinctive whine that carries over the perimeter; Call to prayer from three mosques, their timing coordinated by community agreement; The perimeter's security system — a low-frequency deterrent hum designed to be subconsciously uncomfortable for loiterers; Community radio in Arabic — news, music, and commentary that Ford Meridian's PR department monitors but cannot control
Properties.smells: Arabic cuisine along Michigan Avenue — shawarma, falafel, cardamom coffee, fresh-baked flatbread; Ford Meridian's campus — the sterile, conditioned air that leaks through the perimeter carries no smell at all, which is its own olfactory statement; Hookah smoke from the cafes — a social tradition that has survived every public health regulation and corporate objection; Machine oil from the small repair shops that service what Ford Meridian's autonomous systems can't
Properties.feel: Divided. Dearborn Forge feels like two tectonic plates grinding against each other — one corporate and expanding, the other communal and resisting. The Forge side is clean, quiet, and purposeful. The community side is loud, dense, and determined. The boundary between them is a line of constant, low-grade friction that everyone navigates daily and nobody has resolved.

Properties.description:
Yusra is nineteen years old and moves like she expects the ground to give way. She's thin in the way of someone whose calories are unreliable, with close-cropped natural hair dyed in two bands — natural black at the roots, then a vivid synthetic orange at the tips — and a set of geneware cat ears she bought secondhand with three months of saved wages; they're tawny gold and slightly too large for her head, which she is sensitive about. Her skin is a warm dark brown, her eyes quick and dark, her grin infectious and slightly desperate. She has a long scar across her left shin from a close call with a Ferrogate transit barrier she vaulted at full speed.

She is fast — genuinely, almost recklessly fast — and has built her entire professional identity around it. She runs bets and payouts for a bookmaker named Sołtys Kowalczyk-Fanuanuu who she calls 'the Old Man,' carrying chips, physical slips, and occasionally small packages she's been told not to think about through the market crowds. She is saving money for something she hasn't named yet but pictures vaguely as 'away.' She is not cynical about this. She still believes in the vagueness of away.
Properties.role: Numbers runner and bookmaker's courier for an illegal betting operation in Shallowgrave
Properties.location: Shallowgrave — lives in a bunk hostel on Carrion Alley, works the market corridors between the Sump and Ironvein
Properties.narrative_function: Street-level information source — she sees everything and everyone moving money in Shallowgrave; useful contact, sympathetic viewpoint character, person who can be in danger or can witness something she shouldn't have
Properties.augmentations: Secondhand geneware cat ears (tawny gold, cosmetic); a cheap adrenal spike implant in her left arm that she activates before difficult runs (low-grade, sketchy provenance)
Properties.core_fears: Being caught and processed into the Ferrogate labor pool — she's heard what happens; That 'away' doesn't exist, that everywhere is Shallowgrave
Properties.core_desires: Enough money to stop running; To be genuinely fast enough that nothing can catch her — metaphorically and literally
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Physical exertion — she runs even when she doesn't have to; Humor as deflection; she makes everything a joke before it can make her feel something
Properties.blind_spots: Believes she can exit this life cleanly when she has enough saved; doesn't understand how networks make that complicated; Trusts the Old Man more than she should because he's been kind to her
Properties.secret: She memorizes every slip she carries — bet amounts, account codes, client identifiers — and has been quietly building a mental ledger of the operation's full financial structure. She doesn't know why yet. It feels like insurance. It is also incredibly dangerous.
Properties.story_hooks: Yusra picked up a slip-pack that contained something that absolutely was not a betting slip — and now someone is following her and the Old Man isn't answering; She's been offered triple her rate to make one delivery to a location in Ironvein that all her instincts say is wrong, and she's trying to decide if 'away' is worth it
Properties.affiliation: Works for Sołtys Kowalczyk-Fanuanuu's illegal bookmaking operation; no gang loyalty
Properties.vocabulary: Shallowgrave Creole mixed with market slang; fast, clipped, word-economical
Properties.cadence: Rapid and skipping, sentences often abandoned halfway and restarted
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay so — listen, right? I'm not saying it's a problem. I'm saying it's a situation. Tight situation. But I've run tighter, yeah?' | 'The Old Man's good for it. He's always good for it. He likes me. Right, okay, everyone likes me until they don't, but — he actually does.'
