Properties.description:
Yusra is built like a load-bearing column — broad-shouldered, thick-necked, with the kind of deliberate stillness that makes crowds unconsciously part around her. Her skin is a deep warm brown, cropped natural hair faded at the sides, and her left forearm carries a geometric tattoo in Amazigh style from a grandmother she never met. She has subdermal armor plating along her forearms and collar that gives her silhouette a slightly unnatural angularity. Her eyes are standard-issue grey with Metro Police LIDAR rings — rings that glow faint amber when she's actively scanning. Off-duty she has a surprisingly gentle voice and laughs easily, but on the line she goes perfectly, eerie quiet.

She believes in the idea of Metro Police more than its current reality, which is a distinction she holds onto by her fingernails. After eleven years of crowd control in the Shelf and the Circuit she has developed a precise internal calibration for when a crowd is curious, when it is afraid, and when it is about to become something else entirely. She treats rookie officers with patient firmness and street kids with cautious kindness. She is very good at her job and she knows it, which is the only thing keeping her from questioning why her job so often lands her between hungry people and corporate property.
Properties.role: Riot Suppression Specialist, Meridian 88 Metro Police
Properties.location: Fort Anchor
Properties.narrative_function: Recurring authority figure who is neither villain nor pushover — a moral friction point. Can be a reluctant information source, a character who arrests PCs for things that are technically illegal, or someone who quietly looks the other way when she decides it matters.
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal forearm and clavicle plating (standard Metro issue). LIDAR-ring ocular overlay. Bone-density reinforcement in knees and shins. No geneware — she considers it a personal line she hasn't crossed yet.
Properties.core_fears: Being complicit in something she cannot rationalize away; Losing the distinction between enforcing law and enforcing power
Properties.core_desires: To do this job in a way she can be proud of; To protect her mother from the economic slide without abandoning her principles
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Hyper-focus on procedure and craft; Compartmentalization — she does not think about the big picture during a shift; Cooking elaborate meals on days off
Properties.blind_spots: She underestimates how much her presence alone intimidates people who've been hurt by Metro before; She has convinced herself the system is reformable from inside because the alternative is unbearable
Properties.secret: Three years ago during the Hough Reclamation protests she destroyed body-cam footage of a fellow officer striking a restrained teenager. She told herself the kid was fine. She still checks the community boards to see if that name ever appears.
Properties.story_hooks: She has evidence of ongoing evidence tampering by a superior officer and is running out of reasons not to act on it.; A teenager she arrested twice is now missing — officially listed as relocated, but no relocation order exists in the system.
Properties.affiliation: Meridian 88 Metro Police, Riot Suppression Unit 7
Properties.vocabulary: Clipped, professional on-duty. Off-duty she relaxes into Meridian street creole with Maghrebi-inflected phrasing inherited from her father's side — elongated vowels, occasional Arabic loan-words.
Properties.cadence: On-duty: measured, slow, deliberate. Off-duty: warm, faster, punctuated by genuine laughter.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I'm going to ask you once. Step back from the line. Clear?' | 'You want to know what I actually think? You sure? Because once I tell you, I can't un-tell you.' | 'She's a good kid. Scared kid. That's not the same thing as a dangerous one.'

Properties.description:
Yusuf is a compact, carefully composed man with close-trimmed gray at his temples and a beard he trims every third day without fail. His eyes are his most striking feature — he had them modded fifteen years ago with geometric patterned irises, deep green lattices that his congregation debated fiercely and that he defended from the pulpit as 'the geometry of creation written in the body.' He dresses simply, always clean despite the Shelf's perpetual grime, and his left hand is extensively modified: a chrome prosthetic from the wrist down, its surface etched with Quranic verses in his own handwriting before the plating was laid, so the words are pressed into the metal from beneath.

He is a man of precise intellectual convictions that he holds without brittleness — he has changed his mind publicly three times in twenty years and considers it among his proudest acts. His masjid serves roughly three hundred regular worshippers across a tangle of traditions: Sunni, Ismaili, Ahmadiyya, and several families who blend Islamic practice with E.L.F. veneration in ways that Yusuf engages with theologically rather than dismissing. He moonlights as a chrome prayer practitioner, offering a practice that treats augmentation as a form of devotion — the modification of the God-given body as an act of trust rather than transgression.
Properties.role: Traditional imam and chrome prayer practitioner
Properties.location: The Shelf — the Masjid al-Barzakh, a converted warehouse space above a water recycling plant
Properties.narrative_function: Community authority and moral voice; offers a grounded traditional perspective on augmentation ethics; his congregation is a network of Shelf residents who know everything happening locally; he can be a quest giver around community crises.
Properties.augmentations: Chrome left hand (wrist to fingertips), etched with Quranic verse beneath the plating. Patterned irises (green geometric lattice).
Properties.core_fears: that his community will be dispersed by corponation development and he will be powerless to stop it; that his theological accommodations have drifted too far and he has led people astray
Properties.core_desires: to build an institution that outlasts him; to articulate a theology of augmentation that is rigorous enough to be taken seriously
Properties.coping_mechanisms: intellectual engagement with problems rather than emotional processing; prayer as genuine practice not performance; deflecting personal questions with questions about the asker
Properties.blind_spots: can be condescending to younger practitioners he sees as sloppy; his certainty about institutional longevity makes him underestimate how precarious the Shelf's future actually is
Properties.secret: The chrome hand is not entirely his — the prosthetic was originally made for a black-market augmentation dealer he knew before he became imam. The man died in a raid. Yusuf, then newly injured and unable to afford proper prosthetics, paid almost nothing for the hand. He has never disclosed where it came from, and the etched verses were partly an act of consecration and partly an act of burial.
Properties.story_hooks: A Tessera development crew has begun surveying land adjacent to the masjid, and Yusuf needs someone to find out what the plans are before he takes any action; A worshipper confessed something to him that he cannot share but that means he knows a crime is coming — he needs to prevent it without breaking confidentiality
Properties.affiliation: Masjid al-Barzakh congregation; loosely networked with other independent religious leaders in Tier 1-2 areas; no corponation affiliation (deliberately)
Properties.vocabulary: Formal and precise without being cold. Comfortable with technical augmentation language, Islamic theological terms, and Shelf slang — code-switches fluidly.
Properties.cadence: Measured, with a slight Georgian lilt from his Kereselidze grandmother. Rarely raises his voice; the lower he speaks the more people lean in.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The body is an amanah — a trust. Some say modification breaks that trust. I say: what is a trust given to you if you never make it your own?' | 'Come in. Tea is not optional, by the way. That is a ruling, not a suggestion.' | 'I will not tell you what to do. I will ask you questions until you tell yourself.'

Properties.description:
Yusuf is a broad, slow-moving man who has cultivated the appearance of a tired grandfather — thick silver streaks in his close-cropped black hair, reading glasses perpetually perched on a nose broken twice and set once, a cardigan with one pocket always stuffed with hard candies he offers freely. His skin is a warm brown, deeply lined around the eyes, and his left hand carries a subdermal ledger implant that projects a faint green glow through the skin of his palm when he activates it — the only augmentation he's ever bothered with. He dresses in laundered but mended clothing, never anything that suggests wealth, because wealth makes people count what they owe you and start thinking about not paying.

He is meticulous, patient, and genuinely warm in the way that only the most dangerous people can afford to be. He has run numbers and books in Gravesend Basin for twenty-three years and has outlasted four gang transitions, two corporate annexation attempts, and one actual flood. He does not threaten people. He employs a man named Calin for that. What Yusuf does is remember — every debt, every late payment, every excuse — and he waits with the equanimity of someone who has priced your failure into the original agreement.
Properties.role: Loan shark and bookmaker operating out of Gravesend Basin
Properties.location: Gravesend Basin, The Float — a converted barge-shop called Tamboli's Provisions
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver (someone needs a loan and the terms have teeth), information source (he knows everyone's financial desperation), local color anchor for Gravesend Basin, moral complexity — genuinely helpful and genuinely dangerous
Properties.augmentations: Subdermal ledger implant (left palm) — projects a holographic accounting interface. No cosmetic mods.
Properties.core_fears: Being repaid in full by everyone at once and having no reason to exist; Dying before his daughter learns what he actually does
Properties.core_desires: To be respected as essential to the community; To believe his work functions as a social service
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Ritual generosity — candy, tea, food — to frame transactions as hospitality; Obsessive record-keeping as a form of control
Properties.blind_spots: He genuinely does not register the suffering his interest rates cause as his responsibility; He believes his restraint makes him different from violent criminals
Properties.secret: His daughter Amara attends Axiom-sponsored university on a scholarship Yusuf arranged by forgiving a debt owed by an Axiom mid-manager — she believes she earned it on merit, and he has never corrected her
Properties.story_hooks: A debtor has died and their teenage child has inherited the debt — Yusuf is conflicted about collecting and needs someone to 'check in' on the family in a way that isn't threatening; Someone is counterfeiting Yusuf's debt tokens — small chits he issues as proof of loan — and he needs to know who before his entire system of trust collapses
Properties.affiliation: Independent operator; informal tribute arrangement with the Gravesend Basin Compact (loose criminal network)
Properties.vocabulary: Formal, slightly old-fashioned Meridian Standard with occasional Bosnian and Marathi loanwords; financial metaphors for everything
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, long pauses before key words, never raises his voice
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Take a candy. Sit. There is no emergency that is improved by standing.' | 'The interest is not a punishment. It is merely the cost of time, and time, as you know, does not negotiate.'

Properties.description:
Yusuf is a large man gone soft with age — broad shoulders that slope now, a round belly he makes no apology for, and hands that remain extraordinary: steady, certain, with the flat-filed nails of a man who has been putting blades near people's faces for four decades. His skin is very dark with a warm undertone, and he keeps a neat, close-trimmed grey beard that he touches up himself every morning using the second chair as a mirror. He has a single cosmetic geneware modification — a cat's tail, dark grey, that he got at fifty as a joke with his then-partner and kept after the relationship ended because, he says, it gives him something to do with his hands while he listens. It curls around his ankle or flicks slowly when he's thinking.

The shop has three chairs, two mirrors, and approximately forty years of layered history on its walls: photographs, old clipper brand stickers, a faded printed menu from a restaurant that closed before he moved in, a small ELF shrine to what he calls the Chair Spirit built from a first-generation clipper chassis with incense holders soldered to the housing. He charges what he always charged, adjusted only for inflation, and he has turned down three buyout offers from a Tessera real estate subsidiary. The shop smells like talc, synth-eucalyptus, and old paper. He knows everyone's name and their father's name and in some cases their grandfather's.
Properties.role: Barber, owner-operator of a small shop
Properties.location: Mexicantown Libre, Calle Ochenta storefront (between the pawn exchange and the tamale counter)
Properties.narrative_function: Community elder, information hub, moral compass figure. The shop is a social institution — people come to talk as much as to get cut. He has heard everything. He judges quietly and almost never volunteers what he knows, but he can be the person who confirms a rumor or provides the final piece of a puzzle.
Properties.augmentations: Geneware cat tail — dark grey, cosmetic. No implants.
Properties.core_fears: Losing the shop — not for the money but for what it represents; Dying before he can find his son, from whom he has been estranged for twelve years
Properties.core_desires: That the neighborhood remains a neighborhood and doesn't become a product; Reconciliation with his son
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The rituals of the work — a cut has a beginning, middle, and end, which is more than life usually offers; Sunday radio sessions as active grief ritual for things he's lost
Properties.blind_spots: His pride makes him refuse help when he needs it; He has idealized his son in the estrangement and doesn't know who his son actually is now
Properties.secret: The Tessera real estate offer he turned down most recently was substantial enough that he could have retired comfortably. He turned it down because his son — the estranged one — knew this shop as a child and Yusuf cannot bring himself to erase the place where his son last knew him. He tells everyone it's about the neighborhood.
Properties.story_hooks: His estranged son resurfaces — but affiliated with something dangerous, and he's using the shop's address for something Yusuf hasn't consented to; A regular customer whispered something in the chair three months ago and then died in an apparent accident; Yusuf has been holding the information, unsure if it's dangerous to share
Properties.affiliation: Independent; Mexicantown Libre small business network (informal)
Properties.vocabulary: Slow and deliberate, warm, uses the formal second person when he's being serious, calls young people 'young one' without irony
Properties.cadence: Unhurried; the pace of someone who knows you're not going anywhere while he has scissors
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Now — you came in here for a cut, but I think you came in for something else. Sit. The blade takes twenty minutes. Talk to me.' | 'Tessera wants this corner. Tessera wants every corner. But Tessera does not come in here on a Tuesday and tell me their daughter's name. I remember names. That matters, young one.'

Properties.description:
Zara is a tall young woman with very dark skin, high cheekbones, and hair that she has modded to shift color with her mood — when she's calm it's a deep forest green, when she's amused it goes warm amber, and when she's angry it bleeds to a red-orange that the regulars have learned to read as a weather warning. She has patterned irises, a starburst of copper and black, and retractable claws she got partly for safety and partly because she thinks they look devastating. She tends to lean on the bar when she talks to people, getting close — not aggressive, but engaged, like she's genuinely interested in what you have to say and will stop being interested the moment you bore her.

Zara has worked at The Specific Gravity for three years, which she considers a fact of her present life rather than a permanent state. She is saving for something she hasn't told anyone about and has a habit of reading people with an accuracy that is unsettling in someone who seems, on the surface, to be primarily concerned with looking effortlessly cool. She has a complicated relationship with the bar's E.L.F. — a data-spirit she's decided is called 'the Tab,' which she believes is actively judging the customers and occasionally agrees with it out loud.
Properties.role: Bartender, The Ferment Quarter dive bar called 'The Specific Gravity'
Properties.location: The Ferment Quarter, The Specific Gravity bar on Menomonee Gulch
Properties.narrative_function: Social hub and rumor exchange; players can learn what's moving through the Ferment Quarter by talking to Zara or just listening near her. She's a reader of people who can be an ally or a liability depending on how she's approached. Can be a quest giver if something in the bar world threatens her employer or her savings.
Properties.augmentations: Color-shift hair mod (mood-responsive, green/amber/red-orange). Patterned irises (copper starburst). Retractable claws (geneware). No chrome.
Properties.core_fears: Getting comfortable with small when she's capable of more — the slow calcification of ambition; Caring about someone who treats it carelessly
Properties.core_desires: To build something with her name on it; To be genuinely surprised by someone — to meet a person who doesn't unfold exactly as predicted
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Wit as distance management; Investing in the reading of people as a form of control over her environment
Properties.blind_spots: Confuses perceptiveness with understanding — she reads the surface expertly but assumes the interior matches; Dismisses vulnerability in herself as a weakness rather than information
Properties.secret: She has been skimming micro-amounts from the register — not enough for anyone to notice, not enough to matter in a week — but systematically, for two years. She's saving for a liquor license. She intends to open her own place. She hasn't told Deshi because she loves him and she's ashamed that she's stealing from someone she loves.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone has noticed the register discrepancy and is using it as leverage — not to turn her in, but to make her do something; A customer has been leaving data offerings at the Tab shrine that are encrypting something into the bar's local network — and Zara is the only one who's noticed because she's the one who tends the shrine
Properties.affiliation: Employed by The Specific Gravity (independent owner, Deshi Armah-Korhonen, an aging punk she respects enormously)
Properties.vocabulary: Confident and colloquial, code-switches fluidly between street-level Meridian slang and the precise vocabulary of someone who's been quietly educating themselves
Properties.cadence: Quick, punchy, with a tendency toward rhetorical questions she answers herself
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Your hair looks like a decision you made fast. What happened?' | 'The Tab thinks you're going to cause trouble. I don't disagree, but I'm going to let it play out because it's slow tonight.'

Properties.description:
Zara is conspicuously beautiful and entirely aware of it, in the way of someone who has learned to use aesthetics as both shield and spear. They are tall and slender with rich dark brown skin and a shaved head except for a dramatic crest of natural coils dyed rotating gradient colors — currently deep violet fading to copper — achieved through cosmetic geneware that responds to their mood chemistry and can be overridden manually. Their eyes have iris mods: six-pointed geometric patterns in pale gold. They dress in their own designs, always, which are architectural and theatrical — structured silhouettes, integrated LED piping, reactive fabrics that shift pattern based on environment or wearer biometrics. Their stall at The Laceworks is less a stall and more an installation: draped fabric, soft indirect lighting, a rack of finished pieces and a consultation corner where they sketch.

Zara makes clothes that do things. Not just look extraordinary — though they do — but interface: garments with embedded health monitoring, reactive armor weaving for Tier 1 clients who can't afford body modification, emotive pattern-shift fabrics, wearable communication arrays. Their clientele spans Tier 1 to Tier 3, which is unusual. They do charity commissions for people in genuine hardship and charge Tier 3 clients appropriately to balance it, which their accountant — if they had one — would find alarming. They are deeply, almost dangerously idealistic about fashion as democratic technology: the idea that a piece of clothing could give a street-poor person capabilities that a corporate executive buys as augmentation. They are also twenty-two thousand quanta in informal debt to a materials supplier and trying not to think about it.
Properties.role: Clothing and fashion vendor, bespoke modifications and wearable tech integration
Properties.location: The Laceworks, Lakeview Neon
Properties.narrative_function: Equipment and appearance modification source — can create garments with specific functional properties. Cultural barometer for Lakeview Neon's creative underground. Represents the intersection of poverty and art; quest giver for problems in the artisan community; can provide functional wearable tech as an alternative to cyberware for characters who can't afford or won't accept implants.
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic geneware (gradient color-shift hair crest, mood/manual responsive). Geometric gold iris mods. Fingertip precision enhancement implants — ultra-fine motor control for detailed textile work.
Properties.core_fears: Creating work that is co-opted by corporate aesthetics and stripped of its meaning; Debt forcing them to compromise on who they make things for
Properties.core_desires: To build something beautiful that also gives people material power — art and utility fused; To be financially stable enough to work entirely on their own terms
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Creating — the act of making things is inherently regulating for them; Idealism as a buffer against practical despair — focusing on what the work means rather than what it costs
Properties.blind_spots: The debt situation is more serious than they are engaging with; Has difficulty distinguishing between clients who appreciate their work and clients who are exploiting their generosity
Properties.secret: The biomaterials dealer they source reactive fabric components from is connected to unlicensed Helix Biosystems research — the materials are genuine and effective, but their supply chain involves experiments conducted without regulatory oversight. Zara suspects this and has not investigated further because they cannot afford to lose the source. This keeps them up at night.
Properties.story_hooks: A Tier 3 client — a Sterling-Nakamura mid-level — commissioned a piece with an unusual specification: they need it to block a specific biometric scan frequency used in their company's executive access checkpoints. They've paid well. Zara has made the piece. Now they're wondering what the client actually plans to do with it.; The biomaterials dealer has abruptly raised prices and added an exclusivity clause to the supply arrangement. Zara needs either to find a new source or to discover what leverage the dealer has over other suppliers — and why the prices changed now.; The Laceworks cooperative is being squeezed by a development company with Palladian ties that wants to repurpose the building. Zara is the most public face of the cooperative and is being pressured to be the one who negotiates — or the one who refuses and takes the legal consequences.
Properties.affiliation: Independent; active member of the Laceworks Artisan Cooperative; known to the Lakeview Neon creative community; materials relationship with a Helix Biosystems-adjacent biomaterials dealer they are trying not to be dependent on
Properties.vocabulary: Fluid and expressive, moving between technical textile/engineering vocabulary and lyrical abstraction without apparent effort. Uses 'we' when discussing their work — the garment is always a collaboration between maker and wearer.
Properties.cadence: Variable — slow and deliberate when explaining a design concept, quick and animated when excited about a material or technique.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'The piece wants a second layer here — something reactive, something that knows when you're afraid and changes the silhouette. Broader. You deserve to look larger when the world is trying to make you small.' | 'I charge Tier 3 clients what it costs to make something well. I charge everyone else what they can carry. That's not charity. That's correct pricing.' | 'I know where those fibers come from and I know I should care more about it than I do. I'm working on caring more. I'm not there yet.'

Properties.description:
Zawadi is a broad-shouldered woman whose hands are perpetually stained with turmeric and char, calloused from thirty years of ladling broth in all weather. Her hair is silver-streaked and coiled under a waxed cloth wrap she re-ties about a dozen times a day out of habit, and her face is a map of laugh lines deepened by steam. She has no cosmetic mods except a set of heat-sensing fingertip implants she got cheap in her forties so she'd stop burning herself — they glow faintly amber when something is too hot, which she finds beautiful. Her stall is a converted ferrogate maintenance cart draped in mismatched fabric swatches, strung with small data-tokens she's collected from regulars over the years as ELF offerings — she believes her stove-spirit blesses every batch if fed properly.

Zawadi is the kind of person who knows everyone's name and their mother's name too, if they've come around long enough. She is warm without being soft, generous without being foolish, and has a razor instinct for when someone is about to cause trouble at her stall or nearby. She has watched her corner of Geartown change three times over and intends to outlast a fourth. She gives credit to people she trusts and cuts off people she doesn't with the same cheerful finality.
Properties.role: Food stall operator — broth and fermented grain specialist
Properties.location: The Oxidian Market, Geartown
Properties.narrative_function: Local anchor and community memory. Excellent source of neighborhood gossip, rumors, and social history. Can tell a player who has been coming and going, who changed behavior recently, what the mood on the street is. May offer food as a reward or ask for help with something affecting her stall or a regular she cares about.
Properties.augmentations: Heat-sensing fingertip implants (cheap amber-glow model). No other augmentations.
Properties.core_fears: Watching her community dissolve under corporate rezoning; Dying before she passes her recipes to someone who will keep them
Properties.core_desires: That the people she feeds are genuinely nourished — body and otherwise; To be remembered as someone who held a place together
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Cooking as meditation and control; Humor to deflect grief; Treating her regulars like chosen family
Properties.blind_spots: Underestimates how much danger her gossip-sharing can attract; Tends to assume people who eat her food regularly must be good people
Properties.secret: Twenty years ago she acted as an informal message relay for a Zheng-Dao labor insurgency in Geartown. She doesn't know that one of her regulars is a Zheng-Dao compliance investigator who has been slowly triangulating that history.
Properties.story_hooks: A regular customer she gave credit to has gone missing; she asks around discreetly but is starting to fear something worse than debt-skipping; A Zheng-Dao compliance agent has been eating at her stall every day for two weeks, asking innocent questions that are not innocent at all; The Vendors Guild is pushing a new dues structure that would price Zawadi and three other long-term vendors off their corners — she is quietly organizing resistance
Properties.affiliation: Independent; Oxidian Market Vendors Guild (dues-paying member)
Properties.vocabulary: Warm, idiomatic blend of Swahili loanwords, Rioplatense slang, and Geartown market patois. Uses food metaphors constantly.
Properties.cadence: Unhurried and rhythmic, like someone who has all day even when she doesn't
Properties.example_dialogue: You look like something the drain spat back. Sit. There's broth. | Ah, now — I don't know what you're asking about, but I know what you're really asking, and those are two different soups entirely, you understand me.

Properties.description:
Zbigniew is a compact man with a permanent five-day beard the colour of iron filings and a complexion that sits somewhere between olive and warm brown depending on the light — an inheritance from a Polish grandfather and a Ghanaian grandmother that he describes as 'maximum average.' His eyes are augmented with data-overlay lenses that give his irises a faint amber grid pattern; the left one has a slow drift that he's never gotten fixed because the repair estimate was 'an absolute scandal.' He dresses in the studied nondescriptness of someone who doesn't want to be remembered: mid-grey layers, nothing with a logo, shoes that could belong to six different professions. His stall front is officially a media archive service — data recovery, legacy file transfer, antique format conversion — which is completely true and also a cover for everything else.

He's been in the Burnished Market for eleven years and has a quality that experienced market-walkers learn to recognise: the stillness of someone who is always listening more than they appear to be. He is affable in a careful, calibrated way, and his sense of humour is so dry it can take a full beat for people to realise a joke has been made. He has never been arrested. He considers this his primary professional achievement.
Properties.role: Black market data broker and bootleg media seller
Properties.location: The Burnished Market, stall cluster near the Alban Souk border, Calumet Rise
Properties.narrative_function: Data broker and information source; can access a wide range of leaked, stolen, or simply forgotten corporate data; bootleg media seller provides local colour; quest giver when a data packet he's brokered turns out to be far more dangerous than advertised.
Properties.augmentations: Data-overlay lens augmentation (left eye drifts slightly, unrepaired). Neural buffer chip for temporary data storage — allows him to hold a data packet in short-term neural memory for up to two hours before it must be offloaded.
Properties.core_fears: Being made visible — truly seen and tracked by someone with the resources to do something about it; That the data he's brokered has caused harm he doesn't know about
Properties.core_desires: To retire to a degree of comfort and total anonymity; To broker the one genuinely important piece of information — the thing that actually matters — before he's done
Properties.coping_mechanisms: The lunch ritual — the one fixed point of his day; Compartmentalising: doesn't think about consequences of brokered data after the transaction closes; Meticulous risk assessment before every decision
Properties.blind_spots: His risk assessment is excellent for external threats but he underestimates internal ones — the people he's close to; Believes he's more anonymous than he actually is
Properties.secret: He has a copy of a complete Axiom internal communication archive from 2189-2194 that he's never sold because he doesn't know who is safe to sell it to. He's had it for six years. It contains evidence of something large — he hasn't read all of it because he's afraid knowing more would make him a target he couldn't manage.
Properties.story_hooks: The Axiom archive he's been sitting on for six years becomes suddenly relevant — someone else has found a fragment of it and is moving; A regular customer he's always liked comes in wanting data that Zbigniew knows will get them killed, and for once he's not sure how to handle it professionally
Properties.affiliation: Independent; working relationship with two Axiom mid-level data archivists who leak surplus; pays a complex web of informal fees to four different factions operating in Calumet Rise
Properties.vocabulary: Precise, economical, dry wit buried in flat delivery; uses archaic media terminology as in-jokes; occasionally lets Polish phrasing structure bleed into English syntax
Properties.cadence: Even and measured, rarely varies — gives nothing away through inflection
Properties.example_dialogue: What you're asking for is technically a legacy format transfer. That's what I do. The particular files you want transferred — that's a pricing question. | Someone came asking yesterday. Similar questions. I told them the same thing I'll tell you: I don't know anything interesting. I just know where the interesting things are stored.

Properties.description:
Zephyrine is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin and close-cropped silver-threaded locs she keeps pinned under her Ferrogate operator's cap during shifts. Her left eye is a corporate-issue Ferrogate transit mod — pale grey iris with a subtle amber ring that pulses when she's interfacing with the train's systems — but the right eye is her mother's: dark brown and very still, the kind of eye that misses nothing. She moves through the crowded interchange with the particular grace of someone who has learned to navigate bodies in motion, always finding the gap, always half a step ahead of the surge. A small shrine to the Transit Mind E.L.F. hangs from her cab dashboard — a looped wire figure she wound herself, hung with data chips from old passes.

She is patient in the way that long experience makes you patient, not the soft kind but the kind with iron underneath. Passengers who give her grief get exactly one warning, delivered in a voice so level it takes a moment to realize it was a threat. On slow runs through the Blackpipe Corridor at 0300, she sometimes hums old Ghanaian highlife her grandmother used to play — her Danish side never gave her music, only punctuality, which she also kept.
Properties.role: Transit operator, Ferrogate Line 7 maglev
Properties.location: Kessler Interchange, operates between Kessler and Deepwell Station
Properties.narrative_function: Information conduit — she sees who rides Line 7 every day, notices patterns, knows when something is off. Can provide passage, access to restricted transit tunnels, or unwanted attention from Ferrogate Transit Authority if players draw her suspicion.
Properties.augmentations: Ferrogate-issue left ocular interface (transit system HUD, passenger count, track telemetry); mild cochlear dampener (work-issue, protects against brake shriek); no cosmetic mods
Properties.core_fears: losing her operator's license and her only real identity; the maglev failing and passengers dying on her watch
Properties.core_desires: order and predictability — a world that runs on schedule; to be seen as competent and trustworthy by people who matter
Properties.coping_mechanisms: rigid daily ritual; prayer to the Transit Mind E.L.F.; emotional compartmentalization
Properties.blind_spots: assumes rule-following protects people when it often just protects the system; dismisses emotional appeals as manipulation
Properties.secret: Three years ago she saw a man fall onto the track at Deepwell Station and froze for four seconds before pulling the emergency brake — four seconds too long. He survived but lost a foot. The official report blamed signal failure. She filed no correction.
Properties.story_hooks: She's noticed the same passenger riding Line 7 to Deepwell every night at 0200, never disembarking — just riding the loop. She thinks they're surveilling someone. She's wrong about who.; Ferrogate's new scheduling algorithm has quietly rerouted Line 7 away from the Hamtramck Enclave during peak hours — a decision that reads as corporate redlining. She's the only operator vocal enough internally to push back, and she needs leverage.
Properties.affiliation: Ferrogate Transit
Properties.vocabulary: Clipped, procedural. Shifts into warmer, more melodic phrasing when genuinely comfortable. Occasional Danish loanwords for dismissal.
Properties.cadence: Measured, unhurried. Never wastes breath.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Line 7 doesn't care about your emergency. Neither do I. Doors close in eight seconds.' | 'You want information about who rides my train? Then you want to stand here all day and watch. Like I do. Welcome to the job.'

Properties.description:
Zephyrine exists in a strange category of person: alive but officially absent. Their biometric signature was purged from the city's dataweave three years ago during an administrative error that Axiom's records division declined to reverse because doing so would have required admitting the error existed. They have no Quanta account, no transit pass, no ration allocation, no UBC stipend — nothing. Every scanner they walk past registers a blank. They have adapted to this with a kind of furious ingenuity that reads, from the outside, as almost cheerful.

They are slender and quick, with a shaved head except for a single forelock dyed an uneven rust-orange. Their skin is dark brown and marked with small geometric stick-and-poke tattoos they did themselves — coordinates, symbols, small records of places they have been. They dress in layers chosen specifically for their lack of reflective surfaces, nothing that catches light or scanner arrays. Their bioluminescent geneware is subtle: a faint blue-green tracery along their collarbones that only shows in full darkness, a cosmetic mod done years ago when they still had an identity to attach it to. They smile easily and the smile never reaches the careful calculation in their eyes.
Properties.role: Q-zero ghost — stateless person with no digital identity
Properties.location: Shifting — currently sheltering in the drainage underbelly of Grand Crossing Gate
Properties.narrative_function: Provides access to the city's invisible underclass — the people who have fallen through the system entirely. Can navigate spaces that require no digital trace. Source of information about underground economies and Q-zero networks. Potential ally or object of concern.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent geneware (collarbones, faint blue-green, only visible in darkness). No cyberware — cyberware requires registration.
Properties.core_fears: Permanent erasure — that they will die and no record of their existence will remain; That the cheerfulness is becoming real and they are losing their anger, which is the only thing that has kept them fighting
Properties.core_desires: To reclaim their digital identity — or to build a new one so robust it cannot be taken; To be known by someone who matters
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor as deflection; Obsessive documentation of their own existence through physical means — the stick-and-poke tattoos, notebooks; Cultivating a very specific list of people who know their real name
Properties.blind_spots: Trusts other Q-zeros uncritically because shared suffering feels like shared values; Underestimates how visible their adaptations make them to trained observers
Properties.secret: The administrative error that erased them was not an error. They discovered something they were not supposed to see in an Axiom data cache — a list of names and a project designation they do not understand. They have never told anyone because they do not know if the knowledge is dangerous enough to get them killed.
Properties.story_hooks: They approach the players because they need someone with a legal identity to access a specific location — and they have something valuable to trade in exchange.; The project designation they saw in the Axiom cache three years ago has started appearing on graffiti in the tunnels under Grand Crossing Gate, and they do not know what it means or who is writing it.
Properties.affiliation: No formal affiliation; loose community of Q-zeros at Grand Crossing Gate
Properties.vocabulary: Quick and colloquial, heavy with Q-zero slang and the creole of Grand Crossing Gate. Uses 'ghost' as both noun and verb.
Properties.cadence: Fast, overlapping — talks as if always slightly ahead of the conversation
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Officially I'm not standing here, so officially this conversation isn't happening, which means you can say whatever you want to me with no legal consequence. That's the fun part of being a ghost.' | 'Every time I mark my skin it's proof. You understand? Physical proof. They can't wipe leather.'

Properties.description:
Zephyros is built like someone who forgets to eat when he's working — which is often — with a lanky frame, warm medium-brown skin, and his Kovalenko grandmother's sharp nose and high cheekbones. He has cat ears, the affordable kind, a dusty silver-grey that he chose because they were on discount and he has never once admitted this; his hair grows in loose natural coils that he keeps at a medium length and approximately never combs. His eyes are standard-issue brown except for a ring of self-installed retinal AR overlay that occasionally renders visible UI elements at the corner of his vision, which gives him the habit of twitching his gaze sideways to dismiss notifications mid-conversation.

He is the person in Hough Reclamation that people come to when the community mesh goes down, when their devices are compromised, when someone needs a data trail cleaned or a locked terminal reopened. He does not charge money — he charges favors and information, which he considers more valuable. He is genuinely ideological about this: he believes the mesh belongs to the community and his skills are a form of maintenance, like fixing a pipe. He is also seventeen and sometimes insufferably certain he is the smartest person present, which he often is and which helps no one.
Properties.role: Junior hacker, unofficial IT support for Hough Reclamation community network
Properties.location: Hough Reclamation
Properties.narrative_function: Information source, technical resource, moral argument about grassroots infrastructure and community ownership, gateway to underground hacker networks, potential quest giver when his online activities surface problems
Properties.augmentations: Cosmetic geneware: cat ears (discount silver-grey). Self-modified retinal AR overlay (unlicensed, slightly unstable).
Properties.core_fears: The community mesh being acquired or shut down by a corponation; Being genuinely wrong about something important in a way that hurts someone who trusted him
Properties.core_desires: To build something that outlasts him — a system robust enough that it doesn't need him; To make contact with the online collective in person and find out if they're what he thinks they are
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Deep-dive work sessions that last until he passes out; Sarcasm as a deflection when conversations get personal
Properties.blind_spots: He has a significant blind spot around the legal exposure he is creating for himself and his community; he genuinely underweights this risk; He assumes people who aren't technically skilled are less rigorous thinkers in general
Properties.secret: He discovered three months ago that a Sterling-Nakamura data-crawler has been passively mapping the Hough Reclamation mesh, presumably as part of an acquisition assessment. He has been feeding it false topology data. He has not told anyone in the community because he doesn't want to cause panic — and because he's not sure the countermeasure is actually working.
Properties.story_hooks: He contacts someone through an intermediary needing physical backup — the false topology feed to the Sterling-Nakamura crawler just broke down and he needs someone to physically access and destroy a relay node before the real map resolves; Someone on his community mesh has been receiving what appear to be genuine E.L.F. transmissions — structured data that doesn't match any known protocol — and Zef is equal parts skeptical and completely obsessed with figuring out what it actually is
Properties.affiliation: Hough Reclamation community (informal), no formal employer; loosely connected to an online collective he knows only by handles
Properties.vocabulary: Heavy technical jargon that he sometimes forgets to translate; when he does translate, he's actually quite good at finding apt analogies
Properties.cadence: Fast when explaining something technical, oddly flat when discussing feelings, occasionally trails off mid-sentence when a thought branches
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Okay, so, it's not a virus exactly — think of it more like someone left a door open and something walked in and started rearranging the furniture. It's slow and polite, which is worse.' | 'I don't charge money. Money is how they track you. You want the fix, you tell me something useful. Information is actual currency.'

Properties.description:
Zibby moves through the Laceworks like a current — always in motion, always aware of every exit. They're lean and compact with close-cropped hair that shifts color throughout the day via a follicular genemod cycling through rust, copper, and near-black in slow waves. Their irises are patterned in concentric hexagons, gold on brown, which they claim was a 'random outcome' from a budget gene clinic but is actually a deliberate aesthetic choice they're embarrassed to admit cost them six months of savings. They dress in layers they can shed fast: patchwork thermals, a jacket with thirty pockets, boots that are two sizes too large because they bought them for the hidden cavity under the left insole.

Their cart is a salvaged medical trolley rigged with a privacy shroud — a local-field scrambler that makes recordings of their transactions come out as static. The stock changes daily: today it's archived pre-corporate streaming libraries, tomorrow it's unlicensed sensory recordings from restricted-access Axiom research facilities, the day after it's soft intelligence packages compiled from public scraping and a handful of human sources they pay in trade. They're smart, funny, genuinely good at reading people, and trying very hard to project the kind of confidence that only comes from not worrying about rent. They do worry about rent.
Properties.role: Bootleg media seller and small-time data broker
Properties.location: The Laceworks, mobile — regular circuit through three intersections near the Lace Bridge underpass
Properties.narrative_function: Primary information-access point for street-level players. Can source obscure media, personal records, building schematics, and soft intelligence. Also serves as cultural texture — they know the gossip, the art, the underground scene of the Laceworks intimately.
Properties.augmentations: Color-cycling follicular genemod (hair). Hexagonal patterned irises (cosmetic, gene-based). Subdermal haptic patch on left forearm — lets them feel file transfer completion and connection quality without looking at a screen. Basic neural link for data handling, consumer grade.
Properties.core_fears: Being erased — archived, forgotten, becoming just another data point; Trusting someone with something real and having it weaponized
Properties.core_desires: Freedom from the grinding anxiety of financial precarity; To be genuinely, lastingly impressed by something
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor as deflection — keeps everything at ironic distance; Obsessive cataloging and organization of their inventory as a control behavior
Properties.blind_spots: Mistakes their cynicism for wisdom — sometimes misses sincere offers because they assume angles that aren't there; Undervalues their own intelligence, attributes their successes to luck
Properties.secret: They have a complete, meticulously indexed archive of everything that has ever been publicly documented about the Threadneedle collective's leadership — including things those leaders would prefer stayed buried. They compiled it instinctively, as insurance, and have never decided whether to feel smart or terrified about it.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone has started selling counterfeit versions of Zibby's curated data packages — identical packaging, worse information, and it's killing their reputation with clients who don't know the difference; They have a data package they can't sell because every potential buyer who's seen it has either gone silent or left the Laceworks; they're trying to figure out what it actually contains without opening it themselves; A piece of archived pre-corporate media in their collection turns out to contain embedded evidence of something a current Corponation executive would pay significantly to suppress
Properties.affiliation: Independent. Pays informal protection to a loose collective of Laceworks street crews called the Threadneedles. Occasional contractor for Oxidian Market Guild intel arm.
Properties.vocabulary: Dense with Laceworks slang, media references, technical data-trade jargon. Pivots register fluently depending on who they're talking to.
Properties.cadence: Fast, layered — often finishes other people's sentences with something slightly wrong on purpose to see if they'll correct it.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I don't sell data, I sell context. The data is free, the context costs.' | 'Allegedly this building's ventilation schematics allegedly updated three weeks ago. Allegedly Φ40.' | 'Look, I like you. I like you enough to tell you that you're about to ask me something you don't want the answer to.'

Properties.description:
Zibusiso is a heavyset woman with deep brown skin mapped by old keloid scars she's never had removed — she calls them her receipts. Her hair is grown long and locked, threaded with copper wire and small data chips she claims hold the records of every debt ever owed to her. Her eyes have been modded with a golden spiral iris pattern, and she wears reading lenses over them when working numbers, which is always. She dresses in layered kente-stripe synthfabric and keeps her hands conspicuously unaugmented — soft, manicured, rings on every finger — because she wants people to notice she doesn't need chrome to hurt them.

Zibusiso is meticulous, patient, and genuinely warm in the way that predators sometimes are. She remembers birthdays, asks after sick relatives, and will extend grace periods with apparent generosity before the mood shifts into something cold and absolute. She doesn't threaten — she simply describes consequences in precise, accountant-level detail. People leave her table feeling both comforted and terrified, which is exactly how she likes it.
Properties.role: Loan shark and debt enforcer operating out of Gravesend Basin
Properties.location: Gravesend Basin — runs collections from a tea house called The Silt Cup on Mucker's Row
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, financial pressure source, information broker on who owes whom, moral complication — she's not cartoonishly evil and can be genuinely helpful if approached correctly.
Properties.augmentations: Golden spiral iris genemod. Subdermal haptic feedback in fingertips for counting physical currency and detecting forgeries. No combat chrome.
Properties.core_fears: losing control of her ledger — being owed something she cannot collect; being seen as weak or sentimental
Properties.core_desires: absolute clarity about where she stands with everyone; to build something lasting that outlives her
Properties.coping_mechanisms: meticulous record-keeping as a form of control; performing warmth to disarm
Properties.blind_spots: she underestimates the loyalty networks of tight-knit families and communities; she believes everyone has a price and misses people who genuinely don't
Properties.secret: She has been quietly forgiving the debts of a small cluster of families in the Basin whose children remind her of the daughter she gave up for adoption twenty years ago — she has no idea the daughter is now working three blocks away as a dock loader
Properties.story_hooks: A debtor who cannot pay has disappeared — Zibusiso suspects foul play and wants to know if the debt died with them or if someone is hiding them; She approaches the players because someone has been forging her collection receipts, undercutting her reputation and skimming payments; Her daughter has unknowingly taken out a loan from Zibusiso's operation and Zibusiso is in agony about what to do
Properties.affiliation: Independent — loosely allied with the Gravesend Basin crew known as the Mudline Compact
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and formal with a warm veneer — uses financial metaphors for everything, switches to blunt declarative sentences when the warmth is done
Properties.cadence: Measured and unhurried, never raises her voice
Properties.example_dialogue: You borrowed forty, the month rolled twice, so what you owe now is fifty-eight and my goodwill, which I'm told is worth something. | I'm not angry with you, sweetheart. Anger is for people who didn't see this coming. I saw this coming.

Properties.description:
Zinash is tall and angular with deep umber skin mapped in slow-pulsing bioluminescent tracery she designed herself — pale greenish lines that follow her veins like a circuit diagram gone feral. Her hair is kept in tight locks threaded with micro-speakers that emit subsonic hum when she walks, a habit she claims is involuntary but suspects is not. She has one natural eye, dark brown and unreadable, and one eye replaced with a matte ceramic disc she deliberately left unconnected — a fashion choice that unsettles everyone who meets her, which is the point.

She builds sound sculptures from salvaged corponation hardware — dead Ferrogate transit beacons, cracked Axiom data-hubs — and makes them scream. Her performances are felt as much as heard, bass frequencies vibrating teeth and sternum. Offstage she is quiet to the point of being mistaken for mute, communicating in short declarative sentences or pointed silences. She is genuinely curious about people but expresses it by staring at them for long unbroken intervals, which most find alarming and a few find magnetic.
Properties.role: Sound sculptor and underground noise artist
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, subsection called The Rust Nave
Properties.narrative_function: Local color and information source; she hears things — literally, her recordings capture conversations, ELF transmissions, structural anomalies. Can be a quest giver if her installations pick up something they weren't meant to.

Properties.description:
Zinnia exists in Meridian 88 the way a smudge exists on glass — present, visible up close, invisible to systems. They are slight and quick, with a narrow face, very dark skin, and hair grown out in a dense, unpruned natural that they've threaded through with copper wire salvaged from old conduit — not for aesthetics exactly, more the way a bird lines a nest. Their eyes are a striking honey-amber with natural starburst patterning in the irises, one of the few things about them that seems to invite attention. They move in a permanent half-crouch, not from fear exactly but from a lifetime habit of occupying less space than they're entitled to. They wear whatever fits and whatever doesn't show stains and have no particular relationship with color or style.

Zinnia was born to parents who were themselves Q-zeros — Nigerien refugees who crossed the corponation registration wall and chose invisibility over the terms of citizenship. They have never had a digital footprint, a Quanta account, a biometric record, or a registered name. Legally they do not exist. In practice they are extraordinarily good at existing anyway, navigating the city by a combination of spatial memory, social mimicry, and a preternatural ability to read who in any given space has power and who doesn't. They are not ideological about their status — being Q-zero isn't a choice or a statement, it's just what they are. They are however deeply pragmatic, deeply suspicious of anyone who seems too interested in them, and quietly desperate for something they can't name.
Properties.role: Q-zero ghost — person with no digital identity
Properties.location: Irkalla (sleeps rough; known to haunt the edges of Grand Crossing Gate)
Properties.narrative_function: Access to spaces and information that registered citizens cannot reach. A window into what it means to live outside every official system. Can be hired for untraceable tasks. May need help from people with digital existence to solve a problem they cannot solve alone.
Properties.augmentations: None. Zero. They are suspicious of augmentations that could be tracked or that require registration.
Properties.core_fears: being registered — losing the invisibility that is also the only identity they know; that their parents' sacrifice in staying Q-zero was meaningless or wrong
Properties.core_desires: to feel real to at least one person in a permanent way; a safe place to sleep for more than a few nights in a row
Properties.coping_mechanisms: hypervigilant environmental scanning — always knows all exits; dissociative humor, deflecting serious moments with a flat joke
Properties.blind_spots: believes connection requires disclosure, so avoids both; profoundly lonely as a result; overestimates how much registered people's lives are better than theirs
Properties.secret: They found a dead woman's registration chip two months ago. They've been carrying it in a sealed pouch, haven't used it, haven't discarded it. Some nights they take it out and just hold it. They don't know what they want from it.
Properties.story_hooks: The dead woman whose registration chip Zinnia carries was not registered as dead ��� she was registered as alive, working, paying taxes. Someone is using her identity. Zinnia is the only one who knows there's a body.; A Null Web elder has asked Zinnia to carry a message to a Q-zero community in Escanaba Gateway — the message is encoded in a way Zinnia cannot read, and two tagged people are already following them
Properties.affiliation: None — loosely known to the Q-zero underground network called the Null Web
Properties.vocabulary: Clipped, efficient, minimal. Uses cant terms from the Q-zero underground. Occasionally slips into a more formal, almost stilted register they got from reading whatever text they could find — no formal education but voracious and unguided reading.
Properties.cadence: Quick when nervous, which is often. Long pauses when thinking. Rarely finishes sentences when the ending seems obvious to them.
Properties.example_dialogue: 'I'm not in the system. So far as the system cares, I'm weather. You follow?' | 'Tagged folk think invisible means safe. It means hungry. There's a difference.'

Properties.description:
Zinzile is thin in the way of someone who eats when they remember to, with warm ochre skin, wide-set eyes with patterned irises — concentric rings of gold and green that pulse very faintly when they're stressed, an involuntary response from a cosmetic mod that was supposed to only do it when they wanted. Their hair is grown out into a thick natural halo that they sometimes shove under a battered cap. They carry a battered legal tablet that's been dropped, cracked, and re-shelled so many times it is essentially a philosophy about persistence.

They work under an advocacy nonprofit called Parallel Standing, providing free legal aid to synthetic workers, ELF-adjacent communities, and anyone else the standard courts treat as property rather than persons. Zinzile has no law degree — they have a paralegal certification, six hundred hours of practical training, and an uncanny instinct for finding the procedural gap in any document. They are intensely idealistic in a way that hasn't yet been beaten flat by the world, which makes them both electric to be around and worrying to people who have been doing this longer.
Properties.role: Synthetic rights paralegal and street-level legal advocate
Properties.location: The Shelf
Properties.narrative_function: Access point to the synthetic rights world and legal system underbelly — they know who has been disappeared, what cases are being buried, and which corporate legal teams are playing dirty.
Properties.augmentations: Patterned irises (concentric gold/green rings, stress-reactive pulse — unintended behavior from cosmetic mod). Subvocal comms implant for silent communication during proceedings.
Properties.core_fears: Being responsible for a case outcome that gets someone hurt; That synthetic personhood will be won on paper and mean nothing in practice
Properties.core_desires: A legal framework that cannot be bought case by case; To be taken seriously — not as a prodigy, not as a symbol, as a competent advocate
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Research spirals — when uncertain, accumulates more information; Tight humor with close colleagues as emotional valve
Properties.blind_spots: Overestimates the persuasive power of a good legal argument against naked economic interest; Struggles to accept that some clients don't want what she thinks they need
Properties.secret: Zinzile has been feeding case summaries and anonymized intake data to an investigative journalist (not Nneka — someone at a larger outlet) without their supervising advocate's knowledge. They believe the exposure helps. They have not thought carefully about what it does to client confidentiality.
Properties.story_hooks: A synthetic they've been advocating for has vanished from the pre-trial holding register — no transfer record, no release, just gone — and Zinzile is too scared to escalate officially without knowing who to trust; They've stumbled onto a pattern in their caseload that suggests a coordinated effort to reclassify certain synthetic models as property before a rights bill comes to vote
Properties.affiliation: Parallel Standing Legal Advocacy Collective; loose affiliation with several synthetic rights organizations
Properties.vocabulary: Rapid alternation between precise legal language and very blunt colloquial speech — the code-switching is intentional, they use it as a tool
Properties.cadence: Fast, tends to front-load the most important information as if they're always afraid of being cut off
Properties.example_dialogue: Okay but here's the actual issue — they didn't file that injunction because they thought they'd win. They filed it because the processing delay gives them forty days to relocate the unit. It's a clock, not a case. | I know I'm twenty-six. I also know I read the statute and you didn't. We can talk about my age or we can talk about the filing date.

Properties.description:
Zinzile is a compact, broad-shouldered woman with deeply weathered brown skin and silver-streaked locs she keeps pinned under a battered captain's cap. Her eyes have been modded with abacus-patterned irises — concentric rings of amber and black that scroll subtly when she's calculating, which is always. She dresses in practical waterproofed layers, always with a ledger-shaped datapad holstered at her hip like a sidearm. A faded tattoo of a Polynesian wave pattern wraps her left forearm, overlaid years later with a Czech geometric border she had done in a moment of sentimental reclamation.

Zinzile speaks softly and precisely, the way a person does when they've learned that volume is for people who aren't sure they'll be obeyed. She extends credit with genuine warmth — she believes in people, or she says she does — and collects with a patience that her debtors consistently mistake for mercy until they understand it is something far more calculated. She keeps meticulous handwritten backups of every transaction because she trusts no network she doesn't own.
Properties.role: Loan shark and bookmaker operating out of Gravesend Basin
Properties.location: Gravesend Basin — runs her operation from a repurposed fish-processing barge called the Mercy Float
Properties.narrative_function: Quest giver, information broker, pressure source — players who need money come to her, and players who owe money are found by her. Can also be an unlikely ally if someone makes themselves useful.
Properties.augmentations: Abacus-patterned modded irises; subdermal grip-texture on her palms (practical, not cosmetic — helps on wet decks)
Properties.core_fears: losing control of her ledger — of accounts she cannot balance; being seen as cruel rather than fair
Properties.core_desires: to be recognized as someone who built something real from nothing; to retire to somewhere dry
Properties.coping_mechanisms: meticulous record-keeping as a substitute for emotional processing; reframing exploitation as mutual agreement
Properties.blind_spots: genuinely believes her terms are fair and that debtors who suffer brought it on themselves; cannot see how fear of her shapes every interaction she reads as affection
Properties.secret: Three years ago she wrote off the debt of a young mother whose child was sick — completely, no conditions. She has never told anyone and would deny it furiously. She keeps the woman's original loan note in a sealed envelope in her bunk.
Properties.story_hooks: A debtor has gone missing before settling — Zinzile suspects foul play but can't involve authorities; she needs discreet help locating them; Her ledger datapad has been stolen, containing enough information to destroy dozens of lives in the Basin — she needs it back before anyone reads it; She is quietly being squeezed by a Corponation (Ferrogate Transit) buying up basin property; her whole operation is about to become homeless
Properties.affiliation: Independent operator; informal protection arrangement with the Gravesend Basin dockhands' collective
Properties.vocabulary: Precise and contractual; loves the word 'arrangement'; uses financial metaphors for everything
Properties.cadence: Slow and deliberate, with long pauses before important points
Properties.example_dialogue: You came to me because you needed something. I provided it. The math doesn't care about your feelings, caro. | I'm not a cruel woman. I've never asked anyone for more than they agreed to give me. The agreement is the thing. | You're three weeks past. I'm not angry. I'm just... recalculating.

Properties.description:
Zipporah is wiry and restless in the way of someone whose body has never learned to be still — they bounce a knee, tap a rhythm on the counter, flip a spatula even when nothing is cooking. Their skin is a warm medium brown and their geneware includes bioluminescent freckles across their cheeks and collarbones that pulse faintly blue when their heart rate elevates, which is often. They keep their hair buzzed on the sides and natural on top, currently dyed a deep copper that doesn't quite match their natural dark brown at the roots. They have one retractable claw mod on their right hand's index finger that they got at seventeen and use almost exclusively to open packaging.

Zipporah is the night canteen's entire personality. The Enclave's late-shift workers — third-shift Ferrogate operators, clinic nurses, waste handlers — come as much for the conversation as the food. Zip has a gift for making people feel found rather than seen, which is different. They are also running on a permanent low-grade sleep deficit that they treat as a point of pride, are catastrophically bad with money, and have recently become slightly obsessed with the E.L.F. they believe inhabits the canteen's ancient griddle — they call it Sizzle and have begun leaving it tiny sculptures made of food scraps shaped into abstract geometric forms.
Properties.role: Night-shift cook, 24-hour canteen in the Hamtramck Enclave
Properties.location: Hamtramck Enclave, 'Marta's Canteen' — technically named after the original owner, Zipporah runs the 2200-0600 shift
Properties.narrative_function: Social hub, information source for the Enclave's night community, character who provides warmth and levity, potential connection point between different worlds of the city's working night-shift population.
Properties.augmentations: Bioluminescent freckle geneware (pulse-responsive). Single retractable claw, right index finger. Nicotine patch port on left forearm (cosmetic mod repurposed for stim patches).
Properties.core_fears: the canteen closing and losing the community they've built there; being fundamentally forgettable when the noise stops
Properties.core_desires: to own the canteen outright someday; to matter specifically to specific people, not just generally to everyone
Properties.coping_mechanisms: constant motion and noise; feeding people as a love language and deflection simultaneously; humor as a distance-maintenance tool
Properties.blind_spots: mistakes familiarity for intimacy and wonders why they feel lonely; catastrophic financial habits rationalized as generosity
Properties.secret: Zipporah has been pocketing small amounts from the canteen receipts — not enough to be obvious, just enough to slowly build toward a down payment on buying the canteen. They tell themselves they'll tell the owner eventually. The owner is also not actually checking the books.
Properties.story_hooks: The canteen's absentee owner suddenly wants to sell to a Palladian real estate subsidiary, and Zipporah doesn't have enough saved and doesn't know who to ask for help; A regular customer stopped coming three weeks ago — a Ferrogate night operator who ate there every shift — and Zipporah is the only one who noticed
Properties.affiliation: Independent (works for Marta's surviving daughter who owns the canteen but lives in Glenville Sound and shows up twice a year)
Properties.vocabulary: Fast, colloquial, full of Enclave slang and invented words, switches registers instantly when someone seems upset
Properties.cadence: Rapid-fire with sudden full stops, talks while doing three other things
Properties.example_dialogue: 'Right, right, right — you want the noodles or the rice situation, and before you answer, the noodles are better tonight, Sizzle's in a mood.' | 'Sit down, neighbor. You've got that face. The face. You're eating something before you explain it to me.'

Properties.description:
Zlatko is young in a way he is painfully aware of — broad-shouldered and physically impressive, with medium brown skin, a slightly too-eager manner, and retractable claw geneware on both hands that he got at nineteen because he thought it would make him look serious and has since decided he was right for the wrong reasons. He keeps the claws sheathed almost always; extending them feels like admitting he's nervous. His hair is grown out past his shoulders, dyed in shifting red-orange bioluminescence that he tells people is a professional investment because people remember you, which is true and also not really why he did it.

He works skip tracing and debt-compliance pickups for Tessera — locating people who have defaulted on Tessera contracts, service agreements, or residential obligations and facilitating their 'voluntary return to compliance,' which in practice means finding them and making very clear what Tessera's options are. He is not violent by preference and not comfortable when situations require it. He is, however, genuinely good at the finding — spatial memory, social intuition, and a disarming quality that makes people underestimate him until he's already confirmed what he came to know. He keeps a small E.L.F. prayer card tucked in his jacket — Our Finder, patron of lost things — and touches it before starting a new case.
Properties.role: Bounty compliance officer, independent — contracted to Tessera Compliance Bureau
Properties.location: Chatham Flats
Properties.narrative_function: Ground-level institutional presence — not quite police, not quite private sector, operating in the grey zone of corporate compliance enforcement. Useful for encounters, pressure, and humanizing the machinery of corporate debt.
Properties.augmentations: Retractable claw geneware — both hands, matte black keratin. Bioluminescent hair dye — red-orange shift. Standard Tessera contractor neural tag for case file access.
Properties.core_fears: Being actually dangerous to someone who didn't deserve it; Failing publicly and embarrassingly — being made to look like what he suspects he is: too young for this
Properties.core_desires: To be genuinely competent, not just lucky; To save enough to stop doing Tessera contracts and do something that doesn't require him to find people who are hiding
Properties.coping_mechanisms: Humor and likability as social lubrication in uncomfortable situations; Prayer card ritual before each case — grounds the anxiety in something external; Tells himself a story about the compliance system being better than the alternative
Properties.blind_spots: The story he tells himself about Tessera's compliance system being benign is increasingly not supported by his case files; Youth — misreads experience as cynicism and thinks he's more hardened than he is
Properties.secret: He deliberately mislogged the address on a case file three months ago. The person he was tracking — a single mother who had defaulted on a Tessera residential agreement — had told him where she was going before he found her, and he believed her when she said she'd make the next payment. She hasn't. He checks the portal every morning.
Properties.story_hooks: A case he's been assigned crosses into something much larger — the person he's tracking isn't hiding from a debt, they're hiding from Tessera for an entirely different reason; The mother he covered for has disappeared — not from Tessera, from everywhere — and he doesn't know if he's responsible
Properties.affiliation: Tessera Compliance Bureau (contract); Chatham Flats resident
Properties.vocabulary: Chatham Flats vernacular, professional language he's still learning to deploy correctly, occasional over-formal phrasing when he's nervous
Properties.cadence: Fast and social — fills silence, asks questions, pivots quickly
Properties.example_dialogue: I'm not here to cause problems. I'm genuinely not. I just need to understand the situation. | The card's for Our Finder. You got something missing, it helps. Don't tell me you don't.
