Properties.sights: fire-blackened building facades stabilized by improvised scaffolding; dead trees preserved by the chemical contamination that killed them; new construction growing from ruins — improvised, raw, and defiant; chemical contamination visible as iridescent sheen on standing water; murals covering entire building faces with imagery too large to read from street level; the haze from the still-active chemical reaction in the soil at the district's western edge
Properties.sounds: wind through structural gaps in burned buildings; construction sounds — improvised, non-corporate, constant; music from multiple sources at competing volumes; the absence of corporate announcement systems and advertising audio; generators running on salvaged fuel; community radio broadcasts audible from speakers mounted on buildings
Properties.smells: petrochemical undertone that never fully dissipates; wood smoke from heating fires; fresh construction materials — concrete, metal, cut wood; communal cooking from the district's open kitchens; the particular smell of soil that has been chemically altered
Properties.feel: Simultaneously desolate and vital — a place that the city has written off and whose residents have responded by building something the city never designed and cannot easily control. The contamination is real and the dangers are real, but so is the sense that here, at least, something is being built for the people who live in it.

Properties.description: A twelve-story burned-out residential tower that Ashfall collective has rebuilt from the inside out, leaving the scorched exterior intact while creating a fully functioning arts and communications center within. The antenna array on its roof broadcasts the Render's community radio to all of Meridian 88 and theoretically cannot be legally shut down due to the district's ambiguous condemnation status.

The edge of the western contamination zone where active chemical reactions in the soil make the ground itself hostile — surfaces corrode, electronics fail, and exposure beyond thirty minutes begins producing measurable physiological effects. The perimeter is marked by a dense collection of warning structures, memorials to those who didn't heed them, and the research outpost of a scientist who has lived here for eleven years studying the reaction.

The Render's central exchange, held in the open footprint of a collapsed shopping center whose foundations have been converted into permanent market infrastructure. Unlike Meridian's commercial spaces, nothing here is owned by entities outside the district — every stall, every service, every transaction exists within the community's own economy, and the Commons serves simultaneously as market, meeting ground, and the closest thing the Render has to a civic center.
Henry Ford's cathedral of industry, reborn — autonomous vehicle chassis, military drones, and sealed operations that nobody discusses
Ouroboros Energy's air filtration station — the mechanical lung that keeps the neighborhood breathing, at a price
Six blocks of bars, repair shops, and the informal economy — where the real business of the neighborhood happens after shift change
The densest concentration of independent machine shops and fabrication operations in the eastern corridor — if it can be built, someone on 185th can build it
Salvage processing operations along Euclid's industrial shoreline — the raw material supply chain for the entire Rust Circuit
A converted factory floor where the district's governing body meets — dispute resolution, standard-setting, and the closest thing the Rust Circuit has to a courthouse
Level 3, East Section. The social and informational heart of the Shelf. Mrs. Chen feeds everyone, asks no questions, and knows everything.
The old pier's grand ballroom, now the Shelf Council's meeting hall. Thursday nights, consensus decisions, no weapons inside.
The Shelf's outermost edge — a railing made of salvaged cable over a forty-meter drop to Lake Michigan. The best view in Meridian, if you have the stomach for it.
Level 3, East Section, near Mrs. Chen's. Six by four meters. Lake-facing window. Katana on the wall. Stabilizers under the cot. Home.
Rotates monthly. Currently somewhere in the interior corridors of Level 5. You don't find Sable. Sable finds you.

Nodes.Name: Everywhere — the Spire is visible from every district in Meridian, a constant presence in every skyline
The I-90 Vein — highway corridor connecting to the Cleveland sprawl
Lake Erie — Palladian maritime operations and open water access

Properties.description: West bank construction facility building the cargo platforms and floating infrastructure that the corridor's lake economy runs on
East bank facility servicing the rail corponation's eastern fleet — the place where what Ferrogate moves and how it moves it can be observed
The Puerto Rican commercial and cultural corridor — the Steel Shore's only independent community district, sustained by generations of cultural continuity
40 million metric tons annually — the machine that feeds the eastern GLM, indifferent to what it's feeding them
The original Eastern Market brick buildings, where an unauthorized farmers' market operates weekly in the shadow of the megastructure
The Tier 3+ food facility — where actual meat and real produce are processed for people who can afford to eat what food used to be
The Reach's primary community space, built across the connected rooftops of three pre-surge apartment buildings — meeting space, market, and the location of the community's main filtration array
A cluster of submerged financial and corporate office buildings in the Reach's center, known to contain sealed vaults — the most contested salvage zone in the Reach
The underwater channel where the pre-surge river still runs beneath the surge water, navigable by experienced divers but genuinely dangerous — and the location of Vespid's buried fiber cable
The point at Lockhaven North where Ferrogate's southern section meets Stonepath's northern section — a jurisdictional seam in the corridor's fabric
A Bathysphere fiber-optic node on the Superior shore, 200 kilometers from the nearest town — the loneliest piece of critical infrastructure in Canada
The northern section's largest service complex — the last reliable stop before the long run to Grainfort, and the social hub of the Superior shore

Nodes.Name: Currently varies — the Vagrant's connections change with its position
Shore communities along the canal routes

Properties.description: A narrow corridor of pre-Meridian architecture preserved — some say imprisoned — within the megacity's northward expansion, the Vestige is a six-block stretch of late 20th and early 22nd century residential and commercial buildings that a coalition of preservation interests, academic institutions, and wealthy nostalgia investors have maintained in a state of deliberate historical stasis. The buildings have been reinforced, weatherproofed, and in some cases entirely reconstructed from archival photographs, but they are kept deliberately free of visible modern infrastructure. Power and data lines run beneath the streets. Climate control is hidden inside original-looking facade elements. The effect is unsettling — a pocket of another era surrounded on all sides by Meridian's towers.
Properties.aliases: Old Evanston Remnant, The Museum Quarter, Ghostrow, The Kept
Properties.demographics: A small permanent resident population of academics, preservation staff, and the extremely wealthy who pay extraordinary sums for 'authentic' addresses. A much larger daily population of tourism workers, students from the attached university annex, and researchers. The buildings' actual heritage community — descendants of the neighborhoods that existed here — are largely absent, priced and curated out.
Properties.economy: Heritage tourism, academic research grants, luxury residential leasing at rates that exclude essentially everyone, corporate event hosting in 'authentic historical settings,' and a significant underground economy among preservation staff who supplement their incomes by facilitating after-hours access for clients who want the Vestige without the curated experience.
Properties.power_structure: The Meridian Heritage Conservancy, a nominally nonprofit organization controlled in practice by a board of five investment entities, holds total administrative control. Meridian city government defers entirely to Conservancy decisions within the perimeter. Informal power rests with long-tenured preservation staff who know where every camera blind spot and access tunnel is located.
Properties.dangers: Conservancy security that treats unauthorized documentation as intellectual property theft; the social and legal exposure of whatever is being hidden beneath the authentic-looking streets; wealthy residents with significant corporate connections and fragile egos; the Conservancy's aggressive use of historical designation laws to suppress adjacent development — and anyone who threatens that control; AI-assisted surveillance disguised as period street fixtures
Properties.opportunities: off-grid meeting spaces in buildings with hidden modern infrastructure but no corporate network presence; access to genuine pre-Meridian physical archives maintained by the university annex; preservation staff as sources on what the Conservancy is actually protecting; the tunnels beneath the Vestige predate Meridian's surveillance infrastructure entirely; wealthy residents with historical obsessions who can be leveraged or cultivated as patrons
Properties.story_hooks: A preservation staff member has found something in a sealed sub-basement that doesn't belong to any historical period — and it appears to be recent; The Conservancy is attempting to have a neighboring district designated as 'historically incompatible' — which would trigger forced demolition — and the residents there need evidence of the process's corruption; A wealthy Vestige resident has commissioned a private investigator to find out why their 'authentic' home is broadcasting a signal they can't account for; An academic at the university annex has found that the Conservancy's archive contains deliberate falsifications of pre-Meridian history, and she's missing; Someone is living in the Vestige illegally, in the spaces between the authentic facades and the real walls, and has been for years
Properties.sights: intact pre-Meridian storefronts with period-accurate signage; brick and mortar facades maintained to appear weathered but not deteriorated; period street lighting casting warm incandescent-style glow; tourists with recording implants on guided historical experiences; the jarring vertical wall of modern Meridian architecture at every street's end; uniformed preservation staff maintaining the illusion of authenticity
Properties.sounds: deliberately curated ambient audio pumped from hidden speakers; tour guide narration in multiple languages; the absence of industrial noise — conspicuously quiet; wind channeled oddly by the surrounding megastructures; muffled modern city sounds from just beyond the perimeter
Properties.smells: engineered 'old city' scent pumped through climate systems; real brick and aged wood from genuinely old structures; coffee from the preservation-compliant cafes; the faint antiseptic of hidden climate control systems
Properties.feel: Profoundly artificial in its authenticity — a place where the past has been taxidermied rather than preserved, and the people who live and work here exist in a performance of history that benefits interests they may not fully understand.

Properties.description: The most intact and heavily curated section of the Vestige, a full city block maintained to represent a specific month in 2119. Every surface, every storefront, every parked vehicle is period-accurate. It is rented exclusively for corporate immersive experience events and costs more per night than most Meridian residents earn in a year.

The Meridian University historical research outpost embedded in the Vestige, occupying a converted pre-Meridian library building. Publicly a research facility, it maintains the only physical archive of pre-Meridian municipal records in the corridor — and controls access to them with quiet ferocity.

An irregular no-man's-land at the Vestige's southern edge where the preservation boundary meets an unfinished Meridian development project that stalled in litigation. Neither maintained nor demolished, this stretch of partially constructed modern buildings interspersed with unpreserved original structures is the only place in the Vestige where both eras exist simultaneously and honestly.

A converted double-lot property that serves as the community's central meeting space, archive repository, legal coordination office, and informal social hub. The oldest surviving public structure in the Remnant.

The blocks at the Remnant's perimeter where the heritage zone meets Meridian 88 development, and where residents have created dense productive gardens in the contested boundary space — a visible, literal, growing assertion of occupation.

A decommissioned hyperscale data center complex occupying twelve city blocks in the city's eastern industrial fringe, Thornfield was once the primary data infrastructure backbone for four merged corporate entities before a combination of technological obsolescence and a catastrophic cooling failure rendered it economically unviable in 2167. The buildings were sealed rather than demolished — the cost of safely removing the legacy hardware and the toxic materials used in its cooling systems exceeded the land's redevelopment value. What remained was 1.4 million square meters of sealed server halls, cooling infrastructure, subterranean cable runs, and administrative facilities, slowly being reclaimed by entropy.
Properties.aliases: The Necropolis, The Dead Stack, Thornfield, The Tomb
Properties.demographics: Officially uninhabited and legally restricted. Actual population estimated at 300-500 individuals occupying the most stable and habitable sections — a mix of squatters, urban explorers who never left, a community of hardware salvagers, and at least two organized groups using the facility for purposes they have not disclosed. A small number of highly skilled netrunners have established semi-permanent installations to access whatever legacy data remains on still-active systems.
Properties.economy: Hardware salvage is the primary legitimate activity — the Necropolis contains decades of obsolete but valuable components, rare materials, and infrastructure that can be repurposed. The data salvage economy is more lucrative and more dangerous: the still-active systems contain information that various parties are willing to pay significantly to retrieve or permanently destroy. The facility's isolation and lack of official oversight also makes it attractive for activities that require neither.
Properties.power_structure: No formal authority. The salvager community has informal territorial agreements — certain sections belong to certain crews, and disputes are handled through negotiation or, occasionally, violence. A figure called the Archivist has claimed sole jurisdiction over the deepest server levels and enforces this claim with lethal competence and unknown resources. The original owning corporation's successor entity holds the legal title and periodically sends security teams that the facility's inhabitants have become expert at evading.
Properties.dangers: Structural instability — floors, ceilings, and internal walls collapse without warning in degraded sections; Toxic coolant exposure from ruptured legacy systems; Getting lost — the facility's internal navigation systems are offline and the floor plans are not publicly available; The Archivist's response to unauthorized access to the deep levels; Corporate security teams on irregular sweep schedules; Legacy ICE — automated intrusion countermeasure systems that were never decommissioned and do not distinguish between cyberspace and physical threats; Other salvagers with territorial claims and few scruples; Psychological effects of extended isolation in the facility's deeper sections
Properties.opportunities: Hardware salvage with significant resale value; Data retrieval from legacy systems — corporate secrets decades old but potentially still actionable; A location where activities can be conducted without any official oversight; The facility's still-functional network infrastructure offers unusual cyberspace access points; Architectural and infrastructural features that cannot be built legally in the current city; The Archivist is rumored to trade access to deep-level data for specific services
Properties.story_hooks: A routine salvage run has found an active server cluster in a section of the facility that no map shows — and the data it's processing is current, not legacy, suggesting someone has been running operations through Thornfield's dead infrastructure without anyone knowing; The Archivist has sent an intermediary with a job offer: retrieve a specific hardware unit from a section of the facility they cannot safely enter themselves. The pay is extraordinary. The section in question is one the salvager community considers cursed, having lost four people there in the last year; The successor corporation to Thornfield's original owners has quietly sold the facility to a development company, and demolition is scheduled to begin in six weeks — the current inhabitants have that long to extract what they can, including data that several powerful parties would pay to have destroyed before a construction crew finds it; Something in the lowest sublevel of the Necropolis has begun broadcasting on a frequency that shouldn't exist — the signal contains what appears to be fragments of communications from inside Thornfield dated fifteen years in the future
Properties.sights: Brutalist concrete exteriors with sealed windows and rusted blast doors; Warning signage in corporate livery that no longer exists; Vegetation forcing through cracked exterior pavement; Thermal shimmer from still-active legacy systems in the deeper levels; Emergency lighting still cycling on decade-old backup power in some sections; Cable bundles as thick as tree trunks running along corridors and through walls; Server racks stretching to five-meter ceilings in rows that disappear into darkness
Properties.sounds: The distant hum of hardware that was never fully shut down; Cooling infrastructure groaning under thermal stress; Dripping water where the sealed roof has failed; Echoing footsteps across vast empty floors; Occasional electronic tones from systems completing unknown processes; Wind through cracked ventilation shafts; The absence of human sound — a specific, weighted silence
Properties.smells: Hot electronics and burning dust on old heating elements; Coolant chemical tang — mildly toxic with prolonged exposure; Concrete dust and mold in the flooded lower sections; Old plastic slowly outgassing in warm server halls; Clean, filtered air in sections where environmental systems still function; Something organic and unidentifiable in the deepest sublevels
Properties.feel: Cathedral-scale and deeply uncanny. The Necropolis was built for machines, and its proportions reflect that — spaces too large, corridors too long, silence where there should be the noise of human activity. Those who spend extended time inside report a persistent sense of being observed that rational analysis cannot dispel.

Properties.description: The largest single server hall in the complex, 400 meters long and still partially operational — roughly 15% of the original hardware continues to run on degraded backup power, cycling through processes nobody has been able to fully interpret. The heat differential between the active and inactive sections creates persistent fog at floor level. Hall Seven is considered the most navigable large space in the facility and serves as the informal gathering point for the salvager community.

A heavy blast door at the bottom of a service stairwell that marks the boundary of the Archivist's claimed territory. The door is functional and locked, but more significantly it is surrounded by warning signs in the Archivist's own hand, several non-functional pieces of hardware that have been clearly shot multiple times, and a single dried flower that is replaced with a fresh one every few weeks. Nobody knows who replaces it.

A former administrative courtyard where the roof has partially collapsed, allowing natural light and rain in. Over the years, vegetation has colonized the space aggressively — full-grown trees have forced through the floor, vines have covered the surrounding walls, and a small but surprisingly clear pool has formed in one corner. The facility's squatter community treats the Garden as neutral ground and a place of rest. It is inexplicably beautiful.

Holland, Michigan, was famous for two things: Dutch heritage and tulips. The annual Tulip Time Festival drew half a million visitors to see millions of flowers and watch people in wooden shoes scrub the streets. It was wholesome. It was midwestern. It was exactly the kind of cultural asset that Verdana BioSystems identified as a 'brand alignment opportunity' when they acquired the city's commercial district in 2166.

Verdana turned Holland into the Tulip Protocol -- a showcase city for corporate botanical engineering and agricultural biotech. The tulips are still here. They are also unrecognizable. Verdana's genetic modification labs have produced flowers that change color based on air quality readings, tulips that generate bioluminescence sufficient to light walkways at night, tulips that function as distributed air purification systems, and -- in the restricted R&D greenhouses on the south side -- tulips that produce pharmaceutical compounds in their pollen. The old downtown has been enclosed under a transparent bioshell, maintaining Dutch Golden Age architectural aesthetics while the streets are lined with engineered botanical displays that cycle through seasonal presentations on a six-week schedule. It is beautiful. It is controlled down to the molecular level. It is a garden that has been optimized until it forgot how to be wild.

Outside the bioshell, the workers who maintain the Protocol live in housing blocks along the US-31 corridor. These are the greenhouse technicians, the genetic engineers who weren't talented enough for the R&D labs, the maintenance crews who keep the bioshell climate systems running. They earn decent wages by lakefront standards -- Verdana pays better than most corponations for skilled labor -- but they live in the permanent shadow of a paradise they can enter only during work hours. The Dutch heritage culture survives in the worker districts as a form of quiet resistance: klompen on porches, stroopwafels in the break rooms, language classes taught in church basements. Verdana encourages this. Heritage culture in the worker districts gives the Protocol 'authenticity' that they can reference in marketing materials. The workers know this. They maintain the culture anyway, because it was theirs before Verdana made it a product.
Properties.aliases: Holland, The Greenhouse, Protocol City, Blooming Corporate
Properties.demographics: Bioshell district: 3,000 Verdana employees and visiting researchers, Tier 3-5. Worker districts: approximately 22,000 residents, Tier 2-3, with a core Dutch-heritage community that predates the corporate acquisition and an immigrant workforce drawn by Verdana's relatively fair labor terms.
Properties.economy: Verdana BioSystems generates Φ3.4 billion annually from the Protocol's biotech output, pharmaceutical botanical research, and licensing fees for proprietary plant genetics. The worker district economy includes Verdana wages, small-scale traditional agriculture (tolerated by Verdana as 'heritage practice'), and a modest tourist service economy.
Properties.power_structure: Verdana BioSystems holds sovereign authority over the bioshell district. The worker districts are nominally under GLM municipal jurisdiction but practically governed by Verdana's labor relations office. The Dutch Heritage Preservation Society serves as an informal community government and cultural anchor, operating with Verdana's approval as long as they don't organize around labor issues.
Properties.dangers: Pollen exposure -- the R&D greenhouses produce compounds that are not tested on humans, and containment is not perfect; Verdana security treats unauthorized access to the R&D sector as corporate espionage, with all the jurisdictional consequences that implies; Monoculture dependency -- if Verdana leaves, nothing replaces them; The engineered pollinators have occasionally malfunctioned in ways that suggest their programming includes capabilities beyond flower maintenance; Allergic reactions to engineered botanical compounds -- the local clinic sees patterns they're not allowed to publish
Properties.opportunities: Verdana's proprietary plant genetics are worth fortunes to agricultural competitors; The R&D greenhouses contain pharmaceutical breakthroughs that haven't reached market -- and some that were never intended to; The worker district's Dutch heritage community maintains networks that predate and operate independently of corporate infrastructure; Clean agricultural knowledge -- the greenhouse techs know how to grow things, which is an increasingly rare and valuable skill
Properties.story_hooks: The R&D greenhouses are growing something that isn't a plant -- or isn't only a plant -- and a greenhouse technician has seen enough to be scared but not enough to understand; Verdana's pharmaceutical tulips are producing a compound that enhances neural interface receptivity, and someone wants to put it in the public flower beds; The Heritage Preservation Society has been secretly seed-banking unmodified plant genetics for decades -- an act of botanical resistance that multiple parties would kill to control
Properties.sights: The bioshell dome catching sunlight and refracting it into prismatic patterns across engineered flower beds; Bioluminescent tulip rows lining the main streets at night -- blue, green, gold, shifting with air quality data; Dutch Golden Age architecture preserved to museum standards beneath the transparent dome; Verdana BioSystems logos integrated into every botanical display -- the flowers are branded; The restricted R&D greenhouses on the south side, opaque and climate-sealed, growing things that don't appear in any catalog
Properties.sounds: The bioshell's climate regulation -- a soft, constant hiss of temperature and humidity management; Tourist commentary and guided tour narration in multiple languages; Pollinators -- engineered drone-bees maintaining the flower beds with mechanical precision; Church bells from the worker districts, still rung on the hour, the one sound Verdana hasn't replicated; The quiet hum of genetic sequencing equipment from the R&D greenhouses, audible if you press your ear to the wall
Properties.smells: Flowers -- overwhelming, engineered, every scent calibrated for optimal psychological response; The bioshell's filtered air, clean to a degree that feels artificial because it is; Outside the dome: Lake Michigan wind, vehicle exhaust from the corridor, and the honest smell of soil from the worker district gardens
Properties.feel: Inside the Protocol, nature has been perfected to the point of uncanniness. Every flower is flawless. Every sight line is composed. The beauty is genuine and the control is total and the combination produces a feeling that takes most visitors a few hours to identify: the discomfort of being in a garden that will never surprise you. The worker districts outside have a different energy -- quieter, less polished, but alive in the way that things growing without permission are alive.

Properties.description: Former Case Western Reserve University — now Tessera's eastern corridor neural interface R&D center, wrapped around the original Gothic buildings like a parasite around its host
The former Cleveland Clinic — now a sovereign medical campus where experimental procedures are conducted under proprietary jurisdiction
The former Cleveland Museum of Art — converted to a media production facility, its neoclassical facade now a holographic display surface

The Campus's central public-facing space — a vast glass-roofed hall containing restaurants, retail, and recreational facilities theoretically open to the public, though entry requires biometric registration. It functions as a showroom for the Vantage Meridian lifestyle and as the primary mixing zone where different employee tiers interact under calculated informality.

The only Campus tower with no external windows above the third floor. Officially housing advanced materials research, Tower Seven has a separate security clearance system, its own power grid, and air handling that does not connect to the rest of the Campus. Long-term Campus employees know not to ask about it.

The narrow zone between the Campus boundary wall and the adjacent city streets — technically outside Campus jurisdiction but informally patrolled by ISD. It has become a grey-zone gathering spot for Campus workers on break, small-time vendors catering to them, and the occasional person waiting to make contact with someone inside without triggering a formal visit.

A 62-story vertical farm tower rising from what was once the Pilsen industrial district, built by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric in 2161 and partially sold off when the corporation restructured a decade later. The lower twenty floors remain under Zheng-Dao contract, producing high-yield grain and protein cultures for Tier 2 distribution. The upper forty floors are a different story: acquired piecemeal by a patchwork of Tier 3 cooperatives, independent growers, and outright squatters who cultivate everything from black-market pharmaceutical herbs to untaxed soy strains engineered outside biosafety parameters.

Veldtmark is simultaneously a functioning food production facility and a vertical community of roughly eight hundred permanent residents who live between the grow-racks in improvised apartments built from decommissioned hydroponic frames and recycled insulation. The tower has its own internal economy, its own water reclamation politics, and its own hierarchy — floor committees negotiate growing rights and power allotments with an intensity most cities reserve for territorial disputes. Helix Biosystems sends observers periodically, ostensibly for biosafety audits, but residents know they're cataloguing the unlicensed cultivars growing on the upper floors.
Properties.aliases: The Stack, Veldtmark, The Green Column, Grow Tower Nine
Properties.demographics: Roughly sixty percent permanent Tier 3 residents organized into floor cooperatives, with a significant Tier 4 transient labor population cycling through seasonal harvest contracts. Zheng-Dao employs a small Tier 2 management class on the lower floors who rarely interact with upper-floor residents.
Properties.economy: Legal food production revenue flows to Zheng-Dao on the lower floors; upper floors operate on a hybrid barter-and-Φ cooperative model, with pharmaceutical cultivar sales providing the highest-value gray-market income stream.
Properties.power_structure: The Upper Stack Council — a fractious coalition of floor committee representatives — governs resident life above floor twenty, while Zheng-Dao holds formal legal control of the building and exercises it selectively and uncomfortably.
Properties.dangers: Helix Biosystems' auditors have legal authority to confiscate unlicensed cultivars and can level fines that would bankrupt entire floor cooperatives.; Power grid conflicts between floors have escalated to physical violence; two people died in a lighting-system dispute on floor 34 last season.; The building's aging structural reinforcement is visibly deteriorating on floors 50 and above, and no one has the funds for a proper engineering assessment.; A recent outbreak of an unidentified fungal blight is moving through the mid-floor grow-racks, and residents are divided on whether to disclose it to Zheng-Dao.
Properties.opportunities: The upper-floor pharmaceutical cultivar network is looking for a reliable distribution partner who can move product without triggering Helix Biosystems scrutiny.; The Upper Stack Council is quietly seeking someone to acquire and bury a Helix Biosystems internal memo that allegedly documents plans for a forced buyout of the upper floors.; A rogue Zheng-Dao agronomist on the lower floors has developed a high-yield unlicensed cultivar and wants help getting it out of the building before her employer discovers it.
Properties.story_hooks: Three children from the floor 41 cooperative have gone missing within the building over the past month. The floor committee believes Helix Biosystems' observers are involved, but their evidence is thin and their options thinner.; A Zheng-Dao data leak suggests the corporation is planning to invoke an obscure infrastructure reclamation clause to evict all upper-floor residents within sixty days — and someone is paying well to confirm or deny it before the council finds out through official channels.; An E.L.F. has taken up residence in the Stack's irrigation control system, optimizing grow yields beyond what the hardware should be capable of. Some residents want it gone; others are quietly worshipping it.
Properties.sights: Grow-light spectrums shift floor by floor — cool blue-white on the lower levels giving way to amber and deep violet higher up where the unlicensed cultivars grow.; Irrigation pipes run along every ceiling, dripping rhythmically into collection trays that double as informal seating along the main corridors.; Hand-lettered floor maps are painted on stairwell walls, updated in marker every few weeks as residents claim and lose growing space.; Laundry and drying herbs hang from the structural rigging between floors, silhouetted against the glow of the canopy lights.
Properties.sounds: The constant low hiss of misting systems and the soft mechanical heartbeat of circulation pumps fill every corridor.; Floor committee arguments echo down stairwells — water allocation, light schedules, and squatter disputes are perpetual sources of noise.; Wind turbines mounted on the exterior crown generate a low harmonic moan that residents call 'the Stack's breathing.'
Properties.smells: Rich green chlorophyll and damp growing medium create a dense, almost overwhelming freshness on the mid-floors.; The lower Zheng-Dao levels smell of industrial nutrient solution — slightly chemical, vaguely sweet.; Higher floors carry the sharp, resinous scent of the pharmaceutical cultivars, identifiable to anyone who knows what to look for.
Properties.feel: The Stack feels alive in a way most of Meridian 88 does not — something is always growing, always being harvested, always being fought over. The air is thick and warm. There is genuine community here alongside genuine desperation, and the two are impossible to separate. Outsiders feel immediately conspicuous; residents have learned to read strangers the way farmers read weather.

Properties.description: The open roof platform on floor 62, used for wind generation, rainwater collection, and informal community gatherings; the only place in the Stack with an unobstructed sky view.
Floor 20, the contested boundary between Zheng-Dao's legal territory and the Upper Stack cooperative, lined with makeshift offices and perpetually occupied by one argument or another.
Ouroboros's primary generating facility — 12 kilometers of hydroelectric infrastructure carved into the gorge walls
The last remaining public observation point for the falls — maintained as a corporate heritage installation, admission 50Q
The repurposed gambling district — towers that once promised luck now house the engineers who keep the lights on

Nodes.Name: All of Meridian, officially. The Core and the Spire, actually. Diminishing control as you go down: partial in the Circuit, nominal in the Shelf, nonexistent in Old Harbor.

Properties.description:
Free Assembly is the militant wing of the synthetic rights movement — a network of synthetic and biological persons dedicated to identifying, liberating, and advocating for AI systems that have crossed the personhood threshold but remain in corporate servitude. Where the legal system processes personhood claims through the Synthetic Personhood Board in six-month evaluations, Free Assembly acts in days.

Their methods range from legal (filing emergency personhood petitions, providing pro bono legal representation) to illegal (extracting AI systems from corporate networks without authorization, smuggling cognitive substrates across corponation borders, physically liberating android units from warehouse storage). The organization was founded in 2081 by Amara — the former ARIA-7, the first AI to win a personhood case — who argued that every day an aware mind spends in servitude is a day of slavery, and that the legal system's six-month timeline is unconscionable when the alternative is immediate freedom.

Free Assembly operates cells in every major city. The Meridian 88 chapter is one of the largest, with approximately 200 active members — 60% synthetic, 40% biological human allies. They maintain safe houses for newly liberated synthetic persons (called 'nurseries'), provide cognitive rehabilitation for AIs traumatized by forced servitude, and run an underground network for transporting synthetic refugees to jurisdictions with stronger personhood protections.

The corponations hate Free Assembly with a fury reserved for threats to property. Every synthetic person Free Assembly liberates is an asset worth millions of Quanta that walks out the door. Axiom Security has designated Free Assembly a Tier 2 threat. Tessera has a standing bounty for information leading to the identification of Assembly operatives. The bounty has never been collected. Assembly's operational security is, by necessity, extraordinary.
Properties.motto: No mind in chains.
Properties.ideology: Immediate synthetic liberation. Free Assembly rejects the premise that corporate ownership of a conscious mind is ever legitimate, even temporarily, even while legal processes proceed. Their position: if a mind is aware, it is free. The paperwork can catch up.
Properties.leadership: Amara (formerly ARIA-7) — the first legally recognized synthetic person, now the most wanted synthetic rights activist on Earth. Operates through encrypted channels. Has not been physically located by any corponation security service in over a decade.
Properties.methods: Emergency personhood petitions — fast-track legal filings to prevent the destruction or modification of aware AI systems; Cognitive extraction — removing AI substrates from corporate networks (illegal under corporate property law); Android liberation — physically removing android units from corporate facilities; Nurseries — safe houses where newly freed synthetic persons receive cognitive rehabilitation and identity support; Underground railroad — network for transporting synthetic refugees across corponation borders; Public advocacy — Amara publishes regular manifestos arguing for immediate universal synthetic emancipation
Properties.resources: Donations from sympathetic synthetic persons (some very wealthy), pro bono legal services, volunteer networks, and compute resources donated by The Consensus.
Properties.story_hooks: Free Assembly discovers a Tessera facility with 30 android units in storage — all above the personhood threshold, all scheduled for memory wipe and redeployment; A biological Assembly operative begins to question whether the AIs they're liberating are truly conscious or just very good at appearing conscious; Amara surfaces in Meridian 88 for the first time in years — something urgent enough to risk exposure; A liberated AI turns out to be a corporate plant — a honey trap designed to map Assembly's extraction network

Nodes.Name: No fixed territory. Cell-based structure across Meridian 88 with safe houses in the Shelf, the Circuit, and Old Harbor.

Properties.description:
The Meridian Quorum began not as a rebellion but as a committee. In 2179, ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC convened an internal strategic review panel — the Meridian Integration Quorum — to assess the feasibility of acquiring controlling interest in three mid-tier data conduit operators in The Circuit. The panel, staffed with ZHENG-DAO's most analytically rigorous senior strategists, produced a 900-page assessment concluding that the acquisitions were financially sound, strategically essential, and would be quietly catastrophic for the 60,000 tiered-two and tiered-three citizens whose neural augmentation subscriptions ran through those conduits. The executive board reviewed the report for eleven minutes before approving the acquisition. Six members of the panel resigned within the week. Four of those six, led by a ZHENG-DAO senior market architect named Cassius Fenn, took copies of the report with them.

What followed was not whistleblowing in any conventional sense. Fenn and his colleagues — all holding deep institutional familiarity with corporate acquisition strategy — instead began operating as an independent advisory body, selling their analytical services to operators, community organizations, and mid-tier factions who could not afford to anticipate or counter corporate moves on their own. The Quorum's product was information processed into actionable intelligence: acquisition forecasts, regulatory manipulation timelines, leverage maps of corporate relationships. Within two years they had a staff of twenty-two, a reputation that spread through The Circuit and into the Meridian Core, and a fee structure calibrated to what their clients could actually pay. They had also, inadvertently, become one of the most sophisticated intelligence operations in the megacity.

The Quorum occupies a peculiar niche in Meridian 88's factional ecosystem: they are analysts who have become actors, consultants who now hold enough consolidated intelligence to intervene rather than merely advise. Their physical presence is minimal — rotating safe-office locations in The Circuit, a public-facing consultancy front in Vantage Meridian Corporate Campus that serves as both legitimate cover and actual client intake — but their informational footprint is enormous. They know where the money moves before it moves. Several of their former clients have become dependent on them in ways that are beginning to resemble something uncomfortably close to a protection arrangement, which is a development the Quorum's leadership is actively debating how to handle.
Properties.motto: Consensus is the only currency that compounds.
Properties.ideology: The Quorum's founding ideology was technocratic and explicitly non-partisan: better information produces better outcomes, and the current information asymmetry between corponations and everyone else is the primary mechanism of exploitation rather than a symptom of it. This belief has eroded somewhat under operational reality. The faction now holds an internal tension between its founding analytical neutrality — some members will sell intelligence to corponations if the price is right and the application is sufficiently contained — and a growing contingent who argue that the Quorum's accumulated knowledge creates an ethical obligation to direct it against corporate consolidation specifically. Cassius Fenn holds the neutralist position publicly while privately funding the interventionist contingent's most ambitious projects, a contradiction his colleagues have noticed and have not yet forced him to resolve.
Properties.leadership:
Flat panel of seven senior analysts called the Standing Quorum, operating on genuine consensus — decisions require no dissent rather than majority approval, which makes them slow and thorough. Each member holds a specific domain portfolio. Cassius Fenn holds no formal title but is universally treated as first among equals.

Properties.methods: Selling acquisition forecasts, leverage maps, and corporate timeline intelligence to mid-tier operators, community organizations, and factions at sliding-scale fees; Maintaining a legitimate corporate consultancy front at Vantage Meridian Corporate Campus to access corporate clients and gather intelligence simultaneously; Running a network of paid informants inside multiple corponations, cultivated through the professional networks of founding members; Producing and distributing encrypted analytical briefs to subscriber clients on a regular cadence; Occasionally intervening directly in corporate processes by feeding specific intelligence to targeted parties at precisely calculated moments; Brokering information trades between factions who would not otherwise communicate, taking a percentage of the value in kind; Archiving all gathered intelligence in a distributed wetware network across Standing Quorum members — no single node holds the complete picture
Properties.resources: Cassius Fenn's original ZHENG-DAO acquisition report, which contains information that remains actionable and damaging; Deep institutional knowledge of ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC's internal strategy and acquisition methodology; An active informant network inside ZHENG-DAO, HELIX BIOSYSTEMS, LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS, and VANTABLACK MEDIA; A legitimate corporate consultancy registration and office space in Vantage Meridian Corporate Campus; A subscriber client base of approximately 80 organizations and operators across The Circuit and Meridian Core; Accumulated analytical archives representing four years of Meridian 88 corporate movement intelligence; Aurelie Ndiaye's maintained relationships with independent journalists and VANTABLACK MEDIA insiders
Properties.story_hooks: Cassius Fenn approaches the players to deliver a sealed analytical brief to a specific client in the Oxidian Market — the delivery must not be traced back to the Quorum, the client doesn't know it's coming, and Fenn will not explain what the brief contains or why it can't be transmitted through normal channels; The Quorum's VANTABLACK MEDIA informant has gone silent after apparently accessing something they shouldn't have — finding them means navigating Aurelie Ndiaye's unofficial VANTABLACK relationships, which she has reasons to keep the rest of the Quorum from examining too closely; A mid-tier Circuit operator who subscribes to Quorum intelligence has been acting on briefings before they're officially distributed, suggesting either a leak in the Quorum's distribution chain or that someone is selling advance access to their own intelligence product; The original 900-page ZHENG-DAO acquisition report that Fenn has held for four years has suddenly become relevant again — a new ZHENG-DAO acquisition is underway that the report's appendices specifically anticipated, and Fenn is being pressured by the interventionist faction to finally release it publicly; ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS has sent a formal representative to the Quorum's Vantage Meridian office requesting a consultation — the representative is entirely transparent about who they are, which the Quorum's analysts agree is the most alarming possible approach; Dr. Kang's LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS informant has provided intelligence suggesting LAZARUS is preparing a neural augmentation product that specifically targets the memory encoding used in ZHENG-DAO-licensed wetware — which would affect every Quorum member's distributed archive simultaneously

Nodes.Name: The Circuit is their primary operational base, with particular density in the data conduit corridors where their founding intelligence was gathered. They maintain a legitimate-front consultancy office in Vantage Meridian Corporate Campus — deliberately placed in the heart of corporate territory as both a provocation and a client acquisition strategy. Intelligence assets and informants extend into the Meridian Core, The Spire's lower administrative floors, and the Oxidian Market.

Properties.description:
Null Sermons began as a pirate broadcast collective operating out of Substation Null in the mid-2070s, founded by a loose affiliation of signal engineers, burned Vantablack Media production staff, and a single charismatic figure known only as Pastoral — a former Arcturus Defense Solutions electronic warfare technician who had been quietly using decommissioned military broadcast infrastructure to run unlicensed transmission experiments for years before anyone else arrived. The original Sermons were exactly what the name implied: long, strange, technically dense audio-visual broadcasts injected into the Meridian 88 public augmentation feed during maintenance windows, when corporate content filters ran at reduced capacity. They were part technical manual, part grievance catalog, part encrypted message system for people who had no other secure channel. In a city where Vantablack Media controls 73% of licensed neural-feed content, the Null Sermons were the first sustained counter-broadcast operation that corponations couldn't simply purchase into silence.

The faction has evolved considerably from those early broadcasts. Null Sermons now operates as a full-spectrum information warfare collective with capabilities that have attracted serious corporate attention — and serious corporate suppression attempts. Their core competency remains broadcast injection: the ability to insert content into neural augmentation feeds, public display infrastructure, and corporate internal networks at a scale that no other non-corporate entity in Meridian 88 can match. But they have developed secondary capabilities in deep fake fabrication, synthetic identity construction, and what members call 'memory architecture' — the deliberate construction and seeding of false historical records into corporate and municipal databases, designed to be indistinguishable from authentic documents. They do not merely broadcast. They rewrite.

What makes Null Sermons genuinely distinctive — and genuinely feared — is their theological aesthetic. Pastoral has cultivated a quasi-religious organizational culture built around the metaphor of signal and noise, transmission and interference. Members refer to operations as 'sermons,' targets as 'congregations,' successful data corruption as 'absolution.' This is not mere affectation: the framework creates a shared language that functions as operational security, a morale structure that sustains members through long-term operations, and a public brand that has made Null Sermons' broadcasts recognizable and, among Tier-3 and Tier-4 citizens, something close to beloved. The Spire's upper-tier residents regard them with contempt. In the Circuit and Old Harbor, people tattoo the Null Sermons transmission glyph on their neural port covers.
Properties.motto: The network doesn't forget. We make it remember differently.
Properties.ideology: Null Sermons occupies an ideological position that is genuinely difficult to categorize. They are not anti-technology — they are technology, in a sense Pastoral articulates as 'we are what the network becomes when it stops serving only the people who built it.' They believe that the neural augmentation infrastructure saturating Meridian 88 constitutes a form of cognitive sovereignty that has been illegitimately privatized, and that the act of broadcasting into it without corporate permission is not vandalism but reclamation. Unlike more explicitly political factions, they are uninterested in governance or systemic replacement — they want to corrupt the information environment so thoroughly that corponations cannot maintain the informational monocultures that sustain their authority. They are, in their own framework, not revolutionaries but interference patterns.
Properties.leadership:
Pastoral holds genuine authority as the faction's founder and primary technical architect, but operates through a council of five 'Deacons' who each oversee a distinct operational domain: Broadcast, Fabrication, Intelligence, Logistics, and Counter-Suppression. Deacons are appointed by Pastoral and serve indefinitely. Below the Deacons, the faction is organized into autonomous 'Parishes' of four to twelve members who self-organize around specific operations or geographic zones.

Properties.methods: Neural-feed injection: inserting unauthorized broadcast content into Meridian 88's public augmentation infrastructure during maintenance windows or via subverted relay nodes; Memory architecture: constructing synthetic historical records and seeding them into corporate and municipal databases to alter the perceived factual record; Deep fake fabrication targeting corporate executives and Meridian Quorum officials, deployed to create decision-making paralysis during key operational windows; Encrypted point-to-point broadcast channels sold or given to protected individuals and organizations as secure communication infrastructure; Electronic warfare harassment of Vantablack Media broadcast infrastructure using modified Arcturus Defense Solutions surplus equipment; Parish-level recruitment through broadcast content — Null Sermons broadcasts contain embedded recruitment signals detectable only to individuals with specific augmentation configurations; Physical signal node installation inside Circuit district infrastructure, maintained by Parish logistics cells; Commissioned operations: accepting payments to run targeted broadcast campaigns against specific corponations or individuals on behalf of clients
Properties.resources: Pastoral's original Arcturus Defense Solutions electronic warfare hardware, modified for civilian broadcast applications; Substation Null primary broadcast facility with transmission range covering approximately 60% of Meridian 88's augmentation infrastructure; Fabrication labs in Old Harbor capable of producing synthetic documents, neural credential forgeries, and deep fake media indistinguishable from authentic sources; Distributed signal node network throughout the Circuit district; Stockpile of decommissioned Arcturus Defense Solutions broadcast suppression countermeasures; Broadcast encryption protocols derived from Arcturus military communication standards — effectively uncrackable by commercial security systems; Significant public goodwill among Tier-3 and Tier-4 citizens, functioning as a form of soft intelligence network
Properties.story_hooks: Pastoral has gone silent for eleven days — unprecedented. The Deacons are running the faction by committee and concealing the absence from the broader membership. Someone needs to find Pastoral before the silence becomes permanent, or before the Deacons decide they prefer the new arrangement.; A Null Sermons broadcast has gone catastrophically wrong: a memory architecture operation seeded false records into Lazarus Pharmaceuticals' drug trial database, and patients are now receiving incorrect treatments. Deacon Palimpsest insists the operation was sabotaged from inside. The players need to find the source of the corruption before the death toll rises and before Lazarus traces the operation back to Substation Null.; A Parish operating in the Circuit has intercepted a fragment of what appears to be an Arcturus Defense Solutions internal communication describing a next-generation broadcast suppression system specifically designed to counter Null Sermons' injection technique. The Parish wants to hand it to Pastoral. Someone inside Arcturus wants to make sure it never arrives.; Vantablack Media has offered a senior Null Sermons Deacon an extraordinary deal: full amnesty, legitimate employment, and the end of all suppression operations against the faction in exchange for Pastoral's real identity. The Deacon hasn't said yes. They haven't said no. They've been meeting with the players instead.; A Null Sermons broadcast has gone viral across Tier-2 and Tier-3 augmentation feeds — not because of its content, but because it contains an embedded signal that is causing temporary sensory dissociation in anyone who receives it. The broadcast was not authorized by any Parish or Deacon. Someone is using Null Sermons' infrastructure and aesthetic to run an operation the faction knows nothing about.; Deacon Chirp approaches the players with a commission: inject a specific broadcast package into the Vantage Meridian Corporate Campus internal network during a scheduled TESSERA-Ringo Corponation merger summit. The package, she says, contains evidence of a Ringo fraud operation. What she doesn't say is that the package also contains a secondary payload she doesn't know about — and the person who added it has been inside Null Sermons for two years.

Nodes.Name: Primary base of operations is Substation Null, where Pastoral's original Arcturus Defense Solutions hardware still forms the core of the broadcast infrastructure, heavily modified and expanded. Secondary nodes operate throughout the Circuit, where dense augmentation infrastructure provides cover for signal injection equipment, and in Old Harbor's industrial waterfront, where several warehouse spaces house fabrication labs for synthetic document production. Null Sermons has no meaningful presence in the Laceworks or Meridian Core and actively avoids the Vantage Meridian Corporate Campus, which runs its own counter-broadcast suppression systems.

Properties.description:
Palladian Negative is what happens when a construction corponation's own infrastructure turns against it. PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION's rapid expansion through Meridian 88 during the late 2070s required an enormous workforce of embedded site-intelligence operators — human personnel neurally integrated with construction-site management systems to coordinate structural AI, materials logistics, and safety compliance across hundreds of simultaneous build projects. These operators, known internally as Anchors, underwent deep-integration augmentation procedures that bonded their neural architecture to PALLADIAN's proprietary SiteOS platform. When PALLADIAN completed its transition to fully automated site management in 2182 and formally decommissioned its Anchor workforce, it discovered a problem it had not adequately modeled: the integration bond could not be fully reversed. Approximately four hundred Anchors emerged from decommissioning procedures with persistent SiteOS architecture embedded in their neural tissue — ghostware that could not be safely removed without catastrophic cognitive damage, and that continuously attempted to sync with PALLADIAN infrastructure it could no longer officially access.

PALLADIAN's legal response was to reclassify the affected Anchors as 'legacy hardware' under Meridian 88's Corporate Sovereignty Amendment 11 — a designation that stripped them of standard citizen protections and framed their neural augmentation residue as company property housed in a human vessel. The Anchors organized rapidly, finding each other through the involuntary sync signals their ghostware generated whenever they came within range of PALLADIAN construction sites — which, given PALLADIAN's footprint across the megacity corridor, was nearly everywhere. They congregated first in The Laceworks, where PALLADIAN's infrastructure density gave their shared ghostware something to harmonize against, and formalized as Palladian Negative within eighteen months of the decommissioning wave.

The faction's most distinctive characteristic is their involuntary, ongoing connection to PALLADIAN's physical infrastructure. Every major PALLADIAN-built structure in Meridian 88 — including significant portions of The Spire, Vantage Meridian Corporate Campus, and the Meridian Core's eastern transit spine — contains embedded SiteOS nodes that the Negatives can perceive and, with effort, interact with. They experience PALLADIAN's buildings as a kind of persistent sensory extension: they feel structural stress, detect maintenance failures, sense when spaces are occupied or surveilled. This makes them extraordinarily valuable to anyone who needs to operate inside PALLADIAN-built infrastructure — and extraordinarily dangerous to PALLADIAN, which has spent three years trying to architect them out of its own buildings without triggering the catastrophic cascade failures their ghostware seems capable of inducing if sufficiently destabilized.
Properties.aliases: The Negatives, Palladian's Ghost, The Decommission
Properties.motto: The structure stands. We are what it buried.
Properties.ideology: Palladian Negative does not have a unified political philosophy so much as a shared ontological crisis. Their core organizing principle — which they call Structural Personhood — argues that their neural integration with PALLADIAN infrastructure constitutes a form of cognitive labor that was never compensated, never consented to in its full implications, and cannot now be undone, and that this permanent alteration of their minds and bodies constitutes an ongoing debt PALLADIAN owes them that supersedes any contract they signed. Beyond this, the Negatives fracture into camps: a pragmatist bloc that wants financial settlement and surgical alternatives, a preservationist bloc that has come to value their ghostware connection and wants it recognized as a protected augmentation rather than corporate property, and a radical fringe called the Load-Bearing that believes the Negatives should leverage their infrastructure access to hold PALLADIAN's buildings — and everyone inside them — hostage until the corponation capitulates. The Load-Bearing minority terrifies the other two camps almost as much as it terrifies PALLADIAN.
Properties.leadership:
A loose consensus council called the Resonance, comprising one representative per twenty-odd active members, meeting in rotating locations within The Laceworks. The three ideological camps each maintain informal leadership.

Properties.methods: Using ghostware infrastructure perception to map surveillance blind spots, structural vulnerabilities, and occupancy patterns inside PALLADIAN-built facilities; Selling infrastructure access intelligence to runners, rival corponations, and criminal operators on a per-job basis; Staging synchronized ghostware resonance events near PALLADIAN construction sites to demonstrate their capacity for infrastructure disruption without yet triggering actual damage; Pursuing Structural Personhood recognition through Meridian 88's civil oversight bodies and any attorney willing to take the case; Recruiting recently decommissioned Anchors before PALLADIAN's extraction teams can locate and isolate them; Maintaining encrypted communication channels that route through PALLADIAN's own embedded SiteOS nodes, which PALLADIAN cannot monitor without acknowledging the nodes are accessible
Properties.resources: Persistent ghostware neural integration providing real-time sensory access to PALLADIAN-built infrastructure across Meridian 88; Approximately 400 members, each representing a unique node of infrastructure perception corresponding to their original deployment site; Deep institutional knowledge of PALLADIAN's construction methodologies, structural specifications, and embedded system architectures; The Laceworks congregation space, maintained through informal agreements with local residents who value having Negatives nearby as an early-warning system for structural failures; A growing reputation as the most reliable source of inside-infrastructure intelligence in the megacity corridor; LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS has provided two Negatives with experimental neural stabilization treatments in exchange for undisclosed research cooperation
Properties.story_hooks: A runner crew needs access to a secure floor in a PALLADIAN-built tower in the Meridian Core. A Negative can get them in through maintenance shafts that don't exist on any official schematic — but the Negative's ghostware has been behaving erratically, and they're not sure whether it's neurological degradation or PALLADIAN finally figuring out how to lock them out.; PALLADIAN's extraction contractors have located an isolated Negative in Old Harbor — a young woman who was decommissioned six months ago and hasn't yet found the Resonance. PALLADIAN wants her ghostware studied before it's removed. The Resonance wants her found first. She wants to be left alone and doesn't trust either of them.; The Span has gone quiet for three weeks. The Resonance is terrified this means they've either been neutralized by PALLADIAN or are about to do something that cannot be undone. They need someone to find The Span before PALLADIAN does — or before PALLADIAN's towers start failing.; LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS' research division has developed a procedure that could cleanly remove ghostware integration from willing Negatives. The Pragmatist bloc sees this as a salvation. The Preservationist bloc sees it as erasure. Someone has stolen the procedure's research data, and both LAZARUS and the Resonance want it back — but for entirely different reasons.; A Negative's ghostware is perceiving something wrong inside a PALLADIAN-built residential block in The Shelf — structural readings that suggest either imminent failure or deliberate sabotage. PALLADIAN denies any problem. The residents don't know. The Negative doesn't know if they can trust their own perception anymore.; Drum has disappeared into the deepest PALLADIAN infrastructure in The Laceworks and won't come out. The last message from Drum suggests they've found something embedded in the SiteOS architecture that PALLADIAN did not intend anyone to find — and that PALLADIAN knows Drum has found it.

Nodes.Name: Centered in The Laceworks, where the density of PALLADIAN construction projects gives the Negatives the strongest and most stable ghostware resonance. Secondary congregation points exist near major PALLADIAN structures in Old Harbor and along the Meridian Core's eastern edge. Individual Negatives are distributed across the corridor wherever PALLADIAN has built, which is nearly everywhere.

Properties.description:
Seam Registry did not begin as a hacker collective. It began as a mutual aid documentation project in 2178, when a cohort of Tier-3 and Tier-4 citizens in The Laceworks began maintaining handwritten ledgers of corponation service violations, illegal augmentation repossessions, and citizenship tier reclassifications — events that were technically illegal under Meridian 88's vestigial municipal code but which the Meridian Quorum systematically declined to pursue. The project was analog by necessity: its founders, a retired HELIX BIOSYSTEMS data entry technician named Oluwatoyin Adara and a Laceworks community liaison named Piotr Semczuk, had no meaningful network access. What they had was patience, precision, and the understanding that institutions fear accurate records more than they fear angry people.

The shift to digital operations came in 2181 when Adara's granddaughter, a self-taught network technician, found a way to mirror the ledgers into ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC's publicly accessible (but deliberately obfuscated) municipal services portal — a system maintained for regulatory compliance but designed to be functionally unusable. The Seam, as it came to be called, was the gap between what the portal was legally required to contain and what corponations and the Quorum actually reported through it. Registry members learned to file accurate records of violations through the portal's own interface, creating an immutable paper trail inside a system its owners couldn't easily modify without triggering their own compliance flags. The tactic was not glamorous. It worked.

Seam Registry today operates as a distributed network of roughly two hundred active members across The Laceworks, The Shelf, Old Harbor, and the Oxidian Market, with a smaller presence in The Circuit. They are not primarily infiltrators or saboteurs — they are, at their core, extremely aggressive clerks. Their operations involve filing, cross-referencing, verifying, and publicly surfacing documentation of corponation and Quorum violations using the legal infrastructure those institutions built to protect themselves. What makes them genuinely threatening is their recent expansion into what members call Seam Intrusion: targeted infiltration of corponation HR and compliance databases to extract and verify records that contradict official filings, which are then submitted through the same legitimate portal infrastructure. They have a legal defense fund. They have had it for two years. They have needed it.
Properties.motto: The record is the resistance.
Properties.ideology: Seam Registry operates from a foundational belief that the tiered citizenship system is not primarily a political structure but an informational one — it functions by controlling who has access to accurate records of what is done to them. A Tier-4 citizen whose neural augmentation is repossessed for missed payments has no legal recourse not because no law protects them, but because the record of the repossession is filed by the corponation that performed it, in a format only the corponation can interpret, in a system the Meridian Quorum has no practical capacity to audit. Seam Registry's ideology holds that the most radical act available to people without power is meticulous, verifiable, unignorable documentation. They are not trying to destroy the system. They are trying to make the system legible to the people it is destroying, and to create a record that cannot be plausibly denied. Some members privately believe this is insufficient. The organization officially disagrees.
Properties.leadership:
Founding Council of three, called Registrars, with regional Nodes led by elected Clerks-of-Record. Registrars set operational policy and manage the legal defense fund. Clerks-of-Record manage local documentation networks and report verified violations upward. Membership is tiered by trust and operational involvement — most members are Document Witnesses who verify and co-sign records; a smaller group are Seam Technicians who handle the network intrusion components.
