Properties.sector: Biotech / Genetic Architecture
Properties.founding_story: Founded in 2141 when disgraced University of Chicago geneticist Dr. Priya Suresh-Okonkwo was expelled from the academic system after publishing unauthorized human germline editing results. She sold her research to three venture cartels and incorporated Lacuna Genomics within six months. The name references the deliberate 'gaps' she left in her published work — data voids that concealed her most valuable discoveries. The corponation's founding doctrine holds that the human genome is not a biological fact but a negotiable document.
Properties.security_force: The Suture Corps — a 3,200-person private security division whose soldiers undergo mandatory proprietary genetic augmentation as a condition of employment. Known for their pale bioluminescent dermal markers, which glow faint blue under stress as an unintended side effect of their combat-enhancement packages. Equipped with gene-keyed weapons that detonate lethally if handled by anyone not carrying a Suture Corps genetic signature.
Properties.key_detail: Lacuna's most controversial product line is the PALIMPSEST series — a suite of heritable genetic modifications sold to wealthy clients that can be encoded to activate only in specific offspring generations. Critics call it 'delayed eugenics.' Lacuna calls it 'temporal phenotype scheduling.' Several city-states in Meridian 88 have banned PALIMPSEST products; Lacuna has responded by quietly funding the electoral campaigns of their rivals.
Properties.relationship_to_big_20: Member of the Big 20. Occupies the biotech seat vacated when a predecessor firm was dissolved following the 2158 Sequence Collapse scandal. Frequently in cold conflict with Helix Biosystems over territorial licensing rights in the southern corridor. Maintains a formal non-aggression pact with Lazarus Pharmaceuticals, though intelligence brokers report the pact is eroding.

Nodes.Name: The Lacuna Campus, a 14-square-kilometer fortified biozone built atop the former Zion, Illinois wetlands, surrounded by a controlled environmental buffer zone called the Sterile Ring

Properties.full_legal_name: Lazarus Pharmaceutical & Biological Dependency Sovereignty, Corp-S
Properties.aliases: Lazarus, The Pillars, LPX, The Dealers
Properties.sector: Pharmaceutical Manufacturing, Biological Dependency Engineering, & Medical Infrastructure
Properties.founding_story: Lazarus Pharmaceuticals emerged from the wreckage of the 2136 Corridor Plague — a synthetic respiratory pathogen that killed an estimated 800,000 corridor residents and overwhelmed every existing medical infrastructure system. The plague was later attributed to a failed biological weapons test by an unnamed defense corponation. In the chaos, virologist Dr. Emeka Solano and pharmaceutical chemist Dr. Rina Vasquez — both former employees of collapsed legacy pharma giant MedAxisCorp — developed the only effective treatment protocol using stockpiled lab equipment in a Milwaukee university basement. Rather than release their treatment openly, Vasquez — the business mind of the partnership — structured it as a proprietary sovereign pharmaceutical product and founded Lazarus to manufacture and distribute it exclusively. The corponation that emerged from this founding act has never deviated from Vasquez's original philosophy: that biological dependency is the most durable form of revenue. Lazarus's product lines are specifically engineered to require continuous use, with discontinuation protocols that are technically available but practically prohibitive in cost. Dr. Solano died in 2144; Vasquez continues to serve as CEO at age 71, referred to internally as 'the Architect.'
Properties.security_force: The Immune — a 7,500-person pharmaceutical enforcement and biological security unit responsible for protecting manufacturing facilities, suppressing counterfeit drug operations, and enforcing Lazarus's aggressive intellectual property sovereignty. The Immune is notable for its Biological Response Teams — units trained in pathogen containment, weaponized pharmaceutical deployment, and what internal documents call 'dependency enforcement operations.'
Properties.key_detail: Lazarus's flagship product, NeuroStabil, is a neurological maintenance drug prescribed to an estimated 12 million corridor residents for conditions ranging from anxiety to cognitive enhancement to trauma management. Independent studies suggest NeuroStabil's discontinuation syndrome is so severe that fewer than 3% of patients successfully cease use once started. Lazarus's medical franchise network is structured to make NeuroStabil the default first-line treatment for seventeen different diagnosed conditions.
Properties.relationship_to_big_20: Ranked 6th in the Big 20 by valuation. Lazarus occupies a unique position of biological leverage — an estimated 30% of all Big 20 corponation employees are active Lazarus pharmaceutical customers, and several Big 20 health benefit programs are exclusively supplied through Lazarus franchise clinics. This creates a dependency relationship that Lazarus's negotiating teams exploit with clinical precision.

Nodes.Name: The Lazarus Compound — a sovereign pharmaceutical manufacturing and research enclave in Milwaukee Sector 3, the Lazarus Medical Franchise Network (2,400 sovereign micro-clinics embedded throughout the corridor), and the Lazarus Biological Reserve — a classified research territory in the Upper Peninsula of former Michigan

Properties.full_legal_name: Marrowvault Cryogenic Preservation & Continuity Corponation
Properties.aliases: Marrowvault, The Vault, The Cold, MVC
Properties.sector: Cryogenic Preservation / Life Extension / Estate Management
Properties.employees: 44,700 (direct staff); ~2.1 million (clients in preservation, technically classified as 'suspended stakeholders')
Properties.founding_story: Marrowvault was incorporated in 2131 by a consortium of life-extension researchers, insurance actuaries, and estate lawyers who identified what they called 'the continuity gap' — the absence of any legally recognized, corporately administered framework for long-term human preservation and revival. Early cryonics companies had been ad hoc, poorly funded, and legally precarious. Marrowvault's founders designed something different: a corponation whose sovereign status meant it could enter into preservation contracts that superseded any individual nation-state's inheritance laws, death declarations, or estate proceedings. The pitch was elegant: for a substantial fee, Marrowvault would preserve you, manage your assets in a dedicated trust during suspension, and guarantee revival when either a specified medical condition became treatable or your contract term expired — whichever came first. The wealthy came in droves. By 2145, Marrowvault had 800,000 clients in suspension. By 2160, that number exceeded 2 million. The corponation now manages more accumulated private wealth in trust than the GDP of several small nations, and its legal team is considered the most formidable in the corridor — necessarily so, given that the corponation's business model depends entirely on the enforceability of contracts that span decades or centuries.
Properties.security_force: The Coldkeepers — 8,900 personnel responsible for physical security of the Preserve and transport security for clients in transit. The Coldkeepers are notable for their extreme insularity: they are recruited exclusively from within Marrowvault's own workforce families, creating a hereditary security caste. They operate a fleet of armored cryo-transport vehicles and maintain the Preserve against what internal documentation calls 'vault breach scenarios' — a category that encompasses everything from industrial accidents to deliberate attacks by inheritance-dispute parties.
Properties.key_detail: Marrowvault's revival rate — the percentage of clients successfully revived — is classified proprietary information. Independent estimates based on leaked internal documents suggest it sits between 61% and 74%, a figure the corponation vigorously disputes without providing alternative numbers. More troubling to critics is the 'Suspended Stakeholder' clause in Marrowvault's corporate charter: clients in preservation are legally classified as active corporate stakeholders, meaning their accumulated trust assets generate voting proxies that Marrowvault's executive council controls during suspension. With 2.1 million suspended stakeholders and their associated wealth, Marrowvault's executive council controls a staggering volume of proxy votes across dozens of other corponations' governance structures.
Properties.relationship_to_big_20: Big 20 member, ranked approximately 5th by total assets under management. Other Big 20 members have a deeply ambivalent relationship with Marrowvault — many of their own executives are Marrowvault clients, which means Marrowvault holds leverage over their estates and, through proxy voting, their corponations. Several Big 20 members have quietly attempted to pass corridor-wide legislation limiting Marrowvault's proxy voting rights. None have succeeded.

Nodes.Name: The Marrowvault Preserve — a vast underground sovereign facility complex beneath the southern shore of Lake Michigan, accessible via a fortified surface campus outside the ruins of Gary, Indiana. The underground complex spans approximately 12 square kilometers of pressurized, climate-controlled vault space. Secondary surface facilities in three other corridor locations.

Properties.full_legal_name: Mirrorwell Media & Cognitive Broadcast Corponation, Ltd.-S
Properties.aliases: Mirrorwell, The Well, The Echo House
Properties.sector: Media / Immersive Broadcast & Cognitive Advertising
Properties.employees: 29,000 direct; 1.2 million content licensees and signal hosts
Properties.founding_story: Mirrorwell was founded in 2149 by Celestine Achebe-Rourke, a former neural-interface UX designer who became convinced that traditional media — even immersive VR — was failing because it asked audiences to consume content rather than believe they had created it. Her foundational product, the ECHO ENGINE, was a broadcast algorithm that personalized media feeds so precisely that viewers reported feeling the content had been made specifically for them. The algorithm's secondary effect — that viewers became emotionally unable to consume media from competing platforms — was not disclosed in the original prospectus. Achebe-Rourke called it 'resonance loyalty.' Regulators called it psychological dependency architecture. She incorporated before they could act.
Properties.security_force: The Signal Corps — a lean 1,800-person security division that operates more like an intelligence agency than a conventional force. Signal Corps agents specialize in information warfare, blackmail architecture, and what Mirrorwell internally terms 'broadcast deterrence' — the credible threat of weaponizing a target's personal data, purchasing history, and neural-interface usage logs as public narrative. They have never fired a conventional weapon in a documented engagement.
Properties.key_detail: Mirrorwell's ECHO ENGINE has evolved significantly since 2149. Current internal versions — designated ECHO ENGINE 7.2 — are believed to incorporate predictive emotional modeling that can determine a viewer's psychological vulnerabilities within 11 minutes of engagement and begin targeted cognitive softening within 40 minutes. The corponation insists this is 'personalized engagement optimization.' Three former senior engineers have disappeared after attempting to whistleblow. One reappeared as a Mirrorwell brand ambassador.
Properties.relationship_to_big_20: Member of the Big 20. Holds the media seat and is formally at peace with Vantablack Media, though their relationship is the most hostile non-kinetic rivalry in the Big 20 — a continuous shadow war of audience capture, talent poaching, and algorithmic sabotage. Mirrorwell targets the neural-interface-equipped upper-corridor demographic; Vantablack dominates the physical broadcast and street-level market. Both claim the middle tier is theirs.

Nodes.Name: The Mirrorwell Arcology — a 62-story broadcast and residential tower in the former Chicago Loop, legally designated sovereign territory from the 4th floor upward; floors 1–3 remain Chicago municipal jurisdiction by treaty, creating a unique contested threshold zone locals call 'the Lobby War'

Properties.full_legal_name: NANA Regional Corporation (Sovereign Tribal Entity, Northwest Alaska Territory)
Properties.aliases: NANA, "The Mine" (industry shorthand -- Red Dog is synonymous with NANA), "Zinc Kings" (metals trade slang), "Northwest" (Tribal shorthand)
Properties.stock_designation: Non-tradeable. Hereditary shares only. No external market exists.
Properties.sector: Zinc mining, lead extraction, germanium production, advanced metallurgy, Arctic construction engineering, renewable energy systems, industrial-grade 3D printing feedstock
Properties.valuation: Φ1.7 trillion (estimated; driven by Red Dog Mine expansion and germanium deposits)
Properties.founding_story:
NANA Regional Corporation was established under ANCSA in 1971 to represent the Inupiat people of Northwest Alaska. The name NANA is an acronym that was adopted from the Northwest Alaska Native Association, the predecessor organization that advocated for Native land rights in the region.

NANA's story is the story of Red Dog Mine.

The Red Dog zinc-lead deposit, located in the western Brooks Range approximately 80 kilometers north of Kotzebue, was known to the local Inupiat long before Western geologists arrived. The creek that runs through the deposit ran red with dissolved zinc minerals -- the Inupiat called it "red dog" in their language, and the name stuck. The deposit was formally assessed in the 1970s and determined to be one of the largest zinc-lead deposits on Earth.

Mining began in 1989 under an operating agreement between NANA and Cominco (later Teck Resources), with NANA as the landowner and Teck as the operator. The arrangement was unusual: NANA negotiated a 25% net royalty and an escalating ownership stake that would give NANA full operational control over time. The deal was structured so that NANA would learn the mining business while extracting value from it -- not the colonial pattern of indigenous land being exploited for outside profit, but a deliberate, patient strategy of knowledge transfer.

By 2040, NANA had achieved full operational control of Red Dog. By 2060, NANA had expanded the mine's output and discovered additional deposits in the surrounding geology. By 2090, when the world's other major zinc mines were depleting, Red Dog was still producing -- now under mining protocols designed by NANA engineers trained in the same complex.

Zinc is not glamorous. It does not capture the imagination like rare earth elements or gold. But zinc is essential. Galvanization -- the coating of steel with zinc to prevent corrosion -- is the foundation of every durable steel structure on Earth. Zinc-air batteries are the primary energy storage technology for grid-scale renewable energy. Zinc alloys are critical to aerospace and defense manufacturing. And germanium -- a trace element extracted as a byproduct of zinc refining -- is essential to semiconductor manufacturing, fiber optic systems, and BCI electrode fabrication.

NANA's Red Dog complex produces 18% of the world's zinc, 12% of its lead, and -- critically -- 22% of its germanium. The germanium, an obscure element in most people's understanding, is the hidden leverage: without germanium, you cannot make the fiber optic cables that carry the world's data, the infrared optics that guide the world's weapons, or the semiconductor substrates that power the world's BCIs.

NANA controls this. Quietly. The zinc is visible and understood. The germanium is invisible and essential. NANA prices both according to their value, not their visibility.
Properties.security_force: NANA Northwest Guard: 3,400 personnel. Organized for defense of the Red Dog mining complex and the vast Northwest Alaska territory. Operates from the Kotzebue base and a network of outposts across the Brooks Range and Chukchi coast. The NNG maintains a Mining Defense Division (1,000 personnel dedicated to the Red Dog complex), an Arctic Border Patrol (1,200 personnel covering the Chukchi coastline and Brooks Range passes), and an Air Wing (600 personnel operating helicopters and drones for surveillance and rapid response across the territory). The remaining 600 personnel constitute a reserve force based at Kotzebue. NANA's defensive advantage is the same as every Arctic Tribe's: the terrain and climate are the primary defense. The Brooks Range in winter is impassable to any force not specifically equipped and trained for Arctic mountain warfare.
Properties.key_detail: NANA's germanium production -- 22% of global supply, extracted as a byproduct of zinc refining at Red Dog -- is the most strategically underappreciated resource in the Thirteen Tribes' portfolio. Germanium is essential to fiber optics, infrared optics, and semiconductor substrates. Without NANA germanium, global telecommunications capacity would decrease by an estimated 15% within two years as existing fiber optic cables degraded and could not be replaced. When a Tessera procurement executive asked NANA's board why germanium pricing had increased 8% year-over-year, the response was: "Because it is worth 8% more than it was last year. Next year it will be worth more than that. Zinc corrodes steel without it. Data stops without germanium. We set the price. You decide if you need steel and data."
Properties.relationship_to_big_20:
NANA supplies zinc to construction and defense industries worldwide, including Arcturus (military vehicle galvanization), Palladian Construction (structural steel coating), and Ferrogate Transit (rail infrastructure). Germanium goes to Tessera (BCI substrates), Zheng-Dao (fiber optic networks), and Silkworm Data (data center optical interconnects).

The relationships are transactional and non-negotiable. NANA publishes annual price lists for zinc, lead, and germanium. Corponations order at published prices or they do not order. There are no volume discounts, no long-term contracts, no futures. NANA sells spot. This policy gives NANA maximum flexibility and denies corponations the supply certainty they crave.

The germanium supply is the hidden leverage point. Every corponation that operates fiber optic infrastructure (which is all of them) depends on NANA germanium for maintenance and expansion. This dependency is rarely discussed publicly because acknowledging it would highlight a vulnerability that no corponation wants to advertise.

Nodes.Name: Approximately 38,000 square kilometers of Northwest Alaska, encompassing the western Brooks Range, the Noatak River watershed, and the Chukchi Sea coastline from Kotzebue Sound to Point Hope

Properties.full_legal_name: Nightshade Pharmatech & Cognitive Sciences Corponation
Properties.sector: Pharmaceutical Manufacturing, Cognitive Enhancement & Neurochemical Services
Properties.founding_story: Nightshade Pharmatech was founded in 2140 by neurochemist Dr. Cassia Lorne and black-market pharmaceutical distributor-turned-legitimized businessman Renn Okoro, a partnership that has defined the company's character ever since. Lorne brought rigorous research credentials; Okoro brought an intimate understanding of what people in desperate urban environments actually wanted to buy. Their initial product line was a series of focus-enhancement compounds marketed to corridor factory workers and gig laborers under the brand name 'Clarity' — cheap, effective, and habit-forming in ways that the original trials had technically documented but not prominently disclosed. Clarity became the most widely used cognitive compound in Meridian 88 within four years. When regulatory pressure mounted, Okoro leveraged his old distribution network contacts to accelerate Nightshade's sovereign corponation application, which was granted in 2145. Dr. Lorne died of a cardiac event in 2147; Okoro has run the company alone since, pivoting aggressively into military cognitive enhancement contracts and high-end neurochemical services for corporate executives — a market in which Nightshade's reputation for efficacy, regardless of side-effect profiles, is considered an asset rather than a liability.
Properties.security_force: Nightshade Enforcement Division, called the NED or 'the Doctors' — 4,800 personnel, notable for the fact that all field operatives are required to maintain current pharmaceutical compliance profiles, meaning they are on Nightshade-developed performance compounds at all times while on duty. The Doctors are considered exceptionally capable in short-duration high-intensity operations and considerably less reliable in extended campaigns, for reasons the company attributes to 'protocol optimization cycles.' A dedicated black-operations unit called the Alkaloids handles corporate intelligence and targeted enforcement actions.
Properties.key_detail: Nightshade's Clarity compound line, still the company's highest-volume product by unit, is now in its seventh generation. Clarity-7 is more effective and significantly more dependency-forming than original Clarity — and Nightshade's clinical services division profits handsomely from treating Clarity dependency. Internal documents leaked in 2155 suggested this feedback loop was designed rather than incidental. Okoro called the leak 'competitor sabotage' and the documents 'fabricated.' Sales of Clarity-7 increased 12% the following quarter.
Properties.relationship_to_big_20: Not a Big 20 member. Nightshade has been excluded from membership consideration twice — once due to Lazarus Pharmaceuticals lobbying against them, and once due to a broader ethics vote. Nightshade supplies cognitive enhancement compounds to the security forces of at least six Big 20 members under confidential contracts, which creates a dependency relationship that Okoro is not shy about referencing in negotiations. Lazarus Pharmaceuticals is a bitter rival; Novafold Pharmaceuticals maintains an uneasy non-compete arrangement.

Nodes.Name: Nightshade Campus, embedded within the Detroit Reclamation Zone — a 9-square-kilometer compound built into and over the ruins of a pre-Collapse automotive plant, characterized by its black-glass research towers rising from preserved industrial ruins kept as a deliberate aesthetic statement. The compound includes an internal clinical district where paid trial subjects can reside for extended periods.

Properties.full_legal_name: Novafold Pharmaceutical Sciences & Proteome Engineering Corponation
Properties.sector: Pharmaceutical Sciences & Proteome Engineering
Properties.founding_story: Novafold was created in 2144 through the hostile merger of seven mid-tier pharmaceutical firms by a financier-turned-bioethicist named Cassius Ren, who had made his first fortune shorting health insurers during the Cascade Illness years and his second fortune acquiring their assets after they collapsed. Ren's controversial thesis — published as a 90-page founding manifesto called 'The Proteome Is Property' — argued that pharmaceutical sovereignty required full vertical integration from protein synthesis to population dosing. He died in 2159 under circumstances the Meridian Compact ruled accidental; Novafold's board has never disputed that ruling publicly or privately with any consistency.
Properties.security_force: Novafold Clinical Enforcement Division (NCED) — 22,000 personnel operating under the legal fiction of 'patient safety officers.' NCED agents are licensed to enter any Meridian residential zone to enforce pharmaceutical compliance — a right extracted from the post-Cascade Illness emergency health charters of 2142. In practice, NCED functions as one of the most legally privileged private security forces in the corridor, capable of detaining individuals under 'therapeutic hold' provisions for up to 72 hours without external review.
Properties.key_detail: Novafold's 200 MedNode facilities collect passive biometric and pharmaceutical data on an estimated 28 million Meridian residents. The data architecture of this surveillance system was designed by Cinderblock AI, which means Cinderblock holds the encryption keys. This arrangement is the subject of a sealed arbitration that has been 'ongoing' for four years.
Properties.relationship_to_big_20: Ranked #15. In fierce market competition with Lazarus Pharmaceuticals, with both corponations engaged in what industry observers call 'the quiet drug war' — competing formularies, aggressive clinical territory poaching, and at least three confirmed incidents of sabotaged distribution chains. Helix Biosystems supplies Novafold's base protein synthesis substrate under a contract both parties describe as 'functional but hostile.' Cinderblock AI's MedNode data arrangement remains an unresolved liability.

Nodes.Name: The Novafold Medical Sovereign Zone — anchored by the Novafold Grand Campus in former Ann Arbor, Michigan: a 15-square-kilometer walled research and manufacturing complex. Also maintains 200 sovereign 'MedNodes' embedded in Meridian's residential stacks — miniature clinical facilities that serve as both distribution points and passive population health surveillance infrastructure.

Properties.full_legal_name: Oracle Drift Systems Predictive Analytics & Intelligence Corponation
Properties.aliases: Oracle Drift, The Drift, ODS, The Watchers
Properties.sector: Predictive Analytics / Intelligence Services / Algorithmic Governance
Properties.founding_story: Oracle Drift was founded in 2133 by Dr. Yael Brenner-Okafor, a former intelligence analyst and behavioral economist who left a classified position with a Meridian 88 city-state security apparatus to build what she described as 'the honest version of what governments pretend to do' — systematic, rigorous, apolitical prediction of human and institutional behavior. The corponation's founding product was the DRIFT engine: a predictive modeling system that integrated economic data, behavioral biometrics, social network analysis, and environmental variables to forecast events ranging from commodity price movements to civil unrest to individual executive decision-making. Early clients were financial institutions and logistics corponations. By 2141, Oracle Drift was selling predictive intelligence packages to city-state governments, security forces, and the Big 20. By 2149, it had achieved its unique Distributed Sovereignty status and become something that defied easy categorization: not quite a government, not quite a consultancy, not quite a surveillance apparatus, but containing elements of all three. Brenner-Okafor still serves as Chair of the Executive Oracle — the governing body she designed, which is itself structured according to DRIFT's predictions about optimal decision-making architecture.
Properties.security_force: The Stillkeepers — 6,100 personnel whose primary mandate is protection of Oracle Drift's physical infrastructure and data integrity. The Stillkeepers are notable for being one of the few corponation security forces that operates primarily in the digital domain: roughly 4,000 of the 6,100 are cyber-warfare and intrusion-response specialists. Physical security at the Stillpoint facility is handled by a 700-person hardened marine unit trained for submarine and deep-water operations. Oracle Drift has no conventional military capacity and does not seek one, on the stated grounds that 'anticipation is superior to force.'
Properties.key_detail: Oracle Drift's most controversial product is the Meridian Index — a continuously updated predictive assessment of every named individual, organization, and corponation in the corridor, scoring them across 340 behavioral and institutional variables. The Index is sold under strict confidentiality agreements to clients who include most of the Big 20, several city-state governments, and an unknown number of private parties. Being 'indexed' is not consensual and not disclosed. More than one corponation CEO has made a major strategic decision, only to discover afterward that Oracle Drift had predicted it to within 72 hours — and sold that prediction to their competitors weeks in advance.
Properties.relationship_to_big_20: Big 20 member, ranked approximately 3rd by valuation. Oracle Drift's relationship with other Big 20 members is the most complex in the corridor: it simultaneously serves them as a client intelligence provider and models them as predictive subjects. Every Big 20 member buys Oracle Drift intelligence products; every Big 20 member is also being modeled and predicted by Oracle Drift for sale to others. This dynamic creates a perpetual, unresolvable tension. At least two Big 20 members have attempted to acquire Oracle Drift outright. Both attempts were predicted and countered before they were formally initiated.

Nodes.Name: Oracle Drift claims no contiguous physical sovereign territory in the traditional sense. Instead, it holds 'Distributed Sovereignty' status under a novel legal framework it authored and lobbied into the Meridian 88 Corponation Charter in 2149 — sovereignty that attaches to its server infrastructure wherever that infrastructure is physically located. Its primary data fortress, called the Stillpoint, is a hardened underground facility beneath Lake Superior, accessible only by submarine. Secondary nodes are embedded, under negotiated agreements, within the sovereign territories of eleven other corponations.

Properties.full_legal_name: Ouroboros Energy & Closed-Loop Power Sovereignty, Inc-S
Properties.aliases: Ouroboros, The Snake, OES, The Grid Lords
Properties.sector: Energy Generation, Grid Infrastructure, & Power Sovereignty
Properties.founding_story: Ouroboros was not founded so much as consolidated. In 2135, the Meridian 88 corridor experienced the Blackout Cascade — a seventeen-day total grid failure caused by simultaneous cyberattacks on fragmented municipal power authorities. When the lights came back on, energy attorney and infrastructure speculator Yael Ostrander had quietly purchased the debt and operating licenses of eleven collapsed municipal power entities during the chaos. Over the following decade, she merged, acquired, and in two cases simply absorbed smaller energy providers until Ouroboros controlled the complete generational and transmission backbone of the corridor. Ostrander declared energy sovereignty in 2146, converting her holdings into a formal corponation-state and establishing the legal precedent that power transmission infrastructure constitutes 'vital sovereign territory' under the Corporate Reclamation Acts. She died in 2151 under circumstances officially ruled accidental; the corponation she left behind is run by a board that has maintained her expansion philosophy with mechanical precision.
Properties.security_force: The Current — a 12,000-person grid protection and power-denial warfare unit. The Current specializes in infrastructure defense, electromagnetic pulse operations, and the deployment of 'brownout protocols' — controlled, targeted power reduction to specific sectors as a coercive measure. They are the only known private security force with a dedicated EMP artillery division.
Properties.key_detail: Ouroboros's closed-loop billing system — the PowerBond — automatically deducts energy costs directly from residents' and corponations' financial accounts with no opt-out mechanism. Failure to maintain a positive PowerBond balance results in immediate, automated power termination. The corponation has shut off power to three rival corponation facilities and forty residential sectors in the past five years for non-payment, each time framing it as a 'routine contract enforcement action.'
Properties.relationship_to_big_20: Ranked 3rd in the Big 20 by valuation. Widely considered one of the two or three entities that could theoretically destabilize the entire corridor if it chose to. Every other corponation in the Big 20 pays Ouroboros energy fees and is therefore structurally dependent on it. The relationship is one of deep mutual resentment and absolute practical necessity.

Nodes.Name: The Ouroboros Ring — a continuous sovereign energy corridor running the full 500-kilometer length of Meridian 88, encompassing all primary power transmission infrastructure, the Lake Michigan Thermal Array (submerged geothermal and thermal differential generation), and six fusion micro-reactor clusters designated as sovereign Ouroboros installations

Properties.full_legal_name: Pale Lantern Bioethics & Compliance Sovereign Corponation
Properties.aliases: Pale Lantern, The Lantern, PLB, The Auditors
Properties.sector: Regulatory Compliance, Bioethics Certification & Corporate Audit Services
Properties.founding_story: Pale Lantern was established in 2144 by a consortium of former WHO ethicists, EU regulatory officials, and two disillusioned executives from HELIX BIOSYSTEMS following a series of catastrophic unregulated biotech incidents in the early Meridian 88 period — most notably the 2143 Southfield Graft Cascade, in which an unlicensed neural tissue procedure killed 340 people and left 1,200 with permanent cognitive damage. The founding premise was radical for its time: that ethical compliance itself could be a profitable sovereign enterprise. Corponations would pay for certification because the alternative — being labeled non-compliant by an independent sovereign auditor — would devastate their market valuation overnight.
Properties.security_force: The Pale Lantern Neutral Guard, a deliberately small 800-person force equipped only with non-lethal weapons, whose neutrality is the corponation's most valuable asset. The Guard's mandate is explicitly defensive. Pale Lantern's actual deterrence comes from its Compliance Revocation Authority — the power to publicly strip a corponation's ethical certification, which can trigger automatic stock delisting on three major Meridian exchanges.
Properties.key_detail: Pale Lantern's certification — the Lantern Mark — is required for any corponation operating in biotech, pharmaceutical, neural interface technology, or human augmentation sectors to access Meridian 88's major capital markets. Fourteen of the Big 20 currently hold active Lantern Marks. Three have had their marks suspended at least once. The identity of the three is an open secret that Pale Lantern officially refuses to confirm.
Properties.relationship_to_big_20: Not a Big 20 member and formally refuses the designation, maintaining that membership would compromise its auditor neutrality. This stance is considered either admirably principled or an extraordinarily sophisticated power play, depending on who you ask. Pale Lantern audits the Big 20. The Big 20 cannot audit Pale Lantern. This asymmetry is the source of significant and continuous tension.

Nodes.Name: Lantern Quarter — a 0.8 square kilometer neutral-zone enclave in Detroit's former Midtown district, maintained under strict sovereignty protocols that prohibit armed personnel from any other corponation from entering without Pale Lantern's explicit written authorization

Properties.full_legal_name: Palladian Construction & Urban Reclamation Sovereignty, Ltd-S
Properties.aliases: Palladian, The Builders, PCS, The Wreckingball
Properties.sector: Megastructure Construction, Urban Demolition, & Territorial Reclamation
Properties.founding_story: Palladian was built on a legal innovation as much as a physical one. In 2139, structural engineer and legal theorist Dr. Constance Mura published a landmark paper arguing that the act of construction — the physical transformation of territory — constituted a form of sovereign claim under emerging Corporate Reclamation Law. She then immediately founded Palladian to test her thesis in practice. Acquiring the ruins of Gary, Indiana as her base of operations, Mura developed a construction methodology called 'Territorial Metabolism' — a continuous cycle of demolition, material reclamation, and reconstruction that allowed Palladian to extract value from urban collapse while simultaneously building new corporate infrastructure. The corponation grew explosively during the Meridian 88 expansion boom of the 2040s, becoming the primary contractor for megastructure construction across the corridor. Mura's legal argument was eventually upheld in the 2147 Corridor Corporate Court ruling 'Palladian v. Detroit Municipal Remnant,' establishing construction sovereignty as a recognized legal category. Dr. Mura now serves as both CEO and Chief Legal Sovereign of the corponation.
Properties.security_force: The Foundation — a 15,000-person construction-site security and urban warfare unit equipped with industrial exoskeletons, demolition drone swarms, and mobile fabrication units capable of erecting defensive fortifications in under six hours. The Foundation is notorious for its use of 'structural denial' — the deliberate demolition of infrastructure to reshape battlefield terrain.
Properties.key_detail: Palladian's Detention Architecture division — a side business leasing pre-fabricated sovereign holding facilities to other corponations — generates Φ18 billion annually and has made Palladian the primary provider of private incarceration infrastructure in the corridor. The holding structures are technically Palladian sovereign territory, meaning detainees held within them fall under Palladian rather than corridor jurisdiction.
Properties.relationship_to_big_20: Ranked 11th in the Big 20. Palladian's relationships with other Big 20 members are almost entirely transactional — it has built facilities for nearly all of them and holds construction debt leverage over several. Its Detention Architecture business creates an additional layer of complicated dependency with corponations that use its holding facilities.

Nodes.Name: Palladian Prime — a sovereign industrial zone in the ruins of Gary, Indiana, housing the corponation's primary fabrication yards, materials processing facilities, and the infamous Palladian Detention Architecture (pre-fabricated sovereign holding structures leased to other corponations). Additionally claims 'construction sovereignty' over any active build site exceeding 10,000 square meters anywhere in the corridor.

Properties.full_legal_name: Pelican Drift Aquatics Corponation, Sovereign Marine Enterprise
Properties.sector: Freshwater Resource Extraction / Desalination Technology
Properties.founding_story: Pelican Drift emerged from the ruins of the Great Lakes Water Authority following its privatization under the Meridian Compact's 2136 Resource Sovereignty Amendments. A joint venture between three Scandinavian infrastructure funds and a Chicago-based municipal water utility, it was initially tasked with maintaining potable water delivery to the megacity corridor. Within a decade, it had acquired sovereign status over the processing platforms, developed proprietary low-energy desalination membranes capable of processing microplastic-laden lake water at industrial scale, and pivoted from utility provider to resource corponation. Its founders have long since been diluted out of meaningful equity by successive capital raises.
Properties.security_force: The Warden Fleet — a 3,400-person maritime security force operating 67 armed patrol vessels, 12 submersible interdiction craft, and a network of underwater sensor arrays across claimed sovereign waters. The Warden Fleet has engaged in lethal force against unauthorized water extraction operations on 14 documented occasions since 2144. Cormorant Naval Systems has a standing contract to supply the Warden Fleet's heavier vessels.
Properties.key_detail: Pelican Drift holds the Meridian Compact's exclusive license for commercial freshwater extraction from Lakes Huron and Michigan through 2167. Every liter of potable water consumed by approximately 31 million corridor residents was processed by Pelican Drift infrastructure. The corponation has never publicly acknowledged that it deliberately slowed membrane technology rollout for three years to maintain scarcity pricing.
Properties.relationship_to_big_20: Full Big 20 member, ranked approximately 7th by total valuation. Pelican Drift is considered one of the 'untouchable' members because its product is non-substitutable — no competing corponation can realistically displace it from the water supply chain without triggering a humanitarian crisis that would destabilize the entire Meridian Compact framework.

Nodes.Name: The Drift Yards — a sovereign archipelago of 34 semi-permanent floating platforms anchored across Lake Huron and Lake Michigan, connected by a proprietary fast-transit waterway system. The largest platform, Pelican Prime, spans 4.2 kilometers and serves as the corponation's administrative capital. Total sovereign water-surface area claimed: approximately 900 square kilometers.

Properties.founding_story: Pellucid was incorporated in 2138 by Dr. Ines Okafor-Strand, a former University of Michigan behavioral economist who developed what she called the Transparency Paradox: the more openly you surveil a population, the more compliant and self-regulating it becomes. She sold this idea — and her first commercial surveillance architecture — to three Big 20 corponations within eighteen months. By 2143, Pellucid's predictive compliance software was embedded in the HR infrastructure of over 200 corponations across Meridian 88. Okafor-Strand declared sovereignty in 2145, arguing that a company holding behavioral data on 40 million citizens constituted a de facto state. The legal challenge took two years. She won on the grounds that Pellucid's data reserves qualified as critical sovereign infrastructure.
Properties.security_force: The Lens Division — 6,000 personnel, almost entirely intelligence operatives and cyber-warfare specialists rather than conventional soldiers. Pellucid's security doctrine holds that kinetic conflict represents a surveillance failure. The Lens Division has never lost a perimeter because they neutralize threats before they materialize. Allegedly.
Properties.key_detail: Pellucid's most controversial product is ORACLE-7, a predictive behavior engine that corponations, municipal zones, and private clients use to forecast individual human actions up to 72 hours in advance with a claimed 91% accuracy rate. Civil liberties groups contest both the accuracy claim and the legality of the underlying data collection. Pellucid's legal team has defeated 340 challenges to date.
Properties.relationship_to_big_20: Pellucid holds data contracts with every member of the Big 20 without exception, which gives them a structural leverage position that makes direct conflict with them essentially unthinkable. They are formally neutral in all inter-corponation disputes but are widely suspected of selling predictive intelligence to multiple parties simultaneously — a practice mirroring CDW's arms sales philosophy. Mirrorwell Media and Pellucid maintain a tense co-existence, competing for control of the information economy.

Nodes.Name: The Pellucid Atrium — a gleaming 12-square-kilometer campus in what was formerly downtown Ann Arbor, Michigan. Glass-and-chrome architecture deliberately designed for maximum visibility from the outside, an ironic aesthetic choice given the company's business model.

Properties.full_legal_name: Rendstone Nuclear Power Corponation, Sovereign Energy Enterprise of the Meridian Compact
Properties.sector: Nuclear Energy / Fission Reactor Operations
Properties.founding_story: Rendstone Nuclear was chartered by the Meridian Compact in 2133 as an emergency measure following the cascading failure of the regional power grid during the Winter Collapse of 2132-33, which killed an estimated 14,000 corridor residents. The Compact nationalized the remaining operational reactor assets from four bankrupt utility companies, consolidated them under a single sovereign charter, and issued that charter to a newly formed corponation with mandatory Big 20 membership pre-granted. The founding board was drawn from the nuclear engineering faculties of three surviving universities and a cadre of former US Nuclear Regulatory Commission personnel who had been operating in a freelance advisory capacity since the NRC's de facto dissolution in 2129. The corponation has had seven CEOs in 22 years, all internal promotions from the engineering corps.
Properties.security_force: The Exclusion Guard — 8,400 personnel making it one of the largest corponation security forces in Meridian 88. The Guard operates in three concentric rings around the reactor complex, with escalating rules of engagement. The outer ring conducts standard interdiction. The middle ring operates under standing shoot-on-sight orders for any unauthorized personnel. The inner ring's rules of engagement are classified. The Guard also maintains a 600-person rapid reaction force capable of deploying anywhere in the corridor within four hours, designated for infrastructure protection scenarios.
Properties.key_detail: Rendstone's 11 reactors provide approximately 34% of all electrical power consumed in the Meridian 88 corridor. The corponation's founding charter contains a Compact-ratified provision stating that any military or paramilitary action against Rendstone infrastructure constitutes an attack on the Compact itself, triggering a collective defense obligation from all Big 20 members. This provision has never been tested.
Properties.relationship_to_big_20: Charter Big 20 member with Category One status — one of four corponations designated as 'corridor-critical infrastructure' whose involuntary dissolution or hostile acquisition is prohibited under Compact law. Rendstone participates minimally in Big 20 political maneuvering, preferring to hold its structural leverage in reserve. It is simultaneously the most powerful and most boring member of the Big 20, described by other members' lobbyists as 'the entity you design around, not the entity you negotiate with.'

Nodes.Name: The Rendstone Exclusion Corridor — a 180-square-kilometer sovereign zone surrounding the Rendstone Reactor Complex on the Lake Erie shoreline near the ruins of Toledo, Ohio. The complex contains 11 operational fission reactors of varying generations, a fuel processing facility, and a permanent residential settlement of approximately 28,000 workers and dependents known as Rendstone Township. Properties.full_legal_name: Rictus Entertainment & Immersive Experience Corponation
Properties.aliases: Rictus, The Grin, Ric-E, The House
Properties.sector: Entertainment / Immersive Experience / Neural Recreation
Properties.founding_story: Rictus was founded in 2138 by Casimir Voll, a former theme park architect and neural interface developer who had grown disgusted with what he called 'the flatness of passive media.' Voll's thesis was simple and, critics argued, deeply dangerous: human beings would pay any price for experiences that felt more real than reality. He launched Rictus with a single product — the DeepDream Suite, a full-sensory neural immersion pod that delivered experiences indistinguishable from lived memory. The first Rictus parlor opened in a repurposed Detroit theater in 2138. By 2142, there were 400 locations across the corridor. By 2147, Rictus had declared sovereign territory in Detroit, arguing that its 'experience economy' constituted a new form of civic infrastructure. They weren't entirely wrong. The Detroit Pleasure Corridor now draws more visitors annually than any other single destination in Meridian 88. Voll died in 2155 under circumstances the corponation describes as 'a voluntary full-immersion retirement' — widely understood to mean he jacked into a DeepDream Suite and never came back out. The company has been run by a rotating executive council since.
Properties.security_force: The Smilers — 11,000 security personnel famous for their unsettling customer-service demeanor. Smilers are trained to de-escalate with extreme psychological precision and escalate with equal precision when required. They wear white uniforms with reflective face shields that produce a slight upward curve at the corners — hence the name. The Smilers also operate a covert intelligence division called the Curtain, which monitors for corporate espionage, talent poaching, and what Rictus terms 'experience piracy' (illegal duplication of proprietary neural content).
Properties.key_detail: Rictus's DeepDream technology is both its greatest asset and its most controversial product. Extended use causes a well-documented neurological condition called Drift — a progressive inability to distinguish immersive memory from lived experience. Rictus acknowledges Drift in its user agreements (buried in clause 47-F) but has successfully lobbied against mandatory health warnings in seven of the nine major city-states. The corponation also operates a quiet secondary business: harvesting anonymized emotional and experiential data from DeepDream sessions, which it sells to advertisers, political consultants, and — according to several investigative journalists who have since gone quiet — at least two intelligence agencies.
Properties.relationship_to_big_20: Big 20 member, ranked approximately 8th by revenue. Rictus is simultaneously beloved and feared by other Big 20 members — beloved because its entertainment infrastructure drives consumer spending across all sectors, feared because its data harvesting capabilities give it leverage over virtually everyone. At least three other Big 20 corponations are known to have purchased Rictus experiential data on their own executives.

Nodes.Name: The Rictus Pleasure Corridor — a 14-kilometer strip of sovereign entertainment territory carved through the former downtown core of Detroit, plus six 'Rictus Enclaves' embedded within other city-states across the corridor (negotiated sovereign entertainment zones within host cities). Headquarters: The Grinhouse, a 112-story entertainment megastructure in the heart of the Detroit Corridor.

Properties.full_legal_name: Ringo CorpoNation Holdings, Inc. (Sovereign Charter Entity, Detroit Reclamation Zone)
Properties.aliases: Ringo, "The Ring" (internal culture), "The Machine" (street slang), "Big Orange" (derogatory, referencing the brand color)
Properties.stock_designation: RNGO (Internal valuation; Ringo operates a closed financial ecosystem)
Properties.sector: Fuel, retail, transit, broadband, pharmacy, infrastructure, financial services, residential management
Properties.founding_story:
Ringo did not begin as a corponation. It began as a gas station company.

The Ringo Energy Corporation was founded in 2119 in Houston, Texas, by Samuel Ringo, a third-generation petroleum distributor who operated a chain of 340 fuel stations across Texas, Louisiana, and Oklahoma. Sam Ringo was not a visionary. He was a businessman who understood one thing with perfect clarity: people need fuel, and whoever controls the last mile of fuel delivery controls something more fundamental than any technology company ever will. Technology is optional. Infrastructure is not.

The company's growth in its first decade was unremarkable. By 2129, Ringo Energy operated 2,800 stations across the American South and Midwest. Revenue was Φ12 billion. The stations were clean, reliable, and standardized. The brand color -- a distinctive burnt orange -- was recognizable from every highway in fifteen states. Ringo stations sold fuel, lottery tickets, snacks, and basic automotive supplies. They were invisible in the way that plumbing is invisible: essential, ubiquitous, and beneath the notice of anyone who did not need them at that exact moment.

Then Detroit collapsed.
Properties.relationship_to_big_20:
Ringo does not own a share of the elevator. Ringo owns the ground it stands on -- functionally, if not literally. The Makassar Terminus city operates on Ringo infrastructure: RingoFuel powers the ground vehicles, RingoMart feeds the population, RingoPharma provides medical supplies, RingoTransit moves people around the base, and RingoNet provides broadband. The 340,000 residents of the terminus city live under a hybrid jurisdiction -- Tethys law governs the elevator and its facilities, Ringo law governs the city that surrounds them.

This gives Ringo something unique: it controls the daily life infrastructure of the single most strategically important location on Earth without bearing any of the cost or risk of the elevator itself. If the elevator is destroyed, Ringo loses a city. Tethys loses everything. If the city's infrastructure fails, the elevator's workforce cannot function. The relationship is asymmetric in Ringo's favor -- Tethys needs Ringo more than Ringo needs Tethys, and Catherine Ringo-Vasquez negotiated the subcontract accordingly.

Ringo's REDLINE registry also interoperates with the Tethys Exclusion Registry through the CSES protocol. A person placed on REDLINE for shoplifting at a RingoMart is, by extension, barred from the space elevator. They will never leave Earth. Marcus "Brick" Tallow robbed a gas station. The consequence is that he is permanently barred from the stars. This was not the intent. It is the design.

---

Properties.founding_story: Saltmarsh emerged in 2135 from the wreckage of three collapsed municipal telecom utilities after the Great Signal Blackout — a cascading infrastructure failure that left 40 million Meridian residents without communications for eleven days. The blackout's architect was never officially identified, but Saltmarsh's first CEO, a former signals intelligence officer named Daria Holt, built the entire network on the assumption that it would be attacked again. Every node is hardened, redundant, and capable of autonomous operation. Holt's paranoia became Saltmarsh's brand: 'The signal that doesn't die.'
Properties.security_force: Saltmarsh Signal Guard (SSG) — 19,000 personnel, heavily specialized in electronic warfare and counter-intrusion. Every SSG unit carries a personal signal-hardening suite and is trained to maintain communications infrastructure under active cyberattack. Their most feared capability is the DEADBAND protocol — a localized signal blackout weapon that can silence all non-Saltmarsh communications in a 40-kilometer radius, used twice in corporate conflicts and once, controversially, during a Meridian labor uprising in 2161.
Properties.key_detail: Saltmarsh holds sovereign licensing rights to the 6.8 GHz band across the entire Meridian corridor — a spectrum allocation locked in during the post-blackout emergency charters of 2135 that no subsequent legal challenge has successfully overturned. This means every corponation, government remnant, and private citizen in Meridian is, at some level, a Saltmarsh tenant.
Properties.relationship_to_big_20: Ranked #13. Vantablack Media is their largest content-transmission client and also their most adversarial contract partner — renegotiating aggressively every three years. Cinderblock AI requires Saltmarsh signal infrastructure for all external cognitive leasing. Kelpline Logistics' VINE AI communicates exclusively over Saltmarsh encrypted backbone.

Nodes.Name: Saltmarsh Signal Zones — not a contiguous territory but a patchwork of 4,400 sovereign signal towers, 900 buried fiber nodes, and twelve orbital relay licenses covering the entire Meridian 88 corridor and extending into the surrounding rural collapse zones. Administrative headquarters: the Saltmarsh Spire, a 340-meter communications tower and office complex in former Cleveland.

Properties.founding_story: Scoria Works was founded in 2129 by a worker-led buyout of the collapsed Meridian Heavy Industries conglomerate, structured as a corponation under the 2127 Meridian 88 Labor Sovereignty Act — one of the few entities in the corridor that began as a genuinely worker-owned enterprise. Properties.full_legal_name: Sealaska Corporation (Sovereign Tribal Entity, Southeast Alaska Territory)
Properties.aliases: Sealaska, "The Panhandle" (geographic reference), "Raven and Eagle" (cultural -- referencing the two Tlingit moieties), "Green Gold" (timber trade slang), "The Face" (tourism industry -- Sealaska controls the most visible Alaska tourism infrastructure)
Properties.stock_designation: Non-tradeable. Hereditary shares only. No external market exists.
Properties.sector: Sustainable timber, engineered wood products, carbon credits, tourism, cultural heritage management, cruise ship port operations, wilderness recreation, traditional art and craft export, hydroelectric power
Properties.founding_story:
Sealaska Corporation was established under ANCSA in 1971 to represent the Tlingit, Haida, and Tsimshian peoples of Southeast Alaska. The region is unlike any other part of Alaska: a temperate rainforest archipelago of over 1,100 islands, deep fjords, massive glaciers, and the largest intact temperate rainforest on Earth -- what was formerly the Tongass National Forest.

Sealaska's history with the timber industry is complicated and instructive. In the decades following ANCSA, Sealaska -- like many Native corporations -- logged aggressively. The old-growth Sitka spruce and western red cedar of the Tongass were valuable, and the corporation needed revenue. By the 2000s, Sealaska had logged significant portions of its land, generating controversy and environmental criticism. The logging was legal, commercially rational, and ecologically devastating.

The reversal began in the 2020s. A new generation of Tlingit, Haida, and Tsimshian leaders -- many of them educated in environmental science and traditional ecological knowledge -- pushed Sealaska toward sustainable forestry. The argument was not purely environmental. It was economic: old-growth timber was a depleting asset, but a managed forest was a renewable one. And the standing forest had value that logged land did not: carbon sequestration, watershed protection, wildlife habitat, and the cultural landscape that defined Tlingit, Haida, and Tsimshian identity.

By 2060, Sealaska had transitioned from extraction forestry to sustainable management. Timber harvest was reduced to annual growth increment -- taking only what the forest produced each year, never cutting into the capital. The shift reduced short-term revenue but created a perpetual income stream from engineered wood products, carbon credits, and the most valuable intangible asset in the global economy: intact wilderness.

Tourism became the second pillar. Southeast Alaska -- with its glaciers, fjords, wildlife, and indigenous culture -- had been a major tourist destination since the cruise ship era of the 20th century. Under Sealaska's sovereignty, tourism was restructured from the extractive model (cruise ships dumping thousands of passengers into small communities for a few hours) to a managed experience economy. Visitor numbers were capped. Cultural experiences were designed and led by Tlingit, Haida, and Tsimshian guides. Cruise ships paid substantial port fees and were subject to strict environmental standards. The tourist experience improved dramatically. The revenue per visitor tripled.

Sealaska's third pillar is cultural export. Tlingit, Haida, and Tsimshian art -- carving, weaving, metalwork, and formline design -- is among the most recognized indigenous art traditions in the world. Sealaska operates a cultural heritage division that manages the authentication, production, and sale of traditional art and craft, generating approximately Φ8 billion annually. In a world of synthetic everything, handmade indigenous art carries a premium that no algorithm can replicate.

The Tlingit clan system -- divided into Raven and Eagle moieties, with governance balanced between them -- provides the cultural framework for Sealaska's corporate governance. Board seats are balanced between moieties. Decisions require cross-moiety consensus. The system is ancient, sophisticated, and more stable than any corporate governance structure invented in the last two centuries.
Properties.security_force: Sealaska Coastal Guard: 3,000 personnel. Organized for maritime defense of the Alexander Archipelago and the Southeast Alaska coastline. Operates 12 armed patrol vessels adapted for the narrow channels and fjords of the Inside Passage, shore-based defense installations at key straits and narrows, drone surveillance networks, and a Tourism Security Division (600 personnel) responsible for visitor management and the security of cruise ship port facilities. The archipelago's geography -- over 1,100 islands separated by narrow, winding channels -- creates a defensive environment where local knowledge is the decisive advantage. Sealaska's patrol boat crews know every channel, every current, every rock. Unfamiliar vessels do not.
Properties.key_detail: Sealaska's managed forest produces Φ42 billion annually in engineered wood products (cross-laminated timber, glue-laminated beams, and high-performance wood composites) and Φ28 billion in verified carbon credits. The standing forest -- approximately 16,000 square kilometers of temperate rainforest -- sequesters an estimated 340 million tonnes of CO2 and is valued on the carbon market at approximately Φ29 billion. The forest is the asset. Not the timber -- the forest. When a consortium of carbon credit brokers proposed a deal that would have required Sealaska to guarantee a specific annual carbon credit volume for twenty years, the board declined. "The forest grows at the pace the forest grows," the board chair explained. "We do not make promises about what the forest will do. We observe what it does and sell the result."
Properties.relationship_to_big_20:
Sealaska's relationships with major corponations are primarily in two areas: engineered wood products and carbon credits.

Palladian Construction is the largest purchaser of Sealaska engineered wood products (Φ14 billion annually), using cross-laminated timber in corponation facility construction as a lower-carbon alternative to steel and concrete. Ringo purchases engineered wood for residential construction in its sovereign zones. Multiple corponations purchase Sealaska carbon credits to offset their emissions profiles.

Sealaska's tourism operations interact with corponation cruise lines (several of which are Ringo subsidiaries). The relationship is controlled by Sealaska: visitor caps, environmental standards, port fees, and cultural protocols are non-negotiable. A Ringo cruise subsidiary that violated Sealaska's whale-watching distance protocols in 2184 was banned from Southeast Alaska ports for three years. The ban cost the subsidiary Φ2.1 billion in lost revenue. The whales were unharmed.

Sealaska is the Tribe most likely to engage in cultural soft power -- Tlingit, Haida, and Tsimshian art and design are exhibited in museums, galleries, and public spaces in corponation sovereign zones worldwide. This cultural visibility gives Sealaska a public profile that exceeds its economic weight, and it serves as a constant reminder that the Thirteen Tribes are not simply resource extractors. They are civilizations.

Properties.full_legal_name: Silkworm Data Sovereignty Incorporated

Properties.founding_story: Founded in 2141 by former census actuary Priya Vasanthan-Cole after she discovered that the collapse of three municipal governments had left nearly 900 million personal data records legally ownerless. She filed sovereign claim on the data under the Meridian 88 Corporate Personhood Expansion Act, monetized the archive, and used the proceeds to build the Cocoon within four years. Vasanthan-Cole is still CEO, now 71, referred to internally as the Spinner.
Properties.security_force: The Threadbare — a lean, 3,200-person counterintelligence and data-enforcement unit specializing in information warfare, memory extraction litigation, and the violent recovery of stolen datasets. Threadbare operatives wear matte white bodysuits with no visible insignia and carry nonlethal compliance weapons as standard, lethal as secondary.
Properties.key_detail: Silkworm Data sells predictive behavioral profiles accurate to a 94.7% confidence interval across a 72-hour window. Their most controversial product, the Lifeline Index, assigns every registered Meridian 88 resident a numeric score representing their economic viability — and at least six corponations use it as a hiring prerequisite.

Properties.full_legal_name: Slagworks Industrial Fabrication & Heavy Materials Corponation
Properties.sector: Heavy Manufacturing / Industrial Fabrication / Reclamation Metallurgy
Properties.founding_story: Slagworks was assembled rather than founded — a corporate consolidation event in 2136 in which a private equity consortium acquired seventeen failing Rust Belt steel, fabrication, and reclamation operations and merged them under a single sovereign charter. The driving figure was Benedikt Mrak, a Croatian-American industrial financier who believed the corridor's coming infrastructure boom would create insatiable demand for structural materials and that the only way to meet that demand was vertical integration at massive scale. Mrak was right. As Palladian Construction, Ferrogate Transit, and a dozen other infrastructure corponations exploded in the 2040s, Slagworks became the foundational supplier — the entity that made the steel that built the corridor. The corponation's sovereign territory was established in 2139, largely because no city-state wanted to claim jurisdiction over the environmental catastrophe that Slagworks' operations continued to generate. Mrak died in 2152 of heavy metal toxicity, a fact his corponation marked with a company-wide minute of silence and then immediately suppressed from public record.
Properties.security_force: The Furnace Watch — 19,000 security and enforcement personnel, the largest corponation security force in the corridor outside the Big 20 defense specialists. The Furnace Watch is notorious for its aggressive response to labor actions: Slagworks has the highest rate of security-related worker injuries in the corridor, a distinction it has held for eleven consecutive years. The Watch also operates an industrial espionage division called the Tap, focused on protecting Slagworks' proprietary alloy formulations and reclamation processes.
Properties.key_detail: Slagworks' Reclamation Metallurgy division is its most innovative and most controversial operation. The division processes structural debris from demolished buildings, decommissioned infrastructure, and — under contracts that other corponations prefer not to discuss publicly — wreckage from military and security operations across the corridor. This means Slagworks regularly receives and processes materials containing human remains, classified technology fragments, and chemically hazardous compounds. The corponation's sovereign status means no outside inspector has ever formally audited the Reclamation division's intake manifest.
Properties.relationship_to_big_20: Not currently a Big 20 member, though Slagworks supplies materials to at least 14 of the 20. This dependency gives Slagworks enormous informal leverage, and the corponation has used it — notably in 2158, when it briefly halted steel shipments to three Big 20 members during a sovereign border dispute, triggering a construction crisis across the corridor. Big 20 members have repeatedly discussed vertically integrating their own materials supply to reduce Slagworks dependency. None have succeeded in doing so at scale.

Nodes.Name: The Slagworks Foundry Belt — a continuous sovereign industrial zone spanning 34 kilometers along the southern Lake Michigan shoreline, incorporating the former industrial infrastructure of Gary, Hammond, and East Chicago, Indiana. The zone is one of the most heavily polluted sovereign territories in the corridor, a fact Slagworks considers an operational feature rather than a liability.

Properties.full_legal_name: Stonepath Integrated Logistics & Sovereign Transit Authority, Corp.-S
Properties.sector: Logistics / Heavy Transit & Sovereign Infrastructure Leasing
Properties.founding_story: Stonepath was assembled rather than founded — a 2139 consolidation of eleven failing regional freight operators by logistics financier August Tran-Holloway, who recognized that the collapse of public infrastructure in the early megacity era had created a power vacuum in physical transit. Tran-Holloway did not buy the companies for their assets; he bought them for their right-of-way deeds, easements, and tunnel licenses, then spent four years in corridor courts arguing that a network of sovereign transit infrastructure constituted a sovereign territory under the Meridian 88 Corponation Charter. He won in 2143. The ruling is still contested by seven municipalities and celebrated annually inside Stonepath as 'Right-of-Way Day.'
Properties.security_force: The Transit Authority Enforcement Division (TAED) — 12,000 personnel operating across the sovereign node network. TAED functions as both a security force and a customs authority, with legal power to detain, search, and levy tariffs on any cargo or personnel transiting Stonepath sovereign right-of-way. Their armored transit enforcement vehicles — called 'Milestones' — are a common and intimidating sight at corridor freight junctions.
Properties.key_detail: Stonepath's most valuable and least visible service is the SEALED MANIFEST program — a premium logistics tier in which cargo is transported with zero documentation, zero scanning, and zero third-party disclosure. Clients pay a 400% premium. Stonepath's sovereign right-of-way status means SEALED MANIFEST shipments cannot be inspected by municipal or corridor authorities. The program is used by every member of the Big 20 and by actors that most Big 20 members would prefer not to be associated with.
Properties.relationship_to_big_20: Member of the Big 20. Holds the logistics seat and is in direct rivalry with Kelpline Logistics, which dominates waterway and lake freight while Stonepath controls land and aerial transit. The two corponations maintain a formal freight-sharing treaty that both routinely undermine through subsidiary shell operations. Stonepath is broadly regarded as indispensable — every corponation in the Big 20 uses its infrastructure — which Tran-Holloway's successors leverage as a form of institutional immunity.

Nodes.Name: The Stonepath Transit Sovereignty — not a contiguous territory but a legally recognized network of 340 sovereign transit nodes (depots, tunnels, rail junctions, and aerial docking platforms) distributed across the Meridian 88 corridor, connected by 2,200 kilometers of Stonepath-owned right-of-way designated as sovereign linear territory

Properties.full_legal_name: Sulfur Crown Agriculture & Terraforming Sovereign Corponation
Properties.aliases: Sulfur Crown, The Crown, Yellow Death (derogatory), Crown Ag
Properties.sector: Industrial Agriculture, Soil Remediation & Terraforming
Properties.employees: 540,000 direct field and processing workers; 80,000 administrative
Properties.founding_story: The collapse of industrial Midwestern farming in the 2030s left millions of acres of chemically exhausted, flood-damaged, and contamination-blighted land essentially worthless. Agro-chemist Beaumont Jarvis saw an opportunity no one else wanted. In 2136, he began purchasing blighted farmland at near-zero valuations and applying his proprietary sulfur-catalyzed bioremediation process — a brutal, fast-acting soil restoration technique that worked spectacularly but left the land chemically dependent on Crown's own fertilizer compounds. Critics called it 'agricultural addiction.' Jarvis called it 'a sustainable relationship.' By 2144, Crown controlled enough food-producing territory to meaningfully threaten the caloric supply of three million Meridian 88 citizens, at which point sovereignty was less a legal argument than a statement of existing fact.
Properties.security_force: The Fieldwarden Corps — 35,000 heavily armed agricultural security personnel deployed across Crown Territories. Fieldardens are notorious for aggressive anti-poaching enforcement (the 'poaching' of crops, soil samples, or Crown's proprietary fertilizer compounds). They operate armored agricultural vehicles modified for combat. Rural communities near Crown Territories regard them with a mixture of economic dependency and deep fear.
Properties.key_detail: Sulfur Crown's remediation process, while genuinely effective at restoring blighted soil, renders the restored land chemically dependent on Crown's proprietary AUREATE fertilizer compound. Stopping AUREATE application causes rapid soil collapse within two growing seasons. This has created a captive market of independent farmers and smaller corponations who sold or leased land to Crown, accepted remediation, and now cannot exit the relationship without destroying their agricultural base.
Properties.relationship_to_big_20: Sulfur Crown is a Big 20 member but occupies a peculiar position: they are simultaneously resented and indispensable. Ironclad Agrisystems competes with them directly and bitterly in contested agricultural zones. Ouroboros Energy and Crown have a territorial dispute over former industrial land in Ohio that has produced three armed standoffs in the past decade. Crown supplies food inputs to Lacuna Genomics for agricultural genomics research under a contract that both parties describe as mutually beneficial and observers describe as mutually coercive.

Properties.full_legal_name: Tessera CorpoNation Holdings, Ltd. (Sovereign Charter Entity, Austin Sovereign Zone)
Properties.aliases: Tessera, TessCorp (informal), "The Cathedral" (internal culture), "The Mind" (street slang)
Properties.sector: Brain-computer interfaces, neural technology, cognitive services, behavioral data markets, neural advertising
Properties.founding_story:
Tessera did not begin as Tessera. It began as NeuraLink Systems, Inc., a 2133 reorganization of the original Cortex Dynamics Corp after Aldric Vance's departure from the company in 2131 amid the broader collapse of his business empire. The regulatory enforcement actions against Vance Automotive, the social platform's insolvency proceedings, and the Frontier Launch nationalization crisis left Cortex Dynamics orphaned -- a genuinely promising neural interface company suddenly without its patron billionaire's funding pipeline or media amplification.

What Cortex Dynamics had was talent. The engineering team that had achieved the first fully automated BCI surgical procedure in 2130 -- 94-second insertion, outpatient, local anesthetic -- was the most capable neural interface development group on Earth. They also had 1,400 patients with functioning N1 implants, a dataset of unprecedented depth in human neural signal processing, and a patent portfolio that would take any competitor fifteen years to work around.

Dr. Amara Osei, Cortex Dynamics' Chief Neural Architect, led the management buyout in 2133. She brought in Vikram Chandra, a former McKinsey partner who had run the firm's healthcare M&A practice, as CEO. Chandra's first act was to rename the company Tessera -- from the Latin word for the small tiles in a mosaic, reflecting his stated vision that individual neural connections were tiles in a larger picture of human cognition. The name was elegant, the metaphor was apt, and Chandra meant every word of it. He genuinely believed that neural augmentation would complete the human mind the way a final tile completes a mosaic. This belief would become Tessera's greatest strength and its most dangerous blind spot.

The 2134 Series C funding round brought in Φ4.8 billion from a consortium led by Sequoia Capital's successor fund, SoftBank Vision's remnant entities, and -- critically -- the sovereign wealth fund of the United Arab Emirates, which was already positioning itself for the post-oil economy. The UAE investment came with territorial concessions: Tessera received a 50-year charter to operate a "cognitive technology development zone" in Abu Dhabi, the first instance of a national government granting a neural interface company anything resembling sovereign operational authority.

Chandra saw the template. He spent the next decade acquiring it everywhere he could.
Properties.relationship_to_big_20:
Tessera holds a 12% equity stake in Tethys Orbital Industries and is the exclusive supplier of neural interface technology for orbital personnel. Every climber pilot, tether maintenance worker, and station engineer carries Tessera hardware. The NovaMind Orbital variant is specifically calibrated for microgravity cognitive performance and is the only BCI certified for use above 400 kilometers altitude. Tessera also operates a pharmaceutical research module on Tethys Station Beta, where microgravity biocompatibility coatings for BCI electrodes are manufactured. This makes Tessera a critical node in the elevator's supply chain -- and gives Tessera leverage over Tethys that no equity stake alone could provide.

Tessera's interest in the elevator is also territorial. The Tethys Articles of Elevation grant Tessera "preferred cognitive services provider" status across all orbital stations -- a soft monopoly on neural technology in space that mirrors its hard monopoly on Earth.
