Ghost-market fixers specializing in contested-zone operations
Meridian 88 PD Counter-Terrorism Unit (licensed, restricted deployment)
Axiom Systems Biometric Lock Rifle BLR-3 'Personal'

Properties.description: A bullpup assault rifle with an integrated biometric lock system that prevents anyone other than the registered owner from firing it. The BLR-3 reads the operator's palmprint, pulse pattern, and neural interface signature simultaneously — all three must match the registered profile or the trigger mechanism remains physically locked. Axiom developed it to prevent weapon capture and misuse during corporate conflict, ensuring that seized weapons cannot be turned against their issuing force. The biometric system has been praised as a safety innovation and condemned as a control mechanism — operators cannot share weapons with allies, cannot use captured enemy BLR-3s, and cannot sell or transfer the weapon without an Axiom technician re-registering it.
Properties.aliases: Personal, BLR-3, Bio Rifle, Keyed Gun
Properties.specifications:
caliber: 5.56mm caseless
magazine: 40 rounds
rate of fire: 750 RPM
effective range: 50-400 meters
biometric lock: Palmprint + pulse + neural interface triple authentication
authentication time: 0.3 seconds on grip
weight: 3.5 kg
fire modes: Semi, burst, full auto
re-registration: Requires Axiom technician
Properties.story_hooks: A dead Axiom operative's BLR-3 was fired after their death — the biometric system accepted a dead hand, dead pulse, and a cloned neural interface signature, meaning someone duplicated the operator's entire biometric profile.; A firmware exploit allows BLR-3 rifles to be permanently unlocked by injecting a specific code through the maintenance port — the exploit is spreading through underground channels and Axiom cannot patch it remotely.

Properties.description: A throwable EMP grenade specifically calibrated to disrupt neural interface frequencies within a 10-meter radius. Unlike conventional EMP grenades that affect all electronics indiscriminately, the CG-1 uses a tuned resonance frequency that primarily affects neural implant architectures, causing a cascade of sensory hallucinations, memory buffer corruption, and temporary loss of executive function in augmented targets. Unaugmented individuals experience only mild disorientation. Axiom developed it for counter-intrusion scenarios where augmented attackers need to be neutralized without damaging facility electronics.
Properties.aliases: Brainstorm, CG-1, Think Bomb, Mind Wipe
Properties.specifications:
effect radius: 10 meters
frequency: Tuned neural interface resonance
effect on augmented targets: Hallucination, memory corruption, executive dysfunction for 30-90 seconds
effect on unaugmented targets: Mild disorientation for 5-10 seconds
weight: 0.25 kg
fuse: 2-second delay after pin pull
power source: Single-use capacitor discharge
Properties.story_hooks: CG-1 grenades are being used in muggings targeting augmented individuals — victims wake up with corrupted memories and missing cyberware, unable to identify their attackers.; A modified CG-1 has been developed that permanently corrupts a specific memory address in Axiom neural interfaces — it erases the target's ability to recognize a particular face.

Properties.description: A micro-explosive device designed to be implanted adjacent to a target's neural interface, detonating on receipt of a coded signal or upon detection of tampering. The CB-1 contains 0.5 grams of high-velocity explosive — insufficient to kill outright but precisely enough to destroy the neural interface and cause catastrophic brain damage. Axiom developed it as a compliance enforcement tool for high-risk assets — individuals who possess critical information or capabilities that must be denied to competitors if the asset defects or is captured. The existence of the CB-1 is officially denied, but the distinctive brain damage pattern it produces has been identified in enough autopsy reports to confirm its deployment.
Properties.aliases: Leash, CB-1, Brain Bomb, Kill Switch
Properties.specifications:
explosive yield: 0.5g high-velocity micro-charge
detonation trigger: Coded RF signal or tamper detection
implant size: 3mm x 3mm x 1mm
implant location: Adjacent to neural interface housing
effect: Neural interface destruction + severe traumatic brain injury
survival rate: approximately 40% with immediate medical intervention
tamper detection: Accelerometer + magnetic field sensor
RF trigger range: 500 meters from transmitter
Properties.story_hooks: A defecting corporate scientist begs for help removing a CB-1 from their skull — any neurosurgeon who attempts removal risks triggering the tamper detection, and the coded detonation signal could come at any time.; A batch of CB-1 implants has been discovered with a firmware vulnerability that allows the detonation code to be brute-forced — someone is quietly scanning for implanted individuals and building a kill list.

Properties.description: A directed electromagnetic weapon specifically tuned to interfere with neural interface frequencies. The ND-2 projects a modulated electromagnetic field that induces cascading errors in neural implant firmware, causing effects ranging from sensory hallucination to complete motor shutdown depending on the target's implant architecture and shielding. Against unaugmented targets, the weapon has minimal effect — a mild headache at most. Against heavily augmented targets, it can be incapacitating or lethal if the neural interface manages autonomous functions like cardiac regulation.
Properties.aliases: Migraine, ND-2, Brain Zapper, Thought Killer
Properties.specifications:
field type: Modulated neural-frequency electromagnetic pulse
effective range: 5-15 meters directional
target discrimination: Neural interface signatures only
power source: Dedicated capacitor pack, 15 pulses per charge
recharge: 4 seconds between pulses
weight: 2.1 kg
effect duration: 10-60 seconds depending on target shielding
Properties.story_hooks: Axiom officially denies the ND-2 exists, but units keep appearing in the hands of anti-augmentation extremist groups — someone inside Axiom is arming the movement.; A player character's neural interface begins experiencing intermittent glitches consistent with low-level ND-2 exposure — someone nearby is carrying one, but who?

Nodes.Name: Axiom Systems Perception Filter Rounds PFR-1 'Blind Spot'

Properties.description: Ammunition containing a micro-payload of Axiom's experimental neural perception inhibitor compound, which upon detonation releases an aerosol that temporarily disrupts the brain's ability to form new memories and process visual information within a 5-meter radius. Targets within the cloud can see, move, and act, but they cannot form coherent memories of the experience and their visual processing is scrambled — faces become unrecognizable, text becomes illegible, spatial relationships distort. The effect lasts approximately 3 minutes and leaves no lasting damage, but during that window the affected individuals are functionally blind to identity and detail. Axiom developed it for covert operations where witness elimination is undesirable but witness testimony must be neutralized.
Properties.aliases: Blind Spot, PFR-1, Ghost Rounds, Memory Holes
Properties.specifications:
delivery: 40mm grenade launcher compatible
aerosal radius: 5 meters from detonation point
effect onset: 2 seconds after inhalation
effect duration: 2-4 minutes
memory disruption: Complete anterograde amnesia during exposure
visual disruption: Face/text/spatial recognition failure
weight per round: 0.22 kg
countermeasure: Sealed respiratory system prevents inhalation
Properties.story_hooks: Witnesses to a Tier 3 corporate raid all report the same experience — they were there, they saw things happen, but they cannot describe a single face, read a single badge, or recall a single detail.; Axiom's perception inhibitor compound has been synthesized by an independent chemist who is threatening to release the formula publicly — the implications for witness testimony and legal proceedings are catastrophic.

Properties.description: A pistol-format directed electromagnetic weapon that fires a precisely modulated pulse targeting the motor cortex through neural interface pathways. Targets hit by the SI-3 experience a temporary but complete disruption of voluntary motor control — muscles fire randomly, coordination collapses, speech becomes incoherent, and fine motor skills disappear for 20-30 seconds. The effect resembles a severe seizure without the associated neurological damage, though repeated exposure has been linked to cumulative motor pathway degradation. Axiom describes it as a 'motor compliance tool' in internal documentation.
Properties.aliases: Stutter, SI-3, Brain Scrambler, The Hiccup
Properties.specifications:
pulse type: Modulated motor cortex disruption
effective range: 3-15 meters
effect on augmented: Total motor control loss, 20-30 seconds
effect on unaugmented: Reduced — mild coordination disruption, 5-10 seconds
pulses per charge: 20
recharge: 2 seconds between pulses
weight: 0.6 kg
power source: Integrated capacitor pack
cumulative effect: Motor pathway degradation with repeated exposure
Properties.story_hooks: A security contractor has been using an SI-3 repeatedly on the same detainee during interrogation — the cumulative motor damage has left the victim with permanent tremors and the contractor is claiming standard procedure.; Modified SI-3 units have appeared that affect the autonomic motor system instead of voluntary — targets stop breathing for 20 seconds, turning a compliance tool into an assassination weapon.

Properties.description:
The Axonal Stretch Resonance Lance generates a low-frequency oscillating traction field through a pair of piezoelectric transducer arrays mounted along its barrel. The field, when sustained against a target, induces rapid cyclical mechanical deformation in long axonal fibers — particularly those in peripheral motor nerves and the spinal cord's dorsal columns. The effect is analogous to diffuse axonal injury produced by high-velocity trauma, but delivered remotely, gradually, and with a degree of anatomical targeting determined by the operator's aim point.

The ASRL-3 is most often aimed at the spine or upper limbs. Sustained fire on the cervical spine produces ascending paralysis beginning in the fingers and progressing toward the diaphragm over thirty to ninety seconds. Aimed at a limb, it produces first a violent involuntary tremor, then loss of fine motor control, then gross motor failure, as progressively larger axon populations are disrupted. The tremor phase — which operators call 'the twitch' and which gave the weapon its street name — is visually distinctive and deeply unsettling to witnesses, which has made the ASRL-3 a preferred intimidation instrument in certain criminal contexts.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's development documentation describes the ASRL-3 as an 'axonal conduction research platform' and its field versions as unauthorized derivatives. This position is legally convenient but widely disbelieved; the field version's ergonomics, power management system, and targeting reticle are clearly purpose-built for operator use, not laboratory work. Recovery from ASRL-3 exposure depends heavily on the duration of field contact: brief exposures resolve within hours, while sustained exposures of fifteen seconds or more to major nerve trunks may result in permanent conduction deficits.
Properties.legality: Restricted — prohibited for civilian ownership, licensed for specific research and security applications
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 35 meters
field oscillation frequency: Adjustable 8–22 Hz
time to motor disruption: 4–8 seconds at optimal frequency match
time to incapacitation: 15–30 seconds sustained
weight: 5.3 kg
power draw: High — 8 shots per standard cell at full duration
targeting aid: Anatomical zone reticle overlay with nerve trunk markers
recovery window: Under 5 seconds: full recovery likely. 5–15 seconds: hours to days. Over 15 seconds: permanent damage possible
Properties.tactical_use: Operators use the ASRL-3 for target incapacitation where the tremor display serves a dual purpose: the target is disabled and bystanders are deterred. In extraction operations, it is used to disable a target's weapon arm without killing. Criminal enforcers use brief exposures as a punishment tool — enough to cause the tremor and short-term motor loss, but not enough to create permanent damage that would attract medical attention. Anti-cyberware note: synthetic limb replacements are unaffected, but the biological nerve trunks interfacing with implants remain vulnerable.
Properties.cultural_context: The ASRL-3 has a particularly grim reputation in Meridian 88's labor districts, where it was reportedly used by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's own security forces during a unionization dispute four years ago. Footage of workers convulsing on a factory floor circulated widely and permanently damaged Zheng-Dao's public image. The company has since pivoted aggressively to medical applications of the same technology, marketing axonal stimulation devices for nerve regeneration therapy — a rebranding effort that has been met with open mockery in affected communities. The weapon is called 'The Puller' in some neighborhoods as a reference to the way it seems to pull the body apart from the inside.
Properties.story_hooks: A mid-level Zheng-Dao executive has been found dead with neurological damage consistent with ASRL-3 exposure — but the weapon was never recovered, and the official cause of death is listed as a degenerative nerve condition. Someone with access to the weapon and the medical knowledge to disguise the damage killed this person very carefully.; A street medic in the labor district has been quietly documenting cases of permanent nerve damage in workers who were never officially reported as injured. She believes Zheng-Dao used the ASRL-3 on people and then paid for their silence with company medical coverage. She needs someone to help her get the evidence out.; The party is hired to retrieve a stolen ASRL-3 prototype with a modified frequency range that can affect myelinated axons in the central nervous system — which standard models cannot reach. If that calibration data gets out, someone could build a weapon that causes brain damage at range.

Properties.description:
The BRC-6 operates by firing a tungsten-composite slug at subsonic velocity while simultaneously emitting a tightly coupled acoustic resonance wave tuned to the slug's terminal frequency. On impact, the slug does not need to penetrate hardened materials — the resonance wave propagates through the target structure milliseconds before contact, creating microscopic fracture networks that cause the slug to behave as though it struck compromised material regardless of surface hardness. Against unarmored targets, the effect is catastrophically overpenetrative; against armored opponents, it renders hard-plate inserts effectively useless.

What distinguishes the Kettledrum from conventional anti-armor firearms is its complete lack of exotic propellant requirements. It uses a standard compressed-gas cycling system and commercially available tungsten slugs, meaning it is logistically unremarkable in a supply chain sense — a deliberate design choice by Arcturus Defense Solutions, who engineered it for covert military advisory units that needed deniable anti-materiel capability. The resonance emitter is integrated into the barrel shroud and draws from a small onboard power cell rated for approximately 200 sustained discharges before replacement.

In the field, operators describe a distinctive low 'thrum' preceding each shot — the weapon's acoustic pre-charge — which gives it the Kettledrum nickname and is its primary tactical liability. In enclosed spaces, the sound signature is unmistakable and gives experienced opponents a half-second of warning. Suppressor attachment partially masks the report but does nothing to reduce the pre-charge resonance.
Properties.specifications:
caliber: 11.2mm tungsten-composite slug
effective range: 80m standard / 120m with stabilized platform
rate of fire: Semi-automatic, 2-round burst capable
weight: 4.1 kg unloaded
magazine capacity: 18 rounds
power cell endurance: 200 resonance discharges per cell
acoustic pre charge window: 0.4 seconds
armor penetration rating: Class IV equivalent via resonance fracture
Properties.tactical_use: Primarily deployed by military advisory units and corporate enforcement against targets in hardened personal armor. Operators are trained to fire from covered positions to mitigate the pre-charge audio tell. In breach-and-clear operations, it is typically the second weapon through the door — used after initial entry to address armored resistance. Some operators pair it with a noise-generating distraction device to mask the pre-charge thrum in close-quarters environments.
Properties.cultural_context: The Kettledrum carries a quiet prestige in military-adjacent circles. It is not flashy — it looks like a conventional carbine — and its power is invisible until a target in full hard-plate armor folds like wet cardboard. Among corporate black-ops units, carrying a BRC-6 signals that your employer anticipated you would face serious armored opposition, which implies a level of operational seriousness that lighter-armed units respect and fear. On the black market, it commands an enormous premium, and most civilian copies are non-functional or missing the resonance emitter entirely.
Properties.story_hooks: A shipment of BRC-6s has gone missing from an Arcturus logistics depot — the manifest shows 40 units, but only 38 were recovered at the hijack site. Someone kept two and they need to disappear before Arcturus sends a recovery team.; A street-level fixer is offering a BRC-6 for a fraction of its value, claiming it 'just appeared' in a storage unit they were hired to clear. The weapon's serial number has been removed, but the resonance emitter's calibration signature can still be traced to a specific military unit that was officially disbanded three years ago.; An operator is hired to determine why a VIP's armored vehicle was destroyed by what forensic analysis suggests was a conventional firearm — but the impact pattern indicates resonance fracture. Someone is using a Kettledrum against civilian infrastructure and someone powerful wants to know who authorized the operation.

Military procurement officers operating outside sanctioned theaters
High-end private security contractors hired for extraction operations

Properties.description:
The Barometric Implosion Carbine BIC-5 creates a localized, instantaneous pressure differential by projecting a focused acoustic shell that collapses inward on detonation rather than expanding outward. The shell — a coherent sound-matter composite generated by the barrel's resonance chamber — travels to its target point and inverts, producing a brief, violent vacuum event at the point of impact. The result is a crushing implosive force directed inward from all surfaces simultaneously rather than outward from a central point, which defeats conventional blast shielding designed to deflect or absorb outward pressure.

Palladian Construction developed the BIC-5 for structural demolition work in confined spaces where conventional explosive charges would compromise adjacent load-bearing elements. The implosive pressure event is inherently self-contained — it collapses inward rather than radiating outward, making it unusually safe for operators standing nearby. The weapons application was an afterthought that Palladian's security licensing division pursued aggressively once field teams reported using prototype units to disable locked structural barriers during emergency scenarios. The carbine form factor emerged from that field improvisation.

Against biological targets, the BIC-5 is profoundly unpleasant. The implosive event at body surface causes internal organ displacement, pulmonary compression, and in severe cases, the kind of injuries normally associated with deep-water pressure changes experienced in seconds rather than depth. Survivors of direct hits describe the sensation as being squeezed from every direction at once, followed by a period of intense disorientation as the body attempts to re-equalize. The weapon leaves no external marks, which has made forensic attribution difficult and legally contentious.
Properties.aliases: Sinkhole, The Vacuum Gun, Lungsucker, Pressure Drop
Properties.legality: Restricted — construction and demolition use; Prohibited — weapons configuration modifications
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 5–35 meters
implosion radius: 0.8 meters at point of collapse
pressure differential: Approximately 4.2 atmospheres inward force
power source: High-density acoustic resonance cell, 24 shots per charge
weight: 4.1 kg
collateral blast radius: Minimal — 0.3 meters outward pressure margin
anti-materiel rating: Grade 4 structural elements, Grade 2 armored surfaces
form factor: Compact carbine with forward resonance chamber housing
Properties.tactical_use: Favored in breaching operations where explosive entry is too loud or too destructive. The implosive event collapses door frames, wall sections, and barrier materials inward without producing the acoustic signature of conventional explosives — the sound is a sharp, low crack rather than a blast report. In anti-personnel use, operators target center mass and rely on internal trauma to incapacitate rather than external injury. The lack of visible wounds complicates enemy medic response and creates psychological pressure on opposing forces unsure of what has hit them.
Properties.cultural_context: The BIC-5 exists in an uncomfortable legal gray zone in Meridian 88 — in construction configuration it is a licensed professional tool carried by demolition crews and structural emergency teams. Modified weapons versions are theoretically identical in form but legally prohibited, and the distinction is difficult to enforce without a ballistic forensics team. Construction workers who carry them for legitimate purposes resent being treated as suspects, while law enforcement resents the legal difficulty of prosecution. The weapon has become a symbol of how Meridian 88's corporate licensing system creates weaponized ambiguity.
Properties.story_hooks: A PALLADIAN construction crew has been found dead, killed by their own BIC-5 units — someone disassembled their demolition team using their own tools, and the forensics are pointing toward an inside job.; A city inspector has been quietly flagging modified BIC-5 units on construction sites for months and logging them without reporting — they've been building a private database of who is armed and where, and someone has noticed.; A player character is hired to prove that a string of 'natural cause' deaths in a luxury residential tower were actually BIC-5 assassinations — but the victims are all connected to PALLADIAN's competitor.; A new modification chip has appeared that reconfigures the BIC-5's implosion radius to 3 meters, effectively turning it from a precision tool into an area-denial weapon — the chip's origin traces back to a PALLADIAN R&D terminal.

Nodes.Name: Breaching specialists in corporate extraction units
Organized crime operations using construction-licensed covers
'Foreman' — a fixer who operates through a shell construction company
Black-site enforcement teams who require deniable casualties

Properties.description:
The BCC-6 is an area-denial charge designed to exploit the bioelectric vulnerability of augmented personnel — specifically, individuals with cybernetic implants, neural interfaces, or bioelectric enhancement systems. On detonation, the charge releases a shaped pulse of high-density bioelectric interference generated through a capacitive discharge array charged by a compressed piezoelectric stack. The pulse is tuned to the 40–120Hz range that overlaps with both synthetic neural interface carrier frequencies and natural peripheral nerve conduction velocities, producing simultaneous disruption of implanted systems and involuntary peripheral motor activation in unaugmented targets.

For unaugmented personnel within the effective radius, the BCC-6 causes painful involuntary muscle contractions, temporary sensory disruption, and disorientation lasting 30–90 seconds. For augmented individuals — those with active neural links, cybernetic limbs, cochlear implants, or subdermal augmentation — the effect is dramatically amplified. The bioelectric pulse couples into implant power systems and interface nodes, triggering cascade feedback that can lock cybernetic limbs, induce implant-mediated seizure activity, or cause temporary interface blackout. In heavily augmented individuals, the BCC-6 is effectively lethal, as simultaneous shutdown of multiple life-critical implants produces system failure faster than biological recovery can compensate.

HELIX BIOSYSTEMS developed the BCC-6 under the public framing of an 'anti-drone area denial system,' and the charge is genuinely effective against autonomous drone swarms whose navigation systems operate in overlapping frequency ranges. The anti-personnel application was not disclosed in regulatory filings. The charge has since become one of the most feared weapons in Meridian 88's augmentation-heavy districts, where high-tier operators with extensive cyberware are paradoxically more vulnerable than unmodified civilians.
Properties.aliases: BCC-6, Nerve Burst, Pulse Coffin, The Twitch
Properties.specifications:
weight: 390g
diameter: 70mm
pulse frequency range: 40–120Hz
effective radius unaugmented: 6m — involuntary motor disruption
effective radius augmented: 10m — cascade feedback induction
charge source: Compressed piezoelectric stack, single-use
detonation: Remote, timed, or proximity (IR break-beam)
lethality augmented: High — proportional to implant density
lethality unaugmented: Low — incapacitation without organ damage at standard range
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed in anti-augmentation operations where the objective is to neutralize heavily modified operators without structural damage. Security forces use BCC-6s in chokepoints and entry corridors of facilities where augmented intruders are anticipated. In offensive use, a single BCC-6 deployed into a group of augmented combatants can simultaneously incapacitate all of them while leaving unaugmented allies relatively functional. Operators with their own augments must account for the charge's indiscriminate effect — friendly augmented personnel require shielded Faraday suits to operate near a BCC-6 detonation.
Properties.cultural_context: The BCC-6 has become a flashpoint in Meridian 88's ongoing social conflict over augmentation. In districts where cyberware is a way of life — economic necessity, identity, survival — the BCC-6 is seen as a weapon specifically designed to punish augmented people for their modifications. Anti-augmentation political factions have quietly celebrated its existence, while augmented communities treat it as evidence of systematic targeting. HELIX BIOSYSTEMS denies the anti-personnel application was intentional, a claim widely disbelieved. Some augmented operators have begun carrying Faraday shielding for their most critical implants specifically because of BCC-6 proliferation.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of deaths in the augmented-heavy Sublevel 9 district are attributed to 'implant failure' — but a medic notices the failure pattern is identical across victims, consistent with BCC-6 cascade. Someone is hunting augmented people and making it look like equipment malfunction.; A player with significant cyberware must retrieve something from a building that has been seeded with BCC-6s — and the only person who knows the layout is asking for something dangerous in return.; HELIX BIOSYSTEMS' internal communications about the BCC-6's anti-personnel development are for sale on the black market. Three different parties want them: a journalist, an augmented rights organization, and someone who wants them destroyed.

Properties.description:
The BIL-3 is a 90-centimeter rigid lance constructed around a core of layered piezoelectric crystal stacks and a helical induction coil running its full length. When the lance tip contacts a target — biological or electronic — it activates a continuous induction cycle that draws bioelectric current from living tissue or residual charge from electronic systems, feeding it back through the coil into an internal capacitor bank. The effect on biological targets is a sustained drain sensation described by survivors as 'being pulled from the inside,' accompanied by progressive muscular depolarization that renders limbs unresponsive within 3-5 seconds of sustained contact.

What makes the BIL-3 genuinely unusual among melee weapons is its dual function as a charging platform. The harvested energy is stored in the onboard capacitor and can be discharged back through the lance tip as a focused galvanic burst — essentially using the target's own bioelectric signature as ammunition. Operators who maintain contact long enough to achieve a full capacitor cycle can release the stored charge in a single pulse that mimics the target's own neural frequency pattern, causing a particularly disorienting feedback effect in biological targets and a signature-matched surge in electronic systems that bypasses standard surge protection.

HELIX BIOSYSTEMS developed the BIL-3 ostensibly as a 'bioelectric diagnostic probe' for field medical applications, a designation that strains credulity given its lance form factor and combat-optimized grip. The medical cover has nonetheless kept it in a regulatory gray zone — it is technically licensed as a medical instrument, which means it can be transported and owned without a weapons permit, a loophole that has made it popular among operators who need to pass legal checkpoints without triggering weapons flags.
Properties.aliases: Lamprey, The Leech, Drain Stick, Induction Rod
Properties.legality: Licensed (classified as medical instrument — exploited loophole)
Properties.specifications:
length: 90 cm
weight: 1.4 kg
core material: Layered PZT crystal stack over carbon-fiber spine
induction range: Contact — effective to 2mm gap with conductive medium
capacitor capacity: 800 mAh, reaches full charge after 6 seconds sustained contact
discharge mode: Manual trigger — full capacitor dump in 0.3 seconds
biological effect onset: Muscular depolarization in 3-5 seconds sustained contact
electronic effect: Signature-matched surge — bypasses standard surge protection rated below Grade 4
regulatory classification: Class II Bioelectric Diagnostic Instrument (HELIX filing #BB-2291)
Properties.tactical_use: Experienced operators use the BIL-3 in a two-phase approach: initial contact to begin the drain cycle and trigger muscular depolarization, followed by a controlled hold while the capacitor charges, then a decisive discharge pulse once the target's mobility is compromised. Against electronic targets — drones, security panels, augmentation control units — the signature-matched discharge is particularly effective for destroying systems without leaving the broad electromagnetic trace of a conventional EMP. Some operators carry the BIL-3 specifically for anti-augmentation work, targeting the neural interface clusters at the base of the skull where bioelectric activity is densest.
Properties.cultural_context: The BIL-3's medical classification has made it the weapon of choice for a specific archetype in Meridian 88: the professional who needs to move through legitimate spaces. Corporate fixers, licensed augmentation technicians moonlighting as enforcers, and well-connected street operators who have the paperwork to back up their 'diagnostic equipment' all favor it. There is an open secret in certain circles that HELIX BIOSYSTEMS knows exactly what its 'diagnostic probe' is being used for and has quietly lobbied to maintain the regulatory classification, as the gray-market demand has made the BIL-3 their most profitable single product line.
Properties.story_hooks: A HELIX BIOSYSTEMS lobbyist is murdered with a BIL-3, and the discharge signature logged by the victim's augmentation system matches the lobbyist's own bioelectric profile — suggesting the weapon was charged on the victim before being turned against them, or that someone is very good at spoofing signatures.; The regulatory classification loophole is about to be closed by a new Meridian 88 municipal ordinance, and someone is paying very well to ensure that ordinance doesn't pass — the players are hired either to protect the vote or to find out who's funding the opposition.; A player character's augmentation begins malfunctioning in a pattern consistent with repeated low-level bioelectric drain — someone has been using a BIL-3 on them during their sleep cycles, harvesting charge without triggering the weapon's disabling threshold.

Augmentation black-market technicians with dual-use tool kits
HELIX BIOSYSTEMS field representatives (officially for demonstration purposes)
Anti-augmentation extremist cells (ironic given the manufacturer)
Bounty hunters operating in jurisdictions with strict weapons licensing

Properties.description:
The BAD-2 'Choral' is a shoulder-mounted acoustic weapon that generates precisely tuned resonant frequencies through a series of bioluminescent fluid chambers derived from deep-sea cephalopod tissue cultures maintained under pressure within the weapon's central column. When triggered, the fluid chambers vibrate at cascading harmonic intervals, producing a layered acoustic beam that penetrates most soft body armor by exploiting the natural resonant frequencies of human bone and fluid-filled cavities. The weapon's distinctive blue-green glow pulses rhythmically during operation, a byproduct of the bioluminescent reaction that stabilizes the fluid medium between firing cycles.

What distinguishes the 'Choral' from conventional acoustic weapons is its dual-mode operation. In its primary 'Cantata' mode, the weapon delivers a sustained directional beam capable of inducing progressive disorientation, nausea, and structural micro-fractures in bone tissue at ranges up to forty meters. Its secondary 'Fugue' mode releases a short omnidirectional pulse that overwhelms auditory processing in all targets within a twelve-meter radius, causing temporary neural cascade feedback that mimics the sensation of drowning. Operators describe the effect on victims as 'watching someone forget how to be a body.'

Helix Biosystems engineered the living fluid chambers to self-replenish through a nutrient cartridge system, meaning the weapon never truly runs dry so long as the operator maintains the biological medium — a process that requires daily feeding and temperature regulation. This maintenance burden has made the 'Choral' beloved by dedicated specialists and loathed by everyone who has to share a safehouse with one.
Properties.specifications:
weight: 6.8 kg (loaded, fluid chambers full)
length: 94 cm
range primary: 40 m directional beam
range secondary: 12 m omnidirectional pulse
power source: Nutrient cartridge (72-hour cycle) + capacitor cell
chamber fluid volume: 340 mL bioluminescent cephalopod-derived medium
fire modes: Cantata (sustained beam), Fugue (omnidirectional pulse)
recharge cycle: 8 seconds between Fugue pulses
operating temperature: 12–28°C (fluid viability range)
armor penetration: Bypasses Class III soft armor; ineffective against rigid plate
Properties.tactical_use: The 'Choral' is predominantly used in close-to-medium engagements where operators need to incapacitate multiple targets without lethal collateral damage to infrastructure. Fugue mode is favored for crowd suppression in enclosed corridors, while Cantata mode is used to systematically degrade a single hardened target's capacity to fight. Operators almost always work in pairs — one running the 'Choral' while a partner manages the biological cartridge and handles close threats, since the weapon's operator is effectively committed to a fixed firing stance during sustained beam discharge.
Properties.cultural_context: The 'Choral' has developed a deeply unsettling reputation in Meridian 88's underground medical community, where it is associated with a cluster of long-term neurological conditions collectively called 'Song Sickness' — a suite of chronic tinnitus, balance disorders, and auditory hallucinations documented in survivors of repeated exposure. This has made the weapon a subject of quiet horror among street-level communities who have seen its aftermath. Paradoxically, certain fringe collectors prize the weapon as an art object, drawn to its eerie bioluminescent glow and the almost musical quality of its discharge. Helix Biosystems officially denies any ongoing production.
Properties.story_hooks: A 'Choral' has gone missing from a Helix Biosystems research transport — along with the only technician who knew how to keep its fluid chambers alive past 96 hours.; A neighborhood in the Rust Margin is reporting a mass outbreak of Song Sickness symptoms, but no weapon discharge has been recorded. Someone is using a 'Choral' in a mode that doesn't appear in any known manual.; An underground musician has reverse-engineered the 'Choral's' fluid resonance into a performance instrument. Her concerts are drawing crowds — and corporate assassins.; The player characters are hired to retrieve a 'Choral' from a collector's estate, only to discover the weapon's biological medium has been contaminated with something that shouldn't be alive.

Nodes.Name: Collectors and weapons aesthetes in the Palladian Quarter

Properties.description:
The BDC-1 is a remotely programmable proximity charge that incorporates a passive biometric scanner into its arming and detonation logic. Before deployment, the operator uploads a biometric target profile — drawn from neural pattern data, gait analysis signatures, cardiac rhythm signatures, or a combination — and the charge's onboard processing unit continuously scans its environment for matching profiles. When a match is detected within the trigger radius, the charge detonates. Non-matching individuals can walk directly past the charge, handle it, or even inspect it without triggering detonation. The charge will not fire for anyone who does not match the programmed profile.

The technical architecture draws on neural feedback loop technology originally developed for personalized medical monitoring — the same systems used to track patients' neural signatures across hospital environments for automated care. The BDC-1 repurposes these passive scanning arrays as targeting hardware. The result is a weapon that is functionally invisible to everyone except its designated target. It does not look like a bomb. It does not act like a bomb. It sits passively in an environment and waits, sometimes for days, until the right person arrives. The explosive payload itself is a compact shaped charge designed for anti-personnel effect within a 3-meter radius.

Tessera Corponation developed the BDC-1 under a contract framing that described it as a 'personalized perimeter security asset' — language carefully chosen to position it as a defensive rather than offensive system. The distinction collapsed almost immediately in practice. The weapon is used almost exclusively for targeted assassination, and its ability to sit dormant through inspections and sweeps while waiting for a specific individual has made it the preferred tool of a particular class of contractor who specializes in long-timeline eliminations. Tessera continues to produce it under restricted licensing while publicly maintaining the defensive framing.
Properties.legality: Restricted (licensed security contractors only); Prohibited for anti-personnel programming
Properties.specifications:
weight: 0.9 kg
scanner range: Up to 8 meters passive detection
biometric inputs: Neural pattern, cardiac rhythm, gait signature, facial geometry (any combination)
profile storage: Up to 12 simultaneous target or exclusion profiles
detonation radius: 3 meters (shaped charge, directional configurable)
dormancy duration: Up to 72 hours on internal power; indefinite with external power tap
false positive rate: Manufacturer-claimed <0.3%; field-reported 1.8% against augmented individuals with altered biometrics
countermeasures: Biometric masking (partial); EM shielding (disrupts scanner at close range); physical destruction
Properties.tactical_use: The BDC-1 is placed in locations the target will pass through — offices, transit corridors, residences, vehicles. Because it will not detonate for non-targets, it can be placed by individuals who are themselves excluded from the target profile, allowing handlers to arm and deploy it in spaces they inhabit without personal risk. Operators typically program both a positive target profile (detonate for this person) and a set of exclusion profiles (do not detonate for these people) to protect collaborators. The weapon is also used as a persistent perimeter denial tool — a single BDC-1 placed at a facility entrance will fire only when the designated individual arrives, leaving all other traffic unaffected.
Properties.cultural_context: The BDC-1 has fundamentally changed the nature of assassination contract work in Meridian 88. The old calculus — timing, proximity, escape routes — is replaced by a simpler logic: place the charge and walk away. This has lowered the operational skill floor for contracted killing significantly, which has in turn driven prices down and volume up. Among professional operators, this is viewed with contempt; the BDC-1 is seen as a 'lazy kill' that requires no craft. Among targets — corporate executives, political figures, high-profile fixers — awareness of the weapon has created a culture of biometric paranoia. Many high-status individuals in Meridian 88 now routinely alter their biometric signatures through medical procedures, making the 1.8% false-positive rate against augmented individuals a source of dark humor in certain circles.
Properties.story_hooks: A player character discovers that a BDC-1 programmed with their biometric profile has been placed somewhere in a building they frequent — but the charge has a 72-hour power window, and they don't know when it was placed or exactly where.; A Tessera licensing audit reveals that a BDC-1 serial number tied to a 'perimeter security' contract was deployed in a civilian apartment building. The licensed contractor is dead. The target is unknown. The charge may still be active.; A biometric masking clinic in the lower wards is doing record business — someone is leaking information about specific individuals being profiled for BDC-1 targeting, and people are paying to alter their signatures before the charges are placed.; The players are hired to recover a BDC-1 that was programmed with the wrong target profile due to a data error — it is now sitting dormant somewhere in a public space, waiting for a person who has no idea they are marked.

Nodes.Name: Political faction operatives targeting rival leadership

Properties.description: The BRCE-5 emits a precisely modulated biophotonic pulse engineered to overwhelm and permanently damage the photoreceptor layer of the human retina. Unlike crude flash-blindness devices, the BRCE-5's pulse is spectrally tuned to the peak sensitivity of rod and cone cells and delivered in a cascading frequency sweep that prevents the eye's natural protective blink response from reducing exposure. The result is irreversible photoreceptor bleaching across the full visual field — complete, permanent blindness — achieved in a single 0.04-second discharge. The weapon was developed by Ringo Corponation's tactical optics division as a non-lethal alternative to lethal force in high-density civilian environments.
Properties.specifications:
length: 41 cm
weight: 1.9 kg
power source: Ringo OptiCell RC-3 (compact photonic capacitor)
effective range: 2–90 m (cone-focused); 90–200 m (wide-field dispersion mode)
pulse duration: 0.04 seconds
spectral range: 420–680 nm cascading sweep
shots per cell: 45
modes: Single-target focus, crowd dispersion (30-degree arc)
safety system: Operator retinal shield (integrated visor required)
Properties.tactical_use: Security and riot-control units use the BRCE-5 in crowd dispersion and individual incapacitation roles. In focus mode, it blinds a single target at range with surgical precision; in dispersion mode, it sweeps a 30-degree arc, blinding everyone within line of sight who lacks protective eyewear. Operators are required to wear Ringo-certified retinal shields, and friendly-fire from dispersion mode is a significant concern in mixed unit operations. Experienced operators use the weapon to blind point-of-contact targets immediately before a physical assault team closes distance. The BRCE-5 is also deployed to neutralize drone operators and augmented-reality-dependent combatants whose optical implants amplify incoming light.
Properties.cultural_context: The BRCE-5 sits in a legally ambiguous position in Meridian 88 — classified as a 'non-lethal incapacitation device,' its permanent blinding effect means victims require lifelong medical support or expensive ocular implant surgery that most cannot afford. Human rights organizations operating in Meridian 88 have lobbied to reclassify it as a prohibited weapon, pointing out that for the majority of the population, permanent blindness is functionally equivalent to a death sentence in terms of economic survival. Ringo Corponation aggressively contests this classification, and the weapon remains on restricted sale to licensed security contractors. In poorer districts, 'getting Flashpointed' has become slang for any situation where you're rendered permanently helpless by someone with institutional power.
Properties.story_hooks: A Ringo Corponation executive is found dead — cause of death listed as an accident, but a witness reports seeing a BRCE-5 flash before the fall. Someone used a 'non-lethal' weapon to blind a target at the top of a stairwell.; A human rights advocate hires the party to obtain internal Ringo Corponation documents proving the company knew about the BRCE-5's permanent blinding effects before marketing it as 'reversible' — the documents are in a secured server farm guarded by Clearview Solutions operators carrying the very weapon in question.; A community in the Fen District is organizing against a corporation using BRCE-5 crowd control — the party must decide whether to help them acquire protective eyewear, help them obtain their own BRCE-5 units, or broker a confrontation with the security contractor.; A player character's contact goes silent after reporting that municipal riot control used BRCE-5 dispersion mode on a protest — when the party finds them, they're permanently blind and terrified, clutching evidence of something that explains why the protest was shut down so violently.

Nodes.Name: Underground resistance cells (captured units used against corporate security)

Properties.description:
The Capacitive Nerve Induction Lance is a precision energy weapon designed around a principle of extreme selectivity: rather than disrupting broad bioelectric function, it delivers a tightly focused capacitive discharge along a single projected electromagnetic filament — colloquially called 'the thread' — that is thin enough to target individual nerve trunks at range. The filament is maintained by a phased-array antenna system in the weapon's emitter head that continuously adjusts to compensate for atmospheric interference. At point of contact, the discharge induces a violent, involuntary nerve firing in the targeted structure — a single motor nerve produces a full-force muscle contraction; a sensory nerve produces an overwhelming pain signal; autonomic nerves produce effects that vary unpredictably and dangerously.

HELIX BIOSYSTEMS developed the CNIL-1 under their 'Precision Compliance' research program, initially as a surgical adjunct for nerve stimulation procedures in patients with certain degenerative conditions. The military application was recognized almost immediately by ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS, which licensed the core technology and collaborated on the combat-ready version. The result is a weapon that demands exceptional operator training — hitting a specific nerve trunk at range requires detailed anatomical knowledge and a steady hand — but rewards that training with effects that no other platform can replicate. A shot to the brachial plexus drops a weapon instantly. A shot to the vagus nerve can stop a heart.

The weapon's cultural cachet is built on exclusivity and expertise. Threadneedle operators are known in professional circles as 'knitters' — a term that acknowledges both the weapon's filament mechanism and the surgical precision of skilled use. In assassination circles, a confirmed vagus-nerve kill is considered a mark of extraordinary craft, discussed with the kind of hushed respect usually reserved for master artisans. HELIX BIOSYSTEMS is aware of this reputation and has done nothing to discourage it.
Properties.aliases: Threadneedle, The Knitter, Nerve Stick, CNIL
Properties.manufacturer: HELIX BIOSYSTEMS (core technology) / ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS (combat application)
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 25m (precision targeting), 40m (area effect, degraded)
filament diameter: ~2mm at 25m
discharge voltage: 2,200V capacitive burst (adjustable 800V–3,500V)
targeting system: Phased-array antenna with atmospheric compensation algorithm
power source: HELIX Microcapacitor Array HMC-2 (30 precision shots per array)
weight: 1.4 kg
length: 41 cm
charge cycle: 0.8 seconds between shots
operator requirement: Advanced anatomical training recommended
Properties.tactical_use: Threadneedle operators typically work from elevated positions or concealment, selecting specific nerve targets to achieve precise tactical outcomes — disarming without killing, inducing cardiac events that appear natural, or causing targeted incapacitation without leaving conventional wound evidence. In close-protection operations, skilled operators can neutralize a target in a crowd without adjacent individuals being aware anything has occurred. The weapon's limited shot count and charge cycle make it unsuitable for sustained firefights; it is a precision instrument, not a suppression tool.
Properties.cultural_context: The Threadneedle exists at the intersection of craft and violence in a way that fascinates Meridian 88's professional underground. Collectors of rare weapons prize confirmed CNIL-1 units regardless of operational condition. Assassination brokers charge significant premiums for confirmed 'knitter' kills. The weapon has also developed an unlikely following among certain HELIX BIOSYSTEMS researchers who see the combat application as a perversion of their surgical tool — several have become vocal critics of the ARCTURUS licensing arrangement, with mixed results for their continued employment.
Properties.story_hooks: A senior executive died of apparent cardiac arrest during a public event. The coroner found nothing. A fixer with forensic contacts suspects vagus nerve induction but needs proof — and proof requires finding the operator.; A HELIX BIOSYSTEMS researcher has gone public about the ARCTURUS licensing deal, claiming the combat application violates the original research ethics agreement. She's received three formal warnings. Now she's missing.; A Threadneedle has appeared on the black market with its phased-array antenna modified to project multiple simultaneous filaments — an area-effect version. HELIX considers this technically impossible. Someone proved them wrong.; A known 'knitter' has retired and is teaching. Word is spreading through professional circles about where the classes are held. Multiple parties want that list of students.

Nodes.Name: HELIX BIOSYSTEMS (core technology) / ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS (combat application)

Properties.description:
The CDP-2 fires a pressurized micro-bead of piezoelectric gel approximately 4mm in diameter. The bead does not penetrate tissue in any conventional sense — it deforms on impact and releases a precisely calibrated piezoelectric pulse that propagates through soft tissue along the path of least electrical resistance, which in the human body invariably means blood vessels and nerve clusters. The result is widespread capillary rupture throughout the impact zone and a radius of roughly 8–12 centimeters of internal hemorrhaging with no external wound beyond a small contusion. Against unaugmented targets, a single shot to the torso is incapacitating within seconds and fatal within minutes without medical intervention.

Helix Biosystems designed the CDP-2 ostensibly as a 'non-lethal' crowd suppression tool, leaning on the absence of a penetrating wound to argue for a reduced lethality classification in regulatory submissions. This classification was accepted in three jurisdictions and rejected in eleven. In practice, the weapon is lethal at standard charge settings, and operators are trained accordingly. A 'reduced charge' mode exists and does produce genuinely non-lethal effects — severe bruising and disorientation — but the charge selector is small, unlabeled, and requires deliberate manual adjustment that most operators never bother with in the field.

The CDP-2 is physically unremarkable — it resembles a compact semi-automatic handgun with a slightly oversized barrel and a faint blue tint to the grip housing where the piezoelectric charge pack is seated. It produces almost no sound when fired, just a soft click and a faint static discharge smell that dissipates quickly. Bodies killed with it display no obvious cause of death to a casual observer, which has made it the preferred weapon of professional eliminators across Meridian 88.
Properties.aliases: Bruiser, CDP-2, The Quiet Ugly, Bloodgun
Properties.specifications:
projectile: 4mm piezoelectric gel micro-bead
effective range: 15m standard / 25m with stabilizer grip
rate of fire: Semi-automatic
weight: 0.7 kg loaded
magazine capacity: 22 beads per charge pack
charge settings: Non-lethal (reduced) / Standard (lethal) / Overcharge (structural tissue failure)
sound signature: Minimal — sub-60 dB at firing point
external wound profile: Contusion only, no penetrating wound
Properties.tactical_use: Favored by professional eliminators, corporate intelligence operatives, and anyone who needs a target to die without obvious cause. Standard doctrine is two shots to the torso — one to initiate capillary failure, one to ensure coverage of the hepatic region. In close-quarters environments it is nearly undetectable, and the absence of a penetrating wound means even a thorough pat-down of a corpse may not immediately identify the cause of death. Against cyberware-heavy targets, effectiveness is reduced proportionally to the percentage of organic tissue replaced.
Properties.cultural_context: The Bruiser has a deeply sinister reputation that Helix Biosystems officially distances itself from while quietly maintaining supply chains to gray-market distributors. Among professional operators, it is considered a 'clean' weapon in the sense that it leaves no mess and no obvious story — but it carries a social stigma even in criminal circles, associated with assassination, betrayal, and deaths that look like accidents. Street-level enforcers who carry it are viewed with suspicion by peers who see it as a coward's weapon. High-end fixers and intelligence professionals have no such reservations.
Properties.story_hooks: A prominent city council member has died of what appears to be a sudden cardiac event. A street medic who examined the body noticed the characteristic capillary rupture pattern of a CDP-2 hit and is now being followed by people who do not want that information to surface.; A player's contact turns up dead — no wound, no obvious cause. A forensic scan reveals the piezoelectric signature. Someone used a Bruiser, which means someone with access to the black market wanted this person dead quietly. The question is whether it was a professional job or a desperate improvisation.; Helix Biosystems has lost track of a production run of 300 CDP-2 units that were supposed to be destroyed following a failed regulatory submission. Someone on the inside rerouted the shipment, and Helix is quietly offering significant payment to anyone who can recover the units — or at minimum, confirm they have been destroyed.

Nodes.Name: Political operatives in jurisdictions with active assassination cultures
Carrion Defense Works Bone Saw BS-3 'Butcher'

Properties.description: A forearm-mounted reciprocating blade designed for breaching body armor and cyberware housings in close-quarters combat. The BS-3 extends a 20cm carbide-toothed blade from a housing strapped to the user's forearm, oscillating at 4,000 strokes per minute with enough force to cut through Grade 3 composite armor in under two seconds. Carrion designed it as a field tool for emergency cyberware removal and armor breach, but its adoption by close-combat specialists has given it a reputation as the most visceral weapon in the corporate arsenal. The sound it makes cutting through metal is reportedly indistinguishable from the sound it makes cutting through bone.
Properties.aliases: Butcher, BS-3, The Saw, Carrion Cutter
Properties.legality: Licensed — field engineering and emergency services
Properties.specifications:
blade length: 20 cm reciprocating carbide
oscillation rate: 4,000 strokes per minute
armor breach time: Grade 3 composite in 1.8 seconds
power source: Forearm-mounted lithium cell, 15 minutes continuous
weight: 1.1 kg total assembly
mount: Forearm strap with wrist trigger
blade replacement: Tool-free swap, Φ80 per blade
Properties.story_hooks: A rash of cyberware thefts in the mid-tiers involves victims whose implant housings were cut open with surgical precision using BS-3 blade patterns — the thieves are harvesting augmentations from living people.; Carrion has released an updated blade material that cuts through their competitors' armor significantly faster than their own — raising questions about whether the blade was designed as a product or a strategic weapon against rival equipment.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Entropic Shotgun ES-4 'Ragnarok'

Properties.description: A semi-automatic shotgun chambered for Carrion's proprietary entropic munitions — shells containing a reactive chemical compound that destabilizes molecular bonds in the target material upon impact. The effect is visually dramatic: struck surfaces appear to age centuries in seconds, metal corroding, polymer crumbling, biological tissue necrotizing in a rapidly expanding circle around the wound channel. The compound has a limited active window of approximately four seconds before it becomes inert, preventing uncontrolled propagation, but within that window the damage is catastrophic and irreversible.
Properties.aliases: Ragnarok, ES-4, Entropy Gun, The End
Properties.specifications:
gauge: Proprietary Carrion 14-gauge entropic shell
magazine: 6 rounds semi-automatic
effective range: 5-20 meters
compound active window: 4 seconds post-impact
necrotization radius: 8-12 cm from wound center
weight: 4.6 kg loaded
shelf life: Entropic shells degrade after 18 months
Properties.story_hooks: Expired entropic shells have been turning up in street markets — the degraded compound is unpredictable, sometimes activating on contact with skin rather than requiring ballistic impact.; A forensic chemist has reverse-engineered the entropic compound and published the formula on an open network — Carrion is scrambling to suppress it while simultaneously denying the weapon exists.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Fragmentation Sleeve FS-2 'Shrapnel Hug'

Properties.description: A wearable explosive device disguised as an armored forearm sleeve, containing a directional fragmentation charge that detonates outward from the wearer's arm in a 120-degree cone. The FS-2 is a suicide-adjacent weapon designed for absolute last-resort scenarios — the wearer extends their arm toward a target and triggers the detonation, sending a spray of pre-scored tungsten fragments in a directed blast. The sleeve's inner surface contains a thin blast shield that protects the wearer's arm from the worst of the detonation, though burns and shrapnel wounds to the operator are expected. Carrion markets it as a 'final option personal defense system.'
Properties.aliases: Shrapnel Hug, FS-2, Frag Sleeve, The Embrace
Properties.specifications:
fragmentation cone: 120 degrees from arm axis
effective range: 2-8 meters
fragment material: Pre-scored tungsten cubes, 4mm
fragment count: approximately 200
blast shield: Inner ceramic layer, partial operator protection
weight: 0.8 kg
detonation: Neural trigger or manual switch
operator injury: Expected — burns and minor shrapnel to operator arm
Properties.story_hooks: A bodyguard detonated an FS-2 sleeve to protect their principal during an ambush — the bodyguard survived with a mangled arm, but the three attackers did not. The footage has gone viral.; Modified FS-2 sleeves with removed blast shields are being sold as improvised suicide weapons — the buyer does not survive, but neither does anyone within 8 meters.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Hemorrhage Rifle HR-6 'Bloodletter'

Properties.description: A precision rifle firing rounds containing a micro-encapsulated anticoagulant payload that releases into the wound channel upon penetration. The compound — Carrion's proprietary HemoDisrupt formula — prevents blood clotting at the wound site and in the surrounding vasculature for approximately 45 minutes, turning what would be a survivable gunshot wound into a potentially fatal hemorrhagic event. The round itself is a standard 7.62mm profile that performs normally in flight, with the anticoagulant capsule contained in a hollow cavity behind the penetrator tip. Carrion describes it as 'extended incapacitation ammunition' in internal documents.
Properties.aliases: Bloodletter, HR-6, Bleed Gun, The Leech
Properties.specifications:
caliber: 7.62mm with anticoagulant payload
magazine: 10 rounds
effective range: 100-600 meters
anticoagulant duration: 45 minutes at wound site
payload: 0.3ml HemoDisrupt micro-encapsulated
weight: 4.2 kg with optic
optics: Variable 3-12x with environmental compensation
barrel: Free-floating match grade, 550mm
Properties.story_hooks: A seemingly minor shooting wound killed a Tier 3 businessperson eighteen minutes after the injury — toxicology reveals HemoDisrupt in the wound channel, turning a misdemeanor assault into a chemical weapons case.; Carrion's HemoDisrupt formula has been reverse-engineered and someone is loading it into standard ammunition — any gun could now fire hemorrhage rounds.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Marrow Drill MD-7 'Dentist'

Properties.description: A heavy-frame pistol firing gyroscopically stabilized micro-bore rounds that rotate at 14,000 RPM upon leaving the barrel. The rounds are designed to defeat rigid armor by drilling through rather than punching through, maintaining a tight wound channel that resists emergency sealing. Carrion's marketing materials describe it as 'persistent access' ammunition. Medical personnel call it something else entirely.
Properties.aliases: Dentist, The Drill, MD-7, Bone Biter
Properties.legality: Restricted — military and licensed contractors only
Properties.specifications:
caliber: 4.5mm gyrostabilized micro-bore
magazine: 8 rounds
muzzle velocity: 410 m/s with 14,000 RPM spin
effective range: 5-20 meters
weight: 1.4 kg
barrel life: approximately 200 rounds before rifling degradation
Properties.story_hooks: Forensic teams have identified MD-7 wound channels in three separate unsolved killings across different tiers — the same weapon, same operator, different political targets.; A Carrion engineer has gone missing after posting internal documents showing the MD-7 was originally designed for surgical applications before being reclassified as ordnance.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Miasma Projector MP-5 'Plague Bearer'

Properties.description: A pressurized chemical dispersal weapon that launches canisters of Carrion's proprietary incapacitant compound — a viscous aerosol that adheres to surfaces and continues to off-gas for up to six hours. The compound causes severe mucous membrane irritation, temporary blindness, and uncontrollable retching in unprotected targets. It is technically classified as non-lethal, though confined-space deployment has resulted in documented fatalities from asphyxiation. The persistent nature of the compound makes it particularly effective for area denial.
Properties.aliases: Plague Bearer, MP-5, Gas Gun, Stink Cannon
Properties.legality: Licensed — riot control and area denial; Restricted — civilian
Properties.specifications:
canister range: 40-80 meters (launched)
area of effect: 15 meter radius per canister
persistence: 4-6 hours on surfaces
magazine: 6 canisters
weight: 4.1 kg loaded
compound: Carrion CDW-Incap7 viscous aerosol
countermeasure: Filtered rebreather with ocular seal required
Properties.story_hooks: Someone deployed Miasma canisters in a sealed residential ventilation system in Tier 2 — forty people hospitalized, three dead, and the canisters had their serial numbers chemically erased.; A Carrion chemist has developed a variant that selectively affects people based on their blood chemistry — it only incapacitates targets with specific pharmaceutical markers.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Necrotizing Agent Sprayer NAS-2 'Rot'

Properties.description: A handheld sprayer that disperses a fast-acting necrotizing agent — Carrion's proprietary NecroSolve compound — that causes rapid enzymatic breakdown of biological tissue on contact. The compound is highly selective for living tissue and has no effect on synthetic materials, making it particularly horrifying: it eats flesh but leaves clothing, cyberware, and equipment untouched. A 2-second exposure to the spray causes surface tissue necrosis across the contact area within 30 seconds, progressing to deep tissue destruction within 5 minutes if not neutralized. The compound can be neutralized by alkaline solution, but the window for effective treatment is narrow.
Properties.aliases: Rot, NAS-2, Flesh Eater, Decay Gun
Properties.specifications:
spray range: 1-4 meters
compound: NecroSolve fast-acting necrotizing enzyme
tissue selectivity: Biological only — no effect on synthetics
onset: Surface necrosis in 30 seconds
deep tissue destruction: 5 minutes if untreated
neutralization: Alkaline solution within 2 minutes
reservoir: 10 spray bursts
weight: 0.8 kg
countermeasure: Sealed suit, immediate alkaline flush
Properties.story_hooks: A body was found with NecroSolve exposure patterns — the flesh was destroyed but every piece of cyberware was intact and undamaged, neatly arranged as if someone was harvesting augmentations from the living.; Carrion's NecroSolve compound has been detected in a municipal water supply at extremely low concentrations — not enough to cause necrosis, but enough to cause chronic skin inflammation across an entire district.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Nerve Agent Micro-Dart System NAMDS-1 'Whisper'

Properties.description: A wrist-mounted micro-dart launcher that fires a near-invisible carbon-fiber dart loaded with a fast-acting nerve agent. The dart is 8mm long, thinner than a human hair at its widest point, and delivered by a compressed gas micro-charge that is nearly silent. The nerve agent — Carrion's proprietary NeuroHalt-7 — causes rapid paralysis of the respiratory system within 90 seconds of injection, and the dart is small enough that most targets do not feel the impact. The NAMDS-1 is the weapon of choice for operators who need a target to die quietly, in public, with no apparent cause of death until a very thorough autopsy finds a carbon-fiber splinter smaller than an eyelash.
Properties.aliases: Whisper, NAMDS-1, Silent Needle, The Kiss
Properties.specifications:
dart size: 8mm length, 0.1mm diameter carbon fiber
propulsion: Compressed gas micro-charge, 28 dB acoustic signature
effective range: 1-5 meters
toxin: NeuroHalt-7 fast-acting respiratory paralytic
time to effect: 60-90 seconds
magazine: 3 darts
weight: 0.05 kg total wrist unit
detectability: Dart is undetectable without microscopic examination
Properties.story_hooks: Three high-profile deaths in one month, all attributed to sudden respiratory failure, all in public settings — the connection is invisible without knowing what to look for.; A retired Carrion operative is selling their personal NAMDS-1 along with detailed operational logs of every target they ever hit with it — the buyer gets the weapon and the blackmail material.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Neural Lash NL-3 'Agony'

Properties.description: A flexible polymer whip with embedded electromagnetic emitters along its length that, on contact with a target's cyberware, injects a cascading pain signal directly into their neural interface. The NL-3 does not cause physical damage beyond a superficial welt — its entire function is to hijack the target's pain processing pathways and amplify them to maximum intensity. Augmented targets describe being struck by the Neural Lash as the worst pain they have ever experienced, overriding any pain suppression firmware. Unaugmented targets experience only the physical impact of a polymer whip, which is unpleasant but not extraordinary. Carrion developed it as an interrogation tool.
Properties.aliases: Agony, NL-3, Pain Whip, The Lash
Properties.specifications:
whip length: 2 meters
emitter count: 12 electromagnetic nodes along length
pain induction: Direct neural interface hijacking on contact
effect on augmented targets: Maximum pain response, 5-15 seconds per strike
effect on unaugmented targets: Standard physical whip impact only
power source: Handle-mounted capacitor, 200 strikes per charge
weight: 0.4 kg
pain suppression bypass: Overrides all known commercial firmware
Properties.story_hooks: NL-3 whips are being used in underground fighting pits where augmented fighters compete — the fights are agonizing spectacles that draw wealthy spectators from the upper tiers.; A whistleblower claims Carrion tested the NL-3 on involuntary subjects to calibrate the pain response — the test subjects are still alive and their neural interfaces are permanently damaged.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Pathogen Delivery System PDS-4 'Typhoid'

Properties.description: A weapon system designed to deliver engineered biological agents via aerosolized capsules launched from a modified grenade launcher platform. The PDS-4 fires capsules that burst on impact, releasing clouds of pathogen-carrying particles calibrated for maximum infection rate through respiratory exposure. Carrion offers a range of pathogen payloads — from fast-acting incapacitants that simulate severe flu symptoms to slow-developing agents designed for covert population-level delivery. The system exists in a legal gray zone: Carrion officially markets the launcher for 'agricultural pest control aerosol delivery,' and the pathogen payloads are sold through separate, deniable supply chains.
Properties.aliases: Typhoid, PDS-4, Plague Launcher, Patient Zero
Properties.legality: Prohibited — biological weapon (officially does not exist as weapon)
Properties.specifications:
launcher type: Modified 40mm grenade platform
effective range: 30-100 meters
aerosolization radius: 8 meters from impact
pathogen options: Fast incapacitant, slow-develop covert, targeted genetic-marker selective
infection rate: 85-95% for unprotected respiratory exposure
capsule weight: 0.2 kg
magazine: 6 capsules
launcher weight: 3.8 kg
countermeasure: NBC-grade respiratory filtration
Properties.story_hooks: A mystery illness spreading through Tier 2 has been traced to PDS-4 capsule fragments found in ventilation systems — someone deployed a slow-acting pathogen and the infection is still spreading.; Carrion's genetic-marker-selective pathogen has been loaded into PDS-4 capsules — it only affects people with a specific genetic heritage, making it an instrument of ethnic targeting.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Ricochet Pistol RCH-1 'Billiard'

Properties.description: A smart-round pistol firing self-adjusting polymer-jacketed rounds that can be programmed to ricochet off up to three surfaces before reaching a target. The weapon's integrated LiDAR maps the immediate environment and calculates bounce trajectories in real-time, displaying them on the shooter's HUD as dotted lines. The rounds contain a micro-gyroscope that adjusts the jacket's surface hardness milliseconds before each impact, controlling the angle and energy of each bounce. Carrion marketed it for engaging targets behind cover, but its real cultural impact has been in assassination — killing someone around a corner, from another room, through a ventilation duct.
Properties.aliases: Billiard, RCH-1, Bounce Gun, Corner Shot
Properties.specifications:
caliber: 6mm polymer-jacketed smart round
magazine: 10 rounds
maximum ricochets: 3 per round
energy retention: approximately 60% per bounce
LiDAR range: 30 meters environmental mapping
weight: 1.1 kg
trajectory calculation: 0.3 seconds per bounce path
effective kill range: 15 meters including bounces
Properties.story_hooks: A target was killed in a sealed room with no line of sight from any entry point — forensic trajectory analysis shows a triple-ricochet path through a mail slot.; The RCH-1's LiDAR mapping data is stored locally and can reconstruct a detailed 3D map of every room the weapon has been fired in — stolen units are being used as covert surveying tools.

Properties.description: The CAM-3 operates by firing a compressed canister that ruptures at a programmable altitude, releasing a precisely calibrated aerosol suspension of catalytic oxidizing agents. Upon dispersion, a secondary delayed-ignition charge ignites the cloud, producing a deflagration wave tuned to propagate through enclosed spaces with maximum pressure efficiency. The mortar itself is a stubby, break-action single-shot tube with a digital fuse programmer embedded in the grip — operators dial in burst height, dispersion radius, and ignition delay in seconds.
Properties.specifications:
weight: 4.1 kg loaded
length: 61 cm
effective range: 40��180 m
blast radius: 8–14 m depending on enclosure geometry
canister capacity: Single shot, break-action reload
fuse delay range: 0.3–6.0 seconds
dispersion modes: Point burst, Wide-area fog, Directional fan
Properties.tactical_use: Primarily deployed for building clearance and tunnel engagements where conventional fragmentation is tactically wasteful. Operators fire a round through a doorway or ventilation shaft, letting the cloud settle before detonation — the pressure wave follows corridors and corners in ways solid explosives cannot. Anti-personnel at close range; anti-materiel in confined server rooms or fabrication floors where the overpressure destroys unshielded electronics.
Properties.cultural_context: The CAM-3 has a grim reputation in Meridian 88's underground circuits as the weapon of choice for corporate extraction teams conducting 'structural audits' — euphemism for eliminating squatter communities in reclaimed industrial zones. Street gangs fear it disproportionately because it offers no warning and no cover. Owning one marks a person as either deeply connected to military supply chains or deeply dangerous to approach.
Properties.story_hooks: A CAM-3 canister with a tampered fuse is found in a residential block's HVAC system — the ignition timer is set for the building's peak occupancy hour.; A runner is hired to retrieve a stolen shipment of CAM-3 canisters; the job goes sideways when they discover the 'client' is the same extraction team that cleared their old neighborhood.; An ARCTURUS whistleblower claims the CAM-3's aerosol formula was field-tested on civilian populations before military sale — and has the atmospheric sensor logs to prove it.

Nodes.Name: Black-market arms brokers who don't use what they sell
Tunnel-network enforcers in the Undercroft districts

Properties.description:
The CIDD-3 is a slow-moving, high-endurance drone platform developed by HELIX BIOSYSTEMS as a derivative of their industrial tissue preservation research line. It operates by projecting a focused catalytic beam that accelerates osmotic pressure differentials across cell membranes in targeted tissue, rapidly drawing interstitial fluid outward through a process that mimics, at a greatly accelerated rate, the biochemical mechanisms of severe dehydration. Targets experience acute desiccation effects in exposed tissue — cracking skin, seizing muscles, intense thirst signals — without any actual systemic dehydration occurring, as the effect is surface-local and depth-limited to approximately 4cm of tissue penetration.

The drone's defining characteristic is its patience. The CIDD-3 is not designed for fast engagements. It moves slowly, hovers at a fixed standoff distance, and applies its catalytic beam in sustained, low-intensity pulses optimized for maximum discomfort over time rather than rapid incapacitation. Its autonomous target-lock system uses a proprietary HELIX BIOSYSTEMS moisture-differential sensor array to distinguish living targets from environmental objects with remarkable accuracy, and it will maintain lock on a moving target at walking pace indefinitely until its power cell is exhausted or it is physically destroyed.

Operators have noted that the CIDD-3 produces a faint, distinctive smell — a dry, slightly saline odor — that experienced field personnel have learned to recognize as an early warning. In enclosed environments, this olfactory signature is often the only indication of deployment before effects begin.
Properties.aliases: Husk, The Dryer, Dust Drone, Saltmaker
Properties.specifications:
dimensions: 28cm x 14cm x 14cm
operational speed: Max 4m/s (pursuit mode), 0.5m/s (sustained application mode)
tissue penetration depth: Approximately 4cm
effective range: 2m–10m
targeting system: HELIX proprietary moisture-differential array
power source: Long-duration lithium-polymer cell
battery life: Up to 4 hours continuous operation
weight: 1.8kg
olfactory signature: Faint saline/dry atmosphere odor at close range
Properties.tactical_use: The CIDD-3 excels in siege and containment scenarios where operators want to make a position untenable over time without committing to direct engagement. A single drone deployed into a room or corridor will, within ten to fifteen minutes, make that space miserable enough that most unprotected occupants will seek to leave. Security teams use them to drive targets toward choke points. Interrogators use them in sustained sessions as an alternative to more legally complex methods. Some operators use multiple units in relay — one active, one charging — to maintain indefinite area presence.
Properties.cultural_context: Within Meridian 88's corporate detention system, the CIDD-3 occupies a strange legal grey zone — it is licensed for use in 'compliance facilitation' contexts, a euphemism that has been dissected at length by civil rights advocates. Because it leaves no lasting injury in standard operating parameters, it rarely triggers the medical documentation requirements associated with more overtly damaging weapons.
