Street communities near processing centers refer to people who've been held in CIDD-3 environments as 'Husks' — a term that has spread beyond its origin to describe anyone visibly worn down by institutional pressure.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone is deploying CIDD-3 units in the ventilation network of a residential block — residents are getting sick, the building management claims ignorance, and the drones keep disappearing before investigators arrive.; A HELIX BIOSYSTEMS licensing auditor has gone missing after flagging an anomalous pattern in CIDD-3 deployment logs across three different detention facilities run by the same shell company.; The players are trapped in a building with a malfunctioning CIDD-3 that has locked onto a target designation it cannot find — and its sensor array is broad enough that everyone in the building qualifies.

Nodes.Name: Freelance operators with corporate security licensing

Properties.description:
The CSDD-3 is a mid-altitude dispersal platform roughly the size of a cantaloupe, built around a pressurized bio-ceramic canister housing engineered fungal spore payloads. On deployment it rises to a pre-calculated ceiling, reads atmospheric thermals via onboard microbarometric sensors, and releases a calibrated spore cloud timed to drift across a designated kill zone at walking pace. Spores adhere to exposed skin and synthetic-organic hybrid tissue alike, triggering a rapid catalytic chain reaction in subcutaneous moisture that produces localized heat blistering and systemic inflammatory cascade over roughly ninety seconds.

What distinguishes the CSDD-3 from simple chemical drones is its terrain-reading persistence logic. If wind conditions shift before full dispersal, the drone repositions rather than releasing prematurely — operators in field trials noted it seemed to 'wait' for ideal conditions with uncomfortable patience. This behavioral loop, derived from IRONCLAD AGRISYSTEMS' commercial crop-dusting firmware, gives it an agricultural quality that many find more unsettling than outright aggression.

The canister is modular and field-swappable. Standard loadout is the Rot-3 spore blend, but the black market supplies Desiccant-7 (targeting mucous membranes) and Bleach-Null (suppressing biophotonic implant function). IRONCLAD officially denies any awareness of these aftermarket cartridges.
Properties.specifications:
dimensions: 18 cm diameter sphere, 22 cm with rotors extended
weight: 1.4 kg loaded
flight ceiling: 40 m operational, 120 m transit
payload capacity: Rot-3 spore canister, 180 mL pressurized
dispersal radius: 8–25 m depending on atmospheric conditions
onset time: 60–120 seconds post-contact
loiter time: 22 minutes at operational altitude
power source: Solid-state microcell, non-rechargeable field unit
guidance: Autonomous barometric + GPS dead reckoning
countermeasures: Sealed biosuite rated NBC-2 or higher
Properties.tactical_use: Operators typically deploy CSDD-3 ahead of forced entry operations to clear enclosed courtyards, rooftop positions, or bottleneck corridors. Because it loiters and waits for ideal dispersal conditions, teams can launch it during approach and trust it to act on arrival. Paired with acoustic or visual diversionary tools, it forces defenders to choose between holding position and taking exposure or breaking cover to avoid the cloud. Anti-vehicle use is limited but documented against unshielded driver compartments.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88's mid-tier gang ecology, the CSDD-3 carries a specific class connotation — it's a 'rich crew's weapon,' associated with organizations that can afford to wait and plan rather than brawl. Carrying one signals patience and resources. Street-level operators call it 'the landlord's drone' partly as a slur, associating its slow, inevitable dispersal with eviction and debt collection. IRONCLAD AGRISYSTEMS' branding is still visible on most units, a faint crop-circle logo on the undercarriage, which has become darkly ironic shorthand in the Underbelly districts.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of unexplained skin-blistering incidents in the Terrace Market district traces back to a CSDD-3 unit that never received its shutdown command — it's still loitering somewhere in the ventilation superstructure above the market, waiting for ideal conditions.; An IRONCLAD AGRISYSTEMS whistleblower approaches the party with firmware logs proving the company's R&D division deliberately engineered the Rot-3 spore blend for human targets, not crop pests. The company has already sent a retrieval team.; A buyer wants five CSDD-3 units with Desiccant-7 cartridges for what they claim is a pest control contract. The address on the work order is a refugee resettlement block.

Nodes.Name: Corporate extraction teams (TESSERA CORPONATION security division)
Mid-tier gang enforcers with agricultural district connections

Properties.description:
The CVDC-5 operates by rupturing a pressurized internal canister that releases a heavier-than-air catalytic vapor across a defined radius — typically 8 to 12 meters depending on atmospheric conditions. The vapor itself is inert on dispersal; ignition is triggered by a secondary piezoelectric pulse emitted from the casing 1.4 seconds after rupture, which causes rapid oxidative chain-reaction combustion throughout the suspended aerosol. The result is a brief, intensely hot flash-burn event that consumes oxygen in the area and reaches temperatures exceeding 900°C for approximately 0.6 seconds before dissipating entirely. Unlike conventional incendiaries, it leaves no persistent flame, no structural scorch, and almost no thermal residue.

What makes the CVDC-5 distinctive is the near-invisibility of its effect profile. Security sensors calibrated for conventional explosive signatures — overpressure, optical flash, shrapnel impact — frequently fail to register the detonation until personnel casualties are already logged. The vapor is odorless and colorless. To an unaugmented observer, the charge simply sits on a surface and then, without warning, everyone in the room is dead. Augmented users with thermal overlays can sometimes detect the dispersal cloud if they know what to look for, but the 1.4-second ignition window leaves almost no reaction time.

ArcTurus Defense Solutions developed the CVDC-5 as a room-denial and hostage-rescue inversion tool — the idea being that it could neutralize a contained space without collateral structural damage to high-value facilities. That logic has since been appropriated enthusiastically by extraction teams, corporate saboteurs, and certain factions within the Meridian 88 underground who appreciate that the charge is effectively undetectable post-deployment if the ventilation systems are running.
Properties.specifications:
weight: 1.1 kg
dispersal radius: 8–12 meters (open air), 4–6 meters (enclosed)
ignition delay: 1.4 seconds post-rupture
peak temperature: ~920°C (0.6-second burn window)
casing material: Ablative ceramic composite
trigger mechanism: Piezoelectric ignition pulse, remote detonation optional
residual signature: Minimal — low thermal trace, no shrapnel pattern
shelf life: 18 months sealed, 6 hours once canister integrity is broken
Properties.tactical_use: Operators deploy the CVDC-5 by rolling or placing it into a target space — under a door, through a ventilation duct, or dropped from above through a ceiling breach. The charge is non-threatening in appearance and size, roughly resembling a standard industrial sensor housing. Teams using it typically withdraw to cover before the 1.4-second window closes. It is favored for close-quarters facility clearance where collateral structural damage would compromise extraction routes or alert neighboring security nodes. Some operators use it in tandem with door-seal charges to create fully contained burn events in server rooms or holding cells.
Properties.cultural_context: The CVDC-5 occupies an uneasy place in Meridian 88's weapon culture. Because it leaves no blast crater, no fire, and no obvious cause of death beyond rapid oxygen deprivation and flash-burn trauma, it has become associated with deniable corporate wet work — the kind of job where the client needs the bodies to look ambiguous. Street operators who've encountered its aftermath call it 'the clean kill' with a mix of professional admiration and genuine unease. Carrying one marks a person as either deep-tier military contractor or someone with very specific, very expensive connections. It is not a weapon anyone finds in a crate.
Properties.story_hooks: A coroner in Meridian 88's lower wards keeps flagging deaths that look like sudden cardiac events but match the CVDC-5's burn signature — someone is using the weapon on civilians and covering it as natural causes.; A player character's contact dies in a locked room with no blast damage and no apparent cause. The only witness is a building AI that logged a brief 'sensor anomaly' 1.4 seconds before the contact's vitals flatlined.; An ADS logistics manifest surfaces on the black market listing a shipment of CVDC-5 units consigned to a buyer in the civilian residential sector — someone is planning something that doesn't involve a military target.; A street-level chemist claims she can synthesize the catalytic compound from industrial precursors available in any agri-district. She wants protection. Several parties want her silenced.

Nodes.Name: High-tier fixers specializing in deniable operations
The cleaner archetype known in underground circles as 'the Sommelier'

Properties.description:
The CPC-2 does not fire a traditional projectile. Instead, it discharges a focused column of superheated, electromagnetically compressed gas at pressures sufficient to induce localized cavitation in dense biological tissue — the same phenomenon that destroys the joints of deep-sea divers who ascend too rapidly, reproduced instantaneously at range. The discharge appears visually as a faint shimmer, almost invisible in daylight, with a sharp crack like snapping bamboo. At the point of impact, microscopic gas bubbles form and collapse violently within soft tissue, producing internal rupture without visible external trauma at low power settings. At higher settings, the effect is catastrophically visible.

Zheng-Dao's engineers developed the Bends by adapting industrial ultrasonic cavitation cleaning technology — originally used to strip contaminants from precision circuit components — into a directed-energy weapons platform. The core innovation is the Resonant Pressure Sheath, a conical emitter array at the muzzle that shapes the discharge into a coherent column rather than an expanding cone, preserving destructive pressure over distance. The carbine form factor is compact enough for vehicle use and close-quarters operation, which was the primary design brief from Zheng-Dao's infrastructure security division.

The weapon has two notable operational quirks. First, it is significantly more effective against targets with high fluid content — biological organisms, hydraulic systems, liquid-cooled electronics — and nearly useless against dry, rigid structures. Second, the discharge produces a subsonic resonance in the 18–22 Hz range that some operators report causes mild nausea and disorientation even in the shooter, earning it an unofficial reputation as a weapon that punishes careless use.
Properties.aliases: Bends, Bubble Gun, The Diver, Cavitator
Properties.legality: Prohibited — classified as a directed biological harm emitter under Meridian 88 Statute 7.4.2
Properties.specifications:
discharge type: Superheated compressed gas column, electromagnetically shaped
effective range: 15m (full cavitation) / 60m (reduced-effect zone)
power settings: Three: Sublethal Disruption / Cavity Induction / Full Rupture
power source: Zheng-Dao Type-4 Bioelectric Cell, 40 discharges per cell
weight: 2.9 kg
dimensions: 490mm length, compact carbine profile
target effectiveness: High against biological and fluid-system targets; minimal effect on dry rigid materials
subsonic byproduct: 18–22 Hz resonance pulse, 3m radius around shooter
integrated systems: Pressure gauge, power-mode selector, muzzle sheath alignment indicator
Properties.tactical_use: Enforcement and extraction teams use the Bends primarily in confined, target-rich environments where over-penetration is a liability — server rooms, medical facilities, pressurized transit carriages. The Sublethal Disruption setting is favored for crowd control and detainee compliance, producing incapacitating internal pain without permanent damage. Full Rupture mode is documented in several high-profile corporate assassinations where the lack of visible external trauma allowed time of death to be obscured. The weapon's ineffectiveness against dry rigid structures means operators typically carry a conventional sidearm for dealing with barricades, locks, and armored targets.
Properties.cultural_context: The Bends occupies a deeply uncomfortable place in Meridian 88's cultural landscape. Its prohibition stems not just from lethality but from the nature of the wounds it inflicts — internal, invisible, deniable — which has made it the weapon of choice for actors who need harm to look like something else. Zheng-Dao officially discontinued the CPC-2 following the Statute 7.4.2 ruling, but the discontinuation was widely understood as a paperwork exercise; production moved to unlicensed fabrication partners within six months. Among street-level fixers, offering someone 'a case of the Bends' has become idiom for a targeted, deniable hit.
Properties.story_hooks: A prominent Meridian 88 labor organizer is found dead with no visible wounds — the coroner's report is suppressed, but a street medic who saw the body recognizes the internal rupture pattern of a Bends discharge.; A shipment of Zheng-Dao Type-4 Bioelectric Cells is being moved through the port district — the cells are the right spec for the CPC-2, but the manifest lists them as medical imaging equipment.; An operator reports that their Bends has begun discharging at Full Rupture mode regardless of the power selector setting — and they need it traced to its fabrication batch before they can figure out if it's a fault or a deliberate modification.; A Zheng-Dao engineer who worked on the original CPC-2 project is offering to sell the Resonant Pressure Sheath schematics — but three other buyers are already in the bidding, and not all of them want the schematics to reach market.

Nodes.Name: Corrupt enforcement officers (confiscated units in circulation)
Corporate intelligence operatives requiring deniable lethality

Properties.description:
The CPK-5 consists of a hardened polymer-ceramic knuckle guard housing four resonant emitter nodes, one positioned behind each striking surface. On contact, each node fires a microsecond burst of focused ultrasonic pressure into the target tissue, generating localized cavitation bubbles within fluid-rich biological matter — blood, synovial fluid, vitreous humour. The bubbles collapse almost instantaneously, producing secondary shockwaves that shred tissue from the inside without requiring deep penetration.

What distinguishes the CPK-5 from other percussion-class melee weapons is its selective tissue targeting. The ultrasonic burst frequency is tuned specifically to biological fluid densities, meaning it passes through synthetic augmentation casings and subdermal armor plating with minimal attenuation before detonating inside the soft tissue beneath. Heavily augmented targets — who might otherwise shrug off conventional strikes — are often more vulnerable, not less, as their augmentation infrastructure traps and amplifies the cavitation event.

ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC originally designed the CPK-5 as a 'non-lethal compliance tool' for corporate security, but field reports quickly revealed that repeated strikes to the torso caused internal hemorrhaging, organ rupture, and in several documented cases, vitreous detachment leading to permanent blindness. The 'non-lethal' designation was quietly removed from marketing materials after the third wrongful death settlement.
Properties.specifications:
weight: 0.6 kg per unit (sold as pair)
emitter nodes: 4
frequency range: 18 kHz – 2.4 MHz (auto-tuning on contact)
power source: Integrated micro-capacitor, 40 full-power strikes per charge
recharge time: 6 minutes via standard USB-C hardline
striking surface: Boron carbide ceramic over titanium frame
cavitation depth: Effective to 4 cm sub-surface tissue
augmentation interference: Minimal — passes through Grade 1-3 subdermal plating
Properties.tactical_use: Operators use the CPK-5 in close-quarters scenarios where the target is known to be heavily augmented. Standard practice is to target the neck, temples, and lower abdomen where fluid concentration is highest. Experienced fighters alternate between standard strikes and activated pulses to conserve charge, using the physical impact to set up positioned cavitation bursts. Against unaugmented targets, fighters are advised to use restraint — even a single full-power strike to the skull has caused fatal hemorrhagic events in field use.
Properties.cultural_context: The CPK-5 occupies an uneasy middle ground in Meridian 88's street culture. Corporate security divisions carry them openly as 'compliance tools,' which grants a veneer of institutional legitimacy. Street enforcers who acquire them through gray-market channels wear them as status symbols — possession signals both financial means and a willingness to operate in augmentation-heavy environments. There is a persistent underground rumor, partially substantiated, that ZHENG-DAO sells tuning kits that shift the frequency range to target specific augmentation manufacturers' fluid systems, effectively turning the CPK-5 into a brand-specific weapon.
Properties.story_hooks: A ZHENG-DAO compliance officer is found dead, killed by their own CPK-5 — but the frequency signature logged on the device doesn't match any known tuning profile, suggesting someone modified it remotely mid-strike.; A street surgeon is selling CPK-5 units pre-tuned to detonate specifically inside HELIX BIOSYSTEMS augmentation fluid, suggesting either a corporate espionage operation or a very personal grudge.; A player character with extensive fluid-based augmentation begins experiencing delayed cavitation events — micro-bubbles that didn't fully collapse during a previous fight are now triggering spontaneously, and they need a specialist before the next one hits their spinal column.

Nodes.Name: Underground pit fighters (modified for sport use)
Meridian 88 Transit Authority crowd control units (officially denied)

Properties.description:
The CPP-3 does not attack the eyes. It attacks the visual cortex directly, using a precisely calibrated coherent photonic pulse tuned to penetrate ocular tissue and induce phosphene cascades — false light signals — directly in the brain's visual processing centers. Unlike the Retinal Cascade Emitter which burns the retina, the Phantom Light leaves the physical eye entirely undamaged while flooding the target's visual field with overwhelming blue-white hallucinated light that persists for 40 to 180 seconds depending on exposure duration. The experience is described by survivors as being inside a star.

Arcturus Defense Solutions developed the CPP-3 as a less-lethal alternative to blinding munitions for use in hostage situations where collateral optical damage was a legal liability. The photonic pulse frequency required years of calibration — too low and the effect is merely disorienting, too high and permanent cortical damage results. The production variant sits at a frequency that Arcturus' legal team certified as 'non-permanently injurious' based on studies that have since been contested. Prolonged exposure or repeated use within 24 hours carries documented risk of lasting visual processing damage.

The weapon's most distinctive characteristic is that it functions identically regardless of whether the target's eyes are open, closed, or augmented with standard optical implants. Standard cyberoptic shutters provide no protection — the pulse bypasses the eye entirely. Only full cortical shielding or specialized photonic dampening implants (rare and expensive) offer meaningful resistance. This has made the CPP-3 particularly valuable against augmented targets who believe their cyberoptics make them immune to visual disruption.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 2–35 meters
pulse duration: 0.08 seconds (standard) to 2 seconds (sustained)
power source: Arcturus APack-7 (12 standard pulses)
weight: 2.7 kg
length: 58 cm
disorientation duration: 40–180 seconds per standard pulse
cyberoptic bypass: Confirmed effective against all standard optical implants
risk threshold: Permanent damage risk at 3+ pulses within 24-hour window
housing: Matte slate polymer with Arcturus tactical grip standard
Properties.tactical_use: The CPP-3 is used by specialized law enforcement and military units as a primary breach-support weapon — a point operator fires on the defender immediately before breach to create a window of total visual incapacitation. It is particularly valued in environments where cyberoptic-equipped targets are expected, since conventional flash-bang devices are largely ineffective against augmented subjects. Corporate security teams use it for non-lethal detention of high-value targets. The 35-meter range allows standoff engagement before close-quarters entry.
Properties.cultural_context: The CPP-3 sits in an uncomfortable legal and cultural space — officially restricted rather than prohibited, meaning licensed security contractors can carry it, but its presence in civilian hands triggers immediate law enforcement interest. Among augmented communities there is specific fear and resentment around the weapon, since it specifically negates the protective advantage of expensive cyberoptic work. 'Getting ghosted' has become slang for being hit with a CPP-3, and there is a small underground market for the cortical shielding implants that resist it.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of corporate heists share one signature: security footage shows guards simply stopping and standing still for two minutes before the thieves walk past them — someone has a CPP-3 and knows exactly how to use it.; A character with expensive cyberoptics gets hit with a CPP-3 and is shaken to discover their augmentations offered no protection whatsoever.; Arcturus is quietly recalling a batch of CPP-3s with a calibration defect that places the pulse frequency in the permanent-damage range — they haven't announced why.; An underground clinic is offering 'phantom light immunity' implants of questionable efficacy — someone is making money on fear.

Nodes.Name: Black market operators who've acquired units through supply chain diversion

Properties.description:
The Cochlear Resonant Hemorrhage Projector generates a tightly focused beam of modulated infrasonic and ultrasonic waveforms tuned to the resonant frequency of the cochlear microvascular bed. At operational intensity, the weapon induces rapid capillary rupture within the inner ear, flooding the cochlear duct with blood and destroying the hair cell architecture within seconds. The victim experiences a sensation described as a 'wet crunch' followed by total sensorineural deafness and catastrophic loss of vestibular function.

What distinguishes the CRHP-2 from cruder acoustic weapons is its dual-band targeting algorithm, which first performs a half-second passive sonar sweep to map the target's skull geometry and canal orientation before locking the destructive waveform. This bone-conduction mapping bypasses conventional ear protection entirely — plugs, dampeners, and cybernetic audio filters are useless because the weapon couples directly through the temporal bone. Operators refer to this as 'going through the wall.'

The projector's barrel houses a phased array of forty-eight piezoelectric ceramic emitters arranged in a parabolic configuration, allowing effective range out to roughly thirty meters before waveform coherence degrades. The weapon's most chilling feature is its near-silence during operation — the emitted frequencies are largely imperceptible to bystanders, meaning a target simply collapses without any obvious cause.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 4–30 meters
targeting sweep duration: 0.4 seconds
emitter array: 48-element parabolic piezoelectric ceramic
frequency bands: 18–22 Hz (infrasonic) / 28–34 kHz (ultrasonic) dual-band
power source: High-density capacitor cell, 14 discharges per charge
weight: 3.1 kg
form factor: Carbine-length, matte composite housing
onboard processor: Skull geometry adaptive targeting unit (SGATU-3)
Properties.tactical_use: Primarily used for silent incapacitation of high-value targets in enclosed environments where gunfire would compromise the operator. Favored in close-protection assassination contracts where the client requires deniability — a victim found collapsed with burst eardrums can be attributed to an aneurysm. Operators are trained to keep the sweep phase brief to avoid alerting cyber-augmented targets whose implants may detect the preliminary scan frequency.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88's underground enforcement circles, being 'earwormed' has become slang for a particularly clean, professional kill. Corporate fixers who carry the CRHP-2 are considered high-tier professionals — the weapon is expensive, finicky, and requires licensing through a shell company at minimum. Street-level gangers rarely possess them, which means their appearance in a crime scene signals corporate or state-level involvement. Victims who survive partial exposure and live with permanent deafness often become vocal activists in the city's growing anti-bioweapon movement.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of seemingly natural deaths in the financial district all share the same inner ear pathology — someone is using a CRHP-2 to silence witnesses to a merger fraud.; A black market CRHP-2 unit surfaces with a modified sweep algorithm that targets cybernetic audio implants specifically, destroying expensive hearing augmentations rather than biological tissue — someone is sending a message to the augmented community.; An operator who survived a CRHP-2 attack with partial hearing retains a persistent tonal hallucination at exactly 19 Hz — a frequency that, when analyzed, encodes a data packet.; A CRHP-2 prototype with an extended range module of 80 meters is stolen from an ARCTURUS test facility, and the thief's last known location is a crowded transit hub.

Properties.description:
The CRS-7 generates an extremely narrow coherent radiation beam — a focused column of X-ray band energy approximately 0.3 millimetres in diameter that maintains coherence over short distances before diffraction limits its effectiveness. At this scale and intensity, the beam does not burn or cauterise in the manner of conventional laser weapons; instead, it severs material at the molecular level with near-zero thermal spread. The cut is so precise that biological tissue on either side of the beam path is essentially undamaged — the wound is a clean incision, not a burn channel. This characteristic gives the weapon its name and its disturbing dual-use reputation.

The weapon's operating principle derives directly from surgical radiation technology — specifically, the coherent X-ray scalpels used in precision neurosurgery and microsurgical robotics. LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS developed the CRS-7 as a licensed derivative of their surgical suite technology, initially marketed to corporate medical teams for field surgical applications. The tactical application was noted almost immediately: a weapon that could sever tendons, nerves, or blood vessels with surgical precision, leaving no visible external wound until the target moved and the incision opened, represented a unique capability profile.

The CRS-7's practical limitations are significant: effective range is 3–8 metres, the beam width requires precise targeting (the weapon integrates a targeting assist system, but moving targets at range are challenging), and the power draw limits sustained operation. It is not a weapon for firefights. It is a weapon for situations where a firefight has already been decided and the question is only how much damage to do and where. Its presence in Meridian 88's underworld is small but consistent — it surfaces wherever someone needs work done that looks like an accident or a medical complication.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 0.5–8 metres
beam diameter: 0.3mm (fixed)
thermal spread: Less than 0.1mm from beam centreline
targeting assist: Integrated optical and depth sensor array, 0.1mm targeting resolution
power source: High-density CRS cell (40 seconds continuous emission; field non-replaceable, requires factory recharge)
weight: 0.9 kg
form factor: Resembles a medical instrument — narrow, handheld, with a focusing aperture
radiation exposure: Operator shielding required for prolonged use; single-shot exposure within safe limits
Properties.tactical_use: The CRS-7 is not used in conventional combat. Operators use it in controlled environments — targets who are restrained, unconscious, or unaware. The weapon's most common tactical application is delayed incapacitation: severing a critical tendon or blood vessel in a way that produces no immediate visible effect, allowing the operator to be elsewhere when the target collapses. It is also used for precision sabotage — severing specific components inside sealed devices by passing the beam through thin housing material. The 8-metre effective range and the requirement for a stable firing platform make it impractical in dynamic situations. Operators who carry a CRS-7 are not expecting a fight.
Properties.cultural_context: The Suture exists in a category of weapons that Meridian 88's criminal ecosystem finds genuinely unsettling — not because of raw destructive capacity, but because of what its use implies about the operator. Someone who uses a CRS-7 is patient, technically skilled, and has access to either a LAZARUS medical licence or a black market supply chain sophisticated enough to move medical-grade equipment. The weapon is associated with a specific class of operator: the kind hired to make deaths look like medical events. In the corporate world, the CRS-7 is whispered about in the context of executive suites and boardroom power struggles. Among street operators, its reputation is largely mythological — few have seen one, but everyone knows what it means when the cause of death is listed as 'vascular anomaly.'
Properties.story_hooks: A senior executive has died of what appears to be a spontaneous vascular rupture. The players — hired by the family — discover the death was caused by a CRS-7 incision made twelve hours before collapse. The medical examiner who would have caught it has also died, of the same apparent cause.; A stolen CRS-7 has surfaced in a street market, misidentified as a medical tool. The seller doesn't know what they have. LAZARUS wants it back quietly. The players are in the middle.; A player character with a medical background recognises a wound pattern in a crime scene photograph as consistent with CRS-7 use — but the official investigation has closed the case as natural causes. Reopening it means challenging a verdict that someone powerful has invested in.; LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS is running a black programme to track every CRS-7 that has left their licensed medical supply chain. They've identified seven units in Meridian 88 that are unaccounted for. They want them retrieved or destroyed, and they don't want law enforcement involved. The players discover why when they find the first unit.

Nodes.Name: High-end corporate assassins specialising in natural-cause deaths
Rogue surgeons working outside licensed facilities
Intelligence operatives requiring untraceable incapacitation capability
"The Physician" — an urban legend in Meridian 88's corporate assassination community, believed to be a former LAZARUS surgical researcher

Properties.description:
The CTER-7 operates on a principle of sustained coherent infrared excitation, projecting a tightly collimated beam of mid-infrared photons tuned to the absorption spectra of organic tissue and synthetic polymer composites. The beam does not burn in the conventional sense — it causes rapid molecular vibration at depth, heating targets from the inside out before surface ignition occurs. At full power, a one-second exposure to unarmored tissue produces subcutaneous steam pockets and catastrophic cell rupture across a 4cm penetration depth.

What distinguishes the Ashmaker from older thermal weapons is its adaptive frequency modulation system, which cycles through seventeen discrete infrared bands within a single trigger pull. This cycling defeats most standard thermal-dispersion armor coatings, which are typically tuned to reflect a narrow frequency range. The weapon's focusing array uses a series of chalcogenide glass lenses cooled by a micro-circulation system, allowing sustained fire without bloom degradation.

In the field, the CTER-7 has developed a grim reputation not for its lethality but for the nature of its wounds. Survivors of partial exposure describe a 'cold burning' sensation — the deep tissue damage registers before surface pain receptors fire. Street medics in the Meridian 88 undercity have coined the term 'ashwound' for the characteristic grey-white tissue necrosis it leaves. Arcturus Defense Solutions markets it exclusively to licensed security contractors, though significant numbers have entered black market circulation following the Takamatsu Depot breach of 2198.
Properties.aliases: Ashmaker, The Baker, Cinder Rod, CTER
Properties.specifications:
length: 94cm
weight: 4.2kg unloaded
power source: ADS Type-9 thermal cell, 22 shots at full power
effective range: 180m (focused), 340m (reduced effect)
beam diameter at target: 3.8cm at 50m, 9cm at 180m
frequency range: 3.5–12 micrometers cycling
cooling system: Micro-circulation chalcogenide array, passive bleed vents
fire modes: Pulse (0.3s burst), Sustained (trigger hold, max 4s continuous)
Properties.tactical_use: Operators favor the Ashmaker for breaching scenarios where conventional ballistics risk structural damage or ricochet in confined spaces. The beam passes cleanly through standard polycarbonate barriers and light partition walls, making it effective against entrenched targets behind soft cover. Security contractors use pulse mode for crowd deterrence at range — a 0.3-second exposure to exposed skin is non-lethal but produces immediate incapacitation. Full sustained fire is reserved for hardened targets or armored personnel. The weapon's main tactical liability is its power cell, which drains quickly under sustained use and produces a detectable thermal bloom from the cooling vents after three or more shots.
Properties.cultural_context: The Ashmaker occupies an uncomfortable middle ground in Meridian 88's weapon culture. It is expensive enough to signal corporate affiliation, but its wound profile — the distinctive ashwound — has made it a symbol of particular cruelty in street communities. Gangs that use it are often making a deliberate statement. Among licensed security contractors, it is considered a professional tool with a clinical reputation. There is a persistent underground rumor, largely unverified, that CTER-7 units are quietly distributed to corporate 'pacification teams' for use in labor disputes, which has made the weapon politically charged in union-aligned districts.
Properties.story_hooks: A street medic begins documenting ashwound cases and traces them to a single corporate district — someone is using CTER-7s in a pattern that looks less like security and more like targeted elimination.; A decommissioned lot of CTER-7s was supposed to be destroyed after contract expiry. They weren't. Someone moved them, and the serial numbers have been ground off.; A player character is offered a CTER-7 in exchange for a job — the weapon itself is the payment, which raises the question of why the seller needs the job done quietly enough to part with a Tier 3 asset.

Nodes.Name: Former ADS field testers who retained units post-contract

Properties.description:
The CPDP-1 operates by projecting a tightly focused piezoelectric pulse tuned to the resonant frequency of corneal collagen lamellae. Upon contact with the eye, the pulse induces rapid micro-shear between successive corneal layers, causing progressive delamination from the epithelium down through the Bowman's layer. The effect manifests within seconds as a spreading opaque whitening across the target's visual field — irreversible without immediate surgical intervention.

What distinguishes the Milkscreen from simple blinding agents is its surgical precision and deniability. Unlike chemical or laser-based ocular weapons, it leaves no detectable residue and produces no visible beam. Victims frequently cannot identify the moment of attack, reporting only a sudden 'fogging' before full opacity sets in. The pistol format makes it concealable and deployable at conversational range, ideal for close-quarters operations where discretion is paramount.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric originally developed the CPDP-1 as a non-lethal compliance tool for detention facilities, marketing it as a 'temporary visual suppressor.' Field use quickly revealed the 'temporary' designation to be aspirational. Most victims require full corneal transplant to recover usable vision, and in Meridian 88's tiered healthcare economy, that procedure is well beyond the means of most citizens.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 0.5–4 meters
pulse frequency: 18.4 kHz (tuned to corneal collagen)
charge per shot: 0.7 mJ
battery capacity: 22 shots per cell
dimensions: 14 cm length, 180g
targeting: Passive IR ocular lock, manual override available
housing: Matte polymer, passes most passive scanners
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed almost exclusively in close-range social infiltration scenarios — boardrooms, clubs, transit corridors. Operators typically fire once and withdraw, allowing the weapon's delayed onset to create distance between themselves and the incapacitation event. Effective for eliminating witness capacity without fatalities. Some interrogators use it as a coercive instrument, firing one shot and threatening the second.
Properties.cultural_context: The Milkscreen has acquired a particular dread in Meridian 88's underworld because it is a weapon of humiliation as much as harm. Being 'screened' carries social stigma — it implies the victim was close enough to their attacker to be touched, that they were trusted into proximity. Corporate fixer circles use 'got their eyes done' as slang for a professional embarrassment. Street medics who can perform corneal grafts charge extortionate rates in districts where the weapon circulates.
Properties.story_hooks: A witness to a high-profile corporate murder is found blind in a transit pod — no one in the carriage admits to seeing anything, and the weapon leaves no forensic trace.; A black-market corneal surgeon starts receiving death threats after becoming the only affordable option for Milkscreen victims in the Outerring districts.; A player character is hired to retrieve a stolen CPDP-1 prototype that fires a wider-dispersion pulse — potentially capable of blinding everyone in a standard office room.; A Zheng-Dao Bioelectric compliance officer is quietly selling decommissioned units through a shell distributor; someone wants proof, someone else wants the officer silenced.

Nodes.Name: Sable Rhen, a fixer known for leaving targets 'half-finished'

Properties.description:
The CDP-9 generates a toroidal electromagnetic discharge — a stable plasma ring approximately forty centimeters in diameter — that travels along a line-of-sight trajectory at roughly 180 meters per second. The ring is self-sustaining for approximately 0.4 seconds of flight time, giving it an effective range of seventy meters before field coherence collapses. On contact with a target, the toroid destabilizes and releases its stored electromagnetic energy in an omni-directional burst pattern, simultaneously burning exposed tissue and overloading unshielded electronics within a half-meter radius.

The weapon's distinctive characteristic is its interaction with metallic implants and subdermal augmentations. The discharge preferentially conducts through high-density metallic structures, meaning heavily augmented individuals suffer disproportionately severe secondary effects — internal burns along augmentation pathways, fried neural bridges, and in extreme cases, explosive pressure buildup in sealed implant housings. Against baseline humans, the Sunburn is painful and disorienting; against a chrome-heavy street soldier, it can be catastrophic.

Arcturus Defense Solutions originally developed the CDP-9 as an anti-augmentation crowd control platform for use in labor disputes at high-automation facilities. The implication — that the weapon was designed specifically to punish workers with industrial implants — has made it deeply politically charged. Its appearance in the hands of corporate security forces reliably escalates tensions, and several documented deployments have triggered full-scale riots.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 70 meters (field coherence limit)
discharge diameter: 40cm toroid
travel velocity: 180 m/s
burst radius on impact: 0.5 meters
magazine capacity: 8 charges (capacitor array)
recharge time: 3.5 seconds between shots
weight: 4.1 kg
power source: High-density capacitor bank, external power coupling compatible
Properties.tactical_use: Corporate security teams deploy the Sunburn in anti-riot formations, typically paired with conventional suppression units. The toroidal projectile's visibility — a faintly luminous ring — has a pronounced psychological effect on crowds, and a single discharge into a tightly packed group reliably produces panic and dispersal. In targeted operations against augmented individuals, operators aim for the torso to maximize contact with subdermal implant clusters. Military doctrine recommends against use in environments with significant unshielded electronics, as collateral electromagnetic damage to friendly equipment is common.
Properties.cultural_context: The CDP-9 has become a symbol of corporate anti-labor violence in Meridian 88. Labor organizers photograph it obsessively whenever it appears at a demonstration, and its deployment is treated as a declaration of intent rather than a proportional response. Among heavily augmented communities — dock workers, industrial operators, body-modification subcultures — the Sunburn is spoken of with a particular kind of dread. Getting hit by one is called 'getting coronated,' a bitter irony given that most victims are people whose augmentations were installed to make them more productive for the same corporations deploying the weapon against them.
Properties.story_hooks: A labor organizer hires the players to steal or destroy a shipment of CDP-9s before they reach corporate security ahead of a planned strike.; A heavily augmented player character survives a Sunburn hit but finds one of their implants has developed an unpredictable fault — it now occasionally discharges on its own.; Arcturus Defense Solutions is publicly denying they sold units to a private militia that used them on civilians. The players have evidence that contradicts this — and someone very powerful wants it buried.; A prototype CDP-9 variant surfaces on the black market that can sustain the toroid for twice the normal range. Someone in Arcturus R&D is leaking.

Nodes.Name: Arcturus Defense Solutions contracted security forces
Meridian 88 Municipal Riot Response Unit (disputed — officially denied)
Commander Yusuf Alade-Brennan (documented field commander, Sector 9 labor actions)
Black-market resellers targeting anti-augmentation hate groups

Properties.description:
The CBE-4 operates by projecting a focused burst of low-frequency electromagnetic interference tuned specifically to the oscillation bands of augmented neural tissue. When fired, the emitter generates a cone-shaped pulse that interacts with cybernetic implants in the target's skull — particularly memory indexing chips, cortical overlays, and sensory processing units — causing cascading micro-interruptions that present clinically as sudden, disorienting amnesia. The target does not lose consciousness but instead enters a fugue state lasting between forty seconds and several minutes depending on the density of their implant load. They remain ambulatory but functionally useless: unable to recognize faces, recall mission objectives, or operate complex motor sequences.

What makes the Lacuna distinctive is its surgical specificity. It does not affect unaugmented individuals at all, which makes it uniquely terrifying in a world where most professionals carry at least one neural implant. Corporate security teams with heavy cyberware loadouts are paradoxically more vulnerable than street-level operators with minimal augmentation. This has created a counter-culture of deliberately 'running light' on neural implants among certain mercenary circles who know they operate in Lacuna-hostile environments.

ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC developed the CBE-4 ostensibly as a non-lethal compliance tool for use in corporate detention scenarios. The weapon's designation as 'non-lethal' is technically accurate but practically disputed — targets caught mid-operation, mid-traffic, or in any situation requiring conscious agency have died in significant numbers. On the black market, it is sometimes called 'The Inheritance' because it leaves victims alive but stripped of who they were, at least temporarily.
Properties.aliases: Lacuna, The Bleeder, Gray Fog, Memory Eater
Properties.specifications:
form factor: Handheld emitter, 340mm barrel length, resembles oversized sidearm
effective range: 8–14 meters (cone, 40-degree spread)
power source: Zinc-ceramic capacitor cell, 6 shots per charge
weight: 1.4 kg
pulse duration: 0.3 seconds per discharge
effect duration: 40 seconds to 4 minutes depending on implant load
collateral radius: Cone-shaped — limited splash risk if aimed precisely
recharge time: 90 seconds between full discharges
Properties.tactical_use: Operators use the Lacuna as an opener in close-quarters corporate raids, firing into a security cluster before breaching. A single well-placed pulse can neutralize a four-person augmented security team simultaneously. It is also used in interrogation-adjacent scenarios — firing at a target to temporarily prevent them from accessing encrypted memory or executing a neural dead-man's switch. Extraction teams favor it for disabling high-value targets without causing physical damage that would complicate medical extraction.
Properties.cultural_context: The Lacuna occupies a unique psychological space in Meridian 88's weapon culture. It does not kill, does not visibly wound, and leaves no immediate trace — yet it is feared more viscerally than most lethal weapons by the augmented professional class. To be 'Lacuna'd' is slang for any sudden, humiliating lapse in competence. Corporate executives who survive an attack rarely speak of it publicly; the implication that their augmentations made them vulnerable is professionally damaging. Among street operators, carrying a Lacuna signals a preference for surgical, intelligence-driven work over brute force — it marks someone as a professional who thinks before shooting.
Properties.story_hooks: A fixer wakes up mid-job with no memory of the last six hours — the Lacuna was used on them, but by whom, and what did they do during those six hours?; A ZHENG-DAO whistleblower claims the CBE-4 has a hidden secondary mode that causes permanent rather than temporary erasure — and they have a victim to prove it.; A street operator running deliberately light on implants is hired specifically because they're Lacuna-immune, but the job turns out to be bait.; The black market supply of CBE-4 units has suddenly dried up — someone is buying every unit they can find, and the reason is unknown.

Nodes.Name: High-end fixers with non-lethal contract clauses
Interrogation facilitators working for mid-tier corps

Properties.description: The CPLM-7 is a fixed-wing loitering munition designed for extended area interdiction. Launched from a pneumatic tube canister or hand-thrown, it deploys a 1.4-meter carbon-composite delta wing and enters a silent, engine-off glide pattern over a designated kill zone, periodically reigniting its whisper-turbine to maintain altitude and orbit. The drone carries a shaped-charge warhead with a downward-facing fragmentation sleeve optimized for personnel targets rather than armor—a design choice that reflects its primary use case: denying movement through open urban terrain. It orbits silently at 80–120 meters, waiting.
Properties.aliases: The Halo, Waiting Room, Lazy Eye, Circle Drone
Properties.tier_availability: Military only (licensed variant); Tier 5+ black market (autonomous mode unlocked)
Properties.legality: Prohibited for civilian use; Military Licensed — autonomous mode requires Theater Weapons Authorization
Properties.specifications:
wingspan: 1.4 meters (deployed), 380mm (canister-stored, folded)
mass: 2.1 kg
warhead: Shaped charge with 180-degree downward fragmentation sleeve, lethal radius 8m, casualty radius 22m
loiter endurance: Up to 6.5 hours
operational altitude: 80–120 meters
acoustic signature: Less than 24 dB at operational altitude
target discrimination: Neural feedback loop, adaptive environmental baseline
confirmation window: 4 seconds (operator-confirm mode); 0 seconds (autonomous mode, restricted)
launch method: Pneumatic tube canister (standard) or hand-throw (emergency deployment)
self-destruct: Triggered on battery depletion or operator command; failsafe detonation if tampered
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed to hold corridors, deny extraction routes, or protect static positions without committing personnel. Corporate logistics convoys operating in contested districts use CPLM-7 units to sanitize parallel approach routes during transit windows. Extraction teams plant them as rear-guard measures before breaching an objective, ensuring pursuit is interrupted. The 4-second confirmation window creates a tactical rhythm that experienced operators learn to exploit—engaging a target, forcing them into the kill zone, then confirming strike. Counter-measures include acoustic detection arrays, high-altitude EMP bursts, and the crude but effective tactic of triggering the drone's strike early using a thermal decoy.
Properties.cultural_context: In the districts surrounding Meridian 88's logistics spine—particularly the Overpass Corridor and the Dry Docks—the CPLM-7 has become associated with corporate territorial enforcement during labor disputes and unauthorized market activity. Several widely-documented incidents involving Patience units deployed over informal markets have made the drone a potent symbol of corporate violence against civilian economic life. The phrase 'patience is a weapon' has been adopted by labor organizer collectives as an ironic slogan, and stenciled silhouettes of the delta-wing profile appear frequently as graffiti in affected districts.
Properties.story_hooks: Three CPLM-7 units in autonomous mode have been deployed over a six-block residential area in the Overpass Corridor. No one knows who deployed them or why. The units are still active. Getting residents out means moving through the kill zones.; An ARCTURUS internal memo, leaked to a street journalist, reveals that a CPLM-7 deployment during the Dry Docks labor action was authorized by a mid-level logistics manager, not military command. The manager has since disappeared. The journalist needs protection.; A player character is offered a decommissioned CPLM-7—battery dead, warhead supposedly inert—as payment for a job. Subsequent inspection suggests the warhead is not inert. Someone is trying to get rid of it without handling it themselves.; A Patience unit has been loitering over a specific rooftop in the Kowloon Stack for 11 days without striking. The rooftop is empty. Someone is keeping it aloft deliberately. Why?

Nodes.Name: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS contracted security operations
Black-market arms brokers (autonomous-mode units, limited supply)
Insurgent cells operating in the Dry Docks (captured or purchased units)

Properties.description:
The CDSC-4 operates by superchilling a proprietary suspension of metallic microfilaments to near-absolute-zero temperatures within a pressurized venting chamber, then expelling them in a radial scatter pattern via controlled cryogenic sublimation. Upon contact with biological tissue or conductive surfaces, the filaments undergo rapid thermal expansion as they absorb ambient heat, driving microscopic crystalline fractures into whatever they embed themselves in. Against unarmored targets, the result is a spreading lattice of internal micro-lacerations that are notoriously difficult to treat in field conditions.

What distinguishes the CDSC-4 from conventional cryo-weapons is its dual-phase delivery: the initial cold scatter causes immediate tissue shock and vasoconstriction, while the rebound thermal expansion phase — occurring roughly 4-8 seconds post-impact — causes secondary internal tearing. Operators describe the effect as 'planting seeds that bloom wrong.' The weapon is also uniquely effective against electronic systems, as the filaments can bridge microcontact points inside exposed hardware before the expansion phase shorts them catastrophically.

Manufactured by Arcturus Defense Solutions under a classified contract that has since lapsed, the CDSC-4 entered gray-market circulation after a logistics depot breach in the Meridian 88 outer ring. It has a distinctive wide-bore hexagonal muzzle and a frosted-glass reservoir tank that glows faint blue when charged. The weapon sweats condensation in humid environments, leaving a trail of moisture that experienced operators learn to account for tactically.
Properties.aliases: Frostbite, The Brancher, Dendrite Gun, Snowmaker
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 4–18 meters (scatter cone)
scatter angle: 22-degree radial arc
filament composition: Tungsten-titanium alloy, 0.003mm diameter
operating temperature: -271°C internal chamber
rebound delay: 4–8 seconds post-impact
reservoir capacity: 12 charges
weight: 6.8 kg fully loaded
recharge time: 45 seconds per charge (external cryo-cell required)
dimensions: 58cm barrel, 82cm overall
Properties.tactical_use: Primarily deployed in close-quarters breach scenarios where suppression and disabling without immediate lethality is acceptable — the delayed secondary phase gives operators a window to move before targets are fully incapacitated. Street-level operators favor it for crowd control and forcing retreats. More experienced users exploit the electronics-shorting capability against drone swarms and light mechs by firing into ventilation gaps. The weapon's scatter pattern makes it ineffective beyond 18 meters, limiting its role to interior engagements.
Properties.cultural_context: The CDSC-4 carries a grim reputation in Meridian 88's underground medical community — the micro-lacerations it causes are nearly invisible on initial triage scans, meaning victims often leave care and collapse hours later when the internal bleeding becomes critical. Street surgeons have taken to calling filament wounds 'slow gardens.' Possession of a Frostbite is considered a statement of deliberate cruelty in certain circles, and some fixer networks refuse contracts where one has been confirmed in use, citing liability for untreatable casualties.
Properties.story_hooks: A street surgeon approaches the players: three clients in a week have died 6-8 hours after being cleared as walking wounded. All show the same invisible internal lacing. Someone in the district is using a Frostbite and someone else is covering it up.; An Arcturus Defense Solutions fixer quietly offers a bounty for every CDSC-4 recovered — they claim it's a liability issue, but the serial numbers on the recovered units don't match any official production run.; A player character is hit by filament scatter during an ambush. They feel fine. Properties.description:
The CFDM-4 functions as an area-denial mine that weaponizes rapid thermal collapse rather than explosive fragmentation. When triggered, the device releases a supercooled liquid nitrogen–fluorocarbon suspension under high pressure, generating a localized temperature drop of approximately -140°C within a 5-meter radius in under 300 milliseconds. The initial cold burst is sufficient to induce thermal shock fracturing in exposed biological tissue, hydraulic lines, pneumatic systems, and certain grades of ballistic polymer armor. Materials that survive the cold phase are then subjected to a secondary micro-explosive disbursement — small shaped charges embedded in the mine casing fire outward, turning any ice-crystallized surface in the blast radius into a secondary fragmentation field.

The two-phase kill mechanism — freeze, then shatter — was pioneered by ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC's materials warfare division, originally as a method for disabling cryogenically sensitive bioelectric infrastructure without fire risk. The military application emerged when field engineers noted that the suspension compound caused catastrophic embrittlement in articulated armor joints and cybernetic limb housing. A target who survives the cold burst is often physically immobilized by seized joint systems, making the mine effective as both a lethal and incapacitation device depending on range.

On Meridian 88's black market, 'Coldsnap' mines are prized by teams operating against heavily augmented targets — the embrittlement effect is disproportionately effective against high-density cybernetic installation. Veterans of the corporate border wars describe the aftermath of a CFDM-4 detonation as 'a room full of broken statues,' a description that has become part of the weapon's grim mythology.
Properties.specifications:
primary radius: 5m cryogenic burst
secondary radius: 3m fragmentation
temperature drop: -140°C at ground zero
coolant compound: LN2-fluorocarbon suspension, classified grade
trigger options: Pressure plate, tripwire, IR proximity, remote detonation
arming delay: 4 seconds post-placement
weight: 2.1 kg
height: 11cm diameter disc profile
detonation sequence: Burst phase 0–300ms / fragmentation phase 310–420ms
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed as area-denial in corridors and chokepoints where augmented targets are expected. Particularly effective in server room raids and bioelectric facility assaults where hydraulic and pneumatic systems are present — the cold burst disables environmental support systems simultaneously with personnel. Teams often pair CFDM-4s with thermal imaging to exploit the heat signature contrast of freshly frozen surfaces. Anti-personnel squads targeting heavily cybered enforcers use them as primary engagement tools rather than last resort.
Properties.cultural_context: ZHENG-DAO markets the CFDM-4 to military clients as 'infrastructure-selective area denial,' emphasizing its effectiveness against mechanized targets. In practice, the weapon's ability to selectively devastate augmented humans has made it a symbol of the city's simmering tension between full-flesh populations and the heavily modified. Some anti-augmentation extremist groups have attempted to acquire surplus units, and ZHENG-DAO has faced significant public pressure over its distribution policies. The name 'Brittle' is used derisively by augmented communities to describe the weapon — and sometimes the people who use it.
Properties.story_hooks: A CFDM-4 mine detonates in a civilian augmentation clinic — someone is sending a message, and ZHENG-DAO is desperate to prove the mine wasn't theirs.; The party is hired to clear a derelict facility and discovers it has been mined with CFDM-4s — the placement pattern suggests someone who knew exactly where augmented security personnel would walk.; A ZHENG-DAO insider leaks documents suggesting the CFDM-4's embrittlement compound has long-term neurological effects on survivors — effects ZHENG-DAO has known about for years.; A heavily augmented fixer approaches the party with a contract: steal a pallet of CFDM-4s from a corporate depot before they can be sold to a buyer whose identity she won't reveal.

Properties.description:
The CPE-2 projects a sustained beam of cryogenically accelerated nitrogen-fluoride compound cooled to approximately -196°C through a thermoelectric expansion nozzle, flash-freezing tissue and material on contact. The weapon's operating principle combines rapid endothermic chemical expansion with a focused pressure gradient that drives the cryogenic medium into surface pores and micro-fractures, causing catastrophic embrittlement in both organic and inorganic targets within 1.5 to 3 seconds of sustained exposure.

The distinctive characteristic of the CPE-2 is its secondary 'fracture pulse' feature — a piezoelectric vibration emitter integrated into the barrel shroud that, when activated after a freeze cycle, transmits a precisely tuned mechanical shock through a frozen target. Against armored personnel, this shatters limbs and joint assemblies without requiring direct impact force, effectively defeating articulated plate systems that would resist conventional trauma. Against materials, the pulse can bring down reinforced doors, weapon mounts, and vehicle panels.

OUROBOROS ENERGY developed the CPE-2 originally as an industrial tool for controlled demolition in pressurized environments where thermal charges posed catastrophic risks. Military and enforcement contracts followed within eighteen months of the first commercial release, and the design was quietly hardened for field use. The civilian demolition variant remains available at lower tiers, but the fracture-pulse module is excised and the nozzle geometry limits range to 4 meters.
Properties.legality: Licensed (civilian); Prohibited (fracture-pulse variant without military credential)
Properties.specifications:
operating temperature output: -196°C (nominal)
cryogenic medium: Nitrogen-fluoride compound, pressurized reservoir
reservoir capacity: 8 sustained-beam seconds or 22 burst pulses
effective range military: Up to 9 m (sustained beam); 6 m (fracture pulse)
effective range civilian: Up to 4 m
freeze cycle to embrittlement: 1.5–3 seconds (tissue); 3–6 seconds (Class II armor)
weight: 3.4 kg (loaded)
power source: Thermoelectric cell + pressurized chemical reservoir
length: 61 cm
Properties.tactical_use: CPE-2 operators typically work in pairs: one applies the freeze beam to a target or barrier while the second delivers mechanical force or a fracture pulse to complete the kill or breach. Solo operators learn to integrate freeze-then-pulse into a single deliberate action sequence. The weapon is particularly valued in environments where fire or explosive overpressure would endanger infrastructure — pressurized habitats, chemical storage facilities, and confined server vaults. It is slow compared to kinetic alternatives, demanding careful target selection.
Properties.cultural_context: Among Meridian 88's industrial workforce, the civilian CPE-2 is a common demolition tool with no particular social weight. The military variant, however, is associated with OUROBOROS ENERGY's enforcement arm — a gray-zone private force that operates in the corporation's energy extraction zones. Workers in those zones know what a Frostbite means when it appears: OUROBOROS is done negotiating. In the black market, fracture-pulse modules are sold separately for significant sums, and modified civilian units are a staple of mid-tier criminal arsenals.
Properties.story_hooks: A labor strike in an OUROBOROS extraction zone has turned violent — the corporation's enforcers are using CPE-2s against workers in a pressurized habitat, and the players must intervene without triggering a hull breach.; Someone is selling fracture-pulse modules on the black market using OUROBOROS military serial numbers that predate the CPE-2's public release — implying a secret early production run.; A player character's contact is found frozen solid in a location with no industrial equipment nearby — someone is using a CPE-2 for targeted assassination and making it look accidental.; OUROBOROS contracts the players to recover a stolen military CPE-2 before a rival corporation can reverse-engineer the fracture-pulse module.

Properties.description:
The CSPR-2 delivers a tightly focused ultrasonic pulse tuned to induce rapid phase transition in synovial fluid — the viscous lubricating liquid present in all biological joints. Under the rifle's beam, synovial fluid undergoes a violent cavitation process, briefly forming microscopic crystalline structures that expand and collapse within milliseconds. The mechanical result is catastrophic joint failure: cartilage shear, capsule rupture, and acute inflammatory response, all without any visible external wound. Targets drop and cannot stand. The damage is real, structural, and in most cases permanent without surgical intervention.

The weapon's targeting system requires a 0.3-second dwell time on a specific anatomical zone — typically the knee, hip, or shoulder — before the pulse achieves sufficient depth to trigger the phase cascade. This dwell requirement means the CSPR-2 is not a snap-fire weapon; it rewards patience and positional advantage. Arcturus Defense Solutions engineered a secondary 'scatter mode' into the CSPR-2 that defocuses the beam to affect a broader joint region at reduced intensity, useful against moving targets at the cost of predictable effect severity.

The weapon earned its street name 'Kneemaker' almost immediately after early units leaked into Meridian 88's black market. Its use as a tool of deliberate permanent injury — rather than killing — gave it a particular cultural weight. To be 'kneemade' is a specific category of violence in the city's underworld lexicon, implying a calculated, professional decision to maim rather than kill. This specificity made it a favored instrument of organized crime enforcement and a symbol of a particular kind of cold, methodical cruelty.
Properties.aliases: Kneemaker, The Grinder, CSPR, Fluid Gun
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 5–60 meters
power source: High-density ultrasonic emitter cell, 14 shots per charge
dwell requirement: 0.3 seconds standard, 0.5 seconds scatter mode
joint penetration depth: Up to 9 cm through clothing and soft tissue
weight: 3.4 kg
form factor: Long-barreled precision rifle, integrated anatomical targeting reticle
biological augmentation note: Synthetic joint replacements are fully immune; cartilage-preserving partial augments remain vulnerable
Properties.tactical_use: The CSPR-2 is most effective in overwatch and ambush configurations where the operator can achieve a stable firing position and hold dwell time. Criminal enforcement teams use it to deliver non-fatal but permanent consequences to debtors, informants, or competitors — the implicit message being that the shooter could have killed but chose not to. Military and paramilitary users value it for denial operations: a target with destroyed knees cannot pursue, escape, or fight effectively, freeing the operator to control the engagement tempo. Counter-use training emphasizes constant movement and unpredictable lateral shifts to break dwell acquisition.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88's organized crime hierarchy, the act of 'kneemading' someone carries specific social meaning — it is a statement of ownership, a demonstration that the perpetrator has the patience and resources to choose how much harm they inflict. Street crews who can afford a CSPR-2 and the operator to use it are signaling a level of organizational sophistication. Conversely, victims of the weapon carry their limping gait as a permanent, visible marker of a debt unpaid or a line crossed. Prosthetic joint clinics in the lower districts have quietly built entire service lines around CSPR-2 injuries.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of prominent city officials have been 'kneemade' in public spaces over three weeks. No demands have been made. Someone is sending a message, but no one can agree on what it says.; A CSPR-2 unit recovered from a crime scene has Arcturus Defense Solutions military serial numbers that shouldn't exist on any civilian or black-market unit — it came directly from a military stockpile.; A prosthetic joint surgeon in the lower districts has started keeping records of every CSPR-2 injury she treats. She's noticed a pattern in the targets and is looking for someone to help her understand it.; An Arcturus insider claims the CSPR-2's scatter mode was specifically engineered at a client's request — and that client was not a military organization.

Properties.description:
The DIF-2 exploits the electrochemical conductivity differential between the outer epidermal layer and the subdermal tissue beneath it. By projecting a modulated galvanic induction field tuned specifically to the resistivity of keratin and melanin-dense skin cells, the Flayer induces rapid, uncontrolled ion migration across the dermal barrier — effectively causing the outer skin layer to experience electrochemical dissolution while deeper tissue remains unaffected. The result is an intensely painful surface-level effect that produces the sensation of being flayed alive without immediately life-threatening damage. Extended exposure causes genuine dermal separation.

Helix Biosystems developed the DIF-2 originally as a dermatological instrument for accelerated wound debridement in field surgery — removing necrotic tissue via targeted induction rather than physical scraping. The weaponized variant was a modification that required minimal engineering effort: simply increasing field intensity and broadening the emission cone from surgical precision to area coverage. The weapon's emitter looks almost identical to a medical debridement wand, a fact that has been exploited extensively for smuggling.

At non-lethal settings the DIF-2 is one of the most effective interrogation and compliance tools available — subjects describe the sensation as fire being poured under their skin, and the psychological impact of watching their own skin begin to separate is significant even before serious physiological damage occurs. At maximum output sustained for more than four seconds, tissue damage becomes permanent and potentially fatal through shock and infection exposure.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: Contact to 6 meters (cone emission)
emission cone: 45 degrees at maximum spread
power source: Helix BioCell Mk.2 (continuous 90-second operation per cell)
weight: 0.9 kg
length: 34 cm (wand form factor)
intensity settings: Variable dial, 1–10
medical certification: Carries forged Helix Biosystems surgical instrument certification
thermal signature: Negligible — passes most scanner profiles as medical equipment
Properties.tactical_use: The DIF-2 is primarily a compliance and interrogation weapon rather than a combat tool. Enforcement operators use it at low settings to rapidly clear confined spaces — the effect is too overwhelming for most subjects to push through. In interrogation contexts it is valued for leaving minimal lasting evidence at low settings while being psychologically catastrophic. Combat-trained operators occasionally use it as a close-range deterrent, sweeping the cone across a group to break formation.
Properties.cultural_context: The DIF-2 occupies a specific place in Meridian 88's underground economy: it is the weapon most associated with private detention facilities, corporate black sites, and the interrogation wings of organized crime operations. Its medical origins give it a veneer of clinical detachment that many users find either reassuring or deeply disturbing depending on their perspective. Street medics who discover a DIF-2 in a patient's belongings know to ask very careful questions about where that patient has been.
Properties.story_hooks: A street medic treating a patient with unusual dermal injuries recognizes them as DIF-2 exposure — the patient claims they've never been detained.; The party recovers a shipment of what appears to be Helix surgical equipment; half the 'debridement wands' are DIF-2s with the intensity limiters removed.; A whistleblower from a corporate black site wants to expose DIF-2 use but needs the party to retrieve physical evidence before it's sanitized.; Someone is using a DIF-2 at maximum setting as a murder weapon, targeting people with specific dermal augmentations — the conductivity differential is even more extreme in modded skin.

Properties.description:
The DFAD-1 is a slow-moving, low-altitude deployment drone purpose-built to construct dielectric filament barriers in real time across doorways, corridors, stairwells, and open terrain. It carries a spool of sub-millimeter piezoelectric composite filament — nearly invisible at distances beyond two meters — which it anchors to surfaces using micro-adhesive pitons fired from an onboard pneumatic launcher. Once a filament network is constructed, any conductive surface (including human skin, wet clothing, and most cybernetic chassis components) completing a circuit across two or more strands receives a sharp, high-voltage piezoelectric discharge: non-lethal at standard settings, but sufficient to trigger involuntary muscular contraction and momentary loss of fine motor control.

The DFAD-1's operational profile is inherently architectural. It doesn't pursue targets — it re-shapes the environment to punish movement through it. Operators can pre-program specific filament geometries, or allow the drone to autonomously map a space and generate optimized barrier configurations based on room geometry and estimated foot traffic patterns. A fully deployed web in a standard corridor can process three to five contact events before filament degradation requires restringing. The drone carries enough spool material for approximately 80 meters of filament deployment.

HELIX BIOSYSTEMS' involvement is non-obvious given the weapon's apparent mechanical simplicity, but the piezoelectric composite filament is a direct derivative of their synthetic tendon research program — the discharge profile was tuned to match the threshold for neuromuscular disruption without cardiac risk, a specification that required significant biological modeling.
Properties.specifications:
dimensions: 28 cm length, 14 cm width, hexapod rotor configuration
weight: 1.1 kg
filament spool capacity: 80 m total
filament diameter: 0.3 mm
discharge voltage: 800–1,200 V (adjustable), <0.5 J per event
contact events per strand: 3–5 before degradation
deployment speed: ~4 m of filament per minute
flight ceiling: 8 m (designed for interior use)
battery life: 35 minutes active deployment, 90 minutes standby
detection difficulty: High — filament visible only under UV light or at acute angles
countermeasures: Insulated suit underlayer, UV detection goggles, directed heat (melts filament)
Properties.tactical_use: Security teams deploy DFAD-1 units to establish denial zones around high-value assets, forward operating positions, or escape routes. A single drone can web an apartment's worth of interior space in under ten minutes. Offensive operators use them to channel enemy movement into prepared kill zones — targets who hit a web strand and spasm are predictably funneled toward exits that aren't webbed. In siege contexts, teams run multiple DFAD-1 units sequentially to maintain barrier integrity as strands degrade.
Properties.cultural_context: The DFAD-1 occupies an unusual niche in Meridian 88's weapon culture — it's too slow and non-confrontational for crews that value aggression, but deeply respected among those who prioritize control and preparation. Safe-house operators, information brokers, and reclusive fixers favor it for perimeter security. A space known to be webbed by DFAD-1 filament carries a specific social meaning: whoever occupies it is patient, paranoid, and has thought through the geometry of the room more carefully than you have. Finding a strand while sweeping a location is considered a significant warning sign.
Properties.story_hooks: A contact's safe house has gone dark. When the party arrives, the entire building has been webbed floor-to-ceiling by what appears to be a DFAD-1 running continuously on a loop — but the drone is gone and the contact is still inside, immobilized in a corner, unwilling to speak above a whisper.; HELIX BIOSYSTEMS is suing a third-party manufacturer for producing counterfeit DFAD-1 filament spools. The counterfeit spools have a different discharge profile — one tuned not to stop at the cardiac threshold. Someone is selling them as standard units.; The party needs to cross three floors of a building that a rival crew has had twelve hours to prepare. They've acquired a UV scanner and know DFAD-1 units were delivered. The question is how many webs, and whether the crew knew the party was coming.
