Properties.description:
The DHE-4 operates by projecting a focused dielectric heating field tuned to the resonant absorption frequency of subcutaneous lipid tissue. Unlike thermal weapons that char or ignite surface material, the Blister bypasses the outer dermis almost entirely, depositing concentrated microwave-band energy into the fat and fluid layers beneath. The result is rapid steam generation inside the body — pressure builds faster than the skin can vent it, producing characteristic blistering, rupture, and in sustained exposures, catastrophic subcutaneous delamination.

What distinguishes the DHE-4 from broader-spectrum thermal emitters is its tunable penetration depth. A rotary selector on the grip adjusts the emission frequency across seven discrete bands, allowing operators to target shallow nerve clusters, mid-depth musculature, or deep organ cavities depending on the mission profile. At its shallowest setting, the weapon functions as a non-lethal pain compliance tool. At maximum depth, it is a slow, deliberate execution instrument. This range has made it simultaneously attractive to corporate security contractors and deeply controversial among humanitarian legal bodies.

ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC originally developed the DHE-4 under a medical research contract — the underlying tech was intended for non-invasive tumour ablation. When internal testing revealed its weapons potential, the project was quietly reclassified. The medical division was dissolved eighteen months later. Current production runs are manufactured under a shell subsidiary and distributed through licensed security channels, though the black market supply significantly outpaces official figures.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 4–18 metres
penetration depth range: 2mm–14cm (frequency-dependent)
frequency bands: 7 discrete settings (2.4 GHz – 18 GHz)
power source: DHE cell cartridge (22 sustained exposures per charge)
weight: 2.1 kg
form factor: Compact emitter pistol with rotating frequency collar
heat signature: High (emitter array reaches 340°C during sustained fire)
safety interlock: Biometric grip authentication
Properties.tactical_use: Interrogation-adjacent field work, crowd dispersal at shallow settings, close-quarters anti-personnel at deep settings. Operators frequently use the shallow band to disorient armoured targets whose suits lack microwave shielding on the torso underlay. Sustained mid-band exposure through light cover (wood, plastic, thin composite) is effective — the field degrades slowly through non-metallic barriers. Metallic armour and Faraday-lined suits provide near-complete protection, which limits the weapon's utility against well-equipped military targets.
Properties.cultural_context: The Blister carries a particular stigma even in Meridian 88's desensitised weapons culture. Its association with slow, internal suffering — the sound victims make, described by witnesses as 'wet and muffled' — has given it a reputation as a torturer's weapon. Corporate enforcers who carry it openly are making a specific statement about their employer's methods. In the Underbelly districts, possession of a DHE-4 is treated as evidence of affiliation with certain extraction outfits regardless of stated purpose. Some street medics have learned to reverse-engineer the shallow settings for legitimate burn treatment, which has created a strange parallel legitimacy for the device.
Properties.story_hooks: A shipment of DHE-4s is traced back to a ZHENG-DAO medical subsidiary that officially doesn't exist — someone inside the corp is leaking production records and the players are hired to find out who before the whistleblower reaches a journalist.; A street medic in the Underbelly has been using a modified DHE-4 for tumour ablation on patients who can't afford clinic access. When one of her patients dies from a miscalibrated setting, she becomes the prime suspect in what looks like a targeted killing.; The players are hired to retrieve a DHE-4 prototype — frequency band 8, which doesn't appear on any public documentation — from a corporate courier who has gone off-grid.; An enforcer known for carrying a Blister has been found dead, killed by a wound pattern consistent with DHE-4 exposure. Someone used his own weapon on him and left it at the scene.

Properties.description:
The Dielectric Phase Inversion Glove is a full-hand wearable weapons platform that generates a controlled dielectric phase inversion field across the glove's outer surface, activated through a pressure-sensitive grip trigger integrated into the palm. On contact with a target, the field inverts the dielectric properties of whatever material it touches — organic tissue, polymer armor, composite materials — causing a rapid destabilization of molecular bonding at the contact interface. Against unprotected flesh, this manifests as a severe disruption of nerve conduction and localized cellular delamination; the sensation is described by those who survive brief contact as 'my hand stopped being my hand.' Against armored surfaces, the inversion causes surface-layer spalling and micro-fracturing that degrades protective integrity over repeated contacts.

ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC developed the DPIG-4 as part of their covert operations wearables line, specifically addressing the need for a weapon with zero ballistic signature — no projectile, no beam, no audible discharge. In a world saturated with acoustic and optical sensors, a weapon that kills through a handshake is functionally invisible to most surveillance architectures. The glove itself is visually indistinguishable from premium smart-fabric work gloves at a casual inspection; the activation hardware is embedded in the lining, and the power cell is housed in a slim cuff that passes as a fashion accessory.

The DPIG-4's weakness is its requirement for physical contact, which demands that operators be trained in close-contact engagement. ZHENG-DAO sells it exclusively through channels that require the purchaser to demonstrate certified hand-to-hand combat proficiency — a requirement that is circumvented regularly on the black market. The weapon has a disquieting cultural resonance: in Meridian 88, where business deals, social hierarchies, and criminal agreements are all sealed with physical contact, the idea that a handshake could be a lethal act has entered the city's social paranoia.
Properties.aliases: Secondskin, The Handshake, White Glove, Liar's Hand
Properties.tier_availability: Black market; official sales restricted to ZHENG-DAO approved contractors
Properties.legality: Prohibited — classified as an assassination device under Meridian 88 Covert Weapons Statute 7
Properties.specifications:
activation method: Palm pressure trigger — 0.3 kg activation threshold
field duration: Continuous while grip engaged
power source: ZHENG-DAO FlexCell cuff battery — 40 minutes continuous use
field intensity: Adjustable via thumb-dial: suppression / incapacitation / lethal
weight: 180 grams (glove and cuff combined)
detection: Passes standard metal detection; fails advanced bioelectric scanners
recharge time: 22 minutes via standard port
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed almost exclusively in close-access covert operations: assassinations designed to appear natural, interrogations in monitored environments, and bodyguard-penetration scenarios. Operators are trained to use the suppression setting for control and compliance, escalating only when lethal authorization is confirmed. The glove's invisibility to standard security scans makes it the preferred weapon for operations inside secure facilities where ballistic weapons cannot be brought in. Some operators wear two — one set to suppression, one to lethal — on opposite hands.
Properties.cultural_context: The Secondskin has seeded a specific social anxiety in Meridian 88's business and criminal elite: contact paranoia. High-value individuals have begun refusing handshakes, insisting on observed physical greetings, or wearing their own bioelectric detection rings. The phenomenon has been covered in lifestyle media as a quirky security trend, but its roots are in genuine documented cases of DPIG-4 assassinations. Ironically, ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC's own executive staff are rumored to wear detection hardware at all public appearances.
Properties.story_hooks: A prominent criminal arbitrator dies of apparent cardiac arrest during a deal. The coroner finds nothing — but a street-level fixer notices the arbitrator's hand has a faint cellular delamination pattern that matches DPIG-4 contact. Someone at that table was wearing one.; A DPIG-4 surfaces with its intensity dial removed and replaced with a fixed lethal-only circuit. The modification is clean and professional. ZHENG-DAO wants to know who performed it — because it wasn't one of their engineers.; A new bioelectric detection ring is flooding the market, supposedly able to identify an active DPIG-4 within arm's reach. The rings are real — but they're manufactured by ZHENG-DAO under a shell brand. The company is selling the antidote to its own poison.; An operator is hired to retrieve a DPIG-4 from a target who doesn't know they have it — it was planted in their belongings to frame them for a killing that hasn't happened yet.

Properties.description:
The DVHA-2 exploits a specific vulnerability of the biological eye: the vitreous humor, the gel-like fluid filling the posterior chamber of the eyeball, is a dielectric medium with a distinct electrical permittivity that differs measurably from surrounding tissue. By projecting a rapid-cycling dielectric field tuned to this permittivity differential, the weapon induces micro-agitation within the vitreous humor — essentially causing the gel to vibrate at a frequency that generates internal pressure waves against the retina and the posterior lens. The immediate effect is severe visual disruption: targets experience a blizzard of phosphene flashes, cascading floaters, and a complete loss of coherent image formation for several minutes.

At higher power settings, the DVHA-2's agitation effect can cause partial vitreous detachment — the gel pulling away from the retinal surface — which produces longer-duration visual impairment and, in some cases, permanent retinal complications. Tessera Corponation's medical division originally developed the underlying dielectric targeting technology for ophthalmic surgery, specifically for non-contact manipulation of intraocular structures. The weapons application emerged from a defense contract that Tessera has since officially terminated, though production of the DVHA-2 continues through a subsidiary operating under a different name.

The weapon's street name 'Snowglobe' comes from how affected targets describe their visual experience: a chaotic swirl of bright specks and moving shapes, as if their vision had been shaken like a decorative snow globe. The name has also been applied metaphorically in Meridian 88 street slang — to 'snowglobe' someone means to thoroughly disorient them, whether through the weapon or through information overload and deception.
Properties.aliases: Snowglobe, The Shaker, Floater Gun, DVHA
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 1–35 meters
power source: Compact dielectric field generator cell, 25 shots per charge
effect duration standard: 3–7 minutes complete visual disruption
effect duration high power: Potential partial vitreous detachment; impairment up to 48 hours
weight: 1.4 kg
form factor: Compact sidearm profile with adjustable power dial
targeting requirement: Must achieve line-of-sight to target's eye region; effective through standard eyewear; blocked by opaque face shields
augmentation note: Fully cybernetic ocular replacements are immune; biological eyes with implanted lenses retain partial vulnerability
Properties.tactical_use: The DVHA-2 is a precision blinding tool, most effective in engagements where temporarily removing a target's vision creates a decisive advantage without generating a lethal outcome. Extraction teams use it to blind security personnel at key moments �� a three-minute vision blackout is enough to move a person through a checkpoint. Close-protection operatives carry it as a first-response tool to create distance from an attacker. In competitive underworld contexts, it is used to humiliate rather than harm — 'snowglobing' a rival in public, leaving them stumbling and helpless, is a specific form of social violence. High-power use as a permanent blinding tool is illegal even under its restricted license, a line that operators cross with increasing frequency.
Properties.cultural_context: The DVHA-2 sits at an interesting intersection in Meridian 88's weapon culture. Its restricted-legal status means it appears in both sanctioned security contexts and criminal ones, and the same weapon model is carried by corporate bodyguards and street enforcers alike. The metaphorical use of 'snowglobe' in the city's slang has given the weapon a cultural presence beyond its physical use — media, information brokers, and con artists all use the term. Among the augmentation-reliant community, the weapon represents a specific anxiety about the value of unaugmented biological senses: your eyes are a vulnerability that money can solve, and those who haven't spent that money know it. Tessera Corponation's continued involvement through subsidiaries is an open secret that the city's investigative press has reported on repeatedly without legal consequence.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone has modified a batch of DVHA-2s to lock permanently on high-power mode with the safety override removed. The units are indistinguishable from standard models until fired. They're already in circulation.; A Tessera Corponation subsidiary has been quietly approached by a buyer wanting DVHA-2 units in quantities that suggest crowd deployment — not individual use. The subsidiary contact wants out and needs help disappearing.; Three witnesses to a major corporate crime have all independently reported sudden severe visual impairment that their doctors can't explain through any standard cause. The symptom profile matches high-power DVHA-2 exposure.; A black-market ophthalmologist is offering a vitreous humor replacement procedure that provides immunity to the DVHA-2 — the synthetic gel she's using is proprietary, and its origin traces back to Tessera's original ophthalmic surgery program in ways that shouldn't be possible.

Properties.description:
The DOC-7 is a shaped-charge demolition device engineered to produce a unidirectional pressure wave rather than an omnidirectional blast. Unlike conventional explosives that waste energy in all directions simultaneously, the DOC-7 uses a parabolic copper-composite reflector plate cast directly into the charge body. On detonation, the reflector focuses approximately 78% of the blast energy into a forward cone of roughly 40 degrees, producing an overpressure front capable of collapsing reinforced concrete walls, shearing door mechanisms, and incapacitating personnel in the target corridor without destroying the structure behind the operator.

The charge uses a linear magnetic acceleration trigger system: a small magnetic initiator rail drives a tungsten striker into the primary detonator at precisely calibrated velocity, ensuring consistent detonation timing regardless of ambient temperature or humidity — a common failure point in legacy explosive initiators used in Meridian 88's variable-climate sublevels. This consistency makes the DOC-7 reliable in flooded infrastructure, high-EMF environments, and extreme cold, all common conditions in the city's lower tiers.

PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION originally developed the DOC-7 for controlled demolition of condemned hab-blocks, where precision was necessary to avoid collapsing adjacent structures. The design was licensed to ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS, who militarized it with a magnetic initiator rail and reduced the charge mass for operator carry. The civilian and military versions are nearly identical in external appearance, a fact that has created significant legal ambiguity in Meridian 88's courts.
Properties.manufacturer: PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION (civilian) / ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS (military variant)
Properties.specifications:
weight: 1.2kg
dimensions: 180mm x 90mm x 70mm
blast cone: 40-degree forward arc
effective range: Up to 12m in target cone
blast energy focus: 78% forward, 22% lateral/rear
initiator: Magnetic rail-driven tungsten striker
back blast zone: 2m — operator must not stand directly behind
wall penetration: Up to 220mm reinforced concrete
Properties.tactical_use: Standard use is magnetic attachment to a door, wall, or bulkhead, followed by operator withdrawal to the side — never behind — before remote or timed detonation. The directional blast breaches the target structure and incapacitates anyone within the forward cone, while the operator position avoids the back-blast. In military use, DOC-7s are stacked in sequence for breach-and-clear operations through multiple walls. Some operators use them defensively, mounting them on tripwires to channelize enemy movement into the blast cone.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88's construction and demolition industry, DOC-7s are familiar tools — licensed contractors carry them routinely for teardown work in the condemned mid-tier hab districts. This normalizes their presence in ways that make them difficult to police. The military variant is distinguished by its matte-black housing versus the civilian orange, but both can be operated identically. Criminal organizations favor them for vault breaching. The phrase 'sending the push' has entered street slang as a term for delivering an ultimatum that cannot be refused.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of fatal 'demolition accidents' in the mid-tier hab district all involve DOC-7 detonations — but the buildings weren't condemned, and the victims weren't workers.; A player needs to breach a corporate vault and acquires a DOC-7 through a construction contact — only to discover the device is the military variant, recently stolen, and ARCTURUS is actively tracking it.; PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION's civilian DOC-7 licensing database has been hacked and all records deleted. Someone is making legitimate-looking units disappear off the books.

Nodes.Name: PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION (civilian) / ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS (military variant)
Vault thieves and corporate espionage operators

Properties.description: The DOL-3 projects a sustained stream of catalytically accelerated oxidation agents — a proprietary OUROBOROS ENERGY compound designated OX-7 — delivered in a superheated plasma carrier that allows the agent to penetrate surface coatings and begin attacking the metallic substrates beneath. Against standard materials, this is a moderate industrial cutting tool. Against cybernetic implants, it is a weapon of unusual cruelty: OX-7 is specifically formulated to attack the ferrous and titanium alloys most commonly used in structural cybernetic components, causing rapid surface degradation that generates heat as a byproduct. An implant struck by the Rustmaker does not simply fail — it heats from within as its structural integrity deteriorates, causing thermal burns to surrounding tissue from the inside outward while simultaneously seizing joints and locking mechanical augmentations in place.
Properties.aliases: Rustmaker, The Oxidizer, Iron Lung, Corrosion Rod
Properties.specifications:
form factor: Heavy two-handed configuration, 920mm length, with rear-mounted OX-7 canister and integrated plasma excitation chamber
effective range: Up to 12 meters sustained stream; 6 meters for full catalytic effect
power source: Integrated plasma coil, powered by weapon's own battery cell; OX-7 canister provides approximately 15 seconds of sustained fire
weight: 4.8 kg (with full OX-7 canister)
stream temperature: 400–600°C at plasma carrier exit
OX-7 catalytic onset: 0.8 seconds on contact with target alloy
effect on unaugmented targets: Severe thermal burns — effective but non-specific
effect on cybernetic targets: Structural degradation, thermal seizure of mechanical components, internal thermal burns from implant heat generation
canister replacement time: 12 seconds
Properties.tactical_use: The Rustmaker originated as an industrial tool for controlled demolition of cybernetic infrastructure — primarily used by OUROBOROS ENERGY crews decommissioning old implant manufacturing lines. The weaponized variant entered black market circulation when operators realized its unique effectiveness against heavily augmented combatants who had essentially traded biological vulnerability for cybernetic vulnerability. In combat, it is used at close range against targets whose subdermal plating defeats conventional ammunition — the oxidation agent bypasses surface hardening by attacking material composition rather than structure. It is a last-resort weapon in most operational contexts due to its weight, limited ammunition, and the difficulty of operating it in enclosed spaces.
Properties.cultural_context: The Rustmaker carries significant symbolic weight in Meridian 88's political landscape. Anti-augmentation extremist groups have adopted it as an ideological weapon, and incidents of its use against augmentation clinics and prosthetics workshops have made it a charged symbol. For heavily augmented individuals, the threat of the Rustmaker represents a specific existential horror — not just death, but the betrayal of the body they have built, their augmentations turned against them. OUROBOROS ENERGY has faced significant reputational damage from the weaponized variant's association with extremist violence, despite their insistence that the industrial variant serves legitimate purposes.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of attacks on augmentation clinics using Rustmakers has been attributed to a known extremist group — but the OX-7 compound used is from a batch that was never sold commercially, pointing back to OUROBOROS ENERGY itself.; A character's critical cybernetic limb has been partially oxidized in an attack — it still functions, but structural integrity is compromised and failure is inevitable without replacement they can't afford.; A weapons dealer is offering DOL-3 units at suspiciously low prices in bulk — someone is trying to flood a specific district before an event, and figuring out which event is the urgent question.; OUROBOROS ENERGY hires operators to recover a stolen industrial DOL-3 unit before it can be converted to its weaponized configuration — but the thieves turn out to have more sympathetic motives than expected.

Nodes.Name: Operators working anti-cyborg contracts for unknown clients
OUROBOROS ENERGY security teams (industrial variant, occasionally deployed in facility defense)
A bounty hunter known as 'Patina' who specializes in cybernetic fugitive retrieval and uses the DOL-3 to disable augmented targets non-lethally through implant seizure

Properties.description:
The EDS-2 generates a fine aerosol of electrochemically activated solvent compounds by passing a base liquid reagent through a high-voltage ionization grid immediately before ejection. The ionization process transforms the reagent from an inert transport medium into a highly reactive dissolution agent that aggressively attacks both organic polymers and biological lipid membranes. The spray itself is nearly invisible — a faint iridescent shimmer in direct light — making it exceptionally difficult to detect in dimly lit environments until contact is made.

What makes the EDS-2 distinctively dangerous is the selectivity of its ionization profile. By adjusting the voltage gradient on the ionization grid via a thumb dial on the grip, operators can tune the reagent's reactivity toward organic tissue, synthetic materials, or a balanced blend of both. At maximum organic setting, it strips exposed skin and mucous membranes within seconds; at maximum synthetic setting, it dissolves polymer armor coatings, adhesives, and certain cybernetic housing materials. The mixed setting is considered the most tactically versatile but produces a caustic byproduct fog that requires the operator to wear sealed respiratory protection.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric developed the EDS-2 ostensibly as an industrial decontamination tool for hazardous polymer environments, and it remains technically legal as such in several Meridian 88 jurisdictions — a loophole that has made it a favorite of operators who need plausible deniability on weapon checks. The weapon is recognizable by its wide conical nozzle, dual reagent tanks (one base liquid, one ionization catalyst), and the faint electrical crackling audible during active discharge.
Properties.aliases: Lacquer, The Stripper, Acid Fog, Zheng's Kiss
Properties.legality: Restricted (licensed industrial use only; unlicensed carry Prohibited)
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 2–12 meters (aerosol cone)
dispersal angle: 15-degree cone
reagent capacity: Base tank: 400ml / Catalyst tank: 200ml
ionization voltage: 8,000–14,000V adjustable
tuning modes: Organic (O-mode), Synthetic (S-mode), Mixed (M-mode)
continuous discharge duration: Approximately 22 seconds per full tank
weight: 4.2 kg loaded
operator protection required: Sealed respiratory mask recommended in M-mode
dimensions: 44cm overall, 18cm nozzle assembly
Properties.tactical_use: Operators use the EDS-2 to strip defensive advantages from targets before engagement — dissolving armor polymer coatings, removing adhesive traps, or degrading cybernetic housing to expose internal components. In close-quarters situations, the organic setting is used as a disabling tool: even brief facial exposure causes involuntary eye closure and severe respiratory distress, forcing targets out of cover. Industrial sabotage specialists use the synthetic setting to destroy equipment without leaving ballistic evidence. The aerosol's near-invisibility makes it effective as a trap layer in ventilation systems.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88's corporate espionage circles, being 'lacquered' has become slang for having your defenses methodically stripped before a hostile move — professional, financial, or physical. The EDS-2's industrial licensing loophole is an open secret, and Zheng-Dao Bioelectric has never publicly acknowledged the weapon applications of the device, maintaining a posture of corporate innocence while quietly supplying the gray market. Operators who carry it are often perceived as precise and methodical rather than aggressive — the weapon suggests patience.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of corporate equipment failures across competing firms all show signs of selective polymer dissolution. No ballistic evidence, no witnesses. Someone with an EDS-2 and an industrial license is running a quiet sabotage campaign.; A player is approached by a Zheng-Dao Bioelectric liaison who offers a significant payout to recover a specific EDS-2 unit — serial number provided. They won't say why that specific unit matters.; The players need to get through a door sealed with military-grade polymer adhesive. Someone mentions they know where to acquire a licensed decontamination sprayer.; A victim is found with dissolution injuries inconsistent with any known acid or solvent — the pattern suggests an ionized aerosol. The only legal holders of EDS-2 units in this district are three licensed industrial workers, all of whom have airtight alibis.

Nodes.Name: Corporate sabotage specialists and competitive intelligence operatives
'Varnish' — an anonymous fixer known for leaving dissolved equipment as a calling card
Hazardous materials workers who have quietly modified their units

Properties.description:
The EVSD-4 is a medium-frame area-preparation drone that disperses a proprietary electrochemical vapor compound across a target zone, seeding the atmosphere with ionized particulate that dramatically enhances the conductivity and lethality of subsequent electrical or galvanic weapon discharges. The vapor—a suspension of hygroscopic metallic salt particles developed by OUROBOROS ENERGY for industrial capacitor humidification—bonds to airborne moisture and settles on surfaces, clothing, and exposed skin, creating an invisible conductive network that bridges gaps between targets and dramatically lowers the energy threshold required for electrical disruption.

The Rainmaker operates at low altitude (3–15 meters) to ensure dense, even vapor distribution before ascending to observation altitude. Once a zone has been seeded, galvanic or electrical weapons discharged into it experience dramatically amplified arc propagation—discharges that would normally affect a single target can chain to adjacent persons, and energy weapons operating at sub-lethal settings become lethal within the seeded zone. The vapor disperses naturally within 4–8 minutes in open air or up to 20 minutes in enclosed spaces, giving operators a defined engagement window.

OUROBOROS ENERGY developed the vapor compound for entirely non-military purposes, but RINGO CORPONATION's defense subsidiary recognized its weaponization potential and quietly funded EVSD-4 platform development through a series of subsidiary arrangements. The resulting weapon exists in a legal gray zone: the drone itself is classified as an 'atmospheric preparation system' with no offensive designation, while the vapor compound retains its industrial certification. This regulatory gap has made the EVSD-4 surprisingly accessible through legitimate industrial supply channels.
Properties.legality: Restricted (regulatory gray zone — platform licensed as industrial equipment)
Properties.specifications:
frame dimensions: 620mm x 580mm x 200mm
weight: 4.1 kg (full vapor reservoir)
vapor reservoir capacity: 1.8 liters suspension
effective seeding area: ~200 square meters per full reservoir
seeding altitude: 3–15 meters operational
vapor persistence: 4–8 minutes open air, up to 20 minutes enclosed
arc propagation enhancement: Estimated 3–5x standard electrical discharge range within seeded zone
operational endurance: 35 minutes on internal cell
vapor compound designation: OUROBOROS Type-7 Hygroscopic Metallic Suspension
Properties.tactical_use: Operators deploy the EVSD-4 30–60 seconds before committing to an engagement, seeding the target zone while maintaining cover. Once the vapor has distributed, any electrical or galvanic weapon becomes dramatically more effective—standard-issue galvanic sidearms can chain across groups, and area-denial emitters achieve full coverage at reduced power settings. Teams operating with hardened, insulated equipment gain a significant asymmetric advantage in seeded environments. Counter-tactics focus on either dispersing the vapor (high-velocity fans, rapid ventilation) or detecting the drone before seeding completes. The vapor is colorless but has a faint metallic smell that experienced operators recognize.
Properties.cultural_context: The EVSD-4's industrial legal classification has made it a favorite of operators who want military-grade area preparation without the legal exposure of prohibited hardware. Corporate security consultants treat it as a 'force multiplier' in the euphemistic language of their industry briefings. In Meridian 88's street-level conflict culture, 'calling rain' before a hit has become slang for thorough, professional preparation—implying the operator has resources, planning capability, and access to specialized equipment. Electrical weapon specialists—colloquially known as 'stormcallers'—prize the EVSD-4 as the cornerstone of their operational doctrine.
Properties.story_hooks: A warehouse fire investigation reveals traces of OUROBOROS Type-7 suspension in the debris—the fire was electrical in origin and someone used a Rainmaker to turn a standard arc discharge into a mass casualty event.; A player character notices a faint metallic smell in the corridor ahead—someone has pre-seeded the zone and is waiting with electrical weapons. The drone is still overhead, and disabling it before it completes a second seeding pass becomes an urgent priority.; OUROBOROS ENERGY's legal team has finally noticed the weaponized use of their industrial compound and is preparing to file a regulatory complaint that would close the gray market—RINGO CORPONATION wants the filing delayed or buried, and is looking for leverage against the OUROBOROS executive leading the effort.

Nodes.Name: Corporate security consultants operating in gray-legal space
Industrial sabotage operatives using legitimate procurement channels

Properties.description: The EPD-3 is a medium-chassis hovering drone platform designed to project directional high-voltage electrokinetic pulses against personnel and light electronic systems. Manufactured by ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC, it draws on the company's industrial arc-discharge research to deliver a focused 80,000-volt pulse across a conductive plasma channel ionized by an onboard UV laser. The effect on an unshielded human target at close range is immediate neuromuscular incapacitation; at extended ranges, the pulse degrades to disorientation, involuntary muscle spasm, and—with repeated exposure—cardiac arrhythmia. The EPD-3 is officially classified as a non-lethal deterrence platform, a designation that field experience consistently contradicts.
Properties.aliases: The Zapper, Cloudkill, Tesla Box, Headache Drone
Properties.legality: Restricted — licensed non-lethal designation; repeated-discharge use against personnel classified as aggravated assault under Meridian Code 44.7
Properties.specifications:
dimensions: 480mm x 480mm x 220mm
mass: 3.8 kg
discharge voltage: 80,000V (peak), 12,000V (sustained arc)
effective range: Full incapacitation to 8m; disorientation/arrhythmia risk to 22m
pulse capacity: 14 discharges per capacitor cycle
recharge cycle: 88 seconds (full capacitor recharge)
secondary effect: Electronic disruption — fuses unshielded circuitry within 4m of discharge point
flight endurance: 42 minutes (active discharge operations)
acoustic signature: Audible turbine hum at close range; discharge crack audible to 200m
operator interface: Direct telemetry, AR overlay compatible, semi-autonomous patrol mode available
Properties.tactical_use: Crowd control, building clearance, and anti-drone operations. Corporate security details use paired Thunderhead units to establish non-lethal perimeters around executive assets, with the understanding that 'non-lethal' is a legal rather than physiological description. Anti-cyberware enforcement units deploy them to selectively disable unregistered augmentations before detaining subjects—a tactic that has resulted in multiple deaths where the targeted cyberware included cardiac or respiratory assist systems. Counter-measures include Faraday-weave clothing (reduces but does not eliminate effect), plasma-channel scatter panels, and the crude expedient of keeping a grounded conductor between the drone and the operator's body.
Properties.cultural_context: The Thunderhead occupies a specific cultural role as the face of 'legitimate' corporate violence—the weapon that says 'we're not trying to kill you' while demonstrably trying to hurt you. In augmentation-heavy communities like the Sublevel markets and the prosthetics districts around Helix Row, the EPD-3 is despised with a particular intensity. Anti-augmentation enforcement using Thunderhead units has become a flashpoint in ongoing political tensions around cyberware rights, and the drone's silhouette has appeared in protest art and propaganda from several augmentation-rights organizations. ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC's continued non-lethal classification of the platform despite documented fatalities is a recurring subject of investigative journalism in Meridian 88.
Properties.story_hooks: A modified EPD-3 with its discharge limiter removed has killed three people in the Sublevel markets. MMPD is calling it malfunction. The victims' families are calling it murder. Someone needs to find the operator and the modification source before a fourth deployment.; A ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC engineer has evidence that the company's own internal testing showed cardiac fatality rates of 12% in subjects with common cardiac cyberware—evidence that was buried before the non-lethal certification was filed. She wants out and wants the data published.; A player character with cardiac assist cyberware is told a Thunderhead unit has been assigned to their building's security detail. The building manager says it's standard. It isn't standard. Someone specifically requested it.; A protest in the Helix Row prosthetics district has turned into a standoff. Six EPD-3 units are holding the perimeter. Someone in the crowd has a signal jammer that can kill the units' telemetry—but using it will also kill the medical monitoring signals of three protesters with life-support augmentations.

Nodes.Name: Black-market operators (modified for lethal discharge threshold)

Properties.description: The EBDP-4 delivers a pulsed electrolytic field tuned to disrupt the calcium hydroxyapatite mineral matrix of cortical bone. Rather than fracturing bone mechanically, the weapon induces rapid electrolytic demineralization — stripping calcium ions from the bone lattice through a process similar to accelerated osteoclast activity compressed into milliseconds. The result is a localized region of catastrophically weakened bone that fails under normal mechanical load, causing compound fractures from the target's own movement or the force of incidental contact.
Properties.aliases: Chalk, The Whitener, Bone Dry, Dissolve
Properties.specifications:
length: 55 cm
weight: 2.8 kg
power source: Helix BioElec HBE-7 dual-cell
effective range: 6–70 m
pulse frequency: 3.4 MHz electrolytic field
demineralization onset: Immediate on sustained hit (0.3 second minimum)
target bone density reduction: 60–80% in affected region per full pulse
shots per cell: 18 full pulses
chassis: Medical-grade polymer housing (repurposed surgical device chassis)
Properties.tactical_use: The EBDP-4 is used almost exclusively in ambush and assassination contexts. Operators typically deliver a pulse to a load-bearing structure — femur, tibia, or lumbar vertebrae — and then allow the target to continue moving until natural biomechanical stress causes the weakened bone to fail. The delayed collapse window (2–15 seconds of continued movement) allows an operator to disengage before the target falls, making attribution difficult. Some operators use it to pre-weaken a target before a physical confrontation, ensuring that even minor strikes will cause catastrophic structural failure.
Properties.cultural_context: The EBDP-4 originated as a Helix Biosystems prototype for non-invasive bone density correction in degenerative disease patients — the demineralization function was intended to prepare bone tissue for remineralization therapy. The weaponized version surfaced on the black market roughly eighteen months after the prototype was shelved, suggesting an inside leak. In Meridian 88's underworld, being hit by Chalk is considered one of the most humiliating ways to be taken down — experienced criminals read the injury pattern and know the target was marked in advance, implying either betrayal or surveillance. Helix Biosystems publicly denies any connection to the weapon.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of seemingly accidental falls and sports injuries among mid-level corporate managers are revealed to be EBDP-4 attacks — someone is running a long-term removal campaign designed to look like a bad luck streak.; A black-market dealer offers the party a EBDP-4 unit, but the weapon's internal logs contain targeting data for dozens of past operations — a treasure trove of evidence and a death sentence if the wrong people find out they have it.; Helix Biosystems hires the party to locate and destroy all existing EBDP-4 units before a regulatory investigation connects the weapon's design to their shelved medical prototype — but the party discovers the weapons were deliberately leaked by a Helix executive.; A player character begins experiencing unexplained bone fractures from minor impacts — a delayed-onset EBDP-4 pulse delivered days earlier is slowly destroying their skeletal structure, and they need the specific Helix antidote protocol before it reaches the spine.

Properties.description:
The EOC-8 is a hybrid charge that combines a conventional chemical overpressure detonation with a precisely timed electromagnetic pulse layered on top of the blast wave. The interaction between the two effects is the weapon's central innovation: the overpressure wave physically disrupts shielding and housing on electronic systems in the blast radius at the precise moment the EMP fires, meaning that Faraday-cage protection and hardened electronics — which would normally survive a standard EMP — are caught structurally compromised during the pulse. The result is a combined effect that destroys both shielded and unshielded electronics far more reliably than either component would achieve alone.

For cyberware-dependent individuals in the blast radius, the EOC-8 is catastrophic in ways that go beyond simple system shutdown. Neural interfaces, subdermal processors, and augmented sensory arrays that survive the physical blast are subjected to the EMP while their housing has been fractured by overpressure — a failure mode that most cyberware is not designed to survive. The resulting feedback events range from temporary sensory blackout to permanent neural interface damage depending on the grade of augmentation. High-end military cyberware with triple-redundant shielding has a roughly 40% failure rate within the EOC-8's inner blast radius. Standard commercial augmentation has virtually no survival rate.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric developed the EOC-8 ostensibly as an anti-drone and anti-autonomous-system area denial tool, a framing that allowed them to navigate certain regulatory thresholds. The anti-personnel application against heavily augmented targets was — officially — an unintended consequence discovered during field trials. Unofficially, Zheng-Dao's internal documentation (portions of which leaked in 2197) makes clear the anti-augmentation profile was the primary design target from the beginning.
Properties.aliases: The Flipper, Surge Bomb, Blackout Fist
Properties.legality: Restricted (anti-drone certification required); de facto Prohibited for anti-personnel use
Properties.specifications:
weight: 1.8 kg
blast radius overpressure: 6 meters (lethal), 12 meters (incapacitating)
emp radius: 15 meters (full effect), 25 meters (partial disruption)
pulse timing offset: EMP fires 0.003 seconds post-overpressure initiation
shielding penetration: Effective against Faraday-rated enclosures up to MIL-SPEC Class 4
cyberware failure rate: ~95% (commercial grade), ~40% (military grade) within inner radius
trigger options: Timer, remote, proximity (EM signature detection)
countermeasures: Blast-rated EMP hardening (Class 5+) offers partial protection; no commercial solution provides full immunity
Properties.tactical_use: The EOC-8 is deployed as an area-denial and force-equalization tool in engagements where the opposing force is heavily augmented. Teams that know they are going up against chrome-heavy corporate security or augmented military units use it to strip the enemy's technological advantage before closing to contact. It is also used in facility raids to simultaneously destroy security electronics and disable any augmented defenders in a single detonation. Operators using it take care to deploy from outside the EMP radius or use shielded relay detonators — operators with significant cyberware have been known to trigger their own augmentation failures by detonating the charge at insufficient distance.
Properties.cultural_context: The EOC-8 is politically charged in Meridian 88 in a way few weapons are. In a city where augmentation is deeply tied to identity, class, and survival, a weapon specifically engineered to destroy cyberware carries symbolic weight beyond its tactical function. Anti-augmentation extremist groups have used it as a statement weapon. Corporate security forces use it to 'level the field' against street operators who have invested years of earnings into augmentation. Among heavily augmented communities, being targeted with an EOC-8 is experienced as an existential attack — not just on the body, but on the self. There is a growing movement advocating for its complete prohibition under the same frameworks that govern biological weapons.
Properties.story_hooks: A community leader in a heavily augmented lower-ward neighborhood is killed by an EOC-8 detonation. The blast radius included a medical clinic where three patients with life-support cyberware were also killed. Someone is sending a message — but to whom?; A player character with significant cyberware is informed by a contact that an EOC-8 has been planted somewhere in a building they need to enter. They have to find it before they go inside, or enter knowing what's waiting.; The 2197 Zheng-Dao leak surfaces again, this time with new pages that suggest the EOC-8's design was based on stolen research from a competitor — research that was originally intended to protect cyberware from EMP, not destroy it.; A Zheng-Dao executive offers a substantial contract: recover a shipment of EOC-8 units that went missing in transit. The players discover the shipment was not lost — it was sold internally to a buyer the executive does not want identified.

Nodes.Name: Zheng-Dao internal security rapid response teams
Corporate extraction teams targeting augmented operatives
Military contractors operating in augmentation-heavy zones
Black-market dealer archetype known as 'the Equalizer'

Properties.description: The EPG-5 is a precision electromagnetic pulse device built around a flux compression generator — a one-shot coil system that converts the energy of a compact explosive charge into a directed electromagnetic burst. Unlike broad-spectrum EMP devices, the Deadstop uses a tunable frequency array to target specific electromagnetic signatures, allowing operators to selectively disable cybernetic implants, vehicle electronics, or communications infrastructure while leaving other systems functional. The tuning dial has five preset modes and one manual override requiring a RINGO CORPONATION technician key.
Properties.specifications:
weight: 0.9 kg
diameter: 11 cm
pulse radius: 12 m standard, 6 m in directional mode
frequency modes: Cybernetic neural implants, Vehicle electronics, Communications arrays, Drone guidance systems, Broad-spectrum (all electronics)
detonation delay: 2.5 seconds pull-pin
reuse: Single use — flux coil destroyed on detonation
operator protection: Requires Faraday-lined gloves — unprotected operators within 3 m risk implant damage
Properties.tactical_use: Standard deployment in anti-cyborg operations and vehicle interdiction. Military breach teams use the Deadstop to drop heavily augmented targets before entering — the cybernetic implant mode selectively crashes neural-linked weapons systems, optical overlays, and subdermal armor actuators without triggering cardiac implants, which would constitute a prohibited kill method under Meridian 88 corporate warfare accords. The manual override mode that removes this restriction is why the weapon is classified.
Properties.cultural_context: The EPG-5 occupies an uncomfortable legal grey zone in Meridian 88 — its selective modes are technically compliant with corporate warfare protocols, but the existence of the manual override is an open secret that RINGO CORPONATION refuses to acknowledge. Heavily augmented citizens fear the Deadstop the way unaugmented people fear bullets: it is specifically designed to make their body a liability. Black market units with the technician key already installed command extraordinary prices.
Properties.story_hooks: A RINGO technician key surfaces at a street market — whoever sold it either stole it or is dead, and RINGO's internal security is moving to recover it by any means necessary.; A runner with extensive cybernetic augmentation is hired for a job, only to discover the client's building was just swept with an EPG-5 on broad-spectrum mode — their implants are dead and they're deep inside hostile territory.; An anti-augmentation cell has acquired twelve EPG-5 units with manual overrides and is planning coordinated detonations across the city's most densely augmented districts during a public festival.

Nodes.Name: Law enforcement elite tactical units (licensed, restricted modes only)

Properties.description:
The EAPD-2 is a hovering medium-range directed-effect drone designed to induce rapid and deeply uncomfortable electrostatic polarization within subcutaneous adipose tissue. Operating on a principle adapted from industrial fat-separation processes used in IRONCLAD AGRISYSTEMS food refinement divisions, the drone projects a focused alternating electrostatic field at frequencies between 18–42 kHz, causing lipid molecules in fatty tissue to oscillate, generate internal friction heat, and produce a sensation described by test subjects as 'burning from the inside without any surface heat.' The effect is localized, penetrative, and extremely difficult to shield against with standard ballistic protection.

The EAPD-2 achieves its distinctive targeting precision through a passive thermal differencing system that maps subcutaneous fat distribution in real time, allowing it to concentrate energy on the highest-density adipose regions of a target's body. This makes the weapon non-uniformly effective — individuals with lower body fat percentages experience less acute effects, a fact that has led to significant ethical controversy and several documented cases of operators deliberately targeting individuals based on body composition profiles obtained from medical data leaks.

Beyond pain compliance, sustained exposure causes localized edema, superficial tissue inflammation, and in high-power settings, minor lipid necrosis that resolves over several weeks. The drone itself is deceptively quiet, using magnetic levitation stabilizers rather than rotors, and its electrostatic emission is invisible to the naked eye, making identification of the weapon mid-engagement genuinely difficult.
Properties.aliases: Render, The Fat Burner, Polarizer, Candle Drone
Properties.specifications:
dimensions: 22cm x 18cm x 9cm
operational altitude: 0.5m–6m
effective range: 3m–15m focused beam
frequency range: 18–42 kHz alternating electrostatic
targeting system: Passive thermal differencing array
power source: High-density polymer capacitor bank, field-rechargeable
battery life: 22 minutes continuous operation
weight: 1.1kg
noise signature: Near-silent (magnetic levitation, <18dB operational)
Properties.tactical_use: The EAPD-2 is most commonly used in interrogation-adjacent scenarios where operators need compliance without leaving visible external marks. It is deployed in enclosed spaces — small rooms, vehicle interiors, elevator shafts — where its 15m maximum range is more than sufficient and where the target has limited ability to increase distance from the effect. Field operatives have used it for area denial in corridors, setting the drone to autonomous patrol mode and relying on the extreme discomfort of exposure to prevent passage without a fight. High-tier assassins have used it in conjunction with other weapons to degrade a target's physical capacity before engaging directly.
Properties.cultural_context: The EAPD-2's origins in agricultural fat-rendering technology are not lost on Meridian 88's activist communities, who have used the connection as a rallying point against IRONCLAD AGRISYSTEMS' expansion into defense contracting. 'Rendering' someone has become a politically charged phrase in certain circles, used to describe the corporatization of violence against lower-income citizens who statistically present with higher body fat percentages due to food access disparities — making them more vulnerable to this specific weapon. IRONCLAD officially denies any connection between their agri-processing patents and the EAPD-2's design.
Properties.story_hooks: A whistleblower from IRONCLAD AGRISYSTEMS is trying to leak documents proving the EAPD-2 was designed using classified food-processing patents — and someone very corporate wants them silenced before the story breaks.; The players are hired to retrieve an EAPD-2 from a black market auction, only to discover it's already been used in a high-profile disappearance with no external injuries on the body.; A contact offers the players a 'clean' EAPD-2 with its serial numbers burned — but the drone's targeting logs are still intact, and what they contain is worth more than the weapon itself.

Nodes.Name: High-end fixers with access to prohibited hardware
Underground enforcement arms of food district cartels

Properties.description:
The EDAP-1 projects a focused beam of ionized particles that induces a powerful electrostatic charge differential across the target's outermost dermal layer, causing them to adhere with significant force to any conductive or semi-conductive surface they contact — walls, floors, vehicle chassis, armor plating, or other people. The adhesion force scales with the surface area of contact and the conductivity of the target surface, but in typical urban environments, a fully charged target pressed against a ferroconcrete wall requires approximately 340 kilograms of force to detach. The charge dissipates naturally over four to seven minutes, or can be neutralized immediately with a grounding discharge.

The projector itself is a compact sidearm-profile weapon with a distinctive wide emitter disk at the muzzle. It fires silently, with only a faint blue corona visible at the emitter during discharge. Tessera Corponation designed it for rapid immobilization scenarios — apprehension, perimeter denial, and the specific problem of targets attempting to flee through tight urban terrain. A person adhered to a surface cannot run, and cannot easily use weapons if their hands are stuck to their sides or to each other. The weapon has a secondary 'overcharge' mode that increases the adhesion force to levels that can cause skin tearing if the target attempts to pull free, which Tessera's documentation carefully describes as 'enhanced compliance motivation.'

The street name 'Flypaper' is self-explanatory. 'The Embrace' is the term used by the Meridian 88 warrant enforcement community, delivered with the flat affect of people who have used it enough times that irony is no longer part of the delivery.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 3-22m
adhesion force standard: 340 kg separation force (ferroconcrete reference surface)
adhesion force overcharge: Up to 680 kg separation force
charge duration: 4-7 minutes natural dissipation
grounding neutralization: Immediate via Tessera-compatible grounding rod
weight: 0.9 kg
power source: Integrated ionization cell, 24 standard discharges / 12 overcharge discharges
dimensions: 28cm length
Properties.tactical_use: Most effective in urban pursuit scenarios and confined-space apprehension. Operators fire on a fleeing target as they approach a wall, vehicle, or any surface, causing instant immobilization. In team operations, one operator fires while others close distance — the standard window before dissipation is more than enough for restraint application. Advanced users learn to 'layer' charges on a target who is wearing non-conductive outerwear by targeting exposed skin at the neck, hands, or face. The weapon is significantly less effective against targets with full-body non-conductive insulation, which has created a small market for anti-adhesion undersuits in communities where EDAP-1 deployment is common.
Properties.cultural_context: The EDAP-1 is one of the few exotic weapons in widespread legitimate use by licensed enforcement entities, which has given it an unusual dual reputation. For warrant officers and corporate security, it is a workday tool, worn openly and unremarkable. For the communities they operate in, it has become a symbol of a specific kind of powerlessness — the inability to run, to move, to escape — that resonates beyond its mechanical function. Anti-adhesion clothing has become a quiet form of political statement in certain districts, and the sight of someone in full insulating gear is immediately legible to anyone who knows the context. Tessera Corponation has lobbied to have anti-adhesion clothing classified as obstructing lawful enforcement.
Properties.story_hooks: A prominent activist was found adhered to the exterior wall of a building twelve stories up — the official report says they climbed there, but EDAP-1 residue says otherwise.; Tessera Corponation's grounding neutralization rods have been counterfeited in massive quantities and are flooding the black market — someone wants targets to be releasable without Tessera's knowledge or involvement.; An operator is hired to retrieve a package from a building where every surface has been pre-treated with a conductive coating, turning the entire structure into a potential adhesion trap for anyone carrying an ionized charge.; The overcharge mode on a batch of EDAP-1 units has been factory-set at maximum, and the 'compliance motivation' documentation is starting to look like a cover story for something that was always intended to injure.

Properties.description:
The EFP-1 generates a shaped electrostatic discharge field projected through a parabolic dielectric emitter array, creating a zone of intense charge differential across a target's surface. Unlike simple stun weapons that induce muscle tetany through current passage, the EFP-1's field geometry creates lateral charge migration across the outermost dermal layers, producing a shearing electrostatic force that disrupts the adhesive protein bonds holding epithelial tissue in structural alignment. At low output, this causes intense surface pain and temporary paresthesia. At high output, the effect progresses to partial epidermal separation across exposed skin — a phenomenon the weapon's users describe with clinical understatement as 'flensing.'

The weapon's targeting system includes a passive bioelectric sensor that reads surface charge signatures to distinguish organic targets from synthetic materials, allowing the EFP-1 to selectively affect unarmored biological tissue while having reduced effect on conductive armor plating — which disperses rather than concentrates the field. This selectivity is a deliberate design feature that makes the weapon particularly effective against lightly clothed or partially armored targets while limiting its utility against fully suited opponents. The dielectric emitter array produces a characteristic crackling hiss during charge buildup, providing approximately 0.8 seconds of audible warning before discharge.

ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC developed the EFP-1 under a crowd control contract for an unnamed municipal authority, and its design reflects an interrogation-adjacent philosophy: maximum pain compliance with survivable damage at standard settings. The high-output mode that causes epidermal separation was not in the original specification and emerged from field modifications. ZHENG-DAO officially disavows the modification but has not recalled or redesigned the units in circulation.
Properties.tier_availability: Tier 2+ (crowd control variant); Black market (high-output modification)
Properties.specifications:
emitter array: Parabolic dielectric array, 7-element
field modes: Compliance (pain induction) / Suppression (tetany + disorientation) / Flense (epidermal separation, modified)
target discrimination: Passive bioelectric sensor, organic vs. conductive surface
effective range: Up to 12 m (optimal field coherence)
cone width at 12m: Approximately 1.4 m
charge buildup warning: ~0.8 seconds audible
power source: High-density capacitor bank, 24 compliance / 12 suppression / 6 flense shots
weight: 2.1 kg
length: 46 cm
Properties.tactical_use: Enforcement operators use the EFP-1 in compliance mode for crowd dispersal and suspect restraint, exploiting the pain response to force submission without lasting injury at standard settings. Suppression mode is used for incapacitating targets who resist compliance. The flense modification is employed by black-market users for interrogation and targeted punishment — it is rarely used in open combat due to the charge buildup warning. Operators learn to angle the parabolic array to maximize field coherence against partially covered targets, directing the effect toward exposed skin.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88, the EFP-1 is the weapon most closely associated with institutional violence — the kind wielded by enforcement bodies rather than street combatants. Its crowd-control origin means civilians recognize it as a symbol of authority being applied to bodies. The fact that ZHENG-DAO disavows the high-output modification while it proliferates freely has become a minor political flashpoint; activist groups in the lower districts call it 'plausible deniability with a charge buildup.' Carrying a modified EFP-1 signals affiliation with enforcement culture gone rogue — ex-officers, disgraced security contractors, or corporate interrogators working without oversight.
Properties.story_hooks: A ZHENG-DAO internal memo surfaces proving the corporation knew about the flense modification before it 'emerged' in the field — someone leaked it and is now being hunted.; A municipal enforcement unit is found using modified EFP-1s against a labor protest; the players are hired either to document the incident or to make the evidence disappear, depending on who's paying.; A series of bodies with EFP-1 flense damage appear in a district where no enforcement units operate — someone is using a modified weapon for targeted killings and framing institutional actors.; ZHENG-DAO offers the players a contract to recover all modified EFP-1 units from a specific black-market supply chain, but the players discover the corporation wants them back to reverse-engineer and legitimize the modification.

Properties.description:
The ENAR-3 fires a tight cluster of ultra-fine conductive needles — between 12 and 48 per discharge, depending on the selected spread pattern — each carrying an individually modulated electrostatic charge. Unlike conventional electroshock weapons that rely on a single high-voltage arc, the Porcupine's array approach allows each needle to carry a different charge polarity and magnitude, creating an interference pattern within the target's nervous system rather than a simple override signal. The result is not unconsciousness but a targeted disruption of specific motor pathways — an operator can dial for hand tremor, full arm paralysis, loss of fine motor control, or total lower-body incapacitation while leaving the target fully conscious and vocal.

Ringo Corponation developed the ENAR-3 initially for their detention and interrogation division, where the ability to incapacitate without full unconsciousness had obvious operational value. The needle array design emerged from their bioelectric research partnership with a now-dissolved subsidiary that had been working on neural stimulation prosthetics; the same charge-modulation algorithms that allowed precise muscle activation for rehabilitation patients were, with relatively minor inversion, capable of precise muscle deactivation for detention purposes. The weapon underwent three years of classified field trials before Ringo released it to licensed security contractors.

The needles themselves are 80mm, hair-thin tungsten-alloy filaments with a hydrophilic coating that improves skin conductance on contact. They are single-use, loaded in pre-configured cassettes that color-code the charge pattern for quick selection under stress. The rifle's bulk comes from its charge-modulation processor — a substantial unit mounted above the receiver that operators informally call the 'brain' — which recalculates interference patterns in real time based on target distance and the needle spread achieved at impact.
Properties.aliases: Porcupine, The Needle, Pin-gun, Static Array
Properties.legality: Licensed — Class-B Directed Incapacitation certification required; anti-personnel charge configurations above Level 4 prohibited without military exemption
Properties.specifications:
projectile: Tungsten-alloy conductive needles, 80mm × 0.3mm, hydrophilic coating
needles per discharge: 12–48 (pattern cassette dependent)
charge patterns: 8 pre-loaded (Hand Tremor, Arm Lock, Fine Motor Disruption, Lower Body, Full Body Incapacitation, Cardiac Stress, Sensory Override, Custom Upload)
effective range: 25m full-pattern / 60m reduced-needle contact
power source: Ringo R-Cell Type-9, 30 discharges per cell
weight: 3.4 kg with processor unit
cassette capacity: 1 discharge per cassette; 6-cassette rotary loader standard
processor: RINGO NMP-2 Neural Modulation Processor, real-time interference recalculation
integrated systems: Pattern selector, target-distance rangefinder, needle-contact confirmation indicator
Properties.tactical_use: Detention and compliance teams use the Porcupine as a precision tool rather than a blunt instrument. The ability to selectively incapacitate — disabling a weapon hand while leaving a subject mobile for self-extraction, or immobilizing a fleeing target's legs while preserving their ability to answer questions — has made it standard equipment for high-value apprehension operations. The weapon's limitations are range and the requirement for needle-skin contact; heavy clothing and armor reduce effectiveness significantly, and the single-discharge cassette system means reloading under fire is slow. Operators typically use it in coordinated teams where conventional weapons handle suppression and the Porcupine handles the precise, targeted incapacitation of priority subjects.
Properties.cultural_context: The Porcupine is one of the most politically contentious weapons in Meridian 88's civilian security landscape. Ringo Corponation markets it aggressively as a humane alternative to lethal force, and their public communications emphasize the weapon's precision and reversibility. Critics — particularly the city's medical oversight bodies and several labor advocacy groups — point to the Cardiac Stress charge pattern and the documented misuse of Custom Upload configurations to argue that 'humane incapacitation' is a marketing frame rather than an operational reality. The weapon has become a symbol in ongoing debates about corporate detention rights, and several incidents of ENAR-3 misuse by private security have become flashpoints in Meridian 88's labor politics.
Properties.story_hooks: A Ringo Corponation security officer is found dead from cardiac arrest — the needle puncture marks on their body match an ENAR-3 discharge, but their own weapon's log shows it was never fired.; A batch of Custom Upload cassettes is circulating on the black market with a charge configuration that Ringo's engineers say shouldn't be possible with the standard NMP-2 processor — someone has found a way to flash unofficial firmware.; A labor organizer who was detained by Ringo security last month is reporting persistent motor control issues in their right hand that no clinic can explain — they believe they were hit with an off-book charge pattern and want someone to prove it.; The ENAR-3's Neural Modulation Processor contains a passive data-logging function that records biometric data from every target it hits — and Ringo has been quietly aggregating that data for purposes their licensing agreements don't disclose.

Properties.description:
The ETCC-5 uses electrothermal-chemical propulsion, a system in which a high-voltage electrical discharge is injected directly into a liquid propellant plasma behind the projectile at the moment of firing. The electrical discharge — generated by a capacitor bank integrated into the weapon's fore-end — converts a small volume of liquid propellant into a plasma jet approximately 40 times more energetically dense than conventional propellant gases. This allows the ETCC-5 to drive a standard 8.6mm projectile to approximately 1,850 m/s from a 420mm barrel, producing muzzle energies that exceed most dedicated anti-materiel rifles while maintaining a package compact enough for two-handed field use.

The weapon's plasma generation creates a distinctive secondary effect: a brief, intense flash of blue-white light exits the muzzle at the moment of discharge, visible in peripheral vision at ranges up to 300 meters. This 'Flashpoint' signature is the weapon's most recognizable characteristic and its primary tactical liability. Operators in the field report that the flash is disorienting to targets at close range and has caused temporary photoreceptor disruption in unshielded observers within 50 meters, an unintended secondary effect that ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC has since studied for deliberate exploitation in newer variants. The flash also makes the shooter's position immediately obvious, which has driven extensive tactical doctrine around single-shot engagements and immediate repositioning.

The liquid propellant system uses a sealed, pressurized 40mL cartridge that feeds a 10-round magazine of standard 8.6mm projectiles. Each shot consumes approximately 3mL of propellant, giving each cartridge 13 shots before the propellant is exhausted — slightly more than the magazine capacity, meaning operators typically exhaust ammunition before propellant. The capacitor bank recharges from a rail-mounted power cell between shots, producing a 1.4-second cycling delay that defines the weapon's semi-automatic, deliberate-fire character.
Properties.aliases: Flashpoint, ETC Gun, The Chemist's Rifle, ETCC-5, Plasma Booster
Properties.specifications:
caliber: 8.6x70mm ETC-spec projectile
feed system: 10-round box magazine, 40mL liquid propellant cartridge (integrated)
muzzle velocity: 1,850 m/s
muzzle energy: ~14,200 J
effective range: 800m (personnel), 400m (light vehicle armor)
cyclic rate: Semi-automatic, 1.4s capacitor recharge between shots
weight: 4.1 kg with magazine, 4.7 kg with optics package
dimensions: 760mm length (fixed stock), 420mm barrel
power source: Integrated 72V capacitor bank, powered by 24V rail cell (30 shots per cell)
secondary effect: Blue-white muzzle flash, photoreceptor disruption risk within 50m
Properties.tactical_use: The ETCC-5 is deployed as a precision anti-materiel and anti-personnel rifle where conventional high-caliber weapons would be logistically impractical. Its liquid propellant system eliminates spent brass and produces minimal acoustic signature compared to conventional equivalents, though the muzzle flash negates most of the concealment benefit. Military operators use it for vehicle window defeat, light drone interdiction, and hardened-target precision fire. The 1.4-second cycling delay requires trained trigger discipline — operators are taught to fire, reacquire, and fire again rather than attempting rapid follow-up shots. Special operations units have developed a two-person team doctrine where a spotter calls target transitions to compensate for the inter-shot delay.
Properties.cultural_context: The ETCC-5 is almost entirely absent from civilian Meridian 88 life — its military-only designation is genuinely enforced, and the liquid propellant cartridges are serialized and tracked. When one appears outside military hands, it is significant news. In the city's underground arms trade, a single ETCC-5 commands prices that reflect not just its performance but the risk of possessing it. Military deserters sometimes surface one, and the occasional black-market unit has been traced to ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC's own internal security personnel. The weapon's distinctive blue muzzle flash has entered urban mythology — stories of 'the blue gun' circulate in lower-tier arcology communities as a warning about something dangerous and governmental passing through.
Properties.story_hooks: Three ETCC-5 units have gone missing from a military depot and the serial numbers have been scrubbed — someone inside the logistics chain is selling to a buyer who needs precision fire capability without the military connection; A witness reports seeing the blue flash signature in the direction of a political assassination, but the official investigation insists the weapon used was conventional — someone is lying about the ballistics report; ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC wants to recover a prototype ETCC-5 variant that was taken during a research facility breach before competitors can reverse-engineer the plasma generation system; A former military sniper now operating as a freelancer has an ETCC-5 and is willing to sell — but the buyer realizes the weapon's serial number matches one reported destroyed three years ago in a classified incident

Properties.description:
The ETCL-9 operates by projecting a focused column of electrothermal plasma into an enclosed or semi-enclosed space — a room, a vehicle interior, a corridor — and then triggering a rapid compression wave by collapsing the plasma column's magnetic containment field in a controlled sequence. The result is a brief, violent atmospheric compression event within the target space: a pressure spike lasting approximately 80 milliseconds that is sufficient to rupture eardrums, cause pulmonary barotrauma, and collapse unsupported structural cavities. The plasma itself is secondary — it is the compression wave that constitutes the primary weapon effect. Living targets within the affected space experience the sensation of the air being forcibly removed from their lungs, which is where the nickname 'Ironlung' originates.

Ringo Corponation developed the ETCL-9 in response to a specific tactical problem: neutralizing threats inside armored vehicles and fortified rooms without destroying the structure itself. The weapon is fired at a surface — a wall, a door, a vehicle hull — and the plasma column penetrates through gaps, ventilation openings, or thin materials before the compression event occurs inside. The outer structure remains largely intact while the interior is devastated. This made the ETCL-9 extremely valuable for operations where the goal is to secure a location while preserving its contents, and correspondingly attractive to actors who do not want the evidence of what was inside destroyed.

The weapon is large and unwieldy, requiring a shoulder brace for stable operation. Its barrel is unusually long for an energy weapon — 94cm — because the plasma column requires distance to achieve the coherence necessary for effective penetration. Operators describe the firing experience as violent: the recoil from plasma projection is substantial, and the compression event produces a concussive wave that can affect the operator if they are too close to the target surface.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: Up to 25m to target surface
plasma penetration: Gaps of 4cm or larger; materials up to 8mm steel equivalent
compression event duration: ~80ms
pressure spike: Up to 4.2 atmospheres within affected space
operator safe distance: Minimum 6m from target surface
power cell: Ringo RC-15 high-density cell, 8 discharges
weight: 9.1kg with brace
dimensions: 94cm barrel, 38cm brace extended
effective volume: Spaces up to approximately 45 cubic meters
Properties.tactical_use: The ETCL-9 is a specialist weapon for forced entry denial and vehicle interdiction. Operators use it to clear armored vehicles by firing at door seams or ventilation grilles, or to neutralize fortified rooms without breaching the wall. The 6m safe distance requires operators to work from cover. A common tactic involves two operators — one fires the ETCL-9, the other is positioned to breach the door immediately after the compression event, exploiting the incapacitation window. The weapon is not used in open environments where the compression wave has no enclosed space to reflect and amplify.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88, the Ironlung is associated with corporate raid teams and debt enforcement — entities that need to neutralize people inside spaces without destroying the spaces themselves. The weapon appears in low-district horror stories about corporate collectors arriving to repossess equipment or extract debtors, clearing entire apartments without leaving a mark on the walls. Its restricted status means legitimate possession requires corporate affiliation, which reinforces its association with institutional power. Street-level operators occasionally acquire them for use against armored vehicles, accepting the weapon's bulk as the price of armor defeat.
Properties.story_hooks: A residential block in the lower district has been hit by what forensics identifies as an ETCL-9 discharge — every unit on one floor shows internal barotrauma victims with no external damage to the building. The victims all worked for the same underground data brokerage. Someone wanted the servers intact.; Ringo Corponation is publicly denying that a batch of ETCL-9s sold to a licensed security contractor was diverted to a third party. A logistics worker at Ringo wants to sell evidence of the diversion — but they're asking for protection first.; An operator survives an ETCL-9 attack inside an armored vehicle because of a specific lung augmentation they received years ago. Now someone is trying to find out who has that augmentation — because the survivors of the attack can identify who ordered it.
