Properties.description:
The ECVL-5 delivers a focused beam of targeted microwave-band radiation tuned to the resonant absorption frequencies of adrenal and thyroid tissue. On contact, the beam causes explosive volatilization of the target's endocrine glands — not through burning, but through a rapid-phase transition of the glandular fluid content that causes the tissue to rupture from internal pressure. The immediate effect is a catastrophic hormonal surge as the contents of the destroyed glands flood the bloodstream simultaneously: a single discharge produces cortisol, adrenaline, and thyroid hormone levels exceeding any naturally achievable state by orders of magnitude. The target does not simply collapse — they first experience approximately 8–14 seconds of extraordinary physiological activation before the system crashes.

Those 8–14 seconds are the weapon's defining characteristic and the source of its street name. Targets in the surge phase demonstrate superhuman short-term strength and pain tolerance, complete disregard for self-preservation, and in some cases auditory and visual hallucinations driven by the hormonal cascade. Operators who have not been briefed on this effect have been killed by targets they believed were already incapacitated. After the surge, the target collapses into complete endocrine failure — without immediate and aggressive medical intervention, death follows within 30–90 minutes. LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS developed the resonance calibration data during research into targeted glandular therapy; the weaponized application was not their intent, but the data was stolen and sold to ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS within eighteen months of the research being completed.

The weapon is long-form, resembling a conventional anti-materiel rifle, with a distinctive annular emitter ring at the muzzle. It requires precise targeting — the beam must contact the torso in the correct anatomical corridor to hit the adrenal glands — and comes equipped with a thermal imaging scope that highlights endocrine tissue through clothing and light cover. The weapon is considered one of the most ethically contested in Meridian 88's black market, even among operators with few ethical constraints.
Properties.manufacturer: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS (derived from LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS research data)
Properties.legality: Prohibited — classified as a method of torture and induced death

targeting requirement: Torso hit within 8 cm of adrenal anatomical corridor
surge phase duration: 8–14 seconds post-strike

weight: 7.4 kg
length: 118 cm

Properties.tactical_use: Used almost exclusively as an assassination tool where the operator wants to ensure death without a clean kill shot — the surge phase provides plausible cover ('the target attacked first') before the crash. In military applications it has been deployed to destroy a target's capability to function in a leadership role even if they survive: endocrine failure at this severity leaves survivors with permanent glandular dysfunction requiring lifelong pharmaceutical management. Some operators use the surge phase deliberately, deploying the weapon against a target in a crowd to cause the surging target to create chaos before collapsing.
Properties.cultural_context: The Burnout is known but rarely seen in Meridian 88's street ecosystem — its limited circulation and extreme cost keep it out of ordinary criminal use. It is associated almost entirely with high-level corporate assassination and military black operations. The phrase 'burning someone out' has taken on a secondary meaning in executive circles, referring to any operation that destroys a person's long-term functional capacity while leaving them technically alive. LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS has quietly funded multiple legal challenges to ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS over the stolen research data, but the cases have been repeatedly suppressed. Among street medics, a Burnout victim is considered one of the most difficult emergency presentations possible.
Properties.story_hooks: A LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS researcher is found dead of apparent endocrine failure — but the company's own weapon-attribution team confirms a Burnout discharge. Someone is using the weapon against the very company whose data created it. Why?; A character witnesses a Burnout strike in a public market — the target surges, kills two bystanders, then crashes. The operator vanished. The party must find the shooter before the target's death is ruled a spontaneous medical event.; An underground endocrinologist claims to have developed a pharmaceutical protocol that can prevent Burnout death if administered within the surge window — but the treatment is itself highly illegal and the knowledge makes her a target.; ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS approaches the party to recover a stolen ECVL-5 before it can be reverse-engineered by a competitor. The weapon is somewhere in the lower tiers. So is the person who stole it — and they're still alive, which means they haven't been found yet.

Properties.description:
The EPCR-3 operates by projecting a tightly collimated beam of modulated infrasonic pressure waves tuned precisely to the resonant frequency of the endolymphatic fluid within the inner ear. Upon exposure, the fluid undergoes rapid oscillatory pressure cycling, overwhelming the vestibular system and triggering catastrophic spatial disorientation, nausea, and full postural collapse within seconds. The effect is entirely invisible — no projectile, no flash, no audible report above a low subsonic thrum.

What distinguishes the EPCR-3 from cruder acoustic suppression tools is its adaptive targeting firmware, which samples ambient environmental acoustics and dynamically adjusts the emission envelope to compensate for hard surfaces, wind shear, and intervening crowd noise. At ranges under forty meters, it achieves near-total vestibular disruption even through standard hearing protection. At longer ranges, the effect degrades to sustained nausea and impaired balance — still tactically significant.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric engineered the weapon initially as a crowd suppression platform for high-value transit corridor security, but the design escaped controlled licensing within eighteen months of its first deployment. Street copies exist, though they lack the adaptive firmware and frequently cause permanent vestibular damage at close range — an outcome the original design actively attempts to avoid, if only for liability purposes.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 8–42 meters
power source: High-density capacitor cell, 28 discharge cycles per charge
emission frequency: 0.4–18 Hz, dynamically modulated
onset time: 1.8–4 seconds at full exposure
weight: 3.1 kg
form factor: Bullpup carbine, matte polymer housing
acoustic signature: Sub-threshold for standard hearing; felt as pressure at close range
Properties.tactical_use: Operators use the EPCR-3 as a breach-clearing tool, disabling room occupants before entry without triggering audible alarms or leaving ballistic evidence. It is particularly favored in situations where incapacitation without lethality is legally or contractually required. Security teams use it to collapse fleeing targets in open corridors. Paired with a suppressed sidearm, it constitutes a near-silent takedown platform. Operators are trained to fire in short bursts and reposition, as sustained emission in enclosed spaces can cause reflected pressure buildup affecting the operator.
Properties.cultural_context: Among Meridian 88's corporate security culture, the EPCR-3 occupies a strange moral position — marketed as humane, frequently used brutally. Carrying one signals institutional backing; the weapon is too expensive and too legally encumbered for most freelancers to acquire legitimately. On the street, knockoff versions are called 'spinners' and are associated with a particularly cruel class of debt enforcer who prefers to leave targets helpless rather than dead. Medical examiners have begun flagging suspicious inner ear scarring in assault victims as a distinct forensic signature.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of seemingly random collapses in a crowded market district turns out to be an operator testing range on civilians before a high-profile contract hit.; A knockoff EPCR-3 is sold to a freelancer with a factory defect that locks it at maximum intensity — the seller has already disappeared.; A corporate whistleblower claims Zheng-Dao's 'humane' firmware intentionally logs target biometric data during each discharge and sells it to third parties.; An investigator begins connecting multiple assault victims by their identical vestibular scarring — someone is using the same weapon across very different criminal contexts.

Properties.description: The ESDR-1 projects a focused endothermic energy beam that selectively reduces thermal energy in synovial fluid — the lubricating medium within joint capsules — causing it to thicken and partially crystallize without freezing surrounding tissue. Within two seconds of a sustained hit, the targeted joint becomes nearly immobile, the synovial membrane inflamed and packed with semi-viscous fluid. The effect is excruciatingly painful and incapacitating but does not kill, making the ESDR-1 a precision denial weapon. Helix Biosystems developed the underlying endothermic targeting array as a surgical instrument for joint preservation procedures before Arcturus Defense Solutions licensed the technology for tactical application.
Properties.aliases: Lockjaw, The Freezer, Cold Joint, Creak
Properties.specifications:
length: 94 cm
weight: 4.7 kg
power source: ADS EndoCryo-Pack (field-rechargeable)
effective range: 15–180 m
beam duration: Sustained (0.5–3 second variable burst)
joint lock onset: 1.8–2.5 seconds sustained exposure
recovery time target: 12–40 minutes without medical intervention
optics: Integrated biometric targeting overlay with joint-cavity highlighting
Properties.tactical_use: The ESDR-1 is used predominantly in hostage rescue and high-value capture operations where lethal force is contraindicated. Operators target the knees, elbows, or shoulders of armed subjects to instantly remove their ability to aim or move without requiring lethal engagement. Military units employ it as a 'peel' weapon — stripping a target's mobility before a close-assault team moves in. The integrated biometric overlay highlights joint cavities through light clothing and low-visibility conditions, allowing operators to place shots accurately at distance. At maximum burst duration, the weapon can lock multiple joints on a single target, rendering them fully immobile.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88's military culture, ESDR-1 operators are sometimes called 'sculptors' — a sardonic nod to the idea that they shape the battlefield by deciding who gets to move and who doesn't. The weapon's presence in an operation is read as a signal that command wants prisoners, not bodies. Among resistance cells and underground operators, encountering Lockjaw fire is deeply feared — not because of lethality, but because capture is considered a worse outcome than death in many of Meridian 88's interrogation contexts. There is a black-market trade in stolen ESDR-1 units, particularly among criminal organizations that run their own detention facilities.

Properties.description:
The EDPE-5 operates by generating a precisely calibrated entropic dielectric field — a sustained burst of high-frequency electromagnetic noise shaped into a coherent cone by a series of tuned metamaterial apertures housed in the barrel assembly. On contact with living tissue, the field disrupts the electrochemical gradients of nerve cells and muscle fibers without producing heat or visible light, causing a cascade of involuntary muscular contraction followed by temporary paralysis. On contact with electronic systems, it degrades capacitive insulation at the molecular level, inducing progressive dielectric breakdown across multiple components simultaneously.

What distinguishes the Candle from comparable disruption weapons is its 'fade' characteristic — the entropic field does not cut off sharply when the trigger is released but dissipates over a 1.4-second bleed period, a quirk of the metamaterial aperture design that Arcturus Defense Solutions has never fully corrected. Experienced operators have learned to exploit this, sweeping targets in the final milliseconds of a trigger pull to distribute the bleed across multiple contact zones. The weapon produces a faint amber luminescence at the muzzle during discharge — the source of its nickname.

The EDPE-5 is moderately sized, resembling a flattened carbine, with a matte polymer chassis and a distinctive hexagonal barrel shroud that houses the aperture array. Its power cell is a proprietary format that draws criticism for poor field replaceability, but the cell's high energy density allows for up to 40 full-power discharges before depletion.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 18m cone, 8m optimal
cone angle: 22 degrees
discharge duration: Continuous while trigger held; 1.4s bleed on release
power cell: ADS Type-F proprietary cell, 40 charges
weight: 3.1kg unloaded
dimensions: 62cm length, 14cm width at shroud
paralysis duration: 45–120 seconds depending on exposure
electronic damage: Progressive; full dielectric failure after 3 sustained exposures
Properties.tactical_use: Primarily used for room clearing and capture operations where lethal force is undesirable or politically complicated. Security contractors favor it for detaining high-value targets whose cybernetic implants must remain intact post-capture. The bleed exploit is taught in Arcturus-certified training programs as the 'sweep and fade' technique. Operatives working in narrow corridors report the cone angle as a liability; the weapon performs best in open spaces where the operator can maintain distance.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88's corporate security culture, carrying a Candle signals professional restraint — the weapon of an operator who takes living prisoners. Enforcement divisions of mid-tier corporations issue it as standard kit for internal affairs teams and executive protection details. On the street, it has developed a sinister secondary reputation: kidnapping rings prize it for obvious reasons, and its presence at a crime scene is treated by law enforcement as evidence of premeditated abduction rather than impulsive violence.
Properties.story_hooks: A Candle recovered from a crime scene has a serial number that traces back to a decommissioned Arcturus lot — but the lot was supposedly destroyed in a warehouse fire three years ago. Someone resurrected that shipment.; An operator is hired to capture a target alive using a Candle, but on arrival discovers the target is a child with experimental neural implants — the dielectric field may cause permanent damage rather than temporary paralysis.; The 'fade' bleed characteristic has been discovered to interact catastrophically with a specific brand of cardiac pacemaker implant, producing fatal arrhythmia. Arcturus is suppressing the information. A whistleblower wants it public.

Properties.description:
The Ferroelectric Shatter Sidearm generates a localized ferroelectric inversion pulse within a magnetically confined payload of ceramic-metallic composite microbeads — roughly 400 per charge — held in suspension inside the barrel chamber. When fired, the inversion pulse causes each microbead to undergo rapid piezoelectric expansion at an individually offset frequency, creating a cascade of asymmetric fractures across the entire payload simultaneously. The result is not a spray of intact pellets but a cloud of irregularly fractured shards, each tumbling along a slightly different vector, expanding outward in a pattern more akin to a shattering dinner plate than a conventional shotgun spread.

The FESA-2's lethality is deceptive at a glance — it looks like a stubby, unremarkable sidearm, slightly bulbous at the muzzle. At close range, the fracture-cascade cloud creates wound profiles that confound standard trauma treatment, as fragments arrive at skin at varying angles and velocities, defeating layered soft armor by exploiting gaps between impact zones. At medium range the cloud disperses enough to be largely non-lethal, making it a weapon with an unusually sharp lethality curve. ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS markets it as a 'dynamic area denial sidearm,' which is corporate language for a weapon that is devastating in corridors and useless in open fields.

The FESA-2 earned its street name 'Gravel' not from its payload but from the sound it makes on discharge — a dry, grinding crack rather than a conventional report, as if someone snapped a handful of stones. It is a compact weapon favored by operators who work in enclosed environments: ship interiors, server vaults, transit tunnels. The fracture pattern leaves a distinctive wound signature that forensic teams in Meridian 88 refer to informally as a 'gravel stamp.'
Properties.aliases: Gravel, The Pebble Chucker, Shatterpop, Scatter Mouth
Properties.legality: Prohibited in civilian contexts; licensed for contracted security and military units
Properties.specifications:
effective range: Lethal: 0–6 meters; suppression: 6–14 meters
payload per charge: ~400 ceramic-metallic composite microbeads
charges per magazine: 8
weight: 1.1 kg loaded
dimensions: 22 cm length, 9 cm muzzle width
power source: Integrated ferroelectric capacitor, charges from standard sidearm rail
armor interaction: Defeats soft armor at close range via distributed impact; ineffective against rigid plate
Properties.tactical_use: Standard deployment is as a close-quarters backup weapon for operators breaching confined spaces. Often paired with a primary that handles open engagement. Some users fire a Gravel round into a doorway before entering to suppress occupants without full lethal commitment. Tunnel security teams in Meridian 88's underground infrastructure districts carry it as a primary for exactly this reason. A known tactic is the 'double door' — fire into a room, wait for the sound of impacts, then breach while targets are disoriented.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88's labyrinthine sub-infrastructure — the transit tunnels, server crawlways, and maintenance corridors that form the city's unglamorous skeleton — the Gravel has become a symbol of the workers and security personnel who live and operate in those spaces. Tunnel gangs prize it as a status weapon precisely because it's useless above-ground; owning one signals that you belong to the underground world. Surface-level street culture views it with mild contempt for this reason, calling it a 'mole gun.'
Properties.story_hooks: A series of killings in the transit tunnels all bear the gravel stamp wound signature, but the FESA-2 units licensed to that district are all accounted for. Someone is running an unlicensed unit — or ARCTURUS has a leak in its supply chain.; A tunnel gang leader is found dead with a gravel stamp, killed by their own weapon. The sidearm is missing. Their second-in-command insists it was stolen during a deal, but the meeting location was a dead end with no exits.; ARCTURUS quietly updates the FESA-2 firmware, adding a remote disable feature. Operators who discover this are furious — and one of them is planning to make the update public in the most dramatic way possible.; A forensic investigator builds a career on identifying gravel stamp wounds — until a case comes in where the wound profile matches a FESA-2 but the victim was killed in a location physically impossible to reach with one.

Properties.description:
The FDID-6 is a close-range, high-precision drone developed by ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC as an evolution of their medical ferrofluid delivery research. It carries a pressurized reservoir of bioactive ferrofluid — a suspension of iron-oxide nanoparticles in a carrier medium engineered for rapid transdermal absorption — and delivers it in a fine aerosolized spray at contact range. Once the ferrofluid has been absorbed through skin, ZHENG-DAO's proprietary external magnetic induction array in the drone's chassis can remotely agitate the nanoparticles, generating localized heat, mechanical disruption at the capillary level, and interference with nearby electronic implants through induced magnetic fields.

The weapon's name comes from the visible effect of deployment — the ferrofluid carrier medium has a faint rust-red tint, and targets who have been dosed show a distinctive reddening of exposed skin that fades over several hours as the carrier medium metabolizes. The nanoparticles themselves remain active in superficial tissue for 72–96 hours, during which time the drone or any compatible ZHENG-DAO induction controller can activate the thermal and mechanical effects remotely from up to 30 meters. This creates a delayed-action profile unique among drone platforms: the FDID-6 can mark a target and disengage, with the actual incapacitation triggered later at the operator's discretion.

Against targets with subdermal electronics — implants, neural interfaces, payment chips — the magnetic induction effect is dramatically amplified, causing device malfunctions ranging from temporary shutdown to permanent damage in high-intensity activation. This anti-augmentation profile has made the FDID-6 particularly controversial in heavily augmented communities.
Properties.aliases: Ironblush, Blush Drone, The Painter, Rust Kiss
Properties.specifications:
dimensions: 19cm x 16cm x 10cm
ferrofluid reservoir: 80ml (sufficient for 12–15 target applications)
spray range: Contact to 1.5m
remote activation range: Up to 30m (compatible ZHENG-DAO induction controller required)
nanoparticle active window: 72–96 hours post-application
power source: Dual lithium-ceramic cells
battery life: 40 minutes flight, unlimited induction activations (controller-dependent)
weight: 1.4kg
visible marker: Rust-red carrier tint, fades 4–8 hours post-application
Properties.tactical_use: Specialist operators use the FDID-6 in two distinct phases: a marking phase, where the drone approaches a target under cover of crowd or confusion and delivers the ferrofluid aerosol, and an activation phase, which may occur hours or days later when the operator has positional and timing advantage. Counter-augmentation teams deploy it specifically against high-value targets with known neural or combat implants, using the magnetic interference to disable defensive systems before a direct engagement. Military units have used it to mark individuals in crowds for later remote incapacitation without requiring the drone to be present during the actual operation.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88's augmented communities — particularly the dense implant-user populations of the Zheng-Dao commercial districts — the FDID-6 has achieved a near-mythological status as a weapon of persecution. Stories circulate of people developing unexplained implant failures days after routine crowd exposure, and a minor industry of 'ferrofluid detox' clinics has emerged, most offering useless treatments but some providing genuine nanoparticle chelation therapy. The rust-red blush of recent application has become an object of paranoia — people with naturally ruddy complexions have reported being avoided on public transit.
Properties.story_hooks: Three augmented activists have had their implants fail catastrophically within the same week — the only connection is that all three attended the same public demonstration four days earlier.; A ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC research defector is offering the players the chelation formula for active FDID-6 nanoparticles in exchange for extraction — but they've already been marked.; The players are hired to steal an FDID-6 unit, only to discover the target they're stealing it from has already used it on someone in their network, and the 72-hour window is closing.

Properties.description:
The FIC-6 fires a pressurised payload of magnetically-responsive ferrofluid that, upon impact, is activated by a trailing induction pulse from the weapon's secondary emitter. The fluid — a suspension of iron nanoparticles in a low-viscosity carrier — spreads across the target surface on impact and then responds to the induction pulse by undergoing violent magnetic excitation. The particles heat rapidly, the carrier medium vaporises, and the iron suspension becomes a superheated aerosol that drives through gaps, seams, and porous surfaces with extreme prejudice.

Against armoured targets, the Ironbloom's mechanism is particularly effective because conventional armour design assumes threats from the outside. The ferrofluid finds joints, ventilation gaps, and sensor apertures — and the induction pulse activates it once it has already partially infiltrated the interior. Against unarmoured biological targets, the initial impact distributes the fluid across a wide area before activation, producing an effect operators have described as 'wearing a coat that catches fire from the inside.' The weapon is devastating at close to medium range and becomes increasingly imprecise beyond 20 metres as the fluid disperses.

HELIX BIOSYSTEMS developed the ferrofluid compound originally for targeted drug delivery — the induction activation mechanism was designed to release medication at specific internal sites. The weaponised application was reportedly developed by a contractor working from stolen research, and HELIX has been litigating intellectual property claims against the FIC-6's actual manufacturer (a shell corp believed to be a TESSERA CORPONATION subsidiary) for eleven years without resolution.
Properties.manufacturer: TESSERA CORPONATION (disputed; shell subsidiary 'Irongate Applied Systems')
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 3–22 metres (optimal 8–15m)
payload capacity: 12 shots (ferrofluid canister, field-replaceable)
induction pulse lag: 0.3 seconds post-impact (adjustable 0.1–1.2 seconds)
activation temperature: Nanoparticle excitation reaches 800°C within 0.15 seconds of pulse
power source: Dual cell (pressure system + induction emitter, independent)
weight: 3.8 kg
form factor: Bulky carbine with underslung fluid canister and rear induction housing
armour interaction: Penetrates standard joint gaps; reduced effectiveness against fully sealed suits
Properties.tactical_use: The FIC-6 is most effective when operators can get within 12 metres of a target. The adjustable pulse lag is a critical tactical variable — a shorter lag activates the fluid on the exterior surface, maximising burn area; a longer lag allows the fluid to infiltrate gaps before activation, maximising armour penetration. Experienced operators read the target's armour type before adjusting. The weapon is poorly suited to long engagements due to the canister's 12-shot capacity and the time required to swap canisters under fire. It is almost exclusively used as an ambush weapon or a breach tool in confined spaces.
Properties.cultural_context: The Ironbloom has a specific reputation in Meridian 88's mercenary and enforcement circles: it is considered a weapon for people who want to make a point about armour. Carrying one signals that you expect armoured opposition and have specific ideas about how to handle it. Corporate security teams that encounter FIC-6 use in the field typically escalate their threat assessment immediately — not because the weapon is the most powerful available, but because someone who brought an Ironbloom to a job planned ahead. The ongoing HELIX litigation has given the weapon an additional layer of corporate intrigue, and some operators carry one specifically to antagonise TESSERA's legal opponents.
Properties.story_hooks: HELIX BIOSYSTEMS hires the players to obtain physical evidence linking the FIC-6 to TESSERA's shell subsidiary — evidence that has been locked inside a seized weapon cache held by a third-party gang who don't know what they have.; A player character's armoured contact was killed by an Ironbloom. The adjustable pulse lag was set to maximum — someone knew exactly what armour they were wearing and planned accordingly. This was personal.; A batch of FIC-6 canisters has been adulterated — the ferrofluid compound has been contaminated with a biological agent that aerosolises on activation. Someone is using the weapon's distribution network to deploy a targeted pathogen.; The players are offered a job escorting a shipment of FIC-6s. Midway through, they discover the buyer is a group planning to use them against a civilian target — a corporate housing block whose residents are inconvenient to a development project.

Properties.description:
The GDG-2 is a form-fitting combat gauntlet extending from fingertip to mid-forearm, constructed from a conductive polymer shell over a flexible titanium mesh substrate. Embedded within the palm and finger surfaces are a series of galvanic discharge nodes capable of delivering precisely modulated electrical pulses on contact. Unlike crude shock weapons, the GDG-2 does not simply stun — its discharge profile is engineered to induce involuntary neuromuscular disruption in specific muscle groups, causing targeted tremor, grip failure, or full limb incapacitation depending on where contact is made and which discharge mode is selected.

The gauntlet interfaces with a compact forearm-mounted controller that allows the operator to toggle between three discharge profiles: a grip-failure mode targeting hand and forearm musculature, a leg-incapacitation mode calibrated for thigh and calf contact, and a full-body seizure mode reserved for maximum-force situations. The system includes a biometric lock keyed to the operator's galvanic skin signature, preventing the gauntlet from discharging if removed from its registered user. The polymer shell is rated for light impact protection and provides partial insulation against return electrical hazards.

The GDG-2 was originally developed for law enforcement crowd management and non-lethal suspect control, but its discharge profiles were quietly expanded in the Mk2 revision to include settings that can induce cardiac arrhythmia on sustained contact. This revision was never publicly documented, and ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC has consistently denied any lethality potential in official materials.
Properties.tier_availability: Tier 2+ (law enforcement); Black market (Mk2 full profile)
Properties.legality: Licensed (law enforcement issue); Prohibited (civilian Mk2 profile)
Properties.specifications:
coverage: Fingertip to mid-forearm
discharge nodes: 14
discharge profiles: 3
peak output: 0.8–4.2 joules (profile-dependent)
power source: Forearm-mounted power cell, 200 full discharges per charge
shell material: Conductive polymer over titanium mesh
biometric lock: Galvanic skin signature recognition
weight: 420g
Properties.tactical_use: Law enforcement operators use the GDG-2 to control suspects without drawing firearms in politically sensitive environments. Grip-failure mode is applied during disarming maneuvers. In private security contexts, operators target joint contact points to drop a subject without visible injury, which is valued in corporate settings where discretion matters. Mk2 operators with full profile access use the cardiac mode as a last resort in close-quarters assassination scenarios where silence is paramount.
Properties.cultural_context: The GDG-2 is a symbol of institutional authority in Meridian 88 — seeing an officer wearing one signals you are in a district with resources and governance, for better or worse. Among the underclass, 'getting shook' by a Palsy is a humiliating form of public control that has sparked at least two district-level protests in recent years. On the black market, the Mk2's hidden lethality profile has made it a favorite of corporate cleaners who need deniable methods, and the gauntlet's medical appearance allows it to pass casual inspection.
Properties.story_hooks: A municipal officer dies of apparent cardiac arrest during a routine arrest — witnesses report she was wearing a GDG-2 during the struggle, raising the question of whether the suspect accessed the gauntlet's undocumented lethality profile or whether the device malfunctioned.; A whistleblower from ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC is trying to leak documentation of the Mk2's hidden cardiac mode to a journalist, but they've gone quiet. The last message they sent mentioned someone wearing a Palsy gauntlet had been following them.; A crime lord runs an underground fighting circuit where combatants are required to use GDG-2 gauntlets — the spectacle of watching fighters lose muscular control mid-bout is the main attraction, and the matches are broadcast illegally to wealthy subscribers citywide.

Properties.description:
The GIFDL-2 delivers a precisely calibrated galvanic current payload through a focused electrolytic carrier beam, driving rapid osmotic imbalance in the interstitial fluid of exposed soft tissue. The effect is a sudden, painful redistribution of fluid across cellular membranes in the targeted region — subcutaneous swelling, intense pressure sensation, and temporary loss of fine motor control as nerves compress against distended tissue. At high settings, capillary rupture produces visible bruising within minutes of exposure.

The lance's distinctive feature is its dual-mode emitter: a narrow 'focal' mode that concentrates the effect on a single limb or joint, and a wide 'flood' mode that distributes a milder osmotic disruption across the upper torso. Focal mode is the preferred surgical option for restraint operations — a single discharge to the hand renders grip impossible for up to forty minutes. Flood mode is used for area denial and crowd compliance, producing widespread discomfort without targeting specific anatomy.

Helix Biosystems developed the GIFDL-2 ostensibly for advanced surgical irrigation research, and the cover story has worn increasingly thin over the years. The weapon's design files were subpoenaed in two separate municipal investigations before Helix successfully argued proprietary protection. It remains technically legal in four of Meridian 88's administrative sectors under a medical research exemption that no independent body has reviewed in over a decade.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 4–22 meters (focal), 2–8 meters (flood)
power source: Saline electrolyte capacitor pack, 14 focal or 6 flood discharges
onset time: Immediate pressure sensation; full effect within 8–12 seconds
duration of effect: 25–45 minutes depending on target hydration
weight: 2.7 kg
form factor: Long pistol with swappable emitter head
visible signature: Faint blue-white corona at emitter tip during discharge
Properties.tactical_use: Restraint operatives favor focal mode for clean disarmament — a single shot to the weapon hand ends a confrontation without fatality or loud report. Interrogation contractors use it to produce sustained discomfort for compliance purposes, a use Helix officially denies supporting. Flood mode sees use in tight corridor breaches where multiple targets must be suppressed simultaneously. The weapon's main tactical limitation is its short flood range and the visible swelling it produces, which makes concealment of its use difficult after the fact.
Properties.cultural_context: The GIFDL-2 is deeply associated with Meridian 88's private detention industry — corporate holding facilities, black-site compliance centers, and the euphemistically named 'resolution suites' operated by high-end legal firms. Victims who have been subjected to it often describe the experience in terms of shame as much as pain, a bodily betrayal they find difficult to articulate. Among resistance and labor organizer circles, 'getting bloated' has become shorthand for any encounter with corporate enforcement that leaves no visible evidence for a legal complaint.
Properties.story_hooks: A detainee released from a corporate holding facility shows inexplicable internal bruising that no standard weapon accounts for — a medic who recognizes the pattern knows exactly what it means.; Someone is using a stolen GIFDL-2 in a series of targeted attacks on mid-level corporate managers, leaving them incapacitated but alive with no conventional forensic evidence.; Helix Biosystems is quietly recalling all registered GIFDL-2 units — the reason given is a 'firmware update,' but sources inside the company suggest a catastrophic failure mode has been discovered at high power settings.; A fixer needs a GIFDL-2 sourced quietly for a job that requires a target to appear to have a sudden medical episode rather than an assault.

Nodes.Name: A small number of high-end personal protection operators who use focal mode as a non-lethal deterrent

Properties.description:
The Galvanic Marrow Projector GMP-1 delivers a precisely tuned galvanic current through a directional conductive beam that penetrates surface tissue and targets the high-conductivity environment of bone marrow directly. Bone marrow, suspended in its semi-fluid lipid matrix within the skeletal cavity, conducts galvanic current far more readily than surrounding tissue, allowing the GMP-1 to bypass surface armor and even subdermal plating by routing its effect through the skeletal system rather than against it. The result is an intense, incapacitating pain response originating from deep within the body, accompanied by temporary disruption of the hematopoietic activity that marrow performs — effectively stunning the body's blood production system.

Ringo Corponation developed the GMP-1 for crowd compliance applications following regulatory pressure against lethal crowd control options after the Meridian 88 South Quarter incident. The weapon was marketed as a 'non-lethal deep compliance system' — language that has since been challenged in three separate regulatory reviews, as prolonged exposure causes marrow necrosis and long-term hematological complications that manifest weeks after the initial event. Ringo's legal team has successfully argued that these delayed complications do not constitute immediate lethality, keeping the weapon in a compliance classification rather than a lethal one.

The GMP-1 fires with a low electrical buzz and leaves no visible wound on the target, which made it attractive to security forces wanting deniable compliance options. Users who have been hit describe the sensation as a profound wrongness centered in their bones — not surface pain but something deeper and more disorienting, as if the pain is coming from the inside of the body rather than the outside. The psychological effect is significant and persistent; many survivors report bone-deep anxiety responses for months afterward, triggered by the sound of electrical equipment.
Properties.aliases: Marrowbone, The Deep Ache, Bone Gun, Resonant Pain
Properties.legality: Licensed — certified compliance and security use; Restricted — extended exposure modification; Prohibited — civilian ownership
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 2–20 meters
current delivery: 0.4–2.8 mA adjustable, directed beam
exposure threshold safe: Under 3 seconds continuous
exposure threshold damaging: Over 8 seconds continuous
power source: Galvanic cell pack, 45 shots per charge at standard setting
weight: 2.6 kg
penetration depth: Effective against subdermal plating up to 8mm
form factor: Compact rifle with adjustable exposure dial and beam collimator
Properties.tactical_use: Used in crowd dispersal, detainee compliance, and situations requiring incapacitation without visible injury. Operators are trained to use short exposure bursts to induce compliance without crossing into tissue damage thresholds — though field reports consistently show operators exceeding safe exposure durations during high-stress deployments. The weapon's ability to penetrate subdermal armor makes it effective against heavily augmented targets who have otherwise made themselves resistant to surface-level compliance tools. In extended exposure configurations, used as a slow-acting punishment weapon whose effects are deniable due to the delayed onset of damage.
Properties.cultural_context: The GMP-1 is one of Meridian 88's most politically contested weapons. Compliance forces defend it as a non-lethal option that saves lives; medical researchers and civil rights organizations have spent years documenting the delayed hematological damage that Ringo Corponation's legal team continues to reframe as unrelated health conditions. The weapon has become a symbol of institutional violence that hides behind technicality — the slow ache that the city produces in the people it controls. 'Marrowboned' has entered Meridian 88 slang as a term for someone whose resistance has been broken from the inside, left standing but fundamentally damaged.
Properties.story_hooks: A LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS researcher has quietly been treating an unusual cluster of hematological cases in the lower districts — all with the same damage profile, all claiming they were 'never hit by anything' — and the data is about to go public unless someone stops it.; A player character has been experiencing bone-deep aches for weeks after a crowd compliance incident — a street doctor tells them they have GMP-1 marrow damage, and the statute of limitations on filing a complaint expires in 72 hours.; A modified GMP-1 with the safety limiters removed has been used in a string of apparent natural deaths — the bodies show no external wounds, and the coroner is classifying them as cardiac events.; RINGO CORPONATION is lobbying to remove the exposure duration limits from the GMP-1's compliance classification — a player character is approached by a civil rights organization to steal the internal research documents that would prove the company already knows the current limits are insufficient.

Properties.description:
The Galvanic Myofibril Lash is a flexible close-combat weapon produced by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric, consisting of a 1.8-meter braided cord of synthetic myofibril polymer threaded with a continuous galvanic filament network. When activated, the lash generates a rolling galvanic charge across its entire length, peaking at the tip where contact is most likely. On contact with biological tissue, the charge triggers involuntary myofibril contraction in the target's musculature — not merely painful surface-level stimulation, but a deep galvanic cascade that forces the target's own muscle fibers to seize against themselves, producing acute cramping, postural collapse, and in sustained contact scenarios, localized rhabdomyolysis.

The GML-2's design is informed by Zheng-Dao's extensive proprietary research into synthetic muscle systems for their prosthetics division. The myofibril polymer used in the lash is a byproduct of rejected actuator materials — too brittle for load-bearing prosthetic use but ideal for a flexible weapon that needs to conduct charge without becoming rigid. The polymer gives the lash an unsettling quality in motion: it moves with slightly too much fluid articulation, more like a living appendage than a manufactured cord, and operators who train extensively with it develop an instinctive, almost organic style of combat that observers describe as watching someone fight with a severed limb.

Against cyborg targets, the GML-2 performs inconsistently — heavily augmented individuals with subdermal insulation are largely immune, while those with neural-muscular interface implants can experience catastrophic feedback through the lash's charge interfacing with their augmentation's own signal pathways. Zheng-Dao does not advertise this latter effect.
Properties.specifications:
length: 1.8 meters (active), coils to 0.3m diameter
weight: 0.6 kg
power source: Grip-integrated microcell, 90-minute continuous operation
charge output: 0.4 – 2.8 mA adaptive, tip-concentrated delivery
polymer composition: Zheng-Dao Type-7 rejected actuator myofibril blend
effective range: Contact to 1.8m
augmentation interaction: Unpredictable on neural-muscular interface implants — flagged in safety documentation
Properties.tactical_use: The GML-2 excels in crowd control and restraint scenarios where lethal force is discouraged but reliable incapacitation is required. A skilled operator can use the lash to target specific muscle groups — wrapping it around a target's leg to drop them, snapping it across the forearm to force a weapon drop, or catching it around the neck to trigger cervical cramping that pins a target in place. In anti-personnel applications, the lash is used to keep opponents off-balance and disable their ability to mount effective resistance before a finishing technique. Its reach advantage over conventional melee weapons means operators can engage from outside immediate grapple range, a significant tactical benefit in corridor and doorway engagements.
Properties.cultural_context: The GML-2 occupies an uncomfortable cultural space in Meridian 88 — officially marketed as a non-lethal compliance tool for private security, it is widely known to be capable of causing serious internal injury with sustained application. This ambiguity makes it popular with corporate security contractors who need legal cover for aggressive enforcement while maintaining plausible non-lethality. In the Sublevel districts, modified versions with the charge ceiling removed are a staple of debt-collection work, and the sight of a coiled lash on someone's belt is a recognized signal in the informal economy — this person collects. Zheng-Dao has quietly lobbied against reclassification of the weapon as lethal, citing their prosthetics research partnerships as evidence of corporate good faith.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of deaths attributed to 'cardiac events' in the Sublevel districts all show the same internal muscle damage pattern consistent with a modified GML-2 — someone has removed the safety limiters and is using the weapon to make murders look like natural causes.; Zheng-Dao is offering a significant finder's fee for a stolen research prototype of the GML-3 — the next generation lash with an onboard neural map that can selectively target augmentation interfaces. The prototype is somewhere in the black market, and multiple factions want it.; A player character with neural-muscular interface implants receives a warning from an anonymous source: someone in their social circle is carrying a GML-2, and the interaction with their specific implant model has a documented 60% chance of causing permanent motor damage.

Properties.description:
The GPFE-4 functions by projecting a pulsed galvanic current through a directed beam of ionized saline vapor, creating a conductive pathway that deposits low-frequency electrical oscillations directly into bone tissue. These oscillations do not fracture bone acutely — instead, they induce accelerated piezoelectric fatigue at the microscopic level, progressively weakening the crystalline hydroxyapatite matrix that gives bone its structural integrity. A single sustained exposure of three to five seconds produces microfractures distributed across the targeted load-bearing bone. The target feels a deep ache but remains mobile. Under any significant mechanical stress — running, jumping, a hard fall — the bone fails catastrophically along the fatigue lines.

The delayed-onset nature of the damage is the weapon's defining and most disturbing characteristic. A target struck by the GPFE-4 may not experience incapacitation for minutes or hours after exposure, during which time they appear entirely functional. The weapon is consequently almost impossible to counter in the moment of use — by the time the injury manifests, the operator is long gone. Helix Biosystems developed the GPFE-4 ostensibly as a research instrument for studying accelerated bone fatigue in microgravity simulation environments. Its migration into weapons applications was unofficial and rapid.

The 'Hairline' nickname reflects both the weapon's mechanism — hairline fractures distributed across bone — and the razor-thin margin it exploits between appearing unharmed and being on the verge of catastrophic skeletal failure. Among Meridian 88's medical community, injuries consistent with GPFE-4 exposure are referred to informally as 'slow breaks' or 'time bombs,' and diagnosing them before they manifest requires specialized bone density imaging that most public clinics cannot afford.
Properties.aliases: Hairline, The Stress Gun, Bone Tired, GPFE
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 3–25 meters
power source: Dual-cell galvanic array, 18 exposures per charge
exposure duration for effect: 3–5 seconds continuous
fatigue onset window: Structural failure typically within 20 minutes of significant physical exertion post-exposure
weight: 2.1 kg
form factor: Compact emitter with integrated saline vapor reservoir, pistol-adjacent profile
countermeasures: Bone density augmentation implants reduce susceptibility by approximately 40%; full skeletal composite replacement provides near-immunity
Properties.tactical_use: The GPFE-4 is overwhelmingly a weapon of assassination and sabotage rather than direct confrontation. Operators tag a target in a crowd, during a meeting, or in a casual encounter — the exposure can be disguised as a near-miss or a brush-by in close quarters — then withdraw. The target's subsequent collapse during a foot chase, a physical altercation, or even a fall down stairs reads as an accident or a pre-existing condition. Intelligence operatives prize it for this deniability. In direct combat, it is occasionally used to pre-damage a target before an engagement, ensuring that any physical exertion in the fight will result in sudden incapacitation.
Properties.cultural_context: The GPFE-4 occupies a particularly feared niche in Meridian 88's underworld because it violates the implicit legibility of violence — you cannot see or feel the damage being done to you. It has generated a subcultural paranoia among high-value targets and fixers, some of whom undergo monthly bone density scans as a precaution. Helix Biosystems officially denies any weapons applications of the technology, but three separate corporate espionage investigations have traced GPFE-4 units back to a Helix subsidiary. The weapon is also quietly associated with a specific style of political killing — making deaths look accidental — that has been linked to at least two major power shifts in the city's district governance.
Properties.story_hooks: A city council member died in what was ruled a accidental fall. Her aide is convinced it was deliberate and has bone density scans that don't match the official story — but the scans came from a clinic that has since been bought out and shuttered.; Someone is selling GPFE-4 units with a modification that extends the fatigue onset window to 72 hours. The upgrade makes the weapon even more deniable and someone is distributing it specifically in the financial district.; A street-level runner collapsed mid-job with a femur failure and survived. She doesn't know when she was hit or by whom, but she has a job log from the past week and needs someone to figure out which encounter was the exposure.; Helix Biosystems is quietly funding a bone augmentation clinic in an upscale district ��� one that happens to sell the only commercially available implant that provides meaningful GPFE-4 resistance. The protection racket implications are not subtle.

Properties.description:
The GVDP-1 generates a cloud of electrostatically charged ionic vapor by flash-vaporizing a saline-metallic solution through a galvanic induction chamber. The resulting mist carries a sustained galvanic charge that, upon contact with biological tissue, drives ions through the skin's surface via electrophoretic pressure — bypassing the need for penetration or direct electrical contact. Once ionic particles have penetrated the skin barrier, they create a localized galvanic circuit within the tissue itself, generating heat and electrochemical disruption at the cellular level. The effect is experienced as a deep burning sensation beneath the skin with no visible external cause, accompanied by involuntary muscle fasciculation.

The GVDP-1's vapor cloud persists for approximately 8-12 seconds in still air before dispersing, during which time any target moving through it receives continuous ionic exposure. This area-denial quality distinguishes it from point-target electrical weapons — the cloud hangs in space and punishes movement through it rather than requiring the operator to track a specific target. In enclosed spaces with limited airflow, the persistence time extends significantly, making interior engagements particularly dangerous. The weapon is largely ineffective outdoors in strong wind, a limitation operators learn to account for.

Ringo Corponation produced the GVDP-1 as part of a broader non-lethal compliance tool line marketed to corporate security divisions and private detention facilities. Its civilian applications — crowd management, perimeter enforcement in enclosed facilities — gave it broad initial distribution before its more aggressive applications became apparent. The pistol form factor makes it concealable, and the vapor it produces is colorless in most lighting conditions, contributing to its reputation as a weapon that creates confusion about the source and nature of the attack.
Properties.aliases: Saltlick, The Licker, Brine Gun, Galvanic Mist
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 2–10 meters (cloud projection)
cloud persistence: 8–12 seconds still air; up to 30 seconds in enclosed spaces
ionic penetration depth: 2–4mm subcutaneous
primary effects: Subdermal burning, involuntary muscle fasciculation, disorientation
solution capacity: 18 discharges per reservoir
weight: 1.1 kg loaded
wind sensitivity: Highly susceptible to dispersal above 15 km/h wind
operator protection: Recommended insulated gloves; vapor is self-dispersing at operator distance if fired directionally
dimensions: 22cm overall
Properties.tactical_use: Operators use the GVDP-1 primarily to control space rather than engage specific targets — firing into doorways, corridors, or stairwells to deny passage or flush entrenched opponents. In interrogation and detention contexts, it is used for compliance enforcement with plausible deniability, as the subdermal effects leave no visible marks. Multiple cloud discharges in a confined space can create an environment where sustained presence becomes untenable. Experienced operators combine it with visual obstructions — smoke, darkness — to maximize disorientation.
Properties.cultural_context: The GVDP-1 has become deeply associated with corporate detention and private security excess in Meridian 88. Its origins as a 'non-lethal compliance tool' have made it a symbol of institutional coercion — the kind of violence that doesn't leave marks, that can be denied, that operates in the gap between formal policy and what actually happens in holding facilities. Anti-corporate activists who have experienced detention in Ringo-contracted facilities often describe the Saltlick as emblematic of a particular kind of systemic cruelty: technically legal, officially non-lethal, and quietly devastating. Some carry recovered units as evidence of what was done to them.
Properties.story_hooks: A former detainee from a Ringo Corponation facility is documenting injuries consistent with extended GVDP-1 exposure — injuries that don't appear on any official incident report. She needs someone to get inside the facility and pull the usage logs before a scheduled audit wipes them.; The players are hired to recover a person being held in a corporate facility. The holding wing's ventilation system has been deliberately compromised to extend vapor persistence. The entire wing is effectively a continuous Saltlick environment.; A black-market dealer offers the players a crate of GVDP-1 units at near-cost. The lot numbers match a batch reported stolen from a Ringo Corponation facility during an incident that was officially classified as a maintenance accident.; A player character has been experiencing unexplained subdermal burning sensations for three days. A street medic confirms electrophoretic ionic residue in the tissue — consistent with GVDP-1 exposure. Someone dosed them without their knowledge. The question is when, and who was close enough.

Properties.description:
The GFR-3 operates on stacked linear magnetic acceleration coils arranged in a helical configuration, cycling sub-caliber tungsten-ceramic flechettes at approximately 4,200 rounds per minute. Each flechette — roughly 3mm wide and 22mm long — is ferromagnetically coated along its rear third, allowing the coil stack to grab, accelerate, and release in under 0.8 milliseconds per round. The result is a nearly silent, caseless stream of kinetic penetrators that can saturate a doorframe-sized area at close range or punch through light armor panels at distance.

What distinguishes the GFR-3 from earlier gauss repeaters is its adaptive coil timing system, which reads barrel temperature and magnetic field saturation 200 times per second and adjusts current delivery to maintain consistent muzzle velocity even as the barrel heats. Earlier models suffered from 'velocity drift,' where rounds fired late in a magazine were significantly slower than initial rounds, producing inconsistent terminal performance. The GFR-3 solved this through TESSERA CORPONATION's proprietary FluxSync firmware, which also enables selectable dispersion patterns — tight column for armor penetration, wide fan for crowd suppression.

The weapon uses a 300-round cassette magazine that sits beneath the barrel in a bullpup configuration, giving the GFR-3 a stubby, aggressive silhouette. It has no mechanical action, no ejection port, and minimal moving parts beyond the cassette feed mechanism, which makes it exceptionally reliable in wet or contaminated environments. The lack of a traditional trigger group — replaced by a capacitive palm sensor and a pressure ring around the grip — means the weapon cannot fire if not held correctly, a feature that has made it popular with corporate security who worry about weapon retention.
Properties.aliases: Needlerain, The Sewing Machine, Flechette Storm, GFR-3
Properties.specifications:
caliber: 3x22mm tungsten-ceramic flechette
feed system: 300-round sealed cassette, electromagnetic advancement
rate of fire: 4,200 RPM (cyclic), adjustable to 800 RPM semi-burst
effective range: 12m (fan dispersion), 180m (column mode)
muzzle velocity: 1,050 m/s nominal (FluxSync maintained)
weight: 2.8 kg loaded
dimensions: 410mm length, 240mm height
power source: Integrated 18V lithium-polymer cell, 6 cassettes per charge
operating temperature: -20°C to +65°C
Properties.tactical_use: Corporate security teams use the GFR-3 primarily in column mode for breaching armored targets at short-to-medium range, switching to fan dispersion for room clearing or crowd control. Its silence — the loudest component is the faint magnetic hum and the impact of flechettes — makes it favored for operations where noise discipline matters. The 300-round cassette allows sustained suppressive fire without reloads, though operators are trained to swap cassettes at 150 rounds to avoid feed jams from heat buildup in the advancement mechanism. Some operators tape two cassettes together for rapid exchange.
Properties.cultural_context: The GFR-3 carries a specific social weight in Meridian 88: it is the weapon of the corporate floor. Seen holstered on TESSERA's own lobby security and licensed to a dozen mid-tier corporate clients, the 'Needlerain' is understood as a statement of institutional violence — clean, efficient, calibrated. Street gangs rarely carry them because the cassette magazines are expensive and proprietary. When one appears outside a corporate context, it usually means someone raided a security depot or a corporate operative has gone freelance. The weapon's silence gives it a particular dread reputation in the lower arcologies, where the first sign of a GFR-3 in the room is often the sound of someone else getting hit.
Properties.story_hooks: A GFR-3 cassette recovered from a crime scene is stamped with a TESSERA internal security lot number — meaning it came from inside the building, not from outside; The FluxSync firmware update pushed to all GFR-3 units contains a hidden killswitch that TESSERA can activate remotely, and someone has just discovered this; A weapons tech claims to have cracked the cassette format and is producing third-party flechette loads — TESSERA wants her silenced before the patent violation goes public; An operator whose GFR-3 malfunctioned during a job is suing TESSERA, and the trial is threatening to expose classified use cases for the weapon

Properties.description:
The GCC-9 represents OUROBOROS ENERGY's most aggressive weaponization of their gravimetric induction research — a technology platform the company officially licenses only for industrial compression and materials processing. The device generates an extremely short-duration gravimetric field spike, collapsing a roughly spherical volume of approximately 2 meters in diameter to a transient gravitational pressure roughly 400 times standard. The collapse event lasts approximately 40 milliseconds before field coherence fails and the compressed material is explosively rebounded outward. The inward collapse and outward rebound together constitute the weapon's kill mechanism.

The inward phase crushes everything within the primary radius — biological tissue, structural components, armor plating — into a dense, briefly coherent mass. The rebound phase then expels this compressed material at velocities sufficient to cause catastrophic fragmentation damage out to 15 meters. The resulting debris field is unusual: instead of conventional shrapnel, the rebound produces hyperdense compressed fragments of whatever was caught in the primary collapse, including bone, metal, and polymer fused together under the brief high-gravity event. Forensic investigators describe GCC-9 wound profiles as 'impossible' — fragmentation wounds containing materials from multiple sources compressed into single projectiles.

OUROBOROS ENERGY has invested significant legal resources in suppressing public knowledge of the GCC-9, arguing that the device is a classified industrial tool and that its appearance on the black market represents theft rather than distribution. Field operators who have used the weapon describe a profound psychological effect — the brief visual distortion of the collapse event, a moment where light bends visibly around the detonation point, has led to the name 'The Folding.' There are unverified reports that targets caught at the edge of the primary radius survive with gravitational trauma to dense-tissue organs that manifests days after exposure.
Properties.specifications:
primary collapse radius: 2m diameter sphere
compression factor: ~400x standard gravity
collapse duration: 40ms
rebound fragment velocity: Up to 1,800 m/s
fragmentation radius: 15m effective
field coherence power: Capacitive discharge, 8.4 MJ
weight: 3.2 kg
form factor: Spherical casing, 18cm diameter
detonation: Timed fuse, impact, or remote signal
visual signature: Visible light-lensing distortion at detonation point
Properties.tactical_use: Used as a primary breach-and-clear weapon against hardened defensive positions — the collapse phase eliminates cover and fortification simultaneously with personnel. Military applications include destroying small armored emplacements without air support. The unusual fragmentation profile means conventional ballistic shields provide minimal protection against the rebound phase. Teams deploying the GCC-9 maintain minimum 20-meter standoff distance. The weapon is rarely used in urban environments due to structural collateral damage — it will compromise load-bearing columns within the collapse radius.
Properties.cultural_context: The GCC-9 occupies a mythological space in Meridian 88's weapons underground — most operators have heard of it but few have seen one. OUROBOROS ENERGY's aggressive suppression of information about the device has paradoxically inflated its mystique, and inflated price. Possessing one signals either military-grade connections or extraordinary black-market resources. Among the city's mercenary elite, 'carrying a Sinkhole' is a mark of status as much as capability. The visible light-bending effect at detonation has made the weapon a subject of street-level urban legend — witnesses who don't know what they're seeing describe the detonation as 'the world folding in half.'
Properties.story_hooks: A GCC-9 detonates in a residential tower district, collapsing three floors — OUROBOROS ENERGY arrives before city authorities and begins 'securing the site.' What are they covering up?; The party is offered a contract to transport a GCC-9 across three corporate-controlled districts — the client won't say who the buyer is or what it's for.; A forensic investigator contacts the party after recognizing the impossible wound profiles from a crime scene — she thinks the weapon used was a GCC-9, which means someone with serious resources is operating in the city, and she needs to know who before they use it again.; OUROBOROS ENERGY's internal R&D logs, leaked by a dying whistleblower, suggest the GCC-9 was not developed for industrial use — it was developed to destroy specific types of gravimetric infrastructure, and there is exactly one such installation in Meridian 88.

Properties.description:
The Gravimetric Induction Pistol operates on a principle that remains proprietary to OUROBOROS ENERGY despite years of competitor reverse-engineering attempts: it generates a localized gravimetric anomaly at range by briefly inducing a controlled mass-energy fluctuation through a compact induction array derived from OUROBOROS's experimental power generation research. In practical terms, the weapon projects a field approximately 40 centimeters in diameter that, for a duration of 0.6 to 2.4 seconds, increases effective gravitational acceleration within that field to between 4G and 9G depending on charge level. Targets caught in the field experience sudden, extreme downward force — enough to collapse joints, fracture load-bearing bones, and rupture intervertebral discs at high settings. At low settings, it is sufficient to pin a standing target to the floor and prevent movement.

OUROBOROS ENERGY developed the induction array for entirely different purposes — specifically, for manipulating heavy industrial components in confined spaces where mechanical lifting equipment cannot operate. The weaponization of the technology was, by most accounts, accidental: an industrial incident in which a malfunctioning array pinned three workers to a catwalk for several minutes before losing power demonstrated the technology's potential in a way that OUROBOROS's defense applications division found difficult to ignore. The GIP-4 is the fourth iteration of the resulting weapon program, and the first to achieve a form factor small enough to be carried as a sidearm.

The Undertow has acquired a reputation for the specific, recognizable nature of the injuries it produces. Physicians who treat gravitational compression injuries can identify them immediately — the pattern of skeletal damage, the characteristic joint failures, the bruising geometry — and this has become a forensic liability for operators. In Meridian 88, 'gravity bruising' is increasingly recognized by both law enforcement and insurance forensics, making the Undertow less useful for operators who require deniability. Those who don't require deniability, however, find it extraordinarily effective.
Properties.aliases: Undertow, The Sinker, Gravity Gun, GIP
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 30m
field diameter: 40 cm at target
gravity multiplier: 4G–9G (4 settings)
field duration: 0.6–2.4 seconds (charge-dependent)
power source: OUROBOROS Induction Cell OIC-1 (8 shots at maximum charge, 24 at minimum)
weight: 2.3 kg
length: 28 cm
charge time: 2.1 seconds (maximum charge), 0.7 seconds (minimum charge)
field accuracy: ±12 cm at 30m
Properties.tactical_use: Operators typically use the Undertow to pin targets for secondary actions — restraint, extraction, or follow-up engagement — rather than as a primary damage tool. At maximum charge, it is used as a direct incapacitation or killing tool, particularly effective against targets in elevated positions where sudden gravitational increase causes falls. In confined spaces, operators use it to collapse targets through structural interference — pinning someone against a floor while a ceiling is low enough to cause additional compression injury. The weapon's limited shot count and charge time make it unsuitable as a primary weapon in sustained engagements.
Properties.cultural_context: The Undertow is genuinely rare — OUROBOROS ENERGY produces limited quantities and maintains strict distribution controls, partly for legal reasons and partly because the induction array components are expensive and difficult to manufacture. Possessing one is a statement of access as much as intent. In Meridian 88's criminal ecology, the Undertow is associated with high-end contract work — the kind of operator who carries one is assumed to be expensive, professional, and working for someone with significant resources. The forensic visibility of its injuries has made it a subject of interest in legal circles, where a push to establish 'gravimetric harm' as a distinct criminal category is slowly gaining traction.
Properties.story_hooks: OUROBOROS ENERGY's induction cell supply chain has been quietly disrupted — someone is buying up OIC-1 cells before they reach distribution. GIP-4 units across the city are going dark. Someone wants all the Undertows offline simultaneously.; A forensic physician has published a paper identifying 'gravimetric harm' as a distinct injury classification and linking 11 deaths over three years to GIP-4 use. OUROBOROS's legal department has filed to suppress the paper. The physician has received the filing and is deciding what to do next.; An OUROBOROS industrial facility has reported a theft — not of weapons, but of induction array components. Enough to build several GIP-4 equivalents. Someone is manufacturing unauthorized units.; A high-profile political figure was found dead with injuries consistent with gravitational compression, but no GIP-4 was recovered and no OUROBOROS cells were detected in the environment. Either someone cleaned up perfectly or the technology has been replicated in a form OUROBOROS doesn't recognize.

Properties.description:
The GSP-7 generates a localized tidal gradient — a microscale differential in gravitational field strength across a 15–20 centimeter target zone — using a pair of counter-rotating superconducting mass rings embedded in the weapon's cylindrical body. The gradient is projected as a focused columnar field approximately 3 centimeters in diameter at the point of emission, expanding to roughly 18 centimeters at optimal range. Within this column, the difference in gravitational pull between the near and far edges of the field is sufficient to impose significant shear stress on materials and tissue, stretching and tearing structures along the field axis without any projectile or beam making contact.

The practical effect on unprotected biological targets at full output is severe internal trauma along the field axis — tearing of connective tissue, rupture of fluid-filled structures, and in sustained exposure, fracture of cortical bone. The weapon does not burn, does not leave entry wounds, and produces no visible beam. Forensic examiners encountering GSP-7 casualties without prior knowledge of the weapon frequently misattribute the damage to blunt force or crush injury from environmental sources. This forensic ambiguity is the GSP-7's most valued characteristic in certain professional circles.

TESSERA CORPONATION produced the GSP-7 under a research and development program nominally aimed at materials testing — specifically, evaluating shear resistance in structural composites under variable gravitational loading. The weapons application was, by most accounts within TESSERA, an open secret from the second prototype. Current production is limited, the supply chain is deliberately obscure, and TESSERA officially categorizes the GSP-7 as a 'field gradient analysis instrument' in all public documentation.
Properties.specifications:
field generation: Dual counter-rotating superconducting mass rings
field column diameter emission: ~3 cm
field column diameter optimal range: ~18 cm
optimal effective range: 8–14 m
maximum effective range: 22 m (degraded gradient coherence)
biological effect full output: Internal shear trauma, connective tissue rupture, cortical bone fracture (sustained)
power source: Cryogenic superconductor cell, 9 full-output shots before cell replacement
cell replacement time: Approximately 4 minutes (thermal stabilization required)
weight: 1.8 kg
length: 31 cm
forensic signature: Blunt/crush trauma, no entry wound, no thermal or chemical residue
Properties.tactical_use: The GSP-7 is not a weapon for open firefights — its 9-shot cell limit, 4-minute reload, and relatively modest stopping power at single-pulse output make it unsuitable for sustained engagements. Operators use it for targeted removal of specific individuals in contexts where deniability is the primary requirement. The weapon's lack of visible beam or audible report (beyond a low-frequency hum during field generation) allows shots to be taken in crowds or controlled environments without immediate identification of the shooter or weapon type. Experienced operators aim for the torso to maximize shear contact with organ tissue.
Properties.cultural_context: The GSP-7 is rare enough in Meridian 88 that most street-level operators have never seen one. Its existence is known primarily through rumor and forensic anomalies — deaths that don't quite make sense to medical examiners who aren't looking for the right thing. Among high-tier fixers and corporate wetwork contractors, the GSP-7 is spoken of with the specific reverence reserved for tools that solve problems cleanly. TESSERA's official position that it manufactures 'field gradient analysis instruments' has become a dark joke in certain circles. Possession of a GSP-7 is understood to mean you operate at a level where the rules are written by whoever survives.
Properties.story_hooks: A prominent figure in Meridian 88 dies of what appears to be a catastrophic internal injury with no external cause — the players are brought in to investigate and eventually identify GSP-7 as the mechanism, leading them toward TESSERA's deniable operations arm.; A GSP-7 with a full cryogenic cell turns up in a location it has no business being — a low-tier criminal's stash — and tracing how it got there unravels a chain of deaths and cover-ups reaching into TESSERA's board.; TESSERA hires the players to recover a GSP-7 from a journalist who is about to publish documentation proving the 'field gradient instrument' designation is fraudulent.; A player character is accused of a killing they didn't commit — the forensic evidence matches GSP-7 damage, and someone has gone to considerable effort to place them at the scene, suggesting a high-tier actor who wants them neutralized or controlled.

Properties.description:
The GCE-3 generates a focused graviton field projection that temporarily increases the effective gravitational force acting on a target volume by a factor of between 8 and 22 times standard gravity, depending on output setting. The effect is not a beam in the electromagnetic sense — it is a localized distortion of spacetime curvature within a defined area approximately 1.5 meters in diameter at standard operating range. Targets within the field experience sudden, catastrophic increases in effective body weight: at 8G, an unaugmented human experiences immediate skeletal stress fractures and cardiovascular collapse; at 22G, soft tissue rupture is near-instantaneous. The weapon was developed by Ouroboros Energy as a theoretical physics demonstration platform before its military applications became apparent and Arcturus Defense Solutions acquired exclusive licensing rights.

The GCE-3's technological foundation draws on the same graviton manipulation research that underlies Meridian 88's commercial anti-gravity transit infrastructure, miniaturized and weaponized in a form that remains deeply controversial among the scientific community. The emitter core contains a crystalline graviton lens array that focuses the field projection with high spatial precision — the 1.5-meter effect radius means trained operators can affect a single target in a crowd without impacting bystanders, though field edge effects at the periphery of the compression zone cause significant discomfort and disorientation in adjacent individuals. The weapon's power requirements are enormous by handheld standards, necessitating a dedicated backpack power unit connected by a reinforced umbilical.

The GCE-3 is one of the most legally contentious weapons in Meridian 88. Its use at a labor suppression event in the Palladian Construction sector in 2197 — where seventeen workers were killed and the incident was initially classified as a 'structural collapse' — remains an open wound in the city's political landscape. Ouroboros Energy has faced ongoing regulatory pressure over its foundational research, and the weapon's existence is technically classified at the municipal government level, though this classification is widely understood to be a legal fiction.
Properties.aliases: Flatline, The Press, Gravity Gun, GCE
Properties.manufacturer: OUROBOROS ENERGY (research); ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS (military adaptation)
Properties.specifications:
emitter length: 88cm
emitter weight: 6.1kg
power unit weight: 14.3kg (backpack)
umbilical length: 1.2m
power source: Ouroboros OE-Heavy cell pack, 9 full-power discharges
effect radius at range: 1.5m diameter at 40m
effective range: 12–65m (optimal 20–45m)
compression range: 8G (incapacitation) to 22G (lethal)
