Properties.tactical_use: GCE-3 deployment is handled by two-person teams: one operator carrying the emitter, one managing the power unit and maintaining umbilical clearance during movement. In military applications, it is used for rapid elimination of high-value hardened targets — individuals in powered armor or with heavy augmentation who are resistant to conventional weapons but whose augments provide no protection against gravitational compression. The weapon's 3.8-second recharge cycle makes it unsuitable for sustained engagements; operators typically fire once per target and reposition. The psychological effect on witnesses is severe and has been deliberately exploited in pacification operations — watching a target collapse under invisible force with no audible discharge is profoundly disorienting.
Properties.cultural_context: The GCE-3 is a ghost weapon in Meridian 88's cultural consciousness — officially it does not exist, but its effects are known and documented by street communities, labor organizers, and underground journalists who have been tracking its use since 2197. The Palladian Construction massacre has become a reference point for discussions of corporate violence, and the GCE-3 is the weapon that killed those workers, even if no official record admits it. Among military and elite corporate circles, it is spoken of with the particular reverence reserved for weapons that represent genuine technological dominance. Among everyone else, it is a symbol of how far the powerful are willing to go when they believe there will be no consequences.
Properties.story_hooks: The players stumble onto evidence linking the Palladian Construction massacre to a specific GCE-3 serial number — and that unit is currently in the hands of someone who has no idea what they possess or what it connects them to.; Ouroboros Energy's graviton research division has developed a GCE-4 prototype with a 6-meter effect radius and extended range. Someone inside the company wants it destroyed before it can be weaponized. Someone outside the company wants to acquire it for exactly that purpose.; A municipal investigator has been quietly building a case against Arcturus Defense Solutions for the 2197 massacre. She needs a technical expert who can identify GCE-3 wound patterns in autopsy records — and the players are the only people she can trust who have the relevant knowledge and aren't already compromised.

Properties.description:
The HVP-4 fires a magnetically stabilized tungsten-ceramic projectile wrapped in a rotating electromagnetic sheath that induces a tight helical spin at velocities exceeding 4,200 meters per second. Unlike conventional rifling, the spin is not imparted by barrel grooves but by a series of phased electromagnetic coils along the accelerator rail that fire in precise sequence, allowing the rotation rate to be tuned dynamically via a thumb-wheel adjuster on the receiver. At maximum spin, the projectile generates a secondary vacuum vortex behind its path capable of destabilizing soft tissue and lightweight armor panels through torsional shear stress alone.

What distinguishes the Corkscrew from conventional railguns is its Torsional Cavity Induction system — a secondary coil near the muzzle imparts a brief counter-rotating field to the projectile's outer ceramic sleeve just before exit. This causes the sleeve to fracture in a controlled spiral pattern mid-flight, releasing the denser tungsten penetrator core with an enhanced rotational wobble that defeats layered composite armor by exploiting the angular gaps between laminate sheets. The result is a weapon that transitions from a clean penetrator at close range to a tumbling, spiraling wound-maker at extended distances.

The HVP-4 is a long, ungainly rifle with a pronounced coil housing that runs the length of the barrel, giving it a corrugated, industrial appearance. It runs hot — sustained fire without the integrated coolant sleeve risks coil burnout — but in the hands of a trained operator it is regarded as one of the most mechanically elegant anti-materiel solutions available outside of military procurement channels.
Properties.aliases: Corkscrew, The Drill, Helix Gun, Twister
Properties.legality: Restricted — Anti-materiel classification, requires ADS-issued operator license
Properties.specifications:
projectile: Tungsten-ceramic composite, 12.7mm helical-sleeve penetrator
muzzle velocity: 4,200 m/s at maximum coil output
effective range: 950m penetrator mode / 400m tumble-induction mode
coil stages: 14
power source: Dual ADS-Cell Type-7 capacitor banks
weight: 6.8 kg unloaded
magazine: 12-round ceramic-sleeve cassette
heat threshold: 8 rounds rapid-fire before mandatory coolant purge
spin rate range: 12,000–220,000 RPM (adjustable)
integrated systems: Coolant sleeve, coil-health indicator, spin-rate digital display
Properties.tactical_use: Operators typically deploy the HVP-4 in overwatch roles, using penetrator mode against hardened targets — vehicle plating, reinforced doors, light drones — and switching to tumble mode when engaging personnel in soft armor at mid-range. The spin-rate adjuster allows experienced shooters to dial specific armor-defeat profiles on the fly. Corporate security details have documented its use in hostage-denial scenarios where conventional ammunition would risk over-penetration through walls. The weapon's weight and heat limitations mean it is rarely carried as a primary arm; it is most commonly found slung across the back of a dedicated heavy-support operator who transitions to a sidearm for close-quarters work.
Properties.cultural_context: The Corkscrew has developed a reputation as a craftsman's weapon — complex, demanding, and deeply satisfying to those who master it. In Meridian 88's licensed arms culture, owning an HVP-4 signals technical literacy and financial investment rather than simple aggression. Workshop-district gunsmiths treat it with near-reverence, and the subculture of Corkscrew tuners — operators who swap coil configurations and ceramic sleeve compounds to optimize specific defeat profiles — has produced a secondary market for custom components that rivals the primary weapon in value. It is also associated with Arcturus's mercenary contractor network, and spotting the corrugated barrel on a stranger is widely understood as a signal that the individual is a professional rather than a street-level threat.
Properties.story_hooks: A Corkscrew configured with a non-standard ceramic sleeve compound is recovered at a crime scene — the compound traces back to a LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS research lab with no documented weapons program.; An Arcturus operator license is found to have been issued posthumously, meaning someone is legally carrying an HVP-4 under a dead person's credentials.; A workshop-district tuner claims to have achieved a coil configuration that allows the HVP-4 to defeat the new-generation IRONCLAD AGRISYSTEMS harvester-armor plating — and multiple factions want the formula before it reaches open market.; The spin-rate display on a recovered HVP-4 has been modified to encode encrypted messages visible only at a specific RPM readout — someone is using the weapon as a dead-drop communication device.

Properties.description:
The HVIC-3 operates by projecting a tuned aerosol of catalytic nanoparticles into the breathing zone of a target, where they are subsequently activated by a focused near-infrared trigger pulse from the carbine's secondary emitter. Once inhaled or absorbed transdermally, the particles bind to hemoglobin iron sites and initiate a controlled oxidative cascade, forcing red blood cells into a premature lysis cycle. The effect begins within ninety seconds of exposure and manifests as rapidly progressing hypoxia, subcutaneous hemorrhaging, and systemic pressure collapse. Range is limited to approximately eighteen meters in open air, though enclosed spaces dramatically amplify dispersal efficiency.

What separates the HVIC-3 from cruder aerosol weapons is its selectivity system. Operators can pre-load a biometric exclusion profile — a genetic or proteomic signature — allowing the carbine to suppress activation in targeted individuals while the cloud remains lethal to everyone else in the zone. Zheng-Dao Bioelectric markets this as a 'precision population management tool,' which has done little to soften the weapon's reputation. The carbine itself resembles an oversized pump-action shotgun with a bulbous canister housing beneath the barrel, and emits a faint copper smell during discharge that veteran operators have learned to treat as a serious warning sign.

The nickname 'Redmist' comes not from the aerosol itself, which is invisible, but from the subcutaneous hemorrhaging that gives affected skin a mottled crimson flush in the final stages of exposure. 'The Blush' is used more sardonically, typically by the corporate security contractors who deploy it for crowd suppression in sealed transit hubs and processing centers.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 18m open air / 40m enclosed
canister capacity: 6 discharge cycles per canister
activation delay: 90 seconds post-exposure
exclusion profiles: Up to 4 simultaneous biometric exemptions
weight: 4.2 kg loaded
dimensions: 74cm length
power source: Integrated DAT cell, 30 trigger pulses per charge
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed almost exclusively in enclosed or semi-enclosed environments where aerosol dispersal is predictable. Operators typically seed a space, withdraw, and trigger activation remotely after establishing a perimeter. The exclusion profile system makes it viable for extractions where a target must survive while everyone else in the room does not. Counter-use involves positive-pressure respirators and full dermal sealing, though the near-infrared trigger can sometimes be blocked by certain optical coatings.
Properties.cultural_context: The HVIC-3 exists in a strange public silence — it is widely known among intelligence communities and black-site operators but almost never discussed openly, partly because Zheng-Dao Bioelectric aggressively suppresses documentation of its use. Among corporate fixers, possession of one is considered a statement of institutional backing rather than personal capability. Street operators who come across one typically sell it immediately; the legal exposure is catastrophic and the weapon's use leaves forensic evidence that is difficult to misattribute.
Properties.story_hooks: A transit hub massacre leaves 40 dead with no visible wounds and no weapon recovered — only a faint copper smell in the ventilation system and one survivor with an inexplicable genetic exemption.; A stolen exclusion profile cartridge is being auctioned on the black market, pre-loaded with a biometric signature that nobody can identify but everyone wants.; Zheng-Dao Bioelectric is recalling all HVIC-3 units through a shell contractor — but the recall notices are only going to operators who used the weapon in a specific six-month window, and those operators are going missing.; An operator is hired to protect a VIP, only to discover mid-mission that the client's biometric profile is not in the exclusion cartridge they were issued.

Properties.description:
The Hepatic Glycogen Depletion Projector uses a focused beam of modulated microwave and near-infrared radiation tuned to the absorption and catalytic disruption frequencies of glycogen phosphorylase — the enzyme responsible for mobilizing stored glucose from the liver. By overwhelming hepatic glycogen phosphorylase activity through thermal and photonic excitation, the weapon forces the complete and near-instantaneous liberation of all hepatic glycogen stores into the bloodstream, followed by rapid enzymatic exhaustion that prevents resynthesis. The result is a catastrophic glucose spike lasting approximately ninety seconds, followed by profound hypoglycemia as reserves are depleted and resynthesis is blocked. The target collapses into a hypoglycemic crisis within four to seven minutes.

The HGDP-2 is a weapon of delayed effect, which gives it a distinct tactical character. An operator can tag a target and withdraw entirely before the effect manifests. The initial exposure causes no pain, no visible wound, and no immediate behavioral change — the target simply walks away feeling briefly warm. Minutes later, sweating, confusion, and motor failure set in, followed by loss of consciousness. Without immediate glucose intervention, the hypoglycemic crisis can progress to seizure and death within fifteen to twenty minutes. With intervention, the target survives but requires hours of medical support.

The projector's form factor resembles a standard industrial thermal scanner, providing effective cover in maintenance and technical environments. Ringo Corponation licenses the underlying photonic enzyme excitation technology for legitimate food processing applications, a fact that has been exploited extensively to launder the weapon's supply chain. The HGDP-2 is particularly dangerous to targets with diabetic or metabolic augmentations that suppress normal glucose regulatory responses, as these individuals have reduced capacity to self-correct even partial depletion.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 1–12 meters
exposure duration required: 6–10 seconds for full depletion
onset of hypoglycemic crisis: 4–7 minutes post-exposure
crisis duration without intervention: 15–20 minutes to severe neurological event
beam profile: 15cm diameter focused spot at 8 meters
power source: Compact microwave driver cell, 18 exposures per charge
weight: 1.4 kg
form factor: Handheld scanner form factor, 28cm length
countermeasure: Subcutaneous glucose reservoir implants, metabolic augmentation with active glucose synthesis
Properties.tactical_use: Preferred for social engineering operations and infiltration scenarios where the operator must not be identified as having committed a hostile act. An operative can expose a target in a crowded room, at a reception, or in a corridor and be three blocks away when the target collapses. Emergency responders treat the event as a diabetic episode or sudden metabolic crisis, delaying any forensic investigation. The weapon is also used to incapacitate building security or personal protection details without triggering alarm protocols — a guard who collapses from hypoglycemia does not trigger a gunshot sensor.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88's corporate espionage scene, the HGDP-2 has earned a reputation as the 'socialite's weapon' — it requires proximity but no confrontation, fits in a jacket pocket, and produces a medical event rather than a crime scene. It is associated with a certain class of operator: elegant, patient, comfortable in formal environments. There is a dark irony in its Ringo Corponation origins — a company whose food processing divisions feed millions of Meridian 88's lower-tier citizens is also providing the technology used to silently incapacitate them. Underground medics in the Outer Ring have begun carrying emergency glucose injectors as standard kit specifically because of the weapon's increasing prevalence.
Properties.story_hooks: Three executives from competing corporations collapsed at the same industry gala within forty minutes of each other — officially attributed to a catering contamination incident, but a fixer hired by one family believes a single operator with an HGDP-2 worked the room.; An Outer Ring underground medic has started keeping a tally of 'diabetic crisis' calls that don't match patient histories — she's identified a geographic pattern and wants to hire someone to investigate before more people die.; A Ringo Corponation quality control manager discovers that a batch of 'industrial thermal calibrators' shipped to a distributor matches the HGDP-2 spec sheet exactly — and the distributor doesn't exist.; A fixer is exposed to a sub-threshold HGDP-2 burst as a warning — not enough to incapacitate, just enough to make them sick for a day and leave a forensic trace that says 'we can finish this whenever we want.'

Properties.description:
The Hepatic Vapor Pressure Burst Charge is a contact explosive designed for placement on surfaces where targets are expected to rest, lean, or brace — vehicle seats, chair backs, wall panels, floor tiles. Its detonation sequence uses a ferroelectric compression initiator to generate a precisely shaped pressure wave tuned to maximize coupling with hepatic parenchymal tissue. The charge delivers its energy selectively to the liver's vascular architecture, triggering rapid vapor pressure buildup within sinusoidal spaces and causing catastrophic hepatic rupture with minimal blast damage to surrounding tissue or material.

The engineering basis for the HVPBC-2 emerged from IRONCLAD AGRISYSTEMS' agricultural research into livestock processing optimization — specifically, non-destructive pressure techniques for organ evaluation. The weaponized application was developed under a separate classified contract, though the technical lineage is visible to anyone who examines the ferroelectric compression profile. The charge is approximately the size of a playing card and 4mm thick, making it concealable within standard furnishings with no detectable profile under most security sweeps.

Targets struck by the HVPBC-2 experience an immediate sensation described by survivors as 'a punch from inside' followed by progressive right upper quadrant pain and rapid hemodynamic collapse. Because the external blast signature is minimal — a sharp crack audible only within a few meters — the HVPBC-2 is the weapon of choice for assassinations where the cause of death must appear medical. Coroners unfamiliar with the charge's signature frequently log cause of death as spontaneous hepatic hemorrhage.
Properties.aliases: HVPBC-2, Liver Shot, The Silent Rupture, Yellow Charge
Properties.specifications:
form factor: Flat adhesive charge, 85mm x 54mm x 4mm (playing card profile)
weight: 38g
trigger modes: Pressure contact, remote signal, timer (1s–72h)
effective range: Direct contact to 120mm through intervening material
blast signature: Minimal — audible crack at under 3m, no structural damage
primary effect: Hepatic parenchymal rupture, sinusoidal vapor pressure cascade
time to incapacitation: 8–45 seconds depending on proximity
forensic signature: Mimics spontaneous hepatic hemorrhage in standard autopsy without specialized testing
Properties.tactical_use: Assassination contractors plant HVPBC-2 units in target environments hours or days before the operation, using the timer or pressure-contact trigger to ensure distance at time of detonation. They are embedded in vehicle seats, office chairs, mattresses, and floor panels along known movement routes. Corporate intelligence operatives use them for eliminating targets whose deaths must appear natural. The weapon's low forensic signature makes it particularly valuable in operations where investigation is anticipated.
Properties.cultural_context: The HVPBC-2 has created a specific paranoia culture among Meridian 88's corporate executive class — the 'chair sweep' has become a standard security ritual, and a small industry of HVPBC-2 detection consultants has emerged to service wealthy clients. The irony that the weapon originated in agricultural research is not lost on activists who use it as a case study in dual-use technology corruption. IRONCLAD AGRISYSTEMS has never been prosecuted, and their agricultural division continues to operate the underlying ferroelectric research openly.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of 'natural' executive deaths across competing corporations all share the hepatic rupture signature — someone is running a systematic elimination campaign.; A player character's chair is swept and a live HVPBC-2 is found — it was planted recently, meaning someone has access to their secure space.; An IRONCLAD AGRISYSTEMS researcher wants to defect and bring documentation linking the company's agricultural research directly to HVPBC-2 development.; A batch of HVPBC-2s with defective pressure triggers is circulating — they detonate on placement rather than on contact, killing the operators planting them.

Properties.description: The HDC-2 is a two-stage chemical-explosive device designed for data infrastructure denial. The outer shell contains a conventional shaped charge that ruptures a pressurized inner reservoir filled with a superheated hydrolytic solution — a proprietary TESSERA CORPONATION compound that aggressively attacks organic polymers, fiber-optic cladding, and unshielded circuit substrates on contact. The blast itself is modest; the real damage is the dispersed chemical payload that coats surfaces in a 5-meter radius with a compound that continues reacting for up to 40 minutes after detonation.
Properties.specifications:
weight: 1.2 kg
dimensions: 14 cm x 8 cm cylindrical
blast radius: 5 m primary, 9 m chemical drift
chemical active duration: 35–45 minutes post-detonation
trigger modes: Remote detonation, Timer, Tamper-triggered
neutralization agent: TESSERA proprietary NeutraFlush compound (sold separately)
casing material: Corrosion-resistant ceramic-alloy shell
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed in corporate sabotage operations targeting server farms, communication hubs, and fabrication lines. Teams plant HDC-2 units inside conduit junctions or cable management systems where the chemical dispersal maximizes contact with sensitive infrastructure. Anti-personnel use is considered secondary — the hydrolytic compound causes severe chemical burns, but the weapon is rarely chosen for its human lethality. It is exceptionally effective at making a location digitally dead for hours.
Properties.cultural_context: The HDC-2 is the calling card of data-warfare crews and anti-corporate saboteurs in Meridian 88. Finding one at a crime scene tells investigators less about who planted it and more about what the target was — if someone used a Saltflat, they wanted the data gone more than they wanted people dead. TESSERA markets a civilian variant for 'industrial equipment decommissioning,' which fools no one.
Properties.story_hooks: A runner is hired to plant an HDC-2 in a competitor's server room, only to find the room already destroyed by an identical charge — someone got there first, and the data the runner was supposed to destroy is already gone.; A TESSERA 'decommissioning' team is found dead in an industrial district, their own HDC-2 units detonated around them. The chemical burns suggest the charges were triggered remotely — from inside TESSERA's own network.; The NeutraFlush neutralization compound has been pulled from the market without explanation, and three active HDC-2 sites in the city are now impossible to safely contain.

Properties.description:
The Hydrostatic Nerve Cradle operates by projecting a precisely tuned hydrostatic field envelope around a target's body — a near-invisible shell of pressurized aqueous microparticles suspended in a charged ionic matrix. Once the envelope seals, internal pressure differentials are manipulated in real time, selectively compressing nerve clusters and vascular pathways without breaking skin. The effect is described by survivors as being 'held very tightly by something that knows exactly where to squeeze.' Victims remain conscious, mobile in theory, but functionally paralyzed as the cradle prioritizes motor pathway suppression over pain centers.

What distinguishes the HNC-3 from cruder pressure weapons is its neural feedback architecture, which reads bioelectric fluctuations through the ionic envelope and dynamically adjusts the pressure map. The weapon does not simply crush — it listens, and corrects. Targets who struggle or spike cortisol experience a tightening feedback loop. Calm targets are held in stasis. HELIX BIOSYSTEMS designed it nominally as a non-lethal restraint platform for high-value capture operations, though field reports consistently note that operators who hold the lock for more than forty seconds begin causing irreversible vascular damage.

The HNC-3 is shoulder-mounted with a wrist-linked targeting interface, requiring the operator to maintain line-of-sight within eighteen meters. It has a distinctive low hum during active lock — operators call it 'the lullaby's older sibling,' a reference to the SDE-4 that HELIX publicly denies. The weapon's cultural notoriety stems from its association with corporate extraction teams: it is the preferred tool of those who need someone alive but not resistant.
Properties.aliases: The Cradle, Swaddling, Softlock, Nurse's Arms
Properties.legality: Restricted — Licensed to certified extraction contractors and licensed medical security firms only
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 4–18 meters
lock duration: Continuous while powered; safe threshold 40 seconds
power source: Dual HELIX BioCell 9V cartridges
weight: 3.8 kg (mount) + 0.6 kg (wrist interface)
envelope diameter: Adjustable 0.4–2.1 meters
target capacity: Single-target lock; experimental multi-lock firmware exists on black market
cooldown: 90 seconds between deployments
Properties.tactical_use: Primarily used for live capture operations where target must arrive undamaged. Extraction teams deploy HNC-3 as a closer — entry breached by conventional means, HNC-3 operator hangs back and locks the primary target while teammates neutralize escorts. Interrogation units use it as a coercion tool without leaving forensic marks. Some corporate security details use it for 'polite' detentions of executives suspected of defection.
Properties.cultural_context: The Cradle has become a symbol of corporate overreach in Meridian 88's activist communities — the idea that a corporation has built a weapon specifically designed to hold you alive and helpless for its own purposes. Street art depicting a swaddled figure suspended in a corporate logo is common in contested districts. Ironically, high-end private security for the ultra-wealthy also uses it, rebranded as 'non-lethal executive protection.' Its dual identity — oppressor's tool and luxury service — makes it a flashpoint in class-politics discourse.
Properties.story_hooks: A target who was held in a Cradle for over three minutes reports that they can still 'feel' the pressure at night — HELIX's neural feedback may have left a persistent imprint on their nervous system, and they want answers.; A stolen HNC-3 with a cracked firmware lock is circulating in the underground — the multi-target experimental build. Someone is testing it on crowds.; An extraction contractor refuses a job mid-operation and abandons the Cradle with the target still locked inside. The operator has 40 seconds to find the release key before permanent damage sets in.; HELIX BIOSYSTEMS is quietly recalling HNC-3 units, citing 'calibration variance.' Operators who've used them extensively are being offered suspiciously generous buyback rates.

Properties.description:
The HPL-1 generates a coherent column of hydrodynamic pressure using a resonant fluid compression chamber fed by an onboard micro-reservoir of dense hydraulic fluid. The weapon does not project fluid outward — instead, it generates a standing wave of hydrostatic pressure in the air column between the emitter and the target, exploiting the body's own fluid content as the transmission medium. When the wave reaches a water-dense target (biological tissue, hydraulic systems, fluid-cooled electronics), it couples with the target's internal fluid and induces explosive hydrostatic overpressure within enclosed spaces: sinuses, joint capsules, the chambers of the heart, fluid-cooled cybernetic housings.

Palladian Construction originally developed the HPL-1's core technology for non-explosive demolition of water-saturated geological formations — the same hydrostatic coupling effect that destroys joint capsules works equally well on saturated rock strata and underwater structural elements. The weaponized variant was engineered by a Palladian subsidiary that was subsequently dissolved, with the technology licensed to a series of shell companies before eventually reaching street manufacture. The weapon's industrial origins are visible in its form factor: it looks like a construction tool, heavy and utilitarian, with none of the ergonomic refinement of purpose-built weapons.

Against unaugmented biological targets, the HPL-1 produces a spectrum of effects depending on range and power: at distance, joint pain and disorientation from sinus overpressure; at medium range, ruptured eardrums and hemorrhaging from sinus cavities; at close range, cardiac arrhythmia from heart chamber pressure spikes and potential joint dislocation as capsular fluid flashes to expanded state. Against fluid-cooled cybernetic systems, the weapon is catastrophically effective — it can detonate cooling jackets and pressure housings without any visible external impact.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: Contact to 25 meters
fluid reservoir: 400ml dense hydraulic fluid (onboard, replaceable canister)
power source: Palladian P-Cell Industrial Grade (8 full-power discharges)
weight: 6.8 kg
length: 89 cm
form factor: Industrial demolition tool housing (Palladian PD-Series chassis)
anti-cybernetic efficacy: Highly effective against fluid-cooled systems and hydraulic augmentations
power settings: Low / Medium / High / Overdrive (Overdrive voids all implied warranties)
cooling requirement: 30-second passive cool between High/Overdrive shots
Properties.tactical_use: The HPL-1 is favored in environments where heavily augmented opponents are expected, particularly those with fluid-cooled combat chassis or hydraulic limb augmentations. Operators engaging corporate security with high-end cybernetics use it specifically to detonate cooling systems and disable augmented limbs without requiring the target to be physically struck. At lower power settings it is used as a crowd-control tool in flooded or high-humidity environments where the coupling effect is amplified. The weapon's industrial appearance has been exploited for concealed carry in construction and infrastructure contexts.
Properties.cultural_context: The HPL-1 is associated with the industrial underground — construction workers who've crossed the wrong contractors, infrastructure saboteurs, and the specific flavor of anti-corporate violence that emerges from physically demanding labor sectors. Palladian's corporate logo is still faintly visible on most units despite attempts to grind it off, and this has become a symbol of a certain political identity: the idea that the tools of construction can be turned against the people who own them. Heavily augmented fixers specifically fear the HPL-1 in a way they don't fear most weapons.
Properties.story_hooks: A rash of high-end augmentation failures across the city all share the same internal damage pattern — someone is hunting specific cyberware models with a HPL-1 and a grudge.; Palladian Construction quietly wants to know which subsidiary licensed the HPL-1 technology and to whom — the paper trail was deliberately destroyed.; A character with fluid-cooled augmentations starts receiving anonymous threats referencing 'Deepwater' — someone knows exactly what their implants are vulnerable to.; A construction crew has been using HPL-1s to demolish a building that city records show was never approved for demolition — someone wants whatever is inside gone very quickly.

Properties.description:
The Inductive Thermal Lance is a heavy close-combat weapon produced by Palladian Construction, originally developed as a field tool for emergency structural cutting in collapsed building scenarios. The ITL-5 consists of a 90-centimeter reinforced handle assembly connected to a 40-centimeter ferrous core lance tip surrounded by a tight helical induction coil. When powered, the coil generates a rapidly alternating magnetic field that induces eddy currents directly within the ferrous tip, heating it to operational temperature — approximately 900 degrees Celsius — within four seconds, without any external flame or combustion. The tip glows a deep amber-orange at operating temperature and maintains heat continuously while powered.

The transition from construction tool to weapon was, by most accounts, inevitable given the ITL-5's field profile. Palladian Construction workers in contested infrastructure zones began carrying them as combination tools and deterrents, and the design's robustness — built to function in debris fields, flooded basements, and chemically contaminated environments — made it a natural fit for the kinds of chaotic close-quarters scenarios common in Meridian 88's lower districts. Palladian has never officially marketed the ITL-5 as a weapon, but their industrial sales division has been notably uninterested in investigating end-user applications, and modified versions with sharpened tips and shortened handles have been documented in the hands of non-construction personnel for years.

The ITL-5's combat profile is defined by its ability to defeat armor through thermal transfer rather than kinetic force. Against standard ballistic plate, the lance tip burns through the outer layer within seconds of sustained contact, defeating the material's protective properties before mechanical penetration is attempted. Against biological targets, the cauterizing effect of the weapon simultaneously wounds and seals — a grim feature that operators in extended engagements have described as 'efficient,' as it reduces the user's risk of exposure to target blood.
Properties.specifications:
total length: 130 cm (handle + lance)
lance tip material: High-carbon ferrous alloy, hardened
operating temperature: 900°C sustained at full power
heat up time: 4 seconds to operational temperature
power source: Backpack-mounted high-capacity cell, 40-minute continuous operation; handle-integrated cell available (12-minute operation)
weight: 3.8 kg with handle cell
cooling time: 90 seconds from power-off to safe handling
induction coil material: Wound copper-beryllium alloy, shielded
Properties.tactical_use: In construction and emergency response contexts, the ITL-5 is used for cutting through rebar, locked structural panels, and collapsed framework. In combat, operators use sustained contact pressure to defeat armor before pushing through, a technique that requires the user to maintain engagement range — risky, but devastatingly effective against opponents who rely on hardened protection. The lance's length provides standoff advantage against knife-range weapons, and its weight makes it effective as a bludgeoning implement even when unpowered. Experienced operators carry it unpowered until engagement is confirmed, activating it mid-approach to deny opponents preparation time. The 90-second cooling delay after shutdown is a known vulnerability — an operator who powers down cannot safely stow or conceal the weapon quickly.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88's construction worker communities, carrying an ITL-5 is a normalized part of working in contested infrastructure zones where labor disputes can turn violent and rival crews compete over demolition contracts. The weapon has consequently become associated with organized labor's harder edges — union enforcers and territorial crew bosses are frequently depicted carrying them in the city's underground press. In the upper districts, the ITL-5 is viewed as a working-class weapon, too crude and industrial for corporate security tastes, which has paradoxically made it a symbol of working-district identity. Modified 'dueling' versions with decorative coil wrapping and sharpened tips are carried by gang leadership in the Palladian Construction service districts as an explicit territorial symbol.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of structural fires in a contested district have been started using ITL-5 units — the burns are too precise for accident, and the pattern suggests someone is systematically destroying buildings to clear land for a construction bid. Palladian Construction is a likely beneficiary.; A modified ITL-5 with an induction coil rated far above the standard ceiling has been used in an attack — it reached temperatures that melted through reinforced vault-grade material. Someone has cracked Palladian's design and is manufacturing a version the original engineers say shouldn't be possible.; A players' contact in the construction labor movement has been arrested on weapon charges — an ITL-5 found at a crime scene has been traced to their registered license. They claim it was stolen three weeks ago. Finding the actual user means navigating both corporate security and labor union politics.

Properties.description:
The ISP-2 generates a narrow planar sheet of ionized plasma approximately 1.4 meters long and 2 centimeters wide, sustained at close range by a pair of electromagnetic field guides mounted at the weapon's emitter fork. The plasma sheet is not a beam in the conventional sense — it does not project across distance. Instead, it functions as an extended melee cutting surface, maintained at temperatures exceeding 8,000 Kelvin along its active edge. The weapon is, in practical terms, an energy blade: wielded in close quarters, it cuts through most materials that conventional blades cannot, including hardened ceramic plating and lower-grade ballistic weaves.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric developed the ISP-2 as a response to the increasing prevalence of subdermal armor implants in high-value targets — human tissue reinforced with ceramic mesh or carbon-fiber laminate that defeats conventional blades entirely. The plasma edge interacts with these materials through a combination of thermal ablation and ionic disruption, effectively 'unzipping' the molecular bonds of the implant matrix rather than cutting through it mechanically. Against unaugmented targets, wounds are cauterized on contact, producing less blood evidence and complicating forensic analysis.

The ISP-2 is notoriously difficult to use effectively. The plasma sheet requires the operator to maintain field guide alignment within tight tolerances — any impact to the emitter fork risks field collapse, which releases a brief but violent ionic discharge that can injure the user. Training programs for the weapon are extensive and proprietary to Zheng-Dao's licensed operator network. On the street, self-taught users are identifiable by the characteristic burn scarring on their dominant forearm.
Properties.aliases: Splitvolt, The Divider, Arc Blade, ISP
Properties.specifications:
length: 61cm (handle and emitter fork)
weight: 1.8kg
plasma edge length: 1.4m
plasma edge temperature: ~8,200 Kelvin sustained
power source: ZD Compact Ionic Cell, 14 minutes continuous activation
field collapse risk: High under lateral impact to emitter fork
effective use range: Melee only (0–2m)
cutting capacity: Ceramic plate up to 18mm, carbon-fiber laminate, most biological implant matrices
Properties.tactical_use: The ISP-2 is a close-quarters assassination tool. Operators trained in its use approach targets under cover, activate the blade at the last moment to minimize detection window, and execute precise anatomical cuts — typically targeting the neck, femoral region, or spine where subdermal armor coverage is thinnest. Against heavily augmented targets, the ionic disruption effect means the blade can be used to disable cybernetic limbs by cutting through the interface points between implant and organic tissue. The weapon is largely useless in open combat, as it requires proximity and a trained user to avoid self-injury. Its primary tactical advantage is the cauterizing wound profile, which significantly delays victim response and reduces scene evidence.
Properties.cultural_context: The Splitvolt is deeply embedded in Meridian 88's assassination culture. Zheng-Dao Bioelectric officially denies the weapon exists in its current form, attributing ISP units in circulation to 'prototype leakage' from a discontinued project. Among the city's elite fixers and wetwork contractors, carrying a Splitvolt signals a specific professional identity — someone who works close, works clean, and has the training to back it up. There is a small but visible subculture of underground duelists who use ISP-2s in sanctioned matches, which has given the weapon an unexpected secondary reputation as a status symbol in certain nightlife circles.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of deaths in the corporate tier show the distinctive cauterized wound pattern of an ISP-2. The victims have no obvious connection — except they all had the same subdermal implant manufacturer, and the cuts are always through the implant interface point specifically.; A Zheng-Dao executive wants to recover a prototype ISP-2 variant before it can be reverse-engineered. The problem is it's currently in the hands of an underground duelist who won it in a match and has no idea what they have.; A player character's contact shows up dead with an ISP-2 wound. The weapon was used by someone who clearly had professional training — which narrows the suspect list considerably.

Properties.description:
The Ionic Thermoclastic Rifle functions by projecting a sustained stream of superheated ionized gas — technically a directed plasma jet — at ranges far exceeding conventional flamethrower technology. The key innovation is the magnetic confinement collar at the barrel's terminus, a toroidal field generator that compresses the plasma stream into a coherent column and prevents the lateral thermal bleed that makes conventional plasma projection impractical at range. The result is a weapon that delivers extreme thermal energy to a target at distances up to 60 meters with a column diameter of approximately 8 centimeters at point of impact.

Developed by TESSERA CORPONATION under a military infrastructure contract, the ITR-5 was originally intended for demolition work — specifically for cutting through reinforced structural elements in contested urban environments. Its adoption as a direct combat weapon was, by TESSERA's own internal communications, 'an unanticipated market development.' The weapon's effect on unarmored biological targets is severe and rapid: the plasma column causes flash vaporization of surface tissue and ignition of underlying structures within 2 seconds of sustained contact. Armored targets experience accelerated surface ablation and heat transfer sufficient to cause incapacitation through cookoff of interior equipment.

The Ashmaker has a complex cultural footprint. Its association with demolition work gives it a certain blue-collar credibility in the construction and infrastructure sectors, where modified civilian variants are not uncommon for cutting operations. Its use as a weapon is associated primarily with large-scale violence — building clearances, punitive actions by corporate security against squatter communities — and it carries a stigma that most individual operators find professionally undesirable. Carrying one signals either professional demolition work or a willingness to engage in atrocity.
Properties.aliases: Ashmaker, The Kiln, Cinder Stick, ITR
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 60m (combat), 15m (industrial cutting)
plasma temperature: 4,200°C at emitter, 2,800°C at 60m
column diameter: 8 cm at 60m
fuel source: TESSERA T-Gas Canister TGC-4 (45-second continuous burn per canister)
weight: 6.8 kg (empty), 9.2 kg (full canister)
length: 91 cm
confinement collar: Toroidal magnetic field generator, 0.3-second spool-up
cooling: Forced-air radiative system, 40-second mandatory cooldown after 15-second sustained burn
Properties.tactical_use: Military operators use the ITR-5 for bunker denial, fortification clearing, and area denial in enclosed spaces where the thermal environment becomes a weapon in itself. Combat engineers use it for rapid structural cutting under fire. Against personnel, operators typically use short bursts rather than sustained streams to manage fuel consumption and cooldown cycles. The weapon's size and fuel requirements make it a two-person system in sustained operations — one operator, one reload carrier.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88's construction sector, the ITR-5's industrial variant is a common tool — TESSERA has successfully normalized it as a precision demolition instrument. Workers in the Palladian Construction sphere carry them as standard equipment. The combat variant exists in a different moral register entirely. Its use in the Colvert District clearance operations four years ago — where TESSERA corporate security used ITR-5s to evict and 'sanitize' squatter warrens — left a deep scar in collective memory. The weapon's nickname 'Ashmaker' originated from survivors of that event.
Properties.story_hooks: A TESSERA internal memo has surfaced describing the Colvert clearance operation as a 'field demonstration' of the ITR-5's combat capabilities. Someone leaked it. TESSERA wants it back. The leaker wants it published.; A series of infrastructure sabotage events shows the distinctive cutting pattern of an ITR-5. The targets are all TESSERA-affiliated construction sites. Someone is using their own tool against them.; An industrial variant ITR-5 has been modified for combat and used in three separate murders in the upper districts. The modification is sophisticated — not a field hack. Someone with engineering access is building weapons.; A community in the lower districts has acquired two ITR-5s as a deterrent against corporate clearance operations. They've announced their possession publicly. TESSERA is deciding how to respond.

Nodes.Name: Survivors of the Colvert clearance (as symbol, not users)

Properties.description: The KSP-3 is a single-use, emplaced area-denial weapon produced by Arcturus Defense Solutions, combining magnetic linear acceleration technology with a conventional fragmentation charge in a configuration that produces a directional, high-velocity fragment swarm rather than an omnidirectional explosion. The device is planted and oriented — typically flush against a wall, embedded in a road surface, or mounted to a structural column — and when triggered, a primary charge fractures a tungsten-carbide plate into approximately 340 irregular fragments while a linear magnetic coil array accelerates the swarm to 1,800 m/s across a 30-degree forward arc. The result is a wall of hyper-velocity fragments traveling faster than most personal armor is rated to stop, covering a kill corridor approximately 2 meters wide and 40 meters deep.
Properties.tier_availability: Tier 4+ / Military contract / Black market (high-value, rare)
Properties.legality: Prohibited for civilian use; military deployment requires area-denial authorization under Meridian Urban Combat Protocols
Properties.specifications:
weight: 1.4kg (emplaced unit)
dimensions: 180mm x 120mm x 40mm
fragment count: Approximately 340 irregular tungsten-carbide fragments
fragment velocity: 1,800 m/s at muzzle, 900 m/s at 40m
effective arc: 30-degree forward cone
kill corridor: 2m wide, 40m effective depth
trigger options: Remote wireless, Tripwire (optical or physical), Pressure plate, Timer
emplacement time: Approximately 45 seconds for trained operator
armor penetration: Defeats standard-issue Level IV ballistic plating at 20m
Properties.tactical_use: The KSP-3 is an ambush and area-denial weapon. Operators emplace multiple units along a predicted movement corridor — a hallway, a stairwell, a vehicle approach lane — and detonate them in sequence as targets enter the kill zone. A three-unit staggered deployment can cover 120 meters of corridor with overlapping fragment swarms, making advance through the area nearly impossible without armored vehicle support. Military units use them to hold defensive positions with minimal personnel; street operators use them to protect extraction routes or punish pursuing security forces. The 45-second emplacement time means they can be deployed during a running engagement.
Properties.cultural_context: The Railsplitter is one of the few weapons in Meridian 88 that security analysts treat as a direct indicator of military-grade operational planning. Civilians don't use KSP-3s for robberies. Their presence at a scene indicates either a military unit, a contractor with military sourcing, or someone who spent enough credits on the black market to suggest institutional backing. In the aftermath of the Kessler Corridor Incident of 2194 — where a corporate extraction team emplaced nine KSP-3s in a residential transit tunnel, killing 34 people — the weapons acquired a specific political weight. Anti-corporate activist groups use the Railsplitter as a symbol of corporate violence against civilian infrastructure.
Properties.story_hooks: A transit maintenance worker found a KSP-3 emplaced beneath a pedestrian bridge — it's been there for six months, still live, and whoever placed it never came back to collect it.; A corporate security contractor is selling decommissioned KSP-3s by claiming the magnetic coil array has been disabled — it hasn't, and the buyer is a neighborhood defense collective in a residential district.; An investigation into the Kessler Corridor Incident was closed without charges — a retired forensic analyst has documentation that the fragment signatures match a specific Arcturus production batch traceable to a named client, and she's looking for someone to take the case.

Nodes.Name: Insurgent cells with military supply connections

Properties.description:
The KRE-1 generates a toroidal field of kinoplasmic resonance — a phenomenon in which a sustained electromagnetic standing wave is shaped into a stable ring geometry by a superconducting coil array within the weapon's emitter head. This ring, roughly 90cm in diameter at standard calibration, propagates forward from the muzzle at approximately 180 meters per second and maintains its toroidal form for up to 22 meters before dissipating. Any matter intersecting the ring's plane during propagation is subjected to a violent shearing force as the standing wave collapses against it, transferring its entire energy load into the intersection point as a circular laceration.

The Halo's visual signature is unmistakable: the toroidal field is faintly luminescent in the violet-ultraviolet range, producing a glowing ring that hangs in the air for a fraction of a second before impact. This visibility is both a tactical liability and the source of the weapon's cultural identity — in Meridian 88's underground combat aesthetics, being killed by a Halo is considered a particularly dramatic exit. The ring's geometry means it can theoretically pass through cover — a Halo fired through a window opening will maintain coherence and deliver its energy to whatever occupies the ring's plane on the other side, provided the opening is larger than the ring diameter.

Tessera Corponation designed the KRE-1 for breach and clear operations, where the ability to deliver a cutting force through a doorway or window without exposing the operator to return fire has obvious value. The weapon is heavy and requires a two-second charge cycle between discharges, limiting its rate of fire significantly, but each shot's damage potential is severe — the circular shearing pattern severs limbs and penetrates vehicle windows with equal effectiveness.
Properties.specifications:
ring diameter: 90cm standard; 60–120cm adjustable
propagation velocity: 180 m/s
maximum range: 22m before dissipation
luminescence: Violet-UV, 380–420nm
charge cycle: 2.1 seconds between shots
power cell: Tessera TC-20 superconducting cell, 12 discharges
weight: 8.4kg
dimensions: 78cm length, 31cm width at emitter head
cover penetration: Passes through openings larger than ring diameter intact
Properties.tactical_use: KRE-1 operators work in two-person teams: one operator handles the heavy weapon while a partner manages target acquisition and cover. The standard tactic is indirect fire — the operator positions outside a structure and fires through openings, delivering the Halo to interior targets without breaching. The ring diameter can be reduced to 60cm for narrow apertures, though this increases the energy concentration and correspondingly the damage at impact. The 2.1-second charge cycle means the weapon is never used as a primary firearm; operators carry sidearms for immediate threats.
Properties.cultural_context: The KRE-1's prohibited status means it exists almost exclusively in military and paramilitary hands. Within military culture in Meridian 88, the Halo carries a reputation as an executioner's weapon — precise, deliberate, theatrical. Stories of Halos used in high-profile political assassinations are a staple of conspiracy culture, and the violet ring has become a symbol in underground media representing state violence and corporate enforcement. Anti-corporate graffiti frequently depicts the glowing ring. Among soldiers who have used the weapon in combat, there is a marked tendency toward either pride or deep discomfort — it does not produce indifferent reactions.
Properties.story_hooks: A KRE-1 is used to assassinate a mid-district labor organizer — a target with no obvious military significance. The choice of weapon feels like a message. Someone wanted the death to look like official enforcement even if it wasn't.; A Tessera Corponation logistics manifest surfaces on the black market listing 40 KRE-1 units shipped to a destination that doesn't exist in any official registry. A fixer wants to know where those weapons actually went.; An operator who used the KRE-1 extensively during a corporate conflict is experiencing recurring nightmares of violet rings. A street-level psychtech thinks the superconducting coil's magnetic field may have caused subtle neural damage — and that Tessera knows.

Nodes.Name: High-tier mercenary companies with military contracts

Properties.description: The Lacunar Infarct Induction Carbine delivers a precisely shaped ultrasonic pulse through a parabolic focusing array embedded in its barrel assembly. The pulse is calibrated to induce localized vasospasm in the small penetrating arteries supplying the deep white matter and subcortical structures of the brain — specifically the internal capsule, thalamus, and basal ganglia. The result is a targeted lacunar infarct: a small, contained stroke that produces predictable and selective neurological deficits depending on the pulse parameters loaded into the firing profile.
Properties.legality: Prohibited — classified as a neurological torture device under Meridian 88 Statute 44-C
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 25 meters
pulse duration: 0.8 seconds
firing profiles: Aphasia, Motor Drop, Blank, Archive
effect onset: 3–8 seconds post-pulse
effect duration: 15 minutes to 72 hours depending on profile and individual vasculature
weight: 3.1 kg
power source: Proprietary Helix DAT-cell, 12 shots per cell
detectability: Silent, no visible emission, no thermal signature
Properties.tactical_use: Intelligence and interrogation-adjacent operations. The 'Archive' profile is used before extracting a target to prevent them from forming memory of their capture route or holding location. 'Aphasia' is deployed during negotiations or testimony to discredit a target without visible injury. 'Blank' is used for soft abductions — the target experiences a gap in memory and cannot reliably report what happened. Operators are typically trained neuroscience technicians or intelligence assets, not standard combatants.
Properties.cultural_context: The LIIC-1 exists in Meridian 88's underworld as an almost mythological object — most people have heard of it but few have seen one. It is associated exclusively with corporate intelligence work, and the phrase 'they Lacunaed him' has entered street slang to describe someone who seems present but hollowed out, unable to account for lost time. Survivors of Archive profile exposure often struggle to be believed — their testimony is fragmented and inconsistent in ways that mimic intoxication or fabrication.
Properties.story_hooks: A key witness in a corporate fraud trial has arrived at the hearing with a six-hour memory gap covering the exact period they were supposed to have observed the incriminating transaction. No injury. No toxicology hit. Someone used a Lacuna on them, and the party needs to prove it.; One of the party members wakes up in a location they don't recognize with three hours missing. The only clue is a faint tinnitus in their left ear that a street medic says is consistent with focused ultrasonic exposure.; A Helix Biosystems researcher wants to defect and is willing to hand over the LIIC-1 calibration schematics. The problem is that Helix's intelligence division already knows she's talking to outside parties, and they have at least two Lacunas in the city.

Nodes.Name: High-end fixers specializing in information suppression

Properties.description: The LRC-3 'Mudmaker' is a heavy crew-served weapon that generates a sustained resonance field capable of inducing thixotropic liquefaction in granular and semi-solid substrates — effectively turning compacted soil, concrete aggregate, sand, gravel, and certain composite construction materials into a viscous slurry state for as long as the field is maintained. The weapon operates by broadcasting layered mechanical resonance waves from a parabolic emitter array, overwhelming the cohesive friction bonds between substrate particles and causing the material to behave as a liquid under applied stress. The effect is temporary — substrates re-solidify within sixty to ninety seconds of field termination — but the tactical implications of turning a floor, embankment, or fortified position into quicksand are considerable.
Properties.specifications:
weight: 28 kg (emitter array + crew frame), 18 kg (capacitor backpack)
crew: 2 (operator + power manager)
effective range: 35 m (liquefaction field projection)
field diameter: 4 m at maximum range (adjustable 1–4 m)
liquefaction depth: Up to 1.2 m substrate penetration
field maintenance duration: Continuous while powered; capacitor supports 40 seconds sustained operation
re-solidification time: 60–90 seconds post-field termination
compatible substrates: Compacted soil, sand, gravel, concrete aggregate, clay, certain composite materials
incompatible substrates: Solid rock, reinforced synthcrete panels, metal decking
power source: Dedicated resonance capacitor backpack (single-charge, field-rechargeable)
Properties.tactical_use: The 'Mudmaker' excels in siege and denial scenarios in earthwork or mixed-construction environments. Standard doctrine calls for liquefying approach corridors to immobilize advancing forces, collapsing tunnel sections to cut off retreat, or destabilizing the foundation substrate beneath fortified positions. The 'casting' effect — trapping targets in re-solidified material — is used deliberately in capture operations when targets need to be taken alive and immobile. Operators must account for the weapon's own weight and the risk of liquefying substrate beneath their own position; field accidents involving crew sinkage are common enough to have generated their own safety protocols.
Properties.cultural_context: The 'Mudmaker' has a cult following among Meridian 88's tunnel-runner and underground infrastructure communities, where it is seen as a symbol of the blurred line between construction and destruction that defines the city's lower districts. Palladian Construction's involvement in its creation is considered an open secret — the company's logo appears on early-production emitter arrays, poorly obscured by aftermarket paint. Workers in Meridian 88's extensive below-grade maintenance network tell stories about 'Mudmaker accidents' that are widely understood to be deliberate acts of labor sabotage against corporate infrastructure teams. The weapon is rarely seen above ground.
Properties.story_hooks: A section of Meridian 88's primary transit tunnel has collapsed — official reports cite structural failure, but the substrate shows signs of resonance liquefaction. Someone used a 'Mudmaker' on a load-bearing section, and the city wants answers before more tunnels go down.; A Palladian Construction executive is trying to quietly buy back all existing 'Mudmaker' units on the black market before a regulatory audit connects the weapon's design to the company. They're paying well — but they're also eliminating sellers after the transaction.; The players need to breach a fortified underground compound. A contact offers them access to a 'Mudmaker' — but the power capacitor is damaged, and the only person who can repair it is currently trapped inside the compound they need to breach.; A 'Mudmaker' has been modified to operate at a resonance frequency that affects reinforced synthcrete — something Palladian Construction claimed was impossible. Someone has solved the incompatibility problem, and the implications for Meridian 88's infrastructure are catastrophic.

Nodes.Name: Corporate sabotage specialists targeting competitor infrastructure
Ouroboros Energy subsurface security teams (pipeline protection)

Properties.description:
The LFOR-3 delivers a payload of magnetically responsive ferrofluid nanoparticles via a pressurized aerosol bolt that disperses on skin contact and penetrates subcutaneously through follicular and sweat gland channels. Once embedded in the subcutaneous tissue, an external magnetic pulse from the rifle's secondary emitter aligns and compacts the particles within lymphatic capillaries, causing immediate mechanical occlusion. The resulting blockage triggers rapid localized lymphedema — extreme fluid accumulation in the affected limb or region.

The swelling is not merely cosmetic. Within minutes, the pressure in occluded tissue exceeds compartment syndrome thresholds, causing excruciating pain, loss of motor function, and if untreated, tissue necrosis. The weapon can be tuned to affect a single limb or, with a wider dispersal bolt, to seed multiple lymphatic regions simultaneously. Unlike many exotic weapons in its class, the LFOR-3 is deliberately designed for survivability — the manufacturer positions it as a 'non-lethal incapacitation system' — though death from secondary infection or untreated compartment syndrome is common in populations without access to quality medical care.

Helix Biosystems developed the ferrostatic occlusion mechanism from research into targeted lymphatic drug delivery. The weaponized application was funded through a subsidiary with deliberately obscured corporate parentage. The rifle is now quietly distributed to private security firms as a 'humane deterrent,' with Helix maintaining that adverse outcomes are the result of inadequate post-exposure medical response rather than the weapon itself.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 5–35 meters
bolt type: Pressurized aerosol dispersal, contact-detonated
particle payload: 0.4 mL ferrofluid suspension per bolt
magnetic pulse range: Up to 20 meters post-dispersal
magazine capacity: 12 bolts
onset time: Swelling visible within 90 seconds, incapacitation within 4–7 minutes
weight: 2.6 kg loaded
reversal: Magnetic dispersal wand (sold separately, Helix Biosystems)
Properties.tactical_use: Corporate security teams deploy the LFOR-3 for crowd incapacitation at entry control points, targeting the legs to drop subjects without lethal force. In coercive interrogation contexts, operators target the hands and face to maximize distress. The magnetic dispersal wand — which reverses the occlusion — is used as a bargaining tool during detentions. Skilled operators can target specific limbs with the narrow-cone bolt to selectively incapacitate without affecting mobility entirely.
Properties.cultural_context: Stonewood has become notorious in Meridian 88's poorer districts, where private security firms use it liberally at corporate-owned transit hubs and housing estates. The term 'got stoned' refers to being shot by the LFOR-3, and the distinctive puffy, hard-skinned appearance of untreated lymphedema victims — those who couldn't afford or access the dispersal wand — is visible enough on the streets that it has become a marker of class victimhood. Helix Biosystems' ongoing PR positioning of the weapon as 'humane' is a source of bitter public satire.
Properties.story_hooks: A district health worker is documenting an epidemic of untreated lymphedema cases in a corporate housing estate �� she needs help getting the evidence out before Helix Biosystems' lawyers bury it.; A stolen shipment of dispersal wands is being held ransom by a gang who understand exactly what leverage they have over people who've been shot with Stonewood.; A player character is hit with the LFOR-3 during a routine job gone wrong and has hours to find a dispersal wand before permanent tissue damage sets in.; Helix Biosystems is quietly developing a version with a delayed magnetic trigger — meaning victims can be shot and not know it until they're far from the scene.

Nodes.Name: Mira Osei, a bounty hunter who prefers live captures

Properties.description:
The LRI-5 operates by firing a near-invisible pressurized micro-needle capable of penetrating standard dermal armor at ranges up to twelve meters. Upon subcutaneous delivery, the payload — a proprietary synthetic lymphotropic compound — binds to the target's lymphatic vessels and triggers a rapid cascading inflammatory response. The victim's own immune system becomes the instrument of incapacitation, producing systemic edema, joint failure, and acute respiratory distress within ninety seconds of exposure.

What distinguishes the Floodgate from conventional chemical delivery systems is its integration of piezoelectric disruption circuitry within the needle itself. As the micro-needle penetrates tissue, a brief localized vibration pulse fragments the tip into a mesh of sub-millimeter barbs, anchoring the delivery mechanism and ensuring full compound release even if the target attempts to remove it. This makes post-incident medical intervention significantly more complex and time-consuming.

The weapon's external profile is nearly indistinguishable from a high-end medical auto-injector — a deliberate design choice by Lazarus Pharmaceuticals, whose pharmaceutical division ostensibly produced the chassis for 'field triage applications.' Its plausible deniability as medical equipment has made it a favorite of corporate intelligence operatives and high-society assassins who operate in environments where weapons screening is routine.
Properties.aliases: Floodgate, The Drip, Wet Work Special
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 0–12 meters
payload capacity: 6 doses per magazine
needle diameter: 0.3mm tungsten-ceramic composite
onset time: 60–90 seconds post-injection
weight: 0.4 kg loaded
dimensions: 18cm x 3cm x 2cm
power source: Micro-cell battery, 40 charges
reload time: 4 seconds (magazine swap)
Properties.tactical_use: Operators favor the Floodgate in close-access operations where loud weapons are counterproductive. It is typically deployed in social infiltration scenarios — a handshake, a crowded elevator, a brushing contact in a corridor. The ninety-second delay between injection and incapacitation gives the operator time to establish distance and alibi. Field doctrine recommends pairing deployment with an exit route, as incapacitated targets attract attention. Some operators use it as a non-lethal control tool by using half-doses, which produce debilitating pain without full systemic collapse.
Properties.cultural_context: The Floodgate occupies an unspoken tier of violence in Meridian 88 — the kind that leaves no visible wound and no obvious weapon. In corporate circles, being 'flooded' is understood as an unmistakable message: someone with access and patience wanted you down, not dead. This restraint is often more terrifying than outright assassination. Street operators who carry the LRI-5 are typically regarded with wariness even by peers, as its use implies a willingness to engage in prolonged, calculated cruelty rather than the swift violence most underworld actors prefer.
Properties.story_hooks: A prominent city councilor collapses during a televised session — no projectile, no poison detected in standard tox screens. The players are hired to find out how.; A black-market Floodgate surfaces in a neighborhood clinic, disguised in a legitimate medical kit. Someone is about to use it — but on whom?; Lazarus Pharmaceuticals quietly hires a team to recover all units from a stolen shipment before a regulatory audit traces the serial numbers back to their R&D division.; A player character is injected during a crowd scene and has ninety seconds to find a medical bay — or improvise.

Nodes.Name: Yeva Sorokina (alleged — three unsolved boardroom collapses)

Properties.description:
The MASCR-4 fires a magnetically accelerated aerosol payload of a proprietary crystallization agent — a supersaturated ionic compound developed by Tessera Corponation under a materials science patent — that is absorbed transdermally and through mucous membranes upon impact. Once inside the body, the compound undergoes rapid crystalline precipitation specifically in the synovial fluid of major joints when exposed to the low-frequency resonance field the weapon continuously projects at its target. The result is acute crystalline arthropathy: joints seize, cartilage abrades against crystalline deposits, and mobility collapses within sixty to ninety seconds of exposure.

The weapon's two-stage mechanism — aerosol delivery followed by resonance-triggered precipitation — gives operators tactical control over timing. The crystallization agent alone is inert; it must be activated by the resonance field. An operator can tag multiple targets with aerosol rounds, then trigger crystallization selectively or simultaneously. The effect is agonizing and temporarily disabling but not inherently lethal, and the crystalline deposits dissolve naturally over twelve to thirty-six hours as the body flushes the compound. Permanent joint damage occurs with repeated exposures or in subjects with pre-existing synovial conditions.

Tessera Corponation markets the MASCR-4 through a subsidiary under a 'non-lethal compliance' classification, a designation that has been challenged by three separate medical bodies and upheld on technical grounds each time. The weapon is available at Tier 4 through licensed security contractors and is considered standard equipment for certain high-end private correctional facilities. Its presence on the street is considered a reliable indicator of institutional backing behind whoever is carrying it.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: Aerosol round: 5–35 meters; resonance activation field: 3–20 meters
payload: Supersaturated ionic crystallization compound, proprietary Tessera formulation
magazine capacity: 8 aerosol rounds
crystallization onset: 60–90 seconds post-activation
effect duration: 12–36 hours natural dissolution; permanent risk with repeated exposure
weight: 3.8 kg
form factor: Semi-automatic rifle with integrated resonance emitter and targeting scope
activation control: Manual selective or simultaneous target activation via thumbwheel selector
Properties.tactical_use: Operators use the MASCR-4's two-stage system to tag multiple targets in a crowd or defensive position, then activate crystallization once they are in a controlled position. The selective activation feature allows for negotiation leverage — a tagged subject who does not comply can be crystallized as a demonstration while others are held in reserve. Correctional operators use it to manage population compliance events without the PR exposure of conventional force. The weapon is rarely used at full magazine capacity; the threat of activation after tagging is frequently sufficient for compliance.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88, the MASCR-4 is institutional power made portable. It is the weapon of wardens, compliance managers, and the kind of security contractor who files paperwork. People who have been 'grouted' — the street term, always passive voice — describe a specific kind of helplessness: the knowledge that someone tagged them and waited, that the pain was a decision made at someone else's convenience. Labor organizers in facilities that use the MASCR-4 have begun training members to identify the aerosol round impact, which has a faint antiseptic smell, as an early warning. Tessera's legal team has attempted to have this training material classified as proprietary interference.
Properties.story_hooks: Workers at a Tessera-affiliated facility are organizing, and someone on the inside has smuggled out documentation showing that the 'temporary' crystallization compound has been silently reformulated — the new version does not fully dissolve.; A fixer has tagged a runner with an aerosol round during a job gone wrong and is now demanding renegotiation of terms, with activation as the threat — the runner has a narrow window to find a way to neutralize the compound.; A black-market chemist claims to have reverse-engineered a partial antidote to the crystallization agent and is selling it in small quantities — but Tessera has apparently noticed and is looking for the source.; A licensed MASCR-4 operator has gone rogue and is using the weapon's tagging capability to build a network of involuntary informants across the city, activating anyone who fails to provide information on demand.

Nodes.Name: A known fixer who uses it for debt enforcement, exploiting the activation delay as leverage

Properties.description:
The MTB-7 is a single-edged combat blade, 28 centimeters in length, constructed from a segmented ferromagnetic alloy with a hollow spine housing a miniaturized linear magnetic acceleration coil array. When activated, the coil array generates a rotating magnetic field along the blade's long axis, causing the blade's segmented construction to torque microscopically — approximately 0.4 degrees of torsional flex per segment. The cumulative effect along the blade's length is a continuous corkscrew motion at the cutting edge, invisible to the naked eye but mechanically equivalent to a high-speed drill bit at the point of tissue contact.

The torsional motion transforms the MTB-7's wound profile entirely. A standard thrust with a conventional blade creates a linear puncture channel. The same thrust with the MTB-7 active creates a helical wound cavity that expands as the blade penetrates, shredding tissue in a widening spiral pattern. Extraction is equally destructive — pulling the blade free while active widens the wound channel significantly, a feature that operators describe clinically as 'maximizing effect on withdrawal.' Against augmentation casings, the torsional cutting edge can bore through Grade 1-2 subdermal plating that would deflect a conventional blade entirely.

TESSERA CORPONATION produced the MTB-7 under a defense contract that was subsequently classified, which has led to considerable speculation about which branch of the Meridian 88 municipal authority originally commissioned it. The weapon entered black market circulation approximately 18 months after its presumed initial deployment, suggesting either a supply chain compromise or a deliberate off-the-books distribution strategy by parties within TESSERA. The blade's segmented construction means it can be disassembled into components that individually register as non-weapons on standard scanners, a feature that almost certainly was not accidental.
Properties.specifications:
blade length: 28 cm
total weight: 0.9 kg
blade material: Segmented ferromagnetic alloy (classified composition)
torsion rate: 0.4 degrees per segment per activation cycle
segments: 14 active segments
activation time: 0.2 seconds to full torsion from cold start
power source: Grip-integrated micro-battery, 90 minutes continuous operation
wound profile: Helical cavity, 1.8x standard puncture volume at full depth
scanner profile: Individual components below weapons detection threshold on standard municipal scanners
augmentation penetration: Effective against Grade 1-2 subdermal plating
Properties.tactical_use: The MTB-7 is used almost exclusively in assassination and close-quarters elimination scenarios. The standard technique is deactivated carry with activation occurring at the moment of initial penetration, ensuring the torsion effect is active throughout the full strike depth rather than lost on surface contact. Skilled operators activate on withdrawal rather than on entry when attempting to minimize initial resistance — entering as a conventional blade and activating during extraction to maximize the exit wound. The disassembly capability is used for checkpoint infiltration, with operators reassembling under 40 seconds from component carry.
Properties.cultural_context: The MTB-7 occupies a specific niche in Meridian 88's assassination culture — it is a weapon that signals professional intent and significant resources. Street violence does not require a magnetic torsion blade; its presence at a crime scene is read by investigators and underworld figures alike as a marker of contract killing or institutional violence. The classified origins and TESSERA CORPONATION's official silence on the weapon's existence have made it into something of a collector's item among weapons enthusiasts, with functional units commanding extraordinary black market prices. There are persistent rumors of a civilian 'sport' variant with reduced torsion yield, but no confirmed examples exist.
Properties.story_hooks: A MTB-7 is found at a murder scene, but the wound profile is wrong — the torsion pattern indicates the blade was rotating in the opposite direction from standard factory configuration, suggesting either a modified unit or a second manufacturer producing counterfeits with reversed coil winding.; TESSERA CORPONATION quietly hires the players to recover all black-market MTB-7 units in circulation before a municipal weapons audit that would expose the classified contract's existence — the number of units they're asked to find is significantly higher than the number that should exist if the original contract is accurate.; A player character is given a disassembled MTB-7 as payment for a job, only to discover that one of the segments contains a micro-transmitter broadcasting their location — whoever gave them the weapon wants to know exactly where they go with it.

Nodes.Name: Contract assassins operating at the corporate level
TESSERA CORPONATION covert operations personnel (officially nonexistent)
A small number of elite mercenary operatives with the contacts to source one
Municipal investigators who have logged it as evidence and not returned it

Properties.description:
The MHPR-2 generates a directed magnetohydrodynamic pulse — a propagating wave of coupled electromagnetic and fluid-dynamic force that interacts violently with any ionised or conductive medium in its path. In practical terms, this means the weapon is extraordinarily effective against targets in or near water, electrolyte-rich environments, or any surface where conductive fluid is present. Blood, sweat, hydraulic fluid, coolant lines, and saline-based biological tissue all become force-multiplying conductors when the pulse strikes.

The weapon's mechanism involves a two-stage barrel: the first stage aerosolises a fine mist of ionised saline solution ahead of the pulse (an internal reservoir holds approximately 40 shots worth of medium), and the second stage fires the MHD wave through the freshly conductive air column. The result is a propagating electromagnetic hammer that follows the conductive path with high fidelity.
