Against unprotected biological targets, the effect is described as a full-body cramp followed by vascular rupture in the extremities. Against electronics, it is effectively a targeted EMP with physical force components.

ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS designed the MHPR-2 for naval interdiction and subsurface combat — environments where water is ambient and the weapon's medium requirement is naturally met. Field adaptation by operators working in humid, industrial, and sewage-adjacent environments has expanded its effective theatres considerably. The weapon has an unofficial reputation as the preferred tool of operators working the Meridian 88 canal district and the flooded sub-levels beneath the financial quarter.
Properties.aliases: Saltwater, The Brine, MHD Stick, MHPR-2
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 8–35 metres (medium-dependent)
pulse frequency: Single shot, 2.4-second recharge cycle
saline reservoir: 40 shots (field-refillable with any electrolyte solution)
power source: MHD cell pack (60 pulses)
weight: 4.3 kg
form factor: Long-frame rifle with dual-barrel configuration and reservoir housing
environmental modifiers: Effectiveness increases 40–300% in high-humidity or wet conditions
electronics disruption: Hard EMP effect within 2 metres of pulse impact
Properties.tactical_use: Devastating in flooded environments, sewage tunnels, rain conditions, and near open water. Operators using Saltwater in dry conditions must rely on the onboard saline mist, which reduces effective range and gives targets a brief visible warning (the mist cloud). Experienced users pre-wet target surfaces or coordinate with team members who can introduce conductive medium before firing. The EMP side-effect makes it valuable for disabling drones, vehicle electronics, and cyberware — though the physical force component means targets near electronics will suffer simultaneously. Faraday suits reduce biological damage but do not protect electronics nearby.
Properties.cultural_context: Saltwater is almost exclusively associated with the canal districts and the drowned sub-levels — the flooded infrastructure beneath Meridian 88's financial core that nobody officially acknowledges. The people who live and work in those spaces (unlicensed salvagers, pipe-gangs, sewer-runners, and the communities that have built permanent habitation in the flooded zones) treat the MHPR-2 with a mix of fear and respect. Military surplus units have trickled into those communities over decades, and a Saltwater in the hands of a canal operator signals serious territorial intent. Above ground, the weapon is rarely seen and widely misunderstood.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of deaths in the flooded sub-levels show vascular rupture patterns consistent with MHPR-2 use — but the victims are members of three different pipe-gangs who have been at peace for two years. Someone is trying to restart the canal wars.; An ARCTURUS logistics manifest has surfaced showing a shipment of MHPR-2s destined for a classified naval program was diverted. Forty rifles are unaccounted for. The players are hired to find them before they flood (literally) into the civilian market.; A player character with significant cyberware is warned that someone in the canal district has a Saltwater and knows their route. They need to find a Faraday solution fast.; The flooded sub-levels community is requesting Saltwaters through a fixer network to defend against a corporate reclamation project. The players have to decide whether to supply them, who to source from, and what strings come attached.

Nodes.Name: Canal district salvage crews operating contested territory
Corporate dive teams doing off-book infrastructure work
"Brine" — a semi-legendary canal district fixer who reportedly carries a modified MHPR-2 as her only weapon

Properties.description: The MHSP-2 generates a directed magnetohydrodynamic field that interacts violently with the conductive saline content of biological tissue. When the field engages a target, it induces opposing directional currents through fluid-dense regions — primarily muscle bellies, joint capsules, and organ tissue — creating a shearing force that tears tissue longitudinally without penetrating the skin. The effect is functionally similar to a severe internal strain injury distributed across a limb or torso segment in under a tenth of a second.
Properties.aliases: Riptide, The Puller, Tide Gun, Mag-Shear
Properties.specifications:
length: 29 cm
weight: 1.6 kg
power source: Zheng-Dao ZD-Flux cell (compact MHD)
effective range: 4–35 m
field aperture: Variable, 15–40 cm diameter at target
discharge rate: Semi-automatic, 0.8 second recycle
shots per cell: 34
housing: Polymer-ceramic composite, field-isolated grip
Properties.tactical_use: The MHSP-2 is a compliance and incapacitation weapon when operated at standard settings, capable of dropping a target by destroying muscular cohesion in a limb without lethal injury. At maximum aperture compression, operators can concentrate the shear field to rupture deep connective tissue and cause joint dislocation. Security teams use it for non-lethal extraction of high-value targets where physical integrity matters. Closed-field operators — bodyguards, detention specialists — carry it as a primary sidearm in environments where projectile weapons are scannable but energy sidearms require higher licensing.
Properties.cultural_context: Zheng-Dao Bioelectric markets the MHSP-2 openly to licensed security contractors as a 'humane restraint solution,' and its presence on a guard's hip is a status signal — it says the carrier works for someone who wants live captives, not corpses. In Meridian 88's debt-collection economy, MHSP-2 operators are called 'pullers' — a term that has drifted from the weapon's physics to a professional designation. The weapon is also common in underground fighting arenas where promoters want dramatic incapacitations rather than deaths.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of kidnappings in the financial district share a signature — victims are found with characteristic internal shear injuries but no external marks, suggesting MHSP-2 use by a highly organized extraction team.; A licensed 'puller' approaches the party for help: their MHSP-2 was remotely bricked mid-contract by Zheng-Dao, stranding them in a hostile situation — and now they want to know why the manufacturer killed their weapon.; An underground fight promoter is running MHSP-2-equipped enforcers to rig bouts, and a fighter who survived an 'accidental' incapacitation wants justice.; Zheng-Dao Bioelectric is quietly recalling a batch of MHSP-2 units with a firmware anomaly that causes the shear field to invert — instead of pulling tissue apart, it compresses it catastrophically.

Properties.description:
The MTPL-2 exploits thermoelectric induction to generate rapid, localized heating within the meningeal membranes surrounding the brain. A directional microwave-band emitter penetrates the skull and preferentially excites the fluid-dense dural and arachnoid layers, producing a steep thermal gradient. The resulting expansion of cerebrospinal fluid within the enclosed cranial vault creates acute intracranial pressure spikes, manifesting in the target as sudden incapacitating headache, nausea, loss of motor coordination, and at sustained exposure, hemorrhagic stroke.

The weapon's distinctive characteristic is its graduated effect curve. At low power settings, the MTPL-2 produces a debilitating but non-lethal pressure event lasting several minutes — useful for crowd control or capture operations. At maximum output, sustained for more than three seconds, the cranial pressure becomes unsurvivable without immediate decompression surgery. Operators describe the kill as 'clean from the outside,' with no external wound and internal damage consistent with spontaneous aneurysm.

Arcturus Defense Solutions developed the Crown as a successor to older microwave crowd-dispersal systems, arguing that precision targeting eliminated the indiscriminate harm of area-effect predecessors. The lance form factor allows engagement up to forty meters with a focused beam, making it effective for both individual neutralization and controlled area denial when swept across a crowd. Its use in the Meridian 88 Port Authority Suppression of 2181 — where seventeen dock workers died of 'simultaneous cerebrovascular events' — remains officially uninvestigated.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 2–40 meters
beam width: Adjustable, 0.3° to 12° arc
power settings: 3 (Suppress / Incapacitate / Lethal)
lethal threshold: 3.1 seconds sustained at max output
power source: Dedicated 18V thermal cell, 8 sustained seconds at max
weight: 3.1 kg with cell
cooling: Passive ceramic radiator fins along barrel
Properties.tactical_use: Used by state-contracted security forces for both crowd suppression and targeted assassination with plausible medical deniability. At Suppress setting, operators sweep the beam across gatherings to disperse without direct confrontation. In single-target mode, the Crown is walked up the torso toward the head, maximizing disorientation before the lethal threshold is reached. Military doctrine recommends two-operator teams — one targeting, one providing cover during the extended engagement window.
Properties.cultural_context: Among protest organizers and labor agitators in Meridian 88, the Crown has become a symbol of state violence that cannot be seen or proven. The phrase 'died of a headache' is used bitterly in activist communities to describe colleagues killed at demonstrations. Arcturus Defense Solutions has successfully lobbied for classification of MTPL-2 casualty data as proprietary security information. Possession of the weapon by non-state actors is exceptionally rare and treated by law enforcement as a maximum-priority threat.
Properties.story_hooks: A journalist investigating the Port Authority Suppression of 2181 has obtained internal communications referencing the MTPL-2 — she needs someone to keep her alive long enough to publish.; A stolen Crown surfaces in the Outerring black market; every faction in the city wants it, and the original theft may have been an inside job.; A character with a neural implant discovers their hardware is partially shielding them from the weapon's effect — Arcturus Defense Solutions dispatches a team to quietly recover them for study.; A political candidate drops dead on stage from apparent stroke; the players are hired by a rival campaign to prove it wasn't natural — then hired by someone else to make sure they don't.

Nodes.Name: Arcturus Defense Solutions contracted riot units
Cassius Verne, a disgraced ADS field tester operating independently

Properties.description:
The Mitochondrial Depolarization Pulse Rifle operates by projecting a tightly focused beam of modulated electromagnetic radiation tuned to the resonant frequency of cytochrome c oxidase — the terminal enzyme in the mitochondrial electron transport chain. On contact, the beam disrupts proton gradient maintenance across the inner mitochondrial membrane, causing a cascading cellular energy failure in targeted tissue within seconds. The effect is not thermal; cells simply cease producing ATP at the required rate, and motor function collapses from the inside out.

What distinguishes the MDPR-2 from comparable disabling weapons is its selectivity and depth of penetration. The beam attenuates predictably through soft tissue but loses minimal energy through non-biological materials, allowing it to affect targets through light cover such as clothing, padding, or standard-grade ballistic weave. Operators describe the effect on unprotected targets as a progressive 'shutdown' — first peripheral muscle groups, then respiratory muscles if exposure is sustained beyond two seconds. Death is possible but requires deliberate extended trigger hold, which gives the weapon plausible deniability as a compliance tool.

Arcturis Defense Solutions markets the MDPR-2 as a 'non-lethal escalation platform,' though this classification is widely contested by independent biomedical researchers and three separate municipal oversight bodies. The weapon is heavy, requires a dedicated power cell rated for thirty shots, and produces a faint violet corona at the emitter aperture that experienced operators call 'the bruise.' Field technicians note that partial cyberware integration — particularly subdermal power cells — can create unpredictable secondary ionization in the target's implants.
Properties.legality: Restricted — licensed to law enforcement and licensed private security contractors only
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 40 meters optimal, 70 meters degraded effect
shots per cell: 30
charge time between shots: 2.1 seconds
beam duration for incapacitation: 1.5–2.5 seconds sustained contact
weight: 4.8 kg loaded
emitter aperture: Tunable — 8cm to 30cm beam spread at 40m
secondary hazard: Cyberware interference within 1.5m of beam path
Properties.tactical_use: Used primarily for crowd incapacitation, high-value target capture, and facility lockdowns where lethal force creates legal or political liability. Operators are trained to sweep the beam across a target's torso for rapid effect. Extended trigger holds targeting the chest cavity are classified as lethal use and require separate authorization under most jurisdictions. Effective against unaugmented targets and those with organic musculature; heavily augmented individuals with synthetic muscle replacement show reduced susceptibility.
Properties.cultural_context: The MDPR-2 has become a symbol of corporate overreach in Meridian 88's civil discourse. Footage of security contractors using 'Brownouts' on striking dock workers at the Palladian Construction yard circulated widely on the mesh three years ago, and the weapon is now visually associated with state-adjacent suppression. Activists wear stylized violet corona pins as protest symbols. Conversely, in private security circles, carrying an MDPR-2 signals professionalism and restraint — the idea being that you can stop someone without leaving marks.
Properties.story_hooks: A batch of MDPR-2s has gone missing from an Arcturus depot — the serial numbers filed off. Someone is planning to use them at a public event, but the party must determine whether the intent is suppression or assassination.; A character with subdermal power cells was hit by a Brownout and survived — but something in their implants is now cycling incorrectly, and they're experiencing micro-blackouts. The only technician who understands the interaction works for Arcturus.; A corporate whistleblower has evidence that Arcturus has been quietly shipping MDPR-2 units to a government with a documented record of disappearing dissidents. The weapon is legal. The sale is documented. Nothing is technically illegal. That's the problem.

Properties.description:
The MFW-1 is a compact handle unit approximately 18cm long, housing a motorized spool of single-molecule carbon filament 2.4 meters in length. The filament itself is invisible to the naked eye under most lighting conditions, with a weighted ceramic tip that provides gyroscopic stability during movement. When deployed, the filament is capable of passing through soft tissue, most unarmored materials, and commercial-grade polymers without perceptible resistance. The handle includes a tension-feedback system that transmits tactile information about filament contact to the operator's grip, allowing experienced users to feel what the weapon is cutting without visual confirmation.

The MFW-1's primary engineering challenge — and its principal distinction — is filament retrieval. Early monofilament weapons were single-use, as retrieving a molecule-thin cutting edge without severing the operator's fingers required solving a complex tension management problem. The MFW-1 uses a variable-resistance electromagnetic spool with micro-brake segments that progressively decelerate the filament during retraction, guiding it back along a fixed geometric path rather than free-coiling. This allows reliable retrieval in approximately 1.8 seconds, making follow-up strikes viable within the same engagement.

The weapon is extraordinarily dangerous to untrained users and bystanders alike — the filament is effectively invisible in low light and produces no sound during flight. Several documented incidents involve operators accidentally severing their own fingers or limbs during botched retrieval sequences. TESSERA CORPONATION includes a mandatory certification requirement in the purchase contract, though enforcement of this requirement is understood to be nominal.
Properties.specifications:
handle length: 18cm
filament length: 2.4m
filament material: Single-molecule carbon composite
tip material: Weighted ceramic stabilizer
retrieval time: 1.8 seconds
spool type: Variable-resistance electromagnetic with micro-brake segmentation
power source: Integrated microcell, 6-hour operational life
weight: 310g (handle unit)
Properties.tactical_use: Experienced operators use the MFW-1 in low-light environments where the filament's invisibility is maximized. Standard engagement sequences involve two to three targeted strikes before retrieval, exploiting the fact that targets often cannot identify the weapon responsible for initial injuries. The whip is particularly effective against unarmored targets and for cutting restraints, cables, and equipment. Some operators coat the ceramic tip in bioluminescent paint to track filament position — a modification that partially defeats the invisibility advantage but significantly reduces self-injury incidents.
Properties.cultural_context: The MFW-1 occupies a position of near-mythological fear in Meridian 88's underground. Its prohibition is absolute across all districts, and the few confirmed operators are treated with a mixture of professional respect and personal dread even among hardened criminals. The nickname 'The Seamstress' reflects a dark appreciation for the weapon's precision — it is associated with individuals who kill not out of desperation but out of craft. Possession alone is sufficient for a maximum-security detention order in most of Meridian 88's administered zones.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of deaths in the financial district share a characteristic the coroner cannot explain — clean, straight incisions on bodies that show no other signs of violence. Someone is using a MFW-1 in broad daylight, and the victims have no obvious connection to each other.; A TESSERA CORPONATION executive is trying to quietly acquire back all MFW-1 units currently in circulation — not for legal reasons, but because the filament in this production batch has a hidden manufacturing defect that makes it traceable to a specific facility the company wants to disavow.; A player character is given a MFW-1 as payment for a job, with no training and no manual. The previous owner is dead. The weapon's tension-feedback system seems to be transmitting something that feels less like cutting resistance and more like deliberate patterns.

Nodes.Name: Former corporate intelligence officers operating outside institutional oversight

Properties.description:
The MSIC-3 operates by projecting a narrow-band oscillating magnetic field tuned precisely to the resonant frequency of myelin sheaths — the insulating protein layers wrapped around peripheral nerve fibers. At sufficient intensity, the field induces rapid localized depolarization cascades along motor neurons, causing involuntary and chaotic muscular contraction. The effect is not pain in the conventional sense but rather a catastrophic loss of motor coherence: targets seize, drop objects, and collapse without any damage to underlying tissue.

What distinguishes the Stutterbox from simpler neuromuscular disruptors is its precision calibration system, which uses a passive biometric ranging ping to adjust field frequency on the fly based on estimated target mass and neural density. This allows it to be effective across a wider range of targets — including partially augmented individuals whose peripheral nervous systems remain biological. Heavily cyberized targets with full neural sleeve replacements are largely immune, a limitation that has shaped how the weapon is tactically deployed.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric originally developed the MSIC series as a non-lethal compliance tool for corporate security detachments operating in civilian-dense environments. The 'Stutterbox' nickname emerged from enforcement footage that leaked onto Meridian 88's underground feeds — the stuttering, marionette-like collapse of targets became darkly iconic, and the weapon's reputation for leaving victims humiliated but unharmed made it paradoxically popular with both law enforcement and certain criminal organizations who prefer leverage over corpses.
Properties.aliases: Stutterbox, The Shunt, Jitter Gun, MSIC
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 8–40 meters
power source: Solid-state capacitor cell, 22 shots per charge
field frequency range: 12–38 Hz adaptive
effect duration: 4–9 seconds post-exposure
weight: 2.8 kg
form factor: Compact carbine, collapsible stock
augmentation vulnerability: Ineffective against targets with >60% peripheral neural replacement
Properties.tactical_use: Operators use the Stutterbox in crowd control, hostage extraction, and non-lethal detention scenarios where collateral damage or casualties would create political or legal complications. Security teams pair it with conventional sidearms — the MSIC drops a target long enough for physical restraint, while the sidearm handles threats the carbine cannot address. In criminal contexts, it is used to incapacitate couriers, witnesses, or targets who need to be taken alive. Savvy operators prioritize soft targets in mixed groups, using the chaos of a seizure to create openings.
Properties.cultural_context: The Stutterbox occupies an uncomfortable middle ground in Meridian 88's weapon culture. It is legal enough to be carried by licensed security contractors but stigmatized in street culture as a 'coward's weapon' — something used by people who want control without confrontation. Paradoxically, certain fixers and negotiators carry one openly as a statement of intent: they have no interest in killing you, but they will absolutely put you on the floor. Among the city's augmentation community, the weapon is deeply resented for its implicit targeting of the unaugmented poor, who cannot afford the neural implants that make them immune to it.
Properties.story_hooks: A leaked Zheng-Dao internal memo suggests the MSIC-3's biometric ranging ping is quietly logging target data — body mass, neural density estimates, location — and transmitting it to an undisclosed corporate server.; A prominent street activist has been publicly 'stuttered' three times in a month by unmarked security teams. She's hiring someone to find out who's ordering the hits and why she's still alive.; A shipment of MSIC-3s is moving through the port district with the frequency calibration locked to a specific neural signature — someone is being hunted very specifically.; An underground clinic is offering a peripheral nerve sleeve modification it claims makes the wearer immune to myelin-band weapons. The procedure has a 30% failure rate that the clinic isn't advertising.

Nodes.Name: Street-level fixers who prefer clean work

Properties.description:
The MSP-6 projects a directed myoelectric interference field that hijacks the motor neuron signaling pathway between the brain and skeletal muscle. Rather than inducing pain or unconsciousness, the Marionette intercepts and overrides voluntary muscle control signals, replacing them with a looping pattern of contradictory activation commands. The result is that the target remains fully conscious and cognitively intact while their body ceases to obey them — muscles fire in cycling, uncoordinated patterns dictated by the weapon's signal rather than the target's nervous system. Subjects typically fall, convulse rhythmically, or freeze in a rigid isometric contraction depending on the signal pattern selected.

Ringo Corponation developed the MSP-6 under a contract for a private correctional facility operator seeking alternatives to chemical restraint. The three signal patterns available on the production model — Collapse, Freeze, and Puppet — were each refined through extensive testing that Ringo has declined to document publicly. The Puppet setting, which produces the unsettling rhythmic full-body convulsion that gives the weapon its street name, was reportedly developed for 'aversion compliance training' applications. The weapon found its way out of the correctional supply chain within 18 months of production beginning.

The MSP-6 is uniquely disturbing in that it leaves targets cognitively present throughout the experience — unlike unconsciousness-inducing weapons, subjects remember exactly what happened to their body. Psychological trauma rates among MSP-6 exposure victims are significantly higher than among victims of physically comparable weapons, a fact that is considered a feature by some users. Targets with motor cortex augmentations or neural signal amplifiers are at elevated risk of prolonged effect, as the weapon's field interacts with the amplified signal environment in unpredictable ways.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 3–20 meters
field width: Single-target focus (narrow beam) or 2-meter cone (area mode)
power source: Ringo R-Pack Standard (15 sustained-fire seconds per pack)
weight: 3.4 kg
length: 64 cm
signal patterns: Three: Collapse / Freeze / Puppet
effect duration after release: 8–45 seconds residual motor disruption
augmentation interaction: Elevated risk with motor-cortex augments and neural amplifiers
cognitive effect: None — targets remain fully conscious throughout
Properties.tactical_use: Law enforcement and corporate security use the Collapse setting for non-lethal detention of fleeing subjects, the Freeze setting for crowd control in high-stakes environments, and the Puppet setting is officially not used by licensed operators despite being present on production units. Underground operators use the Puppet setting specifically for psychological impact — the experience of losing body control while remaining aware is reliably traumatizing and produces compliant subjects. The MSP-6 is also used in arena combat as a paid spectacle weapon in venues where the audience pays to watch the effect.
Properties.cultural_context: The Marionette name and its implications have made the MSP-6 a flashpoint in debates about the ethics of non-lethal weapons in Meridian 88. Advocacy groups point out that 'non-lethal' does not mean 'non-harmful' — the psychological damage profile is significant and lasting. Ringo Corponation's correctional services contracts have been the subject of investigative reporting that consistently disappears before publication. Among street operators, carrying a Marionette signals a specific willingness to cause psychological harm, which puts it in a different moral category than most weapons even in underground culture.
Properties.story_hooks: A journalist investigating Ringo Corponation's correctional facilities disappears; the last thing she filed mentioned she'd obtained footage of MSP-6 Puppet setting use on detainees.; A character is hit with a Marionette and experiences the full conscious-but-paralyzed effect — they remember everything, and they want to find out who authorized its use.; An underground arena operator is running Marionette matches as premium entertainment and needs the party to either participate or make the whole operation disappear.; Someone has modified an MSP-6 to broadcast on a wide-area field rather than a beam — and they've used it once already in a crowded transit hub.

Nodes.Name: Ringo Corponation private correctional facility staff
High-end corporate security units (Freeze setting, officially)
Psychological warfare specialists and interrogation contractors

Properties.description:
The Myofascial Thermobaric Dispersal Rocket uses a two-stage warhead in which the first stage aerosolizes a proprietary fluorocarbon compound tuned to the thermal absorption spectrum of subcutaneous fascia, and the second stage ignites the cloud with a piezoelectric spark array. The resulting deflagration couples preferentially with the fascia layer rather than the surrounding air, meaning targets within the cloud experience an interior burn — heat propagating inward through fascial planes — rather than external flame damage. Structures, vehicles, and equipment in the blast radius show minimal thermal scarring.

The MTDR-9 was developed under a classified ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC contract originally framed as a search-and-rescue tool for locating trapped individuals via their thermal signature — the fluorocarbon compound was initially designed to enhance thermal imaging contrast. The weaponization was a downstream application that ZHENG-DAO has consistently denied. The rocket uses a standard 72mm launch tube compatible with widely distributed civilian construction demolition launchers, giving it an uncomfortable degree of accessibility.

In the field, operators describe targets hit by the MTDR-9 as 'sealed' — the fascial burn creates a subcutaneous compartmentalization effect that traps fluid and heat, producing a characteristic swelling pattern. The weapon's street name, 'Peel-and-Seal,' references this effect. Medical responders require specialized protocols to treat MTDR-9 casualties, as standard burn treatment worsens the compartmentalization.
Properties.aliases: MTDR-9, Fascia Burner, The Peel-and-Seal, Skinfire
Properties.specifications:
form factor: 72mm rocket, 610mm length
weight: 1.8kg
warhead stages: Two-stage: aerosolization charge + piezoelectric ignition array
effective radius: 4.0m full effect, 7.0m partial exposure
aerosol dwell time: 0.4 seconds before ignition
thermal selectivity: 87% energy coupling to fascial tissue vs. ambient air
launcher compatibility: Standard 72mm demolition tube (civilian construction grade)
primary effect: Subcutaneous fascial burn, internal compartmentalization
secondary effects: Fluid trapping, progressive swelling, hyperthermia, delayed organ stress
Properties.tactical_use: The MTDR-9 is used in ambush scenarios where operators need to incapacitate multiple targets in an open area without destroying surrounding infrastructure or triggering fire suppression systems that might alert security. Gangs use it for territory enforcement where destroying property would devalue their own holdings. It has also appeared in assassination contracts where the delayed onset of full symptoms allows the shooter to be well clear before medical response.
Properties.cultural_context: The MTDR-9 represents a category of weapon that Meridian 88's underground medical community has organized specifically around — the 'Skinfire Clinics' run by unlicensed surgeons in the Outer Wards specialize exclusively in MTDR-9 casualty treatment. The existence of these clinics is simultaneously a testament to the weapon's prevalence and to the complete absence of legitimate medical infrastructure in affected districts. ZHENG-DAO's public denial of weaponization is treated as a running dark joke; their corporate logo has been found stenciled onto black market units.
Properties.story_hooks: The Skinfire Clinics start seeing casualties with a modified MTDR-9 compound that defeats their specialized treatment protocols — someone upgraded the formula.; A crate of MTDR-9s with ZHENG-DAO internal lot numbers surfaces on the black market, providing undeniable proof of corporate origin.; A player character's contact is hit by an MTDR-9 and needs treatment from a Skinfire Clinic — the clinic's operator wants a favor before they'll help.; A construction worker is hospitalized with MTDR-9 symptoms despite no known attack — someone is testing the weapon covertly in civilian demolition sites.

Nodes.Name: Assassination contractors operating in infrastructure-sensitive zones
Rogue ZHENG-DAO research staff with access to prototype stock
Outer Ward gang leadership as prestige weapons

Properties.description: The NFDU-6 deploys a compressed canister payload of approximately 40,000 monofilament-gauge carbon-nanotube threads, each between 2 and 8 centimeters in length, suspended in a rapidly evaporating aerosol carrier. Upon detonation, the carrier disperses the threads in a roughly spherical cloud 6 meters in diameter that hangs in the air for 8–12 seconds before the threads settle. Any exposed biological tissue moving through the cloud at typical human speed contacts the threads with enough relative velocity to drive them into the skin, where they become embedded. The threads themselves cause only minor immediate irritation — the real effect is on cybernetic systems. Each thread is coated with a piezoelectric polymer that generates a micro-current on flexion, and embedded in sufficient density around a cybernetic joint or implant housing, they create constant low-level signal interference that degrades fine motor control and causes sensory implants to misfire.
Properties.aliases: Threadbare, The Loom, Silk Grenade, Wire Fog
Properties.specifications:
form factor: Cylindrical throw-grenade, 90mm length, 45mm diameter, olive-drab with yellow band
deployment radius: 6-meter sphere at standard detonation
thread count: Approximately 40,000 per unit
thread dimensions: 2–8 cm length, 1–3 nanometer diameter
suspension duration: 8–12 seconds before threads settle
effect on biological tissue: Minor irritation, mild dermal penetration — not acutely dangerous to unaugmented individuals
effect on cybernetics: Signal interference, motor degradation, sensory misfiring — severity scales with augmentation density
duration of effect: Until threads are removed medically; self-clearing in 6–18 hours for peripheral implants, up to 72 hours for dense augmentation
weight: 0.3 kg
Properties.tactical_use: Threadbare is used as an area-denial and force-degradation tool rather than a direct incapacitation weapon. Thrown into a corridor before a breach, it degrades the fine motor performance of every augmented defender who enters the cloud zone — not enough to stop them, but enough to make their aim unreliable and their cybernetic reflexes sluggish. Operators who know they are about to enter a Threadbare-contaminated area sometimes don full-body coverage, but this significantly limits mobility. Medical extraction of threads requires specialized equipment; field removal is ineffective and risks driving threads deeper.
Properties.cultural_context: Threadbare is widely regarded as a 'dirty' weapon even by operators who have few ethical objections to other prohibited arms. The extended duration of its effects, the medical complexity of removal, and the fact that it affects anyone augmented who enters the zone — not just combatants — has given it a reputation for indiscriminate cruelty. HELIX BIOSYSTEMS officially denies manufacturing it, attributing existing units to a 'discontinued experimental program.' Street-level operators who carry Threadbare are often assumed to be working for employers with no interest in clean operations or civilian collateral.
Properties.story_hooks: A civilian medical clinic in a contested district is treating dozens of patients with Threadbare contamination — someone deployed it in a populated area, and the question of who and why has political implications.; A character with extensive augmentation is contaminated and has 72 hours to find someone with the equipment to remove the threads before a critical job — and the only person with the right tools has their own agenda.; A HELIX BIOSYSTEMS internal document surfaces suggesting the NFDU-6 was not discontinued but is in active production for an undisclosed client.; A Threadbare canister is found at a crime scene that should have been a clean corporate operation — someone is trying to frame a known insurgent group.

Nodes.Name: Criminal organizations conducting corporate facility raids
Black market arms dealers as demonstration product
A mercenary crew known only as 'The Weavers' who are rumored to use nothing else

Properties.description: The NDC-7 is an electromagnetic pulse device engineered specifically to target neural interface hardware rather than physical infrastructure, developed jointly by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric and Helix Biosystems under a defense contract that was quietly terminated after field trials produced unacceptable civilian casualty rates. The device detonates in two stages: an initial kinetic micro-burst clears a small physical radius, followed immediately by a precisely tuned electromagnetic pulse optimized for the frequency signatures of common neural interface chipsets. Operators with standard neural augmentation within 12 meters experience anything from temporary sensory disruption to catastrophic interface cascade — a condition colloquially called 'brainstorm,' in which the implant attempts to process the pulse as input data and floods the user's sensory cortex with recursive error signals.
Properties.aliases: Brainstorm, NDC, Ghost Grenade, The Scrambler
Properties.manufacturer: ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC / HELIX BIOSYSTEMS (joint, discontinued contract)
Properties.legality: Prohibited — classified as a neurological weapon under the Meridian 88 Augmentation Protection Statutes; possession is prosecuted as assault with intent regardless of deployment
Properties.specifications:
weight: 290g
diameter: 58mm
kinetic burst radius: 1.5m (fragmentation suppressed, structural disruption only)
emp radius: 12m primary effect, 20m degraded effect
target frequency range: Optimized for 2170–2195 neural interface chipsets (partial effect on older/newer models)
effect spectrum: Minor: sensory static, 30–90 seconds. Moderate: motor control disruption, nausea, 5–20 minutes. Severe: interface cascade, potential permanent damage. Fatal: documented in 7% of field trial subjects with high-integration implants
countermeasures: Faraday-shielded implant housing (rare, expensive), fully analog operators, pre-detonation interface shutdown
Properties.tactical_use: The NDC-7 is used to neutralize augmented security personnel, cyborg combatants, and neural-linked drone operators without destroying physical infrastructure. An operator with no neural implants — increasingly rare in Meridian 88 — can deploy a Brainstorm into a room full of augmented security and walk through the aftermath. Drone operations are particularly vulnerable: pilots whose neural links are disrupted lose simultaneous control of all linked units. The weapon is also used for targeted assassination of high-integration individuals, where the cascade effect produces deaths that superficially resemble implant malfunction.
Properties.cultural_context: The NDC-7 occupies a uniquely disturbing place in Meridian 88's cultural consciousness. In a city where neural augmentation is near-universal among working professionals, a weapon that turns your own implants against you is existentially threatening in a way that conventional explosives are not. The Augmentation Protection Statutes were passed partly in response to early NDC field trial leaks. Among the unaugmented — the 'clean' communities in the outer districts who reject neural integration on religious or political grounds — the Brainstorm is sometimes spoken of with a complicated admiration: proof that augmentation is a vulnerability as much as an advantage.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of 'implant malfunction' deaths among mid-level corporate executives is being investigated by a forensic technician who notices the cascade signature — someone is using NDC-7s and the medical examiner is being pressured to close the cases.; A clean operator is being hired specifically because the job requires walking through a Brainstorm deployment — but the operator starts to suspect they're the distraction, not the asset.; A Zheng-Dao Bioelectric whistleblower claims the NDC program wasn't discontinued — it was refined, and the new version targets a broader frequency range that covers 2195–2205 chipsets, meaning nearly everyone in Meridian 88.

Nodes.Name: ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC / HELIX BIOSYSTEMS (joint, discontinued contract)
Corporate intelligence units targeting augmented rivals
Pre-termination Zheng-Dao field test personnel (some gone rogue)

Properties.description:
The NDP-4 fires a dart-delivered neural feedback payload: a 2mm tungsten needle carrying a microscale piezoelectric transceiver and a burst-charge of neurotransmitter-disrupting polymer gel. On impact — typically at ranges under 40 meters — the needle embeds in soft tissue and the piezoelectric element activates from the kinetic impact, generating a localized electrical field that destabilizes sodium-channel gating in nearby motor neurons. The polymer gel simultaneously releases a fast-acting acetylcholinesterase inhibitor into the surrounding tissue, creating a 3-6 second window of profound motor disruption — the target experiences inability to initiate voluntary movement while remaining fully conscious. The effect is colloquially described as 'being frozen mid-thought.'

The NDP-4 uses a neural feedback loop architecture originally developed by HELIX BIOSYSTEMS for surgical tremor suppression. In its weapons application, the same feedback principle that once stabilized a surgeon's hands is inverted: the transceiver reads the target's local neural activity and generates counter-phase interference signals that scramble motor command transmission. This active interference component extends the disruption window beyond what the chemical payload alone would produce, and means the effect duration varies with the target's neural architecture — individuals with cybernetic motor augmentation may experience shorter disruption (1-2 seconds) or, in documented cases, a paradoxical amplification effect where the augmentation systems attempt to compensate and produce involuntary movement cascades instead.

The pistol itself is compact and conventionally shaped, operating on a CO2-driven dart projector with a 6-round rotary cylinder. Each dart is individually sealed in a nitrogen-purged capsule to preserve the polymer gel payload. The weapon produces minimal sound — a soft pneumatic pop — and no visible projectile, which has made it a favorite of abduction and interrogation specialists who need a target incapacitated without permanent damage and without witnesses understanding what just happened.
Properties.aliases: Stutter, The Hesitator, NDP, Feedback Gun, The Freeze
Properties.specifications:
caliber: 2mm tungsten neural-payload dart
feed system: 6-round rotary cylinder, nitrogen-sealed dart capsules
propulsion: CO2 pneumatic, 12g standard cartridge (18 shots)

Properties.tactical_use: The NDP-4 is almost exclusively used for non-lethal incapacitation in abduction, extraction, and interrogation scenarios. A single dart creates a 3-6 second window during which a target can be physically controlled without resistance. Operators typically work in pairs — one fires the NDP-4 while the second moves immediately to physically secure the target, who will be conscious, aware, and terrified but unable to resist. The 6-round cylinder allows for multiple targets in sequence. Experienced operators carry a secondary conventional firearm for situations where the target proves augmented or where the disruption window is insufficient.
Properties.cultural_context: The NDP-4 occupies a particularly feared niche in Meridian 88's criminal ecosystem because it is understood as a kidnapper's weapon. Its presence at a scene tells investigators that the perpetrators wanted someone alive and mobile — they needed the target incapacitated for seconds, not dead. The weapon is associated with corporate abduction teams, organ-trafficking operations, and political disappearances. Among the city's augmented population, the NDP-4 carries additional dread because of documented cases where heavy motor augmentation caused the 'amplification effect' — victims with full-body cybernetic systems have experienced violent involuntary convulsions lasting minutes rather than seconds of frozen stillness. HELIX BIOSYSTEMS has publicly disavowed any weapons application of their neural feedback research, a statement that has been received with widespread skepticism.
Properties.story_hooks: A recovered NDP-4 dart from a disappearance scene carries a HELIX BIOSYSTEMS batch code that traces to a research division officially shut down two years ago — someone is still manufacturing; A target with Tier 4 motor augmentation experienced the amplification effect and died from the convulsive response — the operator who fired the dart is now being hunted by their own employer to eliminate the witness; Someone is using NDP-4s to abduct low-tier arcology residents who have no augmentation and no one looking for them — the pattern of disappearances only becomes visible when someone starts mapping them; A player character is hit by an NDP-4 dart and experiences the 3-6 second disruption while fully conscious during a critical moment — and sees something they were not meant to see

Properties.description:
The NFC-3 does not fire a conventional projectile. It emits a tightly focused stream of encoded neural feedback signals derived from the operator's own nervous system, sampled in real time through a sensor array embedded in the grip and stock. The signal stream is amplified, phase-inverted, and projected at the target via a coherent electromagnetic emitter in the barrel. When the stream contacts a target with active neural augmentation — cybernetic nervous system components, neural interface implants, or synaptic enhancement hardware — it creates a feedback loop between the target's augmentation and the projected signal, producing effects ranging from temporary motor disruption to complete neurological shutdown depending on the intensity setting and the target's augmentation profile.

Ringo Corponation developed the NFC-3 as a counter-augmentation platform, responding to the tactical problem of heavily cyberware-augmented combatants who could shrug off conventional firearms due to pain suppression systems and reflex enhancements. The feedback loop exploits the fundamental architecture of neural augmentation: the more extensively a target is augmented, the more vulnerable they are to a correctly tuned feedback stream. Against fully unaugmented targets, the NFC-3 is almost entirely ineffective — the emitted signal has no neural hardware to interact with and dissipates without meaningful effect. This limitation is the weapon's defining tactical characteristic.

The grip sensor array must maintain contact with the operator's bare skin to sample the neural signal baseline. Operators wearing full gloves cannot use the weapon effectively — a deliberate design choice that Ringo Corponation defends as a safety feature preventing unauthorized use, though critics note it also makes the weapon impractical in environments requiring full protective equipment. The weapon's emitter produces a faint violet luminescence during discharge that is invisible to standard optics but detectable to augmented visual systems — a cruel irony given the weapon's primary target demographic.
Properties.legality: Prohibited (counter-augmentation weapons treaty violations in 7 jurisdictions)
Properties.specifications:
emission type: Encoded neural feedback signal stream
effective range: 30m (full effect) / 50m (partial effect)
intensity settings: 5 stages — Motor disruption / Sensory overload / Coordination failure / Augmentation lockout / Neurological shutdown
rate of fire: Continuous beam (sustained) / Pulse mode
weight: 2.8 kg
power source: High-density capacitor bank, 40 seconds sustained fire per charge
operator requirement: Bare-skin grip contact for neural signal sampling
effectiveness against unaugmented: Negligible
visual signature: Violet luminescence (invisible to standard optics, visible to augmented vision)
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed specifically against augmented targets in environments where conventional firearms are ineffective due to the target's pain suppression and reflex systems. Standard doctrine is to sweep the beam across the target rather than hold a fixed point, as movement disrupts the feedback loop coherence and reduces effectiveness. In team operations, the NFC-3 operator is typically shielded by conventional firearms users who handle unaugmented threats while the Mirrorgun operator concentrates on augmented targets. The weapon is considered a specialist tool requiring significant operator training to use effectively.
Properties.cultural_context: The Mirrorgun occupies a uniquely contentious space in Meridian 88's cultural landscape around augmentation. For augmented individuals — a significant and politically vocal population — it represents one of the most direct expressions of fear and hostility toward their existence: a weapon designed specifically to hurt people because they have implants. Anti-augmentation political factions have quietly funded Ringo Corponation's development program, while augmentation rights advocates have made the NFC-3 a centerpiece of their arguments that augmented individuals face systematic persecution. In street culture, being targeted with a Mirrorgun is considered a profound insult regardless of whether it causes injury.
Properties.story_hooks: An augmented street medic who treated victims of NFC-3 attacks is now a target herself — someone is using a Mirrorgun to silence witnesses to a corporate operation. She needs protection and the players need to trace the weapon back to whoever authorized its use, which means following a supply chain that Ringo Corponation has deliberately obscured.; A stolen NFC-3 is being used by someone who doesn't understand its limitations — they're firing it at unaugmented targets and getting no results, then escalating to conventional violence in frustration. The players are hired to recover the weapon before its erratic user kills someone, but the recovery means going into territory controlled by an anti-augmentation faction that will not welcome outsiders.; Ringo Corponation approaches the players to field-test a new NFC-3 firmware update that claims to extend effectiveness against partially augmented targets. The test parameters are suspiciously specific, and the 'test subjects' Ringo has identified are activists who have been publicly critical of the weapon's development. The players have to decide whether to run the test, expose Ringo's intentions, or find a third option.

Nodes.Name: Government security forces in jurisdictions with active augmentation restrictions
Neural Resonance Surveillance and Suppression Drone NRSSD-1 'Shepherd'

Properties.description:
The NRSSD-1 is a medium-altitude surveillance and non-lethal suppression drone developed by Ringo Corponation's contested-space management division. At 90 centimeters in rotor diameter, the Shepherd is larger than most urban drones, designed to loiter visibly above crowds, transit zones, and public gatherings. Its primary sensor suite combines optical, thermal, and a low-power neural resonance scanner that can detect elevated stress hormones, rapid heartrate, and adrenaline-response biomarkers in individuals within a 15-meter radius — effectively identifying agitated, frightened, or aggressive people in a crowd before any physical action occurs.

When the onboard threat-assessment algorithm flags a target, the Shepherd deploys one of two responses. The first is the 'Calm' mode: a focused neural feedback emitter directs low-frequency electromagnetic pulses at the target's prefrontal cortex, inducing a sensation of drowsiness, reduced urgency, and mild euphoria. The effect is temporary and non-damaging — subjects typically describe it as 'suddenly feeling tired' without understanding why. The second mode, 'Herd,' activates a directed acoustic discomfort emitter targeting the flagged individual specifically, producing a sensation of pressure and low-grade pain that instinctively drives the subject away from the drone's position — effectively steering people through a space without physical contact.

Ringo Corponation markets the Shepherd as a 'crowd harmony platform' and holds contracts with three of Meridian 88's transit authorities and one stadium management corporation. The drone's visible presence is deliberately designed — its blue running lights and rounded profile are intended to read as benign surveillance rather than weaponized intervention. Civil liberties researchers who have documented the Shepherd's neural feedback capabilities argue that the distinction is meaningless, and that the drone constitutes unconsented neurological intervention at population scale. Ringo Corponation's public affairs division has not formally responded to this characterization.

rotor diameter: 90cm
mass: 6.4kg
operational altitude: 8–40 meters
neural scanner range: 15 meters radius
neural scanner biomarkers: Cortisol, epinephrine, heart rate variability (passive detection)
calm mode range: 12 meters targeted
calm mode effect duration: 4–9 minutes post-exposure
herd mode range: 18 meters directed

Properties.tactical_use: Deployed in advance of or during public gatherings, transit congestion events, and corporate facility approaches. Operators at a remote command station monitor flagged individuals in real time and authorize Calm or Herd responses. In practice, the threshold for intervention is set by the contracting authority — transit agencies typically flag only extreme agitation, while private corporate clients have been documented setting thresholds low enough to target anyone moving with urgency through a space. Multiple Shepherds operating in coordinated patterns can effectively channel crowd movement through desired pathways without any physical barrier or personnel.
Properties.cultural_context: The Shepherd is one of the most politically charged weapons platforms in Meridian 88, precisely because it does not look like a weapon. Its blue lights have become a symbol of what activists call 'soft architecture' — the invisible shaping of behavior through systems people cannot see or consent to. In the Brackwater and outer transit districts, people have developed reflexive responses to the drone's presence: moving quickly, covering their necks, wearing foil-lined hoods. The hood practice has no actual protective effect against the neural emitter but has become a cultural signifier of resistance. Ringo Corponation's 'Shepherd Awareness' public relations campaign, which positions the drones as 'partners in public safety,' has been defaced in every district where it has been posted.
Properties.story_hooks: The party has been hired to extract someone from a transit hub blanketed by Shepherd coverage — the drones will flag and Herd anyone moving with the urgency of a rescue team.; A Ringo Corponation data analyst is willing to sell archived Shepherd neural-scan logs from a specific date — the logs would identify everyone who was in a particular location, including a client's missing person.; Someone has hacked three Shepherd units in the commercial district and set the Calm mode to continuous maximum output — the area has become eerily quiet, with residents sitting down in the street, unable to remember why they were going anywhere.; A civil liberties researcher has documented that Shepherd units deployed near a specific political candidate's rallies are set to Herd threshold ten times lower than standard — someone in the transit authority is suppressing turnout on behalf of a corporate interest.

Nodes.Name: A known political operative who has used Shepherd data logs to identify and track protest organizers

Properties.description:
The NDG-2 is a non-lethal area-denial grenade that disperses a proprietary aerosolized neurochemical agent developed by LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS under contract for Meridian 88's crowd management divisions. On detonation, a binary chemical initiator mixes two stable precursor compounds within the grenade body during a 1.2-second reaction phase, generating the active agent — a synthetic GABAergic compound designated LZR-7 — immediately before aerosol dispersal. This binary approach means the grenade can be stored indefinitely without degradation, solving a persistent shelf-life problem in legacy chemical ordnance.

LZR-7 acts on the central nervous system through inhalation and dermal absorption, inducing acute disorientation, short-term anterograde amnesia, and motor coordination failure within 8–15 seconds of exposure. Effects last 12–40 minutes depending on body mass and respiratory rate. The compound is theoretically non-lethal at standard doses, but LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS' internal trials — several of which were conducted without subject consent, according to leaked documents — showed a 3–7% fatality rate in subjects with compromised respiratory systems or certain genetic profiles. This data was suppressed.
Properties.aliases: NDG-2, Mindfog, The Blank, Whiteroom Egg

shelf life: Indefinite (binary precursor design)

Properties.tactical_use: Used for crowd dispersal, hostage extraction, and covert incapacitation. Security forces deploy NDG-2s into enclosed spaces — transit hubs, protest corridors, corporate lobbies — to incapacitate occupants without structural damage. In covert operations, a single NDG-2 through a ventilation intake can neutralize an entire floor before a team enters. Operators must wear sealed respiratory filtration; partial-filter masks provide insufficient protection. The amnesia effect makes the NDG-2 particularly valued in extraction operations where witnesses must not retain reliable memories.
Properties.cultural_context: The NDG-2 is one of Meridian 88's most politically charged weapons. LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS markets it as a humane crowd-control solution, and licensed security forces use that framing publicly. But the suppressed fatality data has circulated in activist networks for years, and the grenade's association with the city's most violent protest crackdowns has made it a symbol of corporate-state violence. In lower-tier communities, the phrase 'getting blanked' refers to any situation where someone is rendered helpless by institutional power. The antidote is controlled supply, held exclusively by LAZARUS — a fact that critics call deliberate leverage.
Properties.story_hooks: A player wakes up with no memory of the last six hours. A spent NDG-2 casing is on the floor nearby. Something was taken — or done — during the blank.; The suppressed LAZARUS trial data surfaces in full, naming specific subjects and locations. Someone wants it buried again, and the journalist holding it is already missing.; The antidote supply for an NDG-2 mass deployment at a protest has been stolen before it could be administered to affected civilians. LAZARUS wants it recovered quietly — but the thief wants to expose why the antidote was needed at all.

Properties.description:
The NSD-7 is a mid-tier autonomous dispersal platform roughly the size of a human fist, housing a compressed micro-swarm of 400–600 semi-independent sub-drones, each no larger than a fingernail. Upon release, the parent chassis identifies thermal signatures within a programmable radius and detonates its swarm canister, sending sub-units in ballistic arcs calibrated to maximize coverage across irregular terrain. Each sub-drone carries a micro-filament electrode array capable of delivering targeted neurolytic pulses to exposed skin or thin fabric.

What distinguishes the NSD-7 from earlier swarm platforms is its use of distributed piezoelectric power harvesting — each sub-drone recharges its discharge capacitor from ambient vibration and pressure as it lands or crawls across a target's body, meaning a single deployment can sustain harassment for up to eighteen minutes without an external power source. The parent drone also maintains a low-frequency coordination signal that prevents sub-units from clustering inefficiently, spreading them in optimized interference patterns across multiple targets simultaneously.

In practice, the NSD-7 does not kill. It overwhelms. Targets experience cascading muscle convulsions, disorientation, and involuntary vocalization as sub-drones fire in coordinated sequences designed to prevent neurological adaptation. Crowd control units favor it for its deniability — sub-drones are difficult to collect as evidence and degrade in UV light within 36 hours.
Properties.specifications:
parent chassis dimensions: 11cm x 9cm x 7cm
sub drone count: 400–600 units per canister
sub drone dimensions: 14mm x 8mm
operational duration: Up to 18 minutes per deployment
effective radius: 12m dispersal, 25m harassment range
target capacity: Up to 8 simultaneous targets
UV degradation window: 36 hours
weight: 340g (loaded)
power source: Piezoelectric ambient harvesting per sub-drone; lithium-ceramic primary cell in parent chassis
Properties.tactical_use: Operators typically deploy NSD-7 units ahead of advancing forces to soften crowd resistance or flush targets from concealed positions. The drone is released from cover — thrown, dropped from an elevated position, or launched from a standard 40mm compatible tube — and immediately begins autonomous target acquisition. Security teams use them to deny extraction routes, as the sub-drone swarm renders affected areas nearly impassable without full body enclosure. Counter-insurgency operators have been documented using multiple NSD-7 units in overlapping patterns to create sustained area-denial corridors lasting well beyond the initial deployment window.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88's lower districts, 'getting Locusted' has entered street vernacular as a term for being overwhelmed by bureaucratic or corporate harassment — too many small problems arriving simultaneously to address any one of them. The NSD-7's civilian reputation is one of humiliation rather than fear; it is the weapon of administrators and enforcers who want compliance without martyrs. Black market operators have begun stripping the neurolytic payloads and repurposing sub-drone chassis for surveillance, a modification known as 'seeding.'
Properties.story_hooks: A canister of NSD-7 sub-drones has been seeded throughout a luxury residential tower — someone is watching every resident, and the 36-hour degradation window is already ticking.; A runner claims they were Locusted by units bearing a corporate logo that dissolved before any evidence could be gathered. No one believes them until a second victim surfaces.; The players are hired to retrieve an NSD-7 prototype with an experimental sub-drone that does not degrade — Arcturus wants it back before anyone realizes permanent surveillance swarms are already in the field.

Properties.description:
The NID-6 is a pursuit-class drone designed to intercept augmented targets and establish a forced neural feedback loop through close-proximity broadcast. Roughly the size of a clenched fist, the Shepherd operates at extreme speed—reaching 140 km/h in short bursts—to close distance with a fleeing target before deploying a focused neuromorphic broadcast array at ranges under two meters. The broadcast generates synthetic neural noise tuned to the target's detected implant signature, overwhelming voluntary motor control and inducing a temporary dissociative state lasting 8–25 seconds depending on augmentation density.

The Shepherd's most technically sophisticated feature is its implant signature library, updated via encrypted uplink to HELIX BIOSYSTEMS' proprietary neural architecture database. Before deploying its broadcast, the drone spends approximately 1.2 seconds in passive scan mode, identifying the specific neural interface architecture present in the target and selecting the most effective noise profile from its library. Heavily augmented targets with multiple neural systems experience compounding disruption as the drone sequences through overlapping broadcast frequencies. Unaugmented targets experience moderate disorientation and nausea but are largely resistant to the motor control effects.

Helix Biosystems markets the NID-6 as a 'compliance assistance platform' for corporate security and law enforcement, emphasizing its non-lethal profile and selective efficacy. Critics—particularly advocacy groups representing augmented citizens—argue that a weapon specifically designed to be more effective against augmented people represents a form of targeted discrimination, and the Shepherd has become a flashpoint in ongoing debates about augmentation rights in Meridian 88.
Properties.specifications:
dimensions: 180mm x 140mm x 120mm
weight: 0.9 kg
max speed: 140 km/h burst, 80 km/h sustained pursuit
effective broadcast range: <2 meters
scan and lock time: ~1.2 seconds passive scan before broadcast
disruption duration: 8–25 seconds (augmentation-dependent)
implant library entries: 12,000+ neural architecture profiles (updated quarterly)
operational endurance: 18 minutes active pursuit
simultaneous target tracking: Single target per unit
Properties.tactical_use: Law enforcement units deploy Shepherds ahead of crowd dispersal operations, releasing multiple units to pursue and sequentially neutralize high-augmentation individuals identified as high-risk. Corporate security teams use single Shepherds as 'runner stoppers'—releasing one the moment a target breaks into a sprint. The drone's speed advantage over most human targets means interception is near-certain in open terrain; enclosed environments with signal-dampening infrastructure reduce its broadcast efficacy. Counter-tactics include Faraday-lined neural sleeves, spoofing hardware that broadcasts false implant signatures, and simply having minimal augmentation.
Properties.cultural_context: The Shepherd is one of the most politically charged weapons in Meridian 88's security landscape. Pro-augmentation advocacy groups have staged demonstrations outside HELIX BIOSYSTEMS offices, and several underground networks distribute spoofing firmware specifically designed to defeat the NID-6's implant identification system. For law enforcement and corporate security operators, the Shepherd represents the ideal compliance tool—efficient, traceable, and legally defensible. For augmented citizens, it represents a system that has been specifically engineered to make their bodies a liability. The drone's white-and-blue corporate livery has been repainted in black by at least two known vigilante groups who use captured units against corporate security teams.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone has leaked the NID-6's implant library update schedule, allowing a resistance group to pre-spoof their neural signatures—HELIX BIOSYSTEMS wants the leak found and closed before the next quarterly update.; A player character with heavy neural augmentation is being pursued by a Shepherd that has been modified with a custom implant profile specifically tuned to their architecture—someone has accessed their medical records.; A decommissioned batch of NID-6 units was supposed to have their implant libraries wiped before disposal, but they weren't—and whoever bought them from the salvage depot now has a database of 12,000 neural profiles.

Nodes.Name: Corporate extraction teams targeting augmented assets

Properties.description:
The Neuromorphic Pressure Cestus is a combat glove system developed by Tessera Corponation's advanced human-machine interface division, representing a convergence of their proprietary neural feedback architecture with conventional close-combat augmentation. The cestus consists of a form-fitting composite glove with an embedded neuromorphic processing layer — a thin-film synthetic neural network printed directly onto the glove's inner surface and in direct contact with the operator's skin. This network reads the operator's own motor intention signals at the skin surface level, predicting the trajectory and timing of a strike approximately 80 milliseconds before the operator's conscious mind finalizes the movement.

This predictive capability feeds into the cestus's reactive systems: a network of micro-pneumatic pressure cells distributed across the striking surfaces inflates and reconfigures in the 80-millisecond window before impact, dynamically reshaping the glove's contact geometry to maximize force transmission for the specific strike type being thrown. A hook, a straight, an elbow, a palm strike — each receives a different pressure cell configuration optimized for that movement's biomechanical profile. The result is a weapon that makes the operator's natural fighting instincts more effective, rather than requiring them to learn a new system.

Tessera Corponation markets the NPC-1 as 'augmentation that learns you,' and the marketing is largely accurate — the neuromorphic layer adapts over approximately forty hours of use, progressively refining its model of the specific operator's motor patterns. An NPC-1 calibrated to one user is measurably less effective in another's hands, a feature Tessera frames as personalization but which has significant implications for theft, transfer, and the black market.
Properties.specifications:
weight: 0.4 kg per glove
neuromorphic layer: Tessera Type-N thin-film synthetic neural network, skin-contact
prediction window: 80 ms pre-strike motor intention reading
pressure cell count: 224 micro-pneumatic cells per glove
calibration period: ~40 hours of active use for full operator-specific optimization
power source: Integrated flexible microcell, 6-hour operation
cross-operator performance: Approximately 60% effectiveness when used by non-calibrated operator
glove material: Composite ceramic-fiber outer shell, neuromorphic-embedded inner liner
Properties.tactical_use: The NPC-1 is used by close-combat specialists who rely on instinctive fighting styles rather than formalized martial systems — its predictive architecture works best when the operator fights naturally and does not attempt to consciously direct the glove's behavior. Operators report a sensation of hitting 'harder than they should' without understanding why, which Tessera's documentation confirms is the intended user experience. In extended engagements, the glove's adaptive pressure redistribution reduces hand fatigue and impact trauma to the operator, extending effective fighting endurance. The weapon has no active offensive capability — it amplifies what the operator does rather than adding new attack types, which makes it invisible to most weapon detection systems and difficult to classify under existing legal frameworks.
Properties.cultural_context: The NPC-1 occupies a strange position in Meridian 88's augmentation culture — it is simultaneously one of the most sophisticated combat tools available and one of the least visible, lacking the obvious aesthetic of most combat augmentation. Among Tessera Corponation's corporate culture, gifting a calibrated NPC-1 is considered a significant gesture of trust, as a calibrated glove represents the neural signature of its owner in a tangible form. This has given rise to a disturbing black market in 'harvested' calibrations — neuromorphic data extracted from seized or stolen gloves and analyzed to produce detailed models of an operator's fighting patterns, motor habits, and reaction signatures. Tessera Corponation is aware of this market and has been accused of doing nothing because the data itself is commercially valuable.
Properties.story_hooks: A harvested calibration from a deceased Tessera security operative is circulating on the black market — but analysis of the neural signature reveals fighting patterns and stress responses that suggest the operative witnessed something they were not supposed to, and Tessera wants the calibration data destroyed before someone else reads what is in it.; A player character is offered an NPC-1 pre-calibrated to a legendary underground fighter who disappeared six months ago — the glove works better than anything they have ever worn, but they keep having intrusive motor memories that are not theirs, and someone is willing to pay very well to find out who the original owner was.; Tessera Corponation's neuromorphic division has been quietly approached by a defense contractor who wants to use the NPC-1's predictive architecture not for combat, but to build a system that can read an opponent's fighting intentions before they act — a non-contact application that would make the NPC-1's combat use look trivial by comparison.

Properties.description:
The OCPIR-3 operates by projecting a tightly focused beam of modulated osmotic-induction radiation that penetrates the skull and disrupts the choroid plexus — the brain tissue responsible for producing cerebrospinal fluid. The beam artificially accelerates CSF production while simultaneously inducing localized vasoconstriction in the arachnoid granulations, blocking the fluid's reabsorption pathway. Within seconds, intracranial pressure begins to climb, causing escalating symptoms ranging from blinding headache and visual distortion to projectile vomiting and loss of motor control. At sustained exposure, the effect becomes life-threatening.

What distinguishes the Headwater from cruder neural-targeting weapons is its precision gradient control. Operators can dial the induction intensity to achieve calibrated non-lethal incapacitation — a target left writhing but intact — or ramp the beam to levels that risk cerebral herniation. This tunability made it enormously attractive to corporate security contractors who needed a weapon that could be justified in court as 'non-lethal deployment' while still carrying the implicit threat of a lethal setting.

The weapon is built on a long-barreled platform resembling an anti-materiel rifle, fitted with a large-aperture emitter dish that gives it an unmistakable silhouette. Users report that targets struck at mid-range settings describe the experience as 'the worst migraine of my life followed by not knowing where my legs were.' Street medics in Meridian 88's lower tiers have learned to recognize the presentation and carry emergency hypertonic saline kits as a field countermeasure.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 8–120 meters
beam aperture: 14 cm dish emitter
pressure induction range: 5–42 mmHg above baseline ICP
time to incapacitation: 4–18 seconds depending on intensity setting
power source: High-density osmotic-induction cell, 28 discharges per cell
weight: 6.1 kg
length: 112 cm
intensity settings: 9 graduated levels (1 = discomfort, 9 = herniation risk)
cooldown between shots: 3.2 seconds
Properties.tactical_use: Used primarily for crowd control of high-value targets where conventional weapons would cause unacceptable property damage or media optics. Security teams deploy it to collapse a single individual in a group without alerting bystanders to the method. Hostage negotiators in corporate extraction ops use it to silently incapacitate a target holding a dead-man switch. At lethal settings, it has seen use as an assassination tool — the resulting death mimics hypertensive crisis, complicating forensic attribution.
Properties.cultural_context: The Headwater has a particularly dark reputation in Meridian 88's activist and journalist communities. Several high-profile whistleblowers have died of 'sudden intracranial hemorrhage' within days of publishing damaging corporate data, and the weapon is strongly suspected in at least four cases. The phrase 'getting headwatered' has entered street slang to mean being silently neutralized by institutional power — whether by the weapon specifically or by any invisible, deniable force. Carrying one marks a person as either corporate enforcement or extremely well-connected black market. Civilians who acquire them do so almost exclusively for status.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of deaths ruled as natural hypertensive events are actually a coordinated Headwater assassination campaign — the party must find the shooter before the next target, a protected witness, is killed.; A black market OCPIR-3 is found locked to a specific biometric — whoever it's keyed to can never be identified because the weapon's registration has been scrubbed. Who was it built to kill?; A street medic begins stockpiling the antidote kits in a specific district — she knows something is coming, but won't say what.; A corporate lawyer argues in open court that the Headwater's 'non-lethal' classification means its use against protestors was lawful. The party is hired by the families — or by the corporation — to shape the outcome.
