Properties.description:
The Osmotic Pressure Blade is a combat knife developed by Helix Biosystems as a counterintelligence and targeted neutralization tool, distinguished by its hollow ceramic blade construction and an integrated osmotic delivery system embedded in the handle. The blade is permeated by a network of semi-permeable micro-channels connected to a pressurized reservoir in the grip. Upon penetration of biological tissue, the weapon's passive osmotic differential — established by a hyperosmotic solution in the reservoir — draws interstitial fluid from the wound site inward while simultaneously pushing a controlled dose of the reservoir compound outward through the channel network and into the surrounding tissue.

The genius of the OPB-3's design is that it does not rely on injection mechanisms or active pumps — the osmotic differential does the work, and the deeper the blade is seated in tissue, the greater the exchange rate. The reservoir compound is user-configurable: Helix Biosystems offers a proprietary line of combat-grade solutions ranging from rapid coagulants (designed for field surgery applications, the weapon's official cover purpose) to vasoactive compounds, neural disruptors, or custom biologics available through licensed Helix channels. The blade's ceramic construction makes it invisible to standard metal detection, and the reservoir is shielded against spectroscopic surface scanning.

In the field, operators describe the OPB-3 as 'a knife that doesn't stop working after you pull it out' — the osmotic compound continues diffusing through tissue for minutes to hours after a wound is closed, depending on the formulation used. This temporal displacement between the act of stabbing and the onset of the compound's effects has made the OPB-3 a favored tool for operations requiring deniability.
Properties.specifications:
blade length: 14 cm
blade material: Zirconia-reinforced hollow ceramic
reservoir capacity: 3.2 mL
osmotic exchange rate: 0.08 – 0.4 mL/min depending on tissue depth and formulation
detection profile: Non-metallic; reservoir shielded against surface spectroscopy
compatible solutions: Helix Biosystems Series-9 combat biologics (licensed); field-modified reservoirs documented in circulation
blade tensile strength: Rated for bone contact; brittle under lateral torque exceeding 40 Nm
Properties.tactical_use: Operatives use the OPB-3 for targeted elimination with delayed onset, allowing the user to be well clear of a location before a subject becomes symptomatic. In close-protection roles, it serves as a last-resort blade that guarantees a wound is not survivable even if the initial strike is non-fatal. The ceramic construction makes it the preferred blade for facility penetration where weapon screening is a factor. Its weakness — brittleness under lateral torque — means operators train to use it exclusively with straight-thrust technique, avoiding the slashing strokes that would work with a conventional knife. Field surgeons operating in contested environments have also used the OPB-3 with legitimate coagulant reservoirs, though this is considered cover by most intelligence analysts.
Properties.cultural_context: The OPB-3 exists in Meridian 88's underworld as a ghost weapon — known by reputation, rarely seen, and deeply feared when encountered. Its association with Helix Biosystems, a corporation that publicly presents itself as a medical and pharmaceutical entity, gives it a particular cultural horror: the idea that a company building prosthetics and treatments is also quietly manufacturing assassination tools creates a persistent distrust of Helix's public-facing medical products. Black market reservoir compounds for the OPB-3 have created a secondary economy of biologic weapons dealers who operate under the cover of pharmaceutical supply chains. Possessing an OPB-3 in Meridian 88 is a capital offense in three of the city's administrative sectors.
Properties.story_hooks: A prominent civic official has died of what appears to be a sudden autoimmune cascade — a Helix Biosystems compound that takes 72 hours to manifest. The players have three days from the time of death to find who carried the OPB-3 into the official's last public appearance.; A batch of OPB-3 reservoirs has been mislabeled and entered the legitimate pharmaceutical supply chain — Helix Biosystems is running a covert recovery operation, and they are willing to pay extremely well for silence and return of the product.; The players come into possession of an OPB-3 with a partially expended reservoir containing an unidentified compound — a street chemist can analyze it, but the results suggest it is something Helix has not officially developed yet.

Properties.description: The OPIS-1 'Skindeep' is a short-to-medium range delivery weapon developed by Lazarus Pharmaceuticals that uses focused osmotic pressure waves to drive liquid payloads through intact skin and soft tissue without penetrating the surface — no needle, no wound, no visible mark. The weapon generates a precisely calibrated pressure differential at the target surface, temporarily increasing cellular membrane permeability in a localized area and forcing a liquid payload carried in the weapon's pressurized reservoir through the skin barrier and into subcutaneous or intramuscular tissue. The payload — which can be any compound stable in liquid suspension — is delivered in approximately 0.3 seconds and leaves no external evidence of administration beyond a brief, easily-missed reddening of the skin.
Properties.aliases: The Pharmacist, Dose Gun, Membrane Breaker
Properties.legality: Prohibited (tactical variant); Licensed (medical variant, clinical use only)
Properties.specifications:
weight: 0.9 kg (unloaded)
length: 28 cm
effective range: 2–15 m (optimal delivery window)
payload reservoir: 10 mL modular cartridge (standard pharmaceutical form factor)
delivery time: 0.3 seconds (subcutaneous mode), 0.5 seconds (deep drive mode)
delivery modes: Subcutaneous (surface layer), Deep drive (intramuscular)
discharge signature: None (no sound, no visible emission, no detectable beam)
surface evidence: Localized skin reddening, fades within 4–8 minutes
power source: Micro-capacitor cell (200 deliveries per cell)
payload compatibility: Any liquid compound stable in suspension at ambient pressure
Properties.tactical_use: The 'Skindeep' is used almost exclusively in covert operations where the operator cannot afford to be identified as having discharged a weapon. Assassination, targeted incapacitation, covert sedation for abduction operations, and intelligence extraction via pharmacological means are all documented uses. The weapon's short effective range demands operators work in close proximity to targets — crowded spaces, social events, transit corridors — making social engineering skill as important as marksmanship. Counter-detection protocols for the 'Skindeep' are still underdeveloped in most security frameworks, and many deployments are never identified as weapon use at all.
Properties.cultural_context: The 'Skindeep' has generated profound unease in Meridian 88's social fabric because it collapses the boundary between medicine and violence in a way that most weapons do not. The fact that it originated as a medical device — and that its medical variant remains legally available — means that trust in clinical pharmaceutical delivery has been measurably eroded in communities aware of the weapon's existence. Some districts have developed informal protocols around receiving any medical treatment from unknown practitioners. The weapon is particularly associated with Lazarus Pharmaceuticals' corporate intelligence division, which officially denies its existence, and with a loose network of freelance pharmacological operators known in the underground as 'dosers.'
Properties.story_hooks: A senior Meridian 88 council member collapsed during a public address — medical examination shows a compound in their bloodstream that doesn't match any licensed Lazarus Pharmaceuticals payload. Someone synthesized a new cartridge, and the council member's staff wants to know what was delivered before the effects become permanent.; A doser operating in the Palladian Quarter has been selling a payload that induces total, specific memory loss of the past 72 hours — no other cognitive effects, no physical symptoms. The compound shouldn't exist. Someone wants to know who's manufacturing it and why.; The players discover that the social event they've been hired to attend has been identified as a 'Skindeep operation' — someone in the room is planning to dose a target, and the players don't know who the operator is, who the target is, or what's in the cartridge.; Lazarus Pharmaceuticals is quietly recalling a specific medical delivery device model — the same form factor as the 'Skindeep.' They claim a manufacturing defect, but the recall notice was issued forty minutes after a foreign diplomat died in a Meridian 88 hotel.

Properties.description:
The OFH-1 is a compact single-handed impact weapon — visually similar to a geological survey hammer — with a striking face constructed from a piezoelectric transducer array embedded in a dense tungsten carbide head. On impact with bone or bone-equivalent material (including certain ceramic augmentation components), the transducer array reads the resonant frequency of the target structure and, within a single millisecond, fires a return pulse tuned to that structure's harmonic failure frequency. The effect is not merely blunt trauma — it is a precisely engineered fracture event in which the target bone is induced to shatter along its own crystalline stress lines rather than simply breaking under compressive force.

The distinction matters enormously in practice. A conventional hammer blow to a forearm might fracture the ulna in one or two places. The OFH-1's resonance-matched pulse propagates the fracture event along the entire bone simultaneously, producing a catastrophic multi-point failure that is both more immediately disabling and far more difficult to surgically repair. The wave propagation also travels through connected bone structures — a strike to the wrist can produce secondary fracture events in the elbow and shoulder within 0.3 seconds, as the initial resonance pulse travels up the skeletal chain before dissipating. Operators describe this as 'the echo effect.'

OUROBOROS ENERGY originally developed the underlying osseoconductive frequency analysis technology for geological survey work — reading rock strata resonance to identify fracture points before controlled demolition. PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION licensed the technology for structural assessment. At some point between those applications and the current one, an unknown party commissioned a weaponized adaptation. The OFH-1 carries no manufacturer's mark, no serial number, and uses a proprietary transducer compound that materials analysis has not definitively sourced. It exists, officially, as an anomaly.
Properties.aliases: Inheritance, The Heirloom, Bonecaller, Resonance Hammer
Properties.manufacturer: Unknown (base technology derived from OUROBOROS ENERGY and PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION research)
Properties.specifications:
length: 32 cm
head weight: 0.8 kg (tungsten carbide)
total weight: 1.2 kg
transducer array: 48-element piezoelectric array in striking face
frequency analysis time: 0.8 milliseconds from contact to matched pulse output
fracture propagation range: Effective to 60 cm from strike point along connected bone
echo effect delay: 0.1-0.3 seconds per skeletal junction
target materials: Bone, ceramic augmentation components, certain mineral composites
power source: Self-generating — piezoelectric array harvests energy from each strike
manufacturer markings: None — no serial number, no branding
materials analysis: Transducer compound unidentified by three independent laboratories
Properties.tactical_use: The OFH-1 is used in scenarios requiring permanent disablement rather than killing — targets who need to be alive but non-functional, or situations where death would trigger undesirable consequences (insurance claims, family reprisals, political martyrdom). A single strike to any major long bone is sufficient to trigger the resonance cascade; operators target the femur or humerus for maximum echo propagation. Against augmented targets, the OFH-1 is specifically effective against ceramic-composite subdermal plating, which shares sufficient resonance properties with bone to trigger the fracture pulse — a fact that surprises many augmented operators who consider their plating impervious to blunt trauma.
Properties.cultural_context: The OFH-1 has generated genuine unease in Meridian 88's underworld because no one can definitively explain where it came from. Weapons have manufacturers. Manufacturers have records. The OFH-1 has neither, which means either someone has achieved perfect operational security in a city of surveillance, or something institutional has decided to produce an untraceable weapon and has the resources to actually pull it off. The name 'Inheritance' came from the streets — a dark joke about what it leaves behind. Possession is rare enough that encountering one is considered an omen by street operators who are superstitious about such things, and a significant intelligence failure by those who are not.
Properties.story_hooks: The players are hired by OUROBOROS ENERGY's internal security division to trace the OFH-1's manufacturing chain — someone weaponized their proprietary technology without authorization, and the corporation wants to know who before the story becomes public and triggers a product liability cascade.; A prominent Meridian 88 figure is found with injuries consistent with OFH-1 use, but the echo propagation pattern in the forensic report indicates the weapon that struck them has a transducer configuration that doesn't match any known OFH-1 unit — either the weapon has been modified, or there is a second-generation version in circulation.; A player character begins receiving anonymous deliveries of geological survey data — rock strata resonance readings — that, when decoded with the right background in materials science, resolve into the OFH-1's transducer compound formula. Someone wants them to know how it's made, and the question is whether that's a gift, a trap, or a recruitment.

Properties.description: The OFC-7 is a proximity-triggered blast device engineered around a narrow-band resonant frequency array embedded in its casing. Rather than relying on fragmentation or raw overpressure, the charge detonates with a precisely shaped acoustic shockwave tuned to the resonant frequency of human bone — specifically the skull, jaw, and orbital structures. The initial concussive blast is comparatively mild; it is the secondary resonant pulse lasting 0.08 seconds that causes the characteristic bilateral temporal fractures and sinus cavity collapse that give the weapon its street name.
Properties.aliases: Jawbreaker, OFC-7, The Dentist, Bone Bell
Properties.specifications:
weight: 0.6 kg
diameter: 9 cm
trigger modes: Proximity (adjustable 0.5–3 m), Remote detonation, Timer (1–30 seconds)
effective kill radius: 2.5 m
effective injury radius: 6 m
resonant frequency: Classified — estimated 210–240 Hz burst sweep
casing: Low-radar-return polymer composite
Properties.tactical_use: Used almost exclusively in assassination and targeted elimination operations where collateral structural damage must be minimized — the OFC-7 kills people in a room while leaving the room largely intact. Security contractors plant them under chairs, inside door frames, or beneath flooring panels. The injury radius produces immediate incapacitation through vertigo, tinnitus, and jaw dislocation, which makes it useful for capture operations when set to low-yield mode.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88's corporate espionage circles, receiving an OFC-7 in a parcel — unarmed, as a message — is a well-understood death threat. The weapon's clinical precision has made it a status symbol among high-end fixers who want to signal they can afford surgical solutions. ZHENG-DAO officially denies manufacturing it, though their component signatures are unmistakable to anyone with a spectral analyzer.
Properties.story_hooks: A city councilor survives an OFC-7 detonation that should have been fatal — someone swapped the resonance array for a dummy, and the councilor wants to know who saved them and why.; A fixer's safe house is swept and three OFC-7 charges are found inside the walls, already armed. The fixer has no idea who planted them or how long they've been there.; ZHENG-DAO's denial of the OFC-7's existence becomes legally complicated when a forensics team recovers an intact unit with a factory serial number still etched on the internal housing.

Properties.description:
The ORB-3 is a 60cm impact baton constructed from dense polymer composite over a titanium core, with a secondary function as a precision resonance delivery device. The baton's striking surface houses an array of micro-transducers capable of generating targeted ultrasonic pulses at the moment of contact, transmitting vibrational energy directly through struck surfaces — including bone, cartilage, and implant housings — rather than simply delivering blunt kinetic force. A standard impact from the ORB-3 carries the physical effect of the blow plus a concentrated resonance burst that propagates through the target's skeletal structure, inducing acute pain response, joint destabilization, and in repeated strikes, microfracture accumulation in bone density.

The weapon's resonance profile is tunable via a recessed dial at the base of the grip, allowing operators to shift between a bone-conduction pain mode, an inner-ear disruption mode that causes severe vertigo and nausea, and a structural mode intended for use against reinforced materials and door panels. The inner-ear mode is the weapon's most notorious application — a single strike to the shoulder or back of the head can induce complete vestibular disruption lasting between 30 seconds and several minutes, rendering a target unable to stand or orient without causing them any visible external injury.

Helix Biosystems developed the ORB-3 as a crowd-control tool for private security contracts, but the inner-ear mode was discovered and publicized by an independent weapons analyst within a year of launch. The subsequent controversy did not result in the weapon's prohibition but did generate a licensing requirement that is routinely circumvented through intermediary sales.
Properties.specifications:
length: 60cm
weight: 890g
core material: Titanium
shell material: Dense polymer composite
transducer array: 14-element contact surface
resonance profiles: 3
frequency range: 18,000–92,000 Hz (profile-dependent)
power source: Grip-integrated power cell, 3-hour continuous use
tuning interface: Recessed grip-base dial
Properties.tactical_use: Security personnel use the ORB-3 in crowd dispersal and suspect control scenarios where visible injury would create liability or media exposure. Inner-ear mode is applied via strikes to the upper back, shoulder, or base of the skull, and requires minimal accuracy to be effective. Bone-conduction pain mode is used in compliance and detention contexts. Structural mode sees use in breaching operations where a door panel or equipment housing needs to be compromised quickly and quietly. Experienced operators rotate between modes within a single engagement based on target response.
Properties.cultural_context: The ORB-3 has become a symbol of what activists in Meridian 88 call 'clean brutality' — enforcement violence that leaves no marks and therefore no evidence. Several civil rights organizations have campaigned unsuccessfully for its prohibition, and at least one advocacy group distributes inner-ear disruption countermeasures — small foam inserts that partially attenuate the resonance effect — in high-policing districts. Private security firms prize the weapon precisely because its effects are difficult to document, and the licensing requirement is widely seen as a formality that provides legal cover without meaningful restriction.
Properties.story_hooks: A civil rights lawyer is building a case against a private security firm for the ORB-3 deaths of three protesters — but the deaths were officially attributed to pre-existing conditions, and the firm's contract specifically indemnifies them for resonance weapon use. She needs someone to find the security footage that was 'lost.'; A HELIX BIOSYSTEMS engineer who worked on the ORB-3's inner-ear mode has developed a modified version tuned specifically to disrupt a particular line of neural implants — and someone very powerful wants that modification before anyone else gets it.; An ORB-3 unit has been recovered from a crime scene with its resonance log showing a frequency sequence that exactly matches the vibrational signature of a specific building's structural resonance frequency. Someone was testing whether the weapon could be used at scale.

Properties.description:
The OLDI-3 is a contact-delivery weapon disguised as a standard medical injector, approximately the size and weight of a thick pen. On skin contact and trigger depression, it delivers a payload of oxidative iron nanoparticle suspension directly through the dermis via high-pressure micro-needle array, bypassing the need for visible puncture or vascular access. The particles enter the lymphatic system and begin a slow oxidative process that progressively degrades lymph node tissue, producing an expanding cascade of immune dysfunction, chronic inflammation, and eventually systemic failure. The process takes between three days and three weeks depending on the payload concentration and the target's biological constitution.

The insidious design intent of the OLDI-3 is temporal dislocation — the weapon is designed to be used in a moment of brief physical contact (a handshake, a crowd brush, a brief struggle) and to produce consequences that emerge long after any connection to that moment can be established. Lazarus Pharmaceuticals developed it under a medical research exemption, ostensibly to study lymphatic drug delivery mechanisms. The weaponized application was, according to company documentation, entirely unintended, a position that has satisfied no investigator who has examined it. The injector contains no moving parts that would register on standard weapons scanners, and the micro-needle array is indistinguishable from a standard dermal patch applicator.

The name 'Rust' describes the slow, inevitable quality of its effect. 'The Long Shake' refers to the handshake delivery method favored by professional operators, and has entered Meridian 88's political vocabulary as a term for any arrangement where the consequences of a meeting only become apparent weeks later.
Properties.specifications:
delivery method: Contact transdermal, no visible puncture
payload volume: 0.3 mL per injection
onset window: 3-21 days post-delivery
progression rate: Variable by target biology and concentration
injector dimensions: 14cm length, 1.2cm diameter
weight: 38g
payload cartridges: Single-use, 6-cartridge reload block available
scanner profile: Indistinguishable from standard dermal patch applicator on standard weapons scanners
Properties.tactical_use: Exclusively an assassination and political destabilization tool. Operators use it in settings where brief physical contact is possible and plausible — social events, negotiations, medical environments, transportation. Professional operators favor the handshake delivery but also use incidental contact in crowds, staged accidents, and posed medical examinations. The weapon's temporal displacement is its primary tactical value: by the time symptoms appear, the delivery moment is days or weeks past, and establishing a chain of custody to the injector is extraordinarily difficult. Countermeasures involve lymphatic screening protocols and blanket nanoparticle filters, but these are expensive and not routinely deployed.
Properties.cultural_context: The OLDI-3 has created a specific strain of paranoia in Meridian 88's upper political and corporate strata that operators call 'handshake anxiety.' High-value individuals in contested spaces have begun refusing physical contact entirely, conducting all meetings through intermediaries or behind barrier glass. This behavior has in turn become a social signal — someone who will not shake hands is either extremely cautious or has something to hide — which creates its own set of political complications. Among assassination contractors, the OLDI-3 is considered a premium tool, not because it is difficult to use but because its temporal displacement makes attribution nearly impossible, which means the operator's exposure is minimal. Lazarus Pharmaceuticals has never publicly acknowledged the weapon exists.
Properties.story_hooks: A city council member is dying of what appears to be accelerated lymphatic failure — three weeks ago they attended a routine negotiation session with six other people, and now the operator has to figure out which of the five surviving attendees shook their hand.; A batch of OLDI-3 cartridges has been stolen from a Lazarus Pharmaceuticals distribution point, but the theft records show the cartridges contained a modified payload — one that works in hours, not weeks, eliminating the weapon's primary advantage and suggesting someone wants bodies found quickly.; An operator wakes up with symptoms consistent with OLDI-3 exposure and has to reconstruct every physical contact from the past three weeks while the clock runs down.; Lazarus Pharmaceuticals has quietly developed an antidote — but they are only offering it to clients who can prove they were exposed, which requires admitting they know what the OLDI-3 is and how it works.

Properties.description:
The Oxidative Plasma Breath Lance generates a sustained stream of superheated oxidative plasma through a catalytic compression nozzle, but its defining characteristic is the delivery geometry: rather than a focused jet, the OPBL-1 produces a wide, flat, billowing emission — roughly 1.4 meters wide at three meters range — that operators describe as resembling a thrown cloak or a priest's vestment caught in wind. TESSERA CORPONATION's original design brief called for a weapon capable of simultaneous full-torso surface contact, and the Vestment delivers exactly that, enveloping a target in plasma rather than puncturing them with it.

The oxidative component is key to the weapon's particular lethality. Standard plasma weapons inflict thermal damage; the OPBL-1 additionally saturates the plasma stream with a high-oxygen reactive medium, accelerating combustion on contact with organic materials and causing secondary ignition in clothing, hair, and exposed tissue layers. The effect on armored targets is more nuanced — the flat emission wraps around armor edges, finding gaps at joints and seals, which makes it disproportionately effective against targets whose frontal coverage is strong but whose lateral and rear seals are imperfect. TESSERA markets this as 'coverage-adaptive thermal application.'

The OPBL-1 is a two-handed platform, roughly the dimensions of a combat shotgun, with a distinctive flat-mouthed nozzle resembling a wide letterbox slot. It is slow between emissions — the catalytic chamber requires 4 seconds to re-pressurize — and operators are trained to treat each emission as a decisive action rather than suppressing fire. The weapon's cultural weight comes almost entirely from its visual signature: the billowing plasma 'vestment' is unmistakable at range and has become one of Meridian 88's most recognized weapon silhouettes.
Properties.aliases: Vestment, The Cope, Robe, Priest's Breath, Burncloth
Properties.legality: Prohibited — unlicensed possession carries mandatory custodial sentence under Meridian 88 Municipal Code 44-C
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 1–9 meters optimal; degraded beyond 12 meters
emission width: 1.4 meters at 3 meters range; 2.8 meters at 9 meters range
emission duration: 1.8 seconds per charge
charges per canister: 6
re-pressurization time: 4 seconds between emissions
weight: 4.2 kg loaded
armor interaction: Wraps armor edges; highly effective against jointed or segmented protection
Properties.tactical_use: Used by military and paramilitary breach teams for room clearance where multiple targets are expected in close proximity. The wide emission eliminates the need for precise target tracking in chaotic close-quarters environments. Counter-insurgency operations have deployed it for crowd suppression — a use that remains deeply controversial and is technically outside its licensing parameters. Operators often use it as a second weapon after a primary has disrupted a room, delivering the Vestment into a disordered space.
Properties.cultural_context: The Vestment has acquired a grim religious iconography in Meridian 88. Its use during the Sector 9 clearance operations — now referred to obliquely as 'the vestings' by those who lived through them — left a generation of residents with a visceral reaction to its visual signature. Street murals depicting figures consumed in wide flame are a recurring motif in former Sector 9 neighborhoods. TESSERA CORPONATION does not publicly acknowledge the weapon's use in those operations. Militia groups who oppose TESSERA have adopted the vestment silhouette as an accusatory symbol.
Properties.story_hooks: A TESSERA internal memo surfaces suggesting the OPBL-1 was used in Sector 9 under a classified operations order — someone with access to that memo is selling it, and both TESSERA and the resistance want to find them first.; A stolen Vestment appears in a civilian murder scene. The killing doesn't fit any known criminal pattern. Whoever used it knew exactly what they were doing — and apparently didn't care about the forensic signature.; A former TESSERA breach team operator is living quietly in a peripheral district. They left the company after Sector 9. Someone has just slid a photograph of the vestings under their door with a note: 'We know you were there. We know you used it. We need you to testify.'; A new unlicensed Vestment variant is circulating — someone has modified the nozzle geometry to produce a narrower, focused stream. TESSERA wants the modification studied before it reaches the wrong hands.

Properties.description:
The OTDD-4 is a persistent area-heating platform developed by OUROBOROS ENERGY's defense subsidiary from industrial thermal management technology originally designed for pipeline thaw operations in extreme cold environments. The drone carries a focused oxidative catalytic emitter — a system that superheats a concentrated column of ambient air through rapid catalytic oxidation cycling rather than combustion, producing a sustained thermal cone that can raise surface temperatures in a 3-meter radius by 40–90 degrees Celsius depending on proximity and dwell time. The effect on organic targets ranges from rapid dehydration and heat exhaustion at range to contact burns and respiratory damage at close quarters.

The OTDD-4 is not a fast weapon. It moves slowly, holds altitude with deliberate stability, and requires 8–12 seconds of dwell time to produce incapacitating effects on an unprotected target. What it offers is persistence and silence — the catalytic emitter produces no flame, no visible beam, and no significant acoustic signature. Targets describe the experience as standing next to an industrial furnace that appeared from nowhere. The drone's thermal signature is, paradoxically, a liability: most military-grade thermal detection systems will acquire it immediately. It was designed for use against targets without such equipment.

OUROBOROS ENERGY's civilian documentation describes the OTDD-4 as an 'ice management and environmental thermal correction platform.' The same hardware, the same firmware, the same catalytic array. The company notes that operational parameters outside intended use cases are the operator's legal responsibility.
Properties.aliases: Ember, The Cinder, OTDD, Slow Burn
Properties.specifications:
dimensions: 40 cm diameter disc, 18 cm depth
weight: 2.3 kg
thermal output: 40–90°C surface temperature increase at target (proximity-dependent)
effective range: 0.5–4 m thermal cone
dwell time for incapacitation: 8–12 seconds (unprotected target)
flight ceiling: 30 m
battery life: 28 minutes at full thermal output
noise signature: < 22 dB at 5 m
visible emissions: None (no flame or visible beam)
thermal signature: Highly detectable on thermal optics
countermeasures: Thermal-rated suit (Class 3+), thermal detection equipment, distance
Properties.tactical_use: OTDD-4 units are used to flush targets from cover, deny enclosed spaces, and suppress movement without direct confrontation. Operators fly them into rooms ahead of entry teams, forcing occupants into the open or toward prepared positions. In outdoor contexts, they're used against targets in concealed positions who lack thermal detection capability. Extended dwell operations — hovering over a fixed position for the full 28-minute battery cycle — can render a room uninhabitable for hours afterward due to residual surface heat.
Properties.cultural_context: OUROBOROS ENERGY's dual-use strategy with the OTDD-4 is considered one of Meridian 88's more brazen corporate maneuvers. The company openly sells the hardware through industrial supply channels, and the combat firmware is available on the black market for a modest premium. When confronted about documented combat deployments, OUROBOROS' communications team reliably notes that pipeline thaw operations can involve significant thermal output requirements. The drone has consequently become a symbol of corporate accountability theater — a favorite example cited by reform advocates and investigative journalists as evidence that Meridian 88's legal distinctions between industrial and military hardware are functionally meaningless.
Properties.story_hooks: An OUROBOROS ENERGY field technician was found dead in a pipeline maintenance access tunnel — cause of death, thermal exposure consistent with OTDD-4 dwell pattern. The company's own drone killed one of their own people, and the firmware logs have been wiped.; A community organizer in the Underbelly has been receiving OTDD-4 harassment — the drone appears outside her window at night, idles for twenty minutes, leaves. No contact burns, no property damage. Just heat. Just a reminder. The serial number traces to an OUROBOROS industrial supply account.; The party needs to cross a contested building that a well-funded crew has seeded with OTDD-4 units running loiter patterns. The building has no thermal detection equipment. The question is whether they go in blind and fast, or find another way.

Properties.description:
The Periosteal Galvanic Stress Fracture Emitter directs a focused beam of low-frequency alternating electrical current through the target's skeletal structure using transcutaneous capacitive coupling — no physical contact required. The current is modulated to exploit the piezoelectric properties of bone mineral, inducing microscopic oscillatory stress at the crystalline level of hydroxyapatite within cortical bone. Over a sustained engagement of thirty to ninety seconds, this mechanical fatigue accumulates until spontaneous stress fractures propagate through weight-bearing bones. The tibia and femur are primary targets at standard settings; the weapon can be retargeted to the spinal column with a firmware adjustment.

The PGSFE-3 differs from earlier galvanic bone-disruption concepts in its use of a resonance feedback loop: onboard sensors detect the acoustic signature of the target's bone structure through the return signal, allowing the emitter to continuously tune its frequency to the target's specific bone density and mineral composition. This means the weapon is self-optimizing — it gets more efficient the longer it is applied. An operator who holds a target in the beam for the full ninety-second cycle will typically induce complete bilateral tibial fracture, dropping the target without any surface wound, blood, or external sign of cause.

The emitter requires line-of-sight but penetrates most civilian clothing without attenuation. Thick metal plating — the kind found in high-end combat chassis augmentations — can shield the underlying biological bone, but few civilian-grade augments include full skeletal shielding. The weapon's power draw is substantial, and the emitter head generates significant waste heat, requiring a thirty-second cooling cycle between full engagements.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 3–20 meters
minimum engagement time: 30 seconds (hairline fracture)
full effect engagement time: 90 seconds (complete fracture)
resonance feedback update rate: 40 Hz
cooling cycle: 30 seconds between full engagements
power source: High-draw galvanic cell, 4 full engagements per charge
weight: 5.8 kg with power cell
form factor: Heavy carbine with large-diameter emitter head
countermeasure: Full skeletal metal plating (military-grade augmentation only)
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed in situations requiring incapacitation without lethality — hostage scenarios, high-value capture operations, or crowd control where the political cost of deaths is unacceptable but permanent injury is tolerable. Military units use it to collapse enemy combatants in fortified positions without entering the kill zone. The weapon's weight and cooling requirement make it a two-operator weapon in field doctrine — one holds the emitter, one provides security during the cooling cycle. Some operators use sub-threshold pulses to induce bone pain and fracture risk as a psychological pressure tool without committing to a full engagement.
Properties.cultural_context: Among Meridian 88's military and paramilitary contractors, the PGSFE-3 is regarded with a particular dread reserved for weapons that produce suffering without death. Soldiers who have been 'crackerjacked' and survived with multiple spontaneous fractures describe the experience as uniquely dehumanizing — bones break from the inside while the skin remains intact. Veterans' advocacy groups in the city have been pushing for the weapon's classification as a torture device under Meridian 88's internal security codes, so far without success. Tessera Corponation maintains the PGSFE-3 is a 'minimum force compliance tool.'
Properties.story_hooks: A mass casualty event in a transit hub shows forty-seven people with spontaneous bilateral leg fractures and no external wounds — someone used a PGSFE-3 on a crowd, and the only footage shows a maintenance worker with an oversized equipment bag.; A Tessera Corponation engineer who worked on the PGSFE-3's resonance feedback system is trying to defect — she claims the weapon has a classified setting that targets spinal vertebrae and was used in an undisclosed operation.; A fixer is hired to retrieve a stolen PGSFE-3 from a gang that has figured out how to bypass the cooling cycle — making it continuous — but has already used it on two neighborhoods.; The resonance feedback system of a captured PGSFE-3 contains logged bone density profiles from dozens of previous targets — a forensic record of every person the weapon was used on, including several who were reported as natural deaths.

Properties.description:
The PRTD-5 is a close-support targeting and area-denial drone developed by ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS under a joint contract with military medical research divisions. It operates by emitting narrow-band low-frequency acoustic pulses precisely tuned to periosteal resonance frequencies — the vibrational signature of the membrane sheathing bone. At its standard operational distance of 2–6 meters, these pulses produce deep, nauseating ache in weight-bearing joints: knees, hips, ankles, and wrists. The sensation is not structural damage but reads to the nervous system as imminent catastrophic fracture, producing involuntary protective responses including crouching, freezing, and gait collapse.

The PRTD-5 is distinguished from simpler acoustic deterrents by its precision tracking suite. An onboard millimeter-wave radar maps the target's skeletal geometry in real time, allowing the drone to adjust its emission frequency to match individual bone density — thicker cortical bone requires lower frequencies and higher amplitude. This adaptive tuning means the effect is not trivially countered by body armor or padding, which attenuates higher-frequency acoustic weapons but does relatively little against the PRTD-5's deep-penetration range. The drone is roughly the size and shape of a softball, matte gray, and nearly silent in flight.

ACTARUS markets it officially as a non-lethal crowd management tool for use by licensed security contractors. The military variant, designated PRTD-5M, operates at amplitudes that cause genuine microfracture accumulation over extended exposure — a detail absent from the civilian product documentation.
Properties.aliases: Knuckle, The Bone Pointer, PRTD, Rattler
Properties.specifications:
dimensions: 11 cm diameter sphere
weight: 0.62 kg
operational range: 2–6 m standard, 1–3 m PRTD-5M
frequency range: 18–34 Hz adaptive
target acquisition: Millimeter-wave radar, 0.3 s lock time
effect onset: 2–4 seconds post-lock
flight ceiling: 25 m
battery life: 55 minutes continuous operation
noise signature: < 28 dB at 3 m
countermeasures: Acoustic damping exoskeleton underlayer, rated ADA-3 or higher
Properties.tactical_use: Security contractors deploy PRTD-5 units to control movement through checkpoints, suppress crowd rushes, and immobilize fleeing individuals without physical pursuit. In tighter operational contexts — hostage rescue, precision arrest — teams use it to collapse a target's mobility before entry, eliminating the risk of armed resistance during the first seconds of contact. Military units using the 5M variant employ extended loiter patterns over fortified positions, accumulating microfracture damage in defenders over hours of siege.
Properties.cultural_context: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS maintains careful public messaging around the PRTD-5, emphasizing its non-lethal classification and medical research origins. In Meridian 88, it has nonetheless become synonymous with a specific kind of institutional brutality — the kind that leaves no marks. Human rights organizations document its use in labor disputes and protest suppression, where its effects are invisible on post-incident medical scans. The drone's softball-like silhouette has been adopted as an ironic logo by several labor activist groups, printed on shirts alongside the phrase 'non-lethal.'
Properties.story_hooks: A licensed PRTD-5 unit was used during a labor action at an OUROBOROS ENERGY processing facility. Three workers sustained injuries consistent with PRTD-5M exposure — microfracture patterns that shouldn't appear on civilian hardware. Someone swapped the firmware, and ARCTURUS wants it buried.; A PRTD-5 has been loitering above a specific intersection in the market district for six days, tracking and harassing the same elderly shopkeeper. It's licensed to a shell company that dissolved four years ago.; The party is hired to retrieve a PRTD-5M from a military crash site before ARCTURUS' recovery team arrives. The drone is still active, still tracking, and the crash site is not empty.

Properties.description:
The PCR-4 operates by projecting a tightly focused column of oscillating peristaltic pressure waves tuned to the resonant frequency of soft visceral tissue. Unlike blunt trauma weapons that damage through impact, the Constrictor induces rhythmic, involuntary compression cycles in the target's abdominal and thoracic cavities — essentially forcing the body's own musculature to contract violently and out of sequence. At low power, this produces incapacitating nausea, involuntary voiding, and diaphragm spasms that prevent breathing. At full charge, internal organs rupture without any visible external wound.

The weapon was originally developed by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric as a non-lethal crowd suppression tool for use in enclosed transit corridors and arcology common spaces where conventional ballistic discharge was a structural liability. The lethality at upper power registers was considered an acceptable engineering footnote. The emitter array at the barrel's terminus is a concave dish of piezoelectric transducer cells arranged in a Fibonacci spiral, which focuses the wave column to a diameter of roughly 30 centimeters at optimal range.

What makes the PCR-4 distinctively feared is the nature of the wounds it leaves — or rather, doesn't leave. Forensic examination of victims shows no entry wound, no burning, no fracture. Cause of death reads as catastrophic multi-organ failure, consistent with advanced disease. In jurisdictions with overwhelmed forensic infrastructure, Constrictor kills pass unreported as natural causes with disturbing regularity.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 8–40 meters
power source: Zheng-Dao ZD-Cell Type IV (6 shots per cell)
weight: 4.1 kg
length: 71 cm
power settings: Three: Suppress / Incapacitate / Terminate
recharge cycle: 2.2 seconds between shots
emitter array: Fibonacci-spiral piezoelectric dish, 22 cm diameter
acoustic signature: Low subsonic thrum, audible only within 3 meters of operator
Properties.tactical_use: Operators favor the PCR-4 for assassinations requiring deniability, particularly in high-surveillance environments where forensic scrutiny is anticipated. At Suppress setting it is used to break up close-quarters resistance without gunfire noise. Professional contractors specifically request the Terminate setting for high-value political or corporate targets where the death must appear natural. The 40-meter range is considered limiting; most engagements occur within 20 meters.
Properties.cultural_context: The Constrictor carries a specific stigma even among weapons dealers — it is considered a coward's tool, associated with poisoners, assassins-for-hire, and corporate wet-work contractors rather than soldiers or street fighters. Carrying one openly marks you as someone who kills without wanting to be known as a killer. In some underground fighting circuits, being caught with a Constrictor results in permanent exclusion. Paradoxically, it commands a premium price precisely because of this reputation.
Properties.story_hooks: A string of 'natural cause' deaths among city council members all share the same forensic signature — someone has a PCR-4 and a list.; A black market dealer offers the party a Constrictor, but the serial number traces back to a Zheng-Dao internal security locker that was supposedly never manufactured.; A character is accused of a Constrictor killing they didn't commit; someone is framing them using a weapon registered in their name.; Zheng-Dao quietly contracts the party to recover all units from a batch that escaped their supply chain — they're not asking why they want them back.

Nodes.Name: Political fixers operating in arcology governance disputes
Rogue forensic pathologists who resell the weapons alongside falsified autopsy reports

Properties.description:
The Peritoneal Overpressure Detonation Grenade operates by delivering a dense aerosol payload of hygroscopic osmotic agents through a micro-perforated casing breach. Upon detonation, the primary charge ruptures the outer shell and drives the agent cloud transdermally into exposed tissue using a focused hypersonic pressure wave. The agents penetrate the peritoneal cavity lining within 1.8 seconds of initial detonation, triggering catastrophic fluid influx into the abdominal compartment via forced osmotic imbalance.

What distinguishes the PODG-1 from conventional fragmentation ordnance is its near-total absence of shrapnel signature. Targets appear externally unharmed at the blast perimeter, while experiencing acute abdominal compartment syndrome within two to four minutes. The weapon was designed for enclosed urban environments where collateral structural damage is politically undesirable but personnel neutralization is required — a corporate enforcement tool dressed in the language of precision.

On the street, the PODG-1 is called 'Bloater' for the visible abdominal distension that precedes incapacitation. Medics who encounter victims describe a characteristic rigidity and grey pallor that has become grimly recognizable in districts where corporate security contractors operate. There are no visible wounds. There is rarely a survivor.
Properties.aliases: PODG-1, Bloater, The Gut Check, Cavity Round
Properties.specifications:
form factor: Cylindrical grenade, 88mm length, 42mm diameter
weight: 310g
fuse delay: 2.4 seconds (adjustable 1.0–4.0s)
effective radius: 3.5m transdermal delivery cone
lethal radius: 1.8m sustained exposure
agent type: Classified hygroscopic osmogen compound ADS-Peri-7
blast signature: Low yield primary charge, minimal overpressure
secondary effects: Acute abdominal compartment syndrome, diaphragmatic pressure, organ failure within 6–12 minutes untreated
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed in close-quarters enforcement operations, riot suppression of confined crowds, and targeted neutralization where structural integrity of facilities must be preserved. Operators throw or launch the PODG-1 into clustered groups, relying on the delayed onset of symptoms to allow extraction before medical response. Corporate strike teams use it to clear rooms without triggering structural alarms in smart-building systems that monitor explosive overpressure.
Properties.cultural_context: The PODG-1 has become a symbol of corporate deniability warfare in Meridian 88. Because victims show no external trauma, corporate security firms can deny lethal intent — officially classifying the weapon as a 'non-lethal crowd management tool' in internal documentation. Activist medical collectives distribute identification cards to paramedics describing the grey-pallor-rigidity symptom cluster. Carrying a PODG-1 is a signifier of corporate affiliation so strong that street-level operators refuse to touch them, fearing the social contamination.
Properties.story_hooks: A paramedic begins seeing the grey-pallor cluster in victims with no corporate enemy — someone is using PODG-1s against civilians with no clear motive.; A whistleblower inside ARCTURUS has documentation reclassifying the PODG-1 as lethal but the public record still reads non-lethal — they need an extraction.; A player character is framed for a PODG-1 attack they didn't commit; the only evidence is the weapon's chemical signature traced to their safehouse.; A black market lot of PODG-1s surfaces with a corrupted fuse delay — they detonate in under 0.3 seconds, making them lethal to the user.

Persistent Surveillance and Termination Drone PSTD-1 'Shepherd'

Properties.description: The PSTD-1 is a single-target autonomous pursuit drone designed not for immediate lethality but for indefinite surveillance and conditional termination. Roughly the size of a clenched fist, the Shepherd locks onto a biometric profile—gait signature, thermal pattern, or facial geometry—and maintains persistent tracking at distances of up to 1.2 kilometers, hovering at rooftop altitude and transmitting encrypted telemetry to its registered operator. It carries a single-shot linear magnetically accelerated flechette, 4.5mm tungsten-core, capable of killing an unarmored human target at 300 meters. The shot is only fired upon explicit operator command or upon activation of a conditional trigger pre-programmed at deployment.
Properties.aliases: The Eye, Shepherd Dog, Watcher, Leash
Properties.legality: Licensed — conditional termination trigger requires Class-7 Autonomous Lethality Permit; unlocked units Prohibited
Properties.specifications:
dimensions: 112mm x 98mm x 76mm
mass: 340 grams
tracking range: 1.2km (surveillance mode), 300m (termination envelope)
endurance: Up to 72 hours (surveillance mode), 11 hours (active stalk mode)
payload: Single 4.5mm tungsten-core flechette, linear magnetic launch
muzzle velocity: 920 m/s
biometric lock time: 4.2 seconds initial acquisition
re-acquisition after loss: Up to 22 minutes lost contact before profile reset
operator interface: Encrypted short-range telemetry uplink, compatible with standard AR overlays
self-destruct: Thermite core (operator-triggered or tamper-activated)
Properties.tactical_use: Corporate collections agencies and high-end enforcement syndicates use the Shepherd to enforce debt, contract, or territorial compliance without committing personnel. A single operator can manage up to six simultaneously deployed units via AR overlay. Conditional triggers are commonly set to location-based parameters—'fire if target enters District 7' or 'fire if target contacts [named individual]'—making the Shepherd a tool for controlling behavior as much as ending lives. Counter-measures include signal-blocking canopies, thermal masking suits (see: TSI-2 'Cold Case'), and the controversial but effective tactic of feeding the drone a spoofed biometric signature to exhaust its battery on a false target.
Properties.cultural_context: The Shepherd has become a symbol of corporate reach in Meridian 88—the idea that debt and consequence have no geographic limit. ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC's marketing language ('consequence enforcement') has entered common parlance as a euphemism for sanctioned killing, and the phrase 'you've been shepherded' carries a specific, chilling meaning in street vernacular. Among mid-level corporate employees, deployment of a Shepherd against a contractor who failed to deliver is considered a proportionate business response, a normalization that civil rights organizations in the city have repeatedly and unsuccessfully challenged.
Properties.story_hooks: A player character discovers a Shepherd has been tailing them for 11 days. The registered operator is listed as a shell corporation that dissolved 6 days ago. The conditional trigger is unknown—and the drone is still active.; A ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC technician is selling unlocked conditional trigger firmware on the black market. The buyers include at least one person who has already used it. Finding the technician before corporate internal security does is worth a significant payout.; A target the party has been hired to protect is convinced a Shepherd is overhead—but all scans come back negative. Is the paranoia the weapon, or is the drone simply better at hiding than its spec sheet suggests?; The party is offered a job: retrieve a decommissioned Shepherd from a sealed evidence locker at an MMPD substation. The drone inside still has its biometric lock active—and the profile it's locked to belongs to a sitting city councilor.

Properties.description:
The PAN-3 generates a precisely phased acoustic waveform tuned to the resonant frequency of the human vestibulocochlear system — the inner ear structures responsible for both hearing and spatial orientation. Unlike conventional sonic weapons that rely on raw overpressure, the Tinnitus works through resonant coupling: the emitted waveform is calibrated to match and amplify the target's own inner ear fluid dynamics, producing an effect that is neurologically indistinguishable from catastrophic inner ear trauma. Targets experience simultaneous deafness, vertigo, nausea, and — in sustained exposures — permanent damage to the cochlear nerve.

The phasing mechanism is the weapon's key innovation. The PAN-3 uses a forward-facing sensor array to sample ambient sound and the target's own vocalisation or movement noise, then adjusts the emitted waveform in real time to maintain optimal resonant coupling even as conditions change. This makes the weapon significantly more effective than fixed-frequency sonic emitters and allows it to function in noisy environments where broad-spectrum acoustic weapons lose coherence. A secondary 'scatter' mode abandons precision phasing in favour of area suppression, trading neurological targeting for wider coverage.

VANTABLACK MEDIA developed the PAN-3's core phasing technology for audience immersion systems — specifically, for haptic sound environments in their experiential media installations. The weaponised application was developed by ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS under a joint research agreement, a collaboration that VANTABLACK has since publicly distanced itself from while quietly continuing to supply the phasing array components. The weapon's current production status is officially suspended pending a regulatory review that has been pending for six years.
Properties.manufacturer: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS (phasing array components: VANTABLACK MEDIA)
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 2–25 metres (precision mode); 2–12 metres (scatter mode)
waveform adaptation rate: 1,200 adjustments per second
exposure thresholds: Non-lethal (0–3 seconds); Temporary damage (3–15 seconds); Permanent cochlear damage (15+ seconds)
power source: Standard energy cell (90 minutes continuous emission)
weight: 1.6 kg
form factor: Compact emitter with forward sensor ring, resembles a thick-bodied flashlight
mode selector: Precision / Scatter (physical toggle)
countermeasures: Sealed acoustic dampening ear protection provides near-complete immunity; standard ear protection reduces effect by ~60%
Properties.tactical_use: The PAN-3 excels in enclosed spaces where acoustic scatter reinforces the primary beam. Operators use it to disorient and incapacitate targets before entering a room, or to suppress multiple targets simultaneously in scatter mode. In precision mode, it is effective for non-lethal takedowns against unprotected targets — a two-second exposure is sufficient to produce vertigo severe enough to prevent coordinated action. Law enforcement units use it for crowd control and individual apprehension. The weapon's primary vulnerability is its countermeasure profile: any operator who knows they may face a PAN-3 will wear sealed dampening protection, completely neutralising the threat. This makes it most effective as a surprise weapon.
Properties.cultural_context: The Tinnitus has a complicated reputation in Meridian 88. Law enforcement use has made it strongly associated with state-adjacent authority — when civilians see a PAN-3, they assume corporate security or police presence. This association cuts both ways: some operators in grey-area roles carry the weapon specifically to project legitimacy, while others avoid it precisely because it marks them as working for someone official. Among the city's music communities — particularly the underground acoustic performance spaces in the Meridian sub-levels — the weapon is deeply resented. Several prominent performers have suffered permanent hearing damage from PAN-3 exposure during enforcement raids, and the instrument has become a symbol of cultural suppression.
Properties.story_hooks: A beloved underground musician has been left with permanent hearing damage after a raid on a performance space. Evidence suggests the PAN-3 used was deliberately set to maximum exposure — this was not crowd control, it was targeted. The players are hired to find out who gave the order.; VANTABLACK MEDIA is being blackmailed by someone with documentation of their phasing array supply agreement with ARCTURUS. They want the documentation retrieved without it becoming public. The blackmailer has made copies.; A PAN-3 has been modified to operate at a frequency that targets neural tissue rather than the inner ear — a prototype that produces seizures rather than vertigo. Someone has been field-testing it in the transit tunnels. The victims look like they died of natural causes.; The players discover that a particular district's 'noise ordinance enforcement' program has been using PAN-3s on residential areas — not for crowd control, but to make specific blocks uninhabitable, clearing them for a development project.

Properties.description:
The PNSD-1 delivers calibrated pulses of high-intensity visible and near-ultraviolet light designed to overwhelm and temporarily damage the photoreceptor cells of biological eyes while simultaneously triggering a cascade of involuntary neurological responses through the optic nerve. Unlike conventional flashbang devices, the PNSD-1 is a directed weapon — its output is focused into a 15-degree cone, allowing targeted application against specific individuals or small groups without affecting the operator's own visual field. The pulse sequence is not a single flash but a precisely timed series of strobes at frequencies known to trigger involuntary muscular responses, disorientation, and in subjects with certain neural augmentations, partial seizure activity.

Helix Biosystems designed the PNSD-1 originally as a medical research tool for studying photosensitive neurological responses, a fact the company leverages in its public communications to distance itself from the weapon's current applications. The military adaptation came through a licensing arrangement with Arcturus Defense Solutions, which refined the pulse sequencing algorithm to maximize neurological disruption while maintaining technical deniability as a non-lethal system. In practice, subjects with optical augments — which represent a significant portion of the Meridian 88 population — experience substantially more severe effects, as the weapon's frequencies interact destructively with common retinal implant protocols.

The PNSD-1 is compact enough to be handheld, resembling a high-powered flashlight with an integrated power cell. Its unassuming profile has made it popular in environments where carrying visible weapons is socially or legally complicated. It produces no audible discharge and no visible beam in ambient light conditions — the target simply drops. The psychological effect on witnesses is often more disabling than the weapon itself.
Properties.specifications:
length: 28cm
weight: 0.6kg
power source: Helix HB-3 compact cell, 80 pulse sequences per charge
beam cone: 15 degrees
effective range: 0–25m (full effect), 25–60m (partial effect)
pulse frequency range: 8–65 Hz variable sequence
effect on unaugmented targets: Temporary blindness (3–18 minutes), disorientation, nausea, involuntary muscle response
effect on optically augmented targets: Retinal implant feedback loop, potential implant shutdown, extended blindness (30 minutes to permanent in rare cases)
operator protection: Integrated polarizing filter over emitter; operator must not look directly at target during pulse
Properties.tactical_use: The PNSD-1 is used primarily in close-quarters operations where silence and discretion are priorities. A single pulse sequence incapacitates a target for long enough to allow restraint, extraction, or termination. Against augmented targets, operators are trained to exploit the implant feedback vulnerability by activating the weapon at distances under 10 meters, where the pulse intensity is sufficient to trigger the full feedback loop. Corporate intelligence operatives favor the PNSD-1 for snatch operations — a target can be neutralized in a crowded public space without witnesses understanding what happened. The weapon's main limitation is its cone width, which requires reasonably accurate aim, and the operator's own need to avoid direct eye contact with the emitter during discharge.
Properties.cultural_context: The PNSD-1 occupies an unsettling niche in Meridian 88's weapon culture because its effects on augmented individuals are disproportionate and occasionally permanent — which the manufacturer's legal team has successfully argued is a pre-existing vulnerability in the implant, not a weapon defect. This argument has been the subject of significant controversy in districts with high augmentation rates, where the weapon is seen as implicitly discriminatory. Among intelligence operatives and corporate kidnapping specialists, it is considered an elegant tool. Among street communities with high augmentation rates, it is considered a targeted threat, and there are documented cases of violent retaliation against individuals found carrying PNSD-1 units.
Properties.story_hooks: A rash of 'unexplained collapses' in a high-augmentation district are being written off as implant malfunctions. A local fixer suspects PNSD-1 use — someone is systematically blinding specific augmented individuals, and the pattern of targets suggests a list.; Helix Biosystems is facing a class action from individuals permanently blinded by PNSD-1 interactions with their retinal implants. The plaintiffs need someone to extract internal documentation proving the company knew about the vulnerability before licensing the weapon.; A player character with optical augments is targeted with a PNSD-1 and survives with partial damage to their implant. Tracing the weapon back to its source leads somewhere unexpected — not a corporate operative, but someone from their own past.

Nodes.Name: Opportunistic black market buyers exploiting augmented populations

Properties.description:
The Photonic Pressure Cannon generates an intensely focused beam of coherent light in the near-ultraviolet spectrum, but its primary mechanism of harm is not thermal — it is mechanical. By rapidly pulsing the beam at frequencies between 800 and 1200 pulses per second, the PPC-2 creates a phenomenon called laser-induced plasma pressure: each pulse ionizes a thin layer of surface material, and the explosive expansion of that plasma generates a localized pressure wave equivalent to a repeated physical impact. Against unarmored targets, this produces deep subcutaneous bruising, ruptured capillaries, and in sustained exposure, structural damage to underlying bone. Against light armor, it can cause spallation of inner surfaces.

ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS developed the PPC-2 as a crowd-control alternative to kinetic impact rounds, marketing it to municipal contracts across the Meridian 88 administrative zones. The pitch was that it left no ballistic evidence and produced 'compliance injuries' rather than lethality. Field deployment rapidly disproved the lethality claim — sustained bursts to the torso have proven fatal in multiple documented incidents, and the weapon's reputation for 'clean' crowd suppression collapsed within two seasons of its municipal rollout.

The weapon is recognizable by the distinctive purple-white glow of its emitter array and the sharp cracking sound each pulse makes — not unlike rapid applause at close range. Targets who have survived describe the sensation as being hit repeatedly by an invisible fist that somehow leaves no visible entry point. Forensic physicians in the free clinics have taken to calling the characteristic injury pattern 'Arcturus bruising.'
Properties.aliases: Sunburn, The Bleacher, White Hammer, PPC
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 40m (pressure effect), 80m (thermal/flash effect only)
pulse rate: 800–1200 Hz (adjustable)
power source: ARCTURUS Photon Pack AP-3 (20-second continuous burst capacity)
weight: 4.7 kg
length: 72 cm
emitter array: 7-element near-UV coherent array
cooling system: Passive radiative fins with thermal cutoff at 340°C
burst modes: Single pulse, Sustained beam, Area scatter (experimental)
Properties.tactical_use: Municipal units use the PPC-2 for dispersal operations, typically sweeping the beam across crowds in short bursts to drive movement without (officially) causing lethal injury. Military and black-market operators have discovered that sustained torso exposure at high pulse rates is reliably fatal within 8–12 seconds, making it effective for executions that resist standard forensic classification. The weapon's lack of projectile evidence and unusual injury pattern make it attractive to operators who need kills that don't look like kills.
Properties.cultural_context: The PPC-2 is deeply associated with municipal overreach in the political consciousness of Meridian 88's lower districts. Protest movements have adopted stylized imagery of the weapon's purple glow as a symbol of institutional violence. Several prominent activists bear 'Arcturus bruising' scars they display publicly. Conversely, in upper-tier corporate enclaves, the weapon is seen as a responsible alternative to lethal force — a perception that ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS continues to aggressively cultivate despite the mounting injury record.
Properties.story_hooks: A municipal officer's PPC-2 was used in a fatal crowd suppression event. The weapon's serial number traces back to a unit that was officially decommissioned two years ago. Someone is running a ghost inventory.; A forensic physician at a free clinic has quietly documented 34 deaths with Arcturus bruising patterns over 18 months. She's been offered significant money to lose her records. She hasn't decided yet.; ARCTURUS is lobbying to have the PPC-2's injury classification changed from 'potentially lethal' to 'compliance instrument.' They've already secured three council votes. Two more and the municipal contracts expand city-wide.; A resistance cell has acquired a crate of PPC-2 units and is debating whether to use them, destroy them, or make their existence public. They've asked a fixer to broker the decision.

Properties.description:
The PPLE-3 generates an articulated filament of coherent photonic energy sustained by a series of rapidly pulsed micro-lens arrays along a flexible 2.4-meter emitter spine. Unlike rigid beam weapons, the PPLE-3's filament can be directed through physical manipulation of the emitter spine itself, behaving operationally more like a whip or flail than a conventional directed-energy weapon. The photonic filament carries sufficient energy density to cut through unarmored tissue and light materials on contact, while the pulsing frequency creates a secondary pressure wave along the contact surface that disrupts electronics and causes localized electromagnetic interference.

The weapon's defining characteristic is its behavior at the terminal end of the filament. The photonic strand is not uniformly energized — it is densest at the tip, where pulse cycling creates a region of peak photonic pressure approximately 4mm in diameter. This tip delivers a concentrated cutting and burning effect while the rest of the filament causes lesser thermal and pressure damage along its length. Experienced operators exploit this property to deliver precise terminal strikes while using the filament body for area suppression — a combination that requires significant training to master but creates an attack profile that is exceptionally difficult to predict or block.

The PPLE-3 was developed by Tessera Corponation's advanced tools division, initially framed as a precision materials-cutting instrument for industrial applications. Several legitimate industrial models remain in circulation, but the combat-optimized variant features a higher pulse density, a reinforced emitter spine with ergonomic grip nodes, and a secondary frequency mode that shifts the filament's energy profile toward the electromagnetic disruption end of its spectrum — effective against cybernetic systems — rather than the thermal cutting end.
Properties.aliases: Needlepoint, The Lacemaker, Photon Whip, Lightwork
Properties.specifications:
filament length: 2.4 meters (active); emitter spine 0.9 meters
tip energy density: Peak 4mm focal point, 800W/cm² equivalent
filament body effect: Thermal burn and EM disruption along contact length
frequency modes: Thermal-dominant (T-mode) / EM-disruption-dominant (E-mode)
power source: Photonic resonance cell, continuous use 8 minutes per cell
weight: 2.3 kg
operator skill requirement: High — filament control requires dedicated training
dimensions: Emitter spine: 90cm; compact storage: 34cm coiled
Properties.tactical_use: Close-quarters specialists use the PPLE-3 as an active defense and area-denial tool, using the filament body to force opponents to maintain distance while delivering precise terminal strikes to specific targets. In E-mode, operators sweep the filament across cybernetic-heavy opponents to induce system disruptions before closing. The weapon's unpredictable arc makes it extremely difficult to block or dodge in tight spaces. Some operators use the filament to manipulate objects at range — cutting cables, triggering switches — giving it utility beyond direct combat.
Properties.cultural_context: The PPLE-3 has developed a strong aesthetic identity in Meridian 88's underground performance and combat exhibition scenes. The photonic filament produces a visually striking effect — a bright, articulated line of light that leaves afterimage trails in low-light environments — making it popular in staged combat exhibitions and as a status display among those who can demonstrate the skill to wield it. Carrying a Needlepoint and using it well is considered a mark of serious training and discipline. Poorly trained users who pick one up typically injure themselves within minutes, which has filtered the weapon's user base toward the genuinely skilled.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of clean, precise cuts found on victims in an otherwise messy crime scene suggest a PPLE-3 operator. The cuts are surgical — targeting specific cybernetic components rather than causing broad injury. Someone is harvesting augmentations without killing the hosts, but the hosts are dying anyway from secondary complications.; A Tessera Corponation industrial division manager requests help recovering a stolen shipment of PPLE-3 emitter spines. He insists they are industrial units. The serial numbers, when checked, correspond to a combat-variant production run that Tessera officially denies exists.; A player is challenged to a sanctioned duel in an underground exhibition venue. Their opponent uses a Needlepoint with evident mastery. The duel is supposed to be non-lethal. The opponent doesn't seem to know that.; The players need to cut through a photonic-shielded vault door. Someone suggests that a PPLE-3 in E-mode, held against the shielding long enough, might disrupt the frequency lock. It will take approximately 90 seconds of sustained contact. In a guarded facility.

Properties.description:
The Photonic Stress Fracture Pistol PSFP-3 operates on the principle of photoinduced thermal stress — it fires a rapid-pulse infrared laser that heats the surface of a target material faster than the underlying structure can dissipate the energy, creating a steep thermal gradient that induces mechanical fracture along the material's weakest internal lines. Against inorganic targets such as ceramics, composites, and hardened cyberware housing, this produces catastrophic surface cracking and structural failure. Against biological tissue, the effect is a deep, clean laceration as surface cells flash-expand and rupture in a line determined by the beam path.

Helix Biosystems developed the PSFP-3 as a surgical tool before its obvious weapons applications were licensed to civilian security markets. The 'Cleaver' designation emerged from field use — unlike burn weapons, it doesn't char or cauterize, it simply splits. The beam pulse duration is short enough that coagulation is minimal, meaning wounds bleed freely and healing is complicated. Surgeons who work in Meridian 88's trauma wards have a particular hatred for it. The weapon leaves entry wounds that look almost decorative in their precision, which has made it a calling card for certain operators who want their work recognized.

The PSFP-3's distinctive aesthetic is a narrow, matte-black frame with a deep violet indicator light that pulses once before each shot — a safety feature from its surgical origins that became impossible to remove without voiding the power regulation system. Experienced targets have learned to treat that violet pulse as a last warning. In enclosed spaces, the weapon produces a faint crackling sound as materials fracture, which some operators find deeply satisfying and others find unbearable.
Properties.aliases: Cleaver, The Splitter, Glass Gun, Fracture Piece
Properties.legality: Licensed — medical and security use; Restricted — general civilian
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 2–30 meters
beam pulse duration: 0.8 milliseconds per shot
thermal gradient output: 420°C surface differential per pulse
power source: Compact photonic cell, 60 shots per charge
weight: 0.9 kg
anti-materiel rating: Grade 3 ceramic and composite surfaces
biological wound profile: Clean laceration, minimal cauterization, high bleed rate
form factor: Compact sidearm, single-hand operation
Properties.tactical_use: Used in close- to mid-range engagements where precision is prioritized over area effect. Effective against armored targets by targeting joint seams and sensor housings rather than armored faces directly — the fracture propagates along stress lines the operator cannot see but the weapon's targeting assist estimates from surface geometry. In anti-personnel use, operators favor torso and limb shots that maximize blood loss over immediately incapacitating head shots, creating sustained pressure on medical support resources. Often used as a secondary weapon by operators who prefer to disable before finishing.
Properties.cultural_context: The PSFP-3 occupies an uncomfortable space in Meridian 88's weapons culture — it was born in a hospital and carries that clinical precision into violence. Carrying one marks a person as either medically trained, deeply methodical, or both. In the city's underground surgery community, it's both despised and respected: despised because the wounds it creates are difficult and expensive to repair, respected because using one requires genuine understanding of material and biological structure. Some high-end assassins use it specifically because the wounds it leaves are attributed to surgical skill, implying a message beyond the act of killing.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of murders in the medical district have been committed with a PSFP-3 calibrated to replicate botched surgical complications — someone is killing people and making it look like malpractice.; A stolen shipment of PSFP-3s with modified pulse durations that prevent any wound coagulation at all has made it onto the market — the modifications are signed with a HELIX internal engineer's credentials.; A player character is hired to recover a PSFP-3 used in a high-profile killing, but the weapon has been modified to record biometric data on every target it wounds — a database of victims that someone very powerful wants buried.; A street medic has begun using a PSFP-3 for emergency field surgery in the lower districts — technically illegal but saving lives — and the licensing authority wants them arrested while the community wants them protected.
