Properties.description:
The PCR-3 operates on an unusual energy principle: rather than generating its own destructive output, it catalyzes a photovoltaic cascade reaction in surfaces it strikes. A precisely modulated ultraviolet primer beam is fired first, lasting approximately 12 milliseconds, which seeds the target surface with a resonant photoelectric charge. A second, high-intensity visible-spectrum pulse follows immediately, triggering an explosive release of that stored charge across the target's surface area. The result is a directed electrical detonation that originates from the target itself rather than the weapon — armor and shielding that would normally absorb or deflect an incoming energy beam instead become the source of the discharge.

Helix Biosystems developed the PCR-3 as part of a research program into photovoltaic energy harvesting, and the weapon represents a militarized accident — a researcher demonstrated that the cascade reaction could be induced in organic tissue, which has its own weak photovoltaic properties due to melanin and porphyrin compounds in skin and muscle. On living targets, the electrical detonation produces severe burns and cardiac disruption from the inside out. On synthetic materials — particularly the photoreactive polymers used in common body armor — the effect is even more dramatic, causing catastrophic structural failure of the armor itself.

The Tithe's form is elegant and slender, a long-barreled rifle with a dual-emitter muzzle that houses both the UV primer and the visible-spectrum trigger. The barrel is unusually cool to the touch even after sustained use, as the weapon itself generates relatively little waste heat — the energy is deposited in the target. This gives the PCR-3 a deceptively benign appearance that has made it a favorite of collectors and a headache for customs enforcement.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: Up to 340m
primer beam duration: 12ms UV pulse
trigger pulse: High-intensity visible spectrum, 580–620nm
cascade reaction delay: ~3ms between primer and trigger
power cell: Helix HL-12 dual-channel cell, 18 complete shot pairs
weight: 5.2kg
dimensions: 112cm length
anti-armor performance: Exceptional against photoreactive polymer armor; moderate against ceramic plate
thermal signature: Very low
Properties.tactical_use: The PCR-3 excels at long-range anti-personnel and anti-armor engagements where the target's own materials are weaponized against them. Operators are trained to identify armor composition before engaging — the weapon is most effective against modern photoreactive composite armors and least effective against old-fashioned ceramic or metal plate. The low thermal signature and absence of a visible beam (the UV primer is invisible, the trigger pulse brief) makes the Tithe an excellent ambush weapon at range. Licensed military snipers use it for anti-material work when they need to deny an enemy position's equipment.
Properties.cultural_context: The PCR-3's licensing requirement and high price point make it a weapon of elite military and paramilitary units. In Meridian 88, possessing a licensed Tithe is a mark of institutional legitimacy — it signals that the carrier has the corporate or governmental backing to navigate the licensing bureaucracy. Unlicensed copies occasionally surface on the black market, but the dual-emitter calibration is difficult to replicate, and bootleg versions frequently misfire, seeding the operator with the cascade charge instead of the target. Stories of bootleg Tithe accidents — operators detonating their own armor — are common enough to have become cautionary urban legend.
Properties.story_hooks: A licensed PCR-3 is recovered from a civilian massacre. The license traces to a corporate security division that officially disbanded two years ago — but the license was renewed last month by someone with deep system access.; A street-level arms dealer is selling what they claim are PCR-3s at a fraction of market price. Three buyers have already been hospitalized with inside-out burn injuries. The dealer doesn't know the units are miscalibrated — or does they?; Helix Biosystems is quietly recalling a specific production batch of PCR-3s, citing 'calibration variance.' The real reason: a flaw in that batch makes the primer beam interact with a specific neural implant brand, seeding the implant with a cascade charge that can be remotely triggered.

Properties.description: The PHE-3 operates by concentrating a narrow-band photovoltaic excitation beam tuned to the near-infrared absorption spectrum of hemoglobin and subcutaneous capillary tissue. On contact, the beam induces rapid localized vasodilation followed by catastrophic microvascular rupture beneath the skin's surface — a process that leaves no visible external wound for several seconds before hemorrhagic bruising blooms outward. The weapon draws on photonic resonance cycling technology developed by Arcturus Defense Solutions for orbital solar relay systems, miniaturized into a carbine-length chassis.
Properties.aliases: Sunburn, The Cooker, Solaris Stick, Redline
Properties.specifications:
length: 68 cm
weight: 3.1 kg
power source: Dual photovoltaic capacitor cell (ADS-PV9)
effective range: 8–120 m
beam wavelength: 780–850 nm NIR band
charge time: 1.4 seconds per pulse
shots per cell: 22 full-charge pulses
cooling system: Passive ceramic heat sink with gel-phase dissipation fins
Properties.tactical_use: Operators favor the PHE-3 for its delayed wound presentation — targets often continue moving for 4–8 seconds before systemic blood pressure drop incapacitates them, creating confusion among allied personnel. It is used in crowd infiltration scenarios where a clean, invisible first strike is needed before breaking contact. The weapon's lack of visible beam in standard lighting conditions and near-silent discharge make it effective for close-protection ambushes. Experienced operators layer pulses on a single target to accelerate hemorrhagic cascade rather than spreading fire.
Properties.cultural_context: The PHE-3 carries a deeply unsettling reputation in Meridian 88's underground medical community — trauma surgeons at off-grid clinics have named the wound pattern 'sunburn syndrome' due to the characteristic deep bruising that appears hours after death. Street enforcers who carry it are considered especially cruel, as the weapon's delayed effect means victims often don't know they've been hit. Corporate wetwork teams prize it precisely because autopsies frequently misattribute cause of death to natural cardiovascular failure. Ownership is a marker of either serious institutional backing or dangerous black-market connections.
Properties.story_hooks: A string of deaths ruled cardiac arrest are revealed to share the PHE-3's wound signature — someone is running a quiet purge, and the only lead is a black-market parts supplier in the Fen District.; A player character is hit by a PHE-3 pulse during a firefight and doesn't realize it until they collapse twenty minutes later — they have hours to find treatment before internal hemorrhage becomes fatal.; An Arcturus Defense Solutions whistleblower claims the PHE-3's targeting algorithm was calibrated using non-consenting human subjects from a Lazarus Pharmaceuticals clinical program.; A stolen shipment of PHE-3 units surfaces in the hands of a radical anti-corporate cell — they're planning something public, something that will look like a mass medical event.

Properties.description:
The PFP-7 fires a sub-caliber dart tipped with a dense array of piezoelectric crystal elements that, upon impact with a hard surface, generate a precisely timed voltage cascade. This cascade is not intended to harm through electrical discharge — the voltage is too low and too brief for that — but rather to exploit a target material's own structural resonance. The timing of the piezoelectric pulse is tuned to the natural frequency of common construction and armor materials, inducing micro-fractures that propagate outward from the impact point in characteristic spider-web patterns. A single dart will not destroy a reinforced door; three darts placed in a triangular pattern at the correct spacing will cause it to fail catastrophically under its own next load cycle.

Helix Biosystems originally developed the piezoelectric cascade array for non-destructive testing of bone density in their orthopedic implant program — the same resonance-frequency principle used to assess structural integrity without breaking the material was, their weapons division noted, equally applicable to breaking it deliberately. The PFP-7 is the result of that pivot, a compact sidearm that looks deceptively like a low-powered dart pistol and is frequently misidentified as a tranquilizer weapon on first inspection. The dart body is inert and non-toxic; the danger is entirely in what happens to the structure it hits.

Operators familiar with materials science can use the Hairline with extraordinary precision — pre-fracturing a vehicle chassis before a collision, weakening a support column before detonation, or, in the weapon's most disturbing documented application, pre-fracturing bone through light armor before engaging with conventional weapons. The latter use is the primary reason for its restricted classification, as it produces injuries that appear consistent with conventional trauma while concealing a premeditated structural attack.
Properties.legality: Restricted — dual-use classification, licensed for structural engineering; prohibited for anti-personnel piezoelectric application
Properties.specifications:
projectile: 4mm sub-caliber piezoelectric crystal-array dart
propulsion: Compressed gas, low-noise discharge
effective range: 40m accurate dart placement
piezo pulse timing: Adjustable 0.1–2.4 millisecond delay post-impact
frequency profiles: 12 pre-loaded material profiles (concrete, steel, composite armor, ceramic, bone, glass, etc.); custom profile upload via port
power source: Helix HB-2 capacitor cell, 60 darts per charge
weight: 0.9 kg
magazine: 20-dart rotary cassette
integrated systems: Material profile selector dial, pulse-timing display, structural resonance scanner (optional rail attachment)
Properties.tactical_use: The Hairline rewards patience and technical knowledge over aggression. Entry teams use it to pre-weaken barriers before breaching, reducing the force and noise required for the breach itself. Saboteurs favor it for infrastructure attacks — a correctly placed sequence of darts can cause a load-bearing element to fail hours or days later under normal operational stress, providing the operator extensive deniability. In direct combat it is rarely used as a primary weapon; operators who employ it against personnel typically use it in conjunction with a follow-up arm, pre-fracturing armor or limbs before engaging with conventional rounds. The weapon's low noise signature makes it viable for quiet operations where suppressed firearms would still produce detectable sound.
Properties.cultural_context: Among engineers and construction workers in Meridian 88, the PFP-7 is a known and semi-legitimate tool — PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION licensed variants are used routinely in controlled demolition and structural assessment. The street version carries a much darker reputation. The weapon's association with slow, deniable structural failures has given it currency in the corporate sabotage market, and several high-profile building collapses in the Meridian 88 industrial district have been retroactively attributed to Hairline attacks after fracture-pattern analysis. It is also quietly feared in medical circles, as the anti-personnel bone-fracture application produces injuries indistinguishable from accidental trauma on standard imaging.
Properties.story_hooks: Three workers are hospitalized with identical compound fracture patterns following a 'workplace accident' at a Palladian Construction site — a materials engineer recognizes the fracture propagation as PFP-7 work and brings the finding to a fixer before it can be buried.; A licensed Palladian demolition team reports their PFP-7 units were stolen during a job — but the theft was reported a week after the job completed, and the timeline doesn't add up.; A Helix Biosystems researcher is selling custom frequency profiles for the PFP-7 on the dark market — one of the profiles is calibrated for a specific alloy used exclusively in a new generation of ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS body armor.; A city infrastructure inspector discovers hairline fracture patterns on a critical transit bridge's support pylons — the patterns are consistent with PFP-7 pre-fracturing, and the bridge carries 40,000 people per day.

Properties.description:
The PSP-2 uses a piezoelectric pressure chamber to accelerate irregular ceramic-composite shot — colloquially called 'gravel' — through a flared, ported barrel at velocities sufficient to cause severe soft tissue trauma at close range. Unlike conventional propellant-driven scatter weapons, the PSP-2 generates its launch impulse by compressing a stack of lead zirconate titanate crystals through a pneumatic ram driven by a small compressed-gas reservoir. The result is a sharp, high-pressure wave behind a 12-gram load of jagged ceramic pellets, each roughly 4-6mm across and shaped irregularly to maximize tumbling and tissue disruption on impact.

The weapon's defining characteristic is its near-zero electromagnetic signature. The piezoelectric firing mechanism generates no radio frequency emissions, no electrical arc, and no magnetic field detectable by standard security scanners. The ceramic shot is likewise invisible to ferromagnetic detection systems. This makes the PSP-2 exceptionally difficult to detect with the building-security scanner arrays common in mid-tier arcology commercial zones, and has earned it a quiet, persistent presence in spaces where conventional firearms cannot go. The gas reservoir — which looks identical to a standard asthma inhaler canister — provides approximately 8 shots before requiring replacement.

The PSP-2 is manufactured by ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS under a 'less-lethal research' designation, a legal fiction that has persisted because the weapon's lethality at under 4 meters is genuinely inconsistent — it maims reliably, kills only sometimes. At longer ranges it is primarily an incapacitant, shredding exposed skin and eyes without reliably penetrating clothing. This ambiguous lethality has kept it in a legal gray zone, sold openly in several Meridian 88 districts as a 'personal safety device' while remaining functionally a close-quarters weapon capable of ending confrontations permanently.
Properties.aliases: Gravel, The Dentist, Scatter Gun, PSP-2, Stone Thrower
Properties.specifications:
caliber: 12g irregular ceramic composite shot load
feed system: Single-shot break-action, manual reload from 8-round speed strip
shots per reservoir: 8 (standard 45mL compressed CO2 canister)
effective range: 1-4m (lethal potential), 4-15m (incapacitant)
muzzle energy: ~380 J per shot at chamber
weight: 0.6 kg unloaded
dimensions: 185mm length, 110mm height
scanner signature: Non-ferromagnetic, zero RF emission
operating temperature: -5°C to +50°C (reservoir pressure-sensitive)
Properties.tactical_use: The PSP-2 is used almost exclusively as a concealed last-resort weapon in environments with strict security screening. Operators bring it into corporate lobbies, transit hubs, and private event security perimeters where conventional firearms cannot pass. At close range it is deployed against unarmored targets — the irregular shot pattern makes it effective against multiple adjacent targets in very tight spaces like elevator cars or stairwells. Experienced operators aim for the face and throat at close range to maximize incapacitation. The single-shot break-action design requires deliberate reloading, meaning most carriers treat it as a one-shot solution and have a secondary weapon for follow-up.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88, the 'Gravel' has a specific cultural meaning: it is the weapon of people who are not supposed to be armed but are. Fixers carry them to client meetings. Journalists bring them to interviews with dangerous sources. Mid-level corporate employees carry them to office parties where they don't trust their colleagues. The weapon's association with environments where weapons are forbidden gives it a slightly paranoid, defensive connotation — carrying a PSP-2 is understood as a statement that you expect to be betrayed in a place that was supposed to be safe. It is rarely flaunted and almost never discussed openly. When one appears at a crime scene, investigators know the shooter was trying to get somewhere they shouldn't have been.
Properties.story_hooks: A PSP-2 was used to kill a TESSERA executive at a company gala — security footage shows no weapons entering the building, and someone is very interested in making sure that question stays unanswered; ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS is lobbying to reclassify the PSP-2 as a medical device to avoid new firearms regulations, and the lobbyist needs someone to make the opposition go quiet; A player finds a PSP-2 gas canister that has been modified to carry something other than CO2 — the chemical residue is from LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS; The Meridian 88 Transit Authority has quietly upgraded scanner arrays to detect piezoelectric mechanisms, and someone is selling advance warning of scanner locations to PSP-2 carriers

Properties.description:
The PSDG-2 is a contact weapon built around a lattice of synthetic piezoelectric crystal arrays embedded in a rigid gauntlet chassis. On impact, the kinetic energy of a strike is harvested and instantaneously converted into a precisely shaped electrical discharge delivered through conductive fingertip contacts. The discharge is not designed to cause cardiac disruption or burns — it is tuned to the frequency band associated with motor cortex signal propagation, creating a transient desynchronization of voluntary muscle control in the struck region. A blow to the shoulder renders the arm temporarily useless. A strike to the base of the skull produces full-body motor collapse for between four and twenty seconds depending on neural density.

The engineering challenge that Arcturus Defense Solutions spent eleven years solving was achieving consistent piezoelectric output across variable impact force. A glancing blow and a full-force punch needed to produce the same targeted discharge profile, or the weapon's selectivity would be meaningless. The solution was a tiered compression array that buffers excess energy into a capacitor bank and supplements insufficient strikes from reserve, meaning the PSDG-2 delivers identical neurological effect regardless of how hard the operator hits. This made it immediately attractive to operators who lack the physical augmentation typical of close-quarters specialists.

The nickname 'The Politeness' reflects the weapon's peculiar social niche: it is used extensively by corporate security personnel in environments where lethal force would be legally and reputationally catastrophic. A struck individual appears to simply stumble and fall, with no visible wound. The name 'Stutter' comes from the characteristic involuntary muscle tremor that affects targets in the recovery phase, which experienced observers recognize immediately.
Properties.specifications:
discharge frequency: Tuned to 40-80 Hz motor signal band
motor collapse duration: 4-20 seconds depending on target neurology
capacitor reserve: 12 fully buffered strikes before recharge
recharge time: 8 minutes passive / 90 seconds via dock
weight: 1.1 kg
coverage: Full hand and wrist to mid-forearm
compatibility: Requires neural handshake with operator's dermal interface for activation
Properties.tactical_use: Primarily used in escort, detention, and close-protection roles. Operators favor it for subduing targets without producing evidence of assault — the neurological disruption leaves no bruising or burns and resolves completely. In combat, it is paired with conventional restraint tools; the gauntlet drops the target, and the operator secures them before motor function returns. Experienced users learn to target specific nerve clusters to achieve selective disruption — a precise strike to the radial nerve cluster disarms without dropping, useful when a standing, cooperative subject is needed.
Properties.cultural_context: The PSDG-2 occupies an uncomfortable middle ground in Meridian 88's legal landscape. Its license requirements are achievable by corporate security entities but deliberately out of reach for individuals, which means it has become a class marker — a signal that the person wearing it has institutional backing. On the street, it is sometimes called 'the corporate handshake.' Among civil liberties groups, it has become a symbol of plausibly deniable abuse, since victims often cannot prove they were struck. A small counter-culture has emerged around documenting the characteristic recovery tremor on video as evidence.
Properties.story_hooks: A prominent labor organizer is found dead — officially from a fall, but the autopsy shows the neural disruption pattern consistent with a PSDG-2 strike to the brainstem, which should not have been lethal unless the discharge was deliberately overcharged.; A PSDG-2 surfaces on the black market with its neural handshake still active, locked to the biometric of a corporate security officer who was officially reported dead six months ago.; An operator is hired to retrieve a witness who was 'questioned' with a PSDG-2 and now has persistent motor disruption — either the weapon was defective or it was used far beyond spec.; Arcturus Defense Solutions quietly initiates a field recall, citing a 'firmware irregularity' — but the irregularity in question causes the capacitor to discharge into the operator's hand rather than the target.

Properties.description:
The PIW-4 operates by sustaining a magnetically confined filament of superheated plasma approximately 1.8 meters in length, generated from a compressed argon-xenon gas cartridge ionized through a focused microwave emitter housed in the grip assembly. The filament is kept coherent by a series of pulsed toroidal magnetic fields projected along an articulated graphene spine, giving the weapon the appearance and handling characteristics of a conventional whip while delivering contact temperatures exceeding 4,000 Kelvin at the tip.

What distinguishes the PIW-4 from comparable plasma-contact weapons is its variable confinement mode. Operators can tighten the magnetic field to produce a precise cutting edge capable of parting armor plating, or loosen it to create a diffuse thermal bloom that stuns and scorches across a wider surface area. The transition between modes takes approximately 0.3 seconds, requiring trained muscle memory to exploit in dynamic close-quarters situations.

Manufactured under a defense licensing agreement between ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS and a Meridian 88 theater arts collective turned weapons boutique known as the Silhouette House, the PIW-4 carries an unusual cultural dual identity. Its elegant form factor made it a status weapon among high-tier performers and arena fighters before military interest drove up both price and notoriety.
Properties.manufacturer: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS (licensed through Silhouette House Fabrication)
Properties.specifications:
length collapsed: 28 cm
filament length: 1.8 m (operational)
plasma temperature tip: 3,800–4,200 K
power source: Argon-xenon cartridge (12 charges) + integrated capacitor cell
field modes: Tight-cut / Diffuse-bloom
mode switch time: ~0.3 seconds
weight: 1.1 kg
effective range: Contact to 2.1 m
armor penetration: Class III ballistic plate (tight-cut mode)
Properties.tactical_use: Primarily employed in corridor and room-clearance scenarios where rifle-length weapons become liabilities. Operators use tight-cut mode to defeat armor and hardened barriers, then switch to diffuse-bloom to suppress grouped soft targets. The PIW-4 rewards aggressive, mobile fighters who can close distance rapidly. Some specialists wrap the spine around limbs or fixtures to control positioning, using the weapon's reach as a grappling aid before activating the filament.
Properties.cultural_context: The PIW-4 occupies a strange social niche in Meridian 88. Arena circuit fighters adopted it first, drawn to the theatrics of a glowing plasma lash, and it became shorthand for a certain kind of dangerous elegance — wealth combined with genuine lethality. Upper-tier fixers carry them as deliberate statements. Military adoption by ARCTURUS special operations units later lent the weapon a harder reputation, but the aesthetic origin never quite washed out. Owning a Threadbare signals that you can afford something beautiful and are willing to use it.
Properties.story_hooks: A stolen PIW-4 serial number traces back to an ARCTURUS black-site operation that officially never happened — someone is killing witnesses.; The Silhouette House is offering a custom PIW-4 as prize in an underground arena tournament, but the weapon is rigged with a kill-switch tied to a corporate extortion scheme.; A player character finds a PIW-4 with a cracked confinement spine — it works, but the field destabilizes unpredictably, making every use a gamble.; An ARCTURUS quartermaster is quietly selling PIW-4 units to a faction the corporation publicly opposes, and the players are hired to find the leak.

Properties.description:
The PCBC-3 functions by explosively rupturing a double-walled internal canister containing liquefied cryogenic compound held at approximately -196°C under significant pressure. The detonation is not primarily chemical — the explosive charge is minimal, serving only to rupture the canister and propel the cryogenic agent outward in a radial burst. The liquid compound flash-vaporizes on contact with ambient air, creating a localized temperature drop of 80–120°C within the dispersal radius in under 0.4 seconds. Materials and tissues within the primary zone experience extreme thermal shock: metals become brittle, polymers shatter, biological tissue freezes and fractures under mechanical stress.

The PCBC-3's tactical signature is defined by what happens after the initial burst. Unlike heat-based charges, the cryogenic effect persists in the environment for 15–40 seconds depending on ambient temperature and ventilation — the area remains lethally cold long after detonation, and surfaces remain structurally compromised. Armor plating hit by the burst loses significant tensile strength for the duration of the cold window, making it vulnerable to follow-up kinetic impacts that it would normally deflect. Security barriers, reinforced doors, and vehicle hulls can be rendered brittle and then breached with tools or impacts that would otherwise be completely ineffective.

Helix Biosystems developed the PCBC-3 under a cryogenic medical research framework — the same technology used for rapid-freeze tissue preservation in trauma response units. The weaponized variant was not an official Helix product; it emerged from an internal R&D division that was quietly licensing the core compression technology to a third-party arms developer. When the connection became public in 2198, Helix's official position was that the licensing agreement had been unauthorized. Three division heads were terminated. The PCBC-3 continued to circulate.
Properties.manufacturer: HELIX BIOSYSTEMS (core technology, unofficial derivation); field manufacture attributed to unlicensed contractors
Properties.specifications:
weight: 1.6 kg
cryogenic agent: Classified compound (suspected liquefied nitrogen-argon mixture with proprietary accelerant)
dispersal radius: 4 meters (primary zone), 8 meters (partial effect)
temperature drop: 80–120°C within primary zone (0.4-second onset)
cold persistence: 15–40 seconds post-detonation (ambient dependent)
structural effect: Metal tensile strength reduced ~60% during cold window; polymers and ceramics subject to fracture
biological effect: Immediate frostbite to full tissue freeze within primary zone; cold shock incapacitation in secondary zone
trigger mechanism: Impact, timer, or remote detonation
hazard to operator: Significant backblast risk; minimum safe distance 12 meters
Properties.tactical_use: Operators use the PCBC-3 in two primary configurations: as a direct-entry breaching tool and as a personnel-denial charge. For breaching, the charge is placed against a reinforced barrier — a vault door, a security bulkhead, an armored vehicle panel — and detonated to render the material brittle before a follow-up kinetic breach. The combined cryogenic-plus-impact approach can defeat hardened materials in half the time of conventional breaching charges with far less noise. For personnel denial, it is deployed into enclosed spaces to incapacitate or kill augmented and unaugmented targets alike — cyberware offers no protection against rapid temperature drop, and many augmented individuals have less biological insulation than unaugmented counterparts.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88, the PCBC-3 carries a particular association with surgical precision and high professionalism — it is a weapon that requires planning, proper handling equipment, and situational awareness that most street-level operators don't have. The backblast risk means careless users die; the breach applications mean it is almost exclusively used by crews with a specific objective rather than general violence. It has developed a reputation as a 'specialist's tool' and is treated with a degree of respect even by people who oppose its use. The Helix connection has made it a flashpoint in ongoing debates about corporate liability for weaponized medical technology.
Properties.story_hooks: A Helix Biosystems laboratory is breached using a PCBC-3 to crack a cryogenic storage vault. The thieves took one specific tissue sample and left everything else. The sample's existence was not in any public record.; A player character is hired to acquire a PCBC-3 for a client who turns out to be planning to use it against a medical cryogenic storage facility containing hundreds of suspended patients.; The unlicensed contractors manufacturing the PCBC-3 have a sourcing problem: the cryogenic compound requires a Helix-patented precursor. Someone inside Helix is selling it to them, and Helix wants the players to find out who — quietly.; A forensic investigator contacts the players: three recent deaths in separate incidents all show cryogenic tissue trauma consistent with PCBC-3 exposure, but no detonation sites have been found. Someone is using the weapon in a way that leaves no physical evidence of deployment.

Properties.description:
The Pulmonary Alveolar Resonant Collapse Mine is a pressure-triggered area-denial device that detonates with a primary acoustic charge tuned to the resonant frequency of alveolar sac tissue in human lung parenchyma. Rather than generating a lethal overpressure blast, the PARCM-6 produces a precisely calibrated acoustic burst that propagates through the thoracic cavity and causes simultaneous alveolar collapse across both lung fields within the effective radius. The mine's casing is designed to channel the acoustic output in a toroidal pattern at approximately chest height, maximizing coupling with the respiratory system while minimizing ground-transmitted vibration that might trigger secondary devices.

Developed under a LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS research contract nominally studying respiratory disease progression modeling, the PARCM-6's core technology derived from acoustic stimulation arrays used to induce controlled alveolar stress in research subjects. The weaponized variant uses a neural feedback loop in its detonation sequencer to adapt the acoustic burst profile based on ambient sound environment, ensuring consistent resonant output regardless of background noise conditions. This adaptive sequencing was the critical engineering step that transformed a laboratory instrument into a deployable weapon.

In the field, the PARCM-6 is both feared and valued for its aftermath: targets are alive but incapacitated, unable to breathe effectively, requiring immediate medical intervention. This creates a secondary tactical effect — responders drawn to aid casualties enter the mine's area, and operators can set sequential PARCM-6s to detonate on the response pattern. Street medics have developed a grim protocol for 'white lung fields' — areas suspected of PARCM-6 deployment — that involves approach via specific corridors and immediate positive-pressure ventilation equipment.
Properties.aliases: PARCM-6, Breathstopper, The Quiet Field, White Lung Mine
Properties.specifications:
form factor: Disc mine, 180mm diameter, 35mm height
weight: 680g
trigger modes: Pressure plate, seismic proximity, remote command, timer
effective radius: 5.5m full alveolar collapse, 9.0m partial effect
acoustic burst duration: 0.18 seconds
height optimization: Toroidal output centered at 1.1m–1.5m above deployment surface
adaptive sequencing: Neural feedback loop calibrates to ambient acoustic environment in 0.6s
primary effect: Bilateral alveolar collapse, acute respiratory failure
secondary effects: Hypoxia, loss of consciousness within 90 seconds, surfactant damage causing prolonged recovery
Properties.tactical_use: The PARCM-6 is deployed as an area-denial weapon in corridors, stairwells, and chokepoints where personnel movement is predictable. Operators place them in overlapping patterns to create 'white lung fields' — zones where any movement triggers incapacitation. The weapon is particularly effective in multi-story building clearance operations, where stairwells can be mined to prevent both retreat and reinforcement. Counter-operations specialists use the mine's responder-attraction effect deliberately, placing a visible casualty bait in a mined approach corridor.
Properties.cultural_context: The PARCM-6's nominal 'restricted' rather than 'prohibited' classification is the result of LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS successfully arguing before Meridian 88's regulatory body that the weapon's non-lethal design intent qualifies it for controlled civilian security use. The argument is widely considered corrupt — the company's legal team drafted the regulatory language. Among Meridian 88's medical underground, the PARCM-6 is considered the most cynical product of pharma-weapons crossover: a device built from respiratory research, deployed to destroy the respiratory system, manufactured by a company that also sells the ventilators needed to treat its victims.
Properties.story_hooks: A player character stumbles into a white lung field in what should have been a civilian district — someone is testing PARCM-6 deployment patterns on real foot traffic.; A street medic organization asks players to help map and clear a mined district — but the mines are on a neural feedback network and adapt to clearance attempts.; A LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS internal document surfaces showing the PARCM-6 was tested on human subjects in clinical trials disguised as respiratory disease research.; A corporate rival is using PARCM-6s to deny LAZARUS access to a distribution hub — and LAZARUS wants plausibly deniable contractors to clear the field without involving law enforcement.

Properties.description:
The Pulmonary Surfactant Degradation Carbine projects a narrow aerosol beam of catalytic nanoparticulate agents suspended in a pressurized carrier medium. When inhaled, the nanoparticulates bind to pulmonary surfactant molecules lining the alveolar surface of the lungs and initiate an enzymatic cascade that breaks down the surfactant's phospholipid structure. Surfactant prevents alveolar collapse during exhalation; without it, the lungs begin to fail in a manner clinically indistinguishable from acute respiratory distress syndrome — the alveoli collapse, gas exchange fails, and the target experiences progressive respiratory failure within four to twenty minutes of exposure depending on dose and individual lung capacity.

The PSDC-2 is unique among respiratory weapons in that it produces no visible external symptom until the target is already in critical condition. There is no coughing fit, no immediate throat burn, no obvious reaction at the moment of exposure. The target breathes in the carrier medium, experiences nothing unusual, and then — minutes later and potentially in an entirely different location — begins to feel short of breath. By the time they recognize the severity of their condition, they are far from the point of exposure and often far from help. This delay is the weapon's primary tactical feature and its primary atrocity.

Tessera Corponation's life sciences division holds the base nanoparticulate patents and licenses the formulation to Arcturus Defense Solutions for weapons integration, maintaining deniability through contractual separation. Surfactant replacement therapy administered within the first ten minutes of exposure can reverse the degradation process almost entirely; after fifteen minutes, the window closes rapidly. Street medics who operate in areas where the PSDC-2 has been used keep portable surfactant nebulizers on hand, and the presence of these devices in a medic's kit is sometimes used as informal evidence of what weapons are circulating in a given district.
Properties.manufacturer: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS (nanoparticulate formulation licensed from TESSERA CORPONATION)
Properties.legality: Prohibited — classified as a chemical/biological weapon analog under Meridian 88 Municipal Code 91-B; international prohibition pending
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 15 meters direct beam, disperses to 4-meter cloud at range
onset of symptoms: 4–8 minutes post-exposure
time to critical respiratory failure: 12–20 minutes from exposure
lethal without treatment: Yes — approximately 85% lethality without surfactant replacement therapy
treatment window: Effective reversal within 10 minutes; partial reversal to 15 minutes
weight: 2.6 kg
shots per canister: 15 single-target doses
detection: Aerosol is colorless and odorless; requires chemical sensor equipment to detect post-dispersal
countermeasures: Sealed respiratory systems; HEPA-equivalent filtration; surfactant nebulizer therapy
Properties.tactical_use: Used in assassination and targeted elimination operations where the operator cannot remain at the scene and where delayed lethality provides an alibi window. The PSDC-2 is fired in crowded or transient environments — transit hubs, market floors, building lobbies — where the target will disperse naturally before symptom onset. Military applications include denial-of-space operations where personnel must be cleared from a location without visible engagement. Counter-operators carrying this weapon typically have surfactant antidote kits for self-administration in case of accidental exposure.
Properties.cultural_context: The PSDC-2 is known in Meridian 88's medical community primarily through its victims — people who arrive at emergency facilities in respiratory crisis with no apparent cause, no trauma, no toxicology hit on standard panels, and lungs that look on imaging like they have been working without surfactant for fifteen minutes. Physicians who have seen the pattern call it 'dry drowning,' which became 'Drowndry' on the street. Tessera Corponation's involvement in the underlying patent is an open secret in the biomedical community and a source of ongoing tension with the company's public-facing pharmaceutical and healthcare divisions, which market themselves on the basis of 'preserving human vitality.'
Properties.story_hooks: Three people died of apparent respiratory failure at a Tessera Corponation shareholder event last month. The official cause is listed as a ventilation malfunction. A whistleblower inside the company believes the deaths were targeted eliminations using the PSDC-2 — someone killed specific shareholders to shift a board vote — and wants the party to obtain the ventilation system's environmental sensor logs before they are purged.; A street medic has been quietly treating Drowndry survivors and keeping records. She's identified a geographic cluster of exposures that suggests someone is testing the weapon on the population of a specific district. She needs help getting her data to someone who will act on it — but Tessera Corponation's legal team has already been in contact with her building's landlord.; The party is contracted to escort a target to a secure location. Midway through the job, the target begins showing early respiratory distress. Someone dosed them before the party picked them up, and the treatment window is closing. The nearest medical facility is controlled by Lazarus Pharmaceuticals, which has a standing contract with Arcturus Defense Solutions.

Properties.description:
The PSVP-1 uses a focused pyroelectric excitation beam to rapidly heat the lipid-rich sebaceous secretions present on human skin to their volatilization threshold, producing a thin layer of ignitable vapor directly against the target's epidermis. A secondary piezoelectric ignition pulse, delivered 0.4 seconds after the primary beam, ignites this vapor layer. The result is a flash-burn effect that originates on the skin's surface rather than being applied externally — it cannot be blocked by standard fire-resistant outerwear because the fuel source is the body itself.

The weapon's tactical novelty is its ability to defeat fire-protective equipment that would otherwise render incendiary weapons ineffective. Flame-retardant suits, ceramic composite armor, and even experimental aerogel body armor provide no meaningful protection against an ignition event that begins at the skin layer. The burn produced is typically superficial to partial-thickness depending on exposure duration, but the psychological effect of fire appearing beneath armor is profound and immediately disabling in most subjects.

The PSVP-1 is a Ringo Corponation product, developed under a contract that has never been publicly disclosed and which Ringo's legal division actively suppresses inquiry into. The weapon saw limited deployment in a corporate territorial dispute in the outer sectors approximately three years ago, after which two municipal investigators who were building a war crimes case died in unrelated accidents. The weapon's existence is known primarily through survivor accounts and a single partially intact unit recovered by an independent forensic team.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 2–12 meters
power source: Dual-cell pyroelectric and piezoelectric capacitor array, 11 discharge cycles
primary beam duration: 0.4 seconds per cycle
ignition delay: 0.4 seconds post-primary beam
burn depth: Superficial to partial-thickness (exposure-dependent)
weight: 2.2 kg
form factor: Compact pistol configuration with dual emitter ports
armor penetration: Effective against all fire-resistant and most composite body armor
Properties.tactical_use: The PSVP-1 is used primarily to defeat armored targets in close-quarters engagements where conventional weapons have been neutralized by protective equipment. Operators typically fire once to establish the volatilization effect, then the ignition fires automatically. A single discharge is usually sufficient for incapacitation due to pain response even when burn depth is limited. The weapon is rarely used for lethality — it is a compliance and deterrence tool among those who possess it, as the psychological effect of knowing one's armor is irrelevant is significant. Its short range limits utility in open engagements.
Properties.cultural_context: The PSVP-1 exists in Meridian 88's criminal and shadow-military ecosystem as a kind of horror story. Most people who know about it know someone who knows someone — it sits at the edge of verified reality. Among armored security professionals, it represents an existential anxiety: the idea that the protection they rely on could be made worse than useless. Ringo Corponation's involvement is widely suspected in underground circles but unprovable, and those who have tried to prove it have encountered consistent obstruction. The weapon has no street name that is used casually — it is spoken of carefully.
Properties.story_hooks: A burn victim in a hospital shows an injury pattern that a trauma surgeon quietly identifies as inconsistent with any known incendiary — the surgeon contacts someone they trust rather than filing a report.; A partially functional PSVP-1 surfaces at a black-market auction; multiple parties with very different agendas want it, and the auction is about to go violently wrong.; Someone inside Ringo Corponation is willing to hand over the original development contract documentation in exchange for extraction from the company's residential campus.; The outer-sector gang using the recovered unit has begun making demands on neighboring territories, and everyone knows they have something that changes the equation — but nobody wants to be first to find out exactly what.

Properties.description: The PSP-9 'Vertebrae' is a long-barreled precision weapon developed by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric that exploits pyroelectric crystal arrays to generate and project a tightly focused beam of thermal-electric energy specifically tuned to interact with the conductive properties of implanted cybernetic spinal columns — the most common form of structural augmentation in Meridian 88's labor and military populations. When the beam contacts a cybernetic spinal implant, it induces rapid thermal expansion and electrical discharge within the implant's internal architecture, causing catastrophic mechanical failure that translates directly into sudden, total motor paralysis in the target. Against unaugmented targets, the weapon functions as a conventional high-temperature burn lance with reduced effectiveness.
Properties.aliases: The Spine Doctor, Backbreaker, Column Gun
Properties.specifications:
weight: 3.7 kg
length: 88 cm
effective range: 60 m (augmentation detection); 45 m (effective beam range)
beam temperature: 1,100°C at focal point
augmentation detection accuracy: 87% (spinal implants vs. other cybernetics)
power source: Pyroelectric cell (14 shots per cell)
recharge cycle: 3.2 seconds between shots
operating temperature: Above 5°C (crystal coherence threshold)
primary effect augmented: Catastrophic spinal implant failure, immediate motor paralysis
primary effect unaugmented: Severe burn injury, limited structural damage
Properties.tactical_use: The 'Vertebrae' is used almost exclusively in targeted interdiction of augmented security personnel, soldiers, and labor enforcers. Operators identify high-value augmented targets — squad leaders, heavy combat augments, logistics coordinators with neural-spinal interfaces — and prioritize them for 'Vertebrae' engagement before committing to broader firefights. The weapon's limited shots-per-cell demand strict fire discipline; operators are trained to confirm augmentation signatures before firing rather than speculating. In corporate security deployments, the 'Vertebrae' is often used to suppress labor actions, a use that has generated significant political controversy.
Properties.cultural_context: No weapon in Meridian 88 has generated more sustained political outrage than the 'Vertebrae.' Labor organizations across the city's manufacturing sectors have campaigned for years to have the weapon classified as a torture device, citing the nature of spinal implant failure injuries — which, while survivable in a significant portion of cases, often result in permanent paralysis without expensive medical intervention most workers cannot afford. Zheng-Dao Bioelectric maintains that the weapon is a humane alternative to lethal force, a position that has made the company's name synonymous with corporate cynicism in many districts. Operators known to carry the 'Vertebrae' are sometimes targeted for violence by augmented community members.
Properties.story_hooks: A whistleblower within Zheng-Dao Bioelectric claims the 'Vertebrae's' augmentation scanner has a hidden mode that logs target identities and transmits them to a corporate database — effectively creating a registry of every augmented individual the weapon has been aimed at.; A labor organizer who survived a 'Vertebrae' attack is offering significant payment for someone to destroy the corporate security unit responsible — but their plan requires the players to acquire a 'Vertebrae' of their own.; Someone has modified a 'Vertebrae' to target a specific proprietary spinal implant model — one that was installed in thousands of workers during a particular corporate contract. The modified weapon is being used to systematically eliminate everyone who received that implant.; A Zheng-Dao Bioelectric technician is trying to quietly defect, carrying documentation that proves the 'non-lethal incapacitation' classification was falsified from the beginning.

Properties.description:
The PFPS-2 uses a dual-wavelength pyrolytic beam tuned to the specific thermal absorption coefficient of fascial connective tissue — the dense fibrous sheaths that encase every muscle group in the human body. When the beam contacts a target, it selectively superheats the fascial layer without significantly affecting the muscle tissue beneath or the skin above, causing rapid pyrolytic separation: the fascia tears, contracts, and in severe cases vaporizes in localized strips. The result is acute compartment syndrome onset in the affected limb within seconds, accompanied by searing pain as the released pressure differential crushes adjacent nerves and vasculature.

What makes the Peeler distinctively horrifying is its visible effect at high power settings: the skin over the targeted area develops a characteristic rippling, as though something beneath is trying to escape. Operators refer to this as 'the show,' and its psychological impact on bystanders has been documented as a significant secondary effect — witnesses to a Peeler discharge frequently suffer acute stress responses severe enough to require medical intervention. The weapon was originally developed for surgical field applications, intended to replace manual fasciotomy in trauma scenarios, before ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS acquired the underlying patent and adapted it.

The weapon platform is compact and pistol-form, fitted with a twin-emitter head that projects the two wavelengths in precise interference pattern. It has a notoriously short effective range — rarely useful beyond 25 meters — but within that envelope it is considered one of the most reliably incapacitating weapons available. Targets struck in the thigh or forearm are typically unable to use the affected limb for days to weeks even with prompt medical care.
Properties.legality: Prohibited — classified as a torture instrument under Meridian 88 Municipal Code 7.4.12
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 2–25 meters
beam wavelengths: 3.4 μm and 6.1 μm (tuned to collagen absorption peaks)
time to fascial separation: 1.8–6 seconds depending on tissue depth
incapacitation profile: Acute compartment syndrome, 72+ hour recovery minimum
power source: Pyrolytic induction cell, 14 discharges
weight: 1.4 kg
length: 28 cm
emitter head: Twin-aperture interference projector
targeting assist: Thermal contrast overlay (optional heads-up display sync)
Properties.tactical_use: Used in close-quarters scenarios where the operator needs to permanently remove a target's combat capability without killing them — debt enforcement, interrogation preamble, or message-sending contracts. Its short range makes it a contact-to-midrange weapon, typically deployed after a target has been pinned or cornered. Some operators use it in combination with a conventional firearm: the Peeler drops the target's defensive capability in a limb, the firearm handles the follow-through. Organized crime uses it heavily for 'marking' — a single Peeler strike to the dominant hand is a recognizable permanent warning.
Properties.cultural_context: The Peeler is associated almost exclusively with the debt-collection and enforcement ecosystem of Meridian 88's lower corporate tiers. Carrying one is a statement: the bearer doesn't just want you stopped, they want you to remember it. In certain criminal organizations it is carried exclusively by enforcers who have been granted the explicit authority to maim — a status symbol indicating trust from leadership. Victims of Peeler strikes are identifiable to street medics by their scarring pattern, and within survivor communities the weapon has become a rallying symbol of corporate brutality. There is an underground medical collective called 'The Fascial' that provides free reconstructive care to Peeler victims.
Properties.story_hooks: A Peeler with a custom serial number is found at a crime scene where the victim — a Helix Biosystems researcher — died of conventional gunshot. Why bring a Peeler if you were going to shoot them anyway? What were they trying to get first?; The Fascial medical collective is being systematically targeted — someone is eliminating the people who document and treat Peeler victims. The party must protect the collective's lead surgeon before a crucial testimony.; A character receives a Peeler strike as a warning from a creditor. The clock is now ticking on both their debt and their limb function — they need a solution to both.; ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS is lobbying to have the Peeler reclassified from 'torture instrument' to 'less-lethal compliance tool.' Someone is paying the party to make sure that reclassification fails — or succeeds.

Properties.description:
The RTL-8 generates a narrow coherent beam of mid-infrared radiation tuned to the peak absorption frequency of water-bearing biological tissue — approximately 3 micrometers wavelength — delivered through a zinc selenide optical assembly housed in a matte ceramic barrel. Unlike visible-spectrum laser weapons that deposit energy on surface layers, the RTL-8's chosen wavelength penetrates 2–4 millimeters into tissue before converting to heat, cooking target structures from within while leaving the outermost dermal layer initially intact. The subjective experience for unprotected targets is described by medical examiners as 'subsurface thermal necrosis' — the tissue beneath the skin liquefies before the surface shows visible damage.

The RTL-8's power management system draws from a high-density thermal battery that doubles as a heat sink, with a passive radiator array along the weapon's spine that glows a deep amber during sustained operation — a distinctive visual signature that operators sometimes use deliberately as a psychological deterrent. The weapon operates in three modes: pulse (0.1-second burst, low thermal signature), sustained (continuous beam up to 4 seconds before mandatory cooldown), and 'cathedral' mode (maximum output, 1.8 seconds, visible steam or smoke from target, requires 40-second full cooldown).

HELIX BIOSYSTEMS developed the RTL-8 under a medical research contract for non-invasive tissue ablation in surgical contexts, and the weapon's design philosophy still reflects that clinical origin. ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS purchased manufacturing rights after a field evaluation demonstrated its effectiveness against targets in thermal-insulated suits, which conventional laser weapons struggle to defeat. The name 'Hearthstone' emerged from field operators who noted that a weapon firing in cathedral mode warms everything in a 3-meter radius.
Properties.aliases: Hearthstone, The Priest's Torch, Slow Burn
Properties.manufacturer: HELIX BIOSYSTEMS (design origin); ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS (military production)
Properties.specifications:
wavelength: 3.0 micrometers (mid-infrared)
optical assembly: Zinc selenide focusing array
penetration depth tissue: 2–4 mm
beam modes: Pulse (0.1s) / Sustained (up to 4s) / Cathedral (1.8s max output)
cathedral cooldown: 40 seconds
battery capacity: 18 pulse shots / 6 sustained cycles / 3 cathedral shots
effective range: Up to 40 m (optimal); degraded past 60 m
weight: 2.7 kg
length: 54 cm
thermal bleed radius cathedral: ~3 m ambient warming
Properties.tactical_use: RTL-8 operators exploit its subsurface damage mechanism against targets in thermal armor, where conventional weapons struggle. Pulse mode is used for precision suppression at range with minimal collateral heat. Sustained mode handles material cutting — doors, sensor arrays, vehicle optics. Cathedral mode is reserved for hardened single targets or rapid material breaching when time is critical and cooldown is acceptable. The weapon's amber glow during operation is sometimes used deliberately to signal capability and force surrender without firing.
Properties.cultural_context: The RTL-8's medical origin gives it a disturbing dual identity in Meridian 88. Surgeons and HELIX BIOSYSTEMS researchers recognize the design language immediately, which creates a specific kind of horror when the weapon appears in violent contexts. Among military operators it carries a reputation for being 'clean' in the bureaucratic sense — the damage profile is difficult to attribute to a specific weapon in autopsies, which makes it attractive for deniable operations. Street-level criminals rarely encounter it; its presence signals either military or high-tier corporate involvement.
Properties.story_hooks: A HELIX BIOSYSTEMS whistleblower is found dead with RTL-8 tissue damage — but the weapon was supposed to be locked in a military-only supply chain, suggesting someone inside HELIX authorized its use.; The players acquire an RTL-8 with a HELIX medical serial number, not an ARCTURUS military one — tracing its provenance leads to a secret program that was officially cancelled.; An ARCTURUS operator using an RTL-8 in cathedral mode in a confined space has caused structural damage to a civilian habitat; the corporation wants the incident buried and hires the players to manage the aftermath.; A religious cult in Meridian 88's lower districts has acquired an RTL-8 and incorporated it into ritual practice, calling it a 'divine light' — their leader knows exactly what it does and is using it for controlled killings disguised as miracles.

Properties.description:
The RCID-4 is a defensive drone platform designed not to seek targets but to occupy space. Deployed in clusters of six to twelve units, Thornwall drones form an autonomous defensive perimeter around a protected zone, person, or object. Each unit is a flattened disc approximately 18 centimeters in diameter, capable of hovering at fixed coordinates with a positional accuracy of 3 centimeters. The drone's outer rim is lined with 24 directed flechette tubes, each loaded with a single tungsten-tipped gauss-accelerated needle. When an object crosses the drone's proximity threshold at a velocity consistent with a ballistic projectile or aggressive human movement, the relevant flechette tubes fire in a directed pattern toward the intrusion vector.

The Thornwall's threat discrimination uses a combination of radar cross-section analysis and linear magnetic field disruption detection — it can distinguish a thrown object from a person walking, a running attacker from a retreating ally. The discrimination algorithm, developed by Tessera Corponation's autonomous defense division, is licensed separately from the hardware and requires subscription renewal. Operators who let their license lapse find their Thornwall clusters defaulting to a degraded 'velocity-only' discrimination mode that has been responsible for several friendly-fire incidents.

What makes the Thornwall distinctive in the broader drone ecosystem is its role reversal — it is a weapon that does not pursue, hunt, or seek. It simply exists in space and punishes intrusion. This passive-aggressive tactical philosophy has made it enormously popular in corporate interior defense, high-value personal protection, and among wealthy paranoids who want their apartments to fight back. The cultural unease around Thornwall clusters centers on the question of accountability — when a drone fires autonomously and kills someone, the manufacturer's end-user license agreement explicitly transfers all liability to the operator.
Properties.aliases: Thornwall, The Fence, Spinedog, Reactive Shell
Properties.specifications:
unit dimensions: 18cm diameter, 4cm depth
unit mass: 0.9kg
flechette count per unit: 24 directed tubes
flechette type: Tungsten-tipped, gauss-accelerated, 4mm diameter
positional accuracy: 3cm hover precision
discrimination algorithm: Tessera Corponation ThreatLogic v7.1 (subscription required)
standard cluster size: 6–12 units
effective interception radius: Configurable, 1–8 meters per unit
battery life: 14 hours active patrol mode
acoustic signature: 44dB per unit at 3 meters
rearm requirement: Manual flechette cassette replacement, 90 seconds per unit
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed in overlapping clusters to create layered interception zones around a protected asset. Corporate security teams use Thornwall grids in server rooms, executive suites, and transit corridors. Personal protection details deploy three to four units around a principal during stationary meetings. In field operations, operators establish a Thornwall perimeter before conducting activities requiring sustained attention — negotiations, hacking operations, medical procedures. The drones are small enough to fit in a standard cargo case and deploy in under 40 seconds. Experienced operators map their own movement paths through the cluster before activating the system.
Properties.cultural_context: The Thornwall has become a status symbol among Meridian 88's upper-middle corporate class — a way of demonstrating that your personal security budget has crossed the threshold from hired muscle into autonomous systems. The drones are frequently visible in corporate lobbies and executive dining areas, hovering at ceiling height with their flechette rims subtly visible. Interior design firms have begun offering 'Thornwall-integrated aesthetics,' incorporating the drones into architectural lighting schemes. Among activists and civil liberties groups, the autonomous lethal decision-making capacity of the RCID-4 is a rallying cause — three wrongful death suits against Tessera Corponation are currently in arbitration.
Properties.story_hooks: A Tessera Corponation licensing server has been compromised — someone is pushing a firmware update that will set all active Thornwall clusters to velocity-only discrimination mode simultaneously across the city.; The party needs to enter a penthouse protected by a twelve-unit Thornwall cluster — they have the floor plan but need to map the drone positions before moving.; A wrongful death plaintiff has hired the party to obtain internal Tessera documents showing the company knew about the degraded discrimination mode in expired-license units.; A Thornwall unit has gone rogue — its positional anchor has been spoofed and it is now drifting through a residential corridor, firing at movement, and no one can reach the operator's override.

Wealthy paranoid individuals in secured residential towers
