Properties.description: The RFC-11 is an industrial demolition device repurposed from construction technology, manufactured openly by Palladian Construction under its 'controlled demolition solutions' catalog but widely diverted to armed use through commercial procurement loopholes. The device contains two separated chemical reservoirs: a proprietary polyurethane-explosive compound and a catalytic accelerant. When the charge activates, the two compounds mix and expand rapidly into a dense, adhesive foam that fills the target cavity — a pipe junction, door mechanism, wall void, or vehicle undercarriage — before detonating. The foam cures to approximately 40% of its expansion volume in 1.8 seconds, then detonates, directing the majority of its blast force inward along the path of least resistance.
Properties.tier_availability: Tier 2+ (commercial) / Tier 1 (modified combat variants, street market)
Properties.legality: Licensed for demolition use; combat modification is Prohibited; base unit sold legally with contractor certification
Properties.specifications:
weight: 520g (dual-reservoir unit)
expansion volume: Up to 8 liters from 0.4-liter reservoir
cure time before detonation: 1.8 seconds (factory default, field-adjustable 0.5–6s)
blast yield: Equivalent to 200g RDX, directed inward
adhesion: Bonds to concrete, metal, synthetics, and organic tissue on contact
effective use cases: Breaching reinforced doors, disabling vehicle axles, collapsing internal wall structures
hazard: Adhesion to operator skin is a documented field fatality cause
Properties.tactical_use: The RFC-11 is used primarily for breaching and structural disruption. Operators inject the nozzle into a door's locking mechanism or a wall's structural joint, activate the charge, and retreat. The foam expands to fill the cavity, then detonates inward — tearing the mechanism apart from inside rather than requiring a shaped charge on the exterior surface, which is often monitored or armored. Modified combat variants are thrown like grenades, the foam adhering to whatever surface or person it contacts before detonating. The adhesive property makes it particularly feared in close quarters.
Properties.cultural_context: Bloat started as a construction site tool and its street evolution is a story of industrial supply chain failure. Palladian Construction's contractor certification program is notoriously easy to falsify, and RFC-11 units move through hardware distribution networks in bulk. In Meridian 88's outer districts, where buildings are perpetually under renovation, Bloat is common enough that experienced operators check door mechanisms before forcing entry. There is a subculture of modified RFC use among demolition graffiti artists who use low-yield variants to blow decorative cavities into corporate facade panels — a practice known as 'bloat-tagging.'
Properties.story_hooks: A Palladian Construction regional manager is running a side operation selling combat-modified RFC-11s through a shell contractor — a building inspector just found evidence in a collapsed structure that wasn't supposed to collapse.; A string of armored vehicle disablements in the transit corridor all used RFC-11s injected into axle housings — the precision suggests someone with demolition training, not street operators.; A bloat-tag collective accidentally used a combat-modified unit obtained from a street dealer — the resulting explosion killed two people and the group is now being hunted by both the street dealer and the authorities.

Properties.description:
The Renal Tubular Crystallization Lance delivers a sustained beam of targeted ultrasonic energy modulated to excite calcium oxalate precursor molecules already present in the bloodstream, driving rapid nucleation and crystal growth within the renal tubules. Within ninety seconds of sustained exposure, a target develops acute obstructive nephrolithiasis of catastrophic severity — kidney stones forming simultaneously throughout both kidneys at a rate and scale that no biological system can pass or tolerate. The resulting pain is clinically described as among the most severe a human nervous system can register, and internal tubular rupture follows within minutes if the beam is maintained.

The Lance's genius is its exploitation of endogenous chemistry. It does not introduce any foreign substance — it merely accelerates a process the body is already capable of performing. This makes it extraordinarily difficult to counter with standard bioweapon filters or blood-agent scrubbers. The weapon's targeting head uses a focused ultrasonic lens array combined with a millimeter-wave kidney-localizing scanner, allowing operators to engage targets through light cover and most civilian clothing. The beam must be held on target for at least forty-five seconds for reliable crystal induction, meaning it is not a snap-fire weapon — it rewards patience.

Zheng-Dao markets a civilian-grade version of the underlying lens technology as a non-destructive kidney stone treatment device, which has provided convenient legal cover for the weapon's development history. The Lance's power pack is famously efficient, offering up to six sustained engagements before recharge, and the weapon runs nearly silent apart from a faint ultrasonic hiss audible only at close range.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 5–45 meters
minimum dwell time: 45 seconds for reliable induction
lethal dwell time: 90–120 seconds
targeting system: MMW kidney-localizing scanner with ±2cm accuracy
power source: High-efficiency ultrasonic driver cell, 6 full engagements per charge
weight: 4.7 kg with power pack
form factor: Long-arm configuration, collapsible stock
countermeasure resistance: Ineffective against standard biofilters and blood scrubbers
Properties.tactical_use: Used primarily in siege and surveillance situations where an operator can hold a position and engage a stationary or slow-moving target — executive protection failures, guarded safe houses, perimeter containment. The weapon's long dwell time makes it unsuitable for mobile engagements but extraordinarily effective for patient operators. Some interrogators use sub-lethal settings to induce severe pain without permanent organ damage as a compliance tool. The fact that it leaves no external wound and mimics a naturally occurring medical condition makes it prized for deniable operations.
Properties.cultural_context: The RTCL-1 has a grim reputation in Meridian 88's corporate assassination ecosystem as the 'patience weapon' — only operators who are disciplined and methodical choose it. It is associated with a certain old-school professionalism, as opposed to the flashier drone-based or injectable weapons favored by newer contractors. Among medical examiners and forensic specialists, a victim found with bilateral renal crystal damage triggers a specific investigative protocol now informally called a 'Zheng-Dao workup.' Zheng-Dao Bioelectric officially and strenuously denies any connection to the weapon.
Properties.story_hooks: A renowned forensic pathologist is found dead of apparent kidney failure — but a colleague notices the crystal distribution pattern matches RTCL-1 exposure, suggesting someone used the weapon to silence her before she could publish a damning report.; A Zheng-Dao executive quietly approaches fixers to recover a stolen RTCL-1 prototype that has a firmware flaw allowing it to be traced back to an internal product line — before regulators find it.; A vigilante group has acquired an RTCL-1 and is systematically targeting known human traffickers, always at range, always untraceable — law enforcement is divided on whether to pursue them.; A fixer discovers that the 'kidney stone treatment clinic' they visited last month was a front — and the ultrasonic equipment used on them was a modified RTCL-1 that deposited dormant crystal seeds that can be remotely activated.

Properties.description:
The RMIR-5 generates a tightly focused beam of low-frequency resonant energy tuned specifically to the acoustic signature of cancellous bone tissue — the porous, spongy matrix found in the interior of most human long bones and vertebrae. When the beam contacts a target, it induces rapid sympathetic vibration within the marrow cavity, creating an internal pressure wave that does not register on the body's surface. The effect is experienced as a deep, nauseating ache that rapidly escalates to incapacitating pain originating from inside the skeletal structure, with no visible external cause.

What makes the RMIR-5 particularly insidious is its penetration profile. Standard soft armor, tactical plating, and even most hardened cybernetic chassis components are acoustically transparent at the RMIR-5's operating frequency — the beam passes through them as if they aren't present and acts directly on the biological substrate beneath. The only effective countermeasure is bone-density augmentation or full skeletal replacement with non-resonant synthetic materials, both of which are expensive procedures. Standard ballistic protection offers the target no meaningful defense, a fact that has driven significant demand from operators facing heavily armored opponents.

Helix Biosystems developed the RMIR-5 under a medical research designation — the underlying technology was derived from therapeutic bone stimulation devices used in fracture recovery. The weapon's origins in medical technology give it an unsettling clinical quality: its emitter array looks almost identical to a legitimate physiotherapy unit, and its carrying case is indistinguishable from medical equipment. This has made it a significant challenge for checkpoint security to identify.
Properties.aliases: Deepache, The Marrow Caller, Bonewhistle, Paledriver
Properties.tier_availability: Military only / Black market (at extreme premium)
Properties.specifications:
effective range: Up to 200 meters (focused beam)
target tissue: Cancellous bone matrix, primary; cortical bone, secondary at sustained exposure
armor penetration: Acoustically transparent to most soft and hard armor; defeated by full synthetic skeletal replacement
beam duration for effect: 0.8 seconds for onset pain; 3 seconds for incapacitation of most subjects
power source: High-density resonance cell, 40 shots per cell
weight: 5.1 kg
effective countermeasures: Grade IV bone augmentation, full skeletal synthetic replacement, acoustic isolation suits
dimensions: 91cm overall, collapsible to 54cm
Properties.tactical_use: The RMIR-5 is predominantly used for incapacitation rather than lethality — a sustained beam causes complete motor incapacitation within 3-5 seconds as the pain response overwhelms voluntary movement. Operators use it to drop heavily armored targets without triggering the catastrophic structural collapse that lethal weapons produce, making it valuable for capture operations. At extended ranges, brief pulses are used for harassment and disorientation. Military units have deployed it for crowd dispersal where lethal force is politically inadvisable.
Properties.cultural_context: The RMIR-5 has generated significant controversy in Meridian 88's augmentation community. Because its effectiveness depends on the presence of biological bone, those who have undergone skeletal augmentation procedures — often a marker of wealth and corporate affiliation — are immune to its effects, while those who cannot afford augmentation remain vulnerable. This has given the weapon a class-warfare subtext: in certain neighborhoods, carrying a Deepache is read as a statement about who you consider worth threatening. Underground resistance groups have used this symbolism deliberately.
Properties.story_hooks: A union organizer in a lower-tier district has been rendered completely non-functional by what medical scans describe as 'spontaneous internal bone pain of unknown origin.' The players are hired to find the weapon being used before the next public meeting.; A Helix Biosystems researcher contacts the players claiming the RMIR-5 was never supposed to leave the laboratory. She has evidence of an internal leak and needs help tracing the units before a regulatory audit finds them and traces them back to her department.; A player with full skeletal augmentation is the only one immune to an RMIR-5 being used against the party. They are now the only one who can move — and the shooter knows it.; The players recover an RMIR-5 that has been modified beyond factory specifications. The resonance profile has been altered from bone tissue to something else. A Helix Biosystems engineer who examines it goes pale and won't say what the new target tissue is.

Nodes.Name: Military special operations units (confirmed two documented engagements)
'Paledriver' — a mercenary known for capture-and-deliver contracts, whereabouts unknown
Corporate extraction teams operating against unaugmented civilian targets
Resistance cells in lower-tier districts as a symbolic anti-corporate weapon

Properties.description:
The RMDS-4 is a directed-energy area denial platform that projects a diverging cone of millimeter-wave microwave radiation, tuned to the 94 GHz frequency band at which water molecules in the subcutaneous layer of human skin absorb energy most efficiently. The effect on exposed targets is an immediate, overwhelming burning sensation across all exposed skin surfaces — described universally by subjects as being 'cooked from the outside in.' The sensation is intense enough to trigger involuntary flight response in virtually all subjects within seconds, regardless of training or psychological preparation.

Developed by Tessera Corponation's non-lethal security division, the RMDS-4 is explicitly designed not to cause permanent injury under standard exposure protocols. At rated power and exposure times under four seconds, the weapon produces no lasting tissue damage — the burning sensation ceases within seconds of leaving the beam. This has made it extraordinarily attractive to corporate security operations that need to control crowds or breach occupied spaces without generating the liability of lethal force. However, the weapon's power output can be adjusted beyond factory defaults, and modified units operating above rated parameters cause severe epidermal burns, corneal damage, and at extended high-power exposure, fatal hyperthermia.

The RMDS-4 is mounted on a shoulder-rig platform with a 120-degree horizontal sweep and a 30-degree vertical arc, controlled by a handle-mounted targeting interface. The emitter head is recognizable by its distinctive hexagonal radiating array — a design that has become visually synonymous with corporate crowd control in Meridian 88's visual culture, appearing in protest art and propaganda with striking frequency.
Properties.specifications:
platform: Shoulder-rig mounted, single-operator
weight: 11.4kg (rig and emitter)
power source: Tessera Type-6 high-capacity cell, 40 minutes continuous at rated power
frequency: 94 GHz primary, 77 GHz secondary (penetrates light cover)
effective range: 0–50m (primary denial), 50–120m (reduced intensity)
beam spread: 120-degree horizontal sweep, 30-degree vertical arc
rated exposure limit: 4 seconds at standard power (non-injurious)
override capability: Factory-limited; modified units documented at 340% rated output
Properties.tactical_use: Standard deployment places the RMDS-4 operator behind a defensive line, using the wide beam spread to push crowds or groups away from a defined perimeter. In breach scenarios, it is used to clear rooms before entry — the beam passes through standard interior walls at reduced intensity, causing enough discomfort to drive occupants toward exits where entry teams are positioned. Corporate security teams typically deploy one RMDS-4 per four-person unit as a force multiplier. The weapon's main tactical vulnerability is its shoulder-rig format — the operator is relatively immobile during sustained use, and the emitter array is bulky enough to be a targeting priority for hostile snipers.
Properties.cultural_context: The Crowdbreaker is one of the most politically loaded weapons in Meridian 88. Its official designation as a non-lethal system has allowed corporations to deploy it against labor protests, housing disputes, and unauthorized gatherings with legal impunity. The hexagonal emitter array has become a symbol of corporate repression in activist communities — it appears spray-painted on walls, incorporated into protest banners, and tattooed on the bodies of people who survived its use. The existence of modified high-output units is an open secret that Tessera Corponation disputes aggressively, and several journalists who documented RMDS-4 burn injuries in excess of rated parameters have subsequently faced significant legal pressure.
Properties.story_hooks: A protest group has acquired a modified RMDS-4 running at 340% output and is planning to use it — not for crowd control, but as retaliation against a corporate event. The players are asked to stop them, but the client turns out to be the corporation that deployed RMDS-4s against the protesters' community in the first place.; A journalist has documented fatal hyperthermia cases from an RMDS-4 incident and needs the evidence extracted from a Tessera-controlled server before the legal team buries it. The data is real, the risk is real, and Tessera knows someone is looking.; A modified RMDS-4 is being auctioned through a black market channel. Several buyers want it badly enough to kill for it. The players are either protecting the auction, robbing it, or have been hired to ensure a specific buyer doesn't win.

Nodes.Name: Municipal security forces in corporate-administered districts
Underground modification specialists (modified units resold to private buyers)

Properties.description:
The RODC-2 does not explode in any conventional sense. Rather than producing a single detonation shockwave, it generates a rapid sequence of precisely tuned pressure pulses — typically seven to twelve waves fired in 80-millisecond intervals — using a piezoelectric lattice core that converts stored charge into mechanical compression events. The result is a sustained overpressure envelope that interacts destructively with biological tissue while leaving hard structures comparatively intact. Glass survives. Lungs do not.

The weapon was developed by TESSERA CORPONATION's defense subsidiary as a 'precision crowd suppression tool' intended for use in enclosed corporate facilities where conventional explosives would compromise structural integrity. The frequency tuning is calibrated to resonate with pulmonary air columns and middle-ear structures, causing hemorrhagic trauma at ranges where blast-wave weapons would be non-lethal. At close range, the overpressure pulses are sufficient to cause cardiac arrhythmia and cerebral contusion in unshielded targets.

Field operators have noted that the RODC-2 produces an eerie, almost subsonic thudding sensation before casualties begin to manifest — victims often describe feeling 'punched from everywhere at once' before losing consciousness. This perceptual lag has given the weapon a reputation for psychological horror among survivors. The Wavebreaker designation emerged from its use in breaking up fortified positions where combatants had entrenched behind cover — the pressure pulses curve around obstacles with limited but meaningful effectiveness.
Properties.specifications:
pulse count: 7–12 waves per detonation
pulse interval: 80ms
peak overpressure: 4.2 bar at 2m
lethal radius: 4m unshielded
incapacitation radius: 9m
frequency range: 18–140 Hz tunable
weight: 1.4 kg
activation: Proximity fuse, command detonation, or impact
casing: Shock-isolated polymer shell
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed in enclosed spaces — subway tunnels, corporate lobby suppressions, server room raids — where conventional fragmentation would cause collateral structural damage. Used by breach teams as a 'soft clear' before entry, incapacitating occupants without triggering fire suppression systems or structural alarms. Counter-insurgency units use it to clear barricaded positions by exploiting the pressure-curve effect around cover. Targets wearing full respiratory armor retain some protection but are not immune to cardiac and auditory effects.
Properties.cultural_context: TESSERA's marketing materials describe the RODC-2 as 'humane crowd management technology,' a framing that has made it deeply controversial in civil liberties circles within Meridian 88. Labor organizers in the industrial sectors know it as the 'Handshake' — the weapon corporation security teams deploy when they want to end a strike without the optics of visible wounds. The lack of shrapnel and fire damage makes it easy to deny, and TESSERA has aggressively litigated any attempt to classify overpressure trauma as an attributable cause of death.
Properties.story_hooks: A union organizer dies of 'sudden cardiac arrest' during a strike action — the party is hired by her family to prove corporate security used a RODC-2 in the crowd.; TESSERA is quietly recalling all RODC-2 units for a firmware update — a contact inside the company suggests the update includes a remote kill-switch that can be triggered from corporate headquarters.; The party recovers a RODC-2 from a crime scene where the victims show no visible wounds. The local coroner has never seen the trauma pattern before and is asking uncomfortable questions.; A black market vendor is selling RODC-2 units with the frequency lock removed — someone has modified them to target the resonance frequencies of specific cybernetic implants.

Nodes.Name: Underground resistance cells who have acquired captured units
Mercenary firms operating in structure-sensitive environments

Properties.description:
The RCE-6 emits a precisely shaped photonic pulse tuned to the absorption spectrum of rhodopsin and the photosensitive ganglion cells of the human retina, including the modified photoreceptor arrays found in most commercial ocular augmentations. Rather than producing simple flash-blindness through saturation, the Whiteout's pulse chemically depletes the retina's photosensitive compounds and simultaneously overstimulates the optic nerve's signal pathway, producing a cascading neural feedback loop that extends blindness far beyond what simple bright-light exposure would cause. Baseline human targets experience total blindness lasting eight to twenty-five minutes; targets with standard ocular augmentations experience device lockout lasting up to forty minutes as onboard safety systems attempt to reboot fried photoreceptor arrays.

The weapon's targeting system uses a passive infrared rangefinder to shape the photonic pulse into a cone calibrated for the target's estimated eye-level at range, accounting for the natural pupillary dilation of individuals in low-light environments — the conditions in which the Whiteout is most commonly deployed. A secondary spread mode widens the cone to cover a four-meter arc, effective against multiple targets or moving individuals at the cost of reduced per-target duration. The pulse itself is invisible to the human eye during the millisecond of emission but produces a characteristic cyan afterimage in peripheral witnesses.

Helix Biosystems developed the RCE-6 under a joint military contract alongside a companion treatment compound — a rapid rhodopsin restoration agent sold separately at significant markup. The implication that Helix profits from both the weapon and its antidote has not escaped critics, and the company's lobbying against optic augmentation safety standards has drawn sustained attention from watchdog organizations. The weapon is technically classified as a 'non-lethal denial system,' a legal designation that has allowed it to circulate far more widely than its effects arguably warrant.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 3–60 meters
blindness duration baseline: 8–25 minutes
blindness duration augmented: 20–40 minutes (device lockout)
pulse modes: Focused (single target), Spread (4-meter arc)
recharge time: 6 seconds between pulses
magazine capacity: 30 pulses (photonic cell)
weight: 0.9 kg
dimensions: 28cm x 6cm x 5cm
antidote compatibility: Helix Biosystems Rhodopsin Restoration Agent RRA-2
Properties.tactical_use: Security forces and law enforcement deploy the RCE-6 as a primary crowd control and pursuit-termination tool. A blinded target is effectively neutralized without lethal force — they cannot aim, navigate, or resist physical restraint. In pursuit scenarios, operators fire into the path of a fleeing target to produce sudden incapacitation without risk of bystander harm from conventional projectiles. Against augmented targets, the extended lockout duration is particularly valuable: a runner with fried ocular augmentations cannot access navigation overlays, target tracking, or threat-assessment HUDs, reducing them to functional baseline capability in a world built for augmented perception.
Properties.cultural_context: The RCE-6's 'non-lethal' classification is a source of ongoing bitter debate in Meridian 88. In a city where ocular augmentations are not a luxury but a practical necessity for navigation, employment, and survival in many districts, extended blindness carries severe secondary consequences — people are robbed, assaulted, or simply become lost in dangerous areas during the incapacitation window. The fact that Helix Biosystems holds the license on both the weapon and the antidote is widely understood as predatory. Street medics keep RRA-2 in stock as a matter of course, and some community organizations have established rapid-response networks to locate and assist 'whiteout victims' in the hours after deployment.
Properties.story_hooks: A municipal officer uses a Whiteout in a neighborhood where the antidote is unavailable, and three people are seriously harmed during the blindness window. The players are hired — by different clients — to investigate from opposite sides.; Helix Biosystems is quietly suppressing a study showing the RCE-6 causes permanent retinal microstructure damage in approximately 3% of exposures. The researcher who ran the study has disappeared.; A player character is hit with a Whiteout during an ambush and must navigate a hostile environment blind for the next twenty minutes.; The Clarity Collective has obtained a shipment of RCE-6s and is planning a mass deployment at a public event attended by thousands of augmented civilians. The players have forty-eight hours.

Properties.description:
The Scleral Photooxidative Ablation Pistol fires a precisely collimated burst of high-intensity ultraviolet-A and visible violet light specifically tuned to the absorption spectrum of melanin in the retinal pigment epithelium. The burst triggers a cascade of reactive oxygen species generation within the photoreceptor layer, causing immediate and irreversible photooxidative destruction of the macular region. The target experiences a silent, painless flash followed by a central scotoma — a permanent blind spot that expands over the following six hours as the oxidative cascade propagates through adjacent tissue.

The SPAP-4's distinctive design feature is its pre-flash pupil dilation module: a brief sub-threshold pulse of specific wavelengths causes involuntary pupillary dilation in the target half a second before the ablative burst fires, maximizing the amount of destructive light energy that penetrates to the retina. This dilation response is hardwired into the autonomic nervous system and cannot be consciously suppressed. Standard anti-laser eyewear with fixed tint provides reduced but not full protection; only active photochromic lenses with response times under 0.3 milliseconds offer meaningful defense, and few civilians own them.

The weapon was developed by Helix Biosystems under contract for use in riot suppression as a 'non-lethal incapacitant,' a classification that has been widely and bitterly contested. Critics note that permanent bilateral blindness is not meaningfully non-lethal in the context of Meridian 88's streets. The pistol form factor makes it easily concealable, and the silent operation — just a faint violet flash — has made it a weapon of choice for quiet crowd control and targeted political intimidation.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 2–25 meters
pre flash dilation pulse: 0.5 seconds prior to ablative burst
ablative burst duration: 8 milliseconds
wavelength bands: 365nm UVA primary, 415nm violet secondary
power source: Compact photonic cell, 22 shots per charge
weight: 0.9 kg
form factor: Pistol, 19cm overall length
countermeasure: Active photochromic lenses <0.3ms response time
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed in crowd dispersal to permanently blind designated agitators or leadership figures as a deterrent measure. In covert operations, used to silently incapacitate targets in a way that appears accidental or is attributed to industrial UV exposure. Operators in close-quarters situations appreciate the pistol's compactness and the fact that the flash is easily mistaken for camera equipment or a phone screen in a crowd. Some enforcement units carry the SPAP-4 as a secondary weapon specifically for taking out targets who are augmented against conventional firearms.
Properties.cultural_context: The SPAP-4 has become a symbol of state violence in Meridian 88's civil rights discourse. After several documented uses against protesters in the Outer Ring districts, the weapon's violet flash became an iconographic image in anti-corporate art — reproduced on murals, tattoos, and protest flags as a symbol of state-inflicted permanent harm. Survivors who were blinded by the weapon and received no compensation are called 'Whiteouts' in activist circles, and their community is one of the city's most organized political forces. Law enforcement officers who carry the SPAP-4 are sometimes identified and publicly named by underground data brokers.
Properties.story_hooks: A data broker offers a fixer the identity list of every officer issued a SPAP-4 in the last two years — someone is planning something with that list, and the fixer has to decide whether to sell it, suppress it, or warn the officers.; A Helix Biosystems whistleblower claims the SPAP-4 was deliberately mislabeled as non-lethal despite internal studies showing high mortality rates among blinded subjects in Meridian 88's streets — the evidence is encoded in a product lot number.; A Whiteout activist who was blinded by a SPAP-4 has somehow acquired several units and is threatening to use them on the corporate board members of Helix — but the players are hired by both sides.; A black market SPAP-4 modified for full bilateral blindness at 40 meters is found at the scene of a judicial assassination — someone is escalating.

Nodes.Name: Underground fixers with law enforcement connections

Properties.description:
The SRC-2 does not detonate in the conventional sense. It anchors to a surface via four magnetized contact prongs and then drives a precisely tuned low-frequency resonance pulse directly into the substrate — concrete, steel plate, composite flooring, even packed earth. The pulse is calibrated to match the structural resonance frequency of the target material, which the charge's onboard sensor array calculates in the 0.8 seconds after contact. At resonance frequency, the charge amplifies the vibration in a compounding wave pattern until the structural integrity of the material fails catastrophically from within. The external surface may show no visible damage until the moment of collapse.

The SRC-2's defining characteristic is that its destructive energy is entirely directional — downward and outward through the substrate, not upward into open air. Personnel standing on the affected surface experience the failure as the floor or wall simply ceasing to exist beneath them. There is no pressure wave, no heat, no shrapnel — just sudden, catastrophic structural dissolution. This makes standard blast-protection gear completely irrelevant. Hardened armor rated for conventional explosives offers no protection whatsoever if the floor you are standing on liquefies into rubble.

Palladian Construction originally developed resonance-charge technology for controlled demolition of legacy infrastructure in Meridian 88's lower wards — a way to drop a building precisely without disturbing adjacent structures. The SRC-2 is a direct weaponization of that demolition patent, adapted by a third-party contractor that Palladian has spent four years unsuccessfully suing into nonexistence. The original demolition variant required a licensed operator and a 48-hour structural survey. The SRC-2 requires neither.
Properties.manufacturer: PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION (original patent); unlicensed derivative manufacture attributed to RINGO CORPONATION shell subsidiary
Properties.specifications:
weight: 2.3 kg
anchor mechanism: Four-point magnetic contact prongs, rated for steel, concrete, and composite
frequency scan time: 0.8 seconds post-contact
effective radius: 3–7 meters substrate disruption (material-dependent)
energy source: Solid-state capacitor bank, single-use
blast profile: No conventional overpressure; structural failure propagates through substrate
arming delay: User-configurable, 2–30 seconds
countermeasure vulnerability: Frequency-jamming fields can interrupt scan cycle if deployed within 0.8-second window
Properties.tactical_use: The SRC-2 is used almost exclusively for structural breaching and denial operations. Operators plant it on load-bearing floors, walls, or support columns and withdraw before detonation. In multi-story facilities, a single charge placed on a central column can collapse an entire floor section, cutting off pursuit or eliminating a fortified position from below. It is also used offensively in scenarios where targets are wearing blast-hardened gear — the charge's non-conventional damage profile bypasses armor entirely. Some operators use it to breach vaults or reinforced rooms by destroying the structural integrity of the surrounding material rather than attacking the hardened door directly.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88, the SRC-2 has become a symbol of a particular kind of street-level ingenuity — taking corporate infrastructure technology and turning it against corporate infrastructure. Demolition crews in the lower wards sometimes encounter the weapon's aftermath and recognize the resonance pattern from their own legitimate tools, which creates a strange professional kinship with whoever deployed it. Certain radical urban reclamation groups have adopted the SRC-2 as an ideological weapon, using it to collapse corporate-owned development sites. Among conventional arms dealers, it has a reputation for being almost impossible to trace back to a buyer because the structural failure it causes reads as ordinary building collapse.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of 'accidental' building collapses in a contested development zone are actually SRC-2 deployments — but the charges are being planted by someone inside Palladian Construction itself, using access to the original demolition patent to cover their tracks.; A player character is inside a building when the floor begins to fail in a pattern that a demolitions-savvy ally recognizes as resonance collapse. They have approximately 90 seconds before the structural failure reaches their level.; Ringo's shell subsidiary is being investigated, but the investigator keeps dying in building collapses that look accidental. The pattern is too consistent to be coincidence.; A Palladian engineer approaches the players with evidence that someone inside the company has been licensing the SRC-2 technology illegally — and that the buyer list includes several names that should not have access to demolition-grade ordnance.

Structural saboteur archetype known as 'the Architect'
Corporate counter-espionage teams targeting rival facility infrastructure

Properties.description:
The SNFD-1 targets the splanchnic nervous system — the dense network of autonomic nerves governing abdominal organ function — by projecting a modulated neural feedback pulse that overrides normal visceral signaling. The pulse induces simultaneous paradoxical signals across the celiac, superior mesenteric, and inferior mesenteric ganglia: organs receive competing commands to contract and dilate, to accelerate and suppress motility, to activate and inhibit secretion. The result is catastrophic visceral dysregulation — violent involuntary peristalsis, acute nausea and vomiting, loss of bladder and bowel control, and waves of referred pain across the entire abdomen.

The weapon's designers at Ringo Corponation specifically engineered the feedback loop to bypass voluntary nervous system override. Training, pain tolerance, and pharmacological suppressants provide minimal resistance — the splanchnic network is largely inaccessible to conscious control, meaning even highly augmented or conditioned targets respond to the SNFD-1 with full incapacitation. The effect lasts between eight and twenty-five minutes depending on individual physiology, with a lingering period of autonomic instability for up to two hours afterward.

What has made the Gutcheck genuinely feared is its psychological dimension. The profound loss of bodily control it induces — particularly the incontinence — causes acute shame responses that outlast the physical effect. Ringo Corponation's internal testing documentation, leaked in 2183, revealed that the psychological recovery period was considered a 'feature' during development, as targets subjected to the weapon in coercive contexts showed significantly elevated compliance in subsequent interactions. The company has never publicly acknowledged the leak.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 1–15 meters
targeting: Torso-center mass, penetrates standard body armor (no physical penetration required)
pulse modulation: Adaptive — adjusts to target's autonomic baseline within 0.4 seconds
effect duration: 8–25 minutes acute, up to 2 hours residual instability
power source: Compact neural pulse cell, 6 shots
weight: 1.4 kg
form factor: Short carbine, 28 cm, matte black ceramic housing
countermeasures: Partial resistance in subjects with extensive autonomic neural augmentation
Properties.tactical_use: The SNFD-1 is used almost exclusively in close-range coercive and interrogation contexts rather than open combat, as its short range and limited magazine make it impractical for firefights. Operators use it to rapidly incapacitate subjects for restraint and transport, or to degrade a target's psychological state before questioning. Some extraction teams carry one as a 'compliance tool' for managing multiple prisoners. The weapon's lack of visible injury makes it attractive for operations where physical evidence of force must be minimized.
Properties.cultural_context: The Gutcheck has a particular cultural weight in Meridian 88's dissident and activist communities, where it is associated specifically with the tactics of Ringo Corponation's internal affairs and loyalty enforcement divisions. Being 'gut-checked' is understood as a euphemism for coercive detention and psychological breaking. The leaked testing documentation — which circulates in samizdat form across the city's underground networks — has become a radicalizing document, cited in manifestos and organizing materials as evidence of corporate willingness to weaponize shame. Survivors rarely discuss the experience publicly.
Properties.story_hooks: A whistleblower who leaked the SNFD-1 testing documentation is being hunted by Ringo Corponation — the players are hired to extract them, but so is everyone else.; A player character is captured and subjected to the Gutcheck during an interrogation; recovering the memory of what they revealed — and to whom — becomes a driving personal mission.; A black-market dealer is selling SNFD-1 units with a modification that extends the effect duration to several hours — the source of the modification is unknown and deeply alarming to Ringo Corponation.; A support group for Gutcheck survivors has been quietly gathering testimony and building a legal case against Ringo Corponation; someone wants the group's records destroyed before they reach a sympathetic judge.
