Properties.description: A bullpup submachine gun designed for close-quarters corporate facility defense, firing caseless 4mm rounds from a helical magazine that holds 80 rounds. The AS-7 features an integrated friend-or-foe identification system linked to Sterling-Nakamura's employee biometric database — the weapon physically locks its trigger mechanism if pointed at a registered friendly. This IFF system has been both praised as a safety innovation and condemned as a loyalty enforcement tool, since it means the weapon literally cannot be turned against its issuing corporation.
Properties.aliases: Wasp Nest, AS-7, Sterling Buzz, The Nest
Properties.specifications:
caliber: 4mm caseless
magazine: 80-round helical
rate of fire: 900 RPM
effective range: 5-40 meters
weight: 2.4 kg loaded
IFF system: Biometric trigger lock linked to Sterling-Nakamura employee database
fire modes: Semi, burst, full auto
Properties.story_hooks: An AS-7 with its IFF system intact was used to kill a Sterling-Nakamura executive — meaning either the system was defeated or the killer is a registered employee.; A firmware update to the AS-7's IFF database has accidentally flagged hundreds of current employees as hostiles — security teams are finding their own weapons locked out mid-shift.

Properties.description: A medium-sized autonomous combat drone the size of a large dog, equipped with a 5.56mm automatic weapon, thermal/optical sensor suite, and an AI capable of independent target acquisition and engagement. The Wolfhound can operate for 8 hours on a single charge, patrol a designated area autonomously, and engage targets matching its programmed threat profile without human authorization. It moves on four articulated legs that allow it to navigate rubble, stairs, and rough terrain that would defeat wheeled or tracked platforms. Sterling-Nakamura markets it as a 'persistent security presence' for high-value installations.
Properties.aliases: Wolfhound, AHK-7, Hunter Drone, The Hound
Properties.specifications:
armament: 5.56mm automatic, 300-round internal magazine
sensor suite: Thermal + optical + acoustic + motion
autonomous operation: 8 hours patrol, 2 hours active engagement
locomotion: Four articulated legs, 25 km/h maximum
weight: 35 kg
AI capability: Independent target acquisition and engagement
threat profiling: Programmable ROE with biometric whitelist
armor: Resistant to handgun calibers
communications: Encrypted mesh network with other AHK units
Properties.story_hooks: A pack of Wolfhound drones has gone rogue after their command facility was destroyed — they are still following their last programmed patrol pattern, engaging anyone who enters the zone, and nobody can issue a stand-down order.; Someone has hacked a Wolfhound's threat profile to add a specific individual's biometric data — the drone is hunting a person through a residential district.

Properties.description: An elegant walking cane concealing three weapon systems: a 50cm monocrystalline steel blade hidden within the shaft, a single-shot 10mm derringer built into the handle, and a contact taser in the ferrule capable of delivering a 100,000V discharge. Sterling-Nakamura issues the DPC-1 to senior diplomatic staff as a personal defense weapon that maintains the appearance of civilian propriety while providing lethal capability. The cane is constructed from carbon fiber with brass fittings and weighs slightly more than a standard walking cane — not enough to draw suspicion. The blade deploys with a twist-pull of the handle, the derringer fires with a concealed trigger in the grip, and the taser activates by pressing the ferrule firmly against a target.
Properties.aliases: Ambassador, DPC-1, Sword Cane, The Walking Stick
Properties.specifications:
blade: 50 cm monocrystalline steel, concealed in shaft
derringer: Single-shot 10mm, handle-mounted, 5-meter range
taser: 100,000V contact discharge in ferrule
cane length: 95 cm
cane weight: 0.9 kg
construction: Carbon fiber shaft, brass fittings
blade deployment: Twist-pull handle, 0.5 seconds
derringer reload: Breech-load single round
Properties.story_hooks: A diplomat killed an assailant with a DPC-1 blade at a state function — the self-defense was legally justified, but the weapon's existence is now public knowledge and every diplomatic meeting has become a security concern.; Counterfeit DPC-1 canes are being manufactured with lower quality materials — the blades snap during use and the derringers misfire, turning a reliable weapon into a liability.

Properties.description: An ultra-compact ceramic pistol designed to pass through standard security scanning systems undetected. The EDP-1 is constructed entirely from non-metallic materials — ceramic barrel, polymer frame, carbon-fiber internals — and fires caseless ceramic-tipped rounds that are similarly invisible to metal detectors. The weapon holds 4 rounds, has an effective range of 10 meters, and is designed to be concealed within a briefcase, jacket lining, or even a prosthetic limb compartment. Sterling-Nakamura issues it to senior executives as a last-resort personal defense weapon, though its obvious utility as an assassination tool in secured environments has made it the most sought-after concealable weapon in Meridian 88.
Properties.aliases: Handshake, EDP-1, Boardroom Gun, Sterling Compact
Properties.specifications:
caliber: 5mm caseless ceramic-tipped
magazine: 4 rounds
effective range: 3-10 meters
construction: 100% non-metallic — ceramic, polymer, carbon fiber
detectability: Passes standard metal detection and basic material scanning
weight: 0.18 kg
form factor: Credit card width, 12 cm length
barrel life: 20 rounds before ceramic degradation
Properties.story_hooks: A diplomat was shot dead in a Tier 4 secured conference room that had passed full security screening — the only weapon that could have entered is an EDP-1, narrowing the suspect pool to people with Sterling-Nakamura executive access.; A 3D printing schematic for an EDP-1 replica has been uploaded to the open net — the replicas are fragile and inaccurate, but they pass the same security scans.

Properties.description: While not a weapon itself, the HDP-3 is classified as tactical ordnance because of its role in combat operations. The device projects a convincing holographic image of a human figure — complete with simulated thermal signature, acoustic footstep generation, and movement patterns derived from motion-capture libraries — that can draw fire, trigger automated defenses, and deceive security systems. The hologram is projected from a small emitter that can be thrown, placed, or drone-delivered, and the projected figure walks, runs, or takes cover according to pre-programmed behavioral scripts. Against human observers, the deception fails at distances under 5 meters. Against automated systems, it is convincing at any range that the sensors can detect it.
Properties.aliases: Mirage, HDP-3, Holo Decoy, Ghost Maker
Properties.specifications:
projector size: 8 cm diameter disc
projection range: Up to 20 meters from emitter
hologram fidelity: Convincing beyond 5 meters to human observers
thermal simulation: Embedded IR emitter mimics body heat
acoustic simulation: Speaker generates footstep and movement sounds
behavioral scripts: Walk, run, take cover, fire weapon (visual only)
battery life: 10 minutes of projection
weight: 0.15 kg
deployment: Hand-thrown, placed, or drone-delivered
Properties.story_hooks: A witness swears they saw a person flee a crime scene, but security footage shows a holographic projection from an HDP-3 emitter found on the roof — someone used a decoy to create a false witness sighting.; An HDP-3 was used to trigger a SAT-2 autonomous turret into expending its ammunition on a hologram, allowing the real attackers to walk through the now-empty defense perimeter.

Properties.description: A sidearm that fires coded RF rounds which, upon penetrating the skin, broadcast an override signal to the target's neural interface that triggers a mandatory system lockdown. The lockdown disables voluntary motor control for 60 seconds while broadcasting the target's identity, location, and biometric status to law enforcement networks. Sterling-Nakamura developed it under contract with Meridian 88 governance bodies as a 'lawful compliance enforcement tool' — it is essentially a gun that arrests people by hijacking their cyberware. The round's RF signal uses an encryption key that only law enforcement neural interfaces can revoke, making the lockdown non-negotiable. Unaugmented individuals are unaffected by the RF component and experience only a low-velocity impact bruise.
Properties.aliases: Compliance, LOP-1, Law Gun, The Judge
Properties.specifications:
caliber: 6mm RF-coded compliance round
muzzle velocity: 120 m/s — subcutaneous embedding
magazine: 12 rounds
effective range: 5-25 meters
lockdown duration: 60 seconds
motor control override: Full voluntary motor suppression
identity broadcast: Automatic to law enforcement networks
effect on unaugmented: Bruise-level impact only
weight: 0.8 kg
Properties.story_hooks: Black market LOP-1 rounds have been reprogrammed to broadcast a different identity than the target's — someone is using compliance rounds to frame innocent people for crimes.; A vulnerability in the compliance signal encryption has been discovered that allows any RF transmitter to trigger the 60-second lockdown — every augmented person in Meridian 88 is potentially vulnerable.

Properties.description: A purpose-built suppressed pistol designed from the ground up for silent operation rather than having a suppressor added as an afterthought. The SE-9 uses an integral suppressor barrel, subsonic ammunition with a specialized wipe system, and a locked-breech action that eliminates the mechanical noise of a cycling slide. The result is a pistol with an acoustic signature of 22 dB — quieter than a whispered conversation. Sterling-Nakamura designed it for executive protection details who need to neutralize threats in environments where gunfire would cause panic — corporate events, diplomatic functions, crowded transit hubs. The weapon's existence is an open secret in security circles.
Properties.aliases: Hush, SE-9, Quiet Pistol, The Whisper
Properties.specifications:
caliber: 9mm subsonic, proprietary wipe-suppressed
acoustic signature: 22 dB at 1 meter
magazine: 8 rounds
effective range: 5-25 meters
action: Locked-breech, no slide cycling noise
weight: 0.95 kg
suppressor: Integral, non-removable
wipe replacement: Every 50 rounds
barrel length: 22 cm including integral suppressor
Properties.story_hooks: A man was shot dead at a crowded gala and nobody heard anything — the body was not discovered for twelve minutes despite hundreds of people in the room.; A forensic acoustic analyst has developed a method to detect the 22 dB signature of an SE-9 firing using ambient microphone arrays — Sterling-Nakamura wants the research buried.

Properties.description: A shoulder-fired launcher that deploys a weighted conductive net designed to entangle and incapacitate targets. The net spans 4 meters when deployed and carries a conductive mesh that can deliver a sustained taser-grade electrical discharge for up to 30 seconds, keeping the entangled target immobilized. The net's edge weights are designed to wrap around limbs and torso, and the conductive fibers tighten under tension — struggling makes the entanglement worse and increases the contact area for electrical discharge. Sterling-Nakamura markets it as their premier non-lethal capture system.
Properties.aliases: Spider, SNL-2, Net Gun, The Web
Properties.specifications:
net span: 4 meters deployed
electrical discharge: 50,000V taser-grade, 30-second sustained
effective range: 5-20 meters
launcher weight: 4.2 kg
net weight: 1.5 kg per cartridge
cartridges: Single-shot, reload in 8 seconds
conductive fiber: Copper-core polymer weave
tensile strength: Rated to 200 kg pull force
Properties.story_hooks: Modified Spider nets have appeared that replace the electrical discharge with a contact sedative coating — targets are wrapped and unconscious within seconds, ideal for abduction.; A Spider net was used to capture a heavily augmented fugitive, but the electrical discharge interacted with their military-grade cyberware and caused a catastrophic power surge that killed three bystanders.

Properties.description: The simplest possible flamethrower: a can of commercial aerosol product — hairspray, lubricant, insecticide — duct-taped to a piezoelectric igniter salvaged from a kitchen lighter. The flame produced is a 1-2 meter cone of burning aerosol propellant that lasts until the can is empty, typically 15-30 seconds of continuous fire. The Angry Mary is not sophisticated, not reliable, and not safe for the operator, but it costs almost nothing, requires no skill to build, and will absolutely set things on fire. It is the weapon of absolute desperation and has been in continuous use in Meridian 88's lowest tiers for as long as anyone can remember.
Properties.aliases: Angry Mary, Spray and Pray, Can Burner, Hobo Torch
Properties.specifications:
flame range: 1-2 meters
fuel: Commercial aerosol can
burn duration: 15-30 seconds per can
ignition: Piezoelectric lighter element
construction time: Under 1 minute
weight: 0.3-0.5 kg
operator risk: High — can rupture, blowback, and burn injuries common
cost: Φ5-15 total
Properties.story_hooks: A coordinated arson attack using hundreds of Angry Mary devices hit a corporate facility in Tier 2 — the sheer number suggests organized distribution of a weapon anyone can build.; A survival instructor in Tier 1 has been teaching children to build Angry Marys as self-defense tools — the ethics are horrifying but the threat is real and the children are surviving.

Properties.description: A vehicle-mounted improvised weapon created by modifying a motorcycle or small vehicle's exhaust system to inject raw fuel into the exhaust manifold on command, producing a jet of flame from the tailpipe that extends 3-5 meters behind the vehicle. The modification is simple — a secondary fuel injector spliced into the exhaust pipe with a dashboard trigger — and has become common enough in Tier 1 and 2 vehicle culture that mechanics advertise the conversion openly. It is primarily a pursuit deterrent, used to discourage tailgating vehicles and on-foot pursuers, but the flame output is sufficient to cause severe burns and ignite clothing or fuel leaks.
Properties.aliases: Backfire, Flame Pipe, Dragon Tail, Hot Exit
Properties.specifications:
flame range: 3-5 meters behind vehicle
fuel consumption: 2 liters per 10-second burst
ignition: Spark plug in exhaust manifold
installation time: 2-3 hours with basic tools
weight: 3 kg additional hardware
fuel source: Vehicle's primary fuel tank or auxiliary reservoir
fire duration: Limited by fuel supply
Properties.story_hooks: A street racing fatality involved a Backfire system that was remotely triggered — someone hacked the driver's ignition circuit and cooked the rider behind them.; A convoy of modified vehicles with Backfire systems has been running protection for smuggling routes — the wall of fire behind the convoy makes pursuit effectively impossible.

Properties.description: A garden hose or pressure washer connected to a water supply that has been spiked with conductive salt solution, with a high-voltage electrode mounted at the nozzle. The result is a stream of electrified salt water that delivers a sustained electrical shock to anything it contacts. The Baptism is crude, dangerous to the operator, and effective only at close range — but it can incapacitate multiple targets simultaneously by spraying a conductive water stream across a group. The weapon has been adopted by defense-minded communities in Tier 1 who mount it at choke points and doorways as an area denial tool, powered by salvaged electrical panels.
Properties.aliases: Baptism, Shock Hose, Holy Water, The Font
Properties.specifications:
range: 3-8 meters depending on water pressure
voltage: 500-2,000V depending on power source
conductivity enhancement: Salt solution in water supply
power source: Salvaged electrical panel or vehicle battery
water consumption: 5-15 liters per minute
weight: Variable — typically fixed installation
operator risk: Extreme if grounding is improper
Properties.story_hooks: A Baptism system installed at a community entrance killed an intruder when the voltage source overloaded — the community faces prosecution while the intruder was carrying weapons intended for a raid.; Someone is setting up concealed Baptism systems in storm drains that activate when anyone steps in the water — the trap is indiscriminate and has injured several children.

Properties.description: An improvised thermite incendiary device constructed from commercially available iron oxide and aluminum powder packed into a metal container with a magnesium ribbon fuse. The Brimstone burns at approximately 2,500°C for 10-15 seconds, producing molten iron that will burn through virtually any material it contacts — steel plate, engine blocks, vault doors, and human tissue with equal indifference. The device cannot be extinguished once ignited and produces intense white light and acrid smoke. The components are available from industrial supply outlets without restriction, and the assembly requires no specialized knowledge — recipes circulate freely through Tier 1 fabrication networks.
Properties.aliases: Brimstone, Hell Egg, Thermite Bomb, The Melter
Properties.specifications:
burn temperature: approximately 2,500°C
burn duration: 10-15 seconds
penetration: Will burn through 15mm mild steel
ignition: Magnesium ribbon fuse, 3-second delay
weight: 0.5-1.5 kg depending on container
components: Iron oxide powder, aluminum powder, metal container
countermeasure: Cannot be extinguished — must burn out
construction time: 20 minutes with available materials
Properties.story_hooks: A series of vault breaches across Tier 2 all used Brimstone devices to melt through the doors — the thermite composition analysis shows identical chemical ratios, indicating a single supplier.; Someone is dropping Brimstone devices through storm drains into the underground tunnel networks, targeting infrastructure — the fires are unreachable by emergency services.

Properties.description: A handheld ultrasonic weapon cobbled from salvaged industrial cleaning equipment and a focusing horn fashioned from sheet metal. The Choir Boy emits a concentrated beam of ultrasonic energy at frequencies between 20-40 kHz, causing intense pain, disorientation, and at close range, tissue damage to soft organs. The name comes from the high-pitched whine the device produces at the edge of human hearing — a sound operators describe as angelic right before it becomes agonizing. Build quality varies from surprisingly sophisticated to genuinely dangerous to the user.
Properties.aliases: Choir Boy, Screamer, Ear Splitter, The Singer
Properties.specifications:
frequency: 20-40 kHz variable
power output: 140-160 dB depending on build
effective range: 3-15 meters directional
power source: Salvaged industrial battery packs
weight: 1.2-2.5 kg
operation time: 30-90 seconds continuous before overheating
Properties.story_hooks: A wave of Choir Boy attacks in Tier 1 has left dozens with permanent hearing damage — someone is distributing pre-built units for free along with target lists.; A modified Choir Boy has been tuned to interfere with a specific frequency used by Diaspora neural interfaces, causing temporary disconnection — for some users, that disconnection is psychologically devastating.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Confession' Modified Industrial Nail Gun

Properties.description: A construction-grade pneumatic nail gun modified for anti-personnel use by removing the contact safety, extending the barrel with a rifled sleeve, and upgrading the pneumatic charge to industrial compressor levels. The result fires hardened steel framing nails with enough velocity to penetrate light body armor at close range. The weapon is cheap, ammunition is available at any construction supply outlet, and the modifications can be performed with basic tools in under an hour. It has become the signature weapon of Tier 1 enforcement gangs who need deniable armament that can be sourced without touching the weapons black market.
Properties.aliases: Confession, Nail Driver, Crucifier, The Carpenter
Properties.legality: Prohibited — modified industrial tool as weapon
Properties.specifications:
ammunition: 90mm hardened steel framing nails
magazine: 30-nail strip
effective range: 3-12 meters
penetration: Light body armor at 5 meters
rate of fire: Semi-automatic, 2 nails per second
weight: 2.8 kg
power source: Modified pneumatic charge canister, 60 shots per canister
Properties.story_hooks: A series of crucifixion-style killings in Tier 1 — victims pinned to walls with framing nails — has the signature of a single modified nail gun based on the nail batch markings.; A hardware chain is quietly tracking bulk nail purchases and selling the data to corporate security — mapping the supply chain of improvised weapons from the retail end.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Copperhead' Battery Acid Squirt Gun

Properties.description: A modified water pistol or garden sprayer filled with concentrated sulfuric acid harvested from industrial batteries. The Copperhead is the acid attack weapon of Meridian 88's most desperate and vicious operators — cheap to build, easy to conceal, and capable of causing disfiguring chemical burns that no amount of medical treatment can fully repair. The acid is typically concentrated by boiling down battery electrolyte on a hot plate, a process that is itself dangerous and has caused numerous chemical injuries to the builders. The weapon's primary purpose is not killing but terrorizing — the threat of permanent disfigurement is used for intimidation, extortion, and punishment.
Properties.aliases: Copperhead, Acid Squirter, Battery Bleeder, Spit
Properties.specifications:
range: 1-3 meters depending on sprayer type
capacity: 50-500ml depending on container
acid concentration: Variable — typically 30-60% sulfuric acid
container: Modified water pistol, spray bottle, or garden sprayer
weight: 0.2-1.5 kg loaded
construction: Trivial — fill container with acid
countermeasure: Immediate water dilution, medical alkaline flush
Properties.story_hooks: An acid attack campaign targeting augmented individuals is dissolving the skin around cybernetic implant interfaces, causing rejection reactions — the attacks are motivated by anti-augmentation ideology.; A Tier 1 gang is using Copperhead threats as an extortion tool — business owners pay or their employees get acid in the face. Someone needs to shut it down before it escalates.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Dead Man's Hand' Cyber-Integrated Holdout

Properties.description: A single-shot firearm integrated into a prosthetic hand or cybernetic forearm, typically chambered for a heavy-caliber round and fired by a neural trigger linked to the user's interface. The barrel is concealed within the forearm or palm cavity, and the round exits through a disguised port in the palm or between the knuckles. Dead Man's Hand builds are the ultimate concealed weapon — they pass physical pat-downs because they are part of the user's body, and they pass weapons scans because the components are distributed throughout the prosthetic's existing structure. The trade-off is single-shot capacity and the risk of catastrophic damage to the user's own cyberlimb on firing.
Properties.aliases: Dead Man's Hand, Palm Gun, Handshake Special, Last Word
Properties.specifications:
caliber: Variable — typically .45 ACP or 12-gauge slug equivalent
capacity: 1 round
firing mechanism: Neural interface trigger
concealment: Integrated into prosthetic hand/forearm structure
barrel length: 8-15 cm depending on integration
reload: Manual, requires opening maintenance panel
cyberlimb damage risk: 15-30% chance of structural damage per firing
weight: Added 0.3-0.5 kg to prosthetic mass
Properties.story_hooks: A handshake killed a man — the Dead Man's Hand fired during what appeared to be a greeting, and the neural trigger log shows it was deliberate, not accidental.; A cyberlimb clinic is offering Dead Man's Hand integration as an unadvertised service — someone needs to find out who is buying and what they are planning.

Properties.description: A modified paint sprayer loaded with a flammable gel mixture — typically a combination of spray paint, petroleum jelly, and grain alcohol — that produces a sticky, burning stream used for both arson and literal weaponized graffiti. The Ghostwriter fires a 2-meter stream of flaming gel that adheres to surfaces and burns for 30-60 seconds, long enough to permanently mark concrete and steel with scorched patterns. Operators use it to burn political messages, territorial markers, and threat sigils directly into building facades. It is simultaneously a weapon and an art tool, and the most skilled Ghostwriters are respected in Tier 1 culture for their ability to burn elaborate images under pressure.
Properties.aliases: Ghostwriter, Paint Torch, Flame Tag, The Spray
Properties.specifications:
range: 1-3 meters gel stream
fuel: Flammable gel mixture (paint + petroleum jelly + alcohol)
burn duration: 30-60 seconds on surfaces
reservoir: 1-2 liters, good for 3-5 tags or 15 seconds continuous
weight: 1.5-3 kg loaded
ignition: Piezoelectric lighter element at nozzle
adherence: Gel sticks to vertical and overhead surfaces
construction: Modified pump-action paint sprayer
Properties.story_hooks: A Ghostwriter artist known only by their burn-mark style has been leaving prophetic messages scorched into corporate buildings — the messages have been accurately predicting corporate actions weeks before they happen.; A Ghostwriter attack on a residential building went wrong when the gel ignited inside the sprayer, killing the operator — their dying burn-mark is being treated as a martyr's last word.

Properties.description: Improvised caltrops fabricated from broken glass, bent nails, or 3D-printed polymer spikes designed to puncture footwear and vehicle tires. Glass Garden caltrops are scattered in pursuit paths, around defensive positions, or across roadways as area denial tools. The most common variant uses heat-bent roofing nails welded at angles so that one point always faces upward regardless of how the device lands. More sophisticated versions include hollow spikes containing irritant compounds that release into the puncture wound. The name comes from the practice of scattering them across an area like seeds — from above, a deployed field of caltrops on dark pavement is invisible until you step on one.
Properties.aliases: Glass Garden, Spike Seeds, Floor Fangs, Scatter
Properties.specifications:
construction: Bent nails, broken glass, or 3D-printed polymer
spike height: 2-4 cm
deployment density: 20-50 per square meter for effective coverage
weight: 2-5 grams each
packaging: Typically carried in cloth bags of 100-500
cost per unit: Φ0.10-0.50 depending on construction
effective against: Foot traffic, standard vehicle tires, thin-soled footwear
Properties.story_hooks: A major transit route has been seeded with thousands of caltrops embedded with a slow-acting corrosive — vehicles that drive over them experience tire failure hours later, far from the deployment site.; Someone is deploying caltrops around the perimeter of a Tier 1 medical clinic every night, preventing patients from reaching the entrance — the clinic is treating people the deployer wants dead.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Gutter Psalm' Reclaimed Pipe Shotgun

Properties.description: A single-shot break-action shotgun fabricated from reclaimed industrial pipe, a door hinge, and whatever firing mechanism the builder had on hand. The Gutter Psalm pattern has proliferated across Meridian 88's lower tiers through hand-copied fabrication sheets passed between squatter communities. Each one is unique but follows the same basic geometry — a length of Schedule 40 pipe, a crude breech block, and a striker fashioned from a nail or bolt. They are dangerously unreliable, occasionally lethal to the operator, and absolutely everywhere.
Properties.aliases: Gutter Psalm, Pipe Banger, Prayer Stick, Sewer Special
Properties.specifications:
gauge: variable, accepts most 12-gauge shells with shimming
capacity: 1 round
effective range: 2-8 meters
weight: 1.5-3 kg depending on pipe stock
failure rate: estimated 1 in 40 firings results in breech rupture
Properties.story_hooks: A community organizer in Tier 1 has been distributing improved Gutter Psalm schematics with better breech designs — someone wants to know who is arming the lower tiers.; A rash of breech rupture injuries at a free clinic all trace back to a single batch of defective pipe stock deliberately introduced into the supply chain.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Judas Cradle' Electrified Knuckle Frame

Properties.description: A set of articulated steel knuckle guards wired to a concealed capacitor pack worn at the wrist, delivering a high-voltage discharge on impact. The design originated in bare-knuckle fighting circuits in Tier 1 where augmented fighters needed an equalizer against opponents with reinforced skeletal systems. The discharge is enough to override pain suppression firmware in most commercial-grade cyberware, forcing augmented opponents to feel every hit. Build quality varies wildly — some are precision-machined, others are scrap metal and electrical tape.
Properties.aliases: Judas Cradle, Sparknuckles, Zap Hands, Judas
Properties.specifications:
discharge voltage: 800-2,000V depending on build
capacitor recharge: 3-5 seconds between strikes
weight: 0.3-0.6 kg per hand
power source: Wrist-mounted lithium capacitor, 40-60 strikes per charge
construction: Ranges from machined titanium to salvage steel
Properties.story_hooks: A fighting circuit promoter has started requiring Judas Cradles for all competitors — the resulting injuries are drawing attention from people who profit from the fighters staying healthy.; A new variant is circulating that delivers a data-injection payload along with the shock — it's not just hurting people, it's hacking their cyberware on contact.

Properties.description: A retractable monofilament garrote concealed within a standard-looking wristwatch or bracelet. The wire extends from a spring-loaded spool hidden in the band, deploying approximately 60cm of cutting filament that can be used as a traditional garrote or whipped as a short-range slashing weapon. The filament is not true monofilament — it is a braided carbon-steel wire approximately 0.3mm in diameter — but it is thin enough to be invisible in low light and sharp enough to cut to bone with moderate pressure. Retraction is automatic when the deployment button is released, rewinding the bloody wire back into the spool.
Properties.aliases: Lazarus Wire, Choke Chain, The Leash, Wire Smile
Properties.specifications:
wire length: 60 cm deployed
wire diameter: 0.3mm braided carbon-steel
cutting depth: Through soft tissue to bone with 5 kg pressure
deployment: Spring-loaded spool, 0.4 second extension
retraction: Automatic on release
concealment: Standard wristwatch or bracelet housing
weight: 0.08 kg total assembly
Properties.story_hooks: A series of strangulation murders across multiple tiers share identical wound signatures — the wire diameter and cutting pattern match a single manufacturer's output.; A fashion brand has unknowingly begun selling bracelets that contain Lazarus Wire mechanisms — the items were inserted into their supply chain by an unknown party.

Properties.description: A sawed-off shotgun fixed to a stationary mount with its trigger connected to a tripwire or door-opening mechanism, aimed at a kill zone. The Lazybones is the simplest possible automated weapon — a gun pointed at where someone will be, rigged to fire when they arrive. The design requires no electronics, no sensors, and no maintenance — it will wait indefinitely until the wire is pulled. They are deployed in doorways, stairwells, crawlspaces, and any chokepoint where the first person through is guaranteed to be in the line of fire. The weapons are indiscriminate by nature and have killed more unintended targets — children, emergency workers, scavengers — than intended ones.
Properties.aliases: Lazybones, Door Blaster, Welcome Mat, Hello Goodbye
Properties.specifications:
firearm: Sawed-off shotgun, typically 12-gauge
trigger: Monofilament tripwire or door mechanism linkage
firing arc: Fixed — wherever the gun is pointed
effective range: 2-8 meters
setup time: 10-20 minutes
weight: 3-4 kg including mount
power source: None — purely mechanical
indiscriminate: Yes — fires on any trigger activation
Properties.story_hooks: An emergency response team lost a member to a Lazybones trap while responding to a medical call — the building had been abandoned for months but the trap was fresh, suggesting someone set it specifically to kill first responders.; A Tier 1 building has been systematically trapped with dozens of Lazybones devices, turning it into a fortress that nobody can enter without triggering multiple shotgun blasts — the occupant inside has not been seen in weeks.

Properties.description: A concealed blade mechanism strapped to the inner forearm that deploys a 15cm steel blade with a spring-loaded snap triggered by wrist flexion. The Mantis is one of the oldest street weapon patterns in Meridian 88 — simple, reliable, and almost impossible to detect under a jacket sleeve. The blade extends in under 0.2 seconds and locks in position for use as a stabbing or slashing weapon, then retracts with a manual release. Quality ranges from precision-machined titanium builds that cost thousands to bent steel and rubber-band spring mechanisms that cost almost nothing. The pattern has been copied, modified, and reinvented so many times that no single origin can be traced.
Properties.aliases: Mantis, Wrist Blade, Spring Knife, Pop Knife
Properties.specifications:
blade length: 12-18 cm depending on build
deployment time: 0.15-0.3 seconds
mechanism: Spring-loaded with wrist flexion trigger
retraction: Manual release lever
concealment: Under jacket or shirt sleeve
blade material: Steel, titanium, or ceramic depending on build
weight: 0.2-0.5 kg
construction: Ranges from machined precision to scrap improvisation
Properties.story_hooks: A ceramic-bladed Mantis was used to kill a target inside a high-security facility — the ceramic blade passed material scanning and the flexion trigger left no detectable mechanism on pat-down.; A Tier 1 community has developed a tradition where receiving a handmade Mantis from a mentor marks the transition to adulthood — the weapons are ceremonial but fully functional.

Properties.description: A commercially available veterinary tranquilizer rifle modified for anti-personnel use by loading darts with human-dosed sedatives instead of animal compounds. The weapon fires pneumatic darts capable of delivering a fast-acting sedative that renders a human-sized target unconscious within 30-60 seconds depending on body mass and augmentation level. The tranquilizer rifle is legally available for purchase in most jurisdictions as an animal control tool, making acquisition trivially easy. The sedative compounds are sourced from veterinary supply or synthesized from commercially available precursors.
Properties.aliases: Mercy, Tranq Gun, Animal Control, Sleeper
Properties.legality: Legal as veterinary tool — illegal with human-dosed loads
Properties.specifications:
propulsion: Compressed CO2, 90 m/s
range: 10-50 meters
sedative: Modified veterinary compound, human-dosed
onset: 30-60 seconds
effect duration: 2-4 hours depending on dose
magazine: 5 darts
weight: 3.2 kg
acoustic signature: 45 dB
Properties.story_hooks: A series of abductions in Tier 2 all involve victims who remember nothing between a sharp sting and waking up hours later in an unfamiliar location — the dart wounds are consistent with modified veterinary equipment.; A street medic has been using Mercy darts as an improvised anesthetic for field surgery in Tier 1 — the dosing is imprecise and dangerous, but the alternative is operating on conscious patients.

Properties.description: A concealed firearm — typically a sawed-off shotgun or heavy-caliber pistol — connected to a voice-recognition trigger that fires when it detects a specific spoken phrase or voice pattern. The Mockingbird is hidden behind walls, under furniture, or inside containers, aimed at a kill zone, and programmed to fire when the target speaks a particular word or when a specific person's voice is detected. The voice recognition uses salvaged smart-home assistant hardware, which means it is affordable, widely available, and approximately 85% accurate — the 15% error rate means Mockingbirds occasionally fire at the wrong person, which their deployers consider an acceptable margin. The weapon represents the intersection of cheap AI hardware and lethal intent.
Properties.aliases: Mockingbird, Voice Trap, Name Gun, The Listener
Properties.specifications:
firearm: Variable — sawed-off shotgun, heavy pistol, or similar
trigger: Salvaged voice-recognition hardware
activation: Specific phrase or voice-pattern match
accuracy of recognition: approximately 85%
range: Determined by firearm and placement
power source: Battery-powered voice module, 72-hour standby
installation time: 30-60 minutes
concealment: Behind walls, under furniture, inside containers
Properties.story_hooks: A prominent community leader was killed when they said their own name at their front door — a Mockingbird had been installed inside their wall, programmed to their voice pattern.; Mockingbird traps programmed to common greetings have been found in abandoned buildings in Tier 1 — they are not targeted at anyone specific, they are designed to kill whoever enters.

Properties.description: The oldest improvised weapon still in active use — a glass bottle filled with flammable liquid with a cloth wick. In 2200, the Molotov has evolved: Tier 1 chemists mix industrial solvents with gelling agents to create sticky napalm variants that burn hotter, longer, and cling to surfaces. The weapon remains effective against vehicles, barricades, and personnel because fire does not care about armor ratings or augmentation levels. It is the great equalizer of asymmetric conflict.
Properties.aliases: Molotov, Fire Bottle, Cocktail, Street Fire
Properties.specifications:
fuel: Gelled industrial solvent mix
burn temperature: 800-1200°C depending on formulation
burn duration: 30-90 seconds
splash radius: 2-3 meters
weight: 0.5-1 kg
cost: Φ2-10 in materials
construction time: 5 minutes
Properties.story_hooks: A coordinated Molotov attack using a new adhesive gel formulation has set an entire corporate checkpoint ablaze — the gel cannot be extinguished with water and sticks to riot shields.; A chemist in Tier 1 has developed a Molotov formula that burns with a specific color based on chemical additives — gangs are using color-coded fire as territorial signals visible across districts.

Properties.description: A high-powered laser weapon disguised as — or built from — industrial laser cutting modules stacked in series within a tube roughly the size of a flashlight. The Prophet concentrates coherent light into a beam capable of causing instant retinal destruction at distance and thermal burns on skin with sustained exposure. The build uses commercially available laser diodes intended for industrial cutting applications, wired in parallel to achieve dangerous power levels. The weapon is favored by street-level operators for its concealability, silence, and the terrifying precision of a weapon that can blind someone from across a room before they know they are being targeted.
Properties.aliases: Prophet, Pointer Gun, Pen Laser, God's Finger
Properties.specifications:
beam type: Visible coherent light, 450nm wavelength
power output: 5-20W depending on diode count
effective range: Line of sight, lethal to eyes at 500+ meters
thermal effect: Second-degree burns at 5 meters with 3-second exposure
weight: 0.3-0.8 kg
power source: Lithium cell pack, 2-5 minutes continuous
concealability: Flashlight or pen-sized form factor
Properties.story_hooks: A sniper-style blinding campaign has left fourteen people permanently blind in a Tier 2 commercial district — the attacks are precise, targeted, and the weapon leaves no ballistic evidence.; A batch of Prophet builds is circulating that use an unstable diode configuration prone to thermal runaway — the weapons are blinding their users as often as their targets.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Rat King' Cluster Munition Launcher

Properties.description: A improvised launcher cobbled from plumbing fixtures that fires a cluster of small explosive charges bound together with wire — typically six to ten individual charges that separate in flight and scatter across a 5-meter area upon a crude airburst fuse. Each sub-munition is roughly equivalent to a large firecracker in explosive yield, individually non-lethal but collectively capable of causing severe fragmentation injuries, starting fires, and creating enough chaos to cover a retreat or ambush. The Rat King pattern originated in Tier 1 gang warfare and has spread through fabrication networks.
Properties.aliases: Rat King, Cluster Banger, Scatter Gun, Party Favors
Properties.specifications:
sub-munitions: 6-10 per cluster
launch range: 20-60 meters
scatter radius: 5 meters
individual charge yield: approximately 5g equivalent
fragmentation: Wire binding and casing debris
weight: 1.5-2.5 kg launcher, 0.8 kg per cluster
reliability: Approximately 70% — duds and premature detonation are common
Properties.story_hooks: Rat King clusters have started appearing with military-grade sub-munitions instead of improvised charges — someone is feeding real ordnance into the street weapon supply chain.; A Tier 1 community has developed Rat King variants designed specifically to disable surveillance drones — they call it pest control.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Rebar Rose' Improvised Spike Mace

Properties.description: A length of concrete rebar bent into a handle shape with short sections of rebar welded perpendicular to the shaft, creating a crude spiked mace. The Rebar Rose is found throughout Tier 1 wherever construction salvage is available — it requires only a length of rebar, a welding arc, and the willingness to carry something that looks like a medieval weapon reimagined by an industrial accident. Despite its crude appearance, the weapon is brutally effective: the rebar spikes concentrate impact force into small areas, defeating soft armor through penetration rather than blunt force, and the heavy steel construction makes each swing potentially lethal.
Properties.aliases: Rebar Rose, Spike Club, Iron Flower, The Bouquet
Properties.specifications:
shaft length: 40-60 cm
spike count: 4-8 welded perpendicular sections
spike length: 5-10 cm
total weight: 2-4 kg depending on rebar gauge
material: Mild steel construction rebar
construction time: 30 minutes with welding equipment
concealment: Difficult — typically carried openly or in a duffel bag
Properties.story_hooks: A community defense group in Tier 1 has standardized on Rebar Rose weapons and organized patrol schedules — they are providing security where none existed, but their methods are increasingly violent.; A distinctive Rebar Rose with a specific welding pattern has been found at multiple crime scenes — the welder's signature is as unique as a fingerprint to someone who knows what to look for.

Properties.description: A weapon constructed from salvaged motorcycle chain weighted at the tip with a sharpened steel slug, often augmented with welded barbs or razor wire wrapping. The Scorpion Tail has a 1.5-meter reach and can be swung with enough force to crack bone through light armor, while the weighted tip and barbs tear flesh on contact. It folds compact for concealment along a belt or inside a coat sleeve and deploys instantly with a flick of the wrist. The weapon has deep roots in Tier 1 street culture where it serves as both a personal defense weapon and a status symbol — the condition, decoration, and customization of a fighter's chain tells their history.
Properties.aliases: Scorpion Tail, Chain Whip, Rattler, The Stinger
Properties.specifications:
chain length: 1.5 meters
tip weight: 200-400g sharpened steel slug
barb configuration: Variable — razor wire, welded spikes, or hooked links
folded length: 20 cm coiled
weight: 0.8-1.5 kg depending on chain gauge
material: Salvaged motorcycle or industrial chain
Properties.story_hooks: A fighting tournament in Tier 1 exclusively uses Scorpion Tails and has become a major gambling draw — the prize pool has attracted corporate attention and the fighters are being scouted as assets.; A specific chain whip style with distinctive link markings has appeared across three unrelated crime scenes — the markings indicate a single forge source that someone wants found.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Spiderbite' Electrified Barbed Wire Launcher

Properties.description: A spring-loaded tube launcher that fires a compressed bundle of electrified barbed wire that expands on release, creating a 3-meter tangle of sharp, shocking wire that wraps around anything in its path. The wire is standard concertina barbed wire crimped to a battery-powered electrode that delivers repeated electrical shocks through the barbs. The weapon is designed to entangle and incapacitate — targets wrapped in electrified barbed wire cannot move without driving barbs deeper into their skin while receiving continuous shocks. Extraction requires cutting the wire, which itself is dangerous due to the live electrical charge. It is a weapon of cruelty more than lethality, and its use is a statement of intent.
Properties.aliases: Spiderbite, Wire Tosser, Tangle Gun, Barb Launcher
Properties.specifications:
wire length: 5 meters compressed, 3-meter tangle deployed
launch range: 3-8 meters
barb spacing: 5 cm
electrical charge: 400V through wire barbs
battery life: 10 minutes of continuous discharge
weight: 2.5 kg launcher, 1.2 kg per wire bundle
reload: 15 seconds per bundle
extraction time: 5-15 minutes with wire cutters, if you can touch it
Properties.story_hooks: Spiderbite launchers have been deployed as perimeter defense around a Tier 1 refugee camp — the wire tangles are keeping threats out, but they are also keeping people in.; A serial attacker is targeting corporate security patrols with Spiderbites, wrapping individual officers in electrified wire and leaving them for hours before anyone finds them.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Sunday School' Weaponized Religious Artifact

Properties.description: A broad category of improvised weapons concealed within or fabricated from religious objects — crucifixes with hidden blades, prayer beads strung with ball bearings for use as a flail, hollowed scripture books containing pistols, incense burners filled with chemical agents, and ceremonial staffs weighted with lead cores. Sunday School weapons have proliferated in Meridian 88's religious communities where faith and survival intersect. The weapons exploit a cultural reluctance to search religious items at checkpoints and social gatherings, turning devotional objects into a delivery system for violence. The practice is controversial within the communities that produce it — some see it as sacrilege, others as the ultimate expression of a faith tested by circumstance.
Properties.aliases: Sunday School, Holy Weapon, Blessed Hardware, The Sermon
Properties.specifications:
type: Variable — bladed crucifixes, weighted prayer beads, gun-books, chemical incense
concealment: Within culturally protected religious objects
effectiveness: Variable by specific build
detection: Low — cultural reluctance to search religious items
cost: Φ20-500 depending on complexity
construction: Ranges from crude modifications to skilled craft work
Properties.story_hooks: A religious leader was assassinated with a blade concealed in a ceremonial cross — the weapon was handed to them by a congregant during a ritual and the killing was committed in front of hundreds.; A checkpoint security team has begun searching religious items, provoking a community uprising over cultural desecration — but they keep finding weapons, validating the searches they should not be performing.

Properties.description: A pneumatic launcher constructed from salvaged compressed air tanks and steel pipe that fires concrete blocks, bricks, or similarly sized debris at lethal velocity. The Tombstone uses a burst of compressed air to accelerate a rough projectile through a wide-bore barrel, achieving enough velocity to shatter bone and demolish light barriers at close range. Accuracy is abysmal beyond 10 meters, reloading requires manually shoving another block down the barrel, and the compressed air supply lasts for perhaps 6 shots before needing refill. Despite every possible disadvantage, the Tombstone fills a niche in Tier 1 warfare: it uses ammunition that is literally everywhere, and the impact of a 2-kilogram concrete block at 50 m/s is not something that body armor is designed to handle.
Properties.aliases: Tombstone, Block Tosser, Brick Gun, Headstone
Properties.specifications:
projectile: Concrete block, brick, or similar debris (1-3 kg)
muzzle velocity: 40-60 m/s
effective range: 3-10 meters
barrel diameter: 15-20 cm
air supply: 6 shots per tank at 150 PSI
reload time: 5-8 seconds
weight: 8-15 kg depending on construction
accuracy: Approximately 1-meter spread at 5 meters
Properties.story_hooks: A barricaded position in Tier 1 has been holding off security forces using Tombstone launchers — the cheap weapons are surprisingly effective against personnel, and ammunition is the rubble around them.; A modified Tombstone has been built with a narrower bore that fires steel ball bearings at much higher velocity — it is essentially a homemade cannon and someone is using it to puncture vehicle armor.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Tooth Fairy' Pneumatic Bolt Pistol

Properties.description: A modified veterinary captive bolt pistol redesigned for use against humans. The original tool — used for livestock stunning — has been adapted with an extended barrel sleeve, a reinforced bolt, and a higher-pressure pneumatic cartridge that drives the bolt with enough force to penetrate the human skull at contact range. It is a point-blank assassination weapon, silent except for the pneumatic discharge, and leaves a wound that can be mistaken for a blunt force injury by inexperienced medical examiners. The weapon's association with slaughterhouse equipment gives it a particular psychological weight that its users exploit deliberately.
Properties.aliases: Tooth Fairy, Bolt Gun, Stunner, The Dentist's Friend
Properties.specifications:
bolt penetration: 7 cm hardened steel bolt
operating range: Contact only
power source: Single-use pneumatic cartridge
weight: 0.9 kg
reload: 4 seconds per cartridge swap
acoustic signature: 55 dB — comparable to a heavy book dropping
concealability: Fits inside a jacket pocket
Properties.story_hooks: A string of apparent blunt-force homicides in Tier 1 are revealed to be bolt pistol killings when a forensic specialist notices the consistent wound depth and diameter.; A slaughterhouse worker has gone missing along with two dozen pneumatic cartridges and the facility's entire stock of bolt pistol housings — someone is manufacturing Tooth Fairies at scale.

Properties.description: Any standard power tool — circular saw, angle grinder, reciprocating saw, drill — modified for use as a weapon by removing safety guards, locking the trigger in the on position, and in some cases extending the blade or bit for reach. Widowmakers are the weapons of people who cannot afford weapons but have access to a job site. The most common variant is an angle grinder with the guard removed and a cutting disc replaced with a diamond blade, capable of cutting through body armor and bone with equal efficiency. The psychological impact of an attacker running at you with a screaming power tool is significant — it is loud, sprays sparks, and communicates a level of commitment that discourages engagement.
Properties.aliases: Widowmaker, Kill Saw, Murder Drill, Construction Special
Properties.legality: Prohibited when modified — modified power tool as weapon
Properties.specifications:
tool type: Variable — angle grinder, circular saw, reciprocating saw, drill
blade/bit: Standard industrial, often upgraded to diamond or carbide
power source: Tool's original battery or corded
weight: 1.5-5 kg depending on tool
modification: Guard removal, trigger lock, extended blade
effective range: Arm's reach
noise: 85-110 dB — extremely loud
Properties.story_hooks: A construction crew moonlighting as enforcers uses Widowmakers exclusively — their attacks look like workplace accidents and the weapons are their legitimate work tools.; A Tier 1 gladiatorial event features Widowmaker combat — fighters armed with modified power tools in a steel cage, and the audience is placing bets through corporate gambling networks.

Properties.description:
The SVCD-1 is a compact, agile drone platform built around a single, highly specialized function: the generation of precisely calibrated subacoustic waveforms tuned to the resonant frequencies of the human vestibular system. Developed by TESSERA CORPONATION's non-lethal compliance division, the drone produces infrasound pulses in the 0.5–4 Hz range directed through a focused parabolic emitter array at its ventral surface. When these waveforms intersect with a target's inner ear structures, they induce a rapid and total loss of spatial orientation — targets cannot determine up from down, cannot maintain balance, and experience severe nausea within seconds of sustained exposure.

The SVCD-1's engineering challenge was directionality: infrasound at these frequencies is notoriously difficult to focus, and early prototypes affected entire rooms rather than individual targets. TESSERA's solution was a multi-emitter phased array system that uses destructive interference to cancel the waveform outside a narrow 15-degree cone, concentrating the full effect on a single target while leaving adjacent individuals largely unaffected. The system requires continuous tracking to maintain this cone alignment, which is handled by the drone's onboard inertial targeting processor — a TESSERA proprietary unit derived from their precision manufacturing alignment systems.

Beyond immediate incapacitation, repeated or prolonged exposure has been documented to cause lasting vestibular sensitization, where affected individuals experience spontaneous vertigo episodes for weeks afterward when exposed to ordinary low-frequency vibration — engines, heavy machinery, certain music. This residual effect is not listed in TESSERA's official product documentation.
Properties.aliases: Tilt, The Wobbler, Labyrinth Drone, Vertigo
Properties.specifications:
dimensions: 24cm x 20cm x 8cm
infrasound frequency range: 0.5–4 Hz
emission cone angle: 15 degrees
effective range: 4m–20m
time to incapacitation: 3–8 seconds sustained exposure
targeting system: TESSERA inertial precision tracking processor
power source: High-output polymer capacitor array
battery life: 35 minutes continuous operation
weight: 1.6kg
documented residual effect: Vestibular sensitization, duration 1–4 weeks post-exposure
Properties.tactical_use: The SVCD-1 is used primarily to neutralize high-mobility targets — runners, combat-augmented individuals, anyone whose primary defensive asset is speed and agility. A target that cannot stand cannot run. Operators typically deploy the SVCD-1 ahead of a ground team's advance, using the drone to drop a target in place for easy approach and restraint. It is also used in vertical environments — stairwells, scaffolding, elevated platforms — where induced loss of balance carries additional fall hazard. Security teams protecting fixed positions use it as a perimeter drone, set to intercept approach vectors and trigger on any confirmed human signature.
Properties.cultural_context: The SVCD-1 is one of the few drone weapons in common circulation that its manufacturer actively markets by name in public-facing security trade publications, positioning it as a 'precision human compliance instrument.' This visibility has made it a symbol of TESSERA CORPONATION's aggressive normalization of non-lethal weaponry in civilian security contexts. The undocumented residual sensitization effect has become a source of legal action from several advocacy groups, with plaintiffs describing a life altered by vertigo they cannot explain — a condition colloquially called 'Tilt sickness' in affected communities.
Properties.story_hooks: A support group for 'Tilt sickness' sufferers has started quietly collecting evidence of undocumented SVCD-1 residual effects — and their meeting space has just been broken into, with all their records taken.; The players need to cross a TESSERA-secured facility whose SVCD-1 perimeter drones are networked to a central inertial processor — if they can spoof one drone's tracking data, the entire perimeter may be compromised.; A former TESSERA compliance division engineer is auctioning off documentation proving the residual sensitization effect was known before the SVCD-1 went to market — the bidders include journalists, lawyers, and at least one corporate cleanup crew.

Nodes.Name: Private residential tower security teams (upper district)
Freelance crowd management operators with Tier 3 licensing

Properties.description:
The Subarachnoid Shockwave Dispersal Charge is a directional breaching charge that combines a shaped piezoelectric detonation wave with a tightly collimated acoustic frequency package tuned to cerebrospinal fluid resonance. When placed against a surface — wall, vehicle hull, or floor — the SSDC-4's primary piezoelectric initiator fires a shockwave through the intervening material at a frequency calculated to couple maximally with the subarachnoid space of anyone on the opposite side within a 2-meter radius. The result is traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage without structural breach of the barrier itself.

The charge was originally developed as a counter-hostage tool — a way to neutralize armed individuals behind cover without compromising the structural integrity needed for building clearance. The engineering insight was brutal in its elegance: the wall doesn't need to break if the person behind it does. SSDC-4 units are calibrated with an onboard micro-processor that reads surface material density and adjusts detonation profile to maintain resonance coupling across concrete, composite alloy, and reinforced polymer.

Operators call it 'The White Flash' because survivors — those at the edge of the effective radius — report a blinding white visual event with no accompanying sound, followed by hours of confusion and vomiting. Those at the center of the cone are found in what breach teams describe as 'the quiet position': seated, slumped, or standing still, with no visible wounds and no capacity for coherent response.
Properties.aliases: SSDC-4, Brainbreaker, The White Flash, Liquifier
Properties.specifications:
form factor: Flat adhesive charge panel, 200mm x 140mm x 18mm
weight: 420g including adhesive backing
detonation mode: Remote trigger, timer, or contact proximity
effective cone: 2.0m radius, 90-degree arc behind surface
surface penetration: Effective through up to 280mm reinforced concrete equivalent
calibration time: 1.1 seconds automatic surface density scan
primary effect: Traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage, acute intracranial pressure spike
secondary effects: Persistent confusion, photophobia, loss of fine motor control in survivors at range
Properties.tactical_use: Breach teams affix the SSDC-4 to walls, floors, or vehicle hulls before entry, detonating it to incapacitate occupants without alerting building structural sensors or creating entry points that invite counterfire. It is also used in hostage situations to neutralize a room's armed occupants while leaving the structural geometry intact for immediate entry. Some operators use pairs of charges on opposing walls to create overlapping cones that cover an entire room.
Properties.cultural_context: The SSDC-4 occupies a strange legal grey zone in Meridian 88 — its classification as 'restricted' rather than prohibited stems from successful lobbying by TESSERA CORPONATION framing it as a hostage rescue tool. Civil liberties organizations have spent years documenting its use in labor dispute suppression and protest clearance, where the lack of visible structural damage lets operators claim no explosive device was used. Among breach specialists, owning a calibrated SSDC-4 is a professional credential — a sign you work operations too sensitive for conventional entry.
Properties.story_hooks: A journalist investigating labor suppression has evidence an SSDC-4 was used on a union meeting hall — but TESSERA's records show all units are accounted for.; A player character wakes up in a cleared room with no memory of the last six hours — someone used an SSDC-4 on a building they were in.; A calibration error in a recent production batch is causing SSDC-4s to overpenetrate — they're killing instead of incapacitating, and TESSERA is quietly recalling units before anyone notices.; A fence is selling SSDC-4s with the corporate calibration chips still active — meaning TESSERA can track every detonation.

Nodes.Name: TESSERA CORPONATION internal security rapid response
Black market resellers supplying organized crime for vault operations

Properties.description:
The SCL-1 is a slender penetrating weapon — functionally a reinforced spike 22cm in length — constructed from a non-conductive ceramic composite sheath over a tungsten-alloy core that serves as an electrode. Upon penetration of the target's skin, the weapon delivers a precisely directed electrical current along the insertion channel, propagating through tissue fluid and targeting conductive pathways — nerves, blood vessels, and implant wiring — rather than simply burning the entry point. The result is a deeply internal electrical injury that causes systemic nerve disruption, implant damage, and in sustained contact, cardiac and neurological cascade effects that are diagnostically consistent with medical emergencies rather than assault.

The SCL-1 was developed within LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS' research division as a tool for studying in-vivo electrical propagation through augmented tissue — a legitimate research application that was quietly repurposed. The weapon is powered by a slim handle unit that houses a compressed capacitor bank, delivering between one and five joules of current per activation with a charge cycle of approximately 0.4 seconds. The handle is designed to resemble a medical injector at casual inspection, and the ceramic sheath provides no metallic signature under standard scanner profiles.

The weapon's most controversial feature is its documented effectiveness against augmented individuals specifically. Neural implants, subdermal communication arrays, and myoelectric muscle enhancers all provide additional conductive pathways that amplify internal current propagation, meaning the SCL-1 causes significantly greater damage to augmented targets than to unaugmented ones. This inversion of the typical augmentation-as-protection dynamic has made the weapon both feared and sought after in contexts where augmented operatives represent the primary threat.
Properties.specifications:
spike length: 22cm
spike material: Tungsten-alloy electrode core, ceramic composite sheath
handle length: 14cm
power source: Compressed capacitor bank
output range: 1–5 joules per activation
charge cycle: 0.4 seconds
scanner profile: Minimal metallic signature (ceramic sheath)
weight: 290g
disguise profile: Medical injector form factor
Properties.tactical_use: Operators use the SCL-1 in close-contact assassination and targeted incapacitation of augmented security personnel. The spike is inserted in joint gaps, the neck, or the inner arm where skin is thin and vascular density is high. Against augmented targets, even a partial penetration into subcutaneous tissue is sufficient for implant disruption at higher current settings. The medical-device appearance allows concealed carry through many security checkpoints. Operators typically strike once and withdraw, relying on the systemic cascade effects to develop over 30–90 seconds rather than requiring sustained contact.
Properties.cultural_context: The SCL-1 is discussed in Meridian 88's augmentation communities with particular alarm — for heavily augmented individuals, it represents a specific existential threat that standard protective measures do not address. Anti-augmentation extremist groups have been documented acquiring SCL-1 units as ideological weapons, framing their use as 'purification' actions. Among professional operators, it is associated with a very specific kind of cold professionalism — the willingness to kill through what looks like a medical instrument. LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS has never publicly acknowledged the weapon's existence.
Properties.story_hooks: A prominent augmentation rights advocate is found dead of what the coroner rules a cardiac event — but a contact in the medical examiner's office noticed unusual internal burn patterns consistent with subdermal electrical injury and quietly passed the information along.; A shipment of SCL-1 units was intercepted by municipal authorities and logged into evidence — but the evidence locker was accessed three days later, and the weapons are gone. Someone inside law enforcement is distributing them, and the intended recipients are not yet known.; A player character with significant augmentation begins experiencing intermittent implant failures — subtle at first, then cascading. A street medic examining them finds a healed penetration wound they don't remember receiving. Someone used an SCL-1 on them weeks ago, and the damage is only now propagating through their systems.

Nodes.Name: Black market weapons dealers (as high-value trade items)

Properties.description: The Subdermal Ferroelectric Shear Projector fires a focused, rapidly alternating ferroelectric field pulse that penetrates the skin and induces mechanical shear stress in ferromagnetic and piezoelectric materials implanted beneath it — specifically the titanium alloy housings, ceramic substrates, and magnetostrictive actuators common in cybernetic implants. The effect on a heavily augmented target is catastrophic: implant housings fracture along stress lines, flexible circuit substrates delaminate, and the physical interface between biological tissue and synthetic components is violently disrupted. On unaugmented targets, the weapon produces a deep bruising sensation and mild muscle spasm, little more.
Properties.legality: Licensed — civilian ownership prohibited; law enforcement and licensed security use permitted under Augmentation Compliance Framework regulations
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 20 meters (full effect), 35 meters (partial effect)
field pulse frequency: Variable 50–200 Hz alternating
charge levels: Three — Compliance (mild disruption), Suppress (moderate shear), Destroy (catastrophic implant failure)
effect on unaugmented: Minor — deep tissue vibration, transient muscle spasm
effect on heavily augmented: Severe — implant structural failure, biological interface disruption, possible internal hemorrhage at implant sites
weight: 3.8 kg
shots per cell: 20 at Compliance, 12 at Suppress, 6 at Destroy
implant scanner range: 5 meters passive
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed in augmentation-heavy environments where standard lethal weapons create legal liability but operators anticipate encountering heavily modified targets. The Compliance setting is used for crowd work and initial contact. Suppress is used when a target is actively resisting. Destroy is technically reserved for imminent threat scenarios but has been used in documented incidents under disputed circumstances. Counter-augmentation specialists pair the SFSP-4 with conventional sidearms — the Cleaver disrupts a target's combat implants, and the sidearm handles the follow-up.
Properties.cultural_context: The SFSP-4 has become the single most politically charged weapon in Meridian 88's current public discourse. For the city's augmented population — which in some districts constitutes a majority — it represents a weapon designed specifically to harm their bodies in ways the law does not fully recognize as assault. 'Cleaver' is used as both a noun and a verb in augmented communities: to be 'Cleavered' means to have your implants damaged by state or corporate force. Ringo Corponation's public affairs team insists the weapon is non-lethal and that documented deaths following SFSP-4 use were caused by pre-existing conditions, not the weapon. This position has not improved their standing.
Properties.story_hooks: A Ringo Corponation internal memo has leaked suggesting the company knew the SFSP-4's implant scanner had a documented flaw that caused it to register bystanders as primary targets under certain lighting conditions — and shipped the weapon anyway. Someone wants the party to verify the memo's authenticity before it goes to a journalist.; A member of the party has had their implants damaged by an SFSP-4 hit — not in combat, but in what was supposedly a routine compliance stop. The officer who fired it claims the targeting scanner flagged the character as a high-augmentation threat. The scanner logs have been wiped.; An augmented community in the labor districts has obtained three SFSP-4 units through unclear means and is planning to use them against Ringo Corponation security during a planned protest action. The party must decide whether to intervene, facilitate, or stay out of it — and who they'll make enemies of either way.

Properties.description: The SSP-1 fires a tightly collimated beam of coherent ultrasonic pressure tuned to the acoustic impedance boundary between biological tissue and subdermal cybernetic plating. The physics are precise and brutal: where natural flesh meets implanted metal, ceramic, or polymer substrate, there exists a discontinuity in acoustic resistance. The Faultline's beam propagates harmlessly through either medium in isolation but generates violent shear stress exactly at that interface. The result is not an explosion or a puncture but a tearing — implants are forcibly separated from the tissue anchoring them, causing catastrophic internal injury without any visible external wound for several seconds.
Properties.aliases: Faultline, The Splitter, Skin Job, Shear
Properties.specifications:
form factor: Rifle configuration, 780mm total length, integrated targeting scope with impedance-mapping overlay
effective range: Up to 60 meters with full effect; degraded performance beyond 80 meters
power source: High-density piezoelectric stack array, 12 shots per module
weight: 3.1 kg
beam frequency: Adaptive, self-tunes to detected implant interface (0.8–2.4 MHz)
effect onset: 2–4 seconds post-impact
wound signature: Internal hemorrhage, implant displacement, no external entry point
module swap time: 4 seconds
Properties.tactical_use: The Faultline is used almost exclusively for targeted elimination of high-value augmented individuals in situations where forensic ambiguity is operationally desirable. The delayed wound onset and absence of external trauma create a window in which the target may not realize they have been hit, allowing the shooter to withdraw before the effect becomes apparent. Military applications include anti-cyborg operations where conventional ammunition is defeated by subdermal armor plating — the Faultline bypasses surface hardening entirely by attacking the mounting interface rather than the plating itself.
Properties.cultural_context: The SSP-1 is one of the most feared weapons in Meridian 88 precisely because it is invisible in its operation and insidious in its effect. There is no muzzle flash, no audible report beyond a low hum, and the victim typically dies appearing to have suffered a sudden medical event. Among forensic investigators and corporate security analysts, a Faultline kill is identified by the characteristic 'accordion damage' pattern visible on autopsy imaging — implants displaced centimeters from their original positions, surrounding tissue shredded at the interface. It is almost exclusively associated with state-level actors and the most expensive private military contractors, which means encountering one in a street context signals something has gone deeply wrong with the political order.
Properties.story_hooks: A prominent pro-augmentation activist dies of apparent cardiac arrest — but a street-level medic doing the informal autopsy recognizes accordion damage and knows exactly what it means.; A decommissioned ARCTURUS field unit is selling Faultline modules on the black market, and someone needs to find out who their buyer is before the weapon surfaces in a civilian context.; A player character with heavy subdermal plating realizes they are uniquely vulnerable to a weapon they've never had reason to fear before.; The only forensic specialist in Meridian 88 who can definitively identify a Faultline kill has just been offered a very large sum of money to misattribute cause of death in a high-profile case.

Nodes.Name: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS black operations units
Anti-augmentation extremist cells with unusual funding
Elite private military contractors on deniable contracts
A known but unnamed fixer called 'The Orthopedist'

Properties.description:
The SFL-4 fires a tight cluster of 24 steel micro-flechettes from a rotating drum magazine, each flechette coated in a piezoelectric polymer that activates on deceleration within soft tissue. The flechettes themselves are not individually lethal — each is 1.8mm in diameter and 12mm long — but the cluster dispersal pattern, combined with the piezoelectric activation sequence that fires as each dart decelerates, creates a cascading internal disruption effect that is grotesquely effective against unarmored targets. Against light armor, the flechettes lack individual penetrating power, but three or four cluster shots against the same panel can compromise soft armor integrity enough to allow subsequent rounds to penetrate.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's engineering rationale for the piezoelectric coating was ostensibly medical — the activation signature was derived from research into internal tissue stimulation for nerve damage treatment. The SFL-4 was developed under a security applications contract that repurposed this coating for terminal ballistic enhancement. What distinguishes it from conventional flechette weapons is the sequenced disruption cascade: the flechettes do not all activate simultaneously. The deepest-penetrating darts activate first, creating an internal pressure wave that the shallower darts then amplify, producing a disruption effect far larger than the physical volume of the flechettes would suggest.

The weapon's design is deliberately compact — it resembles an oversized semi-automatic pistol with a wide, cylindrical magazine housing — and it is deceptively light for what it does. Operators describe the firing experience as anticlimactic: a soft pneumatic 'pop' and then the target's reaction to 24 piezo-activated micro-darts is rarely anticlimactic at all. The SFL-4 has a disturbing reputation in field medicine; the flechettes are extremely difficult to locate and remove without specialized scanning equipment.
Properties.specifications:
projectile: 1.8mm x 12mm piezoelectric-coated steel micro-flechette
cluster size: 24 flechettes per shot
effective range: 20m (full cluster cohesion) / 35m (partial dispersion)
rate of fire: Semi-automatic, 3-round burst capable
weight: 1.2 kg loaded
magazine capacity: 8 cluster shots per drum (192 flechettes total)
sound signature: Low — pneumatic discharge, sub-70 dB
armor performance: Ineffective against hard plate / degrades soft armor over 3-4 hits
medical complication: Flechettes require dedicated imaging for removal; standard field extraction fails
Properties.tactical_use: The SFL-4 is most effective in close-quarters environments against unarmored or lightly armored targets. Operators typically use it as a secondary weapon for unexpected close encounters where a primary long-arm is impractical to bring to bear. In enforcement contexts, it has been used for crowd suppression at close range, though its lethality at standard settings makes 'suppression' a generous characterization. Some operators carry flechette rounds loaded with tracking compounds rather than piezoelectric coating — a modification that allows the weapon to be used for target tagging, though this requires custom drum magazines.
Properties.cultural_context: The Hornet is illegal in most jurisdictions not because of its lethality per se but because of the medical complications it creates. Several medical ethics organizations have campaigned against it specifically — the flechette retrieval problem means that wounded targets who survive the immediate hit face serious long-term health consequences even with prompt medical care. This has made it politically toxic, which in turn has made it attractive to certain operators who specifically want to create complications beyond the immediate engagement. Among street operators, it has a nasty reputation as a weapon used by people who want their targets to suffer.
Properties.story_hooks: A street medic is seeing an unusual number of patients with internal flechette wounds — the imaging signature is unmistakable — but none of the patients will say where they were shot or who did it. They're all from the same district, and they're all frightened. Someone is using a Hornet on civilians and the victims are too scared to talk.; A Zheng-Dao Bioelectric researcher approaches the players claiming the SFL-4's piezoelectric coating was derived from classified medical research that was stolen from her lab. She wants proof of the theft, which would give her legal grounds to challenge Zheng-Dao's patent and potentially shut down production. Zheng-Dao's internal security is already watching her.; A drum magazine of SFL-4 rounds has been recovered from a crime scene, but the flechettes inside are loaded with an unidentified compound instead of the standard piezoelectric coating. Someone is using a Hornet to deliver something — and the players need to determine what before the next shot is fired.
