Properties.description:
The STVP-2 generates a localized thermal vortex by simultaneously projecting two intersecting subharmonic infrared beams at a target point. Where the beams converge, destructive interference between their waveforms produces a rapidly rotating thermal gradient — a spinning column of alternating hot and cool bands that exerts torsional mechanical stress on any matter caught within it. The effect on organic tissue is visceral: the vortex does not burn so much as it wrings, producing deep-tissue trauma analogous to extreme mechanical torsion while leaving the skin surface comparatively intact. Internal hemorrhaging and structural damage to connective tissue are the primary injury mechanisms.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric developed the STVP-2 originally as an industrial tool for non-contact material stress-testing, and the weapon's lineage is visible in its form factor — it resembles a modified survey instrument more than a firearm, with a wide dual-emitter head mounted on a pistol-grip frame and a large rotary dial on the side for adjusting vortex intensity and rotation frequency. The 'Millstone' nickname refers both to this dial and to the grinding quality of the effect on targets. Operators describe the sound of a firing weapon as a low, nauseating hum that is felt more than heard.

The weapon's primary limitation is its fixed effective range of 6–14 meters — the intersecting beams require a minimum distance to converge properly and lose coherence beyond the maximum. This makes the Millstone unsuitable for long-range engagements, but within its optimal band it produces injuries that body armor is largely ineffective against, as the torsional effect penetrates most rigid materials by exploiting their own internal stress fracture lines.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 6–14m fixed band
vortex rotation speed: 40–800 RPM adjustable
beam wavelength: Dual-channel, 9.4μm and 10.6μm infrared
power cell: Zheng-Dao ZD-8 cell, 22 charges at max intensity
weight: 4.7kg
dimensions: 58cm length, 21cm width at emitter head
armor penetration: High against rigid plate; moderate against ablative mesh
charge time: 0.8 seconds to full vortex coherence
Properties.tactical_use: The Millstone is a close-to-mid-range ambush weapon. Operators typically use it from concealed positions within the 6–14m band, targeting unarmored torsos or limbs. The 0.8-second coherence delay means it performs poorly against highly mobile targets; experienced users pre-aim and trigger the charge before the target enters the optimal zone. The prohibited status means it appears almost exclusively in black market arsenals, used by operators who need to defeat armored targets without the noise signature of kinetic weapons.
Properties.cultural_context: The Millstone occupies a notorious place in Meridian 88's criminal ecology. Because it leaves minimal external marks on victims — the damage is internal — it has been used in murders that were initially misclassified as medical events. Forensic examiners have developed specific autopsy protocols to identify STVP-2 injuries, but these require specialized equipment that only high-tier coroner's offices possess. In lower districts, Millstone killings frequently go unsolved. The weapon is associated with professional contract killing and organized crime enforcement, rather than street violence.
Properties.story_hooks: A series of deaths in a mid-district apartment block are ruled cardiac arrest, but a street-level medic notices the internal injury pattern and recognizes it. Someone is using a Millstone to commit untraceable murders — and the victims all have one thing in common.; Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's official position is that no STVP-2 units were ever converted to weapons — they are all survey instruments. But a player character finds one with a Zheng-Dao military-grade power cell that doesn't exist in any public product catalog.; A black market arms dealer is selling Millstones in bulk — far more units than any one workshop could produce. Either a Zheng-Dao production line has been compromised, or someone has reverse-engineered the design at scale.

Properties.description:
The SCID-2 is a narrow-profile autonomous drone designed to navigate fluid-filled or flooded infrastructure — drainage systems, cooling pipelines, flooded basements, sewage networks, and submerged tunnel sections. At 34 centimeters in length and 6 centimeters in diameter, the Lamprey moves through pipes and conduits inaccessible to conventional platforms. It is propelled by a peristaltic pump drive that mimics biological fluid movement, producing almost no acoustic signature and no visible wake in slow-moving water. Navigation is handled by a combination of sonar mapping and a pre-loaded infrastructure dataset that Helix Biosystems licenses from municipal engineering contractors.

The Lamprey's primary payload is a hydrostatic pressure charge — a compressed liquid charge that the drone positions against a target surface before detonating. In pipe environments, the blast is directional and catastrophic, capable of rupturing reinforced conduit or breaching basement walls from the waterside. In open flooded environments, the drone can operate as a guided mine, positioning itself beneath a target and detonating on proximity trigger. A secondary payload option replaces the hydrostatic charge with a neurochemical dispersal package, releasing a water-soluble incapacitant into a connected fluid system — a capability that regulatory bodies have flagged as a potential mass-casualty tool.

The Lamprey occupies a unique tactical niche in Meridian 88 because the city's infrastructure is extensively flooded and interconnected. The lower districts — particularly the Brackwater and Sump neighborhoods — sit atop a vast network of partially submerged tunnels and service corridors that Lamprey units navigate freely. Helix Biosystems markets the SCID-2 as an infrastructure inspection and repair platform with 'optional security configurations,' a framing that regulators have repeatedly challenged without success.
Properties.aliases: Lamprey, The Swimmer, Drainfish, Pipeline Ghost
Properties.legality: Licensed (inspection) / Prohibited (armed neurochemical variant) / Restricted (hydrostatic variant)
Properties.specifications:
dimensions: 34cm length x 6cm diameter
mass: 1.8kg
propulsion: Peristaltic fluid pump, 8 chamber segments
maximum speed: 3.2 m/s in open water, 1.8 m/s in pipe flow

acoustic signature: Less than 28dB at 2 meters
payload capacity: 400g

Properties.tactical_use: Operators deploy Lampreys through storm drains, toilet connections, flooded access hatches, or any opening exceeding 7 centimeters in diameter. A pre-loaded target coordinate or manual guidance via acoustic pulse directs the drone to its destination. In offensive operations, it is used to breach walls from the unseen waterside, creating entry points or destroying infrastructure nodes. Defensive operators seed flooded tunnel networks with dormant Lampreys set to proximity triggers. The neurochemical variant, though prohibited, is reportedly used by certain factions to contaminate water supplies in targeted buildings — a slow-onset incapacitation method that is difficult to attribute.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88's flooded lower districts, the Lamprey has become a symbol of the city's infrastructure being used as a weapon against its own residents. The Brackwater community has a tradition of 'pipe listening' — pressing ears to drainage pipes to detect the faint peristaltic hum of an approaching unit. Community defense networks have developed acoustic sensors from repurposed audio equipment to monitor local pipe networks. The fact that Helix Biosystems holds the municipal infrastructure data license — meaning their drones navigate the city more accurately than emergency services — is a point of significant political anger.
Properties.story_hooks: A Brackwater community leader hires the party to clear a section of drainage tunnels seeded with dormant Lampreys — someone wants the neighborhood flooded and trapped.; A Helix Biosystems engineer has gone missing after raising internal concerns about the neurochemical dispersal variant being sold through a front company.; The party's safehouse has a basement connection to the Sump network — at 3am, something peristaltic is moving through the pipes toward them.; Someone has been using Lampreys loaded with neurochemical payloads to contaminate the water supply of a specific residential tower — residents are presenting with unexplained neurological symptoms and no one is connecting the cause.

Suborbital Acoustic Relay Drone SARD-1 'Tuning Fork'

Properties.description:
The SARD-1 is a high-altitude loitering drone designed to serve as an acoustic relay node, amplifying and directing subharmonic resonance attacks generated by a ground-based emitter to targets beyond the emitter's direct line-of-sight. Operating at altitudes between 800 and 2,000 meters, the Tuning Fork carries a phased acoustic transducer array that receives a directional subharmonic beam from a paired ground emitter, shifts its phase geometry, and rebroadcasts it downward in a tightly focused cone. The result is precision subharmonic delivery through ceilings, floors, and reinforced structures that would otherwise attenuate or block a ground-level emitter.

The drone's phase-shift architecture is its core technical achievement—conventional acoustic relay systems introduce destructive interference during rebroadcast, dramatically reducing efficacy. The SARD-1 uses a real-time interferometric compensation algorithm developed by ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC to maintain coherent subharmonic output despite the geometry change between receive and transmit angles. This allows operators to deliver resonant structural stress or physiological disruption to targets inside hardened facilities without breaching the structure or alerting occupants to the direction of the attack.

ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC initially developed the SARD-1 for geological survey work—mapping subterranean infrastructure using directed acoustic pulses—before ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS licensed the transducer architecture for weaponized applications. The survey-grade civilian variant still exists and is legally available, creating a persistent gray market where modified survey drones are sold with weapon-grade phase arrays installed by third-party vendors.
Properties.aliases: Tuning Fork, The Fork, Resonator, SARD
Properties.specifications:
operational altitude: 800–2,000 meters
wingspan: 2.1 meters
weight: 7.4 kg
loiter endurance: 6 hours on hydrogen cell
receive array aperture: 340mm phased transducer cluster
rebroadcast cone angle: 4–22 degrees adjustable
phase compensation latency: <8ms
ground emitter pairing: Single emitter per drone (proprietary handshake)
effective footprint at 1000m: ~3 meter diameter ground contact
Properties.tactical_use: Operators position the SARD-1 overhead before a breach or negotiation, using it as a silent standby asset. If a target retreats into a hardened interior space—a panic room, a reinforced office, an armored vehicle—the ground emitter operator redirects the subharmonic beam to the drone, which focuses it through the structure's ceiling onto the target's position. At low intensity, this induces severe disorientation and nausea; at high intensity, it can cause structural resonance in internal hardware, cybernetic housings, and bone density. The drone's altitude makes it nearly invisible and inaudible from ground level, and its attack vector—from above, through the ceiling—is psychologically disorienting for targets who cannot locate the source.
Properties.cultural_context: The Tuning Fork has a reputation in Meridian 88's criminal underworld as the weapon of patient operators—people who plan ahead and are willing to wait. Its deployment requires pre-positioning, emitter calibration, and altitude establishment before an operation begins, which means it is almost exclusively used by professionals rather than opportunists. Intelligence services and well-funded criminal organizations treat SARD-1 acquisition as a mark of operational sophistication. The gray market modified survey variant—sold under the street name 'Geologist'—has made the technology more accessible than ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC's legal team would prefer.
Properties.story_hooks: A corporate executive died of apparent internal hemorrhaging inside a sealed panic room with no signs of forced entry—someone used a Tuning Fork, and the ground emitter operator is still in the building's vicinity.; A 'geological survey' company operating in the warehouse district has been filing flight plans for drone operations at unusual hours—someone needs to find out if their survey drones are carrying weapon-grade arrays.; The players acquire a SARD-1 only to discover it is already paired to a ground emitter they don't have—and the original operator is actively trying to recover their drone.

Subsonic Caseless Bolt Rifle SCBR-1 'Quiet Ledger'

Properties.description:
The SCBR-1 fires a 12.7mm caseless subsonic round using a precision-engineered linear combustion chamber that burns propellant so completely and at such controlled pressure that the muzzle report is reduced to approximately 118 dB without any suppressor — well below the threshold of conventional recognition as a gunshot. Combined with an integrated wet suppressor that uses a sealed liquid baffle system, the total acoustic signature drops to 94 dB: audible at close range but indistinguishable at distance from mechanical noise, HVAC systems, or street clutter. The caseless ammunition eliminates ejection noise entirely, and the manually-operated rotary bolt produces only the soft mechanical click of cycling. At 200 meters in an urban environment, the weapon is functionally silent.

The SCBR-1 was developed by RINGO CORPONATION's advanced projects division under a research contract originally framed around 'acoustic security assessment tools' — a designation that allowed the project to proceed without triggering weapons development review boards. The weapon's 12.7mm subsonic round was engineered specifically to maintain terminal effectiveness despite reduced velocity: the projectile uses a dense tungsten core with a controlled-deformation polymer jacket that produces consistent expansion at subsonic speeds, maintaining wound ballistics comparable to a standard supersonic 7.62mm round. The trade-off is range — effective precision fire is limited to approximately 300 meters, beyond which the heavy subsonic projectile drops steeply.

The weapon's name comes from its role in RINGO CORPONATION's internal mythology as the instrument of quiet corporate accounting — the settling of debts that cannot be settled openly. It is a precision rifle in the traditional sense, manually cycled, requiring a shooter who understands patience and positioning. The wet suppressor requires replacement of the liquid baffle cartridge every 30 shots, and the caseless ammunition is proprietary to RINGO's supply chain, meaning operators must maintain a relationship with RINGO's logistics network to stay armed.
Properties.aliases: Quiet Ledger, The Accountant, SCBR, Whisper Bolt, Ledger
Properties.specifications:
caliber: 12.7x55mm subsonic caseless
feed system: 5-round internal box magazine, top-load stripper clip
action: Manual rotary bolt
muzzle velocity: 310 m/s
effective range: 300m (precision), 500m (area fire)
acoustic signature: 118 dB unsuppressed, 94 dB with integrated wet suppressor
wet suppressor service interval: 30 shots per baffle cartridge replacement
weight: 4.4 kg with suppressor and empty magazine
dimensions: 940mm (deployed), 680mm (folded stock)
ammunition source: RINGO CORPONATION proprietary supply only
Properties.tactical_use: The SCBR-1 is a dedicated precision assassination and long-range interdiction weapon used in urban environments where conventional suppressed fire would still be acoustically detectable. Operators use it from elevated positions — rooftops, upper-floor windows, parking structures — at ranges of 150 to 300 meters against single high-value targets. The manual bolt action requires the operator to be unhurried and certain, as follow-up shots take 2-3 seconds. Most engagements involve one or two rounds. The weapon's proprietary ammunition supply chain creates a natural operational security footprint: anyone using a SCBR-1 is necessarily connected to RINGO CORPONATION's logistics network, which means RINGO always knows when one of their rifles has been used.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88, the 'Quiet Ledger' is understood as RINGO CORPONATION's signature. When a high-profile figure dies from what forensics eventually identifies as a 12.7mm subsonic caseless round, the city's professional class understands immediately: RINGO has called in an account. The weapon's proprietary ammunition is a deliberate strategic choice — it makes the SCBR-1 an instrument of traceable corporate power rather than deniable street violence. RINGO does not deny this. The implicit message is that if you know the weapon exists, you know who sent it. Among the city's mid-tier power brokers, receiving intelligence that a SCBR-1 has been acquired by someone in your circle is a clear warning that a debt or a threat has reached the point of terminal resolution.
Properties.story_hooks: A SCBR-1 round is recovered from an assassination scene, but RINGO CORPONATION claims no sanctioned operation was active — either someone is lying at the executive level or a rogue operative has gone off-ledger; The proprietary ammunition supply chain has been compromised: someone is manufacturing counterfeit RINGO caseless rounds, and the first time a fake round fails in a SCBR-1, the resulting misfire will kill the shooter — who may be a player character; An operator who used a SCBR-1 on a RINGO contract has realized that the weapon's ammunition trail means RINGO can tie them to every job they've ever done — and they want out before that leverage becomes a threat; A journalist has connected three unsolved 'accidental deaths' across the city through ballistic evidence suggesting the same 12.7mm subsonic caseless round — publishing the story means accusing RINGO CORPONATION of murder, and RINGO has already noticed the investigation

Properties.description:
The SCC-9 is a proximity-triggered area-denial charge that functions not through fragmentation or overpressure but through the generation of precisely tuned subsonic acoustic pulses at the moment of detonation. Rather than a single explosive event, the SCC-9 produces a rapid sequence of 14 discrete pressure pulses within a 200-millisecond window, each calibrated to a frequency between 7Hz and 19Hz — the range most effective at inducing resonance in human thoracic and abdominal cavities. The result is severe internal trauma, disorientation, nausea, and in close proximity, rupture of air-filled organs without external visible injury.

The charge body contains a layered piezoelectric pulse generator surrounding a small conventional explosive core. The explosive initiates the sequence, but the piezoelectric stack shapes and amplifies the output waveform, converting raw blast energy into the structured subsonic pulse train. This conversion is approximately 60% efficient, meaning the SCC-9 produces significantly less structural damage than a comparable conventional charge — walls remain intact, infrastructure is undamaged — while maximizing biological effect. ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC developed the underlying pulse architecture for industrial vibration dampening before the application was weaponized.

The SCC-9 is triggered by a passive acoustic sensor that detects footfall vibration, making it one of the few charges in Meridian 88's black market that cannot be defeated by optical or thermal countermeasures. It is also extraordinarily difficult to detect passively — it emits no EM signature, no chemical trace, and its housing is ceramic composite that defeats standard metal detection. Clearance teams in the city's lower tiers have learned to treat any unidentified object on a floor as a potential SCC-9.
Properties.aliases: SCC-9, Gutterpunch, The Hollow, Resonance Mine
Properties.specifications:
weight: 420g
dimensions: 110mm diameter, 45mm height
pulse sequence: 14 pulses over 200ms
frequency range: 7–19Hz subsonic
effective radius: 4m lethal, 8m incapacitation
trigger: Passive acoustic footfall sensor (threshold-adjustable)
housing: Ceramic composite — defeats metal detection
EM signature: None
structural damage: Minimal — optimized for biological effect
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed as a denial mine in corridors, stairwells, and access points where structural preservation is required — server rooms, occupied buildings, vehicles. The lack of structural damage makes post-detonation forensics difficult; victims appear to have collapsed from internal causes. Operators use SCC-9s to defend exfiltration routes, knowing pursuers will encounter the charge without visual warning. Some operators place them beneath floor panels or inside wall cavities where they are effectively undetectable without physical demolition of the surface.
Properties.cultural_context: The SCC-9's invisibility and the nature of its injuries — internal, with no external trauma — have given it a disturbing reputation in Meridian 88's underworld. Victims are found dead or incapacitated with no apparent cause, and the ceramic housing means the charge itself is rarely recovered intact. In districts where ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC has significant presence, the SCC-9 has become associated with their corporate security apparatus — a tool for making problems disappear without obvious violence. The phrase 'hollow kill' in street parlance refers to any death that leaves no obvious trace.
Properties.story_hooks: Three bodies are found in a ZHENG-DAO server facility with no external injuries and no obvious cause of death. The investigating team finds no device — because it's still in the wall, unarmed, waiting.; A player is tasked with clearing a building that has been booby-trapped with SCC-9s by an unknown party. Standard sweeps find nothing. The only way to detect them may be to trigger one.; ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC is suing a competitor for patent violation — claiming the competitor's new 'industrial vibration tool' is a barely disguised SCC-9. The lawsuit is a cover; ZHENG-DAO wants the competitor's research, not justice.

Nodes.Name: Insurgent cells targeting occupied corporate facilities
Military EOD units (for analysis and disposal)

Properties.description: The SPC-Mk2 is a non-fragmenting concussive charge produced by Tessera Corponation's quiet defense subsidiary under a licensing arrangement that has never been publicly acknowledged. Unlike conventional explosives, the Lungcracker generates a precisely tuned subsonic pressure wave rather than a supersonic blast — the detonation is audible only as a deep, resonant thump, producing no flash and minimal structural damage. The wave is calibrated to cause severe barotrauma to unprotected biological tissue within a 4-meter radius: ruptured eardrums, pulmonary hemorrhage, and in close proximity, fatal alveolar collapse. Hardened synthetics and operators in sealed combat rigs are largely unaffected.
Properties.aliases: Lungcracker, SPC, The Whisper Bomb, Soft Kill
Properties.legality: Restricted — listed as 'acoustic research equipment' on corporate procurement manifests; actual explosive classification is disputed in three jurisdictions

Properties.tactical_use: The SPC-Mk2 is a covert assassination and crowd-clearance tool. Intelligence operators plant them in ventilation ducts, under conference tables, or behind wall panels — anywhere biological targets will be present. The lack of visible damage makes post-incident forensics difficult: deaths initially present as sudden cardiac or pulmonary events. Corporate fixers use them to neutralize witnesses in public spaces without triggering panic. In enclosed spaces like elevator cars or server rooms, even a single charge is typically fatal to unprotected personnel.
Properties.cultural_context: The Lungcracker exists in the space between 'weapon' and 'deniable tool,' which is precisely where Tessera Corponation likes to operate. Among Meridian 88's intelligence community, the SPC-Mk2 is a calling card — its use implies resources, patience, and a client who prefers clean outcomes over loud ones. Street operators who come across them rarely understand what they have. There are documented cases of black market buyers detonating them accidentally while examining the device, producing a cluster of unexplained deaths that homicide units attributed to a gas leak.
Properties.story_hooks: Seven executives from competing corporations died of apparent cardiac events at the same industry summit — a street medic doing triage noticed the burst capillaries and knows what barotrauma looks like.; A black market dealer is selling what he calls 'dud grenades' — they're SPC-Mk2s with the trigger set to proximity activation, and they're sitting in a crowded night market.; A journalist investigating Tessera Corponation's defense contracts has obtained a procurement manifest listing 'acoustic research units' shipped to a jurisdiction with an active labor dispute.

Properties.description:
The SDDN-3 deploys a cloud of 400–600 semi-autonomous micro-drones, each no larger than a thumbnail, that distribute themselves across a designated target zone and simultaneously discharge stored dielectric energy into any conductive surface they contact. Each node carries a capacitor array charged via inductive relay from the launch canister, allowing the swarm to sustain its dispersal pattern for up to 90 seconds before terminal discharge. The drones navigate using a low-latency mesh protocol, redistributing around obstacles and reforming after partial neutralization.

What distinguishes the SDDN-3 from conventional area-denial systems is its adaptive saturation logic. If a portion of the swarm is disrupted by EMP countermeasures or physical interference, surviving nodes reassign coverage zones in under 200 milliseconds, ensuring no gap in the dielectric envelope. Targets within the zone experience cascading surface charge buildup across armor, cybernetics, and exposed skin simultaneously, causing localized dielectric breakdown in synthetic materials and severe muscular disruption in unshielded organics.

Originally developed for infrastructure security—specifically to disable unauthorized drones encroaching on TESSERA CORPONATION server campuses—the SDDN-3 was rapidly adopted by paramilitary contractors after field operators discovered its effectiveness against augmented combatants. The swarm's characteristic low hum before dispersal has given it a grim nickname on the streets of Meridian 88's industrial districts.
Properties.specifications:
swarm count: 400–600 micro-drones per canister
drone dimensions: 22mm x 14mm x 8mm per unit
operational duration: 90 seconds sustained dispersal
effective zone radius: 12–18 meters
recharge cycle: Inductive relay from launch canister, 4-minute full recharge
mesh response latency: <200ms redistribution on node loss
canister weight: 2.1 kg
power source: Solid-state capacitor array, per-drone
countermeasure resistance: Partial EMP tolerance via distributed redundancy
Properties.tactical_use: Operators deploy the SDDN-3 into enclosed spaces—corridors, elevator shafts, vehicle bays—ahead of a breach to pre-saturate the zone before entry. The swarm's mesh logic allows it to navigate around cover and reposition under obstacles, making static shielding ineffective. Teams pair the SDDN-3 with hardened armor and insulated cybernetic sleeves. In open terrain, the canister is typically fired via underbarrel launcher at a chokepoint, forcing targets to either push through the swarm or abandon a defensive position. Some operators use partial dispersals to corral targets into kill zones rather than neutralizing them outright.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88's corporate security culture, deploying a Locust is considered an escalation signal—it communicates that the operator is not interested in taking prisoners or preserving infrastructure. TESSERA CORPONATION's original marketing positioned the weapon as a 'precision area-denial solution,' but its reputation on the street tells a different story. Mid-tier fixers who can afford the restricted license use SDDN-3 canisters as a status marker, displaying spent housings on their workspace walls. Scavengers prize dead nodes for their miniature capacitor arrays, which have a thriving secondary market in DIY electronics.
Properties.story_hooks: A spent SDDN-3 canister is found at a crime scene with the TESSERA CORPONATION serial number filed off—someone with corporate access is running unsanctioned operations.; A street-level engineer has reverse-engineered the mesh navigation protocol and is selling modified swarms that ignore corporate IFF signatures, drawing unwanted attention.; The players are hired to clear a building that was hit with an SDDN-3 six months ago—a cluster of nodes went dormant instead of discharging and have been slowly recharging from ambient RF, now nearly at full capacity.

Nodes.Name: Mid-tier fixers operating in industrial districts

Properties.description:
The Synaptic Drift Emitter SDE-4 operates by broadcasting a precisely tuned electromagnetic envelope that interferes with the brain's default mode network — the cluster of regions responsible for maintaining baseline conscious orientation. Rather than inducing unconsciousness directly, it causes a cascading desynchronization of thalamic relay signals, producing a state of dissociative fugue in which targets remain physically mobile but mentally absent, wandering without volition or coherent threat response. The effect is reversible within minutes of exposure ending, leaving no detectable tissue damage.

What makes the SDE-4 distinctive is its selectivity algorithm, developed by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's neurological warfare division after seven years of contested research. The emitter can be calibrated to exclude individuals wearing certified neural dampeners or TESSERA-standard cortical implants, allowing operators to move through a drifted crowd unaffected. This selective broadcast footprint earned it the nickname 'Lullaby' — it puts everyone else to sleep while leaving the user wide awake.

In practice the weapon has a distinctive soft hum at 14 Hz, just below the threshold of conscious hearing, which experienced targets have learned to associate with sudden dissociation. Veteran soldiers operating in zones where SDE-4s are known to be deployed sometimes describe a Pavlovian dread response to low ambient drone sounds — a psychological legacy that persists long after exposure.
Properties.aliases: The Lullaby, Drifter, Sleepwalker, The Quiet Gun
Properties.legality: Prohibited — civilian use; Restricted — licensed security contractors
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 0–18 meters (cone), 0–9 meters (omnidirectional burst)
effect duration: 40–90 seconds post-exposure
power source: Dual-cell bioelectric capacitor pack
weight: 2.1 kg
recharge cycle: 22 seconds between sustained bursts
collateral suppression radius: 12 meters standard, adjustable to 6 meters with exclusion calibration
implant compatibility: TESSERA Mark IV cortical shielding or equivalent required for operator immunity
form factor: Compact sidearm with rotating aperture collar
Properties.tactical_use: Favored by extraction teams who need to neutralize crowds without producing casualties that trigger political consequences. Operators typically lead with a burst mode sweep to disorient a room, then conduct their objective while targets mill aimlessly. Effective in hostage scenarios where distinguishing combatants from civilians is difficult. Requires operators to wear certified neural dampeners, which adds procurement overhead and creates a secondary black market for counterfeit shielding.
Properties.cultural_context: The SDE-4 has become a symbol of sanitized corporate violence — the weapon of choice for entities that want deniability. In Meridian 88's political underclass, being 'lullabied' is slang for having your autonomy stripped without marks left behind, used broadly to describe bureaucratic manipulation, media sedation, and pharmaceutical compliance programs. Carrying one marks a person as either a well-resourced security professional or someone with deeply unsettling intentions. Street medics have started carrying portable EEG patches to diagnose drift exposure in alley clinics.
Properties.story_hooks: A player character wakes up in an alley with two hours missing from memory and no visible injuries — someone used a Lullaby on them, but the question is what they were doing during those two hours.; A shipment of uncalibrated SDE-4 units with no exclusion filtering has hit the black market — meaning anyone using them will drift themselves alongside their targets.; A ZHENG-DAO whistleblower claims the exclusion algorithm has a backdoor that allows the manufacturer to remotely override it, potentially drifting the operators themselves.; A street preacher in the lower districts claims to be immune to Lullaby effects due to a spiritual practice — and the corporation wants to know if that's biologically true.

Nodes.Name: 'Shepherd' — a fixer known for bloodless contract resolutions
