Properties.description:
The SOG-3 is a full-hand combat gauntlet housing a dense array of transcranial magnetic stimulation coils embedded in the palm and finger assemblies. On contact with a target's skull or upper cervical spine, the gauntlet delivers a precisely timed sequence of high-intensity magnetic pulses that induce involuntary neural firing across multiple cortical regions simultaneously. The result is immediate and total motor control disruption — a generalized tonic-clonic seizure that renders the target non-functional for twelve to forty seconds, followed by a period of profound disorientation lasting several minutes.

The SOG-3's engineering challenge was achieving sufficient field strength for reliable neural induction while maintaining a chassis light enough for combat use. Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's solution was a laminated coil architecture using superconductive filament wound at near-molecular density, powered by a forearm-mounted burst capacitor that delivers the full charge in a 0.08-second pulse. The gauntlet requires skin or thin-material contact to function reliably — heavy helmets and full cranial shielding significantly reduce effectiveness, though even partial contact with an unshielded neck produces measurable impairment.

A secondary effect, noted in field reports but absent from official documentation, is the gauntlet's interaction with neural implants. Targets with cognitive augmentations — memory chips, neural co-processors, reflex accelerators — frequently experience device corruption or complete burnout alongside the induced seizure. This has made the SOG-3 particularly feared in circles where neural augmentation is common, as the loss of a high-grade cognitive implant can be professionally and financially devastating beyond the immediate physical harm.
Properties.specifications:
effective contact area: Palm and proximal finger pads, 180cm²
pulse duration: 0.08 seconds
incapacitation duration: 12–40 seconds (seizure), 3–8 minutes (post-ictal disorientation)
charges per capacitor: 14 full discharges
recharge time: 8 seconds between activations
weight: 1.8 kg (gauntlet and forearm capacitor unit)
shielding defeat: Effective against targets with less than 4mm ferrous cranial shielding
power source: Forearm-mounted burst capacitor, induction rechargeable
Properties.tactical_use: The SOG-3 is a close-quarters control weapon, deployed by operators who need targets alive, compliant, or simply non-functional for a defined window. In extraction operations, a single application drops a target without the mess of conventional violence. In interrogation-adjacent contexts, the post-ictal disorientation period — during which targets are conscious but cognitively impaired and highly suggestible — is considered operationally useful by those willing to work in ethically ambiguous territory. Operators typically pair the gauntlet with a conventional weapon in the off hand, as the SOG-3 requires deliberate contact to activate.
Properties.cultural_context: The SOG-3 carries a particular stigma in Meridian 88's augmentation communities because of its documented tendency to corrupt neural implants. Losing a memory implant to a Seizure hit is not just a medical emergency — it can mean the permanent loss of years of stored experience, professional credentials embedded in hardware, or personality-adjacent cognitive modifications. In some subcultures, surviving a SOG-3 hit with a fried implant is spoken of almost like a death — 'the person they were' is gone. This has made the gauntlet a weapon associated with targeted erasure rather than simple violence, and those who carry it are viewed with a particular kind of hostility.
Properties.story_hooks: A player character is hit with a SOG-3 during an ambush and wakes up missing the last six months of memories stored on their neural implant — including something someone clearly didn't want them to remember.; A Zheng-Dao Bioelectric executive is found in a catatonic state with a burned-out cognitive implant. The SOG-3 used was an inside job — it's registered to their own security division.; A street-level operator is selling SOG-3 knockoffs built from scavenged components. The quality control is catastrophic — some units don't stop at 0.08 seconds.; The players are hired to deliver a corporate whistleblower alive and cognitively intact, but the extraction route is guarded by a team known to carry Seizure gauntlets.

Nodes.Name: Sienna Vrak (bounty hunter, known for delivering targets in post-ictal states)
The Undercurrent (data-theft collective rumored to use SOG-3s to wipe rival operators' memory implants)

Properties.description:
The Tectonic Shear Gauntlet is a powered combat gauntlet developed by Arcturus Defense Solutions for close-quarters urban pacification operations. Embedded within its reinforced knuckle array are sixteen independently actuated piezoelectric transducer nodes, each capable of generating a localized shear wave pulse timed to the moment of impact. When the fist connects with a surface — biological or structural — the system fires a cascading lateral stress fracture pattern into the target, multiplying the destructive potential of a single strike by propagating internal rupture along natural material fault lines rather than relying on raw kinetic energy alone.

What distinguishes the TSG-4 from simpler shock gauntlets is its onboard Fault Mapping Processor, a compact subsystem that reads surface impedance data through the fingertip contact pads during the half-second before a committed strike. This allows the weapon to modulate its shear frequency in real time — hardened ceramics, bone, composite armor, and biological tissue all receive individually tuned pulses optimized to their structural resonance. The result is a weapon that hits differently depending on what it hits, adapting like a surgeon's understanding of material science applied through a closed fist.

The gauntlet's external profile is deliberately understated: matte-black articulated plating over a gel-damping inner glove, with no visible emitters or power cells. Operators have noted that its subtlety is part of its psychological value — adversaries rarely recognize the weapon until after the first strike has already shattered something internal.
Properties.specifications:
weight: 1.4 kg (per gauntlet)
power source: Integrated microcell, 200 strike capacity per charge
shear frequency range: 800 Hz – 14 kHz adaptive
transducer nodes: 16
fault mapping latency: < 0.4 seconds pre-strike
armor compatibility: Fits over standard combat gloves up to 8mm composite
recharge time: 45 minutes via inductive pad
Properties.tactical_use: Operators use the TSG-4 in breach-and-clear scenarios where gunfire would compromise structural integrity or trigger acoustic sensors. Against armored targets, repeated strikes to the same location allow the Fault Mapping Processor to progressively deepen fracture networks, effectively softening armor before a finishing blow. In anti-cyborg applications, the shear pulse has demonstrated effectiveness at cracking housing around subdermal implants, causing secondary damage from fragment migration. Special forces units employ the gauntlets in pairs, coordinating simultaneous bilateral strikes to generate intersecting shear wave interference patterns capable of defeating materials resistant to unidirectional stress.
Properties.cultural_context: Within Meridian 88's corporate security apparatus, the TSG-4 has become a quiet status symbol among close-protection details and executive enforcers — the kind of weapon that says its owner doesn't need to draw anything. Street-level fixers who acquire them through grey channels often have one gauntlet rather than a pair, a practical limitation that has ironically become a recognizable aesthetic. The nickname 'The Handshake' originated in the Kovač District after a mid-level trade negotiation ended with one party's lead representative hospitalized with seventeen internal fractures — the other party's representative was never charged, as no weapon was recovered.
Properties.story_hooks: A prototype TSG-5 with an unlocked frequency ceiling has gone missing from an Arcturus R&D facility — it is capable of shear pulses that can fracture load-bearing columns, and someone is using it to systematically destabilize a rival corporation's headquarters building.; The players are hired to authenticate a pair of TSG-4s being sold at a black market auction — but the serial numbers trace back to a classified operation that Arcturus officially denies ever occurred.; A street doctor in the Sublevel circuits has been seeing a pattern of internal injuries consistent with TSG-4 use, all from victims who share one employer — she wants someone to find out who is wearing the gauntlet before her next patient doesn't survive.

Nodes.Name: Corporate enforcers operating under diplomatic immunity
Breach specialists in Tier 4 mercenary outfits
Underground pit fighters in the Sublevel circuits
'Gantry' Velasco, independent contractor and former ADS field tester

Properties.description:
The TODD-2 operates as a swarm-capable photonic denial platform — each individual unit is a flat hexagonal tile roughly 12 cm across, housing a phased array of micro-lensed emitters that produce precisely sculpted coherent light interference patterns. When a single unit detects a target via thermal or motion signature, it positions itself in the subject's visual cone and activates its pattern array, producing a persistent false-geometry overlay in the target's visual field — not blindness, but a convincing spatial hallucination that makes distances, edges, and surfaces unreliable. Targets frequently walk into walls, misjudge step heights, or freeze entirely trying to parse contradictory spatial data.

The TODD-2's genuine tactical edge emerges when multiple units coordinate. Three or more tiles triangulating a single target can produce a full 270-degree interference envelope, effectively trapping the target in a bubble of fabricated geometry. Operators describe the effect as 'putting someone inside a painting.' The swarm communicates via low-power mesh radio with negligible emissions signature, making electronic detection difficult. VANTABLACK MEDIA's involvement in its development is rarely advertised but evident in the emitter array's lineage — it borrows heavily from their immersive architectural projection systems.

The tiles are fragile by drone standards and were never designed for contested airspace. They perform poorly in rain and fail entirely in direct high-lumen environments. Their power cells last approximately 40 minutes at full interference output, after which they return to a designated recovery point or drop to the ground inert.
Properties.specifications:
dimensions: 12 cm hexagonal tile, 1.8 cm depth
weight: 0.19 kg per unit
typical deployment: 6–12 units per operation
interference range: Effective up to 4 m per unit
swarm envelope: Up to 270° visual disruption with 3+ coordinated units
effect duration: Persistent while target remains in range
battery life: 38–42 minutes at full output
flight mode: Near-silent ducted-fan hover, ceiling 12 m
failure conditions: Rain, >8,000 lux ambient light, strong RF jamming
countermeasures: Ocular implants with interference filtering (licensed tier), physical blindfold
Properties.tactical_use: TODD-2 swarms are used almost exclusively for non-lethal containment, high-value capture operations, and crowd control in enclosed spaces. Security firms use them to immobilize individuals without physical confrontation. Criminal organizations deploy them to disorient guards during heists. The tiles are typically seeded through ventilation access or dropped from a building edge before an operation begins. Experienced operators pre-position recovery nets so tiles can be retrieved — they're expensive and traceable if left behind.
Properties.cultural_context: VANTABLACK MEDIA publicly produces immersive installation art and corporate event environments. The TODD-2's existence is one of Meridian 88's more poorly-kept open secrets — media critics have noted that the company's flagship 'Sensory Architecture' exhibitions produce strikingly similar disorientation effects to documented TODD-2 deployments. The drone has become associated with a particular kind of violence that the city's upper tier prefers: clean, deniable, and aesthetically coherent. Victims of TODD-2 encounters frequently report lasting difficulty with spatial perception, an effect VANTABLACK's legal team characterizes as 'pre-existing anxiety.'
Properties.story_hooks: A prominent architect claims she experienced a TODD-2 attack inside a VANTABLACK MEDIA exhibition opening — but the company's lawyers argue she simply had a dissociative episode during an immersive installation. The line between art and weapon is precisely what's on trial.; Someone is deploying TODD-2 units in the Underbelly transit corridors with no apparent objective — targets are disoriented for forty minutes and then released. No theft, no assault. The pattern suggests rehearsal.; A recovered TODD-2 tile has firmware that doesn't match any known variant. The interference pattern it produces isn't designed to disorient — it's designed to implant a specific false memory of a location the target has never been.

Nodes.Name: Art-world fixers and black market couriers

Properties.description: A crew-served directed energy weapon that fires a sustained coherent particle beam capable of ablating solid matter at the molecular level. The AMB-2 does not burn, explode, or impact — it disassembles the target material one molecular layer at a time, converting solid matter into a fine dust that disperses on the wind. Against vehicle armor, the beam carves through plating like an invisible saw. Against structures, it cuts clean holes with mirror-smooth edges. Against biological targets, the effect is so rapid that the nervous system does not have time to register pain before the affected tissue simply ceases to exist. Tessera developed it for precision demolition of contaminated structures, and its military applications are a source of ongoing internal corporate debate.
Properties.aliases: Eraser, AMB-2, Delete Gun, The Cleaner
Properties.specifications:
beam type: Coherent particle beam
effective range: 20-300 meters
abalation rate: 2mm of hardened steel per second of sustained exposure
power source: Vehicle-mounted fusion generator
beam diameter: 5 cm focused
weight: 120 kg on tripod (plus generator)
crew: 2 operators
continuous operation: 60 seconds before emitter cooling required
cooling period: 90 seconds
Properties.story_hooks: A building wall was cut open with mirror-smooth edges in a perfect rectangle — nothing in the conventional weapons catalog makes cuts like that, but a Tessera AMB-2 does.; A Tessera engineer has leaked that the AMB-2's particle beam has an unintended secondary effect — the molecular dust it produces is carcinogenic, and contamination zones around test sites are making people sick years later.

Nodes.Name: Tessera Industries Blackout Carbine BC-4 'Lights Out'

Properties.description: A compact carbine that fires rounds containing Tessera's proprietary PhotoNull compound — a substance that absorbs and suppresses photonic activity within a 3-meter radius of the impact point for approximately 60 seconds. Within the affected zone, all light is absorbed: lamps go dark, screens black out, laser sights disappear, and human vision becomes useless. The compound works by releasing a dense aerosol of photon-absorbing nanoparticles that remain suspended in air, creating a sphere of absolute darkness. Thermal imaging is also degraded within the zone as the nanoparticles absorb infrared radiation. The weapon was designed for tactical entry operations where controlling the visual environment is paramount.
Properties.aliases: Lights Out, BC-4, Dark Gun, Blackout
Properties.specifications:
caliber: 12mm PhotoNull compound round
magazine: 8 rounds
effective range: 20-80 meters
darkness radius: 3 meters from impact
darkness duration: 55-65 seconds
nanoparticle suspension: Aerosol, degrades naturally
thermal attenuation: approximately 70% within zone
weight: 3.1 kg
fire modes: Semi-automatic
Properties.story_hooks: An entire city block experienced 60 seconds of total darkness during which four people were killed — someone used multiple Blackout rounds to cover a coordinated assassination.; Tessera's PhotoNull compound has been loaded into building ventilation systems, creating zones of permanent darkness in occupied structures — someone is weaponizing architecture.

Properties.description: A wrist-mounted penetrating spike connected to the user's neural interface that physically punctures a target's cyberware housing and establishes a direct hardline connection to their implant network. The spike is a 6cm retractable carbon-ceramic needle containing a fiber-optic data conduit that can transmit attack payloads directly into a target's neural architecture, bypassing wireless security protocols entirely. The physical penetration is painful but rarely dangerous — the data payload is where the real damage occurs. Operators use it to inject malware, extract data, override motor functions, or in extreme cases, trigger a neural interface hard reset that can cause permanent cognitive damage.
Properties.aliases: Upload, DS-1, Data Knife, The Spike
Properties.specifications:
spike length: 6 cm retractable
spike material: Carbon-ceramic with fiber-optic core
penetration depth: Sufficient for standard cyberware housing
data transfer rate: 40 Gbps through fiber-optic conduit
deployment: Wrist-mounted spring mechanism, 0.1 second extension
weight: 0.12 kg total assembly
compatibility: Requires user neural interface for payload delivery
Properties.story_hooks: A victim was found with a DS-1 puncture wound but no data payload was delivered — the spike was used purely as a physical weapon, suggesting the attacker wanted it to look like a cyber attack.; A new payload circulating for DS-1 users doesn't attack the target — it copies their entire neural interface memory buffer, stealing the last 48 hours of sensory experience.

Properties.description: Self-guided ammunition compatible with standard 9mm pistol platforms that uses embedded micro-processing and control surfaces to adjust trajectory in flight. Each round contains a thumbnail-sized guidance package with a micro-camera, processing chip, and four piezoelectric fin actuators that can steer the round toward a designated target up to 15 degrees off the original firing axis. The rounds are 'trained' by designating a target through a linked optic — the round's guidance package memorizes the target's visual signature and homes on it after firing. The name comes from the round's ability to 'remember' its target. Accuracy degrades rapidly beyond 30 meters as the control surfaces lack the authority to compensate for ballistic drop at range.
Properties.aliases: Recall, MR-2, Smart Bullets, Thinking Rounds
Properties.specifications:
caliber: 9mm compatible with standard platforms
guidance: Embedded micro-camera + piezoelectric fin steering
course correction: Up to 15 degrees off-axis
effective guided range: 5-30 meters
target designation: Visual signature lock via linked optic
weight per round: 12g (2g heavier than standard 9mm)
processing: Onboard micro-chip, single-use
fin actuators: 4 piezoelectric surfaces
Properties.story_hooks: A target was killed by a 9mm round that forensic analysis shows changed direction mid-flight — the entry angle is physically impossible from any firing position in the room without guidance.; A shipment of Memory Rounds has been intercepted with their guidance packages pre-locked to specific individuals — someone manufactured assassination rounds targeted at a specific hit list.

Nodes.Name: Tessera Industries Metamaterial Cloak Rounds MCR-1 'Vanishing Act'

Properties.description: Rifle ammunition coated with a metamaterial shell that renders the projectile effectively invisible in flight. The MCR-1 round is a standard 7.62mm projectile encased in a metamaterial jacket that bends visible light around the round as it travels, making it undetectable by optical tracking systems and the human eye. The round is still detectable by radar and thermal sensors, but in practical terms, targets cannot see the bullet coming and optical-based defense systems cannot track it. The metamaterial jacket ablates on impact, leaving a standard wound channel with no exotic trace evidence. Tessera developed it for sniper applications where muzzle flash and bullet trace are the primary indicators of shooter position.
Properties.aliases: Vanishing Act, MCR-1, Cloak Bullets, Ghost Shots
Properties.specifications:
caliber: 7.62mm metamaterial-jacketed
optical invisibility: Visible light bending jacket, effective in flight
radar detectability: Standard — metamaterial does not affect radar signature
thermal detectability: Standard — metamaterial does not affect thermal
effective range: 100-800 meters
metamaterial ablation: Complete on impact
weight per round: 12g
compatibility: Standard 7.62mm rifle platforms
Properties.story_hooks: A target was killed by a 7.62mm round that no witness saw and no optical security system detected in flight — only the impact was recorded, making the shooter's position untraceable.; Tessera's metamaterial jacket technology has been reverse-engineered and someone is applying it to larger munitions — RPG warheads that cannot be seen until they hit.

Properties.description: A handheld directed energy device that emits a rapidly cycling pattern of high-intensity light at frequencies calculated to induce seizure-like neural disruption in human visual processing. The OD-4 projects a beam of strobing light that cycles through specific frequencies known to cause photosensitive responses — disorientation, nausea, loss of motor control, and in approximately 3% of targets, full tonic-clonic seizures. The beam is effective against both augmented and unaugmented targets because it exploits fundamental biological visual processing rather than electronic systems.
Properties.aliases: Strobe, OD-4, Flash Gun, Eye Killer
Properties.specifications:
beam type: High-intensity cycling visible light
frequency: Calculated photosensitive disruption pattern
effective range: 5-50 meters directional
effect: Disorientation, nausea, motor loss, 3% seizure risk
power: Rechargeable capacitor, 30 seconds continuous
weight: 0.4 kg
form factor: Pistol-sized handheld
countermeasure: Light-filtering eyewear or closed eyes
Properties.story_hooks: An OD-4 was used in a crowded venue and triggered seizures in eleven people — the operator did not know or care about the 3% seizure risk in a crowd of 400.; A modified OD-4 has been tuned to a frequency that specifically disrupts the visual processing of Axiom-model neural interfaces, causing permanent damage to the optical enhancement firmware.

Nodes.Name: Tessera Industries Phantom Blade PB-1 'Ghost Knife'

Properties.description: A combat knife with a blade forged from Tessera's proprietary metamaterial composite that absorbs electromagnetic radiation across the visible and near-infrared spectrum, rendering it functionally invisible to optical and thermal sensors. The blade appears as a void — a knife-shaped absence of light that the eye struggles to track. The metamaterial construction also gives the blade unusual physical properties: it is extremely hard but brittle, capable of penetrating body armor through sheer material hardness but prone to shattering if used to pry or lever. Each blade is individually manufactured and serial-coded, making them traceable — which has not stopped them from becoming prestige assassination tools.
Properties.aliases: Ghost Knife, PB-1, Tessera Blade, Null Edge
Properties.specifications:
blade length: 18 cm
blade material: Tessera EM-absorbing metamaterial composite
hardness: Exceeds tungsten carbide
optical signature: Absorbs 99.7% of visible and near-IR light
thermal signature: Undetectable to standard thermal imaging
weight: 0.15 kg
fragility: Shatters under lateral stress exceeding 40 Nm
Properties.story_hooks: A Ghost Knife was recovered from a crime scene with its serial code intact — tracing the sale leads to a Tessera executive who reported it stolen six months ago, or claims to have.; A forger is selling counterfeit Ghost Knives made from conventional metamaterial that degrades after weeks — buyers are finding their 'invisible' blades becoming visible at the worst possible moments.

Properties.description: A spool-deployed monofilament wire system designed for perimeter defense and anti-personnel applications. The wire is a single-molecule-thick carbon filament that is effectively invisible to the naked eye and most optical sensors. Once deployed between anchor points, the wire will sever anything that contacts it with sufficient force — limbs, cables, vehicle tires, drone rotors. Tessera packages it with a compact spool housing and magnetic anchor stakes, marketing it as a 'passive security perimeter system' despite its obvious offensive applications.
Properties.specifications:
wire length: 200 meters per spool
wire diameter: single-molecule carbon filament
tensile strength: rated to 400 kg before deformation
cutting threshold: 2 kg of lateral force
anchor type: Magnetic stakes with 50 kg hold strength
weight: 0.2 kg per spool assembly
visibility: Undetectable by standard optical systems
Properties.story_hooks: Monofilament lines have been found strung across a major transit corridor at neck height — someone is targeting a specific vehicle or person who uses that route.; A Tessera facility breach resulted in the theft of 200 spools of PW-1 wire — enough to turn an entire district into a kill zone.

Properties.description: An experimental weapon that generates a localized spatial distortion field at a targeted point, causing matter within the field to briefly phase between states in a way that current physics cannot fully explain. The practical effect is that solid objects within the 1-meter field radius experience a momentary loss of structural integrity — molecular bonds flicker, materials briefly become permeable, and anything caught in the transition snaps back to solidity with catastrophic misalignment. The effect lasts less than a tenth of a second but the material damage is permanent: metal crystallizes along new fault lines, biological tissue suffers cellular disruption, and electronics experience cascading component failure. Tessera's R&D team reportedly does not fully understand why the device works.
Properties.aliases: Glitch, PD-2, Phase Gun, Reality Hiccup
Properties.specifications:
effect radius: 1 meter at target point
effect duration: 0.08 seconds
effective range: 5-20 meters
power source: Experimental spatial distortion generator
weight: 12 kg with power unit
recharge: 120 seconds between activations
activations per power cell: 3
prototypes: 2 confirmed
Properties.story_hooks: A crime scene shows damage consistent with Phase Disruptor exposure — materials aged and crystallized in a perfect sphere — but only two prototypes exist and both are supposedly locked in Tessera's vault.; A Tessera physicist involved in the PD-2 project has disappeared after claiming the device does not distort space — it briefly opens a window to somewhere else, and something on the other side is looking back.

Nodes.Name: Tessera Industries Quantum Entanglement Detonator QED-1 'Certainty'

Properties.description: A detonation system that uses quantum-entangled particle pairs to trigger explosive charges with zero transmission delay and absolute interception immunity. The QED-1 consists of a trigger device and up to 12 paired receiver modules, each containing one half of an entangled particle pair. When the trigger device measures its particles, the entangled partners in the receivers collapse simultaneously, triggering detonation. There is no signal to jam, no frequency to intercept, no wire to cut, and no delay to exploit. The trigger works through any material barrier at any distance. Tessera developed it for controlled demolition in electromagnetically contested environments, but its implications for the bomb disposal profession are existential.
Properties.aliases: Certainty, QED-1, Quantum Trigger, The Inevitability
Properties.specifications:
trigger unit: Handheld, 0.3 kg
receiver modules: Up to 12 paired detonators
activation delay: Zero — quantum instantaneous
interception immunity: Absolute — no signal exists between trigger and receiver
range: Unlimited — quantum entanglement is distance-independent
receiver module size: 4 cm x 2 cm
compatibility: Standard detonator interface
entangled pair lifespan: 30 days from generation before decoherence
Properties.story_hooks: A bomb disposal team encountered an explosive device with no detectable trigger mechanism — no wire, no radio receiver, no timer. The bomb went off while they were examining it, and the trigger was pressed from across the city.; Tessera is desperately searching for three QED-1 receiver modules that went missing from their inventory — somewhere in Meridian 88, three bombs are planted that cannot be disarmed and will detonate the instant someone presses a button.

Nodes.Name: Tessera Industries Sensory Overload Grenade SOG-3 'Flashbang Plus'

Properties.description: An advanced flashbang variant that attacks all five senses simultaneously plus neural interface channels. The SOG-3 detonates with a synchronized package: blinding light across visible and IR spectra, 180 dB acoustic burst, aerosolized capsaicinoid irritant, a burst of electromagnetic interference targeting neural frequencies, and a surface coating on the casing that releases a nausea-inducing olfactory compound on detonation. The combined sensory assault overwhelms both biological and augmented processing capacity, causing a 30-60 second window of total incapacitation regardless of the target's augmentation level or training.
Properties.aliases: Flashbang Plus, SOG-3, Sense Bomb, Full Spectrum
Properties.specifications:
light output: 20 million candela across visible + IR
acoustic output: 180 dB at 1 meter
chemical payload: Aerosolized capsaicinoid + olfactory irritant
EM output: Broadband neural interface disruption
effect radius: 8 meters
incapacitation duration: 30-60 seconds
weight: 0.35 kg
fuse: 1.5-second delay
Properties.story_hooks: An SOG-3 detonated in a crowded nightclub caused permanent sensory damage to twelve patrons — the grenade was thrown as a distraction for a theft, but the confined space amplified the effects beyond safe levels.; A modified SOG-3 has been developed that excludes the electromagnetic component, making it effective only against unaugmented targets — someone is designing weapons that discriminate based on augmentation status.

Nodes.Name: Tessera Industries Void Grenade VG-1 'Black Hole'

Properties.description: An experimental ordnance device that creates a 2-meter sphere of spatial compression lasting 0.5 seconds — everything within the sphere is subjected to extreme compressive forces as space itself contracts, crushing matter into a fraction of its original volume before the effect collapses and space snaps back to normal. The result is a sphere of mangled, compressed debris where intact objects used to be. Tessera's physicists describe it as a 'controlled spatial anomaly' and freely admit they do not fully understand the long-term effects on local spacetime. The Void Grenade is the single most classified item in Tessera's research division, and its existence has been confirmed only by the distinctive spherical compression signatures found at two classified incident sites.
Properties.aliases: Black Hole, VG-1, Void Bomb, The Absence
Properties.specifications:
effect radius: 2-meter sphere
effect duration: 0.5 seconds
compression force: Estimated 50,000 atmospheres within sphere
detonation: 3-second timer after activation
weight: 0.5 kg
form factor: Standard grenade size
prototypes: Estimated 5 units manufactured
side effects: Unknown long-term spacetime distortion
classification: Tessera Ultra-Restricted
Properties.story_hooks: A crime scene contains a perfect 2-meter sphere of crushed, compressed matter — vehicles, building material, and three human bodies reduced to a dense ball. Nothing in any weapons database explains it.; A Tessera researcher involved in the VG-1 program has disappeared after sending encrypted messages claiming the spatial compression events are not contained — each detonation is leaving a permanent microscopic weakness in spacetime that could accumulate.

Nodes.Name: Tethered Orbital Reconnaissance and Suppression Drone TORSD-7 'Kitestring'

Properties.description:
The TORSD-7 is a high-altitude tethered drone platform designed for persistent area suppression and overwatch. Unlike free-flight drones, the Kitestring operates on a conductive monofilament tether up to 180 meters in length, anchored to a ground station the size of a briefcase. The tether serves dual purposes: it provides continuous power to the drone, eliminating battery constraints, and it carries the electrothermal discharge rail that is the platform's primary weapon system. The drone maintains a stable hover via four counter-rotating ducted fans and positions itself above a target area while the ground station operator designates firing solutions through a handheld interface.

The weapon system works by charging the tether itself to extreme voltage and then releasing a directed electrothermal burst downward along a secondary projected filament fired from the drone's undercarriage. The projected filament is a ultra-fine conductive thread, weighted and aimed, that drapes across a target or target area. On contact, the ground station completes the circuit and delivers a high-amperage electrothermal pulse through the filament. The effect on unshielded human targets is immediate cardiac and neuromuscular disruption. On vehicles or electronic systems, the pulse induces catastrophic circuit failure.

The TORSD-7's distinctive silhouette — a hovering shape connected to the ground by a nearly invisible thread — has earned it a reputation for surreal, almost supernatural lethality. Victims and witnesses frequently report not understanding how or from where the strike came. Zheng-Dao Bioelectric developed the platform for infrastructure protection contracts in contested industrial zones, but the design was widely copied and the black market variant, the 'Barefoot,' strips the IFF systems and sells the ground station as a portable backpack unit.
Properties.aliases: Kitestring, The Leash, Overhead, Wire Eye
Properties.tier_availability: Tier 5+ / Military only / Black market (Barefoot variant)
Properties.specifications:
tether length: Up to 180 meters
tether material: Tungsten-carbon composite monofilament, 0.3mm diameter
drone dimensions: 62cm rotor span
drone mass: 3.8kg
ground station mass: 4.2kg
operational altitude: 15–180 meters
discharge voltage: 18,000V peak
projected filament range: 22 meters lateral from hover position
recharge cycle: 4.5 seconds between discharges
wind tolerance: Operational up to 45 km/h crosswind
acoustic signature: 61dB at 30 meters
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed at the perimeter of a defended position to provide persistent overwatch. The ground station operator can designate targets via thermal or optical feed from the drone's sensor package. The near-invisible tether and filament make target identification of the weapon source extremely difficult — most victims are struck before understanding the threat geometry. Used by defensive teams to hold chokepoints, stairwells, and open plazas. The tether's conductive properties also allow the operator to pulse a low-voltage 'warning' discharge through a dropped filament, though field operators rarely use this setting.
Properties.cultural_context: The Kitestring is associated with paranoia and contested space in Meridian 88. In neighborhoods where territorial disputes are common, residents have developed the habit of looking up before crossing open areas — a behavior the local press has termed 'wirewalker's reflex.' The drone's silence and the nearly invisible nature of the tether have made it a subject of urban legend, with some communities attributing unexplained deaths to 'the leash' without being able to prove the weapon's presence. Corporate zones that deploy TORSD-7 systems do not advertise the fact, and the drones are painted to match sky conditions.
Properties.story_hooks: Three bodies have been found in an open plaza with identical cardiac trauma and no visible entry wounds — the local fixer suspects a Kitestring deployment but needs someone to find the ground station anchor point.; A corporate whistleblower is hiding in a building surrounded by an active TORSD-7 perimeter — the party needs to map the tether geometry before attempting extraction.; Someone is selling Barefoot variant ground stations out of a transit locker network — the components are traced to a Zheng-Dao Bioelectric assembly plant with an inside source.; A street kid found what she thought was a fishing line in an alleyway and pulled it — she's in a burn ward now, and her older brother wants the operator's name.

Nodes.Name: High-value corporate site perimeter defense teams
Well-funded territorial gang operations in the outer industrial zones
Black market arms dealers offering the 'Barefoot' variant to mid-tier operators
A known mercenary unit called the Filament Boys, who use the platform as their signature

Properties.description: The TIBC-1 is a magnetically-attached breaching device that uses a staged linear magnetic acceleration system to drive a superheated copper plasma jet through structural barriers at velocities exceeding 2,400 meters per second. Unlike conventional shaped charges that rely on chemical explosive force alone, the Slagwall's magnetic acceleration stage adds a secondary kinetic component that allows it to defeat composite armor plating, reinforced corporate vault doors, and the layered ceramic-steel construction standard in Meridian 88's high-security facilities. The device adheres via four industrial-grade magnetic feet and arms automatically upon contact with ferrous surfaces.
Properties.specifications:
weight: 2.3 kg
dimensions: 22 cm x 18 cm x 6 cm
penetration rating: Up to 28 cm reinforced composite
plasma jet velocity: ~2,400 m/s
detonation modes: Immediate (0.5 second arm), Delayed (5–60 seconds), Remote
safe standoff distance: 12 m minimum
magnetic adhesion rating: Holds on vertical ferrous surfaces up to 40 kg lateral load
back-blast hazard: Severe — 4 m rear exclusion zone
Properties.tactical_use: Purpose-built for breach operations against hardened facilities. Security contractors slap a TIBC-1 on a vault door, pull the pin, and move to standoff — the plasma jet burns a 30 cm entry hole through most barriers in under a second, allowing immediate follow-through. The magnetic auto-arm feature means it can be deployed on moving vehicles or in low-visibility conditions. PALLADIAN originally developed it for demolition and salvage operations; the security contracting market discovered it independently.
Properties.cultural_context: The TIBC-1 is technically licensed for construction and demolition use in Meridian 88, which creates a persistent legal headache for law enforcement — it is functionally identical whether purchased by a salvage crew or a heist team. PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION sells them openly at industrial supply depots, and the licensing requirement is enforced inconsistently enough that anyone with a fabricated contractor ID can walk out with one. It has become the definitive heist weapon in the city's criminal lexicon.
Properties.story_hooks: A PALLADIAN depot reports a shipment of TIBC-1 units stolen — forty units, enough to breach every major corporate vault in the financial district simultaneously. The theft was inside the depot's own delivery schedule.; A runner is hired to plant a TIBC-1 on a specific wall in a corporate building, no questions asked. The wall's location, when mapped, sits directly adjacent to the building's primary life support control room.; A salvage crew using a legitimately licensed TIBC-1 accidentally breaches into a sealed sublevel that doesn't appear on any city plan — and what's inside has been sealed for twenty years.

Properties.description: The TSI-2 is a directed energy weapon that projects a focused beam of concentrated Peltier-effect thermal extraction — colloquially described as 'a heat vacuum' — that does not freeze its target in any conventional sense but instead induces rapid, extreme localized hypothermia by stripping thermal energy from the impact zone faster than biological tissue can compensate. At full power against a human torso, the effect produces a roughly 15-centimeter diameter zone of flash-cooled tissue that seizes muscle fibers, fractures capillary walls, and causes immediate motor failure in the affected area. The surrounding tissue remains at body temperature; only the targeted zone is affected, which creates a wound pattern unlike anything produced by conventional weapons.
Properties.aliases: Cold Case, Freeze Tag, The Inverter, White Ghost
Properties.specifications:
form factor: Compact carbine, 520mm length, distinctive matte-white housing with heat-sink ribbing along barrel
effective range: Up to 35 meters at full effect; partial effect to 50 meters
power source: Liquid-nitrogen-assisted thermoelectric cell, 8 full-power shots or 20 partial shots
weight: 2.2 kg
beam diameter at target: 12–18 cm depending on range
effect onset: Immediate on contact
cooldown between shots: 6 seconds
cell replacement time: 8 seconds
Properties.tactical_use: The Cold Case is primarily used for incapacitation rather than killing — a hit to a limb renders it non-functional for 20–40 minutes as tissue gradually rewarms. Corporate security teams use it for detaining high-value targets who need to be taken alive. Bounty contractors favor it because a torso hit is incapacitating but survivable if medical attention arrives within roughly fifteen minutes, giving them a live delivery option. Against heavily armored targets, the TSI-2 is less effective as armor insulates against thermal extraction — it is specifically optimized for lightly armored, highly augmented targets whose cybernetic components are disrupted by the temperature differential.
Properties.cultural_context: TESSERA CORPONATION markets the TSI-2 aggressively as a 'humane compliance solution,' and there is a glossy corporate legitimacy to the weapon that other entries in this arsenal lack. Licensed security firms display it visibly as a statement of institutional restraint — 'we have the option not to kill you.' On the street, this reputation is regarded with deep suspicion. Operators know that a Cold Case hit to the torso is survivable only with prompt care, and corporate security is not always motivated to provide that care promptly. The weapon's clean white aesthetic and the bloodless nature of its wounds have made it a favorite in corporate propaganda depicting 'responsible force.'
Properties.story_hooks: A bounty contractor delivers a target alive but the target dies of complications from Cold Case exposure two hours later — was it negligence, or did someone slow-walk the medical response intentionally?; A stolen shipment of TSI-2 units has appeared on the black market with the licensing chips removed — someone is planning something that requires the appearance of institutional legitimacy without the paper trail.; A character is hit by a Cold Case round in a situation where medical help is hours away — do they find a solution, or does the clock run out?; TESSERA's 'humane compliance' marketing is being used in a legal case to argue that a security team acted appropriately — but a street medic's testimony about the actual wound progression tells a different story.

Nodes.Name: Certain police auxiliary units in corporate-administered districts

Properties.description:
The TCDS-3 operates by firing a magnetically-stabilized shell casing packed with a proprietary nano-particulate thermite compound developed under contract with ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS. On impact or timed detonation, the outer casing fractures along pre-scored seams, releasing the thermite payload as a cascading aerosol that ignites upon contact with atmospheric oxygen. The burn sequence is not instantaneous — it sustains for four to seven seconds at temperatures exceeding 2,800°C, flowing into gaps, joints, and ventilation channels like liquid fire.

What distinguishes the TCDS-3 from conventional incendiary ordnance is its cavity-seeking behavior. The nano-particulate suspension is electrostatically charged prior to launch, causing particles to be attracted toward metallic surfaces and enclosed spaces — door seams, vehicle chassis, armored suits, server housings. Operators describe the effect as 'painting the inside of a wall.' The weapon is particularly devastating against hardened structures because it burns through reinforcement rather than blasting around it.

On the streets of Meridian 88, the TCDS-3 is called 'Smelter' for obvious reasons. It is a weapon that leaves no survivors in a sealed space and no usable evidence in a burned-out vehicle. Corporate demolition crews use modified variants for precision structural teardown, but the weapon's proliferation into black market channels has made it a favored tool of arsonists-for-hire and syndicate enforcers settling property disputes permanently.
Properties.aliases: Smelter, Drip Round, The Foundryman's Gift
Properties.specifications:
shell diameter: 40mm
burn temperature: 2,800°C sustained
burn duration: 4–7 seconds
effective radius: 3.5m open / 8m enclosed
particle charge: -40 µC/g electrostatic
delivery system: Grenade launcher compatible, single-shot breach
weight: 0.9 kg per shell
safety window: 1.2 seconds post-launch arming delay
Properties.tactical_use: Used primarily for breaching hardened interiors — safe rooms, armored vehicles, reinforced server vaults. Operators fire through pre-drilled access points or ventilation grilles to maximize cavity exposure. Military sappers use it for structural column destruction. Syndicate operatives favor it for evidence elimination after wetwork in corporate offices. Not recommended in confined spaces without full thermal shielding — backwash kills operators who miscalculate room geometry.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88's industrial lower districts, 'getting Smeltered' is slang for any situation where someone is dissolved from the inside out — financially, professionally, or literally. The weapon carries a grim prestige among demolition contractors and a reputation for cruelty among street-level enforcers. Possessing a TCDS-3 shell outside a licensed demolition context marks someone as either very well-connected or very dangerous, often both.
Properties.story_hooks: A licensed demolition crew reports three shells missing from inventory — the shells turn up at the scene of a corporate board member's incinerated penthouse.; A black market arms dealer offers the party TCDS-3 shells at half price, no questions — the shells are stamped with ARCTURUS lot numbers that shouldn't exist for another six months.; Someone used a Smelter shell on a data vault the party was hired to crack. Everything inside is slag. The client insists the data was backed up. It wasn't.; An ARCTURUS whistleblower claims the civilian demolition variant has a hidden firmware flag that can be remotely triggered — every licensed shell in the city is a sleeper weapon.

Nodes.Name: Insurgent cells targeting armored corporate convoys
Rogue ARCTURUS field testers operating off-books

Properties.description: The TDG-9 is a compact thermite dispersal grenade developed by Arcturus Defense Solutions as a breach-and-clear tool for high-value target extraction in reinforced urban environments. Upon detonation, a central pyrotechnic initiator ignites a pressurized thermite slurry suspended in a ceramic-metallic shell, projecting a radial cone of molten iron-aluminum particulate at approximately 2500°C across a six-meter forward arc. The dispersal pattern is directional rather than omnidirectional, controlled by an asymmetric internal baffle that the operator orients before throwing — a deliberate design choice that reduces collateral damage in corridor-heavy environments like arcology maintenance tunnels or corporate server floors.
Properties.legality: Prohibited — civilian possession carries mandatory detention under the Meridian Incendiary Ordnance Accord of 2187
Properties.specifications:
weight: 340g
diameter: 62mm
burn temperature: 2500°C sustained for 4.2 seconds
dispersal arc: Forward 110-degree cone, 6m effective range
fuse types: Impact, Timed (2s / 4s / 6s toggle)
shell material: Ceramic-zirconium composite
effective against: Light vehicle plating, reinforced doors, unshielded synthetics, personnel in standard armor
Properties.tactical_use: Operators orient the baffle ridge by feel and throw the grenade into chokepoints, doorframes, or stairwells ahead of advance. The directional cone means friendlies behind the thrower are largely protected. Used extensively to slag security bulkheads without compromising structural integrity of the floor above — a critical consideration in multi-story arcology raids. Anti-synthetic units favor it because thermite bypasses most synthetic chassis hardening, melting joint mechanisms and optical arrays faster than kinetic rounds.
Properties.cultural_context: The Dragonspittle has a grim reputation in Meridian 88's street mercenary culture. Carrying one signals serious professional intent — it is not a weapon for robbery or intimidation, it is a weapon for removing a door, a turret, or a person from the world with absolute finality. In the Kessler District undermarket, TDG-9s surface occasionally from military theft rings, and their presence in a crew's loadout is treated as an indicator of a high-stakes operation. Corporate security analysts use Dragonspittle sightings at crime scenes to infer operator tier and client budget.
Properties.story_hooks: A TDG-9 with an unfired lot number matching a stolen Arcturus shipment turns up at a civilian fire scene — someone used military ordnance to cover an arson, and the insurance investigator is getting too close to something corporate.; A mercenary crew is hired to retrieve a TDG-9 prototype variant that supposedly burns at 3800°C — whoever developed it isn't in the Arcturus catalog, and the shell markings have been filed off.; A city council member is pushing to reclassify TDG-9s as 'industrial demolition tools' — the operators funding her campaign are not contractors.

Properties.description:
The TSG-4 operates by suspending micronized thermite particles within a viscous aerogel matrix that is ejected outward at detonation rather than simply igniting in place. On trigger activation, a piezoelectric initiator fractures the inner housing and simultaneously ionizes the aerogel medium, causing the thermite suspension to disperse in a controlled radial bloom before secondary ignition commences. This sequence delays the burn by approximately 0.4 seconds — long enough for the gel to adhere to surfaces, personnel, and machinery before the 2,500-degree Celsius reaction begins.

What distinguishes the TSG-4 from legacy incendiary grenades is its adhesive burn behavior. Standard thermite burns downward under gravity; the aerogel matrix holds the reaction in place regardless of surface angle, making it equally effective against vertical bulkheads, overhead infrastructure, and horizontal targets. The burn cannot be extinguished by conventional suppressants — the thermite provides its own oxidizer — and penetrates most civilian-grade armor plating within three to five seconds of contact.

Manufactured under contract for Meridian 88's internal security forces, the TSG-4 has since leaked widely into the black market through supply chain theft at ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS distribution nodes. Street operators call it the 'Slag Egg' for the faint yellow residue it leaves on concrete after burnthrough. Its reputation for destroying entire rooms of electronic infrastructure has made it a preferred tool of corporate saboteurs.
Properties.aliases: TSG-4, Slag Egg, Foundry Pill, Drip Bomb
Properties.specifications:
weight: 310g
diameter: 62mm
burn temperature: 2,500°C sustained
burn duration: 18–22 seconds
dispersion radius: 3.5m adhesive bloom
initiator: Dual piezoelectric fracture cap
housing: Ceramic-composite shell with inner aerogel bladder
delay: 0.4s post-fracture pre-ignition
Properties.tactical_use: Used primarily for denial operations and infrastructure destruction. Operators breach a room, deploy the TSG-4 into the center, and withdraw — the adhesive bloom coats walls, terminals, and occupants before igniting. Favored in server farm raids where data destruction is the objective. Close-quarters use is considered suicidal without full thermal shielding. Some operators use it defensively by rolling it through a doorway to seal a corridor permanently.
Properties.cultural_context: The TSG-4 carries a reputation for cruelty that even hardened operators acknowledge. In Meridian 88's lower districts, being killed by a 'Slag Egg' is considered one of the worst possible deaths — the aerogel adhesion means victims cannot remove the burning material. Corporate security divisions use the weapon's reputation as a deterrent, and rumors of TSG-4 deployment are sometimes enough to disperse resistance. Possession of one marks a carrier as someone who has either deep black-market connections or has raided an ARCTURUS logistics chain.
Properties.story_hooks: A batch of TSG-4s stolen from an ARCTURUS shipment turns up in the hands of a residential protest group — someone is deliberately escalating the conflict.; A player finds a room burned with TSG-4 adhesive residue in a pattern too precise to be combat — it looks like an execution. The victim's identity is erased by the burn.; ARCTURUS is quietly recalling TSG-4 units from the black market, not for legal reasons — a flaw in a recent production batch causes the aerogel to ignite prematurely, before dispersal.

Nodes.Name: Underworld fixers with high-tier supply access

Properties.description:
The TLCR-4 generates a tightly collimated beam of coupled thermal and acoustic energy tuned to the resonant frequency of the human thoracic cavity. At the point of beam convergence, the interaction between the thermal gradient and the acoustic pressure wave creates a localized thermoacoustic oscillation that disrupts the mechanical pressure balance sustaining normal lung inflation. The result is a rapid, involuntary forced exhalation followed by an inability to re-inflate — effectively a temporary pneumothorax induced without any physical penetration of the chest wall. Duration is typically thirty to ninety seconds before the body's compensatory mechanisms overcome the disruption, though repeated application can cause lasting pleural damage.

The weapon's design is deceptively simple in appearance: a long-barreled rifle with an unusually wide muzzle housing the dual emitter array, and a distinctive low hum audible to the operator during charging. It is nearly silent at the target end, producing only a faint subsonic pulse that most targets describe afterward as a 'pressure behind the sternum' immediately before collapse. Helix Biosystems developed it originally as a non-lethal crowd dispersal platform, a designation that has been contested in every jurisdiction that has examined field use data.

The names tell the story of its reception: 'Deflater' is the operator's term, blunt and functional. 'The Quiet Consent' is the name used by the civil enforcement units that deploy it, a piece of institutional language that has since become a darkly ironic shorthand in Meridian 88 for any coercive measure dressed in bureaucratic euphemism.
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 8-55m
collapse duration: 30-90 seconds first application
charge time: 4 seconds to full beam coherence
beam divergence: Less than 0.8 degrees at 50m
weight: 5.8 kg
power source: High-density thermal cell, 18 full-charge discharges
auditory signature: Subsonic at target / 60dB hum at operator position
Properties.tactical_use: Used almost exclusively as a suppression and compliance tool rather than a killing weapon, though the line is thin. Operators fire on targets to drop them to the ground without lethal effect, then close distance during the recovery window. In tactical entries, a TLCR-4 operator covering a doorway can disable anyone who appears in the frame without permanent damage, allowing selective lethality decisions to be made after the fact. It is notably ineffective against targets with significant chest augmentation or sealed respiratory systems, and experienced operators in contested environments often pre-breathe supplemental oxygen to extend their functional window if hit.
Properties.cultural_context: The TLCR-4 has become a flashpoint in Meridian 88's ongoing debate about what constitutes lethal force. Civil enforcement agencies insist it is a non-lethal compliance tool. Medical examiner records tell a different story — repeated application, application to elderly or compromised individuals, and application in physically demanding situations have all produced fatalities. Carrying one is legal with the right licensing, but openly displaying one in working-class neighborhoods has become a reliable way to start a confrontation. Among operators, it has a reputation for reliability but also for creating enemies — people who have been 'deflated' tend to remember it.
Properties.story_hooks: Three people died during a labor action dispersal where TLCR-4s were deployed — Helix Biosystems claims the units were used within spec, but someone has leaked internal data suggesting the rifles were operating at 140% standard output.; An operator is hired to recover a TLCR-4 prototype with an unlocked resonance range that can target non-thoracic cavities — the implications are not non-lethal.; A street medic has started documenting a cluster of pleural damage cases in a specific district, all consistent with repeated TLCR-4 exposure, all in people who claim they have never been 'officially' detained.; A TLCR-4 has been modified to sustain beam output rather than pulse — turning a compliance tool into something that simply does not stop until the operator decides.

Nodes.Name: Corporate extraction teams operating under non-lethal mandates

Properties.description:
The TPC-2 is a full-hand combat glove constructed from heat-resistant composite fiber, with a sealed micro-reservoir embedded in the dorsal housing containing a proprietary aerosolized fuel compound designated ARCTURUS FUEL-7. On impact, a pressure-sensitive detonator in the striking surface triggers a controlled thermobaric microexplosion — a burst no larger than a closed fist, but generating an overpressure wave of approximately 14 PSI at point of contact. The explosion is directed forward along the strike axis, meaning the wearer experiences negligible backblast while the target absorbs the full concussive force.

The thermobaric mechanism gives the TPC-2 a deeply unsettling effect profile. The overpressure wave does not cause the clean, visible trauma of a blade wound — it ruptures eardrums, collapses air pockets in lung tissue, and induces severe disorientation through sinus and inner-ear compression. Targets frequently remain standing for several seconds before the neurological cascade catches up with them, creating a delayed-drop phenomenon that experienced users exploit by landing additional strikes before the target falls. In enclosed spaces — corridors, vehicle interiors, elevator shafts — the reflected overpressure compounds the effect dramatically.

ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS positions the TPC-2 as a 'dynamic entry support tool' for military and law enforcement. Its fuel reservoirs are rated for 12 detonations per cartridge, and cartridges are color-coded by yield — gray for standard, amber for elevated, red for breach-grade. Red-cartridge TPC-2 units have been linked to multiple fatalities in poorly ventilated environments, and their sale outside of military channels is explicitly prohibited under Meridian 88 Municipal Code 7.4.2(c), a law that is enforced approximately never.
Properties.aliases: Smother, The Fist, Overpressure Gloves, Barrics
Properties.specifications:
weight: 1.1 kg per glove
fuel reservoir: 12-strike cartridge, field-replaceable in 8 seconds
overpressure output: 14 PSI at contact point (standard cartridge)
detonation trigger: Pressure-sensitive — activates at 40 N impact force
blast direction: Forward-axis channeled — 92% forward, 8% lateral dispersal
heat resistance: Rated to 1,200°C internal, 200°C external
cartridge variants: Gray (standard), Amber (elevated yield), Red (breach-grade, military restricted)
backblast to user: Negligible on standard and amber; minor thermal sensation on red
Properties.tactical_use: Military operators use the TPC-2 in dynamic entry scenarios where firearms are impractical due to ricochet risk or hostage proximity. The standard technique is a palm-strike to the chest — maximizing lung tissue contact — followed by a second strike to the base of the skull once the target drops. In confined corridor fighting, a single amber-cartridge strike can incapacitate multiple targets through reflected overpressure. Operators are trained to avoid using red cartridges in spaces smaller than 20 cubic meters due to documented self-incapacitation risk from reflected wave.
Properties.cultural_context: The TPC-2 is one of those weapons that everyone in Meridian 88 has heard of but almost no one has seen in person, which has made it into something of a myth. Military veterans who served in corporate conflict zones sometimes speak of 'the gloves that knock you down before you know you've been hit.' On the black market, a functioning TPC-2 pair with a full complement of cartridges commands prices that put it out of reach of street-level operators. Those who do carry them are generally operating at a level of violence that transcends street crime — mercenary contracts, corporate war operations, or the kind of personal vendettas that come with institutional backing.
Properties.story_hooks: A black market arms broker is offering a crate of TPC-2 units with amber cartridges, but the serial numbers have been filed and the fuel compound inside doesn't match ARCTURUS FUEL-7 specifications — someone is manufacturing knockoffs, and the yield variance on the knockoff cartridges is unpredictable.; A veteran with a pair of TPC-2 units is living quietly in the lower districts, but someone has started leaving red cartridges outside their door — a threat, a message, or an invitation.; The players are hired to retrieve a TPC-2 from a crime scene before the municipal investigators catalog it, because the weapon's serial number traces back to an ARCTURUS executive who was supposedly unarmed at the time of death.

Nodes.Name: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS special operations contractors
Former military operators who retained service equipment
One documented use by a Meridian 88 Transit Authority officer (case under internal review)

Properties.description:
The TPIR-1 fires a hollow-bodied frangible projectile containing a micro-canister of binary thermobaric precursor compounds kept separated by a rupturable membrane. On impact with a soft target, the projectile fractures and the membrane ruptures, allowing the compounds to mix and react within the wound cavity over approximately 40 milliseconds — long enough for the target's own tissue to contain the initial reaction, then catastrophically insufficient to contain the overpressure that follows. The result is a wound profile that is dramatically disproportionate to the projectile's caliber, as the thermobaric expansion occurs inside the body rather than outside it. Against hard surfaces, the projectile shatters without triggering the reaction, making it a weapon that is selectively devastating only against soft targets.

Ouroboros Energy's weapons division developed the binary precursor system as a derivative of their work on controlled micro-combustion for miniaturized power cells — the same chemistry that drives their portable energy products, redirected. The TPIR-1 is the only weapon in its class to use a purely internal thermobaric effect; earlier attempts by competitors used external-burst projectiles that produced undirected overpressure and were quickly banned. Ouroboros's innovation was the selective reaction timing, which they achieved through a proprietary membrane compound that responds to the specific mechanical stress of tissue impact rather than hard-surface impact, providing the weapon's remarkable target selectivity.

The rifle itself is unremarkable in appearance — a medium-length, conventionally styled firearm with no exotic external components. The binary canister projectiles require climate-controlled storage to maintain membrane integrity, a logistical limitation that Ouroboros has addressed through an insulated magazine housing with a small thermal regulator. Operators who ignore the storage requirements report a significant rate of dud rounds, and the occasional premature reaction in a poorly maintained magazine has contributed to the weapon's fearsome reputation even among its own users.
Properties.legality: Prohibited — classified under Meridian 88 Anti-Atrocity Statute 12.1 as an unlawful wound-enhancement device
Properties.specifications:
projectile: Frangible hollow-body, 9.5mm, binary thermobaric micro-canister payload
reaction delay: 38–42 milliseconds post-membrane rupture
trigger condition: Membrane ruptures on soft-tissue impact stress; inert on hard-surface impact
effective range: 200m accurate fire
muzzle velocity: 820 m/s
power source: Conventional propellant charge; no external power requirement
magazine: 15-round thermally regulated magazine (operating range: 4°C–22°C)
weight: 3.1 kg with loaded magazine
dud rate: Less than 1% within spec storage; up to 18% outside thermal range
integrated systems: Magazine thermal indicator, binary compound status display (green/amber/red per round)
Properties.tactical_use: Military units that have operated the TPIR-1 in sanctioned contexts use it for high-value target elimination where certainty of incapacitation is non-negotiable and collateral structural damage must be avoided — the weapon's hard-surface inertness means it can be fired in occupied structures without risk of wall penetration or ricochet. Black market operators use it primarily for assassination, as the wound profile is distinctive enough to send a message while the weapon's prohibited status ensures the killing cannot be tied to sanctioned forces. The thermal magazine requirement is a significant field limitation; operators in hot environments report frequent amber-status rounds and have developed improvised cooling rigs that have become a recognizable field modification.
Properties.cultural_context: The TPIR-1 sits at the intersection of Meridian 88's most uncomfortable conversations about corporate weapons development and the ethics of energy conglomerate diversification. Ouroboros Energy is primarily known for its power infrastructure and consumer energy products; the revelation that their micro-combustion research had produced a prohibited anti-personnel weapon created a significant public relations crisis that Ouroboros weathered by emphasizing the military licensing context and officially withdrawing from civilian sales. The weapon's street name — Hollowpoint — is ironic given that conventional hollowpoints are legal and relatively unremarkable; the Hollowpoint's reputation far exceeds its visual appearance, and carrying one in Meridian 88 is understood as a statement of intent that goes beyond simple armament.
Properties.story_hooks: A prominent Ouroboros Energy executive is found dead with a wound profile consistent with a TPIR-1 discharge — the irony is not lost on investigators, but more pressingly, someone has access to a weapon that Ouroboros claims no longer exists.; A shipment of climate-controlled cases is intercepted at the Meridian 88 port authority; the cases contain TPIR-1 magazines maintained at precise thermal spec, but the rounds inside have had their binary membranes replaced with an unknown compound that the port's hazmat team cannot identify.; An Ouroboros Energy micro-combustion researcher approaches a fixer claiming they were coerced into developing the TPIR-1's binary chemistry and want their name removed from the classified patent before it surfaces in a war crimes tribunal.; A field-modified TPIR-1 with an improvised cooling rig is recovered from a crime scene — the modifications are precise enough to suggest a trained engineer, and the cooling rig uses components exclusive to LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS cold-storage equipment.

Nodes.Name: Ouroboros Energy military contract forces (officially retired)
Collectors (inert display rounds; functional weapons rare)

Properties.description:
The TSIL-1 projects a narrow infrared beam tuned to the absorption frequency of sebaceous lipids — the fatty compounds produced by skin glands and present in a thin layer across virtually all exposed biological skin. At sufficient power density, the beam flash-heats this lipid layer to ignition temperature within approximately 0.8 seconds of contact, causing the skin's own oils to combust in a thin, intensely hot surface fire. The burn is shallow but severe, covering whatever area of skin was exposed to the beam. The weapon does not penetrate clothing effectively, making exposed skin — face, hands, neck — the primary vulnerable surface.

The TSIL-1's operational signature is distinctive and deeply unsettling: targets ignite seemingly from the inside out, the fire appearing to originate from the skin itself rather than from any visible external source. The psychological effect on witnesses and adjacent targets is pronounced. Ringo Corponation developed the weapon under a cosmetic-technology research umbrella — the original project involved precision lipid-layer treatments for dermatological applications — before the directed-energy weapons division acquired the underlying emitter technology and repurposed it. The cosmetic origin of the technology is something Ringo's PR division works continuously to suppress.

The weapon's range limitation — effective only to about 20 meters before beam dispersion reduces power density below ignition threshold — and its complete ineffectiveness against covered skin have defined its tactical niche as a close-to-mid-range terror and compliance weapon. The nickname 'Waxwork' refers both to the waxy appearance of healed sebaceous burns and to the way targets move in the moments after ignition — arms extended, stumbling, in a manner observers have described as resembling animated wax figures.
Properties.aliases: Waxwork, The Wick, Sebum Lance, TSIL
Properties.specifications:
effective range: 2–20 meters
power source: High-output infrared emitter cell, 30 shots per charge
ignition dwell time: 0.8 seconds on exposed skin
burn depth: Superficial to partial-thickness; rarely subcutaneous
weight: 1.6 kg
form factor: Slim lance profile, one-handed operation, integrated beam focus dial
clothing penetration: Negligible through standard fabric; thin synthetic materials may partially transmit
augmentation note: Synthetic skin overlays and dermal plating provide full immunity; unaugmented targets are fully vulnerable
Properties.tactical_use: The TSIL-1 is used primarily in close-quarters crowd control and targeted suppression, where its psychological impact is as valuable as its physical effect. Security forces use it to drive crowds, create chokepoints, or force individuals to cover — the instinctive reaction to being ignited is to stop, drop, and cover exposed skin, which halts aggression effectively. In one-on-one engagements, operators target the face and hands to immediately degrade the target's fighting capacity. The weapon's licensing status means it appears in the inventories of private security firms, certain licensed bounty hunters, and upscale personal protection details.
Properties.cultural_context: The TSIL-1's cosmetic-technology origin is a persistent source of dark humor in Meridian 88 — 'Ringo made a skin care product that sets you on fire' is a recurring punchline in the city's underground media. The weapon's licensing status, which makes it technically legal for certain operators, has generated significant controversy: advocacy groups argue that a weapon that causes burns to the face cannot be classified as non-lethal regardless of tissue depth. Ringo Corponation has lobbied successfully twice to maintain its licensed status by funding burn treatment research at public hospitals, a gesture widely described as calculated cynicism. Among high-society protection details, carrying a TSIL-1 is considered a mark of refinement — it implies the operator is expected to deter rather than kill.
Properties.story_hooks: Ringo Corponation's original cosmetic-technology research files have surfaced on the grey market, and they describe a higher-powered variant of the TSIL technology capable of full-thickness burns — a variant that was supposedly never manufactured.; A licensed security firm has been using TSIL-1s in a residential district to clear unhoused individuals from a development site. Three people have been hospitalized. Someone needs to document it before the evidence disappears.; A batch of TSIL-1 units has been modified to bypass the 0.8-second ignition delay, achieving near-instant ignition at the cost of reduced range. The modification suggests a specific workshop, and that workshop is connected to something larger.; A Ringo Corponation lobbyist who shepherded the TSIL-1's licensing approval has quietly started carrying one herself. She's scared of something, and whatever it is, she doesn't think a conventional firearm will stop it.

Nodes.Name: Ringo Corponation's own internal security division

Properties.description: The TFP-6 'Garrote' is a compact two-handed projector that launches a dense web of monomolecular torsional filaments across a target corridor or open space, creating an invisible lattice of cutting wire suspended between electromagnetic anchor nodes fired simultaneously from the weapon's twin barrels. The filaments are composed of carbon-ceramic composite strands under extreme torsional tension — wound so tightly during manufacture that contact with any moving mass causes them to snap-cut rather than deflect, delivering kinetic laceration energy far beyond what their apparent mass would suggest. The anchor nodes embed into walls, floors, and structural surfaces on contact, maintaining filament tension for up to ninety seconds before degrading.
Properties.specifications:
weight: 4.2 kg (unloaded), 5.9 kg (loaded, dual cassettes)
length: 71 cm
filament range: 3–18 m effective web span
anchor node count: 8 per deployment (4 per barrel)
filament tension duration: 90 seconds nominal, 60 seconds under load
cassette capacity: 1 deployment per cassette
reload time: ~45 seconds (manual cassette replacement)
filament visibility: Invisible to naked eye; detectable by Tier 2+ optical enhancement
effective environments: Enclosed spaces, corridors, vehicle interiors, stairwells
contraindications: Open spaces with wind above 15 kph (filament drift degrades lattice integrity)
Properties.tactical_use: The 'Garrote' is a pure area-denial and ambush weapon. Standard doctrine calls for deployment in advance of expected enemy movement — operators establish a filament web across a chokepoint, then trigger pursuit or drive targets into the kill zone. In close-quarters building clearance, teams use the 'Garrote' to seal off retreat routes or cut off reinforcements from a target room. Some operators deploy webs at ankle and throat height simultaneously, using staggered cassettes to create multi-level lattices. Counter-filament protocols exist but require specialized equipment most street-level operators don't carry.
Properties.cultural_context: The 'Garrote' carries a particular stigma even among Meridian 88's mercenary community, where most weapons are accepted as tools of the trade. The nature of filament injuries — clean, almost surgical cuts that can remove fingers, hands, or worse depending on velocity of contact — has given the weapon an association with cruelty that purely kinetic weapons don't carry. Corporate security firms that deploy it publicly face significant reputational risk, so its use is largely deniable and off-the-books. Among Arcturus Defense Solutions' contractor network, 'Garrote' operators are known as 'lacemakers' — a term that carries both professional respect and quiet unease.
Properties.story_hooks: A corporate executive was found dead in a sealed boardroom — the door was locked from inside and every exit was covered in a degraded filament web. The question isn't how the killer got in. It's how they got out.; An Arcturus Defense Solutions shipment of 'Garrote' cassettes has been intercepted and repurposed by a gang controlling the Undertow sewer network — they've been using them to create impassable zones that are slowly starving out competing factions.; A player character's contact has gone silent in a district where someone has been deploying 'Garrote' webs indiscriminately in civilian corridors. The local medical bay is overwhelmed with laceration cases.; Arcturus is quietly offering a bounty for the return of a prototype 'Garrote' variant that fires self-repairing filaments — the kind that don't degrade after ninety seconds.
