weight: 12 kg total system
setup time: 25 seconds to first round
guidance: GPS with inertial backup
Properties.story_hooks: Seismic mortar rounds have been used to collapse tunnel networks under a disputed territory — but the tunnels contained a refugee community that nobody knew about.; A single SM-8 system has gone missing from a Zheng-Dao armory and the serial numbers on mortar impacts across three incidents all match the same launcher.

Nodes.Name: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Tectonic Charge TC-5 'Fault Line'

Properties.description: A specialized demolition charge designed to be buried or anchored to structural foundations, detonating with a shaped downward blast that fractures bedrock and disrupts structural footing. The TC-5 uses Zheng-Dao's resonant detonation technology — the charge fires in a precisely timed sequence of micro-detonations that amplify through the ground substrate like an artificial earthquake, causing foundation failure across a much larger area than the charge's raw explosive yield would suggest. Originally developed for mining and geological survey, the TC-5 has become the preferred tool for infrastructure sabotage — a single charge can collapse a building by undermining its foundations without any visible surface damage.
Properties.aliases: Fault Line, TC-5, Ground Breaker, Quake Charge
Properties.legality: Licensed — demolition and mining; Prohibited — all other use
Properties.specifications:
explosive yield: Equivalent to 5 kg TNT, amplified by resonant detonation
effect radius: 20-meter foundation disruption zone
placement: Buried 1-2 meters or anchored to foundation
detonation sequence: 12-stage resonant micro-detonation over 0.8 seconds
timer options: 30 seconds to 72 hours, or remote trigger
weight: 3.2 kg per charge
form factor: Flat disc, 25 cm diameter
Properties.story_hooks: Three buildings have collapsed in a straight line across Tier 2 over three weeks — geological analysis shows resonant detonation signatures beneath each, suggesting a deliberate campaign of infrastructure destruction.; A TC-5 charge has been found planted beneath a major transit hub but not detonated — the timer was set but the trigger signal never came, suggesting the planter was interrupted or the charge is a warning.

Nodes.Name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Ablative Shroud Mk. IV

Properties.description:
The Ablative Shroud Mk. IV is Arcturus Defense Solutions' fourth-generation ablative coating system, designed as a modular over-armor layer that can be applied to existing body armor or worn as a standalone protective garment. It consists of 64 individually bonded ceramic-aerogel tiles arranged in overlapping scales across a flexible carbon-weave backing. Each tile is designed to fracture and ablate in a controlled pattern upon ballistic or directed-energy impact, dissipating kinetic energy laterally across neighboring tiles and venting thermal energy outward rather than inward. A single tile failure does not compromise the structural integrity of adjacent tiles, giving the Shroud exceptional multi-hit performance before requiring field replacement.

The Mk. IV iteration introduced Arcturus's Fracture-Mapping HUD integration, a thin sensor filament woven through the backing layer that reports real-time tile integrity to any compatible tactical display. This allows the wearer and their team to monitor armor degradation in the field and prioritize tile replacement during pauses in engagement. Replacement tile cartridges — standardized 4x4 packs — are widely available through Arcturus supply chains and several third-party manufacturers, making the Shroud one of the most maintainable armor systems in the Meridian 88 market.

The Shroud is visually distinctive: its overlapping tile pattern gives it a scaled, almost organic appearance, and the fractured tiles left after engagement create a scarred, asymmetric texture that many operators choose not to replace immediately, wearing the damage as a record of engagements survived. Military contractors, mercenary units operating in high-threat zones, and certain well-funded resistance cells all field the Mk. IV, though the cost of replacement tiles is a persistent logistical burden.
Properties.aliases: Peelback, The Onion, ADS Shroud, Mk. Four
Properties.tactical_use: The Shroud's tile-by-tile degradation model encourages operators to rotate their profile during sustained fire, presenting fresh tile sections to incoming rounds. Teams using Fracture-Mapping HUD integration can relay armor status to a squad leader, who can pull heavily degraded operators from the front line. The Shroud performs especially well against burst-fire engagements and directed-energy weapons, which tend to concentrate thermal load — the ablative geometry handles concentrated energy better than distributed ballistic loads.
Properties.cultural_context: Among mercenary units, the condition of a soldier's Shroud tiles is a form of social currency — a fully intact Shroud means you're either new or haven't seen real action, while a heavily scarred set of tiles means you've been in it. Some operators deliberately mismatched tile colors or left cracked tiles in place as a form of personal iconography. Arcturus has tried to capitalize on this by releasing 'Veteran Finish' pre-scarred tiles, which the actual mercenary community largely regards with contempt.
Properties.specifications: weight_kg: 11.2; coverage: Full torso, upper legs, upper arms (modular); tile_count: 64; tile_replacement_unit: 4x4 cartridge pack (16 tiles); impact_resistance_rating: NIJ Level III+ equivalent per fresh tile; directed_energy_attenuation: Up to 85% thermal dissipation on first strike; hud_integration: Compatible with Arcturus Parallax Threat Lattice and third-party displays; operational_lifespan_before_full_replacement: Estimated 3-5 sustained engagements
Properties.story_hooks: A third-party replacement tile manufacturer has begun selling counterfeit cartridges that look identical to Arcturus originals but fail catastrophically on second impact — operators are dying in the field.; An Arcturus logistics depot holding six months of tile inventory has been seized by an unknown faction, creating a critical supply shortage among contracted units who depend on the Shroud.; The Fracture-Mapping sensor filaments have been found to transmit low-bandwidth location data to Arcturus servers — the company claims it's for 'performance analytics,' but the data granularity suggests active surveillance.; A decommissioned Mk. IV Shroud recovered from a crime scene shows tile fracture patterns that forensic analysts claim are inconsistent with any known weapon system — something new is in the field.

Nodes.Name: Sergeant Dava Orel (retired ADS field tester, now freelance)
Arcturus Defense Solutions Albedo Negation Shell

Properties.description:
The Albedo Negation Shell is a form-fitting garment constructed from layered metamaterial tiles bonded to a flexible graphene substrate. Each tile contains a network of micro-actuated photonic crystals that sample incoming light across a 340-degree arc and reemit it with near-zero reflectance variance, effectively rendering the wearer's surface optically inert. The result is not true invisibility but rather a profound visual flatness — the wearer appears as a human-shaped absence of detail, difficult for both organic eyes and standard optical sensors to resolve against complex backgrounds.

What distinguishes the Shell from cruder light-absorption suits is its dynamic tile recalibration system, which adjusts albedo response in real time as ambient light conditions shift. Moving from a floodlit corridor into a shadow-heavy alley, the Shell compensates within 40 milliseconds, preventing the telltale shimmer that marks cheaper alternatives. A passive thermal bleed layer integrated into the outer substrate further reduces IR contrast, though dedicated thermal imaging at close range will still detect a faint silhouette.

The Shell is standard issue for Arcturus field operatives working corporate extraction contracts and is occasionally leaked to black-market buyers at considerable markup. It has become recognizable in certain underworld circles not by sight — obviously — but by the faint mechanical whisper of tile recalibration that trained ears learn to listen for. Street operatives who acquire one often tape over the recalibration vents to muffle this sound, accepting degraded performance in exchange for acoustic discretion.
Properties.aliases: The Erasure, Null Skin, The Dull
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed primarily for close-terrain infiltration where the operative must pass through mixed lighting environments — industrial facilities, server vaults, transit interchange underbellies. Most effective when the wearer remains slow and deliberate; rapid movement creates edge-artifact shimmer that trained sentries can detect. Frequently paired with the Arcturus Tactical Mesh Suppressor to address the suit's residual acoustic signature. Operatives working exterior urban environments often apply a secondary layer of textured fabric over the Shell to break up the unnatural visual flatness that can itself attract attention.
Properties.cultural_context: Within Arcturus contractor culture, earning a Shell assignment is considered a marker of seniority — rookies work in conventional dark-pattern gear and graduate to the Shell only after demonstrating patience under surveillance. On the black market, a Shell commands enough credit to relocate a family to one of the mid-tier residential stacks, and its appearance in street-level hands typically signals either a major corporate leak or a very dead Arcturus operative. Some underground artists have experimented with salvaged Shell tiles as performance material, staging events where performers move through gallery spaces as walking voids.
Properties.specifications: coverage: Full torso, arms, legs; modular hood attachment sold separately; albedo_reduction: 97.3% across visible spectrum; 71% in near-infrared; recalibration_latency: 40ms ambient transition response; power_source: Integrated kinetic harvest cells; 18-hour operational window at moderate activity; weight: 2.1 kg (full suit); tile_count: Approximately 14,000 micro-tiles per suit; acoustic_signature: Low-frequency tile actuator hum, audible within 1.5m in quiet environments
Properties.story_hooks: A Shell surfaces at a street market with its serial number chemically erased — someone needs to know which Arcturus operative it belonged to and whether they're still alive.; A player operative is assigned a Shell for a job but discovers the recalibration tiles have been sabotaged to broadcast a low-frequency tracking signal readable only by a specific third party.; An Arcturus internal audit is hunting a Shell that walked out of a secure facility — the suit's kinetic harvest log contains movement data that maps an entire infiltration route through a supposedly impenetrable installation.; A contact offers to sell a Shell at a fraction of market value; it turns out to be a prototype with experimental tile density that causes neurological discomfort in wearers after extended use.

Nodes.Name: Arcturus Defense Solutions field extraction contractors
Yeva Soldatenko — former Arcturus logistics officer turned independent
Underground performance collective known as The Null Chorus
Arcturus Defense Solutions Atmospheric Breach Torch

Properties.description:
The Atmospheric Breach Torch is a directed thermal cutting tool designed for forced entry through the reinforced composite and ballistic-grade materials used in corporate security architecture. Unlike conventional plasma cutters, which require an inert gas supply and careful standoff distance management, the ABT is self-oxidizing — it carries its own oxidizer in a solid-fuel rod format and operates across a wide range of atmospheric conditions including vacuum, high-pressure environments, and chemically contaminated air. The cutting head generates a focused 3,400°C jet approximately 4cm in diameter that penetrates most structural materials in seconds rather than minutes.

The engineering achievement that separates the ABT from earlier breach torches is the adaptive nozzle geometry. Conventional cutting torches produce a fixed flame profile that becomes inefficient as material composition changes — encountering a steel reinforcement bar mid-cut through synthecrete requires a different energy distribution than continuous substrate. The ABT's nozzle adjusts continuously based on optical and thermal feedback from the cut face, maintaining optimal energy density regardless of what the material behind the surface turns out to be. This is critical in Meridian 88's older structures, where decades of renovation have layered incompatible materials in ways that no blueprint accurately reflects.

ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS developed the ABT for military breaching teams and sells it under strict licensing to law enforcement and corporate security units. The device is explicitly prohibited for civilian ownership in most of Meridian 88's administered districts. This has not prevented a substantial black market supply, primarily sourced from military surplus channels that ARCTURUS itself is suspected of tolerating because surplus units are production overruns that would otherwise be destroyed. Field-stripped versions with the serial number arrays removed are called Blind Torches.
Properties.aliases: ABT, Breach Candle, The Torch, Arcturus Cutter
Properties.tactical_use: Standard deployment is a three-point cut to remove a door hinge array or create a breach aperture in a wall section. Experienced operators use the ABT to cut through vault doors, security bulkheads, and armored vehicle hulls. The self-oxidizing fuel system makes it the only reliable breach tool in sealed environments like vacuum-rated corporate server rooms and pressurized sub-basement facilities. It is also used to sever cable runs, destroy evidence in hardware form, and — in extremis — as an anti-materiel tool against lightly armored targets. The 90-second rod duration requires operators to plan cuts carefully; running out mid-breach is a known operational failure mode.
Properties.cultural_context: The ABT's prohibition status makes it a marker of serious criminal or paramilitary intent — carrying one is not the act of someone who wants to maintain deniability. Among professional breach teams, the ABT is treated with the respect of a precision instrument and the wariness of a liability. Blind Torches (serial-stripped units) are preferred on jobs where leaving the tool behind is part of the plan. There is a professional culture around ABT use that emphasizes discipline and preparation — operators who waste fuel rods or make unnecessary cuts are considered amateurs regardless of their other skills.
Properties.specifications: dimensions: 55cm length, 12cm diameter at fuel chamber; weight: 3.8 kg with full fuel rod; operating_temperature: 3,400°C at cut face; cut_jet_diameter: 4 cm; fuel_rod_duration: 90 seconds continuous burn per rod; rods_per_standard_kit: 4; penetration_rate: 12mm per second through standard synthecrete, 6mm per second through ballistic composite, 18mm per second through structural steel; operating_environment: Atmosphere-independent (self-oxidizing); nozzle_adjustment_cycle: Continuous, 40Hz feedback loop; standoff_requirement: 0 to 8cm (contact to near-contact operation)
Properties.story_hooks: A breach site shows ABT cut marks on a vault that was supposedly opened with the correct access code — someone used the torch after entering legitimately, suggesting they needed to destroy something inside that wasn't supposed to be there.; A shipment of ABT fuel rods has been routed through a legitimate construction supply chain using falsified Palladian Construction manifests — the players are hired to intercept it before it reaches its destination, but the buyer turns out to be someone unexpected.; An ARCTURUS whistleblower claims the company has been deliberately overproducing ABTs and routing the surplus to black market channels through a series of shell logistics companies — the players must decide whether to help expose this or exploit it.; The players are trapped in a sealed facility and the only way out requires breaching a pressure-rated bulkhead — the ABT they have is a Blind Torch with an unknown number of fuel rods remaining, and they won't know until they start cutting.

Nodes.Name: ARCTURUS Defense Solutions military breaching units
Arcturus Defense Solutions Ballistic Helmet BH-9 'Ironhead'

Properties.description: A full-coverage tactical helmet with integrated comms, HUD visor, NBC filter, and NIJ Level IV ballistic protection. The BH-9 uses a composite of boron carbide ceramic and ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene to defeat rifle-caliber threats while remaining under 2 kg. The integrated visor provides thermal, low-light, and AR overlay modes, and the helmet's padded interior includes impact-absorbing gel that reduces concussive force transmission by 80%. It has become the standard-issue helmet for corporate security forces across Meridian 88.
Properties.aliases: Ironhead, BH-9, ADS Helmet, Hard Hat
Properties.specifications: protection: NIJ Level IV — rifle rated; weight: 1.8 kg; visor: Thermal + low-light + AR overlay; comms: Encrypted; info: bone-conduction speaker; face; and neck; NBC filter: Integrated rebreather port; concussion reduction: 80% force attenuation gel; coverage: Full head; HUD: Neural interface compatible
Properties.story_hooks: A BH-9's HUD recorded the wearer's final moments during an ambush — the footage has become evidence in a corporate liability case.; Modified BH-9 helmets with removed IFF transponders are being sold to non-aligned combatants who want the protection without the corporate tracking.

Nodes.Name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Battlefield Communication Drone BCD-4

Properties.description: A high-altitude communication relay drone that provides encrypted communications coverage over a 10 km radius when ground-based infrastructure is unavailable or compromised. The BCD-4 flies at 500 meters altitude and serves as an airborne cell tower, mesh network node, and satellite uplink, enabling full communications capability in areas where jamming, destruction, or simple absence of infrastructure has created communication blackouts. The drone operates for 8 hours and can be replaced by a fresh unit for continuous coverage.
Properties.aliases: BCD-4, Sky Radio, Comm Drone, Signal Bird
Properties.specifications: altitude: 500 meters; coverage radius: 10 km; services: Encrypted voice; info: data; mesh network; satellite uplink; 000 simultaneous users; jamming resistance: Frequency-hopping spread spectrum; flight time: 8 hours; weight: 5 kg; launch: Hand-thrown with assisted takeoff; encryption: Military-grade quantum-key; band capacity: 1
Properties.story_hooks: A BCD-4 was deployed over a Tier 1 district during a communications blackout, providing the first reliable communication access the area had experienced in months — the question of who deployed it and why remains unanswered.; An enemy BCD-4 providing communications to hostile forces was shot down, and its communication logs contained the complete order of battle and operational plans of the opposing force.

Nodes.Name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Combat Exoskeleton Lite CEL-3

Properties.description: A lightweight partial exoskeleton that augments the wearer's lower body and core strength without the bulk of a full tactical exoskeleton. The CEL-3 consists of articulated leg braces, a hip frame, and a spinal support strut that multiply lower body strength by a factor of 3 and increase sprint speed by 60%. The system is powered by a waist-mounted battery and controlled by neural interface or manual input, allowing the wearer to run at 45 km/h, jump 3 meters vertically, and carry loads up to 200 kg without fatigue. The CEL-3 fits under loose clothing, making it the preferred mobility enhancement for operators who need augmented physicality without visible hardware.
Properties.aliases: CEL-3, Light Frame, Boost Rig, Skeleton
Properties.specifications: strength multiplication: 3x lower body; sprint speed: Up to 45 km/h; vertical jump: 3 meters; load capacity: 200 kg without fatigue; coverage: Legs; info: hips; spine; waist-mounted; weight: 4.5 kg; power: 6-hour battery; control: Neural interface or manual input; concealment: Fits under loose clothing
Properties.story_hooks: Security footage shows a suspect running at 45 km/h through a commercial district — far beyond human capability, but no visible augmentation. The CEL-3's concealed profile means witnesses describe an impossibly fast human.; A CEL-3 wearer experienced a servo lockup mid-stride at full speed — the resulting fall at 45 km/h was not survivable, and the manufacturer's logs show the lockup was triggered by an external signal.

Nodes.Name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Compressed Lattice Ascender

Properties.description:
The Compressed Lattice Ascender is a powered climbing and vertical-transit device engineered by Arcturus Defense Solutions for rapid assault and extraction on vertical surfaces in urban environments. The unit clamps onto standard rope, cable, or structural I-beam flanges and uses a contra-rotating lattice motor system to propel the user upward at controlled speed, with a dynamic braking mode that allows controlled descent on the same hardware. Unlike older cam-and-ratchet ascenders, the lattice drive system maintains grip on moving, swaying, or wet lines without user adjustment, and can be operated with one hand once locked to a line.

The device is built to Arcturus's characteristic design language: angular, matte-finished, with minimal external moving parts and a preference for mechanical redundancy over electronic elegance. The primary drive motor is backed by a manual ratchet system that engages automatically on power failure, preventing uncontrolled descent. A secondary clamp jaw, spring-loaded and independent of the drive system, functions as a passive safety at all times. The unit communicates with Arcturus tactical harnesses via a short-range hardwire jack but functions as a fully standalone device without integration.

The Ascender was originally developed for Arcturus's corporate security contracting division and remains on the preferred equipment list for several high-tier private security operators in Meridian 88. Its appearance on the open market through licensed resellers has made it accessible to a broader range of users, though the price point keeps casual ownership rare.
Properties.aliases: Lattice Grip, ADS Climber, The Fist
Properties.tactical_use: Used for rapid vertical insertion on building exteriors, elevator shafts, and structural columns where stairwells are compromised or under observation. Two-person teams using paired Ascenders on a pre-rigged line can close 20 floors of vertical distance in under 90 seconds. The controlled descent mode is used for fast exfil from elevated positions under fire, trading noise discipline for speed. In I-beam mode, the unit can traverse horizontal structural members, enabling cross-building movement through exposed framework in partially demolished or under-construction structures — a common infiltration route in Meridian 88's perpetual construction zones.
Properties.cultural_context: The Ascender's licensing requirement creates a visible class distinction among operators: licensed users are either corporate security personnel, registered contractors, or individuals wealthy and connected enough to obtain a use permit. Unlicensed units circulate on the black market at a significant markup, with the licensing restriction itself serving as a signal of the device's capability. Among private security professionals, carrying an Arcturus Ascender is a mark of employer investment — the firms that issue them are implicitly communicating that their operators are expected to work at height. Freelancers who own one personally are understood to have worked serious contracts.
Properties.specifications: weight: 1.1 kg; ascent_speed: 0.8 to 3.2 m/s variable; descent_speed: Controlled 0.4 to 1.8 m/s; compatible_line_diameter: 8mm to 32mm rope or cable; I-beam flange mode up to 120mm flange width; max_user_weight: 160 kg with equipment; noise_at_full_speed: 52dB at 1 meter; power_source: Arcturus 24V tactical cell, approximately 400m cumulative travel per charge; operating_temperature: -15°C to 55°C; dimensions: 24cm x 14cm x 9cm
Properties.story_hooks: A licensed Ascender recovered from a rooftop exit point has its drive motor's wear pattern analyzed — the contra-rotation ratio indicates heavy use in I-beam mode, consistent with someone who regularly transits through the structural skeleton of a specific under-construction district tower.; A batch of Ascenders was issued to a corporate security team that subsequently disappeared; the licensing database shows the units were checked out but never returned, and their last known location pings have gone dark.; Someone has been modifying Ascenders to remove the speed governor on ascent, creating a device that can close vertical distance almost twice as fast at the cost of significant structural stress on the line — three modified units have been recovered from separate incident scenes in six weeks.

Nodes.Name: Licensed vertical construction and inspection contractors
Municipal emergency response units with Arcturus supply contracts
Arcturus Defense Solutions Hardened Communications Suite HCS-7

Properties.description: A military-grade encrypted communications system hardened against jamming, interception, and EMP attack. The HCS-7 combines multiple communication modes — encrypted radio, laser-link, acoustic modem, and satellite uplink — in a ruggedized unit that automatically switches between channels based on the current threat environment. If radio is jammed, it switches to laser. If laser is blocked, it falls back to acoustic. The system maintains communication under conditions that would silence every other radio on the market. Arcturus issues it to field commanders and sells it to allied military organizations.
Properties.aliases: HCS-7, War Radio, Arcturus Comm, Hard Line
Properties.specifications: modes: Encrypted radio; info: laser-link; acoustic modem; satellite uplink; line-of-sight laser; 500m acoustic; global satellite; shockproof; EMP-proof; encryption: Quantum-key rolling encryption; jamming resistance: Frequency-hopping + mode switching; EMP hardening: Military-grade Faraday enclosure; range: 50 km radio; weight: 1.8 kg; battery: 48-hour multi-mode operation; ruggedness: Waterproof
Properties.story_hooks: An HCS-7's multi-mode capability was the only communication system that functioned during a coordinated jamming attack — the operator's after-action report reveals that the acoustic modem was the only mode that the jammers could not defeat.; A stolen HCS-7 has been modified to monitor all modes simultaneously rather than transmit — it has been turned into a multi-spectrum communications interceptor that can crack every channel except quantum-encrypted ones.

Nodes.Name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Laminar Shadow Bike

Properties.description: The Laminar Shadow Bike is a single-rider pursuit and infiltration motorcycle engineered by Arcturus Defense Solutions for rapid urban movement with minimal sensor footprint. Its frame is constructed from radar-absorbent composite laminate — a layered material that scatters both active sonar and millimeter-wave scanning — while the electric drive system runs through a vibration-damped motor housing that reduces acoustic signature to near-ambient levels at speeds below 80 km/h. The bike rides on self-sealing smart-rubber tires embedded with pressure-sensitive grip nodes that modulate traction in real time based on surface feedback.
Properties.aliases: Shadow Blade, ADS Slick, The Ghost Cycle
Properties.tactical_use: The Shadow Bike is purpose-built for infiltration runs, extraction operations, and counter-surveillance work. Operators use it to approach targets quietly, slip through automated traffic checkpoints, and execute rapid withdrawal after operations without triggering pursuit algorithms. The ECM pod is particularly valued in districts where Tessera Corponation traffic mesh systems are active — it creates a brief but reliable blind spot. Skilled riders have learned to use the Laminar Flow Cowling's micro-actuator adjustments as a subtle handling aid, allowing tight cornering at speeds that would ordinarily destabilize the chassis.
Properties.cultural_context: Within Arcturus Defense Solutions' contractor ecosystem, the Shadow Bike is a status marker — it is issued only to Tier 3 field operatives and above, and being seen dismounting one in certain circles communicates professional standing without words. On the black market, stolen Shadow Bikes command extraordinary prices, and a thriving underground trade in Arcturus-sourced parts has emerged. Street racers covet the bike's performance profile, though the restricted legality means riding one openly in civilian zones is an invitation for serious scrutiny from enforcement.
Properties.specifications: length: 2.1 meters; weight: 187 kg; top_speed: 240 km/h; range: 420 km (single charge); acoustic_signature: Near-ambient below 80 km/h; operator_capacity: 1 rider; power_source: High-density lithium-ceramic battery stack; ECM_range: 15-meter transponder suppression bubble
Properties.story_hooks: An Arcturus field operative's Shadow Bike was found abandoned and still running in a mid-district alley — the rider has vanished, and the ECM pod is broadcasting a distress signal on a frequency only Arcturus should know.; A black market dealer is offering three Shadow Bikes with their serial numbers scrubbed, but the buyer suspects they were stolen from an active Arcturus operation rather than a depot — which means Arcturus is already looking.; A street racer has been winning every underground circuit event for months on a Shadow Bike, and someone very corporate wants to know how she got it and what else she might know.; The crew is tasked with delivering a Shadow Bike to a contact — but during transport, the onboard ECM pod activates and starts suppressing comms in a widening radius, as if someone remotely triggered it.

Nodes.Name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Mortise Channel Spike

Properties.description:
The Mortise Channel Spike is a physical-access communication device designed to establish a hardened, off-mesh encrypted channel by directly interfacing with a building's structural wiring — power conduit, data trunk, or legacy copper telephony infrastructure. A hardened tungsten spike approximately 22cm long, it is driven into any accessible wiring surface and immediately begins negotiating a carrier signal through whatever electrical medium it finds, converting ambient current fluctuations into a low-bandwidth but extremely secure transmission channel. Arcturus Defense Solutions developed it for their tactical breach teams, who needed a communication solution that would function inside signal-suppressed or Faraday-shielded structures where mesh connectivity was unavailable or compromised.

The Spike's encryption layer uses a rolling hardware cipher generated by a physical entropy chip inside the device body — a chip that cannot be interrogated without destroying it, making key extraction forensically impossible after the fact. Two Spikes negotiating on the same electrical system will find each other within 40 seconds and establish an encrypted duplex channel that carries voice at low fidelity and text at full bandwidth. The channel is entirely invisible to wireless surveillance systems and requires physical access to the building's wiring to intercept — a significant operational barrier in most environments.

In the field, the Mortise Spike has developed a reputation for being the communication tool of last resort and, paradoxically, of highest operational security. Using one requires proximity to infrastructure and leaves physical evidence, but it produces a channel that is essentially immune to the city's ubiquitous wireless monitoring. Arcturus sells it exclusively to licensed defense and security contractors, but units surface regularly in the hands of individuals for whom wireless communications have become a liability they can no longer accept.
Properties.aliases: The Tap Root, Hard Line, Mortise
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed in pairs — one Spike placed at an entry or staging point, one carried by the operator inside a target structure. Used when mesh communications are compromised by jamming, Faraday shielding, or hostile signal monitoring. Also used for pre-operation dead drop communication, where both parties agree on a building's electrical infrastructure as their channel. Leaves a physical mark on whatever surface it's driven into, which is a known operational liability.
Properties.cultural_context: The Mortise Spike carries a distinctly military pedigree in Meridian 88's underworld — seeing one in someone's kit suggests either Arcturus training or serious operational experience. It is not a discreet or convenient device, and choosing to use one signals that the user has decided wireless is no longer an acceptable risk. Among security professionals, it is respected as a piece of engineering that prioritizes function over all other concerns. The physical evidence problem is considered a feature by some — it forces operational discipline.
Properties.specifications: dimensions: 22cm spike, 4cm diameter handle with integrated controls; weight: 280g; compatible_infrastructure: AC power conduit (110–480V), structured data cabling, legacy copper telephony, grounding systems; channel_negotiation_time: 40 seconds average between two active Spikes; transmission_bandwidth: Low-fidelity voice (4kbps) and full-bandwidth text/data (up to 128kbps); encryption: Rolling hardware cipher, physical entropy chip — non-extractable; range: Limited by building wiring topology; typically entire structure and adjacent connected infrastructure; battery_life: Passive — draws minimal power from host wiring; indefinite operation
Properties.story_hooks: A Mortise Spike is found still active in the wiring of a building that burned down three weeks ago — it's still receiving, and something on the other end keeps trying to transmit.; Two Spikes have been placed in the same building's infrastructure by different parties who don't know about each other. Both channels are now sharing the same carrier, and each party can hear fragments of the other's communications.; A corporate security team is tracking Spike placement patterns across Meridian 88 — someone has been systematically wiring up buildings in a specific district, and the pattern suggests they're building a hardwired communication network that bypasses the mesh entirely.; The players need to communicate inside a fully signal-suppressed facility. The only option is a pair of Mortise Spikes — but driving one into the building's wiring will trigger a structural current alarm they'll need to defeat first.

Nodes.Name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Null-Seam Signal Shroud

Properties.description:
The Null-Seam Signal Shroud is a portable Faraday enclosure designed to completely isolate any electronic device placed inside it from all external electromagnetic signals — incoming and outgoing. Constructed from twelve interlocking layers of Arcturus's proprietary Ferrolattice fabric, the shroud achieves attenuation exceeding 120dB across frequencies from 100Hz to 40GHz, effectively rendering any device inside it electronically dead to the outside world. It folds to the size of a large envelope, deploys in seconds, and is rated for field use in wet, dusty, and high-vibration environments.

What distinguishes the Null-Seam from cheaper signal-blocking pouches is the seam construction: conventional Faraday bags fail at their closures, where imperfect contact between layers creates signal leakage paths. Arcturus solved this with a magnetic compression seal that creates continuous conductive contact around the entire closure perimeter, eliminating the seam gap entirely. The result is a blocking performance that meets military-grade standards for device isolation, used by Arcturus's own field intelligence units for transporting sensitive hardware through hostile surveillance environments.

The shroud is also used offensively: any device placed inside it is immediately cut off from remote wipe commands, tracking signals, and tamper-detection pings. This makes it indispensable for anyone who has acquired hardware they need to examine without triggering its security protocols — or for anyone carrying a device they do not want broadcasting their location.
Properties.aliases: The Shroud, Null Bag, Signal Coffin
Properties.tactical_use: Operatives use the Null-Seam Shroud to transport acquired hardware — stolen comm devices, lifted data cores, confiscated implants — without triggering remote security responses. A device inside the shroud cannot receive a remote wipe command, cannot ping its owner's network, and cannot transmit location data. It is also used to carry a team's own devices through areas with aggressive signal-harvesting infrastructure, preventing passive logging of device identifiers. Some teams use it as a pre-mission discipline tool: all personal devices go in the shroud before an operation begins, eliminating the risk of accidental transmission.
Properties.cultural_context: The Null-Seam Shroud has become something of a ritual object in professional circles. Pulling one out before a meeting signals that you are serious about operational security — a nonverbal statement that what happens in this room stays in this room. Some fixers require everyone at a negotiation to bag their devices as a condition of the meeting. In the Undercroft, cheaper knockoffs with degraded attenuation performance are sold under various names; savvy buyers test them with a basic RF meter before trusting them with anything important. The genuine Arcturus model is identifiable by a small embossed serial number on the interior lining — knockoffs rarely bother to replicate it.
Properties.specifications: dimensions_folded: 210mm x 150mm x 8mm; dimensions_deployed: 380mm x 280mm interior usable space; weight: 340g; attenuation: 120dB+ across 100Hz–40GHz; closure_type: Magnetic compression null-seam, continuous conductive contact; material: Ferrolattice 12-layer composite, field-rated; environmental_rating: IP67 equivalent (water and dust resistance); deployment_time: Under 5 seconds; capacity: Devices up to 280mm x 180mm x 40mm; multiple smaller devices
Properties.story_hooks: A character recovers a Null-Seam Shroud with a device still inside — the device is still live, meaning someone sealed it and then never came back to open it.; A meeting is called in which all parties must bag their devices — but someone in the room is transmitting anyway, from hardware that shouldn't exist.; The black market is suddenly flooded with counterfeit Null-Seam Shrouds that perform perfectly on an RF meter but contain a passive logging layer that records everything placed inside them.; A character discovers their Arcturus-issue Shroud has a serial number that traces back to a unit reported destroyed in a classified operation two years ago.; A corporate client insists that a delivery be transported inside a Null-Seam Shroud for the entire transit — no exceptions, no checking the contents. The payout is enormous. The reason is never explained.

Nodes.Name: Military and corporate intelligence field units
Arcturus Defense Solutions Parallax Threat Lattice

Properties.description:
The Parallax Threat Lattice is a multi-node passive triangulation system that deploys a network of micro-receiver pods — each no larger than a flattened thumb — across a defined area. These pods communicate via low-frequency encrypted burst transmissions, collectively building a real-time volumetric map of movement, heat displacement, and pressure differentials within the coverage zone. The system's core innovation is its use of parallax mathematics rather than direct emission scanning: rather than broadcasting a detectable signal and reading the return, each pod reads the environment's own ambient energy and computes position data by comparing fractional discrepancies between nodes. The result is a sensor network that generates no active signature and is functionally invisible to most counter-surveillance sweeps.

What distinguishes the PTL from competitor mesh systems is its adaptive node weighting. If one or more pods are destroyed or blocked, the remaining network recalibrates its triangulation geometry within 4–6 seconds, filling the gap with interpolated data drawn from adjacent pod clusters. This makes the system unusually resilient in chaotic environments — firefights, demolition zones, collapsing infrastructure — where conventional sensor nets fail catastrophically. The lattice can track up to 40 distinct movement signatures simultaneously, tagging them with threat-probability indices updated every 200 milliseconds.

Primarily issued to Arcturus strike teams for perimeter defense during extended operations, the PTL has found significant adoption among private security contractors, corporate extraction teams, and high-end fixers who run safe houses requiring persistent area monitoring. The system's civilian black market presence is notable: modified versions with stripped authentication firmware circulate among gang leadership seeking early warning against rival incursions.
Properties.aliases: PTL, the Fishnet, Parallax Rig, Ghost Grid
Properties.tactical_use: Operators deploy PTL pods at choke points, entry vectors, and blind spots before establishing a position or safe house. The system feeds a heads-up threat map to connected tactical displays, allowing a skeleton crew to monitor an area that would otherwise require a full security detail. During extractions or ambush setups, teams seed pods along anticipated enemy approach corridors to receive advance warning. The adaptive recalibration feature makes the PTL particularly valued in breach-and-clear operations where explosive entry destroys forward sensors — the network self-heals and continues providing coverage.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88's corporate security culture, possession of a PTL kit signals professional-grade operational planning. It's not the weapon that marks you as serious — it's the sensor net. Fixers who can afford PTL rigs command higher rates because clients know their safe houses won't get hit blind. Among street-level operators, 'laying the fishnet' has become shorthand for any serious pre-operation surveillance setup, even when no PTL hardware is involved. Stripped civilian versions are a status marker in mid-tier gang leadership — proof you're running an operation, not just a corner.
Properties.specifications: coverage_area: Up to 800 square meters per standard pod kit (12 pods); node_count: 12–48 pods per deployment package; tracking_capacity: 40 distinct movement signatures simultaneously; update_rate: 200ms threat index refresh; recalibration_time: 4–6 seconds after node loss; pod_dimensions: 38mm x 22mm x 8mm (flattened ovoid); deployment_method: Manual placement or pneumatic scatter launcher (sold separately); power_source: Distributed mesh power sharing; 72-hour operational life per pod; active_emission: None (fully passive); detection_modes: Motion, thermal displacement, pressure differential; operating_temperature: -20°C to 60°C; weight_per_kit: 480g (12-pod standard kit)
Properties.story_hooks: A fixer's safe house was hit despite a PTL perimeter being active — either the attackers had PTL-defeating technology or someone on the inside moved the pods; A stripped PTL kit surfaces on the black market with Arcturus authentication firmware still intact, suggesting an inside leak from a licensed operator; A character discovers an unknown PTL network already seeded in a location they believed was unsurveilled — someone else is watching the same target; The PTL's threat-probability indices begin misidentifying a specific individual as 'non-threat' despite obvious hostile action — the person may be carrying some form of signature-masking tech

Nodes.Name: Arcturus Defense Solutions field extraction teams
Professional fixers managing safe house networks

Arcturus Defense Solutions Phantom Trace Spoofer

Properties.description:
The Phantom Trace Spoofer is a compact identity-broadcasting device that simultaneously suppresses the user's genuine electronic identity emissions and substitutes a continuously rotating library of synthetic identities drawn from Arcturus Defense Solutions' proprietary ghost-profile database. The device intercepts signals from the user's personal electronics, embedded identification chips, transit tokens, and biometric broadcast systems, wrapping them in a spoofed identity layer that presents as a convincingly ordinary civilian or service worker to automated scanning infrastructure — access nodes, transit checkpoints, commercial facial recognition systems, and corporate perimeter sensors.

What sets the Phantom Trace Spoofer apart from simpler RFID blockers or identity jammers is its active emission strategy: rather than creating a detectable dead zone where a person's identity should be, it populates that space with a ghost profile that behaves like a real person — complete with synthetic movement history, a plausible employment record stub, and timed identity-rotation that mimics the normal pattern of a worker moving through multiple scan zones. The ghost-profile database receives over-the-air updates through an encrypted Arcturus channel, keeping synthetic identities ahead of blacklist databases. The device also includes a panic-wipe mode that erases operational profiles in under two seconds if the unit is at risk of capture.

Arcturus Defense Solutions markets the Phantom Trace Spoofer exclusively through defense and law enforcement procurement channels, making it officially unavailable to civilian or corporate buyers. In practice, a thriving secondary market exists, fed primarily by equipment recovered from Arcturus field teams and through a small number of internal procurement leaks. Ownership outside of authorized channels is a serious criminal offense in all six of Meridian 88's administrative sectors, a fact that has done little to suppress demand.
Properties.tactical_use: Worn concealed on the body or integrated into a jacket lining. Activated before entering scan-heavy zones such as corporate campuses, transit hubs, or monitored commercial districts. Operatives typically set identity rotation to the 20-minute interval for urban movement and switch to manual rotation during static infiltration phases to avoid triggering anomaly detection from a single identity appearing in multiple scan zones. The device is notably less effective against Arcturus's own scanning infrastructure, which carries a known ghost-profile recognition layer — a fact that Arcturus does not publicize.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88, the Phantom Trace Spoofer is something of a mythologized object — its prohibited status and Arcturus pedigree give it a prestige that operatives at every level aspire to. Owning one signals either genuine connections to defense-sector channels or the resources to pay black-market prices. The device has also become a point of political contention: civil liberties groups cite its existence as evidence that Arcturus Defense Solutions has built a surveillance infrastructure specifically designed to be defeatable only by Arcturus's own clients, creating a two-tiered security landscape in which corporate and state actors operate above the identity-verification systems imposed on ordinary citizens.

Properties.story_hooks: A Phantom Trace Spoofer recovered from a dead operative is still active and rotating through identities — one of those synthetic identities matches a real person who has been reported missing, suggesting the ghost-profile database may have been seeded with identities of real people who were then disappeared.; An Arcturus scanning node in a corporate district begins flagging Phantom Trace Spoofer ghost profiles in real time — someone has updated the detection layer, and every operative currently running a Spoofer in the district is suddenly at risk.; A player is offered a Spoofer at a suspiciously low price. Investigation reveals it has been hardware-modified to transmit a covert location beacon to an unknown third party alongside its spoofed identity broadcasts.; The Meridian 88 underground railroad's supply of Phantom Trace Spoofers has been cut off — the procurement leak inside Arcturus has gone silent, and the players are asked to find out why and restore the supply chain before a major movement of protected individuals is scheduled.

Arcturus Defense Solutions Reactive Plate Carrier Mk. VII

Properties.description: A modular plate carrier incorporating reactive armor elements that detonate outward on ballistic impact, disrupting incoming projectiles before they reach the wearer. Each reactive cell is a micro-explosive sandwich that detonates directionally upon detecting high-velocity impact, defeating armor-piercing rounds that would penetrate conventional plates. The carrier holds 24 reactive cells arranged in overlapping coverage zones, and spent cells can be replaced in the field from standard cartridge packs. The detonation is localized enough that adjacent cells remain functional, though operators report the experience of being 'saved' by a reactive cell as violently unpleasant — you survive, but you feel the explosion.

Nodes.Name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Reactive Shear Mantle

Properties.description:
The Reactive Shear Mantle is a mid-weight ballistic garment built around Arcturus's shear-thickening fluid suspension, housed within a flexible outer membrane that resembles a heavy-duty technical jacket at rest. Under low-velocity contact the material flows and conforms normally, allowing full range of motion. When struck by a high-velocity projectile or blade, the non-Newtonian fluid instantaneously hardens in the impact zone, distributing force across a palm-sized area before returning to its flexible state within fractions of a second. The transition is imperceptible to the wearer in most engagement scenarios.

The Mantle's outer membrane is treated with a ceramic particulate coating that ablates incrementally under sustained fire, buying additional time against automatic weapons before the fluid suspension is compromised. Arcturus markets this as the 'dual-envelope' protection philosophy — the ablative exterior handles the first wave while the reactive core manages penetrators that break through. A chemical indicator strip on the interior collar changes color when fluid suspension integrity drops below operational threshold, giving the wearer a passive readiness check without powered diagnostics.

The Mantle occupies an unusual market position: it is formally classified as personal protective equipment rather than body armor in several jurisdictions due to its non-rigid construction, allowing it to be worn and transported in contexts where plated armor would be flagged. Arcturus has cultivated this ambiguity carefully, and the legal designation is part of the product's value proposition in cities with aggressive gear-check enforcement. Corporate security details, investigative journalists operating in hostile zones, and high-risk financial couriers are among its more visible user populations.
Properties.tactical_use: Preferred in environments where concealment of armor is as tactically important as the protection itself. The Mantle performs well against single high-velocity rounds and edged weapons but degrades under sustained automatic fire faster than rigid plate systems. Operators typically pair it with a sidearm and prioritize mobility and concealment over direct confrontation. The passive integrity indicator is a critical field tool — experienced users check it before re-entry after any engagement.
Properties.cultural_context: The Mantle has become associated with a particular class of urban professional who cannot afford to be seen as a combatant but cannot afford to be unprotected — fixers, high-value couriers, embedded journalists, and corporate negotiators operating in contested territories. Wearing one signals insider knowledge of the gear-check loopholes Arcturus has engineered into its legal classification. In some circles, the Mantle is considered more sophisticated than overt tactical armor, indexing situational intelligence over raw defensive capacity.
Properties.specifications: weight: 3.1 kg; coverage: Full torso, upper arms; ballistic_rating: Class IIIA equivalent at rest; Class III equivalent under shear activation; ablative_layer_endurance: Approximately 12–15 sustained impacts before degradation; shear_activation_time: Less than 0.3 milliseconds; fluid_suspension_volume: 1.4 liters distributed across torso panels; indicator_strip_threshold: Triggers at 40% fluid suspension integrity loss; profile: Indistinguishable from heavy outerwear at visual inspection
Properties.story_hooks: A courier was shot wearing a Mantle that should have stopped the round — the suit's integrity strip was untouched, suggesting the fluid suspension had been replaced with an inert substitute somewhere in the supply chain.; Arcturus's legal classification lobbying for the Mantle is under challenge in three jurisdictions simultaneously; someone is funding the legal opposition, and Arcturus wants to know who before the ruling comes down.; A journalist's Mantle was recovered at a scene with no body — the ablative layer shows a distinctive impact pattern that a forensic specialist believes can be matched to a specific weapon system if the right person examines it.; The licensing database for Mantle ownership in the city has been leaked; the list contains names that should not be wearing licensed protective gear, and someone is using it as a hit list.

Arcturus Defense Solutions Signal Jammer Grenade SJG-3

Properties.description: A throwable device that emits a powerful broadband electromagnetic jamming signal in a 30-meter radius for 5 minutes, disrupting all wireless communications, sensor systems, and neural interface external connections within range. The SJG-3 is used for tactical communications denial — thrown into an area before an assault to prevent defenders from calling for reinforcements or coordinating response. The jamming signal is powerful enough to disrupt hardened military communications and causes painful interference in neural interfaces, which most users experience as a sudden, overwhelming burst of static in their augmented senses.

Nodes.Name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Spectral Deadfall Jammer

Properties.description:
The Spectral Deadfall Jammer is a high-output, selectively configurable signal suppression device designed to deny communications across a defined geographic radius while preserving operator-specified frequency bands for friendly use. Unlike crude broadband jammers that silence everything indiscriminately, the Deadfall uses a continuously updated suppression profile to null targeted frequency ranges while maintaining open corridors for pre-configured channels. The result is a communications blackout that affects every party in the affected zone except those who know which narrow corridors remain open — a tactical asymmetry that gives the operator's team a significant advantage in any scenario where communication is critical.

The device is physically ruggedized to Arcturus's military-grade specifications: a matte-grey rectangular unit roughly the size of a hardback book, with recessed antenna arrays on three sides and a sealed control interface that can be operated with gloves. Deployment takes approximately forty seconds from power-on to full operational suppression, with the suppression profile configurable either in advance via the companion planning software or in the field through the tactile control interface. The Deadfall can be programmed to pulse — cycling suppression on and off at irregular intervals to prevent targets from timing a transmission window — or to ramp up gradually, creating a 'soft' communications degradation that may not be immediately identified as jamming.

The Spectral Deadfall Jammer is officially restricted to licensed security contractors, military units, and certified law enforcement organizations. It is, nonetheless, a fixture of the Meridian 88 black market, where it commands a significant premium. Its primary non-authorized users are high-end extraction teams, corporate espionage operatives, and — with uncomfortable regularity — groups planning coordinated violence who need to ensure that targets cannot call for help.
Properties.tactical_use: Standard deployment involves placing the Deadfall at a central point within the operational area before action commences, with the operator's team already configured to communicate on the preserved corridors. The jammer's moderate detection signature means that extended use in a fixed location risks triangulation, so experienced operators either keep operations short or use multiple units deployed sequentially to shift the apparent jamming source. Pulse mode is favored in scenarios where the goal is to create confusion rather than complete silence — targets attempting to transmit during suppression windows will experience intermittent success, which is often more disorienting than a clean blackout. The Deadfall is frequently paired with Tessera Corponation mesh equipment to ensure operator communications remain robust within the suppressed zone.
Properties.cultural_context: The Spectral Deadfall Jammer is one of the few pieces of equipment in Meridian 88 that carries genuine moral weight in the city's underground culture. Its legitimate applications are understood and grudgingly accepted — corporate security teams use it during sensitive extractions, and licensed contractors deploy it for crowd management operations that most residents already resent. Its illegitimate applications are darker and less easy to rationalize away. The device has been found at the scenes of enough targeted killings and coordinated assaults that carrying one without obvious legitimate context marks an operator as someone willing to work at a certain level of violence. Among fixers and runners, taking a contract that requires a Deadfall is understood to be a statement about the kind of work you are willing to do.

Nodes.Name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Spectral Nullcast Mantle

Properties.description:
The Spectral Nullcast Mantle is a wearable, full-spectrum communications suppression garment — a heavy tactical overcoat lined with a metamaterial mesh that absorbs, scatters, and re-emits incoming and outgoing RF, microwave, millimeter-wave, and infrared communication signals across a configurable suppression envelope extending up to six meters from the wearer. Unlike point-source jammers that broadcast detectable counter-signals, the Mantle operates through passive absorption and chaotic re-emission, creating a zone of signal degradation that registers to external monitoring as environmental noise rather than active interference. Within the envelope, no reliable digital communication can be established or maintained.

The garment's metamaterial lining is woven from Arcturus's proprietary Nullweave filament, a frequency-agnostic absorptive medium that requires no power to maintain baseline suppression. An optional active-mode module draws from an integrated power cell to extend the suppression envelope and add targeted frequency-specific nulling for high-priority bands. The Mantle's outer surface is designed to pass visual and casual tactile inspection as a standard heavy weather coat — seams, buttons, and collar are all functionally realistic.

The Spectral Nullcast Mantle was originally developed for military VIP protection details, where preventing remote detonation signals, covert surveillance transmission, and enemy coordination comms in close proximity to a principal is operationally critical. It has since proliferated into the private security sector and, inevitably, into the hands of well-funded criminal organizations conducting operations where communication blackouts serve as both security measures and psychological tools.
Properties.aliases: Null Mantle, The Blanket, ADS-SNC, Whiteout Cloak
Properties.tactical_use: Worn by the team member closest to a sensitive meeting or transaction to prevent remote surveillance, signal interception, and remote detonation of any concealed devices. Also deployed offensively to deny enemy coordination comms during close-quarters operations. The Mantle creates a 'dead zone' that forces adversaries into face-to-face communication or physical runners, dramatically slowing their response cycles.
Properties.cultural_context: Licensed Mantles are nominally restricted to certified private security contractors and military units, but Arcturus's notoriously permissive licensing review process means they circulate widely among corporate protection details and high-end criminal organizations alike. Wearing one in public is a statement — it announces that whoever you're meeting is important enough, or dangerous enough, to warrant a communications blackout. In certain circles, the sight of a Nullcast Mantle is understood as a signal to put all devices away.

Properties.story_hooks: A city councilor's security detail has begun wearing Mantles to every public appearance, suggesting they're either receiving death threats involving remote detonation or conducting meetings they don't want anyone to monitor — or both.; The players are hired to extract information from a meeting happening inside a Mantle's suppression envelope; their usual remote surveillance and overwatch comms will be useless.; A black-market Mantle is circulating that has been modified to also suppress emergency distress frequencies — whoever modified it wanted to ensure no one inside the envelope could call for help.; An Arcturus licensing record leak reveals that a Nullcast Mantle was purchased by an entity that shouldn't exist — a corporate shell with no employees, no address, and a single transaction history.

Nodes.Name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Tactical Command Gauntlet TCG-5

Properties.description: A forearm-mounted tactical computing and communications platform that integrates real-time mapping, squad tracking, drone control, and encrypted communications into a ruggedized wrist-worn unit. The TCG-5 features a flexible display that wraps around the forearm, providing a large-format tactical map accessible at a glance. It connects to squad members' neural interfaces, displaying their positions, status, and sensor feeds in an integrated common operating picture. The gauntlet can control up to 4 drones simultaneously, manage automated defensive systems, and coordinate fire support requests through an encrypted uplink.
