Nodes.Name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Tactical Mesh Suppressor

Properties.description:
The Tactical Mesh Suppressor is a portable, directional signal denial system designed to sever mesh network connectivity, encrypted comm channels, and emergency broadcast access within a defined operational envelope. Roughly the size and weight of a hardback book, it deploys as a handheld unit or mounts magnetically to surfaces and vehicles. Its suppression field is not a simple broadband jammer — the Suppressor uses Arcturus's Selective Denial Architecture to target specific protocol layers of Meridian 88's civilian and corporate mesh infrastructure while leaving defined frequencies open for operator use, preventing the self-defeating blackout that affects cruder jamming equipment.

The Selective Denial Architecture is the product's defining feature and the basis of its legal classification. By suppressing at the protocol level rather than the frequency level, the Suppressor can deny mesh access, encrypted comms, and automated distress signaling simultaneously without producing the detectable jamming signature that conventional frequency-blocking devices emit. From the outside, affected devices appear to be experiencing routine connectivity degradation — the kind of outage that happens a dozen times a day across Meridian 88's aging infrastructure. Only prolonged, precise spectrum analysis can distinguish a Suppressor field from genuine network failure.

Arcturus sells the Suppressor through its law enforcement and corporate security divisions with appropriate licensing frameworks, and the device appears regularly in the inventories of precinct security teams, corporate extraction units, and private protection details. Its presence on the black market is equally routine, and the gap between the licensed and unlicensed versions is primarily one of firmware — the licensed variant has hardcoded duration limits and automatic logging; the black-market variant does not.
Properties.aliases: The Interdict, Blackout Box, The Warden's Hand
Properties.tactical_use: The Suppressor is standard equipment for corporate extraction teams conducting personnel recovery in hostile precincts — cutting mesh access prevents targets from calling for support or triggering automated alerts. Security teams use it to create communication dead zones around high-value meetings, ensuring that no attendee can transmit from within the envelope. Criminals use it to blind security infrastructure during operations, producing what appears to be a routine connectivity outage in the affected block. Its directional nature allows experienced operators to suppress specific areas while leaving adjacent zones unaffected — surgically isolating a target without triggering the broader alarm that a full-block blackout might generate.
Properties.cultural_context: The Interdict is what people mean when they say a neighborhood 'went dark.' In Meridian 88, sudden mesh dropouts are common enough that most residents have learned to recognize the particular quality of a Suppressor-induced outage versus genuine infrastructure failure — the former tends to have cleaner edges, affecting some blocks precisely while leaving adjacent ones unaffected. Street-level awareness of the Suppressor has generated a folk practice of keeping analog fallbacks: physical signal mirrors, chalk marks, runner networks. Among corporate security professionals, carrying a Suppressor is a mark of operational seriousness. Among the people those professionals are deployed against, it is a symbol of the asymmetry that defines life in the lower precincts.
Properties.specifications: suppression_envelope: Directional cone, 15° to 120° adjustable spread; effective range 40m standard, 180m maximum (reduced fidelity); protocols_targeted: Meridian 88 Civic Mesh v4.1–v6.3, CorpNet Standard B and C, encrypted VoIP over mesh, automated emergency distress broadcast; operator_reserved_bands: Up to 4 user-defined frequency windows; activation_time: 1.8 seconds to full suppression field; power_source: Removable high-density cell, 4-hour continuous operation; weight: 1.1kg; licensed_firmware_limits: 90-minute maximum activation, mandatory event logging to Arcturus compliance server; black_market_firmware: Unlimited duration, logging disabled, suppression envelope expanded by 22%; detection_resistance: Indistinguishable from network degradation to standard intercept equipment; detectable by military-grade spectrum analysis
Properties.story_hooks: A neighborhood has experienced daily mesh outages at the same time each evening for three weeks — someone is running a Suppressor on a schedule, and no one knows why.; The players are mid-operation when the mesh drops. It could be infrastructure failure. It probably isn't.; A licensed Suppressor's compliance logs — which are supposed to transmit automatically to Arcturus's servers — show a 6-hour gap that the device's internal clock doesn't account for. Someone used it off-books, and Arcturus wants to know who.; A contact needs the players to keep a specific area mesh-active during an operation — meaning they need to find and disable a Suppressor that's already in place before the window closes.; Black-market Suppressors with modified firmware are appearing in unprecedented numbers in a particular precinct, suggesting someone is mass-distributing them in preparation for something large enough to require sustained communication blackouts.

Nodes.Name: Syndicate operational crews (black market firmware variant)
Arcturus Defense Solutions Threat Detection Collar TDC-2

Properties.description: A collar-worn sensor array that provides 360-degree threat detection by monitoring acoustic signatures, electromagnetic emissions, laser designators, and chemical agent presence in the wearer's environment. The TDC-2 interfaces with the wearer's neural implant to deliver threat warnings as intuitive spatial awareness — the wearer feels the direction and distance of detected threats as if they had a sixth sense, rather than processing visual alerts. The system can detect an aimed weapon by its electromagnetic signature, incoming projectiles by their acoustic wavefront, and laser designators by reflected scatter. The result is a constant awareness of danger that becomes as natural as hearing.
Properties.aliases: TDC-2, Threat Collar, Danger Choker, Sixth Sense
Properties.specifications: detection modes: Acoustic; info: electromagnetic; laser; chemical; integration: Neural interface spatial awareness feed; coverage: 360 degrees continuous; weapon detection: EM signature of aimed electronics/optics; projectile detection: Acoustic wavefront analysis; laser detection: Scatter reflection identification; chemical detection: VOC sensor array; weight: 0.15 kg; battery: 72-hour continuous
Properties.story_hooks: A TDC-2 wearer detected a threat signature from an empty room — the collar identified electromagnetic patterns consistent with an aimed weapon, but no weapon or operator was found. The signature appeared again 24 hours later.; TDC-2 data logs have been subpoenaed as evidence in a self-defense case — the collar's recordings show exactly when the wearer perceived the threat and whether the response was proportionate.

Properties.description: The Arcturus Ironveil Jammer Cloak is a wearable signal suppression system built into a heavy-weave tactical coat lined with interlocking metamaterial panels that generate a localized electromagnetic interference field extending approximately three meters from the wearer in all directions. Unlike conventional jammers that broadcast disruptive noise across a spectrum, the Ironveil uses destructive wave interference — generating precise counter-signals that cancel incoming and outgoing transmissions at the wave level, producing a bubble of effective electromagnetic silence without the detectable jamming signature that draws security attention. Within the field, all wireless communication, remote detonation signals, tracking pings, and mesh-relay transmissions are suppressed.
Properties.aliases: The Cloak, Ironveil, Faraday Ghost, Signal Coffin
Properties.tactical_use: Operators use the Ironveil to create a communications blackout zone around a target, preventing distress signals, tracking pings, or automated emergency transmissions from escaping during an extraction or termination operation. Security teams walking point through the suppression field are effectively blind to mesh-relay intelligence, which creates tactical windows for ambush. Counter-use involves entering a building or secured area where electronic access systems rely on wireless authentication — the Ironveil renders these systems inoperable, forcing manual override or security escalation that can itself be exploited.
Properties.cultural_context: The Ironveil's prohibited status has paradoxically elevated it to a kind of dark prestige item in Meridian 88's underworld. Owning one is a statement — it says you operate at a level where silencing a target's communications is a professional necessity rather than an incidental benefit. There is a grim shorthand in certain circles: if someone shows up wearing an Ironveil, the meeting was never meant to end with everyone walking away. Corporate security teams are trained to treat the identification of an active Ironveil field as an immediate lethal-threat escalation.
Properties.specifications: suppression_field_radius: 3 meters from wearer; suppression_method: Active destructive wave interference; no detectable jamming broadcast signature; spectra_suppressed: RF 300MHz–300GHz; standard mesh relay bands; remote detonation frequencies; GPS and positioning signals; battery_life: 4 hours continuous; replaceable cell, 90-second swap; activation: Tactile pressure switch, left inner cuff; weight: 2.1kg including battery cell; appearance: Tailored heavy-weave tactical coat; civilian styling, available in four colorways; detection: Field itself is undetectable on standard sweeps; physical metamaterial lining detectable by advanced materials scan
Properties.story_hooks: The party is in a meeting when the room's mesh connectivity drops — someone nearby has activated an Ironveil, and no one at the table admits to owning one.; A witness the party is protecting disappears; their emergency beacon went silent at a precise moment that correlates with Ironveil field suppression, but the coat was never recovered at the scene.; An Arcturus Defense Solutions internal manifest lists twelve Ironveil units as 'field-destroyed' — but forensic analysis suggests they were resold to a private buyer through a shell procurement company.; A player character acquires an Ironveil only to discover its battery cell has been modified to transmit the field's activation timestamps to an unknown receiver — someone wants to know exactly when and where the coat is being used.

Nodes.Name: Arcturus Defense Solutions extraction and termination contractors
Black-market arms dealers conducting sensitive transactions
Certain district-level crime bosses who wear one as a constant deterrent

Properties.description: A compact cyberdeck designed for offensive network intrusion, containing three independent processing cores that can simultaneously attack different security layers of a target system. The Cerberus runs Axiom's proprietary penetration suite — a library of exploit packages, cryptographic attack tools, and social engineering AI modules that adapt to target defenses in real-time. The deck interfaces directly with the operator's neural implant for speed-of-thought interaction and includes a hardware firewall that isolates the operator's neural interface from counterattack. Its triple-core architecture allows parallel attacks that overwhelm security systems designed to handle single-vector intrusions.
Properties.aliases: Cerberus, Hack Box, Axiom Deck, Triple Head
Properties.specifications: processing cores: 3 independent attack vectors; software: Axiom Penetration Suite v7.2; neural interface: Direct connection required; defensive: Hardware firewall + neural isolation layer; cryptographic attack: Quantum-assisted key cracking; weight: 0.4 kg; form factor: Wrist-mounted or belt clip; power: 8-hour battery; attack parallelism: 3 simultaneous intrusion vectors
Properties.story_hooks: A Cerberus deck has been recovered with its attack logs intact, revealing that the operator penetrated a system they should not have been able to crack — the logs show a fourth attack vector that the hardware should not support.; Axiom's Penetration Suite has been updated with a backdoor that reports all successful intrusions back to Axiom — operators using the deck are unknowingly sharing their targets with its manufacturer.

Nodes.Name: Axiom Systems Cognitive Load Balancer CLB-2

Properties.description: An external neural processing unit that connects to the user's neural interface and provides additional cognitive processing capacity for computationally intensive tasks — complex decryption, multi-system network management, real-time data analysis, and parallel cyber operations. The CLB-2 effectively gives the user a second brain dedicated to technical work, allowing them to maintain situational awareness and social function while their augmented processing handles demanding cognitive tasks in the background. The device is worn at the base of the skull and connects through the neural interface's external port.
Properties.aliases: CLB-2, Think Tank, Brain Buffer, Load Balancer
Properties.specifications: processing: Equivalent to 200% baseline neural interface capacity; connection: Neural interface external port; cognitive offload: Decryption; info: analysis; network management; user experience: Background processing without conscious load; weight: 0.15 kg; form factor: Neck-mounted module; battery: 8-hour active processing; heat management: Active cooling micro-fan; compatibility: Standard neural interface architectures
Properties.story_hooks: A CLB-2 user has been running the device continuously for months — the external processor has developed processing patterns that do not match any input from the user's neural interface, as if it is thinking independently.; A compromised CLB-2 has been feeding subtly altered analysis results to its user — the device has been hacked to introduce bias into every decision the user makes based on its processing.

Nodes.Name: Axiom Systems Data Exfiltration Wafer DEW-1

Properties.description: A paper-thin flexible circuit that adheres to any data port and silently copies all data passing through the connection. The DEW-1 is smaller than a postage stamp and can be applied to a data port in under 2 seconds, where it sits flush against the connector housing and is virtually undetectable without physical inspection. The wafer copies all data traffic bidirectionally — incoming and outgoing — to an encrypted micro-storage module that can be retrieved later, or transmits captured data via low-power burst to a nearby receiver. A single wafer can operate for 6 months on its integrated battery, silently capturing every byte that passes through its host port.
Properties.aliases: DEW-1, Data Wafer, Steal Chip, Axiom Leech
Properties.specifications: size: 15mm x 15mm x 0.3mm; application time: Under 2 seconds; detectability: Requires physical port inspection; data capture: Bidirectional; info: all traffic; 50m range; storage: 10 TB encrypted micro-storage; transmission: Optional low-power burst; battery: 6-month operation; compatibility: Universal data port adhesion
Properties.story_hooks: A routine IT maintenance check discovered a DEW-1 on a server room data port that had been capturing traffic for four months — the storage module contained complete copies of every transaction, communication, and security log.; A DEW-1 was found on the neural interface charging port of an executive's desk — it had been copying their neural interface backup data every night for three months.

Nodes.Name: Axiom Systems Distributed Identity Cloak DIC-2

Properties.description: A device that floods local surveillance systems with dozens of false identity signals, making it impossible to determine the wearer's true identity among a crowd of spoofed personas. The DIC-2 broadcasts multiple simultaneous false biometric, neural interface, and Diaspora identity signatures within a 10-meter radius, creating a cloud of phantom identities that overwhelms facial recognition, biometric tracking, and identity correlation systems. Within the cloud, every person appears to be everyone else — faces do not match IDs, neural signatures do not match bodies, and tracking systems lose the ability to associate any specific identity with a specific physical person.
Properties.aliases: DIC-2, ID Fog, Identity Cloud, Axiom Scatter
Properties.specifications: false identity generation: 30 simultaneous phantom signatures; effect radius: 10 meters; affected systems: Facial recognition; info: biometric tracking; neural interface correlation; Diaspora identity; instant effect; result: Complete identity confusion within radius; battery: 4-hour active broadcast; weight: 0.25 kg; form factor: Belt-worn or pocket module; activation: Single button
Properties.story_hooks: A DIC-2 was activated in a crowded transit hub, causing every surveillance system in the area to simultaneously flag 300 identity mismatches — in the confusion, someone walked through security with a weapon that would normally have been detected through identity correlation.; A permanent DIC-2 installation has been discovered in a Tier 3 building, creating an always-on identity fog that makes the building's occupants effectively untrackable — the building has become a haven for anyone who needs to disappear.

Nodes.Name: Axiom Systems Memory Crystal Archive MCA-4

Properties.description: A portable holographic data storage device using Tessera crystal technology in an Axiom-designed security housing. The MCA-4 stores up to 500 petabytes of data in a device the size of a large coin, protected by biometric lock and quantum encryption. If tampered with, the crystal's data can be scrambled in microseconds, destroying the information before it can be extracted. Axiom uses the MCA-4 for field data storage during intelligence operations — an entire corporation's data archive fits in a device that can be swallowed.
Properties.aliases: MCA-4, Mind Vault, Crystal Archive, Axiom Memory
Properties.specifications: storage: 500 petabytes; encryption: Quantum-key protection; biometric lock: Neural interface + fingerprint; tamper response: Microsecond data scramble; size: 3 cm diameter coin; weight: 0.01 kg; data persistence: 10; info: 000+ years; read speed: 100 TB/sec through neural interface
Properties.story_hooks: An MCA-4 was recovered from a dead operative's stomach — the crystal survived digestion and its data is intact, but the biometric lock requires the dead person's neural interface signature to open.; An MCA-4 has been found pre-loaded with data that does not match any known source — the crystal contains what appears to be a comprehensive map of Meridian 88's underground infrastructure, including facilities that officially do not exist.

Nodes.Name: Axiom Systems Neural Dead Drop NDD-2

Properties.description: A concealed device that stores encrypted data accessible only through a specific neural interface authentication. The NDD-2 can be hidden anywhere — embedded in a wall, buried underground, or concealed in everyday objects — and appears as inert material to all scanning methods. When an authorized neural interface comes within 10 cm, the device authenticates the user's neural signature and releases the stored data directly to their implant. The transfer is invisible to external monitoring and leaves no trace on the recipient's interface after the data is read. Axiom designed it for intelligence operations where physical document exchange or electronic transmission are too risky.
Properties.aliases: NDD-2, Brain Drop, Neural Cache, Mind Locker
Properties.specifications: storage: 1 TB encrypted; activation: Neural interface authentication at 10 cm; transfer: Direct to neural interface; info: invisible to monitoring; data persistence: Configurable — single read or persistent; authentication: Unique neural interface signature match; concealment: Appears inert to all scanning methods; size: 2 cm x 1 cm x 0.5 cm; battery: 2-year standby; form factor: Embeddable in any material
Properties.story_hooks: A player character brushes against a wall and their neural interface receives an unexpected data payload — someone planted an NDD-2 keyed to their specific neural signature with a message meant only for them.; A network of NDD-2 devices has been discovered embedded in public infrastructure across Tier 3 — someone has built a city-wide dead drop network for intelligence exchange.

Nodes.Name: Axiom Systems Neural Interface Diagnostic Tool NIDT-3

Properties.description: A handheld diagnostic device that assesses the health and integrity of a neural interface without requiring medical facility access. The NIDT-3 connects to the interface's external diagnostic port and performs a comprehensive assessment — checking processor function, memory integrity, connection quality with neural tissue, firmware version, and security status. The tool identifies hardware faults, firmware corruption, unauthorized modifications, and potential security compromises. Axiom designed it for field technicians maintaining neural interfaces in environments far from clinical facilities.
Properties.aliases: NIDT-3, Brain Doctor, Interface Scanner, Axiom Probe
Properties.specifications: diagnostic scope: Processor; info: memory; neural connection; firmware; security; firmware corruption; unauthorized mods; unauthorized access detection; assessment time: 60 seconds; connection: External diagnostic port; fault detection: Hardware failure; security check: Malware scan; weight: 0.15 kg; battery: 200 diagnostics per charge; output: Detailed report to linked device or neural interface
Properties.story_hooks: An NIDT-3 scan revealed that a patient's neural interface had been modified with firmware not matching any known version — the modification was installed without the patient's knowledge and its function is unclear.; NIDT-3 tools have been modified to inject diagnostic payloads rather than just reading them — the diagnostic connection has been weaponized to compromise the neural interface during what appears to be a routine checkup.

Nodes.Name: Axiom Systems Neural Interface Firewall NIF-3

Properties.description: A hardware security module that installs between a user's neural interface and external data connections, providing real-time monitoring and filtering of all data entering or leaving the neural implant. The NIF-3 analyzes data packets for known attack signatures, anomalous patterns, and unauthorized access attempts, blocking threats before they reach the neural interface's processing core. The firewall includes anti-intrusion countermeasures that can trace and counterattack hostile connections, and a panic-disconnect that physically severs the neural interface from all external connections in an emergency.
Properties.aliases: NIF-3, Brain Wall, Axiom Shield, Mind Guard
Properties.specifications: monitoring: All data in/out of neural interface; threat detection: Known signatures + behavioral analysis; response time: Sub-microsecond packet filtering; countermeasure: Active trace and counterattack capability; panic disconnect: Physical circuit breaker; info: manual activation; weight: 0.02 kg; installation: Inline with neural interface external port; power: Parasitic from neural interface; update frequency: Daily threat signature updates
Properties.story_hooks: A NIF-3's counterattack capability traced a hostile intrusion attempt back to its source — the attack originated from inside the user's own employer's network, revealing internal surveillance of augmented employees.; A firmware update to the NIF-3 introduced a vulnerability that it was supposed to protect against — the update came from Axiom's official channels, raising questions about whether the company is deliberately weakening its own security products.

Nodes.Name: Axiom Systems Parasitic Data Harvester PDH-3

Properties.description: A device designed to be covertly attached to a target's neural interface charging cable, harvesting data from every charging session. The PDH-3 intercepts the data channel that neural interfaces use during charging to perform backup, update, and diagnostic operations, copying the transmitted data to an encrypted internal storage. Over successive charging sessions, the PDH-3 accumulates a comprehensive picture of the target's neural interface contents — communications, stored memories, access credentials, and cognitive enhancement configurations. The device is powered parasitically from the charging cable and adds no detectable load.
Properties.aliases: PDH-3, Data Leech, Axiom Tick, Info Vampire
Properties.specifications: installation: Inline with neural interface charging cable; data capture: All charging session data traffic; storage: 20 TB encrypted; power: Parasitic from charging cable; detectability: No additional load — transparent to diagnostics; size: 1 cm x 0.5 cm inline module; data accumulation: Progressive over successive charging sessions; retrieval: Physical removal or low-power burst transmission
Properties.story_hooks: A PDH-3 found on an executive's charging cable had been accumulating data for nine months — the stored data includes every credential, communication, and stored memory backup from that period.; PDH-3 devices have been found pre-installed in charging cables sold through a major retail chain — thousands of users may have been unknowingly sharing their neural interface data with an unknown collector.

Nodes.Name: Axiom Systems Portable Diaspora Terminal PDT-4

Properties.description: A ruggedized portable terminal that provides Diaspora network access in areas without infrastructure coverage. The PDT-4 establishes a satellite uplink and creates a local wireless hotspot serving up to 50 users within a 100-meter radius. Axiom deploys them in emergency situations and sells them to organizations operating in infrastructure-poor zones. The terminal includes content filtering consistent with Axiom's Automated Censorship Infrastructure, ensuring that even off-grid Diaspora access operates within Axiom's information control parameters.
Properties.aliases: PDT-4, Net Box, Axiom Terminal, Public Access
Properties.specifications: connectivity: Satellite uplink to Diaspora; local coverage: 100-meter wireless hotspot; users: Up to 50 simultaneous; weight: 3 kg; battery: 24 hours operation; form factor: Ruggedized briefcase; content filtering: Axiom ACI integrated; bandwidth: 100 Mbps shared
Properties.story_hooks: A PDT-4 deployed in a Tier 1 dead zone has been modified to bypass the ACI content filter — for the first time, residents are accessing unfiltered Diaspora and discovering how much information has been hidden from them.; Axiom is distributing free PDT-4 terminals in underserved districts as a humanitarian gesture — but each terminal maps every device that connects to it, building a comprehensive census of the off-grid population.

Nodes.Name: Axiom Systems Portable SIGINT Station PSS-2

Properties.description: A compact signals intelligence platform that intercepts, decrypts, and analyzes all wireless communications within a 500-meter radius. The PSS-2 captures radio, cellular, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and Diaspora traffic simultaneously, running real-time decryption against commercial-grade encryption while logging traffic for later analysis of harder targets. The station can identify and track individual devices, map communication networks, and extract content from unencrypted or weakly encrypted channels. Axiom designed it for field intelligence operations.
Properties.aliases: PSS-2, Ear Box, Signal Station, Axiom Listener
Properties.specifications: interception radius: 500 meters; channels: Radio; info: cellular; Wi-Fi; Bluetooth; Diaspora; decryption: Real-time against commercial encryption; device tracking: Individual device identification and mapping; network mapping: Communication relationship analysis; storage: 50 TB traffic logging; weight: 2 kg; battery: 12 hours active interception; form factor: Briefcase-sized portable station
Properties.story_hooks: A PSS-2 deployed near a corporate negotiation captured the entire opposing team's communications — including their bottom-line position, their strategy, and their personal messages, giving the deploying party total information advantage.; A PSS-2 has been found permanently installed in a Tier 3 cafe, capturing all wireless traffic from every patron — the cafe is a front for an intelligence operation that has been running for years.

Nodes.Name: Axiom Systems White Noise Bubble Generator WNB-1

Properties.description: A portable device that generates a precise white noise field in a 3-meter hemisphere, making audio recording and eavesdropping impossible within the zone. The WNB-1 uses adaptive noise generation — it samples ambient sound in real-time and generates complementary frequencies that render speech unintelligible to any recording device or listener outside the hemisphere. Conversation within the zone is clear and normal; conversation recorded within the zone is pure static. The device is standard equipment for corporate negotiation teams, legal consultations, and anyone who needs a private conversation in a world where every surface might contain a microphone.
Properties.aliases: Bubble, WNB-1, Silence Dome, Privacy Field
Properties.specifications: effect radius: 3-meter hemisphere; noise type: Adaptive complementary frequency generation; effect: Speech unintelligible to external listeners/recording; internal effect: Normal conversation unaffected; power: 12-hour battery; weight: 0.3 kg; form factor: Hockey puck sized; info: tabletop or pocket; instant on; activation: Single button
Properties.story_hooks: A WNB-1 was found to have a firmware vulnerability that allows the noise generation to be inverted — instead of blocking recording, it enhances audio capture, turning the privacy device into a surveillance amplifier.; A modified WNB-1 has been developed that generates not just white noise but specific spoken words within the recording band — anyone listening hears a different conversation than the one actually happening.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Ballistic Face Shield BFS-2

Properties.description: A transparent ballistic visor that provides NIJ Level IIIA facial protection while maintaining full visual clarity. The BFS-2 is constructed from layered polycarbonate and ceramic nano-fiber composite, capable of stopping handgun rounds and fragmentary projectiles while being optically clear enough for precision shooting. The visor mounts to standard helmet rails and features an integrated HUD projection layer compatible with most tactical display systems. Anti-fog, anti-scratch, and anti-glare coatings are standard. The visor's lower edge extends to the chin, providing protection that conventional eyewear helmets miss.
Properties.aliases: BFS-2, Face Plate, Carrion Mask, Iron Face
Properties.specifications: ballistic rating: NIJ Level IIIA — stops handgun rounds; material: Polycarbonate + ceramic nano-fiber composite; optical clarity: 97% light transmission; HUD compatibility: Standard projection layer; coatings: Anti-fog; info: anti-scratch; anti-glare; coverage: Full face including chin; mount: Standard helmet rail interface; weight: 0.8 kg
Properties.story_hooks: A BFS-2 stopped a round that would have been fatal, but the visor's HUD layer recorded the muzzle flash position and the shooter's location was transmitted to response teams before they could relocate.; Modified BFS-2 visors with built-in facial recognition overlay have appeared — the wearer sees real-time identity information for every face they look at, sourced from hacked databases.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Bioelectric Camouflage Generator BCG-2

Properties.description: A body-worn device that generates a configurable bioelectric field mimicking the signature of a different person, animal, or no living being at all. The BCG-2 can spoof biometric sensors that detect heartbeat, bioelectric brain activity, galvanic skin response, and body impedance — the sensor reads whatever the BCG-2 tells it to read. The device can make the wearer appear dead to biometric scanners, mimic the bioelectric signature of a specific individual for access control bypass, or generate the signature of an animal to explain detection without raising alarm. Carrion developed it for covert operators who need to defeat biometric perimeter security.
Properties.aliases: BCG-2, Life Mask, Bio Camo, Heartbeat Faker
Properties.specifications: field type: Configurable bioelectric signature; modes: Null (appear dead); info: clone (specific individual); mask (animal); custom; brain activity; skin response; impedance; bioelectric mimicry: Heartbeat; effective range: Overpowers sensors within 2 meters; battery: 8-hour active generation; weight: 0.2 kg; form factor: Belt-worn module; programming: Neural interface or manual preset selection
Properties.story_hooks: A secured area's biometric perimeter showed no living presence during a time when a theft was committed — the intruder used a BCG-2 in null mode, appearing as a walking dead zone to every sensor.; A BCG-2 was used to clone an executive's bioelectric signature and gain access to a biometric-locked facility — the intrusion was undetectable because the sensors saw exactly the right person.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Chemical Hazard Oversuit CHO-4

Properties.description: A full-body protective suit providing Level A chemical, biological, and radiological protection through a multi-layer barrier system with integrated self-contained breathing apparatus. The CHO-4 uses a laminate of chemical-resistant polymer, activated carbon fabric, and vapor-barrier membrane to create an impenetrable barrier against liquid, vapor, and particulate hazards. The suit includes 4 hours of breathing air, communication systems, and a heads-up display showing environmental threat data from integrated sensors. Carrion designed it for their own CBRN operations teams but sells it through their defense catalog.
Properties.aliases: CHO-4, Hazard Suit, Chem Suit, Carrion Skin
Properties.specifications: protection level: EPA Level A — full CBRN encapsulation; layers: Chemical polymer + activated carbon + vapor barrier; breathing: Self-contained; info: 4-hour air supply; biological; radiation detection; communications: Integrated encrypted radio; HUD: Environmental threat data display; sensors: Chemical; weight: 12 kg with air supply; mobility: Reduced — approximately 60% of normal movement; operation time: 4 hours per air bottle
Properties.story_hooks: A team wearing CHO-4 suits entered a contaminated zone and their suits' sensors detected a compound not in any hazard database — the unknown agent was penetrating the activated carbon layer, a protection failure that should be impossible.; CHO-4 suits have been stolen and modified for use in robberies — the full-body coverage and breathing apparatus make the wearer immune to tear gas and chemical deterrents while providing complete visual anonymity.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Chemical Sniffer Drone CSD-3

Properties.description: A small quadcopter drone equipped with a hypersensitive chemical analysis suite that can identify specific compounds in the air at parts-per-trillion concentrations. The CSD-3 flies autonomously through designated areas, sampling atmospheric composition and flagging the presence and concentration of explosives, chemical weapons, drugs, biological agents, and specific industrial compounds. The drone can follow a chemical gradient to its source, effectively tracking a scent like a bloodhound. Carrion designed it for CBRN reconnaissance but its use has expanded to law enforcement, industrial safety inspection, and corporate espionage.
Properties.aliases: Sniffer, CSD-3, Nose Drone, Carrion Dog
Properties.specifications: sensitivity: Parts-per-trillion atmospheric detection; compound library: 4; info: 000+ catalogued chemicals; gradient tracking: Follows concentration to source; flight time: 45 minutes; operating range: 500 meters from controller; size: 20 cm rotor-to-rotor; weight: 0.4 kg; sampling rate: 10 analyses per second; autonomous flight: Programmed search patterns or gradient tracking
Properties.story_hooks: A CSD-3 detected trace explosives in the air of a government building — the gradient tracking led to a maintenance closet containing a device that had been in place for weeks, undetected by every other security measure.; A modified CSD-3 has been repurposed to track specific individuals by their unique chemical signature — body chemistry, soap, diet, and medication create a profile as unique as a fingerprint.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Field Surgical Kit FSK-6

Properties.description: A comprehensive surgical kit designed for emergency field operations — containing scalpels, hemostats, retractors, suture materials, a compact cauterizer, bone saw, and a diagnostic scanner for guiding procedures without imaging equipment. The FSK-6 is designed for trained field medics performing procedures that cannot wait for evacuation to a medical facility — bullet extraction, internal hemorrhage repair, emergency amputation, and cyberware emergency disconnection. The kit includes Lazarus RWCNS nanite injectors for wound closure and a neural interface link that provides AR-guided surgical assistance overlaid on the operative field.
Properties.aliases: FSK-6, Cut Kit, Carrion Surgeon, Field Surgery
Properties.specifications: instruments: 40-piece surgical set; cauterizer: Compact electrocautery unit; bone saw: Oscillating micro-saw; diagnostics: Handheld ultrasound with AR overlay; nanite injectors: 3x RWCNS for wound closure; AR surgical guide: Neural interface overlay; sterilization: UV sterilization lamp; weight: 5 kg in hardened case; shelf life: 5 years for consumables
Properties.story_hooks: An FSK-6 was used to perform field surgery on a shooting victim in a Tier 1 hallway — the AR-guided procedure was performed by someone with no formal medical training who followed the overlay instructions perfectly.; A modified FSK-6 has been configured specifically for forced cyberware removal — the AR guide walks an operator through disconnecting and extracting neural interface hardware from a living subject.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works NBC Threat Assessment Kit NTAK-2

Properties.description: A portable nuclear, biological, and chemical threat assessment system contained in a hardened case the size of a large lunchbox. The NTAK-2 includes a radiation dosimeter, biological agent sampler with rapid gene-sequencing chip, chemical compound mass spectrometer, and an AI analysis module that cross-references detected threats against Carrion's comprehensive threat database. The system can identify a biological agent, assess radiation exposure levels, or categorize an unknown chemical compound in under 90 seconds. Carrion issues the NTAK-2 to their field teams and sells it to corporate emergency response units.
Properties.aliases: NTAK-2, Hazard Kit, NBC Scanner, Threat Box
Properties.specifications: radiation detection: Alpha; info: beta; gamma; neutron; 90-second identification; 4; 000+ compound database; surface swab; and liquid; biological sampling: Rapid gene-sequencing; chemical analysis: Mass spectrometry; AI analysis: Threat assessment and countermeasure recommendation; analysis time: Under 90 seconds for most threats; weight: 3.8 kg in hardened case; sampling: Atmospheric; battery: 100 analyses per charge
Properties.story_hooks: An NTAK-2 deployed at a public event detected a biological agent that does not exist in any database — the AI flagged it as engineered but could not identify its function, and the concentration is increasing.; Carrion's threat database updates are being delayed for non-Carrion customers, meaning corporate response teams are operating with outdated threat data while Carrion's own teams have current information.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Personal Decontamination Kit PDK-3

Properties.description: A compact kit for field decontamination after chemical, biological, or radiological exposure. The PDK-3 contains reactive decontamination wipes that neutralize chemical agents on contact, antibiotic skin wash for biological exposure, a radiation chelation injector that binds radioactive particles for excretion, and a set of disposable coveralls for clothing replacement. The kit provides 15 minutes of treatment — enough to decontaminate a single person from most common CBRN threats if applied within the first 10 minutes of exposure.
Properties.aliases: PDK-3, Clean Kit, Decon Pack, Wash Box
Properties.specifications: chemical decon: 20 reactive wipes; info: neutralizes common agents; 500ml; single dose; biological decon: Antibiotic skin wash; radiation: Chelation injector; clothing: Disposable sealed coveralls; treatment window: Most effective within 10 minutes of exposure; treatment time: 15 minutes complete decon; weight: 1.2 kg; shelf life: 3 years
Properties.story_hooks: A PDK-3's chemical wipes failed to neutralize an unknown agent — the compound is not in Carrion's database and the decontamination protocol needs to be developed from scratch while the clock ticks.; PDK-3 kits have been distributed with expired chelation injectors that provide no radiation protection — whoever replaced the injectors wanted exposed individuals to believe they were safe when they were not.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Rapid Fortification System RFS-3

Properties.description: A set of deployable ballistic barriers that unfold from flat-packed panels into free-standing walls providing cover against rifle-caliber fire. Each RFS-3 panel expands from a 60x40 cm flat pack into a 2m x 1m ballistic wall in 5 seconds using a spring-loaded deployment mechanism. The panels interlock to create longer barrier runs, corner positions, and enclosed fighting positions. The barriers are rated NIJ Level IV and can be refolded for transport after use. A single operator can deploy four panels in under 30 seconds, creating a defensible position from nothing.
Properties.aliases: RFS-3, Insta-Wall, Carrion Barrier, Quick Fort
Properties.specifications: panel deployed size: 2m x 1m x 10 cm; panel packed size: 60 x 40 x 10 cm; deployment: 5 seconds spring-loaded; protection: NIJ Level IV — rifle rated; interlocking: Panels connect for extended barriers; weight per panel: 12 kg; panels per kit: 4; reusable: Refoldable for transport

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Suppression Collar SC-4

Properties.description: A locking collar device that suppresses all neural interface functions while worn, effectively de-augmenting the wearer without surgical removal of their implants. The SC-4 generates a precisely calibrated electromagnetic field that disrupts the neural interface's communication with brain tissue, shutting down all augmented functions — Diaspora access, cognitive enhancement, sensory augmentation, and cyberware control. The collar is locked with a biometric key and includes tamper detection that can administer a painful but non-lethal shock if removal is attempted. Carrion markets it to law enforcement for augmented prisoner management, but its use as a control device for involuntary subjects has been documented.
Properties.aliases: SC-4, Kill Collar, Slave Ring, Carrion Leash
Properties.specifications: effect: Complete neural interface suppression; field type: Calibrated EM disruption; lock: Biometric key; info: tamper-resistant; 50; 000V; tamper response: Non-lethal shock; weight: 0.3 kg; battery: 30-day standby; activation: Instant on collar closure; deactivation: Biometric key required; side effects: Disorientation and nausea during neural shutdown
Properties.story_hooks: SC-4 collars are being used by a trafficking operation to control augmented victims — the collars de-augment them, cutting them off from Diaspora communication and any ability to call for help.; A modified SC-4 has been developed that suppresses specific neural interface functions selectively — it can disable motor control cyberware while leaving sensory functions intact, creating a paralysis device that leaves the victim aware.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Tactical Smoke Grenade TSG-5

Properties.description: A military-grade smoke grenade producing a dense, multi-spectrum obscurant cloud that blocks visual, thermal, and laser observation simultaneously. The TSG-5 generates a 20-meter smoke screen lasting 90 seconds using a combination of hexachloroethane smoke and metallic chaff that attenuates infrared and laser wavelengths. The smoke is non-toxic but extremely dense, reducing visibility to less than 1 meter within the cloud. The grenade is standard equipment for tactical retreat, casualty evacuation, and movement concealment.
Properties.aliases: TSG-5, Smoke Bomb, Carrion Fog, Screen Grenade
Properties.specifications: cloud radius: 20 meters; duration: 90 seconds; obscurant type: Multi-spectrum — visual + thermal + laser; visibility within cloud: Less than 1 meter; toxicity: Non-toxic but respiratory irritant in concentration; weight: 0.3 kg; activation: Pin-pull; info: 2-second delay; wind resistance: Effective in winds up to 15 km/h
Properties.story_hooks: Six TSG-5 grenades deployed simultaneously created a 120-meter smoke screen that blinded every sensor in a corporate perimeter for 90 seconds — the breach team was inside before the smoke cleared.; A modified TSG-5 has been developed that produces smoke with embedded conductive particles — the cloud jams wireless communications in addition to blocking observation.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Terrain Denial Foam Canister TDF-3

Properties.description: A throwable canister that deploys a rapid-expanding structural foam capable of blocking doorways, corridors, and openings in under 5 seconds. The foam expands to 50x its canister volume and hardens to the compressive strength of concrete within 10 seconds of deployment. A single canister can seal a standard doorway with a barrier that requires power tools to remove. The foam is non-toxic and fire-resistant, making it safe for enclosed space deployment. Carrion markets it for emergency barricading, breach denial, and perimeter hardening, but it has been adopted by everyone from home defenders to bank robbers for creating instant obstacles.
Properties.aliases: TDF-3, Block Foam, Wall Can, Barrier Bomb
Properties.specifications: expansion: 50x canister volume in 5 seconds; hardening: Concrete-equivalent compressive strength in 10 seconds; coverage: Seals standard doorway (2m x 0.9m) per canister; fire resistance: Non-combustible; toxicity: Non-toxic during and after curing; removal: Power tools required — saw; info: drill; or jackhammer; weight: 0.6 kg per canister; shelf life: 5 years
Properties.story_hooks: Every exit from a building was sealed with TDF-3 foam simultaneously — someone trapped 200 people inside and the foam barriers will take hours to cut through.; A street community is using TDF-3 to build permanent structures — the foam hardens into walls that are as strong as concrete, and they are constructing entire buildings from throw canisters.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Toxic Environment Mapping Kit TEMK-2

Properties.description: A portable environmental mapping system that deploys ground-level sensors to create a real-time contamination map of the surrounding area. The TEMK-2 includes 12 deployable sensor stakes that monitor air quality, soil contamination, radiation levels, and water toxicity within a 500-meter radius, transmitting data to a handheld display that generates color-coded contamination maps. The system identifies safe corridors through contaminated zones and provides real-time warnings when contamination levels change.
Properties.aliases: TEMK-2, Hazard Map, Poison Chart, Carrion Map
Properties.specifications: sensors: 12 deployable stakes; coverage: 500-meter radius; monitoring: Air; info: soil; radiation; water; 10 seconds each; display: Handheld color-coded contamination map; stake battery: 72 hours per stake; weight: 3.5 kg complete kit; warnings: Real-time contamination level change alerts; deployment: Drive stakes into ground
Properties.story_hooks: A TEMK-2 deployed in a supposedly clean Tier 2 district revealed contamination levels that exceed safety standards — the contamination source is a sealed facility that claims to produce nothing hazardous.; TEMK-2 data from multiple deployments has been compiled to create a comprehensive contamination map of lower-tier Meridian 88 — the map reveals that safe corridors between contaminated zones form a pattern that suggests deliberate boundary management.

Nodes.Name: Carrion Defense Works Whisper Veil Counter-Surveillance Cloak

Properties.description: A hooded cloak woven with active signal-jamming fibers that create a localized dead zone around the wearer, blocking all wireless signals within a 2-meter radius. The Whisper Veil disrupts WiFi, cellular, Diaspora connections, Bluetooth, RFID, and neural interface external communications, making the wearer invisible to wireless tracking while simultaneously preventing any electronic eavesdropping. The fabric contains embedded micro-batteries that power the jamming mesh for 6 hours before requiring recharge. The cloak's visual appearance is nondescript — a plain, dark hooded garment that draws no attention in urban environments.
Properties.aliases: Whisper Veil, Anti-Spy Cloak, Carrion Veil, Silent Shroud
Properties.specifications: jamming radius: 2 meters from wearer; frequency coverage: All commercial wireless bands; effect: Complete wireless signal suppression in radius; power source: Embedded micro-batteries; info: 6-hour operation; recharge: 2 hours from standard power; weight: 1.2 kg; appearance: Plain dark hooded cloak; side effect: Wearer also loses all wireless connectivity
Properties.story_hooks: A murder was committed within a Whisper Veil's jamming radius — no electronic evidence exists for the 2-meter zone around the killing, creating a perfect blind spot in total surveillance coverage.; Modified Whisper Veils with expanded 10-meter jamming radius have appeared on the market — one person wearing it can black out an entire room's communications.

Properties.description:
The Cassandra Intercept Collar is a passive signals intelligence device worn around the neck or wrist — resembling, at a glance, an unremarkable piece of industrial-grade biometric jewelry. Beneath its brushed-titanium housing lies a broadband radio frequency harvester capable of passively recording all unencrypted and weakly encrypted transmissions within a 200-meter radius, logging them to an internal solid-state archive with a 96-hour rolling buffer. The device never transmits, making it essentially invisible to signal-detection sweeps — it only listens.

What makes the Cassandra distinctive is its onboard linguistic processing chip, a stripped-down derivative of corporate-grade natural language AI, capable of real-time transcription, speaker identification across up to twelve simultaneous voices, and keyword flagging. Operators can set watch-word profiles before an operation — names, codewords, technical terms — and the Collar will vibrate subtly against the skin when a flagged term is detected in ambient transmissions. The full intercept archive can be dumped to an encrypted external drive via a shielded inductive port on the device's inner face.

The Cassandra is the preferred tool of intelligence brokers, long-haul surveillance operatives, and corporate espionage specialists who need to build a communications picture of a target environment without ever revealing their presence. It is also quietly popular among Meridian 88's journalist underground, who use it to harvest the ambient chatter of corporate security teams at public events — a practice that is technically illegal under the city's Signals Privacy Statutes but almost impossible to detect or prosecute.
Properties.tactical_use: Worn into target environments where active surveillance equipment would be detected. The operator sets keyword profiles in advance, enters the area of interest, and allows the Cassandra to passively harvest ambient communications — security team chatter, executive conversations, encrypted channels weak enough to crack in real-time. The haptic alert system allows the wearer to respond immediately to flagged transmissions without consulting any visible device. Post-operation, the full archive is dumped and processed by the operator or their intelligence handler to reconstruct a detailed picture of the target's communication patterns.
Properties.cultural_context: The Cassandra occupies a strange position in Meridian 88's shadow economy — it is simultaneously one of the most coveted tools of the intelligence trade and one of the most feared. In corporate circles, awareness of the device's existence has spawned a quiet paranoia about communication hygiene at public events and social gatherings. Wearing a Cassandra into a high-security venue is considered one of the boldest moves an intelligence operative can make, and successful harvests from such operations are spoken of with the reverence of heist stories. Among journalists and civil liberties advocates, the device is a complicated symbol — a surveillance tool that can be turned against the surveillance state.
Properties.specifications: intercept_radius: 200 meters (unobstructed), 80 meters (dense urban); frequency_range: 20 MHz – 6 GHz; archive_capacity: 96 hours rolling buffer, 4TB solid-state; simultaneous_speaker_tracking: 12; keyword_profiles: Up to 500 flagged terms per active profile; transmission_output: None — passive only; data_extraction: Shielded inductive port, encrypted AES-384; battery_life: 18 hours active processing, 72 hours passive logging; dimensions: Collar band: 28 cm x 1.8 cm x 0.9 cm; weight: 85 grams; disguise_rating: Passes as consumer biometric wearable at visual inspection
Properties.story_hooks: A Cassandra archive pulled from a dead intelligence operative contains recordings that implicate a senior Meridian 88 city official in a private conversation with a known organized crime figure — but the recording was obtained illegally, making it simultaneously explosive and legally useless.; Someone has modified a Cassandra to not just listen but subtly retransmit harvested communications with a time delay, effectively turning the wearer into an unknowing relay node for a third party's surveillance network.; A Tessera Corponation executive is offering a significant sum for the return of a specific Cassandra unit — one that was stolen from a company courier. They claim it contains proprietary firmware. The device's current owner doesn't know what they have.; The players are hired to attend a corporate gala wearing Cassandras — but midway through the event, the haptic alert system begins firing continuously, suggesting an enormous volume of flagged transmissions. Someone at this party is running a major operation, and the players are inadvertently harvesting evidence of it.

Properties.description:
The Metabolic Flux Monitor is a wearable biosensing platform developed by Helix Biosystems for field personnel operating under extended physiological stress. Worn as a cuff on the forearm, the device continuously samples transdermal biomarker gradients — including cortisol, lactate, glucose, inflammatory cytokines, and hydration status — and synthesizes these into a real-time physiological load score displayed on a flexible e-ink surface along the outer face of the cuff. An alert system, configurable for audible, haptic, or hardwired output to connected kit, triggers when monitored values cross user-defined thresholds, flagging impending performance degradation before it becomes incapacitation.

Helix designed the Flux Monitor for a dual market: elite athletic performance optimization and corporate field medicine for personnel working in hazardous environments. The underlying sensor array is derived from Helix's clinical diagnostic hardware, miniaturized and ruggedized for continuous wear. What the device does that clinical equipment cannot is contextualize — its onboard inference module correlates biomarker combinations rather than individual values, distinguishing between dehydration-induced lactate elevation and genuine muscle damage, or between acute stress response and the early signature of pharmaceutical interaction. This contextual layer makes it meaningfully more useful than simple threshold monitors.

The Flux Monitor has found a third market that Helix neither advertises nor discourages: operators who need to monitor the physiological state of personnel who cannot or will not self-report. A cuff worn by a team member under duress, in a hostage situation, or operating in conditions that preclude verbal communication provides the team lead with a continuous passive readout of that individual's status.
Properties.aliases: Flux Band, The Ticker, Helix Cuff
Properties.tactical_use: Team leads use the Flux Monitor's wireless telemetry to maintain passive physiological awareness of team members during operations where verbal check-ins are impossible. The cortisol and epinephrine proxy values provide early warning of acute stress events — a sudden spike on a team member operating in a separate location can indicate discovery, confrontation, or injury before any communication is possible. Medical personnel use it to triage personnel after extraction, identifying those with masked injuries or pharmaceutical load that self-reporting would not reveal. Solo operators use the threshold alert system as a fatigue management tool during extended operations.
Properties.cultural_context: The Restricted designation stems from privacy advocacy pressure following documented cases of employers using the Flux Monitor to conduct continuous physiological surveillance of workers without disclosure. In Meridian 88's corporate enclave districts, wearing one is a condition of employment for certain high-value technical personnel — framed as a safety measure, enforced as policy. Outside those enclaves, the cuff is read as either a serious medical tool or a signal that the wearer is operating under someone else's oversight, neither of which is casual. Among freelance operators, wearing one voluntarily signals professionalism; being made to wear one signals something else entirely.
Properties.specifications: weight: 68g; monitored_biomarkers: Cortisol, lactate, glucose, hydration index, IL-6 cytokine proxy, epinephrine proxy; sample_rate: Continuous, primary analysis cycle every 4 seconds; display: Flexible e-ink, 40mm x 12mm active area, visible in direct sunlight; alert_modes: Audible (configurable volume), haptic (vibration), hardwire signal output to connected devices; telemetry_range_wireless: Up to 80m line-of-sight, encrypted short-range band; battery_life: 72 hours continuous operation; water_resistance: IP68; cuff_size_range: Adjustable 140mm to 230mm circumference
Properties.story_hooks: A Flux Monitor recovered from an abandoned safehouse shows 11 days of continuous logged data on an unknown wearer — the physiological profile documents what appears to be prolonged captivity, with stress spikes correlating precisely to times that match a known interrogation protocol.; A corporate wellness program has been quietly issuing Flux Monitors to all mid-tier employees under a 'voluntary' health initiative; a data analyst has noticed that the telemetry is being routed not to medical staff but to the behavioral risk assessment division.; A solo operator's Flux Monitor data is the only record of their final hours — the biomarker sequence documents a pharmaceutical exposure event that the official incident report attributes to unrelated causes.

Properties.description:
The Myomeric Pressure Suit is a biomimetic compression garment engineered around synthetic muscle fiber bundles — myomeric actuators — woven throughout a high-density elastomer frame. At rest, the suit provides consistent compressive force across the wearer's musculature, reducing fatigue and supporting joint stability during prolonged activity. When external impact is detected through the suit's embedded piezoelectric sensor array, the myomeric fibers contract in the affected region within milliseconds, dramatically increasing local tissue density and distributing the impact load across a wider biological surface area. The effect is analogous to tensing a muscle before a blow, executed faster and more precisely than any voluntary human response.

Helix's design philosophy here is fundamentally different from conventional armor: rather than interposing a material barrier between the threat and the wearer, the Myomeric Suit augments the body itself to better absorb and survive trauma. The distinction matters because the suit has no rigid components and no ballistic panels — it does not stop a round, but it significantly improves the wearer's survivability from wounds that would otherwise be incapacitating. Internal bleeding from blunt trauma is measurably reduced. Stab wounds are shallower on average. Bone fractures under compression loads are less frequent. Helix's clinical literature frames the suit as a medical device rather than armor, a classification that carries its own regulatory implications.

The suit requires a baseline biometric intake to tune the myomeric response to the wearer's specific tissue density, body composition, and resting muscle tone. Improperly fitted suits have caused compartment syndrome in documented cases when the contraction response misfired at high intensity across an extended area. Helix's certification process is rigorous, and uncertified suits — which circulate on the grey market — are considered genuinely dangerous by people who understand what they are.
Properties.aliases: Muscle Wrap, The Second Body, Helix Shell
Properties.tactical_use: Not a replacement for ballistic protection — the Myomeric Suit is a survivability multiplier worn beneath other armor or used alone in environments where conventional armor cannot be concealed. Most effective against melee, blunt force, and low-velocity projectiles. Operators who survive gunshot wounds in the suit report significantly reduced secondary trauma and faster recovery. Widely used in combination with the Reactive Shear Mantle by operators who can afford both layers.
Properties.cultural_context: The Myomeric Pressure Suit sits at the intersection of performance enhancement and protection, and its users often frame it in terms of bodily optimization rather than defense. In corporate wellness culture, certified suits are status objects — Helix markets premium configurations to executive health programs. On the street, uncertified grey-market suits are circulated with the understanding that they are dangerous and that wearing one is an act of calculated desperation or ignorance. The clinical framing of the suit as a medical device creates a persistent ambiguity about who is permitted to wear one and under what circumstances.
Properties.specifications: weight: 1.8 kg (full body configuration); coverage: Full body musculature and joint systems; contraction_response_time: 0.22 milliseconds post-impact detection; resting_compression_output: 18–25 mmHg (adjustable by zone); peak_contraction_force: Up to 4x ambient tissue compression in impact zone; calibration_requirement: Mandatory biometric intake; recalibration recommended after significant body composition change; power_source: Integrated flexible micro-cell array (72-hour continuous operation); profile: Invisible under standard clothing
Properties.story_hooks: A grey-market Myomeric Suit has caused a compartment syndrome fatality in the outer districts — the victim was a minor, and someone in the certification chain sold uncalibrated suits knowing the risks; Helix wants the source found before regulators do.; A corporate executive survived an assassination attempt that should have been fatal; the shooter insists the rounds hit center mass, and a Helix insider suggests the executive may have been wearing an unreleased next-generation Myomeric configuration not yet on the market.; A sports league is funding an investigation into a fighter who has won fifteen consecutive bouts without visible injury — the league suspects a Myomeric Suit, but the fighter's medical records have been sealed under a Helix confidentiality agreement.; Someone is distributing calibration override codes for Myomeric Suits on the dark net — the codes allow the contraction response to be triggered remotely, turning the suit into a compression weapon against its own wearer.

Properties.description:
The Nanite Flood Injector is a high-pressure autoinjector housing a concentrated suspension of third-generation repair nanites in a saline-based carrier medium. Upon injection, the nanite payload disperses through the bloodstream and autonomously targets sites of acute tissue damage — sealing ruptured capillaries, bridging torn muscle fiber, and stabilizing fractured bone surfaces using harvested calcium and iron from the surrounding biological environment. The device's onboard microprocessor pre-programs nanite behavior based on a brief biometric handshake with the patient's skin conductance and pulse, allowing it to distinguish between wound types and prioritize repair sequencing.

The Flood Injector's defining characteristic is its speed and bluntness. Unlike precision nanite therapies administered in clinical settings, this device floods the body with a broad-spectrum swarm designed to handle the most common trauma profiles encountered in the field — gunshots, blade wounds, blunt trauma, and chemical burns. The tradeoff is metabolic cost: the nanites consume significant biological resources during operation, leaving the patient exhausted and often nauseated for hours after the repair cycle completes. Repeated use within a short window can cause nanite saturation syndrome, where competing swarms interfere with one another and begin misidentifying healthy tissue as damage sites.

Helix Biosystems markets the Flood Injector primarily to corporate medical response teams and licensed trauma surgeons for emergency pre-op stabilization, but the device has proliferated heavily into the gray and black markets. It is particularly prized by solo operators who cannot afford a dedicated medic. The injector's distinctive amber autoinjector housing and the faint blue luminescence visible through the skin during an active nanite cycle have made it a recognizable — and sometimes feared — sight in Meridian 88's underground clinics.
Properties.aliases: Flood Gun, The Swarm, Nanite Spike, Helix Hammer
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed as a last-resort stabilizer when a patient is at risk of death before evacuation is possible. Field operators self-administer or apply to downed teammates. The post-cycle exhaustion is a known tactical liability — units are trained to inject and immediately move to cover, as the patient will be combat-ineffective for 10–20 minutes during the active repair cycle. Medical personnel use it to buy time before surgery rather than as a standalone cure.
Properties.cultural_context: The Nanite Flood Injector occupies an uncomfortable legal space in Meridian 88. Licensed medical practitioners can prescribe and carry them; unlicensed possession is a gray-market offense that enforcement treats inconsistently depending on district and who's paying protection. In wealthier sectors, the device is a status symbol of preparedness among corporate executives who maintain personal security details. In the Underbelly, it's survival infrastructure. Street medics who carry them are accorded significant respect — and are frequent kidnapping targets by gangs who want a tame healer.
Properties.specifications: dimensions: 18cm length, standard autoinjector form factor; weight: 94g loaded; nanite_payload: ~4.2 billion repair nanites per dose; activation: Single-button autoinjector, intramuscular or intravenous delivery; repair_onset: 45–90 seconds to visible wound closure; full_cycle_duration: 8–14 minutes for complete repair of moderate trauma; metabolic_cost: Equivalent to approximately 6 hours of heavy physical exertion; reuse_interval: Minimum 72 hours between doses to avoid saturation syndrome; doses_per_unit: 1; single_use: true
Properties.story_hooks: A shipment of Flood Injectors has been modified by an unknown party to carry a secondary nanite payload that harvests and transmits biometric data — anyone injected has been unknowingly tagged and monitored. The source of the modification points toward a Helix Biosystems internal division that officially doesn't exist.; Nanite saturation syndrome cases are spiking in the Underbelly, suggesting someone is either selling multi-dose injectors illegally or convincing desperate users to re-dose too soon. A black-market dealer claims the instructions were deliberately misprinted.; A player character who was injected with a Flood Injector weeks ago begins experiencing strange tissue behavior — the nanites never fully deactivated, and something in their biology is being slowly, methodically altered.

Properties.description:
The Olfactory Gradient Probe is a handheld chemical plume detection and source-location instrument that uses an array of 2,400 synthetic chemoreceptor filaments to identify, classify, and triangulate the origin point of airborne chemical signatures. Unlike conventional gas detectors that simply alert to the presence of a substance, the OGP maps concentration gradients across space — effectively 'smelling' which direction a scent is getting stronger — and uses that gradient data to compute a vector toward the emission source. The chemoreceptor array is modeled on vertebrate olfactory epithelium but operates at a sensitivity roughly 80 times greater than baseline human olfaction, capable of detecting compounds at parts-per-trillion concentrations.

Helix Biosystems engineered the OGP originally for pharmaceutical contamination tracing in clean-room environments, but the probe's utility in field applications became rapidly apparent. The device can identify over 14,000 indexed chemical signatures including explosives precursors, specific pharmaceutical compounds, biological markers associated with stress responses (adrenaline metabolites, cortisol derivatives present in sweat), and the proprietary chemical tracers used by several major corporations to mark restricted personnel and assets. A rolling update subscription keeps the chemical index current. The probe's interface presents gradient data as a directional compass overlay with confidence percentages, and can log a full chemical environment profile for later forensic analysis.

The OGP occupies an uncomfortable legal space in Meridian 88. Its capacity to detect stress-chemistry signatures means it can effectively identify frightened or nervous individuals in a crowd — a capability that law enforcement, corporate interrogators, and bounty hunters find enormously attractive and civil liberties advocates find deeply troubling. Helix markets it carefully as an 'industrial and forensic instrument,' but its presence in less scrupulous hands is an open secret.
Properties.aliases: OGP, the Bloodhound, Smell Stick, Gradient Wand
Properties.tactical_use: Operators use the OGP to sweep rooms for hidden individuals using stress-chemistry signatures before entry, trace the path of a target through a space by following adrenaline-metabolite trails, and detect concealed explosives or contraband by identifying precursor compounds. Bounty hunters use it to locate hiding targets in complex environments. Corporate security teams use it to identify unauthorized personnel carrying proprietary chemical tracers. Forensic investigators use it to reconstruct who was present in a space and their approximate physiological state during an incident.
Properties.cultural_context: The OGP has generated significant cultural anxiety in Meridian 88's lower districts, where residents fear corporate security teams sweeping public spaces for stress markers — effectively scanning crowds for anyone nervous enough to be flagged as suspicious. 'Running hot' has become street slang for displaying stress chemistry that would register on a Bloodhound scan. Some underground pharmacies sell compounds that temporarily suppress adrenaline metabolite production, marketed euphemistically as 'calm supplements.' The device is both a serious professional instrument and a symbol of invasive surveillance overreach depending entirely on who's holding it.
Properties.specifications: chemoreceptor_count: 2,400 synthetic filaments; detection_sensitivity: Parts-per-trillion for indexed compounds; chemical_index_size: 14,000+ indexed signatures (base); subscription expands coverage; detection_range: Active sampling to 15m; gradient source triangulation to 60m in still air; triangulation_accuracy: ±3 degrees bearing, ±8m distance at 60m range; biological_markers: Adrenaline metabolites, cortisol derivatives, fear-sweat compound profiles; corporate_tracer_database: 47 known corporate tracer compounds (current subscription); interface: Directional compass overlay with confidence percentage, chemical ID readout; logging: Full chemical environment profile capture for forensic export; dimensions: 280mm x 45mm x 35mm (wand form factor); weight: 340g; battery_life: 18 hours continuous operation; operating_conditions: 0°C to 45°C; humidity 10–95% non-condensing
Properties.story_hooks: A character discovers their safe house has been swept by an OGP — whoever did it now has a full chemical profile of everyone who was present, including stress states during specific moments; A street pharmacist is selling 'calm supplements' that actually suppress OGP-detectable markers — corporate security wants to know who's supplying counter-measure drugs to the population; An OGP sweep at a corporate gala identifies a specific attendee as carrying a proprietary tracer belonging to a rival corporation — but the attendee claims never to have worked for that corp; A character needs to move through a corporate facility where OGP sweeps are conducted — they have 18 minutes to find a route before the device's battery logs are transmitted to security central

Properties.description:
The Pulmonary Resection Bellows is a compact, accordion-framed pneumatic device designed to maintain respiratory function in patients whose pulmonary musculature has been compromised by trauma, toxin exposure, or combat-grade neurotoxic agents. It attaches via a sealed oral-nasal interface and a pair of intercostal anchor clips, mechanically driving inhalation and exhalation cycles calibrated to the patient's blood-oxygen readout through a small embedded biosensor. In field conditions, it can sustain a flatlined respiratory system for up to six hours without recharge.

What distinguishes the Bellows from earlier mechanical ventilators is its adaptive rhythm engine — a low-power analogue processor that modulates breath cadence in response to detected movement, ambient noise, and patient heart rate variability. This means a downed operative being carried through a firefight won't asphyxiate due to positional changes or jostling. The device also features a one-way toxin filter membrane rated for most aerosolized chemical agents found in Meridian 88's contested industrial zones.

The Bellows is standard-issue in Helix Biosystems extraction teams and has found a devoted secondary market among deep-sewer runners and tunnel-breach specialists who work in environments with chronically compromised air quality. Street medics refer to it as 'The Deacon' — something that keeps you breathing when you have no business doing so.
Properties.aliases: The Deacon, Iron Lungs, The Squeezer
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed immediately following chest trauma, drowning events, or neurotoxin exposure that collapses diaphragm function. A medic can attach the Bellows in under forty seconds. Once secured, the patient can be moved, carried, or dragged without interrupting respiratory support. Operators also use it prophylactically before breaching chemically contaminated spaces, running it at low support alongside natural breathing to reduce lung fatigue during prolonged toxic exposure.
Properties.cultural_context: Among extraction crews and tunnel runners, carrying a Bellows is considered a mark of professional seriousness — it signals that you expect casualties bad enough to need sustained life support in the field, and you're prepared for it. In the poorer outer wards, bootleg Bellows units with degraded filter membranes circulate widely, used by residents living near Ouroboros Energy's poorly sealed exhaust stacks. Helix's licensing requirements are widely resented; unlicensed possession in corporate-controlled zones carries fines that price the device out of reach for those who need it most.
Properties.specifications: weight: 1.4 kg assembled; dimensions: 22 cm x 14 cm x 9 cm (collapsed); battery_life: 6 hours continuous operation; breath_rate_range: 8–28 cycles per minute; filter_rating: Class IV aerosolized agents; interface: Sealed oral-nasal mask with intercostal anchor clips (sizes A–D); sensor_refresh_rate: Every 0.4 seconds; compatible_patients: Human baseline, most cyberframe configurations with intact thorax
Properties.story_hooks: A shipment of Bellows units with deliberately degraded filter membranes has been routed to outer ward free clinics — someone is profiting from the failures, and the bodies are starting to pile up.; A player character wakes up post-operation with a Bellows attached and no memory of how they got there — the device's biosensor log contains encrypted movement data from the last six hours.; A Helix Biosystems licensing inspector is found dead in a tunnel with a bootleg Bellows still running on her face, keeping her technically alive despite catastrophic brain death — someone wants to delay the official time of death.; A tunnel runner community has jury-rigged a network of salvaged Bellows units into a crude collective air filtration system for their hab-block — Helix's legal team has arrived to dismantle it.
