Properties.description:
The Ambient Mesh Leech is a passive network parasitism device — a flat, adhesive unit roughly the size of a playing card that attaches to any surface in proximity to active mesh infrastructure and draws communication access from it without registration, authentication, or detectable network presence. It does not connect to the mesh. It infiltrates the connection of something that is already connected, riding the existing authenticated session of a nearby node — a traffic signal, a building management system, a licensed commercial relay — without altering that node's behavior in any measurable way. To the mesh, the Leech does not exist.

Ringo Corponation developed the Leech as an infrastructure audit tool, ostensibly for identifying unauthorized mesh connections by demonstrating how easily they could be established — a rationale that satisfied regulators and provided the legal framework for a product that is, in practice, a highly sophisticated unauthorized access device. The Leech's Phantom Session Architecture generates a synthetic traffic signature that mimics the statistical profile of the host node's normal data throughput, distributing Leech communications invisibly within the host's existing traffic patterns. Extracting the Leech's communications from a captured traffic log requires knowing the Leech's specific session key — without it, the data is indistinguishable from the host node's routine transmissions.

The Leech is a tool of economic necessity as much as operational security. In Meridian 88's lower precincts, licensed mesh access is expensive, monitored, and increasingly tiered — the richest users get the cleanest channels, and the poorest make do with degraded public access points that log everything. The Leech provides clean, unmonitored connectivity by stealing it from infrastructure that has already paid for the privilege. This has made it ubiquitous far beyond the criminal and intelligence communities Ringo nominally targets — it is found in community centers, underground clinics, and housing collectives that cannot afford licensed access and will not tolerate surveillance of what little connectivity they have.
Properties.aliases: The Barnacle, The Free Rider, Ghost Node
Properties.tactical_use: In operational contexts, the Leech is deployed as a semi-permanent communication node — placed once and left in position for the duration of an operation or an extended campaign. Field operatives pair their devices to a Leech attached to nearby infrastructure and communicate through the host node's session without appearing on any network access log. Multiple Leeches can be chained to create a distributed communication network that exists entirely within the legitimate traffic of Meridian 88's own infrastructure. Detection requires physical location and removal of the device — it cannot be remotely identified or disabled. This makes it particularly valuable for long-term embedded operations where operational security must be maintained over weeks or months.
Properties.cultural_context: The Barnacle is, in the lower precincts of Meridian 88, something close to a public utility. Community mesh networks built on Leeches provide connectivity to tens of thousands of residents who have been priced out of licensed access or who refuse to use monitored public terminals. There is an informal culture of Leech placement — experienced users place them in high-traffic locations, share the session keys through trusted networks, and maintain them as a community resource. This has created an uneasy situation for authorities: prosecution requires identifying and charging individuals who are often simply trying to access information, and the Leeches themselves are so small and well-concealed that enforcement sweeps rarely find more than a fraction of active units. Ringo Corponation benefits from studied ambiguity about the product's predominant use, maintaining its 'infrastructure audit tool' designation while quietly enjoying the market that designation provides cover for.
Properties.specifications: dimensions: 8.5cm × 5.4cm × 0.3cm; weight: 18g; host_node_compatibility: Any active Meridian 88 Civic Mesh v3.0+ authenticated node within 6m; detection_resistance: Undetectable by standard mesh monitoring; detectable by traffic forensic analysis with known session key only; bandwidth_parasitism: Up to 40% of host node capacity without degrading host performance; simultaneous_user_capacity: Up to 8 paired devices; power_source: Passive RF energy harvesting from host node emissions, indefinite operation; session_key_length: 256-bit operator-defined; adhesive_rating: Rated for concrete, steel, glass, ceramic; removal leaves no residue; maximum_operational_lifespan: Approximately 4 years before component degradation
Properties.story_hooks: A Leech the players placed three months ago is still active — but someone else has added their devices to the session, meaning an unknown party has been using the players' covert channel as their own.; A sweep of a particular block finds forty-seven Leeches in a six-square-block area, all keyed to the same session — someone built a shadow mesh network of significant scale, and it was used for something that left traces in the traffic logs of every host node involved.; A community organization's Leech network goes dark simultaneously across an entire precinct. Not removed — just dead. Something killed them remotely, which should be impossible.; Ringo Corponation quietly approaches the players to recover a specific Leech from a specific location. They won't say what's on it. They will pay significantly above market rate. The location is in the middle of a district controlled by people who will not appreciate visitors.; A Leech left in place during a previous operation begins transmitting on a new session key that the players never programmed — something is using their hardware to communicate, and it's been doing so for weeks.

Properties.description:
The Composite Surge Frame is Ringo Corponation's entry into the powered exoskeleton market, developed initially for industrial load-bearing applications in Ringo's own logistics and courier infrastructure before being adapted into a protective combat platform. The frame consists of a hardened polymer-composite shell over a motorized titanium alloy skeletal structure, covering the full torso, arms, and legs. Hydraulic micro-actuators augment the wearer's physical strength by a factor of approximately 2.8 and provide load-bearing support that allows the operator to carry armor mass that would be prohibitive without powered assistance. The integrated plating is rated for sustained rifle-caliber fire, making the CSF one of the few commercially available systems offering genuine hard-armor protection to the entire body.

Ringo's engineering philosophy prioritizes durability and repairability over elegance. The CSF uses standardized fastening systems, commercially available hydraulic components, and a modular panel design that allows field replacement of damaged sections using basic tools. This has made the frame remarkably popular in environments far from reliable supply chains — frontier industrial zones, contested territorial borders, and disaster recovery operations where a technician with a socket wrench can keep a frame operational indefinitely. The power system uses a hybrid fuel-cell and capacitor bank that provides 10 hours of standard operation or approximately 4 hours under sustained combat load.

The CSF is bulky, loud in operation, and unmistakably industrial in aesthetic — it does not attempt to conceal itself. Operators in the frame stand roughly 15 centimeters taller than their natural height and move with the deliberate, slightly mechanical gait that hydraulic-assisted movement produces. In Meridian 88's street culture, the CSF has become associated with a specific archetype: the heavily built, pragmatic enforcer who values function absolutely over form, and who is prepared to absorb tremendous punishment in exchange for a complete absence of subtlety.
Properties.aliases: Surge Rig, The Bull, Ringo Exo, CSF
Properties.tactical_use: CSF operators are typically deployed as breaching elements, point personnel in high-fire corridors, or fire support anchors. The frame's strength augmentation allows operators to carry and use weapon platforms that would normally require vehicle or emplacement mounting. The primary tactical limitation is noise — the CSF is audible at significant range, making any form of surprise approach nearly impossible. Standard doctrine pairs CSF operators with lighter, quieter team members who establish position before the frame moves.
Properties.cultural_context: The Composite Surge Frame occupies an interesting cultural position in Meridian 88 — it was designed for industrial workers, not soldiers, and this origin is visible in every aspect of its construction. In some communities, this industrial heritage gives the CSF a kind of working-class authenticity that more expensive, specialized military exoskeletons lack. Ringo has leaned into this with marketing that emphasizes reliability and repairability over performance metrics. Among mercenary units, a CSF operator is colloquially called 'the anchor' — the person who doesn't run, doesn't hide, and makes the enemy come to them.
Properties.specifications: weight_kg: 42; coverage: Full body — torso, arms, legs; strength_augmentation_multiplier: 2.8; impact_resistance_rating: NIJ Level IV equivalent (front torso), Level III (limbs); operational_duration_standard_hours: 10; operational_duration_combat_hours: 4; height_increase_cm: 15; noise_profile_db: Approximately 58dB at walking pace; field_repair_tool_requirement: Standard socket and torque kit; power_system: Hybrid fuel-cell / capacitor bank
Properties.story_hooks: A batch of CSF units sold to a frontier industrial operation has been seized by a local militia — the frames are now being used to hold a settlement hostage, and the players need to find a way to disable them without the standard override codes, which Ringo is withholding.; Ringo Corponation is quietly recalling specific CSF serial numbers due to a hydraulic actuator fault that causes the frame to lock up under sustained fire — but the recall notice hasn't reached operators in active conflict zones.; A CSF unit has been found abandoned in a Meridian 88 storm drain, interior still warm — the operator is gone but signs of a struggle inside the frame suggest they were extracted from it while it was still active.; A Ringo engineer is selling unauthorized CSF modification kits that boost strength augmentation to 4.5x — the modifications work, but the structural tolerances weren't designed for the load and frames are beginning to catastrophically fail mid-operation.

Properties.description: The Deniable Address Shard is a single-use cryptographic identity chip, roughly the size and shape of a broken fingernail, designed to generate a fully authenticated but entirely fictitious network identity that persists for exactly one communication session before the chip's internal logic physically destroys itself through a controlled electrochemical burn. Each Shard is pre-loaded at manufacture with a unique, non-repeating address seed derived from Ringo Corponation's proprietary entropy architecture, guaranteeing that no two Shards ever produce the same identity. The result is a communication session that, to any network observer, appears to originate from a legitimate registered user — one who simply does not exist.
Properties.tactical_use: Operatives use Shards when they need to make contact — with a fixer, a buyer, a target, a handler — without any possibility of that contact being traced back to a persistent identity. The Shard is loaded into any standard comm device via its contact port, used for the duration of the necessary communication, and then discarded. Because the chip physically destroys its own cryptographic material on termination, even a recovered Shard yields nothing actionable. The primary tactical limitation is the single-use nature: operators working extended operations must carry multiple Shards, and their supply chain for resupply becomes a vulnerability in itself. Ringo Corponation distributes them through layered intermediary networks, never directly.
Properties.cultural_context: The Deniable Address Shard occupies a peculiar legal and cultural position in Meridian 88. Technically prohibited under the Unified Network Identity Accountability Act — a piece of legislation that Ringo Corponation's own lobby arm helped draft, a fact not lost on anyone — the Shards are simultaneously one of Ringo's most profitable black-market revenue streams. Street-level users sometimes call them 'Ringo's little joke.' Among criminal defense attorneys, the Shard has become something of a philosophical touchstone: its existence implies that certain conversations are, by design, meant to be held outside the reach of accountability, and the question of who gets to make that determination is genuinely contested.
Properties.specifications: dimensions: 14mm x 6mm x 1.2mm chip format; weight: Less than 1g; session_duration: Single session, maximum 4 hours before forced termination; identity_persistence: Zero — chip destroys all key material on session end or physical compromise; authentication_depth: Passes Tier-2 network identity verification; fails against Tier-4 deep-packet biometric binding; self_destruction_trigger: Session end, physical fracture, or tamper detection; packaging: Sold in heat-sealed foil strips of 6 units; residue: Post-burn chip is inert ceramic; no recoverable data
Properties.story_hooks: A Shard recovered from a compromised drop is supposed to be inert — but the burn didn't complete. Fragments of the session's routing data survived. It's not enough to reconstruct the conversation, but it's enough to identify the network node the call touched.; Someone is selling counterfeit Shards that look identical to genuine Ringo units but don't self-destruct — they quietly transmit a copy of every session to an unknown third party.; A player receives a Shard in the mail with no accompanying message. The implication is clear: someone wants them to use it to make contact, but hasn't told them who to call.; Ringo Corponation's manufacturing facility for Shard entropy seeding has gone dark — no new legitimate Shards have entered the market in six weeks. The price has quadrupled and the counterfeits are multiplying.

Properties.description:
The Distributed Mesh Anchor Drone is a compact autonomous aerial platform developed by Ringo Corponation's infrastructure services division for establishing temporary relay and anchor points in environments where fixed infrastructure is absent, compromised, or actively denied. The drone is approximately 28cm in diameter, uses a shrouded quad-rotor configuration for operation in confined spaces, and carries a retractable 40-meter micro-filament tether that can serve as a physical cable guide, a tensioned anchor line, or a hardwire data conduit depending on the filament spool loaded. Once a target anchor point is identified — a structural beam, ventilation housing, or window reveal — the drone fires a spring-loaded micro-grapple and tensions the tether before entering a low-power hover-hold mode that maintains position with minimal noise and battery draw.

Ringo designed the Anchor Drone as a logistics tool for urban infrastructure inspection and repair, where technicians frequently need to route cables or establish working lines across gaps that are impractical to traverse physically. The drone's autonomous anchor-seeking behavior uses a combination of structural density imaging and load-bearing estimation to select anchor points likely to hold working loads, flagging unsuitable targets before committing the grapple. A simple companion app interface allows operators to designate target zones and minimum load ratings without requiring piloting skill, making the device accessible to non-specialist users.

The tether system's versatility has made the Anchor Drone considerably more interesting to operators outside infrastructure services. A hardwire data filament spool transforms the drone into a rapidly deployable physical network bridge across gaps that wireless signals cannot reliably cross — a feature that has not gone unnoticed by individuals for whom wireless transmission is a liability rather than a convenience.
Properties.aliases: Mesh Kite, Ringo Spider, The Anchor
Properties.tactical_use: Used to establish physical data tether bridges across elevator shafts, atria, and external building faces where wireless signal penetration is unreliable or where wireless transmission represents an interception risk. Extraction teams use the standard tether spool to rig traverse lines across gaps too wide or structurally uncertain for direct crossing. The drone can be pre-programmed with an anchor target and launched from cover, eliminating the need for an operator to expose themselves to establish a crossing point. In multi-floor operations, stacked anchor drones create a managed vertical cable run that can be recovered by drone retrieval rather than manual descent.
Properties.cultural_context: The Restricted classification reflects regulatory concern about unauthorized aerial deployment in dense urban airspace rather than the device's capabilities per se — Ringo lobbied successfully to keep it off the Prohibited list by emphasizing legitimate infrastructure applications. In practice, enforcement is inconsistent, and the Anchor Drone is common enough in construction and utility work that a packed unit in a contractor bag attracts little attention. Among operators who use hardwire data filament spools, the device represents a deliberate philosophical choice: physical data paths over wireless, accepting the operational complexity of tether management in exchange for the security of knowing the signal cannot be intercepted at distance.
Properties.specifications: diameter: 28cm; weight: 640g with standard tether spool; tether_length: 40 meters standard spool; tether_variants: Standard tensioned line (rated 180kg), hardwire data filament (100Mbps capable), hybrid power/data filament; grapple_holding_force: Up to 220kg on rated substrates; flight_noise: 61dB at 1 meter full thrust, 44dB hover-hold mode; battery_life: 22 minutes full flight, 4.5 hours hover-hold mode; max_operating_gap: 38 meters horizontal, 22 meters vertical; companion_interface: Ringo app or standalone controller unit; dimensions_packed: 32cm x 32cm x 8cm folded
Properties.story_hooks: A hardwire filament tether recovered from a decommissioned anchor point in a corporate tower's atrium carries residual data artifacts in its insulation coating — partial fragments of a transmission that was routed through it, enough to indicate the nature of the communication but not its full content.; Three Anchor Drones have been found in hover-hold mode at separate locations across the city, all anchored to the same structural beam type, all with their companion app pairing data wiped — someone has been using them as semi-permanent physical network bridges and is now in the process of recovering them.; A building's automated security system has logged repeated drone intrusions over six weeks, each time the drone anchoring to a specific external feature before entering hover-hold for several hours — the pattern suggests a long-duration physical tap on something attached to that face of the building.

Properties.description:
The Distributed Optic Swarm is a reconnaissance drone system consisting of twelve semi-autonomous micro-units, each approximately the size of a large insect, capable of independent navigation and collective mesh-coordinated surveillance. Each unit carries a wide-aperture optical sensor, a short-range acoustic pickup, and a minimal onboard processor running RINGO's SWARM coordination firmware. Individually, each drone is limited — its optics are adequate but not exceptional, its battery life is measured in minutes, and its processing is insufficient for complex autonomous behavior. Collectively, the swarm is a different instrument entirely.

The DOS's engineering distinction is RINGO's COLLECTIVE APERTURE protocol, which treats the twelve optical sensors as a single distributed imaging array. By correlating the slightly different perspectives of drones positioned across a space, the system constructs composite imagery of significantly higher resolution and depth than any single unit could produce. It also enables triangulation of sound sources, detection of active electronic emissions through multi-point signal comparison, and the identification of targets occluded from any individual drone's line of sight. The operator interface is a wrist-mounted display and a neural-adjacent earpiece that translates swarm data into a navigable overview — experienced operators describe controlling the DOS as developing a sense of the space rather than watching a feed.

RINGO CORPONATION markets the DOS primarily to investigative and intelligence clients — journalists, corporate intelligence firms, and private investigation agencies. Its civilian positioning keeps it below the threshold of military equipment regulation in most districts, though security forces have pushed repeatedly to have it reclassified. The swarm's small individual signature makes it exceptionally difficult to detect with standard anti-drone countermeasures, which are calibrated for larger units. The DOS is widely used and widely feared by anyone who needs to maintain operational security in Meridian 88's layered interior spaces.
Properties.aliases: DOS, The Flies, Ringo Eyes, Scatter Drones
Properties.tactical_use: Standard deployment involves releasing the swarm through a small opening — ventilation gap, mail slot, partial door breach — and using the collective aperture to map an interior space before physical entry. The acoustic triangulation function identifies personnel positions behind walls and through floors with reasonable accuracy. Electronic emission detection locates active devices — security terminals, communication hardware, powered weapons. In extended operations, swarm units can be staged at relay positions to extend communication range through signal-dead areas. Losing units to anti-drone countermeasures degrades but rarely eliminates capability, making the DOS resilient in hostile environments.
Properties.cultural_context: The DOS has a reputation that precedes it in corporate security circles — the discovery of a single swarm unit in a facility is treated as a major security event because the implication is that someone already has a detailed map of the interior. Among investigative journalists and freelance intelligence operatives, the DOS is considered essential equipment, a great equalizer that lets a single operator achieve surveillance coverage that previously required a team. There is a documented subculture of DOS operators who share swarm navigation techniques and COLLECTIVE APERTURE interpretation methods through encrypted forums — RINGO is believed to monitor these forums as a product development intelligence source.
Properties.specifications: unit_count: 12 per swarm kit; individual_unit_dimensions: 3.2cm wingspan, 1.1cm body length; individual_unit_weight: 1.4 grams; individual_battery_life: 8 minutes active flight; collective_imaging_resolution: Equivalent to 40MP at 10 meter range; acoustic_pickup_range: Up to 25 meters per unit; swarm_communication_protocol: Encrypted mesh, 2.4GHz and 5.8GHz adaptive; operator_interface: Wrist display unit plus neural-adjacent earpiece; recharge_time: 22 minutes full swarm via included cradle; minimum_functional_swarm_size: 4 units (degraded performance below 8)
Properties.story_hooks: A DOS swarm is recovered from inside a sealed corporate server room with its memory intact — the flight logs show it was navigating the space for six hours before the facility went into lockdown, and the imagery it captured includes personnel whose presence in that location is officially impossible.; One of the players' swarm units fails to return after a reconnaissance deployment — days later, it reappears in an unexpected location, suggesting it was captured, examined, and deliberately released, possibly with modifications.; RINGO Corponation pushes a mandatory firmware update that introduces a new feature: anonymous telemetry reporting swarm deployment locations back to RINGO's servers. An operator who reverse-engineers the update brings it to the players, and the question is what RINGO is doing with a real-time map of everywhere their product is being used.; A corporate security firm has developed a new counter-swarm protocol that identifies DOS units by their COLLECTIVE APERTURE communication signature — the players must complete a reconnaissance mission using a DOS against a target that is now specifically hardened against it.

Properties.description: The Ringo Corponation Drift Mesh Node is a compact, autonomous wireless relay unit designed to be deployed in environments where conventional fixed-infrastructure communication is unavailable, compromised, or under active surveillance. Roughly the size and weight of a large coin, the Drift Node adheres to any surface via micro-suction backing and immediately begins broadcasting a localized mesh relay point that integrates with other Drift Nodes and compatible devices in range, self-organizing into an encrypted peer-to-peer network without any central routing infrastructure. Up to sixty-four nodes can form a single self-healing mesh, automatically rerouting traffic around destroyed or compromised nodes within milliseconds.
Properties.aliases: Drift Node, Ghost Router, The Floater, Ringo Seed
Properties.tactical_use: Operators seed Drift Nodes throughout a target area in advance of an operation — tucked behind pipes, pressed under window ledges, stuck to the undersides of furniture. The resulting mesh provides a private communication infrastructure that exists entirely within the operational zone, immune to the target facility's own jamming or monitoring systems because it runs on frequencies that appear to be the building's own IoT backbone. Teams use the mesh for real-time coordination, triggering remote devices, and maintaining communication in structures designed to suppress external signals. Post-operation, the nodes are left in place to degrade naturally.
Properties.cultural_context: The Drift Node's legal status and low cost have made it ubiquitous across every tier of Meridian 88's society. Street vendors sell them openly alongside legitimate tech accessories. Their legitimate construction-site use case is real and common enough that possession alone is meaningless as evidence of criminal intent, which is precisely why organized groups prefer them. There is a certain democratic quality to the Drift Node — it is one of the few pieces of serious operational communications hardware available to someone with very little money. Community organizers in contested districts use them to maintain neighborhood communication networks when corporate entities shut down local mesh infrastructure during labor disputes.
Properties.specifications: dimensions: 28mm diameter, 4mm thickness; weight: 6g per node; mesh_capacity: Up to 64 nodes per self-organizing network; range_per_node: 80m line-of-sight; 40m through standard construction materials; encryption: DriftNet 256-bit rolling mesh encryption; transmission_signature: Mimics urban IoT device traffic (utility meters, environmental sensors); memory_wipe: Automatic at 24-hour mark or on tamper detection; housing_degradation: Full biodegradation within 14 days of deployment; power: Micro-battery; 36-hour operational life; packaging: Blister packs of 12 units
Properties.story_hooks: The party discovers an active DriftNet mesh in a building they're sweeping — the nodes are still fresh, meaning whoever deployed them is either still present or left very recently.; A community mesh network built from Drift Nodes in a lower-city district has been quietly co-opted by someone inserting nodes running modified firmware that logs all traffic before forwarding it.; Ringo Corponation's compliance flag system has been sold wholesale to a corporate intelligence buyer — every bulk Drift Node purchase in the past eight months has been logged and cross-referenced with known dissident networks.; A Drift Node that should have wiped and degraded is still active three months after a completed operation, broadcasting on a frequency that doesn't match DriftNet protocol — something is using the hardware as a shell for a different kind of transmission.

Properties.description:
The Fractal Deflection Chassis is a modular hard-plate armor system built on Ringo Corponation's proprietary fractal surface geometry — each plate's exterior is machined into a recursive angular pattern that statistically improves the probability of projectile deflection by altering the angle of incidence across the plate's surface. Unlike conventional flat or curved plates, the fractal geometry means that a round striking anywhere on the plate encounters a micro-angled surface, and a meaningful percentage of rounds that would penetrate a flat plate at a given velocity are instead deflected or tumbled. Ringo's internal testing data, which has been independently contested and partially verified, claims a 22% improvement in deflection rate against standard rifle rounds compared to equivalent-weight flat plate systems.

The modular chassis system uses a standardized attachment rail that allows individual plates to be reconfigured, added, or removed without tools in under two minutes. Ringo markets this as mission-adaptive geometry — operators can prioritize frontal protection, all-around coverage, or a reduced-profile configuration depending on the engagement context. The plates are constructed from a boron carbide and carbon nanotube composite that keeps weight competitive with ceramic alternatives at equivalent protection levels. A color-coding system on each plate's interior face indicates structural integrity, shifting from white to yellow to red as the composite degrades under repeated impacts.

Ringo's background in consumer electronics and communications hardware makes the Chassis an unusual product for a defense market — the company entered personal armor through an acquisition of a small defense materials firm and has approached the category with the modular, user-configurable philosophy that defines its other product lines. The result is a system that experienced operators appreciate for its adaptability and that less experienced users sometimes misconfigure, attaching plates in orientations that create coverage gaps. Ringo's training documentation is thorough but widely ignored.
Properties.aliases: Ringo Plate, The Tessellate, Scatter Shell
Properties.tactical_use: Highly valued by operators who move between different threat environments in a single operation. The reconfiguration speed allows adjustment between engagements — maximum coverage for breaching, reduced profile for movement through confined spaces. The fractal deflection advantage is most pronounced against rifle rounds at oblique angles; it provides less benefit against direct perpendicular impacts at high velocity. Experienced users learn to angle their body positioning to maximize the geometry's deflection probability during engagements.
Properties.cultural_context: The Fractal Deflection Chassis has a reputation as an operator's armor — something for people who understand what they are doing and can use the modularity intelligently. In contrast, it has a secondary reputation as a trap for the inexperienced, who configure it badly and end up with worse coverage than a fixed-plate system would have provided. In Meridian 88's mercenary and freelance security culture, being found dead in a badly configured Fractal Chassis is considered an embarrassing way to go. The angular aesthetic of the fractal plates has also been adopted by certain street fashion movements, leading to civilian replica shells with no protective capacity.
Properties.specifications: weight: 7.2 kg (standard 8-plate configuration); plate_count_range: 4 to 12 plates (standard rail configuration); ballistic_rating: Class IV (standard configuration); Class III (reduced-profile 4-plate); deflection_improvement: Claimed 22% over equivalent flat plate (independently partially verified); plate_reconfiguration_time: Under 2 minutes (full reconfiguration); integrity_indicator_system: Passive chromatic composite degradation display; plate_dimensions: 250mm x 200mm (standard); 150mm x 150mm (reduced); compatible_carriers: Standard MOLLE and Ringo proprietary chassis harness
Properties.story_hooks: A mercenary crew was wiped out in a job that should have been low-risk — forensic analysis of the bodies shows that all of them had their Fractal Chassis plates in an identical non-standard configuration that left their left flanks exposed; someone gave them bad configuration instructions before the job.; Ringo's deflection rate data has been leaked alongside internal documents suggesting the 22% figure was selectively generated; a journalist has the documents and is looking for a technical expert to verify them before publication — Ringo wants the story killed.; A civilian replica shell is circulating in the outer districts that contains a hidden layer of real Ringo composite material — someone is using the fashion market as a distribution channel for unlicensed functional armor.; An operator's Fractal Chassis was recovered at a scene with a unique impact pattern — the fractal geometry recorded the deflection angles of every round it stopped, and a ballistics analyst believes the pattern can be matched to a specific weapon to identify the shooter.

Properties.description:
The Hollow Channel Communicator is a bone-conduction audio device that forgoes all radio transmission in favor of direct physical vibration, transmitting voice communication through contact with any rigid surface — a table, a wall, a vehicle chassis, a railing — that is shared between sender and receiver. Both parties press a small adhesive transducer pad against the same connected physical structure; the sender's voice is converted to vibration, travels through the material, and is reconstructed into audio at the receiver's end. Because the signal never enters the electromagnetic spectrum, it is entirely invisible to radio frequency monitoring, spectrum analysis, and signal intelligence equipment of any kind. There is no transmission to intercept, no frequency to identify, and no encryption to break — because the communication exists only as mechanical vibration within a physical object.

The device's limitations are significant and define its use cases precisely. Both communicating parties must be in contact with the same continuous rigid structure simultaneously, which in practice means the Hollow Channel is used for short-range coordination in confined environments — shared buildings, adjacent rooms, connected vehicles, underground infrastructure. The audio fidelity is acceptable rather than excellent, with some frequency loss through dense or acoustically absorptive materials, and the system cannot carry data, only voice. Ringo Corponation designed the transducer pads to be thin enough to adhere under clothing or inside a jacket lining, making them concealable during covert use.

The Hollow Channel Communicator occupies a niche that other communication tools cannot fill: environments where any electromagnetic emission, however small or encrypted, will trigger automated security responses. High-security corporate vaults, certain government facilities, and the most sensitive private residences in Meridian 88 are swept continuously for RF activity, making conventional comms suicidal for anyone operating covertly inside them. In these environments, the Hollow Channel is not merely useful — it is the only viable option for maintaining contact between team members.
Properties.aliases: Hollow Channel, The Bone Phone, RC-HCC
Properties.tactical_use: In practice, teams using the Hollow Channel Communicator pre-identify shared structural elements in target environments during planning — the steel frame of a building, a shared ventilation duct, a continuous concrete floor — and assign each team member to a contact point along that structure. During operations inside RF-monitored environments, the system allows coordinated action without triggering any electronic countermeasure. The primary operational limitation is that team members must maintain physical contact with the shared surface, which constrains movement. Experienced operators compensate by using the system only for critical coordination moments, maintaining contact briefly to transmit and then moving freely between transmissions. The device is also used for near-silent communication in surveillance scenarios where even whispered speech carries risk.
Properties.cultural_context: The Hollow Channel Communicator is unrestricted in Meridian 88 partly because its use cases are narrow enough that it does not register as a threat to the communications monitoring infrastructure that the city's corporate and municipal authorities depend on. It cannot be used to coordinate large groups across distances, it cannot carry data, and it requires physical proximity to a shared structure. What it can do — allow two or three people in the same building to communicate without any detectable signal — is treated as insufficiently dangerous to regulate. This legal status makes it the only professional-grade covert communication tool that can be openly purchased, which in turn has made it a favorite of corporate security consultants who need to demonstrate to clients that their RF-swept facilities can still support internal coordination.
Properties.specifications: dimensions: Transducer pad: 3.2cm x 2.1cm x 0.3cm; Processing unit: 4.1cm x 2.8cm x 0.9cm; weight: 22g per complete unit (pad + processor); power_source: Integrated micro-cell; 18-hour continuous operation; transmission_medium: Any continuous rigid surface (metal, concrete, glass, composite); effective_range: Up to 60m through steel; 20–35m through reinforced concrete; variable through composites; audio_quality: 70–85% voice clarity depending on surface material and path length; em_emission: Zero detectable electromagnetic output; user_capacity: Up to 6 paired units on a single surface connection
Properties.story_hooks: A building's structural survey reveals that the Hollow Channel has been used to transmit through its frame for months — the transducer pad adhesive residue marks a path that traces a route through the building no authorized personnel should have been taking.; A Ringo Corponation product recall notice goes out for a specific batch of Hollow Channel Communicators, citing 'unintended acoustic resonance behavior' — recipients who investigate discover that the affected units are transmitting a faint secondary signal at a frequency consistent with a surveillance carrier wave.; Two opposing teams inside the same target building independently discover they are both using the Hollow Channel on the same structural element, and can hear each other's transmissions — turning a covert operation into an improvised negotiation.; A murder is committed inside an RF-swept facility with no conventional communications traffic recorded during the relevant window — but forensic analysis of the building's structural steel reveals vibration patterns consistent with Hollow Channel use in the minutes before the victim died.

Properties.description:
The Skinline Codec is Ringo Corponation's answer to the problem of communication in fully jammed or surveilled environments: if radio signals can be intercepted and blocked, transmit through something that isn't radio. The Thread uses the body's own bioelectric field as a carrier medium, encoding encrypted data as micro-variations in the skin-surface electrical potential of a user and transmitting it to another Thread user through direct physical contact — a handshake, a touch on the shoulder, a brush of hands. The contact window required is as brief as 0.3 seconds, enough for a full compressed message packet to transfer completely undetected by any external monitoring system.

The hardware consists of two components: a dermal patch worn on the inside of the wrist or palm, and a thumbnail-sized processing unit that clips to the inside of a sleeve or collar. The patch handles signal encoding and skin-coupling; the processing unit handles encryption, message composition, and the haptic feedback pulse that confirms successful transmission. Messages are composed via subvocal input or a paired micro-interface and delivered to the recipient as text or compressed audio on their own interface. Because the transmission medium is the body itself, no signal leaves the participants — it is, in the most literal sense, a communication that exists only between two people touching.

The Thread emerged from Ringo Corponation's courier and logistics division, originally intended for secure package authentication between bonded couriers who needed to confirm handoff without any electronic record. Its adoption by intelligence operatives and underground networks was immediate and predictable. The device has one significant limitation: it only transmits between two users who both carry active units, meaning it requires prior arrangement and cannot be used to reach anyone outside the immediate physical environment. In practice, this limitation has become a feature — a Thread network is inherently small, trust-based, and geographically bounded.
Properties.aliases: The Thread, Skinline, Ringo Wire, Flesh Carrier
Properties.tactical_use: Thread users pre-load messages or use subvocal input to compose in real time. Transmission occurs on any physical contact between patch-wearing surfaces. In practice, operators develop natural-seeming contact protocols — a greeting handshake, an adjustment of a colleague's collar, a hand on the arm during conversation. The Thread is the only known communication method that remains functional inside a fully active Fallow or equivalent jamming field. Relay chains can be constructed: User A contacts User B, User B contacts User C, allowing message propagation through a room without any single transmission being detectable. The limitation is that all users must be present and the chain must be physically arranged.
Properties.cultural_context: The Thread has developed an almost ritualistic significance among the close-knit cells that use it. In a city saturated with surveillance and signals intelligence, communication that exists only in the moment of physical contact carries genuine intimacy. Some Thread users describe a psychological shift — the knowledge that a conversation truly cannot be intercepted changes how honestly people speak. Among underground networks, a Thread handshake has become a trust ritual that goes beyond its function; you don't give someone your Thread contact unless you're willing to be in the same room with them. The device is also used in a more theatrical context by Meridian 88's high-end social elite, for whom unrecorded conversation at parties has become a status performance.
Properties.specifications: components: Dermal wrist/palm patch + sleeve-clip processing unit; dimensions: Patch: 4cm x 2cm; Processor: 1.8cm x 1.2cm x 0.4cm; weight: Combined 18g; transmission_medium: Skin-surface bioelectric field (no external EM emission); contact_window_required: 0.3 seconds minimum for full packet transfer; message_formats: Compressed text, compressed audio (up to 90 seconds), pre-coded signal bursts; encryption: Per-pair asymmetric key, hardware-bound; network_size: Point-to-point only; relay chains possible through sequential contact; power_source: Body heat thermoelectric, indefinite passive operation; detection_resistance: Absolute during transmission — no EM emission detectable
Properties.story_hooks: A Thread unit has been recovered from a dead operative — its paired unit is still active and worn by someone currently in the city, meaning whoever killed the operative now has an open contact channel to an unknown Thread partner.; The players need to pass a message through a Thread relay chain across a crowded corporate gala without any member of the chain appearing to communicate — requiring them to engineer 'natural' physical contact between seven people over the course of an evening.; Someone is selling Thread pairs pre-keyed to each other on the black market, but the encryption keys were registered to Ringo Corponation's logistics division — meaning the corporation can read every message passed through them.; A Thread chain is the only record of a conversation that took place before a political assassination. Reconstructing what was said requires finding every person in the chain and getting them to admit they were there.

Properties.description:
The Spectral Fold Imager is a compact multi-band imaging device that captures and computationally 'unfolds' overlapping electromagnetic frequency layers to produce a single composite image containing data from visible light, near-infrared, short-wave infrared, and low-frequency microwave bands simultaneously. The device achieves this through a folded optical path — a series of micro-prism cascades that split incoming light into its constituent frequency ranges and direct each band to a dedicated sensor strip, all within a chassis roughly the size of a hardcover book. The resulting composite image, rendered on the device's high-contrast display, shows a scene with extraordinary informational density: concealed objects, heat sources, electronic emissions, and structural anomalies all visible in a single frame coded by color channel.

Ringo Corponation developed the SFI for their media and surveillance divisions, where the need to capture covert footage in varying light conditions without carrying multiple bulky instruments created a clear market gap. The folded optical path design — Ringo's core innovation — allowed dramatic miniaturization compared to conventional multi-spectral rigs without sacrificing image quality. The device can be operated in 'full composite' mode or narrowed to any single frequency band for targeted analysis. A machine-learning interpretation layer flags anomalies automatically: hidden compartments in walls, warm bodies behind barriers, active electronics in supposedly powered-down equipment.

The SFI has become something of a signature instrument for a specific type of Meridian 88 operator: the investigative journalist, the corporate intelligence analyst, the high-end infiltrator who needs to see everything a space is hiding before committing to entry. Ringo markets it through their professional imaging division with conspicuous legitimacy, but the device's surveillance capabilities are extensive enough that several districts have moved to restrict its carry without a media or investigative license.
Properties.aliases: SFI, the Accordion, Fold Eye, Layer Cam
Properties.tactical_use: Operators sweep rooms and corridors before entry to identify warm bodies, concealed weapons, or hidden compartments through walls and barriers. Investigators use the SFI to document hidden infrastructure, concealed evidence, or electronic equipment in locations where visible-light documentation would reveal nothing. Infiltrators use it to map a target building's interior layout by imaging through exterior walls from a safe distance. The ML anomaly flagging allows rapid triage of large spaces — the device highlights what needs closer attention so operators don't miss subtle signatures under pressure.
Properties.cultural_context: The SFI has become culturally associated with a particular archetype in Meridian 88: the person who sees through surfaces, literally and figuratively. Investigative journalists who carry one are both respected and feared — the implication being that nothing you've hidden in your walls or your carefully staged environment is safe from examination. Corporate intelligence runners treat SFI ownership as a baseline professional competency. Among fixers, 'running the accordion' before any new location is considered basic tradecraft hygiene. The licensing requirement for full microwave-band access has created a two-tier market: licensed operators with full capability and unlicensed users with a device that's still powerful but blind to certain frequency ranges.

Properties.description:
The Stacked Lens Courier Drone is a mid-weight autonomous delivery platform built around Ringo Corponation's proprietary multi-aperture optical navigation system — a ring of seven overlapping wide-angle lenses that constructs a continuous 340-degree environmental model updated at 60 frames per second. Unlike conventional drones that rely primarily on LIDAR or GPS, the Stacked Lens uses passive optical triangulation, making it highly resistant to signal jamming and capable of navigating GPS-dark zones such as the Sub-Verge tunnels, shielded corporate campuses, and the electromagnetic noise floors of the Slag Markets. The drone's body is a flattened ovoid roughly the size of a carry case, suspended beneath a contra-rotating six-rotor assembly that minimizes acoustic signature while maintaining lift stability in Meridian 88's variable corridor wind conditions.

The drone's most distinctive feature is its adaptive payload cradle — a reconfigurable internal bay that uses the same tensioned band technology found in Ringo Corponation's logistics packaging line. The cradle reads payload weight and geometry on loading and redistributes its internal tension bands to create a custom-fitted, shock-absorbing housing for whatever is placed inside. This makes the Stacked Lens suitable for fragile, irregular, or sensitive cargo that standard drones would damage in transit. A secondary external hardpoint allows attachment of a standardized cargo module for bulk runs, though this significantly increases acoustic signature and reduces maneuverability.

The Stacked Lens occupies a middle ground in Meridian 88's drone ecosystem: too large and expensive for casual personal use, too commercially available for exclusive corporate deployment. It is the workhorse of independent courier networks, mid-tier logistics contractors, and — with firmware modifications — a favored platform for runners moving sensitive packages through signal-contested terrain.
Properties.aliases: the Stack, Lens Courier, Ringo Flier, Stacker
Properties.tactical_use: In courier and logistics operations, the Stacked Lens is dispatched through pre-mapped optical routes that avoid signal-monitored corridors and ADS interception zones. Its GPS independence makes it reliable in the Sub-Verge and Slag Market districts where competitors' drones fail or are spoofed. For sensitive operations, runners use aftermarket firmware to disable the operator handshake requirement, allowing the drone to operate on a pre-programmed route with no live signal that can be intercepted. The tamper-triggered incineration module is standard for pharmaceutical and data-physical runs.
Properties.cultural_context: The Stacked Lens has become so common in Meridian 88's independent courier ecosystem that its silhouette is essentially ambient — most residents of mid-tier districts no longer look up when one passes. This invisibility is precisely what makes it valuable to runners. There is a specific subculture of drone mechanics in the Verge Corridors who specialize in Stacked Lens modifications: firmware unlocks, acoustic suppression upgrades, and payload bay conversions. A well-modded Stacked Lens is a mark of a serious independent operator. Ringo Corponation is openly aware of the modification subculture and has made no meaningful attempt to suppress it, which some analysts read as deliberate market strategy.

Properties.story_hooks: A Stacked Lens Courier Drone lands on a player character's fire escape and refuses to leave. Its payload bay is locked, its operator handshake is dead, and its last registered flight path originated from a district that was evacuated three days ago.; Someone has been intercepting Stacked Lens drones mid-flight in the Sub-Verge — not stealing the cargo, just accessing the payload bay, replacing the contents with something else, and releasing the drone to complete its delivery. The data is being routed to an undisclosed server. The modification community has noticed.; A courier coordinator is offering triple rates for a single Stacked Lens run through the Null Corridor — a stretch of the Sub-Verge where every previous drone sent in has either failed to return or returned with its payload bay open and empty.

Properties.description: The Tandem Fold Microvan is Ringo Corponation's answer to Meridian 88's chronic spatial scarcity — a compact urban transport vehicle built around a collapsible chassis system that allows the vehicle to compress its width and length by approximately 40% when parked or navigating narrow corridors. The compression mechanism, called the Tandem Fold System, uses a series of interlocking structural ribs and pneumatic sleeve joints to physically reconfigure the vehicle's profile without compromising the passenger or cargo compartment integrity. In its collapsed state, the Microvan occupies roughly the footprint of a large motorcycle.
Properties.aliases: The Ringo Box, Fold Van, Accordion
Properties.tactical_use: The Microvan's ubiquity is its greatest tactical asset — it blends seamlessly into urban traffic and draws no attention from enforcement or corporate security. Operatives use it as a surveillance vehicle, a mobile staging platform, and a getaway vehicle that can squeeze through alley junctions that would stop a conventional car. The cargo configuration has been used to transport everything from medical supplies to bound prisoners. Its collapsible profile also makes it uniquely suited to rooftop transport, stacked parking facilities, and the compressed transit tunnels that connect certain mid-district blocks.
Properties.cultural_context: The Tandem Fold Microvan is the everyman vehicle of Meridian 88 — seen everywhere from corporate campus lots to outer-district street markets. It carries no prestige and considerable practicality, which has made it quietly beloved by working residents and quietly contemptuous to the city's upper tiers. Some outer-district communities have developed a culture of extensively modifying Fold Vans into rolling homes, medical clinics, and workshops, given their spatial flexibility. The vehicle appears in dozens of Vantablack Media productions as shorthand for ordinary, struggling urban life.

Properties.story_hooks: A Ringo Corponation delivery fleet of Fold Vans has been rerouted by a firmware update — every van in the district is now converging on the same address, and nobody at Ringo will admit to pushing the update.; A crew's reliable Microvan has been fitted with a hidden compartment by a previous owner — and that compartment contains something the previous owner clearly died trying to hide.; An outer-district community has converted twelve Fold Vans into a mobile neighborhood — a rolling settlement that uses the vans' collapse function to pack into defensible configurations at night — and someone with real estate interests wants them gone.; A seemingly ordinary Fold Courier delivery van is running a route that doesn't correspond to any registered business — but it makes the same stops, at the same times, every single day.

Properties.description: A compact kit containing tools for replicating and spoofing biometric authentication systems — fingerprint molds, retinal pattern contact lenses, voice modulation software, and gait adjustment insoles. The BSK-2 starts with a target's biometric data (obtained through surveillance, data breach, or physical collection) and produces physical devices that replicate those biometrics well enough to defeat standard commercial scanners. The fingerprint molds use silicone casting from lifted prints, the retinal lenses project a stored pattern over the wearer's own retina, and the voice software processes the user's speech in real-time to match the target's vocal characteristics.
Properties.aliases: BSK-2, ID Faker, Bio Spoof, Sterling Mask Kit
Properties.specifications: fingerprint: Silicone molds from lifted prints; retinal: Pattern-projecting contact lenses; voice: Real-time vocal characteristic modulation; gait: Insoles that alter stride pattern and cadence; preparation time: 2-4 hours per biometric type; effectiveness: Defeats standard commercial scanners; limitations: Does not defeat live tissue verification; weight: 0.5 kg complete kit; shelf life: Fingerprint molds 48 hours; info: retinal lenses 72 hours
Properties.story_hooks: A secured facility was accessed using perfect biometric replicas of an authorized employee — the employee was at home at the time, and the BSK-2 components found at the scene show the biometrics were captured from public surveillance footage.; A BSK-2 has been used to frame a specific individual for multiple crimes — their biometric signatures appear at crime scenes they never visited, and the evidence is convincing enough for arrest warrants.

Properties.description: A wrist-worn device that continuously broadcasts a verified diplomatic immunity credentials signal recognized by law enforcement systems throughout Meridian 88. The DIB-1 contains a quantum-encrypted identity chip that authenticates the wearer's diplomatic status to any scanner or automated system, triggering legal protections that prevent detention, search, or arrest. The bracelet's signal is recognized by autonomous security systems, which stand down when detecting a valid diplomatic credential. Sterling-Nakamura issues them to senior personnel and allied diplomatic staff — the bracelet does not make the wearer invincible, but it makes detaining them a significant legal and political event.
Properties.aliases: DIB-1, Get Out Free, Immunity Band, Sterling Pass
Properties.specifications: broadcast: Continuous diplomatic credential signal; authentication: Quantum-encrypted identity chip; recognition: Compatible with all Meridian 88 law enforcement systems; effect: Triggers diplomatic immunity legal protections; range: 10-meter broadcast radius; battery: 1-year operation; weight: 0.05 kg; tamper detection: Self-wipe on unauthorized removal; form factor: Elegant wrist band; info: corporate branded
Properties.story_hooks: A DIB-1 was used by a murder suspect to walk through a crime scene perimeter — the automated security systems stood down and human officers hesitated to challenge a diplomatic credential, giving the suspect time to escape.; A counterfeit DIB-1 has appeared that broadcasts a valid-seeming diplomatic credential — the forgery is good enough to fool automated systems but will not survive manual verification, creating a narrow window of false immunity.

Properties.description: A briefcase-sized secure container with integrated biometric lock, tamper detection, and thermite self-destruct system. The DSC-5 is designed to transport classified documents, data storage devices, or biological samples with absolute security — any unauthorized opening attempt triggers an internal thermite charge that incinerates the contents at 2,500°C in under 3 seconds. The container's walls are lined with Faraday cage mesh to prevent electromagnetic scanning of contents, and its biometric lock requires fingerprint, voiceprint, and neural interface verification. Sterling-Nakamura issues them to diplomatic staff and high-priority courier services.
Properties.aliases: DSC-5, Kill Box, Sterling Case, Burn Safe
Properties.specifications: biometric lock: Fingerprint + voiceprint + neural interface; tamper detection: Accelerometer + magnetic field + case integrity; self-destruct: Internal thermite charge; info: 2; 500°C in 3 seconds; Faraday shielding: Complete EM isolation of contents; interior volume: 30x20x10 cm; weight: 4.5 kg; exterior: Reinforced carbon-fiber shell; battery: 90-day standby for sensors and lock
Properties.story_hooks: A DSC-5 self-destruct was triggered during a routine customs inspection — the inspector's unauthorized biometric scan activated the tamper detection, incinerating contents that someone very much wanted to know about.; A DSC-5 has been modified to allow remote triggering of the thermite charge — it has been given to a courier as a concealed incendiary device that will destroy whatever room they are in when activated.

Properties.description: A concealed emergency beacon that, when activated, broadcasts an encrypted distress signal containing the user's identity, location, biometric status, and a 10-second audio recording to Sterling-Nakamura's security response network. The ET-5 is designed to be activated covertly — a specific gesture, a pressure pattern, or a neural interface command — without alerting nearby threats. The beacon transmits through multiple redundant channels including satellite, cellular, and mesh network, ensuring the signal gets out even in jammed environments. Sterling-Nakamura guarantees a response within 15 minutes in covered areas.
Properties.aliases: ET-5, Panic Button, SOS Beacon, Sterling Alarm
Properties.specifications: activation: Gesture; info: pressure pattern; or neural command; pendant; or subdermal implant; transmission: Satellite + cellular + mesh network redundancy; data: Identity + location + biometrics + 10-sec audio; encryption: Quantum-key rolling; response time: 15 minutes guaranteed in coverage; weight: 0.02 kg; concealment: Ring; battery: 2-year standby
Properties.story_hooks: An ET-5 activated inside a sealed underground chamber where no signal should have escaped — the beacon's mesh network redundancy found a path through building wiring, and the response team arrived within 20 minutes.; An ET-5 signal was received from a user who was confirmed dead 6 hours prior — either the beacon malfunctioned, or someone is wearing a dead person's emergency transponder.

Properties.description: A handheld document scanner that photographs, OCRs, encrypts, and securely transmits paper documents to a designated secure server in a single operation. The EDS-3 is designed for intelligence gathering — an operator can scan a desk full of documents in under a minute, with each page automatically encrypted before leaving the device's memory. The scanner also detects and flags documents with embedded security features — watermarks, UV-reactive inks, tracking fibers — that could identify the source of a leak. Sterling-Nakamura's legal and intelligence teams use it for everything from corporate espionage to due diligence.
Properties.aliases: EDS-3, Secure Scan, Sterling Reader, Doc Eye
Properties.specifications: scan speed: 1 page per 2 seconds; resolution: 600 DPI with OCR; encryption: 256-bit AES on device; transmission: Burst encrypted to designated server; security detection: Watermark; info: UV ink; tracking fiber identification; 000 pages internal encrypted; storage: 10; weight: 0.15 kg; battery: 4 hours continuous scanning
Properties.story_hooks: An EDS-3 captured in a corporate raid contained scans of 4,000 pages of classified documents — the metadata shows they were scanned over six months from a single office, identifying the leak source.; A modified EDS-3 has been developed that replaces scanned documents with altered versions — the operator scans the original, the device prints a modified copy, and the switch is made in the same operation.

Properties.description: A compact medical kit designed for corporate executive protection details, containing automated diagnostic tools, rapid wound closure compounds, hemorrhage control agents, and three doses of broad-spectrum antitoxin. The EMK-3's centerpiece is its diagnostic scanner — a handheld device that performs a 30-second full-body assessment including blood chemistry, toxicology, and internal injury detection using ultrasound and bioimpedance sensing. The kit includes Lazarus Pharmaceuticals' Rapid Wound Closure Nanite injectors, military-grade hemostatic foam, and a neural interface crash kit for stabilizing augmentation failures.
Properties.aliases: EMK-3, Gold Kit, Sterling Med, Boardroom Medic
Properties.legality: Licensed — medical professionals and authorized security
Properties.specifications: diagnostic scanner: 30-second full body assessment; wound closure: 3x RWCNS nanite injectors; hemorrhage control: 4x hemostatic foam canisters; antitoxin: 3x broad-spectrum doses; neural crash kit: Interface stabilizer + emergency shutdown module; weight: 2.1 kg; form factor: Rigid case; info: 25x15x8 cm; shelf life: 18 months before compound degradation
Properties.story_hooks: An EMK-3's diagnostic scanner has been modified to transmit the results of every scan to a third party — someone has been collecting medical data on every executive the kit has treated.; A counterfeit EMK-3 has surfaced with expired nanite injectors and diluted antitoxin — the counterfeits are packaged identically to genuine kits and have been distributed through legitimate supply chains.

Properties.description: A credit-card-sized device that projects a small holographic display containing the owner's identity information, professional credentials, and an encrypted contact protocol. The HBC-1 is Sterling-Nakamura's standard-issue networking tool for corporate personnel — when two HBC-1 cards are brought within 5 cm of each other, they exchange encrypted identity packets and establish a secure communication channel between the owners' Diaspora profiles. The holographic display can be customized with corporate branding, animated logos, and interactive elements. What makes the HBC-1 notable in security circles is that its exchange protocol has been exploited to deliver malware payloads — a handshake with a modified HBC-1 can inject code directly into the recipient's Diaspora profile.
Properties.aliases: HBC-1, Holo Card, Smart Card, Sterling Card
Properties.specifications: display: Holographic projection; info: 5x3 cm; data exchange: Encrypted NFC at 5 cm range; communication channel: Establishes secure Diaspora link; data capacity: Identity packet + credential verification; battery: 6-month standby; weight: 0.01 kg; form factor: Standard credit card dimensions; customization: Corporate branding and animated elements
Properties.story_hooks: A weaponized HBC-1 was used to deliver a Diaspora profile exploit during a networking event — every person who exchanged cards with the attacker had their secure communications compromised.; A collection of HBC-1 cards found at a crime scene contains encrypted data packets that, when assembled in sequence, form a complete intelligence dossier on a corporate target.

Properties.description: A pendant-worn device that verifies the identity of anyone within 2 meters by cross-referencing their biometric emissions — facial geometry, body heat pattern, gait rhythm, and neural interface signature — against Sterling-Nakamura's identity database. The IVP-2 provides a subtle haptic notification to the wearer indicating whether a person's claimed identity matches their biometric profile. The device is designed for executives and diplomats who need to verify that the person they are meeting is who they claim to be, particularly in environments where ADM-1 disguise systems or Digital Twin impersonation might be in play.
Properties.aliases: IVP-2, Truth Stone, ID Pendant, Sterling Verifier
Properties.specifications: verification method: Multi-biometric cross-reference; biometrics: Facial geometry; info: heat pattern; gait; neural interface signature; database: Sterling-Nakamura identity network; notification: Haptic vibration — confirmed or anomaly; range: 2-meter detection radius; verification time: 3 seconds; weight: 0.03 kg; battery: 30-day standby; form factor: Pendant or lapel pin
Properties.story_hooks: An IVP-2 flagged a meeting participant as an identity anomaly — their biometrics did not match any profile in the database, meaning they are either unregistered or using an identity that does not correspond to any real person.; A sophisticated adversary has learned to spoof IVP-2 verification by replicating all four biometric channels simultaneously — the device confirms an identity that is entirely fabricated.

Nodes.Name: Sterling-Nakamura Legal Evidence Preservation Kit LEPK-2

Properties.description: A forensic evidence collection and preservation kit designed to maintain an unbroken chain of custody from crime scene to courtroom. The LEPK-2 includes tamper-evident collection bags with embedded blockchain verification chips, a portable evidence scanner that photographs and catalogs items with cryptographic timestamps, sterile collection tools, and a sealed transport case with environmental monitoring. Every action taken with the kit is logged to Sterling-Nakamura's Blockchain Governance Protocol, creating an immutable record that cannot be challenged in court.
Properties.aliases: LEPK-2, Evidence Box, Sterling Preserve, Chain Kit
Properties.legality: Licensed — law enforcement and legal professionals
Properties.specifications: collection bags: 50x tamper-evident with blockchain chips; scanner: Photograph + catalog + cryptographic timestamp; tools: Sterile tweezers; info: swabs; scrapers; measurement; transport: Sealed case with environmental monitoring; chain of custody: Immutable blockchain logging; weight: 4 kg complete kit; verification: Any BGP node can verify evidence integrity
Properties.story_hooks: An LEPK-2's blockchain log revealed that evidence was accessed outside the documented chain of custody — someone with physical access tampered with the evidence and the kit recorded it.; A defense attorney has challenged the LEPK-2 system itself, arguing that blockchain-verified evidence creates an illusion of infallibility that prejudices juries against legitimate challenges.

Properties.description: A compact rebreather mask that filters atmospheric contaminants, toxins, biological agents, and particulates while remaining small enough to be worn inconspicuously in urban environments. The PAF-4 covers nose and mouth with a low-profile mesh filter that uses activated charcoal, HEPA filtration, and a catalytic conversion layer that neutralizes chemical agents. The mask is powered by a micro-fan that maintains positive pressure inside the filter zone, preventing unfiltered air from entering through seal gaps. Sterling-Nakamura issues them to personnel operating in Meridian 88's contaminated lower-tier districts.
Properties.aliases: PAF-4, Clean Breather, Air Mask, Sterling Filter
Properties.specifications: filtration: HEPA + activated charcoal + catalytic conversion; protection: Particulates; info: chemical agents; biological aerosols; positive pressure: Micro-fan maintained; battery life: 48 hours continuous; weight: 0.12 kg; form factor: Low-profile nose/mouth mask; filter life: 200 hours before replacement; replacement filters: Φ40 each
Properties.story_hooks: PAF-4 masks have been distributed free in a Tier 1 district as a humanitarian gesture — but the masks contain a micro-transmitter that tracks the wearer's breathing patterns and location.; A contamination event has overwhelmed PAF-4 filter capacity — the masks are providing false confidence while slowly allowing toxins through, and wearers think they are safe when they are not.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Black Widow' Electronic Bait Device

Properties.description: A small device that mimics the signal profile of a high-value electronic target — an unprotected neural interface, an open Diaspora node, or an unsecured corporate data terminal — to lure hackers and cyber-intruders into connecting. When a hostile operator attempts to access the fake target, the Black Widow counter-attacks through the connection, deploying malware, extracting the attacker's location and identity, or injecting a tracking payload into their neural interface. The device is essentially a digital booby trap, punishing anyone who attempts unauthorized access to what appears to be an easy target.
Properties.aliases: Black Widow, Bait Box, Trap Node, Honey Pot
Properties.legality: Legal gray area — defensive countermeasure vs. offensive cyberweapon
Properties.specifications: mimicry: Neural interface; info: Diaspora node; or data terminal signatures; identity extraction; tracking payload; concealable; counter-attack: Malware deployment; trigger: Unauthorized access attempt; response time: Sub-second counter-attack on connection; weight: 0.1 kg; form factor: Small box; battery: 30-day standby; programmable: Multiple trap profiles and response types
Properties.story_hooks: A Black Widow device deployed near a corporate facility caught a hacker — the counter-attack extracted their neural interface identity, revealing them as an employee of a rival corporation conducting espionage.; A network of Black Widow devices has been deployed across a district, creating a minefield for cyber-operators — anyone who scans for targets in the area risks tripping a trap that exposes their identity and location.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Coffin Nail' Lock Bypass Kit

Properties.description: A lockpicking and access bypass toolkit assembled from commercially available and custom-fabricated components, contained in a leather roll the size of a pencil case. The kit includes traditional mechanical picks and tension wrenches for pin tumbler locks, an electronic bypass module for keycard systems, a RFID cloner for proximity access, and a compact decoder for electronic combination locks. The electronic components are built on open-source hardware platforms available from any electronics supplier, and the mechanical picks are ground from spring steel by hand. The Coffin Nail is the most common professional lockpicking kit in the lower tiers, and its presence at a scene is considered strong evidence of premeditated unauthorized entry.
Properties.aliases: Coffin Nail, Pick Set, Skeleton Key, Door Opener
Properties.legality: Legal to own in most jurisdictions — illegal to use for unauthorized entry
Properties.specifications: mechanical picks: 15-piece spring steel set; tension wrenches: 6 varieties; electronic bypass: Keycard system override module; RFID cloner: Copies and replays proximity cards within 5 cm; decoder: Electronic combination lock analysis; weight: 0.3 kg; form factor: Leather roll; info: pencil case sized; learning curve: Basic mechanical picking requires 20+ hours practice
Properties.story_hooks: A locked room mystery — the door was locked from the inside with no sign of picking, but a Coffin Nail kit was found in the room with the victim, suggesting the killer locked themselves in with the target.; A master lockpick who manufactures custom Coffin Nail kits has been selling kits with a hidden tracking device in the leather roll — every kit they sell tells them exactly where unauthorized entries are happening.

Properties.description: A lightweight vehicle cobbled from salvaged motorcycle frames, electric motors from industrial equipment, and battery packs pulled from decommissioned drones. The Coyote is the standard transportation of Tier 1 operators — fast enough to outrun foot patrols, small enough to fit through alleys and maintenance corridors, and built from parts that are available anywhere and traceable nowhere. Each Coyote is unique, reflecting its builder's available materials and priorities. Common configurations include three-wheeled trikes, two-wheeled electric motorcycles, and four-wheeled micro-cars barely larger than a go-kart. Performance varies wildly, but the culture surrounding Coyote builds has become a significant element of lower-tier identity.
Properties.aliases: Coyote, Junk Runner, Scrap Ride, Tier One Wheels
Properties.specifications: top speed: 40-80 km/h depending on build; range: 20-60 km per charge; motor: Salvaged industrial electric; battery: Repurposed drone or vehicle packs; weight: 50-150 kg; configuration: 2-4 wheels; info: builder's choice; construction time: 2-5 days with available parts; reliability: Variable — breakdowns common
Properties.story_hooks: A Coyote racing circuit has emerged that draws spectators from multiple tiers — the races are dangerous, the vehicles are held together with hope and wire, and the prize money comes from corporate gambling syndicates.; A fleet of Coyotes has been standardized and distributed to a Tier 1 courier network — the vehicles are too fast for foot pursuit and too small for vehicle pursuit, creating an untouchable delivery system.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Faraday Blanket' EM Shielding Wrap

Properties.description: A large sheet of conductive fabric that blocks all electromagnetic signals passing through it — wrapping a device, person, or space in the Faraday Blanket creates a complete EM blackout within. The blanket is constructed from copper-nickel mesh woven into a durable fabric backing, flexible enough to wrap around irregular shapes and large enough (2m x 3m) to create a small shielded enclosure. Street operators use it to shield devices from remote tracking, prevent neural interface hacking during sleep, block kill switches in stolen equipment, and create improvised private spaces in surveillance-heavy environments.
Properties.aliases: Faraday Blanket, Dead Wrap, Signal Kill, Ghost Sheet
Properties.specifications: shielding: 80 dB attenuation across 100 kHz to 40 GHz; material: Copper-nickel mesh in fabric backing; size: 2m x 3m; weight: 1.5 kg; blocking capability: All commercial wireless; info: cellular; RFID; GPS; Bluetooth; personal sleeping bag; room partition; 200+ wash cycles before degradation; use cases: Device shielding; durability: Machine washable
Properties.story_hooks: A missing person was found alive, wrapped in a Faraday Blanket in an abandoned building — they had been shielded from all tracking for six days while their neural interface's emergency beacon was blocked.; Faraday Blankets are being used to create EM-dead zones in Tier 1 markets where stolen goods with tracking devices can be safely stripped and resold — the blankets turn crime into an invisible activity.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Iron Curtain' Improvised Ballistic Shield

Properties.description: A ballistic shield fabricated from vehicle door panels, steel plate salvage, or layered industrial materials mounted on improvised handles. The Iron Curtain provides mobile cover against handgun-caliber threats and fragmentary projectiles at a fraction of the cost of commercial ballistic shields. The most common pattern uses an automobile door panel — already designed to absorb impact energy — with welded handle brackets and a viewport cut at eye level. Quality and protection vary enormously, but the cheapest Iron Curtain still beats no cover at all.
Properties.aliases: Iron Curtain, Scrap Shield, Door Shield, Riot Board
Properties.specifications: protection: NIJ Level II to IIIA depending on materials; materials: Vehicle door panels; info: steel plate; layered industrial composites; weight: 8-20 kg depending on construction; coverage: Torso and head from frontal threats; mobility: Reduced — requires one arm to carry; viewport: Cut opening or transparent panel insert; cost: Φ20-100 in salvage materials; construction: 2-4 hours with basic tools
