Properties.story_hooks: A community defense group equipped with Iron Curtain shields held a checkpoint against an armed incursion for 6 hours — the shields stopped dozens of rounds and the footage has become a symbol of lower-tier resilience.; A variant Iron Curtain using layered ceramic tile has tested at NIJ Level IV equivalent — the design has been shared across Tier 1 fabrication networks and is being mass-produced from construction waste.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Last Meal' Emergency Ration Fabricator

Properties.description: A compact device that converts organic waste material — food scraps, plant matter, even paper — into edible nutrient bars through a process of sterilization, chemical breakdown, and reconstitution with added vitamins and binding agents. The Last Meal produces food that is nutritionally complete, bacterially safe, and texturally consistent regardless of input material. It does not taste good — operators describe the output as 'edible cardboard with a chemical aftertaste' — but it sustains life indefinitely from materials that would otherwise be garbage. The device has become essential equipment in Tier 1 where food security is not guaranteed.
Properties.aliases: Last Meal, Food Maker, Ration Box, Survival Kitchen
Properties.specifications: input: Any organic material — food waste; info: plant matter; paper; approximately 400 calories per 100g input; kills all pathogens; output: Nutrient bars; processing time: 20 minutes per batch; nutritional completeness: Full with added vitamin supplement; sterilization: UV + thermal; weight: 1.5 kg; battery: 20 batches per charge; taste: Functionally terrible
Properties.story_hooks: Last Meal fabricators have been distributed free in a Tier 1 district by an anonymous benefactor — the devices work perfectly, but the vitamin supplement capsules contain a tracking compound.; A modified Last Meal has been developed that produces nutrient bars with psychoactive compounds — the food itself is being used as a drug delivery mechanism in communities where people eat whatever is available.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Lighthouse' Improvised Area Illumination Flare

Properties.description: A high-intensity chemical flare modified for area illumination rather than signaling — the Lighthouse produces 50,000 candela of white light for 5 minutes, illuminating a 100-meter radius bright enough to defeat low-light advantage. The flare is launched vertically by a hand-held tube launcher and descends slowly under a small parachute, bathing the area in light that negates night-vision equipment, thermal imaging (by raising ambient thermal signature), and the darkness that night operators depend on. It is the poor person's answer to tactical darkness advantage.
Properties.aliases: Lighthouse, Area Flare, Light Bomb, Street Sun
Properties.specifications: luminosity: 50; info: 000 candela; 100-meter altitude; reduces contrast; duration: 5 minutes; illumination radius: 100 meters; launch: Hand-held tube; descent: Parachute retarded; effect on NV: Overwhelms night vision systems; effect on thermal: Raises ambient thermal; weight: 0.4 kg per flare; cost: Φ10-25
Properties.story_hooks: A night assault was defeated when defenders launched a dozen Lighthouse flares simultaneously — the attackers' night vision and thermal advantage was neutralized instantly, and they were exposed in bright white light to defenders behind cover.; Lighthouse flares have been modified with chemical additives that produce colored light — Tier 1 communities use them as emergency signals visible across districts.

Properties.description: A body-worn harness system designed to conceal multiple weapons, tools, and equipment under standard clothing. The Packrat uses a modular design of pouches, holsters, and clips arranged across the torso, inner thighs, and small of back to distribute weight evenly and minimize visible printing through fabric. A well-fitted Packrat can conceal a pistol, three magazines, a knife, a cyberdeck, a medical kit, and assorted tools without creating visible bulges or asymmetric weight distribution. The harness is custom-fitted to the wearer's body and adjustable for different clothing styles. It has become the standard concealment system for anyone who needs to carry lethal capability through areas where weapons are not welcome.
Properties.aliases: Packrat, Carry Rig, Hidden Holster, Stash Harness
Properties.legality: Legal — concealment harness; illegal if containing prohibited items
Properties.specifications: capacity: Pistol + 3 magazines + knife + cyberdeck + med kit + tools; weight distribution: Even across torso and thighs; printing: Minimal under standard clothing; customization: Body-fitted; info: adjustable modular pouches; material: Nylon webbing with neoprene backing; weight: 0.5 kg empty; accessibility: Draw times under 1.5 seconds for primary weapon; comfort: Designed for 12+ hour continuous wear
Properties.story_hooks: A security checkpoint missed a complete weapons loadout on a suspect who was wearing a custom Packrat — the harness was specifically designed to distribute metal mass below the detection threshold of the checkpoint's scanners.; A Packrat design has been developed with integrated Faraday pouches that shield contained devices from tracking — anything stored in the harness disappears from electronic detection.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Panic Room' Deployable Safe Space

Properties.description: A kit for rapidly converting a standard room into a defensible safe space — including door reinforcement bars, window blocking panels, a white noise generator for acoustic privacy, a Faraday mesh curtain for electronic isolation, and emergency supplies for 48 hours. The Panic Room kit allows anyone to turn a bedroom, office, or closet into a temporary refuge that resists forced entry, blocks surveillance, and sustains the occupant through a crisis. The kit has become standard household equipment in Tier 1 and 2 where personal security is not guaranteed by any authority.
Properties.aliases: Panic Room, Safe Box, Hideout Kit, Bunker Bag
Properties.specifications: door reinforcement: Steel bars; info: resists 500 kg force; standard sizes; 3-meter radius; full room coverage; water; first aid; window panels: Ballistic-resistant polymer; acoustic privacy: White noise generator; electronic isolation: Faraday mesh curtain; supplies: 48-hour food; setup time: 10 minutes for full deployment; weight: 12 kg complete kit; form factor: Duffel bag
Properties.story_hooks: A family in Tier 1 survived a 36-hour siege inside a Panic Room deployment — the door reinforcement held against repeated breaching attempts, and the Faraday mesh prevented the attackers from tracking the family's devices.; Panic Room kits are being sold with a hidden tracking device that reports the deployment location — someone is building a map of every safe room in the lower tiers, which is also a map of people who feel unsafe.

Properties.description: A realistic-looking wallet or purse loaded with expired credit chits, fake identity cards, and a concealed GPS tracker that activates when the wallet is opened. The Paper Tiger is designed to be surrendered during a mugging or pickpocket event, satisfying the attacker's demand while providing nothing of value and tracking the thief's subsequent movements. Some variants include a dye pack that stains the thief's hands, a chemical irritant capsule, or a micro-flashbang that detonates 30 seconds after opening. The device has become common enough that experienced street criminals in Meridian 88 now check wallets for trackers before fleeing.
Properties.aliases: Paper Tiger, Fake Wallet, Mugger's Friend, Decoy Purse
Properties.specifications: contents: Expired credit chits; info: fake IDs; GPS tracker; 72-hour battery; chemical irritant; micro-flashbang; tracker activation: On wallet opening; tracker range: City-wide GPS; optional payloads: Dye pack; weight: 0.15 kg; appearance: Indistinguishable from genuine wallet; battery: 6-month standby; tracker transmission: Encrypted to owner's linked device
Properties.story_hooks: A Paper Tiger tracker led its owner to the location of a organized fencing operation — the wallet was stolen as bait to map the criminal network's physical infrastructure.; A Paper Tiger variant has been weaponized with a shaped explosive instead of a dye pack — several muggers have been killed by wallets that detonate when opened.

Properties.description: A compact toolkit containing a plasma cutting wand, pry bars, lock manipulation tools, and hinge pin extractors — everything needed to gain unauthorized entry through walls, doors, floors, or ceilings. The centerpiece is a miniaturized plasma cutter powered by a belt-mounted battery that can cut through standard construction materials including drywall, wood, light steel, and concrete block. The complete kit fits in a messenger bag and allows a single operator to create a human-sized opening through a standard interior wall in under 3 minutes. The kit has become standard equipment for urban exploration, burglary, and tactical entry operations across the lower tiers.
Properties.aliases: Rathole, Cut Kit, Wall Opener, Entry Tools
Properties.legality: Legal as tools — illegal as burglary kit depending on context
Properties.specifications: plasma cutter: Miniaturized; info: cuts construction steel up to 5mm; 15 minutes cutting time; 3 sizes; battery: Belt-mounted; pry bars: Titanium; lock tools: Manipulation picks + bypass tools; hinge extractors: Universal pin removal; cutting speed: Human-sized wall opening in 3 minutes; total weight: 3.2 kg complete kit; form factor: Messenger bag carrier
Properties.story_hooks: A series of burglaries show identical Rathole entry patterns — the same tool kit, the same cutting technique, and the same operator based on the plasma arc characteristics.; A Rathole kit has been modified with a silent plasma cutter that operates below 30 dB — entry can be made through a wall while people on the other side of the room do not hear it.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Rooftop Express' Zipline Deployment Kit

Properties.description: A portable zipline system consisting of a high-strength cable, pneumatic anchor launcher, and friction-brake trolley that enables rapid transit between buildings across open gaps. The kit fires a cable anchor to a target point up to 100 meters away, tensions the cable with an integrated winch, and provides a trolley handle with variable-friction brake for speed control during the crossing. The system is designed for one-way transit — ascending ziplines are possible but require motorized trolleys that add weight and complexity. Street operators use it for rapid building-to-building movement, escape routes, and tactical repositioning in urban environments.
Properties.aliases: Rooftop Express, Zip Kit, Line Runner, Sky Bridge
Properties.legality: Legal as equipment — illegal when used for unauthorized building access
Properties.specifications: cable length: 100 meters high-strength braided steel; anchor launch: Pneumatic; info: accurate to 1-meter at 50 meters; anchor is expendable; cable strength: 500 kg rated; trolley: Friction-brake speed control; maximum load: 120 kg rider + equipment; setup time: 90 seconds from anchor launch to crossing; weight: 3.5 kg total kit; reusability: Cable and trolley reusable
Properties.story_hooks: A series of Tier 2 rooftop burglaries are connected by zipline anchor marks on building parapets — someone is running a route across the skyline, hitting targets along a planned path.; An emergency evacuation from a burning building was facilitated by a Rooftop Express kit — the operator ziplined 40 people to an adjacent building before fire services arrived.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Sewer Rat' Underground Navigation Kit

Properties.description: A kit for navigating Meridian 88's extensive underground infrastructure — storm drains, maintenance tunnels, abandoned transit lines, and DEAES tunnel networks. The kit includes a chemical light supply, waterproof map case with hand-copied tunnel charts, a gas detection badge that changes color in dangerous atmospheres, a compact rebreather for short exposures, and a sonic locator that maps tunnel geometry by echolocation. The Sewer Rat kit is the standard equipment of underground couriers, smugglers, and the growing population that lives beneath the city.
Properties.aliases: Sewer Rat, Tunnel Kit, Underground Guide, Dark Runner
Properties.specifications: chemical lights: 20x 8-hour sticks; map case: Waterproof with hand-copied tunnel charts; gas detection: Color-change badge for 6 common hazards; rebreather: 30 minutes of filtered air; sonic locator: 20-meter tunnel geometry mapping; weight: 2.5 kg total kit; form factor: Waterproof shoulder bag; water resistance: Full submersion rated
Properties.story_hooks: A Sewer Rat tunnel chart has been found that maps passages no official survey has documented — including one that passes directly beneath a high-security corporate vault.; Underground couriers using Sewer Rat kits have established a delivery network that is faster than surface transit for short distances — packages move through the tunnel system with no surveillance coverage.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Smoke Box' Improvised Concealment Generator

Properties.description: A repurposed theatrical fog machine loaded with an opaque chemical smoke compound that produces a dense white cloud obscuring a 15-meter area within 10 seconds. The Smoke Box is built from salvaged fog machines, modified vaporizer heating elements, or even pressurized cooking oil containers — any device that can rapidly aerosolize a liquid. The smoke compound is typically a mixture of glycol fog fluid and titanium dioxide powder that creates a cloud impenetrable to visible light and degraded for thermal imaging. Street operators use it for escape, ambush concealment, and preventing visual identification during operations.
Properties.aliases: Smoke Box, Fog Can, Blind Maker, Cloud Kit
Properties.specifications: coverage: 15-meter radius dense smoke in 10 seconds; persistence: 3-5 minutes in still air; info: less with wind; visibility reduction: Near-zero at 2 meters; thermal attenuation: approximately 40%; smoke compound: Glycol + titanium dioxide mixture; weight: 1-3 kg depending on build; capacity: 2-4 deployments per tank; operator visibility: Also zero — operator is equally blinded
Properties.story_hooks: A coordinated robbery used six Smoke Boxes simultaneously to blind an entire city block — the smoke coverage was so complete that surveillance footage shows nothing for four minutes across 20 cameras.; A modified Smoke Box has been developed that produces smoke with an embedded irritant — not enough to incapacitate, but enough to make anyone without eye protection unable to keep their eyes open.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Spider Hole' Concealed Position Kit

Properties.description: A kit for creating a concealed observation or ambush position in urban environments — a camouflaged cover that blends with surrounding debris, trash, or construction materials, concealing a person at ground level. The kit includes a collapsible frame covered in adaptable fabric that can be dressed with local materials to match any urban surface — garbage, rubble, dirt, or construction waste. An operator inside a properly prepared Spider Hole is virtually invisible from any angle, and can observe or engage from a position that no one knows exists. The kit has a long history in Tier 1 warfare.
Properties.aliases: Spider Hole, Hide Kit, Ground Blind, Burrow
Properties.specifications: frame: Collapsible aluminum; info: person-sized; optional periscope; cover: Adaptable fabric for local material dressing; setup time: 15-30 minutes for full concealment; observation: Viewing slits; size: 2m x 1m x 0.5m occupied; weight: 2 kg frame and fabric; camouflage: Matches any urban surface with local materials; occupation time: Limited by operator endurance — typically 8-12 hours
Properties.story_hooks: A sniper operated from a Spider Hole in a trash heap for three days, waiting for a specific target — the position was never detected and was only found after the shooting when investigators followed the bullet trajectory backward.; A community defense network has established Spider Hole positions throughout a Tier 1 neighborhood, creating an invisible network of observers that monitors all movement through the area.

Nodes.Name: Street Custom 'Trash Armor' Improvised Body Protection

Properties.description: Body armor improvised from whatever materials are available — layers of duct tape and phone books over vital areas, road sign metal cut into chest plates, layers of ceramic tile taped together, or vehicle floor mats worn as vests. Trash Armor is the protective equipment of people who cannot afford real armor, and its effectiveness varies from surprisingly adequate (layered ceramics can stop handgun rounds) to dangerously inadequate (duct tape and cardboard). The cultural significance of Trash Armor in Tier 1 is that wearing it acknowledges a specific reality: your life is dangerous enough to need armor, and you are poor enough that this is the best you can do.
Properties.aliases: Trash Armor, Garbage Plate, Scrap Vest, Junk Shield
Properties.specifications: protection: Variable — ranges from NIJ Level I to nothing useful; common materials: Ceramic tile; info: road signs; phone books; floor mats; weight: 2-8 kg depending on materials; coverage: Typically front torso only; comfort: Minimal; mobility restriction: Significant with heavier builds; cost: Φ0-20 in salvage materials; construction time: 1-3 hours
Properties.story_hooks: A Tier 1 resident survived a shooting because their Trash Armor — six layers of ceramic floor tile — stopped a handgun round. The incident has become a viral moment that highlights the absurd ingenuity of survival in the lower tiers.; A Trash Armor design using a specific combination of layered materials has been tested and found to outperform some commercial body armor at 1/100th the cost — the design is spreading and corporate armor manufacturers are not happy.

Nodes.Name: Tessera Corponation Acoustic Null Field Emitter

Properties.description:
The Acoustic Null Field Emitter is a palm-sized device that projects a directional anti-phase sound field, effectively creating a cone of acoustic cancellation extending up to four meters from the emitter's face. Tessera Corponation's approach differs from conventional white-noise maskers by targeting the precise frequency signatures of the user's movement and speech in real time — an onboard microphone array samples incoming sound at sub-millisecond latency, generates inverted waveforms, and emits them through a phased array of micro-transducers, canceling the user's acoustic output before it propagates beyond the null cone's boundary.

The device's most technically notable characteristic is its adaptive notch filtering, which allows it to suppress the user's sounds while leaving environmental noise largely intact within the cone — meaning the user can still hear their surroundings clearly while remaining acoustically invisible to listeners outside the field. This bidirectional selectivity is computationally intensive and is the primary driver of the unit's relatively short active window on a single charge. At maximum range and fidelity, the emitter sustains approximately ninety minutes of continuous operation before requiring a recharge or cell swap.

Tessera developed the Emitter originally for use by their Lattice network installation crews, who frequently work in acoustically monitored corporate infrastructure. The device moved rapidly into the broader market when early production units were acquired by several high-profile extraction teams and demonstrated in field conditions. Tessera's official position is that the product is sold for 'sensitive facility maintenance applications,' a description that has satisfied regulators in three of Meridian 88's six administrative sectors.
Properties.aliases: The Silencer Box, Null Cone, Tessera Hush
Properties.tactical_use: Clipped to a harness or held in the lead hand during movement through acoustically monitored spaces. Most effective for small teams of one to three operators moving in close formation within the null cone's arc. Larger teams require multiple units with overlapping coverage. Whisper mode is commonly used during static observation phases to extend battery life. The device does not suppress sound produced outside the user's immediate body — closing a door or dropping equipment will still register on external sensors.
Properties.cultural_context: The Acoustic Null Field Emitter has a reputation in Meridian 88's infiltration community as a 'professional's tool' — compact, effective, and expensive enough to filter out amateurs. Its association with Tessera Corponation's infrastructure crews has given it a degree of plausible deniability that operatives prize. In corporate security briefings, the device is increasingly listed as a primary threat multiplier for intrusion scenarios, and several firms have begun deploying redundant vibration-sensor networks specifically to counter its effectiveness on hard flooring.
Properties.specifications: null_cone_range: 4 meters (maximum), 2.5 meters (optimal fidelity); null_cone_arc: 60-degree forward arc; frequency_range_suppressed: 20 Hz – 18 kHz; suppression_effectiveness: ~94% for speech, ~87% for movement noise (hard surfaces); battery_life: 90 minutes (max range/fidelity), 3.5 hours (reduced 2m range); recharge_time: 1.2 hours; dimensions: 9.4 cm × 4.1 cm × 2.8 cm; weight: 0.19 kg; operating_modes: Active null (full suppression), Whisper mode (speech only, extended battery), Passive monitor (no emission, audio logging only)
Properties.story_hooks: An Acoustic Null Field Emitter is found at the scene of a high-security assassination — the device was left behind deliberately, suggesting either a setup or a panicked exit. Its serial number traces to a Tessera corporate procurement order that officially doesn't exist.; A player's contact needs to pass a message in a room known to be acoustically monitored. They need a Null Emitter, but every unit in the district has been bought up in the last 48 hours by someone preparing for a major operation.; Tessera quietly pushes a firmware update that adds a telemetry ping to all registered Emitters — a whistleblower inside the company warns operatives that their operational movements may now be logged.; A new vibration-sensor countermeasure has been installed in a target facility specifically designed to detect the micro-transducer harmonic signature of the Tessera Emitter, turning the device into a liability rather than an asset.

Nodes.Name: Investigative journalists operating in surveilled zones
Corporate counter-intelligence teams (reversed — used to detect users)
The Stillwater Group (a known freelance operations collective in Meridian 88)
Tessera Corponation Ambient Signal Displacement Array

Properties.description:
The Ambient Signal Displacement Array is a palm-sized device worn on the body or placed as a static field emitter that generates a calibrated bubble of electromagnetic interference designed not to block signals — which would itself be detectable — but to displace and scatter them in ways that mimic natural environmental noise. Where crude jammers create a dead zone that passive monitoring systems immediately flag as an anomaly, the Array samples the ambient signal environment within its operational radius and synthesizes a layered output of false signals, reflections, and interference patterns that make the area appear, to any external monitoring system, as a region of ordinary urban electromagnetic clutter.

Tessera developed the Array's core displacement architecture from research into urban signal mapping — specifically, the problem of predicting how dense city infrastructure affects wireless propagation. The same models that predict signal behavior can be run in reverse to generate convincing synthetic scatter. The Array updates its output profile every 200 milliseconds, adapting to changes in the ambient signal environment to maintain the illusion of naturalness. This makes it effective not only against real-time monitoring but against retrospective signal forensics, since the Array's emissions blend into baseline environmental noise in recorded data.

The device has a secondary function that its documentation quietly omits: at close range, it disrupts the short-range biometric handshake protocols that many corporate access and identification systems use to passively scan nearby individuals. This means that personnel within the Array's radius may fail to register on proximity-based attendance or identity logging systems — a function that makes the Array quietly indispensable for anyone who needs to be somewhere without their presence being logged, without the overt aggression of a full signal jam.
Properties.aliases: The Fog Engine, Ghost Halo, The Scatter
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed in environments where the operative must move through or operate within signal-monitored spaces without triggering passive detection systems. Particularly effective in corporate office environments, transit hubs, and mid-tier residential zones where monitoring relies on signal analysis rather than dedicated active scanning. The biometric handshake disruption function makes the Array valuable for attendance spoofing — an operative can be physically present in a location while appearing absent from all passive logging systems. Multiple Arrays can be networked for coordinated field deployment, though signal bleed between units requires careful spacing to avoid artifacts that advanced monitoring systems may flag.
Properties.cultural_context: The Array's restricted rather than prohibited status is widely attributed to Tessera's regulatory relationships — the technology exists in a grey space that Tessera has carefully maintained by marketing civilian variants as 'signal hygiene devices' for privacy-conscious consumers. This civilian framing has given the Array a dual identity: it is simultaneously a serious operational tool used by professionals and a consumer privacy statement adopted by anti-surveillance activists and individuals who simply object to being passively scanned on their commute. The activist use has been invaluable to Tessera, as it makes blanket prohibition politically difficult. Operatives appreciate the cover but resent sharing shelf space with consumer grade units that perform at a fraction of the specification.
Properties.specifications: operational_radius: Standard mode: 8m; extended mode: 22m (reduced update frequency, higher detection risk); update_cycle: 200ms ambient resample and output adaptation; signal_range_coverage: Effective across 400MHz–28GHz spectrum; biometric_handshake_disruption: Reliable disruption of proximity ID systems within 3m of device center; power_source: High-density micro-cell; 6 hours standard mode, 3.5 hours extended mode; weight: 210g; form_factor: Worn unit (vest clip or underarm mount) or static placement unit (adhesive base); detection_risk: Standard mode: low; extended mode: moderate against Tier 4+ monitoring infrastructure
Properties.story_hooks: A meeting location was supposed to be Array-shielded, meaning no one's presence would be logged — but someone has footage of the meeting anyway, suggesting either a leak or a monitoring technology that defeats the Array's displacement profile.; Tessera's latest Array firmware update contains a hidden secondary reporting function that logs device locations to a Tessera internal server — a discovery that has enormous implications for anyone who trusted the device for operational security.; An Array left in static placement mode in a corporate building has been running for an unknown period, creating a persistent dead zone in the building's passive monitoring coverage that someone has been exploiting for months.; A contact wants the players to acquire a specific Array unit that was used during a high-profile incident — the device's ambient sampling logs contain a unique acoustic-electromagnetic fingerprint of the environment that can place specific individuals at the scene.

Nodes.Name: Priya Chandrasekhar — Tessera's internal security consultant who moonlights as an independent
Transit couriers moving high-value packages through logged corridors
Tessera Corponation Cenotaph Burst Transmitter — 'The Epitaph'

Properties.description:
The Cenotaph Burst Transmitter is a single-use emergency communications device — a hardened cylinder approximately the size of a flare, designed to transmit one compressed message packet across a maximum possible range before destroying itself. Tessera Corponation developed it for deep-cover operatives and isolated field agents who needed a last-resort option when all other communication had failed. The device charges over a period of 60–90 seconds from activation, during which it compresses, encrypts, and fractures the stored message into a multi-frequency burst transmission that fires simultaneously across forty-three frequency bands in a single 0.008-second pulse.

The burst is, by design, impossible to miss and impossible to trace. The transmission is so brief that direction-finding equipment cannot lock a bearing before it ends; the multi-frequency fracturing means no single monitoring system captures the complete message; and the device physically incinerates its own internals after firing, leaving a slag of ceramic and fused circuitry that yields nothing recoverable. Recipients must have a Tessera Cenotaph receiver unit — a small passive module that captures and reconstructs burst fragments across all forty-three bands simultaneously — to decode the message. Without a paired receiver, the burst is unintelligible noise across dozens of bands.

The Epitaph's cultural weight comes from its irreversibility. A device that destroys itself after a single transmission, designed for use when everything else has failed, carries an unmistakable implication. Tessera markets it to corporations for deniable deep-cover operations; the black market sells it to anyone who thinks they might someday need to scream once, very loudly, and then disappear. In Meridian 88 intelligence circles, receiving an Epitaph burst from a contact is understood to mean one of two things: either they've gone dark permanently, or whatever they've just told you is the most important thing they'll ever say.
Properties.aliases: The Epitaph, Cenotaph, Tessera Burst, Dead Shout
Properties.legality: Prohibited (civilian); Licensed (corporate and government intelligence operations)
Properties.tactical_use: The Epitaph is a last-resort or planned-exfiltration tool. Operatives carry it when entering situations where all other communication might be compromised or where a single guaranteed transmission is worth more than ongoing contact. Common uses include: transmitting final intelligence from a compromised position, sending an exfiltration call that cannot be jammed or intercepted, or delivering a pre-composed message on a timer if the operative fails to abort the sequence. The 60-90 second charge window is the critical vulnerability — the device must be activated in advance of the moment transmission is needed. Skilled operators pre-charge the Epitaph before entering a potential compromise situation.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88, the Epitaph has become something of a dark legend — less a piece of equipment than a ritual object. Finding one on a dead operative tells you they died before they could use it; finding the slag of a fired one tells you they did. Intelligence professionals discuss them in hushed, almost superstitious terms. There is a known practice among some deep-cover operatives of recording a personal message on their Epitaph at the start of an assignment — not operational intelligence, but something personal — to be transmitted if they trigger it under duress. Whether this message reaches anyone depends entirely on whether their handler is still monitoring the receiver frequency. Some are not.
Properties.specifications: dimensions: Cylinder, 18cm length x 3.5cm diameter; weight: 0.3kg; uses: 1; charge_time: 60–90 seconds from activation; transmission_duration: 0.008 seconds; frequency_bands: 43; effective_range: Approximately 40km line-of-sight; 15–20km urban; message_capacity: Up to 4 minutes compressed audio or equivalent data; encryption: Paired asymmetric key, hardware-bound to receiver unit; self-destruction: Complete internal thermal incineration within 2 seconds of transmission; detection_resistance: Very high — burst duration prevents direction-finding; multi-band fracturing defeats single-system capture
Properties.story_hooks: A Cenotaph burst is received by a dormant receiver unit in the players' possession — from a contact they believed dead for over a year. The message is fragmented, partially corrupted, and ends mid-sentence.; Someone in the city is firing Epitaphs on a schedule — one every seventy-two hours for the past three weeks. The transmissions are addressed to a receiver that no longer exists. Someone needs to find out who is sending them and why before Tessera Corponation's signals division does.; The players are given an Epitaph pre-loaded with a message they are not permitted to read. Their job is to get it to a specific location and fire it. Whether they follow those instructions is another matter.; A slag-form Epitaph is recovered from a crime scene. Tessera Corponation wants it back — not because of what it was, but because the self-destruction mechanism on this batch was defective, and the internal records may be partially recoverable.

Nodes.Name: Corporate intelligence assets in hostile territory
Handlers and cutouts managing isolated assets
Meridian 88 resistance cells as exfiltration triggers

Properties.description:
The Gradient Veil Transceiver is a palm-sized communications device built around Tessera's Spectral Smear Engine — a hardware-level signal processor that distributes a single transmission across dozens of simultaneous frequency bands at varying power levels, creating what appears on any monitoring sweep as uniform low-level atmospheric noise rather than a coherent broadcast. The receiving unit uses the same Spectral Smear key to reassemble the dispersed signal in real time, producing clean audio output. Without the matching key, the transmission is acoustically and mathematically indistinguishable from interference.

The device is built into a matte-black chassis roughly the size of a cigarette case, with a recessed dial for manual key cycling and a single flush-mounted speaker grille. It pairs with a standard throat mic or a dedicated lapel pickup. The Gradient Veil operates entirely in hardware — there is no software stack to exploit, no firmware to patch, and no network handshake to intercept. Tessera designed it specifically for environments where digital encryption is considered a liability because it can be cracked, spoofed, or exploited through software vulnerabilities.
Properties.aliases: The Veil, Gradient Box, Smear Radio
Properties.tactical_use: The Gradient Veil is favored in hostile electronic environments where opposing forces are running active signal-hunting equipment. Because it produces no distinct transmission spike on any single frequency, it defeats most directional RF detection arrays. Field teams use paired units for two-person secure communication, or run a three-unit cell where one device acts as a relay anchor. The hardware-only architecture means it functions normally inside software-defined radio jamming fields that would disable conventional encrypted comms. Its primary limitation is range — in a city full of signal-absorbing megastructures, 1.5km is often barely enough.
Properties.cultural_context: The Gradient Veil has a reputation for being the tool of professionals who do not trust software. Veteran mercenaries and old-school operatives swear by it precisely because it cannot be hacked remotely — you have to physically take it apart to compromise it. There is a small but devoted subculture of communications specialists who collect and maintain Gradient Veil units from different production runs, treating them as reliable instruments the way a carpenter prizes a particular hand tool. Corporate security divisions use them for internal affairs investigations, specifically because the devices leave no digital audit trail.
Properties.specifications: dimensions: 95mm x 55mm x 12mm; weight: 180g; range: Up to 8km in open terrain; 1.5km in dense urban canyons; encryption: Spectral Smear hardware key, 64-band distribution; power_source: Rechargeable solid-state cell, micro-USB-C compatible; battery_life: 18 hours continuous transmission; frequency_bands: Simultaneous distribution across 64 bands, 300MHz–5.8GHz; key_pairs: Factory-paired in sets of 2; additional units can be keyed by Tessera technicians only
Properties.story_hooks: A pair of Gradient Veil units surfaces at a crime scene — both factory-paired, meaning whoever used them bought them together. Tracing the purchase could crack a long-cold case.; Someone is broadcasting on a Spectral Smear pattern that exactly matches a Tessera key that was supposed to have been destroyed three years ago.; A character receives a Gradient Veil in the mail with no return address, already keyed to an unknown partner unit that is actively broadcasting.; Tessera announces a voluntary recall of a specific production run, citing 'unspecified hardware irregularities' — owners who comply receive a replacement; owners who refuse start having accidents.; A collector's cache of early-production Gradient Veil units is discovered in a condemned building, all keyed to the same frequency cluster — what network did they belong to?

Nodes.Name: Mid-tier criminal organizations with technical discipline

Properties.description:
The Laminar Ghost Chassis is Tessera Corponation's flagship stealth suit — a full-body garment system that combines passive thermal baffling, acoustic dampening laminate, and a dynamic optical surface layer into a unified platform. The outer surface is composed of Tessera's proprietary Fold-Reactive polymer, which samples ambient light from micro-aperture sensors distributed across the suit and re-emits it through a micro-LED matrix on the opposing surface, creating a near-real-time visual camouflage effect that is effective against human observers and most standard optical surveillance systems at ranges beyond four meters. The effect degrades noticeably at close range and breaks down entirely under ultraviolet or multispectral scanning.

Beneath the optical layer, the Ghost Chassis incorporates a passive thermal baffling membrane that suppresses the wearer's infrared signature to approximately ambient temperature within 90 seconds of activation, and an acoustic dampening laminate that reduces movement noise to below 15 decibels at normal walking pace. The suit is powered by a distributed micro-cell array woven through the lining, providing up to six hours of full active operation before requiring recharge. Tessera has positioned the Ghost Chassis as an intelligence-gathering and infiltration tool rather than a combat platform — the underlying armor protection is modest, rated for light fragmentation and minimal ballistic resistance.

The Ghost Chassis is tightly controlled by Tessera, sold exclusively through authorized intelligence-sector procurement channels and issued under strict end-user licensing agreements. Despite this, several units have surfaced in the hands of corporate espionage teams, high-end criminal organizations, and at least one documented case involving a Meridian 88 investigative journalist who used one to document a restricted Tessera research facility — an incident that resulted in significant legal action and the journalist's disappearance.
Properties.aliases: Ghost Suit, The Fold, Laminar Ghost, Tessera Stealth Shell
Properties.tactical_use: The Ghost Chassis is optimized for reconnaissance, infiltration, and exfiltration in controlled environments. Operators are trained to move slowly and deliberately — rapid movement creates artifacts in the optical layer that are detectable even at range. The suit is most effective in low-light conditions where the optical camouflage is supplemented by natural shadow. Standard counter-tactics include UV flood lighting, multispectral scanning sweeps, and acoustic sensors below the suit's dampening threshold.
Properties.cultural_context: The Ghost Chassis exists in a space of near-mythological status in Meridian 88's intelligence and criminal communities. Its rarity and the legal risk of possessing one make it a symbol of extreme capability and resource. Tessera's aggressive enforcement of end-user agreements — including rumored remote-deactivation and self-destruct capabilities built into the power array — means that owning one outside of sanctioned channels is understood to be a direct confrontation with the corporation. Some operators refer to unsanctioned Ghost Chassis units as 'orphans,' acknowledging their precarious status.
Properties.specifications: weight_kg: 6.1; coverage: Full body including hood and gloves; optical_camouflage_effective_range_m: 4+ meters against human/standard optical; optical_camouflage_failure_modes: UV light, multispectral scanning, ranges under 4m; thermal_suppression_activation_time_seconds: 90; acoustic_reduction_db: Below 15dB at walking pace; operational_duration_hours: 6; armor_rating: Light fragmentation only; recharge_time_hours: 3.5
Properties.story_hooks: A Ghost Chassis has been recovered from a crime scene where the wearer was killed — Tessera's recovery team arrived before law enforcement and removed it, but the players witnessed the exchange.; Tessera has remotely deactivated a Ghost Chassis while the operator was in the middle of a deep-cover infiltration — the timing suggests an inside leak, and the operator is now trapped.; A fence is offering a Ghost Chassis at a price that is suspiciously low — the unit may have been allowed to 'escape' Tessera's supply chain as bait for identifying unauthorized buyers.; The investigative journalist who used a Ghost Chassis to document a Tessera facility left encrypted footage that only surfaces when the suit's power array is activated — the suit is the key, and multiple parties want it.

Nodes.Name: Unknown — recovered unit, identity of operator undetermined
Sera Nacht (alias — wanted by Tessera for unauthorized possession)
Tessera Corponation Laminated Acoustic Stratum Probe

Properties.description:
The Laminated Acoustic Stratum Probe is a contact-based listening device engineered to isolate and reconstruct audio signals propagating through solid structural materials — concrete, reinforced polymer, steel plate, and composite building materials. It operates by pressing a laminated piezoelectric sensor array against a surface and applying a micro-vibration calibration pulse, which allows the device's signal processing core to map the acoustic transmission characteristics of that specific material. Once calibrated, it can separate target audio from structural noise, HVAC resonance, and deliberate jamming frequencies with unusual fidelity.

Tessera's core innovation is the stratification algorithm — rather than treating a wall as a single acoustic medium, the LASP models it as a stack of distinct material layers, each with its own transmission coefficient. A poured concrete wall with embedded rebar and a plasterboard interior finish is processed as three separate layers, and the algorithm reconstructs speech by reverse-modeling how sound waves degrade through each stratum. This allows the LASP to achieve intelligible audio recovery through walls up to 40cm of composite thickness that would defeat conventional contact microphones entirely.

The device is marketed to Tessera's corporate intelligence clients and licensed private investigators, but its real reputation was built in Meridian 88's legal gray zones — the towers of the Mid-Ring where corporate tenants conduct sensitive negotiations in conference rooms they believe are acoustically sealed. Counter-surveillance consultants routinely warn their clients about the LASP specifically by name. The device has also become a tool of necessity among political organizers and union coordinators who need to confirm whether a meeting space has been compromised before speaking freely.
Properties.tactical_use: Operators press the sensor pad flush against the target surface and run the calibration pulse before active listening. In the field, users frequently scout surfaces first by touch — looking for vibration nodes near structural supports, which transmit audio more efficiently. The LASP is most effective against interior partition walls rather than load-bearing exterior surfaces. Experienced users carry a small tube of acoustic coupling gel to improve sensor contact on rough or irregular surfaces. The device is used both offensively for intelligence gathering and defensively to sweep a room's perimeter before sensitive conversations.
Properties.cultural_context: The LASP occupies an uncomfortable legal position — restricted but not prohibited, which means possession alone is not an offense, but use in unauthorized surveillance is. This ambiguity makes it a favorite tool of those who operate just below the threshold of criminal liability. Among corporate intelligence professionals, demonstrating familiarity with the LASP's capabilities (and its countermeasures) is a mark of sophistication. In activist and organizing circles, the device has taken on an almost talismanic quality — checking the walls before a meeting is a ritual of operational security that signals seriousness and experience.
Properties.specifications: effective_penetration: Up to 40cm composite material thickness; calibration_pulse: Non-audible micro-vibration, 0.3-second sweep; material_compatibility: Concrete, reinforced polymer, steel, composite laminates, standard drywall assemblies; audio_output: Bone-conduction earpiece or encrypted data buffer; signal_processing: Tessera LASP-4 Stratification Core; power_source: Slim-cell battery, 12-hour active use; form_factor: Handheld probe body with flexible sensor pad, 180mm x 60mm; weight: 290g; data_logging: Encrypted 48-hour rolling buffer, local storage only
Properties.story_hooks: A corporate attorney is found dead, and the only evidence of foul play is a LASP left pressed against the wall of the conference room where she was last heard alive — the device's buffer contains 40 minutes of audio that someone clearly did not want recovered.; A counter-surveillance sweep of a union organizing space turns up a LASP that has been operating continuously for three weeks, but its local buffer has been remotely wiped — someone has been listening and covering their tracks.; Tessera quietly issues a firmware update that introduces a covert transmission channel, uploading audio fragments to a Tessera-controlled server. A whistleblower inside the company wants to get the information out before the update propagates to all active units.; A fixer offers the team a job: recover a LASP that was left behind during a botched extraction from a high-security tower. The problem is the device's buffer contains recordings that multiple powerful parties would kill to control.

Nodes.Name: Investigative journalists operating in hostile environments

Properties.description:
The Lattice Whisper Node is a self-organizing mesh repeater designed to be deployed in clusters, with each unit autonomously discovering, authenticating, and routing through its nearest neighbors to form a decentralized communication backbone that requires no fixed infrastructure. A single Node is functionally useless; a cluster of five or more creates a resilient, self-healing network that can span several city blocks, reroute around destroyed or jammed units, and sustain encrypted voice and data traffic without any connection to Meridian 88's licensed mesh infrastructure. Each unit is roughly cylindrical, about the size of a thumb, and is designed to be adhered to surfaces — undersides of benches, drainage grates, the backs of signage — where it can draw parasitic power from ambient electromagnetic fields and remain active for weeks without a dedicated power source.

The Node's defining technical feature is its adaptive routing intelligence. Rather than using fixed relay paths, the cluster continuously recalculates the most signal-efficient route through its members in response to interference, unit loss, or new additions. A Node that is physically destroyed simply drops out of the network's topology within seconds, and surrounding units redistribute the load. New Nodes introduced to an existing cluster are authenticated via a shared lattice key loaded at deployment, after which they are incorporated automatically. This makes the system highly resistant to targeted disruption — eliminating one Node accomplishes almost nothing.

Tessera Corponation markets the Lattice Whisper Node to corporate security teams for 'temporary infrastructure deployment in low-coverage operational environments,' and it is genuinely used for this purpose. It is also, with near-equal frequency, used by resistance cells, labor organizers, and underground networks to establish communications infrastructure in districts where the licensed mesh is monitored, degraded, or deliberately throttled by municipal authorities.
Properties.tactical_use: A standard deployment involves seeding 8–12 Nodes across a target area in advance of an operation, typically during a reconnaissance pass. Nodes are placed at irregular intervals and heights to maximize coverage and minimize the chance of a single sweep clearing the entire network. Once active, the cluster provides a private encrypted mesh for the operational team that is entirely independent of monitored infrastructure. The cluster can be extended in real time by introducing additional Nodes, making it possible to 'grow' the network ahead of a moving team. For extraction or exfiltration scenarios, pre-staged Nodes along a route allow continuous communication without relying on any surface that could be monitored.
Properties.cultural_context: The Lattice Whisper Node occupies a complicated legal position in Meridian 88. Licensed deployment requires registration of the lattice key with the Municipal Spectrum Authority, theoretically giving authorities access to the network's traffic. In practice, the registration process is slow, inconsistently enforced, and trivially circumvented by generating new lattice keys on unlicensed hardware. This gap between legal requirement and enforcement reality has made the Node a foundational tool for everyone from legitimate corporate security teams to the city's most organized underground networks. Labor organizers in particular have adopted the technology extensively, using pre-staged clusters to maintain communication during actions in districts where municipal mesh throttling is used as a tool of crowd management.
Properties.specifications: dimensions: 2.1cm diameter x 5.8cm length (per unit); weight: 18g per unit; power_source: Ambient EM harvesting; optional micro-cell supplement for low-field environments; minimum_cluster_size: 5 units for stable network formation; range_per_hop: Up to 180m in open conditions; 60–90m through dense construction; network_capacity: Up to 64 simultaneous authenticated users per 20-node cluster; self_healing_time: Unit dropout compensated within 4–9 seconds; operational_lifespan: 14–21 days continuous on EM harvesting alone
Properties.story_hooks: A cluster of Nodes is discovered in a sealed subsection of a Tessera Corponation facility — deployed from the inside, using a lattice key that does not match any registered deployment. Someone inside the company has been running a private network for an unknown period.; Municipal authorities announce a new detection protocol targeting unregistered Whisper Node clusters, but the announcement itself is transmitted over an unregistered cluster — suggesting the leak came from inside the Spectrum Authority.; A player's pre-staged cluster goes active and begins routing traffic that was not generated by their team, suggesting either that someone else has the lattice key or that a compromised Node was introduced into their deployment.; A decommissioned Whisper Node cluster in a demolished district is still active — somehow still harvesting enough power from the rubble to maintain a partial network, and still carrying fragments of encrypted traffic from an operation that ended two years ago.

Properties.description:
The Packet Dissociation Rig is a compact offensive and defensive hacking platform designed around a single foundational principle: any data transmission can be made functionally unreadable if its constituent packets are distributed across enough simultaneous channels with enough temporal jitter between them. The PDR does not encrypt in the conventional sense — it dissociates. Outgoing transmissions are shredded into micro-packets and distributed across dozens of simultaneous frequencies, protocols, and mesh relay nodes with randomized timing offsets. The receiving end, running complementary TESSERA firmware, reassembles them. To any intercepting system, the transmission looks like background noise across multiple unrelated channels.

The rig itself is a matte-black unit roughly the size of a hardback novel, with a fold-out antenna array and a physical interface port for direct-connect operations. Its processing core runs TESSERA's proprietary SCATTER architecture — a dynamic algorithm that continuously adjusts dissociation parameters based on the local signal environment, making the pattern of the transmission itself unpredictable even if an adversary has characterized the method. The rig can operate in passive mode, protecting the user's own transmissions, or in active mode, where it projects dissociation interference across a local area, degrading the coherence of nearby communications it does not control.

The PDR is the standard hacking rig for TESSERA's own field operatives and is sold at significant markup to corporate security firms and licensed government intelligence units. It has a well-developed black market presence because cracked firmware removes the mandatory TESSERA backdoor — a feature the company officially denies exists but which competing intelligence services have documented extensively. The cracked version is called a Ghost Rig and commands a substantial premium over the legitimate hardware.
Properties.aliases: PDR, Dissociator, The Scatter, Ghost Rig
Properties.tactical_use: Operatives use the PDR in passive mode during infiltration to ensure their comms and data pulls are invisible to corporate network monitoring. In active mode, it is deployed to degrade an adversary's coordination during an operation — disrupting their mesh communications without producing the obvious jamming signature that triggers hardened countermeasures. Direct-connect operations allow a skilled operator to interface with hardwired systems, dissociate security handshakes across multiple authentication channels simultaneously, and exploit the resulting desynchronization to force authentication failures. Black-market Ghost Rigs are preferred for operations where TESSERA's backdoor would compromise the mission.
Properties.cultural_context: Owning a legitimate PDR is a marker of serious corporate or government standing — the licensing process is invasive and the cost is prohibitive for most. The Ghost Rig version occupies a different cultural space entirely: it is a status symbol among high-end freelance operatives, a proof of technical sophistication and access to networks that can source and flash the cracked firmware. TESSERA publicly pursues Ghost Rig users aggressively, but the consensus in operational circles is that the company also uses Ghost Rig tracking as an intelligence tool — allowing cracked units to operate long enough to map the networks using them.
Properties.specifications: dimensions: 22cm x 15cm x 5cm; weight: 0.9 kg with antenna array folded; simultaneous_channels: Up to 64; supported_protocols: Mesh, cellular, short-range RF, encrypted corporate bands, legacy infrastructure; passive_mode_range: User's own transmissions only; active_interference_radius: Up to 40 meters (signal-environment dependent); processing_core: TESSERA SCATTER v7.2; interface: Direct-connect physical port plus wireless pairing; battery_life: 6 hours active mode, 18 hours passive mode; firmware_update_requirement: Mandatory monthly via TESSERA network (legitimate units only)
Properties.story_hooks: A Ghost Rig surfaces with firmware that appears to be a genuine cracked version but contains a second-layer backdoor more sophisticated than TESSERA's standard — someone is running a honeypot operation targeting the people who buy Ghost Rigs to avoid TESSERA surveillance.; The players' PDR begins receiving reassembled transmissions it should not have access to, suggesting someone else in their operational area is running a complementary TESSERA unit and inadvertently routing packets through their rig.; A licensed PDR recovered from a corporate operative has its mandatory firmware update log intact — and the update timestamps reveal that TESSERA was pushing real-time location data from the unit during a period when the operative was supposedly running a black-site operation their employer denies authorizing.; A TESSERA engineer approaches the players claiming to have documented the backdoor and wanting to go public — they need the players to extract the evidence from a TESSERA facility while using PDRs that TESSERA can monitor.

Properties.description:
The Peripatetic Address Shell is a signal-routing device that continuously migrates its apparent broadcast origin across Meridian 88's mesh infrastructure, making its user's communications appear to originate from hundreds of different physical nodes in rapid succession. Unlike simple spoofing tools, the PAS does not fabricate false origins — it actually routes signal traffic through a shifting chain of legitimate mesh relays, each hop authenticated by the next, creating a real and traceable path that nonetheless resolves to a different apparent source every 4.3 seconds. Tessera Corponation developed it initially for their own internal security teams, who needed to conduct field communications without creating locatable transmission signatures.

The device's proprietary 'address drift' algorithm is its defining feature — it learns the relay density and traffic load of whatever urban environment it operates in, prioritizing high-traffic nodes where an additional signal is statistically invisible and deprioritizing quiet relays where anomalous traffic might trigger automated flags. The result is a communication device that hides not by going silent, but by becoming indistinguishable from the city's own noise. Users report that in dense districts, the PAS achieves what Tessera's documentation calls 'statistical anonymity' — the probability of tracing a call drops below actionable thresholds within the first two minutes of transmission.

The Shell is physically unassuming — a matte black rectangular unit worn on the forearm or kept in a jacket pocket, with a single earpiece jack and a minimal control surface. Its reputation in the field is excellent among anyone who needs to stay reachable without staying locatable, and Tessera's decision to offer a consumer-licensed version (with reduced hop frequency and mandatory registration) has only deepened the market for unlicensed units with the full drift capability intact.
Properties.aliases: The Ghost Number, Wandering Shell, PAS Unit
Properties.tactical_use: Worn during active operations where maintaining communication without creating a locatable signature is essential. Particularly effective in urban chase scenarios — a runner can stay in contact with support teams without broadcasting a traceable position. Also used by handlers who need to direct field assets without exposing their own location. The latency overhead is negligible for voice and text but makes it unsuitable for real-time data-heavy applications.
Properties.cultural_context: The PAS occupies a peculiar legal gray zone in Meridian 88 — the licensed version is sold openly in electronics markets and is popular among journalists, lawyers, and privacy-conscious citizens. The unlicensed full-drift version is technically a restricted device but is so visually identical to the licensed model that enforcement is inconsistent. Tessera has been accused, credibly, of deliberately engineering this ambiguity to maintain plausible deniability while flooding the market with devices their own security arm relies on.
Properties.specifications: dimensions: 13cm x 6cm x 1.8cm wrist-mount or pocket form; weight: 120g; hop_frequency: Every 4.3 seconds (unlicensed); every 30 seconds (licensed consumer version); relay_chain_length: 8–24 nodes per active session; urban_coverage: Functional in any district with mesh node density above 40 nodes/km²; latency_overhead: 11–18ms added to transmission; battery_life: 16 hours active transmission; output: Standard encrypted voice and text; compatible with most mesh-capable devices
Properties.story_hooks: A PAS unit is transmitting from somewhere in the city on a loop — same message, cycling through thousands of nodes. Someone set it going and never came back to turn it off.; The players are given a PAS unit by a contact who immediately disappears. The unit keeps receiving incoming calls from a number that doesn't resolve to any registered identity.; Tessera's address drift algorithm has developed an unexpected behavior in Meridian 88's current mesh configuration — certain routing paths keep recurring, and someone has figured out how to predict where a PAS user will route next.; A licensed PAS unit was used in a high-profile assassination. The investigators want the players to prove it was unlicensed — or confirm that the licensed version is capable of the same anonymity Tessera claims only the black-market version provides.

Nodes.Name: Anyone who needs to stay reachable but not findable

Properties.description:
The Recursive Fold Microframe is a single-occupant personal vehicle engineered around a central design problem: how to move a person rapidly through Meridian 88's dense urban environment and then make both the person and the vehicle disappear. The Microframe is a motorized two-wheeler in operational configuration, but its carbon-composite frame is built on a recursive folding joint system — a series of interlocking pivot points that allow the entire vehicle to collapse into a carry configuration roughly the size and shape of a large backpack in under eight seconds. The folded unit weighs 14 kg and is carried on an integrated harness. Deployment reverses the process: the rider drops the pack, catches the unfolding frame at hip height, and is in motion within twelve seconds of initiating deployment. The electric motor draws from a solid-state power cell integrated into the frame spine, providing a range of 60 km per charge at urban speeds.

The Microframe's performance in operational configuration is deliberately modest — a top speed of 55 km/h and an agility profile optimized for low-speed precision navigation through pedestrian-dense corridors rather than high-speed open transit. Its value is not in outrunning pursuit but in outmaneuvering it: the ability to enter a transit corridor on foot, deploy a vehicle in a moving crowd, transit to a secondary position, and fold back to foot-mobile before a response can be coordinated. Tessera Corponation's firmware includes a route-learning function that builds a personal map of the rider's habitual transit paths, optimizing folding and deployment point suggestions over time based on observed pursuit patterns and transit density data.

The Microframe was developed by Tessera Corponation's logistics research division as a last-mile delivery solution for high-density urban environments, but its adoption by Meridian 88's runner and courier subculture was rapid and enthusiastic. Tessera Corponation has quietly leaned into this secondary market, offering a 'field edition' with reinforced joints, a reduced acoustic profile, and the route-learning firmware unlocked from its default corporate delivery parameters.
Properties.aliases: the Fold, Microframe, Tessera Folder, Ghost Bike
Properties.tactical_use: The Microframe's primary tactical value is the transition between vehicle and foot-mobile states. A runner using a Microframe can enter a monitored zone on foot, deploy mid-transit to cover distance rapidly, fold before reaching a checkpoint or camera cluster, and continue on foot with no vehicle to search for or impound. The route-learning firmware actively improves this capability over time, identifying optimal fold and deploy points based on coverage gaps and pursuit response times. In courier operations, the Microframe is used for the final and most exposed segment of a run, where the ability to go vehicle-to-foot instantly is more valuable than raw speed.
Properties.cultural_context: The Recursive Fold Microframe has become a specific marker of the professional runner in Meridian 88's courier culture — distinct from the amateur who rides a conventional bike or the corporate operative with an armored vehicle. Owning a Fold signals a certain level of operational sophistication: the understanding that disappearing is more valuable than speed. There is a ritual element to the fold and deploy sequence that experienced riders cultivate; the eight-second fold time is a benchmark that Microframe users practice and compare. The field edition's availability through semi-legitimate channels has made it accessible enough to be common in the Verge Corridors without being so common as to lose its professional association.
Properties.specifications: operational_configuration: Two-wheel motorized personal vehicle; carry_configuration: Backpack form factor, integrated harness; fold_time: < 8 seconds (practiced operator); deploy_time: < 12 seconds (practiced operator); carry_weight: 14 kg; top_speed: 55 km/h; range: 60 km per charge (urban mixed speed); power_source: Integrated solid-state cell (frame spine), induction rechargeable; acoustic_signature: 22 dB at 5 meters (electric drivetrain, no exhaust); frame_material: Carbon-composite recursive joint assembly; firmware: Tessera Transit AI (route learning, deployment point optimization, pursuit pattern analysis)
Properties.story_hooks: A Recursive Fold Microframe is recovered from a canal with its route-learning firmware intact. The routes stored in it map a series of locations across three districts that, connected, form a pattern nobody can immediately explain — but several of the locations are now crime scenes.; Tessera Corponation's route-learning firmware has been collecting anonymized transit data from all registered Microframes and feeding it to an undisclosed analytics system. Someone has obtained a partial data dump and is selling it — and the buyer list includes people who would use it to map runner transit patterns.; A Microframe user is leaving folded units at specific locations across the city as dead drops. The units are unregistered and the route-learning firmware has been wiped, but the carry harnesses all have the same custom modification. Someone is building a network and the player characters keep finding the nodes.; The field edition Microframe has a firmware vulnerability that allows an outside party to activate the route-learning system silently and transmit its data in real time. A Tessera Corponation insider is trying to quietly warn the runner community before the corporate security division realizes the warning is going out.

Nodes.Name: Professional courier runners in the Verge Corridors
Tessera Corponation last-mile delivery operators (corporate fleet)
Independent operatives requiring covert urban transit
Yuna Satch (courier, holds the current unofficial Verge Corridor fold-deploy record at 6.4 seconds)
Gray-market intelligence couriers moving physical data packages
Outer-ring organizers who need to transit between districts without leaving a vehicle trail

Properties.description:
The Recursive Mesh Anchor is a deployable network node disguised as a structural fastener — a thumb-sized titanium spike that, when driven into any conductive surface, broadcasts a self-replicating subnet capable of bridging isolated local networks across a radius of up to 400 meters. The device piggybacks on ambient electrical noise in walls, conduits, and rebar to propagate signal without drawing detectable power draw from any single source. Once planted, it fragments its own address signature recursively every 11 seconds, making passive detection nearly impossible without physical access to the spike itself.

What distinguishes the RMA from conventional signal repeaters is its passive operational profile. It requires no active power cell after initial deployment — the kinetic energy of insertion charges an internal graphene microcapacitor that sustains the device for 72 hours. The spike's exterior is coated in construction-grade polymer composite, making it visually indistinguishable from standard structural anchors used by Palladian and other contractors throughout Meridian 88's lower districts.

The RMA is standard kit for Tessera's own field intelligence contractors and has leaked into the hands of fixers, corporate espionage runners, and union organizers who need persistent comms infrastructure in surveilled buildings. Building security sweeps routinely miss them; the most reliable countermeasure is a physical inspection of every fastener in a structure, which is rarely practical.
Properties.aliases: Ghost Nail, Loop Spike, Tessera Anchor, RMA
Properties.tactical_use: Planted during advance recon of a target building — often during a legitimate contractor visit or building access window. Provides persistent comms relay for a follow-on team operating inside signal-dead zones like server vaults, sub-basements, or Faraday-lined executive floors. Can also be used to bridge two isolated networks for passive data exfiltration over extended periods.
Properties.cultural_context: Among runners in Meridian 88's contractor class, finding a Tessera Anchor in a wall you just drilled is a known occupational hazard and dark joke — 'someone was here before you.' The anchors have become a kind of territorial marker in the grey-market intelligence community, a sign that a building is already compromised or being watched. Corporate security divisions have begun cataloguing anchor placements as a way of mapping rival intelligence networks, which has made the devices simultaneously more valuable and more dangerous to carry.
Properties.specifications: dimensions: 12mm diameter x 38mm length; weight: 47g; operational_duration: 72 hours post-insertion; signal_radius: 400m in conductive-rich environments, 180m in dry concrete; address_rotation_interval: 11 seconds; insertion_tool_required: Standard pneumatic or manual driver; detection_resistance: Passes standard RF sweep; fails only under directed spectral analysis
Properties.story_hooks: A runner plants an RMA only to discover it immediately handshakes with an existing anchor already in the wall — someone has been running a subnet in this building for months.; A Tessera contractor is found dead with every RMA in her kit already deployed in a building she never officially entered.; A building demolition crew accidentally broadcasts a dormant RMA's stored data cache when their cutting equipment charges it back to life.; A corporate security director offers a substantial bounty for whoever can map all active anchors in a rival's headquarters tower — without alerting the rival.

Properties.description:
The Stochastic Blind Ledger is a signal-layer encryption device that operates on a principle Tessera calls 'communicative deniability through noise parity' — in plain terms, it transmits real messages by hiding them inside statistically indistinguishable synthetic noise, making the channel appear to carry nothing but ambient electromagnetic garbage. The Ledger generates a rolling stochastic key synchronized between paired units, allowing both endpoints to extract meaningful data from what looks, to any intercepting party, like random spectrum bleed from aging infrastructure. It requires no dedicated frequency and can ride parasitically on existing signal pollution in Meridian 88's notoriously cluttered electromagnetic environment.

The physical unit is a matte-black rectangular device slightly larger than a deck of cards, with no visible inputs beyond a single recessed pairing port. Operation is intentionally opaque: there are no indicators, no screens, no confirmation signals. Users simply trust the synchronized key or they don't. Tessera designed this as a feature — an interceptor who captures a Ledger unit gains nothing without the paired device and the synchronization seed, which is burned to a one-time substrate during initial pairing and cannot be reconstructed.

The Ledger occupies a peculiar legal space. Tessera sells it openly to licensed corporate communications teams as an anti-industrial-espionage tool, but the same properties that make it attractive to corporations make it equally attractive to everyone else. Meridian 88's corporate security apparatus has been lobbying for stricter licensing requirements for years, so far without success — partly because several of the lobbying corps quietly use Ledgers themselves for communications they'd prefer regulators not see.
Properties.aliases: the Ledger, Scatter Box, Tessera Noise Book
Properties.tactical_use: Used for secure point-to-point communication in environments under active signals intelligence monitoring. The Ledger's strength is in contested urban areas where the existing EM noise floor is high — Meridian 88's older industrial districts are ideal operating environments. Operatives use paired units to pass instructions, coordinates, and intelligence without generating any detectable secure-channel traffic. The absence of confirmation signals requires disciplined communication protocols to avoid misalignment.
Properties.cultural_context: Among Meridian 88's professional intelligence community — corporate, governmental, and freelance — the Ledger has become a marker of serious tradecraft. Receiving one from a handler signals that the operation is being run at a level where even the existence of communication must be deniable. There is a dark humor in the community around the device's silence: 'You'll know it's working when nothing happens.'
Properties.specifications: transmission_range: Up to 2km direct; unlimited via relay infrastructure; bandwidth: Low — optimized for text and compressed audio; video transmission not supported; key_synchronization: Rolling 256-bit stochastic key, re-seeded every 90 seconds; pairing_method: Physical contact pairing via recessed port; one-time substrate burned on pairing; detection_resistance: Transmissions statistically indistinguishable from ambient EM noise at standard analysis depth; deep-spectrum forensic analysis can identify pattern anomalies with sustained effort; dimensions: 9cm x 6cm x 1.8cm; power: Micro-cell, 72-hour active use; trickle-charges from ambient EM in standby
Properties.story_hooks: A player receives a Ledger in a package with no sender information — it's already paired to something, and it's already receiving.; Two Ledger units from the same pairing batch turn up in the possession of people on opposite sides of a corporate conflict; someone sold them both to rivals.; Tessera's licensing division contacts the players: a Ledger was used in connection with a political assassination and they need it recovered quietly before regulators use it as leverage to mandate backdoors in the product line.; A player's Ledger stops producing output mid-operation — either the paired unit was destroyed, or someone found a way to jam the synchronization seed remotely, which shouldn't be possible.

Nodes.Name: Regulatory-adjacent officials engaged in undisclosed communications
Tessera Industries Adaptive Disguise Matrix ADM-1

Properties.description: A facial prosthetic system using programmable matter that can reconfigure itself to replicate any human face from a stored template library. The ADM-1 is a thin membrane applied to the face that reshapes itself to alter bone structure appearance, skin texture, pigmentation, and feature proportions. A single unit can store up to 20 facial templates and switch between them in approximately 8 seconds. The disguise is convincing to human observers and defeats most facial recognition systems, though it cannot replicate retinal patterns or dental structure. Tessera's programmable matter technology gives the mask a lifelike quality that rigid prosthetics cannot match — the disguised face moves, expresses, and ages naturally.
Properties.aliases: ADM-1, Face Swap, Tessera Mask, Identity Kit
Properties.specifications: templates: Up to 20 stored facial profiles; transition time: 8 seconds between faces; material: Programmable matter membrane; facial recognition defeat: Visual + most biometric systems; limitations: Cannot replicate retinal patterns or dental structure; weight: 0.08 kg; application: Adheres to facial skin surface; battery: 12-hour active transformation; info: indefinite static hold; removal: Peels off cleanly without residue
Properties.story_hooks: A murder suspect was positively identified by facial recognition at the crime scene — but they were confirmed to be elsewhere at the time, and the investigation reveals an ADM-1 was used to impersonate them.; An ADM-1 unit has malfunctioned while the wearer was in public — the face began cycling through stored templates uncontrollably, revealing 20 different identities to horrified bystanders.

Nodes.Name: Tessera Industries Compact Evidence Destroyer CED-2

Properties.description: A portable device that destroys physical evidence and electronic data with a combination of thermite incineration and electromagnetic pulse. The CED-2 has two compartments — a thermite chamber that incinerates physical items at 2,500°C, and an EMP generator that permanently destroys electronic data on any device placed within its field. The device is single-use and reduces its contents to unrecoverable ash and magnetically wiped circuits in under 5 seconds. Tessera markets it as a 'classified material destruction system' for authorized disposal of sensitive materials.
Properties.aliases: CED-2, Burn Box, Data Kill, Tessera Shredder
Properties.specifications: physical destruction: Thermite; info: 2; 500°C incineration; permanent data wipe; neural interface authorization; electronic destruction: Focused EMP; destruction time: 5 seconds; chamber volume: 20x15x10 cm; residual evidence: Unrecoverable ash and wiped circuits; weight: 2 kg; activation: Dual-button safety; single use: Device self-destructs with contents
Properties.story_hooks: A CED-2 was activated at a crime scene, destroying all physical and electronic evidence in one 5-second burst — investigators arrived to find a pile of ash and the melted remains of the CED-2 itself.; A CED-2 has been modified with a timer and concealed in a filing cabinet — it is set to destroy the cabinet's contents at a specific time, and finding it before activation requires knowing it exists.
