Nodes.Name: Tessera Industries Deep Scan Penetrating Radar DSR-1

Properties.description: A portable ground-penetrating and wall-penetrating radar system that creates detailed 3D maps of structures, underground spaces, and the contents of sealed containers. The DSR-1 emits ultra-wideband radar pulses that penetrate up to 10 meters through standard construction materials, 3 meters through reinforced concrete, and 20 meters through soil. The return signals are processed into a real-time 3D visualization displayed on the operator's neural interface or a tablet screen. The system can detect human-sized objects through walls, identify voids and hidden chambers in structures, and map underground tunnel networks from the surface.
Properties.aliases: Deep Scan, DSR-1, Wall Looker, X-Ray Box
Properties.specifications: penetration: 10m standard construction; info: 3m reinforced concrete; 20m soil; resolution: 5 cm at 3m depth; visualization: Real-time 3D on neural interface or tablet; frequency: Ultra-wideband 100 MHz - 6 GHz; scan rate: 10 frames per second; weight: 2.5 kg handheld unit; battery: 4-hour continuous scanning; form factor: Handheld unit with directional antenna
Properties.story_hooks: A DSR-1 scan of an unremarkable building revealed a hidden sub-basement that does not appear on any architectural plan — the space is occupied and powered, and its contents are shielded from deeper scanning.; Someone has been using a DSR-1 to map the location of wall safes in residential buildings from the exterior — a string of burglaries targets hidden safes that the victims believed were undetectable.

Properties.description: A full-body suit woven from Tessera's electromagnetic-absorbing metamaterial fibers that renders the wearer nearly invisible to thermal imaging, radar, and passive electromagnetic sensors. The Ghostweave does not provide optical invisibility — you can still be seen with the naked eye — but against the sensor suites that constitute modern security systems, the wearer effectively does not exist. The suit absorbs 99.2% of incident electromagnetic radiation across thermal and radar bands, and its inner surface includes a conductive mesh that contains the wearer's own electromagnetic emissions. In a world where detection relies on sensors rather than eyes, the Ghostweave makes someone a ghost.
Properties.aliases: Ghostweave, Stealth Suit, Shadow Skin, Tessera Ghost
Properties.specifications: EM absorption: 99.2% across thermal and radar bands; optical visibility: Normal — visual detection still possible; EM containment: Inner conductive mesh suppresses wearer emissions; weight: 1.8 kg; form factor: Full body coverage; info: worn under clothing; metamaterial degrades in machine washing; operating duration: Unlimited — passive material properties; maintenance: Hand wash only
Properties.story_hooks: A Ghostweave suit was found at a break-in scene — the suit had been compromised by a chemical agent that caused the metamaterial to fluoresce on security cameras instead of absorb, turning the intruder's stealth suit into a beacon.; Tessera is tracking Ghostweave suits by embedding a unique EM signature in each suit's weave that is detectable by Tessera's own sensors — buyers think they are invisible, but Tessera always knows where they are.

Nodes.Name: Tessera Industries Holographic Distraction Projector HDP-5

Properties.description: A throwable device that projects a 3-meter holographic scene — an explosion, a running person, a vehicle crash, or other attention-grabbing event — that lasts for 15 seconds. The HDP-5 is a single-use distraction tool designed to draw attention and surveillance focus to one location while the operator moves through another. The holographic projection includes simulated sound and a thermal signature generator that fools infrared sensors, creating a multi-sensory deception that is convincing for the critical seconds needed to slip past security.
Properties.aliases: HDP-5, Light Show, Holo Flash, Tessera Distraction
Properties.specifications: projection: 3-meter holographic scene; duration: 15 seconds; sound: Integrated speaker; info: matched to scene; thermal: IR signature generator; scenes: 10 pre-loaded scenarios; weight: 0.15 kg; activation: Twist and throw; range: Projects at point of landing; fidelity: Convincing beyond 5 meters
Properties.story_hooks: An HDP-5 projecting a fake explosion in a crowded area caused a stampede — the hologram was intended as a distraction for a nearby operation, but the panic resulted in injuries and deaths.; HDP-5 units have been modified to project realistic holographic people that walk, talk, and interact — creating phantom witnesses and suspects that complicate crime scene reconstruction.

Nodes.Name: Tessera Industries Metamaterial Lock Pick Set MLP-1

Properties.description: A set of lockpicking tools fabricated from programmable matter that can dynamically reconfigure their shape to match any lock profile. The MLP-1 contains three programmable matter tools that can transform from standard tension wrenches and picks to specialized decoder tools, tubular lock picks, wafer picks, and any other configuration needed for a specific lock type. The tools are controlled through a neural interface that scans the lock's keyway and automatically shapes the tool to match. Where a conventional lockpick set requires 15+ individual tools and extensive practice, the MLP-1 provides a universal solution that adapts itself to the challenge.
Properties.aliases: MLP-1, Shape Picks, Tessera Keys, Universal Picks
Properties.specifications: tools: 3 programmable matter instruments; configurations: Universal — any lock profile; control: Neural interface scan and auto-shape; reconfiguration time: 2 seconds per tool; material: Tessera programmable matter; weight: 0.08 kg total set; form factor: Small case; info: pen-sized tools; battery: 48-hour active use per tool; limitations: Cannot bypass electronic locks — mechanical only
Properties.story_hooks: A lock thought to be unpickable was defeated in under 10 seconds — the only tool capable of that feat is an MLP-1 with its auto-scan feature, and fewer than 100 units exist.; A Tessera insider has leaked the programmable matter blueprint for lock pick configurations — anyone with access to a programmable matter fabricator can now produce MLP-1 equivalent tools.

Properties.description: A pocket-sized holographic projector that creates a 30 cm cube of volumetric imagery, sufficient for displaying 3D maps, schematics, faces, or small-scale tactical models. The MHP-3 is a personal information display device that replaces flat screens with true 3D visualization, interfacing with neural implants for direct data input. Users project building blueprints, rotate 3D models of equipment, display facial identification holos, and visualize tactical situations in miniature. The device has become standard professional equipment for engineers, investigators, and tactical planners.
Properties.aliases: MHP-3, Tiny Holo, Pocket Show, Light Box
Properties.specifications: projection volume: 30 cm cube; resolution: 4K volumetric; input: Neural interface or wireless data connection; brightness: Visible in ambient lighting; weight: 0.05 kg; battery: 12 hours continuous; form factor: Matchbox-sized; interaction: Gesture control through neural interface
Properties.story_hooks: An MHP-3 found at a crime scene was still projecting when investigators arrived — it displayed a 3D map of the building with entry and exit routes marked, a complete tactical plan left behind by the perpetrators.; MHP-3 projectors have been hacked to display subliminal images within their normal holographic output — users are seeing content they did not request, embedded in their legitimate projections.

Nodes.Name: Tessera Industries Optical Fiber Tap Detector OFT-1

Properties.description: A diagnostic tool that detects unauthorized taps on fiber-optic cables by measuring signal loss at micro-dB resolution — far more sensitive than standard network monitoring equipment. The OFT-1 sends a calibrated light pulse through a fiber and measures the return signal with precision that can identify the 0.1 dB loss caused by a micro-bend optical tap. The device maps the location of any detected tap to within 10 cm along the fiber run, allowing physical identification and removal. Tessera developed it as a counter to their own OT-1 optical tap — and sells both the attack and the defense.
Properties.aliases: OFT-1, Fiber Finder, Tap Sweep, Line Clear
Properties.specifications: detection sensitivity: 0.01 dB signal loss resolution; tap localization: 10 cm precision along fiber; scan speed: 1 km of fiber per minute; false positive rate: Less than 0.1%; compatibility: Single-mode and multi-mode fiber; weight: 0.5 kg; battery: 8 hours continuous scanning; output: Fiber loss map with anomaly flags
Properties.story_hooks: An OFT-1 sweep of a corporate network found 23 unauthorized optical taps across the facility — some had been in place for over two years, and the combined data loss is measured in petabytes.; A Tessera OFT-1 has been found to have a firmware modification that causes it to report clean results on fibers that actually have taps — the counter-surveillance tool has been sabotaged to protect existing surveillance.

Nodes.Name: Tessera Industries Optical Tap Micro-Splice OT-1

Properties.description: A miniature fiber-optic tap device that splices into a fiber-optic cable without interrupting service, siphoning a fraction of the light signal for interception. The OT-1 uses a precision micro-bend technique that causes a small percentage of light to escape the fiber at the tap point, where it is captured by a detector and decoded. The signal loss is so small (0.1 dB) that it falls within normal cable attenuation tolerances and is undetectable by standard network monitoring. The device is installed in 30 seconds by a trained operator and can be placed anywhere along an accessible fiber run.
Properties.aliases: Optical Tap, OT-1, Light Leech, Fiber Splice
Properties.specifications: signal loss: 0.1 dB — within normal attenuation tolerance; installation time: 30 seconds; detectability: Undetectable by standard monitoring; data capture: Full signal copy of fiber traffic; storage: 5 TB internal; transmission: Optional burst to nearby receiver; battery: 12-month operation; size: 3 cm x 1 cm attached to fiber; compatibility: Standard single-mode and multi-mode fiber
Properties.story_hooks: A network security audit discovered six OT-1 taps on the backbone fiber connecting a government facility to external networks — the taps had been operational for over a year, capturing every byte of the facility's communications.; An OT-1 was found on a fiber cable that carries quantum-encrypted traffic — while the encryption makes the data unreadable, the tap's metadata capture reveals communication patterns that are intelligence gold.

Nodes.Name: Tessera Industries Phantom Comms Relay PCR-3

Properties.description: A covert communications relay device that can be concealed in walls, under floors, or inside furniture, creating a local encrypted mesh network that does not touch any existing communications infrastructure. The PCR-3 creates an independent communication channel between paired devices using frequency-hopping spread spectrum transmission that is virtually undetectable against the background electromagnetic noise of urban environments. Multiple relays can be daisy-chained to extend range, and the network auto-heals if individual relays are destroyed.
Properties.aliases: Phantom Relay, PCR-3, Ghost Comm, Dark Relay
Properties.specifications: transmission: Frequency-hopping spread spectrum; encryption: 512-bit rolling key; range per relay: 300 meters; daisy-chain: Up to 20 relays per network; self-healing: Automatic rerouting on relay loss; power: 30-day battery or hardwired; size: 8 cm x 5 cm x 2 cm; concealment: Designed for in-wall/under-floor installation; detectability: Below noise floor of standard RF scanners
Properties.story_hooks: A sweep of a corporate building found a 15-relay PCR-3 network that had been operating for over a year — someone built a complete covert communications infrastructure inside the building without detection.; PCR-3 relays have been found in public infrastructure — street lights, bus stops, park benches — creating a city-wide covert communication network that anyone with paired devices can access.

Nodes.Name: Tessera Industries Quantum Key Generator QKG-2

Properties.description: A portable device that generates quantum encryption keys for securing communications, data storage, and access control systems. The QKG-2 uses a miniaturized quantum random number generator to produce encryption keys that are mathematically proven to be uncrackable by any known or theoretically possible classical computing system. Each generated key pair is unique and entangled — compromising one half immediately invalidates the other. The device can produce 1,000 key pairs per hour and is used to secure everything from neural interface communications to physical lock systems.
Properties.aliases: QKG-2, Key Maker, Quantum Lock, Tessera Key
Properties.specifications: key generation: 1; info: 000 pairs per hour; smartphone sized; wireless transfer; or neural interface; key type: Quantum-entangled pairs; security: Mathematically uncrackable by classical computing; compromise detection: Key entanglement invalidation; compatibility: Standard encryption interfaces; weight: 0.2 kg; form factor: Handheld; battery: 72-hour continuous generation; output: USB-C
Properties.story_hooks: A QKG-2 has been generating key pairs with anomalous properties — the entangled keys are correlating with keys generated by a different QKG-2 unit in a different location, as if the quantum states are leaking between devices.; Someone has developed a technique to predict QKG-2 key generation by analyzing the device's quantum random number generator — the keys are still quantum-secure but the generator itself has a bias that can be exploited.

Nodes.Name: Tessera Industries Reality Anchor Projector RAP-1

Properties.description: A device that disrupts holographic projections, augmented reality overlays, and adaptive camouflage systems within a 15-meter radius by emitting a structured light pattern that interferes with the coherent light used by these systems. The RAP-1 essentially forces the visual environment to be real — holograms flicker and collapse, AR overlays glitch and disappear, and active camouflage systems display artifacts that reveal the concealed object. Tessera developed it as a countermeasure to their own holographic and metamaterial products, recognizing that a tool to defeat illusions has as much market value as the illusions themselves.
Properties.aliases: RAP-1, Truth Lamp, De-Glitch, Reality Check
Properties.specifications: effect radius: 15 meters; disrupted systems: Holographic projections; info: AR overlays; active camouflage; AR glitches; camo shows artifacts; method: Structured light interference; effect: Holograms collapse; power: 4-hour battery; weight: 0.5 kg; form factor: Handheld wand or mounted emitter; activation: Continuous emission while powered; limitations: Does not affect passive materials or metamaterial surfaces
Properties.story_hooks: A RAP-1 activated at a social event revealed that three of the guests were holographic projections — no one knew they were not physically present, and the question of who sent the holograms and why they needed to appear present is urgent.; A modified RAP-1 has been developed that forces ROCL augmented reality overlays to display the raw, unmodified physical environment — users describe the experience as seeing their world stripped naked, and some find the real version deeply disturbing.

Nodes.Name: Tessera Industries Signal Cloaking Device SCD-1

Properties.description: A pocket-sized device that masks the electromagnetic emissions of the wearer's neural interface and all electronic devices within a 1-meter radius. The SCD-1 does not jam signals — it absorbs and contains them using a metamaterial shell, preventing any EM leakage that could be detected by passive surveillance. The device makes the wearer electronically invisible without disrupting their own device functionality — they can still use their neural interface and devices normally, but no emissions escape the containment field.
Properties.aliases: SCD-1, Ghost Box, Signal Killer, Tessera Cloak
Properties.specifications: containment radius: 1 meter; method: Metamaterial EM absorption shell; affected emissions: All electronic device EM leakage; user devices: Normal operation within field; external detectability: Zero EM emissions escape; weight: 0.1 kg; battery: 8 hours active; form factor: Pocket-sized cylinder
Properties.story_hooks: An SCD-1 user walked through a total surveillance zone without triggering a single sensor — the only evidence of their passage was a person-shaped absence in the electromagnetic background.; A modified SCD-1 with expanded radius has been deployed in a meeting room, creating a permanently EM-silent space where no electronic surveillance can operate.

Properties.description:
The Thornwire Mesh Beacon is a self-deploying micro-node array that ejects up to forty-seven semi-autonomous signal relays — each no larger than a thumbnail — across a designated area upon activation. These relays anchor themselves to surfaces using barbed micro-hooks, forming a decentralized mesh network capable of routing encrypted communications through hundreds of independent paths simultaneously. The network self-heals when nodes are destroyed or disabled, rerouting traffic within milliseconds and making it nearly impossible for signal-tracing equipment to identify the origin or terminus of any transmission.

What distinguishes the Thornwire from conventional mesh nodes is its hostile-environment calibration. The relays are coated in a radar-absorbent ceramic compound developed in partnership with Arcturus Defense Solutions, and each node autonomously cycles through seventeen frequency bands to avoid detection sweeps. The beacon unit itself is roughly the size of a closed fist, ruggedized against EMPs with a faraday-wrapped core, and can be thrown, mounted, or buried — activating on impact, timer, or remote trigger.

The Thornwire is the backbone comms solution for insurgent cells, fixers coordinating multi-team operations, and corporate black-site security teams who need deniable communications infrastructure that leaves no central point of failure. Street-level crews prize it for its disposability — once a job is done, a single destruct signal reduces every relay to slag, leaving nothing for forensics teams to recover.
Properties.tactical_use: Deployed at the start of an operation to establish a communications backbone that survives partial network destruction. Operators throw or roll the beacon into a target area — interior or exterior — and the nodes scatter and anchor automatically. Team leads can assign frequency partitions to different squad elements, maintaining separation even if one channel is compromised. The self-destruct function is critical for operational security: a single encrypted destruct ping collapses the entire network before extraction, eliminating forensic evidence of the comm infrastructure.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88's underground, 'dropping a Thorn' has become slang for establishing serious operational intent — it signals to crew members that leadership is treating a job as high-stakes, not improvised. Ownership of a Thornwire is a quiet status marker among mid-tier fixers, implying connections to military surplus pipelines or corporate supply leaks. Law enforcement views recovered Thornwire units as evidence of organized criminal infrastructure rather than opportunistic crime, and their presence at a scene typically escalates investigative response significantly.
Properties.specifications: node_count: 47; deployment_radius: Up to 300 meters; network_range: 1.2 km effective, 3 km degraded; frequency_bands_cycled: 17; encryption_standard: AES-512 equivalent (proprietary ADSC cipher); self_destruct_method: Thermal overload, 800°C localized burn; battery_life: 72 hours continuous operation; dimensions: 11 cm x 9 cm x 7 cm (beacon unit); weight: 340 grams; node_dimensions: 1.2 cm diameter per relay; emp_resistance: Class IV Faraday shielding
Properties.story_hooks: A Thornwire beacon is recovered from a crime scene — but its destruct signal was never sent, suggesting the operator was killed or captured before they could wipe it. The mesh logs contain partial routing data that could identify every party involved in the operation.; Someone is selling counterfeit Thornwire units that look identical to the real thing but contain a hidden passive transmitter that reports all communications to an unknown third party. Crews are being burned, and nobody knows why their operational security is failing.; A Thornwire network has been active in the Underlevel for six weeks without a destruct signal — either the operator is still running an operation, or they're dead and the mesh is routing ghost traffic from an unknown source.; Arcturus Defense Solutions is quietly recalling a specific production batch of Thornwire beacons, offering generous replacement terms with no questions asked. The reason given is a 'firmware defect,' but the recall only targets units sold through gray-market channels.

Properties.description:
The Chromatic Null Shroud is a full-body garment woven from Vantablack Media's proprietary photon-harvesting microfiber, capable of absorbing up to 99.96% of incident visible light across a 180-degree arc. Embedded within the weave are micro-actuated chromophore cells that sample ambient light from the environment and dynamically redistribute it across the garment's surface, rendering the wearer as a near-perfect visual void that blends into low-light backgrounds rather than standing out as a silhouette.

What distinguishes the Chromatic Null Shroud from simpler blackout garments is its passive operation mode — it requires no power cell during static concealment, drawing only trace current from body heat via integrated thermoelectric strips. Active dynamic blending, used during slow movement, consumes roughly 0.4W and can be sustained for six hours on a standard micro-cell. The garment's outer layer is also treated with a radar-diffusing aerogel coating that scatters millimeter-wave sensor returns, making it effective against automated perimeter systems.

Originally developed for Vantablack Media's deep-cover documentary crews operating in contested corporate zones, the Shroud quickly found a secondary market among infiltrators, black-bag operatives, and high-end couriers. Its civilian framing as 'broadcast equipment' has kept it in a regulatory gray zone for years, and Vantablack Media has made no apparent effort to close that loophole.
Properties.tactical_use: Best deployed in low-light or no-light environments where visual concealment is the primary concern. Users typically pair it with a separate thermal dampener, as the Shroud offers no IR suppression. Effective for slow crawls through monitored corridors, static observation posts, and close-approach surveillance. The compression pouch form factor means it can be worn under a conventional jacket and deployed quickly in the field.
Properties.cultural_context: In Meridian 88's underground circles, owning a Chromatic Null Shroud is a marker of professional seriousness — it signals that the wearer operates at a level where off-the-shelf dark clothing no longer suffices. Vantablack Media's branding gives it a veneer of journalistic legitimacy that mid-tier operatives exploit shamelessly at checkpoints. Among corporate security analysts, the phrase 'they were wearing the Shroud' has become shorthand for 'we have no visual record of the subject.'
Properties.specifications: visible_light_absorption: 99.96% (static), 97.2% (slow movement); radar_cross_section_reduction: ~68% against 24–77 GHz bands; active_power_draw: 0.4W (dynamic mode); passive_power_draw: 0W (static mode, thermoelectric sustain); battery_life_active: 6 hours (standard micro-cell); weight: 1.1 kg; form_factor: Full-body hooded garment, collapses to 0.4L compression pouch; thermal_bleed: Minimal — no active suppression, upper body heat still visible to IR; wash_cycles_rated: 200 before chromophore degradation
Properties.story_hooks: A Chromatic Null Shroud surfaces on the black market still containing trace DNA from a missing Vantablack Media journalist — someone wants it recovered before forensics teams find it.; A rash of corporate espionage incidents all share one detail: security footage shows nothing. The investigating team must determine whether a Shroud was involved or if something far more sophisticated is at work.; Vantablack Media issues a quiet recall on a specific batch of Shrouds, citing 'chromophore degradation.' Operatives who've used those units start receiving unmarked messages suggesting the garments were also collecting biometric data.; A player needs to acquire a Shroud quickly but the only available unit belongs to a Vantablack Media crew currently embedded in a hostile zone — negotiation, theft, or trade required.

Nodes.Name: Vantablack Media field crews in contested broadcast zones

Properties.description:
The Consensual Blind Relay is a two-party encrypted communication device that functions on a mutual authentication principle — neither party can transmit until both have physically interacted with paired units within a 90-second window. This handshake requirement was originally designed for Vantablack Media's investigative journalism division, where source protection demanded that no communication could be initiated unilaterally or under duress. Each unit generates a one-time cryptographic handshake derived from both users' biometric pressure signatures, creating an encryption key that exists nowhere in either device's memory after the session ends.

The relay itself transmits over a narrow-band compressed audio channel that mimics the acoustic fingerprint of routine data telemetry — the kind of background noise that Meridian 88's mesh infrastructure produces constantly. A conversation between two CBR units looks, to any intercepting system, like a malfunctioning environmental sensor reporting ambient temperature data. Vantablack's engineers spent considerable effort ensuring the mimicry layer holds up against the city's more sophisticated traffic analysis algorithms, and the current firmware version has not been successfully de-anonymized in active testing.

Despite its journalistic origins, the Blind Relay has found a far wider audience. Lawyers conducting privileged consultations, corporate defectors arranging handoffs, and couples conducting affairs in surveilled housing blocks all use variants of the same device. Vantablack officially discontinued the consumer line after regulatory pressure, but the schematics leaked within six months and third-party units now outnumber originals three to one on the gray market.
Properties.aliases: The Handshake Box, Blind Channel, CBR Unit
Properties.tactical_use: Primarily used for pre-arranged communications where both parties can confirm physical safety before the channel opens. The mutual activation requirement means the device cannot be used to surveil or trick a contact — both people must consent in real time. Field operatives use them for dead-drop confirmation, source meetings, and exfiltration coordination where one-sided communication would be a liability.
Properties.cultural_context: The CBR carries a particular cultural weight in Meridian 88's press underground — carrying one is a tacit acknowledgment that you deal in information someone powerful wants suppressed. Among the general population, the device's reputation for absolute discretion has made it a commodity for anyone conducting business they consider private, whether that's labor organizing or infidelity. The original Vantablack-branded units are collector's items among journalists and civil liberties advocates.
Properties.specifications: form_factor: Two paired units, each 8cm x 5cm x 2cm flat card design; weight: 90g per unit; handshake_window: 90 seconds from first unit activation; biometric_input: Grip pressure array — 24-point palm signature; transmission_range: Up to 4km in standard urban mesh density; session_length: Unlimited within active handshake period; re-authentication required every 6 hours; traffic_disguise: Environmental telemetry packet mimicry, updated via firmware; key_retention: Zero — keys purged on session end or unit separation
Properties.story_hooks: A CBR unit is found on a dead informant — its paired unit is still active somewhere in the city, belonging to someone who doesn't yet know their source is gone.; The players receive a CBR unit in the mail with no explanation. Someone wants to meet, but the handshake requires them to show up in person to a location they don't know yet.; A third-party manufactured CBR clone has a subtle flaw in its key disposal — sessions aren't actually being purged. Someone has been quietly archiving conversations for months.; Vantablack Media's legal team is aggressively tracking down the leaked schematics, but the real reason isn't regulatory compliance — the original design contained a hidden channel the engineers never disclosed.

Nodes.Name: Vantablack Media Distributed Echo Mesh Kit

Properties.description:
The Distributed Echo Mesh Kit is a field-deployable mesh networking system packaged as a set of twelve adhesive node discs, each approximately the diameter of a coin and 4mm thick. When placed on surfaces throughout a building, tunnel system, or urban block, the nodes self-organize into a low-power mesh network within ninety seconds, creating a private encrypted communications backbone entirely independent of any existing infrastructure. The mesh operates on frequency-hopping spread spectrum in the sub-GHz band, prioritizing wall penetration and range over bandwidth. The resulting network supports voice, text, and low-resolution positional data for up to eight simultaneous users.

Vantablack Media developed the Echo Mesh Kit ostensibly for their field journalism teams operating in communications-denied environments — protest zones, disaster areas, and regions where corporate or state actors have seized control of local networks. The kit's civilian packaging and media-company branding have allowed it to circulate with relatively light regulatory scrutiny despite capabilities that make it extremely useful for operations that have nothing to do with journalism. Each node is designed to be nearly invisible once placed, with a matte surface that accepts paint, dust, and grime naturally.

The mesh has no central node — if any individual disc is found and destroyed, the network reroutes automatically. Full network collapse requires removal of nine or more of the twelve nodes. The discs are designed to be left behind: they are cheap enough to be considered disposable, and they self-wipe after a factory-set duration between 24 hours and 30 days depending on the configuration selected before deployment.
Properties.aliases: Echo Mesh, The Scatter Kit, Breadcrumbs
Properties.tactical_use: Teams deploy the Echo Mesh Kit before entering a target building or zone, scattering nodes as they move through the space. Once the mesh is live, the team operates on a private network that exists entirely within the physical bounds of the deployment — no signal leaves the mesh perimeter in any meaningful form, and no external network access is required. This makes it invaluable in environments where the local network infrastructure has been compromised or is actively monitored. Nodes are placed in inconspicuous locations: inside ventilation grilles, under furniture, on the backs of doors. A standard sweep by corporate security rarely finds more than two or three before the team has completed its objective.
Properties.cultural_context: The Echo Mesh Kit is ubiquitous enough to have become mundane in certain circles — protest organizers, squatter communities, and underground venue operators all use it to maintain communications during events they expect authorities to disrupt. Vantablack's branding has given the kit a kind of countercultural legitimacy; owning one signals that you operate in spaces where the official network cannot be trusted. More sophisticated users treat the disposable nodes as a philosophy as much as a tool: build what you need, use it, leave it behind. Nothing you create has to be permanent.
Properties.specifications: node_count: 12 per kit; node_dimensions: 28mm diameter, 4mm thick disc; node_weight: 4g each; network_setup_time: 90 seconds from first node placement; range_per_node_hop: Up to 120m in open space; 40m through reinforced concrete; max_simultaneous_users: 8; data_types_supported: Voice, text, compressed positional data; self-wipe_timer: Configurable 24h to 30 days; power_source: Integrated micro-battery per node; non-rechargeable, single-use; battery_life: 72 hours active; 30 days standby
Properties.story_hooks: A mesh network left behind after a job is still active weeks later — someone is using the nodes the team left behind, and they are transmitting something the team was never supposed to see.; A pattern emerges: every major incident in the Undercroft district over the past year has been preceded by an Echo Mesh deployment in the same three-block radius.; A character finds a single Echo Mesh node in their apartment that they did not place — the self-wipe timer has been disabled, and it has been active for six months.; Vantablack Media issues a firmware update that reduces the self-wipe window to a maximum of 48 hours, citing 'environmental responsibility.' The real reason is considerably more sinister.; A derelict building slated for demolition turns out to be the center of an ancient Echo Mesh network still running on the last of its battery reserves — the transmissions contain records of something that was never meant to be found.

Nodes.Name: Infiltration teams and corporate espionage operatives

Properties.description: The Hollow Tongue Relay is a passive dead-drop infrastructure device disguised as an ordinary piece of urban furniture or commercial detritus — a cracked utility panel, a branded vending machine fascia, a municipal drainage marker. Internally it houses a heavily shielded, ultra-low-power mesh node that stores encrypted message packets in a write-once buffer, broadcasting nothing until a specifically keyed query device passes within two meters and triggers a silent, microsecond burst transmission. The relay never initiates contact and emits no continuous signal, making it invisible to both passive monitoring grids and active sweep protocols.
Properties.aliases: Dead Tongue, The Hollow, VBM-HTR, Ghost Post
Properties.tactical_use: Hollow Tongue Relays are placed along established courier routes, safe house approaches, and contested territory boundaries. Operatives pass by without stopping, pulling queued messages with a hand-in-pocket fob sweep that takes under a second. The absence of any meeting, any call, any digital handshake means there is nothing for surveillance networks to flag. Messages can be left by any authorized party, creating asynchronous communication chains that survive the loss or capture of individual nodes.
Properties.cultural_context: Vantablack Media's involvement in dead-drop infrastructure is an open secret in Meridian 88 — the company publicly manufactures urban signage and environmental media installations, providing perfect cover for deploying relays city-wide under municipal contracts. Street networks, resistance cells, and competing corporate factions all use the same underlying hardware, creating a strange shared infrastructure of secrets. Finding an unkeyed relay and cracking its buffer is considered a significant intelligence coup; the black market for harvested relay data is substantial.
Properties.specifications: trigger_range: 0.5–2m proximity activation; burst_duration: 8–40 milliseconds; storage_capacity: Up to 200 encrypted message packets; power_source: Ambient RF harvesting + 10-year solid-state cell; detectability: No continuous emission; burst detectable only within 0.5m with specialized hardware; query_device: Dedicated keyed fob or compatible implant; operational_lifespan: 18–24 months before recommended rotation; form_factor: Variable; disguised as environmental object, 8–30cm housing
Properties.story_hooks: The players discover a Hollow Tongue Relay that appears to be double-keyed — someone has been reading the same dead drop as their contact, and has been leaving counter-messages designed to look like the original sender.; A relay placed by a now-dead resistance leader still contains unread messages that predate the cell's destruction; the contents could expose who betrayed them.; Vantablack Media wins a city contract to install 'smart urban signage' across a district the players operate in — within weeks, their operational security begins inexplicably degrading.; A relay's camouflage housing is so convincing it was accidentally incorporated into a building renovation; the construction crew is now unknowingly carrying it in a sealed wall.

Properties.description:
The Orphan Signal Cartridge is a single-use broadcast device designed to transmit a compressed data package — message, file, or audio — across a wide-area signal burst that is specifically engineered to be unattributable to any sender. Vantablack Media developed it as a tool for protected-source journalism: a whistleblower or field correspondent can load the Cartridge with content, set a timed or proximity-triggered release, and walk away. When it fires, the burst mimics the signal profile of legacy infrastructure bleed — the kind of ghost transmissions that Meridian 88's aging broadcast towers emit constantly — making the source indistinguishable from decades-old equipment noise.

The Cartridge is physically a small cylinder, roughly the size of a flare, with a single data input port and a mechanical timer ring. It contains no identifying markings and is manufactured from materials that resist forensic analysis — the polymer casing dissolves in water over 48 hours, and the internal components are designed to thermally self-erase after transmission. The broadcast itself is a single, non-repeating burst lasting between 0.3 and 1.2 seconds depending on data load, making it nearly impossible to triangulate with standard direction-finding equipment.

Vantablack markets the Cartridge under a press-freedom framework and has successfully lobbied for its classification as a journalism tool rather than a communications device in several jurisdictions. In Meridian 88, this legal ambiguity has made it a staple not just of journalists but of anyone who needs to get information somewhere without leaving a trail. The secondary market for used — but not yet fired — Cartridges is surprisingly active, since buyers trust the single-use design to mean no prior data contamination.
Properties.aliases: the Cartridge, Orphan Drop, Ghost Broadcast
Properties.tactical_use: Used for one-way unattributable transmission of critical information — intelligence packages, evidence, operational orders — to a receiving party without establishing any traceable communication channel. Operatives load the Cartridge, place it in a location that will be abandoned before transmission, and the burst fires autonomously. Receivers monitoring the appropriate frequency range and holding the decryption key retrieve the content. The physical Cartridge is never recovered.
Properties.cultural_context: The Orphan Signal Cartridge has a particular resonance in Meridian 88's journalism and activist communities, where it is understood as a tool of last resort — used when someone has information that needs to exist in the world regardless of what happens to them. Finding a fired Cartridge casing is considered a minor omen in some districts, a sign that someone nearby had something important to say. Vantablack's branding around press freedom gives the device a legitimacy that its actual use in the field often exceeds.
Properties.specifications: data_capacity: Up to 500MB compressed; optimized for text, audio, and still images; transmission_duration: 0.3–1.2 seconds dependent on payload; trigger_options: Mechanical timer (1 minute to 72 hours), proximity sensor (paired device or passive human-presence), manual; signal_profile: Mimics legacy broadcast infrastructure bleed; defeats standard source-attribution at 94% confidence; self-destruct: Thermal erasure of internals post-transmission; casing dissolves in water over 48 hours; receiver_requirement: Any device tuned to receive the broadcast frequency range; decryption requires a paired key loaded at time of data input; dimensions: 18cm x 3cm diameter cylinder
Properties.story_hooks: A Cartridge fires in a district the players are operating in — the content is addressed to them by name, from a sender who claims to already be dead.; A player is handed a loaded Cartridge by a panicked contact who says they can't be seen with it any longer; the timer is already running.; Vantablack Media's legal team reaches out: a Cartridge was used to transmit something that is now causing a diplomatic incident, and they need the players to find whoever loaded it before authorities trace the device back to Vantablack's supply chain.; A series of Cartridges have been firing in sequence across the city over the past week, each containing one piece of a larger message — someone is using them as a distributed dead drop for an audience that knows how to listen.

Properties.description: The Parasocial Carrier Mask is a thin, flexible adhesive overlay — resembling a cosmetic skin patch or AR display membrane — worn on the face, neck, or forearm. It functions by encoding encrypted communication data into the metadata streams of legitimate Vantablack Media social broadcast signals: facial expression data, biometric affectation packets, and audience-engagement telemetry that are continuously transmitted by millions of Meridian 88 residents who use Vantablack's ubiquitous personal broadcast ecosystem. The Mask injects covert data into these streams at the packet level, routing messages through Vantablack's own commercial broadcast infrastructure as invisible passengers inside ordinary social media traffic.
Properties.aliases: The Skin, Face Wire, Persona Channel
Properties.tactical_use: The Mask is the preferred tool for long-range covert communication in environments where any RF transmission would be flagged or traced. The operator simply wears the device while passively existing in any area with Vantablack Media coverage — which is most of the inhabited city — and their messages ride out invisibly inside the ambient social data fog. Because the channel is embedded in commercial traffic generated by millions of simultaneous users, isolating any individual covert signal requires either the Vantablack Media proprietary detection suite or extraordinary analytical resources. The device is particularly valued for communication across corpo border checkpoints and through heavily monitored transit corridors.
Properties.cultural_context: Vantablack Media has aggressively and publicly denied any knowledge of the Carrier Mask's existence, while simultaneously — according to leaks from inside their infrastructure division — maintaining a dedicated team tasked with finding and closing the exploit the device relies on. The cat-and-mouse dynamic has become something of an open secret in Meridian 88's hacker and fixer communities. There is profound irony in the fact that Vantablack Media, whose commercial empire is built on monetizing the intimate details of its users' faces and bodies, has inadvertently created the most robust covert communication channel in the city. Some users wear the Mask as a political statement as much as a practical tool.
Properties.specifications: dimensions: Variable — standard facial overlay 22cm x 14cm; forearm variant 18cm x 8cm; weight: Less than 30g; range: Global, wherever Vantablack Media broadcast infrastructure exists; bandwidth: Up to 800 bps covert channel within standard broadcast stream; encryption: Layered — outer layer mimics legitimate telemetry; inner payload uses 256-bit asymmetric cipher; power_source: Harvested from wearer's skin bioelectricity; no battery required; wear_duration: Up to 96 hours before adhesive degradation; detectability: Indistinguishable from legitimate Vantablack broadcast traffic without proprietary analysis keys
Properties.story_hooks: Vantablack Media's latest platform update appears to have partially patched the exploit — Masks manufactured before a certain date still work, but new ones don't. The value of existing units has tripled overnight.; A player receives a covert message through a Mask they aren't wearing — someone has spoofed their biometric signature and is using their identity as a carrier channel.; Vantablack Media approaches the players with an unusual offer: help them identify who manufactures and distributes the Mask, in exchange for something very valuable. The obvious question is why they don't just fix the exploit instead.; A Mask recovered from a dead operative contains a steganographic payload that, when decoded, appears to be a live feed from inside a Vantablack Media executive's private residence.
