Ouroboros Energy ThermalSink UR-3 District Waste Heat Exchange Network

Properties.description:
The ThermalSink UR-3 is a district-scale thermal infrastructure system that captures waste heat from industrial processes, server farms, transit systems, and dense commercial blocks across a defined urban grid sector and redistributes it as usable thermal energy through a network of insulated glycol-water carrier pipes and heat exchanger nodes. Each node — roughly the size of a utility cabinet — manages bidirectional thermal flow, accepting excess heat from high-output sources and delivering it to residential and commercial buildings for space heating, hot water, and agricultural thermal regulation. The UR-3 improves on earlier district heating models by using Ouroboros's proprietary dynamic routing algorithm, which continuously rebalances thermal loads across the network in response to real-time demand and source availability, reducing peak waste heat venting by up to 67%.

The system is physically anchored to Meridian 88's existing utility conduit infrastructure via Palladian Construction-licensed penetration sleeves, meaning installation requires negotiation with both Ouroboros and Palladian for rights-of-way in newer districts. In legacy zones the pipes often run exposed along building exteriors, wrapped in spray-on aerogel insulation that degrades visibly over years without maintenance. Ouroboros operates the UR-3 networks on a metered access model — buildings tap in through licensed exchange units and are billed per gigajoule of thermal energy consumed, with tiered pricing that penalizes draws during peak industrial input cycles.

The ThermalSink UR-3 has become the backbone of winter habitability in several mid-tier residential districts where building heating systems were never modernized. Ouroboros uses its control of the network's routing algorithm as leverage in municipal contract negotiations — documented incidents of 'thermal rebalancing events' that coincidentally dropped output to districts in payment dispute with the corponation have been reported but never successfully prosecuted. Informal tap-ins using homemade heat exchanger rigs are common in the lower districts and are technically prosecutable as energy theft under Meridian 88's Utility Asset statutes.
Properties.aliases: the Bloodstream, Heat Web, UR-Sink, Ouroboros Loop
Properties.social_impact: Ouroboros Energy's control of the ThermalSink UR-3 network has translated directly into political leverage — the corponation effectively holds veto power over winter habitability in any district connected to its grid. This has made Ouroboros a de facto governance actor in zoning decisions, construction approvals, and labor dispute mediations, since the implicit threat of a 'routing recalibration' during a cold snap carries more weight than most contractual enforcement mechanisms. Residents who have built their survival infrastructure around the network have no realistic exit option, as alternative heating systems would require capital investment far beyond lower-tier means.
Properties.story_hooks: A routing anomaly in the UR-3 network has been quietly diverting excess thermal capacity to an unmapped subterranean location for eleven months — Ouroboros's own engineers either don't know or aren't saying; A whistleblower inside Ouroboros has logs showing deliberate thermal restriction events disguised as algorithmic rebalancing, timed precisely to labor organizing meetings in affected districts; An independent engineer has designed a community-scale thermal buffer tank that could insulate a block from UR-3 supply interruptions — Ouroboros is moving to acquire her workshop through a subsidiary; The ThermalSink network's carrier pipes run directly beneath a district where Dredge Mining Collective has begun exploratory drilling — the vibration is causing microfractures in the pipe joints

Ouroboros Energy VoltCarriage EC-9 Inductive Roadway Transit Pod

Properties.description:
The VoltCarriage EC-9 is a six-passenger autonomous ground transit pod manufactured in partnership between Ouroboros Energy and Cinderblock AI, designed to operate exclusively on Ouroboros-managed inductive charging roadway segments embedded in Meridian 88's primary arterial corridors. The EC-9 carries no onboard battery system of meaningful capacity — instead, it draws continuous power from a resonant inductive coil array beneath its chassis that couples with Ouroboros's embedded road transmitter grid, receiving up to 180 kW while in motion. This design philosophy eliminates charging downtime entirely but creates absolute dependency on Ouroboros-maintained road infrastructure. The pod's Cinderblock AI piloting system manages platooning formations of up to 12 EC-9 units traveling in coordinated convoys at 110 km/h, reducing aerodynamic drag and increasing per-road-segment passenger throughput significantly.

The EC-9 operates on a subscription transit model: Ouroboros sells route access packages tiered by corridor priority, meaning that a premium subscriber's pod receives uninterrupted inductive power and convoy priority queuing, while a basic-tier pod may experience deliberate power-throttling during peak demand — slowing it to a crawl or forcing it to a holding bay while premium traffic passes. The vehicle's exterior is smooth, low-slung, and visually identical across subscription tiers by deliberate corporate policy, which Ouroboros markets as 'egalitarian design.' The pods communicate continuously with the Saltmarsh Telecom AtmoMesh network for environmental routing adjustments and with the PiezoCore LD-5 grid for energy credit accounting when the pod traverses pedestrian-adjacent surface zones.
Properties.social_impact: The VoltCarriage EC-9 has effectively transferred control of Meridian 88's primary road corridors from municipal transit authorities to Ouroboros Energy, since the inductive road segments require Ouroboros maintenance contracts to function and the company retains the right to throttle or deny power to any pod on the network. This has been used at least twice during labor disputes — Ouroboros quietly throttled EC-9 service to districts where union organizing was active, framing the slowdowns as 'infrastructure maintenance.' The subscription model's deliberate visual uniformity masks a deeply hierarchical system: every pod looks the same, but some arrive on time and some spend hours in holding bays, and the difference is entirely determined by ability to pay.
Properties.story_hooks: An EC-9 pod carrying a corporate whistleblower is held in a 'maintenance bay' indefinitely — the Cinderblock AI piloting system shows no fault, but the pod simply will not move; Someone has hacked a stretch of Ouroboros inductive road to broadcast power without authentication — free, untracked EC-9 travel on a three-block corridor, and the city is fracturing over who's responsible; A Cinderblock AI platooning convoy of 12 EC-9s detaches from its scheduled route and begins moving in a coordinated formation toward the Ouroboros district headquarters — all pods empty; Ouroboros is bidding to extend inductive road coverage into Tier 3 districts, which sounds like infrastructure investment until someone reads the service agreement's power-throttling clauses

Nodes.Name: Ouroboros Energy Wireless Neural Interface Charging

Properties.description: A technology that enables neural interfaces to be charged wirelessly through ambient electromagnetic energy in equipped environments, eliminating the need for physical charging sessions. WNIC uses resonant inductive coupling tuned to neural interface power systems, transmitting energy through dedicated emitters installed in walls, ceilings, and furniture. In WNIC-equipped spaces, neural interfaces charge passively and continuously, never running low on power. Ouroboros has deployed the technology in corporate offices, premium residential buildings, and public spaces in upper-tier districts.
Properties.aliases: WNIC, Brain Charge, Wireless Neural, Ouroboros Pulse
Properties.social_impact: WNIC has eliminated one of the few remaining vulnerabilities of neural augmentation — the need to periodically charge the interface, during which functionality is reduced. In WNIC-equipped environments, augmented individuals never experience diminished capability, while unequipped environments become zones of anxiety where interface power levels are constantly monitored. The technology has created a geographic dependency — leaving WNIC zones means returning to manual charging, which many long-term users find psychologically distressing.
Properties.story_hooks: A WNIC installation has been modified to deliver a subtle data payload along with the charging signal — every neural interface in the building is receiving firmware modifications during routine charging.; A WNIC dead zone has appeared in a previously equipped district — someone is jamming the wireless charging frequency, and augmented residents are experiencing simultaneous interface brownouts.

Nodes.Name: Continuous neural interface power without charging sessions
Ouroboros Energy Wireless Power Distribution Grid

Properties.description: A power distribution system that transmits electrical energy wirelessly using focused microwave beams between relay stations positioned across Meridian 88's skyline. The WPDG eliminates the need for physical power cables in many applications, transmitting energy to receiving antennas on buildings, vehicles, and devices within line-of-sight of relay stations. The system operates at 85% efficiency — lower than wired transmission but acceptable for the convenience of wireless delivery. Ouroboros has been gradually replacing wired infrastructure with WPDG in upper-tier districts where the aesthetic and practical benefits justify the efficiency cost.
Properties.aliases: WPDG, Power Beam, Wireless Grid, Ouroboros Broadcast
Properties.social_impact: The WPDG has created districts where power is ambient — devices never need charging, vehicles draw power from the air, and buildings connect to the grid without cables. This convenience has a cost: the microwave beams, while focused, create a background of low-level microwave radiation that has unknown long-term health effects. Ouroboros's own studies show no measurable harm, but independent researchers have noted correlations between WPDG-dense areas and sleep disruption patterns. Additionally, the wireless nature of the power grid makes it possible for Ouroboros to cut power to specific buildings or devices instantly and remotely.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone has built a device that intercepts WPDG power beams and redirects them — they are stealing megawatts of wirelessly transmitted power and using it to run an unauthorized manufacturing facility.; A WPDG relay station has been repurposed as a weapon — its focused microwave beam has been retargeted from power transmission to directed energy attack, and it is capable of cooking anything in its path.

Nodes.Name: Palladian Construction MagRail Spur MRS-17 Elevated Micro-Transit Chassis

Properties.description:
The MagRail Spur MRS-17 is a modular, elevated single-rail transit system manufactured by Palladian Construction and designed to be retrofitted onto existing building facades, skybridge frameworks, and highway overpasses within Meridian 88's dense interior zones. Each spur segment is a 12-meter prefabricated magnetized chassis bolted to structural anchor points, carrying four-passenger pods suspended beneath the rail via opposing permanent magnet arrays and active electromagnetic trim coils. The pods reach a top speed of 140 km/h between designated micro-stops, which are integrated directly into building lobbies at floors two through eight — bypassing street-level congestion entirely. The system is operated under franchise agreements between Palladian and individual district governance bodies, meaning route coverage is wildly inconsistent: Tier 1 arcology corridors enjoy near-seamless networks while outer-ring districts may have orphaned spur segments that dead-end mid-block.

What distinguishes the MRS-17 from earlier maglev transit attempts is its Cinderblock AI-managed adaptive scheduling kernel, which dynamically reroutes pod dispatch based on real-time structural load data fed by embedded piezo sensors in the chassis itself. If a building anchor registers stress anomalies — common in Meridian 88's aging concrete stock — the system autonomously suspends that spur segment and redistributes traffic. Pods are unpressurized but climate-controlled, with transparent polycarbonate shells that have become a status marker: the cleaner and more intact the pod shell, the higher the district tier. Street culture has developed an entire vocabulary around 'spur-watching' — reading the condition of pods overhead to gauge neighborhood wealth at a glance.
Properties.aliases: Spurs, Palladian Runners, The Seventeen, Rack Lines
Properties.social_impact: The MRS-17 has effectively created a second tier of street-level geography in Meridian 88 — those who can access spur stops inside corporate lobbies versus those who must queue at exposed external platforms in weather and violence. Because Palladian sells spur rights by district block rather than city-wide, the network is a patchwork that mirrors and reinforces existing economic stratification with uncomfortable precision. Riders in Tier 1 zones experience seamless door-to-door elevated transit; residents of Tier 3 zones often find the spurs overhead are literally inaccessible — the stops are inside buildings they cannot legally enter.
Properties.story_hooks: A Palladian engineer discovers that a spur segment anchored to a condemned building in the Outer Flats has been quietly kept active — someone is using it for off-manifest pod runs at 3 AM; A Cinderblock AI scheduling anomaly begins routing pods through a spur network that doesn't officially exist on any city infrastructure map; A district council votes to nationalize their local spur segment; Palladian's enforcement response escalates faster than anyone anticipated; A runner needs to cross three corporate-lobby spur stops without valid citizenship credentials — the pods' biometric entry panels are the obstacle

Nodes.Name: Ringo Corponation DriftPack RV-6 Personal Vectored Thrust Harness

Properties.description:
The DriftPack RV-6 is a wearable, short-range personal aerial mobility harness manufactured by Ringo Corponation, designed for individual transit across Meridian 88's mid-to-upper vertical strata where conventional transit infrastructure is sparse or inaccessible. The harness consists of four articulated micro-turbine pods mounted on a carbon-ceramic spine frame worn across the torso and shoulders, fed by a dual CascadeCell supercapacitor bank integrated into the lower back section. At full charge, the RV-6 provides approximately 18 minutes of sustained flight at a maximum altitude of 340 meters above ground level, with a top horizontal speed of 95 km/h. The thrust vector control system interfaces directly with the wearer's center-of-gravity through a gyroscopic feedback harness, allowing experienced operators to fly with minimal manual input, though Ringo markets a neural control module upgrade compatible with their EchoLimb proprioceptive interface platform for users with upper-limb augmentation.

The RV-6 is legally restricted to licensed operators in designated aerial corridors managed by Tessera Corponation's airspace authority, but the black market for unlicensed units has made it one of the most prevalent illegal mobility tools in Meridian 88's upper slum strata. Ringo deliberately engineered the DriftPack with modular components that are individually legal to purchase, a design philosophy that has created a thriving gray-market assembly ecosystem. The harness includes an emergency ballistic parachute deployment system rated to 40 meters minimum altitude, a feature that has become tragically relevant given the frequency of unlicensed use in sub-40-meter inter-building gaps.

Among licensed corporate courier services, the RV-6 is the standard-issue personal transport for Tier 2 rapid-response logistics personnel. Among Tier 4 populations, a working DriftPack assembled from salvage components — known as a 'ghost rig' — represents months of savings and the difference between economic mobility and confinement to a flooded lower district.
Properties.aliases: Drift Rig, Ringo Wings, The Pack, RV-Six, Skimmer Kit
Properties.social_impact: The DriftPack RV-6 has created a sharp and politically charged divide in Meridian 88 between those who can afford licensed aerial mobility and those who risk death assembling gray-market equivalents. Tessera's airspace enforcement drones are programmed to fire suppression charges at unlicensed flyers in restricted corridors, a policy that has killed dozens of Tier 4 riders attempting to reach employment or medical facilities inaccessible by ground transit. Ringo Corponation has publicly condemned unlicensed assembly while quietly maintaining a parts distribution network that makes it trivially possible, a calculated business strategy that generates revenue from both the licensed market and the gray-market assembly ecosystem.
Properties.story_hooks: A Tier 4 teenager who built a ghost rig from salvage has accidentally drifted into a Tessera restricted airspace corridor and been detained — her rig contains components that shouldn't exist on the civilian market; A series of DriftPack failures in the same district have been traced to a single batch of counterfeit CascadeCell modules — someone is deliberately seeding the gray market with sabotaged components; A licensed corporate courier using an RV-6 witnesses something from altitude that they were never meant to see, and now Tessera's enforcement team is hunting them across the mid-city air corridors; Ringo Corponation is developing an RV-6 successor with mandatory real-time telemetry — the existing RV-6 user community, legal and illegal alike, is organizing to resist the update

Ringo Corponation SlipThread MX-3 Urban Cable Micro-Mobility Rig

Properties.description:
The SlipThread MX-3 is a personal urban cable-transit harness system manufactured by Ringo Corponation, designed for individual rapid traversal of Meridian 88's vertical built environment. Unlike the DriftPack RV-6 vectored thrust harness, the MX-3 operates on pre-tensioned synthetic fiber cables — called 'threads' — anchored between buildings at heights between 20 and 200 meters. The user wears a low-profile chest and shoulder rig housing a motorized grip-and-release carriage mechanism, braking regenerative coils, and a Cinderblock AI micro-routing chip that calculates descent angles, load tolerances, and junction transfer points in real time. Threads themselves are maintained under licensed networks in Tier 1 and 2 districts, with Ringo charging monthly access fees for use of certified anchor points. The carriage mechanism reaches travel speeds of up to 60 km/h on a favorable grade and can execute mid-line transfers at junction nodes — small anchor platforms bolted to building facades where multiple cable routes intersect.

The MX-3 was originally marketed to corporate courier services and building maintenance contractors as a faster alternative to elevator banks in dense arcology clusters. Its adoption as a personal mobility system by Tier 1 and 2 residents followed after Tessera Corponation integrated SlipThread access nodes into several of its high-rise residential towers as a premium amenity. The system's social stratification is immediate and visible: certified Ringo network threads are color-coded with luminescent jacketing in upper-tier districts, while the outer rings run unlicensed black-market threads of wildly variable quality — salvaged synthetic cable, improvised anchor bolts, and carriage mechanisms cannibalizedprimarily from the MX-3's own gray-market component supply chain.
Properties.aliases: Threads, Ziplines, Ringo Strings, The Web
Properties.social_impact: The SlipThread MX-3 has created a visible class division written directly into the skyline: in wealthy districts, the luminescent certified thread network is a deliberate architectural feature, a display of connectivity and premium citizenship. In outer-ring zones, the black-market thread networks are dense, tangled, and regularly lethal — anchor failures, overloaded cables, and untested carriage mechanisms produce a steady casualty rate that Ringo's legal team has spent considerable resources ensuring cannot be traced back to component liability. The ability to move rapidly through vertical space without touching the street has become a marker of status and safety simultaneously, since street-level in many districts is genuinely dangerous.
Properties.story_hooks: Someone is systematically cutting certified Ringo threads in a Tier 2 district — not the anchors, just the cables, precisely, in sequence, as if following a map; A Cinderblock AI routing chip in an MX-3 rig begins directing its user to junction nodes that aren't on any official network map — and the threads there are definitely not Ringo-manufactured; A corporate executive is found dead at a thread junction platform in a district she had no business being in — her certified rig shows she traversed six unlicensed threads to get there; Ringo is rolling out MX-4 with a mandatory biometric lock — the entire black-market MX-3 ecosystem is about to be rendered incompatible, and the outer-ring communities that depend on it are organizing

Nodes.Name: Tessera Corponation StratoTram VX-8 Aerial Cable Transit Gondola

Properties.description:
The StratoTram VX-8 is Tessera Corponation's modular aerial gondola transit system designed to thread passenger movement through Meridian 88's densest vertical construction zones, where ground-level congestion and subterranean flooding make conventional transit impractical. Each gondola cabin is a self-balancing, climate-controlled capsule carrying up to 22 passengers, suspended from a tensioned carbon-composite cable network anchored to Palladian-certified building spines. The VX-8 distinguishes itself from earlier cable transit generations through its dynamic cable tension management system — onboard actuators in each gondola communicate with anchor pylons to redistribute load in real time, allowing the system to remain operational in Great Lakes wind events up to Category 3 storm conditions without emergency shutdown.

The gondola cabins themselves are fabricated with AeroSkin-derived adaptive paneling that reduces aerodynamic drag during high-wind conditions and doubles as a surface for embedded Saltmarsh Telecom signal relay nodes, making each passing gondola a mobile component of the city's communications mesh. Tessera integrated a tiered access system into the boarding terminals: Tier 1 and Tier 2 citizens board from enclosed climate-controlled stations with biometric fast-lane processing, while lower-tier riders queue at exposed platform decks with no environmental protection. The class stratification is architectural and deliberate.

The VX-8 network currently spans 34 active corridors across the mid-city strata, with Tessera holding exclusive operating licenses on 28 of them. Competing operators have attempted to establish parallel cable routes only to find that Tessera's anchor agreements with Palladian-constructed buildings create effective monopoly chokepoints over the most economically valuable transit corridors.
Properties.aliases: Sky Tram, The Wire, VX-Eight, Tessera Rope
Properties.social_impact: The StratoTram VX-8 has become one of the most visible symbols of Meridian 88's tiered society — the same cable carries the same gondola, but the experience of riding it is determined entirely by citizenship tier. Tier 4 riders who depend on the VX-8 as their only reliable transit option during flood seasons have documented hypothermia cases from exposed waiting platforms, while Tessera's quarterly reports highlight 'premium ridership satisfaction' metrics. The system's monopoly on anchor rights has made it effectively impossible for municipal or community-operated transit alternatives to emerge in mid-city corridors, cementing Tessera's stranglehold on basic mobility.
Properties.story_hooks: A gondola carrying a Tier 1 corporate delegation has been seized mid-cable by someone who has disabled the anchor pylon release mechanisms — they have demands; A journalist discovers that Tessera has been harvesting biometric boarding data from all tiers of riders and selling it to Arcturus Defense Solutions without disclosure; Three VX-8 corridors simultaneously go dark during a storm event — the backup systems have been deliberately disabled and 200 people are stranded mid-cable across the city; A Tier 4 community organizer has discovered a legal gap in Tessera's anchor agreements that would allow a rival cable route to be established — Tessera's response has been swift and violent

Nodes.Name: Building facade access and maintenance routing
Saltmarsh Telecom AtmoVolt CV-1 Atmospheric Capacitive Energy Harvesting Antenna

Properties.description:
The AtmoVolt CV-1 is a rooftop-mounted atmospheric electricity harvesting system that exploits Meridian 88's persistently elevated atmospheric charge gradient — a consequence of industrial aerosol loading, waste heat convection columns, and the electromagnetic interference profile of the city's dense communications infrastructure. Each CV-1 unit consists of a 4.2-meter aluminum-alloy antenna mast fitted with a corona discharge array of 144 tungsten micro-needle emitters, a high-voltage collection electrode insulated by ceramic standoffs, and a Saltmarsh-designed charge accumulation and rectification module that converts the captured atmospheric potential difference into stable DC output. Under standard Meridian 88 atmospheric conditions, a single CV-1 unit generates a modest but continuous 200–800 W, with significant output spikes during the city's frequent electrical storm events, when instantaneous capture can briefly reach 4–6 kW before the overvoltage protection system engages.

The CV-1 is not a primary generation system — its output is too variable and weather-dependent for baseload applications. Its value proposition is as a supplementary trickle-charge source for capacitor banks, battery arrays, and building energy storage systems, effectively harvesting ambient electrical energy that would otherwise dissipate. Saltmarsh Telecom developed the CV-1 primarily as a self-powering solution for its own AtmoMesh QL-7 air quality sensor nodes, but recognized the commercial potential of the underlying hardware and has since sold installation licenses to building operators, independent power brokers, and infrastructure resellers. The unit's antenna profile is visually similar to standard telecom relay equipment, providing a degree of regulatory ambiguity that has made it popular for installations in areas where energy harvesting permitting is contested or backlogged.

In the upper tiers of Meridian 88's arcology towers and the spire districts, CV-1 arrays are sometimes installed in clusters of 20–50 units across rooftop areas, generating collective outputs of 10–40 kW that meaningfully offset building operating costs. In lower-tier districts, single units are more common, typically wired to community battery banks or directly to high-priority loads like water pumps and medical equipment. The storm-spike behavior has created a niche community of 'stormchasers' — independent operators who monitor weather pattern data and manually connect high-capacity loads to CV-1 outputs during peak atmospheric events to capture free energy bursts.
Properties.aliases: Static Tower, CV-1, Stormtapper, Volta Spike
Properties.social_impact: The AtmoVolt CV-1's visual similarity to legitimate telecom hardware has made it the energy equivalent of a gray market — technically regulated, practically ubiquitous in ways that regulators cannot easily track. Ouroboros Energy has lobbied the Meridian 88 Infrastructure Authority to require CV-1 output to be routed through metered grid interconnects rather than direct building use, arguing that unmetered atmospheric harvesting constitutes 'energy theft from the commons.' The argument is legally novel and largely absurd, but reflects genuine corporate anxiety about a cheap, unmonitorable distributed generation technology proliferating across every rooftop in the city. In Tier 4 communities, CV-1 units are sometimes the only legal power generation hardware residents can acquire and install without corporate intermediaries.
Properties.story_hooks: A cluster of CV-1 units on a Tier 3 arcology rooftop has begun generating output orders of magnitude beyond spec during clear weather — and Saltmarsh Telecom's remote diagnostics show the units are functioning normally, meaning something in the local atmosphere is wrong; An Ouroboros Energy lobbyist is found dead on a rooftop surrounded by CV-1 units, electrocuted — the units are functioning normally, and the atmospheric charge data for that evening shows a perfectly ordinary night; Saltmarsh Telecom is quietly embedding a secondary data-harvesting function in CV-1 firmware updates — the antenna array can be repurposed to intercept unencrypted short-range communications when atmospheric conditions are right, and someone has noticed the pattern in the update logs; A Tier 4 community has wired 60 CV-1 units across their district into a coordinated storm-capture network powerful enough to run a clandestine manufacturing operation — the infrastructure is invisible to corporate grid monitoring, and someone wants to know what they're making

Nodes.Name: Atmospheric electricity and corona discharge physics
Saltmarsh Telecom NerveTap IQ-9 Neural Traffic Metadata Interception Node

Properties.description: The NerveTap IQ-9 is a passive neural-traffic interception system installed within Saltmarsh Telecom's urban mesh relay infrastructure — the same tower and repeater network that carries encrypted neural augmentation traffic between implants and cloud processing services. The IQ-9 hardware module does not decrypt intercepted transmissions; instead, it captures and logs the metadata envelope of every neural data packet passing through its relay node: transmission timing, packet size distributions, handshake signatures, signal modulation fingerprints, and the unique hardware identifiers of transmitting implants. Saltmarsh's analytics backend correlates this metadata stream to construct behavioral and social graphs without ever accessing protected communication content, sidestepping the Meridian 88 Neural Privacy Compact's content-protection provisions.
Properties.aliases: The Sniffer, IQ-Tap, Nerve Hook, Signal Ghost
Properties.tier_availability: Infrastructure-level (passive; affects all neural augmentation users regardless of tier)
Properties.social_impact: The NerveTap IQ-9 has effectively ended the practical anonymity of neural augmentation in Meridian 88, including for citizens who invested heavily in unregistered or black-market implants believing they were operating outside the surveillance grid. The revelation that metadata — not content — is sufficient to identify, locate, and profile augmented individuals has produced a crisis of trust in neural technology itself, with some communities in lower tiers deliberately avoiding augmentation upgrades or using older, less efficient implants that generate less distinctive transmission signatures. For corporate security apparatus, the IQ-9 represents a comprehensive map of the city's augmented population that exists entirely outside legal challenge.
Properties.story_hooks: A crew member's black-market implant has been flagged as a ghost signature by the IQ-9 network — someone is using the Saltmarsh feed to track them, and they need to either go dark or find a way to alter their electromagnetic fingerprint; A Saltmarsh engineer is selling raw IQ-9 metadata pulls for specific geographic zones — the data would expose which corporate operatives were present at a location during a critical incident; Someone has discovered that the IQ-9 network has a ghost signature that has been active for three years with no corresponding registered identity — an augmented individual who exists nowhere in any corporate database; A civil rights organization wants to prove the IQ-9 network exists and is being used for targeting — they need someone to physically retrieve a NerveTap module from a relay tower for forensic analysis
